title: Arthroscopic Rotator Cuff Repair: Know When to Hold 'Em, Know When to Fold 'Em.
authorString: Droz LG, George A, Bravman JT, Lin A, Freehill MT, Klifto CS.
abstractText: Rotator cuff tears represent one of the most common musculoskeletal conditions encountered in orthopaedic surgery, and the decision to repair, partially repair, or forgo primary repair remains one of the most clinically nuanced challenges facing shoulder surgeons. The ideal outcome after rotator cuff surgery depends not only on technical execution but also on appropriate patient selection and preoperative planning. Patient-specific factors including age, diabetes, smoking status, obesity, hypertension, and hypercholesterolemia directly influence tendon biology, healing capacity, and functional recovery. Equally important are tear-specific characteristics such as tear size, chronicity, degree of fatty infiltration, tendon retraction, and residual tendon length, all of which inform the reparability of a given tear. It is important to present a systematic framework for evaluating both patient and rotator cuff characteristics to guide surgical decision making. Using established classification systems including the Goutallier classification of fatty infiltration, the Patte grading of tendon retraction, and the Hamada classification of rotator cuff arthropathy, along with emerging tools such as the Rotator Cuff Healing Index, surgeons can more reliably predict which tears are amenable to repair and which may benefit from alternative interventions such as partial repair or reverse total shoulder arthroplasty. Ultimately, selecting the right procedure at the right time and knowing when not to repair are the cornerstones of excellent outcomes in rotator cuff surgery.

title: Implementation of an Oxytocin Dosing Protocol for Cesarean Delivery.
authorString: Conley RP.
abstractText: Rapid intravenous administration of oxytocin is associated with adverse cardiovascular effects, including hypotension, tachycardia, myocardial ischemia, and stroke. In a community hospital, oxytocin was commonly administered as a rapid free-flow infusion during cesarean delivery, potentially increasing patient risk. The primary aim of this quality improvement project was to implement a standardized oxytocin dosing protocol for cesarean delivery. A secondary aim was to evaluate differences in quantitative blood loss (QBL) before and after implementation. Relevant literature was reviewed and graded using established criteria. The "Rule of Threes" oxytocin protocol was adapted for local cesarean use and implemented following multidisciplinary education. QBL for cesarean deliveries before and after protocol implementation was compared. Thirty-six parturients were analyzed (18 pre- and 18 postimplementation). Mean QBL was 442 ± 161 mL preimplementation and 418 ± 121 mL postimplementation. The difference was not statistically significant (t = 0.26; df = 34; P = 0.8). Implementation of a standardized, lower-dose oxytocin protocol did not increase QBL, suggesting uterine tone and hemorrhage risk were not adversely affected while potentially reducing oxytocin-related cardiovascular risk. Integration of the protocol into infusion pump drug libraries and pharmacy standardization may further enhance medication safety.

title: Cerebral actinomycosis in pediatrics: Brain abscesses caused by Schaalia georgiae.
authorString: Sánchez Marrón A, Antonelli Sanz AS, Gamarra M, Orlando MN, Cazes CI, López EL.
abstractText: Actinomycosis is a rare bacterial infection caused by Gram-positive bacilli of the order Actinomycetales, which are commensals of the oral cavity. Involvement of the central nervous system is exceptional and is usually associated with hematogenous spread from a dental focus. We report a case of cerebral actinomycosis in an immunocompetent pediatric patient following a tooth extraction. We present a 14-year-old female patient with partially corrected congenital heart disease who developed multiple brain abscesses from which Schaalia georgiae was isolated. Surgical drainage and intravenous antibiotic therapy were administered for six weeks, followed by a prescription for long-term oral doxycycline and outpatient follow-up. The nonspecific clinical presentation, polymicrobial nature, and difficulty isolating the organism make diagnosis challenging. This case highlights the importance of considering actinomycosis in the differential diagnosis of pediatric brain abscesses and of a timely medical-surgical approach to improve clinical outcomes and reduce sequelae.

title: Association of Cardiac Rehabilitation with Mortality after Aortic Valve Replacement (TAVI/SAVR): A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
authorString: Cerezo-Arroyo M, Guadalupe-Grau A, Rodríguez-Gómez I, Delgado-Hernando Á, Alegre LM, García-García FJ, Ara I, Valenzuela PL.
abstractText:
Aims

Surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) and transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) treat severe aortic stenosis. Although cardiac rehabilitation (CR) improves functional recovery, its association with mortality remains unclear. We aimed to assess this association in adults following TAVI or SAVR.

Methods

PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception to April 17, 2026. We included randomized and observational studies comparing mortality after CR versus usual care following TAVI or SAVR. Study quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Random-effects meta-analyses and exploratory meta-regressions were performed.

Results

A total of 7 observational studies (n=178,525 participants) were included (six pooled; n=92,213), all focusing on all-cause mortality. Participants reported mean or median ages ranged from 67 to 83.9 years, with 37-66.7% women across studies. All studies were deemed to have a high methodological quality. Pooled results revealed that CR was associated with a lower all-cause mortality risk compared to control groups (HR 0.59 [95% CI 0.41-0.84], p=0.004; I2=95%). Sensitivity analyses yielded similar results, as did sub-analyses restricted to TAVI participants (HR 0.68 [95% CI 0.50-0.92], p=0.012). No sub-analysis could be performed for SAVR participants alone. Exploratory meta-regression analyses found no statistically significant associations between studies' characteristics (e.g., patients' age, CR duration, follow-up length) and effect estimates (all p>0.05), although these findings should be interpreted cautiously given the small number of studies.

Conclusion

Participation in CR after TAVI/SAVR is associated with a lower risk of all-cause mortality. Future studies should determine whether participants' or interventions' characteristics modulate these effects.

title: Procalcitonin-Guided Antibiotic Initiation in Adults Presenting to Emergency Departments With Suspected Infection: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
authorString: Tariq MI, Kukreja NS, Chawla S, samad A, javaid MH.
abstractText: Emergency physicians must balance timely treatment of bacterial infection against unnecessary antibiotic prescribing. We systematically reviewed randomized controlled trials evaluating whether procalcitonin-guided care changes initial antibiotic initiation or prescription in adults presenting to emergency departments with suspected infection. PubMed, Embase, CENTRAL, ClinicalTrials.gov, and WHO ICTRP were searched from inception through August 25, 2026. Trials were pooled when outcome definitions were sufficiently comparable, using random-effects meta-analysis with modified Hartung–Knapp confidence intervals. Ten trials (13,286 participants) were included; four respiratory infection trials (3,602 participants) contributed to the primary synthesis. Procalcitonin-guided care reduced initial antibiotic initiation or prescription (risk ratio, 0.87; 95% confidence interval, 0.82–0.92; I²=0%; high-certainty evidence), corresponding to approximately 89 fewer patients receiving or being prescribed antibiotics per 1,000. Sensitivity analyses produced similar estimates. For 28- to 30-day mortality, the pooled risk ratio across five trials was 0.92 (95% confidence interval, 0.57–1.49; low-certainty evidence); estimates for intensive care unit admission and antibiotic-related adverse events were imprecise. This updated review provides a decision-specific estimate of reduced initial antibiotic prescribing in emergency department respiratory infections and clarifies how differences in outcome definitions, trial designs, and patient populations affect interpretation of earlier syntheses. Effects on mortality and other clinical outcomes remain uncertain overall, and the respiratory prescribing estimate should not be extrapolated to undifferentiated fever, suspected sepsis, or acute heart failure.

title: Impact of Obstructive Sleep Apnea and Its Treatment on Atrial Fibrillation Recurrence Following Catheter Ablation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
authorString: Wahi P, Gilbert J, Borean M, Almaghrabi M, Hameed A.
abstractText: Background and Aims: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is common among patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) and may adversely affect outcomes following catheter ablation. Although continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) therapy has been associated with improved rhythm outcomes in observational studies, its effect remains uncertain. We evaluated the association between OSA and AF recurrence following catheter ablation and the association between CPAP therapy and recurrence among patients with OSA. Methods Ovid MEDLINE, Embase, and Emcare were searched from inception to 27 September 2026 for studies reporting AF recurrence following catheter ablation according to OSA or CPAP treatment status. Random-effects meta-analyses using restricted maximum likelihood estimation were performed to calculate pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Heterogeneity, prediction intervals, small-study effects, and sensitivity analyses were assessed. Risk of bias was evaluated using the Methodological Index for Non-Randomized Studies and Joanna Briggs Institute tools. Results Twenty-two studies met the inclusion criteria, of which 19 studies comprising 5,748 patients contributed to the quantitative synthesis. OSA was associated with an increased risk of AF recurrence following catheter ablation across 16 studies (RR 1.43, 95% CI 1.30–1.58; I² = 16.3%), with a 95% prediction interval of 1.16–1.75. Among patients with OSA, CPAP use was associated with a lower risk of AF recurrence across eight studies (RR 0.60, 95% CI 0.48–0.75; I² = 47.1%); however, the 95% prediction interval (0.33–1.09) included the null. Findings were stable in sensitivity analyses. Conclusion OSA was associated with increased AF recurrence following catheter ablation. CPAP use was associated with lower recurrence among patients with OSA, although moderate heterogeneity, a prediction interval crossing unity, and predominantly observational evidence limit causal inference. Further adequately powered randomized trials are needed to determine whether CPAP directly improves post-ablation rhythm outcomes.

title: The effectiveness of interprofessional collaborative practices in the management of hypertension, diabetes and/or obesity in adults and older adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis
authorString: Molica VKR, Jacinto MMRS, Mingote ALP, Jorge ELGdM, Ferreira EdS, Costa GDd, de Almeida FM, Cotta RMM.
abstractText: Background Interprofessional collaborative practice (ICP), including dietitians, is important for the care of obesity, diabetes and hypertension. However, evidence on the effectiveness of these practices for managing these conditions in adults and older adults is scarce. This study aimed to analyze the effectiveness of ICP involving dietitians in the management of hypertension, diabetes and/or obesity in adults and older adults through a systematic review and meta-analysis. Methods A search was conducted in the PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, LILACS, Scopus, Web of Science and Cochrane Library databases on 28 April 2026, following the PRISMA guidelines. Studies that focused on ICP with dietitian involvement and that assessed glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), systolic (SBP) and diastolic blood pressure (DBP) and body mass index (BMI) were included. The meta-analysis was conducted with the randomized controlled trials using Jamovi software. A random-effects model was adopted, and the effect size was expressed as the mean difference with 95% confidence intervals (95% CI). Heterogeneity was assessed using the I 2 statistic. Methodological quality was assessed with the Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal tools, and publication bias with funnel plots and Egger's regression test, at a 5% significance level. Risk of bias was assessed with the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool. Results Thirty articles were included in the systematic review, of which 10 (1,782 participants) were included in the meta-analysis. Several studies showed positive effects of ICP on the clinical and biochemical outcomes assessed. The meta-analysis showed that ICP reduced HbA1c (− 0.58; 95% CI − 1.00 to − 0.15; p = 0.008) and SBP (− 4.99; 95% CI − 9.89 to − 0.09; p = 0.046), but not BMI (− 1.22; 95% CI − 2.93 to 0.50; p = 0.164) or DBP (− 1.44; 95% CI − 4.18 to 1.30; p = 0.303). All outcomes showed high heterogeneity (I 2  > 75%). Conclusions ICP showed favorable results in the management of diabetes, hypertension and obesity. The meta-analysis indicated the effectiveness of these interventions in reducing HbA1c and SBP. These findings highlight the relevance of interprofessional work, including dietitians, in the care of chronic diseases.

title: Sildenafil for Fetal Growth Restriction - An Individual Participant Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Groom KM, Bruins ME, Liauw J, Jakobsen JC, Olsen MH, Gluud C, Kariya C, Mackay LK, von Dadelszen P, Sharp A, Lim K, Ganzevoort W.
abstractText:
Background

Phosphodiesterase type-5 inhibitors have been investigated as an in utero therapy for fetal growth restriction (FGR).

Methods

We conducted a systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis of randomized trials of phosphodiesterase type-5 inhibitors versus placebo/no treatment in singleton pregnancies with FGR. The primary outcome was infant survival without serious adverse outcome. Secondary outcomes included gestation at birth and birth weight z score among liveborn infants. Predefined subgroups were evaluated.

Results

Of 19 eligible trials, 4 contributed data. Of 492 participants, 240 had been assigned to placebo and 252 to the phosphodiesterase type-5 inhibitor sildenafil. Infant survival without serious adverse outcome occurred in 110 of 240 participants (45.8%) assigned to placebo versus 113 of 252 participants (44.8%) assigned to sildenafil (relative risk [RR], 0.96; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.78 to 1.17). No apparent interaction was observed between subgroups. There was no apparent difference in gestation at birth (mean difference -0.5 weeks; 95% CI, -1.3 to 0.2) or birth weight z score (mean difference, 0.0; 95% CI, -0.2 to 0.2). Persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn occurred in 10 of 176 participants (5.7%) assigned to placebo versus 27 of 197 participants (13.7%) assigned to sildenafil (RR, 2.39; 95% CI, 1.23 to 4.61); nitric oxide was used in 15 of 176 participants (8.5%) assigned to placebo versus 20 of 197 participants (10.2%) assigned to sildenafil (RR, 1.21; 95% CI, 0.64 to 2.29).

Conclusions

Maternal sildenafil therapy for FGR was not associated with improved outcomes for infants. It was associated with persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn but not with an increase in nitric oxide therapy. (Funded by Health Research Council of New Zealand and others; PROSPERO number, CRD42017069688; ANZCTR number, ACTRN12612000584831; ISRCTN number, ISRCTN39133303; ClinicalTrials.gov numbers, NCT02442492 and NCT02277132.).

title: Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve Replacement Versus Medical Therapy for Severe Secondary Tricuspid Regurgitation: The TRIPLACE Registry.
authorString: Scotti A, von Stein P, Puri R, Sturla M, Coisne A, Ludwig S, Echarte-Morales J, Zahr F, Boone R, Kodali SK, Tchétché D, De Backer O, Stolz L, Estevez-Loureiro R, De Marco F, Mangieri A, Garcia SA, Ben Ali W, Mahabadi AA, Ho EC, Cheung A, Biroli M, Curio J, Patrascu A, Alnasser S, Chadderdon S, Kobari Y, Guddeti R, Sievert H, Byrne T, Maisano F, Frerker C, Dumonteil N, Oliva OA, Rudolph TK, Rudolph F, Kirchner J, Krishnaswamy A, Kapadia SR, Del Portillo J, Rodés-Cabau J, Schofer N, Cruz-González I, Adam M, Granada JF, Hausleiter J, Hahn RT, Modine T, Fam N, Latib A, TRIPLACE Investigators.
abstractText:
Background

Severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR) carries a poor prognosis, yet comparative real-world data on transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR) versus medical therapy remain limited.

Objectives

The aim of this study was to compare clinical outcomes of TTVR versus medical therapy in patients with secondary TR.

Methods

This observational study included the TRIPLACE registry (NCT06033274; TTVR cohort, N = 395, 24 centers, 2017-2025) and the Bronx-Valve Registry (NCT05453526; medical therapy cohort, N = 784, single center, 2017-2019). A 30-covariate propensity score was used for overlap weighting, targeting the average treatment effect in the overlap population (ATO). The primary endpoint was the 2-year composite of all-cause mortality or heart failure (HF) hospitalization.

Results

TTVR achieved ≤ mild TR in 93.7% and ≤ moderate TR in 98.7%. In-hospital mortality was 0.8%. The most common 30-day adverse events were new permanent pacemaker implantation (14.8%) and severe bleeding (6.5%). Median follow-up was 363 days (Q1-Q3: 63-1,151 days). After ATO weighting, all covariates included in the propensity score model achieved exact mean balance (maximum standardized mean difference: 0.000). TTVR was associated with a lower 2-year primary endpoint (ATO-HR: 0.60 [95% CI: 0.40-0.89]; P = 0.012) and lower all-cause mortality (ATO-HR: 0.61 [95% CI: 0.38-0.99]; P = 0.044), whereas HF hospitalization did not differ significantly between groups (ATO-cause-specific HR: 0.69 [95% CI: 0.39-1.24]; P = 0.215).

Conclusions

In this observational comparison, TTVR was associated with a lower 2-year risk of all-cause mortality or HF hospitalization compared with medical therapy in patients with secondary TR. These findings should be interpreted in the context of procedure-related risks and the nonrandomized study design.

Registration

(Global Multicenter Registry on Transcatheter TRIcuspid Valve RePLACEment [TRIPLACE]; NCT06033274).

title: Clinical Outcomes Through 12 Months After Drug-Coated Balloon-Based Coronary Intervention: A Single-Center Real-World Registry.
authorString: İşleyen HB, Uzunoğlan S, Şişman BH, Abanoz O, Danışman E, Uluganyan M.

journal.title: Turk Kardiyoloji Dernegi arsivi : Turk Kardiyoloji Derneginin yayin organidir

abstractText:
Objective

Real-world registries complement clinical trial evidence by characterizing outcomes of drug-coated balloon (DCB) interventions across heterogeneous coronary lesions. This study described clinical outcomes through 12 months and the completeness of follow-up in a single-center registry.

Method

Patients who underwent DCB-based coronary intervention at a single tertiary referral center between September 2023 and November 2025 were retrospectively reviewed. The eligible cohort comprised 352 patients and 414 index-procedure lesions; time-to-event analyses included 288 patients with a recorded follow-up interval greater than zero. The primary reported outcome was a post hoc, non-prespecified composite of all-cause death, any myocardial infarction, or target lesion revascularization (TLR). Only events with a valid post-index date were included. Kaplan-Meier estimates were truncated at 365 days.

Results

The median follow-up duration was 202.5 days (interquartile range, 83.5-340.0); 158 (54.9%) and 60 (20.8%) patients had at least 180 and 365 days of recorded follow-up, respectively. During all available follow-up, the study-defined composite occurred in 22/288 patients (7.6%), and TLR occurred in 17/288 (5.9%). The 12-month Kaplan-Meier estimate was 10.5% (95% CI, 6.2%-17.3%; 55 at risk) for the composite and 8.5% (95% CI, 4.6%-15.4%; 56 at risk) for TLR. Exploratory inverse-probability-of-observation-weighted estimates were similar.

Conclusion

In this heterogeneous single-center registry, the 12-month estimates were 10.5% for the composite and 8.5% for TLR, with similar exploratory weighted results. These findings provide contemporary descriptive single-center registry data following DCB-based intervention; however, interpretation should remain cautious because only 20.8% of patients had at least 365 days of recorded follow-up, and only 55-56 patients remained at risk at day 365.

title: SGLT-2 inhibitors across competing pathways of type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease and heart failure
authorString: Owen R, Hazel I, Lyons J, Latimer N, Adler A, Guthrie B, Lyons R, Abrams K.
abstractText: Type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease and heart failure commonly co-exist, yet multi-indication therapies such as sodium-glucose co-transporter-2 (SGLT-2) inhibitors are appraised one indication at a time. Here we combine multi-state models evaluating the natural history of disease including the order in which these conditions accrue, fitted to linked electronic health records for 1.3 million adults in Wales, with treatment effects from randomised controlled trials in a patient-level simulation. Among people diagnosed with at least one of the three conditions, SGLT-2 inhibitors increase mean life expectancy by 1.81 years (95% CI: 0.96, 2.73) compared with standard of care, and delay a subsequent diagnosis of type 2 diabetes by up to 3.09 (95% CI: 1.42, 4.80) years, with the longest delays in people living with both chronic kidney disease and heart failure. In people with type 2 diabetes, treatment reduces the risks of developing chronic kidney disease and heart failure more than the risk of death, so more people die without a further diagnosis; reductions in individual transitions therefore do not translate proportionately into gains in life expectancy. Evaluating multi-indication therapies across whole disease pathways, rather than single conditions, could better inform health policy for people living with multiple long-term conditions.

title: Randomization schemes and Bayesian borrowing of survey-derived control information in a simulated cardiovascular prevention trial: a simulation study based on the 2022 Canadian Community Health Survey
authorString: Rafi SEA.
abstractText: Background: Randomization strategies and external baseline-risk information can influence covariate balance and the operating characteristics of clinical trials. We evaluated these approaches using a population-based virtual patient population. Methods: We used the 2022 Canadian Community Health Survey (CCHS) to construct a virtual population of adults aged 50 years or older for a hypothetical cardiovascular prevention trial. In Part A, four randomization schemes were compared across 2,000 simulated trials of 2,400 participants. In Part B, Bayesian 1:1 and 2:1 designs using a robust mixture prior informed by CCHS prevalence were evaluated across 10,000 simulations per scenario, with varying degrees of prior–data conflict. Results: Minimization improved covariate balance, reducing the mean maximum standardized difference from 0.086 to 0.030, while differences in type I error and power across randomization schemes were small. When external information matched the true control rate, Bayesian borrowing increased power to 88.2% in the 2:1 design. However, prior–data conflict increased type I error to 6.1% and reduced power under certain scenarios. Conclusions: Survey-derived information may improve trial efficiency, but its benefits depend on the accuracy of external baseline-risk assumptions. Prior–data conflict should be carefully evaluated when designing Bayesian trials.

title: Ciprofol versus propofol for gastrointestinal endoscopy in hypertensive patients: a randomized double-blind controlled trial
authorString: Zhuang¹ H, Zhang¹ J, Liu¹ H, Luo¹ M, Zhu¹ Y, Li¹ H, He¹ Q, Lu¹ Y.
abstractText: Background Hypotension during sedated gastrointestinal endoscopy is clinically relevant in patients with hypertension because long-standing hypertension may impair cardiovascular compensation. Propofol can cause dose-dependent cardiovascular and respiratory depression. We compared the incidence of hypotension with ciprofol and propofol in this population. Methods In this single-center, parallel-group, double-blind randomized controlled trial, patients aged 18–75 years with primary hypertension, American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status II–III, and body mass index 18–28 kg/m² who were scheduled for sedated gastrointestinal endoscopy were assigned 1:1, using a computer-generated sequence and sealed opaque envelopes, to ciprofol 0.5 mg/kg or propofol 2.0 mg/kg after sufentanil 0.1 µg/kg. Patients, endoscopists, anesthesiologists, outcome assessors, and statisticians were blinded. The primary outcome was hypotension during the procedure (systolic blood pressure < 90 mmHg or > 30% decrease in mean arterial pressure from baseline). Secondary outcomes included hemodynamic variables, time metrics, rescue vasoactive medication use, and adverse events. Results A total of 122 patients were randomized (61 per group), and all were analyzed. Hypotension occurred in 14 patients (23.0%) receiving ciprofol and 26 (42.6%) receiving propofol (relative risk, 0.54; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.31 to 0.93; absolute risk reduction, 19.7%; 95% CI, 3.0% to 34.9%; P = 0.021). Norepinephrine was given to the same patients per protocol. In unadjusted secondary comparisons, injection pain (0% vs 19.7%; P < 0.001) and respiratory depression (3.3% vs 18.0%; P = 0.008) were less frequent with ciprofol. After adjustment for baseline, mean arterial pressure did not differ significantly between groups at any time point. Induction time, procedure duration, recovery time, and body movement did not differ significantly. All procedures were completed. Conclusions Ciprofol reduced the incidence of hypotension compared with propofol in hypertensive patients undergoing sedated gastrointestinal endoscopy. Lower rates of injection pain and respiratory depression are supportive but require confirmation. Larger multicenter trials are warranted. Trial registration: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR2500110441. Registered on 14 October 2025 (prospectively registered).

title: Selected Topics in Differential Geometry in Biophysics and Medical Physics: A Review of Five Domains
authorString: Sing LY.
abstractText: Biological morphology, molecular mechanics, medical image analysis, and physiological wave propagation frequently obey constraints that are intrinsically geometric rather than Euclidean. This article develops a unified geometric perspective across five selected domains of continuum biophysics and clinical medical physics. First, we explore extrinsic surface geometry, Canham–Helfrich and area-difference elasticity, and Gauss–Bonnet topological barriers in lipid membranes and viral scission. Second, we examine principal \(\mathrm{SO}(3)\) Cosserat frame bundles, twist connections, and the Călugăreanu–White–Fuller theorem in DNA supercoiling and isoform-specific topoisomerase pharmacology. Third, we cover the Cartan–Hadamard symmetric space \(\mathrm{Sym}^+(3) \cong \mathrm{GL}(3,\mathbb{R})/\mathrm{O}(3)\), Log-Euclidean similarity geometry, and multi-fiber spherical extensions in Diffusion MRI and neurosurgical tractography. Fourth, we discuss infinite-dimensional Sobolev metrics on diffeomorphism groups \(\mathrm{Diff}_V(\Omega)\), Euler–Poincaré (EPDiff) geodesic flows, and differential-form dose accumulation in computational anatomy and four-dimensional adaptive radiotherapy. Finally, we address principal gauge connections, Pancharatnam–Berry geometric phases, and topological phase defects in low-Reynolds-number motility, adiabatic MRI pulse design, and cardiac arrhythmia mapping. Alongside pedagogical derivations (collected in technical appendices), we critically compare competing physical models, evaluate numerical discretization pitfalls, uncertainty quantification, and phantom/clinical validation benchmarks, and clarify where idealized geometric invariants must be tempered by physiological dynamics and clinical trial evidence.

title: Evaluation of right ventricular function in patients with severe and very severe mitral stenosis: insights from advanced echocardiographic techniques.
authorString: Bigdelu L, Boskabady M, Moolooghy K, Azari A, Amirbeik L, Dadgarmoghaddam M, Ebrahimi N.
abstractText:
Background

Right Ventricular (RV) failure has a critical role in the onset and progression of clinical symptoms and the prognosis of patients with Mitral Stenosis (MS), but the exact role, effect, and pathophysiology of RV dysfunction in MS are still controversial. In this study, we aimed to evaluate echocardiographic signs of systolic RV dysfunction using Tissue Doppler Imaging (TDI) and Velocity Vector Imaging (VVI) in subjects with severe and very severe MS.

Methods

46 isolated MS cases (23 severe and 23 very severe) and 23 healthy controls were enrolled in this study. RV function was assessed by tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE), fractional area change (FAC), and peak systolic velocity of the tricuspid annulus (S') using TDI, and RV free wall strain (RVFWS) employing VVI. Furthermore, these values correlations with mitral valve area (MVA) and pulmonary arterial pressure (PAP) were assessed.

Results

TAPSE, FAC, S', and RVFWS values were substantially declined in MS cases compared with healthy controls. Moreover, PAP values were considerably increased in MS subjects. Additionally, S' and TAPSE values were significantly lower in very severe MS patients compared with severe patients.

Conclusion

RV systolic function deteriorates in patients with severe and very severe MS. It appears that the degree of the severity of MS can proportionately affect the extent of RV dysfunction and some of its echocardiographic markers such as S' and TAPSE. TDI and VVI can be used as practical early diagnostic methods for RV dysfunction in MS.

Clinical trial number

not applicable.

title: What's good for the gander is good for the goose: might tadalafil be a "polypill" for postmenopausal women?
authorString: Maraghi S, Simon JA.
abstractText: After the Women's Health Initiative Hormone Trial led to reduced use of menopausal hormone therapy, many women missed the "window of opportunity" for treatment. This perspective considers the repurposing of tadalafil, a phosphodiesterase type 5 (PDE5) inhibitor, as a "polypill" for postmenopausal women. PDE5 inhibitors enhance nitric oxide-cyclic guanosine monophosphate signaling, promoting vasodilation, smooth muscle relaxation, and increased blood flow. This mechanism may offer benefits across multiple body systems, including cardiovascular, urogenital, and possibly cognitive systems. These benefits and their long-term effects are well-established in men; limited clinical trials in women suggest similar potential. Existing studies have been small and focused on specific indications rather than long-term outcomes. Large, randomized controlled trials are needed to determine the efficacy and safety of PDE5 inhibition in women and whether the hypothesized benefits would translate into meaningful clinical outcomes.

title: Acute Cardiac Biomarker Responses to High-Intensity Interval and Continuous Running Under Matched Physiological Load in Middle-Aged Recreational Men.
authorString: Menderes Y, Akın Ş, Somay Selbes Y, Lavie CJ, Ekinci YE, İlicepınar ÖF, Karanfiil Y, Demirel HA.
abstractText:
Objective

High-intensity interval exercise (HIIE) is gaining popularity due to its efficiency and cardiovascular benefits. However, it remains unclear whether intermittent supramaximal exercise bouts induce greater acute cardiac biomarker responses than continuous exercise (CE) when overall physiological workload is matched. This study aimed to compare the acute cardiac biomarker responses to HIIE and CE in recreational runners under equivalent exercise conditions.

Methods

Fifteen male recreational runners (41.8 ± 8.3 years; maximal oxygen uptake [VO2max] 46.8 ± 4.1 mL·kg⁻1·min⁻1) completed 2 1-hour outdoor running sessions in a randomized crossover design with 1-2-week washout. Protocols were CE (~72% of velocity at VO2max [vVO2max]) and HIIE (12 × 1-minute intervals at ~107% vVO2max, 4-minutes recovery jogs). Blood samples were collected before (PRE), immediately after (POST), and 3 hours post-exercise (POST+3) to assess serum high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI), N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), creatine kinase-MB, and myoglobin. Heart rate, speed, and percentage vVO2max were comparable between protocols.

Results

High-sensitivity cardiac troponin I increased significantly at POST+3 versus PRE in both protocols (P < 0.001), with no between-protocol differences. Creatine kinase-MB and myoglobin rose significantly at POST and POST+3 in both conditions (P < .05). N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide showed no significant changes between protocols. No biomarker differed between HIIE and CE at any interval, and hs-cTnI and NT-proBNP remained within clinical reference ranges throughout.

Conclusion

When duration and workload are matched, HIIE does not elicit greater acute cardiac biomarker responses than CE, suggesting intermittent supramaximal exercise does not impose greater acute myocardial stress than CE in recreationally active middle-aged men.

title: Albumin alleviates pressure overload-induced heart failure by improving mitochondrial homeostasis via PKA-LKB1-AMPK axis
authorString: AN Q, Ma B, Fu Y, Luo Y.
abstractText:
Aims:

Heart failure (HF) is a global health challenge due to its high incidence, mortality, and socioeconomic burden. Despite medical advancements, HF prognosis remains poor, highlighting the need for enhanced understanding and treatment strategies. Serum albumin, a key circulatory protein, has gained attention as a biomarker in cardiovascular diseases. Low serum albumin levels are linked to HF incidence, progression, and prognosis, suggesting its regulatory role, though mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to elucidate the role of serum albumin in HF pathogenesis and investigate its potential therapeutic effects. Methods and results A mouse model of pressure overload-induced HF was established via transverse aortic constriction (TAC). Serum albumin levels were significantly decreased in HF mice. Administration of recombinant mouse serum albumin (rMSA) effectively restored serum albumin concentrations, improved cardiac systolic function, alleviated cardiac hypertrophy and fibrosis, and reduced inflammatory responses, collectively attenuating disease progression. In contrast, albumin-knockout (Alb⁻/⁻, AKO) HF mice displayed aggravated pathological manifestations compared with wild-type (WT) controls, whereas rMSA supplementation markedly ameliorated these impairments. In vitro experiments demonstrated that rMSA protected against phenylephrine (PE)-induced hypertrophy in cardiomyocytes. To elucidate the underlying mechanism, transcriptomic analyses of cardiac tissues revealed that albumin played a critical role in improving mitochondrial homeostasis. Experimental validation further demonstrated that albumin activated the PKA-LKB1-AMPK signaling axis, leading to improved mitochondrial respiratory function and oxidative phosphorylation, as well as enhanced mitochondrial quality control. These changes promoted fatty acid oxidation and optimized energy metabolism, thereby reversing the energy imbalance underlying cardiac dysfunction. Conclusion Our study suggests that serum albumin exerts a protective effect in HF by improving mitochondrial dysfunction and energy metabolism disorders, thus reversing energy imbalance and mitigating disease progression. These results support recombinant serum albumin as a promising therapeutic for HF, with its mechanism involving the critical improvement of mitochondrial homeostasis.

title: Plasma-Polymerized Polyurethane/Reduced Graphene Oxide Electrospun Patch for Cardiac Tissue Engineering
authorString: Jugie C, Mousavi A, Nemati A, Wertheimer M, Ajji A, Savoji H.
abstractText: Cardiovascular diseases remain the leading cause of mortality worldwide. Traditional treatments, including heart transplantation, are limited by the scarcity of donor organs and the need for lifelong immunosuppression, highlighting the urgent need for alternative therapies. Cardiac patches represent a promising approach to restoring heart function by providing structural support and promoting cardiac tissue regeneration. Here, we developed biocompatible and conductive electrospun cardiac patches, aiming to mimic the structural, mechanical, and electrical properties of the native myocardium. polyurethane (PU) was selected as the base material due to its favorable mechanical properties and biocompatibility. Reduced graphene oxide (rGO) was incorporated into the electrospun PU fibers to enhance electrical conductivity, and a low-pressure plasma-polymerized nitrogen-rich (LPPE:N) coating was applied to improve cell adhesion. The fabricated patches were characterized through various techniques, including scanning electron microscopy, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, tensile testing, and conductivity measurements. Also, in vitro cytotoxicity assay using primary cardiac fibroblasts confirmed the biocompatibility of the patches. These physicochemical, electromechanical, and biological characterizations suggest that the rGO/LPPE:N-functionalized PU patches demonstrate promising potential for cardiac tissue engineering applications.

title: From Genomic Diversity to Molecular Mechanism: Computational Prediction and Structural Insights into Gain-of-Function PCSK9 Variants for Precision Cardiovascular Medicine
authorString: Kulshreshtha A, Kumar Y, Bhatnagar S.
abstractText: Context Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death worldwide, and PCSK9 regulates plasma LDL-C levels via degrading LDLR. Gain-of-function (GOF) variants of PCSK9 increase cardiovascular risk, whereas loss-of-function (LOF) variants have a beneficial effect. Methods The Indigenome database was mined for non-synonymous single nucleotide polymorphisms of PCSK9 using five different tools. Consensus deleterious predictions from three methods were selected. Further, structural stability was studied using I-Mutant2.0 and PremPSv1.0.1. Missense3Dv2 and HOPEv1.1.1 delineated altered residue properties. Modeling and MD Simulation (MDS) of GOF variants of the PCSK9–LDLR complex was done using GROMACS2021.1. Protein structural networks (PSNs) were constructed using WebPSNv2.0. Two known (R357C and R496W) and three novel (S89W, Q413R and R680W) GOF variants of PCSK9 were mined. One was unique to the Indian population (Q413R). MDS of the GOF mutants showed lower residue flexibility with increased LDLR interfacial area comprised of more contacting residues and hydrogen bonds in comparison with wild type. Two known and three predicted GOF variants formed fewer clusters with broadened FEL, lower MMPBSA binding energies and remodeled PSN edges. These findings suggest that GOF associated effects are caused by changes in long range residue connectivity and the dynamic organization of the PCSK9–LDLR complex, providing mechanistic insights into variant specific functional consequences. Comparison of GOF structure, dynamics and PSN with LOF PCSK9 can be used to distinguish the two states. Based on the insights gained into structure activity relationships from this study, annotation of PCSK9 functional variants can advance precision medicine strategies for cardiovascular disease.

title: Impact of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists on Postoperative Complications and Long-Term Outcomes in Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Retrospective Cohort Study Stratified by BMI
authorString: Kishan A, Khela H, Manriquez A, Eward W, Amanatullah D, Lozano-Calderon S, Avedian R.
abstractText:
Purpose: Obesity is a recognized risk factor for adverse outcomes after total knee arthroplasty (TKA), including increased postoperative complications and revision rates. Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists reduce obesity-related health risks; however, their impact on postoperative outcomes in TKA patients, particularly across different body mass index (BMI) categories, remains unclear. This study evaluates the association between GLP-1 receptor agonist use and short- and long-term outcomes following TKA, stratified by BMI.

Methods:

A retrospective cohort study was performed using the PearlDiver database, identifying patients who underwent primary TKA between 2010 and 2021 using ICD-9/10 and CPT codes. GLP-1 receptor agonist users were matched 4:1 to non-users based on age, sex, and Charlson Comorbidity Index. Patients were stratified into six BMI categories (< 19.9, 20.0–24.9, 25.0–29.9, 30.0–34.9, 35.0–39.9, and ≥ 40.0 kg/m²). Outcomes included 90-day medical complications and two-year surgical events.

Results:

Among 47,359 GLP-1 users and 12,032 matched controls, GLP-1 use was associated with significantly lower 90-day postoperative complication rates across BMI categories, particularly among patients with BMI ≥ 30 who had reduced incidences of renal failure, anemia, cardiac arrhythmias, pulmonary embolism, pneumonia, and stroke (p < 0.05). At two years, GLP-1 users demonstrated significantly lower rates of periprosthetic fractures, revision surgeries, mechanical loosening, and prosthetic joint infections, most notably in patients with BMI 25–29.9 and ≥ 30 (p < 0.05).

Conclusion:

GLP-1 receptor agonist use is associated with reduced postoperative complications and improved long-term surgical outcomes, especially in patients with higher BMI, suggesting a potential role in perioperative optimization for obese TKA patients. Level of Evidence III

title: Silent Stroke in a 4-Year-Old Boy During Recovery from Diabetic Ketoacidosis: A Rare Complication with Diagnostic Pitfalls
authorString: Fayyazi A, Amiri E, Darabi D, Hadizadeh A, Janaati F, Darabi M.
abstractText: Background : Stroke is an exceedingly rare complication of diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) in children and may be overlooked due to its atypical presentation. Case : We report a case of previously healthy 4-year-old boy was admitted with severe DKA (pH 6.9, blood glucose 620 mg/dL). On the 3 rd day of ICU admission, post-resolution of acidosis, he developed acute right-sided hemiplegia. Brain MRI demonstrated an acute ischemic stroke in the left middle cerebral artery (MCA) territory, with no evidence of underlying cardiac or thrombophilic abnormalities. Follow-up : The patient was managed with aspirin, adequate hydration, and glycemic control were initiated immediately. At a 3-month follow-up, residual mild hemiparesis persisted despite rehabilitation. Conclusion : This case highlights the importance of considering stroke in children with neurologic deficits during or after DKA, even in absence of conventional risk factors.

title: Disparities and Determinants of Cardio-Cerebrovascular Mortality in Middle Aged Patients With Lung Cancer: a population based SEER cohort study, 2000-2021
authorString: Lee Y, Kim AY, Savadkar A, Woo W.
abstractText:
Background: Advances in lung cancer detection and treatment have improved survival, increasing the relative importance of non-cancer causes of death, particularly cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disease. However, data on cardio-cerebrovascular mortality (CCM) among middle aged patients remain limited.

Methods:

We analyzed patients aged 30 to 59 years with pathologically confirmed lung cancer from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) 17 registries (2000–2021). CCM was defined as death due to cardiovascular or cerebrovascular causes. Kaplan–Meier analyses and Cox proportional hazards models were used to evaluate outcomes and identify predictors.

Results:

Among 185,296 patients, CCM occurred in 2.2%. Incidence increased with age, reaching 2.59% in patients aged 55–59 years. Ischemic heart disease accounted for 51% of CCM events, followed by cerebrovascular events (15.1%). Advanced stage disease was associated with higher CCM risk (stage III: HR 1.58, p = 0.001; stage IV: HR 1.64, p < 0.001). Squamous cell carcinoma was associated with a higher risk compared with adenocarcinoma (HR 1.56, p < 0.001). Non-Hispanic Black patients had significantly higher CCM risk (HR 2.54, p < 0.001). Socioeconomic factors were not independently associated with CCM.

Conclusions:

CCM in middle aged patients with lung cancer increases after age 50 and is associated with advanced stage, squamous histology, and Non-Hispanic Black race. These findings highlight the need for targeted cardio-oncology surveillance and preventive strategies in high-risk populations. Trial registration Not applicable

title: Implementing Screening Questionnaires and a Fish Bone Diagram-Based Program to Enhance the Ability of DBW Education in Hemodialysis Nurses
authorString: Wang JY, Tsai YT, chiang MC, Hsiao JC, Chien CJ, Lin Y, Lin Sj.
abstractText: Background: Dry body weight evaluation to detect high and low hydration status is paramount in daily hemodialysis practice. Our aim is to implement screening questionnaires and fish bone diagram-based program to improve the ability of dry body weight education of hemodialysis nurses. Methods: This pioneer research by four staff members was initially authorized by the medical quality and patient safety talent training project and competition meeting initiated by the administrative units of Taipei City Hospital and then approved by Taipei City Hospital Research Ethics Committee with the case number of TCHIRB-11206015.The study began with screening questionnaires of educational test about dry body weight education. Subsequently, teams composed of nurse faculty were evaluated for three domains of dry body weight evaluation, such as hemodialysis nurse’s knowledge and education skills on dry body weight, body components and body weight assessment equipment and tools. A fish bone diagram for root cause analysis was implemented with improvement of knowledge and skills of dry body weight evaluation of nurse faculty, methods of dry body weight evaluation, equipment for dry body weight evaluation, tools of dry body weight evaluation, environment of dry body weight evaluation, and materials of dry body weight evaluation. Results: Wilcoxon Signed Ranks Test are used to identify statistically significant differences in the scores of between the domain 1 and domain 2, between domain 1 and domain 2A, and between domain 1 and domain 2B. The screening questionnaires revealed. A Fish bone diagram was completed and presented to improve the ability of dry body weight education of hemodialysis nurses with dry body evaluation education sheet, poster and ever scam education software. In addition, suggestions for improving the ability of dry body weight education include inclusion of nutritional staff involvement, post- dialysis cardiac echo for inferior vena diameter, chest ultrasound for B lines, Crit-Line for blood volume monitor, DEXA for body composition evaluation, and selection of topics of food salt and water content, techniques and environment of dry body weight evaluation, bio-impedance, and upper arm anthropometry. Conclusions: Accurate evaluation of dry body weight by clinical evaluation, equipment and tools not only can prevent hemodialysis patients from deterioration of cardiopulmonary function and the chance of emergency dialysis due to high hydration status but also prevent patients from hospitalization due to shock and thrombotic complications due to low hydration status, and therefore reduce their medical costs and improve patient satisfaction and trust in the hospital.

title: Ventricular Noncompaction / Ventricular Hypertrabeculation in the Setting of Heterotaxy Syndrome - A Congenital Disorder of Epicardial Origin?
authorString: Alshahrani DA, Salih HG, Alsaiad AM, Jijeh AMZ, Männer J, Yelbuz TM.
abstractText: Data from animal models show that disrupted embryonic epicardial development can cause ventricular noncompaction/hypertrabeculation (VNC/VHT) and suggest that congenital disorders of visceral left-right patterning (heterotaxy syndrome), particularly bilateral left-sidedness (left atrial isomerism, LAI), may lead to VNC/VHT via embryonic/fetal epicardiopathy. In order to clarify whether the animal model-data fit to humans, we evaluated the prevalence, anatomic associations, and outcomes of VNC/VHT in patients with LAI versus right atrial isomerism (RAI). This retrospective cross-sectional study examined 160 pediatric patients with congenital heart disease and heterotaxy treated at a single center (2000–2023). Patients were assigned to LAI or RAI sub-cohorts; myocardial architecture was determined primarily via rigorous, multi-observer echocardiography. Mid- to long-term survival and freedom from intervention were analyzed by Kaplan–Meier methods. Of 160 patients (median age at diagnosis 1.4 months), 115 (72%) had LAI and 45 (28%) had RAI. VNC/VHT of the morphologic left ventricle was identified in 31 patients (19.3% of the total cohort) and was confined exclusively to LAI (26.9% vs 0% in RAI; p=0.001). Among LAI patients, a strong, statistically significant association was uncovered between VNC/VHT and atrioventricular septal defects (AVSDs), which occurred in 61.3% of VNC/VHT patients compared to 33% without VNC/VHT (p=0.007). Five- and 10-year survival did not differ by VNC/VHT status (p=0.74). However, LAI infants with VNC/VHT underwent first intervention significantly earlier (median 3.3 vs 4.7 months; p=0.035), with 80% requiring a procedure by 12 months versus 66% without VNC/VHT (p=0.04). This study provides the first statistically robust evidence of a specific association between LAI and VNC/VHT and confirm the pathogenetic hypothesis that errors in left-right patterning - specifically bilateral left-sidedness - can lead to VNC/VHT via an embryonic/fetal epicardiopathy. Although long-term mortality is unaffected, VNC/VHT accelerates the need for intervention and warrants intensified surveillance in the first year of life.

title: Using multiomic data to predict postoperative complications after major surgery in the UK Biobank cohort
authorString: Armstrong RA, Yousefi P, Gibbison B, Khandaker GM, Gaunt TR.
abstractText:
Background:

Whilst high-dimensional omic profiles from biobanks can predict long-term disease outcomes, their ability to predict postoperative outcomes is unknown. We investigated whether adding metabolomic and proteomic data from historic samples to standard clinical variables improved the prediction of postoperative complications. Methods We analysed data from 158,156 UK Biobank participants who underwent major surgery. The primary outcomes were postoperative atrial fibrillation, acute kidney injury, acute myocardial infarction, delirium, stroke and surgical site infection. We developed machine learning models (elastic net penalised regression) to compare baseline clinical variables against integrated single- and multiomic datasets. To address sample size constraints in high-dimensional omic subsets, we employed transfer learning from related non-postoperative domains. Results The numbers of cases with omic data varied across outcome phenotypes and feature sets: metabolomic: 144–1596, proteomic: 27–289 and multiomic: 15–219. Baseline clinical models achieved robust predictive performance (AUROC 0.72–0.88, sensitivity 0.71–0.80). The addition of metabolomic and/or proteomic features provided no clinically meaningful improvement in discriminative performance metrics for any clinical phenotypes. Transfer learning from the non-postoperative domain improved the stability of omic models, particularly where the source phenotype matched the postoperative outcome, but did not outperform baseline clinical models. Conclusions The addition of metabolomic and proteomic data from samples collected at a temporal distance from surgery does not improve preoperative risk prediction compared to standard clinical variables. The lack of incremental predictive value suggests that long-term biological trajectories have become manifest in routine clinical data by the time of surgery. The performance of transfer learning from non-postoperative settings may indicate shared biological risk between chronic and acute phenotypes.

title: Fatal dengue cases in travellers from 1995 to 2025: A targeted review.
authorString: Dinjer CS, Grobusch MP, Díaz-Menéndez M, Schmidt-Chanasit J, Schwarz TF, Huits R, Bainbridge CS, Mächler C, Steffen R.
abstractText:
Background

Dengue is a mosquito-borne viral disease endemic in 136 countries and territories, with over 14 million cases and more than 10,000 deaths reported globally in 2024 alone. International travellers are at risk of infection when visiting endemic regions. While dengue in travellers is well described, dengue-related mortality in this population has not been comprehensively synthesised. We compiled and critically assessed available data on reports of fatal dengue cases among international travellers over a 30-year period.

Methods

A targeted review was conducted to identify dengue-related fatalities in travellers from non-endemic countries acquiring infection in endemic regions between 1995 and November 2025. PubMed searches using terms related to dengue, mortality, and travel were complemented by hand-searching conference proceedings, national and international surveillance reports, publicly accessible national infectious disease databases, media reports, and anecdotal notifications. Cases were classified as confirmed or probable based on diagnostic method and/or inclusion in surveillance systems. Data were extracted, cross-referenced to avoid duplication, and analysed descriptively.

Results

Sixty-seven fatal travel-related dengue cases were identified, of which 55 were classified as confirmed/probable and 12 cases had limited information. Of the 55 confirmed/probable cases, 22 reported both country of residence and acquisition, spanning 14 endemic destinations. Confirmed/probable fatal cases occurred among patients aged <1-79 years; 25.5% were female, 21.8% were male, and in 52.7% sex was not documented. Where infection status was available, most were primary infections (9/16). Reported fatal manifestations included neurological, cardiac, haemorrhagic, and hyperinflammatory complications. Diagnostic and reporting heterogeneity was substantial, and surveillance gaps were evident.

Conclusions

Dengue-related mortality among travellers is rare but likely under-recognised and underreported. Strengthened diagnostic capacity and heightened clinical awareness may support earlier recognition and management of severe cases in travellers, while harmonised international reporting systems could improve case ascertainment and contribute to future prevention strategies.

title: Predictors of COVID-19 Hospitalization Costs in a Tertiary Hospital in Kuwait: Evidence From Real-World Data.
authorString: Almari M, O'Neill S, Albazzaz N, Alhenaidi A, Alsalahi S, Alsarhan S, Sadique Z.
abstractText:
Objectives

COVID-19 has imposed significant economic pressures on healthcare systems worldwide, with hospitalization costs constituting a major component. In Kuwait, previous estimates have reported average inpatient costs but lacked granularity on cost predictors across diverse patient subgroups. This study examined predictors of COVID-19 hospitalization costs and variations in costs across admission periods in 2021.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional analysis of all patients (N = 7569) admitted to Jaber Al-Ahmed Hospital, the national tertiary referral center for COVID-19 in Kuwait, in 2021. Patient-level hospitalization costs were derived using the microcosting approach reported previously elsewhere from the same cohort. Multivariable generalized linear models were used to estimate marginal cost differences, while accounting for demographic, clinical, and treatment-related characteristics. The month of admission and pandemic wave were included to assess differences in costs across admission periods in 2021.

Results

Intensive care unit admission and the use of remdesivir, corticosteroids, antibiotics, and immunosuppressants were associated with significantly higher costs. Patients with cardiovascular disease, type 2 diabetes, or cancer also incurred higher costs. COVID-19 vaccination and hypertension were associated with lower costs. South Asian and Arab patients had lower estimated costs than Kuwaiti nationals. Costs declined by 24.7% over the year and by 8.6% across pandemic waves.

Conclusions

COVID-19 hospitalization costs varied substantially by patient characteristics, treatment regimens, and over time. Cost differences suggest further investigation into potential differences in disease severity, treatment pathways, and healthcare access. These findings support the need for data-informed, and equitable healthcare planning.

title: Acute Kidney Injury After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation: An Early-Concentrated Mortality Burden.
authorString: Konuş AH, Akyüz AR.

journal.title: Turk Kardiyoloji Dernegi arsivi : Turk Kardiyoloji Derneginin yayin organidir

abstractText:
Objective

Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a recognized complication of transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), but data based on the updated Valve Academic Research Consortium-3 (VARC-3) definition remain limited. We aimed to determine the incidence of VARC-3-defined AKI, identify factors associated with its development, and characterize its prognostic significance in patients undergoing TAVI.

Method

We retrospectively analyzed 106 consecutive patients who underwent TAVI at a single center and had paired baseline and early postprocedural creatinine measurements. AKI was defined and staged according to VARC-3 criteria. Factors associated with AKI were assessed using univariable logistic regression; survival was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier, Cox regression, and landmark analyses.

Results

AKI developed in 16 of 106 patients (15.1%). Lower baseline left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) and higher procedural contrast volume were the only variables significantly associated with AKI in univariable analysis (both p=0.007). Patients with AKI had markedly reduced survival (log-rank p=0.012). Landmark analysis demonstrated that excess mortality was concentrated within the first six months (hazard ratio [HR] 13.23, 95% confidence interval [CI] 3.30-52.96, p=0.0003), with no significant association thereafter.

Conclusion

VARC-3-defined AKI occurred in approximately one in seven TAVI patients and was associated with substantially impaired survival. The excess mortality associated with AKI was concentrated predominantly within the first six months; among patients with AKI who died, the majority of deaths were classified as cardiovascular. These findings characterize the temporal and cause-specific pattern of AKI-associated mortality and should be interpreted as observational associations rather than evidence of a causal effect of AKI.

title: The Association Between Procedure-Related Complications and Mortality After Valve-in-Valve TAVI: A Single-Center Study.
authorString: Usalp S, Kibar M, Küçük A, Çiçek Ş, Kılıçarslan MF, Erdoğan FB, Bulus Ç, Balaban İ, Çakır H, Zehir R, Kıralı MK.

journal.title: Turk Kardiyoloji Dernegi arsivi : Turk Kardiyoloji Derneginin yayin organidir

abstractText:
Objective

Valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve implantation (ViV-TAVI) is an effective treatment option for failed bioprosthetic valves. However, data on mortality predictors, particularly the relative impact of procedural versus baseline clinical factors, remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate all-cause mortality and identify predictors of adverse outcomes in patients undergoing ViV-TAVI.

Method

This retrospective, single-center study included 32 consecutive patients who underwent ViV-TAVI between 2020 and 2025. Patients were stratified into survivor and non-survivor groups. Clinical, procedural, laboratory, and echocardiographic variables were analyzed. Overall survival was evaluated using Kaplan-Meier analysis, while predictors of mortality were examined using Cox proportional hazards regression.

Results

The mean age was 76.0+-8.0 years, and 50% of the patients were female. During a median follow-up of 534 days, all-cause mortality occurred in 25% of patients. Non-survivors were older (78.5 vs. 75.1 years, P = 0.398) and more frequently female (75% vs. 41.7%, P = 0.220). Major vascular injury with retroperitoneal hemorrhage was significantly more common among non-survivors (P = 0.016) and was strongly associated with mortality in both univariate (HR 7.43, 95% CI 1.43-39.71, P = 0.018) and multivariate analyses (HR 9.5, 95% CI 1.840-49.210, P = 0.008). Baseline echocardiographic and laboratory parameters were not associated with mortality.

Conclusion

In this small exploratory cohort study, major vascular injury accompanied by retroperitoneal hemorrhage was associated with increased midterm mortality. These findings are preliminary and hypothesis-generating and require validation in larger, multicenter studies. The results underscore the potential importance of procedural optimization and the prevention of vascular complications in improving clinical outcomes.

title: Inhibition of HRD1 Alleviates Doxorubicin-Induced Dilated Cardiomyopathy via Regulating the Ubiquitination Degradation of COX5A.
authorString: Ding L, Geng Z, Guo HW, Zhu PX, Shi Y, Sun ZY, Pan MF, Su DM, Wang XY, Chen F, Zhou YB, Li QG.
abstractText: Doxorubicin (DOX), a chemotherapeutic agent, can cause heart failure due to loss of cardiomyocytes through programmed cell death. Mitochondrial dysfunction and programmed cardiomyocyte death are central features of DOX-induced cardiotoxicity (DIC), yet the upstream ubiquitin-dependent mechanism linking proteostasis disturbance to mitochondrial respiratory impairment remains incompletely understood. The E3 ubiquitin ligase HMG-CoA reductase degradation protein 1 (HRD1) plays an important role in cardiac function and survival; whether HRD1 elevation contributes to DIC is unclear. This study aimed to determine whether HRD1 promotes DIC by inducing ubiquitination and degradation of cytochrome c oxidase subunit 5A (COX5A), thereby impairing mitochondrial function and aggravating cardiomyocyte death. DOX-treated C57BL/6J mice, primary cardiomyocytes and AC16 cells were used in this study. DOX increased HRD1 expression in mouse cardiac tissue and cultured cardiomyocytes. Genetic and pharmacological inhibition of HRD1 attenuated DOX-induced cardiac dysfunction and myocardial remodelling. In vitro, HRD1 knockdown alleviated, but HRD1 overexpression aggravated DOX-induced apoptosis- and ferroptosis-related cardiomyocyte injury. Mechanistically, HRD1 was associated with COX5A, a nuclear-encoded subunit of mitochondrial respiratory chain complex IV and promoted its ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation. The catalytically inactive HRD1-C291A mutant attenuated this effect compared with wild-type HRD1. Moreover, we also found that COX5A knockdown abolished the protective effects of HRD1 knockdown; by contrast, COX5A overexpression countered the injury associated with HRD1 overexpression. The present study demonstrates that HRD1 promotes DOX-induced mitochondrial dysfunction, cardiomyocyte death, cardiac dysfunction and myocardial remodelling by mediating COX5A ubiquitination and degradation. These findings identify the HRD1-COX5A axis as a potential therapeutic target for DOX-induced cardiac injury.

title: Clinical and Financial Burden of Infectious Complication After Elective Cardiac Operation in the US.
authorString: Ali K, Dadfar B, Gangavelli T, Wong J, Ali SS, Mehta D, Jampol S, Desai K, Benharash P.

journal.title: Journal of the American College of Surgeons

abstractText:
Background

Healthcare-acquired infections (HAI) after cardiac surgery impose substantial clinical and economic burdens. We examined factors associated with HAI and their relationship with mortality, hospital length of stay, and costs in a national cardiac surgical population.

Study design

Adult (≥18 years) elective hospitalizations involving coronary artery bypass grafting, valve repair or replacement, or combined procedures were identified in the 2016-2022 Nationwide Readmissions Database. Entropy balancing followed by regression was used to evaluate associations between HAI and clinical and economic outcomes.

Results

Among an estimated 962,261 patients, 7.4% developed HAI. After risk adjustment, HAI was associated with greater mortality (adjusted odds ratio [AOR], 5.11; 95% confidence interval [CI], 4.82-5.42), an additional 8.54 hospital days (95% CI, 8.23-8.76), and $41,110 in increased hospitalization costs (95% CI, $39,656-$42,565). Older age (AOR, 1.01/year; 95% CI, 1.00-1.02), female sex (AOR, 1.66; 95% CI, 1.62-1.70), and low-income status (AOR, 1.21; 95% CI, 1.17-1.25) were associated with HAI. Sepsis and bacteremia accounted for the greatest incremental costs per episode and largest estimated annual cost burden.

Conclusions

HAI after elective cardiac surgery is associated with markedly greater mortality, prolonged hospitalization, and substantial additional costs. These findings support prioritizing targeted infection prevention within cardiac surgical quality improvement and healthcare resource stewardship.

title: An Interpretable Machine Learning Model for Early Prediction of Septic Shock in Intensive Care Unit Patients: The Incremental Value of Cardiac Output.
authorString: Yue Y, Luo S, Liu S, Ye W, Xu Y, Xiao K, Li Y.
abstractText: BackgroundEarly identification of septic shock is critical for timely resuscitation, yet conventional vital signs such as blood pressure exhibit physiological lag during the compensatory phase. Whether advanced hemodynamic parameters confer incremental predictive value within machine learning (ML) early warning frameworks remains unquantified.MethodsThis retrospective cohort study used the MIMIC-IV v3.0 database. From 7384 patients with hemodynamic monitoring records, 1716 adult ICU patients contributing 16,140 hourly prediction windows were analyzed. Patients were partitioned into a development set (n = 1372) and a held-out test set (n = 344). Two nested models predicted septic shock within 6 h: a baseline model using routine variables and an enhanced model adding cardiac output (CO), cardiac index (CI), stroke volume index (SVI), and systemic vascular resistance index (SVRI). XGBoost was the primary classifier. Patient-level cross-validation and clustered bootstrap evaluated discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility, while SHAP and ablation assessed feature contributions.ResultsThe enhanced model consistently outperformed the baseline across four algorithms. With XGBoost, cross-validated AUROC improved from 0.862 (95% CI 0.847-0.877) to 0.881 (0.867-0.894), a gain of 0.018 (0.010-0.027; DeLong p = 3.22 × 10-11). Sensitivity increased from 0.249 to 0.316 and F1 from 0.335 to 0.388. Held-out AUROC was 0.819 versus 0.844 (p = 2.06 × 10-6). Calibration was comparable, and the enhanced model provided greater net benefit at threshold probabilities of 0.01-0.49. SHAP ranked CO second only to lactate; removing CO reduced AUROC by 0.017 (0.008-0.024), whereas removing the derived indices had negligible effects.ConclusionsIncorporating cardiac output into routine monitoring models provides robust incremental value for early septic shock prediction. CO captures circulatory compromise masked by compensatory normotension and may support risk-stratified ICU surveillance.

title: Care-Seeking Decision Delay in Acute Myocardial Infarction: A Mixed-Methods Study at a Tertiary Hospital in Guangzhou, China.
authorString: Chen B, Lin L, Huang J, Cao X.
abstractText:
Objectives

To examine the duration and associated factors of care-seeking decision delay in adults with acute myocardial infarction(AMI).

Design

Convergent mixed-methods study.

Sample

233 adults with AMI at a tertiary hospital in Guangzhou, China; 13 participants were interviewed.

Measurements

Care-seeking decision delay was calculated from recalled symptom-onset and decision-to-seek-care times, with >60 minutes classified as delayed care seeking. Symptom recognition-related knowledge and care-seeking concerns were assessed using the Chinese Acute Coronary Syndrome Response Index knowledge subscale and Concerns Questionnaire. Quantitative and qualitative data were analyzed using multivariable logistic regression and content analysis, respectively, then integrated.

Results

Overall, 68.7% of participants experienced care-seeking decision delay. Greater social concerns (aOR = 1.24) and non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (aOR = 6.93) were associated with higher odds of delay, whereas greater concern about serious consequences (aOR = 0.69) and accompaniment by friends or colleagues at symptom onset (aOR = 0.02) were associated with lower odds. Interviews described difficulties in symptom interpretation and attribution, limited awareness of chest pain centers, and distrust of local healthcare services as perceived barriers to timely care-seeking.

Conclusions

Care-seeking decision delay was common. Public health nursing strategies addressing symptom recognition, social concerns, and emergency-care pathway awareness warrant further evaluation.

title: Pulmonary hypertension, pulmonary vascular disease, and right ventricular adaptation in transcatheter tricuspid valve intervention.
authorString: Rommel KP, Tello K, Rosenkranz S, Stolz L, Ludwig S, Fortmeier V, Schöber AR, von Stein J, Kassar M, Gerçek M, Stocker TJ, Körber MI, Kister T, Kalbacher D, Pfister R, Baldus S, Windecker S, Thiele H, Praz F, Rudolph V, Hausleiter J, Lurz P, Kresoja KP.
abstractText:
Background

Severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR) commonly coexists with pulmonary hypertension (PH), which is associated with adverse outcomes after transcatheter tricuspid valve intervention (TTVI). However, the prognostic impact of PH subtypes and pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) thresholds in this setting remains insufficiently defined. We evaluated guideline-based PH classifications and their association with outcomes in a large real-world TTVI cohort.

Methods

In an international multicenter registry, 903 patients with severe TR undergoing TTVI underwent pre-procedural right heart catheterization and were followed for up to two years. PH was defined as mean pulmonary artery pressure >20 mmHg, and PVR was stratified according to guideline thresholds. Endpoints included procedural success, New York Heart Association (NYHA) functional class, and all-cause mortality.

Results

PH was present in 88% of patients; among patients with PH, median PVR was 2.7 WU. A pre-capillary component (PVR >2 WU) was observed in 68%, including 13% with PVR >5 WU. Procedural success was 81%. NYHA functional class improved significantly from baseline to follow-up irrespective of PH status or PVR. Mortality increased with PH and higher PVR. A PVR threshold of >2 WU alone did not discriminate survival, whereas PVR >5 WU identified a high-risk phenotype. An integrated classification combining PH status, PVR >5 WU, and RV-PA uncoupling (TAPSE/PASP <0.30 mm/mmHg) provided effective prognostic stratification.

Conclusion

High procedural success and symptomatic improvement were observed following TTVI across PH subgroups. Although infrequent among TTVI patients, a PVR >5 WU identifies a high-risk phenotype with increased mortality. Comprehensive hemodynamic profiling improves risk stratification and may support patient counselling and informed decision-making.

title: Quality of Care and Outcomes Among American Indian and Alaska Native Patients With Acute Myocardial Infarction: Cardiovascular Health Insights From the American Heart Association Get With The Guidelines Program.
authorString: Hardie L, Shultz K, Regalado S, Begay RL, Tsosie CR, George C, Tennison A, Sandman S, Fanaroff AC, Nathan A, Shin S, Khatana SAM, Deen JF, Eberly LA.
abstractText:
Background

American Indian and Alaska Native (AI/AN) patients in the US face a disproportionate burden of cardiovascular disease, yet data on the quality of care and outcomes in this population are limited. Using the American Heart Association's Get With The Guidelines-Coronary Artery Disease registry, we evaluated the clinical profiles and use of evidence-based therapies among AI/AN patients with acute myocardial infarction compared with White patients.

Methods

We analyzed data from 1955 AI/AN patients with acute myocardial infarction in 45 states participating in the Get With The Guidelines-Coronary Artery Disease program from 2017 to 2022. Six performance measures were evaluated: aspirin within 24 hours, β-blocker and statin at discharge, smoking cessation counseling, ACE (angiotensin-converting enzyme) inhibitor/ARB (angiotensin II receptor blocker) for EF ≤40%, and antiplatelet therapy at discharge. Additional metrics included door-to-balloon time ≤90 minutes for ST-segment-elevation myocardial infarction, cardiac rehabilitation referral, GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1) use for those with obesity and diabetes, and in-hospital mortality.

Results

Compared with White patients, AI/AN patients with acute myocardial infarction were younger, with a higher prevalence of diabetes, obesity, and end-stage renal disease. Overall, the utilization of evidence-based medical therapies and smoking cessation counseling was similar. However, door-to-balloon time ≤90 minutes for ST-segment-elevation myocardial infarction was significantly lower for AI/AN patients (65.5% versus 76.2%; P<0.0001). Cardiac rehabilitation referral was also significantly lower for AI/AN patients (69.1% versus 72.9%; P<0.01). Adjusted in-hospital mortality was higher for AI/AN patients (adjusted odds ratio, 1.27 [95% CI, 1.03-1.56]; P=0.02) when adjusted for patient characteristics, but differences were attenuated after adjustment for hospital characteristics (adjusted odds ratio, 1.13 [95% CI, 0.88-1.47]).

Conclusions

AI/AN patients received similar evidence-based therapies as White patients, but disparities remain in cardiac rehabilitation referral and timely reperfusion. Differences in in-hospital mortality may be attributed to the types of hospitals where AI/AN patients receive care, indicating the need for targeted interventions to improve cardiovascular outcomes in these communities.

title: Second-Line Antihypertensive Drugs and Risk of Microvascular Complications in Patients With Hypertension and Type 2 Diabetes Receiving Renin-Angiotensin System Inhibitors: A Target Trial Emulation.
authorString: Jian Q, Shao H, Scarton L, Farland MZ, Ruzieh M, Singh Ospina N, Winterstein AG, Jiao T.
abstractText:
Background

More than half of the US adults with type 2 diabetes (T2D) have hypertension. Some antihypertensive drugs, particularly thiazide(-like) diuretics (TDs) and β-blockers (BBs), are associated with hyperglycemia, yet long-term impact in patients with both conditions remains limited. We evaluated microvascular complication risk across second-line antihypertensive therapies following first-line renin-angiotensin system inhibitor use.

Methods

A retrospective cohort study using a 15% random sample of nationwide Medicare Fee-for-Service claims from 2011 to 2020 was conducted to emulate a target trial among adults aged 65 years or older with concomitant hypertension and T2D. Two 1:1 propensity score-matched comparisons were conducted: BBs versus calcium channel blockers (CCBs) and TDs versus CCBs, with matching based on demographic characteristics, index year, comorbidities, and concomitant medications. The primary outcome was a composite of diabetic nephropathy, diabetic retinopathy, and diabetic neuropathy identified by International Classification of Diseases diagnosis codes. Patients were followed until the earliest occurrence of new-onset microvascular complication and were censored at disenrollment, death, or study end. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios and 95% CIs.

Results

A total of 27 395 patients were included. In the BBs versus CCBs and TDs versus CCBs cohorts, the mean age was 76 and 75; 40.3% and 39.1% were men, and 8.6% and 11.0% were Black patients. The incidence rates of microvascular complications were 8.89 and 8.33 per 100 person-years among BB and CCB users, respectively, and 7.85 and 7.95 per 100 person-years among TD and CCB users, respectively. Compared with CCB, BB (hazard ratio, 1.07 [95% CI, 1.00-1.14]) was associated with higher risk of microvascular complications, although the risk for TDs (hazard ratio, 0.99 [95% CI, 0.93-1.05]) was nonsignificant.

Conclusions

Compared with CCBs, BBs were associated with modestly higher risk of microvascular complications, although no association was observed for TDs.

title: Perinatal Mortality and Associated Maternal, Obstetric and Health-System Factors in Southwestern Uganda: A Multicentre Cross-Sectional Study in Kabale District
authorString: Twesigomwe AP, Turanzomwe S, Bbosa G, Atwine D, Ninsiima E, Bandoga G, Okello P.
abstractText: Background Perinatal deaths remain a major challenge in Uganda, yet evidence across different levels of maternity care in southwestern Uganda is limited. We estimated facility-based perinatal mortality and examined associated maternal, obstetric and service-related characteristics in Kabale District. Methods This multicentre cross-sectional study systematically sampled 718 women delivering at nine facilities between April and June 2026. Stillbirths from 26 weeks of gestation and early neonatal deaths recorded before discharge or day seven for those still admitted constituted the composite outcome. Associations were assessed using Firth penalized logistic regression, reporting adjusted odds ratios (aORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Results Nineteen perinatal deaths were documented (26.5 per 1,000 births; 95% CI 17.0–41.0). Factors associated with death were no formal education (aOR 7.75, 95% CI 1.43–42.14), adverse obstetric history (4.60, 1.06–19.96), referral from another facility (6.77, 1.84–24.87), preterm delivery (19.69, 5.72–67.77), hypertension in pregnancy (5.80, 1.22–27.58), elective caesarean delivery (5.16, 1.07–24.97) and emergency caesarean delivery (6.98, 1.98–24.66). Conclusion Perinatal mortality was substantial in the sampled facilities. Strengthening early risk recognition, referral pathways and care for preterm newborns may be important. Operative delivery associations should not be interpreted causally. Limited post-discharge follow-up may underestimate mortality through day seven.

title: Clinical Profile and 30-Day Outcomes of Perforated Peptic Ulcer Surgery at a Tertiary Hospital in Ghana: A Prospective Cohort Study
authorString: Agbedinu K, Bilson AJ, Dally CK, Gyedu A, Brenu SG.
abstractText: Background Perforated peptic ulcer (PPU) is a common surgical emergency in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs).
