Factors contributing to post-operative morbidity and mortality have been scarcely studied in developing contexts such as Ghana. This study aimed to investigate the contributions of perioperative risk factors to morbidity and mortality after PPU surgery. Methods Between December 2018 and November 2019, 48 patients had surgery for PPU in our hospital. Data was described with descriptive statistics. Associations between outcome variables and predictor variables were examined with the Chi-square test, and regression analysis was done to determine the predictors of morbidity and mortality. Results Median age was 52 years (range 15–82), 40/48 (83.3%) were male, and 35/48 (72.9%) had gastric perforations. Overall, 30-day morbidity was 43.8%, and mortality was 12.5%. Surgical site infection was the commonest complication (18.7%), followed by pneumonia (12.5%) and intra-abdominal abscess (8.3%). On bivariable analysis, purulent peritoneal aspirate was associated with 30-day morbidity (p = 0.005), while age > 60 years (p = 0.006) and hypertension (p = 0.001) were associated with 30-day mortality. In multivariable analysis, hypertension was associated with increased likelihood of 30-day mortality (adjusted OR 8.8, 95% CI 1.1–70.4; p = 0.040). Purulent aspirate was also associated with 30-day morbidity (OR 7.3, 95% CI 1.7–31.8; p = 0.008). Conclusion PPU in this setting predominantly affected middle-aged men and was associated with substantial postoperative morbidity and mortality. Purulent intraperitoneal contamination was associated with increased odds of postoperative complications, while hypertension was associated with 30-day mortality. Early presentation, aggressive resuscitation, and closer perioperative monitoring of high-risk patients are essential.

title: Relationship between the albumin–corrected anion gap and prognosis among patients with intra-abdominal hypertension: a retrospective study from MIMIC-IV database
authorString: Guo J, Wang J, Zhang X, Xia L, Feng Q, Wu F, Zhuang J, Zhu M.
abstractText: Intra-abdominal hypertension (IAH) is common in ICU patients and associated with high mortality, but reliable prognostic markers remain lacking. This study aims to assess the prognostic value of albumin-corrected anion gap (ACAG) for 7-day all-cause mortality in ICU patients with IAH. A cohort of 617 adult ICU patients with IAH was analyzed, with ACAG levels being assessed as a predictor of 7-day mortality. Higher 7-day mortality was observed in patients with elevated ACAG, with ACAG identified as an independent risk factor for 7-day mortality (HR = 2.043, P < 0.05). ACAG demonstrated good predictive performance (AUC = 0.731), outperforming ALB and showing comparable efficacy to SOFA and AG. Subgroup analysis revealed that lower ACAG values were protective, and the interaction between ACAG and age was significant (P for interaction = 0.032), with a more pronounced prognostic value of ACAG in patients younger than 65 years. Our findings suggest that ACAG is a useful prognostic marker for 7-day mortality in IAH patients, with particular utility in younger populations.

title: Closing the Loop on Automated Feature Engineering: A Heart-Failure Pilot
authorString: Awan T, Hu M, Singh S, Zonooz P, Kumar N, Kachroo P.
abstractText: Heart-failure risk models draw on variables scattered across diagnoses, medications, laboratory results and procedures. The features built from these records are made by hand for each dataset, with no record of the evidence behind them. We evaluate the Nimblemind Multi-Agent System (nMAS), whose recursive self-improvement (RSI) loop proposes features and model weights from published knowledge. Each predictor mined from the heart-failure literature is built as a feature and kept only if it improves a fixed model on the hospital's own patients. The loop was applied to a synthetic cohort of 10,000 records, 31,427 MIMIC-IV patients and 26,168 patients of a United States health system, predicting death within 365 days of a first heart-failure diagnosis. Across four experiments, five iterations of the loop raised holdout AUROC by +0.008 to +0.047 over cleaned baselines. The accepted features were markers that cardiologists generally use, among them estimated glomerular filtration rate, natriuretic peptides, and iron and liver tests. Each accepted feature carries the published sentence, direction and cutoff it was built from, so a clinician can check the feature before it enters a model used for risk stratification, targeting of guideline-directed therapy or timing of referral for advanced therapies. Run inside the health system with no record leaving the institution, the loop raised holdout AUROC from 0.708 to 0.755, and better ranking of patients by risk supports each of these uses.

title: Diverging mortality trajectories of tobacco-documented pulmonary hypertension, COPD, and lung cancer in the United States, 2018-2024.
authorString: Abbas S, Saeed A, Sulaiman S, Al-Sharif Z, Alattal O, Fadell F.
abstractText:
Background

Pulmonary hypertension (PH) mortality may not have followed recent improvements in tobacco-related diseases. We compared PH mortality with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and lung cancer and assessed whether divergence was specific to deaths with documented tobacco use.

Research design and methods

We analyzed Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) WONDER mortality data for US residents aged ≥ 25 years. PH required I27.0 or I27.2 as the underlying cause; COPD and lung cancer formed the benchmark. Age-adjusted mortality-rate ratios for 2018-2024 were modeled using inverse-variance weighting, restricted maximum likelihood, and Knapp-Hartung inference. A post hoc analysis removed the tobacco-documentation requirement.

Results

Among tobacco-documented deaths, PH mortality showed no clear linear change (annual percent change, 0.50%; 95% confidence interval (CI), -1.55% to 2.59%), whereas benchmark mortality declined (-4.83%; 95% CI, -5.51% to -4.15%). The PH-to-benchmark rate ratio increased 5.59% annually (ratio of annual rate ratios, 1.056; 95% CI, 1.035-1.078; p = 0.001). The unrestricted estimate was nearly identical (1.056; 95% CI, 1.032-1.080).

Conclusions

Recent PH mortality diverged from improving COPD and lung-cancer mortality. Because the unrestricted comparison yielded a nearly identical estimate, the divergence cannot be considered tobacco-specific. Death certificates cannot establish smoking exposure, PH phenotype, or causality.

title: A B-cell-cardiac autoantibody-complement axis contributes to myocarditis induced by checkpoint blockade and cardiac irradiation
authorString: Tran DN, Yu S, Nguyen LTK, Lu B.
abstractText: Thoracic radiotherapy and immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) improve outcomes in locally advanced lung cancer but can cause cardiac toxicity. The mechanisms by which radiation-associated cardiac injury develops into autoimmune myocarditis during ICI therapy remain incompletely defined. Using autoimmune-prone A/J mice, we investigated whether cardiac irradiation (CIR) promotes a B-cell-cardiac autoantibody-complement axis during dual PD-1 and CTLA-4 blockade. Dual ICIs plus CIR increased the incidence of myocarditis to 76.2% and cardiac fibrosis to 69.0%. CIR did not further increase global splenic B-cell activation beyond dual ICIs alone but increased cardiac troponin I-reactive B cells and IgG, circulating cardiac autoantibodies (cAAbs), myocardial IgG accumulation, and C3/C3a activation. In mice subsequently found to have grade 3-4 myocarditis on day 21, cAAbs increased by day 7 and continued to rise, preceding histologic identification of severe disease. Cobra venom factor-mediated C3 depletion reduced myocarditis incidence from 90% to 40% and fibrosis from 85% to 35%, while also decreasing B-cell activation and circulating cAAbs. In a separate LLC-OVA tumor model, C3 depletion did not produce an evident loss of the antitumor activity of combined ICIs and radiation under the conditions tested. These findings support a model in which CIR focuses ICI-associated humoral immunity toward cardiac antigens and complement amplifies cardiac injury. The early cAAb rise and protection achieved by C3 depletion provide a rationale for prospective evaluation of cAAbs as a risk marker and complement signaling as a therapeutic target.

title: Correlative mapping links extracellular matrix architecture to local mechanics in cardiac aging
authorString: Ramli MFH, Ghosh A, Hengst RM, Sun AR, Ong HT, Lou Y, Ong HT, Shagirov M, Shen X, Nicholas K, Grenci G, Hiraiwa T, Young JL.
abstractText: Cardiac aging is accompanied by extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling, but how changes in matrix architecture relate to local tissue mechanics remains poorly understood. Here, we quantified six image-derived architectural descriptors across selected ECM components in young and aged murine myocardium and integrated them into an architectural index that we term 'ArchI'. Age-associated architectural changes differed among ECM components, with higher ArchI values observed for fibrillar collagen, fibronectin, and laminin-associated networks. To examine how defined structural changes affect the component descriptors, we developed controlled synthetic geometries and a stochastic network model. These analyses revealed index sensitivity to matrix occupancy, fiber width, and network continuity. We then combined nanoindentation of fresh cardiac tissue slices with subsequent immunofluorescence staining and imaging of collagen to correlate local tissue stiffness with ECM architecture in corresponding regions. Aged myocardium exhibited higher ArchI and Young's modulus, with local heterogeneity in their spatial correspondence. Age-adjusted regression revealed a positive association between ArchI and Young's modulus, with a steeper association in aged myocardium. Together, these findings reveal component-specific ECM remodeling during aging and provide a means to examine spatial structure-mechanics relationships in the aging heart.

title: Left ventricular systolic dysfunction in long-term aficamten therapy for obstructive HCM is rare, transient, and well-tolerated
authorString: Massera D, Owens AT, Abraham TP, Barriales-Villa R, Cooper RM, Elliott PM, Maron MS, Nassif ME, Oreziak A, Saberi S, Solomon SD, Tower-Rader A, Godown J, Heitner SB, Jacoby DL, Kupfer S, Liu X, Malik FI, Sohn R, Wei J, Masri A.
abstractText:
Aims:

: Aficamten, a novel cardiac myosin inhibitor recently approved in several regions for adults with symptomatic obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (oHCM), requires structured echocardiographic monitoring to assess for left ventricular (LV) systolic dysfunction (LVSD). We aimed to describe the incidence, severity, trajectory, and clinical correlates of LVSD during aficamten therapy in patients enrolled in FOREST-HCM.

Methods:

Serial echocardiographic examinations were performed to inform investigator-driven dose adjustments and safety monitoring. Patients were categorized by on-treatment LV ejection fraction (LVEF): any incidence of LVSD (<50%) or no LVSD (always >/=50%). A prespecified subgroup analysis evaluated patients with any LVEF >/=50% to <55%.

Results:

Among 410 patients (mean [SD] age 60.2 [12.8] years, 43.7% female), 12 (2.9%; exposure adjusted incidence rate [EAIR] 2.1/100 patient-years) developed LVSD (none with LVEF <40%); only one event was corroborated by the core laboratory. LVEF recovered to >/=50% in 10 (83.3%) patients after dose reduction and in one after transient interruption. One patient had persistent LVSD, having also experienced LVSD while receiving placebo in the parent study. Concurrent non-serious clinical heart failure occurred in two patients (0.5%; EAIR 0.3/100 patient-years), resolving in one, while the other (with prior LVSD on placebo) permanently discontinued aficamten. Additionally, 47 patients (11.5%; EAIR 8.8/100 patient-years) demonstrated LVEF >/=50% to <55% and remained on aficamten without dose reduction or associated adverse events.

Conclusion:

LVSD was infrequent, mild, reversible, and rarely associated with transient non-serious heart failure symptoms. LVEF >/=50% to <55% appeared clinically benign, supporting structured echocardiographic monitoring and individualized dose optimization.

title: APOE isoforms shape brain network organization and its coupling with cardiac phenotypes in mice
authorString: Badea A, Shahu K, Nadkarni R, Stout JA, Moon H, Mahzarnia A, Han ZY, Tremblay J, Anderson RJ, Foster M, Lutz MW, Laskowitz DT, Badea CT.
abstractText:
Background:

Apolipoprotein E (APOE) isoforms influence Alzheimer's disease susceptibility and cardiovascular physiology, but their roles in functional brain network organization and brain-heart relationships remain incompletely understood. We investigated whether APOE genotype modifies functional brain networks and their cardiovascular, behavioral, and molecular correlates.

Methods:

Resting-state functional MRI was analyzed in 261 mice expressing human APOE2, APOE3, or APOE4, with 31 Apoe-knockout mice as additional comparators. Cardiac computed tomography, regional brain volume, intrinsic T1, cerebral blood flow (CBF), spatial-navigation behavior, and regional transcriptomics were evaluated in partially overlapping or independent cohorts. Covariate-adjusted analyses assessed network topology, regional connectivity, and APOE-dependent brain-cardiac associations, with false-discovery-rate correction within designated testing families.

Results:

Compared with APOE2, APOE4 mice exhibited lower positive functional connectivity strength (beta = -0.542, q = 0.0036), clustering (beta = -0.488, q = 0.0041), and modularity (beta = -0.375, q = 0.0252), together with higher global efficiency and altered persistent topology. Positive regional connectivity was lower in 15 cortical regions within the designated 244-region testing family, with left cingulate area 24b also surviving correction across all 1,464 regional tests (q = 0.0394). Among 108 mice with paired cardiac CT and functional MRI, APOE modified the association between left atrial volume and negative-network beta0 persistence (interaction p = 0.00386; q = 0.0463 across 12 persistence tests), predominantly reflecting a negative association in APOE3 mice; this interaction did not survive correction across all 28 global tests. Complementary regional MRI analyses identified genotype-dependent cardiac associations involving brain volume, intrinsic T1, and CBF, including three anatomically matched T1-CBF associations in limbic-related and pontine regions. APOE4 mice exhibited higher absolute winding number during spatial navigation and lower delayed spatial-memory probe occupancy. Cardiac ejection fraction was associated with acquisition trajectories in a smaller paired cohort. Independent cingulate transcriptomics identified APOE-associated lipid/cholesterol and inhibitory-neuron marker signatures (q < 0.05).

Conclusions:

APOE isoforms are associated with distinct functional brain network architectures and genotype-dependent relationships between cerebral and cardiac phenotypes. Convergence across functional connectivity, regional MRI, behavior, and independent molecular measurements implicates distributed cortical and limbic-related systems, including the cingulate cortex. These findings identify candidate imaging phenotypes for investigating APOE-sensitive brain-heart relationships, without establishing their causal direction or underlying mechanisms.

title: Cardiac-confidence coupling is modulated by sensory but not higher-order uncertainty
authorString: Hoogervorst K, Banellis L, Everaerts S, Bavato F, Tyrer A, Allen M.
abstractText: Confidence, the subjective sense of certainty accompanying decisions, may be shaped by more than the sensory evidence on which the decision itself was based. Cardiac signals have been linked to confidence, with some evidence that this coupling strengthens when sensory evidence is unreliable. However, sensory evidence can be unreliable in different ways: if sensory input is degraded, predictive cues are misleading, or the environment is too volatile for stable expectations to form. These are distinct computational problems, and whether cardiac-confidence coupling is engaged under all of them has not yet been tested. Similarly, whether this coupling predicts individual differences in metacognitive efficiency remains unknown. To address this, we recorded cardiac activity from 167 participants performing a face-emotion discrimination task that orthogonally manipulated sensory precision, cue validity, and block volatility, with trial-wise confidence ratings. Pre-decisional heart rate deceleration was more pronounced under low than high sensory precision. Within this window, trial-level heart rate positively predicted confidence, independently of accuracy and precision. This cardiac-confidence coupling was stronger when sensory precision was low, but cue validity and block volatility did not modulate the coupling. Neither individual resting heart rate variability nor coupling strength predicted metacognitive efficiency. Together, these findings indicate that cardiac-confidence coupling is modulated by sensory uncertainty but not by higher-order uncertainty, consistent with a within-trial interoceptive weighting mechanism rather than a stable individual-differences trait.

title: Multi-omic cardiac adaptation to exercise training identifies adaptive and disease-opposing signatures: findings from MoTrPAC
authorString: Brochet P, MoTrPAC, Many GM, Lindholm ME, Smith GR, Gladkikh S, Keshishian H, Kim DS, Jimenez-Morales DDJ, Montalvo S, Njoroge JN, Bodine SC, Ashley EA, Kraus WE, Walsh MJ, Wheeler MT, Katz DH.
abstractText:
Background: Endurance exercise reduces cardiovascular disease risk, but how this protection is mediated at the molecular level remains incompletely understood.

Methods:

Using multi-omic data from MoTrPAC, we integrated 13,790 selected molecular features across eight cardiac omic layers from 50 female and male rats undergoing 1-8 weeks of endurance training, as well as sedentary controls. Multi-omic temporal programs were defined using MOFA/MEFISTO and compared to physiological adaptation, human cardiac disease signatures, causal cardiomyopathy genes, and cross-tissue responses.

Results:

Seven temporal programs of coordinated molecular responses were identified across cardiac omic layers. Transient metabolic responses showed sex-dependent timing and generally preceded sustained structural changes with limited correspondence to skeletal muscle, while complement proteins declined with training. Among these, a sustained program was associated with improvement of VO 2 max and accounted for 38 of 50 significant overlaps with human cardiac disease signatures, frequently with opposing molecular responses, including reduced Fn1 and increased Klhl40 transcript and protein abundance by 8 weeks. To provide mechanistic context, we examined 112 genes causally linked to inherited cardiac disease, finding significant training-associated changes in 72 genes at the transcript level and 57 at the protein level. Notably, FLNC, BAG3, and PKP2 protein abundance increased, contrasting with reduced-dosage mechanisms in their respective cardiomyopathies. Conversely, disease-aligned and disease-opposing chaperone responses suggested coordinated protein quality-control mechanisms that may contribute to exercise-mediated cardioprotection.

Conclusions:

Endurance training induces coordinated, time-dependent molecular responses across cardiac pathways implicated in human disease, including both disease-opposing changes in known causal genes and disease-concordant stress responses.

title: Prevalence of Cardiovascular Risk Factors and Factors Associated With Hypertension Among Adults in the Municipality of Ngozi (Burundi): A Cross- Sectional Study, 2026
authorString: Mick N, Savadogo LB, Théodore N, Florence M, Hermenegilde N, Loic N.
abstractText: Background A shortage of data on cardiovascular risk factors is observed in Burundi. An analytical cross-sectional study was conducted in May 2026 among households in the commune of Ngozi, with the aim of determining the prevalence of cardiovascular risk factors and identifying the factors associated with high blood pressure. Results A total of 415 participants aged 18 years and over were included in the study. The mean age was 43.4±16.0 and the sex ratio was 0.64. Cardiovascular risk behaviours and their prevalence were, respectively: daily smoking 8.43% (6.1; 11.5), consumption of more than two glasses of alcohol per day 30.84% (26.57; 35.47); insufficient physical activity 16.14% (12.90; 20.01), adding salt to every meal 10.12% (7.5; 13.4), frequent consumption of high-salt foods 4.33% (2.7; 6.7), consumption of at least one sugary drink per day 44.33% (39.61; 49.16), inadequate fruit intake 96.3% (94; 97.8), inadequate vegetable intake 97.9% (92.3; 98.2), the use of firewood 63.37%(58.6; 67.8)) and coal 36.14% (36.1; 40.89)) as cooking fuel, and cooking taking place inside the home 70.6 %(66,22;74,98). The metabolic risk factors and their prevalence were fasting hyperglycaemia 5.3%(3.5; 7.9), high blood pressure 18.55% (15.09; 22.60) and obesity 8.67 per cent (6.31; 11.8). In the multivariate analysis, the factors associated with high blood pressure identified were age (61 years and over adjusted OR 8.25 (3.05; 22.28); 46–60 years adjusted OR 5.11 (1.97; 13.26); 31–45 years adjusted OR 2.89 (1.09; 7.67)); alcohol consumption of more than two units of alcohol adjusted OR 1.87 (1.15; 3.27), obesity adjusted OR 2.8 (1.2; 6.51), being overweight: 2.21 (1.15; 4.26), frequent consumption of high-salt foods: 3.09 (1.03; 9.27). Conclusion The prevalence of behavioural and metabolic cardiovascular risk factors is quite high in the municipality of Ngozi. This study highlights the need to promote cardiovascular risk prevention initiatives in this municipality.

title: Baseline and Dynamic IL-10/IL-2R as Predictors of IVIG Resistance in Kawasaki Disease: A Comparative Study
authorString: Xie Q, Zhang L, Jiao X, Wang H.
abstractText: Objectives Intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) resistance in Kawasaki disease (KD) increases coronary artery lesion risk and necessitates early identification. This study compared the predictive efficacy of baseline serum interleukin-10 (IL-10) combined with interleukin-2 receptor (IL-2R), their dynamic post-treatment changes, and the traditional Kobayashi score for predicting IVIG resistance. Methods This retrospective cohort study enrolled 457 KD patients (November 2019–December 2025). Patients were categorized into IVIG-responsive and IVIG-resistant groups. Pre-treatment IL-10 and IL-2R levels and their 24-hour post-IVIG dynamic changes were measured. Multivariate logistic regression identified independent predictors. ROC curves and Bootstrap resampling (500 times) evaluated predictive performance of three models: pre-treatment IL-10 + IL-2R, dynamic changes, and Kobayashi score. Results Among 457 patients, 73 (15.97%) were IVIG-resistant. Resistant patients had significantly higher pre-treatment IL-10 (37.80 vs. 11.70 pg/mL) and IL-2R (298.20 vs. 159.65 ×10 U/mL), and greater post-treatment declines (both P < 0.001). Multivariate analysis confirmed pre-treatment IL-10 (OR 1.012) and IL-2R (OR 1.007), and their dynamic changes, as independent predictors. The pre-treatment IL-10 + IL-2R model showed excellent discrimination (AUC 0.842), significantly outperforming the Kobayashi score (AUC 0.635, P < 0.001). The dynamic change model performed comparably (AUC 0.832). Bootstrap validation confirmed robustness. Conclusion Both baseline IL-10 + IL-2R and their dynamic changes demonstrate superior predictive value for IVIG resistance compared to the Kobayashi score, supporting integration of cytokine profiling into clinical practice for early risk stratification and personalized treatment in KD.

title: Ferric carboxymaltose has a higher distribution into myocardium than gadobutrol assessed by quantitative T1 mapping in healthy volunteers
authorString: Abdula G, Lundin M, Nickander J, Sörensson P, Sigfridsson A, Themudo R, Ugander M.
abstractText: Ferric carboxymaltose (FCM) improves symptoms, functional capacity and clinical outcomes in patients with heart failure, regardless of ejection fraction or anemia status. We aimed to evaluate and quantify the dynamic tissue distribution of FCM using cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR). This prospective, single-center study was part of the Iron-CMR trial (EudraCT: 2014-002455-26). T1 mapping was performed both pre- and post-contrast to assess relative changes in T1 and the partition coefficient (λ) in myocardium, liver, spleen and skeletal muscle up to 60 minutes after onset of a 15-minute infusion of 20 ml (50 mg iron/ml) FCM in healthy male volunteers. Myocardial λ was compared with that of gadobutrol (0.2 mmol/kg) in an age-matched cohort. Groups were compared using Mann-Whitney U test. Twenty-five healthy males (age 27 ± 3 years) underwent CMR with intravenous FCM (n = 8) or gadobutrol (n = 17). T1 decreased in the myocardium, blood, liver, spleen and skeletal muscle following FCM infusion ( p  < 0.001 for all). FCM λ remained relatively constant in the myocardium and spleen (65 ± 2% and 81 ± 20%, respectively, at 30 minutes), whereas λ increased in the liver and skeletal muscle. Myocardial λ was significantly higher for FCM than gadobutrol (65 ± 2vs 42 ± 1%, p  < 0.0001). CMR T1 mapping enables detection and quantification of the dynamic tissue distribution of FCM in the myocardium, liver, spleen, and skeletal muscle. The higher myocardial λ for FCM compared with gadobutrol suggests greater myocardial distribution than extracellular contrast agents, most likely due to additional distribution into the intracellular space.

title: Subclinical Right Ventricular Dysfunction and Left Atrial Remodeling Across Obstructive Sleep Apnea Severities: A Cross-Sectional Speckle-Tracking Echocardiographic Study
authorString: Kermanshahi¹ TZ, Farahani ZD, Masoud S, Ali¹ N, Abtahi SM, Dayani A, Namazi M.
abstractText:
Background and Objectives: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is strongly linked to cardiovascular morbidity, yet the extent of subclinical right heart remodeling and left atrial enlargement across disease severities remains inadequately characterized. This study aimed to evaluate cardiometabolic characteristics, conventional echocardiographic parameters, and right ventricular (RV) myocardial mechanics using two-dimensional speckle-tracking echocardiography (2D-STE) in patients with severe versus mild-to-moderate OSA.

Methods:

This single-center, cross-sectional observational study enrolled 173 consecutive adult patients (aged ≥ 18 years) evaluated at a tertiary cardiovascular referral center between January 2023 and January 2025. All participants underwent overnight in-laboratory polysomnography (PSG) and comprehensive transthoracic echocardiography within a 4-week interval. Patients were stratified into mild-to-moderate OSA (5.0 ≤ AHI < 30.0 events/h; n = 87) and severe OSA (AHI ≥ 30.0 events/h; n = 86) groups. Multivariable binary logistic and linear regression analyses were performed to identify independent determinants of severe disease and myocardial impairment. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis evaluated the diagnostic discriminative value of echocardiographic parameters.

Results:

Patients with severe OSA were significantly older (53.4 ± 11.2 vs. 47.1 ± 12.8 years, P = 0.001), had a higher body mass index (34.8 ± 4.2 vs. 30.9 ± 3.9 kg/m², P < 0.001), and exhibited a higher male predominance (72.1% vs. 49.4%, P = 0.002) compared to those with mild-to-moderate OSA. Severe OSA was associated with a significantly elevated comorbidity burden, including a higher prevalence of prior cerebrovascular accidents (24.4% vs. 9.2%, P = 0.007). Echocardiographically, patients in the severe group demonstrated marked subclinical myocardial impairment, characterized by significantly reduced RV free-wall longitudinal strain (RV-FWLS: 19 ± 7% vs. 25 ± 4%, P ˂ 0.001) and impaired conventional systolic parameters. Multivariable linear regression identified continuous apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) as an independent predictor of impaired RV-FWLS (B = -0.067, P < 0.001) and elevated pulmonary artery systolic pressure (B = + 0.077, P = 0.007). Furthermore, ROC analysis revealed that left atrial volume index (LAVI) possessed superior diagnostic accuracy for identifying severe OSA (AUC = 0.931, P < 0.0001) compared to RV-FWLS and conventional hemodynamics.

Conclusion:

Severe OSA is independently associated with pronounced subclinical right ventricular longitudinal strain impairment and left atrial remodeling. Two-dimensional speckle-tracking echocardiography and LAVI provide robust diagnostic utility for identifying high-risk patients, emphasizing the critical need for early cardiovascular screening and aggressive management in severe sleep apnea populations.

title: Transient-Based HRV Analysis Reveals Changes in Cardiac Autonomic Dynamics during Repeated Cognitive Engagement
authorString: CHAGNEAUD R, ARSAC LM, BOUGARD C, DIAZ E, DESCHODT-ARSAC V.
abstractText: Transitions from rest to cognitive engagement are common in daily life, particularly among human operators. Repeated cognitive demands may induce adaptation or mental fatigue. Heart rate variability (HRV), a marker of cardiac autonomic regulation, may help characterize these responses. We hypothesized that transient HRV dynamics during rest-to-task transitions would reveal physiological adjustments not captured by conventional steady-state measures. HRV was recorded in 29 healthy young adults during two successive rest-to-task transitions involving visual search and go/no-go tasks. Perceived fatigue, stress, and anxiety were assessed. Conventional HRV indices and entropy were calculated during resting and cognitive phases, while transient low-frequency (LF) and high-frequency (HF) dynamics were characterized during the first minute following each transition using wavelet packet transform analysis. Response times improved during the second cognitive task despite increased perceived fatigue, accompanied by greater cardiac vagal modulation and preserved HRV entropy. Transient HF and LF dynamics differed significantly between transitions. Moreover, transient slope-based indices showed higher discriminative performance (AUC = 0.65–0.70) than conventional steady-state reactivity indices (AUC = 0.47–0.59). These findings suggest that transient HRV analysis provides complementary information on cardiac autonomic responses to repeated cognitive engagement, with potential applications for monitoring human operators.

title: Tumor-Induced Systemic Immune Modulation Protects Against Experimental Colitis
authorString: Awwad L, Livneh I, Aronheim A.
abstractText: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is characterized by chronic, relapsing intestinal inflammation driven by dysregulated immune responses and impaired epithelial homeostasis. Although chronic inflammation is a recognized driver of tumorigenesis, whether established tumors can reciprocally modulate intestinal inflammation remains largely unexplored. Here, we investigated the systemic effects of peripheral tumor growth and tumor microenvironment on experimental colitis. Using dextran sodium sulfate (DSS)-induced colitis in tumor mice bearing, we found that tumor-bearing mice developed significantly milder disease, with reduced Disease Activity Index scores, decreased colonic expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines, and preserved intestinal architecture. Administration of serum from tumor-bearing mice reproduced this protective phenotype, indicating that circulating tumor-induced factors are sufficient to attenuate intestinal inflammation. We next examined TNF-α and IFN-γ, previously identified as mediators of tumor-induced cardioprotection effects and cardiac remodeling. Remarkably, a single administration of recombinant TNF-α and IFN-γ before DSS exposure significantly reduced clinical disease severity and histopathological damage. Protection persisted following a second DSS challenge, demonstrating sustained effects beyond the initial inflammatory episode. Cytokine treatment was also associated with increased colonic expression of anti-inflammatory and reparative macrophage-associated markers, including IL-13 and CD206, together with reduced expression of iNOS. Collectively, our findings reveal an unexpected systemic interaction between cancer and intestinal inflammation, whereby the tumor microenvironment generates circulating signals that suppress experimental colitis. TNF-α and IFN-γ recapitulate this protective response, potentially by immunomodulation of macrophages toward anti-inflammatory resolution and tissue repair.

title: Echocardiography Pathway Improvement to Increase Capacity (EPIIC): A National Scoping Survey of Scientist-Led Echocardiography Clinics in the UK
authorString: Samad NHA, Bassindale G, King E, Demetrescu C, Jowsey F, Sopala J, Ring L, Robinson S, Gamlin W, Augustine D, Bennett S, Paton MF.
abstractText: Background Increasing demand for echocardiography in the United Kingdom (UK), alongside persistent workforce shortages, contribute to diagnostic delays. Scientist-led echocardiography clinics integrating imaging and clinical assessment in a single visit, may improve service efficiency and patient experience. However, the national extent of adoption is poorly characterised, and standardised guidance, competency frameworks and accreditation pathways are lacking. Methods A national cross-sectional online survey, the Echocardiography Pathway Improvement to Increase Capacity (EPIIC), was distributed electronically via British Society of Echocardiography (BSE) communication channels between 1 October 2025 and 15 January 2026. The survey evaluated six domains: demographics, service provision, clinic processes, perceived benefits and challenges, patient feedback and outcomes, and requirements for establishing scientist-led echocardiography clinics. Quantitative data were analysed descriptively to characterise current practice, while free-text responses underwent thematic categorisation. Results A total of 194 respondents completed the survey. Most identified as cardiac physiologists (67%) or clinical scientists (25%), with responses from all UK regions. An established scientist-led clinic was reported by 63% of respondents, with a further 13% reporting a service in pilot phase. Valve disease (81%) and heart failure (20%) were the most common indications. Clinics most frequently saw 0–10 patients per week (48%), with 60-minute appointments (56%). Internal cardiology referrals accounted for 89%. Echocardiography was included in 88% of protocols. Consultant cardiologist support was available in 72%, and structured escalation pathways were reported in 48%. Perceived benefits were strongly endorsed (> 80% agreement) across domains including patient access, waiting times, efficiency, patient experience and staff retention. Key challenges included funding (56%), staffing shortages (51%), accreditation gaps (34%), and limited consultant support (33%). Only 43% of respondents reported routinely collected formal or informal patient feedback, although free-text responses indicate largely positive feedback. Conclusion Scientist-led echocardiography clinics were reported across UK regions and healthcare settings but have developed with substantial variation in governance, competency standards, accreditation and outcome measurement. National and cross-specialty standardisation of scientist-led echocardiography clinics is required, with a purposeful prospective evaluation to determine whether actual clinical, patient and workforce benefits can be delivered consistently and sustainably.

title: Waveform-Free Characterization of Intraoperative Cardiac Arrhythmia: Beat-Timing Signatures, Reproducible Burden Phenotypes, and Cross-Surgical-Context Generalization in an Anesthesiologist- Validated Cohort
authorString: KARA MR.
abstractText: Cardiac arrhythmia during surgery can demand immediate recognition, yet almost every publicly available electrocardiographic resource is drawn from ambulatory or intensive care recordings rather than the operating room. The first large anesthesiologist-validated intraoperative database therefore invites the reflexive response of training yet another waveform-morphology classifier. This study asks a more economical question: how far can intraoperative arrhythmia be characterized without the raw waveform, from expert beat annotations and routine perioperative metadata alone? Across 482 surgical cases and more than 660,000 validated beats, features built from R-peak times and beat-type labels separated five clinically grouped rhythm classes with a balanced accuracy of 0.869. A transparent linear model matched a higher-capacity random forest, indicating that the signal reflects genuine structure rather than model complexity, and it remained accurate on windows the experts flagged as artifact, where morphology-based methods are most vulnerable. The same features resolved three reproducible arrhythmia-burden phenotypes and transferred between surgical departments; older age was the principal adjusted correlate of high burden. Resolving the ectopy classes still relied on the expert beat-type labels rather than interval timing alone. Beat annotations and metadata thus offer a low-cost, interpretable, and transferable baseline for a setting that previously lacked one.

title: A multi-corpus benchmark reveals limits of diagnostic preservation in heart-sound denoising
authorString: Wazed E, Shin C, Jeong H.
abstractText: Heart-sound denoisers are often judged by reconstruction fidelity under artificial noise, leaving diagnostic preservation after transfer insufficiently characterised. We built a multi-corpus benchmark rather than proposing a new architecture. Criterion-based panel construction defined an executable panel of ten learned denoisers trained on a common source corpus, four classical filters and an identity control. We evaluated five 300-recording arms from four phonocardiogram corpora (1,333 unique recordings). Paired comparisons covered 18 artificial-corruption conditions and their no-added-noise passthroughs in three arms, plus two original-recording arms without paired clean references, using four fixed classifiers. Uncertainty used patient clustering where identifiers were available, recording clustering otherwise, and a parent-recording sensitivity analysis for PaHS. Mean AUROC change was +0.014 on the denoiser-development corpus but -0.085 and -0.081 on two external corpora. On external no-added-noise inputs, some learned denoisers reduced AUROC by up to 0.380 and attenuated approximately 91\% of magnitude within detected cardiac-event regions on BMD-HS. On original BMD-HS recordings, the largest AUROC reduction was 0.387, with a 0.767 sensitivity loss at the pre-denoising threshold. Development-distribution benefit therefore did not establish diagnostic preservation after transfer. Target-corpus task effects, no-added-noise behaviour and fixed operating points should be evaluated before integration into a diagnostic pipeline.

title: Life's Essential 8 and Type D Personality Predict Coronary Plaque Instability: An Interpretable Machine-Learning Study
authorString: Zhao X, Ma X, Yu X, Zhou C, Zhao Z, Liu G, Liang X, Yu A, Yu B, Gao X.
abstractText: Background Plaque instability underlies acute coronary events, and early recognition of high-risk patients is central to secondary prevention. Current assessment relies mainly on conventional clinical indices and does not integrate modifiable health behaviours or psychological traits. We therefore developed and validated an interpretable machine-learning model combining the Life's Essential 8 (LE8) cardiovascular health metrics with Type D personality to identify coronary plaque instability. Methods In this retrospective observational cohort study, 1,436 patients with angiographically confirmed coronary artery disease who underwent optical coherence tomography (OCT) at a single tertiary centre between September 2022 and September 2025 were consecutively enrolled. The 1,061 patients admitted up to 31 August 2024 formed the development cohort and were randomly divided 7:3 into training and internal validation sets; the 375 patients admitted thereafter formed the temporal validation set. Candidate predictors spanned demographic, clinical, behavioural and psychological domains. Variables were selected using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression, and six algorithms, including extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), were compared by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration curves and decision curve analysis, with Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) used for model interpretation. Results Ten predictors were retained, eight of them behavioural or psychological: six LE8 components (nicotine exposure, sleep health, blood lipid, blood pressure, healthy diet and physical activity) and two Type D dimensions (social inhibition and negative affectivity). XGBoost achieved AUCs of 0.915, 0.905 and 0.840 in the training, internal validation and temporal validation sets, respectively, with calibration curves close to the ideal line and net benefit above both reference strategies at threshold probabilities of 0.20–0.50. Nicotine exposure, sleep health, social inhibition, blood lipid and negative affectivity ranked highest in importance. The final model was deployed as a web-based calculator for individual risk estimation. Conclusions Modifiable cardiovascular health behaviours, particularly nicotine exposure and sleep health, together with psychological traits, were the dominant information sources for identifying plaque instability. A model built on these dimensions requires only questionnaires, medical history and routine laboratory tests, and provides concrete behavioural targets for early screening and secondary prevention.

title: Nobiletin-Loaded Chitosan Nanoparticles Attenuate Doxorubicin-Induced Cardiotoxicity Through Modulation of Nrf2/HO-1, NF-κB, Mitochondrial Dysfunction, Apoptosis, and Ferroptosis
authorString: Elmorsy EM, Farag AA, Mokhtar MM, Elgendy E, Mousa HR, Kharboush TG, Habotta OA, Rocic P.
abstractText: Doxorubicin (DOX)-induced cardiotoxicity involves interconnected oxidative, inflammatory, mitochondrial, apoptotic, and ferroptosis-related mechanisms. Nobiletin (NOB), a citrus-derived polymethoxyflavone, exhibits antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, but its therapeutic application may be constrained by unfavorable physicochemical and pharmacokinetic properties. This study investigated whether chitosan nanoencapsulation enhances NOB-mediated cardioprotection and explored the involvement of Nrf2, NF-κB, mitochondrial, and ferroptosis-related pathways. Eighty male Wistar rats were allocated to eight groups: control, chitosan, NOB, NOB-loaded chitosan nanoparticles (NOB-CHNPs), DOX, DOX + chitosan, DOX + NOB, and DOX + NOB-CHNPs. NOB and NOB-CHNPs were administered orally at 20 mg/kg/day for four weeks, while DOX was administered intraperitoneally at a cumulative dose of 15 mg/kg during the final two weeks. DOX induced cardiac injury accompanied by oxidative stress, NF-κB-associated inflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, apoptosis, and ferroptosis-related alterations, including dysregulation of Nrf2/HO-1, SIRT1/PGC-1α, and ACSL4/GPX4/SLC7A11 signaling. NOB attenuated these alterations, while NOB-CHNPs generally produced greater effects and better preserved myocardial histology and mitochondrial ultrastructure. Complementary cardiomyocyte experiments using ML385, BAY 11-7082, ferrostatin-1 (Fer-1), and RSL3 provided pharmacological evidence supporting the involvement of Nrf2, NF-κB, and ferroptosis-related mechanisms. ML385 attenuated NOB-CHNP-mediated protection, whereas Fer-1 reproduced key protective responses. NOB-CHNPs reduced DOX-induced C11-BODIPY oxidation from 48.0% to 9.83% (p < 0.0001), while RSL3 partially reversed this effect (36.0%; p < 0.0001 vs. NOB-CHNPs). Collectively, NOB-CHNPs provided greater cardioprotection than free NOB against DOX-induced cardiac injury, with pharmacological intervention supporting contributions from Nrf2-dependent antioxidant defense, NF-κB-associated inflammation, mitochondrial homeostasis, and GPX4-related ferroptosis regulation.

title: M2-US: A Large-scale Multi-domain and Multi-task Ultrasound Image Dataset
authorString: WANG F, Akumu T, Dang VN, Jiménez-Sánchez A, Yang J, Silvestre G, Lekadir K, Bai J, Curran KM.
abstractText: Ultrasound imaging is widely used across clinical specialties. Artificial Intelligence methods have shown remarkable advantages in ultrasound image analysis in recent decades. However, the development of generalizable Artificial Intelligence methods remains limited by the heterogeneity of ultrasound data and the task-specific design of most existing datasets. Here, we present M2-US, a large-scale multi-domain benchmark for unified multi-task ultrasound image analysis. The dataset consists of 67,620 ultrasound images from public datasets and retrospectively collected clinical cohorts. It covers more than 30 anatomical structures and pathological targets across maternal-fetal, cardiac, vascular, abdominal, pulmonary, breast, thyroid, gynecological, and other clinical applications. M2-US supports four major prediction tasks: segmentation, classification, object detection, and landmark regression, organized into 26 subtasks. The dataset provides predefined training, validation, and test partitions, together with task-specific annotations and standardized metadata linking ultrasound images to their corresponding segmentation masks, class labels, bounding boxes, and landmark coordinates. Baseline experiments using Feature Pyramid Network (FPN) and DINOv3 models show the usability of the dataset and evaluation pipeline across heterogeneous ultrasound tasks. To our knowledge, M2-US is the first large-scale ultrasound benchmark comprising data acquired using approximately 24 scanner models from more than 10 manufacturers and covering over 30 anatomical structures and pathological targets. The benchmark supports four major downstream tasks across segmentation, classification, detection, and regression. Together with our evaluation pipeline, the benchmark enables systematic evaluation of task-specific models, multi-task learning methods, foundation model adaptation, as well as cross-domain generalization in ultrasound image analysis.

title: Ursolic Acid-Enriched Fraction Attenuates Diabetic Cardiomyopathy Through Modulation of Inflammatory and Oxidative Stress: An Integrated in-silico and in-vivo Approach
authorString: Biruduraju Y, Komati A, Mandava K, Thakur S, Talari A, Rawool D, Gowtham M.
abstractText: Diabetic Cardiomyopathy (DCM), which is a severe complication of diabetes, has become the leading cause of heart failure in diabetic patients. Role of TLR4-NLRP3 inflammaosome signalling in the pathogenesis of DCM and effect of ursolic acid on DCM is not well explored. The present study evaluated the cardioprotective potential of ursolic acid-enriched fraction (UAEF) using a multi-targeted approach which includes in vitro, in vivo, network pharmacology, and molecular docking studies. Diabetic cardiomyopathy (DCM) was induced in male Wistar rats by streptozotocin (STZ-55mg/kg, ip) and lipopolysaccharide (LPS; 1mg/kg, ip) administration followed by treatment with UAEF at doses of 25 and 50 mg/kg and with metformin (100 mg/kg) as the reference drug. UAEF significantly inhibited α-glucosidase enzyme, free radicals (hydroxyl; p < 0.0132, superoxide; p < 0.0241, and nitricoxide; p < 0.0241), and advanced glycation end-products (p < 0.0136). UAEF contained more 59.35% ursolic acid as evidenced by quantitative RP-HPLC analysis (RT-15.5 minute). Network pharmacology identified 29 common targets, TLR4, NF-κB, TNF-α, IL-1β, RAGE, NLRP3, TXNIP, caspase-1, GSDMD, SIRT1, PGC-1α and TNNT2 emerging as major hub genes. KEGG pathway analysis further identified significant enrichment of the TLR4 signalling pathway, NF-Κb, AGE-RAGE pathway, SIRT pathway AMPK pathway and NLRP3 inflammasome-related signaling pathways. Major hub genes further validated by Molecular docking and qRT-PCR analysis and found that ursolic acid showed favorable predicted affinity for NLRP3 (− 10.5 kcal/mol), IL-1β (− 9.3 kcal/mol) and caspase-1 (− 8.4 kcal/mol) and significant upregulation of mRNA expression of troponin TNNT2 (p<), SIRT1 (p < 0.003), PGC-1α (p < 0.001), TXNIP and downregulation of TLR4, NF-κB, TNF-α, IL-1β, RAGE, NLRP3, caspase-1, GSDMD (p < 0.0001). UAEF improved post parandial glycemic load (p<), Furthermore, UAEF attenuated significantly lipid peroxidation (MDA and 4-HNE; p < 0.0001), and protein oxidation markers (AOPP; p < 0.0001), while significantly restoring catalase and glutathione peroxidase activities (p < 0.0001). UAEF treatment also improved mitochondrial respiratory chain complex activities, with the 50 mg/kg dose significantly enhancing Complex I (p < 0.0019) Complex II (p < 0.0029), Complex III (p < 0.0080), Complex IV (p < 0.0001), aconitase (p < 0.0001), and succinate dehydrogenase activities (p < 0.0001). Histological analysis demonstrated that UAEF significantly preserved myocardial fibrosis, reduced structural disruption, and decreased inflammatory changes. Metformin also displayed significant protection (p < 0.0001). These results suggested that UAEF can prevent and mitigate the development of DCM and associated complications.

title: Biological Determinants of Adverse Drug Reaction Predictability in Drug–Gene Networks
authorString: Chachar MS, Yang H.
abstractText: Adverse drug reactions (ADRs) are a major cause of drug attrition and withdrawal, yet computational models compete on accuracy without asking why some ADRs are more predictable than others. Rather than proposing a more accurate predictor, this study uses an interpretable network model to investigate why individual ADRs differ in predictability. We build a drug similarity network from the drug-gene interaction profiles of 536 drugs and predict 5,599 side effects by harmonic function-based label propagation under five-fold cross-validation. Performance (AUROC 0.670, AUPRC 0.210) exceeded that of a k-nearest-neighbour baseline on the same similarity matrix and fell to chance when the network was shuffled. Because AUPRC depends strongly on ADR frequency, AUROC measured predictability for the 970 ADRs reported for at least 10 drugs; 76% were predicted significantly better than chance. Predictability was strongly associated with target coherence, defined as the extent to which drugs associated with the same ADR are more similar to one another in their gene targets than they are to other drugs (Spearman’s ρ = 0.73). The most predictable ADRs were class effects with over-represented receptor genes, such as coronary arteriospasm (HTR1B, HTR1D), and tardive dyskinesia (DRD2, HTR2A); the least predictable were non-specific reactions of pharmacologically unrelated drugs. Pathway enrichment was found for 88% of the 100 best predicted ADRs, but only 26% of the 100 worst, mainly in neurotransmitter receptor signalling. These results show that ADR predictability reflects the biological coherence of the drugs associated with an ADR, particularly their shared targets.

title: Fructose, Advanced Glycation, and Metabolic Dysfunction: Molecular Pathways Linking Oxidative Stress, Inflammation, and MASLD
authorString: Sodré AFP, Lopes ER, Sloan KP, Sloan LA, Curi R, Haber JFS, Indiane L, Dall'Antonia CT, Bishayee A, Valenti VE, Tanaka M, Hirata M, Hirabara SM, Pithon-Curi TC, Cominato L, Goulart RdA, Barbalho SM.
abstractText: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a major metabolic disorder associated with obesity, type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, and increased cardiovascular risk. Excessive fructose consumption has been implicated in hepatic lipid accumulation, advanced glycation end product (AGE) formation, oxidative stress, and chronic inflammation, potentially contributing to interconnected hepatic and cardiovascular disturbances. This narrative review examines the metabolic and molecular pathways linking fructose metabolism, AGE–RAGE signaling, and cardiometabolic dysfunction, with particular emphasis on the liver–heart axis. Fructose metabolism increases the availability of lipogenic substrates and reactive carbonyl intermediates, which may promote hepatic de novo lipogenesis and endogenous AGE formation. AGE–RAGE signaling can activate oxidative and inflammatory pathways, including reactive oxygen species production, NF-κB signaling, and mitochondrial dysfunction, potentially contributing to hepatic injury, insulin resistance, endothelial dysfunction, and adverse cardiovascular remodeling. Experimental studies provide mechanistic evidence linking fructose exposure and AGE–RAGE-related pathways to hepatic and cardiovascular injury. However, human studies primarily provide separate evidence concerning fructose intake, hepatic steatosis, AGE levels, and cardiovascular risk markers, rather than establishing AGE–RAGE signaling as a mediator connecting fructose exposure to liver and cardiovascular outcomes. Therefore, a major unresolved question is whether AGE–RAGE signaling represents a clinically relevant mechanistic link between fructose-associated liver dysfunction and cardiovascular complications in humans, or whether these processes reflect partially independent metabolic and inflammatory pathways. By integrating experimental and clinical evidence, this review identifies potential therapeutic targets and research priorities while highlighting the need for longitudinal and mechanistic human studies to clarify the clinical relevance of the liver–heart axis.

title: Inflammation-Driven Endothelial Glycocalyx Injury: A Common Mechanism Underlying Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome
authorString: Wang Z, Wang J.
abstractText: Cardiovascular–renal–metabolic (CKM) syndrome is a multisystem disorder driven by interactions among metabolic risk factors, chronic kidney disease (CKD), and cardiovascular disease. Chronic inflammation is central to its pathogenesis. The endothelial glycocalyx (EG), a carbohydrate-rich layer on vascular endothelial cells, maintains vascular homeostasis but is damaged by persistent inflammation. This review summarizes EG structure and function; describes interconnected metabolic, renal, and cardiovascular features of CKM syndrome; and highlights chronic inflammation as a linking mechanism. It discusses how inflammation-induced EG injury promotes disease onset and progression by impairing vascular barrier and filtration functions, anticoagulant and antithrombotic activity, and anti-inflammatory and metabolic regulation. Finally, it explores therapies targeting the inflammation–EG axis. We propose that this axis is a unifying mechanism connecting chronic inflammation with multisystem dysfunction in CKM syndrome. Proinflammatory mediators such as TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β, and NF-κB signaling, may serve as diagnostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets. These insights provide a conceptual framework for future research and integrated treatment strategies for CKM syndrome.

title: Prevalence and Associated Risk Factors of Hypertension and Pre-Hypertension Among the Adult Population: Findings from the Dubai Household Survey, 2024
authorString: Soni MM, Mamdouh HM, Suliman E, AlAbady K, Farooq S, AlRahma AM, Ibrahim G, Khater A, Hassanein M, Alawadi F.
abstractText:
Objectives:

This study aims to determine the prevalence of hypertension (HTN) and pre-hypertension (PHTN) among adults in Dubai, the United Arab Emirates. Furthermore, it seeks to identify the associated sociodemographic characteristics and cardiometabolic risk within this population.

Methods:

This investigation utilized data from the 2024 Dubai Household Health Survey (DHHS), a population-based cross-sectional study employing a multistage stratified cluster sampling methodology. Data on socio-demographic characteristics, behavioral risk factors, blood pressure measurements, anthropometric parameters, and blood glucose levels were collected from 2530 adult participants representing the population of Dubai. All analyses were conducted using R statistical software, incorporating survey analysis procedures to account for the complex sampling design.

Results:

The weighted prevalence of HTN was 36.9% (95% CI: 35.1–40.3), and PHTN was 32.2% (95% CI: 27.9–36.4) among adults aged ≥18 years in Dubai, indicating that 69.1% of the adult population had elevated blood pressure. HTN prevalence increased with age, was higher in males than females, and was more prevalent among non-nationals and those with lower educational attainment. Cardiometabolic risk factors such as high cholesterol (56.6% in HTN, 53.9% in PHTN) and obesity (26.9% in HTN, 20.6% in PHTN) were common in both groups, with diabetes being significantly higher in the HTN group (20.7% vs 11.8%).

Conclusions:

The study reveals a high burden of HTN and PHTN in Dubai's adult population, with significant associations with age, gender, nationality, education, and various cardiometabolic risk factors. These findings underscore the urgent need for targeted public health interventions and early detection strategies to mitigate the rising prevalence of elevated blood pressure and associated cardiovascular risks in Dubai, the UAE.

title: The Accuracy Paradox in Medical AI: Evidence from Subject-Independent ECG Arrhythmia Classification
authorString: Sahed HM, Zaman M, Ozaydin F.
abstractText: Electrocardiogram (ECG) heartbeat classification is an important task for detecting cardiac arrhythmias. However, reliable classification remains challenging because of severe class imbalance and variations in ECG patterns across individuals. This study investigates the performance of two traditional machine learning models, Random Forest (RF) and XGBoost, for subject-independent ECG heartbeat classification using the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database. A total of 100,693 heartbeat segments from 43 subjects were classified into four categories: non-ectopic (N), supraventricular ectopic (S), ventricular ectopic (V), and fusion (F) beats. The dataset exhibited substantial class imbalance, with the fusion class accounting for only 0.80\% of all beats. A feature-based approach was developed using waveform-derived statistical and wavelet features, together with RR-interval features. Both classifiers were evaluated using a 43-fold Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) protocol across three random seeds to assess their generalization to unseen subjects. Performance was measured using accuracy, balanced accuracy, macro-averaged F1-score, and class-wise evaluation metrics. XGBoost achieved a mean macro-F1 score of 0.4950 ± 0.0126 and balanced accuracy of 0.5243 ± 0.0152, outperforming Random Forest, which achieved 0.4413 ± 0.0108 and 0.4623 ± 0.0050, respectively. In contrast, Random Forest achieved higher overall accuracy (0.9212 ± 0.0072) than XGBoost (0.8615 ± 0.0045). Both models showed substantial difficulty identifying fusion beats, with near-zero F1-scores across all evaluated seeds. These findings illustrate the accuracy paradox in a medical AI setting: overall accuracy alone may not adequately represent model performance in highly imbalanced, subject-independent ECG classification. The results also highlight the persistent challenges of minority-class recognition and generalization across individuals.

title: What Factors Influence Willingness to Pay for Home and Community-Based Services Among Older Adults: A Behavioral Economics Perspective.
authorString: Xiao L, Han C, Mohetaer Y.
abstractText: Using data from 10,091 older adults in the 2023 China Longitudinal Aging Social Survey, we estimated linear probability models of willingness to pay for home and community-based care services. Overall, 28.2% were willing to pay for at least one service. Stronger local norms assigning eldercare responsibility to adult children and greater risk aversion were associated with lower willingness to pay. Education, income, public pensions, and the presence of community care facilities were positively associated with willingness to pay. Patterns varied by service type, urban or rural residence, and age group.

title: Behavioral Cardiovascular Health Metrics in Adolescence: Evidence From a Cross-Sectional Analysis of the 2022-2023 COMPASS-Québec Cohort Supporting the Relevance of Including Recreational Screen Time.
authorString: Tock WL, Turcotte-Tremblay AM, Gansaonré RJ, Bélanger RE, Leatherdale ST, Gauvin L.

journal.title: The Journal of adolescent health : official publication of the Society for Adolescent Medicine

abstractText:
Purpose

The American Heart Association's Life's Essential 8 defines cardiovascular health (CVH) through four behavior factors (physical activity, diet, sleep, and nicotine exposure) and four biological factors, but it excludes recreational screen time, a prevalent sedentary behavior increasingly linked to adolescent cardiometabolic risk. We examined whether adding recreational screen time to a behavioral CVH score changes population-level estimates and their sociodemographic and school-level patterning.

Methods

We analyzed cross-sectional 2022 to 2023 COMPASS-Québec data from 17,882 adolescents (ages 11-19 years). The following two behavioral CVH scores were compared: a four-component score (physical activity, diet quality, sleep health, and nicotine exposure) and a five-component score that additionally included recreational screen time. Linear mixed-effects models with school random intercepts examined associations for each score with grade, gender identity, ethnicity, material deprivation, and school type.

Results

Mean behavioral CVH was 74.3 (standard deviation 19.7) for the four-component score and 64.5 (standard deviation 18.6) for the five-component score, a 9.8-point reduction when recreational screen time was included. In both models, higher grade, greater material deprivation, racialized identity, and public rural school attendance were associated with lower behavioral CVH; boys scored higher than girls, gender diverse adolescents scored lower, and students in private schools scored higher.

Discussion

Including recreational screen time lowered population level behavioral CVH estimates without changing the social gradients, indicating that frameworks that exclude it may underestimate adolescent vulnerability. A more behaviorally complete approach could strengthen surveillance, improve intervention targeting, and better support school-based strategies to promote CVH equitably.

title: Smoking Very Low Nicotine Content Cigarettes Produces Measurable Cardiovascular and Autonomic Effects: Evidence Informing FDA-Proposed Reduced Nicotine Standard.
authorString: Anwar M, Pandian S, Posada-Quintero HF, White CM, Shaltout HA, Donny EC.

journal.title: Nicotine & tobacco research : official journal of the Society for Research on Nicotine and Tobacco

abstractText:
Introduction

The FDA proposed limiting nicotine in combustible cigarettes to ≤ 0.70 mg/g to reduce addictiveness. The tobacco industry has argued that such standards would render cigarettes functionally zero nicotine products, an interpretation industry contends exceeds the FDA's statutory authority. This study addresses this argument by extending existing evidence. It examined whether puffing a 0.4 mg/g very low nicotine content (VLNC) cigarette produced autonomic and cardiovascular responses distinct from a nicotine- and tobacco-free cigarette substitute (CS).

Methods

Twenty-four adults who smoke took 8 puffs from a CS followed by a 0.4 mg/g cigarette. ECG (heart rate, RMSSD), the time-varying electrodermal activity index (TVSymp), and arterial stiffness (pulse wave velocity [PWV]) were recorded across pre-puffing, puffing, and post-puffing periods.

Results

Change scores from their respective pre-puffing (Δ) indicated that heart rate increased during puffing (Δ = 3.64 ± 4.26 bpm) and post-puffing (Δ = 2.66 ± 2.80 bpm; Ps < .001 vs. CS). RMSSD decreased during puffing (Δ = -0.14 ± 2.67 ms; P = .03 vs. CS) and post-puffing (Δ = -1.21 ± 2.40 ms; P = .04 vs. CS). TVSymp increased during puffing (Δ = 0.67 ± 0.47; P < .001 vs. CS) and post-puffing (Δ = 0.64 ± 0.47; P = .002 vs. CS). Post-puffing PWV increased (Δ = +0.47 ± 0.69 m/s; P = .004 vs. CS).

Conclusions

Smoking 0.4 mg/g cigarette produced measurable autonomic and cardiovascular effects. These findings inform ongoing regulatory discussions and indicate that VLNC cigarettes are not functionally equivalent to "zero nicotine" products.

title: High-Pressure Controlled-Dissection Coronary Intervention With the Drug-Coated Balloon.
authorString: Lim PO.
abstractText:
Background

Coronary dissection after drug-coated balloon (DCB) predicts late luminal gain, but it is frequently covered with a drug-eluting stent (DES) to avoid acute vessel closure. A "dissected artery that does not occlude" may be possible with controlled dissection using the double buddy-wire cutting technique.

Case summary

Wire cutting followed by DCB infrequently results in striking dissections. Three such cases are presented: A long spiral dissection in the right coronary artery and 2 mid left anterior descending artery dissections. Follow-up coronary angiograms revealed healed, widened coronary arteries.

Discussion

In the SELUTION DeNovo study, DCB + bailout DES is 66% more likely to fail than upfront DES-by the same operators. Wire cutting produces a longitudinal dissection, instead of a circumferential dissection, which can extend as a counterflow flap, the mode of acute vessel closure.

Take-home messages

Lesion preparation consensus for DCB tolerates a 30% residual stenosis and advises bailout stenting for significant dissections. The double buddy-wire cutting technique with high-pressure balloon dilatations may overcome these limitations.

Trials

GRAND-DES (Grand Drug-Eluting Stent registry), REC-CAGEFREE I, SELUTION DeNovo.

title: Simultaneous Mitral and Tricuspid Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair in Transthyretin Cardiac Amyloidosis.
authorString: Singer K, Hauptmann L, Autherith M, Poledniczek M, Schmid L, Bergler-Klein J, Demirel C, Dannenberg V, Bartko PE, Nitsche C.
abstractText:
Background

Cardiac amyloidosis can be accompanied by combined atrioventricular regurgitation, yet same-session transcatheter treatment of both valves in this setting remains rarely reported.

Case summary

A 78-year-old man with wild-type transthyretin amyloid-associated cardiomyopathy, permanent atrial fibrillation, and progressive heart failure under transthyretin amyloidosis-specific medication presented with severe symptomatic mitral and tricuspid regurgitation. Same-session transcatheter edge-to-edge repair was successfully performed using 1 device at the mitral and 2 devices at the tricuspid valve. Mitral and tricuspid regurgitation were reduced from severe to mild-moderate and from torrential to moderate, with intraprocedural final mean gradients of 3 mm Hg and 1 mm Hg, respectively.

Discussion

At 1 year, the patient was in New York Heart Association functional class I and II, and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide had decreased from 2,550 to 726 pg/mL.

Take-home message

In selected patients with transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis with severe symptomatic bivalvular regurgitation, combined transcatheter edge-to-edge repair at both atrioventricular valves may offer an effective treatment option.

title: Recommendations for the use of hormone and nonhormone treatment of vasomotor symptoms of menopause: Menopause Medical Eligibility Criteria (MenoMEC) based on insights from a modified Delphi panel.
authorString: Liss J, Larkin LC, Pinkerton JV, Martin K, Woods G, Dehn B, Shufelt C, Iyer TK, Lustberg M, Simon JA, Neal-Perry G, Epperson CN, Dorotan MKC, Gong CL, Migliaccio-Walle K, Kang A, Boskovic N, Ramsey S, Minkin MJ.
abstractText:
Objectives

To develop a Menopause Medical Eligibility Criteria (MenoMEC) tool to guide individualized, evidence-based care for the treatment of vasomotor symptoms due to menopause.

Methods

We conducted a modified Delphi panel of 15 multidisciplinary experts to establish US-focused consensus recommendations for hormone and nonhormone therapy use in managing moderate-severe vasomotor symptoms, considering various comorbid conditions. An online survey assessed agreement with proposed recommendations using a nine-point Likert scale, with ≥70% agreement defining consensus. Items lacking consensus were discussed in a structured in-person meeting, leading to refined recommendations and final development of the tool.

Results

Panelists affirmed hormone therapy as first-line for eligible women and nonhormone therapy for those with contraindications or who decline hormone therapy. Recommended first-line nonhormone therapy options were selective serotonin/serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors, gabapentin, and oxybutynin, after accounting for contraindications. Neurokinin therapies (eg, fezolinetant, elinzanetant) were supported as first-line but limited by access and cost. Clonidine and most herbal/over-the-counter products were not recommended due to potential adverse effects, drug-drug interactions, or lack of evidence of benefit or harm. Specific recommendations regarding the appropriateness of therapy addressed women with cardiovascular disease, metabolic syndrome, thrombosis, liver disease, smoking, and hormone-sensitive cancers. All panelists agreed that there was an urgent need to provide structured guidance to the clinical community regarding the selection and use of hormone versus nonhormone therapy.

Conclusions

This panel provided structured, symptom-based, and comorbidity-based recommendations to optimize therapy for the management of vasomotor symptoms and supported the development of a MenoMEC guideline for use in primary care clinical settings.

title: Obstructive sleep apnoea and hypertension: pathophysiological links, blood pressure phenotypes and treatment effects.
authorString: Schwarz EI.
abstractText:
Introduction

Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and arterial hypertension frequently coexist and are linked by recurrent nocturnal cardiovascular stress. Intermittent hypoxemia, arousals and intrathoracic pressure swings promote sympathetic activation, vascular dysfunction and abnormal blood-pressure (BP) regulation.

Areas covered

This narrative review integrates epidemiological, mechanistic and interventional evidence on the OSA-hypertension relationship based on a PubMed search (start until September 2026). Particular emphasis is placed on nocturnal hypertension, non-dipping, masked and resistant hypertension; the roles of intermittent hypoxemia, sympathetic overactivity, baroreflex, and endothelial dysfunction; and treatment effects of continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP), mandibular advancement devices and weight loss. Evidence from CPAP-withdrawal trials and recent meta-analyses is used to identify characteristics associated with a greater BP response to OSA treatment.

Expert opinion

The modest average BP reduction with CPAP conceals substantial heterogeneity. Treatment effects are strongest for nocturnal BP and in patients with uncontrolled BP, severe OSA and sufficient nightly treatment exposure. Future cardiovascular OSA management should move beyond the apnea-hypopnea index toward combined characterization of nocturnal physiological stress, clinical OSA phenotype, BP phenotype, and effective treatment exposure.

title: Blood Pressure Phenotypes in Children Aged 6-12 Years: A Pediatric Nephrology Research Consortium (PNRC) Study.
authorString: Jahan A, Abdullah M, McLaughlin M, Cadiz EM, Manchanda E, Chishti A, Murphy M, Twichell S, Mazo A, Samsonov D, Maniar A, Kim H, Lomanta F, Patibandla AC, Frank R, Abboud N, Schuchman M, Srivastava T, Yamaguchi I, Sethna CB.
abstractText:
Background

Ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) enables identification of hypertension phenotypes carrying distinct cardiovascular risk profiles, yet data on phenotype distribution and cardiac outcomes in younger school-age children remain limited.

Methods

This multicenter retrospective cross-sectional study conducted across 11 Pediatric Nephrology Research Consortium sites included children aged 6-12 years without chronic kidney disease who underwent ABPM and echocardiography within 3 months. Blood pressure (BP) phenotypes were classified per the 2022 American Heart Association Scientific Statement on ABPM in Children and Adolescents.

Results

Of 212 children (median age 10.6 years, 45.3% female, median BMI z-score 1.56), sustained hypertension was most prevalent (39.6%), followed by white-coat hypertension (30.7%), normotension (17.0%), and masked hypertension (12.7%). Left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH, left ventricular mass index [LVMI] ≥95th percentile for age and sex) was identified in 49 children (23.1%), present across all phenotypes. No BP phenotype was independently associated with LVH or LVMI in adjusted (for age, sex and BMI z-score) or sensitivity models (site level clustering and device type). BMI z-score was the only independent correlate of LVH (PR 1.36, 95% CI 1.01-1.82, p = 0.04). Nocturnal hypertension was associated with higher LVMI after full adjustment (β = 2.66, 95% CI 0.10-5.21); sensitive to ABPM device type adjustment. Among children with masked hypertension, 88.9% had nocturnal hypertension.

Conclusions

In this multicenter cohort of younger children without CKD, BP phenotype was not significantly associated with LVH; BMI z-score was the most consistent correlate of cardiac remodeling, and nocturnal hypertension showed an exploratory association with higher LVMI after BMI z-score adjustment.

title: Migration of a Right Ventricular Outflow Tract Stent Causing Incomplete Cardioplegic Arrest: Stent Gone Astray!
authorString: Jain AK, Goel K, Mital T, Kohli JK, Patel P.

journal.title: Turkish journal of anaesthesiology and reanimation

abstractText: Right ventricular outflow tract (RVOT) stenting is an established palliative option in tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) when surgical repair poses a high-risk. We report a rare, life-threatening complication in a 4-year-old child with TOF, a hypoplastic pulmonary annulus, and multiple comorbidities that precluded primary corrective surgery. RVOT stenting was therefore planned. During catheterization, the stent embolized, necessitating emergency surgical retrieval. Intraoperatively, the stent was seen lodged across the aortic valve, preventing complete leaflet coaptation, and causing the cardioplegia to leak into the left ventricle. This resulted in an incomplete cardioplegic arrest. Real-time transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) identified the mechanism of cardioplegia failure, delineated the stent position, guided its repositioning, and facilitated successful cardioplegia delivery and definitive surgical repair. This case emphasizes meticulous anatomical evaluation and highlights the indispensable role of intraoperative TEE in high-risk RVOT stenting.

title: Circumflex-perfused mass and mitral regurgitation after coronary bypass.
authorString: Tamagawa Y, Yajima S, Misumi Y, Yoshioka D, Kawamura T, Kawamura A, Saito S, Miyagawa S.
abstractText: BackgroundIschemic cardiomyopathy-associated mitral regurgitation (ICM-MR) may improve after isolated coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG); however, its determinants remain unclear. We investigated left circumflex coronary artery (LCx)-perfused left ventricular (LV) mass volume and regional myocardial mechanics related to ICM-MR improvement after isolated CABG.MethodsData of 22 patients with ICM-MR who underwent isolated CABG (2016-2023) were retrospectively studied using preoperative and 1-year postoperative coronary computed tomography and echocardiography. Patients were grouped by 1-year MR change: improvement (≥1-grade reduction) and non-improvement (no change/worse). Perfused LV mass volume, regional longitudinal strain, and mitral tethering geometry were compared.ResultsAmong the 22 patients, nine (41%) exhibited MR improvement, whereas 13 (59%) did not. The change in the LCx-perfused LV mass volume was significantly greater in the improvement group than in the non-improvement group (11 [3-16] vs 0 [-6-5] mL; p = 0.049). The LCx longitudinal strain substantially improved in the improvement group (-10.3% [-11.6 to -1.4] vs +1.2% [-3.2 to +4.6]; p = 0.016). The improvement group demonstrated greater reverse remodeling: tenting height (-2.2 mm [-2.4 to -0.6] vs -0.5 mm [-0.7 to 0.2], p = 0.007), tenting area (-0.54 cm2 [-0.85 to -0.35] vs  + 0.02 cm2 [-0.07 to + 0.57], p < 0.001), and posterior leaflet tethering angle (-5° [-9 to -2] vs 1° [-2 to 4], p = 0.038).ConclusionsImprovement in ICM-MR after isolated CABG was associated with an increased LCx-perfused LV mass volume, concomitant regional functional recovery, and mitral geometry reversal, suggesting a possible role of LCx territory recovery in mitral regurgitation improvement.

title: Iatrogenic pulmonary artery pseudoaneurysm following chest tube insertion.
authorString: Gorospe L, Lomanto-Navarro LC, Urbano-García J.
abstractText: We report a rare case of pulmonary artery pseudoaneurysm developing immediately after tube thoracostomy in a 62-year-old man with tuberculous pleural effusion. Contrast-enhanced CT demonstrated a pseudoaneurysm arising from a subsegmental pulmonary artery branch associated with lung laceration. The lesion was successfully treated by endovascular coil embolization, with complete clinical and radiological resolution at follow-up.

title: ELISA Measurements Reveal Distinct Types of Antiphosphatidylethanolamine Antibodies.
authorString: Hou S, Liu SL, Lindholm PF, Lee J, Thurman JM, Ramsey-Goldman R, Zhao M.
abstractText:
Purpose

Existing literature on enzyme linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA)-based detection of antiphosphatidylethanolamine (aPE) antibodies indicated that the results were dependent on the assay conditions. The goal of this study was to examine ELISA for aPE antibodies between the presence and absence of adult bovine plasma (ABP), which was recently shown as a source of cofactor for some of the aPE antibodies while it suppresses the reactivity of other aPE antibodies.

Methods

ELISA tests were conducted using egg PE as antigen in 148 random patient plasma samples from Northwestern Memorial Hospital Hemostasis Laboratory in a sample-by-sample comparison with or without ABP for IgG, IgM, and IgA aPE isotypes. A secondary ELISA test was performed using synthetic lamellar (18:1 PE) and hexagonal (20:4 PE) PE as antigens, with or without ABP.

Results

In a sample-by-sample comparison, ELISA results identified two distinct types of aPE antibodies: the ones with elevated reactivity in the presence of ABP and are specific to lamellar PE, versus those with high reactivity in the absence of ABP that lacked collective specificity between lamellar and hexagonal PE.

Conclusion

The data demonstrated that the different results of aPE ELISA in the presence versus absence of ABP indicate two distinct subtypes of aPE antibodies. The ability to differentiate these subtypes of aPE will enable future investigations to better characterize these antibodies.

title: Electrospun scaffolds for MSC-derived secretome delivery.
