title: Effects of Digoxin in Modern Heart Failure Treatment: The DIG-Mod HF Trial.
authorString: Valentim Gonçalves A, Cardim N, Fiarresga A, Pereira-da-Silva T, Ilhão-Moreira R, Galrinho A, Rio P, Aguiar Rosa S, Teresa Timóteo A, Carvalheiro R, Ferreira F, Lopes J, Selas M, Silva F, Viana B, Ferreira RC.
abstractText:
Background

The DIG-Mod HF trial is the first trial to evaluate the mechanistic effects of low-dose digoxin on myocardial work and functional exercise capacity in patients with heart failure (HF) with reduced ejection fraction receiving contemporary guideline-recommended medical therapy (GRMT). Although a recent meta-analysis demonstrated clinical benefit of cardiac glycosides in addition to contemporary GRMT, the mechanistic basis for this effect remains unexplored.

Objectives

The authors aimed to investigate whether low-dose digoxin improves myocardial work and functional exercise capacity when added to optimized GRMT.

Methods

An open-label, randomized crossover trial enrolled 50 patients with HF with reduced ejection fraction on maximally tolerated GRMT. Patients were randomized 1:1 to digoxin 0.125 mg/day plus standard of care or standard of care alone, each for 24 weeks, for a total study duration of 48 weeks. Co-primary endpoints were within-patient changes in peak oxygen consumption (Vo2) and left ventricular global work index.

Results

The study population was highly optimized, with 88% in NYHA functional class II on near-universal quadruple GRMT. Digoxin did not significantly improve peak Vo2 (mean difference: -0.08 mL/kg/min; 95% CI: -1.64 to 1.47 mL/kg/min; P = 0.914). Global work index improved significantly (mean difference: 157.8 mm Hg%; 95% CI: 12.2-303.4 mm Hg%; P = 0.034). N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide and Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-12 score also improved during the digoxin period. The composite safety endpoint did not differ significantly between arms (P = 0.089).

Conclusions

Low-dose digoxin significantly improved myocardial work without improving peak Vo2. Demonstrating these effects in a clinically stable, well-treated population is consistent with an independent pharmacologic effect of digoxin in addition to modern guideline-directed therapy. (Effects of Digoxin in Modern Heart Failure Treatment [DIG-Mod HF]; EU Clinical Trials Register Number: 2024-513448-26-00).

title: Higher Quality Temperature Control Is Associated With Improved Outcomes Following Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: A Multicenter Validation Study.
authorString: Beekman R, McCarthy W, Nguyen C, Tam J, Case N, Elmer J, Roy S, Suliman M, Beiser DG, Helwagen E, Sircelij V, Coulter D, Nassal MM, Salhi HE, Wira C, Perman SM, Gilmore EJ.
abstractText:
Study objective

Hypothermic temperature control has not consistently demonstrated a neuroprotective effect, resulting in heterogeneity of use in clinical practice. We evaluated temperature control quality across 4 institutions and its association with clinical outcomes.

Methods

Retrospective analysis of institutional registry data collected between 2021 and 2024 in survivors of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) with Glasgow Coma Scale Motor score less than 6 from 4 academic centers with established cardiac arrest programs. Eligible patients included those 18 years of age or older, treated with hypothermic temperature control (33-36°C) using a feedback-controlled device, and admitted to an intensive care unit (ICU). A temperature control quality score (0-6) was assigned for each patient. The primary outcome was survival to hospital discharge. The secondary outcome was good neurologic outcome at hospital discharge, defined as a Cerebral Performance Category (CPC) score of 1-2. Univariable and multivariable logistic regressions quantified the relationship between quality of temperature control, as an ordinal variable, and outcomes.

Results

Among 356 included patients, most were male (N=224, 62.9%) with mean (standard deviation [SD]) age 58.1 (15.2) years. Most suffered a nonshockable arrest (N=262, 73.6%) and did not receive layperson CPR (N=225, 63.2%). Median [IQR] Pittsburgh Cardiac Arrest Category score was 4 [3,4], mean (SD) lactate 9.1 (4.1) mmol/L, and pH 7.09 (0.17). Median [IQR] preinduction time was 2.3 [1.5 to 3.5] hours and 150 (42.1%) were treated with early neuromuscular blockade. Adjusting for confounders in the multivariable model, an increase of one-point in the temperature control quality score was associated with improved survival at hospital discharge (odds ratio [OR] 1.32; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.07 to 1.64). A one-point increase in the quality score also resulted in a shift towards lower (improved) CPC score (OR 1.28; 95% CI, 0.05 to 1.55). The direction of effect was consistent across all centers.

Conclusion

In unresponsive survivors of OHCA, an increase in temperature control quality was associated with improved survival and better neurologic outcome; however, confounding by site, injury severity, or perceived prognosis is possible. Lack of temperature control parameter standardization may influence efficacy and practice variability within pragmatic-design clinical trials possibly contributed to neutral trial results. Prospective trials evaluating the importance of temperature control quality and the population most likely to benefit from hypothermic temperature control are essential.

title: Functional Divergence of Upper- and Lower-Body Fat Distribution and Differences in Cardiovascular and Cerebrovascular Disease Risk and Outcomes: A Narrative Review
authorString: Huang X.
abstractText: Traditional obesity risk assessment centers on body mass index (BMI); however, marked differences in cardiovascular and cerebrovascular outcomes despite comparable total adiposity suggest that the regional attributes of adipose tissue have independent explanatory value. Consistent evidence from cohort studies and Mendelian randomization (MR) shows that upper-body (abdominal/truncal) fat is positively associated with cardiovascular and cerebrovascular risk, whereas lower-body (gluteofemoral/leg) fat is independently associated with reduced risk at the adipose depot volume level. In a South Indian dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) study, each 1-SD increase in android fat was associated with an odds ratio (OR) for type 2 diabetes of 6.59 (95% CI, 3.17–13.70) in men, whereas the OR for leg fat was 0.42 (95% CI, 0.24–0.74). A dose-response meta-analysis showed that each 10-cm increase in hip circumference was associated with a 10% lower risk of all-cause mortality (hazard ratio (HR), 0.90; 95% CI, 0.81–0.99); after adjustment for BMI and waist circumference, the association strengthened to an HR of 0.78 (95% CI, 0.66–0.90). Data from the UK Biobank showed that, after adjustment for BMI and waist circumference, each 1-SD increase in hip circumference was associated with a 5% lower risk of coronary heart disease (HR, 0.95; 95% CI, 0.93–0.97). A cross-cohort reclassification analysis showed that among individuals with a "normal-weight" BMI, 5% had an elevated waist circumference and 18% had an elevated waist-to-hip ratio; most of these individuals, who were not identified by BMI-based classification, had a 15%–50% increased risk of cardiovascular outcomes. A Chinese population cohort showed that dynamic changes in the weight-adjusted waist index were independently associated with cardiovascular and cerebrovascular mortality, with the group showing the largest increase having a 1.52-fold higher risk than the lowest group. Upper-body fat risk exhibited a dose-dependent pattern: a high visceral adiposity index was associated with a 55% increased risk of cardiovascular disease (risk ratio (RR), 1.55; 95% CI, 1.36–1.76). The causal signal for visceral adipose tissue (VAT) is highly sensitive to exposure definition and inferential framework. Within an MR framework using MRI-measured VAT volume and BMI adjustment, VAT had no robust effect on atherosclerotic outcomes. In contrast, observational associations of BMI-adjusted MRI-defined VAT showed a positive signal. An MR study across multiple vascular beds used MRI-derived fat depots as exposure measures. After BMI adjustment, each 1-SD increase in gluteofemoral adipose tissue (GFAT) volume was associated with 17%, 24%, and 28% lower risks of myocardial infarction, large-artery atherosclerotic stroke, and peripheral artery disease, respectively. These effects attenuated but remained significant after adjustment for lipids. In contrast, causal estimates for waist-to-hip ratio (WHR) and hip circumference were not robust in sensitivity analyses. Sex-specific MR showed that the causal association between WHR and coronary heart disease was significant in women (OR, 1.16; 95% CI, 1.06–1.26) but not in men. At the mechanistic level, paired chromatin landscape analysis of subcutaneous adipose tissue (SAT) and omental visceral adipose tissue (OVAT) showed that OVAT-specific differentially accessible regions were approximately twice as numerous as those in SAT and were enriched at promoters of cardiomyopathy-related genes. AI-driven large-scale clinical phenotyping in 101,243 patients showed that individuals positive for brown adipose tissue (BAT) had a lower prevalence of cardiovascular and psychiatric diseases. Higher BAT activity was associated with lower odds of cardiometabolic disease, and angiotensin receptor blocker use was positively associated with BAT, suggesting that BAT has preliminary druggable-target signals, although causal and hard-endpoint evidence is not yet established. A retrospective cohort of 13,530 patients undergoing PET/CT further showed that BAT positivity was independently associated with a lower incidence of cardiovascular events (P=0.018). Perivascular adipose tissue (PVAT) and epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) influence arterial stiffness, ventricular remodeling, and arrhythmias through paracrine pathways adjacent to target organs. EAT volume was independently associated with new-onset atrial fibrillation (HR per 1-SD increase, 1.29; 95% CI, 1.05–1.58; still significant after adjustment for BMI and left atrial volume). The CT-accessible Fat Attenuation Index has translated the inflammatory phenotype of PVAT into a clinically deployable prognostic tool; pericoronary adipose tissue (PCAT) attenuation was significantly associated with major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) risk (HR, 1.58; 95% CI, 1.38–1.81) and all-cause mortality (HR, 1.77), but this effect size was highly sensitive to analytical strategy. Radiomic quantification of EAT volume and the PVAT inflammatory phenotype jointly support the feasibility of opportunistic risk stratification. At the intervention level, several lines of evidence jointly support "distribution improvement" as an independent dimension for evaluating interventions beyond weight loss alone. These include CENTRAL/DIRECT-PLUS, the primary and mediation analyses of SELECT, comparisons of VAT reduction across different intervention pathways, the SUMMIT CMR substudy, the DAPA-EAT trial, and evidence on dapagliflozin and EAT. Heart failure outcomes exhibit heterogeneity by ejection fraction phenotype. A prospective cohort of 428,000 participants in the UK Biobank showed that heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) was independently associated with all adiposity measures (VAT: HR, 1.23), whereas heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) was not independently associated with adiposity measures. EAT was consistently associated with harm in HFpEF/heart failure with mildly reduced ejection fraction (HFmrEF) but showed a paradoxical association in HFrEF. Among patients with HFpEF, 91% had an elevated waist circumference and 85% had elevated VAT, but only 38% met the BMI criterion for obesity. The PARAGON-HF trial further showed that the prevalence of central obesity (waist-to-height ratio (WHtR) ≥0.5) in HFpEF was as high as 96%, whereas BMI-defined obesity was present in only 49%. In diabetic HFrEF, cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR)-defined sarcopenic obesity was independently associated with approximately a 3-fold risk of adverse outcomes (HR, 3.03; 95% CI, 1.39–6.63). Three-dimensional deep learning segmentation of whole-body MRI has enabled direct quantification of GFAT and provided incremental discrimination of ΔAUC 0.01–0.02 beyond models already containing BMI and WHR. A sarcopenic obesity index derived from routine CMR (body weight/pectoralis major mass) in 55,768 UK Biobank CMR scans showed that each 1-SD increase was associated with a 31% higher risk of incident heart failure, a 51% higher risk of cardiovascular death, and a 37% higher risk of all-cause death. This index provides a scalable operational tool for characterizing the "fat–muscle configuration." AI-derived MRI body composition analysis further showed that, after full adjustment for BMI and waist circumference, only VAT proportion and skeletal muscle fat fraction independently provided incremental prognostic information for MACE. This suggests that opportunistic radiomic quantification is extending beyond the boundaries of circumference-based proxies. Critical benchmarking of novel body shape indices suggests that BMI combined with WHR captures nearly all body shape information relevant to cardiometabolic disease; novel indices have incremental value but are not yet sufficient to support widespread replacement of BMI + WHR. The Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA) cohort showed that WHR significantly modifies the cardiovascular risk associated with lipoprotein(a) (Lp[a]): individuals with Lp(a) ≥50 mg/dL and WHR ≥90th percentile had the highest atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) incidence (35.7/1,000 person-years). The American Diabetes Association (ADA) 2026 standards and the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome guideline have incorporated distribution indicators such as waist circumference into risk stratification; the Expert Consensus on the Management of Obesity in the Elderly (2026 Edition) further provides diagnostic cutoffs for waist circumference and waist-to-hip ratio in Chinese older adults. This narrative review synthesizes the above evidence, using "functional divergence" as the organizing thread.

title: A shared cardiovascular and cerebrovascular risk marker phenotype: physiological context and prognosis
authorString: Wu J, Chen Q, Chen X, Wu M, Mi S, Shin HJ, Song H, Kim DW, Zhou Z.
abstractText: Abnormalities in routine cardiovascular and cerebrovascular risk markers often cluster. We characterised their common pattern, the shared adverse physiological axis (SAPA), using systolic and diastolic blood pressure, low- and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, triglycerides, glycated haemoglobin, body mass index and C-reactive protein. The pattern recurred across clinical cohorts and genetic data. The genetic direction retained an estimated 71.8-91.1% of the linear genetic information these eight markers carried for myocardial infarction and stroke. At similar total fat, participants with higher SAPA had more visceral and less leg fat. Differences in the variability and regional distribution of body fat contributed to weaker marker covariation at older ages, where anatomical associations persisted. The fixed clinical score also distinguished stroke prognosis among Chinese participants initially classified as low risk. Net stroke probabilities over approximately seven years were 2.560% (95% interval, 1.742-3.431%) and 9.351% (5.906-13.037%) in the low and high SAPA groups.

title: Ipsilateral Retrograde Approach Via CC-0 Septal-to-Septal Invisible Collateral for Uncrossable LAD Stenosis.
authorString: Li J, Han F, Ma D, Huang Z, Wan Q, Wu S, Wen S, Wang F, Huang Y, Kwan TW, Zhang B.
abstractText:
Background

Retrograde percutaneous coronary intervention for non-chronic total occlusion lesions via angiographically invisible septal collateral channels remains technically challenging.

Case summary

A 70-year-old man with recurrent unstable angina after a recent inferior ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction presented with a tortuous, severe stenosis of the mid-left anterior descending artery. Antegrade wiring of the lesion failed despite multiple guidewires with microcatheter support. No angiographically visible collateral channels (CCs) were identified from either the contralateral or ipsilateral circulation; nevertheless, ipsilateral retrograde surfing through an invisible CC-0 collateral successfully crossed from the proximal to the distal septal branches using a Fielder XT-A guidewire, and revascularization was completed successfully.

Take-home message

This case demonstrates that angiographically invisible septal CCs can be traversable, and that a retrograde approach through such channels can effectively revascularize an otherwise uncrossable lesion.

title: Utilization and outcomes of donation after circulatory death donors age greater than age 70 in liver transplantation in the united states.
authorString: Haugen CE, Kelty C, Patel SS, Bencini G, Long SA, Segev DL, Orandi BJ, Massie AB, Quillin RC.

journal.title: Liver transplantation : official publication of the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases and the International Liver Transplantation Society

abstractText: Advances in machine perfusion have transformed liver transplantation (LT) in the US with exponential expansion in donation after cardiac death (DCD) donors within the past five years. Utilization of higher risk DCD donors, such as age≥70, has also increased, but transplant center and organ procurement organization (OPO) use and outcomes compared to similar age donation after brain death donors (DBD) remain unquantified. DCD donors age≥70 and adult LT recipients of donors DCD age≥70, DBD age≥70, and DCD age 55-69 from 1/2022-12/2025 were identified using SRTR data. Utilization of normothermic regional perfusion (NRP) and DCD donors age≥70 by OPO were quantified. Characteristics and outcomes were compared between LT recipients among three donor groups using weighted Cox proportional hazards. Among 438 liver allografts from DCD donors age≥70 recovered, 347 (79%) were transplanted, and those transplanted were more likely to utilize NRP (70.6% vs. 52.7%, p<0.01) and machine perfusion (60.7% vs. 31.9%, p<0.01) compared to non-utilized allografts. Utilization of DCD donors age≥70 increased from 1 in 2022 to 297 in 2025. Over four years, 15 (26%) OPOs recovered zero liver allografts from DCD donors age≥70, and 57 (46%) centers utilized DCD donors age≥70. LT recipients of DCD donors age≥70 has similar mortality compared to LT recipients of DBD donors age≥70 (aHR(95%CI): 1.19(0.64 - 2.21),p=0.58) and DCD donors age 55-69 (aHR(95%CI): 1.08(0.59 - 2.00),p=0.80). Utilization of DCD age≥70 allografts in the US has exponentially increased in the last four years with higher NRP and machine perfusion utilization. Outcomes for LT recipients with DCD donors age ≥70 are similar to DBD donors age≥70. Strategies to increase donation and NRP use for DCD donors age≥70 at OPO and transplant center levels warrant exploration.

title: Von willebrand factor antigen identifies liver-related risk across surgical treatment pathways in hepatocellular carcinoma.
authorString: Pereyra D, Dong Y, Podrascanin V, Dingfelder J, Kenez B, Kern AE, Santol J, Hardy N, Moeckli B, Li Z, Kamath P, Oellinger R, Gyoeri G, Gruenberger T, Warner SG, Smoot RL, Taner T, Heimbach JK, Starlinger P.

journal.title: Liver transplantation : official publication of the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases and the International Liver Transplantation Society

abstractText:
Background

Treatment selection between resection and transplantation for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) considers tumor characteristics and liver function, but may incompletely capture underlying hepatic risk. We assessed the prognostic value of von Willebrand factor antigen (vWF-Ag) across these treatment pathways.

Methods

We studied 345 patients with HCC undergoing resection (n=105) or listed for transplantation (n=240) at two centers. vWF-Ag was measured before resection or at listing. Outcomes included survival, recurrence, and waitlist dropout, with the latter assessed using competing-risk methods. Analyses included cohort-specific vWF-Ag strata, continuous and spline models, adjustment for MELD, up-to-seven sum, and log10(AFP), and treatment interactions.

Results

Overall survival was comparable between strategies when measured from listing or surgery, while recurrence was more frequent after resection (HR 10.0). After resection, rising vWF-Ag was independently associated with higher mortality (adjusted HR 1.042 per 10%) and recurrence (adjusted HR 1.046). At listing, vWF-Ag above 413% was associated with a higher cumulative incidence of dropout (41.6% vs. 25.2% at 24 months), driven by clinical deterioration or death rather than tumor progression, independently of MELD. After transplantation, vWF-Ag did not stratify survival or recurrence, and the vWF-Ag by treatment interaction was significant for mortality and recurrence (all p≤0.01).

Conclusions

In HCC patients, vWF-Ag was associated with adverse outcomes after resection and non-oncological waitlist dropout, but not post-transplant outcomes. This differential association supports the hypothesis that vWF-Ag captures risk linked to the underlying hepatic disease that persists after resection but is attenuated following transplantation. vWF-Ag may complement conventional selection criteria by identifying patients with technically resectable HCC whose prognosis remains compromised by underlying liver disease, supporting prospective evaluation of its role in selecting between resection and transplantation.

title: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy: a genome-wide association meta-analysis and polygenic risk score.
authorString: Lopes LR, Aung N, Van Duijvenboden S, Nicholls HL, Burns R, Jager J, Lorenzini M, Akhtar MM, Protonotarios A, Barbeito-Caamaño C, Larrañaga-Moreira JM, Barriales-Villa R, Coley K, Batini C, Sze G, Tobin MD, John C, Petersen SE, Syrris P, Munroe PB, Elliott PM.

title: Adapting Echocardiographic Foundation Models for Detecting Pulmonary Embolism-Related Right-Heart Strain
authorString: Yang L, Ozkut Y, Bu Z, Li S, Yu C, Situ-LaCasse E, Acuna J, Yarnish A, Demant M, Adhikari SR, Yilmaz A.
abstractText: Pulmonary embolism (PE) is a time-sensitive medical emergency in which rapid recognition of right ventricular (RV) dysfunction by point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) can support early risk stratification. Here, we present HOPE (ecHO-Pulmonary Embolism), a real-world emergency cardiac POCUS video dataset comprising 4,069 patients with suspected PE, and EchoPE, a foundation-model-based video classification framework for detecting PE-associated right-heart phenotypes. HOPE includes five commonly acquired emergency echocardiographic views, with all positive PE cases confirmed by computed tomography pulmonary angiography. EchoPE builds on EchoPrime-pretrained echocardiographic representations and incorporates view recognition, task-specific adaptation, and attention-based interpretability. Experiments suggested that directly transferring EchoPrime representations to this disease-specific task provided limited performance, whereas EchoPE (AUROC 95.2 +/- 0.3) substantially outperformed both EchoPrime with a classification head (AUROC 87.6 +/- 1) and conventional video deep learning baselines. At a fixed sensitivity of 90%, EchoPE achieved a precision of 87.8, compared with 70.7 for EchoPrime. Among adaptation strategies, Low-Rank Adaptation combined with knowledge distillation provided the best balance between PE discrimination and preservation of pretrained echocardiographic semantics. Interpretability analyses showed that the adapted model focused on clinically relevant RV morphological changes, interventricular septal configuration, and informative temporal segments within ultrasound videos. Overall, HOPE and EchoPE demonstrate that echocardiographic foundation models require dataset-specific adaptation to identify PE-related right-heart strain and support the potential use of artificial intelligence-assisted bedside echocardiography for risk warning in acute care settings.

title: Estimated effects of plant- and animal-based protein food strategies on muscle function, strength and lean mass after 6 years: a target trial emulation in the Canadian Longitudinal Study on Aging
authorString: Brassard D, Glenn A, Chevalier S, Ruiz M, Li J, Tessier A.
abstractText:
Background:

Dietary guidelines emphasize the consumption of plant-based protein foods for cardiovascular health. However, it remains unclear how the balance of plant- and animal-based protein food consumption contributes to muscle health.

Objective:

Our objective was to estimate the effect of increasing the consumption of plant- (PLANT) relative to animal-based (ANIMAL) protein foods on physical function, including muscle function, strength, and lean mass, in middle-aged and older adults. We also examined the effects of increasing both protein sources (BOTH), within a healthy dietary pattern (HEALTHY), or limiting animal protein foods consumption (HEALTHY-P+).

Methods:

Non-experimental data from the Canadian Longitudinal Study on Aging (CLSA) comprehensive cohort were used to emulate a target trial. Middle-aged and older adults were followed for 6 years. Sociodemographic and diet data (frequency via the Short Diet Questionnaire) were assessed every three years. Objectively measured outcomes were muscle function (Timed Up&Go, 4-m walking speed, chair rise time), appendicular lean soft tissue (ALST) by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry and handgrip strength. The parametric g-formula was used to account for time-varying confounding and loss to follow-up.

Results:

A total of 21,636 participants were eligible (median [Q1-Q3] age, 62 [54-70] years; 49% female). Across all hypothetical interventions, the HEALTHY intervention consistently improved outcomes. Compared with no intervention, HEALTHY yielded the largest estimated differences: Timed Up&Go (-0.15 s; 95%CI: -0.24, -0.07), chair rise time (-0.03 s; 95%CI: -0.06, -0.01), handgrip strength (+0.5 kg; 95%CI: 0.3, 0.7), and ALST (+0.12 kg, 95%CI: 0.05-0.18). BOTH showed consistent but smaller effect estimates. Further limiting animal protein did not confer additional benefits. Interventions increasing PLANT or ANIMAL alone showed 95%CIs compatible with no effect. Effect estimate magnitudes were below clinically important differences.

Conclusion:

In middle-aged and older adults, findings suggest that a balanced approach to increasing consumption of both animal and plant-based protein foods may yield modest benefits for muscle health compared with no intervention, particularly within a healthy dietary pattern.

title: Transportability of polysomnography-derived sleep physiological fingerprints across cohorts, measurement modalities and time: a four-axis evaluation in four cohorts
authorString: Deng Q, Chen Y, Ma N, Lou X.
abstractText: Epidemiological evidence linking sleep to Alzheimer disease (AD) relies predominantly on self-reported sleep, whereas cohorts with polysomnography (PSG) and cohorts with AD biomarkers rarely share participants. Multifractal long-range-interdependency representations classify obstructive sleep apnoea severity accurately across cohorts, but whether such a physiological fingerprint can be transported between cohorts, between measurement modalities or over time has not been evaluated. We propose four axes of transportability and test them in the Sleep Heart Health Study (n = 5,614), MESA Sleep (n = 2,012), ADNI (n = 2,286) and MrOS Sleep (2,911 men; 1,026 re-examined after 6.37 years; 3,928 scored nights). Axis A1, cross-cohort construct convergence, passed: PSG-derived Sleep Coupling Disruption Index loadings agreed between SHHS and MESA (cosine 0.986; Wasserstein distance 0.0487). Axis A2, incremental validity beyond the apnoea-hypopnoea index, failed: the fully adjusted hazard ratio for incident cardiovascular disease was 1.009 (95% CI 0.941-1.085; p = 0.83) and the C-index was 0.8079 with or without the index; in MrOS, adding a multifractal coupling fingerprint increased R-squared by 0.00058 (likelihood-ratio p = 0.399). Axis A3, proxy identifiability, failed: the reliability ratio linking portable subjective complaints to objective physiological burden was 1.95 x 10-5, with a bootstrap 95% upper bound of 0.00261 and 0.0027 for a semantically optimised proxy, far below the 0.25 floor required for measurement-error correction. Under classical error this implies a 370-fold sample-size inflation; Monte-Carlo power at n = 10,000 was 0.177. A nominally significant association between night-time behaviour and dementia severity would require an implausible true physiological effect of 28.7 standard deviations, and it reversed to -0.0554 after adjustment for total neuropsychiatric burden. The prespecified ADNI primary outcome, plasma pTau217, was null (beta = 0.0033, p = 0.911), as were the MrOS six-year cognitive complaint outcome (beta = -0.0204, p = 0.375) and a 35-event self-reported dementia endpoint (OR = 0.921, p = 0.679). Axis A4, temporal stability, failed: six-year test-retest reliability was r = 0.157 (95% CI 0.096-0.216) for the fingerprint versus r = 0.455 (0.405-0.502) for AHI, despite stable concurrent validity (rho = 0.380 and 0.328 with same-night AHI). Spearman-Brown projection indicates that approximately nine nights must be averaged for the fingerprint to reach a reliability of 0.60, compared with two for AHI. A fingerprint can therefore be reproducible without being transportable. We provide a four-question decision workflow and an eight-item minimum reporting set; subjective sleep complaints should not be substituted for objective sleep physiology in aetiological inference.

title: Calcification Topology Governs Fibrous-Cap Stress in Coronary Plaque: From Finite-Element Analysis to a Fast Surrogate for Digital Twins
authorString: Gharaibeh Y, Lee J, Rababah A, Ghanem R, Al-Ma’aitah M, Wilson DL.
abstractText: Rupture of the thin fibrous cap over a coronary plaque most often causes acute coronary syndromes. Its highest tensile stress (peak cap stress, PCS) is the main mechanical indicator of rupture risk. Calcium is paradoxical: more coronary calcium predicts more events, yet heavily calcified plaques are often stable, whereas spotty calcium is common in culprit plaques. We developed an idealized two-dimensional finite-element model of a coronary thin-cap fibroatheroma (TCFA), verified against analytical solutions. From a baseline TCFA (65 μm cap, 120 mmHg), we varied one feature at a time: calcification depth, arc, and stiffness; cap thickness; necrotic-core size; and blood pressure. A gradient-boosted surrogate was trained on 3000 simulated lesions to predict PCS from imaging-measurable morphology. Moving an identical calcification from deep to superficial raised PCS 3.6-fold (65 to 231 kPa), whereas deep calcification lowered PCS by 41% versus no calcium. Superficial calcification raised PCS only while its lateral edge terminated beneath the cap. On held-out lesions, the surrogate predicted PCS with R² = 0.93, about 10,000 times faster than finite-element analysis. In this idealized model, calcification depth and edge termination, rather than calcium burden, govern fibrous-cap stress, and a fast surrogate makes these mechanics usable within digital twins.

title: Primary Mönckeberg Medial Sclerosis: 30-Year Follow-Up and Whole-Genome Sequencing.
authorString: Lanzer P, Markus A.
abstractText:
Background

Mönckeberg medial sclerosis (MMS) usually accompanies diabetes mellitus or chronic kidney disease and carries a high cardiovascular risk; primary forms are rare and genetically uncharacterized.

Case summary

In 1996, advanced MMS was found incidentally in a 46-year-old man without procalcific risk factors. At 30-year follow-up, he remained asymptomatic. Color-coded duplex ultrasonography and photon-counting detector computed tomography (PCD-CT) showed severe medial calcification from the abdominal aorta to the below-the-knee arteries without hemodynamically relevant stenosis, and arterial stiffness was increased. Whole-genome sequencing found no rare variant in 6 calcification genes; a coronary calcification polygenic score was at the 98.8th percentile.

Discussion

Primary MMS may follow a benign course distinct from secondary forms, possibly reflecting a different pathogenesis. A negative targeted genome analysis does not exclude a genetic cause.

Take-home messages

Medial calcification without diabetes or kidney disease can remain clinically silent for decades. Family segregation and cohort studies are required to define its genetic basis.

title: Prediction of Acetaminophen-Induced Hepatotoxicity in Acetylcysteine-Treated Patients Using Routine Admission Biomarkers.
authorString: Humphries C, Kilpatrick AM, Addison ML, Cartwright JA, Lyall MJ, Schumacher LJ, Forbes SJ, Dear JW.
abstractText:
Study objective

Some acetaminophen-overdose patients develop hepatotoxicity despite acetylcysteine treatment. Established tools struggle to prospectively identify subsequent toxicity. We developed a model using only routine admission biomarkers to identify acetylcysteine-treated patients at highest risk and compared it with the current benchmark, the acetaminophen-aminotransferase multiplication product (AT product).

Methods

Retrospective cohort study of acetaminophen overdose admissions aged 12 years and older (International Classification of Diseases 10th revision code of T39.1) with alanine aminotransferase (ALT) ≤1,000 U/L at admission from 3 UK hospitals (2008-2024). We fitted elastic-net logistic models stratified by presentation ALT. The outcome was peak ALT >1,000 U/L. Performance was assessed on a 25% held-out test set and benchmarked against the AT product >1,500.

Results

Of 4,705 admissions, 119 (2.5%) developed hepatotoxicity. The model used 7 routine blood tests, 4 per stratum. At presentation, those with ALT ≤50 U/L, acetaminophen, sodium, potassium, and lymphocyte count remained in the model. In those with ALT 51 to 1,000 U/L at presentation, ALT, bilirubin, alkaline phosphatase, and lymphocyte count were used. In the test set (n=1,175), it achieved an area under the curve of 0.93 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.89 to 0.97) versus 0.82 (0.72 to 0.91) for the AT product (paired difference 0.11; 95% CI 0.01 to 0.22; P=.03), with higher specificity and a higher positive likelihood ratio at every matched sensitivity. The model had a specificity of 82.5%, whereas an AT product > 1,500 had a specificity of 62.6%. The model positive likelihood ratio was 5.1 versus 2.4 for the AT product, with half the number of false-positive escalations (171 versus 365 per 1,000 patients).

Conclusion

A stratified model using only routine admission biomarkers (the Edinburgh Risk Score) identifies acetylcysteine-treated patients at the highest residual hepatotoxicity risk, outperforming the AT product >1,500 across decision thresholds, supporting selection for intensified therapy.

title: Frequency and Causes of Waveform Capnography Failure After Successful Emergency Tracheal Intubation.
authorString: Driver BE, Robinson AE, Kuo J, Prekker ME.
abstractText:
Study objective

Multidisciplinary guidelines recommend waveform capnography as the preferred method for determining endotracheal tube location after intubation and advise immediate tube removal when the waveform is absent or inadequate unless a fault can be immediately identified and corrected. Because capnography depends on several components that can each fail, an absent waveform does not always indicate an esophageal tube, and removing a correctly placed tube exposes a critically ill patient to the risks of reintubation. How often waveform capnography fails despite correct tracheal placement has been estimated only from trials of colorimetric detectors in populations with high proportions of cardiac arrest, and the causes have not been described.

Methods

We performed a retrospective analysis of a prospectively collected continuous quality improvement database of emergency intubations at an urban, safety-net hospital, including patients aged ≥14 years intubated between January 1, 2022, and April 21, 2025. Trained observers collected intubation data in real time, and the intubating physician completed a structured form after each procedure. The primary outcome was CO2 waveform failure following successful tracheal intubation. Secondary outcomes were the reported cause of failure and whether the tube was removed.

Results

Of 2,875 successful tracheal intubation procedures, 124 (4.3%; 95% confidence interval 3.6 to 5.1%) had CO2 waveform failure despite the tube being located in the trachea. Human error accounted for 83 events (67%), nearly all of which were from the CO2 sampling line not being connected to the bag or the monitor (82 events, 66%). Identified equipment failure accounted for 11 events (9%). The cause was undetermined in 33 events (27%), including 30 (24%) in which the failure was never explained despite confirmed tracheal placement and 3 in which the cause was not formally categorized. The endotracheal tube was removed because of the absent waveform in 1 event (1%).

Conclusion

CO2 waveform failure occurred in approximately 4% of successful intubation procedures.

title: Dual-Chamber Leadless Pacemaker Implantation in Dextrocardia With Situs Inversus.
authorString: Ito N, Aizawa Y, Kobayashi M, Hirayama H, Okajima S, Fujimoto Y, Murata H, Yodogawa K, Asai K, Iwasaki YK.
abstractText:
Background

Dextrocardia with situs inversus presents unique anatomical challenges for cardiac device implantation. AVEIR DR dual-chamber leadless pacemaker system implantation has not previously been reported in this setting.

Case summary

An 84-year-old man with dextrocardia and situs inversus underwent AVEIR DR dual-chamber leadless pacemaker system implantation for symptomatic bradycardia. Preprocedural 3-dimensional computed tomography merged with intraprocedural fluoroscopy, together with right atrial contrast angiography and fluoroscopic guidance, facilitated successful implantation of both devices. The procedure was completed without complications, and the subsequent clinical course was uneventful.

Discussion

To the best of our knowledge, this is the first reported experience of AVEIR DR dual-chamber leadless pacemaker system implantation in a patient with dextrocardia and situs inversus totalis.

Take-home message

Careful preprocedural anatomical planning, catheter manipulation adapted to mirror-image anatomy, and a systematic implantation strategy enabled successful dual-chamber leadless pacemaker implantation in a patient with dextrocardia and situs inversus.

title: Glucocorticoid-Induced Diabetes Mellitus in Tunisia: Incidence and Risk Factors in a Retrospective Cohort Study
authorString: Bel Haj Hassen Y, Ben Nacef I, Kefi A.
abstractText:
ackground: Glucocorticoid-induced diabetes mellitus (GIDM) is a frequent but under-documented complication of systemic corticosteroid therapy. We aimed to estimate its incidence and identify patient- and treatment-related risk factors.

Methods:

We conducted a retrospective, single-centre cohort study in the Department of Endocrinology and Internal Medicine A, Charles Nicolle Hospital, Tunis, between January 2000 and December 2020. Ninety-five adults without known diabetes (baseline HbA1c < 6.5%) starting corticosteroid therapy were followed for GIDM. Univariate predictors (p < 0.05) were entered into a multivariable model.

Results:

Mean age was 42.6 years (M/F ratio 0.79). GIDM developed in 57 of 95 patients (60%), after a median of 20 days (range 7-120); 40% of cases occurred within the first month. The median initial dose was 60 mg/day prednisone-equivalent, and 84% received high-dose therapy. On univariate analysis, older age, family history of type 2 diabetes, higher baseline fasting glucose, higher body weight, and methylprednisolone boluses were associated with GIDM; sex, body mass index and hypertension were not. After adjustment, only family history of type 2 diabetes (RR 1.75, 95% CI 1.18-2.61) and higher baseline fasting glucose (RR 1.37 per 1 mmol/L, 95% CI 1.07-1.75) remained independent predictors.

Conclusion:

GIDM occurred in three-fifths of patients, usually within the first month of therapy. Family history of type 2 diabetes and baseline fasting glucose independently identify patients warranting glycaemic surveillance from treatment initiation.

Keywords:

diabetes mellitus; glucocorticoids; corticosteroids; risk factors; cohort study.

title: External validation of the EK-LEF electrocardiogram model for left ventricular systolic dysfunction in three U.S. health systems
authorString: Malinkovich J, Leshchiner M, Knight B, Gong J, Sinha T.
abstractText:
Background:

Heart failure is projected to affect more than 11 million U.S. adults by 2050, and reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) can be present before symptoms appear. Deep learning models can detect reduced LVEF from the 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG), but most have been tested only in the institutions that developed them, often after excluding patients with prior heart failure or recordings of poor quality. We evaluated EK-LEF, a self-supervised ECG model fine-tuned on low LVEF detection.

Methods:

A bidirectional Mamba encoder was pre-trained on 435,420 unlabeled MIMIC-IV ECGs and fine-tuned on 471,248 ECG–echocardiogram pairs from 235,969 patients at Mayo Clinic Rochester and the Mayo Clinic Health System. Mayo Clinic Florida served as the validation set and Mayo Clinic Arizona, a geographically distinct region, as the internal test set, each evaluated with one pair per patient. For external validation, Dandelion Health ran the model on one ECG from each of 17,500 patients at five hospitals in three U.S. health systems. The reference standard was LVEF ≤ 40% on transthoracic echocardiography within 15 days of the ECG. The primary outcomes were sensitivity and specificity.

Results:

In the Florida validation set of 14,880 patients, 9.9% of whom had LVEF ≤ 40%, the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) was 0.951 (95% CI 0.947–0.955). In the Arizona internal test set of 16,298 patients (prevalence 9.2%), it was 0.955 (0.950–0.959), with a sensitivity of 85.0% (83.1–86.8) and a specificity of 91.7% (91.3–92.2). The signal-quality rule excluded 2.2% of internal test recordings and 0.9% of external ECGs. Among the 17,344 external patients, of whom 9.4% had LVEF ≤ 40%, the model reached an AUROC of 0.912 (0.906–0.919), a sensitivity of 85.7% (84.1–87.4) and a specificity of 81.8% (81.3–82.4), and its negative predictive value was 98.2% (98.0–98.5). Sensitivity ranged from 79.5% to 90.2% between hospitals, and specificity was lowest in patients with a recorded cardiomyopathy (56.1%).

Conclusions:

EK-LEF retained high sensitivity and specificity at hospitals outside the health system in which it was developed. A negative result may help identify patients who do not need echocardiography.

title: Co-occurrence Is Not Evidence: Separating Protein-Disease Findings from Incidental Mentions in HFpEF Literature
authorString: Azat A, De Santana Junior CJ, Cadeiras M, Liem DA.
abstractText: Literature-mining pipelines such as CaseOLAP rank proteins by how often they appear next to a disease term. Appearing next to a disease is not the same as being implicated in it: in our 300-sentence held-out set of PubMed sentences that mention a protein and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), only 115 assert a biological association. The rest report a negative finding or mention the protein in passing, for example as a drug the patients were taking.  We train a sentence-level filter that sorts each protein mention into associated, not_associated or incidental. It is a fine-tuned PubMedBERT trained with class-weighted cross-entropy and R-Drop regularization, combined into a six-model majority-vote ensemble over three random seeds. On the held-out set, with no thresholds tuned on it, the ensemble reaches 85.3% accuracy and 86.1% macro F1 (bootstrap 95% confidence intervals 81.0-89.3% and 82.1-89.7%), against 38.3% accuracy for the co-occurrence baseline, which counts every mention as an association. Single models average 84.4 +/- 0.7% accuracy across seeds. Run after CaseOLAP, the filter removes protein mentions that are not evidence of association from the HFpEF candidate list.  Where the ensemble's majority vote disagreed with the annotation, the annotation was often wrong. Expert review of those sentences corrected 53 of 88 flagged evaluation labels and 109 training labels. Most of the errors came from one flaw in the annotation sheet: in sentences naming several proteins, it did not say which protein the label was for. The audit stage coincided with the largest accuracy gain in the project, but the same stage also changed the evaluation labels and the training loss, so we report it as a chronology, not as a controlled result.

title: Regional brain-age gaps reveal a shared polygenic architecture and regionally patterned clinical and cell-type associations
authorString: Hwang Y, Park K, Lee S.
abstractText: A single brain-age estimate may obscure regional differences in clinical vulnerability. Using voxel-level deep learning, we derived whole-brain and nine regional brain-age gaps (BAGs) spanning cortical, subcortical and cerebellar regions from T1-weighted MRI in 46,254 UK Biobank participants. Genetic correlation estimates in 41,067 participants (rg = 0.56-0.93) exceeded phenotypic correlations across all 45 pairs, yet regional profiles varied across 24 hospital-recorded diagnoses. Oligodendrocyte annotations predominated for whole-brain and cerebellar BAGs, whereas annotations for caudate BAG included astrocyte and vascular classes. In the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative, temporal BAG showed stronger associations with cerebrospinal fluid Aβ42 and cognition than whole-brain BAG when modelled together. A regional model modestly improved discrimination of observed conversion from mild cognitive impairment to Alzheimer's disease during available follow-up compared with a whole-brain model. Polygenic scores showed cross-cohort associations with hypertension and osteoporosis. Regional BAGs provide complementary clinical information within a shared polygenic architecture.

title: Overview of Health Status among Roma Population in Romania: A Scoping Review
authorString: Mangaloiu DV, Bratu EC, Raris-Fierbinteanu CM, Furtunescu FL.
abstractText:
Background:

Roma are widely recognized as Europe ‘s largest ethnic minority and in-dependent estimates suggest that up to two million people live in Romania. Despite well-documented socioeconomic disadvantage, no prior review has synthesized evi-dence on the health status of Roma in Romania.

Objectives:

This scoping review mapped the literature on healthcare access, quality of life, chronic disease burden and communicable disease exposure among Roma communities in Romania.

Methods:

Us-ing the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and PRISMA-ScR guidelines, we con-ducted a systematic search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, Science Direct and supplemented by grey literature and reference-list screening, for studies published 2010–2025 in English or Romanian.

Results:

Thirty-nine sources (35 studies and 4 in-stitutional reports) met the inclusion criteria. Roma communities experience a life-expectancy gap of 3.5–4.6 years, markedly lower preventive-care uptake (39% vs 71% in the general population), and high rates of being uninsured (42–59%). Chronic disease burden was substantially higher than in the general population: hypertension prevalence ranged 33–67%, type 2 diabetes from 10–29%, and obesity from 32–62%, with evidence of earlier onset and more severe complications, including higher pro-gression to chronic kidney disease and end-stage renal disease. Health-related quality of life and mental health indicators were uniformly worse among Roma. Evidence on communicable diseases was sparse but suggested elevated hepatitis B/C prevalence and greater severity of measles and COVID-19.

Conclusions:

Roma communities in Romania experience markedly poorer health outcomes across nearly all domains ex-amined, driven by intersecting socioeconomic, structural and behavioral determinants.

title: Atrial Fibrillation, Atrial Flutter, and Orthodromic Atrioventricular Re-Entrant Tachycardia With a Concealed Left-Sided Accessory Pathway.
authorString: Roy D, Chilton R, Nungaray E, Estrada A, George S, Mullin J.
abstractText:
Background

Accessory pathway (AP)-mediated tachycardias are a common cause of supraventricular tachycardia; however, their relationship with atrial fibrillation (AF) and atrial flutter (AFL) is often under-recognized.

Case summary

A 61-year-old man presented with recurrent narrow-complex tachycardia, AF, and typical AFL occurring in close temporal proximity. An electrophysiology study demonstrated inducible orthodromic atrioventricular re-entrant tachycardia with eccentric retrograde atrial activation, consistent with a concealed left inferoposterior AP. The pathway was successfully ablated. At 9-month follow-up, there was no recurrence of AF, AFL, or supraventricular tachycardia.

Discussion

Prior studies suggest APs may facilitate atrial arrhythmogenesis. This case highlights the interplay between atrioventricular re-entrant tachycardia and atrial arrhythmias and the importance of recognizing multiple mechanisms in a single patient.

Take-home messages

Concealed APs may trigger AF and AFL. Targeted ablation can eliminate multiple arrhythmias.

title: Wearable Tissue Oximetry in Cardiogenic Shock: Microcirculatory Deterioration Preceding Macrohemodynamic Collapse.
authorString: Roumengous T, Chauntry AJ, Baran DA.
abstractText:
Background

Cardiogenic shock can progress rapidly, even when conventional macrohemodynamic vital signs remain stable. Continuous, noninvasive microcirculatory monitoring is uncommon but could provide early signals of impending decompensation.

Fih/early reports summary

The authors report near-infrared spectroscopy and photoplethysmography monitoring with the investigational NIRSense Envello Core wearable device. The patient was a 66-year-old man with complex valvular disease and combined pre/post capillary pulmonary hypertension, who rapidly deteriorated and died despite intensive care unit management.

Discussion

Chest-derived tissue oxygen saturation and perfusion index appeared to signal deterioration ∼4 hours before clinically recognized collapse, and correlated strongly with central venous pressure (r = -0.95; perfusion index) and systolic pulmonary artery pressure (r = 0.87; tissue oxygen saturation).

Novelty

To our knowledge, this is the first continuous microcirculatory characterization of the transition to terminal cardiogenic shock using a wearable near-infrared spectroscopy and photoplethysmography device.

Take-home message

Noninvasive microcirculatory monitoring may detect hemodynamic collapse before conventional vital signs, identifying a potential window for earlier intervention.

title: Blood pressure changes throughout pregnancy as predictors of preeclampsia: a prospective cohort study of low-risk nulliparous individuals.
authorString: Cloutier RM, Dansereau S, Dupont R, Jacques C, Guerby P, Bujold E, Boutin A.

journal.title: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology Canada : JOGC = Journal d'obstetrique et gynecologie du Canada : JOGC

abstractText: Among 835 nulliparous patients who were seen once at each trimester, systolic, diastolic and mean arterial blood pressure (MAP), measured twice on both arms using an automated device after >5 minutes of rest, were stronger predictors of preeclampsia than clinical factors (P < 0.01). At 30-34 weeks, a MAP above 90 mmHg or an increase in MAP of more than 10 mmHg (compared to 11-14 weeks) could have predicted 67% (20/30) of preeclampsia cases, including all (7/7) deliveries with preeclampsia between 32 and 37 weeks. Measuring blood pressure using an automated device and following a rigorous protocol is highly effective to predict preeclampsia at each trimester of pregnancy.

title: Targeted NIRF-OCT Imaging of Inflammatory Atherosclerotic Plaques Using Donor-Acceptor Nanoprobes.
authorString: Huang X, Hou X, Yang F, Wang Z, Wang Z, Ou C, Qu X, Tu S.
abstractText: Current intravascular imaging modalities lack biological insight into atherosclerotic plaque inflammation, a key driver of plaque vulnerability. To address this limitation, we developed a targeted molecular probe for near-infrared fluorescence (NIRF) imaging, integrated with optical coherence tomography (OCT) within a dual-modality catheter. This approach enables co-registered structural and molecular visualization of high-risk inflammatory plaques by detecting osteopontin (OPN)-rich regions associated with macrophage-derived foam cells. We synthesized a planar donor-acceptor small-molecule probe, termed DMe-DFIC, and formulated it into nanoparticles (NPs) exhibiting broad absorption from 600 to 800 nm and near-infrared emission from 900 to 1300 nm. Following conjugation with an anti-OPN antibody, the resulting targeted formulation, designated OPDD NPs, showed preferential accumulation in atherosclerotic iliac-femoral arteries, with fluorescence intensity peaking 12 h after injection. In vivo multimodal NIRF-OCT imaging showed that elevated fluorescence signals were observed in regions exhibiting lipid-associated OCT morphology. Histopathological analyses further confirmed that these regions exhibited substantial lipid deposition, intense OPN expression, and dense macrophage infiltration. Collectively, the integration of targeted OPDD NPs with dual-modality NIRF-OCT imaging provides synchronized structural and molecular characterization of inflammatory plaques, supporting further preclinical evaluation of this approach for inflammation-associated molecular imaging.

title: Successful Double-Valve Replacement in an Adult with Mucopolysaccharidosis VI: A Case Report.
authorString: Hoshina Y, Mishima T, Suzuki S, Onishi R, Okubo Y, Okamoto T, Tosaka Y, Shiraishi S, Tsuchida M.
abstractText:
Introduction

Mucopolysaccharidosis VI (MPS VI) is a rare lysosomal storage disorder involving progressive systemic manifestations, including valvular heart disease. Double-valve replacement (DVR) for MPS VI is rarely reported, and its perioperative management is challenging because of airway and respiratory involvement. This report describes a patient with MPS VI successfully treated with DVR, highlighting perioperative strategies that contributed to a favorable outcome.

Case presentation

A 37-year-old woman with MPS VI (height: 105 cm, weight: 26 kg), who underwent hematopoietic stem cell transplantation and permanent tracheostomy, developed dyspnea associated with aortic regurgitation (AR) and mitral regurgitation (MR). Eventually, she underwent elective DVR along with enzyme replacement therapy. Despite careful airway and respiratory management, pneumonia occurred postoperatively but resolved with antibiotics. She was discharged in good condition on POD 43. At 16 months after surgery, she remained free of heart failure and respiratory failure.

Conclusions

DVR can be performed successfully in adults with MPS VI. Careful perioperative airway and respiratory management is essential, and a preexisting tracheostomy may help secure the upper airway but does not eliminate postoperative pulmonary risk.

title: NLRP3 Inhibition in the Modern Era: Advancing Targeted Pharmacology and Precision Medicine for Cardio-neuroinflammatory Disorders.
authorString: Shafi T, Chandra Pati J, Rana R, Islam MM, Khan MDN, Judder MI, Jain H, Kapil M, Gulati P.
abstractText:
Introduction

The NLRP3 inflammasome is a crucial component of innate immunity and inflammation, triggering caspase-1 activation and facilitating the maturation and release of pro-inflammatory cytokines such as IL-1β and IL-18. Dysregulated activation of NLRP3 is involved in the pathogenesis of cardiovascular, neurological, and metabolic diseases such as myocardial infarction, heart failure, atherosclerosis, stroke, Alzheimer's disease, and diabetic complications. Thus, the inhibition of NLRP3 could be a potential therapeutic approach for chronic inflammation- associated diseases.

Methods

This review summarizes the recent advances in the discovery, preclinical evaluation, and clinical translation of NLRP3 inflammasome inhibitors, with a particular emphasis on smallmolecule agents, including MCC950, dapansutrile (OLT1177), NT-0796, and emerging nextgeneration inhibitors.

Results

Preclinical and preliminary studies in the early phases of clinical trials suggest that NLRP3 inhibition may lead to inhibition of inflammatory signaling, decrease tissue damage, ameliorate cardiovascular outcomes, and offer neuroprotective properties. In contrast with antiinflammatory drugs with a broad spectrum of activity, selective inhibitors of NLRP3 may have higher mechanistic specificity and greater tolerability.

Discussion

Research is currently directed toward improving blood-brain barrier permeability, reducing off-target effects, identifying NLRP3 variants that are associated with resistance, and incorporating patient stratification by biomarkers to better facilitate precision medicine.

Conclusion

Inhibition of the NLRP3 inflammasome is a potential therapeutic target in cardiovascular, neurodegenerative, and metabolic diseases. Ongoing translational research efforts and carefully designed clinical trials are needed to validate their long-term effectiveness, safety, and promise for individualized treatment.

title: Bisphenol A Triggers Macrophage Ferroptosis to Exacerbate Atherosclerotic Lesion Progression by Nuclear Factor-Kappa B (NF-κB) Activation.
authorString: Li Q, Wu Y, Wu X, Li X, Lin L, Xu J, Ye R, Wang X, Li M, Weng L, Wang L, Wu N.
abstractText: BPA, an environmental endocrine disruptor, has been implicated in the progression of atherosclerosis (AS), with evidence suggesting macrophage ferroptosis as a key mechanistic link. This study explored BPA's effects on ferroptosis and inflammatory signaling in ApoE-deficient mice (in vivo) and RAW 264.7 cells (in vitro). In vivo, ApoE-deficient mice modeling AS administered BPA for 3 weeks. Total cholesterol (TC), triglyceride (TG), low density lipoprotein (LDL) and high-density lipoprotein (HDL) of serum were measured by enzymatic method. The plaque area of aortic sinus was analyzed by Hematoxylin-Eosin (HE) staining. The glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) expression of aortic sinuses was analyzed by immunohistochemistry (IHC). In vitro, RAW 264.7 macrophages were treated with BPA and ferroptosis inhibitor ferrostatin-1 (Fer-1) or NF-κB inhibitor JSH-23. Ferroptosis markers (Fe<sup>2</sup>⁺, malondialdehyde (MDA), reactive oxygen species (ROS) and glutathione (GSH)) and proinflammatory cytokine (interleukin 6 (IL-6) and tumor necrosis factor α (TNFα)) were measured using microplate reader. GPX4 and NF-κB expression were analyzed by Western blot and quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR). In mice treated with BPA, the plaque area, TG, LDL, TC, IL-6 and TNFα were increased; GPX4 expression was downregulated compared with control (p < 0.05, separately). In vitro investigations using RAW 264.7 macrophages demonstrated that BPA exposure induced hallmarks of ferroptosis, including iron overload, oxidative stress (elevated ROS and MDA), glutathione (GSH) depletion (p < 0.05, separately), and downregulation of GPX4 (p < 0.05). Concurrently, BPA promoted macrophage polarization toward the proinflammatory M1 type and activated the NF-κB pathway, amplifying inflammatory cytokine release (p < 0.05, separately). Pharmacological inhibition of ferroptosis attenuated ferroptosis of macrophages induced by BPA (p < 0.05, separately), while NF-κB suppression (JSH-23) mitigated inflammatory activation and ferroptotic cell death (p < 0.05). These findings collectively propose a mechanism wherein BPA could exacerbate AS by driving macrophage ferroptosis through NF-κB-dependent oxidative, M1-type polarization and inflammatory cascades.

title: Hemifacial Pigmentation With Retinal, Facial, and Cerebral Arteriovenous Malformations in Wyburn-Mason Syndrome Misinterpreted as Harlequin Syndrome.
authorString: Bechara Ghobril A, Botros S, Shields CL.

journal.title: Journal of pediatric ophthalmology and strabismus

abstractText: An 8-year-old boy with hemifacial color asymmetry mimicking Harlequin syndrome had unilateral vision loss and retinal racemose hemangioma. Magnetic resonance imaging revealed orbital and intracranial arteriovenous malformations, establishing Wyburn-Mason syndrome. Consensus favored conservative surveillance. This case highlights that Harlequin-like presentations with ocular or cutaneous vascular anomalies warrant evaluation and neuroimaging.

title: Sudden Cardiac Arrest As the Initial Presentation of Anomalous Left Coronary Artery Originating From the Pulmonary Artery in a Young Adult: A Case Report.
authorString: Shrestha B, Hey CY, Neoh S.
abstractText: Anomalous left coronary artery from the pulmonary artery (ALCAPA) is a rare congenital heart condition associated with high childhood mortality if untreated. Consequently, diagnosis in asymptomatic adults is exceedingly uncommon. We report a 21-year-old gentleman brought to hospital via the primary percutaneous coronary intervention service after an out-of-hospital ventricular fibrillation arrest while hiking. Following prehospital cardiopulmonary resuscitation and defibrillation, return of spontaneous circulation was achieved; an immediate 12-lead electrocardiogram showed ST elevation. Initial transthoracic echocardiography revealed abnormal myocardial color Doppler flow, suggesting intercoronary collaterals and raising suspicion of a coronary anomaly. Coronary angiography confirmed ALCAPA. He underwent successful reimplantation surgery. Given myocardial fibrosis on cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, a subcutaneous implantable cardioverter-defibrillator was implanted for secondary prevention. Sudden cardiac arrest as the initial presenting symptom is exceedingly rare in an asymptomatic young adult with ALCAPA. High clinical suspicion supports early diagnosis. Multi-modality imaging remains central to diagnosis and device-therapy decisions after corrective surgery.

title: Atrial Septal Defect Repair After Reverse Potts Shunt for Severe Pulmonary Hypertension.
authorString: Miller PC, Miller JR, Balzer DT, Grady RM, Eghtesady P.
abstractText:
Background

Atrial septal defect (ASD) closure in the presence of a functioning reverse Potts shunt (rPS) for pulmonary hypertension (PH) may reduce global hypoxemia without sacrificing right ventricular pressure unloading. However, intracardiac operation after rPS has not previously been reported to guide operative decision-making in this scenario.

Case summary

A 13-year-old girl with a history of rPS for PH presented for ASD closure because of hypoxia and exercise intolerance. To safely close the ASD on cardiopulmonary bypass, the rPS was occluded with a catheter-based balloon.

Discussion

Coexisting ASD and rPS in a patient with severe PH presents a complex hemodynamic scenario. Furthermore, intracardiac operation in the setting of patent rPS and PH presents certain technical challenges. Multidisciplinary care is necessary for safe and effective management of coexisting ASD and rPS.

Take-home message

Balloon occlusion of reverse Potts shunt can be safely performed in select patients to expand feasibility for repair of intracardiac defects in PH.

title: Correction to "Cerebral hemodynamic changes during cardiac surgery: a feasibility MR study in piglets".
Support to Address Excess Weight and Related Physical Health Conditions for Young People With Severe Mental Illness: A Systematic Review With Narrative and Thematic Synthesis.
authorString: Sermin-Reed L, Mills S.

journal.title: Journal of human nutrition and dietetics : the official journal of the British Dietetic Association

abstractText:
Background

Young people with severe mental illness (SMI: psychosis, schizophrenia, and bipolar disorder) are at increased risk of experiencing excess weight and related health conditions, such as cardiovascular disease and Type 2 diabetes. Modifiable behavioural factors and antipsychotic-induced weight gain contribute to this risk. Earlier intervention to prevent and mitigate weight gain provides potential opportunity to improve long-term mental and physical health outcomes in this population.

Aim

To review support provided for young people with SMI, to address excess weight and related physical health conditions.

Methods

Three electronic databases were searched from January 2010 up to December 2025. Grey literature sources, and references and citations of included material were also searched. Full papers presenting qualitative or quantitative data on young people aged 12-18 years with SMI from high/very high development index countries were eligible for inclusion. Risk of bias for included studies was assessed using a validated tool for each study design. Data were synthesised through narrative and thematic synthesis.

Results

Seventeen articles describing 15 unique studies met inclusion criteria. Of the 12 included quantitative articles, five reported behavioural interventions, four reported pharmacological interventions, two reported a combination of these, and one reported a survey of barriers associated with metabolic monitoring. Of the five included qualitative articles, three explored healthcare practitioners' perspectives on metabolic monitoring, and two described participants' experiences of two of the included behavioural interventions. Behavioural interventions showed no statistically significant effects on weight outcomes, although participants reported positive behavioural changes. Pharmacological interventions also demonstrated limited effectiveness in reducing weight-related outcomes, although some evidence suggested attenuation of weight gain. Combined interventions, including metformin or antipsychotic switching plus healthy lifestyle education, provided the strongest evidence of effectiveness, significantly reducing BMI z-scores at 24 weeks. For metabolic monitoring, multi-factorial barriers were identified at the level of patient, provider, and organisation, which could potentially be mitigated through improved training and resources.

Conclusion

Metformin or switching to a lower risk antipsychotic medication, alongside a healthy lifestyle intervention, may be effective to address excess weight in young people with SMI. However, the evidence base is limited by small sample sizes and short follow-up periods. Further robust research is needed to establish the long-term effectiveness and sustainability of interventions.

title: Levistilide A restrains myocardial fibrosis by targeting malate dehydrogenase 2.
authorString: Pan T, Cheng Y, Yan Y, Cao W, Jiang Q, Li P, Zeng H.
abstractText: Myocardial fibrosis is a crucial pathological process of multiple cardiovascular diseases, yet effective therapies remain limited. Levistilide A (LA) is a bioactive constituent derived from the dried rhizome of Ligusticum chuanxiong Hort. (known as Chuanxiong in traditional Chinese medicine) with potential cardioprotective activities, but its therapeutic efficacy against myocardial fibrosis and the underlying molecular targets remain elusive. Here, we show that LA inhibits TGF-β1-induced fibroblast transformation and proliferation in vitro and alleviates myocardial fibrosis in a mouse model following myocardial infarction. By using drug affinity responsive target stability (DARTS), proteomics, and surface plasmon resonance (SPR) approaches, we identify mitochondrial malate dehydrogenase 2 (MDH2) as a putative molecular target of LA. Mechanistically, LA directly binds to MDH2 and suppresses its TGF-β1-induced phosphorylation, thereby inhibiting MDH2 enzymatic activation. This leads to the blockage of the malate-aspartate shuttle (MAS), thereby suppressing the enhanced mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) and ultimately inhibiting fibroblast transformation and myocardial fibrosis. Therefore, our findings reveal that LA alleviates myocardial fibrosis through targeting MDH2-mediated mitochondrial metabolic reprogramming, highlighting MDH2 as a potential therapeutic target and LA as an active compound in the treatment of myocardial fibrosis.

title: Emergency department management of pediatric traumatic arrest.
authorString: Wiltjer R, Wang J.
abstractText: More than 20% of pediatric out-of-hospital arrests are secondary to trauma. It is uncommon for children with traumatic arrest to regain spontaneous circulation, with reported mortality rates typically >90%. Hemorrhage control, early blood administration, and evaluation for reversible causes of arrest should be prioritized. Clinicians should avoid prolongation of resuscitation when efforts are unlikely to be successful, such as when patients have unwitnessed arrest or no signs of life on initial evaluation. This review discusses the most common reversible causes of traumatic arrest as well as important and controversial aspects of treatment, including resuscitative endovascular balloon occlusion of the aorta and emergency department resuscitative thoracotomy. It also addresses which patients are most likely to benefit from resuscitation, how to decide when to terminate resuscitation, and how to debrief after resuscitation.

title: The cost of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease in Australia: estimates from linked state-based health data.
authorString: Randall S, Shakya S, Lee C, Asiamah-Asare B, Gao L, Frith M, Varhol R, Carr MG, Ramakrishnan S, Boyd J, Robinson S.
abstractText:
Objectives

Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a leading cause of acute hospitalisations in Australia, yet its true health system cost is poorly defined. We estimated the direct healthcare costs attributable to COPD using linked primary and secondary care data.

Methods

A cross-sectional analysis of linked general practice, hospital, emergency department and mortality records from Western Australia was conducted. Individuals with COPD who were alive in 2021 were identified from primary care diagnoses, hospital records (International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision, Australian Modification J44) or spirometry recording. Each COPD case was matched to one individual without COPD on age, sex, smoking status and history of atherosclerosis. Direct healthcare costs were calculated from a government payer perspective, including hospitalisations, emergency presentations, general practice services, prescribed medicines, ambulance transport and pathology testing.

Results

The cohort included 6811 patients with COPD (median age 69 years; 51% female) and 6811 matched controls. Individuals with COPD had A$6584 higher adjusted annual healthcare costs than matched controls, with excess costs driven largely by hospitalisations. Hospitalisations accounted for 68% of attributable costs, followed by emergency presentations (17%) and medications (7%). Nationally, COPD accounted for an estimated A$3.87 billion in direct healthcare costs in 2021.

Conclusions

COPD imposes a substantial and preventable health system burden, dominated by hospitalisations for acute exacerbations and comorbid conditions. Improved recognition, maintenance therapy, pulmonary rehabilitation and ambulatory care models may help reduce avoidable admissions and associated costs.

title: Polydatin Inhibits Pulmonary Vascular Remodeling in MCT-Induced PAH via STEAP4/PI3K/AKT Signaling.
authorString: Zheng X, Yu Z, Kong L, He Y, Dan C, Huang Y, Li L, Zheng X.

journal.title: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology

abstractText: Polydatin, a natural compound with recognized cardiovascular benefits, has shown preliminary protective effects against pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), though its underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to investigate its preventive potential and mechanisms as a complementary therapeutic candidate in a monocrotaline (MCT)-induced rat model of PAH. A rat PAH model was established using MCT. Polydatin was administered to evaluate its effects. Right ventricular structure and function were assessed by echocardiography and gross heart specimen analysis. Right ventricular hypertrophy and pulmonary vascular remodeling were assessed by histology and immunohistochemistry. Expression levels of α-SMA, PCNA, and ET-1 were measured. RNA sequencing was performed on lung tissues to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs). Key targets and pathways were further validated using qPCR and Western blot in both rat lung tissues and primary smooth muscle cells. STEAP4 function was confirmed by siRNA knockdown in primary arterial smooth muscle cells. Polydatin treatment significantly ameliorated PAH, improving right ventricular structure and function, reducing right ventricular hypertrophy (ANP/BNP), and inhibiting pulmonary vascular remodeling (α-SMA, PCNA, and perivascular collagen deposition). RNA sequencing identified DEGs modulated by polydatin, enriched in processes related to cell proliferation and differentiation. STEAP4 was identified as a key target reversed by polydatin at both mRNA and protein levels. Further validation confirmed that polydatin inhibits the activation of the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway and suppresses cell proliferation. siRNA-mediated knockdown of STEAP4 reduced PI3K/AKT phosphorylation and inhibited ASMC proliferation, demonstrating that STEAP4 mediates the anti-proliferative effect of polydatin. Polydatin alleviates MCT-induced PAH and associated vascular remodeling primarily by downregulating STEAP4 and inhibiting the PI3K/AKT pathway. This highlights polydatin's potential as a preventive candidate for PAH.

title: Angeloylgomisin O from YiQiFuMai Lyophilized Injection attenuates heart failure by inhibiting endothelial-mesenchymal transition via ACE2.
authorString: Dai S, Huang Z, Liu J, Wu L, Zhao Q, Gong S, Zhang Y, Yu B, Li F, Kou J.
abstractText: YiQiFuMai Lyophilized Injection (YQFM), a modern preparation derived from the traditional Chinese formula Sheng-Mai-San, has demonstrated clinical efficacy in treating heart failure (HF). However, the bioactive constituents responsible for its therapeutic effects and the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. We first demonstrated that YQFM could inhibit endothelial-mesenchymal transition (End-MT), a critical driver of HF pathogenesis. Transcriptomic profiling of human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) revealed that YQFM markedly reversed transforming growth factor beta 1 (TGF-β1)-induced transcriptional alterations. Pathway enrichment analysis identified the renin-angiotensin system (RAS) as a key pathway regulated by YQFM, providing transcriptomic evidence for its involvement. This finding guided our subsequent target-based screening of key RAS-related proteins, including angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE), angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2), angiotensin II type 1 receptor (AT1R), and Mas receptor (Mas). Through molecular docking, cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA), microscale thermophoresis (MST), surface plasmon resonance (SPR) and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, we identified angeloylgomisin O (AO) as the major active constituent with high binding affinity for ACE2. In a coronary artery ligation (CAL)-induced HF mouse model, AO administration improved cardiac function, reduced fibrosis. Further investigations revealed that AO significantly suppressed TGF-β1-induced End-MT in HUVECs, upregulating CD31 and VE-cadherin while downregulating Vimentin, α-SMA, and Slug. Most importantly, AO treatment significantly reversed the suppression of ACE2 in both CAL-induced HF mice and TGF-β1-induced HUVECs. The critical role of ACE2 was corroborated using both agonist and antagonist treatments, which respectively enhanced and attenuated the inhibitory effects of AO on End-MT. These results demonstrate that AO alleviates heart failure primarily through targeting ACE2 and inhibiting End-MT. Our findings provide a mechanistic basis for the clinical application of YQFM and highlight AO as a potential candidate drug for HF.

title: Berberine repurposing for clinical translation: multi-target synergy, combinatorial approaches, and self-assembled delivery strategies.
authorString: Ma Q, Zhang S, Chai Y, Mao X, Xu D, Fu R, Tang Y.
abstractText: Berberine (BBR) is an active component in traditional Chinese medicine with a long history of clinical application. In recent years, its remarkable multi-target pharmacological properties have attracted extensive attention in modern biomedical research. Traditionally known for its antibacterial and anti-inflammatory effects, BBR is now widely used in the treatment of metabolic disorders, cardiovascular diseases, cancer, and neurological diseases. However, due to its low oral bioavailability, clinical translation has been severely limited. Moreover, BBR mainly accumulates in the intestine, resulting in a low systemic exposure level, which leads to a gap between the effective concentration in the preclinical stage and the actual achievable plasma concentration level. This article focuses on the bottleneck issue of BBR's bioavailability, providing a comprehensive and systematic summary from aspects such as multi-target action mechanisms, synergistic combination strategies, carrier-free self-assembling formulation methods, as well as existing research evidence, drug transformation prospects, safety issues, and drug interactions. It clarifies the existing opportunities and challenges of BBR, aiming to promote the further development of BBR therapy and provide new ideas for its clinical translation.

title: Role of PDK4/Nrf2/HO-1-Mediated Oxidative Stress Modulation of Mitochondrial Fatty Acid Oxidation in Protecting Against Doxorubicin-Induced Cardiotoxicity Under Hyperglycemic Conditions.
authorString: Lei Y, Chen Y, Li W, Wang L.
abstractText: Hyperglycemia aggravates Doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity (DIC), a growing complication in diabetic cardiomyopathy. Thus, elucidating the molecular regulatory pathways involved in DIC under hyperglycemic conditions is critical for understanding its pathophysiology and identifying potential therapeutic targets. A DIC model was established by treating HL-1 cardiomyocytes with high glucose and Dox, followed by CCK-8 and TUNEL assays to assess cell viability and apoptosis. Western blotting and RT-qPCR were used to evaluate PDK4 expression, Nrf2/HO-1 signaling, and cardiac injury markers (cTnI, α-SMA). In vivo, STZ and Dox were administered to C57BL/6 J mice to induce DIC, and cardiac histopathology was assessed by H&E, WGA, and Masson staining. Silencing PDK4 effectively activated the Nrf2/HO-1 antioxidant signaling pathway, significantly reduced intracellular accumulation of reactive oxygen species (ROS), and alleviated oxidative stress. Moreover, PDK4 downregulation inhibited aberrantly elevated fatty acid oxidation, thereby improving mitochondrial function and enhancing cardiomyocyte viability.
