These findings were further validated in vivo, where suppression of PDK4 expression alleviated myocardial injury and fibrosis, and markedly improved cardiac dysfunction induced by Dox under diabetic conditions, likely through modulation of the Nrf2/HO-1 axis. In summary, the PDK4/Nrf2/HO-1 axis plays a crucial protective role in regulating Doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity under high-glucose conditions, providing a potential molecular target for mitigating myocardial injury in diabetic patients undergoing Dox treatment.

title: General practitioner attitudes towards the utility of artificial intelligence-augmented clinical decision support for hypertension in Australia and England: a qualitative study.
authorString: Edwards J, Hussain B, Gonzalez-Chica D, Iyen B, Stocks N, Hoon E.
abstractText:
Background

Hypertension remains a persistent global health concern; in Australia, over half of hypertensive patients experience poor blood pressure control (≥140/90 mmHg). Given that hypertension is predominantly managed in primary care, it may represent an ideal setting for implementing novel artificial intelligence (AI)-augmented clinical decision support tools (CDST) for hypertension management. We aimed to explore GP attitudes and experiences on the acceptability and usability of AI-augmented CDST for medication advice in hypertension management.

Methods

This qualitative exploratory study in two jurisdictions with similar primary care settings (Australia and England) used purposive sampling to promote diversity of views. Semi-structured interviews, including two scenarios of AI-augmented CDST, were analysed with thematic analysis.

Results

A total of 22 GPs (Australia 14, England 8) were recruited through existing professional networks. GP attitudes towards AI in primary care hypertension management reflected their pragmatic, patient-centred approach within their specific sociocultural context. Clear country differences reflected a more 'protocolised' approach in England, and a more sceptical perception of the quality and applicability of primary care data Australia. GPs in both countries considered an AI tool broadly trustworthy if endorsed by trusted clinical associations, and highlighted that tools would have limited utility if they could not offer efficiencies (e.g. seamless interoperability and synthesis of patient data in relation to clinical recommendations) that supported the management of complexity for their specific patients.

Conclusion

For AI-augmented CDST to be adopted in primary care, it must align with the workflow, time constraints and relational nature of general practice, while supporting context-sensitive, individualised decision-making.

title: HRS perspective: A new strategic plan for a better tomorrow.
authorString: Al-Khatib SM.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Oral Anticoagulation for Atrial Fibrillation after Intracerebral Hemorrhage: A Systematic Review and Frequentist-Bayesian Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Cheng X, Zhang Y, Wang P, He J, Xiao Y, Fang F.
abstractText:
Background

Atrial fibrillation is a leading cause of ischemic stroke, and oral anticoagulation is commonly used for stroke prevention. However, the use of oral anticoagulation in patients with atrial fibrillation after spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage presents a therapeutic dilemma due to the increased risk of recurrent bleeding. This study aims to update the evidence on the efficacy and safety of oral anticoagulation in this high-risk population.

Methods

We searched the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, MEDLINE, and Embase, from inception to 30 April 2026, for randomized controlled trials comparing the initiation of oral anticoagulation with no anticoagulation in adults with atrial fibrillation after spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage. Frequentist, Bayesian, and trial sequential analyses were used. The primary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular events.

Results

A total of five randomized controlled trials were included, comprising 733 participants. Frequentist meta-analysis showed that oral anticoagulation was associated with a lower risk of major adverse cardiovascular events compared with no anticoagulation [risk ratio (RR) 0.59; 95% confidence interval (CI), 0.37-0.94; I2= 24%]. Bayesian meta-analysis generally favored oral anticoagulation across a range of prior distributions and heterogeneity assumptions, with a probability of RR < 0.8 exceeding 90% in six of ten scenarios.

Conclusions

Starting oral anticoagulation in patients with atrial fibrillation after intracerebral hemorrhage was associated with a lower risk of major adverse cardiovascular events compared with no anticoagulation.

title: Intraoperative Blood Pressure Targeting in Noncardiac Surgery: A Bayesian Random-effects Meta-analysis of Randomized Trials.
authorString: Ripollés-Melchor J, Espinosa ÁV, Monge-García I, Aldecoa C, Malbrain MLNG, Lorente JV, Quintana-Villamandos B, Navarro-Pérez R, Abad-Motos A, Colomina MJ, Ruiz-Escobar A, Budithi R, Fernández-García D, Fernández-Valdes-Bango P, Abad-Gurumeta A.
abstractText:
Background

Whether protocolized intraoperative arterial pressure-targeting strategies provide incremental benefit beyond contemporary usual care remains uncertain. The authors performed a Bayesian meta-analysis of randomized trials in major noncardiac surgery.

Methods

MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched from inception to January 5, 2026, with additional literature surveillance through June 29, 2026. Randomized trials comparing protocolized intraoperative arterial pressure-targeting strategies with usual care or lower-pressure approaches were included. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality; secondary outcomes were acute kidney injury (AKI) and myocardial injury after noncardiac surgery (MINS). Bayesian random-effects meta-analysis was prespecified as the primary analytical framework, with confirmatory frequentist analyses.

Results

Fifteen randomized trials met the inclusion criteria. Mortality (13 trials) remained centered around an odds ratio (OR) of 1.00 (frequentist OR, 1.00; 95% CI, 0.83 to 1.21; Bayesian median OR, 1.00; 95% credible interval [CrI], 0.73 to 1.38), with wide Bayesian prediction intervals (OR, 0.56 to1.78). AKI (14 trials) showed the most favorable estimates (frequentist OR, 0.87; 95% CI, 0.73 to 1.03; Bayesian median OR, 0.88; 95% CrI, 0.70 to 1.05), but estimates remained compatible with no clinically important benefit, heterogeneity was moderate, and leave-one-out analyses, excluding each trial in turn, showed sensitivity to individual trial exclusion. MINS (eight trials) likewise remained compatible with no treatment effect (frequentist OR, 1.04; 95% CI, 0.93 to 1.15; Bayesian median OR, 1.05; 95% CrI, 0.90 to 1.26). Exploratory analyses suggested that any potential renal benefit may depend on the broader hemodynamic context in which arterial pressure targets are implemented.

Conclusions

Protocolized intraoperative arterial pressure-targeting strategies did not demonstrate a consistent incremental benefit over contemporary usual care in major noncardiac surgery. Mortality and MINS remained compatible with no treatment effect. Although AKI showed the most favorable estimates, the evidence remained uncertain, was sensitive to individual trial exclusion, and should be interpreted cautiously.

title: Pulsed Field Ablation Versus Thermal Ablation for Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation: A GRADE-Assessed Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials With Reconstructed Time-to-Event Analysis.
authorString: Gadelmawla AF, Alsubaiei AA, AlSejari NY, Alsultan AM, Artam AS, Abdelsayed K, Alkuwaiti MA, Alomair AA, Mohamed AE, Hageen AW, Abdul-Hafez HA, Alharran AM, Zishiri E, Witt D, Andò G, Sengupta J, Frishman WH, Aronow WS.
abstractText: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) creates myocardial lesions with brief, nonthermal electrical pulses. We synthesized randomized comparisons of PFA with radiofrequency and cryoballoon ablation for pulmonary vein isolation in paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (AF). PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception through October 13, 2026. We included randomized trials enrolling adults with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation and comparing PFA with thermal ablation. Random-effects models pooled risk ratios and mean differences. Leave-one-out and Baujat analyses examined sensitivity and heterogeneity. Time-to-event data were reconstructed from published Kaplan-Meier curves. Four randomized trials, reported in 6 publications, enrolled 1396 participants. For 12-month freedom from atrial arrhythmia, the 4-trial analysis (n=1392) found no significant difference (risk ratio 1.04, 95% confidence interval, 0.92-1.17; P=0.374; I2=3.6%). Reconstructed data comprised 1368 participants and 423 recurrences. Estimated 12-month freedom from recurrence was 70.6% with PFA and 66.7% with thermal ablation (log-rank p=0.097; hazard ratio 0.84, 95% confidence interval, 0.70-1.02). Procedure time was numerically lower with PFA, but the pooled result was nonsignificant and heterogeneous. Fluoroscopy time did not differ significantly; left atrial dwell time was shorter with substantial heterogeneity. No safety outcome differed significantly, and no atrioesophageal fistulas were reported. Randomized evidence indicates similar short-term efficacy for PFA and thermal ablation. The reconstructed survival analysis favored PFA numerically but did not establish a difference.

title: One Anastomosis Gastric Bypass (OAGB) vs Sleeve Gastrectomy (SG) in Patients with Obesity and BMI ≥ 50 kg/m²: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Chouky Kamar M, Astudillo Coello PE.
abstractText:
Background

Patients with obesity and BMI ≥ 50 kg/m² presents unique clinical challenges, often requiring highly effective metabolic and bariatric interventions to achieve substantial weight reduction and obesity-associated medical conditions remission. Sleeve gastrectomy (SG) remains the most frequently performed procedure globally due to its technical simplicity and favorable short-term safety. However, long-term concerns regarding recurrent weight gain (RWG) and suboptimal clinical response (SoCR) in patients with higher baseline BMIs persist. One anastomosis gastric bypass (OAGB) has emerged as a powerful alternative, combining both restrictive and intestinal-rerouting mechanisms to optimize metabolic outcomes. Despite its growing popularity, head-to-head evidence directly comparing the long-term efficacy, safety profiles, and complication rates of OAGB versus SG specifically within patients with BMI ≥ 50 kg/m² demographic remains limited.

Objective

To compare the mid-term efficacy, safety profile, and resolution of metabolic obesity-associated medical conditions between one anastomosis gastric bypass (OAGB) and sleeve gastrectomy (SG) in patients with BMI ≥ 50 kg/m².

Methods

We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials (RCTs) and observational cohorts. We searched PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane through January 2026. Primary endpoint was total weight loss (%TWL). Secondary endpoints were remission of type 2 diabetes (T2D), hypertension remission, and rate of reoperation. Data was pooled using RevMan 5.4, evaluating Risk Ratios (RR) for dichotomous variables and Mean Differences (MD) for continuous variables, with 95% Confidence Intervals (CI).

Results

Eleven studies encompassing a total of 2,539 patients were included in the final review. The pooled analysis demonstrated that OAGB yielded a statistically significant superior Total Weight Loss compared to SG (MD = 9.56; 95% CI [9.01, 10.11]; p < 0.00001). Conversely, there was no statistically significant difference between the two techniques regarding T2DM remission (RR = 1.08; 95% CI [0.97, 1.20]; p = 0.16) or hypertension remission (RR = 1.20; 95% CI [0.98, 1.45]; p = 0.07). Additionally, the reoperation rates were comparable between the OAGB and SG groups (RR = 1.13; 95% CI [0.40, 3.20]; p = 0.82).

Conclusion

In patients with obesity and BMI ≥ 50 kg/m², OAGB provides significantly greater total weight loss compared to SG. Both procedures demonstrate comparable safety profiles and similar effectiveness in the remission of major metabolic obesity-associated medical conditions. OAGB is a highly effective and safe alternative for managing obesity.

title: Ketogenic and low-carbohydrate diets in cardiovascular prevention: can safety and efficacy coexist?
authorString: Parameswaran V, Maron DJ, Gardner C.
abstractText:
Purpose of review

To assess whether low-carbohydrate and ketogenic diets achieve cardiometabolic efficacy while maintaining safety. Particular attention is paid to the quantity and quality of carbohydrate restriction and their replacement foods.

Recent findings

Randomized trials show that short-term improvements in weight and glycemia diminish with longer follow-up, and lipid effects vary with the degree and quality of carbohydrate restriction and their replacement foods. Across 174 randomized trials, triglyceride reductions were similar across moderate-carbohydrate, low-carbohydrate, and ketogenic-carbohydrate diets, whereas LDL-C increases were progressively greater with increasing degrees of carbohydrate restriction. LDL-C responses are heterogeneous, and controlled feeding studies demonstrate increases in small LDL particles and ApoB with ketogenic diets. Substituting carbohydrates with plant protein and unsaturated fats improve triglycerides while lowering LDL-C and ApoB. Prospective cohort studies associate plant-derived low-carbohydrate patterns with lower cardiovascular risk. Clinical cardiovascular-event evidence remains observational.

Summary

Carbohydrate restriction may be compatible with cardiovascular health, but safety and efficacy depend on the quantity and quality of carbohydrate restriction, their replacement foods, and individual lipoprotein response. Cardiovascular outcome trials are needed to determine metabolic and lipoprotein effects of carbohydrate restriction on cardiovascular events, but practical and financial barriers to conducting such trials are prohibitive.

title: Environmental influences and implementation effectiveness of community-based hypertension management: a five-year natural experiment in Southwest China.
authorString: Ren N, Zhang Y, Zhang RX, Yang M, Meng F, Li Y, Zhou J, Fan S.

journal.title: International journal for equity in health

abstractText:
Background

Hypertension management poses significant challenges in regions experiencing rapid urbanization, particularly where healthcare resources vary substantially across urban and rural areas. Luzhou City's community-based hypertension management program, initiated in 2014 and gradually expanded city-wide, provides valuable insights into implementing chronic disease management in diverse socioeconomic settings. This study evaluates the program's effectiveness through a five-year natural experiment, examining detection rates, implementation patterns, and environmental and socioeconomic influences.

Methods

We analyzed health examination data from seven districts and counties of Luzhou City (2019-2023), encompassing 122 townships and streets. Environmental data, including air pollutants, vegetation coverage, and meteorological parameters, were obtained from the Weijing Remote Sensing platform and National Tibetan Plateau Data Center. Spatial autocorrelation analysis and Bayesian spatiotemporal modeling were employed to assess program implementation patterns and environmental and socioeconomic influences on detection rates. Regular calibration of equipment and standardized training of healthcare providers ensured data quality.

Results

City-wide hypertension detection rates increased from 21.60% in 2019 to 29.27% in 2023, with notable regional variations. Less economically developed counties demonstrated exceptional improvements, with Gulin and Luxian achieving the highest annual improvement rates (Estimated Annual Percentage Change [EAPC]: 10.57% and 10.22%, respectively). Middle-aged adults (45-49 years) showed the most substantial improvement (EAPC: 14.45%). Bayesian spatiotemporal modeling identified significant environmental and socioeconomic correlates: average temperature showed the strongest environmental association (RR = 1.0506 per 1 °C, 95% CrI: 1.0186-1.0850), followed by O₃ concentration (RR = 1.0224 per 1 µg/m³, 95% CrI: 1.0158-1.0314). GDP and urbanization rate were negatively associated with detection rates, while hospital bed density showed a positive association (RR = 1.0314 per 1 bed/1,000 population, 95% CrI: 1.0155-1.0521). Spatial analysis revealed persistent clustering patterns (Moran's I: 0.1889-0.2655, P < 0.05), indicating structural influences on program effectiveness.

Conclusions

The successful implementation of community-based hypertension management in resource-limited settings demonstrates the feasibility of reducing healthcare disparities through systematic approaches. The varying effectiveness across regions and age groups, coupled with significant environmental influences, indicates the importance of context-sensitive implementation strategies. These findings provide valuable guidance for chronic disease management in developing regions, emphasizing the potential for achieving health equity through well-structured community health programs.

Clinical trial number

Not applicable.

title: A tiered postmortem work-up for suspected Kounis syndrome: proposal derived from a systematic review of 47 fatal autopsied cases.
authorString: Sirago G, Sebastiani N, Solarino B, Dell'Erba A, Ferorelli D.
abstractText:
Background

Kounis syndrome, the concurrence of acute coronary syndrome with mast-cell- and platelet-mediated hypersensitivity reactions, is increasingly recognised clinically but remains poorly standardised at autopsy.

Methods

We performed a PROSPERO-registered systematic review compliant with PRISMA 2020 and PRISMA-S. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science and Cochrane Library were searched, complemented by citation chasing, an eosinophilic-coronary-disease sensitivity search and hand-searching. Eligible records described fatal autopsied Kounis-spectrum cases, including allergic myocardial infarction and eosinophilic coronary periarteritis/arteritis. The fatal case was the unit of analysis; postmortem biochemistry, mast-cell histology and immunohistochemistry, toxicology and diagnostic certainty were extracted.

Results

Thirty-six records contributed 47 unique fatal autopsied cases from 17 countries (1969-2025). Postmortem tryptase was measured in 6/47 cases (12.8%), histamine in 1/47 (2.1%) and immunoglobulin E in 1/47 (2.1%); any mast-cell-specific tissue method was used in 11/47 (23.4%). Thirty-six cases were type I/type I-like, eight type II/II-like and three type III. Biochemical testing clustered in iatrogenic/periprocedural and type II cases, whereas anti-tryptase immunohistochemistry clustered in the eosinophilic-coronary-periarteritis literature, documenting a dissociation between tissue and biochemical methods. The finding held among definite/probable (tryptase 3/31) and methodologically stronger cases (2/19), and was attenuated, not reversed, among thirteen cases explicitly diagnosed as Kounis syndrome or allergic coronary disease by their authors (3/13).

Conclusion

Reports of fatal autopsied Kounis cases rarely document biochemical testing for mast-cell activation. We propose, for prospective validation, a tiered, indication-driven minimum postmortem work-up, modelled on the multimodal Cianci et al. [52] case, for sudden deaths in which Kounis syndrome enters the differential diagnosis.

title: Heterogeneity of glaucoma polygenic risk score reporting.
authorString: Wang C, Chaurasia AK, Chen C, Craig JE, MacGregor S, Mackey DA, Hewitt AW.
abstractText:
Purpose

Primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) is a leading cause of irreversible blindness globally, including Australia. The utility of polygenic risk scores (PRS), which aggregate numerous genetic variants, offers promise for improving early risk assessment for POAG. This systematic review examines the development of POAG PRS models and evaluates their effectiveness in predicting the risk of the disease.

Method

A systematic literature search was conducted on PubMed, Ovid Medline, Embase, and Scopus on 17 April 2026, screening a total of 2018 articles. Risk of bias was assessed using the PROBAST tool. This review is registered on PROSPERO (CRD420251040141).

Results

Sixty-five studies were included, with 20 articles reporting an original PRS and 45 articles contextualizing a PRS with clinically relevant traits. PRS models varied significantly in the number of SNPs (4 to over 9 million) and sample sizes (672 to over 449,000 individuals) used. Considerable variation exists in the reporting of outcome measures. Reported odds ratios per decile ranged from 1.74 (95%CI 1.71-1.77) to 45.48 (95%CI 29.38-75.39). PRS combined with demographic factors improved predictive power. Ancestry-specific PRSs performed better in their respective ethnic populations. POAG PRSs were associated with clinically relevant traits such as cardiovascular diseases, impaired lung function, and increased urinary sodium excretion.

Conclusion

PRS for POAG shows promise but requires further validation across diverse populations to ensure equitable clinical application. Future research should focus on enhancing the generalizability of PRS and integrating environmental risk factors to improve prediction.

title: Surgical bootcamps in postgraduate surgical training: A narrative review.
authorString: Galvaing G, Galamini PA, Innorta A, d'Ostrevy N.

journal.title: The surgeon : journal of the Royal Colleges of Surgeons of Edinburgh and Ireland

abstractText:
Background and purpose

Surgical training faces a persistent transition gap between medical school and residency, intensified by duty-hour restrictions, patient-safety imperatives, and growing procedural complexity. Surgical bootcamps are short, intensive, simulation-based programmes designed to condense preparation for clinical practice into a defined period immediately before, or at the start of, a new stage of training.

Methods

We conducted a narrative review of PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and ERIC for articles published between January 2013 and June 2025, taking as our starting point the most recent meta-analysis of postgraduate bootcamps, whose search closed in April 2013. Of 1256 records identified, 43 studies were included. Six outcome domains were defined in advance: programme design and format; educational modalities; assessment methods and their validation; learner outcomes; cost and resource requirements; and implementation barriers, including access in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Findings were combined by narrative synthesis; no quantitative pooling or inductive qualitative thematic analysis was undertaken.

Main findings

Bootcamps consistently improve trainees' confidence, knowledge, and technical performance. Gains are attributable to the format itself, which combines brief didactics, deliberate practice on task-specific models, and structured feedback delivered at a high faculty-to-trainee ratio over a compressed period, rather than to any single modality. Competency gains are commonly measured with validated instruments such as OSATS and GEARS. Low- and high-fidelity models perform comparably, so effective programmes can be delivered at widely differing cost, and many curricula also strengthen non-technical skills including communication, teamwork, and crisis management.

Conclusions

Evidence on retention beyond three to six months and on transfer to patient care remains scarce. Priorities are multicentre studies with concurrent controls, longer follow-up, agreement on a core outcome set, and patient-level endpoints.

title: Soluble receptors for advanced glycation end products is associated with cardiac mortality among patients with stable ischemic heart disease: long-term follow-up of the LAERTES study.
authorString: Rallidis LS, Papathanasiou KA, Drosatos IA, Izhar S, Kotakos C, Rallidis SL, Tsoporis JN, Leong-Poi H.

journal.title: Biomarkers : biochemical indicators of exposure, response, and susceptibility to chemicals

abstractText:
Background

It has been suggested that circulating levels of the soluble receptor for advanced glycation end products (sRAGE) is a biomarker of underlying inflammation. There is limited data regarding its prognostic value in patients with stable coronary artery disease (CAD). We explored the long-term prognostic value of sRAGE levels on cardiac mortality in patients with CAD.

Methods

This is a retrospective analysis from LAERTES Study. Serum sRAGE levels were measured at baseline. sRAGE were quantified using DuoSetELISA kit. Primary endpoint was cardiac death and secondary endpoint the composite of non-fatal acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and ischemic stroke.

Results

Data were obtained from 800 patients (13% female, median age 62 years, median follow-up 6 years) of whom 76 died from cardiac death, 84 experienced ACS and 12 had ischemic stroke. Patients with cardiac death were older and had more comorbidities. sRAGE levels were predictive of cardiac death and remained an independent predictor for cardiac death (HR: 1.31, 95% CI: 1.03-1.67, p = 0.027) after adjustment for traditional risk factors and left ventricular ejection fraction. sRAGE levels could not predict the secondary endpoints.

Conclusions

Higher sRAGE levels are independently associated with cardiac mortality among CAD patients.

title: Trends in hypertension and diabetes indicators in Daegu, South Korea (2009-2023): a descriptive epidemiological study.
authorString: Lee YM, Ryu DH, Kim K.
abstractText:
Background

Hypertension and diabetes are chronic diseases contributing to cardiovascular morbidity and mortality worldwide. Characterizing long-term trends in disease indicators is essential for public health planning. This study examined 15-year trends (2009-2023) in hypertension and diabetes indicators among adults aged ≥30 years in Daegu, South Korea, using self-reported Community Health Survey (CHS) and medical utilization data from the National Health Insurance Service (NHIS) based on the International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision.

Methods

A descriptive epidemiological design was used. The CHS diagnosis experience and NHIS medical utilization rates were calculated annually and stratified by age group. Age-standardized rates were estimated by using the 2005 Korean population as the standard. Temporal trends were assessed using simple linear regression, and correlations between the two data sources were evaluated.

Results

Both the CHS diagnosis experience and NHIS medical utilization rates for hypertension and diabetes increased over time. Crude rates increased more rapidly than age-standardized rates, indicating the substantial influence of population aging. The CHS-based estimates were generally lower than the NHIS-based estimates and showed greater year-to-year variability, particularly among older adults. The crude rates from the two sources were strongly correlated, whereas the correlations for age-standardized rates were weaker.

Conclusion

Increasing trends for hypertension and diabetes indicate a growing public health burden in Daegu. Differences between the CHS and NHIS estimates reflect the complementary dimensions of disease surveillance, capturing self-reported diagnosis experience and medication-related healthcare utilization, respectively. A long-term dual-source approach integrating CHS and NHIS data may help address the limitations of state-level surveillance systems and support more robust epidemiological monitoring and informed health policy decision-making.

title: Thick Blood: Fatal Budd-Chiari Syndrome in the Setting of Dehydration.
authorString: Smith M, Jacob-Leonce M.

journal.title: The American journal of forensic medicine and pathology

abstractText: Budd-Chiari syndrome (BCS) is a condition characterized by obstruction of hepatic venous outflow tracts, not due to cardiac disease or sinusoidal obstruction syndrome. Myeloproliferative disorders, hormone-induced hypercoagulability, or thrombophilias are common causes of thrombi. Masses can lead to outflow obstruction of hepatic veins. BCS can lead to fulminant liver failure, requiring rapid diagnosis and intervention to prevent severe morbidity or mortality. We present a case of an 81-year-old woman who was brought to the emergency department after being found down at home. Per family, 2 days prior, she was experiencing nausea and abdominal pain. Upon arrival to the hospital, she had waxing and waning mentation and severe dehydration. Laboratory work-up revealed dehydration due to volume depletion and liver failure. At autopsy, the patient was jaundiced. The liver had multifocal, organizing, occlusive thrombi throughout the hepatic veins. Widespread necrosis, hemorrhage, and congestion of the liver were present. These findings, combined with the antemortem laboratory work-up and the patient's history, were diagnostic for acute BCS. Dehydration is believed to cause narrowing of blood vessels and increased blood viscosity, leading to the development of thromboemboli. This autopsy case seeks to highlight the importance of recognizing dehydration as a risk factor for developing Budd-Chiari syndrome.

title: Minimally invasive and nephron-sparing surgery for renal cancer: a nationwide analysis of 228,185 nephrectomies in Germany, 2011-2024.
authorString: Risch J, Kohler J, Buck L, Weische O, Weiss ML, Henningsen T, Heckmann N, Schließer P, Becker BJ, Voran J, Jarczyk J, Berg S, Nuhn P, Rodler S.
abstractText:
Purpose

Nephron-sparing and minimally invasive surgery are recommended for localised renal cell carcinoma, but the evidence comes from expert centres. We examined whether their advantages hold in routine care and whether access is equitable.

Methods

We analysed all 228,185 adult nephrectomies for renal cancer in the German hospital census, 2011-2024. Outcomes were in-hospital mortality, major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE-RN), acute kidney injury, dialysis and length of stay. Access was compared by mixed-effects logistic regression with random hospital intercepts, procedure type by inverse probability of treatment weighting.

Results

The minimally invasive share rose from 19.7% to 59.4%, robot assistance from 9.7% to 79.4% of those, and partial nephrectomy overtook radical in 2017, reaching 62.5%. Adjusted odds were lower with minimally invasive access for death (odds ratio 0.49, 95% CI 0.42-0.56), MACCE-RN (0.56) and acute kidney injury (0.57), with a 21% shorter stay, and lower still with robot assistance than laparoscopy for acute kidney injury (0.46 vs. 0.72) and dialysis (0.67 vs. 0.92). Partial nephrectomy was associated with lower odds of death (0.61) and dialysis (0.41), without a shift towards patients with greater comorbidity. Minimally invasive surgery had ever been performed in 17.9% of the smallest and 95.9% of the largest centres.

Conclusion

Both approaches became predominant and in routine care were associated with the advantages reported from expert centres. These are observational associations, not evidence of intrinsic superiority: administrative data carry no tumour stage and no follow-up beyond discharge. Adoption depended on hospital volume, not patient characteristics.

title: Progress in Reducing the Black-White Mortality Gap From 1993 to 2023 in the United States: An Analysis of the National Mortality Database.
authorString: Sung H, Jiang C, Gregg EW, Lee D, Islami F, Jemal A.
abstractText:
Background

Reducing racial mortality disparities remains a central goal of U.S. health policy, and progress varies by cause of death.

Objective

To quantify cause-specific contributions to changes in excess mortality rate (EMR) among Black versus White populations.

Design

Cross-sectional temporal analyses.

Setting

Mortality data.

Participants

Non-Hispanic Black and non-Hispanic White decedents stratified by sex and age at death (<20, <65, or ≥65 years).

Measurements

EMRs among Black versus White populations in 1993 and 2023 for all-cause and 24 causes of death, calculated as differences in age-standardized mortality rates, and changes in EMRs, calculated by subtracting the 2023 EMR from the 1993 EMR with cause-specific contribution to all-cause EMR reduction, expressed as a percentage.

Results

In 2023, all-cause EMR for Black versus White persons decreased by 56% (288.5 deaths per 100 000 person-years) for males and by 68% (175.8 deaths per 100 000 person-years) for females compared with 1993. Among males, reductions were predominantly driven by cancer (38.2% [95% CI, 36.4% to 40.0%]), HIV (17.5% [CI, 17.0% to 18.1%]), and heart disease (12.3% [CI, 10.2% to 14.4%]); among females, primary drivers were heart disease (31.9% [CI, 29.8% to 34.0%]), cancer (13.0% [CI, 11.3% to 14.8%]), and HIV (7.9% [CI, 7.5% to 8.3%]). Further gains were limited by lower progress or worsening disparities in maternal death; nephritis and accidents and adverse effects in both sexes; and homicide and legal intervention, diabetes, hypertension without heart disease, and cerebrovascular diseases (≥65 years) in males. Over time, cancer fell from the leading contributor to sixth among males and from second to fifth among females, whereas HIV declined from fourth or fifth to tenth in both sexes as contributors to the Black-White mortality gap.

Limitation

The analysis compared 1993 and 2023, although peak EMR years varied by cause of death, and alternative periods could yield different cause-specific contributions.

Conclusion

Reductions in EMR among Black versus White populations were driven by improvements in mortality from major causes. Shifting drivers of the racial mortality gap highlight priorities for further progress.

Primary funding source

American Cancer Society and Research Ireland.

title: Abdominal aortic aneurysm in patients with malignancy: a population-based claims study.
authorString: Kapalla M, Casties A, Reeps C, Weitz J, Schmitt J, Schoffer O, Busch A, Datzmann T.
abstractText:
Objective

The co-occurrence of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) and malignancy is increasingly relevant in an aging population. However, the population-based co-prevalence, temporal relationship, and potential impact of concomitant cancer on AAA management remain incompletely understood.

Methods

This retrospective population-based cohort study analyzed claims data from 3,088,992 individuals insured by a large German statutory health insurance provider (AOK PLUS) between 2010 and 2023. AAA and cancer cases were identified using standardized ICD-10-GM and OPS codes.

Results

AAA was recorded in 13,494 individuals (period prevalence: 4,368/1,000,000) and cancer in 316,603 (10,249/100,000). A recorded diagnosis of both conditions during the observation period was identified in 4,745 patients (35.2% of patients with AAA), predominantly men (5:1). Among patients with incident diagnoses of both diseases (n = 531), AAA was recorded before cancer in 51.6%, cancer before AAA in 41.2%, and both simultaneously in 7.2%. At the first recorded AAA diagnosis, rupture was less frequently documented in patients with recorded cancer than in those without (2.9% vs. 5.9%; p < 0.001). Among patients with AAA, the proportion undergoing aneurysm repair was comparable between patients with and without recorded cancer (25.5% vs. 26.2%). Exploratory Kaplan-Meier analysis suggested a longer interval from first recorded AAA diagnosis to treatment in patients with recorded cancer (p = 0.041), while competing-risk analysis showed a slightly lower cumulative incidence of repair (p = 0.02) and more frequent death before repair (p < 0.01). Systemic cancer therapies were administered with similar frequency in AAA patients with cancer and the overall cancer cohort (26.5% vs. 28.1%).

Conclusion

The co-prevalence of AAA and malignancy is substantial. In patients with a recorded cancer diagnosis, exploratory analysis suggested a longer observed interval from the first recorded AAA diagnosis to aneurysm treatment, while competing-risk analysis showed a slightly lower cumulative incidence of repair and more deaths before repair. Cancer-related imaging may influence AAA detection, but disease onset and progression could not be assessed. These findings support coordinated vascular-oncology care and warrant further studies integrating detailed clinical and imaging data.

title: Interaction of Gut Microbiota-Derived Metabolites With Inflammatory Markers and Cellular Rejection in Patients With Advanced Heart Failure Treated With Heart Transplantation.
authorString: Sokolski M, Florek K, Ptak J, Żurawska-Płaksej E, Bromage DI, Czapor-Irzabek H, Jarocki M, Bator AA, Buzun W, Łaczmański Ł, Komorowska K, Rakowski M, Bochenek M, Przybylski R, Zakliczyński M.
abstractText: BACKGROUND Gut microbiota-derived metabolites (GMDMs) are involved in the pathophysiology of heart failure (HF) and may play an important role in patients after orthotopic heart transplantation (Htx). This study aimed to evaluate key GMDMs and their relationship with inflammation and the occurrence of acute cellular rejection (ACR) in patients undergoing Htx. MATERIAL AND METHODS This was an observational study that enrolled consecutive patients qualified for Htx between June 2022 and November 2023. The study included 15 healthy volunteers, 20 patients undergoing non-Htx cardiac surgery, and 32 consecutive patients undergoing Htx. The GMDMs trimethylamine oxide (TMAO), indoxyl sulfate, and p-cresol sulfate were evaluated in the serum before the procedure and at 1, 3, and 6 months after procedure in the study and control groups. ACR was diagnosed using endomyocardial biopsies. RESULTS The study group consisted of 32 patients qualified for Htx (78% male, 52±11 years old). Baseline levels of TMAO (0.77 [0.52-1.45] ug/mL) and p-cresol sulfate (9.90 [4.03-18.21] ug/mL) were significantly higher than in the healthy control group (0.28 [0.15-0.51] ug/mL and 4.45 [0.79-8.35] ug/mL, respectively; all P<0.05). Significant correlations were found between TMAO and endothelin (ET-1), as well as with procalcitonin, at 1 and 6 months after Htx. The study group did not show significant changes in metabolites in the follow-up period. Despite GMDMs being higher in the ACR group, the differences did not reach statistical significance. CONCLUSIONS TMAO and p-cresol sulfate were increased in patients with advanced HF. Moreover, TMAO correlated with ET-1 and procalcitonin; however, there was no association between GMDMs and ACR incidence.

title: ATF7 coordinates early transcriptional priming to enable direct cardiac reprogramming.
authorString: Ambroise RL, Zi-Yang Y, Wang H, Wu D, Liu J, Qian L.
abstractText: Direct cardiac reprogramming relies on the canonical transcription factor cocktail MEF2C, GATA4, and TBX5 (MGT), yet successful lineage conversion requires additional non-cocktail regulators that coordinate the chromatin and transcriptional transitions underlying fibroblast-to-cardiomyocyte conversion. Here, we identify Activating Transcription Factor 7 (ATF7) as a critical supporting factor that enables efficient direct cardiac reprogramming. Loss-of-function studies in primary murine cardiac fibroblasts demonstrate that Atf7 knockdown markedly reduces MGT-mediated reprogramming efficiency, with the strongest impairment occurring when Atf7 is depleted during the early priming window of days 0-3. Transcriptomic profiling reveals that Atf7 knockdown disrupts the induction of cardiomyocyte gene programs while restoring expression of fibroblast- and extracellular-matrix-associated pathways, shifting the global expression profile toward a non-reprogrammed state. CUT&RUN mapping across days 0, 3, and 6 of reprogramming shows that ATF7 binds dynamically to lineage-relevant regulatory regions, engaging cardiac loci-including those encoding Gata4 and Tbx5-early in reprogramming, and increasingly occupying fibroblast-associated loci at later stages. Integration of ATF7 binding sites with published single-cell chromatin accessibility data identifies substantial overlap with iCM-enriched regulatory signatures, particularly at day 3, highlighting this stage as a critical node of ATF7 activity. Together, these findings reveal that ATF7 executes a bifunctional regulatory role by simultaneously promoting cardiomyocyte-specific gene activation and repressing fibroblast-associated transcriptional networks. Our study establishes ATF7 as a previously unrecognized regulatory component necessary for efficient MGT-driven cardiac reprogramming and provides a preliminary mechanistic framework for its dual lineage-modulating functions.

title: Nanomaterials for the treatment of aging-related diseases: applications, mechanisms and perspectives.
authorString: Wang C, Xing Y, Zhou X, Zhao F, Shao L.
abstractText: Aging-related diseases (ARDs) are a growing health burden caused by the progressive loss of physiological homeostasis. Aging is driven by interconnected molecular, cellular, and tissue alterations that create shared but heterogeneous pathological bases for these disorders. Conventional therapies often have limited access to pathological tissues and intracellular targets in ARDs. Nanomaterials offer distinct opportunities because their nanoscale dimensions and intrinsic physicochemical properties enable interactions with biological structures from subcellular compartments to aged tissue microenvironments. However, current evidence remains fragmented across nanomaterial design, aging mechanisms, disease contexts, and translational studies. This Review integrates nanomaterial design with aging biology to clarify how nanoscale physicochemical properties shape therapeutic behavior in ARDs. Particular emphasis is placed on the mechanisms by which nanomaterials modulate cellular senescence and the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP), restore proteostasis and autophagy, regulate mitochondrial homeostasis, alleviate oxidative stress and chronic inflammation, and promote tissue regeneration. These mechanisms are further related to major ARDs, including neurodegenerative, cardiovascular, metabolic, and musculoskeletal diseases, as well as cancer, highlighting how disease context and pathological mechanisms shape nanomaterial-based therapeutic strategies. Major barriers to clinical translation are also critically evaluated, together with future research priorities for advancing nanomaterial-based interventions in ARDs. By integrating these dimensions, this Review offers a systematic perspective on how nanomaterial properties can be rationally aligned with aging mechanisms and disease-specific therapeutic needs, while also informing their future clinical translation.

title: TRIB3 Knockdown Attenuates Post-cardiac Arrest Brain Injury with Suppression of Mitophagy: Involvement of AKT-FOXO3a-BNIP3 Signaling.
authorString: Zhao D, Sun Y, Li Q, Yin S, Xiao Z.
abstractText: Brain injury after cardiac arrest and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CA-CPR) is a major cause of poor neurological outcomes among survivors, yet effective mechanism-based interventions remain lacking. Mitophagy maintains mitochondrial homeostasis, but whether increased mitophagy contributes to brain injury after CA-CPR and which upstream factors regulate it remain unclear. Transcriptomic analysis of hippocampal tissue from rats subjected to asphyxial CA-CPR identified tribbles pseudokinase 3 (TRIB3) as one of the most strongly upregulated genes, with its expression approximately 68-fold higher than that in sham controls. TRIB3 was knocked down by adeno-associated virus (AAV) injection into the hippocampal CA1 region 4 weeks before CA-CPR and by lentiviral transduction in H19-7 cells before oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R). TRIB3 knockdown improved neurological function and attenuated hippocampal CA1 neuronal injury in CA-CPR rats. It also attenuated mitophagy, alleviated mitochondrial dysfunction, and reduced neuronal apoptosis in vivo and in vitro. Valproic acid partially counteracted these mitochondrial and anti-apoptotic effects in vitro. Mechanistic analyses in OGD/R-treated cells showed that TRIB3 knockdown increased the p-AKT/AKT and p-FOXO3a/FOXO3a ratios, reduced FOXO3a nuclear accumulation and BNIP3 expression, and decreased FOXO3a enrichment at the Bnip3 promoter. Co-immunoprecipitation assays showed increased TRIB3-AKT association and reduced AKT-FOXO3a association after OGD/R. In vivo, TIC10 treatment partially counteracted the improvements in mitochondrial function and neurological outcomes following TRIB3 knockdown. Together, these findings suggest that TRIB3 may act as a previously unrecognized upstream modulator of mitophagy after CA-CPR, implicate AKT-FOXO3a-BNIP3 signaling, and support further evaluation of TRIB3 as a potential neuroprotective target.

title: Bioelectric signalling: mechanisms, biological functions, diseases, diagnosis and therapy.
authorString: Desoyer C, Ghorbanpour S, Goswami D, Hauser CAE, Moreddu R, Marsh DJ, Baumgartner D, Gentile S, Wang X, Baumgartner C.
abstractText: Bioelectric signalling arises from the coordinated activity of ion channels, transporters, exchangers, and pumps, which establish the membrane potential and ionic gradients, generate endogenous electric fields, and support intercellular bioelectric coupling. These occur in both excitable and non-excitable tissues, where they interact with biochemical, mechanical, metabolic, and transcriptional networks. Excitable tissues serve as established model systems linking ion transport to rapid bioelectric activity and organ function. This review focuses primarily on the less extensively characterised roles of persistent and spatially organised bioelectric states in non-excitable and weakly excitable tissues. Evidence from the fields of development, regeneration, wound repair, immunity, and tissue remodelling suggests that bioelectric states may function as instructive signals, modulators of signalling responsiveness, permissive physiological conditions, or integrated indicators of cell and tissue state. This functional classification provides a framework for interpreting bioelectric alterations associated with cancer, fibrosis, chronic inflammation, metabolic disease, and neurological and cardiovascular disorders. We examine how membrane voltage, calcium signalling, endogenous electric fields, and gap junctional coupling interact with canonical pathways and tissue architecture. Experimental criteria are proposed to distinguish regulatory mechanisms from adaptive or secondary changes. The development of bioelectric diagnostics is evaluated in relation to analytical validity, biological interpretation, clinical validity, and clinical utility, together with therapeutic strategies based on ion channel modulation, electrical stimulation, conductive biomaterials, and bioelectronic interfaces. Integrating quantitative measurements, controlled perturbations, and computational modelling could help define when bioelectric states offer mechanistic leverage, predictive information, or clinically actionable targets.

title: Radiographic vertebral heart size in clinically healthy Shiba Inu dogs.
authorString: Maruyama I, Uemura A, Nakata TM, Yoshida T.

journal.title: The Journal of veterinary medical science

abstractText: Vertebral heart size (VHS) is a widely used radiographic method for evaluating cardiac size in dogs, and breed-related variation has been reported. However, breed-specific VHS data for Shiba Inu dogs have not previously been reported. This retrospective study evaluated VHS in 42 clinically healthy Shiba Inu dogs with no evidence of cardiac disease based on physical examination, thoracic radiography, and echocardiography. VHS was measured using right lateral thoracic radiographs. The mean ± standard deviation VHS was 9.62 ± 0.35 vertebrae. These findings provide baseline radiographic data for clinically healthy Shiba Inu dogs.

title: Platelet activation in chemotherapy: from mechanistic deciphering to precision intervention.
authorString: Xu XR, Rousseau Z, Ni H.
abstractText:
Purpose of review

Chemotherapy-induced thrombocytopenia and thrombosis are clinical paradoxes; patients may have both life-threatening bleeding and thrombotic events simultaneously. Here, we summarize recent advances elucidating this contradiction and introduce a framework for mechanism-guided precision management.

Recent findings

Chemotherapies often induce a platelet hyper-reactive/procoagulant state despite numerical reduction. Based on the latest evidence, we propose a four-tier classification of chemotherapy-induced platelet activation: Type I directly binds to platelet receptors (e.g. doxorubicin-CLEC-2), triggers inside-out signaling, induces thrombosis and platelet clearance; Type II is caused by GSDME-mediated pyroptosis (e.g. cisplatin); Type III (cyclophosphamide, 5-fluorouracil) damages the endothelium and thus recruits and activates platelets; and Type IV (paclitaxel, methotrexate) has dual effects, contextually promoting or suppressing the procoagulant/aggregatory phenotype. Notably, immunotherapies (e.g. immune-checkpoint inhibitors) may also increase cardiovascular risk through platelet activation. New diagnostic biomarkers, including platelet activation markers (e.g., P-selectin, phosphatidylserine exposure, desialylation), glycocalicin for GPIbα shedding and GSDME-N for pyroptosis, will potentially shift platelet monitoring from rudimentary counting to a dynamic functional assessment of pivotal biomarkers.

Summary

Recent findings provide a molecular basis for mechanism-directed thromboprophylaxis and the development of targeted adjunctive therapies in the chemotherapy setting, thus advancing precision oncology medicine that retains antitumor effects and restores platelet functional homeostasis.

title: Approaches to the Management of Splenomegaly and Hypersplenism in Thalassemia and Sickle Cell Disease: A Review and Recommendations for Surgical and Minimally Invasive Interventions.
authorString: Al-Asa'd Y, Qasem N, Alshurafa A, Haik M, Mustafa S, Yassin MA.
abstractText: The spleen is essential for hematologic and immune homeostasis. In hemoglobinopathies such as thalassemia and sickle cell disease (SCD), splenomegaly and hypersplenism are common complications that cause cytopenias, increased transfusion requirements, and significant morbidity. This review evaluates non-pharmacological interventions for managing splenomegaly in these populations. Total splenectomy reduces transfusion needs and resolves hypersplenism but carries significant long-term risks, including overwhelming post-splenectomy infection (OPSI), thromboembolic events, and pulmonary hypertension. Partial splenectomy preserves immune function by retaining ≥25% of splenic tissue, though benefits may be temporary because of remnant regrowth. Partial splenic embolization (PSE) reduces transfusion dependence while preserving splenic immunity and is suitable for non-surgical candidates, with post-embolization syndrome and, rarely, abscess formation as complications. Splenic radiofrequency ablation (RFA) offers modest hematologic improvements and a favorable safety profile but has limited published data, particularly in SCD. Splenic irradiation (SI) is primarily palliative and lacks robust evidence in benign hemoglobinopathies. Managing splenomegaly in thalassemia and SCD requires an individualized approach. While total splenectomy provides definitive results, the high risk of long-term complications warrants careful consideration. Spleen-preserving strategies, particularly partial splenectomy and partial splenic embolization, offer a balanced approach by mitigating hypersplenism while preserving crucial immune function. Minimally invasive techniques such as RFA show promise but require further investigation. Treatment decisions should be tailored to the patient's clinical condition, disease severity, and available healthcare resources.

title: Adrenal Vein Sampling: Impact of Intraprocedural Sedation on Cortisol Levels and the Point-Of-Care Quick Cortisol Assay Kit.
authorString: Phan M, Doery JCG, Fuller PJ, Yang J, Lau KK.

journal.title: Journal of medical imaging and radiation oncology

abstractText:
Introduction

Adrenal vein sampling (AVS) is routinely performed to subtype primary aldosteronism, a common cause of secondary hypertension. Many radiologists administer intravenous sedation during lengthy AVS procedures. The aim of this retrospective study was to determine the impact of sedation on cortisol measurements in AVS.

Methods

Adults who underwent successful AVS with intraprocedural sedation (both midazolam and fentanyl) in 2023 were included. Patients who received alternate sedation or had unsuccessful AVS were excluded. Adrenal and peripheral vein cortisol and aldosterone levels were recorded pre and post sedation, with the Selectivity index (SI) calculated. The number of adrenal vein samples with cortisol levels below 828 nmol/L (threshold for positive Point-of-care Quick-Cortisol Assay (POC-QCA)) was also recorded. Cortisol, aldosterone and selectivity index were compared using median, interquartile range and one-tail paired t-test. Fischer exact test was used to compare the number of negative POC-QCA.

Results

Fifty patients (52% male, mean age 51.3) were included. Following sedation, mean adrenal vein cortisol levels decreased significantly on both the right (2325.5 to 1018.5 nmol/L; p = 0.00012) and left (1659 to 933 nmol/L; p = 0.0020). Median SI also decreased significantly on the right (10.60 to 4.99; p = 0.00041) and left (6.99 to 3.93; p = 0.0012). There was a 90% increase in adrenal vein samples below the POC-QCA threshold (p-value = 0.0038).

Conclusion

Intraprocedural sedation had a significant impact on adrenal vein cortisol levels, which in turn impacts the SI. Interpretation of cannulation success following intravenous sedation based on POC-QCA or laboratory-measured cortisol requires care.

title: Microplastics and the urinary tract.
authorString: Loeb S, Trasande L, Albergamo V.

journal.title: Current opinion in nephrology and hypertension

abstractText:
Purpose of review

Microplastics and nanoplastics have been found in many human tissues including the urinary tract. However, less is known about downstream health impacts.

Recent findings

This review article highlights studies examining MNPs in urolithiasis and urinary tract cancers, including those of the kidney, bladder, and prostate. MNPs have been identified within urinary tract stones, as well as urinary tumor samples. Correlative laboratory studies suggest possible mechanistic pathways that MNPs may contribute to stone formation and carcinogenesis; however, further research is needed.

Summary

Early data suggest that MNPs may be associated with urolithiasis and urinary tract cancers. While preliminary, the growing literature on health impacts from MNPs suggests the importance of reducing individual plastic exposure and more broadly, to the need for greater regulation on plastic production and waste.

title: Intracranial Pressure Waveform Response to Hypertonic Saline Bolus in Patients with Traumatic Brain Injury.
authorString: Legé D, Dias C.
abstractText:
Objective

We aimed to identify features of intracranial compliance (ICC) reflected in intracranial pressure (ICP) waveform morphology following bolus of 20% hypertonic saline (HTS) to manage intracranial hypertension.

Methods

ICP was monitored during 89 HTS injections in ten patients with traumatic brain injury (TBI) and high intracranial hypertension. Pulse amplitude (AMP), P2/P1 ratio, pulse shape index (PSI), and normalized time to peak (TTP) were retrospectively analyzed over 3h including pre-, during, and postinjection interval. Trajectories of mean ICP and ICC surrogates were characterized using linear mixed models to assess individual contributions to the response following HTS injection.

Results

HTS injections induced transient decreases in all variables as follows: ICP [15.6 mmHg, 95% confidence interval (CI; 10.8, 20.3mmHg)], AMP [5.6 (3.5, 7.6mmHg)], P2/P1 [0.49 (0.32, 0.66)], PSI [0.65 (0.43, 0.87)], and TTP [0.054 (0.03, 0.07)]. Baseline P2/P1, TTP, and PSI showed predominantly between-patient variability [variance partition coefficient (VPC) = 0.56, 0.67, and 0.67, respectively], whereas baseline ICP and AMP showed greater within-patient variability (VPC = 0.18 and 0.24). Response-related features were also predominantly characterized by within-patient variability, with VPCs ranging from 0.20 to 0.27 for maximum decrease and from 0.13 to 0.23 for AAC. In random-intercept models, higher baseline ICP was associated with larger reductions in AMP (β = 0.13, p < 10-4), PSI (β = 0.02, p = 10-4), and TTP (β = 0.001, p = 0.034) following HTS administration, whereas baseline morphology metrics did not significantly improve the prediction of ICP reduction after adjustment for baseline ICP. When ICP nadir was modeled directly instead of the baseline-dependent change score, neither baseline ICP nor baseline morphology was significantly associated with ICP nadir. Adjustment for end-tidal CO2 (EtCO2) and prior osmotherapy did not materially alter these association patterns.

Conclusions

ICP waveform morphology, as assessed by P2/P1, PSI, and TTP, is influenced by changes in intracranial pressure but also retains substantial patient-specific variability. In contrast, AMP is primarily driven by changes in intracranial pressure.

title: Too close for comfort: a case report of a transmediastinal arrow injury in a young girl.
authorString: Giraldo-Grueso M, Rosenblum LT, Waltz P, Castro Medina M, Tang RCY.
abstractText: Transthoracic impalement injuries in pediatric patients are exceedingly rare, particularly when critical mediastinal structures are at risk. We report the case of a previously healthy 13-year-old girl who presented as a level 1 trauma case after falling onto an arrow, resulting in impalement through the right shoulder. Imaging revealed that the arrow traversed the right upper lobe of the lung and extended posterior to the carina and main bronchi, raising concern for esophageal and descending thoracic aortic injury. She underwent clamshell thoracotomy with cardiopulmonary bypass for safe evaluation and management. The arrow was removed without complications, pulmonary injuries were primarily repaired, and no esophageal, vascular, or airway injuries were identified. The patient recovered well postoperatively. This case underscores the importance of a multidisciplinary surgical approach, the value of advanced imaging and intraoperative endoscopy, and the utility of cardiopulmonary bypass in the safe management of complex penetrating thoracic trauma.

title: Beyond the spontaneous coronary artery dissection event: understanding psychological and socioeconomic differences among survivors.
authorString: Leissner P, Tornvall P.

title: The Post-ROSC Brugada-Pattern Algorithm: Validation and the Role of Genetic Testing.
authorString: Xu M, Ye W, Cen Y.

title: Comparative efficacy of modern antithrombotic regimens for saphenous vein graft patency after coronary artery bypass grafting: A systematic review and network meta-analysis.
authorString: Ansari AI, Tariq MF, Khan MU.
abstractText: Saphenous vein graft (SVG) occlusion remains common after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) despite aspirin. We compared contemporary postoperative antithrombotic regimens for preserving SVG patency. We conducted a systematic review and frequentist random-effects network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials. MEDLINE, Cochrane CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched through May 2026. The primary outcome was graft-level SVG occlusion. Aspirin was the reference treatment. Inconsistency was assessed using design-by-treatment interaction and node-splitting. Because multiple SVGs could arise from the same patient, we added a post-hoc variance-inflation sensitivity analysis using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) of 0.15, 0.20, and 0.25. Fifteen trials met review criteria; 10 contributed to the primary network (6,934 SVGs, 22 treatment arms, 7 nodes). Aspirin plus ticagrelor reduced SVG occlusion versus aspirin alone (OR 0.53, 95% CI 0.34-0.80; p = 0.003). Aspirin plus clopidogrel showed a non-significant possible benefit (OR 0.62, 95% CI 0.38-1.04; p = 0.070). Other regimens were not significantly different from aspirin. Aspirin plus ticagrelor ranked highest (P-score 0.88). Heterogeneity was moderate (I² = 52.6%). The aspirin plus ticagrelor finding remained significant after clustering variance inflation across ICCs 0.15-0.25 (adjusted OR approximately 0.53; all p ≤ 0.006). Aspirin plus ticagrelor was associated with lower graft-level SVG occlusion, but SVG patency is a surrogate outcome. Randomized evidence has not established corresponding reductions in major adverse cardiovascular events or mortality, while intensified dual antiplatelet therapy may increase bleeding. Treatment should therefore be individualized. This review was not prospectively registered. An a posteriori protocol and data repository was archived on OSF after screening and analysis had commenced: https://osf.io/qfwc9/.

title: When does personalization matter? An evidence-to-action beyond smart devices demonstrating the added clinical value of personalization in precision MedTech.
authorString: Qoronfleh MW.
abstractText:
Background

Precision medicine (PM) seeks to improve prevention, diagnosis, and treatment by incorporating biologic, clinical, environmental, and behavioral variation rather than relying exclusively on population averages. Medical technology (MedTech) provides a practical interface through which this approach can be translated into continuous sensing, decision support, and individualized intervention. We use the term personalized/precision medical devices (PMDs) for a conceptual class of devices that combine person-specific inputs with analytics and device-level configuration or adaptation. PMDs overlap with smart devices, connected health, and digital therapeutics, but are distinguished by their explicit coupling of individualized data to clinically meaningful device behavior.

Methods

This perspective uses a structured narrative literature approach. The literature survey was extended through targeted searches of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, Google Scholar, and major regulatory/standards sources for publications addressing precision or personalized medicine, biosensing, wearable and implantable devices, point-of-care diagnostics, automated drug delivery, digital therapeutics, artificial intelligence (AI), Internet of Medical Things (IoMT), interoperability, regulation, cybersecurity, and health equity [Oct. 2025-Oct. 2026]. Preference was given to peer-reviewed clinical studies, systematic reviews, authoritative regulatory guidance, and international standards. Evidence was synthesized narratively around a device lifecycle framework linking individual profile, sensing, data infrastructure, analytics, actuation, clinical workflow, evidence generation, and governance.

Results

Clinical evidence demonstrates that some components of the PMD concept are already established. In a randomized trial, automated insulin delivery increased time in the target glucose range by 14% points versus sensor-augmented pump therapy at 24 weeks. Remote pulmonary-artery pressure monitoring reduced heart-failure hospitalization by 28% in a prespecified analysis of patients with reduced ejection fraction. In the Apple Heart Study, 419,297 participants were enrolled; 0.52% received an irregular-pulse notification, and atrial fibrillation was identified in 34% of participants who returned an analyzable electrocardiographic patch. Digital therapeutics and adaptive neurostimulation further illustrate how software and implantable systems can individualize treatment, although clinical generalizability and long-term evidence remain uneven.

Conclusions

PMDs should be viewed as an engineering and clinical integration paradigm, not as a new regulatory category. Their value depends less on novelty of individual components than on reliable linkage among person-specific data, clinically validated algorithms, device actuation, and longitudinal feedback. Translation therefore requires evidence generation, interoperability, cybersecurity, lifecycle regulation, accountable AI, and equity-by-design. The next phase of precision MedTech will be defined by selective deployment of these capabilities where individualized sensing and adaptation demonstrably improve clinical outcomes or care efficiency.

title: Association between immune–inflammatory biomarkers and circulating levels of carbohydrate Antigen 125 in heart failure: protocol for a systematic review.
authorString: Fabunmi OA, Mxinwa V, Olaiya AO, Ogunmodede OS, Dludla PV, Nkambule BB.
abstractText: Background Cardiovascular diseases remain one of the leading causes of death worldwide, and heart failure (HF) represents a major global public health challenge, affecting an estimated 64 million people globally. The pathophysiology of HF is multifactorially complex and poorly understood. Understanding the role of inflammation in relation to CA125 levels will consolidate and enhance their clinical and prognostic value in the risk assessment, stratification and clinical management of HF. Hence, this review aims to provide a comprehensive synthesis of the available evidence on the relationship between immune-inflammatory activation and circulating CA125 concentrations in heart failure. Methods An extensive search will be conducted on the following databases: MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science. The Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature (CINAHL) and Cochrane Central Register of Clinical Trials (CENTRAL) will also be searched. Two reviewers will independently screen studies for eligibility using predefined criteria. The quality assessment and risk of bias of included studies will be assessed using the modified Downs and Black’s checklist. The Review Manager will be used for statistical analysis. The overall quality of included studies will be assessed using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation assessment tool. Discussions In HF management, biomarkers are essential for accurate diagnosis and risk stratification. CA125 has emerged as a key link between clinical congestion, immune-inflammatory activation, and adverse patient outcomes; however, current evidence regarding its inflammatory trigger remains fragmented. This review explores whether inflammatory pathways drive CA125 elevation independently of mechanical congestion, establishing its clinical utility and biological significance alongside conventional HF biomarkers. Ethics, patient and public involvement This is a review of existing studies and will not require ethical approval. Hence, patients and the public will not be involved in the study.  Systematic review registration : PROSPERO registration number: CRD42022310386.

title: Early defibrillation in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: A systematic synthesis of the time-dependent decline of shockable rhythms.
authorString: Cianciulli A, Nuccio E, Vellone E.
abstractText: This systematic review aimed to synthesize evidence on how shockable rhythms decline over time in adult out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) and to examine how defibrillation timing relates to rhythm deterioration and clinical outcomes. A systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. Electronic databases were searched for studies reporting initial rhythm distribution and time-to-defibrillation or untreated arrest duration in adult OHCA. Observational cohorts, registry-based studies, physiological waveform analyses, and randomized trials were included. Data were extracted on rhythm prevalence, time-related measures, defibrillation success, and clinical outcomes. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 and ROBINS-I tools. Thirty-eight studies published between 1990 and 2025 were included, encompassing more than 262,700 OHCA cases. Among unselected cohorts, the median prevalence of initial shockable rhythms was 33.5% (IQR 22.6-42.8%). Across study designs, increasing time-to-defibrillation was consistently associated with decreasing shockable rhythm prevalence and progressive transition to non-shockable rhythms. Physiological and AED waveform analyses demonstrated progressive deterioration of ventricular fibrillation with increasing untreated duration. Early defibrillation was associated with higher defibrillation success, increased return of spontaneous circulation, and improved survival outcomes. Shockable rhythms decline progressively with increasing untreated arrest duration, reflecting time-dependent electrical deterioration from ventricular fibrillation or pulseless ventricular tachycardia to non-shockable rhythms. These findings support the concept of a limited early shockable window in cardiac arrest and reinforce the critical importance of minimizing time-to-defibrillation across emergency response systems to improve survival in OHCA.

title: Efficiency, Efficacy, and Energy-Specific Safety of Pulsed Field Versus Thermal Ablation in Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation: Insights From Contemporary Randomized Data (the E<sup>3</sup>-PFA Collaboration).
authorString: Chen S, Ebrahimi R, Qin M, Zhong J, Zhang K, Chu H, Meyer C, Rillig A, Neven K, Heeger CH, Zylla MM, Perrotta L, Ruwald MH, Futyma P, Mulder BA, Zeng R, Hu H, Kiuchi MG, Liu H, Chen M, Pürerfellner H, Martinek M, Boveda S, Xue Y, Hou X, Liu X, Yin X, Jiang C, Yin Y, Schmidt B, Chun JKR, Narayan SM.
abstractText:
Background

Pulsed field ablation (PFA) is an increasingly adopted, minimally thermal modality for the ablation of atrial fibrillation, but its comparative performance versus contemporary thermal ablation strategies remains incompletely defined. We conducted an aggregate-data meta-analysis of contemporary randomized trials to compare procedural performance, safety, and clinical outcomes of PFA versus cryoballoon ablation and radiofrequency ablation in paroxysmal atrial fibrillation.

Methods

A systematic search identified 6 contemporary randomized controlled trials enrolling 2015 patients with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. Study-level random-effects meta-analyses were performed to compare procedural performance, peri-procedural safety, and atrial arrhythmia recurrence, with predefined subgroup analyses according to thermal ablation modality.

Results

PFA was associated with significantly shorter procedure time, left atrial dwell time, and total ablation time than thermal ablation (all P<0.001), whereas fluoroscopy time and anesthetic strategy were comparable between groups. PFA was associated with a significantly lower risk of peri-procedural serious adverse events than thermal ablation (risk ratio, 0.58 [95% CI, 0.35-0.96]; P=0.036). Persistent phrenic nerve palsy and pulmonary vein stenosis occurred exclusively after thermal ablation. Overall, PFA was associated with a lower risk of atrial arrhythmia recurrence than pooled thermal ablation (risk ratio, 0.86 [95% CI, 0.75-0.99]; P=0.03). Subgroup analyses demonstrated a significant reduction in recurrence compared with cryoballoon ablation (risk ratio, 0.80 [95% CI, 0.65-0.97]; P=0.03), whereas outcomes were comparable between PFA and contemporary radiofrequency (risk ratio, 0.93 [95% CI, 0.77-1.13]; P=0.48).

Conclusions

PFA provides greater procedural efficiency, improved peri-procedural safety, and a lower risk of atrial arrhythmia recurrence than pooled thermal ablation in patients with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. The efficacy advantage was primarily driven by comparisons with cryoballoon ablation, whereas outcomes were comparable between PFA and contemporary RFA.

title: Systematic Review of Patient Priorities and Shared Decision Making in Lower Extremity Peripheral Artery Disease Treatment Decisions.
authorString: De Louche CD, Shaltout S, Mazidi M, Beaney T, Bicknell CD, Woodward M, Pouncey AL.

journal.title: European journal of vascular and endovascular surgery : the official journal of the European Society for Vascular Surgery

abstractText:
Objectives

The aim of this review was to synthesise evidence on patient priorities, preferences for treatment, and shared decision making experiences in lower extremity peripheral artery disease (PAD) treatment decisions across intermittent claudication, chronic limb threatening ischaemia, and amputation level contexts.

Data sources

Key databases including MEDLINE and Embase.

Review methods

This was a systematic review (PROSPERO ID: CRD420251106155). Key databases including MEDLINE and Embase were searched for English language studies published from 1 January 2000 to 17 December 2025. Eligible studies included adults with symptomatic PAD, reporting experiences, information needs, priorities, or decision making related to PAD treatment. Two reviewers independently screened studies, resolving disagreements by consensus with a third reviewer. Study quality was assessed using design appropriate tools. Qualitative and quantitative findings were integrated using a structured thematic narrative approach.

Results

Thirty-four studies were included in the systematic review, comprising qualitative, mixed methods, observational registry or cohort, and stated preference studies, and one stepped wedge cluster randomised trial. Most qualitative and cohort studies were rated moderate to high quality. Participant reporting in the 34 studies was limited: seven studies (21%) did not report sex, two (6%) recruited men only, and most mixed sex studies recruited predominantly men; and 18 (53%) did not report ethnicity and, where reported, participants were predominantly White. Across heterogeneous studies, recurring patient valued domains included pain relief, walking ability, independence, emotional wellbeing, function, quality of life, treatment burden, risk, and uncertainty. Decision making processes were shaped by preferred involvement, trust, communication, clarity of options, and continuity of care. Studies identified a mismatch between patients' preferred and experienced decisional roles, with reported involvement lower than desired. Stated preference evidence showed heterogeneity in risk tolerance and treatment trade offs. Trial evidence reported improvements in shared decision making measures and patient knowledge after structured decision support and clinician training.

Conclusion

Patient valued outcomes and treatment trade offs vary across lower extremity PAD contexts and individuals. Shared decision making may help incorporate these priorities into treatment decisions, supported by tailored information, continuity of care, clinician training, and decision support tools.

title: Agents targeting the hallmarks of ageing: the geroscience pipeline in 2026.
authorString: Angioni D, Bellelli F, Michel E, de Souto Barreto P, Lucas A, Donega S, Cesari M, Cummings J, Ferrucci L, Balardy L, Sourdet S, Rolland Y, Vellas B.
abstractText: The hallmarks of ageing provide a conceptual framework for therapeutic development. We searched ClinicalTrials.gov for registered clinical trials that were ongoing as of Jan 1, 2026, and investigated pharmacological and biological agents targeting one or more hallmarks of ageing. Eligible trials were ongoing and involved adults (aged ≥18 years) and tested pharmacological or biological agents or products targeting one or more hallmarks of ageing. The search involved three steps with a focus on identifying trials conducted outside the context of a specific disease, to identify studies aimed at delaying biological ageing and preventing age-related functional decline; identifying trials assessing interventions targeting the most prevalent age-related diseases; and a further search using the names of the agents identified in the first two steps. We included 193 trials investigating 131 candidate treatments. Of these, 41 (21%) involved healthy individuals or individuals at risk of functional decline, and 152 (79%) targeted established age-related diseases. Most trials were early phase, comprising Phase 1 (61 [32%]) and Phase 2 (91 [47%]), and 41 (21%) were Phase 3. Altered intercellular communication was the most frequently targeted hallmark (64 [33%]), followed by deregulated nutrient sensing (48 [25%]), chronic inflammation (32 [17%]), and stem cell exhaustion (26 [13%]). Our findings show that although many ongoing trials target biological mechanisms considered hallmarks of ageing, most studies are in early phases and mainly aim to treat age-related diseases rather than to delay or prevent age-related decline.

title: Effect of Cysteamine on 90-Day Mortality in Patients With Severe Community-Acquired Pneumonia: The REMAP-CAP (Randomized Embedded Multifactorial Adaptive Platform for Community-Acquired Pneumonia) Randomized Clinical Trial.
authorString: Shankar-Hari M, Ryan EG, Pogson D, Golden D, Puxty K, Walden A, Craven TH, Derde L, Gordon AC.
abstractText: Cysteamine has antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory and antibiotic-potentiating effects. We evaluated IV cysteamine in critically ill patients with community-acquired pneumonia within REMAP-CAP (Randomized Embedded Multifactorial Adaptive Platform for Community-Acquired Pneumonia) trial, an international adaptive platform trial evaluating multiple interventions across several therapeutic domains. Adults requiring respiratory or cardiovascular organ support were randomized within the cysteamine domain to IV cysteamine (5 mg/kg every 8 hr for up to 10 d) or control. The dichotomous primary outcome was 90-day all-cause mortality, analyzed using Bayesian logistic regression. Recruitment to this domain stopped for operational futility before predefined statistical thresholds were met. Thirty-six patients received cysteamine (n = 19) or control (n = 17). Ninety-day mortality was 26% vs. 35%, respectively (odds ratio 0.64, 95% credible interval 0.18-2.19), with a 76% posterior probability of benefit. One serious adverse event occurred, unrelated to cysteamine. These preliminary findings suggest possible benefit, but the small sample size precludes definitive efficacy conclusions. Further studies of cysteamine in severe pneumonia are warranted.

title: Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair for Severe Isolated Tricuspid Regurgitation After Extended Follow-Up: The TRI-FR Randomized Clinical Trial.
authorString: Donal E, Dreyfus J, Leurent G, Nejjari M, Auffret V, Guerin P, Modine T, Le Roux PY, Ganivet A, Sportouch-Dukhan C, Lavie-Badie Y, Rouleau F, Diakov C, Vola M, Bernard A, Neylon A, Pierrard R, Ternacle J, Tchetche D, Ghostine S, Ducrocq G, Si Moussi T, Peltier M, Le Dolley Y, Deharo P, Le Ven F, Picard F, Piriou N, Urena-Alcazar M, Laperche T, Jouan J, Bonnet G, de Groote P, Anselmi A, Trochu JN, Steg PG, Coisne A, Oger E, TRI-FR Investigators.
abstractText:
Background

Transcatheter tricuspid edge-to-edge repair (T-TEER) improves symptoms and health status at 1 year in patients with severe tricuspid regurgitation, but its association with clinical events during longer follow-up remains uncertain.

Methods
