This secondary analysis reports extended follow-up of TRI-FR (URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT04646811), a prospectively registered, multicenter randomized trial comparing T-TEER plus optimized medical therapy (OMT) with OMT alone in patients with severe symptomatic tricuspid regurgitation. In total, 300 patients were randomized (152 to T-TEER plus OMT and 148 to OMT alone). Prespecified analyses included time to first heart failure hospitalization (HFH), tricuspid surgery, or cardiovascular death using cause-specific Cox proportional-hazards models and recurrent HFH using the Lin-Wei-Yang-Ying model. A 12-month landmark analysis included patients alive and under follow-up at 12 months.

Results

During a median follow-up of 30.8 months (75th percentile, 41.0; maximum, 56.4), 101 HFHs (17 fatal), 5 additional cardiovascular deaths, and 11 tricuspid surgeries were recorded. Among 81 patients with a first composite event, T-TEER plus OMT reduced the risk versus OMT alone (hazard ratio, 0.56 [95% CI, 0.36-0.88]; P=0.0109). Cardiovascular death or tricuspid surgery did not differ significantly (hazard ratio, 0.75 [95% CI, 0.33-1.71]; P=0.4911). T-TEER plus OMT reduced recurrent HFH (Lin-Wei-Yang-Ying rate ratio, 0.52 [95% CI, 0.32-0.84]; P=0.0073). In the 12-month landmark cohort (n=276), T-TEER plus OMT was associated with lower risks of a first composite event (hazard ratio, 0.40 [95% CI, 0.23-0.70]; log-rank P=0.0009) and recurrent HFH (Lin-Wei-Yang-Ying rate ratio, 0.44 [95% CI, 0.23-0.83]; P=0.0120). Severe or greater tricuspid regurgitation at the last core laboratory assessment was present in 6.77% with T-TEER plus OMT and 53.5% with OMT alone (P<0.0001).

Conclusions

In patients with severe symptomatic tricuspid regurgitation, T-TEER plus OMT reduced first composite events and recurrent HFH compared with OMT alone during extended follow-up. These associations persisted among patients alive and under follow-up at the 12-month landmark.

Registration

URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT04646811.

title: Protection by ascorbate and catechin at high physiological concentrations against myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury in an isolated rat heart model.
authorString: Abou Hadeed A, Omidian K, Rafiei H, Lee P, Bandy B.

journal.title: Applied physiology, nutrition, and metabolism = Physiologie appliquee, nutrition et metabolisme

abstractText: Myocardial ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) injury is an important health concern in myocardial infarction and situations such as angioplasty and cardiac surgeries. Ascorbate (vitamin C) and flavonoids such as catechin are known for their antioxidant activity and are of interest as supplements or added to perfused blood during surgeries to limit I/R injury. While intravenous ascorbate during surgeries has been studied in clinical trials, it has usually been at high pharmacological concentrations (with potential unwanted prooxidant activity). The objectives of this study were to 1) determine the extent to which ascorbate or catechin alone, added to the perfusate at levels which could be in blood after dietary supplementation, can protect myocardial tissue in the reperfusion phase of I/R injury, and 2) evaluate the possible cooperative or synergistic protective effect of ascorbate and catechin when given together. Isolated rat hearts (n=48) were perfused in the retrograde mode with modified Krebs-Henseleit buffer, and following the induction of 30 min global ischemia, ascorbate (150 μM) and/or catechin (5 μM) were added directly into the perfusate during 90 min reperfusion. The experiments showed that 150 μM ascorbate protected the heart against lipid peroxidation and cell apoptosis by 100%, while 5 μM catechin protected by 67% and 90% respectively. Due to the strong protection by ascorbate alone, no cooperative protective effect could be observed when ascorbate and catechin were used together. In conclusion, this preclinical study showed strong protection against myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury by ascorbate in the perfusate at a much lower concentration than most clinical trials, and protection by catechin at a physiological dose.

title: Comparing the Effects of high-quality simulation-based education and video-based education on knowledge, skills, and self-confidence in learning the out-of-hospital chain of survival among adolescent students.
authorString: Zamani M, Keshmiri F, Abarghouei SA, Nasiriani K.
abstractText: Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest is a major public health concern, accounting for a significant number of deaths worldwide. Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) training is recommended for the general population, particularly adolescent students, who represent a substantial segment of society. Effective CPR training may improve bystander response and contribute to better resuscitation outcomes. However, determining the most effective educational approach remains a challenge. This study compared the effects of high-quality simulation-based education (HQSBE) and video-based education (VBE) on the knowledge, performance, and self-confidence of adolescent students regarding the out-of-hospital chain of survival. This randomized pretest-posttest controlled study was conducted among120 male second-grade secondary school students selected through multistage random sampling. Participants were randomly assigned to two groups: the VBE group, which received a 45-minute CPR training video followed by discussion, and the HQSBE group, which received a 45-minute high-quality simulation-based training on the out-of-hospital chain of survival. Knowledge and self-confidence were assessed before, immediately after, and one month after training, while CPR skills were assessed immediately and one month after training. Data were analyzed using repeated-measures analysis of variance, independent- and paired-samples t-tests, Bonferroni-adjusted pairwise comparisons, and using SPSS version 22. A total of 111 students were included in the final analysis.Both groups showed significant changes in CPR knowledge and self-confidence over time (p < 0.001). The HQSBE group achieved significantly higher knowledge, CPR skill, and self-confidence scores than the VBE group immediately after training and at one month (all p < 0.001). CPR skills declined significantly in the VBE group, whereas the decline in the HQSBE group was not statistically significant (p = 0.054). A significant time × group interaction was observed for CPR skills (p = 0.014), indicating different patterns of change between groups. Both VBE and HQSBE improved adolescents' CPR knowledge, practical skills, and self-confidence, while the HQSBE group achieved higher scores for all three outcomes immediately after training and at the one-month follow-up. These findings support the potential value of simulation-based education for school-based CPR training, while VBE may provide a feasible and standardized alternative when simulation resources are limited.

title: Instant message-delivered dyadic intervention in sodium reduction for hypertensive stroke survivors: A randomised controlled trial
authorString: Yan Y, Wang MP, Lau KK, Chen H, Yang Y, Yang Z, Ye F, Montayre J, Lee JJ.
abstractText: High sodium intake is the primary dietary risk factor for stroke. This trial allocated 110 stroke survivor-family caregiver dyads to the intervention(sodium reduction messages plus nurse-led chat support via an instant messaging application) or control group(general stroke-education messages). Stroke survivors showed significant improvements in knowledge, attitude, and practice regarding sodium reduction(KAP) at post-intervention(T1) (β = 10.44, 95% confidence interval[CI] 5.22 to 15.66, d = 0.75) and 2-month follow-up(T2) (β = 9.20, 95% CI 3.70 to 14.70, d = 0.71), systolic blood pressure(SBP) at T1 (β=−6.19, 95% CI − 9.92 to − 2.47, d = − 0.64) and T2 (β=−4.15, 95% CI − 8.13 to − 0.18, d = − 0.42), diastolic blood pressure(DBP) at T1 (β=−3.65, 95% CI − 6.64 to − 0.66, d = − 0.49), self-efficacy at T1, and dyadic relationship at T2. Family caregivers showed improved KAP at both time points and self-efficacy at T1 without increasing caregiving burden. The intervention was an effective and scalable approach to improve sodium reduction-related outcomes and BP control in stroke survivors with hypertension.

title: Real-World Outcomes of First-Line Capecitabine-Oxaliplatin With or Without Bevacizumab for Unresectable Metastatic Colon Cancer: Experience From HoChi Minh City Oncology Hospital in a Lower-Middle-Income Country
authorString: Duc PTH, Trong NT, Quy NH.
abstractText: Background Despite substantial advances in systemic therapy, metastatic colorectal cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. The addition of bevacizumab to oxaliplatin-based chemotherapy has demonstrated improved clinical outcomes in randomized clinical trials. However, real-world evidence from low- and middle-income countries, where access to targeted therapies is often limited by financial constraints, remains scarce. Objective To evaluate the real-world effectiveness and safety of first-line CapeOX with or without bevacizumab in patients with unresectable metastatic colon cancer treated at Ho Chi Minh City Oncology Hospital. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study including 70 consecutive patients with histologically confirmed unresectable metastatic colon adenocarcinoma who received first-line CapeOX alone or CapeOX plus bevacizumab at Ho Chi Minh City Oncology Hospital between June 1, 2021, and June 30, 2023. Tumor response was assessed according to RECIST version 1.1, adverse events were graded using CTCAE version 5.0, and progression-free survival (PFS) was estimated using the Kaplan–Meier method. Results Among patients treated with CapeOX alone, the objective response rate (ORR) was 46.6%, the disease control rate (DCR) was 86.6%, and the median progression-free survival (mPFS) was 9.2 months (95% confidence interval [CI], 8.6–10.8). The most common treatment-related adverse events were thrombocytopenia, neutropenia, diarrhea, nausea, and vomiting, most of which were grade 1–2. In the CapeOX plus bevacizumab group, the ORR and DCR were 55.0% and 92.5%, respectively, with a median PFS of 11.5 months (95% CI, 10.2–13.0). Hypertension was the most common bevacizumab-related adverse event. Overall, toxicities were manageable, and no unexpected safety signals were observed. Conclusions In this real-world cohort from a tertiary oncology center in Vietnam, the addition of bevacizumab to first-line CapeOX was associated with higher response rates and longer progression-free survival compared with CapeOX alone, while maintaining an acceptable safety profile. These findings support the effectiveness and feasibility of bevacizumab-containing therapy in routine clinical practice, particularly in resource-constrained healthcare settings where access to targeted therapy remains limited.

title: Dose-Response Effects of Linoleic Acid-Rich Cottonseed Oil on Markers of Inflammation and Coagulation Potential in Adults at Risk for Cardiovascular Disease.
authorString: Rigdon HC, Hawkins CD, Prater MC, Ward CA, Cooper JA.

journal.title: Journal of the American Nutrition Association

abstractText: Chronic low-grade inflammation and coagulation potential heighten cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk. Cottonseed oil (CSO), an omega-6 (n-6) polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA)-rich oil, has been shown to improve CVD risk factors, indicating that its physiological impacts may differ from previous assumptions. To examine the impact of varying doses of CSO on markers of inflammation and coagulation potential. Ninety adults at risk for CVD completed a randomized controlled trial with a 4-week partial outpatient feeding intervention. Participants were randomized into one of four groups: LOW (n = 23), MID (n = 23), or HIGH (n = 22), providing 10%, 20%, or 30% of estimated energy needs from CSO, respectively, or control (CON) (n = 22), receiving 10% of EEN from an oil mix. Fasting blood draws were collected at pre- and post-intervention and analyzed for markers of inflammation (tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), interleukin-6 (IL-6), C-reactive protein (CRP), interleukin-1β (IL-1β)) and coagulation potential (tissue factor (TF) and plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 (PAI-1)). To account for multiple outcomes, p-values were adjusted using the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) procedure. There were no significant main effects or interactions for fasting IL-6, TNF-α, or PAI-1 across the intervention. Although significant unadjusted group, visit, and group-by-visit effects were observed for CRP, IL-1β, or TF, only the main effect of group for CRP remained significant following the FDR procedure (FDR p = 0.03), with post hoc analyses indicating lower concentrations in HIGH vs. both LOW (p = 0.02) and MID (p < 0.01), regardless of visit. No other findings remained significant after FDR correction. Adults at risk for CVD did not experience worsening of inflammation and coagulation potential markers when consuming CSO-enriched diets across a range of doses. This demonstrates that n-6 PUFAs may not negatively impact these CVD risk factors, even in less healthy populations. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier NCT05686954.

title: Right Ventricular Reverse Remodeling Without Pulmonary Vascular Unloading During Sotatercept Therapy: An Invasive Pressure-Volume Loop Study.
authorString: Kremer N, Lemay SE, Valasarajan C, Thal BR, Harth S, Rako ZA, Janetzko P, Yogeswaran A, Wang S, Olapoju SO, Sanda M, Mamazhakypov A, Vanderpool RR, Gattenlöhner S, Rosenkranz S, Ballmann F, Rischard FP, Waxman AB, Kojonazarov B, Schermuly RT, Potus F, Provencher S, Seeger W, Ghofrani HA, Pullamsetti SS, Bonnet S, Tello K.
abstractText:
Background

Sotatercept improves hemodynamics and functional capacity in pulmonary arterial hypertension; however, its direct actions on the right ventricle (RV) remain poorly understood. We investigated whether sotatercept exerts intrinsic RV protective effects beyond pulmonary vascular unloading.

Methods

In this registry-based cohort study, 28 consecutive patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension between April 2024 and September 2025 underwent right-heart catheterization with conductance-catheter RV pressure-volume analysis and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging before sotatercept initiation and again after a median of 6.1 months of treatment. Hemodynamic nonresponse was defined as a decrease in mean pulmonary arterial pressure by <10%. Reproducibility was tested in 2 independent sotatercept-treated cohorts (SPECTRA [Sotatercept Phase 2 Exploratory Clinical Trial in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension], n=20, cardiac magnetic resonance; Cologne, n=20, echocardiography).

Results

Among 28 patients (17 [61%] female; median age, 48 [IQR, 34-67] years), 21 (75%) were responders and 7 (25%) nonresponders. In responders, sotatercept significantly decreased mean pulmonary arterial pressure (52.0 [IQR, 49.0-65.0] to 39.0 [IQR, 32.0-42.0] mm Hg; P<0.001) and pulmonary vascular resistance (10.7±3.9 to 6.7±2.3 Wood units; P<0.001) without changing cardiac output, reduced RV end-diastolic volume (222 [IQR, 183-242] to 160 [IQR, 129-204] mL; P<0.001) and RV mass (42.8 [IQR, 33.6-56.0] to 33.1 [IQR, 28.2-44.4] g; P<0.001), and improved 6-minute walk distance by +64 m (95% CI, 27 to 102; P=0.002). Ventricular-arterial coupling (end-systolic/arterial elastance) improved although load-independent contractility decreased alongside the decrease in effective arterial elastance. By contrast, nonresponders demonstrated a clinical-hemodynamic disconnect. Despite persistently elevated RV afterload and unchanged end-systolic/arterial elastance, a significant reduction in RV mass (56.1 [IQR, 45.9-81.0] to 46.4 [IQR, 35.9-59.4] g; P=0.003) was observed, accompanied by a significant decrease in B-type natriuretic peptide levels, whereas 6-minute walk distance did not change significantly (+15 m [95% CI, -12 to 42]; P=0.23); the difference in 6-minute walk distance change between groups did not reach significance (P=0.10). Reduction in RV mass and chamber size was observed in the absence of pulmonary vascular unloading among hemodynamic nonresponders to sotatercept in 2 independent cohorts.

Conclusions

In primary and validation cohorts, structural RV reverse remodeling after sotatercept initiation occurred independent of pulmonary vascular unloading. This pattern is not fully explained by pulmonary vascular unloading and raises the possibility of an effect of sotatercept on the myocardium itself. Improvement in exercise capacity was observed within the hemodynamic responder group only.

title: The effects of a Graduated Exercise-Based Prehabilitation Program on physical function and respiratory muscle strength(GEtFit) in individuals awaiting Cardiac Surgery: A RCT study protocol.
authorString: Katijjahbe MA, El-Ansary D, Azmi NA, Ahmad S, Ismail N, Royse C, Royse A, Haron H, Abdul Manaf MR, Wen APY, Ismail I, Md Ali NA.
abstractText: Preoperative exercise-based rehabilitation programs have gained recognition as a safe intervention to improve physical readiness for surgery, functional capacity, and quality of life. However, evidence supporting exercise-based prehabilitation in patients undergoing cardiothoracic surgery remains limited. The protocol describes a randomised control trial comparing a graduated exercise-based prehabilitation compared to early upper limb exercise on physical function and recovery for patients awaiting cardiac surgery. This prospective, randomized controlled trial incorporates concealed allocation, assessor blinding, and intention‑to‑treat analysis. The study aims to determine the effects of a graduated exercise‑based prehabilitation program in enhancing physical function, assessed using the 6‑minute walk test, and respiratory muscle strength in individuals scheduled for cardiothoracic surgery. Secondary objectives include evaluating effects on patient‑reported outcomes (pain and fatigue), upper‑limb function, multidomain recovery, anxiety and depression, quality of life, and postoperative complications, including pulmonary and sternal complications. A total of 140 participants undergoing elective cardiothoracic surgery via median sternotomy will be randomly assigned to receive either standard care or a graduated exercise‑based prehabilitation intervention incorporating an additional respiratory muscle training protocol not included in routine cardiac rehabilitation. The primary hypothesis will be tested by comparing baseline to 4‑week changes between groups. Data will be analyzed using mixed model ANCOVA with statistical significance set at p < 0.05. Recruitment for the trial is currently ongoing. Despite heterogeneous regimens and inconsistent outcomes, exercise‑based prehabilitation in cardiac surgery warrants adoption, as frail, comorbid patients benefit in recovery and quality of life where findings will guide optimal exercise dosage and intensity. Australia and New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry (ANZCTR) 2024 (ACTRN12624000932561). version 2 dated 13 November 2025.

title: Comparative effectiveness of initiating nifedipine versus labetalol in early gestation for chronic hypertension in pregnancy.
authorString: Latour CD, Ponder M, Boggess K, Edwards JK, Funk MJ, Hinton SP, Schnitzer ME, Suarez EA, Wood ME.

journal.title: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM

abstractText:
Background

Following the Chronic Hypertension and Pregnancy (CHAP) trial, clinical guidelines were changed to recommend pharmacologic treatment of both mild and severe chronic hypertension during pregnancy. However, uncertainty remains regarding the comparative safety and effectiveness of commonly used first-line agents, nifedipine and labetalol. Evidence from randomized trials is limited, and ongoing trials may have restricted generalizability to real-world populations. Prior observational studies have largely restricted analyses to pregnancies ending in delivery, potentially introducing selection bias and precluding evaluation of miscarriage, an important but understudied outcome. Robust real-world evidence that captures the full spectrum of pregnancy outcomes is therefore needed to inform clinical decision-making.

Objectives

We conducted a target trial emulation to compare nifedipine versus labetalol initiation before 23 weeks' gestation for risk of pregnancy loss (miscarriage or stillbirth) and preterm birth (<37 weeks) among a cohort of pregnancies with observed (e.g., live birth, spontaneous abortion) and unobserved (i.e., lost to follow-up) outcomes.

Study design

We used a novel algorithm to identify pregnancies in the Merative MarketScan Commercial Claims and Encounters Database with estimated last menstrual periods between July 1, 2016 and February 1, 2022. We included those with a new nifedipine or labetalol fill before 23 weeks' gestation. We estimated risks, risk differences (RDs) per 100 pregnancies, and risk ratios (RRs) among nifedipine versus labetalol initiators using a weighted Aalen-Johansen estimator to account for confounding, informative censoring, and competing risks. We also conducted a post hoc analysis to estimate the comparative effect of nifedipine versus labetalol on risk of preeclampsia. We considered multiple sensitivity analyses to evaluate the robustness of our primary results to assumptions regarding informative censoring, gestational age misestimation, residual confounding, outcome misclassification, target population misspecification, and measurement error in censoring dates.

Results

We identified 987 nifedipine and 4,570 labetalol initiators during the study period; 22.2% of nifedipine and 10.0% of labetalol initiators filled a prescription for a different antihypertensive over follow-up. The weighted risk of pregnancy loss was 7.0% among nifedipine and 6.0% among labetalol initiators (RD=1.1 [-0.7, 2.8]; RR=1.18 [0.87, 1.59]). Weighted risks of preterm birth were 29.4% versus 22.2%, respectively (RD=7.2 [3.9, 10.5], RR=1.32 [1.13, 1.55]). In post hoc analyses, the weighted risks of preeclampsia were 38.6% versus 33.9%, respectively (RD=4.7 [0.7, 8.7], RR=1.14 [1.01, 1.28]). Findings were consistent across sensitivity analyses.

Conclusions

Compared to labetalol initiators, nifedipine initiators experienced an increased risk of preterm birth but not pregnancy loss. The elevated risk of preterm birth may be explained by an increased risk of preeclampsia among nifedipine initiators, resulting in medically indicated preterm birth. These findings may reflect differences in adherence, patient characteristics, or clinical context in real-world practice and should be interpreted alongside existing trial evidence supporting the use of either medication.

title: Family Resilience and Dyadic Health Outcomes in Heart Failure: An Integrative Review of Pathways and Underlying Mechanisms.
authorString: Zhu Z, Li S, Ji S, Yang R, Wang W, Hou Y.
abstractText: Heart failure (HF) affects more than 64 million people worldwide and places substantial physical, emotional, and financial burdens on patients and family caregivers. Although family resilience is a crucial protective factor in chronic illness, evidence concerning its role in HF dyads remains fragmented because quantitative and qualitative findings have not been sufficiently integrated across populations and study designs. This integrative review synthesized evidence on family resilience in HF patient-caregiver dyads, examined its mechanisms and asymmetric effects, and identified implications for practice and research. A systematic search of 13 databases was conducted from inception to February 15, 2026. Of 677 records identified, 34 studies met the inclusion criteria. Design-appropriate tools were used for quality appraisal, and thematic synthesis was guided by the Walsh Family Resilience Framework. Family resilience operated through three core dimensions: belief systems, organizational patterns, and communication processes. Its protective effects were mediated by mutuality, resilience, and self-efficacy and moderated by factors including disease stage and gender. Dyadic care and management patterns ranged from patient-oriented and caregiver-oriented approaches to collaborative and complementary approaches. Four intervention strategies were identified: assessment and stratification, dyadic interaction and caregiver empowerment, multi-target integration, and strengths-based care. These findings support the development of family-centered care programs to improve continuity of care, quality of life, and health outcomes in HF dyads. Longitudinal studies and randomized clinical trials are needed to further examine the dynamic nature of family resilience.

title: Time to treatment of critical hypertension within 30 minutes and obstetrical outcomes.
authorString: Kobara E, Miller E, Rajesh R, Vertichio R, Akerman M, Prasannan L, Suhag A.

journal.title: The journal of maternal-fetal & neonatal medicine : the official journal of the European Association of Perinatal Medicine, the Federation of Asia and Oceania Perinatal Societies, the International Society of Perinatal Obstetricians

abstractText:
Objective

This study aimed to evaluate whether treatment of critical hypertension within 30 min, compared to treatment greater than or equal to 30 min, is associated with lower severe maternal morbidity (SMM).

Study design

This retrospective cohort study analyzed pregnant patients with singleton gestations ≥20 weeks with critical hypertension [defined as persistent HTN with 2 consecutive SBP ≥160 or DBP ≥110 mm HG at least 15 min apart], who delivered between January 2021 and December 2022 at a single tertiary care center. Time to treatment was measured from the confirmatory second blood pressure reading to the time of antihypertensive administration. The study compared Group A (treatment time <30 min) with Group B (treatment time ≥30 min). The primary outcome was composite SMM, and secondary outcomes included composite severe neonatal morbidity (SNM), preterm birth, placental abruption, non-reassuring fetal heart tracing (NRFHT), and postpartum readmission. Multivariable logistic regression was adjusted for a set of baseline confounders. Statistical significance was set as p < 0.05.

Results

Out of 370 patients screened, 271 met inclusion criteria (214 in Group A and 57 in Group B). Median time to treatment was 11 min (IQR 6-17) in Group A and 47 min (IQR 38-194) in Group B. Compared with Group B, patients in Group A were younger and had higher admission systolic and diastolic blood pressures. SMM occurred in 27 (12.6%) patients in Group A and 11 (19.3%) in Group B (unadjusted odds ratio [OR] for Group B vs. Group A 1.66, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.77-3.58; adjusted OR 1.77, 95% CI 0.80-3.91). SNM occurred in 56 (26.2%) and 14 (24.6%) patients, respectively (unadjusted OR 0.92, 95% CI 0.47-1.81). Results were consistent across sensitivity analyses, and no secondary outcome differed significantly between groups.

Conclusion

In this single-center retrospective cohort, we did not detect a statistically significant difference in SMM between patients treated within 30 min and those treated later. The confidence intervals were wide and do not exclude a clinically important benefit of earlier treatment, and these findings should not be interpreted as evidence of equivalence. Treatment of acute-onset severe hypertension as soon as reasonably possible should remain the standard, and adequately powered prospective studies, including randomized trials, are needed to define the optimal treatment interval.

title: First-in-Man Use of the Tau20-RETROmapping System to Identify and Guide Ablation of Ectopy-Triggering Ganglionated Plexuses During Sinus Rhythm as Nonpulmonary Vein Drivers of Atrial Fibrillation.
authorString: Kay J, Koutsoftidis S, Bissett S, Demircali AA, Zheng Q, Heaney F, Coyle C, Jones O, Kim MY, Jose I, Chow JJ, Malcolme-Lawes L, Lim E, Fudge M, Wright I, Keene D, Arnold A, Koa-Wing M, Ng FS, Qureshi N, Peters N, Whinnett Z, Lim PB, Baykaner T, Zaman J, Lewalter T, Temelkuran B, Linton N, Drakakis E, Kanagaratnam P.
abstractText:
Background

Pulmonary vein (PV) isolation is ineffective in a proportion of patients with atrial fibrillation (AF). The Tau20-RETROmapping system was developed to help identify non-PV drivers of AF. We tested the feasibility of using the system to guide ablation of non-PV drivers during sinus rhythm.

Methods

This was a prospective feasibility study of only non-PV ablation in patients with symptomatic AF. The Tau20-RETROmapping system was used to identify ectopy-triggering ganglionated plexus (ET-GP) in the left atrium with synchronized high-frequency stimulation (50 mA, 40 Hz, 80 ms, 15 trains) during sinus rhythm. ET-GP sites were ablated with radiofrequency lesions until they were nonfunctional. Triggered atrial tachycardias were also mapped and ablated. Patients were followed for 12 months with scheduled Holter monitoring and patient-activated ECG recordings. The primary end point was atrial arrhythmia lasting ≥30 seconds after a 90-day blanking period.

Results

Twenty-three patients were recruited: 8 patients with AF despite durably isolated PVs and 15 undergoing a first procedure for persistent AF. On average, 85±15 sites were tested in patients with isolated PVs (2.5±0.9 previous AF ablations, 61±9 years, LVEF 58±5%, LAd 41±2 mm), identifying 11.8±3.8 ET-GPs. Four of the eight patients also had ablation of triggered atrial tachycardias. Of the 15 patients undergoing a first procedure for persistent AF (duration 2.8±1.1 years, continuous AF ≥6 months in 80%, 64±7 years, LAd 43±2 mm), 10 completed a full left atrial ET-GP map of 102±37 tested sites. identifying 14±4.5 ET-GP sites. After a mean follow-up of 12 months and cessation of antiarrhythmic agents, arrhythmia-free survival was 63% in patients with durably isolated veins and 60% in those undergoing a first procedure for persistent AF.

Conclusions

The Tau20-RETROmapping system can identify and guide ablation of high-frequency stimulation-provoked ectopy-triggering ganglionated plexus during sinus rhythm as potential non-PV drivers of AF. This feasibility study shows promising outcomes that need exploration in larger randomized controlled studies.

title: Global and local genetic correlations between hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and atrial fibrillation: comparison of two linkage disequilibrium reference panels
authorString: Xu D, Yu Z, Li A, Liu Z, Chen Q, Liu J, Sun H.
abstractText: Background Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and atrial fibrillation are clinically associated, but their genetic associations may differ in direction across the genome. We examined their overall and local genetic correlations and whether local findings persisted after changing the linkage disequilibrium reference panel. Methods We reanalyzed public genome-wide association summary statistics, retaining the original variant set and 695 previously eligible regions. Each region used the same final variants with the 1000 Genomes European and UK Biobank European reference panels. Genome-wide uncertainty was calculated from the complete sampling covariance matrix. Local analyses used separate Benjamini–Hochberg and Benjamini–Yekutieli corrections, each with a fixed family of 695 tests. Results The genome-wide genetic correlation was 0.0964 (standard error 0.0442; 95% confidence interval 0.0098–0.1830; P = 0.0291). Local correlations were estimable in 542 regions with the 503-person 1000 Genomes panel and 192 with the 100000-person UK Biobank panel. Benjamini–Hochberg correction identified 38 and 10 significant regions, respectively. Among 187 regions estimable with both panels, 150 had the same sign and 37 had opposite signs. Eight regions were significant with both panels, including four positive and four negative correlations; four also passed Benjamini–Yekutieli correction with both. All eight belonged to the 45 regions significant in the original analysis. Conclusions A small positive overall correlation coexisted with local correlations in both directions. However, local estimability and significance depended on the reference panel, even with matched variants. The comparison reused the same disease association data and is not independent replication. Mixed ancestry in the cardiomyopathy study and incomplete variant-level cohort information limit interpretation of these regional findings. Clinical trial registration Clinical trial number: not applicable.

title: Cross-Registry Coverage of Registered Septal-Reduction Studies for Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: A WHO ICTRP Audit
authorString: Sui Y, Nie X, Tang J, Xing Q.
abstractText: Background Septal-reduction therapy is the definitive treatment for drug-refractory outflow tract obstruction in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, but the composition of its registered evidence is unknown. Methods We searched the WHO International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (ICTRP) on 9 October 2026 using nine prespecified searches covering the condition and all septal-reduction modalities. Eligibility required a septal-reduction modality in the WHO Trial Registration Data Set intervention field or, failing that, the title; pharmacological-only and peri-procedural-care studies were excluded. Registry source, prospective registration, recorded recruitment country, portal-visible results and record freshness were extracted; proportions carry Wilson 95% confidence intervals and contrasts are reported as odds ratios. Results The nine searches returned 210 rows representing 92 unique registrations, of which 73 were eligible (ClinicalTrials.gov 40, ChiCTR 27, four further registries 6). A recruitment country was recorded for 63 registrations, 48 in China. Percutaneous or endocardial septal ablation accounted for 29 of the 45 China-recruited registrations using that technique or surgery, versus 3 of 20 elsewhere (odds ratio 10.3, 95% CI 2.6–40.4; p = 0.0003); significance was not preserved under the most conservative assignment of the ten registrations lacking a recorded country (p = 0.075). Prospective registration was recorded for 40 registrations (54.8%) and portal-visible results information for 1 (1.4%, 95% CI 0.2–7.4). Conclusions The retrieved portfolio is concentrated in two registries, dominated by registrations recruiting in China, and almost devoid of portal-visible results information, although registered studies have published findings. Completion date and summary results already form part of the WHO Trial Registration Data Set; the priority is timely, complete entry and verified transmission of those elements to the aggregator.

title: Depression, diabetes, hypertension and the risk of incident dementia: a 3-million-person multicenter cohort study using Italian administrative health data.
authorString: Zenesini C, Cascini S, Picariello R, Profili F, Belotti LMB, Maniscalco L, Fantaci G, Acampora A, Ribaudo M, Gnavi R, Francesconi P, Vignatelli L, Nonino F, Bargagli AM, Tarantino D, Salemi G, Matranga D, Vanacore N.
abstractText:
Introduction

To address dementia as a major public health challenge, we evaluated the impact of hypertension, diabetes, depression, and their interactions on dementia onset using an Italian common data model.

Methods

A cohort of over 3 million individuals aged 50 years or older, initially free from dementia, depression, diabetes and hypertension, was followed across five Italian regions and cities (2011-2022). All pathological conditions were identified from algorithms applied to administrative health data. Time-dependent exposures were analyzed using competing risks regression, adjusted for confounders, with mortality as a competing event, and pooled via meta-analysis.

Results

Of the total cohort, 33% lived in Latium, 29% in Piedmont, 27% in Tuscany, 6% in Bologna and 4% in Trapani. The five cohorts showed similar mean age (63-65 years) and a slight predominance of women (52-55%). Dementia risk was strongly associated with depression (sub-hazard ratio [SHR]=4.55; 95% CI: 3.22-6.42), followed by diabetes (SHR=1.33; 1.08-1.63) and hypertension (SHR=1.11; 0.95-1.29). No significant exposure interactions were observed. A 3-year lag sensitivity analysis confirmed these associations with attenuated effect sizes.

Discussion

Depression showed the strongest association with dementia onset. These findings highlight the crucial need for early interventions on psychiatric and metabolic risk factors and support the use of common data models for multi-regional epidemiological research.

title: Prevalence and associated factors of peripheral arterial disease in hemodialysis patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authorString: Lou X, Wu L, Wei J, Chang L.
abstractText:
Background

Peripheral arterial disease (PAD) is common in hemodialysis patients and associated with adverse outcomes, but its prevalence and associated factors remain heterogeneous.

Methods

PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, Cochrane Library, Scopus, CINAHL, CNKI, and Wanfang were searched from inception to April 8, 2026. Cross-sectional and cohort studies reporting PAD prevalence or associated factors were included. Random-effects models were used. Heterogeneity was explored using subgroup, meta-regression, and sensitivity analyses.

Results

The pooled prevalence was 23% (95%Confidence Intervals [CI], 20%∼26%) based on ankle brachial index ≤ 0.9, 42% (95%CI, 29%∼56%) based on ultrasonography or other imaging, and 19% (95%CI, 11%∼33%) based on clinical criteria. Both research regions and proportion of male were associated with heterogeneity. Factors associated with PAD included abdominal obesity (Odds Ratio [OR]=5.41), diabetes mellitus (OR=2.90), cardiovascular disease (OR=2.01), cerebrovascular disease (OR=1.91), male sex (OR=1.70), smoking (OR=1.64), hypertension (OR=1.34), C-reactive protein (OR=1.06), age (OR=1.04), low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (OR=1.02), dialysis vintage (OR=1.01), albumin (OR=0.97), high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (OR=0.94), Black race (OR=0.78), and serum creatinine (OR=0.75). Associations varied by diagnostic criteria.

Conclusions

PAD is common in hemodialysis patients, with prevalence varying substantially by diagnostic criteria and study settings. Several demographic and clinical characteristics were associated with PAD; however, most evidence was derived from cross-sectional studies and was of low or very low certainty. These findings should not be interpreted causally. Standardized diagnostic criteria and well-designed prospective studies are needed to improve the certainty and comparability of future evidence.

title: What Drives Length of Stay After Elective Spine Surgery? Insights from a Decade of Predictive Modeling
authorString: Cho HN, Jeong S, Guo Y, Lopez A, Bow H, Zheng K.
abstractText: Objective: Predicting length of stay after elective spine surgery is essential for optimizing patient outcomes and hospital resource use. This systematic review synthesizes computational methods used to predict length of stay in this patient population, highlighting model performance and key predictors. Methods: Following PRISMA guidelines, we systematically searched PubMed, Google Scholar, and ACM Digital Library for studies published between December 1 st , 2015, and December 1 st , 2024. Eligible studies applied statistical or machine learning models to predict length of stay for elective spine surgery patients. Three reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data. Results: Of 1,263 screened studies, 29 met the inclusion criteria. Length of stay was predicted as a continuous, binary, or percentile-based outcome. Predictive models included logistic regression, random forest, boosting algorithms, and neural networks. Model performance varied across studies, with many reporting AUCs between 0.70 and 0.80, while a few reported higher values of 0.94 to 0.99. Machine learning approaches, including K-Nearest Neighbors and Naive Bayes, demonstrated strong performance in individual studies, although consistent superiority over traditional statistical models was not established. Common predictors included age, comorbidities (particularly hypertension and diabetes), BMI, surgical type and duration, and the number of spinal levels involved. External validation practices and reporting standards varied considerably across studies. Discussion: There is growing interest in artificial intelligence and machine learning in length of stay prediction, but lack of standardization and external validation limits clinical utility. Future studies should prioritize standardized outcome definitions and transparent reporting needed to advance real-world deployment. Conclusion: Machine learning models offer strong potential for length of stay prediction after elective spine surgery, highlighting their potential for improving discharge planning and hospital resource management.

title: Systematic Review of COVID-19 Vaccine Adverse Events, Efficacy, and Immunogenicity Among U.S. Military Health System Beneficiaries.
authorString: Pérez Koehlmoos T, Apilado KP, Chuang K, Janvrin M, Kanagaratnam A, Mani V, Mooney A.
abstractText:
Introduction

COVID-19 vaccination was implemented throughout the Military Health System (MHS) to protect beneficiary health and maintain operational readiness. Although vaccine safety, effectiveness, and immunogenicity have been extensively evaluated in civilian populations, evidence specific to U.S. military personnel and other MHS beneficiaries has not previously been synthesized. This systematic review assessed adverse events, vaccine effectiveness, and immune responses following COVID-19 vaccination among MHS beneficiaries.

Materials and methods

This study was a sub-analysis of a broader scoping review of COVID-19 vaccination outcomes. Seven bibliographic databases and relevant government and health organization websites were searched for English-language peer-reviewed and grey literature published from December 2020 through September 30, 2025. Eligible studies included active duty service members, retirees, or eligible dependents who received a U.S.-authorized COVID-19 vaccine. Paired reviewers independently conducted study screening, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment using Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal tools. Disagreements were resolved through consensus.

Results

Of 9,396 records identified in the parent scoping review, 14 studies met eligibility criteria for the MHS population, including 7 cohort, 5 cross-sectional, and 2 case-control studies published between 2022 and 2025. Twelve studies had low overall risk of bias and 2 had moderate risk. Six studies evaluated adverse events and 8 evaluated vaccine effectiveness or immunogenicity. Severe adverse events following vaccination were uncommon. Although myocarditis and pericarditis occurred more frequently after vaccination than among unvaccinated individuals, their incidence was substantially higher following SARS-CoV-2 infection. Vaccination was also associated with reduced risks of post-infection venous thromboembolism, kidney complications, prolonged illness, and persistent symptoms. Vaccine effectiveness against infection was 89.2% during the pre-Delta period and 70.2% during Delta predominance, with mRNA-1273 demonstrating the highest effectiveness. Immunologic studies showed robust humoral and cellular responses following vaccination. Booster vaccination and hybrid immunity increased the magnitude, breadth, and durability of antibody responses, including improved neutralization of immune-evasive variants.

Conclusions

COVID-19 vaccination was safe, immunogenic, and effective among MHS beneficiaries. Severe vaccine-associated adverse events were rare, while vaccination reduced infection, severe illness, long-term complications, and adverse outcomes associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection. Booster vaccination and hybrid immunity enhanced protection against emerging variants. These findings support continued evidence-based vaccination strategies to protect beneficiary health, force readiness, and deployability.

title: Partial Splenic Artery Embolization as a Bridging Strategy for Coronary Revascularization in Non-ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction Complicated by Thrombocytopenia Due to Hypersplenism: A Case Report and Literature Review.
authorString: Yilmaz Y, Kapcik M, Oktay A, Asik M.

journal.title: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions

abstractText: Managing acute coronary syndrome in patients with severe thrombocytopenia remains a major clinical challenge. The high risk of bleeding often contraindicates dual antiplatelet therapy and invasive procedures, creating a dilemma for clinicians when urgent revascularization is required. A 74-year-old male with a history of colorectal carcinoma and splenic vein thrombosis presented with non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI). Laboratory evaluation revealed severe, refractory thrombocytopenia (36,000/μL) due to hypersplenism. Given the high surgical and bleeding risk, partial splenic artery embolization (PSE) was performed as a bridging therapy. Platelet counts increased to 131,000/μL within 5 days enabling safe percutaneous coronary intervention for a critical 90% stenosis in the left anterior descending artery. The patient was discharged without periprocedural or early postprocedural complications and with normalized platelet counts. PSE represents an effective, minimally invasive bridging strategy to safely increase platelet counts in high-risk patients with NSTEMI complicated by hypersplenism-related thrombocytopenia, thereby enabling timely and safer coronary revascularization.

title: Conduction System Pacing With DF-1 ICD Systems Using a Medtronic 3830 Lead: A Feasibility Study.
authorString: Mrozek M, Azad N, Ocomen R, Shami ME, Kim M, Rose M, Tietema J, Khaleel I, Albano A, Baman J, Brunner M, Dahu M, Dandamudi S, Gauri A, Jawad W, Lacombe A, Tankut S, Chalfoun N.
abstractText:
Background

Patients with implantable cardioverter-defibrillators (ICDs) who require ventricular pacing are at risk for pacing-induced cardiomyopathy (PICM) from chronic right ventricular (RV) pacing. Conduction system pacing (CSP), particularly left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP), offers more physiologic ventricular activation, but integration with ICD therapy remains challenging. The DF-1 ICD connector standard provides an opportunity to incorporate a separate CSP lead while maintaining high-voltage ICD therapy. We evaluated the feasibility of an alternative ICD configuration using a DF-1 defibrillation lead paired with a Medtronic 3830 CSP lead connected to a dual-chamber ICD generator.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective case series of 17 consecutive patients who underwent this configuration at a single center between October 2022 and August 2025. For subgroup analyses, patients were stratified by baseline left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) as LVEF ≤ 50% (n = 9) or LVEF > 50% (n = 8). QRS duration, LVEF, left ventricular end-systolic dimension (LVESD), tricuspid regurgitation (TR) severity, and device outcomes were assessed during follow-up.

Results

Median follow-up was 15.0 months (IQR 6.2-19.2). The Medtronic 3830 lead was successfully implanted in all 17 patients, with confirmed LBBAP in 16 patients (94.1%) and deep septal pacing without definitive left bundle branch capture in one patient. No CSP lead revisions for mechanical or electrical failure were required. Among patients with paired measurements, LVEF increased from 41.6% ± 15.0% to 45.9% ± 14.1%, although the change was not statistically significant (p = 0.169), while LVESD decreased from 4.33 ± 0.72 cm to 3.89 ± 0.79 cm (p = 0.022). In paired subgroup analyses, patients with baseline LVEF ≤50% demonstrated an increase in LVEF from 31.9% ± 6.2% to 40.1% ± 14.3% (p = 0.053) and a decrease in LVESD from 4.62 ± 0.65 cm to 4.11 ± 0.71 cm (p = 0.048), whereas patients with baseline LVEF >50% demonstrated no significant change in either measure. QRS duration did not change significantly in either subgroup. Overall TR severity did not change significantly (Bhapkar p = 0.337), although 5 of 12 patients with paired imaging experienced at least a one-grade increase in TR severity and no patient developed new severe TR. Two patients (11.8%) died during follow-up, with neither death attributed to the device configuration.

Conclusion

An ICD configuration using a DF-1 defibrillation lead paired with a Medtronic 3830 CSP lead on a dual-chamber generator was technically feasible, with successful 3830 lead implantation in all patients, confirmed LBBAP in 94.1%, and no CSP lead revisions for mechanical or electrical failure during intermediate-term follow-up. Patients with baseline LVEF ≤50% demonstrated numerical improvement in LVEF and a reduction in LVESD, while ventricular function remained stable in those with LVEF >50%. These exploratory findings require confirmation in larger prospective comparative studies.

title: Evaluation of Publicly Available Online Information on Triggers of Myocardial Infarction.
authorString: Hunt L, Riegel M, Tofler G, Heighes P, Buckley T.
abstractText:
Background & aim

Many individuals seek online information about myocardial infarction (MI) for convenience and accessibility. However, the quality and completeness of information on MI acute risk factors, also known as triggers, remain unclear, limiting its value as a patient education resource. This study aimed to assess the content and presentation of publicly available websites addressing MI triggers.

Method

A systematic web-based search using Google identified publicly accessible websites on MI triggers. The first 10 relevant results for each search term were assessed using the Quality Component Scoring System and the Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool (PEMAT-P). Website content was systematically analysed for the presence and quality of information.

Results

Seventeen (17) websites were included. Most focussed on chronic risk factors, while triggers were largely under-represented. Overall website quality was low, with deficiencies in authorship transparency, citation practices, and evidence-based guidance. The PEMAT-P evaluation showed that understandability was generally adequate and clear, whereas actionability was consistently low, with limited actionable guidance. Only two websites explicitly used the term 'trigger' and addressed MI triggers, identifying five known triggers: physical exertion (n=2), anger (n=2), respiratory infection (n=1), meteorological stress (n=1), and overeating (n=1). Most websites (n=16, 94%) did not quantify MI risk following trigger exposure, and none addressed hazard periods or temporal patterns. Prevention strategies focussed mainly on chronic risk factors, with little guidance specifically targeting MI triggers.

Conclusions

Online information on MI triggers remains sparse and of limited quality, providing few actionable resources for patient education. Trigger-related information is rarely identifiable unless users search explicitly for a specific trigger, which limits its visibility in routine patient education resources and may reduce public recognition of acute risks, delaying timely preventive action. Improving the clarity and actionability of online resources can empower patients and facilitate targeted interventions to reduce MI risk and improve cardiovascular outcomes.

title: The Australian Cardiovascular Risk Calculator and Atherosclerotic Vascular Disease Risk in Community-Dwelling Older Women.
authorString: Smith C, Sim M, Via JD, Nguyen DT, Lim WH, Zhu K, Coats AJS, Figtree G, Prince RL, Lewis JR.
abstractText:
Background

The Australian cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk calculator (AUS-CVD-RC) was developed to improve CVD risk prediction in Australians, and launched in 2023. We tested the validity of the AUS-CVD-RC with long-term atherosclerotic vascular disease (ASVD) risk in a cohort of community-dwelling older women.

Methods

The study included 905 older women (70 to <80 years of age) from Western Australia recruited in 1998 (baseline). Women with chronic kidney disease and prevalent ASVD were excluded. AUS-CVD-RC were calculated at baseline and grouped into low (<5%), moderate (5% to <10%) and high (≥10%) risk. Atherosclerotic events, comprising hospitalisations and/or deaths, over 5, 10, and 14.5 years were obtained from linked health records.

Results

Over 5 years, 9.3% of women experienced an ASVD-related event, increasing to 21.1% and 37.0% at 10 years and 14.5 years, respectively. Compared to women with low risk, those with moderate (hazard ratio [HR] 2.89 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.32-6.32) and high risk (HR 6.34 95% CI 2.64-15.23) had greater hazards for an ASVD-related event over 5 years. Similar associations were observed at 10 and 14.5-years. Unadjusted event rates (%) over 5 years by AUS-CVD-RC risk groups were: low 7.4 (95% CI 3.0-15.3); moderate 20.3 (95% CI 15.5-26.2); and high risk 42.7 (95% CI 25.3-67.4). Despite this, the predictive utility for AUS-CVD-RC and ASVD events over these three different follow-up periods had an area under the curve of <0.70.

Conclusions

We demonstrate the AUS-CVD-RC identifies community-dwelling older women with a higher risk of ASVD, a population where risk prediction remains challenging. Future research should explore if the inclusion of women-specific factors may improve prognostic performance.

title: Association of Estimated Insulin Sensitivity With Cardiovascular Disease in Individuals Without Diabetes: Use of Traditional and Machine Learning.
authorString: Fang H, Chen X, Qin D, Wang X, Zheng Y, Chen X, Lin J, Chen K.
abstractText: The predictive role of the Estimated Insulin Sensitivity (e-IS) index, serving as a surrogate marker for insulin resistance, in cardiovascular disease (CVD) and mechanisms remains underexplored in nondiabetic populations. We aimed to evaluate the association of e-IS with CVD incidence and its predictive utility for CVD risk. We analyzed a national prospective cohort of participants without CVD or diabetes at baseline from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study and an external validation cohort from the Second Affiliated Hospital of Wenzhou Medical University. We used Cox proportional hazards models and restricted cubic splines to explore relations. Mediation analyses were performed to explore whether inflammation and kidney disease mediated the relation between e-IS and CVD outcomes. In addition, we used machine learning to develop an e-IS-based CVD prediction model, which underwent external validation. A total of 1,083 incident CVD cases occurred. Lower e-IS levels were associated with greater CVD risk, with no evidence of a nonlinear association based on restricted cubic splines. Mediation analysis revealed that high-sensitivity C-reactive protein and estimated glomerular filtration rate accounted for 3.06% and 5.47% of the association with CVD, respectively. Integrating e-IS into a basic model significantly improved the concordance statistic for CVD (0.708 vs 0.684) and yielded robust net reclassification (net reclassification improvement, 0.318; P < .001). The machine learning model achieved area under the curve values of 0.738 for CVD, 0.754 for heart disease, and 0.719 for stroke, respectively, with consistent external validation. Our findings indicate that e-IS might be an independent predictor of CVD in nondiabetic populations, mediated in part by high-sensitivity C-reactive protein and estimated glomerular filtration rate. Incorporating e-IS into risk models might enhance prediction accuracy and support personalized risk stratification.Abstract available in: يبرع (Arabic); हिन्दी (Chinese); Francais (French); Deutsch (German); हिन्दी (Hindi); Indonesian (Indonesian); (Japanese); Portugues (Portuguese); Español (Spanish).

title: Telomere Biology, Vascular Aging, and Hypertension: Mechanistic Pathways, Cellular Senescence, and Cardiovascular Risk.
authorString: Minari TP, Consenso-Martin LN, Vilela-Martin JF.
abstractText: Hypertension is a major global health challenge and a leading risk factor for cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. Beyond established hemodynamic, neurohormonal, and inflammatory mechanisms, biological aging processes may contribute to vascular dysfunction and cardiovascular risk. Telomeres are specialized DNA-protein structures that protect chromosome ends and maintain genomic stability. Although progressive telomere shortening has been associated with cellular senescence, oxidative stress, inflammation, and endothelial dysfunction, telomere dysfunction may also occur independently of substantial changes in mean telomere length, including through telomere uncapping, oxidative DNA damage, replication-associated lesions, and impaired shelterin-mediated protection. This narrative review examines the relationship between telomere biology, vascular aging, and hypertension, integrating epidemiological, genetic, and experimental evidence. Particular attention is given to DNA damage response pathways, mitochondrial dysfunction, cellular senescence, the senescence-associated secretory phenotype, endothelial impairment, and vascular remodeling. Human studies frequently report associations between shorter leukocyte telomere length and hypertension; however, findings from genetic studies are not uniform, and some Mendelian randomization analyses suggest that genetically determined longer telomere length may be associated with higher blood pressure or selected cardiometabolic traits. Moreover, leukocyte telomere length does not necessarily reflect telomere integrity in vascular tissues. Nutritional, environmental, and pharmacological factors that may influence telomere biology are also discussed, distinguishing observational associations from experimental and clinical evidence. Overall, current findings support a potential relationship between telomere dysfunction and vascular aging, but do not establish whether telomere alterations are independent causal determinants of hypertension, consequences of chronic vascular stress, or markers of shared biological processes. Further longitudinal, tissue-specific, and mechanistic studies are required to clarify these relationships and determine the clinical utility of telomere-related biomarkers.

title: Connect Proctoring: A Novel Educational Model for Training in Interventional Cardiology.
authorString: Ungureanu C, Brilakis ES, Mouthuy FP, Soetens R, Marynissen T, Thayse K, Popa D, Ayoub M, Mashayekhi K, Avran A.
abstractText: To evaluate the feasibility, procedural outcomes, and educational value of Connect Proctoring - a structured remote training framework combining theoretical education with real-time audiovisual supervision of live chronic total occlusion (CTO) percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) procedures. Operator training in CTO PCI represents one of the most demanding learning pathways in interventional cardiology. The continuous development of new devices and techniques requires fast and efficient methods of learning and expertise maintenance. Prospective evaluation of CTO cases performed by operators interested in learning advanced techniques for CTO. Four interventional cardiologists performed 12 CTO PCI procedures in total (3 consecutive interventions per trainee) as primary operators under real-time remote supervision by one external expert proctor. The trainee theoretical knowledge was assessed before and after the programme in all four trainees, followed by a structured surveys. Trainee theoretical knowledge improved by a mean of 23 percentage points (51% to 75%; range +20 to +28 points), with improvement observed in all 4 trainees. The overall trainee survey mean was 4.5/5.0; the clinical decision-making domain scored 4.9/5.0. Proctors agreed 3 cases are insufficient for independent CTO PCI (mean 1.7/5.0) but sufficient to improve parallel wiring competency (3.3/5.0). Technical success was 92 % (11/12). Mean Japanese Multicenter CTO Registry score was 1.9 ± 0.7; 83% moderate-to-severe calcification. True vessel perforation requiring treatment occurred in 2 cases (17%), both managed successfully without tamponade or mortality; 2 further cases showed minor contrast staining requiring no treatment. Local expert intervention was required for retrograde manoeuvres (3/4 retrograde cases), 2 antegrade dissection and re-entry (ADR) steps, and 1 delayed tamponade after distal vessel perforation requiring coil embolisation. Connect Proctoring could be considered a promising educational method that when applied within a structured framework, supports the operators in the adoption of a new CTO PCI devices and techniques. A complete complications- management training must be fulfilled before any remote-only application. Multicentre prospective validation is required before broader implementation.

title: Innovations in Temporary Mechanical Circulatory Support in Cardiogenic Shock.
authorString: Bernhardt AM, Gage A, Jumean M, Kalra S, Schrage B, Tayal R, Panoulas V, Møller JE, Schlöglhofer T, Brailovsky Y, Burkhoff D, Kanwar MK.

journal.title: The Journal of heart and lung transplantation : the official publication of the International Society for Heart Transplantation

abstractText: Temporary mechanical circulatory support (tMCS) can provide rapid hemodynamic stabilization in cardiogenic shock (CS), creating a bridge to myocardial recovery, durable MCS or heart transplantation. Contemporary platforms remain constrained by risk of vascular and hemocompatability-related adverse events, restricted patient mobility and support duration. These limitations have become increasingly relevant as tMCS use expands beyond acute myocardial infarction-related CS to the highly heterogeneous heart failure-related and postcardiotomy shock states. Next generation tMCS technologies seek to address these issues through lower-profile access, improved hemocompatibility, dedicated right- and biventricular support, extended support duration with greater support capabilities, enhanced patient mobility, and integrated physiologic monitoring. This State-of-the-Art Review examines the design rationale, technological maturity, and emerging clinical evidence for these platforms, while highlighting clinical, data-related, engineering and regulatory gaps in the field. Ultimately, the challenge for next-generation tMCS is not simply to deliver greater flow, but to provide appropriate, phenotype-directed circulatory support while minimizing the biological, vascular, and operational costs.

title: Ex Situ Echocardiography During Normothermic Perfusion: Serial Physiologic Full Cardiac-Output Assessments for Transplant Suitability.
authorString: Alexander WD, Nakashima T, Hernandez BA, Zimmerman KG, King SD, Raza SS, Ling C, Rojas-Peña A, Drake DH.

journal.title: The Journal of heart and lung transplantation : the official publication of the International Society for Heart Transplantation

abstractText:
Background

Clinical normothermic ex situ donor-heart perfusion (NEHP) uses retrograde aortic infusion which prevents hemodynamic assessment. We sought to optimize and validate guideline-directed ex situ echocardiography (ESE) for assessment of transplant suitability using a novel full-cardiac output (FCO) circuit.

Methods

Following transthoracic echocardiography (TTE), porcine hearts were procured and maintained on NEHP for 24 hours. At hours 1, 12, and 24, maintenance NEHP was transitioned to low-preload working-heart mode (LPWH). Although not physiologic, LPWH ensured optimal coronary perfusion and allowed ESE. Hearts were transitioned to physiologic FCO mode and ESE was repeated. NEHP was returned to maintenance. LPWH-ESE and FCO-ESE parameters were compared to determine their ability to stratify function.

Results

Forty-two echocardiograms (6 TTE, 36 ESE) were performed (n=6; 55±8 kg; female 50%; hearts 311±40gm). When compared to FCO-ESE, LPWH-ESE at hour 1 underestimated function (cardiac output (CO) 0.78±0.38 vs 3.26±1.70L/min, p=0.012; cardiac index (CI) 0.0024±0.0010 vs 0.0102±0.0048L/m/gm, p=0.009; stroke volume (SV) 8.0±3.5 vs 30.0±8.2mL, p=0.001; stroke work (SW) 279±102 vs 1683±1134mL/mmHg, p=0.026) and correlation was poor (R2 0.22-0.36). FCO-ESE successfully stratified function between hours 1 and 12 (LVEF 54.6±13.0 vs 33.6±6.0%, p=0.011; CO 3.26±1.70 vs 1.37±0.86L/min, p=0.003; CI 0.0102±0.0048 vs 0.0053±0.0027L/m/gm, p=0.016; SV 30.0±8.2 vs 15.3±6.6mL, p=0.001; SW 1683±1134 vs 686±472mL/mmHg, p=0.029), hours 12 and 24 (LVEF 33.6±6.0 vs 53.0±8.2%, p=0.036, and hours 1 and 24 (SV 30.0±8.2 vs 23.1±6.6mL, p=0.032). LPWH-ESE could not.

Conclusion

Physiologic FCO guideline-directed ESE should facilitate determination of transplant suitability in currently discarded donor hearts and thereby increase the number available for transplantation.
