title: Association of time-updated diabetes and cardiovascular disease with mortality in the Tehran Lipid and Glucose Study.
authorString: Masrouri S, Ebrahimi N, Mirzad M, Tabrizi T, Azizi F, Hadaegh F.
abstractText: In this 2-decade, time-updated analysis of more than 10,000 Middle-Eastern people, diabetes conferred a risk comparable to established CVD for cardiovascular and non-cardiovascular mortality, whereas their coexistence conferred substantially higher risk only for the former.

title: Early Perioperative Outcomes of Unicompartmental Knee Arthroplasty in Octogenarians Versus Younger Patients.
authorString: Feyel S, Boisrenoult P, Djebara AE, Pujol N.
abstractText: Unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA) is increasingly performed at both extremes of age, yet early complications have rarely been compared between the youngest and the oldest candidates. This study compared 90-day complication rates after UKA between patients younger than 60 years and patients 80 years or older. This single-center retrospective study included all UKAs performed between 2015 and 2025: 73 patients (86 knees) younger than 60 years and 98 patients (111 knees) 80 years or older. Major complications comprised deep infection, early revision, pulmonary embolism, cardiovascular events, stroke, and death; all other complications were minor. Active range of motion, hospital-stay data, and operative time were also compared. Rates of major complications (three [3.5%] versus six [5.4%]; P = 0.73) and minor complications (six [7.0%] versus nine [8.1%]; P = 1.00), active range of motion (112.7 ± 10.6 versus 114.6 ± 9.0°; P = 0.30), and lengths of stay (3.0 ± 1.5 versus 3.0 ± 1.8 days; P = 0.39) were comparable in younger and older patients. Younger patients were less often transferred to a rehabilitation facility (22.1 versus 36.9%; P = 0.03) and had a longer operative time (77.3 ± 30.2 versus 65.4 ± 17.7 minutes; P = 0.01). There were no pulmonary embolisms, cardiovascular events, or deaths. Early complication rates after UKA were comparable in patients 80 years or older and in those younger than 60 years, despite a higher comorbidity burden in the older group. When the indication is appropriate, age alone should not preclude UKA.

title: Identifying Undiagnosed Diabetes and Mortality Risk in Hypertensive Patients: Development and Web Deployment of a Clinical Screening Tool.
authorString: Ni C, Zhao X, Huang J, Zhao K, ZhangMD M, Shen X, Zhang W.

journal.title: The American journal of the medical sciences

abstractText:
Background

Hypertension substantially increases diabetes risk, yet routine screening with fasting plasma glucose (FPG) and hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) may miss early cases. This study evaluated the additional diagnostic and prognostic value of oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) in hypertensive patients. A predictive model was also developed to identify high-risk individuals for targeted OGTT screening.

Methods

A cross‑sectional analysis with linked mortality data was conducted using the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES, 2005‑2016). A two-stage screening (FPG/HbA1c, then OGTT) was applied. The association between isolated OGTT positivity (2-h PG ≥11.1 mmol/L with normal FPG/HbA1c) and all-cause mortality was assessed using Cox proportional hazards models. A nomogram for predicting isolated OGTT positivity was developed, internally validated, and benchmarked against machine learning algorithms. An interactive online calculator was deployed.

Results

Among initially screen-negative hypertensive patients, OGTT identified previously undiagnosed diabetes in 5.81%, a rate 4-fold higher than in non-hypertensives (P<0.001). Isolated OGTT positivity was independently associated with a 48% increased risk of all-cause mortality​ (HR 1.48, 95% CI: 1.06-2.06). The prediction nomogram, which incorporates four routine variables (age, FPG, HbA1c, and the triglyceride-glucose index [TyG]), demonstrated strong discrimination, with a C-index of 0.798 in internal validation. It performed comparably to four machine learning algorithms while offering superior clinical interpretability. A web-based calculator was also provided for implementation.

Conclusion

In hypertensive patients with normal FPG/HbA1c, supplementary OGTT identifies a substantial burden of undiagnosed diabetes that is linked to increased mortality. The nomogram (using age, FPG, HbA1c, and TyG) enables clinicians to selectively target OGTT to high-risk individuals, potentially improving risk-stratified screening.

title: Haemodynamic, functional and biomarker responses in obese patients undergoing pulmonary endarterectomy: a comparative cohort study.
authorString: de Freitas-Filho O, Simões EA, Salibe-Filho W, Roquim AC, Querido MAG, Galas FRBG, de Aguiar YRF, Gobbo LM, Terra-Filho M, Pêgo-Fernandes PM, Jatene FB.

journal.title: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care

abstractText:
Background

Obesity is common in chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH), but comparative data on haemodynamic recovery, biomarker kinetics and functional outcomes after pulmonary endarterectomy (PEA) remain limited.

Objectives

To compare haemodynamic, biomarker, functional and perioperative outcomes by obesity status after PEA.

Methods

Single-centre cohort of 202 consecutive patients undergoing PEA for CTEPH (January 2015-February 2024), stratified by BMI (obese ≥30 kg/m², n = 62; non-obese, n = 140). Serial biomarkers were analysed using log-transformed linear mixed-effects models (LMM; group × time interaction as primary test, Bonferroni-corrected contrasts). Haemodynamics were compared by ANCOVA adjusted for baseline, cardiac index using BSA (Mosteller), and NYHA class by exact test and adjusted logistic regression.

Results

The LMM group × time interaction was significant only for CK-MB [F(4; 669.3)=2.67; p = 0.031]; the single Bonferroni-significant contrast was at ∼24 h (geometric mean 42.2vs 29.3 ng/mL; p = 0.012). Troponin [F(4; 538.4)=1.69; p = 0.151] and CPK [F(4; 685.9)=1.13; p = 0.341] interactions were not significant. Postoperative cardiac index (2.70 vs 2.74 L/min/m²; p = 0.77) and ANCOVA-adjusted ΔPVR (p = 0.39) did not differ. Postoperative NYHA class I was less frequent in obese patients (47.8%vs 70.8%; adjusted OR 0.45, 95% CI 0.21-0.99). Cumulative mortality at 30 days was 9.7% in obese and 11.4% in non-obese patients (p = 0.81).

Conclusion

In this single-centre observational cohort, obesity was not associated with significant differences in postoperative haemodynamics, length of stay or short-term mortality, although estimates were imprecise. Obese patients less often achieved NYHA class I. These hypothesis-generating findings do not support excluding patients from PEA evaluation on the basis of BMI alone.

title: Association Between Self-Reported Walking Pace and Incident Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease in Midlife and Later Life.
authorString: Kumar M, Zhao S, Robinson P, Kuchel GA, Fortinsky RH, Alexander KP, Coll P, Kuo CL.
abstractText: A slow walking pace is associated with increased risk of mortality and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD). However, little is known about how increasing chronological age affects this association. This study aims to assess the association between self-reported walking pace and incident ASCVD across chronological age groups. The study involved participants aged 40 to 73 years without ASCVD at recruitment from the UK Biobank. We identified participants who developed ASCVD during follow-up using UK Biobank first-occurrence data based on ICD-10 (International Classification of Diseases-10th Revision) codes from multiple data sources. Participants self-reported baseline walking pace as brisk, average, or slow via an online survey question. We analyzed associations among walking pace, chronological age, and incident ASCVD during follow-up. Among the 301,869 participants in this cohort study, 18,029 (6%) were slow walkers, 155,892 (52%) were average walkers, and 127,948 (42%) were brisk walkers. The mean follow-up duration was 13.4 years (SD = 1.8). During follow-up, 3,831 (21%) participants in the slow-walking group developed ASCVD, compared with 10,714 (8.4%) in the brisk-walking group. The adjusted subdistribution hazard ratio (sHR) for developing ASCVD among slow walkers, compared with brisk walkers, gradually decreased with increasing chronological age (age 45: sHR = 1.79 [1.58-2.03] vs age 65: sHR = 1.28 [1.22-1.35]). Significant interactions were observed between age, modeled as a continuous variable, and both average and slow walking pace relative to brisk walking (P < 0.001). Self-reported walking pace was independently associated with incident ASCVD, with a stronger adjusted association observed among younger than older participants.

title: Optical Coherence Tomography can identify Non-Ischemic Lesions that have a Benign Outcome from those with High-Risk of Future Events. Insights from a Patient Level Pooled Analysis of COMBINE (OCT-FFR) and PECTUS-Obs Prospective Natural History Studies.
authorString: Kedhi E, Belanger P, Rroku A, Roleder T, Hermanides RS, Alfonso F, de Luca G, Malinowski K, Volleberg R, Mol JQ, Meuwissen M, Van Royen N.
abstractText:
Background

Whether all lipid-rich plaques (LRP) or only thin-cap fibroatheromas (TCFA) are at risk for future events, remains unclear.

Methods

Individual patient data from two prospective studies, the COMBINE FFR-OCT and PECTUS-obs trials, performed respectively in a diabetes mellitus (DM) and myocardial infraction, (MI) patients, were pooled. Patients carrying ≥1 fractional-flow reserve (FFR) negative, optical coherence tomography (OCT) -assessed, lesions (target lesions) were divided in two groups. The first group represented patients with non-LRP and the second those with LRP. The second group was further divided in LRP-TCFAs and LRP thick-cap fibroatheromas (ThCFAs). Patients with plaque rupture or erosion were further excluded from the Non-LPR and ThCFA groups. The primary endpoint was target-lesion failure, defined as cardiac death, target-vessel myocardial infarction and target-lesion revascularization at 2 years.

Results

Pooling of the two trials resulted in 722 patients carrying non-destabilized, ≥1 FFR-negative, OCT assessed lesions, of which 165 (22.8%) had non-LRP while 557 (77.2%) had LRP. In the LPR group, 224 patients (40.2%) had TCFA morphology. The primary endpoint was 29(5.2%) vs 4(2.4%) (HR 2.21, CI: (0.78-6.28), p= 0.14) in the LRP versus non-LRP groups. However, within LRP groups TCFAs were associated with a significantly higher primary endpoint rate than ThCFAs; 20 (8.9%) vs 9 (2.7%), (HR 3.22, CI: 1.46-7,11, p < 0.01).

Conclusion

At 2 years only TCFAs were associated with a high rate of TLF while the remaining non-ischemic LRP and non-LRP plaques had a very benign outcome under optimal statin-based medical treatment.

title: Ten-year clinical outcomes after successful percutaneous coronary intervention compared with medical treatment in patients with chronic total occlusion and preserved left ventricular ejection fraction.
authorString: Yu HY, Ahn J, Rha SW, Choi BG, Choi SY, Byun JK, Lee Y, Baskoro AP, Pratama AR, Susanti M, Chesario MS, Park S, Choi CU.
abstractText: The long-term clinical benefit of revascularization in patients with chronic total occlusion (CTO) and preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF ≥50%) remains uncertain. This study aimed to investigate the clinical impact of CTO revascularization in patients with preserved LVEF compared with those receiving optimal medical treatment (OMT) up to 10 years. A total of 939 patients with CTO and preserved LVEF were analyzed, including those treated with OMT (OMT group; n = 492) or successful percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI group; n = 447). The primary endpoint was cardiac death, and the secondary endpoint was major adverse cardiac events (MACE) during a 10-year follow-up period. To adjust for baseline differences, inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) was applied, yielding weighted cohorts of 934 OMT and 920 PCI patients. Time-to-event outcomes were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards models. A Fine-Gray model was additionally used to account for competing non-cardiac death. After IPTW adjustment, the weighted sample sizes were 934 in the OMT group and 920 in the PCI group. During a median follow-up of 5.2 years (interquartile range, 2.9-10.0 years), the incidence of cardiac death was significantly lower in the PCI group than in the OMT group (2.0% vs. 6.3%, p = 0.001), whereas MACE did not differ significantly. The incidence of myocardial infarction (MI) was also lower in the PCI group (3.5% vs. 7.0%, p = 0.021). The cause-specific association with cardiac death (HR, 0.30; 95% CI, 0.14-0.65; p = 0.001) was attenuated in the Fine-Gray competing-risk analysis (sHR, 0.31; 95% CI, 0.10-1.02; p = 0.054). All-cause mortality and Hard MACE did not differ significantly between groups. In CTO patients with preserved LVEF, successful CTO PCI was associated with a lower incidence of cardiac death during long-term follow-up compared with OMT. These findings suggest that successful CTO revascularization may have a favourable prognostic association in patients with preserved LVEF. However, this association was attenuated after accounting for competing non-cardiac death, warranting cautious interpretation of the potential long-term prognostic association.

title: Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: A Review.
authorString: Ommen SR.
abstractText:
Importance

Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is defined as left ventricular hypertrophy of greater than 15 mm in any part of the left ventricular wall in the absence of valvular disease, uncontrolled hypertension, or other chronic conditions causing severe left ventricular hypertrophy such as uncontrolled hypertension or cardiac amyloidosis. Most people with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy have a normal lifespan; however, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is associated with a 0.8% annual incidence of sudden cardiac death.

Observations

Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy affects an estimated 0.2% of people worldwide (including more than 600 000 people in the US) and is typically diagnosed with echocardiography. Approximately 35% to 40% of patients report effort-related dyspnea, chest pain or pressure, or lightheadedness. Approximately 30% to 40% of people with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy have a pathogenic gene variant that encodes for cardiac sarcomere proteins (predominantly myosin binding protein C, myosin heavy chain, and troponin). Other patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy may have a polygenic predisposition and/or nongenetic risk factors. The sarcomeric gene variants cause hypercontractility and delayed relaxation of the cardiac sarcomere, which characterizes the underlying pathophysiologic problem in people with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Approximately 60% to 70% of patients have obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, characterized by dynamic left ventricular outflow tract obstruction due to basal septal hypertrophy. The remainder do not have outflow tract obstruction and, therefore, have nonobstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy should participate in regular low- to moderate-intensity physical activity (such as brisk walking, jogging) as part of a healthy lifestyle. Medical therapies such as β-blockers (eg, metoprolol, bisoprolol, nadolol) and nondihydropyridine-class calcium channel blockers (eg, verapamil or diltiazem) are first-line medical therapy for patients with symptoms due to hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. If first-line therapies do not relieve symptoms, alternative treatments include disopyramide, which improves symptoms in approximately 60% of patients, cardiac myosin inhibitors (mavacamten or aficamten), which improve symptoms in approximately 70% to 80% of patients, or procedures to thin the septal wall of the left ventricle, including percutaneous alcohol septal ablation, which improves symptoms in approximately 75% to 80% of patients, or surgical septal myectomy, which improves symptoms in approximately 90% to 95% of patients. Guidelines recommend that first-degree relatives of patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy undergo screening for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with genetic testing or echocardiography.

Conclusions

Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is caused by a monogenetic pathogenic variant in approximately 30% to 40% of patients and can cause effort-related dyspnea, chest pain or pressure, or lightheadedness. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is associated with an incidence of sudden cardiac death of 0.8% per year. First-line therapies for symptomatic hypertrophic cardiomyopathy are β-blockers (eg, metoprolol, bisoprolol, nadolol) or nondihydropyridine calcium channel blockers (eg, verapamil, diltiazem).

title: Concomitant transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis in TAVR candidates: phenotype, in-hospital outcomes, and CT-derived extracellular volume in an Iranian cohort.
authorString: Behnemoon M, Taghavi S, Firouzi A, Pouraliakbar H, Naderi N, Omidvar R, Mirtajaddini M, Fattah Jahromi ZS, Khalili Y, Hatami MF.

journal.title: The Egyptian heart journal : (EHJ) : official bulletin of the Egyptian Society of Cardiology

abstractText:
Background

Severe aortic stenosis (AS) and transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTR-CA) coexist in older patients, but optimal screening for occult ATTR-CA in transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) candidates remains uncertain. This study characterized the phenotype of TAVR candidates, examined factors associated with in-hospital outcomes, and assessed whether cardiac computed tomography (CT)-derived extracellular volume (ECV) contributes to ATTR-CA detection.

Methods

Prospective single-center cohort of 70 consecutive patients aged 60 years or older with severe AS referred for TAVR assessment between June and December 2023. All patients underwent technetium-99 m pyrophosphate (99mTc-PYP) scintigraphy and CT-derived ECV, with CT-ECV positivity defined as ECV 30% or greater. Outcomes were ascertained during the index hospitalization: mortality, acute kidney injury (AKI), length of stay, and permanent pacemaker implantation.

Results

Mean age was 75.0 ± 8.4 years and 38 patients (54.3%) were men. In-hospital mortality occurred in 2 patients (2.9%), AKI in 14 (20.0%), and permanent pacemaker implantation in 15 (21.4%); median hospital stay was 6 days. PYP-positive ATTR-CA was identified in 4 patients (5.7%). CT-ECV positivity was present in 8 patients (11.4%), including 3 of the 4 PYP-positive cases. Against PYP positivity, CT-ECV showed a sensitivity of 75.0% (95% CI, 19.4-99.4), specificity of 92.4% (83.2-97.5), positive predictive value of 37.5% (8.5-75.5), and negative predictive value of 98.4% (91.3-100.0).

Conclusion

Against PYP scintigraphy, CT-ECV showed high specificity and negative predictive value with low positive predictive value, but these estimates rest on four PYP-positive patients and are exploratory. One PYP-positive patient had an ECV below the threshold, so a negative result cannot exclude ATTR-CA. These data support the feasibility of deriving ECV from an acquisition already performed for procedural planning; clinical usefulness as a screening strategy remains to be established.

title: Outcomes of surgical ablation for atrial fibrillation in adults with congenital heart disease.
authorString: Kakutani R, Koide M, Kunii Y, Yashima M, Cao Y.
abstractText:
Objective

To evaluate the outcomes of concomitant surgical ablation for atrial fibrillation in adults with congenital heart disease.

Methods

We retrospectively analyzed 42 patients (mean age, 58.5 ± 14.3 years) who underwent the maze procedure or pulmonary vein isolation concomitantly with intracardiac surgery between September 2003 and November 2022. None of the patients underwent surgery primarily for arrhythmia management.

Results

Twenty-nine patients underwent the modified Cox maze procedure; two patients additionally underwent a combination of right atrial maze and pulmonary vein isolation, one patient underwent right atrial maze alone, and ten patients underwent pulmonary vein isolation alone. Over a mean follow-up of 39 ± 34.9 months, late mortality occurred in five patients, including two cardiac deaths. Recurrent atrial fibrillation was observed in 11 patients. Atrial fibrillation recurrence-free rates were 85.4%, 81.9%, and 75.6% at 1, 3, and 5 years, respectively. During follow-up, one patient experienced an ischemic stroke, and three patients required implantation of a new pacemaker. Exploratory analysis suggested that advanced age at the time of surgery was associated with atrial fibrillation recurrence.

Conclusions

Concomitant surgical ablation for atrial fibrillation was suggested as a safe and effective treatment in adults with congenital heart disease. Earlier intervention, conducted before advanced age, may be associated with improved long-term rhythm outcomes.

title: Blood Lead, Cadmium, and Mercury and Cardiometabolic Disease in Korean and U.S. Adults: Population-Specific Associations with Hypertension and Cross-Nationally Consistent Inverse Associations with Diabetes.
authorString: Zhao F, Zhang Y, Shi J.
abstractText: We harmonized nationally representative data on 18,871 Korean adults (KNHANES; 9 survey cycles, 2005-2017) and 16,159 U.S. adults (NHANES 2007-2012) and related blood lead (Pb), cadmium (Cd), and mercury (Hg), individually and as mixtures, to hypertension, diabetes, dyslipidemia, and cardiovascular disease, with prospective mortality added in the U.S. cohort. In design-based survey-weighted logistic models, positive associations with hypertension were confined to Korea (Pb 1.15, Cd 1.18, and Hg 1.07 per doubling), whereas in the United States neither Pb (OR 1.03) nor Cd (OR 1.05) was associated with hypertension. Hg showed divergent directions (OR 1.07 in Korea versus 0.96 in the U.S.). Inverse associations with diabetes were directionally consistent across populations (Pb: OR 0.80 in Korea and 0.66 in the U.S.). Nine associations survived false-discovery-rate control across the 24 primary tests: Pb, Cd, and Hg with hypertension, Pb with diabetes, and Cd with dyslipidemia in Korea; and Pb, Cd, and Hg with diabetes and Hg with dyslipidemia in the U.S. The inverse direction of the diabetes associations is most plausibly explained by reverse causation rather than a protective effect. Nonlinearity was significant in only 5 of 18 dose-response panels. Stratification on fish/seafood consumption did not explain the divergent mercury findings: interaction tests were not significant for any outcome (P 0.40-0.87), and seafood-related confounding remains one plausible but unproven explanation. Quantile g-computation showed a positive joint effect on hypertension in Korea (OR 1.20, 95% CI 1.12-1.28) but a null joint effect in the U.S. (OR 0.99, 95% CI 0.91-1.06). In prospective linkage to national death records through 2019 (14,468 adults, 1,957 deaths), Cd predicted all-cause mortality (HR 1.21 per doubling, 95% CI 1.14-1.29) and Pb was associated with mortality (HR 1.08, 95% CI 1.01-1.16). Hg was inversely associated (HR 0.86, 95% CI 0.82-0.90), a pattern consistent with confounding by seafood-related factors. Metal-cardiometabolic associations are only partly transportable across exposure environments and should be reported per population and per outcome.

title: Clinical analysis of patients with refractory status epilepticus in a tertiary hospital in northern Ceará, Brazil: a case series.
authorString: Afonso AJA, Carvalho FCP, Melo GBJ, Ribeiro EML.
abstractText:
Background

Refractory status epilepticus (RSE) is a neurological emergency associated with high morbidity and mortality. Despite its clinical significance, data from regional tertiary centers in Brazil remain limited.

Objective

To characterize the clinical profile of RSE patients and to identify predictors associated with in-hospital mortality.

Methods

In the current retrospective case series, we analyzed 21 patients hospitalized between 2023 and 2025 in a tertiary hospital in in the northern region of the state of Ceará, Brazil. Cases were identified via electroencephalography (EEG) screening and medical record review, following the diagnostic criteria of the International League Against Epilepsy (ILAE) for RSE.

Results

The mean age of the sample was 54.05 (median: 62) years, with 61.9% of female subjects. Hypertension (52.4%) and diabetes (28.6%) were the primary comorbidities. Depressed consciousness occurred in 76% of the cases. Prevalent metabolic disturbances included hypernatremia (85%) and metabolic acidosis (50%). The in-hospital mortality rate was 57.14%. The statistical analysis revealed a strong positive correlation between age and mortality (r = 0.72; p = 0.001). Notably, a significant negative correlation was found between overt motor seizures and death (r = -0.66; p < 0.001), with motor symptoms acting as a survival predictor (odds ratio [OR] = 31.50).

Conclusion

In the cohort of the present study, RSE was associated with high lethality, especially in older patients. The inverse association between motor symptoms and mortality suggests that non-convulsive presentations delay diagnosis, leading to worse outcomes. These findings emphasize the urgent need for institutional protocols prioritizing continuous EEG monitoring and early therapeutic escalation in regional tertiary centers.

title: Comprehensive care for acute ischemic stroke in older adults: experience from a geriatric unit.
authorString: Jiménez-Ruiz A, Becerra-Aguiar NN, Gómez-López DJ, Hernández-Montoya AS, Sotelo-Ramírez JA, Gómez-Figueroa E, Del Real GA, Ruiz-Sandoval JL.
abstractText:
Background

The global aging population has led to an increased burden of stroke, which remains a leading cause of mortality and disability. In Mexico, acute ischemic stroke (AIS) prevalence and risk factors are documented, but geriatric-specific management remains underexplored.

Objective

To analyze the clinical, diagnostic, and therapeutic approach to AIS in elderly patients in a Geriatric Unit, aiming to identify trends and areas for improvement.

Methods

We conducted a cross-sectional study of patients aged ≥ 65 years with AIS at the Unidad de Atención Geriátrica de Alta Especialidad "Pablo Jiménez Camarena" (UNAGAE) of Antiguo Hospital Civil de Guadalajara Fray Antonio Alcalde, between January 2022 and July 2023. Demographic, clinical, radiological, and etiological data were analyzed. Stroke subtypes were classified using the Trial of Org 10172 in Acute Stroke Treatment system. Statistical analyses included logistic regression models to assess mortality predictors.

Results

A total of 119 patients (mean age 75.4 years, 50% male) were analyzed. The most common risk factors were hypertension (76%), smoking (53%), and diabetes (45%). Intravenous thrombolysis was received by 11%, despite 41% arriving during the therapeutic window. Cardioembolism (29%) and large-artery atherosclerosis (16%) were the most frequent subtypes, but 49% remained undetermined (incomplete evaluation). In-hospital and 30-day mortality rates were 24% and 7%, respectively. Higher National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale admission rates (OR = 1.18; p < 0.001) were significantly associated with in-hospital mortality.

Conclusion

The present study underscores important gaps in the management of AIS among elderly patients, particularly the underutilization of acute interventions and incomplete diagnostic assessments. Optimizing emergency response times, improving etiological evaluations, and enhancing public awareness of stroke symptoms could improve patient outcomes.

title: ICU Admission and Mortality in Thyroid Storm and Impending Thyroid Storm: A 15-Year Cohort Study.
authorString: Zhang ED, Hussain I.

journal.title: Endocrine practice : official journal of the American College of Endocrinology and the American Association of Clinical Endocrinologists

abstractText:
Objective

To determine the demographics, clinical features, and outcomes of patients with thyroid storm and impending thyroid storm at a single center, as well as identify features associated with severe disease and mortality. We also compared clinical characteristics and outcomes between patients with impending thyroid storm and thyroid storm.

Methods

This was a retrospective cohort study of patients age 18 years or older with a clinical diagnosis of thyroid storm or impending thyroid storm at two affiliated tertiary academic hospitals between 2006 and 2021. The primary outcome was characteristics associated with a composite outcome of ICU admission or death.

Results

Among 106 patients, atrial fibrillation (OR 4.09; 95% CI 1.21 to 13.85; p=.02) and acute respiratory failure (OR 22.18; 95% CI 2.29 to 215.19; p=.008) were significantly associated with ICU admission or death. Fever (p=.02) and acute respiratory failure (p=.03) differed significantly between the impending thyroid storm and thyroid storm groups.

Conclusion

This cohort is among the largest single-center studies of thyroid storm reported in the United States. Atrial fibrillation and acute respiratory failure were significantly associated with ICU admission or death. Acute respiratory failure also differed significantly between impending thyroid storm and thyroid storm groups, suggesting that pulmonary complications, although not included in existing diagnostic criteria, may indicate more severe disease and poorer outcomes.

title: Deep Learning-Derived Cardioembolism Probability from Diffusion-Weighted Imaging Predicts Occult Atrial Fibrillation: A Prospective Multicentre Validation.
authorString: Ryu WS, Kim BJ, Lee M, Kim D, Jeong SW, Gwak DS, Kim JT, Park MS, Choi KH, Kim CK, Park D, Choi JC, Cha JK, Kim DH, Hong JH, Park H, Sohn SI, Kwon JH, Kim WJ, Bae HJ, Kim DE.
abstractText:
Background

The Trial of Org 10172 in Acute Stroke Treatment (TOAST) classification remains the dominant framework for ischaemic stroke aetiology, yet inter-observer agreement rarely exceeds κ 0.6. Deep learning algorithms trained on diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) have shown retrospective promise, but prospective multicentre validation is lacking.

Methods

We conducted a prospective diagnostic accuracy study across nine stroke centres in Korea. Consecutive patients with acute ischaemic stroke who underwent DWI within seven days of onset were enrolled between May and September 2023. A commercially deployed convolutional neural network classified each case into four modified TOAST categories (large-artery atherosclerosis [LAA], small-vessel occlusion [SVO], cardioembolism [CE], and other/undetermined) and generated a continuous CE probability score. The reference standard was site-specific expert adjudication based on the complete diagnostic workup.

Results

Among 617 patients (mean age 68.9 years, 62.2% male), overall agreement was 75.7% (Cohen's κ 0.643, 95% CI 0.594-0.691). CE sensitivity reached 95.5% and SVO sensitivity 90.6%. Among 426 patients without prior atrial fibrillation (AF), the CE probability score predicted newly detected AF with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.722 (95% CI 0.634-0.806). The highest-risk quintile showed an AF rate of 17.1% (number needed to screen [NNS] 5.9) versus 4.9% (NNS 20.2) in the remaining quintiles.

Conclusions

A DWI-based deep learning algorithm achieved substantial agreement with expert stroke neurologists for stroke classification. The CE probability score predicted occult AF from a single DWI sequence. This exploratory finding warrants confirmation in adequately powered prospective studies before clinical implementation.

title: The role of percutaneous trans-hepatic and trans-splenic variceal obliteration in uncontrolled gastric variceal bleeding.
authorString: Yi K, Park YJ, Lee H, Kwon H, Woo HY, Heo J, Kim CW.
abstractText:
Background/aims

Gastric variceal bleeding (GVB) is a serious complication of portal hypertension, with limited therapeutic options when conventional endoscopic and radiologic interventions are not feasible. Percutaneous trans-hepatic and trans-splenic variceal obliteration (PTVO) has been described as a salvage therapy; however, clinical evidence regarding its efficacy and safety remains scarce.

Methods

We retrospectively analyzed 23 cirrhotic patients (median age, 58 years; 18 men) who underwent PTVO for uncontrolled GVB between October 2017 to July 2024 at a tertiary hospital. Primary endpoints were technical success and postprocedural changes in liver function. Secondary endpoints included complications, length of hospital stay (LOS), rebleeding rates, and survival.

Results

PTVO was technically successful in all patients without procedure-related complications. Hepatic function, which was assessed by Child-Pugh, model for end stage liver disease, and albumin-bilirubin scores, remained stable during 12-month follow-up. The median LOS was 13 days (range, 3-48). During a mean follow-up of 45.6 months, rebleeding occurred in 10 patients (43.5%). Accounting for death as a competing event, the cumulative incidence of rebleeding was 18% at 6 weeks and 22.9% at 1 year. The Kaplan-Meier estimated survival probabilities were 91.1% and 61.1%, respectively.

Conclusions

In this small, retrospective cohort of highly selected patients with uncontrolled GVB for whom conventional treatment options were not feasible, PTVO was technically feasible in all cases. Among patients with available follow-up, no apparent deterioration in liver-function measures was observed. These findings provide preliminary descriptive evidence supporting PTVO as a possible rescue option in this clinical setting.

title: The cost of digitoxin unavailability in Germany: modelled clinical and economic consequences in heart failure.
authorString: Boettger P, Sossalla S, Böhm M, Bavendiek U, Bauersachs J.

journal.title: Clinical research in cardiology : official journal of the German Cardiac Society

abstractText:
Objective

Digitoxin reduced all-cause death or hospitalisation for worsening heart failure in symptomatic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction in the published DIGIT-HF trial. Germany's only marketed oral digitoxin product became unavailable on 1 July 2026, with resupply expected after 212 days. We estimated its clinical and economic consequences.

Methods

A counterfactual decision-analytic model combined published aggregate DIGIT-HF event rates, German diagnosis-related group costs, statutory tariffs, acquisition costs and quality-adjusted life-year estimates to compare uninterrupted supply with a 212-day interruption. Outcomes were clinical events, expenditure and net monetary benefit, extrapolated nationally under two population scenarios, with deterministic and exploratory Monte Carlo sensitivity analyses.

Results

Per 1000 eligible patients, uninterrupted supply corresponded to 16.8 fewer primary composite events and, estimated separately, 9.9 fewer heart failure hospitalisations. Nationally, the interruption corresponded to approximately 1700 to 3000 additional primary composite events and 1000 to 1800 heart failure hospitalisations. The net change in hospital and drug acquisition expenditure was small, as avoided digitoxin purchases largely offset additional hospital costs. At €20,000 per quality-adjusted life-year, maintained availability yielded a trial-aligned national net monetary benefit of €13.2 to €22.8 million, versus annual digitoxin expenditure of €6.7 to €11.6 million.

Conclusions

A 212-day digitoxin supply interruption may result in approximately 1700 to 3000 additional primary composite events and may forgo an estimated €13.2 to €22.8 million in net monetary benefit, while producing only a small change in hospital and drug acquisition expenditure. Thus, reliable supply of low-cost cardiovascular medicines is clinically and economically relevant.

title: Proposal for Preference-Informed Win Statistics and Use to Re-Analyze Seven Heart Failure Pharmacotherapy Trials.
authorString: Turgeon RD, MacDonald BJ, Hawkins NM, Marquis-Gravel G.
abstractText:
Aims

Win ratios (WRs) allow simultaneous evaluation of multiple outcomes using hierarchical composite endpoints, but outcome hierarchies are typically determined by researchers without patient input.We sought to develop a patient preference-informed approach to constructing hierarchical composite endpoints for WR analysis and use it to re-analyze heart failure (HF) pharmacotherapy trials.

Methods

We synthesized patient preference data from multiple sources to derive two preference-informed hierarchical composite endpoints: tolerability-over-quality of life (QoL) (in descending order, primary: death, HF hospitalization, side-effects, QoL) and QoL-prioritized (QoL, death, HF hospitalization, side-effects). We then re-analyzed individual participant-level data from seven RCTs (n=15,357) using these preference-informed hierarchies and, for comparison, a conventional hierarchy (death, HF hospitalization, QoL, side-effects) with two to four components.

Results

Of seven re-analyzed trials, five showed consistent results across preference-informed and conventional WRs, indicating preference insensitivity. Two trials exhibited preference-sensitive findings. In TOPCAT-Americas, benefit with spironolactone over placebo was attenuated in the tolerability-over-QoL hierarchy (WR 1.03 [95% confidence interval 0.92-1.15] versus conventional four-component WR 1.13 [1.01-1.26]), reflecting large between-group differences in side-effects. In BEST, the benefit of bucindolol over placebo was attenuated and no longer statistically significant with the QoL-prioritized hierarchy (WR 1.07 [0.98-1.16] versus conventional four-component WR 1.15 [1.05-1.26]), despite favorable effects on all four components.

Conclusions

Integrating empirically-derived patient preferences into hierarchical composite endpoints provides a pragmatic and generalizable approach to evaluating the net clinical benefit of HF pharmacotherapy using WRs. These results highlight the value of incorporating patient priorities into trial design and interpretation, and in therapeutic decision-making.

title: Clinical profiles and associated outcomes of distinct inflammatory phenotypes in patients with acute heart failure.
authorString: Baumhove L, Ceelen DCH, Fujimoto Y, van Essen BJ, Verstappen GMPJ, Zonneveld L, Beldhuis IE, Zijlstra SN, Dunnink A, Cotter G, van Veldhuisen DJ, van der Meer P, Voors AA, Matsue Y, Damman K, Ter Maaten JM, Bomer N.
abstractText:
Background

Elevated levels of inflammatory biomarkers are common in acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF) and have been associated with disease progression, diminished diuretic response and adverse outcomes, but a comprehesive understanding of specific inflammatory phenotypes remains elusive. We aimed to identify clinical characteristics, decongestion trajectories and outcomes across inflammatory profiles.

Methods

Plasma levels of 34 cytokines were measured in 270 patients hospitalized for ADHF enrolled in PUSH-AHF. Unsupervised clustering analyses were performed on cytokine levels to identify patient subgroups based on their inflammatory phenotype. Clinical characteristics, diuresis, natriuresis and clinical outcomes were compared among clusters. We validated our findings in the Japanese JEDI-AHF cohort (n=301) using Random Forest-based cluster projection derived from cytokine levels.

Results

Four distinct inflammatory clusters were identified: a low-inflammation cluster, a low-grade eotaxin-dominant cluster, and two NF-κB-related inflammatory clusters characterized by IFN-γ/Th1 and Th17/IL-17-dominant responses, respectively. Patients in the low-inflammation and eotaxin-dominant-clusters had the most favourable outcomes. Patients within the IFN-γ/Th1-dominant cluster more often had pre-existing heart failure and reduced kidney function. Patients in the Th17/IL-17-dominant cluster predominantly presented with new-onset heart failure, preserved kidney function, the highest NT-proBNP levels and the most impaired natriuresis and diuresis. The IFN-γ/Th1-dominant cluster was associated with an increased risk of 180-day all-cause mortality (HR=2.59 95%CI [1.22-5.49]) compared to the low-inflammation cluster. External validation in JEDI-AHF showed similar findings.

Conclusion

Distinct inflammatory phenotypes are present in patients with ADHF and associate with distinctly different clinical profiles, decongestion trajectories and outcomes. This underscores the heterogeneity of inflammation in ADHF and suggests a potential for personalized anti-inflammatory interventions.

title: Twenty-One Years of Bariatric Surgery in Benin Republic: Evolution of Techniques and Outcomes.
authorString: Lawani I, Amouzou EYO, Imorou Souaibou Y, Hounsou RN, Adagba Gayito R, Yevidé BA, Gbessi MEM, Nedelcu M, Gbessi DG, Jean Léon OT.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: J Laparoendosc Adv Surg Tech A
journal.title: Journal of laparoendoscopic & advanced surgical techniques. Part A
journal.isoabbreviation: J Laparoendosc Adv Surg Tech A

abstractText:
Background

Bariatric surgery was introduced in the Republic of Benin in 2005, yet, as in many sub-Saharan African countries, it has remained almost entirely undocumented.

Objective

To describe how bariatric surgical techniques and their outcomes have evolved in Benin over a 21-year-period.

Methods

Retrospective cohort study including all patients who underwent bariatric surgery between January 1, 2005, and January 31, 2026, at two hospitals in Cotonou, Benin.

Results

A total of 111 patients were included (mean age, 43.3 years; women, 85.6%; mean body mass index, 43.2 kg/m2). The procedures performed were laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy (50.5%), adjustable gastric banding (37.8%), open sleeve gastrectomy (10.8%), and gastric bipartition (.9%). Gastric banding was discontinued in 2011, and laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy has been the standard procedure since 2012. Excess weight loss at 48 months was 50% after sleeve gastrectomy versus 21% after gastric banding. At 48 months, sleep apnea, hypertension, and diabetes persisted in 8%, 11%, and 12% of patients after sleeve gastrectomy, compared with 35%, 36%, and 40% after gastric banding. Morbidity and mortality rates were 6.3% and 1.8%, respectively.

Conclusion

Bariatric surgery in Benin has successfully shifted to a minimally invasive approach, but its volume remains very low.

title: Outcomes of Catheter Ablation for Ventricular Arrhythmias Performed With ECMO Support: A 10-Year Institutional Experience.
authorString: Sagawa Y, Afzalian A, Oraii A, Gardziejczyk P, Zado E, Wald J, Biscotti M, Cevasco M, Enriquez A, Hanumanthu BKJ, Guandalini G, Markman T, Shivamurthy P, Kumareswaran R, Riley MP, Deo R, Lin D, Schaller RD, Garcia FC, Nazarian S, Callans DJ, Supple GE, Frankel DS, Dixit S, Epstein AE, Marchlinski FE, Hyman MC.
abstractText:
Background

Patients requiring extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) for cardiogenic shock or hemodynamic instability due to ventricular arrhythmias (VAs) represent an extremely high-risk but understudied population. We aimed to evaluate the intraprocedural stability, predictors of in-hospital mortality, and long-term outcomes in patients undergoing ECMO-supported VA ablation.

Methods

This retrospective cohort study included 57 patients undergoing 64 catheter ablations of VAs with ECMO support (2016-2025). Independent predictors of in-hospital mortality were identified using multivariable-adjusted logistic regression.

Results

The median age of the patients was 62 years, and 70% had ischemic cardiomyopathy. At ECMO initiation, 40 patients (70%) presented with cardiogenic shock and 43 (75%) with electrical storm. ECMO provided robust stability; minimum mean arterial pressure was similar between ventricular and nonventricular tachycardia (55 versus 60 mm Hg; P=0.124). In-hospital mortality was 42% (24/57 [95% CI, 30%-55%]). Multivariable analysis identified age (odds ratio [OR], 1.18 per year [95% CI, 1.05-1.38]; P=0.004), ischemic cardiomyopathy (OR, 24.3 [95% CI, 2.3-700.57]; P=0.005), chronic kidney disease (OR, 9.76 [95% CI, 1.89-73.26]; P=0.006), and New York Heart Association class III or IV (OR, 12.72 [95% CI, 1.86-158.46]; P=0.008) as mortality predictors, whereas VA elimination was an independent protector against in-hospital death (OR, 0.12 [95% CI, 0.01-0.77]; P=0.025). In patients presenting with electrical storm (n=43), VA elimination (n=33) was associated with significantly lower in-hospital mortality than VA recurrence (n=10; 27% versus 80%; P=0.007). Among survivors (n=33), 3-year survival was 78.0%, with low rates of cardiac death (3%, 1/33) during follow-up (11 [3-38] months).

Conclusions

ECMO-supported VA ablation is feasible and provides procedural stability. Although survival is limited by baseline reserve, VA elimination is associated with improved in-hospital outcomes, serving as a bridge to recovery or clinical decision.

title: Cardiovascular Outcomes Following Smartwatch Irregular Rhythm Notification: Findings From the Apple Heart Study.
authorString: Perez-Guerrero E, Parsa S, Gjermeni D, Sakalaki M, Yu K, Hedlin H, Desai M, Alipour P, Russo AM, Granger CB, Kowey PR, Hills MT, Rumsfeld J, Turakhia MP, Mahaffey KW, Perez MV, Apple Heart Study Investigators.
abstractText:
Background

Smartwatch irregular rhythm notifications (IRNs) can identify atrial fibrillation. IRNs' association with broader cardiovascular outcomes is unclear. We evaluated whether receipt of an IRN in the AHS (Apple Heart Study) was associated with subsequent self-reported cardiovascular events.

Methods

We performed a post hoc analysis of the AHS, a prospective trial in the United States. Participants were enrolled via an iPhone app from 2017 to 2018; those who completed the end-of-study survey were included. The exposure was IRN receipt. Outcomes were self-reported new heart failure, myocardial infarction, stroke/transient ischemic attack, pulmonary embolism, and a composite of these events (major adverse cardiovascular events). Multivariable-adjusted logistic regression models included age, sex, heart failure, hypertension, diabetes, prior stroke/transient ischemic attack/systemic embolism, and vascular disease.

Results

Among 293 944 participants who completed follow-up, 929 (0.32% [95% CI, 0.30%-0.34%]) received an IRN. Participants with an IRN were older, more often male, and had a greater burden of cardiovascular risk factors. At the end-of-study survey, completed 5 to 14 months after enrollment, IRN receipt was associated with higher adjusted odds of self-reported heart failure (odds ratio, 5.43 [95% CI, 3.09-9.57]), stroke/transient ischemic attack (odds ratio, 3.51 [1.91-6.45]), pulmonary embolism (odds ratio, 4.43 [1.92-10.20]), and major adverse cardiovascular events (odds ratio, 4.01 [2.80-5.73]). Among participants with an IRN but without atrial fibrillation, IRN receipt remained associated with statistically significantly higher adjusted odds of self-reported heart failure and major adverse cardiovascular events.

Conclusions

Receipt of a smartwatch IRN was associated with higher odds of subsequent self-reported cardiovascular events beyond atrial fibrillation. These findings suggest that IRNs may identify individuals at elevated short-term cardiovascular risk.

title: CACNA2D2 Regulates Mitochondrial Function to Attenuate Fibrosis and Atrial Fibrillation via the cGAS-STING Pathway.
authorString: Jiao Y, Xu J, Cai D, Lu T, Wan X, Li H, Bao X, Liao Y, Shen Y, Chang ACY, Han W.
abstractText:
Background

Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common sustained cardiac arrhythmia and is thought to be driven by atrial fibrosis. A previous study has identified the expression of calcium voltage-gated channel auxiliary subunit alpha2delta2 (CACNA2D2) is significantly downregulated in patients with AF, but its functional role remains unclear.

Methods

We analyzed CACNA2D2 expression levels using public databases and clinical samples. Fibroblast-specific Cacna2d2 knockout and overexpression models were established to assess its role in atrial fibrosis through in vivo electrophysiological recordings, histopathologic analysis, in vitro mitochondrial function assays, and biochemical studies. We also evaluated the role of Cacna2d2 in doxorubicin/myocardial infarction-induced cardiac fibrosis and carbon tetrachloride-induced liver fibrosis models.

Results

We observed α2δ2 (encoded by CACNA2D2) expression was significantly reduced in patients with AF and Ang II (angiotensin II)-induced AF mouse models. Fibroblast-specific knockout of Cacna2d2 exacerbated Ang II-induced atrial fibrosis, increasing AF susceptibility and duration, whereas overexpression reversed these effects. In cardiac fibroblasts, Cacna2d2 overexpression blocked induction of ACTA2 (α-SMA) and COL1A1 (Col1). Mechanistically, Cacna2d2 localized to mitochondria when overexpressed in fibroblasts, blocked TGF-β (transforming growth factor-beta)-induced reactive oxygen species production and inhibit the leakage of mitochondrial DNA through the BAX/BAK channel, suppressing the activation of the cGAS-STING pathway. Notably, exogenous supplementation of Cacna2d2-overexpressing mitochondria significantly suppressed TGF-β-induced α-SMA and Col1 expression in fibroblasts. Cacna2d2 knockdown increased mortality and α-SMA expression, aggravating cardiac fibrosis in doxorubicin-treated mice, whereas its overexpression attenuated myocardial infarction-induced cardiac fibrosis and carbon tetrachloride-induced hepatic fibrosis.

Conclusions

Our study demonstrates that Cacna2d2 exerts antifibrotic effects by preserving mitochondrial function and preventing mitochondrial DNA-cGAS-STING pathway activation, identifying Cacna2d2 as a promising novel target for fibrotic diseases, including AF.

title: Initiation of SGLT2 inhibitors among adults with type 2 diabetes and cardiorenal disease in the All of Us Research Program, 2019–2023
authorString: Kebeba M, Taa L, Alemu G, Lema K, Kayamo L, Oljira C, Awol K.
abstractText:
Background:

Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors reduce cardiovascular and kidney events in adults with type 2 diabetes(T2DM) and cardiorenal disease, but treatment initiation among eligible patients remains incompletely characterized. We estimated the cumulative incidence of recorded SGLT2 inhibitor initiation and associated participant characteristics in a diverse U.S. cohort. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study leveraging electronic health record data from the All of Us Research Program. Adults with confirmed type 2 diabetes, at least one co-occurring cardiorenal condition (atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, heart failure, or chronic kidney disease), and no prior SGLT2 inhibitor use were followed from the earliest date all criteria were met during 2019–2023. The 365-day cumulative incidence of initiation was estimated using the Aalen–Johansen method, accounting for competing risk of all-cause mortality. Cause-specific modified Poisson regression with robust error variance yielded adjusted risk ratios (aRRs) for initiation predictors Results Among 9,333 eligible participants, 637 had recorded SGLT2 inhibitor initiation within 365 days (estimated cumulative incidence, 6.85% (95% CI 6.34–7.36)). The 365-day incidence was 8.40% among individuals with heart failure, 6.65% with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, and 5.28% with chronic kidney disease. Initiation was more likely with heart failure (RR 1.51, 95% CI 1.29–1.76), and glycated hemoglobin ≥9.0% versus <7.0% (RR 2.61, 95% CI 2.07–3.28), but less likely with chronic kidney disease (RR 0.63, 95% CI 0.54–0.74), age ≥75 versus 45–64 years (RR 0.51, 95% CI 0.40–0.65), and non-Hispanic Black versus non-Hispanic White race and ethnicity (RR 0.79, 95% CI 0.65–0.97). Conclusions Fewer than 1 in 10 eligible, untreated adults with T2D and cardiorenal disease initiated SGLT2 inhibitor therapy within one year. Even with expanding guideline indications, substantial implementation gaps persist, particularly among patients with CKD, older adults, and non-Hispanic Black adults. Targeted health systems are imperative to optimize the use of guideline-recommended cardiorenal therapies.

title: A model-based approach to identifying atypical type 2 diabetes: UK population-based study
authorString: Dinsdale MM, McGovern AP, Cardoso P, Güdemann LM, Jansz TT, Jones AG, Hattersley AT, McKinley TJ, Shields BM, Young KG, Dennis JM.
abstractText: Aims Approaches to meaningfully identify individuals with differing prognosis at type 2 diabetes diagnosis are lacking. We aimed to assess whether QDiabetes, a validated routine clinical feature-based model to predict risk of type 2 diabetes onset, could be applied at the point of diagnosis to identify people with atypical type 2 diabetes with differing risk of complications and treatment requirements. Methods We included adults newly diagnosed with type 2 diabetes between 2013-2023 in population-representative UK primary care data (Clinical Practice Research Datalink). Individuals with low predicted QDiabetes risk (≤5.6%) were classified as atypical type 2 diabetes and matched up to 1:4 by age, sex and calendar year to typical type 2 diabetes (QDiabetes risk >5.6%). We compared 10-year risks of microvascular, macrovascular, acute complications, mortality and glucose-lowering treatment initiation. For complications, multivariable Cox models estimated adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs), adjusting for age, sex, year of diagnosis, ethnicity, deprivation and baseline HbA1c. Results Of 276,117 individuals newly diagnosed with type 2 diabetes, 30,397 (11.0%) were classified as atypical type 2 diabetes using our approach. Compared with the wider typical type 2 diabetes population (n=245,720; 89.0%), they were younger (54 vs 60 years), leaner (26.4 vs 34.0 kg/m  2 ) and had higher HbA1c at diagnosis (68.0 vs 60.0 mmol/mol). In matched analyses, the atypical type 2 diabetes group had a higher risk of severe retinopathy (aHR 1.33, 95% CI 1.23-1.44), similar risk of severe neuropathy (aHR 0.92, 0.84-1.01), and lower risk of severe nephropathy (aHR 0.81, 0.73-0.90). Despite lower predicted baseline cardiovascular risk in those with atypical type 2 diabetes, risks of myocardial infarction (aHR 0.99, 0.89-1.11) and stroke (aHR 0.92, 0.81-1.04) were similar, while heart failure risk was lower (aHR 0.72, 0.67-0.78). Atypical type 2 diabetes was also associated with higher risks of diabetic ketoacidosis, severe hypoglycaemia, non-cardiovascular mortality and insulin initiation.  Conclusion Type 2 diabetes onset risk prediction models used at the point of diagnosis may represent a pragmatic approach to identify people with an atypical type 2 diabetes phenotype. Despite fewer conventional risk factors, the phenotype identified had a poor prognosis and could provide a practical target for personalised type 2 diabetes management to reduce risk of long-term complications.

title: Intravenous Inotropes and Mortality in Takotsubo Syndrome: A Nationwide Cohort Study from the SWEDEHEART Registry
authorString: Gudmundsson T, Jha S, Petursson P, Råmunddal T, Angerås O, Rawshani A, Fröbert O, Alfredsson J, Ekenbäck C, Henareh L, Skoglund K, Ljungman CE, Bollano E, Mohammad MA, Hagström H, Jernberg T, Erlinge D, Redfors B, Omerovic E.
abstractText:
Background:

Takotsubo syndrome, which predominantly affects women, is thought to be precipitated by catecholamine excess, yet unstable patients often receive intravenous inotropes. We examined the association between intravenous inotropes and 30-day mortality in a nationwide cohort.

Methods:

We identified all patients with a first angiographic diagnosis of Takotsubo syndrome in the Swedish Coronary Angiography and Angioplasty Registry from 2008 through August 2025, linked to coronary care and population registers. The primary analysis was a Cox model for 30-day death among patients with a coronary care record, adjusted for age, sex, diabetes, smoking, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and Killip class, with multiple imputation. Sensitivity analyses varied the covariates and standard errors and examined days 0 to 7 and 8 to 30 separately, and the association was estimated in women and men with an interaction term.

Results:

Of 3,458 patients (79.4% women), 141 (4.1%) received inotropes: 3.6% of women and 5.8% of men. Thirty-day mortality was 19.9% in treated and 1.7% in untreated patients. The unadjusted hazard ratio was 12.89 (95% CI, 8.20 to 20.26) and the adjusted hazard ratio 6.49 (3.49 to 12.08; P<0.001; E-value, 12.5). In sensitivity analyses, the hazard ratio ranged from 3.37 (1.88 to 6.03), with presenting symptom and laboratory values added, to 6.62 (3.63 to 12.08). The hazard ratio was 8.82 (4.47 to 17.39) for days 0 to 7 and 2.47 (0.65 to 9.36) for days 8 to 30, and 6.43 (3.15 to 13.16) in women and 6.59 (2.79 to 15.58) in men (P=0.96 for interaction).

Conclusions:

Intravenous inotropes were associated with higher 30-day mortality in Takotsubo syndrome, in both women and men, with most of the excess in the first week.

title: Metabolic Health in the Horn of Africa: Insights from the 2020 Somalia and Somaliland Health and Demographic Surveys
authorString: Jama A, Ali S, Magan S.
abstractText:
Background: The epidemiology of insulin resistance (IR) and its role in cardiometabolic disorders, such as diabetes and heart disease, remains underexplored in rural and nomadic communities. Few studies compare these populations within the same region. Using survey data from Somalia and Somaliland, this study examines differences in metabolic disease burden amid urbanization, dietary change, and shifting lifestyles.

Methods:

This retrospective cohort study analyzed data from the 2020 Somalia (SHDS) and Somaliland (SLHDS) Health and Demographic Surveys. National prevalence estimates for chronic disease, diabetes, hypertension, cardiovascular outcomes (heart disease and stroke), and behavioral risk factors (tobacco and khat use) were extracted from published tables to calculate prevalence ratios (PR) and coefficients of variation (CV) by sex and residential setting (urban, rural, nomadic).

Results:

Among those with physician-diagnosed chronic disease (Somalia 5.7%; Somaliland 6.9%), diabetes accounted for 20.4% and 19.1%, and hypertension for 33.3% and 41%, respectively. Diabetes prevalence was about fivefold higher in urban than nomadic groups in Somalia (1.5% vs 0.3%; PR = 5.3) and nearly tenfold higher in Somaliland (2.0% vs 0.2%; PR = 9.4). Males had a higher diabetes burden (Somalia PR = 1.3; Somaliland PR = 1.5), while females had higher hypertension (Somalia 34.7%; Somaliland 45.4%). Diabetes variability across settings (CV: Somalia 50%; Somaliland 73%) indicated marked geographic disparity.

Conclusion:

Urbanization increases metabolic disease, but nomadic groups, though using khat more often, do not show higher hypertension. More complete data, including lipid profiles, are needed to understand emerging cardiometabolic risks.

title: Platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio for risk stratification and prediction of 28-day all-cause mortality in critically ill ICU patients with COPD complicated by atrial fibrillation: a retrospective cohort study based on the MIMIC-IV database
authorString: Qiao Y, Ren Z, Liu Y, Li J, Cheng A, Wang J, Liu J.
abstractText: Background Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and atrial fibrillation (AF) frequently co-occur in critically ill patients, and their interaction substantially increases short-term mortality. Simple, low-cost bedside prognostic biomarkers for this high-risk subgroup remain limited. The platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), derived from routine complete blood count, reflects pro-thrombotic status and immune exhaustion. This study aimed to evaluate the predictive value of admission PLR for 28-day all-cause mortality in ICU patients with concomitant COPD and AF. Methods This retrospective observational cohort study was performed using the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care-IV (MIMIC-IV) v3.1 database. Adult ICU patients with concurrent ICD-10-coded COPD (J43, J44) and atrial fibrillation (I48) were included. Only the first ICU admission per patient was retained. PLR was calculated as platelet count divided by absolute lymphocyte count using laboratory values obtained within the first 24 h after ICU admission. The primary endpoint was 28-day all-cause mortality starting from ICU admission. Multivariable Cox proportional-hazards regression, restricted cubic spline (RCS), Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve were applied. LASSO regression was used for variable screening. Predefined subgroup analyses were performed to assess effect modification, and interaction terms were tested. Internal validation was conducted via 1000-time bootstrap resampling. This study followed the STROBE reporting guideline. Results In total, 688 eligible ICU patients with COPD and atrial fibrillation were enrolled, and the 28‑day all‑cause mortality reached 16.4%. After adjusting for multiple clinical confounders, elevated admission PLR was an independent risk factor for 28‑day mortality. Restricted cubic spline regression identified a significant dose‑response non‑linear association between PLR and mortality risk. Kaplan‑Meier survival analysis demonstrated gradually worse survival across PLR tertile groups: 28‑day mortality was 8.7% in the lowest tertile, 14.8% in the middle tertile, and 25.7% in the highest tertile (P‑for‑trend < 0.001). Subgroup analysis showed the prognostic association of high PLR (T3 vs T1) was stable across all predefined strata, without statistically significant interaction. For predicting 28‑day mortality, the AUC of admission PLR was 0.662 (95%CI 0.612‑0.711), with an optimal cut‑off value of 178.0 (sensitivity 68.1%, specificity 59.0%). Conclusions Admission PLR is an independent prognostic biomarker for 28‑day all‑cause mortality in critically‑ill ICU patients with COPD complicated by atrial fibrillation. This inexpensive, readily‑available hematological index shows promising performance for bedside risk‑stratification, and its prognostic effect was robust across multiple clinical subgroups. Further multi‑centre and external‑cohort validations are required before widespread clinical application.

title: Prognostic Value of Admission Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio for One- Year All-Cause Mortality in Older Adults with Chronic Heart Failure: A Retrospective Cohort Study
authorString: Jia D, Yang Z, Liu H, Luo Z, Wang J.
abstractText: Background Heart failure remains a major contributor to morbidity and mortality among older adults. Individuals with chronic heart failure (CHF) frequently present with multiple comorbidities, reduced physiological reserve, and persistent vulnerability after hospitalization, highlighting the need for simple and accessible markers to improve prognostic assessment in this high-risk population. The neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), derived from routine blood counts, reflects systemic inflammatory status and may provide additional prognostic information. However, the association between admission NLR and post-discharge mortality in older adults with CHF remains incompletely characterized. Methods This retrospective cohort study included 147 older adults with chronic heart failure who were admitted to the Department of Cardiology, Beijing Geriatric Hospital, between January 2019 and May 2020. Baseline demographic characteristics, clinical parameters, laboratory findings, echocardiographic measurements, and medication information were collected. Patients were followed for 1 year after hospital discharge, and the primary outcome was all-cause mortality. Univariable and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression analyses were performed to identify factors associated with mortality. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis and Kaplan–Meier survival analysis were conducted to evaluate the prognostic value of admission NLR. Results During the 1-year follow-up period, 37 patients (25.2%) experienced all-cause mortality. Compared with survivors, non-survivors had higher admission heart rate, BNP levels, neutrophil counts, and NLR values, together with lower hemoglobin, lymphocyte counts, and prealbumin levels. In multivariable Cox proportional hazards analysis, higher admission NLR remained independently associated with an increased risk of 1-year all-cause mortality (hazard ratio [HR], 1.081; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.002–1.166; P = 0.043). ROC curve analysis demonstrated modest discrimination of admission NLR for mortality risk stratification (area under the curve [AUC], 0.617; 95% CI, 0.509–0.725). Patients with an admission NLR ≥ 7.83 had higher observed mortality than those with lower NLR values (52.4% vs. 20.6%, log-rank P = 0.005). Conclusion Elevated admission NLR was independently associated with an increased risk of 1-year all-cause mortality after hospital discharge among older adults with chronic heart failure. Although NLR alone demonstrated limited discriminatory ability, it may provide complementary prognostic information for identifying patients at higher risk of mortality. Further prospective multicenter studies are warranted to validate these findings and determine whether incorporating NLR into existing clinical assessment strategies can improve risk stratification in older adults with CHF.

title: Surgical versus Endoscopic Gastrojejunostomy for Malignant Gastric Outlet Obstruction: A Real-World Nationwide Analysis
authorString: Philip AM, Pinnam BSM, Sheikh I, Kohli S, Varma R, Amdetsion GY, Guifarro D, Mutneja H.
abstractText: Background. Malignant gastric outlet obstruction (MGOO) is a debilitating complication of advanced upper gastrointestinal and periampullary malignancy. Endoscopic ultrasound-guided gastrojejunostomy (EUS-GJ) has emerged as a minimally invasive alternative to surgical gastrojejunostomy (SGJ), but comparative data on broader postprocedural complications and reintervention remain limited. Methods. We performed a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX US Collaborative Network. Adults with gastric, pancreatic, or duodenal malignancy who underwent EUS-GJ or SGJ were identified by procedure codes. 1:1 propensity score matching balanced demographics, comorbidities, and baseline laboratory values, yielding 760 patients per group. Outcomes were assessed at 30- and 90-days using risk ratios, odds ratios, and Kaplan-Meier and Cox hazard ratios (HR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI). Results. At 30 days, EUS-GJ was associated with lower risks of blood transfusion (HR 0.41; 95% CI 0.28–0.61), ileus or bowel obstruction (HR 0.26; 0.14–0.48), acute kidney injury (HR 0.70; 0.49–1.00), venous thromboembolism (HR 0.53; 0.31–0.90), and hospital readmission (HR 0.64; 0.53–0.76). These reductions persisted at 90 days, with an additional reduction in sepsis (HR 0.64; 0.46–0.89). Gastrointestinal bleeding, respiratory failure, and heart failure did not differ. EUS-GJ carried a higher 90-day reintervention rate (4.3% vs 1.7%; HR 2.78; 1.46–5.28). A borderline 30-day mortality signal (HR 1.44; 1.02–2.02) was not sustained at 90 days and was attenuated by residual confounding (E-value 2.23). Conclusions. In real-world practice, EUS-GJ was associated with lower postprocedural morbidity and healthcare utilization than SGJ, at the cost of higher reintervention. These findings support EUS-GJ as a palliative option for MGOO at centers with advanced endoscopic expertise.

title: Association and Comparative Predictive Performance of TyG-BMI for Incident Cardiovascular Disease in Adults With Hypertension: A Prospective CHARLS Cohort Study
authorString: Wei Y, Liu X, Wang Z, Luo Y, Yun C, Liu K, Zhai X, Tang X.
abstractText: The triglyceride-glucose body mass index (TyG-BMI) integrates insulin resistance and obesity and may provide additional information for cardiovascular risk assessment. However, its association with cardiovascular disease (CVD) and its predictive value relative to other TyG-related indices remain uncertain in adults with hypertension. We included 3,092 participants aged ≥ 45 years with hypertension and without CVD at baseline from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study and followed them through 2018. During a median follow-up of 8 years, 886 participants developed CVD, including 659 cases of heart disease and 329 cases of stroke. Higher TyG-BMI was associated with greater cardiovascular risk, particularly for heart disease, while associations with stroke were weaker. Dose-response analyses suggested largely linear relationships with CVD and heart disease. Using five machine learning algorithms, we further assessed the incremental predictive value of TyG-BMI and other TyG-related indices. Adding TyG-BMI to the basic clinical model improved the area under the curve from 0.593 to 0.636 and yielded greater improvement in risk classification than the other indices. TyG-BMI may therefore provide complementary information for cardiovascular risk assessment in middle-aged and older adults with hypertension.

title: Discordant associations of herpes zoster vaccination with mortality and vascular events in adults with hypertension, diabetes and hyperlipidemia A propensity score matched TriNetX cohort study
authorString: Li A, Wu Y, Chen C, Chang Y, Hsu J, Chiu K.
abstractText: Background Reported mortality associations after herpes zoster vaccination may not reflect the direction of associations with vascular events. We examined mortality, individual vascular diagnoses, and their timing in adults with coexisting hypertension, diabetes, and hyperlipidemia. Methods This exploratory retrospective study used aggregate TriNetX results for patients aged ≥ 50 years at qualifying vaccination or immunization encounters on or after 1 January 2021. Zoster vaccine recipients were matched 1:1 to patients with Z23-coded immunization encounters and no recorded zoster vaccination at any time (36,988 per group). We examined platform-exported Cox estimates, Kaplan-Meier curves, and fixed-time estimates; non-fatal Kaplan-Meier estimates were interpreted as net risk rather than competing-risk cumulative incidence. Results Recorded mortality was lower in the zoster cohort (hazard ratio [HR] 0.51, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.47–0.55), whereas cerebrovascular disease (HR 1.20, 95% CI 1.13–1.29) and myocardial infarction (HR 1.14, 95% CI 1.05–1.25) had higher recorded hazards. Three-year mortality estimates were 2.52% versus 5.01%, and mortality curves separated within 30–90 days and hazards were nonproportional. The death-inclusive composite HR was 0.94 (95% CI 0.90–0.98), with three-year estimates of 9.63% versus 9.88%. All 41 evaluable matched standardized mean differences were below 0.10. Conclusions Lower recorded mortality did not coincide with lower recorded vascular event hazards. Reporting individual endpoints and mortality timing alongside a death-inclusive composite provides a more complete account of these associations. Residual confounding, comparator selection, and limitations of aggregate follow-up data preclude causal conclusions about cardiovascular benefit or harm.

title: Predicting 7-Day Major Complications in Hip Fracture Surgery: A Prognostic Model and Temporal Validation
authorString: Sura-amonrattana U, Saetan S, Saepoo P, Srinonprasert V, Kunin M, Saeliw R, Himkhun L, Thephamongkhol K, Tongsai S, Lekpet K, Tantigate D.
abstractText: Background Major complications within the first week after hip fracture surgery are prevalent and clinically significant. Existing preoperative risk models primarily predict mortality or overall risk, rather than early postoperative morbidity. This study aimed to develop and temporally validate a prognostic model predicting major complications within the 7 days post-hip fracture surgery, utilizing routine comprehensive geriatric assessments and admission laboratory parameters. Methods This prognostic study developed a model using a cohort of consecutive patients aged 65 years or older admitted with fragility hip fractures to a university hospital in Bangkok, Thailand (September 2017–December 2020). Temporal validation utilized a subsequent cohort (January 2021–November 2022). All patients were managed within an orthogeriatric fast-track pathway. Nineteen pre-specified candidate predictors spanning comprehensive geriatric assessment domains and routine laboratory values were evaluated. The primary outcome was any major complication (myocardial infarction, heart failure, stroke or transient ischemic attack, venous thromboembolism, respiratory failure, shock, or death) within the 7 days post-surgery. Predictors were selected via least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, with optimism estimated through internal bootstrapping. Results Among 1020 derivation cohort patients (median [IQR] age, 82 [77–87] years; 77.5% female), 87 (8.5%) experienced major complications. Six predictors were retained: age, Clinical Frailty Scale, Charlson Comorbidity Index, serum albumin, serum sodium, and routine medication count. The model demonstrated an apparent C-statistic of 0.729 (95% CI, 0.671–0.785) and an optimism-corrected C-statistic of 0.712. A derived bedside score (range, 0–21) yielded a corrected C-statistic of 0.707. Complication rates increased progressively across four risk categories from 1.2% to 18.8% (odds ratio per category increase, 2.42; 95% CI, 1.86–3.16). In temporal validation (427 patients; 40 events), the model maintained a C-statistic of 0.703 (95% CI, 0.614–0.790; calibration slope, 0.840). This discrimination significantly outperformed existing standard risk indices (all p ≤ 0.002). Conclusions Integrating comprehensive geriatric assessment data with routine laboratory parameters provided more accurate risk stratification for early postoperative complications compared with conventional instruments. External validation is required prior to broad clinical implementation.

title: Role of Epicardial Connections in persistent and Recurrent Left Atrial Tachyarrhythmias
authorString: Haddadin F, Carcora Y, Zhi E, Rizvi M, Sharma Y, Fram M, Kamal A, Li S, Tholakanahalli V.
abstractText: Background: Catheter ablation is a primary treatment for atrial fibrillation (AF), yet 30% of patients experience recurrence due to epicardial connections. This study investigates the role of these connections in left atrial tachyarrhythmias. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 204 patients undergoing radiofrequency ablation (RFA) for persistent or recurrent atrial tachyarrhythmias between January 2020 and December 2022. Epicardial connections were identified in 40 patients (19.6%) using high-density (HD) mapping, with missing isochrones and specific activation patterns. Patient demographics, echocardiographic parameters, and mapping results were analyzed. Epicardial connections were mapped to the Vein of Marshall (VOM), Bachman Bundle, Septoatrial Bundle, and Septopulmonary Bundle. Results: The cohort had a mean age of 74±6.4 years, predominantly male (95%). The most common epicardial connection was the VOM (52.5%), followed by the Bachman Bundle (22.5%), Septoatrial Bundle (15%), and Septopulmonary Bundle (10%). Recurrence of atrial fibrillation or atrial tachyarrhythmias occurred in 47.5% of patients’ post-ablation. Hospitalization within three months occurred in 22.5% of patients, and 12.5% experienced mortality within the same period. Conclusions: Epicardial connections are an important substrate for persistent and recurrent left atrial tachyarrhythmias and should be considered when conventional endocardial mapping findings do not fully explain arrhythmia mechanisms. In this cohort, the Vein of Marshall and Bachmann Bundle were the most frequently identified epicardial connections. Recognition and targeted ablation of these pathways may facilitate arrhythmia termination and improve procedural success in selected patients undergoing catheter ablation.

title: Guanxinning tablet attenuates carotid artery stenosis in Tibetan minipigs induced by a high-fat diet.
authorString: Qiu Q, Huang J, Yu C, Wang M, Pan Y, Shen P, Xu S, Gan Q, Chen M, Chen J.
abstractText: Carotid artery stenosis (CAS), a progressive narrowing of the carotid artery primarily driven by atherosclerosis, is a major risk factor for ischemic stroke. Guanxinning tablet (GXN), a well-established traditional Chinese medicine formula, is widely used in cardiovascular diseases; however, its therapeutic efficacy and underlying mechanisms against CAS remain largely unexplored. This study aims to investigate the effects of GXN on CAS and elucidate its underlying mechanisms. An accelerated CAS model was established using a high-fat diet (HFD) combined with left common carotid artery balloon injury in Tibetan miniature pigs. After 10 weeks of GXN administration, we evaluated systemic blood lipid profiles, carotid plaque burden via ultrasonography and arteriography, and serum biomarkers reflecting inflammation, oxidative stress, and endothelial injury. Comprehensive histopathological examinations (including H&E, Oil Red O, Masson's trichrome, EVG, and immunohistochemical stainings) of carotid tissues were subsequently performed. The results demonstrated that GXN significantly reduced cholesterol levels, attenuated carotid plaque area, and mitigated the severity of atherosclerotic lesions. Furthermore, GXN decreased lipid deposition and collagen accumulation while inhibiting vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) migration and intimal hyperplasia. Mechanistically, GXN suppressed oxidative stress and downregulated the expression of NF-κB, MMP-9, ICAM-1, and intimal α-SMA, thereby alleviating the inflammatory response and contributing to plaque stabilization. In summary, GXN ameliorates CAS by improving lipid metabolism, suppressing oxidative stress and inflammatory responses, and inhibiting VSMC proliferation and neointimal hyperplasia, highlighting its potential as a promising therapeutic agent for CAS.

title: Longitudinal Trends in Secondary Cardiovascular Prevention After Peripheral Artery Disease Diagnosis
authorString: Kallis K, Kumar P, Kang-Sim E, Neels N, Deng J, Quitevis CR, Alsaigh T, Ross EG.
abstractText:
Background:

Peripheral artery disease (PAD) is associated with substantial cardiovascular and limb-related morbidity, making long-term cardiovascular prevention an important part of care. However, longitudinal patterns of guideline-based quality measure achievement after PAD diagnosis remain poorly characterized in broad clinical populations.

Methods:

We conducted a retrospective cohort study using Epic Cosmos electronic health record (EHR) data to identify adults aged 18 to 75 years with PAD diagnosed from 2019 to 2023. Four cardiovascular prevention components based on Merit-based Incentive Payment System (MIPS) Quality Measures were assessed annually after PAD diagnosis: blood pressure target achievement, documented tobacco-free status, antiplatelet therapy, and statin therapy. Complete achievement was defined as meeting all four measures. We assessed quality-measure achievement across groups, three-year quality-index trends, and associations between complete achievement and subsequent outcomes.

Results:
