Myocardial differential molecules were primarily enriched in cytochrome P450-mediated metabolism and detoxification pathways, with representative molecules including Adh6 and Cyp4f5. Hippocampal differential molecules mainly involved neuroactive ligand-receptor interactions, neural signal transduction, and synaptic regulation pathways, with representative molecules including Adra2b and Chrna3. These findings suggest that a S-band microwave exposure induces heart-brain axis autonomic regulatory imbalance, electrophysiological abnormalities, and synchronized changes in central neural signaling and peripheral metabolic detoxification. These results provide an experimental basis for risk assessment and protective strategies against high-power microwaves.

title: Dose-dependent maternal LV systolic compromise in hypertensive pregnancy: Novel predictors and cumulative remodelling from recurrent exposure.
authorString: Yadav P, Modi JN, Pushpalatha K, Khadanga S, Patel S.
abstractText:
Objectives

To characterise severity-graded cardiac compromise, dose-response trends, multivariable predictors, and the cumulative cardiac impact of recurrent hypertensive exposure in an Indian tertiary-care cohort with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP).

Study design

Prospective observational study, AIIMS Bhopal (February 2021-August 2022).

Study group

100 HDP women (gestational HTN 37, pre-eclampsia 46, chronic HTN 12, superimposed PE 5); Comparison: 50 normotensive term women. Transthoracic Doppler echocardiography (Philips EPIQ 7C); HDP per ACOG; diastolic dysfunction (DD) per ASE/EACVI 2016.

Main outcome measures

DD prevalence (primary); LVEF, concentric LVH, structural and Doppler parameters; Jonckheere-Terpstra trend, Cochran-Armitage, multivariable regression with VIF, and ROC analyses.

Results

LVEF was lower in HDP (p < 0.001; d = -0.60), with monotonic dose-response (p = 0.002) and independent multivariable effect (β = -5.19; p < 0.001). DD prevalence was 4% vs 2% (OR 1.85; p = 0.67) - underpowered (post-hoc power 0.12). Concentric LVH was confined to the Study Group (5%; chronic HTN 25%, superimposed PE 20%). Prior HDP history predicted cumulative remodelling: DD 17.4% vs 0.8% (p = 0.002); concentric LVH 17.4% vs 0.8% (p = 0.009); any cardiac abnormality 21.7% vs 3.1% (p = 0.007). LV wall thickness predicted LVH as determined by RWT (AUC 0.929; cutoff >9.5 mm).

Conclusions

HDP produces severity-graded subclinical systolic compromise in the index pregnancy; cumulative structural remodelling concentrates in women with prior HDP, chronic HTN, and early-onset disease, supporting targeted echocardiographic surveillance.

title: Implementation of nurse-led frontal electroencephalography for early neurological assessment in patients after cardiac arrest: the FRONT study.
authorString: van de Pol I, Court A, van Helden J, Seeber A, Scholten E, Moeniralam H, Lagerburg V, Schoonhoven L, Stalpers D, Wieske L.
abstractText: Continuous electroencephalography (cEEG) is a valuable tool for neurological prognostication after cardiac arrest. However, registration is often delayed by time-consuming electrode placement and limited availability of EEG technicians. This study investigated the implementation of a frontal EEG (fEEG) configuration using 6 self-adhesive electrodes by nurses within 3 h of Intensive Care Unit (ICU) admission in patients after cardiac arrest. The FRONT study followed a type 3 hybrid design. Nurses were trained to start an fEEG through a theoretical and practical session and were supported by a Step-by-Step interactive guide. Knowledge, attitude, and practice surveys were completed by nurses at baseline and after each fEEG application. Correct and timely application was measured prospectively in 60 patients. At baseline, the survey response rate was 46% (49/107); after application, it was 68% (41/60). Most nurses (84%) reported having sufficient knowledge of fEEG electrode placement and monitoring. The interactive guide was frequently used (98%) during fEEG initiation; the median application time was 20 min [IQR: 15-25]. All nurses found early fEEG monitoring meaningful; perception improved since implementation (3.98 ± 0.78 vs 4.54 ± 0.51, p < 0.001). During the implementation, an fEEG was applied in 88% of patients (53/60), including 73% (44/60) within 3 h. Electrode placement was confirmed as correct by EEG technicians in all evaluated patients. ICU nurses were able to apply fEEG monitoring with high levels of adoption, acceptability and fidelity following a short, multifaceted training program combined with an interactive guide. Further research is needed to clarify the interpretability, diagnostic performance, prognostic value, and clinical utility of nurse-led fEEG monitoring in post-resuscitation care. Early bedside EEG assessment by trained ICU nurses may facilitate timely neurological evaluation in routine clinical practice.

title: Beyond PREVENT-HF: Assessing the Added Value of NT-proBNP and Imaging for Prediction of Heart Failure.
authorString: Black N, Soltani F, Priestner L, Jenkins DA, Bradley J, Peek N, McDonagh T, Williams SG, Henderson A, Simpson J, Docherty KF, McMurray JJV, Petrie MC, Miller CA.
abstractText:
Background

Risk prediction models for incident heart failure (HF) may enable targeted primary prevention. The American Heart Association developed the PREVENT (Predicting Risk of CVD EVENTs) equations for incident HF (PREVENT-HF).

Objectives

The purpose of this study was to externally validate PREVENT-HF in a European community-based population and assess the incremental value of N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) and imaging biomarkers.

Methods

PREVENT-HF was externally validated and recalibrated in 428,084 participants from UK Biobank. Calibration, discrimination, and net clinical benefit were assessed within a competing risks framework. The incremental predictive value of NT-proBNP (N = 43,329) and cardiovascular magnetic resonance-derived variables (N = 58,360) was evaluated in dedicated subcohorts.

Results

Over a median follow-up of 14.1 years, 10,296 participants (2.4%) developed incident HF. PREVENT-HF substantially overpredicted HF risk (observed-to-expected ratio: 0.40), though discrimination was good (area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve: 0.742). Net clinical benefit was observed only under simulated higher-incidence scenarios. NT-proBNP was strongly and independently predictive of incident HF after adjustment for PREVENT-HF (subdistribution HR: 1.61; 95% CI: 1.52-1.70), significantly improving discrimination (change in area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve: 0.038) and net clinical benefit across all incidence scenarios. Body surface area-indexed left atrial volume, indexed left ventricular mass, left ventricular ejection fraction, and global longitudinal strain were independently predictive of HF after adjustment for PREVENT-HF. After additional adjustment for NT-proBNP, only indexed left atrial volume and left ventricular ejection fraction remained independently predictive.

Conclusions

PREVENT-HF requires recalibration for European populations and generates net clinical benefit only in higher-risk populations. NT-proBNP significantly augments PREVENT-HF and should be incorporated as a continuous predictor. Imaging-derived variables provide modest further prognostic information, which may support staged screening approaches.

title: Pro-platelet basic protein as an inflammatory molecular link between osteoporosis and coronary heart disease in postmenopausal women via MAPK-dependent macrophage modulation.
authorString: Lu F, Xing F, Liu C, Xing Y, Yang K, Dong G, Liu C, Nie X, Zhao X, Han G, Tian R, Wang K, Yang P, Kong N.
abstractText: Postmenopausal women frequently suffer from the co-occurrence of osteoporosis and coronary heart disease (CHD). However, existing studies on this association are largely limited to clinical and epidemiological observations, while the immunoinflammatory mechanisms underlying this comorbidity remain poorly understood. Herein, bioinformatic screening revealed that pro-platelet basic protein (PPBP), a chemokine, was co-upregulated in both diseases, which was also observed in serum samples from postmenopausal women, indicating PPBP as a candidate inflammatory molecular link connecting bone and cardiovascular homeostasis. We therefore selected PPBP for experimental validation. In vitro, PPBP knockdown inhibited both RANKL-induced osteoclast differentiation and ox-LDL-induced foam cell formation, while PPBP overexpression exerted opposite effects. These functional changes were accompanied by altered CXCR2 protein expression and phosphorylation of ERK, JNK and p38. Notably, in PPBP-overexpressing cells, CXCR2 inhibition can reduce MAPK phosphorylation, while pharmacological inhibition of MAPK signaling attenuated osteoclast differentiation and foam cell formation. In vivo, elevated PPBP expression levels were detected in serum and target organs of OVX osteoporotic mice and high-fat-diet-fed LDLR -/- atherosclerotic mice relative to control animals, which was associated with well-defined pathological biomarkers of each disease. Collectively, this study identified PPBP as a candidate inflammatory molecular link between osteoporosis and CHD. Targeted PPBP knockdown and pharmacological inhibition of downstream CXCR2 and MAPK signaling may represent a promising preclinical research direction. These findings provide new insights into the immunoinflammatory basis of osteoporosis-CHD comorbidity and offer pre-clinical evidence for disease management in postmenopausal women.

title: Reversal of Late Gadolinium Enhancement MRI-Assessed Left Atrial Fibrosis Following Cardioversion in Persistent Atrial Fibrillation.
authorString: Qin F, Chen Y, Xia T, Fang Z, Liu D, Song W, Chen W, Du H, Wang N, Xiao P, Chen W, Zhang B, Chen J, Gan C, Zhou P, Zhu X, Ran H, Guo D, Ling Z, Yin Y.

journal.title: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI

abstractText:
Background

Previous studies have shown that atrial fibrillation (AF) cardioversion may reverse atrial remodeling.

Purpose

To investigate whether LGE-MRI-assessed left atrial (LA) fibrosis regresses after persistent atrial fibrillation (PersAF) cardioversion to sinus rhythm, and to analyze the relationship between fibrosis change and traditional volume-based measures of LA reverse remodeling.

Study type

Prospective.

Population

Fifty-three patients following cardioversion for PersAF.

Field strength/sequence

3 T, cine balanced steady-state free precession cine and 3D inversion recovery gradient-echo sequences.

Assessment

MRI was performed 1-3 days after AF-cardioversion (early follow-up), and again at 3 months (late follow-up). Image analysis was performed by two observers using CVI42 and ADAS software. Data were compared between early and late follow-up. LA fibrosis on LGE-MRI was categorized by the image intensity ratio (IIR): core zone (IIR > 1.61) and border zone (0.97 < IIR ≤ 1.61). Maximum LA volume (LAVmax), LA ejection fraction (LAEF), LA strain, and left ventricular mass were assessed from cine data. An LAVmax reduction ≥ 15% from early to late follow-up defined LA reverse remodeling.

Statistical tests

Early and late follow-up data were compared using paired t-tests. Multivariable analysis was performed to assess the associations between changes in LA border and core zone and other LA parameters. A p-value < 0.05 was considered significant.

Results

Seventeen patients had volume-based LA reverse. Compared with early follow-up, LA border zone (22.2 [11.8-37.0] vs. 18.1 [11.8-25.2] cm2) and core zone (0.9 ± 3.0 vs. 0.1 ± 0.6 cm2) were significantly decreased. LAVmax was significantly reduced (97.2 ± 26.3 vs. 109.4 ± 32.7 mL), and LAEF (44.1 ± 15.8 vs. 32.2% ± 13.1%) and LA strain (27.4 ± 14.1 vs. 18.2% ± 8.6%) improved. Volume-based LA reverse remodeling was unrelated to ΔLA border (p = 0.955) or Δcore zone (p = 0.301).

Data conclusion

PersAF conversion to sinus rhythm resulted in a reduction in LGE-defined atrial enhancement, LAV reduction, and improved function. Fibrosis regression was independent of volume-based LA reverse remodeling.

Evidence level

2.

Technical efficacy

Stage 4.

title: Senescence markers diverge in space, timing, and phenotypic relevance during skin aging in mice.
authorString: Duan Sahbaz B, Ozturk Gurgen H, Lamotte B, Puttagunta S, Durham E, Garrido A, Can B, Fernandez ME, Oglesby E, Morrell CH, Lehrmann E, Rindone AN, Cherry C, Daswani PS, Camandola S, Bernier M, Cosgrove BD, De S, Baker DJ, Elisseeff J, Price NL, de Cabo R.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
journal.title: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
journal.isoabbreviation: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A

abstractText: The cell theory of aging posits that senescent cells accumulate with age, altering their environment and causing functional organ decline. The dynamics of their accumulation during normal aging and the extent to which it contributes to age-associated damage and disease remain unclear. Using the Study of Longitudinal Aging in Mice, which tracks two strains in both sexes, we identified skin health as a strong predictor of frailty. Quantification of three canonical senescence-associated markers (p16, p21, and γH2AX) in the skin of 320 animals showed variable effects of age on marker abundance: p16 increased with age, whereas p21 and γH2AX showed little or nonuniform changes. Associations between marker burden and age-related phenotypes were highly heterogeneous and varied by marker, sex, and strain. These findings underscore a complex, context-dependent relationship between senescence-associated markers and aging phenotypes, challenging the view that senescent cell accumulation uniformly drives organ decline.

title: Association between physical activity and obesity among young adults in Perak, Malaysia.
authorString: Sivapregas D, Bineid MM, Cheah ESG, Quen PL, Dhanapal ACTA, Vimaleswaran KS.
abstractText: Obesity remains a major health concern in Malaysia, particularly among young adults, where it contributes to the early onset of chronic diseases and reduces quality of life. This study investigated the relationship between physical activity and obesity indicators among young Malaysian adults. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 300 healthy participants aged 18-25 years from tertiary institutions in Perak, Malaysia. Anthropometric parameters, including height, weight, waist circumference, and hip circumference, were measured according to standard procedures to assess both overweight/obesity (based on BMI) and central obesity (based on WC). Socio-demographic information was collected using a validated questionnaire, and physical activity was evaluated using the Global Physical Activity Questionnaire (GPAQ), which captures total activity and domain-specific activities related to work, transport, and recreation. Descriptive statistics were used to determine the prevalence of obesity and physical inactivity and to explore their distributions across socio-demographic groups. Logistic regression was performed to examine associations between physical activity domains and obesity indices. Overweight/obesity and central obesity were observed in 34% and 32% of participants, respectively, while one-third (33%) were physically inactive. Higher household income was significantly associated with a greater prevalence of overweight/obesity (p = 0.003). After adjusting for potential confounders, total physical activity was inversely associated with both overweight/obesity and central obesity, with higher activity levels associated with lower odds of adiposity. Domain-specific analyses revealed that transport-related and recreational activities were significantly associated with a lower odds of obesity (p < 0.05 for all), whereas work-related activities showed no significant relationship. Physical activity was inversely associated with obesity indicators, though the strength of this relationship varied across activity domains. The findings emphasise the need to promote active lifestyles among young adults in tertiary education settings.

title: "You become free, you can tell her anything": Perceptions of a peer-based medication delivery implementation strategy to improve hypertension medication adherence in western Kenya.
authorString: Watiri C, Wachira J, Njuguna B, Gjonaj J, Kangogo K, Korir M, Laktabai J, Manji I, Pastakia SD, Tran DN, Vedanthan R.
abstractText: Medication adherence is a critical component of improving hypertension-related cardiovascular disease outcomes. Challenges with access to and possession of medication contribute to poor adherence. To address these challenges, we aim to implement a strategy in rural western Kenya that combines peer delivery of medications and health information technology. We sought to assess stakeholder perceptions of the planned implementation strategy, recognizing the importance of these perceptions to optimize successful implementation. Focus group discussions were conducted among people living with hypertension, community members, and health workers. In addition, key informant interviews were conducted with public sector health administrators.. Deductive codes were generated based on a priori themes, including perceptions of peers being involved in health service provision, medication delivery, psychosocial support, and the use of health information technology. The investigator team pooled codes according to conceptual alignment and integrated them into common themes after joint review and discussion. NVIVO 12 was used for data analysis. The Peers and Technology for Adherence, Access, Accountability, and Analytics (PT4A) implementation strategy was perceived to have both benefits and potential challenges. Major themes included the importance of trust resulting from a safe space to share experiences with peers, increased access to medications, improved hypertension management at the facility and community levels, and anticipated improved health outcomes for people living with hypertension. The success of the program was felt to rely heavily on the peers' competency and how well they communicated, which was viewed as a potential challenge by some stakeholders. This study was able to identify key perceptions regarding an implementation strategy that combines peer medication delivery and health information technology to improve hypertension medication adherence. Pre-implementation stakeholder engagement can unearth unique perspectives around perceived benefits and challenges that can be used to refine strategies to increase implementation success of evidence-based interventions in new contexts. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier (NCT number): NCT05051124.

title: Overview of recruitment strategies to reach the million milestone and characterization of the Million Veteran Program cohort.
authorString: Whitbourne SB, Williams AR, Brewer JVV, Deen J, Lord EM, Murphy S, Li Y, Ho YL, Pyatt M, Wolfrum S, Nguyen XT, Churby L, Villafranca A, Nikolaev E, Franklin A, Harrington KM, Pourali R, Shayan S, Selva L, Pyarajan S, Cho K, Moser J, Huang G, Tsao PS, Muralidhar S, Gaziano JM, VA Million Veteran Program.
abstractText: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Million Veteran Program (MVP) began in 2011 with the goal of recruiting at least one million Veterans to participate in a large population genetic and health research program. The Million Milestone Campaign (MMC) was implemented between 2022 and 2023 to reach pre-pandemic recruitment rates and the millionth enrollee by Veterans Day of 2023. The objectives are to describe and evaluate the enrollment yield of MMC recruitment strategies and to characterize the cumulative MVP cohort. During the MMC, multiple recruitment strategies, including paper invitation mailings, recruitment calls, mass emails, enroll by mail invitations, and digital marketing, were implemented using a "surround sound" model. Strategy effectiveness was assessed for each enrollment modality from September 2022 through July 2024. Email and digital media reach were measured by click-through rates and ads viewed. Standard mean differences were used to compare the demographics of enrollees during the MMC with those of enrollees prior, and the cumulative MVP cohort with those of non-MVP VA users. More than 6.5 million Veterans were contacted and 109,912 enrolled during the MMC. Enrollment rates from recruitment calls (13.7%) were highest, followed by invitations to enroll by mail (7.8%), email (0.8%), and paper invitations (0.6%). Emails yielded the most enrollments (n = 46,999, 43% of total enrollments), followed by recruitment calls (n = 22,069, 20%), paper invitations (n = 16,062, 14.6%), and invitations to enroll by mail (n = 7,762,7.1%). There were small differences in demographics between those enrolled during the MMC and prior enrollees (n = 906,672); likewise, the cumulative cohort (N = 1,016,584) of largely male participants resembles the non-MVP VA user population. In the year leading to the culmination of one million MVP participants, the multi-strategy MMC resulted in recruiting nearly 110,000 Veterans and informing ongoing recruitment. Combined strategies used in a surround sound model of recruitment yielded enrollments aligned with pre-pandemic rates and accumulated one-tenth the largest cohort of Veterans in VA research history. MVP's integration within the VHA as a learning health care system, along with linkages to health records and other data sources, is a resource for investigators to improve Veteran health care with precision medicine.

title: DEL-1 deficiency exacerbates inflammation-driven cardiac dysfunction during angiotensin II-induced hypertension.
authorString: Maslakova A, Knyrim M, Marterstock M, Das A, Speier S, Mirtschink P, Chavakis T, Deussen A, Baksi A, Kopaliani I.
abstractText: Hypertension is associated with inflammatory activation in the heart that contributes to cardiac remodelling and functional impairment, yet the mechanisms that regulate these cardiac inflammatory responses remain incompletely understood. Developmental endothelial locus-1 (DEL-1) is a secreted immunomodulatory glycoprotein that regulates leukocyte recruitment and inflammation resolution; however, its constitutive role in cardiac inflammation and remodelling during hypertension has not been defined. Here, we investigated the function of DEL-1 during angiotensin II (ANGII)-induced hypertension using Del1-deficient mice. Echocardiographic analysis revealed a distinct temporal pattern of cardiac remodelling during ANGII infusion. Del1<sup>KO</sup> mice developed early systolic dysfunction accompanied by diastolic alterations three days after ANGII infusion, whereas wild-type (WT) littermates maintained preserved systolic performance at this stage. Importantly, these functional differences occurred in the absence of differences in arterial pressure, suggesting a blood pressure independent mechanism. Flow cytometric analysis demonstrated markedly enhanced recruitment of neutrophils and inflammatory Ly6C<sup>hi</sup> monocytes into Del1<sup>KO</sup> hearts during the early phase of hypertension, indicating amplified inflammatory activation. This was accompanied by activation of the bone marrow haematopoietic compartment, characterized by an early expansion of long-term haematopoietic stem cells, followed by a transient increase in haematopoietic progenitor populations during the intermediate phase of hypertension. During later stages of hypertension, systolic function partially recovered in Del1<sup>KO</sup> mice but was accompanied by exaggerated hypertrophic remodelling and increased cardiac fibrosis. Together, these findings identify DEL-1 as an endogenous regulator that restrains early cardiac inflammation at the onset of hypertension and supports balanced cardiac adaptation during prolonged hypertensive stress. KEY POINTS: Hypertension is associated with cardiac inflammation and remodelling, but endogenous mechanisms that restrain early inflammatory cardiac injury remain incompletely defined. Developmental endothelial locus-1 (DEL-1) deficiency caused early systolic dysfunction and diastolic alterations during angiotensin II-induced hypertension, despite no early difference in arterial blood pressure. Loss of DEL-1 amplified early recruitment of neutrophils and Ly6C<sup>hi</sup> inflammatory monocytes to the heart and was associated with activation of the bone marrow haematopoietic compartment. At later stages, systolic function partially recovered in Del1<sup>KO</sup> mice, but this was accompanied by exaggerated fibrotic remodelling and increased profibrotic gene expression. These findings identify endogenous DEL-1 as a protective regulator that limits early inflammatory cardiac injury and supports balanced cardiac adaptation during hypertensive stress.

title: An Intra- and Inter-Individually Insensitive PCG Monitoring SoC for Long-Term Wearable Devices.
authorString: Wang Y, Chen Z, Zhao H, Zhao Y, Martins RP, Chan CH, Zhang M.

journal.title: IEEE transactions on biomedical circuits and systems

abstractText: The phonocardiogram (PCG) is capable of detecting structural cardiac anomalies, enabling real-time wearable monitoring using integrated neural networks (NNs). However, it encounters challenges such as fluctuations in diagnostic accuracy due to intra- and inter-individual variability, underutilization of NN hardware across heterogeneous algorithms, and unnecessary energy loss caused by always-on analog-front-ends (AFEs) and convolutional NNs (CNNs). This article presents a fully integrated, robust, and extremely low-power PCG monitoring System-on-Chip (SoC) that utilizes CNNs. It features three key techniques: 1) a dynamic framing mechanism combined with on-chip training to enhance classification stability against individual variability; 2) a reconfigurable computing array (RCA) that supports filtering, dynamic time warping (DTW), inference, and training to improve hardware utilization; 3) a comprehensive clock- and power-gating scheme for the AFE and CNN to boost energy efficiency. The prototype PCG SoC, using a 28-nm CMOS process, achieves 98.9% classification accuracy on the Yaseen dataset. In addition, it maintains an average accuracy of 97.1% with a standard deviation of 0.72% across the evaluated heart-rate range of 60-120 bpm, while consuming only 0.36 μJ per classification.

title: Long-Term Nonmalignant Chronic Health Conditions in Childhood, Adolescent, and Young Adult Differentiated Thyroid Carcinoma Survivors and the Impact of Radioactive Iodine Therapy: Evidence from Real-World Data.
authorString: Yackobovitch-Gavan M, Bello R, Oron T, Lazar L, Hayek S.

journal.title: Thyroid : official journal of the American Thyroid Association

abstractText:
Background

Differentiated thyroid carcinoma (DTC) is the most common endocrine malignancy in children, adolescents, and young adults (CAYA) with survival exceeding 98%. Real-world data on long-term nonmalignant chronic health conditions (CHCs) remain scarce.

Objective

To characterize long-term nonmalignant CHCs in CAYA DTC survivors relative to cancer-free controls and explore associations with radioactive iodine (RAI) exposure.

Methods

This retrospective cohort study used Clalit Health Services electronic health records (Israel, 1982-2022) comparing 5267 DTC survivors (diagnosed at age < 40) with 21,062 matched cancer-free controls. Incident CHCs occurring ≥2 years post-DTC diagnosis/index-date were assessed across metabolic, cardiovascular, renal, hepatic, gastrointestinal, pulmonary, skeletal, autoimmune/rheumatologic, and emotional domains and were evaluated using Cox proportional hazards models to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). RAI subgroup analyses were exploratory.

Results

During a median follow-up of 14.7 years (interquartile range 8.8-23.2), the risk of developing ≥1 CHC did not differ significantly between DTC survivors and cancer-free controls (54.4% vs. 52.0%; HR, 1.05; 95% CI, 1.00-1.11; p = 0.066). Survivors were more likely to experience multimorbidity (≥2 CHCs 35.7% vs. 32.0%) and had higher risks of several specific organ-system conditions: osteoporosis (HR 1.33; 95% CI: 1.14-1.56), chronic kidney disease (HR 1.61; 95% CI: 1.32-1.96), gastroesophageal disorders (HR 1.35; 95% CI: 1.26-1.45), dyslipidemia (HR 1.23; 95% CI: 1.16-1.32), and hypertension (HR 1.21; 95% CI: 1.13-1.29). Pulmonary, cardiovascular, autoimmune, hepatic, and clinically diagnosed emotional disorders did not differ significantly between groups. Exploratory analyses revealed a dose-dependent RAI risk gradient (1 course: HR 1.20; 95% CI: 1.06-1.35; ≥2 courses: HR 1.33; 95% CI: 1.16-1.52).

Conclusions

Despite excellent overall survival, CAYA DTC survivors face a modest overall increase in CHC risk alongside notably greater multisystem morbidity. RAI-associated risk trends are exploratory and need further research. These findings support risk-adapted therapy and structured long-term survivorship monitoring.

title: Validation of 1 T MRI in Cuprizone-Induced Demyelination in C57BL/6 Mice: Comparison with Histology and 7 T MRI.
authorString: Krasnov MS, Volodina VV, Zaitsev PE, Pavlova OS, Antonov SA, Maksaeva AO, Apukhtina UA, Likhov AR, Zherdeva VV.
abstractText: To evaluate the feasibility of noninvasive monitoring using 1 Tesla (T) MRI for assessing white matter damage in a cuprizone-induced model of demyelination in specific-pathogen-free (SPF) C57BL/6 mice. Demyelination was induced in SPF C57BL/6 mice by administering a diet supplemented with 0.2% cuprizone for 6 weeks. In vivo MRI scans were acquired using a low-field 1 T MRI, including T2-weighted imaging (T2WI) with a fast spin-echo (FSE) sequence (TR/TE = 5600/82.2 ms). For validation, high-field MRI was performed on a 7 T preclinical scanner, generating T2WI, T1-weighted imaging (T1WI), magnetization transfer ratio (MTR) maps, and T2 relaxation time maps. Histological analysis served as the gold standard for validation. Brain sections were stained with Luxol Fast Blue to assess myelin content and Hematoxylin & Eosin for general morphology and cellularity. Quantitative region-of-interest (ROI) analysis was focused on the medial part of the corpus callosum. Statistical significance between groups was assessed using Student's t‑test, with a significance threshold set at p < 0.005. 1 T MRI revealed a statistically significant increase in the mean T2WI signal intensity in the corpus callosum of cuprizone‑treated mice compared to controls (p < 0.005). This finding was corroborated by high-field 7 T MRI, which demonstrated a concomitant increase in both T2WI and T1WI signal intensities, as well as a decrease in MTR values within the same region. Histological assessment confirmed the MRI observations, revealing significant demyelination and atrophy of the corpus callosum in the cuprizone group assessed by 25-30% reduction in corpus callosum area compared to controls (p < 0.01). The spatial pattern of signal alterations on MRI closely matched the distribution of histological damage. Low-field 1 T MRI provides a reliable means of detecting corpus callosum demyelination in the cuprizone mouse model. The proposed T2‑weighted imaging protocol, which requires no contrast agents, minimal infrastructure costs, and straightforward postprocessing, offers a practical tool for longitudinal monitoring and for evaluating the extent of lesion involvement in preclinical studies of demyelinating diseases.

title: Recent-Onset Atrial Fibrillation: What to Do for Maximum Impact a Matter of Time, Choices and Real-world Challenges.
authorString: Ballatore A, Poggio A, De Ferrari GM, Anselmino M.
abstractText:
Purpose of review

The aim of this narrative review is to provide a practical and current perspective on how care for recent onset atrial fibrillation (AF) can be optimized, taking into account both the principles of AF care described in current guidelines and barriers in clinical practice. Within this framework, the latest evidence on anticoagulation, long-term rate versus rhythm control and comorbidities management is presented. Areas of clinical uncertainty are illustrated to help both cardiologists and emergency medicine physicians navigate new-onset AF.

Recent findings

Early rhythm control can improve AF outcomes among recent onset AF patients, with catheter ablation emerging as a disease-modifying strategy, leading to improved long-term outcomes and a lower rate of arrhythmia recurrences compared with antiarrhythmic drugs. Early rhythm control, together with structured risk factors modification and oral anticoagulation can strongly influence the course of AF and are particularly effective in the early stages of AF. Patient education, starting from the Emergency Department is pivotal in shaping the future trajectory of AF patients.

title: Thymol Modulates Cardiac and Skeletal Muscle Gene Expression in a D-Galactose/Aluminum Chloride-Induced Oxidative Damage Model in Rats.
authorString: Hacımustafaoğlu F, Çaykara Peran B, Erzurumlu Y, Serdaroğlu E, Çevreli B.
abstractText: Aluminum chloride and D-galactose are commonly used to induce experimental conditions characterized by redox imbalance, inflammatory activation, and senescence-like tissue alterations. This study investigated whether thymol modulates selected molecular responses in cardiac and skeletal muscle tissues in a D-galactose/aluminum chloride-induced oxidative damage model. Forty male rats were divided into four groups of ten rats each: control, oxidative damage, oxidative damage plus thymol, and thymol alone. Oxidative damage was induced by D-galactose and aluminum chloride administration, and thymol was administered by oral gavage. Cardiac Myh7, Hif1a, Vegfa, and Nos3 expression was evaluated to represent contractile/remodeling, hypoxia-related, angiogenic, and endothelial responses, respectively. In skeletal muscle, Bdnf, Sod1, Cat, and Tnf were assessed as markers of neurotrophic/metabolic regulation, antioxidant defense, and inflammatory signaling. The oxidative damage model decreased cardiac Myh7 and Hif1a expression and reduced skeletal muscle Bdnf, Sod1, and Cat expression, while increasing skeletal muscle Tnf expression. Thymol partially improved these alterations and increased cardiac Vegfa and Nos3 expression. These findings suggest that thymol modulates redox-, inflammatory-, endothelial-, angiogenic-, and antioxidant defense-related gene expression in cardiac and skeletal muscle tissues under oxidative damage conditions.

title: Association Between Low-Carbohydrate Diets and Periodontitis: Results From a Nationwide Cross-Sectional Study Using NHANES 2009-2014 Data.
authorString: Xu X, Zeng F, Bao D, Ji Z, Huang Y.
abstractText: To our knowledge, no epidemiological study has investigated the associations of a low-carbohydrate diet (LCD) on periodontitis in a free-living population. We aimed to explore the associations between LCDs and periodontitis in a nationally representative sample of U.S. adults, focusing on the quality and type of macronutrients. Dietary intake was measured using two 24-h dietary recalls, and overall, healthy, and unhealthy LCD scores were calculated based on the proportion of energy from total and subtype carbohydrates, proteins, and fats. We used binary logistic regression to examine the association between LCD adherence and periodontitis, and ordinal logistic regression to further evaluate periodontitis severity. Among 9764 adults aged 30-80 years, the overall LCD score was not associated with periodontitis after multivariable adjustment. However, every 5-point increase in the healthy LCD score was associated with 7% lower odds of periodontitis (OR = 0.93; 95% CI: 0.89-0.96), while every 5-point increase in the unhealthy LCD score was associated with 7% higher odds (OR = 1.07; 95% CI: 1.03-1.11). Compared with the lowest quartile, participants in the highest quartile of healthy and unhealthy LCD scores had 20% lower odds (OR = 0.80, 95% CI: 0.69-0.91, p trend = 0.002) and 27% higher odds (OR = 1.27, 95% CI: 1.11-1.45, p trend = 0.002) of periodontitis, respectively. In exploratory subgroup analyses, potential interactions were observed for smoking (p interaction = 0.024), physical activity (p interaction = 0.004), and hypertension (p interaction = 0.038). Our results suggest that the relationship between LCDs and periodontitis depends on the quality and types of macronutrients consumed.

title: Expanding the Clinical Spectrum of ALAS2-Associated Protoporphyria: Fatal Liver-Predominant Disease Without Recognised Photosensitivity in a Black South African Child.
authorString: Nevondwe P, Beretta M, Visagie JL, Vorster CB.
abstractText: X-linked protoporphyria (XLP) is a rare disorder caused by gain-of-function variants in ALAS2 and is classically characterised by painful childhood-onset photosensitivity. Severe hepatobiliary disease is an uncommon but potentially fatal complication and may pose a diagnostic challenge when characteristic photosensitivity is not recognised. We report an 8-year-old Black South African boy with progressive liver disease characterised by recurrent acute-on-chronic liver failure, cholestatic liver injury, portal hypertension, variceal haemorrhage and hepatic encephalopathy. Despite extensive metabolic, infectious, autoimmune and hepatological investigations, no unifying diagnosis was established. Characteristic photosensitivity was not reported or recognised during life. Whole-exome sequencing identified the recurrent pathogenic hemizygous ALAS2 variant NM_000032.5:c.1706_1709del (p.Glu569GlyfsTer24), which was independently confirmed by Oxford Nanopore long-read whole-genome sequencing and bidirectional Sanger sequencing. The molecular findings, together with the clinical and histopathological phenotype, supported ALAS2-associated protoporphyria. This report adds to the limited published literature on genetically characterised XLP and expands the recognised clinical spectrum by documenting a fatal liver-predominant presentation in which characteristic photosensitivity was not recognised during life. To our knowledge, this is the first genetically confirmed case reported in a Black African child and the first report of the recurrent c.1706_1709del variant in this population, extending its documented occurrence across diverse ancestral backgrounds.

title: Neobladder Impact on Liver Function: A Nationwide Analysis.
authorString: Lee CU, Kim JH, Kim JW, Lee YS, Min K, Tae JH, Choi SY, Park M, Lee Y, Choi J.
abstractText:
Background

Radical cystectomy (RC) with urinary diversion alters gastrointestinal and metabolic physiology. Orthotopic neobladders (NBs) have traditionally been viewed with caution in patients with hepatic concerns owing to potential reabsorption of urinary solutes. This study aimed to investigate the long-term risks of de novo liver disease, hypertension (HTN), and diabetes mellitus (DM) after RC, challenging the prevailing assumption of hepatic toxicity from NB diversion.

Methods

This retrospective nationwide cohort study used data from the Korean National Health Insurance Service database (2010-2023). Patients without preoperative liver disease, HTN, or DM were included. Primary endpoints were the incidence of liver disease, HTN, and DM. Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) balanced covariates in NB and ileal conduit (IC) groups. Cox proportional hazard models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs).

Results

In the IPTW-adjusted cohort (n = 22,144), NB was associated with a 29% lower risk of de novo liver disease compared with IC (HR, 0.71; 95% confidence interval, 0.59-0.84; P < 0.001). Patients with NB also demonstrated a lower incidence of liver cirrhosis (2.04% vs. 2.63%; P = 0.003). In the open-surgery subgroup, NB was associated with reduced risks of HTN (HR 0.92; P < 0.001) and DM (HR, 0.94; P = 0.028). Limitations include the retrospective design and use of administrative codes as diagnoses.

Conclusion

Contrary to long-standing concerns regarding urea reabsorption, NB diversion was associated with a lower incidence of de novo liver disease and better metabolic preservation than IC diversion.

title: AI-Assisted Multimodal Imaging Integration for Individualized Transseptal Puncture Planning During Atrial Fibrillation Ablation.
authorString: Liu Z, Wang J, Wang W, Sun Y, Zhou J, Liu Y, Cao M, Wang S, Zou C.

journal.title: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine

abstractText: Transseptal puncture (TSP) is a critical step during atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation, and accurate anatomical understanding of the interatrial septum is essential for individualized procedural planning. Intracardiac echocardiography (ICE) provides real-time visualization of septal anatomy but is limited by its two-dimensional representation and operator dependence. This study developed an artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted multimodal imaging framework integrating preprocedural computed tomography angiography (CTA) with intraoperative ICE to provide patient-specific three-dimensional (3D) anatomical guidance for TSP planning. This single-center study enrolled 700 patients undergoing AF ablation. An AI framework was developed using data from 500 patients to perform automated segmentation, 3D reconstruction, and CTA-ICE multimodal image integration. The framework was evaluated in an independent temporal validation cohort of 200 patients. The primary outcome was the influence of AI-assisted anatomical information on individualized TSP planning, assessed by changes in puncture strategy following AI-assisted assessment. Secondary outcomes included decision confidence, planning time, interreader agreement, and procedural feasibility. The AI framework achieved an overall Dice similarity coefficient of 0.854 for automated anatomical segmentation and a Dice coefficient of 0.862 for 3D left atrial reconstruction. In the temporal validation cohort, at least one AI-recommended adjustment was incorporated into the final TSP strategy in 68 patients (34.0%). The recommendations addressed involved three key components of TSP planning: puncture site category in 52 patients (26.0%), puncture direction in 61 patients (30.5%), and puncture trajectory or angle in 74 patients (37.0%). AI-assisted assessment increased decision confidence (4.3 ± 0.6 vs. 3.4 ± 0.8, p < 0.001), reduced planning time (28.7 ± 10.3 vs. 42.5 ± 15.2 s, p < 0.001), and improved interreader agreement for anatomical assessment. In the temporal validation cohort, acute successful TSP was achieved in 196 patients (98.0%), with a mean transseptal time of 6.8-2.5 min and an overall complication rate of 3.0%. AI-assisted integration of preprocedural CTA with intraoperative ICE provides patient-specific 3D anatomical information that supports individualized TSP planning. The proposed framework demonstrated feasibility and compatibility with anatomical assessment and procedural planning, hopefully contributing to improve procedural or clinical outcomes.

title: Development of a Clinician-Level Measure of Comprehensiveness and Its Associations With Primary Care Quality.
authorString: Chung Y, Bazemore A, Shuemaker J, Bal P, Phillips R.
abstractText:
Purpose

The purpose of this study was to develop a novel digital quality measure of comprehensiveness for primary care clinicians and to evaluate its association with care quality.

Methods

We developed a clinician-level comprehensiveness measure based on the range of services provided using existing literature, the American Board of Family Medicine certification scope of practice surveys, and a technical expert panel. We applied the measure to electronic health record data from more than 1,000 primary care practices in the Primary Care Information Management and Evaluation Registry in 2018-2019. We used descriptive analyses to assess variation in clinician comprehensiveness scores, and bivariate and multivariate linear regression models to test associations with quality of care.

Results

The 2,117 primary care clinicians studied had a mean comprehensiveness score of 0.51 on a scale from 0 to 1, with higher scores denoting provision of a greater range of services. Higher scores were associated with better quality of care, particularly with respect to cancer and depression screenings and diabetes care. When scores were converted to a 100-point scale, a 10-point increase in score was associated with a 3.3-percentage point (5.2%), 2.1-percentage point (4.8%), and 2.8-percentage point (4.2%) increase in breast, cervical, and colorectal cancer screening rate, respectively, and a 5.1-percentage point (14.3%) increase in depression screening. Increasing scores were similarly associated with improved quality of diabetes care, but no associations were found with body mass index screening or hypertension control.

Conclusions

The findings of this study align with those of prior studies of primary care comprehensiveness measures and outcomes. Using expert input and empirical testing, we developed an easily implementable quality measure that meets digital measurement requirements and that is associated with improved quality of clinical care, supporting its integration into performance reporting and value-based payment models.Abstract available in: يبرع (Arabic); हिन्दी (Chinese); Francais (French); Deutsch (German); हिन्दी (Hindi); Indonesian (Indonesian); (Japanese); Portugues (Portuguese); Español (Spanish).

title: Pre-Pregnancy and Contraceptive Care Experiences Among Black and Latina Women With Type 2 Diabetes and Hypertension: A Qualitative Study.
authorString: Marshall C, Nguyen A, Kang M, Schiavon SL.
abstractText:
Purpose

Previous research has shown unmet needs for family planning care for individuals with type 2 diabetes (T2D) and hypertension, both of which disproportionately impact non-Hispanic Black and Hispanic individuals. This study aimed to explore and describe experiences of pre-pregnancy and contraceptive counseling and care among reproductive-aged Black and Latina patients with T2D or hypertension or both.

Methods

We purposively sampled 32 non-pregnant Black or Latina patients from Federally Qualified Health Centers who had T2D or hypertension or both. We conducted semistructured interviews, asking participants about experiences receiving pre-pregnancy and contraceptive care and about family planning goals and desires. We analyzed data using thematic analysis.

Results

Participants reported receiving limited information from clinicians about the potential impact of T2D or hypertension on pregnancy. However, many parous participants learned about these impacts through their experiences with pregnancy complications. Many participants described feeling pressured by clinicians to use contraception. Participants with hypertension also encountered challenges obtaining their desired contraceptive methods due to their condition. We found that the presence of a strong patient-clinician relationship can positively influence patients' receptivity to clinician-initiated conversations about family planning goals.

Conclusions

This study indicates a need to develop patient-centered approaches that address information needs and recognize the complexity of pre-pregnancy and contraceptive care in the context of T2D and hypertension. Additionally, greater attention to the unique challenges that Black and Latina women face in their health care must be considered.

title: Clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential and progression of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation.
authorString: Kim JH, Ahn HJ, Han S, Lee SR, Oh S, Koh Y, Choi EK.
abstractText:
Background

Clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) is associated with incident atrial fibrillation (AF). However, its relationship with AF progression remains unclear.

Objective

To assess whether CHIP is associated with AF progression.

Methods

We prospectively enrolled patients with paroxysmal AF who underwent deep targeted sequencing for CHIP mutations between April 2021 and December 2022. Variant allele fraction (VAF) ≥2.0% defined CHIP. The primary endpoint was documented AF progression, defined as either (1) AF documented on at least two separate 12-lead ECGs obtained >1 week apart, or (2) 100% AF burden on extended ECG monitoring. We assessed the association between CHIP and AF progression using Cox proportional hazards regression. In patients with available left atrial (LA) electroanatomical mapping, we compared low-voltage areas (LVA) by clonal hematopoiesis (CH) status (VAF ≥1.0% cutoff).

Results

Among the 310 patients (mean age 65.7±5.7 years), CHIP was present in 64 patients (20.6%). Over a mean follow-up of 2.6±1.0 years, documented AF progression occurred in 10/64 (15.6%) patients with CHIP and 15/246 (6.1%) without CHIP. CHIP was independently associated with AF progression [adjusted hazard ratio 3.38, 95% CI 1.45-7.85; P = 0.005]. In an exploratory mapping subgroup, extensive LVA (≥10.0%) was more frequent in CH [24.4% vs 9.5%; unadjusted OR 3.10, 95% CI 1.10-8.71] and numerically higher at the VAF ≥2.0% cutoff.

Conclusion

In patients with paroxysmal AF, CHIP was associated with a 3.4-fold higher risk of documented AF progression. Exploratory mapping findings suggest a possible association between CH and advanced atrial substrate, warranting further validation.

title: Arrhythmia-specific timing of first detection during extended textile ECG monitoring: a recording-level cumulative incidence analysis.
authorString: Gonzálvez B, Castrejón-Castrejón S, Díez A, Llorca D, Ruiz J, García CZ, Gómez RM, Merino JL.
abstractText:
Background

Extended ambulatory electrocardiographic monitoring improves detection of intermittent arrhythmias, but real-world recordings often have variable duration, and conventional diagnostic-yield curves may not account for censoring.

Methods

We retrospectively analysed 9629 anonymized ambulatory ECG recordings of at least 24 h acquired in routine clinical practice between 2018 and 2024. Endpoints were first ECG-defined detection of atrial fibrillation (AF) burden ≤1% and ≤ 10%, non-sustained ventricular tachycardia (nsVT), pauses >3 s, bradycardia <40 beats/min for ≥60 s, and premature ventricular contraction (PVC) burden >10%. Arrhythmias were algorithm-flagged and staff-verified. Kaplan-Meier estimates were used to derive day-30-normalized cumulative incidence functions (CIF*).

Results

Arrhythmias of interest were detected in 3611 recordings (37.5%). Median observed monitoring duration was 15.4 days (interquartile range 8.2-28.2). At day 14, CIF* was 65.8% for AF burden ≤1%, 71.0% for AF burden ≤10%, and 71.1% for nsVT, indicating continued first detections during days 14-30. In contrast, PVC burden >10% accumulated early, with CIF* of 59.6% at 24 h and 71.5% at 5 days.

Conclusions

In this large recording-level cohort, first ECG-defined detection timing differed by arrhythmia target. Low-burden AF and nsVT continued to accrue after day 14, whereas frequent PVC burden was usually identified earlier. These findings support target-specific monitoring strategies, while clinical actionability could not be assessed in this anonymized variable-duration dataset.

title: Therapeutic Effects of Low-Frequency Renal Nerve Neuromodulation in a Preclinical Model of Obesity-Induced Hypertension.
authorString: Salman IM, Ameer OZ, Hassan SF, Sridhar A, Hsieh YH, Lewis SJ.
abstractText: Obesity-associated hypertension is increasingly prevalent and often resistant to pharmacological treatment. The renal nerve is a promising target for neuromodulation due to its critical role in blood pressure (BP) regulation. This study investigated the efficacy and physiological impact of low-frequency renal nerve stimulation (RNS) in Zucker fatty rats (ZFRs), a preclinical model of obesity-induced hypertension. Thirteen anesthetized male ZFRs underwent surgical implantation of bipolar stimulating electrodes on the left renal nerve. RNS was applied at 2.5 Hz and 5.0 Hz (0.5 mA, 0.5 ms, 30 s) while continuously recording mean arterial pressure (MAP), heart rate (HR), hindquarter flow (HQF), and ipsilateral and contralateral renal cortical perfusion (RCP). Hindquarter resistance (HQR) and renal cortical resistance (RCR) were calculated from MAP and corresponding flow values. Baseline MAP was 115 ± 5 mmHg. RNS at both frequencies produced immediate reductions in MAP (2.5 Hz: 29 ± 6 mmHg; 5.0 Hz: 30 ± 6 mmHg) without significant changes in HR. Both frequencies similarly increased HQF, with a corresponding decrease in HQR. Ipsilateral RCP was reduced at both frequencies, with a greater decrease observed at 5.0 Hz. RCR was reduced to a similar extent on both sides, with contralateral RCP significantly reduced only at 2.5 Hz. Low-frequency RNS effectively lowers BP in ZFRs possibly via reflex-mediated vasodilation. Reductions in renal vascular resistance despite reduced flow likely reflect compensatory renal vasodilation. Importantly, the 2.5 Hz protocol achieved similar BP-lowering effects with a smaller impact on renal perfusion, supporting its potential as a safer neuromodulatory strategy in obesity-related hypertension.

title: An Adverse Outcome Pathway-Based Hierarchical Ensemble Framework for Mechanistic Hazard Identification of Drug-Induced Heart Failure.
authorString: Sha F, Gong J, Zhang W, Li N, Huang X, Li X.
abstractText: Drug-induced heart failure arises through multiple molecular initiating events and key events that conventional single-endpoint approaches cannot capture. We developed a four-tier adverse outcome pathway (AOP)-based hierarchical ensemble framework encoding the AOP 558 causal chain-phosphodiesterase 4D (PDE4D) inhibition, cAMP elevation and calcium dysregulation, and heart failure-into tier-specific prediction models. Hierarchical here refers to the AOP tier structure (MIE-KE1-KE2-AO), not cross-tier stacking. By integrating multi-source public databases, four molecular fingerprints, and six algorithms, the tier-specific consensus models achieved AUC values of 0.920-0.990 in internal validation. External validation on the FDA DICTrank reference list yielded an AUC of 0.667 (vs. 0.5), an accuracy of 75.9% (below the 84.0% majority-class baseline), and a sensitivity of 26.5% (9/34). SHAP analysis identified tier-specific structural features associated with PDE4D binding, cAMP signaling, and calcium homeostasis. This framework supports tier-level mechanistic hazard characterization of drug-induced heart failure.

title: Alignment to the Mexican Dietary Guidelines 2023 and its Association with Nutritional Status and Cardiometabolic Indicators in Mexican Women.
authorString: Chavarría-Ornelas P, Rodríguez-Ramírez S, Shamah-Levy T, Trejo-Valdivia B.
abstractText:
Background

Adult women have the highest prevalence of obesity in Mexico. However, previous studies found no significant associations between dietary quality scores based on the 2015 Mexican Dietary Guidelines and health outcomes in Mexican women.

Objective

To evaluate alignment with the Mexican Healthy and Sustainable Dietary Guidelines (GASS, by its acronym in Spanish) 2023 among Mexican women of childbearing age and analyze its association with nutritional status and cardiometabolic indicators.

Methods

A cross-sectional, observational study was conducted using a subsample of 3,612 non-pregnant, non-lactating women aged 20-49 years from the National Health and Nutrition Survey 2018-19, with anthropometric, biochemical and dietary information. Multiple logistic regression models estimated associations between GASSMx-2023 scores and binary health outcomes, while multinomial logistic regression was used for outcomes with more than two categories.

Results

Overall alignment with GASS was low. Moderate alignment was associated with lower relative risk ratios (RRR) of obesity measured by body mass index, and lower odds of abdominal obesity, arterial hypertension and dyslipidemias among women aged 20-39 years. Lower RRR of prediabetes and diabetes and lower odds of hypertriglyceridemia were also observed in women aged 30-39 years. In contrast, among women aged 40-49 years, high alignment was associated with higher RRR of diabetes and higher odds of low HDL cholesterol.

Conclusion

The association between GASS alignment and health outcomes differed by age, with more favorable associations among women aged 20-39 years and some unfavorable associations among women aged 40-49 years. The GASSMx-2023 index may be useful tool for evaluating and monitoring interventions promoting GASS recommendations.

title: Association of pre-pregnancy obesity with residual preeclampsia risk among high-risk women receiving low-dose aspirin prophylaxis.
authorString: Luo D, Huang L, Li Y, He Y.
abstractText:
Objective

Preeclampsia (PE) is a major cause of maternal and neonatal morbidity. This study aimed to determine whether pre-pregnancy obesity was associated with residual PE risk among high-risk women receiving low-dose aspirin (LDA) prophylaxis.

Methods

This retrospective cohort study screened 482 women with pre-pregnancy obesity. Of these, 100 women classified as high risk by the Fetal Medicine Foundation (FMF) model constituted the study group. Using 1:2 propensity score matching based on maternal age, parity, and first-trimester mean arterial pressure, 200 LDA-treated high-risk women with a normal pre-pregnancy BMI were selected as controls. Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate the associations of pre-pregnancy obesity and other clinical factors with PE.

Results

Among 11,395 deliveries, 482 occurred in women with pre-pregnancy obesity (prevalence, 4.23%). In the obesity group, the crude incidence of PE was 26.0% (26/100), with 8.0% (8/100) being preterm PE. In the normal-BMI control group, the incidence was significantly lower at 13.0% (26/200), with 6.0% (12/200) being preterm PE. Multivariate analysis identified chronic hypertension (aOR = 4.79, 95% CI 2.06-11.11) and gestational weight gain (GWG) (aOR = 1.09 per kg, 95% CI 1.02-1.16) as significant independent predictors of PE. The adjusted association between pre-pregnancy obesity and PE did not reach conventional statistical significance (aOR = 2.04, 95% CI 0.98-4.17; P = 0.053).

Conclusions

Among high-risk women receiving LDA prophylaxis, those with pre-pregnancy obesity had a higher crude incidence of PE than normal-BMI controls, although the adjusted association did not reach conventional statistical significance. Greater GWG was independently associated with PE risk and may contribute to the residual risk observed in this population. These findings support incorporating gestational weight counselling and management into comprehensive care alongside indicated pharmacological prophylaxis.

title: Association Between Cardiorespiratory Coupling and Exercise Capacity in Patients with Chronic Heart Failure.
authorString: Martins de Abreu R, Cairo B, Bari V, Burzo I, De Maria B, Bandera F, Piepoli M, Porta A.
abstractText:
Objective

This study evaluates the association between cardiorespiratory coupling (CRC) and exercise capacity, estimated via peak oxygen consumption (VO2peak), in patients with chronic heart failure (CHF).

Approach

Twenty-five CHF patients underwent VO2peak assessment during cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET). Electrocardiogram and respiratory flow (R) were recorded during spontaneous breathing before (PRE) and after (POST) CPET. Time- and frequency-domain heart period (HP) variability indexes were calculated. Bivariate CRC indexes were computed in high frequency (HF, from 0.15 to 0.4 Hz) band, such as the transfer function gain and phase from R to HP variability, squared coherence between HP variability and R in the HF band [K2HP‒R(HF)], and causal squared coherence from R to HP and vice versa. Correlation analysis of VO2peak with HP variability and CRC indexes in PRE and with their POST-to-PRE variations was performed in the overall cohort and in subgroups with preserved ejection fraction (pEF) and reduced ejection fraction (rEF).

Main results

No significant association of HP variability and CRC markers with VO2peak was found in PRE. In contrast, over the entire CHF group the POST-to-PRE variation of K2HP‒R(HF) showed a significant positive correlation with VO2peak, thus indicating that reactivity in recovering CRC after intense physical exercise is linked to exercise capacity. This association remained significant when considering exclusively pEF patients. Causal CRC indexes failed in this regard.

Significance

These findings suggest that K2HP‒R(HF) represents a candidate marker to estimate exercise capacity in CHF deserving further examination over larger databases.

title: Insights into the health and social care research priorities for ethnic minority groups: Findings from a UK survey.
authorString: Ekezie W, Chudasama YV, Czyznikowska B, Cassambai S, Mbah J, Curtis F, O'Mahoney LL, Willis A, Khunti K, Farooqi A.
abstractText:
Background

People from ethnic minority backgrounds have a higher risk of some health conditions when compared to majority populations. Hence, representing all ethnic groups is critical in research studies. We conducted a research priority setting study to ascertain the health and social care research areas of interest to ethnic minority populations.

Methods

We used a cross-sectional design to conduct a priority exercise using a survey between February and September 2023. We used a 29-item questionnaire, which included demographic questions and 37 health and social care research topic areas. Research priorities were collected through distributed paper and online survey formats. Recruitment occurred through community centres, social media and online news networks. Respondents were asked to select all research areas of interest for ethnic minorities in the UK. Selected priorities were ordered using the Standard Competition Ranking. Descriptive and subgroup analyses of the priority rankings were also conducted by ethnicity, sex, age groups, and long-term conditions (LTCs) status.

Results

The survey was completed by 982 participants representing five broad ethnic categories (Asian, Black, White-Other, White-UK and Mixed). Most participants were South Asians, 35-44 years old, females, and lived in the East Midlands region. 37% had existing LTCs. Overall, the top health priority areas with over 25% nominations were cancer, mental health, type 2 diabetes, dementia, arthritis and hypertension. Social care priorities were consistent across ethnic groups, with most areas selected by approximately 25% of participants in all ethnic groups, but the top five areas of interest were healthcare access, alcohol and drug misuse, education, discrimination and domestic violence. There were, however, variations in the significance, relevance, and ranking of the priorities across different ethnicities, sexes, age groups, and the existence of LTCs, highlighting the heterogeneity and unique interests of the participants.

Conclusions

The top-ranked health research priority areas reflect the increasing burden of LTCs, the possible presence of multiple long-term conditions, the related complexity of healthcare management, and their impact on ethnic minorities. Also, most social care topics were of high importance to all ethnic groups. Future research efforts in the UK should emphasise these topics for study populations and develop research agendas that are of significant concern to the community. Key research priorities and questions for future consideration are also provided.

title: Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) Summit on Genetics in Kidney Health: A United States Perspective.
authorString: Rastogi A, Rhee CM, Chang AR, Chapman AB, Chebib FT, Cheung M, Dahl NK, Fornoni A, Franceschini N, Freese ME, Gbadegesin R, Harris PC, Java A, King JM, Kiryluk K, Lieske JC, Lerma EV, Mehta A, Moyer AM, Norouzi S, Onuchic-Whitford AC, Mehr AP, Qazi Y, Roberts MB, Russell B, Sampson MG, Shah S, Thomas CP, Vena N, Wallace E, Weinstock BA, Gharavi AG, Wang X.

journal.title: Clinical journal of the American Society of Nephrology : CJASN

abstractText: Genetic testing and genomics are now essential components of precision kidney care, with the potential to inform diagnosis, management, family planning, and transplant decisions. Expansion of genetic testing is increasingly feasible with continuing improvements in diagnostic yield and variant interpretation as well as declining costs. The Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) Genetics in Kidney Health Summit convened experts in nephrology, genetics, genetic counseling, and related disciplines, together with patients and caregivers, to identify strategies for incorporating genetic testing more fully into kidney care in the United States. Patients and caregivers described genetic testing as a possible means of obtaining clarity about the cause of disease, even when treatment options are limited, and of informing reproductive decisions and cascade testing in at-risk relatives. Reflecting these perspectives, summit participants discussed a shift from criteria-based selection toward a more inclusive testing strategy, reframing the question "who should be tested?" to "who should not be tested?" To avoid exclusion of patients who could benefit from genetic testing, testing strategies should be broad and inclusive, potentially approaching universal testing within key clinical contexts, such as early-onset disease, atypical clinical features, family history of CKD, CKD of unexplained cause, or the presence of extrarenal manifestations. To address the current shortage of experts in nephrogenetics and genetic counselors, collaboration of major American nephrology and genetics organizations is needed to enhance kidney genetics training for both trainees and practicing clinicians. Centers of excellence, which at minimum should include a nephrologist with demonstrated expertise in genetic kidney diseases, at least one genetic counselor, and access to accredited laboratories and bioinformatics, can provide guidance to community nephrologists through telemedicine, virtual case discussions, and shared protocols.

title: Effects of switching from conventional renin-angiotensin system inhibitors to angiotensin receptor neprilysin inhibitor on renal function in patients with chronic kidney disease: a retrospective exploratory analysis.
authorString: Suehiro Y, Kidoguchi S, Nakashima D, Maruyama Y, Yokoo T.
abstractText:
Background

Angiotensin receptor neprilysin inhibitor (ARNI) is widely used in the management of heart failure and provides well-established clinical benefits. However, its effects on renal function in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) remain unclear.

Methods

This study included 107 patients with CKD who were switched from renin-angiotensin system (RAS) inhibitors to an ARNI. Annualized changes in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) over approximately 6 months before and 12 months after switching to an ARNI (ΔeGFR), as well as changes in urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio (UPCR) and blood pressure, were evaluated.

Results

ARNI treatment was not associated with significant changes in ΔeGFR or UPCR (ΔeGFR: - 3.7 ± 10.4 mL/min/1.73 m2/year vs. - 1.1 ± 5.3 mL/min/1.73 m2/year, P = 0.07; UPCR: 0.70 g/gCr [0.17-1.73] vs. 0.41 g/gCr [0.18-1.62], P = 0.11). In contrast, both systolic and diastolic blood pressures decreased significantly following the switch to an ARNI. The effects on eGFR and systolic blood pressure were consistent regardless of baseline renal function, degree of proteinuria, or underlying kidney disease.

Conclusions

In this study, neither ΔeGFR nor proteinuria changed significantly over the 12-month follow-up period following the switch from RAS inhibitors to an ARNI. In contrast, substantial reductions in blood pressure were observed across different levels of baseline renal function. However, the small sample size may have limited the statistical power to detect significant effects of ARNI on renal function, raising the possibility of a type II error. Further studies with larger sample sizes are warranted.

title: Determinants of patients' trust in their usual nephrologists during renal replacement therapy selection: a nationwide multicenter cross-sectional study in Japan.
authorString: Kei N, Ryohei I, Hiroo K, Tatsunori T, Tadashi S, Yugo S, Noriaki K.
abstractText:
Background

Patient trust in physicians is an essential component of treatment decision-making. However, factors associated with trust and its impact on renal replacement therapy (RRT) modality selection remain unclear. We examined the determinants of patients' trust in their usual nephrologist and its association with dialysis modality selection in Japan.

Methods

We conducted a cross-sectional study of patients requiring RRT (n = 429). Trust was assessed using the Wake Forest Physician Trust Scale (WFPTS). Multivariable linear regression analysis was performed to identify factors associated with trust. The association between trust and selection of peritoneal dialysis (PD) versus hemodialysis (HD) was evaluated using multivariable logistic regression analysis.

Results

Repeated RRT outpatient visits were significantly associated with higher trust scores (standardized β = 0.108). However, this association was attenuated after adjustment for follow-up duration, suggesting that longitudinal continuity of care may underlie the observed relationship. WFPTS scores did not differ significantly between the PD and HD groups (p = 0.200), and trust was not independently associated with PD selection (odds ratio, 1.004; 95% confidence interval, 0.988-1.021).

Conclusions

Patients' trust in their usual nephrologist was associated with repeated clinical encounters and may be primarily shaped by continuity and duration of care. However, trust was not independently associated with dialysis modality selection, suggesting that clinical and social factors may play a more prominent role in decision-making. Alternatively, trust may facilitate a patient-centered decision-making process in which either modality is selected according to individual preferences.

title: Changes in muscle sympathetic nerve activity following SGLT-2 inhibitor initiation in patients with chronic heart failure.
authorString: Nelles D, Nagel L, Weber M, Vogelhuber J, Zimmer S, Nickenig G, Becher MU, Öztürk C.

journal.title: Clinical research in cardiology : official journal of the German Cardiac Society

abstractText:
Background

Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT-2) inhibitors improve outcomes in heart failure (HF), but their effects on sympathetic nervous system activity in humans remain incompletely characterized. We investigated longitudinal changes in directly measured muscle sympathetic nerve activity (MSNA) after SGLT-2 inhibitor initiation in patients with chronic HF.

Methods

In this prospective, single-arm longitudinal study, 70 patients with stable chronic HF across the spectrum of left ventricular ejection fraction underwent baseline assessment including microneurography, echocardiography, laboratory testing, NYHA assessment, and Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire (KCCQ) evaluation. Follow-up assessments were available in variable numbers depending on the respective parameter; paired MSNA measurements were available in 45 patients. Mean follow-up was 8.2 ± 6.3 months. MSNA was quantified using event-count measures expressed as events per minute and events per 100 heartbeats.

Results

Paired MSNA measurements were available in 45 patients. Median MSNA event count per minute decreased from 107.6 [68.6-126.5] to 64.5 [44.5-76.2] events/min (Hodges-Lehmann change - 34.80, 95% CI - 44.04 to - 26.59; p < 0.001), and MSNA event count per 100 heartbeats decreased from 75.8 [53.4-97.8] to 46.2 [31.6-62.6] events/100 heartbeats (change - 27.63, 95% CI - 33.30 to - 21.91; p < 0.001). LVEF increased by 6.03 percentage points (p < 0.001), NT-proBNP decreased (p = 0.001), NYHA class improved (p < 0.001), and KCCQ Overall Summary Score increased by 19.76 points (p < 0.001). Changes in MSNA were not significantly associated with changes in LVEF, NT-proBNP, NYHA class, or KCCQ score.

Conclusion

SGLT-2 inhibitor initiation in chronic HF was followed by a marked reduction in directly measured MSNA and concurrent improvement in cardiac and clinical parameters. Controlled mechanistic studies are required to determine whether these changes are directly attributable to SGLT-2 inhibition.

title: Pumpless extracorporeal lung assist device in the management of idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension - implantation, weaning and explantation in a bridge-to-decision concept.
authorString: Kari FA, Hörer J, Schneider C, Haas N, Pattathu J, Maskos A, Michel SG.

journal.title: Multimedia manual of cardiothoracic surgery : MMCTS

abstractText: Via a primary sternotomy approach, cardiopulmonary bypass is established in a standard fashion including a separate vent in the main pulmonary artery. The outlet cannula, an angled Berlin Heart EXCOR cannula, is implanted into the body of the small, underfilled, left atrium using felt-supported single sutures. The inlet cannula, a 12 mm Berlin Heart graft adapter cannula connected to a 12 mm Terumo prosthesis and draining deoxygenated blood from the main pulmonary artery, is tunnelled through the epigastric skin and subsequently anastomosed with the main pulmonary artery. A low-resistance oxygenator (QUADROX, Maquet) is used for paracorporeal lung assist.

title: Efficacy of an automated vestibular function diagnosis and treatment system combined with habituation training in refractory benign paroxysmal positional vertigo.
authorString: Li Y, Liu H, Gao Y, Jia W.
abstractText:
Objective

To evaluate an automated vestibular function diagnosis and treatment system (SRM-IV system) combined with habituation training in patients with refractory benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV).

Methods

Clinical data were collected from 81 patients with refractory BPPV from December, 2023 to December, 2024. Thirty-eight received SRM-IV repositioning plus habituation training (intervention), and 43 received SRM-IV alone (control). Training was remotely supervised for three months. Follow-up was at six months.

Results

Residual vertigo duration was shorter in the intervention group (6.7 ± 1.4 vs. 8.9 ± 1.6 days, p < 0.001), and the Dizziness Handicap Inventory score reduction was greater (54.5 ± 12.0 vs. 42.7 ± 11.6, p < 0.001); both were confirmed after adjustment for baseline scores (analysis of covariance, p < 0.001). Recurrence did not differ significantly between groups (28.9% vs. 34.9%, p = 0.64). Hypertension independently predicted recurrence (OR 3.65, 95% CI 1.21 to 11.05, p = 0.022). After excluding hypertensive patients, recurrence was lower in the intervention group (10.7% vs. 33.3%, p = 0.04).

Conclusion

Combined habituation training shortened residual vertigo and improved dizziness-related disability in refractory BPPV. The recurrence benefit became evident after excluding patients with hypertension. Blood pressure control may warrant attention in this population.

title: Caught in the Autoimmune Crossfire.
authorString: Varda A, Fernando S, Boyle T.
abstractText:
Introduction

Drug-induced lupus and vasculitis may occur independently or as overlapping syndromes, with numerous implicated drugs. Anti-histone antibodies assist in differentiating these entities from their idiopathic counterparts (1). We present a case of a man in his 80s with drug-induced lupus and vasculitis, complicated by treatment-resistant hypertension and thrombocytopenia.

Method

Case presentation featuring clinical progress, investigations, and targeted literature review.

Results

The patient presented with progressive breathlessness, pleuritic chest pain, and fevers without an identifiable infective focus. CT chest revealed bilateral lower lobe ground-glass changes and pleural effusions. He subsequently developed lower limb purpura and bicytopenia (Hb 81 g/L, platelets 109 × 109/L). C-reactive protein (CRP) was 146 mg/L. Acute renal impairment was also evident with Cr 209 uM and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) 25 mL/min/1.73 m2, alongside microscopic haematuria (<20% dysmorphic red cells) and proteinuria. Serology showed >1:160 perinuclear anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies (pANCA) with anti-myeloperoxidase (MPO) and anti-PR3 antibody levels of >222 IU/L and 20 IU/L, respectively. A 1:2,560 homogeneous ANA was detected with elevated anti-double-stranded DNA (108 IU/mL) and anti-histone (9.7 U) antibodies, along with a low C4 0.13 g/L level. Serology was negative for anti-phospholipid and anti-glomerular basement membrane (GBM) antibodies. Cryoglobulins were absent. Renal biopsy showed pauci-immune glomerulonephritis with secondary tubular and interstitial damage. A fluorodeoxyglucose-positron emission tomography (FDG-PET) scan excluded large-vessel vasculitis and malignancy. A novel finding of myocarditis was identified on echocardiogram and confirmed on cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). The most likely culprit, hydralazine, was ceased. Modifications were made to his antihypertensive regimen, with a decision to continue methyldopa, although blood pressure control remained suboptimal. He was pulsed with intravenous methylprednisolone followed by a tapering course of prednisolone and induction doses of rituximab. Disease activity markers, including anti-histone antibody levels, improved, and he remains in remission on maintenance rituximab.

Conclusion

This case highlights overlapping hydralazine-induced lupus and ANCA-associated vasculitis. Anti-histone antibody levels were a useful adjunct to monitor disease activity and exclude methyldopa as the primary inciting agent. Treatment with rituximab was shown to be effective.

title: Self-reported sleep problems and associated factors among older adults in Malaysia: An ethnic subgroup analysis.
authorString: Cheah YK, Johar H, Su TT.

journal.title: Cranio : the journal of craniomandibular practice

abstractText:
Objective

This study examines factors associated with self-reported sleep problems within a large sample of older Malaysian adults from diverse ethnic groups.

Methods

Cross-sectional data from the South East Asia Community Observatory Health Survey 2018 and ordered probit models were used for analysis.

Results

Malay females were more likely to report mild-to-severe sleep problems than males. Malays and Chinese who were older were more likely to report mild-to-severe sleep problems compared to younger ones. Among Malays, smoking was associated with the likelihood of reporting mild-to-severe sleep problems. Higher income, physically active and obese older Chinese adults were less likely to report sleep problems than others. Being diagnosed with hypertension among Chinese and diabetes among Indians was associated with a higher probability of reporting mild-to-severe sleep problems.

Conclusion

Sociodemographic characteristics, lifestyles and health profiles are key factors associated with self-reported sleep problems among various ethnic groups of Malaysian older adults.

title: Living with chronic heart failure in a digital era: Exploring patients' lived experiences of telemedicine and self-management.
authorString: Juul NK, Sorknæs AD, Rothmann MJ, Auscher S, Egstrup K.
abstractText: IntroductionChronic heart failure (CHF) affects patients' emotional, physical and social lives.
