As healthcare systems face rising demand and workforce shortages, telemedicine has become increasingly important as a way to support person-centred care. This study explored lived experiences of patients with heart failure and how they perceive and integrate telemedicine into everyday life.MethodsA qualitative study was conducted using semistructured interviews with 15 patients receiving outpatient CHF care in Denmark between December 2022 and May 2023. A phenomenological-hermeneutic approach guided the study, and data were analysed using Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis to capture how participants made sense of living with heart failure and engaging with telemedicine.ResultsFour themes were identified: (1) the emotional impact of receiving the diagnosis, (2) navigating everyday life with CHF, (3) adjusting future expectations and (4) integrating technology into the treatment experience. Telemedicine enhanced participants' sense of control, safety, flexibility and continuity of care. However, challenges emerged related to emotional communication, self-assessment tasks and limited digital literacy, particularly among those in vulnerable positions.DiscussionTelemedicine supported involvement and self-management, but its benefits were shaped by individual circumstances, digital skills and the extent to which emotional, relational and clinical needs could be addressed digitally. To ensure equitable access and effective engagement, telemedicine must be tailored to patients' needs. These findings highlight that telemedicine can improve continuity but may widen inequities if digital competencies are not addressed and can guide healthcare professionals and policymakers in designing accessible, person-centred telemedicine solutions.

title: AI-derived retinal vascular metrics and MoCA-B-defined mild cognitive impairment in type 2 diabetes: a community-based cross-sectional study.
authorString: Sun R, Ying H, Zhao S, Wang J, Xu L, Jiang S, Luo Y, Yan C, Ran M, Yang K, Hu Y.
abstractText:
Background

Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a major risk factor for mild cognitive impairment (MCI). As an embryological extension of the brain, the retina offers a unique window into cerebral microvascular health; artificial intelligence (AI) now enables objective, large-scale quantification of retinal vascular parameters to investigate this association.

Objective

To quantify retinal vascular metrics using AI in community-managed T2DM patients and examine their association with MCI.

Methods

This cross-sectional study enrolled T2DM patients from four community health centers in Guiyang, China. Fundus photographs were analyzed using an AI platform with established performance in previous studies to derive vascular density (VD), fractal dimension (FD), and other metrics. Cognitive function was assessed using the basic version of the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA-B), with MCI status determined by MoCA-B cut-offs. Separate logistic regression models were constructed for each retinal indicator as the sole exposure variable, with identical DAG-derived covariate sets introduced sequentially. Stratified and sensitivity analyses assessed robustness.

Results

Among 630 community‑dwelling patients with T2DM, the prevalence of MCI was 33.2% (n = 209). Multivariable logistic regression models adjusted for age, BMI, educational level, hypertension, and HbA1c showed that VD (per 1% increment: OR = 0.987, 95% CI 0.979, 0.995), FD (per 0.1 increment: OR = 0.221, 95% CI 0.050, 0.982), and fractal dimension of the vessel centerline (FDVC, per 0.1 increment: OR = 0.359, 95% CI 0.131, 0.983) were nominally associated with lower odds of MCI in exploratory analyses. Stratified analyses indicated consistent directions of these associations across subgroups defined by age and diabetes duration. Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of the associations for VD and FDVC.

Conclusion

VD, FD, and FDVC were nominally associated with MoCA‑B‑defined MCI in community‑dwelling patients with T2DM in exploratory analyses, suggesting that these measures may serve as candidate imaging correlates of microvascular alterations underlying MCI.

title: Plasma electrolyte changes can modulate post-repolarisation refractoriness in the human atrium
authorString: Corrado C, Roney CH, Narayan SM, Giles WR, Niederer SA.
abstractText: Changes in plasma Na+, K+ and Ca2+ levels are common in patients with chronic kidney disease or gastrointestinal disorders, or in those taking certain medications, and may promote atrial fibrillation or impair drug-induced cardioversion. Post-repolarisation refractoriness (PRR) is an established mechanism by which antiarrhythmic drugs suppress tachyarrhythmias. We investigated how changes in extracellular Na+, K+ and Ca2+ concentrations ([Na+]o, [K+]o, [Ca2+]o) modulate ionic currents and PRR in healthy and fibrotic human atrial tissue. We used a multi-scale computational framework comprising an isolated atrial myocyte, a one-dimensional atrial tissue strand, and a virtual cohort of 14 left atrial digital twins, combined with Gaussian process emulators and variance-based global sensitivity analysis. Changes in [K+]o strongly modulated PRR by altering the inward rectifier K+ current (IK1), shifting the resting potential and thereby regulating Na+-current availability. In contrast, [Na+]o had only a weak effect on PRR, mediated primarily through the Na+/Ca2+ exchanger, and [Ca2+]o had a negligible effect. Tissue PRR was more sensitive to electrolyte changes than myocyte PRR, reflecting electrolyte-dependent alterations in the safety factor for action potential propagation. Changes in [K+]o also substantially affected arrhythmia vulnerability, increasing inducibility and prolonging rhythm disturbances. We conclude that extracellular K+ is the principal plasma electrolyte determinant of atrial PRR and arrhythmia burden, acting primarily through IK1. Monitoring and maintaining serum K+ within the normal range may be important for managing atrial arrhythmia risk.

title: Clinical review before execution of executable guideline encodings: a prospective registered study of three ocular hypertension guidelines
authorString: Ragosta A, Bruni F.
abstractText:
Objective:

To determine whether executable encodings of three ocular hypertension guidelines, produced under a prospectively frozen pipeline barring author-defined operationalisations, are judged faithful by independent clinical review before execution, and to characterise findings on retained content, exclusions and divisions.

Methods:

Under a registered protocol, one ophthalmologist encoded European Glaucoma Society (EGS), American Academy of Ophthalmology (AAO) and National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) guidelines; a second encoded a sample. A gate barred author-defined operationalisations. Before execution, two other ophthalmologists reviewed branches, exclusions and division records against predefined materiality criteria.

Results:

The gate admitted 0, 2 and 1 branches (EGS, AAO, NICE) from 748, 322 and 198 eligible units. Review of these branches raised no primary finding (AAO 0/2, NICE 0/1); at these denominators, uninformative. In the overlap, one NICE omission (laser trabeculoplasty) was judged material. The exclusion reviewer flagged material source-stated decision content in 601/2,109, 216/234 and 151/179 excluded passages. A masked post-hoc reader agreed with 31/50, 11/50 and 28/50 sampled flags; he judged 1/246 passages directly relevant to the initial treat-or-observe decision and 0/100, 0/68 and 8/78 needed to preserve a retained unit's meaning. No synthetic case resolved to observation.

Conclusion:

Without author-defined choices, few branches were instantiable and none resolved to observation. Fidelity was not determinable at these denominators; exclusion flags were reader-dependent, and some NICE exclusions may have carried meaning needed by retained units. Exclusion review shows what a scope restriction sets aside; its reproducibility must be established before it measures fidelity.

title: Classifying chronic kidney disease from non-invasive questionnaire features in adults with long-standing diabetes in Bangladesh: model development, internal validation and the limits of small-sample evidence
authorString: Anan A, Arshi UT, Islam RN.
abstractText:
Background:

Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a common complication of diabetes, and in Bangladesh laboratory testing for it is not always available. Questionnaire answers could help decide whom to test first, but small machine-learning studies often report optimistic accuracy. Methods We analysed a public dataset of 400 adults with at least 10 years of diabetes attending a tertiary hospital in Dhaka, 185 with a hospital diagnosis of CKD. A pre-specified ridge logistic regression using 20 non-invasive features was developed and internally validated with nested cross-validation (five folds, ten repeats), compared with lasso, random forest and gradient boosting, and assessed for discrimination, calibration and net benefit. Simulations examined case-enriched sampling and single train/test splits. Results The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was 0.75 (95% confidence interval 0.70–0.80; optimism-corrected 0.76). Flexible algorithms were not detectably better (differences −0.005 to +0.006). Calibration within the sample was good (slope 1.06, 0.79–1.33), and testing the highest-scoring 30% of patients would have found 48% of CKD cases. The sample was smaller than the 883 patients recommended. Urinary infection, body-mass index, insulin use, diabetes duration and pain-killer use were positively associated with CKD and diet adherence negatively; regular walking and hypertension showed directions opposite to clinical expectation, consistent with features recorded after diagnosis. The yearly history added no reliable information. In simulation, case-enriched sampling preserved the AUC but overstated absolute risk (mean predicted risk 0.37 at a true prevalence of 0.10). Over 300 random 80/20 splits of the same data, the test AUC ranged from 0.61 to 0.87; reporting the best of ten splits would overstate it by about 0.07. Conclusions Questionnaire features moderately distinguished patients with an existing CKD diagnosis. Whether they identify patients before diagnosis requires external validation in patients assessed before CKD status is known. The study was not registered.

title: Some Benefit More, Some Benefit Less: Trends in Smoking and Quitting by Sex, Race, Ethnicity, and Poverty Level Among California Adults With a History of Hypertension
authorString: Assari S, Najand B.
abstractText: Objective. To examine how current cigarette smoking and the percentage of ever smokers who had quit changed from 2019 to 2024 among California adults with a history of hypertension. Methods. We analyzed annual weighted California Health Interview Survey estimates for 2019–2024. We compared Latino and non-Latino Black adults separately with non-Latino White adults, compared adults at or below 200% of the federal poverty level (FPL) with those above it, and examined trends among female adults. We examined current smoking among all adults with a history of hypertension and the percentage who had quit among ever smokers. Results. Among adults with a history of hypertension, current smoking fell from 9.3% to 5.8% among non-Latino White adults, rose from 4.7% to 6.4% among Latino adults, and fell from 9.3% to 8.7% among non-Latino Black adults. Among ever smokers, the percentage who had quit rose from 80.9% to 86.5% among non-Latino White adults. It fell from 82.3% to 76.0% among Latino adults and from 74.2% to 72.0% among non-Latino Black adults. Current smoking fell from 9.9% to 8.9% at or below 200% FPL and rose from 5.4% to 5.6% above 200% FPL. Among female adults, current smoking fell from 7.1% to 5.2%, and the percentage who had quit rose from 78.6% to 80.7%. Conclusions. Among California adults with a history of hypertension who had ever smoked, the percentage who had quit rose among non-Latino White adults and fell among Latino and non-Latino Black adults. Current smoking prevalence fell in the lower-income group and rose slightly in the higher-income group. The quit ratio declined less in the lower-income group. Among female adults, current smoking fell and the quit ratio rose. Direct male estimates were unavailable, so sex differences could not be tested.

title: The Interaction Effect Between Antihypertensive Medication and Depressive Symptoms on Uncontrolled Hypertension Using Regression Survey Analysis and Random Forest Tree Approach
authorString: Tang S, Khamidov S, Zheng L.
abstractText: 1 in 5 individuals with hypertension have their blood pressure uncontrolled, and 70 percent of those failed to control their blood pressure using medications. Depression has shown to be a potential risk factor for uncontrolled hypertension investigating the moderator effect of antihypertensive use on the association between depression and uncontrolled hypertension may guide blood pressure control. A total of 39,467 individuals from NHANES data were used to investigate this association through multivariable logistic regression and Random Forest models. Adjusted logistic regression model showed that among individuals who used antihypertensive medication, depression score was associated with an increase in 0.04 odds (95% CI: 0.02, 0.06) of having uncontrolled hypertension. The GLM and Random Forest models exhibited high sensitivity (>98%) but low specificity (~9%), indicating strong detection of uncontrolled hypertension but poor differentiation of negative cases. Logistic regression had a slightly higher AUC (0.79) than RF (0.78), suggesting better discriminative ability. Future studies should investigate bias and other mapping areas.

title: SpecMFM-Net: A Spectrogram-Enhanced Multi-Scale Feature Modulation Network with Medical-Prior-Guided Transfer Learning for Atrial Fibrillation Detection
authorString: Sun Y, Yan Q, Tang H, Wu Y, Fu R, Cui H, Wu X, Xie L.
abstractText: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is a prevalent cardiac arrhythmia whose timely detection is critical for improving patient outcomes. Deep learning has achieved remarkable success in data-rich image, video, and text tasks and has also been widely applied to ECG-based AF detection. However, ECG analysis is often constrained by limited high-quality annotations because rhythm-level labeling requires expert interpretation and substantial time cost. Models trained under such annotation-limited conditions are prone to overfitting, resulting in restricted detection performance and weak generalization in practical scenarios. To address this issue, this paper proposes a spectrogram-enhanced multi-scale feature modulation network (SpecMFM-Net) with medical-prior-guided transfer learning for AF detection. Raw ECG signals are first converted into super-resolution spectrograms using the fractional adaptive superlet transform (FASLT), which adaptively balances time-frequency resolution and better captures rhythm evolution and transient AF-related patterns. SpecMFM-Net is then pretrained on a source dataset to acquire domain-relevant medical priors and then fine-tuned on the target data. It further integrates multi-scale feature modulation and BiLSTM temporal modeling to enhance discriminative temporal-spectral representations for AF classification. The SpecMFM-Net achieved an average macro F1 score of 90.04% in 5-fold cross-validation on CinC2017 dataset and 91.54% in cross-dataset testing on AFDB dataset, demonstrating promising precision and generalization for AF detection under limited high-quality annotations.

title: Amiodarone-associated torsades de pointes after catheter ablation for atrial flutter and atrial fibrillation: a case report and literature review
authorString: Zhang¹ L, Xiao¹ J, Cai¹ G, Gu J.
abstractText: Background Amiodarone, a class III antiarrhythmic agent, is widely prescribed for its proven antiarrhythmic efficacy, yet it carries risks of multiorgan toxicities involving the heart, thyroid gland, lung, liver, and ocular structures. Although amiodarone-related torsades de pointes (TdP) is uncommon, this life-threatening arrhythmia may lead to syncope and even cardiac arrest. Case Presentation We describe the clinical course of a 76-year-old female patient with a dual-chamber pacemaker who was admitted due to chest tightness and palpitations. Coronary angiography ruled out significant coronary artery disease. The patient underwent radiofrequency catheter ablation for atrial flutter and atrial fibrillation. Intravenous amiodarone was initiated about 1 hour after the procedure, followed by oral maintenance therapy. The first clinical event (syncope) occurred approximately 36 hours after the ablation, and the first TdP confirmed by Holter monitoring occurred approximately 51 hours after the ablation. ‌Electrocardiograms (ECG) revealed a prolonged QT interval. QTc interval was 446 ms (baseline) → 490 ms (immediately post-albation, pre-amiodarone) → 528 ms (near TdP onset). Pacemaker interrogation documented the arrhythmia episodes. Complete clinical recovery was attained following the cessation of amiodarone administration and intravenous replenishment of potassium and magnesium. Conclusion Measurable QTc lengthening occurred shortly after ablation before amiodarone was started. This case underscores the critical need for close surveillance of the QTc interval when amiodarone is administered during the early post-ablation period.

title: Intensive hydration protocols and heart failure-compatible signs and/or symptoms in cisplatin-treated cancer patients: a prospective observational cohort study.
authorString: Martinez-Callejo V, Llado-Jordan G, Rodriguez-Borregan JC, Peinado II, Escudero-Vilaplana V, Rivera-Herrero F, Ochagavía-Sufrategui M, Valencia-Soto CM, Barbadillo-Villanueva S, Rioja-Carrera M, Fernández-Cueto AG, Villacañas-Palomares MV, Abad NA, Gomez-Mediavilla B.
abstractText: Introduction: Cisplatin-based chemotherapy requires intensive hydration protocols to prevent nephrotoxicity, involving rapid administration of large fluid volumes. The potential cardiovascular impact of hydration-associated fluid overload remains poorly characterized. This study aimed to determine the proportion of patients presenting signs and/or symptoms compatible with heart failure following these protocols and to explore associated factors. Methods A prospective, observational, single-center cohort study was conducted between January and December 2021 at Hospital Universitario Marqués de Valdecilla, Spain. Adult patients with solid tumors receiving cisplatin-based chemotherapy with intensive hydration were consecutively enrolled. The primary outcome - occurrence of at least one sign and/or symptom compatible with heart failure - was assessed through electronic health record review and a structured questionnaire. Exploratory multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify associated factors. Results Twenty-nine of 120 patients (24.17%) presented at least one sign and/or symptom compatible with heart failure, most frequently palpitations (10.00%), dyspnea (9.17%) and edema (9.17%). In the multivariable logistic regression model, age ≥ 70 years (adjusted OR 2.93; 95%CI 1.13–7.61; p = 0.027) and administered volume per 500 ml increment (adjusted OR 2.96; 95%CI 1.06–8.27; p = 0.038) showed statistically significant associations with the outcome. Prior ischemic heart disease showed an elevated but non-significant estimate (adjusted OR 3.90; p = 0.075). Conclusion Age ≥ 70 years and administered volume showed statistically significant associations with the main outcome. Findings are hypothesis-generating and do not establish a causal relationship between hydration and the observed manifestations. Larger prospective studies with objective cardiovascular assessment are needed to confirm these findings and to evaluate individualized hydration strategies.

title: Association of the Triglyceride-glucose Index and Remnant Cholesterol with Retinopathy among Community- dwelling Older Adults in China
authorString: Yang J, Li Y, Zhang J, Han X.
abstractText: Background and Purpose: The increasing burden of microvascular eye diseases due to aging and metabolic diseases is a significant concern. However, evidence of the independent association between the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index and remnant cholesterol (RC) and retinal arteriosclerosis in older adults remains limited. This study aimed to analyze the prevalence of retinal arteriosclerosis among community-dwelling older adults and explore the correlation and predictive value of these indicators for retinal artery stenosis. Methods: A cross-sectional study design was used. From March to October 2025, older adults aged ≥ 65 years from seven communities on a street within the Suzhou High-tech Zone were selected as study participants. Data were collected through questionnaire surveys, biochemical lipid testing, and Keith–Wagener–Barker fundus grading examinations to analyze the association between the relevant indicators and retinal artery stenosis. Results: A total of 990 elderly individuals were included in this study. Fundus grading results indicated that 39 cases (3.9%) were normal, 440 cases (44.4%) were classified as grade I, 439 cases (44.3%) were classified as grade II, 66 cases (6.7%) were classified as grade III, and 6 cases (0.6%) were classified as grade IV. Participants were categorized into groups based on the presence or absence of retinal artery stenosis. The two groups exhibited statistically significant differences in gender, body mass index, smoking history, hypertension, diabetes, TyG index, and RC levels (all P < 0.05). Spearman's rank correlation analysis revealed a positive correlation between TyG index and RC with the grade of fundus lesions (r = 0.190, P < 0.001; r = 0.169, P < 0.001). Multivariable logistic regression revealed that gender (odds ratio [OR] = 0.709), body mass index (BMI) (OR = 1.058), and diabetes (OR = 1.555) were independent risk factors for retinal arteriolar stenosis (all P < 0.05). After further adjustment for TyG index and RC, both markers revealed significantly elevated risks in the highest tertile (TyG Q3: OR = 2.012; RC Q3: OR = 2.036, both P < 0.001), with RC Q2 also demonstrating a significant increase (OR = 1.614, P = 0.002), and both exhibited significant linear trends across tertiles ( P for trend < 0.001). Notably, the effects of gender, BMI, and diabetes were partially attenuated and became non-significant after adjustment (all P > 0.05). The area under the curves (AUCs) of TyG index and RC for predicting retinal arteriolar stenosis were 0.613 and 0.604, respectively. Conclusion: The prevalence of retinal arteriosclerosis in this community-based elderly population is notably high. TyG index and RC have been identified as independent risk factors for retinal arteriolar stenosis, exhibiting significant dose-response relationships ( P for trend < 0.001). However, their predictive performance as standalone markers is limited (AUC = 0.60), suggesting that they may function more effectively as complementary metrics alongside conventional risk factors rather than as independent diagnostic tools.

title: Predicting Acute Pyelonephritis With Clinical and Ultrasound Findings: Development of the Pyelo Prediction Score
authorString: Boccatonda A, Brighenti A, Tiraferri V, Natale FD, Agostinelli D, Masi L, Venturoli N, Gessaroli E, Comai G, Serra C.
abstractText: Background Diagnostic uncertainty frequently complicates the assessment of suspected acute pyelonephritis (APN). We aimed to develop a bedside score combining clinical characteristics and B-mode ultrasound findings to support diagnostic stratification before contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS). Methods This prospective, single-center observational study included consecutive episodes referred to a tertiary-care ultrasound service for suspected APN. All underwent B-mode ultrasound and CEUS. The reference outcome was the final discharge diagnosis, incorporating clinical, laboratory, microbiological, and imaging findings. A seven-predictor logistic regression model was obtained. Coefficients were converted into integer points. Discrimination and threshold-specific performance were evaluated, with exploratory analysis by renal transplant status. Results Among 329 episodes, 80 (24.3%) were classified as APN. The score included cortical hypo- and hyperechogenicity, globular renal morphology, flank pain, immunosuppression, renal calculi, and arterial hypertension, with a theoretical range of − 2 to 20 points. Area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve was 0.789. At ≥ 4 points, sensitivity was 51.3% and specificity 90.0%. At ≥ 1 point, sensitivity was 90.0% and negative predictive value 91.7%; eight APN episodes remained below threshold. At ≥ 7 points, specificity was 99.2% and positive predictive value 91.7%. Apparent discrimination was 0.813 in transplant recipients and 0.784 in non-transplant patients. Conclusions The Pyelo Prediction Score showed promising discrimination in a specialist referral cohort, but low scores did not reliably exclude APN. External validation is required before using the score to guide contrast-imaging decisions.

title: SGLT2 inhibitor prescribing among adults with type 2 diabetes and cardiorenal disease in a retrospective cross-sectional electronic health record study
authorString: Özturan¹ A, Şanibaş² AV, Demir² AK.
abstractText: Background Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors provide cardiorenal benefits, but their use in routine diabetes care varies. We quantified documented prescribing among adults with type 2 diabetes, recorded cardiorenal disease, and examined associated factors. Methods We conducted a single-center retrospective cross-sectional electronic health record study of 7266 adults attending general internal medicine in Türkiye in 2025. A prespecified potential eligibility phenotype comprised recorded kidney disease, heart failure and/or atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease with estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) ≥ 20 mL/min/1.73 m². We summarized prescribing proportions with Wilson 95% confidence intervals (CIs); we used chi-square tests for group comparisons, and we examined associated factors using logistic regression. Results Phenotype status was indeterminate in 1419 participants, and 81 assessable participants had eGFR < 20 mL/min/1.73 m². Among 5766 participants in the primary analysis, 2436 (42%) met the phenotype; 296 had documented SGLT2 inhibitor prescribing (12%; 95% CI 11–14). Prescribing was more frequent among participants meeting the phenotype than among those not meeting it (12% vs 8.6%; odds ratio 1.47, 95% CI 1.24–1.75; P < 0.001), although the association was weak (phi = 0.058). Prescribing did not differ significantly across seven cardiorenal subgroups (P = 0.627). Documented metformin and insulin use were associated with prescribing in the complete-case multivariable model (n = 2113). Conclusions Documented SGLT2 inhibitor prescribing was recorded in 12% of adults meeting the prespecified phenotype. Electronic case-finding may support targeted medication review, but incomplete prescription capture and unmeasured contraindications limit assessment of individual treatment appropriateness.

title: Clinical characteristics and factors associated with insulin resistance in children with primary hypertension: a retrospective study
authorString: Li Y, Lin Y, Li Y, Wu C, Lin T, Jiang H, Shi L.
abstractText: Objectives To investigate the clinical characteristics and factors associated with insulin resistance (IR) in children with primary hypertension. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 612 children aged 10–17 years who were newly diagnosed with primary hypertension at the Capital Center for Children’s Health, Capital Medical University. Based on the homeostatic model assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR), participants were classified into the non-IR group (n = 143) and the IR group (n = 469), and their clinical data were compared. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify factors independently associated with IR. A nomogram was developed based on the final multivariable model and internally validated using 1000 bootstrap resamples. Multivariable linear regression with log-transformed HOMA-IR was performed as a sensitivity analysis. Results IR was identified in 469 of 612 children (76.6%). Compared with the non-IR group, the IR group had higher BMI, a higher prevalence of obesity and stage 2 hypertension, higher levels of fasting blood glucose, fasting insulin, uric acid, total cholesterol, triglycerides, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, and non-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, a higher 24-h systolic blood pressure index, and a higher prevalence of cardiac damage. However, age and levels of high-density lipoprotein cholesterol and homocysteine were lower in the IR group (all p  < 0.05). Multivariable logistic regression showed that younger age (OR = 0.74, 95% CI: 0.64 to 0.86), obesity (OR = 6.08, 95% CI: 3.64 to 10.13), and higher triglyceride levels (OR = 2.62, 95% CI: 1.47 to 4.67) were independently associated with IR in children with primary hypertension (all p  < 0.05). The nomogram showed good discrimination (AUC = 0.829, 95% CI: 0.789–0.869), with a bias-corrected C-index of 0.823 after bootstrap validation. Calibration curves and decision curve analysis (DCA) indicated good calibration and potential clinical net benefit. The sensitivity analysis yielded consistent results. Conclusions IR was common among children aged 10–17 years with primary hypertension. Younger age, obesity, and higher triglyceride levels were independently associated with IR. The nomogram may help identify children with primary hypertension who are at high risk for IR, providing a convenient tool for clinical screening.

title: Retinal Arteriolar Vessel Density and Thalamic T2 Hyperintensity in Arterial Hypertension: An Oculomics Study Using Automated Fundus Image Analysis
authorString: Geis C, Germán-Salló M, Baróti B, Pál T, Preg Z, Nemes-Nagy E, Haba H, Csincsik L, Tripon RG.
abstractText: We retrospectively examined whether automatically derived retinal vascular parameters are associated with the extent of thalamic T2 hyperintensity on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) in hypertensive patients. In 42 consecutively enrolled hypertensive patients who underwent 1.5 T MRI and colour fundus photography within seven days, the thalamic T2-hyperintense area fraction (T2HAF) was quantified on three axial T2-weighted slices with ImageJ, using a fixed threshold, by a radiologist blinded to the retinal data. Fundus photographs were analysed with AutoMorph. Associations between T2HAF and 11 retinal vascular parameters were assessed with generalised estimating equations (GEE) clustered by patient and adjusted for age and sex; multiplicity was controlled with the Benjamini–Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR). Of 84 photographs, 44 (28 patients) were gradable. Higher T2HAF was associated with lower arteriolar vessel density (β = −4.5 × 10⁻⁴ per percentage point, 95% CI − 6.7 to − 2.2 × 10⁻⁴; P < 0.001; q < 0.001) and remained robust after small-sample correction and in sensitivity analyses. Inverse associations with fractal dimension (P = 0.012) and with the central retinal arteriolar equivalent in zones B (P = 0.040) and C (P = 0.048) did not remain significant after FDR correction. The magnification-independent arteriole-to-venule ratio was also inversely associated with T2HAF (zone C: P = 0.001). These hypothesis-generating findings suggest that automated fundus image analysis may offer a non-invasive approach for studying thalamic T2 hyperintensity and, potentially, thalamic small vessel pathology; they warrant validation in larger, controlled cohorts with multisequence MRI. Step-by-step AutoMorph and ImageJ protocols are provided.

title: Latent profile analysis and influencing factors of health problem-solving ability among elderly patients with hypertension
authorString: Zhan X, Cai P, Peng N, Zhao X.
abstractText: Objective To identify latent profiles of health problem‑solving ability among elderly patients with hypertension and analyse influencing factors for each profile, thereby providing evidence for developing personalised strategies to enhance this ability. Methods Elderly patients with hypertension attending a tertiary-A hospital in Guizhou Province between February and October 2024 were recruited via convenience sampling. Participants completed questionnaires, including the Chinese-version Health Problem‑Solving Scale, Hypertension‑related Knowledge Scale, Hypertension Patient Self-Efficacy Questionnaire, Social Support Rating Scale, and a sociodemographic and clinical characteristics questionnaire. Latent profile analysis (LPA) was conducted using Mplus software to identify profiles of health problem‑solving ability. Multinomial logistic regression analysis was applied to explore associated influencing factors. Results A total of 423 elderly patients were included. Three latent profiles of health problem‑solving ability were identified : the Low-Ability Avoidance Profile (14.9%), the Moderate-Ability Impulsive/Careless Profile (27.7%), and the High-Ability Negative-Transfer Profile (57.4%). Multinomial logistic regression revealed that hypertension-related knowledge, treatment method, blood pressure control status, social support, and self‑efficacy level were significant influencing factors of health problem‑solving ability. Conclusions Substantial heterogeneity in health problem‑solving ability exists among elderly patients with hypertension. Therefore, clinical nurses should implement personalised interventions tailored to these specific profiles to enhance patients’ health problem-solving skills and self-management outcomes, thereby facilitating better disease control and preventing complications.

title: PECAM-1 as an endothelial gateway for vascular-targeted drug delivery: structural basis, mechanotransduction, and translational opportunities.
authorString: Li H, Liu X, Zhang H, Zhou Y, Huang M, Jiang L.

journal.title: Journal of controlled release : official journal of the Controlled Release Society

abstractText: Platelet endothelial cell adhesion molecule-1 (PECAM-1/CD31) is a junctional adhesion and signaling receptor that is abundant on vascular endothelium and is also expressed on platelets and several leukocyte populations. It regulates leukocyte transendothelial migration, endothelial barrier function, mechanotransduction, platelet inhibitory signaling, and angiogenesis. Its abundant luminal expression and accessibility from the bloodstream have also made PECAM-1 an attractive target for vascular drug delivery and biomaterial engineering. This Review examines the structural features, extracellular interactions, and intracellular signaling mechanisms that determine PECAM-1 targetability. We further discuss its roles in vascular inflammation, atherosclerosis, ischemic injury, thrombosis, hematologic disorders, and cancer, distinguishing receptor blockade or activation from PECAM-1 targeted cargo delivery. Particular attention is given to delivery design, including epitope selection, ligand format, multivalency, carrier properties, intracellular trafficking, luminal anchoring, and cargo-specific requirements. We also evaluate translational factors that may determine targeting performance, including administration route, pharmacokinetics, species differences, disease-associated changes in the vascular microenvironment, manufacturing reproducibility, and patient variability. Together, current evidence supports PECAM-1 as a functional vascular receptor, an endothelial delivery address, and a bioactive interface for vascular devices, while emphasizing that successful translation requires careful matching of target biology, delivery design, therapeutic cargo, and disease context.

title: Anionic lipids regulate PLCβ membrane recruitment.
authorString: Crawford MA, Bennett MB, Qin Y, Cano KE, Gonzalez TG, Mojidra R, Falzone ME.
abstractText: Phospholipase C-β (PLCβ) enzymes are essential effectors of G protein-coupled receptor signaling that hydrolyze phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate at the plasma membrane to generate the second messengers inositol trisphosphate and diacylglycerol. PLCβs play essential roles in diverse physiological processes, including cardiac and neuronal function, macrophage activation, and the pathogenesis of diseases such as hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. PLCβ enzymes are unique in that they are aqueous-soluble and must partition onto the membrane surface to access their substrate, making membrane association a critical regulatory step. For example, we recently demonstrated that Gβγ activates PLCβ by membrane recruitment and orientation of the catalytic core on the membrane surface. Although PLCβ membrane recruitment is required for function, the molecular determinants governing this process remain incompletely understood. Using a quantitative membrane partitioning assay, we show that robust membrane association of PLCβ requires anionic phospholipids, whereas polar phospholipids cannot substitute. Membrane partitioning exhibits a steep dependence on anionic lipid abundance, which is mediated by electrostatic interactions between negatively charged lipids and basic residues within the distal C-terminal domain of PLCβ. We further demonstrate a functional crosstalk between G proteins and anionic lipids to regulate PLCβ membrane recruitment, such that the magnitude of Gβγ-dependent recruitment is dictated by membrane anionic lipid content. These findings reconcile previous discrepancies regarding Gβγ-mediated PLCβ membrane recruitment and establish membrane electrostatics as a key regulatory input that integrates lipid composition with G protein signaling to regulate PLCβ activity.

title: Genetically proxied NLRP3 activity and coronary artery disease risk: a drug-target Mendelian randomization study
authorString: Hirschmüller N, Carter P, Burgess S, Allara E, Peters JE, Gaziano L, Mustafa R, Clarke MCH, Mallat Z, Paul DS, Butterworth AS.
abstractText:
Background and Aims:

Preclinical studies implicate NLRP3 inflammasome activation, which drives release of interleukin-1β and interleukin-18, in vascular inflammation and atherosclerosis, and selective NLRP3 inhibitors are now in clinical development. However, whether lowering NLRP3 activity reduces coronary artery disease (CAD) risk in humans is unknown. We used human genetics to estimate this effect and its mediating pathways.

Methods:

A genetic NLRP3 activity score was derived by combining the effects of eight cis-NLRP3 variants on NLRP3 expression and three inflammatory biomarkers: C-reactive protein, glycoprotein acetylation, and neutrophil count. The score was validated against circulating interleukin-1β and interleukin-18. Drug-target Mendelian randomization was used to estimate its association with CAD, cardiometabolic traits and other diseases studied in NLRP3 inhibitor trials. Mediation by cardiometabolic risk factors was quantified using the product-of-coefficients method.

Results:

A lower genetically proxied NLRP3 activity score was associated with lower circulating interleukin-1β and interleukin-18, but with higher CAD risk (OR = 1.21, 95% CI 1.02 - 1.45, P = 0.032). It was also associated with higher systolic blood pressure, apolipoprotein B levels, and type 2 diabetes risk, which together mediated an estimated 87% of the association with CAD. The residual direct association with CAD was attenuated (OR = 1.03, 95% CI 0.85 - 1.24, P = 0.79). In contrast, a lower score was nominally associated with lower risk of gout, pericarditis, and Parkinson's disease.

Conclusions:

Lifelong lower genetically proxied NLRP3 activity was associated with higher CAD risk, largely mediated by adverse cardiometabolic effects, with no evidence of protection after accounting for them. These findings do not provide genetic support for lowering NLRP3 activity to reduce CAD risk.

title: Complete Recovery From Severe Anthracycline-Induced Cardiomyopathy: Unmasking a Pathogenic MYH7 Variant Through Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Imaging
authorString: Le P, Tong H, Nguyen L, Pham S.
abstractText: The prevention and management of cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction (CTRCD) have become increasingly important. Recent studies have revealed the crucial role of genetics in determining the susceptibility to the development of CTRCD, supporting a "second-hit" hypothesis where genetic variants predispose the myocardium to injury from cardiotoxic agents. We present a case of a 31-year-old woman with breast cancer who developed severe, early-onset CTRCD following a moderate dose of anthracycline and HER2-targeted therapy. Despite her young age and the absence of conventional cardiovascular risk factors, her left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) plummeted to 16%. Through the use of multimodal imaging, particularly cardiac magnetic resonance with tissue characterization, we detected severe biventricular dysfunction and a mid-wall late gadolinium enhancement pattern. Further investigation with genetic testing identified a pathogenic frameshift variant in the MYH7 gene, which was also confirmed in her son and symptomatic mother through cascade screening. Notably, after six months of optimized medical therapy, the patient achieved complete functional recovery (LVEF 53%). This case underscores the potential role of genetic screening in identifying patients at risk for severe CTRCD and advocates for personalized chemotherapy and proactive cardioprotective strategies.

title: Quercetin attenuates atherosclerosis via TNF-α/IRF-1-mediated suppression of the NLRP3/caspase-1 pyroptosis pathway
authorString: Wu D, Bai Y, Guo Q, Ren S, Zhang X, He H, Zhang Y, An D.
abstractText: Despite the established anti-atherosclerotic properties of quercetin, the molecular mechanisms underlying its regulation of macrophage pyroptosis, a key driver of plaque instability, remain poorly understood. We investigated whether quercetin suppresses pyroptosis through coordinated inhibition of the tumor necrosis factor alpha/interferon regulatory factor-1 (TNF-α/IRF-1) axis and the NOD-like receptor family pyrin domain-containing 3 (NLRP3)/caspase-1 signaling pathway, two critical mediators of inflammasome activation. Atherosclerosis (AS) was induced in apolipoprotein E knockout mice fed a high-fat diet for 12 weeks, followed by oral administration of quercetin (50 mg/kg/day) or the caspase-1 inhibitor VX-765 (10 mg/kg/day) for 8 weeks. In parallel, THP-1–derived foam cells were treated with 80 µg/mL oxidized low-density lipoprotein (ox-LDL) for 48 h, quercetin (10 µM, administered 24 h after ox-LDL exposure), or VX-765 (10 µM, administered 24 h after ox-LDL exposure). Cardiac function, serum and cell supernatant cytokines (interleukin 1 beta [IL-1β], IL-18, TNF-α, and interferon beta [IFN-β]), and pyroptosis-related proteins (NLRP3, caspase-1, gasdermin D [GSDMD], IRF-1, and TNF-α) were evaluated using echocardiography, histopathology, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays, immunofluorescence, and immunoblotting. Quercetin significantly improved cardiac function, reduced the aortic plaque area, and decreased serum IL-1β levels by 23.5% (P < 0.01) and TNF-α levels by 15.7% (P < 0.05). Mechanistically, quercetin inhibited IRF-1 nuclear translocation, suppressed transcriptional activation of caspase-1 and GSDMD, and inhibited NLRP3 inflammasome activation, thereby attenuating caspase-1–dependent GSDMD cleavage. These findings suggest that quercetin may represent a promising flavonoid-based therapeutic strategy for inflammation-driven AS.

title: "I just assumed that you just were born with small veins and that's that…": A Qualitative Study of the Experiences of Black and Hispanic Americans Living with Peripheral Artery Disease.
authorString: Bolden DM, Ritger C, Lockhart S, Garcia-Hernandez S, Erpenbeck K, Hanratty R, Hogan S, Huebschmann A, Peterson PN, Dorsey B.

journal.title: Journal of racial and ethnic health disparities

abstractText:
Background

The clinical outcomes of adults living with peripheral artery disease (PAD) have been reported. However, the experience of Black and Hispanic American adults living with PAD, remains understudied. Guided by a multilevel health disparities framework, the aim of this qualitative study was to explore patient factors that may contribute to disparities in disease outcomes.

Methods

Thirty Black and Hispanic American adults with confirmed diagnosis of PAD participated in semi-structured interviews between July 2022 and January 2023. Participants were recruited from an academic medical center and a network of federally qualified health centers affiliated with a safety-net hospital in Denver, Colorado. All interviews were audio-recorded, professionally transcribed and analyzed using Kilbourne et al.'s multilevel framework, which examines the origins of health and healthcare disparities through a health services research lens. The analysis explored patient-level determinants of disparities within the healthcare system.

Results

Overarching themes included: 1) persistent confusion and misunderstanding about PAD, 2) debilitating pain and the loss of physical freedom from PAD, 3) when PAD forces people out of work, 4) PAD and the loss of social connection and 5) emotional unraveling, fear, and psychological distress from PAD.

Conclusions

Through seeking to understand the experience of Black and Hispanic American individuals living with PAD, this study suggests PAD may often be unmanaged, exacerbating and complicating the physical, mental, and emotional symptoms associated with this disease.

title: Transcatheter Closure of Residual Shunt Using the Coil-in-Plug Method After Amplatzer Vascular Plug Implantation for Tubular Patent Ductus Arteriosus in Infants: Two Case Reports.
authorString: Fujino M, Nakamura K, Sasaki T, Kawasaki Y, Sugiyama H.
abstractText: Transcatheter closure of a wide, short tubular patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) in infants is challenging because devices may protrude into adjacent vessels. The Amplatzer Vascular Plug I (AVP I) has no retention disk and suits tubular morphology, but its lack of internal fabric increases the risk of residual shunting. The coil-in-plug (CIP) method, in which microcoils are deployed within a previously implanted AVP I, has been proposed to overcome this limitation. We report two infants with a large PDA and slight aortic isthmus narrowing who underwent implantation of an 8-mm AVP I. Persistent residual shunting prompted staged CIP procedures two months later, allowing time for endothelialization. Detachable microcoils were delivered through a microcatheter, achieving complete occlusion without complications. CIP may be a rescue option for residual shunting after device placement in infants with challenging tubular PDAs, provided sufficient time has elapsed for device fixation.

title: Computed tomography assessment of distal anastomotic new entries after type A dissection repair.
authorString: van Dinter S, van Sambeeck P, Hasami N, Geeraedts T, Jaap Janssen J, Nauta F, Saouti N, Heijmen RH.

journal.title: Multimedia manual of cardiothoracic surgery : MMCTS

abstractText: Distal anastomotic new entries after type A aortic dissection repair provide a communication between the prosthetic lumen and the residual false lumen. Their presence is associated with distal aortic dilatation and reintervention, yet they often remain underreported on routine computed tomography angiography. This video tutorial describes a systematic approach on how to identify and measure these entries using multiplanar reconstruction. The distal anastomosis is first aligned in two orthogonal planes, using external felt reinforcement as a landmark when available. The complete anastomotic circumference is inspected to establish direct continuity between the prosthetic lumen and the false lumen. The entry is then separately aligned to obtain an en face, perpendicular view, allowing measurement of its maximum dimensions. Examples after hemiarch and zone 2 arch replacement illustrate the distinction between anastomotic entries and other sources of false-lumen perfusion. Longitudinal cases demonstrate persistent patency with aortic enlargement, spontaneous closure and thoracic false-lumen resorption 2 years after branched endovascular treatment. This approach supports consistent anatomical assessment, as well as longitudinal reporting.

title: Sucrose Non-fermenting Related Kinase (SNRK) Deficiency-Mediated Osteogenic Differentiation in Vascular Smooth Muscle Cells Exacerbates Vascular Calcification
authorString: Ouyang L, Yu C, Ye W, Zhang Z, Nie H, Cheng J, Chen X, Xie C, Liu Z, Su X, Huang H, Zou M.
abstractText:
Background:

The differentiation of vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) into an osteogenic phenotype is a critical step in vascular calcification progression. Sucrose non-fermenting related kinase (SNRK), a member of the AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) family, has been implicated in diverse cellular functions and pathological conditions. However, whether SNRK is involved in VSMC osteogenic differentiation and calcification remains undefined.

Methods:

Three mouse models were used to evaluate the contributions of SNRK in vascular calcification: Myh11-CreERT2-driven VSMC-specific SNRK knockout in C57BL/6J mice subjected to vitamin D3 overload or adenine diet, and Apoe-/- mice with VSMC (Myh11-CreERT2)-, endothelial cell (Cdh5-Cre)-, or macrophage (LysM-Cre)-specific SNRK knockout on a chronic western diet. The in vitro calcification was modeled by treating primary mouse aortic VSMCs and human aortic VSMCs (HASMCs) with phosphate (Pi).

Results:

Cross-species transcriptomic analyses reveal reduced SNRK expression in murine vascular calcification and human calcified plaques. Human femoral artery samples from the elderly individuals with calcification exhibited reduced SNRK protein levels compared to non-calcified samples. In patients with chronic kidney disease, leukocyte levels of SNRK antisense RNA 1 (SNRK-AS1) were positively correlated with thoracic artery calcification Agatston scores. In parallel, decreased SNRK expression was observed in aortic arteries from three mouse models of calcification and in VSMCs treated with phosphate. Notably, VSMC-specific deletion of SNRK exacerbated calcific lesions, accompanied by upregulation of both runt-related transcription factor 2 (RUNX2) and msh homeobox 2 (MSX2). Conversely, SNRK deletion in either endothelial cells or macrophages had no impact on vascular calcification. Further, overexpression of SNRK in VSMCs, achieved via intravenous injection of an adeno-associated virus (AAV) ligated with VSMC Tagln promoter encoding Snrk, significantly attenuated vascular calcification along with reduced expression of osteogenic markers. Further interactome analysis demonstrated that SNRK directly binds to β-Catenin, a critical regulator of vascular calcification, through the amino acid sequence 270-765. Mechanistically, SNRK facilitated the interaction between β-Catenin and cullin 1/β-TrCP E3 ubiquitin ligase complex, promoting ubiquitin-proteasome-mediated degradation of β-Catenin and subsequently reducing the expression of osteogenic markers in VSMCs.

Conclusions:

We conclude that SNRK safeguards against vascular calcification by preventing β-Catenin/RUNX2/MSX2-mediated VSMC osteogenic differentiation.

title: Imaging-derived wall shear stress and strain reflect local mechanical vulnerability in BAV aortic aneurysm
authorString: Neave L, Nightingale M, Beddoes R, Jadli AS, Patel VB, Garcia J, Fedak PW, Martino ESD.
abstractText: BAV-associated ascending aortic aneurysm is primarily assessed by maximum diameter, which provides limited insight into regional wall integrity and mechanical properties. This study investigated non-invasive, imaging-derived wall shear stress (WSS) and local wall strain reflect region- and layer-specific aortic properties through a multi-scale analysis integrating in vivo biomechanics, RNA expression, and ex vivo mechanical testing. Ascending aortic aneurysm specimens were collected from 10 BAV patients and tissue samples were spatially matched to local imaging measurements. Biaxial, uniaxial, and delamination testing was conducted to characterize the mechanical behaviour of the composite wall, media, adventitia, and layer interface, while quantitative real-time PCR was used to assess COL1A1 and COL3A1 expression. Higher WSS was associated with evidence of localized tissue remodeling, including reduced medial transition-zone onset, reduced medial thickness, and greater energy loss in the media, adventitia, and composite wall. WSS was also positively associated with collagen gene expression, suggestive of increased matrix remodeling activity. Higher wall strain was associated with reduced axial strength and stiffness in the composite wall and adventitia, together with reduced medial stiffness. Increasing age was associated with widespread decrease in the mechanical properties of the wall layers and interface, while maximum diameter showed fewer associations with the tissue properties evaluated. These findings demonstrate distinct associations between imaging-derived WSS and wall strain and local aortic wall properties, with WSS relating predominantly to medial remodeling and strain to reduced tissue stiffness and strength. Together, these findings support further investigation of WSS and wall strain as non-invasive markers associated with regional aortic wall mechanical properties in BAV-associated ascending aortic aneurysm.

title: Clinical Presentation and Surgical Outcomes in Adolescents and Pre-Adolescents with Vascular Rings
authorString: Nandagiri V, Cole L, Falek C, Brown J, Karnett L, Castellanos DA, Walsh E, Zurakowski D, Zendejas B, Baird CW.
abstractText: Background Vascular rings (VRs) produce multiple respiratory and swallowing symptoms, which may vary by age. This study characterized symptoms for pre-adolescent and adolescent VR patients and evaluated whether surgical intervention is associated with clinical improvement. Methods Single-institution, retrospective review of patients aged 9–21 years with complete and incomplete VRs. Patients with complex cardiovascular comorbidities, esophageal atresia/tracheoesophageal fistula, or prior VR repair were excluded. Symptoms were compared pre and postoperatively. Results 49 patients (median age 13.1 years, IQR 11.2–16.1) were included. Diagnoses consisted of right aortic arch with aberrant left subclavian artery (n = 25), double aortic arch (n = 7), left aortic arch with aberrant right subclavian artery (n = 16), and right aortic arch with mirror-image branching and a left ligamentum (n = 1). At baseline, specific individual symptoms and overall symptom counts did not differ significantly between the surgical (n = 33) and non-surgical (n = 16) cohorts. Significant symptom reduction among the surgical cohort was observed for adaptive eating behaviors (pre-op 76% vs. post-op 9%, p < 0.001), dysphagia with solids (pre-op 49% vs. post-op 9%, p < 0.001), sensation of food getting stuck (pre-op 39% vs. post-op 15%, p = 0.039), dyspnea on exertion (pre-op 76% vs. post-op 15%, p < 0.001), chest pain (pre-op 46% vs. post-op 9%, p < 0.001), increased URIs (pre-op 36% vs. post-op 3%, p < 0.001), and chronic cough (pre-op 30% vs. post-op 0%, p = 0.002). Conclusion Pre-adolescent and adolescent vascular ring patients present with specific symptoms, such as dyspnea on exertion, chest pain, and adaptive eating behaviors. Surgical repair is associated with symptom reduction. Improved symptom recognition can optimize VR management.

title: Postnatal Diagnosis of Mosaic Trisomy 20: A Report of 3 New Individuals and Review of the Literature.
authorString: Balton EV, Simpson D, Miranda C, Petersen A, Granger L, Byers PH, Chanprasert S, Horike-Pyne M, Miller DE, Ranchalis J, Rosenthal EA, Solomon AK, Stergachis AB, Sybert VP, Wener MH, Undiagnosed Diseases Network, Jarvik GP, Blue EE, Love-Nichols J, Dipple KM, Leppig KA, Adam MP, Glass IA, Paschal CR, Kumar RD.

journal.title: American journal of medical genetics. Part A

abstractText: Mosaic Trisomy 20 (T20) is a well described laboratory finding in the prenatal setting, often considered a culturing artifact. Knowledge of the mosaic T20 phenotype is limited, although a core set of recurring findings have been proposed: sloped shoulders, spinal abnormalities, chronic constipation, hypotonia, and learning disabilities. We present three new individuals with postnatal confirmation of mosaic T20, characterize their phenotypes, and compare them with 22 other clinically affected individuals identified in the literature. We used constitutional karyotype analysis of skin fibroblasts to diagnose three unrelated individuals with mosaic T20: an 8 year-old female with mildly dysmorphic features, congenital heart defect, multi-cystic kidney, chronic constipation, scoliosis, vertebral fusion anomalies, and developmental delay; a 21 year-old male with congenital heart defect, varied skeletal anomalies, renal disease, and linear hyper- and hypo-pigmentation of skin; and a 2 year-old generally non-dysmorphic and normally developing male with prenatal finding of mosaic T20 on amniocentesis later confirmed on postnatal testing. We present three new individuals with postnatally confirmed mosaic T20, refine the core phenotype from infancy to early adulthood, and discuss strategies to improve the rate of diagnosis and longitudinal follow-up.

title: Improving Prenatal Coarctation of the Aorta Screening With Dynamic Routing Knowledge Distillation and Capsule Networks: A Multicenter Study.
authorString: Song S, Yang P, Yang Y, Luo Y, Zhang P, Zeng S.
abstractText:
Objective

Coarctation of the aorta (CoA) is one of the most common congenital heart defects, yet prenatal diagnosis remains difficult because of its variable and subtle anatomical presentation. To address this challenge, we developed KDCoANet, a dynamic routing knowledge distillation framework designed to identify fetuses with suspected CoA from fetal echocardiography.

Methods

We conducted a multicenter retrospective analysis of 576 video segments from 377 pregnancies. In the first stage, a high-capacity teacher model learned rich feature representations. In the second stage, we compared three training strategies for lightweight student models (FastViT, ShuffleNet, and SqueezeNet): a general group, traditional knowledge distillation, and a proposed dynamic routing distillation strategy with capsule networks (DR+Caps) to align high-order feature distributions between teacher and student models. Performance was compared with that of the general group using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC).

Results

KDCoANet achieved an AUC of 0.937 in the validation dataset and 0.888 in the multicenter dataset, with sensitivities of 0.909 and 0.800, specificities of 0.800 and 0.827, and F1 scores of 0.847 and 0.800, respectively. The proposed method also produced statistically significant AUC improvements over both the general group and traditional distillation (p < 0.05). DR+Caps increased specificity and reduced the false-positive rate among prenatally suspected cases, which is clinically important in prenatal CoA screening.

Conclusion

KDCoANet improves diagnostic accuracy through dynamic routing distillation and capsule network-based feature alignment. The dynamic routing strategy substantially improves the alignment of high-order feature distributions between teacher and student models, resulting in better performance than traditional distillation methods. Its lightweight design enables rapid deployment in fetal echocardiography, with the potential to improve detection rates and reduce missed diagnoses.

title: Decreased Preoperative Left Atrial Function and Synchrony in Patients with Postoperative Dysfunction After Ventricular Septal Defect Repair.
authorString: Lloyd W, Adamson GT, Kaplinski M, Arunamata A, Reddy CD, Punn R.
abstractText: Ventricular septal defect (VSD) repair is the most common type of congenital heart surgery, yet little is known about left atrial (LA) mechanics before and after repair. We sought to characterize changes in LA size and function following VSD repair and evaluate whether preoperative LA mechanics are associated with postoperative left ventricular (LV) dysfunction. We hypothesized that LA mechanics worsen immediately after VSD repair and abnormal preoperative LA mechanics are associated with more severe postoperative LV dysfunction. We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study in children with isolated, moderate or larger VSDs with preoperative LV ejection fraction (EF) > 50%, who underwent surgical repair between June 2012 to April 2023. LA and LV volumes were measured. LA and LV strain and synchrony were assessed using speckle-tracking echocardiography (TomTec Arena). Three primary endpoints included LA opposing wall delay, LA dyssynchrony index, and LA global longitudinal strain (GLS). All other LA and LV measures were secondary and considered exploratory and hypothesis generating. 175 patients were included. Postoperative LV dysfunction (EF ≤ 50%) occurred in 71 patients (41%), including 24 patients (14%) with EF ≤ 40% defined as severe postoperative dysfunction. After surgery, LA volume, EF, regional strain, global longitudinal strain, and synchrony all decreased. Among patients with postoperative EF ≤ 40%, preoperative LA volumes and dyssynchrony were increased, and pre and postoperative LA strain were decreased. VSD repair is associated with an immediate impairment of LA mechanics, including a reduction in LA size, ejection fraction, strain, and synchrony. These changes in the primary endpoints were robust to correction for multiple comparisons. Patients who developed severe postoperative LV dysfunction also had significantly lower postoperative LA strain. Preoperative LA dyssynchrony and reduced preoperative LA reservoir function were associated with severe postoperative LV dysfunction on adjusted analysis but did not remain significant after correction for multiple comparisons, therefore should be regarded as hypothesis-generating and warrant confirmation in a larger, prospective designed cohort.
