title: Transcatheter Tricuspid Edge-To-Edge Repair Versus Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve Replacement for Severe Symptomatic Tricuspid Regurgitation.
authorString: Puri R, Scotti A, Tereshchenko LG, Russo G, Thiele H, Alessandrini H, Andreas M, Connelly KA, Estevez-Loureiro R, Hahn RT, Maisano F, Hausleiter J, Urena M, Monivas V, Pedrazzini G, Adamo M, Sievert H, Webb JG, Tang GHL, Stolz L, Lurz P, Kresoja KP, Benito-Gonzalez T, Sturla M, Zahr F, Boone R, Kodali S, Tchétché D, De Backer O, Coisne A, Ludwig S, Garcia SA, Adam M, De Marco F, Ho EC, Cheung A, Biroli M, Patrascu A, Alnasser S, Chadderdon S, Kobari Y, Echarte-Morales J, Byrne T, Frerker C, Dumonteil N, Oliva OA, Rudolph TK, Rudolph F, Guddeti R, Bakhtadze B, Krishnaswamy A, Kapadia SR, Portillo JD, Rodés-Cabau J, Schofer N, Cruz-Gonzalez I, Granada J, Modine T, Fam N, Latib A, Taramasso M.
abstractText:
Background

Transcatheter tricuspid edge-to-edge repair (T-TEER) and transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR) are both approved for severe symptomatic tricuspid regurgitation (TR) but lack head-to-head comparison.

Objectives

This study sought to compare 1-year outcomes of T-TEER vs TTVR using causal inference in a harmonized real-world cohort.

Methods

TRIVALVE (International Multisite Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve Therapies Registry) (T-TEER, n = 384) and TRIPLACE (Global Multicenter Registry on Transcatheter TRIcuspid Valve RePLACEment) (TTVR, n = 398) registries were harmonized (n = 782). Inverse probability weighted survival time estimated study group average treatment effect (ATE) and treated-study group average treatment effect on the treated (ATET) effects on time to all-cause death, heart failure hospitalization (HFH), tricuspid valve (TV) reintervention, bleeding, and their composite major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), balanced for 14 baseline clinical/echocardiographic covariates, were undertaken.

Results

Median follow-up by reverse Kaplan-Meier estimates was 276 days (IQR: 58-365). TTVR achieved near-complete TR elimination vs persistent mild-moderate residual TR post-T-TEER [median (IQR) grade 0 (0-1) vs 2 (1-2)]. Modeling demonstrated an early all-cause mortality penalty for TTVR (ATE: -81.3 days, P = 0.002; ATET: -79 days, P = 0.003) with a corresponding overall MACE signal (ATE: -70.7 days, P = 0.001; ATET: -69.3 days, P = 0.012).

Conclusions

Despite more complete TR reduction, orthotopic TTVR may be associated with earlier all-cause mortality and MACE penalty over T-TEER. This hypothesis-generating analysis should spur further research to identify the optimal patient phenotype for T-TEER and TTVR technologies.

title: External validation of the fullPIERS model for predicting adverse maternal outcomes among Swedish women with preeclampsia.
authorString: Dahlberg L, Sandberg T, Imberg H, Andersson J, Pontoppidan A, Carlberg N, Bucher V, Junus K, Wesslén E, Cluver C, Wikström AK, Wallin N, Bergman L.
abstractText:
Introduction

Preeclampsia affects 3%-4% of all pregnancies in the Nordic countries. It is a leading cause of maternal morbidity and mortality. Using risk stratification for women diagnosed with preeclampsia could potentially reduce adverse maternal outcomes. The fullPIERS model is a clinical prediction tool that has not been validated in the Nordic countries. We therefore aimed to externally validate the fullPIERS model among Swedish women with preeclampsia.

Material and methods

Data were obtained from two Swedish prospective cohort studies. Predictor variables were assessed within 24 h of inclusion. Outcomes were assessed at 48 h and 7 days after inclusion. The performance of the fullPIERS model was evaluated by discrimination using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and by risk stratification at prespecified risk cutoffs. Analyses were conducted with and without hematological outcomes (blood transfusion or severe thrombocytopenia).

Results

In total, 617 women were enrolled between May 2019 and March 2025. Adverse maternal outcomes occurred in 34 (5.5%) women within 48 h and 68 (11.0%) within 7 days. The fullPIERS model demonstrated modest discrimination for predicting adverse maternal outcomes within 48 h (AUC 0.64; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.54, 0.74) and within 7 days (AUC 0.64; 95% CI: 0.57, 0.71). When analyses were restricted to nonhematological outcomes (n = 14 for 48 h and 19 for 7 days), the AUC was 0.79 (95% CI: 0.68, 0.89) within 48 h and 0.78 (95% CI: 0.69, 0.87) within 7 days. At a low-risk threshold of < 0.01, 297 (48.1%) women were classified as low risk, of whom one developed a nonhematological adverse outcome within 48 h, corresponding to a sensitivity of 0.93 (95% CI: 0.69-0.99) and a negative predictive value of 1.00 (95% CI: 0.98-1.00).

Conclusions

Overall, the fullPIERS model demonstrated poor clinical utility in identifying low-risk and high-risk individuals for adverse maternal outcomes among Swedish women with preeclampsia. When hematological outcomes were excluded, the model improved its ability to identify women without adverse maternal outcomes. The model may have clinical utility facilitating physicians in identifying those who could be managed with a lower level of surveillance.

title: An Orange a Day Keeps the Doctor Away: A Spectrum of Cases of Scurvy, From Classic Skin Findings to Severe Pulmonary Complications.
authorString: Kieffer H, Laws J, Clegg J, Coates A, Gaietto K, Patterson S, Wong M, Essakow J.
abstractText: Vitamin C deficiency, otherwise known as scurvy, is uncommon in the United States but affects at-risk populations with nutritionally limited diets. In pediatric populations, this most commonly impacts children with developmental disorders such as autism spectrum disorder, malabsorption diseases including Crohn's Disease, and those with end-stage renal disease. The most common symptoms include gingival hyperplasia, petechiae, corkscrew hair, and joint/lower extremity pain. However, there are acutely life-threatening presentations of scurvy that are not well characterized in the literature and may be overlooked in the clinical setting given their rarity. This case series describes four patients with severe dietary restriction in the setting of developmental delays who were found to have vitamin C deficiency but presented with a spectrum of symptoms, from the classic skin and musculoskeletal findings to severe respiratory failure with suspected pulmonary hypertension. We also present the first reported case of scurvy-induced pulmonary hemorrhage in a pediatric patient. Each patient initially had a similar progression of symptoms but ultimately demonstrated variation in the extent and severity of them. Cases 2-4 all had normalization of respiratory symptoms and laboratory and radiographic findings following vitamin C supplementation. Through this case series, the similarities of our patients' presentations prior to the development of life-threatening complications are highlighted to raise awareness of risk factors and warning signs. The main objective of this series is to encourage clinicians to assess for scurvy and other nutritional deficiencies in at-risk patients with the intention of preventing the development of more life-threatening sequelae. We also suggest the need for further targeted research to better understand why not every patient develops these respiratory complications.

title: 3-D Ultrasound as a new indicator for Optic Nerve Sheath Volume.
authorString: Wang S, Gao Y, Zhang J, Fang Y, Liu Y, Chen Y, Wang L.
abstractText:
Objective

Traditional 2-D ultrasonographic measurement of the optic nerve sheath diameter has been utilized to estimate intra-cranial pressure but limitations remain, underscoring the need for more advanced imaging approaches. This study aimed to use 3-D ultrasound to determine the normative range of internal optic nerve sheath volume (ONSV) in healthy adults and identify potential factors influencing ONSV.

Methods

A total of 69 healthy participants (26 males, 43 females) were included, with 3-D ultrasound of the optic nerve sheath performed for each participant. Each observer performed ONSV measurements twice, and all measurements were independently completed by two investigators to calculate intra- and inter-observer reliabilities.

Results

The mean age of participants was 47.32 ± 15.08 y (range: 19-75 y), with a mean body mass index of 23.76 ± 4.26 kg/m². The average ONSV was 0.028 ± 0.006 mm³ (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.027-0.029 mm³), with no significant difference observed between the left and right eyes (p > 0.05). Simple linear regression analysis revealed no significant correlations between ONSV and age, sex, body mass index or waistline (all p > 0.05). The intra-observer reliability was 0.939 (95% CI, 0.910-0.967, p < 0.001), with an inter-observer reliability of 0.883 (95% CI, 0.816-0.926, p < 0.001).

Conclusion

3-D ultrasound provides a reliable, non-invasive technique to assess ONSV. The normative ONSV range established in this study offers a foundation for future clinical applications, particularly in the non-invasive monitoring of elevated intra-cranial pressure.

title: Comparative evaluation of intranasal simvastatin-loaded transbilosomes versus oral simvastatin suspension in attenuating heart failure in rat models induced by doxorubicin and ischemia/reperfusion.
authorString: Rofaiel Wahba Rofaiel M, Mahmoud DM, Baali FH, Belal A, Yousef Gushgari O, Ahmed Bawaked R, Abdullah Al Shwail F, Girgis Shahataa M, Fouad AG, Naguib DM, Ghalwash MM.
abstractText: Simvastatin (SMS) has profound lipid-independent 'pleiotropic' effects that benefit heart failure (HF), but its poor solubility and bioavailability limit its efficacy. This study developed nasal simvastatin-loaded transbilosomes (SLT) to improve drug solubility and bioavailability and mitigate HF. To develop an optimal SLT formulation, the Box-Behnken design was employed. The effectiveness of the nasal SLT was evaluated in vivo using rat models of HF induced by either doxorubicin or ischaemia/reperfusion. Relative to free SMS, the optimal SLT achieved a release increase of 3.81-fold, increased bioavailability by 6.35-fold, enhanced permeation by 7.46-fold, and increased the cardiac accumulation by 1.96-fold. Compared to the oral SMS group, the nasal SLT group exhibited significantly lower levels of triglycerides, cholesterol, LDL, CK-MB, LDH, troponin I, NT-proBNP, NO, MDA, and heart rate, being 1.49-fold, 1.47-fold, 1.40-fold, 1.48-fold, 1.42-fold, 1.59-fold, 1.42-fold, 2.0-fold, 1.90-fold, and 1.99-fold lower, respectively. Conversely, HDL, GSH, SOD, ejection fraction, and fractional shortening increased by 1.5-fold, 1.95-fold, 1.48-fold, 1.48-fold, and 1.42-fold, respectively. Histopathology examination validated the efficacy of the nasal SLT formulation. While these findings represent nasal SLT as a promising insight in alleviating HF, future work is recommended to fully elucidate the distinct contribution of isolated vehicle and route controls.

title: Renovascular hypertension.
authorString: Moulson A, Tran A.

journal.title: CMAJ : Canadian Medical Association journal = journal de l'Association medicale canadienne

title: Risk and Outcomes of Acute Aortic Events in Patients With Polycystic Kidney Disease.
authorString: Lee KT, Chang MY, Ling AW, Li SY, Chen SW, Lai EC, Tsai DH, Cheng YT, Wang CL, Chu PH.

journal.title: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society

abstractText:
Background

This study evaluated whether polycystic kidney disease (PKD) is associated with an increased risk of life-threatening acute aortic events (AAEs) and adverse clinical outcomes.

Methods and results

This retrospective cohort study used the Taiwan National Health Insurance Research Database (NHIRD) from 2000 to 2022. Patients with PKD were propensity score-matched 1 : 10 to controls from an age- and sex-matched control pool. The mean follow-up was 9.5 years. The primary outcome was the incidence of AAE, defined as aortic rupture, aortic dissection, or death due to aortic disease. Secondary outcomes were in-hospital and post-discharge complications. The matched cohort comprised 3,655 patients with PKD and 36,550 controls. PKD was associated with significantly increased risks of aortic rupture (hazard ratio [HR] 4.20; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.74-10.16), aortic dissection (HR 2.31; 95% CI 1.50-3.54), and death due to aortic disease (HR 3.82; 95% CI 2.02-7.23). Among 40,995 admissions for AAEs, patients with PKD had a higher risk of new-onset dialysis (odds ratio 2.59; 95% CI 1.13-5.91). After discharge, patients with PKD also had higher risks of stroke, readmission, and new-onset maintenance dialysis than controls.

Conclusions

PKD was associated with increased risks of life-threatening AAEs and subsequent adverse outcomes. These findings support heightened clinical awareness and risk-based cardiovascular assessment in select high-risk patients.

title: [Chronic spinal muscular atrophy presenting with monomelic amyotrophy involving the ‍left lower limb].
authorString: Maruta K, Miyamoto M, Tashiro K.
abstractText: A 69-year-old man with familial hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (TNNT2 missense mutation) presented with gradually progressive atrophy and weakness of the left thigh. No family history of neurologic or neuromuscular disease was apparent. Weakness of the left lower limb first became apparent in his late 30s. At age 62, the patient noted atrophy of the left thigh; at 66, he underwent cervical laminectomy and at 67, lumbar laminectomy. Neither operation resulted in clinical improvement. Symptoms were limited to the left lower limb and progressed very slowly. Neurologic examination disclosed marked atrophy of the left quadriceps femoris and mild atrophy of the left tibialis anterior. Mild weakness was evident in the left hamstrings, iliopsoas, and quadriceps; in the last of these, fasciculations were noted. Deep tendon reflexes were decreased in the upper extremities and absent in the lower extremities. No Babinski or other pyramidal tract sign was elicited. No bulbar dysfunction, sensory disturbance, or autonomic dysfunction was apparent. Nerve conduction studies were normal. Electromyography (EMG) showed high amplitudes and long-duration action potentials in the left vastus medialis and tibialis anterior muscles. Abnormalities suggesting denervation were found in both arms and legs, especially on the left. While clinical signs favored monomelic amyotrophy involving the left leg, EMG findings suggested chronic spinal muscular atrophy.

title: [A case of aortic saddle embolism with diagnosis difficulty due to transient symptom improvement following early recanalization].
authorString: Mitsuhashi M, Usami T, Seko K, Kano Y, Toyoda T, Takada K.
abstractText: A 70-year-old man with obesity, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, dyslipidemia, and atrial fibrillation was admitted with paraplegia, sensory impairment, and lower limb pain. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) revealed occlusion of the distal abdominal aorta, and he was initially diagnosed with Leriche's syndrome. His symptoms promptly improved; however, they recurred on hospital day 4, accompanied by progressive rhabdomyolysis and renal impairment. Magnetic resonance imaging of the lower extremities showed multiple muscle infarctions. His condition subsequently improved, and he was able to walk with a walker. Contrast-enhanced CT on hospital day 35 demonstrated recanalization of the occluded vessels, and he was finally diagnosed with aortic saddle embolism. This case illustrates that early recanalization can cause transient symptom improvement, potentially leading to diagnostic difficulty.

title: Association of Lipoprotein(a) with long-term survival outcomes in Chinese patients with coronary artery disease: A large-scale cohort study from the CIN-II registry.
authorString: Lu X, Yuan Z, Yuan G, Huang Z, Huang H, Ling Y, Ruan H, Zhang W, Deng J, Guo W, Chen S, Liu J, Chen J, Liu Y.
abstractText:
Background and aims

Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is an independent risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. However, data on Lp(a) distribution and prognostic thresholds in Asian patients with coronary artery disease (CAD) remain limited and may differ from Western populations. This study investigated the association of Lp(a) with cardiovascular and all-cause mortality in CAD patients.

Methods

This retrospective cohort study included 51,489 patients with CAD (mean age, 62.7 years; 23.5% female) from the Cardiorenal Improvement-II (CIN-II) registry. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models assessed associations of Lp(a) categories (<30, 30-50, ≥50 mg/dL) with cardiovascular and all-cause mortality. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis investigated the Lp(a) dose-response relationship with mortality. Mediation analysis evaluated high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) and fibrinogen (FIB) as mediators.

Results

Among 51,489 participants, the median Lp(a) was 17.2 mg/dL (interquartile range [IQR]: 9.0-37.1 mg/dL), with 12.77% (n = 6577) and 18.10% (n = 9317) having 30-50 and ≥ 50 mg/dL. During the median 5.2-year follow-up, 3833 (7.44%) cardiovascular and 8332 (16.18%) all-cause mortality occurred. After multivariable adjustment, patients with Lp(a) of 30-50 mg/dL and ≥50 mg/dL had higher cardiovascular mortality risk (hazard ratio [HR] 1.32, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.20-1.45; HR 1.42, 95% CI 1.31-1.54; both p < 0.001). RCS analysis demonstrated a non-linear association with cardiovascular mortality, rising to a plateau (p for non-linearity < 0.001). Hs-CRP and FIB statistically mediated 3.55% and 23.80% of Lp(a) association with cardiovascular mortality (both p < 0.001).

Conclusions

Nearly one-third of CAD patients had Lp(a) ≥30 mg/dL. Higher Lp(a) was independently associated with increased risk of cardiovascular and all-cause mortality, with this association statistically mediated by inflammation and fibrinolysis.

title: Biochemistry and Pathophysiological Role of Specialized Pro-Resolving Lipid Mediators (SPMs) in Cardiovascular Disease
authorString: Ivchuk V.
abstractText: The essay reviews the biochemical and pathophysiological aspects of specialized pro-resolving lipid mediators (SPMs) – lipoxins, resolvins, protectins and maresins – in the context of cardiovascular diseases. It is shown that SPMs, which are formed from polyunsaturated fatty acids with the participation of lipoxygenases and cyclooxygenases, exert their action through specific G-protein-coupled receptors (ALX/FPR2, GPR32, ChemR23, GPR18), promoting efferocytosis, polarization of macrophages into the M2 phenotype and suppression of pro-inflammatory signaling pathways. Experimental data on the cardioprotective role of SPMs in atherosclerosis, myocardial infarction and heart failure are presented. At the same time, analytical and translational limitations are critically analyzed: ultralow concentrations of SPMs in biological fluids, methodological difficulties in quantitative determination, as well as contradictory data on the activation of their receptors. It is argued that further progress requires a transition from measuring concentrations to assessing functional activity and developing stable synthetic analogues and targeted delivery systems. The essay is intended for scientists in the fields of biochemistry, molecular biology, and cardiology.

title: Visualizing periarticular inflammation of the shoulder and pelvic girdles in polymyalgia rheumatica with [<sup>68</sup>Ga]Ga-DOTA-Siglec-9 PET/CT.
authorString: Petzinna SM, Küppers J, Schemmer B, Gheitasi R, Jamin RN, Baerlecken N, Essler M, Schäfer VS.
abstractText:
Background

Polymyalgia rheumatica (PMR) and giant cell arteritis (GCA) are increasingly recognized as phenotypic variants within a shared disease spectrum. While [18F]fluorodeoxyglucose ([18F]FDG)-positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) can detect musculoskeletal and vascular involvement, its reliance on glucose metabolism limits inflammation-specificity. The vascular adhesion protein-1 (VAP-1)-targeted tracer [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-Siglec-9 has shown promise in GCA. This study evaluates its potential for detecting periarticular inflammation in PMR.

Methods

Patients with PMR underwent [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-Siglec-9 PET/CT with musculoskeletal and vascular ultrasound. Tracer uptake was measured in periarticular and vascular regions and compared with patients with active GCA. Soluble VAP-1 (sVAP-1) and matrix metalloproteinases (MMP-2/-3/-9) were measured in patients with PMR and GCA, as well as in healthy controls, who did not undergo imaging.

Results

Eight PMR patients were imaged and compared with sixteen GCA patients as well as eight healthy controls. In comparison to GCA-only patients, an increased periarticular tracer uptake across the shoulder and pelvic girdle was found in PMR (maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) 2.65±0.52 vs. 1.96±0.57; p<0.001). Tracer uptake was inversely associated with recent prednisolone exposure across periarticular and vascular territories (all p<0.05). Circulating sVAP-1 was inversely associated with MMP-2 (r=-0.58; p=0.008). Moreover, MMP-2 and MMP-3 were negatively associated with vascular tracer uptake (e.g. aortic arch SUVmax/MMP-2 r=-0.69; p=0.001).

Conclusions

This pioneering study demonstrates that [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-Siglec-9 PET/CT detects periarticular inflammation in PMR. Inverse associations between tracer uptake and recent glucocorticoid exposure suggest potential treatment-related modulation. The associations between MMPs, sVAP-1, and tracer uptake provide hypothesis-generating insights into a VAP-1/MMP-axis potentially shaping the PET signal. Our findings position [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-Siglec-9 PET/CT as a promising inflammation-specific biomarker for disease activity assessment and phenotyping in PMR and GCA.

title: Outcomes of Pediatric Heart Transplantation at China's Largest Center: A 10-Year Retrospective Analysis of Survival and Associated Factors.
authorString: Zeng T, Lai J, Wang Y, Yim WY, Xiong T, Qian X, Peng Y, Wang G, Dong N, Li F.
abstractText:
Background

Pediatric heart transplantation (HTx) is a critical therapy for end-stage heart failure. We analyzed 202 pediatric HTx cases from a large cardiac transplant center in China to describe survival outcomes, perioperative management, and factors associated with mortality.

Methods

We retrospectively analyzed 202 pediatric HTx recipients from 2015 to 2024. The primary endpoint was survival after HTx. Baseline characteristics, survival, and mortality risk factors were analyzed.

Results

Annual volume increased from 4 to 32 cases. Mean recipient age was 9.28 ± 4.34 y, and dilated cardiomyopathy was the most common indication (48.51%). The 1, 3, and 5-y survival rates were 89.2% (95% CI, 0.849-0.937), 84.3% (95% CI, 0.790-0.899), and 84.3% (95% CI, 0.790-0.899), respectively. In multivariable Cox regression, preoperative mechanical ventilation was associated with mortality at 1 y (HR = 7.84, 95% CI, 2.62-23.48; P < 0.001) and 5 y (HR = 4.98, 95% CI, 1.83-13.54; P = 0.002). Longer postoperative ventilation time was also associated with mortality at 1 y (HR = 1.01 per day, 95% CI, 1.00-1.03; P = 0.043) and 5 y (HR = 1.01 per day, 95% CI, 1.00-1.03; P = 0.022).

Conclusions

This 10-y cohort describes pediatric HTx outcomes in China. Survival was comparable with contemporary registry outcomes. Distinct cohort features included prolonged cold ischemia time, broader donor to recipient weight ratios, and limited ventricular assist device use. Preoperative mechanical ventilation and longer postoperative ventilation time were associated with higher mortality. These findings provide a center perspective for programs with different donor availability, recipient profiles, and support strategies.

title: Early Post-Approval Reporting of Ziftomenib in the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System: A Disproportionality Analysis
authorString: Olorunkemi OD.
abstractText:
Purpose:

To describe early post-approval reports for ziftomenib, an oral menin inhibitor approved in November 2025 for NPM1-mutated relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia (AML), in the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS), and to screen them for disproportionate reporting.

Methods:

Seven FAERS quarterly releases (2025 Q1 to 2026 Q3) were used, each case was counted once, and cases first received from 13 November 2025 to 30 September 2026 were included (1,202,628 cases). Cases with ziftomenib as primary suspect were compared with all other primary-suspect cases and with cases of other AML-targeted drugs, using reporting odds ratios (ROR), proportional reporting ratios and the information component. Revumenib served as a secondary reporting comparator. All analyses were run in Python.

Results:

There were 62 ziftomenib cases (489 for revumenib). Nine terms met the screening rule against all other cases, led by death (14 cases). Against other AML-targeted drugs, death, infection, pneumonia and platelet count decreased no longer met the information component rule, while pruritus, product use in unapproved indication and pericarditis (3 cases) did. Differentiation syndrome, a boxed warning, had 3 cases. QT prolongation was reported once for ziftomenib and 24 times for revumenib.

Conclusions:

No clearly unexpected signal was found. Pericarditis is a hypothesis to revisit as reports accrue. Spontaneous reports cannot show causation or incidence.

title: Venous flow dynamics in post-stroke hemiparetic lower extremity motor dysfunctions.
authorString: Külekçioğlu S, Guven H.
abstractText:
Objective

To assess venous flow impairments in post-stroke hemiparetic lower limbs by comparing venous pump capacity (VPC) and venous refilling time (VRT) between affected and unaffected sides, and to examine their associations with motor function, spasticity, and functional independence.

Design

Retrospective cross-sectional study.

Setting

Outpatient Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation and Cardiovascular Surgery clinics at a tertiary care hospital in Türkiye. Participants: Forty-three adults (mean age: 62.6 ± 11.5 years) with hemiparesis persisting ≥ 3 months were included. Patients with hemiplegia, chronic venous disease, peripheral arterial disease, or systemic illness were excluded. Participants were identified via consecutive sampling from existing plethysmographic records.

Interventions

Not applicable.

Main outcome measure(s)

Primary outcomes were VPC and VRT, measured bilaterally using digital photoplethysmography (D-PPG). Secondary measures included Brunnstrom stage, Barthel Index, and Modified Ashworth Scale.

Results

VPC and VRT were significantly reduced in hemiparetic limbs (VPC: 1.07 ± 0.43 vs. 2.24 ± 0.74%; VRT: 9.26 ± 3.42 vs. 19.4 ± 2.0 seconds; p < 0.001), consistent with impaired calf muscle pump function. Interlimb VRT asymmetry decreased with higher Brunnstrom stage (ρ =  -0.35, p = 0.022) and Barthel Index (ρ =  -0.38, p = 0.012) and was associated with hemiparetic side (p = 0.0027), suggesting motor function influences venous return. A borderline association with spasticity (p = 0.066) suggests altered muscle tone may further disrupt hemodynamics. VPC differences showed no significant clinical correlations.

Conclusions

Hemiparetic limbs exhibit marked venous flow impairment, likely attributable to reduced calf pump activity. This dysfunction may be physiologically linked to motor recovery and functional status. Integrating venous assessment into stroke rehabilitation may help prevent thromboembolic complications and improve circulatory outcomes.

title: From Channelopathy to Cardiomyopathy: How Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Reframes Inherited Arrhythmias
authorString: Mohamed KA, Elshabrawi MN, Alkasir A, Hanfy A, Saifuddin M, Perucki W, Abdelhamid M.
abstractText: Inherited arrhythmia syndromes have traditionally been classified as either primary electrical disorders or structural cardiomyopathies, a framework that increasingly fails to capture the tissue-level abnormalities identified across this spectrum. Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging has emerged as a pivotal tool in reframing this paradigm by combining precise ventricular phenotyping with myocardial tissue characterization. In classic channelopathies such as long QT syndrome and catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, CMR remains primarily exclusionary, while in structural diseases such as arrhythmogenic and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, it directly identifies the arrhythmogenic substrate through late gadolinium enhancement and parametric mapping. Brugada syndrome occupies an intermediate position, with emerging evidence of subtle right ventricular outflow tract abnormalities challenging its classification as a purely electrical disorder. This review examines the disease-specific diagnostic yield of CMR, its expanding role in risk stratification and implantable cardioverter-defibrillator decision-making, and future directions including artificial intelligence-driven analysis and genotype-phenotype correlation.

title: Development and In Vivo Feasibility of a Wirelessly Powered Light-Emitting Stent-Graft for Photobiomodulation in a Porcine Aortic Model.
authorString: Kawai R, Nakai M, Ishida M, Saguchi T, Tatehara I, Bando S, Yasutomi M, Sugihara E, Okada Y, Ogawa E, Saito K.
abstractText:
Objectives

Stent-graft (SG) infection is a serious complication of endovascular aneurysm repair. Although photobiomodulation (PBM) may have bacteriostatic effects, there is currently no established technology to deliver near-infrared light to deeply implanted SGs. In this study, we developed a wirelessly powered light-emitting SG and evaluated its feasibility.

Methods

A light-emitting SG was fabricated by attaching 7 plastic optical fibers (outer diameter, 250 μm; light-diffusing length, 10 cm) to a 14-mm-diameter, 10-cm-long SG, enabling red light emission along the SG. We also developed a dedicated delivery system and a wireless power transmission system with an implantable light source. The SG was implanted in the abdominal aorta of 2 pigs via laparotomy, and the light source was implanted in the subcutaneous tissue of the lower abdomen. Light emission from the SG was evaluated under wireless power transmission from an external power source.

Results

The light-emitting SG was successfully deployed in both pigs. Stable light emission was confirmed during wireless power transmission.

Conclusions

A wirelessly powered light-emitting SG was successfully deployed, and stable red light emission was demonstrated in a porcine abdominal aortic model. This device may provide a novel platform for future therapeutic applications, including PBM-based infection control.

title: The role of SIRT3 in abdominal aortic aneurysm via regulating the PINK1/Parkin-mediated mitophagy pathway.
authorString: Hu L, Zhang X, He X, Wei G, Zhang J, Wang Z, Guo Z.
abstractText:
Background

Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a fatal vascular disease lacking effective pharmacological treatments. Mitophagy dysfunction is implicated in AAA, yet its upstream regulators remain unclear. This study aimed to identify key mitophagy-related genes and explore the role of SIRT3 in AAA formation.

Methods

Integrated bioinformatics analysis was performed on the GSE51227 dataset to identify MRDEGs, followed by protein-protein interaction (PPI) network analysis to screen hub genes. Validation was conducted using the independent GSE51228 dataset, human AAA tissue specimens, and CaCl2-induced AAA model. In vitro loss-of-function experiments were performed in human aortic smooth muscle cells using siRNA targeting SIRT3. In vivo, local shRNA-mediated Sirt3 knockdown was performed in mouse aortas to assess its effect on aortic structure and mitophagy-related gene expression.

Results

Thirty-three MRDEGs were identified, and PPI network analysis revealed 14 hub genes, including Pink1, Sirt3, and Ppargc1a. qRT-PCR and immunohistochemistry confirmed significant reduction in PINK1, SIRT3, and PPARGC1A expression in human AAA tissues. In vitro, SIRT3 knockdown reduced mitochondrial content and suppressed PINK1 and Parkin expression. In vivo, local Sirt3 knockdown induced significant aortic dilation, medial thinning, and decreased Pink1/Parkin expression, phenocopying key features of AAA.

Conclusion

SIRT3 deficiency impairs PINK1/Parkin-mediated mitophagy, triggering mitochondrial dysfunction and aortic remodeling. The SIRT3-PINK1 axis represents a novel therapeutic target for preventing AAA formation.

title: Mannose-Functionalized Fe<sub>3</sub>O<sub>4</sub>-Polyamidoamine Dendrimer Nanocomplexes with Unusual T1 MRI Response for Targeted Atherosclerosis Imaging.
authorString: Kou H, Qi L, Quirk JD, Yang H.
abstractText: Atherosclerosis continues to represent a significant risk underlying many cardiovascular events. Developing clinically adaptable imaging of atherosclerosis could be effective in diagnosing and monitoring the progression of atherosclerosis or its response to therapy. Iron oxide nanoparticles are widely studied as T2-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) contrast agents, generating dark, negative signals. However, their potential as T1-weighted agents-despite the clinical advantages of producing bright, positive signals critical for vascular imaging-has remained largely underexplored, particularly in the context of atherosclerosis. In this work, we report on the development of mannose-functionalized Fe3O4-polyamidoamine (PAMAM) dendrimer nanocomplexes, which possess unusual T1-weighted MRI contrast property. It is confirmed that ultrasmall Fe3O4 nanoparticles under 5 nm are uniformly distributed in the PAMAM matrix and act as "cross linker" forming a complex with a size of 70 nm. This mannose decorated nanocomplex produces an enhanced T1-weighted signal in in vivo studies, with a 12% signal increase in atherosclerotic plaques, indicating its potential clinical use for targeted imaging of atherosclerosis and the development of a theranostic platform.

title: Pancreatic Ischemic Necrosis Caused by Cholesterol Crystal Embolization Following Total Arch Replacement: A Case Report.
authorString: Ami K, Matsumoto M, Nakano M, Nobori C, Yoshida Y, Tai K, Murase T, Takebe A, Kamei K, Matsumoto I.
abstractText:
Introduction

Acute pancreatitis is a recognized but uncommon complication of cardiovascular surgery. Cholesterol crystal embolization (CCE), a systemic ischemic disease, is a rare and potentially overlooked cause of pancreatic injury after cardiovascular surgery. Pancreatic involvement is uncommon, particularly when it progresses to extensive pancreatic necrosis requiring surgery. In this study, we report a case of CCE presenting as recurrent pancreatitis after total arch replacement that progressed to extensive pancreatic ischemic necrosis requiring total pancreatectomy.

Case presentation

A 56-year-old man underwent total arch replacement for thoracic aortic aneurysm and subsequently developed acute pancreatitis with hepatic and renal dysfunction. Although his condition initially improved with conservative management, the pancreatitis recurred approximately 2 months after surgery and progressed to extensive, treatment-refractory pancreatic necrosis. He was referred to our institution approximately 4 months after surgery. CT revealed marked diffuse pancreatic enlargement with patchy low-attenuation areas, findings suggestive of extensive pancreatic necrosis. Because of persistent inflammation, disseminated intravascular coagulation, and deterioration of his general condition, total pancreatectomy was performed as a life-saving measure. Histopathological examination revealed widespread pancreatic necrosis and numerous cholesterol crystal emboli in small intrapancreatic arteries, thus establishing the diagnosis of pancreatic ischemic necrosis caused by CCE. On POD 20, the patient developed hemorrhage from the gastroduodenal artery. Although hemostasis was achieved by transcatheter arterial embolization, the patient subsequently developed septic shock and died on POD 22. Autopsy revealed ascending colon necrosis with cholesterol crystal emboli in small arteries and widespread CCE in other organs, including liver, kidneys, stomach, small intestine, and adrenal glands, demonstrating multiorgan involvement of CCE.

Conclusions

CCE should be considered in the differential diagnosis of unexplained, recurrent, or progressive pancreatitis following cardiovascular surgery or endovascular intervention. Furthermore, multiorgan involvement demonstrated at autopsy highlights that CCE presenting predominantly with pancreatic involvement may also affect other organs, warranting careful assessment for additional organ involvement.

title: Late Post-Bentall Pseudoaneurysm From a Prior Graft De-Airing Site.
authorString: Karacelik M, Saritas B, Turhan S, Sendur H, Yildiz E, Sert C.
abstractText:
Background

Late pseudoaneurysm after Bentall repair usually arises from an anastomosis or coronary button; a focal midgraft defect is uncommon.

Case summary

A 48-year-old man presented during the second postoperative year with retrosternal pressure. Computed tomography angiography showed a 93 × 80 mm pseudoaneurysm with a small midgraft communication and sternal apposition. Femoral cardiopulmonary bypass and cooling to 18 °C preceded controlled resternotomy during 3 minutes of total circulatory arrest. A 5 × 5 mm graft defect at a site consistent with prior graft de-airing was repaired with pledget-reinforced polypropylene sutures. Direct operative inspection confirmed intact graft anastomoses and coronary buttons; cultures were negative.

Discussion

A prior graft puncture may become a late failure site. Retrosternal pseudoaneurysm requires preplanned circulatory control for safe re-entry.

Take-home message

Consider prior graft puncture when the source is midgraft, and establish peripheral circulatory control before high-risk resternotomy.

title: Anesthetic Technique and Hospital Length of Stay in Modern Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
authorString: Whitener GB, Francis LR, Steinberg TB, Whitener SK, Carroll DB, Wolf BJ, Pope NH, Amoroso NS, Zeigler SM, Katz MR, Steinberg DH.
abstractText:
Background

Observational studies have suggested that monitored anesthesia care (MAC) improves hospital throughput in transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), though these findings largely reflect earlier practice patterns with longer hospitalizations, evolving care pathways, and limitations inherent to retrospective designs.

Methods

We conducted a single-center, prospective randomized controlled trial of 170 patients undergoing elective transfemoral TAVR. Patients were randomized 1:1 to MAC or general endotracheal anesthesia (GETA) with intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography. The primary outcomes were hospital length of stay (LOS), 30-day mortality, and intensive care unit (ICU) admission. The secondary outcome was paravalvular regurgitation (PVR). Other prospectively tracked perioperative efficiency metrics included procedure time and operating room time.

Results

There was no significant difference in hospital LOS between the two groups (median difference in LOS, MAC vs GETA: 0.02 days (95% confidence interval [CI], -0.09 to 0.15 days); P = 0.631). There were no 30-day deaths in either group. ICU admission rates (P = 0.634) were similar between arms. No significant differences were observed in PVR rates (P = 0.934), procedure time (P = 0.142), or operating room time (P = 0.439).

Conclusions

In a modern TAVR program, anesthetic technique did not influence hospital LOS or other clinical endpoints during the study. These findings suggest that the efficiency differences previously associated with MAC may not persist in current TAVR practice. Anesthetic choice can be individualized without substantially altering hospital throughput in similar practice settings.

title: Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve Replacement in a 9-Year-Old Boy Using a 48-mm Self-Expanding Transcatheter Bioprosthesis.
authorString: Rajkumar C, Berman D, Nageotte S, Patel D, Hurd CW, Menda J, Thornton G, Nakamura M, Makar M, Zahn E, Makkar R.
abstractText:
Objective

A 9-year-old boy with hypoplastic left ventricle developed severe tricuspid regurgitation and symptomatic right heart failure after complex biventricular conversion. Given 4 prior sternotomies, transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR) was considered. Computed tomography demonstrated severe septal leaflet tethering and posterior leaflet-papillary muscle continuity, limiting leaflet-dependent devices. Our objective was deployment of a self-expanding Intrepid valve that anchors without leaflet capture.

Key steps

A 48-mm Intrepid valve was implanted transfemorally through a 35-F sheath under transesophageal echocardiographic and fluoroscopic guidance, achieving stable positioning and excellent tricuspid regurgitation reduction.

Potential pitfalls

Abnormal anatomy may compromise leaflet-dependent stability. Large-bore venous access requires careful planning in pediatric patients, and post-TTVR anticoagulation is necessary to reduce prosthetic valve thrombosis risk.

Take-home messages

In selected pediatric patients at high surgical risk, TTVR may provide an effective alternative therapy. When leaflet anatomy is unfavorable, devices that anchor independently of leaflet capture may offer a practical solution.

title: Incomplete atrioventricular septal defect as an incidental finding in an African lion (<i>Panthera leo</i>) cub during an acute multi-organ crisis: case report.
authorString: Patil S, Rajhans U, Mhase A, Srivastava G, Nighot N.
abstractText:
Background

Congenital heart defects are reported less often in non-domestic than in domestic species, although reports now span felids, primates, ungulates, and marine mammals. Atrioventricular septal defects (AVSDs), which arise from abnormal development of the endocardial cushions, are among the less frequently reported congenital heart defects in animals.

Case description

A 137-day-old female African lion cub (13.14 kg) was presented with generalized weakness, incoordination, dyspnea, and dehydration. Initial investigations revealed severe hypoglycemia, hemoconcentration, marked hepatocellular and muscle enzyme elevation, hyperkalemia, and an elevated cardiac troponin I concentration (8.9 ng/mL). Transthoracic echocardiography, performed after metabolic stabilization, incidentally identified a 2.2-cm defect in the primum portion of the atrial septum adjacent to the atrioventricular valves, consistent with an incomplete AVSD, with predominant left-to-right shunting and right ventricular volume overload. An agitated saline study additionally demonstrated a right-to-left shunt component. Despite supportive care, the cub developed azotemia and conjugated hyperbilirubinemia and died on day 4. Necropsy confirmed a 2 × 2.5-cm defect extending from the mid-atrial septum to the atrioventricular valves, right heart volume overload, right ventricular interstitial fibrosis, and multi-organ damage.

Conclusion

The incomplete AVSD in this cub was an incidental finding during a systemic illness, and its contribution to the fatal outcome cannot be determined. To the authors' knowledge, this is the first report of an AVSD in a lion.

title: Combined off-pump coronary artery bypass grafting and esophagectomy: a systematic review and patient-level meta-analysis.
authorString: Mylonas KS, Karagkounis T, Stefatou KM, Zoupas I, Ziogas IA, Schizas D, Avgerinos DV, Stavridis GT, Chan JL.
abstractText:
Background

We conducted an individual patient data meta-analysis to evaluate perioperative and long-term outcomes of combined esophagectomy with concomitant off-pump coronary artery bypass grafting (OPES) in patients with concurrent esophageal cancer and coronary artery disease.

Methods

A PRISMA-compliant search was performed up to January 19, 2025, in PubMed, Embase and Cochrane. Time-to-event data were reconstructed using Kaplan-Meier curves from source literature.

Results

A total of 66 patients with concurrent esophageal cancer and critical coronary artery disease underwent OPES. Tumors were located in the esophagus in 69.7% (95% CI: 57.1-80.4%) of the patients and at the esophagogastric junction in 30.3% (19.6-42.8%). A single-incision approach was used in 95.5% (95% CI: 87.3-99.0%) of the cases, with the remainder requiring two incisions. No intraoperative deaths were reported. Pooled 30-day mortality rate was 0.3% (95% CI: 0.0-4.9%) and overall postoperative complication rate was 33.5% (95% CI: 15.5-53.9%). Pooled overall survival rates at one, three, and five years were 95.1% (95% CI: 86.2-98.3%), 74.3% (95% CI: 59.4-83.9%), and 37.7% (95% CI: 21.2-52.3%), respectively, with corresponding disease-free survival rates being 92.4% (95% CI: 81.4-96.1%), 54.8% (95% CI: 38.3-67.6%), and 38.9% (95% CI: 22.4-55.1%).

Conclusions

OPES appears to be a safe and effective procedure for the simultaneous management of esophageal cancer and critical coronary artery disease in selected patients.

title: Untargeted Metabolomics Profiling of Conotruncal Heart Defects Patient-Derived Fibroblasts.
authorString: Andhela LS, Kawathe R, Oza PS, Joshi MB, Uttarilli A, Chinthakindi S.

journal.title: Rapid communications in mass spectrometry : RCM

abstractText:
Rationale

Conotruncal heart defects (CTDs) are severe congenital cardiac malformations whose underlying molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Although the clinical and genetic characteristics of CTDs have been extensively investigated, their metabolomic insights remain poorly characterized. Defining disease-associated metabolic alterations may improve our understanding of CTD pathogenesis.

Methods

Untargeted metabolomic profiling was performed on patient-derived fibroblast cell lines representing tetralogy of Fallot (TOF), DiGeorge syndrome (DGS)-associated transposition of the great arteries, truncus arteriosus (TA), and three age-matched healthy controls. Experiments were performed in biological triplicates. Data acquisition was conducted on Vanquish Horizon UHPLC coupled to an Orbitrap Q Exactive Plus operated in both positive and negative ESI. Data interpretation and statistical analyses were performed using Compound Discoverer 3.3 and MetaboAnalyst 6.0.

Results

Database annotation identified 112, 109, and 101 putative features in TOF, DGS, and TA fibroblasts, respectively. Differential analysis revealed that 35, 33, and 30 features were significantly altered. PCA and volcano plots revealed clear separation between diseased and control fibroblasts. Pathway enrichment analysis demonstrated dysregulation of purine, branched-chain amino acid, vitamin B6, glutathione, and energy metabolism, indicating altered mitochondrial function, redox homeostasis, and nucleotide turnover across all three CTD subtypes.

Conclusions

Untargeted LC-Orbitrap-HRMS metabolomics comprehensively identified metabolic alterations, including both shared and subtype-specific findings, providing insights into metabolic pathways associated with CTDs. These findings may provide a preliminary insight into further research in CTDs pathogenesis.

title: Effects of Iloprost on Nitric Oxide Biomarkers in Patients With Septic Shock and Severe Endotheliopathy.
authorString: Mortensen KM, Itenov TS, Stensballe J, Johansson PI, Perner A, Kristiansen KT, Søe-Jensen P, Clausen NE, Lindhardt A, Hillig T, Jensen CAJ, Bestle MH.
abstractText:
Background

Septic shock is characterized by profound endothelial dysfunction, which may involve changes in the prostacyclin and nitric oxide (NO) pathways and contribute to immune dysregulation, coagulopathy, and vascular instability. Iloprost has shown potential to modulate NO biomarkers in non-septic conditions. We investigated whether treatment with the prostacyclin analog iloprost affected plasma concentrations of the NO biomarkers ADMA, SDMA, arginine, and homoarginine in patients with septic shock and severe endotheliopathy.

Methods

This preplanned sub-study of the randomized, blinded COMBAT-SHINE trial enrolled 274 adult ICU patients with septic shock and severe endotheliopathy (defined as soluble thrombomodulin (sTM) > 10 ng/mL) who had consented to the use of data. Five participants from the full trial population withdrew consent. Participants were allocated to a 72-h infusion of iloprost (1 ng/kg/min) versus placebo. Plasma concentrations of ADMA, SDMA, arginine, and homoarginine were measured at 0, 24, 48, and 72 h. Changes in biomarker concentrations were assessed using linear mixed models, with predefined subgroup analyses. All results were considered exploratory.

Results

In explorative analyses, iloprost treatment, compared with placebo, did not statistically significantly change plasma concentrations of ADMA and SDMA (estimated difference in means -4% (95% CI: -13%, 6%; p = 0.4) and-2% (95% CI: -14%, 10%; p = 0.7), respectively), or plasma concentrations of arginine and homoarginine (estimated difference in means 9% (95% CI: -6%, 27%; p = 0.2) and 17% (95% CI: -3%, 42%; p = 0.10), respectively). None of the NO biomarkers changes over time (0-24 h, 24-48 h, or 48-72 h) differed between the iloprost and placebo groups (all p > 0.3). Findings were consistent across predefined subgroups.

Conclusions

In this sub-study of a randomized clinical trial of adults in the ICU with septic shock and severe endotheliopathy, infusion of iloprost 1 ng/kg/min for 72 h did not affect plasma concentrations of the NO biomarkers ADMA, SDMA, arginine, and homoarginine.

Editorial comment

This substudy of a larger trial of iloprost versus placebo for sepsis outcomes (COMBAT-SHINE trial) examined specifically nitric oxide markers in a septic shock and epithelial injury cohort. Iloprost treatment at the tested dose did not appear to affect markers of nitric oxide measured as ADMA, SDMA, arginine or homoarginine levels.

title: Association Between Myocardial BOLD Reactivity and Peripheral Microvascular Function Assessed by Flow-Mediated Skin Fluorescence.
authorString: Castelein J, Sabisz A, Glińska A, Żarczyńska-Buchowiecka M, Romanowska-Kocejko M, Rygusik M, Hellmann M, Borra RJH, Dorniak K.
abstractText: Cardiac blood oxygen level-dependent (BOLD) MRI during breath-hold provides a contrast-free myocardial-specific readout of vasoreactivity. We tested whether myocardial BOLD reactivity covaries with peripheral microvascular function measured by flow-mediated skin fluorescence (FMSF), thereby assessing concordance between two physiologically distinct vascular beds. Twenty-eight participants underwent a mid-diastolic cardiac BOLD MRI at 1.5 T during end-expiratory breath-hold, alongside forearm FMSF during transient brachial artery occlusion. Participants were classified as having FMSF-normal reactivity (NR) or FMSF-abnormal reactivity (AR) based on predefined FMSF criteria (i.e., one or more of the following: reactive hyperemia response [RHR] < 30% or hypoxia sensitivity [HS] < 25). Heartbeat-to-heartbeat myocardial T<sub>2</sub> and T<sub>2</sub>* slopes (ms/hb) and absolute changes (ΔT<sub>2</sub>, ΔT<sub>2</sub>*) were compared between cohorts and correlated with FMSF parameters. Compared with AR, the NR showed greater T<sub>2</sub> slope (0.1 ± 0.2 vs. -0.2 ± 0.3 ms/hb; p = 0.002), T<sub>2</sub>* slope (0.1 ± 0.2 vs. 0.0 ± 0.1 ms/hb; p = 0.016), ΔT<sub>2</sub> (1.3 ± 2.2 vs. -1.9 ± 2.9 ms; p = 0.003) and ΔT<sub>2</sub>* (2.4 ± 2.8 vs. -0.1 ± 2.1 ms; p = 0.013). After Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction across 44 correlations, IR index correlated with T<sub>2</sub> slope (r = 0.58, q = 0.050), IR max correlated with T<sub>2</sub> slope (r = 0.57, q = 0.050), and HS correlated with ΔT<sub>2</sub>* (r = 0.53, q = 0.050). Interreader reproducibility was good for myocardial BOLD-derived slopes and ΔT<sub>2</sub>* (ICC = 0.80-0.86) and moderate for ΔT<sub>2</sub> (ICC = 0.66). Within this long-COVID cohort, myocardial BOLD reactivity covaried with peripheral microvascular reactivity at the group level. Cardiac BOLD MRI may serve as a myocardial-specific probe of microvascular function within a broader systemic vascular phenotype.

title: Cerebral microvascular vasospasm after stroke and cardiac arrest: mechanisms of no-reflow and therapeutic opportunities.
authorString: Novotny ME, Østergaard L, Granfeldt A, Staehr C.
abstractText: Acute ischaemic stroke and resuscitation after cardiac arrest are often accompanied by persistent cerebral microvascular dysfunction, known as the no-reflow phenomenon, which may contribute to secondary brain injury despite successful macrovascular reperfusion. Although no-reflow is a multifactorial process, microvascular vasospasm may represent a central and potentially modifiable component of the broader microvascular response. Increasing evidence from preclinical studies indicates that microvascular vasospasm arises from a complex interplay between neuronal, glial, endothelial, and mural cell signalling within the neurovascular unit. Key mechanisms include peri-infarct and anoxic spreading depolarisations, endothelin-1- and 20-HETE-mediated vasoconstrictor signalling, and Ca2+ overload in vascular smooth muscle cells and low-order capillary ensheathing pericytes, which together promote sustained vasocontraction and impaired capillary perfusion. In addition, endothelial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and inflammatory processes further exacerbate microvascular dysregulation during ischaemia-reperfusion, potentially impairing glymphatic transport. Experimental imaging studies demonstrate that these mechanisms evolve dynamically over time. While the onset of microvascular vasoconstriction may be similar after stroke and cardiac arrest, the underlying mechanisms driving these changes can differ between these conditions. This review summarises current knowledge of the mechanisms underlying cerebral microvascular vasospasm following cerebral ischaemia-reperfusion and discusses potential therapeutic targets aimed at preventing spreading depolarisation and relaxing vascular smooth muscle cells and pericytes to restore microcirculatory flow after hypoxic-ischaemic brain injury.

title: Haemostasis in Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease.
authorString: Ferdinande K, Senzolo M, Campello E, Simioni P, Zanetto A.

journal.title: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver

abstractText: MASLD is the most prevalent chronic liver disease and a significant cause of liver-related morbidity and mortality. Portal hypertension may develop before advanced fibrosis, driven by vascular and metabolic alterations that concurrently affect systemic haemostasis and promote intrahepatic interactions between endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, and haemostatic pathways. Once cirrhosis is established, the rebalanced haemostatic state is largely independent of aetiology, with impaired fibrinolysis representing the principal MASLD-associated difference. In non-cirrhotic MASLD, increasing in vivo platelet activation, a progressive procoagulant imbalance between factor VIII and protein C, and reduced fibrinolysis, including increased plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 and prolonged clot lysis, have been described, although their attribution to MASLD is complicated by the concomitant metabolic factors. Clinically, MASLD is associated with increased risks of venous thromboembolism, portal vein thrombosis, and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, increasing with disease severity; however, prospective data linking specific haemostatic alterations to incident thrombosis remain lacking. Within the liver, platelets act as central hubs interacting with dysfunctional liver sinusoidal endothelial cells, hepatic stellate cells, Kupffer cells, and hepatocytes, orchestrating platelet-neutrophil crosstalk, neutrophil extracellular trap formation, and coagulation activation, thereby promoting immunothrombosis, hepatic stellate cell activation, microvascular remodelling, and fibrogenesis. Coagulation proteases may additionally contribute to MASLD progression through protease-activated receptor signalling in hepatocytes and hepatic stellate cells. These observations raise the hypothesis that antiplatelet and anticoagulant therapies could modify MASLD progression, although evidence remains predominantly preclinical and observational. This review synthesizes haemostatic balance and thrombotic complications in MASLD, the endothelial-inflammation-haemostasis axis in MASLD progression, and emerging perspectives.

title: The Cardioprotective Effect of Fosinopril on Myocardial Infarction (MI) is Associated With the AMPK/mTOR Pathway.
authorString: Ren PH, Zhang ZM, Tan WL, Zhu HP, Li ZQ.

journal.title: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology

abstractText: To investigate the impact of fosinopril on cardiac function and its regulatory role in autophagy and the AMPK/mTOR pathway in a rat model of myocardial infarction (MI). MI was induced in rats by ligation of the left anterior descending coronary artery. MI modeling was verified by serum cardiac enzyme assays. Cardiac functions and histological change were determined by echocardiography, hematoxylin-eosin (HE) staining, and Masson's trichrome staining. Autophagy-associated factors were evaluated using western blotting and RT-qPCR. Apoptosis was analyzed by TUNEL assay, while alterations in the phosphorylation of the AMPK/mTOR pathway were determined by western blotting. Serum CK-MB and cTn-I levels were significantly elevated in MI rats, confirming myocardial injury. MI rats showed disordered myocardial architecture with inflammatory infiltration, compromised cardiac function (increased left ventricular end-systolic diameter and left ventricular end-diastolic diameter, decreased left ventricular fractional shortening and left ventricular ejection fraction) and myocardial fibrosis. Molecularly, RT-qPCR showed no significant changes in LC3 and p62/SQSTM1 mRNA levels, but Beclin-1 mRNA expression was elevated in MI rats and partially reversed by fosinopril. Western blotting revealed an increased LC3b-II/LC3b-I ratio and Beclin-1 protein expression, as well as decreased p62/SQSTM1 protein expression in MI rats. The TUNEL assay showed elevated apoptotic rates. MI also altered the phosphorylation status of the AMPK/mTOR pathway. Fosinopril reversed these changes except for the mRNA levels of LC3 and p62/SQSTM1. Fosinopril ameliorates MI-induced cardiac dysfunction and myocardial fibrosis. Its cardioprotective effects may be attributed to the regulation of autophagy (via Beclin-1 and other autophagy-related proteins) and apoptosis through normalization of the dysregulated AMPK/mTOR pathway.

title: HIV Co-Infection and Hepatic Outcomes in Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease.
authorString: Hafez Y, Shaik NA, Kilani Y, Ibrahim EA, Gontar A, Nasir AB, Abdelghany O, Cardinale V, Frey LJ, Farmer AD, Syn WK.

journal.title: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver

abstractText:
Background & aims

MASLD affects roughly one-third of people with HIV (PWH), yet data on advanced hepatic outcomes are limited. We examined the association of HIV co-infection with hepatic outcomes in propensity score-matched adults with MASLD.

Methods

Using the TriNetX US Collaborative Network (~114.6 million patients), we identified adults with MASLD stratified by HIV status, excluding viral hepatitis, alcohol-related and other chronic liver diseases. Patients were 1:1 propensity-matched on demographics, BMI, smoking, cardiometabolic comorbidities, laboratory values and medications, then followed for 5 years (Kaplan-Meier, Cox, competing-risk analyses). Primary outcomes were all-cause mortality and a composite hepatic decompensation endpoint (ascites/spontaneous bacterial peritonitis, variceal disease, portal hypertension, hepatic encephalopathy, hepatorenal/hepatopulmonary syndrome or liver transplantation).

Results

After matching (6666 per group), HIV-positive patients had a higher risk of the composite hepatic outcome (HR 1.25, 95% CI 1.04-1.50) and lower all-cause mortality (HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.62-0.88). Individual outcomes, including cirrhosis (HR 1.32, 95% CI 0.98-1.78), were not statistically significant. Severe immunosuppression (CD4 < 200 cells/μL) more than doubled composite hepatic risk (HR 2.11, 95% CI 1.11-4.00), while ART exposure showed no effect (HR 1.00, 95% CI 0.68-1.48). Descriptive competing-risk analyses (unmatched) showed higher cirrhosis incidence despite lower mortality.

Conclusions

After comprehensive metabolic matching, HIV co-infection remained associated with modestly increased composite hepatic decompensation, while individual endpoints such as cirrhosis were attenuated, consistent with residual ascertainment bias from greater healthcare contact. Severe immunosuppression, not ART exposure, identified a high-risk subgroup. These findings support targeted liver surveillance in PWH with MASLD, especially at low CD4 counts.

title: Cardioprotective Potential of 2-(2-Nitrophenyl)-1,3-thiazolidine-4-carboxylic Acid Against Rotenone-Induced Hematological Alterations and Cardiac Oxidative Toxicity in Sprague Dawley Rats.
authorString: Kousar S, Perveen S, Kanwal S, Ajmal I, Haider I, Hameed R, Alsobaie S, Alqarni S, Bakhsh A.

journal.title: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology

abstractText: Rotenone (ROT), a potent mitochondrial complex-I inhibitor, is increasingly associated with systemic biochemical disturbances, including hematological imbalance and oxidative stress-mediated organ toxicity, particularly cardiac injury. The present study evaluated the cardioprotective potential of 2-(2-nitrophenyl)-1,3-thiazolidine-4-carboxylic acid (2,2Np-1,3TZD-4-CA) against ROT-induced hematological and cardiac dysfunctions in rats through biochemical, antioxidant, and histopathological assessments. Forty-two male rats were divided into experimental groups and treated intraperitoneally with ROT (2.5 mg/kg) alone or in combination with 2,2Np-1,3TZD-4-CA at doses of 10 or 30 mg/kg for 21 days. Hematological and serological parameters were evaluated using blood samples, while cardiac tissues were analyzed for oxidative stress biomarkers, including malondialdehyde, superoxide dismutase, and catalase, along with histopathological examination. ROT administration significantly altered hematological indices, elevated lipid peroxidation, and suppressed antioxidant enzyme activities in cardiac tissue (p < 0.05). However, treatment with 2,2Np-1,3TZD-4-CA dose-dependently restored hematological parameters, reduced malondialdehyde levels, and enhanced superoxide dismutase and catalase activities. Histopathological observations further demonstrated substantial attenuation of ROT-induced myocardial damage. These findings suggest that 2,2Np-1,3TZD-4-CA exerts significant protective effects against ROT-induced systemic and cardiac oxidative toxicity, highlighting its pharmacological and protective potential.

title: Innovations in intradialytic hypotension management: pathophysiology, precision monitoring, and emerging therapeutic strategies.
authorString: Bizer B, Thongprayoon C, Kashani K.
abstractText: Intradialytic hypotension (IDH) is one of the most frequent and consequential complications of maintenance hemodialysis, affecting up to 40% of treatments depending on the definition used. IDH is independently associated with myocardial stunning, cerebral hypoperfusion, loss of residual kidney function, vascular access failure, and increased mortality. Despite extensive investigation, heterogeneity in diagnostic criteria, incomplete mechanistic understanding, and reliance on intermittent blood pressure measurements continue to limit prevention and management. We performed a narrative review of clinical trials, observational studies, systematic reviews, and guideline statements addressing intradialytic hypotension in adult hemodialysis populations. Evidence was synthesized across pathophysiologic mechanisms, monitoring strategies, and therapeutic approaches, including conventional and digital health interventions. IDH arises from an interplay of ultrafiltration-plasma refill mismatch, impaired vascular responses, reduced cardiac reserve, osmotic and thermal shifts, and medication effects. Epidemiologic estimates vary due to inconsistent definitions, although a nadir systolic blood pressure below 90 mmHg shows the strongest and consistent association with mortality. Traditional intermittent cuff-based blood pressure monitoring underestimates the burden and severity of IDH. Advanced monitoring approaches, including continuous noninvasive blood pressure measurement, volume assessment tools, and integrated dialysis machine feedback systems, enable improved detection of subclinical and evolving hypotension. Recent machine learning and artificial intelligence models leveraging clinical and real-time intradialytic data demonstrate strong performance for IDH prediction and support individualized ultrafiltration and dry weight optimization. Overall, IDH remains a multifactorial and under-recognized driver of morbidity in hemodialysis patients, and integration of precision monitoring with AI-enabled analytics may improve hemodynamic stability and clinical outcomes.

title: Clinical Outcomes Associated With Routine Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in Patients With Coronary Artery Disease Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
authorString: Alwaily ZA, De SK, Alowami M, Mohamed MA, Thirupathy U, Ibraheem MR, Sheen AI, Ur Rahman O, Amladi A, Malik J, Hassan EIE, Ahsan A, Noor L.
abstractText: The optimal strategy for managing concomitant coronary artery disease (CAD) in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) remains uncertain. We performed an updated meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with conservative or deferred management in patients with CAD undergoing TAVI. Major electronic databases were systematically searched for eligible RCTs. Risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using a random-effects model, with sensitivity analyses performed to assess robustness and explore the influence of individual studies on heterogeneity. Three RCTs were included. Routine PCI was not associated with a significant reduction in mortality or major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events compared with conservative or deferred management. However, PCI was associated with significantly higher risks of major bleeding (RR, 1.57; 95% CI, 1.06-2.33; P = 0.02) and any bleeding (RR, 1.77; 95% CI, 1.27-2.48; P < 0.001), while urgent revascularization was less frequent with PCI. Sensitivity analyses demonstrated that individual studies influenced heterogeneity for selected outcomes, although the overall findings remained broadly consistent. Among patients with CAD undergoing TAVI, this pooled analysis of the available randomized evidence shows that an unselective, routine strategy of PCI does not reduce mortality, myocardial infarction, or major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events compared with a conservative or deferred strategy, while increasing bleeding and reducing the subsequent need for urgent revascularization. Rather than indicating that coronary intervention is unnecessary, these findings clarify the precision and consistency of this tradeoff across the available trials and support a selective, individualized strategy in which PCI is reserved for clinically or physiologically significant coronary disease rather than performed routinely on the basis of angiographic appearance alone.

title: Prognostic Impact of Serum Magnesium Levels in Heart Failure: Updated Evidence From a Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Khraisat O, Muhammad H, Abakar AO, Ortega G, Diab I, Khraisat A, Khouday C, Batiha A, Patel D, Pietrandrea P, Tayeb T, Gregorio J, Balla S.
abstractText: Heart failure (HF) carries high morbidity and mortality, and the prognostic role of serum magnesium remains unclear. This updated systematic review and meta-analysis assessed associations between magnesium abnormalities and outcomes in HF. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane were searched through March 2026 for observational cohorts, registries, and post hoc randomized controlled trial analyses in adults with HF. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality; secondary outcomes were HF hospitalization and cardiovascular (CV) mortality. Random-effects models pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Risk of bias was assessed using the Quality in Prognosis Studies tool and the revised Cochrane Risk-of-Bias Tool for Randomized Trials. Twelve studies including 648,602 patients were analyzed. Hypermagnesemia was associated with higher all-cause mortality (RR 1.38, 95% CI 1.32-1.44; I2 = 6%), HF hospitalization (RR 1.30, 95% CI 1.11-1.51; I2 = 81%), and CV mortality (RR 1.41, 95% CI 1.19-1.66; I2 = 42%). Hypomagnesemia was associated with modestly higher all-cause mortality (RR 1.15, 95% CI 1.01-1.31; I2 = 70%), with no significant association with HF hospitalization or CV death. Associations were consistent across studies published before and after 2010 and between observational cohorts and post hoc trial analyses, with no significant subgroup differences. The association between hypermagnesemia and all-cause mortality was unchanged after excluding the largest study (RR 1.38, 95% CI 1.25-1.53; I2 = 13%). Serum magnesium abnormalities, especially hypermagnesemia, are associated with worse outcomes in HF. Hypomagnesemia shows a smaller, less consistent association. Because hypermagnesemia may largely reflect renal dysfunction and greater disease severity, these findings represent prognostic associations rather than evidence of causality; prospective studies should determine whether monitoring or correcting magnesium abnormalities improves HF outcomes.

title: Remote Endocrinology Support for Primary Care Clinicians Managing Type 2 Diabetes: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials
authorString: Alshehri A, Naif Al-Dahmashi D, Safaq Al-Dahmashi F, Taif Al-Dahmashi R, Atallah Alanazi D, Atallah Alenazi Y, Khalid Alanazi R, Mohammed Al-Anazi S, Ayed Al-Anazi A, Hamoud Al-Anazi S, Naif A. Alanazi R, Inad S. Alanazi S, Alenezi S, Talal S. Alanazi S, Saad Zaid Alanazi F.

title: Comparative efficacy of different digital technologies in adults with insomnia: a systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
authorString: Wang X, Zhao Y, Wang L, Du C, Ding K, Wen Q, Liang W, He T.

title: Effect of Cysteamine on 90-Day Mortality in Patients With Severe Community-Acquired Pneumonia: The REMAP-CAP (Randomized Embedded Multifactorial Adaptive Platform for Community-Acquired Pneumonia) Randomized Clinical Trial.
authorString: Shankar-Hari M, Ryan EG, Pogson D, Golden D, Puxty K, Walden A, Craven TH, Derde L, Gordon AC, Randomized Embedded Multifactorial Adaptive Platform for Community-Acquired Pneumonia Investigators.
abstractText: Cysteamine has antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory and antibiotic-potentiating effects. We evaluated IV cysteamine in critically ill patients with community-acquired pneumonia within REMAP-CAP (Randomized Embedded Multifactorial Adaptive Platform for Community-Acquired Pneumonia) trial, an international adaptive platform trial evaluating multiple interventions across several therapeutic domains. Adults requiring respiratory or cardiovascular organ support were randomized within the cysteamine domain to IV cysteamine (5 mg/kg every 8 hr for up to 10 d) or control. The dichotomous primary outcome was 90-day all-cause mortality, analyzed using Bayesian logistic regression. Recruitment to this domain stopped for operational futility before predefined statistical thresholds were met. Thirty-six patients received cysteamine (n = 19) or control (n = 17). Ninety-day mortality was 26% vs. 35%, respectively (odds ratio 0.64, 95% credible interval 0.18-2.19), with a 76% posterior probability of benefit. One serious adverse event occurred, unrelated to cysteamine. These preliminary findings suggest possible benefit, but the small sample size precludes definitive efficacy conclusions. Further studies of cysteamine in severe pneumonia are warranted.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Revefenacin Versus Glycopyrronium in Indian Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) Patients: A Randomized, Active-Controlled, Phase III Trial
authorString: Ahuja A, Jain M, Sahoo S, Honnavar S, Shukla A, Verma S, Patel C, Patel B, Reddy D, Someshwar A, Parmar D, Kansagra K, Pathak H.

title: The Role of Osteopontin in the Progression and Prognosis of Coronary Artery Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Bi JJ, Yu W, Song L, Hu YM, Wang SH, Huang XC.
abstractText: Individuals with coronary artery disease (CAD) have a high residual cardiovascular risk. Osteopontin (OPN) may be involved in CAD progression, but its prognostic value remains unclear. This meta-analysis appraised the association between circulating OPN and clinical outcomes in CAD. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library were retrieved up to April 9, 2026. Cohort or cross-sectional studies were included. Random- or fixed-effects models were employed to pool hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Heterogeneity was assessed utilizing I2, and leave-one-out sensitivity analysis was performed. Nine prospective cohort studies (6955 CAD patients) were included. Elevated OPN levels were associated with an increased risk of major adverse cardiovascular events in continuous (HR = 1.23, 95% CI: 1.06-1.43) and categorical analyses (HR = 1.54, 95% CI: 1.02-2.32), with substantial heterogeneity in both analyses. Continuous OPN was associated with all-cause mortality (HR = 1.05, 95% CI: 1.02-1.08), while no association was observed for categorical OPN. High OPN increased risks of recurrent myocardial infarction (HR = 2.25, 95% CI: 1.44-3.51) and heart failure readmission (HR = 2.36, 95% CI: 1.65-3.39). OPN showed no significant association with cardiovascular mortality. Sensitivity analysis revealed limited stability of pooled major adverse cardiovascular events estimates for categorical OPN. In conclusion, circulating OPN may have potential value in predicting some adverse outcomes in CAD patients, and its predictive efficacy varies by outcome type and definitions of OPN. Given high heterogeneity and unstable estimates in some analyses, standardized prospective studies are needed to validate this finding.
