title: Left Atrial Stiffness Index and Prognosis Across Heart Failure Phenotypes in Acute Heart Failure: Insights from the STRATS-AHF Registry.
authorString: Lee JH, Park JH, Hwang IC, Park JJ, Park JB, Cho GY.
abstractText:
Aims

The left atrial stiffness index (LASI), calculated as mitral E/e' divided by LA reservoir strain, reflects atrial myopathy and elevated filling pressure but has been studied mainly in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF). We examined whether LASI predicts all-cause mortality and HF hospitalization, and adds to established risk factors, across HF phenotypes in acute heart failure (AHF).

Methods and results

We analyzed 3,133 patients with AHF from the multicenter STRATS-AHF registry, classified by LVEF into HFrEF, HFmrEF, and HFpEF. During a median follow-up of 32.5 months, 616 (19.7%) had HF admissions, and 1,281 (40.9%) died. After adjustment, each doubling of LASI was associated with mortality (HR 1.13, 95% CI 1.08-1.19), as was LASI above the exploratory cutoff of 1.0 (HR 1.27, 95% CI 1.11-1.46). The association was similar across phenotypes (P for interaction = 0.65) and extended to HF hospitalization and the composite of death or HF hospitalization. LASI added modestly to established predictors; after adjustment for NT-proBNP, its association was not significant in patients with a measured value (HR 1.03, 95% CI 0.97-1.10) but persisted after multiple imputation in the whole cohort (HR 1.10, 95% CI 1.04-1.15).

Conclusion

In patients hospitalized for AHF, a higher LASI independently predicted all-cause mortality and HF hospitalization across HF phenotypes. Obtained from the admission echocardiogram, LASI captures an atrial component of risk that LVEF does not reflect, although part of this information overlaps with that of NT-proBNP; whether it can guide management remains to be tested.

title: Dual Pathway Modulation with SGLT2 Inhibitors and Aldosterone Synthase Inhibitors in Cardio-Kidney Disease: Rationale and Trial Design of the EASi Program.
authorString: Fioretti F, Böhm M, Bozkurt B, Costanzo MR, Dinh W, Rossello X, Lund LH, Mentz RJ, Petrie MC, Pitt B, Prochaska JH, Shah SJ, Taub PR, Viethen T, Butler J.
abstractText: Cardio-kidney diseases share interconnected pathophysiology where renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) overactivation drives pathologic hemodynamic, neurohormonal, inflammatory, and fibrotic changes leading to progressive cardiac and kidney dysfunction. Current RAAS-modulating therapies are limited by residual RAAS risk and aldosterone breakthrough despite angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor or angiotensin receptor blocker therapy, incomplete blockade of aldosterone with mineralocorticoid receptor (MR) antagonists, hyperkalemia, and suboptimal implementation. Aldosterone synthase inhibitors (ASi) act upstream of the MR to lower aldosterone production, modulating both MR-dependent and MR-independent aldosterone effects without competing for receptor occupancy. Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) reduce adverse cardiovascular and kidney events through cellular, hemodynamic and metabolic effects. The complementary mechanisms of SGLT2i/ASi (SASi) may provide improved cardio-kidney protection. The EASi program will determine whether SASi therapy, added to background guideline-directed therapy including an ACE inhibitor, ARB, or ARNI as appropriate, can improve cardiovascular and kidney outcomes beyond SGLT2 inhibitor monotherapy. EASi-PROTKT (∼11,800 participants) evaluates prevention of incident heart failure events or cardiovascular death in patients with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and established cardiovascular disease. EASi-HF Preserved (∼6,000) and EASi-HF Reduced (∼4,200) evaluate cardiovascular death and first heart failure events across the LVEF spectrum. EASi-KIDNEY (∼11,000) evaluates kidney disease progression and cardiovascular endpoints in chronic kidney disease patients with and without type 2 diabetes. EASi-SYNC (∼500) is a Phase 2 trial comparing SASi versus staggered initiation of SGLT2i and ASi in patients with CKD. Together, these trials will enroll >33,000 participants and test whether SASi can redefine standard of care across the cardio-kidney disease spectrum.

title: Design and rationale of a prospective cohort study integrating cardiovascular, metabolic, and cognitive outcomes across the spectrum of chronic kidney disease: the Vasc-CKD study.
authorString: Neofytou IE, Roumeliotis A, Roumeliotis S, Arampatzis S, Sgouropoulou V, Varouktsi G, Tsinari A, Stamou A, Kontogiorgos I, Leivaditis K, Kocic G, Veljkovic A, Bittner R, Jaminon A, Schurgers LJ, Liakopoulos V.
abstractText: We present the study design and protocol of a single-center, prospective cohort study in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) (n = 497). The objective of this study is to provide an integrated and comprehensive characterization of cardiovascular disease, oxidative stress, mineral and bone disorder, vascular calcification propensity, and cognitive function across the full spectrum of CKD, including non-dialysis CKD, hemodialysis, and peritoneal dialysis. Participants will be followed systematically for two years, with the collection of hard clinical endpoints, including major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), initiation of dialysis, and all-cause mortality.Previous research in CKD has largely examined these domains in isolation-for example, studies focusing on arterial stiffness and cognitive decline, or investigations into the prognostic value of individual biomarkers of calcification and mineral metabolism, such as fibroblast growth factor-23, fetuin-A, or matrix GLA protein (MGP), for cardiovascular outcomes and renal disease progression. In contrast, the present protocol is designed to integrate these interrelated pathophysiological pathways within a single, unified framework.This protocol provides a transparent methodological reference for planned longitudinal and nested analyses arising from this large cohort. By capturing various phenotypic data across CKD stages, it aims to enhance understanding of the interactions between cardiovascular pathology, metabolic disturbances, and cognitive impairment in CKD. If the proposed associations are confirmed, the resulting dataset may support improved risk stratification, facilitate the identification of high-risk phenotypes, and generate testable hypotheses for future interventional studies targeting oxidative stress, vascular calcification propensity, or arterial stiffness in the CKD population.

title: Structural insights into three key platelet receptors for the discovery and development of anti-thrombotic therapies: PAR-1, αIIbβ3, and GPVI.
authorString: Slater A.
abstractText: Cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of mortality worldwide and is strongly driven by thrombosis, which underlies events including stroke, myocardial infarction, pulmonary embolism, and deep vein thrombosis. Platelets are anucleate cell fragments produced by megakaryocytes that are essential for haemostasis but also make major contributions to pathological thrombosis. Although platelet receptors are major targets for antithrombotic therapy, current agents remain limited by bleeding risk, and no new antiplatelet drug has been approved since Cangrelor in 2015. The present review focuses on three structurally and mechanistically distinct platelet receptors with major relevance to drug discovery: PAR1, integrin αIIbβ3, and glycoprotein VI. These receptors represent key nodes spanning the G protein-coupled receptor, integrin, and immunoglobulin superfamily classes, and recent structural studies have clarified their activation mechanisms and drug-binding modes. I highlight how these insights have informed current inhibitors and are guiding the development of safer next-generation antithrombotic therapies. Finally, advancements in studying protein structure and their future impacts on drug design and optimisation are discussed.

title: Elevated blood pressure is independently associated with atherosclerosis in asymptomatic, low-risk individuals.
authorString: Devesa A, García-Lunar I, Rossello X, Oliva B, Moreno-Arciniegas A, Pérez-García CN, Mendieta G, Pizarro G, Gómez-Talavera S, Mass V, Pérez-Herreras C, Bernal JA, McEvoy JW, Fernández-Ortiz A, Sanchez-Gonzalez J, García-Alvarez A, Ibanez B, Fuster V.
abstractText:
Aims

In 2024 European Society of Cardiology (ESC) Guidelines, treatment recommendations for elevated blood pressure (BP) are based primarily on SCORE2 estimated cardiovascular risk. Screening for silent atherosclerosis is recommended (class IIb) to guide treatment decisions only in individuals with an intermediate SCORE2 (5-<10%). Those with SCORE2 < 5% are not recommended for pharmacological intervention. Whether elevated BP is associated with silent atherosclerosis (a known independent predictor of mortality) in low-risk individuals (<5%) is unknown. This study aimed to evaluate atherosclerosis across BP categories in asymptomatic, low-risk individuals from the Progression of Early Subclinical Atherosclerosis (PESA) study.

Methods and results

PESA participants not receiving antihypertensive medications were included. Participants underwent screening of carotid and femoral atherosclerosis (3D vascular ultrasound), as well as coronary calcium scoring (CACS, by non-contrast CT) at enrollment and at 6 years follow-up. Office BP at enrollment was categorized according to the 2024 ESC guidelines as non-elevated (<120/70 mmHg), elevated (120-139/70-89 mmHg), and hypertension (≥140/90 mmHg). Global plaque volume (GPV) was defined as the sum of bilateral carotid and femoral plaque burden. Progression of plaque or CACS was calculated as the change between baseline and follow-up. A total of 3833 participants (45.5 ± 4.2 years, 61% male) were included. 1619 had non-elevated BP, 2041 had elevated BP, and 173 had hypertension. Mean SCORE2 was 2%, and 94% of the cohort had a SCORE2 < 5% (94% in those with elevated BP). Among individuals with elevated BP, 49% had peripheral atherosclerosis, and 22% had CAC. Compared with the non-elevated BP group, and after adjusting for age, sex, and other cardiovascular risk factors, elevated BP was significantly associated with higher prevalence of peripheral atherosclerosis, greater GPV, and greater atherosclerosis progression over 6 years. Similar associations were observed in the hypertension group. Within the elevated BP group, individuals at the lower end of the range (120-129/70-79 mmHg) had increased peripheral atherosclerosis but not CACS, while those at the higher end (130-139/80-89 mmHg) showed both higher prevalence of peripheral atherosclerosis and CACS.

Conclusion

In this low-risk, asymptomatic population, elevated BP was independently associated with greater atherosclerosis burden and progression. While peripheral atherosclerosis was higher across the entire spectrum of elevated BP, CACS was only significantly higher in individuals in the higher-end values of BP. Silent atherosclerosis determination provides complementary information to conventional risk assessment in individuals with elevated BP and a low SCORE2.

title: Impact of nationwide resident mass resignation on clinical outcomes of patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction in a metropolitan area: a retrospective observational study.
authorString: Kim Y, Moon S, Ahn JY, Ryoo HW, Jung H, Lee DE, Lee D, Oh J, Kim JH, Lee SH, Kim G.
abstractText: We evaluated the emergency treatment processes and in-hospital outcomes of patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) during the nationwide mass resignation of residents that began in South Korea in 2024. This multicenter retrospective observational study compared adult patients with STEMI who presented to five hospitals with regional or local emergency medical centers in Daegu during March to December 2023 (pre-resignation) and 2024 (resignation period). Extensively incomplete records and documented onset-to-door intervals >72 hours were excluded. Treatment intervals, procedures, hospital length of stay, and mortality were compared between the periods. Among 692 patients (446 pre-resignation; 246 resignation period), the median emergency medical services scene arrival-to-hospital arrival interval increased from 20.5 to 29 minutes (p<0.01). The median door-to-balloon time and emergency department length of stay decreased from 81 to 72 minutes and from 135 to 62 minutes, respectively (both p<0.01). Coronary angiography was performed in 95.7% and 92.7% of patients, respectively (p=0.09). The hospital length of stay and onset-to-balloon time did not differ significantly between groups. In-hospital mortality was 36/446 (8.1%) versus 16/245 (6.5%; p=0.46), respectively; the absolute difference was -1.5 percentage points (95% confidence interval, -5.4 to 2.9). These findings suggest the preservation of core in-hospital STEMI care among patients who reach participating hospitals. Unadjusted comparisons and limited deaths preclude conclusions regarding equivalent survival or regional access to care.

title: Osteoporosis is associated with higher five-year surgical complication rates after total shoulder arthroplasty.
authorString: Carroll D, Duncan P, Rogalski B, Ponce B, Eichinger J, Friedman R.
abstractText: Existing retrospective studies of total shoulder arthroplasty (TSA) in patients with osteoporosis are limited by short follow-up and small cohorts and may underestimate long-term complications. The purpose of this study is to evaluate the association between osteoporosis and medical and surgical complications after primary TSA. Of 99,028 patients who underwent primary TSA between January 2010 and April 2018, 13,138 had a preoperative diagnosis of osteoporosis and 85,890 did not. Patients with osteoporosis were older, more often female, and more comorbid. Kaplan-Meier analysis compared the cumulative incidence of surgical outcomes, and multivariable Cox models adjusted for age, sex, and Charlson Comorbidity Index compared complications. Patients with osteoporosis had a higher five year risk of revision TSA (3.59% vs. 3.29%; HR: 1.26; 95% CI: 1.13-1.39; p < 0.001), with higher risks of periprosthetic fracture (HR: 1.26; 95% CI: 1.06-1.50; p = 0.008) and mechanical loosening (HR: 1.19; 95% CI: 1.05-1.36; p = 0.006), and a borderline association with dislocation (HR: 1.12; 95% CI: 1.00-1.26; p = 0.049). Medical complications were also increased, including deep vein thrombosis (HR: 1.20; 95% CI: 1.10-1.31), pulmonary embolism (HR: 1.20; 95% CI: 1.09-1.33), pneumonia (HR: 1.13; 95% CI: 1.06-1.21), fluid and electrolyte imbalance (HR: 1.47; 95% CI: 1.27-1.71), transfusion (HR: 1.21; 95% CI: 1.10-1.34), urinary tract infection (HR: 1.19; 95% CI: 1.15-1.23), and myocardial infarction (HR: 1.15; 95% CI: 1.04-1.28). A preoperative diagnosis of osteoporosis is associated with a higher 5-year risk of revision, periprosthetic fracture, and mechanical loosening after primary TSA.

title: Suspected Incidental Release of Cardiac Tamponade From Chest Compressions in a Dog.
authorString: Alfonso Castro A, Shugg R.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: J Vet Emerg Crit Care (San Antonio)
journal.title: Journal of veterinary emergency and critical care (San Antonio, Tex. : 2001)
journal.isoabbreviation: J Vet Emerg Crit Care (San Antonio)

abstractText: To describe the clinical presentation, management, and outcome of a dog with suspected pericardial effusion and cardiac tamponade that may have been released with chest compressions during CPR. A dog was presented to a primary care veterinarian for dyspnea. Thoracic radiographs showed a globoid cardiac silhouette and no pleural effusion. The dog was transferred immediately to a referral veterinary hospital and was unresponsive and pulseless on arrival. Chest compressions were commenced as part of CPR, and return of spontaneous circulation was achieved. Thoracic radiographs after return of spontaneous circultation showed a more normal-appearing cardiac silhouette and new pleural effusion. An echocardiogram showed a right auricular mass. The dog died at home approximately 48 h after initial presentation. This report describes the first known case of suspected incidental release of cardiac tamponade temporally associated with chest compressions in a dog.

title: Global reporting of Brugada syndrome in VigiBase®: A disproportionality analysis.
authorString: Schoretsanitis G, Crettol S, Ansermot N, Maurizi N, Girardin FR, Paulzen M, Raschi E.
abstractText:
Background

Brugada syndrome (BrS) represents a rare but potentially malignant cardiac channelopathy, which may be precipitated by drugs, although data mainly derive from case reports/series.

Objective

To describe the global reporting of BrS with drugs, including co-occurrence patterns, and identify novel potential associations.

Methods

We used VigiBase® to perform descriptive and disproportionality analyses. The reporting odds ratio (ROR) and Bayesian information component (IC) with relevant 95% confidence/credibility intervals (95% CI) were used as disproportionality measures to identify signals of disproportionate reporting (SDR). We performed a network analysis to assess the co-occurrence patterns of related medications based on Jaccard similarity.

Results

We included 544 deduplicated cases of BrS (94.7% serious events, 30.9% females, median time to onset of 30 days, 40.8% physician-reported, 63% from North America), with bupropion (n = 50), nortriptyline (n = 40) and flecainide (n = 34) as most frequently reported suspected drugs. Among 39 drugs with at least four reports, 32 emerged with an SDR, of which 17 were not listed in the BrS website (http://www.brugadadrugs.org), such as clozapine and loperamide (often overdosed). The co-occurrence network included 17 medications, regardless of the labelled role (suspected, interacting or concomitant), with a total of 12 potential co-occurrences; fentanyl exhibited the highest closeness centrality (1.0), whereas the strongest co-occurrence was reported between bupropion and nortriptyline (Jaccard similarity of 0.31).

Conclusions

Notwithstanding limitations related to pharmacovigilance and the complex BrS pathophysiology, we identified 32 medications with over-reporting of BrS, including 17 drugs not listed in the BrS website as well as clusters in affective disorders and anaesthesia.

title: Surgical Treatment of Superior Mesenteric Arteriovenous Fistula after an Unsuccessful Endovascular Approach: A Case Report.
authorString: Huaccha-Rodríguez JP, Coaguila Charres AM.
abstractText: A superior mesenteric arteriovenous fistula (SMAVF) is an uncommon connection between the superior mesenteric artery and vein, usually secondary to surgery or trauma. Manifestations range from abdominal pain to portal hypertension. Although endovascular management is often preferred, surgery may be required in complex cases. We report the case of a 40-year-old male with a history of two laparotomies who presented with an acute abdomen. Computed tomography revealed aneurysmal venous dilation, and arteriography confirmed an SMAVF. After an unsuccessful attempt at endovascular coil embolization due to the high-flow shunt, the fistula was successfully closed by surgical ligation. Open surgery remains a definitive and effective option when an endovascular approach is unsuccessful, unavailable, or unsuitable.

title: Reduced papillary muscle uptake on stress 13N-ammonia PET is associated with higher myocardial flow reserve and may reflect relative tracer distribution.
authorString: Tanaka I, Kiriyama T, Imai S, Kobayashi R, Hayashi N, Kanaya K, Hayashi H, Kumita SI.
abstractText: Reduced papillary muscle tracer uptake on stress 13N-ammonia myocardial perfusion PET is common, but its physiological basis remains unclear. We investigated the association between papillary muscle uptake patterns and quantitative myocardial perfusion parameters. This retrospective study included 63 patients with known or suspected ischemic heart disease (mean age: 74 ± 10 years; 45 men) who underwent rest-stress 13N-ammonia PET. Patients were classified into fixed and reduced papillary muscle uptake groups by visual assessment. Global, remote, and papillary muscle-adjacent myocardial blood flow (MBF) and myocardial flow reserve (MFR) were compared between the groups. Multivariable logistic regression assessed the association between reduced papillary muscle uptake and remote MFR after adjustment for left ventricular (LV) geometry and function. Reduced papillary muscle uptake was associated with higher global and remote MFR and higher remote stress MBF. Remote MFR showed the most pronounced group difference (2.00 ± 0.34 vs. 1.71 ± 0.57; P < 0.001). Papillary muscle-adjacent stress MBF and MFR were significantly higher in the reduced papillary muscle uptake group. In multivariable analyses, the association between higher remote MFR and reduced papillary muscle uptake remained positive after separate adjustment for left ventricular end-diastolic volume (LVEDV), left ventricular end-systolic volume, and left ventricular ejection fraction and remained significant after adjustment for LVEDV. Reduced papillary muscle uptake during stress on 13N-ammonia PET was associated with higher remote and papillary muscle-adjacent MFR. These findings support relative tracer distribution during hyperemia as a plausible explanation, and LV geometry and function may also contribute.

title: Associations of ambulatory and office blood pressure profiles with left ventricular geometric remodeling in children with primary hypertension.
authorString: Li YY, Lin Y, Liu YY, Liu Y, Li YQ, Zhang J, Jiang H, Shi L.
abstractText:
The purpose of this study is to evaluate the associations of office and ambulatory blood pressure (BP) parameters with left ventricular (LV) geometry in pediatric primary hypertension. In this retrospective cross-sectional study, 322 children with primary hypertension were enrolled. LV geometry was classified using LV mass index and age-adjusted relative wall thickness (RWT) into four categories: normal geometry, concentric remodeling, eccentric hypertrophy, and concentric hypertrophy. Multivariable logistic regression (adjusted for BMI Z-score) evaluated associations of office and ambulatory BP parameters, including the office - daytime BP difference, with LV geometry. Within the subgroup with abnormal RWT, concentric hypertrophy was compared with concentric remodeling, and an interaction model assessed whether the association of the difference with LV mass index differed by RWT status. Of 322 children (age 13.0 [11.0, 14.0] years; 78.3% boys), 56 had abnormal LV geometry: 31 concentric remodeling, 16 eccentric hypertrophy, and 9 concentric hypertrophy. Concentric remodeling was associated with higher ambulatory BP, particularly diastolic BP, whereas concentric hypertrophy was associated with office BP indices but no ambulatory BP measure. Among 40 children with abnormal RWT, the office - daytime BP difference was associated with concentric hypertrophy rather than concentric remodeling, and with LV mass index in children with abnormal but not normal RWT (interaction P < 0.001), also after adjustment for office BP.

Conclusion

In children with primary hypertension, concentric remodeling was associated with higher ambulatory BP, while concentric hypertrophy was associated with office BP and the office - daytime BP difference. Assessing the office - daytime difference alongside ambulatory BP parameters may help identify children with abnormal LV geometry.

What is known

• Elevated blood pressure in childhood is linked to left ventricular hypertrophy, but studies rarely separate concentric remodeling from eccentric and concentric hypertrophy.

What is new

• In 322 Chinese children with hypertension, concentric remodeling was associated with ambulatory blood pressure, while concentric hypertrophy was associated with the office-daytime blood pressure difference, a measure not previously examined in relation toleft ventricular geometry in children.

title: Association of exogenous irisin treatment with DWORF micropeptide expression in the cardiac muscle of a diet-induced obese mouse model.
authorString: Rahman TU, Rasool A, Ullah K, Alwaili MA, Al-Hoshani N, Nabi G.

journal.title: Pflugers Archiv : European journal of physiology

abstractText: Irisin is expressed in the cardiac muscle, which promotes the browning of white adipose tissue, enhancing thermogenesis and energy expenditure, and DWORF (Dwarf Open Reading Frame) regulates cardiac muscle contractility. This study aims to investigate the cardiac muscle expression of irisin and DWORF micropeptide in the diet-induced obese (DIO) mouse model (500 µg/kg irisin; 04 weeks old) and explored their expression after irisin administration. A DIO mouse model was developed by feeding a high-fat diet (HFD-feeding: 10 weeks). We observed that a prolonged HFD does not significantly affect serum irisin and cardiac muscle expression in the DIO group. However, after exogenous irisin administration, a reduced body weight and a high serum irisin level were observed. Furthermore, DIO mice show decreased levels of DWORF protein expression and mRNA level in the cardiac muscles however, after irisin administration into the DIO mice, we noticed a significant increase in the expression of DWORF micropeptide in the cardiac muscle at proteins and mRNA levels. Based on our findings, we concluded that the possible stimulatory effect of irisin on the DWORF micropeptide and its potential to reduce body weight could contribute significantly to therapeutic strategies in the future.

title: Gender Representation in Leadership of Pediatric Hospital Subspecialty Organizations.
authorString: Sharpe HJ, Li J, Davis A, Allan JM, Kim JL, Patel MD, Purkey NJ, Han P, Chitkara R, Machut K.
abstractText: Equity in leadership of hospital-based pediatric organizations at the national level is essential to supporting a diverse workforce and patient population. To determine the gender representation of women on leadership committees and boards of external organizations compared with their representation in the workforce of neonatal-perinatal medicine, pediatric critical care medicine, pediatric hospital medicine, and pediatric cardiac critical care. Cross-sectional observational study of publicly available data in 2024. Primary outcome was representation of women in external leadership of selected subspecialties. Measures included demographic and institutional variables of American Board of Pediatrics (ABP) and external leadership organizations. A total of 771 individuals across 41 external organizations were included. Women constituted 54% of these ABP-certified hospital-based subspecialists and 47.7% of identified leaders (P < .05). The representation of women was 45.5% after excluding nonphysician leaders. Women represented 35% of those holding "top seats," including president, chair, editor-in-chief, or equivalent titles. Of the categories of external organizations, women were least likely to be represented as leaders of research-oriented organizations at 42.8%. We were unable to determine the candidacy or selection process for leadership for more than 70% of the organizations. Among this subset, only 42.7% of leaders were women. Women pediatric physicians were significantly underrepresented in external leadership positions compared with the workforce in an aggregate of hospital-based subspecialties. A lack of transparency in leadership selection may contribute to gender inequities in leadership. Opportunities exist for promoting leadership that is representative of the workforce.

title: Cross-Sectional Study of Multiple Sclerosis Nurse Care in Australia: Care Provision, Value, Estimated Avoided Costs, and Recommendations-Part 2.
authorString: Campbell JA, Chen J, Bardsley B, Shapland S, Burke T, McKay F, Taylor BV, van der Mei I.
abstractText:
Background

In Australia, multiple sclerosis specialist nurses (MSSNs) are an integral part of the multidisciplinary health care team; however, their numbers have decreased in recent years. Few data exist on the care MSSNs provide and the cost-saving measures associated with their services. Our aim was to describe the provision and value of MSSN care and to estimate potential avoided costs.

Methods

Cross-sectional survey data on MSSN care (provider, length of care, contact frequency, consultation types and satisfaction, and support types) and perceived value and effects were collected in 2020 from 1417 Australians with MS. Descriptive analysis was used, and potential avoided costs were estimated.

Results

Most respondents reported that MSSN care was somewhat or very helpful (78%, 522 of 667). The most frequent support types related to information about and management of MS symptoms and treatments and their side effects. Not having MSSN care access would have resulted in more general practitioner (21.2%, 147 of 693) or neurologist (21.1%, 146 of 693) appointments and hospital visits (5.3%, 37 of 693). If those without access gained access, their associated health care costs would have been reduced by 10% or 20%, generating potential avoided costs of AU $74.7 million and AU $149.4 million in 2024, respectively.

Conclusions

This cross-sectional study suggests that tailored MSSN services reduce the need for more costly care and that MSSN care is a highly cost-effective model of care.

title: Clinical translation of viral targeting of the endothelium in pulmonary vascular diseases.
authorString: Cao Z, Körbelin J.
abstractText:
Introduction

Pulmonary vascular diseases are characterized by endothelial dysfunction and progressive vascular remodeling. Most pulmonary vascular diseases, such as pulmonary hypertension, are rare but fatal. Although current therapies improve hemodynamics and clinical outcomes, they do not consistently restore endothelial homeostasis or reverse vascular remodeling, highlighting the potential of gene therapy as a disease-modifying strategy.

Areas covered

This narrative review examines the pulmonary vascular endothelium as a therapeutic target and discusses its heterogeneity, disease-dependent targetability, and its interactions with the other components of the vascular wall. We review adeno-associated viral, adenoviral, lentiviral and bocaviral vectors, including capsid/envelope engineering, receptor-mediated targeting, transcriptional and post-transcriptional restriction, and delivery routes. Therapeutic strategies such as gene replacement, transcription-factor delivery, and gene suppression are discussed, with particular emphasis on BMPR2. Translational barriers including viral vector immunity, species-dependent tropism, biodistribution, durability, controllability, manufacturing, and patient selection are also considered.

Expert opinion

Pulmonary endothelial gene therapy represents a highly promising but clinically immature approach. Progress will depend on vectors that achieve selective transduction of pulmonary endothelial cells while minimizing off-target accumulation. Improved preclinical models including large animals or human tissue may guide vector development. Novel targeted vectors will enable effective gene transfer, thereby reducing dose and vector-based immunotoxicity.

title: Isolated Liver and Combined Liver-Pancreas Transplantation in Cystic Fibrosis: An Australia and New Zealand Expert Consensus Statement.
authorString: Bolia R, Oliver M, Bishop J, Evans HM, Holmes K, Hopkins P, Jones R, Kanellis J, Kotsimbos T, Lewindon P, Majumdar A, Massie J, Marasco S, Ooi CY, Paraskeva M, Pleass H, Robinson PD, Sivam S, Snell G, Stormon M, Tallis C, Volovets A, Wong G.
abstractText:
Objectives

There are challenges around how transplant listing criteria, timing, waitlist management and graft selection might effectively meet the needs of people with cystic fibrosis (pwCF) and advanced liver disease. A committee was assembled to formulate an approach for isolated liver transplant (LT) and combined liver-pancreas transplant (LPT) in this population.

Methods

Twenty-two adult and paediatric transplant surgeons, hepatologists, gastroenterologists, pulmonologists, nephrologists and a transplant clinical nurse consultant devised questions regarding pre- and post-transplant management, including indications, contraindications and timing of LT and LPT in pwCF. PubMed literature search was performed for each question. Recommendations were voted on using the Delphi process, with ≥ 70% agreement to approve recommendations.

Results

Twenty-nine questions were evaluated, of which 21 recommendations were approved. Broad consensus was that pwCF should receive priority on LT waiting lists because of the multi-system nature of CF (16/22, 73%). Prioritisation determined by consensus from the transplanting unit was considered the fairest approach (19/22, 86%). The committee recommended that combined LPT be considered in all patients with CF-related diabetes evaluated for LT (19/22, 86%). Recommended indications for LT included hepatic synthetic dysfunction and advanced portal hypertension (20/22, 91%); while uncontrolled systemic infection (21/22, 95%), poor lung function [FEV1 < 40%] (17/22, 77%) and severe portopulmonary hypertension (16/22, 73%) were proposed as contraindications. Poor treatment adherence or psychosocial concerns were considered relative contraindications (17/22, 77%). Quality of life should be factored in when considering LT (21/22, 95%). Portosystemic shunt placement may bridge patients with intractable variceal bleeding to LT (20/22, 91%). Aggressive pre-transplant nutritional optimisation (22/22, 100%), individualised perioperative antimicrobial prophylaxis (21/22, 95%) and postoperative renal-sparing immunosuppression protocol for all (18/22, 82%) were recommended.

Conclusions

These consensus recommendations provide criteria outlining indications, contraindications and timing for LT and LPT as well as CF-specific transplant considerations in Australia and New Zealand. They are intended to be paired with published guidelines to reduce practice variability and improve care.

title: Changes in senescence biomarkers, frailty, and physical function during the first year after kidney transplantation.
authorString: Niu J, Khairallah P, Hickson LJ, White TA, LeBrasseur NK, Lorenz EC.
abstractText: Pre-transplant senescence biomarkers are associated with frailty in patients undergoing kidney transplantation (KT). We examined the relationship between changes in senescence biomarkers, frailty, and physical function during the first year post-KT. Plasma concentrations of senescence biomarkers, frailty (Physical Frailty Phenotype), and physical function (Short Physical Performance Battery) were simultaneously measured. Relaxed least absolute shrinkage and selection operator methods were used to select variables for multivariable models. Among 188 participants, mean age was 53 ± 13 years, 62% were male, 34% had diabetes, and 30% underwent deceased donor KT. During the first year after KT, age ≥ 60 was associated with smaller reductions in GDF-15 and IL-8, whereas Black race was associated with greater reduction in RAGE. Alemtuzumab was associated with smaller reduction in IL-7 compared to other induction agents, whereas deceased donor KT was associated with greater reduction in PAI-1. On multivariable analysis, more improvement in frailty was significantly associated with reduction in uPAR concentrations (β - 0.23, 95% CI - 0.38 to - 0.08, p = 0.003). Changes in biomarker concentrations were not independently associated with changes in physical function. Whether interventions affecting the abundance or behavior of senescent cells may counter frailty in KT recipients warrants further exploration.

abstractText: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a highly fatal vascular disease,yet effective pharmacological interventions to halt its progression are currently lacking.In recent years,vitamins have garnered significant attention as potential nutritional intervention targets due to their diverse physiological functions.This review systematically summarizes the research progress in the correlation between vitamins and AAA pathogenesis,and delves into the roles of vitamins in modulating key pathological processes such as inflammation,oxidative stress,matrix degradation,vascular smooth muscle cell function,and vascular calcification.Furthermore,this review analyzes the limitations of available studies and outlines future directions for nutritional interventions in AAA,with the ultimate goal of providing novel insights and scientific evidence for formulating the prevention and treatment strategies for AAA.

title: Efficacy of Daptomycin Plus Fosfomycin in Enterococcus faecium and Enterococcus faecalis Experimental Endocarditis With Diverse Resistance Profiles.
authorString:
García de la Mària C, Cañas MA, García-González J, Krivak F, Nin-Blanch J, Hernández-Meneses M, Falces C, Maristany M, Canela J, Espasa M, Perissinotti A, Vidal B, Tolosana JM, Quintana E, Llopis J, Moreno A, Arias CA, Cuervo G, Miro JM, Hospital Clínic Endocarditis Study Group
.
abstractText:
Background

Enterococcal infective endocarditis (IE) remains a therapeutic challenge. Recommended regimens are limited by toxicity and suboptimal bactericidal activity. We evaluated the in vitro activity of daptomycin (DAP)-fosfomycin (FOM) against Enterococcus faecalis and Enterococcus faecium isolates with diverse resistance phenotypes and assessed the efficacy in the rabbit model of experimental endocarditis (EE).

Methods

Eighteen isolates were studied using time-kill assays under initial standard inoculum (ISI) and initial high inoculum (IHI) conditions. A rabbit aortic valve EE model was performed using 3 selected strains and human-equivalent pharmacokinetics simulating DAP (10 mg/kg/day) and FOM (2 g every 6 hours). Outcomes included bacterial densities in vegetations and tissues, sterilization rates, and emergence of resistance.

Results

Daptomycin-fosfomycin showed synergy against all vancomycin-susceptible (VAN-S) and vancomycin-resistant (VAN-R) isolates under ISI conditions; synergy was reduced under IHI conditions. In vivo, DAP-FOM significantly reduced bacterial counts in vegetations versus DAP alone against VAN-R E. faecium (P = .002) and VAN-S high-level aminoglycoside resistance [HLAR] E. faecalis (P = .029). For the third strain (VAN-S, non-HLAR E. faecalis), the combination was not significantly more active than DAP monotherapy. Daptomycin-resistant isolates emerged with DAP monotherapy in 60% of rabbits infected with VAN-R E. faecium and in 20% of those infected with VAN-S HLAR E. faecalis but were not detected in rabbits infected with VAN-S non-HLAR E. faecalis. No DAP-resistant isolates were selected in groups receiving DAP-FOM.

Conclusions

Daptomycin-fosfomycin demonstrated synergistic activity and improved efficacy in experimental enterococcal IE, particularly against VAN-R E. faecium, and prevented selection of daptomycin-nonsusceptible isolates.

title: Racial Differences in Transthyretin Cardiac Amyloidosis: A Systematic Review of Genotype, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Outcomes
authorString: Alexander O, Ajekiigbe VO, Woldehana DA, Olawale MO, Oyelude SO, Oloruntoba FG, Oladejo BP, Ayedun SA, Almustapha H, Eltayeb M, Mohammed RS, Abafita HK.
abstractText: Background Transthyretin (TTR) amyloidosis, a form of Cardiac Amyloidosis, is characterized by gradual accumulation of TTR, disrupting the anatomy and physiology of various organs, especially the heart; it has increasingly become a common cause of cardiac failure, morbidity, and mortality. Different genetic variants have been identified that are influenced by race and ethnicity, and the existing evidence affects treatment and clinical outcomes. However, the extent of this influence on the genetic variant is not fully understood. Methods The review protocol was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261404519) and conducted in line with PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Six electronic databases were searched between June and July 2026: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, ClinicalTrials.gov, CINAHL, ScienceDirect, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), and 1,073 studies were retrieved. Following removal of duplicates, studies reporting race and ethnicity in confirmed ATTR-CM were included, and two independent reviewers screened the studies, assessed the risk of bias, and extracted the data. Data were synthesized narratively due to significant methodological differences. Results 941 out of 1,073 were screened, and 78 studies underwent full-text screening. 9 studies met the inclusion criteria. These studies showed a complex interplay between race/ethnicity and genetic carriage in transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis. p.V1421 mutations were significantly higher in black patients (79%) compared to white patients (1%). Invasive diagnostic tests are more common among the black patients compared to white counterparts (62.3 vs 17.7%), non - invasive techniques such as bone scintigraphy are more common with white patients (70.6% p = 0.016). Black patients with ATTRwt-CA, compared with non-black patients, received significantly lower disease-modifying therapy (68.4% vs 88.4%). More advanced forms of the disease, with higher risk of mortality, thromboembolism, heart failure, and frequent hospitalization, are more common with the black and Afro-Caribbean patients, although the disparities were absent or attenuated in some studies with more equitable access to treatment. Conclusion Differences in race and ethnicity do exist in patients with confirmed ATTR-CM and involve genetic, diagnostic, and clinical outcomes. Genetic factors alone cannot fully explain these disparities and may reflect socioeconomic disadvantage and unequal healthcare access. Large multicenter studies are needed to explain these mechanisms and identify ways to reduce these disparities.

title: Comparative Efficacy of Pharmacological Treatments for Resistant Hypertension: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
authorString: Zhao P, Fu W, Cui L, Huang W, Lin L.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

Resistant hypertension substantially increases cardiovascular and renal risk, while evidence for emerging pharmacological therapies is rapidly evolving.

Methods

We systematically searched PubMed, Web of Science, CENTRAL, and Embase from inception to January 3, 2026, for randomized controlled trials evaluating pharmacological treatments for resistant hypertension. Primary outcomes were changes in office and 24-hour systolic blood pressure; secondary outcomes included office and 24-hour diastolic blood pressure and adverse events.

Results

Thirty randomized controlled trials evaluating 18 agents in 10 446 participants were included. Spironolactone produced the greatest reduction in office systolic blood pressure (mean difference, -11.36 [95% CI, -14.97 to -7.74] mm Hg; high confidence), whereas baxdrostat produced the greatest reduction in 24-hour systolic blood pressure (mean difference, -15.81 [95% CI, -21.79 to -9.82] mm Hg; high confidence). Bisoprolol showed the greatest reduction in office diastolic blood pressure (mean difference, -6.24 [95% CI, -11.23 to -1.25] mm Hg; high confidence), while propranolol showed the greatest reduction in 24-hour diastolic blood pressure (mean difference, -8.90 [95% CI, -17.28 to -0.52] mm Hg; very low confidence). Lorundrostat reduced the odds of at least 1 adverse event versus placebo (odds ratio, 0.53 [95% CI, 0.34-0.82]). Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists showed a relative advantage in systolic blood pressure control in subgroup analyses. Confidence ratings reflect individual comparisons rather than overall network stability.

Conclusions

Spironolactone remains the pharmacological therapy with the strongest evidence for resistant hypertension. Amiloride may be an alternative for patients intolerant of spironolactone, although evidence remains limited. β Blockers may be considered for predominant diastolic hypertension or sympathetic overactivity, but this should be interpreted cautiously given the low confidence in the evidence for 24-hour diastolic blood pressure. Aldosterone synthase inhibitors and endothelin receptor antagonists are additional therapeutic options.

title: CMR Assessment of Myocardial Reperfusion Following PPCI With or Without Manual Thrombus Aspiration in STEMI With High Thrombus Burden: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
authorString: Mikawy ME, AlGhazawy A, Elhammady W, Badran H, Shahata H, Khalil S, Nour A.

journal.title: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions

abstractText:
Background

ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) remains a leading cause of morbidity and sudden cardiac death worldwide. Although primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PPCI) is the guideline-recommended reperfusion strategy, lesions with a high thrombus burden remain a clinical challenge, and routine manual thrombus aspiration is no longer recommended on the basis of all-comer trials with clinical endpoints. We used cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging to evaluate myocardial reperfusion after PPCI with or without adjunctive manual thrombus aspiration in patients restricted to the highest angiographic thrombus burden.

Methods

One hundred STEMI patients presenting within 12 h of symptom onset, all with angiographic TIMI thrombus grade V, were randomized 1:1 (computer-generated sequence, concealed allocation) to manual thrombus aspiration followed by stenting (Group A, n = 50) or conventional PCI alone (Group B, n = 50). The trial was not prospectively registered, and no a priori power calculation was performed (predefined convenience sample). Echocardiographic and CMR images were analyzed by two independent readers blinded to treatment allocation. CMR was performed at 3 months, and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) were recorded to 6 months.

Results

Baseline characteristics were similar between groups, and no patient was lost to follow-up. On unblinded angiographic assessment, Group A had higher rates of final TIMI III flow (92% vs. 68%; risk difference 24%, 95% CI 8.4-38.6; p = 0.005) and MBG III (80% vs. 60%; risk difference 20%, 95% CI 2.0-36.4; p = 0.049). Three-month CMR showed higher LVEF (48.0% vs. 35.8%; mean difference 12.2, 95% CI 9.8-14.5), smaller infarct size (17.0% vs. 29.2% of LV mass; mean difference -12.2, 95% CI - 14.5 to -9.8), and greater stroke volume index (42.0 vs. 32.2 mL/m2; mean difference 9.8, 95% CI 7.4-12.1) in Group A (all p < 0.001). At 6 months, heart failure hospitalization was less frequent in Group A (2 vs. 10 events; 4% vs. 20%; unadjusted p = 0.028; exploratory), whereas differences in recurrent MI (4% vs. 16%; p = 0.092) and CV death (2% vs. 14%; p = 0.059) were not statistically significant. No stroke occurred in either group.

Conclusions

In this small, single-center trial of STEMI with the highest angiographic thrombus burden, manual thrombus aspiration was associated with higher angiographic reperfusion rates (assessed without blinding) and, on 3-month CMR, smaller infarct size and better ventricular function; these effect sizes are large and are probably overestimated. Clinical-event differences are exploratory: heart failure hospitalization was less frequent (2 vs. 10 events; unadjusted p = 0.028), whereas recurrent MI and cardiovascular death did not differ significantly. Given the absence of trial registration and an a priori power calculation, and the lack of an early CMR scan to assess microvascular obstruction and intramyocardial hemorrhage, these hypothesis-generating findings do not challenge the recommendation against routine aspiration and require confirmation in adequately powered, preregistered multicenter trials.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Jailed Balloon-Proximal Optimization Technique Versus Jailed Wire Technique for Preventing Side Branch Occlusion During Percutaneous Coronary Intervention of True Non-Left Main Bifurcation Lesions: A Multicenter, Open-Label, Randomized Controlled Trial.
authorString: Gao C, Dai H, Han J, Li D, Lu X, Liu H, Zhe H, Liu P, Bai B, Zheng J, Chen B, Li G, Wang J, Li Y, Guo W.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText: The jailed balloon technique prevents side branch (SB) occlusion during coronary bifurcation stenting but is complex. We developed a jailed balloon-proximal optimization technique (JB-POT) to simplify jailed balloon technique and compared its efficacy and safety with conventional jailed wire technique (JWT) for non-left main bifurcation lesions. In this multicenter randomized controlled trial, 110 patients with true non-left main bifurcation lesions (Medina 1,0,1; 1,1,1; 0,1,1) were randomized to JB-POT (N=55) or JWT (N=55). The primary end point was SB occlusion rate after main vessel stenting/proximal optimization technique. Secondary end points included stent malapposition, target lesion failure (composite of cardiovascular death, target vessel myocardial infarction, and revascularization), stent thrombosis, procedure time, and contrast volume. JB-POT significantly reduced SB occlusion (1.8% versus 20%; P=0.006), shortened procedure time (67 [53-85] versus 82 [62-99] minutes; P=0.009), and lowered contrast volume (140 [120-160] versus 160 [130-190] mL; P=0.002) versus JWT. Severe stent malapposition occurred in 5.5% (JB-POT) versus 0% (JWT) (P=0.242). Perioperative target lesion failure (P=0.475) and stent thrombosis (P=0.242) were comparable, but JB-POT showed a tendency for improved 12-month target lesion failure-free survival (P=0.023) and a nonsignificant trend toward reduced stent thrombosis (P=0.079). Multivariable analysis identified diabetes (odds ratio [OR], 7.26), SB ostial stenosis (OR, 1.09), balloon number (OR, 1.96), and diastolic blood pressure (OR, 1.07) as exploratory SB occlusion associates. JB-POT significantly reduced SB occlusion, procedure time, and contrast volume versus JWT in non-left main bifurcation percutaneous coronary intervention, with comparable periprocedural safety. It represents a novel SB protection strategy, particularly beneficial in acute myocardial infarction, renal dysfunction, or consecutive bifurcation lesions. URL: https://www.chictr.org.cn; Unique Identifier: ChiCTR2300071356.

title: Impact of Guideline-Based Indications on Outcomes in Asymptomatic Patients With Severe Aortic Stenosis: Insights From the AVATAR Trial.
authorString: Banovic M, Iung B, Brkovic V, Putnik S, Boskovic N, Wojakowski W, Deja M, Cohen DJ, Van Mieghem NM, Barbato E, Kotrc M, Salizzoni S, Bartunek J.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

It is unknown whether current class IIa recommendations correctly identify asymptomatic patients with severe aortic stenosis who derive enhanced benefit from aortic valve replacement (AVR). We investigated whether the presence of a class IIa recommendation per European Society of Cardiology guidelines for AVR at the time of randomization affected the outcome of patients enrolled in the AVATAR (Aortic Valve Replacement Versus Conservative Treatment in Asymptomatic Aortic Stenosis) trial.

Methods

The AVATAR trial population included 157 patients with asymptomatic severe aortic stenosis who were randomized to early AVR (n=78) or conservative management (n=79). The primary outcome comprised all-cause mortality or major adverse cardiovascular events composed of acute myocardial infarction, stroke, and unplanned heart failure hospitalization, which was compared between groups using a stratified proportional hazards model.

Results

Among AVATAR trial population (mean age, 67 years; 43% women), 62 patients (39.5%) had a class IIa recommendation for AVR at the time of enrollment. The primary composite outcome was more frequent in patients with a class IIa indication for AVR versus those without a guideline indication (46.8% versus 27.4%; P=0.010). In stratified analyses, the benefit of early AVR was consistent among patients with a class IIa guideline recommendation at baseline (hazard ratio [HR], 0.48 [95% CI, 0.23-1.00]) and among patients without a class IIa guideline recommendation (HR, 0.29 [95% CI, 0.12-0.73]; P-interaction=0.389).

Conclusions

Asymptomatic patients with severe aortic stenosis and with a class IIa indication for AVR had worse long-term outcomes compared with patients without a class IIa indication at the time of randomization. There is no evidence that presence of a class IIa indication modified the benefit of early AVR.

title: Testosterone therapy and anabolic steroid use: why cardiovascular risk discussions must separate the two.
authorString: Farzam K.
abstractText: Cardiovascular discussions about testosterone often combine exposures that differ in indication, formulation, dose, duration, and concomitant drug use. Appropriately indicated testosterone replacement, prescribing without adequate diagnostic confirmation, nonprescribed testosterone, and multi-agent androgen regimens should not be treated as interchangeable. This Perspective article proposes an exposure-based framework that distinguishes therapeutic evidence from studies of nonmedical use and experimental mechanisms. Randomized trials provide reassurance about major adverse cardiovascular events within the populations and observation periods studied, but do not establish lifelong safety or equivalence across formulations. The atrial fibrillation finding in TRAVERSE requires separate consideration of its absolute and relative magnitude. Conversely, imaging and cohort studies associate nonmedical androgen use with ventricular dysfunction and cardiovascular disease, although they do not provide a direct quantitative comparison with replacement therapy. Low endogenous testosterone and metabolic disease also require balanced interpretation: association does not establish that treatment prevents cardiovascular events. More precise terminology, realistic clinical assessment, and longitudinal exposure documentation can improve both patient care and research without minimizing either inappropriate prescribing or the harms of nonmedical androgen use.

title: Prevalence of a Bicuspid Aortic Valve Among Patients Undergoing Surgery for Aortic Dissection and the Influence of Native Aortic Valve Morphology on Surgical Outcome: A Retrospective Observational Study.
authorString: Gopakumar D, Sreekantan R, Jyothi A, Pillai V.
abstractText: Background A bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) is associated with aortopathy and an increased risk of aortic dissection, but most patients presenting with dissection have a tricuspid aortic valve. We determined the proportion of patients with BAV among those undergoing surgery for aortic dissection and compared operative strategy, morbidity, mortality, and survival by native valve morphology. Methods This retrospective single-centre study included 132 consecutive patients who underwent surgery for aortic dissection between 2000 and 2025. Dissection was diagnosed by CT, and valve morphology (bicuspid or tricuspid) was determined by intraoperative inspection. Categorical variables were compared using Fisher's exact test, continuous variables using the Mann-Whitney U test, and survival using Kaplan-Meier analysis with the log-rank test. Results  The mean age was 47.6 ± 13.0 years, and 102 patients (77.3%) were male. Supracoronary ascending aortic replacement (SCAAR) was performed in 102 patients (77.3%) and a Bentall procedure in 30 (22.7%). Ten patients (7.6%, 95% CI: 4.2-13.4%) had a bicuspid valve. Assuming a general-population BAV prevalence of 0.5-2%, this corresponds to an estimated relative risk of dissection of about 4-16. Overall mortality was 14.4% (19 patients), including 17 in-hospital deaths (12.9%). Mean follow-up was 4.70 ± 4.80 years (range: 0-22). Age, ICU stay, and hospital stay did not differ between the groups. Bicuspid patients more often underwent a Bentall procedure (50.0% vs 20.5%, p = 0.047) and had higher mortality (40.0% vs 12.3%, p = 0.037). Survival differed between the groups (log-rank χ² = 5.100, p = 0.024), with the divergence occurring early after surgery. Conclusions BAV was present in 7.6% of patients undergoing surgery for aortic dissection, which suggests a higher relative risk of dissection than in the general population, although most dissections occurred with tricuspid valves. Bicuspid morphology was associated with more frequent root replacement and higher early mortality.

title: Bisphenol A and Its Analogues in Hypertension: Molecular Mechanisms, Epigenetic Regulation, and Therapeutic Perspectives-A Narrative Review.
authorString: Thiruvengadam R, Singh CD, Thiruvengadam M, Kim JH.
abstractText: Hypertension is a leading risk factor for cardiovascular disease, including heart failure, stroke, and peripheral artery disease, with a lifetime risk exceeding 90% among adults aged 55-65 years. Its pathophysiology involves arterial stiffness, blood pressure variability, hormonal and neuronal dysregulation, age-related renal change, and endothelial dysfunction. Environmental endocrine disruptors, notably bisphenol A (BPA) and its analogues, are widely used in plastics and epoxy resins and may contribute by interacting with estrogen receptors and disrupting hormonal homeostasis, although human clinical evidence remains limited. This narrative review synthesizes epidemiological evidence, molecular mechanisms, and emerging therapeutic strategies linking bisphenol exposure to hypertension. The literature was identified through PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar for publications from 2000 to 2025 and appraised with reference to the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles (SANRA). The mechanisms considered include oxidative stress, TGF-β/SMAD and MAPK signaling, the PI3K/AKT axis, and FOXO transcription factors, together with epigenetic alterations such as DNA methylation and histone modification. Human studies are appraised separately from experimental work, and exposure relevance, administered dose, and non-monotonic dose-response relationships are addressed explicitly. Therapeutic approaches are organized as exposure reduction, treatment of established cardiovascular effects, mechanism-directed strategies, and experimental approaches including nanoparticle-mediated delivery, chronotherapy, and RNA-based therapeutics; all remain preclinical and none has been evaluated specifically in BPA-associated hypertension. Because the human evidence is predominantly cross-sectional and the mechanistic data derive largely from experimental models, the relationships described should be regarded as associations and plausible mechanisms rather than established causal pathways.

title: A Contemporary Analysis of Microaxial Pump-Associated Cardiac Perforation Events From the FDA MAUDE Database.
authorString: Rafique S, Sagalov A, Tamimi RA, Ghanem F, Patel R, Kapur N, Hafiz AM.

journal.title: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions

abstractText: Percutaneous microaxial pumps are used in cardiogenic shock and high-risk percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), but left ventricular (LV) perforation is an infrequent but serious complication. In 2023, an FDA advisory warned of increased perforation risk. To describe clinical setting, patterns, high-risk subgroups, and outcomes of LV perforation in real-world reports. We queried the FDA Manufacturer and User Facility Device Experience (MAUDE) database (2016-2024) for Impella adverse-event reports, screened narratives for perforation terms, and manually adjudicated suspected cases to confirm LV perforation and extract device, clinical setting, presentation, management, and outcomes. Among 24,424 Impella reports, 188 involved LV perforation (0.77%). Impella CP accounted for 52.7% and Impella 5.5 for 41.5% (few with 5.0/2.5; none with RP). Annual LV perforations per 1000 reports declined from 166.7 (2016) to 5.2 (2024). Events occurred most often during cardiac surgery (27.1%), acute coronary syndrome (19.1%), or high-risk PCI (17.0%). Intraprocedural diagnosis occurred in 76.2% and was more common with 5.5 versus CP (83.3% vs. 67.7%). With intraprocedural diagnosis, mortality was 24.6% for 5.5 and 28.4% for CP, versus 66.7% for both when diagnosis was post-procedural. Pericardial effusion (34.9%) and hypotension (28.6%) were common. Repair was attempted at 72.9% and reduced mortality, particularly for CP (19.7% with repair vs. 64.7% without; p < 0.001). Overall mortality was 30.2%, without differences by sex or race. LV perforation reported with Impella devices is rare but carries high mortality; earlier recognition and prompt repair are associated with improved survival.

title: Changes in combustible cigarette, heated tobacco product and electronic cigarette use and cardiovascular risk among adults with type 2 diabetes: A Korean national retrospective cohort study.
authorString: Cho HK, Park S, Choi S, Kim K, Lee K, Park SM.
abstractText: Heated tobacco products (HTPs) and electronic cigarettes (ECs) are increasingly used as alternatives to combustible cigarettes (CCs), but their cardiovascular implications in type 2 diabetes remain unclear. We examined the associations between changes in smoking patterns, including self-reported changes from CCs to HTPs and/or ECs between two health screenings, and subsequent cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk among smokers with newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes. Nationwide retrospective cohort study using the Korean National Health Insurance Service data. Cause-specific Cox proportional hazards regression models estimated adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs), with competing-risk, overlap-weighting and other sensitivity analyses. Republic of Korea, using biennial national health screenings 2010-2020, with follow-up through 31 December 2022. A total of 63 969 individuals aged ≥ 40 years who were current CC smokers within two years of a new diagnosis of type 2 diabetes between 2010 and 2016 and who completed two health examinations were included. Product-use status was self-reported at two health screenings. According to status at the second screening (2019-2020), participants were categorized as successful quitters, continued CC users, exclusive HTP/EC users or concurrent users of CC and HTP/EC. The primary outcome was incident CVD, defined as hospitalization for ≥2 days due to coronary heart disease (CHD) or acute stroke (total stroke, TS). Compared with continued CC use, complete quitting was associated with lower risks of CVD (aHR = 0.72; 95% CI = 0.65-0.80), CHD (aHR = 0.76; 95% CI = 0.68-0.86) and TS (aHR = 0.64; 95% CI = 0.54-0.76). Exclusive HTP/EC use (aHR = 0.83; 95% CI = 0.62-1.11) and concurrent use (aHR = 0.88; 95% CI = 0.73-1.05) were not statistically significantly associated with overall CVD risk. In exploratory analyses based on 9 events, exclusive HTP/EC use was associated with lower risk of acute stroke compared with continued CC smoking (aHR = 0.49; 95% CI = 0.25-0.94). Estimates were directionally consistent across competing-risk, overlap-weighting and alternative-definition sensitivity analyses. Among Korean smokers with type 2 diabetes, complete smoking cessation is associated with lower risks of cardiovascular disease, coronary heart disease and stroke, but exclusive use of heated tobacco products and electronic cigarettes is not statistically significantly associated with overall cardiovascular disease risk and a lower risk of stroke rests on very few events. Therefore, complete smoking cessation should remain the preferred clinical recommendation for smokers with type 2 diabetes.

title: Predicting Major Adverse Events With Cardiac Resynchronization, Leadless, and Conduction System Pacemaker Implantation.
authorString: Reinhardt SW, Wang Y, Aldaas O, Paredes MCT, Minges KE, Marshall K, Denton B, Zimmerman S, Hsu JC, Freeman JV.
abstractText: Large-scale contemporary risk prediction models for adverse events after pacemaker implantation are lacking. The National Cardiovascular Data Registry EP Device Implant Registry has collected data on pacemaker implantations including cardiac resynchronization therapy pacemakers (CRT-P), leadless pacemakers, and His/left bundle pacemakers since April 2021. To produce a standardized risk model for in-hospital complications following CRT-P, leadless, and His/left bundle pacemaker procedures. Data from 21,211 novel pacemaker procedures across 179 hospitals from January 2022 to June 2024 were used to develop and validate a model to predict in-hospital complications. The overall in-hospital complication rate was 2.00% (range 1.69%-2.23% and interquartile range 1.98%-2.01%), which varied somewhat by device type: CRT-P 1.76%, leadless pacemaker 2.51%, and His/left bundle pacemaker 1.85%, p = 0.0052. Prior MI, prior cardiac arrest, sodium >145 mEq/L, and being hospitalized for cardiac or non-cardiac reasons not related to the procedure were the most significant risk factors for complications. The model demonstrated moderate discrimination with a C-index of 0.714 for the total cohort; this varied somewhat but showed helpful discrimination for each device-type (C-index of 0.716 for CRT-P, 0.795 for leadless pacemakers, and 0.663 for His/left bundle pacemakers). We developed a risk model for CRT-P, leadless, and conduction system pacemakers with overall helpful risk prediction, although it varied by device type. Modifications to the EPDI Registry data collection form and larger numbers of procedures in the registry over time will allow for separate, device-specific risk models in the future that may offer improved performance.

title: National trends in diet-related mortality and disability-adjusted life years in Spain, 1990-2023: the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.
authorString: López-Gil JF, López-Moreno M, Quesada G, Miño C, Ridgell L, Quiroz-Cárdenas F, Cisneros-Vásquez E, Yáñez-Sepúlveda R, Wei CF, Yon DK.

journal.title: International journal of food sciences and nutrition

abstractText: Suboptimal diet is a major modifiable risk factor for non-communicable diseases (NCDs), but its burden in Spain has not been quantified with Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2023 estimates. We extracted GBD 2023 estimates of diet-attributable deaths and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) for 15 dietary risks among adults aged ≥25 years in Spain (1990-2023) and applied joinpoint regression and Das Gupta decomposition. In 2023, 36,954 deaths (95% uncertainty interval [UI] 16,422-55,921) and 800,138 DALYs (350,398-1,121,373) were attributable to diet, representing 9.4% of adult NCD deaths and 6.7% of adult NCD DALYs. The largest contributors were low whole-grain intake (10,365 deaths), high red meat (6,293) and high processed meat intake (4,931). Cardiovascular diseases accounted for most diet-attributable deaths. Age-standardised mortality declined, whereas the number of deaths changed little (+9.0%; 95% UI -6.1 to 43.2) because population growth and ageing offset falling age-specific rates.

title: Association Between Dupilumab and Risk of Cardiovascular Diseases Among US Patients With COPD: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
authorString: Hung CT, An CY, Suk CW, Alam U, Hung SH.
abstractText:
Background

Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is associated with substantial cardiovascular morbidity. Although dupilumab reduces COPD exacerbations, its cardiovascular effects remain uncertain.

Objective

This study aimed to evaluate the association between dupilumab and cardiovascular disease risk among patients with COPD.

Methods

This retrospective cohort study used the US TriNetX electronic health records database with a new-user design. Patients aged ≥40 years with COPD between October 1, 2024, and June 1, 2025, receiving triple inhaler therapy were included. Patients initiating dupilumab within 30 days after COPD exacerbation were compared with those receiving triple inhaler therapy. Outcomes included acute myocardial infarction (AMI), cerebral infarction, heart failure, and atrial fibrillation/flutter (AFib/AFl). Propensity score matching (1:1) was used to balance covariates. Cox models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

Results

Among 72 113 patients with COPD, 1352 matched pairs were analyzed. Dupilumab was associated with increased risks of heart failure (HR, 1.73; 95% CI, 1.44-2.08) and AFib/AFl (HR, 1.57; 95% CI, 1.24-1.99) compared with triple inhaler therapy. No associations were observed for AMI (HR, 1.38; 95% CI, 0.92-2.06) and cerebral infarction (HR, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.48-1.45). Associations with heart failure and AFib/AFl remained consistent across sensitivity analyses and were observed in both eosinophil subgroups.

Conclusion and relevance

Higher rates of heart failure and AFib/AFl were observed among dupilumab initiators than patients receiving triple inhaler therapy alone. Given the residual confounding, these findings do not establish a causal cardiovascular effect of dupilumab. Further studies are needed to confirm these findings.

title: Robotic Endoscopic Off-Pump Pericardiectomy: Early and Long-Term Outcomes.
authorString: Qin H, Nisivaco S, Thacker J, AlJamal YN, Balkhy HH.
abstractText:
Objective

To review the perioperative and long-term outcomes of robotic, endoscopic, off-pump pericardiectomy for constrictive and recurrent pericarditis at a tertiary referral center.

Methods

We retrospectively reviewed 21 consecutive patients who underwent robotic endoscopic off-pump pericardiectomy from 2013 to 2024. The mean follow-up duration was 63.7 ± 51.1 months. Survival outcomes were estimated using Kaplan-Meier methods and compared using the log-rank test or Cox regression.

Results

The mean patient age at the time of surgery was 58.0 ± 15.5 years. No patient required conversion to sternotomy or cardiopulmonary bypass. There was no mortality within 6 months. Mean intensive care unit and hospital lengths of stay were 1.8 ± 1.0 and 3.7 ± 1.7 days, respectively. After surgery, right atrial pressure decreased from 20.1 ± 7.7 to 9.6 ± 5.0 mm Hg (P < 0.001), and the cardiac index increased from 2.2 ± 0.5 to 3.3 ± 0.4 L/min/m2 (P < 0.001). At the current follow-up, overall mortality was 26%, with the median survival not reached. Estimated survival at 1, 5, and 10 years was 94%, 76%, and 66%, respectively. Preoperative heart failure was associated with shorter survival (P = 0.005), whereas idiopathic etiology was associated with a more favorable survival than known causes or risk factors (P = 0.045).

Conclusions

Robotic, endoscopic, off-pump pericardiectomy was feasible and showed favorable perioperative outcomes and long-term survival. In experienced programs, this approach may represent a reasonable, minimally invasive alternative for selected patients requiring pericardiectomy.

title: Characteristic and Outcomes of Patients With ST-Segment-Elevation Myocardial Infarction Who Have Nonsystem Reasons for Delay in Treatment: A Report from the American Heart Association GWTG-CAD Registry.
authorString: Lee TC, Jollis JG, Hong H, Jiang T, Norland K, Zhao J, Henry TD, Jacobs AK, Goyal A, Granger CB, Thomas K, Tamis-Holland JE.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText: Timely treatment improves outcomes in ST-segment-elevation myocardial infarction. The American Heart Association's GWTG (Get With The Guidelines) registry tracks treatment times and designates exceptions for patients with nonsystem reasons for delay (NSD). However, these exception practices limit our understanding of the impact of NSD on patient outcome and quality of care. We analyzed patients with ST-segment-elevation myocardial infarction undergoing primary PCI in the GWTG-CAD (GWTG-Coronary Artery Disease) registry from January 2019 to December 2021. We examined characteristics and outcomes for patients with and without reported NSD, and classified NSD into critical (cardiac arrest, intubation, left ventricular support device) and noncritical categories. Multivariable logistic regression assessed the association between NSD and in-hospital mortality. We analyzed hospital ranking stability using all-patient rankings as reference, comparing current practice (all NSD excepted) versus an alternative approach (only critical NSD excepted). Among 74 372 patients, 23.9% had reported NSD. Mortality was higher in patients with NSD (15.4% versus 2.7%, adjusted odds ratio [OR], 2.61 [95% CI, 2.41-2.83]), driven by critical NSD (adjusted OR, 4.61 [95% CI, 4.15-5.12]), though noncritical NSD also remained elevated (adjusted OR, 1.57 [95% CI, 1.42-1.73]). Compared with all-patient reference rankings, current exception practice was associated with ranking instability: only 71% (emergency medical services) and 69% (walk-in) of top-25% hospitals retained their status, with median ranking changes of 40 to 50 positions (ρ=0.77, 0.70). Rankings stabilized when only critical NSD were excepted (91% and 87% retention; ρ=0.95, 0.95). NSD in ST-segment-elevation myocardial infarction care is common and associated with higher mortality. Noncritical NSD exceptions are associated with hospital ranking instability, suggesting these exception criteria warrant refinement.

title: Utility of apolipoprotein C3/A2 ratio for cardiovascular risk assessment in statin-treated patients following percutaneous coronary intervention.
authorString: Usuda H, Ikegami R, Akiyama T, Tashiro K, Washiyama Y, Yoneyama S, Nishida K, Kubota N, Okubo T, Ozaki K, Hoyano M, Inomata T.
abstractText: In secondary-prevention patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) on LDL-lowering therapy, the clinical utility of apolipoproteins (Apos) for risk stratification remains unclear. This study investigated whether combined Apo A2 (associated with HDL metabolism) and Apo C3 (associated with triglyceride metabolism) evaluation predicts cardiovascular events.We analyzed 649 statin-treated patients undergoing PCI with drug-eluting stents for acute or chronic coronary syndrome (2016-2022) with measured serum Apo levels. Patients were categorized by median Apo A2 and Apo C3 levels into three groups: low-Apo A2 and high-Apo C3; low-Apo A2 or high-Apo C3; and high-Apo A2 and low-Apo C3. During follow-up, 124 patients (19.1%) experienced major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs). The low-Apo A2 and high-Apo C3 group had the highest incidence (50.9% vs. 34.5% vs. 21.5%) and independently predicted MACE on multivariable Cox analysis (hazard ratio, 1.52; 95% confidence interval, 1.02-2.28). The Apo C3/Apo A2 ratio (cutoff = 0.414) was significantly associated with MACE, revascularization, and heart failure rehospitalization (log-rank p = 0.001, 0.006, and 0.003). Each 0.1 increase was associated with a 23% higher MACE risk.Among statin-treated post-PCI patients, concurrent low-Apo A2 and high-Apo C3 identified a high-risk subgroup for MACE. The Apo C3/Apo A2 ratio may serve as a novel marker for residual cardiovascular risk stratification beyond LDL-cholesterol.

title: Corticosteroid regimens and clinical courses during tapering in patients with cardiac sarcoidosis: insights from a nationwide JROAD-DPC database.
authorString: Kitai T, Sakamoto T, Yoshii T, Kurashima S, Irie Y, Moriuchi K, Amano M, Okada A, Amaki M, Kanzaki H, Izumi C.
abstractText: Corticosteroid therapy remains the cornerstone of treatment for cardiac sarcoidosis (CS). Nevertheless, data on the optimal initial dosage, appropriate tapering schedules, and suitable maintenance dosages remain limited. This study sought to characterize real-world corticosteroid therapy regimens and the clinical course during corticosteroid tapering in patients with CS. From the Japanese Diagnosis Procedure Combination database, 6282 hospitalized patients with CS were identified between 2012 and 2022. Among them, 3067 patients who were newly initiated on corticosteroid therapy during hospitalization were analyzed. Corticosteroid dosing patterns and clinical outcomes during tapering were evaluated. The mean age was 63 ± 11 years and 62.0% were female. The mean initial corticosteroid dose was 30.3 ± 6.9 mg/day. Corticosteroid dose was gradually tapered to 21.4 ± 9.8, 15.7 ± 6.9, 12.2 ± 5.7, 10.4 ± 5.0, 9.3 ± 4.5, and 9.0 ± 4.6 mg/day at 30, 60, 90, 120, 150, and 180 days, respectively. By day 180, 83.7% of patients were maintained on ≤10 mg/day. During corticosteroid tapering, 17.1% of patients required corticosteroid dose escalation. During follow-up, 965 patients (31.5%) were rehospitalized; among them, 48.0% required corticosteroid escalation and 2.6% received second-line immunosuppressive therapy. In contemporary clinical practice, most patients with CS are initiated on approximately 30 mg/day of corticosteroids which are tapered to ≤10 mg/day within 6 months. However, a non-negligible number of patients required corticosteroid dose escalation, reflecting the challenges of long-term disease control and the need for close monitoring during corticosteroid tapering.

title: Cardiac PIEZO 1 Channels Modulate Anxiety.
authorString: Summers J, Miklja Z, Weaver A, Taha J, Yakimchuk A, Kramm C, Li Y, Taha W, Afonso L, Farrow S, Woodman R, Lockette W.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText: Conscious cardiac interoception explains the ability of some individuals to "feel" their heartbeat without taking their pulse. Subconscious cardiac interoception detects heart signals from baroreceptors without subjective awareness. We used photoplethysmography to determine if contrasting sensitivity of PIEZO 1 (human mechanosensitive stretch channels) mediates each form of cardiac interoception and feelings of anxiety. In healthy volunteers, conscious cardiac interoception was increased with lower heart rates and greater stroke volumes but not associated with anxiety. Disruption of Piezo 1 (rodent mechanosensitive stretch channel) in cardiac sensory neurons enhanced anxiety in rodents. PIEZO 1 sensitivity correlated inversely with state anxiety scores in men and women (r=-0.6495, P=0.0004, n=25). Cold pressor test-induced changes in cardiac work were greater in subjects with lower PIEZO 1 sensitivity when compared with subjects with higher PIEZO 1 sensitivity (values expressed as median percentage increase in rate pressure product, 27.6 [interquartile range, 19.2-35.8] versus 8.4 [interquartile range 0.38-19.13], P=0.0093). Those with lower anxiety also had enhanced coefficients of variation in their instantaneous baroreceptor gain at rest (values expressed as medians, 1.417 [interquartile range 0.8482-1.585] versus 0.7518 interquartile range [0.5947-0.8226], P=0.0082). We propose that a reduction in PIEZO 1 sensitivity causes errors in subconscious interoception and leads to anxiety and increased cardiac workloads. We also report testosterone, which is anxiolytic, enhanced, whereas the stress hormone corticosterone, decreased Piezo 1 gene transcription. Selectively enhancing subconscious interoception by increasing PIEZO 1 sensitivity may reduce anxiety and improve cardiovascular health outcomes.

title: Ambient Air Pollution, Weather and Placental Abruption (APWA): Design, Data Linkage and Preliminary Findings.
authorString: Ananth CV, Shi M, Pearl M, Pearce JL, Ross Z, Shukle JT, Rosenfeld EB, Martinez V, Wilson A, Friedman AM, Schwartz J, Kioumourtzoglou MA, Papatheodorou S, Kirby RS.
