abstractText: Ambient fine particulate matter and gaseous exposures can induce oxidative stress, resulting in a pro-inflammatory response and a thrombotic state. Because these processes can occur during pregnancy, a large epidemiological study was designed to test the hypothesis that ambient air pollution and weather exposures pre-conception and in early pregnancy are associated with chronic abruptions, whereas exposures a few days prior to delivery are associated with acute abruptions. To describe the design, methods and characteristics of the multi-state cohorts in the US, comprising the Ambient Air Pollution, Weather and Placental Abruption (APWA) project. All women who delivered in California, Florida, Massachusetts and South Carolina, USA, from 2000 to 2016. Population-based, retrospective birth cohort study. We linked vital records data on live births and foetal deaths to delivery hospitalisations to capture abruption diagnosis. Daily air pollution and weather exposures were modelled using geocoded residence-at-delivery data from 90 days prior to the last menstrual period to 12 months after delivery. We examined ambient fine particulate matter (aerodynamic diameter of ≤ 2.5 μm) and gaseous pollutants (nitrogen dioxide and ozone). Weather-related exposures included the daily mean and maximum temperatures, relative humidity and dew point. Across the four states, of 14,756,201 birth records, 94% (n = 13,612,485) deliveries were linked to hospitalisations, air pollution and weather exposures. The prevalence rates of abruption were 1.0% (n = 86,803) in California, 1.0% (n = 31,500) in Florida, 1.4% (n = 16,597) in Massachusetts and 1.2% (n = 10,030) in South Carolina. The distributions of air pollutants and weather-related variables were similar between abruption and non-abruption births. However, these factors exhibited geographic heterogeneity across states and between the warm and cold seasons. The APWA project aims to examine how air pollution and weather affect abruption. Strong linkage rates and geographic heterogeneity in environmental exposures provide an important foundation for achieving APWA's objectives.

title: Causes of First-week Mortality in Slower- and Fast-Growing Danish Broilers.
authorString: Al-Saeedi TA, Ida CN, Shibuya M, Kabell S, Jens P.
abstractText: Demand for slow-growing broilers in Europe is rising due to welfare concerns about rapid growth. First-week mortality (FWM), caused by infections and non-infectious factors, affects flock health. Data on slower-growing strains regarding FWM are limited. This study described first-week causes of death in commercial Danish broilers and included secondary exploratory comparisons among Rustic Gold, Ross 308-LD, and Ross 308-HD flocks. The study involved three rotations per farm/group (36 flocks, excluding three) and examined causes of death through necropsies of 2,022 dead chicks, with bacteriological examination performed in chicks with suspected infection. Of the recorded causes of death, 47% were classified as non-infectious and 53% as infectious based on predefined diagnostic criteria; individual chicks could have more than one recorded cause. The five most common causes of FWM, listed by frequency, were sepsis, cardiovascular collapse, renal disorders, leg disorders, and navel and yolk sac infection. No statistically significant differences were detected among Rustic Gold, Ross 308-LD, and Ross 308-HD in FWM proportions (all Tukey-adjusted p ≥ 0.207), causes of death, or related lesions (all overall BH-adjusted p-values ≥ 0.085). The most common bacterial species isolated across all organs of broiler chicks were Escherichia coli (62.4%) and Enterococcus faecalis (22.8%). In conclusion, exploratory comparisons under the commercial conditions evaluated detected no statistically significant differences in first-week mortality or recorded causes of death among Rustic Gold, Ross 308-LD, and Ross 308-HD flocks.

title: DNA barcoding and cellular senescence in atherosclerosis: Vascular smooth muscle cell lineage tracing and potential for future Senotherapeutics.
authorString: Pandey AC, Tsakiris E.
abstractText: Cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, and substantial risk persists even with optimal preventive therapy. Cellular senescence is a state of growth arrest accompanied by a senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) and has emerged as a candidate driver of vascular disease states. Recently, vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) have moved from passive bystanders in vascular diseases, including atherosclerosis, to pivotal cells integral to many facets of plaque biology. Within the lesion microenvironment, VSMCs undergo phenotypic switching and de-differentiation into macrophage-like, osteogenic, fibromyocyte, and senescent states, frequently extinguishing canonical lineage markers. However, defining the independent contribution of senescent VSMCs is complicated by two converging problems: the absence of a universal, specific senescence marker, and the loss of identity that accompanies VSMC trans-differentiation. We argue that DNA barcoding, a high-resolution, marker-independent lineage-tracing strategy matured in hematology and oncology, can address both obstacles. Building on the established foundation of multicolor reporters, we contrast static high-diversity libraries with evolving CRISPR-Cas9 recorders and human-translatable retrospective approaches, emphasizing that barcoding reports clonal lineage and must be paired with single-cell and spatial transcriptomics to position the senescent state on a reconstructed clonal tree. We further appraise emerging senotherapeutics, whose inconsistent and occasionally harmful in vivo results reflect a failure to identify the target cell rather than a failure of pharmacology. This distinction argues for lineage-restricted targeting. Integrating clonal barcoding, spatial multi-omics, and senescence atlases may help resolve the role of VSMC senescence in atherogenesis and enable cell-state-specific therapy.

title: Real-World 30-day Outcomes Following Commercial Adoption of the GORE EXCLUDER Thoracoabdominal Branch Endoprosthesis: A National Medicare Analysis.
authorString: Darling JD, Li S, Huang CY, van Galen I, Heindel P, Secemsky EA, Zettervall SL, Hicks CW, Schermerhorn ML, Stangenberg L.
abstractText:
Introduction

The Thoracoabdominal Branch Endoprosthesis (TAMBE) recently received FDA approval as the first off-the-shelf endovascular device for complex aneurysmal disease involving the visceral aorta. Prior to formal FDA approval, a pivotal pre-approval analysis demonstrated high procedural success, low perioperative morbidity, and no perioperative mortality. Using Medicare Fee-for-Service (FFS) data, we sought to evaluate real-world adoption patterns and 30-day outcomes following TAMBE implementation nationwide.

Methods

Medicare Fee-for-Service beneficiaries undergoing TAMBE between October 2024 and December 2025 were identified using the TAMBE-specific ICD-10-PCS code (X2VE3SA). Outcomes were compared to a contemporaneous cohort undergoing ≥4-vessel F/BEVAR in 2023, the year preceding TAMBE approval. Primary outcomes included 30-day mortality, stroke, myocardial infarction (MI), acute kidney injury (AKI), spinal cord ischemia (SCI), bowel ischemia, and reintervention, and were analyzed using Fine-Gray competing-risk regressions with adjustment for demographic, clinical, and procedural characteristics. Pre-specified sub-analyses examined outcomes by aortic indication, hospital procedure volume, and adoption period. Consistent with CMS small-cell suppression policy, any outcome frequencies <11 events were masked and not reported.

Results

The primary cohort consisted of 869 patients treated at 351 hospitals, compared with 678 patients undergoing 4-vessel F/BEVAR. TAMBE was associated with significantly higher unadjusted 30-day mortality (6.7% vs. 4.0%; P=.02), though this difference did not persist after adjustment (adjusted HR 1.37 [0.85-2.21]). No differences were observed in stroke (<1.3% vs. <1.6%), MI (2.0% vs. <1.6%), AKI (7.2% vs. 6.9%) or SCI (5.0% vs. 4.1%) (all P>.05). The majority of implanting hospitals (N=195; 56%) performed a single TAMBE during the study period, and 30-day outcomes did not differ significantly by hospital volume after adjustment. A sensitivity analysis restricted to unambiguously coded, elective TAMBE cases compared with elective F/BEVAR showed similarly elevated 30-day mortality (6.8% vs. 4.0%), albeit not statistically different following adjustment (aHR 1.46 [0.75-2.84]).

Conclusion

In this national analysis of Medicare FFS beneficiaries, real-world 30-day outcomes following TAMBE in the first year-plus of commercial availability were notably worse than those reported in the pivotal trial and early single-institution post-market series, with a nearly 7% 30-day mortality rate that persisted across indications, hospital volumes, and time periods. The rapid dissemination of TAMBE to over 351 hospitals, most performing only a single procedure, highlights a fundamental tension between the device's off-the-shelf accessibility and the institutional readiness required for safe deployment, underscoring the need for ongoing post-market surveillance, structured proctorship programs, and a more deliberate approach to patient and operator selection as TAMBE adoption continues.

title: Functional reserve as a complementary dimension of cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic burden: Independence transitions and long-term mortality.
authorString: Huang R, Huang M, Zhang R.
abstractText: People with similar cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) burden may differ in daily function. We examined independence transitions and mortality using cohort-specific functional measures. The China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) contributed 13,658 intervals from 10,381 participants for analyses of loss and observed recovery of independence in daily activities. The National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) contributed 13,764 adults and 2905 deaths for survey-weighted mortality analyses using a physical-function-based functional-reserve proxy. Both analyses used cohort-specific operational CKM strata. In CHARLS, adjusted probability differences comparing advanced clinical cardiovascular disease with low CKM burden were + 10.53 percentage points for loss of independence (95% confidence interval [CI] +7.70 to +13.37) and - 16.01 for observed recovery (95% CI -20.42 to -11.60). Both contrasts retained their direction when death was a mutually exclusive state at the next scheduled wave. In NHANES, adjusted standardized 10-year mortality risk differences comparing impaired with preserved physical function were + 6.28 percentage points (95% CI +4.36 to +8.20) in metabolic/kidney burden, +14.06 (+8.91 to +19.20) in advanced burden and + 3.13 (-0.32 to +6.59) in low burden. Relative mortality contrasts varied over follow-up (global P = .001). Advanced CKM burden was associated with less favorable independence transitions. Mortality differences by physical function were clearest in the two higher-burden strata and less precise in low CKM. Disease burden and observed function provide complementary information about vulnerability in later life.

title: Sex differences in ischemic heart disease mortality among patients with rheumatoid arthritis: a literature review.
authorString: Lancarotte I, Nobre MRC, Mansur AP.
abstractText: Cardiovascular Diseases (CVD) are the leading cause of mortality among patients with Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA), exhibiting incidence rates significantly higher than those in the Reference Population (RP). Chronic inflammation, traditional cardiovascular risk factors, and potential adverse effects of RA treatments contribute to this increased risk. This literature review examined sex differences in Ischemic Heart Disease (IHD) mortality among RA patients. We searched PubMed, EMBASE, and the Cochrane Library using the keywords "rheumatoid arthritis AND cardiovascular disease OR ischemic heart disease AND mortality". We included observational studies, reviews, and meta-analyses published in English until April 2022. Eligible studies reported data separately for males and females. Outcomes were analyzed for differences in IHD mortality relative to the RP and between sexes. Of 43 primary studies on CVD, 6 examined IHD mortality in men and women separately. Study durations ranged from 4- to 21-years, with follow-up periods averaging 7.05- to 11.4-years. Female participants represented 53.2% to 74.0% of the sample, with a mean age of 54.0- to 60.4-years. The total sample size included 47,144 patients. In four out of five studies, the Standardized Mortality Ratio (SMR) for IHD was higher in women with RA compared to the RP (SMR range: 1.41-1.95). Among men, three of five studies reported an SMR higher than the RP (range: 1.41-1.63). One study found that the risk of IHD mortality was greater in women than in men. Another study, using the age-adjusted incidence rate ratio, found higher IHD mortality in RA patients compared to the non-arthritis group (women: 1.6; men: 1.4) but noted no conclusive sex differences. IHD mortality in RA patients was higher than in RP, both for women and men. Women lost their typical protective advantage of a later onset of IHD, highlighting RA's substantial impact on cardiovascular outcomes in women.

title: Lifestyle Factors and Cardiometabolic Diseases in Middle-Aged and Older Adults: A Mixed Graphical and Bayesian Network Analysis With Sex-Specific Comparison.
authorString: Yao Z, Wang Y, Wang M, Tang H, Shi S, Zhong Z, Luo A.
abstractText: To examine the complex relationships between lifestyle factors and cardiometabolic diseases and to explore sex-specific network structures and dependency patterns among middle-aged and older adults. This cross-sectional study used data from Wave 5 (2020) of the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study. Lifestyle factors included physical activity, sleep duration, smoking, and alcohol consumption. Cardiometabolic diseases were identified based on self-reported physician diagnoses. Mixed graphical models and Bayesian networks were applied to investigate conditional associations, potential dependency structures, and sex differences. The study was reported according to the STROBE checklist. A total of 18,548 participants were included. In the mixed graphical models, alcohol consumption and physical activity showed the highest bridge expected influence in men, whereas physical activity and smoking were the most influential bridge nodes in women. Network Comparison Tests indicated no significant sex difference in global network strength, whereas network structure differed significantly between men and women. Bayesian network analysis identified a common dependency pattern across sexes involving physical activity, dyslipidemia, and diabetes. Sex-specific dependency patterns were also observed: alcohol consumption, stroke, heart disease, and diabetes were linked in a prominent pattern among men, whereas smoking, heart disease, and stroke were linked among women. In sensitivity analyses incorporating sociodemographic covariates, lifestyle-CMD associations remained evident in the overall sample and among women, whereas the corresponding associations were no longer clearly evident in the male network. Lifestyle behaviours and cardiometabolic diseases showed distinct network association patterns between men and women. However, the male-specific Bayesian network findings were sensitive to the inclusion of sociodemographic covariates and should be interpreted cautiously. These findings provide insights into the complex associations between lifestyle behaviours and cardiometabolic diseases. Longitudinal and intervention studies are needed to confirm effects and sex differences. Comprehensive, person-centred lifestyle assessment is important for the prevention and management of cardiometabolic diseases (CMDs). Network-based approaches may help identify complex associations between lifestyle behaviours and CMDs, providing insights for sex-sensitive behavioural assessment and risk stratification. No patient or public contribution.

title: Emerging Therapeutic Strategies Targeting Ferroptosis in Cardiomyocyte Injury: Molecular Mechanisms and Future Perspectives.
authorString: Thangavel L, Maida Engels SE.
abstractText: Ferroptosis is a regulated, iron-dependent form of cell death characterized by excessive lipid peroxidation resulting from disrupted iron homeostasis and impaired cellular antioxidant defenses. Increasing evidence identifies ferroptosis as a central contributor to cardiomyocyte injury in ischemia-reperfusion injury, anthracycline-induced cardiotoxicity, metabolic cardiac disorders, diabetic cardiomyopathy, and heart failure. Unlike apoptosis, necroptosis, autophagic cell death, and pyroptosis, ferroptosis is driven by glutathione depletion, glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) inactivation, and uncontrolled lipid peroxide accumulation, making it a distinct and potentially reversible therapeutic target. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the molecular mechanisms regulating cardiac ferroptosis, emphasizing the roles of GPX4, Solute Carrier Family 7 Member 11 (SLC7A11), Nuclear factor Erythroid 2-related Factor 2 (NRF2), Acyl-CoA Synthetase Long-Chain Family Member 4 (ACSL4), Ferroptosis Suppressor Protein 1 (FSP1), Dihydroorotate Dehydrogenase (DHODH), and ferritinophagy, together with their interactions with other regulated cell death pathways. We further discuss emerging therapeutic approaches, including natural phytochemicals, small-molecule ferroptosis inhibitors, and gene- and molecular target-based strategies, together with the cardio-oncology implications of inhibiting ferroptosis and the translational prospects offered by nanoparticle-based delivery, multi-omics integration, and artificial intelligence-assisted predictive modeling. Current translational challenges, including the absence of validated ferroptosis-specific biomarkers, limited human-relevant disease models, and interpatient heterogeneity, are critically evaluated. By integrating molecular mechanisms, therapeutic advances, and translational perspectives, this review provides an updated framework for understanding ferroptosis in cardiovascular toxicity and identifies key opportunities for developing clinically translatable ferroptosis-targeted cardioprotective strategies.

title: [Acute coronary syndromes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation].
authorString: Molnár B, Ahres A, Baranyai T, Pintér T, Fülöp G, Fontos G, Vértesaljai M, Dénes M, Pál M, Kolossváry M, Piróth Z, Jánosi A, Andréka P.
abstractText: Nearly half of patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation have concomitant significant coronary artery disease. In patients with severe aortic stenosis and coexisting obstructive coronary artery disease, several issues remain controversial, including the optimal diagnostic evaluation, the choice of treatment strategy (surgical, percutaneous, or conservative), the indication for and extent of coronary revascularization, and, if percutaneous coronary intervention is performed, its optimal timing. After transcatheter aortic valve implantation, selective coronary cannulation may be challenging in a subset of patients, an issue of increasing clinical relevance as accumulating evidence in recent years has progressively expanded transcatheter aortic valve implantation indications to patients with longer anticipated survival. Although the likelihood of requiring invasive coronary angiography or percutaneous coronary intervention after transcatheter aortic valve implantation is expected to increase in these patients, coronary events occurring during the post-transcatheter aortic valve implantation period - particularly life-threatening acute coronary syndromes - remain insufficiently characterized with respect to their incidence, clinical characteristics, predictors, and outcomes. In addition to conventional atherothrombotic mechanisms, the transcatheter heart valve itself may contribute to the development of acute coronary syndromes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation. Furthermore, the presence of a transcatheter heart valve may complicate invasive management because of technical challenges related to coronary access. This may be of particular importance in patients presenting with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction after transcatheter aortic valve implantation, in whom rapid and reliable coronary access and time-critical reperfusion are essential. The Gottsegen National Cardiovascular Center is one of the leading high-volume centers nationwide for the treatment of patients with severe aortic stenosis. Since the initiation of the institutional transcatheter aortic valve implantation program in 2008, more than 3000 procedures have been performed. Analysis of this large-scale registry may contribute to a better understanding of the currently unknown incidence, clinical characteristics and outcomes of acute coronary syndromes among patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation in Hungary. Orv Hetil. 2026; 167(47): 1887-1899.

title: Neuroimaging Profiling of Residual Ischemic Risk in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation and Acute Ischemic Stroke.
authorString: Kim DY, Han SG, Guk HS, Jeong HG, Lee KJ, Kim BJ, Han MK, Kim BK, Choi KH, Kim JT, Yum KS, Shin DI, Kim DE, Park JM, Kang K, Kim JG, Lee SJ, Lee M, Oh MS, Yu KH, Lee BC, Park HK, Cho YJ, Hong KS, Kang CH, Kim JG, Choi JC, Park H, Hong JH, Sohn SI, Park TH, Lee JY, Lee K, Kim WJ, Kwon JH, Kwon DH, Lee J, Ryu WS, Kim M, Lee H, Lee J, Gorelick PB, Bae HJ.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

Predicting recurrent ischemic stroke (RIS) in patients with acute ischemic stroke and atrial fibrillation remains a clinical challenge, as traditional risk scores such as CHA2DS2-VASc (congestive heart failure, hypertension, age ≥75 years, diabetes, previous stroke or transient ischemic attack, vascular disease, age 65 to 74 years, and sex category) often fail to account for the mechanistic insights provided by brain imaging. We aimed to evaluate the comprehensive role of neuroimaging parameters in identifying residual RIS risk and to determine their incremental value over clinical scoring systems.

Methods

In this nationwide, multicenter, prospective cohort study (East Asian Ischemic Stroke Patients With Atrial Fibrillation Study, Part II [EAST-AF]), we enrolled 2270 patients with acute ischemic stroke and atrial fibrillation from 14 stroke centers. We performed hierarchical profiling of magnetic resonance imaging parameters, including acute and chronic infarction characteristics and cerebral small vessel disease markers. Two-year cumulative incidences and adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) were estimated using cause-specific hazard models.

Results

During a median follow-up of 431 days, 123 patients experienced RIS (2-year cumulative incidence, 5.6%). The 2-year cumulative incidence of RIS was significantly higher in patients with chronic nonlacunar infarction (7.3% versus 4.6%; aHR, 1.50 [95% CI, 1.01-2.23]) and lacunes (9.0% versus 4.7%; aHR, 1.91 [95% CI, 1.28-2.86]). Mechanistically, lacunes in medullary artery territories, indicative of embolic sources, significantly increased RIS risk (aHR, 2.65 [95% CI, 1.56-4.49]), whereas those in deep perforator territories did not (aHR, 1.54 [95% CI, 0.94-2.53]). Notably, adding these neuroimaging markers to the CHA2DS2-VASc score significantly improved the model's discriminative ability, increasing the C statistic from 0.53 to 0.63 (P<0.001).

Conclusions

Comprehensive neuroimaging profiling, particularly focusing on embolic-pattern markers such as chronic infarctions and medullary lacunes, is essential for identifying high-risk patients with atrial fibrillation who may require intensified secondary prevention. Our findings suggest that imaging-based risk stratification provides critical prognostic information beyond conventional clinical scores.

title: An "Out-Of-The-Box" Use of the Export Advance Aspiration Catheter for PressureWire X Delivery in Challenging Coronary Anatomy.
authorString: Kumrić M, Crnčević N, Božić J.

journal.title: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions

abstractText: This technique describes a novel method for facilitating delivery of the pressure guidewires in challenging coronary anatomy, particularly in tortuous vessels. Pressure guidewires can be difficult to advance because their handling characteristics differ from conventional workhorse wires. Standard wire-exchange techniques are also limited because the pressure wire must be equalized in the ascending aorta before intracoronary measurements and its proximal receiver should remain connected thereafter. To address this problem, the Export Advance aspiration catheter is used as a supportive delivery conduit for the pressure wire. This approach provides additional support and directional control while preserving the required pressure-wire setup and equalization. The technique may therefore offer a simple and readily available solution for advancing pressure guidewires across complex or tortuous coronary segments when conventional direct wiring is difficult.

title: Superior Vena Cava Compromise During Transcatheter Atrial Septal Defect Closure: A Lesson in Implantation Geometry.
authorString: Maximilian P, Marina N, Haas N, Jakob A.

journal.title: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions

abstractText: Transcatheter closure procedure of multifenestrated aneurysmal atrial septal defects (ASDs) remains technically challenging: Optimal device selection and positioning should achieve complete closure of all fenestrations while accommodating the complex three-dimensional atrial septal anatomy and its relationship to adjacent cardiac structures. Because superior vena cava (SVC) obstruction is exceedingly rare, it may easily be overlooked unless caval venous inflow is systematically evaluated by transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) after device deployment following a pre-release TEE checklist. We report the case of a 5-year-old girl with a multifenestrated aneurysmal secundum ASD. A Uni-occluder was not available; therefore, a patent foramen ovale (PFO) occluder was used for defect closure, which resulted in near-complete obstruction of the SVC by the right atrial disc of the device. The complication was recognized after positioning by intraprocedural TEE, prompting device retrieval prior to release. Subsequent closure with a dedicated ASD occluder achieved complete closure of all fenestrations without compromising caval venous return. This case highlights the importance of a concept we refer to as implantation geometry: the interplay between device-specific design, the implantation site, and complex three-dimensional septal anatomy. Recognition and careful assessment of this relationship will help optimize procedural planning and improve procedural safety in selected patients with complex, multifenestrated ASDs. Comprehensive three-dimensional anatomical assessment, appropriate device selection, and systematic TEE evaluation of the cavoatrial junction before device release are essential for safe transcatheter closure of multifenestrated ASDs-even when defect sizing appears appropriate. In particular, the geometric characteristics of PFO occluders, including their relatively large right atrial disc, should be considered when assessing the risk of SVC obstruction.

title: The Piezo1 Paradox in Aging and Age-Related Disease: Bidirectional Mechanosensory Dysfunction and Therapeutic Implications.
authorString: Zhai X, Li B, Feng J, Zhang X, Duan X.
abstractText: Aging is accompanied by profound changes in the mechanical properties of tissues, driving cellular dysfunction, and age-related diseases. Central to this process is Piezo1, a key mechanosensitive ion channel that converts physical stimuli into intracellular Ca2+ signals. This review synthesizes current evidence illustrating the dual, context-dependent role of Piezo1 in aging-termed the "Piezo1 Paradox." In certain tissues such as bone and bone marrow stromal cells, aging is associated with a loss of Piezo1 function, impairing mechanotransduction, and tissue maintenance. Conversely, in vascular, fibrotic, and some metabolic tissues, aging leads to Piezo1 overactivation, promoting inflammation, fibrosis, and cellular senescence. We explore how these divergent changes contribute to prevalent age-related disorders including osteoporosis, cardiovascular disease, neurodegeneration, and metabolic dysfunction. Furthermore, we discuss emerging therapeutic strategies that aim to restore Piezo1 signaling within a tissue-specific "Goldilocks zone," highlighting pharmacological modulators, biophysical interventions, and targeted delivery systems. By framing Piezo1 as a tunable mechanosensory node, this review underscores its potential as a therapeutic target for promoting healthy aging and mitigating age-related pathologies.

title: Mechanistic Insights into Celastrol's Anti-Inflammatory Effects: From Molecular Targets to Therapeutic Potential.
authorString: Khatami SH, Moshari M, Gouhari F, Ehtiati S, Ariannik M, Talebi S, Ahmadi Abdashti AR, Fakhrzadegan M, Zandi R.
abstractText: Chronic inflammation is a central pathogenic driver of a wide spectrum of diseases, including autoimmune disorders, neurodegenerative conditions, cardiovascular diseases, and metabolic syndromes. Despite advances in anti-inflammatory therapeutics, limitations such as incomplete efficacy and adverse effects necessitate the discovery of novel multitarget agents. Celastrol, a pentacyclic triterpenoid quinone methide derived from Tripterygium wilfordii Hook. f. (thunder god vine), has emerged as a potent natural product with remarkable pharmacological properties. This review comprehensively analyzes the mechanism underlying the anti-inflammatory effects of celastrol, with a particular focus on the nuclear factor-kappa B (NF-κB) and NLRP3 inflammasome axis because of their central role in mediating the therapeutic efficacy of celastrol. We highlight its ability to modulate key signaling pathways, including NF-κB inhibition, heat shock protein 90 (Hsp90) disruption, NLR family pyrin domain containing 3 inflammasome suppression, and the regulation of oxidative stress via the nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2/heme oxygenase-1 axis. We examined the therapeutic potential of celastrol across various disease models and demonstrated its efficacy in attenuating pathologies such as rheumatoid arthritis (RA), neuroinflammation, atherosclerosis, inflammatory bowel disease, and obesity-related metabolic disorders. Furthermore, we address the significant pharmacokinetic challenges hindering clinical translation, such as poor water solubility and limited oral bioavailability, and discuss innovative formulation strategies, including liposomal, polymeric, and targeted nanoparticle delivery systems designed to increase efficacy and minimize toxicity. By synthesizing current knowledge on the molecular targets and therapeutic applications of celastrol, this review underscores its promise as a multitarget anti-inflammatory agent and outlines future directions for structure-activity relationship studies, combination therapies, and clinical development.

title: Spinal Cord Injury-Induced HDL Remodeling Contributes to Accelerated Atherosclerosis.
authorString: Richey LE, Bailey WM, Saini MK, Walker JE, Kopper TJ, Stewart AN, Howatt DA, Daugherty A, Gordon SM, Park AJ, Gensel JC.
abstractText: Individuals with spinal cord injury (SCI) develop accelerated atherosclerosis that is incompletely explained by traditional cardiovascular risk factors. Although elevated low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) is strongly associated with atherosclerosis in the general population, lipoprotein profiles after SCI are characterized by reduced high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) without LDL-C elevation, suggesting altered HDL biology. In this study, we examined HDL composition and function in humans and animals with SCI. In humans, HDL-C was reduced in both the subacute (1-6 months) and chronic (>1 year) phases after SCI. Subacute plasma proteomics revealed remodeling of HDL protein networks, including loss of structural apolipoproteins and enrichment of complement and innate immune proteins. Functionally, HDL from SCI mice promoted proinflammatory macrophage gene expression relative to sham HDL. Finally, deletion of apolipoprotein A-I, the principal structural apolipoprotein of HDL, attenuated atherosclerosis following SCI in vivo. Together, these findings identify proinflammatory HDL remodeling as a mechanism contributing to accelerated atherosclerosis after SCI.

title: Barriers to successful ECMO clinical research: A ClinicalTrials.gov analysis of trial termination.
authorString: Ahmed YB, Noda K, Woo HYJ, Soulé Z, Kwon DK, Allegakoen J, Wang S, Cao M, Whitman GJR, Cho SM.

journal.title: The International journal of artificial organs

abstractText: The rate, timing, reasons, and correlates of premature study termination have not been described for extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO). Cross-sectional analysis of ECMO-focused studies on ClinicalTrials.gov (retrieved 22 May 2026) with blinded re-screening and adjudication. Reasons for termination were coded independently by two reviewers. Associations were tested with Fisher's exact, Firth logistic, and cause-specific Cox models, with completion as a competing event. Of 450 studies, 36 (8.0%, 95% CI 5.8%-10.9%) had been terminated or withdrawn, with cumulative incidences of 8.9% at 3 years and 11.7% at five. Sponsor or organizational decisions (36.1%) and recruitment failure (33.3%) led the reasons, and none was stopped for safety. After adjustment, no design characteristic was independently associated with termination. The unadjusted FDA excess was explained by United States location (adjusted OR 9.82, 95% CI 4.17-23.49). Recruitment status was unknown for 27.4% of non-United States versus 5.4% of United States studies. About one in 12 registered ECMO studies had been terminated or withdrawn, rising to one in 8 by 5 years. Discontinuation was attributed to organizational and recruitment factors rather than to safety, and the United States excess likely reflects differences in registry reporting practice.

title: Isoliquiritin ameliorates diabetic cardiomyopathy through inhibiting the TLR4/NF-κB signaling.
authorString: Yin J, Zhang Y, Jin W, Cong J.
abstractText:
Objective

The aim was to explore the function of isoliquiritin (ILQ) on diabetic cardiomyopathy (DCM) and its potential mechanisms.

Methods

The roles of ILQ on cardiac function and myocardial damage of DCM rats were assessed using myocardial enzymes measurement, echocardiography, HE staining, WGA staining, Masson staining and western blot. The effects of ILQ on cardiomyocyte apoptosis and inflammation in myocardial tissues of DCM rats were evaluated by using TUNEL and western blot. In vitro, the roles of ILQ on HG-induced H9C2 cells damage were assessed by using CCK-8, western blot and flow cytometry. The mechanisms of ILQ in DCM were explored by using network pharmacology analysis, CETSA, DARTS assay, western blot, immunofluorescence staining, CHX chase assay, ubiquitination assay and rescue experiments through TLR4 overexpression.

Results

ILQ was demonstrated to improve cardiac function, and alleviate cardiac hypertrophy and fibrosis in DCM rats. ILQ inhibited cardiomyocyte apoptosis and alleviated inflammation in DCM rats. ILQ treatment also repressed HG-induced H9C2 cell fibrosis, apoptosis and inflammation. Mechanically, ILQ could suppress the protein expression of TLR4 in H9C2 cells via enhancing its ubiquitination. Besides, ILQ could inhibit TLR4/NF-κB signaling in both HG-induced H9C2 cells and DCM rats. The rescue experiments indicated that TLR4 overexpression reversed the effect of ILQ on HG-induced H9C2 cell damage.

Conclusion

ILQ might ameliorate DCM through repressing TLR4/NF-κB signaling, thus reducing myocardial fibrosis and hypertrophy, and suppressing cardiomyocyte apoptosis and inflammation.

title: Clinical features, diagnosis and outcomes of camrelizumab-induced myocarditis.
authorString: Hu X, Pan Y, Wu Z, Sun W, Wang C.
abstractText: Background This study aimed to perform a pooled analysis of published case reports and case series to summarize the clinical characteristics, treatment patterns, and outcomes of camrelizumab-induced myocarditis.Methods Clinical reports of camrelizumab-induced myocarditis published up to May 31, 2026 were collected by searching Chinese and English databases; clinical data were then extracted and retrospectively analyzed.Results A total of 21 male (63.6%) and 12 female (36.4%) patients were enrolled, with a median age of 67 years (range: 44-77). The median time from camrelizumab initiation to myocarditis onset was 22.5 days (range: 1-180), and the median number of treatment cycles administered was 2 (range: 1-12). Patients were asymptomatic (18.2%) or experienced fatigue (36.4%), chest tightness (33.3%), shortness of breath (27.3%), palpitations (21.2%), and ptosis (21.2%). Laboratory tests revealed elevated cardiac injury biomarkers in affected patients. Electrocardiographic findings were variable, including normal tracings, ST-T segment changes (62.5%), sinus tachycardia (28.1%), premature ventricular contractions (18.8%), right bundle branch block (18.8%), and atrioventricular block (15.6%). Following camrelizumab discontinuation and treatment with systemic steroids plus intravenous immunoglobulin, 81.8% of patients achieved gradual symptomatic improvement. Ultimately, 12.1% of patients died of myocarditis-related complications.Conclusion Myocarditis is a fatal immune-related adverse event of camrelizumab. Cardiac injury biomarkers, clinical symptoms, and electrocardiographic changes should be routinely monitored during camrelizumab therapy. Individualized therapeutic regimens should be formulated according to disease severity, with systemic steroids and intravenous immunoglobulin as the first-line treatment.

title: Anatomic-Hemodynamic Discordance in Low-Flow, Low-Gradient Aortic Stenosis: A Clinical Challenge.
authorString: Mousavi RA, Argulian E, Clavel MA, Basera P, Enwere C, Soroa M, Schober A, Kammerlander AA, Alizadeh L, Ferrandez-Escarabajal M, Onishi T, Mannina C, Safi L, Khera S, Tang GHL, Dangas GD, Sharma SK, Kini AS, Halperin JL, Bhatt DL, Pibarot P, Lerakis S.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

Anatomic assessment using aortic valve calcification (AVC) and hemodynamic evaluation with dobutamine stress echocardiography are recommended to diagnose true severe low-flow, low-gradient aortic stenosis (AS); however, concordance between methods is limited. The mean gradient (MG) to effective orifice area (EOA) ratio has recently been proposed for hemodynamic assessment, with ≥25 indicating severe AS. We aimed to evaluate concordance between anatomic and hemodynamic AS severity defined by AVC and MG/EOA.

Methods

Patients with low-flow, low-gradient AS were stratified by MG/EOA (≥25 versus <25) and sex-specific AVC cutoffs into concordant severe (MG/EOA ≥25, high AVC), concordant nonsevere (MG/EOA <25, low AVC), discordant hemodynamic severe/anatomic nonsevere (MG/EOA ≥25, low AVC), and discordant anatomic severe/hemodynamic nonsevere (MG/EOA <25, high AVC).

Results

Among 431 patients (mean age, 80±8 years; 36% women), median AVC was 1631 (interquartile range, 1156-2330) Agatston units in men and 1080 (interquartile range, 719-1553) Agatston units in women. Hemodynamic severe AS occurred in 289 (67%), and anatomic severe AS in 159 (37%). Concordant grading was observed in 243 (56%) patients. Among hemodynamic severe AS, 159 (55%) were anatomic nonsevere, and among anatomic severe AS, 29 (18%) were hemodynamic nonsevere. Across 25 combinations of AVC and MG/EOA thresholds, concordance ranged from 36.7% to 64.7% and remained below two thirds.

Conclusions

Concordance between AVC and MG/EOA is modest and remains limited across alternative thresholds, with most discordance due to hemodynamic severe/anatomic nonsevere AS. This may reflect limitations of current AVC cutoffs or indicate earlier disease detection by hemodynamic assessment, leaving optimal management of discordant patients uncertain.

title: β-hydroxybutyrate and cancer: an update on conflicting roles and therapeutic targeting.
authorString: Wu S, Xie A, Zhang M, Wang J, Zeng W, Zhang Y, Ye J, Zhou L.
abstractText: Cancer metabolic reprogramming is a hallmark of malignancy, within which ketone body metabolism, particularly β-hydroxybutyrate (BHB), has garnered significant attention due to its complex and paradoxical roles in tumor biology. This review systematically examines the multifaceted functions of BHB in cancer, spanning molecular mechanisms to clinical translation, and synthesizes the conflicting evidence regarding its tumor-suppressive and tumor-promoting effects. We first explore the potential of BHB as a diagnostic, prognostic, and predictive biomarker, where its differential abundance across cancers such as colorectal and pancreatic cancer underscores its context-dependent nature. We then examine the underlying molecular mechanisms that account for these opposing effects. A key focus of this review is the integration of recent advances in combination therapies involving BHB alongside chemotherapy, targeted therapy, immunotherapy, and physical treatments, highlighting its emerging potential as a promising sensitizer for combination regimens. Finally, we systematically outline the core controversies and challenges in the field, attributing the diversity of BHB effects to heterogeneity in tumor metabolic phenotypes, molecular subtypes, and the tumor microenvironment. By constructing a framework that integrates mechanistic diversity, clinical evidence, and combination therapeutic strategies, this review underscores the imperative to shift from a "one-size-fits-all" paradigm toward precision stratification based on tumor metabolic phenotypes, thereby providing a theoretical foundation for the development of safe and effective BHB/ketogenic diet-based combination therapies.

title: Development and performance evaluation of a prediction model for identifying high risk populations for inaccurate initial triage in adult emergency settings.
authorString: Chunyu W, Dongyue S, Ying Z, Cheng C.
abstractText: Emergency Department (ED) crowding has been recognized as a major public health problem worldwide. Excessive triage will prolong patients' waiting time and increase the workload of triage nurses while inadequate triage may raise the risk of adverse medical safety events. This study aimed to identify high risk populations for inaccurate initial triage in adult emergency settings, construct a risk prediction model, and evaluate its predictive value. This single-center retrospective observational study enrolled adult patients triaged in the ED from January to December 2024, and a total of 5321 patients were finally included. Descriptive statistics were computed, and univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were conducted. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and Hosmer-Lemeshow test were applied, and the diagnostic sensitivity and specificity of the model were calculated. Night shift attendance(OR = 1.383), chief complaint of digestive system symptoms(OR = 1.707), chief complaint of trauma(OR = 2.727)，chief complaint of cardiovascular system(OR = 0.651), triage level 1(OR = 0.057), and heart rate(OR = 0.948) were influencing factors for the accuracy of initial triage among adult emergency patients. The multivariate logistic regression prediction model constructed based on these factors had an AUC of 0.723(95%CI: 0.697-0.749), with a sensitivity of 64.6% and a specificity of 70.9%. The prediction model established in this study enables triage nurses to early identify high-risk populations with inaccurate initial triage in adult emergency settings.

title: Electro-Structural Remodeling Reversal With Myosin Inhibitor in Apical Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.
authorString: Wu X, Wang L, Zhang M, Xu L, Wang D, Jiang W, Song L, Kang L.
abstractText:
Background

Myosin inhibitor is a novel treatment for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), but evidence for the efficacy in apical hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (AHCM) is lacking.

Case summary

A 41-year-old man with AHCM presented with progressive dyspnea and chest pain despite beta-blocker therapy. Besides classic electrocardiography changes, echocardiography revealed a high-velocity apical jet. Mavacamten 5 mg daily was initiated. By week 32, N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide and apical flow velocity normalized. T-wave inversion was absent at week 89 and was normalized by week 135. At week 145, magnetic resonance showed no further progression of myocardial fibrosis.

Discussion

To our knowledge, this is the first report of a myosin inhibitor reversing symptoms, structural remodeling, and electrophysiological abnormalities in AHCM. Patients with AHCM could benefit from long-term treatment, and the electrocardiogram may serve as a marker of therapeutic response.

Take-home messages

Myosin inhibitors may benefit ventricular remodeling, especially electrophysiological abnormalities, in patients with AHCM. Further research is warranted.

title: The association of triglyceride-glucose-weight-adjusted waist index with cardiovascular disease risk in a population with operationalized cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome stages 0-3: Insights from CHARLS.
authorString: Zhao P, Gan W, Shi D, Qu H, Shi J, Ma Z, Qiu Z, Li G, He T, Chen M, Li D.
abstractText: The triglyceride-glucose-weight-adjusted waist index (TyG-WWI) is a novel composite marker of metabolic dysfunction in cardiovascular disease (CVD). Its association with incident CVD across cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome stages 0-3 remains unevaluated. CKM syndrome stages were operationalized using the variables available in CHARLS. Because cardiac injury biomarkers and coronary artery calcium scores were unavailable, stage 3 was defined using surrogate criteria: eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m2 or a Framingham Risk Score ≥20%. In this longitudinal cohort study, 5788 adults with complete data for operationalized CKM syndrome stages 0-3 from the CHARLS dataset (2011-2020) were included. Cox regression, restricted cubic splines, subgroup analysis, integrated discrimination improvement (IDI), continuous net reclassification improvement (NRI), median improvement (MED), and variance inflation factor (VIF) were conducted. Elevated TyG-WWI was associated with increased cumulative CVD incidence. In fully adjusted models, TyG-WWI was independently associated with CVD risk (HR = 1.051, 95% CI: 1.001-1.103), with a linear dose-response relationship. Subgroup analyses were consistent, with no significant interactions (all P > 0.05). Incremental predictive metrics (IDI, continuous NRI, MED) were not significant (all P > 0.05), and all VIFs were <5. TyG-WWI is positively and linearly associated with incident CVD among individuals with operationalized CKM stages 0-3 in this complete-case sample, suggesting potential utility as a reference indicator for cardiovascular risk appraisal. Its incremental predictive value beyond conventional risk factors was limited, and selection bias from missing data warrants cautious generalization. Not applicable.

title: NAMPT and NAD<sup>+</sup> in health and disease: emerging perspectives from molecular mechanisms to therapeutic strategies.
authorString: Wang L, Deng X, Su Y, Liu C, Luo Y, Deng X, Wang L, Chen J, Wu T.
abstractText: Nicotinamide phosphoribosyltransferase (NAMPT) is the rate-limiting enzyme of the nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD⁺) salvage pathway and a key regulator of cellular energy metabolism, redox homeostasis, stress responses, and NAD⁺-dependent signaling. Through its intracellular form iNAMPT, NAMPT sustains NAD⁺ production and the activity of enzymes such as sirtuins, PARPs, and CD38; its extracellular form eNAMPT has also been implicated in interorgan communication and inflammatory signaling. Here, we review the molecular basis of the NAMPT-NAD⁺ axis, including NAD⁺ biosynthetic pathways, subcellular compartmentalization, circadian regulation, and the distinct proposed functions of iNAMPT and eNAMPT. We then evaluate its physiological and pathological roles in metabolic disorders, liver diseases, cancer, inflammatory and cardiovascular conditions, and neurodegenerative diseases. Current evidence supports a context-dependent role for NAMPT: reduced NAMPT activity and NAD⁺ depletion may contribute to metabolic dysfunction, tissue injury, and neuronal vulnerability, whereas elevated NAMPT activity can promote tumor metabolic fitness and inflammatory responses. However, NAMPT expression alone does not reliably indicate NAD⁺ pathway dependence, because outcomes are influenced by tissue context, disease stage, NAD⁺ consumption, precursor availability, and NAPRT-mediated metabolic bypass. Therapeutically, NAD⁺ precursors, NAMPT activation, and indirect modulators may be relevant in selected degenerative and metabolic settings, whereas NAMPT inhibitors remain under investigation for cancer. Their translation is limited by systemic NAD⁺ depletion, hematological and gastrointestinal toxicity, pharmacokinetic constraints, and tumor heterogeneity. Future progress will require tissue-selective modulation, direct pharmacodynamic monitoring, and biomarker-guided patient stratification.

title: From prophylaxis to precision immunotherapy via engineering vaccine platforms.
authorString: Cabral-Miranda G, Silva JDQ, Hamaguchi B, Giugni FR, Durães-Carvalho R, Cabral-Marques O, Câmara NOS, Sabino EC, Krieger JE.
abstractText: Vaccines are evolving from antigen-delivery products into modular technologies designed to elicit specific immune functions. Although prophylactic vaccination aims to establish protective memory before exposure, therapeutic vaccination must redirect immunity in the presence of persistent antigen, immune suppression or pathological tissue remodeling. In this Review, we examine how antigen architecture, innate sensing, antigen-presenting-cell targeting, platform design and administration route jointly determine vaccine-induced immune programmes. We compare the distinct requirements of prevention and treatment, focusing on cancer, chronic viral infection and fibrosis, and assess the opportunities and limitations of RNA vaccines, viral vectors, virus-like particles, adjuvants and combination strategies. We then consider how systems vaccinology and artificial intelligence can inform immunogen design and response prediction, while distinguishing computational promise from experimentally validated benefit. We argue that clinical progress depends on matching each vaccine formulation to a defined biological barrier and demonstrating tissue-level activity, safety, durability and practical deployability. This framework connects vaccine engineering to measurable protective or therapeutic outcomes without assuming that any single platform is universally optimal. By integrating immunological principles with advances in vaccine engineering, this Review provides a conceptual basis for selecting and combining technologies according to disease-specific requirements. Ultimately, this perspective may help guide the development of more precise, adaptable and clinically relevant vaccination strategies, bridging the gap between platform innovation and improved outcomes in prevention and therapy.

title: Smyd1 regulates H3K4me3 to support adaptive fatty acid oxidation in the adult heart during lipid overload
authorString: Mukai R, Oka S, Sung E, Takayama K, Ikeda S, Matsushita M, Takada T, Sadoshima J.
abstractText: Obesity and metabolic syndrome are major risk factors for heart failure, and impaired fatty acid oxidation (FAO) is a key contributor to metabolic dysfunction in obesity-related cardiomyopathy. However, how the heart maintains FAO and adapts to chronic lipid overload remains poorly understood. Here, we identify SET and MYND domain-containing protein 1 (Smyd1), a muscle–specific histone methyltransferase, as an early compensatory regulator of cardiac metabolism in response to lipid overload. In wild-type mouse hearts, high–fat diet (HFD) feeding induced transient increases in Smyd1 expression and H3K4me3 levels during the early–to–mid phase of metabolic stress, both of which returned to baseline levels during prolonged HFD exposure. Single–cell RNA sequencing further revealed that this adaptive increase in Smyd1 expression occurred predominantly in cardiomyocytes. In contrast, cardiac-specific Smyd1 heterozygous knockout mice exhibited accelerated cardiac dysfunction, left ventricular dilation, increased myocardial fibrosis, and reduced survival following HFD feeding. Mechanistically, Smyd1 deficiency impaired the adaptive upregulation of key FAO–related genes and reduced cardiac FAO activity. Furthermore, co-immunoprecipitation analysis revealed an interaction between Smyd1 and peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha (PPARα), suggesting a potential mechanism by which Smyd1 supports FAO gene expression. Taken together, these findings identify Smyd1 as an early compensatory regulator that supports FAO–dependent metabolic adaptation and protects the heart against lipid overload-induced cardiac dysfunction. This adaptive mechanism, involving H3K4me3 regulation and the Smyd1–PPARα interaction, may provide potential therapeutic targets for therapeutic strategies aimed at preserving cardiac metabolic flexibility in obesity-related cardiomyopathy.

title: Evaluation of post-occlusion hepatofugal blood flow on surgeon decision making during ligation of portosystemic shunts in 53 dogs.
authorString: Ray SE, Folk CA, Bechtold MA, Center SA, Flanders JA, Lopez DJ.
abstractText:
Objective

To determine whether hepatofugal contrast flow or caudal vena cava (CdVC) contrast filling during post-occlusion intraoperative mesenteric portovenography (PO-IOMP) were associated with the degree of extrahepatic portosystemic shunt (EHPSS) ligation performed.

Study design

Retrospective observational cohort study.

Animals

A total of 53 dogs.

Methods

Data were collected retrospectively for dogs that underwent suture ligation of a single EHPSS with concurrent intraoperative mesenteric portovenography (IOMP). Review of IOMP studies was performed in a blinded manner by a single author. Logistic regression was used to evaluate associations between PO-IOMP interpretations and the degree of EHPSS ligation selected by the primary surgeon. Identified associations were further investigated using a multivariable model to control for confounding variables.

Results

Complete ligation was performed in 37/53 dogs (69.8%), partial ligation in 13/53 (24.5%), and no ligation in 3/53 (5.7%). Hepatofugal contrast flow during PO-IOMP was identified in 21/53 dogs (39.6%). Dogs with hepatofugal contrast flow during PO-IOMP were more likely to have undergone incomplete ligation (partial or none) when controlling for confounding variables (odds ratio [OR] 7.06, 95% CI: 1.49-33.44, p = .014). Absence of CdVC filling during PO-IOMP was identified in 11/53 dogs (20.8%). No association was identified between dogs lacking CdVC filling during PO-IOMP and incomplete EHPSS ligation (OR 1.43, 95% CI: 0.35-5.79, p = .617). Non-responsive postoperative portal hypertension was identified in 2/53 dogs (3.8%), both necessitating euthanasia.

Conclusion

Hepatofugal contrast flow on PO-IOMP was associated with the decision to perform incomplete EHPSS ligation.

Clinical significance

The identification of post-occlusion hepatofugal contrast flow may aid in patient-specific EHPSS ligation decision making.

title: Metabolic phenotypes and female reproductive impairment: cross-sectional associations with infertility and impaired fecundity.
authorString: Hu X, Zhang Y, Wu J, Jiang X.

journal.title: Gynecological endocrinology : the official journal of the International Society of Gynecological Endocrinology

abstractText:
Background

The joint role of adiposity and metabolic dysfunction in female reproductive impairment remains uncertain. We examined cross-sectional associations of metabolic phenotypes with infertility and impaired fecundity in women of reproductive age.

Methods

We analyzed 4,862 women from pooled 2011-2019 survey data. Normal weight was defined as BMI 18.5-24.9 kg/m2 and overweight/obesity as BMI ≥ 25 kg/m2. Metabolic unhealth was defined by the presence of at least one of three survey indicators: hypertension, diabetes/prediabetes, or dyslipidemia. Survey-weighted logistic regression, sensitivity analyzes, subgroup interaction tests, and restricted cubic spline models were used.

Results

Among 4,862 women, 575 (11.8%) met the infertility outcome and 774 (15.9%) met the impaired-fecundity outcome. Relative to metabolically healthy normal weight (MHNW), fully adjusted odds ratios for infertility were 1.28 (95% CI 1.04-1.58) for MUNW, 1.32 (1.00-1.75) for MHO, and 1.43 (1.16-1.76) for MUO. For impaired fecundity, the corresponding estimates were 1.24 (0.95-1.60), 1.28 (1.00-1.65), and 1.40 (1.13-1.74). Exploratory subgroup analyzes did not support a robust age-specific interaction after multiplicity control, and spline analyzes provided mixed evidence for continuous adiposity measures.

Conclusions

The metabolically unhealthy overweight/obesity phenotype showed the most consistent association with infertility and impaired fecundity. These cross-sectional findings support an association between combined adiposity and metabolic abnormalities and reproductive impairment, but they do not establish causality and require confirmation in prospective studies.

title: Different diameters of particulate matter exposure and health outcomes: An umbrella review.
authorString: Lu G, Jin Y, Zeng B, Luo Y, Zhu G, Zhou X, Zhang Z, Huang W, Wei C, He Y, Zuoqiu S, Zou X, Zhan Y, Yang L, Qiu S, Wei Q.
abstractText: Airborne particulate matter (PM) is a pervasive environmental hazard, yet the comparative toxicity of different aerodynamic diameters-particularly sub-micron particles (PM<sub>1</sub>)-remains insufficiently characterized in environmental health risk assessments. To address this, we conducted an umbrella review systematically synthesizing observational meta-analyses to evaluate the dose-response associations between PM fractions (PM<sub>10</sub>, PM<sub>2.5</sub>, and PM<sub>1</sub>) and diverse health outcomes. By harmonizing effect estimates and assessing evidence quality via the GRADE framework, we observed a potential 'size effect' influencing pollutant toxicity. Our comparative analyses suggested that PM<sub>1</sub> may be associated with relatively stronger adverse effects than larger fractions across multiple physiological domains. Notably, PM<sub>1</sub> exposure was associated with the highest relative risks for metabolic disorders, including metabolic syndrome (RR=1.30), childhood obesity (RR=1.41), and childhood hypertension (RR=1.61), significantly outpacing the effects of PM<sub>2.5</sub> and PM<sub>10</sub>. Furthermore, moderate-quality evidence highlighted a striking systemic vulnerability, with PM<sub>1</sub> demonstrating a robust association with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD, RR=1.59). Similar size-dependent toxicity gradients were observed for neurodevelopmental (autism) and respiratory (asthma) outcomes. The amplified toxicity of PM<sub>1</sub> is likely mediated by its higher alveolar deposition efficiency, larger specific surface area for toxicant adsorption, and enhanced capacity to translocate across biological barriers (e.g., air-blood barrier) to induce systemic oxidative stress. These findings highlight that current air quality regulations, which predominantly rely on PM<sub>2.5</sub> and PM<sub>10</sub> mass concentrations, may not fully capture the systemic and metabolic health burdens of smaller particles. Incorporating size-resolved PM<sub>1</sub> monitoring into environmental safety frameworks could be an important step toward better estimating human health risks and developing targeted mitigation strategies.

title: Network pharmacology and molecular dynamics uncover RMJ's targets and mechanisms for treating atherosclerosis.
authorString: Wang W, Wang J, Wang H, Zhang H, Lin Y, Gu Y.
abstractText:
Objective

Atherosclerosis involves complex pathogenesis including inflammation, lipid disorders, and abnormal autophagy, yet current treatments are limited by adverse reactions and drug resistance, highlighting the need for novel strategies.

Methods

This study adopted network pharmacology, molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulation to explore the multi-target mechanism of Soft Pulse Decoction (RMJ) in treating atherosclerosis (AS) and its autophagy-regulating effect, combined with in vivo rabbit experiments for verification.

Results

Core targets of RMJ predicted by network pharmacology involve the PI3K/Akt and MAPK pathways, regulating cell proliferation, apoptosis and autophagy. Molecular dynamics simulations identified four stable high-affinity compound-target complexes. In vivo rabbit experiments further showed that RMJ reduced serum lipid levels and carotid plaque area, accompanied by activation of the PI3K/Akt/mTOR pathway and inhibition of excessive plaque autophagy. These experiments supported the involvement of the PI3K/Akt/mTOR pathway but did not directly confirm that RMJ constituents target ESR1 or PIK3CA in vivo.

Conclusion

This study provides a theoretical basis for further investigation of the traditional Chinese medicine compound Soft Pulse Decoction, and also offers a new perspective for the development of anti-atherosclerosis drugs from the perspective of autophagy. The link between the TCM principle of "tonifying the kidney and benefiting qi" and the molecular effects of the identified compounds remains a hypothesis requiring further validation.

title: Novel Proteolyzed Aortic Extracellular Matrix Substrate Coating as a Model to Assess Aneurysmal Smooth Muscle Cell Behavior <i>In Vitro</i>.
authorString: Krajewski T, Ramamurthi A.
abstractText: Abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAAs) are localized expansions of the abdominal aortic wall that grow slowly to potentially fatal rupture. AAAs result from irreversible loss of structural extracellular matrix (ECM) due to upregulated proteolytic activity. Surgery to treat AAAs is risky; therefore, new drug-based approaches are needed to slow aneurysm growth by reversing ECM pathophysiology. This necessitates the study of disease-relevant cells in vitro, in this case smooth muscle cells (SMCs); however, current in vitro models are limited due to SMC dedifferentiation on conventional plastic substrates, which cause a loss of disease-relevant features. This study generated a physiologically relevant culture model to assess matrix regenerative and reparative responses of AAA SMCs. We developed a surface coating of ECM from digested aortic wall tissue that mimics the AAA microenvironment and maintains the diseased phenotype of AAA SMCs in vitro. When cultured on ECM substrates, late passage SMCs (EaRASMCs) from a rat elastase injury AAA model retained spindle-shaped morphology, gene expression indicative of a synthetic phenotype, and increased chemoattractant expression. These behaviors are more evocative of subprimary aneurysmal cells compared with traditionally cultured SMCs, demonstrating the capability of our native ECM substrate to modulate and promote pathophysiologically relevant SMC phenotypes in vitro. This model system offers a promising platform for screening aneurysmal SMC responses to therapeutics similar to expected in vivo outcomes.

title: RIPK4 links NF-κB-associated signaling and VEGF production to melanoma-endothelial communication.
authorString: Wroński N, Łoboda A, Gazda A, Wolnicka-Głubisz A.
abstractText:
Purpose

Melanoma progression is driven by aberrant intracellular signaling and reciprocal communication with the tumor microenvironment. Although receptor-interacting protein kinase 4 (RIPK4) has been implicated in melanoma progression, its role in tumor-endothelial communication remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated the contribution of RIPK4 to melanoma-endothelial communication, focusing on its association with NF-κB signaling and VEGFA expression, and their role in melanoma-derived paracrine activation of endothelial cells.

Methods

CRISPR/Cas9-edited A375 RIPK4 knockout (A375 RIPK4.KO) and WM266.4 RIPK4-deficient (WM266.4RIPK4.KO) melanoma cells, together with their respective controls, were analyzed in two- and three-dimensional culture models. VEGFA expression and secretion, NF-κB-associated signaling, and RIPK4-associated changes in the melanoma secretome were assessed by qPCR, ELISA, Western blotting, and angiogenesis protein arrays. The functional consequences were evaluated using conditioned media in human aortic endothelial cell tube formation assays and the chick chorioallantoic membrane (CAM) model.

Results

RIPK4 depletion was associated with reduced p65 phosphorylation and increased IκBα expression, accompanied by decreased VEGFA expression and VEGF secretion. Restoration of RIPK4 reversed these changes, restoring p65 phosphorylation, reducing IκBα expression, and increasing VEGF levels. Secretome profiling revealed reduced VEGF and amphiregulin and increased pigment epithelium-derived factor following RIPK4 depletion. Conditioned media from RIPK4-deficient cells impaired endothelial tube formation, which was restored by recombinant VEGF165. In CAM, RIPK4 depletion reduced CD34 and VEGFR3 (FLT4), without significantly affecting overall vascularization.

Conclusion

RIPK4 is associated with NF-κB signaling and VEGF production in melanoma cells and contributes to the regulation of the melanoma secretome and melanoma-endothelial communication. These findings support a role for RIPK4 in modulating paracrine signals that influence endothelial cell behavior, although the direct mechanistic contribution of NF-κB to RIPK4-mediated VEGFA regulation remains to be established.

title: Factitious Disorder Presenting as Recurrent Aortic Emergencies: A Case Report.
authorString: Unrue EL, Cooper NT, Salzler GG, Ryer EJ, Elmore JR.

journal.title: The American journal of case reports

abstractText: BACKGROUND Factitious disorder, historically known as Munchausen's syndrome, is a psychiatric condition characterized by the intentional fabrication or induction of symptoms without obvious external incentives. Patients frequently present with dramatic, medically convincing concerns that can mimic life-threatening illnesses and prompt extensive diagnostic evaluations. Although hemorrhagic presentations have been described, presentations mimicking catastrophic vascular disease are uncommon and pose unique challenges for emergency medicine and vascular teams. CASE REPORT A 37-year-old man with a subsequently documented diagnosis of factitious disorder repeatedly presented to multiple hospitals with dramatic hematemesis concerning for an aortoenteric fistula. Over an 8-year period, he underwent multiple diagnostic evaluations and several aortic interventions, including endovascular aortic repair and later explantation, despite repeated studies showing no aortoenteric pathology. In 2024, he developed bilateral renal artery occlusions secondary to focal aortic dissection requiring emergent stenting. A psychiatric evaluation at an outside institution ultimately diagnosed Munchausen syndrome. Recurrent presentations across healthcare systems, repeatedly negative diagnostic evaluations, inconsistent objective findings, and family-reported discovery of vials containing a red blood-like fluid provided additional evidence concerning for deliberate symptom fabrication. CONCLUSIONS This case report shows how factitious disorder can mimic life-threatening vascular disease. While urgent pathology must be excluded, recurrent high-acuity presentations accompanied by inconsistent objective findings should prompt cross-institutional record review, multidisciplinary evaluation, and broader diagnostic consideration to prevent unnecessary procedural escalation and iatrogenic harm, facilitate earlier diagnostic recognition, and support appropriate psychiatric intervention.

title: 2026 updated recommendations of the Psoriasis Working Group (GPS) of the Spanish Academy of Dermatology and Venereology for biologic therapy in moderate-to-severe psoriasis: Management of special populations, comorbidities, and treatment-related risks-Part 2.
authorString: López-Ferrer A, Puig L, Carrascosa JM, Belinchón I, Daudén E, de la Cueva P.
abstractText: The Psoriasis Working Group (GPS) of the Spanish Academy of Dermatology and Venereology regularly updates its recommendations for the management of moderate-to-severe psoriasis. The expanding availability of biologic therapies, biosimilars, and oral small-molecule treatments, together with emerging evidence on their efficacy and safety, requires updated guidance for special populations, patients with comorbidities, and treatment-related risk management. This document provides evidence-informed recommendations to support individualized therapeutic decision-making. Recommendations were developed using the nominal group technique, supported by a scoping review of the literature. Two coordinators appointed a panel of GPS experts and defined the clinical questions and topics requiring revision. With the assistance of an information specialist, MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched through October 2025. Evidence was selected from systematic reviews, meta-analyses, clinical trials, and high-quality real-world studies. Relevant national and international clinical practice guidelines and consensus documents were also reviewed. Previous recommendations were revised, and new recommendations were developed, evaluated by the expert panel, and refined through successive review rounds. Updated recommendations address biologic therapies, biosimilars, and oral small-molecule treatments for moderate-to-severe psoriasis. Management considerations include older adults, pediatric patients, pregnancy, breastfeeding, conception planning, poor treatment adherence, multiple treatment failures, and psoriasis affecting special anatomical sites. Recommendations also address treatment selection in patients with obesity, metabolic syndrome, psoriatic arthritis, inflammatory bowel disease, depression, malignancy, cardiovascular disease, heart failure, chronic kidney disease, neurologic disorders, lupus, and other autoimmune diseases. Treatment-related risk management encompasses pretreatment assessment, laboratory and clinical monitoring, vaccination, infection and latent tuberculosis screening, neurotoxicity, perioperative management, adverse events, and treatment discontinuation. Multidisciplinary care is emphasized throughout. These updated recommendations provide an evidence-informed framework for individualized systemic treatment of moderate-to-severe psoriasis in special populations and patients with comorbidities. Treatment selection should integrate disease characteristics, comorbidities, patient preferences, available evidence, and treatment-specific safety considerations. Ongoing risk assessment, appropriate monitoring, and multidisciplinary collaboration are essential components of long-term psoriasis management.

title: Removing the signal is not correcting the imbalance: sFlt-1-depletion trials in preeclampsia need fetal as well as maternal endpoints.
authorString: Mureșan MC, Mureșan MB.
abstractText: Selective sFlt-1 depletion prolongs very preterm preeclamptic pregnancies. Because sFlt-1 mediates maternal disease but does not measure the uteroplacental supply deficit, maternal and fetal responses may become dissociated. We argue that controlled trials should prespecify fetal and neonatal co-primary endpoints alongside maternal outcomes, avoid using maternal markers as substitutes for fetal assessment, and define fetal delivery criteria and trial stopping rules in advance.

title: Managing environmental enteropathy among Egyptian infants and children with growth faltering.
authorString: Nassar MF, Emam EK, Allam MF, Hamdy AM, Abdelhaleem BA, Radwan NA, Emam AM, Ibrahim HE.
abstractText:
Background

Environmental enteropathy (EE) is an acquired subclinical inflammation of the small bowel mucosa, leading to reduced nutrient absorption and increased intestinal permeability. There are currently no universally accepted protocols for the diagnosis and treatment of EE.

Objective

The primary aim of this clinical trial was to assess the prevalence of EE among children with faltering growth (FG). Determination of the dietary requirements in pediatric FG with EE and highlighting the histopathologic changes in the small intestine in such conditions were the secondary objectives.

Patients and methods

The current study recruited 200 patients (their age range was 6-58 months) diagnosed as GF at the Pediatric Clinical Nutrition Clinic, Children`s Hospital, Faculty of Medicine, Ain Shams University (Cairo, Egypt), during the period from April 2022 till June 2023. The first phase of the study was a cross sectional interventional one where all patients underwent nutritional rehabilitation using diet regimen including polymeric milk formula. Patients whose weight z score was still below - 2 SD for age and sex after 12 weeks were considered as non-responders and were enrolled in the second phase, when esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD) and mucosal biopsies were done. In the latter phase, patients with EE received nutritional rehabilitation regimen using peptide-based milk formula with assessment of anthropometric measurements after 8 weeks of follow up.

Results

Out of the studied cases, 170 were responders, and 30 were non-responders, 24 of the non-responders underwent EGD with biopsies and all were diagnosed as EE with prevalence of 12% among the studied patients with GF as the least possible prevalence. Total histology scores of the EE fell between those of the controls and celiac disease reference samples with cut off values > 3 and ≤ 14 for EE, ≤ 3 for controls and > 14 for celiac disease. There was a significant increase in weight and height z scores among patients of EE on peptide-based formula compared to polymeric formula.

Conclusion

EE isn`t uncommon and should be suspected when provision of catch-up nutrients can`t correct FG. Peptide-based formula has a possible beneficial effect on growth of patients with EE.

Trial registration

The clinical trial was registered at Protocol Registration and Results System with number NCT06497907 (12/07/2024).

title: Diet Quality as Assessed by the Healthy Eating Index, Alternate Healthy Eating Index, and Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension Score, and Health Outcomes: a Third Systematic Review Update and Meta-Analysis of Cohort Studies.
authorString: Wan CS, Cheung VHI, Musgrave-Takeda M, Hoffmann G, Morze J, Schwingshackl L.

journal.title: Journal of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics

abstractText: How diet quality, as measured by different diet quality indices, is associated with non-communicable disease incidence and mortality remains uncertain. This study aimed to update the body of evidence on the associations between diet quality, as assessed by the Healthy Eating Index (HEI), Alternate Healthy Eating Index (AHEI), and Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) score, and health outcomes. PubMed, Embase, and Scopus databases were used to update the search until February 3, 2025. Pooled relative risk (RR) with 95% CI for the highest versus the lowest category of diet quality was estimated using a random-effects model. Heterogeneity was explored using Cochran´s Q test and I2 statistic with 95% CI. Risk of bias was assessed using the ROBINS-E tool, funnel plots, and Egger's regression test. Certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE. The current update identified 96 new reports (total now 207), including data from 3,976,111 individuals in the general population and 55,572 cancer survivors. All HEI, AHEI or DASH scores were inversely associated with risk of all-cause mortality (all indices combined: RR 0.82, 95% CI: 0.77 to 0.87), cardiovascular disease incidence (combined RR 0.83, 95% CI: 0.74 to 0.92) or mortality (combined RR 0.78, 95% CI: 0.71 to 0.85), cancer incidence (combined RR 0.88, 95% CI: 0.78 to 0.99) or mortality (combined RR 0.85, 95% CI: 0.76 to 0.95), and type 2 diabetes incidence (combined RR 0.78, 95% CI: 0.67 to 0.92), with moderate to low certainty of evidence. Among cancer survivors, moderate to low certainty of evidence was rated for the inverse association between diet quality indices and all-cause mortality (combined RR 0.83, 95% CI: 0.77 to 0.90). The etiology of non-communicable diseases contributes to the heterogeneity of findings. Different diet quality indices have varying levels of certainty of evidence for each non-communicable disease incidence and mortality, underscoring the importance of defining high diet quality in nutritional guidelines.

title: Revascularisation Strategies in Dialysis-Dependent Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischaemia.
authorString: Li Z, Hu L, Gu Y.
abstractText:
Background

We reviewed dialysis-specific evidence on bypass and endovascular treatment for chronic limb-threatening ischaemia to assess how the available comparisons inform the initial revascularisation decision.

Methods

We searched four bibliographic databases and one trial register through 12 September 2026. We synthesised comparisons without meta-analysis and graded certainty for eight outcomes. We applied nested restrictions by excluding mixed-open comparisons, retaining adjusted or matched comparisons, then excluding success-selected cohorts and abstract-only reports.

Results

Sixteen reports represented 13 study families. Comparisons differed in whether they captured treatment attempted, treatment received or successful procedures. Selected comparisons reported associations favouring bypass for limb or wound outcomes. In the as-treated dialysis analysis of the Best Endovascular versus Best Surgical Therapy in Patients with Critical Limb Ischaemia trial, single-segment great saphenous vein bypass was associated with lower reintervention hazard (hazard ratio 0.48, 95% confidence interval 0.25-0.94) and higher mortality (1.69, 1.06-2.70) than endovascular treatment. The estimate for amputation or death was imprecise (1.47, 0.95-2.27). Death handling for reintervention was unclear. Mixed-open comparisons suggested lower early amputation and more bleeding and wound complications. After successive restrictions, the remaining evidence did not establish an initial-strategy preference.

Conclusions

In dialysis-dependent CLTI, SSGSV bypass was associated with lower reintervention hazard but higher mortality in the as-treated BEST-CLI comparison; other favourable limb findings came from non-equivalent cohorts. These associations do not establish a net advantage or preferred initial strategy.
