Decisions should weigh limb threat, anatomy, conduit suitability, expected survival, perioperative risk, functional goals and treatment burden.

title: Real-world Gastrointestinal, Pancreaticobiliary, Cardiorenal, Metabolic and Nutritional Outcomes of GLP-1 or GIP Receptors Agonists -based Therapy in Chronic Pancreatitis.
authorString: Dhali A, Maity R, Khan F.

journal.title: Journal of gastrointestinal and liver diseases : JGLD

abstractText: Glucagon-like peptide-1(GLP-1) receptor agonists and dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP)/GLP-1 receptor agonists are increasingly used for metabolic disease, but their safety profile in patients with chronic pancreatitis (CP) remains uncertain. We compared several gastrointestinal, cardio, renal and metabolic outcomes in patients with CP exposed to dulaglutide, semaglutide, or tirzepatide versus propensity-matched unexposed controls. We conducted a retrospective, propensity score-matched cohort study using the TriNetX federated real-world data platform. Adults with CP were classified by recorded exposure to dulaglutide, semaglutide, or tirzepatide versus no recorded exposure to those drugs. Risk analyses and Kaplan-Meier time-to-event analyses were done. After matching, median follow-up was 588 (IQR 831) versus 879 (IQR 807), respectively. Nausea/vomiting occurred in 656/4,938 (risk 0.133) versus 1,099/5,585 (risk 0.197), with risk ratio (RR) 0.675 (95%CI: 0.618-0.738) and hazard ratio (HR) 0.710 (95%CI: 0.645-0.783). Bowel obstruction/ileus occurred in 241/9,103 (risk 0.026) versus 466/8,949 (risk 0.052), with RR=0.508 (95%CI: 0.436-0.592) and HR=0.556 (95%CI: 0.476-0.649). Upper gastrointestinal bleeding occurred in 355/8,536 (risk 0.042) versus 608/8,657 (risk 0.070), with RR=0.592 (95%CI: 0.521-0.673) and HR=0.659 (95%CI: 0.578-0.751). Biliary/procedural outcomes were lower, including cholecystectomy (risk 0.023 vs 0.049; HR=0.486, 95%CI: 0.412-0.572) and ERCP (risk 0.026 vs 0.064; HR=0.420, 95%CI: 0.362-0.488). Recurrent acute pancreatitis occurred in 329/5,639 exposed patients (risk 0.058) versus 579/5,499 controls (risk 0.105), with HR=0.584 (95%CI: 0.510-0.669). Additional associations included lower insulin initiation (risk 0.178 vs 0.269; HR=0.731, 95%CI: 0.658-0.812), heart failure (risk 0.061 vs 0.101; HR=0.687, 95%CI: 0.613-0.770), myocardial infarction (risk 0.039 vs 0.054; HR=0.818, 95%CI: 0.712-0.939 and acute kidney injury (risk 0.086 vs 0.150; HR=0.643, 95%CI: 0.580-0.712), malnutrition (risk 0.049 vs 0.107; HR=0.491, 95%CI: 0.438-0.550). Exposure to dulaglutide, semaglutide, or tirzepatide was associated with lower recorded risks across several gastrointestinal, cardio, renal and metabolic outcome domains. These findings should be interpreted with caution, and further prospective studies are required to confirm the same.

title: Lifestyle‐ and health‐related challenges in children with autism spectrum disorder: A systematic review
authorString: Imam S, Rahman M, Uddin M, Morad M, Saha A, Kundu S.

journal.title: PCN reports : psychiatry and clinical neurosciences

title: Severe maternal morbidity in patients with cardiovascular disease and hypertensive disorders of pregnancy.
authorString: Pullins MJ, Quist-Nelson J, Fuller M, Roberts ET, Federspiel JJ, Lindley K, Boggess K, Meng ML.

journal.title: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM

abstractText:
Background

Cardiovascular disease (CVD) and hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) are independently associated with increased risk of severe maternal morbidity (SMM). While prior studies have characterized adverse pregnancy outcomes among patients with CVD, limited data have evaluated how the development of HDP influences non-transfusion SMM across specific cardiac subtypes, particularly through the postpartum period, in large contemporary U.S. cohorts.

Objective

To assess the impact of HDP on non-transfusion SMM among patients with CVD during delivery and within 90 days postpartum.

Study design

Retrospective cohort study using the Premier Healthcare Database of pregnant patients ≥18 years delivering between 2015 and 2020. Patients without CVD were compared to those with six CVD subtypes present on admission (aortic, ischemic, congenital, pulmonary hypertension, cardiomyopathy, and valvular). The primary outcome was non-transfusion SMM during delivery hospitalization and within 90 days postpartum, stratified by CVD and HDP subtype (gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, and preeclampsia with severe features), estimated as covariate-adjusted predicted rates (%). Secondary outcomes included SMM subtypes, ICU admission, and all-cause readmission within 30 and 90 days, reported as crude rates and adjusted odds ratios (aORs).

Results

Of 4,606,247 births, 18,771 (0.4%) had CVD, and 12.0% had HDP. HDP was associated with higher adjusted predicted non-transfusion SMM rates, independent of CVD, with increasing risk across HDP severity and marked heterogeneity by CVD subtype. Patients with CVD had consistently higher SMM across all HDP subtypes. The highest delivery hospitalization SMM rates occurred among patients with cardiomyopathy (25.6%) and pulmonary hypertension (33.2%) with preeclampsia with severe features; this pattern persisted through 90 days postpartum. Acute respiratory distress syndrome and mechanical ventilation were the most common SMM types during delivery, while heart failure/pulmonary edema predominated postpartum. Cardiomyopathy (aOR 9.02) and pulmonary hypertension (aOR 4.37) had the highest odds of ICU admission; readmission risk was also highest in pulmonary hypertension (30-day aOR 1.77; 90-day aOR 1.76) and cardiomyopathy (30-day aOR 1.42; 90-day aOR 1.68).

Conclusion

HDP significantly increases risk of non-transfusion SMM in patients with CVD, particularly in pulmonary hypertension and cardiomyopathy, and in those with preeclampsia with severe features.

title: Age-Dependent Prognostic Significance of Anemia After Acute Coronary Syndromes.
authorString: Cordero A, Cid-Alvarez B, Arrarte V, Alvarez-Alvarez B, García-Acuña JM, Rodriguez-Mañero M, Sandín M, Agra-Bermejo R, Mazón P, González-Juanatey JR.
abstractText: Anemia is common in patients with acute coronary syndromes, but whether its prognostic significance varies according to age remains uncertain. We retrospectively analyzed 8,684 consecutive patients admitted with acute coronary syndromes to 2 tertiary hospitals in Spain. Baseline hemoglobin and anemia were evaluated in relation to in-hospital mortality, heart failure, and major bleeding, and to long-term all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, heart failure hospitalization, and major bleeding. Multivariable logistic, Cox regression, and competing-risk models were used. Interactions between age and hemoglobin or anemia were assessed. Median hemoglobin was 14.0 g/dL, and 21.8% of patients had anemia. Lower hemoglobin was independently associated with higher risks of in-hospital mortality, heart failure, and major bleeding. During a median follow-up of 58 months, lower hemoglobin and anemia were associated with all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, heart failure hospitalization, and major bleeding. Significant interactions were observed between age and both hemoglobin and anemia. The excess risk associated with lower hemoglobin and anemia progressively decreased with advancing age and was markedly attenuated in patients aged ≥75 years. In conclusion, hemoglobin and anemia are independent predictors of adverse outcomes after acute coronary syndromes, but their long-term prognostic significance is strongly modified by age. Their association with adverse events is substantially greater in younger patients and attenuated in those aged ≥75 years.

title: The Impact of Preoperative Atrial Fibrillation on Outcomes Following Left Ventricular Assist Device Implantation.
authorString: Oates CP, Armijo-Alba J, Basyal B, Hadadi CA, Rodrigo ME, Lam PH, Shah M, Molina EJ, Sheikh FH.
abstractText: A preoperative history of atrial fibrillation (AF) in patients receiving durable left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation has been associated with postoperative morbidity and mortality. It is uncertain how the type of preoperative AF (paroxysmal vs. persistent/permanent) impacts clinical outcomes in patients on LVAD support. We sought to determine how the presence and type of preoperative AF affect patient mortality following LVAD implantation. A single-center retrospective analysis was performed of patients who underwent LVAD implantation from 2006-2022. Patients with AF prior to LVAD implantation were characterized as having paroxysmal or persistent/permanent AF for comparison. A total of 289 patients (37%) with a history of preoperative AF underwent LVAD implantation. Paroxysmal AF (78.9%) was more common prior to LVAD implant than persistent/permanent AF (21.1%). The incidence of 30-day and 2-year all-cause mortality were significantly higher amongst patients with preoperative persistent/permanent AF compared to patients without reoperative AF (30-day mortality: 16.4% vs 6.4%, p=0.005; 2-year all-cause mortality: 44.3% vs 24.2%, p=0.001). Over long-term follow-up, the risk of all-cause mortality was significantly higher for patients with preoperative persistent/permanent AF compared to patients without preoperative AF controlling for age, sex, race, class III antiarrhythmic medications, destination therapy and device design (sdHR 1.94; 1.34-2.79 95% CI, p≤0.001). In contrast, there was no significant difference in mortality at 30-days or 2-years between patients with preoperative paroxysmal AF and those without preoperative AF (30-day mortality: 5.7% vs 6.4%, p=0.408; 2-year all-cause mortality: 27.2% vs 24.2%, p=0.010). The risk of long-term mortality was also not significantly different (sdHR 1.19; 0.95-1.5 95% CI, p=0.137). In conclusion, a preoperative history of persistent/permanent AF is associated with increased risk of mortality following LVAD implantation, but there is no significant difference in survival between patients with preoperative paroxysmal AF and those without AF.

title: Increases in the isocapnic buffering period reduce cardiac events in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction - a prospective cohort study.
authorString: de Andrade GN, Nascimento JA, das Dores Cruz F, de Oliveira PA, Agostinho DR, Bocchi EA, Cahalin LP, Nakagawa NK.
abstractText: We aimed to investigate the role of the isocapnic buffering period, the difference between the oxygen consumption at the anaerobic threshold and the respiratory compensation point, to predict hospitalization and death in patients with Heart Failure (HF). Prospective cohort study. Patients with HF with reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF < 40%, NYHA I, II, and III). Cardiopulmonary test data, muscle strength, and Quality of Life (QoL) were measured at baseline. Patients were followed over 48-months for cardiac events (hospitalization and cardiac-related death). Seventy-three patients (∼58-years, 73% male, LVEF = 31%) were followed. Seventeen patients had cardiac events, and 56 patients were free of cardiac events. Both groups showed similar peak oxygen consumption (p = 0.597), inspiratory muscle strength (p = 0.351), and quadriceps muscle strength (p = 0.059). Using the multivariate analysis by the Cox proportional hazard model, the increase of one unit (mL/kg/min) in the isocapnic buffering period decreased the risk of cardiac events by 26% (p = 0.034) and higher scores (≥ 45-points) in the Minnesota Living with Heart Failure questionnaire were associated with increased risk (4.5-fold) of cardiac events (p = 0.020). As a preliminary finding, the isocapnic buffering period is an independent predictor of hospitalization and death in patients with mild and moderate HF. Additionally, self-reported QoL is a useful tool to follow functional status and cardiac events in patients with HF.

title: Shikonin in Cardiovascular Inflammatory Injury: Immunometabolic Regulation, Mitochondrial Homeostasis, and Regulated Cell Death.
authorString: Wang Y, Du L, Gao W.
abstractText: Cardiovascular inflammation is sustained by reciprocal changes in immune-cell metabolism, mitochondrial function, and stress-responsive cell death. Shikonin, a naphthoquinone derived from the roots of Lithospermum erythrorhizon and related medicinal plants, is widely used experimentally as an inhibitor of pyruvate kinase M2 (PKM2) and also modifies redox and stress-response signaling. Cardiovascular studies now extend from endothelial cells and vascular smooth muscle cells to experimental atherosclerosis, myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury, cardiac remodeling, pulmonary hypertension, cardiotoxicity, and thrombosis. The strongest cardiovascular evidence concerns PKM2-dependent glycolysis: shikonin suppresses inflammatory metabolic activation in macrophages and lymphocytes, reduces foam-cell formation and vascular smooth muscle-cell proliferation, and attenuates metabolic remodeling in cardiac and pulmonary vascular models. Mitochondrial membrane potential, reactive oxygen species, NRF2-dependent antioxidant responses, and fission-related proteins are also responsive to shikonin in cardiovascular models. Apoptosis and inflammasome-associated signaling show context-dependent activity, while other regulated cell-death pathways require interpretation within the specific experimental system. Emerging liposomal and hydrogel formulations offer avenues for tissue-selective delivery, with vascular reactivity and hemostatic safety central to cardiovascular translation. Overall, shikonin represents a promising preclinical scaffold for immunometabolic modulation and formulation-specific cardiovascular investigation.

title: The Incidence of Stroke and the Population Attributable Fraction of Its Risk Factors in Thailand: Prospective Findings from the Thai Epidemiologic Stroke (TES) Study.
authorString: Hanchaiphiboolkul S, Puthkhao P, Tantirittisak T, Worakijthamrongchai T, Thiraworawong T, Komonchan S, Termglinchan T, Suwanwela NC, Towanabut S.
abstractText: Data on incidence of stroke are scarce in developing countries and little is known about the contribution of known risk factors in this population. The aim of our study was to determine the incidence of first-ever stroke in general population and population attributable fraction (PAF) of its risk factors in Thailand. Thai Epidemiologic Stroke (TES) study is a prospective community-based cohort study that recruited participants from the general population from five regions of Thailand. Between 2004 and 2006, 19,620 participants aged 45 to 80 years, free of stroke, took part in the baseline survey. The participants were followed up for first-ever stroke. Cox proportional hazards models were used to identify factors associated with incident stroke, with Fine-Gray competing-risk models accounting for non-stroke death as a sensitivity analysis. Mutually adjusted population attributable fractions were estimated for modifiable risk factors consistently associated with incident stroke. During a median follow-up of 10.2 years, 925 participants developed a first-ever stroke. The crude incidence rates per 100,000 person-years was 561.0 (95%CI, 526.0-598.3). Incidence adjusted to the WHO standard population (2000-2025) aged 45-74 years was 509.5 per 100,000 person-years. Hypertension had the highest PAF (21.3%), followed by low education (15.4%), low personal income (14.2%), smoking status (9.9%), and diabetes mellitus (7.2%), respectively. The total PAF for these five significant risk factors was 68.0% (95% CI: 58.4%-77.7%). The incidence rate of stroke in Thailand is higher than that of several other countries, particularly developed countries. About 68.0% of all strokes in Thailand are attributable to five modifiable risk factors. Among these factors, hypertension is the most important.

title: CADASIL Argentine Registry (CADASILAR): Establishment of a Harmonized Multicenter Registry with Preliminary Clinical and Cognitive Insights from Latin America.
authorString: Ardohain Cristalli CA, Rosales J, Alonso J, Calandri I, Gonzalez-Aquines A, González F, López JI, Morello-García F, Selvaggi V, Aguilar M, Allegri R, Chabriat H, Chaves H, Mezmezian MB, Muiño-Acuña E, Pujol Lereis V, Saks DG, Sevlever G, Kauffman M, Cristalli DO.
abstractText: Cerebral autosomal dominant arteriopathy with subcortical infarcts and leukoencephalopathy (CADASIL) is the most common monogenic small vessel disease. Despite extensive characterization in Europe and Asia, data from Latin America remain limited. This study aimed to describe the structure of the Argentine CADASIL registry (CADASILAR), a harmonized multicenter initiative, and to report preliminary findings from its cross-sectional cohort. CADASILAR is an observational, referral-based, multicenter registry comprising two phases: a cross-sectional cohort (CADASILAR-C) and a planned three-year longitudinal follow-up (CADASILAR-Long). Here we report preliminary descriptive and bivariate analyses from CADASILAR-C. Definitive or possible CADASIL diagnoses were included based on genetic testing, skin biopsy, or clinical and neuroimaging criteria. A total of 109 patients were included in the CADASILAR-C cohort, 50.5% were female, and mean age at symptom onset was 42.4 ± 12 years. Ischemic stroke was the most frequent initial manifestation (28/109, 25.7%), followed by migraine with aura (19/109, 17.4%). History of cognitive decline was documented in 48.6% of patients (53/109). Among those with Mini-Mental State Examination data (49/109), 24.5% had scores indicative of cognitive impairment (10/49). An exploratory analysis among those with cognitive impairment showed a statistically significant difference in the frequency of hypertension (80.0% vs 33.3%, p=0.012), overweight (40.0% vs 10.3%, p=0.044), and obesity (40.0% vs 2.6%, p=0.004). On neuroimaging, periventricular and deep white matter hyperintensities, and temporal lobe lesions were the most frequent features observed. All genetic variants identified were cysteine-altering variants. CADASILAR represents the first structured, multicenter effort to systematically characterize CADASIL in Latin America, providing a harmonized framework for the collection of clinical, cognitive, neuroimaging, and genetic data across centers. This approach aims to improve case identification, facilitate inter-cohort comparability, and support future longitudinal research in the region.

title: Environmental noise and cardiometabolic health: a transatlantic perspective.
authorString: Münzel T, Osborne MT, Basner M, Röösli M, Angell SY, Banks JL, Sørensen M, Rajagopalan S.
abstractText: Environmental noise is a pervasive but under-recognized cardiovascular and metabolic risk factor. Drawing on prior expert reviews and large-scale epidemiologic and mechanistic studies, this review synthesizes evidence on the burden, major clinical associations, biological pathways, vulnerable populations, and mitigation strategies relevant to cardiovascular health. Road traffic noise is consistently and dose-dependently associated with higher risks of ischaemic heart disease, stroke, heart failure, diabetes, sleep disturbance, and adverse mental health outcomes, whereas for railway and aircraft noise, the evidence base is less consistent, although important associations are increasingly reported. Translational human imaging studies, controlled exposure experiments, and animal models converge on a common pathway in which chronic and intermittent noise exposure activates stress-responsive neural circuits, increases sympathetic and hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis activity, promotes oxidative stress, endothelial dysfunction, and vascular inflammation, and may thereby accelerate cardiometabolic disease. Noise frequently co-occurs with air pollution, heat, and adverse social and built environments, particularly in socioeconomically disadvantaged communities, and these combined exposures may contribute additively to cardiovascular risk. These effects are especially relevant in urban populations with nighttime exposure and multiple co-exposures. Despite this growing evidence base, environmental noise remains largely absent from contemporary cardiovascular risk assessment tools, prevention guidelines, and routine patient counselling, representing a missed opportunity for risk reduction. Effective mitigation will require a hierarchical strategy combining source reduction, health-informed urban and transport planning, and targeted individual protection. Reducing environmental noise exposure should be recognized as an important opportunity to protect and advance cardiovascular and metabolic health in the 21st century.

title: Complications and Management of Thoracic Surgery: Pertinent Information for Intensivists and Hospitalists.
authorString: Shah R, Bremner R, vanSonnenberg E.
abstractText: Thoracic surgery presents unique postoperative challenges that intensivists and hospitalists frequently encounter in both ward and intensive care settings. This review provides a practical overview of common procedures, potential complications, and evidence-based management strategies tailored to intensivists and hospitalists. Topics include the role of imaging, ventilatory support, and pain control, as well as integration with Anesthesiology, Pulmonology, Radiology, and Respiratory Therapy. Major complications and their corresponding management-such as air leaks, atelectasis, pneumonia, atrial fibrillation, bronchopleural fistula, and empyema-are discussed in detail, with emphasis on early recognition and intervention. This paper offers a concise guide for the management of postoperative thoracic surgery patients by outlining key principles most relevant to intensivists and hospitalists in daily practice.

title: Serum fibroblast growth factor-23 and risk of incident stroke and dementia: The Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities Study.
authorString: Lutsey PL, Sauerer DM, Michos ED, Selvin E, Rebholz CM, Gottesman RF, Alonso A, Matsushita K, Sedaghat S.
abstractText: BackgroundElevated concentrations of fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23), a hormone involved in bone mineral and vitamin D metabolism, may be associated with risk of stroke and dementia through inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, vessel calcification and stiffness, and axonal degeneration.ObjectiveWe tested the hypothesis that elevated FGF23 is associated with increased risk of dementia and stroke.MethodsFGF23 was measured in serum samples collected in 1990-1992 from 12,391 participants of the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities study. Participants were followed through 2019 for incident stroke and dementia. Cox regression was used to examine the associations of FGF23 (in quintiles) with risk of stroke and dementia, with adjustment for demographics, cardiovascular and dementia risk factors, and kidney function.ResultsParticipants (mean 56.9 years; 57% female) were followed a median of 24 years; 1183 developed stroke and 2402 developed dementia. Participants in the highest versus lowest quintile of serum FGF23 were at elevated risk of stroke [HR (95% CI): 1.27 (1.06-1.51)] and dementia [HR: 1.21 (1.06-1.38)] independent of baseline demographics. Associations attenuated with additional adjustment for traditional cardiovascular risk factors [HR<sub>stroke</sub>: 1.20 (1.00-1.45); HR<sub>dementia</sub>: 1.17 (1.03-1.35)], and became even weaker after accounting for eGFR [HR<sub>stroke</sub>: 1.13 (0.94-1.37); HR<sub>dementia</sub>: 1.14 (1.00-1.31)]. The associations of FGF23 with incident stroke and dementia were not modified by categories of age, sex, race, or eGFR.ConclusionsHigher FGF23 was associated with modestly greater risk of stroke and dementia in this population-based sample, though the association was largely attenuated after adjustment for traditional cardiovascular risk factors and kidney function.

title: One-Year Results From the EMBRACE Registry Evaluating the GORE VIABAHN VBX Balloon Expandable Endoprosthesis during BEVAR for Complex Abdominal and Thoracoabdominal Aneurysms.
authorString: Bertoglio L, Hoksbergen AWJ, Giudice R, Pratesi G, Resch T, Martinez Lopez I, Mansour W, Rinaldi E, Wanhainen A, Dias N, Budtz-Lilly J, Salmeron LM, Johannesdottir B, Nordhus KC, Manstad-Hulaas F, EMBRACE study investigators (to be indexed on PubMed).

journal.title: Journal of endovascular therapy : an official journal of the International Society of Endovascular Specialists

abstractText:
Objective

The stability of bridging stents is critical to ensure the effectiveness and safety of branched endovascular aortic repair (BEVAR) for complex and thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysms (TAAA). The goal of this multicenter registry was to assess the clinical performance and safety of the GORE VIABAHN VBX Balloon Expandable Endoprosthesis (VBX Stent Graft) as a bridging stent in BEVAR.

Methods

The EMBRACE registry is a multicenter study across 14 European centers with retrospective enrollment and prospective follow-up. Patients were divided into BEVAR and fenestrated endovascular aneurysm repair (FEVAR) arms. This analysis reports the BEVAR cohort, which included patients receiving the VBX Stent Graft as a bridging stent for at least 1 visceral vessel. The primary endpoint was patient-level primary patency at 12 months. Secondary endpoints included technical success, reintervention, and target vessel patency assessed annually for up to 5 years. Secondary safety outcomes included major adverse events and aneurysm-related mortality.

Results

A total of 165 patients (69.1% male, mean age 72.5 ± 9 years) were enrolled, receiving 454 VBX Stent Grafts (26.0% celiac trunk, 28.9% superior mesenteric artery (SMA), 21.8% left renal, and 23.3% right renal artery). VBX Stent Graft technical success was 99.6%. Thirty-day mortality was 7.9%, with major adverse events in 15.2% (1.8% respiratory failure, 7.3% renal function deterioration, 0.6% bowel ischemia, 4.2% paraplegia, and 1.8% major stroke). Freedom from aneurysm-related mortality was 92.1% at 30 days and 90.2% at 1 year. Freedom from patient-level VBX-related reintervention was 91.7%. Patient-level primary patency and secondary patency were 97.7% and 98.5%, respectively. Freedom from target vessel instability at the patient level was 90.4%.

Conclusion

Short-term findings from this multicenter registry confirm that the VBX Stent Graft is a safe and effective bridging stent for BEVAR, demonstrating high technical success, excellent 1-year patency, and low rates of target vessel instability. Ongoing follow-up will evaluate mid-term durability.Clinical ImpactBridging stent performance is fundamental to the success of branched endovascular repair, yet multicenter, real-world data remain limited. This analysis from the EMBRACE registry demonstrates high technical reliability, excellent 1-year target vessel patency, and low rates of VBX Stent Graft-related reintervention. Technical failures were uncommon and were primarily associated with inadequate distal landing zones, highlighting the importance of procedural planning. These findings provide clinicians with contemporary evidence supporting the VBX Stent Graft as a safe and effective bridging stent for BEVAR and may inform procedural decision-making to optimize target vessel durability.

title: Insights into Channelopathies and Sport: The Genotype-Positive/Phenotype-Negative Athlete from Molecular Diagnosis to Management.
authorString: Diebold I, Hahn F, Martens E, Schön U, Wacker-Gußmann A, Laugwitz KL, Halle M, Winkelmann J, D Ascenzi F, Sarma S, Niederseer D, Saguner AM, Rattka M, Castelletti S, Wernhart S.
abstractText: Channelopathies, diseases with ion channel perturbations, are a major cause of sudden cardiac death in athletes. Advances in genetic testing have identified a growing population of athletes carrying (likely) pathogenic variants in cardiac ion channel genes who remain phenotypically silent. These genotype-positive/phenotype-negative (G+/P-) individuals present a distinct clinical challenge. Standard preparticipation screening, designed around phenotypic findings, provides little guidance for their management. A critical gap exists in providing prognostic guidance based on the involved gene, specific variants, and its molecular consequences. Beyond a critical review of existing literature, we provide a mechanistically anchored framework for variant-specific arrhythmic risk stratification across the major channelopathy genes. For each gene, we translate molecular pathophysiology into clinically actionable risk profiles and examine how exercise-specific triggers, including adrenergic surge, electrolyte shifts, and sympathovagal imbalance, interact with the underlying molecular substrate to modulate arrhythmic vulnerability. Standard diagnostic tools ranging from electro- and echocardiography, exercise stress testing, and pharmacological provocation to emerging modalities such as electroanatomic mapping and magnetocardiography are evaluated for their capacity to unmask subclinical disease and refine sports eligibility decisions. The case for an interdisciplinary sports-cardio-genetic board is made alongside a call for international collaborative registries, as existing evidence in G+/P- athletes is largely absent. The integration of artificial intelligence and telemonitoring into longitudinal athletic surveillance is discussed as a pragmatic strategy for early phenotype detection. Ultimately, guidance for the G+/P- athlete rests on a thorough understanding of the causative genetic variant and its pathophysiological consequences.

title: Massive ascites with preserved serum albumin in adult anorexia nervosa: Impact on eating behavior and weight-based treatment assessment.
authorString: Mashimoto M, Kora T, Sakamoto Y, Masuda A, Chiba H, Ozone M.

journal.title: PCN reports : psychiatry and clinical neurosciences

abstractText: Ascites is a rare complication of anorexia nervosa (AN) and is typically associated with hypoalbuminemia. Its influence on eating behavior and on the evaluation of treatment response remains poorly characterized. A 30-year-old woman with AN presented with massive ascites despite a preserved serum albumin level, a presentation not previously reported in adults. Imaging, ascitic fluid analysis, and serological testing excluded cirrhosis, malignancy, infection, and autoimmune serositis. The fluid showed a high serum-ascites albumin gradient (SAAG, 2.1 g/dL) with preserved protein (3.1 g/dL) and normal lactate dehydrogenase. Although the SAAG was high, there was no evidence of portal hypertension, and the mechanism remains undetermined. Serum and ascitic carbohydrate antigen 125 were elevated and normalized as the ascites resolved. Ascites-related symptoms, including early satiety, abdominal pain, and nausea, further reduced oral intake, while fluctuations in body fluid obscured the weight gain expected from nutritional rehabilitation, making weight-based assessment of treatment efficacy difficult. The ascites resolved with nutritional therapy and diuretics. Ascites can develop in adult patients with AN even when serum albumin is preserved. Beyond the psychopathology of AN, somatic symptoms caused by ascites may influence eating behavior and contribute to weight loss. Because fluctuations in body fluid can confound weight-based assessment of treatment response, comprehensive clinical evaluation incorporating abdominal imaging, rather than body weight alone, is warranted.

title: Recorded Urinary Ketone Results After Initiation of SGLT2 Inhibitors in Patients With and Without Diabetes: A Single-Center Retrospective Descriptive Study.
authorString: Iwasawa M, Nagasaki I, Yasui M, Kobayashi M, Inano H, Shimizu N, Hayashi A, Otori K.
abstractText: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) are prescribed for diabetes, chronic heart failure, and chronic kidney disease but are rarely associated with ketoacidosis, including euglycemic ketoacidosis. Although ketonuria is nonspecific and is not diagnostic of ketoacidosis, a positive urinary ketone result may prompt further clinical assessment. This study compared the proportion of participants with a recorded urinary ketone result after SGLT2i initiation between those with and without diabetes. This retrospective, single-center descriptive study included adults who initiated SGLT2i therapy at the study hospital between April 2022 and March 2023 and continued treatment for at least 180 days. Urinary ketone results, semiquantitative grades, and selected gastrointestinal symptoms documented in the electronic health record were assessed. Among 465 participants, a urinary ketone result was recorded in 273 of 350 participants in the diabetes group (78.0%) and 65 of 115 participants in the non-diabetes group (56.5%) (odds ratio, 2.73; 95% confidence interval, 1.74-4.26). During follow-up, 27 participants had a positive urinary ketone result; the highest recorded grade was 2+ or higher in 17 (63.0%). Among 127 participants without a recorded urinary ketone result, selected gastrointestinal symptoms were documented in 11 (8.7%), and no blood ketone result was identified for these participants. No documented hospital admissions for ketoacidosis were identified in the study hospital records. The proportion of participants with a recorded urinary ketone result after SGLT2i initiation was lower in the non-diabetes group than in the diabetes group. Although urinary ketone positivity alone cannot confirm ketoacidosis, a positive semiquantitative result may prompt context-based clinical review and, when clinically indicated, confirmatory evaluation. These findings suggest the importance of maintaining awareness of SGLT2i-associated ketoacidosis, including euglycemic ketoacidosis, regardless of diabetes status, and a potential role for pharmacists in facilitating context-based ketone assessment when clinically indicated.

title: Intercalated disc distribution of sodium and potassium channels on vulnerability to conduction block in cardiac tissue.
authorString: Pan J, Veeraraghavan R, Hanna P, Shivkumar K, Qu Z.
abstractText: In cardiac tissue, myocytes are electrically coupled via gap junctions or ephaptic interactions. Ephaptic coupling requires that the sodium (Na+) channels are densely distributed in the intercalated disc. In addition to Na+ channels, other ion channels are also densely distributed in the intercalated disc. In this study, we perform computer simulations to investigate how the intercalated disc localization of Na+ and potassium (K+) channels influences the vulnerability to conduction block in cardiac tissue. We show that when gap junction conductance is normal, a narrow cleft eliminates the vulnerable window (VW), a time window in which a premature beat conducting from the short action potential duration (APD) region toward the long APD region fails in the steep APD gradient region. The reduction in VW is due to shortening of APD in the long APD region, which reduces the APD gradient to suppress VW. The change of APD is mainly due to self-attenuation of Na+ current caused by ephaptic effect and K+ accumulation caused by the junctional inward rectifier K+ current. Na+ current self-attenuation is that opening of the Na+ channels in the cleft membrane lowers the potential in the cleft space to reduce the Na+ current by mainly reducing the driving force. When gap junction conductance is reduced to very low levels, a narrow cleft increases VW due to Na+ current self-attenuation and elevation of resting potential due to K+ accumulation, which affect conduction restitution properties to increase VW. In conclusion, ephaptic coupling or intercalated disc localization of Na+ and K+ channels can promote or suppress vulnerability to conduction block in cardiac tissue, depending on their effects on APD and conduction velocity restitution properties, which still follows the same kinematic theory developed previously.

title: Projected Demand for Cardiac Electrophysiology Procedures in Australia to 2040: A National Population-Based Modelling Study.
authorString: Wadforth B, Tu SJ, Wheaton R, Ganesan AN.
abstractText: Cardiac electrophysiology services are expanding rapidly owing to an ageing population, increasing prevalence of cardiac arrhythmias, expanding indications for catheter ablation and cardiac implantable electronic device (CIED) therapy, and continued advances in procedural technology. Despite this, the future demand for electrophysiology procedures has not been estimated. We conducted a national population-based forecasting study using Australian Institute of Health and Welfare hospital procedural data between 2010 and 2024. Catheter ablation and CIED procedures were identified using Australian Classification of Health Interventions procedure codes. Historical trends in procedural volume and population-adjusted utilisation were evaluated. Future procedural demand to 2040 was estimated using linear regression and generalised additive models. Between 2010 and 2024, 612,302 cardiac electrophysiology procedures were performed in Australia. Annual procedural volume increased from 28,805 to 55,919 procedures, representing a 94.1% increase. Catheter ablation activity increased by 200.8%, compared with 60.9% for CIED procedures. Atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation demonstrated the greatest absolute increase in procedure volume (7,582 annual procedures, 471.8%), while ventricular ablation demonstrated the greatest proportional increase (1,862.7%) from a low baseline volume. Forecast modelling projected total electrophysiology procedural activity to increase to 80,185 procedures annually by 2040 (95% confidence interval [CI], 76,237-84,133), representing a 43.4% (95% CI, 36.3-50.5%) increase from 2024. Catheter ablation demand is projected to increase by 54.2%, compared to 37.1% for CIED procedures, with AF ablation accounting for the largest increase in future procedural demand. Cardiac electrophysiology procedural demand in Australia is projected to increase substantially over the coming decades. The anticipated growth is driven predominantly by continued growth in catheter ablation, particularly AF ablation. These findings provide an evidence base to support planning of future electrophysiology workforce requirements, procedural infrastructure and healthcare resource allocation to ensure sufficient capacity to meet the growing demand for electrophysiology services.

title: Restoring mitophagy and oxidative phosphorylation coupled with ferroptosis suppression through Huoxue Tongmai formula ameliorates cardiac function in heart failure.
authorString: Lian Y, Chen Y, Lin Y, Yin J, Cao Y, Yan X, Li F, Feng L, Li Q.
abstractText: Huoxue Tongmai formula (XMT), a hospital-prepared traditional Chinese medicine formulation, has demonstrated clinical efficacy against cardiovascular diseases. However, its mechanisms in ameliorating myocardial hypertrophy remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to investigate the cardioprotective effects of XMT in a murine model of pressure overload-induced cardiac hypertrophy and to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms. Bioactive constituents of XMT were characterized using HPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS. In vivo assessments were conducted in a transverse aortic constriction (TAC)-induced cardiac hypertrophy mouse model, followed by transcriptomic profiling to identify differentially regulated pathways. In vitro experiments using angiotensin II (Ang II)-stimulated cardiomyocyte hypertrophy were performed to validate the protective effects and mechanisms of XMT. XMT administration significantly ameliorated TAC-induced cardiac dysfunction, as evidenced by improved echocardiographic parameters (LVEF, LVFS, and SV), as well as attenuated ventricular wall thickening and cardiac mass enlargement. XMT also reduced myocardial injury, interstitial fibrosis, and serum levels of NT-proBNP, cTn-T, CK-MB, and LDH. Notably, XMT suppressed pathological hypertrophic remodeling, reflected by decreased HW/TL and HW/BW ratios, reduced cardiomyocyte cross-sectional area, and downregulated expression of hypertrophic marker genes (Nppa, Nppb, and MYH7). Transcriptomic analysis revealed that XMT modulated pathways associated with mitochondrial function, oxidative phosphorylation, and mitophagy. Mechanistically, XMT upregulated the mitophagy regulators PINK1, Parkin, and FUNDC1, attenuated mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, and preserved mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) content. Moreover, XMT suppressed ferroptosis in hypertrophic hearts, as evidenced by increased GSH content, elevated GPX4 and SLC7A11 expression, and reduced MDA, total iron, and PTGS2 levels. In vitro, XMT exerted protective effects against Ang II-induced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, as demonstrated by enhanced cell viability, reduced LDH release, preserved mitochondrial membrane potential (ΔΨm), and marked suppression of mitochondrial ROS generation. XMT-medicated serum also attenuated Ang II-induced lipid peroxidation as measured by C11-BODIPY assay. Moreover, Seahorse-based metabolic flux analysis indicated that XMT significantly improved mitochondrial respiratory function, evidenced by elevated basal and maximal oxygen consumption rates (OCR). Concurrently, XMT attenuated the compensatory upregulation of glycolysis, as shown by a reduced extracellular acidification rate (ECAR) and diminished glycolytic reserve. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that XMT alleviates pressure overload-induced cardiac hypertrophy by enhancing mitochondrial respiration and promoting mitophagy, positioning it as a promising therapeutic candidate for hypertrophic heart failure.

title: Impact of intermittent hypoxia on drug-metabolizing enzymes and transporters and drug pharmacokinetics: an underestimated concern in obstructive sleep apnea patients?
authorString: Peyronnel C, Minovés M, Briançon-Marjollet A, Gaucher J, Faivre S, Baillieul S, Brossette M, Jambon-Barbara C, Pépin JL, Revol B, Tamisier R, Stanke-Labesque F, Gautier-Veyret E.
abstractText: Obstructive sleep apnea syndrome (OSA) is a prevalent and life-threatening respiratory disease. Marked by intermittent hypoxia (IH) and chronic inflammation, OSA frequently co-occurs with comorbidities like hypertension, diabetes, dyslipidemia or depression, necessitating various medications. However, the response to some treatments is notably compromised in OSA patients, manifesting as reduced efficacy and/or increased incidence of adverse events. The mechanisms underlying this altered pharmacological response remain unelucidated. Although comorbidities may substantially contribute to these alterations, IH and inflammation, key features of OSA, are known to modify drug-metabolizing enzymes and transporters (DMETs). We therefore hypothesized that OSA/IH may affect DMETs, thereby altering drug pharmacokinetics and drug response. This narrative review synthesizes existing literature regarding the impact of OSA/IH on DMETs and pharmacokinetics both in experimental models and human, along with the underlying mechanisms exploring the roles of pro-inflammatory cytokines, transcription factors and epigenetics. Subsequently, we discuss the potential consequences of these IH-induced DMETs alterations on drug response in OSA patient population. In this purpose, we examine the hypothesis of pharmacokinetic modifications for each drug (or pharmacotherapeutic class) whose response appears altered in OSA patients. Additionally, we analyze the pharmacokinetic profile of the most commonly dispensed medications in OSA patients in order to identify additional drugs whose efficacy or safety might be compromised by IH-induced DMETs alterations. Finally, in the absence of conclusive clinical evidence, we propose priority research areas to better characterize the impact of OSA/IH on DMETs, pharmacokinetics, and drug response, and the underlying mechanisms.

title: Cardiopulmonary exercise testing responses to treatment in patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension and cardiopulmonary comorbidities.
authorString: Baccelli A, Rinaldo RF, Davies RJ, Gin-Sing W, Vigo B, Lo Giudice F, Haji G, Howard LS.
abstractText: Current ESC/ERS guidelines suggest that initial monotherapy should be considered for pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) with cardiopulmonary comorbidities. However, data on the cardiopulmonary physiological responses to treatment in this subset of patients remain limited. Our aim was to evaluate the cardiopulmonary exercise and gas exchange response to treatment in patients with PAH and cardiopulmonary comorbidities. Do patients with PAH and a cardiopulmonary phenotype display a worse exercise capacity and gas exchange response to treatment? Incident treatment-naïve patients with idiopathic, heritable, drug/toxins-induced, HIV, and connective tissue disease-associated PAH were analysed at first follow-up. Comorbid patients were defined based on the presence of ≥3 risk factors among obesity (body mass index ≥30 Kg/m2), systemic arterial hypertension, diabetes mellitus, coronary artery disease, smoking history and transfer factor of the lung for carbon monoxide (TLCO) <45% predicted. A total of 178 patients were included: 52 with comorbidities and 126 without. Comorbid patients were older, predominantly male, and had a lower baseline exercise capacity, despite comparable hemodynamics. There were no differences in therapy, with approximately one third of patients receiving combination therapy in both groups at the time of reassessment. At follow-up, both groups demonstrated similar adjusted improvements from baseline in peak oxygen uptake, oxygen pulse, ventilatory efficiency and 6-minute walk distance, all known prognostic markers in PAH. However, comorbid patients exhibited a significantly worse gas exchange response to treatment, with an adjusted widening of the peak A-a gradient of +1.23 kPa compared with -0.35 kPa in patients without comorbidities (p=0.003). PAH patients with and without cardiopulmonary comorbidities achieve similar improvements in exercise capacity after treatment. However, the worse gas exchange response to exercise among comorbid patients warrants caution, careful monitoring and further research to confirm this finding.

title: Lactobacillus plantarum CCFM639 attenuates high-salt-induced hypertension involving IL-17A signaling suppression.
authorString: Lv X, Guo M, Zhang X, Liu L, Zhu Y, Wang Z, Yu F, Wang X, Feng L, Tian D, Zhou T.
abstractText: Chronic high-salt (HS) intake induces hypertension and is associated with reduced intestinal Lactobacillus. This study investigated underlying mechanisms for Lactobacillus plantarum CCFM639 (CCFM639) alleviating HS-induced hypertension. Hypertensive mice were established using an 8% HS diet, and blood pressure (BP), vascular function, gut microbiota, intestinal immunity, and inflammatory signaling were evaluated by radiotelemetry, pressure myography, 16S rRNA sequencing, histology, flow cytometry, qPCR, ELISA, and Western blot. CCFM639 significantly reduced BP, preserved intestinal barrier integrity, partially restored microbial dysbiosis, and suppressed ileal inflammation. Mechanistically, CCFM639 reduced IL-6 levels and inhibited the Interleukin-22 (IL-22) /STAT3/ Serum amyloid A (SAA) pathway, thereby limiting T helper 17 (Th17) cells activation and Interleukin-17A (IL-17A) production in the ileal lamina propria. IL-17A neutralization reproduced the antihypertensive and vasoprotective effects of CCFM639, accompanied by improved endothelium-dependent relaxation and reduced eNOS Thr495 phosphorylation and Ras homolog family member A (RhoA) expression. Consistently, CCFM639 supplementation reduced BP in hypertensive patients with high urinary sodium excretion, and the reduction in serum IL-17A levels was positively correlated with BP improvement. These findings demonstrate that CCFM639 supplementation increases intestinal Lactobacillus abundance and suppresses IL-17A signaling, thereby alleviating HS-induced hypertension.

title: Determinants of discordance between spot urine protein-to-creatinine ratio and 24-hour proteinuria during pregnancy.
authorString: Geçici NA, Demir FN, Kayıkçı U.
abstractText: To evaluate the diagnostic performance of the spot urine protein-to-creatinine ratio (UPCR) for detecting significant proteinuria during pregnancy, investigate factors associated with diagnostic discordance between spot UPCR and 24-h urine protein measurement, and identify predictors of false-negative UPCR results. This retrospective study included 145 pregnant women who underwent both spot UPCR and 24-h urine protein measurement during the same clinical evaluation. Patients were classified into four groups according to concordance between the two methods (true positive, true negative, false positive, and false negative). Diagnostic performance of spot UPCR was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. Clinical and laboratory characteristics were compared between concordance groups, and multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify independent predictors of diagnostic discordance and false-negative UPCR results. Spot UPCR showed moderate diagnostic performance for detecting significant proteinuria, with an AUC of 0.728, sensitivity of 57.1%, and specificity of 81.7%. Diagnostic discordance occurred in 29.0% of patients, with false-negative results accounting for most discordant cases. Among women with significant proteinuria confirmed by 24-h urine collection, 42.9% had UPCR values below the conventional diagnostic threshold. Urine sampling after 12:00 PM was independently associated with both diagnostic discordance and false-negative UPCR results. Although spot UPCR provides a practical alternative to 24-h urine collection, its diagnostic performance was only moderate, with a substantial proportion of false-negative results. Spot UPCR should be interpreted alongside the clinical presentation, and urine collection timing should be considered when interpreting results and planning clinical management.

title: Distinct Treg-Mediated Cardiac Remodeling in HFpEF Mice Treated With Neonatal Mesenchymal Stem Cells and Their Secretome.
authorString: Ge ZD, Han J, Takaesu F, Brazhkina O, Mishra R, Sharma S, Chen L, Fu X, Filipp M, Wai CM, Shao NY, Sinha A, Saha P, Puvvala A, Tulshyan A, Ventura L, Thakkar S, Bilewska A, Stefanowicz A, Guru SA, Gunasekaran M, Yang E, Dawn B, Yang P, Shah SJ, Thorp E, Davis ME, Kaushal S.
abstractText: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction lacks effective disease-modifying therapies. We show that neonatal mesenchymal stem cells and their secretome improve diastolic function by expanding regulatory T cells, reducing inflammation and fibrosis. Our new causal machine learning framework, variable importance prediction for cellular function, identified causal immune pathways driving cardiac functional improvement and revealed regulatory T cells as a therapeutic target.

title: Women's experiences of gynaecological surveillance in Lynch syndrome.
authorString: Johnson JE, Dore M, Saso S, Balega J, Duncan T, Smith T, Monahan KJ, Davidson EJ.
abstractText: Gynaecological surveillance is offered in Lynch syndrome despite limited evidence for its clinical effectiveness. Invasive gynaecological investigations often cause pain and distress, but experiences vary and little is known about the psychological burden of repeated testing. We evaluated the lived experiences of annual gynaecological surveillance in women with and at risk of Lynch syndrome. Recruitment occurred via hospital clinics, social media, and Lynch Syndrome UK. Participants completed a semi-structured questionnaire by telephone. Quantitative data were summarised descriptively. Free-text responses were recorded verbatim, coded inductively and grouped thematically, with outputs reviewed by a second researcher. Overall, 104 women participated: 93 had confirmed Lynch syndrome and 11 had a strong family history of Lynch syndrome cancers (median age: 41 years). Median pain scores were 7/10 for outpatient hysteroscopy (IQR 6-9) and endometrial biopsy (IQR 6-10), versus 3/10 for pelvic examination and transvaginal ultrasound scan (both IQR 2-4). Among participants undergoing annual surveillance (75/104), 74 (98.6%) found surveillance reassuring, but 44 (58.6%) reported surveillance-related anxiety. 51 (68%) said they attended all scheduled surveillance visits. Free-text responses identified anticipatory procedural distress and cancer worry, particularly fear of adverse findings. Participants described surveillance as necessary given the limited non-surgical alternatives. Although regular gynaecological surveillance provides reassurance, it imposes considerable physical, psychological and practical burdens. Addressing this requires a dual approach: immediate optimisation of pain management and psychological support within current clinics, alongside a long-term shift toward non-invasive diagnostic innovations to fundamentally transform the healthcare experiences of high-risk cohorts.

title: Advanced Heart Failure Therapies in Patients with Cancer or Cancer History: Review and Clinical Practice.
authorString: Gerhard EF, Viny A, Gejman RS, Cherng HJ, Pumpalova Y, Latif F, Maurer M, Sayer G, Uriel N, Raikhelkar J.
abstractText: This review summarizes current literature on advanced HF therapies including LVAD and HT in patients with cancer or cancer history, outlining pathophysiology, evolving epidemiology, and management in the contemporary era. Cancer survivors and HF patients are a growing population. Outcomes in LVAD patients with a history of malignancy show mildly reduced survival, increased GI bleeding, though similar rates of other adverse outcomes to non-cancer survivors. Malignancy risk in HT is multifactorial with contributions from age, immunosuppression, and history of PTM. For management of post-HT malignancies, strategies including immunosuppression reduction and mTOR inhibitors may improve outcomes. Cancer and cancer history play a significant role in the evaluation and management of patients undergoing LVAD or HT. Multidisciplinary evaluation including oncology, advanced HF, and cardio-oncology is essential for ideal candidate selection and nuances of management thereafter. Future studies are needed to better understand pathophysiology and management of advanced HF therapies in this population.

title: The role of transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation in cardiac fibrotic remodeling.
authorString: Lin H, Li J, Yu X, Meng L, Shao X, He L.
abstractText: Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) is being investigated as a non-invasive approach to cardiac fibrotic remodeling. This narrative review examines auricular afferent pathways, systemic responses and their duration, myocardial collagen in animal models, and human cardiovascular observations. Tracing and nerve-interruption experiments in cats and rodents identify vagal and non-vagal sensory pathways. Human brain imaging, muscle sympathetic recordings, and heart-rate variability measure different responses without identifying the initiating auricular afferent. Plasma obtained from healthy volunteers after tragus stimulation reduced acute ischemia-reperfusion injury in recipient isolated rat hearts; pharmacological and spleen-status comparisons supported cholinergic and splenic involvement. Canine post-infarction studies and rodent models of hypertensive or cardiometabolic heart failure with preserved ejection fraction report lower terminal myocardial collagen. In some rodent experiments, α7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor antagonism attenuated the tissue response, and comparable blood-pressure lowering did not reproduce it. These findings implicate mechanisms beyond unloading, but the reviewed studies have not demonstrated regression of fibrosis documented before treatment. Human trials report changes in acute injury, longitudinal strain, inflammation or arrhythmia alongside neutral controlled outcomes; none of the trials reviewed measured myocardial fibrosis. Further studies should connect cellular mechanisms to regional collagen measurements and assess serial fibrosis-sensitive imaging alongside function, treatment exposure and safety. taVNS may limit cardiac fibrotic remodeling, but its antifibrotic efficacy in humans remains unproven.

title: Impact of Patient-Reported Allergies on Clinical Outcomes Following Surgical Treatment of Insertional Achilles Tendinopathy.
authorString: Tran S, Lachance AD, Bauer R, Lee W.
abstractText: BackgroundPatient-reported allergies (PRAs) have been associated with worse outcomes after several orthopaedic procedures, including total hip and knee arthroplasty, but their effect after surgical treatment of insertional Achilles tendinopathy (IAT) is unknown. This study investigated whether the number of PRAs is associated with functional outcomes and postoperative complications after surgical treatment of IAT.MethodsWe retrospectively reviewed 28 patients (mean age, 54.8 years; 28.6% male; mean follow-up, 15.9 months) who underwent surgical treatment of IAT, stratified by number of PRAs: 0 (n = 10), 1 to 5 (n = 11), and >5 (n = 7). Primary outcomes were the Foot and Ankle Ability Measure (FAAM), Visual Analog Scale (VAS) pain, and Short Form-12 Physical and Mental Component Summary (PCS-12, MCS-12) scores at the most recent follow-up; SF-12 scores were available for 19 patients. Secondary outcomes were postoperative complications. Multivariable linear regression was used to adjust for baseline differences between groups.ResultsMedian FAAM scores were 60.0, 72.0, and 61.0 in the 0, 1 to 5, and >5 PRA groups (P = .87), and median VAS scores were 3.5, 2.0, and 3.0 (P = .47). PCS-12 (39.2, 37.4, and 51.6; P = .30) and MCS-12 (56.1, 52.3, and 56.5; P = .76) did not differ significantly. Hypertension and asthma were more prevalent in the >5 PRA group (P = .003 and P = .037). Achilles tendon rupture occurred in 2 (20.0%), 1 (9.1%), and 0 patients (P = .41) and 1 wound dehiscence occurred in the 1 to 5 group (P = .45); complication rates did not differ significantly among groups. After adjusting for ASA class, hypertension, and asthma, the number of PRAs was not significantly associated with any patient-reported outcome, although confidence intervals were wide.ConclusionIn this retrospective cohort, no statistically significant association was identified between the number of PRAs and functional outcomes or complication rates following surgical management of IAT. Given the limited sample size and heterogeneous allergy profiles, these findings should be interpreted cautiously.Level of Evidence:Level III: Retrospective cohort study.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Algorithm for Detection of Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy Compared with a Standard Electrocardiogram.
authorString: Morrison A, Sirgi Y, Spetko N, Song Y, Angell-James C, Cassidy M, Waks JW, Tahir U, Strom JB.
abstractText:
Background

Artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiography (AI-ECG) may facilitate detection of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), but its ability to identify higher-risk patients undergoing clinical evaluation for HCM remains uncertain.

Objectives

To evaluate the diagnostic and prognostic performance of a commercially available AI-ECG algorithm among patients undergoing cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) for suspected or established HCM.

Methods

We studied 102 patients with HCM and 302 age-, sex-, and year-matched controls without HCM who underwent clinically indicated CMR. An AI-ECG algorithm was applied to the first available ECG preceding CMR. Diagnostic performance, incremental value beyond standard ECG features, and associations with clinical outcomes were assessed.

Results

ECGs preceded CMR by a median of 1.1 years. AI-ECG demonstrated moderate sensitivity (51.1%) and high specificity (96.1%) for identification of phenotypic HCM and incrementally improved discrimination and reclassification beyond demographic and conventional ECG variables (net reclassification improvement 0.19, p<0.001). Within one year of CMR, a positive AI-ECG was independently associated with the composite outcome (adjusted HR 2.68, 95% CI 1.42-5.09; p=0.003), driven by ICD placement and septal reduction therapy. Among patients with HCM, while exploratory, an AI-ECG probability ≥ 0.99 identified those at highest risk for subsequent events (HR 2.92, 95% CI 1.59-5.35; p=0.011).

Conclusion

In conclusion, among patients undergoing clinical evaluation for HCM, AI-ECG provided incremental diagnostic value beyond conventional ECG parameters and identified individuals at increased risk for subsequent treatment-related clinical outcomes.

title: β-Myosin inhibition in skeletal muscle: Mavacamten’ s impact on the diaphragm
authorString: Sarfraz A, Nayak A, Holler T, Kraft T, Amrute-Nayak M.
abstractText:
The diaphragm, a primary respiratory muscle, contains nearly equal proportions of slow, Type-1 and fast, Type-II muscle fibers. Muscle fiber types -classified based on their shortening velocities and force generation abilities -are largely determined by distinct myosin II isoforms. Mavacamten (MAVA), a small molecule inhibitor of β-cardiac myosin ATPase, is currently used for the treatment of obstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy (HOCM). Notably, β-myosin heavy chain (β-MyHC) is not restricted to the ventricular myocardium but is also expressed in slow fibers, raising concerns about off-target effects of therapy used to treat cardiomyopathic conditions. Given that nearly 50 % of the fibers express β-MyHC in the diaphragm, we hypothesize that Mava may affect diaphragm muscle activity. Using an in vitro motility assay, we investigated the effects of Mava on native myosins isolated from rabbit diaphragm muscle and measured the velocity of actin and regulated thin filaments. Mava caused a dose-dependent decrease in myosin-driven actin filament velocity, with an apparent IC 50 of 1350 nM. Importantly, this inhibition was reversible upon drug washout, indicating a non-permanent modulatory effect. To determine the drug’s fiber-type specificity, we tested pure slow- and fast-myosin isoforms from the slow-twitch M. soleus and fast-twitch M. psoas. Both isoforms were inhibited by Mava, but slow myosin exhibited nearly 20-fold greater sensitivity than fast myosin, suggesting a potentially stronger impact on slow fibers. Interestingly, the slow myosin isoform showed even higher sensitivity to Mava than β-cardiac myosin. Further mechanistic analysis distinguished two modes of action: (i) promotion of OFF state of myosin, likely reducing a pool of active motors interacting with actin filaments, and (ii) modulation of the actomyosin biochemical cycle. Altogether, given the diaphragm’s reliance on both fiber types for sustained respiratory function, this off-target effect may impair respiratory performance in patients undergoing therapy, underscoring the need for respiratory function monitoring. The studies have direct implications for understanding the modulation of myosin function under physiological and pathophysiological conditions as well as following pharmacological interventions.

Statement of significance

By directly evaluating the effects of mavacamten (MAVA) on diaphragm myosin, this study bridges a critical mechanistic gap between cardiac myosin pharmacology and respiratory muscle physiology. Our findings show that MAVA strongly inhibits slow skeletal myosin activity, which accounts for nearly 50% of the diaphragm myosin population. In addition, we distinguished two distinct inhibitory modes of action for myosins in different conformational and functional configurations. This work establishes a framework for understanding MAVA’s potential off-target effects on respiratory mechanics and provides a foundation for future investigation into its consequences for diaphragm contractility in HCM patients undergoing MAVA treatment.

title: Histopathological evolution of transient zolbetuximab-induced protein-losing gastropathy: insights from two surgical cases.
authorString: Kaida S, Mukaisho KI, Fukuo A, Otake R, Takebayashi K, Hosoi K, Kageyama Y, Nakayama T, Kushima R, Tani M.

journal.title: Virchows Archiv : an international journal of pathology

abstractText: Zolbetuximab, a claudin 18.2 (CLDN18.2)-targeted antibody, can cause gastritis and hypoalbuminemia, but the histopathological basis and reversibility of this toxicity remain incompletely understood. We examined two patients who underwent gastrectomy after zolbetuximab-containing chemotherapy. Both developed diffuse erythematous hypertrophic gastropathy with severe hypoalbuminemia that subsequently improved despite continued therapy. Resected specimens showed extensive oxyntic gland loss, marked foveolar hyperplasia, MUC6-positive pseudopyloric m​etaplasia, preservation of the Ki67-positive proliferative isthmic compartment, and G-cell hyperplasia. Residual differentiated glandular cells strongly expressed CLDN18.2, whereas expression was weak in the proliferative compartment. In one patient, gastritis completely resolved in the remnant stomach one year after distal gastrectomy. These findings are consistent with preferential injury to CLDN18.2-expressing differentiated gastric epithelium with relative preservation of regenerative capacity, providing a histopathological framework for the transient nature of zolbetuximab-induced protein-losing gastropathy.

title: Very late local recurrence of chromophobe renal cell carcinoma 15 years after nephrectomy: a case report.
authorString: Saklis A, Hatzichristodoulou G.
abstractText:
Background

Chromophobe renal cell carcinoma (chRCC) is a rare subtype of renal cell carcinoma, accounting for approximately 5% of cases. Although generally associated with a favorable prognosis, late recurrences may occur. Local recurrence more than a decade after nephrectomy is exceptionally rare, and optimal management remains poorly defined.

Case presentation

We report a 79-year-old Greek man who underwent radical left nephrectomy and adrenalectomy in 2009 for a 13 × 10 × 9 cm moderately differentiated chRCC, classified in the original pathology report as pT2 pNX pMX, G2, R0. Fifteen years later, he presented with progressive limitation of left hip flexion and increasing constipation. Contrast-enhanced CT demonstrated a solitary 9 × 8 × 7.5 cm left para-aortic retroperitoneal mass without radiologically detectable distant metastatic disease. Biopsy findings were consistent with recurrent renal cell carcinoma. The lesion was clinically classified as a local recurrence based on its location within the previous nephrectomy operative field and the absence of other metastatic lesions, although a solitary metastasis could not be unequivocally excluded histopathologically. After multidisciplinary assessment, complete surgical resection with systematic retroperitoneal lymph-node dissection was performed. Histopathological examination showed morphological features compatible with recurrence or metastasis of the previous chRCC, tumor-free margins, tumor-free sampled peritumoral skeletal muscle, and 0/16 involved lymph nodes. Immunohistochemical analysis was not performed. At 1-year follow-up, the patient remained clinically well with no radiological evidence of local recurrence or distant metastatic disease.

Conclusion

Very late recurrence of chRCC may occur after a prolonged disease-free interval. In carefully selected patients with isolated and potentially resectable recurrence, complete surgical resection may represent a feasible treatment option within an individualized multidisciplinary approach. The 1-year follow-up in this case is insufficient to establish long-term oncological control, and continued surveillance is warranted.

title: En Bloc Pelvic Lymph Node Dissection Using the da Vinci SP System for Endometrial Cancer.
authorString: Kanno K, Iwata T, Sawada M, Andou M.
abstractText:
Background

Although sentinel lymph node mapping has become the standard approach for surgical staging in early-stage endometrial cancer, systematic pelvic lymph node dissection (PLND) continues to play an important role in selected patients with intermediate- and high-risk disease.1 Furthermore, PLND is a fundamental surgical procedure, performed not only for gynecologic oncology procedures, but also for colorectal and urologic oncology procedures.2,3 This video demonstrates the key anatomical landmarks and our standardized anatomy-based concept for en bloc PLND, followed by its implementation using the da Vinci SP surgical system (SP), a newer single-port robotic platform.

Methods

A 66-year-old woman with preoperatively diagnosed early-stage uterine serous carcinoma (p53-positive) underwent single-port robotic staging surgery, including simple hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, pelvic and para-aortic lymph node dissection, and partial omentectomy.

Results

The procedure was completed without intraoperative complications. A standardized, anatomy-based approach using reproducible anatomical landmarks facilitated safe and systematic en bloc PLND. Suspension of the vesicohypogastric fascia (umbilical artery) provided stable exposure of the retroperitoneal space, while the articulating snake-like instruments of the SP platform enabled precise traction and countertraction, facilitating meticulous dissection throughout the procedure. Final histopathological examination confirmed stage IIC uterine serous carcinoma. The patient subsequently received adjuvant paclitaxel-carboplatin chemotherapy and remains disease-free at the latest follow-up.

Conclusions

The SP platform enables standardized, anatomy-based, en bloc PLND while adhering to fundamental oncologic principles. The anatomical concepts and technical strategies may facilitate reproducible surgical practice and may be applicable across multiple specialties in pelvic oncology.

title: The relationship between socio-environmental factors, brain growth and cognition in middle childhood.
authorString: Bonthrone AF, Gal-Er B, MacLeod R, Chew A, van der Meijden MEM, Price A, Kelly C, Pushparajah K, Simpson J, Egloff A, Arulkumaran S, Casella C, Brackenier Y, Cordero-Grande L, Malik S, Hajnal JV, Edwards AD, Nosarti C, O'Muircheartaigh J, Counsell SJ.
abstractText:
Background

The relationship between socio-environmental factors, brain growth, and cognition in childhood is unknown. This study aimed to characterize associations between (i) regional brain growth from birth to 6-8 years and socio-environmental factors; and (ii) regional brain growth and cognitive outcomes in middle childhood.

Methods

One hundred and thirty-seven 6-8-year-old children (25 with congenital heart disease) underwent neonatal and paediatric brain MRI and a full-scale IQ assessment. Data on household income, maternal education, neighborhood deprivation, and early cognitively stimulating home environment were collected. Regional brain growth (extracerebral CSF, ventricles, cortical grey matter, white matter, deep grey matter, cerebellum, brainstem) from the neonatal period to 6-8 years was assessed using Gaussian process regression.

Results

Low household income was associated with reduced cortical grey matter growth (B, 95% CI -1.14, -1.88 to -0.396; pFWE = 0.044) and extracerebral CSF expansion (-1.55, -2.51 to -0.585; pFWE = 0.042). Higher cortical grey matter (3.89, 1.12-6.65; pFWE = 0.038) and brainstem (3.24, 0.894-5.58; pFWE = 0.038) growth were associated with better full-scale IQ. Brainstem (p = 0.014), but not cortical grey matter (p = 0.177), remained significant after adjustment for socio-environmental factors.

Conclusions

Support for financially vulnerable families may promote brain growth. Brainstem growth is a brain correlate of childhood cognition independent of the effects of socio-environmental factors.

Impact

One hundred and thirty-seven children (25 with congenital heart disease) underwent neuroimaging at birth and at 6-8 years and a full-scale IQ assessment at 6-8 years. Household income, maternal education, neighborhood deprivation and early home environment data were collected. After adjustment for other socio-environmental factors and group, low household income was associated with reduced cortical grey matter growth and extracerebral CSF expansion. Higher cortical grey matter and brainstem growth were associated with higher full-scale IQ in middle childhood. Household poverty was linked to reduced brain growth, while cortical grey matter and brainstem growth were associated with cognitive abilities in childhood.

title: Gestational co-exposure to PM<sub>2.5</sub> and heat impaired cardiac development in offspring.
authorString: Liu Z, Yang S, Ding R, Tian L, Lv J, Chen G, Sun Z, Guo Y, Duan J.
abstractText: Air pollution and extreme heat frequently co-occur, yet their combined effects on cardiac development following gestational exposure remain poorly understood. We investigated the effects and potential mechanisms of gestational co-exposure to PM<sub>2.5</sub> and heat. Pregnant mice were exposed to filtered air, PM<sub>2.5</sub> (10 μg/m<sup>3</sup>), heat (39 ℃), or both for 2 h/day from embryonic day 6.5 (E6.5) to E18.5, and offspring hearts were evaluated on postnatal day 1 (P1). Gestational co-exposure increased ventricular wall thickness and impaired systolic function, accompanied by inflammatory cell infiltration, oxidative damage, and mitochondrial ultrastructural changes. Integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses revealed that co-exposure altered pathways related to energy metabolism, including inositol phosphate metabolism and pantothenate and CoA biosynthesis. Further analysis of the differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and differentially abundant metabolites (DAMs) revealed that myo-inositol levels and Ucp2 expression were reduced after co-exposure. These changes are noteworthy because myo-inositol has been linked to congenital heart defect risk, while UCP2 contributes to neonatal cardiomyocyte metabolism. Experimental validation further showed that co-exposure decreased ATP content, downregulated cardiac development-related genes, and increased the protein expression of DRP1 and FIS1. Collectively, these findings suggest that mitochondrial dysfunction may contribute to impaired cardiac development following gestational co-exposure, with reductions in myo-inositol levels and UCP2 expression potentially involved in this process. These findings provide preliminary mechanistic insights into the developmental cardiotoxicity of combined environmental exposures.

title: ALCAPA: Use and Necessity of Different Surgical Techniques.
authorString: Harris L, Mohammad Y, Pavlovsky E, Dorton CW, Erez E, DiMaio JM, Squiers JJ, Schaffer JM, Brinkman WT, Harrington K.
abstractText: Anomalous left coronary artery from the pulmonary artery (ALCAPA) is a rare congenital heart disease in which the origin of the left coronary artery from the pulmonary artery leads to myocardial ischemia. Although most patients present in infancy, rare cases are diagnosed in adulthood. Coronary reimplantation remains the gold standard intervention. However, there is no consensus on the preferred secondary procedure if direct reimplantation is not possible. We present a 3-patient case series of adults with ALCAPA undergoing surgical repair. Each patient underwent a unique surgical correction: direct reimplantation, interposition graft repair, or Takeuchi repair. These cases demonstrate that with appropriate preoperative planning and familiarity with various repair techniques, satisfactory short-term postoperative outcomes can be achieved in adults with ALCAPA.
