title: Train hard, recover smart: the supplement framework to enhance exercise recovery in recreational and elite-level athletes.
authorString: Conti F, Garner D, Galpin AJ.

journal.title: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition

abstractText: Background: Exercise-induced inflammation and muscle damage are frequent consequences of structured physical activity that facilitate muscle growth and subsequent training adaptations. Performance improvements are strongly dependent upon athletes' capacity to successfully recover from previous sessions or challenging efforts, particularly when opportunities to rest and recover are limited. Nutritional practices centered around acute or chronic ingestion of certain foods or dietary bioactive compounds have been shown to accelerate neurophysiological and subjective recovery outcomes and may be worthy of consideration in both recreationally active and professional athletic populations. Methods: This review provides a comprehensive summary of dietary strategies to promote exercise recovery that are supported by robust scientific evidence, including systematic reviews, randomized clinical trials, and observational studies up to August 2025. Results: Despite substantial variability in evidence quality, identified nutrients, dietary supplements, and bioactive compounds of greatest interest for athletes are omega-3 fatty acids and creatine monohydrate, while additional compounds showing promising results in improving subjective or objective recovery metrics such as inflammatory biomarkers, muscle soreness, and fatigue include magnesium, taurine, curcumin, L-Carnitine, Ashwagandha, anthocyanins, L-Citrulline, gingerol, tart cherry, beetroot, and pomegranate juice. Nutrients or compounds often popularized but requiring further investigation, current research gaps, and methodological limitations within the available body of literature are also discussed. Conclusion: The findings outlined in this review may inform evidence-based recovery nutrition strategies for both elite and recreational athletes.

title: Prognostic significance of incident microalbuminuria in a real-world population at increased cardiovascular risk: A report from a global federated research network.
authorString: Busti M, Monzo L, Rastogi T, Savarese G, Baudry G, Girerd N.
abstractText:
Aim

Despite growing interest in biomarker-based risk stratification for incident heart failure (HF), the prognostic value of newly detected microalbuminuria is poorly defined. This study evaluated its association with incident HF and cardiorenal outcomes in a large real-world cohort.

Methods

A total of 985,367 patients aged 40-80 years at increased cardiovascular (CV) risk but with no prior HF or chronic kidney disease (CKD) stage ≥3 was included from the TriNetX Global Research Network. Patients with persistent normoalbuminuria (UACR <30 mg/g) were compared to those with newly detected microalbuminuria (UACR 30-300 mg/g). The primary outcome was a composite of incident HF or all-cause mortality over a maximum 5-year follow-up. Propensity score matching was performed to balance baseline characteristics.

Results

After matching, 150,250 patients were included in each group. Over a median follow-up of 2.5 [IQR range, 3.6] years, newly detected microalbuminuria was associated with a higher risk of the primary composite outcome (HR 1.29 [95% CI 1.25-1.34]), as well as higher incident HF (HR 1.31 [95% CI 1.26-1.36]), all-cause mortality (HR 1.43 [95% CI 1.35-1.51]), HFrEF (HR 1.61 [95% CI 1.51-1.71]), HFpEF (HR 1.37 [95% CI 1.29-1.45]), acute myocardial infarction (HR 1.33 [95% CI 1.25-1.41]), ischemic stroke (HR 1.27 [95% CI 1.20-1.35]) and increased risks of CKD progression to stage 3 (HR 2.80 [95% CI 2.67-2.93]) and stage 4 (HR 4.71 [95% CI 4.11-5.40]). In exploratory subgroup analyses, renal function showed the largest number of nominal interaction findings.

Conclusions

In this real-world cohort of patients at increased CV risk, newly detected microalbuminuria was associated with higher cardiorenal risk, supporting further evaluation of UACR for early risk stratification.

title: Associations of Clinical Characteristics and Lipid-Lowering Therapy With the Carotid Plaque Lipidome.
authorString: Seidlová A, Svoboda N, Voldřich R, Polášková L, Bechyňská K, Kosek V, Pulkrabová J, Hajšlová J, Školoudík D, Netuka D.
abstractText:
Background

Carotid atherosclerosis is a major risk factor for ischemic stroke. Plaque lipidomics may complement clinical assessment by providing biochemical insight into plaque heterogeneity and associations with risk factors and therapy.

Methods

Patients undergoing carotid endarterectomy between 2020 and 2023 (age 18-90 years) were included. Plaques were excised en bloc, snap-frozen, sectioned, and analyzed by UHPLC-HRMS. A representative lipidomic profile per patient was calculated as the median across plaque sections. Associations with clinical characteristics and lipid-lowering therapy intensity were assessed using univariate testing, ANOVA, correlation analysis, and decision-tree models.

Results

The cohort comprised 82 patients. Sex showed the strongest lipidomic signal, with higher plasmalogen abundance in plaques from female patients and higher ceramides, diacylglycerols, and triacylglycerols in plaques from male patients. Hypertension was associated with increased sphingolipids and reduced plasmalogens, whereas diabetes mellitus showed differences across multiple lipid classes (e.g., cholesteryl esters, lysophosphatidylcholines, plasmalogen phospholipids, and sphingomyelin). Lipid-lowering therapy intensity was associated with distinct lipidomic patterns, with higher levels of selected cholesteryl esters in patients without statin therapy and more prominent ether-linked TAGs and plasmalogen phospholipids in high-intensity statin users.

Conclusions

Carotid plaque lipidomic composition is associated with clinical characteristics and lipid-lowering therapy, capturing biologically meaningful heterogeneity of atherosclerosis.

title: Machine learning-derived discordance between predicted mortality risk and valve surgery utilisation in infective endocarditis: a nationwide population-level analysis including injection drug use-associated disease.
authorString: Elbana MK, Amin A, Ahmed GM, Mohamed Mostafa ME, Sherif A, Khalafallah MA.
abstractText:
Background

Infective endocarditis (IE) carries high mortality, and valve surgery is indicated in selected patients on the basis of specific clinical circumstances assessed by a multidisciplinary Endocarditis Team. Predicted mortality risk is not equivalent to surgical indication; nevertheless, how surgical utilisation is distributed across the spectrum of illness severity at the population level has not been described. We used machine learning (ML) to describe population-level variation in valve surgery utilisation across strata of predicted in-hospital mortality risk, with a secondary focus on injection drug use (IDU)-associated IE.

Methods

We analysed adult hospitalisations with an IE diagnosis code in the National Inpatient Sample (2016-2022). Co-primary outcomes were in-hospital mortality and valve surgery. Weighted multivariable logistic regression identified factors independently associated with each outcome. Machine learning models (LASSO, random forest, and XGBoost) were trained using demographic, clinical, and hospital characteristics recorded during the hospitalisation, with temporal validation (2016-2020 training; 2021-2022 testing) and supplementary 5-fold cross-validation. Because diagnoses are recorded for the entire hospitalisation, the models were framed as retrospective, discharge-level risk classification rather than prospective prediction. Model performance was evaluated using AUROC, AUPRC, Brier score, and F1 score, and SHAP analysis was used for model interpretability.

Results

Among 125,100 IE hospitalisations (weighted ≈ 625,500), in-hospital mortality was 10.1% and the valve surgery rate was 8.3%. In the 2021-2022 temporal test set, the XGBoost mortality model achieved an AUROC of 0.842 (95% CI 0.836-0.848) and an AUPRC of 0.395 (event rate 11.8%), and the surgery model an AUROC of 0.857 (0.850-0.864) and an AUPRC of 0.403 (event rate 8.5%). Observed mortality increased approximately 80-fold across predicted-risk quintiles (Q1: 0.4% to Q5: 35.5%), whereas surgery rates varied only modestly (Q1: 5.6%; Q4: 10.8%; Q5: 9.5%). In SHAP analysis, mortality predictions were most strongly influenced by clinical severity markers (APR-DRG mortality risk, age, APR-DRG severity), whereas surgery predictions were most strongly influenced by age and hospital characteristics (bed size, teaching status, transfer-in), together with arrhythmia. IDU-associated IE (23.3%) had lower adjusted mortality (aOR 0.64, 95% CI 0.62-0.65) and was only weakly associated with surgery after adjustment (aOR 0.97); surgery rates were comparable between IDU and non-IDU hospitalisations at similar predicted risk. Mortality increased from 8.2% (2016) to 11.9% (2022; P-trend < 0.001), while surgery rates remained stable. Findings were unchanged after excluding APR-DRG variables.

Conclusion

At the population level, valve surgery utilisation in IE varied little across a wide gradient of predicted in-hospital mortality and was more closely associated with patient age and hospital characteristics than with markers of illness severity. Because administrative data cannot establish surgical indication, operability, or patient preferences, these findings describe variation in utilisation rather than under-treatment of individual patients. IDU status was not a dominant correlate of surgical utilisation once predicted risk was considered. These hypothesis-generating findings warrant confirmation in clinically detailed cohorts that capture guideline-defined surgical indications.

Trial registration

Not applicable.

title: Post-MI Left Ventricular Pseudoaneurysm Incidentally Revealed by CT Renal for Flank Pain-A Case Report.
authorString: Rahman H, Alfilfil WA.
abstractText: Post-MI LV pseudoaneurysm with contained rupture and apical thrombus was incidentally discovered in a 55-year-old diabetic hypertensive male presenting with flank pain and haematuria. ECG and labs confirmed late anterior STEMI with cardiogenic shock (SCAI-B). He underwent Dor procedure, triple CABG, and IABP support with postoperative stabilization. This case is reported because LV pseudoaneurysm is a rare, life-threatening complication that can present with atypical, non-cardiac symptoms such as flank pain rather than classic chest pain, and its incidental detection on a non-cardiac CT study underscores the diagnostic value of maintaining a broad differential in patients with cardiovascular risk factors. It illustrates how prompt multimodal imaging and timely surgical referral can substantially improve outcomes in a condition that otherwise carries very high mortality if missed.

title: Association Between Peripheral and Coronary Subclinical Atherosclerosis Burden in Midlife.
authorString: García-Lunar I, Fuster V, Kofoed KF, Pérez-García CN, Larsen AF, Gómez-Talavera S, Moreno-Arciniegas A, Pizarro G, Taylor D, Mass V, García-Martí G, Devesa A, Vazirani R, Fernández-Ortiz A, Navarro Á, Collet-Billon A, Fuster JJ, Sánchez González J, Bundgaard H, García-Álvarez A, Ibanez B.
abstractText:
Background

Atherosclerosis, silent in its early stages, underlies most cardiovascular manifestations. The inter-relation between silent atherosclerosis across vascular territories remains insufficiently characterized.

Objectives

The aim of this study was to assess the association between peripheral and coronary atherosclerosis in asymptomatic individuals.

Methods

A subgroup of individuals of the PESA (Progression of Early Subclinical Atherosclerosis) cohort underwent contrast-enhanced coronary computed tomography angiography in addition to peripheral (carotid and femoral) atherosclerosis assessment using 3-dimensional vascular ultrasound. Peripheral global plaque volume was calculated as the sum of bilateral carotid and femoral plaque burden using an artificial intelligence-based automated approach. Coronary computed tomographic angiographic images were qualitatively evaluated for the presence and severity of coronary atherosclerosis (percentage stenosis) and quantitatively for coronary artery calcium score (CACS) and global coronary plaque volume measurement.

Results

A total of 374 participants (mean age: 55 years, 34% women, 63% with CACS = 0) were included. Peripheral atherosclerosis was present in 75%. Peripheral global plaque volume was significantly associated with the presence, severity, and burden of coronary atherosclerosis (coronary plaque volume) (r = 0.69; P < 0.001). After adjustment for age, sex, and conventional risk factor profile, individuals with peripheral atherosclerosis had nearly 3 times greater odds of having coronary atherosclerosis than those without (OR: 2.66; 95% CI: 1.50-4.72; P = 0.001). Both carotid and femoral atherosclerosis remained significantly and independently associated with coronary plaque. Among participants with CACS = 0, noncalcified coronary plaque was detected in 12.0%, nearly all of whom (93%) had concomitant peripheral atherosclerosis.

Conclusions

Peripheral and coronary atherosclerosis were strongly correlated in asymptomatic persons. Both carotid and femoral atherosclerosis were associated with coronary artery disease independently of each other.

title: Zhenwu Decoction improves mitochondrial metabolism in pressure-overload cardiac dysfunction with involvement of PGC-1α.
authorString: Liu C, Zhang Z, Meng T, Li C, Wang B, Fu Q, Wang H, Ge P.
abstractText:
Background

Pressure-overload cardiac dysfunction is accompanied by impaired mitochondrial respiration and oxidative injury. The contribution of PGC-1α-associated regulation to the metabolic effects of Zhenwu Decoction (ZWD) remains unclear.

Purpose

To examine the contribution of PGC-1α to ZWD-associated changes in mitochondrial metabolism during pressure overload.

Study design

A transverse aortic constriction (TAC) mouse model and angiotensin II (Ang II)-challenged H9c2 cardiomyoblasts were studied. PGC-1α involvement was examined using SR-18292 treatment and siRNA-mediated suppression.

Methods

Mice received ZWD at 4.32, 8.64 or 17.28 g crude-drug equivalents/kg/day for 4 weeks after postoperative assessment. We assessed cardiac function, Masson-positive collagen area, redox indices, energy metabolites, mitochondrial ultrastructure and respiratory-complex activities. Cardiac metabolomics and computational target analysis were combined with fluorescence, extracellular-flux, transcript and protein measurements in H9c2 cells. Cells received 10% (v/v) serum from ZWD-dosed rats.

Results

ZWD treatment was associated with improved systolic indices, lower Masson-positive collagen area and changes in myocardial ATP, redox indices and respiratory-complex activities. Of 651 evaluated metabolomic features, 175 differed between TAC and control samples (54 increased and 121 decreased). ZWD-treated and untreated TAC samples differed in 104 features (60 increased and 44 decreased; six samples per group). Succinate and malate changed in opposite directions in TAC hearts and shifted towards control levels with ZWD. In H9c2 cells, serum treatment was associated with changes in mitochondrial readouts and higher PGC-1α, SIRT3 and PPARγ expression. Partial PGC-1α suppression attenuated several serum-associated responses.

Conclusion

The findings associate ZWD treatment with improved mitochondrial metabolic indices and implicate PGC-1α-associated regulation. The cellular intervention evaluates a mixture in serum from dosed animals; its active circulating constituents and the direct molecular interactions remain to be identified.

title: Bedside electromagnetic neuronavigation for cranial access procedures in neurotrauma and neurocritical care.
authorString: Aabedi AA, Sibih YE, Caldwell DJ, Letchuman V, Velasco MCV, Amorim E, Haddad AF, Chang D, Chung JE, Wang MB, Osorio RC, Chyall L, Halabi C, Hinson HE, Sun PP, Saigal R, DiGiorgio AM, Huang MC, Tarapore PE, Manley GT, Yue JK.
abstractText:
Background

Bedside cranial access devices (external ventricular drain (EVD), subdural evacuation port system (SEPS), parenchymal intracranial pressure (ICP) monitor) are foundational to neurotrauma and neurocritical care. Craniometric-based techniques are limited by aberrant anatomy, clot-filled ventricles, and complex extra-axial collections. Bedside electromagnetic (EM) neuronavigation registered to computed tomography (CT) imaging may enable precise targeting without requiring transport to the operating room, general anesthesia, or rigid cranial fixation.

Methods

We retrospectively reviewed patients undergoing bedside cranial procedures with EM-neuronavigation (Medtronic StealthStation) from November 1, 2025 to July 21, 2026 at our Level I trauma center neurocritical care unit for distorted anatomy, atypical targets, and/or high consequences of imprecision. Outcomes included device function, post-procedure neuroimaging confirmation of device placement, and navigation-related complications.

Results

Ten patients underwent 15 EM-navigated bedside procedures (11 EVDs, 2 SEPS, 2 parenchymal ICP monitors). Clinical indications included aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage, traumatic brain injury, loculated subdural hematoma, ventriculitis, ventricular trapping, obstructive hydrocephalus, and intracerebral hemorrhage. Notably, EM-navigation enabled dual-catheter placement to access non-communicating ventricular compartments and optimized SEPS placements at maximal extra-axial collection thickness while avoiding vascular membranes. All procedures achieved intended device function and intended positioning on post-procedure imaging. There were no complications or revision procedures related to EM-navigation.

Conclusions

In this single-center proof-of-principle series, bedside EM-navigation was feasible, safe, and readily integrated into high-risk patient care workflows in neurocritical care. Whether bedside neuronavigation improves procedural precision, supports clinician education, or reduces operative and transport needs was beyond the scope of the current study and requires well-designed prospective evaluation.

Level of evidence

Level V, Therapeutic/Care Management.

title: Integrating UHPLC-Q/TOF MS, network pharmacology and experimental validation to reveal the potential mechanisms and bioactive components of Zhuang medicine Longzuan Tongbi granules against rheumatoid arthritis.
authorString: Yao L, Li M, Cheng S, Zhang H, Fang G, Zhang Q, Pang Y, Abliz Z, Zhou W.

journal.title: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology

abstractText:
Background

Longzuan Tongbi granules (LZTBG), a clinically validated eight-herb Zhuang medicine formula containing alkaloids, flavonoids, coumarins, and lignans, exerts anti-RA effects through multi-component, multi-target regulation. However, due to the complexity of its chemical composition, the anti-RA material basis and underlying mechanisms of LZTBG have not been systematically explored.

Purpose

The objective of this study was to identify the active components and molecular mechanisms of LZTBG in the therapy of RA.

Methods

The chemical constituents of LZTBG were comprehensively characterized using UHPLC-Q/TOF MS coupled with feature-based molecular networking (FBMN). Serum pharmacochemistry was performed to identify absorbed components and investigate their in vivo metabolic patterns in rats. Network pharmacology combined with previously published metabolomics data was employed to predict core targets and potential regulatory pathways. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations were conducted to validate target-ligand interactions. Finally, in vitro experiments using LPS-induced RAW264.7 macrophages were performed to verify the anti-RA effects and underlying mechanisms of the candidate compounds via ELISA, qRT-PCR, and Western blot analyses.

Results

A total of 235 chemical constituents were characterized in LZTBG, with alkaloids and coumarins identified as major active types. Serum pharmacochemistry detected 74 LZTBG-related compounds in rat plasma, revealing structure-dependent disparities in metabolic behaviors. Network pharmacology integrated with metabolomics highlighted ALOX5, MAPK3, and PIK3CA as core targets, with ALOX5 prioritized based on high-confidence protein-protein interaction evidence and topological significance. KEGG enrichment indicated primary involvement of lipid and atherosclerosis pathways. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations demonstrated that bergapten, magnoflorine, and marmesin bound stably to these targets, with MAPK and ALOX5 complexes displaying optimal structural stability. In vitro validation confirmed that these compounds significantly suppressed LPS-induced upregulation of IL-1β and TNF-α, downregulated ALOX5, MAPK3, and PIK3CA mRNA and protein expression, and inhibited ERK1/2 phosphorylation in a dose-dependent manner.

Conclusion

This study systematically elucidates that bergapten, magnoflorine, and marmesin are the principal active components of LZTBG against RA. The therapeutic effects are mediated through multi-component, multi-target regulation of the MAPK/ERK and PI3K/Akt signaling pathways and their downstream inflammatory target ALOX5. The integration of multi-omics data with experimental validation provides a robust paradigm for deciphering the complex mechanisms of traditional medicines and highlights ALOX5 as a promising therapeutic target for RA intervention.

title: A novel small-molecule inhibitor of proteoglycan GAG-chain elongation that alone or in combination with rosuvastatin inhibits lipid deposition in the aortic walls of high-fat fed ApoE<sup>-/-</sup> mice.
authorString: Afroz R, Malapitan SM, Xu S, Little PJ, Kamato D.
abstractText: Subendothelial retention of atherogenic lipoproteins by vascular proteoglycans is a key initiating event in atherosclerosis. The elongation of glycosaminoglycan (GAG) chains on proteoglycans enhances lipid binding and retention. We have shown that the Smad2 transcription factor in the linker region is a common signalling intermediate that regulates GAG chain elongation in vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs). This study used a small molecule kinase inhibitor to investigate whether inhibition of the Smad2 transcription factor and GAG chain elongation in vitro correlates with a reduction in lipid deposition in vivo. We identified a potent new kinase inhibitor, Cyc12068, and tested its effects on PDGF-mediated GAG chain elongation in VSMCs by measuring mRNA expression of GAG biosynthesis genes and [<sup>35</sup>S]-sulfate incorporation into secreted proteoglycans. ApoE<sup>-/-</sup> mice were fed a high-fat diet for 12 weeks and treated with Cyc12068 alone or in combination with rosuvastatin. Aortic wall lipid deposition was quantified by en face Oil Red O staining. Plasma lipid parameters and aortic mRNA expression of GAG elongation genes were assessed. Cyc12068 dose-dependently inhibited PDGF-induced expression of GAG biosynthesis genes, [<sup>35</sup>S]-sulfate incorporation into secreted proteoglycans, and biglycan GAG chain elongation in VSMCs. Cyc12068 also suppressed PDGF-mediated Smad2 linker region phosphorylation. In high-fat diet-fed ApoE<sup>-/-</sup> mice, Cyc12068 reduced aortic wall lipid deposition both as monotherapy and in combination with rosuvastatin. Unlike rosuvastatin, Cyc12068 did not alter plasma lipid parameters, indicating that its anti-atherogenic effect was independent of systemic lipid lowering. Cyc12068 also reduced aortic expression of GAG elongation genes, whereas rosuvastatin no effect on this pathway. By demonstrating a reduction in aortic wall lipid deposition when Cyc12068 was administered alone or with rosuvastatin, these findings identify inhibition of proteoglycan GAG chain elongation as a potential vessel wall-directed strategy that is mechanistically distinct from lipid lowering therapy.

title: Anaesthetic management for first-trimester pregnancy termination in a patient with uncorrected persistent truncus arteriosus: a case report.
authorString: Zhan Y, Wang R, Xie H.
abstractText: Persistent truncus arteriosus (PTA) is a rare cyanotic congenital heart defect with substantial cardiovascular risk during pregnancy. We report a gravida 1, para 0, 20-year-old woman with unrepaired PTA undergoing suction curettage at 6 weeks and 2 days of gestation. She had chronic hypoxaemia and secondary erythrocytosis, with no chronic medications or previous surgery. Echocardiography showed a 16-mm ventricular septal defect with predominant right-to-left shunting, and approximately 50% truncal override. A left radial arterial catheter was placed before low-dose combined spinal epidural anaesthesia with isobaric bupivacaine 0.5% 6 mg (1.2 mL) administered intrathecally. Norepinephrine was infused at 0.02 μg/kg/min. Haemodynamics remained stable at baseline and oxygenation did not deteriorate below preprocedural levels; crystalloid administration was 100 mL and blood loss 10 mL. Intensive care unit monitoring continued through postoperative day 1, and she was discharged on day 2. The approach was feasible and well tolerated in this patient.

title: Segmental aortic energy loss in patients with bicuspid aortic valve.
authorString: Harada M, Skarlatoudi M, Shehu N, Stern H, Ewert P, Meierhofer C.

journal.title: International journal of cardiology. Heart & vasculature

abstractText:
Background

Altered aortic flow dynamics are observed in patients with bicuspid aortic valve (BAV), but their local energetic characteristics remain incompletely understood. The primary objective was to compare total and segmental energy loss (EL) between patients with BAV without significant valve dysfunction and matched controls. The subsequent clinical and structural course of the BAV cohort was described.

Methods

Sixteen patients with BAV and 16 matched controls underwent baseline four-dimensional flow cardiovascular magnetic resonance. Total and segmental aortic EL were quantified and normalized to flow. Commissural orientation was assessed. Clinical follow-up was available in all 16 patients with BAV, and paired baseline and approximately 10-year CMR assessments of aortic dimensions were available in 14.

Results

Mean flow-normalized EL was approximately twofold higher in patients with BAV from the sinus of Valsalva to proximal ascending aorta (0.78 [0.59-1.14] vs 0.40 [0.29-0.67] mW/[L/min]; P = 0.015) and from proximal to distal ascending aorta (1.26 [0.79-1.59] vs 0.64 [0.39-1.07] mW/[L/min]; P = 0.013). Commissural angle was not significantly associated with segmental EL. No major BAV-related cardiovascular complications occurred during follow-up. In paired examinations, maximum ascending aortic diameter increased from 3.40 ± 0.67 to 3.75 ± 0.67 cm (P < 0.001), whereas the body surface area-indexed increase was attenuated (1.88 ± 0.29 to 1.97 ± 0.33 cm/m2; P = 0.056).

Conclusions

Segmental aortic EL was increased in patients with BAV despite the absence of significant valve dysfunction. The approximately 10-year follow-up provides descriptive clinical and structural characterization but does not establish a relationship between baseline EL and subsequent outcomes.

title: Simple Adiposity Measures Discriminate MASLD by Transient Elastography in People With HIV: Results From a US Multicenter Cohort.
authorString: Wegermann K, Wilson LA, Vilar Gomez E, Crandall H, Price JC, Sterling RK, Heath SL, Sulkowski M, Loomba R, Naggie S, Chalasani N, Lake JE.
abstractText:
Background

Forty percent of people with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) (PWH) have metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), but simple clinical tools for risk stratification do not exist. We evaluated whether adiposity indices are associated with MASLD in PWH and whether performance varies by race or ethnicity.

Method

We examined PWH from a prospective, cross-sectional study conducted by the NIDDK-funded HIV NASH CRN. Participants had suppressed HIV-1 RNA and underwent vibration controlled transient elastography and anthropometric measurements. The primary outcome was MASLD, defined as controlled attenuation parameter (CAP) ≥263 dB/m with ≥1 cardiometabolic risk factor without heavy alcohol use or viral hepatitis. Adiposity indices included waist circumference (WC), body mass index (BMI), waist-to-height ratio (WHtR), body roundness index (BRI), relative fat mass (RFM), visceral adiposity index, and waist-to-hip ratio.

Results

Among 990 PWH, 445 (44.9%) had MASLD. All adiposity indices were strongly associated with MASLD (P < .001). Several adiposity indices had good discrimination for MASLD in the overall cohort, including WC (area under the receiver operating curve 0.79, 95% CI .76-.81), WHtR (0.77 [.74-.80]), BRI (0.77 [.74-.80]), and BMI (0.75 [.72-.78]). WC, RFM, WHtR, and BRI had significant interactions with race (interaction P < .05). Adiposity indices overall performed better in Black and Hispanic PWH compared to White PWH.

Conclusions

In PWH, adiposity indices were strongly associated with MASLD, though their discriminatory ability varied by race and ethnicity. Simple anthropometric indices may provide practical tools for MASLD risk assessment that could be tailored by race and ethnicity.

title: Diagnostic yield of genetic testing in heart transplant recipients with non-ischemic cardiomyopathy: A single-center cohort study
authorString: Bertelli M, Shokravi A, Christian S, Mahon N, Archer L, Fine N, Howlett J, Lyons K, Ballantyne B, Sharma N, Marcadier J, McBride K, Harper L, Miller R, Kiamanesh O.

title: Challenges in left bundle branch area pacing in children and congenital heart disease: technical limitations, diagnostic pitfalls, and physiologic insights.
authorString: Leung HT, Tsao S, Tam TK, Cheng YW, Kwok SY.
abstractText:
Aims

Left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) in children is complicated by small cardiac dimensions, congenital heart disease (CHD), and the uncertain applicability of adult diagnostic criteria. This study evaluated paediatric LBBAP procedural success, technical adaptations, and diagnostic challenges.

Methods and results

Retrospective analysis of consecutive patients ≤ 18 years of age undergoing attempted LBBAP between January 2021 and June 2025. Sixteen patients (median 13.3 years) were included; three of them had CHD. Transoesophageal echocardiogram (TEE) was used to guide most procedures (15 out of 16). In structurally normal hearts, LBBAP success was 61.5%, correlating with older age (P = 0.048). Standard adult-configured sheaths caused oblique septal trajectories; conversely, atrial-septal-oriented sheaths (C315-S4/S5) ensured perpendicular fixation, enabling success in children weighing as little as 20.2 kg. Final V6 R-wave peak time (V6RWPT) < 75 ms had a poor specificity (11%) in confirming left bundle branch capture, with 53.8% of the patients met this threshold during right ventricular septal pacing. Similarly, the adult V6-V1 interpeak interval criterion (>44 ms) yielded a suboptimal overall diagnostic accuracy of 37.5%. Successful LBBAP was associated with reduced left ventricular end-diastolic dimension Z-scores (P = 0.045) and septal-to-posterior wall motion delay (P = 0.048). In CHD cases, scarring and cardiac rotation rendered standard electrical criteria non-diagnostic; however, TEE-guided left ventricular subendocardial placement maintained stable pacing and preserved synchrony.

Conclusion

Paediatric LBBAP requires adapted delivery sheaths to overcome geometric mismatches. Adult electrocardiographic criteria, including V6RWPT and V6-V1 interpeak difference, lack accuracy to define LBB capture in children. Clinically, LBBAP effectively improves left ventricular dyssynchrony.

title: National Mortality Patterns of Congenital Anomalies Among Children in Saudi Arabia.
authorString: Alnuwaysir N, Alturki H, Dabbour J.
abstractText:
Background

Congenital anomalies (CAs) remain a major contributor to child mortality worldwide, yet national mortality pattern data from Saudi Arabia remains limited. This study aimed to describe national mortality patterns of eleven CA categories among children aged 0-14 years in Saudi Arabia (2021-2023).

Methods

A descriptive cross-sectional analysis of aggregated mortality data was conducted using nationally reported mortality data from the WHO Mortality Database. Eleven CA categories classified under ICD-10 (Q00-Q99) were analyzed. Mortality counts, relative contributions, cause-specific mortality fractions (CSMF), age-specific distributions and sex differences were summarized.

Results

A total of 4218 deaths attributable to CAs were recorded during 2021-2023, with higher mortality counts in 2023 (1821) than in 2021 (947). Congenital heart anomalies (CHDs) remained one of the leading causes across all years, accounting for 553, 773, and 775 deaths in 2021, 2022, and 2023, respectively. Overall, CHDs accounted for the largest mortality burden (49.81%, n = 2,101), followed by "other congenital anomalies" (42.67%, n = 1,800) and Down syndrome (3.82%, n = 161). Mortality was heavily concentrated in infants aged < 1 year, representing 3256 deaths (77.2%) of all deaths. CHDs consistently showed high infant mortality, reaching a peak infant CSMF of 15.78% in 2022. A slight male predominance was observed overall (53.1% males vs. 46.9% females; M/F ratio 1.13).

Conclusion

National mortality counts were higher in 2023 than in 2021, with most deaths occurring among infants and congenital heart anomalies accounting for the largest proportion of mortality, highlighting the need for continued national surveillance and further.

title: Primary Treatment of Congenital Aortic Stenosis in Infants: A Comparative Analysis of Balloon Aortic Valvuloplasty and Surgical Aortic Commissurotomy.
authorString: Ravshanovich KA, Semenovich SY, Nazarovna AE, Aleksandrovich NK, Vladimirovich RE, Nersesovich MS, Aleksandrovich SI.

journal.title: Journal of the Saudi Heart Association

abstractText:
Objective

To compare the efficacy and safety of balloon aortic valvuloplasty (BAV) and surgical aortic commissurotomy (SAC) as primary treatment strategies for congenital aortic stenosis in infants during the first year of life.

Methods

This retrospective two-center cohort study included 89 infants with congenital aortic stenosis treated between April 2015 and June 2025 at two tertiary centers. Patients were divided according to the initial intervention: BAV (n = 39) and SAC (n = 50). The primary endpoint was any repeat intervention on the aortic valve. Secondary endpoints included hospital and late mortality, recurrent hemodynamically significant aortic stenosis, and clinically significant aortic regurgitation. To reduce treatment-selection bias, propensity score matching (PSM) was performed using age, sex, body weight, body surface area, and distal aortic arch Z-score, yielding 33 matched pairs. Time-to-event outcomes were analyzed using Kaplan-Meier curves and compared with the log-rank test. Cox regression analysis was used to identify risk factors for reintervention.

Results

In the matched cohort, both strategies achieved initial technical success with no in-hospital deaths in either group. SAC provided superior early hemodynamic relief, with lower intraoperative peak gradient (21.0 [13.0-31.0] vs 30.0 [20.0-41.0] mm Hg; p = 0.048), lower intraoperative mean gradient (10.5 [8.0-14.0] vs 20.0 [12.0-25.0] mm Hg; p = 0.005), and lower discharge peak and mean gradients (25.0 [18.0-35.0] vs 39.0 [32.0-50.0] mm Hg, p < 0.001; and 15.0 [11.0-22.0] vs 24.0 [15.0-27.0] mm Hg, p = 0.023, respectively). However, SAC was associated with longer procedural duration, longer mechanical ventilation, longer intensive care and hospital stay, and greater need for inotropic support. During follow-up, severe aortic regurgitation developed significantly more often after BAV than after SAC (18.7% vs 0%; p = 0.012). Although the rates of reintervention and restenosis did not differ significantly in the matched cohort, Kaplan-Meier analysis showed superior freedom from reintervention after SAC at 45 months (30.5% [95% CI, 15.6%-46.9%] vs 12.3% [95% CI, 2.8%-29.3%]; log-rank p < 0.001). Freedom from restenosis was also higher after SAC (30.5% [95% CI, 15.6%-46.9%] vs 15.4% [95% CI, 3.4%-35.4%]; log-rank p = 0.039). Low body weight at the time of the initial procedure was the only independent predictor of reintervention.

Conclusion

In this retrospective matched cohort of infants with congenital aortic stenosis, SAC was associated with lower early residual transvalvular gradients and fewer observed cases of severe AR, but required a more invasive procedure and longer postoperative recovery. BAV provided faster recovery and remains an important option, particularly in critically ill or low-weight infants.

title: From fetus to mother: fetal identification of cardiospondylocarpofacial syndrome leading to maternal diagnosis-a case report.
authorString: Sienczyk J, Rzucidło-Szymańska I, Szymecka-Samaha N, Kosińska-Kaczyńska K, Brawura-Biskupski-Samaha R.
abstractText:
Background

Cardiospondylocarpofacial syndrome is a rare genetic disorder associated with multisystem anomalies and fetal growth restriction. Prenatal diagnosis is uncommon, with only 1 case reported to date. This case report aims to add to the prenatal as well as postnatal phenotypic features of cardiospondylocarpofacialsyndrome and highlight characteristics that may facilitate earlier recognition and diagnosis.

Case presentation

This is a case of a 29-year-old woman and her 6 pregnancies with 2 live births. Prenatal diagnostic testing in 1 of her pregnancies identified a pathogenic variant in the mitogen-activated protein kinase 7 gene. This finding subsequently enabled the identification of the same pathogenic variant in the mother. We present the clinical manifestations of the multiple comorbidities of the patient as well as the ultrasound findings of the fetuses with mitogen-activated protein kinase 7 mutation and their neonatal outcomes. Prenatal evaluation of the fetuses revealed fetal growth restriction, craniosynostosis, hypospadias sine hypospadia, and congenital heart defects. The mother suffered from arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy with left ventricular damage, chronic kidney disease because of focal segmental glomerulosclerosis after tuberculosis of the kidneys and digestive tract, scoliosis, short stature (153 cm), facial dysmorphia, and otosclerosis with hearing loss.

Conclusion

This case expands the known prenatal phenotypic spectrum of cardiospondylocarpofacialsyndrome syndrome and underscores the importance of integrating advanced molecular diagnostics with detailed fetal imaging in evaluating ultrasound-detected anomalies.

Modified Frozen Elephant Trunk Repair for Aortic Coarctation with Segmental Post-stenotic Aneurysms.
authorString: Dat PQ, Hoang MNT, Van Phuc D, Do TD, Long NP.

journal.title: Journal of the Saudi Heart Association

abstractText: Aortic coarctation can be complicated by descending thoracic aortic aneurysms in adults. A 31-year-old man presented with exertional chest pain radiating to the back. Preoperative evaluation showed a 27-mmHg arm-leg systolic pressure gradient, echocardiographic coarctation with a 10-mm narrowest diameter and 25-mmHg gradient, and computed tomography showing two segmental post-stenotic aneurysms, the largest measuring 62 mm. He underwent one-stage modified frozen elephant trunk repair using a Medtronic thoracic stent graft sutured to a surgical graft. The postoperative gradient decreased to 5 mmHg, with stable 9-month follow-up.

title: The effects of different prone positioning angles on cardiopulmonary function in children after congenital heart disease surgery: a randomized controlled trial.
authorString: Huang X, Han J, Wang Y, Huang J, Hou Z, Wang S, Qiu H, Jing X, Yan F.
abstractText:
Objective

To evaluate the effects of different head-elevated prone positioning angles on oxygenation, respiratory mechanics, hemodynamics, and enteral nutrition tolerance in children after congenital heart disease（CHD）surgery, and to determine the optimal intervention angle.

Methods

In this randomized controlled trial, 102 mechanically ventilated children after congenital heart disease surgery were randomly assigned to the 10°, 30°, or 45° group. 98 completed the protocol and were analyzed. All patients received standardized prone positioning for at least 12 hours per day. The primary outcome was the PaO₂/FiO₂ ratio and respiratory mechanics (lung compliance, airway resistance, and respiratory rate). Secondary outcomes included gastric residual volume, hemodynamic parameters, and complications. Repeated outcomes were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models, whereas change scores were compared using one-way ANOVA or Kruskal-Wallis tests, as appropriate. This trial was retrospectively registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT07323979) on 24/12/2025 after study completion.

Results

Oxygenation improved over time in all three groups. The 10° group showed the greatest early improvement in oxygenation, the 30° group demonstrated the most favorable overall performance in lung compliance, airway resistance, and respiratory rate, and the 45° group showed the greatest reduction in gastric residual volume but more pressure-injury events were observed. Overall, the findings suggest different benefit-risk profiles across the three evaluated angles, with the 30° position representing a reasonable option when respiratory mechanics, enteral nutrition tolerance, and safety are considered together.

Conclusion

Considering pulmonary function, enteral nutrition tolerance, and safety, the 30° head-elevated prone position may be considered a reasonable intervention angle for children after CHD surgery.

Implications for clinical practice

In clinical practice, a 30° head-elevated prone position may offer a balanced postoperative strategy for mechanically ventilated children after congenital heart disease surgery by improving respiratory mechanics, supporting enteral feeding tolerance, and helping standardize nurse-led prone positioning practice in the CICU to support safer early postoperative recovery.

title: Incremental prognostic value of inflammatory biomarkers for 28-day mortality in patients with sepsis presenting to the emergency department: a retrospective 24-hour landmark cohort study.
authorString: Wang P, Tan G, Xu N, Xi C, Jing Y, Tang F, Li R, Xu J, Xia H.
abstractText:
Background

Inflammatory biomarkers are associated with outcomes in sepsis, but prognostic association does not necessarily imply additional predictive information beyond clinical severity. We evaluated the incremental prognostic value of procalcitonin (PCT), the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), and the monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio (MLR) at a 24-hour landmark.

Methods

This single-center retrospective cohort included 248 adults admitted through the emergency department with sepsis between January 2024 and April 2026. The primary analysis included 243 patients alive 24 h after arrival and used 50 multiply imputed datasets. Fixed-horizon logistic models compared a clinical base model comprising sex, albumin, lactate, and APACHE II with models that added continuous PCT alone or PCT, NLR, and MLR together. Internal validation used ordinary bootstrap optimism correction with 1000 patient-level resamples and multiple imputation nested within resampling; within each resample, separate MICE runs completed the incomplete bootstrap sample and the original cohort used to evaluate the bootstrap-fitted models (five imputations each). A 0-3-point equal-weight inflammatory score based on within-cohort Youden cut-offs was examined as a secondary exploratory analysis.

Results

Forty-six patients in the landmark cohort died by day 28. Exploratory pooled comparisons did not provide evidence that adding PCT improved the clinical base model (P = 0.775) or that adding PCT, NLR, and MLR together improved it (P = 0.428). The odds ratios per doubling were 0.943 (95% CI 0.817-1.089) for PCT, 1.350 (0.937-1.943) for NLR, and 0.866 (0.681-1.101) for MLR. Optimism-corrected AUCs were 0.749, 0.743, and 0.728 for M0, M1, and M2, respectively. The corrected AUC difference between M2 and M0 was -0.022 (95% CI -0.030 to 0.023). The apparent association of the fixed-cut-off score was no longer supported after repeating the complete cut-off search procedure (selection-adjusted P = 0.295). A first-laboratory sensitivity analysis retaining all 248 patients and 51 deaths yielded a similar pattern (exploratory pooled P = 0.951).

Conclusions

PCT, NLR, and MLR did not provide evidence of incremental predictive value in this exploratory single-center cohort. The within-cohort equal-weight inflammatory score was subject to substantial cut-off selection uncertainty and remains exploratory. Neither the model nor the score should guide clinical decisions before independent evaluation.

title: The Effectiveness of Parent Educational Program on Knowledge and Caregiving Performance for Children With Congenital Heart Disease: A Randomized Clinical Trial Study.
authorString: Hakim A, Hosseini N, Behbahani SR, Haghighizadeh MH.
abstractText:
Background

Congenital heart disease is the most common type of congenital defect.

Objectives

This research was conducted with the aim of the effectiveness of parent educational Program on knowledge and caregiving performance for children with congenital heart disease.

Design

This clinical trial study was conducted on 86 parents who have children with congenital heart disease. The samples were randomly divided into two intervention (43 people) and control (43 people) groups using a permutation block design.

Methods

The data were collected using a demographic information questionnaire, a knowledge assessment questionnaire, and a caregiving performance assessment questionnaire. The collected data were analyzed with SPSS22 software and using paired t-test, independent t-test, chi-square, and covariance analysis.

Results

The findings of the research indicated that after teaching the intervention group, the average parents care knowledge increased significantly compared to the control group (P < 0.001). Also, there was a statistically significant difference between the average parent Caregiving performance in the intervention group compared to the control group (P < 0.001).

Conclusion

Based on the results of this study, the implementation of the educational program is a suitable method to increase the level of knowledge and parent Caregiving performance for children with congenital heart disease.

title: Development and validation of a machine learning model for heart failure in older patients with atrial fibrillation.
authorString: Chen W, Wu Y, Yao Z, Wu J, Gao H.
abstractText:
Objective

This study aimed to develop and internally evaluate a machine learning (ML) model based on real-world data for identifying clinically adjudicated heart failure (HF) during hospitalisation in older patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) and to compare various models for such an assessment approach.

Methods

Older patients with AF who were admitted to the General Hospital of Ningxia Medical University between 2023 and 2024 were included. Demographic characteristics, vital signs, comorbidities, medication use, and routine laboratory measurements were extracted from electronic medical records. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression was used to select candidate predictors, after which five ML models were developed and compared. Separate, non-overlapping training and test sets were used for model development and evaluation. Model performance was assessed in terms of discrimination, calibration, potential clinical net benefit, and interpretability.

Results

This study included 1,989 patients, 11% of whom experienced HF during hospitalisation. Through LASSO regression, 16 key variables were identified, including age, vital signs, comorbidities, and multiple hematologic indicators. Among the five models, XGBoost performed the best on the test set (AUROC 0.737), exhibiting balanced accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity without marked overfitting. The calibration curve demonstrated strong concordance between model predictions and actual risks. The decision curve analysis (DCA) demonstrated high net benefit within the 5%-40% threshold range. SHAP analysis identified age, RDW series indicators, anemia indicators, and infection-related variables as the most significant features, aligning with the pathophysiology of HF.

Conclusion

The XGBoost model for identifying clinically adjudicated HF among hospitalised older patients with AF showed moderate discriminatory ability, calibration, and exploratory findings from decision curve analysis, as well as high interpretability. This model may serve as an exploratory admission-based assessment approach for identifying patients who meet the prespecified criteria for HF during hospitalisation. Prospective external validation is required before its potential clinical application can be determined.

title: Knockdown of TRIM47 Attenuates Pressure Overload-Induced Heart Failure by Inhibiting NLRP3 Inflammasome Activation.
authorString: Li J, Bao L, Liu Z, Zhang J, Zhang Y, Sun X, Sun B.
abstractText:
Background

The ubiquitinated protein TRIM47 participates in the inflammatory regulation of various organ injuries, but its role in pressure overload-induced heart failure remains unclear.

Objective

The aim of this study is to investigate the protective effect of TRIM47 knockdown against pressure overload-induced myocardial injury.

Methods

A TAC mouse model of heart failure was established, and myocardial TRIM47 knockdown was achieved through targeted cardiac injection of AAV-sh-TRIM47. Heart weight/body weight ratio (HW/BW) and heart weight/tibia length ratio (HW/TL) were measured, and ANP/BNP mRNA levels were used to assess myocardial injury. HE and WGA staining were used to observe cardiomyocyte hypertrophy; Masson and Sirius red staining were used to detect myocardial fibrosis; TUNEL staining and apoptosis-related protein analysis were used to detect cardiomyocyte apoptosis; and Western blotting was used to detect the expression levels of key molecules in the NLRP3 inflammasome.

Results

TRIM47 was highly expressed in the left ventricle of mice with heart failure. In the TAC group, mice showed increased HW/BW and HW/TL ratios, as well as elevated ANP and BNP mRNA levels. Cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, disordered myofiber arrangement, increased collagen deposition and expression of fibrosis-related proteins, and myocardial apoptosis were observed. Increased expression of inflammasome activation-related proteins, including NLRP3, cleaved caspase-1, mature IL-1β, and IL-18 was also observed. Knockdown of TRIM47 reversed these pathological changes.

Conclusion

TRIM47 is abnormally upregulated in the myocardium in pressure overload-induced heart failure. TRIM47 knockdown alleviates TAC-induced heart failure by inhibiting myocardial hypertrophy, fibrosis, apoptosis, and NLRP3 inflammasome activation.

title: Demographic, clinical and echocardiographic profile of adult patients with congenital heart disease at a leading cardiovascular healthcare facility of Pakistan: A descriptive cross-sectional study.
authorString: Ahsan AK, Shaikh AS, Khokhar RA, Alisher N, Ayyaz M, Mohsin M.
abstractText:
Objective

To assess the demographic, clinical, and echocardiographic characteristics of adults with congenital heart disease (CHD).

Methods

A descriptive cross-sectional study was performed at the department of pediatric cardiology, National Institute of Cardiovascular Diseases (NICVD), Karachi, Pakistan, from November 2022 to October 2023. Inclusion criteria were adult patients (≥18 years of age) diagnosed with CHDs (both already diagnosed and newly diagnosed).

Results

Of 184 patients, 100 (54.3%) were male. Mean age and BMI were 25.66 ± 9.19 years and 17.75 ± 4.32 kg/m2. Seventeen (9.2%) adult CHD patients were newly diagnosed. Shortness of breath, cyanosis, palpitation, and chest pain, were reported in 158 (85.9%), 65 (35.3%), 52 (28.3%), and 51 (27.7%) patients. Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF), atrial septal defect (ASD), ventricular septal defect (VSD), and patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) were the most common CHD types, noted in 46 (25.0%), 35 (19.0%), 32 (17.4%), and 12 (6.5%) patients respectively. ASD was significantly more prevalent in females than in males (82.9% vs. 17.1%, p < .001), and it was significantly more frequent in 18-30 age group (p < .001). TOF was more common in 18-30 age group (p = .013). VSD was significantly more prevalent in males (p = .028).

Conclusions

TOF, ASD, VSD, and PDA were the most frequent types of adult CHDs. Notably, 9.2% of patients were newly diagnosed, suggesting potential underdiagnosis or late detection. With a substantial portion of the population experiencing CHD-related symptoms with some diagnosed only in adulthood, demand for dedicated centers equipped with expertise in managing adult CHD becomes evident.

title: Neonatal Hypernatremic Dehydration Presenting as Fever Without a Source: A Case Report.
authorString: Madaeng T, Bongkotwilawan N, Ruangkit C, Soonsawad S, Chongthavornvasana S.
abstractText: Diagnosis of neonatal hypernatremic dehydration can be challenging, as it may present with nonspecific clinical symptoms such as fever and irritability, and a history of poor feeding may be absent. A high index of suspicion from physicians is therefore required. Our report describes a 5-day-old female neonate who presented with acute febrile illness and presumptive compensated shock, along with hypernatremia and multiple electrolyte derangements. Her parents reported normal feeding and voiding history. However, even a seemingly reassuring history can be misleading, underscoring the importance of detailed history taking.

title: Barriers to advancement in academic medicine among women selected to participate in leadership training.
authorString: Singer K, Wruble L, Pasquali SK.
abstractText:
Background

While the representation of women in medicine has increased in recent years, advancement into leadership roles lags behind. Solutions often focus on providing women with leadership training, yet the experience of participants in such programs and ongoing barriers remain understudied.

Methods

All women selected to participate in an 18-month institutional leadership program in medicine launched in 2014 and designed to support advancement to senior leadership roles were invited to complete an electronic survey regarding current barriers. Descriptive results from structured survey questions and free-text options are reported.

Results

Of 114 participants, 67 responded (59%). Most (79%) were 15+ years from training and held a variety of mid-level leadership roles. Less than half reported that institutional leaders had proactively discussed advancement and future opportunities with them, including chairs (40%), divisional leadership (26%), hospital leaders (15%), and the dean's office (15%). Nearly half (45%) had never applied for a higher-level leadership position. Of those who were offered such a role 56% turned it down, most often due to insufficient resources/compensation. Overall, the most common barriers to advancement reported were lack of sponsorship (67%) and mentorship (48%), implicit (61%) or overt (39%) bias, and a pre-determined candidate in mind (56%), with 48% also reporting challenges with personal/family responsibilities. Free-text responses highlighted similar themes to the quantitative data.

Conclusions

This study of a unique cohort of mid-career women leaders suggests additional efforts beyond leadership training alone are needed to advance women in medicine to senior leadership roles. Our findings highlight current barriers and opportunities for future efforts focused on the organizational culture women are navigating including support for sponsorship and mentorship, addressing biases, and succession planning models.

title: Long-term durability of surgical and transcatheter bioprosthetic pulmonary valves: BPV durability: time to dysfunction and failure.
authorString: Ramaki S, Gröning M, Jørgensen TH, Nielsen DG, Nissen H, Jensen AS, Schmidt MR.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Eur Heart J Valvular Struct Heart Dis
journal.title: European heart journal. Valvular and structural heart disease
journal.isoabbreviation: Eur Heart J Valvular Struct Heart Dis

abstractText:
Background and aims

Pulmonary valve replacements (PVR) with bioprosthetic pulmonary valves (BPV) increases. This study aimed to assess BPV durability as time to dysfunction and failure, risk factors for reduced durability, and impact on mortality.

Methods and results

Data from a Danish nationwide cohort who underwent surgical or transcatheter PVR with a BPV between 1976 and 2021 were obtained. Bioprosthetic valve dysfunction was categorized into (i) structural valve deterioration (SVD) as moderate [pulmonary stenosis (PS) with peak velocity >3 m/s = PG ≥ 36 mm Hg or >mild pulmonary regurgitation] or severe (>4 m/s = PG ≥ 64 mm Hg or severe regurgitation), (ii) patient-prosthesis mismatch (PPM) (PG ≥ 20 mm Hg on the last echocardiography ≤90 days), and (iii) infective endocarditis (IE). Bioprosthetic valve failure (BVF) was defined as redo PVR. 680 PVRs were performed in 439 patients. Median follow-up was 14 years [Inter-quartile range (IQR): 8-21]. Median time to moderate SVD was 6 years (IQR: 1-17), to severe SVD 21 years (IQR: 17-NA), and to BVF 17 years (IQR: 15-18). PPM occurred in 41%. Cumulative incidence of IE was 17% after 25 years. PS was the leading cause of moderate (62%) and severe SVD (54%), then regurgitation (32% and 43%) and combined disease (6% and 3%). Younger age at PVR and PPM was associated with increased risk of SVD and BVF, while PPM and redo-interventions increased risk of IE. SVD was not associated with mortality (P = .08 for moderate, P = .56 for severe SVD).

Conclusions

Moderate dysfunction occurred early after PVR, but takes years to progress to severe dysfunction or failure. Younger age and PPM increased SVD and BVF risk. PPM and redo-interventions increased IE risk. SVD was not associated with mortality.

title: META ANALYSIS OF THE APPLICATION EFFECT OF POSTOPERATIVE PSYCHOLOGICAL NURSING EVALUATION TOOLS FOR CHILDREN WITH CONGENITAL HEART DISEASE
Beyond just survival: updates on adult congenital heart disease care.
authorString: Cao JY, Baker D, Cordina R, Celermajer D.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Eur Heart J Valvular Struct Heart Dis
journal.title: European heart journal. Valvular and structural heart disease
journal.isoabbreviation: Eur Heart J Valvular Struct Heart Dis

abstractText: Survival into adulthood is now the norm for individuals born with congenital heart disease, with over 90% of children reaching adult life. Yet for many, particularly those with complex lesions, childhood intervention does not equate to a cure. Adults with congenital heart disease (ACHD) face ongoing risks of haemodynamic complications, end-organ dysfunction, and premature morbidity. In this review, we present recent advances in ACHD care across five domains: lifelong care models, diagnostic techniques, management strategies, genetic and precision medicine, and machine learning. We highlight the pivotal role of specialized, multidisciplinary care in improving outcomes, and the need for structured transition programmes to ensure continuity from paediatric to adult services. Emerging priorities include reproductive counselling, exercise prescription, and psychosocial support. Advances in cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging, electrophysiological mapping, and four-dimensional flow imaging now offer unprecedented anatomical and haemodynamic insights. Recent trials have demonstrated encouraging results for novel heart failure therapies and pulmonary vasodilators in lesion-specific subgroups, while transcatheter technologies continue to expand therapeutic options for patients with complex anatomy. Genetic testing and machine learning are beginning to reshape risk stratification and workflow efficiency, though challenges remain in their implementation. As this population ages and acquires new comorbidities, care models must evolve to move beyond just survival, but towards improving quality of life, preserving organ function, and anticipating future needs. This review aims to support clinicians and researchers in meeting these challenges and advancing the next era of ACHD care.

title: Management of bicuspid aortic stenosis.
authorString: Samim D, Siepe M, Çelik M, De Backer O, Borger MA, Windecker S.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Eur Heart J Valvular Struct Heart Dis
journal.title: European heart journal. Valvular and structural heart disease
journal.isoabbreviation: Eur Heart J Valvular Struct Heart Dis

abstractText:
Aims

Bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) disease is the most common congenital heart lesion and is associated with premature leaflet degeneration, aortic stenosis (AS), aortic regurgitation (AR), endocarditis, and ascending aortic pathologies. This review aims to summarize the key issues frequently associated with BAV and their impact on treatment decision-making, with a particular focus on surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) versus transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) in patients presenting with AS.

Methods and results

Patients with BAV experience a 70% lifetime risk of aortic valve surgery, often at a younger age than those with a trileaflet anatomy. BAV is present in up to 40% of patients undergoing SAVR, which remains the standard of care in low-risk patients. TAVI has emerged as a less invasive treatment alternative with favorable short- and mid-term outcomes in appropriately selected BAV patients. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing TAVI and SAVR have systematically excluded BAV patients, except for the UK TAVI trial and recent NOTION-2 trial, the latter signalling a potentially increased risk of all-cause mortality, stroke, and re-hospitalization rates at 1 year among low-risk BAV patients undergoing TAVI. Dedicated RCTs comparing TAVI and SAVR for BAV stenosis are in preparation and will inform future guidelines.

Conclusion

Treatment decisions for BAV patients should be individualized by Heart Teams, considering periprocedural risk, comorbidities, aortic root anatomy, and life expectancy. Future trials in this specific population will clarify the optimal role of TAVI and SAVR in managing BAV-related aortic stenosis.

title: Artificial intelligence in valvular heart disease: current evidence and future perspectives.
authorString: Theriault-Lauzier P, Suc G, Sengupta PP, Avram R, Bruce C, Bohbot Y, Ben Ali W, Dreyfus J, Piazza N, Burwash IG, Enriquez-Sarano M, Modine T, Messika-Zeitoun D.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Eur Heart J Valvular Struct Heart Dis
journal.title: European heart journal. Valvular and structural heart disease
journal.isoabbreviation: Eur Heart J Valvular Struct Heart Dis

abstractText: Valvular heart disease (VHD) is emerging as the next major epidemic in cardiovascular care, driven by the ageing population. The advent of less invasive alternatives to surgery-namely, transcatheter therapies-has revolutionized patient management, while simultaneously introducing new layers of complexity. Artificial intelligence (AI) holds significant promise to transform the care of patients with VHD across all dimensions, including diagnosis, prognostication, disease progression, and therapeutic decision-making. In this review, we provide a comprehensive overview of the current evidence, and discuss the challenges, risks, and future directions associated with the integration of AI in the management of VHD.

title: 2D and 3D iPSC-CM models for studying cardiac toxicity and disease.
authorString: Heathershaw CW, Shakeriastani K, Latham OL, Roddey JT, Maxwell JT.
abstractText: Advances in human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) technology have enabled the generation of robust, cardiac-specific, in vitro systems for cardiac disease modeling, drug screening, and cardiotoxicity studies. Human iPSCs can be differentiated into iPSC-derived cardiac myocytes (iPSC-CMs), a model cell population able to recapitulate the phenotypes of complex cardiac diseases-mirroring both the observations made with in vivo animal models and the clinical manifestations seen in human patients. To improve the physiological relevance of iPSC-CM model systems, researchers are shifting from 2D to 3D models and incorporating a variety of cardiac specific cell types including cardiac fibroblasts, and vascular endothelial cells. In this paper, we will review the development of 2D and 3D iPSC-CM models, survey the various disease contexts in which these models have been utilized, and discuss the benefits and limitations of each strategy.

title: Incessant Ventricular Tachycardia in Infant With Structurally Normal Heart: Is it Truly Benign or a Old Wives' Tale.
authorString: Mohsin M, Sangi R, Sheikh AS.
abstractText: Idiopathic ventricular tachycardia (VT) is a rare form of arrhythmia in neonates that can be life-threatening prompting its timely diagnosis and importance of treatment to avoid serious complications, that is; heart failure. We describe a neonate with an incessant idiopathic ventricular tachycardia presented with heart failure and severe left ventricular dysfunction. This infant presented with poor feeding, irritability, increase work of breathing, and heartbeat of 260/min. The electrocardiogram (ECG) showed wide complex tachycardia and the echocardiogram showed a structurally normal heart with dilated cardiomyopathy. The clinical signs and chest X-ray changes were consistent with cardiac failure but preserved peripheral perfusion. This presentation, the sustained VT and the global cardiac failure makes the treatment challenging; therefore, early diagnosis of incessant VT in neonate is important for better prognosis.

title: Towards Automated Initial Probe Placement in Transthoracic Teleultrasound Using Human Mesh and Skeleton Recovery
authorString: Lee YC, Black D, Yeung R, Salcudean S.
abstractText: Cardiac and lung ultrasound require operators to locate patient-specific intercostal acoustic windows and adjust probe position, rotation, and force to acquire standard views. In teleultrasound, experts may navigate using ultrasound images after approximate placement, but limited 3D perception makes remote guidance of initial placement difficult. We present tUS-PIPG, a framework for teleultrasound Patient registration and anatomy-informed Initial Probe placement Guidance. A novice captures calibrated RGB and depth images using a mixed reality headset. An edge server reconstructs the patient’s body surface and estimates skeletal landmarks from multiview RGB images and an accumulated depth point cloud. The method leverages spatial and temporal consistency across observations to achieve robust, training-free human registration. Skeletal landmarks guide estimation of intercostal regions, and the headset overlays virtual probe placement on the reconstructed body surface. We evaluated registration and placement guidance in a healthcare setting across multiple transthoracic cardiac and lung scan planes in situ. In a pilot study with five healthy volunteers, mean surface error was 15 mm, and mean error relative to palpated anatomical landmarks was 41.0 mm. These results suggest that the framework can effectively provide novice operators with a warm start in positioning the probe for remote expert adjustment.

title: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of SAM3 for Left Atrium Segmentation from MR Images for Improved Planning and Guidance of Cardiac Ablation Interventions
authorString: Kundu B, Poudel N, Simon R, Linte C.
abstractText: Foundation models such as Segment Anything Model 3 (SAM3) have demonstrated strong generalization in natural images through prompt-driven segmentation. However, their applicability to medical imaging remains unclear due to the domain-specific visual characteristics and task requirements. In this work, we investigate the domain adaptability of SAM3 for left atrium (LA) segmentation from cardiac MRI, a challenging, yet clinically critical task in the context of image-guided cardiac interventions, specifically aimed at improving planning and guidance of catheter-based cardiac ablation therapy in arrhythmia patients. We first evaluate SAM3 in a zero-shot setting using text prompts and show that performance remains limited despite descriptive prompt formulations, highlighting a fundamental mismatch between semantic prompting and the visual cues required for medical image segmentation. To address this limitation, we study two parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) strategies, including LoRA and a prompt-free adapter-based framework. Our comprehensive experimental results demonstrate that LoRA achieves stronger performance (Dice 90.6% and 91.7%) over zero-shot baselines and cross-dataset generalization. LoRA leverages the semantic priors, while the adapter provides stable predictions with improved computational efficiency. In particular, adapter training reduces per-epoch training time by over 7× compared to LoRA, while maintaining comparable segmentation performance. These findings reveal a key trade-off between generalization and efficiency and show that semantic guidance from text prompts and feature-level adaptation to modality-specific visual cues offer two viable, complementary pathways for adapting SAM3 to cardiac MRI. Our code is available here.

title: Underrecognised legacies of preeclampsia: a biosocial DOHaD perspective for research in sub-Saharan Africa.
authorString: Penkler M, Conrad ML, Fahlbusch FB, Robb J, Ertl J, Lobmaier SM, Okan O, Adjei RO, Winkler AS, Priller J, Krudewig C, Klug SJ, Osmani V, Mall V, Steinert J, Struck N, Maiga-Acofaré O, Amuasi J, Gyanteh YO, Larbi A, Dassah ET, Müller R, Prazeres da Costa C.
abstractText: Preeclampsia is often approached as an acute obstetric complication, yet its longer-term implications for maternal and offspring health remain insufficiently understood, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA). Preeclampsia is a significant contributor to maternal and perinatal morbidity and mortality worldwide, with a disproportionate burden in SSA. Although its clinical management has improved, particularly in high-income countries, important questions remain regarding its causes, long-term consequences, and the extent to which existing evidence applies to SSA populations. In this viewpoint, we propose that conceptualising preeclampsia in SSA through a biosocial Developmental Origins of Health and Disease (DOHaD) lens provides a useful framework for investigating how biological, social, and environmental processes jointly shape maternal and offspring health across the life course. We review evidence and identify four priority domains for investigation: understanding context-specific causes and mechanisms; improving detection, care-seeking, and health system pathways; examining long-term maternal and offspring outcomes; and strengthening research infrastructures. We argue that advancing research on preeclampsia in SSA requires interdisciplinary approaches that integrate biological, clinical, epidemiological, and qualitative research. Such a research agenda has the potential to improve understanding of preeclampsia beyond its acute manifestations and to inform more equitable strategies for maternal and child health across the life course.

title: Automated aortoiliac calcification segmentation from arterial-phase computed tomography scans: development and validation
authorString: Liu BC, Fisher AT, Melbourne J, Fereydooni A, Berens P, Lakshmi A, Jensen ME, Rodriguez F, Chaudhari AS, Arya S.
abstractText:
Introduction

Arterial calcium is widely used as a biomarker for coronary artery disease but is underutilized in peripheral artery disease (PAD) due to challenges in automated measurement of peripheral vascular calcium. We developed a fully automated deep-learning pipeline for measurement of aortoiliac calcium from arterial-phase, contrast-enhanced abdominopelvic computed tomography angiography (CTA) to extract this important PAD biomarker.

Methods

The pipeline uses two nnU-Net models for aortoiliac arterial segmentation and identification of calcified voxels. We trained on 56 computed tomography (CT) scans and validated on 106 scans by comparing the pipeline’s calcium estimation from CTA against calcium burden on corresponding non-contrast phase CT within manually segmented arterial contours across a range of radiodensity thresholds (100–1000 Hounsfield units [HU]). Using the non-contrast HU threshold that maximized correlation between measures, we performed linear regression with five-fold cross-validation between pipeline-estimated and non-contrast calcium quantities, and risk reclassification analysis across quartiles using Monte Carlo simulations to compare pipeline and non-contrast-derived calcium burden quartiles while measuring quadratically weighted kappa.

Results

Non-contrast calcium burden calculated from voxels with attenuation ≥400 HU correlated best with CTA calcium burden (Pearson r=0.952 for aortic calcium; Pearson r=0.955 for iliofemoral calcium) and was used for subsequent analysis. Five-fold cross-validation of non-contrast calcium volume prediction from pipeline-estimated CTA calcium burden, using ≥400 HU to define non-contrast calcium voxels, demonstrated aggregated Pearson r>0.91 for all held-out folds in all three arterial regions tested. In risk reclassification analysis, quadratically weighted kappa for agreement between predicted and ground truth calcium quartile classifications was κ=0.88 for the aorta, κ=0.84 for bilateral iliofemoral arteries, and κ=0.80 for all regions.

Conclusion

Aortoiliac calcium burden can be accurately quantified from CTA with excellent reproducibility against calcium voxels ≥400 HU on non-contrast imaging. Quantification of this important biomarker expands opportunities for improved peripheral vascular disease diagnosis and risk prediction.
