title: Targeting the TWEAK-exosomal miR-7 axis attenuates pressure overload induced cardiac remodelling and fibrosis
authorString: Burman P, Bharati P, Khatoon A, Tripathi S, Tomar MS, Shrivastava A, Jagavelu k, Gupta SK, Hanif K, Moharana B.
abstractText:
Background:

Cardiac fibrosis contributes to the progression of pathological hypertrophy toward heart failure. However, the mechanisms underlying TWEAK-mediated cardiomyocyte-fibroblast crosstalk remain poorly understood. This study investigated the role of exosomal miR-7 in TWEAK-induced cardiac fibrotic remodeling.

Methods:

Cardiomyocytes were stimulated with recombinant TWEAK (200 ng/ml), and secreted exosomes were isolated and characterized. Exosomal uptake and profibrotic responses were evaluated in cardiac fibroblasts. The contribution of exosomal miR-7 was investigated using antagomiR-7 and GW4869-mediated inhibition of exosome secretion. Raf-1/AKT and TGF-β1/SMAD signaling were examined. Integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic profiling was performed using RNA sequencing and GC-MS. In vivo validation involved systemic administration of TWEAK-induced exosomes and pharmacological TWEAK inhibition using aurintricarboxylic acid (ATA) in a transverse aortic constriction (TAC) model.

Results:

Exosomes from TWEAK-stimulated cardiomyocytes were taken up by cardiac fibroblasts, enhancing migration and upregulating α-SMA and TGF-β1. TWEAK enriched miR-7 in these exosomes, raising miR-7 levels in recipient fibroblasts. Inhibiting miR-7 attenuated fibroblast activation, while blocking exosome secretion reduced miR-7 transfer and fibrotic responses. Mechanistically, miR-7 suppressed Raf-1/AKT signaling and enhanced TGF-β1/SMAD signaling. Multi-omics analyses revealed coordinated metabolic and transcriptomic remodeling, including altered energy metabolism, extracellular matrix pathways, and SMAD, PI3K, and hypoxia-related signaling. Systemic administration of miR-7-enriched exosomes exacerbated cardiac fibrosis in vivo, whereas ATA-mediated TWEAK inhibition in TAC reduced hypertrophy, fibrosis, and exosomal miR-7 levels.

Conclusion:

These findings establish a TWEAK-exosome-miR-7 axis as a mediator of cardiomyocyte-fibroblast crosstalk, identifying exosomal miR-7 as a key regulator of cardiac fibrotic remodeling and TWEAK as a potential therapeutic target.

title: The chloroplast CLP chaperone-protease system controls the steady-state abundance of the singlet oxygen sensors EXCUTER 1 and 2.
authorString: Ravenburg CM, Routray P, Bouchnak I, Yuan B, Julkowska MM, van Wijk KJ.
abstractText: The chloroplast Caseinolytic Protease (CLP) chaperone-protease is essential for chloroplast biogenesis. CLP substrate selection is aided by the N-recognin CLPS1 and CLPF adaptors. They interact with each other and the CLPC1 chaperone, but their specific functions are poorly understood. We employed in vivo CLPC1 substrate trapping in Arabidopsis by expressing a 35S:CLPC1-TRAP-STREPII transgene in wild-type (WT), clpf, clps1, and clpfclps1 to test the consequences of the loss of these adaptors on CLPC1-trapped proteins. Immunoblotting and protein half-life experiments were carried out for identified CLP substrates. Expression of the 35S:CLPC1-TRAP-STREPII in clps1cpf was embryo lethal. CLPF was trapped at a reduced level in clps1, supporting CLPS-CLPF interactions. Chloroplast 1O2 sensor EXECUTER1 (EX1) was trapped in WT and clps1 but not significantly in clpf. Steady-state protein accumulation of EX1 and its homolog EX2 increased 30-fold in the CLPC1-TRAP lines and clpr2-1, but not in clpf or clps1. In planta experiments showed that the half-life of EX1 is c. threefold longer in clpc1-1 than in WT, but EX1 half-life was unaffected in clpf. We conclude that the CLP system plays a key role in EX1,2 homeostasis by keeping their intra-chloroplast concentrations low through continuous degradation, upstream of their 1O2 signaling function.

title: Elevated blood lead levels among pregnant women in Amran, Yemen: Socio-demographic correlates and associations with a history of spontaneous abortion.
authorString: Qasem L, Al-Shami A, Yahya TAA, Al-Maktari LA, Al-Maqhafi M, Al-Marqasi A.
abstractText:
Background

Lead exposure in pregnant women is a critical public health concern, particularly in resource-limited settings where environmental regulations are less stringent. Prenatal lead exposure (Pb) is associated with various adverse maternal and fetal outcomes. Therefore, this study aimed to assess blood lead levels (BLLs) among pregnant women in Amran, Yemen, and to identify health risks associated with environmental, behavioral, and socio-demographic factors.

Methods

A cross-sectional multi-center study was conducted between August and November 2024, involving a sample of 150 pregnant women (aged 20-41 years) recruited across public and private healthcare facilities in Amran. Data were collected via structured questionnaires, and venous blood samples collected in K2 EDTA were analyzed using atomic absorption spectrophotometry (UNICAM 929AA). Statistical analysis was performed using SPSS version 24, with a significance threshold of P < 0.05.

Results

The results revealed a critically high prevalence of heavy metal exposure, with 82.7% of the sampled cohort exhibiting BLLs above 10 µg/dL. The median BLL of the sample was 40.8 µg/dL (IQR: 19.0-62.0), ranging from 1.0 to 143.0 µg/dL. Multivariable logistic regression identified a history of spontaneous abortion as a significant independent factor strongly associated with elevated BLLs (AOR = 5.88, 95% CI: 1.66-20.89, p = 0.006). Notably, the wide confidence interval indicates statistical imprecision due to limited reference cell counts. Elevated blood lead levels were positively, but non-significantly, associated with residential proximity to petrol stations and battery recycling sites, para-occupational exposure, and current smoking. Conversely, maternal age, formal education level, and housing type showed no significant independent association with lead levels.

Conclusion

This study identifies a severe public health crisis in Amran, highlighting the need for immediate investigations to identify sources of lead exposure, strengthened environmental regulation, and the integration of routine blood lead level screening into antenatal care. Such measures could help identify women with critically elevated BLLs who require close monitoring and follow-up.

title: Analysis of adverse reactions to low-dose dexamethasone in bronchopulmonary dysplasia of extremely premature infants: a retrospective study.
authorString: Zhuang G, Xie X, Chen J.
abstractText:
Background

Bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) represents a prevalent complication among extremely premature infants. Nonetheless, the optimal dosage, treatment duration, and safety profile of dexamethasone require further validation through clinical research. This study investigates the efficacy and safety of low-dose dexamethasone intervention for BPD in extremely preterm infants and establishes an evidence-based foundation for monitoring adverse drug reactions within this population.

Methods

A retrospective analysis was conducted on 68 cases of extremely preterm infants between March 2016 and January 2024. Among them, 41 cases received dexamethasone treatment (dexamethasone group) while 27 cases did not (control group). The control group received standard respiratory support, nutritional support, anti-infection measures, and other conventional treatments, whereas the dexamethasone group received low-dose dexamethasone in addition to standard care. The primary outcome was a composite endpoint of severe BPD or in-hospital death. Multivariable binary logistic regression was performed adjusting for gestational age, birth weight, and respiratory severity score (RSS). The study compared the extubation success rate, severe BPD incidence, and adverse reactions between the two groups.

Results

After adjustment for gestational age, birth weight, and RSS, dexamethasone was associated with lower odds of the composite endpoint of severe BPD or death (adjusted OR = 0.26, 95%CI 0.09-0.55, P = 0.003) and severe BPD among survivors (adjusted OR = 0.27, 95%CI 0.10-0.59, P = 0.005), and higher odds of extubation success (adjusted OR = 2.88, 95%CI 1.20-7.57, P = 0.024). Hyperglycaemia occurred more frequently in the dexamethasone group (41.5% vs. 18.5%, adjusted OR = 2.04, 95%CI 0.82-4.97, P = 0.121), although the difference did not reach statistical significance.

Conclusion

In this single-center retrospective cohort, low-dose dexamethasone was associated with lower odds of severe BPD or death and higher odds of extubation success after adjustment for gestational age, birth weight, and respiratory severity. Clinically relevant increases in adverse events, particularly hyperglycaemia, cannot be excluded given the limited sample size. Long-term growth was not assessed. These findings require validation in larger multicenter prospective studies.

title: Clinical characteristics and indicators associated with poor in-hospital prognosis among children with severe pertussis in Shandong Province, China (2022-2024).
authorString: Wang P, Li J.
abstractText:
Background

Pertussis is a life-threatening respiratory infection among young infants. This retrospective study enrolled only children already diagnosed with severe pertussis. We aimed to describe clinical characteristics and identify indicators associated with poor in‑hospital prognosis within this severe cohort, rather than exploring predictors for progression from mild to severe pertussis.

Methods

A retrospective observational study was conducted among 80 children diagnosed with severe pertussis who were hospitalized between January 2022 and December 2024. Clinical data, laboratory results, treatment, and outcomes were collected. Multivariate logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis were applied to screen indicators associated with composite poor in-hospital prognosis and evaluate their prognostic performance.Composite poor in-hospital prognosis was defined as new in-hospital adverse events including invasive mechanical ventilation, pertussis encephalopathy with persistent neurological sequelae, or all-cause in-hospital death; 6 out of 80 participants met this composite endpoint. White blood cell count was included as a continuous variable in multivariate regression. The optimal cutoff of > 30 × 10⁹/L was derived from ROC analysis for descriptive and potential bedside reference only and was not used for regression modelling.

Results

The median age was 4 months and 19 days (range, 1 month 14 days to 5 years); 65.0% (52/80) of patients were infants ≤ 3 months who could not receive routine diphtheria, pertussis, and tetanus (DPT) vaccine. All patients presented paroxysmal cough, and 95% had inspiratory whoop. Leukocytosis (WBC > 20 × 10⁹/L) was observed in 45.0% of children; 75.0% had patent foramen ovale (PFO), and 18.80% developed secondary cardiac abnormalities. Erythromycin combination therapy carried a significantly higher risk of liver dysfunction than monotherapy (36.40% vs. 8.60%, P < 0.05). Multivariate logistic regression identified three independent correlates of composite poor prognosis: unvaccinated status (OR = 4.2, 95%CI 1.8-9.6, P = 0.001), mixed bacterial-viral co-infection (OR = 3.5, 95%CI 1.2-10.1, P = 0.023), and elevated continuous white blood cell count (OR = 5.1, 95%CI 2.3-11.4, P < 0.001). Given the limited number of poor-prognosis events (n = 6), these adjusted associations should be interpreted cautiously as exploratory findings.ROC analysis using continuous WBC count yielded an AUC of 0.678, whereas the combined prognostic model derived from multivariable logistic regression achieved an AUC of 0.689.

Conclusions

Infants aged ≤ 3 months constituted the majority of children hospitalized with severe pertussis. After adjusting for age-related vaccination eligibility, unvaccinated status, mixed bacterial-viral co-infection, and higher white blood cell count were independently associated with poor in-hospital prognosis. ROC analysis demonstrated only modest discriminative performance of these indicators; at present, they serve merely as potential references and require external validation before any clinical application.

Trial registration number

Not applicable.

title: Population-specific genetic variants and related health outcomes in a cohort of Inuit children in Nunavut.
authorString: Gonzalez-Lema J, Allen J, Agyemang E, Patterson M, Miners A, Sheffield H, Caughey A, Pham-Huy A, Kovesi T, Shapiro AJ, Kernohan K, Yeh E, Yeh A, Mears A, Lacaria M, Collins S, Braschel M, Marcadier J, Otley A, Akearok GH, Doucette M, Rockman-Greenberg C, Chakraborty P, Caron N, Lehman A, Arbour L.
abstractText:
Introduction

Like all populations, Inuit children experience rare genetic conditions. Awareness of the unique Inuit genetic architecture allows the identification of specific variants associated with autosomal recessive conditions affecting child health across the Arctic. As a priority, the impact of the IFNAR2 c.157T>C variant causing IFNAR2 Deficiency, DNAH11 c.4095+2C>A causing Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia, and SI c.273_274delAG causing Congenital Sucrase-Isomaltase Deficiency (CSID), along with other disease-causing variants were assessed to determine the potential health outcomes on infant and child health in Nunavut.

Methods

With the direction of Nunavut Tunngavik Incorporated and the Government of Nunavut Department of Health a research group was established utilizing local and national expertise. Newborn dried screening blood spots of a 4-year cohort of infants born to residents of Nunavut between January 1st, 2010, and December 31st, 2013, were genotyped (n=2947) followed by linkage of a subset of the cohort to a database with demographic and health information collected from records spanning from birth to 5 years (n=2206 Inuit children). Live birth prevalence (LBP) of cases and carrier frequencies were first estimated for the full cohort and recalculated for the subset with linked data. Health visit information was reviewed for phenotype features consistent with the conditions of interest. In addition, baseline characteristics, and health visits for CSID cases were compared to those without the variant.

Results

LBP of cases due to homozygosity of the DNAH11, IFNAR2 and SI variants were 1/1474, 1/737 and 1/28; carrier frequency was 1/13, 1/18 and 1/4, respectively. Four children with IFNAR2, one with DNAH11, and 83 with SI homozygosity were linked to health data, confirming phenotypes consistent with the conditions. CSID was associated with significant increased health care utilization for gastrointestinal illness visits before age two (OR=1.9, 95% CI 1.2-3.0). However, breastfeeding for up to six months was found to be protective, with a reduced number of health care visits (OR=0.80, 95% CI 0.63-1.0).

Conclusion

We describe the presence and health impact of three autosomal recessive conditions in a Canadian Inuit population. Genetic testing, practitioner education, and Inuit-informed management strategies are urgently needed to address these conditions and improve outcomes.

title: Transfusion practices among children admitted to a South African PICU following cardiac surgery.
authorString: Fitzwanga K, Argent AC, Morrow BM, Salie S.

journal.title: The Southern African journal of critical care : the official journal of the Critical Care Society

abstractText:
Background

Blood products may be required in patients undergoing cardiac surgery; however, there is a paucity of data on blood transfusion guidelines in the perioperative and postoperative cardiac surgery period.

Objectives

To describe the prevalence of blood product transfusion, factors associated with transfusion and outcomes in patients who received blood products following cardiac surgery.

Methods

This was a prospective, single-centre observational study that consecutively recruited 126 children aged <18 years admitted to the paediatric intensive care unit (PICU) following cardiac surgery between July 2017 and January 2018. Demographic, intraoperative and postoperative blood product transfusion data were extracted from patient records, entered into a standardised case record form and analysed using Statistica version 13 (StatSoft Inc, USA). Statistical significance was set at p<0.05.

Results

Of the recruited children, 53% received blood products, with 30.9% receiving cryoprecipitate, 22.2% receiving packed red blood cells, 18.3% receiving albumin, 15.9% receiving fresh frozen plasma and 15.1% receiving platelet concentrates. Factors associated with the use of blood products included previous cardiac surgery, younger age, lower weight and prolonged coagulation parameters (p<0.05). Receiving blood products was associated with worse outcomes: a standardised mortality ratio of 3.1 v. 0 (p<0.0001), median (IQR) PICU length of stay of 5 (3 - 11) v. 2 (2 - 5) days (p<0.0001), and duration of mechanical ventilation of 47 (22 - 132) v. 20 (6 - 27) hours (p<0.0001).

Conclusion

There is a high prevalence of blood product use in children in the PICU following cardiac surgery, and this is associated with worse outcomes.

Contribution of the study

This is the first South African study to describe the use of all major blood product types, not only red blood cells, and their indications in children following paediatric cardiac surgery. It demonstrates a markedly different transfusion pattern from that reported in North American PICUs, with cryoprecipitate, rather than red blood cells, being the most frequently used product. Blood product use was common and was independently associated with worse outcomes, including longer PICU stays, prolonged ventilation and higher standardised mortality. These findings highlight the need for locally developed, evidence-based transfusion protocols to support blood product stewardship, particularly in resource-constrained settings that depend on voluntary blood donation.

title: Ring chromosome 7 syndrome with severe hypertriglyceridemia and mild echocardiographic abnormalities: a case report.
authorString: Ma R, Liu Y, Wei F.
abstractText:
Background

Ring chromosome 7 [r(7)] is an extremely rare constitutional chromosomal abnormality. The most frequently reported features include growth retardation, pigmented skin lesions, and microcephaly. However, the full phenotypic spectrum remains incompletely defined, particularly with regard to metabolic abnormalities and mild cardiovascular findings.

Case presentation

We report a 14-year-old Chinese girl referred for severe short stature. She had microcephaly, mild-to-moderate intellectual disability, bilateral epicanthal folds, left strabismus, multiple scattered pigmented melanocytic nevi, a bilateral single palmar crease, and lumbar scoliosis. Laboratory testing revealed severe hypertriglyceridemia (9.19 mmol/L). Echocardiography showed a small pericardial effusion and mild tricuspid regurgitation. Conventional cytogenetic analysis identified a mosaic karyotype of 46,XX,r(7)(p22q36)[56]/45,XX,-7[4], with no normal peripheral blood cell line detected. Whole-exome sequencing did not identify additional pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants relevant to the phenotype. Chromosomal microarray analysis and parental karyotyping were unavailable.

Conclusions

This case may broaden the reported clinical spectrum of ring chromosome 7 syndrome by highlighting severe hypertriglyceridemia as a potentially under-recognized metabolic manifestation. It also suggests that mild echocardiographic abnormalities may occur in addition to the major congenital cardiac defects described in some previously reported patients. The prolonged diagnostic delay underscores the importance of early chromosomal evaluation in children with unexplained growth failure accompanied by dysmorphic features, neurodevelopmental concerns, or characteristic skin findings.

title: Pulsed field ablation of incisional right atrial flutter in a patient with a repaired atrial septal defect while avoiding right phrenic nerve injury: A case report.
authorString: Scaglione M, Spinoni EG, Lamanna A, Geuna F, Gagliardi M, Battaglia A.

title: Spondyloocular Syndrome: Clinical Spectrum, Molecular Basis and Therapeutic Insights.
authorString: Qadir A, Ganie SA, Misgar RA.

journal.title: Indian journal of endocrinology and metabolism

abstractText: Spondyloocular syndrome (SOS) is a genetically determined bone fragility disorder marked by early vertebral collapse and consistent ocular involvement, most notably congenital cataracts. Owing to substantial clinical overlap, SOS is frequently misdiagnosed as osteogenesis imperfecta; however, multisystem involvement including coarse facial features, genitourinary anomalies, cardiac defects and hearing loss should prompt consideration of this distinct entity. The disorder arises from loss-of-function alterations in XYLT2, which encodes xylosyltransferase-2, an enzyme essential for initiating proteoglycan glycosaminoglycan chain synthesis, and belongs to the expanding group of disorders known as linkeropathies. To date, only 27 cases have been reported worldwide. This review synthesises existing global evidence on SOS and highlights our clinical experience with zoledronic acid therapy, offering practical insights into diagnosis and management. Early recognition and timely genetic testing, particularly whole-exome sequencing, are essential to avoid diagnostic delay and optimise patient outcomes.

title: Machine learning insights on stress hyperglycemia ratio and mortality in congestive heart failure patients with cerebrovascular disease: an analysis of the MIMIC-IV database.
authorString: Sun L, Ji R, Wang Y, Wang T, Zhao Z, Yuan J, Yuan Q, Ning B.
abstractText:
Background

The stress hyperglycemia ratio (SHR), calculated as Admission Blood Glucose (aBG) / (28.7 × glycated hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) %) - 46.7, integrates acute and chronic glycemic status and predicts adverse cardiovascular events, yet its prognostic value remains unclear among CHF patients complicated with cerebrovascular disease (CVD). This study aimed to explore the association between SHR and all-cause mortality in this specific Intensive Care Unit (ICU) population and provide evidence for targeted glycemic management.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective cohort study utilizing the MIMIC-IV database. Among 11,196 ICU patients admitted for CHF between 2008 and 2019, 10,214 patients were excluded due to missing HbA1c or admission blood glucose data, resulting in a final analytical cohort of 982 patients. Restricted cubic splines (RCS) and Kaplan-Meier (K-M) curves were employed to illustrate the dose - response association between the SHR and all-cause mortality. Stratified multivariable Cox regression was utilized to estimate hazard ratios, stratified by cerebrovascular disease status. Multiple machine learning models were developed to predict 30-day all-cause mortality, with CatBoost demonstrating the optimal predictive performance. Log-odds-scale SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) values were calculated to quantify the prognostic impact of each variable.

Results

A total of 982 CHF patients were enrolled, including 320 with concomitant CVD. RCS revealed a linear positive dose-response association between SHR and 30-day and 365-day all-cause mortality among CHF patients with CVD. K-M curves demonstrated that higher SHR quartiles were associated with worse 30-day and 365-day survival among patients with CVD. After full covariate adjustment, patients in the highest SHR quartile showed significantly elevated 30-day mortality risk [HR = 2.79, 95% CI 1.21-6.42, P = 0.016], with a significant linear trend across SHR quartiles (P for trend = 0.004). Consistently, the highest SHR quartile predicted higher 365-day mortality risk [HR = 2.02, 95% CI 1.12-3.66, P = 0.02], accompanied by an overall positive linear trend [P for trend  = 0.014]. No independent prognostic effect of SHR was observed in patients without CVD. SHAP analysis confirmed SHR as a key predictor for short-term all-cause mortality, and the optimal CatBoost model achieved moderate discriminative performance (AUC = 0.77).

Conclusion

Elevated SHR was independently associated with higher 30-day and 365-day all-cause mortality risk solely in critically ill CHF patients with concomitant CVD. The SHR index enables risk stratification and personalized glycemic management for this high-risk ICU cohort.

title: Severe neonatal long QT syndrome type 3 treated with genotype-directed therapy and early left cardiac sympathetic denervation: a case report.
authorString: Greco A, Martínez-Barrios E, Lujan A, Campuzano Larrea Ó, Sarquella-Brugada G.
abstractText:
Background

Long QT syndrome type 3 may present in foetal or neonatal life with QT prolongation, 2:1 atrioventricular (AV) block, and life-threatening ventricular arrhythmias. Early recognition and individualizes genotype-directed management may be lifesaving.

Case summary

A neonate delivered after foetal bradycardia and intermittent 2:1 AV block presented with severe QT prolongation and recurrent torsades de pointes. The functional 2:1 AV block persisted despite beta-blockade and magnesium administration. Because of recurrent ventricular arrhythmias, video-assisted thoracoscopic left cardiac sympathetic denervation (LCSD) and implantable loop recorder were performed on Day 8 of life. Genetic testing identified a de novo likely pathogenic SCN5A_p.(Ala1656Val) missense variant. Subsequent lidocaine testing demonstrated marked QT shortening, supporting sodium channel-mediated disease and guiding treatment with mexiletine and flecainide. Long-term follow-up required implantable cardioverter-defibrillator therapy, but arrhythmic burden progressively improved.

Discussion

This case supports the potential role of early multimodal treatment in malignant neonatal long QT syndrome type 3, combining LCSD, continuous rhythm monitoring, and genotype-directed sodium channel blockade.

title: Intensified background therapy enhances mortality benefit of SGLT2 inhibitors in heart failure: a retrospective cohort study.
authorString: Zhang Q, Fan F, Yang F, Zhou Z, Jia J, Jiang J, Gao Y, Wang Y, Li L, Liao Y, Li W, Dong Y, Li X, Zhou J, Gong Y, Yang J, Huo Y.
abstractText:
Background

SGLT2 inhibitors (SGLT2is) improve outcomes in patients with heart failure (HF), but their effects may depend on background medical therapy. The Heart Failure Collaboratory score, which incorporates medication type and dose, may modify the benefit of SGLT2is. To evaluate the association between the scoring system and the mortality benefit of SGLT2 inhibitors in patients with heart failure.

Methods

This retrospective multicenter cohort study used real-world data from the Chinese Cardiovascular Association Database-HF Center (HFC) Registry. 52 hospitals were selected with 26 HFCs and 26 NHFCs. Patients with a diagnosis of HF and one-year follow-up from July 1, 2022, to March 31, 2023, were included. The primary outcome was one-year all-cause mortality. Cox regression and multivariable fractional polynomial interaction (MFPI) models were used to assess the effect of SGLT2is on mortality risk across Heart Failure Collaboratory scores.

Results

A total of 4,077 patients (median age 70.0 years; 60.1% male) were included. SGLT2is was associated with reduced mortality risk in the overall population (adjusted hazard ratio (aHR) 0.71, 95% CI 0.60-0.85). A significant interaction was observed with the score (P interaction = 0.009), with SGLT2is therapy associated with a greater reduction in mortality risk among patients scoring ≥ 5 (aHR 0.60, 95% CI 0.46-0.78), whereas no significant association was observed in those scoring < 5 (aHR 0.98, 95% CI 0.76-1.26). MFPI analysis further demonstrated greater mortality risk reduction in SGLT2is user than nonuser, as the score increased (P interaction = 0.003), and also in patients with LVEF > 40% (P interaction = 0.021).

Conclusion

The mortality benefit was more pronounced when other triple therapy agents were adequately applied.

Clinical trial number

ChiCTR1800017226.

title: Multistage cardiac surgery, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, and advanced wound care in a critically ill neonate: a case report.
authorString: Castiello G, Giamberti A, Varrica A, Reali M, Lo Rito M, Torchio F, Isgrò G, Satriano A, Messina C, Chessa M, Ghizzardi G, Caruso R.
abstractText:
Background

Neonates with complex congenital heart disease (CHD) frequently require early and staged surgical interventions, which carry a high risk of postoperative complications. The coexistence of an interrupted aortic arch, ventricular septal defect (VSD), and mitral valve stenosis represents a rare and particularly high-risk constellation. This case is noteworthy for the integration of multistage cardiac surgery, prolonged extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO), and an innovative wound management strategy combining negative pressure wound therapy (NPWT) with topical oxygen-enriched gel.

Case presentation

We report the case of a one-month-old Romanian female infant diagnosed with type A interrupted aortic arch, VSD, and mitral valve stenosis. The initial surgical procedure included aortic arch reconstruction, VSD closure with a bovine pericardial patch, and mitral valve repair. Severe residual mitral regurgitation necessitated immediate initiation of veno-arterial ECMO, followed by mitral valve replacement with a Melody bioprosthesis. On postoperative day 19, thrombotic obstruction of the prosthetic valve required a third surgical intervention for clot removal, after which ECMO was discontinued. Delayed sternal closure was performed on day 26, but wound dehiscence developed on day 33. Management included NPWT combined with topical oxygen-enriched gel for 33 days, followed by gel monotherapy for 38 additional days. Complete secondary intention healing was achieved after 73 days. Despite developing Pseudomonas aeruginosa sepsis and late-onset Staphylococcus haemolyticus bacteremia, the patient recovered fully without neurological deficits or wound-related sequelae.

Conclusions

This case highlights the feasibility of combining advanced surgical management with innovative wound care strategies in critically ill neonates with complex CHD. The successful integration of NPWT and topical oxygen therapy promoted wound healing after delayed sternal closure, even in the context of severe infection and prolonged ECMO support. These findings suggest that tailored, multidisciplinary approaches may optimize outcomes in high-complexity neonatal cardiac cases.

title: Clinical and instrumental phenotyping of gait in subjects with Cri du Chat syndrome.
authorString: Agostini B, Vaghi G, Corrado M, Grillo V, Martinis L, Gjini M, Campese I, Giraudo M, Cammarota F, Ravaglia S, Croce MG, De Giorgis V, Politano D, Castiglia SF, Trabassi D, Serrao M, Danesino C, Guala A, Tassorelli C, De Icco R, “ABC Study Group”.
abstractText:
Background

Cri du Chat syndrome (CdCS) is a rare genetic disorder characterized by disabling psychomotor and gait impairments. The aim of this study is to assess and characterize CdCS gait through a comprehensive and validated set of trunk acceleration-derived gait indexes by means of inertial gait analysis.

Methods

In this cross-sectional study, we enrolled 38 CdCS individuals (age 22.6 [18.4-26.0] years, 52.6% females) and 39 healthy subjects (HS) matched for age, sex and speed of gait. Besides the conventional spatio-temporal parameters we calculated: the harmonic ratio (HR, primary outcome), the largest Lyapunov exponent for short time-series (sLLE), the percent determinism in recurrence quantification analysis (RQA).

Results

Compared to HS, CdCS gait was characterized by lower HR (CdCS: 1.6 [1.4-1.7] vs. HS: 2.6 [2.4-2.7], p = 0.001), lower RQA (p = 0.001) and higher sLLE (p = 0.001). In CdCS individuals, we also found a higher stride time, along with a lower cadence and range of pelvic obliquity during gait (p < 0.025 for all comparisons). Logistic regression analysis identified HR and RQA in the antero-posterior plane and the range of pelvic obliquity as the independent and most relevant features able to differentiate gait of CdCS subjects from HS.

Conclusions

Our study provides a comprehensive description of CdCS gait pattern, predominantly characterized by reduced symmetry, rhythmicity, and stability.

Trial registration

The study protocol was approved by local Ethical Committee (CE Pavia, Approval Number: 2022-3.11/797) and pre-registered on www.

Clinicaltrials

gov (NCT05887739).

title: ER stress and structural changes induced by rare WFS1 variant identified in autosomal dominant form of WFS1-related disorder.
authorString: Borecka S, Zahradnikova A, Varga L, Stanik J, Hromnikova D, Sabo M, Sklenar M, Baglaeva I, Iaparov B, Cagalinec M, Skopkova M, Gasperikova D.
abstractText:
Background

WFS1‑related disorders encompass a broad phenotypic spectrum ranging from classical autosomal-recessive Wolfram syndrome to autosomal-dominant Wolfram‑like disorders. Dominant variants may disrupt endoplasmic reticulum (ER) homeostasis, calcium handling, and ER-mitochondria communication. Here, we report a Slovak male patient with a complex multisystem Wolfram‑like phenotype and identify a rare heterozygous in‑frame deletion in WFS1 (c.2608_2619del, p.870_873del). We aimed to determine its pathogenic potential through structural modelling and functional assays.

Methods

The genetic aetiology was investigated by Sanger sequencing, WGS and MLPA. Structural consequences of the deletion were analysed using AlphaFold3 modelling of wild‑type and mutant wolframin, followed by hydrogen‑bond quantification in ChimeraX. Functional studies were performed in HeLa cells expressing wild‑type WFS1, the rare p.870_873del variant, and two pathogenic controls (p.E809K, p.P724L). ER morphology was assessed by confocal microscopy. ER stress activation was quantified using ERSE‑luciferase reporter assays, XBP1 splicing analysis, and qPCR of UPR‑related genes. Mitochondrial fusion dynamics were measured using the photoconvertible mito‑KikGR1 system.

Results

The patient presented with early‑onset insulin‑dependent diabetes mellitus, bilateral cataracts, sensorineural hearing loss, autism spectrum disorder, paroxysmal events, and additional systemic comorbidities. Genetic analysis identified a de novo in‑frame deletion affecting four amino acid residues. Structural modelling showed that the deleted region contributes to a C‑terminal hydrogen‑bonding network, and its loss resulted in a significant reduction of stabilizing interactions. Although ER morphology remained preserved, cells expressing the p.870_873del variant displayed markedly reduced mitochondrial fusion, comparable to both pathogenic controls, indicating impaired ER-mitochondria crosstalk. Functional assays further demonstrated pronounced ER stress, evidenced by significantly increased ERSE‑luciferase activity, increased XBP1 splicing, upregulation of DDIT3 (CHOP), and mild induction of HSPA5 (BiP), consistent with activation of the unfolded protein response.

Conclusions

We identified a rare likely pathogenic p.870_873del WFS1 variant associated with an autosomal-dominant WFS1‑related disorder and a multisystem Wolfram‑like phenotype. Combined structural and functional evidence indicates that this variant disrupts protein stability, activates ER stress, and impairs ER-mitochondria communication, supporting its potential pathogenic role.

title: Electrocardiographic abnormalities associated with obesity in adolescents and young adults: physiologic variants or true pathology? A cross-sectional study.
authorString: Oyebanji AH, Adeoye BO, Ezekpo OO, Adelekan OE, Ezigbo CF, Akano OP.
abstractText:
Background

Obesity is defined by the World Health Organization as abnormal or excessive fat accumulation that poses a risk to health. It has reached epidemic proportions globally and carries significant cardiovascular risk, particularly in adolescents and young adults. Electrocardiographic (ECG) changes are well documented in obese adults; however, the extent and nature of these changes in healthy obese and non-obese young people remain poorly characterized. This study aimed to determine whether obesity-related ECG abnormalities are confined to obese adolescents and young adults or are equally observed across other body mass index (BMI) categories.

Methods

A cross-sectional descriptive study was conducted among 172 apparently healthy participants aged 10 to 24 years, recruited using a multi-stage stratified random sampling method. Participants were categorized into three BMI groups (normal weight, overweight and obese) according to CDC-BMI percentile for age criteria. A 12-lead resting ECG was performed on each participant using a Grandfield Medical three-channel ECG machine with automated analysis secondarily validated by a clinician. Anthropometric, clinical, and biochemical parameters were also obtained. Data were analyzed using SPSS version 23.0, and a p-value below 0.05 was considered statistically significant.

Results

Females constituted 59.3% of participants (M: F ratio approximately 1:1.5), with a mean age of 18.1 years (SD 3.77) and mean BMI of 27.2 kg/m² (SD 5.74). ECG abnormalities were observed overall in 43% of participants after excluding physiologic variants. Statistically significant findings included prolonged P-wave duration consistent with left atrial enlargement (p = 0.01), prolonged PR interval (p = 0.025), and T-wave flattening in inferior and lateral leads (p = 0.017). T-wave flattening was most prevalent in the normal BMI group (42%). Age-related differences were identified for pulse rate and early repolarization pattern (ERP), both were significantly higher in early adolescents aged 10 to 14 years (p < 0.001). P-axis values were significantly higher in young adults aged 20 to 24 years than in middle adolescents aged 15 to 19 years (p = 0.005). T-axis measurements was significantly greater in males than females (p = 0.016). Other findings including arrhythmias, left ventricular hypertrophy, right ventricular hypertrophy, atrial enlargement, and early repolarization pattern (ERP) were observed but did not reach statistical significance across BMI groups. QTc interval and QRS voltage were normal across all groups.

Conclusion

The majority of ECG findings observed in this study are consistent with physiologic variants distributed across all BMI categories. These findings are not confined to obese individuals, which challenges the assumption that such ECG changes are obesity-specific. Early screening in this age group may assist in differentiating true cardiac pathology from normal physiological variants, which has normal healthy spectrum of body functions or structure and requires no treatment modality because it represent the natural range of human diversity.

Clinical trial number

Not applicable.

title: Association between LDL-C/HDL-C ratio and atrial fibrillation risk in chronic heart failure patients.
authorString: Yan S, Hong X, Chen L, Lin X.
abstractText:
Background

Lipid levels are negatively correlated with atrial fibrillation (AF) in the general population. We aimed to investigate the correlation between low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C)/high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) ratio and AF in chronic heart failure (CHF).

Methods

We enrolled 1,294 consecutive CHF patients. The LDL-C/HDL-C ratio was categorized into quartiles: Q1 (< 1.80), Q2 (1.80-2.43), Q3 (2.44-3.29), and Q4 (> 3.29). The relationship between the LDL-C/HDL-C ratio and AF in patients with CHF was analyzed by univariate and multivariate analyses through binary logistic regression, and sensitivity and subgroup analyses were performed for the multivariate results to validate the robustness of the multivariate results and assess the influence of confounding variables.

Results

The LDL-C/HDL-C ratio was inversely associated with the prevalence of AF in patients with CHF. When modeled by quartiles as a categorical variable, the trend P-value remained consistent with the continuous analysis. Sensitivity analyses excluding patients with stroke, dilated cardiomyopathy, or atherosclerosis confirmed the association (full model P for trend < 0.05), indicating robust results. In subgroup analyses, the association was not significantly influenced by confounding variables (P for interaction > 0.05).

Conclusions

The LDL-C/HDL-C ratio was independently and inversely associated with prevalent AF among patients with chronic heart failure. This readily available metric may help identify CHF patients who could benefit from enhanced AF screening.

title: The IO PhD International Research Program 15 years later: where do we stand?
authorString: Gazzolo D, Gavilanes DAW, Zimmermann L, Vles HJS, van Bel F, Visser GHA.
abstractText:
Background

International doctoral research programs represent an effective model for fostering scientific collaboration and training clinician-scientists. The Italia-Olanda PhD International Research Program (IO PhD), established in 2010, was designed to promote translational research in neonatology and perinatal medicine through a structured international network.

Methods

A bibliometric analysis was conducted to evaluate the scientific output of the IO PhD between 2010 and 2024. Publications were identified through PubMed searches and manual screening of full-text articles based on acknowledgment statements referring to the program. Bibliometric indicators included publication output, journal characteristics, research topics, and citation metrics.

Results

A total of 85 peer-reviewed publications were identified over the study period. Scientific productivity increased during the first decade, followed by stabilization in recent years. A progressive shift toward higher-impact journals was observed, with a significant increase in Q1 publications over time as well as citation metrics (impact factor, h-index). The main research areas included neonatal biomarkers (34%), perinatal hypoxia (21%), respiratory disorders of prematurity (16%), nutrition (12%), infections (6%), and other topics (11%). Overall, the publications generated 1508 citations, with a mean of 18 citations per article and an h-index of 24.

Conclusions

Over a 15-year period, the IO PhD has produced a consistent and impactful body of scientific literature. The program represents a successful model of international doctoral training, supporting translational research and fostering the development of early-career clinician-scientists in neonatology and perinatal medicine.

title: Pulmonary hydatid cyst presenting with altered consciousness in a 19-year-old Afghan migrant: a case report and review of the literature.
authorString: Lotfi MA, Pourmasumi S, Mehdizadeh S, Jawed I, Xu X, Palanivelu P, Zakeri MA.
abstractText:
Background

Hydatid disease is a parasitic infection caused by the larval stage of the tapeworm Echinococcus granulosus. Clinical manifestations vary based location and size of the cyst. While pulmonary hydatid cysts are well-documented, neurological presentations such as altered consciousness are exceptionally rare and have never been reported in Afghan migrants. This case highlights a novel clinical manifestation in a vulnerable population with limited healthcare access, underscoring the urgent need for systematic screening and heightened clinical awareness in host countries.

Case presentation

This study details the case of a 19-year-old Afghan woman with a left pulmonary hydatid cyst who presented with dyspnea, chest pain, myalgia, and decreased consciousness. The diagnosis was established based on radiological findings and clinical presentation. The patient underwent complete surgical excision of the cyst and was discharged in a stable condition after an uneventful postoperative period. She was followed up for 6 months, with no evidence of cyst recurrence and complete clinical recovery. Additionally, a focused review of the literature identified 15 case reports of hydatid cyst in immigrant populations.

Conclusion

Although rare in some regions, pulmonary hydatid cysts remain a critical differential diagnosis in migrants from endemic areas. This case underscores the importance of timely diagnosis, precise imaging, and a multidisciplinary therapeutic approach combining surgical intervention and pharmacotherapy. A Comparative analysis of the existing literature demonstrates that combined treatment yields favorable clinical outcomes and reduces recurrence risk. Heightened clinical awareness, particularly in migrant populations is essential to prevent severe complications. Most importantly, it exposes a systemic gap: migrants from high-risk areas are rarely screened for echinococcosis. We urge health systems to incorporate routine serology and chest imaging into migrant health protocols, a low-cost, high-impact intervention that can prevent avoidable complications and advance health equity.

title: Diagnostic value of systemic immune-inflammation index versus lactate dehydrogenase in early prediction of severe mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia in children: a retrospective matched case-control study.
authorString: Chen W, Wu N, Liu B, Zhang W.
abstractText:
Objective

This study aims to investigate the diagnostic utility of the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) and lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), as well as their combined models, for the early prediction of severe mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia (SMPP) in children.

Methods

This retrospective matched case-control study analyzed data from 100 hospitalized children (50 SMPP cases and 50 non-SMPP controls, 1:1 matched) at Xi'an Children's Hospital between June 2023 and June 2024. Laboratory indicators, including SII, LDH, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), C-reactive protein (CRP), and procalcitonin (PCT), were collected at admission. Independent risk factors were identified through logistic regression. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, DeLong test, and Youden index were used to evaluate predictive efficacy.

Results

The SMPP group showed significantly prolonged fever duration, higher peak temperature, elevated CRP and PCT levels, increased rates of glucocorticoid and bronchoscopy use, and longer hospitalization (all P < 0.05). SII, NLR, PLR, and LDH were significantly higher in the SMPP group, with SII showing the largest effect size (r = 0.720). After adjusting for age and duration of fever before admission, multivariate analysis confirmed SII (aOR = 1.013, 95% CI: 1.006-1.019, P < 0.001) and LDH (aOR = 1.029, 95% CI: 1.009-1.050, P = 0.005) as independent risk factors. SII alone demonstrated superior predictive performance (AUC = 0.918, 95% CI: 0.863-0.972; sensitivity 78.0%, specificity 94.0%) compared with LDH (AUC = 0.797, 95% CI: 0.708-0.886; P = 0.025). The SII-LDH combined model achieved an AUC of 0.950 (95% CI: 0.910-0.990; sensitivity 82.0%, specificity 98.0%), showing no significant difference versus SII alone (P = 0.083) but significantly outperforming LDH alone (P < 0.001).

Conclusion

The study showed superior discriminatory capability of SII compared to LDH in identifying SMPP within this cohort. These results imply that SII could serve as a valuable biomarker for early risk assessment, pending prospective multicenter validation prior to standard clinical adoption.

title: Clinical spectrum of intracellular cobalamin metabolism disorders: a single-center retrospective study from the United Arab Emirates.
authorString: Shamsi AA, Abuhaltem O.
abstractText:
Background

Cobalamin is essential for DNA synthesis and for methylmalonyl-CoA mutase and methionine synthase activity. Inherited disorders of intracellular cobalamin (Cbl) metabolism are single-gene defects affecting absorption, transport, or intracellular processing, with variable phenotypes depending on the severity and location of the defect. Data from high consanguinity populations, such as the UAE, are limited.

Aim

To describe the clinical, biochemical, and molecular characteristics of patients with intracellular Cbl metabolism disorders at Tawam Hospital, UAE.

Methods

Retrospective review of patients followed between January 2010 and December 2025. Data included demographics, clinical features, laboratory and radiological findings, molecular results, treatment, and outcomes.

Results

Twelve patients were identified: 8 CblC, 1 CblE, 1 CblG, and 2 unclassified. Consanguinity was present in 75%. The earliest diagnosis was at 8 days; 91.6% were symptomatic. Presentations included seizures (58%), apparent life-threatening events (33%), hydrocephalus and cytopenia (25% each), global developmental delay, osteoporosis, hypothyroidism, hypogonadism, multicystic kidney, and psychiatric symptoms. Homocysteine was elevated in all. The MMACHC c.271dupA variant was common; a novel variant in the MTRR gene was identified. All received parenteral hydroxocobalamin, betaine, and carnitine with partial biochemical improvement. The newborn-screened patient had a favorable outcome.

Conclusion

This cohort broadens the phenotypic spectrum to endocrine, renal, and psychiatric manifestations. Early diagnosis and hydroxocobalamin treatment improve outcomes, though neurocognitive and ophthalmologic complications persist.

title: Steatotic liver disease subtypes exhibit distinct risk patterns of tachyarrhythmias and bradyarrhythmias.
authorString: Lin Y, Chen QF, Xia T, Chew NWS, Lian LY, Zhang N, Targher G, Byrne CD, Fan RC, Lv KK, Lip GYH, Sperling LS, Wang XD, Fudim M, Ju S, Zhou XD, Zheng MH, CHAIN Consortium.
abstractText:
Background and aims

Steatotic liver disease (SLD) is independently associated with cardiovascular disease; however, data on cardiac arrhythmias across individual SLD subtypes remain scarce. This study aimed to investigate associations between distinct SLD subtypes and arrhythmia risk.

Methods

Using prospective UK Biobank data, participants were classified into four groups: no-SLD, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), metabolic dysfunction and alcohol-associated steatotic liver disease (MetALD), and alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD). The primary outcome was incident overall arrhythmias, and secondary outcomes were specific arrhythmia subtypes. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models assessed associations, and exploratory analyses evaluated subtype‑specific risk patterns.

Results

Among 428,609 participants followed for a median of 14.23 years (IQR: 12.64-15.30), the cumulative incidence of arrhythmias increased progressively from no-SLD to MASLD, MetALD, and ALD (8.22%, 13.60%, 14.15%, and 16.43%, respectively). All SLD subtypes were independently associated with a higher risk of overall arrhythmias (MASLD: aHR = 1.39, 95% CI 1.36-1.42; MetALD: aHR = 1.43, 95% CI 1.38-1.48; ALD: aHR = 1.65, 95% CI 1.57-1.74; all P < 0.001). Atrial fibrillation and flutter (AF/AFL) accounted for 85.39% of tachyarrhythmias, and risk increased stepwise across the MASLD-MetALD-ALD spectrum. In contrast, bradyarrhythmias showed a distinct risk hierarchy, with MetALD conferring the highest risk (aHR = 1.44, 95% CI 1.32-1.56; P < 0.001), followed by MASLD (aHR = 1.39, 95% CI 1.32-1.47; P < 0.001) and ALD (aHR = 1.38, 95% CI 1.21-1.58; P < 0.001). Exploratory analyses suggested that alcohol‑related subtypes were more strongly associated with tachyarrhythmias than with bradyarrhythmias.

Conclusions

SLD subtypes were independently associated with a higher risk of incident arrhythmias, and the risk of AF/AFL increased stepwise across the MASLD-MetALD-ALD spectrum. Bradyarrhythmia risk was predominantly observed in metabolically related SLD subtypes. These findings suggest that SLD subtype classification is a relevant consideration for future risk stratification research, although its clinical applicability warrants further investigation.

title: Haptoglobin is associated with nocturnal blood pressure non-dipping in children with chronic kidney disease.
authorString: Lu PC, Liao WT, Hsu CN, Tain YL.
abstractText:
Background

Blood pressure (BP) follows a circadian rhythm that depends partly on endothelial nitric oxide (NO) bioavailability. Cell-free hemoglobin rapidly scavenges NO, and haptoglobin functions as a capacity-limited plasma buffer facilitating hemoglobin clearance. Whether reduced circulating haptoglobin contributes to circadian rhythm-related vascular dysregulation in pediatric chronic kidney disease (CKD) remains unclear.

Methods

Sixty children with CKD were enrolled, and plasma haptoglobin levels were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Twenty-five participants underwent 24-hour ambulatory BP monitoring. Nocturnal systolic BP non-dipping was defined as <10% decline in nighttime values. Multivariable Firth penalized logistic regression adjusted for age and sex. Restricted cubic spline modeling assessed dose-response patterns.

Results

Fifteen of 25 children (60%) exhibited nocturnal non-dipping. Plasma haptoglobin levels were significantly lower in non-dippers than in dippers. Each 10 mg/dL increase in haptoglobin was independently associated with lower odds of non-dipping (adjusted OR 0.74, 95% CI 0.49-0.99; p = 0.044). Spline modeling suggested a threshold-like increase in risk at lower concentrations.

Conclusion

Lower circulating haptoglobin is independently associated with nocturnal BP non-dipping in children with CKD. These findings suggest that reduced hemoglobin-buffering capacity may contribute to impaired circadian BP regulation, although mechanistic confirmation is required.

title: Serum sestrin2 as a potential prognostic biomarker for acute ischemic stroke.
authorString: Jin Z, Yu X, Jia M, Gao X, Tan Y.
abstractText:
Background

Sestrin2 has been reported to be associated with the occurrence of acute ischemic stroke (AIS), but its prognostic significance in patients with AIS remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the prognostic value of serum sestrin2 in patients with AIS and to develop a prognostic model incorporating serum sestrin2.

Methods

This observational study primarily comprised a retrospective prognostic cohort with an embedded exploratory cross-sectional comparison. A total of 100 patients with AIS and 47 healthy controls were enrolled. Serum sestrin2, interleukin-6 (IL-6), and interleukin-1β (IL-1β) levels were measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Associations between serum sestrin2 and clinical characteristics were analysed, and multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify independent predictors of unfavorable outcome, defined as a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score > 2 at 3 months. A prognostic nomogram was developed and internally validated using bootstrap resampling.

Results

Compared with healthy controls, patients with AIS had significantly higher serum sestrin2 and IL-6 levels, although this comparison should be interpreted cautiously because of the age imbalance between groups. Among the 100 patients with AIS, 26 were classified as having an unfavorable functional outcome (mRS > 2) at 3 months. Serum sestrin2 levels were positively correlated with both IL-6 concentrations and mRS scores. After adjustment for age and major vascular risk factors, higher serum sestrin2 levels and NIHSS scores remained independently associated with unfavorable 3-month outcomes. Compared with the NIHSS-alone model, the addition of serum sestrin2 significantly improved overall model fit, although improvements in discrimination and reclassification metrics were not statistically significant. A nomogram incorporating these two variables demonstrated good discrimination (AUC 0.897, 95% CI 0.830-0.963), satisfactory calibration, and favorable performance after bootstrap internal validation. Decision curve analysis suggested potential clinical value for early risk stratification.

Conclusions

Serum sestrin2 was independently associated with unfavorable functional outcomes in patients with AIS and may serve as a complementary prognostic biomarker. A prognostic nomogram incorporating serum sestrin2 and NIHSS score demonstrated promising predictive performance and may provide complementary information for early risk stratification after AIS. External validation is required before clinical implementation.

Trial registration

ChiCTR2600124185 (Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, Registered 8 May 2026).

title: Prevalence and factors associated with early childhood caries among three-year-old children attending child welfare clinics in Kalutara District, Sri Lanka: a cross-sectional study.
authorString: Nilmini KWDE, Wijesinghe MSD, Ratnayake NC.
abstractText:
Background

Early childhood caries (ECC) remains a significant public health challenge in Sri Lanka, despite established preventive programs. Evidence on socio-behavioural and child-related factors associated with ECC among three-year-old children, particularly at the district level, is limited. This study assessed the prevalence of ECC and socio-behavioural and child-related factors associated with ECC among three-year-old children attending child welfare clinics (CWCs) in Kalutara District, Sri Lanka.

Methods

We conducted a cross-sectional study involving 1,197 mother-child dyads attending CWCs in the Kalutara District from May to September 2025, following the Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (STROBE) guidelines. Children aged three years (completed third but not fourth birthday) were included using multistage cluster sampling with probability proportional to size (PPS). Data on sociodemographics, dietary habits, and oral health behaviours were collected using a pre-tested, expert-validated, interviewer-administered questionnaire. Dental examinations were performed by a calibrated examiner using World Health Organization (WHO) criteria. Multivariable logistic regression identified variables independently associated with ECC (dmft ≥ 1).

Results

The prevalence of ECC was 51.8% (95% CI: 49.0-54.7), with severe ECC in 28.6% of the sample. The mean dmft score was 1.89 (± 2.84). Factors independently associated with ECC included lower maternal education (aOR 1.98, 95% CI: 1.20-3.29), daily sweet consumption (aOR 1.76, 95% CI: 1.24-2.49), daily sugared beverage intake (aOR 1.77, 95% CI: 1.26-2.49), previous dental discomfort (aOR 11.22, 95% CI: 7.11-17.70), caregiver-reported dental anxiety/fear-related delay in dental attendance (aOR 3.44, 95% CI: 2.31-5.13), and frequent medication use (aOR 1.91, 95% CI: 1.19-3.04). Caregiver-assisted toothbrushing (aOR 0.41, 95% CI: 0.25-0.66) and fluoridated toothpaste use (aOR 0.54, 95% CI: 0.31-0.94) were associated with lower odds of ECC.

Conclusions

Over half of the three-year-old children in the Kalutara District had ECC. Modifiable dietary and oral hygiene behaviours were important factors associated with ECC. Strengthening caregiver-focused preventive interventions through CWCs, alongside population-level sugar reduction strategies, could substantially reduce the ECC burden.

Trial registration

Not applicable.

title: Evaluation of spirituality among primary caregivers in a perinatal palliative care program in Mexico.
authorString: Valle-Gutiérrez A, Mendoza-Martínez MG, Peláez-Ballestas I, Guadarrama-Orozco JH.
abstractText:
Background

Perinatal palliative care seeks to maximize quality of life through physical, social, psychological, and spiritual care, supporting families from diagnosis through bereavement. Spirituality (the search for meaning and connection, and religiousness, a system of beliefs and rituals linked to the divine) shape the experience of illness and death, yet are often sidelined in medical care. Evaluating spirituality is essential but complex, as it requires translating an abstract concept into a socio-clinical measure and is limited by health professionals' lack of training. Tools such as FICA (Faith, Importance, Community, and Address in care) can facilitate this process.

Objective

To explore the spiritual dimensions and needs of caregivers of newborns in palliative care, using the FICA tool as an evaluation guide.

Methodology

Semi-structured interviews with primary caregivers, guided by the FICA dimensions, were recorded and transcribed for thematic narrative analysis. Participants provided informed consent.

Results

Caregivers of nine newborns were invited; seven caregivers of five newborns accepted. Ages ranged from 18 to 53 years; most belonged to extended nuclear families, lived in urban areas, and were traditionally Catholic. Most recognized their spiritual beliefs and needs and the importance of spirituality in their lives; six of seven belonged to informal spiritual communities. The affective dimension predominated, and anguish and abandonment emerged as spiritual symptoms.

Conclusion

FICA helps identify caregivers' spiritual dimensions, their community support, and how prayer, ritual, and family support provide comfort. Routine spiritual evaluation could help detect spiritual suffering and guide better support strategies from health professionals in perinatal palliative care.

title: Electrical stimulation promotes cardiomyocyte differentiation and cardiac development.
authorString: Wu Y, Zhang F, Wang Y, Peng W, Zhang H, Ma Y, Liu C, Li X, Jiang Z, Hu S, Liang G, Han Y, Xiao M, Lei W, Tang M.
abstractText:
Background

Electrical signals play critical roles in early heart development by regulating cardiomyocyte differentiation, proliferation, and energy metabolism. However, the mechanisms by which electrical stimulation (ES) influences early cardiac development remain incompletely understood.

Methods

Human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (hiPSC-CMs) and zebrafish embryos were employed as complementary in vitro and in vivo models. hiPSC-CMs were subjected to continuous ES from the cardiac mesoderm stage (day 4) to day 10 of differentiation. Cellular analyses included immunofluorescence, calcium imaging, proliferation assays, ATP quantification, and qRT-PCR. Zebrafish embryos were subjected to continuous ES for 10 h and 24 h post-fertilization (hpf), respectively. Subsequently, at 36, 48, and 72 hpf, the heart rate, contractile function, proliferation of cardiac cells, and vascular development were assessed. RNA sequencing was conducted on hiPSC-CMs and zebrafish embryos to assess transcriptomic changes, followed by bioinformatic pathway enrichment analysis. Functional studies involved siRNA mediated GATA4 knockdown in hiPSC-CMs, and in zebrafish embryos treated with a gata4 inhibitor, to systematically evaluate the effects of gata4 on cardiac function.

Results

ES significantly enhanced hiPSC-CMs differentiation, calcium handling, sarcomere maturation, proliferation, and energy metabolism, accompanied by upregulation of RYR2 and oxidative phosphorylation genes. In zebrafish embryos, ES accelerated body growth, yolk absorption, heart rate, cardiac contractility, and intersegmental vessel development. Transcriptomic analysis revealed upregulation of genes associated with sarcomere structure, calcium signaling, and energy metabolism, consistent with increased cardiac function and vascular development. Further investigation demonstrated that ES upregulated the expression of GATA4; GATA4 knockdown reduces hiPSC-CMs differentiation, while its inhibitor 3i 1000 abolishes ES enhanced zebrafish heart contractility. These findings indicate that GATA4 plays a significant role in the regulation of cardiac differentiation and heart development by ES.

Conclusion

ES promotes early cardiac cell differentiation and cardiovascular development by enhancing energy metabolism, associated with increased GATA4 related transcriptional activity. These findings offer mechanistic insights into bioelectrical cardiac development, laying a foundation for regenerative therapies for congenital and early-stage heart diseases.

title: Cardiac stem cells as a source of myocardial regeneration.
authorString: Payushina O, Pykhanova V, Tsomartova D, Chereshneva E, Kartashkina N, Tsomartova E, Kosobutskaya S, Zharikova T, Pires LAS, Pontes-Silva A, Zharikov Y.
abstractText: According to traditional concepts, cardiac muscle tissue is considered incapable of regeneration at the cellular level because it does not contain cambial elements that could replace lost cardiomyocytes. As a result, various myocardial injuries result in closure of the defect with a connective tissue scar, followed by the development of heart failure. However, the results of some studies over the past two decades indicate the presence of a heterogeneous population of stem and progenitor cells in the heart. Available data indicate that these cells can facilitate the restoration of pathologically altered myocardium by differentiating into its cellular components (endothelial cells, vascular smooth muscle cells, and possibly cardiomyocytes) or by exerting a paracrine regulatory influence on damaged tissue. The discovery of cardiac stem cells has opened new perspectives in the treatment of various heart diseases. At the same time, data on their regenerative potential, particularly regarding their ability to differentiate into cardiomyocytes, are controversial, and the therapeutic efficacy of their transplantation in patients remains questionable. In particular, new methods of genetic lineage-tracing have revealed that the c-kit and Sca-1 markers, traditionally used for sorting cardiac stem cells, predominantly identify endothelial lineage cells lacking cardiomyogenic potential. This review examines the phenotypic and functional characteristics of different cardiac stem cell populations, their localization in the heart, age-related dynamics, changes in pathological conditions, as well as mechanisms of their pro-regenerative effects, and potential clinical applications.

title: Measles pneumonia, pneumomediastinum, pneumothorax, and pneumopericardium in an infant: a rare association in an epidemic context.
authorString: Oudrhiri Safiani M, Zarouali H, El Harrak S, Ed Dafali L, Ziani H, Ennafiri M, Bentalha A, El Koraichi A, Ech Cherif El Kettani S.
abstractText:
Background

Measles is a highly contagious viral infection that most often affects unvaccinated children. The most frequent manifestation is respiratory involvement, which can progress to severe forms such as measles pneumonia. Air leak syndrome, comprising pneumomediastinum, pneumothorax, and pneumopericardium, is an exceptional and life-threatening complication that can precipitate respiratory failure.

Case presentation

We report the case of a five-month-old infant with measles pneumonia, further complicated by an Air leak syndrome consisting of pneumomediastinum, pneumothorax, and pneumopericardium. The association of measles pneumonia on the one hand and pneumothorax, pneumomediastinum, and pneumopericardium on the other is exceedingly rare, with only a limited number of similar cases described in the literature. Despite appropriate respiratory support, the infant died after forty-eight hours.

Conclusion

Through this case, we revisit the underlying pathophysiology of measles pneumonia and air leak syndrome, the diagnostic approach, and the various therapeutic options. This case report highlights the importance of early recognition of Air leak syndrome and the central role of vaccination in preventing this serious disease.
