title: Metabolic and Signaling Pathways of Macrophage Reprogramming in Atherosclerosis and Myocardial Infarction.
authorString: Ding Z, Wang Y, Chen S, Yu L.
abstractText: Atherosclerosis and myocardial infarction remain the predominant contributors to mortality despite advances in interventional cardiology. Chronic inflammatory responses mediated by macrophages serve as a critical determinant of the pathogenesis of cardiovascular diseases. This review systematically dissects the immunometabolic and signaling networks underlying macrophage reprogramming, with a focus on key cardiovascular diseases. We assess the characteristics of M1 macrophages, which involve aerobic glycolysis, activation of the pentose phosphate pathway, and disruption of the tricarboxylic acid cycle, compared to M2 macrophages that rely on oxidative phosphorylation and fatty acid oxidation. Integrated signaling pathways dynamically regulate these metabolic programmes-centred on TLR/NF-κB-mediated inflammatory priming, JAK/STAT-dependent transcriptional polarization, and PI3K/Akt/mTOR-AMPK-PPARγ metabolic checkpoints, which interpret microenvironmental signals to control macrophage polarization. Within atherosclerotic lesions, we demonstrate that M1-dominant macrophage populations exacerbate plaque inflammation and compromise structural integrity, whereas M2 macrophages augment inflammatory resolution and tissue restoration. Following myocardial infarction, the timely therapeutic reprogramming from M1 to M2 phenotype is essential for efficiently attenuating adverse cardiac remodeling and improving cardiac function. Targeting metabolic enzymes and signaling pathways offers a promising strategy for reprogramming macrophages and mitigating cardiovascular diseases.

title: Multi-omics analysis identifies the super-enhancer-driven gene NPW in left-sided obstructive lesions-associated cardiac remodeling.
authorString: Qian Z, Yang C, Wu Y, Zhao Y, Huang J, Li Y, Li X, Yu Y, Lu Y.

journal.title: Cellular and molecular life sciences : CMLS

abstractText: Left-sided obstructive lesions (LSOLs), represented by coarctation of the aorta (CoA), cause persistent vascular pathology and pressure overload that can lead to pathological cardiac remodeling. However, the epigenetic changes associated with local vascular abnormalities and ventricular remodeling remain incompletely understood. We performed H3K27ac chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing (ChIP-seq) and RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) in paired aortic tissues from patients with CoA to characterize region-associated super-enhancer (SE) landscapes and transcriptional alterations. Integrated multi-omics analysis, together with single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) from LSOLs patients, identified neuropeptide W (NPW) as a SE-associated candidate. c-JUN CUT&RUN-qPCR showed AP-1 enrichment at successfully amplified NPW-associated SE regions (Peak1). In primary smooth muscle cells (SMCs), broad BET inhibition or NPW silencing was associated with reduced contractile-marker expression, whereas exogenous NPW attenuated angiotensin II-induced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy in vitro. Plasma NPW levels were lower in patients with CoA and were associated with echocardiographic indices of remodeling. These findings identify NPW as a SE-associated candidate pathway in CoA and provide supportive evidence for broader relevance to LSOLs-associated cardiac remodeling.

title: Percutaneous management of atrial flow regulator thrombosis in failing Fontan: a case report.
authorString: Quarta MT, Piccinelli E, Rebonato M, Pilati M, Butera G.
abstractText:
Background

Concomitant thrombosis of the Fontan conduit and atrial flow regulator highlights the marked prothrombotic milieu characteristic of failing Fontan circulation.

Case summary

We report a case of a 12-year-old with double inlet left ventricle, malposition of the great arteries, and aortic arch hypoplasia who underwent single ventricle palliation with Fontan completion at the age of 7 years. Over the following years, he developed protein-losing enteropathy associated with ascitic and pleural effusions; therefore, fenestration of the Fontan conduit was performed using an atrial flow regulator. Despite anticoagulation therapy with rivaroxaban, thrombosis of the atrial flow regulator occurred 1 month after implantation. The device was retrieved after multiple attempts using a grasping forceps, but conduit thrombosis occurred. Fenestration stenting was performed, and thromboaspiration was successfully performed, protecting the systemic circulation with a balloon inflated across the fenestration. At the 6-month follow-up, the patient remained haemodynamically stable, with a patent fenestration and no evidence of visceral effusions.

Discussion

This case underscores the challenges of managing device-related thrombosis in patients with failing Fontan circulation and demonstrates the potential role of a fully percutaneous treatment strategy.

title: AI assistance for fetal ultrasound interpretation in a multi-reader study.
authorString: Morisset C, Logé-Munerel F, Corda G, Besson R, Amabile C, Khalil A, Stirnemann J, Oyelese Y, Ville Y.
abstractText: Prenatal detection rates of congenital anomalies range from 25 to 90%. Artificial intelligence (AI) may improve detection by supporting physicians during image interpretation. We performed a multireader, multicase retrospective study of Sonio Suspect (FDA‑cleared, K243614; Paris, France) detecting 8 fetal abnormal ultrasound findings on still images: malposition of the great vessels, absence or unusual size of at least one of the three vessels, disequilibrium or absence of at least one of the two ventricles, thoracic situs inversus, abdominal situs inversus, non-visibility of a single stomach bubble or abnormally big stomach, absence of the cavum septum pellucidum, absence of the corpus callosum. Thirteen U.S. physicians (maternal-fetal medicine, obstetrics/gynecology, radiology) reviewed 750 images (250 with abnormal findings) once unassisted and once with AI. With AI assistance, AUC presented a mean improvement of 21.9 percentage points (68.9% to 90.9%, p < 0.001). With AI, sensitivity was overall improved (88.5% vs. 54.2%, p < 0.01), as was specificity (87.9% vs. 80.7%, p < 0.01), inter-reader agreement (72% vs 26%) and interpretation time (23 vs 40 s per image). AI assistance significantly improved reader performance in detecting fetal abnormalities without compromising specificity.

title: Dilatation of the ascending aorta in bicuspid aortic valve patients with and without concomitant aortic coarctation.
authorString: Wulffeld S, Schmiegelow MDS, Oksjoki R, Nielsen DG, Raunsoe J, Bruun NE, Procida K.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Eur Heart J Valvular Struct Heart Dis
journal.title: European heart journal. Valvular and structural heart disease
journal.isoabbreviation: Eur Heart J Valvular Struct Heart Dis

abstractText:
Background

In bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) aortopathy, concomitant aortic coarctation and bicuspid aortic valve (cBAV) is considered an aggravating risk factor which may indicate earlier prophylactic intervention. This assumption is challenged by recent studies in children or young adults, reporting smaller aortic diameters in cBAV patients compared with those with isolated BAV (iBAV) disease, but these findings should be confirmed in adult patient populations.

Aims

To assess the association between aortic coarctation and aortic dilatation in adult BAV patients.

Methods and results

In a prospective cohort study, we included 141 cBAV patients and 828 iBAV patients from outpatient clinics. Maximal diameters of the aortic root and tubular ascending aorta were measured on transthoracic echocardiograms. Aortic diameters, significant aortic dilatation at baseline (≥50 mm or Z-score ≥ 4), and annual aortic growth rates were compared between groups taking possible confounders into account. Compared with iBAV patients, cBAV patients had smaller crude and adjusted diameters (adjusted mean difference: -3.27 mm [-4.49 mm; -2.05 mm]) and a lower likelihood of significant aortic dilatation at baseline (adjusted odds ratio [95% confidence interval]: 0.55 [0.30; 1.01], P = .05). We observed no differences in aortic root dimensions or in aortic growth rates between cBAV and iBAV patients.

Conclusions

cBAV was associated with less pronounced dilatation of the tubular ascending aorta in adult BAV patients.

title: Fibrosis Without Macrocalcification: A Novel <i>In Vitro</i> Model to Study Aortic Valve Disease.
authorString: Le Nezet E, Marqueze-Pouey C, Vaillancourt K, Couture V, Côté N, Clavel MA.
abstractText:
Background

The absence of medical treatment for fibrocalcific aortic valve stenosis (FCAVS), despite its high incidence in high-income countries, emphasizes the need to discover novel therapeutic targets. Given the sex-specific differences in fibrotic and calcific pathways in FCAVS, in vitro approaches capable of independently dissecting these 2 processes must be developed. In this project we aim to characterize a new medium able to induce fibrosis specifically in valvular interstitial cells (VICs).

Methods

Human VICs were isolated from 10 explanted tricuspid aortic valves (5 men and 5 women) and treated with fibrotic and fibrocalcific media for 0, 7, and 14 days.

Results

As expected, the fibrotic medium increased fibrotic markers (elevated procollagen I, procollagen III, and matrix metalloproteinase-2 levels), whereas the fibrocalcific medium induced calcification (decreased total Ca2+ levels in supernatants and increased calcific nodules detected by Alizarin Red staining) associated with mild fibrosis, in both male and female VICs (elevated procollagen I and procollagen III levels) without major sex-specific differences.

Conclusions

This novel fibrotic medium allows for the independent analysis of fibrotic pathways, distinct from calcification ones, in male- and female-derived VICs. The minimal sex-specific differences within each media suggest that sex-specific differences in FCAVS may be driven more by the surrounding milieu than by intrinsic cellular sex. This medium may help improve our understanding of the pathophysiologic processes underlying FCAVS.

title: Menstrual, Reproductive, and Menopausal Histories of Female Patients with Cardiovascular Disease: A Cross-Sectional Study.
authorString: Goulets D, Quansah DY, Mir H, Kodua AT, Edwards J, Heshka J, Parast N, Koopman Z, Mullen KA.
abstractText:
Background

Female-specific factors may influence cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk; however, their distribution across different CVD diagnoses is not well characterized. This study examined associations between female-specific health factors and CVD subtype among female patients with established CVD.

Methods

This cross-sectional study included female patients aged ≥ 18 years with a diagnosis of CVD who received care at the University of Ottawa Heart Institute between June 2022 and December 2023. Participants were categorized by primary diagnosis: arrhythmia, coronary artery disease (CAD), cardiomyopathy, congenital heart disease, heart failure, valvular heart disease, peripheral vascular disease, or cerebrovascular disease. We examined the associations between female-specific factors and each diagnosis, compared with all other CVD diagnoses and adjusted for age.

Results

Among the 2228 respondents, the most common diagnoses were arrhythmia (30.8%) and CAD (27.7%). Early menarche was more common among participants with CAD (odds ratio [OR] 1.60, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.11-2.31). Irregular menstrual cycles were more common among female patients with congenital heart disease (OR 1.43, 95% CI 1.01-2.02). Female patients with CAD also had greater odds of having gestational diabetes (OR 1.94, 95% CI 1.29-2.90), hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (OR 1.52, 95% CI 1.08-2.12), and premature menopause (OR 1.36, 95% CI 1.01-1.83). Migraine was associated with peripheral vascular disease (OR 1.97, 95% CI 1.18-3.29), and vasomotor menopausal symptoms were frequently reported by female patients with cerebrovascular disease (OR 2.45, 95% CI 1.10-5.49).

Conclusions

Female-specific reproductive and hormonal factors differed across CVD diagnoses among female patients with established CVD. These findings highlight the importance of incorporating reproductive and hormonal history into cardiovascular risk assessment, and they support the need for further research on sex-specific pathways underlying various CVD subtypes.

title: Cause of death in a contemporary cohort of patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension.
authorString: Papadopoulos GE, Arvanitaki A, Ziampa K, Mouratoglou SA, Chrysochoidis-Trantas T, Simitsis P, Demerouti E, Karyofillis P, Tsiapras D, Frogoudaki A, Mpatsouli A, Dima E, Zimpounoumi-Keratsa PN, Anthi A, Zacharias A, Pitsiou G, Frantzeskaki F, Tsangaris I, Bechlioulis A, Naka KK, Stamatopoulou V, Mitrouska I, Leontsinis I, Brili S, Ritsatos K, Manginas A, Skoularigkis I, Anastasiadis G, Giannakoulas G.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Eur Heart J Valvular Struct Heart Dis
journal.title: European heart journal. Valvular and structural heart disease
journal.isoabbreviation: Eur Heart J Valvular Struct Heart Dis

abstractText:
Background

In pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), contemporary risk tools primarily estimate all-cause mortality, offering limited insight into what patients die from.

Aims

We aimed to characterize cause of death across baseline mortality risk strata and to examine baseline factors associated with PAH-related versus non-PAH-related death in a national PAH cohort.

Methods and results

Adult patients with Group 1 PAH registered in the Hellenic Pulmonary Hypertension Registry (2015-2024) were classified according to ESC/ERS three-strata risk score at baseline. Cause of death was adjudicated as PAH-related or non-PAH-related and further categorized. We modelled cause-specific mortality using competing-risk models with prespecified predictors. Model performance was summarized by discrimination and calibration. Among 462 patients followed for a median (IQR) of 2.2 (5.7) years, 163 deaths occurred; cause was adjudicated in 149 cases (55% PAH-related, 45% non-PAH-related). PAH-related deaths increased across risk strata, whereas the pattern of non-PAH causes did not differ significantly. Sepsis was the leading non-PAH cause. In multivariable competing-risk analyses, higher baseline risk for mortality and male sex independently aligned with PAH-related death, while older age aligned with non-PAH death. Discrimination was acceptable: AUC 0.77 (95% CI 0.70-0.83) for non-PAH death and 0.75 (95% CI 0.68-0.80) for PAH-related death. Integrated Brier score (IBS) improved versus null models, and calibration was good across the central predicted-risk distribution.

Conclusion

In contemporary PAH, what patients die from differs by baseline risk. PAH progression dominates in high-risk patients, whereas competing causes, especially sepsis, remain influential across strata. Cause-specific modelling may refine counselling, prevention, and resource allocation beyond all-cause risk alone.

title: Evolution of echocardiographic changes in aortic stenosis and the association with rapid valvular progression.
authorString: Venema CS, van Bergeijk KH, Panaou K, Krikken JA, Trenkwalder T, Joner M, Mordi IR, Lang CC, Girerd N, Clavel MA, Lipsic E, Voors AA, Wykrzykowska JJ.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Eur Heart J Valvular Struct Heart Dis
journal.title: European heart journal. Valvular and structural heart disease
journal.isoabbreviation: Eur Heart J Valvular Struct Heart Dis

abstractText:
Background

Data on the chronological progression of myocardial changes during the course of aortic stenosis remain limited. In addition, it is unknown whether faster progression of aortic stenosis is associated with accelerated myocardial remodelling.

Aims

To describe the evolution of structural and functional echocardiographic changes over time in patients with moderate aortic stenosis and evaluate the association with rapid valvular progression.

Methods and results

In this retrospective longitudinal study, we included patients with a diagnosis of moderate aortic stenosis and serial echocardiograms. Changes in echocardiographic variables over time were analysed using linear mixed-effects models. This study included 467 patients with moderate aortic stenosis (median age 69 years, 36% female) with 2806 echocardiograms (median of six per patient). Over a median follow-up of 4.3 years, 47% of patients developed severe aortic stenosis. Most echocardiographic variables changed linearly over time, with impaired relaxation, concentric remodelling and left atrial dilatation occurring early. Concentric hypertrophy developed only after aortic stenosis became severe. Rapid valvular progression was weakly associated with the rate of myocardial changes. Rapid progression of left ventricular mass index was accelerated by comorbidities and was associated with an increased risk of heart failure hospitalizations.

Conclusions

During progression of aortic stenosis, left atrial dilatation and impaired relaxation occur early, whereas concentric hypertrophy is a late finding. Rapid valvular progression is only weakly associated with enhanced myocardial remodelling, which is accelerated by comorbidities.

title: The contemporary and historical burden of arrhythmias in patients with congenital heart disease.
authorString: Eckerström F, Dellborg M, Kok WG, Eriksson P, Mandalenakis Z.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Eur Heart J Valvular Struct Heart Dis
journal.title: European heart journal. Valvular and structural heart disease
journal.isoabbreviation: Eur Heart J Valvular Struct Heart Dis

abstractText:
Background

Arrhythmias constitute a significant concern in patients with congenital heart disease (CHD) but temporal trends remain unknown.

Aims

To describe the burden of arrhythmias and dissect the impact of era of birth, lesion complexity, and age in both children and adults with CHD born in Sweden.

Methods and results

In a population-based cohort study, patients diagnosed with CHD (n = 63 431) born in 1970-2017 were identified in the Swedish National Patient Register. Each patient was matched by age and sex with 10 control subjects (n = 583 100) from the general population. Fine-Gray competing risk and Cox proportional-hazards regression were used; risk estimates were compared with matched controls. During median follow-up of 19 years (total range: 0-53 years), 1895 new events of supraventricular arrhythmias were registered, yielding a hazard ratio (HR) of 8.0 [95% confidence interval (CI) 7.6-8.5], along with 371 new ventricular arrhythmias (HR 13.0; 95% CI 11.2-15.2). Complex CHD was associated with higher risk, irrespective of type, than non-complex CHD, and patients born in 1990 or later displayed lower risk for both supraventricular and ventricular arrhythmias, irrespective of age and CHD complexity, than those born before 1990. Patients aged 18-39 years with non-complex and complex CHD born before 1990 displayed HRs of 6.9 (95% CI 6.1-7.8) and 23.9 (95% CI 19.4-29.5) for supraventricular arrhythmias, respectively, versus 3.2 (95% CI 2.7-3.9) and 13.9 (95% CI 9.8-19.7) in those born in 1990 or later.

Conclusions

The risk of arrhythmias was generally high across the CHD population and increased with increasing age and lesion complexity. Importantly, patients born in 1990 or later demonstrated lower risk for both supraventricular and ventricular arrhythmias than those born before 1990.

title: SPARK score: comprehensive risk stratification in patients with moderate aortic stenosis.
authorString: Godino C, Gaspardone C, Besana D, Romagnolo D, Tripoli A, Morosato M, Raone L, Oro P, Sparasci FM, Barone G, Mazza R, Ancona F, Fiore G, Ingallina G, Margonato D, Gatto P, Beneduce A, Buzzatti N, Denti P, Melillo F, Ferlini M, Agricola E, Maisano F, Margonato A.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Eur Heart J Valvular Struct Heart Dis
journal.title: European heart journal. Valvular and structural heart disease
journal.isoabbreviation: Eur Heart J Valvular Struct Heart Dis

abstractText:
Background and aims

Patients with moderate aortic stenosis (AS) have an increased risk of adverse cardiovascular (CV) outcomes. The present study aimed to identify the predictors of adverse CV outcomes in patients with moderate AS and combine them in a new scoring system suitable for risk stratification.

Methods and results

This multicentre, retrospective study enrolled consecutive patients diagnosed with moderate AS at three Italian centres between 2019 and 2023. The primary endpoint was a composite of CV death or heart failure (HF) hospitalization. Patients who developed severe AS during follow-up were censored to restrict the analysis to moderate AS-related events.The study included 520 patients (mean age 78 ± 9 years; 46% female). During a mean follow-up of 2.0 ± 0.9 years, 59 patients (11.4%) experienced the primary endpoint. The independent predictors of primary endpoint were as follows: (1) lateral E/e' > 14 (HR 4.35, 95% CI 2.63-7.7; P < .001), (2) LVEF <50% (HR 3.39, 95% CI 1.98-5.81, P < .001), (3) PASP >40 mmHg (HR 1.99, 95% CI 1.17-3.39, P = .011), (4) Hb <13 mg/dL (HR 1.94, 95% CI 1.01-3.79, P = .049), and (5) eGFR <45 mL/min (HR 1.87, 95% CI 1.07-3.27, P = .028). A new scoring system (the SPARK score) was developed and internally validated based on these variables (high- vs. low-risk SPARK score: HR: 7.3; 95% CI 4.4-12.3; P < .001).

Conclusions

The SPARK score, based on accessible clinical, laboratory, and echocardiographic parameters, offers a practical approach to tailor risk stratification in moderate AS patients with initial signs of myocardial damage. Further studies are required to evaluate its impact on clinical outcomes.

title: Clinical characteristics, treatment strategies, and outcomes of patients with aortic valve infective endocarditis with and without aortic root abscess: insights from the NIDUS registry.
authorString: Stybe T, Alhakak A, Graversen PL, Hadji-Turdeghal K, Bruun NE, Møller JE, Petersen JK, Jensen AD, Povlsen JA, Moser CE, Smerup M, Jensen HS, Jørgensen PG, Østergaard L, Bundgaard H, Iversen K, Køber L, Linde JJ, Fosbøl EL.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Eur Heart J Valvular Struct Heart Dis
journal.title: European heart journal. Valvular and structural heart disease
journal.isoabbreviation: Eur Heart J Valvular Struct Heart Dis

abstractText:
Background and aims

Aortic root abscess is a severe and diagnostically challenging complication of infective endocarditis (IE). This study aimed to examine differences between IE patients with and without aortic root abscesses in patient characteristics, treatment strategies, and clinical outcomes.

Methods

We conducted nationwide, unselected, registry-based cohort study using National Danish Endocarditis Studies registry. All patients with aortic valve endocarditis in Denmark from 2016 to 2021 were included. Clinical and microbiological characteristics, treatment, and mortality were compared according to status of aortic root abscess. Mortality was adjusted for clinically relevant covariates.

Results

The study population included 1902 patients with aortic endocarditis, of whom 316 (17%) had an aortic root abscess. Patients with an abscess versus those without were significantly younger (median 71.5 vs 75.1 years, P-value ≤.001), more often male (76.3% vs. 69.7%, P-value = .02), prosthetic valve (50.0% vs. 30.4%, P-value ≤.001), AV-block (10% vs 1.7%, P-value ≤.001), coagulase-negative staphylococci and streptococci in their blood cultures, and were surgically treated (59.5% vs 16.1%). In multivariable Cox regression, patients with abscesses had significantly higher 1-year mortality rate compared with those without (HR 1.41, 95% CI: 1.13-1.76). When stratifying for surgery, non-operated patients with an abscess had the highest 1-year mortality 55.4%, alongside a high pre-operative risk (median age 79, 38% not self-reliant, more comorbidities including 12% active cancer).

Conclusions

Aortic root abscess was present in 17% of patients with aortic valve endocarditis and was associated with distinct clinical and microbiological characteristics, a higher frequency of complications, greater prevalence of surgery albeit a higher mortality rate compared with those without an abscess.

title: Tricuspid regurgitation is a barrier to guideline-directed medical therapy implementation in patients with acute decompensated heart failure and reduced ejection fraction.
authorString: Brollo E, Cocianni D, Barbisan D, Perotto M, Contessi S, Rizzi JG, Savonitto G, Zocca E, Soranzo E, Chiarini A, De Luca A, Merlo M, Sinagra G, Stolfo D.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Eur Heart J Valvular Struct Heart Dis
journal.title: European heart journal. Valvular and structural heart disease
journal.isoabbreviation: Eur Heart J Valvular Struct Heart Dis

abstractText:
Background

Guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) reduces mortality in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), but multiple barriers prevent the correct implementation of recommended treatments.

Aims

We sought to evaluate the role of tricuspid regurgitation (TR) as an obstacle for GDMT implementation in a cohort of HFrEF patients after an episode of acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF).

Methods

We enrolled patients hospitalized for ADHF with left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) ≤ 40%. TR severity was categorized as moderate-severe or trivial-mild. Optimization of renin-angiotensin system inhibitors/angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitors (RASi/ARNi), beta-blockers and mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (MRA) therapy was defined when patients were prescribed these drugs at ≥50% of the target dose (TD) at 1-year follow-up.

Results

858 patients were enrolled. At 12 months, patients receiving ≥50% TD of RASi/ARNi, beta-blockers and MRA were 51%, 29%, and 47% respectively. After adjustment for multiple confounders, moderate-severe TR was inversely associated with the likelihood of ≥50% TD up-titration of RASi/ARNi (OR = 0.572, P = .029) and of beta-blockers (OR = 0.526, P = .038), but not of MRA (OR = 0.995, P = .984). RASi/ARNi and beta-blockers optimization was associated with lower 1- and 5-years all-cause mortality risk regardless the severity of TR. The association between RASi/ARNi optimization and 5-years survival was more pronounced in patients with moderate-severe TR vs patients with trivial-mild TR (P for int = .039).

Conclusions

The severity of TR in ADHF is a determinant of poor implementation of RASi/ARNi and beta-blockers therapy at 1-year follow-up; however, the lower mortality associated with treatment optimization was not influenced by TR severity.

title: Clinical practical advice for anaesthetic management of adults with congenital heart disease undergoing non-cardiac surgery: A clinical consensus statement of the ESC Working Group on Adult Congenital Heart Disease, the European Society of Anaesthesiology and Intensive Care, the European Association of Cardiothoracic Anaesthesiology and Intensive Care and the International Society of Adult Congenital Heart Disease.
authorString: Dos-Subirà L, Rijs K, Ribas-Ball M, Brida M, Clift P, Diller G, Gatzoulis M, Heggie J, Longrois D, Meier S, Prieto-Arévalo R, Ranucci M, Rex S, Ruperti FJ, Schindler E, Von Dossow V, Roos-Hesselink J.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Eur Heart J Valvular Struct Heart Dis
journal.title: European heart journal. Valvular and structural heart disease
journal.isoabbreviation: Eur Heart J Valvular Struct Heart Dis

abstractText: Adult congenital heart disease (ACHD) patients often require non-cardiac surgery (NCS) and the need of such interventions is growing as the population ages. The intricacies inherent to their distinct physiology pose ACHD patients at a higher risk of perioperative complications, perioperative mortality, longer length of stay, and higher hospital charges compared with the general population. While 2020 ESC guidelines comprehensively address most aspects of ACHD care, they do not cover this specific area. Furthermore, although risk assessment for non-cardiac surgery is included in the 2022 ESC Guidelines on Cardiovascular Assessment and Management of Patients Undergoing Non-Cardiac Surgery, the unique pathophysiology of ACHD patients necessitates tailored considerations. The aim of this clinical consensus statement is to address the specific situations and needs of ACHD patients undergoing NCS from a multidisciplinary and practical point of view and to describe the organization of care for this complex group of patients. A group of experienced professionals from 4 cardiology and anaesthesiology scientific societies [the ESC Working Group on ACHD, the European Society of Anaesthesiology and Intensive Care (ESAIC), the European Association of Cardiothoracic Anaesthesiology and Intensive Care (EACTAIC), and the International Society of Adult Congenital Heart Disease (ISACHD)] have evaluated the available scientific data and reached expert consensus in areas of gaps in evidence.

title: Frequency of Readmission of Pediatric Patients With Respiratory Diseases in the PIMS Hospital of Pakistan: A Study of Cause and Effect.
authorString: Ahmad N, Chauhan AN, Huda M, Abbas A, Qamar NU, Shah FA, Ahmad R, Yasmeen N.
abstractText:
Background

Hospital readmission with respiratory diseases among pediatric population remains the leading concern for healthcare services due to their increased morbidity, burden on healthcare and resource utilization. Understanding the factors related to readmission may help improve outcomes and lessen preventable hospitalization. This study was conducted to determine the rate of rehospitalization among pediatric population and to identify the risk factors for hospital readmission.

Methods

A retrospective cross-sectional study of pediatric patients with respiratory diseases was conducted at a tertiary care hospital in Pakistan from 1st January 2024 to 31st December 2024. Data was collected from a medical record through a structured proforma. Variables like age, gender, diagnosis, severity of disease, previous hospitalization, compliance to treatment, and length of stay in hospital were analyzed. Statistical analysis was performed using SPSS 27 version.

Results

During the study period, there were 2123 pediatric admissions among which 583 admissions were related to respiratory diseases. In the duration of one month (30-days), the readmission rate in total pediatric admissions was 6.92%. Readmissions were significantly associated with younger age, compliance to the treatment, disease severity, and previous hospitalization. Among respiratory diseases, bronchiolitis, pneumonia, and asthma were significantly associated with readmission.

Conclusion

Pediatric respiratory readmissions were significantly associated with younger age, disease severity, poor treatment compliance, and previous hospitalization.

title: Machine Learning in Neonatal Respiratory Distress Syndrome: From Early Warning to Clinical Translation.
authorString: Fadavi N, Mansouri SS, Fakhimi-Derakhshan K, Soflaee M, Shahhosseini B, Mirhaghjoo ZS, Pourghasem M, Vajari AH, Bahrami R, Neamatzadeh H.
abstractText: Neonatal respiratory distress syndrome (NRDS), driven by pulmonary surfactant deficiency in preterm infants, is a leading cause of neonatal morbidity and mortality. This narrative review synthesises machine learning (ML) applications across the NRDS spectrum-from prenatal risk stratification to long-term complication prediction-appraised against the TRIPOD+AI (2024) framework. Reported discrimination is high but heterogeneous (AUC 0.78-0.99); the most robust estimate is the prospective Korean Neonatal Network study of 13,087 very-low-birthweight infants across 76 hospitals (full-model AUROC 0.9187; testing 0.9216). Ensemble methods and deep-learning architectures tend to outperform logistic regression, often by modest margins. Emerging modalities-lung-ultrasound radiomics, cry-signal analysis (∼95% accuracy, controlled datasets), and ATR-FTIR spectroscopy-remain research-stage. Reporting deficits are near-universal: <20% report calibration, none conduct prospective fairness audits, <15% release code. Clinical translation requires federated-learning consortia, explainable AI, prospective external validation, and structured implementation science.

title: Current Status of Fetal Cardiac Care in Germany from a Pediatric Cardiology Perspective: A Consensus Statement on Behalf of the Fetal Cardiology Working Group of the German Society of Pediatric Cardiology.
authorString: Linden K, Kovacevic A, Junge C, Heilmann A, Rammes S, Hecht T, Wacker-Gussmann A, Herberg U.
abstractText: Fetal cardiology has become an important subspecialty in Pediatric Cardiology. It includes prenatal detection of congenital heart defects and arrhythmia as well as prenatal therapeutic procedures, planning of perinatal management, and the important part of parental counseling. Currently available methods to diagnose congenital heart disease prenatally, major requirements for parental counseling, available prenatal treatment options, and perinatal care of fetuses and newborns are outlined. A risk-stratified level of care classification system is proposed. This consensus statement of the Fetal Cardiology Working Group of the German Society of Pediatric Cardiology gives an overview about the current status of fetal cardiology in Germany from a Pediatric Cardiology perspective emphasizing that detection rates in Germany stay behind in international comparison due to the minimal requirement of displaying a 4-chamber-view only in screening guidelines according to the "Mutterschaftsrichtlinie." We require mandatory views of the outflow tracts and the 3-vessel-trachea view in the 19 to 22 weeks' examination.

title: The role of Clinical Valve Coordinators: a clinical consensus statement of the European Association of Percutaneous Cardiac Interventions and the Association of Cardiovascular Nursing & Allied Professions of the ESC.
authorString: Lauck SB, Højberg Kirk B, McCalmont G, Frank D, de Ronde-Tilmans M, Kelly F, Praz F, Rudolph T, Audren A, Hee C, Calvo E, Durand E, Wundram S, Saia F, Germinal F, Longoni M, Akodad M, Grygier M, Gilard M, Muir DF.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Eur Heart J Valvular Struct Heart Dis
journal.title: European heart journal. Valvular and structural heart disease
journal.isoabbreviation: Eur Heart J Valvular Struct Heart Dis

abstractText:
Background

Transcatheter options are increasingly available for the treatment of valvular heart disease. The role of the clinical valve co-ordinator is ideally positioned to improve access to care, quality of outcomes, and patient experiences, contribute to efficiencies, and support the growing number of heart valve centres. International societies and guidelines recommend the inclusion of the clinical valve co-ordinator in multidisciplinary Heart Teams to support patients, contribute unique expertise to team-based care, and help programmes expand access to care. The role of the clinical valve co-ordinator is unevenly adopted in Europe.

Aims

To provide guidance on developing, implementing, and sustaining the role of clinical valve co-ordinators to support patients and programmes.

Methods and results

We outline a comprehensive framework of the competencies and professional development aligned with the needs of patients with aortic, mitral, and tricuspid disease, discuss requirements for infrastructure and successful organizational integration in valvular heart disease teams and programmes, and propose preliminary indicators to measure role impact and address the current gap in evidence to guide role development across diverse regions. The clinical valve co-ordinator plays a vital role as a central member of the multidisciplinary team to support the care requirements of people with complex valvular heart disease in the rapidly evolving clinical context of treatment options and management strategies.

Conclusion

The document provides a roadmap for the development, implementation, and evaluation of a pan-European initiative to improve the delivery of valvular heart disease services and optimize the experience of care of patients and their family.

title: Skeletal phenotype in patients with diabetes and chronic kidney disease: the sweeter it is, the slower it goes.
authorString: Duque EJ, Moysés RMA.

title: Postoperative Acute Kidney Injury in Children Undergoing Major Non-Cardiac Surgery: Protocol for a Multicentre Study (POAKIDS).
authorString: Emami A, La Porta E, Jungner Å, Andersson A, Thorlacius EM, Luther T, Frykholm P, Neto LFS, Modiri AR, Lindestam U, Brynolf A, Quintão VC, Stubelius I, Bastianello M, Petrov I, Kralik S, Bouvet L, Stankovic N, Becke-Jakob K, Bertolizio G, Engelhardt T, Riva T, Fuchs A, Malagon I, Ekstein M, von Ungern-Sternberg BS, Larsson A, Disma N, Vutskits L, Frithiof R.
abstractText:
Background

Acute kidney injury (AKI) is associated with increased mortality and adverse long-term outcomes. Postoperative AKI is a common and recognised complication after surgery in adults. In children, AKI following paediatric cardiac surgery has been extensively studied. However, the incidence and characteristics of postoperative AKI after non-cardiac surgery in children remain poorly defined, with existing evidence largely derived from retrospective and single-centre studies.

Methods

POAKIDS is an international, multicentre, prospective observational study including hospitalised children aged 0-16 years undergoing major non-cardiac surgery under general anaesthesia. Postoperative AKI will be defined according to the Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO). The primary outcome is the incidence of postoperative AKI. Secondary objectives include evaluation of established and novel urinary biomarkers as predictors of postoperative AKI and exploration of perioperative potential predictors of renal injury. The maximal follow-up is seven postoperative days. Sample size is based on the incidence estimate, with a planned inclusion of 2000 patients. Data will be analysed using descriptive statistics, agreement analyses, and exploratory regression models.

Discussion

This study aims to provide robust prospective data on the incidence of postoperative AKI in children undergoing major non-cardiac surgery and to improve understanding of perioperative renal injury in this population. By combining standardised AKI definitions with systematic biomarker assessment, the results are expected to inform future preventive strategies and guide the design of interventional studies targeting postoperative renal injury in paediatric perioperative care.

title: Effects of probiotic supplementation on serum zonulin levels in patients with chronic kidney disease: a randomized clinical trial.
authorString: Autran HSL, Pinto DQM, Brito EHS, Meneses GC, Lopes NC, Almeida IM, Araújo KMDR, Furtado JFCU, Ribeiro PVC, Aguiar ROA, Pierre DP, Feitosa ID, Silva Junior GBD.
abstractText:
Introduction

Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is associated with intestinal dysbiosis, systemic inflammation, and impaired intestinal barrier function. Serum zonulin has been proposed as an indirect marker of intestinal permeability, although its clinical relevance in CKD remains uncertain.

Objective

To evaluate the effect of probiotic supplementation on serum zonulin levels in patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis.

Methods

In this randomized, placebo-controlled, triple-blind clinical trial, 40 hemodialysis patients were assigned to receive either a probiotic formulation or a placebo for six months. The primary outcome was the between-group difference in change in serum zonulin from baseline to follow-up. Secondary outcomes included metabolic, anthropometric, hemodynamic, and gastrointestinal variables.

Results

Serum zonulin increased in both groups, with no significant between-group difference (placebo: 288.2 to 425.3 ng/mL; probiotic: 239.5 to 453.7 ng/mL; p = 0.882; ANCOVA p = 0.463). Pre-dialysis urea decreased within the probiotic group, but the between-group difference was not significant (p = 0.305). Serum phosphorus showed a greater reduction in the probiotic group than in the placebo group (p = 0.011; ANCOVA p = 0.011). No significant differences were observed for anthropometric or hemodynamic outcomes.

Conclusion

Six months of probiotic supplementation did not significantly reduce serum zonulin levels in hemodialysis patients. Although a favorable effect on serum phosphoruswas observed, these findings do not support a measurable impact of this probiotic regimen on serum zonulin and highlight the need for larger studies incorporating direct assessments of intestinal permeability and gut microbiota.

title: Acute Effects of Two Warm-Up Protocols on Sprint Interval Swimming Performance and Physiological Responses in Trained Athletes: Implications for Swimming Training Practice.
authorString: Dalamitros AA, Semaltianou E, Dopsaj M, Martín-Rodríguez A, Zhou Z, Aguilera JFT, Manou V.
abstractText: This study examined the acute effects of two practice-based warm-up (WU) protocols on sprint interval swimming performance, physiological and perceptual responses, and stroke characteristics. Fifteen competitive swimmers (World Aquatic Points: 611.2) completed two randomized sessions. Following a 1200 m general WU, swimmers performed either a critical-speed protocol (CSp; 8 × 50 m) or a sprint-interval protocol (SIp; 4 × 15 m maximal efforts). After 4 min passive recovery, swimmers completed a main interval set (MIS; 2 × 4 × 25 m maximal swims). Muscle oxygen saturation (SmO<sub>2</sub>), heart rate (HR), blood lactate concentration (BLa), and rating of perceived exertion (RPE) were recorded at three testing points. Swimming time, fatigue index (FI), velocity decrement (Vdec), and total stroke count (TS) were assessed during the MIS. No significant protocol main effect was detected for MIS time, FI, Vdec, SmO<sub>2</sub>, or HR; however, MIS time showed a protocol × set interaction (p = 0.024), and TS was higher following SIp (p = 0.025). BLa values across testing points were 3.80 ± 1.61, 8.17 ± 2.39, and 10.53 ± 3.64 mmol·L<sup>-1</sup> following CSp, and 4.20 ± 1.45, 11.61 ± 2.60, and 12.77 ± 2.48 mmol·L<sup>-1</sup> following SIp (time and protocol effects: p < 0.001; protocol × time interaction: p = 0.006). RPE was higher following SIp (p < 0.05). The protocols elicited different metabolic and perceptual responses and performance trajectories across sets, without a significant overall protocol effect on swimming time. Coaches may select WU configurations according to the intended metabolic and perceptual stimuli.

title: Exploring the Nephroprotective Potential of Plants: A Comprehensive Review of Bioactive Compounds.
authorString: Rauf F, Javied S, Wahid M, Ahsan MZ, Munir AB, Mubarak MS.

journal.title: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology

abstractText: Kidneys are important in maintaining physiological homeostasis by regulating fluid balance and removing metabolic waste. However, chronic diseases and exposure to nephrotoxic agents can impair renal function, leading to progressive kidney damage. The literature search was conducted on published articles from 2000 to 2025 using the keywords nephroprotection and plant-derived compounds. Kidney diseases occur in more than 850 million people globally, and it is estimated that the disease will be among the leading causes of death by 2040, which demonstrates an increasing public health issue. Plant-based therapies are also emerging as potential nephroprotective agents due to their diverse bioactive compounds and relatively good safety profiles. Bioactive compounds, especially flavonoids and other polyphenolic compounds, have been shown to have renoprotective effects by acting as antioxidants, anti-inflammatory agents, and cytoprotectants. Such compounds have shown positive results in preclinical models and a few clinical trials. Moreover, recent developments in drug delivery systems have enhanced the bioavailability and therapeutic effects of plant-based compounds. Although these results are encouraging, several obstacles stand in the way of their clinical implementation. These are the lack of human studies, inadequate pharmacokinetics, unstandardized preparations, and inadequate long-term safety information. Finally, plant-based nephroprotective strategies hold promise for therapeutic development. However, well-designed clinical trials are essential to validate their safety, efficacy, and applicability in human populations. This review critically assesses the therapeutic value of medicinal plants and their phytochemicals in the treatment of kidney diseases.

title: A dual-mechanism framework for imbalanced right ventricular ejection fraction estimation from 2D echocardiography.
authorString: Dong S, Wang N, Sun Y, Hu X, Zhao Y, Wang G, Luo G.
abstractText:
Background

Right ventricular ejection fraction (RVEF) is a clinically essential indicator of right ventricular systolic function and a well-established predictor of outcomes in cardiovascular disease. Reduced RVEF is strongly correlated with adverse clinical events such as heart failure progression, recurrent hospitalization, and increased mortality. Accurate and reliable estimation of RVEF is therefore crucial for risk assessment and guidance of treatment strategies.

Purpose

Addressing the problem of imbalanced regression in RVEF estimation, we introduce a dual-mechanism framework that improves both robustness and generalization when learning from two-dimensional echocardiography (2DE) videos.

Methods

Our approach integrates Gaussian Kernel Constrained Mixup, which expands and smooths the training distribution via structured sample synthesis, and Feature Space Calibration, which imposes ordinal constraints on the latent representation using weighted contrastive learning. This combined strategy enhances both data efficiency and feature-label consistency across the entire value range. The well-trained model can be seamlessly integrated into clinical workflows to assist physicians in rapid patient screening. It enables efficient, high-throughput analysis of echocardiographic videos, providing reliable RVEF estimates that help identify high-risk patients at an early stage and support large-scale preliminary screening in resource-limited settings.

Results

On the RVENet dataset comprising 3583 echocardiographic videos, our method achieved state-of-the-art performance with a mean absolute error (MAE) of 4.03±3.23% and an R2 of 0.67. Evaluation on an independent external test cohort of 128 videos demonstrated generalization, with an MAE of 3.71±2.54% . Stratified analysis confirmed consistent performance across diverse RVEF ranges, indicating robustness to imbalanced data distribution.

Conclusions

The proposed framework effectively tackles data imbalance and regression bias in RVEF estimation through dual mechanisms that improve both sample diversity and feature discriminability. It exhibits good accuracy, generalizability, and balanced performance across the RVEF spectrum. The implementation of our approach is publicly available at https://github.com/Wnssl/DIRVEF.

title: Association of Type of Anti-Hypertensive With Unplanned Healthcare Utilization After Delivery Among Individuals in a Postpartum Remote Hypertension Monitoring Program.
authorString: Echeng N, Talbot S, Konecke N, Machado S, Jackson TL, Hunt W, Simmons D, Meija-Castillo M, Smith HA, Grobman WA, Hauspurg A, Tuuli MG, Lewkowitz AK.
abstractText:
Objective

Nifedipine and labetalol are commonly prescribed first-line antihypertensive medications for patients with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP), although outcomes related to their use may differ. Prior studies suggest that nifedipine may reduce rates of postpartum readmission compared with labetalol; however, whether this association persists in the setting of remote blood pressure monitoring is unclear. We aimed to evaluate whether unplanned healthcare utilization differed among participants in a postpartum remote monitoring program who were prescribed nifedipine versus labetalol.

Study design

Postpartum patients with HDP at our tertiary care hospital are offered enrollment in a remote self-measured blood pressure (SMBP) program. This prospective observational cohort analysis included patients with HDP who were prescribed nifedipine alone or labetalol alone during the delivery hospitalization or after discharge. Patients receiving combination therapy or other antihypertensive agents were excluded. The primary outcome was a composite of postpartum readmission or emergency department (ED) presentation for hypertension-related reasons within 30 days of delivery hospitalization. Secondary outcomes included hypertension-related severe maternal morbidity (SMM) after discharge, adherence measures, and sustained engagement with the SMBP program. Adjusted relative risks were estimated using generalized linear models controlling for maternal age and HDP diagnosis.

Results

Among 2,644 patients enrolled in the SMBP program, 571 were prescribed either labetalol alone (n=143; 25%) or nifedipine alone (n=428; 75%). In multivariable analysis, the risk of the composite outcome of hypertension-related postpartum readmission or ED presentation was similar between those prescribed labetalol versus nifedipine (18% vs 17%; adjusted relative risk 1.07, 95% CI 0.65-1.77). Secondary outcomes were also similar between groups.

Conclusion

In our remote SMBP program for postpartum patients with HDP, there was no difference in the risk of hypertension-related unplanned healthcare utilization between those prescribed labetalol alone and those prescribed nifedipine alone. These findings suggest that within a structured postpartum SMBP program, antihypertensive choice alone may matter less than the monitoring framework itself.

title: Deep learning reconstruction for low-dose thoracic CT of calcification inserts: A phantom study of CNR, noise magnitude, and noise texture.
authorString: Hsiao YY, Lu CC, Kao HC, Chen TR.

journal.title: Journal of applied clinical medical physics

abstractText:
Purpose

To compare filtered back projection (FBP), 50% Adaptive Statistical Iterative Reconstruction-Veo (ASiR), and medium-strength deep learning image reconstruction (DLIR) for hydroxyapatite calcification inserts under different dose, tube-voltage, and phantom-size conditions using contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR), background noise magnitude, and noise power spectrum (NPS) analysis.

Methods

A QRM-Thorax containing a QRM-CCI D100 cardiac calcification insert was scanned on a GE Revolution Apex CT system using institution-defined routine and low-dose protocols at 80, 100, 120, and 140 kVp, with and without an Extension Ring L. Images were reconstructed at 2.5-mm thickness using FBP, ASiR, and DLIR. CNR was evaluated for 3- and 5-mm inserts at 200, 400, and 800 mg HA/cm3. Background noise was assessed from a calcification-excluded mask. For NPS analysis, 10 calcification-free images were analyzed for each acquisition condition. Total two-dimensional NPS power, power-weighted normalized radial NPS, and power-weighted mean spatial frequency were calculated.

Results

DLIR reduced background noise magnitude and increased CNR relative to FBP across the evaluated conditions, whereas differences relative to ASiR varied with insert size, density, tube voltage, and phantom size. Across all 16 protocol, phantom-size, and tube-voltage combinations, ASiR and DLIR reduced total 2D NPS power by 58.1% and 75.8%, respectively, relative to FBP; DLIR reduced total power by 41.9% relative to ASiR. ASiR produced a more consistent shift toward lower power-weighted mean spatial frequencies, averaging 12.4% below FBP, whereas the shift with DLIR was smaller and more condition dependent, averaging 3.2% below FBP.

Conclusions

In this controlled phantom study, DLIR reduced total noise power and improved CNR relative to FBP, but its incremental difference from ASiR was task and protocol dependent. CNR and noise magnitude should be interpreted together with NPS because nonlinear reconstruction methods can alter both noise magnitude and spatial-frequency distribution.

title: Body Composition by Dual-Energy X-Ray Absorptiometry and Cardiometabolic Health in 46 044 Multi-ethnic Asian Adults.
authorString: Wang X, Xie W, Mina T, Low DY, Lam B, Sadhu N, Jain PR, Ng HK, Tay D, Loh M, Ngeow J, Elliott P, Riboli E, Lee ES, Lee J, Best J, Wansaicheong G, Chambers J.

journal.title: Journal of cachexia, sarcopenia and muscle

abstractText:
Background

Body composition varies by age, sex, and ethnicity and is associated with cardiometabolic health. We aimed to characterise the distributions of body composition indices and their relationships to cardiometabolic health among 46 044 adults from three major Asian ethnic groups living in an urban Asian setting.

Methods

The Health for Life in Singapore (HELIOS) study is a population-based prospective cohort of multi-ethnic Singapore citizens or permanent residents aged 21-85 years. Using cross-sectional baseline dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) data, we assessed age, sex, and ethnic variation in eight body composition indices, including fat mass index, visceral adipose tissue (VAT) mass, trunk/limb fat ratio, android/gynoid fat ratio, lean mass index, appendicular lean mass index, appendicular lean mass/body mass index (BMI) and fat/lean mass ratio. Percentile curves were generated using generalised additive models for location, scale and shape. Associations between sex- and ethnicity-specific deciles of each index and modified metabolic syndrome score were evaluated using linear regression.

Results

Among 37 290 Chinese, 3733 Malays and 5021 Indians recruited in 2018-2026, women had higher fat mass index (mean: 9.67 vs. 7.84) and fat/lean mass ratio (0.75 vs. 0.49), but lower values in other indices than men (all p < 0.001). Across Asian ethnic groups, Chinese had lowest fat mass index (mean: 8.49 vs. 10.73 vs. 11.0 in Chinese, Indians and Malays), VAT mass (567 vs. 691 vs. 654), appendicular lean mass index (5.84 vs. 6.37 vs. 6.59), and fat/lean mass ratio (0.62 vs. 0.76 vs. 0.74) but higher trunk/limb fat ratio (1.14 vs. 1.09 vs. 1.04, all p < 0.001). These ethnic variations were most evident at higher BMI. VAT mass, trunk/limb fat ratio, android/gynoid fat ratio, and fat/lean mass ratio increased with age ( r : 0.08 to 0.28), whereas lean mass parameters decreased with age ( r : -0.19 to -0.13, all p < 0.001). Most parameters were positively associated with modified metabolic syndrome score, whereas appendicular lean mass/BMI showed an inverse association. Across deciles of all parameters evaluated, Chinese had lower levels of modified metabolic syndrome score (all p < 0.003) than Indians and Malays.

Conclusions

DXA-derived body composition varied substantially by ethnicity, particularly at higher BMI, and was associated with graded differences in metabolic risk. Chinese consistently showed lower risk than Indians and Malays across adiposity deciles. These findings support ethnicity-specific interpretation of cardiometabolic risk and highlight the need for further research to establish clinically meaningful target ranges for the prevention of cardiovascular and metabolic diseases.

title: Development of a slice-specific ct dose library with interpolation methods for organ dosimetry in MIRDct.
authorString: Baggett JM, Dinwiddie LE, Dawson RJ, Ramos JCO, Kayal G, Carter LM, Kesner AL, Bolch WE.

journal.title: Journal of applied clinical medical physics

abstractText:
Objectives

To develop a slice-specific dose library and supporting interpolation scheme for proper estimation of organ doses from CT scans based on the UF/MSK mesh-type adult and pediatric phantom series.

Methods

Monte Carlo (MC) simulations were performed using the Particle and Heavy Ion Transport code System (PHITS) for selected adult female and pediatric male phantoms across a user defined CT source term. Dose profiles were calculated on a 1-cm slice basis and categorized by tissue type (distributed vs. non-distributed). Linear interpolation of slice doses within a height series was evaluated using multiple phantom subsets and compared against MC results.

Results

Slice-by-slice linear interpolation produced total organ dose estimates within 5% of MC values for most studied tissues, with all errors below 7%. Mean errors for abdomen, chest-abdomen-pelvis and cardiac scan ranges were also below 5%, and mean errors for individual slices were below 3%. The method performed well across various interpolation schemes, especially when phantoms were selected based on similar construction methods.

Conclusions

This approach enables accurate, scalable organ dose estimation with reduced computational demands. The resulting dose library and interpolation method will be integrated into the MIRDct platform, a dosimetry tool for calculating total organ dose values across a wide range of CT parameters. MIRDct is freely available to the medical imaging community at MIRDsoft.org.

title: A meshfree method for robust evaluation of wall shear stress in patient-specific vascular geometries.
authorString: Starakas SV, Bourantas GC, Lampropoulos DS, Sakellarios A, Katsakiori PF, Fotiadis DI, Sbalzarini IF, Kagadis GC.
abstractText:
Background

Wall shear stress (WSS) is an important hemodynamic marker of vascular disease, yet its accurate estimation in patient-specific geometries remains challenging. Because WSS is derived from the velocity gradient at the vessel wall, it is highly sensitive to how well the near-wall region is resolved. Finite-volume simulations on unstructured meshes can therefore yield inaccurate WSS values unless dedicated boundary-layer meshes are used, a difficulty that is amplified in complex, image-derived geometries where variations in vessel shape and curvature complicate gradient reconstruction at the wall. Methods that reconstruct wall velocity gradients accurately on irregular point distributions, without relying on specialized near-wall meshing, are therefore needed.

Purpose

We present the meshfree Discretization-Corrected Particle Strength Exchange (DC PSE) methodology for accurate wall shear stress (WSS) computation in patient-specific vascular geometries represented by unstructured point clouds.

Methods

The proposed framework reconstructs spatial derivatives directly on irregular node distributions. The methodology is validated using fully developed Poiseuille flow, for which analytical solutions for both velocity and WSS are available. The proposed scheme is applied to transient blood flow simulations in patient-specific arterial geometries reconstructed from medical imaging. Mesh refinement convergence studies were performed to verify the accuracy and numerical robustness of the proposed approach. Velocity fields were computed by solving the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations using the OpenFOAM finite-volume solver, while WSS was evaluated from the reconstructed wall velocity gradients using the proposed DC PSE formulation. Numerical predictions were compared with WSS obtained directly from OpenFOAM.

Results

The proposed methodology accurately reproduced the analytical WSS distribution for the benchmark problem, achieving a normalized root mean square error (NRMSE) of 1.2×10-4 , compared with 1.2×10-2 obtained with OpenFOAM post-processing tools using a reference finite-volume solution. The reconstructed velocity derivatives remained stable on irregular point distributions. In patient-specific blood flow simulations, the proposed framework produced smooth and physically consistent WSS distributions throughout the cardiac cycle, accurately resolving regions of elevated and low shear associated with vessel curvature and bifurcations.

Conclusions

The DC PSE framework provides an accurate, robust, and computationally efficient approach for WSS estimation in image-based cardiovascular Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) simulations. By improving the reconstruction of wall velocity gradients on complex geometries, the proposed methodology substantially enhances the accuracy of wall-derived hemodynamic metrics without requiring specialized boundary-layer meshes. The method offers a flexible post-processing framework that can be readily integrated into existing CFD pipelines and has significant potential for patient-specific cardiovascular modeling and computational medical physics applications.

title: Dose‑dependent image quality behavior of recently introduced clinical deep learning CT reconstruction methods.
authorString: Meier JG, Somasundaram E, Brady SL.

journal.title: Journal of applied clinical medical physics

abstractText:
Background

Deep learning reconstruction (DLR) algorithms are increasingly used in CT to reduce image noise and support radiation dose reduction. However, DLR methods may alter spatial resolution and noise texture depending on dose level, reconstruction kernel, matrix size, and vendor implementation.

Purpose

To characterize how decreasing radiation dose affects noise magnitude, noise texture, and task-based spatial resolution for two recently available clinical CT deep learning reconstruction algorithms: Canon Precise IQ Engine (PIQE) super-resolution DLR and GE HealthCare TrueFidelity DLR.

Methods

The American College of Radiology CT accreditation phantom was scanned on an Aquilion ONE/INSIGHT Edition scanner (Canon Medical Systems USA) and a Revolution Apex scanner (GE HealthCare) across 12 dose levels. CTDIvol ranged from 0.7 to 20.0 mGy for Canon and from 0.68 to 20.46 mGy for GE. Canon images were reconstructed using filtered back projection (FBP) with a 512 matrix and PIQE Levels 1-3 with Body, Lung, and Cardiac kernels using a 1024 matrix. GE images were reconstructed using FBP and TrueFidelity low, medium, and high strengths with Standard, Lung, Bone, and Bone Plus kernels using a 512 matrix. Task-based spatial resolution was evaluated using the task transfer function (TTF). Noise magnitude and texture were evaluated using the noise power spectrum (NPS), including the Noise Magnitude Ratio (NMR), defined as the square root of the ratio of NPS areas between the DLR and the FBP reference, and the Central Frequency Ratio (CFR), defined as the ratio of the center of gravity of the NPS between DLR and FBP, reflecting noise texture shifts.

Results

At a high-dose comparison of 16.0 mGy for Canon and 16.43 mGy for GE, PIQE produced kernel-dependent changes in bone TTF50% relative to matched FBP, ranging from a 21.3% decrease to a 83.6% increase across kernels and DLR strengths. TrueFidelity increased bone TTF50% relative to matched FBP moderately across all evaluated kernels and strengths, with changes ranging from 3.7% to 14.7%. As dose decreased, PIQE TTF50% and TTF10% decreased substantially across evaluated kernels and inserts, whereas TrueFidelity TTF values remained relatively stable. PIQE produced lower NMR values than TrueFidelity. With decreasing dose, PIQE also demonstrated decreasing NMR and CFR values, indicating greater relative noise reduction accompanied by a shift toward lower-frequency noise texture.

Conclusions

PIQE and TrueFidelity demonstrated distinct dose-dependent image quality behavior. PIQE provided substantial noise reduction and high task-based spatial resolution at higher dose levels, consistent with its 1024 matrix super-resolution implementation, but showed stronger dose dependence in TTF, NMR, and CFR. TrueFidelity demonstrated more stable spatial resolution and noise texture across dose levels, with more modest noise reduction. Although newer DLR algorithms demonstrate substantial potential for noise reduction, their effects on spatial resolution, noise magnitude, and noise texture must be characterized before aggressive dose reductions are implemented.

title: Cyanidin-3-O-Glucoside Attenuates Articular Cartilage Damage in Experimental Osteoarthritis and Is Associated With Nrf2/HO-1 Signaling.
authorString: Lu J, Ru Q, Lian Y, Liu Y, Guo X, Yu Z.

journal.title: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology

abstractText: Cyanidin-3-O-glucoside (C3G) has antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activity, but its effects in experimental osteoarthritis (OA) remain unclear. We investigated C3G-associated responses in IL-1β-stimulated rat chondrocytes and in rats with monosodium iodoacetate (MIA)-induced OA. Matrix-based proteomic profiling was used to characterize treatment-associated protein-expression changes and to prioritize candidates for targeted experiments. In chondrocytes, C3G partially attenuated IL-1β-associated loss of viability and reduced inflammatory and oxidative-stress markers. C3G treatment was associated with increased NRF2 nuclear accumulation and increased HO-1 and NQO1 expression, whereas NRF2 knockdown attenuated these in vitro responses. In the MIA-induced OA model, C3G treatment was associated with lower OARSI scores, increased COL2A1 and ACAN expression, and reduced MMP13 and ADAMTS5 expression. These findings support the involvement of NRF2-associated signaling in the in vitro response to C3G, but do not establish the upstream mechanism of NRF2 regulation or NRF2 dependence in vivo.

title: Electrophysiological "Brain Power" Dissipation: MEG Model-Dependent Power Estimates and Regional Metabolic Correlates.
authorString: Nathan V, Hoeltershinken M, Hill E, Wolters CH, Baillet S.
abstractText: The human brain is often described as remarkably energy efficient, with its metabolic power consumption estimated at approximately 20 watts (W). Biophysical models partition this metabolic budget across cellular processes, including neuronal signaling. However, the electrical power dissipated by the synchronized cortical activity measurable with noninvasive electrophysiology remains unknown and should not be equated with total cortical energetic demand. Here, we used magnetoencephalography (MEG) source imaging of resting-state activity to estimate electrical power dissipation in cortical gray matter. Across 30 participants, mean total primary power summed over the modeled cortical source space was 6.6 × 10<sup>-9</sup> W. We interpret this value as an empirical, model-dependent power estimate for the synchronized component of cortical activity accessible to MEG, rather than as an estimate of total cortical power. Targ‑eted sensitivity analyzes and order-of-magnitude checks suggested that the tested methodological choices could shift the estimate by approximately one to two orders of magnitude, but not enough to bridge the gap with metabolic benchmarks. Under a magnitude-based root-mean-squares approximation, finite-element estimates of secondary-current dissipation were approximately 30% of primary power in four central-tendency exemplars. Spatial patterns of MEG-derived power showed associations with PET-derived oxygen metabolism and transcriptomic maps of ketone metabolism, with heterogeneous effects across functional networks. These results define the scope and limitations of MEG-derived electrophysiological power estimates and motivate multiscale models linking synchronized electrical activity to regional metabolism.

title: Foot Conditions in Community-Dwelling Older Adults: Prevalence, Sex Differences and Associated Factors in a Mediterranean Urban Cohort.
authorString: Torralba-Estellés J, Sales Castellanos C, Alarco Colera D, Garcia-Pando C.

journal.title: Journal of foot and ankle research

abstractText:
Background

Foot conditions are prevalent in older adults, but most prevalence estimates come from institutionalised cohorts or self-reported surveys, and examination-based evidence from community-dwelling Mediterranean populations is limited.

Methods

Cross-sectional study of 602 community-dwelling adults aged 65 years or older (74.4% women) examined at university podiatry clinics in Valencia, Spain. A 54-item questionnaire and a standardised examination of 16 foot conditions were completed. Associations were tested with chi-squared tests and, where appropriate, odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated to quantify the strength and precision of association. Multivariable logistic regression models were fitted for the four most prevalent conditions.

Results

The most prevalent conditions were callosities (66.6%), hallux valgus (59.3%), onychogryphosis (46.8%) and foot pain (42.2%). Eight conditions differed by sex (all p < 0.05): women had more callosities (74.6% vs. 43.5%) and hallux valgus (66.1% vs. 39.6%), and men had more hammer toe (37.0% vs. 25.0%) and onychomycosis (35.1% vs. 21.7%). A prior history of the same condition was the strongest associated factor, followed by female sex. In multivariable models (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve 0.74-0.83), regular physical activity was associated with lower odds of foot pain (adjusted OR 0.64, 95% CI 0.44-0.92) and onychogryphosis (0.69, 0.48-1.00), foot orthoses with lower odds of hallux valgus (0.37, 0.19-0.71) and onychogryphosis (0.24, 0.13-0.42), and diabetes mellitus with higher odds of onychogryphosis (3.32, 2.11-5.22).

Conclusions

Foot conditions affect most community-dwelling Mediterranean older adults and differ by sex. Regular physical activity and foot orthoses were associated with lower odds of specific conditions and are potentially modifiable targets, although the cross-sectional design precludes causal inference. These findings support routine podiatric screening of older patients.

title: Evolution of the Transplant Pharmacist Workforce in U.S. Solid Organ Transplant Programs: A 10-Year Follow-up National Survey.
authorString: Kaiser TE, Pilch NA, Trofe J, Taber D.

journal.title: Journal of the American College of Clinical Pharmacy : JACCP

abstractText:
Background

The roles and responsibilities of transplant pharmacists (TxPharms) continue to evolve. The aim of this survey was to obtain responses from individuals who identify as United States TxPharms and compare results with a similar 2013 survey.

Methods

Initial survey dissemination occurred electronically to American Society of Transplantation Pharmacy Community of Practice (AST TxPharm COP) and American College of Clinical Pharmacy (ACCP) Transplant Practice Research Network (PRN) members.

Results

Between November 2023 and May 2024, 173 TxPharms responded representing 102/249 of U.S. accredited transplant centers compared with 176 respondents representing 113/278 centers in 2013, at survey response time. The 2023 survey found that core competencies continue to expand in providing direct patient care across all phases of transplant and living donation care and organ types. Staffing limitations and payor/formulary/medication access issues were the most common practice barriers reported. The average job satisfaction rating was 71% (where 0% is not satisfied at all to 100% completely satisfied). When asked how likely in the next 12 months one was to leave clinical practice, 32% answered yes or maybe. In 2023, 93% (95/102) of centers reported full-time equivalent (FTE) numbers. The TxPharm FTEs per 100 cases based on total number of transplants performed per transplant center median (range) estimates showed little change between 2013 and 2023 (1.5 [0-21.4] vs. 1.4 [0.1-7.1]), despite significant increases in waitlisted patients, transplantation volumes, and expansion of ambulatory services compared with 2013.

Conclusion

Despite substantial growth in U.S. waitlist and solid organ transplant volumes over the past decade, TxPharm FTEs per 100 transplants showed little change between 2013 and 2023. Most TxPharms are satisfied with their jobs and responsibilities, but challenges include high workloads and workforce attrition. These findings highlight a widening mismatch between transplant activity and the available TxPharm workforce.

title: Dexmedetomidine Dosing Evaluation for Sedation in Neonates Undergoing Therapeutic Hypothermia.
authorString: Lo T, Kang HB, McNair C, Wilson D, Bizzarri J, Kalish BT, Tam EWY, Seto W, Chung E.
abstractText:
Objectives

Recently, dexmedetomidine has replaced opioids for sedation in neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) patients with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE). The study objectives were to describe dosing patterns, evaluate compliance, and compare effectiveness and safety between the original (pre-implementation) and revised (post-implementation) in-house dexmedetomidine dosing guidelines.

Study design

This was a retrospective cohort study that included neonates with HIE admitted to a level IV NICU for therapeutic hypothermia comparing two dexmedetomidine dosing regimens: (1) pre-implementation: starting dose of 0.05 μg/kg/h followed by titration by 0.05 μg/kg/h every 6 h as needed, and (2) post-implementation: 0.2 μg/kg/h followed by titration by 0.1 μg/kg/h every 30-60 min as needed.

Results

A total of 106 neonates were included: 50 in the pre-implementation group and 56 in the post-implementation group. Compliance to post-implementation formulary recommendations was 69.6% for initial doses, 62.5% for dose increases, and 44.6% for dose decreases. An increased odds of opioid exposure (adjusted odds ratio: 7.13, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.59-51.5, p = 0.02) and greater proportion of bradycardia (21.4% vs. 4%, p = 0.03) were observed in the post-implementation group. No significant differences in effectiveness end points or hypotension were observed between groups (p ≥ 0.05).

Conclusion

Compliance with formulary-recommended dexmedetomidine dosing was variable and dose decreases were common in the post-implementation group. The post-implementation dosing approach was not associated with improved effectiveness outcomes (sedation) but was associated with greater opioid exposure and more bradycardia, supporting the need for further prospective evaluation to determine the optimal dexmedetomidine dosing in neonates undergoing HIE.
