title: Update in alternative donor strategies in heart and lung transplantation.
authorString: Constable Y, Ngai J.
abstractText:
Purpose of review

Alternative donor strategies in cardiothoracic transplantation are becoming routine. This review covers recent developments and their implications for the anesthesiologist.

Recent findings

Donor scarcity is a principal constraint on heart and lung transplantation. Donation after circulatory death (DCD) and the adoption of machine preservation have reshaped the donor pool. This review covers literature comparing thoracoabdominal normothermic regional perfusion with direct procurement and preservation, warm ischemic thresholds and their relationship to primary graft dysfunction, normothermic and hypothermic ex-situ perfusion, 10 °C static cold storage, and ex-vivo lung perfusion, and discusses the ethics of DCD. Extended-criteria and hepatitis C virus-viremic donors are now used routinely, and cardiac xenotransplantation is entering clinical study. Each advance alters graft physiology at reperfusion and the timing of perioperative services. Research into cardiac xenotransplantation is ongoing.

Summary

These strategies enlarge the donor pool and introduce novel graft physiological concerns, as well as ethical concerns, for the anesthesiologist.

title: When Mnemonics Outlive the Evidence: Lessons From Acute Coronary Syndrome Across the Nursing Education Continuum.
authorString: Hutton DM.

journal.title: Journal of continuing education in nursing

abstractText:
Background

Clinical mnemonics are widely used in nursing education to simplify complex concepts and support knowledge acquisition, retention, and clinical recall. However, they may persist after the evidence that originally informed them has evolved.

Method

This discussion article draws on current literature, historical reflection, and more than three decades of cardiovascular teaching observations to examine the evolution and continued recognition of the acute coronary syndrome (ACS) mnemonics MONA, AMONTH, and NOAH.

Results

The discussion illustrates how these mnemonics reflected different stages in ACS management and how memorable educational tools may remain embedded in nursing education and practice despite changes in clinical evidence.

Conclusion

Clinical mnemonics should be periodically reviewed and revised to maintain alignment with contemporary evidence. The evolution of ACS mnemonics highlights broader implications for knowledge translation, curriculum renewal, and continuing professional development across the nursing education continuum.

title: Performance of Neurocritical Care Nurse Practitioners and Physician Assistants in Cardiac Arrest Scenarios After Simulation Training.
authorString: Harrison DS, Albin CSW, Woods EO, Mahajan R, Busler A, Aghajan Y, DiFancesco MF, Cricco-Lizza E, Blake A, Vollbrecht H, Webb AJ, Zafar SF, Bevers MB.

journal.title: Journal of continuing education in nursing

abstractText:
Background

This study was conducted to determine whether brief simulation training fosters competence in cardiac arrest management by neurocritical care (NCC) advanced practice providers (APPs).

Method

The NCC APPs completed pre-course knowledge and confidence assessments, then participated in a scored cardiac arrest simulation (pretest). Participants then practiced cardiac arrest leadership in an unscored simulation and completed post-course assessments. Then 4 to 8 weeks later, the APPs completed delayed assessments followed by a second scored cardiac arrest simulation (posttest).

Results

After the simulation course, one of 11 APPs passed the posttest. Knowledge and confidence scores improved on the immediate post-assessments (mean [standard deviation], 64% [14.2%] vs. 87% [9.0%], p = .001; median [range], 3.1 [2.3-4.1] vs. 3.8 [3.5-4.4], p = .02) without decay at the delayed post-assessments.

Conclusion

This brief simulation exercise did not foster competence in cardiac arrest management for most NCC APPs. Alternative strategies to develop cardiac arrest management competence among NCC APPs should be investigated.

title: Rehospitalizations after acute myocardial infarction in patients diagnosed by coronary angiography - the MADDEC study.
authorString: Aitokari LJ, Vuorinen J, Hernesniemi J.
abstractText: Objectives. The rate of rehospitalizations and fatal adverse events after myocardial infarction (MI) is reportedly high in previous studies and reducing these events is considered an important goal. This study aimed to clarify the rate of serious events leading to hospitalization or death after invasively managed MI in a contemporary setting. Design. In a retrospective registry study, the rate of serious adverse events leading to rehospitalizations or death during the first year after MI was examined from Tampere University hospital records. Study population consisted of all consecutive MI patients who underwent coronary angiography at Tays Heart Hospital between 2012 and 2016. This study focused on bleeding events, cerebrovascular events, exacerbation of heart failure, recurrent MI and unstable angina pectoris leading to rehospitalization. Results. During the five-year period, 2904 consecutive patients were treated for MI and successfully discharged or transferred to a primary health care unit (95.5% of all patients). 4.8% of these patients died during the first year after MI with 66.2% of all deaths due to cardiac causes, fatal bleeds, infections, or cerebrovascular events. Of all patients, 17.8% were rehospitalized for these causes and adding events leading to death without rehospitalization, the rate of serious events was 18.8%. Age but not sex, associated significantly with the rate of serious adverse events with the cumulative incidence exceeding 20% in patients aged 70-79 years and reaching 29% in patients ≥80 years. Conclusions. Cause-specific rehospitalization rates were low, but highly dependent on age.

title: Losartan use, left ventricular function and remodeling in hypertensive patients with aortic stenosis: the HYTAS prospective comparative cohort study.
authorString: Abdoun K, Demers K, Pibarot P, Tastet L, Ali M, Salaun E, Poirier P, Powers A, Dahl J, Beaudoin J, Clavel MA.

journal.title: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging

abstractText:
Purpose

Hypertension is highly prevalent in patients with aortic stenosis (AS) and contributes to adverse left ventricular (LV) remodeling. We investigated the association between losartan treatment and LV remodeling and function in hypertensive patients with mild-to-moderate AS.

Methods

In this prospective comparative cohort study, 18 AS patients receiving losartan were individually matched with 18 controls from the PROGRESSA cohort not receiving renin-angiotensin system inhibitors. Patients underwent echocardiographic assessment at baseline and two years. Between-group changes were compared within matched pairs, with baseline-adjusted sensitivity analyses.

Results

All losartan-treated patients completed follow-up without permanent treatment discontinuation or treatment-related serious adverse events. Systolic blood pressure decreased significantly within the losartan group, but the between-group difference in blood pressure changes was not significant (p = 0.17). Losartan was associated with a more favorable evolution of absolute global longitudinal strain (GLS), which persisted after baseline adjustment (adjusted between-group difference: +2.34%; 95% confidence interval 0.18-4.49; p = 0.04). Although LV end-diastolic diameter and relative wall thickness showed significant differences in unadjusted longitudinal analyses, these differences were no longer significant after baseline adjustment (p = 0.40 and p = 0.30, respectively). No significant between-group differences were observed in LV ejection fraction.

Conclusion

In this small, non-randomized prospective study of hypertensive patients with mild-to-moderate AS, losartan treatment was associated with a more favorable evolution of LV GLS over two years. Associations with LV remodeling were not significant after baseline adjustment. These exploratory findings do not establish causality or treatment safety and warrant confirmation in larger, adequately powered randomized controlled trials.

title: A pilot randomized feasibility trial of perioperative melatonin for cardiac arrhythmias during CPB weaning, sedative and analgesic medication use, and mechanical ventilation following CABG.
authorString: Mohebbi Z, Firouzbakht B, Hakiminia B, Askari A, Roozbakhshian N, Maharlui FM.

journal.title: Daru : journal of Faculty of Pharmacy, Tehran University of Medical Sciences

abstractText: Perioperative complications remain common following coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). Although melatonin may have cardioprotective and sedative-sparing effects, its feasibility and potential effects on early postoperative cardiac rhythm and recovery in patients undergoing CABG remain unclear. To assess the feasibility of a future definitive randomized controlled trial (RCT) of perioperative melatonin in patients undergoing on-pump CABG and to obtain preliminary estimates of its effects on cardiac arrhythmias during cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) weaning, duration of mechanical ventilation, and postoperative sedative and analgesic medication use. In this pilot randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled feasibility trial, 22 adults undergoing elective on-pump CABG were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive oral melatonin (3 mg) or placebo nightly, from three nights before to three nights after surgery. Feasibility outcomes included recruitment, retention, protocol adherence, completeness of outcome assessment, and intervention safety. Exploratory clinical outcomes included cardiac arrhythmias during CPB weaning, duration of mechanical ventilation, and postoperative sedative and analgesic medication use. Twenty-two participants were randomized. The recruitment rate was 68.75%, while retention, protocol adherence, and completeness of outcome assessment were all 100%; no treatment-related adverse events were observed. Arrhythmias during CPB weaning occurred in 2 of 11 participants (18.2%) in each group (OR, 1.00; 95% CI: 0.11-8.73). The median duration of mechanical ventilation was 9.5 hours with melatonin and 15.0 hours with placebo (Hodges-Lehmann estimate of the between-group location shift, -3.30 hours; 95% CI: -6.90 to 1.05). Postoperative sedative and analgesic medication use was generally comparable between groups, although the corresponding effect estimates were imprecise. Melatonin was feasible and well tolerated in this pilot cohort, with no treatment-related adverse events observed. The exploratory estimates were imprecise and do not provide evidence of efficacy, supporting a larger, adequately powered randomized trial to further evaluate the efficacy and safety of melatonin. IRCT20250206064666N1, date of registration: 2025-02-24.

title: Multimodal lifestyle strategies for ADT-induced osteosarcopenia and metabolic dysfunction in prostate cancer.
authorString: Ambrosio F, Persia M, Bellieni A, Tagliaferri L, Gambacorta MA, Frascino V, Abbatecola G, Landi F, Colloca GF.

journal.title: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer

abstractText: Androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) is associated with significant changes in body composition, promoting bone and muscle loss and increasing the risk of osteosarcopenia. This condition predisposes patients to adverse events such as falls, fractures, loss of functional autonomy, and increased cardiovascular risk, with possible repercussions on oncological outcomes and, in general, on patients' quality of life. This narrative review explores the available evidence on the role of exercise, nutrition, and the use of drug therapies in the prevention and management of ADT-induced osteosarcopenia, identifying the future perspectives in the integrated management of patients with prostate cancer undergoing hormone treatment. This review explores studies published over the last 15 years and aims to select scientific contributions concerning the effects of physical exercise, nutrition, or combined interventions on musculoskeletal health in subjects undergoing androgen deprivation therapy. Resistance training represents a promising non-pharmacological approach for the management of ADT-induced musculoskeletal alterations. Such programs have demonstrated efficacy in preserving lean body mass, potentially mitigating bone loss, and improving physical performance. While antiresorptive agents remain the primary intervention for bone preservation, lifestyle measures constitute an essential component of a multimodal approach to the care of patients undergoing ADT. Preventing ADT-induced osteosarcopenia is a critical challenge for the quality of life of men with prostate cancer. Current research and clinical care trends are moving toward flexible, integrated models that include exercise and nutrition in standard, patient-centered cancer care pathways. The early integration of these interventions into clinical pathways represents a concrete prospect for improving overall outcomes in patients with prostate cancer. Long-term randomized studies with functional and molecular endpoints are desirable to validate and personalize preventive strategies.

title: Treatment burden and long-term morbidity after transoral robotic vs. nonrobotic surgery for oropharyngeal cancer.
authorString: Choi N, Moon SJ, Park SH, Kim Y, Cheong TY, Shin DW, Kim HK, Oh D, Kang D.
abstractText: Transoral robotic surgery (TORS) is widely used in the surgical management of oropharyngeal cancer, yet its longer-term consequences beyond survival and perioperative care remain uncertain. We examined 4,173 patients who underwent surgery for oropharyngeal cancer using nationwide Korean National Health Insurance Service data from 2010 to 2023. Of these, 2,430 received TORS and 1,743 received nonrobotic surgery. Treatment groups were balanced using stabilized inverse probability weights. Blood transfusion occurred in 16.0% of the TORS group and 19.6% of the nonrobotic surgery group (OR = 0.77;95%CI = 0.66-0.91). Opioids were used within 30 days by 76.7% and 83.8% of patients, respectively (OR = 0.64;95%CI = 0.55-0.75). Postoperative radiotherapy within 180 days was recorded less often following TORS (HR = 0.84;95%CI = 0.78-0.91). Mortality did not differ materially between approaches (HR = 1.04;95%CI = 0.92-1.17). Aspiration or bronchopneumonia rates were 4.5 and 7.4 per 1,000 person-years after TORS and nonrobotic surgery, respectively (HR = 0.61;95%CI = 0.42-0.88). The corresponding rates for the composite psychiatric outcome were 38.9 and 46.9 per 1,000 person-years (HR = 0.83;95%CI = 0.71-0.97). These results indicate that comparison of robotic and nonrobotic surgery may be more informative when postoperative treatment burden and morbidity during survivorship are considered together with mortality. Residual confounding from unmeasured tumor characteristics remains possible.

title: Early childhood outcomes in survivors of congenital chylothorax: a single-centre retrospective cohort study.
authorString: Engelbert M, Le Duc K, Chopinet C, Thumerelle C, Gilliot S, Storme L, Boukhris MR.
abstractText: Congenital chylothorax is a rare neonatal condition and the most common cause of pleural effusion in neonates. Although neonatal morbidity and mortality have been described, outcomes beyond the neonatal period remain incompletely characterised. This study aimed to describe respiratory, developmental, and feeding outcomes during early childhood after congenital chylothorax. We conducted a single-centre retrospective cohort study including infants with congenital chylothorax managed at Lille University Hospital between 2011 and 2023. Cases were identified through an electronic database search and confirmed by individual medical record review. Follow-up data between 1 and 3 years of age included growth, respiratory symptoms and healthcare use, chylothorax recurrence, developmental outcomes, and feeding difficulties. Among 260 medical records screened, 34 infants with congenital chylothorax were included. Four died during the neonatal period. Follow-up data were available for 26 of the 30 survivors (87%) at a median age of 2.0 years [1.5-2.0]. Chylothorax recurred in one child (4%). Seventeen children (65%) received inhaled respiratory medications, 11 (42%) had respiratory symptoms, and 14 (54%) required hospital readmission. Developmental delay was identified in six children (23%) and feeding difficulties in four (15%). Nine children (35%) had no respiratory, neurodevelopmental, or feeding problems identified during follow-up. Chylothorax recurrence was uncommon during early childhood, whereas respiratory medication use and hospital readmissions were frequent. Developmental and feeding difficulties were also documented in a subset of survivors. Although these outcomes cannot be attributed solely to congenital chylothorax, the findings highlight the importance of structured multidisciplinary follow-up. • Congenital chylothorax is a rare neonatal condition associated with substantial neonatal morbidity and variable outcomes. • Data beyond the neonatal period remain limited and are derived mainly from small cohorts, with respiratory and neurodevelopmental outcomes incompletely characterised. • Chylothorax recurrence was uncommon during early childhood, whereas respiratory symptoms and healthcare use remained frequent. • Developmental and feeding difficulties affected a subset of survivors, while 35% had no respiratory, neurodevelopmental, or feeding problems identified during follow-up.

title: Extravascular Implantable Cardioverter-Defibrillators in Children: Real World Evidence.
authorString: Luxford JC, Khuong JN, Manning D, Asakai H, Turner C, Ayer J, Liava'a M, Lawley CM.
abstractText: The extravascular implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (EV-ICD) is a novel substernal ICD with limited reports in children and adolescents. Single-centre review of EV-ICDs in children <18-years. Clinical, peri-procedural, and electrocardiographic data reviewed, including device performance in routine exercise stress testing. Median follow-up 10.9 (IQR 7.5 - 12.5) months. Between April 2025-April 2026, 15 EV-ICDs were successfully implanted by a single cardiothoracic surgeon: median age 13.8-years, IQR 10.2-16.4; 11 (73%) male; weight 52 kg, IQR 38.2-64.1; BSA 1.6 m<sup>2</sup>, IQR 1.2-1.8. Smallest child was 4-years, 17.3 kg (BSA 0.7 m<sup>2</sup>). Indications were primary (n = 10) and secondary (n = 5) prevention. Underlying diagnoses included cardiomyopathy (n = 9), channelopathy (n = 3). One child had a previous sternotomy and another severe chest-wall deformity. Median anaesthetic time was 148 min (IQR 130-161), surgical time 68 min (59-88), fluoroscopy time 2.6 min (2.2-3.8). Median 3 (IQR 2-4) day hospitalisation. Two children experienced early complications. In one child, defibrillator threshold testing terminated ventricular fibrillation (VF) into ventricular tachycardia (VT) requiring CPR and a decision to use external cardioversion. The child fully recovered. One adolescent experienced profound bradycardia and syncope early post anaesthesia. R-wave amplitude at implant (5mV, IQR 4.2 - 6.7), discharge (5, IQR 2.8 - 8.1) and latest follow-up (5.8, IQR 3.2 - 13.7) was stable. Device sensing during routine exercise stress testing has been appropriate. There has been one successful appropriate high voltage therapy and no inappropriate high voltage therapy. This is the largest single-centre series internationally, demonstrating reliable paediatric EV-ICD implantation and short-term device performance. Ongoing paediatric surveillance is necessary.

title: Past, present and future of Estetrol (E4); a natural fetal estrogen for human use.
authorString: Coelingh Bennink HJT, Afors K, Douxfils J, Graziottin A, Benagiano G, Stanczyk FZ, Westhoff CL, Gemzell-Danielsson K.
abstractText: Estetrol (E4) is a natural estrogen produced by the fetal liver with a distinctive pharmacologic profile separating it from other natural and synthetic estrogens. Encompassing 25 years of research and development, this review summarizes the history, biochemistry, pharmacology, clinical development, and potential future applications of E4. Essential features of E4 are (1) its high oral bioavailability, long half-life and minimal binding to sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG), enabling once-daily oral use, and (2) the limited effects on liver function, especially on hemostatic factors, resulting in a lower risk of venous thromboembolism compared to other natural and synthetic estrogens. Estetrol is further characterized as a natural estrogen with selective tissue activity, with a limited impact on breast tissue and cardiovascular and metabolic parameters, while preserving efficacy including bone mass protection. Estetrol therefore has the potential for a markedly improved safety profile. Clinically, the E4/drospirenone (DRSP) combined oral contraceptive (COC) is available worldwide since 2022 and provides effective contraception, a predictable bleeding profile, and a favorable tolerability profile. In phase 2 and 3 studies in postmenopausal women, oral E4 improves vasomotor symptoms, vaginal and urogenital complaints, and quality of life and wellbeing. Ongoing research is exploring wider uses, including combination with the oral GnRH antagonist relugolix for a COC with a focus on the perimenopausal transition and possible applications of E4 in gynecology, endocrinology, obstetrics, neurology and oncology, especially the treatment of advanced breast and prostate cancer.

title: CCTA-derived anatomical features and exploratory risk stratification of severe stent-jailed left circumflex coronary artery narrowing for non-true left main bifurcation lesions.
authorString: Okutsu M, Kajiya T, Kurogi K, Nakano Y, Sadamatsu K, Fujimoto Y, Hasegawa K, Noji Y, Hozawa K, Nakamura S.

journal.title: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging

abstractText: Provisional stenting is recommended in percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for non-true left main bifurcation lesions (LMBLs); however, unexpected severe stent-jailed left circumflex coronary artery (LCX) narrowing is a clinical concern, and its prediction remains challenging. This study aimed to investigate anatomical features associated with LCX narrowing following provisional stenting for non-true LMBLs without significant LCX lesions and to derive an exploratory risk score using coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA). This was a multicenter retrospective observational study that enrolled patients who underwent CCTA before PCI for non-true LMBLs with provisional stenting from December 2019 to May 2024. Quantitative CCTA analysis of LMBL was performed, and severe stent-jailed LCX narrowing, defined as angiographic stenosis ≥90%, was assessed. Anatomical features associated with LCX narrowing were identified using multivariable analysis, and a CCTA-derived exploratory risk score was derived. Overall, 109 patients were recruited, 16 (14.7%) of whom had severe stent-jailed LCX narrowing. Multivariable analysis identified the following parameters as associated with LCX narrowing: left anterior descending artery-LCX vessel angle ≤86°, area stenosis (AS) of the distal LM (LMd) ≥54%, AS of the ostial LCX ≥63%, and calcium thickness of the LMd ≥0.5 mm. An exploratory risk score based on these four features showed a stepwise increase in the incidence of severe LCX narrowing, with a C-statistic of 0.877. CCTA identified anatomical features associated with severe stent-jailed LCX narrowing following provisional stenting. An exploratory risk score was derived from these features.

title: Integrated myocardial work phenotyping in professional football players and non-professional comparators.
authorString: Refoyo E, García-Yébenes M, Troya J, Celada OL, Villalón JM.

journal.title: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging

abstractText: To explore integrated cardiac profiles in professional football players and non-professional comparators and assess their sensitivity to demographic, body-size and haemodynamic differences. This cross-sectional analysis included 49 professional players (39 men, 10 women) and 48 hospital-staff comparators recruited as healthy volunteers (31 men, 17 women). Principal component analysis (PCA) of 28 standardised clinical, echocardiographic, deformation and myocardial-work measures preceded k-means clustering without study-group labels. Sensitivity analyses addressed age, sex, blood pressure, body-size indexing and exclusion of myocardial work while retaining global longitudinal strain (GLS). Five components explained 62.2% of variance. The three-profile solution had a silhouette coefficient of 0.252 and mean resampling adjusted Rand index (ARI) of 0.820. Profile A contained 55 participants, including 41 players (74.5%); profiles B and C contained 4/17 and 4/25 players. Profile A combined larger chambers with preserved global work efficiency; profile B had higher systolic and diastolic blood pressure, greater wasted work and lower efficiency. Age-adjusted and jointly age-, sex- and blood-pressure-adjusted analyses yielded agreement ARIs of 0.448 and 0.097. Without myocardial work, 95/97 participants and all 49 players retained profile membership (ARI 0.950). Integrated phenotyping identified overlapping cardiac profiles associated with professional football, principally reflecting chamber size, demographics and loading conditions. Myocardial-work indices described pressure-strain and efficiency patterns but had little additional influence on profile allocation beyond the remaining measures, including GLS. Their incremental clinical utility requires external validation.

title: Coronary artery calcium burden and coronary CT angiography evaluability in patients undergoing hemodialysis.
authorString: Masuda T, Nakaura T, Funama Y, Oku T, Okimoto T.

journal.title: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging

abstractText: To investigate the association between coronary artery calcium (CAC) burden and coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) evaluability in patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis. This retrospective single-center study included 65 patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis who underwent coronary artery calcium scoring and CCTA for evaluation of suspected coronary artery disease. The right coronary artery, left anterior descending artery, and left circumflex artery were independently assessed by two blinded observers using a four-point image-quality scale. Arteries scored 3 or 4 were considered evaluable, and limited evaluability was defined as at least one non-evaluable major coronary artery. Associations were assessed using Spearman correlation, established CAC-score categories, receiver operating characteristic analysis with bootstrap confidence intervals, and multivariable logistic regression. The median total CAC score was 671 (interquartile range, 251-1,774). All three major coronary arteries were evaluable in 26 patients (40.0%), whereas 39 (60.0%) had limited evaluability. Median CAC scores increased stepwise as the number of evaluable arteries decreased from three to zero (162.5, 677.0, 1,663.0, and 2,180.0; Spearman's ρ = -0.608, P < 0.001). CAC score ≥ 400 was associated with limited evaluability (odds ratio, 6.30; 95% CI, 2.10-18.90; P < 0.001). The AUC was 0.831 (bootstrap 95% CI, 0.723-0.925). After adjustment for age and sex, each approximate doubling of CAC score was associated with higher odds of limited evaluability (adjusted odds ratio, 2.01; 95% CI, 1.40-2.88; P < 0.001). Increasing CAC burden was associated with a progressive reduction in CCTA evaluability in patients undergoing hemodialysis. CAC scoring may help anticipate technical limitations of CCTA and inform coronary imaging strategy.

title: Effects of Dietary Supplements on Resolution Biology.
authorString: Martindale RG, Mundi MS, McClave SA.

journal.title: Current topics in microbiology and immunology

abstractText: Dietary supplements are consumed by up to 50-75% of the US population with omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) being one of the most consumed. These supplements can exert diverse and potential biologically beneficial effects on the resolution of inflammation. Despite the widely available literature in clinical chronic disease settings, the influence of dietary supplements on the resolution phase of inflammation has only recently been recognized. Resolution of inflammation is a biologically active, tightly regulated process partially mediated by endogenously synthesized specialized pro-resolving mediators (SPMs) that aid in restoration of cellular and tissue homeostasis without immune suppression. Among dietary supplements, omega-3 PUFAs, notably the 20-carbon eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) and 22-carbon docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), serve as the principal substrates for SPM biosynthesis. However, the conversion of dietary omega-3 fatty acids into bioactive mediators is constrained by several factors, including enzymatic bottlenecks, metabolic disease, genetic variability, sex differences, and competing lipid pathways. Emerging evidence, much of which is from preclinical models, suggests that both omega-3 supplementation and direct SPM administration can enhance resolution capacity across multiple organ systems, including the gastrointestinal tract, cardiovascular system, musculoskeletal tissues, nervous system, respiratory system, and reproductive system. This chapter reviews the mechanistic basis by which dietary supplements influence effective resolution biology, which includes efferocytosis, macrophage reprogramming, and epithelial repair systems. The chapter also evaluates current clinical evidence and outlines possible future directions for precision nutrition strategies targeting endogenous resolution pathways.

title: Clinical, metabolic and transcriptomic effects of congenital DLK1 deficiency in women who had central precocious puberty.
authorString: Bellido More CC, Seraphim CE, Menezes-Silva L, Ortiz Rojas C, Canton APM, Brito VN, Rochitte C, Montenegro L, Abreu AP, Kaiser UB, Câmara NOS, Latronico AC.

journal.title: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism

abstractText:
Background

Loss-of-function mutations in Delta-like Noncanonical Notch Ligand 1 (DLK1), a maternally imprinted gene at chromosome 14q32.2, are rare causes of central precocious puberty (CPP) associated with metabolic dysfunction in both sexes.

Objective

To explore the clinical, metabolic and transcriptomic consequences of congenital DLK1 absence in women who had CPP in their childhood.

Methods

Peripheral blood from eight women from three distinct families who carried DLK1 deletions and exhibited undetectable circulating DLK1 serum levels were evaluated. 3T3-L1 cell differentiation into adipocytes was induced using DLK1-deficient serum from these women. In addition, mitochondrial function, cellular metabolism (Seahorse XL Analyzer), and whole blood transcriptomic profiling (RNAseq) were evaluated.

Results

Women with congenital DLK1 deficiency had increased visceral and subcutaneous adipose tissue on abdominal computed tomography. DLK1-deficient serum promoted greater adipogenesis of 3T3-L1 cells compared with control subjects serum. Flow cytometry revealed increased mitochondrial mass and oxidative stress in leukocytes in the patients. In addition, their leukocytes had decreased oxygen consumption and increased extracellular acidification. Whole blood transcriptomic profiling identified upregulation of several genes involved in neutrophil activation and inflammatory signaling, including obesity-associated genes (OLFM4 and LCN2).

Conclusions

We demonstrated distinct metabolic profiles in women with congenital DLK1 deficiency. The absence of DLK1 leads to increased adiposity, mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and upregulation of genes involved in immune-related pathways, particularly neutrophil activation.

title: Incremental associations of pharmacological components in heart failure with mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction: a systematic review and component network meta-analysis.
authorString: Omrani MA, Baskaran BS, Jafari A, Ez Eddin L, Ahmadi F, Chhabra M, Lê ML, Abdullah S, Clemens K, Muanda FT.
abstractText:
Introduction

We conducted a component network meta-analysis (CNMA) of phase 3/4 randomized trials to evaluate incremental effects of pharmacological therapies in heart failure with mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction (HFmrEF/HFpEF; LVEF > 40%).

Methods

MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane were searched through 1 August 2025 (updated 30 March 2026). We performed an additive CNMA evaluating cardiovascular death or first heart failure hospitalization (HFH) and assessed certainty of evidence.

Results

Twenty-four trials and five secondary reports were included. The primary network was sparse (10 trials, 12 regimens), constraining interaction detection and component stability. Incretin-based interventions (pooling semaglutide and tirzepatide, iHR 0.69, 95% CI 0.53-0.91), SGLT-2 inhibitors (0.80, 0.74-0.88), ARNis (0.82, 0.68-0.99), and MRAs (0.89, 0.81-0.98) showed significant component associations, driven principally by fewer HFHs. No drug class significantly reduced mortality. SGLT-2 inhibitors and MRAs remained significant across sensitivity analyses except LVEF ≥ 50%, with SGLT-2 inhibitors most precise. ARNi benefits lost significance under stricter background therapy thresholds (>60%) and contemporary trial restrictions. Evidence for incretins was low-certainty and sensitive to trial selection.

Conclusions

SGLT-2 inhibitors and MRAs provide the most robust incremental benefit, while evidence for other drug classes remains context-dependent. These findings should guide research priorities rather than define combination regimens.

Protocol registration

http://www.crd.york.ac.uk PROSPEROidentifier is CRD420251107058.

title: Anticoagulants compared with aspirin in patients with embolic strokes of undetermined source: an individual participant data meta-analysis of randomised trials.
authorString: Katsanos AH, Sharma M, Diener HC, Kamel H, Poli S, Donnan GA, Elkind MSV, Geisler T, Easton JD, Tirschwell DL, Serna-Higuita LM, Granger CB, Longstreth WT, Poli K, Saver JL, Kronmal RA, Toyoda K, Broderick JP, Elm JJ, Taylor A, Islam S, Xu L, Hart RG, Shoamanesh A.
abstractText: Direct-acting oral anticoagulation did not reduce recurrent stroke compared with aspirin in randomised controlled trials (RCTs) of embolic stroke of undetermined source (ESUS), and subgroup benefits suggested by analyses of individual RCTs were inconsistent across trials. We aimed to evaluate the effect of anticoagulation on the risks of recurrent stroke and major bleeding in patients with ESUS, overall and in prespecified subgroups using individual participant data from RCTs. In this systematic review and meta-analysis, we searched MEDLINE and Scopus for RCTs published between April 1, 2014, and March 1, 2025, without language restriction, comparing anticoagulants with aspirin in patients with ESUS. Non-randomised studies and studies not enrolling patients with ESUS were excluded. We requested individual participant data from the principal investigators of all eligible trials. The primary outcomes were recurrent stroke and major bleeding. For each outcome of interest, we estimated the treatment effect for the overall trial population separately within each trial and the resulting overall treatment estimates were subsequently pooled across trials. Risk of bias was assessed with the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool (version 2.0) for the primary efficacy outcome of stroke recurrence. Hazard ratios (HRs) with corresponding 95% CIs were estimated following adjustment for prespecified covariates and pooled by use of the random-effects model. This study is registered with PROSPERO (CRD42025644724). Our systematic database search identified 1170 records. Of these studies, four were eligible for inclusion in the analysis, including a total of 13 970 participants. Mean age of participants was 66 years (SD 10·6); 5486 (39·3%) participants were female and 8484 (60·7%) were male. Across all trials, 6989 patients were assigned to receive a direct-acting oral anticoagulant and 6981 were assigned to receive aspirin. The hazard for recurrent stroke was similar between participants allocated to anticoagulant or aspirin (399 of 6989 patients [4·6 events per 100 patient-years] in the anticoagulant group vs 417 of 6981 [4·8 events per 100 patient-years] in the aspirin group; adjusted HR 0·94, 95% CI 0·78-1·14), without evidence of heterogeneity across studies (I2=5%, p for Cochran's Q test=0·37). The hazard for major bleeding was also similar between the two groups (149 of 6989 patients [1·6 events per 100 patient-years] in the anticoagulant group vs 106 of 6981 [1·1 events per 100 patient-years] in the aspirin group; adjusted HR 1·19, 95% CI 0·52-2·73), but heterogeneity was present across studies (I2=79%, p for Cochran's Q test=0·0023). Anticoagulation did not reduce the risk of recurrent stroke after ESUS when compared with aspirin, and the risk of major bleeding did not differ significantly between the two treatments. A possible benefit from anticoagulation in patients with ESUS and left atrial enlargement, as shown in a hypothesis-generating subgroup analysis, should be investigated in future trials. Division of Neurology Innovation Fund, McMaster University.

title: Reduced mortality with low-dose rivaroxaban in patients with coronary artery disease: a meta-analysis.
authorString: Palmerini T, Nardi E, Lezzi M, Bruno AG, Lombardi L, Chi G, Taglieri N, Ghetti G, Orzalkiewicz M, Saia F, Galli M, Gibson CM.
abstractText: The optimal antithrombotic therapy (ATT) for patients with coronary artery disease (CAD) is still a matter of debate. In this regard, the role of low-dose rivaroxaban remains controversial. The authors performed a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCT) comparing low-dose rivaroxaban vs standard ATT across the spectrum of CAD. RCTs were searched through MEDLINE, EMBASE, and Cochrane databases, and international meeting proceedings. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality. Results are reported as incidence rate ratio (IRR) of low-dose rivaroxaban vs standard ATT. Five trials including 37 709 randomized patients were identified. Low-dose rivaroxaban was associated with significantly lower rates of all-cause mortality (IRR = 0.83; 95% CI, 0.70-0.98; P = .02), driven by a significant reduction in cardiovascular mortality (IRR = 0.82; 95% CI, 0.69-0.97; P = .02). Low-dose rivaroxaban was also associated with a significant reduction in myocardial infarction (IRR = 0.88; 95% CI, 0.79-0.99; P = .04), major adverse cardiovascular events (IRR = 0.85; 95% CI, 0.76-0.95; P less than .01), and stroke (IRR = 0.71; 95% CI, 0.55-0.91; P less than .01). Stroke reduction was driven by a significant reduction in ischemic strokes (IRR = 0.60; 95% CI, 0.49-0.74; P less than .01), not offset by an increase in hemorrhagic strokes. In contrast, low-dose rivaroxaban increased major bleeding (IRR = 1.46; 95% CI, 0.99-2.17), but not fatal bleeding. In patients with CAD, low-dose rivaroxaban significantly reduces all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, and stroke, but increases major bleeding compared with standard ATT.

title: Compared strategies of carotid revascularization periprocedural risks and long-term outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials of stenting versus endarterectomy.
authorString: Rao SR, Tharakan M, Chou BC, Verma U, Shakir HJ, Janjua MB.
abstractText: Carotid endarterectomy (CEA) remains the benchmark open revascularization strategy for appropriately selected patients with extracranial carotid stenosis, whereas carotid artery stenting (CAS) provides an endovascular alternative when cervical exposure, medical comorbidity, or anatomic factors make open surgery less favorable. Balancing periprocedural stroke, myocardial infarction, cranial nerve injury, and long-term stroke risk remains central to contemporary cerebrovascular decision-making. This study compared periprocedural and exploratory long-term outcomes after CAS versus CEA using randomized head-to-head trial evidence across trial eras. PubMed, EMBASE, CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched through April 2026. Eligible studies were randomized trials directly comparing CAS with CEA in adults with extracranial carotid stenosis. Arm-level event counts were extracted. Random-effects risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using inverse-variance models with DerSimonian-Laird estimation. Hartung-Knapp intervals and absolute risk differences were added to support sensitivity analysis and clinical interpretation. The primary endpoint was 30-day stroke or death. Secondary endpoints included periprocedural stroke, death, myocardial infarction (MI), cranial nerve injury, disabling stroke or death, and exploratory long-term stroke-related outcomes. Six randomized cohorts contributed to the primary endpoint; up to eight contributed to secondary analyses. Thirty-day stroke or death occurred in 244 of 5285 patients assigned to CAS (4.6%) and 156 of 4522 assigned to CEA (3.4%), corresponding to an absolute excess of 1.2 percentage points with CAS and a pooled RR of 1.42 (95% CI, 1.12-1.81; I²=27.9%). Periprocedural stroke was also more common after CAS (291/6305 [4.6%] vs. 186/5546 [3.4%]; RR, 1.44; 95% CI, 1.18-1.75; I²=9.1%). Periprocedural death did not differ significantly (RR, 1.30; 95% CI, 0.77-2.19). MI (RR, 0.45; 95% CI, 0.29-0.71) and cranial nerve injury (RR, 0.05; 95% CI, 0.02-0.11) favored CAS. In a prespecified sensitivity analysis excluding CAVATAS-because most patients in its endovascular arm underwent balloon angioplasty rather than stenting-the primary result was unchanged (RR, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.17-1.95). Exploratory long-term stroke-related outcomes did not differ significantly (RR, 1.05; 95% CI, 0.87-1.26), although endpoint definitions and follow-up windows varied substantially. In randomized head-to-head trials, CAS was associated with higher early stroke and stroke-or-death risk than CEA, whereas MI and cranial nerve injury were reported less often after CAS. Selection of open versus endovascular carotid revascularization should be guided by symptom status, age, lesion morphology, cervical and arch anatomy, perioperative cardiac risk, and operator outcomes.

title: Association of Clonal Hematopoiesis Mutations With Incident Atrial Fibrillation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Nasrollahizadeh A, Mehdizadeh M, Armani Moghadam S, Rahmati S, Javankiani S, Khan HR.
abstractText:
Background

Clonal hematopoiesis (CH) has been linked to cardiovascular disease through inflammation-related pathways, but its association with atrial fibrillation (AF) remains uncertain.

Objectives

The purpose of this study was to systematically review and meta-analyze evidence on the association between CH mutations and AF, with planned analyses by hematologic cancer status, variant allele frequency (VAF), mutations, and sex.

Methods

PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science were searched from inception to May 6, 2026, for studies reporting adjusted quantitative associations between CH and incident AF. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed. Study quality was assessed using the Risk Of Bias In Non-randomized Studies-of Exposures tool.

Results

Five studies comprising 7 cohorts and 299,215 participants were included. In populations without cancer, CH defined by VAF ≥2% was not significantly associated with AF (HR: 1.02; 95% CI: 0.97-1.07; I2 = 0%). Large CH clones (VAF ≥10%) were associated with a modestly higher AF risk (HR: 1.11; 95% CI: 1.01-1.22; I2 = 0%). Mutation-specific analyses did not show statistically significant associations for DNMT3A, TET2, or ASXL1 individually, and no sex-based effect modification was observed. In hematologic cancer populations, CH mutations were significantly associated with higher AF risk (HR: 3.22; 95% CI: 1.02-10.13; I2 = 0%). Sensitivity analyses and wide prediction intervals warrant cautious interpretation, particularly for the VAF ≥10% and hematologic cancer analyses.

Conclusions

The association between CH and AF may vary by clonal burden and hematologic cancer status. However, evidence remains limited and observational. Larger studies with standardized CH and AF definitions are needed to clarify clinical relevance.

title: Quality, Power, and Fragility of Randomized Controlled Trials in ANCA-Associated Vasculitis: A Systematic Review.
authorString: Ivković V, Bruchfeld A, Floyd L, Oh SS, Park PG, Stevens KI, Shin JI, Kronbichler A.

journal.title: American journal of kidney diseases : the official journal of the National Kidney Foundation

abstractText:
Rationale & objective

Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) changed the management of ANCA-associated vasculitides (AAV). However, their quality and statistical power to detect the outcomes vary. This study aimed to evaluate the robustness of RCTs in AAV regarding quality and statistical power as well as the stability of trial findings, termed fragility.

Study design

Systematic review of RCTs published up to May 1, 2025.

Setting & study populations

RCTs evaluating therapies in AAV.

Selection criteria for studies

Reports of the primary findings of RCTs' in which over 50% of participants had AAV.

Data extraction

Screening was performed by two authors and extraction by one, with verification of extracted information implemented for 20% of trials. RCT quality was assessed using the modified Jadad score (mJS). Reporting of statistical sample size calculations or power analysis was recorded. The Fragility Index (FI) and Reverse FI (RFI) were calculated for each trial as the number of participants whose outcome would have needed to switch from event to non-event, or vice versa, to change the RCT result and interpretation.

Analytical approach

Continuous variables were described by mean and standard deviation (SD) or by median and interquartile range. Between-group comparisons were conducted using the Student's t-test or Mann-Whitney U-test. Categorical variables were described as counts and percentages. Between-group comparisons were conducted using ANOVA, the Kruskal-Wallis test, and Fisher's Exact test, with correlations tested using Pearson's correlation coefficient or Spearman's rank correlation, depending the normality of the distribution. Linear regression was used to test associations between variables.

Results

Four (7%) RCTs were of poor quality, 18 (32%) were of moderate quality, and 34 (61%) were of high quality. RCT quality improved over time and was associated with larger RCTs. Thirty-five (63%) RCTs reported sample size or power calculation, of which 20 (57%) did not enroll sufficient patients. The median FI of all RCTs was 5.0 (25th to 75th percentile: 1.0 to 5.0, min-max: 0 to 10). A total of 5 (38%) RCTs had a higher number of patients lost to follow-up, withdrawn, or dropped out than the FI. The median RFI was 5.0 (25th to 75th percentile: 3.0 to 7.3, min-max: 1 to 16).

Limitations

Not all trials reported all the characteristics studied.

Conclusion

Most trials in AAV were of good quality, but were small, frequently underpowered, and highly fragile. A shift in the outcomes of only five participants on average, often fewer than the number of participants lost to follow-up, would have been sufficient to change findings.

title: Culprit vessel TIMI 0-1 flow identifies a high-risk subgroup of NSTEMI patients with multivessel disease: a post-hoc analysis of the SLIM randomized clinical trial.
authorString: Lux AÁ, Betti M, Pustjens TFS, Bova R, Heuts S, van 't Hof AWJ, Rasoul S, SLIM trial investigators.
abstractText:
Background

Occlusive myocardial infarction (OMI) is a specific, high-risk subgroup of non-ST elevation myocardial infarction. To estimate the impact of this clinical entity, this post-hoc analysis of the SLIM trial uses decreased TIMI flow (0 or 1) and patent flow (TIMI 2-3 flow) as surrogates to characterize these patient groups and their outcomes in a cohort with NSTEMI and multivessel coronary artery disease.

Methods

The SLIM trial randomized NSTEMI patients with multivessel disease to complete or culprit-only revascularization; we included 474 patients with available angiographic data in the current analysis. One-year Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (MACE: all-cause death, non-fatal MI, any revascularization, and stroke) were assessed using Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, and the association between study groups and outcomes was evaluated in crude and adjusted Cox proportional-hazards models.

Results

TIMI 0-1 patients were younger (62 vs. 67 years, p<0.001), predominantly male (84.9% vs. 69.3%, p<0.001), with higher baseline biomarker levels. Routine interpretation of admission ECGs failed to differentiate occlusion status (reported ST-deviation 32.1% vs. 33.2%, p = 0.835). In the TIMI 0-1 flow group, the circumflex artery was the culprit more often (45.3% vs. 27.7%, p < 0.001). Although unadjusted MACE at 1-year follow-up was comparable (p=0.061), adjusted models showed that decreased flow was associated with MACE at one year (MACE: aHR 2.09, p=0.026).

Conclusions

This post-hoc analysis of the SLIM trial shows that TIMI 0-1 flow during the index procedure is an indicator for a high-risk subgroup of NSTEMI patients with multivessel disease who face a higher risk of MACE at one year.

title: Effects of Dapagliflozin on Inflammatory Biomarkers and Associations With Clinical Outcomes in CKD: Findings From the DAPA-CKD Trial.
authorString: Moedt E, Heerspink HJL, Gottschal P, Greasley PJ, Sabatine MS, Rossing P, Wheeler DC, Bakker SJL, Coca SG.

journal.title: American journal of kidney diseases : the official journal of the National Kidney Foundation

abstractText:
Rationale & objective

Inflammation is a key driver of chronic kidney disease (CKD). This study evaluated the effects of dapagliflozin (DAPA) on inflammatory biomarkers and examined their associations with clinical outcomes.

Study design

Randomized controlled trial.

Setting & participants

2,795 participants in the DAPA-CKD trial.

Exposures

Dapagliflozin, 10 mg daily, versus placebo and baseline levels of plasma TNFR-1, TNFR-2, and KIM-1, serum IL-6, hs-CRP, and uric acid, as well as urinary uric acid, KIM-1, and MCP-1.

Outcomes

Four prespecified time-to-event outcomes: the primary outcome was a composite of ≥50% eGFR decline, kidney failure, or death from renal or cardiovascular causes. A kidney outcome was defined as the primary composite without cardiovascular death, and a cardiovascular outcome was defined as a composite of heart failure hospitalization or cardiovascular death. An additional secondary outcome was all-cause mortality. Biochemical outcomes were levels of plasma TNFR-1, TNFR-2, and KIM-1, serum IL-6, hs-CRP, and uric acid, as well as urinary uric acid, KIM-1, and MCP-1 one year after randomization.

Analytical approach

Multivariable proportional hazards models were used to assess associations between biomarkers and outcomes, and analysis of covariance was used to assess treatment effects of dapagliflozin.

Results

Higher baseline levels of plasma TNFR-1, TNFR-2, and KIM-1, serum IL-6 and hs-CRP, and urinary KIM-1/Cr and MCP-1/Cr were independently associated with increased risk of clinical outcomes. Participants randomized to dapagliflozin had significantly reduced levels of plasma KIM-1, serum uric acid, and urinary MCP-1/Cr and KIM-1/Cr compared with placebo after 1 year of treatment, while a significant increase in urinary uric acid/Cr was observed. Early increases in TNFR-1 and TNFR-2, and urinary uric acid/Cr, KIM-1/Cr, and MCP-1/Cr from baseline to year 1 were associated with a higher subsequent risk of the primary composite outcome (HRs per SD 1.59 [95% CI 1.37-1.86], 1.19 [95% CI 1.01-1.40], and 1.36 [95% CI 1.11-1.65], 1.27 [95% CI 1.06-1.51], and 1.42 [95% CI 1.13-1.79], respectively).

Limitations

Biomarkers were measured at only two time points, analyses were post hoc with potential residual confounding. Missing biomarker data in a substantial proportion of participants creates the potential for selection bias.

Conclusions

In patients with CKD, inflammatory biomarkers are strongly associated with clinical outcomes and may be modifiable with dapagliflozin. Early changes in these biomarkers are associated with subsequent outcomes, supporting their role in monitoring treatment response and disease progression.

title: Nutrition, metabolism, and cardiovascular longevity-what is established, what is hypothesis?
authorString: Rossmeißl A, Timper K.
abstractText:
Background

Cardiovascular aging is the rate-limiting process for human life expectancy and healthspan. Nutrition and metabolism are the most widely available geroprotective targets, yet the underlying evidence is markedly uneven.

Objective

To define which nutritional and metabolic interventions are established for cardiovascular longevity, or better healthy aging, and which remain hypothetical.

Methods

Narrative review of randomized trials, cohort studies, and mechanistic work on dietary patterns, energy balance, meal timing, food quality, supplements, and biomarkers of biological aging.

Results

Whole dietary patterns (Mediterranean, "Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension" [DASH], sodium reduction) reduce hard cardiovascular endpoints, and the causal roles of apolipoprotein B (apoB)-containing lipoproteins, blood pressure, and adiposity are firmly established. Pharmacologically induced weight loss via glucagon-like peptide‑1 (GLP-1)-based drugs reduces cardiovascular events to a degree not achieved by lifestyle programs, shifting clinical nutrition toward preservation of lean mass and micronutrient adequacy. By contrast, isolated nutrients and supplements, a specific geroprotective effect of intermittent fasting, and the clinical utility of epigenetic aging clocks remain unproven. Randomized caloric restriction slows the epigenetic pace of aging only modestly and has so far not demonstrated mortality benefit in humans.

Conclusion

Nutrition acts on cardiovascular longevity mainly through established risk factors rather than through demonstrated extension of maximum lifespan. Nutritional recommendations should make this distinction explicit, and longevity research requires endpoint-driven trials rather than surrogate markers only.

title: BEAT-SC: randomized, controlled, double-blind phase III study of bevacizumab plus atezolizumab and chemotherapy as first-line treatment of extensive-stage small cell lung cancer.
authorString: Nishio M, Yamamoto N, Ohe Y, Watanabe S, Ren X, Murakami S, Yang N, Yoneshima Y, Li G, Katakami N, Liu X, Yamamoto S, Nakagawa Y, Hayashi M, Qian C, Nanki T, Han B.

title: IASLC Multidisciplinary Recommendations for Assessment and Reporting of Lymph Node Treatment Response in Lung Cancer Resection Specimens After Neoadjuvant Therapy.
authorString: Berezowska S, Dacic S, Weissferdt A, Cooper WA, Wynes MW, Wistuba II, Travis WD, Voting Expert Panelists.

journal.title: Journal of thoracic oncology : official publication of the International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer

abstractText: Pathologic response (PR) after neoadjuvant therapy is an established surrogate endpoint in lung cancer clinical trials. Although IASLC recommendations standardizing PR assessment in primary tumors are widely adopted, guidance for evaluating treatment response in regional lymph nodes (LNs) has been lacking. The IASLC has developed multidisciplinary consensus recommendations for LN assessment in resected lung cancer specimens following neoadjuvant therapy. A core group of IASLC pathologists drafted statements addressing key aspects of gross and microscopic LN evaluation. These were refined through a two-round Delphi process involving 48 international experts in thoracic oncology, surgery, radiology, and pathology. Consensus was predefined as ≥85% agreement. Experts reviewed, commented upon, and voted on 13 final recommendations. All 13 recommendations reached consensus (86-100%). Key statements include: defining pathologic complete response (pCR) as the absence of residual viable tumor (RVT) in both lung and LNs; introducing MPR(N+) for cases with ≤10% RVT at the primary site but residual nodal disease; requiring estimation of RVT, stroma, and necrosis across LN stations; accepting unweighted ("eyeball") microscopic assessment; encouraging reporting of metastasis size; and advising complete LN submission with selective use of deeper levels and/or immunohistochemistry. The recommendations further clarify interpretation of direct tumor extension into LN, interpretation of psammoma bodies or acellular mucin, and interactions with ypTNM staging principles. These IASLC multidisciplinary recommendations provide the first standardized framework for assessing treatment response in LNs after neoadjuvant therapy in lung cancer and are intended to improve diagnostic reproducibility, support trial harmonization, and to outline research opportunities.

title: Low-Carbohydrate, Animal-Centered Diets and Plant-Based Diets Exert Opposing Effects on Cardiometabolic Diseases.
authorString: Najjar RS.
abstractText: Low-carbohydrate, animal-centered (LCAC) diets are promoted for the prevention and treatment of type 2 diabetes (T2D) and cardiovascular disease (CVD) because randomized trials have shown short-term reductions in select risk factors, such as body weight, triglycerides, and glycated hemoglobin. However, controlled feeding studies have shown increases in low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), apolipoprotein B, and circulating free fatty acids with LCAC diets. Importantly, LCAC diets can also drive lipotoxicity and inflammation. These latter pathological biochemical effects directly act on pathways involved in the development of T2D and CVD. In contrast, high-carbohydrate, unrefined plant-based diets in these conditions reduce insulin requirements even without weight loss, lower blood pressure and medication use, and improve atherogenic lipoproteins and inflammation. Meta-analyses of randomized trials demonstrate reductions in LDL-C, apolipoprotein B, and glycated hemoglobin with vegetarian or vegan diets. Further, plant-based dietary interventions have also shown regression of coronary atherosclerosis and improvements in myocardial perfusion and cardiac function, an effect absent from LCAC diet literature. Thus, public health efforts aimed at the prevention and treatment of T2D and CVD should continue to focus on improving the quantity and quality of plant foods consumed rather than carbohydrate restriction alone.

title: Coated versus non-coated flow diverter stents for intracranial aneurysm embolization: a propensity score-matched cohort study.
authorString: Popica DA, Mihalea C, Caroff J, Rodriguez-Erazú F, Diaz IM, Ismail M, Silva-Pozo A, Cadilha H, Akimoto T, Malita DC, Ikka L, Chalumeau V, Plaforet V, Spelle L, Cortese J.

journal.title: Journal of neuroradiology = Journal de neuroradiologie

abstractText: Coated flow diverters (FDs) were developed to reduce thromboembolic complications and to potentially facilitate endothelialization. We compared coated versus non-coated FDs for intracranial aneurysm embolization. We retrospectively analyzed 286 consecutive unruptured aneurysms in 262 patients treated with FDs between 2018 and 2024 from a prospectively maintained single-center database. Ten aneurysms treated under single antiplatelet therapy within a randomized trial were excluded before matching, so that the propensity score model was built within a uniformly dual-antiplatelet population. The primary outcome was periprocedural thromboembolic events; secondary outcomes were hemorrhagic complications, FD-related and permanent morbidity, complete occlusion and relevant neointimal hyperplasia (NIH). Matching was performed 2:1 on patient demographics, cardiovascular risk factors, aneurysm location, morphology and size, neck coverage and follow-up duration. After matching, 114 non-coated and 57 coated aneurysms were analyzed. Thromboembolic events were less frequent in the coated group without reaching statistical significance (5.3% vs 14.9%; risk difference -9.6%, 95% CI -18.1 to +0.9; relative risk 0.35, 95% CI 0.11-1.15; p=0.08). Rates of relevant NIH (>25%) were similar (17.5% vs 13.2%, p=0.44), as were complete occlusion rates (77.2% vs 71.9%, p=0.46). FD-related and permanent morbidity did not differ significantly. In this exploratory analysis, coated FDs showed a numerically lower rate of thromboembolic events that did not reach statistical significance, with no significant differences in NIH or in angiographic and clinical outcomes. Further development of coating technologies, along with larger multicenter studies and longer follow-up, is needed to better define their potential to improve outcomes.

title: High-Dose vs Standard-Dose Influenza Vaccine and Patient-Reported Symptom Burden in Older Adults - A Substudy of the DANFLU-2 Randomized Clinical Trial.
authorString: Davidovski FS, Skaarup KG, Søndergaard CS, Shaikh N, Wolff PS, Bartelt-Hofer J, Harris RC, Loiacono MM, Modin D, Jessen R, Lapage JMJ, Shaw DS, Steenhard N, Martel CJ, Larsen CS, Larsen L, Wiese L, Dalager-Pedersen M, Claggett BL, Solomon SD, Sivapalan P, Stæhr Jensen JU, Johansen ND, Biering-Sørensen T.

journal.title: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America

abstractText: High-dose inactivated influenza vaccine (HD-IIV) reduces laboratory-confirmed influenza (LCI) and severe outcomes compared with standard-dose inactivated influenza vaccine (SD-IIV), but effects on patient-reported symptom burden are uncertain. To compare symptom burden after HD-IIV versus SD-IIV among older adults with symptomatic LCI and assess feasibility of home-based self-swabbing with digital patient-reported outcomes. Prespecified exploratory substudy of the randomized, open-label DANFLU-2 trial. Nationwide in Denmark within the DANFLU-2 randomized trial during the 2024 to 2025 influenza season. Community-dwelling adults aged 65 years or older enrolled in DANFLU-2 who consented to participate in the Homeswab substudy. Participants were assigned 1:1 to HD-IIV or SD-IIV and received self-swab kits with digital symptom questionnaires for influenza-like illness episodes. Symptom burden among participants with LCI, assessed with the validated Respiratory Infection Intensity and Impact Questionnaire (RiiQ). Feasibility was assessed by swab return, RT-qPCR analyzability, RNase P positivity, and questionnaire completion. Among 10,140 randomized participants (HD-IIV, 5040; SD-IIV, 5100; mean age, 73.2 years; 50.3% female), 1280 swabs were received and 1273 were analyzable. 121 swabs (9.5%) tested positive for influenza (HD-IIV, 44; SD-IIV, 77), and RNase P positivity was 97.8% (1245 of 1273). Among participants with LCI, 97 (80.2%) completed at least 1 symptom questionnaire. Respiratory and systemic symptom severity did not differ between groups. Post hoc relative vaccine effectiveness of HD-IIV versus SD-IIV against LCI was 42.2% (95% CI, 16.4% to 60.0%). The symptom-burden analysis was limited by few breakthrough infections and incomplete questionnaire completion. Home-based self-swabbing with digital patient-reported outcome collection was feasible at scale among older adults in a vaccine effectiveness trial, but symptom burden after LCI did not differ between HD-IIV and SD-IIV.

title: Contextualized vs usual cardiopulmonary resuscitation skill stations: a simulation-based, randomized trial.
authorString: Brøgger MØ, Wittig J, Løfgren B, Riis DN, Harrits AS, Krogh K, Lauridsen KG.
abstractText: We aimed to investigate whether training on a contextualized skill station combined with in-bed cardiopulmonary resuscitation instructions improves the number of excellent chest compressions in a simulated in-hospital cardiac arrest scenario compared to a standard table-based skill station. This randomized, multicenter trial included nurses and nurse assistants from two Danish emergency departments. Participants were trained in chest compressions on a contextualized skill station with the manikin on a bed (intervention) or on a skill station table (control). Participants completed two one-minute sessions with audiovisual feedback, repeated after 2-4 weeks. Skills were assessed in a 2-min in-hospital cardiac arrest scenario 4-8 weeks after the first training session. The primary outcome was the number of excellent chest compressions defined as guideline-compliant depth and rate. We included 65 participants. The intervention group training on the contextualized skill station performed more excellent compressions with a median (quartile 1; quartile 3) of 70 (27; 140) vs 23 (2; 93) (p = 0.01) compared to the control group. In addition, the intervention group performed more compressions with guideline-compliant depth (118 (53; 155) vs 78 (16; 127), p = 0.02), and more compressions with guideline-compliant rate (134 (86; 152) vs 58 (22; 134), p = 0.01) compared to the control group. More participants in the intervention group initiated compressions by jumping onto the bed (85%) compared to the control group (43%), p = 0.002. There was no significant difference in time to first compression. Training on a contextualized skill station with a manikin on a bed significantly increased the number of excellent chest compressions compared to skill station training with the manikin on a table. These findings highlight the importance of integrating clinical factors such as bed adjustments when implementing skill stations for CPR training in emergency departments to facilitate the transfer of skills.

title: Percutaneous Electrical Nerve Field Stimulation: Revitalizing the Management of Neurogastrointestinal Motility Disorders.
authorString: VonAxelson AE, Santucci NR.
abstractText: Neurogastrointestinal motility disorders and disorders of gut-brain interaction (DGBI) are difficult to treat, particularly with pharmacotherapy alone. This review examines percutaneous electrical nerve field stimulation (PENFS) as a non-invasive neuromodulation therapy, addressing its potential mechanistic rationale, clinical evidence, patient selection, practical implementation, and future directions of research. PENFS appears to act through several pathways: limbic modulation via the central nucleus of the amygdala, altered vagal afferent signaling at the nucleus tractus solitarius, and effects on an enteric nervous system that continues to mature through adolescence. Randomized sham-controlled trials and a multicenter registry show improvement in pain, nausea, and disability alongside a favorable safety profile. Auricular allodynia and impaired cardiac vagal efficiency are emerging as markers of treatment response. PENFS is a safe, effective, non-pharmacologic option across the DGBI spectrum. Formal dose- and duration-response work, adult trials, and long-term durability data remain the principal gaps, though work is ongoing.

title: Integrating miRNA bioinformatics and nanotechnology for precision diagnosis and therapy in hypertension.
authorString: Salah AN, Mansour RM, Abdel Mageed SS, El-Dakroury WA, AlFarsi K, Sayed GA, Ibrahim AA, AbdAlhafiz AI, Elshamy AA, Mohammed OA, Abokhalil RN, Megahed MA, Doghish AS.
abstractText:
Introduction

Hypertension is a leading contributor to cardiovascular and renal morbidity worldwide, and its management remains largely empirical. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) regulate pathways central to blood-pressure homeostasis and are stable in the circulation, positioning them as candidate noninvasive biomarkers and therapeutic targets for precision antihypertensive strategies.

Areas covered

This review examines circulating miRNA signatures reported in hypertensive patients, including miR-21, miR-145, miR-122 and miR-155, and their association with target-organ damage. Discrepancies between cohorts are appraised in relation to sample matrix, comorbidities, detection platform and normalization, and the pre-analytical standardization required for reproducible measurement. Mechanistic roles in renin-angiotensin-aldosterone signaling, renal sodium handling, endothelial function and oxidative stress are discussed, with bioinformatics and machine-learning pipelines for biomarker discovery, their validation requirements, and preclinical nanocarrier platforms providing proof of concept for miRNA delivery without established clinical efficacy or safety.

Expert opinion

miRNA-guided diagnosis and therapy in hypertension remains preclinical; no miRNA nanomedicine has entered hypertension-focused clinical trials. Clinical translation will depend on harmonized sampling and normalization, externally validated multi-cohort machine-learning signatures, and nanocarriers with demonstrated cytosolic delivery and acceptable repeated-dose safety. Stepwise integration of these strands offers the most realistic route to translation.

title: Regulatory roles of microRNA‑145 in cardiovascular diseases (Review).
authorString: Jian RH, Huang S.
abstractText: MicroRNA‑145 (miR‑145) is a non‑coding RNA involved in vascular remodeling, myocardial injury and fibrosis, and it contributes to the onset and progression of several cardiovascular disorders. Accumulating evidence indicates that the functions of miR‑145 depend on cell subtypes and pathological microenvironments. miR‑145 exerts dual regulatory effects in atherosclerosis, myocardial ischemia‑reperfusion injury, hypertension, pulmonary arterial hypertension ventricular remodeling and heart failure. In some settings, for example in cardiomyocytes subjected to myocardial ischemia‑reperfusion injury (MIRI), miR‑145 can suppress disease progression and protect the myocardium and vasculature; conversely, it may trigger tissue injury and exacerbate disease in specific cell types and pathological setting; for example, in cardiac microvascular endothelial cells during MIRI. Abnormal expression of miR‑145 is associated with disease severity, risk stratification and the incidence of long‑term adverse cardiovascular events, suggesting its potential as a molecular biomarker for early screening, disease assessment and prognosis of cardiovascular diseases (CVDs). Unconjugated or unformulated miR is limited by poor in vivo stability, rapid degradation by ribonucleases and low cellular transfection efficiency. To address these limitations, three major delivery platforms, namely extracellular vesicles, viral vectors and nanoparticles, have been developed for targeted delivery of miR‑145 and these platforms differ in biosafety, delivery efficacy and modifiability. As research advances in nucleic acid‑based targeted therapeutics, several miR‑based agents have entered clinical trials, supporting the development of targeted interventions for CVDs. The present review examined the dual regulatory mechanisms, potential clinical applications and current delivery technologies of miR‑145 across CVDs. The translational progress and limitations of current miR therapeutics were reviewed, as well as unresolved controversies and unanswered scientific questions. The present work aimed to inform further mechanistic studies of miR‑145 and the research, development and clinical translation of cardiovascular nucleic acid‑targeted therapies.

title: Efficacy and feasibility of prehabilitation for cardiorespiratory functional capacity and respiratory muscle strength in cardiac surgery (PRECICA-I study).
authorString: Izquierdo-García J, Plaza-Manzano G, Fabero-Garrido R, Ojeda-García C, Del-Corral-Núñez-Flores T, Sanz Ayán MP, López-Marcos JJ, Eixerés Esteve A, Moreno Muñoz G, López-de-Uralde-Villanueva I.

journal.title: Anales del sistema sanitario de Navarra

abstractText:
Background

To evaluate the feasibility and efficacy of a short-term, face-to-face prehabilitation programme in patients awaiting elective cardiac surgery, focusing on cardiorespiratory functional capacity, respiratory muscle strength, frailty, psychological distress, quality of life, and hospital length of stay.

Methods

This single-blind randomised controlled trial included patients awaiting coronary, valvular, or aortic surgery. Participants were assigned to a prehabilitation group (two sessions per week of respiratory physiotherapy, strength training, and health education) or a control group (incentive spirometer). Functional capacity (6MWT), respiratory strength (MIP/MEP), frailty (SPPB), handgrip strength, quality of life (SF-12), physical activity (IPAQ), anxiety and depression (HADS) were assessed before the intervention and one week after discharge; hospital length of stay was also assessed.

Results

Thirty-six patients (44% female; mean age 66.5 years) were included in the prehabilitation (n=24) and control (n=12) groups. Feasibility was high, with 92% adherence and no adverse events. Waist circumference, MIP, handgrip strength, and anxiety levels decreased significantly from pre-intervention to follow-up in both groups. In the control group, MEP also decreased significantly, while frailty increased. The only significant between-group difference was observed for MEP, with greater deterioration in the control group (Cohen's d=0.8).

Conclusions

Short-term, face-to-face prehabilitation is feasible and may help mitigate the loss of expiratory muscle strength following elective cardiac surgery, although it does not improve functional capacity. Larger trials are needed to confirm its broader clinical benefits and to assess the impact of sex.

title: Improvements in Aerobic Conditioning and Exercise-Associated Anxiety Following Pediatric Cardiac Telerehabilitation Training in Pediatric Patients with Congenital Heart Disease: A Randomized Controlled Trial
authorString: Fremed MA, Mundo RSD, McCown ME, Asiedu Q, Zewde YT, Ortiz Z, Gibbs D, Madej M, Liberman L, Layton AM.
abstractText:
Purpose: Pediatric cardiac telerehabilitation (PCTR) may expand access to care; however, data supporting the effectiveness of this rehabilitation modality are limited.

Methods:

We performed a prospective, randomized controlled trial to determine the effectiveness of PCTR on exercise capacity, quality of life, and mood in children with congenital heart disease (CHD). Patients performed cardiopulmonary exercise testing and completed questionnaires at enrollment and after completion. The PCTR group completed 12 weeks of PCTR (three sessions per week: one to two supervised, one to two independent) with a personalized exercise prescription, single-lead electrocardiogram monitor, stationary bicycle, free weights, resistance bands, and activity tracker. Controls received an activity tracker and continued regular daily activities.

Results:

Twenty-eight patients enrolled; five withdrew. Of the 23 who completed the program (13 PCTR, 10 control), median age was 14 years (interquartile range [IQR] 13–17), 32% were female, and median body mass index was 20.4 kg/m² (IQR 18.8–22.8). Controlling for age and gender, PCTR significantly improved oxygen consumption (VO2, mL/kg/min) at the anaerobic threshold (median change: controls −0.5 [IQR −3.4 to 5.6] vs. PCTR 2.7 [0.1–4.3], p < 0.01) and at peak exercise (controls −0.2 [−1.4 to 1.17] vs. PCTR 3.5 [0.6–5.7], p < 0.01). Exercise-associated anxiety (Exercise Sensitivity Questionnaire) also improved with PCTR (controls −1 [−7 to 9] vs. PCTR −11 [−22 to −8], p = 0.02). Other parameters improved within the PCTR group but did not differ significantly from controls.

Conclusion:

PCTR significantly improves aerobic exercise capacity and exercise-associated anxiety in children and adolescents with CHD. Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06819059; registered 6 February 2025 (retrospectively registered).
