title: Transcatheter edge-to-edge versus surgical repair in primary degenerative mitral regurgitation: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authorString: Londoño Barrientos M, Molano Rivera JF, Amarillo Gutiérrez D, García Vallejo S, Araque JC, Vélez LA.
abstractText:
Objectives

To compare transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) with surgical mitral valve repair in adults with primary degenerative mitral regurgitation (DMR).

Methods

PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Ovid MEDLINE, Scopus and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched to 23 October 2025 (PROSPERO CRD420251153452). The primary analysis included studies of DMR with a surgical repair comparator; cohorts with a predominantly replacement comparator and administrative registries entered separate sensitivity analyses. Odds ratios (OR) were pooled with the Mantel-Haenszel method, with random-effects models as sensitivity analyses. Certainty was rated with GRADE.

Results

Nine studies were included; five (775 patients) formed the primary analysis. TEER was associated with more residual mitral regurgitation of at least moderate grade (OR 8.21, 95% CI 4.56-14.79) and more mitral reinterventions (OR 4.10, 1.69-9.94), and with fewer transfusions (OR 0.11, 0.05-0.23), less new-onset atrial fibrillation (OR 0.09, 0.03-0.28) and a shorter hospital stay (random-effects mean difference -3.6 days, -6.2 to -1.0). Early mortality did not differ significantly (OR 2.03, 0.62-6.61; 12 deaths), but the interval was too wide to establish equivalence. Four of the five primary studies ended enrolment before 2018. Certainty was low to very low.

Conclusions

Surgical repair remains the reference treatment for patients with favourable operative risk and repairable anatomy. TEER is a valuable alternative for carefully selected patients in whom procedural safety or surgical risk predominates, at the cost of less complete and less durable correction. The absence of a significant difference in early mortality does not demonstrate equivalence.

title: End-stage renal disease in people taking lithium: a systematic review.
authorString: Nguyen L, Chirakijja T, Scanlon C, Panat MJ, Elias A.
abstractText:
Background

Lithium is an effective maintenance treatment for Bipolar Affective Disorder. However, it is also associated with renal impairment. End-Stage Renal Disease (ESRD) is the most severe form of chronic kidney disease (CKD) and has significant morbidity and mortality.

Objective

To conduct a systematic review on ESRD incidence in adult patients taking lithium for mood disorders.

Methods

The search was conducted on EMBASE, MEDLINE, PsycINFO, and CENTRAL for relevant articles. Relevant bibliographies were also searched. Original research in English, reporting on ESRD in adults with affective disorders on lithium, was included. End-stage renal disease was defined as estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate (eGFR) < 15mL/minute/1.73m2 or renal replacement therapy (RRT). Studies with lithium exposure for a mean duration of less than five years were excluded.

Results

Eight retrospective cohort studies were included. Studies were heterogeneous, making direct comparisons difficult. Results showed that ESRD occurs rarely, less than 1% in the absence of a pre-existing renal disease, and typically after decades of lithium exposure. In the presence of chronic kidney disease, discontinuation of lithium after a point of return was not necessarily associated with lower rates of ESRD. However, the trajectory of renal function after discontinuation of lithium remains debatable warranting further prospective studies. There were inconsistent results regarding how confounding factors, such as hypertension and diabetes, contributed to ESRD risk in lithium users.

Conclusion

End-stage renal disease is a rare outcome that develops after decades of lithium treatment. The literature on ESRD associated with lithium is limited by the long latency of ESRD, retrospective study designs, and confounding covariates.

title: TTR-stabilising medicines for the treatment of transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy.

Objectives

The objectives are as follows: Primary objective To assess the effects of TTR-stabilising medicines (tafamidis and acoramidis) compared to usual care or placebo on all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalisations in people with ATTR-CM. title: The Coronary Artery Disease Education Questionnaire (CADE-Q) in Cardiovascular Care: A Scoping Review.
authorString: Vieira AM, Benetti M, Ghisi GLM.
abstractText: Patient education is a core component of cardiac rehabilitation (CR) and secondary prevention of cardiovascular disease, supporting disease understanding, self-management, and adoption of heart-healthy behaviours. The Coronary Artery Disease Education Questionnaire (CADE-Q) was developed as a standardised instrument to assess disease-related knowledge among individuals with cardiovascular conditions. Since its development, multiple versions and translations have been created and applied in diverse populations and settings worldwide. This scoping review aimed to map the global use of CADE-Q instruments, including populations, contexts, knowledge outcomes, and psychometric properties reported across studies. This scoping review followed Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and was reported according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). Databases searched included Ovid MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane Central, Emcare, EBSCO CINAHL, Web of Science Core Collection, Global Index Medicus and ProQuest Dissertations & Theses. Studies were eligible if they used the CADE-Q or any of its versions to assess disease-related knowledge in adults. Data were charted using a standardised extraction tool and synthesised descriptively. Sixty-six studies involving 14,714 participants across 26 countries were included. The CADE-Q Short Version was the most frequently used instrument (n=36), followed by CADE-Q II (n=17) and the original CADE-Q (n=13), administered in 19 languages. Most studies were conducted in CR settings. Baseline knowledge levels were generally moderate relative to maximum scores. Lower knowledge was commonly observed in risk factor and psychosocial health domains, while knowledge related to nutrition and exercise was generally higher. In intervention and longitudinal studies, knowledge typically improved following structured educational interventions, particularly within CR programs. Twenty validation studies reported acceptable psychometric properties across versions and languages, including good internal consistency, test-retest reliability, and evidence of structural and construct validity. CADE-Q instruments are widely used globally to assess cardiovascular disease knowledge and demonstrate consistent psychometric performance across diverse settings. Moderate knowledge levels and persistent gaps in risk factor and psychosocial domains suggest a need for more targeted patient education. These tools may support personalised educational interventions in clinical practice, while future research should prioritise implementation and validation in underrepresented populations and regions.

title: Women-focused education in cardiac rehabilitation: study protocol of a pilot randomised controlled trial assessing feasibility, implementation and acceptability in Canada.
authorString: Kümmel Duarte C, Carvalho C, Hébert AA, Matthews J, Jenkinson L, McKinley G, Bouchard K, Reed J, Maukel LM, Oh P, Bertagnolli M, Ross MK, Ghisi GLM.

title: Cardiovascular and lipid parameters in pediatric inflammatory bowel disease: systematic review & meta-analysis.
authorString: Karatisidou V, Stoimeni A, Gkiourtzis N, Glava A, Saliakellis E, Fotoulaki M, Papadopoulou-Legbelou K.
abstractText: Although inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) may lead to an increased risk of cardiovascular disease, evidence regarding cardiovascular and lipid parameters in childhood is limited. We compared vascular markers, blood pressure and lipid levels between patients with pediatric or childhood-onset IBD and controls. This study was performed according to the Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions and adhered to PRISMA guidelines. A search of major databases (MEDLINE/PubMed, Scopus and Cochrane Library) was conducted from inception until April 24, 2025 (CRD420251039588). The study quality was evaluated using the modified Newcastle-Ottawa Scale; statistical analysis was conducted using R software. Reactive hyperemia index (RHI) was lower in three studies, involving 109 participants (MD - 0.25, 95% CI - 0.48 to - 0.02; p = 0.03). No statistically significant difference in carotid intima-media thickness (cIMT) was detected based on six studies. Primary systolic blood pressure (SBP) pooling across ten studies, was also not statistically significant (MD 0.84 mmHg, 95% CI - 0.67 to 2.35; p = 0.28). The exclusion of one influential study resulted in a small difference in SBP (MD 1.89 mmHg, 95% CI 1.17 to 2.61). Primary analyses detected no statistically significant differences in diastolic blood pressure or lipid levels. Lower RHI suggests possible early endothelial dysfunction, but the evidence is preliminary. No difference was observed in cIMT, DBP and lipid levels between the two groups. Future prospective cohort studies should investigate the longitudinal changes in these parameters, in order to elucidate whether early alterations lead, in the long-term, to increased cardiovascular morbidity in adulthood. • Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is characterized by persistent gastrointestinal inflammation and immune activation. • IBD may lead to an elevated risk of cardiovascular disease. However, limited data exist regarding cardiovascular parameters on pediatric IBD patients. • Lower Reactive Hyperemia Index (RHI) suggests possible endothelial dysfunction; carotid intima-media thickness (cIMT) and lipid levels remain inconclusive. • No statistically significant difference in cIMT was detected between participants with IBD and controls; primary systolic blood pressure (SBP) pooling was not statistically significant; a small increase appeared only after exclusion of one study.

title: Decompressive surgery in infants and very young children (≤ 3 years): A systematic review.
authorString: Ganesh S, Joseph J.

journal.title: Child's nervous system : ChNS : official journal of the International Society for Pediatric Neurosurgery

abstractText:
Background

Decompressive surgery in infants and very young children presents unique challenges related to cranial development, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) disturbances, and subsequent reconstruction. This systematic review evaluated the indications, operative techniques, postoperative complications, and outcomes of conventional decompressive craniectomy and bone-preserving expansile procedures in children aged ≤ 3 years.

Methods

PubMed, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library were systematically searched for English-language clinical studies involving age-eligible children. Study characteristics, operative details, complications, and outcomes were extracted and synthesized descriptively. Methodological quality was assessed using Joanna Briggs Institute checklists. Meta-analysis was not undertaken because of clinical and methodological heterogeneity.

Results

Of the 1970 identified records, 46 publications were included, predominantly case reports and small case series. Indications included traumatic brain injury, cerebrovascular events, hemorrhage, and other causes of severe cerebral swelling. Procedures comprised conventional bone-out decompression and various bone-preserving techniques. Hydrocephalus, subdural and extracranial fluid collections, CSF leakage, wound complications, and bone-related morbidity were reported. Conventional decompression introduced subsequent reconstruction requirements and potential bone-resorption complications. Bone-preserving approaches maintained native cranial bone but were not free of CSF-related complications, altered bone fusion, or later reconstructive procedures. Inconsistent outcome definitions, age-specific denominators, and follow-up prevented reliable comparative estimates.

Conclusion

Evidence on decompressive surgery in children aged ≤ 3 years remains limited by small, heterogeneous studies and inconsistent outcome reporting. Although both conventional and bone-preserving techniques are feasible, their comparative effectiveness remains uncertain. CSF-related complications and reconstructive morbidity warrant particular attention. Standardized complication reporting and long-term assessment of cranial growth and neurodevelopment are essential to guide surgical decision-making.

title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Cardiac Auscultation for Detecting Clinically Significant Valvular Heart Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Saeed H, Nasir TB, Rehman A, Majeed U, Hussain I, Khalid S, Tahirkheli NK.
abstractText: Early identification of clinically significant valvular heart disease (VHD) remains challenging because echocardiography is resource-intensive and conventional auscultation is operator-dependent. Artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled analysis of digital heart sounds has emerged as a promising screening strategy, but its overall diagnostic performance has not been systematically evaluated. We conducted a Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses of Diagnostic Test Accuracy studies-compliant systematic review and diagnostic test accuracy meta-analysis of studies evaluating AI-enabled cardiac auscultation against transthoracic echocardiography for detecting clinically significant VHD, defined according to each study's echocardiographic criteria. MEDLINE, Embase, and CENTRAL were searched through July 2026, and pooled sensitivity, specificity, summary receiver operating characteristic area under the curve, diagnostic odds ratio, and accuracy were estimated using random-effects models. Eight studies comprising 4374 analyzed participants were included. AI-enabled cardiac auscultation demonstrated a pooled sensitivity of 72% (95% CI 54-85%) and specificity of 82% (95% CI 74-88%) for detecting clinically significant VHD. The summary receiver operating characteristic area under the curve was 0.814 (95% CI 0.569-0.888), and the pooled diagnostic odds ratio was 11.39 (95% CI 3.76-34.47), corresponding to positive and negative likelihood ratios of approximately 4.0 and 0.34, respectively. Overall pooled diagnostic accuracy was 78% (95% CI 67-86%). Subgroup analyses demonstrated substantially higher sensitivity for studies evaluating isolated aortic stenosis than composite VHD (92% vs. 55%; P < 0.001), whereas specificity was comparable. AI-enabled cardiac auscultation demonstrates promising diagnostic performance for identifying clinically significant VHD and may serve as a front-line screening tool to prioritize patients for echocardiography. Future prospective multicenter studies using standardized recording protocols and external validation are needed before widespread clinical implementation.

title: Balloon-Expandable Versus Self-Expanding Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation in Patients with Bicuspid Aortic Valves: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Chidambaram DS, Manokar DP, Jebaraj D, P DM, V DM, Raja DD, Nitheshkumar D, G DS, E DS, Senguttuvan DN, Shah DAH, Vaikom S Mahadevan D.
abstractText:
Background/objectives

The comparative performance of balloon-expandable (BEV) and self-expanding (SEV) transcatheter heart valves in bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) stenosis remains uncertain.

Methods

We systematically reviewed contemporary BAV-TAVR literature published from 2015 to 2025. The broader qualitative evidence map comprised 69 reports, including device-specific and comparative cohorts; however, only studies with extractable arm-level BEV-versus-SEV data were eligible for quantitative comparative pooling.

Results

Three head-to-head cohorts contributed to early/30-day device success (BEV 302/353; SEV 160/181). The pooled RR for SEV versus BEV was 1.03 (95% CI 0.96-1.09; I2=0%). Two cohorts contributed to 30-day permanent pacemaker implantation (PPI), showing a numerically higher but non-significant risk with SEV (RR 2.01; 95% CI 0.93-4.37; I2=0%). Only one study provided compatible 30-day arm-level data for moderate-or-greater paravalvular leak (PVL), precluding pooling. Adjusted and single-arm observational evidence suggested possible platform-specific differences in hemodynamics, PVL and conduction outcomes, but these data were not interpreted as evidence of comparative equivalence or superiority.

Conclusions

Available head-to-head evidence does not demonstrate a clear difference in early device success between contemporary BEV and SEV in BAV, but the evidence is sparse, predominantly observational and imprecise. The findings should not be interpreted as proof of equivalence. Prospective comparative studies with standardized BAV phenotyping are required.

title: Anatomic feasibility of the Endo-Bentall and Endo-Wheat procedures: a systematic review.
authorString: Nana P, Apostolidis G, Panuccio G, Torrealba J, Chaveles A, Schäfer A, Brickwedel J, Kölbel T.
abstractText:
Background

The Endo-Bentall/Endo-Wheat approach could expand the invasive management of ascending pathologies in high-risk patients. This systematic review investigated the anatomic feasibility of the Endo-Bentall and Endo-Wheat in patients with diseases affecting the ascending aorta and aortic root.

Methods

A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus and CENTRAL databases from their conception to 15 July 2026 according to the PRISMA guidelines and PICO model was performed. Observational studies reporting on the anatomic feasibility of the Endo-Bentall/Endo-Wheat procedures using imaging evaluation of patients with type A aortic dissection (TAAD) or ascending aortic aneurysms were eligible. The risk of bias was assessed with the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. A narrative synthesis was chosen.

Results

From 356 reports, six retrospective studies (627 patients) were included; two evaluating the eligibility in patients with ascending aortic aneurysm (80; 12.7%) and four in patients with TAAD (547; 87.3%). Studies used high-quality computed tomography angiographies and dedicated software for the assessment. The eligibility of an Endo-Bentall in patients with ascending aortic aneurysm was 75.9%; reported in one study. The aortic annulus diameter was eligible in 78-100%. Adequate landing for bridging stents into the left main coronary artery (LMCA)was 89.6%. Distal landing into the ascending aorta was adequate in 88.0%, according to Rylski, while extending the repair into the arch could increase the applicability. The eligibility rate was 63.7-100% in the TAAD population. The use of an overexpanded valve could increase the eligibility. The aortic annulus diameter was eligible in 82-95.4% while adequate landing for bridging into the LMCA could be achieved in 83.3%. Distal landing into the ascending aorta was adequate in 14.0-100.0%.

Conclusions

According to the available evidence, an Endo-Bentall or Endo-Wheat approach seems feasible in almost 2/3 of patients with diseases affecting the proximal ascending aorta and aortic root. Further studies are needed.

title: Hidden Drowsiness in Wakefulness: Differences in Resting-State EEG Profiles in Natural Short Sleepers Versus Recommended Length Sleepers.
authorString: Cassim TZ, Williams PG, Baron K, Euler MJ.
abstractText: Chronic insufficient sleep affects cardiovascular, endocrine, immune and nervous systems and is linked to cognitive decline and increased mortality. Among habitual short sleepers, a subgroup known as natural short sleepers (NSS) report sleeping ≤ 6 h per night without experiencing subjective daytime dysfunction. However, discrepancies between subjective and objective markers of alertness raise questions about their true cognitive state. NSS have been described as high in behavioural activation, a phenotype overlapping with ADHD and mania in which dysregulation of resting-state brain arousal has been well documented. Despite these parallels, few studies have investigated the neurophysiological features of NSS. The current study examined resting-state EEG in NSS and recommended-length sleepers (RLS) during eyes-open conditions. Results showed that NSS exhibited significantly higher global alpha power and regionally steeper aperiodic exponents, particularly in occipital areas, both markers of increased drowsiness. Although global exponent values did not differ significantly, a significant Group × Region interaction was observed and NSS showed a trend toward increasing aperiodic exponents over time, suggesting less stable wakefulness under low-stimulation conditions. These findings point to subtle neurophysiological differences in NSS, raising the possibility that their perceived resilience to short sleep may mask underlying drowsiness.

title: Engineered Outer Membrane Vesicle Nanoengagers Potentiate NK Cell Immunotherapy through Immune Bridging and Mitochondrial Apoptosis Priming.
authorString: Yin S, Yu J, Li J, Wang Y, Li R, Tian F, Li Z.

journal.title: Molecular therapy : the journal of the American Society of Gene Therapy

abstractText: Natural killer (NK) cells hold considerable promise for cancer immunotherapy, but their efficacy is frequently restricted by poor tumor infiltration and insufficient tumor-specific recognition. Here, we present a tumor-responsive outer membrane vesicle (OMV)-based nanoengager that enhances NK cell-mediated antitumor immunity by combining immune-cell engagement with mitochondrial apoptosis priming. OMVs derived from Escherichia coli were engineered to display a bispecific engager (TKD-Huhf) on the vesicle surface via genetic membrane anchoring, and an MMP2-cleavable linker was incorporated to enable tumor microenvironment-responsive release, thereby coordinating OMV activity with engager-mediated immune bridging in a spatiotemporal manner. The OMVs sensitized tumor cells to NK-mediated killing by inducing mitochondrial apoptosis, characterized by cytochrome c release, MCL-1 downregulation, and mitochondrial membrane depolarization. Concurrently, released engager bridged NK and tumor cells, promoting NK-tumor-cell association and enhancing NK-cell-mediated cytotoxicity. Moreover, engineered TKD-Huhf OMVs significantly suppressed tumor growth in both A20 lymphoma and 4T1 breast cancer models, accompanied by enhanced infiltration and activation of NK cells and T cells within tumors. Collectively, this study establishes engineered OMVs as a modular immunotherapeutic platform that couples death sensitization with immune synapse reinforcement, providing a mechanistically grounded and rational strategy to improve NK cell-directed anti-tumor immunotherapy.

title: Complex Endovascular Repair for Genetically-Triggered Aortic Disease in Italy (CENTRAL Multicentric Registry).
authorString: Ferrer C, D'Oria M, Gargiulo M, Gallitto E, Kahlberg A, Valente FBA, Antonello M, Piazza M, Tshomba Y, Tinelli G, Bertoglio L, Melloni A, Pratesi G, Esposito D, De Donato G, Simonte G, Isernia G, Veraldi GF, Martelli E, Lepidi S, Giudice R, For CENTRAL Study Collaborators.

journal.title: Journal of endovascular therapy : an official journal of the International Society of Endovascular Specialists

abstractText:
Background

The role of fenestrated and branched endovascular aortic repair (F/BEVAR) in patients with genetically triggered aortic disease and connective tissue disorders (CTDs) remains controversial due to concerns regarding long-term durability and disease progression. This multicenter study aimed to evaluate early and mid-term outcomes of F/BEVAR in patients with CTD treated for thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysms (TAAAs).

Methods

This retrospective multicenter study included all consecutive CTD patients with genetically triggered aortic disease undergoing F/BEVAR for TAAA between 2013 and 2024 at 12 Italian centers. Primary endpoints were technical and clinical success, early and mid-term survival, and major adverse events (MAEs). Secondary endpoints included target vessel instability and the need for reintervention. Survival and freedom from adverse events were estimated using Kaplan-Meier analysis.

Results

A total of 45 CTD patients (62.2% male; mean age, 56.4 ± 11.7 years) were treated with F/BEVAR. Marfan syndrome was present in 80% of patients, and 68.9% were treated for post-dissection TAAA. Most patients presented with type II TAAA (91.1%), and 88.9% had undergone at least 1 prior aortic operation. Technical and clinical success were achieved in 86.6% and 82.2% of cases, respectively. Early mortality and MAEs occurred in 4.4% of patients. During a mean clinical follow-up of 35.0 ± 33.9 months, estimated overall survival at 12, 24, and 36 months was 90.0%, 86.7%, and 79.2%, respectively, with no aorta-related deaths. At a mean imaging follow-up of 33.8 ± 32.2 months, target vessel patency was 98.8%. Target vessel instability occurred in 40% of patients, and 42.2% required 1 or more secondary interventions. Reintervention-free survival at 12, 24, and 36 months was 75.6%, 72.4%, and 59.0%, respectively. No baseline, anatomic, or procedural variable independently predicted late adverse outcomes.

Conclusions

In this cohort of CTD patients, predominantly treated in complex redo settings, F/BEVAR demonstrated acceptable early and mid-term outcomes. Late adverse events and reinterventions were frequent but consistent with the natural history of CTD-related aortic disease and were not driven by identifiable baseline factors. These findings support the role of F/BEVAR as a valuable approach within a comprehensive, lifelong management strategy for CTD patients rather than as a definitive alternative to open surgery (OS).Clinical ImpactPatients with genetically triggered aortic disease often require multiple interventions throughout their lifetime because of the progressive nature of the underlying aortopathy. In this context, fenestrated/branched endovascular aortic repair (F/BEVAR) should not be considered an alternative to open surgery, but rather a complementary approach within the long-term management of these patients. This multicenter study provides one of the largest dedicated experiences with F/BEVAR in this challenging population, showing that acceptable early and mid-term outcomes can be achieved even in complex redo and post-dissection settings. These findings support the integration of endovascular techniques into individualized, lifelong aortic treatment strategies at experienced centers, acknowledging the need for continued surveillance and secondary interventions.

title: Fermentable dietary fiber controls blood pressure by lowering large intestinal pH and activating the proton-sensing receptor GPR65.
authorString: Xie L, R Muralitharan R, Dinakis E, Antonacci S, Leung KC, McArdle Z, Mirabito Colafella K, Nakai M, Paterson M, Peh A, Jama HA, Salimova E, Anderson D, Barbaro-Wahl A, Knezic A, Ang C, Alam MJ, Yap YA, Creek DJ, Robert R, O'Donnell JA, Mackay CR, Marques FZ.
abstractText: High blood pressure (BP) is the most common cause of death globally due to increased risk of cardiovascular disease. Fermentable dietary fibers regulate BP through gut microbial production of short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), acidic metabolites. How SCFAs regulate BP remains unclear. Here we show that, in a phenome-wide association study, the proton-sensing G protein-coupled receptor GPR65 gene is associated with human hypertension and cardiorenal phenotypes. Fermentable dietary fibers, delivered as a type 2 resistant starch (RS2), regulated luminal and interstitial tissue pH in the large intestine through gut microbial SCFA production in mice. High RS2 intake reduced pH, increased cAMP production via GPR65 signaling and CREB phosphorylation, and restricted the release of pro-hypertensive inflammatory cytokines by CD8<sup>+</sup> T cells. Gpr65<sup>-/-</sup> mice spontaneously developed hypertension, cardiac and renal hypertrophy, and fibrosis. The benefits of a high-RS2 diet, which prevented these effects, were reduced in Gpr65<sup>-/-</sup> mice. Adoptive transfers revealed that GPR65 deficiency in CD8<sup>+</sup> T cells explained this phenotype.

title: Association of Mediterranean-DASH intervention for neurodegenerative delay (MIND) diet with cognition and total and cardiovascular mortality: results from the HAPIEE cohort.
authorString: Wong MMH, Yau YC, Kozela M, Pajak A, Pikhart H, Bobak M, Stefler D.
abstractText: The Mediterranean-DASH Intervention for Neurodegenerative Delay (MIND) dietary pattern, developed to slow cognitive decline, has been linked to cardiometabolic benefits and lower mortality. Its associations with cognition and mortality have not been studied in Eastern European populations. This study aimed to assess the relationship between MIND diet, cognition and mortality in Eastern European adults. Data from 15,427 adults aged 45-69 years at baseline in the Czech and Polish cohorts of the Health, Alcohol and Psychosocial factors in Eastern Europe prospective cohort were analyzed. Baseline MIND diet scores (range 0-15), derived from validated food frequency questionnaires, were classified into three groups: low (<6), moderate (6-7), and high (>7). Trained nurses assessed cognitive domains at baseline. Deaths were ascertained via national registries. Multivariable regressions estimated the MIND diet-mortality and MIND diet-cognition associations, adjusting for sociodemographic and lifestyle characteristics. Over about 20 years of follow-up, 3,792 deaths occurred. After controlling for age and sex, MIND diet adherence was associated with lower total and CVD mortality and better cognitive outcomes. However, after full adjustment, the associations were no longer significant (high vs low adherence for all-cause mortality: HR = 1.01, 95%CI:0.93-1.10; for CVD mortality: HR = 1.01, 95%CI:0.88-1.16), and only the positive association with verbal fluency remained significant (high vs low: coefficient 0.058, SE 0.024, p = 0.015). This study of MIND diet in Central and Eastern European cohort did not find clear evidence on mortality, but the results on cognition, particularly verbal fluency, were generally consistent with the literature.

title: Ginsenoside Rh1 alleviates myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury via macrophage polarization and ERK pathway modulation.
authorString: Wang J, Li N, Fang H, Li Z, Ye J, Wang M, Sun G.
abstractText: Inflammation plays a crucial role in the early stages of myocardial ischemia-reperfusion (MI/R) injury, with macrophages being key contributors to this process. Ginsenoside Rh1 (G-Rh1) is a danmarane-based tetracyclic triterpenoid saponin found in plants of the genus Panax, such as ginseng and Panax notoginseng. G-Rh1 can be absorbed by the human body and is beneficial for protecting the heart and has anti-inflammatory effects. This study established rat model of MI/R induced by ligation of the left anterior descending artery, and administered G-Rh1 and the positive drug diltiazem (DTZ) by gavage. The results showed that G-Rh1 treatment could reduce the area of myocardial infarction, improve cardiac function, alleviate myocardial inflammatory infiltration and pathological damage. In addition, in the G-Rh1 treatment group, the M1-type macrophage marker was significantly down-regulated, while the M2-type macrophage marker was significantly up-regulated. G-Rh1 may exert protective effects on myocardial tissue in association with regulation of macrophage polarization. Meanwhile, G-Rh1 inhibited the activation of the ERK pathway after LPS-induced polarization of macrophages. In RAW264.7 macrophages, G-Rh1 reduced the mRNA expression levels of M1-type biomarkers induced by LPS and reduced the number of M1-type macrophages. Interestingly, under LPS stimulation, G-Rh1 inhibited the activation of ERK pathway and the polarization of M1 macrophages, corresponding with reduced production of inflammatory cytokines. In summary, these findings indicate that the cardioprotective effect of G-Rh1 is associated with the reduction of M1-polarized macrophages, the increase of M2-polarized macrophages and the inhibition of the ERK signaling pathway. This effect subsequently alleviates inflammation caused by MI/R and improves cardiac dysfunction.

title: The atherosclerotic cardiovascular-kidney-liver-metabolic burden in the Asia-Pacific, 1990-2050: A global burden of disease 2023 analysis.
authorString: Nagarajan S, Himan HR, Tan EE, Kok J, Chen Y, Jayabaskaran J, Kong G, Chew HSJ, Muthiah MD, Matthias T, Khan MS, Chew D, Mamas MA, Zhou X, Hausenloy D, Richards AM, Lip GYH, Chan MY, Chew NWS, Asia-Pacific Cardiovascular Research (ASPIRE) Network.
abstractText:
Background

Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death worldwide, with the Asia-Pacific region bearing over half of this burden. The cardiovascular-kidney-liver-metabolic (CKLM) framework unifies the interrelated conditions of cardiovascular disease (CVD), chronic kidney disease (CKD), metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and obesity, which synergistically contribute to heightened cardiovascular risk. However, the combined CKLM burden in the region has not been characterised.

Methods

Using the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023, we examined mortality and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) of CKLM diseases across 39 Asia-Pacific countries from 1990 to 2023, with forecasts to 2050. The CKLM burden was organized into metabolic antecedents (comprising CKD, MASLD, T2DM and obesity) and downstream atherosclerotic CVD (comprising ischemic heart disease, stroke, aortic aneurysm, and peripheral artery disease).

Findings

In 2023, the Asia-Pacific recorded 286.9 million CKLM-related DALYs (53.2% of global burden), with an age-standardised DALY rate of 6390.9 per 100,000 population. From 1990 to 2023, crude DALYs rose by 78.7%, outpacing the global trends (61.1%), while age-standardised DALYs fell by 25.0% - driven by improvements in atherosclerotic CVD (-35.2%) but counterbalanced by a 20.4% rise in metabolic antecedents. By 2050, age-standardised DALY rates are projected to show a 7.0% point-estimate increase regionally against an estimated 14.9% global decline, with metabolic antecedents likely to expand from 29.9% to 36.2% of the total burden between 2026 and 2050. Intraregional disparities exist across sociodemographic strata, subregions, and age-sex categories. Risk-deleted analyses identify high systolic blood pressure, high fasting plasma glucose, and dietary risks as the highest-yield modifiable targets.

Interpretation

The worsening Asia-Pacific CKLM trajectory is decoupling from improving global trends, driven by a compositional shift from atherosclerotic CVD toward upstream metabolic antecedents. Integrated interventions addressing multiple key modifiable risks are needed.

title: Temporal changes of ECG progression in arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy.
authorString: Sriskandarajah R, Minopoli TC, Canu A, Maritsa D, Tardo D, Halim K, Casian M, Abioye D, Morris-Rosendhal D, Malhotra A, Specterman M, Tome M, Papadakis M, Sharma S, Behr ER, Finocchiaro G.
abstractText:
Background

Exercise may influence phenotypic expression in arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy (ACM). We investigated ECG progression in a large ACM cohort, focusing on exercise exposure.

Methods

Of 202 retrospectively assessed patients, including genotype-positive/phenotype-negative individuals, 163 had ≥2 analysable ECGs and were stratified into "sedentary/low" and "moderate/high" exercise groups based on post-diagnosis exercise intensity. The primary composite endpoint included major ventricular arrhythmias, appropriate implantable cardioverter-defibrillator interventions, sudden cardiac arrest and sudden cardiac death.

Results

Among 163 patients, (56% male; mean age 47 ± 16y)almost one-third (n = 52, 32%) continued moderate/high-intensity exercise and 107 (66%) exhibited abnormal baseline ECGs (anterior T-wave inversion (ATWI) n = 42, 26%). At follow-up, 9% developed new ATWI and 45% demonstrated TWI progression (TWI deepening and/or extension). PKP2 carriers more frequently demonstrated ATWI progression (p = 0.002). Baseline low QRS voltages (LQRSV) were found in 12%; 6% developed new LQRSV during follow-up and 23% exhibited substantial total limb‑lead QRSV reduction. Among 22 genotype-positive/phenotype-negative individuals, none developed ATWI progression or experienced the primary arrhythmic event. Abnormal ECG prevalence increased within the moderate/high-intensity exercise group (55% to 72%; p = 0.027), although exercise was not independently associated with composite ECG progression (adjusted OR 1.49, 95% CI 0.72-3.11). Over 4.6 ± 2.5 years, 28 patients (17%) experienced primary events. Baseline inferior TWI (HR 3.79, 95% CI 1.60-8.97, p = 0.002) and total limb lead QRSV <3 mV (HR 2.40, 95% CI 1.05-5.48, p = 0.037) were independently associated with arrhythmic risk.

Conclusions

ECG abnormalities evolve across the ACM spectrum. Exercise was not independently associated with ECG progression. Baseline inferior TWI and reduced total limb‑lead QRSV may aid arrhythmic risk assessment.

title: Clinical characteristics and prognosis of heart failure patients referred to cardiac rehabilitation: SEC-EXCELENTE-IC registry.
authorString: Esteban-Fernández A, Bonilla-Palomas JL, Muñiz J, González-Manzanares R, Recio-Mayoral A, Mirabet S, de Blas-Ruiz C, Castro-Conde A, Palau P, Anguita-Sánchez M, Anguita-Gámez M.
abstractText:
Introduction and objectives

To assess the referral rate to cardiac rehabilitation (CR), the clinical profile of referred vs nonreferred patients, and the association between referral and clinical events in Spanish heart failure (HF) units.

Methods

The SEC-EXCELENTE-IC registry is a prospective, multicenter observational cohort of patients with HF in units accredited by the Spanish Society of Cardiology. Patients were classified according to CR referral and were followed up for up to 400 days for all-cause death, HF hospitalization or decompensation, and the combined endpoint of death or HF hospitalization, with outcomes analyzed using Cox regression.

Results

Of 2236 patients, 219 (9.8%) were referred to CR. Referred patients were younger (65.2  ±  11.7 vs 71.7  ±  12.2 years), more often male (73.5% vs 63.2%) and more frequently had an ischemic etiology (50.5% vs 28.8%), fewer comorbidities and more frequent use of quadruple therapy (59.4% vs 46.0%); 74.4% had HF with reduced ejection fraction (11.9% had HF with preserved ejection fraction, and 13.7% HF with mildly reduced ejection fraction). The lower crude rate of the combined endpoint (HR, 0.75; 95%CI, 0.56-1.01) was no longer observed after adjustment (HR, 0.99; 95%CI, 0.71-1.38), with consistent findings in sensitivity analyses.

Conclusions

CR referral was infrequent and preferentially directed toward younger patients with ischemic HF with reduced ejection fraction, a lower comorbidity burden, and optimized therapy, whereas older patients, patients with multimorbidity, and those with HF with preserved ejection fraction remained underrepresented. The lower crude event rate was no longer observed after adjustment for measured baseline characteristics, and the observational design does not allow conclusions on the effect of CR itself.

title: Traditional Chinese Medicine-Derived Natural Products: Potential Effects on Mitochondrial Energy Metabolism in Heart Failure.
authorString: Yu H, Li M, Wang Q, Chen L, Wu Y, Zhan S, Chen X, Cai Y, Meng L, Chen H, Xu Y.
abstractText:
Background

Heart failure (HF), the end-stage of cardiovascular disease (CVD), affects over 64 million people globally. There is an alarming trend of earlier onset, which poses a substantial healthcare burden. Although guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) has significantly improved clinical outcomes, residual morbidity and mortality remain considerable, highlighting the need for additional therapeutic strategies. Mitochondrial energy metabolism (MEM) plays an important role in HF pathophysiology and represents a potential therapeutic target. Traditional Chinese Medicine-derived natural products (TCM-derived NPs) contain diverse bioactive constituents that may influence myocardial energy metabolism and related pathological processes, warranting further investigation into their potential role in HF management.

Purpose

This review aims to synthesize current evidence on the involvement of MEM in HF and the potential regulatory effects of TCM-derived NPs. It further integrates mechanistic evidence with exploratory network pharmacology and molecular docking analyses to identify candidate compound-target relationships and discuss their translational implications.

Methods

The following keywords were used: "heart failure," "traditional Chinese medicine," "ATP synthesis," "oxidative phosphorylation," "fatty acid oxidation," "glucose metabolism," "mitochondrial membrane potential," "reactive oxygen species," "energy metabolism," "mitochondrial dynamics," "calcium signaling," and "energy coupling." Potential targets of NPs were obtained from the Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) Systems Pharmacology Database and Analysis Platform. We collected disease-related targets from Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man, GeneCards, and the Therapeutic Target Database. Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analysis was performed using the Database for Annotation, Visualization and Integrated Discovery (DAVID). Protein-protein interaction (PPI) networks were constructed using STRING and analyzed in Cytoscape 3.10.0 to identify candidate hub genes. Ten representative bioactive compounds were separately examined through exploratory molecular docking with the candidate hub proteins.

Results

Herb-frequency analysis of 132 clinical studies identified 15 high-frequency Chinese medicinal herbs for subsequent computational analysis. The literature synthesis highlighted oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS), fatty acid and glucose metabolism as key processes involved in myocardial energetic remodeling in HF. Separately, KEGG enrichment analysis identified pathways related to metabolic regulation, cellular stress, and inflammation, including lipid and atherosclerosis, PI3K-Akt, HIF-1, insulin, and TNF signaling pathways. PPI analysis prioritized AKT1, JUN, TP53, MAPK1, and MAPK3 in the MEM-related network and STAT3, TNF, TP53, IL6, and ESR1 in the inflammation-metabolism crosstalk network, yielding nine unique candidate hub genes after deduplication. Molecular docking of ten representative bioactive compounds with these nine candidate proteins yielded predicted docking scores ranging from -4.5 to -9.7kcal/mol.

Conclusion

The available evidence supports MEM as an important component of HF pathophysiology and suggests that selected TCM-derived NPs may influence multiple MEM-related processes relevant to HF. By integrating mechanistic, clinical, and computational evidence, this review provides a structured framework for understanding NPs-MEM-HF relationships and offers a basis for future mechanistic validation and clinical translation.

title: Failure to Rescue After Coronary Bypass Surgery: 1,613,669 Patients from the Society of Thoracic Surgeons Adult Cardiac Surgery Database.
authorString: Hameed I, Kurlansky PA, Jalali P, Chou A, Lieu D, Ermer T, Zaky M, Schwann TA, Gaudino M, Habib RH, Pelletier MP.
abstractText: Failure to rescue (FTR), death after a postoperative complication, is an emerging quality metric because hospital mortality differences reflect complication management more than complication occurrence. Contemporary benchmarks for isolated coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) are lacking. We hypothesized that FTR varies between hospitals independently of patient risk. We analyzed 1,613,669 isolated CABG operations at 1,165 hospitals in the Society of Thoracic Surgeons (STS) Adult Cardiac Surgery Database (2014-2024). FTR was death during the index hospitalization or within 30 days after stroke, renal failure, prolonged ventilation, or reoperation for bleeding. The primary analysis was multivariable logistic regression among complicated patients, adjusted for a priori covariates from the 2023 STS risk model, with hospitals grouped into observed-to-expected (O/E) mortality tertiles. Of 1,613,669 patients, 147,852 (9.2%) had at least one major complication; 23,025 died, yielding a national FTR rate of 15.6%. Across O/E tertiles, FTR rose from 11.9% to 20.0% (1.68-fold) while complication frequency rose from 8.0% to 11.0% (1.38-fold). Predictors included emergent status (odds ratio 4.57, 95% CI 3.88-5.37); highest-tertile hospitals had greater FTR odds (2.33, 2.10-2.58). FTR rose from 12.5% (2014) to 17.3% (2020-2021) and was 16.1% (2024) (odds ratio per year 1.03, 95% CI 1.02-1.03; p<0.001), while mean predicted mortality fell from 1.92% to 1.72%. FTR remains a substantial contributor to operative mortality after isolated CABG, with wide inter-hospital variation driven by institutional rescue capacity. Reducing mortality may require investment in early recognition systems, protocolized escalation pathways, and dedicated cardiovascular ICU infrastructure.

title: Lung-to-heart delivery: Inhalable nanomedicine for cardiovascular disease treatment.
authorString: Li J, Peng F, Wang S, Zhou F, Qiu Z, Yuan J, Liao T, Yang Y, Li C.
abstractText: Cardiovascular diseases remain a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Although current pharmacological treatments have improved clinical outcomes, most primarily alleviate symptoms or modulate downstream pathways and have limited capacity to correct the underlying disease processes. Peptide- and nucleic acid-based therapeutics offer greater molecular specificity, but their clinical use is hampered by poor stability, low bioavailability, inefficient cardiac delivery, and off-target exposure after systemic administration. Pulmonary delivery provides a non-invasive alternative that bypasses hepatic first-pass metabolism, enables rapid absorption, and may reduce systemic adverse effects. However, effective Lung-to-Heart delivery requires careful control of aerosolization, aerodynamic deposition, pulmonary retention, biological barrier transport, and myocardial accumulation. These considerations have stimulated growing interest in inhalable nanoparticle-based cardiovascular therapeutics, yet the relevant design principles and translational evidence remain scattered. In this review, we summarize the physicochemical properties, biomaterials, formulation methods, and inhaler technologies that govern the pulmonary deposition and biological fate of inhalable nanoparticles. We discuss their interactions with airway mucus, mucociliary clearance, pulmonary immune surveillance, and the alveolar-capillary barrier, as well as strategies for enhancing myocardial targeting. We further review emerging applications in heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and cardiomyopathy, with particular emphasis on the delivery of peptides, nucleic acids, and other precision therapeutics. Finally, we examine key challenges in pulmonary safety, pharmacokinetics, manufacturing reproducibility, scale-up, and regulatory evaluation. This review connects pulmonary drug delivery with cardiovascular nanomedicines and provides a practical basis for developing non-invasive, rapid-acting, and myocardium-targeted therapies.

title: Brominated polyunsaturated lipids from the marine sponge Xestospongia sp.: dual TDP1/TDP2 inhibitory activity and cardioprotective potential.
authorString: Lei YH, Xie J, Hao AL, Liu BB, Gao X, Shi YY, Zhang MD, An LK, Liu ZQ, Zhang CX.
abstractText: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) and cancer remain the leading causes of global mortality. The overexpression of TDP1 (The DNA-repair enzymes tyrosyl-DNA causes tumor drug resistance, so it is a promising strategy to inhibit TDP1/TDP2 in order to overcome tumor drug-resistance. Marine brominated polyunsaturated lipids are a class of bioactive secondary metabolites with broad pharmacological potential, yet their dual activities against TDP1/ TDP2 and myocardial injury remain largely unexplored. Using a targeted isolation strategy guided by Global Natural Products Social Molecular Networking (GNPS) and characteristic bromine isotope peak ratios, we isolated seven new brominated polyunsaturated lipids, xestonarienes A-G (1-7), along with twelve known analogs (8-19), from the sponge Xestospongia sp. collected at Weizhou Island, China. Their structures were elucidated using 1D and 2D NMR spectroscopy, high-resolution electrospray ionization mass spectrometry (HRESIMS), and literature comparison. The bioactivity revealed that compound 1 significantly inhibited both Tyrosyl-DNA phosphodiesterases 1 (TDP1, IC50 = 14.0 ± 2.2 μM) and Tyrosyl-DNA phosphodiesterases 2 (TDP2, IC50 = 7.2 ± 0.8 μM), while compound 18 showed potent inhibition against TDP1 (IC50 = 6.3 ± 1.9 μM). Furthermore, compounds 8-17 exhibited low cardiomyocyte toxicity at 10 μM, and 10 and 15 more significantly improved H9c2 cell viability under oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) than the positive control. Network pharmacology, molecular docking, and GO/KEGG pathway enrichment analyses were employed to explore the potential mechanisms of action. These proved that brominated polyunsaturated lipids function as potent, dual TDP1/TDP2 inhibitors and cardioprotective agents.

title: Intraoperative serum sodium variation and postoperative complications: a single-center prospective cohort study in pediatric cardiac surgeries.
authorString: de Mello EG, de Barros GA, da Costa JM, Cascudo MM, Módolo CL, Junior PDN, Alves RL, Módolo NS.
abstractText: To assess intraoperative serum sodium variation in children undergoing low- to moderate-risk cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) and examine its association with a composite postoperative outcome. A total of 214 children were evaluated. Intraoperative serum sodium variation was defined as the difference between the highest and lowest observed concentrations. Its association with the composite outcome - defined as neurological, renal, cardiac, or pulmonary complications and/or death - was assessed using univariate and multivariable analyses. Mortality was additionally evaluated in exploratory unadjusted analyses. Eighty-three children (38.8%) experienced the composite postoperative outcome. Median (interquartile range) intraoperative serum sodium variation was greater in patients with the composite outcome than in those without it (15.0 [10.2-20.0] vs. 8.0 [[5.0-12.0] mmol/L, p < 0.001). In exploratory analyses, variation was also greater among non-survivors than survivors (24.0 [20.0-26.5] vs. 10.0 [6.0-15.0] mmol/L, p < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, sodium variation remained independently associated with the composite outcome (OR, 1.13; 95% CI, 1.06-1.19), together with CPB duration, peak intraoperative arterial lactate level, and body weight. Greater intraoperative serum sodium variation was independently associated with a higher probability of the composite postoperative outcome in children undergoing cardiac surgery with CPB. Exploratory unadjusted analysis also demonstrated greater sodium variation among non-survivors; however, the limited number of deaths precluded adjusted mortality analysis.

title: Etomidate vs Propofol for Anesthetic Induction: Association With 30-Day Mortality and Postoperative Complications in a Propensity Score-Matched Retrospective Cohort Study.
authorString: Kachhwaha A, Applegate RL, Singh PN, Pandey P, McCabe MD.
abstractText: Etomidate is commonly used for induction in hemodynamically unstable patients to preserve cardiovascular stability. However, concerns persist regarding potential adverse outcomes, including adrenal suppression and increased mortality. We evaluated whether intravenous anesthetic induction with etomidate was independently associated with adverse postoperative outcomes as compared to propofol induction. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 155,667 adult surgical patients undergoing induction with etomidate or propofol at our academic health system. Patients younger than 18 years of age, those receiving preoperative mechanical ventilation, and those with American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status VI were excluded. The primary outcome was all-cause 30-day mortality; secondary outcomes included sepsis, acute coronary syndrome (ACS), cardiogenic shock, and acute kidney injury (AKI). Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for demographic, comorbidity, physiologic, and surgical factors. Given substantial baseline imbalance between induction groups, propensity score matching (1:1) using the same covariates was performed. Sensitivity analyses included adjustment for neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, complete-case analyses, and interaction testing. A total of 155,667 patients met inclusion criteria, including 3846 (2.5%) who received etomidate and 151,821 (97.5%) who received propofol. Thirty-day mortality occurred in 1151 patients (0.74%). Unadjusted mortality was higher in the etomidate group (227/3846 [5.9%]) than in the propofol group (924/151,821 [0.61%]). After multivariable adjustment, etomidate use remained independently associated with increased 30-day mortality (aOR 1.44; 95% CI, 1.21-1.72; P < 0.001). Propensity score matching (n = 3832 per group) reduced the average standardized mean difference from 0.398 before matching to 0.023 after matching. The association persisted in the matched cohort (aOR 1.43; 95% CI, 1.14-1.78; P = 0.002), with observed mortality of 225/3832 (5.9%) among etomidate recipients and 157/3832 (4.1%) among propofol recipients, corresponding to an absolute risk difference of 1.8% and a number needed to harm of 56. In the matched cohort, etomidate was also associated with higher odds of sepsis (aOR 1.28; 95% CI, 1.08-1.52), acute coronary syndrome (aOR 1.24; 95% CI, 1.09-1.41), cardiogenic shock (aOR 1.56; 95% CI, 1.21-2.01), and acute kidney injury (aOR 1.27; 95% CI, 1.11-1.45). Post-induction hypotension was lower in the etomidate group (aOR 0.40, 95% CI 0.32-0.49; P < 0.001). Findings were consistent across sensitivity analyses. Etomidate induction was associated with increased 30-day mortality and major postoperative complications. Given the observational design, results should be interpreted with caution.

title: Impact of Early Reexploration on Patient Outcomes Following Cardiac Surgery.
authorString: Großmann C, Leschinsky O, Krasivskyi I, Kuhn EW, Bakhtiary F, Conradi L, Wahlers TCW, Eghbalzadeh K.
abstractText: Reexploration after cardiac surgery remains a rare but serious complication and consequently leads to higher morbidity and mortality. To prevent hemodynamic instability and compromised outcome early identification and treatment are crucial. In this retrospective single-center cohort study, we analyzed all consecutive patients with reexploration after elective cardiac surgery to evaluate the timing and outcome of reexploration.Between January 2012 and June 2022, a total of 520 out of 22,473 patients required reexploration following elective cardiac surgery (2.3%). Patients were stratified as follows: an early reexploration group, defined as reexploration ≤12 hours after cardiac surgery, including n = 321 patients (group 1) and a late reexploration group, defined as reexploration occurring >12 hours after the index procedure, including n = 193 patients (group 2). There were no significant differences in baseline characteristics such as age, Euroscore, or preoperative anticoagulation.Events in group 2 occurred significantly more often due to cardiac tamponade (43.8% vs. 20.4%, p ≤ 0.001). Patients in group 2 had a higher incidence of postoperative dialysis (37.0% vs. 17.1%, p ≤ 0.001) and an extended overall hospital stay (median 21.5 vs. 15.0 days, p ≤ 0.001). In-hospital mortality was also significantly increased in patients in group 2 (31.1% vs. 15.3%, p ≤ 0.001).In conclusion, timing of reexploration after cardiac surgery has a substantial impact on patient outcomes. We found that in patients with a late reexploration the postoperative complications and mortality are significantly higher than in patients with early reexploration. This emphasizes the importance of timely decision-making regarding reexploration to improve patient prognosis.

title: The ErbB4 Agonist JK07 Attenuates Heart Failure-Related Gene Expression and Activates Reparative Cardiac Pathways in a Murine HFrEF Model.
authorString: Civati C, Van den Bogaert S, Goovaerts BK, Cools JMT, McNally JP, Dong J, De Keulenaer GW, Segers VFM.
abstractText: Selective activation of the neuregulin-1 (NRG-1)/ErbB pathway is a promising strategy for cardiac repair in heart failure (HF), but recombinant NRG-1 therapies are limited by poor stability and nonselective receptor activation. JK07 is a novel biologic that combines the epidermal growth factor-like domain of NRG-1 with an ErbB3-antagonist antibody, enabling preferential ErbB4 activation. In a murine myocardial infarction-induced HF model (left ventricular ejection fraction <40%), mice received single or repeated doses of JK07 (1 mg/kg) or vehicle. Cardiac structure and cellular responses were assessed using echocardiography, histology, and single-nucleus RNA sequencing. JK07 reduced interstitial fibrosis and increased capillary density while inducing robust, transient, cell-specific transcriptional responses, most pronounced 1 day after treatment. Cardiomyocytes showed enhanced ErbB4 expression and metabolic pathways, fibroblasts adopted reparative phenotypes, and endothelial cells exhibited transient angiogenic activation. JK07 also preserved mitochondrial respiration in cardiomyocytes under inflammatory stress, supporting ErbB4 activation as a potential therapeutic strategy for HF.

title: The right heart blind spot: right ventricular dysfunction, tricuspid regurgitation velocity, and mortality in a critical-care echocardiography study.
authorString: Hernandez C, Odukudu GD, Fay C, Brodeur S, Henriques King M.

journal.title: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care

abstractText:
Background

The Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score does not directly assess right ventricular (RV) function or pulmonary pressure.

Objectives

To examine associations of RV dysfunction and tricuspid regurgitation (TR) velocity with mortality across total SOFA bands and in patients with low cardiovascular SOFA.

Methods

We studied adults in MIMIC-IV-ECHO with interpretable RV function and echocardiography within seven days of ICU admission, retaining one eligible stay per patient. Logistic models adjusted for first-day total SOFA, age, sex, left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), and Charlson index. We also examined patients with cardiovascular SOFA 0-1 and no recorded first-day continuous vasoactive treatment.

Results

Among 19,686 patients, 3393 (17.2%) died in hospital. In 12,882 patients with low cardiovascular SOFA, severe RV dysfunction (adjusted odds ratio 2.30, 95% CI 1.69-3.13) and higher TR velocity (OR 1.46 per 1 m/s, 95% CI 1.30-1.65) were associated with mortality. High TR velocity with RV dysfunction was associated with 9.61 percentage points higher adjusted mortality than low measured TR velocity with normal RV function (95% CI 6.19-13.02). At total SOFA 0-4, TR velocity >3.4 m/s compared with measured velocity ≤2.8 m/s was associated with higher model-adjusted mortality (risk ratio 1.74, 95% CI 1.41-2.15; risk difference 4.43 percentage points, 95% CI 2.46-6.39).

Conclusion

RV dysfunction and elevated TR velocity, suggestive of pulmonary hypertension, were associated with mortality at low cardiovascular SOFA. Elevated TR velocity also marked higher observed mortality at low total SOFA.

title: Diagnostic accuracy of bicycle ergometry for ischemic heart disease using stress computed tomography myocardial perfusion imaging with vasodilator testing as the reference standard.
authorString: Marzoog BA, Chomakhidze P, Kopylov P.

journal.title: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care

abstractText: Exercise bicycle ergometry remains widely available for suspected ischemic heart disease (IHD), but its accuracy against stress computed tomography myocardial perfusion (CTP) imaging is uncertain. To evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of bicycle ergometry for detecting stress-induced myocardial perfusion defects on adenosine triphosphate stress CTP. This prospective, single-center, observational diagnostic accuracy study included 80 adults aged ≥40 years with suspected IHD/chronic coronary syndrome, written informed consent, and protocol-defined pre-test probability of IHD between 1% and 33%. Participants with diabetes mellitus, recent acute coronary syndrome or myocardial infarction, acute inflammatory disease, major respiratory disease, contraindications to exercise testing, radiocontrast or adenosine triphosphate allergy, eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m², or other protocol-defined non-inclusion criteria were not enrolled. Recruitment was eligibility-based and was not documented as consecutive. Bicycle ergometry was the index test. Stress-induced myocardial perfusion defect on CTP was the reference standard. In the primary analysis, only clearly positive bicycle ergometry was classified as index-test positive; suspicious/equivocal and negative tests were classified as non-positive. A sensitivity analysis classified suspicious/equivocal tests as positive. Stress CTP showed perfusion defects in 31/80 participants. In the primary analysis, sensitivity was 12.90% (95% CI, 3.63-29.83%), specificity 73.47% (58.92-85.05%), LR+ 0.49 (0.17-1.36), LR- 1.19 (0.96-1.47), and accuracy 50.00% (38.60-61.40%). When suspicious/equivocal tests were classified as positive, sensitivity was 48.39% (30.15-66.94%), specificity 53.06% (38.27-67.47%), LR+ 1.03 (0.64-1.65), LR- 0.97 (0.63-1.50), and accuracy 51.25% (39.81-62.59%). In this cohort, bicycle ergometry showed limited accuracy for detecting ATP stress CTP-defined myocardial perfusion defects; these findings should not be generalized to ischemic heart disease overall.

title: Safety, Signal Quality, and Patient Satisfaction With Insertable Loop Recorder Implantation by Specialized Electrophysiology Nurses: Prospective Observational Study.
authorString: Lillo Rodenas I, Reig Gómez H, Ajo Ferrer R, Carrillo Molina ÁM, Ajo Ferrer M, Ghodbane Kiamouche S, Martínez Martínez JG.
abstractText:
Background

Insertable loop recorders (ILRs) are subcutaneous cardiac monitoring devices used in the diagnosis of arrhythmias and in the etiological investigation of syncope and cryptogenic stroke. Device miniaturization and procedural simplification have facilitated implantation in ambulatory settings. The involvement of specialized electrophysiology nurses may help meet rising clinical demand, although evidence in our setting remains limited.

Objective

This study aimed to analyze implantation safety, detection signal quality, adverse events during follow-up, and patient satisfaction when the procedure was performed by specialized nurses.

Methods

This prospective observational study (the CARDIONURSE study) was conducted in the Arrhythmia Unit of Hospital General Universitario Doctor Balmis between February 2022 and May 2023. Thirty-five patients with a clinical indication for ILR implantation were included. The procedure was performed by 2 specialized nurses under medical supervision. Sociodemographic, clinical, and technical implantation variables were collected, including detection signal amplitude (mV), together with adverse events and follow-up outcomes at 1 and 6 months. Patient satisfaction was assessed using a study-specific questionnaire at 4 time points. Descriptive statistical analysis was performed.

Results

Mean age was 71.1 (SD 11.3) years, and 62.9% (22/35) were women. The most frequent indication was syncope (27/35, 77.1%), followed by suspected atrial fibrillation (AF) in cryptogenic stroke (6/35, 17.1%). No objective procedural complications occurred (35/35, 100% of procedures); mild, transient procedural pain was reported in 5.7% (2/35) of patients, and the procedure lasted less than 5 minutes in 74.3% (26/35) of procedures. Mean signal amplitude was 0.45 (SD 0.29) mV, with a visible P wave in 94.3% (33/35) of patients. No wound-related adverse events were recorded among the 85.7% (30/35) of patients with available follow-up data at 6 months; data were unavailable for the remaining 5 patients. A diagnosis was obtained in 20% (6/30) of patients with an available diagnostic outcome at 6 months. Overall, 97.1% (34/35) of patients reported maximum or very high satisfaction with the intervention, and 100% (35/35) with the care received.

Conclusions

ILR implantation by specialized electrophysiology nurses in an ambulatory setting is a safe, fast, and technically adequate procedure, with adequate signal quality and high patient satisfaction. These findings support the feasibility of specialized nursing as ILR implanters in similar ambulatory care settings, although confirmation in larger, multicenter studies is warranted before broader implementation.

title: Relationships between participation in leisure activities and mortality risk among adults aged 65 years and older in China: A propensity score-weighted cohort study.
authorString: Sun Z, Zuo C, Wu Y, Chen T.
abstractText:
Background

Leisure activities have been recognized as significant determinants of health among older adults; however, evidence of their association with mortality among Chinese elderly people remains limited.

Objective

To examine the dose-response association between leisure activity participation and all-cause mortality risk among adults aged 65 years and older.

Methods

Using data from the 2008-2018 Chinese Longitudinal Healthy Longevity Survey (CLHLS), we investigated the association of leisure activity participation with all-cause mortality in older adults aged ≥65 years. Multinomial propensity score-based inverse probability weighting (IPW) was used to balance the measured covariates, and time-dependent Cox proportional hazards models were utilized to estimate hazard ratios (HRs)with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Stratified subgroup analyses were performed by age and sex.

Results

Among adults aged 65 years and older, an inverse dose-response association was observed between leisure activity count and mortality risk: each additional activity was associated with a 10% lower all-cause mortality risk (HR: 0.90, 95% CI: 0.87-0.92). Compared with never participants, almost daily engagement in housework, outdoor activities, garden work, reading newspapers or books, playing board/card games,, raising domestic animals or pets, watching TV or listening to the radio, and organized social activities was associated with a lower mortality risk. No significant age or sex interaction was observed for total leisure activity count (all P values for interactions>0.05). A significant age interaction was detected for board/card games (P for interaction=0.025).

Conclusions

Participation in leisure activities was associated with lower all-cause mortality among Chinese adults aged 65 years and older. Encouraging older adults to engage in a diverse range of leisure activities may enhance their quality of life and support China's long-term goal of healthy aging.

title: Light-guided photophosphorylation nanorobot rescues injured cardiomyocytes via in situ bioenergetic restoration.
authorString: Yue T, Mao M, Lin X, Huang Y, He Q.
abstractText: Myocardial injury is a leading cause of death worldwide and is accompanied by profound mitochondrial bioenergetic dysfunction in impaired cardiomyocytes. Restoring cellular bioenergetic homeostasis could be a promising strategy to promote cardiac repair; however, current clinical adenosine triphosphate (ATP) injection therapies yield limited efficacy due to the inability to achieve in situ, targeted delivery. Here, we develop a photoactivated phosphorylation nanorobot engineered to rescue impaired metabolism via targeted, in situ ATP synthesis within cardiomyocytes. These Janus photophosphorylation nanorobots are fabricated through mechanical extrusion-assisted phase separation, enabling the asymmetric integration of chromatophore-coupled FoFl-ATPases. Under structured near-infrared irradiation, the nanorobots exhibit synergistic FoFl-ATPase rotation, which simultaneously drives active propulsion and high-yield ATP catalysis. Following targeted internalization and efficient lysosomal escape, the nanorobots achieve deep penetration into injured myocardial tissue. Intracellularly, the localized elevation of ATP rebalances the NAD+/NADH ratio, suppresses pathological mitochondrial permeability transition pore (mPTP) opening, and mitigates calcium ion overload-collectively restoring mitochondrial integrity and promoting functional myocardial recovery. This self-propelled, bioenergy-restoring nanoplatform represents a rationally designed strategy for targeted therapy of energy-deficient cardiomyopathies.

title: Allograft function in kidney transplant recipients following COVID-19.
authorString: Sandes-Freitas TV, Requião-Moura L, Garcia VD, Manfro RC, Deboni LM, Esmeraldo RM, Ferreira GF, Andrade LGM, Romão EA, Tedesco-Silva H, Domingues-da-Silva RO, Ferreira GS, Soares MO, Abbud-Filho M, Medina-Pestana J, COVID-19-KT Brazil Study Group.
abstractText: This multicenter cohort study assessed the impact of COVID-19 on kidney function in kidney transplant recipients (KTRs) at 12 months after SARS-CoV-2 infection. The final analytic cohort comprised 1,145 KTRs diagnosed with COVID-19 between March-2020 and December-2021, after exclusion of patients who died or experienced graft loss within 90 days of diagnosis. Kidney function at one year was evaluated, as were variables associated with graft loss or a decline in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) ≥30% from baseline. eGFR trajectories were analyzed using a multi-step missing-data approach. At the time of COVID-19 diagnosis, the median time from transplantation was 5.9 years (IQR 2.5-10.4), and the median eGFR was 52 mL/min/1.73m² (IQR 38-68). The cumulative incidence of acute rejection at 12 months was 1.0%; 3.1% of patients died and 3.3% experienced graft loss. Mean eGFR declined by 3.77 mL/min/1.73m² (95%CI, -4.70 to -2.83) in the imputed dataset. In multivariable analysis, diabetes (OR 1.56; 95%CI 1.05-2.33;p = 0.029), hospitalization during COVID-19 (OR 1.79; 95%CI 1.19-2.69;p = 0.005), and acute rejection (OR 16.67; 95%CI 4.59-60.57;p < 0.001) were independently associated with the composite outcome of graft loss or ≥30% decline in eGFR, whereas higher baseline eGFR was protective (OR 0.89 per 10 mL/min/1.73m² increase; 95%CI 0.82-0.97;p = 0.007). In conclusion, although acute rejection and graft loss were uncommon, COVID-19 was associated with a statistically significant reduction in eGFR over 12 months that exceeded the trajectory previously reported for stable KT cohorts, raising concerns about long-term graft outcomes.

title: Prevalence and factors associated with post-tuberculosis lung disease among children and adolescents in Kenya: A multi-centre study.
authorString: Sammy MK, Omar A, Cheruiyot I, Kipkorir V, Maleche-Obimbo E.
abstractText: Most patients survive tuberculosis (TB) with treatment. However, emerging evidence reveals occurrence of a post-TB sequelae termed post TB lung disease (PTLD) that affects survivor's long term lung health. Evidence on PTLD in children and adolescents is limited. We evaluated the prevalence and factors associated with PTLD in children and adolescents completing treatment for intrathoracic TB in Nairobi, Kenya. A cross-sectional study done on participants<20 years at the end of treatment for intrathoracic TB in Nairobi. After obtaining informed consent and assent, we interviewed and examined participants, reviewed their medical records, and conducted a six-minute walk test (6MWT) for children >5 years. Post-TB sequelae was defined as persistent respiratory symptoms and/or abnormal respiratory signs after TB treatment. Descriptive statistics were computed for prevalence of post-TB symptoms and signs, and logistic regression analysis performed to evaluate factors associated with post-TB sequelae. We enrolled 107 participants, of median age 6.3 years; 59% were female and 12% had Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) co-infection. Persistent respiratory symptoms were present in 29%; commonest being cough (21.5%). Abnormal respiratory signs were present in 51%; commonest being tachypnea (27%). Of 56 participants who did the 6MWT, 58% walked <70% of their expected distance. Overall, 57.0% (95% CI 47.1-66.5) had at least one while 33.6% (95% CI 23.8-41.6%) had two or more persistent symptoms and/or abnormal respiratory signs. Hospitalization at diagnosis (aOR 10.26 (1.76-59.79) and older age (aOR 1.13, 95% CI 1.01-1.26) were independent predictors of PTLD. A significant number of children and adolescents have persisting respiratory disease post-TB and it is more common among older children, and those with severe disease at TB diagnosis. There is need to institute routine assessment of children and adolescents at the end of TB treatment to identify those with sequelae, and provide post-TB care.

title: Acute pulmonary embolism: long-term cause-specific mortality in a Chinese nationwide registry.
authorString: Cheng CY, Liu MY, Zhu XJ, Zhou YP, Qiu JY, Huang SS, Wang PR, Wang LT, Lai DS, Pan H, Lian TY, Jiang X, Li X, Huo Y, Jing ZC.
abstractText: Long-term cause-specific mortality after acute pulmonary embolism (PE) remains poorly characterized. This study investigated cumulative mortality, temporal changes in causes of death, and associated factors in a national registry. This registry-based cohort study consecutively enrolled 66 192 acute PE patients from 3223 Chest Pain Centres across China (2018-2023) (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT04014972). Mortality was ascertained through national registry linkage. Cumulative incidence functions estimated temporal mortality patterns, while Fine-Gray models exploratorily examined factors associated with cause-specific mortality. At 60 months, cumulative all-cause mortality was 22.41% (95% confidence interval [CI] 21.92-22.91), comprising cardiovascular (CV) (11.84%, 95% CI 11.46-12.23) and non-CV mortality (10.57%, 95% CI 10.22-10.92). Causes of death varied over time: acute PE and ischaemic heart disease (IHD) predominated initially, malignancy peaked at 1-3 months, and IHD was the largest named cause in each interval beyond 12 months. Among CV deaths, IHD was the predominant cause (35.7%); malignancy (43.3%) and chronic pulmonary disease (24.6%) predominated among non-CV deaths. Men had higher cumulative CV and non-CV mortality than women; while women only had a higher proportion of CV causes among deaths. All-cause mortality increased with age (from 11.52% at <55 to 38.51% at ≥75 years); acute PE/malignancy dominated in younger patients, while CV/pulmonary disease prevailed in older ones. Exploratory analyses identified age, Western China residence, and vital signs as factors associated with mortality. Among patients hospitalised with acute PE, 5-year cumulative mortality was 22.4%, and nearly half of deaths were from non-CV causes. Shifting mortality patterns highlight the need to evaluate risk-adapted long-term follow-up strategies.

title: The Association of Fragmented QRS on Electrocardiography With Cardiovascular Events and Mortality in Hemodialysis Patients.
authorString: Arslan G, Oktan MA, Heybeli C, Kaya D, Sifil AA.

journal.title: Hemodialysis international. International Symposium on Home Hemodialysis

abstractText:
Introduction

Fragmented QRS on 12-lead electrocardiography (ECG) is a marker of myocardial fibrosis, but its clinical significance in hemodialysis patients remains poorly characterized. We evaluated the prevalence of fragmented QRS on the baseline ECG and its association with cardiovascular events and all-cause mortality.

Methods

This retrospective cohort study included 101 patients with end-stage renal disease who started hemodialysis at a tertiary center between 2008 and 2020 (mean follow-up 132 ± 102 months). Fragmented QRS was defined per Das et al.

Criteria

To avoid immortal time bias, exposure was defined using the baseline ECG only. Cardiovascular events were analyzed by multivariable logistic regression adjusted for prespecified clinical covariates and mortality by Cox regression.

Findings

The mean age was 70.9 ± 12.6 years and 63 patients (62.4%) were male. Baseline fragmented QRS was present in 28 patients (27.7%). These patients had a higher prevalence of coronary artery disease (57.1% vs. 28.2%, p = 0.007), lower sodium (136 ± 3.7 vs. 139 ± 3.6 mmol/L, p = 0.001), lower ferritin (476 ± 545 vs. 726 ± 582 ng/mL, p = 0.023), and lower left ventricular ejection fraction (53.4% ± 12.8% vs. 60.1% ± 6.1%, p = 0.024). Cardiovascular events occurred in 43 patients (42.6%) and were more frequent with baseline fragmented QRS (75.0% vs. 30.1%, p < 0.001). After adjustment for age, sex, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, coronary artery disease, and dialysis duration, baseline fragmented QRS remained independently associated with cardiovascular events (odds ratio 10.9, 95% CI 2.33-50.6, p = 0.002). All-cause mortality occurred in 32 patients (31.7%) and was not associated with baseline fragmented QRS (age- and sex-adjusted hazard ratio 1.14, 95% CI 0.54-2.44, p = 0.730).

Discussion

Baseline fragmented QRS was common in hemodialysis patients and was independently associated with cardiovascular events, but not with all-cause mortality. Given that ECG is readily available, noninvasive, and inexpensive, fragmented QRS may serve as a useful risk marker; however, larger prospective studies are needed before routine implementation.

title: Takotsubo syndrome: Phenotype, pathophysiology, and the problem of incomplete recovery.
authorString: Mahmud A, Ferreira D, Sato N, Ray M, Collins NJ, Boyle AJ, Ngo DTM, Sverdlov AL.
abstractText: Takotsubo syndrome (TTS) is a heterogeneous acute heart failure syndrome with diverse triggers, varied phenotypes, important acute complications, and not insignificant long-term morbidity and mortality. This review examines TTS across phenotype, pathophysiology, diagnosis, management, and long-term outcomes. Contemporary registry data show that many cases arise in the setting of acute medical, neurological, or other physical stress rather than isolated emotional distress. Trigger profile, comorbidity burden, and right ventricular involvement may be more clinically informative than ventricular pattern alone. TTS is more likely to reflect several interacting processes than a single unifying mechanism. Sympathetic activation, coronary microvascular dysfunction, inflammation, endothelial injury, impaired myocardial energetics, and brain-heart axis dysregulation may all contribute to the final phenotype. Diagnosis still commonly begins with an acute coronary syndrome-like presentation but is best made through the overall pattern of presentation and multimodality imaging, rather than as a diagnosis of exclusion. Acute management remains largely supportive and should be guided by haemodynamic phenotype. A central theme of this review is that recovery in TTS is often incomplete.
