It is recommended to take hormonal therapy to escape from these problems. Although hormonal therapy has some benefits, there are severe health-related risks like cardiovascular disease and ovarian cancer. These problems forced to search for safer alternatives like phytoestrogen. The objective of this study was to test the efficacy of friedelin as an estrogen. Friedelin is a plant-derived triterpenoid compound. Ovariectomized rats were given friedelin for 28 days, and after that behavioral parameters were recorded along with other analyses like serum estradiol level estimation, uterine histology, and deciduoma formation. Estradiol-driven gene expression (mRNA and protein level) was also checked, along with immunofluorescence localization; these genes were estrogen receptor alpha (ER-α), estrogen receptor beta (ER-β), complement component 3 (C3), early growth response 1(EgR1), and proliferating cell nuclear antigen (PCNA). Progesterone-like activity of friedelin was also checked. Improved behavioural responses were recorded, with significant increases in serum estradiol levels and epithelium thickness along with increased endometrial gland numbers. The significant upregulation of estrogen-responsive genes was found at the mRNA and protein levels in friedelin-treated groups. The localization of these genes was found primarily in endometrial stroma, luminal, and glandular epithelium. Deciduoma formation occurred only in the progesterone-administered group which denies friedelin's progesterone-like activity. The friedelin showed estrogen-like activity. Further, preclinical and clinical investigations are needed to establish friedelin's safety and efficacy for medical applications.

title: Sauchinone protects against pathological cardiac hypertrophy by targeting the TLR4-NF-κB and CDK4-PI3K-Akt signaling pathways.
authorString: Xu T, Zhang K, Yu Y, Tang X, Dou M, Guo Y, Hang J, Li Y, Lu X, Sun N, Yang H, Ye C.
abstractText: Pathological cardiac hypertrophy is a major contributor to heart failure and remains insufficiently targeted by current therapies that primarily focus on hemodynamic regulation rather than underlying molecular mechanisms. Sauchinone, a bioactive lignan isolated from Saururus chinensis, has been reported to exert anti-inflammatory and cardioprotective effects. However, its role in pathological cardiac hypertrophy and the associated mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the therapeutic effect of sauchinone on pathological cardiac hypertrophy and to elucidate its potential mechanism. The H9c2, a rat cardiomyocyte cell line, along with human embryonic stem cells-derived cardiomyocytes (hESC-CMs), were employed to investigate the therapeutic potential of sauchinone on angiotensin II (Ang II)-induced hypertrophy in vitro. An established mouse model of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) and transverse aortic constriction (TAC)-induced cardiac hypertrophy model were used for the animal studies. The investigation combined proteomics with molecular docking to explore the mechanisms by which sauchinone influences pathological cardiac hypertrophy. Sauchinone significantly attenuated cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, as evidenced by reduced cell size and decreased expression of hypertrophic markers in both H9c2 cells and hESC-CMs. In vivo, sauchinone markedly improved cardiac structure and function, reduced myocardial hypertrophy and fibrosis, and restored systolic and diastolic function in HCM and TAC mice. Mechanistically, quantitative proteomics and pathway enrichment analyses revealed that sauchinone significantly inhibited the PI3K-Akt and NF-κB signaling pathways, which was further confirmed by reduced phosphorylation of key pathway components. Notably, protein-protein interaction analysis, molecular docking, and target engagement assays demonstrated that sauchinone directly interacts with cyclin-dependent kinase 4 (CDK4) and Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4), suggesting a dual-target mechanism. Collectively, these findings indicate that sauchinone alleviates pathological cardiac hypertrophy by coordinately suppressing inflammatory and growth signaling pathways via targeting the TLR4-NF-κB and CDK4-PI3K-Akt axes. Sauchinone may therefore represent a promising multi-target therapeutic candidate for the treatment of pathological cardiac hypertrophy.

title: Current approaches and future directions of Endothelin-1 detection.
authorString: Basuki SA, Jiwanti PK, Wardhana BY, Gunawan AW, Tomisaki M, Santoso D, Einaga Y, Setyawan D.

journal.title: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry

abstractText: Endothelin-1 (ET-1) is a peptide comprised of 21 amino acids that exhibits the strongest vasoconstrictor effect identified in the human body. Beyond its role in vascular tone regulation, ET-1 functions as a critical mediator of inflammation, fibrosis, and cellular proliferation. Elevated ET-1 levels are consistently observed in cardiovascular diseases (hypertension, heart failure, atherosclerosis), pulmonary arterial hypertension, chronic kidney disease, diabetic nephropathy, and various malignancies. This establishes ET-1 as a potential biomarker for early detection, disease classification, and therapy assessment. This review offers an extensive analysis of ET-1 biology, its clinical importance, and the detection methods that are currently accessible. We assess traditional methods such as enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), radioimmunoassay (RIA), liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS), and surface plasmon resonance (SPR), in addition to new electrochemical biosensing technologies. Electrochemical biosensors, leveraging antibody-antigen or aptamer-target interactions, present a transformative alternative offering rapid response, portability, and suitability for point-of-care applications. This review identifies current challenges, highlights recent technological advances, and outlines future directions for translating ET-1 biosensing from research laboratories to clinical practice, ultimately aiming to improve patient outcomes through earlier and more accessible diagnostics.

title: Sema4D Deficiency Protects Against Sepsis-Associated Liver Injury by Modulating Ferroptosis-Associated Responses and Macrophage Polarization.
authorString: Liu X, Wu B, Yu D, Qiao A, Liang R, Zhang L, Wei S, Yang J, Yan Y, Liao Y, Tan L, Wu B.
abstractText: Sema4D contributes to inflammatory responses, but its role in sepsis-associated liver injury remains unclear. We examined this role using Sema4D-knockout mice, hepatic Sema4D overexpression, and LPS-treated AML12 hepatocytes and RAW264.7 macrophages. Sema4D levels were elevated in the serum of patients with sepsis, mouse liver tissues after cecal ligation and puncture (CLP), and LPS-treated cells. Sema4D knockout reduced serum aminotransferase levels and hepatic histological injury at 24 h after CLP, whereas overexpression aggravated liver injury. Seven-day survival was numerically higher after knockout, but the difference was not statistically significant (n = 10 per group; log-rank P = 0.0751). Proteomic analysis identified ferroptosis among the enriched pathways. Sema4D knockout or knockdown reduced TFR1, NCOA4, and ROS signals and increased GPX4 expression. Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed changes in hepatic myeloid cell populations and gene expression. Further analyses showed lower expression of examined M1-associated markers and higher expression of selected M2-associated markers following Sema4D knockout or knockdown, with opposite changes after overexpression in RAW264.7 cells. Sema4D manipulation altered MEK/ERK phosphorylation signals, and U0126 attenuated several ferroptosis-associated changes induced by overexpression. These findings demonstrate that Sema4D deficiency protects against liver injury at 24 h after CLP, attenuates ferroptosis-associated responses, and alters macrophage polarization-associated marker expression. The U0126 experiments further support the involvement of MEK/ERK signaling in the ferroptosis-associated effects of Sema4D.

title: Oleic Acid Modulates Prostanoid Levels and Reduces Nitric Oxide Production in Cultured Endothelial Cells.
authorString: Juarez-Navarro K, Villa-Martínez E, Sánchez-Herrera DP.
abstractText: Cardiovascular diseases are commonly associated with endothelial dysfunction, in which alterations in lipid metabolism and intracellular lipid droplet accumulation have been implicated. However, the mechanisms by which monounsaturated fatty acids, particularly oleic acid (OA), reprogram the broader balance of endothelial vasoactive mediators and endothelial cell function remain incompletely understood. In the present study, we evaluated the impact of OA on lipid droplet (LD) formation and endothelial function in murine brain endothelial cells (bEnd.3). OA induced significant, time- and concentration-dependent LD accumulation without compromising viability, and pharmacological inhibition of adipose triglyceride lipase (ATGL) with Atglistatin further increased LD content, confirming active LD turnover. OA treatment (0.5mM, 24h) reduced acetylcholine-stimulated nitric oxide production, increased oxidative/nitrosative stress, and decreased the eNOS dimer-to-monomer ratio alongside ~50% lower eNOS protein, independent of changes in calcium signaling. OA also reduced thromboxane A2 (TXA2) while increasing prostacyclin production, paralleled by decreased thromboxane synthase and increased COX-2 and prostacyclin synthase expression. In wound healing assays, OA impaired endothelial migration, requiring intact NO- and cyclooxygenase-derived signaling, as blockade of either pathway (L-NAME, piroxicam) further reduced migration, and ATGL-dependent lipid droplet turnover also contributed to migratory capacity. These findings demonstrate that OA treatment, accompanied by lipid droplet accumulation, coordinately reprograms vasoactive mediator production and impairs endothelial migration. The shift toward reduced NO production and migratory capacity reflects a maladaptive endothelial phenotype, whereas the reduction in TXA2 and upregulation of prostacyclin represent an adaptive, vasoprotective mechanism counteracting NO loss, together revealing complex pathophysiological remodeling triggered by endothelial lipid overload.

title: Myocardial Extraction Fraction and Circulation-Dependent Changes of <sup>99m</sup>Tc-4BOH: Implications for Quantitative SPECT Myocardial Perfusion Imaging.
authorString: Ding D, Gu Y, Zhang Y, Wang K, Ju M, Zhou Y, Ren W, Song S, Zhong H, Wang X, Ma T, Fang W, Wang L.

journal.title: Journal of nuclear cardiology : official publication of the American Society of Nuclear Cardiology

abstractText: Quantitative myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI) requires tracers with high myocardial extraction fraction (EF) and favorable kinetic properties. Although 99mTc-4BOH has demonstrated favorable myocardial imaging characteristics, its myocardial extraction behavior and the factors that may influence EF in the circulation have not been fully characterized. Myocardial EF and retention kinetics of 99mTc-4BOH were evaluated using isolated Langendorff-perfused rat hearts across low-, intermediate-, and high-flow conditions (5.0, 8.4, and 16.0 mL/min) and compared with 99mTc-Teboroxime and 99mTc-Sestamibi. Time-dependent changes in myocardial EF were assessed at 2, 4, and 10 min after tracer administration in vivo. Potential blood-related mechanisms were investigated by in vitro incubation with whole blood, plasma, and erythrocytes at the same time points. 99mTc-4BOH demonstrated a high and flow-independent myocardial EF across the tested flow rates (mean values, 96.5%-99.5%), comparable to 99mTc-Teboroxime and consistently higher than 99mTc-Sestamibi at each flow rate. Despite similarly high extraction, 99mTc-4BOH exhibited greater myocardial retention than 99mTc-Teboroxime. Following in vivo circulation, myocardial EF progressively declined to approximately 84% at 2 min and 57% at 10 min. In vitro incubation with whole blood or plasma had minimal effects on EF, whereas erythrocyte-associated tracer exhibited a time-dependent decline from approximately 92% at 2 min to 59% at 10 min, suggesting that erythrocyte interaction contributes to, but does not fully explain, the loss of EF observed after circulation. 99mTc-4BOH exhibits near-complete, flow-independent myocardial EF and greater retention than 99mTc-Teboroxime, supporting its potential as a tracer for quantitative SPECT MPI. The time-dependent decline in EF following circulation has important implications for kinetic modeling and suggests that early post-injection imaging data may be preferable for myocardial blood flow quantification.

title: One-Year Survival After Hybrid Stage 1 Single Ventricle Palliation - The Impact of Institutional Experience.
authorString: Wright LK, Bigelow AM, Camacho M, Davis JA, Carrillo SA, Salavitabar A, Abdelshahid M, Davidson E, Wride J, Cabrera AG, Yerebakan C, Texter K, Galantowicz M.
abstractText: The hybrid stage 1 palliation (HS1P), an alternative to the Norwood procedure for hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HLHS), is often reserved for high-risk patients. We aimed to evaluate the survival of HS1P through one year when used as standard palliation strategy for HLHS and similar lesions and to assess changes in survival over time. Retrospective cohort study of all infants who underwent HS1P for single ventricle palliation. A structured protocol for patient management was developed between 2009 and 2017, with all components implemented by June 2017. Patients were stratified into two cohorts based on timing of HS1P: Era 1 (January 2002 - May 2017), and Era 2 (June 2017 - December 2024). The primary outcome was survival through one year. A total of 281 infants underwent HS1P, 221 in Era 1 and 60 in Era 2. Median age at HS1P was 6 days for both groups. Balloon atrial septostomy at the time of HS1P was significantly more common in Era 2 (43% vs 4% in Era 1), as was use of smaller bands (p <0.001 for both). One-year survival was significantly higher in Era 2 compared to Era 1 (83% vs 65%, p=0.01), and this benefit persisted in multivariable analysis. In this study of HS1P used as standard palliation, contemporary survival was excellent with significant improvements in outcomes in more recent years. Further study is needed to understand longer-term outcomes and the interplay of patient risk factors, to help guide best practices.

title: Examining the intersection of extreme heat exposures, social determinants of health, and adverse pregnancy outcomes: a scoping review.
authorString: Rattan JE, Lindley SM, Preer Ii B, Hanumanula D, Aluri AS, Douglas O, Kirksey KR, Billings RR, Blanton OF, Martin S, Malenda A, Tita A, Burris HH, Jackson P, Sinkey R, Howell EA, Abadi AM, Patel RC, P3 EQUATE Network Social Determinants of Health Core Group.

journal.title: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM

abstractText: Extreme heat exposure during pregnancy is associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes (APOs), complications themselves linked to long-term maternal cardiovascular risk, and these effects appear to vary by social and environmental context (e.g., neighborhood deprivation, greenness, and rural-urban residence). We describe the U.S. evidence and characterize how social determinants of health (SDoH), particularly area-level measures, are defined in this literature. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science Core Collection were searched through July 14, 2025, plus secondary searches in September 2025. We included U.S.-focused empirical epidemiologic studies and evidence syntheses that (1) assessed extreme heat exposure in pregnancy; (2) incorporated at least one individual- or area-level SDoH as exposure, covariate, or effect modifier; and (3) reported at least one APO, from preterm birth, low birth weight, stillbirth, hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, and gestational diabetes to composite APOs, severe maternal morbidity, and acute cardiovascular events. Two reviewers independently screened records; a senior reviewer resolved conflicts. Data were extracted into standardized forms and synthesized narratively. Per scoping review guidance, formal risk-of-bias assessment was not performed. We included 37 studies (28 empirical and 9 reviews). Heat exposure was typically defined using percentile-based thresholds (most commonly the 90th or 95th local percentile), heat-wave definitions, apparent-temperature metrics, or absolute cutoffs, with the week before delivery the most frequent window. Preterm birth was the most evaluated outcome, followed by birthweight-related outcomes and stillbirth. Individual-level socioeconomic measures (e.g., education, insurance) appeared in nearly all empirical studies, whereas area-level measures-neighborhood income or poverty, deprivation indices, greenness or tree canopy, heat-trapping land cover, region, and rural-urban residence-appeared in fewer than half. Five of 12 studies incorporating area-level SDoH reported stronger heat-APO associations in disadvantaged or lower-greenness settings. Examples include heat-associated stillbirth risk only in the most deprived neighborhoods; heat-preterm birth associations strongest where both greenness and socioeconomic status were low; and stronger heat-gestational diabetes associations with lower greenness. U.S. studies reported associations between extreme heat in pregnancy and multiple APOs. Area-level SDoH and environmental context were inconsistently incorporated. Standardized use of place-based measures may better identify communities most vulnerable to heat and inform equity-focused, climate-resilient maternal health research and action. Heat exposure in pregnancy is linked to adverse outcomes, and risk may be higher in neighborhoods experiencing socioeconomic deprivation, highlighting the need to measure area-level social determinants in climate-maternal health research.

title: Elevated S-adenosylhomocysteine is associated with impaired macrophage cholesterol efflux involving alterations in TFEB-V-ATPase lysosomal signaling.
authorString: Yang Y, Xiao Q, Chen J, Gao Z, Su W, Deng S, Zhang Y, Nie J, Huang Y, Lian S, Li J, He J, Liu C.
abstractText: Elevated plasma S-adenosylhomocysteine (SAH) levels increase the risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Since lipophagy maintains cholesterol homeostasis through hydrolysis of cholesterol esters to support efflux, its impairment reduces cholesterol efflux. We aimed to explore the association of elevated SAH with macrophage foam-cell cholesterol handling and the potential mechanisms involving autophagy-related lipid processing and cholesterol efflux. We explored the associations between plasma SAH levels and cholesterol efflux capacity (CEC) in the Guangdong Coronary Artery Disease (CAD) Cohort. Adenosine dialdehyde (AdOx) was used to increase intracellular SAH levels in THP-1 macrophage foam cells, followed by evaluation of cholesterol efflux and autophagy-related lipid handling. We investigated the molecular mechanisms by examining regulators, including ABCA1, vacuolar-type H+-ATPase (V-ATPase) subunits, and transcription factor EB (TFEB). Torin 1 was used to assess changes in TFEB-related signaling and cholesterol efflux. We found that plasma SAH levels were inversely associated with CEC in CAD patients. In vitro, AdOx treatment increased intracellular SAH and reduced ABCA1 expression and ApoA-I-dependent cholesterol efflux. AdOx treatment was accompanied by reduced TFEB nuclear translocation, lower ATP6V1H and lysosomal acid lipase (LAL) expression, altered LC3/p62 levels, and increased lysosomal cholesterol. Torin 1 partially restored TFEB-related gene expression and ApoA-I-dependent cholesterol efflux. These findings support the involvement of TFEB-V-ATPase-related lysosomal signaling in AdOx-associated changes in macrophage cholesterol handling. Elevated S-adenosylhomocysteine is associated with impaired macrophage cholesterol efflux involving alterations in TFEB-V-ATPase lysosomal signaling, identifying SAH metabolism and TFEB-V-ATPase signaling as potential targets for further investigation.

title: Serum aldosterone concentrations in Cavalier King Charles Spaniels across ACVIM stages of myxomatous mitral valve disease and their associations with echocardiographic indices.
authorString: Lewicki M, Kumiega E, Wojtczak Z, Noszczyk-Nowak A.
abstractText: Myxomatous mitral valve disease (MMVD) is common in Cavalier King Charles Spaniels (CKCS) and may involve activation of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS). This study evaluated serum aldosterone concentrations across ACVIM MMVD stages in CKCS and its association with selected echocardiographic indices. Eighty-four client-owned CKCS were staged according to ACVIM guidelines (A, n = 11; B1, n = 58; B2, n = 7; C, n = 8), and serum aldosterone was measured using the LIAISON® Aldosterone chemiluminescent immunoassay on the DiaSorin LIAISON® XL automated analyzer. In the comparison of serum aldosterone concentrations between the combined ACVIM groups A+B1 and B2+C, the group effect did not reach statistical significance in the multivariable analysis based on complete cases (p = 0.072). In the unadjusted comparison, dogs with ACVIM-defined left-sided cardiac remodeling and/or congestive heart failure (B2+C) had higher median serum aldosterone concentrations than dogs not fulfilling ACVIM criteria for stage B2 or C disease (A+B1) (707.0 [445.0-1150.0] vs. 469.5 [333.5-730.5] pmol/L; p = 0.045), with a moderate rank-biserial effect size (r_rb = 0.332; 95% CI: 0.025-0.612). No significant associations between serum aldosterone concentration and echocardiographic variables remained after false discovery rate (FDR) correction, either in the whole cohort or in the B2+C subgroup. These results suggest a possible difference in serum aldosterone concentrations between broader clinically defined MMVD groups. However, this association was attenuated after multivariable adjustment, and associations with individual echocardiographic indices were not confirmed after correction for multiple testing. The results should therefore be considered preliminary and hypothesis-generating.

title: Biomimetic-Inspired Limited Basement Membrane Proteolysis Modulates Mesenchymal Stem Cell Transmigration while Preserving Endothelial Quiescence on Xenogeneic Extracellular Matrix Scaffolds.
authorString: Hussein K, Somasekhar L, Radyna D, Guarino ID, Dasari S, Griffiths LG.
abstractText: The success of tissue-derived acellular extracellular matrix (ECM) scaffolds for blood contacting applications depends on preserving basement membrane (BM) integrity to promote quiescent reendothelialization, while simultaneously facilitating progenitor cell infiltration to repopulate underlying stromal compartments. However, achieving this balance remains a central challenge in vascular tissue engineering. This study aimed to determine whether biomimetic-inspired limited proteolysis using proteinase K (PK) can modulate BM structure to enhance mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) transmigration (i.e., stromal repopulation), while maintaining scaffold integrity and BM-mediated endothelial cell (EC) quiescence. Antigen-removed bovine pericardium (AR-BP) ECM scaffolds were treated with increasing PK concentrations (0-20 µg/mL) and characterized using histology, immunofluorescence for bovine BM components (i.e., laminin and collagen IV (Col IV)), and biomechanical testing. Human MSC transmigration was assessed through DAPI staining, quantitative migration analysis, and migratory mechanism probed using RNA sequencing. Human aortic endothelial cells (HAECs) were seeded to evaluate EC polarization, adherens junction organization, new BM synthesis (i.e., human laminin and Col IV), nitric oxide production, and inflammatory response. PK treatment (2-5 µg/mL) preserved BM components and mechanical properties, while significantly enhancing MSC migration compared to untreated scaffolds. Excessive proteolysis (20 µg/mL) disrupted BM structure and compromised mechanical stability. Transcriptomic analysis identified 114 upregulated genes in PK-treated scaffolds, predominantly associated with cell migration, proliferation, and cytoskeletal remodeling. Immunofluorescence staining demonstrated that HAECs formed a quiescent, polarized monolayer with organized adherens junction proteins, preventing platelet activation and preserving nitric oxide production on PK 0-2 µg/mL scaffolds, whereas higher PK levels impaired endothelial function, increased new BM production, platelet activation and inflammatory signaling. These findings demonstrate that biomimetic-inspired limited BM proteolysis defines a functional threshold that optimizes scaffold bioactivity. Fine-tuning proteolytic processing enables a balance between structural preservation and cellular permissiveness, providing a potential strategy to promote functional human cellular repopulation, integration and remodeling in future cardiovascular applications. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: A key challenge in vascular tissue engineering is balancing reendothelialization with stromal recellularization. The basement membrane, while essential for maintaining healthy endothelial function, acts as a barrier to stromal cell migration. Here, we demonstrate that controlled enzymatic modulation can selectively "permeabilize" the basement membrane, enabling stem cell transmigration and stromal repopulation, while preserving mechanical integrity and supporting endothelial health. Importantly, we identify a functional threshold that governs this balance, beyond which structural and functional compromise occurs. These findings provide a simple and translatable strategy for improving vascular graft design, with significant implications for enhancing integration and long-term clinical performance.

title: Middle Cardiac Vein Mapping with Multielectrode Catheters to Guide Ablation of Scar-Related Ventricular Tachycardia.
authorString: Gad M, Stuckey M, Alkhunaizi F, Ahmed B, Oraii A, Afzalian A, Markman T, Hyman M, Shivamurthy P, Peters C, Hanumanthu B, Mirwais M, Kumareswaran R, Guandalini G, Riley M, Nazarian S, Tschabrunn C, Lin D, Schaller R, Dixit S, Supple G, Callans D, Frankel D, Garcia F, Marchlinski F, Enriquez A.
abstractText:
Background

The coronary venous system offers an alternative route for mapping and ablation of ventricular arrhythmias, especially in presence of epicardial or intramural substrate.

Objective

To investigate the feasibility, diagnostic yield and outcomes of middle cardiac vein (MCV) mapping using multielectrode catheters to guide ablation of scar-related ventricular tachycardia (VT).

Methods

We included patients with structural heart disease and VT undergoing ablation in which MCV mapping was performed using multielectrode catheters. Left ventricular (LV) and/or right ventricular (RV) endocardial mapping was performed depending on the VT morphology, and the ablation strategy was selected based on endocardial and MCV activation in addition to pace mapping and/or entrainment.

Results

Thirty-three patients (60.5±13.6 years, 73% nonischemic) were included. VT was inducible in 97% of patients, with a median of 4 VT morphologies per patient. MCV and endocardial mapping suggested an epicardial circuit in 21 patients and epicardial access was obtained in 13 of them (percutaneous approach in 11 and surgical window in 2). Additionally, mapping was consistent with an intramural circuit in 3 patients, which were treated with sequential RF ablation from LV and RV (n = 3) and ethanol ablation (n = 2). There were no complications related to MCV mapping. Over a median follow-up of 13 months, 8 patients (24%) had VT recurrence.

Conclusions

MCV mapping with multielectrode catheters is safe and facilitates identification of epicardial or intramural VT circuits, guides the need for epicardial access and provides an opportunity for therapeutic interventions such as venous RF delivery or ethanol infusion.

title: The Portuguese National Registry of Cardiac Imaging (RNPIC): Initial results from a nationwide multicenter survey.
authorString: Bettencourt N, Ferreira AM, Matos P, Ferreira C, Ferreira N, Bicho JA, Abecasis J, Freitas P, Vasconcelos M, Teixeira T, Oliveira L, Pereira A, Mendes L, Manuel Oliveira J, Jalles N, Duarte S, Daniel PM, Plácido R, Pedro P, Marques H, Almeida AG.

journal.title: Revista portuguesa de cardiologia : orgao oficial da Sociedade Portuguesa de Cardiologia = Portuguese journal of cardiology : an official journal of the Portuguese Society of Cardiology

abstractText: Advanced cardiac imaging techniques, including cardiac computed tomography (CCT), cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR), and nuclear cardiology, are increasingly central to cardiovascular care. This study describes the initial results of the Portuguese National Registry of Cardiac Imaging (RNPIC), focusing on center-level availability, patient profile, access, and clinical utilization. Between March and April 2023, all Portuguese centers performing CMR, CCT, or nuclear cardiology were invited to register prospectively all referred patients who provided informed consent over 30 consecutive days. Data on demographics, cardiovascular risk factors, clinical history, imaging modality, and delay between referral and scan were collected. Centers were also characterized in terms of institutional setting and available imaging techniques. A total of 44 centers and 3315 exams were included (patient age: 62.3±12.6 years; 40.3% female). CCT was the most frequently used modality (52%), followed by CMR (33%) and nuclear cardiology (15%). Compared to CCT and CMR, patients undergoing nuclear cardiology were older and had a higher burden of cardiovascular risk factors and prior events. Among examinations with valid referral and examination dates, median time between referral and scan was shortest for CCT (26 days [IQR 9-57]), followed by CMR (31 days [IQR 11-79]) and nuclear cardiology (35 days [IQR 17-65]). Delays were consistently longer in public than in private institutions across all modalities, with an overall median waiting time of 53 versus 22 days, respectively (p<0.000001). A significant proportion of referrals to both functional or anatomical tests was related to screening for obstructive coronary artery disease in asymptomatic patients, accounting for 8.6%, 11.7%, and 32.2% of CCT, CMR, and nuclear cardiology cases, respectively. This first nationwide registry provides a comprehensive overview of cardiac imaging practice in Portugal. Important differences in patient profile, technique utilization, and access times were identified across imaging modalities and healthcare sectors. A relevant proportion of imaging studies were performed in asymptomatic individuals without clearly documented guideline-based indications in the registry, highlighting the need for improved referral pathways, educational efforts, and future appropriateness-focused studies.

title: Port-Hopping Technique for Robotic Mediastinal Lymph Node Dissection.
authorString: Murakami J, Yoshimine S, Tanaka T.
abstractText: Standard port configurations for robotic-assisted thoracic surgery lobectomy often restrict instrument angles and limit visualization during mediastinal lymph node dissection. We describe "port-hopping," in which the scope and instruments are exchanged among the docked robotic arms without moving ports or re-docking. In this maneuver, performed after lobectomy or before bronchial transection for subcarinal dissection, the third-arm role moves to the ventral-most arm, while the other roles shift one port dorsally. A vessel sealer holding a gauze pledget provides planar retraction for en bloc dissection. Port-hopping allows the console surgeon to control exposure without assistant-dependent retraction and is simple and feasible.

title: Continual learning in oncology AI: A framework for safe clinical translation.
authorString: Muneer A, Huang P, Kavitha MS, Zafar A, Salehjahromi M, Sheshadri A, Wu CC, Carter BW, Haymaker CL, Soto LS, Jaffray D, Rice DC, Liao Z, Chang JY, Altan M, Vokes NI, Heymach JV, Zhang J, Wu J.
abstractText: AI models remain largely static, yet cancer care never stands still. Evolution of scanning technology, imaging protocols, staging criteria, therapies, and patient populations can silently erode model performance and patient safety. Continual learning (CL) enables models to continuously acquire new knowledge, while minimizing catastrophic forgetting. Here, we review CL methods and their oncology applications, predominantly in imaging and pathology, and discuss CL as an option for maintaining foundation models, alongside recalibration and retraining. We examine translational barriers, including hidden regressions in underrepresented populations, label and concept drift, privacy constraints on data retention, and evaluations divorced from clinical timelines. We propose six criteria for safe clinical translation: temporally faithful evaluation, calibration stability, subgroup safety, governance-compatible replay, model versioning with regression testing, and prospective clinical validation. Adaptive oncology AI is a safety-critical systems problem, and these criteria position CL as a plausible foundation for establishing future-robust superintelligent clinical systems.

title: Spatial transcriptomics uncovers pharmacokinetic and tumor-intrinsic determinants of resistance to trastuzumab deruxtecan in breast cancer.
authorString: Park C, Choi M, Koh J, Bae S, Choi H, Na KJ, Kim YJ, Ham S, Lee J, Shin Y, Lee DW, Lee KH, Ryu HS, Kim TY, Im SA.
abstractText: Trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) is effective in both HER2-positive and HER2-low metastatic breast cancers, but clinical responses are heterogeneous. To delineate spatial determinants of response, we perform spatial transcriptomics in patients treated with T-DXd. More spatially dispersed HER2 expression in cancer cells correlates with improved response, consistent with the bystander effect. In HER2-positive tumors, resistant fragments show downregulation of ERBB2 expression and activation of PI3K and EGFR pathways, with possible involvement of autocrine amphiregulin-EGFR signaling. In HER2-low tumors, resistance is associated with pharmacokinetic barriers: resistant fragments exhibit increased cancer-to-vessel distance, reduced colocalization of HER2 with cathepsin linker-cleaving enzymes, and diminished predicted peritumoral payload concentration. Exploratory longitudinal analyses of paired pre-treatment and post-progression samples reveal increased cancer-to-vessel distance at resistance. Our study identifies spatial features associated with ADC response and resistance in clinical samples and provides a rationale for further investigation of candidate determinants.

title: Long-term O<sub>3</sub> and PM<sub>2.5</sub> exposure and dynamic progression of cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome: A longitudinal cohort study.
authorString: Li S, Wei Y, Ni W, Zhu C, Zhang Y, Zhang H, Zheng Y, Li Z, Zhao Z, Li H, Zhou C, Liu C, Yuan X, Wang J, Xu J.
abstractText: To examine the associations of long-term ozone (O3) and fine particulate matter (PM2.5) exposure with dynamic forward progression of cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome, including early and advanced progression. Participants enrolled in the Shenzhen Healthy Aging Research Cohort during 2018-2023 were followed through 2024. Consecutive valid health examinations defined risk intervals, with preceding-365-day mean O3 and PM2.5 exposures updated at each interval start. Multistate Cox models with participant-clustered robust variance estimated hazard ratios (HRs) for overall, early (ending in stages 1-2), and advanced (ending in stages 3-4) nonfatal progression. Additional single-pollutant and multipollutant models were fitted in a common sample with complete exposure data for six pollutants. Among 493,388 participants contributing 1,029,004 risk intervals, 162,083 forward progression events occurred. Per interquartile-range increase in O3 (7.431 µg/m3), HRs (95% confidence intervals) were 1.151 (1.138-1.165) for overall, 1.113 (1.090-1.138) for early, and 1.172 (1.156-1.189) for advanced progression. Corresponding estimates for PM2.5 (5.008 µg/m3) were 1.054 (1.030-1.078), 1.073 (1.030-1.118), and 1.055 (1.027-1.085). O3 associations were comparatively consistent across six-pollutant common-sample and multipollutant analyses, whereas PM2.5 estimates showed greater sensitivity to analytical specifications. Long-term O3 and PM2.5 exposures were associated with higher hazards of nonfatal CKM progression in the primary analyses. These findings support consideration of ambient air pollution in comprehensive CKM prevention.

title: Association Between Sit-to-Stand Ground Reaction Force and 1-Year Frailty Deterioration in Community-Dwelling Older Adults.
authorString: Miyake Y, Makizako H, Akaida S, Shiratsuchi D, Tateishi M, Kuratsu R, Takenaka T, Kubozono T, Ohishi M.

journal.title: Journal of the American Medical Directors Association

abstractText:
Objectives

To examine the association between ground reaction force (GRF) parameters during sit-to-stand motion and 1-year frailty deterioration in community-dwelling older adults using sex-specific analysis.

Design

A 1-year longitudinal observational study.

Setting and participants

This study included 232 community-dwelling older adults who completed health checkups at baseline (2021) and 1-year follow-up (2022) without frailty at baseline.

Methods

Frailty status, assessed using the Kihon checklist, was categorized into robust, prefrailty, and frailty categories. Participants with a 1-year deteriorated frailty status were assigned to the "Deterioration group." GRF parameters measured during the sit-to-stand motion included force [the peak force divided by body weight (F/w)], rapid force production (the RFD divided by body weight), and postural fluctuation (the ratio of mediolateral to vertical force fluctuation; Vx/Vw). Logistic regression analysis was performed using deteriorated frailty status as the dependent variable and GRF parameters as independent variables (covariates: age, polypharmacy, and baseline Kihon checklist points). To account for differences in lower-extremity strength, the analysis was conducted separately by sex.

Results

The prevalence of 1-year deteriorated frailty ("Deterioration group") was 15.8% among males and 15.3% among females. Logistic regression analysis revealed that F/w was significantly associated with deteriorated frailty status only in females (odds ratio, 0.93; 95% CI, 0.87-0.99). Other GRF parameters were not significantly associated with deteriorated frailty status.

Conclusions and implications

Our findings revealed that F/w, a force-generation parameter during the sit-to-stand motion, was associated with deteriorated frailty in community-dwelling older females, underscoring the importance of evaluating force-generation capacity during sit-to-stand motion in community-based health assessments.

title: Aortic Valve Stenosis Screening Using Deep Learning on Noninvasive Arterial Pressure Waveforms.
authorString: Kassab J, Harb SC, Arafati A, Gonzalez Reyes MA, Vlaar APJ, Veelo DP, Kho E, Schenk J, Ramchand J, Collier P, Miyasaka R, Grimm R, Griffin BP, Kapadia SR.
abstractText:
Background

Aortic stenosis (AS) presents a significant health burden. Early identification of significant AS, defined as at least moderate AS, may facilitate timely confirmatory testing, referral, and management.

Objectives

This study sought to develop and externally validate a deep learning model applied to arterial pressure waveforms obtained from a noninvasive finger-cuff system to screen for significant AS, using transthoracic echocardiography as the reference standard.

Methods

This prospective international multicenter cohort study was conducted from December 2020 through July 2025. Participants underwent concurrent transthoracic echocardiography and noninvasive arterial pressure waveform acquisition. A 1-dimensional convolutional neural network was developed using the Cleveland Clinic development cohort and evaluated in a temporally distinct, multicenter validation cohort including sites in the United States, Spain, and the Netherlands.

Results

Significant AS was present in 307 of 3,634 (8.4%) patients in the development cohort and 241 of 1,336 (18.0%) in the validation cohort. In the validation cohort, the model demonstrated an area under the curve of 0.893 (95% CI: 0.876-0.910), with a sensitivity of 92.5% (223/241; 95% CI: 88.5%-95.2%), negative predictive value of 97.5% (706/724; 95% CI: 96.1%-98.4%), specificity of 64.5% (706/1,095; 95% CI: 61.6%-67.3%), and positive predictive value of 36.4% (223/612; 95% CI: 32.7%-40.3%). For severe AS, the area under the curve was 0.906 (95% CI: 0.890-0.922), with a sensitivity of 94.3% (183/194; 95% CI: 90.1%-96.8%), negative predictive value of 98.5% (706/717; 95% CI: 97.3%-99.1%), specificity of 64.5% (706/1,095; 95% CI: 61.6%-67.3%), and positive predictive value of 32% (183/572; 95% CI: 28.3%-35.9%).

Conclusions

Deep learning applied to arterial pressure waveforms obtained from a finger-cuff system serves as a promising screening test for significant AS.

title: Hemodynamic Effects of Three Different Mechanical Circulatory Support Strategies in Isolated Acute Right Heart Failure.
authorString: Bari G, Mariani S, De Piero ME, Dickstein M, Schreuder J, Schmitto J, Di Mauro M, van Bussel B, Lo Coco V, Gazzaniga G, Meyer T, Li T, Haverich A, Lorusso R.

journal.title: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)

abstractText: Although acute right ventricular failure (aRVF) is commonly treated with venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA ECMO), this approach may increase complications. We compared femoro-femoral VA ECMO, single-lumen cannula femoro-pulmonary artery (V-Pa), and double-lumen cannula right atrium-to-pulmonary artery (RA-Pa) support configurations in a swine model of ischemic aRVF-induced cardiogenic shock. Twenty-six adult German Landrasse swine were randomly assigned to the three study groups. Systemic oxygen delivery was the primary end-point; secondary end-points included hemodynamic parameters and complications. Systemic oxygen delivery remained stable during support without intergroup differences. Mean arterial pressure showed higher values in the V-Pa group compared with RA-Pa at 2 hours (65 ± 10 vs. 48 ± 8 mm Hg; p = 0.010) and 3 hours (62 ± 9 vs. 47 ± 10 mm Hg; p = 0.042). Mean pulmonary artery pressure was higher after V-A ECMO (20 ± 5 mm Hg) initiation compared with V-Pa (11 ± 5 mm Hg, p = 0.013) or RA-Pa (11 ± 3 mm Hg, p = 0.006) support. During support, the V-A ECMO group exhibited the lowest EtCO2 and highest carotid flow (p = 0.039 and p < 0.001, respectively). Challenges were noted with double-lumen cannulation due to anatomical constraints. Pulmonary artery cannulation-based support was noninferior to V-A ECMO in terms of oxygen delivery, with lower pulmonary pressures and preserved transpulmonary flow. Femoral vein-to-pulmonary artery configuration showed favorable short-term hemodynamics and easier cannulation compared with RA-Pa.

title: <i>Roseburia intestinalis</i> counteracts TBEP-exacerbated atherosclerosis.
authorString: Liu L, Gan T, Yang L, Wang Z, Lv X, Wang X, Zhang K, Kan H, Gao M, Pan L, Mao A, Zhou T.
abstractText: Interactions between serum metabolites and vascular endothelial cells directly influence atherosclerotic lesions. It is essential to identify and understand the effects of the complex profile of serum metabolites on vascular pathology. In this study, we found that coronary lesion severity positively correlated with serum levels of the organophosphate ester tris (2-butoxyethyl) phosphate (TBEP), while TBEP levels inversely correlated with gut Roseburia intestinalis abundance. Western diet supplemented with TBEP substantially exacerbated atherosclerosis in apolipoprotein E-/- (ApoE-/-) mice. We found that TBEP enhanced AMP-activated protein kinase α (AMPKα) phosphorylation, reduced nuclear translocation of active sterol regulatory element-binding protein 1c (SREBP1c) fragments, suppressed Patatin-like phospholipase domain-containing protein 3 (PNPLA3) protein expression in endothelial cells, and increased lipid deposition. Oral R. intestinalis supplementation reduced fecal and serum TBEP levels and attenuated TBEP-driven atherosclerotic lesions. We highlight that TBEP aggravates endothelial lipid accumulation and atherosclerosis, suggesting that targeting gut microbiota may serve as a promising strategy against TBEP-exacerbated atherosclerosis.

title: Complex IV maturation coordinates postnatal mitochondrial and metabolic development.
authorString: Popovic M, Cabrera-Orefice A, Isermann L, Croon M, Zecic A, Meisterknecht J, Alameldin Y, Hanehalli V, Siibak T, Frezza C, Wittig I, Trifunovic A.
abstractText: The perinatal heart undergoes a rapid metabolic transition from glycolysis to fatty acid oxidation that requires extensive mitochondrial remodeling, yet the molecular checkpoints that coordinate this process remain poorly defined. Using temporally resolved proteomics and complexome profiling of developing mouse hearts from late gestation through early postnatal life (E18.5 to P10), we identify a discrete developmental window in which respiratory chain architecture is remodeled to enable metabolic commitment. Complex IV (CIV) emerges as a central structural determinant of this transition, undergoing isoform-specific reassembly and transient suppression at birth before incorporation into mature respiratory supercomplexes. We identify the CIV subunit COX7C as a developmentally regulated determinant of CIV maturation, with its abundance increasing during maximal respirasome assembly and the switch to fatty acid oxidation. Loss of COX7C impairs terminal CIV maturation, prevents incorporation of heart-specific isoforms, and destabilizes the respirasome organization. Notably, this defect causes a selective secondary failure of complex I completion, demonstrating that respirasome formation is required for catalytic CI maturation in vivo. Consequently, cardiac-specific COX7C deficiency fails to complete the perinatal metabolic transition, leading to the collapse of fatty acid oxidation, activation of nucleotide and serine-glycine-one-carbon metabolism, attenuated activation of the mitochondrial integrated stress response, and a metabolically and structurally compromised state unlikely to support the increasing energetic demands of the postnatal heart. Together, these findings define a developmentally timed, CIV-dependent assembly step that couples respiratory chain assembly to postnatal cardiac metabolic fate and provide a temporal framework for mitochondrial maturation in the developing heart.

title: Descriptive histological study of the sympathetic innervation of the human internal thoracic artery as a pedicle and a skeletonized graft.
authorString: Federspiel JM, Möhle RA, Hohl M, Abeln KB, Tschernig T, Kettner M, Kessler T, Tokcan M.
abstractText: The internal thoracic artery is an important graft used in coronary artery bypass surgery. However, there is a debate on the best practice regarding harvest, i.e., skeletonized or pedicled preparation. It remains controversial how skeletonization affects internal thoracic artery innervation. The presented exploratory study aimed to complement previous studies with a detailed histomorphological and histomorphometric analysis of the bilateral structure of the internal thoracic artery wall and innervation after skeletonized and pedicled preparation. Overall, 25 nitrite pickling salt and ethanol fixed corpses were included in the study. The left and right internal thoracic artery samples were both skeletonized and pedicled and divided into a proximal and a distal segment. Hematoxylin-eosin and Elastica van Gieson stains, and S100-, calcitonin gene-related peptide-, and tyrosine hydroxylase-immunolabeling were used to histomorphologically and histomorphometrically assess the samples. Explorative statistical analyses including age, sex, and the hierarchical data structure were computed. No significant atherosclerotic changes were observed in the intimal layer in any of the specimens. A relevant portion, i.e., 11/25 left and 13/25 right internal thoracic artery samples, presented with alterations of at least 50% of the tunica media assessed. No indication for a relevant impact of age and sex on the analyses of interest was found. As compared to pedicled vessels, skeletonized vessels showed a drastically reduced number of nerves accompanying the vessel. A great portion of the nerves following the internal thoracic artery was tyrosine hydrolase-immunoreactive. In summary, the histology-centered analyzes showed that skeletonization impacts internal thoracic artery innervation by drastically reducing the number of nerves accompanying the vessel. The analysis further revealed that internal thoracic artery medial degeneration is a frequent observation in elderly individuals. Further studies are needed to determine the impact of medial degeneration and hampered innervation on graft function.

title: JUVENILE IDIOPATHIC ARTHRITIS IN CHILDREN WITH TYPE 1 DIABETES: IMPACT OF CURRENT MEDICAL TREATMENT OPTIONS ON ANTHROPOMETRY AND METABOLIC CONTROL.
authorString: Klauser K, Bechtold-Dalla Pozza S, Ziegler J, Klinkert C, Mönkemöller K, Galler A, Holder M, Hörtenhuber T, Lilienthal E, Rosenbauer J, Holl R.
abstractText: Children with both type 1 diabetes (T1D) and juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) face increased disease complexity due to overlapping autoimmune and inflammatory processes. This study aimed to assess anthropometric, metabolic, and cardiovascular risk factors compared to children with T1D alone. Data from the Diabetes Patient Follow-up (DPV) registry (1995-2023) were analyzed, comparing 489 children with T1D and JIA to 67,462 children with T1D only. Children with T1D and JIA used diabetes technologies (insulin pumps, CGM, AID systems) more frequently with similar HbA1c levels. Between 2014-2019 and 2020-2023, HbA1c levels significantly improved in the JIA group, while BMI and height approached the T1D only group. Despite increased disease burden, children with T1D and JIA achieve glycemic control comparable to those with T1D alone. Nonetheless, elevated cardiometabolic risks highlight the need for tailored, interdisciplinary care strategies.

title: Induction of a Porcine Coronary Artery Perforation Model: A Comparison of Three Techniques.
authorString: Hyun DY, Park DS, Jeong MH, Sim DS, Hong YJ, Na MH, Jin YJ, Cho KH, Oh S, Kim JH.
abstractText: Coronary artery perforation (CAP) is a rare but life-threatening complication of percutaneous coronary intervention. Reliable preclinical models are essential for evaluating covered stents and other emerging coronary devices. This study established a reproducible porcine model capable of consistently inducing severe CAP and compared three perforation techniques for CAP induction. Three coronary perforation techniques were sequentially evaluated in 10 Yorkshire swine: guidewire penetration, scoring balloon pullback, and the sharpened catheter shaft technique. Perforation induction was assessed using coronary angiography according to the Ellis classification. The guidewire technique produced angiographically confirmed perforations in 2 of the 10 animals (20%), whereas the scoring balloon pullback technique failed to produce perforations in any animal. By contrast, the sharpened catheter shaft technique successfully induced Ellis Class III CAP in all animals (10/10, 100%). Initial balloon tamponade achieved hemostasis in 5 of the 10 animals (50%), and final hemostasis was achieved in 6 of the 10 animals (60%) after additional balloon tamponade in selected cases. Ventricular fibrillation occurred in four animals (40%), while echocardiography demonstrated hemopericardium in four animals (40%) and scant pericardial effusion in three animals (30%). Optical coherence tomography (OCT) and histological analyses consistently demonstrated severe structural vessel wall injury at the perforation sites. The sharpened catheter shaft technique enabled reproducible induction of Ellis Class III CAP in a porcine model, with angiographic, OCT, and histological findings consistent with severe vascular injury. This model may serve as a practical preclinical platform for evaluating covered stents and other emerging coronary devices.

title: Effects of the 2024 physician work-hour restrictions on Japanese surgeons.
authorString: Hasegawa H, Kakeji Y, Yamauchi H, Inomata M, Akashi-Tanaka S, Ara M, Ito K, Itoh S, Eguchi H, Kawase K, Kinoshita Y, Kiyozumi Y, Kobayashi S, Shibasaki I, Shirota C, Suzuki H, Takasu C, Fujikawa A, Bessho S, Horiuchi K, Maemura K, Maruo A, Miura T, Miyamoto Y, Yajima T, Yasuda A, Yamaguchi T, Iwanaka T, Baba H, Taketomi A, Committee for Improvement of Surgeons’ Work Environment.
abstractText: The current study investigated the impact of the April 2024 physician work-hour restrictions on Japanese surgeons. This web-based survey examined changes before and after the implementation of work-hour restrictions and their effects on medical care systems and patient safety. Hospitals were required to employ physicians under the following categories: category A, which allows up to 960 h of overtime annually, and categories B, C-1, and C-2, which allows up to 1,860 h of overtime annually. In total, 6,245 responses were analyzed. Approximately 8.1% of Category C-1 physicians had arrangements that enabled them to return to their homes within the stipulated time after night shifts. Furthermore, 28.5% of category B and C-2 physicians had such arrangements. Most respondents did not report changes in time usage before and after work-hour restrictions. However, 20.8% stated that their self-study time increased and 17.2% reported a decrease in academic activities. Approximately 31.5% reported a reduction in their income, and 37.3% had increased work-related stress levels. Moreover, 9.8% responded that restrictions decreased patient safety. Approximately 52.1% of the members rated the work-hour restrictions as poor. In light of the concerns expressed by surgeons, the effects of work hour restrictions should be further examined.

title: Unraveling protective effect of silymarin and silymarin nanoparticles on doxorubicin-induced cardiac toxicity via amelioration of oxidative stress, apoptosis and inflammation.
authorString: Mohammed HH, Mohammed SN, Shaker ES, El-Tahawy NGF, Ibrahim MFG.
abstractText: Doxorubicin is one of the most important chemotherapies, it treats many types of cancers but it has toxic effects on heart tissue as it causes oxidative stress, apoptosis and inflammation which limits the therapeutic usage of doxorubicin as an anticancer drug. Herbal extracts as silymarin have a cardioprotective effect and silymarin nanoparticles (SiNPs) improve the poor bioavailability of silymarin. To assess a comparison between the possible protective effect of Silymarin and its nanoparticles on doxorubicin induced cardiotoxicity and to assess the possible mechanisms. Forty-eight rats were divided into four groups: Control group, Doxorubicin group (Dx-group), Silymarin treated group (s-group) and Nanosilymarin treated group (SiNPs-group). Measurement of cardiac enzymes (CK, LDH, AST and ALT), malondialdehyde (MDA) and Glutathion (GSH) in the heart tissue, and histological approaches by light microscope, transmission electron microscope and immunohistochemical study for activated -caspase 3 and IL-6 were done. Dx-group showed significant (p < 0.05) increase in cardiac enzymes levels, significant (p < 0.05) increase in MDA levels in cardiomyocytes and significant (p < 0.05) decrease in GSH level compared to control group, also strong immunopositivity of IL-6 (p < 0.05) and activated-caspase 3(p < 0.01) and histological degenerative changes in the heart tissue. These changes improved in S-group but SiNPs-group showed better findings. Doxorubicin had an apparent damaging effect on cardiac tissue structure by different mechanisms as oxidative stress, apoptosis and inflammation and co-administration with natural compounds as silymarin improves the toxic effect of doxorubicin but silymarin nanoparticles give better effect than silymarin which is suggestive of improved bioavailability and targeted delivery.

title: Intracardiac hemodynamics in critical illness: paradigm evolution from mechanistic understanding and standardized assessment to a holographic future.
authorString: Cui X, Wang X.
abstractText: Hemodynamic disorders in critical illness extend beyond simple "hypotension" or "low cardiac output." They reflect decompensation of the cardiovascular system driven by the HOUR (Host/Organ Unregulated Response). In critical illness, the heart is not merely an isolated pump; it is also a central target and effector organ directly affected by systemic stress. This review summarizes advances in intracardiac hemodynamic assessment in critically ill patients. First, we describe hemodynamic mechanisms within the HOUR framework and emphasize the need to shift cardiac assessment from reliance on macroscopic parameters toward the study of intracardiac hemodynamics. Second, we discuss the methodological core, the "Intracardiac Hemodynamics 10-Step Assessment Process (10 s-ICEe)," which uses ten standardized steps to provide a systematic, closed-loop evaluation of the physiological pathway from venous return and transvalvular blood flow to arterial ejection. This process provides a practical link between mechanistic understanding and bedside decision-making in the ICU. Third, we examine how emerging technologies, including VFM, HyperDoppler, echoPIV, and 4D Flow MRI, are advancing assessment beyond one-dimensional velocity measurements toward multidimensional analysis of intracardiac vortices, energy loss, and blood flow vectors. We also consider the potential of "holographic cardiac assessment" to integrate structural, functional, blood flow, and perfusion information. This review aims to establish a comprehensive system for assessing intracardiac hemodynamics in critical illness, spanning basic assessment, advanced technologies, and integrated interpretation. It outlines the rationale and pathway for shifting hemodynamic management from structural observation to functional optimization, and from reliance on single parameters to system-level integration.

title: Stratification of the risk of septic complications at discharge in bariatric surgery: setting a new score.
authorString: Moroso F, Polese L, Frigo AC, Albanese A, Pozza G, Prevedello L, Fioretto P, Foletto M.
abstractText: Early detection of septic complications after metabolic bariatric surgery remains a relevant clinical challenge, particularly in the context of early discharge promoted by ERAS protocols. Identifying simple and readily available markers may facilitate timely recognition of individuals at higher risk of infectious complications after discharge. A cohort of 1001 consecutive individuals undergoing metabolic bariatric surgery was analyzed. Clinical and laboratory parameters were collected on postoperative day (POD) 1 and POD3, including body temperature (BT), white blood cell count (WBC), C-reactive protein (CRP), and hemoglobin. Complications were classified according to the Clavien-Dindo system. Univariate and multivariate analyses were used to identify independent predictors of septic complications, which were subsequently integrated into a combined ROC model from which a predictive score was derived. Septic complications occurred in 2.20% of individuals, while leaks were observed in 0.50%. BT, WBC, CRP, and hemoglobin on POD3 were the parameters most strongly associated with septic complications. The combined ROC curve yielded an AUC of 0.8527. Optimal cutoffs (BT > 37 °C, WBC > 11.3 × 103/mL, CRP > 56 mg/L, hemoglobin < 13.3 g/dL) were used to construct a 0-4-point score. With a cutoff ≥ 2, the score achieved approximately 75% sensitivity and specificity, with a negative predictive value of 99.27%. The post-test probability of septic complications was 0.73% when the score was below the selected cutoff. The proposed score, based on routine parameters available on POD3, represents a simple and potentially useful tool for stratifying the risk of infectious complications after discharge. Its performance exceeds that of individual markers. Validation in larger and multicenter populations will be required to confirm its reliability and define its clinical applicability.

title: G protein-coupled receptor sensing of extracellular long-chain ceramides in atherosclerosis: asymmetric evidence for CysLT2R and P2Y6R and potential amplification in chronic kidney disease.
authorString: Wang Z, Li X, Gao Y, Guo Q, Zhang Z, Li M.

journal.title: Inflammation research : official journal of the European Histamine Research Society ... [et al.]

abstractText:
Background

Residual atherosclerotic risk persists despite intensive lipid-lowering therapy, particularly in chronic kidney disease (CKD). Circulating ceramides predict cardiovascular outcomes, while their extracellular receptor-mediated actions are less well characterized.

Methods

This narrative review used structured searches of five databases through August 9, 2026, without language restrictions. Two authors independently selected and appraised studies, with disagreements adjudicated by a third. Evidence was classified according to mechanistic directness.

Results

For this review, C16-C20 N-acyl ceramides are operationally termed long-chain species. Ceramide-bound CysLT2R-Gq structures provide direct evidence of ligand recognition, whereas support for P2Y6R remains primarily functional, mutational, and disease-model based. Cer16:0-associated receptor signaling enhances Gq/Ca²⁺ responses and NLRP3 inflammasome output under experimentally primed conditions. Additional ceramide-responsive receptors include FPR2, supported by ceramide-bound Gi structures, and GPR64/ADGRG2, investigated in a distinct cancer context. Experimental Cer16:0 concentrations exceed a reference total-plasma concentration by approximately 30-151-fold. Human genetic support for receptor-specific causality is limited, and CKD-dependent amplification has yet to be demonstrated.

Conclusions

Extracellular ceramide sensing may connect sphingolipid signaling with atherosclerosis through receptor-dependent pathways. Independent replication, carrier-resolved exposure measurements, and cell-specific receptor investigations are required before therapeutic translation.

title: Left Atrial Appendage Function vs. Geometry: Predicting Thrombus Risk in Atrial Fibrillation.
authorString: Pamuk FÖ, Dönmez E, İnan D, Ziyrek M.

journal.title: Turk Kardiyoloji Dernegi arsivi : Turk Kardiyoloji Derneginin yayin organidir

abstractText:
Objective

Left atrial appendage (LAA) thrombus and/or spontaneous echo contrast (SEC) may occur despite adequate anticoagulation in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF). This study aimed to evaluate whether mitral annular geometry (annular area and sphericity) and the angle between the mitral annular plane and the Coumadin ridge are associated with LAA thrombus and/or SEC in anticoagulated patients with AF.

Method

We retrospectively enrolled 133 consecutive patients with AF (≥2 years' duration) receiving anticoagulant therapy who were referred for ablation or cardioversion. Preprocedural TEE provided measurements of LAA fractional area change (FAC), flow velocity, MAP-Coumadin ridge angle, mitral annular area, and sphericity. Logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of thrombus/SEC.

Results

LAA thrombus/SEC was present in 44 patients (33.1%). Compared with unaffected patients, those with thrombus/SEC had lower LAA FAC (0.26+-0.13 vs. 0.37+-0.12, P < 0.001), a larger mitral annular area (992.50+-210.81 vs. 898.75+-159.04 mm², P = 0.009), lower LVEF, more frequent heart failure, and larger cardiac dimensions. The MAP-LAA angle and sphericity were similar between the groups. On multivariable analysis, LAA FAC was the sole independent predictor (OR 0.49 per 10% increment, 95% CI 0.32-0.70, P < 0.001; AUC 0.72, cutoff 0.20, sensitivity 44%, specificity 96%). Mitral annular area showed modest discriminatory ability (AUC 0.64) and did not significantly improve the model when combined with FAC (P = 0.39).

Conclusion

LAA FAC is a strong independent predictor of thrombus/SEC in anticoagulated patients with AF, underscoring the primacy of appendage contractile function over geometric parameters. Mitral annular enlargement provides only marginal incremental value, whereas the MAP-LAA angle does not contribute. Routine measurement of LAA FAC provides a simple, reproducible echocardiographic tool for thrombus risk stratification.

title: The genetic architecture of lipoprotein(a): simplicity, complexity, and mutability
authorString: Mukamel RE, Rubinacci S, Kamitaki N, Handsaker RE, Hujoel MLA, Tang D, McCarroll SA, Loh P.
abstractText: High levels of lipoprotein(a) (Lp(a)) increase risk of cardiovascular diseases. Lp(a) concentration is primarily determined (>80%) by genetic variation at  LPA , particularly by its large, size-polymorphic kringle IV-2 (KIV-2) repeat. However, because variation of the KIV-2 repeat is difficult to measure, the precise ways that genetic variants at  LPA and other loci determine Lp(a) levels have been unclear, especially in individuals of non-European ancestry. Here, we developed new computational techniques to accurately genotype KIV-2 variation in whole-genome-sequenced population cohorts. Applying these methods to UK Biobank (n=490,414) and All of Us (n=245,394) provided insights into the genetic determinants of Lp(a) and the mutational dynamics of the KIV-2 repeat, which we found expands or contracts intra-allelically once every ∼500 generations. Variation in Lp(a) levels among people of all genetic ancestries was accurately predicted by a single, transferable genetic model capturing  cis -epistatic effects of KIV-2 length and protein-altering polymorphisms in  LPA . Controlling for predicted effects of  LPA alleles revealed an additional, highly polygenic contribution to Lp(a) variation:  LPA -adjusted Lp(a) levels associated with genetic variation at over 300 loci (  P <5x10  -8 ), much like other blood lipids. These results elucidate the genetic architecture and mutational origins of Lp(a) variation, showing how detailed characterization of a largely monogenic trait can provide surprising insights for complex trait genetics.

title: Treg- and CD8-Specific PD-1 Deficiency Reveals That CD8⁺ T Cell-Intrinsic Signaling Uniquely Restrains Pressure Overload Inflammation and Heart Failure
authorString: He X, Weng X, Pan L, Niu Z, Bhattarai U, Xu R, Wang D, Zeng H, Chen J, Clemmer JS, Singh A, LaMarca B, Blazar BR, Hall M, Chen Y.
abstractText:
Aims

PD-1 signaling limits cardiac remodeling and heart failure (HF). Whether this protection depends on PD-1 signaling intrinsic to CD8⁺ T cells or on regulation by other immune populations, including regulatory T cells (Tregs), remains unclear.

Methods and results

Using transverse aortic constriction (TAC), we studied global PD-1-knockout (KO) mice with or without CD8⁺ T cell depletion, CD8⁺ T cell-specific (PD1KO CD8 ), and Treg-specific PD-1-KO mice. We assessed left ventricular (LV) remodeling, genomic profiles, immune infiltration, and the therapeutic impact of C-X-C motif chemokine receptor 3 (CXCR3) blockade. CD8⁺ T cell depletion abolished TAC-induced left ventricular (LV) hypertrophy, fibrosis, and dysfunction of global PD-1-KO mice. PD1KO CD8 mice had normal baseline cardiac function but, after TAC, showed reduced survival, worse LV dysfunction and fibrosis, and greater immune cell infiltration. CD8⁺ T cells from PD1KO CD8 mice showed increased activation and proliferation, with increased production of cytotoxic molecules, such as IFN-γ⁺ and granzyme A, both at baseline and after TAC. Post-TAC transcriptomics revealed enhanced inflammatory pathways and suppressed metabolic pathways in PD1KO CD8 hearts. TAC also increased LV CXCR3 + CD8 + T cell accumulation and CXCL9/CXCL10 expression in PD1KO CD8 mice. CXCR3 neutralizing antibody treatment reduced LV CD8 + T cell accumulation and attenuated cardiac dysfunction. In contrast, Treg-specific PD-1 deficiency did not alter baseline or TAC-induced cardiac remodeling.

Conclusions

CD8⁺ T cell-intrinsic PD-1 restrains TAC-induced HF, whereas Treg-intrinsic PD-1 is dispensable. CXCR3-dependent recruitment drives pathological CD8⁺ T cell accumulation, identifying PD-1/CXCR3 axis as a key regulator of CD8⁺ T cell-mediated cardiac injury.

title: Plasma Proteogenomic Uncovers Novel Molecular Mechanisms of Soluble Endoglin and Identifies AZI2 as a new Player in Arteriovenous Malformations in Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia
authorString: Munsch G, Proust C, Richter CE, Germain M, Tusseau M, Guilhem A, Mohamed S, Richardot C, Samaria F, Thibord F, Caro I, Bardel C, Struck E, INVENT Consortium, Olaso R, Deleuze J, Debette S, Peiretti F, Butler LM, Jaspard-Vinassa B, Shavit JA, Rossi E, Dupuis-Girod S, Trégouët D, Soukarieh O.
abstractText: Endoglin is a transmembrane glycoprotein that plays a key role in vascular development, angiogenesis and endothelial homeostasis. Its soluble form (Sol-ENG), generated through proteolytic shedding of the membrane-bound protein, has been implicated in the pathophysiology of numerous cardiovascular diseases, ranging from common conditions such as preeclampsia and thrombosis to rare diseases such as hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (HHT). Leveraging large-scale genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics and metabolomics data from public and original resources, we identify a molecular signature of 24 markers associated with plasma levels of Sol-ENG. This signature was enriched in genes coding for GPI-enchored proteins and included metabolites participating to glycosylation and redox homeostasis. Furthermore, we observed that ABO blood groups and genetically predicted plasma levels of 5-Azacytidine Induced 2 (AZI2) associate with the risk of arteriovenous malformations in HHT patients. This study provides new insights into the physiological mechanisms underlying Endoglin regulation and opens clinical perspectives for the management of HHT patients.

title: Epidemiology of Cardiac Structure and Function Among African Caribbeans in Tobago: A Population-based Cohort Study
authorString: Deb Nath N, Miljkovic I, Katz R, Hosner J, Mallugari RR, Cvejkus RK, Cruz LA, Wheeler V, Thomas CN, Gupta DK, Kuipers AL.
abstractText:
Background:

Individuals of African genetic ancestry are at high risk for heart failure (HF), which is often preceded by cardiac structural and functional abnormalities. Nevertheless, little is known about cardiac structure and function among Afro-Caribbeans residing in Tobago. This study aimed to investigate the epidemiology of cardiac structure and function among African Caribbeans in Tobago. Methods: A total of 924 participants (41-83 years) underwent clinical evaluation and transthoracic echocardiography. Images were analyzed for left ventricular (LV) mass index (MI), left atrial volume index, diastolic dysfunction (DD), LV ejection fraction (LVEF), global longitudinal strain (GLS), E/e′ ratio, E/A ratio, and other echocardiographic measures. Cardiac structure and function were evaluated by age, sex, and HF stage.

Results:

The mean age was 61.7 years, with 61.4% women, 47.8% obesity, and 20.2% diabetes. Average systolic blood pressure was approximately 140 mmHg, and 76.7% had hypertension. Abnormal LV geometry was present in 77.1% of participants, predominantly concentric remodeling (69.5%). The prevalence of DD was 13.4%, LVEF <50% was 1.5%, and abnormal GLS (≤-18%) was 5.2%. Women had significantly higher E/e′ ratios and a higher prevalence of Stage A and Stage B HF, whereas men had a higher prevalence of symptomatic (Stage C) HF. Participants aged 65-83 years had significantly higher E/e′ ratio, concentric remodeling, and LV hypertrophy than those aged 41-57 years.

Conclusions:

Women and older adults have higher LV structural abnormalities and DD than men and younger adults. These results will be helpful to inform public health priorities related to cardiovascular health in Tobago.

title: Noninvasive Cardiac Arrest Recognition Using Wearable Sensors in a Porcine Model of Ventricular Fibrillation
authorString: Englhardt Z, Bin Saeed M, Razi A, Ayoub I, Baetiong A, Patel S, Gazmuri RJ, Sunshine JE, Iyer V.
abstractText:
Background:

Wearable detection of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) could improve survival, given the prognostic importance of time to resuscitation and that 50% to 75% of events are unwitnessed. Existing systems may be limited by their form factor and by specificity achieved at the cost of sensitivity. We investigated whether the raw photoplethysmography (PPG) signal from low-cost wearable sensors contains a distinct signature of circulatory arrest.

Methods:

Ventricular fibrillation (VF) was electrically induced in 9 invasively monitored pigs while raw PPG was recorded with a wearable-class sensor. PPG dynamics after VF onset were related to aortic and right atrial pressures. A heuristic detection algorithm was evaluated for sensitivity and latency by leave-one-out cross-validation in the porcine data and for false positives in 57,857 hours of free-living PPG from 115 human participants.

Results:

After VF onset, the raw PPG showed a reproducible exponential decay (time constant 10.53 s; coefficient of variation 8.9% to 17.0% over the first 10 s) that tracked rising right atrial pressure (r = 0.90), reflecting arterial-to-venous blood redistribution. The algorithm detected VF in 8 of 9 animals (sensitivity 0.889; 95% CI, 0.518-0.997) with a median latency of 57.2 s. In the human cohort, it produced 2.73 false positives per user-year (95% CI, 1.62-4.31), comparable to current systems.

Conclusions:

Raw wearable PPG encodes circulatory collapse during VF, as supported by invasive hemodynamic measurements. While preliminary, these results suggest the potential for wearable-based OHCA detection with improved sensitivity, reduced latency, and comparable specificity.

title: Automated echocardiography image quality assessment and its association with AI performance
authorString: Lopez-Gutierrez P, Garrido-Oliver J, Bragulat-Arevalo M, Betancur-Rengifo JP, Cauwenberghs N, Morales-Galan A, Elbatel M, Boonstra MJ, Ferrando F, Majul H, Rivas Catoni L, Grieve SM, van der Zwaard S, Qin Y, Asselbergs FW, Kuznetsova T, Teixido-Tura G, Lee AP, Li X, Lekadir K, Galian-Gay L, Rodriguez-Palomares J, Ferreira-Gonzalez I, Dux-Santoy L, Guala A.
abstractText:
Background:

Echocardiographic image quality influences clinical interpretation, yet its definition remains subjective and its impact on artificial intelligence (AI) systems has not been systematically evaluated. We developed EchoQuality, a deep-learning model for automated echocardiography quality assessment, and quantified the effect of image quality on AI performance across a broad range of tasks. Methods A multidisciplinary co-creation process established a definition of echocardiographic image quality, which was used to annotate 6,474 videos for EchoQuality development and internal testing, and 1,000 videos for external testing. The impact of image quality on the performance of state-of-the-art AI models was subsequently assessed for the prediction of 12 measurements, and the detection of 5 moderate dysfunctions and 6 cardiac diseases across five international cohorts totalling 762,588 videos from 25,205 echocardiography studies. In addition, a quality-aware aggregation strategy was developed to mitigate the impact of low-quality images. Results EchoQuality achieved a performance comparable to the inter-observer agreement, while the agreement with an expert in a prospective, blinded best-clip selection experiment was 90.4%. In downstream AI uses, high-quality studies resulted in the highest performance in 97 of 122 (80%) of evaluations. The median performance gaps between high- and low-quality videos were 10% [5-20%] in the prediction of quantitative measurements (R2), 14% [7-20%] in the identification of moderate dysfunctions (sensitivity), 12% [3-20%] in the detection of diseases (sensitivity), 12% [9-15%] in view identification (accuracy), and 3% [2-5%] in left-ventricular segmentation (Dice score). Performance gaps were consistent across state-of-the-art models, datasets, and tasks. Finally, a quality-aware aggregation strategy improved performance in 88% (63 of 72) of the evaluations, with a median relative improvement of 5% [1-15%]. Conclusions EchoQuality provides an automated assessment of echocardiographic image quality, a major determinant of AI performance. Incorporating quality-awareness may improve the robustness and clinical reliability of echocardiographic AI systems.

title: MAGNITUDE OF METABOLIC SYNDROME AND ITS ASSOCIATED FACTORS AMONG PATIENTS WITH TYPE 2 DIABETES MELLITUS WHO ARE ON FOLLOW-UP AT ASELLA REFERRAL AND TEACHING HOSPITAL DIABETIC CLINIC, ASELLA, OROMIA, ETHIOPIA IN 2022.
authorString: Mitiku NT, Nigatu LM, Shanka NY.
abstractText:
Background:

- Type 2 Diabetes mellites and Metabolic syndrome are global public health problems, and their burden is rising, particularly in developing countries. Metabolic syndrome (syndrome X, insulin resistance syndrome) consists of a constellation of metabolic abnormalities that confer increased risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD) and diabetes mellitus. There are limited data on prevalence of metabolic syndrome in type II DM patients in Ethiopia and in the horn of Africa at large, and no research has been done in our institution on this topic.

Objective:

- To determine the prevalence of metabolic syndrome and its associated factors in patients with type 2 diabetes on follow up at Asella Referral and Teaching Hospital diabetes follow up clinic, Asella, Oromia, Ethiopia.

Method:

- Cross-sectional, prospective, hospital-based survey was conducted to assess the prevalence of metabolic syndrome and its associated factors in type II DM patients among those who visited diabetic follow-up clinic of Asella referral and teaching Hospital. All type II DM patients, who visited the diabetic follow-up clinic in the study period was included in the study. 285 participants were selected using systemic random sampling technique. Data was collected from patients and their chart and filled on a checklist by trained data collectors. Data was entered to epi-data cleared and analyzed by SPSS version 26.0 and Odds ratio with 95% CI and P-value of <0.05 was considered for declaring level of significance.

Results:

- Using the NCEP-ATP III criteria the magnitude of Metabolic syndrome was 75.1% in this study. Among the components of Metabolic syndrome high blood pressure was the commonest (70.9%) followed by low HDL Cholesterol (70.5%), high Triglyceride (46%) and high Waist circumference (12.6%) respectively. Female and Male had comparable prevalence of Metabolic syndrome and the study showed that 55.4% of participants were taking Lipid lowering medications.
