Ric-8B bound nucleotide-free Gαolf and Gαs with high affinity (KD, 21 and 29 nmol/L) through Arg75 and promoted their folding, stability, membrane localization, and cAMP signaling. Disrupting this interface reduced macrophage inflammasome activation and cholesterol accumulation. In Ldlr-/- chimeras, the targeted interference peptide localized to plaque macrophages, suppressed lesional Gαs/olf activity, and reduced atherosclerosis; these effects were absent with a nonbinding control peptide or Ric-8BR75E. In male patients' carotid plaques, plasma IFN-γ (interferon-γ) correlated with macrophage-associated Ric-8B S468/T473 phosphorylation. IFN-γ activated a STAT1 (signal transducer and activator of transcription 1)-independent ERK2 (extracellular signal-regulated kinase 2)-casein kinase 2 α catalytic subunit pathway that phosphorylated Ric-8B at S468/T473, enhancing chaperone activity. Phosphomimetic substitution lowered the pooled fitted oxLDL EC50 for cAMP generation (11.5 versus 27.7 µg/mL in wild-type cells) without increasing basal cAMP; replicate-level EC50 estimates did not differ significantly (P=0.17). This substitution restored the atherogenic phenotype suppressed by Ifngr1 deficiency in obese, but not nonobese, chimeras.

Conclusions

Ric-8B sustains macrophage Gαs/olf-cAMP signaling and atherogenesis. Obesity-associated IFN-γ enhances macrophage responses to oxLDL through STAT1-independent ERK2-casein kinase 2 α catalytic subunit-Ric-8B signaling, supporting a 2-hit mechanism and identifying the Ric-8B-Gα interface as a potential therapeutic target.

title: AMOTL2: A key regulator of mechanotransduction in development, vascular disease and cancer.
authorString: Fonseca P, Zhang Y, Holmgren L.
abstractText: Mechanical forces play a fundamental role in regulating cell behavior during development, tissue homeostasis, and disease. The angiomotin family protein AmotL2 has emerged as a central integrator of mechanotransduction, linking cell-cell adhesion, cytoskeletal tension, and nuclear architecture to transcriptional control. Through its ability to connect cadherin-based junctions to radial actin filaments and the nuclear lamina, AmotL2 establishes a continuous mechanical axis that enables cells to sense and respond to extracellular forces. This function is essential for epithelial organization, vascular morphogenesis, and endothelial responses to shear stress, in part through regulation of Hippo pathway effectors such as YAP and TAZ. Dysregulation of AmotL2 contributes to pathological states, including abdominal aortic aneurysm, where reduced AmotL2 impairs endothelial mechanotransduction, and cancer, where induction of the p60AmotL2 isoform disrupts polarity, alters nuclear mechanics, and promotes invasive behavior. Emerging evidence further suggests that AmotL2 regulates transcription through direct effects on nuclear structure and chromatin accessibility, positioning it as a key regulator of force-dependent gene expression. In this review, we summarize the structural and mechanistic basis of AmotL2 function and discuss its roles in development, vascular biology, and cancer, highlighting its potential as a therapeutic target in diseases driven by altered mechanotransduction.

title: Association between red blood cell indices and abdominal aortic calcification: Results of a nationwide survey.
authorString: Yang Q, Nie S, Li X, Feng N, Zheng X, Dai Z, Su L.
abstractText:
Objectives

Vascular calcification has been linked to Red Blood Cell Indices (RBIs). This study aimed to investigate the association between RBIs and Abdominal Aortic Calcification (AAC).

Methods

This study investigated RBIs and AAC using cross-sectional data from 2,823 participants in the 2013‒2014 U.S. National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES). Weighted linear/logistic regression were used to assess the association between RBIs and AAC, complemented by Restricted Cubic Spline (RCS) dose-response analysis as well as subgroup analyses to ensure the robustness of the results.

Results

Among participants, 261 (9.25%) had severe AAC, and 602 (21.32%) had mild-to-moderate AAC. Regression analysis showed that Red Blood Cell count (RBC-count) and Hematocrit (HCT) significantly negatively correlated with AAC score and severe AAC risk (p < 0.05). RCS analysis revealed L-shaped nonlinear relationships (RBC-count with AAC score/severe AAC; HCT with AAC score), with inflection points at 4.59 million cells/uL (RBC-count) and 41.32% (HCT). Subgroup analyses demonstrated consistent associations across demographic/clinical strata, except for a significant gender interactions observed (RBC-count: p for interaction = 0.058; HCT: p for interaction = 0.002). In males, RBC-count and HCT showed negative associations with severe AAC risk (RBC-count: OR = 0.40, 95% CI 0.26, 0.60; HCT: OR = 0.91, 95% CI 0.87, 0.96), whereas female associations were nonsignificant.

Conclusion

RBC count showed an L-shaped negative correlation with both AAC scores and severe AAC, while HCT also exhibited an L-shaped negative correlation with AAC scores. This indicates their potential value as auxiliary biomarkers for AAC detection and prevention strategies.

title: DDR2 plays an endothelial cell-intrinsic role during breast tumor angiogenesis and metastasis.
authorString: DiMauro A, Brenot A, Morikis VA, Lesage J, Weber JH, Melam A, Martin JA, Stewart SA, Weber JD, Longmore GD.
abstractText: Tumor angiogenesis is a process of new blood vessel formation from pre-existing vessels. It is controlled by communications between tumor cells and tumor associated stromal cells with adjacent endothelial cells (ECs). In tumor cells and cancer associated fibroblasts (CAFs) the collagen receptor DDR2 contributes to breast cancer invasion and metastasis. In CAFs, DDR2 influences the secretion of growth factor such as the pro-angiogenic VEGF. As such, DDR2 has been suggested to contribute to tumor angiogenesis, but whether through EC-intrinsic actions or via factors secreted by tumor cells or CAFs has not been established. Human breast tumor scRNAseq data and multiplex immunohistochemistry (mIHC) analyses revealed that a subset of tumor ECs, perhaps migratory tip-like cells, and lymphatic endothelial cells (LECs) express DDR2, particularly in metastatic TNBC tumors. To determine if DDR2 played an endothelial cell-intrinsic role in breast tumor angiogenesis and metastasis, we selectively deleted Ddr2 in ECs using the inducible Cdh5-CreERT2 allele in the context of the MMTV-PyMT metastatic mouse breast tumor model. This resulted in decreased lung metastases without any change in primary tumor burden or total tumor ECs. There were, however, significant alterations in endothelial vessel length in primary tumors. Ddr2-deleted mice also exhibited defects in normal angiogenesis. Using 3D microfluidic devices, primary cells, and aortic ring outgrowth assays genetic depletion and chemical inhibition of Ddr2 resulted in reduced EC migration and decreased tip cell like gene expression. Together, these data define a role of EC DDR2 in normal and breast tumor angiogenesis that could contribute to metastasis.

title: 2-hydroxyglutarate-dependent inhibition of TET2 is a molecular link between metabolic reprogramming and smooth muscle cell differentiation
authorString: Esparza Pinelo JE, Robin A, Richard A, Dosunmu A, Garcia Serrano J, Gonzalez AD, Krenz H, Chen J, Carrera M, Bornes KE, Roy SS, Chatthopadhyay A, Milewicz DM, Gottlieb E, Kwartler CS.
abstractText:
Background

Smooth muscle cell (SMC) phenotypic modulation is accompanied by metabolic reprogramming, but the mechanisms linking metabolism to contractile gene expression remain unclear. We investigated whether 2-hydroxyglutarate (2-HG), an inhibitor of α-ketoglutarate-dependent dioxygenases, links metabolic changes to regulation of ten-eleven translocation 2 (TET2) in Acta2 R179C/+ SMCs

Methods

Primary wild-type (WT) and Acta2 R179C/+ mouse aortic SMCs were treated with nicotinamide riboside (NR), exogenous R&L-2-HG, or cholesterol. Endogenous accumulation of L-2HG was achieved by lentivuris-mediated knockdown (KD) of L2hgdh. We assessed contractile marker expression, cellular metabolism, TET2 chromatin occupancy, and DNA methylation and hydroxymethylation. L-2HG levels were assessed using liquid chromatography/mass spectroscopy. Carotid artery 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC) staining was assessed in mice after left carotid artery ligation.

Results

Acta2 R179C/+ SMCs have elevated 2-HG, reduced TET2 expression and chromatin occupancy, and lower 5hmC enrichment at CArG-containing SMC loci, consistent with repressed TET2 activity. NR boosts oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS), reduces 2-HG in WT and mutant SMCs, increases TET2 expression and 5hmC enrichment, and reduces global 5-methylcytosine. Carotid artery 5hmC staining shows changes in the same direction, but group differences are not statistically significant. Exogenous L-2-HG attenuates NR-induced contractile marker expression in Acta2 R179C/+ SMCs and also decreases contractile marker expression, reduces TET2 occupancy and 5hmC enrichment, and shifts WT SMC metabolism toward glycolysis, phenocopying the metabolic state of Acta2 R179C/+ SMCs. Endogenous accumulation of L-2HG by L2hgdh KD reduces contractile markers in WT SMCS. Cholesterol reduces TET2 and contractile marker expression, decreases 5hmC enrichment, and increases global DNA methylation.

Conclusions

These findings support a role for 2-HG in coupling metabolic state to epigenetic changes associated with SMC phenotypic modulation. NR-associated differentiation coincides with increased TET2 expression and DNA hydroxymethylation, identifying metabolic regulation of the SMC epigenome as a potential approach to preserving contractile gene expression.

title: Building an Auditable Reference Standard for Clinical Information Extraction from Transesophageal Echocardiography Reports
authorString: MacKay EJ, Kaplan MS, Yuan M, Chen AL, Ge Y, Canales L, Yu E, Shad R, Zhang B, Pouch AM.
abstractText:
Objectives:

To develop an auditable, two-institution reference standard for intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) reports and evaluate whether reviewer disagreement identifies limitations in the underlying clinical information model. Materials and Methods We selected 300 reports (150 per institution) from 925 at the University of Pennsylvania and University of Washington using random sampling and enrichment for challenging documentation. Four trained abstractors applied a shared 39-variable V1 codebook. Independent paired comparisons included 297 reports; three historical reports contributed only to the final reference standard. Categorical agreement used exact agreement and unweighted Cohen's κ; numeric left-ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) used exact agreement and mean absolute differences. Disagreements underwent structured expert adjudication and reason classification. Additional analyses assessed reviewer-pair, sampling-stratified, and population-weighted agreement. Results Among 11,583 formal reviewer-comparison cells, 10,293 (88.9%) were resolved by reviewer agreement and 1,290 (11.1%) required targeted expert adjudication (1,289 tasks). Codebook/schema ambiguity (40.8%) and interpretation/classification differences (25.2%) together accounted for 66.0% of targeted tasks. Adjudication was concentrated in aortic dissection, valve type, and post-intervention findings. Categorical κ ranged from 0.364 to 0.960 and was inversely correlated with targeted-adjudication burden (Spearman ρ=−0.884; 95% CI, −0.955 to −0.734). Sampling-weighted κ changed by no more than 0.05 for 32 of 35 categorical variables. Discussion Structured adjudication identified recurring schema and interpretation challenges beyond individual abstraction errors, providing specific targets for information-model refinement. Conclusion As NLP and LLM-based abstraction tools move toward clinical use, the reference standards used to evaluate them require comparably rigorous development, adjudication, and independent validation.

title: Real-world safety assessment of Mpox Vaccine in Catalonia: Retrospective Cohort Study of Adverse Events of Special Interest and Breakthrough Infections
authorString: Rodriguez¹˒² AS, Roigé-Peña¹ V, Convertino¹˒⁴ I, Solórzano¹˒⁵ M, Far¹ M, Villalobos¹ F.
abstractText: Mpox vaccination with the Modified Vaccinia Ankara-Bavarian Nordic (MVA-BN) vaccine has been used to protect people at increased risk of infection, but real-world safety data from Europe remain limited. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 8,039 adults in Catalonia, Spain, who received at least one MVA-BN dose between June 13, 2022 and December 31, 2024, using routinely collected primary care and linked hospital records. We looked for five prespecified adverse events of special interest (myocarditis, pericarditis, thrombocytopenia, anaphylaxis and generalized convulsive seizure) within 28 days after each dose, and described mpox infections diagnosed after vaccination. Participants were predominantly men (97.7%) and aged 26–45 years (68.0%). Adverse events were rare: fewer than five cases of pericarditis occurred within 28 days of vaccination (day 19 after the first dose), and no other event of special interest was identified in that window. Sixteen participants (0.20%; 95% confidence interval 0.11–0.32%) had a recorded mpox diagnosis after vaccination. These findings provide preliminary, region-specific reassurance about the short-term safety of MVA-BN. However, events were few, there was no unvaccinated comparison group, and the study cannot establish causality or vaccine effectiveness. Continued monitoring of vaccine safety is warranted.

title: Transfemoral-TAVR Through Right Aortic Arch and Iliac Tortuosity: A Stepwise Guide to Overcoming Anatomical Barriers.
authorString: Patrascu A, Töpper A, Omran A, Eichstaedt H, Fleißner F, Moazzezi S, Eldergash OA, Martens A, Elsaesser A.
abstractText:
Objective

This study aims to demonstrate a systematic, step-by-step transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVR) strategy in a patient with right aortic arch (RAA), aberrant supra-aortic branching, Kommerell diverticulum, and severe bilateral iliac artery tortuosity.

Key steps

1) Preprocedural computed tomography planning for annular sizing, access evaluation, and fluoroscopic angle optimization. 2) Ultrasound-guided bilateral femoral access with hybrid closure strategy (suture-/plug-based vascular closure devices). 3) Navigation of kinked iliac arteries with gradual increase in wire stiffness and tapered dilator. 4) Modified delivery system flexion to navigate the right aortic arch. 5) Partial proximal balloon inflation (2-3 cm3) to facilitate annular crossing.

Potential pitfalls

Right femoral access may cause excess torsion along the RAA. RAA geometry impedes coaxial alignment and may cause delivery system stalling. A horizontal aorta increases difficulty crossing the annulus.

Take-home message

With meticulous computed tomography-based planning, transfemoral TAVR can be performed safely in patients with congenital aortic arch anomalies and challenging peripheral vasculature.

title: Transcatheter Closure of a Septal Occluder Erosion 2 Decades After Implantation.
authorString: Parker E, Hlaing SH, Aroney N, Walters L, Aroney C, Walters D.
abstractText:
Background

Atrial septal defects (ASDs) are the most common congenital heart defects. Transcatheter device closure is a viable alternative to surgical closure of secundum ASDs. Over the years, multiple device-related complications have been reported. These include device embolization, cardiac erosion, aortic regurgitation, infective endocarditis, arrhythmias, and thromboembolic events.

Case summary

Our case presents a rare instance of ASD occluder device erosion into the right atrium over 2 decades after implantation, presenting with hemolysis. The fistula was successfully treated with a transcatheter closure approach.

Discussion

To our knowledge, this is the longest reported period of ASD device erosion after index implantation. Multimodality imaging was used to characterize the defect and assess its suitability for a transcatheter approach.

Take-home message

Maintain a high index of suspicion for device-related complications, including erosion, even decades after the initial procedure.

title: Same-Day TAVR and Femur Fracture Repair in a 103-Year-Old Woman: Beyond Chronologic Age.
authorString: Gupta R, Sullivan MP, Ali ST, Gorji R, Ditah C, Kalra A.
abstractText:
Clinical condition

A 103-year-old woman with critical nonrheumatic calcific aortic stenosis was transferred to an academic medical center after an urgent femoral fracture fixation was deferred because of high perioperative cardiac risk.

Key questions

Why was transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) chosen before orthopedic surgery, and why was balloon aortic valvuloplasty not an optimal bridge? What was the severity and clinical impact of post-TAVR aortic regurgitation? How did procedural risk influence sedation and anesthesia? How did multidisciplinary teams coordinate expedited care?

Outcome

TAVR was performed to reduce intraoperative cardiac risk, followed by open reduction and internal fixation later the same day. Structural heart, anesthesia, orthopedic, rehabilitation, and social work teams coordinated expedited treatment and recovery planning.

Take-home messages

Severe aortic stenosis and acute fracture require coordinated, time-sensitive management. TAVR may facilitate timely orthopedic surgery and reduce immobilization-related decline. Candidacy should consider frailty, functional status, physiologic reserve, procedural risk, recovery potential, and patient goals, not age alone.

title: Macroscopic evidence of regression of sinus dilatation inside the Florida sleeve.
authorString: Ito H, Inoue R, Narukawa T, Tanabe M, Sakakibara S, Sakamoto S, Yamauchi T.
abstractText: The Florida sleeve procedure is a valve-sparing technique for aortic root aneurysms. Because redo surgeries are rare, macroscopic evidence of how the native aorta adapts inside the graft has never been reported. We report two reoperative cases performed for recurrent aortic regurgitation and infective endocarditis 12 and 14 months, respectively, after the initial Florida sleeve procedure. Intraoperatively, the previously folded, aneurysmal native aortic walls had neatly regressed and tightly adhered to the graft's inner surface, obliterating any potential dead space. These cases provide the first macroscopic evidence of true biological reverse remodeling inside the Florida sleeve.

title: The Ross procedure: Technical principles, operative strategy, and pitfalls for long-term success.
authorString: Alsoufi B.
abstractText: The Ross procedure remains an attractive aortic valve replacement strategy for children, adolescents, and selected young adults. Pulmonary autograft replacement provides excellent hemodynamics, freedom from anticoagulation, growth potential in children, and favorable long-term survival in appropriately selected patients. These advantages, however, come at the cost of substantial technical complexity. Small imperfections during autograft harvest, implantation, coronary transfer, or root reconstruction can result in early dysfunction, coronary complications, or late autograft dilatation and failure. The purpose of this review is to summarize a practical and reproducible approach to the Ross procedure with emphasis on operative strategy, technical details, Ross-Konno modifications, autograft stabilization techniques, and avoidance of common pitfalls. Rather than advocating a single technique, we emphasize fundamental principles that permit adaptation to patient anatomy while maintaining the geometric integrity of the left ventricular outflow tract, aortic root, and pulmonary root.

title: A feasibility pilot study of a resource-adapted ECMO-based ex vivo heart perfusion platform.
authorString: Sudakevych S, Chaikovska S, Maruniak S, Kovtun G, Hulitskyi B, Kuzmych I, Renna LA, Roberts T, Batchinsky A, Todurov B.
abstractText: BackgroundCold ischemic injury remains a major limitation in heart transplantation, particularly when donor organs must be transported over long distances. Normothermic ex vivo heart perfusion may reduce ischemic damage and enable functional assessment of the organ before implantation; however, the cost, system complexity, and logistical requirements of commercial systems limit broad implementation outside well-resourced transplant programs.MethodsA compact, resource-adapted ex vivo heart perfusion device (Ukrainian patent UA 156631 U) was evaluated during normothermic perfusion of three explanted human hearts at 34°C. Perfusion targets included aortic inflow of 700-800 mL/min, with epinephrine titrated as needed. Arterial perfusate was sampled at baseline and hourly to assess acid-base status, electrolytes, glucose, lactate, hemoglobin, and myocardial injury markers. Heart weight was recorded before and after perfusion, and myocardial tissue underwent semi-quantitative histopathologic evaluation. Given the exploratory design, results were summarized descriptively as individual case values over time.ResultsAcross all three experiments, normothermic ex vivo perfusion was associated with progressive metabolic stabilization. pH increased from baseline acidosis (6.95-7.00) to near-physiologic values by 180 minutes (7.30-7.33). Uncorrected lactate values declined to <5 mmol/L by 180 minutes in all cases, while glucose decreased steadily and electrolytes remained within narrow ranges. Myocardial injury markers increased after reperfusion, with the steepest rise during the first hour, followed by slower increases thereafter. Heart weight increased modestly (3.53%-4.58%), consistent with mild edema, and histopathology showed predominantly mild-to-moderate changes. No air embolism or device-related mechanical complications were observed.ConclusionIn this early three-case feasibility study, a resource-adapted ECMO-based platform successfully maintained aortic inflow and supported ex situ perfusion of explanted human hearts for 4-6 hours, while enabling continuous metabolic assessment. These findings demonstrate the technical feasibility of the platform and support its potential as an accessible alternative for prolonged normothermic heart perfusion in resource-limited settings. Further controlled studies incorporating direct aortic root pressure monitoring, standardized functional assessment, and transplantation endpoints are warranted to validate its performance and clinical applicability.

title: Double-Chambered Left Ventricle Complicated with Thrombosis Presenting with Unilateral Limb Weakness as the Initial Manifestation: A Two-Case Report
authorString: Yuan J, Ma L, Zhang M, Fan B, Zhou N.
abstractText: Double-chambered left ventricle (DCLV) is a rare congenital heart disease. Its clinical manifestations in children are often subtle and may be easily overlooked or misdiagnosed. This case report describes two children with type A DCLV complicated by ventricular thrombosis and cerebral infarction who presented with unilateral limb weakness as the initial symptom. Case 1 involved a 5-year-old boy who developed right-sided limb weakness after convulsions and was subsequently diagnosed with cerebral infarction. The primary disease was DCLV complicated with thrombosis. During the waiting period for the surgery, the right hemiplegia worsened. The emergency cranial CT indicated that the cerebral infarction had worsened with a small amount of bleeding. After the acute phase of intracranial hemorrhage had resolved, surgical correction of the DCLV and thrombus removal were performed. The patient recovered well after the operation. Limb movement returned to normal during nearly 3 years of follow-up. Case 2 involved a 1-year-6-month-old boy who suddenly experienced right-sided limb dysfunction. After examination, it was found that it was a case of DCLV combined with thrombus detachment into the cerebral blood vessels. Emergency cardiac surgery was performed, and limb function partially improved 8 months after the operation. For children presenting with unexplained unilateral limb paralysis and acute cerebral infarction, cardiac screening should not be overlooked. The timing of surgery should be individualized according to the intracranial condition, and combined treatment involving malformation correction, thrombus removal, and postoperative rehabilitation should be implemented to improve long-term outcomes. This study reports only 2 cases, and further large-sample studies are needed to explore the clinical characteristics and long-term prognosis of this disease.

title: Relationships between cardiac magnetic resonance-derived myocardial, hepatic, and splenic extracellular volumes in Fontan patients: A FORCE registry study
authorString: Shade JE, Clair NS, Alsaied T, Dorfman AL, Fogel MA, Ghelani S, Krishnamurthy R, Lam CZ, Lee CK, Muthurangu V, Robinson JD, Slesnick TC, Weigand J, Wu FM, Rathod RH.
abstractText: Background Fontan-associated liver disease (FALD) is common in Fontan patients and traditional serum markers are insensitive for detecting it. Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR)-derived myocardial extracellular volume (ECV) correlates with biomarkers of myocardial fibrosis. Objectives This study investigates the associations between CMR-derived myocardial, hepatic, and splenic ECV as potential non-invasive indicators of FALD. Methods This study was a retrospective analysis of patients with single-ventricle congenital heart disease from the Fontan Outcomes Registry using Clinical Examinations (FORCE), with CMRs between 2014 and 2022 with T1 mapping. Fontan patients were compared to patients with transposition of the great arteries (TGA). Results There were 210 Fontan CMRs and 25 TGA CMRs included. Hepatic ECV (41.7 ± 4.0 vs 32.3 ± 4.6, p < 0.001) was elevated in Fontan vs TGA patients despite no significant differences in myocardial or splenic ECV. There was a moderate correlation between hepatic and splenic ECV in both groups (r = 0.46, p < 0.05). In Fontan patients only, there were modest correlations between myocardial vs hepatic ECV (r = 0.34, p < 0.001) and myocardial vs splenic ECV (r = 0.37, p < 0.001). These relationships persisted in multivariate regressions. Conclusions Fontan patients have elevated hepatic ECV compared to TGA patients. Myocardial ECV is positively correlated with both hepatic and splenic ECV in Fontan patients, but not in TGA patients. This suggests that elevated myocardial ECV— which may be a marker for diastolic dysfunction— might be associated with elevated hepatic and splenic ECV (potential markers of FALD) in Fontan patients.

title: Conceptual and psychometric characteristics of instruments used in adults with CHD quality of life research: a scoping review.
authorString: Latham R, Seaton SE, Smith L, Rowe M, Nyakila C, Lotto R.
abstractText:
Background

Improved survival among people with congenital heart disease (CHD) has increased the emphasis on quality of life as a long-term outcome. However, inconsistent distinctions between quality of life, health-related quality of life, health status and functioning complicate the interpretation of this evidence. Examining the conceptual basis and measurement properties of instruments used in contemporary CHD research is therefore necessary to establish which outcomes are being assessed.

Aim

To identify instruments used in studies reporting quality of life outcomes in adults with moderate or severe CHD, classify their intended constructs and summarise reported evidence of validity, reliability and suitability.

Methods

This scoping review followed Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and PRISMA-ScR reporting guidance. CINAHL, MEDLINE, PsycINFO and Scopus were searched for English-language quantitative and mixed-methods studies published from 2015 in high-income countries. Citation mining identified instrument development and validation literature. Instruments were classified by their primary intended purpose, and reported psychometric evidence and study definitions of quality of life were summarised descriptively.

Results

Sixty-six records published between 2015 and 2026 identified 16 instruments. Five measured overall quality of life, eight assessed health-related quality of life, health status or functioning, and three were disease-specific. Studies using overall quality of life measures more commonly defined the construct, whereas those using short-form health surveys frequently reported quality of life without conceptual clarification. Validation evidence supported some instruments in adult CHD populations, although the suitability of measures developed for paediatric populations remained uncertain.

Conclusion

Contemporary CHD research reports conceptually distinct outcomes under the term quality of life, limiting comparability and interpretation. Explicit definitions and instrument selection informed by the intended construct and population are required to strengthen the assessment of patient-reported outcomes.

title: Maternal obesity and risk of congenital heart disease in offspring: a nationwide population-based study.
authorString: Choi S, Kim TE, Kim YJ, Park S, Chung S, Son JS, Park HW.

journal.title: Journal of developmental origins of health and disease

abstractText: Maternal obesity is a well-established risk factor for adverse pregnancy outcomes, but its association with congenital heart disease (CHD) in offspring remains uncertain, particularly across different body mass index (BMI) categories and CHD subtypes. Evidence from Asian populations is limited, despite distinct BMI distributions and classification criteria. We conducted a nationwide retrospective cohort study using the Korean National Health Information Database, including 779,091 live births from 2014 to 2021. Maternal pre-pregnancy BMI was classified according to Asia-Pacific criteria. Offspring CHD was identified using ICD-10 codes Q20-Q26. Subtype analyses were performed for ventricular septal defect (VSD), atrial septal defect (ASD), pulmonary valve stenosis, and other major CHD subtypes. Inverse probability of treatment weighting was applied to balance covariates across BMI categories, and robust Poisson regression was used to estimate RRs and 95% CIs. Compared with the normal BMI group (18.5-22.9 kg/m<sup>2</sup>), adjusted RRs for CHD were 1.08 (95% CI 1.06-1.10) for overweight at risk (23.0-24.9 kg/m<sup>2</sup>), 1.13 (95% CI 1.11-1.15) for obese class I (25.0-29.9 kg/m<sup>2</sup>), and 1.37 (95% CI 1.35-1.40) for obese class II (≥30.0 kg/m<sup>2</sup>). Maternal underweight (<18.5 kg/m<sup>2</sup>) was not significantly associated with CHD risk (RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.97-1.00). Maternal obesity was associated with a dose-dependent increase in overall CHD risk, while subtype associations were not significant after adjustment. These findings support public health strategies emphasizing weight management before conception to reduce the burden of congenital heart anomalies.

title: CTA-Guided Anatomical Targeting for Bachmann's Bundle Pacing: First-in-Human Study.
authorString: Cano Ó, Tretter JT, Rad G, Ugarteburu M, Asyraf T, Spaziani S, Zaretsky L, Osca J, Maceira AM, Ben-Haim S.
abstractText:
Background

Bachmann's bundle pacing (BBP) is an emerging physiological atrial pacing strategy, but implantation relies on fluoroscopic landmarks and iterative electrophysiological mapping. Whether patient-specific computed tomography angiography (CTA) can facilitate anatomical targeting of Bachmann's bundle has not been investigated.

Objective

To evaluate the feasibility, safety, procedural performance, and anatomical impact of CTA-guided anatomical targeting for BBP.

Methods

This retrospective, single-center, first-in-human study compared 49 consecutive patients undergoing CTA-guided BBP with 28 undergoing conventional electrogram- and fluoroscopy-guided implantation.

Results

Using predefined electrocardiographic criteria, successful BBP was achieved in 65 of 77 patients (84%) and was higher with CTA guidance (92% vs. 71%; P=0.024). CTA-guided implantation resulted in a different distribution of final lead positions, with more leads at the predefined B2-B3 target than with the conventional approach (76% vs. 42%; P=0.006; odds ratio 4.20; 95% CI, 1.52-11.60). CTA guidance reduced implantation time (median 2.0 [1.0-3.0] vs. 4.0 [3.0-7.0] minutes; P<0.001), fluoroscopy time (0.4 [0.2-0.6] vs. 1.6 [1.1-2.9] minutes; P<0.001), and lead deployment attempts (1.0 [1.0-2.0] vs. 2.0 [1.8-3.2]; P=0.001), and increased first-pass success (67% vs. 25%; P<0.001). In patients with successful BBP (n=65), BBP shortened P-wave duration in all cases (161±13 to 142±15 ms; relative reduction 11.6±4.4%; P<0.001), with similar reductions irrespective of implantation strategy. No acute lead-related complications occurred, and electrical performance remained stable during short-term follow-up.

Conclusions

CTA-guided anatomical targeting for BBP is feasible and safe. Compared with conventional implantation, this anatomy-first strategy improves procedural efficiency, supporting anatomical guidance as a feasible approach to physiological atrial pacing.

title: Clopidogrel-Based Versus Aspirin-Based Double Antithrombotic Therapy After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in Atrial Fibrillation Patients: Results of the ASAF-PCI Registry.
authorString: Panevino R, Pompei G, Fabbri E, Sanna S, Casu G, Ottani F, Pizzi C, Tarantino F, Santarelli A, Grilli R, Diemberger I, Rubboli A.

journal.title: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions

abstractText:
Background

In patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), current guidelines recommend a brief period of triple antithrombotic therapy (TAT) consisting of an oral anticoagulant (OAC), aspirin and clopidogrel, followed by double antithrombotic therapy (DAT) with OAC plus clopidogrel. Evidence on aspirin as an alternative to clopidogrel within DAT remains limited.

Aims

The present analysis aimed at describing contemporary use of aspirin- versus clopidogrel-based DAT and to compare 12-month clinical outcomes.

Methods

In this multicenter, observational study, consecutive patients with AF undergoing PCI between January 2019 and December 2023 and discharged on DAT with OAC plus aspirin or clopidogrel were included. The primary endpoint was the 12-month incidence of net adverse clinical events (NACE), composite of all-cause death, non-fatal myocardial infarction (MI), non-fatal stroke, urgent revascularization, and major bleeding. Secondary composite and individual endpoints were also assessed. Multivariable logistic regression was used to adjust for baseline imbalances.

Results

Among 445 patients, 291 (65.4%) were discharged on clopidogrel-based DAT and 154 (34.6%) on aspirin-based DAT. Baseline characteristics were largely comparable. NACE occurred in 15.1% versus 13.6% of patients (OR 1.13, 95% CI 0.64-1.98; p = 0.674), with no significant difference after multivariable adjustment (adjusted OR 1.15, 95% CI 0.59-2.26; p = 0.677). No significant between group differences were observed for secondary composite or individual efficacy and safety endpoints.

Conclusions

In this real-world cohort of AF patients undergoing PCI, aspirin- and clopidogrel-based DAT with OAC were not associated with significantly different 12-month outcomes. These hypothesis-generating findings require confirmation in adequately powered randomized trials.

title: Apixaban reduces hepatic decompensation in patients with cirrhosis (ApiHep): A randomized controlled trial.
authorString: Agarwal A, Biswas S, Aggarwal A, Saxena S, Dass J, Lewis MG, Kumar S, Jain S, Swaroop S, Chauhan VS, Agarwal A, Aggarwal M, Mishra AK, Goyal A, Gamanagatti S, Sharma R, Sardana V, Agarwal S, Yadav A, Mahapatra SJ, Gunjan D, Nayak B, Shalimar.
abstractText:
Background

Evolving data suggest that anticoagulation is safe in cirrhosis and may improve decompensation-free survival in select patients. This study aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of the direct oral anticoagulant apixaban in patients with cirrhosis.

Methods

In this open-label randomized controlled trial with blinded endpoint assessment, adult patients (18-60y) with cirrhosis (Child-Pugh B7-C10) without splenoportal axis thrombosis were randomized (1:1) to receive apixaban (2.5 mg twice daily) along with standard medical therapy (SMT) or SMT alone for 12 months. The primary outcome was the comparison of the proportion of patients with hepatic decompensation at 1 year. Secondary outcomes included frequency of liver-related events, overall and liver-related mortality, and adverse events (AEs).

Results

One hundred thirty-four patients (mean age 43.4±9.5 y; Child-Pugh B/C:115/19) were randomized (67 Apixaban+SMT and 67 SMT). Patients receiving apixaban experienced significantly lower rates of hepatic decompensation compared with SMT (33.1% vs. 54.3%; absolute risk reduction 21.2% [95% CI: 4.5%-38.2%]; p=0.013). Although rates of ascites (6.4% vs. 17.4%), HE (21.2% vs. 36.0%), and variceal bleeding (7.5% vs. 14.6%) were lower among patients receiving Apixaban+SMT as compared with SMT alone, the differences were not statistically significant. No significant between-group differences in all-cause and liver-related mortality at 1 year were noted. There were no significant between-group differences in AEs (55.2% vs. 53.7%), any bleeding (41.8% vs. 46.3%), and major bleeding (9.0% vs. 11.9%) events.

Conclusions

Apixaban significantly reduced hepatic decompensation events without increasing hemorrhagic episodes in Child-Pugh B7-C10 cirrhosis (CTRI/2023/09/058018).

title: Testosterone Therapy and Sexual Health in Men and Women: Is There a Role for Long-Acting Subcutaneous Pellets?
authorString: Rojas-Zambrano JG, Molina-Varas EA, Rojas-Zambrano A.
abstractText: Testosterone influences sexual desire and sexual response in men and women, but the clinical reasons for prescribing it differ between the sexes. In men, treatment is reserved for symptomatic hypogonadism confirmed by repeated morning measurements, and placebo-controlled trials show improvements in libido and sexual activity, with smaller and less consistent effects on erectile function. In women, the indication with the strongest support is hypoactive sexual desire disorder after menopause, where randomized trials of transdermal testosterone show moderate gains in desire, arousal, orgasm, and satisfaction, along with less sexual distress. Subcutaneous testosterone pellets release the hormone for several months after a single office procedure and appeal to patients who prefer infrequent dosing. Most of the evidence for testosterone therapy, however, comes from transdermal and injectable preparations. Pellet studies in men describe steady release, a predictable duration of action, extrusion as the most frequent complication, and erythrocytosis that cannot be corrected by lowering the dose once the pellets are in place. The few randomized comparisons of pellets with other formulations were small, did not include transdermal testosterone, and were not designed around validated sexual-function outcomes. In women, pellets are used off-label, are often compounded, and can produce serum concentrations well above the female physiological range; current professional guidance advises against their use for hypoactive sexual desire disorder. This narrative review describes the physiology of testosterone in both sexes, the diagnostic criteria and validated instruments used to assess sexual function, the trial evidence for testosterone therapy, and the pharmacology, effectiveness, and safety of pellets. Pellets are a reasonable option for selected hypogonadal men who do not seek fertility, accept a formulation that cannot be quickly reversed, and agree to hematocrit monitoring. In women, current guidance does not support their use, and any exception requires informed consent, close monitoring, and acknowledgment that it departs from that guidance.

title: Comparing the effects of biological nurturing versus the WHO/UNICEF 20-hours course method on early breastfeeding problems: A cross-sectional study.
authorString: Grandinetti A, Buchini S, Concina F, Knowles A, Travan L, Milinco M, Ronfani L.
abstractText:
Introduction

Biological nurturing (BN) is a neurobehavioral approach to breastfeeding that promotes a comfortable, laidback maternal position to facilitate effective attach and reduce breast problems. Although BN has shown to be effective in a variety of settings, its implementation in hospital context has not been thoroughly evaluated. The aim of this observational study was to evaluate the effectiveness of BN, compared to the WHO/UNICEF 20-h course method, on the occurrence of breast problems and the prevalence of exclusive breastfeeding during hospital stay and the 24 hours before discharge, and to compare these results with those obtained from a randomized controlled trial (RCT) conducted in the same hospital in 2018.

Methods

A cross-sectional study was conducted at IRCCS Burlo Garofolo Pediatric Hospital (Trieste, Italy) between June and September 2022. Ninety women who gave birth at the hospital and were breastfeeding during hospital stay after delivery were enrolled in the study and asked to complete a questionnaire. The primary study outcome was the frequency of women who were breastfeeding according to the BN approach (BN group) or according to the WHO/UNICEF 20-h course method (WHO/UNICEF group) during hospital stay, and to compare the prevalence of breast problems between the two groups.

Results

Sixty-five out of 90 women (72.2%) breastfed according to the BN approach and 25 (27.8%) to the WHO/UNICEF 20-h course method. During hospital stay, 55.4% of women (n = 36) experienced breast problems in the BN group and 76.0% (n = 19) in the WHO/UNICEF group. The prevalence of exclusive breastfeeding was significantly higher in the BN group than in the WHO/UNICEF group during hospital stay (86.2% vs. 64.0%; p = 0.02) and in the 24 hours prior to hospital discharge (81.5% vs. 56.0%; p = 0.01).

Conclusions

The BN approach applied in the real-life situation of a paediatric hospital was effective in preventing breast problems and increasing exclusive breastfeeding rates.

title: Lipid-Lowering Strategies in the Era of Early Atherosclerosis Detection: 2026 ACC Scientific Statement: A Report of the American College of Cardiology.
authorString: Greenland P, Badimon L, Bittner V, Bonaca MP, Hlatky MA, Lau ES, Mehta LS.

journal.title: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

abstractText: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) begins early in life, driven in large part by cumulative exposure to low-density lipoprotein cholesterol and other atherogenic lipoproteins. Contemporary evidence from epidemiologic cohorts, genetic studies, imaging studies, and lipid-lowering trials supports a paradigm of earlier identification and more sustained treatment of individuals at increased ASCVD risk. This American College of Cardiology Scientific Statement reviews the rationale for early adoption of lipid-lowering strategies, with emphasis on lifetime lipid burden, inherited and acquired risk enhancers, and the role of subclinical atherosclerosis assessment. Available clinical trial data suggest that greater absolute low-density lipoprotein cholesterol reduction and longer treatment duration can reduce ASCVD events, even though direct evidence remains limited in younger populations at low short-term risk. Atherosclerosis detected by imaging may identify individuals whose ASCVD risk is underestimated by traditional calculators, but optimal strategies for screening, treatment thresholds, safety, adherence, cost-effectiveness, and value require further study. Clinicians should integrate estimated short- and long-term risk, lipid burden, risk enhancers, imaging findings when appropriate, and patient preferences to guide individualized, shared decision making to reduce lifetime ASCVD risk.

title: Takotsubo Syndrome in Acute and Chronic Neurological Conditions: A Systematic Review of Cardiac Phenotypes and Clinical Outcomes.
authorString: Jangirashvili T, Parthiv O, Kurtsikidze S, Srinivas S, Oboladze M, Yassine M, Maghradze N, Khaburdzania B, Ali MMAMY.
abstractText: Takotsubo syndrome (TTS) is an acute, usually reversible form of left ventricular dysfunction that mimics acute coronary syndrome and carries a long-term prognosis comparable to that of myocardial infarction. Its pathogenesis has been linked to the brain-heart axis, and TTS has been described after acute neurological events and in patients with chronic neurological disease. However, the evidence remains fragmented across individual conditions, and acute triggers are rarely distinguished from pre-existing disorders. The objective here is to systematically review primary observational evidence on TTS in adults with acute and chronic neurological conditions, with emphasis on the temporal relationship, cardiac phenotypes, complications, and clinical outcomes, and to summarize the mechanistic evidence reported by the included studies. A systematic literature search was conducted across PubMed/MEDLINE, ScienceDirect, Google Scholar, and ResearchGate (January 2016 to September 2026) in accordance with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines, supplemented by citation searching. Eligibility criteria, data extraction, and quality appraisal with the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale were predefined. Of 3170 records, 16 primary observational studies were included: five multicenter registry analyses, four administrative database analyses, five cohort studies, one case-control study, and one cross-sectional study. Reviews and case reports provided context only, and reports from overlapping data sources were not pooled. In the International Takotsubo Registry, an acute neurological disorder preceded TTS in 6.7% of 2402 patients, most often seizures, intracranial hemorrhage, or cerebral ischemia, and TTS was diagnosed within two days of neurological symptoms in 87.3%. In the German-Italian-Spanish Takotsubo Registry, 17% of 2301 patients had a neurological disorder, mostly pre-existing. Neurologically associated TTS showed lower left ventricular ejection fraction (37.4% vs 41.0%), more cardiogenic shock (15.1% vs 8.6%), and higher in-hospital mortality (17.4% vs 4.0%; adjusted odds ratio 3.20), which reached 30.4% after intracranial hemorrhage. A neurological disorder independently predicted long-term mortality (hazard ratio 1.72). Migraine was associated with lower adjusted mortality, whereas amyotrophic lateral sclerosis was associated with a more severe in-hospital course. Ballooning patterns differed only modestly, and chest pain was reported in 29.0% of neurologically associated cases compared with 72.9% of other cases. Evidence for traumatic brain injury was limited to one strain-defined cohort and coded trauma data, and direct mechanistic measurements were scarce. Neurological disease identifies a higher-risk subgroup of patients with TTS who often present without chest pain. TTS should be considered in patients with acute neurological events who develop unexplained hemodynamic instability, electrocardiographic changes, or troponin elevation, and echocardiography should anticipate more severe systolic dysfunction. The evidence base is small, partly overlapping, and diagnostically heterogeneous, and outcomes were reported as all-cause. Prospective studies with standardized diagnostic criteria and separate reporting of cardiac and neurological outcomes are needed.

title: Risk factors for venous thromboembolism in adults with sepsis: Protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authorString: Ji H, Lin Z, Liang Z, Shao F.
abstractText:
Introduction

Adults with sepsis are at increased risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE), encompassing deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE), because of sepsis-related inflammation, endothelial injury, coagulation activation and treatment-related exposures. Although several potential risk factors have been reported, the evidence remains fragmented and findings are inconsistent across populations, VTE subtypes and diagnostic approaches. This protocol aims to prespecify transparent and reproducible methods for a systematic review and meta-analysis of factors associated with incident VTE in adults with sepsis.

Methods and analysis

Prospective and retrospective cohort studies and case-control studies involving adults with sepsis or septic shock will be included. Studies evaluating potential risk factors for incident VTE after sepsis onset or diagnosis will be eligible. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, CINAHL and the Cochrane Library will be searched from inception to the final search date, supplemented by grey-literature searching and citation screening. Two reviewers will independently perform study selection, data extraction and risk-of-bias assessment. Where sufficient comparable data are available, random-effects meta-analysis will be conducted, with adjusted estimates prioritised. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses will be performed to explore heterogeneity, and certainty of evidence will be assessed using the GRADE approach adapted for prognostic-factor evidence.

Prospero registration number

CRD420261465429.

title: Prevalence and Mental and Physical Health Correlates of Cardiovascular Disease Among Older US Veterans: Results From the 2025-2026 National Health and Resilience in Veterans Study.
authorString: Yang A, Manaswi A, Fischer MW, Fischer IC, Na PJ, Ripp JA, Pietrzak RH.

journal.title: The primary care companion for CNS disorders

abstractText: Objective: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of morbidity and mortality in the United States, and older military veterans are at particularly high risk. This study aims to determine the prevalence and temporal stability of CVD in a nationally representative sample of older US veterans and identify correlates of CVD and related multimorbidity. Methods: Data were analyzed from 1,944 veterans aged ≥60 years from the 2025-2026 National Health and Resilience in Veterans Study (NHRVS). Weighted z-tests, multivariable logistic regression, and Bonferroni-corrected comparisons assessed CVD prevalence trends relative to the 2019-2020 NHRVS and identified correlates. Results: Overall CVD prevalence was 25.7% (n = 486), unchanged from the 2019-2020 NHRVS (25.2%; P= .69), as were rates of heart disease (19.0% vs 19.2%) and myocardial infarction (8.3% vs 10.1%). Stroke/TIA prevalence was higher in 2025-2026 (6.3% vs 4.5%; P= .005), though comparability was limited by the addition of TIA in the later wave. CVD was associated with significantly higher odds of major depression (odds ratio [OR]= 1.88), gambling disorder (OR = 1.69), sleep disorder (OR = 1.90), and insomnia (OR=1.68) but lower odds of lifetime suicide attempt (OR = 0.31), alongside higher odds of respiratory disease (OR = 1.98), kidney disease (OR = 1.85), and chronic pain (OR = 1.65). Independent correlates included older age (OR = 1.06), male sex (OR = 2.17), hypertension (OR = 1.48), hypercholesterolemia (OR = 1.66), diabetes (OR = 1.98), and cumulative trauma burden (OR = 1.10). Prim Care Companion CNS Disord2026;28(6):26m04309. Author affiliations are listed at the end of this article.

title: Integrative 3D imaging and deep learning approach reveals cardiac fibroblast dynamics after myocardial infarction.
authorString: Barrado-Ballestero S, López-Moreno M, Cobos-Figueroa J, Hahn M, Pogontke-Díaz C, Biering-Sørensen T, Salinas CG, Guadix JA, Perez-Pomares JM, Ruiz-Villalba A, Roostalu U.
abstractText: Cardiac fibroblasts (CFs) are key mediators of heart failure progression, driving fibrotic scar formation after myocardial infarction (MI). Conventional preclinical assessment of MI relies on two-dimensional histology, which cannot resolve the three-dimensional (3D) architecture of the injured heart. Understanding the molecular mechanisms of CF activation is critical for identifying new drug targets, yet spatial mapping of gene expression in intact hearts remains challenging. To address this, we developed a high-throughput imaging pipeline that combined single-cell-resolution gene expression profiling in cleared whole hearts with light-sheet fluorescence microscopy and an AI-driven analysis framework optimized for MI characterization. Using this approach, we mapped expression of periostin (Postn), collagen triple-helix repeat containing 1 (Cthrc1), and asporin (Aspn) - genes associated with CF activation. These markers were detected by day 3 post-infarction in the endocardium and border zone, preceding collagenous scar formation, then expanded across the infarcted myocardium before declining toward baseline during scar maturation. These findings revealed a spatially organized progression of fibrosis-associated gene expression that began in defined regions of the injured heart and subsequently extended throughout the infarcted myocardium. Whole-organ gene-expression imaging combined with deep-learning-based analysis enabled quantitative spatiotemporal mapping of molecular remodeling and provides a framework for investigating disease progression in intact organs.

title: Shared genetic architecture between digestive infectious diseases and cardiovascular diseases: a genome-wide cross-trait analysis
authorString: Ni J, Pan J, Chen Y.
abstractText:
Background:

Digestive infectious diseases and cardiovascular diseases may share common genetic, inflammatory and immune-related mechanisms. However, the shared genetic architecture between these disease groups, the specific pleiotropic loci involved and the potential contribution of intestinal infectious diseases (IID) to cardiovascular risk remain incompletely understood. Methods We analysed publicly available genome-wide association study summary statistics for 36 binary traits of European ancestry, including 16 digestive infectious disease traits and 20 cardiovascular traits. Univariate linkage disequilibrium score regression was used to estimate SNP-based heritability and prioritise traits. Global and local genetic sharing were evaluated using cross-trait LDSC and SUPERGNOVA. Multi-trait analysis of GWAS, cross-trait sensitivity analyses, FM-summary fine-mapping and Bayesian colocalisation were used to identify and refine pleiotropic loci. Candidate genes and biological functions were investigated using MAGMA, tissue- and cell-type-specific enrichment analyses, transcriptome-wide association analysis and protein-wide association analysis. Bidirectional two-sample Mendelian randomisation and two-step mediation analyses using three independent gut microbiome GWAS resources were subsequently performed. Results Sixteen traits passed heritability quality control, yielding 39 trait pairs with significant global genetic correlations after Bonferroni correction. MTAG identified 41 candidate SNP records and 14 trait-pair-specific lead-SNP records representing eight unique SNPs; 39 candidate records and 12 lead records involved IID. Fine-mapping and colocalisation prioritised eight records representing four unique variants. Locus-based gene prioritisation retained 24 candidate genes across four pairs. Gene-set enrichment identified 43 significant trait-pair-GO term associations, and tissue enrichment identified seven significant associations. Transcriptome-wide analyses implicated 21 candidate genes, and proteome-wide analyses identified four associations involving three proteins. After false discovery rate (FDR) correction, forward MR supported associations of IID liability with cardiac arrhythmias, myocardial infarction, atrial fibrillation and flutter, and ischaemic heart disease; reverse MR supported only cardiac arrhythmias to IID. Five positive exploratory microbiota-IID-cardiovascular mediation patterns were described. Only the Oxalobacter-IID-cardiac arrhythmias indirect effect reached unadjusted P < 0.05. Conclusions Digestive infectious diseases, particularly IID, share substantial genetic architecture with cardiovascular diseases. Integrative genetic analyses identified recurrent pleiotropic loci, candidate genes and putative microbiome-mediated pathways linking IID with cardiovascular outcomes. These findings provide testable hypotheses for further functional validation and clinical investigation.

title: Kidney Function Variability and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Heart Failure: Effects of Empagliflozin in the EMPEROR-Reduced Trial
authorString: Kunitake M, Higuchi K, Sakai Y, Fukumoto Y.
abstractText:
Background:

Although sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors improve cardiovascular and kidney outcomes in patients with heart failure (HF), the prognostic significance of intraindividual kidney function variability and its modification by SGLT2 inhibition remain unclear. We investigated these relationships in patients with HF with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF).

Methods:

This secondary analysis included 3,492 patients from the EMPEROR-Reduced trial. A location-scale joint model (LSJM) simultaneously evaluated the associations of estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) levels, longitudinal slopes, and intraindividual variability from day 28 onward with the composite outcome of cardiovascular death or HF hospitalization. Patients were stratified into tertiles of estimated eGFR variability using common cutoffs across the empagliflozin and placebo groups, allowing comparisons of cardiovascular outcomes at comparable variability levels.

Results:

Greater intraindividual eGFR variability was independently associated with increased cardiovascular risk (hazard ratio: 1.08 per 1 mL/min/1.73 m2 increase in estimated standard deviation; P < 0.001). The model incorporating eGFR levels, slopes, and variability demonstrated the best fit. Empagliflozin significantly reduced eGFR variability compared with placebo (standard deviation ratio: 0.93; P = 0.005) and attenuated annual eGFR decline by 1.83 mL/min/1.73 m2/year, despite an initial eGFR reduction of approximately 2.5 mL/min/1.73 m2. Event-free survival progressively decreased with increasing eGFR variability in both treatment groups. Importantly, within each variability tertile defined by common cutoffs, empagliflozin-treated patients consistently exhibited higher event-free survival than placebo-treated patients.

Conclusion:

In patients with HFrEF, greater intraindividual eGFR variability was independently associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes, beyond eGFR levels and slopes. Empagliflozin reduced kidney function variability and attenuated long-term eGFR decline, with more favorable cardiovascular outcomes observed even among patients with comparable levels of kidney function variability.

title: Three Simultaneous Cardioembolic Sources in Ischemic Stroke.
authorString: Velásquez-Trujillo LA, Bucheli-Enríquez VR, Ayala-Zapata S, Barbosa-Balaguera S, Dussan-Delgado MJ, Herrera Escandón Á, Kuratomi-Nakamura K.
abstractText:
Background

The simultaneous convergence of 3 independent cardioembolic sources in a single patient is exceptional.

Case summary

A 77-year-old man presented with an extensive left middle cerebral artery ischemic stroke. Transesophageal echocardiography revealed a 30- × 30-mm left atrial myxoma and a 10- × 16-mm anterior mitral leaflet vegetation with perforation and severe regurgitation; monitoring documented new-onset atrial fibrillation. Despite negative blood cultures, infective endocarditis was diagnosed by the 2023 Duke-ISCVID criteria. He underwent myxoma resection, mitral valve replacement, and splenectomy; histopathology showed acid-fast bacilli in the myxoma and valve, with Mycobacterium tuberculosis confirmed on serum polymerase chain reaction. He died postoperatively from refractory multiorgan failure.

Discussion

These 3 coexisting sources, the myxoma, a tuberculous mitral vegetation, and new-onset atrial fibrillation, constitute the "three-headed monster."

Take-home message

Transesophageal echocardiography and specimen histopathology are decisive when multiple cardioembolic sources coexist, and tuberculosis should be considered in culture-negative endocarditis.

title: Excimer Laser Coronary Angioplasty for Entrapped Guidewire Retrieval During Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.
authorString: Ren J, Kang H, Liu Z, Wang B.
abstractText:
Background

Guidewire entrapment is a rare (0.2%-0.8%) but serious complication of percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), typically occurring in heavily calcified lesions, chronic total occlusions, or during bifurcation stenting. When conventional retrieval fails, surgical removal carries high morbidity.

Case summary

A 60-year-old man with 3-vessel coronary disease, prior inferior wall myocardial infarction, hypertension, and diabetes underwent staged PCI. A workhorse guidewire became entrapped in the distal left circumflex artery. Conventional retrieval attempts using multiple guidewires, microcatheters, and low-profile balloons failed. Excimer laser coronary angioplasty (ELCA) successfully freed the wire. Postprocedure angiography revealed TIMI flow grade 3 with localized dissection hematoma.

Discussion

To our knowledge, this is the first report of successful ELCA-assisted retrieval of an entrapped workhorse guidewire in a nonchronic total occlusion lesion after conventional techniques failed. ELCA offers a safe, surgery-sparing bailout option by ablating surrounding fibrocalcific tissue or polymer coating.

Take-home message

For entrapped guidewires refractory to conventional PCI retrieval, ELCA offers a safe, surgery-sparing alternative by ablating adjacent tissue or polymer coating, and early use prevents wire fracture, perforation, and emergent bypass grafting.

title: Epidemiology of Complications After 1434 Foot and Ankle Surgeries at a Large Medical Center Performed Without Tourniquet.
authorString: Durudogan EH, Bergman R, May JM, Kadakia AR.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: J Am Acad Orthop Surg Glob Res Rev
journal.title: Journal of the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons. Global research & reviews
journal.isoabbreviation: J Am Acad Orthop Surg Glob Res Rev

abstractText:
Introduction

Tourniquet use in foot and ankle surgery is common, but controversial because of associated ischemia-related tissue injury and thrombotic risk. It is unclear whether the benefits of tourniquet use outweigh its risks. There is a paucity of literature evaluating the complication profile of tourniquet-free procedures. The aim of this study was to characterize complication rates and evaluate the safety of tourniquet-free foot and ankle surgery.

Methods

A retrospective review of tourniquet-free foot and ankle procedures performed by a single fellowship-trained surgeon at a tertiary academic medical center from January 2018 to December 2022 was conducted. Demographics, comorbidities, and procedure types were recorded. Complications included superficial infection, deep infection, noninfectious revision surgery, and venous thromboembolism (VTE) within 90 days. Associations between patient factors and complications were analyzed using chi-square testing.

Results

A total of 1434 tourniquet-free procedures were performed in 1165 patients (mean age 48.9 ± 16.4 years; mean body mass index [BMI] 29.6 ± 7.2 kg/m2). Superficial infection occurred in 2.7%, deep infection in 0.98%, and noninfectious revision surgery in 0.98% of procedures. The rate of VTE was 1.6% (0.4% pulmonary embolism, 1.3% deep vein thrombosis). Diabetes, age, BMI, sex, procedure type, and opioid use were not associated with complications. Chronic pulmonary disease and hemiplegia/paraplegia were linked to higher deep infection rates. Revision surgeries were more frequent among patients with congestive heart failure, peripheral vascular disease, pulmonary disease, renal disease, and mild liver disease. VTE risk was elevated among tobacco users, Hispanic patients, and those with a history of myocardial infarction, renal disease, or mild liver disease.

Conclusion

Tourniquet-free foot and ankle surgery demonstrated rates of infection, revision surgery, and VTE comparable to those reported for procedures performed with a tourniquet. Medical comorbidities and tobacco use were risk factors, whereas age, BMI, sex, diabetes, procedure type, and opioid use were not. These findings support the safety of a tourniquet-free approach and aid perioperative risk assessment and patient counseling.

title: Clinically Suspected Fulminant Myocarditis Following PCR-Confirmed Pertussis in an Infant: A Case Report.
authorString: Isaa J, Fasfoos A, Hmidat F, Hroub N, Hosheya M, Qutaina T.
abstractText: Cardiac involvement following pertussis infection is uncommon but may be associated with severe clinical deterioration in infants. We report the case of a 3-month-old girl who developed shock, ventricular arrhythmias, and severe biventricular systolic dysfunction approximately 2 weeks after PCR-confirmed Bordetella pertussis infection. Echocardiography demonstrated marked left ventricular dilatation, global hypokinesia, and a left ventricular ejection fraction of 28%. Troponin I was markedly elevated. The clinical presentation was consistent with suspected fulminant myocarditis, although definitive myocardial confirmation was unavailable. The infant received intensive supportive care, inotropic treatment, heart failure medications, antiarrhythmic therapy, and intravenous immunoglobulin, with subsequent clinical and echocardiographic improvement. She was discharged in a stable condition but died unexpectedly approximately 2 months later. The immediate cause of death remained undetermined. This case emphasizes the importance of early cardiac assessment and structured post-discharge surveillance in infants with severe cardiac dysfunction following pertussis infection.

title: Long-term complication profiles following transsphenoidal and transcranial resection of adult craniopharyngioma: A retrospective cohort study.
authorString: Zeng WL, Singla A, Cote DJ, Daggupati S, Dallas J, Briggs RG, Zada G.
abstractText:
Introduction

Craniopharyngiomas arise in the sellar/suprasellar region and are managed with maximal safe resection via transsphenoidal (TSR) or transcranial (TCR) approaches. The optimal approach remains contested, as treatment must balance tumor control against long-term visual, endocrine, neurologic, and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) leak-related morbidity. Longitudinal complication and morbidity profiles of craniopharyngioma resection in adults remain limited. We evaluated approach-specific long-term outcomes in a large multi-institutional adult cohort.

Methods

In a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX network, adult craniopharyngioma patients undergoing TSR or TCR were compared using unmatched analyses and propensity score matching (PSM). Matching characteristics included demographics, comorbidities, presenting features, and prior radiation. Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HR) at 1, 5, 10, and 15 years from surgery.

Results

We identified 2,558 (41.0%) patients who underwent TSR and 1,452 (23.3%) who underwent TCR. Patients selected for TCR had more preoperative hydrocephalus and diabetes insipidus (DI), whereas TSR patients had more hypopituitarism. After PSM (1,199 pairs), TSR carried higher early CSF-leak risk (1-year HR:1.65, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.25-2.19, p < 0.001) but lower rates of 1-year mortality (HR:0.54, 95%CI:0.33-0.91, p = 0.02), hydrocephalus (HR:0.35, 95%CI:0.18-0.71, p = 0.002), blindness (HR:0.54, 95%CI:0.33-0.86, p = 0.009), and adjuvant radiation (HR:0.70, 95%CI:0.52-0.94, p = 0.02). At 10 years, TSR was associated with lower hydrocephalus (HR:0.57, 95%CI:0.35-0.93, p = 0.02), DI (HR:0.69, 95%CI:0.52-0.91, p = 0.01), and blindness (HR:0.61, 95%CI:0.43-0.86, p = 0.01), but higher hypopituitarism (HR:1.24, 95%CI:1.06-1.46, p = 0.01), higher composite endocrine morbidity (HR:1.23, 95%CI:1.03-1.46, p = 0.02), and persistently elevated CSF leak (HR:1.32, 95%CI:1.02-1.72, p = 0.04). Findings at 5 and 15 years were concordant.

Conclusions

Adults with craniopharyngioma experience substantial long-term visual, endocrine, hydrocephalus-related, and treatment-related morbidity. TSR and TCR were associated with distinct long-term complication profiles, with TSR generally associated with lower rates of hydrocephalus, blindness, epilepsy, and DI but higher rates of CSF leak and hypopituitarism. These findings provide long-term population-level estimates that may inform surgical counseling and postoperative surveillance.

title: An association between chronic pulmonary disease and the occurrence of chronic liver disease among middle-aged and older adults in China: Evidence from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study.
authorString: Kong L, Jiang S, Shi L, Zhao H, Yu Y.
abstractText:
Background

The significant morbidity and mortality associated with chronic liver disease (CLD) have been a longstanding concern. While it has been demonstrated that chronic pulmonary disease (CPD) may contributes to impaired liver function, the precise correlation between CPD and CLD remains ambiguous. The objective of this study is to investigate the potential association between CLD and CPD.

Methods

This was a cross-sectional secondary analysis based on the 2018 wave of the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS). Chinese middle-aged and older adults aged ≥ 45 years; participants with key variable missing values were excluded, and a total of 9 126 subjects were finally enrolled (239 with CLD, 8 887 without CLD). Exposure was physician-diagnosed CPD; participants without CLD served as the comparison group, and the primary outcome was physician-diagnosed CLD. Weighted chi-square tests were used for baseline comparison. Three multivariable logistic regression models were built to evaluate the association between CPD and CLD. Smoothed curve fitting, and risk-stratified analysis were further performed to verify the robustness of results.

Results

Based on the 9,126 subjects, the prevalence of CLD was 2.62% (95%CI: 2.31-2.97), and the prevalence of CPD was 4.45% (95%CI: 4.04-4.90). In unadjusted model, CPD was associated with higher odds of CLD, crude OR = 3.38 (95%CI: 2.25-4.93, p < 0.001). After full adjustment for multiple confounding covariates, CPD remained an independent risk factor for CLD (OR = 2.03, 95%CI: 1.32-3.04, p < 0.001). The smoothed curve showed a positive correlation between CPD status and CLD risk. Stratified analysis confirmed the stability of this association across different subgroups.

Conclusions

A strong link was found to exist between CPD and CLD, providing a new perspective on the prevention and treatment of CLD.

title: Bevacizumab and thrombosis risk in cancer patients with COVID-19: A national retrospective cohort study (TIC-TAC).
authorString: Migeon A, Laurent E, Chautard R, Desmars H, Vigny P, Lecuyer AI, Grammatico-Guillon L, Lecomte T.
abstractText:
Background

Cancer patients treated with bevacizumab are at increased risk of thromboembolic events. COVID-19 is also associated with thromboembolism, but its impact on thromboembolic risk in cancer patients receiving bevacizumab remains unclear. The TIC-TAC study aimed to assess whether COVID-19 diagnosis is associated with an increased risk of venous thromboembolic events (VTE) within 30 days or arterial (ATE) thromboembolic events within 90 days in this population.

Methods

A retrospective nationwide cohort study was conducted using the French national health data system. Cancer patients treated with bevacizumab between January 2019 and December 2021 were included. Bevacizumab exposures were used as statistical unit, and defined to 5 half-lives (100 days) after its administration. COVID-19 diagnosis was defined by ICD-10 codes or positive virological tests. The primary outcome was the occurrence of VTE or ATE during hospitalization. Cox models with time-dependent exposure and Fine and Gray competing-risk models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HR) and subdistribution hazard ratios (SHR), with death considered as a competing risk.

Results

Among 58,855 patients (median age 67 years, 79.9% with metastatic disease), 5,589 VTE and 1,926 ATE were recorded over 46,750 and 46,915 person-years, respectively. COVID-19 diagnosis was associated with a higher risk of VTE within 30 days after diagnosis in crude (HR 1.89, 95% CI 1.55-2.29) and adjusted Cox models (aHR 1.99 [1.64-2.43]), as well as in the Fine and Gray model (aSHR 1.70 [1.40-2.07]). However, the unadjusted absolute risk increase was modest: one additional VTE per 64.6 person-months of COVID-19 exposure. A significant interaction between COVID-19 diagnosis and anticoagulant therapy was observed in the VTE Cox model (p = 0.007), but not in the Fine and Gray model. No significant association was found between COVID-19 diagnosis and ATE risk.

Conclusion

The study showed that 30 days period after a COVID-19 diagnosis could be associated with an increased risk of VTE in cancer patients treated with bevacizumab. However, the absolute risk difference, although unadjusted and therefore uncertain, appeared modest. Causality cannot be established in this retrospective design. No significant association was observed for ATE.

title: Stroke Death Rates Among Adults Aged ≥18 Years - United States, 2000-2024.
authorString: Tong X, Delara D, Coronado F, Carlson SA.

journal.title: MMWR. Morbidity and mortality weekly report

abstractText: In 2024, stroke was the fourth leading cause of death in the United States. A 2017 report found that beginning during 2013-2015, earlier declines in stroke death rates stalled or reversed among some populations of U.S. adults aged ≥35 years. This report examines 25-year trends in stroke death rates among U.S. adults aged ≥18 years across age, sex, and geographic areas, using 2000-2024 National Vital Statistics System mortality data. During 2000-2024, the age-adjusted stroke death rate among U.S. adults aged ≥18 years declined from 81.4 per 100,000 population to 51.9 (average annual percentage change = -2.0%), with declining trends across all age groups, sexes, U.S. Census Bureau regions, and U.S. jurisdictions except Delaware. Overall rates declined during 2000-2009 (annual percentage change [APC] = -5.2%), remained stable during 2009-2018, increased during 2018-2021 (APC = 4.0%), and declined again during 2021-2024 (APC = -2.4%). However, during the most recent trend periods, rates increased among adults aged 35-44 years, those aged ≥85 years, women, residents of the Midwest and South U.S. Census Bureau regions, and in 12 U.S. jurisdictions. Despite long-term declines in stroke death rates, the recent increase in trends in some demographic groups and geographic areas underscore the importance of continued surveillance to identify adults at increased risk for stroke and implement focused prevention and management efforts.

title: Outcomes of spontaneous portosystemic shunt embolization for hepatic encephalopathy in cirrhosis-the OPAL study.
authorString: Jeffrey AW, Liu K, Adams LA, Kutaiba N, Sinclair M, Testro A, Goodwin M, Pow R, Strasser SI, Spencer J, O'Beirne J, Sawhney R, Schildkraut T, Bell S, Ngu N, Corlette L, Di Bartolomeo A, Wallace M, Ebert MA, Roberts SK, Kemp W, Reiberger T, Laleman W, Martínez J, Tsochatzis EA, Tandon P, Hernandez-Gea V, Simón-Talero M, Genescà J, Majumdar A.
abstractText:
Background and objective

Embolization of large spontaneous portosystemic shunts (SPSSs) has emerged as a treatment for hepatic encephalopathy (HE). This retrospective multicenter Australian study investigated outcomes of SPSS embolization for persistent HE.

Design

Patients with cirrhosis and overt HE (grade II or more) from January 2000 to April 2025 were studied for recurrence of HE 3- and 12-month post-embolization using competing-risks analysis, along with change in maximum HE grade, ascites, variceal bleeding, and hospitalisations 1 year before and after embolization. A case-control study considering cumulative incidence of HE, liver-related death (LRD) or liver transplant (LT) was compared to those with HE and large SPSSs with no embolization from the Baveno-VI-SPSS database.

Results

Of 95 patients that underwent SPSS embolization with a median baseline MELD of 13 (IQR 11-16), 86 and 72% remained free of HE at 3 and 6 months. One year prior to embolization, 57 (60%) patients had West-Haven grade 3-4 HE, and 84% (48 patients) improved to HE grade ≤ 2 following embolization (p < 0.001). Higher MELD was not associated with worse outcome, and there was no difference in variceal bleeding or ascites post-embolization. Major procedural events occurred in seven patients (7%), with one LT and one death. Compared to matched historical controls without embolization (n = 149), there was a reduction in LRD/LT in the embolization group (sHR 0.59, 95% CI 0.40-0.88, p = 0.010), persisting on inverse probability of treatment weighting.

Conclusion

SPSS embolization reduced severity and frequency of persistent HE in cirrhosis, and was not associated with increased ascites or variceal bleeding. The association of embolization with reduced LRD/LT requires further study.

title: Risk of myocardial infarction subtypes in systemic lupus erythematosus: a matched nationwide cohort study.
authorString: Samuelsson I, Nguyen NV, Skeppholm M, Svenungsson E, Arkema EV.
abstractText:
Objective

Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is associated with an increased risk of myocardial infarction (MI), often assumed to be due to coronary artery disease (CAD), although this has not been directly demonstrated. We therefore estimated the risk of incident MI, MI with CAD (MI-CAD), and MI with non-obstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA) associated with SLE.

Methods

Individuals aged 18-80 years with incident SLE were identified in the National Patient Register (NPR) during 2006-2021 using ICD-10 codes. Up to ten population-based comparators without SLE were matched on age, sex, and residential location. Follow-up continued until fatal or non-fatal MI, death, emigration, or end of study. MI was identified using the NPR, the Cause of Death Register, and SWEDEHEART, which provided MI-CAD and MINOCA classifications defined by ≥ 50% or < 50% coronary obstruction on angiography. Incidence rates, rate differences, and cause-specific hazard ratios were estimated using Poisson and Cox regression, adjusted for age, sex, and education.

Results

We included 3,894 individuals with SLE and 38,168 matched comparators (84% women; median age 45 years). During a median follow-up of 7 years, MI occurred in 129 individuals with SLE and 584 comparators. SLE was associated with increased risks of MI (HR 2.4; 95% CI 2.0-2.9), MI-CAD (HR 2.4; 95% CI 1.9-3.1), and MI with missing angiography data (HR 2.9; 95% CI 2.1-3.9), but not MINOCA (HR 0.9; 95% CI 0.4-2.2).

Conclusion

These findings support an important role for obstructive CAD in the excess risk of MI observed in SLE.

title: Severe Hypertension in the Young: Case Report.
authorString: Hanna S, Vinitsky H, Sharashidze V, Merati M, Brandes L, Galetta S.
abstractText:
Background

Hypertension is a modifiable risk factor for neurovascular disease that has become a more prevalent threat to brain health among younger patients.
