Severe hypertension can present with both systemic and neurologic features that are important diagnostic clues to recognize, but may overlap with those of vasculitis, reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome, and genetic leukoencephalopathies.

Results

We discuss the case of a 36-year-old man who presented with likely acute on chronic hypertension and thunderclap headaches. Evaluation demonstrated a cerebral vasculopathy, diffuse cerebral white matter changes atypical for his age, multifocal subcortical diffusion restriction, pontine hemorrhages, classic hypertensive retinopathy, nephropathy without nephritis, left ventricular hypertrophy, aortic dilation, and intracranial hypertension with papilledema, bilateral transverse sinus stenoses, and bilateral abducens palsies. Vasculopathy failed to improve with intra-arterial vasodilators. Brain biopsy did not reveal vasculitis.

Conclusions

This case highlights the clinical and radiographic spectrum of the neurologic, ophthalmologic, and systemic findings of uncontrolled hypertension. We emphasize how, due to the absence of adaptive, protective vascular changes, consequences of hypertension may occur in younger patients despite blood pressure elevations that seem less severe in comparison to the higher elevations of older and more chronically hypertensive patients.

title: Advances in obstetric anesthesia care in patients with severe cardiac comorbidities.
authorString: Kraitem A, Christenson E, Meng ML.
abstractText: This review aims to update the reader about recent clinical practice recommendations in caring for the cardio-obstetric patient. The emergence of pregnancy heart teams has facilitated multidisciplinary communication for caring for a pregnant patient with cardiac disease. The utilization of noninvasive diagnostic modalities such as brain natriuretic peptide and bedside transthoracic echocardiography can yield quick actionable results regarding therapeutic options. Vaginal delivery remains the preferred mode of delivery for the vast majority of pregnant patients with cardiovascular disease. Timely and effective use of mechanical circulatory support in pregnancy can be beneficial for patients in cardiogenic shock or decompensated heart failure. Anesthesiologists are essential team members within the pregnancy heart team and should familiarize themselves with the evidence-based guidelines for caring for pregnant patients with cardiac disease.

title: Moderate-to-vigorous physical activity, longitudinal blood pressure trajectories, and hypertension-related outcomes in older adults at high cardiovascular risk: a cohort study
authorString: Fornara E, Hernandez MH, Goday A, Camps-Vilaro A, Toledo E, Salas-Salvado J, Estruch R, Ros E, Cueto-Galan R, Fiol M, Lapetra J, Timiraos J, Serra-Majem L, Pinto X, Ruiz-Canela M, Vazquez-Lorente H, Fito M, Hernaez A.
abstractText:
Background:

We aimed to investigate the association between moderate-to-vigorous leisure-time physical activity (MVLTPA) and longitudinal trajectories of systolic (SBP) and diastolic (DBP) blood pressure, as well as the incidence of high blood pressure and antihypertensive drug initiation, in adults aged 60-80 years at high cardiovascular risk.

Methods:

In participants from the PREDIMED trial (61% women; 5,254 participants), MVLTPA was assessed using the Minnesota Leisure Time Physical Activity Questionnaire and expressed as cumulative average metabolic equivalent of task-minutes/day. SBP and DBP trajectories were modelled using mixed-effects models with cubic splines (>100 [adequate] vs <100 [insufficient] metabolic equivalent of task-minutes/day). First occurrence of high blood pressure (SBP >140 mmHg or DBP >90 mmHg) and antihypertensive drug initiation were assessed with Cox models (adequate vs insufficient, and continuous MVLTPA).

Results:

SBP and DBP declined with increasing age, with no clinically meaningful differences between MVLTPA groups. The association between adequate MVLTPA and incident high blood pressure was null (HR 1.11, 95% CI 0.94-1.32). However, adequate MVLTPA was associated with a 17% lower risk of antihypertensive drug initiation (HR 0.83, 95% CI 0.71-0.98). The association appeared stronger in women (HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.58-0.94) than in men (HR 0.98, 95% CI 0.78-1.22) (p-value for sex interaction = 0.058). A modest inverse linear dose-response association between MVLTPA and risk of antihypertensive drug initiation was also observed (per 25 metabolic equivalent of task-minutes/day: HR 0.99, 95% CI 0.97-1.00; p-value = 0.022).

Conclusions:

In older adults at high cardiovascular risk, MVLTPA was not associated with clinically meaningful differences in SBP or DBP trajectories or incident high blood pressure, but was associated with a lower risk of antihypertensive drug initiation. These findings support promoting habitual physical activity as part of cardiovascular risk management in older adults.

title: Real-World Cuff-Measured Blood Pressure Trajectories in 20,003 Consumer Wearable Users
authorString: Cheung CP, Cohen JG, Bhatt AB, Curran D, Parola LR, Fielding F, Chapman CJ, von Hippel W, Holmes KE, Grosicki GJ.
abstractText: Consumer wearables increasingly allow users to log cuff-measured blood pressure (BP), but resulting BP trajectories are uncharacterized. In this retrospective cohort study, 20,003 adults with Elevated BP or Stage 1 or Stage 2 Hypertension logged BP via a consumer wearable platform. We modeled 6-month trajectories with linear mixed-effects models and examined associations of ≥5 mmHg reduction with engagement and wearable-derived metrics. Adjusted systolic reductions ranged from −2.6 mmHg (95% CI −3.1 to −2.2) in Elevated BP to −12.1 mmHg (−12.5 to −11.7) in Stage 2 Hypertension; diastolic reductions were −3.7 and −9.2 mmHg in Stage 1 and Stage 2. Overall, 50.2% achieved a ≥5 mmHg systolic reduction and 27.9% reached normal BP. App time, journaling, AI Coach use, and BP logging were associated with higher odds of reduction; longer sleep and greater physical activity accompanied lower BP. These associational findings support consumer wearables as potentially scalable BP-monitoring platforms.

title: FTH1 Suppresses Aldosterone Biosynthesis in Association with Inhibition of cAMP-PKA-CREB Signaling Pathway.
authorString: Cui X, Wang J, Du B, Zhu S, Peng C, Xu Y, Huang W, Gao R, Xiong Y, Wang Y, Hu J, Yang S, Li Q, Ma L.
abstractText: Primary aldosteronism is a leading cause of endocrine hypertension, with aldosterone-producing adenoma (APA) being a major subtype. Although ferritin heavy chain 1 (FTH1) is reportedly elevated in APA, its role in aldosterone synthesis remains unclear. This study examined FTH1 expression in APA and non-functional adrenal tumor specimens, revealing marked upregulation of FTH1 that positively correlated with plasma aldosterone levels. To determine its function, Fth1cKO mice with Cyp11a1-Cre-mediated Fth1 knockout in steroidogenic tissues and FTH1-overexpressing H295R cells were generated. Under basal conditions, neither deletion nor overexpression affected aldosterone production. However, following sodium restriction, female Fth1cKO mice exhibited significantly increased serum aldosterone and adrenal Cyp11b2 expression without changes in adrenal iron content, a response absent in males. Transcriptomic profiling indicated enhanced steroid hormone biosynthesis and cAMP signaling. Consistently, FTH1 overexpression in H295R cells suppressed stimulated aldosterone secretion and CYP11B2 expression, accompanied by reduced PKA/CREB phosphorylation. These findings identify FTH1 as a negative regulator of aldosterone biosynthesis under pathological stimulation and raise the possibility that its elevation in APA may represent a compensatory response on excessive steroidogenesis.

title: GO- and calcium silicate NP-modified diamides for enhanced antimicrobial activity: structural, morphological, and <i>in silico</i> investigations.
authorString: Alizadeh F, Huseynzada A, Israyilova A, Malikova N, Gasimov E, Rzayev F, Yolchuyeva U, Hasanova U, Abbasov V, Gakhramanova Z, Huseynova A, Huseynova L, Khalafova I.
abstractText: We herein report the preparation and investigation of antimicrobial nanohybrid systems based on antimicrobial diamides and GO, as well as CaSiO3 NPs. Diamides were synthesized by condensation of 4-nitrobenzoyl chloride with aromatic diamines under catalyst-free conditions, followed by non-covalent conjugation of the obtained compounds with GO and CaSiO3. Synthesized diamides, NPs, and nanoensembles were investigated by spectroscopic, microscopic, and diffraction techniques. The obtained two-component nanohybrid systems were examined against bacterial and yeast strains, which demonstrated their potent antimicrobial efficacy in comparison to parent compounds and NPs alone; in particular, F8@GO MIC in the case of B. cereus was 8 µg mL-1. Furthermore, the ultrastructural investigations of bacterial cells treated with F8@GO using TEM demonstrated significant morphological changes such as extensive cytoplasmic rarefaction, disruption of intracellular organization and ghost cell formation in contrast to control bacterial cells. Taking into account the phenotypic damage observed in TEM analysis, key cell division and peptidoglycan-synthesizing as well as glycolytic enzymes were selected for molecular docking analysis that revealed a promising binding affinity between the targeted compound F8 and the identified pocket on TubZ. Furthermore, a 100 ns molecular dynamics simulation provides consistent, multi-parameter evidence for a stable and well-tolerated TubZ-F8 complex.

title: Rapid Endoscopic Improvement of Melphalan-Associated Esophageal Mucosal Injury After Allogeneic Stem Cell Transplant.
authorString: Wood C, Dave S, Beniwal-Patel P, Sobin WH.
abstractText: Acute esophageal necrosis (AEN) is a rare complication of medications, infections, malnutrition, hypoxemia, cancer, sepsis, or trauma characterized grossly by circumferential necrotic mucosa and histologically by the destruction of the esophageal mucosa and submucosa. A middle-aged woman was diagnosed with AEN on post-transplant day 4 after an allogeneic peripheral blood stem cell transplant with fludarabine and melphalan. Her extensive necrosis resolved spontaneously within 8 days with only supportive care. Drug-induced AEN is rare but should be identified immediately with upper endoscopy if a patient develops signs of gastrointestinal bleeding after starting chemotherapeutic medications.

title: Robotic Versus Endoscopic Approach in Single-port Nipple-sparing Mastectomy With Direct-to-implant Prepectoral Breast Reconstruction.
authorString: Li M, Shen G, Li S, Jiang H, Lang R, Wang Z.

journal.title: Plastic and reconstructive surgery. Global open

abstractText:
Background

This study compares surgical and implant-related outcomes between robotic and endoscopic approaches in single-port nipple-sparing mastectomy with direct-to-implant prepectoral breast reconstruction.

Methods

In this retrospective cohort study, 54 patients undergoing nipple-sparing mastectomy with prepectoral reconstruction were divided into a robotic group (n = 21) and an endoscopic group (n = 33). Perioperative variables, including operative time, blood loss, drainage duration, hospital stay, and costs, as well as postoperative complications, were analyzed and compared between the 2 groups.

Results

Median follow-up was 4.45 months for the robotic group and 8.73 months for the endoscopic group. The robotic approach required significantly longer operative time (244.32 ± 43.10 versus 178.72 ± 47.53 min, P < 0.001) and incurred substantially higher cost (US $14,464.77 ± $503.38 versus $10,303.79 ± $1017.26, P < 0.001). No significant differences were observed in intraoperative blood loss, length of hospital stay, drainage duration, or postoperative complication rates between the 2 groups.

Conclusions

Robot-assisted nipple-sparing mastectomy with direct-to-implant prepectoral reconstruction is currently associated with longer operative time and higher cost compared with the endoscopic approach. Larger prospective studies with extended follow-up are needed to assess its oncological safety and aesthetic outcomes.

title: Physics-Based Flow-Mediated Dilation Reveals Altered Mechanotransduction in Type 1 Diabetes.
authorString: Zhou B, Santhanam S, Sidnawi B, Marshall L, Simon AB, Nicholson MS, Harris RA, Wu Q.
abstractText: Objective: To evaluate the first clinical application of the Wu-Sidnawi biophysical framework to flow-mediated dilation (FMD) test and investigate whether it could provide complementary mechanistic characterization of vascular alterations associated with type 1 diabetes (T1D). Impact Statement: This study demonstrates the clinical utility of the Wu-Sidnawi framework by providing complementary mechanistic insight into vascular function and suggesting altered model-derived vascular mechanotransduction from routine FMD measurements. Introduction: FMD test is a widely used noninvasive assessment of endothelial function, but conventional metrics do not explicitly characterize the mechanobiological processes governing the vascular response. The Wu-Sidnawi framework dynamically models the complete FMD response and estimates 5 physiologically meaningful parameters representing distinct aspects of vascular biomechanics. Methods: Previously acquired FMD recordings from 69 individuals with T1D and 38 healthy controls were reanalyzed. Continuous brachial artery diameter-time profiles were used to estimate model-derived parameters. Conventional and model-derived metrics were compared between groups, and correlation, covariate-adjusted regression, and logistic regression analyses with internal cross validation were performed to evaluate their relationships and ability to characterize vascular alterations. Results: Conventional FMD metrics, including percentage FMD, showed no statistically significant group differences. In contrast, the vaso-mechanotransduction index was nominally lower in participants with T1D ( 1.39±0.90vs.1.76±1.16×10-3,P=0.045 ), indicating altered model-derived vaso-mechanotransduction. Wu-Sidnawi parameters provided information complementary to conventional metrics, and combining both parameter sets increased McFadden's pseudo-R 2 from 0.008 to approximately 0.11. Conclusion: The Wu-Sidnawi framework extends conventional FMD analysis by providing complementary model-derived biophysical descriptors that improve characterization of vascular dysfunction in T1D.

title: Activity-specific social participation and multiple dimensions of smoking behavior among older adults in China: A cross-sectional secondary analysis of CHARLS 2020.
authorString: Bao R, He J, Ha L.
abstractText:
Introduction

Social participation is often treated as health-promoting, but its association with smoking may differ by activity and smoking outcome. We examined cross-sectional associations of eight activity types with smoking status, daily cigarette count, and former-smoking status.

Methods

This cross-sectional secondary analysis included CHARLS 2020 respondents aged ≥60 years with classifiable smoking status and complete outcome-specific data. Eight previous-month indicators covered interacting with friends; playing mahjong, chess, or cards or going to a community club; helping non-co-residents; going to a sport, social, or other club; community organizations; volunteering; education or training; and other activity. Community-clustered multivariable models included all eight indicators simultaneously; false discovery rate correction was applied within each outcome.

Results

Analyses included 7804 participants for current versus never smoking, 2376 current smokers for daily cigarette count, and 3871 ever smokers for former versus current smoking. For the combined item, current-smoking prevalence was 43.9% among participants versus 27.1% among non-participants. Participation was associated with higher adjusted odds of current smoking (AOR=1.78; 95% CI: 1.48-2.14; q<0.001) and a 14% higher expected cigarette count (AIRR=1.14; 95% CI: 1.06-1.22; q=0.002). For 'going to a sport, social, or other club', current-smoking prevalence was 14.9% among participants versus 30.3% among non-participants; participation was associated with lower adjusted odds of current smoking (AOR=0.57; 95% CI: 0.42-0.77; q=0.001) but not cigarette count. No activity met the FDR threshold for former versus current smoking.

Conclusions

Treating social participation as a single favorable exposure would obscure opposite, outcome-specific associations. Distinguishing activity contexts and smoking dimensions provides a basis for longitudinal research on peer and venue characteristics.

title: Secondary aldosteronism due to premature renal artery atherosclerosis in X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy.
authorString: van Rossum N, Boily P, Lefebvre M, Carpentier AC, St-Jean M.
abstractText: X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy (ALD), an uncommon cause of adrenal insufficiency, requires lifelong surveillance of adrenal function. Glucocorticoid deficiency is reported in approximately 80% and mineralocorticoid deficiency in 50% of patients with ALD. In 2014, we took over the follow-up of a 31-year-old man who had been diagnosed with ALD in 1991. In 1995, he was treated with hematopoietic stem cell transplantation and was supplemented with hydrocortisone 10 mg/m<sup>2</sup> and fludrocortisone 0.05 mg daily. In 2015, resistant hypertension and hypokalemia were noticed and persisted despite discontinuation of fludrocortisone. Biochemical analysis showed secondary aldosteronism. Doppler ultrasonography was compatible with a hemodynamically significant right renal artery stenosis. Furthermore, significant aortic atheromatosis was described on abdominal computed tomography, which was disproportionate for the patient's age and risk factors. Spironolactone was added to his antihypertensive medication, which normalized blood pressure and hypokalemia. In 2022, he presented with severe hypotension and acute renal failure. All his antihypertensive medications were stopped because secondary aldosteronism had been resolved. The renal Doppler showed severe right renal artery stenosis with severe renal atrophy. Thus, he spontaneously infarcted his right kidney that was inducing secondary aldosteronism, confirming he had persistent inducible zona glomerulosa cells.

title: Impact of autoimmune disease family history on clinical features in patients with persistent antiphospholipid antibodies: The CAPSTONE (Chinese AntiphosPholipid Syndrome cohorT cOllaborative NEtworks) cohort study I.
authorString: Wang Z, Zhou Y, Xue J, Liu D, Wang M, Duan X, Yang X, Gai Y, Liu L, Zhao Y, Huang C, Qi W, Jiang H, Li M, Zeng X, Zhao J, CAPSTONE.
abstractText:
Background

A family history of autoimmune disease (AIDFH) is noted in patients with antiphospholipid syndrome (APS), yet its clinical significance remains underexplored. This study aims to assess the impact of AIDFH on clinical and immunological features of individuals with persistent antiphospholipid antibody (aPL) positivity.

Methods

Data were drawn from the Chinese AntiphosPholipid Syndrome cohorT cOllaborative NEtworks (CAPSTONE), the first prospective, multicenter cohort of participants with confirmed persistent aPL positivity in China. Patients from five CAPSTONE sites (Oct 2022-Oct 2024) were stratified by AIDFH status. Demographic, clinical, and serological parameters were compared. Whole-exome sequencing (WES) was performed, and human leukocyte antigen (HLA) alleles were analyzed.

Results

Among 936 patients, 72 (7.7%) reported AIDFH. These patients had earlier disease onset (27.6 years vs. 29.8 years, P = 0.027), more overlap with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) (43.1% [31/72] vs. 29.4% [254/864], P = 0.016), and higher antinuclear antibody (ANA) positivity (73.9% [51/69] vs. 55.1% [441/801], P = 0.002). In those meeting the 2006 revised Sydney classification criteria for APS, AIDFH correlated with lower frequency of primary APS, and increased rates of pulmonary embolism, chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension, valve thickening, and various ANAs. Subgroup analysis showed that family history of SLE was linked to more SLE overlap, and elevated ANA, anti-dsDNA, anti-ribosomal ribonucleoprotein antibody (anti-rRNP), and Coomb's positivity. Among 374 patients with WES data, HLA-DRB1*08:02 was significantly more frequently shown in AIDFH-positive patients (P = 9.3 × 10-5).

Conclusion

Our cohort shows that in patients with persistent aPL positivity, those with AIDFH may have unique clinical and immunogenetic backgrounds. This study provides preliminary evidence for further studies focusing on genetic predisposition and mechanisms. We call for raised attention of AIDFH as a potential risk factor, and further studies are needed to provide suggestions on prognosis and overall management of patients with persistent aPL positivity.

title: A microbial metabolite reframes the gut-kidney axis in calcium oxalate nephropathy<sup>†</sup>.
authorString: Abdelhalim KA.
abstractText: Kidney stone disease has long been viewed primarily as a disorder of urinary supersaturation, with therapeutic strategies focusing on reducing urinary oxalate and preventing crystal formation. Increasing evidence, however, suggests that renal epithelial injury, immune responses, and the gut microbiota are integral components of disease pathogenesis. In their recent article, published in The Journal of Pathology, Li, Chen, Lin, Jian et al provide compelling evidence that microbiota-derived tryptophan metabolism constitutes an important regulator of calcium oxalate nephropathy. Through integrated metagenomic and metabolomic analyses of patients with calcium oxalate stones, followed by mechanistic validation in experimental models, the authors identify indole-3-propionic acid (IPA) as a key microbial metabolite depleted in stone formers. They further demonstrate that IPA protects against renal crystal deposition by activating aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) signaling, inducing suppressor of cytokine signaling 3 (SOCS3), suppressing STAT1 activation, and ultimately limiting tubular epithelial apoptosis. Beyond identifying a candidate therapeutic metabolite, this study shifts the current paradigm from considering the gut microbiota solely as a regulator of intestinal oxalate metabolism to recognizing microbial metabolites as active mediators of renal injury and repair. These findings broaden our understanding of the gut-kidney axis and provide a framework for developing microbiome-based therapeutic strategies targeting host signaling pathways in nephrolithiasis. © 2026 The Pathological Society of Great Britain and Ireland.

title: Pulmonary hypertension due left heart disease is associated with increased UTP-dependent contraction in pulmonary veins.
authorString: Garcia A, León P, Fonseca M, Fernández-Moya A, Zúñiga-Maria C, Müller M, Gómez M, Michea L, Henriquez M.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Am J Physiol Lung Cell Mol Physiol
journal.title: American journal of physiology. Lung cellular and molecular physiology
journal.isoabbreviation: Am J Physiol Lung Cell Mol Physiol

abstractText: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) secondary to left heart disease (group II) is a fatal syndrome and the most prevalent form of PH. PH-II is characterized by an increase in total pulmonary vascular resistance (TPVR). Recent studies in patients found an association between remodeling of small-diameter pulmonary veins (SPV) and the severity of PH-II, suggesting that increased SPV contractility and/or remodeling may contribute to increased TPVR. Purinergic agonists can induce contraction and vascular remodeling via purinergic receptors on vascular smooth muscle cells, and purinergic receptor signaling is implicated in other forms of PH. Thus, we hypothesized that PH-II alters purinergic receptors in SPV, contributing to increased TPVPR. The study of PH-II is limited due to the lack of suitable experimental models. Therefore, we first evaluated three experimental strategies to induce PH-II in rats: abdominal aortic constriction, renovascular hypertension, and transverse aortic constriction (TAC). Physiologic, echocardiographic, morphometric, and molecular biology studies indicated that only TAC rats developed PH-II. Next, we evaluated whether TAC-induced PH-II modified the contractile response to purinergic agonists in SPV. Studies in precision-cut lung slices showed that SPV from TAC-induced HP-II presented an increased contractile response to UTP. Both lung tissue and laser-microdissected SPV from TAC-induced PH-II rats showed higher purinergic receptor expression as compared with lung tissue and SPV from control rats. Also, lungs from TAC-induced PH-II rats showed SPV hypertrophy and SPV wall remodeling, associated with perivascular/peribronchial immune cell infiltration. These results suggest that purinergic receptors of SPV are implicated in PH-II development.

title: YAP/TAZ-TEAD as an Executor of Focal Adhesion Mechanotransduction Suppressed by the Hippo Pathway.
authorString: Hong W.
abstractText: Although the Hippo pathway is a well-established negative regulator of the YAP/TAZ-TEAD1-4 transcriptional complex, the molecular mechanisms that actively sustain YAP/TAZ-TEAD activation remain poorly defined. Integrating recent literature with systematic Cancer Dependency Map (DepMap) codependency analysis, we propose a working model wherein the TAZ/YAP-TEAD complex functions as a nuclear executor of the focal adhesion mechanotransduction cascade. This mechanotransduction arm is predicted to initiate at the plasma membrane by integrins α<sub>v</sub>β<sub>5</sub> (ITGAV/ITGB5), N-cadherin (CDH2), and lysophosphatidic acid receptor 1 (LPAR1), which likely engage PKN2 and MARK2/3 signaling kinases downstream of the focal adhesion complex. Conversely, a cell-surface triad comprising NRP1, PLXNA1, and KIRREL1 and EPHA2 may act as an upstream activator of the inhibitory Hippo pathway. Collectively, we propose that TAZ/YAP-TEAD activity is governed by a dynamic, reciprocal antagonism between the Hippo pathway and focal adhesion-mediated mechanotransduction, with the latter serving as a positive driver sustaining YAP/TAZ functional activity.

title: Development of a deep learning model to automatically localize anatomic landmarks important for intraperitoneal free fluid detection during focused assessment with sonography in trauma (FAST).
authorString: Schnittke N, Lee H, Ghoshal G, Thomas C, Baloescu C, Hicks B, Feuerherdt M, Gregory C, Kessler DO, Moore C, Parker M, Petrovich M, Rizzo J, Sabbaj A, Silver A, Sreenivasan A, Thompson MA, Zhang Y, Mukaddim RA, Schmidt S, Chen G, Wilson MG, Zahiri M, Gregory K, Raju B.
abstractText:
Background

The Focused Assessment with Sonography in Trauma (FAST) exam allows clinicians to rapidly identify intraperitoneal free fluid (FF), which can accumulate in several discrete anatomic locations. These locations represent potential spaces and are defined by adjacent key organ features. Satisfactory evaluation of these organ features is necessary to obtain a complete FAST exam. We sought to develop an algorithm that accurately identified relevant organs important for the FAST exam.

Methods

Data was used from 218 prospectively enrolled subjects with positive and negative FAST exams yielding 2,218 videos and 323,304 frames. Images were frame annotated for the presence of the following key organ features: liver, caudal liver tip, spleen, caudal spleen tip, kidney, diaphragm, and bladder. Data were randomly split into training, validation, and test sets in a 6:2:2 ratio for training a deep learning model using the YOLOv5 object detection algorithm. Diagnostic accuracy of the test set is reported at the frame and video levels.

Results

At the frame level, the mean average precision (mAP50) was 0.71. At the video level, the mean F1 score for organ detection was 0.85. Video level detection of anatomic locations (defined by the co-incidence of two relevant organ structures) of potential FF accumulation showed a mean F1 of 0.79. At the video level, the model was optimized to favor a higher mean specificity (0.90, 95% CI 0.89-0.92) at the expense of a slightly reduced mean sensitivity (0.88, 95% CI 0.85-0.90). The inference speed was 26 ms per frame (38 frames per second) on a mobile tablet.

Conclusions

This organ detection algorithm identifies the key organ features and their interfaces, which are important for FF assessment. The algorithm has a low inference speed that approximates real time temporal resolution, providing a foundation for future work supporting automated image capture and quality assessment.

title: Maintaining integrity amidst turmoil: A qualitative exploration of parental coping process during hematopoietic stem cell transplantation for pediatric cancer.
authorString: Pouraboli B, Maleki M, Nayeri ND, Hamidieh AA, Mardani A.
abstractText:
Background

Childhood cancer, particularly pediatric hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT), imposes profound psychosocial and socioeconomic challenges on parents. This study aimed to develop a grounded theory explaining the dynamic coping process experienced by parents during their child's HSCT journey.

Methods

This qualitative study used Corbin and Strauss's (2015) grounded theory approach to develop an explanatory account of the parental coping process during pediatric HSCT. Twenty Persian-speaking parents of children undergoing HSCT at a tertiary care center in Iran were recruited through purposive and theoretical sampling. Data collection began with unstructured interviews and progressed to in-depth semi-structured interviews. Data were analyzed through constant comparative analysis, including open, axial, and selective coding.

Results

Parental coping during pediatric HSCT was a multifaceted, non-linear process shaped by evolving stressors and adaptive responses. The analysis generated a grounded theory centered on the core category, "maintaining integrity amidst turmoil," which reflected parents' efforts to manage their central concern, "entrapment in adversity," arising from perceived threats and trapped in suffering. Coping was mediated through two key strategies: "health-seeking behaviors" and "emotional and cognitive coping efforts". Contextual factors, including a "continuum of support systems" (ranging from empowering healthcare interactions to systemic inadequacies) and "beliefs and individual situation" (cultural, spiritual, and personal values), significantly influenced coping trajectories. Outcomes included "relative adaptation" and "self-actualization".

Conclusions

Tailored support systems that address systemic gaps and cultural beliefs are essential for fostering adaptive coping. Strengthening health-seeking and emotional-cognitive strategies can promote functional stability and personal growth among parents.

title: Untargeted plasma metabolomics reveals metabolite alterations and pathway perturbations in gestational diabetes mellitus.
authorString: Chaiyachate K, Pongsamakthai M, Jamnongkan W, Phetcharaburanin J, Sawatjui N, Kraiklang R, Charoensri S, Jusakul A.
abstractText:
Objectives

Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is defined as glucose intolerance first detected during pregnancy and is associated with adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes. Metabolomics provides a system-level approach to characterize metabolic alterations associated with gestational insulin resistance. This study aimed to identify plasma metabolite differences between women with GDM and normal glucose tolerance (NGT) and to evaluate the discriminatory performance of a metabolite-based panel.

Methods

Plasma samples from 270 pregnant women (169 GDM and 101 NGT) were analyzed using an untargeted 1H nuclear magnetic resonance (1H NMR)-based metabolomics approach. Differential metabolites were identified using univariate, followed by multivariate modeling and regression adjustment for maternal age and pre-pregnancy body mass index. Discriminatory performance was evaluated using Random Forest (RF), Partial Least Squares-Discriminant Analysis (PLS-DA), and Linear Support Vector Machine (Linear-SVM) models with Receiver Operating Characteristic curve analysis. Pathway enrichment analyses were performed using KEGG and SMPDB, and disease-based enrichment was assessed using HMDB.

Results

Among 31 identified metabolites, 14 differed significantly between GDM and NGT. Integration of univariate and multivariate analyses prioritized nine metabolites-acetone, citrate, glucose, succinate, glycine, 3-hydroxybutyrate, leucine, phenylalanine, and the CH = CH bond of unsaturated lipids-that remained independently associated with GDM after covariate adjustment. All nine metabolites were elevated in the GDM group. A nine-metabolite panel achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.76 (95% CI: 0.70-0.81) using the RF model. Pathway enrichment identified valine, leucine, and isoleucine biosynthesis and ketone body metabolism as significantly enriched pathways. HMDB-based disease enrichment showed overlap with preeclampsia-related metabolic signatures.

Conclusion

Untargeted 1H NMR metabolomics, combined enrichment analyses, identified coordinated metabolic disturbances in GDM involving amino acid and ketone body metabolism. A nine-metabolite panel demonstrated moderate discriminative performance and provides mechanistic insight into GDM-associated metabolic adaptations, supporting their potential utility for future biomarker validation and translational studies.

title: Prevalence and determinants of psychological distress among adults living with multimorbidity of chronic non‑communicable diseases: A cross‑sectional study in the Volta Region of Ghana.
authorString: Dowou RK, Ayanore M, Kugbey N, Tarkang EE, Arthur LE, Ampomah ME, Nortey AN, Owusu-Agyei S.
abstractText: Psychological distress is common among patients with chronic non-communicable diseases (CNCDs), yet little is known about its prevalence and determinants among people living with multimorbidity in Ghana. This cross-sectional study examined the prevalence of psychological distress and the socio-demographic, occupational, and psychosocial factors associated with it among adults with multiple CNCDs in the Volta Region of Ghana. A total of 1,177 adults aged 18 years and above with confirmed CNCD diagnoses were recruited from three referral hospitals. Data were collected using structured questionnaires covering demographics and psychosocial functioning, together with the DASS-21, PHQ-9, and GAD-2 instruments, and logistic regression identified factors associated with each distress outcome. Overall, 58.8% of patients experienced psychological distress, including clinically significant anxiety in 38.8%, depression in 20.5%, and stress in 19.8%. Patients aged 30-39 years had higher odds of depression than those under 30 (AoR 3.89). Being married (AoR 2.52), divorced (AoR 3.17), or widowed (AoR 2.79) was associated with higher odds of anxiety. At roughly GHS 10 to $1, patients earning less than GHS 500 (AoR 2.43) or GHS 500-1000 (AoR 2.76) had higher odds of anxiety than those with no income. Rural residence was linked to higher odds of both anxiety and depression (AoR 2.24 for each). Media exposure once weekly (AoR 0.34) or more than five times weekly (AoR 0.44) was associated with lower odds of depression compared with no exposure. Living with a CNCD for 5-10 years increased the odds of anxiety (AoR 1.55) and stress (AoR 1.43), while a duration beyond 10 years raised the odds of depression (AoR 1.74) and anxiety (AoR 1.96). Poor perceived quality of life was associated with anxiety (AoR 1.61) and stress (AoR 1.44). Distress is highly prevalent, so mental health screening and psychosocial support must join CNCD care.

title: Improving offloading in diabetic feet: 3D-printed custom accommodative insoles outperform standard of care.
authorString: Muir BC, Nickerson KA, Carranza C, Varre MS, Nagle-Christensen A, Heino D, Li EY, Ledoux WR, Telfer S.
abstractText:
Introduction

3D-printed custom accommodative insoles may offer improved plantar pressure offloading compared to standard-of-care (total contact EVA base with a 4-mm Plastazote-PORON foam top layer) insoles for individuals with diabetes. We have developed two versions of 3D-printed accommodative insoles that have patient-specific geometries as well as patient-specific stiffnesses and structural behaviors. The purpose of this study is to determine if two styles of novel 3D printed accommodative insoles (pressure-based and finite element-based), with patient-specific geometries as well as local patient-specific stiffnesses, can provide greater reductions in plantar pressures for at-risk areas of the foot without increasing pressure in the regions adjacent compared to the standard-of-care and no insole, in individuals with diabetes.

Methods

Twenty-five adults with diabetes and high plantar pressure completed walking trials under no insole, standard-of-care, pressure-based insole, and finite element-based insole conditions. Peak plantar pressure and pressure-time integral were measured in high-risk regions of interest and adjacent regions. Participant comfort and preference were recorded.

Results

All insoles significantly reduced peak plantar pressure and pressure-time integral by greater than 14% in the regions of interest compared to no insole (p < 0.001). Compared with the standard-of-care, pressure-based insole and finite element-based insole further reduced peak pressure (22% and 24%, respectively) and pressure-time integral (19% and 35%, respectively) in the region of interest (p < 0.001). Finite element-based insole reduced pressure-time integral and peak plantar pressure in adjacent regions (p < 0.01), indicating broader offloading. Participant preferences and feedback indicated improvements in fit and comfort are needed across all insoles before clinical implementation.

Conclusion

There is potential for personalized, 3D-printed custom accommodative insoles as a patient-centered approach to offloading plantar pressure in individuals with diabetes. These technologies may support more effective and tailored strategies in preventing diabetic foot complications.

title: Statin use is associated with reduced negative symptoms in schizophrenia spectrum disorders: A longitudinal observational study.
authorString: Dielemans DAM, Gangadin SS, Crutzen S, Steinz C, Wahab RJ, Castelein S, Liemburg EJ, Veling W, Visser E, Huizer K, Sommer IEC, de Haan L, van Beveren NJM.
abstractText: Inflammation has been implicated in the pathophysiology of schizophrenia spectrum disorders (SSD), suggesting that anti-inflammatory strategies might offer therapeutic potential. While statins exert anti-inflammatory effects and may reduce negative symptoms, findings on their efficacy remain inconsistent. We investigated whether statin use is associated with changes in symptom severity in SSD. This longitudinal cohort study used real-world data from the Pharmacotherapy Monitoring and Outcome Survey (PHAMOUS), an annual routine outcome monitoring program in the Netherlands. Data were collected from 2013 to 2024. Participants with SSD who were not using statins at baseline and had no recorded substance-related disorders other than cannabis or alcohol were included. Individuals who initiated statin therapy during the observational period were classified as statin users, all others were classified as non-users. Outcomes were changes in log-transformed Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS) negative subscale scores and, secondarily, total and other subscale scores over time. Among the included participants, 264 initiated statin therapy, whereas 2,952 participants did not use statins during the study period. After one year, statin use was associated with a credible reduction in PANSS negative subscale scores (adjusted posterior mean = -0.358, 95% CI [-0.533, -0.174], PD = 1), corresponding to an approximately 3.6- point lower score when using the baseline median score of 11 as a reference. No credible evidence of mediation by C-reactive protein, LDL cholesterol, triglycerides, waist circumference, or blood pressure was observed. The association with lower negative symptom scores was also observed among patients with continued statin use over three years. Statin use was associated with reduced negative symptom severity in individuals with SSD. Beyond their established cardiometabolic benefits, statins may also have therapeutic potential for negative symptoms in SSD.

title: Secondary pseudotumor cerebri syndrome following depressed skull fracture: a case report and review of the literature.
authorString: Datta D, Ghosh R, Shah D, Ghosh AK.

journal.title: Child's nervous system : ChNS : official journal of the International Society for Pediatric Neurosurgery

abstractText: Secondary pseudotumor cerebri syndrome is an uncommon delayed complication of traumatic injury to the dural venous sinuses, particularly in children with skull fractures overlying venous sinuses. We report the case of a 4-year-old boy who presented with episodic headache and medial deviation of the left eye, 2 months after a conservatively managed occipital depressed skull fracture. Examination showed left lateral rectus palsy and grade III papilledema, with preserved visual acuity. Magnetic resonance venography demonstrated stenosis of the right transverse sinus at the site of the previous fracture, a hypoplastic left transverse sinus, and radiological features of raised intracranial pressure, including empty sella and tortuous optic nerves. Lumbar puncture confirmed elevated cerebrospinal fluid opening pressure with normal laboratory evaluation, establishing the diagnosis of secondary pseudotumor cerebri due to post-traumatic venous sinus outflow compromise. Given the delayed presentation and the concern that fracture elevation would not rapidly restore venous drainage due to chronicity, the child underwent lumboperitoneal shunt placement. He had prompt improvement in headache and complete resolution of the abducens palsy, with resolution of papilledema 2 weeks later. A literature review identified 36 reported cases of secondary pseudotumor cerebri following skull fracture, most commonly involving the superior sagittal sinus and usually caused by extrinsic compression from depressed bone fragments. Surgical elevation remains the most frequently reported treatment, however, CSF diversion, anticoagulation, decompressive craniectomy, venous angioplasty, and repeated lumbar puncture have also been used. This case highlights the need to consider delayed venous outflow obstruction after skull fracture and to individualize management according to timing, sinus anatomy, and mechanism of obstruction.

title: Longitudinal Multimodality Imaging of Cardiovascular Abnormalities Following Definitive Chemoradiation for Lung Cancer: A Retrospective Cohort Study
authorString: Nguyen T, Salama V, Schmidlen JA, Lilly PM, Wen S, Dunham N, Siochi RA, Zeb I, Naklah B, Clump DA, Pifer PM, Hanna MF.
abstractText:
ABSTRACT

Background/Objectives

Cardiovascular complications following definitive chemoradiation therapy (CRT) for lung cancer are well recognized, but their longitudinal imaging manifestations remain incompletely characterized. We aimed to characterize cardiovascular abnormalities across multiple imaging modalities and electrocardiography during lung cancer survivorship.

Methods

This retrospective single-center study included patients treated with definitive CRT between 2013 and 2025 who underwent baseline and follow-up cardiovascular assessments. Findings from computed tomography, echocardiography, myocardial perfusion imaging, coronary angiography, and electrocardiography were categorized into exploratory, literature-informed cardiovascular phenotype domains across five follow-up intervals. Longitudinal patterns were evaluated using generalized estimating equations (GEE). and exploratory associations with clinical cardiovascular adverse events (CVAEs) were assessed using χ² or Fisher’s exact tests.

Results

Eighty-six patients were included (mean age, 66 ± 9.1 years; 46 women). Baseline coronary, thoracic aortic, and valvular calcification were common, affecting 72%, 88%, and 50% of patients, respectively. During the first 0–6 months, reduced LV systolic function (53%), valvular dysfunction (35%), and pericardial effusion (19%) were observed. Pericardial effusion was observed in 37% at 1-2 years, while calcification progression and pulmonary vascular abnormalities were identified during later follow-up intervals. Longitudinal analyses suggested positive associations between successive follow-up categories and calcification progression (average OR, 4.30), pulmonary artery enlargement (OR, 1.49; 95% CI, 1.10-2.02; P = 0.01 ), right-heart abnormalities (average OR, 1.65), and arrhythmia (OR, 1.76; 95% CI, 1.30-2.38; P < 0.001 ). Exploratory associations between imaging abnormalities and clinical CVAEs were also observed.

Conclusions

Longitudinal multimodality cardiovascular assessments identified heterogeneous cardiovascular abnormalities across follow-up intervals following definitive CRT for lung cancer. Larger prospective studies are needed to validate these observations.

title: Nine Novel Sonographic Signs
authorString: Ji X.
abstractText: Ultrasound is a widely used imaging modality in clinical practice, and sonographic signs serve as valuable teaching tools that aid in pattern recognition and diagnosis. This review consolidates five novel sonographic signs previously proposed by the author, including the Cracked Earth Sign for subcutaneous edema, the Mushroom Cap Sign for localized gallbladder adenomyomatosis, the LTS Sign for dilated cardiomyopathy, the LTI Sign for endocardial fibroelastosis, and the Three Pipes Sign for the suprasternal long-axis view of the aortic arch. The SFH Sign for advanced cervical insufficiency, the Gentle Upslope Sign for the parvus–tardus waveform, the Fenestrated Ring Sign for diffuse gallbladder adenomyomatosis, and the Tadpole Tail Sign for the renal artery origin are proposed for the first time in this paper. Collectively, these nine signs span the fields of superficial ultrasound, abdominal ultrasound, echocardiography, vascular ultrasound, and obstetric ultrasound. For each sign, its naming logic, definition, clinical implications, and teaching value are described. This review aims to facilitate a better understanding of these signs and to promote their use as teaching aids in ultrasound education.

title: Mechanical Tricuspid Valve Thrombosis Treated With Ultrasound-Assisted Catheter-Directed Thrombolysis.
authorString: Stock J, Disney L, Schenk A, Gurley J.
abstractText:
Background

Mechanical tricuspid valves are remarkably susceptible to acute mechanical valve thrombosis (MVT). Current guidelines suggest reoperation or systemic thrombolysis for left-sided MVT. These treatments carry substantial operative and bleeding risks, limiting their application. A better nonsurgical treatment for MVT is needed.

Case summary

Six patients with suspected acute tricuspid MVT were treated with ultrasound-assisted catheter-directed thrombolysis (USCDT). Improvement in symptoms, leaflet mobility, and tricuspid regurgitation severity occurred in 5 of 6 cases with no observed complications. WHY BEYOND THE GUIDELINES?: Tricuspid MVT is not addressed in current guidelines because of a paucity of available data.

Discussion

USCDT represents a novel treatment alternative for tricuspid MVT. Direct contact between the USCDT catheter and the mechanical valve may enhance alteplase activity and thrombus dispersion.

Take-home message

USCDT may represent an alternative to contemporary treatments for tricuspid MVT and warrants further investigation.

title: Tissue repair and regeneration: molecular mechanisms and therapeutic interventions.
authorString: Zhang M, He J, Li Q.
abstractText: Tissue injury is a pervasive feature of human disease, yet adult mammals exhibit limited regenerative capacity. A central determinant of regenerative outcomes is the inflammatory response, which orchestrates tissue repair through mechanisms that are evolutionarily conserved from Drosophila to mammals. Following injury, inflammation drives debris clearance, promotes the release of cytokines and growth factors, and contributes to the restoration of functional cells. However, dysregulated or unresolved inflammation can impair healing, drive scar formation, and ultimately result in organ dysfunction or failure. Here, we focus on recent advances in the spatiotemporal regulation of inflammation during tissue repair that have reshaped our understanding of its underlying mechanisms. We synthesize findings on the dynamic progression of repair from inflammatory initiation to active resolution and stem cell activation, highlighting features of immune cell plasticity and heterogeneity within injury-specific microenvironments, as well as the existence of pivotal macrophage-fibroblast interactions. Furthermore, we delineate the pleiotropic and context-dependent roles of key cytokines and signaling pathways in coordinating these processes. Finally, we discuss current and emerging therapeutic strategies, emphasizing the paradigm shift from broad immunosuppression toward precise modulation of inflammatory networks to promote regeneration and prevent fibrosis. Future progress hinges on integrating multiomic spatial atlases, precision immunomodulation, and standardized therapeutic protocols to decipher and manipulate immune-regenerative crosstalk, thereby driving the development of next-generation regenerative therapies.

title: AortoBVI: A Machine Learning-derived Risk Stratification of Ascending Aortic Aneurysms Predictable by Imaging
authorString: Chung JC, Tajeddini F, Eliathamby D, Bhatt N, Su H, Seo H, Holt D, Ouzounian M, Hanneman K, McIntosh C, Simmons CA.
abstractText:
Background

Current diameter-based risk stratification for ascending aortic aneurysms incompletely captures patient-specific dissection risk. Here, we apply machine learning to ex vivo aortic biomechanics to define a tissue-derived risk continuum, termed aortic biomechanical vulnerability index (AortoBVI), and use magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to predict this index in vivo.

Methods

Ascending aortic tissue from 353 aneurysms, 45 normal aortas, and 46 acute aortic dissections underwent biomechanical testing. Biomechanical features were used to train a classifier distinguishing normal-like, intermediate, and dissection-like biomechanical phenotypes. Magnetic resonance imaging was performed on 38 aneurysm patients pre-operatively and 8 normal controls.

Results

The classifier achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.901 (95% CI 0.836-0.954). Among 38 aneurysms with pre-operative MRI, a model combining age, aortic stiffness index (ASI), and aortic pulse wave velocity (aPWV) estimated AortoBVI (R 2 = 0.580), identifying dissection-like aneurysms with an AUC of 0.928 (95% CI 0.826–0.994. These results significantly outperform aortic diameter (R 2 = 0.116, AUC 0.620).

Conclusion

These findings demonstrate substantial biomechanical heterogeneity at similar aortic diameters and support biomechanics-based risk stratification of ascending aortic aneurysms.

Clinical Perspective

What is New?

AortoBVI integrates five ex vivo biomechanical measurements into a continuous index anchored to normal and acute-dissection tissue phenotypes. Among 353 ascending aortic aneurysms, tissue-derived AortoBVI revealed substantial biomechanical heterogeneity despite similar aortic diameters. A model combining age with MRI-derived aortic stiffness index and aortic pulse wave velocity estimated tissue-derived AortoBVI more accurately than maximum aortic diameter.

What Are the Clinical Implications?

Aortic diameter alone does not fully capture the biomechanical variation among ascending aortic aneurysms. MRI-based AortoBVI could provide a non-invasive approach to biomechanical phenotyping that complements diameter-based assessment. Biomechanically phenotyping patients with ascending aortic aneurysms using AortoBVI may help individualize surveillance intensity and the timing of surgery.

title: Immunoglobulin G4-Related Pericarditis With Forkhead Box P3-Positive Cells in Lymphoid Follicles Identified by Pericardial Biopsy: A Case Report.
authorString: Odaka H, Gosyono R, Shimada K, Takita Y, Kawaharada Y, Tokairin T, Kasashima S.
abstractText: T-follicular regulatory (Tfr) cells have been implicated in immunoglobulin G4-related disease (IgG4-RD). A 62-year-old woman presented with dyspnea caused by recurrent right pleural effusion. Serum IgG4 level was elevated to 194 mg/dL, and computed tomography revealed right pericardial thickening. Because pleural fluid studies were nondiagnostic and no macroscopic pleural abnormalities were found during surgery, an abnormal pericardium was biopsied. Histology showed lymphoplasmacytic infiltration with an IgG4/IgG ratio > 85% and 63.3 IgG4-positive plasma cells/high-power field. Numerous forkhead box P3 (FOXP3)-positive cells were present within the lymphoid follicles, suggesting the involvement of regulatory T-cell/Tfr-related immune responses. The patient was diagnosed with IgG4-related pericarditis and treated with prednisolone 0.6 mg/kg, resulting in marked reduction of pleural effusion. FOXP3-positive cells may provide adjunctive immunopathological information, and biopsy of an abnormal pericardium may aid in diagnosis when pleural and pericardial lesions coexist.

title: Assessment of aspirin response in patients undergoing neuroendovascular treatments: A comparison of five platelet function tests across two platforms.
authorString: Sakayori T, Shoda K, Nakanishi R, Ueno Y, Kanbe A, Oka A, Mizutani D, Kitagami M, Kitano K, Kikuchi R, Enomoto Y.
abstractText: Aspirin is widely used for periprocedural antiplatelet therapy in neuroendovascular procedures; however, variability in patient response poses clinical challenges. This study aimed to assess five platelet function tests on two different platforms: light transmission aggregometry (LTA) using the CN-6000 device and the VerifyNow system, which were utilized to assess patients undergoing neuroendovascular procedures. A total of 124 patients who underwent elective neuroendovascular procedures and received perioperative aspirin-based antiplatelet therapy between September 2020 and December 2023 were retrospectively reviewed. Platelet function was assessed at three time points: before surgery, 1-3 days after surgery, and 1 month following the procedure. The assessments included maximum aggregation (MA) induced by 1 mM arachidonic acid (AA), 10 μM ADP, and 1 μg/mL collagen, as well as collagen-induced platelet aggregation level (CPAL) and aspirin reaction units (ARU). Significant perioperative changes were observed only with 1 mM AA MA, which increased immediately after surgery (p < 0.001) and decreased at 1 month (p = 0.013), while other tests showed no significant differences. Correlation analysis revealed the strongest association between 1 mM AA MA and 1 μg/mL collagen MA (r = 0.65), followed by CPAL (r = 0.62). ARU correlated modestly with LTA-based measures (r ≤ 0.34). Receiver operating characteristic analysis identified CPAL >6.0 and collagen MA > 43.2% as equivalent to AA MA > 20%. In this cohort, perioperative changes were detected by 1 mM AA MA but not by the other platelet function tests, and correlations between VerifyNow ARU and LTA-based measurements were modest. However, the clinical significance of these differences remains to be established. Automated LTA using CN-6000 may offer a practical option for aspirin monitoring in patients undergoing neuroendovascular procedures. Further prospective studies are warranted to validate its clinical utility.

title: Development and validation of an intra-procedural predictive model for radial artery spasm in patients undergoing transradial percutaneous coronary intervention-chronic total occlusion.
authorString: Zhang W, Fan Z, Yan L, Wang D.
abstractText:
Background

To develop and internally validate a robust predictive model for radial artery spasm (RAS) to facilitate real-time intra-procedural risk stratification and intraoperative strategy optimization during chronic total occlusion percutaneous coronary intervention (CTO-PCI).

Research design and methods

This retrospective study analyzed 1,327 patients undergoing CTO-PCI between January 2020 and November 2025. The dataset was divided into a derivation cohort (n = 929) and an internal validation cohort (n = 398) using a 7:3 ratio. Independent risk factors for RAS were identified through multivariate analysis to construct a logistic regression model. Model performance was rigorously assessed via AUC, calibration plots, bootstrap validation with optimism correction, Brier score, calibration slope, and decision curve analysis.

Results

Female gender, anxiety status, diabetes mellitus, hyperlipidemia, frequent catheter exchange, multiple radial artery punctures, and prolonged procedure duration were identified as independent predictors of RAS (p < 0.05). Model demonstrated excellent discriminative ability, with optimism-corrected AUCs of 0.974 in derivation cohort and 0.980 in internal validation cohort. Calibration curves, calibration slopes (0.958 and 0.864), and Brier scores (0.048 and 0.035) revealed strong agreement between predicted and observed outcomes.

Conclusions

This model is specifically designed for intra-procedural dynamic risk assessment, integrating procedural factors as cumulative risk indicators. External validation is required before routine clinical implementation.
