The 1-year calibration estimate remained least precise, with only five NOAF events by 1 year in the validation cohort.

Conclusion

In patients with SSS who remained free of atrial arrhythmia through the 3-month post-implantation landmark, a five-variable landmark model showed moderate optimism-corrected discrimination in the development cohort and promising same-centre temporal validation performance, particularly at 2 and 3 years after the landmark. The limited number of validation events, particularly at 1 year, warrants cautious interpretation. Prospective multicentre external validation is required before clinical implementation.

title: Biomechanical analysis of pneumothorax: tissue failure, computational simulation, and clinical translation.
authorString: Liu A, Wang T, Liang R, Li C, Xu H, Ahmed AWH, Yu C, Weng Z, Fan J, You J, Cui X, Zhang Y.
abstractText: From a biomechanical perspective, the development and persistence of pneumothorax are closely associated with damage to or functional failure of tissue structures responsible for maintaining pleural-cavity airtightness and pressure coupling. This review aims to summarize advances in the understanding of the mechanical mechanisms and computational modeling of pneumothorax development, lung collapse, and re-expansion, and to evaluate their potential for clinical translation. Three conceptual modes of tissue failure are outlined: stress-driven, material-driven, and overload-driven failure. The review also discusses the applications of hyperelastic, viscoelastic, and poroelastic constitutive models, as well as computational methods, including cohesive zone models (CZMs), the extended finite element method (XFEM), finite element analysis (FEA), and fluid-structure interaction (FSI) modeling. Current research remains constrained by insufficient characterization of material properties, limited representation of tissue heterogeneity, and inadequate experimental and clinical validation. These limitations reduce the comparability of model predictions and hinder their application to individualized clinical management. At present, these models are primarily used to elucidate biomechanical mechanisms and compare tissue responses under different conditions. Their practical utility in risk assessment, surgical planning, and optimization of drainage strategies requires further validation. Future research should prioritize the measurement of material properties, patient-specific model development, and rigorous experimental and clinical validation to provide a more reliable quantitative basis for mechanistic investigations and clinical decision-making in pneumothorax.

title: Point-of-care ultrasound in neonatal necrotizing enterocolitis: integrating clinician-performed evidence and nurse-led implementation.
authorString: Fu J, Wang Y, Kang X, Zhou H, Ding L, Wang S, Fu Y, Li B, Jiang Y, Zhang X, Xiao T.
abstractText: Neonatal necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is one of the most severe gastrointestinal emergencies in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU), for which early identification, accurate assessment, and dynamic monitoring are critical for improving outcomes. Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) has emerged as a non-invasive, reproducible, and portable imaging modality with unique advantages for NEC assessment. However, direct evidence on nurse-led POCUS specifically in NEC remains scarce; most published ultrasound studies have been conducted by radiologists, sonographers, or neonatologists. This review synthesizes evidence from two sources: (1) clinician-performed POCUS technical evidence in NEC, including the detection of pneumatosis intestinalis, portal venous gas, and hemodynamic alterations; and (2) nurse-led implementation evidence derived from POCUS programs in other neonatal or critical care settings, including screening workflows, documentation standards, and training requirements. We discuss the current evidence base, highlight the gap between clinician-performed technical evidence and nurse-led implementation, and propose a framework for integrating POCUS into NICU nursing practice. By critically synthesizing the available evidence, this review aims to provide practical guidance for future nurse-led POCUS programs in NEC and to outline priority areas for prospective research.

title: Sulodexide versus low-molecular-weight heparin in critically ill neonates: a propensity score-matched retrospective cohort study.
authorString: Wei M, Xiong Y, Zhang F, Wang Y, Zeng J.
abstractText:
Background

Critically ill neonates are at high risk of thrombosis, inflammation, and antimicrobial exposure in the neonatal intensive care unit, but evidence guiding adjunctive anticoagulant selection remains limited. We compared the clinical, laboratory, and safety outcomes associated with sulodexide (SDX) and low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH).

Methods

This single-center retrospective cohort study included critically ill neonates treated with sulodexide or low-molecular-weight heparin. Propensity score matching (PSM) yielded 85 matched pairs. The primary outcome was relative percentage change in D-dimer from baseline to treatment end. Secondary outcomes included other coagulation, hematological, blood-gas, and respiratory-support measures. Inflammatory status and antimicrobial defined daily doses (DDDs) were exploratory outcomes. Bleeding events first documented after treatment initiation were assessed as safety outcomes.

Results

Among 234 eligible neonates, 85 matched pairs were analyzed. D-dimer change did not differ significantly between groups [-70.2% (-82.0, -50.5) vs. -72.0% (-87.1, -42.2); between-group effect, 1.4 percentage points; 95% CI, -8.3 to 9.7; P = 0.765], and no other coagulation, hematological, or blood-gas outcomes differed significantly. Among neonates with abnormal baseline inflammatory status, CRP/hs-CRP improvement occurred in 12/12 (100.0%) and 7/11 (63.6%) in the SDX and LMWH groups, respectively (P = 0.037), suggesting a potential difference in inflammatory response. SDX remained associated with lower observed DDDs after multivariable adjustment, although this association was not robust in calendar-period sensitivity analyses. Bleeding was first documented after treatment initiation in 24/85 (28.2%) SDX-treated and 18/85 (21.2%) LMWH-treated neonates, respectively. Among neonates with bleeding, first documentation occurred during active treatment in 9/24 (37.5%) and 14/18 (77.8%), respectively.

Conclusion

No significant between-group differences were observed in the primary D-dimer or other coagulation outcomes. A higher proportion of CRP/hs-CRP improvement was observed in the SDX group, although this finding was exploratory and based on a small subgroup. The lower observed DDDs were not robust to calendar-period analyses and should not be attributed to a drug-specific effect. Bleeding was numerically more frequent in the SDX group overall, whereas a greater proportion of bleeding cases in the LMWH group were first documented during active treatment. The observed timing pattern does not establish a causal relationship with treatment. These retrospective findings require cautious interpretation and prospective confirmation.

title: Nonlinear evolution of acoustic characteristics of bowel sounds in preterm infants.
authorString: Lu M, Zhang L, Qin T, Jin Z, Zhou P.
abstractText:
Introduction

Gastrointestinal function can be assessed through bowel sounds, which objectively indicate gastrointestinal movement. However, the conventional method of abdominal auscultation has considerable limitations. This study aimed to investigate the evolutionary patterns of acoustic characteristics of bowel sounds in preterm infants, explore their variation with postmenstrual ages (PMAs), and quantify the association between PMA and bowel sound maturity to characterize the developmental trajectory of intestinal motility in preterm infants.

Methods

Twenty-seven preterm infants (gestational age: 30-36 + 6 weeks) were enrolled in this study. A convolutional neural network-based smart device was used to monitor bowel sounds 1-4 times weekly for ≥3 h from day 1 to 30 after birth. Parameters, including bowel rate (number of bowel sounds per minute), frequency, and number of durations >2 s per min, were collected. Loess regression and derivative analysis were employed to characterize the dynamic progression of the bowel sound parameters relative to PMA, whereas Mann-Whitney U or Kruskal-Wallis H tests were utilized to assess between-group differences.

Results

A nonlinear dynamic change was observed in the relationship between characteristic parameters of bowel sounds in preterm infants and PMA. A significant transition occurred at 33.1 weeks of PMA. The PMA groups showed a significant difference in both between-group and multiple comparisons (P < 0.001).

Conclusion

Bowel sound parameters demonstrated a nonlinear evolution with PMA, with an inflection point at 33.1 weeks that was synchronized with the critical maturation period of the enteric nervous system/interstitial cells of Cajal network. These parameters may serve as objective markers for assessing the dynamic maturation of the gastrointestinal system in preterm infants.

title: Cost-Effectiveness of Alcohol Use Disorder Treatment for Alcohol-Associated Liver Disease.
authorString: Gerber A, Agyekum A, Yang JY, Varghese S, Chang C, Thuluvath AJ, Verna EC, Im GY, Hur C.
abstractText:
Importance

Alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) is a leading cause of liver-related mortality and liver transplant. Combined behavioral interventions (CBI) and medications for alcohol use disorder (MAUD) are underutilized. Thus, it is critical to identify optimal therapeutic and cost-effective windows for CBI and MAUD in patients with ALD at earlier fibrosis stages.

Objective

To evaluate the cost-effectiveness of naltrexone and CBI in preventing cirrhosis in patients with ALD compared with no treatment.

Design, setting, and participants

This economic evaluation used a Markov state-transition model simulating lifetime disease progression and health care costs associated with ALD. The simulated patient cohort began at 45 years of age with active AUD and stage 3 fibrosis (F3) and could experience progression to compensated or decompensated cirrhosis.

Exposure

All patients were assumed to complete a 16-week course of naltrexone along with 52 weeks of CBI.

Main outcomes and measures

Primary outcomes included total health care cost, quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs), and incremental cost-effectiveness ratios. Secondary outcomes included liver-related mortality and progression to compensated and decompensated cirrhosis. Scenario and sensitivity analyses were performed to determine outcomes at earlier stages and with varied cost and model parameters.

Results

Without intervention, 61% of the cohort died from liver-related causes, 88% developed compensated cirrhosis, and 66% of those experienced progression to decompensated cirrhosis, with a lifetime cost of $79 799 per person. With treatment initiated at F3, liver-related mortality was reduced to 58%, lifetime compensated cirrhosis to 87%, and lifetime progression to decompensated cirrhosis to 62%, with a lifetime cost of $78 673. The treatment strategy dominated because the lifetime costs were lower and more QALYs were gained when compared with untreated natural history. Treatment was preferred in sensitivity analyses at relapse rates to 100% and adherence greater than 0%, in scenario analyses when treatment was initiated at stages F2 and F1, and for the models including societal and AUD costs.

Conclusions and relevance

In this economic evaluation of AUD treatment for patients with ALD, treating patients with ALD with naltrexone and CBI at F3 saved cost and was more effective than no treatment, reducing progression to compensated and decompensated cirrhosis. The results remained true at stages F1 and F2 fibrosis and when considering the societal costs and the costs of AUD. Future studies should include prospective evaluations of screening strategies combined with early treatment, as many patients are diagnosed at advanced stages of ALD.

title: Low-Voltage Area-Guided Ablation for Persistent Atrial Fibrillation: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.
authorString: Kivan H, Sondoqah H, Kaff AMAAA, Eldahrawy M, Mustafa AM, Htoon A, Qandeel F, Alababneh A, Khalid A, Youseif AL, Alghzawi HM, Ibraheem M.

journal.title: Annals of noninvasive electrocardiology : the official journal of the International Society for Holter and Noninvasive Electrocardiology, Inc

abstractText:
Background

Low-voltage areas (LVAs) may represent arrhythmogenic substrate in persistent atrial fibrillation (AF), but the benefit of adjunctive LVA-guided ablation remains uncertain.

Methods

We performed a PRISMA-compliant systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials comparing LVA-guided ablation with non-LVA-guided strategies in persistent or non-paroxysmal AF. Searches were updated through September 2, 2026. The primary outcome was atrial arrhythmia recurrence; time-to-event hazard ratios (HRs), repeat ablation, procedural outcomes, and safety were secondary outcomes.

Results

Eight randomized trials involving 1656 patients contributed to the primary analysis. LVA-guided ablation reduced atrial arrhythmia recurrence (RR 0.77, 95% CI 0.65-0.91; p = 0.003; I2 = 36.6%), although the 95% prediction interval included no benefit (0.51-1.17). The pooled HR was also favorable (HR 0.71, 95% CI 0.53-0.96; p = 0.026; I2 = 67.2%). Omitting IDEAL-AF attenuated both estimates and eliminated most heterogeneity. Mapping-before-randomization trials with documented LVAs did not differ from randomization-before-mapping trials (interaction p = 0.76). Repeat ablation was reduced (RR 0.69, 95% CI 0.49-0.97), while procedure time, fluoroscopy time, and major safety outcomes were not significantly different.

Conclusions

LVA-guided ablation was associated with fewer atrial arrhythmia recurrences and repeat procedures, but the pooled effect was strongly influenced by IDEAL-AF and remained heterogeneous across documented-LVA trials. Standardized mapping and ablation protocols are needed before the magnitude of benefit can be considered established.

title: Predictive Value of Serum Fibrinogen-to-Albumin Ratio in Young Patients With Coronary Heart Disease and its Correlation With Coronary Lesion Severity.
authorString: Gao YM, Cai TZ, Ma HL.
abstractText:
Objective

Predictive value of Fibrinogen-to-Albumin Ratio (FAR) in young patients with coronary heart disease (CHD) and its correlation with the severity of coronary artery lesions.

Methods

We enrolled 472 young patients hospitalized at our hospital from August 2013 to August 2024 who underwent coronary angiography (CAG) and divided into a CHD group (n = 212) and a non-CHD group (n = 260) based on CAG results. Univariate analysis was conducted on all variables. Subsequently, Lasso regression analysis (LASSO) and bidirectional stepwise logistic regression were used to identify the independent risk factors to construct a prediction model. ROC, calibration, and clinical decision curves evaluated model performance. CHD patients were grouped by Gensini tertiles to compare FAR differences, and ROC curve analyzed FAR's predictive value for moderate-to-severe stenosis.

Result

Univariate analysis showed statistically significant differences in multiple indicators including FAR (p < 0.05). Finally, seven indicators including FAR were included to establish the model. The results of ROC curve analysis showed that FAR and joint mode had predictive value for CHD (p＜0.05), The AUC of FAR was 0.643, and that of the combined model was 0.847. FAR was positively correlated with Gensini score (rs = 0.215, p < 0.001). FAR was positively correlated with the Gensini score (rs = 0.215, p < 0.001), showed an upward trend with increasing lesion severity (p = 0.046), and yielded an AUC of 0.596 for predicting moderate-to-severe stenosis (p < 0.05).

Conclusion

FAR and the prediction model have predictive value for CHD in young adults; FAR has limited predictive performance for the severity of coronary artery lesions and can serve as an auxiliary reference indicator.

title: Teach-Back-Based Interventions for Parents and Caregivers in Pediatric Healthcare: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials.
authorString: Şenol Ş, Ozcelik H, Avcı HH.
abstractText: Background/Objectives: Teach-Back is a closed-loop communication strategy used to verify understanding of health information. This review examined Teach-Back-based interventions for parents and primary caregivers in pediatric healthcare. Methods: Following PRISMA 2020 and PRISMA-S, this PROSPERO-registered review (CRD420261504251) searched PubMed/MEDLINE, CENTRAL, CINAHL Ultimate, Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, ClinicalTrials.gov, and WHO ICTRP without language or publication-year restrictions. Eligible studies were randomized controlled trials involving parents or primary caregivers of children aged 0-18 years. Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 and certainty of evidence with GRADE. Owing to clinical and methodological heterogeneity, findings were synthesized narratively. Results: Nine randomized controlled trials (1299 participants; individual study sample sizes ranging from 26 to 398) were included. The most consistent benefits were observed for medication dosing accuracy/safety (moderate-certainty evidence) and selected caregiver medication or safe-dose knowledge outcomes (low-certainty evidence). Certainty was low for asthma control and HbA1c and very low for oral health/care performance, asthma-related healthcare utilization, diabetes self-care, and caregiver self-efficacy. No principal-outcome assessment was judged to be at low risk of bias. Conclusions: Interventions incorporating Teach-Back may improve selected caregiver outcomes, particularly medication safety and knowledge. However, heterogeneity, multicomponent interventions, and methodological limitations restrict conclusions about the independent effect and generalizability of Teach-Back across pediatric settings.

title: Epidemiology and seasonality of respiratory syncytial virus among hospitalized pediatric patients with lower respiratory tract infections in Negeri Sembilan, Malaysia (2017-2024).
authorString: Iderus NHM, Singh S, Ng DC, Ghazali SM, Ghazali NM, Lim MC, Ahmad NAR, Ruslan Q, Liew CH, Ali MM, Abidin NZZ, Yusoff NHM, Gill BS, Omar MA, Ahmad LCRQ.
abstractText:
Background

Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) remains a significant public health concern globally, with distinct seasonal patterns in temperate regions, while tropical settings experience RSV year-round with seasonal fluctuations. This study investigated seasonality and exogenous factors influencing RSV cases among hospitalized children under 12 years in Negeri Sembilan, Malaysia.

Methods

Weekly laboratory-confirmed RSV-positive cases among hospitalized pediatric patients presenting with acute lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs) across 417 continuous WHO epidemiological weeks (EpiWeek 1, 2017 to EpiWeek 52, 2024) were analyzed using decomposition and autocorrelation functions. Relationships between RSV and co-circulating viruses, meteorological variables, and holidays were assessed via cross-correlation and Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average with Exogenous variables (ARIMAX) modeling.

Results

A total of 6,545 (14.29%) samples were RSV-positive from a total of 45,817 tested. Historical peaks (July-September) were disrupted during 2020-2023 but re-established in 2024. The ARIMAX (2,0,4) (1,0,0)52 model revealed that RSV dynamics were driven primarily by internal autoregressive patterns rather than meteorological factors. Major public holidays exhibited a significant dual effect, with an immediate decrease in reported cases (p = 0.012) followed by a significant surge (p = 0.014). Influenza activity was a significant predictor with a one-week lag (p = 0.012).

Conclusion

The pandemic temporarily shifted RSV seasonality, which has since normalized. The associations with holiday periods and influenza activity suggests that behavioral factors and viral interference may influence RSV circulation. These findings emphasize the need for dynamic surveillance to optimize the timing of future RSV immunizations in Malaysia.

title: A Rare Coexistence of Coronary and Aortic Arch Anomalies in a Case of Complex Congenital Heart Disease and Their Clinical Impact.
authorString: Jain T, Singh R, Yadav N, Arumugam G.

journal.title: Heart views : the official journal of the Gulf Heart Association

abstractText: Coronary artery anomalies are uncommon in congenital heart disease (CHD), with left anterior descending (LAD) and left circumflex (LCx) variants being particularly rare and clinically relevant. Their coexistence with complex aortic arch anomalies is exceptional and poses major diagnostic and surgical challenges. We report a 19-year-old female with complex CHD post-Fontan surgery with worsening dyspnea. Computed tomography (CT) angiography demonstrated a patent Fontan circuit with separate origins of the right coronary artery (RCA), LAD, and LCx; anomalous anterior cusp origins of the RCA and LAD; a shepherd's crook course of the LAD; and a retroaortic LCx arising from the posterior cusp. An unreported aortic arch configuration consisting of truncus bicaroticus with aberrant right subclavian artery and segmental right common carotid artery agenesis was also identified. This case underscores the indispensable role of CT angiography in comprehensive anatomical delineation and procedural planning, as such anomalies, though incidental, substantially increase the risk of cannulation failure, surgical injury, and ischemic complications in surgically modified CHD.

title: Hyperuricemia and Gout: Ancient Ailments' Advanced Approaches (A Narrative Review).
authorString: Al Mahmood MR, Kashpya SS.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Clin Med Insights Arthritis Musculoskelet Disord
journal.title: Clinical medicine insights. Arthritis and musculoskeletal disorders
journal.isoabbreviation: Clin Med Insights Arthritis Musculoskelet Disord

abstractText: Hyperuricemia (HUA) and gout are evolving global health challenges, transitioning from localized joint pathologies to recognized systemic metabolic disorders. While traditionally associated with the appendicular skeleton, emerging evidence highlights a profound "extra-articular" burden affecting multiple organ systems. Although uric acid (UA) is often marked by its adverse effects, it exhibits significant physiological roles, including neuroprotective antioxidant properties. Comorbidities and systemic involvement are intertwined with HUA. Various factors contribute to the development of HUA, but there are options for reducing serum UA levels. The pathophysiology of HUA can be categorized into overproduction, underexcretion, and combined mechanisms, emphasizing that precision in subtyping is critical for optimizing pharmacological efficacy. Furthermore, this review analyzes the shifting paradigm in dietary management and the complexities of treating multi-system comorbidities related to HUA. We summarize the pathology and consequences of HUA and gout, alongside assessment strategies, investigations outline, differentials search, and evidence-based management protocols.

title: Dual Left Anterior Descending with Common Trunk of Dominant Left Anterior Descending and Acute Marginal Branch - A Rare Pattern.
authorString: Sharma A, Kaur G, Verma M, Singhal M.

journal.title: Heart views : the official journal of the Gulf Heart Association

title: Association of Peak Circulatory Power with Invasive Hemodynamic Severity in Pulmonary Hypertension.
authorString: Song Y, Shi C, Gu YL, Li M, Zhao MJ, Dou TT, Du L, Li RX, Feng X, Yan XX.
abstractText: Background: Peak circulatory power (CP), derived from peak oxygen uptake per kilogram (peak VO2/kg) and peak systolic blood pressure (SBP), has prognostic value in cardiovascular disease, but its association with invasive hemodynamic severity in pulmonary hypertension (PH) remains unclear. We examined the relationship between peak CP and mixed venous oxygen saturation (SvO2) and other hemodynamic markers in patients with PH. Methods: This retrospective cross-sectional study included 133 adults with confirmed PH who underwent cardiopulmonary exercise testing and right heart catheterization before targeted therapy. Linear regression adjusted for age and sex evaluated associations between peak CP and SvO2, pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR), mean pulmonary arterial pressure (mPAP), N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), and six-minute walk distance (6MWD). Exploratory receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis assessed the ability of peak CP to identify SvO2 ≤ 65%. Results: Median age was 33 years, and 62.4% were female. After adjustment for age and sex, lower peak CP was associated with lower SvO2 (B per 100-unit increase = 0.30, 95% CI: 0.10-0.50, p = 0.011), higher PVR (B = -0.20, 95% CI: -0.40 to -0.10, p = 0.001), higher mPAP (B = -0.70, 95% CI: -1.10 to -0.20, p = 0.003), higher NT-proBNP (B = -19.0, 95% CI: -30.9 to -7.0, p = 0.002), and shorter 6MWD (B = 2.40, 95% CI: 0.50-4.30, p = 0.015). Peak CP identified SvO2 ≤ 65% (15/133, 11.3%) with an AUC of 0.781 (95% CI: 0.674-0.888), similar to peak VO2/kg (AUC 0.783). Conclusions: In patients with PH not receiving targeted therapy, lower peak CP is age- and sex-adjusted associated with lower SvO2, higher PVR, higher mPAP, higher NT-proBNP, and shorter 6MWD, suggesting that peak CP reflects exercise cardiovascular reserve and hemodynamic severity. Thresholds and discriminatory estimates require prospective validation.

title: Recurrent Acute Liver Failure as the First Manifestation of <i>ARCN1</i>-Associated Disorder Caused by a Terminal Exon Frameshift Variant.
authorString: Shleptsova V, Nuzhnaya E, Taran N, Tatarsky E, Nikolaeva A, Sviridov P, Strokova T, Semenova N.
abstractText: Background: ARCN1-related syndrome (short stature-micrognathia syndrome, SSMG; OMIM #617164) is an autosomal dominant disorder caused by loss-of-function variants in the ARCN1 gene, which encodes the δ-COP (COPD) subunit of the COPI coatomer complex. The condition is classically characterized by intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR), short stature with rhizomelic shortening, microcephaly, micrognathia, facial dysmorphism, and global developmental delay. Methods: Clinical examination, blood tests and genetic analysis were performed. Whole-exome sequencing and Sanger analysis were conducted, followed by bioinformatics analysis and ACMG-based variant interpretation to identify and characterize the pathogenic variant. Results: We report a male proband with a previously undescribed variant in the ARCN1 gene, presenting with an atypical phenotype. Notably, the patient lacked the classical syndromic features, including short stature, microcephaly, IUGR, and developmental delay. The predominant clinical manifestation was transient hepatic dysfunction occurring during febrile episodes, which resolved between acute events. On physical examination, rhizomelic shortening and dysmorphic facial features, including mild micrognathia, were found. Overall, identified symptoms were mild in severity, which may be associated with the variant's location within the gene. Conclusions: We describe a novel likely pathogenic variant in the ARCN1 gene associated with a mild phenotype of SSMG. This case expands the phenotypic spectrum of ARCN1-related syndrome and highlights the importance of considering this diagnosis in patients with unexplained recurrent liver injury, even in the absence of classical syndromic features.

title: Kabuki Syndrome: Epigenetic Mechanisms, DNA Methylation Signatures, and Diagnostic Advances.
authorString: Zabudskaya K, Ryzhkova O.
abstractText: Kabuki syndrome (KS) is a rare multisystem developmental disorder characterized by distinctive facial features, developmental delay, hypotonia, and variable congenital anomalies. Most molecularly confirmed cases are associated with pathogenic variants in KMT2D (KS type 1) or KDM6A (KS type 2), genes encoding regulators of chromatin modification and gene expression. However, a subset of individuals with a clinical diagnosis of KS remains molecularly unresolved, while variants of uncertain significance may complicate diagnostic interpretation. DNA methylation episignatures have emerged as complementary molecular biomarkers that may support the interpretation of uncertain genetic findings and help clarify selected diagnostically unresolved cases. This review examines the molecular and epigenetic mechanisms underlying KS, summarizes the evidence for KS-associated DNA methylation episignatures, and discusses their potential applications in clinical diagnostics. Particular attention is given to the interpretation of episignature classifier results, the available evidence on diagnostic performance, and methodological limitations, including the representation of different variant classes and the interpretation of negative or inconclusive results. The review also considers genotype-phenotype correlations, genetic counseling, and clinical management in the context of current diagnostic approaches. Although episignature analysis may provide valuable functional evidence complementary to genetic testing, its results should be interpreted alongside clinical findings and molecular data. Further validation in well-characterized cohorts is needed to define its diagnostic utility across the full spectrum of KS-associated genetic variation.

title: Evaluation of antibiotic prescribing in dental practices in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania and a comparison with national and international prescribing practices - a retrospective look at the situation in 2015.
authorString: Tellez Sanz M, Hübner NO, Al-Nawas B, Kramer A.
abstractText:
Introduction

The aim of this study was to evaluate the antibiotic prescribing practices of dental practitioners and dental clinics in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania with regard to therapeutic and prophylactic indications, microbiological diagnostics, level of knowledge, and factors influencing prescribing behavior, to draw conclusions for antibiotic stewardship (ABS).

Method

The study was conducted as a cross-sectional survey and included all private dental practices which could be contacted via the Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania Dental Association, as well as university and hospital dental clinics. The questionnaire included sociodemographic data, therapeutic and prophylactic antibiotic prescriptions, selection of antibiotics, usage of microbiological diagnostics, knowledge levels, and factors influencing prescribing behavior. Data collection took place in 2015 via post.

Results

Of 1,470 dentists contacted, 533 took part in the survey (response rate 36.3%). The majority stated that they prescribed 1-3 antibiotics per week. Clindamycin was the most commonly used antibiotic for odontogenic abscesses, apical periodontitis, peri-implantitis and osteomyelitis, followed by amoxicillin. For acute necrotizing ulcerative periodontitis and acute necrotizing ulcerative gingivitis, metronidazole was the preferred choice, followed by amoxicillin and clindamycin. 58.1% of participants recommended antibiotic therapy for 5 days, 34.5% for 3-5 days, and 7.4% for 1-3 days. 71% of participants stated that they did not request microbiological testing prior to antibiotic therapy, and only 28.3% would order an antibiogram if the antibiotic had no effect.Personal experience and the current resistance profile were named as the most important factors influencing prescribing behavior. 91.2% of dentists were not influenced by patient expectations. For 71.5%, price was not a factor. There was a significant correlation between the number of years in practice and prescribing frequency, in which younger and more experienced dentists tending to be more cautious in their prescribing. 44.8% of respondents rated their knowledge of antibiotic stewardship (ABS) as satisfactory, 33.8% as good and 6.2% as very good. 90.0% of participants stated that their last training course on ABS had taken place 1-3 years ago. 91.9% would attend a training course (again).The indication for endocarditis prophylaxis was largely restricted to high-risk patients, whereas antibiotic prophylaxis in patients with large-joint prostheses was not limited to risk-based indications.

Discussion

The prescribing patterns did not align with current guidelines. The low usage of microbiological diagnostics indicates further room for improvement in the implementation of ABS.The importance of personal experience as a key influencing factor in antibiotic prescribing underscores the need to regularly organize targeted training initiatives to implement regional ABS programs.

Conclusion

The rational prescribing of antibiotics in dentistry is not merely a technical challenge in its own right, but part of global efforts to combat antibiotic resistance. Every prescribing decision should contribute to preserving efficacy for future generations. The key to responsible and sustainable antimicrobial therapy in dentistry lies in combining scientific evidence, clinical expertise, and an understanding of regional specificities.

title: The Chemical, Physical and Biological Hazards in Bee Products: A Comprehensive Review.
authorString: Makarewicz M, Drożdż I, Duda A.
abstractText: This review consolidates data on the most significant chemical, biological, and physical contaminants found in honey and other bee products that may have a negative impact on human health. It focuses on the various groups of compounds that affect the safety and quality of these bee products, such as pesticides, heavy metals, antibiotic residues, allergens, phytotoxins, 5-hydroxymethylfurfural, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, mycotoxins, and microplastics. The levels of these contaminants and the related hazard risk they pose are presented in one place. The sources of these contaminants, as well as the influence of various factors (e.g., geographic region, apiary location, nectar-producing plant species and measurement method) on their concentrations, are also discussed. The levels of contaminants reported in the literature were compared with current standards and regulations to determine the actual risk to consumer health by calculating the hazard quotient. A risk assessment matrix summarising the risk arising from different groups of contaminants in specific types of apicultural products and showing the possibility of cumulative exposure is provided. Gaps in the current state of knowledge and directions for future research were also identified.

title: Pilomatricoma in Turner Syndrome: Association with Renal Malformations and Analysis of the Vitamin D Pathway.
authorString: Barrientos R, Rodríguez-Jurado R, Torres Espíndola LM, Sáez-de-Ocariz M, Velázquez Aragón J, Pérez González Ó, Villarroel Cortés C, Rodríguez Morales M, Frías S, Velázquez Cruz R.
abstractText: Pilomatricoma is a rare benign cutaneous neoplasm that may occur more frequently in syndromic conditions such as Turner syndrome (TS). This study aimed to evaluate the prevalence and clinical characteristics of pilomatricoma and its association with clinical factors, serum vitamin D (VD) levels, and genetic variants in the VD pathway in patients with TS. Clinical variables and serum VD levels were obtained from medical records, and single-nucleotide variants in the GC, NADSYN1, and VDR genes were analyzed by allelic discrimination using real-time polymerase chain reaction. Among 97 patients with TS, six cases of histopathologically confirmed pilomatricoma were identified, corresponding to a prevalence of 6.2%, with lesions predominantly located on the head and upper extremities. Four patients (66.7%) had renal malformations. In exploratory multivariable analysis, renal malformations were significantly associated with pilomatricoma (adjusted OR = 14.2; 95% CI: 2.1-95.4; nominal p = 0.008; FDR-adjusted p = 0.032). No significant associations were observed with serum VD levels or the analyzed genetic variants. These findings suggest that pilomatricoma may be more frequent in TS than previously reported and identify an exploratory association between pilomatricoma and renal malformations. Given the small number of pilomatricoma cases, this association requires confirmation in larger independent cohorts.

title: Food Folate Quality: Linking Dietary Sources, Bioavailability, and Human Health.
authorString: Wang CC, Lin BF, Hsieh CC.
abstractText: Food folate concentrations do not necessarily predict the amount available for human metabolism. This narrative review summarizes how dietary sources, analytical methods, and digestive processes influence interpretations of food folate quality. Literature was identified through PubMed using searches covering 2000-2026, selecting studies relevant to food sources, measurement, bioavailability, and human health. We propose a framework linking food folate, analytical reliability, bioaccessibility, absorption, and biological efficacy. Major sources include leafy vegetables, legumes, fruits, grains, and liver, but folate content varies with food type, origin, and processing. Natural food folates require matrix release and polyglutamate hydrolysis before absorption, limiting comparisons based on concentration alone. Adequate folate intake is closely linked to reduced risks of folate-deficiency anemia and fetal neural-tube defects, and some studies have investigated its role in regulating cardiovascular, cognitive, metabolic, immune, and cancer-related effects. Adverse effects of high folic acid exposure depend on dose, vitamin B<sub>12</sub> status, and study design; the role of circulating unmetabolized folic acid remains uncertain. Overall, a diverse diet rich in natural folate supports nutritional adequacy, while targeted fortification and supplementation need to avoid excessive exposure. Evaluating food folate quality requires both accurate measurements and evidence of bioavailability.

title: Recognizing Declining Right Ventricular Reserve in Pediatric Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension: A Clinical Framework for Discordant Multimodal Findings.
authorString: Zheng X, Hua Y, Zhou K.
abstractText: Right ventricular (RV) failure is a major determinant of clinical deterioration in pediatric pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), yet loss of RV reserve is difficult to recognize before overt low-output failure. Pulmonary artery pressure may remain stable or fall as RV pressure-generating capacity declines. Other commonly followed variables may also diverge: tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion can remain preserved despite worsening RV free-wall strain or cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR)-derived ejection fraction; natriuretic peptides may rise before conventional echocardiographic changes; and symptoms may deteriorate while estimated pressure appears unchanged. This focused narrative review integrates pediatric evidence with selected physiologic data to examine the interpretation of such discordance. We distinguish three clinical states-maintained adaptation, suspected loss of reserve, and overt decompensation-without proposing a new risk score. Assessment is organized around the clinical question left unanswered after the initial review. Signal quality and serial comparability are checked first, followed by transient modifiers of loading conditions and biomarker concentration. CMR helps resolve uncertainty about RV volume or global function, whereas right-heart catheterization directly defines pulmonary vascular load, filling pressure, and forward output when these measurements will affect management. Direct pediatric evidence supports serial assessment of RV and right atrial remodeling, myocardial deformation, CMR-derived function, natriuretic peptide trajectories, right atrial pressure, cardiac index, and mixed venous oxygen saturation, but no isolated variable has been validated as an independent treatment threshold. Concordance, direction, and rate of change across domains may improve recognition of declining RV reserve while limiting escalation driven by measurement noise.

title: Copper Deficiency and Other Micronutrient Deficiencies During Prolonged Jejunal Versus Gastric Enteral Nutrition in Children.
authorString: Raya-Muñoz J, Martinez BMDC, Bermejo MF, Álvarez-Beltrán M, Cabello-Ruiz V, Redecillas-Ferreiro S, Segarra-Cantón O.
abstractText: Background/Objectives: Copper deficiency is described in adults on prolonged jejunal enteral nutrition, but paediatric evidence remains scarce. We compared the prevalence, timing and consequences of copper and other micronutrient deficiencies in children on prolonged jejunal versus gastric enteral nutrition. Methods: Ambispective observational cohort study at a tertiary paediatric centre. Children aged 0-18 years receiving at least 80% of their nutritional requirements through an enteral device for more than three months were studied; pre-existing malabsorption was an exclusion criterion. Groups were defined by feeding route (jejunal or gastric). Serum copper, zinc, iron and selenium were assessed longitudinally, with concurrent C-reactive protein < 2 mg/dL. Results: Forty-six patients were included (jejunal, 31; gastric, 15). Copper deficiency occurred in 9 of 31 jejunal patients (29.0%) and in no gastric patient (risk difference 29.0%, 95% CI 4.9-46.6%; p = 0.021). Iron deficiency was the commonest abnormality (71% versus 60%; p = 0.51). Six of the nine copper-deficient children developed anaemia or neutropenia; all normalised after oral copper sulfate given through the gastric route. Conclusions: In this single-centre cohort, prolonged jejunal feeding was associated with more frequent copper deficiency despite adequate intake; larger studies should confirm this. We suggest monitoring serum copper from three months after post-pyloric feeding starts.

title: Transitional Fetal Circulation: A Comprehensive Review of Physiological Adaptation, Failure, and Neonatal Outcomes.
authorString: Moravineni UR.
abstractText: The change from fetal to neonatal circulation is one of the most rapid and consequential physiological reorganizations in human life, and it is more accurately described as an integrated cardiopulmonary and placental sequence than as simple closure of fetal shunts. Before birth, the placenta is the organ of gas exchange, pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) is high, and the ductus venosus, foramen ovale, and ductus arteriosus sustain a parallel circulation that preferentially directs relatively oxygenated umbilical venous blood to the myocardium and brain. At birth, lung aeration, clearance of fetal lung liquid, a rise in alveolar and arterial oxygen tension, and mechanical recruitment of the pulmonary microvasculature produce a steep fall in PVR and a several-fold increase in pulmonary blood flow. Pulmonary venous return then replaces umbilical venous return as the dominant source of left ventricular preload, while interruption of the low-resistance placental circuit raises systemic vascular resistance (SVR) and left ventricular afterload. These pressure and flow changes, rather than any intrinsic anatomical event, drive functional closure of the foramen ovale and progressive constriction of the ductus arteriosus. Failure or delay of this coordinated sequence produces a spectrum of hemodynamic disorders: persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn (PPHN), myocardial dysfunction, inadequate preload, hemodynamically significant patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) in the preterm infant, and decompensation of previously unrecognized duct-dependent congenital heart disease. The mechanisms include incomplete alveolar recruitment, hypoxemia, acidosis, inflammation, impaired nitric oxide (NO)-soluble guanylate cyclase (sGC)-cyclic guanosine monophosphate (cGMP) signaling, excess endothelin-1 and Rho-kinase activity, oxidative stress, ventricular maladaptation, and adverse ventriculo-ventricular interaction. Because hypoxemia, hypotension, acidosis, and poor perfusion are shared surface features of mechanistically distinct states, assessment based on blood pressure or oxygen saturation alone is inadequate. This review synthesizes fetal circulatory physiology, the molecular and mechanical basis of normal transition, the principal failed-transition phenotypes, and contemporary physiology-guided monitoring and management. It integrates recent evidence on deferred and physiology-based cord clamping, including the 2023 individual participant data meta-analysis of preterm cord management and the 2024 ABC3 randomized trial; the 2024 American Society of Echocardiography update on targeted neonatal echocardiography; the 2025 American Heart Association and American Academy of Pediatrics neonatal resuscitation guidelines; randomized and network meta-analytic evidence on PPHN pharmacotherapy; and the shift from routine early PDA closure to selective, phenotype-based management. A mechanistic understanding of transitional circulation allows earlier recognition of neonatal cardiovascular compromise and discourages the indiscriminate treatment of numerical hypoxemia or hypotension.

title: Neonate With Hydrops Fetalis, Chylothorax, and an FLT4 Variant: A Favorable Outcome.
authorString: Rustom H, Koiala S, Al-Janabi F, Wolf L, Nanda VC.
abstractText: Congenital chylothorax is the most common cause of pleural effusion in newborns and may progress to nonimmune hydrops fetalis (NIHF). FLT4 encodes vascular endothelial growth factor receptor 3 (VEGFR-3), a receptor tyrosine kinase critical for lymphangiogenesis; pathogenic variants can impair VEGFR-3 signaling and disrupt lymphatic development. Although FLT4 has been implicated in congenital chylothorax, favorable postnatal outcomes with conservative management alone have not been well described. We present the case of a male infant born at 34 + 1 weeks' gestation with prenatal hydrops fetalis, polyhydramnios, ascites, and bilateral pleural effusions. Chest tubes drained fluid with triglycerides reaching 625 mg/dL after feeds were initiated, consistent with chylothorax. Infectious, metabolic, immune-mediated, and anatomic evaluations were unremarkable. Trio whole-exome sequencing revealed a maternally inherited heterozygous FLT4 c.3824G>T (p.Ser1275Ile) substitution, classified as a variant of uncertain significance. Several features suggest possible clinical significance, including absence from population databases, damaging in silico predictions, location within the tyrosine kinase domain, and prior reports of the same variant presenting with severe prenatal lymphatic disease. The mother carried the same heterozygous variant with no known history of lymphedema or peripheral edema, consistent with incomplete penetrance. After approximately six weeks on medium-chain triglyceride formula, the chylothorax resolved, and the infant was transitioned to breast milk and discharged on day of life 75 on room air without dietary restrictions. This case suggests that a favorable neonatal outcome may be achievable with conservative management in certain neonates with NIHF and congenital chylothorax harboring FLT4 variants, pending further genotype-phenotype characterization.

title: Surgical Ventricular Restoration With the Dor Procedure for Anterior Left Ventricular Aneurysm and Suspected Rupture: A Case Report.
authorString: Seretakis G, Stanitsa N, Tempelis E, Samiotis I, Gissis I, Dedeilias P, Kokotsakis J.
abstractText: Surgical ventricular restoration (SVR) using the Dor procedure has become uncommon in the era of early myocardial revascularization and optimized medical therapy. However, in carefully selected patients with advanced left ventricular (LV) remodeling or suspected ventricular rupture, SVR remains a critical surgical option. We report the case of a 55-year-old who presented with chest pain and progressive dyspnea one month after an untreated myocardial infarction. Imaging revealed a large anterior LV aneurysm with features suggestive of a contained rupture. Despite revascularization of the left anterior descending (LAD) artery, the patient developed hypotension requiring inotropic support and underwent urgent SVR using the Dor procedure. Intraoperative findings confirmed extensive dyskinetic myocardium, a large laminated thrombus, and a sealed rupture of the apical wall. The thrombus was evacuated and the dyskinetic segment excluded using a tailored Dacron patch. The postoperative course was uneventful. At the latest follow-up, 22 months after surgery, the patient remained clinically stable, with a left ventricular ejection fraction above 30% and no arrhythmic events; however, apical dyskinesia with aneurysmal dilation had reappeared, indicating that remodeling may continue after SVR. This report highlights that the Dor procedure remains a valuable and potentially life-saving intervention in selected patients with post-infarction LV aneurysms complicated by suspected rupture, particularly when timely diagnosis and surgical intervention are achieved.

title: Oocyte lipid damage from maternal ageing marks neurodevelopment in mouse offspring.
authorString: Gulzar H, Musson R, Depciuch J, Gąsior Ł, Bisogno S, Sarna M, Heber MF, Skałka J, Molina DA, Kiełbus M, Bodzon-Kulakowska A, Suder P, Alluhaibi L, Maximenko A, Ptak GE.
abstractText:
Study question

Is advanced maternal age (AMA) associated with lipid dysregulation in oocytes that correlates with the intergenerational persistence of altered lipid homeostasis and neurodevelopmental pathway signatures in downstream offspring?

Summary answer

Lipid profile alterations characterized in AMA oocytes are associated with distinct lipidomic and spectral variations in the foetal brain and yolk sac, displaying intergenerational persistence that extends up to the fourth generation (F4), independently of the gestational uterine environment.

What is known already

AMA is a recognized prenatal risk factor for neurodevelopmental conditions in offspring. However, whether early-life oocyte lipid variations correlate with altered lipid profiles and molecular signatures in the developing brains of subsequent generations remain uncharacterized.

Study design size duration

This controlled animal model study compared oocytes, blastocysts, and foetuses from AMA mice (8-16 months old) to those from young maternal age (YMA, 3-4 months old) controls and featured an embryo transfer (ET) of AMA blastocysts into young surrogates and longitudinal, lineage-specific tracking up to the F4.

Participants/materials setting methods

Complementary approaches, including liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) proteomics and lipidomics, Matrix-Assisted Laser Desorption/Ionization-Tandem Time-of-Flight mass spectrometry (MALDI-TOF/TOF MS), RNA sequencing, atomic force microscopy, Coherent Anti-Stokes Raman Scattering (CARS) chemical imaging microscopy, Raman and Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopies, and histology were conducted on single oocytes, blastocysts, and foetal structures (brain and yolk sac) from AMA and YMA mice. ET was utilized to decouple the oocyte-derived phenotype from the effects of an ageing maternal uterine environment.

Main results and the role of chance

AMA oocytes and preimplantation blastocysts exhibited significant lipid droplet and lipid membrane alterations, a higher relative absorbance of intracellular lipid bands, and altered expression of lipid-regulatory transcripts, corresponding to early embryonic pathway shifts. Following the ET of AMA blastocysts to young surrogates (ET AMA group), distinct lipidomic variations and structural alterations were observed in the F1 yolk sac and foetal brains. Furthermore, these lipid-associated spectral and molecular signatures displayed intergenerational persistence, tracking through the yolk sac, brain, and oocytes of the third- (F3) and fourth-generation (F4) descendants derived from the oocyte of AMA progenitors.

Large scale data

The transcriptomic data have been deposited in the NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) under accession number GSE349634. Processed transcriptomic, lipidomic, and proteomic datasets, together with the shared transcript-protein analysis, have been deposited in RODBUK under DOI https://doi.org/10.57903/UJ/LVQ7FU. All datasets are publicly available.

Limitations reasons for caution

This study was conducted exclusively in a mouse model. Given species-specific variations in baseline oocyte lipid content and developmental kinetics, these findings require cautious interpretation before extrapolation to human clinical contexts. Additionally, the exact molecular and epigenetic mechanisms underlying the intergenerational persistence of these lipid signatures warrant further characterization.

Wider implications of the findings

These findings demonstrate an association between early-life oocyte lipid changes and downstream pathway-level molecular signatures of neurodevelopmental alterations. By establishing an intergenerational pathway that persists independently of the maternal uterine environment, this work introduces a novel framework linking metabolic programming at conception to neurodevelopmental outcomes, offering new directions for reproductive medicine and translational neuroscience.

Funding

This research was funded by National Science Centre of Poland Grants 2021/41/B/NZ3/03507 and 2019/35/B/NZ4/03547 (to G.E.P.), 2022/44/C/NZ4/00076 (to M.F.H.), and 2019/35/N/NZ3/03213 (to Ł.G.), and the program 'Excellence initiative-research university' for the AGH University of Krakow (A.B.-K.). Proteomics was supported by the subsidy no 16.16.160.557 of the Polish Ministry of Science and Higher Education (to P.S.). Raman analysis at the National Synchrotron Radiation Centre SOLARIS was supported by the Ministry of Science and Higher Education, Poland, under contract no. 1/SOL/2021/2.

Disclosures

The authors declare no competing interests.

title: Polycythemia vera and JAK2 unmutated erythrocytosis: Overview of updates in diagnosis and management from 2026.
authorString: Georgiou M, Curto-Garcia N, Sriskandarajah P.
abstractText: Polycythemia vera (PV) is a JAK2-mutated myeloproliferative neoplasm characterized by clonal erythrocytosis. Patients can often present with significant symptoms as well as thrombotic events. There have been significant developments in terms of risk stratifying this condition, particularly in the era of next generation sequencing, as well as development of novel therapies. This is a narrative review article that gives an update on these recent changes, as well as an overview of the management of JAK2 unmutated erythrocytosis.

title: From Incidental Cardiomegaly to a Rare Right Coronary Artery-to-Coronary Sinus Fistula: Unravelling the Cause of Left Ventricular Dilatation.
authorString: Abdelkader AH, Raslan M, Elhaw A.
abstractText: We present the case of an asymptomatic 68-year-old woman in whom mild cardiomegaly identified incidentally on chest radiography initiated a stepwise investigation for otherwise unexplained left ventricular dilatation. Transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated mild left ventricular dilatation with preserved systolic function, a markedly dilated right coronary artery, a prominent coronary sinus, and abnormal continuous left-to-right flow. However, the anatomical origin of the suspected shunt remained uncertain. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging showed borderline increased left ventricular end-diastolic volume with preserved systolic function and a pulmonary-to-systemic flow ratio (Qp: Qs) of 1.7:1, confirming a haemodynamically relevant left-to-right shunt but failing to identify its anatomical source. Persistent investigation with cardiac computed tomography angiography ultimately demonstrated a markedly dilated and tortuous dominant right coronary artery draining through a narrow aperture into a dilated coronary sinus, establishing the diagnosis of a right coronary artery-to-coronary sinus fistula. Despite the shunt and mild left ventricular dilatation, the patient remained asymptomatic with preserved biventricular function and no evidence of myocardial fibrosis or ischaemia. Following specialist congenital cardiac multidisciplinary review, conservative management with interval imaging surveillance was recommended. This rare case highlights the importance of pursuing the underlying cause of otherwise unexplained cardiac chamber dilatation. It demonstrates the complementary roles of multimodality cardiovascular imaging when the physiological significance of a shunt is apparent, but its anatomical source remains uncertain.

title: Effects of Intravenous Dexamethasone on IL-6 Levels in Children Undergoing Cardiac Surgery With Cardiopulmonary Bypass.
authorString: Al-Mahmud M, Das RS, Yeasmeen S, Saha SK, Saha P, Ahmad MA, Prima TA, Meena A, Suravi AS, Rahman MM.
abstractText:
Background

Cardiopulmonary bypass provokes a systemic inflammatory response in children, with interleukin-6 (IL-6) levels rising rapidly after bypass. Corticosteroids are frequently used to blunt this response, but paediatric evidence remains inconsistent.

Objective

To evaluate whether a single intravenous dose of dexamethasone reduces the post-bypass increase in plasma IL-6 and improves early postoperative outcomes in children undergoing cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass.

Methods

This single-centre quasi-experimental study enrolled 46 children aged one month to 12 years undergoing elective repair of congenital heart disease between January 2025 and August 2025. Participants were purposively recruited and alternately allocated to intravenous dexamethasone (1 mg/kg, maximum 10 mg; n=23, 50.0%) or 2 mL normal saline (n=23, 50.0%) after induction of anaesthesia. Plasma IL-6 was measured before drug administration, two hours after cardiopulmonary bypass, and 24 hours after bypass. Haemodynamic variables, oxygen saturation, extubation time, and intensive care unit stay were recorded.

Results

The median IL-6 increase from baseline to two hours was lower with dexamethasone than with saline (261.90 pg/mL, interquartile range: 195.0-824.0, versus 447.0 pg/mL, interquartile range: 261.70-1,230.20), but the difference was not statistically significant (p=0.177). At 24 hours, the median change from baseline was 8.20 pg/mL in the dexamethasone group and 13.0 pg/mL in the saline group (p=0.350). Blood pressure, oxygen saturation, and extubation time were comparable. First-postoperative-day heart rate was higher with dexamethasone (143.63 ± 18.93 versus 117.76 ± 19.57 beats/min; p=0.001), and median intensive care unit stay was longer (120 versus 95.5 hours; p=0.001).

Conclusions

A single dose of intravenous dexamethasone at 1 mg/kg, capped at 10 mg, did not significantly attenuate the IL-6 response after paediatric cardiopulmonary bypass. The higher heart rate and longer intensive care stay observed in the dexamethasone group should be treated as exploratory because allocation was nonrandom and perioperative complexity was not adjusted for.

title: From Prevalence to Prediction: A Cross-Sectional Study to Develop a Novel Risk Score for Hearing Loss in High-Risk Neonates in South India.
authorString: Sachithanandam ST, Baskaradass R.
abstractText:
Background and aim

Neonates admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) with multiple risk factors are more likely to develop hearing loss. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of hearing loss, identify its predictive factors, and develop a novel clinical risk score for hearing loss among high-risk neonates.

Materials and methods

This cross-sectional study included 105 high-risk neonates admitted to the NICU from July 2024 to June 2025. The hearing assessment protocol included transient-evoked otoacoustic emissions at discharge and at six weeks of corrected age, followed by diagnostic brainstem-evoked response audiometry at three months. Associations between risk factors and hearing loss were analyzed using logistic regression. A novel clinical risk score was developed using the factors significantly associated with hearing loss.

Results

The prevalence of hearing loss among high-risk neonates was 4.8% (95% CI, 1.6%-10.8%). Hearing loss was significantly associated with intrauterine toxoplasmosis, perinatal asphyxia, neonatal hyperbilirubinemia (NNH) requiring exchange transfusion, stage II or higher hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy, neonatal sepsis, neonatal seizures, syndromic or craniofacial anomalies, and ototoxic drug exposure (p < 0.05). The clinical risk prediction model, developed using significant predictive factors and assigning double weight to intrauterine toxoplasmosis and NNH requiring exchange transfusion, achieved a sensitivity of 60% and a specificity of 96% at a cutoff score of ≥3.

Conclusions

The prevalence of hearing loss among high-risk neonates was 4.8%. The novel clinical risk score developed in this study may help guide targeted screening, timely diagnosis, and early intervention for hearing loss.

title: Severe Bacterial Infections and Sepsis in Children and Adolescents in São Paulo, Brazil: A Population-Based Time-Trend Study, 2015-2025.
authorString: Lima ALB, Martins JS, Carvalho IR, Manara CDS, Rodrigues SB, Almeida JP, Marins MM, Florence PZ, Fernandes AC.
abstractText:
Background

Severe bacterial infections and sepsis are leading causes of pediatric hospitalization and death worldwide, yet recent Brazilian population-based data spanning the COVID-19 pandemic and distinguishing severe bacterial infection broadly from strict septicemia remain scarce.

Objectives

To describe hospitalization trends, mortality, and factors associated with in-hospital death among children and adolescents with severe bacterial infections and sepsis in São Paulo State, Brazil, from 2015 to 2025, comparing the broad cohort with a strict-sepsis subgroup.

Methods

Population-based, repeated cross-sectional study in São Paulo State, Brazil, 2015-2025, using Hospital Information System of the Brazilian Unified Health System (Sistema de Informações Hospitalares do Sistema Único de Saúde, SIH/SUS) records for hospital admissions of individuals aged 28 days to 19 years. The primary exposure was age group (infant, preschool-age, school-age, adolescent); the primary outcome was in-hospital death. Poisson regression estimated the annual trend in the number of admissions. Crude relative risks (RR) were calculated directly from contingency data; adjusted RR (aRR) were obtained by predictive marginal standardization from a multivariable logistic model, with modified Poisson regression (robust variance) as a sensitivity analysis.

Results

Among 553,218 hospitalizations (277,644; 50.2% male), overall case fatality was 1.6% (8765 deaths). Compared with infants (case fatality 1.8%; 3038/170,495), adolescents had over double the risk of death (crude RR 2.16, 95% CI 2.06-2.27), while preschool-age (RR 0.47, 95% CI 0.44-0.50) and school-age children (RR 0.59, 95% CI 0.54-0.63) had lower risk. Male sex carried modestly higher risk (RR 1.16, 95% CI 1.11-1.21), and comorbidity (49,952; 9.0% of admissions) more than tripled risk (RR 3.22, 95% CI 3.07-3.38). The number of admissions declined over the study period (Poisson regression trend ratio 0.96 per year, 95% CI 0.96-0.97), with a pronounced, non-linear drop during the pandemic and partial recovery thereafter. The strict-sepsis subgroup comprised 27,181 admissions (4.9% of the cohort) but had a case fatality of 14.7% (3985 deaths), nine times that of the broad cohort.

Conclusions

Severe bacterial infections impose a substantial, age-concentrated hospital burden among Brazilian children, while strict sepsis, though comparatively uncommon, remains markedly lethal. Distinguishing these entities is important for surveillance and resource planning.

title: Morphometric Study of the Mitral and Tricuspid Annuli in Fresh Cadaveric Human Hearts From Uttar Pradesh, India.
authorString: L K K, Chopra J, Rai A, Rani A, Verma A, Singh H.
abstractText:
Background

Accurate knowledge of mitral and tricuspid annular morphometry is fundamental to the planning of valve repair, annuloplasty, and transcatheter interventions. Population- and ethnicity-specific reference data remain limited for fresh human hearts in Uttar Pradesh.

Objective

This study aims to determine the anteroposterior and transverse diameters of the mitral and tricuspid valve annuli in fresh human cadaveric hearts of the North Indian population and to compare these findings with existing anatomical and echocardiographic literature.

Methods

This cross-sectional analytical study was conducted on 100 fresh human cadaveric hearts. The right atrium and left atrium were opened along standard anatomical planes to expose the tricuspid and mitral annuli, respectively. The anteroposterior and transverse diameters of both annuli were measured using a digital vernier caliper.

Results

The mean anteroposterior and transverse annular diameters of the mitral valve were 2.7 ± 0.4 cm and 2.9 ± 0.3 cm, respectively. The mean anteroposterior and transverse annular diameters of the tricuspid valve were 3.1 ± 0.3 cm and 3.3 ± 0.4 cm, respectively. the mean area of the mitral valve orifice was 6.19 ± 1.34 cm², while that of the tricuspid valve orifice was 8.07 ± 1.70 cm².

Conclusion

 This study provides descriptive anatomical reference data for mitral and tricuspid annular dimensions in fresh human cadaveric hearts from the Uttar Pradesh population.

title: Processed Electroencephalography-Guided Total Intravenous Anesthesia in a Malignant Hyperthermia-Susceptible Child Undergoing Ventricular Septal Defect Repair: A Case Report.
authorString: Was A, Narayan M, Decker J, Sood V.
abstractText: Malignant hyperthermia (MH) is a rare, life-threatening reaction to certain anesthetic medications that can occur during surgery. Managing an MH-susceptible child for congenital cardiac surgery is particularly challenging: cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB), with its attendant hypothermia and subsequent rewarming, can obscure the early signs of an MH crisis. Total intravenous anesthesia (TIVA) is utilized for MH-susceptible patients, but titrating anesthetic depth during CPB can be complicated, and processed electroencephalography (pEEG) has been studied sparingly in the pediatric cardiac population. We describe the anesthetic management of a two-year-old, 10.4-kg child with a likely pathogenic variant in the ryanodine receptor 1 (RYR1) gene who underwent ventricular septal defect (VSD) repair with CPB. A trigger-free environment was established, general anesthesia was maintained with a propofol-based TIVA technique, and anesthetic depth was monitored with a SedLine® brain function monitor (Masimo Corporation, Irvine, USA), using the raw electroencephalogram (EEG), spectral edge frequency 95 (SEF95), and density spectral array (DSA). The intraoperative course was uneventful, and no features of MH developed. This case illustrates the feasibility of pEEG-guided TIVA in an MH-susceptible child undergoing congenital cardiac surgery with CPB, and the value of interpreting the spectral display rather than a single index value during hypothermia and rewarming.

title: Characteristics of pediatric central venous catheter malfunction and subsequent catheter-related deep vein thrombosis.
authorString: Bala NS, Boulil Z, Krava E, Witmer C, O'Brien SH, Ji L, Young G, Jaffray J.

journal.title: Research and practice in thrombosis and haemostasis

abstractText:
Background

Central venous catheters (CVCs) are increasingly placed in children; however, malfunction and deep vein thrombosis (DVT) are reasons for frequent removal.

Objectives

The objective of this study was to evaluate variables associated with CVC malfunction and, subsequently, the development of CVC-related DVT (CR-DVT).

Methods

This subanalysis of the multicenter, prospective Clot Incidence Rates in Central Lines study enrolled children aged 6 months to <18 years with newly placed peripherally inserted central catheters or tunneled lines from 2013 to 2018. Time from CVC placement to first malfunction was analyzed in the full cohort using univariable and multivariable Weibull regression. Among CVCs that malfunctioned, time from first malfunction to CR-DVT was analyzed to assess tissue plasminogen activator (t-PA) use and subsequent thrombosis.

Results

Malfunction occurred in 380/1951 CVCs (19.5%). In multivariable analysis, prior CVC use (hazard ratio [HR], 1.51; 95% CI, 1.19-1.90; P = .001), multilumen catheters (HR, 2.89; 95% CI, 2.30-3.65; P < .001), and >2 insertion attempts (HR, 2.21; 95% CI, 1.42-3.45; P < .001) were associated with a higher risk of malfunction, whereas catheter size >4 French and interventional radiology placement were associated with a lower risk. Among malfunctioning CVCs, 22/380 (5.8%) developed CR-DVT, with a median time to CR-DVT of 6 days after malfunction. Increasing t-PA use showed a nonsignificant trend toward higher subsequent CR-DVT.

Conclusion

CVC malfunction is common and associated with several modifiable catheter-related factors. Six percent of malfunctioning CVCs develop CR-DVT, and repeated t-PA use and persistent CVC dysfunction may warrant further evaluation for underlying thrombosis.

title: Epidemiology of urinary <i>Escherichia coli</i> from a population-based surveillance in three U.S. counties, August 2023.
authorString: Brandenburg JM, Curtis L, Raymond RE, Ansari U, Campbell DE, Gargis AS, Kent AG, McKay SL, Parker EC, Longson R, Smith G, Jacob JT, Rebolledo PA, Dumyati G, Looi HC, Tellerman J, Guh AY, Grome HN.
abstractText: Population-based surveillance of urinary Escherichia coli was conducted in three U.S. counties. Findings included high incidence among females and older adults, resistance to recommended urinary tract infection treatments, and O serotypes common among invasive disease. The study emphasizes the value of understanding the epidemiology and resistance profiles to guide treatment.

title: Time is Brain: A Nurse-Informed Multicenter Analysis of Hospital-Based Mechanical Thrombectomy Pathway Efficiency (HASTE).
authorString: Remington GM, Nadimpalli G, Rolli M, Roderman N, Cain R, Pieprzyca S, Philpot D, Wiggins E, Jauch EC, Arnold-Egloff S.
abstractText:
Background

Swift response and successful reperfusion are major determinants of outcome in acute ischemic stroke due to large vessel occlusion. Quality initiatives in stroke care have shown that organized, protocol-driven practice can shorten treatment times and improve safety-sensitive clinical outcomes, yet thrombectomy workflow variation persists across health systems, and few studies have translated workflow findings into operational recommendations.

Methods

This retrospective, multicenter study evaluated mechanical thrombectomy workflow performance across 16 facilities in a large United States health system from August 2020 through December 2021. Elastic net regularization was applied to patient-level characteristics to generate residual durations for door-to-imaging, door-to-puncture, imaging-to-puncture, puncture-to-reperfusion, and door-to-reperfusion times. Residual durations were evaluated using iterative multivariable linear regression to identify facility-level workflow indicators associated with shorter times while adjusting for confounders. Statistically significant indicators were reviewed by a multidisciplinary HASTE (Hospital-bAsed Protocol to Standardize ThrombEctomy) Working Group and translated into evidence-informed preferred practices.

Results

Workflow indicators associated with faster reperfusion were identified and organized into 3 domains: people, process, and technology. Prominent findings included clearly defined team roles and responsibility, standardized workflow protocols and preparation, direct communication, and remote neuro-imaging review. Direct-admit patients had a median door-to-reperfusion time of 127 minutes (interquartile range [IQR], 96-166), whereas interfacility-transfer patients had a median door-to-reperfusion time of 73 minutes (IQR, 53-116). Patients treated at facilities reporting a standardized mechanical thrombectomy protocol demonstrated shorter median door-to-reperfusion times for both direct-admit patients (111 vs 148 minutes) and interfacility-transfer patients (66 vs 87 minutes).

Conclusion

Across 16 facilities, faster reperfusion was associated with workflow characteristics involving role clarity, direct communication, standardized preparation, and technology-enabled imaging review. Multidisciplinary interpretation of these findings informed real-world translation of care pathway tactics to improve thrombectomy pathway reliability and efficiency.

title: A Sequential Treatment of Keloids: Multiple-Hole Punch Excision Combined With Superficial Radiation and Drug.
authorString: Gong Z, Jing W, Zhang Z, Rao W, Lei W, Yang J, Ai Y, Tao X.
abstractText:
Background

Dense and multiple keloids present significant therapeutic challenges due to their stubborn nature and high recurrence rates. Although various treatment options exist, optimizing current approaches and integrating them into a rational, systematic regimen for keloid management remains a difficult clinical problem.

Aims

This study aims to establish an effective multimodal sequential treatment protocol for patients with dense, multiple keloids.

Methods

A total of 87 patients with 285 keloid lesions were enrolled from September 2023 to April 2024. All cases underwent a sequential treatment: Stage I involved drug-assisted multiple-hole punch excision followed by adjuvant superficial radiotherapy; Stage II consisted of periodic intralesional injections of betamethasone and 5-fluorouracil. Clinical outcomes, recurrence, and adverse events were evaluated at 12-month follow-up. The POSAS and VSS scores were recorded at each time point.

Results

At 12 months post-treatment, marked improvement was achieved in 78 patients (89.66%), with improvement in 7 (8.04%) and ineffective results in 2 (2.30%). The POSAS and VSS scores were recorded before treatment and at follow-up points at 30, 60, 90, 180, and 360 days. All patients developed varying degrees of local hyperpigmentation within 2 months after Stage I of multi-hole punch excision. In 80.75% of cases, the hyperpigmentation resolved within 3 months following Stage I, with the longest duration of resolution being 12 months. During Stage I, four cases of localized ulcers and five instances of acute radiation dermatitis appeared. All adverse reactions were effectively alleviated. No other adverse reactions occurred.

Conclusion

This sequential treatment protocol offers a practical, minimally invasive, and effective option for patients with multiple, dense keloids.

title: Factors influencing prognostic outcomes in children on noninvasive continuous positive airway pressure ventilation: A retrospective study.
authorString: Huo P, Liang M, Cui Y, Liu J, Ji L.
abstractText:
Objective

To investigate factors influencing prognostic outcomes in children receiving non-invasive continuous positive airway pressure (nCPAP) ventilation.

Methodology

Clinical data of 158 children who received nasal nCPAP at Hebei Children's Hospital from February 2023 to May 2024 were retrospectively analyzed. During 72 hours of treatment, the patients were divided into a favorable-prognosis group (112 cases) and a poor-prognosis group (46 cases). Logistic regression was used to identify risk factors for poor prognosis. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was used to evaluate the predictive value of the identified factors.

Results

Of the 158 children, 112 (70.9%) had a favorable prognosis and 46 (29.1%) had a poor prognosis. Significant between-group differences were observed in age and underlying diseases (P < 0.05). A decreased P/F ratio, elevated PCT, higher initial CPAP pressure, higher initial FiO2, and vasoactive drug administration were independently associated with poor prognosis (P < 0.05). The respective AUCs of these factors were 0.944, 0.820, 0.850, 0.868, and 0.594.

Conclusion

A decreased P/F ratio, elevated PCT, higher initial CPAP pressure, higher initial FiO2, and vasoactive drug administration were independently associated with poor prognosis in children receiving nCPAP.

title: Comparison of short-term myocardial perfusion and clinical outcomes between balloon stent kissing technique and junctional wire technique strategies in true bifurcation lesions of the left anterior descending artery and diagonal branch.
authorString: Ren K, Wang H, Li X.
abstractText:
Objectives

To compare procedural, clinical, and myocardial perfusion outcomes associated with the Balloon Stent Kissing Technique (BSKT) and Junctional Wire Technique (JWT) in patients with true bifurcation lesions of the left anterior descending artery (LAD) and diagonal branch.

Methodology

A retrospective analysis included data from 235 patients who underwent treatment of true bifurcation lesions of the coronary LAD and diagonal branch at Tianjin University Chest Hospital, China; between February 2023 to October 2024. All patients were followed up for one year. Based on the technique, patients were divided into the BSKT (n=111) and the JWT (n=124) groups. Efficacy, safety profiles, and myocardial perfusion parameters were compared between the two groups.

Results

In the unadjusted analysis, BSKT was associated with a higher immediate stent implantation success rate and a lower incidence of provisional stenting (PS-T) due to branch compromise. After adjustment for potential confounders, the association with immediate stent implantation success was attenuated and became borderline significant. No statistically significant between-group differences were detected in the one-year clinical outcomes; however, the small number of events limited definitive comparison between the two strategies. On postoperative Day 1, BNP and cTnT levels remained lower in the BSKT group after correction for repeated longitudinal comparisons, whereas the difference in CK-MB was attenuated after multiple-comparison correction. At six months, the BSKT group showed more favorable selected SPECT-derived parameters, including a lower stress myocardial perfusion score, fewer resting and stress myocardial perfusion-defect segments, and a narrower range of abnormal myocardial perfusion, whereas the resting myocardial perfusion score did not differ significantly between groups.

Conclusion

Compared with JWT, BSKT was associated with more favorable findings in side-branch protection and selected short-term functional outcomes in patients with LAD-diagonal branch true bifurcation lesions, whereas comparative long-term clinical outcomes remain uncertain.

title: A Novel SERPINC1 Mutation in a Teenager With Antithrombin Deficiency Leading to Pulmonary Embolism and Deep Vein Thrombosis: Implications for Diagnosis and Management.
authorString: Guan W, Zhao Q, Liu Z.
abstractText: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is uncommon in adolescents, and hereditary thrombophilia should be considered in unprovoked or progressive cases. We report a 16-year-old Chinese male with pulmonary embolism and extensive deep vein thrombosis that progressed despite anticoagulation with low-molecular-weight heparin followed by unfractionated heparin.
