Antithrombin (AT) activity was persistently reduced (36%-49%; reference range, 80%-120%), and activated partial thromboplastin time remained subtherapeutic despite heparin dose escalation, suggesting functional heparin resistance. Switching to argatroban achieved clinical stabilization. Whole-exome sequencing identified a previously unreported heterozygous SERPINC1 variant (NM_000488.4: exon5: c.1153 G > T; p.Gly385Cys), classified as a variant of uncertain significance. The patient's mother and sister carried the same variant and had reduced AT activity. The patient was subsequently transitioned to rivaroxaban and remained asymptomatic during follow-up. AT activity remained reduced at 1 and 2 years, while follow-up imaging showed a reduction in pulmonary arterial thrombotic burden but persistent lower-extremity venous thrombi. This case highlights the importance of evaluating AT deficiency in young patients with unprovoked or progressive VTE and the need for further evidence to establish the clinical significance of novel SERPINC1 variants.

title: Deep Learning-Based Classification of Pulmonary Hypertension Using Early-Fused CTPA and Pulmonary Artery Segmentation Maps.
authorString: Hu S, Li M, Li M, Zhang C, Xie S, Lin Y, Li D, She J.
abstractText: Computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA) is vital for diagnosing pulmonary hypertension (PH), especially thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH). However, manual image interpretation of CTPA often leads to misdiagnosis. This study aims to automatically segment the pulmonary artery from CTPA images and develop a deep learning model by fusing CTPA images with pulmonary artery segmentation results to distinguish pulmonary hypertension (PH vs. subjects without PH (no-PH)) and its PH subtype, CTEPH (CTEPH, other PH vs. no-PH). The study included 92 patients with CTEPH, 85 patients with other types of PH, and 140 no-PH. We completed the image preprocessing and segmentation of the pulmonary arterial tree of all the sample data. Based on four deep learning model classifiers-ResNet50, DenseNet, SENet, and Swin Transformer, we respectively developed four distinct network architectures: Single input channel for CTPA images, as well as early, middle, and late fusion strategies that combine CTPA images with their corresponding pulmonary vascular segmentation maps. The performance of the testing experiments has shown that the DenseNet (CTPA-seg) early fusion model achieves optimal performance in the binary classification task of pulmonary hypertension (PH vs. no-PH), with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.927. Meanwhile, the Swin Transformer (CTPA-seg) early fusion model shows the best performance in the ternary classification of pulmonary hypertension subtypes (CTEPH, other PH vs. no-PH), achieving an AUC of 0.855. Compared with models that only use clinical images, the early feature fusion strategy shows significantly higher accuracy in classifying and diagnosing PH, which is beneficial for the differential diagnosis of CTEPH.

title: SysteMatic LeARning With Technology in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension (SMART PAH): A Mixed Methods Pilot Feasibility Study of the Impact of Video-Assisted Education in PAH.
authorString: Sese DG, Persaud P, Qaiser KN, Wang Y, Wang X, Rysczka H, Elghaffar A, Mahmood M, Taylor N, Powers R, Bhardwaj A, Iskandar JP, Durham L, Neuendorf K, Harper LJ, Highland KB.
abstractText: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) carries physical, emotional, and psychosocial burdens. Despite therapeutic advances, patients report limited disease understanding. The Systematic Learning with Technology in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension (SMART PAH) study evaluated feasibility and utility of a video-assisted education intervention. We conducted a mixed-methods pilot study in PAH. Participants accessed 12 web-based videos and completed pre- and post-intervention assessments over 4 weeks. Outcomes included PAH knowledge, Patient Activation (PAM), Patient Health Questionnaire-8 (PHQ-8), Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7), and EmPHasis-10 scores. Usability was assessed using the Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool and semi-structured interviews. Descriptive statistics and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests were used. Eighteen patients were enrolled (median age 59 years; 67% female; 44% idiopathic PAH, 27% connective tissue disease (CTD)-associated PAH). Most were WHO Functional Class II (50%), and 71% were low-risk by REVEAL Lite 2, with a median 6-min walk distance of 425 m. Post-intervention, PAM scores significantly improved (p = 0.014), indicating patient activation. Secondary outcomes showed trends toward improvement (PHQ-8: 4.0 → 2.5, p = 0.23; GAD-7: 2.5 → 1.0, p = 0.72; EmPHasis-10: 15 → 9, p = 0.18). Knowledge gains were greatest for "Travel & Living with PAH" (p = 0.18) and "Palliative Care & PAH" (p = 0.026). Qualitative analysis identified domains through which the intervention supported patient needs. Participants described the program as accessible, empowering, and confidence-building. SMART PAH was feasible, acceptable, and associated with improved patient activation. Limited by sample size, findings suggest that video-based education may address informational gaps and enhance patient engagement in PAH. Further studies are needed to evaluate long-term effects on patient-centered and clinical outcomes.

title: The population prevalence of Down syndrome in Trentino region (Northeast Italy) in 2025.
authorString: Pertile R, Rivieri F, Santoro M, Mantovani W.
abstractText: Down syndrome (DS) is the most common autosomal aneuploidy compatible with postnatal survival and the leading genetic cause of intellectual disability worldwide. In Italy, reliable population-based prevalence estimates are still lacking at both national and regional levels. We conducted a population-based study in the Trentino region using a multisource record-linkage approach. Individuals with DS born from 1945 onwards were identified through multiple health, administrative and social databases, including the Congenital Anomalies Registry (EUROCAT member). Vital status was ascertained up to 1 January 2025. Birth prevalence (1960-2025 and 1990-2025) and point prevalence were calculated, stratified by age and sex. As of 1 January 2025, 403 individuals with DS were resident in Trentino, corresponding to a prevalence of 7.37 per 10 000 inhabitants [95% confidence interval (CI) 6.65-8.09]. Birth prevalence trends showed a decrease in live births with DS over time, alongside an increase in terminations of pregnancy for foetal anomaly, while total birth prevalence (including terminations) increased. In 2020-2025, total birth prevalence was 35.4 per 10 000 births and 10.1 per 10 000 for live births only. Among individuals aged 5-49 years, prevalence appeared relatively constant across age groups, with no evidence of a linear trend with age. This is the first Italian population-based study providing a direct prevalence estimate of DS in a well-defined area using an integrated multisource approach. The observed prevalence is consistent with other high-income countries and reflects reduced live births and improved survival. These findings highlight the need for healthcare systems to address the growing adult population with DS and support evidence-based planning of services.

title: Secular Trends in Myocardial Infarction and Coronary Death: Data Over Four Decades From the Population-Based Augsburg Myocardial Infarction Registry.
authorString: Schmitz T, Kirchberger I, Raake P, Linseisen J, Meisinger C.
abstractText:
Background

Acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and coronary heart disease (CHD) are major causes of morbidity and mortality worldwide, accounting for approximately 9.24 million deaths globally in 2022. In Germany, CHD caused approximately 119 800 deaths in 2023. The aim of this study was to analyze secular trends in event rates and mortality on the basis of registry data from southern Germany.

Methods

The population-based Augsburg Myocardial Infarction Registry was established in 1985. It records all hospitalized cases of AMI and all CHD deaths in the Augsburg study region.

Results

From 1985 to 2023, age-standardized event rates fell from 633 to 274 per 100 000 men and from 156 to 79 per 100 000 women aged 25 to 74. The decline was driven by decreases in first event rates from 414 to 222 in men and from 127 to 69 in women, and by decreases in re-event rates from 219 to 52 in men and from 29 to 10 in women (all rates per 100 000 in the group in question). Over the same period, CHD mortality fell from 352 to 86 per 100 000 men and from 58 to 27 per 100 000 women, and there was also a decline in 28-day case fatality. The percentage of patients receiving percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) rose to nearly 90% in both sexes.

Conclusions

Despite declining age-standardized rates, the absolute numbers of AMI events and CHD deaths remain high because of the aging of the population. Long-term, population-based registries remain essential for monitoring trends and providing a basis for healthcare planning and prevention.

title: Multimodality Imaging in the Evaluation of Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.
authorString: Cutts J, Kramer C.
abstractText: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is characterized by pathologic hypertrophy in the absence of a potentially causative disease process and carries increased risk of heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and sudden cardiac death. Synergistic use of multi-modal imaging is pivotal and necessary in the diagnosis and management of patients with, or at risk for, HCM. Echocardiography, cardiac MR, and cardiac computed tomography each have important roles and limitations in assessing the morphologic changes responsible for symptoms and morbidity in HCM. In this article, we will explore these modalities and their roles in evaluating HCM.

title: Risk Factors for Progression in Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.
authorString: Sengupta S, Wazade A.
abstractText: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is one of the important causes of sudden cardiac death (SCD) in younger people and athletes. It is important to identify the risk factors for SCD in individuals with HCM. This article, based on recent systematic literature studies, will focus on the risk factors for progression in patients with HCM. The article discusses the established risk factors, such as a family history, unexplained syncope, and some new risk factors. The findings of this article demonstrate that there is a need for further research on individual risk factors and risk stratification in HCM patients remains a clinical challenge.

title: Phenotyping the Many Faces of Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.
authorString: Geenty P, Gray B, Thomas L.
abstractText: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is the most common inherited cardiomyopathy and is defined by the presence of left ventricular hypertrophy 15 mm or greater in the absence of any other identifiable cause. Beyond this definition, clinical phenotype is heterogeneous, and associated clinical manifestations occur in varying proportions of patients, including left ventricular outflow tract obstruction, systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve with associated mitral regurgitation, ventricular arrhythmias, and sudden cardiac death. Accurate clinical phenotyping allows the identification of groups with distinct natural history and prognosis, with risk stratification being crucial for prevention of sudden cardiac death.

title: Systemic Lupus and Other Autoimmune Disorders During Pregnancy.
authorString: Patton KA, Siddique F, Lal AK.

journal.title: Rheumatic diseases clinics of North America

abstractText: Rheumatologic conditions occur in reproductive aged women, requiring a multidisciplinary approach to care. Patients require coordinated care with obstetrics, maternal fetal medicine, and rheumatology. Many drugs used for the care of rheumatologic conditions are safe in pregnancy, but detailed review should occur, ideally preconception, so the patient can be on the safest regimen while maintaining disease control. Anti-Ro/SSA and anti-La/SSB antibodies particularly pose unique risks of neonatal lupus syndrome, including cardiac manifestations. Medical management is unique to each disease and includes ultrasounds and antenatal testing to optimize both maternal and fetal well-being and minimize perinatal risks.

title: Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: Patient Selection, Referral Timing, and Advanced Therapy Options.
authorString: Abusafia M, Jadam S, Ospina S, Desai MY.
abstractText: In this review, we provide a detailed up-to-date summary of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM). From the complex and diverse presentations to the individualized clinical profiles, we delve into the different aspects of HCM diagnosis, management, and follow up. We discuss imaging modalities and their indications as well as current guidelines for both pharmacological and surgical treatment options. We also review the data regarding emerging therapies.

title: Strategy for Exercise Restriction in Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.
authorString: Lee HJ.
abstractText: This article outlines the evolving evidence and guidelines surrounding exercise in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), challenging the traditional paradigm of universal restriction. It highlights that most patients with HCM can safely engage in physical activity (PA) and improve cardiovascular outcomes. Recent evidence demonstrates that vigorous PA improves functional capacity and does not increase adverse events in most low-risk HCM patients. Contemporary guidelines advocate for individualized exercise recommendations based on comprehensive risk stratification and shared decision-making. A clinical framework is proposed to support tailored exercise prescriptions and shared decision-making.

title: The Role of Medical Therapy in Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: An Updated Review.
authorString: Lee JW, Chun KH, Choi EY, Seo J.
abstractText: This review highlights recent advances in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) treatment, focusing on how to effectively implement both traditional and novel pharmacologic strategies in clinical practice. Traditional medications like beta-blockers and calcium channel blockers continue to play a critical role. However, new treatments, such as cardiac myosin inhibitors, provide an innovative approach for relieving symptoms, especially in obstructive HCM cases. Emerging therapies, including sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors, sacubitril/valsartan, and ninerafaxstat, show promising benefits. Proper management of related conditions such as atrial fibrillation and heart failure is also essential. A comprehensive approach that considers individual patient characteristics and the specific subtype of HCM is essential for achieving optimal outcomes.

title: The Evolving Landscape of Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: Phenocopies and Diagnostic Pathways in Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.
authorString: Son JW, Nam JH, Choi KU, Hong GR.
abstractText: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is an inherited myocardial disease defined by unexplained thickening and hypertrophy of ventricular myocardium. However, several other conditions-"phenocopies" or mimics-can present with a similar hypertrophic phenotype. This article details the major HCM phenocopies, including infiltrative and storage diseases (amyloidosis, Fabry, Pompe, and Danon), systemic granulomatous disease (sarcoidosis), mitochondrial disorders, physiologic hypertrophy (athlete's heart), and hypertensive heart disease and aortic stenosis. We describe their distinguishing clinical features, multimodality imaging findings, pathophysiology, and key diagnostic clues highlighting red-flag signs and recent advances in diagnostics.

title: Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy in the Absence of "Hypertrophy": A Precision Medicine Reappraisal.
authorString: Vega-Adauy J, Urbina J.
abstractText: Fixed wall thickness cutoffs have historically defined hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), yet this rigid approach overlooks patients with early, segmental, or morphologically subtle disease. Subthreshold phenotypes-particularly in women, individuals with short stature, and those with apical or focal variants-may not meet conventional criteria despite exhibiting pathologic features. This article examines the limitations of absolute diagnostic thresholds and advocates for a precision medicine framework. Integrating cardiac magnetic resonance imaging with individualized metrics and architectural markers enhances diagnostic accuracy, identifies nonclassical presentations, and facilitates earlier disease recognition, ultimately improving care across the heterogeneous spectrum of HCM.

title: Redefining Left Ventricular Systolic Dysfunction in Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: Ejection Fraction and Global Longitudinal Strain.
authorString: Kwak S, Kim HK.
abstractText: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is an inherited disease characterized by increased myocardial thickness without cardiac, systemic, or metabolic causes to explain the observed left ventricular (LV) hypertrophy. Importantly, LV systolic dysfunction influences symptoms, heart failure, and the risk of SCD in HCM. LV global longitudinal strain (LV-GLS) is a sensitive marker for detecting subclinical LV dysfunction and improving risk stratification. Integrating LV-GLS with other imaging biomarkers, such as late gadolinium enhancement and left atrial reservoir strain, may improve risk prediction. Future research should focus on refining LV-GLS cutoffs and exploring its utility for personalized risk assessment in HCM.

title: Navigating the Evolving Landscape of Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.
authorString: Vega-Adauy J, Hong GR, Bossone E.

title: Total Endovascular Aortic Arch Repair: A Review of Current Technologies and Clinical Decision Frameworks.
authorString: Calanni Macchio C, Damiano A, Ahmadi-Hadad A, Baiano S, Comentale G, Pilato E.
abstractText: Endovascular technologies offer less invasive alternatives to open aortic arch repair in high-risk patients. This review evaluates contemporary total arch reconstruction platforms. PubMed literature through February 2026, manufacturer documentation, and ClinicalTrials.gov were reviewed. Branched, fenestrated, and alternative devices were assessed regarding anatomy, procedural characteristics, and clinical outcomes. No formal systematic review or meta-analysis was performed. Technical success rates reached 90-100%. Branched devices enable three-vessel revascularization, while fenestrated systems accommodate complex anatomy. Stroke rates ranged from 3.7% to 11%; endoleaks and reinterventions remained concerns. To date, anyway, device selection, anatomical suitability, planning, and institutional expertise are essential for optimal outcomes.

title: Medical Imaging Analysis of X-Ray, MRI, and CT Scans for Clinical Diagnostics.
authorString: Deng J, Wu P, Chen Z, Xiao Y, Lin H, Ji Z.
abstractText: This chapter focuses on the clinical applications of three mainstream medical imaging modalities-X-ray, CT, and MRI-providing a systematic analysis of their imaging mechanisms, typical indications, strengths, and limitations. The diagnostic performance of each modality is compared across various disease scenarios. With the rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI), medical imaging analysis is advancing toward greater intelligence and standardization. Deep learning-based techniques for image recognition and lesion segmentation have significantly improved diagnostic accuracy and efficiency. Meanwhile, emerging technologies such as multimodal image fusion, remote collaborative reading, and radiomics are expanding the clinical boundaries of medical imaging. These innovations have found broad applications across the nervous, respiratory, cardiovascular, oncologic, and chronic disease domains. This chapter reviews the core clinical values of X-ray, CT, and MRI, integrates recent AI-driven advances, and explores the evolving role of imaging technologies in the era of precision medicine.

title: The Transformative Role of Artificial Intelligence in Wearable Health Monitoring: Applications in Diagnosis, Therapy, and Rehabilitation.
authorString: Shen X, Luo X, Sun Y, Zhu Z, Liu S, Xiong Z, Li X, Chen S, Yang Y, Yang L, Luo Y, Lei Y, Zhao C, Xu W, Li K, Chen H, Huang W, Liao J.
abstractText: This chapter explores the transformative impact of artificial intelligence (AI)-augmented wearable technology in dynamic health monitoring across diagnosis, treatment, and rehabilitation. Innovations include real-time cardiovascular disease detection, AI-driven continuous glucose monitoring for diabetes, and neurological disorder tracking using flexible electroencephalograph (EEG) sensors. Therapeutic advances feature smart drug-delivery patches responsive to biomarkers, remote intervention systems, and surgical tools like augmented reality (AR) navigation. Rehabilitation breakthroughs encompass wearables for motor recovery, cardiopulmonary optimization, and neurorehabilitation using brain-computer interfaces. Future progress hinges on multifunctional hardware, federated learning for privacy, explainable AI, and standardized regulations.

title: Tailored Therapies Guided by Multi-Omics Integration: Principles, Applications, and Future Directions.
authorString: Yu L, Pan M, Chen Y.
abstractText: Molecular and clinical profiling increasingly informs patient stratification and treatment selection in precision medicine. This transition is largely driven by high-throughput omics technologies-spanning genomics, epigenomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, and microbiomics. These technologies provide complementary information on molecular variation in health and disease. Although analyzing a single omics layer is informative, it does not fully describe the interactions among different molecular layers. Integrating data across multiple molecular layers provides a much broader context. This multi-omics approach helps researchers map complex regulatory networks, identify candidate biomarkers and potential therapeutic targets. This review outlines the current state of multi-omics in personalized medicine. We detail the basic principles and recent progress in core technologies, highlighting rapidly developing areas such as single-cell multi-omics, spatial omics, and liquid biopsies. The chapter discusses key applications in oncology, cardiovascular disease, neurodegenerative disorders, and rare diseases, showing how multi-omics improves molecular subtyping, target identification, disease mechanism analysis, and diagnostics. Furthermore, we examine the computational strategies required to integrate these large datasets, specifically addressing issues like high dimensionality, data heterogeneity, and missing values. Significant technical and translational barriers are also evaluated, alongside ethical, legal, and social implications (ELSI)-such as data quality, clinical validation, cost-effectiveness, privacy, and healthcare equity. Finally, the review looks at future directions, focusing on ongoing technological innovations, the expanding role of artificial intelligence, and the integration of digital health data. We conclude by assessing both the practical hurdles and the long-term impact of multi-omics on delivering individualized patient care.

title: Simple HPTLC Methods for the Detection of Adulterations of Rhodiola rosea With Rhodiola crenulata Rhizomes.
authorString: Bampali-Thumann E, Reinhard S, Hauer H, Kulić Ž.
abstractText: Rhodiola rosea L. (Crassulaceae) roots are commonly used in Europe, North America, and Asia in herbal medicinal preparations. In Traditional Chinese Medicine, several Rhodiola species, including Rhodiola crenulata (Hook. f. & Thomson) H. Ohba, are used for herbal preparations. Due to similar morphology of the rhizome, R. crenulata is a common adulterant in the R. rosea value chain. We developed a synthesis protocol for crenulatin, a substance present in R. crenulata, and tested its presence in 13 genuine R. rosea samples from different cultivation areas in Germany and Italy. None of the R. rosea samples contained crenulatin, making it a potential marker compound for adulteration testing. Furthermore, two thin-layer chromatography methods were developed in order to detect potential adulterations down to 1%. The simplicity and efficiency of the two thin-layer chromatography methods make them particularly suitable for routine quality control in laboratories with limited infrastructure, including pharmacies.

title: Intracardiac Flow Dynamics: Insights from HyperDoppler.
authorString: Mele D, Beccari R, Smarrazzo V, Maglione M, Pedrizzetti G.
abstractText: The study of intracardiac flow dynamics through contrast-enhanced ultrasound and 4-dimensional flow MRI has expanded our understanding of cardiac chamber function beyond conventional assessments of myocardial motion and deformation. However, routine clinical use of these techniques remains constrained. HyperDoppler represents an emerging ultrasound-based approach that derives 2-dimensional intracardiac velocity vector fields from standard color Doppler data, allowing for both qualitative and quantitative evaluation of flow patterns without requiring contrast agents, thereby enhancing its practicality in clinical settings. This article outlines the underlying principles of HyperDoppler, methods for qualitative and quantitative assessment, and its current and prospective clinical applications.

title: Parent-Child Physiological Synchrony: Links With Parent Emotion Regulation and Children's Independent Emotion Regulation.
authorString: Perry NB, Akinmola-Milone T, Bryan AE.
abstractText: Developmental theories propose that physiological synchrony is a key process through which co-regulatory experiences support children's emerging capacity for independent emotion regulation. Caregivers' emotion regulation abilities are also theorized to influence their capacity to engage in synchronous interactions, thereby shaping co-regulatory experiences. Despite these propositions, few studies have empirically examined these developmental processes. The current study examined associations between parent-child respiratory sinus arrhythmia (RSA) synchrony during dyadic problem solving and children's physiological (i.e, RSA reactivity) and behavioral regulation during a subsequent independent challenge. The study also examined whether parents' emotion regulation difficulties predicted RSA synchrony and whether synchrony statistically accounted for associations between parents' emotion regulation difficulties and children's regulatory outcomes. Participants included 57 preschoolers (M_age = 4.26 years; 49% male) and their parents (50 mothers, 7 fathers). Families were predominantly White (68%), with 62% reporting a master's degree or higher. Greater parent-driven RSA synchrony during dyadic interactions was associated with reduced reliance on distraction and help-seeking strategies during the independent problem-solving task but was not associated with children's physiological regulation. Parents reporting greater difficulties maintaining goal-directed behavior and less emotional awareness exhibited lower levels of parent-driven synchrony, and synchrony emerged as an indirect pathway linking these parent characteristics to children's behavioral regulation. Findings provide preliminary support for physiological synchrony as a developmental mechanism linking parent emotion regulation to children's independent emotion regulation during early childhood.

title: Urinary extracellular vesicle-associated IL-6 and cathepsin D for early identification of chronic kidney disease in high-risk patients.
authorString: Ku-Centurion M, Cortes-Sanabria L, Verdugo-Molinares MG, Cerino-Recinos JL, Palomo EA, Castro-Sanchez L, Meseguer A, Arévalo J, Fabres PHL, Cueto-Manzano AM, Melo Z.
abstractText:
Background

Early chronic kidney disease (CKD) is frequently asymptomatic and remains underdiagnosed in high-risk populations. Urinary extracellular vesicles (uEVs) provide a non-invasive source of kidney-related biomolecules and may improve early detection strategies. We evaluated uEV-associated interleukin-6 (IL-6), cathepsin D (CTD), and transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β) as candidate biomarkers for early CKD, including sex-stratified patterns.

Methods

In this cross-sectional study, 230 adults at high risk (type 2 diabetes mellitus and/or systemic arterial hypertension) were classified as having normal kidney function (NKF) or CKD stages G1-G4. uEVs were isolated using a standardized protocol and characterized by scanning electron microscopy, Raman spectroscopy, dynamic light scattering, and Western blot for Alix and flotillin-1. Total uEV-associated protein was quantified, and CTD, IL-6, and TGF-β were measured in uEV preparations.

Results

uEVs displayed expected morphology and marker expression. Particle size distributions differed by sex and CKD status. Total uEV protein content did not significantly differ across CKD stages. uEV-associated IL-6 was significantly higher in G1 compared with NKF (p ≤ 0.05). CTD showed a decreasing trend from G1 to G4 with stage- and sexspecific differences, most evident in women at G1. uEV-associated TGF-β did not differ significantly across stages.

Conclusions

uEV-derived IL-6 and CTD show potential as non-invasive indicators of early CKD, with clinically relevant sex-dependent patterns, while TGF-β may provide complementary information. Standardized uEV isolation and measurement workflows are essential for biomarker reproducibility and future clinical translation.

title: Combining Data Science and Computational Cardiology: A New Paradigm for Cardiovascular Medicine to Accelerate Clinical Translation.
authorString: Franzese M, Bossone E.

title: Factors associated with mood and anxiety disorders in patients with cancer: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
authorString: Li M, Zhou X, Deng Z, Jung M, Lu J, Stave CD, Spiegel D, Langston ME, Chung BI, Bondy ML.
abstractText:
Background

Mood and anxiety disorders are common in cancer survivors, and are associated with worse outcomes; however, systematic identification of high-risk patients remains limited, despite screening and intervention guidelines. A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted to identify risk factors for mood and anxiety disorders, including diagnoses and clinically significant symptoms, in adult cancer survivors.

Methods

PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, PsycINFO, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched for cohort and case-control studies published from January 2000 to November 2024 that evaluated cancer-related, sociodemographic, lifestyle, and psychosocial risk factors in adults with breast, lung, colorectal, prostate, stomach, liver, or pancreatic cancer. Random-effects models with robust variance estimation pooled relative risks (RRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for factors assessed in ≥5 studies.

Results

Fifty of the 53 eligible studies were included in the meta-analysis. Consistent risk factors included high tumor stage (vs. low; n = 28; RR, 1.55; 95% CI, 1.21-1.97), more physical comorbidities (vs. fewer; n = 36; RR, 1.57; 95% CI, 1.34-1.84), prior psychiatric history (high vs. low burden; n = 13; RR, 4.85; 95% CI, 2.77-8.50), female sex (vs. male; n = 19; RR, 1.52; 95% CI, 1.32-1.75), underweight body mass index (vs. normal; n = 6; RR, 1.93; 95% CI, 1.55-2.44), unmarried status (vs. married; n = 25; RR, 1.35; 95% CI, 1.14-1.58), and current smoking (vs. never; n = 12; RR, 1.27; 95% CI, 1.12-1.46). Suggestive associations, although less consistent in sensitivity analyses, were observed for high tumor grade, more extensive surgery, low income, low education, and low social support.

Conclusions

Several clinical and social factors were associated with increased risk of mood and anxiety outcomes in adult cancer survivors. These findings may support risk-based psychiatric screening and early intervention in resource-limited oncology settings.

title: Ketogenic Diet Effects on Liver Health in Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease: A Systematic Review.
authorString: Palumbo P, Krishnapillai H, de Vreeze F, Buzzetti E, Koek GH.

journal.title: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver

abstractText: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is the most prevalent chronic liver condition and is linked to unhealthy lifestyle patterns. Dietary modification remains the cornerstone of management. Among available nutritional strategies, ketogenic diets (KDs) have gained increasing attention. This systematic review evaluated the impact of KD, versus no dietary intervention or control diets, on hepatic and metabolic outcomes in adults with MASLD. Following PRISMA guidelines, PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science were searched through June 2026. Two reviewers independently screened records, assessed eligibility and extracted data. Risk of bias was evaluated using CASP for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and ROBINS-I for non-randomized studies. Meta-analysis was not feasible due to study heterogeneity. Fourteen studies were included: five RCTs and nine prospective cohorts, involving 776 adults with MASLD and/or hepatic steatosis. KD was associated with improvements in MASLD severity indices, anthropometric measures, lipid profile, glycaemic markers and liver enzymes. Among RCTs, liver fat decreased by -4.77% (PDFF) to a 77% (relative MRI-LFF), with reductions in body weight (up to -12.0 kg) and waist circumference (up to -9.6 cm). Prospective studies showed similar findings, including reductions in controlled attenuation parameter (up to -57 dB/m), intrahepatic triglyceride (-31%) and Fatty Liver Index (-14.03 points). Evidence regarding liver stiffness and fibrosis-related outcomes was more limited and less consistent. KD may improve disease severity, hepatic steatosis, anthropometric measures, glycaemic control, lipid metabolism and liver-related biochemical markers in adults with MASLD. However, methodological heterogeneity precludes outcomes assessment, and limited evidence on fibrosis-related evidence precludes firm conclusions. Larger, longer-standardized RCTs are needed to clarify KD's role in MASLD management.

title: Effectiveness of a Nutritional Supplement With Anti-Inflammatory Compounds and Olive Oil in Malnourished Patients.
authorString: Vidal-Casariego A, Gómez JJL, Almeida JMG, Aguilar IV, Baena JMG, Pérez CT, Milla SP, Ricciardi PM, Prol AR, Luna PPG, Gil BM, Iglesias Hernández NC, Luengo Pérez LM, de Luis Román D.

journal.title: Journal of cachexia, sarcopenia and muscle

abstractText:
Background

Disease-related malnutrition (DRM) with systemic inflammation is associated with poor clinical outcomes and muscle mass loss. This study in a real-world clinical practice examined whether an oral nutritional supplement (ONS) enriched with anti-inflammatory compounds-eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA), docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) and extra-virgin olive oil (EVOO)-was associated with improvements in nutritional status, muscle mass and functional performance in patients with inflammation-related DRM.

Methods

In this 12-week prospective multicenter cohort study, adults diagnosed with DRM and elevated C-reactive protein (CRP > 3 mg/L) received either an anti-inflammatory ONS or standard ONS, both combined with dietary counselling and a structured physical activity programme. Outcomes included anthropometry, body composition (bioimpedance and ultrasound), muscle function, inflammatory markers and quality of life.

Results

Of 266 participants (mean age 66.6 ± 12.9 years; 61.7% male), those receiving the anti-inflammatory ONS (n = 165) achieved significantly greater increases in fat-free mass (Δ +1.20 vs. -0.85 kg; p = 0.022), skeletal muscle index (Δ +0.12 vs. -0.21 kg/m2; p = 0.022) and rectus femoris circumference by ultrasound (Δ +0.43 vs. -0.13 cm; p = 0.042) compared with controls (n = 101). Functional improvements were also superior: Chair stand repetitions increased significantly (Δ +0.90 vs. +0.03 times; p = 0.025), with a trend toward reduced Timed Up and Go time. Quality of life improved significantly across physical and mental domains in the anti-inflammatory group (e.g.

, vas

Δ +11.1 vs. -10.8; p < 0.001). After adjustment for baseline values, age, sex, GLIM severity, CRP and primary diagnosis, differences remained significant for SMI (0.10 kg/m2; 95% CI, 0.01-0.19), fat-free mass, muscle circumference, chair stand and EQ VAS (12.85 points; 95% CI, 5.61-20.08), but not for handgrip strength. Twelve-week mortality was higher with the anti-inflammatory ONS (11.5% vs. 4.95%; adjusted OR, 3.35; 95% CI, 1.06-13.81).

Conclusions

In this post hoc analysis, the use of an ONS enriched with EPA, DHA and EVOO, combined with physical activity and dietary counselling, was associated with greater gains in muscle mass, lower-limb strength and quality of life in patients with inflammation-associated DRM, but also with higher short-term mortality. Because residual confounding cannot be excluded, these findings are hypothesis-generating; randomized controlled trials with prespecified safety outcomes are needed.

title: Cryo-EM reveals how omecamtiv mecarbil readies myosin for phosphate release.
authorString: McMillan SN, Winkelmann DA, Muench SP, Scarff CA.

journal.title: Acta crystallographica. Section D, Structural biology

abstractText: Omecamtiv mecarbil (OM) was considered to be a cardiac muscle activator in clinical trials for alleviation of systolic heart failure. Yet, it was later shown to be a potent inhibitor of myosin motor activity. Its binding to myosin prevents the force-generating lever swing but also accelerates the release of inorganic phosphate (P<sub>i</sub>), such that in muscle OM enhances overall force production by cooperatively increasing the number of actomyosin cross-bridges. The structural basis by which it accelerates P<sub>i</sub> release remains poorly understood. Here, using cryogenic electron microscopy, we determined the structure of the human β-cardiac myosin motor domain in the presence of MgATP and OM to 3.2 Å global resolution. The structure adopts a primed state with well resolved OM density within its established binding pocket, and density within the active site consistent with a post-hydrolysis MgADP·P<sub>i</sub> state. OM stabilizes interactions bridging the converter and N-terminal subdomains of the myosin motor, inducing a 11° lever rotation and altering relay-helix conformation relative to the drug-free motor to prevent the force-generating lever swing. Comparison of this structure with that of bovine cardiac myosin with OM and MgADP·vanadate bound, determined by crystallography, revealed subtle but meaningful differences. OM remodels the nucleotide-binding site, shifting the P<sub>i</sub> density ∼2 Å towards its proposed exit pathway. This altered P<sub>i</sub> coordination provides a plausible structural rationale for a mechanism by which OM accelerates the weak-to-strong actomyosin-binding transition, key to its therapeutic function. By stabilizing a conformation in which P<sub>i</sub> is not coordinated to MgADP, P<sub>i</sub> is likely freely released upon opening of its exit pathway. This structural observation is also consistent with previous kinetic studies that showed that OM shifts the equilibrium constant for ATP hydrolysis towards the post-hydrolysis state. This mechanistic understanding will be beneficial to the development of more effective myosin-targeting therapeutics.

title: Antiplatelet Use in the Setting of Therapeutic Anticoagulation: A Scoping Review.
authorString: Ammar A, Edwin SB, Reed JB, Kaatz S, Barnes GD, Giuliano C.
abstractText: Patients receiving therapeutic oral anticoagulation (OAC) often have indications for antiplatelet therapy. Historically, antiplatelet agents have been used alongside therapeutic anticoagulation, increasing the risk of bleeding without a proven reduction in thrombosis. This scoping review summarizes recent evidence evaluating OAC monotherapy compared with combination therapy consisting of OAC plus antiplatelet agent among patients with atrial fibrillation and stable coronary artery disease, cerebrovascular disease, and prosthetic heart valves. We searched PubMed, Embase, CENTRAL, and International Pharmaceutical Abstracts to identify randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating these strategies. Included studies enrolled adults receiving therapeutic anticoagulation across different cardiovascular disease states that reported efficacy and safety outcomes. Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data, with disagreements resolved by a third reviewer. Published subgroup analyses of included RCTs were also reviewed. After screening 10,008 records, 11 RCTs met inclusion criteria. Evidence supporting OAC monotherapy was observed in patients with atrial fibrillation and stable coronary artery disease; OAC monotherapy consistently reduced bleeding without increasing ischemic events compared with combination therapy. Similar reductions in bleeding were observed in patients with cerebrovascular disease, although evidence remains limited by small sample size and early trial termination. Among patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement with an indication for chronic anticoagulation, OAC monotherapy reduced bleeding without compromising ischemic outcomes. Evidence supporting discontinuation of antiplatelet therapy in patients with mechanical heart valves remains limited. Additional RCTs are needed to better define the role of antiplatelet therapy in cerebrovascular disease, prosthetic heart valves, and other high-risk populations.

title: Individualised Versus Conventional Balloon Dilation for TIPS: Hepatic Encephalopathy in a Propensity-Matched Before-After Study.
authorString: Ji PC, Huang GP, Huang JY, Luo WJ, Hu SJ, Yang Y, Xu ZG.

journal.title: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver

abstractText:
Background and aims

Hepatic encephalopathy (HE) is a major complication of transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS). Stent under-dilation reduces HE, but a fixed diameter cannot be individualised to patient risk. An individualised scoring system tailoring balloon diameter to patient characteristics, without compromising efficacy or increasing variceal re-bleeding or stent dysfunction, is needed.

Methods

In this retrospective study, 717 patients with cirrhosis underwent TIPS with 8-mm covered stents between December 2015 and December 2023. Patients received conventional 8-mm full dilation (n = 408; before December 1, 2020) or individualised dilation (n = 309; from December 1, 2020 onward), with the balloon diameter (5-7 mm) chosen by an 11-factor scoring system. The primary endpoint was overt HE (West Haven grade II-IV) within 6 months. Propensity score matching, inverse probability weighting, Fine-Grey and E-value analyses were performed.

Results

Six-month overt HE was lower in the individualised group (14.6%; 45 of 309) than in the conventional group (27.5%; 112 of 408), yielding an absolute risk reduction of 12.9 percentage points (number needed to treat, 8; p < 0.001). After propensity score matching on 18 covariates (259 pairs), the conditional odds ratio was 0.42 (95% CI, 0.27-0.66; p < 0.001), consistent with inverse probability weighting (odds ratio, 0.47). Six-month re-bleeding (1.5% vs. 1.3%), stent dysfunction (3.9% vs. 4.2%) and ascites improvement (61.0% vs. 62.1%) did not differ significantly.

Conclusions

An individualised balloon dilation strategy incorporating an 11-factor scoring system was associated with reduced post-TIPS HE, with no clear difference in variceal re-bleeding, stent dysfunction or ascites recurrence.

Trial registration

Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR2400087533.

title: Pedicled Radial Artery Perforator Flaps for Reconstruction of the Upper Limb: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Single-Arm Studies.
authorString: Savaris DF, Arend RB, Kieling DM, Lima NL, Corin AS, Savaris MV, Valério NDR, Moura NO, Cambruzzi G, Ieggli P, Kim JH, Alves GI, Mocelin R.
abstractText:
Introduction

The radial artery perforator flap (RAPF) is a perforator-based option for covering hand and distal forearm defects that preserves the radial artery. Although its use is increasingly reported, available evidence is confined to small, uncontrolled series, and the complication profile, functional results, and the specific role of the pedicled RAPF among contemporary local, regional, and free-flap alternatives have not been synthesized. This review aimed to describe, without any comparative claim, the outcomes reported after pedicled RAPF in upper limb reconstruction.

Methods

We searched MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science through August 28, 2025, following PRISMA guidelines, for studies of pedicled RAPF (propeller or advancement; fasciocutaneous or adipofascial) including at least three patients; we excluded free radial artery perforator flaps. Because all eligible studies were single-arm, we performed a proportional (single-group) meta-analysis with 95% confidence intervals under a random-effects model, with I2 and leave-one-out sensitivity analyses; no relative effect measure or between-technique comparison was possible.

Results

Of 356 records identified, 10 single-arm studies with 152 patients met the inclusion criteria. Functional outcomes could be harmonized in only three studies comprising 33 of the 152 patients: excellent in 39% (95% CI 0.23-0.56), good in 52% (95% CI 0.34-0.69), and fair in 6% (95% CI 0.00-0.16). Pooled complication rates were low: infection 1%, venous congestion 0% (95% CI 0.00-0.02, although congestive episodes were reported in individual series), partial necrosis 2%, and epidermolysis plus venous congestion 2%; partial necrosis plus epidermolysis was rare (1%) but heterogeneous (I2 = 65.2%) and driven by a single small study. Unplanned secondary intervention was required in 11% (95% CI 0.04-0.19). Donor-site closure was reported for 56 patients, of whom 34 (60.7%) required a split-thickness skin graft. Certainty of evidence (GRADE) was low or very low for every outcome.

Conclusion

Small, predominantly retrospective case series report generally favorable functional results and low complication rates after pedicled RAPF. These uncontrolled data do not establish superiority or equivalence to the classic radial forearm flap or to other reconstructive alternatives, and do not demonstrate reduced donor-site morbidity or superior esthetic outcomes; comparative studies with standardized outcomes are required.

title: Intraoral Subsite, Histopathological Subtype, and Completeness of Pathological Characterization as Determinants of Cancer-Specific Mortality in Minor Salivary Gland Carcinoma: A Population-Based Competing-Risks Analysis of 5820 Tumors.
authorString: Rmaidh ZJ, Mafrachi A, Alghzawi HM.
abstractText:
Objectives

To quantify how completely intraoral minor salivary gland carcinomas are characterized pathologically across subsites, and whether subsite and subtype predict cancer-specific death after accounting for characterization, competing mortality, and stage.

Materials and methods

SEER cohort (17 registries, 2000-2023) of 5820 tumors in 5777 patients. Cause-specific Cox, Fine-Gray, and Lunn-McNeil models adjusted for age, sex, race, subtype, grade, stage, era, and treatment were refitted without treatment and after excluding unclassified histology and unrecorded grade. Cause-of-death coding was checked by relative survival.

Results

Unclassified histology ranged from 8.7% (retromolar area) to 57.5% (mobile tongue) and unrecorded grade from 23.1% to 61.8% (both p < 0.001); unclassified histology was itself prognostic (hazard ratio 2.95, 95% CI 2.37-3.68). Ten-year cancer mortality ranged from 10.1% (buccal mucosa) to 35.1% (mobile tongue; p < 0.001); adjusted hazards were 2.03 (1.60-2.57) for mobile tongue, 2.01 (1.58-2.55) for floor of mouth, and 1.70 (1.26-2.30) for gingiva/alveolus. After excluding unclassified histology and unrecorded grade, floor of mouth (2.20, 1.48-3.26) and gingiva/alveolus (2.53, 1.47-4.35) persisted, whereas the mobile-tongue estimate became imprecise (1.61, 0.86-3.01). Other-cause mortality overtook cancer mortality at 9.4 years (13.2 years without a prior malignancy); 27.1% of other-cause deaths were second malignancies. Conditional 5-year cancer mortality in 10-year survivors was 12.7% for adenoid cystic and 1.2% for mucoepidermoid carcinoma. Machine learning gave no meaningful gain over logistic regression.

Conclusions

Completeness of pathological characterization in registry data is patterned by anatomy and strongly prognostic, so anatomical prognosis and registry documentation are entangled; it is not a measure of diagnostic quality. Floor of mouth and gingiva/alveolus are robust subsite determinants of cancer death; the mobile-tongue excess cannot be separated from incomplete characterization. Competing mortality is substantial, largely from second malignancy. Findings may help inform risk-adapted surveillance, but cancer-specific mortality alone cannot define its intensity.

title: Impact of Frailty on Long-Term Outcomes in Patients After Acute Kidney Injury.
authorString: Chen JY, Pan SY, Teng NC, Chen L, Wu VC.

journal.title: Journal of cachexia, sarcopenia and muscle

abstractText:
Background

Frailty is increasingly recognized as a determinant of adverse outcomes after acute illness, reflecting diminished physiological reserve and vulnerability to stressors. However, its long-term prognostic significance following dialysis-requiring acute kidney injury (AKI-D) remains uncertain. We aimed to examine the association between frailty and long-term outcomes in patients with acute kidney disease (AKD) after recovery from AKI-D.

Methods

We did a nationwide cohort study using Taiwan's National Health Insurance Research Database. Adults aged 18 years or older who were admitted with dialysis-requiring acute kidney injury between 1 January 2015 and 30 September 2022 and remained dialysis-free for 90 days after discharge were included. Follow-up began 90 days after discharge and continued until the occurrence of an outcome of interest or 31 December 2023. The primary outcomes were all-cause mortality, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and major adverse kidney events (MAKE).

Results

Of 18 525 survivors after AKI (mean age 68.3 years, 58.8% men), frailty was classified as fit (3768, 20.3%), mild (8443, 45.6%) or moderate-severe (6314, 34.1%) using a claims-based multimorbidity frailty index. Over a median follow-up of 2.35 years, mild frailty was not significantly associated with all-cause mortality compared with the fit group (aHR, 1.06; 95% CI, 0.99-1.13), whereas moderate to severe frailty conferred a higher risk (aHR, 1.17; 95% CI, 1.09-1.25). For MACE, mild frailty was associated with an adjusted subdistribution hazard ratio (sHR) of 1.21 (95% CI, 1.08-1.34) and moderate to severe frailty with an sHR of 1.37 (95% CI, 1.22-1.53), compared with the fit group. For MAKE, the respective sHR were 1.07 (95% CI, 1.00-1.15) and 1.13 (95% CI, 1.04-1.22). In longitudinal analysis of the 2016-2018 subgroup, the proportion of fit individuals remained stable over five years, while the prevalence of moderate to severe frailty declined, primarily due to a progressive increase in cumulative mortality from 22% to 55%.

Conclusion

Frailty was highly prevalent among survivors after dialysis-requiring AKI and showed a clear, dose-related association with subsequent death, cardiovascular events and kidney events. These findings support the incorporation of frailty assessment into post-AKI care to enable risk stratification and guide targeted interventions aimed at improving long-term outcomes.

title: Oxycodone-Related Deaths Identified in Forensic Autopsies in Western Denmark, 2013-2025: A Retrospective Observational Study.
authorString: Andersen CU, Thomsen AH, Hasselstrøm JB.
abstractText: Non-medical use of prescription opioids including oxycodone is an increasing concern in Denmark, particularly among young individuals. The present retrospective observational study aimed to investigate whether the annual number of fatal oxycodone poisonings increased over time in a population of decedents undergoing forensic autopsy in Western Denmark. We used retrospective data from the autopsy reports of all decedents with oxycodone detected in postmortem femoral blood from May 2013 through 2025 (n = 183). Among these, 107 (59%) died from poisoning involving oxycodone. The number of annual oxycodone poisonings increased from four in 2014 to 16 in 2025. The number of decedents with no apparent prescription for oxycodone and decedents with illicit drug use increased as well, and other psychoactive drugs were frequently detected in oxycodone poisonings. Twenty-seven decedents (15%) were young, defined as age ≤ 25 years. Nineteen (70%) of these 27 died from accidental oxycodone poisoning, 16 (84%) during 2020-2025. Attention deficit hyperkinetic disorder was reported as a comorbidity in 10 (37%) of the young decedents. In conclusion, the present study demonstrates an increasing annual number of oxycodone poisonings among forensic autopsy cases in Western Denmark and suggests that further investigations and preventive efforts in the young may be warranted.

title: Selexipag as a Therapeutic Alternative for Treprostinil-Induced Thrombocytopenia in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension: A Case Report.
authorString: Kido K, Madgula A, Coons JC, Caccamo M, Sokos G.
abstractText: Parenteral prostacyclin pathway agent-induced thrombocytopenia may require dose reduction or therapy discontinuation to mitigate the adverse events. However, the pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) guidelines do not suggest any strategy to overcome treprostinil-induced thrombocytopenia. Selexipag is an oral, non-prostanoid, selective IP receptor agonist. This is the first case report proposing the use of selexipag, due to its minimal thrombocytopenia risk, when severe treprostinil-induced thrombocytopenia occurs in practice. A 66-year-old woman presented to the hospital with new-onset PAH and right ventricular dysfunction. Due to the high mortality risk, the patient was initially started on intravenous treprostinil. The clinical course was complicated by probable treprostinil-induced thrombocytopenia. Due to the need for prostacyclin pathway therapy, the decision was made to switch from intravenous treprostinil to oral selexipag. The nadir platelet count was 30,000/μL. Approximately 72 h after discontinuation of treprostinil and maintaining selexipag 1600 mcg twice daily, the platelet count improved to 46,000/μL on the day of discharge. Several days after discharge, the platelet count further improved to 55,000/μL. The repeated platelet count 1 month after discharge normalized to 329,000/μL. Our case report described the successful use of selexipag to overcome treprostinil-induced thrombocytopenia, owing to its limited effect on platelet aggregation.

title: Factors Associated With Prolonged Length of Stay in Adult Clinical Admissions: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
authorString: Rinaldi JR, Mascarenhas SHZ, Brassolatti D, Neves FF.

journal.title: Journal of evaluation in clinical practice

abstractText:
Background

Hospital admissions account for a substantial proportion of healthcare expenditure, motivating the study of factors associated with extended hospitalization and resource use. Routine clinical and care complexity information may be relevant to discharge planning, but whether incorporating these measures into clinical workflows improves patient or service outcomes requires prospective evaluation.

Objective

To examine the associations of early clinical and functional measures and events occurring during hospitalization with prolonged length of stay among adult clinical admissions to a public university hospital, including the contributions of two structured assessment instruments.

Methods

This retrospective cohort study analysed 250 clinical admissions at a Brazilian university hospital. Prolonged length of stay was defined according to Brazilian Unified Health System criteria. Associations between the Blaylock Risk Assessment Screening Score, Fugulin Scale, and prolonged length of stay were examined using simple and multivariable logistic regression. Apparent model discrimination was assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis; no internal validation was performed.

Results

Prolonged length of stay occurred in 39.6% of admissions. Among these, excess days beyond expected length of stay represented 30% of all bed days. The Fugulin Scale remained associated with prolonged length of stay in the adjusted model (odds ratio = 1.14; 95% confidence interval, 1.05-1.25), whereas the Blaylock Risk Assessment Screening Score was no longer significant after adjustment (p = 0.390). Intensive care unit admission and genitourinary diagnoses were also associated with prolonged length of stay (odds ratios of 2.85 and 6.08, respectively). Healthcare-associated infections were recorded in only 11 admissions; although their adjusted odds ratio was 7.10, the wide 95% confidence interval (1.22-41.22) indicates substantial uncertainty. The model had an area under the curve of 0.783 and a Nagelkerke R2 of 0.307. Because intensive care unit admission and healthcare-associated infections may occur after the initial assessment, these performance estimates do not represent admission-time prediction.

Conclusion

The Fugulin Scale score was associated with prolonged length of stay in this retrospective analysis, while intensive care unit admission and healthcare-associated infections reflected events in the evolving hospital course. Whether using the Fugulin Scale improves prediction, discharge planning, or resource allocation requires prospective evaluation. The combined model should not be used as an admission-time prediction tool.

title: Uremic toxin clearance in pediatric hemodialysis: fishing upstream may improve the catch.
authorString: Goldstein SL.
abstractText: Hemodialysis adequacy is based on dialytic clearance of blood urea nitrogen. Yet, small solute clearance assessment does not reflect uremic toxin clearance, which are larger in size and contribute to the proinflammatory and cardiovascular morbidity seen in younger dialysis populations. Convective clearance by pre-membrane or post-membrane hemofiltration enhances larger molecule clearance. Post-hemofiltration is more efficient, but volumes are limited by hemoconcentration in the dialyzer. Agbas et al. provide a method with improved clearance of many uremic toxins with pre-hemofiltration in this prospective pediatric crossover trial.

title: Spiritual Well-Being and Psychosocial Adjustment Among Adults Receiving Maintenance Haemodialysis: A Cross-Sectional Study.
authorString: Skoulatou M, Kalemikerakis I, Govina O, Kavga-Paltoglou A.
abstractText:
Background

Psychosocial adaptation is a key determinant of quality of life for individuals receiving maintenance haemodialysis; however, its relationship with spiritual well-being is not thoroughly explored.

Objectives

To examine psychosocial adaptation to illness in relation to spiritual well-being among adults with kidney failure receiving maintenance haemodialysis, and to identify associating socio-economic and clinical factors.

Methods

This cross-sectional study was conducted in five Greek public haemodialysis units. Eligible participants were adults, diagnosed with kidney failure, receiving maintenance haemodialysis for at least 6 months. Data were collected via structured interviews using the Psychosocial Adjustment to Illness Scale-Self Report, the Spiritual Well-Being Scale, and a study-specific demographic/clinical questionnaire. Descriptive statistics and univariate analyses were performed (p < 0.05).

Results

In a sample of 130 participants, mean Psychosocial Adjustment score was 49.84 ± 24.61, indicating moderate adaptation difficulty, while mean Spiritual Well-being score was 80.45 ± 19.65, suggesting moderate-to-high spiritual well-being levels. Higher Spiritual Well-being scores were significantly correlated with lower Psychosocial Adjustment scores. Among the dimensions of Spiritual Well-being, Alienation from God showed the strongest negative correlations with key psychosocial domains, including health care orientation, family relationships, social environment, and psychological distress. Poorer adaptation in specific Psychosocial Adjustment domains was associated with the presence of diabetes mellitus, cardiovascular disease, younger age, female gender, lower educational level, lower income, and unmarried status.

Conclusions

Spiritual Well-being is positively associated with psychosocial adaptation among individuals undergoing haemodialysis, indicating a potentially protective role. Integrating spiritual care and targeted psychosocial interventions into routine kidney care may improve adaptation outcomes.

title: Cap-independent translation: a developmental perspective.
authorString: Liang J, Stainier DYR, Bellec M.
abstractText: Precise control of protein synthesis is essential for developmental processes, enabling cells to adapt to different physiological conditions, including stress. While canonical cap-dependent translation is considered the most important mechanism of translation initiation in eukaryotes, many developmental transitions occur when cap-dependent translation is impaired, including during reduced mTOR signaling, metabolic constraints, hypoxia, and cellular stress. In these conditions, cap-independent translation initiation emerges as an alternative mechanism. Here, we first summarize the molecular mechanisms underlying cap-independent translation and then review evidence supporting its role across developmental processes, including early embryogenesis, germ cell development, cell fate decisions, and tissue-specific differentiation. We also discuss experimental approaches used to identify and validate cap-independent translation, along with their limitations. We then propose future directions to investigate the physiological relevance of cap-independent translation during development.

title: [Advance in the application of FBN1 genetic testing in genetic counseling and family management of Marfan syndrome].
authorString: Xiao W, Lu Y, Shen N.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Zhonghua Yi Xue Yi Chuan Xue Za Zhi
journal.title: Zhonghua yi xue yi chuan xue za zhi = Zhonghua yixue yichuanxue zazhi = Chinese journal of medical genetics
journal.isoabbreviation: Zhonghua Yi Xue Yi Chuan Xue Za Zhi

abstractText: Marfan syndrome (MFS) is an autosomal dominant connective tissue disorder mainly affecting the cardiovascular, ocular, and skeletal systems. Fibrillin-1 (FBN1) is the primary causative gene for MFS. Molecular testing can not only facilitate early detection and differential diagnosis but also provide a basis for familial cascade testing, prenatal diagnosis, and long-term risk stratification. In 2024, the ClinGen FBN1 Variant Curation Expert Panel published an ACMG/AMP gene-specific refinement consensus for the classification of FBN1-related MFS variants, emphasizing the uniform reference transcript, standardized phenotypic data collection, family segregation evidence, and quantitative application of phenotype-specific evidence. Guided by this consensus, this review has summarized FBN1 testing technologies, variant interpretation, quality control, family screening strategies in international guidelines, and implementation pathways in domestic laboratories. It also compared the difference in MFS family screening strategies among three guidelines from the United States, Europe, and Japan. Furthermore, management recommendations are proposed from the laboratory medicine perspective for special scenarios such as newborns/children, prenatal diagnosis, variants of uncertain significance (VUS), and variant-negative relatives, with an aim to provide a reference for clinical laboratories to achieve accurate diagnosis and family management of MFS.

title: [Expert consensus on the diagnosis and treatment of Kabuki syndrome (2026 Edition)].
authorString: Committee on Adolescent Medicine and Health, Chinese Medical Doctor Association, Endocrine, Genetic and Metabolic Disorders Group of Pediatric Endocrinology Branch, Chinese Medical Association, Genetic Diagnosis Branch of Chinese Society of Human Genetics, Chen R, Gong C, Wang X.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Zhonghua Yi Xue Yi Chuan Xue Za Zhi
journal.title: Zhonghua yi xue yi chuan xue za zhi = Zhonghua yixue yichuanxue zazhi = Chinese journal of medical genetics
journal.isoabbreviation: Zhonghua Yi Xue Yi Chuan Xue Za Zhi

abstractText: Kabuki syndrome (KS) is a rare genetic disorder with multi-system involvement, including distinctive facial features, intellectual disability, growth retardation, and congenital malformations, e.g., cardiovascular malformation, cleft palate, and anal atresia. The major pathogenic genes for KS are KMT2D and KDM6A, which encode a histone methyltransferase and a histone demethylase, respectively, and epigenetically regulate the expression of downstream genes. To improve the diagnosis and treatment of KS in China, the Committee on Adolescent Medicine and Health of the Chinese Medical Doctor Association, Subspecialty Group of Endocrinology, Genetics and Metabolism of the Society of Pediatrics of the Chinese Medical Association, and the Branch of Genetic Diagnosis of the Genetics Society of China convened leading domestic experts in medical genetics, pediatric endocrinology, genetics and metabolism, and developmental-behavioral pediatrics. Following extensive discussion and multi-round revision, the panel has formulated this consensus to provide guidance for standardizing diagnosis, treatment and genetic counseling for KS.

title: The Role of Extracardiac Uptake in [<sup>99</sup>mTc]Tc-DPD Scintigraphy in Patients With ATTRwt.
authorString: Asaad E, Akdemir DS, Pernice HF, Wetzel P, Wieder NW, Barzen G, Gröschel JW, Schumacher AE, Spethmann S, Heidecker B, Werhahn SM, Herzler P, Wetz C, Hahn K.

journal.title: Journal of the peripheral nervous system : JPNS

abstractText:
Background and aims

Quantification of the soft tissue uptake in 99mTc-DPD has emerged as a promising imaging biomarker in ATTRwt. Recent findings suggest a potential role of [99mTc]Tc-DPD soft tissue uptake in the diagnosis of polyneuropathy in these patients.

Methods

In this registry study, we analyzed all patients who presented at the Amyloidosis Centre Berlin and underwent a standardized diagnostic protocol comprising a multidisciplinary examination, neuroelectrophysiology, ECG, biomarkers, [99mTc]Tc-DPD scintigraphy and echocardiography, without other causes of polyneuropathy. We analyzed the planar scans using soft-tissue-to-bone and heart-to-hemithorax ratios. We assessed the subcutaneous fat uptake using SUVmean derived from SPECT/CT.

Results

Of the 72 patients, 57 ATTRwt patients were included in the analysis. Among these, the prevalence of polyneuropathy and cardiomyopathy was 60% and 95%, respectively. The neurographic pattern was mainly axonal (53%) or mixed (32%). Patients with polyneuropathy showed significantly higher SUVmean in axillary subcutaneous tissue compared to those without (p-value = 0.002). There was no correlation between extracardiac tracer uptake and polyneuropathy severity by using the NIS.

Interpretation

Our results indicate that amyloid load in soft tissue may serve as a potential indicator of peripheral neurological involvement. Future studies are required to explore the utility of DPD scintigraphy for outcome assessment in treated patients.

title: Synthetic Data in MR Spectroscopy: Current Practices, Applications, and Considerations.
authorString: LaMaster JT, Gudmundson AT, Abaei A, Alcicek S, Alvarado A, Andronesi O, Bell T, Bogner W, Bugler H, Craven AR, Cudalbu C, Davidson A, Davies-Jenkins CW, Deelchand D, Edden R, Esmaeili M, Fleischer CC, Gad A, Genovese G, Gurbani S, Harris AD, Henry PG, Igwe KC, Joy A, Julià-Sapé M, Kim H, Kreis R, Lam F, Landheer K, Lanz B, Lee CY, Ligneul C, Merkofer JP, Miller JJ, Mosso J, Motyka S, Mougel E, Mullins PG, Murali-Manohar S, Najac C, Nakajima S, Oeltzschner G, Özdemir İ, Ozturk-Isik E, Palombo M, Pilatus U, Platek J, Rodriguez EP, Qu X, Rizzo R, Rodgers CT, Rodriguez Y, Sammi MK, Sarma MK, Saviola F, Schrantee A, Shamaei A, Simicic D, Soher BJ, Sollmann N, Song Y, Stanley JA, Strasser B, Susnjar A, Swanberg KM, Thomas MA, Tkáč I, Tu Z, van de Sande DMJ, Van Praagh E, Weiser PJ, Widmaier M, Wilson M, Wu CJ, Xin L, Zöllner HJ, Kaiser A.
abstractText: Synthetic data generation has become an increasingly important component of methodological development in magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS), particularly in contexts where ground-truth in vivo measurements are limited, noisy, or inaccessible. This review provides a structured overview of current practices in synthetic MRS data generation, with emphasis on the physical, biochemical, and computational assumptions that underpin commonly used models. A decomposition of synthetic MRS data is presented in terms of core building blocks, including basis sets, signal formation models, and metabolite parameter distributions such as concentration and relaxation properties. This framework is extended to advanced components required for realistic data synthesis, including baseline and nuisance signals, spatial encoding effects such as coil sensitivities and field inhomogeneities, k-space sampling and gradient imperfections, as well as sample-specific and temporal dynamics. Beyond single-voxel modeling, synthetic data generation across multiple MRS modalities is discussed, including functional MRS, diffusion-weighted MRS, and spectroscopic imaging, with emphasis on modality-specific challenges such as physiological variability, motion, and confounding signal contributions. The role of synthetic data in clinical and preclinical research, acquisition optimization, software validation, and emerging artificial intelligence applications is further examined, with particular attention to domain shift and representational realism. Current practices in validation, reporting standards, and data accessibility are also reviewed, and key gaps limiting reproducibility and interoperability across studies are identified. Overall, this work provides a unified conceptual framework for synthetic MRS data generation, clarifies underlying assumptions across modeling choices, and outlines open challenges toward improving realism, standardization, and utility in both methodological and translational applications. Conducted by the MRS Synthetic Data Working Group under the Code & Data Sharing Committee of the MRS Study Group of the International Society for Magnetic Resonance in Medicine (ISMRM), this review encompasses the existing literature, supplemented by the collective experience and in-house methodologies of its contributors, providing a community perspective that extends beyond the published record.

title: Semaglutide-Induced Weight Loss Does Not Impair Muscle Function and Improves Endurance Running Capacity in Obese Mice.
authorString: Minderis P, Cesanelli L, Sviderskis M, Venckunas T, Gray SR, Ratkevicius A.

journal.title: Journal of cachexia, sarcopenia and muscle

abstractText:
Background

Semaglutide, a member of the glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, induces substantial weight loss, primarily through appetite suppression and reduced energy intake. In addition to fat mass reduction, a considerable loss of lean body mass is also observed. How these effects compare to conventional caloric restriction is unclear. The aim of the current study was to compare the effects of semaglutide injections and energy-matched caloric restriction on skeletal muscle mass, function and exercise capacity.

Methods

An 8-month-old high-fat diet-induced obese male C57BL/6J mice were pair-fed (n = 14), with one receiving semaglutide injections (SEMA; 30 μg/kg/day) and the other undergoing energy-matched caloric restriction (CR; sham PBS injections) for 28 days. A group of obese mice (n = 12) continued unrestricted high-fat feeding and served as controls (CON). Body mass and energy intake were monitored daily. During the final week, exercise capacity was assessed using a progressive treadmill test with oxygen consumption and lactate measurements. At study completion, mice were euthanized, and slow- and fast-twitch muscles (soleus [SOL] and extensor digitorum longus [EDL]) were dissected, weighed and used for ex vivo assessment of mechanical and contractile properties.

Results

Despite similar energy intake, SEMA mice lost more body mass than CR mice (20.9 ± 4.9 vs. 14.8% ± 5.8%, p < 0.01). Both groups exhibited lower SOL muscle mass compared with CON (10.0 ± 0.7 mg; SEMA: 9.1 ± 0.8 mg, p < 0.01; CR: 9.4 ± 0.7 mg, p < 0.05), whereas EDL muscle mass was not significantly different. During the treadmill test, SEMA mice displayed higher relative VO2peak (43.4 ± 3.0 mL/min/ kg0.75) compared with CR (40.8 ± 2.6 mL/min/kg0.75, p < 0.05) and CON (38.6 ± 2.69 mL/min/kg0.75, p < 0.001), together with advantages in running distance and maximal running speed, which were largely attributable to lower body mass. SOL and EDL force, normalized to muscle mass and PCSA, did not differ between groups (SOL: 21.2 ± 2.8 N/g and 22.4 ± 3.1 N/cm2 [SEMA], 20.8 ± 2.4 N/g and 21.7 ± 2.5 N/cm2 [CR], 19.7 ± 3.5 N/g and 20.4 ± 3.7 N/cm2 [CON]; EDL: 22.8 ± 2.2 N/g and 17.0 ± 2.0 N/cm2 [SEMA], 24.5 ± 2.5 N/g and 18.2 ± 2.0 N/cm2 [CR], 22.9 ± 2.1 N/g and 16.8 ± 1.8 N/cm2 [CON]). Muscle contraction and relaxation kinetics as well as stretched induced hysteresis and relaxation were similar across groups.

Conclusions

In obese mice, semaglutide induces greater weight loss but similar muscle loss than energy-matched caloric restriction, while improving aerobic endurance without compromising skeletal muscle function.

title: Clinical Impact of the AISF STEPS-MASH Algorithm: Real-World Application in Tertiary Hepatology Practice.
authorString: Pugliese N, D'Ambrosio R, Armandi A, Liguori A, Lombardi R, Terracciani F, Pennisi G, Mantovani A, Dalbeni A, Ferri S, Perbellini R, Maffi G, Perna F, Gentilucci UV, Fracanzani A, Miele L, Bugianesi E, Lampertico P, Piscaglia F, Aghemo A, Petta S, Ravaioli F.

journal.title: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver

abstractText:
Background and aims

The approval of resmetirom and semaglutide for non-cirrhotic people living with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) and significant fibrosis has created a need for pragmatic strategies to identify treatment candidates in routine practice. We assessed the real-world applicability of the AISF STEPS-MASH algorithm and characterised the treatment status of people reaching final assessment in tertiary hepatology centres.

Methods

We retrospectively applied the AISF STEPS-MASH algorithm to all consecutive adults undergoing vibration-controlled transient elastography (VCTE) at nine Italian tertiary hepatology centres between January and June 2025. Step S defined a broad screening pool (controlled attenuation parameter [CAP] ≥ 248 dB/m and/or a metabolic referral indication). People with CAP-defined steatosis, at least one cardiometabolic risk factor or metabolic referral indication, and no documented competing liver disease aetiology were assigned to the Primary pathway; all others were analysed separately as the Non-primary pathway. Step T applied liver stiffness measurement (LSM) ≥ 8.0 kPa, excluding LSM ≥ 20.0 kPa and/or platelet count < 150 × 109/L. Step E classified safety-related conditions as label-defined contraindications, warnings requiring monitoring, or interactions requiring treatment modification or temporary deferral. Stepwise attrition across Steps S, T and E was quantified.

Results

Of 8194 people screened, 8150 (99.5%) had paired CAP and LSM data. Step S criteria were met by 4371 (53.6%), of whom 2300 entered the Primary pathway and 2071 the Non-primary pathway. Initial Step T criteria were met by 1041 people (23.8% of Step S; 12.8% of the evaluable cohort), and 750 reached the final Step T population after excluding 291 people with LSM ≥ 20.0 kPa and/or thrombocytopenia: 458 Primary and 292 Non-primary. Within the final Step T Primary pathway, 317 people (69.2%) had a treatment status compatible with both drugs without modification, 140 (30.6%) required medication or clinical optimisation, and one (0.2%) had a formal contraindication. The Non-primary pathway contained an adjudication reservoir of 191 people with an operational MASLD phenotype and a competing aetiology. The final Step T Primary pathway corresponded to 56.2 people per 1000 evaluable VCTE examinations, approximately one in every 18.

Conclusions

In tertiary hepatology practice, the AISF STEPS-MASH algorithm translated broad VCTE activity into a focused treatment-assessment population. Nearly one third of those assessed required medication or clinical optimisation before treatment, a proportion likely to vary across clinical settings, and the pathway also identified people requiring advanced liver disease surveillance or aetiological adjudication.

title: Fat Fraction Mapping in the Presence of Magnetic Field Inhomogeneities With Phase-Cycled bSSFP at 3 T.
authorString: Acikgoz BC, Mackowiak ALC, Bongiolatti-Rossi GMC, Haeussler A, Peper ES, Ledoux JB, Obmann VC, Huber AT, Vietti-Violi N, Hilbert T, Bastiaansen JAM.
abstractText: Magnetic field inhomogeneities (ΔB<sub>0</sub>) can cause fat-water swaps in proton density fat fraction (PDFF) mapping using phase-cycled balanced steady-state free-precession (bSSFP). In this work, a graph-cuts-based smoothness-imposing optimization was developed to estimate ΔB<sub>0</sub> from phase-cycled bSSFP data obtained in fat-water compartments. Data were acquired in phantoms spanning PDFF of 0%-100% to quantify robustness to ΔB<sub>0</sub> and to determine the effect of RF excitation angle (α) on PDFF estimation. The approach was further tested in healthy volunteer knee data (n = 9) and chronic liver disease patients data (n = 5). Phase-cycled bSSFP-based ΔB<sub>0</sub> and PDFF maps were compared with multi-echo gradient-echo (MEGRE) reference maps in phantoms and knees. In liver patients, PDFF maps were compared visually and by retrospective ROI analysis with reference quantitative Dixon (qDixon) PDFF maps. Estimated ΔB<sub>0</sub> maps matched the reference, with a root-mean-squared error (RMSE) of 9 ± 2 Hz for a ΔB<sub>0</sub> range of ±400 Hz in phantoms and 17 ± 4 Hz for a range of ±150 Hz in knees. PDFF mapping accuracy improved after ΔB<sub>0</sub> correction, with mean RMSE reduced from 35% ± 9% to 3.55% ± 0.92% and mean R<sup>2</sup> increased from 0.29 ± 0.3 to 0.99 ± 0 (p < 0.0001) across the six phantom experiments (mean ± SD of experiments). PDFF quantification showed significant bias for α = 5°, 40°, and 45° (bias = 2.7%, -2.9%, and -5.8%; p < 0.05), whereas no significant bias was observed for 10° ≤ α ≤ 35° (p > 0.05). Mean PDFF differences versus MEGRE reference were 2.4% ± 3%, -0.1% ± 0.8%, and 0.2% ± 0.3% for muscle, subcutaneous fat, and bone marrow, respectively.
