In liver patients, whole-liver ROI analysis demonstrated a mean PDFF difference of 3% relative to qDixon. Fat-water swaps were successfully removed in knee and patient liver PDFF maps. These results demonstrate that the proposed approach accurately estimates ΔB<sub>0</sub> and mitigates fat-water swaps in phantoms and healthy volunteer knees, while the patient liver study demonstrates the technical feasibility of the proposed framework for phase-cycled bSSFP-based PDFF mapping in vivo.

title: Left Without Treatment: An Observational Comparative Analysis of Emergency Department Patients Who Did Not Wait and the Treated Cohort.
authorString: Osman AD, Bhowmik J, Millar R, Mansouri N, Goh-Davis H, Gunarathne L, Yeak D, Ben-Meir M, Braitberg G.
abstractText:
Background

Patients who leave the Emergency Department (ED) before receiving care, known as Did Not Wait (DNW), pose potential safety risks that may reflect system pressures. Understanding differences between DNW patients and those who remain for care can inform strategies to reduce adverse outcomes.

Methods

A quantitative comparative observational study, guided by the STROBE checklist, was conducted in a quaternary ED in Victoria, Australia, comparing DNW patients with those who received treatment.

Results

Of 37,137 presentations, 1064 (2.9%) were DNW, while 36,073 (97.1%) were treated. DNW patients were younger than treated patients (median age 37 vs. 46 years; p < 0.001), and more likely to be triaged to lower acuity categories (p < 0.001). Nevertheless, 36.4% of DNW patients were triaged as Australian Triage Scale Category 3. Compared with busy conditions severe overcrowding was associated with more than double the odds of DNW (AOR = 2.53; 95% CI: 1.99-3.24; p < 0.001), while dangerously overcrowded conditions increased the odds more than 15-fold (AOR = 14.99; 95% CI: 10.15-22.05; p < 0.001).

Conclusion

Study findings suggest that extreme crowding, rather than patient characteristics, is the principal determinant of DNW. These shifts focus from descriptive patient profiling towards interpreting DNW as an indicator of system performance.

title: Small Molecule-Mediated Nrf2 Activation as a Neuroprotective Approach in Multiple Sclerosis.
authorString: Borole A, Boguszewski K, Furmanski P, Suh N.
abstractText: Multiple sclerosis is a chronic inflammatory autoimmune disease resulting in progressive demyelination of the central nervous system, leading to symptoms such as motor discoordination, cognitive deficits, and ocular dysfunction. Oxidative stress is a crucial component in the pathogenesis of multiple sclerosis, with reactive oxygen species contributing to myelin destruction, neuronal injury, and disruption of the blood-brain barrier resulting in symptom progression. For this reason, reducing oxidative stress has gained attention as a promising mechanism of disease control. Nuclear factor erythroid-2-related factor-2 (Nrf2) is a master regulator of the cellular antioxidant and anti-inflammatory response throughout the body, including the central nervous system. Nrf2 functions as a transcription factor to activate the expression of genes involved in detoxification and antioxidant defense, thus playing a critical role in limiting neuronal oxidative damage resulting from multiple sclerosis. Since no curative treatments are currently available for multiple sclerosis, recognizing potential new drugs that target earlier stages of the disease may be a viable strategy to intervene in disease progression and improve quality of life for the patient. This review explores how Nrf2 is a promising target for intervention in multiple sclerosis and that many Nrf2 activators exhibit robust efficacy, highlighting their potential as novel agents for multiple sclerosis treatment.

title: Simvastatin Alleviation of Trimethyltin-Induced Hippocampal and Behavioral Impairments via Improvement of Antioxidants, Mitochondrial Health, and Energy Homeostasis.
authorString: Salari A, Taheri M, Khalili M, Roghani M.
abstractText: Mitochondrial dysfunction and antioxidant deficiency are key contributors to the pathogenesis of Alzheimer's disease (AD). Trimethyltin (TMT) induces selective hippocampal damage associated with redox disequilibrium, neuroinflammatory responses, mitochondrial dysfunction, and impaired energy homeostasis, leading to cognitive decline. The present study evaluated whether simvastatin as a lipid-lowering and protective medicine could mitigate TMT-induced behavioral abnormalities by improving hippocampal antioxidant status, mitochondrial integrity, and energy homeostasis. Rats were assigned to control, control + simvastatin (30 mg/kg), TMT, TMT + simvastatin (10 mg/kg), and TMT + simvastatin (30 mg/kg) groups. TMT was injected IP (once, 8 mg/kg) to instigate neurotoxicity. Following three weeks of treatment, locomotor activity and conditioned learning and memory deficits were analyzed using open-field and passive avoidance tests, respectively. Besides, hippocampal levels or activity of nitrite, glutathione (GSH), glutathione peroxidase (GPx), myeloperoxidase (MPO), and β-site APP-cleaving enzyme 1 (BACE1), mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP), and AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) were measured. Simvastatin treatment (30 mg/kg) was associated with higher latency in the passive avoidance test and longer rearing in the open field test in TMT-intoxicated rats. Additionally, simvastatin improved hippocampal GSH, GPx, MMP, and AMPK and mitigated MPO activity relative to the TMT group but did not significantly affect nitrite or BACE-1 activity. Collectively, simvastatin mitigated TMT-induced neurobehavioral impairment, partly through restoration of antioxidants and mitochondrial health in association with AMPK.

title: Prevalence and Characteristics of Potential QT-Interval-Prolonging Drug-Drug Interactions in Patients Receiving Oral Anticancer Drugs.
authorString: Alhurayri F, Younis IR, Jalal SI, Logan TF, Maniar R, Bray SM, Quinney SK, Desta Z, Skaar TC, Tisdale JE, Shugg T.
abstractText:
Background

Patients with cancer are at increased risk of QT interval prolongation because of polypharmacy and concomitant use of QT-prolonging medications. Drug-drug interactions (DDIs) may further increase this risk. Outpatient electrocardiogram (ECG) monitoring appears to be underused among patients receiving oral anticancer drugs (OADs). Our study objective was to evaluate the prevalence and characteristics of potential QT interval-prolonging drug-drug interactions (QT pDDIs) in patients with cancer receiving OAD therapy.

Methods

A retrospective observational study was conducted using electronic health record data from 3697 patients with advanced cancer. Patients who received at least one OAD were included in the analysis. Potential QT-related DDIs were identified through overlap prescriptions of concomitant medications associated with QT prolongation and/or Cytochrome P450- (CYP-) or drug transporter-mediated interactions during OAD exposure. Descriptive analyses were performed to characterize the prevalence and types of QT pDDIs.

Results

Of the 3697 patients, 1732 (46.8%) received at least one OAD and were included in the analysis. Of these, 17.1% experienced at least one QT pDDI. Among those patients, 47.5% experienced PD-QT pDDIs only, 21.2% experienced PK-QT pDDIs only, and 31.3% experienced both PD- and PK-QT pDDIs during OAD exposure. Concurrent PD and PK mechanisms occurred simultaneously in 30.6% of patients with QT-pDDIs. Approximately 48% of identified QT pDDIs involved at least one OAD, most commonly pazopanib (13.5%), palbociclib (11.3%), and vandetanib (8.4%).

Conclusion

QT pDDIs were common among patients with cancer receiving OADs, highlighting the importance of comprehensive DDI screening, careful medication review, and enhanced cardiac monitoring strategies in oncology practice.

title: Exploring Capability, Opportunity and Motivation in Weight-Related Communication: Service User and Staff Experiences in a UK-Based Secure Mental Health Unit.
authorString: Mak NKN, Dibb B, Stokes N, Barley EA, Zasada M.

journal.title: International journal of mental health nursing

abstractText: Excess weight and related health conditions are highly prevalent in secure mental health settings, yet engaging service users in weight-related discussions remains challenging. Nursing staff are well placed to lead these conversations, but must navigate competing priorities, role boundaries and concerns about negative responses, while service users may experience cognitive and motivational difficulties. This study examined barriers and enablers to weight-related discussions from the perspectives of service users and nursing staff within UK-based low- and medium-secure units. A qualitative design was used. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 20 service users and 10 nursing staff. Data were analysed using framework analysis informed by behavioural theory to identify factors influencing engagement in weight-related communication. Findings showed that engagement was shaped by interacting individual, relational and organisational factors. Nursing staff identified communication skills, experience and access to resources as key enablers but reported barriers including limited training, competing demands and concerns about damaging therapeutic relationships. Service users described barriers including cognitive challenges, environmental restrictions and beliefs about medication-related weight gain, alongside motivational factors such as emotional eating. Across both groups, relational dynamics, including trust, power and communication style, were central in determining whether discussions were initiated and sustained. Within this unit context, weight-related discussions in secure mental health settings are not solely clinical tasks but relational practices. Improving engagement requires strengthening staff communication skills, creating supportive environments and embedding collaborative, personalised approaches within routine care. While findings reflect a single UK setting, the relational and structural mechanisms identified offer transferable insights for co-designing physical health communication strategies across similar secure mental health services.

title: The Psychological and Relational Impact of Mayer-Rokitansky-Kuster-Hauser Syndrome: Perspectives of Patients, Mothers and Partners.
authorString: Li K, Wakefield CE, McGill BC, Deans R.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Aust N Z J Obstet Gynaecol
journal.title: The Australian & New Zealand journal of obstetrics & gynaecology
journal.isoabbreviation: Aust N Z J Obstet Gynaecol

abstractText:
Background

Mayer-Rokitansky-Küster-Hauser syndrome (MRKHS) is a rare reproductive disorder with long-term psychosocial impacts. However, understanding of family and partner relationships that integrates the perspectives of patients, parents, and partners remains limited.

Aims

To evaluate the psychosocial impact of MRKHS with a focus on psychological and relational functioning, from patient, parent, and partner perspectives in an Australian cohort.

Materials and methods

Patients with MRKHS aged ≥ 18 years (n = 23), their parents (n = 8), and partners (n = 3) were recruited from a tertiary centre in Sydney, Australia. Three tailored questionnaires used validated self-report measures to assess physical and psychological health, family functioning, relationship satisfaction, fertility-related quality of life (QoL), sexual function, and personal identity. Comparison data were drawn from published validation studies.

Results

Patients with MRKHS reported comparable self-perceived health and relationship satisfaction to reference groups, but higher anxiety (p = 0.002), more significant dyspareunia (p = 0.006), and poorer perceived family functioning (p < 0.001). They reported better overall fertility-related QoL than couples undergoing fertility treatment (p = 0.03) but had lower scores on the relationship subscale (p = 0.002). MRKHS had a central impact shaping self-identity (p = 0.002). Mothers and partners reported positive wellbeing and family or relationship functioning, although the findings are preliminary due to the limited sample size.

Conclusion

MRKHS affects multiple facets of patients' lives, particularly psychological well-being, pain-related sexual function, family dynamics, and personal identity. Optimal care should incorporate tailored psychological support and facilitate open communication between patients and their support network. Larger studies are warranted to examine the psychological impact of MRKHS on parents and partners.

title: Operationalizing a Framework for Appraising Seriousness to Guide Decision-Making in Prenatal Care.
authorString: Kleiderman E, Laberge AM, Newson AJ, Freeman L, Ravitsky V, Boardman F.
abstractText: The seriousness of a genetic condition plays an important role in shaping expectant parents' understanding of results and options following prenatal testing. Yet it is well recognized that the decisions that follow such testing can be fraught. One key concern is that prenatal care professionals can emphasize biomedical or clinical interpretations of seriousness at the expense of more contextual elements as they relate to the circumstances and values of expectant parents. In this article, we draw on three exemplar clinical case studies to demonstrate how a framework for considering seriousness can be employed to expand the breadth and depth of conversations between prenatal care professionals and expectant parents, encourage shared meaning-making around seriousness, and support expectant parents to navigate prenatal decision-making in a way that aligns with their preferences, values, and circumstances. Our framework provides an underpinning structure to the conversations and conceptual spaces in which parental perceptions of seriousness are contextualized and animated. This, in turn, can lead to more effective counseling and improved decision-making based on relevant and contextualized information.

title: Practical Tools for Using Evidence of Mechanisms to Establish Correlations.
authorString: Illari P, Russo F.

journal.title: Journal of evaluation in clinical practice

abstractText:
Rationale

Evidential pluralism is the view according to which we need to think about varieties of evidence. Specifically, to establish causal claims (in medicine and elsewhere), we need evidence of correlation and evidence of mechanisms. The publication of Parkkinen et al. (2018) marked an important moment in the debate, establishing EBM+ as a methodological approach able to expand mainstream methods of evidence-based medicine to seriously consider evidence of mechanism, alongside evidence of correlation. After that, however, some publications strengthen the distinction between evidence of correlation and evidence of mechanism.

Aims and objectives

In this paper, we aim to return to the original formulations of evidential pluralism and to stress how much evidence of correlation and of mechanism are intertwined, rather than separated.

Method

We explain why practical tools that were originally developed in Parkkinen et al. (2018) can prove very useful in assessing evidence, without presupposing strict and artificial separations of kinds of evidence, and even in cases with partial knowledge. We use research on the effects of vitamin D deficiency as an illustration, although our arguments are very general in character.

Results and conclusion

Our thesis is that evidence of mechanism is in fact necessary to establish good quality evidence of correlation, in the sense that considerations about mechanisms inform the choice of variables and their measurement in essential ways, in any correlational study.

title: Prediction Beyond Established Models in Steatotic Liver Disease: Which New Predictors Add Value?
authorString: Zifan A, Liatsis P.

journal.title: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver

abstractText:
Background & aims

Biomarkers, non-invasive tests (NITs), imaging, genetics and machine learning are increasingly used for risk stratification in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and related liver disease, yet their incremental predictive value beyond established models remains unclear. We developed an evidence map to characterise incremental predictive value beyond established clinical models.

Methods

We searched PubMed using four search families, supplemented by ClinicalTrials.gov and seed-literature/backward-citation searching. Searches covered January 2000 through August 26, 2026 without a language restriction. Records were normalised, deduplicated and processed through deterministic prescreening followed by a downstream targeted-selection stage; the archived workflow does not preserve the exact final targeting rule used to define the structured analytic corpus. A locally hosted large language model (LLM) pipeline extracted prespecified evidence fields, with deterministic consistency checks and study-level adjudication of all 44 full-text candidates. A post hoc blinded audit of 100 analytic records assessed agreement between the automated candidate flag and blinded reference adjudication.

Results

Of 3230 unique discovery records, 1352 entered structured analysis and 44 underwent full-text adjudication. Twenty-two (50.0%) demonstrated incremental predictive value, including 15 without reported validation, 5 with internal validation and 2 with independent external or temporal validation. The latter represented 2/44 (4.5%) of strict full-text candidates and 2/1352 (0.15%) of the structured analytic corpus; the 0.15% figure is an evidence-funnel yield, not a prevalence estimate. The two independently validated studies addressed distinct contexts: PNPLA3/TM6SF2 augmentation of established non-invasive fibrosis tests for advanced fibrosis in MASLD with type 2 diabetes, and the Non-Invasive CSPH Estimated Risk (NICER) model incorporating spleen stiffness measurement (SSM) for clinically significant portal hypertension (CSPH) in compensated advanced chronic liver disease. Calibration was explicitly identifiable in 6 of 22 incremental studies; 5 were judged adequate and 1 unclear.

Conclusions

The literature contains substantial incremental model development but limited independently validated evidence of added predictive value beyond established frameworks. The two validated studies should be interpreted within their distinct populations, endpoints and clinical pathways.

title: [Prenatal and postnatal phenotypes of a child with Genitopatellar syndrome due to variant of KAT6B gene and literature review].
authorString: Hu L, Wang N, Lu W, He H, Ying Y, Fang Y, Shen B.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Zhonghua Yi Xue Yi Chuan Xue Za Zhi
journal.title: Zhonghua yi xue yi chuan xue za zhi = Zhonghua yixue yichuanxue zazhi = Chinese journal of medical genetics
journal.isoabbreviation: Zhonghua Yi Xue Yi Chuan Xue Za Zhi

abstractText:
Objective

To explore the clinical information and genetic characteristics of a child with Genitopatellar syndrome (GPS) and summarize relevant findings through a literature review.

Methods

A child with GPS diagnosed at the Department of Neonatology of Taizhou Hospital in Zhejiang Province in February 2024 was selected as study subject. Clinical data were collected, and trio Whole-exome sequencing (trio-WES) was carried out. Based on guidelines from the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG), the pathogenicity of candidate variant was assessed. Amino acid conservation was analyzed using MEGA, and three-dimensional structures of the wild-type and mutant proteins were predicted and compared using AlphaFold3 and PyMOL. A retrospective analysis was also conducted by searching the PubMed, Wanfang Data Knowledge Service Platform, and China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI) databases for case reports or studies of genetically confirmed GPS. This study was approved by the Medical Ethics Committee of the hospital (Ethics No.: L2024-10-06-01).

Results

The patient, a one-day-old male, had presented with genital abnormalities, clubfoot, polycystic kidneys, atrial septal defect, and agenesis of corpus callosum. Increased nuchal translucency and cervical lymphatic hygroma were detected during the first trimester of pregnancy. Trio-WES results revealed that he has harbored a de novo heterozygous c.3696del (p.Glu1233LysfsTer10) frameshift variant in exon 18 of the KAT6B gene (NM_012330.4). The variant was previously unreported, and its frequency in the general East Asian population has not been documented. Based on the ACMG guidelines, the variant was classified as likely pathogenic (evidence criteria including PS, PM, and PP). Protein homologous sequence alignment analysis suggested the variant site to be highly conserved across multiple species. Homology modeling and structural comparison further revealed varying degrees of change in the hydrogen bonding of amino acids adjacent to the variant site and in the two- and three-dimensional structures of the protein. Literature review has identified 19 patients, with the study cohort comprising 16 survivors (10 males, 6 females) and 3 non-survivors (1 male, 2 females). All patients exhibited varying degrees of genital anomalies, facial dysmorphism, corpus callosum dysgenesis, and flexion contractures of the hips and knees (19/19, 100.0%). Developmental delay/intellectual disability was observed in 17 patients (17/19, 89.5%), hydronephrosis/multiple renal cysts in 16 patients (16/19, 84.2%), patellar hypoplasia in 15 patients (15/19, 78.9%), congenital heart disease in 13 patients (13/19, 68.4%), and prenatal abnormalities were detected in 8 patients (8/19, 42.1%). Current management of the disease is primarily supportive and symptomatic, with the most effective measures including oxygen therapy, gastrostomy tube feeding support, and joint corrective surgeries.

Conclusion

The c.3696del (p.Glu1233LysfsTer10) variant of the KAT6B gene probably underlay the pathogenesis of GPS in this child. Above finding has expanded the genotypic and phenotypic spectra of this syndrome. GPS may present with increased nuchal translucency accompanied by cystic hygroma during the first trimester. Additionally, the literature review in this study has systematically summarized the prenatal and postnatal phenotypic features, poor prognosis, and current clinical interventions for GPS, which may provide more robust evidence-based support for clinical diagnosis, treatment strategy selection, and prognostic evaluation.

title: Acute reduction in inferior vena cava diameter following alcohol consumption: a substudy of a pilot cluster-randomized trial
authorString: Shimada K, Hadano T, Yoshimoto H, Iioka Y, Minami K, Inaba T, Kodaira T, Gosho M, Fukuda T, Komano Y, Umeda K, Iwase M, Kusano Y, Kawabata T.
abstractText: Background Acute alcohol consumption induces cardiovascular and diuretic effects; however, its influence on intravascular volume distribution remains poorly understood. Inferior vena cava (IVC) ultrasonography is a non-invasive method for assessing intravascular volume status, but changes in IVC morphology following alcohol consumption have not previously been investigated. This study evaluated acute changes in IVC measurements and vital signs after alcohol consumption. Methods This prespecified physiological substudy analyzed 59 healthy adult social drinkers enrolled in a pilot cluster-randomized trial. Maximum IVC diameter and respiratory collapsibility were assessed immediately before and after a standardized 2-hour ad libitum drinking session. Heart rate, blood pressure, breath alcohol concentration, and alcohol intake were serially measured throughout the session. Exploratory univariable linear regression analyses were performed to identify factors associated with post-drinking IVC diameter and changes in IVC diameter. Results Maximum IVC diameter significantly decreased after alcohol consumption, from 14.4 ± 3.4 mm to 10.8 ± 3.0 mm (paired t test, P  < 0.001). The proportion of participants with respiratory collapsibility ≥ 50% increased from 79.3% to 91.4%, although this difference was not statistically significant (McNemar's test, P  = 0.096). During alcohol consumption, heart rate and shock index gradually increased, whereas systolic and diastolic blood pressure decreased. In exploratory analyses, pre-drinking maximum IVC diameter was the strongest predictor of post-drinking IVC measurements and was inversely associated with the change in IVC diameter from baseline (β = −0.653; 95% CI, − 0.862 to − 0.444; P  < 0.001). Conclusions Acute alcohol consumption was associated with a significant reduction in maximum IVC diameter, suggesting alterations in intravascular volume distribution beyond previously recognized cardiovascular responses. The magnitude of this reduction was strongly associated with pre-drinking IVC diameter, highlighting the potential importance of baseline intravascular volume status in determining the physiological response to alcohol.

title: ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI PET/CT in cardiac Anderson-Fabry disease: novel insights into disease assessment from a case series.
authorString: Fortuna I, Soeiro P, Moreira H, Faria T, Santos J, Vasconcelos M, Marques C, Oliveira A, Oliveira JP, Martins E.
abstractText: Anderson-Fabry disease (AFD) is an X-linked lysosomal disorder in which cardiac involvement is the main cause of morbidity and mortality, manifesting as left ventricular hypertrophy, heart failure, arrhythmias, and myocardial fibrosis. Myocardial fibrosis is a key pathophysiological process associated with an adverse prognosis. While cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) identifies established myocardial fibrosis, fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (FAPI) PET enables the molecular assessment of FAP-associated activity. By complementing conventional CMR parameters, including late gadolinium enhancement and native T1 mapping, FAPI PET may improve the characterization and phenotypic classification of cardiac involvement in Anderson-Fabry disease. We report three cases of AFD patients, who underwent Gallium-68-fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (⁶⁸Ga-FAPI) PET-CT as part of a prospective study designed to assess myocardial fibrosis. Overall, ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI uptake closely correlated with CMR findings, reinforcing the role of cardiac fibroblast activation as a relevant pathogenic mechanism in AFD. These findings highlight this new molecular imaging as a promising tool for early detection, risk stratification, and therapeutic guidance in AFD.

title: Embolic stroke and breakthrough thrombosis on direct oral anticoagulants in Libman-Sacks endocarditis associated with antiphospholipid syndrome: a case-based review.
authorString: Angelopoulou F, Stathopoulou D, Vlachogiorgos K, Almpanis G.
abstractText: Libman-Sacks endocarditis (LSE) is a characteristic cardiac manifestation of antiphospholipid syndrome (APS), but its presentation and management in the era of direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are poorly characterised. We describe a 37-year-old man with obesity, type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease and recurrent unprovoked deep vein thrombosis who developed multiple embolic strokes while taking rivaroxaban. Transoesophageal echocardiography showed a sessile aortic valve mass; repeated blood cultures and <sup>18</sup>F-FDG PET-CT were negative, and lupus anticoagulant was the only antiphospholipid antibody detected (probable APS). He was switched to low-molecular-weight heparin and acenocoumarol and the mass was excised; histology showed an organised fibrinous thrombotic vegetation, although papillary fibroelastoma could not be fully excluded. Following the CABARET recommendations, we searched MEDLINE/PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science and DOAJ for reports published between January 2020 and September 2026 and included 62 case reports/series (63 patients) and four cohort studies. Median age was 40 years (range 19-78); 22/60 patients (37%) were men; 34/63 (54%) had primary APS and 6 (10%) catastrophic APS. When reported, the antibody profile was triple-positive in 22/39 (56%) and lupus-anticoagulant-only in 4/39 (10%). The mitral valve was involved in 41/62 (66%), the aortic in 19/62 (31%) and the tricuspid in 7/62 (11%). Ischaemic stroke occurred in 29/63 (46%) and heart failure or severe valve dysfunction in 31/63 (49%). Of 16 patients anticoagulated at diagnosis, 10 (63%) were receiving a DOAC. Valve intervention was performed in 35/63 (56%) and 4/63 (6%) died. LSE should be sought in patients with APS who have embolic events, particularly while on DOACs; the evidence remains observational.

title: Benchmarking heart failure care: the ANZACS-QI Heart Failure Registry Pilot implementation and results (ANZACS-QI 86).
authorString: Easton A, Kerr AJ, Wells S, Doughty RN, McLachlan A, Morgan M, Balzat U, Brannigan H, Adkin S, Lund M, Poppe KK, Harwood M, Grey C, Selak V, Harrison W, Chan DZ.
abstractText:
Aims

Heart failure is a major healthcare problem in Aotearoa New Zealand. As therapies advance and become increasingly complex it is essential that we systematically characterise phenotype and monitor adherence to relevant guidelines to drive quality improvement. Here we report the results of the ANZACS-QI Heart Failure Registry Pilot, implemented in Northern Region hospitals.

Methods

Age-stratified random sampling was used to identify a representative cohort of patients hospitalised with heart failure (2022 and 2023) using national administrative datasets. The electronic clinical records were reviewed and data entered into the web-based registry. Pre-specified outcomes that were analysed included rates of left ventricular assessment (left ventricular ejection fraction [LVEF]) and prescription of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT).

Results

The cohort comprised 328 patients and registry form completion rates were high (98%). LVEF assessment rates within 2 years of the index hospital discharge were 81%. Of those with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction that survived until discharge (n=137), only 13 (9%) met the composite medication indicator of being prescribed (or with documented contraindication/intolerance) all four GDMT classes. This was largely driven by 92 (67%) being ineligible for subsidy for sodium glucose co-transporter-2 inhibitors; however, prescription rates of the other GDMT classes were suboptimal.

Conclusions

Our study highlights that there is a considerable gap between guideline recommendations and real-world practice. Following pilot completion, performance indicators have been established and the registry has expanded with the goal for it to become national. The successful implementation of the registry is an important step in quality improvement for patients hospitalised with heart failure.

title: Postoperative Troponin Elevation Predicts 30-Day and 12-Month Mortality in Geriatric Patients Undergoing Hip Fracture Surgery: A 339-Patient Cohort Study
authorString: Keidan T, Amster-Kahn H, Rosen K, Ramroth-Stich N, Yilmaz E, Koenigshausen M, Spieckermann A, Schildhauer TA, Koutras C.
abstractText:
Purpose: Postoperative myocardial injury after noncardiac surgery (MINS) is a frequent but often silent complication associated with increased mortality. Older adults undergoing hip fracture surgery represent a high-risk trauma population with limited physiological reserve, in whom even small postoperative troponin elevations may reflect clinically meaningful cardiac stress. This study examined the association between postoperative troponin elevation and mortality following surgery for low-energy hip fractures in geriatric patients.

Methods:

We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of 339 geriatric patients who underwent operative treatment for proximal femur fractures between June 2017 and January 2020. Demographic data were collected directly from patients at hospital intake and supplemented with information from the national israeli health maintenance organization (HMO) registry. Cardiac troponin I (cTnI) levels were routinely measured within 72 hours postoperatively. MINS was defined as cTnI > 30 ng/dL irrespective of ischemic symptoms. Mortality data (30-day and 12-month all-cause death) were obtained from the HMO. Logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of mortality.

Results:

MINS occurred in 45.7% (155/339) of patients. MINS-positive patients were older, had a higher comorbidity burden, and more frequently had ischemic heart disease or peripheral vascular disease. Mortality was significantly higher among MINS-positive patients at both 30 days (21.9% vs. 3.8%) and 12 months (48.4% vs. 14.7%) compared with MINS-negative patients (both p  < 0.01). In multivariable analysis, MINS was the strongest independent predictor of mortality at 30 days (OR 9.03) and 12 months (OR 6.06). Kaplan–Meier curves demonstrated significantly reduced survival in the MINS-positive group.

Conclusions:

Postoperative myocardial injury is associated with increased short- and long-term all-cause mortality, even in the absence of typical ischemic symptoms. Routine postoperative troponin measurement may help identify high-risk orthopedic trauma patients who could benefit from closer monitoring and optimized postoperative management.

title: Mortality due to sepsis is increasing among patients with cirrhosis compared with other chronic diseases: US trends, 1999-2024.
authorString: Ouranos K, Nakapakorn C, Michael M, Koutouratsas T, Mylona EK, Shehadeh F, Kodali S, Victor DW, Noureddin M, Kalligeros M, Simonetto DA, Olson JC, Asrani SK, Mylonakis E, Patidar KR.
abstractText:
Background

Sepsis is a major contributor to death across chronic diseases, but population-level trends in sepsis-associated mortality among decedents with cirrhosis relative to other chronic conditions remain incompletely characterized. We evaluated US national trends in sepsis-associated mortality among decedents with cirrhosis, congestive heart failure (CHF), and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).

Methods

We analyzed the CDC WONDER Multiple Cause-of-Death database (1999-2024) to identify decedents with cirrhosis, CHF, or COPD, and sepsis as a contributing cause of death. Age-adjusted sepsis-related mortality rates per 100,000 US population were calculated, and Joinpoint regression estimated average annual percent change (AAPC). Prespecified analyses evaluated trends by age, sex, race, liver disease etiology, and infection source.Results:Sepsis-related mortality increased most rapidly in decedents with cirrhosis, with an AAPC more than 4-fold higher than CHF [AAPC 3.29% (95% CI 2.96-3.54) vs. 0.78% (95% CI 0.34-1.21)], while COPD showed no significant increase [AAPC -0.12% (95% CI -0.62 to 0.23)]. Among decedents with cirrhosis, mortality increased across demographics, particularly among American Indian/Alaska Native individuals, White individuals, females, and adults aged ≥65 years. Source-specific increases in cirrhosis were greatest for genitourinary infections, followed by pneumonia and intra-abdominal infections. By cirrhosis etiology, the steepest increases occurred in MASLD [AAPC 11.36% (95% CI 9.46-13.30)], followed by alcohol-associated liver disease [AAPC 5.04% (95% CI 4.45-5.61)].

Conclusions

At the population level, average age-adjusted sepsis-related mortality increased substantially faster in decedents with cirrhosis than in CHF and COPD, with the greatest increases observed in decedents with MASLD and alcohol-associated liver disease. As the epidemiology of chronic liver disease shifts, cirrhosis is emerging as a critical target for sepsis prevention, earlier recognition, and disease-specific care pathways aimed at improving survival.

title: Study on Effective Factors of Secondary Prevention in Ischemic Stroke Recurrence
authorString: Mamdouhi V, Sahrai H, Hashemilar M, Rostami R, Esfanjani RM, Farhoudi M.
abstractText: Background and Aim: Recurrent ischemic stroke is a major contributor to long-term disability and healthcare burden. Identifying clinical and modifiable factors associated with recurrence is essential for improving secondary prevention. This study aimed to investigate factors associated with recurrent ischemic stroke, with particular emphasis on vascular risk factors, stroke severity, rehabilitation, lifestyle modification, and adherence to preventive pharmacotherapy. Methods In this retrospective case-control study, 194 patients admitted with ischemic stroke to Imam Reza Training Hospital, Tabriz, Iran, between 2016 and 2023 were evaluated. The study included 97 patients with recurrent ischemic stroke. Demographic characteristics, vascular risk factors, National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS), modified Rankin Scale (mRS), rehabilitation utilization, lifestyle factors, and use of secondary prevention medications were assessed. Between-group and within-patient comparisons were performed using appropriate parametric and non-parametric statistical tests. Results A history of hypertension was more common among patients with recurrent stroke than controls (83.5% vs. 60.8%, p < 0.001). Patients who subsequently experienced recurrent stroke had lower NIHSS scores at initial admission (median 8 vs. 10, p = 0.057) and at discharge (median 5 vs. 9, p = 0.003) than controls. Among patients with recurrent stroke, stroke severity increased at the time of recurrence, with median NIHSS increasing from 8 to 10 (p = 0.019). During the interval between the first and recurrent stroke, use of anticoagulants decreased from 28.6% to 17.5% (p < 0.001), lipid-lowering therapy from 70.1% to 49.5% (p = 0.001), and antiplatelet therapy from 72.2% to 48.4% (p < 0.001). At recurrence, fasting blood glucose increased from 109 to 117 mg/dL (p < 0.001), while HDL cholesterol decreased from 36 to 33 mg/dL (p = 0.002). Conclusion Recurrent ischemic stroke was associated with hypertension, a history of previous cerebrovascular events, reduced use of secondary prevention medications, lower utilization of inpatient rehabilitation, and adverse metabolic changes. Although patients who subsequently experienced recurrence initially had less severe strokes than controls, neurological severity increased at the recurrent event. These findings highlight the importance of sustained pharmacological treatment, vascular risk-factor control, and rehabilitation as components of secondary stroke prevention. Prospective multicenter studies are warranted to determine the extent to which improving adherence and risk-factor management can reduce recurrence.

title: Addressing Disparities in Hypertension Control: The Potential Role of New Drugs and Devices in 2026 and Beyond.
authorString: Odo CC, Reddy T, Ogunniyi MO, Ferdinand KC, Ilonze OJ.
abstractText:
Purpose of review

Hypertension is the leading modifiable cardiovascular risk factor in the United States, with racially/ethnically diverse populations experiencing a disproportionate burden, associated with social, structural, and potentially biological determinants. This review examines how recently approved and investigational pharmacologic therapies and device-based interventions may advance hypertension control in 2026 and beyond, with deliberate attention to the strength and applicability of the available evidence in racially/ ethnically diverse populations.

Recent findings

Aldosterone synthesis and mineralocorticoid receptor signaling represent important advances beyond the present guidelines for resistant hypertension and cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic risk reduction. For instance, baxdrostat, a recently approved aldosterone synthase inhibitor (ASI), has demonstrated clinically meaningful blood pressure reductions. In addition, lorundrostat, an investigational ASI, provides a model for racially representative trial design through the intentional enrollment of Black and Hispanic/Latino participants and consistent efficacy across racial subgroups. In contrast, pivotal finerenone trials demonstrated improved cardiac and renal outcomes but included limited representation of Black adults. Additional approved therapies include an agent targeting the endothelin pathway, aprocitentan, and device-based interventions via renal denervation therapy, although their effectiveness in diverse populations remains unknown. Therapies targeting natriuretic peptide signaling remain investigational but could potentially expand the therapeutic landscape. Advances in antihypertensive therapy offer new opportunities to improve blood pressure control and reduce cardiovascular risk beyond the 2025 American Heart Association (AHA) and American College of Cardiology (ACC) AHA/ACC High Blood Pressure Guideline-directed approach. Ensuring equitable benefit from these innovations requires that therapeutic innovation be coupled with deliberate efforts to ensure equitable delivery and benefit across populations.

title: Dexmedetomidine-associated bradycardia in perioperative and critical care settings: a cross-database pharmacovigilance study using FAERS and JADER.
authorString: Ye C, Zhang S, Zhu J, Wang M, Sun J, Xu Y.
abstractText: Dexmedetomidine (DEX) is a highly selective α2-adrenoceptor agonist widely used for sedation in perioperative and critical care settings. Although bradycardia is a recognised adverse effect, its temporal reporting patterns and associated clinical characteristics remain incompletely characterised. This study investigated DEX-associated bradycardia using two independent spontaneous reporting systems. We conducted a retrospective pharmacovigilance study using the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) and the Japanese Adverse Drug Event Report (JADER) database from 2004Q1 to 2025Q3. Reports suggestive of perioperative or critical care use were identified using predefined proxy indicators. Disproportionality analyses were performed to detect cardiovascular safety signals. Time to onset (TTO) patterns were evaluated using Weibull modelling, and factors associated with bradycardia reporting were examined using multivariable case-non-case logistic regression. Sensitivity analyses assessed the consistency of the findings. Among 2505 DEX reports, 717 involved bradycardia-associated events (FAERS, n = 327; JADER, n = 390). Bradycardia showed prominent disproportionality signals in both databases. Among 198 reports with valid TTO data, the median onset time was 0 days in both databases, with similar Weibull shape parameters (FAERS, β = 0.849; JADER, β = 0.847), suggesting early clustering of reported events. Pre-existing cardiovascular disease showed the strongest adjusted association with bradycardia reporting (OR 4.88, 95% CI 3.92-6.09), followed by concomitant opioid use (OR 1.74, 95% CI 1.37-2.22) and β-adrenoceptor blocker exposure (OR 1.85, 95% CI 1.08-3.13). These associations were generally consistent across sensitivity analyses. DEX-associated bradycardia showed consistent reporting signals across FAERS and JADER, with reported onset times frequently concentrated near treatment initiation. Cardiovascular disease and concomitant opioid or β-adrenoceptor blocker exposure were associated with higher odds of bradycardia reporting. Although spontaneous reporting data cannot establish causality or quantify incidence, these findings provide complementary post-marketing evidence supporting careful cardiovascular assessment and haemodynamic monitoring during DEX administration.

title: Fresh frozen plasma administration during cardiopulmonary bypass was not associated with postoperative transfusion requirements after elective total aortic arch replacement: a retrospective cohort study.
authorString: Kato M, Nakaoku Y, Ogata S, Nishimura K, Maeda T.
abstractText:
Purpose

Cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) during total aortic arch replacement (TAR) is associated with coagulopathy. We investigated whether fresh frozen plasma (FFP) administration during CPB was associated with postoperative transfusion requirements and coagulation profiles after TAR.

Methods

This single-center retrospective cohort study included adult patients who underwent elective TAR. Patients were categorized according to whether FFP was administered during CPB. The primary outcome was postoperative FFP transfusion from CPB separation to 12 h after intensive care unit admission. Secondary outcomes included perioperative plasma-derived product use, postoperative bleeding, re-exploration for bleeding, and serial coagulation parameters. Multivariable regression analyses were performed to adjust for potential confounders.

Results

Data from 156 patients were analyzed, including 111 patients in the Pre-FFP group and 45 in the Control group. Baseline characteristics were generally comparable, although deep hypothermic circulatory arrest duration and CPB fluid management differed between the groups. The adjusted mean difference in total post-CPB FFP transfusion units between the Pre-FFP and Control groups was - 1.54 units (95% confidence interval, - 7.51 to 4.43). No significant differences were observed in perioperative plasma-derived product use or bleeding outcomes. Although fibrinogen concentrations were higher and activated partial thromboplastin time and prothrombin time-international normalized ratio were shorter at the end of CPB in the Pre-FFP group, these differences largely resolved after CPB.

Conclusion

FFP administration during CPB was associated with transient improvement in coagulation parameters but was not associated with postoperative transfusion requirements or bleeding outcomes in adult patients undergoing elective TAR. Larger studies are needed to confirm these findings.

title: Emerging mechanisms of megakaryocyte and platelet production.
authorString: Lu S, Ravid K.
abstractText: Studies have shown that megakaryopoiesis has expanded beyond the traditional thrombopoietin-driven pathway, revealing a complex developmental state and local context that, together, determine megakaryocyte (MK) maturation and platelet production. As understanding of this field grows, so does its impact on platelet-associated disease. This review outlines some emerging regulators of MK development and platelet biogenesis, culminating with their relevance to advancing in vitro platelet production. Newly identified regulators have linked MK maturation to its microenvironment through mechanosensitive ion channels and integrins as well as to its metabolic state through redox balance, lipid remodeling, and mitochondrial function. Additionally, transcriptional, posttranscriptional, and inflammatory factors contribute significantly to MK development. In platelet biogenesis, studies continue the ongoing debate over pulmonary contributions while defining new cytoskeletal and metabolic regulators of proplatelet formation. Efforts to generate platelets in vitro have also increased with development of systems utilizing induced pluripotent stem cells, bioreactors, and molecular signals but remain limited by inefficient generation of activatable platelets. Megakaryopoiesis and thrombopoiesis are context-dependent processes that are influenced by microenvironmental, metabolic, transcriptional, and inflammatory factors. Defining these networks advances potential therapeutic targets for platelet disorders and development of scalable donor-independent platelet generation in vitro.

title: Phase Angle Deviation is Associated with Multidomain Disease Burden in Adults Across a Broad Age-range
authorString: Boschiero D, Boschiero A, Ilich J.
abstractText: Phase angle (PhA) is a bioelectrical parameter associated with body cell mass, fluid distribution, frailty, and adverse clinical outcomes. Because PhA varies with age and sex, absolute values are difficult to interpret. Whether deviation from age- and sex-expected PhA reflects multidomain clinical burden across adulthood is unknown. We investigated whether phase angle deviation (ΔPhA), defined as observed PhA minus age- and sex-expected PhA, is associated with the presence and accumulation of clinically confirmed diagnoses across five major clinical domains in adults 18 to 90 years. Outcomes were the presence of at least one clinically confirmed diagnosis in the cardiovascular, malignant, psychological, chronic inflammatory, or metabolic-syndrome domain and the number of domains present. Modified Poisson regression estimated adjusted Prevalence Ratios (PRs), and multivariable linear regression quantified the burden gradient. The analysis included 94,552 adults (60,803 women [64.3%]; mean [SD] age, 46.44 [15.10] years), including 51,955 controls and 42,597 participants with at least one clinical domain. Each 1° lower ΔPhA was associated with a 13.3% higher adjusted prevalence of at least one domain (PR, 1.133; 95% CI, 1.123–1.144; p < .001). Compared with controls, adjusted ΔPhA was − 0.154° with one domain, -0.209° with two, -0.317° with three, and − 0.391° with four or more domains. In conclusion, PhA values below those expected for age and sex were associated with progressively greater multidomain disease burden.

title: Percutaneous Management of a Retained Coronary Snare Fragment: Retrieval-Related Side-Branch Perforation and Migration to the External Iliac Artery: A Case Report
authorString: Kilinc AY, Aydin MT.
abstractText: Background Retained or fractured intracoronary devices are uncommon but potentially serious complications of complex percutaneous coronary intervention. Retrieval may itself cause vascular injury or systemic embolization and can require several bailout techniques. Case presentation: A 50-year-old man was referred after a chronic total occlusion intervention at another institution had been complicated by guidewire fracture and subsequent fracture of the snare used for retrieval. The retained snare fragment extended from the right coronary artery toward the aorta. Repeat snaring and a three-wire knot technique were unsuccessful. Balloon-assisted retrieval mobilized the fragment but caused disengagement of the system; the fragment escaped into the systemic circulation and was localized to the right external iliac artery. Control coronary angiography demonstrated perforation of the side branch used for balloon anchoring. Extravasation persisted despite prolonged balloon inflation, and microcatheter delivery for coil embolization was unsuccessful. The perforated branch was therefore occluded with a cut balloon. After angiographic hemostasis, the embolized snare fragment was captured with a peripheral snare and removed through the sheath. The patient remained hemodynamically stable, developed no tamponade, and had no procedure-related complication at 3 months. Conclusion This case illustrates a stepwise percutaneous strategy for a cascade of device-related complications. Maintaining control of the foreign body, rapidly reassessing the coronary circulation after device migration, prioritizing active coronary perforation, and retaining alternative embolization options when microcatheter delivery fails were central to successful management.

title: Risk Stratification, Prevalence, and Predictors of High Risk for Obstructive Sleep Apnea–Hypopnea Syndrome Among Adults With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus in Northern Uganda
authorString: Ewutia GM, Nalukenge JM, Ogwal S, Owiny D, Otika D, Okello MO, Oriba DL, Bongomin FO, Ebbs DS, Bongomin F.
abstractText: Background Obstructive sleep apnea-hypopnea syndrome (OSAHS) is a common but frequently underdiagnosed condition among adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Despite this substantial burden, the prevalence and associated factors of OSAHS among adults with T2DM in Uganda remain insufficiently documented, limiting the integration of OSAHS screening into routine diabetes care. Methods Between 1 November 2025 and 31 May 2026, we conducted a hospital-based cross-sectional study among adults with T2DM attending Gulu Regional Referral Hospital and St. Mary’s Hospital–Lacor in Gulu City, northern Uganda. Participants were consecutively enrolled using convenience sampling. OSAHS risk was assessed using the STOP-BANG questionnaire, with scores of 0–2, 3–4, and ≥ 5 indicating low-, intermediate-, and high-risk OSAHS, respectively. Anthropometric measurements, blood pressure, and random blood glucose (RBG) levels were recorded. Adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were reported, and p < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Results A total of 250 participants were enrolled, with a mean age of 54.2 ± 14.8 years. Among participants with T2DM, 18.8% (n = 47; 95% CI: 14.0%–23.6%) were at high risk for OSAHS, 41.2% (n = 103) at intermediate risk, and 40.0% (n = 100) at low risk. The most frequently reported STOP-BANG components were tiredness (66.8%), hypertension (62.0%), and snoring (44.0%), while observed apnoea, male sex, age > 50 years, neck circumference > 40 cm, and BMI > 35 kg/m² were reported in 14.4%, 19.6%, 11.2%, 2.0%, and 0.8% of participants, respectively. Male participants had a higher prevalence of high-risk OSAHS than female participants (aPR 1.399, 95% CI: 1.241–1.577; p < 0.001). Hypertension was also independently associated with high-risk OSAHS (aPR 1.168, 95% CI: 1.040–1.311; p = 0.009). Compared with single participants, widowed participants had a higher prevalence of high-risk OSAHS (aPR 1.199, 95% CI: 1.007–1.428; p = 0.042). Conclusion Nearly one in five adults with T2DM attending the two tertiary hospitals in Gulu City were at high risk for OSAHS. Routine OSAHS screening in T2DM care, particularly among men, older adults, and those with hypertension or obesity, could support earlier identification and referral, improve clinical outcomes, and reduce the burden of this treatable comorbidity.

title: Metformin in Advanced Chronic Kidney Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Pinilla J, Arslan F, Campoverde C, Napoli F, Coy Z, Hassan S, Dibo P.
abstractText: To evaluate associations of metformin exposure with all-cause mortality, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) and lactic or metabolic acidosis in adults with Type 2 diabetes and advanced CKD (estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) < 30 mL/min/1.73 m2) not receiving chronic dialysis. We searched PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science and Cochrane from inception through 5 September 2026 for observational cohort studies evaluating metformin exposure in this population. Comparator strategies included non-use, discontinuation and alternative glucose-lowering therapy. Data were synthesized using Bayesian random-effects models with empirical heterogeneity priors (primary) and frequentist random-effects models. Certainty of the evidence was assessed using the GRADE framework. Ten cohort studies were included. For ESKD, the pooled hazard ratio (HR) from the Bayesian analysis was 0.64 (95% CrI: 0.45-0.92; 99% posterior probability of HR < 1). Estimates for MACE (HR 0.88, 95% CrI: 0.72-1.08) and all-cause mortality (HR 0.89, 95% CrI: 0.73-1.10) were imprecise. Lactic or metabolic acidosis showed an increased-risk estimate with a wide CrI (HR 1.39, 95% CrI: 0.76-2.49). Certainty of the evidence was very low for all outcomes. For ESKD, the pooled Bayesian estimate was below the null, whereas estimates for all-cause mortality and MACE remained uncertain, and an increased risk of acidosis could not be excluded. Given the very low certainty of the evidence and the heterogeneity of treatment strategies, these findings should be interpreted with considerable caution. Further randomized or well-designed observational evidence using clearly defined treatment strategies is needed.

title: Peripartum Cardiomyopathy in Pakistan: A Systematic Review of Clinical Outcomes, Maternal and Obstetric Characteristics
authorString: Asare EK, Asim A, Cummings CH, Jackson L, Okeke CS, Lackland T.
abstractText: Background Peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM) is an important cause of maternal cardiovascular mortality, particularly in low- and middle-income countries due to limited access to specialized cardiac care. This systematic review aims to synthesize evidence on the proportions of mortality, recovery of left ventricular function, cardiovascular complications, and maternal and obstetric characteristics among women with PPCM in Pakistan. Methods A systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA guidelines. PubMed, Google Scholar, PakMediNet, and the Cochrane Library were searched from January 2000 to May 2026 for studies reporting PPCM outcomes in Pakistan and registered with PROSPERO (ID: CRD420261403054). Eligible studies included observational studies and case series involving women diagnosed with PPCM. Extracted data included study design, sample size, mortality, recovery of left ventricular systolic function, cardiovascular complications, and obstetric characteristics. Pooled proportions were calculated descriptively using aggregate study data. The quality of study was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist. Results Seven studies were included. Mortality outcomes were reported in six studies including 315 patients, with 49 deaths recorded, yielding an overall mortality proportion of 15.6%. Recovery of left ventricular systolic function was reported in four studies including 160 patients, of whom 97 achieved recoveries, corresponding to an overall recovery proportion of 60.6%, predominantly defined by improvement in left ventricular ejection fraction during 6–12 months of follow-up. Pulmonary edema was the most frequently reported cardiovascular complication (21.6%), while thromboembolic events (17.9%), cardiogenic shock (13.1%), ventricular tachycardia (9.9%), and atrial fibrillation (9.4%) occurred less frequently. Among the reported maternal characteristics, obesity was the most common (62.9%). Multiparity was the predominant obstetric characteristic (69.1%), whereas pregnancy-related hypertensive disorders, primigravidity, and multiple gestation were reported in 34.1%, 22.9%, and 9.7% of women, respectively. Conclusion PPCM in Pakistan remains associated with considerable mortality and a substantial burden of cardiovascular complications. Obesity, multiparity, and pregnancy-related hypertensive disorders were the predominant maternal and obstetric characteristics, highlighting the importance of early recognition, timely cardiac assessment, and multidisciplinary care to improve maternal outcomes. Clinical trial registration Not applicable.

title: Prehabilitation Beneficial Effects in Patients Undergoing Cardiac Surgery: A Systematic Review.
authorString: Patsaki I, Mitsiou G, Kourek C, Andrikopoulos A, Raidou V, Koulopoulou M, Avgerinos D, Panagiotou C, Dimopoulos S.
abstractText: Cardiac surgery is associated with postoperative functional impairment that affects quality of life. Prehabilitation programmes may improve functional recovery in patients undergoing cardiac surgery who are at risk of postoperative complications. This systematic review aimed to present current evidence on the effectiveness of prehabilitation programmes in patients undergoing elective cardiac surgery. PubMed, Scopus and ScienceDirect were searched for relevant studies according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses statement and the Cochrane Collaboration Handbook. Eligible studies included adults undergoing cardiac surgery who participated in a prehabilitation programme. Only randomised controlled trials or clinical trials published in English were included. Outcomes of interest were respiratory function, exercise capacity and length of stay. Methodological quality was assessed using the PEDro (Physiotherapy Evidence Database) scale. The study was registered with the Open Science Framework (DOI: 10.17605/OSF.IO/NV3GF). The search identified 658 studies, of which 19 met the inclusion criteria. Most studies used inspiratory muscle training as the preoperative intervention. Prehabilitation significantly increased maximal inspiratory pressure in six studies and the 6-minute walk test in five of seven studies, while reducing mechanical ventilation duration in six studies, intensive care unit length of stay in four of seven studies and postoperative pulmonary complications. Methodological quality was moderate, with a median score of 5 (range, 2-8). Prehabilitation exercise-based programmes improve inspiratory muscle strength and functional capacity while reducing postoperative pulmonary complications, mechanical ventilation duration and intensive care unit length of stay.

title: Impact of SGLT2 Inhibitors on Renal Function in Patients with Heart Failure: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authorString: Sinha A, Desai N, Nadarajah R, Levya F, Patel PA.
abstractText:
Aims

Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors are an integral part of heart failure (HF) therapy. The purpose of this study was to elucidate the effect of SGLT2 inhibitors on renal function, in HF patients, over longer-term follow-up. This could be compared to existing data in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) and type 2 diabetes mellitus T2DM.

Methods

A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted in patients with HF treated with SGLT2 inhibitor (PROSPERO ID: CRD42024562311). Searches were performed across five databases from inception to 31 October 2024 identifying randomised controlled trials. Included studies were appraised using the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool. Two primary outcomes were investigated, composite renal event and AKI (acute kidney injury). Relative risk (RR) was pooled with 95% CI using the statistical software 'R'.

Results

Thirteen trials involving 90,413 participants were included. Median follow-up was 2.3 years, and data of 32,957 patients with HF was extracted. In patients with HF, SGLT2 inhibition reduced renal specific composite outcomes by 28% (RR 0.72; 95% CI 0.57-0.91). Additionally, AKI was reduced in HF patients taking SGLT2 inhibitors (RR 0.75; 95% CI 0.65-0.86). Subgroup analysis showed no differences in patients with and without HF, or when stratified by baseline renal function.

Conclusion

These results encourage use of SGLT2 inhibitors to retard progression of kidney disease and AKI. This benefit was seen in all trials, irrespective of concurrent comorbidities. Despite the acute dip in eGFR, SGLT2 inhibitors should be continued to maximise benefit, even in patients with HF.

title: Efficacy and safety of four-point scleral fixation of intraocular lenses in eyes without adequate capsular support: a systematic review and meta- analysis
authorString: Dolar-Szczasny J, Drab A, Rejdak R.
abstractText: Background Four-point scleral fixation is increasingly used for secondary intraocular lens (IOL) implantation in eyes without adequate capsular support, yet pooled estimates of its visual benefit and complication profile are lacking. We aimed to quantify visual outcomes and postoperative complications after four-point scleral IOL fixation. Methods This systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA 2020 and registered retrospectively in OSF Registries (doi:10.17605/OSF.IO/DTY7X). The final searches of PubMed, Embase, Europe PMC and the Cochrane Library (CENTRAL) were completed on 5 November 2026. Studies of ≥ 4 eyes undergoing sutured or flanged four-point scleral fixation of a posterior chamber IOL were included. Within-study changes in logMAR visual acuity and intraocular pressure (IOP) were pooled with random-effects models (REML with Hartung-Knapp adjustment), and complication incidences with random-intercept logistic generalized linear mixed models. Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 and an adapted Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, and certainty of evidence with GRADE. Results Sixty-seven studies (approximately 3,250 eyes; two randomized) were included. Best-corrected visual acuity improved by 0.57 logMAR (95% CI 0.44–0.70; 37 studies, 1,552 eyes; I² = 97%) and uncorrected distance visual acuity by 0.83 logMAR (95% CI 0.53–1.14; 7 studies, 211 eyes). Results were robust in sensitivity analyses and did not differ by suture material or technique (p = 0.56). Mean IOP fell slightly (0.97 mmHg, 95% CI 0.02–1.93; 17 studies). The most frequent complications were ocular hypertension (15.9%, 95% CI 12.4–20.3), cystoid macular oedema (10.1%, 7.2–14.0), corneal oedema (9.9%, 5.3–17.7) and hypotony (7.5%, 5.1–10.9). Other pooled incidences were glaucoma (4.2%), vitreous haemorrhage (4.3%), IOL tilt/decentration (2.4%), retinal detachment (1.5%), IOL dislocation (1.3%), endophthalmitis (0.7%) and suture-related complications (0.8%). Certainty of evidence was very low across all assessed outcomes. Conclusions Four-point scleral fixation of posterior chamber IOLs was associated with improved visual acuity and a low incidence of serious postoperative complications, including retinal detachment, IOL dislocation and endophthalmitis. Ocular hypertension and cystoid macular oedema were among the most frequently reported complications, highlighting the importance of postoperative monitoring. However, the very low certainty of the available evidence limits the strength of these conclusions. Further prospective comparative studies with standardized outcome definitions and long-term follow-up are warranted to better define the efficacy and safety of four-point fixation relative to alternative IOL fixation techniques.

title: Rationale and Design of the MICRA-HYBRID Trial: Multivessel Minimally Invasive Coronary Bypass Grafting as HYBRID Revascularization Versus Conventional Off-pump Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting.
authorString: Cenik I, Oosterlinck W, Woorst JT, Soliman-Hamad M, Teeuwen K, Koene B, Jacobs S, Bennett J, van 't Veer M, Tonino P, Akca F.
abstractText:
Background

Coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) remains the gold standard for patients with complex three-vessel coronary artery disease (CAD). It offers durable long-term outcomes, but introduces substantial short-term surgical trauma. Multivessel hybrid coronary revascularization (multivessel-HCR) with minimally invasive left anterior descending (LAD) and circumflex artery (Cx) grafting combined with percutaneous right coronary artery (RCA) intervention (PCI) might reduce postoperative morbidity, improve early recovery and offer similar long-term outcomes.

Trial design

This investigator-initiated, dual-center, randomized clinical trial investigates whether multivessel-HCR is superior to off-pump CABG (OPCAB) in patients with three-vessel CAD. Eligible patients have angiographically significant disease of all three major epicardial vessels with or without left main involvement. In total, 250 patients will be randomized 1:1 with stratification for diabetes. Both surgical strategies will use a total arterial, anaortic off-pump approach. Multivessel-HCR consists of minimally invasive LAD and Cx grafting followed by PCI of the RCA. In the OPCAB-arm, all significant coronary targets will be surgically revascularized. The primary endpoint is 30-days textbook outcome, defined as the composite absence of mortality, re-exploration, type 5 myocardial infarction requiring acute PCI or graft revision, tamponade, stroke, transient ischemic attack, wound infection, new-onset atrial fibrillation, pneumonia, pleural effusion requiring chest drainage, and prolonged hospitalization. Key secondary endpoints include quality of life and recovery questionnaires, pulmonary recovery and short-term hospital costs. Follow-up includes 5-year major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events.

Conclusion

The MICRA-HYBRID trial will compare in a randomized fashion multivessel hybrid revascularization with OPCAB in patients presenting with 3-vessel CAD.

title: Debridement Versus Endovascular Revascularization for Diabetic Foot Ulcers With Borderline Infrapopliteal Ischemia: A Prospective Cohort Study.
authorString: Shahat M, Ali S, Ayman Shaamash K, Hassab Allah AES, Elbadawy A, Rocha Neves J.

journal.title: Journal of endovascular therapy : an official journal of the International Society of Endovascular Specialists

abstractText:
Background

Diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) complicated by infrapopliteal peripheral arterial disease (PAD) represent a major cause of morbidity and nontraumatic lower-limb amputation worldwide. In patients with borderline ischemia, the optimal management strategy remains unclear, with some clinicians advocating conservative debridement while others favor early endovascular revascularization.

Aim

To compare clinical outcomes of conservative management with surgical debridement versus an endovascular-first strategy followed by debridement in patients with DFUs and borderline infrapopliteal PAD.

Methods

This prospective nonrandomized study included patients with DFUs and borderline infrapopliteal PAD treated at a tertiary vascular center between March 2020 and March 2024. Patients with ankle-brachial index (ABI) values of 0.5-0.8 or falsely elevated ABI (>1.3) with preserved distal flow were included. Participants were managed with either conservative treatment (surgical debridement alone) or endovascular revascularization followed by debridement. Clinical, anatomical, and radiological assessments included the WIfI classification, Global Limb Anatomic Staging System (GLASS), and Peripheral Arterial Calcification Scoring System (PACSS). Propensity score matching (PSM) was used to balance baseline characteristics between groups. Primary outcomes included wound healing and amputation-free survival (AFS) at 12 months.

Results

A total of 426 patients were analyzed (264 debridement and 162 revascularization). Patients undergoing revascularization had a greater burden of advanced limb disease, with a significantly higher prevalence of WIfI stage IV ulcers (51.9% vs 31.8%, P = .005), more advanced GLASS stage, and higher PACSS grades, whereas baseline cardiovascular comorbidities including hypertension, coronary artery disease, chronic kidney disease, and previous vascular intervention were comparable between groups. After PSM, 2 balanced cohorts of 100 patients each were compared. Amputation-free survival was similar between the debridement and revascularization groups (74% vs 70%, P = .824). Rates of major adverse limb events and overall mortality were also comparable. Multivariate analysis identified wound depth and GLASS stage as strong predictors of major amputation, while direct angiosomal revascularization was associated with improved wound healing and reduced limb-loss risk.

Conclusions

In patients with DFUs and borderline infrapopliteal ischemia, conservative management with timely debridement may achieve outcomes comparable with endovascular revascularization. Anatomical disease severity and wound characteristics appear to be stronger determinants of prognosis than the choice of revascularization strategy.Clinical ImpactThis study highlights the importance of individualized treatment selection in patients with diabetic foot ulcers and borderline infrapopliteal ischemia. Wound depth and anatomical disease complexity should be carefully considered when determining the need for endovascular intervention. In selected patients, timely debridement may be a reasonable management option, while direct angiosomal revascularization may offer additional benefits when an endovascular procedure is indicated. These findings may help clinicians refine treatment strategies and avoid unnecessary interventions without compromising limb-related outcomes.

title: Current Patterns and Best Practices for Prescribing Novel Heart Failure Medications in Children: A Science Advisory From the American Heart Association.
authorString: Price JF, Hong B, Jacobson-Kelly AE, Jeewa A, Lin K, Martinez H, Menachem J, Procaccini D, Rossano J, Exil V, American Heart Association Council on Lifelong Congenital Heart Disease and Heart Health in the Young, Pediatric Heart Failure and Transplantation Committee; Council on Clinical Cardiology; and Council on Cardiovascular and Stroke Nursing.
abstractText: Robust evidence from randomized controlled trials of novel heart failure medications in adults has demonstrated improved quality of life, reduced hospitalizations, and decreased mortality, informing current treatment guidelines. In contrast, data supporting the clinical benefits of newer heart failure therapies in children remain limited. To assess contemporary prescribing practices and clinician perspectives, we surveyed pediatric heart failure physicians across the United States and Canada regarding the use of angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitors, sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors, and iron replacement therapy in children. We also reviewed the existing pediatric literature and summarized reported side effects, dosing experience, and practical guidance for the use of these therapies in the absence of rigorous evidence.

title: The Pharmacological Basis of SGLT2 Inhibitor-Mediated Kidney Protection: From Proximal Tubular Mechanisms to Clinical Outcomes.
authorString: Zaitoon H, Abdul-Ghani M, DeFronzo RA.
abstractText: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) remains the leading cause of chronic kidney disease (CKD) worldwide despite advances in glycemic control, blood pressure management, and renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system blockade. The introduction of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors has fundamentally changed the management of CKD by consistently reducing kidney disease progression and cardiovascular events in patients both with and without diabetes. These findings indicate that the benefits of SGLT2 inhibition extend beyond glucose lowering and reflect broader effects on cardiorenal physiology. This review examines the pharmacological mechanisms underlying SGLT2 inhibitor-mediated kidney protection, integrating experimental evidence with findings from major clinical outcome trials. Current evidence supports a hierarchical mechanistic model in which inhibition of proximal tubular sodium-glucose reabsorption represents the primary pharmacological event, restoring tubule-glomerular feedback, reducing intraglomerular pressure, and lowering tubular transport workload. These upstream hemodynamic and metabolic effects are thought to initiate downstream improvements in kidney oxygen balance, mitochondrial function, inflammation, oxidative stress, and fibrosis, although the relative contribution of these pathways remains incompletely defined. We further examine how contemporary clinical trials validate this mechanistic framework across diverse CKD populations, including patients with and without diabetes and across a broad range of kidney function and albuminuria. Finally, we discuss the implications of these findings for phenotype-specific treatment strategies, rational combination therapy with complementary kidney-protective agents, and future directions in biomarker-guided precision medicine. Collectively, current evidence supports SGLT2 inhibitors as integrated cardiorenal therapies that modify fundamental determinants of CKD progression and provide the pharmacological foundation of contemporary kidney-protective treatment.

title: Managing post-bariatric weight recurrence with new obesity management medications.
authorString: Masi D, De Domenico F, Zanghi Buffi V, Tozzi R, Cipriani V, Di Gioia L, Di Molfetta S, Caruso I, Cipriani F, De Luca M, Castagneto-Gissey L, Perrini S, Gianfrilli D, Isidori AM, Giorgino F, Mingrone G, le Roux CW, Manfrini S, Clément K, Watanabe M, Tuccinardi D.
abstractText: Recurrent weight gain (RWG) following metabolic and bariatric surgery (MBS) represents a major challenge in the long-term management of obesity and is distinct from insufficient weight loss and suboptimal clinical response, which reflect a primary inadequate response. RWG is defined as regain of ≥25% of the maximum weight lost, assessed ≥24 months after surgery. It affects approximately 35% of patients within 5 years of sleeve gastrectomy and approximately 15% within 5 years after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass. With longer follow-up, the number of affected patients rises to about one-third. RWG is multifactorial: genetic predisposition, preoperative metabolic phenotype, inadequate or failed surgical anatomy, and neurohormonal and adipose tissue adaptations interact over time to cause it, and no single variable accounts for it. Randomized evidence indicates that the operation itself is a determinant of long-term response: Roux-en-Y gastric bypass elicits greater postprandial GLP1 secretion, more durable weight loss and higher rates of type 2 diabetes mellitus remission than sleeve gastrectomy, so procedure selection warrants as much attention as postoperative management. Treatment should therefore be specific to phenotype and procedure, escalating from lifestyle optimization to obesity management medications, endoscopic revision and revisional surgery, if needed. Randomized data now support semaglutide after MBS, whereas evidence for tirzepatide, combined endoscopic-pharmacological strategies, or treatment sequencing remains observational and real-world adherence is a major constraint. Multimodal, integrated approaches combining behavioural, pharmacological and surgical strategies could help to improve treatment strategies for patients who experience RWG. This Review discusses the factors that contribute to RWG after MBS, considerations for clinical management of RWG, and questions that future research should aim to address to improve and maintain weight loss and other clinical outcomes after MBS. The Review also discusses clinical approaches to insufficient weight loss and suboptimal clinical response after MBS.

title: PRovisional versus Focal OSTial Stenting for Isolated Ostial Disease Occurring in Coronary Bifurcations (The PROST Trial)-Rationale and Design.
authorString: Ekmejian A, Collins N, Ada C, Chandrasekhar J, Jain P, Hallani H, Lee A, Arunothayaraj S, Lo S, Al Mukhtar O, Biswas S, Adams H, Bhindi R.
abstractText: Isolated branch ostial coronary bifurcation lesions (Medina 0,1,0 and 0,0,1) remain one of the least studied lesion subsets in percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Two techniques, provisional stenting and focal ostial stenting, are commonly used in clinical practice. However, no randomised controlled trial has directly compared these treatment approaches. The PRovisional vs Precision OSTial Stenting (PROST) trial is a prospective, multicentre, open-label, randomised controlled trial comparing provisional stenting with precision focal ostial stenting in patients undergoing PCI for isolated branch ostial coronary bifurcation lesions. A total of 274 patients will be randomised in a 1:1 ratio across participating Australasian centres. The trial is embedded within the Australasian Bifurcation Coronary Registry and incorporates mandatory intravascular imaging guidance, independent angiographic core laboratory assessment, and blinded clinical event adjudication. The primary endpoint is target lesion failure at 24 months, defined according to Bifurcation Academic Research Consortium criteria. To our knowledge, the PROST trial is the first randomised study evaluating provisional versus precision focal ostial stenting for isolated branch ostial coronary bifurcation lesions. Its findings will address an important evidence gap and have the potential to inform future clinical practice and guideline recommendations.

title: Dietary sodium restriction enhances the renoprotective efficacy of endothelin-A receptor antagonism in proteinuric chronic kidney disease.
authorString: Pugh D, Chapman GB, James V, Armstrong A, Chapman FA, Melville V, Bruce L, Goddard J, Webb DJ, Bailey MA, Dhaun N.
