abstractText: Endothelin-A receptor antagonists (ERAs) are emerging as an important treatment for proteinuric chronic kidney disease (CKD). As with renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) inhibition, dietary sodium intake may influence their therapeutic efficacy, but this has not been investigated. Here, we examined whether dietary sodium restriction enhances the systemic and kidney effects of acute selective endothelin-A (ETA) receptor antagonism in proteinuric CKD. In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover study, 12 adults (mean age 46 years) with non-diabetic proteinuric CKD (mean eGFR 55 mL/min/1.73 m2; median proteinuria 1.8 g/day) receiving maximally tolerated RAAS inhibition completed two 14-day dietary interventions (habitual dietary sodium intake [13.3 g salt/day] and dietary sodium restriction [6.3 g salt/day, approximating guideline-recommended levels]) in random order. During each dietary period, participants underwent two study visits and received intravenous infusion of either placebo or the selective ET A receptor antagonist, BQ123. Systemic hemodynamics, arterial stiffness, kidney hemodynamics and proteinuria were assessed following each intervention. BQ123 produced comparable reductions in systolic blood pressure (about 12-14 mmHg), systemic vascular resistance and arterial stiffness under both dietary conditions and increased kidney blood flow (about 320-335 mL/min) irrespective of dietary sodium intake. In contrast, significant reductions in glomerular filtration rate (peak placebo-adjusted reduction: about 5 mL/min/1.73 m2), effective filtration fraction (peak reduction about 1.5%), and proteinuria (about 300 μg/min) were observed only during dietary sodium restriction and not during habitual sodium intake. Dietary sodium restriction enhances the short-term kidney efficacy of selective endothelin-A receptor antagonism in proteinuric CKD while preserving its beneficial systemic hemodynamic effects. As ERAs become established therapies for proteinuric kidney disease, these findings suggest that adherence to dietary sodium restriction may maximize their kidney-protective benefits. Whether the acute changes demonstrated here translate into long-term kidney protection requires prospective evaluation.

title: Trial design and methods of home-based exercise tele-rehabilitation in high-risk veterans: Impact of COVID-19 exposure and socioeconomic factors.
authorString: Ryan AS, Rathbun AM, Cassady S, Jaber S, Griffith K, Marconi VC, Oursler KK, BOOST Project Team.
abstractText:
Background

Successful rehabilitation strategies for Veterans during and post Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) is a high clinical research priority. Long-term effects of COVID-19 on cardiopulmonary and physical function are uncertain, and rehabilitation should be feasible for Veterans. The objectives of this clinical trial are to investigate the effect of home-based supervised exercise via tele-rehabilitation on cardiopulmonary and physical function outcomes, its' impact on recovery defined by World Health Organization's International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) components, and its effect on self-efficacy, inflammatory and oxidative stress biomarkers in adults who have had SARS-CoV-2 infection.

Methods

In the Home-Based Exercise Tele-Rehabilitation in High-Risk Veterans: Impact of COVID-19 Exposure and Socioeconomic Factors (BOOST) trial (NCT05425264), 80 middle-aged and older adults (>50 years) will be enrolled with documented COVID-19 > 90 days prior to enrollment and diagnosed with ≥2 conditions: hypertension, diabetes and/or pre-diabetes, cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, dyslipidemia or 1 condition and BMI > 30 kg/m2. Veterans will participate from home in the 12-week exercise intervention that will consist of virtual supervised group exercise classes. Procedures before and after the intervention will include cardiopulmonary exercise testing, pulmonary function tests, assessments of physical function, and questionnaires targeting exercise self-efficacy.

Discussion

This novel 12-week exercise intervention program, which was designed to promote health in Veterans who have a history of SARS-CoV-2 infection, will provide critical information on the benefits of exercise on cardiopulmonary and physical function in this heterogenous population.

title: Use of Synchronous, Interruptive Electronic Health Record-Embedded Medication Alerts to Improve Evidence-Based Medication Prescribing: Randomized Comparative Effectiveness Trial of Two Prescriber Alerts.
authorString: Barnes G, Choi SY, Errickson J, Seagull FJ, Fabbri M, Saraswat A, Dorsch MP, Lanham MSM, Smith SN.
abstractText: Antithrombotic stewardship is critical for reducing preventable harm from inappropriate anticoagulant prescribing. Electronic health record (EHR)-embedded clinical decision support (CDS) alerts can prevent prescribing errors at the point of care, but their real-world effectiveness is variable and often limited by alert fatigue and poor workflow integration. Whether augmenting interruptive medication alerts with just‑in‑time access to clinical pharmacists improves prescriber response remains unclear. This study aimed to (1) compare the effectiveness of synchronous, interruptive direct oral anticoagulant (DOAC) prescribing alerts with and without an embedded clinical pharmacist referral option for correcting inappropriate new prescriptions within 7 days, and (2) evaluate the system‑level impact of implementing synchronous DOAC alerts on inappropriate prescribing over time. We conducted a prescriber‑level randomized comparative effectiveness trial within a large US academic health system. Prescribers who placed an inappropriate ambulatory apixaban or rivaroxaban order were randomized to receive an interruptive EHR alert either with or without an embedded clinical pharmacist referral link. The primary outcome was any change to the prescription within 7 days. In parallel, a system‑level interrupted time series analysis examined weekly proportions of inappropriate DOAC prescriptions (secondary outcomes) from 24 months before through 29 months after alert implementation. Exploratory outcomes included adverse events within 30 days and alert implementation metrics. Among 2082 prescribers writing DOAC prescriptions during the study period, 300 (14.4%) triggered at least one inappropriate prescription and were randomized; after prespecified exclusions, 758 alerts across 286 prescribers were analyzed. Overall, 28.9% (219/758) of alerts led to a prescription change within 7 days. The proportion of alerts leading to a prescription change did not differ between alerts with and without pharmacist referral (difference 1 percentage point [95% CI -7 to 9]). The system‑wide proportion of inappropriate DOAC prescriptions exhibited a significant downward preimplementation trend (-0.04 percentage points per week [95% CI -0.06 to -0.02]), followed by an immediate 3.5‑percentage‑point absolute reduction at alert launch (to 9.7%), with no subsequent slope change. Adverse events within 30 days were uncommon and similar across arms. Adding an embedded pharmacist referral option to an interruptive DOAC prescribing alert did not increase short‑term prescription changes. However, the implementation of synchronous, user-centered alerts was associated with a system-level reduction in inappropriate DOAC prescribing. These findings support a complementary digital stewardship model in which high‑value, point‑of‑order alerts prevent routine prescribing errors, while clinical pharmacists focus on complex and longitudinal medication management. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05351749; https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05351749.

title: CD4+ T cell anergy in transplantation tolerance requires continuous Treg-dependent control of IL-2 availability.
authorString: Cassano A, Abbondanza D, Wang Y, Wu S, McIntosh CM, Wang P, Allocco JB, Kwan M, Mora-Cartin R, Craddock E, Andrade MS, Chong AS, Alegre ML.
abstractText: Donor-specific transplantation tolerance promises to free recipients from complications associated with lifelong immunosuppression. Anergy, a CD4+ conventional T cell (Tconv)-intrinsic state of long-term hypofunction, is thought to arise when T cells encounter cognate antigen in the absence of costimulation. Anti-CD154 (αCD154), an antibody that blocks T cell costimulation and is currently in clinical trials, can induce donor-specific transplantation tolerance in mice in association with anergy of Tconvs recognizing persistently expressed alloantigens. Using murine models of fully mismatched cardiac allograft tolerance or repeated alloantigen exposure, we demonstrate that αCD154 is not sufficient and regulatory T cells (Tregs) are necessary to induce and sustain αCD154-mediated alloreactive Tconv anergy. Transient depletion of Tregs disrupted the induction of αCD154-mediated Tconv anergy, and in mice with established tolerance, Treg depletion transcriptionally and functionally reinvigorated previously anergic Tconvs. Mechanistically, Treg depletion increased IL-2 availability and IL-2R signaling in Tconvs, and exogenous IL-2 could bypass Treg-mediated control to partially restore Tconv function. Thus, the state of αCD154-mediated Tconv anergy is less cell-intrinsic than previously thought and requires Tregs to limit IL-2 availability for both its induction and its continuous enforcement. Selecting immunosuppressive drugs that preserve this Treg function may be critical for achieving stable clinical transplantation tolerance.

title: Discontinuation and Non-Publication of Cardiotoxicity Clinical Trials: A Cross-Sectional Study.
authorString: Wang X, Wang S, Li Y, Zhang Z, He C, Fu C, Wei Q.
abstractText: Cardiotoxicity from anticancer therapies poses a major clinical challenge, yet the integrity of related clinical trials remains underexplored. We performed a cross-sectional analysis of cardiotoxicity trials registered on ClinicalTrials.gov, identifying 245 eligible studies with 199 completions and 46 discontinuations, of which 82 were published. Observational trials had high completion rates (59/65) yet suffered from profound dissemination failure, with only 13 published. Multicenter design showed a significant independent association with publication (adjusted OR 10.50, 95% CI 1.95-82.00, P = 0.010). In contrast, interventional trials faced greater operational attrition, with Phase II trials exhibiting a particularly high proportion of termination. Notably, trials enrolling ≤ 26 participants were associated with markedly lower odds of completion (adjusted OR 0.04, 95% CI 0.01-0.13, P < 0.001). Among interventional trials, international recruitment was the factor most strongly associated with publication (adjusted OR 3.07, 95% CI 1.27-7.66, P = 0.014). These findings delineate distinct translational barriers across study designs in cardio-oncology. Future priorities should include mandating transparent reporting of completed observational research and strengthening multinational collaboration in interventional trial networks to mitigate discontinuation risk and ensure a robust evidence base for cardiovascular protection.

title: Imaging- and phenotype-guided calcium modification in complex PCI: a framework for device selection, procedural reassessment, and selective escalation.
authorString: Assayed A, Gruhonjic H, Minasyan A, Fabian D, Suwwan N, Prashad R.

journal.title: The Egyptian heart journal : (EHJ) : official bulletin of the Egyptian Society of Cardiology

abstractText: Severe coronary artery calcification presents a major challenge during percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), contributing to impaired lesion crossing, inadequate balloon expansion, and stent underexpansion. Multiple calcium-modification technologies are available; however, optimal device selection depends on lesion morphology, anatomical characteristics, and procedural response. To provide an imaging- and phenotypeguided framework for selecting and escalating calcium modification strategies during complex PCI, integrating contemporary evidence, procedural reassessment, and emerging technologies. This narrative review synthesizes contemporary consensus statements, randomized trials, prospective device studies, observational investigations, and meta-analyses addressing intravascular ultrasound (IVUS), optical coherence tomography (OCT), calcium morphology, lesion crossability and expandability, calcium-modification mechanisms, combination strategies, anatomical considerations, procedural complications, and resource utilization. Available calcium-modification modalities-including rotational and orbital atherectomy, intravascular lithotripsy (IVL), excimer laser coronary atherectomy, and specialized balloon-based techniques-provide complementary mechanisms of calcium modification. Evidence from trials such as PREPARE-CALC, ECLIPSE, and ROLLER COASTR-EPIC22 highlights the importance of distinguishing procedural success, imaging-defined stent expansion, and longer-term clinical outcomes. No single technology demonstrates universal superiority across all calcified lesion phenotypes. An integrated strategy incorporating calcium morphology, intravascular imaging, lesion crossability, balloon expandability, and reassessment after each intervention may support more rational device selection and selective escalation. Particular considerations include calcified nodules, left main and bifurcation lesions, tortuous anatomy, procedural complications, and resource availability. An imaging- and response-guided approach offers a practical framework for calcium modification during complex PCI. The principal objective is to achieve adequate lesion preparation and optimal stent expansion while minimizing vessel injury and unnecessary device utilization. Prospective validation of this framework is warranted.

title: Divergent activation of the RXFP1 relaxin receptor by protein and small-molecule agonists.
authorString: Osei-Owusu J, Girbau T, Wang X, Smith JS, Shen P, Erlandson SC, Williamson AK, Cong X, Grinstaff MW, Kahne DE, Bechara C, Kruse AC.
abstractText: The relaxin receptor RXFP1 is a therapeutic target owing to its potential benefits in the treatment of fibrosis and heart failure. Protein and small-molecule agonists are currently in midstage clinical trials for various forms of heart disease. In this work, we present three cryo-electron microscopy structures of RXFP1: ligand-free, bound to the native agonist relaxin-2, and bound to the small-molecule drug candidate AZD5462. These structures reveal that relaxin-2 engages the receptor's ectodomain, whereas AZD5462 binds to the transmembrane domain. Together with hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry, we show that relaxin-2 induces reorganization of the linker domain into a helical secondary structure. By contrast, AZD5462 stabilizes an active conformation through a distinct set of conformational rearrangements. Altogether, our findings define divergent activation mechanisms for protein and small-molecule agonists of RXFP1.

title: A Self-Management Support Intervention to Improve BP among Patients with CKD: Kidney Awareness Registry and Education Trial.
authorString: Tuot DS, Evans JL, Plantinga LC, McCulloch CE, Velasquez A, Schillinger D, Handley MA, Hsu CY, Powe NR.

journal.title: Clinical journal of the American Society of Nephrology : CJASN

abstractText:
Background

Low-income patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) face a high burden of adverse health outcomes. We assessed the effectiveness of a community health worker (CHW)-led self-management support intervention to improve health among adults with CKD and hypertension who receive primary care in urban safety-net clinics.

Methods

Randomized controlled trial [Kidney Awareness Registry and Education) in which low-income, English-, Spanish-, or Cantonese-speaking adults with CKD and systolic blood pressure (SBP) >130 mmHg recruited from two different public health care delivery systems in San Francisco, California, and Oakland, California, were randomized to participate in a 6-month self-management support intervention or usual care. The primary outcome was the between-group difference in SBP change after one year. Secondary outcomes included the between-group differences in changes of: urine albumin-creatinine ratio (UACR), patient-reported awareness of CKD, self-efficacy of chronic disease management, communication with providers, medication adherence, and quality of life at one year.

Results

Among 238 participants with mean age of 62 years, a median (interquartile range, [IQR]) SBP of 144 (134, 159) mmHg, median (IQR) eGFR of 54.2 (42.1, 76.6) ml/min/1.73 m2 and UACR of 203 mg/g (IQR: 43, 827), of whom 34.5% had limited English proficiency and 62.0% had food insecurity, 129 were randomized to the self-management support intervention and 109 were randomized to usual care. Randomization to intervention led to a statistically larger decline in SBP compared to usual care at 12 months (difference-in-differences estimate: -10.8 mmHg; 95%CI: -16.8, -4.8). Change in UACR was not statistically different by study arm. Change in CKD awareness was higher in the intervention arm compared to usual care (ratio-in-odds ratios estimate: 2.9; 1.0-8.1), but no statistically significant differences in other behavioral outcomes were noted.

Conclusion

A CHW-led self-management support program improves SBP and CKD awareness among low-income patients with moderate CKD.

title: Genetics of hypertension.
authorString: Danielli M, Munroe PB.

journal.title: Current opinion in nephrology and hypertension

abstractText:
Purpose of review

Hypertension genetics is transitioning from discovery into clinical applications: there are numerous genome-wide association studies (GWAS) of blood pressure (BP) and more recently resistant hypertension, polygenic risk scores are available, and there is regulatory approval of a novel class of antihypertensive treatment. This review highlights recent discoveries and clinical implications.

Recent findings

A GWAS of greater than 1 million individuals identified 2103 independent BP signals, explaining more than 60% of common-variant heritability; many candidate genes are expressed in kidney tubular epithelia and adrenal zona glomerulosa. A GWAS (>23 000 cases) of resistant hypertension identified 24 loci with candidate genes mapping to the aldosterone-potassium axis, providing genetics support for selective aldosterone synthase inhibitors and overlap with BP loci. Clinical trials using aldosterone synthase inhibitors, and angiotensinogen-silencing RNA therapies are in Phase 2-3 trials; aprocitentan received regulatory approval for resistant hypertension in 2024.

Summary

The genetic architecture of hypertension spans Mendelian disease genes to thousands of common variants, with kidney tubular biology and the aldosterone axis as central biological themes. Multigene panels, primary aldosteronism screening, and mineralocorticoid axis evaluation before accepting apparent resistance are ready for clinical implementation. Polygenic risk scores show promise for trial enrichment and pharmacogenomic stratification, but are not yet ready for individual clinical decisions.

title: Clinical Outcomes of Peripartum Cardiomyopathy in Sub-Saharan Africa: A Systematic Review
authorString: Asare EK, Asim A, Lackland T, Cummings CH, Jackson L, Moustapha M, Onyemkpa C.
abstractText: Background Peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM) is a severe form of pregnancy-associated heart failure with significant maternal morbidity and mortality, particularly in Sub-Saharan Africa where variations in diagnosis and management exist. Therefore, this systematic review aimed to synthesize the available evidence on mortality and recovery outcomes of peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM) among reproductive women in Sub-Saharan Africa. Methods We conducted a systematic review of quantitative studies published from January 2000 to December 2025, following PRISMA guidelines and registered with PROSPERO (ID: CRD420261376381). Searches were performed in PubMed, Web of Science, Google scholar, and the Cochrane Library using combinations of PPCM-related terms and all SSA country names. Eligible studies were observational cohort studies reporting at least one of the following outcomes: mortality, or recovery of left ventricular function, which were included. Data were extracted into standardized tables and synthesized descriptively. Determinants and prognostic factors associated with outcomes were also recorded and summarized narratively. The quality of study was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist. Results Six cohort studies from South Africa, Zambia, Nigeria, Uganda, Burkina Faso, and Zimbabwe met the inclusion criteria, comprising a total of 651 women with PPCM. Across the studies included, 100 deaths were reported, corresponding to an overall mortality of 15.4%. Recovery of left ventricular function was achieved in 197 patients, representing an overall recovery rate of 30.1%. Recovery was assessed between 6 and 12 months postpartum and was generally defined by a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of ≥ 50% or > 55%. Conclusion Peripartum cardiomyopathy in Sub-Saharan Africa is associated with high mortality and relatively low rates of recovery of left ventricular function. The wide variation in outcomes highlights gaps in early diagnosis and access to effective care. Strengthening early detection and optimizing management are essential to improving maternal outcomes in the region.

title: Outcomes of Endovascular Repair for Stanford Type B Aortic Dissection with Concurrent Retrograde Intramural Hematoma Involving the Aortic Arch and/or Ascending Aorta (Zone 0-2) in a Chinese Population: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Kwan KJS, Li HL, Qi R, Dong Z, Cheng SW.
abstractText:
Objective

To evaluate the outcomes of thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) for type B aortic dissection (TBAD) with concurrent retrograde intramural hematoma (RTIMH) involving the aortic arch, with or without further extension into the ascending aorta.

Methods

A systematic search of MEDLINE and EMBASE to June 2026 was performed. Studies reporting TEVAR outcomes in adults with TBAD-associated RTIMH, defined as a primary intimal tear at or distal to Ishimaru zone 3 with retrograde intramural hematoma extension into zones 0-2, were included. Co-primary outcomes were technical success and post-TEVAR retrograde type A aortic dissection (RTAD), defined as the new development of a communicating dissection flap within the previously non-flow intramural hematoma. Secondary outcomes included early mortality, stroke, type I endoleak, reintervention, survival, aortic rupture, and aortic remodelling. Proportions were pooled using single-arm random-effects meta-analysis following logit transformation; remaining findings were synthesised narratively.

Results

Seven retrospective cohort studies comprising 342 patients, all from mainland Chinese institutions, were included. The pooled technical success rate was 99% (95% CI 97-99%; I2 = 0.0%). The pooled post-TEVAR RTAD rate was 3% (95% CI 1-8%; I2 = 7.6%), with all events preceded by proximal stent-graft-induced new entry. Secondary outcomes included pooled 30-day mortality of 2% (95% CI 1-4%; I2 = 0.0%), aortic rupture of 2% (95% CI 1-4%; I2 = 0.0%), reintervention of 7% (95% CI 5-11%; I2 = 0.0%), late all-cause mortality of 4% (95% CI 3-6%; I2 = 0.0%), and type I endoleak of 4% (95% CI 2-7%; I2 = 0.0%). All studies reporting pre- and post-procedural imaging demonstrated reductions in ascending aortic diameter and hematoma thickness, with complete ascending IMH resolution in 52.5-100% of patients.

Conclusions

TEVAR is technically feasible with low perioperative mortality and consistent aortic remodelling in selected patients with TBAD-associated RTIMH. Post-TEVAR RTAD and type I endoleak represent the principal procedure-specific risks. Contemporary evidence remains limited to small retrospective cohorts from a single geographic region.

title: Prenatal exposure to per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances and blood pressure in childhood: A systematic review of prospective observational studies.
authorString: Brosset E, Moutchou H, Fraser WD, Ngueta G.

journal.title: International journal of hygiene and environmental health

abstractText:
Background

Prenatal exposure to per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) may affect early-life cardiovascular programming, but epidemiological findings regarding blood pressure outcomes in children remain inconsistent. This systematic review synthesized evidence on associations between prenatal PFAS exposure and blood pressure or hypertension in children and adolescents.

Methods

Following Cochrane recommendations and PRISMA 2020 guidelines, PubMed, Scopus, MEDLINE (EBSCO), and Embase were searched through 02 November 2026. The search strategy was developed with an information specialist. Prospective studies reporting prenatal PFAS exposure and offspring blood pressure outcomes were included. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-E. Due to substantial methodological heterogeneity, findings were synthesized narratively without meta-analysis.

Results

Thirteen prospective cohort studies from North America, Europe, and Asia were included. Associations between individual PFAS and systolic or diastolic blood pressure were generally small and inconsistent across compounds, exposure windows, and ages at outcome assessment. Evidence regarding PFAS mixtures was similarly heterogeneous, with some studies reporting associations with systolic blood pressure or cardiometabolic outcomes, while others observed null or inverse associations. Heterogeneity in exposure assessment, mixture modeling approaches, and outcome definitions precluded quantitative synthesis.

Limitations of evidence

The evidence was limited by heterogeneity across studies, potential residual confounding, differences in exposure assessment and outcome definitions, and varying risk of bias.

Interpretation

Current evidence suggests that prenatal PFAS exposure may influence offspring BP, but findings remain inconsistent. Harmonized longitudinal studies with standardized exposure assessment and robust mixture methodologies are needed to clarify the role of early-life PFAS exposure in pediatric cardiovascular risk.

title: Prevalence of Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension Associated with Congenital Heart Disease Following Defect Correction: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
authorString: Krishnathasan K, Constantine A, Dimopoulos K, Wort SJ, Quyam S, Condliffe R, Clift P, Jansen K, Moledina S, CHAMPION steering committee.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Eur Heart J Qual Care Clin Outcomes
journal.title: European heart journal. Quality of care & clinical outcomes
journal.isoabbreviation: Eur Heart J Qual Care Clin Outcomes

abstractText:
Importance

Understanding the disease burden of repaired pulmonary arterial hypertension associated with congenital heart disease (PAH-CHD) is essential for guiding healthcare strategies, yet data are lacking in this area.

Objective

To estimate the prevalence of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) following defect correction in patients with congenital heart disease (CHD).

Data sources

A systematic review and meta-analysis was performed using PubMed, Embase and Cochrane databases.

Study selection

Longitudinal cohort published between 1970-2023 involving CHD patients who underwent defect correction and were subsequently diagnosed with PAH were reviewed. Eligible studies reporting the prevalence of repaired PAH-CHD at least 3 months post-repair was included. Study selection was conducted independently by two reviewers. The primary outcome was the prevalence of PAH in patients following CHD defect correction.

Results

Across 58 studies (7,036 participants), the random-effects pooled prevalence of reported post-repair PAH/PH was 10.8% (95% CI 7.3-15.0, I2 = 95.6%; prediction interval 0-50.1%). Prevalence was 9.0% (95% CI 3.3-17) in studies using right heart catheterisation, 19.3% (CI 10.6-29.7) in studies using echocardiography and 16.1% (CI 8.6- 25.1%) in studies using both modalities (p=0.19). Prevalence was highest in the adult-only cohort (18.5%, 95%CI 11.8-26.2) and lower in paediatric only (7.6%, 95%CI 3-13.5) and mixed-age cohorts (7.5%,95%CI1.7-16.3), p=0.039. Preoperative pulmonary hypertension (PH) was the strongest predictor of post-repair PAH and remained predictive on adjusted meta-regression (p<0.01).

Conclusion and relevance

PAH following defect repair remains a significant clinical dilemma requiring standardised diagnostic criteria and robust risk stratification tools to guide management.

title: World Health Organization non-laboratory-based 10-year cardiovascular disease risk prediction model in adults without established disease.
authorString: Olfati S, Shokraee K, Monsef I, Zorger AM, Franco JV, Skoetz N.

journal.title: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews

abstractText:
Objectives

This is a protocol for a Cochrane review (prognosis). The objectives are as follows: The objective of this review is to evaluate the prognostic performance of the World Health Organization (WHO) non-laboratory-based CVD risk prediction models in adults aged 40 years to 74 years without established CVD. To do this, we will assess the discrimination, calibration, and clinical applicability of the models in external and internal validation studies. Population Adults aged 40-74 years without established CVD, in primary prevention settings. Index prognostic model The WHO non-laboratory-based 10-year CVD risk prediction model, which estimates future cardiovascular risk using demographic and clinical predictors without requiring laboratory measurements. Comparator No comparator is required, as this review evaluates the external predictive performance of the WHO non-laboratory-based 10-year CVD risk prediction model rather than comparing different prediction models. Outcomes Calibration and discrimination of 10-year CVD risk. Timing Risk prediction is performed at baseline using the WHO non-laboratory-based model, with outcomes predicted over a 10-year time horizon. Setting Primary prevention and routine care settings, including resource-limited contexts where laboratory-based cardiovascular risk assessment is not readily available.

title: Genetic variants of transthyretin amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy associated with low sensitivity to bone scintigraphy: a systematic review.
authorString: Giannino F, Licordari R, Piccolo A, Bianchi L, Colarusso L, Marazia S, Minutoli F, Aquaro GD, Inserra MC, Di Bella G.

journal.title: Amyloid : the international journal of experimental and clinical investigation : the official journal of the International Society of Amyloidosis

abstractText:
Background

Transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTR-CA) is characterized by amyloid deposition and frequently leads to a progressive cardiomyopathy with poor prognosis. Bone scintigraphy with 99mTc-labeled tracers is the cornerstone of noninvasive diagnosis, yet several hereditary TTR variants are associated with false-negative or low-grade tracer uptake.

Objectives

To identify all TTR variants associated with false-negative bone scintigraphy in hereditary ATTR-CA and discuss clinical implications.

Methods

Medline, Scopus, and Cochrane were searched from inception to July 2025 per PRISMA guidelines. Eligible studies included observational studies, case series, and case reports of patients with confirmed ATTR-CA undergoing TTR genetic testing and 99mTc scintigraphy.

Results

Nineteen studies (108 patients) met inclusion criteria. Thirteen pathogenic TTR variants were associated with low or absent uptake (Perugini grade 0-1); p.Val50Met, p.Phe84Leu, and p.Ser97Tyr were most consistently implicated, while p.Val142Ile showed false-negative results in ∼5-10% of carriers. In 11 of 13 variants, advanced structural cardiomyopathy was confirmed despite negative scintigraphy.

Conclusions

Bone scintigraphy has important limitations in specific hereditary TTR variants. A negative scan does not exclude cardiac involvement in genetically at-risk patients. Multimodal strategies including CMR and histological assessment are essential for timely diagnosis.

title: Electroacupuncture as an adjunctive treatment for non-dipper hypertension: study protocol for a multicentre, randomised, sham-controlled trial.
authorString: Chen Y, Lai SH, Hu WX, Zhang B, Zhang C, Lu L, Zhu B, Chen L.

title: Characteristics of ischemic stroke patients with left atrial appendage thrombus detected by cardiac photon-counting detector computed tomography.
authorString: Pinho J, Kammer S, Halabi NS, Elhalal M, Kirschfink A, De Beukelaer F, Ridwan H, Marx N, Weyland CS, Schulz JB, Reich A.
abstractText:
Background

The early identification of left atrial appendage (LAA) thrombus in acute ischemic stroke (AIS) or transient ischemic attack (TIA) patients can have relevant treatment and prognostic implications. We investigated the prevalence of LAA thrombus in AIS/TIA patients and analyzed baseline characteristics and short-term outcomes according to the presence of LAA thrombus.

Methods

We analyzed stroke patients who were admitted consecutively in our comprehensive stroke centre between March 2023 and December 2025 and received cardiac photon-counting computed tomography (CT) implemented in the acute stroke imaging protocol. We analyzed baseline clinical characteristics, echocardiographic and laboratory biomarkers, in-hospital mortality and in-hospital ischemic stroke recurrence according to the presence of LAA thrombus.

Results

We included 577 patients with a median age of 75 years, 49.6% were female, and LAA thrombus was found in 49 patients (8.5%). The presence of LAA thrombus was independently associated with atrial fibrillation (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 16.09, 95% confidence interval [95%CI] = 4.55-56.90, p < 0.001), severe left atrial dilatation (aOR = 3.48, 95%CI = 1.18-10.26, p = 0.009) and higher NT-proBNP (aOR per 1000pg/mL-increment = 1.10, 95%CI = 1.01-1.19, p = 0.022). In-hospital mortality was higher in patients with LAA thrombus (p = 0.003), but this association did not persist after adjustment for clinical stroke severity. In-hospital ischemic stroke recurrence was similar in both groups.

Conclusions

Stroke patients with LAA thrombus detected on cardiac CT performed as part of the acute stroke imaging protocol have different baseline characteristics which are indicative of more severe underlying atrial substrate for arrhythmogenesis.

title: Could Results from the VESALIUS-CV Trial Change the Current Management of Dyslipidemia by Primary Care Clinicians?
authorString: Morales J, Lopez A, Uusinarkaus K, Lee KJ, Sibartie M, Wojcik C.
abstractText: The continuum of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. While significant therapies have evolved over the years, implementation challenges still exist. This publication reviews the roles of primary care clinicians (PCCs) in managing patients with dyslipidemia with or at risk of developing ASCVD. It also discusses how lipid management guidelines have evolved over the years, how such guidelines have affected lipid management by the primary care community, and how recent findings in a pre-event cardiovascular outcomes trial (VESALIUS-CV) will likely impact the primary care community's role in lipid management. Despite new guidelines and recent clinical data, most patients with ASCVD in the real world are undertreated and above therapeutic low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) goals. PCCs should aim to treat lipids to guideline-recommended LDL-C goals to manage an expanding population of patients who need intensive lipid management. Furthermore, ASCVD prevention should be conceptualized as a continuum of risk rather than solely as binary primary or secondary prevention categories, and PCCs should adjust their practice accordingly.

title: Ten myths about milrinone in pediatric cardiogenic shock.
authorString: San Geroteo J, Naudin J, Geslain G, Dauger S.
abstractText: Cardiogenic shock (CS) is a severe and increasingly common condition in children, representing a global health and economic burden. Inodilators (i.e., vasoactive agents with inotropic and vasodilator effects), most commonly dobutamine and milrinone, are the cornerstone of pharmacological treatment for CS in children. Although pediatric guidelines still recommend dobutamine as the first-line inodilator in CS, the use of milrinone has become predominant in this indication. Milrinone is a phosphodiesterase - 3 inhibitor that is thought to exert inotropic and lusitropic effects and is commonly regarded as offering several theoretical advantages over dobutamine. Based on a critical review of current evidence, we examine here ten myths about milrinone in pediatric CS. The hemodynamic profile of milrinone in CS appears to rely primarily on vasodilation, with limited evidence for clinically meaningful inotropic or lusitropic effects. Current data support a neutral effect on myocardial oxygen consumption and an efficacy in preventing low cardiac output syndrome after pediatric cardiac surgery, while milrinone clearance is reduced in acute kidney injury with unclear clinical significance. However, no consistent evidence demonstrates milrinone's superiority over dobutamine in reducing mortality, length of hospital stay, or tachyarrhythmia, nor its greater efficacy in patients receiving beta-blockers. Its presumed benefits in newborns and in patients with right ventricular failure or pulmonary hypertension remain uncertain and warrant further investigation. What is known: • Milrinone is a phosphodiesterase-3 inhibitor that is thought to exert inotropic and lusitropic effects. • Milrinone has become the preferred inodilator over dobutamine in pediatric cardiogenic shock. What is new: • Milrinone's efficacy appears to stem from vasodilation rather than significant inotropy or lusitropy. • No consistent evidence shows its superiority over dobutamine; further study is warranted.

title: LPAR5 restrains sepsis-induced immunosuppression by limiting STING-mediated dendritic cell ferroptosis and ISG<sup>+</sup> cDC2 subset emergence.
authorString: Zheng Y, Zhu S, Tang Y, Long J, Xu B, Li T, Chen H, Liu W, Chen X, Li J, Peng C.
abstractText: Sepsis-induced immunosuppression is a major cause of secondary infection and mortality, yet the mechanisms governing dendritic cell (DC) dysfunction and loss remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify lysophosphatidic acid receptor 5 (LPAR5) as a critical regulator of DC survival and immune competence during sepsis. Integrative analysis of septic murine transcriptomic datasets and qRT‒PCR profiling of peripheral blood from patients with sepsis revealed the conserved upregulation of LPAR5, predominantly in conventional DCs (cDCs) in mice, and lower LPAR5 expression was associated with greater disease severity. Conditional deletion of Lpar5 in cDCs accelerated DC depletion, impaired DC maturation and antigen presentation, diminished naive CD4+ T-cell priming, and exacerbated bacterial burden, secondary infection, and mortality. Single‑cell RNA sequencing of splenic DCs from LPAR5‑deficient mice revealed that excessive stimulator of interferon genes (STING)‑type I interferon signaling with two parallel features, namely, ferroptotic death of cDCs and the emergence of an immunosuppressive interferon‑stimulated gene‑positive (ISG+) cDC2 subset, exacerbated immune paralysis. Mechanistically, LPAR5 interacts with the C-terminal tail of STING, limiting TANK-binding kinase 1 (TBK1) recruitment and restraining STING-dependent lipid peroxidation and ferroptotic death. Pharmacological inhibition of ferroptosis in vivo and of STING or TBK1 signaling in vitro restored DC survival. These findings define a previously unrecognized LPAR5-STING-TBK1 axis that safeguards DC homeostasis and identify the ISG+ cDC2 subset as a pathogenic contributor to sepsis-induced immunosuppression, highlighting LPAR5 as a potential therapeutic target to preserve antimicrobial immunity in sepsis.

title: REACH: A multidimensional index for measuring community concordance in US children's hospitals.
authorString: Dutta S, Ward VL, Hickey P, Mack T, Hall M.
abstractText: Equitable access to pediatric healthcare is essential for improving health outcomes and assessing health system accountability. Existing metrics for measuring hospital concordance with surrounding communities are adult-centric or sensitive to hospital catchment area definition. Through REACH (Representation and Equity in Area-based Child Hospitalizations) index, we aimed to develop a multidimensional, robust, and standardized concordance measure that combines four sociodemographic dimensions, ethnicity, payor, race, and sex, into a composite score that is comparable across hospitals. Using 695,046 inpatient and observation encounters from 48 U.S. children's hospitals in the Pediatric Health Information System (PHIS) for 2023 and 2023 American Community Survey (ACS) five-year estimate, we defined hospital catchment areas and calculated dimension-specific concordance indexes using weighted Chi-square divergence between observed hospitalizations and expected pediatric population. The four indexes were aggregated into a composite REACH score with 95% confidence intervals. Robustness of REACH was assessed using Spearman correlation between unrestricted and two conservative catchment definitions across 48 hospitals. REACH scores ranged from 0.89 to 0.98. All hospitals demonstrated high (≥0.80) to very high (≥0.90) concordance, with 60% of hospitals scoring ≥0.95. REACH was stable across catchment definitions, with strong correlations (ρ ≥ 0.7); all hospitals stayed in the high-to-very high range. Overall, 87.5% of hospitals retained their concordance category, while six showed modest downward shifts (from very high to high) under the most conservative definition. REACH offers an effective framework to measure community concordance in pediatric hospitals, with potential future applications for benchmarking, quality improvement, and policy development to advance equitable healthcare access.

title: Food Environments, Structural Disadvantage, and Risk of Gestational Diabetes and Preeclampsia.
authorString: Amoah AA, Wychgram C, Curriero FC, Bennett WL, Gross SM, Ogunwole SM.

journal.title: Women's health issues : official publication of the Jacobs Institute of Women's Health

abstractText: Obesity is a modifiable risk factor for gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) and preeclampsia, conditions that elevate maternal morbidity, mortality, and long-term cardiovascular risk. Lifestyle interventions are standard preconception recommendations for risk reduction, yet their feasibility is shaped by neighborhood and structural contexts. To explore these relationships, we evaluated associations of GDM and preeclampsia with neighborhood food environments, access to vendors authorized to accept benefits from the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC), and racialized economic segregation. We conducted a retrospective cohort study using electronic medical records from individuals with live births (N = 12,635) at three Maryland hospitals (2016-2021). Neighborhood exposures included the following: 1) food swamps-areas with a high density of unhealthy food retailers relative to healthy ones-measured using the modified Retail Food Environment Index (mRFEI); 2) racialized economic segregation, measured using the Index of Concentration at the Extremes (ICE); and 3) WIC vendor density per 1,000 residents. All exposures were modeled in tertiles, with the lowest tertile (Q1) indicating the most disadvantaged or lowest access and the highest (Q3) as reference. We used multivariable logistic regression with generalized estimating equations to assess associations with GDM and preeclampsia. Lower WIC access (lowest vs. highest tertile: adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.20; 95% confidence interval [CI] [1.02, 1.41]) and greater neighborhood disadvantage (ICE Q1 vs. Q3: aOR, 1.21; 95% CI [1.01, 1.44]) were associated with higher odds of GDM. No neighborhood measures were consistently associated with preeclampsia. Structural disadvantage and lower WIC vendor density were associated with higher odds of GDM but not preeclampsia. Expanding nutrition assistance infrastructure and addressing neighborhood disadvantage may improve maternal cardiometabolic health.

title: Heart Failure-Related Cardiogenic Shock: A Distinct Haemometabolic Syndrome.
authorString: Eng-Frost J, Burdeniuk C, Chan A, Parvar S, Gunton J, De Pasquale CG.
abstractText: Cardiogenic shock (CS) is increasingly recognised as a heterogeneous syndrome, with heart failure-related cardiogenic shock (HF-CS) now representing the predominant aetiology. However, contemporary diagnostic and therapeutic frameworks remain largely extrapolated from acute myocardial infarction-related cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS), despite fundamental differences in pathophysiology and clinical trajectories. In HF-CS, pathophysiology is better conceptualised as a haemometabolic construct in which congestion, impaired forward flow, and systemic metabolic dysfunction interact to drive progressive multiorgan failure. These processes are often poorly captured by conventional blood pressure (BP)-based definitions of CS, particularly in heart failure, where patients may have persistently low yet compensated baseline BP. Although the Society of Cardiovascular and Angiographic Interventions shock classification provides a useful severity-based framework, emerging evidence supports a more integrated diagnostic approach that incorporates biomarkers such as lactate, mixed venous oxygen saturation, and invasive haemodynamic profiling. Together, these measures may improve risk stratification and better guide the timing and selection of escalation strategies. In parallel, multidisciplinary shock team models may improve outcomes in HF-CS, particularly when implemented early, before irreversible end-organ dysfunction develops. Future advances in HF-CS will require a shift away from BP-centric definitions derived from AMI-CS towards a comprehensive haemometabolic framework integrating congestion, perfusion, and haemometabolic status. Prospective HF-CS specific trials evaluating early, phenotype-guided care within structured, protocol-driven systems are essential to improving outcomes in this growing and clinically complex population.

title: Cross-Disciplinary Collaboration in Ventricular Arrhythmia Ablation: A New Paradigm From Procedure to a Program of Care.
authorString: Sood A, Turnbull S, De Silva K, Bhaskaran A, Huang K, Hashimoto K, Campbell TG, Bennett RG, Kumar S.
abstractText:
Background

Catheter ablation of ventricular arrhythmias (VA) can be complex, requiring multidisciplinary expertise for safe and comprehensive patient management. We assessed the extent of perioperative multidisciplinary collaboration for VA ablations.

Method

We retrospectively identified 363 cases of VA ablation at an expert referral centre between 2017 and 2021. For these cases, extent of multidisciplinary involvement, PAINESD and MORTALITIES-VA scores, outcomes of ventricular tachycardia (VT) recurrence or premature ventricular complex (PVC) burden, cardiac transplantation and all-cause mortality were assessed.

Results

Of the 363 cases of VA ablation, 185 (51.0%) were elective and 178 (49.0%) were emergent. Most cases required peri-procedural involvement by another specialist (in addition to a cardiac electrophysiologist) (n=231 [63.6%]), including an intensivist in 97 (26.7%), anaesthetist in 87 (24.0%), geneticist in 38 (10.5%), cardiothoracic surgeon in 32 (8.8%), a heart failure and transplant cardiologist in 24 (6.6%), and immunologist in 16 (4.4%). The median PAINESD score was 6.2 (interquartile range [IQR] 0-9), and the median MORTALITIES-VA score was 3.0 (IQR 0-9). Subgroups with higher PAINESD and MORALITIES-VA scores and requiring more specialists in their care were emergent VA ablations (median 8 vs 3 [p<0.001], median 7 vs 0 [p<0.001], median 2 vs 0 [p<0.001], respectively), non-PVC ablations (median 6 vs 0 [p<0.001], median 4.5 vs 0 [p<0.001], median 1 vs 0 [p<0.001], respectively), and patients with structural heart disease (median 8 vs 0 [p<0.001], median 6 vs 0 [p<0.001], median 1 vs 0 [p<0.001], respectively). In PVC ablations the median reduction in PVC burden was 96.5%, and in non-PVC ablations the VT recurrence rate was 39.9%. In the follow-up period, cardiac transplantation was required by 2.9% of patients, and 12.5% of patients died.

Conclusions

Patients undergoing VA ablation require multidisciplinary involvement for optimal care, with multiple specialties involved in the peri-ablation period.

title: Associations of GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Usage With Clinical Outcomes of Limb Osteomyelitis in Type 2 Diabetes.
authorString: Perng PC, Chang Y, Wong CE, Huang CY, Lee JS, Khor WT, Perng PS, Lai YH.
abstractText: Patients with type 2 diabetes are prone to limb osteomyelitis, a condition associated with high morbidity and mortality. The relationship between glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1RA) use and outcomes in these patients remains unclear. We performed a retrospective cohort study using a large federated database from 2015 to 2024. Adult patients with type 2 diabetes (ICD-10 E11) and limb osteomyelitis were identified. GLP-1RA exposure was defined as use within 6 months prior to the diagnosis of osteomyelitis. Patients with end-stage renal disease, malignancy, or human immunodeficiency virus infection were excluded. Outcomes included all-cause mortality, amputation, sepsis, major adverse cardiovascular events, acute respiratory distress syndrome, and acute kidney injury. Propensity score matching was applied to balance baseline characteristics and disease severity. A total of 21,858 patients were identified. After propensity score matching, 2615 patients remained in each cohort with balanced baseline characteristics. GLP-1RA use was associated with lower mortality, with rates of 1.0% at 6 months (HR 0.48, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.30-0.78) and 4.7% at 3 years (HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.49-0.78). Compared with non-users, GLP-1RA users also had lower risks of amputation, sepsis, acute respiratory distress syndrome, and acute kidney injury. No significant differences were observed in major adverse cardiovascular events at either 6 months (odds ratio [OR], 0.88; 95% CI, 0.74-1.04) or 3 years (OR, 0.89; 95% CI, 0.78-1.02). Among patients with type 2 diabetes and limb osteomyelitis, GLP-1RA use was associated with lower risks of mortality, sepsis, acute respiratory distress syndrome, and acute kidney injury. These findings suggest a potential supportive role for GLP-1RAs in this high-risk population, although further studies are needed to clarify the underlying mechanisms.

title: Association of Preoperative Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter-2 Inhibitor Use with Postoperative Acute Kidney Injury and Recovery Outcomes Following Major Gastrointestinal Surgery.
authorString: Hussain K, Woldesenbet S, Angez M, Ali A, Faizan MA, Pawlik TM.

journal.title: Journal of gastrointestinal surgery : official journal of the Society for Surgery of the Alimentary Tract

abstractText: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors are increasingly used in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and may have established cardiovascular and renal benefits. However, the association with postoperative kidney injury and other surgical outcomes remains uncertain. We evaluated the association between preoperative SGLT2 inhibitor use and postoperative outcomes among patients with T2DM undergoing major gastrointestinal (GI) surgery. Epic Cosmos, a multicenter electronic health record database, was used to identify adults with T2DM who underwent major GI surgical procedure between 2018 and 2024. Preoperative SGLT2 inhibitor exposure was defined as continuous use during the 6 months before surgery, allowing interruptions of less than 5 days. The primary outcome was AKI within 7 days after surgery, identified using ICD-10 diagnosis codes, with creatinine-based AKI assessed as a complementary outcome. Entropy balancing and weighted regression models were used to evaluate associations between SGLT2 inhibitor use and postoperative outcomes. Among 201,123 patients, 11,750 had qualifying preoperative SGLT2 inhibitor exposure and 189,373 did not. ICD-10-based AKI occurred in 17.4% of SGLT2 inhibitor users and 21.2% of nonusers. After entropy balancing, SGLT2 inhibitor use was associated with lower odds of ICD-10-based AKI (OR, 0.85; 95% CI, 0.81-0.89) and creatinine-based AKI (OR, 0.87; 95% CI, 0.82-0.92). SGLT2 inhibitor use was also associated with lower odds of prolonged length of stay (OR, 0.77; 95% CI, 0.73-0.81), ICU stay (OR, 0.90; 95% CI, 0.85-0.95), 30-day mortality (OR, 0.42; 95% CI, 0.35-0.49), and 90-day mortality (OR, 0.50; 95% CI, 0.44-0.56), and higher odds of discharge home (OR, 1.38; 95% CI, 1.32-1.44). In contrast, SGLT2 inhibitor use was associated with higher odds of DKA within 7 days after surgery (OR, 3.59; 95% CI, 300.07-4.18). Among patients with T2DM undergoing a major GI surgical procedure, preoperative SGLT2 inhibitor use was associated with lower postoperative AKI but higher DKA. These data may help inform perioperative use SGLT2 inhibitors among patients undergoing GI surgery.

title: International Expert Consensus Statement on Contemporary Prevention and Management of Postoperative Delirium in Cardiac Surgery.
authorString: Abdulaziz S, Zaaqoq AM, Cho SM, Butt S, Alohali AF, Fraser JF, Amer M, Mufti H, Tronstad O, Bainbridge D, De Somer F, AlThenayan E, Sin YKK, Nagpal D, Ramanathan KR, Diaz-Gomez JL, Combes A, Soliman Aboumarie H, Flaws D, Wong SR, Malik S, Griffin M, Samoukovic G, Jones PM, Gellert GJ, Alreshidan M, Sinasac K, Guarracino F, Paternoster G, Engelman D, Arora R, Lorusso R.
abstractText: Postoperative delirium is among the most frequent neurocognitive complications of cardiac surgery, with reported incidence ranging from 14% to more than 50% depending on patient population and operative complexity. It is independently associated with prolonged mechanical ventilation, extended intensive care unit and hospital stay, long-term cognitive decline, and increased mortality. Despite this burden, prevention and management strategies remain inconsistent across institutions worldwide. An international multidisciplinary expert panel applied a structured PICOT (Population, Intervention, Comparison, Outcome, Timing) framework to predefined clinical questions spanning four perioperative phases: preoperative, intraoperative, postoperative and intensive care, and recovery after intensive care. Designated expert groups synthesized available evidence through structured literature reviews, and consensus recommendations were developed using a modified Delphi methodology. The panel developed 14 consensus statements. Preoperatively, routine screening with the Montreal Cognitive Assessment and Clinical Frailty Scale, and multicomponent optimization are recommended. Opioid-sparing multimodal analgesia is recommended, whereas perioperative dexmedetomidine in place of benzodiazepines, cerebral oximetry, processed electroencephalography-guided anesthesia depth monitoring, and optimized oxygen delivery may be considered. In intensive care, validated delirium screening paired with sedation assessment, daily awakening and breathing trials, structured multicomponent care bundles, correction of reversible precipitants, and circadian-supportive environments are central. After transfer from intensive care, continued ward screening and structured post-discharge cognitive follow-up are recommended. These statements provide a framework for preventing and managing postoperative delirium after cardiac surgery and advocate a coordinated multimodal approach. Standardizing screening, prevention bundles, and long-term follow-up within routine clinical pathways is recommended as a core institutional priority.

title: SMOC1 and SMOC2 in organ fibrosis: The direction of the effect is set by the responding cell and its ionic environment, not by the ligand alone.
authorString: Shang Q, Hu H, Li Y.
abstractText: Organ fibrosis is the shared terminal phenotype of chronic injury, and is usually treated as a target for inhibition. In the heart that assumption fails. The scar formed during the first week after acute myocardial infarction (MI) prevents the wall from giving way, and its load-bearing capacity is not a function of how much collagen it contains: fibroblast-specific deletion of CCN1 leaves collagen content and myofibroblast conversion unchanged, yet disorganises the fibril network and markedly increases post-MI rupture and mortality. Secreted modular calcium-binding proteins SMOC1 and SMOC2, members of the SPARC family, were long confined to skeletal and ocular development and to cancer, entering fibrosis biology only in the past decade. Evidence places SMOC2 on the profibrotic side in five organs, yet the same protein protects the renal tubule during acute kidney injury through integrin β3 and the CCND1-CDK4/6 axis. Conversely, SMOC1 is secreted transiently by cardiomyocytes after MI; cardiomyocyte-specific deletion doubles the incidence of rupture and AAV9-mediated overexpression reduces it. The same protein inhibits ALK5/SMAD2 signalling in endothelium through endoglin while activating it in fibroblasts through a complex containing the glutamyl-prolyl-tRNA synthetase EPRS. We argue, therefore, that their output is a property of the responding cell and its ionic environment, not of the ligand alone: it is set by the auxiliary-receptor repertoire the cell displays, the calcium concentration its EF-hand pair reads in calcifying tissue, and the phase of injury. Therapy should accordingly target scar quality locally and transiently rather than SMOC signalling globally.

title: One-Year Outcomes of Surgical Versus Endovascular Revascularization for Acute Limb Ischemia in the SAPLING-ALI Registry.
authorString: Hata Y, Iida O, Haraguchi T, Uchikawa T, Matsuda D, Koyama E, Yoshii D, Masuda M, SAPLING-ALI Investigators.
abstractText:
Objective

Despite the increasing use of endovascular therapy as an alternative to surgery for acute limb ischemia, individualized treatment selection remains challenging. We compared outcomes of endovascular therapy versus surgery and sought to identify patient characteristics favoring either strategy.

Methods

This multicenter retrospective study included consecutive patients with acute limb ischemia (Rutherford category 1-2b) who underwent revascularization at 13 Japanese institutions between July 2011 and March 2025; patients with thrombosed popliteal artery aneurysm were excluded. The primary outcome was amputation-free survival, defined as freedom from major amputation or death from any cause. The primary analysis was a Cox model adjusted for 13 baseline covariates with hospital as a categorical covariate; propensity score weighting was used as a sensitivity analysis. Subgroup analyses were performed to identify characteristics favoring either strategy.

Results

Of 978 patients (endovascular therapy, n = 607; surgery, n = 371), those treated with endovascular therapy more often had diabetes, hemodialysis, dementia, and non-ambulatory status. Unadjusted 1-year amputation-free survival was lower with endovascular therapy than with surgery (68.7% vs 76.3%; log-rank P = .001), but the adjusted hazard ratio for death or major amputation was 1.03 (95% confidence interval, 0.77-1.38; P = .84). Results were consistent with overlap weighting (hazard ratio 1.15; 95% confidence interval, 0.93-1.42) and across other sensitivity analyses. Thirty-day mortality was 13.1% after endovascular therapy and 8.9% after surgery (P = .05), and the difference was attenuated after weighting. No subgroup favoring either strategy was identified (all P for interaction ≥ .18).

Conclusions

Unadjusted amputation-free survival was lower after endovascular therapy than after surgery, but the difference disappeared after adjustment for patient characteristics and hospital, and no subgroup favoring either strategy was identified. Endovascular therapy, being less invasive, may be a reasonable alternative to surgery for acute limb ischemia.

title: Cardiovascular Outcomes of Semaglutide in Adults With Congenital Heart Disease.
authorString: Chough I, Rahmani AR, Kalogeropoulos A.
abstractText: Adults with congenital heart disease (ACHD) increasingly develop type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and obesity, yet are excluded from cardiovascular outcome trials, and the effects of semaglutide here are unknown. Using the TriNetX Research Network, we conducted a retrospective new-user active-comparator study of adults with ACHD and T2DM initiating semaglutide (n = 2,385) or a dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) inhibitor (n = 2,889) from December 2017 to December 2025. Cohorts were 1:1 propensity score matched, yielding 1,422 pairs followed for 3 years, with a sensitivity analysis matched on 27 lesion categories. Semaglutide was associated with lower all-cause mortality (7% vs 12%; hazard ratio [HR] 0.66, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.51 to 0.85), hospitalization (40% vs 55%; HR 0.68, CI 0.61 to 0.76), and emergency department (ED) visits (35% vs 43%; HR 0.85, CI 0.75 to 0.96). Major adverse cardiovascular events (HR 0.71), heart failure (HR 0.74), and stroke (HR 0.65) were also lower; myocardial infarction and arrhythmia were not. Mortality, hospitalization, and ED visits were significant at 1, 3, and 5 years and in every sensitivity analysis; the cardiovascular associations were not. Congenital aortic valve disease was twice as common among semaglutide initiators before matching (23% vs 12%), and every great-complexity lesion comprised ≤10 patients per arm. A prespecified negative control was elevated in every analysis. In conclusion, semaglutide was associated with lower mortality and acute care utilization in a predominantly simple-to-moderate complexity ACHD population, but an elevated negative control indicates residual differences in healthcare engagement; these findings are hypothesis-generating.

title: Timing of Coronary Angiography After Successful Fibrinolysis and Clinical Outcomes in ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction Patients.
authorString: Li S, You B, Yin P, Xiang D, Zhou M, Wang Y, Zhang R, Huo Y, Jin Y, Liu F.
abstractText: For patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) who cannot undergo timely primary percutaneous coronary intervention, fibrinolysis followed by routine angiography is recommended, but the clinical outcomes associated with different angiography intervals within the guideline-recommended window remain uncertain. In this nationwide retrospective cohort of 130,322 patients treated between 2018 and 2023, 74,021 underwent angiography 2-6 hours and 56,301 underwent angiography 6-24 hours after successful fibrinolysis. The 2-6-hour group more frequently had TIMI flow grade <3 at initial angiography (35.97% vs 29.86%; adjusted odds ratio [OR], 1.28; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.16-1.39) but had less new-onset heart failure (7.34% vs 8.30%; adjusted OR, 0.89; 95% CI, 0.84-0.95), with no significant differences in in-hospital bleeding or mortality. During available follow-up, angiography within 2-6 hours was associated with lower all-cause mortality (adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 0.87; 95% CI, 0.78-0.98) and cardiac death (adjusted subdistribution HR, 0.85; 95% CI, 0.76-0.95). In conclusion, among patients with STEMI undergoing angiography after successful fibrinolysis, a T2C interval of 2-6 hours was associated with lower long-term mortality and less new-onset heart failure without increased in-hospital bleeding or mortality, providing large-scale real-world evidence supporting further prospective evaluation of angiography timing within the recommended 2-24-hour window.

title: Temporal plasma proteomic differences between women with takotsubo syndrome and ST-elevation myocardial infarction identified by proximity extension assay.
authorString: Kakaei Y, Kalani M, Jha S, Andersson EA, Sevastianova V, Omerovic E, Arif M, Redfors B.
abstractText:
Background

Takotsubo syndrome (TS) and ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) present with similar acute clinical features but arise from distinct pathophysiological mechanisms. We aimed to characterize temporal differences in circulating plasma between TS and STEMI using proximity extension assay-based proteomics. To minimize confounding by sex-related differences in protein expression, we restricted analyses to women.

Methods

Plasma samples were collected from 38 women with TS and 34 women with STEMI at the acute, subacute, and late phase following presentation. Protein abundance was quantified using the Olink proximity extension assay platform. Differential abundance between TS and STEMI was assessed using linear regression models adjusted for age and sampling day, with false discovery rate correction. Pathway over-representation analysis was performed on differentially abundant proteins.

Results

Few proteins differed between TS and STEMI at the acute and late time points. In contrast, the subacute phase demonstrated a markedly larger number of proteins increased in TS relative to STEMI. Pathway enrichment analysis of proteins increased in TS revealed representation of cytokine and interleukin signaling, innate immune system pathways, and receptor tyrosine kinase-mediated signal transduction. No coherent pathway signature was observed among proteins increased in STEMI at this time point.

Conclusion

These findings highlight the subacute phase as a key interval for distinguishing plasma protein profiles between these clinically overlapping syndromes.

title: Readmission outcomes after left atrial appendage occlusion in older adults with atrial fibrillation and bleeding or anticoagulation-alternative indications: A landmark analysis of the nationwide readmissions database, 2018-2020.
authorString: Hazique M, Noor M, Burhan M, Nair D, Medranda GA, Alraies MC, Goldsweig AM.
abstractText:
Background

Left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) is increasingly used in older adults with atrial fibrillation (AF) at risk of bleeding or contraindication to long-term anticoagulation, but its association with age and frailty is poorly described.

Methods

Adults ≥65 years with nonvalvular AF at elevated thromboembolic risk whose index admission carried a coded bleeding event or an anticoagulation-alternative indication were identified in the Nationwide Readmissions Database (2018-2020). Patients alive at the 90-day landmark were stratified by LAAO vs. no LAAO within 90 days. The primary outcome was all-cause readmission during days 91-270. Survey-weighted logistic regression and propensity-score matching were used to estimate odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

Results

Among 1,244,671 patients, 2070 underwent LAAO at a mean of 52.4 ± 23.4 days after index. LAAO was associated with higher adjusted odds of all-cause readmission (aOR 1.31, 95% CI 1.15-1.49) and cardiovascular readmission (aOR 1.33, 1.14-1.55). Bleeding readmission was also higher. In-hospital death at readmission did not differ. Age-by-frailty-by-LAAO interaction was not significant (p = 0.85), although subgroup analyses were underpowered.

Conclusions

In older adults with AF and a bleeding event or an anticoagulation-alternative indication who were alive at 90 days, inpatient LAAO was associated with higher subsequent readmissions, including bleeding. Out-of-hospital deaths were not captured, and death competes with readmission, so higher readmission does not mean a worse net clinical outcome. These associations may reflect differences in baseline bleeding risk, inpatient exposure capture, and residual confounding.

title: Temperature Deviation from Prior Exposure: Dynamic Temperature Fluctuations and Cause-Specific Mortality in Four Chinese Megacities.
authorString: Ma P, Zhou K, Yang Y, Zhang Y, Zhang X, Wang S.
abstractText: Dynamic temperature fluctuations are a key driver of morbidity and mortality. Incorporating dynamic thermal adaptation, this study hypothesized that deviations between current and prior thermal environments modulate subsequent thermophysiological regulation, and quantified the health impacts of the temperature deviation (TD) metric as an added stressor. Cause-specific mortality data were collected from Harbin, Beijing, Chengdu, and Shanghai between 2010 and 2016, comprising 249,100 respiratory and 740,925 cardiovascular death cases. We used quasi-Poisson models to investigate the association between TD and cause-specific mortality in four Chinese cities with distinct climatic conditions. Models were stratified by seasonal temperature trends, with RRs referenced to the stratum-specific median TD. Warming episodes was associated with increased mortality risks in all four cities, yet the TD-mortality associations differed among the cities. At +3°C over lag 0-21 d, the strongest positive-TD associations were observed for respiratory mortality in Beijing during the cooling period (RR=1.694, 95% CI: 1.354-2.120) and for cardiovascular mortality in Shanghai during the warming period (RR=1.287, 95% CI: 1.193-1.389). During the cooling periods, a delayed association only emerged at extreme temperature drops in the two northern cities, whereas cumulative RRs at moderate cooling (-5 and -3 °C) remained below unity. In comparison, elevated mortality risks in the southern cities were associated with moderate cooling at lags of 7-15 d. Specifically, over lag 0-21 d at -3 °C, the highest cumulative cardiovascular RR was observed in Chengdu (1.200, 95% CI: 1.041-1.382). Moreover, negative TDs were inversely associated with mortality risks across all four cities under warming trends. Our findings reveal city- and season-specific patterns in the health impacts of dynamic temperature fluctuations, highlighting the need for location- and season-specific health risk mitigation and climate adaptation strategies.

title: Departure From Planned 39-Week Delivery for Fetal Congenital Heart Disease: Indications for Earlier Birth.
authorString: Packer CH, Ronai C, Carreon CK, Morton SU, Guseh SH, Wilkins-Haug LE.
abstractText:
Objective

Delivery >39 weeks' gestation is recommended for fetuses with congenital heart disease (FCHD). However, hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP), maternal diabetes and fetal growth restriction (FGR) are more common in these pregnancies and often necessitate early delivery. We evaluated indications for delivery at <39 weeks and examined maternal covariates, cardiac diagnoses and placental pathology.

Study design

This retrospective observational study included maternal-fetal dyads with prenatally diagnosed, structurally isolated, genetically unremarkable FCHD delivered at a single center. Gestational age and delivery indication were obtained from medical record. Placental pathology was assessed using Amsterdam criteria. Regression models evaluated associations with gestational age and neonatal mortality.

Results

46.3% (99/214) delivered <39 weeks; 65.6% (65/99) were due to maternal or fetal compromise, and 34.3% (33/99) to obstetric indications. HDP (20.1%) was strongly associated with <39-week delivery (32.3% vs 9.6%, p<0.001) and the greatest reduction in gestational age (-2.31 weeks, p<0.001). Multivariable analysis identified preeclampsia, type 2 diabetes, lower birthweight Z-score, and race as independent predictors of earlier delivery (p<0.05). Neonatal mortality was higher with maternal/fetal indications (15.7%) versus obstetric (5.4%) or elective FCHD delivery (5.6%) (p=0.02).

Conclusion

Nearly half of FCHD infants delivered before 39 weeks, largely due to maternal and placental disease, underscoring the importance of placental health in this population.

title: Bilateral mastectomy in small ruminants: Clinical indications, surgical outcomes, and long-term development.
authorString: Sendag S, Trzebiatowski L, Wehrend A.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Tierarztl Prax Ausg G Grosstiere Nutztiere
journal.title: Tierarztliche Praxis. Ausgabe G, Grosstiere/Nutztiere
journal.isoabbreviation: Tierarztl Prax Ausg G Grosstiere Nutztiere

abstractText: The objective of this clinical case series was to evaluate bilateral mastectomy in small ruminants with chronic mammary disorders as a long-term clinical and welfare-oriented therapeutic intervention, with particular emphasis on postoperative wound healing, long-term survival, and owner-reported assessment of treatment success. This clinical case series comprised 21 consecutive small ruminants, including goats (n=17) and sheep (n=4), presented to our clinic for bilateral mastectomy due to mammary disorders unresponsive to medical therapy. Surgical indications included endocrine-related false lactation (alone or in combination, n=12), mastitis (abscess-forming or gangrenous, n=10), cisternal rupture (n=3), and mammary neoplasia (n=1). All procedures were performed under general anesthesia using standardized surgical techniques. Long-term follow-up was conducted through structured owner interviews assessing survival status, condition of the surgical site, and willingness to repeat the procedure under similar clinical circumstances. Bilateral mastectomy was successfully completed in 20 animals without intraoperative complications. One goat with extreme mammary hypertrophy (12 kg gland weight; 60 kg body weight) died intraoperatively. No major intraoperative hemorrhage was observed, and cardiovascular failure was considered the most likely cause of death based on the clinical circumstances. A postmortem examination was not performed. During long-term follow-up, 5 animals died due to causes unrelated to the surgical procedure, whereas 15 animals were reported to be alive and clinically stable without mastectomy-associated health problems. Surgical site healing was considered satisfactory in the vast majority of cases. All owners reported satisfaction with the outcome and stated that they would elect mastectomy again if required. Bilateral mastectomy in small ruminants demonstrated favorable long-term survival, low procedure-related mortality, and high owner-perceived therapeutic value. Beyond its established role in chronic and gangrenous mastitis, the procedure proved particularly relevant for endocrine-related false lactation, an under-recognized surgical indication. These findings support bilateral mastectomy as a viable, welfare-oriented therapeutic strategy in goats and sheep with severe mammary pathology refractory to medical management.

title: Baseline QRS duration is not an independent predictor of one-year outcomes in a large native African cohort of chronic heart failure: Insight from the Ibadan Heart Failure Project.
authorString: Orimolade OA, Ezeh CH, Ogah CM, Alabi OG, Makinde OZ, Ademola OJ, Inedu PO, Ademowo-Olusanya OO, Ogah F, Aje A, Orimadegun BE, Adegoke O, Adebayo OM, Adeoye AM, Oladapo OO, Adebiyi AA, Orimadegun AE, Ogah OS.

journal.title: Journal of the National Medical Association

abstractText:
Background

Prolonged QRS duration reflects ventricular conduction delay and electrical dyssynchrony. It is associated with adverse outcomes in heart failure, but evidence from contemporary African chronic heart-failure cohorts remains limited.

Objective

To evaluate the relationship between baseline QRS duration and one-year mortality, rehospitalization and the composite of mortality and/or rehospitalization among adults with chronic heart failure in Ibadan, Nigeria.

Methods

This prospective observational study analyzed data from the Ibadan Heart Failure Project. Adults aged 18 years or older with chronic heart failure, baseline QRS duration, one-year follow-up/vital-status information and valid outcome time were included. QRS duration was analyzed primarily as <120 ms versus ≥120 ms. Mortality was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier curves and Cox proportional-hazards models; rehospitalization and the composite outcome were analyzed using logistic regression.

Results

The current analysis was based on participants recruited between 01 January 2016 and 27 June 2023. The final analytic cohort comprised 1047 patients; 380 (36.3%) had QRS ≥120 ms. Patients with prolonged QRS were older, more often male, more likely to have kidney dysfunction and had more adverse echocardiographic remodeling. One-year mortality was higher with QRS ≥120 ms than QRS <120 ms (84/380, 22.1% versus 106/667, 15.9%; log-rank p = 0.012). In univariable Cox analysis, QRS ≥120 ms was associated with mortality (HR 1.44; 95% CI 1.08 to 1.92; p = 0.012). After multivariable adjustment, this association was attenuated (adjusted HR 1.12; 95% CI 0.80 to 1.58; p = 0.504). Adjusted associations with rehospitalization (OR 1.09; 95% CI 0.55 to 2.15; p = 0.813) and the composite outcome (OR 1.19; 95% CI 0.82 to 1.71; p = 0.361) were also non-significant.

Conclusion

In this Nigerian chronic heart-failure cohort, QRS ≥120 ms identified a higher-risk clinical phenotype and poorer crude one-year survival. After adjustment, it was not an independent predictor of mortality, rehospitalization or the composite outcome.

title: Fully Automated, Explainable AI Analysis of Coronary CTA Improves Prediction of Major Cardiovascular Events.
authorString: Gulsun MA, Singh V, Lira J, Sami S, Gupta P, Agarwal S, O'Donnell TP, Laidlaw M, Shaw RE, Sharma P, Gupta H.
abstractText: Coronary artery disease (CAD) remains a major global cause of morbidity and mortality. Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) is central to noninvasive diagnosis and risk assessment, yet current workflows are labor-intensive and depend on semiquantitative scoring systems that do not fully leverage prognostic information in CCTA. The objectives of the study were to develop and validate a fully automated, explainable artificial intelligence (AI) system (AI-automated coronary analysis [ACA]) for comprehensive CCTA analysis to predict major adverse cardiovascular events and compare its performance with conventional risk markers. AI-ACA automatically extracts a suite of CCTA-derived biomarkers, including stenosis severity, plaque burden, and composition; AI-derived CAD - reporting and data system (CAD-RADS) (AI-CADRADS); coronary tortuosity; and subtended myocardial mass, to generate interpretable risk estimates. In a retrospective cohort (n = 1,702), we compared AI-ACA with Agatston score, standard demographic risk markers, and AI-CADRADS. Model explainability was assessed using Shapley Additive Explanations. AI-ACA demonstrated higher predictive performance (area under the curve [AUC]: 0.81) than Agatston score (AUC: 0.76) and demographic markers (AUC: 0.67), and similar performance to AI-CADRADS (AUC: 0.81). AI-ACA showed better prognostic discrimination than Agatston score, reflected by a higher Harrell C-index (0.791 vs 0.742) and greater separation in event-free survival on Kaplan-Meier analysis (log-rank 31.79 vs 13.71). Shapley Additive Explanations analysis identified total plaque volume and burden, maximum stenosis severity, and AI-CADRADS as the strongest contributors to risk estimation.
