A fully automated and explainable AI platform for CCTA enables comprehensive quantitative characterization of CAD without manual intervention. Although prognostic performance was comparable to AI-CADRADS and modestly higher than Agatston score, the platform provides transparent biomarker-based risk assessment and scalable analysis that may facilitate broader clinical implementation of quantitative CCTA.

title: Adjuvant breast cancer radiotherapy after total body irradiation for haematopoietic stem cell transplantation: First reported case series on safety and feasibility.
authorString: Loap P, Kirova Y.

journal.title: Cancer radiotherapie : journal de la Societe francaise de radiotherapie oncologique

abstractText: Total body irradiation is used in conditioning regimens before haematopoietic stem cell transplantation for acute leukaemia. Women who subsequently develop breast cancer present a unique challenge, as adjuvant breast or chest wall radiotherapy constitutes a form of reirradiation. No previous series has reported outcomes in this setting. This study aimed at assessing the tolerance of adjuvant breast radiotherapy in patients previously treated with total body irradiation for haematopoietic stem cell transplantation conditioning. We retrospectively reviewed all women treated at the institut Curie who had received total body irradiation before autologous or allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation for acute leukaemia and later underwent surgery followed by adjuvant breast or chest wall radiotherapy. Data collected included leukaemia treatment details, breast cancer characteristics, adjuvant therapy, and toxicity. Survival and disease control were assessed from the date of breast cancer diagnosis. Five patients met inclusion criteria. Median age at the time of leukaemia diagnosis was 39 years; median interval between total body irradiation and breast radiotherapy was 18 years. Histology was invasive ductal (n=2), lobular (n=2), or mixed carcinoma (n=1). Two patients presented with lymph node metastases. Radiotherapy techniques included isocentric lateral decubitus three-dimensional radiotherapy (n=2), volumetric modulated arctherapy (n=2), and field-in-field intensity-modulated radiotherapy (n=1), all in free breathing; no boost was delivered. Hypofractionation (40.05Gy delivered in15 fractions) was used in two patients. Acute toxicity was limited to grade 1 radiodermatitis in three cases; no grade 2 or worse acute event, nor late cardiac, pulmonary, nor cutaneous toxicity occurred. Median follow-up was 58 months; one patient developed distant relapse at 33 months; no death occurred. Adjuvant breast or chest wall radiotherapy after prior total body irradiation was feasible and well tolerated in this series, with minimal acute toxicity and no late organ effects. Modern techniques and careful planning may allow safe treatment in selected patients.

title: Ninety-Day Acute Ischemic Stroke Readmission in People Hospitalized With Migraine With Aura: A National Cohort Study.
authorString: Strelecky L, Shu L, Spears R, Bakradze E, Salehi Omran S, Field TS, Nguyen TN, Siegler JE, Stretz C, Furie K, Yaghi S.
abstractText: Migraine with aura is recognized as a risk factor for acute ischemic stroke (AIS). However, the short-term risk of stroke, particularly within 90 days of hospitalization for migraine, has not been thoroughly evaluated on a national scale. This study aims to address this gap by examining the association between migraine with aura during admission and 90-day AIS readmission. Using the Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project's Nationwide Readmissions Database between 2016 and 2019, we identified patients in the United States who received a diagnosis of migraine during admission, either principal or nonprincipal. The reference group for analysis contained all adult patients admitted during the study period without a principal or nonprincipal diagnosis of migraine. The primary outcome was subsequent admission for AIS within 90 days. Diagnoses were identified using standard and validated ICD-10-CM codes. Three patient groups were delineated: migraine with aura, migraine without aura, and unspecified migraine. Inverse probability of treatment weighting and multivariable Cox regression models were used to assess the risk of AIS across these 3 patient groups, adjusted for risk factors. Among 64,808,935 patients (mean age 56.19 years, 60.0% female) admitted during the study period, 1,257,671 (1.94%) patients were admitted with any migraine diagnosis, of which 78,650 (6.25% of migraine cohort) were admitted with a principal diagnosis of migraine. In total, 75,460 (0.12%) were admitted with migraine with aura. Within 90 days, 272,812 (0.42%) patients were readmitted with AIS. After adjusting for cardiovascular risk factors, migraine with aura was associated with an elevated risk for 90-day AIS (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 1.98, 95% CI 1.68-2.35, p < 0.001). In the primary analysis, similar risk was not demonstrated in the overall migraine group (aHR 1.00, 95% CI 0.94-1.06, p = 0.960), migraine without aura group (aHR 0.86, 95% CI 0.62-1.21, p = 0.392), and unspecified migraine group (aHR 0.96, 95% CI 0.90-1.03, p = 0.257); however, modest associations emerged in sensitivity analyses. Among hospitalized patients, migraine with aura was associated with an increased risk of AIS within 90 days. These findings underscore the importance of careful vascular risk assessment in this population. Future research should investigate the pathomechanisms underlying this association.

title: State of The Art of The da Silva's Cone Operation for Treatment of Ebstein's Anomaly.
authorString: Silva JPD, Morell V, Cascudo MM, Castro-Medina M, Bezerra RF, Castro RM, Guilhen JC, Silva LDFD.
abstractText: Ebstein's anomaly (EA) is a complex congenital heart disease caused by embryological failure of the tricuspid valve (TV) leaflet delamination, leading to displacement of the leaflets and right ventricular myopathy. In 1958, Hunter and Lillehei began developing surgical techniques for the repair of EA. Their technique was followed by many others. However, those techniques presented significant limitations due to the wide range of anatomical variations in the disease. The Da Silva Cone repair (CR) for EA emerged as the most anatomical repair technique for all forms of the disease, yielding the best results for most patients. Since CR can be performed with low mortality and morbidity, is effective and durable, and rarely requires TV replacement, it has been widely adopted. It allowed that surgical intervention can be indicated before the development of significant right ventricular dilatation or dysfunction. CR can be applied to any age, but it carries more risk in the neonate with critical EA. Therefore, neonates with critical EA may benefit from a staged approach, performing the Starnes procedure in the neonatal period and the CR later. The 2025 American Association for Thoracic Surgery expert consensus on managing EA covered preoperative evaluation, surgical indications, and contraindications in neonates, children, and adults. Additionally, the expert consensus discussed the approach to cardiac arrhythmias associated with EA and alternative procedures for select cases, including TV replacement and a bidirectional cavopulmonary shunt, depending on patient characteristics. They also agreed that the CR repair of the TV is beneficial when surgery is indicated.

title: Data-driven clinical decision trees and generative topographic mapping to guide stroke rehabilitation program allocation.
authorString: Komaris DS, Anagnostou P, Nikolopoulos S, Tsaopoulos D, Guillen-Sola A, Duarte E, Bellfield RAA, Ortega-Martorell S, Olier I, Kompatsiaris I.
abstractText:
Background

Early and timely admission to post-stroke rehabilitation remains a key determinant of optimal functional recovery. In this study, we present a structured framework for the development and evaluation of multivariable prediction models and Classification and Regression Tree (CART) decision-support tools to guide patient allocation across diverse subacute rehabilitation settings.

Methods

We have constructed a heterogeneous synthetic dataset of 700 stroke patients characterized by 49 demographic, clinical, and functional variables derived from multiple, literature-reported, statistical distributions of patient populations. Subsequently, the dataset was independently annotated by an expert panel of clinicians, who assigned each stroke patient to one of seven rehabilitation programs ranging from home-based to high-intensity hospital-based care (target outcome). Feature importance analysis identified cognitive function status, National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score, age, presence of early seizures, and alcohol consumption as the most influential predictors of rehabilitation program allocation. Six supervised classifiers were then trained to predict rehabilitation program allocation, along with shallow CARTs of different depths. Internal evaluation used 200 repetitions of stratified ten-fold cross-validation, with metrics calculated from pooled out-of-fold predictions and summarized as mean and standard deviation.

Results

In internal evaluation against the expert-assigned labels, the XGBoost and the best-performing CART model achieved mean accuracies of 0.832 and 0.847 and balanced accuracies of 0.381 and 0.393, respectively. Both exceeded the institutional benchmark, which achieved accuracy of 0.753 and balanced accuracy of 0.325. Key predictors included cognitive function status, NIHSS score, age, presence of early seizures, and alcohol consumption. In addition, Generative Topographic Mapping (GTM) facilitated the exploration of patient relationships within different prediction models that may help distinguish clusters with similar phenotypes, i.e., patient groups with shared clinical characteristics. It further enabled the visual comparison of stroke rehabilitation program predictions across models (e.g., baseline versus CART model). This allowed for assessment of program recommendations by the developed models in transparent and meaningful ways, and the identification of patient characteristics influencing divergent model decisions.

Conclusions

This study demonstrates the feasibility of developing and evaluating multivariable prediction models for rehabilitation program allocation using an openly shared and expert-annotated dataset. This framework offers a transparent and adaptable foundation for developing bespoke, data-driven decision-support systems in stroke rehabilitation. Ultimately, the proposed approach promotes interpretable, context-sensitive, and individualized rehabilitation planning adaptable to varying clinical resources and practices.

title: Transition metal-based nanocatalysts for bidirectional immunomodulation: from catalytic anti-inflammation to catalytic immunotherapy.
authorString: Yang B, Shi J.
abstractText: Immune homeostasis is crucial for health, yet its hyperactivation or suppression poses significant therapeutic challenges. Nanocatalysts, especially transition metal-based nanocatalysts, are powerful chemical tools for immunomodulation. They work by precisely regulating chemical species in pathological microenvironments. These nanocatalysts serve two therapeutic purposes. First, antioxidative nanocatalysts scavenge excess ROS. This "cools down" hyperactivated immunity in inflammatory diseases, such as cardiovascular disorders, neuroinflammation, and bone diseases. Second, pro-oxidative nanocatalysts generate ROS. This "heats up" suppressed immunity in cancer and infections, mainly by inducing immunogenic cell death. This tutorial review elucidates the chemical basis of nanocatalytic bidirectional immunomodulation, discussing related catalytic and therapeutic mechanisms based on typical paradigms. Rational design of nanocatalysts determines which chemical reactions occur. These reactions lead to different immunoregulatory outcomes. Nanocatalytic bidirectional immunomodulation provides a richer set of chemical tools to meet the requirements of immune activation or suppression during disease treatments. Most existing reviews have focused on unidirectional nanocatalytic therapy. This tutorial review is the first work to systematically unify nanocatalytic anti-inflammation and nanocatalytic immunotherapy from the perspective of "bidirectional immunomodulation".

title: Implementation Feasibility and Clinical Utility of Phenomapping in Dilated and Hypokinetic Non-dilated Non-ischemic Cardiomyopathy.
authorString: Wang Y, Tse JJ, Abdelhaleem A, Dykstra S, Hasanzadeh F, Rivest S, Flewitt J, Feng Y, Howarth AG, Lydell CP, Kolman L, Miller RJH, Fine NM, Labib D, White JA.
abstractText:
Aims

Despite phenotypic heterogeneity, the management of idiopathic non-ischemic cardiomyopathy (NICM) remains generalized and dominantly guided by left ventricular (LV) ejection fraction (EF) and NYHA class. We aimed to develop a point-of-service phenomapping pathway for dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) and hypokinetic non-dilated cardiomyopathy (HNDC) at time of CMR imaging leveraging the integration of i) patient self-reported health status, ii) imaging phenotype, and the iii) electronic health record (EHR).

Methods and results

1,355 patients (752 DCM and 603 HNDC) were followed for the composite MACE outcome of mortality, heart failure hospitalization or ventricular arrhythmia. K-means clustering was independently applied to DCM and HNDC derivation cohorts using 55 routinely captured features (16 patient-reported health variables, 19 CMR-derived, 14 EHR-derived, and 6 combined features), identifying three phenogroups in each cohort. Over a median of 3.9 and 3.7 years, 145 DCM patients (22%) and 65 HNDC patients (13%), respectively, experienced MACE. Adjusting for age, sex, NYHA class, and LV EF, phenogroup membership was independently associated with future outcomes. In DCM, the adjusted HR (95% CI) of phenogroups 2 and 3 versus Phenogroup 1 were 2.8 (1.6-4.8) and 3.5 (1.9-6.5), respectively (p<0.001 for both). In HNDC, Phenogroup 3 demonstrated an adjusted HR of 4.2 (1.7-10.2; p=0.001) versus Phenogroup 1. Prospective phenogroup assignment was enabled by a decision tree-classifier and validated in a temporal hold-out cohort.

Conclusion

Phenomapping delivers incremental value to LVEF and NYHA for identification of high-risk NICM patients. These findings support value from standardized, point-of-service data integration for the delivery of phenomics-driven personalized care.

title: Blood pressure and arterial stiffness in the pathway between long-term PM2.5 exposure and cardiovascular risk: exploratory mediation analysis in middle-aged and older adult men.
authorString: Veronesi G, Cestaro SA, De Ponti R, Giusti EM, Schnabel RB, Gianfagna F, Ferrario MM.
abstractText:
Aims

The extent to which blood pressure (BP) and arterial stiffness mediate the association between long-term PM2.5 exposure and cardiovascular risk, and whether individuals with metabolic impairment are more susceptible, remain unclear.

Methods

Within the "Risk of Cardiovascular diseases and abdominal aortic Aneurysms in Varese" (RoCAV) cohort, we retained 2119 men aged 50-75 and free of coronary heart disease (CHD) and stroke at baseline; carotid-femoral Pulse Wave Velocity (cfPWV) was measured in a subset of 1015 using an automated oscillometer. Exposure was the 12-month mean PM2.5 concentration before baseline (EXPANSE models); outcome was incident major acute CHD or stroke (MACE), fatal or non-fatal. We estimated the mediating contribution of BP and cfPWV through Marginal Structural Models and Aalen survival models, with individual- and area-level confounders.

Results

In a median follow-up of 7.6 years, 178 MACE events occurred (rate=1155 per 100,000 person-years), and 76 (1086/100,000 p-y) in the cfPWV subset. Systolic BP, mean BP, brachial pulse pressure and cfPWV were highest in the most exposed. Each 1-µg/m3 increase in PM2.5 was associated with 151 (95%CI:21-282) additional MACE events per 100,000 p-y, of which 48 (95%CI:17-79) were mediated by cfPWV (mediated proportion: 32%). Systolic BP and brachial pulse pressure each mediated about 16% of the PM2.5-associated risk. The cfPWV-mediated effect was enhanced in men with impaired glucose (96;95%CI:38-155) and elevated LDL-cholesterol (88;95%CI:28-147).

Conclusions

Large-artery stiffness substantially contributes to the MACE burden associated with chronic PM2.5 exposure, especially in men with metabolic impairment. Monitoring cfPWV may help incorporate environmental risk into cardiovascular prevention.

title: What's Blood Got to Do with It? Identifying MPDS® Dispatch Codes Most Commonly Associated with Prehospital Blood Administration.
authorString: Khan S, Malani E, Eisenman J, Matthews P, Burch K, Dworkin M, Starr-Leach K, Aber D, Conrad J, Dattoli J, Sebastianelli E, Snyder R, Rosenbaum R.
abstractText: This study aimed to identify Medical Priority Dispatch System (MPDS®) codes most frequently associated with prehospital blood utilization. We examined Delaware's prehospital blood database to determine dispatch codes where low titer group O positive whole blood (LTOWB) was administered. We calculated the number of blood units under each dispatch code within the study period (May 2023- February 2026). Using this data, we identified the MPDS® codes associated with the highest number of blood units, including the top five codes overall, top medical codes, and as well as blood utilization rates for penetrating versus blunt traumas. The most frequent blood utilization came from the following dispatch codes: 29D02 (traffic collision, high mechanism) 32 patients, 27D04G (penetrating trauma with central wounds) 32 patients, 29D02M (auto versus pedestrian) 28 patients, 29D05 (traffic collision with entrapment) 24 patients, and 29D02L (auto versus bicycle/motorcycle) 20 patients. These five dispatch codes accounted for 29% of all prehospital LTOWB utilized within the 33-month study period. Analyzing blood utilization for non-traumatic dispatch codes revealed: 21D04/21D04M (dangerous hemorrhage, medical) 18 patients, 21D03/21D03M (hemorrhage, not alert, medical) 13 patients, 9E01/M9E01/M9E02 (cardiac or respiratory arrest/death, not breathing) 13 patients, and 21D05/21D05M (hemorrhage, abnormal breathing, medical) 7 patients. These four dispatch codes accounted for 11% (51 patients) of LTOWB utilization. When performing odds ratio analysis to determine odds of blood administration, we found 27D04G, 29D02M, and 29D02L to be statistically significant with 95% confidence intervals of [0.35- 0.87], [2.42- 5.72], [1.47- 3.91], and odds ratios of 0.55, 3.72, and 2.40, respectively. Additionally, our analysis demonstrated that patients with MPDS® coding for penetrating trauma with a delta level priority (27D) have higher likelihood of prehospital blood administration than delta priority high mechanism traffic incidents (29D). This comparison showed an OR of 10.40 that blood would be given to the penetrating trauma patient with a 95% confidence interval of [7.93- 13.66]. Specific MPDS® codes are strongly associated with prehospital blood utilization. Identifying these patterns offers a unique opportunity for emergency medical services systems to implement automatic blood dispatch protocols based on dispatch code.

title: Chest Computed Tomography Receipt Beyond 5 Years After Lung Cancer Diagnosis and Survival.
authorString: Yoon DW, Kang D, Jeong BH, Choi HL, Park J, Lee SH, Shin DW, Kim HK.
abstractText: Long-term lung cancer (LC) survivors remain at risk of LC events (LCEs), including late recurrence and second primary LC, beyond 5 years after diagnosis, but the role of computed tomography (CT) surveillance beyond 5 years remains uncertain. To evaluate whether CT receipt beyond 5 years after LC diagnosis is associated with LCEs and survival. This nationwide population-based cohort study used sequential target trial emulation with monthly eligibility reassessment and time-updated propensity score matching based on data from the Korean National Health Insurance Service database. Patients diagnosed with LC from 2006 to 2019 were followed up through December 31, 2024. Long-term LC survivors were eligible for trial entry 5.5 years after diagnosis if they had no administrative evidence of active or recurrent LC, a prior LCE, or another primary cancer. Data were analyzed between January 1, 2026, and February 28, 2026. CT receipt beyond 5 years after LC diagnosis, defined as chest CT during the 1-month assessment window at each monthly trial baseline, compared with no CT receipt. The primary outcome was LCE occurrence, defined by new LC-specific special copayment registration after the monthly trial baseline. Secondary outcomes were all-cause mortality, surgical resection after LCE detection, and subsequent mortality. The cohort of 55 694 LC survivors (mean [SD] age, 63.3 [10.9] years; 58.0% male) contributed 2 629 462 eligible person-trials. Matching yielded 583 756 person-trials per group. During a median (IQR) follow-up of 2.74 (1.16-5.18) years, CT receipt was associated with a higher incidence of LCEs (2.49% vs 1.97% per year; hazard ratio [HR], 1.28 [95% CI, 1.26-1.29]) and lower all-cause mortality rate (2.62% vs 4.33% per year; HR, 0.66 [95% CI, 0.65-0.67]) compared with no CT receipt. Among patients with an LCE, CT receipt was associated with greater odds of surgical resection after LCE (odds ratio, 1.46 [95% CI, 1.41-1.52]) and a lower subsequent mortality risk (HR, 0.63 [95% CI, 0.61-0.64]). These associations were observed more frequently among females (HR, 0.47 [95% CI, 0.44-0.49]), older adults (HR, 0.57 [95% CI, 0.54-0.60]), and never smokers (HR, 0.55 [95% CI, 0.53-0.57]). In this cohort study, CT receipt beyond 5 years after LC diagnosis was associated with increased detection of LCEs, greater use of surgical resection after an LCE, and a lower all-cause mortality rate. These findings support further evaluation of risk-adapted CT surveillance beyond 5 years in selected LC survivors.

title: Racial trauma and criterion a: On the nature of discrimination, threat, and danger.
authorString: Kendall-Tackett K.

journal.title: Psychological trauma : theory, research, practice and policy

abstractText: The Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, fifth edition, text revision, Criterion A for posttraumatic stress disorder describes potential traumatic events as actual or threatened death, serious injury, or sexual violence. On its face, racial discrimination, particularly when individual discriminatory experiences, does not meet conventional trauma criteria. This commentary considers whether racial discrimination could be a source of perceived threat and considers how this might be relevant regarding the trauma diagnosis. Drawing on research in psychoneuroimmunology, neuroscience, and social rejection, this commentary examines the physiological mechanisms through which perceived discrimination activates the body's threat-response systems. Evidence suggests that racial discrimination activates neurobiological threat pathways involving the amygdala, anterior cingulate cortex, hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, and inflammatory response system. Studies have linked perceived discrimination to elevated inflammatory markers, including C-reactive protein and interleukin-6, as well as adverse cardiovascular, metabolic, and reproductive outcomes. Research on social rejection provides a theoretical framework for understanding why seemingly minor discriminatory experiences may cumulatively signal danger and activate physiological defense mechanisms. Racial discrimination can function as a biologically meaningful threat even when individual experiences fall outside current Criterion A definitions. Incorporating evidence of physiological threat activation into trauma research and reconsidering how subjective and cumulative threats are addressed in posttraumatic stress disorder diagnostic criteria may provide a more comprehensive understanding of racial trauma and its health consequences. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

title: Estimated pulse wave velocity acceleration is an algebraic function of its own inputs: incremental prognostic value of blood-based biological age beyond chronological age and blood pressure in older US and Chinese adults.
authorString: Wang H, Chen J, Wu Y, Zhang J, Li J.
abstractText: Estimated pulse wave velocity (ePWV) is widely reported as a measure of vascular age, yet it is computed from chronological age and mean blood pressure (MBP); whether its age-residualized component, ePWV acceleration, carries information beyond those inputs has never been tested. Among 3972 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) participants aged 60 or older (1034 deaths, 330 cardiovascular) we asked whether ePWV acceleration is a quantity distinct from its own inputs, and compared its prognostic value with blood-based biological age, based on PhenoAge and the Klemera-Doubal method (KDM), for all-cause and cardiovascular mortality, validating the comparison in two Chinese cohorts (CHARLS, n = 7892; CLHLS, n = 560). Within each risk branch of the estimating equation, ePWV acceleration was reproduced exactly from its own inputs (R2 approximately 1; residual standard deviation below 1 × 10⁻11 m/s) and correlated 0.990 with MBP, whereas the blood-based accelerations were uncorrelated with MBP. PhenoAge acceleration (hazard ratio per standard deviation 1.82, 95% confidence interval 1.68 to 1.97) and KDM acceleration (1.64, 1.53 to 1.76) predicted mortality, were well calibrated, retained incremental discrimination once spline age and MBP were modeled (change in Harrell C + 0.036 and + 0.032), and did so under machine-learning survival models and in both Chinese cohorts. ePWV acceleration added none (- 0.0001) and was not jointly estimable with MBP. Within the indices examined, blood-based biological age carried transportable prognostic information beyond chronological age and blood pressure, whereas age-residualized ePWV was an algebraic re-expression of its inputs.

title: Short-acting induction, long-acting maintenance: real-world trajectories of GnRH antagonist and agonist therapy for prostate cancer in Japan.
authorString: Pinton P.
abstractText: The relative cardiovascular safety of gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) antagonists and agonists remains unresolved, and little is known about how the two classes are sequenced in routine Japanese practice. We described initiation and 12-month trajectories of GnRH therapy and explored factors associated with antagonist selection. Retrospective descriptive study of a Japanese hospital-based administrative database (Medical Data Vision). Men with newly recorded prostate cancer (July 2023-December 2024) initiating degarelix, originator or generic leuprorelin, or goserelin were included. Treatment status at 12 months was classified as continuation, switch, discontinuation or not evaluable. Proportions are reported with Wilson 95% confidence intervals (CIs); subgroups were compared with chi-square tests on aggregate counts. Among 6808 men (median age 76 years), 1997 (29.3%) initiated degarelix. Within 12 months, 1086 degarelix initiators (54.4%; 95% CI 52.2-56.6) switched to an agonist, mainly originator leuprorelin (66.2% of switches), whereas only 6 of 4811 agonist initiators (0.1%) switched to degarelix. Long-acting (3- or 6-month) agonist depots rose from 37.3% at initiation to 62.9% at 12 months. Among patients with available prostate-specific antigen (PSA) values, degarelix was initiated in 75.9% of those with PSA  ≥  100 ng/mL versus 35.3% of those with PSA 20-99 ng/mL (p  <  0.001). Degarelix initiation did not differ by history of myocardial infarction (29.6% vs 29.3%) or angina (29.2% vs 29.3%; both p  =  1.00). In Japan, degarelix was often used as a short-term induction agent, particularly when PSA was high, before transition to long-acting agonists, irrespective of coronary history.

title: Spexin attenuates isoproterenol-induced myocardial injury in rats: association with reduced PANoptosis-associated markers, NINJ1, HMGB1, and neuropeptide Y.
authorString: Altinbas B, Sen Halicioglu B, Görücü Yılmaz S, Cetin Z, Bozkurt AS, Yalcin M, Pazarbasi ED, Gültekin M.
abstractText: Acute myocardial injury is characterized by oxidative stress, inflammation, and convergent regulated cell-death responses. Spexin (SPX) is a pleiotropic neuropeptide involved in cardiovascular and metabolic regulation and has been reported to have antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and cytoprotective effects. However, its role in PANoptosis-associated myocardial injury remains unclear. Because apoptosis, pyroptosis, and necroptosis may act in concert during myocardial damage, we examined whether SPX is associated with modulation of PANoptosis-related responses in an isoproterenol (ISO)-induced rat model. Myocardial injury was induced by subcutaneous ISO administration (100 mg/kg, twice at 24-h intervals), followed by intraperitoneal SPX treatment (35-70 µg/kg) for 7 days. Serum and myocardial tissues were analyzed for cardiac injury markers, inflammatory cytokines, oxidative stress indices, neuropeptide Y (NPY), and high-mobility group box 1 (HMGB1). Immunohistochemistry was used to assess nerve injury-induced protein 1 (NINJ1), cardiomyocyte markers, and PANoptosis-associated proteins related to apoptosis, pyroptosis, and necroptosis. ISO caused marked myocardial injury, inflammatory and oxidative imbalance, increased NINJ1 immunoreactivity and HMGB1 levels, elevated NPY levels, reduced NK2 homeobox 5 and cardiac troponin T immunoreactivity, and upregulation of PANoptosis-associated markers, including Cleaved Caspase-3/7, Cleaved Gasdermin-D, NOD-like receptor family pyrin domain-containing 3, phospho-receptor-interacting protein kinase 1/3, and phospho-mixed lineage kinase domain-like protein. Both SPX doses were associated with attenuation of several ISO-induced alterations; however, no consistent dose-dependent pattern was observed across the assessed outcomes. These findings support an association between SPX treatment and reductions in integrated cell-death-associated marker immunoreactivity, membrane damage-related inflammatory responses, and neurohumoral stress in experimental myocardial injury.

title: Cardiogenic shock phenotypes and outcomes under percutaneous left ventricular support: results from a 9-year single-center real-world cohort.
authorString: Chatzis G, Syntila S, Schuett H, Lapp H, Fichera CF, Schieffer B, Goebel B, Markus B, Kreutz J, Sassani K, Waechter C, Ausbuettel F, Kano F.

journal.title: Clinical research in cardiology : official journal of the German Cardiac Society

abstractText:
Background

Refractory cardiogenic shock (CS) remains associated with unacceptably high mortality despite advances in intensive-care and coronary intervention strategies. Percutaneous left ventricular support using Impella is widely used, yet real-world outcomes may differ substantially by underlying shock etiology and phenotype.

Methods

We performed a retrospective single-center cohort study of adults treated with Impella 2.5/CP for refractory CS over a 9-year period. Patients were classified as acute coronary syndrome (ACS), dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM)/myocarditis, severe aortic stenosis (AS), sepsis-associated CS, or other causes. Endpoints were all-cause in-hospital and 12-month mortality. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, lactate, vasoactive score, Impella type was conducted; a sensitivity model additionally included creatinine.

Results

Among 409 patients (mean age 69.99 ± 11.56 years; 75.6% male), ACS was the leading phenotype (n = 269), followed by DCM/myocarditis (n = 53), AS (n = 32), sepsis-associated CS (n = 36), and other causes (n = 19). Impella CP was used in 227 patients (55.5%). Overall in-hospital mortality was 48.9% and differed across phenotypes, being highest in sepsis-associated CS (80.6%; chi-squared p < 0.001). Sepsis remained independently associated with in-hospital death after adjustment (adjusted odds ratio 4.65, 95% CI 2.03-12.07, p = 0.0006) for major confounders; finding was consistent after additional adjustment for creatinine (adjusted odds ratio 4.17, 95% CI 1.63-12.26, p = 0.0023). Major bleeding occurred in 14.9%, limb ischemia in 11.7%, pseudoaneurysm in 4.9%, and stroke in 1.0% of the patients. Twelve-month survival analysis also demonstrated phenotype-dependent patterns (log-rank p < 0.01).

Conclusion

In refractory CS treated with Impella outcomes are strongly phenotype-dependent. Sepsis-associated CS represents an extreme-risk phenotype with poor short- and long-term survival, suggesting phenotype-guided patient selection and prospective validation of escalation strategies.

title: Lipoprotein(a): An underrecognized cardiovascular disease risk factor in primary care.
authorString: Hellier S.
abstractText:
Abstract

In the US, cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of death for men and women of most racial and ethnic groups. An estimated 20%-25% of people have elevated lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] levels; however, it is an underrecognized risk factor for atherosclerotic heart disease and calcific aortic valve disease. Lp(a) levels are genetically determined and unaffected by lifestyle modifications and statin therapy. It is recommended that Lp(a) be measured in all adults at least once for risk assessment. Primary care nurse practitioners are well positioned to perform risk stratification, provide patient education, and manage elevated Lp(a) levels.

title: Subclinical hairy vetch (Vicia villosa) hypersensitivity in cattle with concurrent infectious diseases.
authorString: Mendes RE, Blubaugh AL, Sebastián Pineda DA, Corbett MP, Maboni G, Goggans AB, Morris ERA, Rissi DR.
abstractText: Systemic granulomatous disease in cattle is primarily caused by Vicia villosa (hairy vetch) hypersensitivity. This report describes an unusual mortality outbreak associated with diverse secondary disease processes in a beef cattle herd exposed to vetch. The farm managed adult Angus cows split into herd A (n = 30, purchased 1-year prior) and herd B (n = 35, a closed herd). All 12 deaths occurred in herd A. Eleven of the deceased cows lacked classic signs of vetch hypersensitivity (alopecia, pruritus, pyrexia, hemorrhages, and lymphadenomegalia). Four animals were autopsied, initially suggesting distinct causes of death: hemorrhagic bowel syndrome with pneumonia, retained placenta, hemorrhagic diathesis with cardiac clostridiosis, and suppurative bronchopneumonia. Despite early autopsies not raising suspicion of vetch hypersensitivity, the discovery of 1 animal with alopecia during the fourth autopsy prompted questioning and confirmation of V. villosa consumption. This fourth cow was the first with gross lesions characteristic of vetch hypersensitivity. All autopsied cattle had mild (cases 1-3) to moderate (case 4) granulomatous inflammation with occasional multinucleated giant cells affecting lymph nodes, kidneys, liver, and heart. The presence of diverse disease processes, the majority attributable to bacterial infections, in all autopsied cattle suggests that subclinical vetch hypersensitivity, in combination or not with other factors, might have predisposed the herd to secondary fatal infections, a feature previously unreported in the literature. Ultimately, this outbreak underscores a critical principle in diagnostic pathology: a comprehensive, accurate clinical history is vital for a correct and timely diagnosis, especially when classic clinical presentations are absent.

title: Discontinuation of Anticoagulation in Patients at Relatively High Risk of Stroke After Successful Catheter Ablation for Atrial Fibrillation: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
authorString: Lee YS, Yang PS, Kang DS, Bae HJ, Kim M, Kim HJ, Park H, Kim D, Kim JB, Joung B.
abstractText: Oral anticoagulant (OAC) discontinuation after atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation may be feasible in selected patients; however, outcomes in those at high stroke risk remain unclear. This study aimed to evaluate associations between OAC discontinuation beyond 1 year after ablation and thromboembolic or bleeding events across CHA2DS2-VA risk strata. Patients without AF recurrence within 12 months of catheter ablation and with CHA2DS2-VA scores ≥2 were identified from the Korean National Health Insurance Service database and classified as OAC continuers or discontinuers based on prescription coverage at the 12-month landmark. The primary outcome was a composite of stroke or systemic embolism and major bleeding. Doubly robust estimation combined overlap weighting with covariate-adjusted Cox regression, stratified by CHA2DS2-VA score (2-4 and ≥5). Among 3,637 patients (mean age: 60.8 ± 9.7 years, 27.1% female, mean CHA2DS2-VA 3.2 ± 1.3), discontinuation in those with scores of 2-4 (n = 3,054) was associated with lower risks of the composite event (HR: 0.61; 95% CI: 0.38-0.96) and major bleeding (HR: 0.51; 95% CI: 0.29-0.90), without increased stroke or systemic embolism (HR: 0.73; 95% CI: 0.34-1.58). In those with scores ≥5 (n = 583), discontinuation was not significantly associated with any outcome, and tests for interaction were not significant (all P > 0.46). In this nationwide cohort, OAC discontinuation beyond 1 year after AF ablation was associated with decreased bleeding risk without a corresponding increase in thromboembolic events among patients with CHA2DS2-VA score 2 to 4.

title: Long-Term Milrinone as a Bridge to Recovery in Fontan-Associated Protein-Losing Enteropathy.
authorString: Breitschopf H, Aggarwal A.
abstractText:
Background

Protein-losing enteropathy (PLE) occurs in 5% to 18% of post-Fontan palliation patients with a historical mortality rate of 50%. Treatment of PLE continues to be challenging because of limited understanding of its pathophysiology.

Case summary

A 14-year-old boy with double outlet right ventricle and left ventricular hypoplasia with an extracardiac Fontan developed refractory PLE. He was started on long-term, outpatient milrinone at 0.5 μg/kg/min. Over 15 months, ventricular function improved and PLE resolved. Recovery was sustained 8 months after milrinone discontinuation.

Discussion

Milrinone's augmentation of cardiac output and reduction in pulmonary vascular resistance may directly address PLE physiology. Long-term milrinone therapy has primarily been studied as a bridge to transplant. Notably, this case highlights milrinone's use as a bridge to recovery. The 15-month duration of milrinone was safe without adverse outcomes.

Take-home message

Long-term outpatient milrinone therapy may serve as a bridge to recovery in patients with refractory Fontan-associated PLE.

title: Cardiac Function Profiling of Preeclamptic Patients by Impedance Cardiography.
authorString: Belk SS, Novotny S, Amin G, Losordo L, Butler KR, Booz GW, LaMarca B, Morris R.
abstractText: Preeclampsia is associated with cardiac dysfunction during pregnancy and increased long-term cardiovascular risk. Although thoracic fluid content (TFC) is increased in preeclampsia, its relationship to cardiac performance remains unclear. This study used impedance cardiography to characterize maternal hemodynamics and to evaluate the associations among TFC, cardiac performance, and disease severity. A retrospective analysis included 645 pregnant women, comprising 128 normotensive controls, 170 women with moderate preeclampsia, and 347 with severe preeclampsia. Thoracic fluid content increased progressively across preeclampsia severity groups. Stroke volume index and cardiac index were lower, while systemic vascular resistance index was higher, primarily in women with severe preeclampsia. Correlation analysis demonstrated an inverse association between stroke volume index and systemic vascular resistance index, whereas associations between thoracic fluid content and other hemodynamic measures were comparatively weak. These findings suggest that increased thoracic fluid content in preeclampsia is not strongly explained by variations in systemic vascular resistance or indexed cardiac output and stroke volume alone.

title: Long-Term Neurologic Complication and Healthcare Burden in Infants Receiving Extracorporeal Life Support: A Nationwide Population-Based Cohort Study.
authorString: Kang M, Lee D, Yu H, Choi I, Koh E, Kim WK, Kim YO, Song MK, Schmitt KRL, Jeong IS, Yoo S, Cho HJ.

journal.title: Pediatric critical care medicine : a journal of the Society of Critical Care Medicine and the World Federation of Pediatric Intensive and Critical Care Societies

abstractText:
Objectives

To evaluate survival, neurologic complications, and healthcare burden in infant extracorporeal life support (ECLS) recipients using nationally representative administrative data from a single-payer healthcare system.

Design

Retrospective, population-based cohort study.

Setting

South Korea's National Health Insurance Service, covering 97% of the population.

Patients

Infants under 1 year who received ECLS between 2009 and 2022.

Interventions

None.

Measurements and main results

Of 698 infants who underwent ECLS, 212 infants (30.4%) survived during follow-up (estimated 1-yr mortality: 67.1%). Among survivors, 128 (60.4%) developed neurologic injuries, including acute events such as ischemic stroke, hemorrhagic stroke, and hypoxic-ischemic brain injury (HIBI), as well as long-term sequelae such as cerebral palsy, epilepsy, hearing loss, and developmental delay. Most acute neurologic injuries were diagnosed within the first year, whereas developmental delay showed prolonged diagnostic windows extending up to 12 years. Survivors with neurologic injury had significantly longer hospital stays (432.1 vs. 182.3 d; p < 0.001) and higher cumulative healthcare costs during long-term follow-up. Median index hospitalization costs were USD 36,000-37,000. The burden analysis showed distinct profiles across neurologic complications: developmental delay was the most prevalent sequela, whereas HIBI was associated with the highest cumulative healthcare cost despite lower prevalence.

Conclusions

Neurologic complications following ECLS in infants are common and impose substantial long-term healthcare burden. These findings highlight the need for early risk stratification, structured neurologic and neurodevelopmental monitoring, and sustained rehabilitation planning in this high-risk population. This study provides a foundation for international benchmarking and health policy planning in pediatric critical care.

title: Prevalence and Characteristics of Coma in Latin American Critical Care Units: The COMA LATAM Study.
authorString: Giglio A, Reccius A, Ferre A, Pino M, Carvajal C, Ciarrochi N, Vences M, Mejia-Mantilla J, Carrizosa J, Crespo M, Heredia-Orbegoso GO, Flecha J, Melgarejo D, Pichardo-Viñas M, Perez C, Paranhos J, Orellana-Jimenez C, Heredia J, Mora J, Fischer D, Aguilera S, Suarez JI, and members of the Coma in Latin America (COMA LATAM) group, on behalf of the Latin American Brain Injury Consortium (LABIC) and the Curing Coma Campaign, Colombia and Costa Rica and Cuba and Dominican Republic and Ecuador and El Salvador and Guatemala and Honduras and Mexico and Panama and Paraguay and Peru and Puerto Rico and Uruguay and Venezuela.
abstractText: To determine the point prevalence of coma across Latin American critical care units, characterize its etiology, and explore short-term outcomes. Multinational, cross-sectional point prevalence study with exploratory 14-day follow-up assessment. Three hundred ninety-two hospitals across 19 Latin American countries, including ICUs, intermediate care units, neurocritical care units, cardiovascular ICUs, and trauma ICUs. Adult patients (≥ 18 yr) meeting the Coma Epidemiology, Evaluation, and Therapy care survey (COME-TOGETHER) criteria on May 28, 2024. Patients under deep sedation or pharmacological coma induction were excluded unless the coma state preceded pharmacological intervention. None (observational study). Among 8305 critically ill patients, 1145 met coma criteria (point prevalence 13.8%), with country-specific rates ranging from 5.1% to 36.8%. Individual patient data were available for 729 patients (63.7%). Traumatic brain injury was the leading individual cause (24.8%), followed by hypoxic-anoxic brain injury (14.6%) and intracerebral hemorrhage (13.5%). When categorized by pathophysiology, vascular causes predominated (48.6%), followed by traumatic brain injury (24.8%) and other causes (26.6%). Age-stratified analysis revealed trauma predominantly affecting younger patients, while cerebrovascular causes predominated in older groups. Among patients with 14-day follow-up data (29% of cohort), mortality was 29.2%, with 67.7% of survivors recovering from coma. Only the Charlson Comorbidity Index was independently associated with implementation of life-sustaining therapy limitations (adjusted odds ratio, 1.22; 95% CI, 1.15-1.30; p < 0.001). Coma affects nearly one in seven ICU beds across Latin America, with substantial country variation and distinct age-dependent etiology patterns. The significant burden highlights the need for targeted prevention strategies and specialized neurocritical care resources throughout the region.

title: Modulating Platelet Reactivity with GLP-1RAs in Diabetes: Mechanistic Insights, Potential Benefits, and Clinical Limitations in Atherothrombotic Prevention.
authorString: Nusca A, Di Bitonto MP, Santella C, Lentini AE, Rasi A, Beato S, Gatto L, Ricottini E, Mangiacapra F, Cammalleri V, Prati F, Ussia GP.
abstractText: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have redefined cardiovascular medicine, reducing major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) through pleiotropic mechanisms that transcend glycemic and weight control. While their cardioprotective benefits are well-established, their direct impact on platelet activity-a key driver of atherothrombotic risk-remains a compelling frontier. This narrative review first addresses the heightened atherothrombotic risk characteristic of patients with diabetes and the clinical challenges posed by their suboptimal response to standard antiplatelet regimens. Subsequently, it explores experimental evidence on the antiplatelet properties of GLP-1RAs. Mechanistically, GLP-1RAs exert a dual inhibitory action: direct modulation involves the activation of platelet-surface GLP-1 receptors, triggering the PKA signaling cascade and VASP phosphorylation, which in turn suppresses calcium mobilization and aggregation. Indirectly, these agents restore vascular health by enhancing nitric oxide bioavailability, preserving endothelial glycocalyx integrity, and shifting perivascular adipose tissue toward an anti-inflammatory phenotype. Furthermore, GLP-1RAs mitigate the pro-thrombotic milieu by attenuating glycemic variability and systemic inflammatory cascades. However, these compelling experimental findings do not currently translate into clear clinical impact, and a clinical gap persists: while reductions in mortality and stroke risk are firmly established, the specific efficacy of GLP-1RAs in preventing acute coronary events is still evolving. In conclusion, GLP-1RAs emerge as multifaceted tools with significant cardiovascular protection, offering a synergistic approach to secondary prevention in high-risk cardiometabolic patients; however, how these favorable outcomes are mediated by antiplatelet properties warrants dedicated prospective investigations to translate experimental findings into clinical certainty.

title: Cost-effectiveness analysis of new-generation drug-eluting stents for myocardial infarction: a nationwide population-based study.
authorString: Tung YC, Chang GM.

journal.title: International journal for quality in health care : journal of the International Society for Quality in Health Care

abstractText: Drug-eluting stents (DESs) are the preferred treatment for myocardial infarction (MI) but are not reimbursed under some national health insurance (NHI) systems. Therefore, those who care about long-term effectiveness might face economic limitations when selecting DESs. Moreover, limited information is available concerning the cost-effectiveness analysis of new-generation (including second- and third-generation) DESs. We used nationwide population-based data to evaluate the cost-effectiveness of new-generation DESs compared to bare-metal stents (BMSs) from the NHI perspective. We included all 10,672 MI patients who underwent stent implantation in 2018 in Taiwan and were followed to 2023 through Taiwan's NHI database. After 1:1 propensity score matching, 3,913 patients were in each BMS and DES group. Multivariable Cox and linear regression models were performed to evaluate the effect of DES use on 1-, 2-, and 5-year mortality and medical cost, respectively. Then, the incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs) were calculated. Patients receiving DESs had 52%, 48%, and 43% lower risks of 1-, 2-, and 5-year mortality and NT$27,839 higher 1-year costs compared to those receiving BMSs, respectively. The 1-, 2-, and 5-year ICERs for DESs were NT$463,983, NT$241,299, and NT$302,750 per death avoided, respectively. New-generation DESs are cost-effective based on the cost-effectiveness threshold recommended by the World Health Organization. Considering the effectiveness and cost of new-generation DESs, including reimbursement for this technology under the NHI system would benefit beneficiaries and enhance long-term survival for MI.

title: Sex-specific differences in mortality in obstructive sleep apnea: results from the Sleep Apnea Patients in Skaraborg (SIS) Study.
authorString: Peker Y, Holtstrand Hjälm H, Thunström E, Glantz H, Pihtili A, Eulenburg C.

journal.title: Annals of the American Thoracic Society

abstractText: Sex differences in mortality among patients with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) remain incompletely understood. We analyzed data from the Sleep Apnea Patients in Skaraborg (SIS) Study, including adult patients with OSA defined as an apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) ≥5 events/hour. OSA severity was classified as mild (AHI 5-14.9), moderate (AHI 15-29.9) or severe (AHI ≥30). All-cause mortality was assessed over a median follow-up of 5.9 (interquartile range 4.6-7.2) years using multivariable Cox regression adjusted for age, obesity, current smoking status, diabetes mellitus, Epworth Sleepiness Scale score, hypertension, cardiovascular disease, and cerebrovascular disease. Interaction between sex and OSA severity was tested, and analyses were stratified by age (≤50 and >50 years). The cohort comprised 3,843 patients with 421 deaths. Despite lower OSA severity, women had an overall mortality of 10.0% (120/1,203), compared with 11.4% (301/2,640) in men. Men had higher mortality than women in severe OSA (HR 1.50; 95% confidence interval (CI) [1.09; 2.05]; p = 0.011), whereas no sex differences were observed in mild and moderate OSA (HR 0.95; 95% CI [0.61; 1.50]; p = 0.850 and 1.09; 95%CI [0.73; 1.63]; p = 0.662; interaction p = 0.110) . In age-stratified analyses, among patients ≤50 years, women demonstrated higher mortality than men irrespective of the severity of OSA (HR for men versus women 0.34; 95%CI [0.14; 0.87]; p = 0.024), while among patients >50 years, men with severe OSA had the highest mortality risk (HR 1.58; 95%CI [1.15; 2.18]; p = 0.005). Treatment was associated with reduced mortality in patients >50 years (HR 0.52; 95%CI [0.40; 0.67]; p < 0.001). Mortality risk among patients with OSA varied according to sex, age, and OSA severity. Our findings suggest potentially distinct risk patterns, with higher mortality observed among younger women and among older men with severe OSA. The findings in younger patients should be interpreted cautiously because of the limited number of events.

title: Diagnostic yield and biomarker Kinetics of an institutional CK-MB trigger for emergency coronary angiography after elective cardiac surgery.
authorString: König KC, Wiebe J, Günther T, Vitanova K, Maurer L, Cassese S, Schunkert H, Lange R, Kastrati A, Krane M.
abstractText: This study evaluated the diagnostic yield, biomarker kinetics, and outcomes of an unstratified institutional CK-MB trigger (≥120 U/L) for emergency coronary angiography after elective cardiac surgery. In this retrospective study (2016-2023), 225 of 7,111 elective cardiac surgery patients (3.2%) with postoperative CK-MB levels ≥120 U/L underwent emergency coronary angiography regardless of symptoms. Serial CK-MB trajectories (4h to POD3) were analyzed across surgical entities. New pathological coronary findings were identified in 113 patients (50.2%; CP group), while 112 showed no relevant abnormalities (49.8%; CN group). Diagnostic yield varied dramatically by procedure type: 88.5% in isolated CABG (predominantly distal anastomotic lesions) vs. <28% in isolated valve surgery (mainly mechanical suture or cannulation trauma). In serial analyses, catheter-negative valve patients exhibited a sharp early "trauma peak" at 12 hours followed by rapid clearance, whereas true ischemic compromise produced sustained plateaus through POD2. The CP group required significantly longer intensive care (7 vs. 5 days; p < 0.001) and hospital stays (16.5 vs. 14 days; p < 0.001). Thirty-day mortality did not differ significantly (17.7% vs. 14.3%; p = 0.484). While an unstratified CK-MB trigger demonstrates high diagnostic yield in CABG patients, it causes a high rate of unnecessary catheterizations in valve surgery due to transient surgical trauma washout. Rigid biomarker cutoffs without kinetic tracking and procedural stratification are clinically insufficient.

title: Charcot-Leyden crystals drive a localized inflammatory niche around mucus plugs in Allergic Bronchopulmonary Aspergillosis.
authorString: Aegerter H, Janssens I, Verstraete K, Malfait T, Heyndrickx I, Ahmed E, Burgelman J, Smole U, Ulrichts H, Van Acker T, Stortelers C, Ceuppens S, De Prijck S, Vanheerswynghels M, Dupont S, Wayenberg A, Baeke F, Goncalves A, Maes T, Jonckheere L, Vande Weygaerde Y, Schaballie H, Schelstraete P, Riemann S, Brusselle GG, Hoogenboom R, Vu H, Madder A, Rüthing M, Strube U, Hartmann G, Schmidt SV, Bormans G, Cleeren F, Kleynhans J, Magnen M, Looney MR, Raymond W, Charbit A, Fahy JV, Savvides SN, Van Braeckel E, Lambrecht BN.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Am J Respir Crit Care Med
journal.title: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine
journal.isoabbreviation: Am J Respir Crit Care Med

abstractText: Mucus plugging causes airflow obstruction, morbidity, and mortality in chronic respiratory diseases. Charcot-Leyden crystals (CLCs), formed from eosinophil-derived Galectin-10, are frequently observed in pathologic mucus, but their role in disease is unclear. To define the prevalence, inflammatory context, and functional role of CLCs in mucus plugs, using acute allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis (ABPA) as a model of eosinophilic muco-obstructive disease. Airway samples from 19 patients with acute ABPA and 61 disease controls were analyzed for CLCs and Galectin-10. Paired samples from plugged and unplugged bronchial mucosal biopsies defined the spatial relationship between CLCs and inflammation. A novel mouse model demonstrated the contribution of CLCs to airway obstruction and inflammation and enabled evaluation of CLC-directed imaging and therapy. Airway CLCs were a sensitive and specific marker of acute ABPA. CLC-containing mucus plugs were surrounded by a localized type 2 inflammatory niche, alongside eosinophils, neutrophils and extracellular traps, whereas inflammation was minimal in unplugged airways from the same patients, or plugs lacking CLCs. In mice, CLC-containing plugs induced persistent airway obstruction and local inflammation, both reduced by a crystal-dissolving anti-Galectin-10 antibody. Galectin-10 concentrations provided a quantitative biomarker of acute ABPA, while a CLC-targeted positron emission tomography tracer enabled noninvasive visualization of crystal-rich plugs. CLC-containing mucus plugs form focal inflammatory niches in acute ABPA, and experimental CLC deposition is sufficient to promote persistent airway obstruction and inflammation. These findings identify CLCs as a biomarker, imaging target, and tractable therapeutic target in eosinophilic muco-obstructive airway disease.

title: Aortic Root Remodeling Patterns and Outcomes Five Years Following Contemporary Root Replacement Strategies in Young Patients: A Single-Center Experience.
authorString: Nwanna-Nzewunwa O, Otoruko M, Jaquiss RDB, Andersen ND, Davies RR, Reyes KM.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: World J Pediatr Congenit Heart Surg
journal.title: World journal for pediatric & congenital heart surgery
journal.isoabbreviation: World J Pediatr Congenit Heart Surg

abstractText: Background: Long-term dimensional remodeling patterns after contemporary aortic root operations in young patients have historically not been well characterized and this may inform surgical decision-making.Methods: We evaluated longitudinal aortic root and annular remodeling patterns and clinical outcomes after the Bentall, Ross, or Valve-Sparing Root procedures from January 1, 2000 to December 31, 2024.Results: Sixty patients underwent aortic root replacement. Of these, 17 had the Bentall procedure (BP), 20 had the Ross procedure, and 23 had Valve Sparing Aortic Root Replacement (VSARR). On average Ross patients (4 years) were younger than BP (16 years) and VSARR (16 years) (p = .0001). Marfans (20%, 12/60), Down Syndrome (3%, 2/60) and Loeys-Dietz (3%, 2/60) were prevalent. All Marfan patients (n = 12) underwent VSARR (p = .006). The leading surgical indications were aortic regurgitation (78%, 47/60), aortic stenosis (58%, 35/60), and aortic aneurysm (46%, 28/60). Mortality rate was 7% (n = 4/60) and no statistically significant difference in survival was observed (p = .94). Reoperation occurred in 3 of 60 patients (5%). Four of 60 patients (7%) had endocarditis. At 5 years, the change in aortic root size was significantly different across operation types (p = .041), with significant dilation noted in the Ross cohort.Conclusions: Ross patients demonstrated greater neoaortic root enlargement at 5 years, although valve competence was generally preserved. Given the differences in age, underlying pathology, and surgical selection among the groups, these findings should be interpreted as descriptive remodeling patterns rather than evidence of the superiority of one operative strategy.

title: Endovascular Recanalization of Chronically Occluded Femoropopliteal Bypass Grafts: Feasibility and Early Clinical Outcomes.
authorString: Khalil E.

journal.title: Journal of endovascular therapy : an official journal of the International Society of Endovascular Specialists

abstractText:
Background

Chronic occlusion of femoropopliteal bypass grafts remains a complex clinical challenge, particularly in patients with peripheral arterial disease (PAD) who have limited surgical options and high operative risk. Although redo bypass surgery has traditionally been considered the standard treatment, it is associated with increased morbidity. Advances in endovascular techniques have expanded revascularization strategies; however, data on graft-directed endovascular recanalization remain limited.

Methods

This retrospective single-center study included 32 consecutive patients who underwent endovascular recanalization for chronically occluded femoropopliteal bypass grafts between January 2018 and December 2024. A stepwise graft-directed technique was applied, consisting of intraluminal guidewire crossing, sequential balloon predilatation, and stent implantation along the graft body and anastomotic segments when necessary. Technical success, procedural safety, and changes in ankle-brachial index (ABI) were evaluated.

Results

The mean age of the patients was 69.8 ± 9.6 years, and 68.8% were male. Technical success was achieved in 30 patients (93.8%). Median ABI improved significantly from 0.34 (interquartile range [IQR]: 0.22-0.48) before intervention to 0.71 (IQR: 0.58-0.84) after revascularization. Stent implantation was performed in all patients, with a median of 3 stents per case. Periprocedural complications occurred in 2 patients (6.3%) and were managed conservatively or by endovascular means. No procedure-related mortality or major limb loss was observed during hospitalization.

Conclusion

Stepwise endovascular recanalization of chronically occluded femoropopliteal bypass grafts is feasible and safe, providing favorable early technical and clinical outcomes. This graft-targeted approach may expand the endovascular treatment spectrum for PAD patients who are poor candidates for surgical reintervention and should be regarded as a procedural optimization strategy rather than a replacement for redo bypass surgery.Clinical ImpactGraft-directed endovascular recanalization of chronically occluded femoropopliteal bypass grafts demonstrated high technical success (93.8%), improved limb perfusion, and low periprocedural complication rates. This minimally invasive approach may represent a feasible revascularization option for selected high-risk patients with limited surgical alternatives. Further studies are warranted to establish its long-term durability.

title: Physiological Impact of Mechanical Ventilation on Remote Organs.
authorString: Epler KE, Kumar AJ, Pearce AK, Rolfsen M, Ji M, Ely EW, Bassi T, Orr JE, Kuebler W, Malhotra A, Hepokoski M.
abstractText: Mechanical ventilation is the most widely utilized life support modality worldwide and a necessary, lifesaving intervention in several critical illnesses. Decades of work have elucidated the deleterious impact that injurious ventilator settings have on the lung, which has translated to standard practices of ventilator support that have improved outcomes. Unfortunately, mechanical ventilation is still associated with morbidity and mortality rates that remain unacceptably high. Multiple organ failure is a major cause of death during mechanical ventilation, yet the impact of mechanical ventilation on remote organ systems, such as the brain, heart, and kidney, has received less attention. In this review, we summarize the physiological consequences of mechanical ventilation on extrapulmonary organs and highlight gaps in current knowledge that have precluded the development of novel treatment approaches.

title: Intended bilateral cardiac sympathetic denervation in children and young adults with severe adrenergically mediated ventricular arrhythmias: a single-centre experience.
authorString: Uysal S, Ali Hasan A, Ertuğrul İ, Karagöz T, Yılmaz M.
abstractText: Left cardiac sympathetic denervation is established for selected high-risk inherited arrhythmia syndromes, but evidence for an intended bilateral strategy in children and young adults remains limited. We evaluated the rationale, feasibility, safety, follow-up ascertainment, and outcomes of intended bilateral cardiac sympathetic denervation. Consecutive children and young adults undergoing intended bilateral cardiac sympathetic denervation between January 2015 and November 2025 were reviewed. The operation targeted the lower stellate component and upper thoracic sympathetic chain bilaterally, usually through single-port thoracoscopic access. Outcomes were obtained from specialist cardiology follow-up, electrocardiography, Holter monitoring, exercise testing when available, inpatient telemetry, device interrogation, and medication records. Thirty-seven patients were operated. Mean age was 12.4 years. Bilateral denervation was completed in 36 patients; 1 underwent left-sided denervation only owing to intraoperative haemodynamic instability. Single-port access was used in 30 patients. There were no intraoperative deaths, unplanned full thoracotomy conversions, intercostal injuries, reoperations for surgical complications, or denervation-related permanent pacing. Procedure-attributable morbidity comprised one mild Horner syndrome and one self-limited axillary wound complaint. Among 36 patients with post-discharge follow-up, 32 remained free from the primary malignant ventricular arrhythmic endpoint. Estimated malignant ventricular arrhythmia-free survival was 95.8 per cent at 1 year and 89.4 per cent at 3 years. Intended bilateral cardiac sympathetic denervation was feasible and had low procedure-attributable morbidity in selected young patients. It should be interpreted as an adjunct to multidisciplinary arrhythmia care, not as a replacement for medication, device surveillance, or follow-up.

title: Incidence, Risk Factors and Natural History of Atrial Arrhythmias in Patients With Systemic Right Ventricle.
authorString: Havangi S, Vijayakumar K, Ahmad R, Connolly HM, Egbe A, Burchill LJ, Nallathambi NK, McLeod CJ, Chiriac A, Nguyen D, Asirvatham SJ, Madhavan M.
abstractText:
Background

The incidence and risk factors for atrial arrhythmia (AA; atrial fibrillation and atrial flutter) in adults with systemic right ventricle (sRV), specifically congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries and dextro-transposition of the great arteries palliated with atrial switch procedures, are not well understood. This study aims to better define these risks.

Methods

Adults with sRV presenting to Mayo Clinic between 2000 and 2022 were identified. Their clinical characteristics, electrocardiographic, and echocardiographic parameters at the time of first presentation were recorded. The incidence of sustained AA (>30 seconds) during follow-up was documented. Cox regression analysis was used to identify associations of incident atrial fibrillation/atrial flutter and mortality during follow-up.

Results

Among 447 patients with sRV (median age, 33.1 [24.6-42.8], 55.9% male, 247 cm3-TGA; 200 dextro-transposition of the great arteries postatrial switch), AA was present at first visit in 113 (25.3%). Out of the remaining 334 patients, new-onset AA occurred in 125 (37.4%) patients during a median follow-up of 11.1 years (interquartile range, 3.6-19.3). Isolated atrial fibrillation was observed in 89 (37.4%), isolated atrial flutter in 76 (31.9%), and both atrial fibrillation and atrial flutter in 73 (30.7%) patients. In multivariable analysis, the risk factors for incident AA included age (hazard ratio, 1.04 [1.03-1.06]; P<0.001), d-TGA (hazard ratio, 1.96 [1.00-3.85]; P=0.05), and QRS duration (hazard ratio, 1.01 [1.00-1.02]; P=0.02). AA was associated with hospitalization for heart failure in 19% of patients. Among those treated with anti-arrhythmic drugs and ablation, recurrence occurred in over 50% of patients. AA was not an independent predictor of mortality.

Conclusions

AA occurred in more than half of this cohort with sRV, with risk increasing significantly after the third decade of life. Advancing age, dextro-transposition of the great arteries, and prolonged QRS duration were associated with increased risk of AA. Close monitoring for AA and early interventions are warranted in all adults with sRV.

title: Longitudinal NT-proBNP Target Attainment and Clinical Outcomes in Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction: A Landmark Analysis of the GUIDE-IT Trial.
authorString: Nyirenda N, Stafford PL, Bolaji O, Balogun T, Udoh K, He Z, Bandaru J, Vidic A, Phiri J, Kabwe JC, Forde AT, Kwon Y, Chihota B, Breathett K, Mehta N, Lin E, Bilchick KC, Addison D, Mazimba S.
abstractText: Serial N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) measurements are prognostic in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), but the prognostic significance of longitudinal target attainment remains uncertain. We performed a secondary 180-day landmark analysis of the GUIDE-IT trial among participants with at least two NT-proBNP measurements through day 180 and follow-up beyond the landmark. The analytic cohort was restricted to participants who remained event-free according to the broad raw-record endpoint and under observation at the 180-day landmark. The exposure was the proportion of pre-landmark visits with NT-proBNP ≤1000 pg/mL, modeled per 10% increase and as ≥50% versus <50% attainment. The outcome was time to first recorded all-cause hospitalization or death. Cox models adjusted for age, sex, treatment arm, log2-transformed baseline NT-proBNP, New York Heart Association class, atrial fibrillation, and kidney disease. Among 324 participants, 155 experienced hospitalization or death; complete-case models included 319 participants and 154 events. Each 10% increase in target attainment was associated with lower risk (hazard ratio [HR] 0.89, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.84-0.96; P=0.001), as was ≥50% versus <50% attainment (HR 0.44, 95% CI 0.27-0.71; P<0.001). Target attainment improved model fit beyond clinical characteristics and baseline NT-proBNP (likelihood-ratio P<0.001), but not after inclusion of the most recent pre-landmark NT-proBNP measurement (HR 0.97 per 10% increase, 95% CI 0.90-1.06; P=0.51). Greater longitudinal target attainment was associated with lower subsequent risk, although its prognostic information substantially overlapped with the most recent NT-proBNP measurement.

title: Atrial fibrillation is associated with higher stroke risk but not with higher mortality in patients with heart failure: A nationwide analysis.
authorString: Sundström J, Gustafsson S, Lindholm D.
abstractText:
Background

While atrial fibrillation/flutter (AF) has been associated with increased risk of mortality in patients with heart failure (HF), it is unknown whether AF confers an increased risk on its own, i.e., not mediated through the increased risk of stroke. We aimed to investigate the age- and sex-specific prognostic impact of AF and stroke (alone and in combination) in patients with HF by using multistate modeling to account for events occurring during follow-up. Secondary aims were to investigate temporal trends in transition rates and in anticoagulant use in patients with AF and HF.

Methods

This was a Swedish nationwide cohort study that included adult patients with HF diagnosed between 2004 and 2025. We used multistate modeling to account for occurrences of AF and stroke both at baseline and during follow-up. With Poisson regression in generalized additive models, we assessed age- and sex-specific transition rates between the different disease states, and in a separate model including time period, we assessed temporal trends in transition rates. Finally, as oral anticoagulants influence stroke risk in patients with atrial fibrillation, we estimated temporal, sex-specific trends in their use.

Findings

We identified 704,852 patients (47% women) with HF, who were followed for a total of 2.9 million person-years. AF was associated with an increased risk of stroke but did not associate with an increased risk of death on its own. In the early study period, women, compared with men, were less likely to receive oral anticoagulants, but their use increased over time, more in women than in men. During the same period, there was a decline in stroke risk, with a greater absolute improvement in women than in men.

Conclusions

In this study of patients with HF, AF was not associated with an elevated direct risk of mortality. Over time, the risk of stroke decreased in patients with HF and AF, temporally coinciding with a marked uptake of direct-acting oral anticoagulant (DOAC) use, with the largest improvement seen among women.

Funding

This study was supported by unrestricted funding from Anders Wiklöf.

title: Beyond health behaviours: Decomposing cause-specific associations between neighbourhood deprivation and mortality in Busan, South Korea.
authorString: Ko YG, Lee JH.
abstractText: Health behaviours are widely thought to explain why residents of deprived neighbourhoods die earlier, but it is unclear whether their contribution is similar across causes of death. We analysed 203 small administrative areas (eup/myeon/dong) in Busan, South Korea, using an ecological cross-sectional design. Deprivation was measured with 11 census indicators. Twenty-two indicators from the Korea Community Health Survey were grouped into three domains: core health behaviours (such as smoking, high-risk drinking and walking), health status (such as diagnosed hypertension or diabetes, obesity and depressive symptoms), and healthcare use and awareness. Regression-based decomposition with cluster-bootstrap confidence intervals estimated how much of the association between deprivation and age-standardised mortality in 2020-2024 each domain statistically accounted for, for all-cause and six cause-specific outcomes. Deprivation was associated with higher mortality from every cause. Core health behaviours accounted for 0-24% of these associations, and their share did not differ significantly between causes. Health status accounted for 49.6% (95% CI 19.1 to 99.5) of the association with cerebrovascular mortality, and after correction for multiple comparisons significantly more than for external causes (borderline for suicide). This share remained above zero with population weighting, district fixed effects, adjustment for density and urban-rural status, and spatial-error models, but not consistently in earlier overlapping periods. Cause-specific differences in the decomposition were more evident for area-level health status than for core health behaviours. Efforts to reduce inequalities in cerebrovascular mortality may benefit from attention to cardiometabolic disease burden and its management in deprived neighbourhoods, alongside behavioural and structural measures.

title: The JRS guideline for the management of drug-induced lung disease.
authorString: Ushiki A, Bando M, Miyazaki Y, Abe S, Ishii H, Hattori N, Kusumoto M, Chiba H, Terasaki Y, Ichikado K, Tomioka H, Suda T, Tsushima K, Takada T, Yokoyama A, Nagaoka T, Tasaka S, Hanaoka M, Japanese Respiratory Society Committee for the formulation of the Management of drug-induced lung disease [3rd Edition].
abstractText: This consensus statement from the Japanese Respiratory Society summarizes updated recommendations for the diagnosis and treatment of drug-induced lung injury (DLI). DLI includes respiratory disorders caused by prescription drugs, over-the-counter medicines, herbal agents, and supplements. Clinical manifestations range widely from mild and reversible conditions to severe and life-threatening disease. Among these, diffuse alveolar damage (DAD) is particularly important because it is associated with severe respiratory failure, poor treatment response, fibrosis, and high mortality. An accurate diagnosis requires careful exclusion of other causes, especially respiratory infections, heart failure, and progression of the underlying disease. Chest computed tomography imaging has a central role in diagnosis and classification, particularly for distinguishing DAD from non-DAD patterns such as organizing pneumonia, hypersensitivity pneumonitis, and nonspecific interstitial pneumonia. Biomarkers including Krebs von den Lungen-6, surfactant protein-A, and surfactant protein-D may assist in disease evaluation and monitoring. Major causative agents include anticancer drugs, immune checkpoint inhibitors, molecular target drugs, antimicrobial agents, and antirheumatic drugs. Risk factors include older age, pre-existing interstitial lung disease, smoking history, impaired respiratory function, and combination chemotherapy. The cornerstone of management is prompt discontinuation of the suspected drug, followed by glucocorticoid therapy according to disease severity and appropriate respiratory support. Early recognition, multidisciplinary evaluation, and close monitoring are essential for improving patient outcomes.

title: Longitudinal optic nerve sheath diameter trajectories in neurocritical care patients after mechanical thrombectomy or decompressive craniectomy: A descriptive bedside ultrasound study.
authorString: Tan S, Yan J, Jiang H, Deng L, Song Y.
abstractText:
Background

Longitudinal optic nerve sheath diameter (ONSD) measurements after neurosurgical procedures remain incompletely characterized. We aimed to describe postoperative ONSD trajectories in selected disease-surgery cohorts.

Methods

This single-center prospective observational study included 80 patients with clinically and radiologically defined suspected intracranial hypertension: 40 undergoing mechanical thrombectomy (MT) for anterior-circulation ischemic stroke and 40 undergoing decompressive craniectomy (DC) for intracerebral hemorrhage or traumatic brain injury. Forty healthy volunteers provided a local reference. Bedside ONSD was measured with a standardized protocol on postoperative days 0-9 and summarized using observed daily means and linear mixed-effects spline models.

Results

Of 800 planned patient measurements, 733 were available. Healthy volunteers had a mean ONSD of 4.11 ± 0.54 mm. In the MT group, mean ONSD increased from 5.55 ± 0.62 mm on day 0 to an observed maximum of 5.91 ± 0.77 mm on day 5, then declined. In the DC group, daily means ranged from 5.18 to 5.33 mm.

Conclusions

In these selected cohorts, mean ONSD reached its observed maximum on postoperative day 5 after MT and varied within a narrow range after DC. Whether these changes exceeded measurement variability remains uncertain. Further validation is needed before using these observations to infer intracranial pressure changes or guide treatment.

title: Prognostic Impact of Checkpoint Inhibitor Pneumonitis: Results from a Multicenter Prospective Observational Study (CS-Lung004).
authorString: Yamaguchi K, Yano J, Kanaji N, Hirakawa T, Matsumoto N, Miyazaki K, Okimoto T, Ando C, Higo H, Yanai M, Kurose K, Nagasaki Y, Watanabe M, Oyama K, Toyoda Y, Taguchi Y, Tada S, Fujita S, Iwamoto H, Hattori N.
abstractText:
Introduction

Checkpoint inhibitor pneumonitis (CIP) is a potentially life-threatening adverse event caused by anti-programmed death-1 (PD-1) and programmed death ligand-1 (PD-L1) antibodies. However, paradoxical findings have been reported regarding the association between overall survival (OS) and CIP. This study aimed to prospectively evaluate the relationship between the 2-year OS and CIP in patients receiving first-line treatment, including anti-PD-1/PD-L1 antibody therapy, using 3-month and 1-year landmark analyses.

Methods

A multicenter prospective observational study was conducted between December 2021 and November 2023 to evaluate the prognostic impact of CIP, based on timing and severity, in patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).

Results

Although no significant difference in OS was observed between patients with and without CIP developed within 2 years or 1 year, the 3-month landmark analysis showed that patients who developed CIP within 3 months had significantly shorter OS than those who did not (median OS from the 3-months landmark: 11.1 months with CIP versus not reached without CIP; log-rank p = 0.011). In multivariate Cox regression analyses, using patients without CIP as the reference group, CIP within 3 months was significantly associated with impaired overall survival (any-grade CIP: hazard ratio [HR] = 2.22, 95% confidence interval [CI]=1.21-4.09; Grade 3-5 CIP: HR=3.37, 95% CI=1.57-7.23).

Conclusion

This was the first prospective study to demonstrate the prognostic value of CIP. CIP within 3 months after the initiation of first-line treatment, including anti-PD-1/PD-L1 antibody, especially Grade 3-5 CIP, was associated with shorter OS in patients with NSCLC.
