title: Intracranial aneurysm risk and cerebrovascular outcomes in thoracic versus abdominal aortic aneurysms: a national analysis of 114,805 hospitalizations.
authorString: Ghaith AK, Boktor B, Alasadi Y, Ghaith M, Radwan H, Salem MM, Yang L, Amatya B, Hamouda AM, Arar A, Selvakumar K, De Llano J, Fox WC, Tawk R.
abstractText:
Background

Aneurysmal disease is increasingly recognized as a systemic vasculopathy, yet large-scale comparisons between thoracic (TAA) and abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAA) regarding intracranial aneurysm (ICa) burden and cerebrovascular outcomes remain limited. This study leverages a nationally representative database to compare the frequency of coded coexisting ICa, cerebrovascular events, and in-hospital outcomes between TAA and AAA, and to identify factors associated with coexisting ICa.

Methods

A retrospective cohort study using the National Inpatient Sample (2000-2020) identified adult hospitalizations with TAA or AAA that included an aortic aneurysm repair; dissections and thoracoabdominal or unspecified-site aneurysms were excluded. Propensity score matching (1:1, nearest-neighbor, caliper 0.2 SD) adjusted for demographic and clinical differences, with covariate balance assessed by standardized mean differences. Primary outcomes included administratively coded coexisting ICa and cerebrovascular events (ischemic stroke, hemorrhagic stroke, coded subarachnoid hemorrhage [SAH]). Secondary outcomes included mortality, length of stay, charges, and discharge disposition. Multivariable logistic regression and exploratory random forest machine learning examined factors associated with coded ICa. Counts are unweighted NIS discharge records.

Results

Among 114,805 hospitalizations (2.3% TAA, 97.7% AAA), coded coexisting ICa was present in 168 (0.15%); its frequency was higher in TAA than in AAA before matching (1.0% vs. 0.1%, p < 0.001) but not after matching (1.0% vs. 0.7%; OR 1.45, 95% CI 0.79-2.65; p = 0.23). The propensity-matched analysis (n = 5,330) demonstrated higher rates of ischemic stroke (5.5% vs. 3.9%, p = 0.007), hemorrhagic stroke (0.5% vs. ≤0.4%, p = 0.007), and coded SAH (0.8% vs. ≤0.4%, p = 0.003) in TAA; E-values indicated that these hemorrhagic associations were robust to residual confounding, whereas ischemic stroke and mortality differences were sensitive to residual imbalance in atrial fibrillation and repair modality. In multivariable analysis, TAA was independently associated with coded coexisting ICa (aOR 1.17, 95% CI 1.07-1.27). Female sex showed the strongest association (aOR 2.56), followed by smoking, hypertension, and dyslipidemia. TAA had higher mortality (4.9% vs. 3.0%), longer stays (9.83 vs. 6.21 days), greater non-home discharge (53.7% vs. 28.3%), and higher charges (all p < 0.001). Among all hospitalizations with an unruptured aortic or intracranial aneurysm diagnosis, the TAA share increased from approximately 11% to 35% between 2003 and 2020. Machine learning identified age as the most influential variable, with key interactions involving age × female sex and age × vascular comorbidities.

Conclusions

TAA is associated with higher coded cerebrovascular event rates, worse in-hospital outcomes, and greater healthcare utilization than AAA. Because ICa in administrative data are identified through clinical recognition rather than systematic screening, these data should not be construed to mean that ICa are more prevalent among patients with TAA, although cerebrovascular events appear more frequent and more morbid in this population. Prospective imaging-based studies are needed before targeted intracranial screening can be recommended, particularly for younger women with TAA and vascular comorbidities.

title: Serum Renin As a Prognostic Biomarker in Children With Sepsis-Associated Acute Kidney Injury.
authorString: Clover-Brown I, Standage SW, Ceschia G, Pode-Shakked N, Atreya MR, Lautz AJ, Zingarelli B, Kaplan J, Cvijanovich NZ, Fitzgerald JC, Bigham MT, Jain PN, Schwarz AJ, Lutfi R, Thomas NJ, Baines T, Haileselassie B, Weiss SL, Fuhrman DY, Goldstein SL, Stanski NL, Genomics of Septic Shock Investigators.

journal.title: Pediatric critical care medicine : a journal of the Society of Critical Care Medicine and the World Federation of Pediatric Intensive and Critical Care Societies

abstractText: Renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) derangement contributes to acute kidney injury (AKI) and is associated with poor outcomes in critical illness. Serum renin, a clinically available biomarker of RAAS derangement, is associated with poor outcomes in critically ill adults and children. Renin has not been evaluated in children with sepsis-associated AKI (SA-AKI), either alone or in combination with other prognostic enrichment tools, including the recently derived pediatric sepsis-associated AKI (pSAKI) subphenotypes. Secondary analysis of a multicenter, prospective, observational study of pediatric septic shock. Ten U.S. PICUs from January 2002 to February 2025. Patients 0-18 years old with early SA-AKI (serum creatinine-based Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes stage 1-3 on days 1-2 of admission) with residual day 1 serum available for renin measurement. None. Seven hundred eight patients were examined by renin tertiles. The highest renin tertile cohort (T3, > 247 pg/mL) had one fewer severe AKI-free day (4 [0-6] vs. 5 [1-7] T2 vs. 5 [2-7] T1; p < 0.001), higher day 7 severe AKI rates (47% vs. 32% vs. 27%; p < 0.001), fewer PICU-free days, and higher 28-day mortality rates. In multivariate analysis incorporating markers of illness severity, including age, T3 was independently associated with fewer severe AKI-free days (β = -0.5; se = 0.2; p = 0.01), fewer PICU-free days, and higher adjusted odds of day 7 severe AKI and 28-day mortality. Patients were assigned to either the pSAKI-1 or pSAKI-2 subphenotype to assess for additional enrichment. T3 patients had uniformly worse outcomes among the less severe pSAKI-1 subphenotype but not among pSAKI-2 patients. Worsening RAAS derangement, as evidenced by increasing renin concentrations, is associated with worse outcomes in children with SA-AKI. Serum renin may provide clinically useful prognostic enrichment in this population, both alone and in combination with the pSAKI subphenotypes.

title: Bioresorbable permanent-magnet beacons for tracking internal biomechanics during free movement
authorString: Nie Z, Lin X, Wan J, Xu J, Wu K, Wang Y, Zhang C, Yang C, Zhong R, Sun N, Man W, Huang Y, Zhang S, Wu D, Wang Y, Wang Y, Hong M, Sun Y, Hu H, Koo J, Han M.
abstractText: Perioperative complications represent a global health burden that can be reduced through timely interventions guided by continuous physiological monitoring. Bioresorbable sensors excel through natural degradation without subsequent surgical extraction, but motion artefacts disrupt their accurate measurement. We synthesize bioresorbable permanent-magnet nanocomposites from aligned iron nanowires as implantable beacons. These beacons intrinsically generate magnetic fields responsive to biomechanical changes, thereby enabling wireless and chipless monitoring. An artificial-intelligence-enhanced wearable magnetic-field camera decodes these spatial maps into calibrated values that tolerate vigorous movement. The system achieves a displacement-equivalent mean absolute error of 2.74 μm. Experiments in rat models demonstrate intracranial pressure tracking with clinical-grade accuracy during vigorous activities, and longitudinal monitoring of intracranial hypertension associated with ischaemic stroke during natural behaviours.

title: Association between Hemoglobin Levels and Heart Failure following Acute Myocardial Infarction: A Retrospective Study
authorString: Xie Y, Hu C, Wang N, Xiang H, Wu Y, Liu S.
abstractText: Background and Aims: Low hemoglobin (Hb) concentrations and anemia are frequently encountered among individuals with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and have been tied to unfavorable prognoses. We aimed to evaluate the association between admission Hb levels and anemia status and the risk of in-hospital heart failure after acute myocardial infarction (post-MI HF) in patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) undergoing emergency percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Methods A total of 506 STEMI patients who received emergency PCI were enrolled in this single-center, retrospective investigation. Post-MI HF was diagnosed in accordance with guideline-recommended clinical and objective criteria. The analytical strategy comprised multivariable logistic regression, restricted cubic spline (RCS) modeling, subgroup and interaction testing, and E-value sensitivity analysis. Results During hospitalization, 47 patients (9.3%) developed post-MI HF. In the fully adjusted model, each 1 g/L increase in Hb was associated with 2.1% lower odds of post-MI HF [odds ratio (OR) 0.979, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.960–0.998, P = 0.029]. Anemia was present in 113 patients (22.3%); anemic patients had a higher incidence of post-MI HF (18.6% vs. 6.6%) and significantly higher odds of post-MI HF (adjusted OR 3.15, 95% CI 1.56–6.39, P = 0.001). RCS analysis showed an approximately linear inverse association between Hb and post-MI HF risk (P for overall = 0.041; P for nonlinearity = 0.236). Diabetes mellitus and smoking modified the association (P for interaction = 0.022 and 0.001, respectively). The E-value was 5.75 (lower limit 2.49). Conclusion Among STEMI patients managed with emergency PCI, a lower Hb concentration at admission and the presence of anemia were each independently linked to a heightened likelihood of post-MI HF. Admission Hb may therefore serve as a convenient marker for early risk stratification of post-MI HF.

title: Association Between Grip Strength-to-Body Weight Ratio and Cardiometabolic Multimorbidity: A Cross-Sectional Study from CHARLS
authorString: Li A, Bai X, Han X, Chen S.
abstractText: Background Cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM), defined as the coexistence of two or more cardiometabolic diseases, represents a growing public health challenge among aging populations. Grip strength relative to body weight may serve as a more equitable indicator of muscular fitness across different body sizes. Grip strength-to-body weight ratio (GWR) may be a simple marker for assessing cardiometabolic risk.This study aimed to investigate the association between GWR and CMM in middle-aged and older Chinese adults. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional analysis using data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS), including 18,184 participants aged 45 years and older. GWR was calculated as the ratio of grip strength (kg) to body weight (kg). To facilitate interpretation, we multiplied the original GWR by 10 to create GWR10. Thus, each unit increase in GWR10 corresponds to a 0.1-unit increase in the original GWR ratio. CMM was defined as the presence of two or more conditions among hypertension, diabetes, heart disease, stroke, and dyslipidemia. Multivariable logistic regression models were constructed to examine the association between GWR and CMM. Results The prevalence of CMM was 20.3% (n = 3,700). Higher GWR was markedly associated with lower odds of CMM (adjusted OR = 0.79, 95% CI: 0.76–0.81, P < 0.001) per unit increase. This finding is notable. Compared with the lowest quartile (Q1), the highest quartile (Q4) showed a 72% reduction in CMM odds (adjusted OR = 0.28, 95% CI: 0.24–0.33, P < 0.001). A significant age-stratified interaction was observed (P for interaction = 0.001), with the strongest inverse association in the 55–64 age group (OR = 0.74, 95% CI: 0.71–0.78). A nonlinear relationship was observed between GWR and CMM (P for nonlinearity < 0.001), with a breakpoint at GWR10 = 3.459 (corresponding to original GWR = 0.3459). Subgroup analyses showed consistent associations across sex, education, marital status, rural/urban residence, smoking, drinking, and physical activity groups (all P for interaction > 0.05). Conclusions Higher GWR was significantly associated with lower odds of CMM in a nonlinear manner and independently associated with reduced odds of CMM in middle-aged and older Chinese adults, with a significant age-modifying inverse association. GWR may serve as a practical clinical indicator for identifying individuals at risk for cardiometabolic multimorbidity.

title: sST2 and CA125 identify distinct biological phenotypes and predict one-year mortality in very old patients hospitalised for decompensated HFpEF
authorString: Cuenda BDH, Croset F, Pisón EP, Nieva AP, Campos J, Melero MG, Pérez C, Vergara M, Castro APC, Rodríguez JEO, Pomana B, Ledesma NB, Fernández C, Fabregate M, Román MM, Sánchez O, Llàcer P, Manzano L.
abstractText: Background: Risk stratification remains challenging in very old patients hospitalised for decompensated heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF). Soluble suppression of tumorigenicity 2 (sST2) and carbohydrate antigen 125 (CA125) reflect complementary pathophysiological domains related to fibro-inflammatory stress and systemic congestion. We evaluated whether their combined assessment identifies distinct prognostic phenotypes. Methods Prospective observational cohort of 175 consecutive patients aged ≥ 80 years admitted for decompensated HFpEF. Four phenotypes were defined by sST2 (cut-off 35 ng/mL) and CA125 (cut-off 35 U/mL): both low, sST2 high only, CA125 high only, and both high. Primary endpoint was one-year all-cause mortality. Results Among 164 patients with complete biomarker data, one-year mortality ranged from 18% in the dual-low phenotype to 43% in the dual-high phenotype, with significant differences across phenotypes (log-rank p = 0.013). After multivariable adjustment, the both-high phenotype was associated with higher mortality compared with the both-low phenotype (HR 2.43, 95% CI 1.01–5.85; p = 0.048). Frailty and lower systolic blood pressure were also independent predictors, whereas BNP was not. When modelled continuously, sST2 was independently associated with mortality (HR 1.51 per SD, 95% CI 1.12–2.05; p = 0.007), with no evidence of non-linearity. Neither rehospitalisation nor the composite endpoint differed significantly across phenotypes. Conclusions Combined assessment of sST2 and CA125 identified distinct prognostic phenotypes in very old patients hospitalised for decompensated HFpEF. Concurrent elevation of both biomarkers was associated with higher one-year mortality, supporting further evaluation of multidimensional biomarker phenotyping in this understudied population.

title: Postoperative complications in older patients with hip fracture: risk profiles and short-term outcomes from the GIOG 2.0
authorString: Cavalli A, De Vincentis A, Pedone C, Ferrara MC, Trevisan C, Tassistro E, Valsecchi MG, Mazzola P, Pizzonia M, Cena P, Mussi C, Sergi G, Ungar A, Volpato S, Papalia R, Incalzi RA, Bellelli G.
abstractText: Purpose To identify pre- and perioperative risk factors for postoperative complications and the impact of such complications on length of stay (LOS) and in-hospital mortality in older hip fracture (HF) patients. Methods the Italian GIOG 2.0, a multicenter, prospective, observational study including patients aged 65 years or more, with proximal HF and free from metastatic cancer, admitted in 14 Italian orthogeriatric wards. Associations of postoperative complications with patient and procedure-related factors and hospital short term outcomes were examined using uni- and multivariable regression analyses. Results A total of 1,637 patients were included; 76% were female, with a mean age of 83.6 years. Overall, 42% of patients experienced at least one complication, including postoperative delirium (POD) (28%), cardiac events (27%), pneumonia (19%), and urinary tract infection (UTI) (17%). Independent correlates of POD included age, dementia, psychoactive drug use, and ASA score > II. Pneumonia was independently associated with age, ADL disability, preoperative delirium, surgical delay, and urinary catheter (UC) use, and negatively with general anesthesia. Cardiac complications were associated with age, heart failure, COPD, polypharmacy, and UC use. UTI was strongly associated with UC use, with variability across enrolling centers (p < 0.001). All complications were associated with increased LOS, whereas only pneumonia independently increased in-hospital mortality (Odds Ratio 5.06, 95% CI 1.68–15.30, p = 0.003). Conclusions Postoperative complications in orthogeriatric patients are associated with adverse short-term outcomes. Potentially modifiable perioperative factors—particularly UC use, surgical delay, psychoactive medication exposure, anesthesia type, and polypharmacy—may represent targets for preventive strategies in older HF patients.

title: FGF23 and Cardiac Remodeling in Chronic Kidney Disease: A Rapid Review and Exploratory Quantitative Synthesis.
authorString: Chakola JJ, Nithianantham SR, Rath A, Rajendren K, Rangarajan J, Sekar M, Ramanathan G.
abstractText: Left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH), elevated left ventricular mass index (LVMI), diastolic dysfunction, heart failure, and cardiovascular mortality are common in chronic kidney disease (CKD). Fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23) rises early in CKD and is linked to cardiac remodeling, but consistency across studies is unclear. We conducted a rapid review of FGF23 and cardiac outcomes in CKD, incorporating a reanalyzed unpublished single-center cohort, and pooled effect estimates where at least 2 studies reported comparable metrics. A structured web-based search (August 2026) identified 11 candidate studies on FGF23 and cardiac outcomes in CKD; 9 met eligibility, including 1 unpublished investigator-held cohort (n = 80) reanalyzed for this review. Pooling (inverse variance) was performed only where at least 2 studies reported comparable metrics; all pooled estimates are exploratory, below the prespecified 3-study minimum. For FGF23 and LVH, using a derived LVH variable from the present cohort, a pooled log-FGF23 odds ratio (OR) across 2 adult-CKD studies (n = 242) was 1.33 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.92-1.93), I2 = 78%; a pediatric study (OR 2.53, n = 587) was consistent in direction but unpooled. For LVMI, correlations were not pooled; a Chronic Renal Insufficiency Cohort cohort showed higher LVMI only in the top quartile. For heart failure/cardiovascular mortality, a pooled hazard ratio across 2 studies (n = 374) was 2.37 (95% CI 1.47-3.84), I2 = 0%, with LVMI mediating only 7-22% in Chronic Renal Insufficiency Cohort. FGF23 was not significantly associated with diastolic dysfunction after adjustment (OR 1.51/standard deviation, 95% CI 0.92-2.47). The available evidence, though sparse and heterogeneous, is directionally consistent with a positive FGF23-cardiac remodeling association in CKD. Certainty is very low throughout; a full multi-database search is needed before a definitive conclusion.

title: Association between atherosclerotic lower extremity peripheral artery disease and physical activity on carotid intraplaque haemorrhage.
authorString: Mura M, Rivoire E, Josset L, Jazzar G, Della-Schiava N, Chirico EN, Millon A, Pialoux V, Long A, Thomas A.
abstractText:
Aim

Lower extremity peripheral arterial disease (LE-PAD) combined with carotid atherosclerotic plaques increases carotid plaque instability and the risk of ischemic events. The benefits of regular physical activity (PA) on morbidity, mortality, and long-term quality of life in LE-PAD patients were previously demonstrated. The aim is to explore the association of PA levels and intercurrent LE-PAD on carotid plaque instability markers.

Methods

Patients with asymptomatic carotid stenosis>50% were divided into two groups: LE-PAD (+) and LE-PAD (-). PA levels were assessed using validated questionnaires, allowing further stratification into subgroups. Carotid plaque instability, particularly intraplaque haemorrhage (IPH), was assessed by magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).

Results

Fifty-two patients were included (30 LE-PAD (+), 22 LE-PAD (-)). Among physically inactive patients, LE-PAD (-) patients presented a lower IPH score (estimate: -0.75, 95% CI: -1.33; -0.16, P=0.014). These differences were not observed in physically active ones. Moreover, in LE-PAD patients, physically active patients had a lower score of IPH than the less active ones (estimate: -0.54, 95% CI: -1.08; -0.01, P=0.048).

Conclusion

Patients with carotid atherosclerosis and LE-PAD that are inactive have higher intraplaque haemorrhage. Regular physical activity could therefore help mitigate carotid plaque instability in these patients.

title: Ultrasound Thermal Strain Imaging for Atherosclerosis Plaque Characterization: Image Acquisition, Processing, and In Vivo Results in a Porcine Model.
authorString: Sheng Z, Wei R, Chen M, Kohyama K, Wielgat MB, Kinoshita S, Richards TD, Cormack JM, Phillippi JA, Shanmuganayagam D, Tzeng E, Geng X, Jiang X, Kim K.
abstractText: The accumulation of lipids in atherosclerosis plaque (AP) is one of the key features associated with plaque rupture, which can lead to heart attack and stroke. To predict rupture-pone cases, ultrasound thermal strain imaging (US-TSI) can identify lipids based on the contrast of the echo shift gradient between water-bearing tissue and lipids induced by different speed-of-sound (SoS) changes when temperature increases. However, US-TSI faces technical challenges in vivo: 1) heating a sufficiently large tissue volume within the imaging field-of-view (FOV) safely, uniformly, and effectively; 2) thermal-induced echo shifts (< 10 μm) are often masked by physiological motions greater than 50 μm. This study aimed to overcome these obstacles. We developed a new US-TSI transducer design along with image acquisition and processing techniques. Specifically, a co-registered multi-beam approach was used to enlarge the diagnostic FOV and a wavelet-based motion analysis was conducted to reconstruct extremely small SoS change-induced echo shifts in vivo. Experiments were conducted on a tissue-mimicking phantom, a human carotid endarterectomy (CEA) sample, and in the femoral artery of a hypercholesterolemic pig. Experimental US-TSI results were compared to the histology for lipid staining. Experiments with the tissue-mimicking phantom and CEA sample demonstrated the capability of large-FOV US-TSI. Successful in vivo US-TSI lipid detection was achieved, for the first time, in a large animal AP model. This work introduces new methods to enable in vivo US-TSI for AP lipid detection, paving the way for further validation in pre-clinical large animal studies and translational human subject studies on carotid artery.

title: Atherogenic Index of plasma as feasible biomarker (Index) for plaque instability: An observational cross-sectional study in tertiary care hospital in North India
authorString: Bajpai A, Kamlesh R, Kumar B, Mirza AA, Sharma N.
abstractText: Background Cardiovascular Diseases are the root cause of fatality globally which is responsible for vast number of deaths. Atherosclerosis has a progressive core from stable to unstable plaque which leads to the morbidity and mortality. There are various biomarkers to identify this unstable plaque but still search for biomarker is in this field required to identify the simple and economical biomarker so we have done study on Atherogenic Index of plasma (AIP) as biomarker of plaque instablility. Methods We conducted study on total 150 coronary artery disease (CAD) patients 75 of each group (stable and unstable atherogenic plaque). Biochemical parameters analyse by using Fully automated clinical chemistry analyzer (Backman Coulter). AIP calculated by using formula log(TG/HDL). The receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was used to find the sensitivity, specificity, and area under the curve (AUC). Results A cutoff point for AIP in distinguishing between stable and unstable atherogenic plaques was established using a ROC curve, which shows 93% sensitivity and 0.668 AUC. Conclusion Based on this study, AIP is an independent biomarker for plaque instability. It is cost effective and can done routinely.

title: Neurological manifestations in pediatric COVID-19: a comparative single-center study.
authorString: Ibrahim H, Mansour M, Ahmed AR, Rushdy M, ElGammal MM, Zaitoun R.
abstractText:
Objective

To compare clinical characteristics, investigations, management, and outcomes of hospitalized children with SARS-CoV-2 infection with and without neurological involvement, and to determine whether neurological disease reflects systemic severity or a distinct clinical pattern.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective observational study of children aged 1 month-16 years with laboratory-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection admitted to a tertiary pediatric center between June 2022 and June 2023. Patients were divided into those with neurological manifestations (ND group, n = 24) and those without neurological involvement (non-ND group, n = 23). Demographic features, clinical presentation, laboratory and neuroimaging findings, treatment, and outcomes were compared.

Results

Children with neurological involvement were significantly older (median 5.75 vs. 3.00 years, p = 0.022) and less likely to present with fever or systemic inflammatory features. They demonstrated lower inflammatory markers and significantly less cardiac involvement, including dilated cardiomyopathy. Common neurological presentations included encephalopathy (50%), headache (45.8%), and seizures (20.8%). 37% met MIS-C criteria. Neuroimaging revealed lacunar infarctions, demyelinating white matter lesions, longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis, and cauda equina nerve root enhancement. Despite similar mortality rates, children with neurological involvement had a significantly higher rate of incomplete recovery, with more than a quarter experiencing persistent neurological sequelae (29.2% vs. 4.3%, p = 0.048).

Conclusion

Neurological manifestations of pediatric COVID-19 represent a clinically distinct pattern characterized by limited systemic inflammation but an increased risk of persistent neurological sequelae. Early neurological evaluation, appropriate neuroimaging, and structured long-term follow-up are warranted even in the absence of severe systemic illness.

title: miRNA Regulation of the FGF23-Klotho Pathway Mitigates Adverse Cardiac Remodeling During Nocturnal Hemodialysis.
authorString: Alberga CA, Hauck L, Grothe D, Premsingh BP, Chan CT, Billia F.

journal.title: Clinical journal of the American Society of Nephrology : CJASN

abstractText:
Background

Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of morbidity and mortality in patients with ESKD. Dysregulation of the fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23)/Klotho axis has been implicated in uremic cardiomyopathy, however the mechanism linking dialysis intensity to the regulation of this pathway remains poorly defined.

Methods

We analyzed serum samples from ESKD patients transitioning from conventional to nocturnal hemodialysis (NHD). Left ventricular mass (LVM) was measured by echocardiography before and after transition. Patients were stratified as LVM regressors [ ≥ 10% decrease in LVM; n = 6] or LVM progressors [ ≥ 10% increase in LVM; n = 7]. Circulating microRNAs (miRs) and serum FGF23 and alpha Klotho were quantified. Mechanistic relevance was tested in an angiotensin-II model of cardiac hypertrophy using FGF23 suppression via an antisense oligonucleotide gapmer, or antagomirs targeting miR-200c-3p.

Results

Among 13 patients transitioning to NHD, LVM regressors required fewer antihypertensive medications than at baseline (P<0.001) with improved metabolic parameters (urea 12.9 vs. 16.6 mmol/L, P<0.01) and higher hemoglobin (109 vs. 95 g/L, P<0.01). We identified six differentially expressed miRs (let-7a/g/i, miR-200c, miR-1 and miR-30c) that targeted the FGF23/Klotho signaling axis. LVM regressors also demonstrated significantly lower circulating FGF23 levels than LVM progressors [60 (28, 160) vs 668 (73, 1734) pg/mL, P<0.05]. In the angiotensin-II murine model of cardiac hypertrophy, FGF23 gapmer treatment or miR-200c-3p inhibition reduced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy and attenuated interstitial fibrosis while restoring FGF23/Klotho signaling through the suppression of extracellular signal-regulated kinase 1/2 phosphorylation, activation of dual specificity phosphatase-1 and inducing antioxidant gene expression.

Conclusions

Collectively, these exploratory findings link dialysis intensification to miR-mediated regulation of the FGF23/Klotho axis, demonstrating that targeting this regulatory network is sufficient to suppress pathological cardiac remodeling. These data provide a mechanistic basis for the cardiovascular benefits of nocturnal hemodialysis and identify the FGF23/Klotho axis as a candidate therapeutic target warranting further validation.

title: Diabetic foot disease.
authorString: Armstrong DG, Boulton AJM, Brennan MB, Lazzarini PA, Lo ZJ, Sen CK, Venermo M, Hicks CW.
abstractText: Diabetic foot disease (DFD) encompasses the lower-extremity complications of diabetes mellitus, including peripheral neuropathy, peripheral artery disease, ulceration, infection and amputation. An estimated 199 million people worldwide had DFD in 2017, including 18.6 million with foot ulcers, which precede most lower-extremity amputations. The 5-year mortality approaches 30% after ulceration and >70% after major amputation, rivalling that of many advanced cancers. DFD disproportionately affects socioeconomically disadvantaged, rural and underserved populations, creating wide disparities in outcomes. Although DFD has traditionally been viewed as a neuropathic complication of diabetes mellitus, most clinically overt disease is neuroischaemic. Neuropathy permits injury to go unnoticed, whereas peripheral artery disease, which is present in ~50% of patients with foot ulcers, impairs healing and substantially increases the risk of amputation. The Wound, Ischemia and foot Infection (WIfI) classification has therefore emerged as a unifying framework for risk stratification, whereas multidisciplinary 'toe and flow' teams and advances in revascularization, wound care and pressure offloading have transformed management. Even after ulcer healing, recurrence reaches 40% at 1 year and ~60% within 3 years, reframing ulcer healing as remission rather than cure and emphasizing the need for lifelong surveillance and secondary prevention.

title: Prognostic utility of transvalvular flow rate in patients with low-gradient aortic stenosis undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation.
authorString: Xi B, Usami K, Sato K, Kawamatsu N, Yamamoto M, Machino-Ohtsuka T, Hiraya D, Watabe H, Hoshi T, Ishizu T, Seo Y, JSE-TAVI Investigators.
abstractText:
Background

Flow assessment helps determine the severity of low-gradient (LG) aortic stenosis (AS). Transvalvular flow rate (FR) may classify flow status differently from stroke volume index (SVi). This study compared their prognostic utility in patients with LG-AS undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI).

Methods

This post hoc analysis of a multicenter registry included 205 patients with severe symptomatic LG-AS who underwent TAVI. Low flow (LF) was defined separately as SVi ≤35 mL/m2 or FR ≤200 mL/s. The primary endpoint was all-cause death.

Results

SVi classified 74 patients (36%) as having LF, whereas FR classified 131 (64%) as having LF, including 63 with normal flow according to SVi. FR was correlated with LVEF (r = 0.457, P < 0.001) and natural-log-transformed E/e' (r = -0.205, P = 0.010). Patients with LF according to either measure showed greater recovery in left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF). In the multivariable Cox model, FR ≤200 mL/s was not associated with all-cause mortality (HR, 0.764; 95% CI, 0.376-1.551; P = 0.456).

Conclusion

FR identified more patients with LF than SVi but did not show an association with outcome after TAVI. These findings do not support prioritizing FR over SVi in patients with LG-AS.

title: Percutaneous Local Antibiotic Irrigation for Aortic Graft Infection After Endovascular Repair: A Single-Center Experience and Systematic Literature Review.
authorString: Ibrahim A, McGreevy DT, Chwich J, Hörer T, Djavani Gidlund K.

journal.title: Journal of endovascular therapy : an official journal of the International Society of Endovascular Specialists

abstractText:
Background

Aortic graft infections (AGIs) are a severe complication following open aortic surgical repair (OSR) and endovascular aortic repair (EVAR). Endograft extirpation and aortic reconstruction remain the gold standard treatment according to European guidelines. The aim is to present a single-center experience using a percutaneous local antibiotic irrigation strategy in selected patients with AGI after EVAR, with a systematic literature review.

Methods

Patients with AGI after endovascular aortic repair treated with computed tomography (CT)-guided local antibiotic irrigation (2011-2023) were included. Outcomes were assessed using clinical, microbiological, and radiological follow-up, with mortality and reinfection evaluated up to 3 years. A systematic search of PubMed and Cochrane was conducted. The review was not registered, and formal bias assessment was not performed.

Results

Among 665 endovascular repairs, 14 patients developed AGI. Eight patients were treated with CT-guided antibiotic irrigation. Infection resolved in 4 patients (n = 4/8), and 1 patient (n = 1/8) was treated as a bridge to open aortic surgical repair OSR. Persistent infection was observed in 3 patients (3/8). Cumulative mortality was 0% at 30 days (n = 0/8), 13% at 90 days (n = 1/8), and 50% (n = 4/8) at 1 to 3 years. Three patients (n = 3/8) died from recurrent infection. The literature review identified 6 studies, adding 28 cases. All patients were treated with antibiotic irrigation either as primary therapy or as a bridge to OSR. Short-term/30-day mortality ranged from 0% to 22%, except for 1 study, with mortality of 50%. Most studies achieved effective infection control in high-risk surgical candidates.

Conclusion

In highly selected groups of patients who are not candidates for extensive surgery such as aortic reconstruction, percutaneous local antibiotic irrigation may be an alternative treatment method.Clinical ImpactAGI after endovascular repair carries high mortality, current guidelines recommendation is endograft extirpation and aortic reconstruction. This may not be feasible for frail patients. This single-center case series along with literature review of 6 studies suggest it may be feasible with minimally invasive CT-guided percutaneous drainage with local antibiotic irrigation in carefully selected patients who are unfit for major surgery.

title: Developing structure and strategies for analysis of circulating biomarkers to detect and monitor abdominal aortic aneurysms.
authorString: Lindsey ML, Shivam P, Nde PN, Roy J, Baxter BT, Terrin M, Matsumura JS, Gaye A, Curci JA.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol
journal.title: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
journal.isoabbreviation: Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol

abstractText: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a multifactorial disease characterized by progressive remodeling of the aortic wall. Current clinical management includes screening ultrasound for diagnosis, and routine aortic imaging to monitor growth in patients with small AAA and surgical exclusion of larger AAA. With the evolution of a diverse array of multianalyte assessments from peripheral blood, comprehensive assessments of circulating biomarkers in patients with AAA is possible. In the context of this dynamic disease process, circulating markers - paired with clinical and imaging data - provide an opportunity to identify specific active biologic processes that influence the natural history of the disease. We propose a disease-specific framework for understanding relationships between circulating markers and imaging within a novel three class structure. Class I associations correlate with aortic size and presence of AAA and may be related to the mechanisms of initial formation. Class II associations track with change in aneurysm MTD and may be related to mechanisms of AAA growth and rupture risk. Class II may be clinically relevant for the identification of targets for modification that could alter the natural history of established AAA. Class III associations relate to static or dynamic morphologic features such as mural thrombus or calcifications that have less well-defined associations with clinical outcomes. Identified and appropriately classified markers can provide specific avenues for novel therapeutic and diagnostic options to reduce morbidity and mortality in patients with AAA.

title: Evaluation of D-dimer Levels for the Differential Diagnosis of Acute Chest Pain in Hong Kong: A Single-Centre Retrospective Study D-dimer for Chest Pain Diagnoses
authorString: Li RST, Li KJKW, Cattermole G, Leung LY, Hung KKC, Cheng RCH, Man SY, Graham CA.
abstractText: Background D-dimer is elevated in acute aortic syndrome (AAS) and pulmonary embolism (PE), but local comparative data is limited. This study explores D-dimer's diagnostic value for AAS to inform acute chest pain management. Methods This retrospective single-centre study in Hong Kong evaluated adult emergency department (ED) patients presenting with chest pain between 2020 and 2025. Patients with D-dimer testing were grouped by diagnosis: AAS, PE, ischaemic heart disease (IHD), or non-specific chest pain (CP). Outcomes included D-dimer levels, diagnostic performance of D-dimer for AAS and PE, computed tomography (CT) utilization, 7- and 30-day mortality, hospital length of stay, and 28-day readmission rates. Results Among 1,019 included patients, median D-dimer levels were 329, 531, 3738, and 4693 ng/mL for CP, IHD, PE, and AAS, respectively. The AUROC for distinguishing AAS from non-AAS was 0.84 (95% CI: 0.79–0.89). D-dimer ≥ 2000 ng/mL was associated with significantly higher mortality. ED-based CT scans were performed in only 3 (27.3%) of AAS and 15 (6.3%) of PE patients. Conclusions This study reports the first local data characterising D-dimer levels across acute chest pain aetiologies, with the highest values observed in AAS and PE. The notably low CT rates in both the AAS and PE groups highlight an unanswered clinical need, and prospective multicentre studies integrating biomarkers with validated clinical decision tools are warranted to optimise risk stratification and CT utilisation for high-risk ED patients with chest pain.

title: Adjunctive Intra-Aortic Balloon Pump During Venovenous Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation for Severe Respiratory Failure With Cardiac Dysfunction: A Retrospective Cohort Study
authorString: Wei J, Hu H, Gan Y, Shao H, Shen L, Zeng Z.
abstractText: Background Evidence regarding intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) use during venovenous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV-ECMO) is limited. We examined clinical outcomes and hemodynamic trajectories in patients with severe respiratory failure and cardiac dysfunction treated with or without adjunctive IABP. Methods In this single-center retrospective cohort study, five patients who received VV-ECMO + IABP were compared with 24 patients who received VV-ECMO only (16 original controls and eight additional controls with high-dose vasopressor exposure). The primary outcome was ventilator-free days through day 28 (VFD-28). Secondary outcomes included 7-day norepinephrine-equivalent and vasoactive-inotropic score (VIS) area under the curve (AUC), 72-hour lactate AUC, renal replacement therapy (RRT), mortality, and bleeding. The main sensitivity analysis compared the five VV-ECMO + IABP patients with all eight additional controls who had a norepinephrine-equivalent dose of at least 0.5 µg/kg/min on one or more days from D0 through D7. Additional sensitivity analyses used the 16 original controls and the four additional controls who met the high-dose threshold at D0. Results The VV-ECMO + IABP group had higher baseline SOFA scores, PEEP, and D0 norepinephrine-equivalent doses than the VV-ECMO-only group. Median VFD-28 was 0.0 days (interquartile range [IQR], 0.0–6.9) versus 0.7 days (IQR, 0.0–9.9; P =  0.740; rank-biserial correlation, − 0.10; 95% CI, − 0.54 to 0.41). Norepinephrine-equivalent AUC was 0.89 versus 0.76 (µg/kg/min)·day ( P =  0.600), VIS AUC was 89.2 versus 68.8 score·days ( P =  0.780), and verified 28-day mortality was 40.0% versus 37.5% ( P =  1.000). RRT duration was 5.0 versus 1.0 days ( P =  0.041), and recorded bleeding occurred in 80.0% versus 37.5% of patients ( P =  0.144). In the 5-vs-8 sensitivity analysis, VFD-28 was 0.0 versus 0.0 days ( P =  1.000), norepinephrine-equivalent AUC was 0.89 versus 2.01 (µg/kg/min)·day ( P =  0.268), and verified 28-day mortality was 40.0% versus 37.5% ( P =  1.000). Conclusions In this small retrospective cohort, adjunctive IABP during VV-ECMO was not associated with higher VFD-28, lower cumulative vasoactive exposure, or lower 28-day mortality. These findings require confirmation in studies with prospective cardiac phenotyping and larger samples.

title: Night shift work and subclinical cardiac remodelling: a multi-omic CMR study in 42 671 individuals.
authorString: Gao Y, Wang Y, Shi Z, Shi Q, Zhang C, Chen D, Gu Y, Hu H, Wang X, He B, Ma C, Guo Q, Gao C, Zhang Z, Geng B, Li M.
abstractText:
Aims

Whether frequent night-shift work is associated with a distinct subclinical cardiac phenotype and accompanying molecular alterations remains uncertain.

Methods and results

We analysed 42 671 UK Biobank participants without baseline cardiovascular disease who underwent cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR). Night-shift frequency was classified into four categories, and 15 CMR measures were assessed using multivariable regression. Compared with day workers, frequent night-shift workers showed greater left ventricular global wall thickness [standardized β = 0.092, 95% CI 0.050-0.135; false discovery rate (FDR) < 0.001] and left ventricular mass-to-volume ratio (β = 0.072, 95% CI 0.021-0.123; FDR = 0.019), with lower left ventricular end-diastolic volume index, right ventricular end-diastolic volume index, right ventricular stroke volume index, and maximal right atrial volume index (all FDR < 0.05). Left ventricular global circumferential strain was less favourable (β = 0.092, 95% CI 0.040-0.144; FDR = 0.002), whereas left ventricular ejection fraction and global longitudinal strain were not significantly associated. Proteomic (n = 4889) and metabolomic (n = 42 671) analyses identified exploratory inflammatory, vascular, and lipid-related correlates. Mediation analyses identified FDR-significant indirect-effect estimates involving left ventricular end-diastolic volume index for three proteins and four metabolites. Two-sample Mendelian randomization identified associations between selected molecular features and CMR traits, although directions were not uniformly concordant with the observational estimates.

Conclusion

Frequent night shift work was associated with greater concentric left ventricular geometry, lower cardiac chamber volumes, and less favourable circumferential strain, together with inflammatory and lipid-related molecular correlates. Prospective studies are required to determine temporal relationships and long-term clinical relevance.

title: Cross-View Constrained Encoder and Cross-Modal Semantic-Hierarchy Fusion Network for Congenital Heart Disease Identification.
authorString: Yang X, Zhao M, Bai Y, Yuan T, Peng B, Li Y, Lin J.

journal.title: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine

abstractText: Congenital heart disease (CHD) is a common structural birth defect, and early screening is important for improving prognosis. Clinical cardiac ultrasound combines brightness-mode (B-mode) and color Doppler images from multiple standard views to assess cardiac morphology and hemodynamic abnormalities. Existing case-level models remain limited in modeling information exchange among standard views within each modality and cross-modal fusion between B-mode morphology and Doppler hemodynamics. The proposed Cross-View Constrained Encoder and Cross-Modal Semantic-Hierarchy Fusion Network (CVCE-CMSHFNet) addresses these limitations through two complementary components: a Multi-View Constrained Encoder (MVCE) and a Bidirectional Progressive Semantic-Hierarchy Fusion (BiPSHF) module. MVCE models relationships among the eight standard views within each modality. Sinkhorn-constrained transport and a parallel gated transformation update the view representations. Training-time Intra-Modal View Covariance Diversity Regularization (IVCDR) separately penalizes covariance similarity among B-mode view representations and among Doppler view representations. BiPSHF performs bidirectional cross-modal interaction at the view, view-group, and case levels. The view-group level organizes the eight standard views into four study-specific groups based on anatomical relationships and clinical assessment roles. CVCE-CMSHFNet aims to support clinical diagnosis by providing a case-level CHD probability for physician reference. Evaluation included 384 complete eight-view dual-modality cases from a 506-subject single-center echocardiography database. CVCE-CMSHFNet achieved 95.64% accuracy, 95.23% F1 score, 97.05% AUC, 94.44% sensitivity, and 96.67% specificity.

title: The Case for Interpretable Geometry: Statistical Shape Models vs. Curvature-Based Descriptors in Aortic Disease Classification.
authorString: Nguyen D, Pugar JA, Pocivavsek L.
abstractText:
Purpose

Quantifying aortic morphology is central to surgical planning for thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR), yet no consensus exists on how best to represent three-dimensional aortic shape for outcome prediction. Two broad strategies have emerged: statistical shape analysis (SSA), which relies on statistical methods and dimensionality reduction to capture the most significant shape modes, and geometrically-informed approaches that extract descriptors grounded in differential geometry. Here, we directly compare these paradigms on a cohort of 290 CTA scans classified by surgical outcome (non-pathological, successful TEVAR, failed TEVAR).

Methods

For the geometrically-informed approach, we use a two-dimensional feature space using fluctuation in integrated Gaussian curvature δK and mean aortic radius R. For SSA, we construct a point-cloud shape model with dimensionality reduction using Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and evaluate classification performance as a function of the number of retained principal components. Both approaches are evaluated by repeated cross-validation grouped by patient, with all scaling, PCA, and hyperparameter selection performed within the training folds, and by external testing on scans from the GORE TAG 08-01 trial.

Results

SSA's leading principal components encode variations in global aortic size and shape and are statistically redundant with (R, δK ), yet they lack a one-to-one correspondence with interpretable anatomical quantities. With the same number of dimensions, the geometric descriptors classified at least as well as SSA (Gaussian process classification, cross-validated weighted F1 of 85.8% versus 84.9%). SSA's cross-validated F1 peaked with two principal components (83.1%) and declined as more were added, although its training-set accuracy rose above 90%, which indicates overfitting. On the independent trial cohort, in which every patient required TEVAR, SSA classified 50.7% of scans as non-pathological, compared with 21.2% for the geometric approach, suggesting better generalizability.

Conclusion

Two physically defined descriptors classified aortic disease at least as well as the leading SSA modes and transferred better to an independent cohort. SSA modes offer an intuitive visualization of how shape varies across a cohort, but geometric descriptors, which are measured identically for any patient and do not depend on the cohort used to build a model, provide a more robust basis for patient-level classification.

title: The histone demethylase KDM6B preserves adipogenic balance by restraining hypermetabolic LYVE1<sup>+</sup> perivascular macrophages.
authorString: Aznar B, Mezdari Z, He J, Ballaire R, Diedisheim M, Anisov D, Orliaguet L, Leveau C, Julla JB, Anagnostopoulos G, Kong WT, Chiral M, Chen L, Li Q, Chokr D, Nemazanyy I, Legoix P, Soprani A, Lindén D, Fan R, Velho G, Le Goff W, Treuter E, Gautier JF, Chakarov S, Ginhoux F, Toubal A, Venteclef N.
abstractText: White adipose tissue expandability protects against metabolic disease, yet the epigenetic programmes that maintain the macrophage states supporting this adaptation remain poorly defined. Here we show that the H3K27 demethylase KDM6B sustains LYVE1+ adipose tissue perivascular macrophages (PVMs) during diet-induced white adipose tissue expansion, thereby maintaining adipogenic balance. In humans, KDM6B expression in adipose tissue macrophages associates with insulin sensitivity, glycaemic control and reduced inflammation. In mice, myeloid Kdm6b deletion reprogrammes septal and capsular LYVE1+ macrophages towards a CLEC1A+ hypermetabolic perivascular state, leading to defective adipogenesis, adipocyte hypertrophy, vascular rarefaction, inflammation and impaired glucose homeostasis. Mechanistically, KDM6B limits H3K27me3 deposition at the Bmp2 locus to maintain macrophage-derived BMP2 signalling to adipose progenitors. Myeloid Bmp2 deletion partially recapitulates Kdm6b-deficient adipose dysfunction, whereas recombinant BMP2 promotes homeostatic tissue remodelling. Collectively, KDM6B acts as an epigenetic switch controlling the metabolic fate of LYVE1+ PVMs, maintaining the balance between adipogenesis-supportive and metabolic PVM states that determine adipose tissue expandability and metabolic homeostasis.

title: Space-map: 3D single-cell atlas reconstruction from serial sections.
authorString: Han R, Ruan C, Zhao B, Tan Y, Monte E, Wei B, Bi J, Karathanos TV, Laquindanum R, Charville GW, Lin Y, Ling N, Ford JM, Nolan GP, Wang M, Zhu C, Snyder MP.
abstractText: High-resolution three-dimensional (3D) tissue atlases promise to link cellular architecture to tissue function, but assembling them from serial sections containing millions of cells remains challenging. Here we present Space-map, an accurate and efficient method for reconstructing 3D tissue models from high-content spatial molecular profiles. Space-map combines multiscale feature matching with large deformation diffeomorphic metric mapping to automate global alignment across serial sections while preserving local microanatomy. We generate spatial transcriptomics (Xenium; ~2.7 million cells) and proteomics (CODEX; ~4.8 million cells) datasets from serial sections to build 3D models of a colon polyp and healthy intestinal tissues. These models reveal cell-type heterogeneity in the polyp and preserved crypt and glandular architecture and mucosal-cavity continuity in healthy intestines. Benchmarking on our own and publicly available datasets demonstrates that Space-map achieves substantially higher registration accuracy and up to a tenfold speedup over existing methods, supporting its use as a robust framework for constructing 3D human tissue atlases at single-cell resolution.

title: Mapping the two faces of the blood-brain barrier.
authorString: Montagne A.
abstractText: In brain capillaries, flattened endothelial cells separate the blood from the brain across luminal and abluminal membranes that are approximately 200 nm apart. Amick and colleagues now resolve this hidden polarity in vivo, identify sequence motifs that direct proteins towards the brain-facing membrane, and show that membrane distribution can change with the time of day.

title: Long-Term Outcomes of Parenteral Prostacyclin Use in Adults With Congenital Heart Disease-Associated Pulmonary Hypertension.
authorString: Jakubowski BR, Sande-Docor G, Kentros PA, De La Rosa II, Ortiz Berrio MA, Kearney K, Tan W, Shah T, Bartolome S, Chin KS.
abstractText:
Background & aim

Robust evidence to inform the use of parenteral prostacyclin agents (PPAs) in adults with congenital heart disease-associated pulmonary arterial hypertension (CHD-PAH) is lacking. We aimed to evaluate long-term haemodynamic, functional, and survival outcomes in a contemporary single-centre cohort of patients with CHD-PAH treated with PPA.

Method

We performed a retrospective cohort study of adults with CHD-PAH treated with parenteral prostacyclin therapy at a single tertiary centre from 2000 to 2024.

Results

Twenty-nine patients initiated a PPA between 2000 and 2024 (epoprostenol, n=17, intravenous treprostinil, n=7, subcutaneous treprostinil, n=5). Median age at initiation was 36 years, and two-thirds had unrepaired congenital lesions. At first follow-up, right heart catheterisation after starting PPA therapy, prostacyclin therapy was associated with significant reductions in mean pulmonary artery pressure (-7.7 mmHg; p=0.003) and pulmonary vascular resistance (-5.4 Wood Units; p=0.001), as well as increases in cardiac index (1.2 L/min/min2; p=0.002), and pulmonary artery oxygen saturation (9%; p=0.005). Haemodynamic improvements were similar between patients receiving epoprostenol and those receiving treprostinil. Five- and 10-year survival rates were 86% and 58%, respectively, and three patients were able to undergo delayed defect closure.

Conclusions

In adults with CHD-PAH, parenteral prostacyclin therapy is associated with significant improvements in pulmonary haemodynamics and functional capacity, along with favourable long-term survival. These findings highlight the need for larger multicentre studies to refine patient selection and optimise treatment strategies.

title: Sedentary Behaviour and Physical Activity in Brazilian Participants of Cardiac Rehabilitation Programs: Association With Heart Rate Variability Indices.
authorString: Silva JPLN, Soares JCÁ, Valente HB, Moliterno AH, Ribeiro F, Laurino MJL, Silva AVB, Colombo E, Silva AKF, Vanderlei LCM.
abstractText: We aimed to evaluate the association of sedentary behaviour (SB) and physical activity (PA) levels with heart rate variability (HRV) indices in participants of cardiac rehabilitation programs (CRPs). This cross-sectional study included participants enrolled in CRP in Presidente Prudente, Brazil. Individuals diagnosed with cardiovascular disease or cardiovascular risk factors were eligible if they were participating in a rehabilitation program and had no cardiac arrhythmias that could affect HRV analysis. SB and PA were assessed using accelerometry, and HRV indices (root mean square difference of successive RR intervals [rMSSD], standard deviation of NN intervals [SDNN], low frequency [LF,] and high frequency [HF]) were evaluated from RR interval recordings obtained using a heart rate monitor. Associations between movement behaviours and HRV indices were analysed using quantile regression. Significance was set at 5%. The final sample consisted of 70 participants (52.86% women) with a mean age of 67.17±9.98 years. In the model adjusted for age, sex, rehabilitation time, and beta-blocker use, negative associations were found between the percentage of time in SB and the LF (β: -7.423; p=0.016) and HF (β: -5.434; p=0.030) indices, and positive associations between moderate-to-vigorous PA (MVPA) and LF (β: 3.856; p=0.034 for time in MVPA; β: 35.328; p=0.031 for percentage of time in MVPA); steps per day and LF (β: 0.033; p=0.002) and HF (β: 0.022; p=0.011); and steps per minute and SDNN (β: 2.141; p=0.001), rMSSD (β: 2.127; p=0.001), LF (β: 33.505; p<0.001), and HF (β: 19.097; p=0.008). Longer time in SB was associated with worse HRV indices, whereas higher PA levels were associated with a more favourable HRV profile in CRP participants. These findings support CRP strategies that reduce SB and encourage daily movement.

title: Association Between Immediate Postoperative Mean Pulmonary Artery Pressure and Heart Failure Readmission After Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting.
authorString: Li J, Wang H, Zhang M, Zhang C.
abstractText:
Background

Readmission occurs frequently after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG); however, factors that specifically predict heart failure (HF)-related readmission are not well defined. To assess the relationship between immediate postoperative mean pulmonary artery pressure (mPAP) and the risk of HF readmission following CABG.

Method

A secondary analysis of 1,593 patients undergoing CABG used publicly available data to assess the association between immediate postoperative mPAP and hospital readmission for HF. Univariate and multivariate Cox proportional hazards regression models were employed, adjusting for relevant clinical confounders. Receiver operating characteristic curve analysis was performed to evaluate the ability of mPAP to predict HF readmission.

Results

Over a median follow-up of 3.8 years, 241 patients (15.13%) experienced HF readmission. A fitted curve showed a linear relationship between immediate postoperative mPAP and HF readmission risk. Multivariable analysis demonstrated that a 1 mmHg increase in mPAP was independently correlated with a greater risk of HF readmission (hazard ratio [HR] 1.03; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.01-1.06; p=0.005). In analysis using mPAP categories, patients with intermediate (15-30 mmHg) and high (>30 mmHg) mPAP levels exhibited significantly greater adjusted risks of HF readmission than those in the low mPAP group (≤15 mmHg), with HRs of 2.00 (95% CI 1.04-3.84) and 2.19 (95% CI 1.05-4.59), respectively.

Conclusions

In patients undergoing CABG, higher immediate postoperative mPAP was independently linked to a dose-dependent rise in the risk of HF readmission.

title: Mechanisms and management of multimorbidity in patients with COPD.
authorString: Vogelmeier CF, Wen F, Christenson SA, Alagappan V, Heble J, Criner GJ.
abstractText: Multimorbidity, defined as the presence of two or more chronic conditions, represents a significant challenge in the management of COPD, a complex and highly prevalent disease. The coexistence of chronic conditions such as cardiovascular or metabolic diseases increases the frequency and severity of COPD exacerbations, complicates treatment decisions and worsens patient outcomes. These coexisting diseases may share underlying mechanisms, including systemic inflammation, oxidative stress and risk factors such as smoking, which accelerate disease progression. In this review, we discuss the prevalence and clinical significance of multimorbidity in COPD, with a focus on shared risk factors, the pathophysiological mechanisms and the impact on outcomes. Additionally, we examine current disease management strategies for COPD and multimorbidity, highlighting the need for a multidisciplinary, personalised approach, and discuss the role of biomarkers in coexisting conditions.

title: Predictors of methotrexate treatment failure in tubal ectopic pregnancy: Retrospective cohort study.
authorString: Cetin F, Kayar İ, Birge Ö.

journal.title: The Journal of international medical research

abstractText: ObjectiveThis study aimed to identify clinical, biochemical, and ultrasonographic factors associated with methotrexate treatment failure in patients with tubal ectopic pregnancy.MethodsData from 168 patients who received systemic methotrexate treatment for tubal ectopic pregnancy between January 2016 and April 2026 were retrospectively reviewed. Treatment success was defined as a reduction in beta-human chorionic gonadotropin levels to <5 IU/L without surgery. Statistical analyses included the Mann-Whitney U test, Fisher's exact test, logistic regression, and receiver operating characteristic analysis.ResultsTreatment success and failure occurred in 125 (74.4%) and 43 (25.6%) patients, respectively. In univariable analysis, smoking, white blood cell count, C-reactive protein, fasting blood sugar, endometrial thickness, yolk sac, fetal cardiac activity, day 4 beta-human chorionic gonadotropin, and day 7 beta-human chorionic gonadotropin were significantly associated with treatment failure. In multivariable analysis, smoking (odds ratio = 25.3; 95% confidence interval: 4.4-146.1), C-reactive protein (odds ratio = 1.36; 95% confidence interval: 1.10-1.67), fasting blood sugar (odds ratio = 1.09; 95% confidence interval: 1.03-1.15), and endometrial thickness (odds ratio = 1.87; 95% confidence interval: 1.38-2.54) were independently associated with treatment failure. The presence of a yolk sac showed strong discriminatory performance in univariable analysis (sensitivity: 95%; specificity: 98%; apparent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve = 0.97). The day 7/4 beta-human chorionic gonadotropin ratio was not included as an independent predictor because it overlaps with the biochemical criteria defining treatment failure.ConclusionsSmoking, higher C-reactive protein and fasting blood sugar levels, and increased endometrial thickness were independently associated with methotrexate treatment failure. The day 4-7 beta-human chorionic gonadotropin decline was considered an early post-treatment response marker rather than a pretreatment predictor. Although the multivariable model showed high apparent discrimination, the absence of internal validation may have resulted in model optimism. Therefore, the model should be considered exploratory rather than clinically validated. Larger independent cohorts with internal and external validation are required before clinical application.

title: RIPK2 is associated with inflammatory plaque macrophage phenotypes and modulates NF-κB and MMP9-related responses in THP-1-derived macrophages.
authorString: He W, Zhang Q, Qing X, Chen Y, Liang G, Zhang W, Gao Y, Ma J.
abstractText: Atherosclerosis is sustained by inflammatory macrophage phenotypes, but the upstream signalling regulators that connect human plaque heterogeneity with macrophage activation remain incompletely defined. Here, we integrated public human plaque transcriptomic cohorts, single-cell plaque mapping and THP-1-derived macrophage experiments to evaluate receptor-interacting serine/threonine-protein kinase 2 (RIPK2) in atherosclerotic inflammation. RIPK2 was consistently upregulated in plaque tissue and associated with tumour necrosis factor, nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB), cytokine, complement and interferon-response pathways. Single-cell analysis localised RIPK2 predominantly to macrophages, with inflammatory and matrix-remodelling signatures in RIPK2-high cells. A targeted plaque-stage analysis showed a modest, probe-dependent association. In oxidised low-density lipoprotein (ox-LDL)-stimulated THP-1-derived macrophages, RIPK2 depletion reduced p65 and MMP9 responses, and wild-type reconstitution partially restored selected readouts. A phosphorylation time course and individual or combined NOD1/NOD2 depletion supported early NOD-associated RIPK2 signalling, with residual responses. Quantified p65 nuclear localisation provided an additional pathway readout. Conditioned-medium zymography showed changes in the 92-kDa pro-MMP9-associated gelatinolytic signal; induction of the active 82-kDa form was not established. GSK583 concentration responses were evaluated alongside viability and LDH measurements, which did not show a comparable monotonic deterioration as cytokine secretion declined. These findings support functional involvement of RIPK2 in THP-1 inflammatory responses and identify a macrophage-associated feature of human plaques. Primary human macrophage validation and the molecular links between RIPK2, NF-κB and MMP9 remain to be established.

title: Chronic hypoxia drives coronary artery pathology via TRPC3/4-mediated Ca²⁺ influx and phase separation-dependent cGAS-STING activation.
authorString: Li HB, Liu JY, Zheng SY, Chen QY, Sun YZ, Gui LX, Lin MJ, Lin DC.
abstractText:
Aims

Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is frequently complicated by coronary artery remodeling and dysfunction, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly defined. This study investigated whether and how chronic hypoxia drives coronary artery dysfunction through TRPC3/4-mediated Ca²⁺ influx and cGAS-STING activation in smooth muscle cells (SMCs).

Methods and results

A rat model of PH was established by exposure to chronic hypoxia. Coronary artery structure and function were assessed by histology and wire myography. In vitro experiments were performed using cultured SMCs, with molecular and cellular analyses including qPCR, western blotting, immunofluorescence, live-cell imaging, mitochondrial assays, and cell-free phase separation assays. PH rats exhibited increased coronary TRPC3/4 expression, enhanced Ca²⁺ influx, and coronary hypercontractility. In cultured SMCs, hypoxia induced mitochondrial dysfunction, mtDNA release, and cGAS condensate formation. TRPC3/4-mediated Ca²⁺ overload promoted mitochondrial damage and cGAS phase separation, while STIM1/ORAI1-mediated store-operated Ca²⁺ entry (SOCE) further contributed to STING activation. Cell-free assays demonstrated that Ca²⁺ promoted cGAS phase separation in both the presence and absence of dsDNA, and this effect was dependent on the cGAS intrinsically disordered region (IDR). Importantly, CIP3 attenuated cGAS phase separation and downstream STING signaling, thereby mitigating hypoxia-induced SMC proliferation, migration, and phenotypic switching. In PH rats, short-term treatment with VAPG-targeted CIP3 reduced right ventricular systolic pressure, attenuated pulmonary and coronary vascular remodeling, and improved coronary contractile responses.

Conclusion

Our findings establish a novel mechanistic axis wherein chronic hypoxia drives coronary artery dysfunction via TRPC3/4-mediated Ca²⁺ influx and phase separation-dependent cGAS-STING activation. In our experimental models, targeting cGAS phase separation, particularly through IDR-directed intervention, may represent a promising therapeutic strategy for PH-associated vascular pathology.

title: Eximer Laser Coronary Atherectomy in the Current era of Complex Percutenoues Coronary Intervention: New Insights from the ACCELERATE (eAst siCily exCimEr LasER ATherEctomy) Registry.
authorString: Tomasello SD, Rochira C, Mazzapicchi A, Azzarelli SA, Giorgio AD, Scardaci F, Monaco S, Argentino V, Motta S, Sacchetta G, Barrano G, Contarini M, Amico F.
abstractText: Excimer laser coronary atherectomy (ELCA) is a debulking option for treating complex coronary lesions. Recently, interesting clinical data came to the light from a multi-center prospectical study (the ACCELERATE Registry) which enrolled 320 consecutive patients treated with ELCA. The aim of the present study is to evaluate the differences in terms of procedural, in-hospital and long-term outcomes between patients treated for calcified de novo lesions (CDNL) and intrastent restenosis (ISR) in the ACCELERATE Registry. Between July 2018 and May 2024, 320 consecutive patients (mean age 71 ± 9 years) with 429 lesions treated with ELCA were included in the registry. Among them, 156 patients had 197 CDNL, while 164 patients had 232 ISR, with 205 cases due to neointimal proliferation and 27 cases to stent under-expansion. The cohort was characterized by high anatomical complexity and an elevated cardiovascular risk, with a Syntax score of 20.00 ± 10.2 and an STS score of 2.8 ± 2.3. Procedural success was achieved in 97% of cases (99% CDNL vs. 95.1% ISR), and complete revascularization was performed in 74% of cases. In conclusion the results of this study confirm safety and effectiveness of ELCA in treating complex coronary lesions and suggest that ELCA may offer superior long-term outcomes in patients with CDNL compared with ISR, particularly in reducing the incidence of TLR at long-term follow up.

title: Oxidative stress biomarkers and residual cardiovascular risk in atherosclerosis: A narrative review of mechanistic rationale, prognostic associations, and translational barriers.
authorString: Iova V, Trache D, Mitu O, Perone F, Treteanu AR, Gherasie F, Davos CH, Abras M, Busnatu SS.
abstractText: Despite major advances in lipid-lowering therapy, residual cardiovascular risk persists in patients with atherosclerotic disease, highlighting limitations of conventional risk factors in capturing biological processes involved in disease progression. This review examines the potential relevance of three interconnected oxidative stress-related biomarkers-oxidized low-density lipoprotein (oxLDL), myeloperoxidase (MPO), and soluble lectin-like oxidized low-density lipoprotein receptor-1 (sLOX-1)-with a primary focus on their potential complementary role in cardiovascular risk assessment in coronary artery disease (CAD). MPO can promote LDL oxidation and oxLDL formation, while oxLDL activates LOX-1-related pathways involved in oxidative stress, inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, and vascular injury; proteolytic cleavage of LOX-1 generates circulating sLOX-1. We synthesize evidence regarding associations of these biomarkers with CAD and cardiovascular outcomes and consider whether their combination with established clinical risk factors and risk scores could provide additional information on residual cardiovascular risk. Evidence from carotid and peripheral atherosclerotic disease and from chronic comorbid conditions is considered mainly as supportive biological and clinical context. However, substantial heterogeneity in study populations, clinical endpoints, analytical methods, and reported biomarker thresholds limits direct comparison and prevents conclusions regarding a validated role in clinical risk re-stratification. We therefore propose the combined assessment of oxLDL, MPO, and sLOX-1 as a hypothesis-generating multimarker strategy for evaluation in prospective studies, rather than an established approach for risk classification or treatment guidance.

title: Dose-adjustable amlodipine tablets engineered by semi-solid extrusion 3D printing at room temperature for point-of-care applications.
authorString: Khalid GM, Kashif S, Rami M, Falahie A, Bello MG, Hadjipour A, Robinson L, Kavanagh O, Hassan SM, Gresley AL, Bendicho-Lavilla C, Goyanes A, Basit AW.
abstractText: Conventional technologies make it difficult to manufacture personalised oral dosage forms for thermosensitive active pharmaceutical ingredients. In addition, there are several drawbacks to the one-size-fits-all approach for hypertension management. For instance, commercial amlodipine products are available as amlodipine salts in limited fixed-dose strengths, which do not accommodate personalised dosing. This proof-of-concept study investigates the feasibility of using semi-solid extrusion (SSE) 3D printing at room temperature to fabricate dose-adjustable, antihypertensive drug susceptible to thermal degradation as oral solid dosage forms, with amlodipine free base as a model drug for point-of-care applications. A single amlodipine-loaded pharma-ink (2.5%w/w) was used to manufacture 3D printed tablets (printlets) containing 5, 7.5 and 15 mg of amlodipine free base by varying printlet dimensions. The printlets were characterised for physical properties, drug content, dissolution, solid-state properties and morphology using HPLC, SEM-EDX, DSC, PXRD, FTIR, Raman spectroscopy and solid-state NMR. Dose-adjustable printlets were successfully 3D printed at room temperature with acceptable drug content (96.8-104.9%), rapid disintegration (<5 min) and immediate drug release (t80% 9-22 min). Solid-state characterisation supports the physicochemical integrity of amlodipine following printing and drying, while HPLC showed no evidence of degradation products. The same pharma-ink enabled accurate fabrication of multiple dose strengths without reformulation. SSE 3D printing provides a simple approach for compounding personalised, dose-adjustable amlodipine free base tablets under mild processing conditions, avoiding its degradation. In addition, this approach could address the conventional manufacturing challenges associated with poor flowability of amlodipine base. The technology offers considerable potential for decentralised point-of-care manufacture of thermosensitive medicines and supports future implementation of personalised cardiovascular therapies.

title: Development and In-Vitro Validation of the First Functional, Patient Specific, Metal Additively Manufactured Aneurysm Clip.
authorString: Civilla L, Dodier P, Lazic D, Harakály GA, Moedder D, Zopf LM, Mallouhi A, Marik W, Moscato F.
abstractText: Recent aneurysm clip improvements enhance biocompatibility and imaging artifacts through new materials, while design remained limited. This study aimed to investigate the feasibility of 3D printing aneurysm clips, including the development of the first functional, patient-specific, metal 3D-printed clip. A 5.8 mm wide case of unruptured intracranial aneurysm previously treated with aneurysm ligation through clipping was included, and a complete imaging dataset acquired and segmented. One standard and one patient-specific clip design were evaluated using a Finite Element Model (FEM) simulation to assess clip blade dimensions with respect to the aneurysm sac. Metal 3D printing was employed to produce the clip blades, then assembled with standard clip springs. The produced prototypes were then tested on a silicone 3D-printed physical simulator under exoscope visualization and indocyanine green angiography in a neurosurgical laboratory. Occlusion of the implanted patient-specific clip was then assessed using CT imaging. The FEM simulations confirmed design adequacy, with the patient-specific design reducing maximum strain and stress than the standard design respectively of 4.3% and 14%. Both 3D-printed clip designs presented self-occluding functionality, with a maximum dimensional deviation of 90 μm, and a tip-to-tip aperture capacity reduced from 9 mm of traditional clips to 7 mm and 6 mm, respectively. The 3D-printed clips fully occluded the silicone aneurysm sac. The patient-specific design avoided dog-ear formation and improved vascular reconstruction, then radiologically confirmed. Metal 3D printing enabled the first self-closing, patient-specific aneurysm clip, with functional feasibility demonstrated in a simulated setting; comprehensive mechanical characterization is the next step toward clinical application.

title: Bedside ECMO Cannulation by Intensivists and Emergency Physicians.
authorString: Sheehan J, Hansen SJ, Heather B, Erickson H, Simpson NS, Robinson AE, Hu M, Prekker ME.
abstractText: The number of centers capable of initiating extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) for critically ill patients with refractory cardiac or respiratory failure is expanding. Historically, patients were taken to the operating room or catheterization laboratory for ECMO cannulation by cardiothoracic surgeons and perfusionists. More recently, non-surgeons who have undergone specialized training are performing percutaneous ECMO cannulation and initiation of support at the bedside at some centers. This approach is attractive, in part, because of the timely initiation of ECMO and avoidance of the risk of patient deterioration during transport to a procedural area. The purpose of this article is to provide a roadmap for intensivists and emergency physicians to lead ECMO bedside procedures including veno-venous (VV), veno-arterial (VA), and hybrid veno-arteriovenous (V-AV) cannulation at ECMO-capable centers. These procedures demand cognitive and technical skills that are already foundational to critical care practice, including vascular access guided by point-of-care ultrasound and leadership during a dynamic resuscitation. A team-based approach to bedside ECMO cannulation is presented and illustrated with figures and video, including preparation, procedural execution, subsequent patient management, and programmatic considerations such as training and credentialing requirements.

title: Liberation from Veno-venous Extracorporeal Life Support (VV-ECLS) for Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS): the Liberate VV-ECLS study: an international survey.
authorString: Al-Fares A, Al-Rashed M, Al-Mumin A, Del Sorbo L, Fan E.
abstractText: The use of veno-venous extracorporeal life support (VV-ECLS) for severe acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) has increased substantially worldwide. However, approaches to liberation from extracorporeal support remain poorly defined, with no standardized protocols or validated readiness criteria. What are the global practices for VV-ECLS liberation among Extracorporeal Life Support Organization (ELSO) centers? Where is there variability in readiness assessment, liberation strategies, and use of standardized protocols? We formulated a cross-sectional survey of 25 questions regarding liberation practices among ECLS providers. Questions focused on assessed parameters for readiness to liberate, determination of liberation success, and strategies to optimize it. Surveys were distributed electronically to 765 institutions globally registered with ELSO between July 1st and Aug 15th, 2022. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize responses. Of 765 centers contacted, 340 (44%) responded, with 209 (61%) reporting use of VV-ECLS. Most centers were adult-focused, intensivist-led programs with moderate annual volumes. Most respondents (58%) prioritized VV-ECLS liberation before liberation from mechanical ventilation. Readiness for liberation was most determined by improvement in oxygenation under lung-protective ventilation (92%) and respiratory system compliance (90%), while fewer centers used inspiratory effort indices (34%). Liberation strategies were heterogeneous, with progressive reduction of sweep gas flow being most common (40%). Liberation trial duration varied widely (median 120 minutes; mean 497 ± 635 minutes), and most centers performed one trial per day. Arterial blood gas abnormalities (90%) and clinical signs of respiratory distress were the primary indicators of liberation failure. Only 42% of centers reported using a formal liberation protocol. VV-ECLS liberation practices vary substantially across centers and are largely guided by institutional experience rather than standardized evidence. These findings highlight the need for validated physiologic predictors and protocolized strategies to optimize safe and timely liberation from VV-ECLS.

title: Elevated serum levels of interferon-stimulated gene 15 are associated with the prevalence of hypertriglyceridemia.
authorString: Zheng X, Xiang Q, Huang X, He Y, Xu J.

journal.title: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry

abstractText:
Background

Hypertriglyceridemia (HTG) is a prevalent dyslipidemia worldwide and an independent risk factor for cardiovascular disease and acute pancreatitis. Interferon-stimulated gene 15 (ISG15), a ubiquitin-like protein involved in innate immunity, has recently been implicated in metabolic disorders, but its relationship with HTG remains unexplored.

Methods

This study included 295 Chinese participants (184 with HTG and 111 without HTG). Serum ISG15 levels were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, and associations with HTG were assessed using logistic regression, restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves. Findings were validated in high-fat diet (HFD)-induced HTG mouse through western blotting, immunohistochemistry, and histological analyses.

Results
