Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA) is a pervasive cardiovascular risk factor linked to accelerated aging. We investigated the underlying tissue-specific and systemic epigenetic mechanisms and the role of cellular senescence in the pathophysiology of OSA and associated cardiovascular disease (CVD).

Methods

C57BL/6J male mice were exposed to intermittent hypoxia (IH) or room air (RA) (n=25 mice/group) for 7 to 210 days. DNA methylation profiling was conducted on left cardiac ventricle and peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) and the impact of IH duration was studied using regression models. Epigenetic age acceleration (EAA) was calculated using a multi-tissue epigenetic clock. The role of p16-mediated senescence in IH-induced vascular dysfunction was assessed using transgenic mouse models (n=8 mice/group).

Results

IH exposures increased blood pressure and altered endothelial function in male mice. IH/RA differentially methylated positions (DMPs) were identified in left cardiac ventricle (n=5,747) and PBMCs (n=1,307), with minimal overlap (n=163, p=8.03 x 10-8). Both tissues differed in the EAA trajectory throughout the exposures. Epigenetic changes linked to cardiac dysfunction and cellular senescence, highlighting the Cdkn2a gene (encoding the p16 protein, a marker of cellular senescence). p16 expression was increased in aortic endothelial cells following IH. Systemic ablation of p16-expressing cells reversed IH-induced hypertension and restored coronary flow reserve.

Conclusions

IH induces duration-dependent, tissue-specific epigenetic dysregulation and accelerated biological aging with p16-mediated cellular senescence as a primary driver. Targeting the senescent endothelium can revert OSA-induced vascular dysfunction, thereby establishing a novel mechanistic framework for cellular senescence as a therapeutic target in OSA.

title: Tricuspid subvalvular apparatus involvement of ANCA-associated vasculitis: A diagnostic challenge mimicking infective endocarditis.
authorString: Khanfar A, Hoefen R, Biederman L, Ocon AJ.
abstractText: Antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated vasculitides (AAV) are small-vessel vasculitides with heterogeneous clinical manifestations. Cardiac valvular involvement is rare and may closely mimic infective endocarditis, posing significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. Tricuspid valve involvement, especially at the subvalvular apparatus, is particularly uncommon. We report a case of a 46-year-old man who presented with constitutional symptoms, pulmonary nodules with cavitation, acute kidney injury, venous thromboembolism, and positive c-ANCA with anti-proteinase-3 antibodies. Transesophageal echocardiography revealed a serpiginous vegetation attached to the tricuspid subvalvular apparatus, initially raising concern for infective endocarditis. However, extensive infectious evaluation, including multiple blood cultures, was negative. Kidney biopsy demonstrated pauci-immune crescentic and necrotizing glomerulonephritis, supporting a diagnosis of granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA). Antibiotics were discontinued, and the patient was treated with glucocorticoids, rituximab, and avacopan, resulting in marked clinical improvement. Follow-up echocardiography demonstrated complete resolution of the subvalvular apparatus vegetation without surgical intervention. This case highlights a rare presentation of GPA with tricuspid subvalvular apparatus involvement and underscores the importance of distinguishing AAV-related endocardial disease from infective endocarditis. Histopathologic findings, particularly renal biopsy, can be critical in establishing the correct diagnosis. Recognition of this entity is essential, as appropriate immunosuppressive therapy may lead to resolution of valvular lesions and avoidance of unnecessary antimicrobial therapy or surgical intervention.

title: Preferential Conduction Along the Epicardial Ventricular Septum During Idiopathic Ventricular Arrhythmias Originating From the Basal LV Summit: A Pitfall for Anatomical Ablation.
authorString: Yamada T, Mori S, Litovsky SH, Kay GN.
abstractText: An anatomical ablation of idiopathic ventricular arrhythmias (VAs) originating from the left ventricular summit (LVS) is delivered from endocardial sites across the myocardium adjacent to the site of the VA origin with the guidance of transvenous epicardial mapping. Therefore, electrophysiological information obtained by transvenous epicardial mapping should be carefully interpreted. This study investigated ventricular activation patterns within the great cardiac vein (GCV) during idiopathic LVS VAs. We studied 38 consecutive patients who underwent a successful endocardial ablation of idiopathic LVS VAs at the left ostial process, left coronary sinus, and commissure between the left and right coronary cusps. Twenty-nine patients exhibited a radial activation pattern in which the earliest ventricular activation was recorded around the junction between the GCV and anterior interventricular vein (AIVV). The remaining 9 patients exhibited a septal activation pattern in which the earliest ventricular activation was recorded within the AIVV, with the activation sequence being from the AIVV to GCV. The septal group mainly exhibited left bundle branch block pattern, whereas the radial group exhibited right bundle branch block pattern (P < 0.0001). The distance between the earliest ventricular activation site within the GCV or AIVV and the successful ablation site was significantly larger for LVS VAs with a septal activation pattern than those with a radial activation pattern. During idiopathic basal LVS VAs, activation from those VA origins often preferentially conducted along the ventricular septum. It should be kept in mind that this unusual activation pattern may mislead the mapping and catheter ablation of LVS VAs.

title: Prehospital Management of Pediatric Traumatic Out-of-Hospital Circulatory Arrest - A Joint Position Statement.
authorString: Anders JF, Harris MI, Adelgais KM, Remick KE, Cicero MX, Nagler J, Jaeger L, Knoles C, Pappas PA, Vaughan E.
abstractText: Policy statements and clinical policies are the official policies of the American College of Emergency Physicians and, as such, are not subject to the same peer review process as articles appearing in the journal. Policy statements and clinical policies of ACEP do not necessarily reflect the policies and beliefs of Annals of Emergency Medicine and its editors.

title: The broken heart (takotsubo) syndrome in orthopedics.
authorString: Katsanos S, Kafkas N, Vaishya R, Mavrogenis AF.
abstractText: The broken heart, or takotsubo syndrome, is a specific cardiomyopathy characterized by a striking morphological distortion of the left ventricle during an acute episode. Within the realm of non-cardiac surgeries, orthopedic procedures are increasingly recognized as primary triggers for perioperative takotsubo syndrome. Whether manifesting in the wake of high-energy traumatic skeletal disruption, an acute fragility hip fracture in an elderly individual, or during a meticulously planned elective total joint arthroplasty, takotsubo syndrome introduces an immediate, life-threatening challenge that can rapidly derail an otherwise successful orthopedic intervention. This article presents the epidemiology, clinical and laboratory findings of broken heart syndrome in orthopedic patients, and discusses the current management and outcome of these patients.

title: Physiological Impact of Chest Wall Closure in Infants Post-Cardiac Surgery. Implications for Mechanical Ventilation.
authorString: Rodriguez Guerineau L, Reise K, Floh A, Granton J, Feder J, Nonoyama M, Katira BH, Barron D, Foroutan F, Schwartz SM, Brochard L.

journal.title: Pediatric critical care medicine : a journal of the Society of Critical Care Medicine and the World Federation of Pediatric Intensive and Critical Care Societies

abstractText:
Objectives

To assess the effect of delayed sternal closure post-cardiac surgery on respiratory system mechanics and hemodynamics.

Design

Prospective single-center physiologic study.

Setting

Cardiac PICU.

Patients

Infants (< 1 yr old) with delayed sternal closure post-cardiopulmonary bypass for correction or palliation of a congenital heart disease.

Interventions

Four ventilation conditions were studied: 1) baseline: positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) 5 cm H2O and low tidal volume (Vt; 6-7 mL/kg); 2) PEEP 5, high Vt (9-10 mL/kg); 3) PEEP 3, low Vt; and 4) PEEP 8, low Vt. Respiratory rate was adjusted to end-tidal carbon dioxide. Measurements were repeated after sternal closure.

Measurements and main results

Esophageal pressure (Pes), transpulmonary pressure (PL), normalized respiratory system elastance (Ers) in cm H2O/(mL/kg), and hemodynamics, including transmural pressures, were obtained before and after sternal closure. The open-sternum model used assumes that the chest wall maintains a vertical pleural pressure gradient, with the most nondependent lung exposed to atmospheric pressure. A nondependent inspiratory PL greater than 23 cm H2O was used as a marker of overdistention, and end-expiratory PL 0-2 cm H2O was considered to prevent collapse. Ten patients were included: median (interquartile range) age 32 days (18-50 d) and weight 3.1 kg (3.0-3.5 kg). Chest closure increased Pes in all conditions and Ers in most conditions, except for PEEP 8 low Vt. Chest closure reduced expiratory PL in all conditions, at baseline from -0.5 cm H2O (-1.2 to -0.1 cm H2O) to -2.5 cm H2O (-3.1 to -1.8 cm H2O). Sternal closure impacted nondependent inspiratory PL differently depending on the ventilator settings. High Vt was the condition more frequently associated with high nondependent inspiratory PL greater than 23 cm H2O. Blood pressure was maintained with fluids or vasopressors. Central venous pressure increased after closure, but the transmural filling pressure remained unchanged.

Conclusions

Infants with delayed sternal closure exhibited elevated Pes and Ers after chest wall closure. Under the model assumptions, during the open-chest phase, high Vt was more frequently associated with high nondependent PL, suggesting overdistention. Sternal closure made expiratory PL more negative. These findings suggest that individualized PEEP and Vt adjustments guided by Pes could be considered to help preserve expiratory PL and minimize the risk of overdistension before and after chest closure.

title: The Current State of Ventilator Liberation Practices and Outcomes in the United States-A Report From the Ventilator Liberation For Kids (VentLib4Kids) Collaborative.
authorString: Loberger JM, Napolitano N, Gaies M, Mastropietro C, Steffen KM, Nishisaki A, Khemani RG, Abu-Sultaneh S.

journal.title: Pediatric critical care medicine : a journal of the Society of Critical Care Medicine and the World Federation of Pediatric Intensive and Critical Care Societies

abstractText: Describe and explore interunit baseline ventilator liberation practices and outcomes related to the 2023 Pediatric Ventilator Liberation Guidelines within the original cohort of Ventilation Liberation For Kids (VentLib4Kids) Collaborative units. Observational cohort study. Nineteen VentLib4Kids ICUs in the United States (13 general medical/surgical, five cardiovascular, and one mixed). First planned extubation attempt where code status allowed reintubation in patients younger than 19 years old, endotracheally intubated for any indication between July 1, 2023, and June 30, 2024. None. A total of 2315 ventilator courses were included. Most were 28 days to younger than 6 years old (65.5%) and had a lower respiratory infection diagnosis (23.8%). Prematurity (13.2%) was the most common comorbidity. Spontaneous breathing trial exposure demonstrated the highest guideline concordance at 74.6% (median; interunit range [IUR], 49.6-100%), whereas maximal inspiratory pressure testing was lowest (3.7%; IUR, 0-62.4%). Most courses (55.5%; IUR, 19.8-99%) included an air leak test. Among those without an air leak noted or greater than 25 cmH2O, 70.1% were exposed to dexamethasone in concordance with the guidelines. Initiation of dexamethasone greater than or equal to 6 hours before extubation predominated (81.1%) at a median dose of 0.5 mg/kg/dose in exposed groups. Planned postextubation high-flow nasal cannula (44.3%) and bilevel positive airway pressure (18.6%) were most common. Unit-level use of any planned postextubation noninvasive respiratory support ranged from 20.6% to 100%. Among infants, planned continuous positive airway pressure was used in 6.7% of subjects. Among all courses, 10.4% (IUR, 4.5-19.2%) ended with extubation failure (reintubation within 48 hr). Baseline VentLib4Kids practices demonstrate varying degrees of concordance with guideline recommendations along with significant interunit variation. These results align with prior international survey data and support the need for structured, multicenter quality improvement and guideline implementation strategies.

title: Totally endoscopic aortic valve replacement for quadricuspid aortic valve.
authorString: Iwakura T, Sakumoto K, Ono M, Yano A, Marui A, Nakahara Y.

journal.title: Multimedia manual of cardiothoracic surgery : MMCTS

abstractText: Quadricuspid aortic valve is a rare congenital anomaly that commonly presents with progressive aortic regurgitation and requires surgical valve replacement. Whether this anatomy can be safely addressed through a totally endoscopic approach has not been demonstrated in detail. We present a 62-year-old man with severe aortic regurgitation due to a Hurwitz-Roberts type A quadricuspid aortic valve who underwent totally endoscopic aortic valve replacement. The procedure was performed through a standardized three-port right thoracotomy with femoral arterial and venous cannulation under vacuum-assisted venous drainage. After transthoracic external aortic cross-clamping, myocardial protection was achieved with blood cardioplegia delivered directly into the coronary ostia, and the four-cusped valve was excised under three-dimensional endoscopic magnification. A 23 mm bovine pericardial bioprosthesis was implanted with 15 everting mattress sutures of coated polyester braid, secured with automated titanium fasteners. The patient was extubated soon after the operation and discharged on postoperative Day 10. Echocardiography at 3.5 months confirmed normal prosthetic function with a mean gradient of 14 mmHg and progressive left ventricular reverse remodelling. This video tutorial illustrates a reproducible step-by-step workflow for totally endoscopic aortic valve replacement applied to quadricuspid aortic valve, and provides practical guidance for surgeons encountering this anatomy.

title: One-stage open repair of the aortic arch and descending thoracic aorta through a left thoracotomy.
authorString: Guzmán S X, Ascaso M, Pruna-Guillen R, Gasser S, Mancebon F, Quintana E.

journal.title: Multimedia manual of cardiothoracic surgery : MMCTS

abstractText: Extensive aortic aneurysm disease presents a significant therapeutic challenge, requiring individualized management based on aneurysm morphology, anatomical location and patient comorbidities. Treatment options include open surgical repair, endovascular techniques or hybrid approaches. The choice between a simultaneous or staged strategy must balance the risks inherent to each. Staged repair may decrease operative complexity but can be unsuitable for rapidly enlarging aneurysms due to the increased risk of rupture between procedures. Conversely, a single-stage intervention entails longer operative and ischaemic times, greater bleeding risk and the need for wider exposure. Presented here is the case of a 79-year-old male with extensive aneurysmal disease involving the aortic arch (43 × 39 mm) and distal descending thoracic aorta (66 × 56 mm). Surgical treatment was indicated due to rapid aneurysm expansion (>5 mm/year). Anatomical characteristics were unfavourable for endovascular repair, and a staged approach was deemed inappropriate given rapid growth and complex anatomy. Therefore, a one-stage replacement of the aortic arch and descending thoracic aorta (zones 1-5) was performed under hypothermic circulatory arrest through a left thoracotomy, with reconstruction of the left carotid and left subclavian arteries. Postoperative recovery was uneventful, and at 1-year follow-up the patient remains clinically and radiologically stable.

title: Minimally invasive aortic valve replacement through right anterior thoracotomy with concomitant thoracoscopic ablation.
authorString: Vleeschouwer B, Soenens G, Ballaux P, Cathenis K, Fleerakkers J, François J.

journal.title: Multimedia manual of cardiothoracic surgery : MMCTS

abstractText: Both minimally invasive aortic valve replacement through right anterior thoracotomy and thoracoscopic ablation are safe and feasible techniques with proven results in terms of long-term survival, a reduced postoperative recovery period and continued freedom from disease. The combination of these techniques has not yet been documented. Here, a rib-sparing right anterior thoracotomy with percutaneous femoral cannulation and aortic valve replacement was combined with a left thoracoscopic ablation using bipolar radiofrequency energy and left atrial appendage closure with epicardial occlusion device was performed. This video tutorial depicts the surgical approach and presents short-term outcomes of a small case series.

title: Type 3 aortopulmonary window: surgical repair technique.
authorString: Alkhalifa F, Alalyani Y, Almannaei L, Rahmani B, Awan A, Schweiger M, Alomair M.

journal.title: Multimedia manual of cardiothoracic surgery : MMCTS

abstractText: A 2-week-old, 3.5 kg neonate presented with congestive heart failure and a cardiac murmur. Echocardiography demonstrated a large type III aortopulmonary window associated with a large secundum atrial septal defect. Biventricular systolic function was normal, the pulmonary valve was competent, and both branch pulmonary arteries were well formed. No coronary artery anomalies were identified. Through a median sternotomy, cardiopulmonary bypass was established with aortic and bicaval cannulation, and the branch pulmonary arteries were controlled. Following aortic cross-clamping and cardioplegic arrest, the window was exposed, allowing direct visualization of the defect margins, coronary artery origins, branch pulmonary arteries and pulmonary valve. The aortopulmonary septum was reconstructed with a bovine pericardial patch, preserving branch pulmonary artery alignment and avoiding distortion or obstruction. The atrial septal defect was partially closed, leaving an approximately 4 mm fenestration. The patient was weaned from cardiopulmonary bypass. Cardiopulmonary bypass and aortic cross-clamp times were 67 and 49 minutes, respectively, and total operative time was 3 hours. Long-term follow-up was unavailable. This case illustrates patch repair of a large type III aortopulmonary window under direct visualization of adjacent structures, with attention to preserving great vessel geometry and branch pulmonary artery. Long-term outcomes could not be assessed because follow-up data were unavailable.

title: Investigation of the potential mechanisms associated with the effects of the novel 2-trifluoromethyl-4-aminoquinazoline derivative KZL-064 on vascular endothelial injury.
authorString: Cui X, Zhang Q, Li J, Guan Z, Zhu W, Xu L, Sun G.

journal.title: Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine

abstractText: BackgroundCoronary atherosclerotic heart disease is a major cardiovascular disease that poses a serious threat to human health. Quinazoline derivatives possess diverse biological activities and considerable structural modifiability, making them valuable candidates for drug development.ObjectiveThis study aimed to investigate the potential mechanism by which the novel 2-trifluoromethyl-4-aminoquinazoline derivative KZL-064 protects against vascular endothelial injury.MethodsNetwork pharmacology, single-cell transcriptomic analysis, and functional experiments were integrated to identify and prioritize a candidate functional target of KZL-064. An oscillatory shear stress-induced endothelial cell injury model was established to evaluate the protective effects of KZL-064. The functional involvement of the candidate target was further examined through HDAC1 overexpression and knockdown experiments.ResultsHDAC1 was identified as a prioritized candidate functional target potentially associated with the effects of KZL-064 and was significantly upregulated in atherosclerotic lesions. HDAC1 overexpression aggravated endothelial injury, whereas KZL-064 markedly alleviated oscillatory shear stress-induced damage. This protective effect was substantially diminished following HDAC1 knockdown. Further analysis indicated that KZL-064 was associated with the partial restoration of endothelial homeostasis and the modulation of inflammatory and cell cycle-related genes in an HDAC1-related context.ConclusionKZL-064 alleviates OSS-induced endothelial cell injury and is associated with modulation of inflammatory and cell cycle-related genes. HDAC1 was identified as a prioritized candidate functional target potentially involved in the action of KZL-064. These findings suggest potential relevance to atherosclerosis-associated endothelial dysfunction, while direct HDAC1 binding, enzymatic inhibition, target selectivity, and in vivo anti-atherosclerotic efficacy remain to be established.

title: Interdisciplinary Collaboration as Key Factor for the Optimization of Advanced Heart Failure Treatment.
authorString: Berliner D, Arima N, Jakstaite AM, Dogan G, Hanke JS, Bavendiek U, Soltani S, Knigge S, Schmack B, Ruhparwar A, Bauersachs J, Schmitto JD.
abstractText: Heart failure (HF) remains a major global health problem, with outcomes in advanced stages continuing to be poor despite the development of medical therapy and interventional strategies. This report proposes the concept of Interdisciplinary Heart Failure Collaboration (IHFC), a structured framework designed to optimize patient outcomes through coordinated, cross-sectoral care, focusing on the management of advanced HF. The IHFC integrates a broad spectrum of healthcare professionals-including cardiologists, cardiac surgeons, nurses, anesthesiologists, intensivists, psychologists, ventricular assist device (VAD) coordinators, and many others-to provide optimal care from outpatient diagnosis to post-discharge long-term management. The model consists of three core management phases: 1) pre-hospital management, which includes outpatient clinic visits, accurate diagnosis and timely referral; 2) intra-hospital management, comprising interventional and surgical treatment including durable VAD implantation and heart transplantation; 3) post-discharge management; post-interventional and post-operative care, rehabilitation and long-term follow-up, patient education and support for self-care. In addition, this report discusses current challenges in implementation, including the need for standardized protocols and effective communication among team members. Rather than replacing existing HF care systems, the IHFC provides a practical framework for integrating established multidisciplinary principles across the entire clinical trajectory of advanced HF and may be adapted to different healthcare settings.

title: Direct and Indirect Mechanisms of Cardiac Dysfunction Following Severe Acute Kidney Injury in Rats.
authorString: Boykin O, Bryant M, Mosley O, Oglesby O, Moronge D, Buncha V, Sun J, Bagi Z, Polichnowski AJ, O'Connor PM.
abstractText: Acute renocardiac syndrome (cardiorenal syndrome type 3) occurs when acute kidney injury (AKI) leads to acute cardiac dysfunction. The objective of this study was to determine the effects of severe AKI on cardiac function in rats and to distinguish changes driven by kidney injury from those resulting from loss of renal function.  Studies were performed in male and female Sprague-Dawley rats. Animals underwent unilateral nephrectomy (Sham), unilateral nephrectomy combined with 45 minutes of renal ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI), or bilateral nephrectomy (NX). Cardiac function was assessed by echocardiography 24 or 48 hours after surgery. Blood and tissues were collected for biochemical and histological analyses. Body, heart, and lung weights did not differ among groups, whereas kidney weight was significantly increased following IRI. At 24 hours, diastolic filling velocities were significantly elevated in IRI rats compared with Sham and NX animals, but these differences resolved by 48 hours. In contrast, indices of enhanced systolic contractility were observed in both IRI and NX groups. These changes tended to normalize in IRI animals but persisted or worsened in NX rats over time. NX rats also developed significant metabolic and electrolyte abnormalities, including reduced blood pH, bicarbonate, sodium, calcium, and hematocrit, together with elevated potassium concentrations. Diastolic dysfunction occurred only in the presence of an injured kidney, whereas systolic alterations were observed following both IRI and bilateral nephrectomy. These findings suggest that kidney injury and loss of renal function contribute to distinct components of acute renocardiac syndrome.

title: Three-Year Outcomes of Endovascular Therapy Using Covered Stent-Grafts Versus Interwoven Nitinol Stents in Severely Calcified Femoropopliteal Artery Disease From a Retrospective Multicenter Registry.
authorString: Horie K, Takahara M, Nakama T, Tanaka A, Tobita K, Hayakawa N, Mori S, Iwata Y, Suzuki K.

journal.title: Journal of endovascular therapy : an official journal of the International Society of Endovascular Specialists

abstractText:
Purpose

This study aimed to compare the long-term safety and efficacy of Viabahn covered stent-grafts (CSG) and Supera peripheral stents (SPS) in calcified femoropopliteal artery lesions.

Materials and methods

We retrospectively analyzed 341 cases who had Rutherford class 2 to 6 peripheral artery disease and underwent endovascular therapy (EVT) with either CSG (n = 137) or SPS (n = 204) for femoropopliteal lesions with bilateral calcification assessed by fluoroscopic image based on Peripheral Arterial Calcium Scoring System classification, between April 2017 and February 2021 at 7 cardiovascular centers in our country.

Results

Following propensity score (PS) matching, the final study population comprised 142 matched patients with no remarkable intergroup difference in baseline characteristics. The 3-year primary patency was 70.9% in the CSG group and 56.2% in the SPS group, respectively, and was not statistically different (P = .083). Moreover, no significant difference was noted in freedom from target lesion revascularization (72.8% vs 63.5%, P = .16), limb salvage rate (100.0% vs 96.2%, P = .32), and overall survival rate (67.6% vs 66.6%, P = .61). Stratification analysis revealed that advanced age and current smoking had a significant interaction on the association of CSG versus SPS implantation with restenosis (interaction P < .05).

Conclusion

In patients with severely calcified femoropopliteal lesions, the 3-year primary patency was not significantly different between EVT using CSG and SPS following PS matching.Clinical ImpactSevere calcification in femoropopliteal disease remains a challenge for EVT. Covered stent-graft and SPS are reliable devices for calcified femoropopliteal lesions. We compared the 3-year outcomes in patients undergoing EVT using either CSG or SPS. Following the propensity matching, the 3-year primary patency was not different at 70.0% and 56.2% (P = .083) in the CSG (n = 71) and SPS (n = 71) groups, respectively. Moreover, no significant difference was noted in freedom from target lesion revascularization and limb salvage rate.

title: Hybrid Repair of a True Left Subclavian Artery Aneurysm After Coronary Bypass: A Tailored Strategy to Avoid Pitfalls.
authorString: Brizzi S, Barillà D, Baronetto N, Salvioni R, Civilini E.

journal.title: Journal of endovascular therapy : an official journal of the International Society of Endovascular Specialists

abstractText: True subclavian artery aneurysms are rare and clinically and technically challenging, particularly when located proximal to a patent left internal mammary artery (LIMA) coronary bypass, where preservation of myocardial perfusion is mandatory. We report the case of a 75-year-old man with an incidentally detected left subclavian artery aneurysm located just proximal to a patent LIMA-left anterior descending artery bypass. Previous sternotomy and left thoracotomy precluded conventional open repair, while the absence of adequate proximal and distal landing zones ruled out a conventional endovascular approach. A single-stage hybrid strategy was therefore adopted, consisting of a carotid-subclavian bypass via a supraclavicular approach, distal aneurysm exclusion using a vascular plug, and final proximal exclusion with a thoracic endograft. The postoperative course was uneventful, and the patient was discharged on postoperative day 3. At 6-month follow-up, computed tomography angiography demonstrated complete aneurysm exclusion, patency of the carotid-subclavian bypass and the LIMA graft, and preserved vertebral artery flow. This case highlights how a carefully planned hybrid repair can represent a safe and effective option for complex proximal subclavian artery aneurysms in patients with prior coronary bypass surgery.Clinical ImpactIn patients with a patent LIMA-LAD bypass, repairing a proximal left subclavian artery aneurysm comes down to one priority: myocardial perfusion must never be interrupted. This case offers a practical framework for avoiding the main pitfalls. Revascularization must come before exclusion, and every step should be planned to preserve coronary flow, from clamping to plug placement to endograft coverage. Following this sequence allows a complex repair to be performed safely with off-the-shelf devices.

title: Right Ventricular Cardiomyocyte Dysfunction and Arrhythmogenesis in a Bleomycin-induced Mouse Model of Group 3 Pulmonary Hypertension.
authorString: Behrmann AJ, Roselli S, Shahid A, Nyanyo K, Patel A, Hayden MR, Cayton J, Norton CE, Domeier TL.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol
journal.title: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
journal.isoabbreviation: Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol

abstractText: Group 3 pulmonary hypertension (PH) occurs when lung diseases induce hypoxic vasoconstriction and pulmonary vascular remodeling. The increase in pulmonary vascular resistance elevates right ventricular (RV) afterload leading to progressive ventricular dysfunction. The mechanisms underlying cardiomyocyte dysfunction in Group 3 PH remain poorly characterized, despite RV pathology representing a critical component of disease progression. Using a mouse model of intratracheal bleomycin-induced PH, we tested the hypothesis that RV function and cardiomyocyte excitation-contraction coupling (ECC) are impaired in PH. Male and female mice were administered intratracheal saline (Sham) or bleomycin to induce PH and assess for sex differences across cardiac parameters. Langendorff-perfused working heart preparations revealed that PH mice display greater RV pressure development, elevated end diastolic pressure, and more spontaneous ventricular arrhythmias versus Sham. Structurally, hearts of PH mice exhibited increased RV hypertrophy and fibrosis versus Sham, with the hypertrophic response more pronounced in males versus females. To assess Ca2+ dynamics and cellular contractile function, enzymatically isolated cardiomyocytes were subjected to electrical field stimulation (0.5-4 Hz, fura-2 dye). RV cardiomyocyte ECC was impaired in PH versus Sham mice, including elevated diastolic Ca2+ and shorter diastolic sarcomere lengths, depressed Ca2+ transient and sarcomere contraction amplitudes, and slower Ca2+ decay rates with slower sarcomere relaxation. Left ventricular (LV) cardiomyocytes did not display these changes. Taken together, these data indicate impairment in RV ECC in the bleomycin-induced PH model, highlighting multiple Ca2+ handling abnormalities that may contribute to the RV dysfunction and arrhythmogenesis observed clinically in PH.

title: The K<sup>+</sup>-dependent Na<sup>+</sup>/Ca<sup>2+</sup>-exchanger 4 is localized to intracellular membranes and modulates Ca<sup>2+</sup> signaling and proteostasis in choroid plexus epithelial cells.
authorString: Hassan MT, Sharma S, Lytton J.

journal.title: American journal of physiology. Cell physiology

abstractText: Na+/Ca2++K+-exchangers (NCKX) are a family of five membrane proteins that transport 1 Ca2+ and 1 K+ in exchange for 4 Na+ ions. The fourth member, NCKX4, is widely expressed in the body and contributes to several neuronal functions including olfaction, vision, memory and satiety. We recently showed that NCKX4 in brain is expressed at intracellular sites in choroid plexus epithelial cells (CPECs), despite being mostly localized to the plasma membrane in other brain regions. In this study, we extend our investigation of NCKX4 in light of this unexpected localization to examine its intracellular distribution and physiological role in CPECs. The NCKX4 protein expressed in CPECs contains an additional 19 amino acids due to alternative splicing, and immunolabeling indicated that it localizes to small acidic compartments likely associated with secretory and/or endosomal pathways. Loss of NCKX4 did not lead to detectable changes in CPEC ultrastructure or ventricular volume. However, proteomic screening of choroid plexus tissues from wildtype and Nckx4-/- mice showed alterations in protein abundance and expression profiles, while cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) proteomic profiles and ionic concentrations remained unchanged. Interestingly, we found consistent sex-dependent differences in both choroid plexus and CSF proteomes, primarily involving immune-related proteins. CPECs lacking NCKX4 displayed similar Ca2+ signal dynamics to wildtype controls under baseline conditions, but showed a slower decay of the Ca2+ signal following strong serotonin stimulation. Together, these data highlight the intracellular localization of NCKX4, its contribution to Ca2+ handling in CPECs, and its novel role in protein homeostasis in the choroid plexus.

title: Sex-Specific Association of Estrone-Estradiol Balance With B-Type Natriuretic Peptide in Older Adults With Heart Failure.
authorString: Nakamura S, Numata G, Tokiwa H, Taguchi A, Toyoda M, Kohno T, Maki H, Shiraishi Y, Takeuchi S, Goda A, Daigo K, Yamamoto N, Adachi Y, Kato T, Kawahara T, Ueda K, Amiya E, Hatano M, Fujita H, Ieda M, Hiroi Y, Kato N, Sasano T, Takeda N, Kohro T, Hirota Y, Komuro I, Wada Y, Takimoto E.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol
journal.title: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
journal.isoabbreviation: Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol

abstractText: Estrone (E1), the predominant circulating estrogen after menopause, may exert biological effects distinct from, and potentially opposite to, those of estradiol (E2), raising the possibility that the relative E1/E2 balance has physiological significance. However, the clinical significance of the E1/E2 balance in heart failure (HF) remains unknown. We investigated the associations of circulating E1, E2, and their balance with B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) by sex. We analyzed a multicenter cross-sectional cohort of 260 adults aged 60-89 years (102 men and 68 women with HF; 49 men and 41 women without HF). Associations with ln(BNP) were evaluated using multivariable models with sex interactions. E1 and E2 were analyzed separately and jointly, and the joint model was reparameterized into the E1/E2 balance [ln(E1/E2)] and overall estrogen level [ln√(E1×E2)]. Neither E1 nor E2 was significantly associated with ln(BNP) in separate models. However, in joint models, E1 and E2 showed opposite associations after mutual adjustment, which were reversed between sexes. The E1/E2 balance was positively associated with ln(BNP) in men (β=0.828; P=0.003) but negatively associated in women (β=-0.961; P=0.010) (sex interaction P<0.001). In contrast, overall estrogen level was not associated with ln(BNP) in either sex. Among participants without HF, no sex-dependent pattern was observed, and the balance-by-sex association differed according to HF status (three-way interaction P=0.010). These findings suggest that the E1/E2 balance, rather than overall estrogen level, is a sex-specific hormonal correlate of BNP in older adults with HF.

title: Apo(a) Determines Cell State and Plaque Composition in Advanced Atherosclerotic Lesions in Mice.
authorString: Assini JM, Pang S, Chuecos MA, Lagor WR, Andrews T, Boffa MB, Koschinsky ML.
abstractText:
Background

Elevated Lp(a) (lipoprotein[a]) is an independent and causal risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, and patients with high Lp(a) demonstrate more severe plaque pathology. However, the mechanism driving the impact of Lp(a) on atherogenesis in vivo remains unclear.

Methods

We generated transgenic mice expressing human apo(a) (LPA), which forms a noncovalent complex with mouse apo B100, and compared them to wild-type mice. After 6 or 24 weeks of a high-fat, high-cholesterol diet and hepatic Ldlr knockdown, atherosclerotic lesion composition by histopathologic staining and immunofluorescence imaging was assessed. Single-cell RNA-sequencing of 24-week lesions was performed to identify the cell types within the atherosclerotic plaque, differentially expressed genes, and biological pathways affected by the LPA transgene.

Results

High apo(a) levels in both sexes of LPA mice significantly increased lesion area in the aortic sinus compared with wild-type controls after 24 weeks of feeding. LPA mice demonstrated more severe atherosclerosis features, such as increased necrotic area and oxidized phospholipid deposition, increased calcification, and disorganized collagen accumulation in a thinner fibrous cap. Our single-cell RNA-sequencing analysis revealed that the greatest transcriptomic effects in LPA mice occurred in resident-like macrophages, whereby gene signatures associated with smooth muscle cell differentiation, extracellular matrix/actin organization, and TGF-β (transforming growth factor-beta) signaling were upregulated and immune-response/chemokine signaling programs were downregulated. Reclustering of resident-like macrophages revealed a subpopulation that, in addition to myeloid markers, expresses mesenchymal/stromal-associated genes; RNA velocity analysis revealed that these cells were in a transitionary cell state, resembling a more mesenchymal phenotype compared with classically defined resident-like macrophages. This differentiation phenomenon is known as macrophage to mesenchymal/myofibroblast transition. Moreover, we found increased abundance of transitionary macrophage to mesenchymal/myofibroblast transition cells within lesions from LPA mice compared with wild-type mice.

Conclusions

Our data establish a novel role for apo(a) in macrophage to mesenchymal/myofibroblast transition as a possible contributor to the proatherosclerotic effects of Lp(a).

title: Clonal hematopoiesis and the risk of major age-related eye diseases.
authorString: Xie R, Finger RP, Garzone D, Peng L, Brenner H, Schöttker B.
abstractText: Clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP), an age-related hematologic condition associated with systemic inflammation, has uncertain associations with major eye diseases. We aimed to investigate the association of CHIP, including its major genetic subtypes and clone sizes, with the risk of cataract, glaucoma, age-related macular degeneration (AMD), and diabetic retinopathy (DR). UK Biobank participants enrolled during 2006-2010 were followed by linked electronic health records until March 2022. Whole-exome sequencing identified CHIP as somatic driver mutations with variant allele frequency ≥ 2%. Multivariable Cox regression was applied to assess hazard ratios (HR) with 95% confidence intervals (95%CI). The DR analysis was restricted to participants with diabetes. Of 436,469 participants (mean age, 56.4 years; 54.5% women), 14,110 (3.2%) had CHIP. During a median 14.4-year follow-up, 31,165 cataract, 12,393 glaucoma, 13,644 AMD, and 2,692 DR diagnoses occurred. CHIP was associated with cataract (HR [95%CI]: 1.08 [1.03-1.14]), AMD (HR [95%CI]: 1.12 [1.04-1.21]), and DR (HR [95%CI]: 1.48 [1.25-1.74]), but the association with glaucoma overall did not reach statistical significance (HR [95%CI]: 1.08 [0.99-1.17]). The glaucoma association was statistically significant among participants without hypertension (HR [95%CI]: 1.22 [1.06-1.40]; P for interaction = 0.012). Associations varied by clone size and driver gene. Hematologic and inflammatory biomarkers mediated less than 5% of associations. CHIP was associated with incident cataract, AMD, and DR, and with glaucoma in participants without hypertension. These findings position CHIP as a potential non-ocular risk marker for several major age-related eye diseases. However, except for DR, effect sizes were small.

title: [Stress factors and coping strategies in the nursing and care of patients with a left ventricular assist device (LVAD) suffering from treatment-resistant heart failure-a qualitative study of nursing staff in German intensive care units].
authorString: Deumler ML, Trummer A, Koch S.
abstractText:
Background

Critical care nurses play a vital role in the care of patients with a left ventricular assist device (LVAD) and must be able to cope with various challenges. The aim of this study was to gain insight into the experiences of critical care nurses in caring for patients with a LVAD, to identify potential stressors, and thereby to determine the need for support.

Methods

As part of a qualitative research design, nine intensive care nurses from Germany were interviewed between April and June 2025 using semi-structured, guided interviews. Data analysis was conducted using content analysis structured according to Kuckartz.

Results

The greatest challenges for intensive care nurses were a lack of knowledge regarding the specific nursing requirements and the use of the LVAD, as well as structural and personnel-related conditions. While coping strategies are already in place, the majority of nurses would like to expand their knowledge.

Conclusion

By identifying various stressors, specific support services can be expanded or established for everyday clinical practice. Potential measures include building and regularly updating foundational knowledge through structured training programs, as well as ensuring that counseling services are readily available. In addition, specialized communication training and standardized work procedures are recommended.

title: Clinical Characteristics and 2-Year Follow-Up of Patients With Takayasu Arteritis and Pulmonary Artery Involvement.
authorString: Sevik G, Abacar K, Avcu A, Kocakaya D, Baltacioglu F, Direskeneli H, Alibaz-Oner F.
abstractText:
Background & aim

The frequency of pulmonary arterial (PA) involvement (PAI) in Takayasu arteritis (TAK) has been reported to range from 14.0% to 57.0%. PAI may be associated with a worse prognosis; therefore, early detection and treatment of PAI may improve the disease course. This study assessed the characteristics and follow-up of TAK patients with PAI.

Method

Seventy-two TAK patients (62 female, 10 male) who underwent computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA) to investigate PAI were included. A radiologist reviewed CTPA images, and PAI was characterised by increased pulmonary artery wall thickness, stenosis, and/or thrombosis.

Results

The mean age was 46.4±13.0 years, and nine patients had active disease. The treatments for TAK were immunosuppressives (IS) in 62 (86.1%), biological treatment in 25 (34.7%), glucocorticoids (GCs) in 30 (41.7%), and acetylsalicylic acid (ASA) in 50 (69.4%) patients. Twenty-two (30.6%) patients had pulmonary symptoms, most commonly dyspnoea and chest pain. PAI was detected in 13 (18.1%) patients, and PA thrombosis unrelated to vasculitis was present in five (6.9%) patients. Among PAI patients, IS treatment was changed in nine (69.2%), GC dose was increased in eight (61.5%), and anticoagulants were started in seven (53.8%). Pulmonary symptoms (92.3% vs 16.9%), C-reactive protein (CRP) (25.8 vs 4.0 mg/L), and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) (34.5 vs 16.2 mm/h) values were significantly higher in patients with PAI (p<0.001, p=0.001, p=0.008). PAI was significantly lower in patients using ASA (30.8% vs 69.2%) (p=0.002). After 2 years of follow-up, one patient with PAI had a relapse of TAK and three patients had chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension.

Conclusions

PAI was present in 18.1% of TAK patients, and pulmonary symptoms, higher ESR and CRP values, and less frequent ASA use were associated with PAI.

title: International expert Delphi consensus on the management of metabolic dysfunction- and alcohol-associated liver disease (MetALD).
authorString: Idalsoaga F, Khan MQ, Alkhouri N, Rinella M, Wong VW, Lee BP, Isaacs S, Maiwall R, Moeller G, Winder S, Chen VL, Krag A, Moreno C, Cortez-Pinto H, Kulkarni AV, Mellinger J, Trepo E, Shubrook J, Im G, Cusi K, Bansal M, Haque L, Louvet A, Israelsen M, Noureddin M, Sanyal A, Arrese M, Díaz LA, Bril F, Arab JP.
abstractText:
Introduction and objectives

Metabolic dysfunction- and alcohol-associated liver disease (MetALD) describes steatotic liver disease in individuals with cardiometabolic dysfunction and alcohol consumption. As MetALD-specific evidence remains limited, practical guidance is needed for diagnosis, fibrosis assessment, alcohol use disorder management, cardiometabolic treatment, and transplant evaluation.

Materials and methods

We conducted a two-round modified Delphi study with an international multidisciplinary expert panel. Statements were developed after a targeted literature review and organized into four domains: diagnosis and disease stratification, alcohol use assessment and alcohol use disorder treatment, metabolic and cardiometabolic management, and liver transplant assessment. Statements were rated on a five-point Likert scale. Consensus agreement was predefined as a median score ≥4, ≥70% of ratings in the 4-5 range, and interquartile range ≤1.

Results

All 30 experts from 10 countries participated in round 1, and 29 (97%) in round 2. In round 1, 31 of 33 statements met agreement criteria; two were revised and re-evaluated. After round 2, consensus was achieved for all statements. The panel recognized MetALD as having dual metabolic and alcohol-related drivers and endorsed systematic cardiometabolic assessment, longitudinal quantification of alcohol intake, selective use of direct alcohol biomarkers, and stepwise noninvasive fibrosis risk stratification. Recommended care integrates individualized goals for alcohol reduction or abstinence, evidence-based alcohol use disorder treatment, structured lifestyle intervention, weight loss, physical activity, and optimization of diabetes, dyslipidemia, and hypertension. Transplant assessment should be individualized and multidisciplinary.

Conclusions

This consensus provides practical recommendations for integrated MetALD care and identifies priorities for future clinical research and external validation.

title: DESCRIPTION OF TREATMENT PATTERNS AND POPULATION CHARACTERISTICS OF PRE-DIALYSIS CKD PATIENTS IN THE NEPHROSCREEN SURVEY.
authorString: Vachek J, Oulehle K, Pejřilová D, Vařejková M, Doležal T, Ryšavá R, Lapka M.

journal.title: Journal of renal nutrition : the official journal of the Council on Renal Nutrition of the National Kidney Foundation

abstractText:
Objective

To characterize real-world clinical practice, patient profiles, and the use of ketoanalogue (KA)-supplemented low-protein diets (LPD) (KA+LPD) in dialysis-naïve patients with advanced chronic kidney disease (CKD) in the Czech Republic.

Methods

This multicenter cross-sectional observational survey included adult patients with CKD stages 4-5 not yet on dialysis, recruited from 18 nephrology outpatient clinics and dialysis centers between April and November 2022. Clinical, laboratory, anthropometric, and nutritional data were collected from medical records and patient questionnaires. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize data, and multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify factors associated with prescription of KA therapy. A sensitivity analysis accounted for physician-level clustering.

Results

A total of 792 patients were included (mean age 72.7±12.3 years; 54.9% male). Most patients had CKD stage 4 (76.4%), with a mean eGFR of 18.0 ± 6.0 ml/min/1.73 m2. KA were prescribed in 38.1% of patients. In multivariable logistic regression, KA prescription was associated with CKD stage 5 (OR 3.30, p <0.001), lower serum albumin, hypertension as CKD etiology, and lower medication burden, while older age was generally associated with a lower likelihood of prescription. Patients receiving KA had lower eGFR and higher urea and creatinine levels but showed no evidence of worse nutritional or metabolic status compared with non-users.

Conclusion

KA use in advanced CKD is common but varies substantially and appears influenced by both patient characteristics and physician-level practice patterns. In this cross-sectional cohort, KA-treated patients showed no evidence of worse nutritional or metabolic status compared with non-users; however, prospective studies are needed to evaluate longitudinal clinical outcomes.

title: Progressive corneal denervation in Pitx2-associated developmental glaucoma with female-predominant corneal remodeling.
authorString: Sarkis S, Dumon L, Girard M, Megido AC, Cazvieille C, Schverer M, Daien V, Johansen B, Chamard C, Delettre C, Michon F.
abstractText: Pitx2-associated developmental glaucoma is characterized by anterior segment dysgenesis, ocular hypertension, and optic neuropathy, but its consequences for corneal sensory innervation remain poorly defined. We examined male and female Pitx2<sup>egl1/egl1</sup> and Pitx2<sup>+/+</sup> mice at 1 and 3 months using intraocular pressure measurements, fundus imaging, visual evoked potentials, optic nerve ultrastructure, corneal βIII-tubulin whole-mount imaging, mechanical sensitivity testing, and bulk RNA sequencing of corneas and trigeminal ganglia. Mutant mice developed ocular hypertension, posterior segment abnormalities, reduced visual evoked potential amplitudes, and optic nerve degeneration. Corneal epithelial nerve fiber volume was preserved at 1 month but reduced in both sexes at 3 months, indicating progressive denervation in an untreated genetic model. Mechanical sensitivity was reduced in mutant males, whereas female values did not differ detectably between genotypes. Factorial transcriptomic analysis included sex, genotype, and their interaction. Female mutant corneas showed 634 strict differentially expressed genes, with enrichment of complement, cytokine, extracellular matrix, focal adhesion, p53-related, glycan, and metabolic pathways. No comparably robust gene set was detected in male corneas. Additional diagnostics indicated small male genotype effects at the gene level and a diffuse aggregate sex-conditioned signal that was not resolved at single-gene false-discovery-rate level. Whole-mount KRT17 immunolabeling showed expansion of the KRT17-positive epithelial domain in female mutant corneas, providing orthogonal spatial support for an epithelial remodeling component of this signature. Whole-trigeminal-ganglion bulk RNA-seq detected few significant changes, but dilution of cornea-projecting neurons within the whole ganglion precludes concluding that these neurons were unresponsive. These findings identify progressive corneal denervation as an underrecognized component of Pitx2-associated developmental glaucoma and define female-predominant corneal remodeling as a hypothesis-generating molecular feature rather than a proven sex-specific mechanism.

title: Early Childhood CASPR2 Autoimmunity with Prominent Autonomic Dysfunction: Diagnostic Challenges and Effective Immunotherapy.
authorString: Ehl CS, Berger SD, Meyer-Ruhnke L, Schlotawa L, Kettwig M, Gaertner J, Marten LM.
abstractText: CASPR2-associated neurological diseases cover a broad clinical spectrum, with limbic encephalitis and Morvan syndrome representing the most characteristic autoimmune phenotypes. We report the case of a 2-year-old boy who presented with abdominal and generalized pain, refusal to eat or drink, weight loss, loss of mobility, and behavioral changes, including sleep disturbances. Further clinical evaluation revealed pharmacoresistant arterial hypertension and hyperhidrosis. Extensive diagnostic testing excluded infectious and toxic causes. CASPR2 antibodies were detected in both serum and cerebrospinal fluid. Initial therapy with corticosteroids and intravenous immunoglobulins resulted in only minimal clinical improvement. Significant clinical recovery was only achieved after escalation of immunotherapy with plasmapheresis and subsequent B-cell-depleting therapy with rituximab. At the most recent follow-up visit, seven months after the first rituximab infusion, the patient showed complete recovery without residual symptoms. This case underscores the diagnostic challenges of CASPR2-associated autoimmunity in early childhood and highlights the importance of early recognition of this rare but treatable disease.

title: Snapshot of pregnancy Hypertension and Preeclampsia content on TikTok - a look at themes and quality.
authorString: Sarker M, Jacobs E, Wiley R, Katlaps I, Emeruwa UN.
abstractText:
Objective

We analyzed the most viewed hypertensive disorders of pregnancy content on TikTok, specifically characterizing the themes, assessing the quality, and determining how metrics differs for healthcare provider created content.

Study design

We conducted a cross-sectional study of the top 100 English videos by play count using the hashtags #preeclampsia, #preeclampsiaawareness, #gestationalhypertension, #pregnancyhypertension, #eclampsia, and #postpartumhypertension. Videos were generated using the TikTok Data Extractor by Apify.

Main outcome measures

The primary outcome was content quality via the Global Quality Score (GQS) - a validated tool ranging from 1 (low, use discouraged) to 5 (high, medically useful). Secondary outcomes included the number of videos relevant to the hashtag, and assessments of medical claims content using mDISCERN. Secondary analysis included sub-stratifying by healthcare provider status.

Results

Of the top 600 videos across all hashtags, 527 (87.8%) were relevant and 109 (20.7%) videos were created by healthcare providers. The median [interquartile range (IQR)] GQS for all videos was 1 (Anonymous. Gestational Hypertension and Preeclampsia: ACOG Practice Bulletin, Number 222. Obstet Gynecol [Internet]., 2020; Williamson et al., 2023 [1,3]) suggesting videos were low quality and not useful. The GQS for healthcare provider content was higher (3 [1.5,3] versus 1 (Anonymous. Gestational Hypertension and Preeclampsia: ACOG Practice Bulletin, Number 222. Obstet Gynecol [Internet]., 2020; Khosla et al., 2021 [1,2]), p < 0.01). Only 47 (8.9%) videos made medical claims and the overall median [IQR] mDISCERN score was 2 (Anonymous. Gestational Hypertension and Preeclampsia: ACOG Practice Bulletin, Number 222. Obstet Gynecol [Internet]., 2020; Williamson et al., 2023 [1,3]) and was higher for healthcare provider content (2 [1.5,3] versus 1 [0,1], p < 0.01). Moreover, content by healthcare providers was more accurate (84.4% versus 13.3%, p < 0.01).

Conclusion

The TikTok hypertensive disorders of pregnancy content, while relevant, is of low quality and usefulness. Of the content making medical claims, the accuracy was higher for healthcare provider created content. This identifies an opportunity for healthcare professionals to create reliable, accessible content as an alternative for patient education.

title: Attitudes toward hypertension prevention and life satisfaction in older adults: An indirect association through perceived health.
authorString: Ayık DB, Yel F, Doğan DA.
abstractText:
Objective

This study examined whether perceived health showed an indirect association in the relationship between attitudes toward hypertension prevention and life satisfaction among older adults.

Methods

This cross-sectional study included 303 individuals aged 65 years and older with no prior diagnosis of hypertension in Alanya, Türkiye. Data were collected using a Personal Information Form, the Attitudes Scale towards Prevention of Hypertension (ASPH), the Perception of Health Scale (PHS), and the Life Satisfaction in the Elderly Scale (LSES). Pearson correlation, multiple linear regression, adjusted regression, and covariate-adjusted mediation analyses with 5000 bootstrap samples were performed.

Results

Attitudes toward hypertension prevention and perceived health were positively associated with life satisfaction. In the main regression model, both attitudes toward hypertension prevention (β = 0.422, p < 0.001) and perceived health (β = 0.334, p < 0.001) were significantly associated with life satisfaction, explaining 46.2% of its variance (R² = 0.462). These associations remained significant after adjustment for sociodemographic and health-related covariates (β = 0.363 and β = 0.241, respectively; both p < 0.001). Covariate-adjusted mediation analysis showed a significant indirect association between attitudes toward hypertension prevention and life satisfaction through perceived health (B = 0.0765, 95% bootstrap CI [0.0366, 0.1182], p < 0.001), accounting for 23.4% of the adjusted total association.

Conclusion

More favorable hypertension prevention attitudes and better perceived health were associated with higher life satisfaction. Perceived health showed a significant indirect association between prevention attitudes and life satisfaction. Longitudinal studies are needed to clarify the temporal and causal nature of these relationships.

title: Feasibility and Adherence of a Multicomponent Digital Health Monitoring Platform in Ambulatory Heart Failure: Multicenter Observational Study.
authorString: McLeod CJ, Bruce C, Singh Rajput K, Ross JS, Velarde SJL, Dwiyasa F, Hao C, He Y, Zawada S, Majmudar M.
abstractText:
Background

Digital health platforms combining wearable biosensors with smartphone apps offer scalable approaches to heart failure (HF) management, yet sustained patient engagement and initial technology adoption, particularly among older adults, remain uncertain.

Objective

We conducted a prospective, multicenter observational study to explore the feasibility and adherence of using a digital health monitoring platform for 8 weeks in a population of ambulatory patients with HF.

Methods

In this prospective multicenter observational study, patients with New York Heart Association (NYHA) class I to III HF were prescreened across 6 institutions in the United States and Singapore. Participants wore an Everion multisensor armband and an Apple Watch continuously and completed daily electrocardiograms (ECGs), daily symptom questionnaires, weekly voice recordings, and biweekly KCCQ-12 (Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-12) assessments. Prespecified end points included recruitment yield, device wear-time, task-specific compliance, dropout rate, and adverse events.

Results

Of 3386 prescreened individuals, 520 (15.4%) were clinically eligible; 66 consented (1.9% of prescreened; 12.7% of eligible), with technology-related concerns driving most declinations. Among 65 enrolled patients (mean age 56.5, SD 12.3 years; n=53, 81.5% male), 52 (80%) completed 8 weeks. Mean daily wear-time was 11.7 (SD 5.7) hours, significantly exceeding the 8-hour benchmark (P<.001). Task completion rates were 76.6% (2788/3640, daily ECG), 68.5% (2493/3640, daily symptoms), 86.5% (450/520, weekly voice), and 88.1% (229/260, biweekly KCCQ-12). Adherence did not differ significantly by age group (P=.81). No serious device-related adverse events occurred.

Conclusions

Enrolled patients with HF, including older adults, sustained robust engagement with a multicomponent digital platform over 8 weeks. However, technology-related concerns prevented most eligible patients from enrolling, identifying adoption, not adherence, as the primary barrier to scalable remote monitoring.

Trial registration

ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04191356; https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04191356.

title: Risk of Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension Following Anemia in Young Adults: A Retrospective Cohort TriNetX Database Study.
authorString: Butt FR, Dhivagaran T, Sachdeva K, Ahmed Y, Muayad J, Tao BK, Sundaram ANE, Mollan SP, Sharma RA.
abstractText:
Background and objectives

Anemia has been associated with idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH) in small studies, but whether severity modulates IIH risk remains unclear. This study evaluated the hazard of incident IIH after mild, moderate, and severe anemia in young adults.

Methods

Using the TriNetX Research Network (111) health care organizations), adults aged 18-50 years with persistent anemia (≥2 hemoglobin values) were stratified as mild (11.0-12.9 g/dL), moderate (8.0-10.9 g/dL), or severe (<8.0 g/dL) and matched 1:1 to controls (Hb ≥ 13.0 g/dL) by propensity score matching on demographics, body mass index, comorbidities, and socioeconomic factors. The primary outcome was incident IIH; Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) at 6 months, 1 year, and 3 years. Sensitivity analyses applied the World Health Organization (WHO) women's mild threshold and compared patients with vs without iron supplementation.

Results

After matching, 1,240,670 mild anemia patients (mean age 29.0 ± 8.7 years, 83.4% female), 666,515 moderate (29.7 ± 8.1, 86.3% female), and 114,785 severe (31.0 ± 8.9, 75.4% female) were compared with equal-sized control cohorts. Hazard of incident IIH was elevated at every severity and time interval. At 6 months, HRs were 1.45 (95% CI 1.29-1.63), 1.61 (1.39-1.86), and 2.53 (1.82-3.52) for mild, moderate, and severe anemia. At 1 year, HRs were 1.35 (1.22-1.49), 1.33 (1.17-1.51), and 1.94 (1.46-2.58). At 3 years, HRs were 1.17 (1.08-1.26), 1.15 (1.04-1.27), and 1.40 (1.11-1.76); all estimates remained significantly elevated, although CIs overlapped across severity bands. The WHO women's threshold sensitivity yielded concordant, modestly stronger estimates (6 months: HR 1.99 [1.73-2.30]; 3 years: 1.43 [1.31-1.58]). Iron supplementation was associated with reduced IIH hazard (HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.62-0.93; n = 340,660 per group).

Discussion

Anemia is associated with elevated hazard of incident IIH in young adults across all severity bands. Point estimates were higher with greater anemia severity and at earlier follow-up, but CIs overlapped across severity bands, so a severity gradient could not be established. Iron supplementation was associated with reduced hazard. Findings are limited by observational design, administrative case identification, and low absolute incidence; anemia represents a potentially modifiable factor warranting evaluation in patients with papilledema.

title: Short-Term Outcomes Following Surgery for Brachial Plexus Disorders and Related Nerve Procedures: Impact of Diabetes in a National Cohort of 4,040 Patients.
authorString: Lee JJ, Matar DY, Huang W, Klimitz FJ, Mayrhofer-Schmid M, Tuffaha S, Hundeshagen G, Orgill DP, Harhaus L, Panayi AC, Aman M.
abstractText:
Background

Brachial plexus disorders can be debilitating, yet national patterns in patient demographics, procedural complexity, and outcomes remain poorly defined. Diabetes mellitus, which is known to impair wound healing, may further worsen perioperative outcomes, but its impact across large cohorts undergoing brachial plexus surgery is still unclear.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective analysis of American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program (ACS-NSQIP) from 2008 to 2024 identifying adult patients undergoing surgery for brachial plexus disorders (a heterogeneous, decompression-predominant population) using ICD and CPT codes. Demographics, comorbidities, operative details, and 30-day outcomes were characterized and compared across diabetic and nondiabetic patients. Multivariable logistic regression with Firth's penalized likelihood was performed to identify independent predictors of surgical complications (primary outcome) and of medical complications, reoperation, and readmission (secondary outcomes).

Results

Among 4040 patients, the median age was 36 years (IQR 26 to 47), 55.0% were female, and most procedures were elective (96.5%). Nerve decompression was the most common procedure (85.3%), whereas complex reconstruction was infrequent (nerve transfers 4.8%, nerve grafting 4.0%), consistent with a broader, less trauma-predominant population than traditional reconstructive series. Diabetes was present in 174 patients (4.3%) and was associated with older age (median 51 vs. 35 y), higher body mass index, obesity (61.5% vs. 29.2%), hypertension (59.8% vs. 12.8%), renal failure (8.6% vs. 0.5%), and ASA class III status (59.8% vs. 18.4%). Operative time (median 143 min) and length of stay (median 2 d) did not differ by diabetes status. Diabetic patients had higher unadjusted rates of reoperation (7.5% vs. 2.7%, P<0.001), readmission (7.4% vs. 3.3%, P=0.01), surgical complications (5.2% vs. 1.4%, P<0.001), and medical complications (5.2% vs. 1.7%, P=0.003). After multivariable adjustment, diabetes remained independently associated with surgical complications (aOR 3.38, 95% CI: 1.44-7.27, P=0.007) and reoperation (aOR 2.64, 95% CI: 1.30-5.02, P=0.009), but not with medical complications or readmission.

Conclusions

Short-term complications after brachial plexus surgery are uncommon but influenced by comorbidity burden. Diabetes was independently associated with higher odds of surgical complications and reoperation. Diabetes and the broader comorbidity burden should be weighed in perioperative risk assessment and counseling for patients undergoing brachial plexus surgery.

title: Adiposity profiles in relation to cardiometabolic disease risk in South African adults with HIV on long-term antiretroviral therapy.
authorString: Magodoro IM, Micklesfield LK, Manne-Goehler J, Ntusi NAB, Siedner MJ, Goedecke JH.
abstractText:
Background

In high-income countries (HICs), antiretroviral-treated (ART) HIV promotes adverse fat redistribution, contributing to excess cardiometabolic risk in persons with HIV (PWH). Whether this occurs in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) remains unclear. We compared adiposity and cardiometabolic profiles between ART-experienced PWH and HIV-uninfected peers in South Africa.

Methods

Participants from the Middle-Aged Soweto Cohort completed anthropometry, blood pressure, fasting glucose and lipids, 2-h oral glucose tolerance testing and dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry for regional adiposity. Prevalent diabetes, hypertension and dyslipidemia were assessed. ART-experienced PWH were propensity-score matched 1:many to peers without HIV (PWoH) on age, lifestyle, socio-economics and body mass index (BMI) category, stratified by sex. Sex-specific HIV-related cardiometabolic and regional fat differences were evaluated using standardized mean differences (SMD) and p-values. Semi-parametric models examined associations between visceral (VAT) and subcutaneous (SAT) adipose tissue and glucose homeostasis indices.

Results

Eighty male PWH (mean BMI 23.2 kg/m2) and 56 female PWH (31.1 kg/m2) were matched to 159 male PWoH and 92 female PWoH (all matching SMD <0.09). Median ART duration was 5.2 years in males and 7.0 years in females; median CD4+ counts were 413 and 620 cells/mL, respectively. ART comprised predominantly non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (~86%) and protease inhibitors (~18%). There were no significant HIV-related differences in subtotal or regional fat (arm, leg, trunk, android, gynoid, VAT or SAT) in either sex. Conversely, male PWoH had significantly higher prevalences of diabetes (9.0% vs. 3.8%; SMD = 0.22; p = 0.031) and hypertension (48.7% vs. 42.5%; SMD = 0.33; p = 0.022) compared with male PWH. No such differences were observed in females. VAT, but not SAT, was positively associated with post-load glucose in both sexes (p < 0.017), regardless of HIV status-linearly in males and non-linearly in females.

Conclusions

Contrary to HIC evidence, controlled HIV on long-term ART was not associated with differential fat accumulation or adverse cardiometabolic profiles in this South African cohort. Unexpectedly, male PWH had better cardiometabolic profiles than matched PWoH, while females had comparable profiles. Further research should examine qualitative adipose tissue differences at ectopic depots-liver, skeletal muscle and pancreas-and their associations with incident cardiometabolic disease in SSA.

title: Myeloid immune dynamics and potential reprogramming in high-altitude disorders: temporal trajectories, endothelial crosstalk, and translational implications.
authorString: Pang L, Yang L.
abstractText: High-altitude hypobaric hypoxia rapidly alters circulating myeloid-cell distribution, inflammatory signaling, metabolism, and vascular interactions, but these changes are often interpreted without sufficient attention to exposure phase, tissue compartment, or persistence after recovery. This narrative review addresses a central conceptual problem: transient leukocyte mobilization and cytokine elevation are not equivalent to durable myeloid reprogramming. Evidence from human field studies, patient cohorts, hypobaric-hypoxia models, mechanistic normobaric-hypoxia experiments, and related vascular-disease models is organized within a three-level framework comprising transient exposure responses, functional adjustment during ongoing hypoxia, and persistent cell-intrinsic reprogramming. We map these states from the first hours after ascent through acclimatization, prolonged exposure, decompensation, and return to low altitude, emphasizing hypoxia-inducible-factor-dependent immunometabolism, mitochondrial stress signaling, inflammasomes, chromatin regulation, and myeloid-endothelial crosstalk. Disease-specific appraisal suggests that high-altitude pulmonary edema (HAPE) involves complex interactions among elevated pulmonary vascular and capillary pressures, alveolar-capillary barrier dysfunction, and inflammatory responses, with inflammation potentially contributing to disease susceptibility and progression; experimental evidence implicates microglial-neurovascular interactions in high-altitude cerebral edema (HACE), but direct human causal evidence is limited; and high-altitude pulmonary hypertension (HAPH) currently has the most extensive combined human observational and experimental evidence for monocyte-macrophage involvement. Candidate biomarkers and therapeutic targets remain exploratory and are discussed in relation to sampling phase, clinical context, evidence strength, and safety constraints; prospective disease-specific validation is required. Candidate biomarkers and therapeutic targets are aligned with sampling phase, disease stage, evidence strength, and safety constraints. The resulting time-resolved, evidence-calibrated model separates reversible acclimatization from pathological decompensation and true persistence after stimulus withdrawal. Longitudinal within-person recovery studies combining sorted-cell functional assays, metabolic flux, chromatin profiling, and spatial localization are required to define the prevalence, cellular breadth, and clinical consequences of persistent high-altitude myeloid reprogramming and inform future trials of disease-specific adjunctive therapy.

title: ACR Appropriateness Criteria® Chronic Liver Disease: 2026 Update.
authorString: Expert Panel on Gastrointestinal Imaging, Fung A, El Khouli RH, Schooler GR, Batie D, Elojeimy S, Singal AK, Smith EN, Thakrar KH, Wahab SA, Wang SS, Korngold EK.

journal.title: Journal of the American College of Radiology : JACR

abstractText: Chronic liver disease, caused by a range of etiologies, can lead to progressive liver function deterioration, hepatic fibrosis, cirrhosis, and, ultimately, end-stage liver disease. With cirrhosis and end-stage liver disease, complications include portal hypertension, gastrointestinal hemorrhage, refractory ascites, hepatic encephalopathy, and primary hepatocellular carcinoma. Imaging plays an important role in the diagnosis, treatment response assessment, and surveillance of chronic liver disease, specifically of hepatic hemochromatosis, steatosis, and fibrosis, in an effort to prevent progression to cirrhosis. This document reviews the imaging modalities best suited for these clinical scenarios, and a summary of current evidence is provided to support the use of various modalities for each of the clinical contexts. The American College of Radiology Appropriateness Criteria are evidence-based guidelines for specific clinical conditions that are reviewed annually by a multidisciplinary expert panel. The guideline development and revision include an extensive analysis of current medical literature from peer reviewed journals and the application of well-established methodologies (RAND/UCLA Appropriateness Method and Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation or GRADE) to rate the appropriateness of imaging and treatment procedures for specific clinical scenarios. In those instances where evidence is lacking or equivocal, expert opinion may supplement the available evidence to recommend imaging or treatment.

title: Non-dipper Hypertension Is Associated with Multilevel Vascular Alterations but Not Capillary Rarefaction: A Cross-sectional Vascular Phenotyping Study.
authorString: Aydın MZ, Kuzu Z, Teber MK, Çetinkaya Y, Şen Ö, Sunkak S, Doğan R, Tanboğa İH.
abstractText: To compare endothelial function, carotid remodeling, renal microvascular injury, and nailfold capillaroscopy across control, dipper, and non-dipper participants and to test whether non-dipper hypertension reflects isolated nocturnal blood pressure dysregulation or broader vascular alteration. This cross-sectional study included 74 normotensive controls and 157 treatment-naive patients with newly diagnosed essential hypertension, classified by ambulatory monitoring as dipper (n = 70) or non-dipper (n = 87). All underwent flow-mediated dilation, carotid intimamedia thickness, urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio, and nail-fold capillaroscopy. Regression models adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, diabetes mellitus, and 24-hour systolic blood pressure. Twenty-four-hour systolic blood pressure did not differ between dipper and non-dipper hypertension (143.1 vs. 146.5 mmHg; P = .161), whereas nighttime systolic blood pressure was markedly higher in non-dippers (121.8 vs. 144.5 mmHg; P < .001). Non-dippers had lower flow-mediated dilation (-2.5 [-4.5, 0.8] vs. 3.0 [-2.5, 5.6]%; P < .001); higher carotid intima-media thickness (1.01 [0.86, 1.06] vs. 0.85 [0.67, 1.01] mm; P < .001); and more frequent dilated capillaries (43.0% vs 20.0%; P = .003), microhemorrhages (31.4% vs 15.7%; P = .026), retinopathy (36.1% vs. 19.4%; P = .030), and left ventricular hypertrophy (47.4% vs. 30.9%; P = .044). Capillary density did not differ. After adjustment, non-dipper status remained associated with flow-mediated dilation (-4.22 percentage points; 95% CI, -7.15 to -1.30), carotid intima-media thickness (0.087 mm; 0.025-0.149), and dilated capillaries (odds ratio, 3.17; 1.50-6.71). The carotid association was directionally consistent across measurement-scale strata but significant only among measurements not requiring unit conversion. Non-dipper hypertension identified a multilevel vascular phenotype not explained by 24-hour pressure load and without capillary rarefaction.

title: Sociodemographic Factors Associated With Hypertension Among People With diabetes: Evidence From Electronic Health Records in Qassim.
authorString: Alhurishi SA, AlGhaith NI, Alharbi MS, Alsadhan N.

journal.title: Journal of diabetes science and technology

abstractText: Diabetes and hypertension are major public health problems in Saudi Arabia. Yet, evidence from Qassim is limited. This study aims to estimate the prevalence of registered diagnosed diabetes and hypertension in 2025 and to examine the association between hypertension and selected characteristics among individuals with diabetes in the Qassim region. A cross-sectional study design has been used. First, we describe registered diagnosed diabetes and hypertension among people with diabetes in 2025. Then, a multivariable logistic regression model was employed to estimate the association between hypertension and covariates: age, type of diabetes, gender, and location. A total of 63 094 people with diabetes were identified. The crude prevalence registered diagnosed with diabetes in Qassim in 2025 was 21.83% among Saudi adults aged 20 years and older. 42.5% had a concurrent diagnosis of hypertension. The risk of being diagnosed with diabetes and hypertension was significantly higher among females (odds ratio [OR] = 1.274, 95% CI, 1.232-1.318) and type 1 diabetes (OR = 1.274, 95% CI, 1.175-1.381) Moreover, the risk increased significantly with advancing age, with the highest odds observed among individuals aged 65 years and older (OR = 9.880, 95% CI, 9.234-10.571). There was a significant difference in the association between having hypertension and location. Older adults and women with diabetes should be prioritized for hypertension prevention and management. Although location was significantly associated with the odds of hypertension, the observed differences did not suggest a sufficiently distinct geographic pattern. Planning culturally appropriate health promotion interventions to improve the prevention and control of both diabetes and hypertension is recommended.

title: Adaptive Immunity Governs Regional Aortic Remodeling in Hypertension via Perivascular Adipose Tissue Plasticity.
authorString: Xu Y, Snider JC, Bersi MR.
abstractText:
Background

Hypertension drives heterogeneous aortic remodeling, but the mechanisms underlying regional disparities remain unclear. We hypothesized that T-cell adaptive immunity orchestrates spatial differences in hypertensive vascular dysfunction by modulating perivascular adipose tissue (PVAT) phenotype and immune-metabolic crosstalk.

Methods

Wild-type, lymphocyte-deficient Rag1-/-, and T-cell-reconstituted Rag1-/- mice were subjected to AngII (angiotensin II)-induced hypertension. We integrated biaxial mechanical testing, bulk transcriptomics, and PVAT morphological and secretome analyses to investigate the role of T-cell adaptive immunity in hypertension.

Results

T cells promote maladaptive structural remodeling in the descending thoracic aorta, marked by wall thickening, reduced circumferential stiffness, and inflammatory gene upregulation (Il6, Ccl2) while simultaneously restraining a protective metabolic program (Pparg, Adipoq) in the infrarenal abdominal aorta that promotes hypertensive resilience.
