PVAT heterogeneity emerged as a key regulator whereby thoracic PVAT maintains a stable resident T-cell population that licenses pathological wall thickening and proinflammatory secretome shifts in response to hypertension. Conversely, the abdominal PVAT niche functions as a dynamic inflammatory environment where T-cell adaptive immunity restrains latent thermogenic plasticity (Ucp1 upregulation). Adaptive immune deficiency unmasked this compensatory abdominal adaptation in Rag1-/- mice, which paradoxically reversed hypertensive stiffening and enhanced vascular compliance. T-cell reconstitution restored the regional hypertensive vascular and PVAT remodeling, confirming that adaptive immunity manages a critical trade-off between structural stability and metabolic plasticity of the aorta-PVAT complex.

Conclusions

This work identifies PVAT as an immune-metabolic switch governing regional susceptibility to vascular remodeling, offering spatially resolved strategies to preserve aortic compliance in hypertensive disease.

title: Convergent Genomic Signatures of Selection in Thar: Genetic trade-offs for desert survival
authorString: Rathod SM, Jain R, Mukerji M.
abstractText:
Background:

Desert environments provide a setting for natural biological experiments to cope up with simultaneous stressors of extreme temperatures, aridity, UV exposure, and limited food resources. Biological adaptations that support living in such an environment could become liabilities when the environment and lifestyle change due to gene-environment mismatch. We explored whether genetically and culturally diverse endogamous native populations of the Thar exhibit convergent signatures of selection to desert conditions and whether the selected loci have implications in traits and disease susceptibilities relevant to non-native transitions.

Results:

We report 348 high-confidence variants across 45 candidate genes from a study on 176 individuals from eight genetically distinct Thar populations. These genes identified from humans and other desert inhabitants display convergent evolution with multiple selection scans (PBSn1, Tajima`s D, iHS, and XPEHH) in diverse Thar populations. Prominent genes include ZNF385D, SGCZ, SARDH, SLC12A3, etc. Selected variants essential in the desert environment were associated with complex traits like lipid metabolism, hypertension, renal and cardiovascular diseases, and addiction in GWAS and PheWAS. Noteworthy, in a syntenic locus, eQTLs in SARDH, which modulates DBH implicated in addiction, suggest a potential link with survival advantage in an uncertain desert environment. Likewise, a selected variant (rs7204044) in SLC12A3, implicated in hypertension in non-desert populations, seems to be a key to water-salt homeostasis in desert natives.

Conclusions:

These findings suggest that variants linked to adaptive traits in desert conditions could be linked to maladaptation in an altered environment. This has potential health consequences in climatic and lifestyle transitions among native inhabitants.

title: Predictors of Higher-Intensity Care in Epinephrine-Treated Emergency Department Encounters for Anaphylaxis and Allergic Reactions: A Retrospective Cohort Study With Internal Validation
authorString: Aktaş RS, Büyükkaya MŞ, Atik Ö, Okucu Ö, Adıgüzel N.
abstractText: Background Clinicians treating anaphylaxis in the emergency department (ED) have little objective guidance on which patients will need more than a single dose of epinephrine. We examined whether features recorded at the initial ED assessment are associated with higher-intensity care and tested the stability of these associations across approaches to missing data, repeat encounters, and outcome definition. Methods Adult ED encounters that received epinephrine for anaphylaxis or an allergic reaction were drawn from MIMIC-IV-ED. The primary outcome was a composite of recurrent epinephrine, intensive care unit (ICU) admission, mechanical ventilation, or vasopressor use. A prespecified seven-variable logistic model (age, sex, ambulance arrival, initial oxygen saturation, asthma, hypertension, food trigger) was fitted with multiple imputation. Sensitivity analyses used complete cases, a saturation-free model on all encounters, a first-encounter cohort, and patient-clustered standard errors. Internal validation nested the imputation step inside bootstrap resampling and repeated 10-fold cross-validation on all encounters. ICU admission, recurrent epinephrine, and life support (ventilation or vasopressor) were modeled separately. Results Among 424 encounters (399 patients), 185 (43.6%) met the primary outcome; none died in hospital. Asthma (adjusted odds ratio 3.65 (1.45–9.23)), hypertension (3.45 (1.64–7.29)), older age (1.16 (1.02–1.33) per decade), and a food trigger (2.50 (1.22–5.12)) were associated with the outcome. The food estimate weakened in complete cases (1.71 (0.77–3.80)) because encounters lacking an initial saturation were disproportionately food-triggered and severe; the saturation-free model on all 424 encounters reproduced the association (2.43 (1.19–4.95)). Age, asthma, and hypertension estimates were similar in the first-encounter cohort and with clustered errors. Discrimination was modest (nested cross-validated AUC 0.682; bootstrap-corrected calibration slope 0.90). Asthma, hypertension, and food trigger were more strongly related to ICU admission (AUC 0.883) than to recurrent epinephrine. The lowest tertile of cross-validated risk still had an event rate of 30.3%. Conclusions Asthma, hypertension, older age, and a food-related trigger identify epinephrine-treated encounters at higher risk of escalation, particularly ICU-level care. None of the examined risk strata had an event rate low enough to support routine immediate discharge. Timing of ICU-level events relative to the first dose could not be verified; external validation is required.

title: Malignant Graves' Orbitopathy Complicated by Endophthalmitis, Vision Loss, and Antithyroid Drug- Induced Agranulocytosis: A Case Report
authorString: Mabrouk M, Chehida AB, Bchir N, Bouchoucha S, Elguiche D, Mnasriya S, Zouaoui C, Ouertani H.
abstractText: Introduction Severe forms of Graves' orbitopathy (GO) account for only a minority of cases, delayed diagnosis and management may result in sight-threatening complications, including orbital infection, and irreversible vision loss. Herein we report a case of a 77-year-old woman with severe GO complicated with endophtalmitis and anti-thyroid drug (ATD) induced agranulocytosis. Case Presentation A 77-year-old woman was referred for evaluation and management of Graves' disease associated with severe GO. Seven months before presentation, she developed progressive left-sided proptosis, conjunctival hyperemia and ocular pruritus. Initial ophthalmological management was limited to lubricating eye drops. Over the following months, her condition deteriorated with ocular pain, complete restriction of left ocular motility, and marked visual impairment. Hyperthyroidism was confirmed. Ophthalmological examination demonstrated a left corneal abscess complicated by corneal perforation sealed by iris prolapse, circumferential corneal neovascularization, ocular hypertension, and no light perception. Hyperthyroidism was initially treated with carbimazole and propranolol. One month later, the patient developed severe ATD-induced agranulocytosis with erythroderma, fever, and acute kidney injury, requiring immediate discontinuation of antithyroid therapy. Following stabilization, Lugol's iodine was administered before total thyroidectomy. Management of the orbitopathy included tarsorrhaphy, prolonged intravenous antibiotic therapy, intravenous methylprednisolone, and mycophenolate mofetil. Despite successful control of the infectious and inflammatory process, irreversible vision loss occurred, ultimately necessitating enucleation of the left eye. Conclusion This case highlights the devastating consequences of delayed diagnosis and treatment of Graves' orbitopathy, which may progress to irreversible blindness. It also illustrates the potential impact of antithyroid drug-induced agranulocytosis on the development of infectious complications.

title: Histological differences between patients with porto-sinusoidal vascular disorder and fibrosis regression of chronic hepatitis B: an analysis based on machine learning algorithms
authorString: Li Z, Wang J, Li M, Ren Y, Tai DCS, Fu Q, Liu C.
abstractText: Background Porto-sinusoidal vascular disorder (PSVD) alters portal hemodynamics, leading to portal hypertension without obvious fibrosis. Incomplete septal fibrosis (ISF) is recognized as one of the pathological hallmarks of PSVD; however, the differences in ISF between patients with PSVD and those with fibrosis regression remain controversial. This study aimed to analyze the vascular and fibrotic characteristics of liver biopsies between two cohorts using machine learning algorithms. Methods 41 patients with PSVD and 40 with chronic hepatitis B who achieved fibrosis regression after 48 weeks of entecavir treatment were enrolled. The fibrosis stage was assessed using the Ishak system. Images of unstained liver biopsy slides were obtained using second-harmonic generation/two-photon excited fluorescence. Machine learning algorithms were adopted for the analysis: arterial density (AD), portal vein density (PVD), central vein density (CVD), collagen proportionate area (CPA), and different areas of CPA on the portal area, zones 1/2/3, and ISF. Results In contrast to fibrosis regression, patients with PSVD had significantly higher AD (17.98 ± 10.38/mm² vs 8.59 ± 8.28/mm², P < 0.05) and CVD (6.93 ± 4.93/mm² vs. 3.30 ± 2.40/mm², P < 0.05), while PVD (19.18 ± 13.37/mm² vs. 33.05 ± 22.61/mm², P < 0.05) was significantly lower. PSVD had more collagen fibers and longer and wider collagen distribution in the portal area (P < 0.05). In contrast, in the ISF, patients with PSVD had fewer collagen fibers and shorter collagen distribution (P < 0.05). Conclusion This study not only revealed the pathological differences in vascular and fibrotic changes between patients with PSVD and fibrosis regression in chronic hepatitis B, but also clarified the commonalities of ISF.

title: Left Atrial Slow-Conduction Regions as Predictors of Pulmonary Vein Isolation Outcome in Persistent Atrial Fibrillation
authorString: Musella AM, Limite LR, Bortone A.
abstractText: PURPOSE Recurrence after durable pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) is common in persistent atrial fibrillation (AF), and left atrial (LA) slow-conduction regions are potential contributors. We assessed their impact on PVI outcomes in persistent AF. METHODS Fifty consecutive patients with persistent AF undergoing first-time PVI were prospectively enrolled. After sinus rhythm restoration by electrical cardioversion, high-density LA mapping was performed during coronary sinus pacing before PVI. Slow-conduction regions corresponded to discrete zones bordered by lines of block and characterized by fragmented electrograms, decremental conduction, and a conduction velocity about 70% slower than that of the remaining LA. Median follow-up was 18 months. RESULTS Slow-conduction regions were found in 27 of 50 patients (54%). AF or atrial tachycardia recurred in 9 of 27 patients with slow-conduction regions (33%) versus 1 of 23 without (4%; log-rank P  = 0.010). At redo (mean, 7 months), PVI was durable in 8 of 10 patients, with unchanged slow-conduction regions. Slow-conduction region presence was the strongest independent predictor of recurrence (odds ratio 6.36; 95% confidence interval 1.26–63.06; P  = 0.023), regardless of voltage. Restricting to durable PVI and no new substrate, recurrence was 8 of 26 with slow-conduction regions versus 0 of 22 without (log-rank P  = 0.005). CONCLUSIONS In persistent AF, the absence of LA slow-conduction regions predicts near-complete response to PVI alone, whereas their presence predicts recurrence despite durable PVI, supporting patient selection and tailored ablation.

title: Diagnostic accuracy of community health worker blood pressure measurements against 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring: Validating task-shifting for hypertension screening in urban slums of central India
authorString: Lahiri A, Prakash P, Shrivastava N, Chouhan RN, Joshi A, Joshi R, Pakhare AP.
abstractText: Background & objectives: Hypertension is one of the leading causes of cardiovascular disease in India, yet the screening cascade under the National Programme for Non-Communicable Diseases (NP-NCD) suffers from substantial attrition at each referral step. Task-shifting blood pressure (BP) measurement directly to Accredited Social Health Activists (ASHAs) could bypass this attrition, but evidence validating ASHA-measured BP against ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM)—the gold standard—is lacking. This study evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of ASHA-measured BP against 24-hour ABPM for hypertension detection in urban slums. Methods In this cross-sectional diagnostic accuracy study, 111 adults (≥ 30 year) from urban slums of Bhopal underwent BP measurement by trained ASHAs using validated digital devices (Omron HEM-7120) following a two-visit protocol, followed by 24-h ABPM (Schiller BR-102 plus). Diagnostic accuracy and agreement (Bland-Altman, Cohen’s kappa, intraclass correlation) were computed against ABPM. Results ABPM-defined hypertension prevalence was 25.2 per cent (28/111). The two-visit ASHA protocol showed sensitivity 85.7 per cent (95% CI: 68.5–94.3), specificity 90.4 per cent (82.1–95.0), positive predictive value 75.0 per cent, negative predictive value 94.9 per cent and Cohen’s kappa 0.73 (substantial agreement). Single readings had significantly more false positives (McNemar P = 0.025). Bland-Altman analysis showed mean systolic BP bias of + 3.1 mmHg (limits of agreement: −18.7 to + 24.8) against 24-h ABPM. White-coat hypertension was 7.2 per cent and masked hypertension 3.6 per cent on two-visit ASHA protocol compared to 24-h ABPM. Interpretation & conclusions: ASHA-measured BP using a two-visit protocol demonstrates good diagnostic accuracy and substantial agreement with ABPM. These findings provide robust evidence that ASHAs can measure blood pressure as reliably as any industry-standard measurement, supporting task-shifting of BP measurement to ASHAs to achieve realistic screening with higher yield and better follow-up of persons with hypertension in the community. Single readings should be avoided due to higher false-positive rates.

title: An online support program for patients with heart failure: Co-designing with patients and heart failure nurses.
authorString: Säfstræm E, Stræmberg A, Lundberg M, Karlstræm P, Lans C, Liljeroos M.
abstractText:
Aim

Persons with heart failure may need support to manage the symptoms and recommended treatment. Therefore, we aimed to develop an online support program for patients newly diagnosed with heart failure through a co-design process.

Method and results

The co-design process evolved over four phases: gathering experiences, identifying needs, developing, and finalizing a prototype of the online support program. The process included interviews with oncology nurses with experience of using a support program (n = 7) and workshops with heart failure nurses (n = 5) and patients with heart failure (n = 10). Designers and content creators were also involved in the process. The co-design process resulted in a prototype of a support program "Living with heart failure", including eight modules with a total of 49 web pages that provide information on the diagnosis, treatment, self-care, and lifestyle adaptation. The information is presented in texts, recorded lectures, interviews, pictures, images, and patient narratives. The program includes features such as reporting weight and blood pressure and allows secure messaging between patients and nurses.

Conclusion

The co-design method was feasible for developing a support program to be used by patients with heart failure and heart failure nurses. The implementation and effectiveness of the support program remain to be evaluated.

title: Linked suppression in transplantation: mechanistic boundaries and therapeutic opportunities.
authorString: Chandraker A, Tripathi S.

journal.title: Current opinion in nephrology and hypertension

abstractText:
Purpose of review

Linked suppression is often used to explain how antigen-specific regulatory T cells (Tregs) might control a complex, multivalent alloimmune response. This review separates linked suppression from bystander suppression and infectious tolerance and considers how direct, indirect, and semi-direct allorecognition define the antigen-presenting cell (APC) substrate on which it can occur.

Recent findings

Classic transplantation models showed that regulation directed to one antigen can restrain responses to additional antigens when they are physically linked within a graft or presented by the same APC. The breadth and mechanism may vary with donor-antigen burden and the degree of HLA sharing. Relevant interactions appear concentrated in the graft and draining lymph nodes rather than peripheral blood. CTLA-4-dependent B7 removal, local adenosine generation, and spatial organization within APC-rich niches are plausible mechanisms. Small-animal islet, minor-antigen-mismatch, and TCR-transgenic models provide tools to test these variables. Early clinical studies establish feasibility but do not yet prove linked suppression in humans.

Summary

Linked suppression is a strong preclinical principle and a useful therapeutic objective, but it is not yet a validated clinical mechanism. Trials should combine product characterization and tracking with linkage-dependent assays, tissue analysis, donor-versus-third-party testing, and protocolized immunosuppression reduction.

title: Timing of reported systolic dysfunction with mavacamten relative to echocardiographic monitoring schedules: a FAERS disproportionality analysis
authorString: Chen X, Chen Z, Kang Y.
abstractText:
Aim:

In April 2025, the US prescribing information for mavacamten allowed eligible stable patients to extend echocardiographic monitoring to every 6 months from week 12. We examined when systolic dysfunction-related events are reported relative to this schedule.

Methods:

We analyzed US Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) reports from April 2022 to June 2026 listing mavacamten as primary or secondary suspect (n = 4953), using disproportionality analysis with restricted comparators. Time to onset was calculated after additional deduplication across case identifiers. Reporting density (events/30 days) was compared across monitoring intervals, restricted to reports with ≥12 months or ≥2 years of potential observation.

Results:

Ejection fraction decreased had the highest reporting odds ratio (ROR) among clinical terms with ≥10 reports (n = 181; ROR 53.64, 95% confidence interval [CI] 46.10–62.41) and remained elevated against a cardiomyopathy-spectrum comparator (ROR 3.23, 95% CI 2.23–4.67). Among 88 cases (median time to onset 125.0 days), reporting density fell from 13.21 events/30 days in the first 12 weeks to 3.79 from week 12 to month 9, without a clear difference from months 9–12 (rate ratio 1.14, 95% CI 0.48–3.01). With ≥2 years of potential observation, density was higher from week 12 to month 12 than in months 12–24 (rate ratio 3.68, 95% CI 1.38–11.40; 6 later events).

Conclusion:

Reporting density was highest in the first 12 weeks, with no clear further decline during the rest of the first year. This period warrants evaluation in eligible cohorts with documented echocardiography.

title: Complete Atrioventricular Block in Severe Guillain–Barré Syndrome: A Case Report
authorString: Xie W, Cao J, Jiang L, Lu W, Cao Y, Xu Q.
abstractText: Background Guillain–Barré syndrome (GBS) is an acute immune-mediated polyradiculoneuropathy that can progress to profound muscle weakness and respiratory failure. Cardiovascular autonomic dysfunction is another potentially life-threatening complication, manifesting as marked fluctuations in heart rate and blood pressure or severe arrhythmias. Among these manifestations, complete atrioventricular block (CAVB) is particularly severe and rarely reported in adults with GBS, potentially causing profound bradycardia and hemodynamic instability. Its unpredictable onset presents a diagnostic and management challenge, emphasizing the need for continuous cardiac monitoring, early recognition, and timely intervention. Case presentation: A 42-year-old woman with congenital right renal agenesis and end-stage renal disease was admitted with progressive limb weakness, followed by respiratory failure requiring invasive mechanical ventilation. Cerebrospinal fluid albuminocytologic dissociation and abnormal nerve conduction findings supported the diagnosis of GBS. Despite sinus rhythm on admission, bedside monitoring on Day 6 detected CAVB with bradycardia (43 beats/min) and hypotension (80/50 mmHg). An immediate 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) confirmed CAVB with a ventricular escape rhythm, prompting temporary transvenous pacing and subsequent hemodynamic stabilization. Serial high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I levels remained within the reference range, and a preceding echocardiogram showed preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (60%). She received plasma exchange and later intravenous immunoglobulin because severe weakness persisted. Subsequent cardiac monitoring documented no further CAVB, and the temporary pacemaker was removed on Day 19. Follow-up coronary computed tomography angiography showed atherosclerosis without significant stenosis. At three months, ECG confirmed normal atrioventricular conduction without reported recurrent bradycardia or syncope. The overall clinical course supported GBS-associated cardiovascular autonomic dysfunction as the primary explanation for CAVB. Conclusions This case describes severe GBS complicated by hemodynamically unstable CAVB, clinically attributed to GBS-associated cardiovascular autonomic dysfunction. Prompt recognition and temporary transvenous pacing were followed by hemodynamic stabilization, with subsequent pacemaker removal and normal atrioventricular conduction at three months. This case underscores the importance of continuous cardiac monitoring, careful etiological assessment, and individualized management of severe conduction disturbances during GBS.

title: The Cardiovascular Benefit of Menopausal Hormone Treatment is Age-Dependent in Ldlr-/- Mice
authorString: Zhu L, Lalisan C, Gavin C, Litts B, Zhong M, Rein J, An J, Boobalan R, Wang Y, Aelst AV, Chinnarasu S, Xu Y, Linton M, Stafford J.
abstractText:
Background: The risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) increases in women after menopause, coinciding with declining estrogen levels. However, menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) has not consistently reduced ASCVD events in post-menopausal women, despite improvements in lipid profiles. The mechanisms underlying the diminished cardiovascular protective effects of estrogens during MHT remain poorly understood.

Methods:

Atherosclerosis was established in 11-month-old female Ldlr -/- mice through Western diet feeding. To investigate the effects of menopause and menopausal 17β-estradiol (E 2 ) treatment on atherosclerotic burden during lipid normalization, mice were switched to a chow diet and subjected to ovariectomy (OVX) with and without E 2 treatment. To determine the contribution of inflammation to ASCVD risk during MHT, a cohort of mice received Ifnγ -/- bone marrow transplantation (Ifnγ -/-BM ) before hormone treatment. To assess the influence of age on ASCVD risk during MHT, parallel studies were conducted in young mice, beginning at 3 months of age. Outcomes included lipid profiles, HDL function, circulating cytokines, atherosclerotic burden, liver lipid metabolic pathways and transcriptomic profiles, and hepatic estrogen receptor signaling.

Results:

OVX increased atherosclerotic burden compared with sham-operation, E 2 treatment following OVX failed to reduce atherosclerosis in older mice but reduced atherosclerosis in young mice during chow diet-induced lipid normalization. In older mice, E 2 treatment elevated circulating IFNγ, impaired HDL antioxidant and cholesterol efflux functions, and increased plaque inflammation and features of plaque vulnerability. Suppression of inflammation through Ifnγ -/-BM transplantation restored HDL function and the ability of E 2 treatment to reduce atherosclerosis in older mice. In contrast, E 2 treatment following OVX in young mice reduced systemic and improved HDL function. E 2 treatment increased liver fatty acid metabolic signaling in both older and young mice but increased liver 4-HNE levels only in older mice. The age-dependent response was associated with remodeling of hepatic estrogen receptor (ER) expression, characterized by reduced ERα and increased G protein-coupled ER expression with aging. Liver transcriptomic analyses identified inflammatory and interferon-associated signatures following OVX+E 2 treatment in older mice. qPCR analyses across older and young mice suggested age-associated differences in inflammatory transcripts in response to E 2 .

Conclusions:

These findings suggest that aging alters hepatic responses to E 2 treatment following ovariectomy, promoting oxidative stress and inflammatory signaling that contribute to persistent systemic inflammation and compromise the ability of E 2 to reduce atherosclerosis.

title: Hyperhomocysteinemia promotes femoral artery calcification via glycolysis-lactate-driven KDM3B lactylation and downstream pro-calcific transcriptional programming.
authorString: Ou-Yang S, Qin X.
abstractText: Hyperhomocysteinemia (HHcy) is a significant independent risk factor for vascular calcification, such as Femoral Artery Calcification. However, the precise mechanisms linking HHcy to the Femoral Artery Calcification, particularly the role of metabolic and epigenetic reprogramming, remain poorly defined. This study combined clinical data from 103 patients with lower limb arterial occlusion, a long-term HHcy mouse model induced by a high-methionine diet, and in vitro experiments using human aortic vascular smooth muscle cells (HA-VSMCs) treated with homocysteine (Hcy). Metabolic profiling was performed using stable isotope-resolved metabolomics (<sup>13</sup>C-MFA) and Seahorse Analyzer. Clinical data confirmed a correlation between plasma Hcy levels and femoral artery calcification severity. In HA-VSMCs, Hcy (100 μM) promoted calcification and similarly enhanced glycolytic flux, leading to lactate accumulation. This lactate served as a substrate for protein lactylation. Lactylation proteomics identified the histone demethylase KDM3B as a key target. Hcy-induced lactylation at the K449 site enhanced KDM3B protein stability. KDM3B knockdown attenuated Hcy-induced calcification. Mechanistically, KDM3B mediated the transcriptional upregulation of pro-calcific genes (ALS2, IL20RB, NCF1) by reducing repressive H3K9me2 marks at their promoters. Rescue experiments confirmed ALS2 and NCF1 as critical downstream effectors. In mice, HHcy induced significant femoral artery calcification, but pharmacological inhibition of KDM3B significantly attenuated HHcy-induced femoral artery calcification. In all, our findings uncover a defined pathway wherein HHcy-driven glycolytic metabolic remodeling generates lactate to trigger site-specific KDM3B lactylation-stabilization. This KDM3B-driven transcriptional programme promotes femoral artery calcification, identifying the KDM3B-ALS2/NCF1 axis as a promising therapeutic target for vascular calcification.

title: Computed tomography extracellular volume fraction in canine hepatic fibrosis: a retrospective preliminary study.
authorString: Goda Y, Seki A, Hanazono K, Tamura M, Yamamoto S, Sakai T, Sakatani A, Torisu S, Miyoshi K.
abstractText: Liver biopsy remains the gold standard for diagnosing hepatic fibrosis in dogs; however, its invasive nature limits suitability for repeated assessment. Computed tomography-extracellular volume fraction (CT-ECV) has been investigated as a quantitative imaging measure associated with hepatic fibrosis in humans; however, its characteristics in dogs with spontaneous hepatic fibrosis remain incompletely understood. This retrospective study aimed to compare hepatic CT-ECV between dogs with only histopathologically normal biopsied hepatic lobes and dogs with at least one biopsied hepatic lobe showing clinically significant fibrosis, and to explore the ability of CT-ECV to discriminate between these groups. Thirty-six client-owned dogs that underwent triple-phase contrast-enhanced CT and liver biopsy were analyzed. Histopathologic examination identified 47 histopathologically normal hepatic lobes from 26 dogs and 27 hepatic lobes with fibrosis from 11 dogs; one dog contributed hepatic lobes to both categories. CT-ECV was calculated from changes in hepatic and aortic attenuation between pre-contrast and equilibrium phase images, with correction for hematocrit. For the principal doglevel analysis, 25 dogs were classified as normal and 11 as fibrotic, and dog-level CTECV was calculated as the mean across all biopsied hepatic lobes. Mean dog-level CT-ECV was 21.46 ± 3.02% in the normal group and 32.75 ± 10.67% in the fibrosis group. After adjustment for CT scanner, CT-ECV was significantly higher in the fibrosis group, with an estimated mean difference of 12.10 percentage points (robust 95% CI, 4.60-19.59; P =.002). Dog-level receiver operating characteristic analysis yielded an area under the curve of 0.865 (95% CI, 0.726-1.000). An exploratory candidate threshold of 29.56% provided a sensitivity of 63.6% (95% CI, 30.8-89.1%) and a specificity of 100% (95% CI, 86.3-100%). Intra-observer repeatability was high (intraclass correlation coefficient, 0.886). These findings provide preliminary evidence that CT-ECV is associated with clinically significant hepatic fibrosis in dogs. Further studies using standardized imaging protocols and independent clinical populations are required to validate its diagnostic performance and the proposed exploratory threshold.

title: Human CD47 Expression on Porcine Endothelial Cells Regulates Natural Killer Cell Function via SIRPα.
authorString: Tran T, Kemter E, Galdina V, Kartmann H, Mahesh A, Zhang X, Urquidi O, Galvão DR, Pereira SF, Gigli M, Grimus S, Kurome M, Zakhartchenko V, Kessler B, Yang K, Lickert H, Wolf E, Reichart D, Puga Yung GL, Seebach JD.

journal.title: American journal of transplantation : official journal of the American Society of Transplantation and the American Society of Transplant Surgeons

abstractText: Natural killer (NK) cells are pivotal in xenograft rejection, targeting porcine endothelial cells. CD47 acts as a "don't eat me" signal by binding to signal regulatory protein alpha (SIRPα),suppressing immune activation. While this axis has been well characterized in macrophages, its influence on NK cell-mediated xenograft rejection remains unclear. We investigated whether expression of human CD47 (hCD47) on porcine aortic endothelial cells (PAECs) from transgenic pigs inhibits human NK activity. Under static conditions, hCD47 expression on PAECs significantly reduced direct NK cytotoxicity. In microfluidic systems simulating physiological conditions, GGTA1-KO/hCD47-TG PAECs were associated with reduced NK cell-mediated lysis and motility compared with WT PAECs. However, with heat-inactivated human plasma containing anti-pig non-αGal antibodies, hCD47 expression did not protect αGal-knockout PAECs from NK cell-mediated antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC). Single-cell RNA sequencing showed overall homogeneous NK subtype distribution between WT and hCD47-expressing PAEC conditions. However, a small set of differentially expressed genes showed increased inhibitory receptor expression and reduced effector, activation, and proliferation signatures in NK cells exposed to hCD47. These findings identify hCD47 as an effective checkpoint against direct NK cytotoxicity, but insufficient to prevent ADCC, underscoring the need for combinatorial strategies to achieve durable protection from NK-driven xenograft rejection.

title: Robotic aortic valve replacement with a sutureless valve, through a 3 cm transaxillary incision: a step-by-step surgical guide.
authorString: Varshney S, Varshney S, Sonkusale M.

journal.title: Multimedia manual of cardiothoracic surgery : MMCTS

abstractText: Robotic aortic valve replacement remains a challenging procedure, limiting its widespread adoption. We present our technique of robotic aortic valve replacement with da Vinci X system, with a sutureless valve (Perceval Plus), where we have tried to simplify the procedural steps. These can be very easily adopted by surgeons worldwide. The procedure includes port placement, docking, incision planning, femoral cannulation, aortotomy, valve excision, implantation tips for the sutureless valve, and aortotomy closure. The refinement of this approach has been associated with rapid postoperative recovery, with the patient walking in less than 24 hours after surgery. This step-by-step video tutorial will help surgeons worldwide in the adoption of robotic aortic valve replacement techniques.

title: Bicuspidization of a severely dysplastic aortic valve in a neonate.
authorString: Kozyrev I, Vergnat M, Suchowerskyj P, Bierbach B, Arenz C, Asfour B.

journal.title: Multimedia manual of cardiothoracic surgery : MMCTS

abstractText: Severe congenital aortic valve stenosis in neonates remains a challenging lesion requiring individualized treatment. While balloon aortic valvuloplasty and surgical valvotomy are established treatment options, neonates with severely dysplastic valve morphology may benefit from anatomical valve reconstruction in addition to relief of obstruction. This video tutorial demonstrates our technique of bicuspidization of a severely dysplastic neonatal aortic valve by commissural reconstruction, extensive leaflet shaving and limited free-edge remodelling. Our ultimate goal of tricuspid valve repair was impossible in this scenario.

title: Transaxillary direct-view aortic valve replacement with Intuity Elite rapid-deployment valve.
authorString: Galeazzi M, Mali E, D'Alessio S, Giusti M, Zingaro C, Malvindi P, Berretta P, Di Eusanio M.

journal.title: Multimedia manual of cardiothoracic surgery : MMCTS

abstractText: We present a minimally invasive aortic valve replacement performed through a right transaxillary minithoracotomy. This approach uses a single 4-5 cm lateral incision, minimizing chest wall trauma while providing excellent cosmetic results. It redefines surgical perspective by offering a direct, non-mediated view of the aortic valve with a naturally perpendicular trajectory to the annular plane. This results in optimal eye-hand alignment, shorter working distance and enhanced operative control, simplifying the procedure, not only compared to endoscopic or robotic techniques, but also to right anterior minithoracotomy, where direct vision is obtained through a less favourable trajectory and a more limited anterior intercostal space. The procedure is performed using standard instruments and standardized set-up, without the need for specialized or expensive technologies, improving reproducibility and scalability. Its intrinsic simplicity makes it particularly suited for fast-track protocols, facilitating on-table extubation and early mobilization. The combination with rapid-deployment valves further streamlines the operation by reducing cardiopulmonary bypass and cross-clamp times, while the transaxillary exposure ensures accurate annular alignment and controlled, symmetrical deployment. In this case, the patient was extubated on-table and discharged home after 5 days, illustrating how this approach can simplify minimally invasive aortic valve surgery while maintaining safety and precision.

title: Ross procedure through hemisternotomy.
authorString: Komarov R, Tlisov B, Babakulova N, Kasim T, Lutsenko I, Kazban N, Al Atrach M.

journal.title: Multimedia manual of cardiothoracic surgery : MMCTS

abstractText: Ministernotomy is not a common approach in aortic root surgery. However, in our opinion, during the Ross procedure, and considering certain anthropometric parameters and the presence of an experienced aortic team, ministernotomy is a convenient approach for adequate visualization of the structures of the right ventricle outflow tract and the aortic root. Our team presents a successful clinical case of surgical treatment of a 24-year-old patient with a bicuspid aortic valve, annuloaortic ectasia (aortic annulus diameter of 30 mm) and grade 3 aortic regurgitation. In this specific clinical case, we demonstrate the step-by-step Ross procedure using ministernotomy.

title: Towards an understanding of injury in aortic tissue prior to actual failure: quantification of mechanically induced collagen damage using collagen hybridizing peptides
authorString: Pukaluk A, Haspinger DC, Wolinski H, Viertler C, Nawroth JC, Holzapfel GA.
abstractText: The development, validation, and optimization of endovascular aortic devices require quantitative assessment of tissue damage occurring during surgical interventions. Until now, this assessment—before complete failure—has been largely unfeasible for lack of a suitable methodology. Recently developed collagen hybridizing peptides (CHPs) allow selective detection of damage to collagen, the primary load-bearing constituent of the aortic wall. However, their application in large, mechanically loaded arteries has not yet been established. Therefore, we optimized an experimental workflow for large arteries that accounts for their energy-storage function and geometrical constraints; furthermore, we have characterized the tissue’s autofluorescence and selected a suitable CHP fluorophore. Specimens from a single porcine aorta were examined using uniaxial tensile testing, histological analysis, fluorescence spectral analysis, confocal microscopy, and quantitative image analysis to present collagen damage as a function of tissue stretch. The workflow detected load-induced collagen damage before tissue failure, whereas histological evaluation showed no obvious load-induced disruption. Damage scores were comparable between the undeformed control and the specimen stretched by a factor of 1.2, while specimens stretched beyond 1.2 exhibited elevated scores. This pattern corresponded to higher complication rates with excessive stent oversizing. Furthermore, the proposed protocol can be adapted for  ex vivo stent deployment experiments to compare collagen damage resulting from various aortic device designs and deployment conditions. Quantitative damage metrics could inform structurally motivated constitutive material models for computational simulations of endovascular interventions. Combined with histological and structural analyses, this workflow could also help link tissue composition—or organization—to individual susceptibility to damage.

title: Helical tomotherapy-based total body irradiation for hematopoietic stem cell transplantation: dosimetric, toxicity and survival outcomes in adults and children
authorString: Khattabi¹ Y, Jolnerovski¹ M, Diallo² A, Meknaci³ E, Grandgirard³ N, Marchesi³ V, Rubio⁴ M, Pochon⁵ C, Campidelli⁵ A, D'Aveni-Piney⁵ M, Gehin¹ W, Martz¹ N, Bruand¹ M, Stefani¹ A, Charra-Brunaud¹ C, Faivre¹ J.
abstractText: Background Total body irradiation (TBI) remains a cornerstone of conditioning regimens before hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, particularly in lymphoid malignancies. Helical tomotherapy may improve dose homogeneity and organ-at-risk sparing compared with conventional techniques. We evaluated the dosimetric characteristics, toxicity profile and clinical outcomes of helical tomotherapy-based TBI in adults and children. Methods This retrospective single-centre study included all consecutive patients treated with helical tomotherapy-based TBI at the Institut de Cancérologie de Lorraine between March 2020 and July 2024. TBI consisted of 12 Gy in 6 fractions (n = 21) or 8 Gy in 4 fractions (n = 27), delivered twice daily, or 2 Gy in a single fraction (n = 20). Toxicities were graded using CTCAE v5.0. Dosimetric parameters were analysed by dose regimen and age group, and relapse incidence, progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) were estimated. Results Sixty-eight patients were included (48 adults, 20 children); median follow-up was 18.5 months. Median PTV D90/D10 was 0.94 in both groups. In children treated with 12 Gy, median mean lung and kidney doses decreased from 8.5 and 12.1 Gy to 7.9 and 9.9 Gy after the introduction of paediatric-specific constraints in October 2022. The most frequent acute toxicities were fatigue (97%), anorexia (88%) and mucositis (78%), mostly grade 1–2. Grade ≥ 3 mucositis occurred in 10.4% of adults and 50% of children, and grade ≥ 3 anorexia in 58% of children receiving 12 Gy; no grade ≥ 3 radiation pneumonitis was observed. Late toxicities included chronic renal impairment (n = 2) and chronic pulmonary toxicity (n = 1) in adults, and hypothyroidism, growth impairment, chronic pericarditis, optic neuropathy and primary ovarian insufficiency (one each) in children. The 2-year cumulative incidence of relapse was 16.7% in adults and 20.0% in children; 2-year OS was 62.2% and 95.0%, and 2-year PFS 59.6% and 80.0%, respectively. Conclusions Helical tomotherapy-based TBI provided homogeneous target coverage and lung sparing with acceptable acute toxicity in adults and children, and paediatric-specific constraints improved kidney and lung sparing. Longer follow-up is required to assess late effects.

title: Natural history of trivial and mild aortic regurgitation in children with normal trileaflet aortic valves
authorString: Ebreo C, Nielsen J.
abstractText: Background Aortic regurgitation (AR) in trileaflet valves carries important morbidity in adults but is rare in children; its natural history, particularly for mild AR, is poorly defined. Objective To describe the natural history of trivial and mild AR in children with normal trileaflet aortic valves and normal aortic dimensions. Methods Retrospective cohort study at a single tertiary center (2011–2022). Children 0–17 years of age with normal trileaflet aortic valves and AR on at least two echocardiograms were included; structural or functional heart disease, genetic and metabolic syndromes, dilation of the aortic annulus or root, and inadequate image quality were exclusion criteria. Aortic and left ventricular (LV) dimensions were measured per American Society of Echocardiography guidelines; AR severity was graded by the interpreting cardiologist, and progression was assessed by side-by-side comparison of serial studies. Results Of 671 reports listing AR, 42 patients (45% trivial, 55% mild) met criteria. Median age was 9.6 years; median interval between studies was 35 months. AR was unchanged in 62% (26/42), improved in 33% (14/42), and worsened in 5% (2/42); in both children in whom AR worsened the aortic and LV dimensions remained normal. No child developed more than mild-to-moderate AR. Conclusions Trivial and mild AR in children with normal trileaflet valves and normal aortic dimensions was stable or improved in 95% over a median 35-month follow-up. Surveillance every 2–4 years is supported by our findings, with closer follow-up for children with concomitant heart disease or in those who develop aortic dilation.

title: Aortic stiffness and brain perfusion: a population-based study.
authorString: Gardarsdottir M, Sigurdsson S, Forsberg L, Mitchell GF, Launer LJ, Aspelund T, Gudnason V, Arnar DO.
abstractText:
Objectives

The objective was to examine the association of aortic stiffness and age with brain perfusion, brain structure, and cognitive function in a population-based sample.

Design

The sample included randomly selected descendants from a large community study. Aortic stiffness was assessed using carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity (CFPWV) measured by applanation tonometry. Brain perfusion and structural brain measures were obtained using magnetic resonance imaging, and cognitive performance was evaluated using standardized neuropsychological tests. Participants were stratified by the median CFPWV (≤ or >8.6 m/s) for comparison and associations were examined in multivariable regression analyses adjusted for age, sex, heart rate, mean arterial pressure, use of antihypertensive medication and CFPWV.

Results

The study included 269 subjects, average age 62 years. Participants with higher aortic stiffness (>8.6 m/s) were older, had higher heart rate, blood pressure, and more frequently used antihypertensive medication. Total brain, grey matter, and white matter perfusion were significantly lower in those with higher aortic stiffness. Relative brain volume was lower, and white matter hyperintensity (WMH) burden higher in unadjusted analyses, whereas cognitive performance did not differ. In multivariable models, increased aortic stiffness was independently associated with lower total brain perfusion, while chronological age was independently associated with lower brain volumes and greater WMH burden.

Conclusions

These findings indicate that aortic stiffness and aging represent related but distinct contributors to brain health. Aortic stiffness was independently associated with reduced brain perfusion, whereas age was the dominant determinant of structural brain changes.

title: Geranylgeranylacetone attenuates atherosclerosis via the Matcap2-Apelin-ABCA1/ABCG1 signaling axis.
authorString: Chen Y, Qiu J, Li M, Wu Y.
abstractText:
Background

Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease remains a leading global health threat, driven by macrophage foam cell formation and chronic inflammation. Geranylgeranylacetone (GGA), an anti-ulcer drug known to induce heat shock proteins, may confer cardiovascular benefits, yet its direct anti-atherosclerotic mechanisms are not fully understood.

Methods

ApoE-/- mice fed a high-fat diet received GGA (400 mg/kg/d) for 12 weeks. Atherosclerotic lesions, plaque composition (necrotic core, collagen, macrophage infiltration), plasma lipids, and cytokine levels were evaluated. In vitro, THP-1-derived foam cells were treated with Ox-LDL and GGA (0.1-100 μmol/L). Cholesterol efflux, lipid accumulation, and the expression of Matcap2, Apelin, ABCA1/ABCG1, apolipoproteins, and inflammatory factors were measured. siRNA silencing was used to validate the Matcap2-Apelin-ABCA1/ABCG1 axis.

Results

GGA significantly reduced aortic plaque burden, increased collagen content, decreased macrophage infiltration, lowered total cholesterol, triglycerides, and LDL-C, raised HDL-C, and improved inflammatory cytokine profiles (decreased IL-6 and TNF-α; increased IL-10) in ApoE-/- mice. In foam cells, GGA enhanced cholesterol efflux, reduced cholesteryl ester content and lipid droplets, and upregulated Matcap2, Apelin, ABCA1/ABCG1, and ApoA1/A2/A4, while downregulating ApoB, IL-6, and TNF-α. Silencing either Matcap2 or Apelin abrogated GGA-induced upregulation of ABCA1/ABCG1, cholesterol efflux, and the protective apolipoprotein and anti-inflammatory phenotypes.

Conclusion

GGA attenuates atherosclerosis by activating the Matcap2-Apelin-ABCA1/ABCG1 signaling axis, thereby promoting reverse cholesterol transport and resolving inflammation. These findings support GGA as a promising repurposed drug with both cardioprotective and gastroprotective benefits.

title: Left Atrial Appendage Closure Versus DOAC Therapy in Atrial Fibrillation: A Phenotype-Centered Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomized Trials.
authorString: Kumar A, Arham M, Kumar P, Ali Z, Srivastava K, Tahir HB, Hameed H, Shafique M, Kainat F, Waqar H, Kumar S, Jabbar ABA, Garcia M, Mann JA, Becker RC.
abstractText:
Introduction

Left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) has emerged as a selective alternative to long-term oral anticoagulation in appropriately selected patients with non-valvular high-risk atrial fibrillation (AF). However, individual contemporary RCTs remain underpowered to detect infrequent but clinically important outcomes.

Methodology

This meta-analysis was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261384938). A systematic literature search was conducted to identify RCTs comparing LAAC with direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) therapy in patients with non-valvular high-risk AF. Statistical analyses were performed using R, with a two-sided significance threshold of p < 0.05.

Results

Five RCTs (n = 6,239; LAAC: 3,126; DOACs: 3,113) with 1:1 non-inferiority design were included. There were no significant differences between LAAC and DOACs for the composite endpoint, all-cause mortality or stroke. Systemic thromboembolism was significantly higher with LAAC (RR 2.53, 95% CI 1.04-6.19; p = 0.04; I² = 28.9%). LAAC was associated with significantly lower rates of minor bleeding (RR 0.48, 95% CI 0.40-0.58; p < 0.01; I² = 6.9%) and nonprocedural clinically relevant bleeding (RR 0.56, 95% CI 0.48-0.65; p < 0.01; I² = 0.0%). Pericardial effusion was significantly higher with LAAC (RR 2.35, 95% CI 1.15-4.83; p = 0.02; I² = 0.0%). Serious adverse events were modestly but significantly higher in the LAAC group (RR 1.08, 95% CI 1.02-1.14).

Conclusion

In contemporary randomized trials, LAAC and DOAC-based therapy showed no significant differences in mortality or overall stroke outcomes but demonstrated divergent safety tradeoffs. LAAC was associated with less nonprocedural clinically relevant bleeding, while systemic thromboembolism, pericardial effusion, and serious adverse events occurred more frequently with device-based therapy. These findings support phenotype-specific selection of LAAC rather than routine substitution for evidence-based anticoagulation.

title: Therapeutic lactate in critically ill patients: Fuel, fluid, or drug?
authorString: Hørsdal OK, Nalos M, Nielsen R.
abstractText: Lactate occupies a paradoxical position in critical care. Traditionally regarded as a marker of physiological stress, it is increasingly recognized as an important metabolic substrate with potential therapeutic effects. In their meta-analysis of randomized trials, Labenbacher and colleagues summarize the current clinical evidence for hypertonic sodium lactate treatment (HSL) across heterogeneous critically ill populations. Although no mortality benefit can be established, the available evidence raises several important mechanistic and methodological questions. First, "lactate therapy" is not a single intervention as HSL simultaneously alters lactate availability, sodium load, tonicity, and acid-base balance. Second, currently used regimens differ markedly in dose, duration, and achieved plasma lactate concentrations, precluding a meaningful dose-exposure-response framework. Third, the physiological response may depend strongly on the underlying hemodynamic and metabolic phenotype with signals of improved cardiac output in some cardiovascular settings but inconsistent findings across other disease states. At this stage, the key question is therefore not simply whether lactate "works" nor whether it improves mortality, but which physiological effect is being targeted, in which patient phenotype, at what exposure, and through which mechanism. Future studies should disentangle the metabolic, osmotic, vascular, and acid-base effects of lactate-containing solutions before definitive clinical outcome trials are undertaken.

title: Adverse Effects of Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) Inhibitors in Pediatric Heart Failure: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Proportions.
authorString: Cakan B, Ardali A, Odemis E.
abstractText:
Objective

Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors have become a foundational therapy for adult heart failure across the entire spectrum of ejection fraction, but their safety profile in children with heart failure has not been quantitatively synthesized. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of proportions to summarize the incidence of adverse events associated with SGLT2 inhibitors in pediatric heart failure.

Study design

In this systematic review and meta-analysis of proportions (PROSPERO CRD420261355711; PRISMA 2020), five databases were searched through June 2026 for studies of any design reporting adverse events among pediatric patients receiving an SGLT2 inhibitor for heart failure. Random-effects incidence estimates were pooled using logit-transformed proportions with restricted maximum-likelihood estimation and modified Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman confidence intervals; risk of bias and GRADE certainty were assessed.

Results

Ten studies (573 unique children; 2023-2026) were included; eight studies (572 patients; maximum pooled denominator 474) were meta-analyzed, and one case report was summarized narratively. Dapagliflozin accounted for 94.1% of exposures. Study-level dapagliflozin doses ranged from 0.11 to 0.23 mg/kg/day, while the single cohort reporting empagliflozin used a median dose of 0.13 mg/kg/day. No regimen was derived from pediatric heart-failure pharmacokinetic data, and in the only cohort reporting a comparison, infants received a higher weight-normalized dose than older children (0.18 versus 0.16 mg/kg/day). Pooled incidences were: any adverse event 21.2% (95% CI 10.7-37.8%), acute kidney injury 10.7% (3.5-28.1%), urinary tract infection 7.8% (4.8-12.4%), treatment discontinuation 7.0% (4.5-10.6%), all-cause mortality 5.6% (2.4-12.5%), hypoglycemia 2.9% (0.9-9.3%), genital mycotic infection 2.7% (0.9-8.2%), and diabetic ketoacidosis 1.3% (0.4-3.9%). No deaths were attributed to therapy, and no cases of euglycemic ketoacidosis or Fournier gangrene occurred. Directional efficacy signals were consistently favorable, with left ventricular ejection fraction improving in five of six cohorts and natriuretic peptide levels declining across all seven in which they were assessed.

Conclusions

SGLT2 inhibitors had a tolerable safety profile in pediatric heart failure, mirroring the adult experience. Adequately powered randomized trials with standardized adverse-event grading are needed.

Registration

PROSPERO identifier no. CRD420261355711.

title: Morning Versus Evening Antihypertensive Medication and Risk of Cardiovascular Disease: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
authorString: Jaiswal V, Nain P, Nasir YM, Garimella V, Shrestha AB, Shama N, Jaiswal A, Fonarow GC, Frishman WH, Aronow WS.
abstractText: Hypertension significantly contributes to the risk of cardiovascular disease and associated mortality. The timing of medication use and associated cardiovascular outcomes is not well established, with conflicting results. We evaluated the association between morning versus evening antihypertensive medication and cardiovascular outcomes. We performed a systematic literature search on PubMed, Scopus, and ClinicalTrial.gov for relevant randomized controlled trials (RCTs) from inception until June 5, 2026. Studies were considered eligible for inclusion if patients with hypertension received antihypertensive medication in the intervention group during the morning/daytime and in the control group in the evening. Odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using a random-effect model, and a P value of <0.05 was considered statistically significant. Six RCTs with 46,857 patients (23,488 assigned to morning antihypertensive medication and 23,369 assigned to evening antihypertensive medication) were included in the analysis. The mean age of patients was 63.3 years. Pooled analysis demonstrated no statistically significant difference between morning and evening antihypertensive medication dosing for all-cause mortality (OR 1.30, 95% CI 0.92-1.85, P = 0.14), major adverse cardiovascular events (OR 1.28, 95% CI 0.93-1.76, P = 0.13), or stroke (OR 1.45, 95% CI 0.96-2.19, P = 0.08). This meta-analysis supports the findings of the BEDMED 2025 trial, with no significant differences between morning and evening administration of antihypertensive drugs and cardiovascular outcomes.

title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and the Risk of Glaucoma and Ocular Hypertension: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Alotaibi HA, Alshaibani AK, Alzahrani RM, Alanazi BR, Alamoudi A, Almutairi GM.
abstractText:
Topic

Whether glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1RA) use is associated with a lower risk of incident glaucoma or ocular hypertension (OHT) in adults, and whether the association differs by diabetes status or comparator.

Clinical relevance

Glaucoma is the leading cause of irreversible blindness worldwide, and every licensed treatment targets lowering intraocular pressure (IOP); none protects retinal ganglion cells directly. GLP-1RAs are widely prescribed and have been proposed to be neuroprotective, so whether this class of medication alters glaucoma risk matters at prescribing and to the search for pressure-independent treatment. Four earlier meta-analyses found no significant association but pooled non-equivalent comparators.

Methods

Systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies, following PRISMA 2020 and registered on PROSPERO (CRD420251082642). PubMed was searched on 15 April 2026 and updated to 30 August 2026, with CENTRAL, Europe PMC, the first 100 Google Scholar results and bidirectional citation tracking as supplementary sources. Eligible studies were retrospective cohort or nested case-control studies of GLP-1RA exposure with incident glaucoma, OHT or IOP change as the outcome and with adjustment for confounding. Two reviewers screened, extracted and applied ROBINS-I. Estimates were pooled by DerSimonian-Laird random effects, with a Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman (HKSJ) interval, a 95% prediction interval and GRADE.

Results

Ten studies were included from 406 screened records. Six cohorts covering 225,814 matched or analysed patients were pooled. GLP-1RA use was associated with a lower incidence of recorded glaucoma or OHT (pooled hazard ratio 0.69, 95% CI 0.59 to 0.80; HKSJ CI 0.56 to 0.85), but heterogeneity was 58.5%, the 95% prediction interval (0.44 to 1.08) included no effect, and certainty was low. The association held after all TriNetX studies were removed (0.78, 0.71 to 0.85) and after restriction to open-angle outcomes (0.66, 0.53 to 0.82). Diabetes status, comparator type and data platform could not be separated.

Conclusion

Low-certainty observational evidence suggests GLP-1RA use is not associated with a higher risk of glaucoma or OHT and may be associated with a lower one. Confounding by indication, coded outcome ascertainment and a prediction interval that includes no effect mean protection has not been shown. The findings support reassurance and the randomized trial under way.

title: Impact of dynamic pump speed adjustment versus constant speed in left ventricle assist device patients on exercise performance: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
authorString: Quick Lourenço de Lima S, Freitas Silva V, de Medeiros Fernandes M, Pereira Silva R, Filipe Cavalcante Uchoa Furtado J, Liberata Barbosa Bandeira L, Giorgi J, Alves Lopes R.
abstractText: BackgroundAdjusting pump speed in patients with left ventricular assist devices (LVADs) during exercise may improve hemodynamics and enhance functional capacity in advanced heart failure, but its clinical benefit over fixed-speed operation remains uncertain. We evaluated whether dynamic, exercise-driven LVAD speed modulation improves physical performance compared to fixed-speed settings.Methods and resultsPubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were systematically searched for studies comparing dynamic adjustment versus fixed pump speed control during exercise in patients with LVADs. Continuous outcomes were analyzed using mean differences (MD), and binary outcomes using risk ratios (RR), with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Statistical analysis was performed using R (version 4.3.1). Eight studies were included, with study sample sizes totaling 124 participants; seven used crossover designs and one used a non-randomized repeated-measures design. Potential overlap between two reports from Jung et al. precluded interpretation of this total as the number of unique participants. Dynamic pump-speed modulation was associated with higher peak oxygen uptake (VO<sub>2</sub>) (MD 1.07 mL/kg/min; 95% CI 0.73 to 1.41; p < 0.001; I<sup>2</sup> = 42%) and LVAD pump flow at peak/end of exercise (MD 1.24 L/min; 95% CI 0.68 to 1.79; p < 0.001; I<sup>2</sup> = 89%). No differences were observed in peak cardiac output (MD 0.12 L/min; 95% CI -0.74 to 0.98; p = 0.786; I<sup>2</sup> = 67%) or ventilatory efficiency, assessed by the VE/VCO<sub>2</sub> slope (MD -1.58; 95% CI -3.25 to 0.09; p = 0.063; I<sup>2</sup> = 76%).ConclusionDynamic LVAD speed adjustment may improve exercise capacity, as suggested by higher peak VO<sub>2</sub>, although peak cardiac output and ventilatory efficiency showed no clear improvement. Given the small studies, heterogeneous protocols and possible participant overlap, it remains uncertain whether this apparent benefit is sustained or clinically meaningful to patients.

title: Vernakalant Versus Other Antiarrhythmic Drugs for Pharmacological Cardioversion of Recent-Onset Atrial Fibrillation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis With Trial Sequential Analysis.
authorString: Elawfi B, Elazab A, Thobaiti FTA, Alnefaie RS, Bukhader HM, Alqahtani AA, Almarshoodi KA, Imran HM, Elkasaby MH, Frishman WH, Aronow WS.
abstractText: Vernakalant is an atrial-selective antiarrhythmic drug for the rapid conversion of recent-onset atrial fibrillation, but its effectiveness relative to alternative drugs remains uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis included studies comparing intravenous vernakalant with another antiarrhythmic drug in adults with recent-onset atrial fibrillation. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched through March 2026. The primary outcome was conversion to sinus rhythm; secondary outcomes were time to conversion, electrical cardioversion, and adverse events. Random-effects models, trial sequential analysis, and GRADE were used. Nine studies (3 randomized, 1 quasi-randomized, and 5 observational; 1788 patients or episodes) compared vernakalant with amiodarone, ibutilide, flecainide, procainamide, or propafenone. Conversion occurred in 69.0% of patients receiving vernakalant and 53.0% of those receiving a comparator (odds ratio [OR], 2.52; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.51-4.21; I2 = 72%). Heterogeneity was explained by the amiodarone comparisons (OR, 18.14; interaction P < 0.001); against the other comparators, the OR was 1.77 (95% CI, 1.41-2.22; I2 = 0%). Vernakalant shortened time to conversion among responders (mean difference, -19.3 minutes; 95% CI, -24.2 to -14.4) and reduced electrical cardioversion (OR, 0.50; 95% CI, 0.34-0.73), without a significant difference in adverse events (OR, 0.78; 95% CI, 0.57-1.08). The cumulative Z-curve crossed the trial sequential monitoring boundary, but the certainty of evidence was low for all outcomes.

title: Long-Term Cardiovascular Adverse Events in Patients with Chronic Myelogenous Leukemia Treated with Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors.
authorString: Zureigat H, Mohamed AN, Govande S, Zabor EC, Alchirazi MA, Dhakal A, Mushtaq A, Rehman N, Foster P, Elghoul Y, Berube B, Ramonfaur D, Francis B, Jain AG, Molina JC, Balderman S, Singh A, Gerds AT, Advani AS, Carraway HE, Kalaycio M, Mukherjee S, Moudgil R, Mustafa Ali MK.
abstractText:
Background

patients with chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML) treated with tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) are at risk for cardiotoxicity. Risk estimates from clinical trials may be limited by healthier populations and short follow-up durations.

Materials and methods

we evaluated the incidence of cardiovascular adverse events (CVD-AE) and echocardiographic changes as a secondary outcome in CML patients on TKIs, accounting for cardiovascular risk from prior TKI exposure. CML patients treated with TKIs at Cleveland Clinic (2007-2022) were included. TKIs analyzed were imatinib, dasatinib, nilotinib, bosutinib, ponatinib, and asciminib. Data included demographics, comorbidities, treatments, and follow-up. Outcomes were overall survival and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE): acute coronary syndrome (ACS), heart failure, stroke, peripheral arterial disease, and revascularization. Pleural effusions, pericardial effusions and pulmonary hypertension were assessed. Echocardiograms were collected at baseline. Multivariable Cox regression and generalized linear mixed models were applied.

Results

among 357 patients (median age 56; 57% male; 85% White), 518 CVD-AE occurred during median follow-up of 7.2 years. Compared with imatinib, nilotinib was associated with increased ACS (HR 3.5, P = 0.02), dasatinib with heart failure (HR 2.5, P = 0.04), and dasatinib, and asciminib with pleural (HRs 3.5, 5.8; P < 0.05) and pericardial effusions (HR 5.1, 21.6; P < 0.05). Dasatinib was associated with lower venous thrombosis (HR 0.1, P = 0.02). MACE incidence did not differ significantly among TKIs. Among 69 patients with serial echocardiograms, ponatinib decreased left ventricular ejection fraction (β = -5.2, P = 0.008) and bosutinib increased global longitudinal strain (β = 3.0, P = 0.037).

Conclusion

Cardiovascular risks differ among TKIs, and therapy duration influences echocardiographic changes.

title: Quality of Life and Participant Satisfaction in the ACAF Clinical Trial: Advanced Care Planning in Heart Failure.
authorString: Sánchez B, Vicente MJ, Mower L, López G, Aguilar F, García R, Higginbotham K, Jones ID, Velasco T, Herreros B.
abstractText:
Introduction

A clinical trial, the ACAF study (Advanced Care Planning in Heart Failure), was designed to evaluate the effectiveness of an Advance Care Planning (ACP) programme in patients with advanced heart failure (HF). This article presents the results regarding quality of life and participant satisfaction in the ACAF study.

Methods

A multicentre randomised clinical trial was conducted in four hospitals. Patient allocation to the study groups was performed using alternate sampling. The ACP programme was applied to the intervention group, while the control group received the routine follow-up in heart failure outpatient clinics. Quality of life was assessed using the Minnesota Living with Heart Failure Questionnaire, and satisfaction was evaluated using a questionnaire specifically developed for the project.

Results

A total of 67 patients were recruited and randomly assigned to the intervention group (n = 29; 43.3%) and the control group (n = 38; 56.7%). Quality of life was assessed at baseline and at 1-year follow-up: 58 in the baseline analysis and 42 at 1 year, with 18 losses to follow-up (8 voluntary withdrawals, 5 deaths, 7 incomplete questionnaires, and 1 exclusion due to tumor diagnosis). After one year, quality of life improved in both groups, with no statistically significant differences between them. The satisfaction questionnaire indicated a very satisfactory experience among patients who participated in the programme.

Conclusions

The implementation of a PADS programme in patients with advanced heart failure is associated with a high level of satisfaction among participants, who positively value shared decision-making. Furthermore, the programme does not worsen quality of life compared with standard follow-up in heart failure clinics, supporting its safety and acceptability in this clinical setting.

title: Integrating the common-sense model of self-regulation into early progressive mobilization program in patients hospitalized for acute decompensated heart failure: a randomized controlled trial.
authorString: Liu X, Yu M, Ning L, Ba Y, Ni J, Chen T, Zhang Q, Zheng B.

journal.title: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care

abstractText:
Background

Patients hospitalized with acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF) have impaired physical function. Concerns about safety, falls and a perceived need for bed rest, may restrict mobility and contribute to deconditioning.

Objectives

To evaluate an early progressive mobilization program based on the Common-Sense Model of Self-Regulation (CSM) in patients hospitalized for ADHF.

Methods

A randomized trial with blinded assessment assigned 174 patients to routine care (n = 87) or the CSM-based program (n = 87). The intervention comprised four 40-60-minute face-to-face interviews and one 15-20-minute telephone consultation. Outcomes included 6-minute walk distance (6MWD), grip strength (GS), 30-second arm curl test (30s-ACT) performance, cardiac output (CO), thoracic fluid content (TFC), systolic time ratio (STR), and Exercise Benefits/Barriers Scale (EBBS) scores.

Results

Least-squares mean differences (95% CIs) favored the intervention for 6MWD (16.91 m, 1.98-31.83; P = 0.026), exercise-benefit scores (6.00, 0.99-11.01; P = 0.019), and exercise-barrier scores (-2.54, -4.82 to -0.26; P = 0.029). Quantile-regression differences (95% CIs) were significant for GS (males: 3.20 kg, 1.10-5.60; P = 0.006; females: 3.10 kg, 0.50-5.80; P = 0.007), 30s-ACT performance (2.00 repetitions, 0.00-4.00; P = 0.046), CO (0.80 L/min, 0.40-1.20; P < 0.001), TFC (-3.00 kΩ⁻¹, -5.00 to 0.00; P = 0.01), and STR (-0.05%, -0.08 to 0.02; P = < 0.001). Subgroup analyses suggested greater 6MWD improvement in subgroups defined by BMI 18.5-23.9 kg/m², NYHA class I-III at admission, and anemia.

Conclusion

The CSM-based program improved functional and hemodynamic outcomes and exercise perceptions.

title: Dominant A1 Flow Diverter Deployment for Bilateral-Supply Anterior Communicating Artery Aneurysms: A Single-Center Retrospective Experience in 30 Consecutive Patients
authorString: Ding Z, Guan T, Li Z, Huang J, Jin D, An T, Cheng G, Liu Y.
abstractText: Background Anterior communicating artery (AComA) aneurysms with bilateral anterior cerebral artery (ACA) supply pose unique challenges for flow diverter (FD) deployment owing to small parent vessel caliber and hemodynamic vulnerability. Evidence supporting a dominant A1 strategy in this population remains limited. Methods Thirty consecutive adults with unruptured bilateral-supply AComA aneurysms treated with FD implanted exclusively in the dominant A1 between April 2023 and February 2026 were retrospectively identified from a single-center database (Chinese Clinical Trial Registry ChiCTR2600117882, retrospectively registered January 12, 2026). Inclusion required angiographic confirmation of bilateral ACA supply and unilateral A1 dominance (asymmetry ratio ≥ 1.1 on DSA). Preprocedural dual antiplatelet therapy (≥ 5 days) was verified by platelet function testing when available. Follow-up combined modified Rankin Scale (mRS) assessment with DSA scheduled at 6 and 12 months and annually thereafter. The primary endpoint was adequate angiographic occlusion (O'Kelly–Marotta [OKM] C + D) at last follow-up. Secondary endpoints were complete occlusion (OKM D), composite major complications, and absence of treatment-related neurological worsening (mRS stability or improvement from baseline). Results All 30 procedures were technically successful (100.0%). Median age was 59 years (interquartile range 54–62); 60.0% were male. Hyperlipidemia was present in 53.3%, hypertension in 50.0%, prior ischemic stroke in 40.0%, and admission mRS > 0 in 26.7%. Median parent vessel diameter was 2.25 mm; median A1 asymmetry ratio was 1.40, with left dominance in 63.3%. Nine FD models were used; median diameter difference < 0.3 mm in 46.7%. At a median angiographic follow-up of 7.5 months (DSA ≥ 6 months in all patients; ≥12 months in 40%), complete occlusion (OKM D) was achieved in 24/30 (80.0%) and adequate occlusion (OKM C + D) in 26/30 (86.7%), increasing to 30/30 (100.0%) when the four collar-sign borderline cases were counted as adequate. The composite major complication rate (symptomatic ischemic stroke, symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage, or mortality) was 6.7%. No patient experienced treatment-related neurological worsening. No mortality, retreatment, or loss to follow-up occurred. Conclusions Dominant A1 FD deployment is technically feasible and achieved high rates of adequate angiographic occlusion without treatment-related neurological worsening in bilateral-supply AComA aneurysms. Longer-term durability and prospective multicenter validation are warranted.

title: Cost-effectiveness of a transvalvular microaxial flow pump in infarct-related cardiogenic shock from the perspective of German statutory health insurance.
authorString: Boettger P, Sossalla S, Buerke M, Birkner B, Wild EM.

journal.title: Expert review of pharmacoeconomics & outcomes research

abstractText:
Background

In infarct-related cardiogenic shock, a transvalvular microaxial flow pump reduced 180 day mortality but increased adverse events. We evaluated its cost-effectiveness for German statutory health insurance (SHI).

Research design and methods

A cohort state-transition model compared the two strategies over a lifetime horizon: a 180 day acute phase from trial outcomes, and chronic states with or without heart failure. Costs and quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs) were discounted at 3% in 2023 euros. Parameter uncertainty was assessed probabilistically and unresolved acute payments by threshold analysis.

Results

The pump yielded 1.06 additional QALYs at incremental costs of €38,121 and an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio of €36,083 per QALY. At an illustrative willingness-to-pay threshold of €50,000 per QALY, the probability of cost-effectiveness was 86%. Bleeding 21.8 versus 11.9%, limb ischemia 5.6 versus 1.1%. Due to the lack of arm-specific case-group data, the reference analysis assumed no between-arm difference in acute payments; net monetary benefit (NMB) remained positive below €14,703.

Conclusions

Under the reference assumptions, the pump may be cost-effective for German SHI, conditional on an unresolved acute payment difference in which arm-specific routine billing data could be determined.

Clinical trial registration

https://www.clinicaltrials.gov identifier: NCT01633502. This economic analysis was not performed separately.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Acute Carotid Stenting for Tandem Lesions in Acute Ischemic Stroke: A Multicenter, Real-World Registry Cohort Study
authorString: Chen H, Sun J, Zheng C, Wang K, Yi T, Cai W, Li J, Hu W, Han H, Cai X.
abstractText: Background Whether to routinely stent extracranial carotid lesions during endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for anterior circulation tandem lesions remains debated. Because current evidence relies heavily on Western cohorts with different stroke etiologies, we investigated the efficacy and safety of acute extracranial stenting in a real-world Chinese cohort predominantly characterized by atherosclerosis. Methods We retrospectively analyzed patients with anterior circulation tandem lesions treated with EVT within 24 hours of onset across seven comprehensive stroke centers in China (July 2021–December 2023). Patients were stratified into acute stenting and non-stenting groups. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to evaluate 90-day functional independence (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] 0–2), 90-day vascular patency (> 50% residual stenosis), and safety outcomes. Results Of 142 patients (95.8% atherosclerotic etiology), 113 (79.6%) underwent acute stenting and 29 (20.4%) received non-stenting management, with a higher baseline rate of complete extracranial occlusion in the stent group (69.0% vs. 37.9%, p = 0.002). The stent group achieved a higher rate of 90-day functional independence (61.9% vs. 44.8%). After multivariable adjustment, acute stenting was independently associated with improved 90-day functional independence (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 3.27, 95% CI 1.24–8.66, p = 0.017), markedly reduced > 50% residual stenosis at 90 days (4.6% vs. 32.1%; aOR 0.04, 95% CI 0.01–0.24, p < 0.001), and lower odds of overall in-hospital complications (31.2% vs. 52.0%; aOR 0.34, 95% CI 0.12–1.00, p = 0.049). Complete reperfusion, 48-hour intracranial hemorrhage, and 90-day mortality did not differ significantly between groups. Conclusion In this real-world Chinese cohort, acute extracranial stenting during EVT for tandem lesions improved 90-day functional outcomes and vascular patency while reducing in-hospital complications without increasing bleeding or mortality risks, awaiting confirmation from randomized trials.

title: Genetically Proxied NLRP3 Inflammasome Downregulation and Cardiovascular Disease
authorString: Zuckerman BP, Zangas P, Zhang L, Osadcha A, Zhao SS, Georgakis MK.
abstractText:
Background

The inhibition of NOD-, LRR- and pyrin domain-containing protein 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome is an emerging therapeutic strategy for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD). Although early clinical trials demonstrate reductions in inflammatory biomarkers, whether these translate into cardiovascular benefit remains uncertain. We investigated the potential efficacy and safety of NLRP3 inhibition using human genetics.

Methods

We developed a cis -genetic instrument for NLRP3 downregulation using C-reactive protein (CRP) associated variants (P<5×10⁻⁸) within the NLRP3 locus (±100 kb of NLRP3 transcription start site) from 575,531 participants. Mendelian Randomization and colocalization analyses assessed the effect of the genetic instrument against gene expression of NLRP3 and other inflammatory mediators in immune cells, downstream inflammatory biomarkers, and pharmacodynamic responses to the NLRP3 inhibitor ruvonoflast. Two-sample Mendelian randomization assessed cardiovascular, cardiometabolic, and infectious outcomes, followed by phenome-wide analyses of 1,387 clinical outcomes.

Results

Using 14 variants in the NLRP3 locus, we constructed a genetic instrument that corresponded to a 19% difference in circulating CRP between the extreme percentiles of its distribution. Colocalisation evidence suggested the effects on CRP to be driven by reduced NLRP3 expression in naïve monocytes (PP.H4=98.7%). In accordance with the expected biological role of NLRP3, genetically proxied NLRP3 downregulation by the constructed instrument was associated with lower IL-18 (β=−0.11; 95%CI, −0.14 to −0.08) and IL-6 (β=−0.15; 95%CI, −0.17 to −0.12) and broadly similar pharmacodynamic effects to the NLRP3 inhibitor ruvonoflast across 8 biomarkers. Genetically proxied NLRP3 inhibition was associated with lower risk of recurrent pericarditis (OR per 19% decrease in CRP, 0.68, 95%CI, 0.58-0.80), but slightly elevated risk of coronary artery disease (OR, 1.06; 95%CI, 1.03–1.08) and peripheral arterial disease (OR, 1.10; 95%CI, 1.04–1.15) and no effect on ischaemic stroke (OR, 0.98; 95%CI, 0.94-1.02). The instrument was also associated with higher carotid-intima-media thickness and a worse cardiometabolic profile with increasing effects on blood pressure, waist-to-hip ratio, LDL cholesterol, and triglycerides. We found no associations with increased risk for prespecified infectious disease outcomes.

Conclusions

A genetic proxy for NLRP3 inflammasome downregulation reproduced key molecular effects of pharmacological NLRP3 inhibition but was not associated with reduced ASCVD risk.

Clinical perspective

What is new?
