- We developed a genetic proxy of NLRP3 inflammasome downregulation comprising 14 variants within the NLRP3 locus. - Mirroring the biology of NLRP3 signaling, genetically proxied NLRP3 downregulation was associated with lower IL-6 and IL-18 concentrations and showed broadly concordant biomarker effects with the oral NLRP3 inhibitor, ruvonoflast. - Despite mimicking pharmacologic NLRP3 inhibition at a biomarker level, genetically proxied NLRP3 downregulation was not associated with reduced lifetime cardiometabolic risk.

What are the clinical implications?

- In view of emerging therapeutic efforts to target NLRP3 inflammasome, we could not find human genetic evidence supporting that NLRP3 downregulation could reduce risk of cardiovascular events.

title: Longitudinal laboratory patterns and subsequent mortality in intensive care admissions with evidence of active abdominal aortic aneurysm: a MIMIC-IV landmark study
authorString: Hongfei A, Yuan F, Jinghan L, Yihe G, Xuanzhe G, Zezheng Z, Yaling L, Shuo W, Zhihua R, Zhong C, Yaoguo Y.
abstractText: Background Intensive care unit (ICU) admissions involving abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) are heterogeneous, and conventional summary values may obscure temporal change. We evaluated whether ordered laboratory measurements identify reproducible patterns associated with subsequent mortality in admissions with active AAA evidence. Methods We conducted a retrospective MIMIC-IV v3.1 landmark study. Active AAA evidence required a principal diagnosis, rupture code, repair code, or text-supported rupture or repair. Admissions alive and hospitalized at ICU hour 72 were eligible. Six laboratory markers were summarized in three consecutive 24-hour windows. Twelve posterior-sampling iterative imputations were followed by Gaussian mixture models and consensus clustering. Subsequent mortality was analyzed using logistic regression with patient-clustered robust standard errors. Results Of 1,343 AAA-coded ICU admissions, 526 had active AAA evidence. After excluding 16 deaths and 59 live discharges before hour 72, 451 admissions from 433 patients remained. The selected solution comprised a lower-intensity pattern (n = 289) and a multisystem derangement pattern (n = 162), with a median adjusted Rand index of 0.926. Subsequent mortality was 3.5% and 12.3%, respectively. After adjustment for age, sex, and chronic kidney disease, the odds ratio was 3.79 (95% confidence interval, 1.40-10.25; P = .009). Sensitivity estimates were directionally consistent across alternative covariate, cohort, completeness, and marker specifications. In post hoc analyses, excluding creatinine disrupted class agreement (adjusted Rand index, -0.011) and attenuated the association (odds ratio, 1.65; 95% confidence interval, 0.67–4.06); additional adjustment for early creatinine yielded an odds ratio of 2.57 (95% confidence interval, 0.87–7.58). Conclusions Ordered 72-hour laboratory measurements identified two reproducible patterns associated with subsequent mortality. The classification was substantially anchored by renal function and should be viewed as exploratory rather than as an AAA-specific subtype or clinical prediction tool. Trial registration Clinical trial number: not applicable.

title: The efficacy of adding leg wrapping to prophylactic norepinephrine infusion in reducing the incidence of post-spinal hypotension in elective cesarean section: a prospective double-blinded randomized clinical trial.
authorString: Abdelhady MA, Hamed MA, Abdelrayif AM, Mohammed AA, Bassiouny MM, Ragab MH.

journal.title: Journal of anesthesia, analgesia and critical care

abstractText:
Background

Various pharmacological and non-pharmacological methods have been studied in the literature to reduce the incidence of post-spinal maternal hypotension. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of adding bilateral lower-limb wrapping to a prophylactic norepinephrine infusion in reducing the incidence of hypotension in parturients receiving intrathecal anesthesia for cesarean delivery.

Methods

This prospective randomized trial included parturients undergoing elective cesarean section under spinal anesthesia. Parturients were divided into the following: norepinephrine group (N) (n = 84), and norepinephrine and leg wrapping group (NW) (n = 84). The 0.05 µg/kg/min norepinephrine infusion continued until 5 min after fetal delivery. The primary outcome was the incidence of post-spinal maternal hypotension. Secondary outcomes included the incidence of maternal severe hypotension, bradycardia, tachycardia, hypertension, nausea, vomiting, post-delivery hypotension, and neonatal outcomes.

Results

The final analysis included 168 patients. The incidence of hypotension in the NW group was lower than in the N group (7/84 [8.3%], 18/84 [21.4%], respectively) with P = 0.017, RR = 0.39, and CI: (0.17-0.88). According to the Kaplan-Meier curve with the log-rank test, the time to post-spinal maternal hypotension differed significantly (P = 0.016), with a restricted mean time of 21.1 min in the NW group and 19.7 min in the N group (hazard ratio = 2.82 for the N group vs. NW, 95%CI: (1.18-6.76). Furthermore, a repeated-measures analysis revealed significant group-by-time interactions for both heart rate (P = 0.003) and systolic blood pressure (P = 0.028), demonstrating superior longitudinal hemodynamic stability in the NW group. No statistically significant between-group differences were detected for secondary maternal and neonatal outcomes.

Conclusion

When added to a prophylactic 0.05 µg/kg/min norepinephrine infusion, leg wrapping decreased the incidence of postspinal maternal hypotension and enhanced hemodynamic stability over time during elective cesarean delivery.

Trial registration

This study was registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06496061; principal investigator: Mohamed Ahmed Hamed; date of registration: 11/07/2024; no protocol amendments or study changes after trial start).

title: Major Bleeding After Catheter-Directed Thrombolysis for Acute Pulmonary Embolism: Derivation and Transferability of the F-HARP Risk Assessment Model.
authorString: Tsaftaridis N, Fürbringer-Schwarz A, Fumagalli RM, Catalani F, Rimann L, Madaro B, Avgerinos E, Bikdeli B, Bura-Riviere A, Chaer RA, Engelberger RP, Farmakis IT, Graif A, Guirado L, Jaber WA, Klein F, Klok FA, Konstantinides SV, Kroupa J, Kucher N, Lokken RP, Monreal MM, Obradovic S, Ozcinar E, Rossi JS, Ruzsa Z, Seropian IM, Sharifi M, Spyropoulos AC, Stewart L, Wolf S, Barco S.

journal.title: Journal of thrombosis and haemostasis : JTH

abstractText:
Background

Catheter-directed thrombolysis is an established reperfusion strategy for intermediate- or high-risk acute pulmonary embolism. No validated model exists to predict early major bleeding in this population.

Objectives

To derive a baseline-only risk assessment model for major bleeding after catheter-directed thrombolysis, and to assess its transferability in an independent cohort.

Patients/methods

We pooled patient-level data from 16 cohort studies and randomized trials of catheter-directed thrombolysis for acute pulmonary embolism. The most stable baseline predictors of major bleeding were identified by adaptive LASSO across 1000 bootstrap iterations. Candidate models including 2 to 6 of these predictors were compared on optimism-corrected discrimination and calibration. The selected model was applied to an independent cohort from the RIETE registry.

Results

Of 1246 patients with outcome data and without contraindications to thrombolysis, 75 (6.0%) experienced major bleeding, including 10 intracranial hemorrhages. On internal validation, the F-HARP model (Female sex, Hypertension, Age, high-Risk Pulmonary embolism) showed an optimism-corrected area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.695 (95%CI: 0.639-0.755). In the independent cohort (N=566), patients classified as high risk had higher odds of major bleeding within 30 days than the remainder (11.2% vs. 3.8%; OR 3.18, 95%CI: 1.44-7.05). AUROC was 0.638 (95%CI: 0.519-0.742) and calibration slope 0.630 (95%CI: 0.153-1.107).

Conclusions

The F-HARP model uses four readily available baseline predictors to identify a subgroup at meaningfully higher odds of major bleeding after catheter-directed thrombolysis. A powered external validation is required prior to its use for precise risk quantification.

title: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors And Depression in Atrial Fibrillation: Design of the SAD-AF Randomized Controlled Trial.
authorString: Koh Y, Lu L, Chen L, Das SK, Virk S, Liang D, Thakur U, Anderson RD, Al-Kaisey A, Lee G, Pathik B, McLellan A, Morton J, Voskoboinik A, SandersP, Davey CG, Kistler P, Kalman J, Wong M.
abstractText:
Background

Atrial fibrillation and depression are frequently comorbid, with autonomic dysfunction as a potential shared underlying pathophysiology. However, the effect of the treatment of depression on atrial fibrillation has not been well characterized, despite previous investigation of selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors into other forms of cardiovascular disease such as coronary artery disease.

Objective

To test whether escitalopram, a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor, reduces AF-related symptoms, AF burden and AF presentations to hospital compared to placebo, in addition to standard of care.

Methods

Multicenter, randomized, single-blind, parallel-group superiority trial. Eligible participants are aged 18-80 years with paroxysmal or persistent atrial fibrillation, with the goal of rhythm control, who also score 8 or more on the PHQ-9 questionnaire (out of a maximum score of 27). 154 patients will be randomized to escitalopram or placebo in doses of 5mg to 20mg, titrated to individual patient response. The primary outcome is the Atrial Fibrillation Effect on Quality of Life (AFEQT) score. Secondary outcomes include AF burden, adherence to lifestyle risk factor management including self-rated physical activity index (EPIC-PAQ-S questionnaire), general quality of life (SF-36 questionnaire), and hospital presentations for atrial fibrillation. Rhythm monitoring for AF burden will be undertaken with either mobile single lead ECG monitoring (Alivecor Kardiamobile), ECG-capable smartwatch, Holter monitoring or interrogation of pre-existing cardiac electronic implantable device. Autonomic metrics will be assessed by non-invasive recordings of blood pressure and heart rate variability.

Conclusions

The study aims to determine the impact of managing AF with a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor, with a patient-centered primary outcome.

title: Average Acceleration as a Measure of Physical Activity Across Sensor Locations in Participants With Heart Failure or Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease and Healthy Volunteers: Secondary Analysis.
authorString: Sillén L, Tamayo-Elizalde M, Shaw H, Lopez RB, Sillén H.
abstractText:
Background

Average acceleration derived from wearable sensors offers a simple, continuous measure of physical activity and mobility that may overcome the limitations of complex accelerometer algorithms or site-based assessments in clinical trials. However, evidence supporting the use of average acceleration in patients with heart failure (HF) and/or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) remains limited.

Objective

This study aimed to evaluate how average acceleration can be used to assess walking-related outcomes in both laboratory and free-living settings and to assess the influence of sensor location on these measurements in participants with HF or COPD and healthy volunteers.

Methods

Using data from the Mobilise-D Technical Validation Study, including structured, laboratory-based tasks and free-living assessments using sensors placed on the foot, lower back, and wrist, we analyzed average acceleration metrics computed as Euclidean norm minus one (ENMO), ENMO >0, and Euclidean norm (EN) from band-pass filtered triaxial acceleration (0.29-10 Hz; fourth-order Butterworth). During walking bouts, average acceleration was correlated with walking speed and cadence for each sensor location and cohort (HF, COPD, and healthy adults); sensor-location effects and cohort-specific sensitivity were evaluated. Linear mixed-effects models included participants as random intercepts and walking speed as both a fixed effect and a random effect.

Results

Average acceleration showed a strong positive association with walking speed during straight-walking laboratory tasks across all sensor locations, with foot sensors showing the strongest association, followed by lower-back sensors and then wrist sensors. In complex walking tasks and free-living walking bouts, the strength of these associations decreased, and location effects were more pronounced. Across cohorts during free living, filtered EN r2 ranged from 0.711 to 0.818 for the foot, from 0.439 to 0.673 for the lower back, and from 0.067 to 0.146 for the wrist. The strength of the association for wrist data improved only during free-living sustained walking bouts (>10 seconds), although these associations were weaker than those for the foot and lower back. The Pearson correlation was marginally stronger for ENMO >0 than for filtered EN, but filtered EN preserved more signal by mitigating the influence of gravity and noise. Linear mixed-effects models showed that the variance could be largely attributed to stable participant-specific differences.

Conclusions

Average acceleration showed potential as a measure for capturing walking-related activity in adults with HF or COPD and in healthy adults when using appropriate sensor placement. The strength of the association depended strongly on sensor placement, with the foot showing the most consistent relationship, the lower back providing a reasonable alternative, and the wrist showing weaker performance, particularly during free living. We recommend that trials use standardized reporting of sensor location, filtering parameters, and walking-bout definitions and prioritize foot or lower-back placement for walking-related end points.

title: State and trait anxiety following prenatal moderate- versus light-intensity exercise: a secondary analysis of a randomized trial.
authorString: Hicks L, Crandell J, Williams E, Logan J, Pomeroy A, Yeo S.
abstractText:
Purpose

Prenatal anxiety may increase as pregnancy progresses, yet little is known about longitudinal patterns of state and trait anxiety among pregnant individuals participating in exercise interventions of differing intensities. This study examined state and trait anxiety across late pregnancy among pregnant individuals with obesity randomized to moderate-intensity walking or light-intensity stretching and explored associations between changes in anxiety and gestational hypertension.

Methods

This secondary analysis used data from the Prenatal Heart Smart randomized trial. Seventy-six pregnant individuals with obesity completed the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI) at approximately 28, 32, and 37 weeks' gestation after randomization to moderate-intensity walking (n = 42) or light-intensity stretching (n = 34). Linear mixed-effects models compared state and trait anxiety between intervention groups at the two follow-up assessments, accounting for baseline anxiety and repeated measurements. Because no significant intervention-group differences were observed, groups were combined to examine changes in anxiety across late pregnancy using paired t-tests. Exploratory analyses examined associations between anxiety change scores and gestational hypertension.

Results

State and trait anxiety did not differ significantly between the walking and stretching groups at either follow-up assessment (all p ≥ .38). Despite previous evidence that anxiety may increase during late pregnancy, both state and trait anxiety remained relatively stable from approximately 28 to 37 weeks' gestation. Mean state anxiety scores were 30.0, 29.6, and 29.6 across the three assessments, respectively, while mean trait anxiety scores were 31.1, 32.1, and 30.4; neither measure changed significantly over time (all p ≥ .19). Exploratory analyses identified no significant associations between changes in anxiety and gestational hypertension after covariate adjustment. The small number of preeclampsia cases precluded analysis.

Conclusions

State and trait anxiety remained stable across late pregnancy among pregnant individuals with obesity participating in either moderate-intensity walking or light-intensity stretching, with no significant differences in anxiety outcomes between intervention groups. The stability of both situational and dispositional dimensions of anxiety across the third trimester adds to limited longitudinal evidence on prenatal anxiety during structured exercise participation. Because both groups received active exercise interventions and baseline anxiety was relatively low, the observed stability cannot be attributed to exercise. Studies including non-exercise comparison groups and participants with greater baseline anxiety are needed to determine whether exercise modality or intensity contributes to the maintenance of psychological well-being during late pregnancy.

title: A retrospective evaluation of temporal aggregation and creatinine reuse in critical care records
authorString: Yu T.
abstractText: Background Research using intensive care records often represents treatment and physiology in fixed time bins and reuses earlier laboratory measurements. Whether these choices preserve the intended measurements requires empirical evaluation. We examined crystalloid exposure reconstruction, recorded-panel availability and agreement between reused and subsequently measured creatinine. Methods This retrospective methodological study used MIMIC-IV 3.1 records from adults with coded diabetes, hypertension and early physiological stress. A fixed 6–12-hour crystalloid dose was reconstructed from four-hour grids with four phase offsets and compared with recorded-event interval overlap. Physiological-panel eligibility required timely documentation and was evaluated under creatinine age limits of 0–24 hours. At observed repeat-test times, the new creatinine was withheld and compared with the latest previously available value. Uncertainty used 2000 patient-cluster bootstrap resamples. A separate eICU 2.0 analysis assessed population-specific interface coverage. Results The master cohort contained 12175 stays in 10183 people. Among 10717 stays observed through 15 hours, fixed-target dose-category disagreement ranged from 5.66% (95% interval 5.21–6.12) to 16.01% (15.30–16.67) across grid phases. Four consecutive eligible panels were available in 146 stays (1.20%) without creatinine carry-forward, 6456 (53.03%) with a 12-hour limit and 8755 (71.91%) with a 24-hour limit. In 35081 paired repeat tests, mean absolute creatinine differences across prior-value age groups of 0–4, > 4–8, > 8–12 and > 12–24 hours were 0.155, 0.169, 0.177 and 0.188 mg/dL. Corresponding proportions differing by at least 0.3 mg/dL were 16.43%, 21.03%, 21.78% and 24.10%; severe creatinine-stage proxy disagreement was nonmonotonic at 3.12%, 3.85%, 3.63% and 3.11%. Conclusions Four-hour aggregation did not reliably preserve a fixed six-hour exposure. Reusing creatinine expanded operational panel availability but showed imperfect agreement at clinically selected retesting times. These complementary analyses do not establish accuracy in unmeasured intervals or a safe universal carry-forward limit. Measurement audits should accompany temporal dataset construction before treatment-response modelling. Clinical trial registration Not applicable. This study did not assign an intervention.

title: Additive Renoprotection of SGLT2 Inhibitors and ACEi/ARBs Against Contrast-Induced Nephropathy in PCI: A Prospective Observational Study.
authorString: Maher KA, Fahmy MS, Elshaer OA, Dawoud RN, Elgamal RM, Elsayed KR, Abdelmoneim DAM, Abdelfattah ME, Biomy R, Salama MK.

journal.title: Turk Kardiyoloji Dernegi arsivi : Turk Kardiyoloji Derneginin yayin organidir

abstractText:
Objective

Contrast-induced nephropathy (CIN) is a common complication of percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) have renoprotective effects; however, data on chronic SGLT2i therapy for CIN prevention, particularly when combined with renin-angiotensin system (RAS) blockade, remain limited.

Methods

This prospective cohort study included 249 patients undergoing PCI between August 2024 and December 2025, comprising 126 SGLT2i users and 123 non-users. Low-osmolar non-ionic contrast media were used during the procedures. CIN was defined as an increase in serum creatinine of ≥0.5 mg/dL or ≥25% from baseline within 48 hours of contrast exposure, potentially missing cases with later peaks. Given the occurrence of only 29 CIN events, predictors were identified using Firth's penalized regression. Sensitivity analyses were performed using inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) and the KDIGO acute kidney injury criteria. The interaction between SGLT2i and ACEi/ARB use was tested using penalized regression for CIN and factorial analysis of variance for ΔCr and ΔeGFR.

Results

Despite higher rates of diabetes and heart failure among SGLT2i users, the incidence of CIN was lower in this group (7.1% vs. 16.3%, p=0.025), with smaller increases in ΔCr (0.05 vs. 0.08 mg/dL, p<0.001) and smaller declines in ΔeGFR (-3.30 vs. -5.20 mL/min/1.73 m², p=0.009). Penalized regression confirmed independent protective associations for SGLT2i use (OR 0.39, 95% CI 0.16-0.91) and ACEi/ARB use (OR 0.17, 95% CI 0.06-0.41). IPTW yielded consistent estimates (OR 0.30 and 0.12, respectively), with all standardized mean differences <0.05. The results were robust when the KDIGO criteria were applied, and the protective effects were most pronounced in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD). The greater effect associated with ACEi/ARB use may have been related to hydration volumes of 16.9-17.6 mL/kg, which are within a beneficial range.

Conclusion

Chronic SGLT2i therapy was associated with a lower incidence of CIN and attenuated renal function decline after PCI. Concomitant ACEi/ARB use provided additive and independent protection, particularly in patients with CKD. These findings support the continuation of SGLT2i therapy during contrast exposure; however, randomized controlled trials are required to establish causality because of the observational design and small number of events.

title: Venous Vascular Closure System Versus Conventional Figure of Eight Suture Following Single Shot Device Pulmonary Vein Isolation: The VASC-AF Study.
authorString: Heeger CH, Rolfes H, Töllner L, Maurer T, Sultan A, Vogler J, Willems S, Feibel A, Rafieé F, Ghanem A, Bergmann MW.

journal.title: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology

abstractText:
Aims

Optimization of femoral venous access management has become increasingly important as catheter ablation of atrial fibrillation (AF) continues to evolve towards greater safety with accelerated recovery pathways. We evaluated the efficacy and safety of a bioabsorbable venous vascular closure system (VCS) compared with a conventional figure-of-eight (F8) suture and manual compression following contemporary single-shot pulmonary vein isolation (PVI).

Methods and results

VASC-AF was a prospective, multicentre, randomized controlled trial performed at three German electrophysiology centres. One hundred consecutive patients undergoing single-shot PVI were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to femoral venous closure using the VASCADE MVP VCS; (n=50) or conventional F8 suture (n=50). The primary efficacy endpoint was time to ambulation. The primary safety endpoint comprised major periprocedural adverse events requiring medical intervention before hospital discharge.Baseline characteristics and procedural variables were comparable between study groups. Median time to ambulation was significantly shorter following vascular closure with VCS compared with F8 sutures (120 [120-150] vs. 180 [180-240] min; P=0.015). Likewise, time to haemostasis (0.5 [0.5-2] vs. 1 [1-2] min; P=0.021) and time to discharge eligibility (2.5 [2.1-3.0] vs. 4.0 [3.0-5.0] h; P=0.019) were significantly reduced.Major adverse events occurred infrequently and did not differ significantly between groups. In contrast, vascular closure using VCS significantly reduced minor vascular access complications (6% vs. 26%; P=0.006), groin pain, and patient discomfort while improving overall post-procedural satisfaction.

Conclusion

Among patients undergoing contemporary single-shot AF ablation, use of a bioabsorbable VCS significantly accelerated post-procedural recovery while maintaining a comparable major safety profile. Reduced access-site complications and improved patient-reported outcomes support VCS as an important component of enhanced recovery pathways following AF ablation especially in an ambulatory or Same-Day Discharge setting.

title: Controversy: Adjunctive ablation lesions are needed beyond pulmonary vein isolation in treating persistent atrial fibrillation: Pro and Contra.
authorString: Natale A, Kalman JM, Mohanty S, Virk SA, La Fazia VM, Zou F, Di Biase L.

journal.title: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology

abstractText: Catheter ablation for persistent atrial fibrillation remains less effective than for paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, despite pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) forming the foundation of both procedures. Ablating beyond the pulmonary veins, including treatment of non-pulmonary vein triggers, posterior wall isolation, linear lesions, vein of Marshall ethanol infusion, isolation of the superior vena cava, coronary sinus or left atrial appendage, and modification of regions identified by fibrosis or low voltage has grown interest. Although observational and mechanistic studies have often been encouraging, randomized trials of empirical adjunctive ablation have produced inconsistent or neutral results. Pulsed field ablation has renewed the debate by facilitating rapid ablation of extra-pulmonary vein tissue. The PIFPAF-PFA trial did not demonstrate a significant reduction in its primary endpoint of atrial tachyarrhythmia recurrence lasting at least 30 seconds with adjunctive posterior wall isolation. However, separation of the recurrence curves and exploratory signals for reduced arrhythmia burden and fewer prolonged episodes raise questions about lesion strategy and the clinical relevance of conventional recurrence definitions. These findings do not establish routine posterior wall isolation, but they illustrate why a neutral binary endpoint may not fully characterize treatment effects on recurrent AF. The controversy now extends beyond whether additional ablation is beneficial to which mechanisms should be targeted, which patients should receive adjunctive lesions, how energy source affects lesion durability and safety, and whether success should be defined by any brief recurrence or by clinically meaningful arrhythmia burden. This article examines the evidence supporting and opposing ablation beyond PVI in persistent AF.

title: Effect of multivitamin-mineral supplementation on cardiovascular-related functional health status in older adults: secondary findings from the COSMOS randomized clinical trial.
authorString: Bekele BB, Zhu H, Hamaya R, Manson JE, Sesso HD, Dong Y.
abstractText: Declines in cardiovascular-related functional health status are common with aging, yet the long-term effects of multivitamin-mineral (MVM) and cocoa extract (CE) supplementation on patient-reported outcomes remain unclear in older adults. This prespecified secondary analysis of the COcoa Supplement and Multivitamin Outcomes Study (COSMOS) examined whether daily MVM or CE influenced Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire (KCCQ) scores in generally healthy older adults and those with pre-existing heart conditions. COSMOS was a 2 × 2 factorial, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of 21,442 US adults (men ≥ 60, women ≥ 65 years) without major cardiovascular disease at baseline. All participants were included in intention-to-treat (ITT) analyses of physical ability score (PAS), symptom burden (SB), and clinical summary score (CSS), representing KCCQ outcomes over 3 years. Linear mixed-effects models estimated treatment effects, with prespecified subgroup analyses among participants with cardiac conditions. Among a total cohort of over 21,000 participants, those taking a daily MVM versus placebo had small but statistically significant improvements in SB (MD 0.44, 95% CI 0.13-0.74) and CSS (MD 0.33, 95% CI 0.09-0.57) (both P < 0.05), with no significant effect on PAS, compared to placebo. CE supplementation had no overall effect. Exploratory subgroup analyses suggested heterogeneity in MVM effects according to carotid stenosis status, with year 3 ITT differences of 5.13 points for PAS and 4.95 points for CSS (P-interaction = 0.012 and 0.009, respectively). For CE, the primary ITT analysis provided limited evidence of subgroup benefit. This is the first large randomized clinical trial to evaluate the long-term effects of MVM and CE supplementation on KCCQ-assessed cardiovascular functional health in older adults. Our findings provide new evidence that daily MVM supplementation, but not CE, is associated with small improvements in cardiovascular-related functional health status among older adults, warranting further investigation. The trial was registered at https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02422745 ; unique identifier: NCT02422745.

title: Therapeutic options to support septal reduction therapy for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy patients.
authorString: Shah S, Sheashaa H, Brahier E, Smedira NG, Keen SK, Desai MY.
abstractText:
Introduction

Obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is characterized by dynamic left ventricular outflow tract obstruction that can cause substantial symptoms and morbidity. The expanding range of pharmacologic, surgical, and transcatheter options has made treatment selection increasingly complex.

Areas covered

This narrative review examines conventional medical therapy, cardiac myosin inhibitors, surgical septal myectomy, alcohol septal ablation, and emerging investigational septal reduction strategies. It also discusses patient selection, procedural risks, multimodality imaging, and the importance of experienced hypertrophic cardiomyopathy centers. A targeted narrative search of English-language literature indexed in PubMed was conducted from April through 31 July 2026, considering clinical trials, observational studies, guidelines, and relevant reviews.

Expert opinion

Cardiac myosin inhibitors are likely to modify the timing of septal reduction therapy rather than replace it. Future progress will depend on mechanism-based treatment selection, appropriate early referral, rigorous validation of emerging procedures, and integration of advanced imaging and multidisciplinary expertise to match each patient with the most suitable therapy.

title: The synergistic pharmacodynamics of Vitamin D3 and Vitamin K2: An exhaustive narrative review of evidence-based medicine on skeletal integrity, cardiovascular protection, and systemic calcium homeostasis.
authorString: Hasan KM.
abstractText: BackgroundThe co-supplementation of Vitamin D3 (cholecalciferol) and Vitamin K2 (menaquinone) represents a paradigm shift in nutritional pharmacology, moving toward a systems biology approach for regulating calcium homeostasis. Mechanistically, Vitamin D3 upregulates the expression of Vitamin K-dependent proteins-Osteocalcin and Matrix Gla Protein-while Vitamin K2 acts as the essential cofactor for their activation via gamma-carboxylation. This cascade directs calcium into the bone matrix and inhibits ectopic soft tissue calcification.AimThis review evaluates the synergistic pharmacodynamics and clinical efficacy of D3 and K2 co-supplementation in addressing the "Calcium Paradox," where calcium is concurrently lost from the skeleton and deposited in arterial walls.MethodsA narrative synthesis of relevant randomized-controlled trials and clinical literature was conducted to assess the impact of combined supplementation on bone turnover biomarkers, lumbar spine bone mineral density (BMD), and the progression of coronary artery calcification (CAC).SummaryEvidence demonstrates that combined supplementation consistently reduces undercarboxylated osteocalcin levels and attenuates age-related BMD decline in postmenopausal populations. In the cardiovascular domain, the pivotal AVADEC trial indicates that while established aortic valve calcification may be refractory, co-supplementation significantly decelerates CAC progression in high-risk subjects. The analysis further highlights the pharmacokinetic advantages of the menaquinone-7 homolog over menaquinone-4 and emphasizes the critical safety contraindication for patients on Vitamin K antagonists like warfarin. Current evidence supports D3 and K2 co-supplementation as a robust, dual-action therapeutic strategy for optimizing skeletal integrity and vascular health.

title: Limited arch repair versus extended arch repair for acute type A aortic dissection: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis.
authorString: Lang Q, Gong X, Qin C, Meng W, Xiao Z.
abstractText:
Objective(s)

To compare early and long-term outcomes of limited arch repair versus extended arch repair for acute type A aortic dissection.

Methods

Comparative studies evaluating limited (proximal) arch repair and extended arch repair were included. Studies with mixed isolated ascending or nonseparable proximal comparators were excluded from the primary synthesis. Random-effects meta-analyses using restricted maximum likelihood with Hartung-Knapp adjustment were performed to pool risk ratios for early binary outcomes and hazard ratios for long-term outcomes.

Results

Twenty-five reports were included in the updated systematic review. After endpoint-specific adjudication of potentially overlapping institutional cohorts, the number of reports contributing to each pooled analysis varied by outcome. EAR was associated with a higher risk of early mortality (RR 1.31, 95% CI 1.01-1.70) and re-exploration for bleeding (RR 1.23, 95% CI 1.04-1.45). No statistically significant associations were detected for postoperative stroke (RR 1.07, 95% CI 0.96-1.20) or dialysis (RR 1.21, 95% CI 0.99-1.49). HR-based analyses showed no statistically significant association with overall survival (HR 1.32, 95% CI 0.91-1.92) or distal aortic reintervention (HR 1.01, 95% CI 0.07-13.78).

Conclusions

In retrospective observational comparisons, EAR was associated with higher early mortality and re-exploration for bleeding, whereas no statistically significant associations were detected for postoperative stroke or dialysis. No statistically significant associations were detected for overall survival or distal aortic reintervention. These findings do not establish causal effects of repair extent and remain limited by confounding by indication.

title: Proteome- and phenome-wide studies identify circulating protein drivers of kidney diseases.
authorString: Triozzi JL, Mamak F, Wilson OD, Chen HC, Yu Z, Gravel-Pucillo K, Ferolito BR, Cho K, Gaziano JM, Muralidhar S, Ikizler TA, Robinson-Cohen C, Giri A, Tao R, Pereira AC, Hung AM, VA Million Veteran Program.
abstractText:
Introduction

Proteome-wide Mendelian randomization (PWMR) provides a genetic framework to identify circulating proteins causally implicated in chronic kidney disease (CKD) and prioritize them for drug discovery. However, the diverse etiologies of CKD and clinical presentations make it difficult to translate proteomic findings into actionable targets. Here, we studied protein associations with longitudinal kidney outcomes, CKD subtypes, and phenome-wide traits to identify proteins that are causally relevant and pharmacologically actionable.

Methods

We performed a PWMR study using cis-pQTLs as genetic instruments for 2807 circulating proteins from four proteogenomic cohorts (ARIC, Fenland, deCODE, and UK Biobank) and tested their effects across four kidney outcomes (eGFR, incident CKD, incident kidney failure, annualized eGFR slope) in up to 464,631 of Million Veteran Program participants. Proteins meeting proteome-wide significance underwent sensitivity testing, Bayesian colocalization, and external replication in CKDGen Consortium information. The same instruments were re-tested against nine diagnosis code-defined CKD subtypes using genome wide association studies meta-analysis across the Million Veteran Program participants, UK Biobank, and FinnGen, and against 1020 phecodes to distinguish kidney-restricted from systemic effects. Druggability was evaluated using ChEMBL annotations layered onto high-confidence STRING protein-protein interaction networks.

Results

We identified 93 proteins with proteome-wide significance, and twelve remained robust across sensitivity testing (ANGPTL3, FAM213A, GCKR, GSTA1, IDI2, INHBA, INHBC, MANBA, MICB, MST1, NRG4, UMOD). Forty-seven proteins mapped to at least one of nine kidney disease subtypes, with distinct patterns across diabetic, hypertensive, and glomerular kidney diseases. Phenome-wide testing separated seven proteins with kidney-restricted associations from those with broader systemic effects. Thirty-four proteins were pharmacologic targets, nominating candidates such as IL-1 pathway blockade for diabetic kidney disease and ANGPTL3 inhibition for podocyte protection.

Conclusions

Our integrative PWMR framework resolves circulating protein targets across CKD etiologies, separates kidney-restricted from systemic effects, and delivers actionable targets that may accelerate therapeutic innovation for CKD. About one-third of the 93 proteins could be targeted with existing or investigational medications.

title: Correspondence: Reply to "Heterogeneity in dosages and treatment conditions forms a blurred picture of the results".
authorString: Hussain M, Hassan M, Sohaib A, Ahmed T, Khan S, Hannan A, Dhedhi HAA, Naz A, Cheema AH, Ahmed F.
abstractText: Jumani et al. raised concerns about our systematic review and meta-analysis of zilebesiran in adults with hypertension, concerning dose heterogeneity, differences in trial conditions, and statistical methods. In this reply, we clarify that the primary analysis was pre-specified to include one comparison per trial, using the 300 or 400 mg dose at 6 months. The pooled blood pressure estimates therefore did not combine different doses. We agree that the dose subgroup analyses were underpowered and exploratory, and we did not conclude that doses are equivalent. We also acknowledge that trial populations, background antihypertensive therapy, and follow-up differed, and that the "mild to moderate" label should be interpreted cautiously. With only two trials per efficacy outcome, between-study variance cannot be estimated reliably and prediction intervals cannot be calculated. The pooled estimates should therefore be regarded as preliminary. These points support our call for larger, long-term trials with active comparators.

title: Cardiac Structure and Function After Preeclampsia, Including Global Longitudinal Strain: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Sethi Y, Kumar S, Arora M, Padda I, Almakadma AH, Farid M, Frishman WH, Aronow WS.
abstractText: Preeclampsia is associated with an increased long-term risk of cardiovascular disease and heart failure, particularly heart failure with preserved ejection fraction. Whether abnormalities of cardiac structure and function persist after delivery, and whether global longitudinal strain (GLS) detects subclinical myocardial dysfunction when left ventricular ejection fraction is preserved, remains incompletely defined. We updated the evidence on postpartum cardiac structure and function after preeclampsia and synthesized postpartum GLS. Of the 27 studies in the index review, 25 provided re-extractable arm-level data; with 5 new studies, the data set comprised 30 reports and 32 comparisons. Prior preeclampsia was associated with a higher left ventricular mass index (MD, 5.24 g/m2; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.77-7.70; k = 25), greater relative wall thickness (MD, 0.03; 95% CI, 0.01-0.05; k = 16), higher E/e' (MD, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.42-1.51; k = 15), and lower E/A (MD, -0.10; 95% CI, -0.19 to -0.02; k = 23). Left ventricular ejection fraction did not differ (MD, -0.62 percentage points; 95% CI, -1.51 to 0.27; k = 25), nor did isovolumic relaxation or deceleration time. GLS was less negative after preeclampsia (MD, 2.05 percentage points; 95% CI, 0.34-3.76; k = 4).

title: Data-Driven Phenotyping of Stage 2 Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome Among U.S. Adults.
authorString: Yao L, Yuan K, Ding X, Fan Y, Yu R, Kianoush S, Zuniga E, Farestveit L, Yang Q, Tantisattamo E, Zheng K, Odegaard A, Chow S, Wong N, Fan W.
abstractText: Stage 2 cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome is common and represents an important window for primary prevention, but it encompasses heterogeneous cardiometabolic risk profiles. We aim to identify the distinct phenotypes of stage 2 CKM among U.S. adults and characterize their temporal trends, sociodemographic distribution, and mortality risks. We analyzed 8,761 adults aged ≥20 years with stage 2 CKM from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey, 1999 to 2018, with mortality follow-up through 2019. Latent profile analysis incorporated 9 age-residualized, standardized biomarkers across adiposity, blood pressure, glycemic, lipid, and kidney domains. We assessed the prevalence, trends, and sociodemographic distribution of the distinct stage 2 CKM phenotypes. Survey-weighted Cox models estimated mortality associations using CKM stages 0/1 as the reference. Four phenotypes were identified: lean-hypertensive (23.3%), overweight-dyslipidemic (40.7%), obesity-metabolic (26.2%), and hyperglycemic-albuminuric (9.8%). From 1999-2000 to 2017-2018, hyperglycemic-albuminuric increased from 6.0% to 12.1% and obesity-metabolic from 22.3% to 30.6%, whereas lean-hypertensive declined from 31.0% to 20.8% (all P for trend<0.001). Hyperglycemic-albuminuric was disproportionately prevalent among non-Hispanic Black adults and those with lower income or educational attainment. During a median 10-year follow-up, 484 deaths occurred, including 117 cardiovascular disease deaths. Hyperglycemic-albuminuric was associated with the highest risks of all-cause (HR: 2.59; 95% CI: 1.95-3.45) and cardiovascular disease mortality (HR: 4.49; 95% CI: 2.47-8.15). Stage 2 CKM comprises distinct phenotypes with differing cardiometabolic risk profiles, temporal trends, sociodemographic patterns, and mortality risk among U.S. adults. These findings underscore the need for targeted and equitable CKM prevention and management strategies.

title: Assessing proper patient-reported outcomes after recent discharge in acute heart failure - a longitudinal study.
authorString: Wagner T, Zhou L, Magnussen C, Reichenspurner H, Kirchhof P, Grahn H.
abstractText: Acute decompensation of heart failure (HF) is a major cause of hospital admissions and adverse outcomes. Patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) offer valuable insights into patient experience and may support treatment decisions. This study aimed to assess PROMs in patients hospitalized for acute decompensated HF at multiple time points after discharge to evaluate the feasibility of repeated PROM assessments and to capture changes in health status, medication management, and quality of life. Consecutive patients hospitalized for decompensated HF completed PROMs at 30 days, 6 months, and 12 months post-discharge. Collected data included demographics, comorbidities, hospitalizations, medication use, and PROMs using the KCCQ-12, PROMIS Physical Function Shortform 4a (PROMIS-4a), and PHQ-2. Generic quality of life was assessed with the EQ-5D. Among 99 patients (median age 66 years, 33% women, 90% NYHA III/IV on admission, 89% rehospitalized for HF within 12 months), all PROM instruments indicated substantial disease burden. Strong internal consistency observed (Cronbach's alpha 0.75-0.90). PROMIS-4a was negatively associated with age (p < 0.01) and with sex (p = 0.04), while KCCQ-12 was associated with age (p = 0.04). All PROM scores improved during follow-up. Cardiovascular events-including transplantation, rehospitalization, emergency treatment, and therapy failure-did not significantly affect PROM trajectories. Repeated assessment of patient-reported outcomes after HF decompensation is feasible. Using one or two PROM instruments may be sufficient, as the measures showed parallel development. Preliminary findings indicate that PROMs capture aspects of patient health not fully explained by HF severity or treatment modalities.

title: Cardiometabolic multimorbidity and functional disability in middle-aged and older adults: a harmonized multicohort study.
authorString: Kong F, Wu J, Li Y.
abstractText: Cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) is highly prevalent in aging populations, yet its association and underlying mechanisms with functional disability (FD) remain insufficiently understood. This study aimed to investigate CMM-FD relationship, quantify the influencing mechanisms, and explore heterogeneity across different CMM patterns and population subgroups. A multicohort study was conducted by pooling harmonized longitudinal data from three international aging cohorts. CMM was defined as the co-occurrence of at least two cardiometabolic diseases, including hypertension, diabetes, heart diseases, and stroke. FD was measured through difficulty performing basic or instrumental activities of daily living. Logistic regression models were used to estimate associations and heterogeneities, and Kohler-Holm-Breen decomposition was used to quantify mediating contributions. CMM prevalence was 22.53%, and FD prevalence was 23.01%. CMM was strongly associated with higher odds of FD (OR = 2.940; p < 0.001), with consistent findings across all countries and FD subtypes. Respiratory, neuropsychiatric, and sensory conditions jointly explained 20.44% of the association, with psychological problems contributing the largest share. CMM patterns involving stroke generally showed high odds of FD, while the four-disease combination had the largest overall point estimate. Middle-aged, male, married, childless, non-retired, and smoking older adults exhibited a stronger CMM-associated elevation in odds of FD. Early identification of high-risk CMM patterns, routine screening for functional and psychological, cognitive, respiratory, and sensory symptoms, and targeted follow-up for individuals with stroke-containing or complex CMM patterns may reduce the risk of functional deterioration and support independent living in aging populations.

title: Association of premorbid TyG index with Sepsis-Associated acute kidney injury and 60-Day mortality in patients with or without Obesity: A retrospective cohort study.
authorString: Cui J, Dong Y, Domecq Garces JP, Wang J, Chen K, Kashani M, Kashani KB.
abstractText:
Objective

Association of premorbid triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index and the risk and outcomes of sepsis-associated acute kidney injury (SA-AKI).

Methods

In this historical cohort study, we enrolled adult patients with sepsis at Mayo Clinic between 2018 and 2025. The primary outcome was SA-AKI incidence, and the secondary outcome was 60-day mortality. Logistic regression, Cox regression and restricted cubic spline analyses were performed.

Results

Among 3,960 patients with sepsis, 2,144 (54.1%) developed AKI, and 23.3% died within 60 days. Higher premorbid TyG index showed a statistically significant but modest association with SA-AKI (OR 1.18, 95% CI 1.07-1.32). This association was evident in non-obese patients but not in obese patients (P for interaction = 0.022). Higher TyG-BMI was associated with lower 60-day mortality, with each 10-unit increase corresponding to a 2.3% reduction in risk; however, this finding appeared to be predominantly driven by BMI and should be interpreted cautiously in light of the obesity paradox. Severe AKI remained independently associated with increased 60-day mortality (HR 1.32, 95% CI 1.14-1.54).

Conclusions

A higher premorbid TyG index is associated with increased SA-AKI risk, particularly among non-obese patients with sepsis. The noted association was largely driven by BMI, and severe AKI remained a strong predictor of death.

title: Analysis of single-cell sequencing data reveals metabolic reprogramming characterized by high PDK4 expression in non-inflammatory myocardial fibrosis.
authorString: Yan L, Yang S, Wang X, Chen L, Hu B, Gong L, Liu L.

journal.title: Translational research : the journal of laboratory and clinical medicine

abstractText: Myocardial infarction (MI) is a metabolic disorder that poses a notable threat to human health, with post-MI heart failure (HF) markedly affecting patient prognosis. The overactivation of inflammation and fibrosis serves an important role in the progression of post-MI HF; however, the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. The present study aimed to investigate the associations among metabolic reprogramming, inflammation and fibrosis after MI. By integrating single-nucleus RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics data from MI and dilated cardiomyopathy, a common metabolic feature, glycolysis, was identified. This feature was shared by cardiomyocytes and monocytes in myocardial infarction and was specifically localized to the peri‑infarct region. Pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase 4 was identified as a core gene linking metabolic reprogramming to fibrosis. A mouse model of MI was established by permanent ligation of the left anterior descending coronary artery. PDK4 knockout was applied to evaluate its role in post-infarction fibrotic remodeling. Furthermore, the results of the present study revealed a cross-cellular metabolic reprogramming process mediating chronic inflammatory cell interactions. In conclusion, the findings of the present study suggested that targeting metabolic reprogramming may offer a promising strategy for preventing inflammation and fibrosis to mitigate post-MI HF.

title: SGLT2 Inhibitors Versus Metformin as First-Line Therapy for Cardiorenal Outcomes: A Target Trial Emulation Among New Users With Type 2 Diabetes.
authorString: Kung FP, Tsai CF, Chang YT.
abstractText:
Objective

To compare cardiorenal and mortality outcomes associated with initiation of sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors versus metformin as first-line glucose-lowering therapy among new users with type 2 diabetes.

Patients and methods

Using a target trial emulation design with TriNetX Global Collaborative Network data, we identified adults (≥18 years) with type 2 diabetes who were new users of SGLT2 inhibitors or metformin from January 1, 2018, through December 31, 2023, with follow-up through June 10, 2025. The primary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Secondary outcomes included individual MACE components, major adverse kidney events (MAKE), acute heart failure, all-cause mortality, and kidney failure requiring kidney replacement therapy. Propensity-score matching yielded 36,720 pairs.

Results

Over median follow-up of 2.5 and 3.5 years in the SGLT2 inhibitor and metformin groups, respectively, SGLT2 inhibitor initiation was associated with lower risks of MACE (HR, 0.88; 95% CI, 0.84-0.92), all-cause mortality (HR, 0.73; 95% CI, 0.68-0.77), stroke (HR, 0.84; 95% CI, 0.79-0.90), cardiac arrest (HR, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.68-0.95), and acute heart failure (HR, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.92-0.97). Myocardial infarction risk was similar between groups (HR, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.91-1.04). Kidney failure requiring kidney replacement therapy also did not differ significantly between groups (HR, 1.00; 95% CI, 0.87-1.14).

Conclusion

Among new users with type 2 diabetes, first-line SGLT2 inhibitor initiation was associated with lower risks of MACE and all-cause mortality than metformin, while the risk of kidney failure requiring kidney replacement therapy was similar between groups.

title: Differential Reverse Remodeling but Preserved Clinical Benefit of Sacubitril/Valsartan in Ischemic vs Non‑Ischemic HFrEF.
authorString: Carluccio E, Dini FL, Correale M, Dattilo G, Ciccarelli M, Masarone D, Ghio S, Mercurio V, Beltrami M, Ruocco G, Nodari S, Barillà F, Ambrosio G, Piepoli M, Paolillo S, Sinagra G, Palazzuoli A, Working Group on Heart Failure of the Italian Society of Cardiology.
abstractText:
Background

Sacubitril/valsartan is associated with left ventricular reverse remodeling (LVRR) and improved outcomes in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). However, differences in LVRR between ischemic and non-ischemic HFrEF and its relationship with clinical outcomes remain unclear.

Methods

In this multicenter, open‑label study, cardiac remodeling changes from baseline to 8-12 months after sacubitril/valsartan initiation were retrospectively compared between ischemic and non‑ischemic HFrEF patients. The outcome endpoint was a composite of all‑cause mortality/HF-rehospitalization.

Results

Among 608 patients enrolled, 302 (49.7%) had ischemic etiology. Baseline LVEF, end-diastolic volume index (LVEDVi) and end-systolic volume index (LVESVi) were similar between ischemic and non-ischemic groups. Both groups showed significant improvement at follow-up in LV volumes and LVEF (P<0.001 for all). However, adjusted mixed-effects models showed smaller LVEF gains (2.44% vs 4.51%, interaction P<0.0001) and smaller LVESVI reductions (-4.68 mL/m2 vs -7.43 mL/m2, interaction P<0.0001) in ischemic patients, while LVEDVi changes did not differ between the two groups (interaction P=0.263). Over a median follow-up of 63 months (IQR 32-77), 249 patients reached the composite endpoint. In multivariable analysis, LVRR was associated with the endpoint independent of etiology. In an exploratory analysis, LVRR accounted statistically for approximately 9% (95% CI 1.40-26.1%; p=0.0164) of the modeled pre-to-post association with outcome.

Conclusion

Significant LVRR after sacubitril/valsartan was observed in both ischemic and non-ischemic HFrEF, although the magnitude of improvement was smaller in ischemic disease. LVRR was associated with more favorable outcomes regardless of etiology, but only a modest proportion of the modeled pre-to-post association with outcome was statistically attributable to LVRR.

title: Preoperative RAAS Blockade Does Not Associate With Vasoplegia After Cardiopulmonary Bypass.
authorString: Tingey SD, Schachner B, Behr P, Schaich C, DuPlooy J, Seoane J, Cordell M, Khanna AK, Chappell MC, Imielski BR.
abstractText:
Introduction

Postcardiotomy vasoplegia affects ∼20% of cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) patients and associates with acute kidney failure, prolonged hospital stay, and mortality. Preliminary work revealed that nonvasoplegic CPB patients exhibit an immediate and robust increase in renin and Angiotensin II (Ang II), while vasoplegic patients exhibit a blunted renin and Ang II response. As many cardiac surgery patients are receiving renin-angiotensin-aldosterone (RAAS)-modifying medications preoperatively, this cohort study investigated if preoperative use of RAAS-inhibiting medications is associated with CPB-associated vasoplegia.

Methods

Sixty-six elective CPB patients at our tertiary referral center were prospectively enrolled and categorized as vasoplegic or nonvasoplegic based on immediate postoperative vasopressor requirements and cardiac index. Rates of preoperative medication use between nonvasoplegic and vasoplegic patients were compared: ACE inhibitors (ACEIs), angiotensin II receptor blockers (ARBs), beta-adrenergic blockers, ARB-neprilysin inhibitors (ARNI), statins and mixed polypharmacy groups were evaluated.

Results

Forty-nine patients were non-vasoplegic controls compared to 17 vasoplegic patients. All three patients on ARNI preoperatively became vasoplegic (3/17 (17.6%), versus 0/49 nonvasoplegic (0%), P = 0.015). For all other groups - patients on a beta blocker, ACEI, ARB, statin, or any combination of these medications - rates of pre-operative medication did not associate significantly with vasoplegia status.

Conclusions

The use and timing of discontinuation of pre-operative beta-adrenergic blocker, ACEI, ARB, and statin did not correlate with the incidence of post-operative vasoplegia. The use of ARNIs was positively associated with vasoplegia in a limited sample size. As a result, we believe post-CPB vasoplegia may have a separate pathway from preoperative RAAS modulators that requires further investigation.

title: Long cervicothoracic posterior instrume ntation and fusion: A retrospective complication analysis of 15 years of ACS-NSQIP data.
authorString: Yazdanpanah S, Guedikian C, Ravipati S, Romoff M, Hanks HE, Baz S, Cowman AW, Lee YP, Mills ES, Bhatia NN, Park DY, Hashmi SZ, Wu HH.

journal.title: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia

abstractText:
Background

Long cervicothoracic posterior instrumentation and fusion carries known perioperative risk, yet 30-day morbidity and independent predictors remain poorly characterized at scale. Therefore, this study aims to provide a multi-institutional analysis of 30-day adverse events and predictors of morbidity following long cervicothoracic posterior instrumentation and fusion.

Methods

Patients undergoing long cervicothoracic posterior instrumentation and fusion (2010-2024) were identified in the ACS-NSQIP database using a CPT-derived cohort definition framework composed of three query pathways, utilizing primary procedure codes for cervical arthrodesis, thoracic arthrodesis, and multi-level posterior segmental instrumentation. The primary outcome was any adverse event (AAE) within 30 days. Secondary outcomes included major, minor and infection-related complications. Exploratory multivariable logistic regression identified independent associations with AAE, with threshold analysis performed for significant continuous predictors.

Results

A total of 235 patients were included (mean age = 64.4 ± 11.0 years; 51.1% male; body mass index = 29.1 ± 6.9 kg/m2). AAE occurred in 30.2% of patients, most commonly postoperative transfusion (16.6%) and return to the operating room (7.7%). Major, minor, and infection-related complications occurred in 25.1%, 11.1%, and 9.8% of patients, respectively, while 30-day mortality was 0.9%. Operative time (odds ratio [OR] = 1.004), chronic steroid use (OR = 7.080), medication-required hypertension (OR = 2.677), and neoplastic/pathologic fracture diagnostic family relative to the degenerative/myelopathic reference family (OR = 4.804) were independently associated with AAE. Threshold analysis identified a 495.5-minute operative time cut-point (95th percentile), above which the AAE rate increased from 27.8% to 75.0% (OR = 7.935), highlighting disproportionate morbidity among extreme cases.

Conclusion

Nearly one-third of patients experienced a 30-day adverse event following long cervicothoracic posterior instrumentation and fusion, with considerably elevated risk concentrated among exceptionally prolonged surgeries. Identified predictors further characterize the procedure-specific perioperative profile of this cohort and may help to inform risk stratification and case planning, pending validation through future large-scale, longitudinal investigation.

title: Congestion Assessed With Inferior Vena Cava Ultrasound Predicts Long-Term Outcomes in Acute Decompensated Heart Failure.
authorString: Sampath-Kumar R, Levine OP, Villarreal-Gonzalez M, Fenerty AL, Toomu S, Kraushaar M, Ben-Yehuda O.
abstractText:
Background

Inferior vena cava (IVC) parameters relate to clinical outcomes in retrospective acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF) studies, but prospective data on long-term outcomes and quality of life are unavailable.

Objectives

The objective of the study was to evaluate the prognostic value of IVC parameters for clinical outcomes and their association with quality of life.

Methods

Patients admitted for ADHF were prospectively enrolled from January 2022 to May 2024. Point-of-care IVC ultrasound was performed at admission and discharge. The Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire (KCCQ) was evaluated at baseline, 1, 6, and 12 months. The primary endpoint was the composite of all-cause mortality and ADHF rehospitalization at 12 months.

Results

A total of 100 patients (median age 67 years, 28% women, 45% NYHA functional class III/IV, 65% heart failure with reduced ejection fraction) were included. The primary endpoint occurred in 50 patients (9 deaths and 41 ADHF hospitalizations). In multivariable analysis, admission minimum IVC sniff diameter >1.6 cm (HR: 3.71; 95% CI: 1.97-7.01; P < 0.001), admission maximum IVC diameter >2.3 cm (HR: 2.70; 95% CI: 1.46-4.96; P = 0.001), discharge minimum IVC sniff diameter >1.3 cm (HR: 2.27; 95% CI: 1.24-4.14; P = 0.008), and discharge sniff IVC collapsibility index <36% (HR: 3.16; 95% CI: 1.64-6.06; P < 0.001) were independent predictors of the primary endpoint. KCCQ scores improved during follow-up (Ptime<0.001) but were not associated with the primary endpoint. Patients with admission minimum IVC sniff diameter >1.6 cm had lower KCCQ scores throughout the study period (Pgroup = 0.03).

Conclusions

In ADHF patients, IVC parameters predict 12-month outcomes and may serve as objective markers to identify residual congestion and stratify risk.

title: Atrial Fibrillation and Risk of Late-Onset Dementia: A Danish Nationwide Cohort Study.
authorString: Middelfart C, Tønnesen J, Rasmussen PV, Pham MHX, Zörner CR, Ruwald MH, Torp-Pedersen C, Andersen MP, Nielsen BR, Hansen ML.
abstractText:
Background

Atrial fibrillation (AF) is associated with substantial cardiovascular morbidity, but its relationship with dementia remains incompletely understood.

Objectives

The objectives of the study was to examine the association between AF and late-onset dementia in a nationwide Danish cohort.

Methods

In this Danish nationwide registry-based cohort study, individuals aged ≥50 years with first-time AF between 2005 and 2025 were matched 1:5 with controls from the general population on age, sex, and calendar year. Late onset dementia was defined as a first-time dementia diagnosis or antidementia medication initiation at age ≥65 years. Cumulative incidences were estimated at 1, 3, and 5 years, and associations were assessed using multivariable Cox regression. Secondary outcomes were thromboembolic events and all-cause mortality.

Results

A total of 326,687 AF patients and 1,633,435 matched controls were included (median age 75 years; 55% male). The median follow-up was 8.6 years. AF was associated with an increased hazard of late-onset dementia (HR: 1.14; 95% CI: 1.12-1.17), which persisted after adjustment for cardiovascular comorbidity (HR: 1.17; 95% CI: 1.15-1.19) and exclusion of individuals with prior thromboembolic events (HR: 1.16; 95% CI: 1.13-1.18). The association remained stable across calendar periods, whereas the hazard of thromboembolic events attenuated over time.

Conclusions

AF was associated with late-onset dementia after adjustment for cardiovascular risk factors and exclusion of individuals with prior thromboembolic events. The stable association over 2 decades, despite attenuation of the association with thromboembolic events, suggests that dementia is an important long-term consequence of AF.

title: Outcomes Among Patients Receiving Watchman LAAO vs Antiplatelet Therapy: A Report From the GWTG-AFIB Registry.
authorString: Friedman DJ, Ayodele I, Holmes D, Alhanti B, Ellenbogen KA, Fonarow GC, Kent AP, Jackson KP, Joglar JA, Lewis WR, Russo AM, Vemulapali S, Piccini JP.
abstractText:
Background

Although Watchman left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) was approved for patients with atrial fibrillation who can tolerate short term anticoagulation, many patients are poor candidates for any duration of anticoagulation.

Objectives

The objective of the study was to compare 1-year outcomes among patients receiving Watchman LAAO vs antiplatelet monotherapy.

Methods

We performed an overlap weighted observational comparative effectiveness analysis of postdischarge outcomes among Medicare beneficiaries in the Get With The Guidelines-AFIB Registry who received LAAO or antiplatelet therapy. Cox Regression was used for all-cause mortality and cause-specific hazard models were used for nonfatal outcomes. A win ratio was calculated with the following endpoint hierarchy: 1) all-cause death; 2) stroke, systemic embolism, or transient ischemic attack (TIA); 3) major bleeding (excluding gastrointestinal bleeding); and 4) gastrointestinal bleeding.

Results

A total of 1,427 patients who received LAAO and 2,284 patients who received antiplatelet therapy were studied (overall median age 77 years, 49.3% female, median CHA2DS2-VASC score 5). Through the first 45 days, the adjusted risk of stroke, TIA or systemic embolism, major bleeding, or death was lower among patients who received LAAO (HR: 0.26; CI: 0.17-0.41; P < 0.001). Between 46 days and 1 year, the risk for the composite outcome was lower among patients who received LAAO (HR: 0.61; CI: 0.48-0.78; P < 0.001). The win ratio at 1 year was 2.71 (95% CI: 1.92-3.83; P < 0.0001), indicating significantly better outcomes among LAAO patients.

Conclusions

Among patients with atrial fibrillation, treatment with LAAO was associated with a lower risk of stroke, TIA or systemic embolism, major bleeding, or death compared to antiplatelet therapy.

title: Five-year risk of cardiovascular events in women with history of pregnancy complicated by fetal growth restriction.
authorString: Anand K, Bucci T, Sudell M, Lip GYH, Merriel A.

journal.title: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology

abstractText:
Objective

To evaluate the association between fetal growth restriction (FGR) and adverse maternal cardiovascular outcomes within 5 years postpartum.

Methods

This was a retrospective study that used a global federated health research network (TriNetX) in which diagnoses are coded using the International Classification of Diseases, tenth revision, Clinical Modification system (ICD-10-CM). Nulliparous women aged ≥ 18 years, without prior cardiovascular disease and with a singleton pregnancy delivered between April 2006 and December 2020, were categorized by the presence or absence of FGR (ICD-10-CM: O36.5). 1:1 propensity-score matching (PSM) was applied using two models: Model 1, matching for pre-existing cardiovascular risk factors; and Model 2, matching for both pre-existing and other pregnancy-related cardiovascular risk factors. Cox regression proportional hazard models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% CI for a maternal composite cardiovascular outcome including heart failure, acute myocardial infarction and cerebral infarction/ischemic stroke within 5 years postpartum, and for each of these components individually.

Results

After PSM, 84 863 women per group were analyzed in Model 1 and 84 861 per group in Model 2. FGR was associated with an increased risk of the composite cardiovascular outcome (Model 1: HR, 1.33 (95% CI, 1.16-1.52); Model 2: HR, 1.31 (95% CI, 1.15-1.50)), as well as with an increased risk of each of the components of the composite outcome individually: heart failure (Model 1: HR, 1.29 (95% CI, 1.08-1.54); Model 2: HR, 1.30 (95% CI, 1.09-1.56)), acute myocardial infarction (Model 1: HR, 1.55 (95% CI, 1.16-2.08); Model 2: HR, 1.53 (95% CI, 1.15-2.05)) and cerebral infarction/ischemic stroke (Model 1: HR, 1.38 (95% CI, 1.09-1.74); Model 2: HR, 1.33 (95% CI, 1.06-1.68)) within 5 years postpartum.

Conclusions

FGR in a first pregnancy is associated with increased maternal composite cardiovascular risk, including heart failure, acute myocardial infarction and cerebral infarction/ischemic stroke, within 5 years postpartum. These findings suggest that FGR may be a marker of early cardiovascular vulnerability. However, residual confounding, particularly by unmeasured timing or severity of pre-eclampsia, cannot be excluded. Also, FGR was identified using coding constructs based on electronic health records, which may include overlap with broader 'suspected poor growth' phenotypes such as small-for-gestational age, hence potentially diluting the observed associations. Earlier risk assessment and preventive strategies may help to reduce the risk of long-term morbidity and mortality in this population. © 2026 The Author(s).
