title: Clinical and operational practices to facilitate safe medication use in the care of hospitalized patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension.
authorString: Smith ZR, Kelly B, Guido M, Raymond-Forde S, Mazur J.

journal.title: American journal of health-system pharmacy : AJHP : official journal of the American Society of Health-System Pharmacists

abstractText:
Purpose

The purpose of this manuscript is to review evidence-based practices for the safe inpatient use of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) medications and facilitate effective transitions of care.

Summary

Patients with PAH can present to the hospital with clinical conditions related to PAH, acute conditions unrelated to PAH, or complications of targeted PAH medications. Rapid triage and assessment of hospital capabilities pertaining to PAH medication use is essential to facilitate continued care or transfer to an expert PAH center. An assessment of hospital-specific capabilities should include the availability of specialists experienced in PAH, the formulary status of PAH medications, and clinician proficiency in the use of parenteral prostacyclin agents. Continuation or modification of PAH medications should be coordinated with the patient's primary PAH specialist. The use of targeted medications for PAH should be guided by multidisciplinary policies with procedures to ensure safe practices and compliance with risk evaluation and mitigation strategy programs, where applicable. Coordination of medication access and facilitating safe transitions of care at hospital discharge is multifaceted as agents are specialized and some are only dispensed by specialty pharmacies.

Conclusion

Management of a patient's PAH pharmacotherapies in the hospital setting should involve clinicians with expertise in the use of PAH targeted therapies, be guided by standardized medication-use procedures, and involve care coordination to facilitate safe hospital discharge.

title: Cluster analysis of high-cost patients in Japan: A longitudinal study using health insurance data.
authorString: Matsuo Y, Yamauchi K.
abstractText: This study aimed to identify distinct patterns of medical expenditure trajectories among high-cost patients in Japan and characterise the identified groups using diagnostic and health check-up data, including laboratory test results. This retrospective study analysed data from 190,190 high-cost patients (top 5% of annual medical expenditure in fiscal year 2021) in the Japanese JMDC Claims Database. Five-year healthcare expenditure trajectories were classified using K-means clustering. The resulting clusters were characterised according to demographic characteristics, disease patterns, hospitalisation rates, and health check-up data. Eighteen clusters were identified and further grouped into four descriptive types of expenditure trajectory. The 'over-30-million-yen (200,000 USD)' type included two clusters with rare, high-cost diseases such as haematological disorders, chronic viral hepatitis, and sphingolipid metabolism disorders. The 'flat' type (four clusters) showed relatively smooth expenditure patterns over time, associated with chronic conditions like dialysis and secondary cancers. In contrast, the 'gradual peak' type exhibited costs that increased over time, largely due to malignant neoplasms. Meanwhile, the 'sharp peak' type was characterised by sudden cost surges driven primarily by inpatient care, with a high prevalence of angina and atrial fibrillation. By analysing five-year expenditure trajectories at the individual level, this study identified distinct longitudinal patterns and provided a descriptive framework for understanding heterogeneity among high-cost patients.

title: Cannabis-related disorders, hospitalization, and cardiovascular outcomes in patients with heart failure: A real-world propensity-matched cohort study.
authorString: Dalal N, Sanadi M, Karim HS, Bengoa DS, Desai S, Munagala M, Azocar RJ, Divya A.

journal.title: Clinical research in cardiology : official journal of the German Cardiac Society

abstractText:
Background

The clinical implications of cannabis exposure in patients with heart failure remain uncertain. We evaluated the associations between a documented cannabis-related disorder (CRD) and hospitalization and cardiovascular outcomes in a large real-world heart failure cohort.

Methods

We performed a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX US Collaborative Network. Adult patients with heart failure (ICD-10-CM I50) were identified and stratified by the presence or absence of cannabis-related disorder (ICD-10-CM F12) recorded within 1 year on or before the first heart failure diagnosis, which served as the index date. The primary outcome was all-cause hospitalization at 1 year. Secondary outcomes included stroke, myocardial infarction, end-stage renal disease, atrial fibrillation/flutter, and all-cause mortality. Follow-up began 1 day after the index date; patients with a prior history of a given outcome were excluded from that analysis. One-to-one propensity score matching was performed using 26 baseline covariates.

Results

After matching, 30,624 patients were included in each cohort. At 1 year, a documented CRD was associated with a higher risk of hospitalization (57.5% vs. 45.1%; HR, 1.468; 95% CI, 1.436-1.501; p < 0.001). A documented CRD was also associated with significantly higher all-cause mortality (10.4% vs 9.3%; HR, 1.147; 95% CI, 1.090-1.207; p < 0.001), stroke (2.9% vs 2.3%; HR, 1.263; 95% CI, 1.138-1.401; p < 0.001), and myocardial infarction (6.0% vs 4.4%; HR, 1.415; 95% CI, 1.307-1.531; p < 0.001). Atrial fibrillation/flutter and end-stage renal disease did not differ. The hospitalization association persisted after excluding the first 30 days of follow-up (HR 1.252; 95% CI 1.226-1.280; p < 0.001), was similar in women and men, and remained in multivariable Cox models (adjusted HR 1.521; 95% CI 1.503-1.539; p < 0.001).

Conclusions

In this real-world propensity score-matched cohort of patients with heart failure, a documented cannabis-related disorder was associated with higher risks of hospitalization and selected adverse cardiovascular outcomes. Prospective studies with precise cannabis exposure characterization are needed to confirm these associations.

title: Inverse Association Between Triglyceride-Glucose Index and Ischemic Stroke in critically ill patients with Atrial Fibrillation
authorString: Wang W, Wang L, Li Z, Li X, Luo C, Dong Y, Gao H.
abstractText: Background: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common cardiac arrhythmia in critically ill patients and is associated with an increased risk of ischemic stroke (IS). The triglyceride–glucose (TyG) index, a simple surrogate for insulin resistance, has been linked to IS in general and diabetic populations, but its association with IS in critically ill patients with AF remains unclear. Methods: In this retrospective cohort study, we used the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) database as the internal cohort and the eICU Collaborative Research Database (eICU-CRD) for external validation. Logistic regression, restricted cubic splines (RCS), receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, and subgroup analyses were applied. Results: Among 1,295 patients, the proportion of IS was 48.72%. After full adjustment, each 1-unit increase in the TyG index was associated with a lower risk of IS (OR, 0.72; 95% CI, 0.58–0.88; P = 0.002). Compared with tertile 1, tertile 3 had a lower risk of IS (OR, 0.65; 95% CI, 0.46–0.92; P = 0.016). RCS showed a nearly linear relationship ( P for nonlinearity = 0.427). The AUC for TyG alone was 0.603, which improved to 0.919 after incorporating LASSO-selected variables. External validation in the eICU-CRD (1,304 patients) reproduced the inverse association (tertile 3 vs. tertile 1: OR, 0.68; 95% CI, 0.48–0.96; P = 0.027; continuous: OR, 0.73; 95% CI, 0.59–0.90, P = 0.003). Subgroup analyses showed significant inverse associations in male patients, non-White patients, those aged <65 years, those with myocardial infarction, those without diabetes, and those with malignant cancer, with no significant interactions. Conclusions: In critically ill patients with AF, a higher TyG index was independently associated with a lower risk of IS, and this inverse association was externally validated. The TyG index alone has limited predictive value, but it improves IS prediction when incorporated into a multi-variable model. Its prognostic value appears context-dependent and should be interpreted with caution in critically ill populations.

title: Chronic Hypertension and the Effect of Mean Arterial Pressure Strategies in Septic Shock: A Two-Cohort Target Trial Emulation Using Bayesian g-Computation
authorString: Zoidl P, Pannold J, Schadler P, Klivinyi C, Sartori S, Schreiber N.
abstractText: Background Chronic hypertension shifts renal autoregulation rightward, and in the SEPSISPAM trial, a higher mean arterial pressure (MAP) target reduced renal-replacement therapy (RRT) in hypertensive patients. We tested whether chronic hypertension modifies the effect of sustained higher versus lower MAP strategies on new RRT and mortality in septic shock. Methods We performed a Bayesian target trial emulation in 13,714 adults with sepsis receiving vasopressors from MIMIC-IV (n = 7,181) and eICU-CRD (n = 6,533). From 6 hours after vasopressor initiation, two sustained 48-hour strategies were compared: interval-mean MAP ≥ 73 mmHg versus 65–72 mmHg, followed by usual care to day 28, using a Bayesian parametric g-formula with time-varying confounders and competing risks. The prespecified estimand was the strategy × hypertension interaction. Results For RRT, the interaction odds ratio was 1.20 (95% credible interval [CrI] 0.88–1.65); for mortality, 1.04 (0.73–1.48). Additive interactions were + 0.5 (− 1.1 to 2.1) and − 1.3 (− 2.6 to − 0.1) percentage points. The posterior probability of an RRT interaction as protective as SEPSISPAM implied (odds ratio ≤ 0.53) was below 0.01%, and the probability that it lay between 0.80 and 1.25 was 59%. Estimates were stable across 17 sensitivity analyses, including a prior centred on the SEPSISPAM subgroup (0.89, 0.69–1.16). Conclusion Chronic hypertension did not modify the renal or mortality effect of sustained MAP strategies in septic shock; a history of hypertension alone does not support a higher MAP target for renal protection.

title: Specification sensitivity of physiological clustering in intensive care: a retrospective methodological case study
authorString: Yu T.
abstractText: Background Physiological clusters are often evaluated by resampling stability and outcome differences. These checks answer different questions from robustness to measurement representation. We examined whether a reproducible intensive-care partition remained consistent under defensible changes in observation eligibility, renal representation and numerical estimation. Methods This retrospective methodological case study used MIMIC-IV, including 55,125 four-hour periods from 9,040 adults with coded diabetes, hypertension and early physiological stress. A three-component Gaussian mixture used arterial pressure, heart rate, recorded urine output and creatinine. Patient-disjoint analyses evaluated resampling, observation rules and absolute versus relative creatinine. A post-rejection amendment fitted 90 multistart seed models across nine specifications, selecting solutions by training likelihood within each specification. A planned quantile-spline prognostic comparator was rerun after identifying a uniform-knot implementation deviation. An eICU audit evaluated external measurement feasibility. Results Fixed-preprocessing bootstrap agreement had median adjusted Rand index (ARI) 0.944. After multiseed estimation, absolute and relative creatinine partitions in the same 9,232 test periods had ARI 0.377 (conditional patient-bootstrap 95% interval 0.351 to 0.404). Selecting higher-likelihood solutions also weakened the earlier apparent freshness robustness of absolute creatinine in the reference-available subgroup. In 1,441 twelve-hour test patients with 157 deaths, adding state to the corrected source-physiology model changed AUROC by ‑0.00068 (95% interval ‑0.00565 to 0.00438). Across 208 eICU hospitals, nine had no records meeting the urine-label screen; measurement equivalence remained unresolved. Conclusions High resampling stability did not establish specification invariance. The observed partitions were associated with risk, but did not demonstrate added discrimination in the tested physiological comparator or establish clinical response phenotypes. The contribution is a reproducible, bounded demonstration of the different evidence supplied by numerical stability, representation robustness and clinical validation.

title: The Importance of Liver Density on CT Scan in Heart Failure Patients
authorString: Saadat M, Mirtajaddini M, Naderi N, Pouraliakbar H, Goli P, Taghavi S, Omidvar R, Gharoy H, Birgani AH.
abstractText: Introduction Heart failure (HF) is a major global health problem associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. Hepatic involvement is common in HF and may reflect the severity of systemic congestion and impaired hemodynamics. Although liver function tests and bilirubin levels have been investigated as prognostic markers in HF, the clinical significance of liver density measured by computed tomography (CT) has received less attention. This study aimed to evaluate the association between liver density on CT scans and clinical, laboratory, echocardiographic, and prognostic parameters in patients with HF. Methods This retrospective cross-sectional study included 145 patients with HF admitted to a tertiary heart center between 2020 and 2022. Adults with HF with reduced or mid-range ejection fraction confirmed by echocardiography were included. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, chest CT, and echocardiographic data were obtained from medical records. Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS version 24.0. Continuous variables were expressed as mean ± standard deviation and categorical variables as frequencies. Associations were assessed using independent t-tests and chi-square tests. A p-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Results The mean age was 42.8 ± 10.5 years, and the mean BMI was 27.06 ± 4.44 kg/m². Most patients were male. Edema and ascites were positively associated with liver density, whereas LVEDD (r = − 0.32) and SPAP (r = − 0.276) showed significant negative correlations. No significant association was observed between liver density and TAPSE (r = 0.056). Electrolytes, creatinine, and liver function tests were also associated with liver density. Patients with cardiac-related mortality had a mean liver density of 47.29 ± 7.1 HU, and this association was statistically significant (P = 0.029). Conclusion Liver density measured on chest CT may provide useful prognostic information in patients with HF and could serve as an additional imaging marker for clinical risk assessment.

title: Clinical and Aetiological Patterns of Paediatric Heart Failure in Nigeria: Insights Into Soluble ST2 as an Emerging Biomarker
authorString: Benjamin N, Sadoh WE, Abiodun MT.
abstractText: Background Paediatric heart failure remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality in low- and middle-income countries. Soluble suppression of tumorigenicity-2 (sST2) is an emerging biomarker of myocardial stress and remodelling, but evidence in African children is limited. This study assessed the clinical and aetiological patterns of paediatric heart failure and the relationship between heart failure and plasma sST2 levels among Nigerian children. Methods This analytical cross-sectional study was conducted at the Emergency Paediatric Unit, University of Benin Teaching Hospital, Nigeria, from March to October 2024. A total of 408 children were enrolled, comprising 204 children with clinically diagnosed heart failure and 204 age- and sex-matched healthy controls. Sociodemographic, clinical, anthropometric and laboratory data were collected. Heart failure severity was assessed using the Modified Ross Classification, while plasma sST2 levels were measured and compared between groups and across aetiological categories. Results Children younger than one year accounted for 87 (42.6%) cases, while 139 (68.1%) were from lower socioeconomic groups. Most had mild (107, 52.5%) or moderate (91, 44.6%) heart failure. Pneumonia (76, 37.2%), severe malarial anaemia (65, 31.9%) and congenital heart disease (36, 17.6%) were the leading causes. Cases had significantly higher pulse and respiratory rates and lower BMI-for-age z-scores than controls (p < 0.001). Median plasma sST2 was significantly higher in cases than controls (6.26 [3.79–15.98] vs 4.05 [2.25–6.35] ng/mL; p < 0.001) and varied significantly by aetiology (p = 0.037), with highest levels in malignancy-related and pericardial heart failure. No significant sex-related differences were observed. Conclusion Paediatric heart failure was predominantly associated with pneumonia, severe malarial anaemia and congenital heart disease. Plasma sST2 was significantly elevated and varied by aetiology, suggesting potential utility as a biomarker of myocardial stress. Longitudinal studies are warranted to establish its prognostic value.

title: Scaling PROMs Implementation Across Clinical Pathways: Lessons from Hospital Moinhos de Vento's Experience with ICHOM Standard Sets.
authorString: Pille A, Wolf JM, Maccari JG, Martins SCO, Polanczyk CA, Nasi LA.

journal.title: NEJM catalyst innovations in care delivery

abstractText: This case study presents the 7-year experience of Hospital Moinhos de Vento (HMV), a leading private hospital in Brazil, in implementing patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) through the International Consortium for Health Outcomes Measurement (ICHOM) standard sets. The primary objective was to share practical insights into how PROMs were operationalized across multiple departments and conditions, highlighting implementation strategies, scalability, and challenges. Between 2017 and 2024, PROMs were embedded in clinical workflows across nine health conditions, including stroke, heart failure, breast cancer, and prostate cancer. Results showed improved adherence to data collection and enhanced patient-clinician communication. The authors retrospectively applied the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) to map barriers and enablers. Although substantial clinical improvements were observed, they present these as contextual trends within a broader quality improvement ecosystem rather than establishing direct causal attribution to PROMs alone. Key factors for successful scaling included strong institutional leadership, the establishment of a Clinical Practice Office (CPO), shared digital infrastructure, and continuous process improvement. The case underscores that effective PROMs implementation requires deliberate planning, cultural change, and investment in interoperable systems. By detailing the who, how, and when of implementation, this article serves as a practical guide for health care organizations aiming to integrate patient-centered outcomes into routine care.

title: Prognostic Value of Left Ventricular Kinetic Energy Assessed by 4D Flow CMR in Dilated Cardiomyopathy: A Prospective Multicenter Cohort Study.
authorString: Wang W, Wang J, Zhu R, Gao Y, Liu J, Wu L, Wang W, Huo H, Liu T, Wang X.
abstractText:
Background

Alterations in left ventricular intracavitary hemodynamics can occur early in the course of nonischemic dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM). However, the association between 4-dimensional (4D) flow cardiac magnetic resonance parameters and adverse outcomes in patients with DCM remains unclear. We aimed to evaluate whether 4D flow cardiac magnetic resonance parameters can predict adverse outcomes in patients with DCM.

Methods

In this multicenter prospective cohort study, 675 adult patients with DCM (mean age, 56 years; 399 men) from 3 medical centers and 80 age- and sex-matched healthy controls underwent 4D flow cardiac magnetic resonance. Left ventricular flow components and kinetic energy parameters were quantified. The primary end point was a composite of heart failure events, including heart failure-related death, unplanned heart failure hospitalization, or cardiac transplantation.

Results

During a median follow-up of 42 months, 58 patients (8.6%) experienced the primary end point. Compared with controls, patients with DCM exhibited reduced peak systolic kinetic energy normalized to EDV (KEiEDV) and peak E-wave KEiEDV; these differences were more pronounced in those who developed the primary end point. In univariable Cox regression, direct flow, residual volume, peak systolic KEiEDV, and peak E-wave KEiEDV were significant predictors of the primary end point (all P<0.05). After adjustment for left ventricular ejection fraction, NT-proBNP (N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide), extracellular volume fraction, extent of late gadolinium enhancement, peak systolic KEiEDV (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.39 [95% CI, 0.28-0.53]), and peak E-wave KEiEDV (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.35 [95% CI, 0.26-0.48]) remained independently associated with the primary end point (both P<0.001). Furthermore, these 2 kinetic energy parameters provided incremental prognostic value beyond clinical markers and conventional imaging markers for predicting the primary end point.

Conclusions

In patients with DCM, decreased peak systolic KEiEDV and peak E-wave KEiEDV, as measured by 4D flow cardiac magnetic resonance, are independently associated with poor prognosis and provide incremental prognostic value for risk stratification beyond clinical and conventional imaging markers.

title: PREVENT Risk Stratification for Intensive Blood Pressure Intervention and Life Expectancy in Rural China: A Post Hoc Analysis of the China Rural Hypertension Control Project.
authorString: Wang C, Chen Y, Jiang X, Ouyang N, Wu B, Xu J, Zhang X, Li H, Yin Y, Miao W, Li W, Chen J, Tan X, Tian X, Zhang C, He C, Ye N, Li G, Guo X, Sun Y.
abstractText:
Background

The 2025 American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology guideline adopted the Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events (PREVENT) equations to guide antihypertensive treatment, but whether PREVENT risk groups identify patients who benefit more from intensive blood pressure (BP) control is uncertain. We evaluated intensive BP control across PREVENT risk groups in the China Rural Hypertension Control Project.

Methods

We analyzed 21 872 hypertensive adults from 326 Chinese villages. Participants received intensive BP control (target <130/80 mm Hg) or usual care and were classified as low risk (<5%), borderline risk (5.0%-7.4%), intermediate risk (7.5%-19.9%), or high risk (≥20%). The primary outcome was a composite of major cardiovascular events (myocardial infarction, stroke, heart failure, or cardiovascular death). Safety, net benefit, and life expectancy were assessed.

Results

Over a median of 3.02 years, intensive BP control was associated with lower cardiovascular risk in the low-risk (hazard ratio, 0.53 [95% CI, 0.29-0.97]), intermediate-risk (hazard ratio, 0.58 [95% CI, 0.49-0.69]), and high-risk groups (hazard ratio, 0.60 [95% CI, 0.47-0.77]), but not the borderline-risk group (hazard ratio, 0.80 [95% CI, 0.51-1.26]). No significant treatment-by-risk interaction was observed. Adverse events increased mainly in intermediate- and high-risk groups. Net benefit was favorable across all groups and greatest in the high-risk group. At 45 years of age, estimated life expectancy gains were 0.94 years overall, 0.71 years in the intermediate-risk group, and 1.26 years in the high-risk group.

Conclusions

Intensive BP control was associated with lower cardiovascular risk in 3 PREVENT risk groups, with favorable net benefit across all groups. Absolute benefit and estimated life expectancy gains were greatest among high-risk participants. PREVENT risk stratification may inform intensive BP control in community-based hypertensive populations.

title: Evaluation of the ESC Guideline based risk stratification of syncope patients in the emergency department A post-hoc analysis of the SYNERGY-trial.
authorString: Boel TT, van de Griendt TM, Ootes M, van Zanten S, de Jong JSY, Ghariq M, Bootsma M, Hemels MEW, Kaal ECA, Koomen EM, Groothuis JGJ, Peeters SYG, de Groot JR, Thijs RD, de Lange FJ.

journal.title: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology

abstractText:
Background

Syncope accounts for approximately 1% of all emergency department(ED) visits. With 1-year mortality rates reaching up to 33% in certain arrhythmogenic aetiologies, adequate assessment in the ED is imperative. The risk stratification as described in the 2018 European Society of Cardiology(ESC) guidelines on syncope is widely used in clinical practice, but has never been validated. We therefore aimed to determine the ability to identify cardiac syncope of the composite guideline-based RISC-score, and investigate the association of individual risk-features and cardiac aetiology.

Methods

520 patients presenting with syncope to the ED of five Dutch hospitals were included. Adjudicated diagnoses were established by a multidisciplinary expert-panel following one-year of critical follow-up. ED-documentation was analyzed for the presence of guideline risk-features. Overall discriminative ability of the guideline-based RISC-score was evaluated using receiver-operating-characteristic(ROC) curve-analysis. Uni- and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to assess the predictive ability of the individual risk-features.

Results

50 patients(9.6%) were adjudicated with a cardiac aetiology of syncope. The RISC-score demonstrated excellent discriminative ability with an area-under-the-curve(AUC) of 0.928. The guideline based cut-off threshold of 2 points yielded a sensitivity of 96.0%, a specificity of 78.5%, a positive predictive value of 33.2% and a negative predictive value of 99.5%. Multivariate regression analysis identified age, no warning-symptoms, angina pectoris, unevaluated systolic murmur, atrial fibrillation, syncope during exertion and bifascicular-block as independent predictors of cardiac syncope.

Conclusion

The ESC-guideline based RISC-score can be reliably and safely used for excluding a cardiac aetiology of syncope in patients in the ED.

title: Loss of the clock protein PERIOD1 causes sex-specific impacts on the heart in Dahl salt-sensitive rats.
authorString: Eikenberry SA, Juffre A, Sharma R, Cheng KY, Gegoutchadze K, Johnston JG, Costello HM, Crislip GR, Zietara A, Dissanayake LV, Broderick B, Cook E, Alsheikh D, Staruschenko A, Bruno KA, Gumz ML.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol
journal.title: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
journal.isoabbreviation: Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol

abstractText: Salt-sensitive (SS) hypertension is a driver of cardiovascular disease. Circadian biology is implicated in hypertension. One component of the circadian molecular clock, the protein PERIOD1 (PER1), is involved in blood pressure regulation. We previously published that loss of PER1 (PER1 KO) in a rat model of SS hypertension, the Dahl SS rat, is associated with exacerbated renal injury and hypertension, as well as disrupted circadian regulation of heart rate. The cardiac and sex-specific impacts of PER1 KO in SS hypertension are undetermined. We utilized male and female PER1 KO and Dahl SS rats to investigate changes in the cardiac transcriptome, revealing sex-dependent shifts in gene expression. Male PER1 KO rats exhibited upregulation of genes associated with extracellular matrix remodeling. Consistent with this, male, but not female PER1 KO rats showed higher cardiac fibrosis compared to their Dahl SS counterparts. Terminal measurements revealed that male, but not female PER1 KO rats had increased blood pressure compared to Dahl SS controls. Given the lack of an apparent phenotype in females, only male subjects were used for subsequent ultrasound echocardiography studies. We determined longitudinal in vivo cardiac function in male rats during normal salt and 14 days of high salt diet. This revealed reduced stroke volume and decreased cardiac output at baseline, prior to exposure to high salt diet in male PER1 KO rats. These results indicate that impaired cardiac function may predispose PER1 KO rats to salt-sensitive hypertension.

title: Angiotensin and high-salt diet induce systemic inflammation and alter cardiac resident macrophage phenotype in Balb/CJ and C57BL/6J mice.
authorString: Becirovic-Agic M, Jönsson S, Isackson H, Tareg I, Tveitarås MK, Skogstrand T, Karlsen TV, Lidén Å, Leh S, Ericsson M, Reed RK, Marks-Hultström M.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol
journal.title: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
journal.isoabbreviation: Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol

abstractText: Acute decompensation of heart failure is associated with high mortality and the role of genetic risk factors remain poorly understood. Balb/CJ mice rapidly decompensate following a treatment with angiotensin II and high-salt diet (AngII+Salt). They present with reduced cardiac output, peripheral edema, and high mortality while C57BL/6J are protected. The aim of this study was to identify molecular pathways that explain the detrimental cardiac adaptations in Balb/CJ compared to C57BL/6J mice. Both Balb/CJ and C57BL/6J mice showed signs of cardiac hypertrophy after treatment with AngII+Salt, whereas only Balb/CJ mice developed substantial pulmonary edema and reduced cardiac output. Cardiac gene expression was measured using microarrays in Sham, AngII, Salt and AngII+Salt treated Balb/CJ and C57BL/6J. Already at baseline, cardiac gene expression was significantly different between the strains. Following AngII and AngII+Salt treatment, angiotensin II was the main driver of cardiac gene expression. Enrichment analysis of genes containing SNPs and exhibiting differential expression following AngII, Salt or AngII+Salt treatment identified several immune-related pathways. Angiotensin II was the dominant driver of systemic inflammation in both strains, measured as plasma IL-6, IL-16 and CCL2. Interestingly, combining angiotensin II and high-salt diet exhibited a synergistic effect on systemic inflammation. AngII+Salt altered phenotype of cardiac resident macrophages in both strains without affecting immune cell infiltration. In conclusion, angiotensin II is the main driver of cardiac gene expression following AngII+Salt treatment which is associated with systemic inflammation and altered cardiac resident macrophage phenotype in both Balb/CJ mice and C57BL/6J mice.

title: Cardiovascular Disease Prevention in Emerging Adults: A Narrative Review of Hypertension Knowledge, Cardiovascular Risk Perception, Self-Efficacy, and Life's Essential 8 Behaviors.
authorString: Miezah D, Marfo R, Omidiji OJ, Abubakari M, Shi L, Wright JA, Hayman LL.
abstractText:
Background

Cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, making early prevention a public health priority. Emerging adulthood (18-29 years) is a critical period for establishing lifelong cardiovascular health behaviors, yet adherence to the American Heart Association's Life's Essential 8 (LE8) health behaviors remains suboptimal among this population.

Objective

To synthesize evidence on hypertension-related cardiovascular knowledge, cardiovascular risk perception, self-efficacy, and LE8 health behaviors among emerging adults within the Health Belief Model.

Methods

A narrative review was conducted using PubMed, CINAHL, Web of Science, APA PsycINFO, and Google Scholar. English-language publications (2000-November 2025) examining hypertension-related cardiovascular knowledge, cardiovascular risk perception, self-efficacy, or LE8 health behaviors were reviewed. Findings were synthesized using a Health Belief Model-guided narrative approach.

Results

Thirty-nine studies were included. Hypertension-related cardiovascular knowledge alone appeared insufficient to promote sustained engagement in LE8 health behaviors. Emerging adults frequently underestimated their cardiovascular risk despite modifiable risk factors. Self-efficacy may facilitate the translation of cardiovascular risk awareness and motivation into healthy behaviors. The synthesis informed a proposed HBM-guided framework in which knowledge may inform cardiovascular risk perception, risk perception may strengthen motivation for preventive action, and self-efficacy may facilitate healthy eating, physical activity, nicotine avoidance, and adequate sleep. These proposed relationships require empirical testing.

Conclusions

Cardiovascular disease prevention among emerging adults requires more than education. Interventions should strengthen cardiovascular risk perception and self-efficacy while addressing social and structural barriers. The proposed framework provides a theory-informed foundation for cardiovascular nursing practice, future research, and intervention development.

title: Divergent Burden of Rheumatic and Non-Rheumatic Heart Disease in the MENA Region (1990-2023): A Retrospective Global Burden of Disease Analysis and Projections to 2050.
authorString: Al-Harbi FA, Alkuwaiti MA, Alsaif AK, Aljabr MN, Aldhowayan LT, Alsulmi SR, Alsulmi SS, Almushiqh OA, Alroshodi A, Tesfaye M, Ashraf H.
abstractText:
Background and aims

Valvular heart disease in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region reflects two distinct processes. Rheumatic heart disease (RHD), which is tied to poverty and untreated streptococcal infection, and non-rheumatic valvular heart disease (NRVHD), which is linked to population aging and metabolic risk. This study compared the burden of both conditions across the region from 1990 to 2023.

Methods

Age-standardized mortality, incidence, and prevalence rates per 100,000 population were obtained from the Global Burden of Disease database for 21 MENA countries. Joinpoint regression estimated the average annual percentage change (AAPC), pairwise comparison tested whether the two conditions diverged, and mortality was projected through 2050.

Results

RHD mortality fell from 5.87 to 2.19 per 100,000 (AAPC -2.97%), despite a slight increase in incidence and a doubling of prevalent cases to 3.36 million. In contrast, NRVHD mortality rates remained stable while absolute deaths nearly tripled, accompanied by steady increases in incidence and prevalence, with prevalent cases more than tripling to 557,576. Women carried a higher RHD burden, whereas men accounted for the greater increase in NRVHD burden. The temporal trends for RHD and NRVHD were statistically distinct across all outcomes. By 2050, RHD mortality is projected to decline by approximately 51%, compared with a 2.9% decline in NRVHD mortality.

Conclusion

RHD and NRVHD exhibit contrasting trajectories across the MENA region, reflecting differences in their underlying epidemiology. These patterns call for distinct public health strategies, with greater emphasis on primary prevention of RHD and expansion of diagnostic and surgical capacity for NRVHD.

title: Management of the hospitalized patient who uses ketamine.
authorString: Haber LA, Kolnik A, Taub J, Lyden JR, Terasaki D.
abstractText: Ketamine use is increasing across medical and nonmedical settings, with expanding off-label outpatient and telehealth-based prescribing, leading hospitalists to care for patients with acute ketamine intoxication, withdrawal, and chronic complications. Acute ketamine intoxication presents as a dissociative toxidrome managed with supportive care, low-stimulation environments, and benzodiazepines for agitation. Withdrawal is characterized primarily by neuropsychiatric symptoms, with limited evidence guiding treatment beyond symptomatic management. Chronic use may result in multisystem complications, including uropathy, cholangiopathy, cardiomyopathy, and neuropsychiatric sequelae, which can mimic common inpatient conditions. Hospitalization represents a key opportunity to identify ketamine use disorder, initiate harm reduction strategies, and manage complications.

title: Effect of High-Intensity Statin Therapy on Coronary Plaque Composition Assessed by Machine Learning-Based Optical Coherence Tomography Analysis.
authorString: Saboe A, García-García HM, Rubio P, Bakir EO, Cellamare M, Zhang C, Koskinas KC, Bourantas CV, Räber L.
abstractText: The value of artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted optical coherence tomography (OCT) for assessing longitudinal changes in coronary plaque composition remains uncertain. We performed a post hoc, vessel-level substudy of the Integrated Biomarkers and Imaging Study-4 (IBIS-4), using AI-assisted tissue characterization of serial OCT images from nonculprit coronary vessels in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction treated with high-intensity rosuvastatin. Baseline and follow-up measurements were compared using paired nonparametric analyses. Serial analyzable imaging was available in 45 vessels from 33 patients. Minimum fibrous-cap thickness increased from 93.98 to 117.26 μm (p = 0.027), and mean cap thickness increased from 309.20 to 353.12 μm (p < 0.001). Lipid volume decreased from 28.36 to 22.88 mm³ (p = 0.002), and the relative lipid component decreased from 18.34% to 17.06% (p = 0.044). Relative fibrous tissue percentage increased from 70.10% to 74.52% (p = 0.001), whereas absolute fibrous tissue volume did not significantly change. Calcification volume did not significantly change (p = 0.307), but relative calcific burden increased from 7.60% to 8.49% (p = 0.020). In conclusion, AI-assisted analysis of serial IBIS-4 OCT imaging reproduced a plaque-stabilization signature characterized by fibrous-cap thickening, lower lipid burden, and increased calcific signal after high-intensity statin therapy, supporting further study of AI-assisted plaque analysis in longitudinal coronary imaging investigations.

title: Salidroside Alleviates Atherosclerosis by Inhibiting Ferroptosis Through the RAG1/Keap1/Nrf2 Axis.
authorString: Song X, Yang Q, Yang J, Xu J, Xiang Y, Liu Y, Chi H.
abstractText:
Background

Atherosclerosis(AS) underlies the pathogenesis of many cardiovascular diseases. Ferroptosis, a lipid peroxidation-dependent modality of programmed cell death, contributes to AS. Salidroside (SAL), the major bioactive constituent of Rhodiola rosea, confers anti-AS effects. In the present study, we aimed to investigate whether SAL alleviates AS by repressing ferroptosis and to explore its associated molecular mechanisms.

Methods

A high-fat-diet-induced atherosclerotic model was established in ApoE-/- mice with intraperitoneal SAL treatment. We assessed SAL's therapeutic effect and ferroptosis-related markers. In vitro, RAW264.7 macrophages were stimulated with oxidized low-density lipoprotein (ox-LDL) to mimic atherosclerosis and treated with SAL. Ferroptosis-associated proteins, nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2) pathway activity, Kelch-like ECH-associated protein 1 (Keap1) expression and ubiquitination, and E3 ligase recombination-activating protein 1 (RAG1), were detected. Finally, shRNA-lentivirus-mediated RAG1 knockdown was performed to validate the mechanism.

Results

SAL significantly attenuated AS progression in ApoE-/- mice. Moreover, SAL inhibited macrophage ferroptosis both in vivo and in vitro. Mechanistically, SAL activated the NRF2 pathway by promoting NRF2 nuclear translocation, as the specific inhibitor ML385 reversed SAL-induced upregulation of glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) and solute carrier family 7 member 11 (SLC7A11; also known as xCT), and diminished the SAL's antioxidant cytoprotection. Additionally, SAL upregulated the E3 ligase RAG1, which enhanced Keap1 ubiquitination, leading to reduced Keap1 protein levels, subsequent NRF2 activation, and ultimately ferroptosis suppression. Knockdown of RAG1 abolished all these effects.

Conclusion

Collectively, our findings suggest that SAL attenuates AS, at least partially, by modulating the RAG1-Keap1-Nrf2 axis to suppress macrophage ferroptosis, which may offer a novel therapeutic perspective for this disease.

title: Sex differences in temporary mechanical circulatory support, vascular complications, and mortality in acute myocardial infarction with cardiogenic shock: a contemporary national analysis, 2016 to 2023.
authorString: Polana V, Godishala V, Koneru D, Karipineni S, Patel N, Nanavaty D, Singh S, Sanka S, Senkandlapuram R, Ayala-Rodriguez C, Reddy S.
abstractText:
Aims

Women with acute myocardial infarction and cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS) have historically received mechanical circulatory support (MCS) less often than men and have had higher mortality. Whether these differences persist in the contemporary era, and how vascular and access complications differ by sex across device types, is uncertain.

Methods and results

Using the National Inpatient Sample (2016 to 2023), we identified 66 381 admissions (331 905 weighted) with acute myocardial infarction and a secondary diagnosis of cardiogenic shock, of whom 34.2% were women. MCS was classified as intra-aortic balloon pump, percutaneous left ventricular assist device, or extracorporeal membrane oxygenation. Associations with female sex were estimated using survey-weighted logistic regression; race and hospital region, unavailable in 2023, were adjusted in a 2016 to 2022 sensitivity analysis. After adjustment, women were less likely than men to receive any MCS [odds ratio (OR) 0.77, 95% CI 0.74 to 0.80] and each device. Women had higher in-hospital mortality overall (OR 1.17, 1.13 to 1.22) and among recipients (OR 1.18, 1.11 to 1.26), without significant variation by device (interaction P = 0.74). Women had more acute limb ischaemia (OR 1.76) and blood transfusion (OR 1.27), consistently across device types. In sequential models further adjusted for device and coded complications, the mortality difference persisted (OR 1.22).

Conclusion

In contemporary practice, women with AMI-CS received less MCS and had higher mortality and more access-site complications than men. The mortality difference persisted after adjustment and should be interpreted cautiously, as residual confounding by unmeasured shock severity cannot be excluded.

title: Surgical management of late Stanford type A aortic dissection following previous coronary artery bypass grafting: a consecutive case series.
authorString: Keltchev A, Kardashev N, Vasilev S.
abstractText: Late Stanford type A aortic dissection (ATAAD) after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) is rare and technically challenging, particularly in patients with patent bypass grafts. We retrospectively analyzed three consecutive patients undergoing surgical repair of late ATAAD after CABG, focusing on operative strategy and temporary percutaneous balloon occlusion of the left internal mammary artery (LIMA) graft. Three patients underwent repair 3-11 years after CABG and all had a patent LIMA graft. Ascending aortic replacement was successfully performed in all patients, including one Bentall procedure and one concomitant biological aortic valve replacement. Temporary percutaneous LIMA balloon occlusion was successfully used in all cases to facilitate myocardial protection. No operative mortality, permanent neurological complications, or graft-related adverse events occurred. At 12 months, all patients were alive with patent grafts and stable aortic repair. Temporary percutaneous LIMA balloon occlusion may facilitate myocardial protection during complex redo aortic surgery.

title: Saint-Bonnet classification performance for the critical limb threatening ischemia diagnosis with duplex ultrasonography.
authorString: Wolfstirn R, Pénélope T, Allemang-Trivalle A, Chevalier L, Blanchet-Deverly A.
abstractText:
Background

Critical limb threatening ischemia (CLTI) is the most advanced stage of lower extremity arterial disease (LEAD) and is associated with an increased risk of amputation and mortality. The main means for CLTI diagnosis is the use of toe pressure (TP). Duplex ultrasonography (DUS) flow analysis by using the Saint-Bonnet classification could assess arterial impairment, but its relationship with CLTI defined by TP has not been evaluated. The first objective was to assess the relationship between Saint-Bonnet classification at ankle and hemodynamic CLTI, defined by TP≤30mmHg, and its diagnostic performance. The second objective was to study the correlation between systolic rise time and TP.

Material and methods

This retrospective observational study included patients undergoing lower-limb arterial DUS and TP at the University Hospital Center of Guadeloupe between June 2022 and November 2023. Statistical analyses included univariate and multivariable analyses, diagnostic performance assessment and Pearson correlation.

Results

One hundred and fifty-three patients were included (276 lower limbs). CLTI was significantly associated with 0 and E categories of Saint Bonnet in univariate (P<0.001) and multivariable analysis (P<0.001), with 94% specificity and 65% positive predictive value. N, A or B categories appeared to rule out CLTI, with a 100% negative predictive value in a population at high risk of mediacalcosis. No significant correlation was found between Systolic rise time and toe pressure (P=0.0773).

Conclusion

Saint Bonnet Classification may help in the diagnosis of CLTI, but these findings need confirmation in a larger prospective diagnostic and prognostic study.

title: Comparative Early Outcomes of Total Transfemoral vs. Upper Extremity Access for Thoracoabdominal Multibranch Endoprosthesis (TAMBE) Implantation.
authorString: Tackett C, Brinster C, Pyun A, Hong Y, Miklid U, Han K, Han SM.

journal.title: European journal of vascular and endovascular surgery : the official journal of the European Society for Vascular Surgery

abstractText:
Objective

Early experience with the Thoracoabdominal Multibranch Endoprosthesis (TAMBE) device relied on routine upper extremity access (UEA), but total transfemoral approaches have emerged to minimise aortic arch manipulations and the risk of neurological complications. The aim of this study was to evaluate outcomes following total transfemoral access (TFA) vs. UEA for TAMBE implantation.

Methods

A retrospective review of consecutive patients undergoing TAMBE implantation at a single centre between April 2020 and January 2026 was performed. Patients were stratified by access strategy into TFA and UEA. The primary outcomes were thirty day mortality and major adverse events (MAEs).

Results

One hundred patients underwent TAMBE implantation during the study period, of whom 32 underwent TFA and 68 UEA. The majority of aneurysms treated were thoraco-abdominal aortic aneurysms (61%), and 45% of patients had a prior endovascular intervention with no significant difference between groups (all p > .050). Mean operative time (232.8 ± 92.4 minutes vs. 250.8 ± 77.3 minutes; p = .18) and fluoroscopy time (59.2 ± 28.4 minutes vs. 48.3 ± 21.6 minutes; p = .066) were not statistically different between groups. Technical success was 91% in the TFA group compared with 99% in the UEA group (p = .095). Thirty day mortality (3% vs. 3%; p = 1.0) and MAEs (16% vs. 13%; p = .76) were not statistically different between TFA and UEA groups. Spinal cord ischaemia rates were 16% for the TFA group and 7% for the UEA group (p = .16), with most cases mild and resolved by discharge (80%). No stroke events occurred in either group. At 6 months, overall branch patency was 92% (78 of 85 branches from 22 patients), including 83% (15 of 18 branches from five patients) in the TFA group and 94% (63 of 67 branches from 17 patients) in the UEA group (p = .16).

Conclusion

In this single centre experience, total transfemoral TAMBE implantation was performed in selected patients, and no statistically significant differences were detected in thirty day mortality, MAEs, and technical success between access strategies. Larger studies are needed to determine whether clinically meaningful differences exist.

title: A temporary fix: assessing the safety, efficacy, and various applications of temporary externalized pacemakers.
authorString: Schiefer L, Sheppard G, King A, Banchs J, Exaire JE, Widmer RJ, Mixon TA.
abstractText:
Background

Temporary active-fixation pacemakers (TAF-PMs), consisting of a screw-in pacing lead connected to an external generator, may offer advantages over conventional balloon-tipped temporary pacemakers, including more secure lead placement, greater patient mobility, and reduced need for intensive care monitoring. We evaluated the safety and clinical utility of this strategy across multiple pacing indications.

Methods

We conducted a single-center, retrospective study of 100 adults who underwent TAF-PM placement between June 2019 and November 2024. Through chart review, data were collected on demographics, pacing indications, duration of temporary pacing, complications, and subsequent need for permanent pacemaker implantation (PPMI). The primary outcome was successful discontinuation of temporary pacing without subsequent PPMI.

Results

Pacing indications included spontaneous progression of conduction system disease (60%), transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR)-related conduction abnormalities (12%), acute myocardial infarction (AMI)-related conduction abnormalities (12%), and ongoing infection precluding PPMI (16%). Thirty-eight patients (38%) did not undergo subsequent PPMI. Among patients with TAVR- and AMI-related conduction abnormalities, 75% avoided PPMI. Three patients (3%) experienced lead dislodgement. No new infections, lead perforations, significant bleeding, or cardiac arrests attributable to the TAF-PM strategy were documented.

Conclusion

Temporary pacing using a screw-in lead affixed to an external generator is safe, effective, and reversible across multiple clinical scenarios, allowing sufficient time to assess the need for permanent pacing.

title: Long-term outcomes and benchmarks of redo surgical aortic valve replacement in Japanese patients: insights from a multicenter registry.
authorString: Handa K, Maeda K, Yanagino Y, Ohmori T, Ohtani A, Misumi Y, Kawamura A, Yoshioka D, Shimamura K, Miyagawa S.
abstractText:
Objective

Long-term outcomes following redo surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) in Asian patients, who typically have smaller body size than Western populations, remain poorly defined. Contemporary benchmarks are needed as transcatheter aortic valve-in-surgical aortic valve procedures expand.

Methods

We analyzed 122 patients who underwent redo SAVR for prosthetic valve failure at 8 centers between 2015 and 2023. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality. Secondary endpoints were cardiac mortality and major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE).

Results

Median age was 75 years, 50% were male, median body surface area was 1.5 m2, and median Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality (STS-PROM) was 7.4%. All-cause mortality at 1, 3, and 5 years was 9.9, 15.8, and 26.2%, respectively. Five-year all-cause mortality was higher in patients with STS-PROM ≥ 8% than in those with STS-PROM < 8% (45.2% vs. 15.5%; P < 0.001), but was not associated with age ≥ 75 years. Cardiac mortality at 1, 3, and 5 years was 6.8, 10.9, and 12.4%, respectively. Five-year cardiac mortality was higher in patients with STS-PROM ≥ 8% (20.9% vs. 7.7%; P = 0.047), but was not associated with age ≥ 75 years. MACCE at 1, 3, and 5 years was 15.8, 19.7, and 31.9%, respectively, and was associated with both STS-PROM ≥ 8% (44.2% vs. 25.1%; P = 0.008) and age ≥ 75 years (42.4% vs. 22.9%; P = 0.011). STS-PROM ≥ 8% and hemodialysis independently predicted mortality.

Conclusions

Redo SAVR was performed primarily in older, small-bodied, and relatively high-risk Asian patients.​ Careful patient selection may be warranted, particularly in patients with high STS-PROM or those undergoing hemodialysis.

title: Postoperative Inflammatory Response After Cardiac Surgery: Magnitude, Timing, and Prognosis.
authorString: Tazibet A, Coisne A, Jungling M, Vincentelli A, Juthier F, Girard A, Shorten L, Woitrain E, Lemesle G, Robin E, Staels B, Moussa MD, Ninni S.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

Cardiac surgery triggers a systemic inflammatory response. While this response is commonly interpreted as a marker of postoperative complications, its prognostic significance on short- and long-term death remains poorly characterized. We assessed the association between postoperative inflammation and short- and long-term all-cause death after cardiac surgery.

Methods

In a single-center retrospective cohort of patients undergoing cardiac surgery between 2011 and 2024, postoperative CRP (C-reactive protein) measurements and peak of postoperative CRP (CRPmax) and its timing were assessed. Association between CRPmax tertiles, delayed CRPmax (after postoperative day 3), and 30-day or 5-year all-cause death were evaluated using multivariable Cox regression models.

Results

A total of 7283 patients were included (mean age, 64.9 years; 72% men; 54% underwent coronary artery bypass grafting, 31% aortic valve replacement, and 94% on-pump surgery). Median CRPmax was 184 interquartile range, 134-246) mg/L. Median postoperative CRP peaked on postoperative day 3. Patients in the highest CRPmax tertile (tertile 3) more frequently presented with obesity, diabetes, peripheral vascular disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and chronic kidney disease. Compared with the lowest tertile, CRPmax tertile 3 was independently associated with higher 30-day (adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 2.56 [95% CI, 1.78-3.68]; P<0.001) and 5-year all-cause death (adjusted HR, 1.41 [95% CI, 1.22-1.62]; P<0.001). A delayed CRPmax was independently associated with increased 30-day (adjusted HR, 2.61 [95% CI, 1.94-3.52]; P<0.001) and 5-year mortality rate (adjusted HR, 1.56 [95% CI, 1.37-1.77]; P<0.001). These associations persisted after adjustment for postoperative infection.

Conclusions

Both the magnitude and timing of postoperative CRP peak were independently associated with short- and long-term death after cardiac surgery, irrespective of postoperative infection. These findings support close postoperative inflammatory monitoring after cardiac surgery.

title: Integrative Analysis of Cuproptosis-Related Genes and Repurposable Therapeutic Agents in Type A Aortic Dissection.
authorString: Tang C, Dai Y, Chen T, Shao J, Zhu T, Ye J, Shu Y.
abstractText:
Background

Stanford type A aortic dissection (AAD) is a life-threatening vascular emergency characterized by high mortality and a lack of targeted pharmacological interventions. Cuproptosis, a recently defined copper-dependent regulated cell death modality, has been implicated in various cardiovascular pathologies, yet its specific molecular role in the development of AAD remains largely unexplored.

Methods

We performed an integrated bioinformatics analysis using three independent GEO datasets (GSE107844, GSE147026, and GSE190635) to identify cuproptosis-related differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in AAD tissues. A panel of diagnostic biomarkers was selected using three machine learning algorithms: Random Forest, Support Vector Machine-Recursive Feature Elimination (SVM-RFE), and Boruta. The expression of identified hub genes was validated in clinical patient samples and a BAPN/Ang II-induced AAD mouse model via qRT-PCR and histological staining. Potential therapeutic agents were identified through the Drug-Gene Interaction Database (DGIdb) and validated using molecular docking.

Results

A total of 31 cuproptosis-related DEGs were identified. Six key genes were identified via PPI and machine learning algorithms. The differential expression patterns of these genes were validated by qRT-PCR in both AAD mouse model and clinical tissues. Subsequently, clinical correlation analysis revealed that MT1G and NLRP3 expression correlated significantly with inflammatory (white blood cell count, IL-6) and coagulation markers (D-dimer). The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) for MT1G and NLRP3 was comparable to that of D-dimer, indicating their potential value as biomarkers. Via screening using the DGIdb and validation by molecular docking, compounds such as Buthionine sulfoximine (targeting MT1G), dapansutrile (targeting NLRP3), and ARP100 (targeting DBT) demonstrated favorable binding affinity to their targets.

Conclusion

Our findings suggest that cuproptosis-related genes may play a role in AAD pathogenesis and provide candidate biomarkers and therapeutic leads for further investigation.

title: Transcatheter Thrombus Removal With the Penumbra Indigo Lightning System in Children With Congenital Heart Disease.
authorString: Balachandran AN, Hill KD, Chamberlain RC, Fleming GA.

journal.title: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions

abstractText: Thromboembolic complications in children with congenital heart disease (CHD) carry significant morbidity and mortality, particularly in patients with single ventricle physiology. Current management strategies, including systemic anticoagulation, thrombolytics, and surgical thrombectomy, each carry substantial risks in this population. Transcatheter aspiration thrombectomy represents an emerging alternative. We retrospectively reviewed all pediatric patients with CHD at our institution who underwent transcatheter aspiration thrombectomy using the Penumbra Indigo Lightning System between January 2024 and February 2025. Patient demographics, cardiac diagnosis, thrombus location, procedural details, and clinical outcomes were recorded. Five patients (age 5 months to 9 years; weight 6.3-25.9 kg) with diverse CHD diagnoses underwent six thrombectomy procedures. Thrombus locations included the Fontan circuit, inferior vena cava, pulmonary arteries, and internal jugular veins. Technical success with angiographic restoration of antegrade flow and no residual gradient across the segment of interest, was achieved in all cases (100%). Blood loss ranged from 6 to 23 mL/kg; all patients required packed red blood cell transfusion. No significant intraprocedural hemodynamic instability occurred. Three patients were discharged home with confirmed vessel patency on follow-up imaging (echocardiography and/or vascular ultrasound at 4-6 months post intervention). Two patients, both on extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) support prior to the procedure, subsequently died from causes unrelated to the thrombectomy intervention. In this limited case series, the Penumbra Indigo Lightning System demonstrated feasibility for transcatheter thrombus removal in pediatric patients across a spectrum of CHD. Given the limited number of available catheter systems in this population, this approach may be considered as a first-line or adjunct therapy in select patients when conventional medical management is insufficient or contraindicated. Further prospective studies are needed to define optimal patient selection, procedural techniques, and post-procedural management.

title: Infant mortality due to congenital heart disease in Brazil: a nationwide study of regional inequality and diagnostic imprecision, 2010-2024.
authorString: Bandeca ECM, Bandeca TC, Manso PH.
abstractText:
Objective

Congenital heart disease (CHD) is the leading cause of congenital anomaly-related deaths. In Brazil, a country marked by heterogeneous access to specialized care, mortality due to CHD may reflect disease severity and regional differences in diagnosis, screening, and treatment.

Methods

The authors characterized temporal trends, regional and federative-unit patterns of CHD-related infant mortality in Brazil from 2010 to 2024 using data from the Mortality Information System (SIM) and Live Birth Information System (SINASC). The primary case definition was restricted to ICD-10 codes Q20-Q26. Temporal trends were evaluated via Prais-Winsten regression and linear regression with Newey-West standard errors to calculate the Annual Percent Change (APC) and 95% confidence intervals (CI).

Results

Between 2010 and 2024, Brazil recorded 45,543 CHD deaths in children under one year (108.3 deaths per 100,000 live births). The Central-West and the Southeast had the highest and the lowest regional rates (125.70 and 104.38 per 100,000). National mortality notification increased (APC was 0.623%; 95% CI: 0.201 - 1.047; p = 0.012), with significant increases in the North (APC, 2.363%; p < 0.001) and Northeast (APC, 0.994%; p = 0.007), while other regions remained stationary. Over half of the deaths occurred in the neonatal period (52.8%).

Conclusion

Infant mortality notification due to CHD in Brazil increased from 2010 to 2024, showing marked regional inequalities. Rising trends in the North and Northeast and the high proportion of post-neonatal deaths suggest that delayed diagnosis, referral limitations, continuity-of-care gaps, and diagnostic imprecision in death certification influence preventable mortality.

title: Universal ECG Screening for School-Age Children: A Pediatric Cardiology and Public Health Perspective.
authorString: Mitani Y, Idriss SF, Vetter VL, Berger S, Atkins DL.
abstractText: Sudden cardiac death in the young remains an important public health concern extending beyond competitive athletes. Recent advances, including the 2025 AHA/ACC (American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology) Scientific Statement, the 2024 CSRC (Cardiac Safety Research Consortium) Think Tank Report, pediatric electrocardiogram (ECG) interpretation, disease-specific risk stratification and treatment, shared decision-making, and implementation strategies, provide a timely opportunity to reconsider the potential role of universal ECG screening in school-age children. This state-of-the-art review synthesizes contemporary evidence on the epidemiology, diagnostic value, ethics, implementation, and international experience of ECG-inclusive screening. The available evidence supports a contemporary framework for evaluating its value not only in preventing sudden cardiac death but also in facilitating earlier detection and management of childhood-onset cardiovascular diseases, with possible downstream benefits in mortality, morbidity, and health care burden. Future research should determine how universal ECG screening can be effectively implemented and evaluated across diverse health care systems.

title: Patients with Congenital Heart Disease have Inferior Intent-to-Treat Outcomes When Listed for Pediatric Heart Transplantation.
authorString: Gomes-Jourdan N, Orioha C, Fatima M, Rana A.
abstractText: While the impact of patient characteristics on waitlist and post-transplant mortality in pediatric heart transplantation has been widely studied, these metrics are limited in their ability to provide a complete picture for patients and their families. In contrast, less prevalent in the literature is an intent-to-treat analysis approach, which provides a single data point that encompasses both of these measures. This retrospective study examines pediatric patients listed for heart transplantation in the United Network for Organ Sharing (UNOS) database between 2016 and 2025, evaluating the impact of transplant indication on intent-to-treat outcomes following the implementation of the 2016 allocation policy, which prioritizes children with congenital heart disease (CHD) on inotropic support. Kaplan-Meier analysis by transplant indication was performed across all pediatric patients listed during the study period, followed by Cox regression analyses using clinical and demographic covariates. In this initial analysis, CHD patients had poorer intent-to-treat outcomes. Risk and protective factors in this particularly high-risk population were then identified using univariable Cox regression. Significant factors (p < 0.05) were entered into a multivariable Cox regression, which was used to generate a predictive score for one-year intent-to-treat mortality (c-statistic = 0.74). Risk factors significant in the multivariable analysis were age 0-1 years, geographic region, public (rather than private) insurance, need for life support and/or hemodialysis, and low serum albumin level. Following external validation and study of transplant timing on outcomes, these findings may serve as an additional tool to identify and prioritize high-risk patients and target modifiable risk factors.

title: In Situ Pericardial Roll Repair for Infantile Scimitar Syndrome.
authorString: Najm HK, McLendon L, Ibrahim A, Chovwen Md PE, Al Mosa A, Costello J, Ahmad M, Suntharos P.
abstractText:
Background

Scimitar syndrome is a rare congenital anomaly characterized by anomalous right pulmonary venous drainage. Prognosis varies according to age at presentation, with the infantile form carrying higher morbidity and mortality. Surgical repair remains challenging because of the risk of postoperative pulmonary venous obstruction.

First-in-human/early reports summary

We report an 8-week-old infant with a scimitar vein, ventricular septal defect, and atrial septal defect who underwent repair using the in situ pericardial roll technique. The postoperative course was complicated by progressive baffle stenosis that was successfully treated with transcatheter implantation of a drug-eluting stent.

Discussion

This case demonstrates the feasibility of the technique in infants and the suitability of the reconstructed pathway for successful catheter-based reintervention.

Novelty

To the best of our knowledge, this is the youngest reported patient to undergo in situ pericardial roll of a scimitar vein.

Take-home message

In situ pericardial roll repair is feasible in infants and can provide a pathway amenable to transcatheter treatment of postoperative stenosis.

title: Glenn Takedown Reconstruction Technique During Biventricular Conversion: A Contemporary Single-Center Experience.
authorString: Chen YC, Nathan M, Baird CW, Emani SM.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: World J Pediatr Congenit Heart Surg
journal.title: World journal for pediatric & congenital heart surgery
journal.isoabbreviation: World J Pediatr Congenit Heart Surg

abstractText: BackgroundGlenn takedown is an important component of staged biventricular conversion after superior cavopulmonary connection. We evaluated contemporary superior vena cava (SVC) reconstruction strategies, their evolution, and outcomes.MethodsWe reviewed consecutive patients undergoing Glenn takedown during biventricular conversion at Boston Children's Hospital from 2014 through 2024. Rescue takedowns returning patients to a systemic-to-pulmonary artery (PA) shunt or continued single-ventricle palliation were excluded. Reconstruction was classified as direct SVC-right atrial anastomosis, anterior patch/right atrial flap, interposition conduit, or mixed/asymmetric reconstruction.ResultsAmong 162 patients, reconstruction techniques used were anterior patch/right atrial flap in 120 (74.1%), interposition conduit in 33 (20.4%), direct anastomosis in 3 (1.9%), and mixed/asymmetric reconstruction in 6 (3.7%). Median age was 3.9 years (interquartile range [IQR], 2.8-5.6). Interposition use increased from 2 of 66 (3.0%) from 2014 to 2018 to 31 of 96 (32.3%) from 2019 to 2024 (P < .001). SVC reintervention occurred in two of 162 patients (1.2%) and pulmonary artery reintervention in 4/162 (2.5%) patients during a median follow-up of 1.52 years (IQR, 1.08-4.42). Temporary junctional rhythm occurred in 8/162 (4.9%); 7/162 (4.3%) received permanent pacemakers for atrioventricular block. All-cause mortality was 9.3% (15/162).ConclusionsGlenn takedown during biventricular conversion can be achieved using several reconstruction techniques selected according to individual anatomy. Our current practice favors interposition grafting when a tension-free native-tissue connection cannot be achieved, or additional space is required. SVC- and PA-related reinterventions were uncommon during available follow-up; longer surveillance is needed to assess late conduit-related outcomes.

title: Design and rationale of MIRACLE, a prospective multicenter cohort study with integrated biobanking in cardiogenic shock.
authorString: Heidenreich A, Buellesbach A, Lindner D, Schmitz R, Ewen S, Wolf D, Olivier CB, Nieters A, Franke K, Wengenmayer T, Zeymer U, Keller T, Westermann D, Bacmeister L.
abstractText:
Rationale

Cardiogenic shock carries high mortality, yet most evidence comes from patients with shock related to acute myocardial infarction. Cohorts that combine serial staging, repeated biobanking, and structured assessment of survivors across severity stages and etiologies are scarce.

Objective

MIRACLE (multimodal phenotyping in patients referred with acute cardiac failure) aims at multimodal phenotyping and risk stratification of patients with cardiogenic shock across etiologies. The primary endpoint is all-cause mortality at 30 days.

Design

Prospective, observational, multicenter cohort study with an embedded biobank. Adults with Society for Cardiovascular Angiography and Interventions (SCAI) stage B preshock or stage C to E shock of any etiology are enrolled in intensive and intermediate care units. Patients with a large anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction without shock are enrolled as controls (SCAI A) for shock related to myocardial infarction. SCAI stages are reassessed during the first 24 hours after admission to intensive care and at study visits on days 1, 3, and 5 and at discharge from intensive care, each with biobanking. Follow-up extends to 12 months and includes a visit at 6 months with repeat biobanking, exercise testing, cognitive assessment, and patient-reported outcomes.

Sites

Four centers in Germany.

Estimated enrollment

Approximately 600 patients, ≥ 500 day-1 samples.

Enrollment dates

August 2024 to the middle of 2027 (estimated).

Current status

As of 30 September 2026, 449 patients with shock or preshock and 22 controls had been enrolled. Blood samples on day 1 were obtained in 88% of eligible patients, and follow-up at 6 months was completed in 86% of eligible survivors, at the study site in 148 and by telephone in 62. Mortality at 30 days was 15% in SCAI stage B and 63% in stage E (overall 35%). Enrollment is limited to German academic centers, and very early deaths may have been missed.

Trial registration

ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT07515508, https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07515508.

title: Anticholinergic burden and mortality among adults with cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome: Evidence from a nationally representative U.S. cohort.
authorString: Liao C, Zhang Q, Zeng Y, Hu R, Wan R, Liu H, Hong K.
abstractText:
Background

Anticholinergic burden has been linked to adverse clinical outcomes, but its prognostic impact in cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome remains unclear. This study investigated its associations with CKM stages and mortality.

Methods

Data were obtained from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey. Anticholinergic burden was assessed using the Anticholinergic Drug Scale (ADS) and Anticholinergic Cognitive Burden (ACB) scale. Survey-weighted regression models were used to evaluate its associations with CKM stages and mortality, supplemented by competing-risk analyses for cardiovascular mortality.

Results

26,357 CKM participants were included (median age, 51.0 years; 52.5% male). ADS scores were significantly associated with CKM stages, with scores ≥3 (versus 0) showing greater odds of stages 2, 3, and 4 versus stage 1 (odds ratios: 1.77, 3.81, and 4.68, respectively; all P ≤ 0.003). During a median follow-up of 110.0 months, 4708 all-cause and 1280 cardiovascular deaths were documented. Compared with participants with ADS score of 0, those with ADS scores of 1-2 and ≥ 3 had increased risks of all-cause mortality, with hazard ratios (HRs) of 1.27 (95% CI: 1.15-1.40; P < 0.001) and 1.50 (95% CI: 1.34-1.68; P < 0.001), respectively. Similar association was observed for cardiovascular mortality, with corresponding HRs of 1.61 (95% CI: 1.34-1.93; P < 0.001) and 2.10 (95% CI: 1.68-2.63; P < 0.001). These findings remained consistent in competing-risk analyses for cardiovascular mortality. Similar associations were observed using the ACB scale and across CKM stages.

Conclusions

Higher anticholinergic burden was associated with advanced CKM stages and increased both all-cause and cardiovascular mortality. Further prospective studies are warranted to validate these findings.

title: Ventral hernia with loss of domain: a multimodal strategy with botulinum toxin, progressive pneumoperitoneum, omentectomy, and retromuscular reconstruction. Case report and literature review.
authorString: Brito Sosa G, Redroban Estrada LP, Iraizoz Barrios AM, Cepero Barroso JM.
abstractText: Ventral hernias with loss of domain represent a major reconstructive challenge, owing to the anatomical and functional changes that hinder tension-free fascial closure and increase the risk of intra-abdominal hypertension. We present the case of a 71-year-old woman with an 8-year history of primary ventral hernia, moderate obesity and progressive colicky abdominal pain. Abdominopelvic computed tomography revealed a hernia with severe loss of domain (Sabbagh index 36.5%). She was treated by a multidisciplinary team, achieving weight reduction and preoperative expansion of the abdominal cavity using type A botulinum toxin and progressive pneumoperitoneum. Cholecystectomy, omentectomy, open hernioplasty with retromuscular reconstruction and sublay mesh placement were performed. The outcome was favourable. This case demonstrates that a multimodal, sequential and individualized strategy achieves tension-free repair, restores abdominal wall function, and reduces the risk of complications in hernias with loss of domain.

title: Cardiorenal biomarker‑enhanced model for left ventricular hypertrophy in non-dialysis chronic kidney disease.
authorString: Ma X, Wang Y, Ruan Y, Zhu J, Yao Y, Zhang Y, Li J, Yu Y, Sun Y, Liu N.
abstractText:
Background

Left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) acts as a key factor for determinant of adverse cardiovascular outcomes in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD). Echocardiography is the standard method for LVH assessment. Yet asymptomatic LVH patients are often overlooked or missed in routine screening. Whether a biomarker-enhanced model improves detection of prevalent LVH in non-dialysis CKD remains unclear.

Methods

This cross-sectional study included 647 non-dialysis patients with CKD. We developed a clinical model based on female, age, body mass index, systolic blood pressure, hypertension, cardiovascular disease, estimated glomerular filtration rate, and serum phosphorus. Cardiorenal biomarkers, including urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR), N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), and soluble suppression of tumorigenicity 2 (sST2), were then added to assess their incremental value. Model performance was evaluated using discrimination, calibration, bootstrap internal validation, and decision curve analysis.

Results

LVH was present in 131 patients (20.2%). In multivariable analysis, female, hypertension, serum phosphorus, UACR, and sST2 were independently associated with LVH. NT‑proBNP was associated with LVH in univariable but not multivariable analysis. The clinical model had an AUC of 0.789. Adding three biomarkers improved the AUC to 0.812 (95% CI, 0.769-0.856), with lower Brier score and AIC. Bootstrap internal validation showed an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.790 and Brier score of 0.129. Decision curve analysis suggested higher net benefit for the biomarker-enhanced model across most threshold probabilities.

Conclusions

A biomarker-enhanced model incorporating UACR, NT-proBNP, and sST2, have potential clinical applications to help prioritize echocardiography referrals for asymptomatic CKD patients who may have prevalent LVH.

title: Association of apolipoprotein E gene polymorphism with cognitive function and brain structural burden in elderly patients with intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis.
authorString: Pan L, Zheng G, Ou K, Jiang L, Wang B, Chen C.
abstractText:
Objectives

To investigate whether apolipoprotein E (ApoE) ε4 carrier status is associated with 3-month cognitive performance and structural brain injury in older patients with intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis (ICAS).

Methods

This prospective cohort study enrolled 150 patients aged ≥60 years with ICAS (≥50% stenosis on MRA/CTA). ApoE ε4 carriers (n = 21, 14.0%) were compared with noncarriers. Primary outcome was 3-month Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) score. Secondary cognitive outcome was 3-month Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) score. White matter hyperintensity burden defined as Fazekas score ≥2 was primary structural outcome. Multivariable linear and logistic regression models adjusted for age, sex, education, symptomatic ICAS, hypertension, and diabetes. Firth's penalized logistic regression addressed near-complete separation in the Fazekas analysis. .

Results

ApoE ε4 carrier status was associated with lower 3-month MoCA (β = -1.887, 95% CI: -3.359 to -0.415, P = 0.013) and MMSE scores (β = -1.931, 95% CI: -3.177 to -0.685, P = 0.003). The structural analysis yielded association with Fazekas score ≥2 (Firth OR = 6.144, 95% CI: 1.331 to 59.563, P = 0.017), although this estimate was imprecise and hypothesis-generating. Additional adjustment for baseline cognitive scores changed the cognitive estimates.   .

Discussion

In older patients with ICAS, ApoE ε4 carriage is associated with poorer 3-month global cognitive performance. Given the modest sample size, few ε4 carriers, short follow-up, and single-center design, larger multicenter studies with longer follow-up are needed to clarify the longitudinal relationship between ApoE ε4 status and cognitive change.

title: Bailout rotational atherectomy rather than repeat balloon inflation after balloon rupture with extensive dissection and Ellis type II perforation in an undilatable calcified lesion.
authorString: Ouerghi K.
abstractText: A 91-year-old woman, autonomous and in excellent general condition, on apixaban for paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, was referred for disabling angina. Angiography showed two tight, heavily calcified stenoses of the mid and distal right coronary artery. During predilatation of the distal lesion, a 3.0×30mm semi-compliant balloon ruptured at 16 atm on a calcified nodule, causing an extensive dissection with intramyocardial contrast staining (Ellis type II perforation) and transient flow impairment, with ST-segment elevation, hypotension and acute pulmonary edema. Flow normalized spontaneously, but the lesion remained undilatable. Any new balloon inflation would have loaded the same nodule, with a risk of a second balloon rupture and of Ellis type III perforation, in a patient receiving apixaban, heparin, aspirin and clopidogrel.
