After recovery of TIMI 3 flow, hemodynamic stabilization and diuretic therapy, the guidewire, which had remained in the true lumen, was exchanged through a 135-cm Caravel microcatheter for a RotaWire Floppy, and bailout rotational atherectomy was performed with a 1.5-mm burr. An undersized 2.5-mm balloon then expanded without indentation, and two drug-eluting stents were implanted without extension of the dissection. At 24 months, the patient remained asymptomatic, without bleeding or thrombotic events. The absence of intravascular imaging is the main limitation of this case: upfront IVUS or OCT assessment of the calcium could have led to planned plaque modification and avoided the complication.

title: Recompensation in autoimmune hepatitis.
authorString: Lai JC, Wong YJ, Yip TC, Kulkarni AV.

journal.title: Digestive and liver disease : official journal of the Italian Society of Gastroenterology and the Italian Association for the Study of the Liver

abstractText: Autoimmune hepatitis (AIH) is an immune-mediated liver disease in which persistent necroinflammation drives progressive fibrosis, cirrhosis, and ultimately portal hypertension-related decompensation. Effective immunosuppression may halt hepatic inflammation, thereby inducing biochemical (and histological) remission, facilitating regeneration of hepatic function, clinical recompensation, and fibrosis regression. Studies indicate that approximately 19-54% of immunosuppressed patients achieve recompensation. Lower Child-Pugh score, lower immunoglobulin G levels, and a complete biochemical response are associated with higher recompensation rates, whereas advanced-grade hepatic encephalopathy and a higher Model for End-stage Liver Disease score are associated with lower recompensation rates. Recompensation improves prognosis and transplant-free survival compared with non-recompensated AIH patients. However, recompensation should not be equated with resolution of portal hypertension or a reduced risk of hepatocellular carcinoma, which may persist and continue to require surveillance and treatment. CONCLUSION: Recompensation in AIH is possible and confers better clinical outcomes. However, with the definition of aetiological control less well defined, data remain heterogeneous.

title: Lupus Nephritis in Pregnancy: A Case-Based Approach to Diagnosis and Management.
authorString: Ankawi G, Lightstone L, Koubar SH.
abstractText: Pregnancy presents both a unique opportunity to diagnose previously unrecognized lupus nephritis (LN) and a critical period that influences long-term renal and maternal outcomes in women with established disease. For many young women, pregnancy represents their first significant interaction with the healthcare system. Abnormal findings such as persistent hematuria or proteinuria should not be dismissed as physiologic changes of pregnancy; rather, they should prompt appropriate evaluation for underlying kidney disease. In selected cases, kidney biopsy remains an important diagnostic tool during pregnancy when the results are expected to alter management. In women with established LN, disease activity at conception is the strongest modifiable predictor of maternal and fetal outcomes. Consequently, pregnancy should ideally be planned during sustained disease quiescence, underscoring the importance of preconception counseling, avoidance of unplanned pregnancies, and optimization of pregnancy-compatible immunosuppressive therapy. Pregnancy in women with LN poses several unique diagnostic and therapeutic challenges, including risk stratification, medication adjustments, prevention of disease flares, and management of maternal and fetal complications. A major clinical challenge is differentiating an LN flare from preeclampsia, as both conditions share overlapping clinical and laboratory features but require fundamentally different management strategies. Advances in angiogenic biomarkers, fetal surveillance, and multidisciplinary care have improved the ability to distinguish these conditions and optimize outcomes. Using a real clinical case scenario, this review discusses current evidence on the diagnosis and management of LN before and during pregnancy, including preconception counseling, disease monitoring, therapeutic considerations, and maternal and fetal risk assessment, emphasizing the importance of individualized, multidisciplinary care.

title: Allostatic load is not associated with augmented vasoconstrictive response to cold pressor test or functional sympatholysis in Black emerging adults.
authorString: Blake EF, Eagan LE, Weiner CM, Mascone SE, Lefferts EC, Tyrell FA, Ranadive SM.
abstractText: Black individuals are disproportionately affected by hypertension (HTN), even after controlling for conventional risk factors (i.e., obesity, smoking, physical fitness). Emerging evidence implicates chronic psychosocial stress, including discrimination/race-related events, in HTN development. Allostatic load (AL) reflects the cumulative adverse impact of repeated activation of compensatory physiological responses to psychosocial stressors. We assessed the associations between AL and disruptions in vascular parameters that may indicate heightened HTN risk in Black emerging adults. Forearm blood flow (FBF) and vascular conductance (FVC) were measured during sympathoexcitation (cold pressor test; CPT), alone and with handgrip exercise, (EX + CPT) in 35 Black undergraduate students (24F/11M, 20 ± 1 years). AL was determined using both clinical cutoffs (AL-CC) and individual z-scores (AL-z) from nine biomarkers (heart rate, systolic blood pressure (BP), diastolic BP, C-reactive protein, glucose, creatinine, total cholesterol/HDL-C ratio, cortisol, %body fat). Higher scores reflected greater AL burden. AL scores were overall low (AL-z: 0.003 ± 3.9; AL-CC: 1.6 ± 1.2). Reductions in FBF and FVC during EX + CPT (∆FBF: -3.58% ± 3.14%; ∆FVC: -12.56% ± 6.77%) were significantly attenuated (P < 0.001) as compared to CPT alone (∆FBF: -24.15% ± 7.95%; ∆FVC: -35.54% ± 9.20%). AL was not correlated with CPT-FBF, -FVC or with functional sympatholysis magnitude (%); however, blunted diurnal cortisol slope correlated with larger reductions in CPT-FBF (r = -0.55, P = 0.00328), and increased FBF- (r = 0.49, P = 0.00957) and FVC- (r = 0.43, P = 0.0283) lysis. These findings suggest hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis dysregulation in Black emerging adults may elicit exaggerated vasoreactivity to sympathoexcitatory stress.

title: A bailout strategy for CRT implantation: Retrograde coronary venous wiring with venoplasty and wire externalization.
authorString: Tirumalai Nc P, Barwad P, Shankar M, Nema R.
abstractText: Left ventricular (LV) lead delivery failure remains a major limitation of cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT), particularly in patients with complex coronary venous anatomy. We report a 65-year-old woman with non-ischemic cardiomyopathy (LVEF 30%, LBBB, QRS 170 ms) referred for CRT-D after a failed implantation attempt elsewhere. Coronary sinus angiography revealed a small-calibre high lateral vein and a lateral vein with severe post-ostial stenosis. After unsuccessful antegrade wiring, a retrograde strategy was employed: a microcatheter and Fielder XT-A guidewire traversed epicardial collaterals from the posterior to the lateral vein. The Fielder XT-A was then exchanged for a 300-cm RG3 guidewire, which was externalized using a gooseneck snare to create a through-and-through rail. Sequential balloon venoplasty (1.5-2.5 mm) dilated the stenotic segment, enabling successful quadripolar LV lead placement. The D1-M2 vector achieved a capture threshold of 1.2 V at 0.5 ms without phrenic nerve stimulation. At 12-month follow-up, the patient improved to New York Heart Association class I with LVEF 45% and no heart failure admissions. This case demonstrates the sequential application of retrograde coronary venous wiring, wire exchange, snare-assisted externalization, and balloon venoplasty-techniques adapted from interventional cardiology-to overcome severely stenotic coronary venous anatomy when conventional antegrade approaches fail. Advanced coronary intervention techniques may provide a reproducible bailout strategy for achieving optimal LV lead positioning in patients with complex coronary venous anatomy.

title: Brain volumes and their relationship with cerebral microbleeds and cognition in middle-aged adults with type 1 diabetes.
authorString: Kyläheiko I, Kuusela L, Claesson TB, Tarkkonen A, Martola J, Paajanen TI, Virkkala J, Groop PH, Thorn LM, Tatlisumak T, Putaala J, Gordin D, Jokinen H, FinnDiane Study Group.
abstractText:
Aims

Type 1 diabetes (T1D) is associated with brain volumetric alterations, cerebral microbleeds (CMBs), and cognitive deficits. We examined brain volumes and their direct and combined associations with CMBs on cognitive performance in T1D.

Methods

Adults with T1D (n = 163; age 46 ± 8 years; diabetes duration 31 ± 10 years; 53% women) and 48 matched controls underwent brain MRI and clinical and neuropsychological evaluations. Volumetric MRI measures included total brain (TBV) and white matter volume (WMV), and volumes of cortex, thalamus, hippocampus, nucleus accumbens, and choroid plexus.

Results

Individuals with T1D had smaller TBV, WMV, cortex, thalamus, and nucleus accumbens volumes, and larger choroid plexus, than controls (Cohen's d = 0.39-0.54). Those with T1D and ≥3 CMBs (n = 25) had smaller TBV, WMV, and cortex, thalamus, and nucleus accumbens than those with 0-2 CMBs (n = 138; Cohen's d = 0.54-0.92). Brain volumes were not directly linked to cognition, but CMB burden moderated the associations between TBV, WMV, nucleus accumbens, and choroid plexus and cognitive performance (standardized β: -0.61-(-0.51) and 0.54-0.75, pFDR = 0.006-0.048).

Conclusions

Middle-aged individuals with T1D showed smaller global and regional brain volumes and larger choroid plexus than healthy controls. Individuals with CMB burden showed associations between brain volumetric alterations and cognitive deficits.

title: Characterization of the Urine Proteome Using the Olink Explore 3072 Platform.
authorString: Meier M, Schoberth M, Li Y, Borisov O, Uluvar B, Willeke C, Meiselbach H, Eckardt KU, Schilling O, Köttgen A, Haug S.
abstractText:
Introduction

Urinary proteins are valuable biomarkers for physiological processes and early detection/monitoring of kidney diseases. However, comprehensive quantification and characterization of the urine proteome using a high-throughput platform remains limited.

Methods

Using the affinity-based Olink Explore 3072 proteomics assay, we quantified 2868 proteins in urine samples from 1268 participants of the German Chronic Kidney Disease (GCKD) study.

Results

Protein detectability in urine, defined as the percentage of samples with measurements above the limit of detection, showed a bimodal distribution: 659 (23%) proteins had high (over 80%) and 1336 proteins (47%) had low (under 20%) detectability, with stable detectability across strata of albuminuria and kidney function. More than 95% of highly detectable proteins had previously been identified in urine by mass spectrometry. Highly detectable proteins were enriched for extracellular, exosomal, and cell surface localization, and for expression in hepatocytes, immune cells and kidney proximal tubule cells. Comparison with plasma detectability from the UK Biobank Pharma Proteomics Project identified proteins of likely kidney origin, including LRP2 (megalin) and NPHS2 (podocin). In a multivariable adjusted model of 13 clinical variables, albuminuria and an individual's sex showed significant associations with 779 and 670 proteins, respectively. Specific chronic kidney disease etiologies showed associations with 105 proteins, although etiology explained only a small proportion of protein variance. Correlation analysis revealed biologically meaningful protein clusters reflecting shared cellular compartments, tissue of origin, and molecular interactions.

Conclusions

Large-scale urine proteomic profiling using a high-multiplex affinity-based platform captures biologically meaningful molecular variation associated with clinical variables and chronic kidney disease, providing a valuable resource for biomarker discovery and future targeted studies.

title: Micro- and Nanoplastic Exposure and Cardiometabolic Health: A Nutrition-Focused Critical Review.
authorString: Cakici C, Yesildemir O, Arslan S, Amorim MJB.
abstractText: Micro- and nanoplastics (MNPs) have emerged as potential environmental determinants of human health because of their widespread presence in food, drinking water, food-contact materials, and the broader environment. This nutrition-focused critical review evaluates current evidence linking MNP exposure with cardiometabolic health by integrating dietary exposure pathways, toxicological mechanisms, experimental findings, emerging human evidence, and precautionary exposure-reduction approaches. Available studies suggest that MNPs may interfere with metabolic homeostasis through oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, chronic inflammation, endocrine disruption, intestinal barrier impairment, gut microbial dysbiosis, and the release or transport of plastic-associated chemicals. These processes have been implicated in biological alterations related to cardiovascular disease, dyslipidemia, insulin resistance and type 2 diabetes, obesity, hypertension, and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease. However, the strength of evidence differs substantially across outcomes. Most mechanistic findings originate from in vitro and animal studies, frequently using particle types and exposure doses that may not fully represent typical human exposure. Human studies remain limited and are predominantly observational, precluding firm causal inference. Major knowledge gaps include the absence of standardized analytical and biomonitoring methods, heterogeneity in particle size and polymer composition, uncertainty regarding environmentally relevant doses, and the scarcity of prospective epidemiological studies. Overall, current evidence supports biological plausibility but remains insufficient to establish MNP exposure as an independent causal cardiometabolic risk factor. Standardized exposure assessment, long-term human studies, and better integration of dietary, environmental, and clinical data are needed.

title: Drug Development in Pediatric Heart Failure: Current Landscape and Future Directions.
authorString: Sekar P, Pizzato PE, Mattsson U, Bartley N, Li H, Learoyd M, Siapkara A, Zee P, Lorts A, Daly KP.
abstractText: Pediatric heart failure (HF) remains an important area of unmet medical need. Pharmacological treatments primarily consist of adult drugs used off label in children. HF regulatory guidance specific to pediatric drug development is limited. The diversity in underlying pathophysiology necessitates a shift toward a mechanism-of-action driven approach. We examine the current landscape of pediatric HF, identify key challenges and opportunities for drug development, and discuss a paradigm shift to a new high-level HF phenotype classification system for pediatric HF. Pediatric extrapolation utilizing pharmacokinetics and bridging biomarkers, especially given the absence of validated surrogate endpoints, remains a promising strategy for subsets of pediatric HF physiology. Ongoing reorganization of pediatric regulatory frameworks presents a key opportunity to promote harmonization between pediatric requirements from regulatory agencies across jurisdictions. We describe innovation in pediatric HF treatment through use of extrapolation, bridging biomarkers, and adaptive trial design.

title: Clinical Risk, Carotid Plaque Burden, Cardiac Remodeling, and Left Ventricular Diastolic Dysfunction in Asymptomatic Adults Referred for Exercise Stress Echocardiography.
authorString: Naqvi TZ, Van Woerkom RC, Baxter CM, Stepanek J.

journal.title: Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography : official publication of the American Society of Echocardiography

abstractText:
Background

Exercise stress echocardiography (SE) assesses inducible ischemia but may not identify subclinical atherosclerosis or early cardiac remodeling. We evaluated the prevalence of subclinical carotid atherosclerosis and its relationships with clinical risk estimates, cardiac remodeling, and diastolic function in asymptomatic adults referred for exercise SE.

Methods

In this prospective, blinded cohort study, 73 consecutive asymptomatic adults without known cardiovascular disease (CVD) underwent treadmill SE, carotid ultrasonography for carotid intima-media thickness (CIMT), plaque presence and burden, and resting echocardiography. Radial-artery tonometry (RAT) was performed in 33 participants. Ten-year risk was estimated using the Framingham general CVD risk score (FRS), Pooled Cohort Equations for atherosclerotic CVD (PCE-ASCVD), and Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease EVENTs (PREVENT) equations for ASCVD, total CVD, and heart failure (PREVENT-HF).

Results

Among 70 evaluable participants, 69 (98.6%) had negative SE findings for inducible ischemia; one demonstrated a hypertensive myopathic response. Carotid plaque was present in 46 participants (65.7%), and isolated CIMT >75th percentile without plaque was present in 6 (8.6%), yielding a combined prevalence of subclinical carotid atherosclerosis of 74.3%. Plaque prevalence increased across FRS, PCE-ASCVD, and PREVENT-ASCVD categories but remained 45.8% among participants classified as low risk by PREVENT-ASCVD. All five clinical risk estimates correlated with plaque number, maximum plaque thickness, total plaque area, and relative LV wall thickness. Greater plaque area was associated with higher relative wall thickness, left ventricular (LV) mass index, and diastolic-function grade. PREVENT-HF showed the strongest numerical correlations with diastolic-function grade and average E/e'. In a model incorporating plaque area and PREVENT-HF, PREVENT-HF was independently associated with diastolic dysfunction (OR per SD, 2.60; 95% CI, 1.30-5.20; P=.007), whereas plaque area was not. Exercise duration and rate-pressure product were not associated with plaque burden.

Conclusions

Among asymptomatic adults with CVD risk factors referred for exercise SE, inducible ischemia was uncommon despite a high prevalence of subclinical carotid atherosclerosis. Carotid plaque burden and clinical risk estimates were associated with cardiac remodeling and diastolic function, while PREVENT-HF was independently associated with diastolic dysfunction. These findings support complementary characterization of subclinical vascular and cardiac abnormalities but do not establish incremental outcome prediction, altered treatment eligibility, or replacement of clinically indicated stress testing by carotid imaging.

title: Long-term outcomes of renal denervation in patients with resistant hypertension.
authorString: Bustos-Merlo A, Fajardo-Muñoz A, Rico-López D, Bretones-Del Pino T, Sánchez-Gila J, Roa-Chamorro R, Molina-Navarro E, Jaén-Águila F.
abstractText:
Objective

To evaluate the medium- and long-term outcomes of renal denervation (RD) in patients with resistant hypertension (RH), focusing on blood pressure (BP) control, antihypertensive drug burden, and renal safety.

Methods

Prospective observational study including 51 patients with RH treated between 2020 and 2024 with radiofrequency RD using the Symplicity Spyral™ system. BP values, antihypertensive therapy, estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), and procedural complications were assessed over a 24-month follow-up.

Results

Systolic BP was significantly reduced, with a mean overall decrease of -12.3 mmHg at the end of follow-up (p < 0.001), while diastolic BP decreased by -5.1 mmHg at 24 months (p = 0.01). The number of antihypertensive drugs was significantly reduced, and 82.6% of patients achieved clinical success. A mild decline in eGFR was observed without clinical relevance. Age ≥50 years was associated with a higher likelihood of response. Major complications were infrequent (4.3%).

Conclusions

RD is an effective and safe therapeutic option for selected patients with RH, providing sustained BP reduction and a decreased need for antihypertensive medication.

title: Baseline sarcopenia and subsequent dementia after incident atrial fibrillation or flutter in the UK Biobank.
authorString: Yu Y, Ling T, Li X, Zhang N, Pan W, Lin C, Xie Y, Bao Y, Luo Q, Wei Y, Qi J, Liqun W.

journal.title: The journal of nutrition, health & aging

abstractText:
Background

The association between sarcopenia and dementia after incident atrial fibrillation or flutter (AF/flutter) remains uncertain.

Methods

We studied 30,743 UK Biobank participants free of AF/flutter at recruitment who subsequently had a first recorded AF/flutter event. Sarcopenia was assessed at recruitment; dementia follow-up began at that event. Analyses used Cox and Fine-Gray models, propensity-score matching and restricted cubic splines. Exploratory analyses tested interactions with AF/flutter, heart failure and coronary artery disease status at entry.

Results

Sarcopenia was present in 2,279 participants (7.4%). Over a median 4.27 years after AF/flutter entry, 1,155 developed dementia. Recruitment preceded entry by a median 8.50 years. Fully adjusted analyses included 26,430 participants and 998 all-cause dementia events. Sarcopenia was associated with all-cause dementia in Cox (hazard ratio [HR], 1.41; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.16-1.72) and Fine-Gray models (subdistribution HR, 1.31; 95% CI, 1.08-1.59). The matched Cox HR was 1.35 (95% CI, 1.09-1.66). Fully adjusted Cox HRs were 1.64 (95% CI, 1.15-2.35) for vascular dementia and 1.34 (95% CI, 0.92-1.93) for Alzheimer's disease. No interactions with cardiovascular condition status were detected.

Conclusions

Sarcopenia assessed at recruitment was associated with all-cause dementia after incident AF/flutter. Prospective studies should assess the clinical value of muscle measurements near AF/flutter diagnosis.

title: Association of objectively measured physical activity with incident spinal stenosis in a Fitbit-linked cohort from the All of Us Research Program.
authorString: Wang B, Wang I, Chen A, Lambrechts M.

journal.title: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia

abstractText:
Background

Physical activity is associated with numerous health benefits, but its relationship with the development of spinal stenosis remains unclear. We evaluated whether objectively measured physical activity using consumer wearable devices is associated with incident spinal stenosis.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective cohort study using prospectively collected wearable and electronic health record data from the NIH All of Us Research Program. Adults with at least 6 months of qualifying Fitbit data linked to electronic health records were followed from the end of their sixth qualifying month. Physical activity was quantified using monthly mean daily step counts and minutes of fairly and very active activity. Incident spinal stenosis, cervical stenosis, and lumbar stenosis were identified using standardized SNOMED concepts mapped to the OMOP Common Data Model. Time-varying Cox proportional hazards models with physical activity lagged by 12 months estimated hazard ratios (HRs) for the 75th versus 25th percentile of exposure, adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, education, race, smoking, diabetes, osteoarthritis, hypertension, prior spine pain, comorbidity burden, and health care use, with multiple imputation for missing covariates.

Results

Among 48,709 participants free of spinal stenosis at baseline, 1,494 developed spinal stenosis during 161,900 person-years of follow-up (median 3.42 years), including 640 cervical and 982 lumbar cases. Participants at the 75th percentile of daily steps had a lower hazard of spinal stenosis than those at the 25th percentile (HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.77-0.92). Estimates were similar for cervical stenosis (HR 0.81, 95% CI 0.71-0.92) and lumbar stenosis (HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.77-0.95), and formal tests found no difference between the two. Very active minutes were associated with a lower hazard of any and cervical stenosis (HR 0.89, 95% CI 0.83-0.96, and HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.74-0.94) but not, after adjustment for multiple testing, lumbar stenosis (HR 0.91, 95% CI 0.84-1.00). Fairly active minutes were not associated with stenosis, and we found no evidence of nonlinear dose-response relationships. The association of steps with lumbar stenosis weakened to the null with a 36-month lag, and the association with cervical stenosis was not confirmed under a stricter case definition.

Conclusions

Higher daily step counts were associated with a lower hazard of coded spinal stenosis, with similar associations for cervical and lumbar disease. The associations were modest, and reverse causation, outcome misclassification, and unmeasured confounding could explain part or all of them. LOE: III.

title: Thermodynamic Response During Invasive Cardiopulmonary Exercise Testing.
authorString: Miyashita S, Lane J, Paul D, Yano Y, Naito T, Tonelli AR.
abstractText:
Background

Core temperature is continuously measured during invasive cardiopulmonary exercise testing (iCPET), but its physiologic and clinical significance remains poorly defined.

Objectives

The purpose of this study was to characterize exercise core temperature responses during iCPET and determine whether temperature-derived metrics are associated with cardiopulmonary reserve, abnormal physiologic phenotypes, and clinically relevant iCPET thresholds.

Methods

We studied 396 adults undergoing iCPET for unexplained exertional intolerance. Core temperature was measured using the thermistor of a pulmonary artery catheter. Temperature-derived metrics included peak exercise temperature, increase in temperature from baseline to peak exercise, and increase in temperature indexed to peak workload. Associations with hemodynamic and gas-exchange variables were assessed using age- and sex-adjusted models. Area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve (AUC) analyses evaluated discrimination for normal vs abnormal iCPET findings and selected physiologic thresholds.

Results

Participants were 50.6 ± 16.0 years old, and 66% were female. Core temperature increased during exercise from 37.0 °C ± 0.34 °C at baseline to 37.5 °C ± 0.51 °C at peak exercise, with a mean increase of 0.40 °C ± 0.37 °C. Temperature-derived metrics were directly associated with peak cardiac index and percent-predicted peak oxygen uptake and inversely associated with pulmonary artery occlusion pressure/cardiac output slope and minute ventilation/carbon dioxide production slope. Temperature responses were blunted in heart failure, pulmonary hypertension, chronotropic incompetence, and impaired peripheral oxygen extraction. For identifying a normal test, age- and sex-adjusted AUCs were 0.70 for peak exercise temperature, 0.74 for increase in temperature, and 0.68 for workload-indexed temperature increase.

Conclusions

Exercise core temperature responses during iCPET reflect hemodynamic augmentation and aerobic performance and may provide a simple adjunctive physiologic marker for clinically relevant exercise abnormalities.

title: 24-hour Movement Guideline Adherence and Cardiometabolic Health among Adults with Disabilities: Analysis of NHANES 2013-2018.
authorString: Liang Y, Zhu X, Haegele J.

journal.title: Applied physiology, nutrition, and metabolism = Physiologie appliquee, nutrition et metabolisme

abstractText: A growing body of evidence has examined the association between adherence to the 24-hour movement guidelines and cardiometabolic health outcomes. However, it remains unclear whether these associations extend to adults with disabilities, a population experiencing substantial health disparities. Therefore, this study examined the association between adherence to the 24-hour movement guidelines and cardiometabolic health among adults with disabilities. This cross-sectional study used data from the 2013-2018 cycles of the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES). A nationally representative sample of U.S. adults with disabilities (n = 4,985) was included. Survey-weighted logistic regression models with multiple imputation were used to examine associations between guideline adherence and cardiometabolic health. Subgroup analyses were conducted across cardiometabolic outcomes and functional disability types. The results showed that participants meeting three guidelines had higher odds of being free from cardiovascular disease (AOR = 2.05, 95% CI: 1.42-2.94), obesity (AOR = 1.99, 95% CI: 1.44-2.75), hypertension (AOR = 1.75, 95% CI: 1.22-2.50) and type 2 diabetes (AOR = 1.60, 95% CI: 1.14-2.24), than those meeting none of the guidelines. Meeting two guidelines was associated with higher odds of being free from hypertension and obesity. Associations between guideline adherence and cardiometabolic health varied across functional disability subgroups. These findings suggest that adherence to a greater number of movement guidelines is associated with having more favorable cardiometabolic health profiles for adults with disabilities. Exploratory subgroup analyses showed variation in the associations across disability types, further research is needed to determine whether associations differ across functional impairment groups and whether movement recommendations should be tailored accordingly.

title: A statistical framework to identify gene-gene interactions underlying multiple dichotomous phenotypes from genotype data.
authorString: Wang S, Zhu X, Li Y, Jia G.
abstractText: Identifying gene-gene (G × G) interactions across multiple dichotomous phenotypes is challenging due to the extreme sparsity of SNP-derived interaction matrices and the reduced statistical power associated with binary outcomes. Existing G × G association methods are restricted to either single or multiple continuous phenotypes. Here we introduce GiMat (Gene Interaction and Multiple-phenotype Association Test), a statistical framework that extends multivariate kernel regression to model G × G interactions jointly across dichotomous phenotypes, while explicitly capturing homogeneous and heterogeneous interaction effects. Extensive simulations demonstrate that GiMat controls type I error conservatively and adapts power flexibly to different types of relationships between interaction effects and phenotypes. Applied to type 2 diabetes and hypertension comorbidity in the UK Biobank, GiMat identified four previously unreported G × G interaction pairs associated with both phenotypes. This scalable framework enables robust discovery of complex genetic interactions underlying multiple correlated phenotypes.

title: Anemia and Iron Status in Pregnant and Postpartum Women With Acute Heart Failure.
authorString: Nair M, Choudhury SS, Sundar A, Rao S, Deka G, V CS, Rani A, Ismavel VA, Kakoty SD, Mahanta P, Zahir F, Roy I, Deka R, Opondo C, Agarwal M, Krasner S, Leeson P, Lakhal-Littleton S, Casadei B, Armitage J.
abstractText:
Importance

In low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), iron-deficient anemia is highly prevalent and may compound the cardiovascular stress of pregnancy, yet its contribution to maternal acute heart failure (AHF) is poorly understood.

Objectives

To investigate the association of maternal anemia and iron status with AHF in pregnancy and post partum in India.

Design, setting, and participants

This multicenter, unmatched, prospective case-control study recruited participants from 10 hospitals across 4 Indian states from February 2019 to November 2024. Incident cases were pregnant or postpartum women with clinically diagnosed AHF. Controls were women without history or symptoms of heart disease within 48 hours post partum. Data were analyzed from March 2025 to April 2026.

Exposures

Maternal anemia and iron status. Blood samples collected at recruitment were analyzed for hemoglobin, ferritin, transferrin saturation, soluble transferrin receptor, and hepcidin.

Main outcomes and measures

The outcome of interest was AHF, defined using clinical criteria. Multivariable logistic regression models assessed associations of iron status and anemia with AHF, adjusting for potential confounders, including hypertensive disorders of pregnancy. Subgroup analyses were performed in women with echocardiographic abnormalities and peripartum cardiomyopathy. The discriminatory capacity of a model including anemia present before AFH onset vs a model with established risk factors only was examined using receiver operating characteristic curves.

Results

Among 532 women with clinically diagnosed AHF (median [IQR] age, 25 [21-29] years) and 1091 controls (median [IQR] age, 25 [21-28] years), moderate and severe anemia were associated with 1.5-fold (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.52; 95% CI, 1.13-2.05) and 5-fold (aOR, 5.06; 95% CI, 3.02-8.48) increased odds of AHF, respectively, compared with women without anemia. Higher soluble transferrin receptor levels (aOR, 1.44; 95% CI, 1.31-1.57) and the lowest hepcidin quintile (aOR, 2.65; 95% CI, 1.69-4.14), both indicative of iron deficiency, were independently associated with AHF. These associations persisted after adjusting for hypertensive disorders of pregnancy and after excluding women with preexisting cardiac conditions, and they were consistent in subgroups with echocardiographic abnormalities and peripartum cardiomyopathy. Adding anemia to established risk factors improved model discrimination for identifying AHF risk, increasing the AUC from 78% (95% CI, 76%-81%) to 83% (95% CI, 80%-85%) (P < .001).

Conclusion and relevance

This case-control study found that maternal anemia and iron deficiency were independently associated with AHF during pregnancy and post partum. Further studies are needed to determine whether preventing or treating iron deficiency and anemia can reduce AHF risk and improve maternal outcomes.

title: Sustained Anlotinib-Based Combination Therapy Beyond Progression in Advanced Soft Tissue Sarcoma: A Large Multicenter Real-World Study.
authorString: Yuan Y, Ye T, Fan L, Sun X, Wang J, Luo Z, Chen J.
abstractText:
Introduction

Multitarget antiangiogenic tyrosine kinase inhibitors play a pivotal role in the treatment of soft tissue sarcoma (STS), but acquired resistance is common, and treatment discontinuation at progression may trigger tumor rebound. Evidence for continuing antiangiogenic therapy beyond progression in STS remains limited. This study evaluated the efficacy and safety of sustained anlotinib-based combination therapy in patients with advanced STS who had progressed on prior anlotinib therapy.

Methods

This retrospective study reviewed patients with advanced STS from four representative Chinese sarcoma centers. Patients who received anlotinib-based combinations after progression on prior anlotinib were included. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS). Secondary endpoints included overall survival (OS), objective response rate, disease control rate (DCR), and safety.

Results

Between February 15, 2020, and March 31, 2023, 217 patients were included. The median age was 61 (range, 26-88) years, and 131 patients (60.4%) were male. With a median follow-up of 7.4 months, the median PFS was 4.2 (95% CI, 3.7-4.5) months, with a 21.9% 6-month PFS rate. The median OS was not reached, and the 6-month OS rate was 91.4%. No objective responses were observed, but stable disease was achieved in 158 patients, resulting in a DCR of 72.8%. The most common treatment-related adverse events were hypertension (20.7%) and hand-foot syndrome (14.7%), and no unexpected toxicities were observed.

Conclusion

Sustained anlotinib-based treatment beyond disease progression showed promising clinical activity in patients with advanced STS, with a safety profile generally consistent with that previously reported for anlotinib. These findings warrant validation in future studies.

title: Urinary Sodium-to-Potassium Ratio in Hypertension: From Epidemiologic Marker to Clinical Tool?
authorString: Wehbe F, Alyahya N, Hiremath S.
abstractText:
Purpose of review

This review evaluates whether the urinary sodium-to-potassium (Na/K) ratio can move from an epidemiologic biomarker of dietary electrolyte balance to a clinically useful tool in hypertension care, focusing on biological rationale, measurement, interpretation, blood pressure associations, cardiovascular-kidney outcomes, and limitations.

Recent findings

Population-based, repeated-measurement, and treated-hypertension studies link higher urinary Na/K ratios with higher blood pressure, hypertension risk, poorer blood pressure control, and selected cardiovascular outcomes. Associations appear strongest when measurements are repeated and interpreted alongside home blood pressure. Emerging consensus recommendations and self-monitoring studies suggest practical implementation pathways, while salt-substitution trials support the broader importance of modifying sodium-potassium balance. The urinary Na/K ratio is physiologically grounded and clinically promising, but it is not yet a validated treatment target. Clinical translation requires standardized measurement protocols, validated thresholds across diverse populations, intervention trials, and safety data in high-risk groups.

title: miR-6891 predicts atrial fibrillation recurrence and promotes fibroblast dysfunction.
authorString: Wang HL, Li YP, Feng XM, Chen X, Liu J, Wang HX.
abstractText: The molecular mechanisms underlying AF pathogenesis and post‑ablation relapse remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to investigate the expression profile and prognostic value of miR‑6891 in AF, as well as its functional role and downstream mechanism in Ang II‑stimulated atrial fibroblasts. Serum miR‑6891 levels were measured by RT‑qPCR, and its recurrence‑predictive performance was evaluated by ROC curve. Multivariate logistic regression was performed to identify independent risk factors for post‑ablation recurrence. In vitro assays, human atrial fibroblasts were treated with Ang II to mimic pathological remodeling. Cellular migration, proliferation, ferroptosis markers (GSH‑Px, ROS, MDA, Fe²⁺), inflammatory cytokines (TNF‑α, IL‑6, IL‑1β), and fibrosis‑related proteins (Collagen I, MMP9, Collagen III) were assessed. Target prediction and validation were conducted using bioinformatics and dual‑luciferase reporter assays. Functional rescue experiments were performed by co‑transfection with PTEN siRNA. miR‑6891 was significantly upregulated in serum of AF patients compared with controls and exhibited favorable predictive accuracy. Multivariate logistic regression identified miR‑6891 and hs‑CRP as independent predictors of recurrence. In vitro, miR‑6891 inhibition suppressed Ang II‑induced migration, proliferation, ferroptosis, inflammation, and fibrosis. Mechanistically, Ang II downregulated PTEN, an effect reversed by miR‑6891 inhibitor. Silencing PTEN partially abrogated the protective effects of miR‑6891 inhibition on cellular dysfunction, ferroptosis, inflammation, and fibrosis. miR‑6891 is upregulated in AF and serves as a novel candidate independent predictor of post‑ablation recurrence. It mediates Ang II‑induced pathological changes in atrial fibroblasts by directly targeting PTEN, suggesting that miR‑6891 may represent a novel therapeutic target for AF management.

title: Integrated radiomics-deep learning modeling of hepatic vasculature for enhanced noninvasive prediction of portal hypertension and high-risk gastroesophageal varices.
authorString: Qiu Q, Zheng R, Wang C, Wang H, Lin J.
abstractText:
Objectives

To evaluate whether CT-derived radiomics and deep learning features can improve non-invasive risk stratification of clinically significant portal hypertension (CSPH) and high-risk gastroesophageal varices (HRVs) in cirrhotic patients.

Materials and methods

This retrospective study included 454 cirrhotic patients from center A and 77 from center B. CSPH labels were available only for patients from center A. Patients in both centers with available endoscopic findings were classified as HRVs or non-HRVs. A dual-path modeling framework integrating radiomics and deep learning-derived features extracted from multiple major hepatic vessels was developed, and was compared with single-path (radiomics-only and deep learning-only), single-vessel, vascular geometric, and clinical-feature-based models. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC).

Results

For CSPH prediction, the dual-path model achieved the highest AUC (0.892 vs. 0.678-0.870 for the other models; P < 0.05 for most comparisons). For HRVs prediction, the proposed model achieved AUCs of 0.790 and 0.782 in the internal and external test set, respectively. The proposed model consistently outperformed the single-path models (0.625-0.648; all P < 0.05), single-vessel models (0.526-0.642; all P < 0.05), the vascular geometric model (0.528; P < 0.01), and the clinical-feature-based models (0.327-0.728; P < 0.001 for the APRI-based model) in the external test set.

Conclusion

A dual-path model integrating multi-vessel radiomics and deep learning features demonstrates robust predictive performance for CSPH and HRVs in cirrhotic patients. This approach may provide a new non-invasive alternative for risk stratification and clinical management of portal hypertension-related complications.

title: Abbreviated brain magnetic resonance imaging protocol using fluid-attenuated inversion recovery and diffusion-weighted imaging in pediatric emergency neuroimaging.
authorString: Çetinoğlu YK, Kurt Koçak M, Karaoğlu P, Akgül F, Ünalp A, Apa H, Coşkun M.
abstractText:
Background

Rapid brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) protocols may reduce radiation exposure and sedation requirements in pediatric emergency neuroimaging.

Objective

To evaluate the feasibility and clinical adequacy of an abbreviated brain MRI (abMRI) protocol featuring fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) and diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) in pediatric emergency neuroimaging.

Materials and methods

This retrospective cohort study included pediatric emergency department patients who underwent abMRI between July 2023 and July 2025. The protocol consisted of axial diffusion-weighted imaging and axial fluid-attenuated inversion recovery obtained with motion-resistant radial filling, with an acquisition time of approximately 220 s. Technical success and clinical adequacy were evaluated using image quality, emergency observation, pediatric neurology follow-up, and full-protocol MRI when clinically indicated.

Results

Among 971 attempted examinations, diagnostic-quality images were obtained in 951, yielding a technical success rate of 97.9% (95% confidence interval [CI] 96.8-98.7%). The mean age was 7.61±5.46 years, and 480 patients (50.5%) were boys. Of the 951 diagnostic examinations, 649 underwent no further neuroimaging. Full-protocol MRI was performed in 302 patients. Eight false-negative cases were identified. The overall clinical adequacy rate was 99.2% (943/951; 95% CI 98.4-99.6%). Clinically inadequate examinations were more frequent in patients with suspected intracranial hypertension (P<0.001).

Conclusion

Diffusion-weighted imaging- and motion-resistant radial FLAIR-based abMRI appears feasible and clinically adequate as an initial imaging approach for selected pediatric emergency neuroimaging indications. Full-protocol MRI remains preferable when intracranial hypertension is suspected.

title: Comprehensive comparison of echocardiographic and invasive hemodynamics in a real-world pulmonary hypertension cohort.
authorString: AlRahimi JS, Alotaibi A, Bagais A, Bamardouf O.
abstractText:
Background

Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) is the preferred initial modality for evaluating suspected pulmonary hypertension (PH), yet its accuracy compared with right heart catheterization (RHC) remains variable, particularly in heterogeneous populations. We assessed multiple TTE-derived hemodynamic parameters against invasive measurements in a real-world PH cohort.

Methods

We retrospectively analyzed 125 adults who underwent TTE and RHC within 72 h (2020-2023). Hemodynamic parameters included systolic, diastolic, and mean pulmonary artery pressure (sPAP, dPAP, mPAP), pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (PCWP), and pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR). Mean PAP was estimated from pulmonary regurgitation velocity and right ventricular outflow tract acceleration time (AT). We evaluated correlation, Bland-Altman agreement, diagnostic accuracy, and inter-observer reproducibility.

Results

PH prevalence by RHC was 81.6%. TTE correlated moderately with RHC for sPAP (r = 0.62), mPAP (r = 0.48-0.50), PCWP (r = 0.51), and PVR (r = 0.50). TTE systematically underestimated pulmonary pressures and PVR, and overestimated PCWP, with wide limits of agreement across all parameters. Against RHC-defined PH (mPAP > 20 mmHg), TTE showed high positive predictive values for TTE sPAP ≥ 25 mmHg (86.4%) and AT-derived mPAP ≥ 20 mmHg (94.7%), but low to modest negative predictive values (53.3% and 38.8%, respectively). Doppler PVR showed high specificity (93.3%) and positive predictive value (97.5%), but modest sensitivity (60%). Inter-observer agreement was excellent for sPAP (ICC = 0.87).

Conclusions

In a real-world, mixed-etiology PH cohort, TTE reliably identifies elevated pulmonary pressures but lacks precision for exact hemodynamic quantification. While valuable for screening, TTE cannot replace RHC for definitive diagnosis or hemodynamic classification, supporting a complementary diagnostic approach.

title: Hemodynamic burden of mitral annular calcification: improved estimation by left atrial expansion index.
authorString: Strosio M, Genovese D, Ferrara L, Mazzi L, Miotto A, Tarantini G, Corrado D, Marra MP.
abstractText:
Background

Mitral annular calcification (MAC) is associated with heart failure, yet its independent hemodynamic impact on pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (PCWP) remains incompletely defined. Moreover, accurate non-invasive estimation of PCWP in patients with moderate-to-severe MAC remains challenging.

Aim

We sought to quantify the independent association between MAC and PCWP and evaluate whether the left atrial expansion index (LAEI) improves the detection of elevated PCWP.

Methods

We conducted a single-center, retrospective study enrolling patients undergoing right heart catheterization with transthoracic echocardiography performed within 24 h. Patients were divided into the no/mild MAC and moderate-to-severe MAC groups. To assess the independent association between MAC severity on PCWP, a propensity score matching analysis was performed. In the subgroup of patients with moderate-to-severe MAC, the diagnostic performance of LAEI for the identification of elevated PCWP was compared against the current guidelines proposed algorithm.

Results

Propensity score matching yielded 70 well-balanced matched pairs (N = 140) from 1,029 eligible patients. Moderate-to-severe MAC was independently associated with higher PCWP (+ 3.6 mmHg; 95% CI: 1.5-5.7; p < 0.001) compared with no/mild MAC. In patients with moderate-to-severe MAC and sinus rhythm, the current guideline algorithm showed lower performance (sensitivity 60.0%, specificity 65.7%) than lnLAEI < 3.69 (sensitivity 74.3%, specificity 77.1%). In addition, LAEI remained applicable even in the presence of atrial fibrillation.

Conclusions

Moderate-to-severe MAC is independently associated with higher PCWP. In this population, lnLAEI improves non-invasive estimation of PCWP and may represent a valuable adjunctive echocardiographic marker for refining the assessment of hemodynamic burden and diastolic dysfunction.

title: Bent Ab Interno Needle Goniotomy combined with phacoemulsification compared with phacoemulsification alone for mild to moderate glaucoma
authorString: Cox RA, Cronin B.
abstractText: Background Bent Ab Interno Needle Goniotomy (BANG) is a low-cost goniotomy technique. Previous studies of BANG combined with phacoemulsification have treated 30 to 100 degrees of trabecular meshwork. This study compares the reduction in intraocular pressure (IOP) and topical glaucoma medications (TGMs) after phacoemulsification combined with 120 degrees of BANG, and after phacoemulsification alone. Methods A total of 80 eyes of 42 patients were included in this retrospective case-control study. Twenty-six eyes with primary open angle glaucoma, normal tension glaucoma, or ocular hypertension underwent BANG combined with phacoemulsification, and 54 non-glaucomatous control eyes underwent standard phacoemulsification surgery. Results At 12 months, the average intraocular pressure of the Phaco + BANG group remained stable (17.5 ± 5.1mmHg vs 17.8 ± 4.1mmHg, p = 0.86), while the average number of topical glaucoma medications was reduced (1.4 ± 1.2 vs 0.3 ± 0.6, p < 0.001). For the Phaco-only group, there was a modest decrease in the average intraocular pressure (14.7 ± 3.8mmHg vs 11.9 ± 2.2mmHg, p < 0.001). In the Phaco + BANG group, all eyes that were on no topical glaucoma medications, remained on no drops, and the average intraocular pressure reduced (22.8 ± 3.0mmHg vs 16.4 ± 2.0mmHg, p = 0.011). This reduction was not significantly greater than in the Phaco-only group (p = 0.11). Eyes with baseline IOP above the median (16.5mmHg) had a reduction in IOP at 12 months, while eyes below the median had an increase. At 3 months, no topical glaucoma medications were required for 76.9% of eyes (20 of 26). At 1-day, 73.5% of eyes had a small hyphaema, all of which resolved spontaneously. Conclusions In eyes with glaucoma, combining BANG with standard phacoemulsification was associated with a reduction in topical medication burden, with IOP stable over 12 months, without substantial additional cost. Future research should include a glaucomatous control group that was not available for this study.

title: Sequential integration of pre-discharge lung ultrasound and the MEESSI-AHF score for safe emergency department discharge in decompensated heart failure: a prospective multicentre cohort study
authorString: Arrese MT, Fuertes PR, Rausell PB, Dueñas RS, Laredo EE, Sánchez GGdC, Luordo D, Caiza GCM, Chen YT, Miró Ò, Llorens P.
abstractText: Background Early revisit or readmission is common after direct emergency department (ED) discharge for decompensated heart failure (DHF, previously termed acute heart failure). We evaluated whether pre-discharge lung ultrasound, quantified as the number of lung fields with B-lines (NLFB-L), improves 30-day risk stratification, alone or integrated with the Multiple Estimation of Risk based on the Emergency department Spanish Score in patients with Acute Heart Failure (MEESSI-AHF). Methods Prospective multicentre cohort study of 96 adults with DHF discharged directly from the EDs of four Spanish tertiary hospitals between November 2023 and January 2026. The primary outcome was heart failure-related ED revisit or hospital readmission within 30 days. Associations were assessed with logistic regression (two-variable models), discrimination with the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) compared by the DeLong test, and the optimal NLFB-L threshold with the Youden index. A sequential strategy stratified risk by pre-discharge congestion (NLFB-L < 5 vs ≥ 5), refined by baseline MEESSI-AHF category (low vs non-low). Results The primary outcome occurred in 26 patients (27.1%). NLFB-L was independently associated with the outcome after adjustment for natriuretic peptide levels (adjusted odds ratio 1.51 per additional lung field; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.21–1.90; p < 0.001). NLFB-L discriminated better than the MEESSI-AHF score (AUC 0.849 vs 0.670; DeLong p = 0.0037), whereas combining both did not improve discrimination (AUC 0.853; p = 0.953). The optimal threshold was NLFB-L ≥ 5 (69.2% sensitivity, 82.9% specificity, 87.9% negative predictive value). NLFB-L < 5 carried a 12.1% event rate; among patients with NLFB-L ≥ 5, event rates were 35.7% with low-risk and 81.3% with non-low-risk MEESSI-AHF (odds ratio 31.42 versus NLFB-L < 5, 95% CI 7.32–134.85; p < 0.001). Conclusions Pre-discharge NLFB-L strongly predicted 30-day heart failure-related revisit or readmission. The added value of the MEESSI-AHF score emerged with sequential integration: a non-low MEESSI-AHF category refined prognosis only in patients with persistent congestion; when both are present, direct ED discharge should be reconsidered. Trial registration: Not applicable (observational study, not registered).

title: Serial Endoscopic Variceal Band Ligation for Esophageal Varices Due to Portal Hypertension: A Prospective Observational Study from Southern Rajasthan
authorString: Falwaria S.
abstractText: Background Esophageal variceal hemorrhage is a major decompensating event in portal hypertension. Endoscopic variceal band ligation (EVBL) controls bleeding by mechanically strangulating varices while avoiding the deeper tissue injury associated with sclerosant injection. Although EVBL is established in acute hemostasis and secondary prevention, the number of sessions required for eradication and the practical pattern of short-term adverse effects may vary with disease severity, referral pathways, and follow-up adherence. This study evaluated serial EVBL in adults treated at a tertiary-care hospital in Udaipur, Rajasthan. Methods This hospital-based prospective observational study included 40 adults with portal hypertension and esophageal varices who underwent EVBL at the American International Institute of Medical Sciences between April 2023 and March 2025. Participants were assessed clinically and with routine laboratory testing and abdominal imaging when indicated. Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy was repeated at four-week intervals, with further EVBL until complete variceal obliteration. Outcomes were summarized using frequencies, proportions, and means. The principal outcomes were number of sessions to obliteration, change in endoscopic grade, recurrence at six months, and procedure-related adverse effects. Results The participants were 31 men and 9 women, aged 31–80 years. Hematemesis was the leading presenting complaint in 20 patients (50.0%), followed by melena in 10 (25.0%). Cirrhosis was the recorded cause of portal hypertension in 31 patients; the reported etiologic distribution was alcohol-associated disease in 21 (52.5% of the cohort), chronic hepatitis B in 11 (27.5%), and non-alcoholic fatty liver disease in 8 (20.0%). Twenty-six patients (64.0%) were Child–Pugh class A, 12 (30.0%) class B, and 2 (6.0%) class C. At baseline, 10 patients had grade I, 16 grade II, and 14 grade III varices. Five patients achieved obliteration by eight weeks and 35 by 12 weeks; the mean number of sessions was 2.875. At six-month endoscopy, 25 patients returned: 18 had no reappearance and 7 underwent repeat EVBL for recurrent varices. Retrosternal pain occurred in 12 patients (30.0%), fever in 4 (10.0%), and hematemesis in 2 (5.0%); no stricture was recorded. Conclusions In this single-centre cohort, serial EVBL achieved documented obliteration in two or three sessions for all patients who completed the eradication protocol, with mostly transient adverse effects. The six-month assessment was limited by loss to follow-up, and recurrence among reviewed patients supports continued surveillance. The findings support a pragmatic four-week EVBL pathway but should not be interpreted as comparative evidence of superiority over pharmacological or shunt-based strategies.

title: Cardiac amyloidosis masked by anchoring bias in a patient with repaired atrial septal defect: a case report
authorString: Jiang Y, Zhang T, Ma X.
abstractText: Background: Cardiac amyloidosis (CA) is an infiltrative cardiomyopathy that frequently mimics other cardiac conditions and is easily overlooked once a structural cardiac diagnosis has been established. We report a case of systemic lambda light-chain (AL) amyloidosis unmasked four years after surgical repair of an atrial septal defect (ASD), highlighting the diagnostic anchoring bias that delayed recognition. Case presentation: A 75-year-old woman presented with refractory heart failure four years after surgical repair of an ASD. Her progressively worsening symptoms had been attributed solely to the pre-existing structural heart disease. On readmission, transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated biatrial enlargement, severe mitral and tricuspid regurgitation, biventricular wall thickening with a granular sparkling appearance, and a small pericardial effusion. Three-dimensional speckle-tracking echocardiography revealed profoundly reduced left ventricular global longitudinal strain (GLS, -6.0%) with relative apical sparing, and reduced right ventricular free-wall longitudinal strain (-8.1%). Electrocardiography showed atrial fibrillation, intraventricular conduction delay, and poor precordial R-wave progression. Serum immunofixation electrophoresis detected a lambda-type monoclonal protein, with a markedly elevated free lambda light chain and a decreased kappa/lambda ratio. Abdominal fat pad biopsy showed Congo red-positive amyloid deposits, and electron microscopy revealed rigid, non-branching amyloid fibrils measuring 8-12 nm in diameter, confirming systemic AL amyloidosis. According to the revised Mayo 2012 staging system (NT-proBNP 29,218 pg/mL), she was classified as stage III. The patient declined bone marrow biopsy and clone-directed chemotherapy and was transferred to another hospital for further management. Conclusions: Once a structural cardiac diagnosis is established, clinicians are prone to anchoring bias and may overlook coexisting infiltrative disease. In patients with refractory or progressive heart failure after correction of structural heart disease, systematic reassessment-including strain echocardiography, monoclonal protein screening, and tissue biopsy-should be pursued to unmask CA and enable timely, potentially life-prolonging therapy.

title: Dysregulated Cytosolic Redox Homeostasis in Patient-Derived Takotsubo Syndrome Cardiomyocytes
authorString: Priya VV, Maurer W, Seedorf AA, Cárdenas-Arciniegas JC, Hillemann A, Streckfuss-Bömeke K, Katschinski DM.
abstractText: Takotsubo syndrome (TTS) is an acute stress-associated heart failure syndrome in which catecholamine excess is thought to interact with an intrinsic myocardial vulnerability. Oxidative stress has been implicated in its pathophysiology, but the underlying redox alterations in patient-derived cardiomyocytes remain poorly defined. We therefore investigated basal redox and metabolic homeostasis in induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes from two TTS patients and two control lines. Cytosolic and mitochondrial H₂O₂-sensitive HyPer7 signals, glutathione redox potential ( E GSH ), total NADP/NADPH abundance, ATP content, and 4-hydroxynonenal were assessed under unstimulated conditions. Basal HyPer7 ratios were not consistently altered in the TTS lines. In contrast, cytosolic E GSH was altered in both TTS lines, although in opposite directions. TTS5 showed more reducing E GSH , along with reduced ATP and increased lipid peroxidation, whereas TTS8 showed more oxidized E GSH with largely preserved metabolic and lipid-peroxidation parameters. These findings indicate that TTS cardiomyocytes exhibit intrinsic but heterogeneous disturbances in cytosolic redox conditions. Patient-specific differences in how redox balance, metabolism, and oxidative damage interact may contribute to individual susceptibility to stress-induced myocardial dysfunction. These findings identify disturbed coordination of cytosolic redox homeostasis and cellular metabolism as an intrinsic feature of patient-derived TTS cardiomyocytes that may contribute to susceptibility to acute stress-induced myocardial dysfunction.

title: Maternal and Fetal Risk Factors for Congenital Abnormalities of the Kidney and Urinary Tract: A Hospital-based Case-control Study in Southern China
authorString: Bu W, Li X, Hu S, Chen S, Wan Z, Zhao Z.
abstractText: Background The aetiology of congenital abnormalities of the kidney and urinary tract (CAKUT) remains incompletely understood, despite several risk factors having been reported in previous literature. Maternal and fetal‑related clinical characteristics are hypothesised to contribute to CAKUT susceptibility, yet epidemiological evidence remains inconsistent. This study aimed to evaluate maternal and fetal risk factors for CAKUT among infants in southern China to improve understanding of this common congenital malformation. Methods A retrospective hospital‑based case‑control study was performed at a tertiary women‑and‑children hospital in Hainan, China, from January 2021 to October 2025. Newborns diagnosed with CAKUT served as cases, and newborns without CAKUT were selected as controls adopting a 1:5 individual‑matching design based on neonatal sex and date of birth (± 3 days). In total, 109 CAKUT cases and 545 matched controls were included. Maternal demographic and clinical information were obtained via telephone interviews and routine survey data; clinical perinatal information was validated against hospital medical records. We compared maternal and fetal characteristics between offspring with and without CAKUT. Multivariable conditional logistic regression was applied to identify independent risk factors for CAKUT. Results After adjusting for confounding variables, advanced maternal age (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 2.58, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.33‑5.01), gestational hypertension (aOR = 3.48, 95%CI 1.32‑9.23), maternal hypothyroidism (aOR = 9.84, 95%CI 1.70‑56.99), multiple pregnancies (aOR = 7.68, 95%CI 1.07‑54.85), and preterm gestational age (aOR = 4.65, 95%CI 1.78‑12.75) were independently associated with elevated CAKUT risk. Hydronephrosis was the most frequent CAKUT subtype observed in this cohort. Conclusions Advanced maternal age, gestational hypertension, hypothyroidism, multiple pregnancies, and preterm gestation were associated with increased CAKUT risk in this hospital‑based sample. These findings may support early identification of high‑risk pregnancies and provide evidence for clinical prevention and management of CAKUT in Hainan.

title: Retrobulbar hemodynamic characteristics of glaucoma suspects assessed by color Doppler imaging
authorString: Bernales S, Becerra C, Bustamante-Vargas A, Mayorquín-Ruiz M, Arriaga-Perez A, García-Vásquez R, Diaz-Gonzalez S, Galvez-Olortegui J.
abstractText: Background/Aims To evaluate retrobulbar haemodynamic parameters in glaucoma suspects using colour Doppler imaging (CDI) and other eye characteristics such as intraocular pressure (IOP), structural optic nerve parameters and ocular perfusion pressure (OPP). Methods A descriptive cross-sectional, single-centre study was conducted among glaucoma suspects. Doppler ultrasound was used to assess haemodynamic parameters such as peak systolic velocity (PSV), end-diastolic velocity (EDV), and resistance index (RI) in the ophthalmic artery (OA), central retinal artery (CRA), and nasal and temporal short posterior ciliary arteries (nSPCA and tSPCA). IOP, systemic blood pressure (BP), OPP, and optical coherence tomography (OCT) parameters were recorded. A secondary analysis was performed to compare retrobulbar haemodynamic parameters between glaucoma suspects with and without DM2. Results A total of 134 eyes from 73 patients were included. The mean age was 59.5 years, and the majority of participants were female (65.7%). The prevalence of type 2 diabetes mellitus and systemic hypertension was 27.3% and 24.7%, respectively. Mean PSV, EDV and RI where 38.54 ± 11.16, 8.72 ± 2.88 and 0.77 ± 0.06 for OA; 13.86 ± 3.50, 4.70 ± 1.30 and 0.66 ± 0.06 for CRA; 11.29 ± 3.50, 4.69 ± 1.23 and 0.57 ± 0.07 for nSPCA; and 11.71 ± 3.36, 4.79 ± 1.17 and 0.58 ± 0.07 for tSPCA. Eyes of patients with DM2 exhibited decreased velocities and increased RI when compared to eyes of the non-DM2 patients. Conclusion This study characterized PSV, EDV, and RI values in the retrobulbar circulation of a glaucoma suspect cohort, providing hemodynamic information in a population for which such data were previously unavailable. PRECIS Colour Doppler imaging successfully characterized retrobulbar blood flow velocities and resistance indices in glaucoma suspects. Furthermore, participants with type 2 diabetes exhibited significantly decreased vascular velocities and increased resistance compared to non-diabetic individuals.

title: Multiverse analysis suggests that aneurysm location and admission condition modify the comparative effectiveness of clipping and coiling for ruptured aneurysms
authorString: Kim JH, Heo J, Moon E, Jung M, Kim D, Kim H, Park D.
abstractText: Whether a ruptured intracranial aneurysm is treated by microsurgical clipping or endovascular coiling is often decided by operator preference, and evidence from East Asian populations is limited. Because observational comparisons depend on many analytical choices, we applied a multiverse framework to a nationwide Korean registry of aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage. Of 2,539 patients from 25 tertiary centers (2015–2017), 746 with anterior circulation aneurysms treated by a single modality were analyzed. We generated 8,964 analytical specifications combining missing-data strategies, propensity-score models and balancing methods, and summarized the 108 specifications that achieved covariate balance. Admission neurological severity and age were the most consistent predictors of unfavorable 1-year functional outcome. Coiling was directionally favored in 105 of 108 specifications (97.2%), but no specification showed a statistically significant overall difference. Interaction analyses suggested heterogeneity: clipping was favored for middle cerebral artery aneurysms, whereas coiling was favored for anterior cerebral and posterior communicating artery aneurysms and for patients with severely impaired consciousness or hypertension. These findings argue against a universal default and support individualized, data-driven selection of treatment modality.

title: Infliximab for refractory non-infectious uveitis: 10-year safety and steroid-sparing outcomes from an ophthalmology-led service
authorString: Braithwaite T, Langley L, Ramsewak S, Jackson D, Sinha A, Kaur K, Riga V, Addison P, Pavesio C, Galloway J, D’Cruz D, Virgo J.
abstractText: Background: To describe the real-world safety, steroid-sparing effect, treatment duration, infusion interval, and operational features of a medical ophthalmology-led biologic service managing non-infectious uveitis(NIU) patients with infliximab(IFX).  Methods: Retrospective cohort review of patients receiving IFX for NIU at a tertiary NHS centre from March 2016 to March 2026. Primary outcomes were adverse events(AEs), serious adverse events(SAEs) and discontinuations; secondary outcomes were oral corticosteroid requirement and visual acuity. Results: 44 patients contributed 1208 months of IFX exposure (100.7 patient-years), with a median of 21.5 months(IQR 9.5–32.0). 37/44 (84%) had previously received adalimumab. AEs were reported by 20/44 (45%), including infections in 10/44 (23%) and rash in 9/44 (20%). SAEs occurred in 2/44 (5%): incident heart failure and anaphylaxis, each in 1/44 (2%). AEs led to discontinuation in 8/44 (18%). By 12 months, 10/44 (23%) had stopped IFX, most commonly due to ineffectiveness. Worse eye visual acuity changed by <15 ETDRS letters from baseline in 29/33 (88%), improved by ≥15 letters in 3/33 (9%), and worsened by ≥15 in 1/33 (3%). Among those using prednisolone at baseline, the median daily dose fell from 15 mg to 5.5 mg by month 12; at latest review (median 27 months) the median was 4.0 mg/day, with 18/21 (86%) taking ≤5 mg/day and 5/21 (24%) steroid-free. Conclusions: IFX was generally well tolerated and was associated with lower corticosteroid requirements in NIU. A medical ophthalmology-led biologic infusion service is feasible and safe but close collaboration with other medical specialties is critical for safe governance and delivery.

title: Pulmonary Artery Dissection in Unrepaired Patent Ductus Arteriosus: Hemodynamic-Guided Ductal Closure.
authorString: Rodríguez Barajas DA, Villarraga Márquez NJ, Castañeda HA, Ortega DA, Calderón CH, García ÁA, Cáceres E, Trujillo PS, Ríos EG.
abstractText:
Background

Pulmonary artery (PA) dissection is a rare and potentially fatal complication, usually associated with severe pulmonary hypertension, PA aneurysms, or congenital heart disease. Evidence regarding management remains limited.

Case summary

A 30-year-old man with unrepaired patent ductus arteriosus presented with acute chest pain and was diagnosed with PA dissection, giant PA aneurysm, severe pulmonary regurgitation, and pulmonary hypertension. He underwent urgent surgical repair, pulmonary valve replacement, and PA reconstruction. Given uncertain operability, transient intraoperative ductal reopening produced acute hemodynamic deterioration and right ventricular dysfunction, whereas occlusion improved pulmonary hemodynamics, supporting definitive closure.

Discussion

PA dissection associated with patent ductus arteriosus is exceptionally uncommon and presents complex management challenges. This case illustrates the value of intraoperative hemodynamic assessment when conventional operability evaluation is not feasible.

Take-home message

Intraoperative hemodynamic testing may help guide ductal closure in selected high-risk patients with uncertain operability.

title: The Role and Molecular Mechanism of E4BP4 in Pathological Cardiac Hypertrophy via Targeting TRAIL.
authorString: Su YC, Huang DR, Hu H, Wen Q.

journal.title: The Kaohsiung journal of medical sciences

abstractText: Pathological cardiac hypertrophy (PCH) leads to heart failure. Tumor necrosis factor-related apoptosis-inducing ligand (TRAIL), a multifunctional cytokine, affects cardiovascular diseases. E4-binding protein 4 (E4BP4), implicated in cardiac stress, reportedly suppresses TRAIL. However, their role in PCH remains unclear. This study aims to investigate the role of E4BP4 in PCH and its underlying mechanism. Transverse aortic constriction (TAC) was used to induce PCH in mice. Echocardiography assessed cardiac function at 4, 6, 8, and 12 weeks post-surgery. Masson staining, immunofluorescence, qRT-PCR, and western blot were used to evaluate myocardial hypertrophy, fibrosis, and expression of E4BP4, TRAIL, and related receptors. Angiotensin II (Ang II)-induced hypertrophy was established in primary mouse cardiomyocytes. Cells were transfected with E4BP4 silencing or overexpression vectors. qRT-PCR, western blot, ELISA, phalloidin staining, and luciferase reporter assays measured E4BP4, TRAIL, receptors, hypertrophy/apoptosis markers, cell size, and E4BP4-TRAIL promoter binding. In hypertrophic mice, left ventricular ejection fraction and fractional shortening decreased, while left ventricular end-systolic diameter and mass increased, accompanied by aggravated myocardial fibrosis and abnormal hypertrophy markers. Ang II-induced cardiomyocytes showed increased cell area and abnormal expression of E4BP4, TRAIL, hypertrophy markers, and apoptosis-related proteins. Silencing E4BP4 exacerbated these changes, whereas overexpression reversed them. Luciferase assay confirmed that E4BP4 directly inhibited TRAIL promoter activity. In conclusion, E4BP4 mitigates hypertrophy and apoptosis by inhibiting TRAIL promoter activity and regulating TRAIL and its receptors, offering a potential therapeutic target for PCH.

title: Enhanced antihypertensive efficacy of selenium-enriched black tea is associated with galloylated catechin enrichment: integrating chemical profiling, molecular modeling, and animal studies.
authorString: Shi H, Shi J, Wu M, Wang Y.

journal.title: Journal of the science of food and agriculture

abstractText:
Background

Selenium-enriched tea has been reported to exhibit enhanced antihypertensive efficacy; however, the key bioactive constituents and their molecular targets remain undefined. To elucidate the relationship between selenium-induced compositional alterations and antihypertensive effects, we employed a high-salt diet-induced hypertensive rat model combined with chemical profiling, network pharmacology, and molecular dynamics simulations.

Results

Selenium biofortification of the tea plant increased the contents of galloylated catechins (epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG) and epicatechin gallate (ECG)) in the resulting black tea. In hypertensive rats, selenium-enriched black tea (Se-BT) exhibited superior antioxidative, anti-inflammatory, and antihypertensive effects compared with conventional black tea (BT), increasing serum endothelial nitric oxide synthase (eNOS) activity and nitric oxide (NO) levels (+39.32% and +12.20%, respectively, compared with BT). Network pharmacology identified galloylated catechins (EGCG, ECG, and gallocatechin gallate (GCG)) as major bioactive constituents associated with hypertension, and KEGG (Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes) enrichment pointed to pathways converging on eNOS-mediated NO signaling. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations suggested that galloylated catechins preferentially occupy a common binding pocket adjacent to the eNOS BH4-binding region and that EGCG, as the representative galloylated catechin, maintained a stable binding mode throughout the simulation.

Conclusion

Selenium enrichment enhances the antihypertensive efficacy of black tea, primarily through the accumulation of galloylated catechins. These findings suggest that the stable binding of galloylated catechins to eNOS may provide a structural basis for the experimentally observed enhancement of eNOS activity and NO production. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

title: Electroconvulsive Therapy in a Patient with Schizophrenia and Coexisting Right Frontoparietal Neoplastic Lesion: A Case Report with Literature Review.
authorString: Tennety V, Patil S.
abstractText:
Abstract

Co-occurrence of primary brain tumors and schizophrenia presents diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) has historically been considered contraindicated in patients with intracranial lesions. A 27-year-old female with an 11-year history of schizophrenia presented with worsening psychosis, irritability, and aggression. She was previously diagnosed with diffuse midline glioma, which was inoperable and treated with temozolomide. Due to partial response to amisulpride, she received four sessions of modified ECT (mECT) following a multidisciplinary evaluation ruling out intracranial hypertension. The treatment was well-tolerated with rapid reduction in psychotic symptoms, agitation, and aggression, without neurological deterioration or seizure-related complications. Thus, this case demonstrates that mECT can be safely administered in select patients with schizophrenia and co-occurring high-grade glioma, challenging historical contraindications. Early neuroimaging is essential in treatment-resistant or atypical psychosis to exclude underlying structural pathology.

title: Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction in Low-Income Settings: Performance and Challenges of Screening Scores in a Population-Based Cohort in Haiti.
authorString: Yan LD, Sauveur RS, Celestin K, Macajou KJW, Ogyu A, Rouzier V, Apollon A, Marx D, Bennett C, Alexandre W, Malebranche R, Théard M, Brisma JP, Ward M, Dupnik K, Kwan GF, Deschamps MM, Pape JW, Dávila-Román VG, McNairy ML.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is rapidly increasing in low- and middle-income countries, however detection remains challenging. We assessed 2 screening scores developed in high-income settings, H2FPEF and HFA-PEFF, against physician-adjudicated HFpEF in a population-based cohort from Haiti.

Methods

The primary outcome was prevalent HFpEF defined by (1) physician adjudication, (2) H2FpEF score, (3) HFA-PEFF score. The cross-sectional cohort comprised 3003 adults from the Haiti Cardiovascular Disease Cohort, with sociodemographic, clinical, electrocardiography, echocardiography and BNP data available. We compared physician-adjudicated HFpEF participants to those screening positive (intermediate-high H2FPEF and HFA-PEFF scores) using interrater reliability (Cohen's kappa, Krippendorff's alpha). Diagnostic performance of H2FPEF and HFA-PEFF against physician adjudication, used as a pragmatic reference standard appropriate for Haiti and similar settings, was calculated via sensitivity, specificity, and predictive values.

Results

Age-adjusted HFpEF prevalence was 9.5% (95% CI: 8.3-11.0) by physician adjudication, 10.2% (95% CI: 9.0-11.7) by H2FPEF, and 8.6% (95% CI: 7.5-10.0) by HFA-PEFF. Adjudicated HFpEF participants were young (median age 57), had high prevalence of hypertension (70%), obesity (33%), and no atrial fibrillation. Agreement between all 3 scores was moderate-substantial (alpha 0.57, 95% CI: 0.55-0.59), with the highest pair-wise agreement between physician adjudication and HFA-PEFF (kappa 0.62, 95% CI: 0.57-0.67). HFA-PEFF had higher sensitivity and similar specificity relative to H2FPEF.

Conclusions

In this Haitian cohort, prevalent HFpEF occurred in relatively young participants with high hypertension and obesity rates and negligible atrial fibrillation. HFA-PEFF exhibited higher concordance and sensitivity than H2FPEF versus physician adjudication. Tailored, non-invasive HFpEF screening scores for low- and middle-income countries are needed to address this growing global epidemic.

title: 2025 Harriet Dustan Lecture: Sex Differences in Immune-Mediated Hypertension: Why Menopause Matters.
authorString: Brooks HL, Sylvester MA, Michea L.
abstractText: Hypertension is an inflammatory disease with the immune system playing a key role in mediating hypertensive outcomes and end-organ damage. The risk of hypertension is greater in men than in women before women enter menopause. After menopause, a woman's risk for developing hypertension increases and accelerates beyond that of age-matched men. Moreover, after menopause, the rate of hypertension control in women is lower than in men. Indeed, cardiovascular drug efficacy in women is different from that in men, with recent studies highlighting serious side effects of angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors and β-blockers in postmenopausal women. Despite these sex differences, sex-specific clinical practice guidelines are still sparse, as is the consideration of a woman's hormonal status. In addition, preclinical models of immune-mediated hypertension are still mainly performed in male animals. The goal of this review is to highlight recent advancements in the field of sex differences in immune-mediated hypertension and to identify the major gaps in understanding immune mechanisms that lead to hypertension development in males and females, and as menopause progresses.

title: Biological Aging Associates With Preeclampsia and Gestational Hypertension.
authorString: Li X, Mo Y, Lin Y, Tang S, He J, Pan XF, Zhao H, Zhu C, Zhao J.
abstractText:
Background

Biological aging is a fundamental driver of chronic disease, yet its role in the cause of preeclampsia and gestational hypertension remains poorly defined.
