Methods

We used a multimodal framework that triangulated genetic, epidemiological, and experimental approaches to assess the associations of biological aging with preeclampsia and gestational hypertension. Publicly available human and mouse transcriptomic data were analyzed to identify shared aging- and preeclampsia-associated signatures, while the potential of nicotinic acid to alleviate aging- and preeclampsia-related features was further evaluated in experimental models.

Results

Two-sample Mendelian randomization demonstrated that biological age acceleration was associated with higher odds of preeclampsia (odds ratio, 1.55 [95% CI, 1.22-1.96]; P=2.67×10-4) and gestational hypertension (odds ratio, 1.56 [95% CI, 1.12-2.19]; P=0.009), while positive genetic correlations were also observed for both outcomes. In the nested case-control study, higher early pregnancy biological age acceleration was consistently associated with preeclampsia risk in both primary (odds ratio, 1.16 [95% CI, 1.01-1.35]; P=0.047) and sensitivity (odds ratio, 1.14 [95% CI, 1.03-1.29]; P=0.042) analyses, with the associations persisting after covariate adjustment and exclusion of systolic blood pressure from biological age acceleration calculation. Mouse models exhibited preeclampsia-like features accompanied by concordant alterations in biological age-related biomarkers and telomere dysfunction. These changes were partially attenuated by nicotinic acid treatment, whereas placental organoids showed limited growth responses to nicotinic acid. Complementing these phenotypic observations, transcriptomic analyses identified shared aging- and preeclampsia-associated signatures across human and mouse data sets.

Conclusions

Convergent evidence links biological aging with preeclampsia and gestational hypertension, particularly biological age acceleration with preeclampsia. Experimental findings provide complementary context but do not establish a specific mechanism or therapeutic role for nicotinic acid.

title: Shifting the Pressure-Natriuresis Curve: The Cellular Mechanisms of Female Renal Resilience.
authorString: Layton A, Edwards A, McDonough AA.
abstractText: Female and male kidneys exhibit markedly different patterns of transporter abundance and activity along the nephron, yet the physiological significance of the differences remains incompletely understood. Recent experimental and computational studies suggest that many of these differences can be interpreted through the lens of pressure natriuresis, the kidney's primary mechanism for long-term regulation of extracellular volume and arterial pressure. We review evidence that the female nephron exhibits a transport architecture that may facilitate enhanced pressure natriuresis and greater flexibility in effective circulating volume regulation. This framework provides new insights into sex differences in acute and chronic blood pressure control and connects pressure-natriuretic mechanisms with renal adaptations during pregnancy and lactation, hypertension, and aging.

title: Myocardial Hmgcs2-Driven Ketogenesis Promotes Atrial Fibrillation in Diabetes.
authorString: Wang L, Tan R, Sun Y, Xu G, Su Q, Yang X, Shehata M, Yin X, Cingolani E, Liu Y.
abstractText:
Background

Type 2 diabetes (T2DM) increases the risk of atrial fibrillation (AF). Elevated circulating ketone bodies (β-hydroxybutyrate [β-OHB]) in T2DM are considered hepatic in origin and benefit the heart via energy provision. Although we found ketogenesis enzyme Hmgcs2 (3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA synthase 2) upregulated in both atrial and ventricular tissues of T2DM mice, alongside increased cardiac and circulating β-OHB. Whether enhanced Hmgcs2 is related to AF, ketogenesis-dependent or independent, remained unclear.

Methods

T2DM mice were induced by high-fat diet and followed by streptozocin injection. Cardiac-specific Hmgcs2 overexpression and cardiomyocyte-specific Hmgcs2 knockout were conducted in T2DM mice. Cardiac function and left atrial diameter were evaluated using echocardiography, and cardiac electrophysiology was examined through electrical mapping. Programmed electrical stimulation was delivered to induce AF. Blood metabolomics from the coronary sinus and left atria of patients with or without T2DM were analyzed.

Results

The heart functioned as a primary ketogenic organ in T2DM mice via upregulating Hmgcs2, surpassing the liver. Hmgcs2-mediated shunting of fatty acid-derived acetyl-CoA into ketogenesis depleted myocardial energy reserves, exacerbated oxidative stress, and caused mitochondrial injury, ultimately increasing AF inducibility and diastolic dysfunction. In addition, cardiac-derived β-hydroxybutyrate released into circulation prolonged action potential duration in atrial cardiomyocytes. Mechanistically, Hmgcs2-mediated cytosolic β-hydroxybutyrylation targeted Oxct1 (3-oxoacid CoA-transferase 1) for degradation, blocking cardiac ketolysis. Blood metabolomics from the coronary sinus and left atria confirmed active cardiac ketogenesis in patients with T2DM and heart-derived ketone release into systemic circulation. Venous plasma β-OHB levels positively correlated with atrial low-voltage burden and postablation AF recurrence. Cardiomyocyte-specific Hmgcs2 knockdown improved cardiac utilization of fatty acids, β-OHB, and glucose in T2DM mice by suppressing cardiac ketogenesis; this intervention, with reduced circulating β-OHB, attenuated diabetes-associated AF.

Conclusions

Cardiac Hmgcs2 represented a novel therapeutic target for diabetic AF and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.

title: Clinical Perspectives on Heart-Kidney-Brain Crosstalk.
authorString: Steinbach EJ, Crile MA, Jalal DI, Harshman LA.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol
journal.title: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
journal.isoabbreviation: Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol

abstractText: Cardiovascular, kidney, and neurological diseases are highly prevalent and frequently co-occur, reflecting an integrated heart-kidney-brain axis linked by shared hemodynamic, neurohormonal, and inflammatory pathways. This crosstalk maintains perfusion, blood volume, and metabolic homeostasis through coordinate signaling via the circulation, autonomic nervous system, and renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system. When dysregulated, these same pathways perpetuate injury across organs, transforming adaptive responses into maladaptive cycles of dysfunction.This review synthesizes current understanding of the physiology and molecular mechanisms underlying heart-kidney-brain interactions, emphasizing hypoperfusion, neurohormonal activation, and convergent pathways of oxidative stress and inflammation as central drivers. Key amplifiers, including iron dysregulation, uremic toxin accumulation, and disordered mineral metabolism, extend injury systemically, contributing to cardiac remodeling, kidney disease, progression, and neurological disease. Clinically, this axis manifests as interconnected syndromes such as cardiorenal syndrome, cerebrovascular disease, and cognitive impairment. Emerging biomarkers and imaging modalities reveal overlapping signals across organs yet are rarely integrated in practice. Notably, neurological outcomes remain underrepresented in cardiovascular and kidney research despite their profound impact on quality of life, particularly in the pediatric population where disease affects lifelong development. We highlight gaps in mutli-organ diagnostic frameworks, biomarker standardization, and translational models, and propose future research directions in the heart-kidney-brain axis. Recognizing the heart, kidney, and brain as a unified system is essential to improving risk stratification, preventing multi-organ injury, and advancing patient-centered care.

title: Photoacoustic imaging assessment of acute kidney injury associated with experimental necrotizing enterocolitis.
authorString: Guglani A, Singh A, Mootz C, Ellison MA, Cruz-Diaz N, Garg PM, Weis JA, Weis VG.

journal.title: American journal of physiology. Renal physiology

abstractText: Background: Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is a devastating gastrointestinal condition increasingly recognized to cause systemic complications, including acute kidney injury (AKI). However, the underlying mechanisms and variations in renal impairment remain largely unknown, and there is a lack of non-invasive imaging methods for detecting early kidney injury. Methods: We evaluated kidney injury through a multimodal approach, using a neonatal rat model of experimental NEC. Plasma and renal tissue were analyzed for pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β) by ELISA. Histological analysis and immunofluorescence staining were used to identify renal abnormalities and expressions of KIM-1 and NGAL. Photoacoustic imaging (PAI) was used to assess renal oxygenation and total hemoglobin as functional imaging biomarkers of kidney injury. Results: NEC pups showed significant elevations of systemic and renal cytokines, as well as increased expression of KIM-1, NGAL and CD31 in proximal tubules of the kidney. Histological examination further confirms renal injury in the NEC cohort. PAI demonstrated reduction in renal oxygen saturation, offering non-invasive assessment of physiological kidney damage. Conclusion: This study characterizes AKI associated with NEC as an inflammatory and hypoxic response in the neonatal rat NEC model and introduces PAI as a promising imaging modality for non-invasive evaluation of renal injury in NEC.

title: The Mylk3 variant associated with loss of full-length MLCK3 is widespread in C57BL/6N and related NIH-derived mouse substrains.
authorString: Göktaş SŞ, Mekada K, Dalla Costa AP, Velasco RQS, Duarte JMN, Castilho RF, Meissner A, Francisco A.
abstractText: Genetic variation among C57BL/6 mouse strains may influence cardiovascular phenotypes and contribute to inter-study variability in biomedical research. We investigated the distribution of the Mylk3 c.-5T>A variant, previously shown to cause loss of cardiac myosin light-chain kinase (MLCK3) and late-onset dilated cardiomyopathy, across C57BL/6 lineages. The variant was homozygously present in C57BL/6N and C57BL/6By strains but absent from C57BL/6J-derived mouse strains. This distribution indicates that the variant was established before divergence of the C57BL/6By branch, although its precise origin cannot be determined from contemporary samples. Despite preserved Mylk3 transcript abundance, C57BL/6N hearts lacked full-length MLCK3 protein. These findings exemplify how genetic differences between seemingly identical wild-type backgrounds can introduce significant confounding factors, highlighting the importance of accurate substrain identification and reporting for experimental design, interpretation, and reproducibility. Highlighting the broader relevance of these findings, a survey of 1238 recent open-access articles from cardiovascular journals found that 35% reported the use of C57BL/6 mice without specifying the N or J substrain. Altogether, our findings identify the Mylk3 variant as a lineage-defining feature of C57BL/6N mice and related substrains, with potential implications for cardiovascular studies using this background.

title: Associations of 6PPD-quinone exposure with macrophage-related LYN, SOCS3, and TIMP2 signatures in cardiometabolic multimorbidity.
authorString: Zhu Y, Zhang W, Wang X, Zhang C, Yang G, Li A.
abstractText: N-(1,3-Dimethylbutyl)-N'-phenyl-p-phenylenediamine quinone (6PPDQ) is a widespread tire-derived contaminant linked to cardiotoxicity and metabolic dysfunction, but its role in cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) remains unclear. Using chronic kidney disease, type 2 diabetes, and ischemic heart disease as surrogate models, we combined network toxicology, multi-omics, machine learning, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to identify candidate common molecular drivers of 6PPDQ toxicity and CMM pathogenesis. LYN, SOCS3, and TIMP2 were consistently dysregulated across the three disorders. Docking and MD simulations indicated plausible 6PPDQ binding and relative conformational stability to all three proteins, without confirming actual binding or quantitative affinity ranking. Single-cell RNA-seq of diabetic cardiomyopathy (DCM) and diabetic nephropathy (DN) showed predominant enrichment of these targets in macrophages, while CellChat predicted disease-associated communication patterns (macrophage-fibroblast in DCM; macrophage-endothelial in DN). Dose-response screening identified 20 ng/mL-an estimated high-exposure dose under heavy pollution-as the peak-effect concentration for target-gene modulation and M1-marker (iNOS, CD80) induction; it was used thereafter, although extrapolation to typical exposure warrants caution. At this concentration, 6PPDQ induced RAW264.7 morphological remodeling, intracellular ROS accumulation, and M1-like polarization, characterized by upregulation of iNOS, CD80, LYN, and SOCS3, repression of TIMP2, and elevated proinflammatory cytokines (IL-6, TNF-α, IL-1β). These findings associate 6PPDQ-induced macrophage inflammation and ECM-related changes with coordinated LYN/SOCS3/TIMP2 dysregulation, providing a framework linking 6PPDQ exposure to CMM-related inflammatory-fibrotic signatures.

title: Objectively-Measured vs Self-Reported Physical Activity and Coronary Artery Calcification in Older Adults: The ARIC Study.
authorString: Sun D, Etzkorn LH, Mok Y, Zhang C, Cui E, Norby FL, Tang W, Pankow JS, Ballantyne CM, Schrack JA, Blaha MJ, Matsushita K, Chen LY.
abstractText:
Background

Coronary artery calcification (CAC) is a marker of subclinical coronary atherosclerosis and tool for cardiovascular risk assessment. Despite established cardiovascular benefits of physical activity, its relationship with CAC remains unclear.

Objectives

The objectives of the study was to evaluate the cross-sectional association of objectively-measured and self-reported physical activity with Agatston CAC scores.

Methods

We analyzed data from 1,429 older adults in the ARIC (Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities) study. Objective physical activity was measured using an accelerometer embedded in the Zio XT ECG patch monitor. Self-reported activity in the past year was assessed via the modified Baecke Questionnaire. CAC was derived from noncontrast cardiac-gated computed tomography.

Results

The median age was 78 years; 61% of participants were females, and 23% were Black. The Spearman correlation coefficient between objectively measured and self-reported average daily hours of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) was 0.40. We observed a significant J-shaped association between objectively measured MVPA and CAC. The estimated mean Agatston score was highest at 197 (at 0 hours/day of MVPA) and reached its nadir of 94 at 0.74 hours/day of MVPA. Beyond 0.74 hours/day of MVPA, the estimated mean Agatston score showed a slight upward trend. In contrast, there was no significant association between self-reported MVPA and CAC.

Conclusions

In older adults, objectively-measured physical activity demonstrated a J-shaped relationship with CAC, with the lowest Agatston score observed at approximately 45 minutes of MVPA daily. Self-reported activity inadequately captures this association, highlighting the importance of objective physical activity assessment in cardiovascular risk evaluation.

title: Beyond metabolites: A wearable biointerface integrating antibody and aptamer probes for the real-time tracking of proteins in vivo.
authorString: Zheng H, Shafique F, Qian AS, Garg M, Gessler F, L'Heureux Hache J, Quach QM, Trigatti BL, Poudineh M, Soleymani L.
abstractText: Continuous monitoring of protein biomarkers could transform the management of acute and chronic diseases. Despite tremendous potential, wearable health monitors have remained largely limited to metabolites and small molecules. A key challenge is the limited availability of biointerfaces that reversibly track low-abundance proteins in vivo without user intervention. Here, we present the Differential Aptalyzer, a minimally invasive hydrogel microneedle platform for continuous monitoring of proteins in skin interstitial fluid. The platform combines high-affinity antibodies for selective target capture with aptamers for reversible electrochemical signal transduction. When integrated into a differential electrochemical chip and pulse-assisted sensor regeneration, this approach enables continuous monitoring of proteins in a wearable format. Using cardiac troponin I (cTnI) as a clinically relevant model analyte, Differential Aptalyzer offers a broad dynamic range (0.003 to 0.640 nanograms per milliliter) and strong specificity against interfering proteins. This platform reliably tracks both rising and falling exogenous cTnI levels injected into healthy mice, as well as endogenously elevated cTnI in a double-knockout mouse model of coronary artery disease, demonstrating its capability in continuous protein monitoring and identifying coronary artery disease cohorts.

title: Smartphone-Based Cuffless Blood Pressure Estimation Using a Multiple Regression Model: Revalidation and On-Demand Performance Under Real-World Conditions.
authorString: Yamakoshi T, Rolfe P, Yamakoshi KI.
abstractText:
Purpose

Consistent blood pressure (BP) management is crucial for cardiovascular health; yet conventional cuff-based methods remain cumbersome for frequent use. Although cuffless BP technologies are advancing, further validation in daily life is still required. Building on our preliminary work, this study aims to revalidate and further develop a practical, sustainable smartphone-based BP estimation method using multiple regression model (MRM) and assess on-demand performance under real-world conditions.

Methods

Calibration models were constructed using 101 datasets from 13 healthy participants. Target variables were brachial cuff-based systolic and diastolic BP (SBPc/DBPc). Predictor variables reflecting BP regulation were pulse rate index (PRI: ln(PR)) and peripheral vascular resistance index (VRI: |ln(mNPV)|; mNPV: modified normalized pulse volume), derived from smartphone-based fingertip green-light photoplethysmography. Model performance was evaluated by independent validation in additional participants (n = 11) under normal living conditions by comparing estimated BP (SBPe/DBPe) with concurrent cuff-based measurements.

Results

Over 1-2 weeks, 168 datasets (13-21 per participant) were collected. Mean absolute errors (MAEs) were 3.2 ± 2.59 mmHg for SBP and 4.7 ± 2.78 mmHg for DBP. A longitudinal case study over 20 months in one participant (752 datasets) demonstrated lower MAEs: 1.6 ± 1.16 mmHg for SBP and 2.4 ± 1.71 mmHg for DBP.

Conclusion

The proposed MRM-based method demonstrates practical BP estimation accuracy in daily life. Although further calibration studies are warranted, its long-term stability and smartphone compatibility offer notable advantages for routine BP monitoring. This approach represents a promising, convenient cuffless alternative for integration into mobile healthcare platforms and daily BP management.

title: Immunosenescence in Metabolic Disorders: From Cellular Mechanisms to Therapeutic Strategies.
authorString: Guo D, Chen Q, Cai H, Lu Y.
abstractText:
Purpose of review

This review comprehensively examines the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying the crosstalk between metabolic disorders and immunosenescence and elucidates the fundamental roles of clonal hematopoiesis (CH) and immune surveillance while critically evaluating both classical and emerging therapeutic strategies that target these pathways.

Recent findings

Recent evidence indicates that immune cells displaying senescence-associated phenotypes accumulate in adipose tissue, liver, and vasculature, where they exhibit mitochondrial dysfunction, epigenetic remodeling, and a maladaptive senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) driven by NF-κB and C/EBPβ. Key SASP components, including interleukin-6 (IL-6), tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), and CCL2, together with p53/p21- and p16/RB-mediated cell-cycle arrest and cGAS-STING pathway activation, contribute to adipocyte hypertrophy, insulin resistance, hepatic steatosis, and dyslipidemia. These changes are associated with the accelerated progression of obesity, type 2 diabetes, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), and atherosclerosis. Additionally, CH and impaired immune surveillance exacerbate chronic metabolic inflammation. This review discusses classical interventions, including metabolic modulators, senolytics, and senomorphics, alongside emerging strategies such as Proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTAC)-based senolytics, CH-targeted approaches, and mitochondrial-targeted therapies, emphasizing mechanistic differences and supporting clinical evidence. Nevertheless, challenges related to achieving tissue-specific delivery while minimizing systemic toxicity remain unresolved. Immunosenescence plays a dual role; transient and context-dependent SASP signaling can contribute to tissue repair, whereas persistent or dysregulated SASP activity can promote pathology. Currently, validated clinical tools for assessing immune-driven metabolic dysfunction are lacking. This absence of standardized evaluation frameworks hinders the translation of these therapies into clinical practice, highlighting the necessity for a theoretical foundation to guide precision treatment of obesity-related metabolic diseases and to promote healthy aging.

title: The Menopausal Transition as a Critical Window for Cardiovascular Risk Modification and Intervention Opportunities.
authorString: Mehta JM, Manson JE.
abstractText:
Purpose of review

This review examines the cardiometabolic changes that occur during the menopausal transition (MT), emphasizing how hormonal fluctuations may contribute to the development of adverse cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk factors. It identifies gaps in evidence regarding safe and effective treatments for cardiometabolic risk reduction during the MT.

Recent findings

The MT is characterized by hormonal shifts driving adverse changes in body composition, lipid profiles, vascular function, and metabolic regulation. These alterations are associated with accelerated progression of cardiovascular risk factors and may contribute to the increase in CVD risk observed after menopause. Growing evidence suggests that the MT represents a distinct period of cardiometabolic vulnerability and provides an opportunity for early risk identification and prevention. Lifestyle and behavioral modifications, as well as control of blood pressure, lipids, and other established risk factors, are the foundations of risk-reducing management and treatment. Early cardiometabolic risk assessment and individualized, lifestyle -centered management are essential to optimize cardiovascular outcomes during the MT. Further research is needed to clarify therapeutic strategies for this critical window in women's cardiometabolic health.

title: Gut Microbiota, Red Wine and Atherosclerosis.
authorString: da Luz PL, Favarato D.
abstractText:
Purpose of review

To review the relationships among gut microbiota, dietary patterns, red wine (RW) consumption, and atherosclerosis, with emphasis on microbiome-related metabolic pathways and their potential relevance to cardiovascular prevention.

Recent findings

Recent evidence has expanded our understanding of the microbiome-metabolome interface in cardiometabolic disease. Dietary patterns can modify microbial diversity and metabolites involved in inflammation, glucose homeostasis, and cardiovascular risk. Recent studies also support associations between wine-related dietary exposures, gut microbiota composition, and circulating metabolites. In the Wine Flora Study, moderate RW consumption was associated with broad shifts in gut microbiota and plasma metabolomic profiles without modifying plasma trimethylamine N-oxide. The gut microbiota participates in multiple metabolic pathways relevant to cardiovascular health and atherosclerosis. Diet is an important determinant of microbiome composition, and RW polyphenols may influence microbial and metabolic profiles. Nevertheless, a healthy diet, regular physical activity, smoking avoidance, and weight control remain cornerstones of cardiovascular prevention.

title: Single-dose neonatal gene therapy preserves motor coordination and extends survival of Polg -deficient mice
authorString: Zanin S, Moriceau S, Afram E, Perez-Cartier MT, Gaborit C, Simon Sola M, Kneeland SC, Murray SA, Munnich A, Ruzzenente B, Metodiev MD.
abstractText: POLG mutations are the most common single nuclear gene cause of mitochondrial disease. POLG disease spans a spectrum of clinical presentations with variable age of onset and severity. Early-onset disease is often severe and fatal (e.g., Alpers syndrome, myocerebrohepatopathy), while late-onset disease can be relatively mild (e.g., progressive external ophthalmoplegia). POLG disease is incurable, with few symptomatic treatments available, none of which can prevent its progression. Gene replacement therapy has the potential to halt or prevent POLG disease, but its development has been hindered by the large size of the  POLG cDNA and the scarcity of suitable mouse models. Here, we developed a bespoke  Polg knockout (KO) mouse model by inactivating the  Polg locus in parvalbumin-expressing neurons (e.g., Purkinje cells) and fast-twitch skeletal muscle fibers. KO mice developed progressive motor coordination deficits, respiratory chain deficiency in Purkinje cells and skeletal muscle, and died prematurely. We also developed nine AAV-based gene therapy vectors and confirmed their ability to express the human POLγA protein in different mouse tissues. A single high-dose administration of either of two lead candidates into  Polg KO neonates preserved respiratory chain activity in Purkinje cells and skeletal muscle, delayed the onset of motor coordination deficits, and extended lifespan. Thus, our work provides preclinical proof of concept for gene replacement therapy for POLG disease, establishing the feasibility of this approach and laying the foundation for further development in the field.

title: Multidisciplinary perioperative management of emergency laparoscopic appendectomy for perforated appendicitis in a child with Duchenne muscular dystrophy: a case report
authorString: Zhang Q, Zhang Z, Hu M, Zhang G.
abstractText: Background: Children with Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) are vulnerable to anesthesia-associated rhabdomyolysis-like events, hyperkalemia, postoperative respiratory failure, and occult cardiomyopathy. These risks complicate emergency abdominal surgery, where delayed source control may worsen sepsis. Detailed pediatric perioperative reports describing multidisciplinary risk mitigation for emergency abdominal surgery in DMD remain extremely limited, and practical clinical pathways are lacking. Case presentation: A 9-year-old Han Chinese ambulatory boy with genetically confirmed DMD (exon 51 deletion) presented with 40 hours of right lower quadrant pain, peritoneal irritation, a fecalith on ultrasound, markedly elevated inflammatory markers (C-reactive protein 186.84 mg/L), and elevated creatine kinase (5139 U/L). Focused preoperative cardiopulmonary assessment showed preserved left ventricular systolic function and no biochemical evidence of acute myocardial injury. An urgent multidisciplinary meeting involving pediatric surgery, anesthesiology, pediatric intensive care, neurology, and endocrinology was convened within 6 hours of admission. Hybrid single-incision laparoscopic appendectomy with an additional 5-mm assisting trocar was performed under non-trigger total intravenous anesthesia, with strict avoidance of succinylcholine and volatile anesthetic agents, serial arterial blood gas and potassium monitoring, perioperative steroid bridging, readiness for malignant hyperthermia-like deterioration including immediate availability of dantrolene, and planned postoperative pediatric intensive care unit admission. Intraoperative findings confirmed perforated gangrenous appendicitis with diffuse purulent peritonitis. The patient was extubated shortly after PICU arrival, developed no perioperative hyperkalemia, arrhythmia, pigmenturia, or MH-like hypermetabolic signs, and recovered uneventfully after staged antibiotic therapy. Conclusions: This case illustrates a practical perioperative pathway for emergency abdominal surgery in a selected ambulatory child with DMD and supports timely minimally invasive source control when perioperative risk mitigation is protocolized. However, it should not be interpreted as a representative model for all patients with Duchenne muscular dystrophy, particularly those with advanced cardiopulmonary impairment or more complex airway and metabolic risk profiles.

title: Optimization of anesthesia strategies for transapical beating-heart septal myectomy in hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy: a retrospective cohort study of 119 patients
authorString: Yao W, Li Y, Li R, Liu Y, Chen Y, Yang J, Ibáñez C, Wei X, Xu Q.
abstractText: Background Our institution recently reported transapical beating-heart septal myectomy (TA-BSM) as a novel surgical procedure for patients diagnosed hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), which avoided cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) procedure. Herein, we identified the details of the anesthesia strategy in TA-BSM via retrospective analysis to guide perioperative anesthetic management. Methods 119 patients undergoing TA-BSM were retrospectively evaluated, and comprehensive perioperative data were collected including endotracheal intubation type about single or double lumen tube, anesthetic protocols, surgical team cooperation, hemodynamic fluctuations, and perioperative complications. According the endotracheal intubation type, the recruited patients were divided into the single-lumen tube (SLT) group and the double-lumen tube (DLT) group. Results Baseline characteristics showed that 17 patients (14.29%) were aged ≥ 65 years and 71 patients (59.66%) were basal-mid septal myocardial hypertrophy. Isoproterenol provocation was performed in 68 patients, and hypotensive episodes requiring intervention was decreased from 32 patients before resection to 15 patients after resection during provocation period. With precise anesthetic management, perioperative vital signs were remained stable on the basis of autologous blood transfusion in 88 patients (mean ± SD, 448 ± 250 mL). Postoperatively, no significant differences were showed between SLT group and DLT group in the residual left ventricular outflow tract obstruction (LVOTO) or postoperative complications (risk ratio, 0.679; 95% CI, 0.328 to 1.405; P = 0.296). Conclusion There was little impact for the endotracheal tube choice on the surgical outcomes of TA-BSM. Anesthetic management should prioritize the precise regulation of circulatory fluctuation during isoproterenol provocation, meticulous volume status maintenance, and emergency treatment for acute complications.

title: Integrative Network Toxicology, Transcriptomics Profiling, and Molecular Docking Analysis of Potential Mechanisms Linking Tris(1,3-dichloro-2-propyl) Phosphate (TDCPP) Exposure to Atherosclerosis
authorString: Sastrawan IGG, Indriyani NKV, Guna NKSD, Dewi NNA, Suastika LOS, Ghapor AAA, Sadikan MZ.
abstractText: Tris(1,3-dichloro-2-propyl) phosphate (TDCPP) is an organophosphate flame retardant widely detected in the environment, raising concerns regarding its long-term health effects. Epidemiological studies have associated TDCPP exposure with the risk of cardiovascular diseases. However, the mechanisms by which TDCPP exposure may contribute to cardiovascular diseases, particularly through atherosclerosis formation, remain unclear. Our study aimed to investigate the potential biomolecular mechanisms linking TDCPP to atherosclerosis through in silico analyses, including network toxicology, protein-protein interaction (PPI) network analysis, transcriptomic profiling, and molecular docking. Genes related to TDCPP and atherosclerosis were retrieved from open-access databases. We identified 125 intersecting genes between TDCPP- and atherosclerosis-related gene sets, which were associated with inflammatory signaling pathways, particularly cytokine- and chemokine-related processes and leukocyte migration. PPI network analysis identified CCR1, CCR2, CCR7, CXCR3, and JAK3 as potential core gene targets. Further analysis of potential cellular targets by mapping to a human atherosclerotic plaque single-cell transcriptomic atlas indicated that these five genes were mainly expressed in immune-cell populations, particularly myeloid and lymphoid cells. Transcriptomic analysis showed higher expression of all five genes in atherosclerotic tissues than in controls across arterial territories, while CCR1, CCR2, and JAK3 consistently showed higher expression in advanced atherosclerotic lesions. Molecular docking revealed that CCR7 and CCR2 had favorable docking scores with TDCPP (-5.801 and -5.627 kcal/mol, respectively). Overall, our findings indicate potential molecular mechanisms linking TDCPP to atherosclerosis through chemokine-mediated immune-cell trafficking and inflammatory signaling. Further studies are necessary to validate the relevance of these candidate targets and pathways.

title: Early Detection of Maternal Supraphysiological Hypercholesterolemia: Development and Internal Validation of a Machine Learning Model and Characterization of First- Trimester Atherogenic Biomarkers
authorString: Serra R, Cantin C, Medina-Ortiz D, Sepúlveda-Peñaloza A, Morales A, Ríos V, Peñailillo R, Monteiro LJ, Carter SW, Kemp MW, Illanes SE, Leiva A.
abstractText: Background Maternal supraphysiological hypercholesterolemia (MSPH), defined by total cholesterol ≥ 290 mg/dL at term in women without pre-existing dyslipidemia, is associated with a more atherogenic profile and adverse cardiovascular consequences for mother and offspring. Because MSPH is recognized only late in pregnancy, early markers identifying at-risk women are lacking. We aimed to develop and internally validate supervised machine learning models using first-trimester clinical and biochemical measurements to predict MSPH at term, and to characterize early atherosclerosis-related biomarkers in women who developed MSPH. Methods This prospective observational cohort included 160 women with singleton, uncomplicated pregnancies recruited at two prenatal centers in Santiago, Chile. Predictors comprised 11 first-trimester anthropometric, metabolic, hemodynamic, and lipid-related variables. ApoB, ApoA1, oxidized LDL, and malondialdehyde were measured in a subgroup (n = 78). Third-trimester lipid measurements, used to define MSPH, were excluded as predictors. A complete-case dataset (n = 148) and a median-imputed full-cohort (n = 160) were evaluated. Multiple classifier families, preprocessing strategies, and internal-validation schemes, including stratified train-test splits, k-fold cross-validation, and leave-one-out validation, were benchmarked within leakage-controlled pipelines. Stochastic partitioning strategies were evaluated across fixed random seeds, and model selection prioritized predictive performance, stability, and parsimony. Interpretability was assessed using SHAP and permutation importance. Results Of 160 women, 44 (27.5%) developed MSPH. First-trimester total and LDL cholesterol showed the strongest between-group differences, while multivariable exploratory analyses indicated substantial overlap between groups. The selected Linear Discriminant Analysis pipeline achieved a ROC-AUC of 0.77 and a PR-AUC of 0.52. At the fixed operating threshold of 0.60, sensitivity was 0.62, specificity 0.79, accuracy 0.75, and MCC 0.40. Outputs were interpreted as discrimination scores rather than calibrated absolute risk estimates. SHAP and permutation importance identified first-trimester total cholesterol as the dominant predictor. Women who subsequently developed MSPH also showed higher first-trimester ApoB and malondialdehyde. Conclusions First-trimester clinical and lipid measurements contain discriminatory information for subsequent MSPH, with total cholesterol providing the strongest contribution. Atherogenic and oxidative alterations are also detectable in the first trimester of pregnancies that later develop MSPH. These findings support further evaluation of interpretable first-trimester risk assessment approaches; external validation is required before clinical application. Trial registration : Not applicable. Analytical code: https://github.com/kren-ai-lab/MSPH_classification_models.

title: Late-Presenting Asymptomatic Balanced Double Aortic Arch Associated With Tetralogy of Fallot: Definitive Surgical Correction.
authorString: Talwar S, Das D, Bhende VV, Roy SA, Krishnakumar M, Gohil AA, Sharma AS, Mehta DV.
abstractText: Asymptomatic balanced double aortic arch (DAA) is rarely associated with tetralogy of Fallot (TOF). Balanced DAA may present with symptoms caused by tracheal or esophageal compression. However, the lack of consensus on the management of asymptomatic DAA poses a dilemma regarding the need for surgical intervention. We report a case of asymptomatic balanced DAA associated with TOF in an eight-year-old boy who presented with exercise intolerance, fatigue, and increasing cyanosis. Doppler showed severe right ventricular outflow tract obstruction. Intracardiac repair proceeded without ring division. On postoperative day 15, echocardiography showed a peak outflow tract gradient of 28 mmHg and free pulmonary regurgitation.

title: Distinct clinical-immunological subtypes define prognostic heterogeneity in anti-U1RNP-positive connective tissue diseases.
authorString: Liu D, Zhang J, Zhang J, Hu N, Huang J, Luo J, Ju B, Wang Y, Li Q, An Q, Xu Q, Lv X, He L.
abstractText:
Objective

Anti-U1 ribonucleoprotein (U1RNP) antibody-positive connective tissue diseases (CTDs) exhibit marked clinical heterogeneity that is not adequately captured by conventional diagnostic classifications. This study aimed to identify intrinsic clinical-immunological subtypes and assess their prognostic implications.

Methods

In this single-center retrospective cohort, 358 patients with anti-U1RNP-positive CTDs were analyzed using multiple correspondence analysis and hierarchical clustering. Key discriminative features were identified through least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. Peripheral blood lymphocyte subsets were assessed by flow cytometry, and long-term survival was compared using Kaplan-Meier analysis.

Results

Clustering analysis identified three clinical-immunological subtypes with significant differences. Cluster 1, the "mild immunological type", was characterized by minimal autoantibody positivity and relatively normal lymphocyte counts, and exhibited the most favorable prognosis. Cluster 2, the "exocrine gland-joint-muscle involvement type", presented with prominent sicca symptoms, arthralgia, elevated creatine kinase (CK), and interstitial lung disease (ILD), and had an intermediate prognosis. Cluster 3, the "severe systemic type", was associated with marked pericarditis, renal injury, multiple autoantibody positivity, and widespread lymphopenia, and had the poorest survival. LASSO analysis highlighted normal T lymphocyte and T follicular helper cell counts for cluster 1, elevated CK and rheumatoid factor for cluster 2, and anti-dsDNA/anti-nucleosome antibodies, elevated D-dimer, and major organ involvement for cluster 3.

Conclusion

Anti-U1RNP-positive CTDs comprise distinct clinical-immunological subtypes with different clinical features, immune profiles, and prognostic outcomes. Subtype-based stratification may facilitate precision management, particularly for patients with multiple autoantibody positivity and severe lymphopenia who are at high risk of poor prognosis.

title: Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance for the Diagnosis and Monitoring of Takayasu Arteritis in Children.
authorString: Yin AL, Milano EG, Brogan P, Eleftheriou D, Tann O, Mortensen K, Taylor AM, Muthurangu V, Quail MA.

journal.title: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance

abstractText:
Background

Imaging evidence of vasculitis is mandatory for classification of Takayasu arteritis (TA) in children, yet the ability of a negative study to exclude the diagnosis has not been evaluated. We aimed to determine the negative predictive value (NPV) of cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) for excluding TA in children, to describe the imaging phenotype at diagnosis, and to characterise interval change on serial imaging.

Methods

This retrospective study included all children who underwent CMR for suspected or established large vessel vasculitis at a single tertiary centre between May 2018 and November 2025. The protocol comprised contrast-enhanced angiography, 3D balanced steady-state free precession (bSSFP) imaging, black-blood imaging and late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) of vessel walls. TA was classified by the EULAR/PRINTO/PRES paediatric criteria. A true negative was defined as a negative baseline CMR with no emergence of TA over at least 6 months of documented follow-up. Interval change on serial CMR was classified per scan pair as improved, unchanged or worsened, recording wall findings (thickening, LGE) and luminal findings (stenosis, dilation) separately, by two readers.

Results

161 children underwent 222 CMR studies. Of 156 initial diagnostic studies, 10 (6%) showed TA and 146 were negative. No child with a negative baseline CMR developed TA during a median follow-up of 3.6 years (IQR 2.1 to 4.7), corresponding to an observed NPV of 100% (95% CI 97.5 to 100). Positive initial studies were characterised by aortic wall thickening and LGE in 7 of 10 children (70%), these were concordant in every child; extra-aortic involvement was present in 7 (70%). Fifteen children with TA underwent serial CMR (51 interval comparisons; inter-reader agreement 90%, weighted κ 0.86, 95% CI 0.71 to 0.96): 11 intervals (22%) showed improvement, 20 (39%) no change and 20 (39%) worsening. Two children had a previously undescribed imaging finding of focal 3D bSSFP signal abnormalities at sites of disease, consistent with a local susceptibility effect that improved or resolved with treatment.

Conclusions

In a tertiary referral population, no child with a negative CMR developed TA during follow-up. Serial CMR detected interval change with high agreement between readers. These findings support CMR as a reliable investigation for both the exclusion and longitudinal monitoring of TA in children.

title: External Manual Aortic Compression as a Temporizing Measure During Inter-Facility Transfer of a Woman With Life-Threatening Obstetric Hemorrhage in a Resource-Limited Setting: A Case Report From Ethiopia
authorString: Addis NA, Yigzaw KT, Fikru MG, Kebede FS, Fetene MA.
abstractText: Severe postpartum hemorrhage can be fatal when blood products, devices, and transfer are unavailable. External manual aortic compression (EMAC) may reduce distal blood flow temporarily. A 24-year-old woman at 37 weeks and 2 days presented after five hours of vaginal bleeding and developed shock following vaginal delivery, with blood loss exceeding 3,000 mL. Initial measures failed to control bleeding. Because the referring facility had neither blood products nor a non-pneumatic anti-shock garment, the attending gynecologist maintained EMAC for approximately 65 minutes during ambulance transfer. At the referral hospital, she received eight units of whole blood and three units of fresh frozen plasma and underwent B-Lynch uterine compression suturing. She developed acute kidney injury requiring three hemodialysis sessions. Renal function recovered, and she remained well through 12 months. This case illustrates EMAC as a temporary bridge to definitive treatment, not a substitute for urgent transfer, resuscitation, transfusion, or hemorrhage control.

title: Pre-planned anesthetic strategy for a penetrating ballistic injury involving the aortic root and tracheal carina: a case report
authorString: Gao W, Li R.
abstractText:
Background: Penetrating thoracic trauma simultaneously involving the great vessels and the central airway is rare and poses exceptional anesthetic challenges. Reports detailing the anesthetic management of retained metallic fragments lodged adjacent to both the aortic root and the tracheal carina are scarce. We present such a case, managed without cardiopulmonary bypass, together with a review of comparable published cases. Case presentation: A 36-year-old woman sustained a penetrating right anterior chest wall injury from a shattered metal grinding wheel. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography localized two irregular metallic fragments at the aortic transverse sinus and embedded in the tracheal carina. After multidisciplinary planning, anesthesia was induced with a rapid-sequence technique using hemodynamically stable agents (remimazolam, etomidate, sufentanil, and mivacurium). A left-sided double-lumen tube was placed on the first attempt under direct laryngoscopy, and one-lung ventilation with zero positive end-expiratory pressure was maintained for 75 minutes while cardiac and thoracic surgical teams sequentially removed both fragments. Central venous pressure-guided restrictive fluid management was applied; neither cardiopulmonary bypass nor vasoactive support was required. The patient was extubated 12 hours postoperatively and discharged on postoperative day 12 after successful treatment of postoperative pneumonia.

Conclusions:

A pre-planned anesthetic strategy combining rapid-sequence induction with hemodynamically neutral agents, lung isolation with protective zero-PEEP ventilation, and central venous pressure-guided restrictive resuscitation can support combined great-vessel and carinal foreign-body surgery without cardiopulmonary bypass. In this case, multidisciplinary rehearsal, contrast-enhanced CT-based planning, and readiness for rapid escalation were central to the favorable outcome.

title: Longitudinal Trends of Intact and Ruptured Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Repairs in the United States: A Cross-Sectional Study.
authorString: Luu IY, Hong AT, Lin F, Han SM, Pyun AJ, Miranda E, Zenilman A, Tan TW.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted access to elective procedures and routine care. Given the risk of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) rupture, understanding repair trends is important to assess the impact of the pandemic on vascular outcomes.

Methods

This repeated cross-sectional analysis used the TriNetX network, a multicenter US electronic health records database. We included 423 874 patients diagnosed with AAA from 2016 to 2024. Patients were categorized by clinical presentation-intact AAA and ruptured AAA-and stratified by surgical approach: endovascular aneurysm repair or open aneurysm repair. Annual trends in AAA repair rates were assessed using joinpoint regression to calculate annual percentage change.

Results

Among 19 330 AAA repairs, 3791 (19.6%) were open aneurysm repair, and 15 539 (80.4%) were endovascular aneurysm repair. From 2018 to 2024, 1623 repairs (9.9%) were for ruptured AAA and 14 835 (90.1%) were for intact AAA. The rate of intact AAA repairs initially remained stable from 2018 to 2022 but significantly decreased after the pandemic from 2022 to 2024 (annual percentage change, -2.87% [95% CI, -10.95 to -1.00]). In contrast, ruptured AAA repairs rates shifted sharply during the pandemic, with an established prepandemic decline in ruptured repairs from 2018 to 2020 (annual percentage change, -11.48%) reversed, with an increase from 2020 to 2022 (annual percentage change +12.01%), before declining from 2022 to 2024 (annual percentage change, -11.00%).

Conclusions

In this retrospective cross-sectional study, repairs for intact AAA declined, while repairs for ruptured AAA increased during the pandemic period. These trends suggest that potential delays in routine surveillance and elective surgery during the pandemic may have increased acute presentations.

title: Genetically homogeneous C57BL/6J and C57BL/6N mice exhibit differential physiological dysfunction compared to genetically heterogeneous UM-HET3 mice.
authorString: Sabouri M, Li Z, Irwin BJ, Sen JB, Samarah L, Bernardo J, Zheng X, Machin DR.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol
journal.title: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
journal.isoabbreviation: Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol

abstractText: The most commonly used animal models in biomedical research are genetically homogeneous C57BL/6 mice. We recently demonstrated that genetically heterogeneous UM-HET3 mice have greater vascular function than C57BL/6 substrains, including lower aortic stiffness and greater endothelium-dependent dilation. To expand on our previous studies, we examined metabolic, microcirculatory, hematological, and inflammatory phenotypes in C57BL/6J, C57BL/6N, and UM-HET3 mice. UM-HET3 mice exhibited greater body mass and lower non-fasting blood glucose compared to C57BL/6 substrains (P<0.05). Glucose tolerance was greater in UM-HET3 and C57BL/6N compared to C57BL/6J mice (P<0.05), while insulin sensitivity was greater in UM-HET3 and C57BL/6J compared to C57BL/6N mice (P<0.05). UM-HET3 mice had greater mesenteric microvascular density, glycocalyx integrity, and glycocalyx thickness than both C57BL/6 substrains (P<0.05). UM-HET3 mice also had lower total white blood cell concentration, higher neutrophil and lower lymphocyte proportions than C57BL/6J, and higher hemoglobin, hematocrit, MCV, and MCH than C57BL/6 substrains (P<0.05). Cytokine profiling revealed differences between UM-HET3 and C57BL/6J in G-CSF, IL-1β, IP-10, MIP-2, and VEGF, as well as between UM-HET3 and C57BL/6N in IFN-γ, IL-5, and IP-10 (P<0.05). Coefficients of variation were similar across strains for most outcomes, indicating that genetic heterogeneity in UM-HET3 mice did not increase variability. These findings demonstrate metabolic, microcirculatory, hematological, and inflammatory differences in UM-HET3 compared to C57BL/6 substrains, and between C57BL/6J and C57BL/6N mice. UM-HET3 mice appear to have a healthier physiological phenotype than C57BL/6 mice, indicating their potential as a research model; however, whether these differences persist with aging or predict later-life health outcomes remains unknown.

title: Functional Somatic Symptoms in Paediatric Patients With Congenital Heart Disease.
authorString: Riordan G, Gnanappa G, Zhu J, Hurwitz S, Scher S, Kozlowska K.

journal.title: Journal of paediatrics and child health

abstractText: Aberrant stress-system activation or dysregulation affects the cardiovascular system through various pathways, including the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, autonomic nervous system, neuro-endocrine system, and a range of neurophysiological intermediaries. In children with congenital heart disease-who have high rates of adverse childhood experiences, comorbid medical conditions, and neurodevelopmental issues-this activation/dysregulation commonly results in functional cardiac symptoms such as orthostatic intolerance, (functional) chest pain, and syncope-like presentations. Despite the obvious need, research into stress-system responses in children with congenital heart disease is limited. This article reviews commonly encountered clinical scenarios with the goal of encouraging practitioners to recognise the interconnections between structural cardiac lesions in children, stress-system activation/dysregulation, and functional somatic symptoms. Children with congenital heart disease and comorbid functional symptoms require comprehensive management strategies. We propose a framework to help clinicians facilitate appropriate treatment.

title: Assessment of conversational pragmatics (ACP): Validation of a screening tool for pragmatic difficulties in children aged 6-11 with spoken language difficulties.
authorString: Gentilleau-Lambin P, Mortain L, Labreuche J, Nicli J, Dondel A, Medjkane F, Lemaître MP.

journal.title: Archives de pediatrie : organe officiel de la Societe francaise de pediatrie

abstractText:
Introduction and objective

Pragmatics-the ability to use language appropriately in social contexts-is a multidimensional skill involving verbal and non-verbal communication, social cognition, and executive functions. While pragmatic difficulties are recognized across neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs), their assessment remains challenging due to terminological heterogeneity and a lack of standardized tools. This study aimed to validate the Assessment of Conversational Pragmatics (ACP), a 26-item parental questionnaire designed to identify pragmatic difficulties in French children aged 6-11.

Materials and methodology

The study included 947 children: 549 typically developing (control), 299 with Language Difficulties (LgD) of whom 229 were identified as having a Developmental Language Disorder (DLD), and 99 verbal persons with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Principal component analysis confirmed the ACP's unidimensional structure, with excellent internal consistency (Cronbach's α, 0.90; 95% CI, [0.87;0.91]). Test-retest reliability was good (ICC = 0.78; 95% CI, [0.66;0.86]), and external validity was supported by strong correlations with the CELF-5 Pragmatic Profile (rs = 0.81).

Results

The ACP effectively discriminated between the three groups, with median scores of 68 [IQR, 62-74] (control), 55 [IQR, 47-64] (LgD), and 44 [IQR, 37-64] (ASD) (p < 0.001). Optimal cut-off scores were identified: ≤58 indicated a 60% risk of language difficulties, and ≤46 a 58% risk of ASD. However, the ACP did not differentiate between children with LgD and specific developmental language disorder (DLD), likely due to recruitment bias in specialized centres.

Conclusion

This study demonstrates the ACP's robustness as a screening tool for pragmatic difficulties, offering a quick, reliable, and free resource for healthcare professionals. Its use of parent-reported data addresses the challenge of assessing pragmatic skills in clinical settings, where one-on-one interactions may not reveal a child's full communicative profile. The ACP's standardization across distinct populations provides a valuable clinical aid for early identification and referral, supporting timely intervention for children at risk of pragmatic impairments.

title: Mechanical Atrioventricular Valve Thrombosis After Warfarin Interruption in Two Patients with Single Ventricle Physiology.
authorString: Takao H, Sugiyama K, Toda K, Hirano A, Ishido H, Hoashi T, Suzuki T, Kojima T, Masutani S.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: World J Pediatr Congenit Heart Surg
journal.title: World journal for pediatric & congenital heart surgery
journal.isoabbreviation: World J Pediatr Congenit Heart Surg

abstractText: Thrombosed mechanical atrioventricular (AV) valves are catastrophic in patients with functional single-ventricle physiology; however, anticoagulation management during intercurrent illness is not well defined. We retrospectively reviewed 2 patients with functional single-ventricle physiology who underwent mechanical AV valve replacement at our institution. Mechanical valve thrombosis with leaflet immobility was diagnosed by cinefluoroscopy or echocardiography and confirmed intraoperatively. Two patients developed thrombosed mechanical AV valves after temporary warfarin cessation for supratherapeutic PT-INR during gastroenteritis. Case 1 (hypoplastic left heart syndrome following Glenn procedure, mechanical tricuspid valve) developed single-leaflet immobility after warfarin was withheld and low-dose vitamin K2 was administered for a PT-INR of 7.1. Case 2 (right atrial isomerism, Fontan circulation, mechanical common AV valve) developed bilateral leaflet immobility despite sustained PT-INR >4.0. Operative findings confirmed fresh thrombus without pannus in both cases. Valve thrombosis may occur after warfarin interruption even when PT-INR remains therapeutic, and reliance on PT-INR alone may underestimate thrombotic risk.

title: Delayed Diagnosis of Coronary Sinus Ostial Atresia in a Single-Ventricle Patient.
authorString: Sriram V, Thankavel P, Guleserian K, Murthy R.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: World J Pediatr Congenit Heart Surg
journal.title: World journal for pediatric & congenital heart surgery
journal.isoabbreviation: World J Pediatr Congenit Heart Surg

abstractText: Coronary sinus ostial atresia is a rare congenital anomaly that is often clinically silent; however, hemodynamic compromise can occur if venous drainage is interrupted. We present a 4-month old infant with hypoplastic left heart syndrome who previously underwent palliation with a Norwood procedure. During bidirectional Glenn palliation, ligation of a 2-mm left superior vena cava resulted in coronary sinus dilation and myocardial edema, raising suspicion for coronary sinus ostial atresia. The coronary sinus was unroofed, and the child recovered well.

title: Ventricular Morphology and Atrioventricular Valve Regurgitation in Adults Post-Fontan: Associations With Exercise Hemodynamics.
authorString: Van den Eynde J, Van De Bruaene A, Egbe AC, Van Belle H, Jain CC, Borlaug BA, Reddy YNV, Connolly HM, Dearani JA, d'Udekem Y, Budts W, Eleid MF, Miranda WR.
abstractText:
Background

Right ventricular (RV) dominance and atrioventricular valve regurgitation (AVVR) are associated with adverse outcomes post-Fontan palliation, but their underlying hemodynamic correlates, particularly during exercise, remain incompletely characterized.

Methods

In this cross-sectional cohort, exercise hemodynamics by ventricular morphology and AVVR severity were assessed invasively (supine exercise catheterization) in 108 individuals and semi-invasively (semisupine exercise with echocardiography and peripheral venous pressure) in 108.

Results

Age of the invasive cohort was 32.1 (25.6-37.2) years; 41 had RV dominance, 19 had moderate or severe AVVR, and 16 had both. Resting and peak mean pulmonary artery pressure and pulmonary artery wedge pressure were similar across ventricular morphologies and AVVR severity. However, RV dominance was associated with lower systemic (systemic blood flow, 67% [22-93] versus 86% [63-105] predicted; P=0.006) and pulmonary (pulmonary blood flow, 57% [33-75] versus 72% [61-89] predicted; P<0.001) cardiac output responses to exercise and steeper Δpulmonary artery pressure/Δpulmonary blood flow, (4.3 [2.6-10.6] versus 3.0 [1.7-4.8] mm Hg/L per minute; P=0.004). Patients with moderate or severe AVVR showed a similar pattern, with lower systemic blood flow (64% [19-92] versus 77% [57-101], P=0.10) and pulmonary blood flow (57% [36-74] versus 70% [55-88] predicted, P=0.03) responses. Findings were replicated in the semi-invasive cohort, where RV dominance and moderate or severe AVVR were associated with lower peak systemic blood flow and higher Δperipheral venous pressure/Δ systemic blood flow, despite similar peak peripheral venous pressure.

Conclusions

Resting and exertional pulmonary artery wedge pressure, pulmonary artery pressure, and peripheral venous pressure are unrelated to ventricular morphology and AVVR severity. Conversely, impaired flow augmentation and steeper pressure-flow relationships during exercise were associated with RV dominance and moderate or severe AVVR, emphasizing the role of dynamic provocation to unmask occult cardiovascular reserve limitations.

title: Systematic Transesophageal Echocardiographic Identification of Tricuspid Valve Commissures and Subvalvular Apparatus.
authorString: Cammalleri V, Khalique OK, Tavernese A, Ussia GP.
abstractText: Transcatheter tricuspid valve (TV) intervention is rapidly evolving and several classes of therapeutic devices are currently in development. The anatomic knowledge of the TV is the cornerstone for transcatheter patient selection, and the successful implantation of the devices depends on imaging guidance. Anatomically, leaflets are separated by the commissures, which have peculiar findings: they are supported by fan-shaped chords and do not open directly into the annulus, but a few millimeters of the leaflet tissue remain, similar to small scallops. While a comprehensive echocardiographic assessment of TV has been extensively reported, few papers have focused on analyzing commissures and their impact on interventions. This paper aims to introduce a novel echocardiographic approach focusing on TV commissures, and provide a dedicated transesophageal imaging protocol and methodology for recognizing their anatomic landmarks. Multiple dedicated transesophageal views are comprehensively reported for each commissure, in order to ensure a guide for emerging transcatheter procedures.

title: Suture-Only vs Hybrid Closure Techniques for Vascular Access Haemostasis in Percutaneous Cardiovascular Procedures: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Banga A, Misra S, Rathore SS, Agrawal A, Ganatra S, Latina J, Gannon S, Dani S.
abstractText:
Background

Vascular complications and bleeding increase morbidity and mortality after percutaneous cardiovascular procedures, including transcatheter aortic valve replacements (TAVR) and percutaneous endovascular aneurysm repair (pEVAR), often from vascular closure device (VCD) failure. We compared suture-only (SO) with suture and plug-based hybrid (HSP) vascular closure technique for vascular access haemostasis after percutaneous procedures such as TAVR and pEVAR.

Method

We performed a systematic literature search of randomised controlled trials (RCT) and observational studies using PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, ScienceDirect, and ClinicalTrials.gov following the PRISMA guidelines. The study protocol was registered at PROSPERO (ID: CRD42024627875). We calculated the relative risk (RR) and 95% confidence interval (CI) for individual end points of vascular complications, bleeding risk, VCD failure, and mortality, using random-effects models to report overall effect sizes.

Results

Nine studies, including two RCTs and seven observational studies, comprising 3,765 patients (SO, 1,971; HSP, 1,790), were analysed. The SO strategy was associated with a significantly higher risk of vascular complications (RR 1.95; p<0.01), bleeding (RR 2.14; p=0.01), and VCD failure (RR 4.00; p<0.01) compared with the HSP technique. No significant difference was noted in all-cause mortality (RR 1.61; p=0.11) between the two groups, although the analysis was limited by the relatively small number of observed events and wide CIs.

Conclusions

Use of the HSP technique for vascular access haemostasis after TAVR or pEVAR was associated with significantly lower rates of vascular complications, bleeding, and VCD failure compared with SO closure, without a significant difference in mortality.

title: Perioperative outcomes after total coronary revascularization via left anterior thoracotomy (TCRAT): A systematic review and single-arm meta-analysis.
authorString: Abu Hantash N, Abu Yosef M, Alagha S, Elmanaseer SM, Aldeeb OM, Varghese D.
abstractText: BackgroundTotal coronary revascularization via left anterior thoracotomy (TCRAT) is a sternum-sparing approach to multivessel coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). Published evidence is predominantly observational. This review summarizes reported perioperative outcomes after TCRAT; its principal quantitative synthesis is single-arm and does not establish comparative effectiveness against conventional CABG.MethodsThis systematic review followed PRISMA 2020 guidance and was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261437661). PubMed and Scopus were searched from inception to May 1, 2026. Studies reporting perioperative or clinical outcomes in adults undergoing TCRAT were eligible. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I for comparative non-randomized studies and the JBI checklist for case series. Random-effects meta-analysis of proportions used the Freeman-Tukey double-arcsine transformation; continuous outcomes were pooled using random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood estimation.ResultsSeven cohorts comprising a reported total of 1869 patients were included. The pooled in-hospital/short-term mortality estimate was 0.92% (95% CI, 0.28-1.83%; I2 = 48.8%), and the pooled stroke estimate was 0.76% (95% CI, 0.10-1.82%; I2 = 61.6%). Pooled incidences of postoperative atrial fibrillation and re-exploration were 11.53% and 3.44%, respectively; deep wound infection was uncommon (0.15%). Pooled mean cardiopulmonary bypass and aortic cross-clamp times were 146.17 and 78.05 minutes. Estimates for operative times and length of stay were highly heterogeneous. The exploratory diabetes-stratified analysis did not detect a statistically significant mortality difference (p = 0.8443).ConclusionThe available cohorts describe the perioperative outcomes reported after TCRAT in selected patients and centers. These single-arm pooled estimates should not be interpreted as evidence of equivalence, superiority, or non-inferiority compared with conventional CABG. Larger, well-adjusted comparative studies with standardized outcomes and long-term follow-up are needed.

title: Heart Failure Beyond Valve Treatment　- Mechanisms, Predictors, and Therapeutic Strategies After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
authorString: Kitahara H, Matsuura K, Kobayashi Y.

journal.title: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society

abstractText: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) has become an established treatment for severe aortic stenosis across the spectrum of surgical risk, substantially improving symptoms and clinical outcomes. However, heart failure (HF) remains a major cause of hospitalization and mortality after TAVR, indicating that relief of valvular stenosis alone may not completely eliminate HF risk. HF after TAVR is multifactorial, reflecting residual cardiac damage and incomplete reverse remodeling, concomitant cardiovascular abnormalities, procedure- and prosthesis-related factors, underlying HF substrate, and systemic comorbidities. Importantly, both the baseline extent of cardiac damage and its persistence after TAVR are associated with adverse outcomes, highlighting the importance of serial assessment beyond procedural success. In addition, many patients undergoing TAVR are elderly and have features of HF with preserved ejection fraction, which may contribute to persistent HF despite successful valve intervention. Emerging evidence, including randomized trial data on sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors, suggests that targeted pharmacological therapy may reduce residual HF risk after TAVR. In this review we summarize the epidemiology, clinical impact, mechanisms, risk stratification, and management of HF after TAVR, and discuss future strategies for its prevention and treatment.

title: The Electrocardiogram as a Preventive Biomarker: From Conventional Risk Markers to Actionable Artificial Intelligence - A Narrative Review.
authorString: Garcia R, Menet A, Duchateau J, Fiorina L, Moufidi A, Taieb J, Lequeux B, Piot O.
abstractText: The electrocardiogram (ECG) is an established tool in cardiovascular prevention, identifying silent arrhythmias, hypertrophy, prior myocardial infarction, conduction disease, and inherited electrical disorders. However, conventional interpretation captures only a fraction of the information embedded in the cardiac electrical signal. Because the ECG is inexpensive, non-invasive, standardized, and already acquired at scale, it provides an attractive substrate for artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled screening and risk stratification. Deep-learning models can identify latent signatures of ventricular dysfunction, structural heart disease, atrial fibrillation, cardiomyopathy, heart failure, and mortality risk. Importantly, evidence is beginning to extend beyond retrospective validation: prospective implementation studies have increased disease detection, while randomized data suggest that AI-ECG-guided clinical alerts may improve outcomes in selected high-risk populations. Whether such benefits extend to preventive populations remains uncertain. This review examines the preventive role of conventional, ambulatory, and wearable ECGs and distinguishes AI applications for detection, prediction, prognostication, treatment selection, and longitudinal monitoring. We argue that performance metrics alone are insufficient. Preventive value requires a defined target population, calibrated and externally validated predictions, an appropriate confirmatory test, a feasible clinical workflow, and an intervention proven to improve outcomes. The most credible near-term applications are those that triage patients to established diagnostic pathways, such as echocardiography or prolonged rhythm monitoring. The central challenge is therefore to transform accurate AI-ECG predictions into actionable, affordable, scalable, safe, and equitable prevention.

title: Zero Iodine Contrast Endovascular Aortic Repair Using Carbon Dioxide Angiography is Associated with Lower Rates of Renal Deterioration: A Multicentre, Prospective, Propensity Matched Study.
authorString: Chisci E, Quaglino S, Colacchio EC, Mezzetto L, Falso R, Simonte G, Gargiulo M, Melani C, Lazzarotto T, Michelagnoli S, Zero Iodine Contrast EVAR Collaborative Study Group.

journal.title: European journal of vascular and endovascular surgery : the official journal of the European Society for Vascular Surgery

abstractText:
Objective

This prospective, multicentre, non-randomised, observational cohort study evaluated the association between a carbon dioxide (CO2) only angiography strategy during endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) and midterm renal outcomes compared with procedures requiring adjunctive iodinated contrast media (ICM).

Methods

Consecutive patients undergoing EVAR with a standardised CO2 only protocol were included. Patients were stratified according to intra-operative contrast use (CO2 only vs. CO2 + ICM). The primary endpoint was renal deterioration, defined as a persistent increase of one or more chronic kidney disease (CKD) stage(s) confirmed on two consecutive follow up assessments. Secondary endpoints included mortality, re-intervention, and aneurysm related outcomes. Propensity score matching (PSM) was performed to adjust for baseline differences. Multivariable regression and time to event analyses were conducted.

Results

Of 291 patients (median age 78 years), 239 (82%) underwent CO2 only EVAR and 52 (18%) required adjunctive ICM. At midterm follow up (up to 24 months; mean follow up 18 months), renal deterioration was less frequent in the CO2 only group than in the CO2 + ICM group (5% vs. 23%; p < .001). Patients treated with CO2 only angiography had a significantly lower serum creatinine and higher estimated glomerular filtration rate at follow up (p < .001 for both). These findings were confirmed after PSM, with renal deterioration occurring in 6% vs. 23% of patients (p = .023). In the matched cohort, CO2 only angiography remained independently associated with lower odds of CKD stage progression (odds ratio 0.14, 95% confidence interval 0.03 - 0.45; p < .001). Thirty day and midterm mortality and endoleak rates were similar between groups, whereas re-interventions were more frequent in the CO2 + ICM group.

Conclusion

A zero iodine contrast, CO2 only angiography strategy during EVAR was associated with a lower rate of renal deterioration. Because patients requiring adjunctive ICM were identified intra-operatively rather than randomly allocated, residual confounding by indication cannot be excluded, despite propensity score matching. These findings support the feasibility of a CO2 first strategy and justify confirmation in randomised studies.

title: Impact of high-intensity foundational medical therapy on outcomes across risk profiles in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.
authorString: Laxmi SR, Chellasamy RT.
abstractText: Heart failure (HF) is a major global health challenge, characterized by high morbidity, mortality, frequent hospitalization, and substantial healthcare costs, despite recent therapeutic advances. In heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF; LVEF < 50%), foundational medical therapy (FMT), as defined in the 2026 European Society of Cardiology (ESC) guidelines-comprising renin-angiotensin system inhibition or angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitors, beta-blockers, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists, and sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors-reduces morbidity and mortality, but its benefit depends on how completely, how quickly, and how intensively these therapies are implemented. This narrative review evaluates whether the benefit of early, comprehensive, high-intensity FMT in HFrEF differs according to specific baseline risk modifiers, drawing on the STRONG-HF trial and its secondary analyses, other randomized evidence, and real-world studies. In STRONG-HF, a high-intensity care strategy that combined rapid up-titration of renin-angiotensin system inhibitors, beta-blockers, and mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists with close post-discharge follow-up reduced the composite of all-cause death or HF readmission at 180 days, driven mainly by fewer HF readmissions; all-cause mortality alone was not significantly reduced, and sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors were not part of the protocolized strategy. Secondary analyses found no significant heterogeneity of this effect across MAGGIC risk tertiles or systolic blood pressure strata, whereas associations between higher attained doses and better outcomes were observational. Meta-analyses of randomized trials additionally support early initiation of mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists and sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors after decompensation. Prognostic scores, physiological parameters, and treatment-exposure measures are treated as distinct constructs rather than as an interchangeable single risk category. The review also addresses tools for risk prognostication, the boundary between FMT optimization and evaluation for mechanical circulatory support in advanced HF, and the real-world barriers to implementation, including patient comorbidity, therapeutic inertia, health-system constraints, and cost. Available evidence supports early initiation and structured optimization of FMT in appropriately selected HFrEF patients, with no convincing evidence that higher baseline risk alone justifies therapeutic inertia; however, the independent contributions of treatment completeness, dose intensity, and monitoring intensity, the optimal sequencing, and individualized dose targets remain uncertain, particularly in very high-risk and underrepresented populations, and warrant further prospective study.

title: Supra-Inguinal Fascia Iliaca Block Versus Iliohypogastric-Ilioinguinal Block During Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation (TAVI) Under Conscious Sedation: A Patient- and Outcome Assessor-Blinded Randomized Trial.
authorString: Besatrous JNN, Haggag AM, Daniel SH, Shabayek MI.
abstractText:
Background

Transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TF-TAVI) is increasingly performed under conscious sedation (CS), yet optimal analgesia for femoral access remains debated. Regional anesthesia techniques such as the supra-inguinal fascia iliaca block (SIFIB) and iliohypogastric-ilioinguinal block (II-IHB) may offer improved analgesia compared with conventional local infiltration.

Aim

To compare SIFIB and II-IH block in enhancing CS quality during TF-TAVI, focusing on analgesic requirements, patient and surgeon satisfaction, and conversion to GA.

Methods

This patient- and outcome assessor-blinded randomized controlled trial included 45 patients scheduled for transfemoral TAVI, allocated equally to SIFIB, II-IHB, or control (local infiltration). All procedures were performed under standardized CS with dexmedetomidine. Primary outcomes were rescue analgesia and conversion to general anesthesia. Secondary outcomes included pain and sedation scores, hemodynamic and respiratory variables, pacing, vascular complications, and hospital stay.

Results

Rescue analgesia was required in 33.3%, 46.7%, and 40.0% of patients in the SIFIB, IIIHB, and control groups, respectively (p = 0.927); fentanyl consumption was comparable (p = 0.525). Conversion to general anesthesia occurred in 0%, 13.3%, and 26.7%, respectively (p = 0.141). Both blocks reduced intraoperative pain versus control (SIFIB, p < 0.001; IIIHB, p < 0.001) and were associated with lower intraoperative heart rate (p = 0.005 and p = 0.015, respectively). Postoperative pain, mean arterial pressure, oxygen saturation, pacing, and vascular complications did not differ significantly. Hospital stay was shorter after SIFIB than after IIIHB (p = 0.019) or local infiltration (p = 0.004).

Conclusion

No statistically significant between-group differences were found in the primary outcomes of rescue analgesia or conversion to general anesthesia. Both regional blocks reduced intraoperative pain scores compared with local infiltration. SIFIB was associated with a shorter hospital stay; however, this secondary finding is exploratory and requires confirmation in larger studies. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT06911463.

title: Predictors and Mid-Term Outcomes of Vascular Complications After Large-Bore Plug-Based Access-Site Closure in Patients Undergoing Transfemoral TAVI: A CHOICE-CLOSURE Substudy.
authorString: Roeßler A, Dumpies O, Hartung P, Loria JRD, Richter I, Lankisch N, Feistritzer HJ, Majunke N, Kiefer P, Noack T, Desch S, Thiele H, Abdel-Wahab M.

journal.title: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions

abstractText:
Background

The plug-based MANTA (Teleflex, Pennsylvania, USA) vascular closure device (VCD) is an alternative to suture-based VCDs for large-bore arterial closure after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), but has been associated with higher rates of vascular complications. Predictors and outcomes of these complications are not well-analyzed, especially regarding the self-resorbing characteristics of the MANTA VCD.

Objectives

To identify predictors of access-site related vascular complications following transfemoral TAVI with the MANTA VCD, and to assess mid-term outcomes and late-onset events (after 30 days) in affected patients.

Methods

This prospective substudy of the CHOICE-CLOSURE trial included all patients randomized to vascular closure with the MANTA VCD at the Leipzig Heart Center. Patients with vascular complications, defined according to the Valve Academic Research Consortium (VARC)-2 criteria, underwent additional clinical and ultrasound follow-up, at least 6 months after the index procedure. Predictors of vascular complications were assessed through multivariable analysis.

Results

Of 237 patients treated with the MANTA VCD, 46 (19.4%) had an access-site related vascular complication. Pre-procedural dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) was the only independent predictor in multivariable analysis (Odds ratio 4.27, 95% confidence interval 1.58-11.59, p = 0.004). At a mean follow-up of 13.5 months, no new vascular complications occurred.
