Patients with an over-stented MANTA VCD (n = 5) had no in-stent stenosis, and stent diameters further expanded by 12.5% to 20.0%.

Conclusion

Pre-procedural DAPT independently predicted vascular complications after TAVI in MANTA patients. Patients with vascular complications had no further access-site late-onset events, and endovascular stenting of a MANTA VCD appeared safe.

title: Goodbye to randomized controlled trials on mechanical circulatory support.
authorString: Otterspoor LC, Donker DW.

title: Hemoglobin levels and early dynamics in cardiogenic shock: prognostic insights from the Altshock-2 registry.
authorString: Bertaina M, Pagnesi M, Tavazzi G, Frea S, Viola G, Maj G, Dini CS, Belfioretti L, Briani M, Trombara F, Ravera A, Sabatino M, Merello G, Riccardi M, Cesari A, Guarnieri G, Villanova L, Boretto P, Gravinese C, Colombo CNJ, Camporotondo R, De Luca L, Cucchi D, Valente S, Marini M, Metra M, Pappalardo F, Sacco A, Altshock-2 registry investigators.
abstractText: Anemia is common in cardiogenic shock and may further impair oxygen delivery in a setting of reduced cardiac output. However, its prognostic role across cardiogenic shock etiologies and the relevance of early hemoglobin (Hb) changes remain uncertain. This analysis included 817 patients enrolled between March 2020 and November 2024 in the prospective multicenter Altshock-2 registry. Anemia was defined using WHO sex-specific criteria, and admission Hb was categorized into tertiles. The primary endpoint was in-hospital mortality. Associations of admission and 24-h Hb with mortality were evaluated using logistic regression adjusted for demographics, comorbidities, and cardiogenic shock etiology (model A) or metabolic and hemodynamic severity (model B). Anemia was present in 415 patients (50.8%) at admission and in 533 (67%) at 24 h. In-hospital mortality decreased across increasing admission Hb tertiles (44.2, 29.3, and 21.5% in T1, T2, and T3, respectively; P < 0.001). Admission Hb was inversely associated with primary endpoint in both model A [adjusted odds ratio (aOR) per 1 g/dl increase 0.87; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.80-0.93; P < 0.001] and model B (aOR 0.87; 95% CI 0.81-0.93; P < 0.001). After accounting for admission Hb, 24-h Hb was not independently associated with the primary endpoint and did not improve model fit (likelihood-ratio P = 0.264 and P = 0.577 for models A and B) nor discrimination (ΔAUC = 0.001 and -0.001, respectively). There was no statistical evidence of effect modification by cardiogenic shock etiology or sex. Lower admission Hb was independently associated with increased in-hospital mortality. In contrast, 24-h Hb provided no incremental prognostic information beyond admission Hb. Admission Hb may therefore contribute to multidimensional risk assessment in patients with cardiogenic shock.

title: Pulmonary Artery Pressures Predict Heart Failure Events Following Heart Failure and Non-Heart Failure Events.
authorString: Lindenfeld J, Costanzo MR, Ducharme A, Desai AS, Mehra MR, Zughaib ME, Horstmanshof DA, Chien CV, Maisel A, Sears SF, Smart FW, Johnson NN, Henderson JD, Lee FS, Zile MR, GUIDE-HF Investigators.
abstractText: It is uncertain whether pulmonary artery pressure (PAP) within the first week after either hospitalization for a non-heart failure event (HFE) or hospitalization or urgent visit for a HFE predicts the risk of recurring events. This study aims to determine if PAP following a non-HFE or HFE predicts subsequent events within 90 days. The authors examined non-HFE and HFE in patients with heart failure (HF) treated with remote hemodynamic-guided management using a wireless PAP sensor in the GUIDE-HF study. They compared PAP trends before and after a non-HFE or HFE and stratified the admitting and discharge PAP during the index event into groups with a subsequent HFE, non-HFE, or no further events within 90 days. Following index non-HFE (615 events, n = 425), post-discharge diastolic PAP was significantly higher in patients with a subsequent HFE (23.3 ± 7.9 mm Hg) (n = 97) vs patients with a subsequent non-HFE (20.4 ± 7.3 mm Hg; P = 0.0046) (n = 189) or no further events (20.9 ± 7.4 mm Hg; P = 0.015) (n = 329). Following index HFE (539 events, n = 358), post-discharge diastolic PAP was numerically higher in patients with a subsequent HFE (23.9 ± 6.9 mm Hg) (n = 199) than in patients with a subsequent non-HFE (22.0 ± 7.1 mm Hg; P = 0.078 (n = 102) and in those with no further events (22.0 ± 7.6 mm Hg; P = 0.021) (n = 238). Similar trends were observed for HF with reduced ejection fraction and HF with preserved ejection fraction subgroups and with systolic and mean PAP. Persistently elevated PAP early after discharge following either an index non-HFE or an HFE is associated with the risk of a subsequent HFE. (Hemodynamic-GUIDEd Management of Heart Failure [GUIDE-HF]; NCT03387813).

title: Lipoprotein(a) and incident peripheral artery disease in the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities Study.
authorString: Lema K, Stapp EK, Kou M, Ballew SH, Ding N, Hoogeveen RC, Ballantyne CM, Salameh MJ, Matsushita K, Power MC.
abstractText:
Background and aims

Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is an atherogenic, prothrombotic lipoprotein linked to atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, but prospective data on its association with peripheral artery disease (PAD) in large, diverse U.S. cohorts are limited. We characterized the association of Lp(a) with long-term incident PAD risk in a diverse, community-based U.S.

Cohort

Methods

We included Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities (ARIC) Study participants attending Visit 4 (1996-98) with measured Lp(a) and no prevalent PAD. Lp(a) was natural logarithm (ln)-transformed and categorized as <30, 30-50, and >50 mg/dL. Incident PAD was identified from hospitalization and procedure codes through 2019. Hazard ratios (HRs) were estimated using Cox models adjusted for confounders; Fine-Gray models and cumulative incidence functions accounted for competing mortality.

Results

Among 9727 participants (mean age 63.1 years, 53.9% women, 20.4% Black), 825 incident PAD events occurred over a median 22.5 years of follow-up. Lp(a) was <30 mg/dL in 69.7%, 30-50 in 11.7%, and >50 in 18.6%. Fully adjusted HRs were 1.27 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.03-1.57) for 30-50 mg/dL and 1.32 (95% CI, 1.11-1.57) for >50 mg/dL versus <30 mg/dL; each unit increase in ln(Lp(a)) was associated with an HR of 1.14 (95% CI, 1.07-1.20). Estimates were similar accounting for competing mortality, and cumulative incidence differed across categories (p < 0.001). The association did not differ by baseline statin use.

Conclusions

Higher Lp(a) was independently associated with greater long-term PAD risk in a community-based cohort, supporting Lp(a) as a risk factor for lower-extremity atherosclerotic disease and its value for risk stratification.

title: Right ventricular apical hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with asymmetric left ventricular septal involvement decades after heart transplant: a case report.
authorString: Wilbur A, Sinha A, Catania R, Lin A, Tibrewala A.
abstractText:
Background

Long-term heart transplant (HT) survivors are an expanding population at risk for late, underrecognized complications. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy developing in the cardiac allograft is exceptionally rare, and right ventricular involvement complicates risk stratification for sudden cardiac death.

Case summary

A 30-year-old woman who underwent heart transplantation at 5 weeks for hypoplastic left heart syndrome was found to have right ventricular apical hypertrophy on surveillance transthoracic echocardiography. Sixteen months later, echocardiography demonstrated worsening right ventricular apical hypertrophy and new asymmetric left ventricular septal hypertrophy, without outflow tract obstruction. Cardiac magnetic resonance confirmed right ventricular apical hypertrophy (22 mm) extending into asymmetric septal hypertrophy (15 mm) with patchy late gadolinium enhancement involving approximately 30% of the myocardial mass, consistent with right ventricular apical variant hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with asymmetric left ventricular septal involvement. She remained asymptomatic. Given the extensive late gadolinium enhancement burden, a subcutaneous implantable cardioverter-defibrillator was placed for primary prevention of sudden cardiac death. She remains asymptomatic 16 months later with no device-detected arrhythmias.

Discussion

To our knowledge, this is the first report of right ventricular apical hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with left ventricular septal involvement in a HT recipient. Cardiac magnetic resonance characterized structurally significant but clinically silent disease, supporting a lower threshold for its use when surveillance echocardiography is abnormal after transplantation. Extensive late gadolinium enhancement in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy involving the right ventricle may warrant greater weight in sudden cardiac death risk stratification than current guidelines specify.

title: Echocardiographic Left Atrial Stiffness Index as a Predictor of All-Cause Mortality in Non-Ischemic Dilated Cardiomyopathy.
authorString: Sánchez-Sánchez I, Olmos C, Zulet P, Moreira IM, Gil-Abizanda S, Blázquez N, Restrepo A, Alberto de Agustín J, Islas F.

journal.title: Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography : official publication of the American Society of Echocardiography

abstractText:
Aims

Reliable predictors of adverse outcomes in non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy (NIDCM) remain limited. We aimed to evaluate the association between the left atrial stiffness index (LASI) and all-cause mortality in patients with NIDCM and to assess its prognostic value beyond established left atrial and diastolic markers.

Methods

Retrospective analysis of a prospectively recruited cohort of patients diagnosed with NIDCM between 2018 and 2022. All patients underwent comprehensive transthoracic echocardiography at the time of diagnosis. Left atrial (LA) strain was measured retrospectively from stored baseline echocardiograms using two-dimensional speckle-tracking analysis, and LASI was calculated as the ratio of E/e' to LA reservoir strain. Multivariable analyses were performed to identify variables independently associated with all-cause mortality.

Results

Among 200 patients (mean age 61.7 years; 40% women), 33 (16.5%) died over a median follow-up of 43.8 months. In multivariable Cox regression analysis, variables independently associated with all-cause mortality were LASI (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 1.92, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.33-2.77), age (HR 1.05, 95% CI 1.02-1.08) and right ventricular-pulmonary artery (RV-PA) coupling index (HR 0.25, 95% CI 0.07-0.89); the model showed good discrimination (optimism-corrected C-index 0.766). LASI remained independently associated with mortality when modeled together with left atrial volume index (LAVi) and with E/e'.

Conclusion

In NIDCM, LASI provides prognostic information for all-cause mortality beyond other morphological and functional LA markers. Given the single-center design and the limited number of events, these findings warrant external validation.

title: Association between Physical Function and Incidence of Atrial Fibrillation: The Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities (ARIC) Study.
authorString: Pae BJ, Li L, Wood K, Soliman EZ, Chen LY, Norby FL, Windham BG, Alonso A.
abstractText:
Background

Poor physical function is linked to higher cardiovascular disease risk, but its association with atrial fibrillation (AF) remains understudied. Investigating this relationship could highlight a novel target for AF prevention.

Methods

4,803 participants without AF from the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities (ARIC) Study cohort assessed in 2011-2013 were studied. Physical function was measured using Short Physical Performance Battery (SPPB), 4-meter walk time, and grip strength. Hospital discharge codes and death certificates ascertained incident AF through 2022 (through 2020 for Jackson participants). Cox regression assessed the association between physical function and incident AF risk, adjusting for multiple covariates. Z-score transformations identified the measure most strongly associated with incident AF risk, and SPPB component analysis identified the most influential SPPB component.

Results

Mean age of study participants was 75.1 ± 5.0 years (41.2% male, 22.2% black). During a median follow-up of 9.2 years, 809 incident AF events occurred. SPPB (HR: 0.93, 95% CI: 0.90-0.96, per 1-point increase) and grip strength (HR: 0.87, 95% CI: 0.78-0.96, per 10kg increase) were inversely associated with incident AF risk, while 4-meter walk time (HR: 1.08, 95% CI: 1.03-1.13, per 1-second increase) was positively associated with incident AF risk. SPPB had the strongest association with incident AF risk. Within SPPB, only the chair stand component was significantly associated with incident AF risk.

Conclusions

Better physical function is associated with reduced incident AF risk, with SPPB showing the strongest association. Given the modifiable nature of physical function, these findings highlight a potential novel target for AF prevention in aging populations.

title: Clonal hematopoiesis and cardiovascular immunological memory: From epigenetically reprogrammed hematopoiesis to precision cardiovascular immunology.
authorString: Zhao X, Guan X, Wang X, Yu Y, Zhang C.
abstractText: Clonal hematopoiesis is an age-related condition characterized by somatic mutations in hematopoietic stem cells and progenitor cells, resulting in an imbalance in the production of circulating blood cells, but not meeting the diagnostic criteria for hematological malignancies. Initially regarded as a precursor state of a myeloid tumor, it has now been confirmed as an important regulator of cardiovascular disease risk. The strongest evidence pertains to atherosclerotic cardiovascular diseases, but there are also reports indicating its association with heart failure, atrial fibrillation, ischemic stroke, and thrombotic complications. Current research increasingly suggests that the mechanisms linking hematopoietic clonality to cardiovascular damage include inflammatory bone marrow hematopoiesis, alterations in the innate immune signaling pathways, activation of inflammasomes, interactions between platelets and neutrophils, and abnormal tissue remodeling. This review explores the role of innate immune reprogramming related to clonal hematopoiesis in cardiovascular diseases. Clonal hematopoiesis and trained immunity are related but distinct phenomena: clonal hematopoiesis originates from somatic mutations and clonal selection, while trained immunity refers to the continuous functional reprogramming of innate immune cells and their precursor cells. The potential fusion of these two factors may affect the generation of bone marrow cells in subsequent stress states, inflammatory responses, and interactions with cardiovascular tissues. This article focuses on three mechanism axes. Firstly, experimental models have confirmed that TET2 mutations are related to the hematopoietic process and can activate inflammasomes and the IL-1β signaling pathway. Secondly, DNMT3A mutations may affect hematopoietic function and bone marrow cell function through different epigenetic programs, although their impact on the cardiovascular system is not yet fully clear. Thirdly, the hematopoietic process related to JAK2V617F may be involved in the interaction between platelets and neutrophils, as well as the thrombotic-inflammatory process. Finally, we explore how the type of driver mutation, variant allele frequency (VAF), clonal dynamics, inflammatory activity, and cardiovascular phenotype can provide guidance for precise cardiovascular research. This comprehensive framework is currently still a mechanistic hypothesis that requires further validation, rather than an established clinical diagnosis.

title: Incidence of Pacing-Induced Cardiomyopathy in Active-Fixation Leadless Pacemakers.
authorString: Kopreski C, John K, Huang J, Karimianpour A, Deering T, Sotolongo A, Hoosien M, El-Chami M, Bhimani A, Nilsson KR.
abstractText:
Introduction

Pacing-induced cardiomyopathy (PICM) is a known complication of high right ventricular (RV) pacing burden with transvenous pacemakers, but its incidence with active-fixation leadless pacemakers (LPs) is unknown. This study's aim was to determine the incidence of PICM among patients implanted with LPs using helix-based active fixation and assess its association with heart failure hospitalizations (HFH).

Methods and results

This multi-center retrospective cohort study included patients implanted with active-fixation LPs between 2021 and 2025. Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) measurements were obtained pre- and post-implant. Inclusion criteria were: de novo pacemaker implant, ≥ 20% RV pacing burden, baseline LVEF of > 50%, and > 30 days of follow-up. PICM was defined as a ≥ 10% reduction in LVEF from baseline to a value < 50%, with no other identifiable causes for left ventricular dysfunction. Patient demographics, comorbidities, procedural history, and baseline pacemaker, electrocardiographic, and echocardiographic data were compared between patients with and without PICM. Categorical variables were analyzed using the "N-1" Chi-squared or Fisher's exact test and continuous variables with Welch's t-test. Cox proportional hazards models were used for univariate analysis of PICM and HFH. Among 164 patients implanted with active-fixation LPs, 57 met inclusion criteria (mean age 78 ± 11 years). Dual-chamber systems accounted for 47.4% of implants, and 96.5% of ventricular devices were placed in the low RV septum. Six patients (10.5%) developed PICM during 14.2 ± 10.9 months of follow-up, with a mean time to onset of 7.5 ± 2.4 months. Baseline characteristics did not differ significantly between patients with and without PICM. At the time of diagnosis, those with PICM had a greater decline in LVEF (23% vs. 2%, p < 0.001). Although RV pacing burden was higher in PICM patients (88.8% vs. 76.6%), this difference was not statistically significant. PICM was a strong predictor of HFH (HR: 6.9, p = 0.007).

Conclusion

PICM occurred in 10.5% of patients receiving active-fixation LPs with high ventricular pacing burden. Our findings highlight the importance of standardized follow-up echocardiography within the first year post-implant to improve surveillance and timely recognition of PICM.

title: Mortality and inpatient hospitalizations by anti-plasma cell dyscrasia treatment patterns among patients with cardiac light chain amyloidosis: results from a US administrative claims database.
authorString: Thompson J, Chow C, Catini J.
abstractText: Aim: To gain insights into real-world mortality and hospitalization among newly diagnosed patients with light chain (AL) amyloidosis initiating anti-plasma cell dyscrasia treatment. Materials & methods: This retrospective, noninterventional, observational study evaluated real-world mortality by treatment patterns and hospitalization among adult patients newly diagnosed with AL amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy in the US IQVIA PharMetrics claims database. Data from treatment initiation (index date) to 365 days postindex were evaluated. Patients receiving treatments for AL amyloidosis in the year prior to the index date were excluded. AL-, cardiac-, and cardiac/renal-related healthcare resource utilization were assigned using the International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision. Summary statistics are reported by cardiac or cardiac/renal involvement. Results: A total of 198 patients with cardiac AL amyloidosis were included in this study (mean age, 64.8 years; 70.7% male). The 1-year mortality and condition-related hospitalization rates among all patients were 9.1% (18 of 198) and 65.7% (130 of 198), respectively. Daratumumab was prescribed for 138 (69.7%) patients, with 1-year mortality and condition-related hospitalization rates of 7.2% (10 of 138) and 67.4% (93 of 138), respectively. Daratumumab was not prescribed for 60 (30.3%) patients, with 1-year mortality and condition-related hospitalization rates of 13.3% (8 of 60) and 61.7% (37 of 60), respectively. One-year mortality and condition-related hospitalization rates among patients with only cardiac involvement (n = 66) were 7.6% (5 of 66) and 45.5% (30 of 66), respectively, and 9.8% (13 of 132) and 75.8% (100 of 132), respectively, among patients with cardiac and renal involvement (n = 132). Conclusion: Treatment patterns varied considerably among patients with AL amyloidosis. Mortality and hospitalizations were higher among patients with both cardiac and renal involvement than among those with only cardiac involvement.

title: Real-world safety profiles of newer antiseizure medications: A pharmacovigilance study based on FDA Adverse Event Reporting System database.
authorString: He Z, Li T, Chang Y, Liu Y, Song M, Zou Y, Xu C, Yang X, Li B, Fang F.

journal.title: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape

abstractText:
Objective

This study aimed to systematically evaluate and compare the post-marketing safety of four newer antiseizure medications (ASMs)-brivaracetam (BRV), cannabidiol (CBD), cenobamate (CNB), and fenfluramine (FFA).

Methods

A pharmacovigilance study was conducted using data from the FAERS database (Q1 2016-Q4 2024). Disproportionality analyses were performed to detect adverse event (AE) signals using three algorithms. Subgroup analyses were stratified by age, sex, reporter, and treatment strategy. We employed multivariable logistic regression, adjusted for covariates including age, sex, weight, dose, and concomitant medications, to validate associations between ASMs and specific AEs and to identify potential influencing factors. Bayesian network analysis was conducted to explore conditional dependencies among variables. Hospitalization risk was evaluated based on system organ classes.

Results

After data cleaning, 13 763 reports were included. We identified 308 positive preferred term (PT) signals. Seizure-related AEs were frequently reported. All four ASMs had the PT of seizure cluster, with each exhibiting distinct AE profiles: BRV with psychiatric disorders, CBD with gastrointestinal events, CNB with visual dysfunction, and FFA with valvular heart disease (VHD). Children had higher reporting odds of seizure with BRV and CBD, while reporting odds of FFA-related VHD were lower in children; polytherapy was associated with higher reporting odds of somnolence, and AE reporting patterns varied by reporter source. Both CBD-related gastrointestinal events and FFA-related cardiac events exhibited dose-dependent effects. Infection-related AEs were associated with higher odds of hospitalization for multiple ASMs.

Significance

This study comprehensively characterizes the safety profiles of newer ASMs and highlights the importance of tailored AE monitoring based on specific ASM and patient characteristics.

title: Body composition and mortality across the reproductive cycle: findings from the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis.
authorString: Liang I, Flynn S, Watson K, Horwich T, Karlamangla A, Srikanthan P.
abstractText:
Objective

There are greater changes in body composition during the menopause transition than at other stages in a woman's reproductive cycle. We studied fat mass (FM) and fat-free mass (FFM) in participants at different reproductive stages at the beginning of the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA) and evaluated their association with major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and total mortality.

Methods

In 3,439 women from MESA, equations to determine FM and FFM were derived from bioelectrical impedance analysis performed at exam 5 and applied to exam 1. Women were divided into three groups: reproductive phase (before final menstrual period [FMP]), menopause phase (FMP to 2 years subsequently), and late menopause phase (>2 years after FMP). Adjusted Cox multivariate models evaluated the association between FM, FFM, anthropometric measures, and MACE/total mortality.

Results

In the full cohort, higher FM was significantly associated with increased MACE (HR per kg, 95% CI: 1.03 [1.01-1.05]) and mortality (1.03 [1.01-1.05]), while higher FFM was associated with lower mortality (0.96 [0.93-1.00]). In the menopause phase, FM and FFM showed clinically significant associations with total mortality (FM 1.18 [1.02-1.38]; FFM 0.71 [0.50-1.00]). These associations were not observed in women aged 48-52 years old.

Conclusion

Higher FM is associated with a higher risk of MACE/total mortality, whereas higher FFM is associated with a lower risk of total mortality. Associations noted in women in the menopause phase but not among similarly aged women suggest ovarian aging may influence these relationships.

title: Prevalence and clinical correlates of elevated high-sensitivity C-reactive protein in patients presenting with acute coronary syndrome: a single-center retrospective study.
authorString: Tsiamis N, Afendoulis D, Kotoulas SC, Tountas C, Romiou A, Zacharakis D, Kole C, Michailidi E, Tsalamandris S, Kakkavas A, Kartalis A, Kitsiou A, Toutouzas K.
abstractText:
Background

High-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP) reflects systemic inflammation. The frequency of hsCRP >2 mg/L, a threshold used in anti-inflammatory trials, among patients presenting with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) is incompletely characterized.

Methods

We retrospectively analyzed consecutive patients presenting with ACS at Sismanoglio General Hospital of Athens between January 2023 and May 2024 who had hsCRP measured on arrival. We assessed the frequency and magnitude of hsCRP elevation, clinical and laboratory associations, and factors associated with hsCRP >2 mg/L after adjustment for age.

Results

Of 103 patients, 93 (90.3%) had hsCRP measured and were included (median age: 65 years; interquartile range: 58-73; 84.9% male). Elevated hsCRP (>2 mg/L) occurred in 67.7%, and 25.8% had hsCRP >10 mg/L. Median hsCRP was 3.8 mg/L (interquartile range: 1.3-10.2), without a significant difference between ST-segment elevation and non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction presentations (3.2 vs. 6.0 mg/L; P = 0.15). After mutual adjustment and adjustment for age, diabetes (adjusted odds ratio: 4.46; 95% confidence interval: 1.40-14.15; P = 0.011) and current smoking (adjusted odds ratio: 4.74; 95% confidence interval: 1.65-13.59; P = 0.004) remained associated with elevated hsCRP.

Conclusions

Two-thirds of patients had hsCRP >2 mg/L at ACS presentation. Diabetes and smoking were independently associated with elevation. These findings quantify the proportion meeting an inflammatory trial entry criterion but do not establish persistent inflammation or support anti-inflammatory treatment. Prospective studies with serial measurements and clinical outcomes are needed to determine whether elevation persists and identifies modifiable risk.

title: Electrophysiological Markers in Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: Enhancing Sudden Cardiac Death Risk Prediction with Index of Cardiac Electrophysiological Balance and Its Corrected Variant.
authorString: Balaban İ, Tanyeri S, Karaduman A, Kültürsay B, Gültekin Güner E, Keten MF, Efe SÇ, Alizade E.
abstractText:
Background

Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is characterized by asymmetric left ventricular hypertrophy and myocardial fibrosis, which significantly increases the risk of sudden cardiac death (SCD). Existing risk stratification models are limited in predicting SCD risk in patients within the "gray zone"-those with intermediate risk. This study investigates the prognostic utility of the Index of Cardiac Electrophysiological Balance (ICEB) and its corrected variant (ICEBc) in predicting ventricular arrhythmias (VAs) in HCM. To evaluate the predictive value of ICEB and ICEBc for Life-Threatening Arrhythmias (LTA) and non-sustained ventricular tachycardia (NSVT) in HCM and compare their performance with traditional repolarization parameters and the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) SCD Risk Score.

Methods

A retrospective observational study was conducted at a single center, including 127 HCM patients categorized into 3 groups: LTA (n = 45), NSVT (n = 29), and control (n = 53). Electrocardiographic parameters, including ICEB, ICEBc, Tp-e interval, Tp-e/QTc ratio, and QRS-T angle were measured. Multiple logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analyses were performed to identify independent predictors of VAs.

Results

The ICEB and ICEBc were significantly lower in LTA and NSVT groups compared to the control group (P < .001), indicating increased arrhythmogenic risk. The ROC curve analysis showed that ICEB and ICEBc had superior predictive power for LTA and NSVT compared to traditional markers and the ESC SCD Risk Score, with the highest area under the curve (AUC) for the Base + ICEB Model (AUC = 0.79).

Conclusion

The ICEB and ICEBc are robust markers of repolarization heterogeneity and effective predictors of VAs in HCM patients. Their integration into existing risk stratification models could enhance predictive accuracy, particularly for gray zone patients.

title: Digital Necrosis as an Initial Manifestation of a Myeloproliferative Neoplasm.
authorString: He AQ, Waitt T, Hernandez NS, Lombana N, Broderick MT, Czerwinski WL.

journal.title: Plastic and reconstructive surgery. Global open

abstractText: Digital necrosis is a clinical presentation of the hand, which may indicate an underlying systemic condition. We report a 76-year-old woman who presented to the hospital with left ring fingertip digital necrosis. Despite prior blunt trauma, significant laboratory abnormalities suggested potential for alternative underlying causes. Inpatient care consisted of allopurinol, intravenous fluids, and broad-spectrum antibiotics. The region of dry gangrene eventually fully declared and autoamputated during outpatient workup. Two months later, the patient presented to the emergency department with idiopathic leukocytosis and was diagnosed with a JAK2 V617F myeloproliferative neoplasm via peripheral blood smear. Unfortunately, the patient died 2 weeks later due to hemorrhagic conversion of an ischemic stroke. Earlier consideration of underlying malignancy may be crucial in prompting appropriate treatment measures in patients presenting with unexplained digital necrosis.

title: Operative management and outcomes of symptomatic carotid near occlusions stenosis.
authorString: Dimov A, Toma A, Kletzer J, Niesen WD, Kreibich M, El Mokhtari Y, Czerny M, Kondov S.
abstractText:
Objective

To present the outcomes of carotid endarterectomy (CEA) in patients with symptomatic carotid near-occlusion (CNO) and to compare these outcomes with those of patients with symptomatic non-CNO carotid stenosis.

Methods

This retrospective analysis included patients who underwent CEA of the internal carotid artery between January 2011 and December 2025. Outcomes in patients with symptomatic CNO were compared with those in patients with symptomatic non-CNO using propensity score matching on sex, age, amaurosis fugax, hyperlipidaemia, emergency status, and shunt as matching covariates. The primary endpoint was perioperative stroke, defined as a stroke occurring within 30 days after surgery. Secondary endpoints were cranial nerve injury, cerebral hyperperfusion syndrome, myocardial injury after non-cardiac surgery, surgical revision, bleeding complications, reintubation, and in-hospital mortality.

Results

In the unmatched cohort, 1,321 patients underwent carotid endarterectomy (CEA), of whom 85 (6.4%) presented with symptomatic CNO. After propensity score matching (2:1), 255 patients were analysed, comprising 85 with symptomatic CNO and 170 matched controls with symptomatic non-CNO stenosis. Baseline and operative characteristics were well balanced. The perioperative stroke rate was similar between patients with symptomatic CNO and those with symptomatic non-CNO stenosis (1.2% vs. 2.4%). No significant differences were observed in myocardial injury (2.4% vs. 2.4%, p>0.9), cerebral hyperperfusion syndrome (13% vs. 14%, p>0.9), cranial nerve injury (5.9% vs. 4.1%, p=0.5), surgical revision (7.1% vs. 5.9%, p=0.7), or postoperative bleeding (5.9% vs. 5.3%, p>0.9).

Conclusion

Carotid endarterectomy using the eversion technique appears feasible and can be performed with an acceptable perioperative complication rate in selected patients with symptomatic carotid near-occlusion. Although no statistically significant differences in perioperative outcomes were observed compared with patients undergoing CEA for conventional symptomatic carotid stenosis, the limited sample size and low event rates preclude conclusions about equivalence. Further studies with larger cohorts and long-term neurological follow-up are warranted to establish the clinical benefit of surgical revascularisation in this patient population.

title: TAVI versus SAVR in adults with bicuspid aortic valve and heart failure.
authorString: Mortada I, Lee AW, Ebel G, Long N, Buckingham D, Boyars MC, Blackwell TA, Jneid H.
abstractText:
Background

The optimal valve replacement strategy for adults with bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) and heart failure remains uncertain. We compared outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) versus surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR).

Methods

Using the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network, we identified adults with BAV and heart failure diagnoses during 2020-2024 who underwent TAVI or SAVR. Patients with endocarditis, heart transplant, ventricular assist devices, concomitant non-aortic valve surgery, or coronary artery bypass grafting were excluded. Propensity score matching incorporated demographics, comorbidities, medications, and clinical measurements. All-cause mortality was the primary outcome; secondary outcomes included acute myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke, and all-cause hospitalization. Outcomes were assessed over 2 years using Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional hazards analyses. Hernia and upper respiratory infection served as prespecified falsification endpoints.

Results

Propensity score matching yielded 383 patients per group, with a mean age of 65.7 years. Mortality occurred in 22 TAVI patients (5.7%) and 14 SAVR patients (3.7%; HR 1.57, 95% CI 0.80-3.07). No statistically significant differences were detected in mortality, acute myocardial infarction (HR 1.34, 95% CI 0.84-2.14), ischemic stroke (HR 1.11, 95% CI 0.67-1.83), or all-cause hospitalization (HR 0.93, 95% CI 0.79-1.10). Falsification endpoints did not differ significantly. Left ventricular ejection fraction was recorded in 27.4% of matched TAVI patients and 26.4% of matched SAVR patients.

Conclusion

The imprecise mortality estimate did not exclude clinically important harm associated with TAVI. These observational findings are hypothesis-generating and do not establish equivalence or noninferiority.

title: Survival and Aortic Reintervention Following Hemiarch vs. Extended Arch for Acute Type A Dissection in Patients Over Age 65.
authorString: Spratt JR, Beaver TM, Jacobs JP, Cameron D, Arnaoutakis GJ, Desai ND, Atshan R, Chang SC, Preventza O, Habib RH, Martin TD.
abstractText:
Background

Although ascending hemiarch replacement is considered standard, some have advocated extended arch reconstruction as the preferred strategy in acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD). Patients aged ≥65 years have increasing competing risk of non-aortic death, potentially undermining the late benefits of extended arch for ATAAD. The impact of hemiarch vs extended arch for ATAAD on long-term survival and aortic reintervention in this population is examined.

Methods

Patients aged ≥65 years undergoing non-elective hemiarch or extended arch for ATAAD in the Society of Thoracic Surgeons Adult Cardiac Surgery Database with Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services linkage (July 2017-2023,N=3,562;2,442[68.6%] hemiarch;1,120[31.4%] extended arch) were compared. Primary endpoints were long-term mortality and aortic reintervention beyond 30 days and were analyzed by Kaplan-Meier and cumulative incidence functions, followed by multivariable regressions.

Results

Hemiarch patients tended to be slightly older (73.8±6.1vs.73.1±5.9 years), female (46.6%vs.39.6%), and hyperacute ATAAD (80.1%vs74.7%). Malperfusion was more frequent in extended arch (27.8% vs 20.6%). Extended arch patients had: i) longer cardiopulmonary bypass, cross-clamp, and circulatory arrest times and ii) more frequent antegrade and/or retrograde cerebral perfusion. Short-term outcomes and rates of concomitant procedures were similar between groups. Risk-adjusted analysis showed no treatment effects for survival, aortic reintervention, operative mortality, and stroke.

Conclusions

Extended arch for treatment of ATAAD in patients aged ≥65 years was not associated with improved mortality or aortic reintervention compared to hemiarch at intermediate followup. Absent patient-specific indications, hemiarch may be sufficient in patients aged ≥65 years with ATAAD.

title: Continuous Kidney Replacement Therapy in Patients Requiring Mechanical Circulatory Support: A Practical Review.
authorString: Teixeira JP, Neyra JA, Tolwani AJ, Wille KM.

journal.title: American journal of kidney diseases : the official journal of the National Kidney Foundation

abstractText: Mechanical circulatory support (MCS) devices, including intra-aortic balloon pumps, micro-axial flow pumps, venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, and ventricular assist devices, have become increasingly common in managing advanced heart failure and cardiogenic shock. Acute kidney injury (AKI) occurs in up to 85% of MCS patients, with 30-45% treated with kidney replacement therapy (KRT). Continuous KRT (CKRT) is generally preferred in this population due to superior hemodynamic tolerability and precise volume control. However, providing CKRT to MCS patients presents unique challenges, including securing a functional vascular access, circuit integration considerations, dual-device blood flow optimization, and anticoagulation management. This review provides practical guidance for nephrologists caring for patients treated with both MCS and CKRT. We describe current MCS technologies and discuss evidence-based approaches to CKRT prescription including modality selection, timing of initiation, vascular access techniques, and anticoagulation strategies. We also address volume management, safety monitoring, and troubleshooting common complications. Despite high short-term mortality, many survivors achieve renal recovery by hospital discharge, emphasizing the importance of optimized CKRT delivery in this complex population.

title: Branched Endovascular Aortic Repair as a Salvage Strategy after Failed Chimney Endovascular Aortic Repair: An International Multicentre Cohort.
authorString: Simonte G, Usai MV, Isernia G, Parlani G, Hörer TM, Gallitto E, Tsilimparis N, Reutersberg B, Dias NV, Austermann MJ, D'Oria M, BEVARinCHEVAR collaborative group.

journal.title: European journal of vascular and endovascular surgery : the official journal of the European Society for Vascular Surgery

abstractText:
Objective

Chimney endovascular aortic repair (chEVAR) failures, often manifesting as late type Ia endoleaks or sac expansion, present a formidable surgical challenge. Due to the variable upward orientation of pre-existing chimney stents, fenestrated solutions are frequently technically precluded. This study aimed to evaluate the outcomes of branched endovascular aortic repair (BEVAR) as a salvage strategy for late chEVAR failure within a multicentre international cohort.

Methods

A retrospective analysis was conducted on 29 consecutive patients (median age 81.0 years, interquartile range [IQR] 66.0, 83.0) treated across 13 European centres (2013 - 2025) for failed chEVAR using branched endografts. The primary endpoints were technical success, thirty day clinical success, and procedure related complications. Secondary endpoints included overall survival, freedom from re-intervention, and target visceral vessel (TVV) patency.

Results

The median interval from index chEVAR to BEVAR re-intervention was 48.5 months (IQR 30.0, 80.8). Acute urgent or emergent procedures accounted for 17% of cases (n = 5), while 31% (n = 9) underwent expedited repair for large aneurysms. Off the shelf devices were utilised in 41% of cases. A total of 106 TVVs were incorporated through branches, with a mean of 3.7 vessels per patient. Technical success was achieved in 97% (28 of 29). There was no peri-operative mortality or open surgical conversion. Significant complications included two cases (7%) of severe spinal cord ischaemia. The thirty day clinical success rate was 90%. At a median follow up of 19 months (IQR 9, 40), the Kaplan-Meier estimate for overall survival was 92% at 1 year. TVV patency was 100%, with only one renal artery re-intervention for in stent re-stenosis. Freedom from branch related re-intervention was 96% at 1 year.

Conclusion

Salvage of failed chEVAR using branched endografts is technically demanding but yields excellent early results. In experienced centres, BEVAR appears feasible and offers one potential salvage option in selected patients with suitable anatomy, particularly when an off the shelf solution is required.

title: Palliative Cardiac Surgery for Trisomy 13 and Trisomy 18 Improves Heart Failure and Facilitates Transition to Home Care
authorString: Katayama Y, Isobe S, Tanaka K, Fujii T, Kawamura Y, Kawai R, Takatsuki S, Ogata K, Hine K, Masumoto K, Yoda H.
abstractText: Background Congenital heart disease (CHD) occurs in 80%–90% of infants with trisomy 13 (T13) and trisomy 18 (T18). Although surgical intervention remains controversial due to limited life expectancy, palliative cardiac surgery may improve heart failure symptoms and facilitate transition to home care. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical profiles, surgical outcomes, and discharge rates of infants with T13 and T18 who underwent cardiac surgery. Methods We retrospectively reviewed 22 consecutive patients with T13 or T18 and CHD who underwent initial cardiac surgical intervention between April 2013 and March 2024 at our institution. Results The cohort comprised 22 patients (T18: n = 19; T13: n = 3). Primary intracardiac diagnoses were ventricular septal defect (VSD) in 12 cases, double outlet right ventricle (DORV) in 6 cases, patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) in 3 cases, coarctation of the aorta (CoA) complex in 1 case, and interrupted aortic arch (IAA) in 1 case. All initial surgical interventions were performed off-pump. At surgery, the median age was 25 [interquartile range (IQR) 16–30] days, body weight was 1.59 [1.35–1.75] kg, and median height was 41.0 [38.6–44.3] cm. Median gestational age at birth was 37 [34–38] weeks, and 14 patients had a prenatal diagnosis. Associated comorbidities included gastrointestinal anomalies in 7 cases, neurological conditions in 3 cases, and respiratory disorders in 2 cases. Serial measurements of serum B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) levels demonstrated a statistically significant reduction postoperatively (preoperative: 736.5 [441.2–3316] pg/mL vs. postoperative: 164.7 [133.2–335.6] pg/mL; p < 0.05). Postoperative complications occurred in 5 patients (23%), including phrenic nerve palsy (n = 2), chylothorax (n = 2), and arrhythmia (n = 1). Overall, 18 patients (82%) were successfully discharged home (home oxygen therapy: n = 5 [23%]; tracheostomy: n = 2 [9%]). Two patients (9%) subsequently achieved definitive biventricular repair. Total overall mortality was 36% (n = 8), with a 90-day mortality rate of 4% (n = 1) and an in-hospital mortality rate of 14% (n = 3). Conclusion Palliative cardiac surgery in selected infants with T13 and T18 effectively alleviates heart failure and facilitates transition to home care. Surgical strategies should be tailored to individual family values and clinical conditions through multidisciplinary shared decision-making.

title: Relationship Between Timing of Surgery and Procedure-Specific Outcomes in Neonates and Infants for Congenital Heart Surgery.
authorString: Ali Bukhari SM, Mehta R, Aydin MI, Haverty MC, Desai M, Tongut A, Puente BN, Franklin WJ, Yerebakan C, d'Udekem Y.
abstractText:
Background

Determining the right timing for neonatal heart surgery remains difficult. In a large multicenter cohort, we studied the relationship between birthweight, timing of surgery, and outcomes to identify optimal surgical timing.

Methods

Using the Society of Thoracic Surgeons Congenital Heart Surgery Database from 2010-2022, we retrospectively reviewed infants who underwent surgery within 90 days of birth. Procedures analyzed included coarctation of aorta (CoA), ventricular septal defect (VSD) repair, atrioventricular septal defect (AVSD) repair, tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) repair, Norwood procedure, and arterial switch operation (ASO). Birthweight, prematurity, and genetic syndromes were analyzed as predictors of operative mortality using categorical and continuous models, including nonlinear spline analysis. Patients were divided into five birthweight categories for risk comparison.

Results

The cohort included 35,315 patients: 26,367(74.7%) neonates and 8,948(25.3%) infants. Low birthweight (<2500g) was present in 15.8% of neonates and 59.9% of infants. Operative mortality was highest in the 0-1kg group (9%, p<0.001). Continuous birthweight was a predictor of mortality (OR=0.45 per 100g increase; 95% CI: 0.40-0.51; p<0.0001). Neonatal age at surgery, prematurity, and genetic syndromes were independently associated with increased mortality. For Norwood procedures, mortality increased below 1.8kg and before 5 days of age; for ASOs, lowest risk occurred between 1.8-3.5kg and after 5 days of age. In AVSD, VSD, and CoA, neither birthweight nor timing significantly affected mortality.

Conclusions

Except for Norwood and ASO procedures, weight and timing had limited impact on mortality, supporting individualized surgical decision-making rather than reliance on historical weight thresholds.

title: Preoperative Serum Biomarkers Improve Prediction of Poor Postoperative Outcome After Cardiopulmonary Bypass Compared With Clinical Variables in Neonates.
authorString: Gardner MM, Balcarcel D, Chen F, Huff A, Olsen R, Winser K, Kennedy A, Bogner HR, Feng R, Mai AD, Gonzalez V, Fraietta J, Padiyath A, Weiss SL, Gaynor JW, Yehya N.
abstractText:
Importance

Neonates undergoing surgery for congenital heart disease (CHD) are at risk for poor postoperative outcomes after cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB), including death, prolonged ICU stay, and ICU readmission. Current prognostic models rely predominantly on nonmodifiable clinical factors.

Objectives

To utilize machine learning methods to compare the predictive utility of preoperative blood biomarkers vs. clinical features alone for ICU-30, a validated composite outcome after neonatal CPB that includes postoperative 30-day morbidity and mortality.

Design, setting, and participants

Prospective observational single-center cohort study of consecutively enrolled neonates younger than 30 days undergoing CPB for CHD.

Main outcomes and measures

Plasma and clinical data were collected from consecutively enrolled neonates younger than 30 days immediately before CPB. Thirty-seven biomarkers were measured by individual or multiplex enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay and tested for association with ICU-30, defined as 1) mortality within 30 days of CPB, 2) ICU stay longer than 30 days, or 3) ICU readmission within 30 days. Predictive performance of extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), least absolute shrinkage and selection operator, and random forest (RF) models was compared using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC). For XGBoost, the top 20 features were identified based on model importance (gain).

Results

Biomarkers were available for 144 neonates. Most were male (51%), White (64%), and non-Hispanic (75%). Most operations were Society of Thoracic Surgeons-European Association for Cardiothoracic Surgery (STAT) category 3 (32%) or STAT category 5 (29%). ICU-30 occurred in 29 neonates (20%). Using combined clinical and biomarker data, XGBoost demonstrated moderate discrimination for ICU-30 (AUROC, 0.74), outperformed RF (AUROC, 0.72), and LASSO (AUROC, 0.70). Biomarkers alone performed better (AUROC, 0.72) than clinical data alone (AUROC, 0.67) with XGBoost. The top two features in the combined XGBoost model were neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin (NGAL) and trefoil factor 3 (TFF3). Using Shapley additive explanation to assess both predictive impact and directionality, the most influential features were NGAL, a disintegrin and metalloproteinase with a thrombospondin type 1 motif, member 13 (ADAMTS13), and angiopoietin-2 (Ang-2).

Conclusions and relevance

Among neonates with CHD requiring CPB, multibiomarker models improved prediction of poor postoperative outcome compared with clinical variables alone. The most informative model features included markers of renal injury/perfusion and gastrointestinal epithelial injury (NGAL and TFF3), as well as vascular injury and inflammation (ADAMTS13 and Ang-2). These findings support further investigation of biomarker-informed risk stratification and may provide insight into pathophysiologic mechanisms underlying adverse postoperative outcomes.

title: The association of sildenafil and sexual function in women with pulmonary arterial hypertension associated with congenital heart disease: Subanalysis of the COHARD-PH registry.
authorString: Ismawardika A, Ratna Gharini PP, Anggrahini DW, Hartopo AB, Cipta CE, Bramantyo BB, Dinarti LK.
abstractText: Globally, approximately 1% of live births are associated with congenital heart disease (CHD), representing the most common congenital abnormality. Roughly 10% of adult CHD patients suffer from pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), a condition that may progress to right heart failure and mortality if untreated. Sildenafil is frequently prescribed for PAH; however, its effects on sexual function in patients with CHD remain poorly studied. We performed an observational study employing a retrospective cohort design to evaluate clinical data from patients with CHD treated at Sardjito Hospital, Yogyakarta, between January 2019 and July 2025. Study participants were stratified into two groups, consisting of those receiving sildenafil therapy and those not treated with sildenafil. Eligible participants were required to have been sexually active within the preceding four weeks. Sexual function in both treatment groups was evaluated using the Female Sexual Function Index (FSFI) questionnaire. As many as 78 subjects met the criteria and completed the FSFI questionnaire. Fifty-seven and 21 participants were assigned to the sildenafil-exposed group and to the non-exposed group, respectively. Among those receiving sildenafil, 35.1% (20 patients) experienced sexual dysfunction, while 64.9% (37 patients) had normal sexual function. Bivariate analysis revealed a significant relationship between sildenafil use and sexual dysfunction in the study subjects (p=0.033; 95% CI 0.12-0.94). Multivariate analysis revealed that sildenafil consumption was linked to a lower occurrence of sexual dysfunction (OR 0.13; p=0.005; 95% CI 0.03-0.53). To conclude, sildenafil therapy in women with PAH-CHD was associated with reduced likelihood of sexual dysfunction.

title: Outcome After Late Pulmonary Valve Replacement in Repaired Tetralogy of Fallot.
authorString: Quennelle S, Viau F, Casalta AC, Resseguier N, Ovaert C, Habib G, Macé L, Lenoir M, Aldebert P.
abstractText: The optimal timing of pulmonary valve replacement (PVR) in adults with repaired Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) and severe pulmonary regurgitation remains controversial. Current recommendations rely largely on right ventricular volumetric thresholds derived from cohorts undergoing intervention during adolescence or early adulthood, although their prognostic value remains debated. To identify predictors of postoperative morbidity and mortality after PVR in patients aged ≥30 years with repaired TOF, with a specific focus on invasive preoperative hemodynamic parameters. We conducted a retrospective single-center study including patients aged ≥30 years with repaired TOF who underwent surgical PVR between 2009 and 2018. The primary outcome was a composite endpoint including supraventricular arrhythmia, cardiovascular rehospitalization, or all-cause death during follow-up. Clinical, imaging, and hemodynamic variables were analyzed using univariate and multivariate logistic regression. Forty-eight patients (mean age at PVR 41 ± 9.8 years) were included, with a mean follow-up of 52 months. The primary outcome occurred in 23 patients (48%). Preoperative signs of advanced disease, including right heart failure, left ventricular dysfunction, and a history of syncope or ventricular tachycardia, were associated with adverse outcomes. Although right ventricular end-diastolic volumes were markedly increased in both groups, they were not associated with the primary outcome. Conversely, right ventricular end-systolic volume and, particularly, right ventricular end-diastolic pressure (RVEDP) showed stronger prognostic value. In multivariable analysis, RVEDP remained the only independent predictor of postoperative morbidity and mortality (OR 1.49, 95% CI 1.01-3.40; p = 0.04). In adults aged ≥30 years with repaired TOF undergoing PVR, elevated RVEDP is a key predictor of postoperative morbidity and mortality, whereas right ventricular end diastolic volumes on MRI are not. Invasive hemodynamic assessment may help refine the timing of PVR in this "senior" population.

title: Long-term trajectories of intrinsic capacity and risk of cardiometabolic multimorbidity and its subtypes in older US adults: A 19-year prospective cohort study.
authorString: Huang J, Sun R, Zhao D, Lai X, Chen L, Liu X, Paek SC.
abstractText:
Background

Intrinsic capacity (IC) changes with aging, but the association between its long-term trajectories and subsequent cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) remains unclear. We examined the associations of long-term trajectories of IC with incident CMM and its subtypes among older US adults.

Methods

Data were drawn from the Health and Retirement Study. Group-based trajectory modeling identified IC trajectories using five assessments across waves 3-7. Participants with CMM during this period were excluded. Incident CMM, defined as the coexistence of at least two of diabetes, heart disease, and stroke, was assessed over up to 19 years of subsequent follow-up. Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

Results

Among 3707 participants, four IC trajectories were identified: very high-late decline (17.53%), high-gradual decline (45.59%), moderate-gradual decline (29.24%), and low-persistent decline (7.63%). During 33,744 person-years of follow-up, 638 participants developed CMM. Compared with the very high-late decline group, fully adjusted HRs were 1.53 (95%CI = 1.19-1.96), 1.75 (1.31-2.33), and 2.38 (1.61-3.52) for high-gradual decline, moderate-gradual decline, and low-persistent decline groups, respectively. Associations were observed across all three CMM subtypes, and generally persisted in sensitivity analyses, including alternative IC scoring approaches.

Conclusions

Less favorable long-term IC trajectories were associated with higher subsequent CMM risk. Repeated IC assessments may provide useful information for identifying older adults at elevated cardiometabolic risk.

title: Temporal and Vessel-Specific Relationship Between Post-PCI Fractional Flow Reserve and Long-Term Clinical Outcomes.
authorString: Kanaji Y, Hwang D, Usui E, Ueno H, Sayama K, Watanabe T, Watanabe T, Murakami R, Hosokawa K, Chung J, Yang S, Shin ES, Nam CW, Lee HJ, Matsuo H, Choi KH, Lee JM, Matsuo A, Doh JH, Chen SL, Koo BK, Kakuta T.
abstractText:
Background

Post-percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) fractional flow reserve (FFR) reflects residual physiological impairment after stent implantation and is a proven predictor of procedural success and prognosis. However, the temporal dynamics of its prognostic utility and its potential variation according to the target vessel remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to explore vessel-specific post-PCI FFR thresholds and evaluate their prognostic consistency over 5 years.

Methods

We analyzed 2128 patients undergoing successful drug-eluting stent implantation from the international Post-PCI FFR Extended registry. Patients were stratified according to the target vessel: left anterior descending artery (LAD) versus non-LAD. The primary end point was 5-year target vessel failure, defined as a composite of cardiac death, target vessel myocardial infarction, or target vessel revascularization. Restricted cubic spline models were used to explore the continuous association between post-PCI FFR and target vessel failure and to identify vessel-specific risk thresholds. Temporal prognostic performance was assessed via 3-year landmark analysis and time-dependent receiver-operating characteristic curves.

Results

During 5-year follow-up, target vessel failure occurred in 176 patients (11.7%) with LAD lesions and 74 patients (11.7%) with non-LAD lesions. Lower post-PCI FFR was independently associated with a higher risk of target vessel failure in both LAD and non-LAD vessels. Spline analyses characterized vessel-stratified risk patterns, and exploratory comparisons used post-PCI FFR cut points of 0.83 for LAD and 0.94 for non-LAD vessels. Landmark analysis indicated that the excess hazard associated with suboptimal FFR was predominantly concentrated within the first 3 years postprocedure. Nevertheless, time-dependent receiver-operating characteristic analysis demonstrated modest but stable discriminatory power of post-PCI FFR throughout the 5-year follow-up.

Conclusions

Post-PCI FFR provides sustained 5-year prognostic insight, though the exploratory vessel-stratified cut points require external validation. Although the associated risk is highest in the early to mid-term period, predictive discrimination persists long-term. These findings advocate for vessel-specific interpretation of post-PCI physiology to refine risk stratification and patient management.

title: Antithrombotic therapy in patients with atrial fibrillation and acute coronary syndrome treated with percutaneous coronary intervention. -insights from the SWEDEHEART registry.
authorString: Skibniewski M, Batra G, Charitakis E, Janzon M, Karlsson LO, Mohammad MA, Zwackman S, Venetsanos D, Alfredsson J.
abstractText:
Aims

The aim of this study was to study temporal changes in antithrombotic therapy and to assess associations between common treatment strategies and clinical outcomes.

Methods

Patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) and acute coronary syndrome (ACS) undergoing PCI between 2010 and 2022 were identified from the SWEDEHEART registry. The three most common antithrombotic treatment strategies were: 1. Vitamin K antagonist (VKA)-based, 2. Direct oral anticoagulant (DOAC)-based, and 3. Platelet inhibition (PI) only. Outcomes were major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE; all-cause death, myocardial infarction (MI), or stroke), and net adverse cardiovascular event (NACE; MACE or major bleeding). Cox regression models were created to adjust for differences in baseline characteristics.

Results

In total, 15,358 patients were included, 29% were women and median age was 76 years. At discharge, 4155 (27%) received VKA-based, 4962 (32%) DOAC-based therapy, and 6241 (41%) PI only. The proportion treated with oral anticoagulants increased from 27% in 2010 to 82% in 2021. VKA-, and DOAC-based strategies were both associated with adjusted lower adjusted risk of MACE, (aHR 0.80, 95% CI 0.73-0.89) and (aHR 0.82, 95% CI 0.74-0.90) and NACE (aHR 0.86, 95% CI 0.78-0.94) and (aHR 0.85, 95% CI 0.77-0.93), respectively, compared with PI only, with no difference between the two OAC strategies.

Conclusions

In patients with AF undergoing PCI for ACS, the use of oral anticoagulants increased over time. Both a VKA- and DOAC-based strategy were associated with lower MACE and NACE, with no significant difference between the two strategies.

title: Myocardial infarction risk across cancer subtypes - a nationwide registry-based follow-up study.
authorString: Shanmuganathan JWD, Baech J, Polcwiartek CB, Yonis H, Schou M, Andersen MP, Torp-Pedersen C, Poulsen LØ, Gislason G, Butt JH, Køber L, El-Galaly T, Søgaard P, Mamas MA, Freeman P, Jacobsen PA, Kragholm K.
abstractText:
Background

As cancer survival improves, a growing population of patients is exposed to elevated cardiovascular risk. We compared the one-year risk of myocardial infarction (MI) across 13 cancer types using patients with low-risk skin tumors as a cancer-active reference group.

Methods

In this nationwide registry-based cohort study, we included 660,531 Danish patients diagnosed with one of 13 cancer subtypes between 2000 and 2023. Patients with prior MI or coronary revascularization were excluded. Standardized one-year absolute risks of MI were estimated using the Aalen-Johansen estimator with inverse probability of treatment weighting, while relative risks were estimated using g-computation based on cause-specific Cox models for MI and all-cause death.

Results

Compared with patients with low-risk skin tumors, the relative risk of MI was highest in multiple myeloma (RR 1.80, 95% CI 1.34-2.26), bladder cancer (RR 1.52, 95% CI 1.26-1.78), kidney cancer (RR 1.51, 95% CI 1.20-1.82), leukemia (RR 1.45, 95% CI 1.16-1.75), and gastrointestinal cancer (RR 1.37, 95% CI 1.24-1.50). Standardized one-year MI risk remained below 1% across all cancer subtypes, ranging from 0.31% in breast cancer to 0.91% in multiple myeloma. One-year all-cause mortality varied markedly across cancer subtypes, from 2.2% in patients with low-risk skin tumors to 71.9% in patients with hepatobiliary and pancreatic cancer.

Conclusions

One-year MI risk varied across cancer subtypes. Relative and standardized absolute MI risks were highest in patients with multiple myeloma, with increased risks also observed in several other cancer subtypes. These findings represent MI risk in the presence of substantial competing mortality and should not be interpreted as differences in underlying biological susceptibility to MI.

title: Renal denervation in patients with chronic kidney diseases: current evidence and future perspectives.
authorString: Zhang Z, Ma J, Chen X, Peng Y.
abstractText: Renal denervation (RDN) is an emerging minimally invasive technique that has been approved as an adjunctive therapy for resistant hypertension. Sympathetic activation is a shared pathological mechanism of hypertension and chronic kidney disease (CKD), and the kidney plays a crucial role in mediating this process. In recent years, RDN has demonstrated promising therapeutic potential for the management of patients with CKD. However, this technique still faces challenges such as heterogeneous efficacy and potential safety concerns. This review comprehensively summarizes the latest advances in the efficacy and safety of RDN in patients with CKD, and proposes critical perspectives to address the existing challenges.

title: Veriset™-Assisted Cortical-Sparing Reconstruction With Inner-Layer Renorrhaphy Versus Conventional Double-Layer Renorrhaphy During Robot-Assisted Partial Nephrectomy: A Propensity Score-Matched Analysis.
authorString: Khalil IA, Sweidat A, Al-Emadi I, Younes N, Mansour A, Al Jalham K, Al Rumaihi K, Al-Ansari A, Aboumarzouk O.
abstractText: This study aimed to compare perioperative, renal functional, and postoperative outcomes of Veriset™-assisted cortical-sparing reconstruction with inner-layer renorrhaphy (VCS-ILR) versus conventional double-layer renorrhaphy (DLR) in robotic-assisted partial nephrectomy. We retrospectively evaluated 311 patients who underwent robotic-assisted partial nephrectomy between January 2011 and April 2026, including 207 treated with DLR and 104 with VCS-ILR. Propensity score matching was performed at a 1:1 ratio using age, sex, Charlson comorbidity index, diabetes, hypertension, chronic kidney disease, tumour size and nephrometry score. Eighty-nine matched pairs were analysed. Compared with DLR, VCS-ILR was associated with a shorter warm ischaemia time (18.48 ± 5.93 vs. 20.33 ± 5.09 min; p = 0.035), a smaller early postoperative decline in eGFR (-1.90 ± 14.35 vs. -10.39 ± 16.51 mL/min/1.73 m2; p = 0.0004), and a smaller absolute decline in eGFR at the last follow-up (-1.16 ± 13.41 vs. -6.23 ± 16.30 mL/min/1.73 m2; p = 0.037). Operative time (219.91 ± 65.47 vs. 197.03 ± 62.98 min; p = 0.023) and estimated blood loss (244.49 ± 196.05 vs. 159.31 ± 104.20 mL; p= 0.0005) were longer and greater, respectively with VCS-ILR. Overall postoperative complication rates were similar. No recurrence or progression occurred in either matched group. Oncological outcomes were interpreted descriptively because of unequal follow-up. VCS-ILR was associated with smaller early and intermediate-term declines in eGFR and a shorter warm ischaemia time, but with a longer operative time and greater estimated blood loss. These findings should be interpreted as associations given the retrospective design and temporal separation between cohorts.

title: Consensus Statements on the Clinical Practice for Patients With Fontan-Associated Liver Disease.
authorString: Kanto T, Akagi T, Yamagishi H, Ohfuji S, Tokuhara D, Kusano H, Sakamori R, Tateishi R, Kogiso T, Yoshizumi T, Muneuchi J, Toh N, Inuzuka R, Ohuchi H.

journal.title: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society

abstractText: The Fontan procedure has been transformative for patients with univentricular physiology. By using a single ventricle as the systemic pump and relying on passive venous return to drive pulmonary circulation, Fontan circulation alleviates cyanosis and heart failure, allowing children to engage in normal activities during school and adolescence. Nevertheless, Fontan circulation is characterized by chronically elevated systemic venous pressure, which leads to systemic venous congestion and long-term multiorgan effects. Fontan-associated liver disease (FALD) is now recognized as a major long-term complication. Approximately 50% of patients develop hepatic abnormalities within 10-20 years after surgery, and some progress to cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Despite this risk, strategies to identify individuals at high risk for early HCC and to provide better prognostic information remain limited. This article compiles knowledge from congenital heart disease specialists and hepatologists on FALD, including areas where evidence is limited. By facilitating early diagnosis, structured follow-up, and multidisciplinary management of FALD, this initiative aims to improve outcomes, build a nationwide clinical experience, and ultimately support the development of formal, evidence-based guidelines for FALD management.

title: Adventitial Cystic Disease of the Popliteal Artery in a Young Female: A Case Report.
authorString: Tsuchida Y, Kamiya K, Tsuchida H, Higuchi M, Chiba Y.
abstractText:
Introduction

We report a rare case of adventitial cystic disease (ACD) of the popliteal artery in a 23-year-old woman presenting with intermittent claudication.

Case presentation

CT and MRI scans revealed a multilocular cyst compressing the right popliteal artery, with extension into a branch. The patient underwent surgical resection of the cyst and the affected artery, followed by reconstruction using an autogenous vein graft. A literature review of 172 Japanese cases confirmed that this is the youngest patient documented in Japan, regardless of gender.

Conclusions

Although ACD predominantly affects middle-aged men, this case emphasizes the need to consider ACD in the differential diagnosis of intermittent claudication even in very young patients with a low risk of atherosclerosis.

title: Chest Pain in Children and Adolescents in the Emergency Department: A State-of-the-Art Narrative Review of Epidemiology, Risk Stratification, and Evidence-Based Management.
authorString: Rath S, Akoum A, Keithley R, Fahmy K, Aponte Y, Shehadeh MH, Alsabri M.
abstractText:
Background

Chest pain accounts for approximately 0.5%-1% of pediatric emergency department (ED) visits and is a frequent source of anxiety for families and clinicians. Although concern for cardiac disease often drives evaluation, true cardiac etiologies are rare, typically representing only 1%-2.5% of cases. The challenge in pediatric emergency care lies in distinguishing the small subset of patients with potentially life-threatening conditions from the large majority with benign causes, while avoiding unnecessary testing and radiation exposure.

Methods

We conducted a state-of-the-art narrative review synthesizing contemporary literature on the epidemiology, differential diagnosis, cardiac risk stratification, diagnostic testing, and emerging technologies relevant to pediatric chest pain evaluation in the ED. Emphasis was placed on structured clinical assessment and evidence-based use of diagnostic modalities.

Results

Most pediatric chest pain is noncardiac, with musculoskeletal causes predominating, followed by psychogenic, pulmonary, and gastrointestinal etiologies. Cardiac causes remain uncommon but require systematic identification through careful history, focused physical examination, and electrocardiography. High-risk features include exertional pain, syncope, abnormal examination findings, concerning family history, and abnormal ECG results. Standardized clinical pathways reduce unnecessary imaging and cardiac testing without compromising diagnostic safety. Chest radiography and troponin testing have limited utility when used indiscriminately, whereas point-of-care ultrasound offers a radiation-free adjunct in selected cases. Emerging tools such as teletriage and artificial intelligence-assisted diagnostics show promise but require further validation in pediatric populations.

Conclusion

Pediatric chest pain is usually benign but necessitates structured, risk-stratified evaluation to safely exclude serious disease. Judicious testing guided by clinical assessment improves efficiency, minimizes radiation exposure, and supports high-value, patient-centered emergency care.

title: Wearable acoustic cardiography for detection of left ventricular and valvular dysfunction: a prospective diagnostic accuracy study.
authorString: Xie S, Wu Y, Li R, Cai Y, Huang J, Wu J.
abstractText:
Background

Preoperative cardiac evaluation based on history and physical examination is subjective, risking delayed diagnosis or excessive echocardiography. Acoustic cardiography (ACG) synchronizes ECG and heart sound analysis for rapid point-of-care cardiac screening. We evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of wearable ACG for left ventricular dysfunction, significant valvular dysfunction, and the consistency of ACG-aided preoperative risk assessment with expert consensus.

Methods

This prospective single-center study enrolled consecutive patients undergoing major elective non-cardiac surgery. Echocardiography served as the reference standard; the primary endpoint was LVEF <40%.

Results

Among 262 patients, ACG showed excellent performance for LVEF <40% (AUC=0.979, sensitivity 93.3%, specificity 96.4%). It achieved substantial agreement with echocardiography for significant valvular dysfunction (κ=0.69). Adding ACG improved consistency with expert consensus versus physical examination alone (κ=0.71 vs 0.55).

Conclusions

Wearable ACG provides high accuracy for preoperative screening of systolic and valvular dysfunction. It facilitates targeted echocardiography referral. Further trials are needed to verify its impact on referral decisions and perioperative outcomes.

Trial registration

ChiCTR2300073695.

title: Clinical, Electrophysiological Profile and Outcomes in Patients With Permanent Junctional Reciprocating Tachycardia.
authorString: Hafeesa NM, Kakarla S, Abhilash SP, Vijay J, Kumaran AKV, Namboodiri N.
abstractText:
Background

Permanent junctional reciprocating tachycardia (PJRT) is an uncommon form of re-entrant supraventricular tachycardia that can lead to tachycardia-induced cardiomyopathy (TIC). This study aims to describe a cohort of individuals with PJRT, outline their clinical and electrophysiological profiles, and evaluate various treatment strategies and long-term outcomes.

Methods

This retrospective study included patients diagnosed with PJRT. Electrophysiological confirmation of the diagnosis was available for 24 patients who underwent radiofrequency catheter ablation (RFCA). Outcomes were assessed from the index ablation to the most recent follow-up at the time of data collection.

Results

31 patients (median age 15 years [IQR 6.5-25 years]) with PJRT were included of whom 14 (45.2%) had TIC. 24 patients (77.4%) underwent RFCA, while 7 (22.5%) received medical management. Initial procedural success was achieved in 23 of 24 patients (95.8%). Recurrence occurred in 2 of 24 patients (8.3%); both were successfully re-ablated. Ultimately, all ablated patients were arrhythmia-free (24/24; 100%) at a median follow-up of 5.5 years (IQR 2.75-16.3 years). Two patients experienced major complications: spasm of the right posterolateral branch (RPLB), which was managed medically, and occlusion of the posterolateral branch (PLB) requiring stenting. Complete regression of TIC was observed in patients who underwent ablation (11/11).

Conclusions

This is the largest single-center report from Asia characterizing clinical spectrum of PJRT. RFCA provides an effective and durable treatment for PJRT. Careful attention to the proximity of the ablation site to the coronary circulation and atrioventricular node is essential to minimize rare but serious complications.

title: Fractional Flow Reserve in the Era of Artificial Intelligence: Review of the Current Literature.
authorString: Fernandes M, Sousa LC, Parente MPL, Silva S, Pinto SIS.
abstractText:
Purpose

Given the global prevalence of coronary artery disease (CAD) and atherosclerosis, there is a critical need for accurate non-invasive diagnostic approaches. The current diagnostic procedures in the hospital are invasive, costly, and may pose potential risks to the patients. While computational fluid dynamics (CFD) based diagnostic approaches can have high accuracy, their extensive computational requirements render them impractical for local hospital use. Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based methodologies for predicting fractional flow reserve (FFR) in coronary arteries with stenosis have gained attention for their nearly instantaneous and accurate results, holding significant potential for impacting healthcare outcomes. The objective of this study is to present the current uses of AI for non-invasive FFR computation and understand the current state of this technology, address current limitations and suggest potential directions for future research.

Methods

This work provides a comprehensive review of AI-based approaches for the non-invasive measurement of the FFR. This research emphasizes key factors including the different possible algorithms, their inputs, the sample of patients, and statistical indexes such as accuracy, sensitivity and specificity of the predictions.

Results

The reviewed literature shows that AI methodologies lead to low computational times and high accuracy values and, therefore, are promising alternatives for accurate FFR prediction in atherosclerotic coronary arteries. The accuracy of the results was highly linked to the inputs used in the algorithms, and there is no consensus as to the most relevant inputs. Despite the evident advantages, the widespread implementation of ML approaches in hospitals still faces challenges such as lack of data, image quality, and result interpretability and explainability.

Conclusion

AI emerges as a promising tool for non-invasive FFR computation, leading to high accuracy in CAD assessment. Addressing the identified challenges is crucial for enhancing diagnostic capabilities and patient care for CAD in hospitals.

title: Coronary coronary microvascular dysfunction and physiologically non-obstructive plaque progression in patients with acute coronary syndromes.
authorString: Yi B, Zeng M, Cui Z, Chen Y, Xu L, Zhang D, Zhao C, Ren H, Shao S, Wang W, Sun Q, Li M, Li L, Qin Y, Xu Y, Li S, Zhang Y, Wei X, Tu S, Mintz GS, Jia H, Yu B, Hu S.
abstractText:
Background

Coronary microvascular dysfunction is common in coronary heart disease, yet its role in plaque progression remains unclear. This study aims to investigate the association between coronary microvascular dysfunction and the progression of physiologically non-obstructive atherosclerotic plaques.

Methods

A total of 198 patients with acute coronary syndrome who underwent optical coherence tomography imaging of at least one non-culprit vessel at both baseline and 1-year follow-up were included. Angiography-derived microcirculatory resistance (AMR) was measured in non-culprit vessels with a Murray law-based quantitative flow ratio (μQFR) > 0.80. Serial changes in plaque morphological characteristics were compared between plaques in high (AMR ≥ 2.50) and low (AMR < 2.50) AMR vessels.

Results

Among 172 non-culprit vessels (278 plaques) with μQFR >0.80, elevated AMR was identified in 60 vessels (92 plaques). Plaques in the high AMR group exhibited significantly less fibrous cap thickening and a smaller reduction in maximum lipid arc than those in the low AMR group. Furthermore, thin-cap fibroatheromas (TCFAs) in the high AMR group showed a significantly lower rate of regression to non-TCFAs (43.8% vs. 81.5%, p = 0.011). Multivariate analysis identified AMR as an independent predictor of changes in fibrous cap thickness (β: -3.12 [-5.53-0.70], p = 0.011) and maximum lipid arc (β: 1.91 [0.10-3.73], p = 0.039).

Conclusions

Our findings indicate that coronary microvascular dysfunction is associated with attenuated plaque stabilisation in physiologically non-obstructive lesions, suggesting that integrated microvascular and plaque assessment warrants further investigation.

title: Monocyte-mimetic nanoprobe enables longitudinal MRI of Atherosclerotic Inflammatory dynamics.
authorString: Rousseau J, Wang TY, Wu SP, Beeman SC, Wang KC.
abstractText: Noninvasive monitoring of plaque inflammatory dynamics remains an unmet need. We previously developed a monocyte-mimetic nanoprobe, MoNP-SPION, for MRI detection of atherosclerotic lesions. Here we demonstrate MoNP-SPION enables longitudinal tracking of plaque-associated inflammatory status in atherosclerotic mice. Following 16 weeks of plaque induction, mice were maintained on high-fat diet or switched to chow for 6 weeks to model persistent versus resolving plaque inflammation. MoNP-SPION-enhanced MRI was performed at 3- and 6-weeks following diet adjustment, and arterial tissues were collected for histological analysis at the 6-week endpoint. Mice maintained on high-fat diet exhibited persistent hypointense T2* signal at the carotid bifurcation and aortic root, whereas chow-transitioned mice showed progressive signal attenuation, consistent with histological evidence of diet-induced reduction in plaque burden and inflammation.
