These findings establish MoNP-SPION as a molecular MRI probe for longitudinal assessment of plaque inflammatory dynamics, supporting its potential for monitoring atherosclerosis progression and therapeutic response.

title: Auditing the adversarial robustness of genomic foundation models with SafeGenes.
authorString: Zhan H, Barbour C, Moore JH.
abstractText: Genomic foundation models (GFMs) such as evolutionary scale modeling (ESM) are increasingly applied to variant effect prediction in clinical genomics, yet their adversarial robustness remains underexplored. We present SafeGenes, an evaluation framework combining input-space attacks, a discrete single-nucleotide variant (SNV)-reachable HotFlip attack, and a soft-prompt-triggered backdoor. Across cardiomyopathy and arrhythmia datasets, iterative attacks severely degrade discrimination: projected gradient descent (PGD) reduces the area under the curve (AUC) by more than 30 percentage points, and the false-positive rate at 95% sensitivity collapses to nearly 1.0, misclassifying virtually all benign variants as pathogenic. The backdoor selectively elevates the pseudo-log-likelihood ratio (PLLR) scores of benign variants and transfers across ESM architectures. A single population-observed background substitution inverts pathogenicity ranking below chance, lowering the AUC from 0.76 to 0.39, showing that these vulnerabilities are biologically realizable. SafeGenes provides an open auditing framework for adversarial robustness in genomic AI.

title: Identifying Plasma Proteins for Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy Penetrance and Severity in Pathogenic Variant Carriers and Noncarriers.
authorString: Hassanzada F, van Vugt M, Jansen M, Baas AF, Te Riele ASJM, Dooijes D, van der Crabben SN, Jongbloed JDH, Cox MGPJ, Amin AS, Lekanne Deprez RH, Ruijsink B, Kuster DWD, van der Velden J, Bezzina CR, Asselbergs FW, van Tintelen JP, van Spaendonck-Zwarts KY, Schmidt AF.
abstractText:
Background

Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is a clinically variable disease in onset and progression. Pathogenic MYBPC3 variants account for a substantial proportion of HCM diagnoses.

Objectives

This study sought to identify protein biomarkers associated with HCM penetrance and severity.

Methods

Olink-assayed plasma proteins of 144 pathogenic MYBPC3 variant carriers were evaluated for associations with HCM severity based on diagnostic criteria (unaffected, mildly, or severely affected). Identified proteins were replicated in the UK Biobank considering time to onset of HCM (67 cases), cardiomyopathy (156 cases), and associations with left ventricular maximum wall thickness (6,492 participants). After prioritizing proteins on cardiac tissue expression and druggability, we examined disease penetrance through associations with heart failure (HF) and arrhythmic outcomes in 272 UK Biobank participants with known pathogenic HCM variants free of cardiomyopathy at proteomics assessment.

Results

Among pathogenic MYBPC3 variant carriers, we identified 27 proteins associated with HCM severity, of which 22 replicated in the UK Biobank. Six proteins were prioritized (N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide [NT-proBNP], growth/differentiation factor [GDF]-15, fibroblast growth factor [FGF]-23, adrenomedullin [ADM], renin [REN], and neural cell adhesion molecule 1 [NCAM1]), of which 5 associated with disease penetrance in pathogenic variant carriers: NT-proBNP and REN associated with increased HF and arrhythmic risk, GDF-15 and FGF-23 with HF risk, and NCAM1 with arrhythmic risk.

Conclusions

Through the integration of proteomic analyses in both clinical and general population cohorts, we replicated and prioritized 6 proteins associated with HCM penetrance and severity. These findings highlight potential plasma-based markers for diagnosis and disease monitoring, as well as promising targets for future therapeutic development.

title: Molecular targets and potential pathways associated with DEHP-exacerbated atherosclerosis: A combined bioinformatics and experimental study.
authorString: Xu N, Wang T, Lin F, Lin W, Zeng Y, Ren X, Xu J, Lin C, Shi H, Li C.
abstractText: Atherosclerosis (AS) is a chronic inflammatory disease characterized by lipid deposition and plaque formation in arterial walls, representing the leading cause of cardiovascular disease. Recent studies indicate that the environmental endocrine disruptor di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP) may aggravate atherosclerosis, yet its underlying mechanism remains unclear. This study integrates bioinformatics and experimental approaches to elucidate the molecular targets and pathogenic mechanisms of DEHP in atherosclerosis. ADMET and ProTox analyses revealed multi-organ toxicity risks, particularly nephrotoxicity and hERG blockade. Network toxicology identified 55 shared targets between DEHP and atherosclerosis, with 7 candidate hub targets (BCL2, MAPK8, CASP3, MMP9, STAT1, CTSS, MAPK14) showing significant interactions. Functional enrichment indicated involvement in oxidative stress, apoptosis, and inflammatory pathways, validated by differential expression in human atherosclerotic plaques (GEO: GSE100927). Molecular docking revealed strong binding of DEHP to MMP9 (-7.8 kcal/mol), moderate binding to MAPK14 (-6.9 kcal/mol), MAPK8 (-6.4 kcal/mol), BCL2, CASP3, and CTSS (all -5.2 kcal/mol), and weak binding to STAT1 (-4.7 kcal/mol). In vivo, DEHP exposure accelerated high-fat diet induced atherosclerotic lesions, manifesting as dyslipidemia, increasing plaque area, reducing collagen content, and compromising plaque stability. Mechanistically, DEHP may promote atherosclerosis through altered expression of candidate hub targets in oxidative stress, inflammation, apoptosis, and extracellular matrix degradation pathways.

title: A full-length isoform atlas of the non-failing and failing human heart
authorString: Ye B, Noureen M, He F, Lingamgunta L, Zheng S, Li F, Wang X.
abstractText:
ABSTRACT

Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) and ischemic heart disease (IHD) are leading causes of heart failure, yet isoform-level changes in the failing heart remain poorly defined because reference annotations are derived largely from healthy tissues and short-read sequencing cannot reliably reconstruct full-length transcripts. We sequenced six human left ventricles (non-failing, DCM, and IHD; n = 2 each) with PacBio HiFi long reads and curated 48,232 isoforms across 11,760 genes, including 15,535 novel NIC and NNC isoforms. Independent evidence supported most novel structures: 81.7% of isoforms with novel splice junctions had short-read support for all novel junctions, and a cardiac CAGE atlas supported the 5′ ends of 93% of NIC and 86% of NNC isoforms. Novel isoform diversification was concentrated in sarcomere genes and persisted after accounting for gene complexity, expression, sequencing depth, and transcript length. We then augmented GENCODE v43 with 18,637 non-FSM long-read isoforms and re-quantified two independent short-read cohorts (MAGNet and GSE116250). For most genes carrying a transcript that changed more than 2-fold in DCM, the gene itself changed less than 2-fold, so these changes are not apparent at the gene level. Of 626 transcripts differentially expressed in both cohorts, 98% changed in the same direction, including all 100 long-read isoforms among them. The resource is available through CardioIsoMap, an interactive isoform-centric portal ( https://cardioisomap.streamlit.app/ ). This study provides a comprehensive isoform-resolved reference of the human heart in health and disease.

title: Calsarcin-1 modulates the muscle LIM protein/Z-disc complex mechanosensing in familial hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
authorString: Li X, Lu Y, Li X, Riaz M, Blum T, Luo H, Hoareau M, Liu Y, Fooladi S, Xing Q, Gokhan I, Li X, Park J, Yue L, Campbell SG, Qyang Y.
abstractText:
ABSTRACT

BACKGROUND

Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is an inherited cardiac disease mainly caused by sarcomeric mutations. The Z-disc is a critical mechanosensory interface linking sarcomeric stress to biochemical signaling, yet the role of calsarcin-1 in maintaining Z-disc integrity remains unclear. Patient-specific iPSC-CM-based engineered heart tissues (EHTs) are being developed for disease modeling and drug screening; however, the loading conditions to recapitulate pathological mechanical stress remain underdeveloped.

METHODS

HCM patient heart, three patient-specific iPSC lines (MLP-W4R;MYH7-R723C, MYH7-R663H, and MYBPC3-V321M), derived cardiomyocytes (iPSC-CMs), and engineered heart tissues (EHTs) were employed. Calsarcin-1 expression was assessed, and its role in MLP/Z-disc mechanosensing was investigated through gain- and loss-of-function approaches. An EHT bioreactor was developed to recapitulate HCM-associated elevated afterload, electrical pacing, and cyclic mechanical loading; isogenic wild type and MLP-W4R iPSC lines were generated by genome editing. Calsarcin-1 treatment to rescue the hypertrophic phenotype of isogenic (Iso) MLP-W4R iPSC-CM-EHTs was evaluated.

RESULTS

Calsarcin-1 was markedly downregulated in myocardium from an HCM proband carrying heterozygous MLP-W4R and MYH7-R723C variants, as well as in patient-specific iPSC-CMs and EHTs, accompanied by marked upregulation of the hypertrophic markers atrial natriuretic factor ( ANF ) and brain natriuretic peptide ( BNP ). Ectopic expression of calsarcin-1 via viral infection in MLP-W4R;MYH7-R723C iPSC-CMs stabilized the MLP/Z-disc machinery and reversed hypertrophy in all three patient-specific iPSC-CMs (MLP-W4R;MYH7-R723C, MYH7-R663H, and MYBPC3-V321M). Knockdown of calsarcin-1 attenuated the rescue effect of MLP overexpression in MLP-W4R;MYH7-R723C iPSC-CMs. Isogenic wild type and MLP-W4R iPSCs were generated by correcting mutations in MLP-W4R;MYH7-R723C iPSCs. Moreover, we developed a 3D-EHT bioreactor system that integrates controlled mechanical loading and electrical pacing to recapitulate the elevated afterload and cyclic mechanical stress characteristic of HCM. The additional mechanical resistance imposed by high afterload prolongs TTP and RT50 and increases the normalized force-time integral (nFTI), suggesting that excessively high afterload drives pathological remodeling in IsoMLP-W4R-iPSC-CM-EHTs. More importantly, calsarcin-1 significantly rescued both systolic and diastolic dysfunction of IsoMLP-W4R-iPSC-CM-EHTs exposed to pathological high afterload.

CONCLUSIONS

Calsarcin-1 is a nodal regulator of pathological cardiac remodeling that restores MLP/Z-disc mechanosensing. A patient-derived EHT bioreactor model recapitulating pathological HCM loading identifies calsarcin-1 as a potential therapeutic target.

title: Uric acid/HDL-cholesterol ratio and uric acid/mean erythrocyte aggregation ratio in subclinical carotid atherosclerosis.
authorString: Caimi G, Lo Presti R, Urso C, Brucculeri S, Carlisi M.
abstractText: Background and aimSeveral literature studies have highlighted an association between elevated serum acid levels and cardiovascular diseases, including atherosclerotic disease, with also a link in case of normal uricemia values; in relation to this relation, in this new study regarding our cohort of subjects with subclinical carotid atherosclerosis, we have examined the uric acid/HDL-C ratio and the uric acid/mean erythrocyte aggregation ratio.MethodsOur retrospective, cross-sectional, and explorative study population includes 100 subjects (43 men and 57 women) with subclinical carotid atherosclerosis; in this population we have evaluated: serum uric acid, HDL-Cholesterol, mean erythrocyte aggregation, uric acid/HDL-C ratio (UHR) and uric acid/mean erythrocyte aggregation ratio (UEAR).ResultsFrom the obtained data we observed that only UHR is able to discriminate the subgroups of the whole cohort assembled according to the number of cardiovascular risk factors and according to the degree of insulin resistance evaluated with some surrogate indices; moreover, the UHR is positively correlated with each index of insulin resistance.ConclusionThese data confirm the possible utility of UHR, and at the same time, despite the premises, the UEAR does not seam to have, at now, any particular role in this clinical condition.

title: The follow-up results of partial clipping for unruptured intracranial aneurysms: The role of coil embolization after partial clipping.
authorString: Park HC, Moon E, Park JC, Ahn JS, Choi JH.

journal.title: Journal of cerebrovascular and endovascular neurosurgery

abstractText:
Objective

Microsurgical treatment of complex intracranial aneurysms, particularly those with atherosclerosis of the aneurysm, or parent artery or incorporated branch vessels, poses significant technical challenges. This study aimed to evaluate the follow-up outcomes of partial clipping and the results of subsequent coil embolization.

Methods

We retrospectively analyzed 25 patients with unruptured intracranial aneurysms who underwent intentional partial clipping, of whom 18 subsequently underwent endovascular treatment.

Results

Aneurysms were located in the anterior cerebral artery (ACA, n=10), distal internal carotid artery (n=7), middle cerebral artery (n=6), and posterior circulation (n=2). The mean maximal aneurysm size was 6.2±2.2 mm. Partial clipping was performed because of severe atherosclerosis (n=12), poor visualization (n=7), or branch adhesion (n=6). Seven patients received no additional treatment (four with complete occlusion and three with near occlusion). Thirteen patients underwent simple coil embolization, four underwent stent-assisted coiling, and one underwent flow diversion. After endovascular treatment, 16 of 17 patients (94.1%) with follow-up imaging had complete occlusion; one had minor recanalization. One patient had computed tomography (CT) findings suggestive of minor leakage at 1 month; another experienced hemorrhage during coil retrieval.

Conclusions

When complete clipping is technically unfeasible or high-risk, this staged hybrid strategy may provide a useful treatment alternative in selected patients. Aneurysm shrinkage or occlusion was observed in some cases after partial clipping. However, these findings should be interpreted with caution because post-clipping hemodynamic alterations, natural history, or thrombotic changes may have contributed.

title: Interatrial Septal Disorders are Independently Associated with Delayed Post-Exercise Heart Rate Recovery in Athletes.
authorString: Komici K, Femminella GD, Nardone A, Bencivenga L, Petraglia L, Aversa LS, Rengo G, Guerra G.
abstractText:
Background

Interatrial septal disorders (IASD) are among the most common congenital cardiac anomalies. Their impact on cardiac autonomic function in athletes remains poorly defined. In this study, we aimed to evaluate the prevalence of IASD and their association with cardiac autonomic function, assessed by heart rate recovery (HRR), in a cohort of adult athletes.

Methods

This cross-sectional study enrolled 1,018 adult athletes undergoing pre-participation cardiovascular screening at the Exercise and Sports Medicine Unit of ''A. Cardarelli'' Hospital, Campobasso, Italy, between January 2024 and May 2025. Trans-thoracic echocardiography with contrast imaging was performed to diagnose IASD. HRR was assessed during exercise stress testing using the Modified Bruce Protocol. ΔHRR was calculated as the change from peak heart rate during exercise to that measured during 1st, 2nd, 3rd, and 4th minutes of recovery.

Results

IASD were identified in 331 athletes (32.5%), including patent foramen ovale (12.5%), redundant interatrial septum (21.7%), atrial septal aneurysm (3.3%), and ostium secundum (1.7%). Athletes with IASD exhibited significantly lower ΔHRR at 1 min (30.8 ± 13.9 vs. 39.9 ± 18.1 bpm, p < 0.001) and 2 min (61.0 ± 17.9 vs. 66.1 ± 16.7 bpm, p < 0.001) post-exercise. On multivariable regression, IASD was the strongest independent predictor of impaired ΔHRR 1 (β =- 11.19, p < 0.001).

Conclusion

IASD are prevalent in athletes and independently associated with delayed post-exercise early HRR, suggesting an impairment in post-exercise vagal reactivation.

title: Post-Traumatic Abdominal Aortic Dissection Associating Solid Organ Injury in a Child.
authorString: Guanà R, Ahmed OY, Marchetto C, Alhellani H, Discalzi A, Gennari F.
abstractText:
Introduction

Handlebar injuries are frequent events in children, often perceived as minor, but may result in severe intra-abdominal damage.

Case presentation

We report the case of a 13-year-old boy who sustained a blunt abdominal trauma following impact against a bicycle handlebar. In this case, the trauma produced an unusual and potentially life-threatening combination of lesions, including massive hemoperitoneum, a deep hepatic laceration, a severe pancreatic injury with disruption of the main pancreatic duct, and a post-traumatic dissection of the infrarenal abdominal aorta.

Results

The patient was admitted in critical condition and underwent prompt clinical, laboratory, and radiological evaluation. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography revealed the extent of the abdominal injuries and confirmed the vascular involvement. Given the complexity and severity of the findings, management required a rapid multidisciplinary approach involving pediatric surgeons, interventional radiologists, vascular surgeons, and gastroenterologists. The infrarenal aortic dissection was treated urgently with an endovascular approach using the placement of a covered stent, allowing successful exclusion of the lesion and stabilization of the vascular injury while avoiding open surgery. The hepatic injury was managed conservatively with close hemodynamic and radiological monitoring. During the subsequent clinical course, the patient developed a large post-traumatic pancreatic pseudocyst related to the pancreatic duct disruption. This complication was successfully treated with endoscopic ultrasound-guided drainage using a lumen-apposing metal stent (LAMS), which allowed effective internal drainage and progressive resolution of the collection.

Conclusions

This case highlights the potentially severe nature of bicycle handlebar injuries in children and emphasizes the importance of maintaining a high index of suspicion for occult intra-abdominal and vascular injuries. Early diagnosis and timely multimodal management are crucial to optimize outcomes in these complex traumatic scenarios.

title: An MRI-Based Framework for Patient-Specific Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Mechanics Assessment.
authorString: Caruso G, Dux-Santoy L, Guala A, Bragulat-Arévalo M, Teixidó-Turà G, García-Reyes M, Rodriguez-Palomares JF, Bellmunt S, Martínez MÁ, Peña E.
abstractText:
Purpose

To develop and validate a patient-specific Bayesian inverse modeling framework for the simultaneous estimation of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) wall and intraluminal thrombus (ILT) material properties using in vivo magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).

Methods

Finite element models (FEMs) of four AAA patients were constructed from MRI geometries. Bayesian optimization combined with Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) was applied to identify nonlinear anisotropic material parameters minimizing the discrepancy between FE-predicted and MRI-derived displacements. Validation was performed against equibiaxial mechanical tests on tissues excised from the same patients. Sensitivity analyses assessed the impact of wall thickness and ILT inclusion on stress predictions.

Results

Bayesian-identified parameters closely matched experimental equibiaxial responses, reproducing both displacement magnitudes and anisotropy. RMSE values between FE-predicted and MRI-derived displacements were low, confirming high model fidelity. Peak wall stresses (PWS) distributions revealed that ILT significantly attenuates wall stress, with stress concentrations localized in ILT-free regions. Moderate variations in wall thickness or ILT material properties had limited impact on PWS locations, while exclusion of ILT markedly increased predicted stresses.

Conclusion

The proposed Bayesian framework provides a robust, patient-specific methodology for accurate estimation of AAA wall and ILT mechanical properties, enabling reliable prediction of wall stress distributions and highlighting the protective role of ILT. This approach has potential to improve individualized rupture risk assessment and inform clinical decision-making.

title: Complete Response to Pembrolizumab in a Case of Microsatellite Instability-High, Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer With Somatic MSH2 Mutation.
authorString: Gunji K, Hoshi S, Maruya M, Hagino R, Onagi A, Tanji R, Hata J, Akaihata H, Ogawa S, Kojima Y.
abstractText:
Introduction

Microsatellite instability-high status has been associated with response to immune checkpoint inhibitors. However, clinical data on microsatellite instability-high castration-resistant prostate cancer and temporal changes in mismatch repair status remain limited.

Case presentation

A 77-year-old man with castration-resistant prostate cancer underwent comprehensive genomic profiling, which showed microsatellite instability-high and tumor mutational burden-high status with a somatic MSH2 (c.366+1G>C) variant. Pembrolizumab decreased prostate-specific antigen levels and achieved a radiological complete response. Serial immunohistochemistry demonstrated preserved MSH2 expression at diagnosis and loss after docetaxel treatment, establishing a temporal change in MMR protein expression during the clinical course.

Conclusion

Serial biopsies demonstrated a temporal loss of MSH2 expression, suggesting that MMR function and MSI status may have changed during treatment. However, acquisition of MSI-H could not be established because baseline molecular MSI status was unavailable. This case highlights the potential value of re-biopsy and reassessment of current tumor biology.

title: Precise anatomical landmark annotation of the cardiac conduction system on cardiac computed tomography angiography.
authorString: Tretter JT, Asyraf T, Ugarteburu M, Spaziani S, Perez-Salas N, Webb N, Zaretsky L, Ben-Haim S.
abstractText:
Background

CTA-based estimation of the conduction system from anatomical landmarks underpins a visualization platform (CARA) used in structural heart interventions and conduction system pacing.

Objective

To quantify the precision and reliability of the annotation method and the bias of trained readers relative to an expert reference standard.

Methods

The expert who defined the method and 6 trained readers each annotated 8 landmarks representing the sinus and atrioventricular nodes, His bundle course (Point B), left bundle branch origin (Point C), and course of Bachmann's bundle (B2-B5), in addition to the three aortic leaflet nadirs on 50 CTA studies in 3 sessions. Repeatability and reproducibility were assessed, referenced to clinically accepted error margins (2-5 mm). Intraclass correlations (ICC) were computed on heights above the aortic annular plane. 3D bias relative to the expert was tested for equivalence within half the margin.

Results

Repeatability SD was 1.67-3.98 mm and reproducibility SD 2.03-5.60 mm; all mean deviations were within margin, with 88.6-97.4% of repeat reads and 71.4-94.9% of reader means within margin. Inter-observer ICC on annular heights was 0.76-0.82 for the atrioventricular and 0.79-0.98 for the atrial points. Shared bias relative to the expert was 0.14-3.24 mm, within margin for all landmarks and equivalent within half the margin for sinus node, Point B, B2 and B3; at B3 and B2, 95% and 83% of the apparent separation was repeatability noise.

Conclusion

The method meets its clinically accepted margins with millimeter precision and good-to-excellent reliability, and transfers from expert to trained readers with bias within margin.

title: Patient-Reported Symptoms and Arrhythmias During Continuous ECG Monitoring After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation.
authorString: Bettelini AS, Moser C, Brügger J, Jordan F, Nussbaumer I, Scharf L, Knecht S, Serban T, Stump R, Preis S, Stolte T, Nestelberger T, Kolb R, Baraki H, Schaer B, Krisai P, Schaerli N, Kühne M, Sticherling C, Mahfoud F, Badertscher P.
abstractText:
Background

Wearable ECG patches after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) enable continuous rhythm monitoring and allow symptoms reporting via trigger buttons and diary entries. However, the reliability of triggered events to identify clinically relevant arrhythmias after TAVI is uncertain.

Objectives

We systematically analyzed patient-triggered events and their corresponding rhythm findings during 14-day ECG patch monitoring after TAVI.

Methods

Adult patients undergoing TAVI at a Swiss tertiary centre were prospectively enrolled and monitored with a 14-day ECG patch before discharge. Patients recorded any cardiac-related symptoms using the patch trigger button and/or diary function.

Results

Among 315 patients (median age 82 years [78-87], 43% female), median analyzable duration was 14 days [13-14]. At least one patient-triggered event was recorded in 94 patients (30%), with a median of 2 events per patient [1-4]. Atrial fibrillation (AF) was detected in 85 patients (27%), including 17 patients (5.4%) with new AF; however, only 20 patients with AF (24%) reported symptoms during AF episodes. Pauses occurred in 58 patients (18%) and high-grade atrioventricular block in 32 patients (10%), with no associated patient-triggered events. Ventricular tachycardia (≥4 beats) occurred in 165 patients (52%) and was entirely asymptomatic. Of 348 evaluable symptom-triggered events, 153 (44%) occurred without associated arrhythmia. The most frequent arrhythmias associated with symptom-triggered events were premature atrial contractions (21%), AF (14%), and premature ventricular contractions (11%).

Conclusions

After TAVI, patient-triggered events during ECG patch monitoring poorly reflect objectively documented arrhythmias and fail to identify many clinically relevant rhythm disturbances. These findings support systematic continuous ECG surveillance beyond symptom-driven monitoring strategies after TAVI.

title: Global Research Landscape of Recurrent Osteoporotic Vertebral Compression Fractures: A Bibliometric Analysis of Risk Factors, Prevention, and Prediction (1993-2024).
authorString: Jin H, Ma J, Yang S, Wang H.
abstractText:
Objectives

Recurrent osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures (ROVCFs) remain a clinical challenge because they are associated with pain, spinal instability, and disability, particularly in older populations. This study presents a bibliometric and visual analysis of global research on risk factors, prevention, and prediction related to ROVCFs from 1993 to 2024.

Methods

The Web of Science Core Collection was searched on January 10, 2025, for English-language Articles and Review Articles published from 1993 to 2024. VOSviewer, CiteSpace, and the R package bibliometrix were used to analyze publication and citation characteristics, collaboration networks, keyword co-occurrence patterns, thematic clusters, and keyword citation bursts.

Results

A total of 381 eligible publications on risk factors, prevention, and prediction related to ROVCFs were included in the analysis. Annual publication output generally increased over the study period, particularly after 2008. China, the USA, and Germany were the most productive countries, while Chang Gung Memorial Hospital, Capital Medical University, and Guangzhou University of Chinese Medicine were leading institutions. Spine, European Spine Journal, and Osteoporosis International were the top publishing journals. Within the present dataset, Chen Hao and Lin Wei-Che had the highest h-index values, followed by Chen Zhi. Keyword co-occurrence analysis revealed seven major research clusters: (1) osteoporosis-related risk factors, (2) percutaneous vertebroplasty (PVP)-related factors, (3) intravertebral clefts (IVC) factor for cemented vertebrae, (4) anti-osteoporosis drugs for refractures, (5) predictive model validation, (6) adjacent vertebrae refractures, and (7) kyphotic deformity. Keyword-burst analysis highlighted growing research attention to bone mineral density, management, prevention, vertebroplasty, and kyphoplasty.

Conclusion

This bibliometric analysis delineated the global research landscape and thematic structure of ROVCF research. The major themes involved osteoporosis-related risk factors, vertebral augmentation-related factors, intravertebral clefts, anti-osteoporosis treatment, adjacent vertebral fractures, kyphotic deformity, and prediction-model development. Further multicenter research is needed to evaluate and externally validate refracture-risk prediction approaches.

title: Computational Fluid Dynamics Analysis of Percutaneous left ventricular assist device Support Modes on Ventricular Hemodynamics and Hemocompatibility.
authorString: He Y, Feng X, Yu H, Wu Y, Zhang F, Chen H, Xie Q, Wang X, Chen Z.
abstractText: Percutaneous left ventricular assist devices (PLVADs) provide cardiac support in heart failure, yet the hemodynamic effects of varying support levels and the balance between ventricular unloading and blood trauma remain unclear. This study employed numerical simulations to analyze a PLVAD-supported left ventricle under three pump speeds: low, high, and normal control. Analysis encompassed both conventional hemodynamic parameters (e.g., TAWSS, OSI, RRT) and validated mathematical model. Results showed that PLVAD support enlarged the vortex core and increased vorticity in the left ventricle, while reducing them at the aortic outlet. It effectively lowered ventricular wall pressure-achieving unloading-but also decreased aortic outlet WSS. Furthermore, PLVAD elevated OSI and ECAP while reducing TAWSS and RRT, effects that intensified at higher speeds. Increased speed also raised non-physiological scalar shear stress (SSS) and platelet activation, significantly increasing the hemolysis index in the rotational domain and elevating blood damage risk in the ventricular chamber compared to normal physiology. In conclusion, while PLVAD effectively unloads the ventricle, it impairs flow pulsatility and hemocompatibility. Controlling high-speed-induced SSS and platelet activation is critical to mitigate hemolysis. Monitoring hemocompatibility indicators-especially in the apical and aortic outlet regions-is essential due to their link with thrombosis and adverse events.

title: SOX4 suppresses vascular calcification via DNA-binding-independent regulation of the USP10–HNRNPC–WNT5A axis
authorString: Chen J, Cai H, Jin X, Li Y, Zhu Y, Ma K, Liu H, Zhu X, Yu L, Qiu C.
abstractText:
Background

Vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) osteogenic differentiation drives vascular calcification, yet the endogenous mechanisms that restrain this transition remain poorly defined. SOX4 has recently emerged as a regulator of phenotype switching in endothelial and epithelial cells, but whether it governs VSMC fate and vascular calcification is unknown.

Methods

SOX4 expression was examined in human calcified arteries, in vitamin D3 (VitD3)-treated mouse aortas and in phosphate-treated human aortic smooth muscle cells. Loss- and gain-of-function experiments, an HMG-box-deleted SOX4 mutant, co-immunoprecipitation combined with mass spectrometry, ubiquitination and protein stability assays, RNA immunoprecipitation sequencing and mRNA decay assays were combined with VSMC-specific Sox4 knockout mice and pharmacological WNT5A inhibition.

Results

SOX4 protein was upregulated in calcified VSMCs and arteries, yet SOX4 loss aggravated and SOX4 overexpression attenuated VSMC osteogenic differentiation. A SOX4 mutant lacking the HMG-box retained anti-calcific activity, placing the function outside DNA binding. SOX4 interacted with HNRNPC and attenuated the HNRNPC–USP10 association, promoting K48-linked ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of HNRNPC. HNRNPC bound WNT5A mRNA and was required for its stability, so that SOX4 reduced WNT5A expression. VSMC-specific Sox4 deletion aggravated VitD3-induced aortic calcification together with HNRNPC and WNT5A upregulation. Strengthening this braking axis with the WNT5A antagonist BOX5 attenuated VSMC osteogenic differentiation in vitro and vascular calcification in vivo in both genotypes, identifying WNT5A as a pharmacologically accessible node downstream of SOX4 loss.

Conclusions

SOX4 restrains VSMC osteogenic differentiation through post-transcriptional control of cell fate, defining a SOX4–HNRNPC–WNT5A axis and identifying it as a pharmacologically accessible target for vascular calcification.

title: GS-ECG: a generalist–specialist approach to structural heart disease prediction from electrocardiograms
authorString: Mi J, de Vries CF, Connelly DT, Wu H.
abstractText: Structural heart disease (SHD) often goes undiagnosed, and echocardiography, the standard test, cannot be offered to every patient promptly. AI analysis of routine electrocardiograms (ECGs) could help prioritize who is scanned first. ECG foundation models promise broad applicability across ECG tasks, but SHD abnormalities are novel targets, defined by echocardiography and outside the labels on which these models were pretrained, so how best to use them is unclear. Rather than adapting the foundation model to these targets, we propose GS-ECG, a synergistic generalist–specialist approach that keeps it frozen and pairs it with a compact specialist, DGRNet, trained on novel SHD targets. In this setup, the generalist summarizes each recording in long-context features, while DGRNet focuses on SHD-specific waveform morphology at beat-level resolution, with a receptive field of about two cardiac cycles per feature. We evaluated GS-ECG in two health systems: MIMIC-IV-Ext-SHD (49,229 patients), a new public benchmark, and the EchoNext-Mini Dataset (36,286 patients). Full fine-tuning of the foundation model improved mean AUPRC by only 1.3–3.6% over freezing it, whereas DGRNet alone exceeded fine-tuning by 6.1–6.4%. Combining the frozen generalist with DGRNet in GS-ECG performed best, exceeding fine-tuning by 8.1% in both datasets while training 4.9% as many parameters; its composite SHD AUROC was 0.825 and 0.839. Against the published EchoNext-Mini Model on its own dataset, GS-ECG found 17–25% more patients with aortic stenosis, mitral regurgitation or tricuspid regurgitation among the top 5% ranked for echocardiography. Pairing frozen foundation models with purpose-built specialists offers an efficient route to clinical targets that lie beyond pretraining labels.

title: 3D pattern of cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA) from leptomeninges to vascular layers of the human cerebral cortex in comparison to age- and amyloid-beta (Aβ) burden-related capillary CAA.
authorString: Yilmazer-Hanke D, Alexiou P, Tuzzi E, Wiesner D, Laible M, Osterloh A, Hanke J.
abstractText: In cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA), the relationship of perivascular β-amyloid (Aβ) deposits to Aβ in vessel walls and AD-related pathology is not fully understood. Here, we performed 3D analyses of vascular and perivascular circumferential/dyshoric Aβ deposits with Aβ17-24- and Aβ1-40-labeling antibodies using single-/double-/multi-label immunostaining in thick brain sections, and in tissue sequentially cleared with DEEP-Clear and CUBIC-L in human CAA. Arterial and capillary walls showed both Aβ1-40 and Aβ17-24 labeling, extending over several branching points, with vessel segments containing Aβ1-40 considerably dilated. Ten distinct 3D arterial/arteriolar and capillary CAA categories were identified and quantified with Aβ17-24 in the leptomeninges, and vascular layers (superficial, middle, deep, and juxtacortical) of nine cerebral cortical areas. While four categories reflected Aβ in arterial walls (tunica media and adventitia) and the perivascular brain parenchyma (fleecy or fibrillary), in six capillary CAA categories three showed gaps between dyshoric Aβ deposits and Aβ in capillary walls, and three were gapless (dyshoric Aβ deposits attached to capillary walls). Factor analysis extracted the factors "arterial CAA," "Aβ load-related capillary CAA" with gaps, and gapless "age-related capillary CAA," with factor 1 associated with the APOE ε4 genotype, factor 2 with cortical Aβ burden, and factor 3 with age. Leptomeningeal/superficial cortical vascular layers were more severely affected in "arterial CAA," while the two capillary CAA types were prominent in middle/deep cortical layers. Layer and age distribution of Aβ1-40 was similar to Aβ17-24 in all three CAA types. Thus, our 3D CAA analyses using thick brain sections and light sheet microscopy distinguished arterial CAA from two different capillary CAA types. Opposite layer patterns of arterial and capillary CAA and the distinction of two capillary CAA forms based on their relationship either to Aβ load/APOE ε4 genotype or age suggests differences in CAA pathogenesis and mechanisms in pericapillary Aβ drainage.

title: Atlas of meniscal cells from different species and characterizing meniscal endothelial and smooth muscle cells.
authorString: Zhang M, Huang J, Cai Z, Lin X, Li D, Xu J, Ma R, Sun H.
abstractText:
Aims

The meniscus is a vital biomechanical component of the knee, but a comprehensive understanding of its cellular composition across species is lacking. This study aimed to construct the first cross-species cellular atlas of the meniscus by defining conserved and species-specific cell populations, with particular focus on characterizing smooth muscle cells, to better understand knee joint biology and pathology.

Methods

We performed single-cell RNA sequencing analysis on meniscal tissues from multiple species, including mice, rats, beagles, goats, and humans, encompassing both healthy individuals and patients with osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, or discoid meniscus. This approach enabled detailed cell type classification, marker gene identification, and histological validation through immunohistochemistry and Masson staining. Functional experiments were performed to investigate the role of smooth muscle cell-enriched genes.

Results

Our analysis revealed nine distinct cell types common across all species. Their proportions varied significantly between species, with rat meniscus showing the closest cellular composition to human. A major finding was the consistent presence of actin alpha 2 (ACTA2)-positive smooth muscle cells, located primarily in the meniscal surface zone, which were significantly reduced in pathological conditions. Intersection of bulk RNA-seq and single-cell data identified three conserved smooth muscle cell-enriched genes (SPARCL1, S1PR3, ARHGAP6), functional assays showed that S1PR3 signalling modulates meniscal matrix gene expression (collagen type 1, alpha 1 (COL1A1)). Masson staining further confirmed organized smooth muscle fibres in canine and goat menisci.

Conclusion

This study establishes the first cross-species cellular atlas of the meniscus, identifying both universal and divergent cellular features. The discovery of a conserved smooth muscle cell population that diminishes in disease states, coupled with the identification of S1PR3 as a regulator of matrix gene expression, provides new insight into meniscal degeneration and highlights ACTA2+ smooth muscle cells as a potential therapeutic target for knee joint disorders.

title: Modified Supra-Annular Aortic Valve Replacement with Florida Sleeve Aortic Root Reinforcement for Aortic Regurgitation Associated with Behçet's Disease.
authorString: Fu XM, Zhou YZ, Zhou XM.
abstractText: Patients with Behçet's disease who undergo aortic valve replacement for aortic regurgitation face significant risks of paravalvular leakage and prosthetic valve detachment. We describe a novel surgical strategy that combines supra-annular mechanical prosthesis implantation with Florida sleeve aortic root reinforcement. By anchoring the prosthetic valve to an external Dacron graft rather than the inflamed native annulus, this strategy aims to reduce these risks in patients with Behçet's disease and aortic regurgitation.

title: Severe Pannus Formation with Coronary Artery Obstruction after the Ozaki Procedure: A Case Report.
authorString: Kitada Y, O'Connor D, Takeda K.
abstractText: We report a case of severe pannus formation causing coronary artery obstruction after aortic valve neocuspidization (the Ozaki procedure). A 64-year-old woman who had undergone the Ozaki procedure for aortic stenosis presented with chest pain. She was diagnosed with obstruction of the right coronary artery ostium and moderate aortic regurgitation and stenosis. Redo aortic valve replacement and coronary artery bypass grafting were subsequently performed. Surgery revealed severe circumferential pannus on the aortic side of the neocusps, with obstruction of the right coronary artery ostium. The pannus and cusps were removed completely; after aortic annular enlargement, the aortic valve was replaced. The patient's postoperative course was uneventful. This is the first case report of coronary obstruction due to pannus formation after the Ozaki procedure.

title: Acute hypertension causes focal coronary artery perivascular cGAS-, IRF3, and IFNAR-dependent type I interferon responses
authorString: Castellanos von Borstel G, Wright SJ, Gunes BB, Ninh VK, Zhang B, Hong JM, Padrós-Valls R, Golts E, Hu J, Fu Z, King KR.
abstractText: Hypertension exposes coronary arteries to dynamic mechanical forces that alter the structural integrity and lead to pathologic changes such as aneurysm, dissection, or atherogenesis. Although the effects of chronic hypertension have been extensively studied, the early molecular responses to increased luminal pressure remain poorly understood. Here, we find that acute hypertension in murine coronary arteries induced by transverse aortic constriction (TAC) causes focal perivascular type I interferon (IFN) responses in the vessel wall in contrast to comparatively homogeneous perivascular fibrosis. Spatial transcriptomics and RNAscope independently demonstrate spatially clustered expression of interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs) in the walls of pressurized left and right coronary arteries in the first week after TAC. Genetic disruption of cGAS or IRF3 each markedly attenuated the perivascular ISG response, indicating the response is a consequence of DNA sensing. Pharmacologic disruption of type I IFN signaling using an anti-IFNAR antibody abolished pressure-induced induction of focal ISG expression suggesting the pathway can be inhibited therapeutically. Since focal type I IFN signaling in the infarct borderzone of the left ventricle increased risk of dilation and rupture, we propose that focal perivascular type I IFN signaling in the vessel wall may serve as a nidus for analogous pathologies like aneurysm, dissection, or atherogenesis and represent a potential target for therapy.

title: Myocardial splice associations after aortic valve replacement in a secondary RNA sequencing analysis
authorString: Xu D, Yu Z, Li A, Liu Z, Chen Q, Liu J, Sun H.
abstractText: Background Left ventricular hypertrophy does not regress equally in all patients after aortic valve replacement. We examined whether myocardial splice differences associated with remodelling labels persisted after individual samples were excluded, and what these differences could change in reference transcripts and proteins. Results We reanalysed 41 public myocardial RNA-sequencing samples labelled as persistent hypertrophy (HYP, n = 21) or reverse remodelling (REV, n = 20). Of 156,111 candidate splice events, 70 met the full-cohort selection criteria. Twenty-two events in 19 genes were selected with unchanged direction in all 41 leave-one-out analyses. Both local splice alternatives matched reference transcripts for 16 events. A score derived separately within each training set could be calculated for every excluded sample. Its area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.648, compared with 0.998 when selection and assessment used the full cohort. DGLUCY long-site inclusion averaged 0.766 in HYP and 0.605 in REV; the difference remained positive after each sample was removed. Complete reference sequence comparisons linked the 15-base splice-site difference to the five-amino-acid segment AGAYK. This sequence alternative is already recorded in UniProt. Conclusions The analysis identified internally stable myocardial splice associations and mapped selected events to reference sequences. The modest leave-one-out discrimination and unresolved correspondence between the 41 public samples and the original 40-person clinical cohort preclude a validated prognostic interpretation. Independent outcome-linked data are needed to test these associations.

title: Comparative real-world outcomes of LifeStream and Viabahn VBX balloon-expandable covered stents for iliac artery occlusive disease.
authorString: Tomoi Y, Takahara M, Ogata K, Takei T, Soga Y, Ando K.
abstractText:
Purpose

Balloon-expandable covered stents (CSs) are increasingly used for complex iliac artery occlusive disease, but direct comparative data among CS platforms remain limited. This study compared 1-year restenosis and clinical outcomes between the LifeStream and Viabahn VBX CSs in patients undergoing endovascular treatment (EVT).

Methods

This multicenter retrospective study included 226 patients who underwent EVT for symptomatic iliac artery occlusive disease using either the LifeStream CS (n = 95) or Viabahn VBX CS (n = 131). Outcomes included restenosis, clinically driven target lesion revascularization (CD-TLR), re-occlusion, conversion to bypass surgery, and perioperative complications (POCs). Between-group comparisons were performed using inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) based on propensity scores.

Results

One-year follow-up data were available for 163 of 226 patients (72.1%), and 10 restenosis events occurred during follow-up. After IPTW adjustment, the balance of measured covariates was substantially improved. The estimated 1-year freedom from restenosis was 95.8% (95% confidence interval [CI], 93.1-98.6%) in the LifeStream group and 95.8% (95% CI, 93.1-98.6%) in the Viabahn VBX group, with no statistically significant between-group difference (p = 0.99). No significant differences were detected in freedom from CD-TLR (99.2% [95% CI, 98.0-100.0%] vs. 96.7% [95% CI, 94.3-99.2%]; p = 0.13), re-occlusion (100.0% [95% CI, 100.0-100.0%] vs. 98.1% [95% CI, 96.3-99.9%]; p = 0.091), conversion to bypass surgery (100.0% [95% CI, 100.0-100.0%] vs. 98.2% [95% CI, 96.4-100.0%]; p = 0.083), or POCs.

Conclusion

In this IPTW-adjusted multicenter retrospective study, no statistically significant differences in 1-year restenosis or other clinical outcomes were detected between the LifeStream and Viabahn VBX balloon-expandable CSs. These findings should be considered hypothesis-generating because of the small number of events, incomplete follow-up, and potential residual confounding.

title: Clinical and Hemodynamic Outcomes After Transcatheter Fontan Fenestration Closure: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
authorString: Duras E, Balık RŞ, Çilsal E, Ugan Atik S, Gökalp S, Şerifoğlu Ş, Şahin M, Güzeltaş A.

journal.title: Turk Kardiyoloji Dernegi arsivi : Turk Kardiyoloji Derneginin yayin organidir

abstractText:
Objective

To describe the indications, hemodynamic changes, and intermediate-term outcomes of transcatheter Fontan fenestration closure in a single-center retrospective cohort.

Method

This retrospective, single-center cohort study included all consecutive patients who underwent transcatheter closure of a surgically created Fontan fenestration between January 2015 and April 2025. Demographic, anatomical, echocardiographic, hemodynamic, procedural, and follow-up data were collected from medical records. The primary endpoint was the change in resting systemic arterial oxygen saturation. Secondary endpoints included changes in mean Fontan pressure, periprocedural complications, late Fontan-related morbidities, and the need for re-fenestration. Patients were also classified as undergoing early (≤24 months after Fontan completion) or late (>24 months after Fontan completion) fenestration closure.

Results

Sixteen patients (50% male) were included, and 75% had an extracardiac conduit Fontan. The median interval between Fontan completion and fenestration closure was 18.5 months, and 62.5% of the patients underwent early closure. Desaturation was the primary indication (87.5%), whereas suspected or documented systemic embolism accounted for 12.5% of cases. The baseline mean Fontan pressure was 12.0+-3.0 mmHg, and systemic oxygen saturation was 82.7+-10.0%. After closure, the mean Fontan pressure increased slightly to 12.9+-3.0 mmHg (P = 0.056), whereas oxygen saturation improved to 95.4+-3.5% (P < 0.001). During a median follow-up of 5.7 years, 93.8% of the patients remained free from major Fontan-related complications and the need for re-fenestration.

Conclusion

In carefully selected patients with a fenestrated Fontan circulation, transcatheter closure guided by balloon test occlusion was associated with a marked improvement in systemic oxygenation and only a small increase in mean Fontan pressure. Given the limited sample size and retrospective design, comparisons related to the timing of closure should be interpreted as exploratory, and closure decisions should be individualized based on clinical and hemodynamic assessments.

title: Congenitally Corrected Transposition of the Great Arteries: A Narrative Review of Diagnosis, Management, and Clinical Considerations.
authorString: Han J, Luo E, Al-Fakhoury J, Gastelum S, Singh N, Frishman WH, Aronow WS.
abstractText: Congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries is a rare congenital heart defect caused by abnormal looping of the developing heart that results in double discordance of the atrioventricular and ventriculoarterial connections. In these patients, blood will flow through the heart in a physiologically correct direction; however, the morphologic right ventricle becomes responsible for pumping blood to the systemic circulation. The tricuspid valve also becomes the systemic atrioventricular valve. This places patients at risk for progressive right ventricular dysfunction, tricuspid regurgitation, heart failure, arrhythmias, and atrioventricular block. The clinical presentation is highly variable, with some patients being diagnosed during infancy, while others remain asymptomatic and may be diagnosed in adulthood. Typically, the diagnosis is made using echocardiography as the main first-line imaging test. Management is nuanced and consists of surgical versus nonsurgical intervention. Surgical treatment has increasingly shifted from physiologic repair toward anatomic repair, including double-switch procedures that place the morphologic left ventricle in the systemic position. Despite major improvements in diagnosis and treatment, important questions remain about the best timing of intervention, long-term medical therapy, and risk prediction. Larger registries, prospective studies, improved imaging, and new biomarkers may help guide more individualized care and improve long-term outcomes for patients with congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries. However, due to the high risk for deteriorating cardiac function and cardiac-related events, these patients should be carefully monitored for life.

title: Hedgehog Signaling-Dependent Heterochronic Control of Cardiomyocyte Differentiation Establishes Distinct Cardiac Progenitor Fields.
authorString: Canac R, Mikolajczak W, Tarampoulous I, Dreyer KS, Nolasco MJ, Theisen JWM, Guzzetta A, Pott S, Moskowitz IP.
abstractText:
Background

The mammalian heart is formed from distinct cardiac progenitor fields: the first heart field (FHF), second heart field (SHF), and juxta-cardiac field (JCF). How these fields are established remains one of the oldest questions in cardiac biology and is central to understanding congenital heart disease, which differentially affects derivatives of the individual fields. Previous work has demonstrated that the fields emerge and differentiate at distinct times; however, the mechanisms underlying their establishment have remained elusive. Here, we implicate Hedgehog signaling-dependent heterochronic control of cardiac differentiation in the emergence of different heart fields.

Methods

We assessed Hedgehog signaling activity by assembling a cardio-mesodermal single-cell atlas. We analyzed Hedgehog ligand gene expression by confocal imaging in gastrulating mouse embryos. We investigated the necessity of Hedgehog signaling using 2 distinct genetic Hedgehog loss-of-function mouse models, analyzed by single-nucleus RNA sequencing analysis.

Results

Our results show that Hedgehog signaling mediates field-specific heterochronic control of differentiation timing that orchestrates the establishment of the SHF and JCF as distinct from the FHF. We identify a common cardiac progenitor transcriptomic state from which all 3 fields emerge. We show that the SHF and JCF are established coincident with Hedgehog signaling reception, whereas the FHF evades Hedgehog pathway activity and rapidly differentiates. We find that Hedgehog ligand expression sandwiches the cardiac mesoderm emerging from the primitive streak, spatially coordinating SHF and JCF establishment. Partial depletion of Hedgehog signaling causes premature activation of the cardiac differentiation program in the SHF and JCF. Complete ablation of Hedgehog signaling results in failed SHF and JCF establishment.

Conclusions

Our findings reveal a Hedgehog signaling-dependent, non-cell-autonomous heterochronic mechanism required for SHF and JCF formation. This heterochronic mechanism provides a new paradigm for understanding the ordered temporal emergence of the cardiac progenitor fields that support the development of the 4-chambered heart, as well as a general model for the emergence of progenitor fields that drive organogenesis across the mammalian body plan.

title: Feasibility and safety of leadless pacemaker implantation via the right internal jugular vein: primary results of the VAMPIRE multicenter prospective study.
authorString: Ollitrault P, Clerici G, Mussigbrodt A, Khoury MAL, Bauley K, Behar N, Kilani MB, Bisson A, Citerne O, Ferchaud V, Font J, Gras M, Haddad C, Jacon P, Marzak H, Clementy N, Bello H, Savoure A.
abstractText:
Background

Leadless pacemakers (LPs) are usually implanted through the femoral vein. The right internal jugular vein (RIJV) approach has emerged as an alternative, but evidence remains limited to retrospective single-centre series.

Objective

To evaluate the feasibility, procedural success, and 30-day safety of a first-line RIJV approach for LP implantation.

Methods

The VAMPIRE study (NCT06455566) is a prospective, investigator-initiated, multicenter registry enrolling consecutive patients with a guideline-directed LP indication across 15 tertiary centres in France (May 2024-May 2026). The primary endpoint was major procedure- or system-related complications within 30 days.

Results

Of 294 screened patients, 272 (92.5%) underwent a first-line RIJV approach. The cohort was elderly (median age 79 [73-85] years), predominantly male (63.6%), with high comorbidity burden including atrial fibrillation in 51.5%, chronic kidney disease in 34.9%, and cancer in 22.4%. High-degree atrioventricular block was the primary indication in 84.9%; 65.8% of procedures were performed urgently. Successful LP implantation was achieved in 266 of 272 patients (97.8%; 95% CI 95.3-99.2%), with septal deployment in 94.3%. Median procedure time was 30 [25-40] minutes and median fluoroscopy time 2.5 [1.1-7.0] minutes. Major complications occurred in 6 of 272 patients (2.2%; 95% CI 0.8-4.7%; p<0.001).

Conclusion

In this prospective multicenter registry of a first-line RIJV approach for LP implantation, feasibility and procedural success were high, and 30-day major complications rate low. These results support the RIJV route as a safe and broadly applicable access strategy for LP implantation. However, dedicated studies are needed to compare safety versus the femoral approach.

title: Biocompatibility evaluation of a dECM-enriched alginate-gelatin bioink-derived hydrogel for vascular tissue engineering.
authorString: Potere F, Del Carmen A, Chao CL, Mantero S, Boschetti F, Jiang B.
abstractText: Decellularized extracellular matrix (dECM)-based biomaterials have gained increasing attention in vascular tissue engineering due to their bioactivity and tissue-specific composition. In this study, we evaluated the in vitro cellular response and short-term in vivo biocompatibility of a dECM-enriched alginate-gelatin bioink-derived hydrogel previously developed for bioprinting applications. Hydrogel constructs containing porcine aorta-derived dECM or without dECM (control) were assessed using human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs), human aortic smooth muscle cells (HASMCs), a whole-blood clotting assay, and subcutaneous implantation in rats. HUVECs cultured on the dECM-containing hydrogel showed approximately two- to four-fold higher metabolic activity than those cultured on the control formulation, with a significant formulation × time interaction, whereas HASMCs showed an overall lower metabolic activity in the dECM-containing formulation without a significant formulation × time interaction. Whole-blood clotting kinetics did not significantly differ between formulations in this preliminary assay. Following subcutaneous implantation, both formulations exhibited an early peri-implant host response characterized by serous fluid accumulation and macrophage presence, with collagen-containing peri-implant tissue observed during the 2-week study period. Within the limited animal sample, no statistically significant formulation-dependent differences were detected in the quantified histological or immunofluorescence endpoints. Overall, these findings provide preliminary evidence supporting the short-term biological compatibility of the dECM-enriched hydrogel and warrant further evaluation in bioprinted constructs and physiologically relevant vascular models.

title: Percutaneous Versus Surgical Access for Transfemoral TAVR: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Vascular Complications.
authorString: Coutinho ML, Bregalda Neves CR, Torres IO, Delgado LM, Saes GF, Zerati AE, D'Oria M, Leão PP.
abstractText:
Objective

To compare vascular complications between percutaneous and surgical access during transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve implantation (tf-TAVI) and estimate pooled outcomes following percutaneous access.

Design

Systematic review and meta-analysis of comparative and single-arm studies.

Data sources and review methods

PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to 8 July 2026 (PROSPERO CRD420261454909). Comparative (odds ratio [OR]) and single-arm (pooled proportion) random-effects meta-analyses were performed. Subgroup, meta-regression, sensitivity, and publication-bias analyses were conducted for the primary outcome. Risk of bias was assessed with ROBINS-I, ROBINS-I Single Arm, and RoB 2.

Results

Ten comparative studies (4 736 patients) and eight single-arm studies (5 113 patients) were included. Major vascular complications did not differ significantly between percutaneous access and surgical cutdown (OR 0.83, 95% CI 0.61-1.14; I2 = 41.8%; 95% prediction interval 0.39-1.78), with no significant differences in secondary clinical outcomes, including hospital length of stay (mean difference -0.96 days, 95% CI -2.38 to 0.47; p = .19). In the single-arm analysis, pooled major vascular complications after percutaneous TAVI were 5.20% (95% CI 3.52-7.63%; 95% prediction interval 1.43-17.21%; I2 = 91.1%), with 30-day mortality of 2.20% (95% CI 1.41-3.40%; 95% prediction interval 0.72-6.46%; I2 = 66.9%). Funnel plot asymmetry (Egger's p = .034) was attributable to a single zero-event study and was not confirmed by the Peters test (p = .651) or after its exclusion (p = .164).

Conclusion

Percutaneous femoral access was not associated with a statistically significant difference in major vascular complications or other clinically relevant outcomes compared with surgical cutdown in anatomically suitable patients treated at experienced centres; residual confounding cannot be excluded, and this evidence is largely observational and should be considered hypothesis-generating pending confirmation in randomized trials.

Registration

PROSPERO (CRD420261454909).

title: Planned percutaneous coronary intervention around transcatheter aortic valve implantation: a GRADE-assessed meta-analysis of randomized trials.
authorString: Gowaily I, Awad A, Ibrahim AA, Elgendy MS, Jabbar ABA, Shubietah A, Ghallab M, Elmogy A, Abuelazm M, Aboeata A.
abstractText:
Background

Severe aortic stenosis and coronary artery disease frequently coexist in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). We compared planned percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) around TAVI with an initially conservative or deferred PCI strategy.

Methods

We searched PubMed, Cochrane, Scopus, and Web of Science through 15 April 2026. Risk ratios with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using random-effects models. Exploratory reconstruction was a secondary analysis. The study protocol was prospectively registered in PROSPERO with the following ID: CRD420261397950.

Results

Three randomized controlled trials including 1156 patients were identified. Planned PCI was not associated with significant differences in all-cause mortality (risk ratio = 0.90, 95% CI = 0.70-1.15), trial-defined major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE; risk ratio = 0.91, 95% CI = 0.70-1.18; supportive and exploratory because composite components differed), cardiovascular death (risk ratio = 0.74, 95% CI = 0.51-1.08), or myocardial infarction (risk ratio = 0.86, 95% CI = 0.45-1.63). It was associated with fewer urgent (risk ratio = 0.33, 95% CI = 0.13-0.87) and any subsequent revascularizations (risk ratio = 0.25, 95% CI = 0.07-0.87), but more trial-reported major bleeding (risk ratio = 1.57, 95% CI = 1.07-2.32; definitions varied) and any bleeding (risk ratio = 1.77, 95% CI = 1.27-2.47).

Conclusion

Routine planned PCI around TAVI was not shown to reduce mortality or major ischemic outcomes. It was associated with fewer subsequent revascularizations and more trial-reported major bleeding and any bleeding, supporting selective, individualized decision-making.

title: Purkinje-Targeted Catheter Ablation for Refractory Ventricular Fibrillation and Polymorphic Ventricular Tachycardia: A Systematic Review, Network Meta-Analysis, and Meta-Regression.
authorString: El-Shirbiny H, Abdel-Maboud M, Imnadze G, Darma A, Biomy R, Salama MK, Haseeb WA, Didenko M, Trajkovska N, Fink T, Maher KA, Sciacca V, Sohns C, Sommer P, Khalaph M.
abstractText:
Background

Ventricular fibrillation (VF) and polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (PVT) are major causes of sudden cardiac death. Although Purkinje-targeted catheter ablation has emerged as a rescue therapy for refractory ventricular arrhythmias, the comparative safety and efficacy of trigger-focused ablation versus Purkinje de-networking (PDN) remain uncertain.

Objective

To synthesize clinical outcomes for Purkinje-targeted interventions across diverse arrhythmic phenotypes.

Methods

We searched PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Ovid, and CENTRAL for studies enrolling adults with recurrent or refractory ventricular fibrillation (VF) or polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (PVT). We performed pairwise and network meta-analyses using random-effects models. We evaluated the certainty of evidence using GRADE frameworks (PROSPERO: CRD420261423684).

Results

We included 22 studies involving 959 patients. Among PDN cohorts, pooled mortality was 13.5% (n = 435; 16 cohorts; 95% CI: 9.0%-20.1%; I2 = 99.28%), acute success was 83.5% (n = 388; 14 cohorts; 95% CI: 78.9%-88.4%; I2 = 34.33%), and VF/PVT recurrence was 18.9% (n = 412; 15 cohorts; 95% CI: 15.7%-22.6%; I2 = 0%). Compared with standard ablation, PDN showed nonsignificant reductions in mortality (RR 0.672, 95% CI: 0.267-1.69; I2 = 0%) and recurrence (RR 0.820, 95% CI: 0.239-2.807; I2 = 70.33%). In the primary network meta-analysis, PDN ranked highest for acute success (SUCRA 86.27%) and freedom from recurrence (77.05%). However, in a sensitivity analysis of comparative trials (9 trials; n = 457), trigger-focused ablation ranked highest for acute success (SUCRA 88.08% vs. 51.52% for PDN). New-onset LBBB occurred in up to 20.8% after substrate-based PDN.

Conclusions

In this exploratory network meta-analysis, PDN ranked favorably for acute procedural success and short-term arrhythmia freedom. However, low-certainty evidence, imprecise estimates, and substantial clinical heterogeneity preclude definitive conclusions about its comparative efficacy. Large-scale randomized trials are needed to establish its clinical benefit.

title: Heat-Based Therapies in Hypertension Management: A Systematic Review of Physiological Mechanisms.
authorString: Matutina IS, Ikwuka DC, Olubiyi MV, Niyodusenga A, Adeniyi MJ, Walle M, Owu DU, Okeke OC, Onaadepo O, Feyitimi AA, Eze ED, Ime AU, Jimoh A, Umar AH, Ani EJ, Alagbonsi AI, Wondimu DH.
abstractText:
Background

Hypertension is a major modifiable risk factor for several cardiovascular diseases, leading to the need for investigations of user-friendly and less costly nonpharmacological interventions, including passive heat therapies. This study synthesized information on heat-based therapies used in prehypertension and hypertension management, as well as their clinical efficacy, physiological mechanisms, and translational potential.

Methods

We systematically reviewed 13 eligible human studies published between 2000 and 2025 per the PRISMA 2020 checklist, assessed randomized studies with RoB 2 and nonrandomized studies with ROBINS-I, and used SWiM-guided narrative synthesis because interventions, populations, comparators, and outcomes were heterogeneous. Certainty was assessed using GRADE. The review protocol was not preregistered.

Results

Acute blood-pressure reductions and changes in vascular or autonomic markers were reported in some populations, but sustained comparative effects in hypertension remain uncertain. In hypertensive participants, both hot and thermoneutral immersion were associated with reductions in 24-h blood pressure (BP), limiting heat-specific attribution. A single pooled effect estimate and corresponding 95% confidence interval were not calculated. The benefits were linked to lower sympathetic activity, more nitric oxide availability, lower endothelin-1 levels, and less oxidative stress. Outcome-specific GRADE certainty was very low for SBP and DBP and the assessed mechanistic domains.

Conclusion

Passive heat exposure can produce short-term reductions in BP and changes in vascular function, but sustained antihypertensive efficacy, particularly when evaluated with 24-h ambulatory BP in patients with established hypertension, remains uncertain. Mechanistic findings from heart-failure and peripheral artery disease (PAD) cohorts are indirect evidence for uncomplicated hypertension. Passive heat should not replace established antihypertensive treatment. Safety evidence is limited to selected, often supervised populations, and larger trials with ambulatory BP and systematic adverse-event assessment are needed.

title: Transapical Beating-Heart Septal Myectomy for Symptomatic Nonobstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: Initial Clinical Experience.
authorString: Fang J, Chen Y, Zhou W, Li R, Gong C, Du J, Wang H, Wang Q, Cheng L, Wang C, Chen T, Ma Y, Zhu Y, Zhou J, Zhu X, Schaff HV, Liu Y, Wan S, Wei X.
abstractText:
Background

Nonobstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (nHCM), defined as hypertrophic cardiomyopathy without left ventricular outflow tract obstruction, remains challenging to treat because of its heterogeneous pathophysiology. This study evaluated the safety and efficacy of transapical beating-heart septal myectomy in patients with symptomatic nHCM.

Methods

Patients with symptomatic, drug-refractory nHCM were prospectively enrolled to undergo transapical beating-heart septal myectomy through a left minithoracotomy. Under real-time transesophageal echocardiographic guidance, septal myectomy was tailored to relieve systolic cavity obliteration and mid-to-apical ventricular obstruction and to enlarge the left ventricular cavity. The primary end point was procedural success at 6 to 12 months postoperatively, defined as fulfillment of all prespecified criteria compared with baseline: ≥1-class improvement in New York Heart Association functional class, ≥10-point increase in Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire score, ≥10-mL increase in stroke volume, and normal or grade I diastolic function.

Results

Between January 2023 and January 2025, 97 consecutive eligible patients with nHCM underwent transapical beating-heart septal myectomy at Tongji Hospital. At postoperative 6 to 12 months, procedural success was achieved in 87.6%. Specifically, New York Heart Association functional class I increased from 0% at baseline to 93.8% at follow-up, the median Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire score improved from 64 (interquartile range, 56-69) to 87 (interquartile range, 82-92; P<0.001), the stroke volume increased from 53.5 mL (interquartile range, 41.0-66.6 mL) to 70.8 mL (interquartile range, 61.3-82.3 mL; P<0.001), and normal or grade I diastolic function increased from 65.6% to 97.9%. Among patients who underwent paired cardiopulmonary exercise testing (n=58), peak oxygen uptake increased by 1.1±2.9 mL/kg/min (P=0.008). In an exploratory, hypothesis-generating analysis of 12 patients with paired 13N-ammonia positron emission tomography, coronary flow reserve increased from 1.8±0.3 to 2.0±0.4 (P=0.034). Adverse events included mitral valve injury (n=1) and ventricular septal perforation (n=1), the latter resulting in 1 postoperative death.

Conclusions

Transapical beating-heart septal myectomy was associated with favorable left ventricular geometric remodeling and meaningful improvements in symptoms, health status, and functional capacity in selected patients with symptomatic nHCM. Being a potential therapeutic option for a previously difficult-to-treat population, it warrants further evaluation in controlled, multicenter studies.

Registration

URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT05648825.

title: Pediatric Cardiac Surgery in the Pre-Conflict Era: A Retrospective Analysis of the Surgical patterns and outcomes Medani Heart Center, Sudan (2019–2022)
authorString: Hassan S, Mohieldeen A, Fargalla M, Elmostafa B, Mohammed Y.
abstractText: Background Pediatric cardiac care in sub-Saharan Africa is characterized by a significant surgical-medical gap, where late referrals and infrastructural limitations complicate outcomes for congenital and acquired heart disease. While Medani Heart Center (MHC) emerged as a critical tertiary referral hub in Sudan to address these geographic and systemic barriers, the 2023 conflict has fundamentally disrupted these specialized services. Documenting the clinical and procedural patterns established prior to this crisis is essential to providing a baseline for assessing current survival gaps and guiding future service restoration. This study evaluates the surgical patterns, patient demographics, and perioperative outcomes of pediatric cardiac patients managed at the MHC between 2019 and 2022. Methods We conducted a retrospective, observational cohort study of pediatric patients aged under 18 years who underwent cardiac surgical intervention at the Medani Heart Center (MHC), Sudan, between January 1, 2019, and December 31, 2022. Data were retrieved from the center’s official registry for 250 patients who met the inclusion criteria. Although the study was intended to extend into 2023, data from January 2023 onward were lost due to the destruction of the center's infrastructure during the national conflict. This analysis represents the final, verified clinical record of the MHC’s pediatric cardiac services prior to the suspension of operations. Results Among the 250 pediatric cardiac surgical patients analyzed, the majority were males (54.8%) and predominantly school-age children (54.0%). Procedures comprised structural congenital repairs (ventricular septal defect [VSD] 24.4%, atrial septal defect [ASD] 10.0%, patent ductus arteriosus [PDA] 9.2%), complex cyanotic anomaly corrections (Tetralogy of Fallot 18.8%), and valvular interventions (23.6%). Surgical volume peaked in 2021 (38.4%) before stabilizing in 2022. Post-operative outcomes were largely favorable, with 83.6% of patients experiencing an uneventful recovery and 87.2% requiring an intensive care unit (ICU) stay of 5 days or fewer. The overall mortality rate was 4.0%. Conclusion This study confirms that a high-volume regional pediatric cardiac surgical program can deliver efficient, high-quality care, evidenced by an 83.6% complication-free recovery rate and streamlined ICU management. The surge and subsequent stabilization of procedural volumes indicate a maturing clinical workflow capable of managing complex congenital and valvular cases. These findings validate the effectiveness of past clinical protocols while highlighting an essential baseline for future cardiovascular care reconstruction in the region. Clinical trial number: Not applicable.

title: Final 5-year results of the Thoracic Branch Endoprosthesis Feasibility Trials for Treatment of Aortic Arch Aneurysms.
authorString: Maximus S, Huang Y, Dake MD, Fischbein MP, Bavaria JE, Desai ND, Singh MJ, Fillinger M, Suckow BD, Matsumura JS, Patel HJ, Makaroun MS, Oderich GS.
abstractText:
Objective

To report final 5-year outcomes from prospective multicenter feasibility studies of the GORE® TAG® Thoracic Branch Endoprosthesis (TBE) for aneurysms involving the proximal descending thoracic aorta and aortic arch (zones 0-2).

Methods

Forty consecutive patients (23 male; mean age, 74±10 years) were enrolled at six sites in prospective, nonrandomized feasibility trials (2014-2016). Patients underwent TEVAR with proximal TBE in zone 0/1 (n=9; NCT02264977) or zone 2 (n=31; NCT02021812). A clinical events committee adjudicated aneurysm-related and all-cause mortality, major adverse events, and cerebrovascular events. Core laboratory analysis assessed endoleaks (types I-IV), aneurysm sac enlargement, device migration, and side branch patency. Five-year cumulative risk rates (2006 days) were estimated using Kaplan-Meier analysis.

Results

The median follow-up time among survivors was 60.2 months (range, 25.8 to 66.0), with 17 patients completing the required 5-year clinical and imaging follow-up across both studies. Eleven late deaths occurred; KM-estimated cumulative risk of 5-year all-cause mortality was 29% (95% CI: 17%-46%). One zone 2 death was adjudicated as aortic-related (2.5%; 95% CI: 0.4%-16%) due to ascending aortic rupture, with no ruptures occurring within treated aortic segments. Reintervention risk through 5 years was low (KM-estimated cumulative risk, 5.1%; 95% CI: 1.3%-19%), with two events, both in the zone 2 cohort. Five patients experienced stroke events through 5 years, corresponding to a KM cumulative risk of 19.0% ( 95% CI: 7.2%-43%), two in zone 2 and three in zone 0/1. Two patients had target vessel instability (5.0%, 95% CI: 0.6%-16.9%). Two side-branch patency events occurred in zone 2: one complete side-branch occlusion in the LSA associated with transient mild arm claudication and one asymptomatic partial occlusion, primary patency through 5-year follow-up was 94.8% (37/39 evaluable patients). Core laboratory identified endoleaks in 12 patients (30.8%; 95% CI: 15%-45%). Three patients (7.7%) had a type I or III endoleak by 5 years, all in the zone 2 arm; these included type IA in one patient (2.6%) and type III in two patients (5.1%). Additionally indeterminate (n=8, 20.5%) and type II (n=6, 15.4%) endoleaks were observed. Cumulative risk rate of aneurysm sac enlargement through 5-years was 15.0% for all patients (95% CI: 5.6%-30.3%), with events occurring in three zone 2 patients and one zone 0/1 patient.

Conclusions

At 5 years, the early feasibility studies demonstrated excellent side branch patency, a low incidence of type IA endoleak, low aortic-related mortality, and no rupture within the treated aortic segments. Larger studies are needed to better define zone-specific cerebrovascular risk and long-term durability.

title: Association between periodontitis and coronary plaque composition: can early periodontal treatment influence coronary artery disease progression? A study protocol for a prospective, randomized controlled trial.
authorString: Weichsel L, Elsayed A, Kögel M, Pfisterer SG, Lähdeniemi IAK, März W, Katus HA, Frey N, Korosoglou G.
abstractText:
Objective

The (PERIOdontitis and Coronary Artery Disease) PERIOCAD study aims to investigate the association between periodontitis and coronary artery disease (CAD) in patients undergoing cardiac computed tomography angiography (CCTA) and the effectiveness of early versus late periodontitis (PD) treatment on systemic inflammation and CAD progression.

Background

PD and CAD are common diseases, sharing underlying molecular mechanisms, like systemic inflammation and endothelial dysfunction. Epidemiological and genetic studies suggest a strong link between PD and CAD. Yet, it remains unclear whether treatment of periodontitis may attenuate progression of arteriosclerosis. CCTA enables reproducible quantitative assessment of coronary plaque volumes and composition, providing metrics for both cross-sectional associations and longitudinal changes of plaque burden.

Methods

PERIOCAD is a prospective, randomized, controlled trial (RCT) aiming to enroll 200 patients who undergo clinically indicated CCTA. All participants will undergo comprehensive periodontal status assessment and patients diagnosed with PD (estimated n = 100) will be randomized 1:1 to either early, systematic PD therapy (intervention arm) or delayed care after 2 years (control arm). CCTA analysis will include quantitative plaque volumes and composition, assessment of high-risk plaque features and evaluation of pericoronary adipose tissue attenuation (PCAT). Cardiac and inflammatory biomarkers will be assessed at baseline and after 24 months. Follow-up evaluations are scheduled at 12 and 24 months to reassess periodontal status. In addition, changes in plaque burden will be longitudinally assessed in case of clinically indicated repeat CCTA scans. The primary endpoint is the influence of periodontal treatment on cardiac and inflammatory biomarkers at 24 months. Secondary endpoints include major adverse cardiovascular events during follow-up, changes in plaque parameters and PCAT on serial CCTA, and associations between CCTA metrics and PD at baseline.

Discussion

PERIOCAD is expected to provide unique insights regarding the relationship between PD and CAD, being to our knowledge the first RCT to investigate the impact of PD therapy on systemic inflammation and CAD progression in symptomatic patients. Our findings could have significant implications for interdisciplinary cardiovascular disease prevention strategies and public health policies.

Trial registration

German Clinical Trials Register DRKS00038470 (Date of registration:2025-11-24).
