title: Repurposing drugs for aortic aneurysm: unlocking new therapeutic opportunities.
authorString: Li YH, Wang X, She ZH, Zhang Z.
abstractText: Aortic aneurysm (AA) is a life-threatening vascular disease for which no pharmacological therapy has been proven to effectively limit disease progression. Drug repurposing (DR), which leverages existing drugs with established safety profiles, offers a promising and cost-effective strategy to accelerate therapeutic development for AA. In this review, we summarize recent advances in DR research for AA, highlighting the emerging framework that integrates computational prediction with experimental and clinical validation. We discuss key repurposed drug candidates, evaluate the current state of translational evidence, and examine the challenges that have hindered clinical success despite encouraging preclinical findings. Finally, we outline opportunities to enhance target identification, patient stratification, and clinical trial design. By bridging mechanistic discovery and translational application, DR may provide a practical pathway toward effective medical therapies for aneurysmal disease.

title: CT-Derived Leaflet Sizing Discrepancy Is Associated With Valve-Related Events After Aortic Valve Neocuspidization
authorString: Yokawa K, Tanaka Y, Ishihama T, Uesugi K, Ishimoto K, Higuma T, Yoshida K, Obo H, Wakiyama H.
abstractText: Background Accurate leaflet sizing is essential for aortic valve neocuspidization (AVNeo), yet objective anatomical references for selecting leaflet size remain limited. We investigated whether the discrepancy between a patient-specific computed tomography (CT)-derived anatomical reference and intraoperatively selected leaflet size was associated with valve-related events after AVNeo and assessed the reproducibility of the CT-derived measurements. Methods We retrospectively investigated 32 consecutive patients who underwent AVNeo with preoperative ECG-gated CT. A CT-derived reference leaflet size was geometrically estimated from the intercommissural distance. Sizing discrepancy was defined as the difference between the CT-derived reference and intraoperatively selected leaflet size, with maximum Δ representing the largest discrepancy among the three cusps. Interobserver reproducibility was assessed using independent measurements by a radiologic technologist, an experienced cardiovascular surgeon, and a cardiovascular surgery trainee. Associations with valve-related events were assessed using Cox proportional hazards and receiver operating characteristic analyses, and interobserver reliability was evaluated using intraclass correlation coefficients. Results During a median follow-up of 23 months, valve-related events occurred in eight patients. Greater maximum Δ was associated with valve-related events (hazard ratio, 1.39 per 1-mm increase; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.09–1.78; P  = 0.004). Exploratory receiver operating characteristic analysis identified 4.9 mm as the optimal cutoff (area under the curve [AUC], 0.818; 95% CI, 0.647–0.989), and patients with maximum Δ ≥ 4.9 mm had lower valve-related event-free survival (log-rank P  = 0.020). Interobserver reliability was moderate to good, with intraclass correlation coefficients of 0.726 (95% CI, 0.339–0.881), 0.703 (95% CI, 0.231–0.879), and 0.832 (95% CI, 0.516–0.932) for the right coronary, left coronary, and noncoronary cusps, respectively. Observer-specific AUCs for maximum Δ were 0.776 for the radiologic technologist, 0.818 for the experienced cardiovascular surgeon, and 0.667 for the cardiovascular surgery trainee. Conclusions Greater discrepancy between the CT-derived anatomical reference and intraoperatively selected leaflet size was associated with subsequent valve-related events after AVNeo. CT-derived measurements showed moderate-to-good interobserver reliability, although discriminatory performance varied among observers. These findings support further investigation of CT-derived anatomical sizing as a patient-specific reference for AVNeo, while highlighting the need for standardized measurement methods and external validation in larger cohorts. Clinical trial registration Not applicable. This study was a retrospective observational study and was not a clinical trial.

title: Atrial Fibrillation Screening-to-Anticoagulation Pathways in Low- and Middle-Income Countries: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Jamileh E, Muhammad F, Farooq O, Al-Kindi S, Dakhil Z, Alasnag M, Al Suwaidi J, Refaat MM, Hosseini K, Al Mahmeed W, Somani R, Zakkar M, Ng GA, Antoun I.
abstractText:
Background

Atrial fibrillation (AF) is an important cause of preventable stroke in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where diagnostic and treatment gaps may limit screening effectiveness.

Objectives

This study aims to evaluate AF screening in LMICs as a screening-to-anticoagulation pathway, focusing on reach, equity, diagnostic confirmation, anticoagulation uptake, and health-system capacity.

Methods

MEDLINE via PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science, and CENTRAL were searched from inception to July 2026. LMIC studies reporting population-facing AF screening or screening-linked care were included. Logit-transformed proportions were pooled using restricted maximum-likelihood random-effects models with modified Hartung-Knapp CIs; binomial-normal generalized linear mixed models were used in sensitivity analyses. Pathway stages were synthesized from outcome-specific study subsets rather than a single longitudinal cohort.

Results

Thirty-seven reports from 13 LMICs and 1 multinational cohort were included. Across 22 community- or population-based studies, confirmed AF averaged 1.24% (95% CI: 0.79%-1.94%; I2 = 98.8%; 95% prediction interval: 0.16%-8.83%). Newly detected AF averaged 0.95% (95% CI: 0.43%-2.11%; I2 = 99.2%; prediction interval: 0.08%-9.97%). In separate study subsets, prior AF awareness was 50.7%, study-defined high stroke risk or oral anticoagulation indication was 78.9%, and oral anticoagulation coverage among study-defined eligible/high-risk participants was 22.8%. Reach ranged from 9.7% to 98.8%, and confirmation completion was 57.5% to 61.8% in 2 programs.

Conclusions

AF screening in LMICs identifies substantial but highly variable detection and treatment gaps. Pooled proportions should be interpreted as cross-study summaries rather than expected rates for a specific setting. Effective programs require representative reach, timely confirmation, appropriate stroke-risk and valvular assessment, access to anticoagulation, and longitudinal follow-up.

title: Comprehensive meta-analysis and meta-regression of peripartum cardiomyopathy: risk factors, cardiac function, and maternal-neonatal outcomes in 66,908 PPCM patients.
authorString: Zenjaya KT, Christopher C, Timothy RA, Thiehunan CC, Sukmawati SAPW, Pintono K, Muliyanto JA, Ricardo E, Nugrahani ASD, Hoevelmann J.

journal.title: The Egyptian heart journal : (EHJ) : official bulletin of the Egyptian Society of Cardiology

abstractText:
Background

Peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM) is a potentially life-threatening condition and often diagnosed late, with many patients presenting in advanced heart failure. This study aimed to examine the demographics, risk factors, comorbidities, clinical characteristics, treatment patterns, and maternal and neonatal outcomes METHODS AND RESULTS: This meta-analysis followed PRISMA guidelines. A total of 4,341 records up to May 2025, were identified and 122 eligible studies reporting PPCM clinical characteristics, treatments, and outcomes were included. Heterogeneity was explored through meta-regression analyses assessing demographic, clinical, and study-level variables. An aggregate of 66,908 PPCM patients were reported across the included studies, with a pooled mean age of 30.1 years. Black or African women accounted for a disproportionately large proportion of the reported population compared with other racial groups. Approximately 62% of women presented with advanced heart failure (NYHA class III/IV). Pre-existing diabetes mellitus (OR 5.09) and hypertensive disorders, including pre-existing hypertension (OR 10.07), gestational hypertension (OR 7.75), and pre-eclampsia (OR 9.27), were associated with higher odds of PPCM. The pooled mean LVEF at diagnosis was 29.98%, which subsequently improved to 46.47% at 6 months and 49.12% at 12 months. Despite over half of PPCM patients achieving LVEF recovery (55%), maternal mortality remained high at 6% and neonatal mortality at 4%. Pharmacological treatments for PPCM varied widely, with high heterogeneity suggesting substantial differences in prescribing practices across studies.

Conclusion

The high prevalence of NYHA class III/IV symptoms at diagnosis underscores the importance of early detection and monitoring, while the variation in reported use of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) across studies highlights potential opportunities to optimize treatment in patients with PPCM. The observed improvement in LVEF during follow-up indicates that cardiac recovery is possible in patients with PPCM. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously given the observational nature and substantial heterogeneity of the included studies.

title: The gut microbiome and incident atherosclerotic cardiovascular events: Prospective analyses in three Swedish cohorts
authorString: Pertiwi K, Hammar U, Dekkers KF, Coward E, Kambur O, Baldanzi G, Delgado-Velandia M, Sayols-Baixeras S, Yuan S, Persson P, Gabrielsson D, Miari M, Volpiano CG, Méric G, Jönsson D, Engström G, Smith JG, Michaëlsson K, Melander O, Ärnlöv J, Knight R, Hofmann R, Niiranen T, Havulinna AS, Salomaa V, Hveem K, Ohlsson C, Orho-Melander M, Larsson SC, Fall T.
abstractText:
ABSTRACT

Background

Variation in the gut microbiome composition has been associated with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) in case-control designs. We aimed to investigate associations with incident ASCVD events applying a prospective design to reduce the impact of reverse causality.

Methods

We assessed associations between gut microbiome features measured by shotgun metagenomic sequencing and incident total ASCVD, ischemic heart disease (IHD) and ischemic stroke, including fatal and non-fatal events as defined by registry follow-up in 17,216 participants from three Swedish population-based cohorts (SCAPIS, SIMPLER, and MOS). Results from Cox proportional hazards regression models adjusted for demographic, and lifestyle factors, medication, and prevalent diabetes were combined across cohorts using a fixed-effect meta-analysis accounting for multiple testing. Associations were tested for replication in HUNT and FINRISK.

Results

During a median of 6-8 y follow-up, 769 incident ASCVD events occurred. Species diversity was inversely associated with ASCVD and IHD, with a hazard ratio for IHD of 0.86 per SD increase in species richness (95% CI: 0.79-0.95). Sixty-eight common species (i.e., present in ≥30% individuals) were associated with incident IHD after adjusting for sex and birth country, but only eight remained in fully adjusted models, including Ruminococcus_B gnavus . Among others, inverse associations were observed for SFEL01 sp004557245 and Fimadaptatus sp900553645 from Christensenellales , an order in which butyrate production has been reported. Streptococcus mutans and Limosilactobacillus fermentum, oral-associated species previously associated with coronary atherosclerosis, were associated with a higher risk of incident IHD, which remained after adjustment for dental health. Replication analysis in the HUNT study supported the finding for S. mutans . No associations were observed with ischemic stroke.

Conclusions

Gut species diversity and specific species abundance were associated with incident IHD, providing evidence supporting a protective role of two Christensenellales species and an adverse role of oral species and R. gnavus in the development of IHD.

title: Navigating Severe Aortic Stenosis in Hip Fracture Surgery: Perioperative Management and Surgical Timing.
authorString: Bui R, Dong JL, Tran A, Achanta L, Hasoon J, Abd-Elsayed A, Kaye AD, Nguyen A.
abstractText: Severe aortic stenosis presents a significant challenge in patients requiring urgent hip fracture surgery. Although aortic stenosis increases the risk of cardiovascular complications and mortality, delaying fixation may independently contribute to morbidity, functional decline, and mortality. This creates a dilemma regarding whether to proceed directly to surgery or delay fracture repair for aortic valve intervention. This review examines management of patients with severe aortic stenosis pending urgent hip fracture surgery, with emphasis on timing, preoperative evaluation, anesthetic selection, and hemodynamic management. Current evidence suggests that asymptomatic patients with preserved left ventricular systolic function and stable hemodynamics may often undergo timely fracture fixation with appropriate monitoring. In contrast, symptomatic patients, those with ventricular dysfunction or hemodynamic instability, and patients with particularly severe disease may require evaluation for valvular intervention. When intervention is indicated, transcatheter aortic valve replacement may offer a more rapid treatment in certain patients, while balloon aortic valvuloplasty may serve as a temporizing strategy. For patients proceeding directly to fracture fixation, preservation of preload, systemic vascular resistance, coronary perfusion, and sinus rhythm is essential. Current evidence does not establish a clear superiority of general versus neuraxial anesthesia, supporting individualized anesthetic planning and avoidance of abrupt hemodynamic changes. Ultimately, management should balance the risks of delaying fracture fixation against the risks of surgery through coordinated, multidisciplinary decision-making.

title: Real-World 2-Year Outcomes of the Inspiron™ Biodegradable Polymer Sirolimus-Eluting Stent.
authorString: Soccol RC, Ribeiro HB, Lasevitch R, Pellegrini D, Silva EERD, Mattos CAS, Lima Filho A, Takeshita N, Câmara SSP, Costa Junior JR, Freitas LZF, Sabedotti M, Teixeirense PT, Truffa MAM, Gasperi R, Abreu ES, Bassani IA, Mangione JA, Cavalieri M, Alves GMP, Andrade PB, Maestri R, Cavalcanti RRC, Paiva MS, Hirga MO, Arruda JA, Pivatelli FC, Zandomenico JG, Caramori PRA.
abstractText:
Background

The Inspiron™ sirolimus-eluting stent (SES) is a third-generation coronary stent featuring thin struts and an abluminal biodegradable polymer coating. Although it is widely used in Brazil, long-term real-world evidence remains limited.

Objectives

To evaluate the safety and effectiveness of the Inspiron™ SES over 24 months in an unselected population undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI).

Methods

This pooled analysis included 2,803 consecutive patients who underwent Inspiron™ SES implantation between June 2017 and January 2022 at 25 Brazilian centers. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as the composite of cardiovascular death, MI, and target lesion revascularization (TLR) at 24 months. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, Cox proportional hazards regression, and restricted cubic spline models were used. A two-sided p-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.

Results

At 24 months, the cumulative incidence of MACE was 6.7%, with rates of 5.4% for all-cause mortality, 2.3% for cardiovascular mortality, 1.2% for MI, 0.9% for TLR, and 0.6% for definite or probable stent thrombosis (ST). Patients with a vessel diameter < 2.5 mm had significantly higher rates of MACE, cardiovascular death, repeat revascularization, and ST (p = 0.022). Independent predictors of MACE included older age (p = 0.034), left main or three-vessel coronary artery disease (p = 0.024), and acute coronary syndrome as the indication for PCI (p < 0.001).

Conclusions

In this large real-world registry, the Inspiron™ SES demonstrated favorable safety and effectiveness through 24 months, with low rates of ST and repeat revascularization despite the inclusion of complex coronary lesions.

title: Stress Echocardiographic Strain-Dyssynchrony Interactions Identify Prognostic Phenotypes in Chagas Cardiomyopathy: A Pilot Study.
authorString: Athayde GAT, Borges BCC, Pinheiro AO, Souza AL, Oliveira CP, Martins SAM, Teixeira RA, Siqueira SF, Mathias W, Martinelli Filho M.
abstractText:
Background

Mechanical heterogeneity is a hallmark of advanced cardiomyopathy, although stress echocardiography traditionally focuses on ischemia or global systolic reserve. Exercise stress echocardiography may identify distinct mechanical phenotypes in chronic Chagas cardiomyopathy (CCC) through integrated assessment of strain and dyssynchrony behavior.

Objective

To investigate the interaction between contractile reserve and intraventricular dyssynchrony (IVD) during exercise stress echocardiography and its association with clinical outcomes in patients with CCC.

Methods

Forty patients with severe CCC (left ventricular ejection fraction ≤ 35%, non-LBBB QRS morphology) underwent symptom-limited treadmill stress echocardiography. Global longitudinal strain (GLS), IVD, and conventional echocardiographic parameters were assessed at rest and immediately after peak exercise. Patients were stratified into four groups according to GLS and IVD variation. The primary endpoint was a composite of death, heart transplantation, or hospitalization for heart failure over a 2-year follow-up. Statistical significance was defined as p < 0.05.

Results

After a median follow-up of 729 days, 20 patients (50%) reached the primary endpoint. Patients without contractile reserve and without dyssynchrony improvement during exercise had significantly lower event-free survival compared with the remaining groups (p < 0.01). When analyzed separately, both absence of contractile reserve and unfavorable dyssynchrony response were associated with adverse outcomes. In multivariable analysis, only right ventricular function remained independently associated with the primary outcome (hazard ratio 0.83, 95% confidence interval 0.71-0.96; p = 0.014).

Conclusions

Integration of strain-derived contractile reserve and IVD during physiologic stress may help identify prognostic phenotypes beyond ejection fraction in CCC and supports the concept of dynamic mechanical phenotyping in advanced cardiomyopathy.

title: Healthcare providers' knowledge on Chagas disease in endemic areas from Pará in the Amazon, Brazil: an evaluation during in loco professional trainingsFIRST REVIEW ROUND - REVIEWERS' COMMENTSREVIEWERS' COMMENTS.
authorString: Saraiva RM, Sangenis LHC, Veloso HH, Portela LF, Varela MC, de Souza DDSM, Pinto AYDN, Valente SA, Valente VDC, Ribeiro RMDS, Amador ECDC, Meis J, Garzoni LR, Tapajós A, Monteiro EDA, Menna-Barreto RF.
abstractText:
Background

Chagas disease (CD) has a high mortality and socioeconomic burden in endemic regions. In Brazil, the State of Pará in the Amazon concentrates the majority of acute CD cases. Improving healthcare professionals' knowledge on CD is a promising strategy to mitigate the disease consequences.

Objectives

To evaluate and improve knowledge on CD of healthcare professionals who work in several municipalities of the State of Pará, our team offered short courses about crucial aspects of this disease, including diagnosis, prognosis and therapeutics.

Methods

During 2018 and 2019, three 16-hour courses were offered to a total of 144 healthcare professionals (40 physicians and 104 nurses and other healthcare professionals) from 19 municipalities in the State of Pará. Questionnaires were applied before and after the courses to assess their level of knowledge on CD and the degree to which they retained the information. A qualitative questionnaire was used during the first two courses, and a questionnaire with multiple-choice questions was used in the third course.

Findings

Among those who answered the qualitative questionnaire before attending the courses, although most participants could name the causative agent of CD, only 64.0% (48/75) knew the name of the drug used for CD treatment, 38.7% (29/75) knew the treatment duration, and 13.3% (10/75) were familiar with the main adverse reaction associated with benznidazole (BZN) use. Among the professionals who answered the multiple-choice questionnaires applied during the third course, the rate of correct answers increased significantly from 40.6 ± 10.7% before the course to 55.2 ± 5.3% after the course (p < 0.0001).

Main conclusions

A low level of knowledge on CD was found among healthcare professionals from Amazon region and is a matter of concern. Continued medical and healthcare providers education is necessary to improve this reality.

title: Delayed Clinical Recognition of Postinfarction Ventricular Septal Rupture After Initially Uncomplicated PCI: A Case Report.
authorString: Aden AS, Ahmed SA, Waberi MM, Kuru Ö, Abdirahman AM, Ahmed AA, Jayte M, Abdi IA, Ahmed AA, Aydin MZ, Dahir OF.
abstractText:
Background

Ventricular septal rupture (VSR) is a rare but potentially fatal mechanical complication of acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Although its incidence has declined with advances in reperfusion therapy, delayed clinical recognition may remain challenging, particularly in patients who are initially hemodynamically stable.

Case presentation

A 62-year-old man with hypertension presented with a 13-day history of chest pain. He was hemodynamically stable on admission, with ST-segment elevation in the inferior leads and an elevated cardiac troponin I level of 4.78 ng/mL. Coronary angiography demonstrated 99% stenosis of the right coronary artery (RCA) and 65%-70% stenosis of the left anterior descending (LAD) artery. The RCA lesion was successfully treated with balloon predilatation and drug-eluting stent implantation, restoring thrombolysis in myocardial infarction (TIMI) Grade III flow without immediate complications. Echocardiography performed before PCI and repeated before discharge showed no evidence of VSR or another mechanical complication. The patient was discharged the following day but returned 4 days later with worsening dyspnea, orthopnea, bilateral inspiratory crackles, and a new pansystolic murmur. Urgent transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated a 21-mm VSR involving the basal inferior interventricular septum, with left-to-right shunting, a left ventricular ejection fraction of 60%, preserved right ventricular systolic function, severe mitral regurgitation, and an estimated pulmonary artery systolic pressure of 25 mmHg. After approximately 14 days of stabilization and observation following diagnosis, he underwent surgical VSR repair and mechanical mitral valve replacement for severe mitral regurgitation. Postoperative echocardiography showed no reported residual abnormalities, and he remained clinically stable at 2-month follow-up.

Conclusions

This case highlights the importance of considering postinfarction VSR when new heart failure symptoms and a pansystolic murmur develop after an initially uncomplicated PCI, even when early echocardiographic examinations show no mechanical complication. Prompt echocardiographic reassessment and multidisciplinary management are essential for timely diagnosis and definitive treatment.

title: Valve Embolisation During Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation (TAVI): Clinical Outcomes and CT-Derived Anatomical Characteristics.
authorString: Dalip D, Banning A, Rajendra R.
abstractText: Background Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has transformed the management of severe aortic stenosis, offering an effective alternative for elderly patients and those at high surgical risk who are not ideal candidates for open-heart surgery. Of late, there is an expansion into intermediate- and low-risk populations as well. Transcatheter valve embolisation or migration (TVEM) is a rare but potentially fatal complication. Predictors of TVEM are incompletely understood, and there is a gap in evidence, looking specifically at the CT-derived anatomical characteristics of TVEM. Aim This study aimed to quantify the incidence of TVEM in a high-volume tertiary centre and characterise anatomical patterns in patients experiencing TVEM during TAVI. Methods This is a retrospective, single-centre study. Patients registered as having TVEM were identified using the local database from June 2014 to June 2024. Case notes of these patients were then studied to assess the management of TVEM and outcomes. For this cohort of patients, preprocedural CTs were analysed in detail, including annulus perimeter and area, qualitative leaflet calcification grading (moderate, severe, very severe), presence of annular/aorto-mitral curtain (AMC) calcification, and minimum sinus of Valsalva (SOV) diameter. Procedural data included initial embolised valve type and the bailout strategy. Results The incidence of TVEM was 0.51% with a 30-day mortality of 40% and average length of stay in hospital of 11.5 days, compared with the uncomplicated TAVI length of stay averaging 2.1 days. There was a periprocedural complication of stroke in 10% of patients (1 patient) and no vascular access site complication. Leaflet calcification was severe or very severe in 9/10 patients, with AMC calcification present in half. The mean minimum SOV diameter was 28.7 +/- 3.5 mm (23-34 mm), and several cases demonstrated markedly constrained aortic root anatomy. All embolised valves were self-expanding devices. In 4/10 cases, a balloon-expandable THV was used as the second device, while 6/10 were treated with another self-expanding THV. Conclusion Findings suggest that TVEM is a rare complication associated with substantial short-term mortality. Severe leaflet calcification, AMC calcification, and smaller SOV dimensions were frequently observed in this cohort, and all embolised valves were self-expanding. These findings are descriptive and hypothesis-generating; without a comparator group, their association with embolisation risk cannot be established. However, these anatomical findings warrant careful preprocedural assessment, while prospective comparative studies are needed to determine their association with TVEM risk.

title: Cardiac Involvement in Patients With Chagas Disease Is Associated With an Increased Risk of Ischemic Stroke.
authorString: da Silva Júnior JA, do Nascimento EGC, Amaral DAS, Chagas AFD, Ferreira PDO, Rocha TRD, de Andrade MF, Andrade CM.
abstractText:
Context

A substantial proportion of patients with Chagas disease experience cardioembolic cerebrovascular events, which are common and potentially severe and account for a relevant proportion of Chagas disease-related deaths.

Aims

To analyze potential factors associated with the risk of ischemic stroke in patients with Chagas disease.

Settings and design

A descriptive, observational, cross-sectional study based on the systematic analysis of data from patients with Chagas disease.

Methods and materials

A total of 186 patients were evaluated using a clinical and epidemiological protocol. Assessments included the NYHA and ACC/AHA-DC heart failure classifications, the ischemic stroke risk score, and the Rassi score. Data were analyzed using binomial regression models, Pearson's chi-square test, and descriptive statistics for the variables studied.

Results

Ischemic stroke risk was significantly associated with the clinical form of Chagas disease. A normal cardiothoracic index was associated with a low risk of ischemic stroke, suggesting that an abnormal cardiothoracic index may be associated with a moderate-to-high risk of ischemic stroke.

Conclusions

Patients with the cardiac form of Chagas disease are more likely to have a moderate-to-high risk of ischemic stroke, highlighting the need for closer attention to these individuals. Further studies are needed to identify additional factors that may influence ischemic stroke risk.

title: Association of Nontraumatic Osteonecrosis of the Femoral Head With Major Cardiovascular and Cerebrovascular Events: A Nationwide Cohort Study of Korea.
authorString: Chung SW, Lee YJ, Koo KH, Ha YJ.
abstractText:
Background

Nontraumatic osteonecrosis of the femoral head (ONFH) is associated with systemic comorbidities and vascular risk factors, raising the possibility of an association with major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCEs). This study aimed to evaluate its long-term association with MACCEs.

Methods

Data were obtained from the Korean National Health Insurance Service Sample Cohort 2.0 (2006-2015). Incident ONFH cases diagnosed between 2008 and 2010 (n = 1,150) were initially matched with 1:5 controls (n = 5,750) by age, sex, residential area, and index year. To further improve covariate balance, additional propensity score (PS) matching was performed (1:5), yielding a PS-matched cohort of 6,038 participants (ONFH, n = 1,130; controls, n = 4,908). MACCEs (myocardial infarction, unstable angina, revascularization, heart failure, and stroke/transient ischemic attack) were tracked for up to seven years, and associations were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards models.

Results

In the PS-matched cohort, MACCEs occurred more frequently in the ONFH group than in controls (19.4% vs. 15.3%), with reduced MACCE-free survival (log-rank P < 0.001). Incidence-rate analysis showed an increased risk of MACCEs (incidence rate ratio [IRR], 1.29; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.11-1.50) and cardiovascular events (IRR, 1.42; 95% CI, 1.18-1.71), whereas cerebrovascular events were not significantly different (IRR, 1.11; 95% CI, 0.86-1.43). In multivariable Cox models, ONFH was associated with a higher risk of MACCEs (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.19; 95% CI, 1.02-1.38). Sensitivity analyses excluding patients with systemic autoimmune diseases and excluding glucocorticoid users showed consistent results.

Conclusion

In this nationwide cohort, nontraumatic ONFH was associated with an increased long-term risk of MACCEs, driven mainly by cardiovascular events. These findings suggest that nontraumatic ONFH may serve as a clinically relevant marker of increased cardiovascular risk, supporting attention to cardiovascular risk assessment in patients with ONFH.

title: Does Mild Anemia Associate With 3-Month Vascular Outcomes in Severe Acute Ischemic Stroke?
authorString: Kim H, Kim JT, Park MS, Lee JS, Kim BJ, Kang J, Kim DY, Lee KJ, Kim CK, Park JM, Kang K, Lee SJ, Kim JG, Cha JK, Kim DH, Park TH, Lee JY, Lee K, Lee J, Kwon DH, Hong KS, Cho YJ, Park HK, Lee BC, Yu KH, Oh MS, Lee M, Kim DE, Gwak DS, Choi JC, Kang CH, Kwon JH, Kim WJ, Shin DI, Yum KS, Sohn SI, Hong JH, Lee SH, Kim C, Park KY, Jeong HB, Lee J, Bae HJ.
abstractText:
Background

Anemia has been shown to be independently associated with poor outcomes in critically ill patients. Despite this, the impact of hemoglobin (Hb) levels on prognosis among patients with severe acute ischemic stroke (AIS) requiring neurocritical care has not been well established. We therefore sought to evaluate the relationship between Hb levels and clinical outcomes in this population.

Methods

This study was an analysis of a prospective, multicenter, nationwide stroke registry between January 2011 and April 2023. We included patients within 7 days of onset AIS whose severity of National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale more than 16 scores. Hb levels were categorized into 4 groups; 1) moderate to severe anemia (Hb < 11 g/dL), 2) mild anemia(men: 11.0-12.9 g/dL, women: 11.0-11.9 g/dL), 3) normal (men: 13.0-17.0 g/dL, women: 12.0-15.5 g/dL), 4) polycythemia (men > 17.0 g/dL, women > 15.6 g/dL). The primary outcome is defined as a composite of recurrent stroke, myocardial infarction (MI), and all-cause mortality within 3-month.

Results

A total of 8,615 patients with severe AIS were included in the final analysis (mean age, 74.3 ± 12.1 years; 47.8% male). The prevalence of moderate-to-severe anemia was 15.9%, mild anemia 17.0%, normal Hb levels 62.4%, and polycythemia 4.6%. Compared with patients with normal Hb levels, those with mild or moderate-to-severe anemia exhibited higher 3-month rates of the composite outcome of recurrent stroke, MI, and all-cause mortality. After multivariable adjustment, both mild and moderate-to-severe anemia remained independently associated with an increased risk of the 3-month composite outcome (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.15; 1.04-1.28; P = 0.009).

Conclusion

In patients with severe AIS requiring neurocritical care, lower Hb levels were independently associated with an increased risk of 3-month composite vascular outcomes, even at the level of mild anemia.

title: Evidence for interventions in healthcare settings targeting adult patients with multimorbidity in low- and middle-income countries: a mixed-methods systematic review.
authorString: George T, de Mendonça L, Inbarani E, Oommen AM, Kalimuthu M, McMorrow R, Chandiraseharan VK, Kang G, Sudarsanam TD, Klaic M, Manski-Nankervis JA.

title: Beyond the Guidelines: Successful CRT-D Rescue in Patients Unable to Tolerate Guideline-Directed Medical Therapy.
authorString: Srikanth S, Yousif A.
abstractText:
Background

Current ACC/AHA/HFSA guidelines endorse cardiac resynchronization therapy with defibrillation (CRT-D) as a Class I recommendation for patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), left bundle branch block (LBBB), and QRS ≥150 ms but only after at least three months of maximally tolerated guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT). A critical and under-addressed clinical scenario exists - patients with electromechanical dyssynchrony who cannot achieve GDMT optimization due to hypotension, renal dysfunction, or inotrope dependence. Current guidelines do not provide a recommendation pathway for this population, leaving clinicians without evidence-based guidance in a high-stakes decision context.

Case presentations

We present two patients with advanced non-ischemic cardiomyopathy, LBBB with markedly prolonged QRS duration (166-168 ms), and LVEF <20%, both of whom were inotrope-dependent and unable to tolerate GDMT. Neither met traditional prerequisites for CRT-D implantation. Following multidisciplinary evaluation, both patients underwent successful CRT-D implantation, were weaned from intravenous inotropic support, improved from NYHA Class IV to Class II at one year, and had no heart failure hospitalizations during follow-up, with meaningful gains in LVEF in both cases.

Clinical implications

CRT-D may serve as a salvage or enabling therapy in select patients with advanced HFrEF and electrical dyssynchrony who are unable to complete the recommended GDMT optimization period. Prospective studies are needed to refine selection criteria in this high-risk population.

title: Toddalolactone inhibits the activation of fibroblasts in skin fibrosis by regulating MAOA.
authorString: Wang Y, Li S, Song H, Yang C.
abstractText: Skin fibrosis is characterized by excessive deposition of extracellular matrix driven by activated fibroblasts, leading to varying degrees of patient discomfort, deformity, disability, and even death. In vitro studies using mouse primary skin fibroblasts (PSFs) and patient-derived primary keloid fibroblasts (KFs) demonstrated that toddalolactone (Tod) significantly inhibited fibroblast proliferation, migration, and activation and suppressed the TGF-β1/Smad and TGF-β1/non-Smad pathways in these cells. In a bleomycin (BLM)-induced mouse model of skin fibrosis, Tod treatment significantly reduced dermal thickness and collagen deposition in mouse skin, decreased skin hydroxyproline content, and inhibited fibroblast activation as well as the TGF-β1/Smad and TGF-β1/non-Smad pathways in vivo. In a keloid xenograft mouse model, Tod treatment significantly reduced the relative weight of keloids in mice. Histopathological analysis revealed that Tod alleviated the degree of keloid fibrosis and collagen aggregation while inhibiting fibroblast activation in keloid tissue. Furthermore, molecular docking identified monoamine oxidase A (MAOA) as a potential target of Tod. Cellular thermal shift assays and MAOA knockdown using siRNA in PSFs and KFs demonstrated that Tod inhibits the TGF-β1 pathway and suppresses fibroblast activation by inhibiting MAOA. Collectively, the findings reveal that Tod regulates the TGF-β1/Smad and TGF-β1/non-Smad pathways through inhibiting MAOA, thereby affecting skin fibroblast activation and alleviating skin fibrosis.

title: Associated comorbidities among people living with HIV: A retrospective matched cohort study in Spain.
authorString: Peribáñez-García R, Santos-Mejías A, Moreno-Juste A, Poblador-Plou B, Laguna-Berna C, Gimeno-Miguel A, Gimeno-Feliu LA.
abstractText:
Background

People living with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection (PLWH) have more comorbidities and higher mortality than their non-HIV counterparts, in spite of their improving survival.

Aim

This study aimed to: 1) characterize a cohort of PLWH using real-world data from the public health system users in Aragon region, Spain; 2) compare the prevalence of specific long-term conditions between PLWH and a matched cohort of people not living with HIV (PNLWH); 3) determine the association between HIV infection and these conditions, controlling for key confounders (sex, year of birth, geographic area, socioeconomic status, and country of birth); and 4) determine whether PLWH are diagnosed with other new comorbidities earlier than PNLWH.

Methods and findings

Retrospective observational matched cohort study of 8,302 PLWH matched 1:2 in Aragon, Spain. PLWH had higher multimorbidity burden (median 2 (interquartile range 1, 5) vs 2 (0, 4), increasing with age especially in women, and experienced approximately twice the mortality observed among PNLWH (20,8% in PLWH vs 8,6% in PNLWH). Mental health problems, cardiovascular events, neoplasms and hepatic diseases were more common in PLWH, and these conditions were recorded earlier compared with PNLWH. In men LWH under 45 years, depression showed an adjusted odds ratio (OR) of 2.23 (1.73-2.88). In women LWH aged 45-65 years, congestive heart failure showed an adjusted OR of 60.9 (8.70-426.06). They tended to be diagnosed less frequently with classic cardiovascular risk factors like obesity, or dyslipidemia (OR 0.74 [0.67-0.83] in males aged 45-65 years).

Conclusions

PLWH experienced a higher burden of morbidity and approximately twice the mortality rate of PNLWH. They were also diagnosed with new chronic conditions at an earlier age than PNLWH. Although PLWH had a higher incidence of cardiovascular events, they had fewer recorded diagnoses of certain cardiovascular risk factors. The existence of different comorbidity profiles in both cohorts shows us that further investigation is needed to assess the influence of HIV infection with respect to the diagnosis and management of comorbidities.

title: Carotid plaque detection in patients with type 2 diabetes: development, interpretability, and limited transportability of a clinical model.
authorString: Liu X, Xu G, Wang XJ.
abstractText:
Objective

To develop and evaluate a parsimonious model for detecting prevalent carotid plaque in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), and to assess its interpretability, robustness, and transportability.

Methods

This retrospective cross-sectional study enrolled 2,035 hospitalized patients with T2DM, randomly assigned 70:30 to training and test sets. Bidirectional stepwise regression screened 39 candidate variables; stability was assessed by bootstrap resampling (1,000 replicates) and penalized regression. Performance was compared with random forest and XGBoost, and TreeSHAP was used for interpretability. Interaction terms, a non-medication model, and high-sensitivity thresholds were evaluated. The model was applied to an independent cohort of 3,191 health-screening individuals, with updating assessed by split-half validation.

Results

Eight predictors were retained. The test-set AUC was 0.827 (95% CI 0.791-0.862), versus 0.804 for random forest and 0.816 for XGBoost (P = 0.023 versus random forest). Only age and statin use were selected in 100% of bootstrap resamples. Removing statin use and GLP-1RA lowered the AUC to 0.787 (ΔAUC - 0.040, P < 0.001), retaining a history of coronary heart disease. No interaction term was significant (joint P = 0.511). In the external cohort, the AUC was 0.666 with marked miscalibration; updating left discrimination unchanged, and at 85% sensitivity, specificity was 33.4%.

Conclusion

An eight-variable logistic model using routinely available variables performed comparably to machine learning models for detecting prevalent carotid plaque in the development cohort. However, variable selection was unstable, and statin use was the strongest but indication-confounded correlate. External discrimination was moderate and did not improve after recalibration, indicating limited transportability. The model is best regarded as an exploratory candidate requiring further setting-specific validation, rather than one that may already aid in the detection of clinical cases.

title: Carboxypeptidase B1: A novel, targetable contributor to thromboembolic complications in severe acute pancreatitis?
authorString: Barmettler NK, White CM, Gawargi FI, Maginot ER, Moody TB, Clegg AA, Hamed M, Moore PK, Wu C, Aftabjahani A, Kim P, Henry R, Barrett CD.

journal.title: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery

abstractText:
Background

Severe acute pancreatitis (SAP) is associated with increased thrombotic risk. Systemic release of pancreatic proteases in SAP may alter susceptibility to endogenous fibrinolysis, but this remains unexplored. Pancreatic carboxypeptidase B1 (CPB1) is a protease activated by trypsin that shares cleavage specificity with thrombin-activatable fibrinolysis inhibitor, which cleaves C-terminal lysine residues off fibrin, impairing co-localization of tissue plasminogen activator (tPA) and plasminogen and rendering clots resistant to fibrinolysis. We hypothesized that circulating CPB1 would be elevated in SAP patients and contribute to fibrinolytic resistance.

Methods

Plasma and clinical data were prospectively collected from SAP patients (n=15), matched critically ill controls without pancreatitis (n=13), and healthy controls (n=4) with IRB approval and informed consent. CPB1 levels were measured through ELISA. Clot lysis assays assessed fibrinolysis in response to tPA. Healthy control plasma was tested with and without porcine pancreas CPB1 to assess the effect of CPB1 on fibrinolysis. Transition midpoints (TM's) were defined as the time to 50% clot lysis. Clinical data were analyzed using Mann-Whitney U and Fisher exact tests. Assay results were analyzed using Kruskall-Wallis test. Significance was set at P<0.05.

Results

Demographics were similar between groups. SAP patients had markedly elevated CPB1 levels (154.0 [58.4-388.0] ng/mL) compared with sick (7.0 [4.1-15.6] ng/mL, P<0.0001) and healthy controls (4.0 [2.1-4.4], P<0.001). Healthy control plasma supplemented with porcine pancreas CPB1 demonstrated complete disruption of fibrinolysis compared with healthy plasma without CPB1. SAP patients had the highest resistance to tPA-induced fibrinolysis, with significantly higher baseline TMs than critically ill controls (42.0 [21.7-126.6] vs. 22.8 [18.3-33.7], P=0.04).

Conclusions

Patients with SAP have uniquely elevated circulating levels of CPB1, which may contribute to thromboembolism in SAP through fibrinolytic resistance. Further investigation into targeted CPB1 inhibition as a potential therapeutic strategy in SAP is warranted to potentially reduce development of organ failure and mortality.

Level of evidence

N/A (Basic Science).

title: Dietary patterns and atherosclerosis: contemporary evidence and clinical implications.
authorString: Patel K, Khanna S, Nerlekar N, Bhat A.
abstractText: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) remains the leading global cause of death, and diet represents an important modifiable target for prevention. Contemporary evidence supports a shift from nutrient-based to dietary-pattern approaches with Mediterranean, DASH and high-quality plant-based diets associated with favourable effects on cardiovascular risk factors, including lipid profiles, inflammation, blood pressure and metabolic health. Conversely, Western and ultra-processed-food patterns are associated with increased ASCVD risk, potentially mediated through dyslipidaemia, visceral adiposity, inflammation and oxidative stress. Additional dietary approaches, including the Nordic, Portfolio, low-carbohydrate and intermittent fasting diets, have demonstrated effects on selected cardiometabolic risk factors, although evidence for long-term cardiovascular outcomes remains limited. Advances in metabolomic profiling provide further insight into diet-related cardiometabolic risk and may facilitate further precision-nutrition approaches. Concurrently, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and SGLT2 inhibitors have expanded therapeutic options for cardiovascular risk reduction. Reducing the global ASCVD burden requires integration of dietary, pharmacological, clinical and policy strategies. Nutrition should remain central to ASCVD prevention rather than a secondary adjunct.

title: Peripheral Artery Disease in Acute Care Settings: Diagnosis and Management of Common Presentations and Emergencies: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.
authorString: Rymer JA, Banerjee S, Beckman J, Damluji AA, McGinigle KL, Kirksey L, Parikh SA, Sullivan AE, Kohlman-Trigoboff D, Wilkins L, Secemsky E, American Heart Association Acute Cardiac Care and General Cardiology Science Committee of the Council on Clinical Cardiology; Council on Cardiovascular and Stroke Nursing; Council on Cardiovascular Radiology and Intervention; Council on Lifelong Congenital Heart Disease and Heart Health in the Young; Council on Peripheral Vascular Disease; and Council on Quality of Care and Outcomes Research.
abstractText: People with peripheral artery disease (PAD) are often misdiagnosed or diagnosed late and, even after diagnosis, are undertreated with both pharmacologic and invasive therapies. The disease is associated with an increased risk of mortality, myocardial infarction, stroke, other vascular disease, limb loss, and reduced quality of life. Although the risks and long-term management of PAD are well documented, these risks are acutely magnified when PAD exists as a comorbidity in patients hospitalized for other cardiovascular or medical conditions. Procedures requiring vascular access for the treatment of acute myocardial infarction, cardiogenic shock, or valvular heart disease, as well as procedures for the treatment of the patient's underlying PAD, require special consideration in patients with PAD. Familiarity with the use and placement of mechanical circulatory support in patients with PAD, as well as the management of recent endovascular or surgical vascular interventions, is essential for providing appropriate care in the acute care setting.

title: From interpretation to implementation in cardiovascular care.
authorString: Lancellotti P.
abstractText: Translating evidence into better outcomes requires both careful interpretation and effective implementation. The studies featured in this issue of Acta Cardiologica address mechanical bumping during cryoablation of atrioventricular nodal re-entrant tachycardia, myocardial infarction in young adults, prevention of contrast-induced nephropathy, intravascular imaging in left main intervention, atrial and atrioventricular remodelling in heart failure, the implementation of SGLT2 inhibitors and cardiovascular risk reduction in Belgium, successive cardiovascular risk score updates, transcatheter aortic valve implantation, and infective and rheumatic heart disease. Collectively, they show that methodological rigour and pragmatic implementation strategies remain equally essential to improve patient care.

title: Society for Vascular Surgery Vascular Quality Initiative Contemporary Benchmarks: Thoracic Endovascular Aortic Repair.
authorString: Sickels AD, Wang GJ, Caputo FJ, Beck AW, Han S, Chou EL, Ochoa Chaar CI, Eldrup-Jorgensen J, Rowse J.
abstractText:
Objective

To describe contemporary outcomes as well as temporal trends of in-hospital mortality and complication rates for patients undergoing thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) across indications and levels of urgency, establishing a benchmark for future analytic efforts.

Methods

The VQI TEVAR and complex EVAR registry was queried for procedures performed between January 2014-December 2024. Primary outcomes included in-hospital mortality and major complications. Analyses were stratified by indication to include descending thoracic aortic aneurysms (DTAA), dissections, and trauma. Aneurysms involving the aortic arch (i.e. landing zone < 2) or extending to the visceral segment and distally (i.e. landing zone >5) were excluded. Linear regression and the Cochran Armitage test for trend were used to analyze yearly mortality and complication rates over time. Mortality and complication end-points were further analyzed using logistic regression with and without risk-adjustment.

Results

Over the ten-year study period, 4,632 TEVARs were performed for DTAA, 6,701 for dissection, and 2,321 for trauma. For patients undergoing TEVAR for DTAA, in-hospital mortality declined significantly for both elective (2014, 3.9% versus 2024, 1.0%, -0.26 percentage points per year, p=0.01) and nonelective cases (2014, 16.7% versus 2024, 8.7%, -0.63 percentage points per year, p=0.04). There was also a decline in in-hospital mortality among elective dissection patients (2014, 3.7% versus 2024, 0.5%, -0.17 percentage points per year, p=0.03). Elective TEVAR overall is associated with a mortality rate of less than two percent per year. The in-hospital complication trends declined significantly for patients undergoing TEVAR for DTAA - elective patients experienced a decline in complication rates by -1.13 percentage points per year (2014, 24.8% versus 2024, 11.5% p<0.001) and non-elective patients experienced a decline in complication rates by -2.0 percentage points per year (2014, 40.5% versus 2024, 25.2%, p<0.001). Dissection patients undergoing elective repair had a decrease of -0.8 percentage points per year (2014, 16.9% versus 2024, 9.2%, p<0.001). Nonelective dissections repairs had a complication rate of 36.4% in 2014 vs 34.1% in 2024, p=0.874). Trauma patients tended toward higher complication rates over time, with a rate of 21.6% in 2014 and 32.2% in 2024, p=0.06) Trauma patients experienced an overall increase in in-hospital mortality of +0.38 percentage points per year (2014, 9.8% versus 2024, 9.4%, p=0.01).

Conclusion

Temporal trends within the VQI demonstrate improvements in mortality and complication rates for patients undergoing TEVAR for DTAA and elective dissection repair, with contemporary yearly mortality rates of less than two percent. Patients undergoing non-elective dissection repair and those with traumatic indications represent challenging and complex pathologies requiring further research to identify opportunities to improve outcomes.

title: Recurrent prosthetic valve endocarditis with suspected perivalvular abscess caused by Staphylococcus caprae in a bone marrow transplant recipient: a case report.
authorString: Nakajima T, Iba Y, Shibata T, Nakazawa J, Kouzu H, Iyama S.

journal.title: The Egyptian heart journal : (EHJ) : official bulletin of the Egyptian Society of Cardiology

abstractText:
Background

Infective endocarditis (IE) in bone marrow transplantation (BMT) recipients is uncommon but carries high mortality. Recurrent prosthetic valve endocarditis (PVE) in immunocompromised hosts presents particular challenges in surgical decision-making. Staphylococcus caprae, a coagulase-negative staphylococcus of caprine origin, is rarely implicated in human IE. We report a rare case of recurrent S. caprae PVE with suspected perivalvular abscess in a BMT recipient managed with advance care planning (ACP) and home-based palliative care.

Case presentation

A 63-year-old male had undergone allogeneic BMT for high-risk myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) and was receiving immunosuppression for chronic graft-versus-host disease. Approximately 13 months after BMT, he developed cardiogenic shock due to S. caprae IE causing severe aortic regurgitation and underwent emergency aortic valve replacement (AVR) with a 27-mm INSPIRIS RESILIA bioprosthesis (Edwards Lifesciences) and concomitant coronary artery bypass grafting. The initial event has been previously reported. Approximately eight weeks after completion of a 42-day antimicrobial course, he was readmitted with fever and rigors, and blood cultures again grew S. caprae with an antimicrobial susceptibility profile indistinguishable from that of the index isolate; strain-level molecular typing was not performed. Transesophageal echocardiography approximately one month later showed an isoechoic structure at the subaortic curtain, raising suspicion of a perivalvular abscess. Blood cultures remained positive, and a new paravalvular leak developed during follow-up. Through serial multidisciplinary consultations, re-operation was judged to carry prohibitive risk, and the patient declined further surgery. Home-based palliative care with long-term suppressive oral linezolid was chosen in accordance with his preferences. He died peacefully at home with his family approximately 13 months after the index cardiac surgery and 10 months after recurrent bacteremia.

Conclusions

Recurrent S. caprae PVE with suspected perivalvular involvement in a BMT recipient poses difficult management decisions. Residual prosthetic or perivalvular infection is a plausible explanation, but re-infection cannot be excluded. When reoperation is high risk and inconsistent with the patient's wishes, ACP-guided palliative care with suppressive antimicrobial therapy may be an individualized option.

title: Golgi-retained TNFR1 variants induce stress-driven inflammation in a subset of systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis.
authorString: Cruz AC, Csomos K, Nakano H, Ujhazi B, Panipinto PM, Chou SR, Krantz M, Rosenbaum ED, Correia Marques M, Felicelli C, Fu TM, Foell D, Yeung RS, Weiss PF, Naz F, Bergeron LL, Millwood M, Lake C, Nagao K, Schaughency P, Chen V, Lack J, Verweyen EL, Schulert G, Yu K, INCHARGE Consortium, Dell'Orso S, Wu H, Deng Z, Randazzo D, Ombrello MJ.
abstractText: Systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis (sJIA) is a complex inflammatory disease characterized by recurrent fevers, arthritis, and systemic hyperinflammation; however, its underlying etiology remains poorly understood. Tumor necrosis factor receptor 1 (TNFR1, TNFRSF1A), the prototypical TNF superfamily receptor, signals through its ligand (tumor necrosis factor, TNF) to activate NF-κB-dependent proinflammatory pathways while also promoting cell death. Through family-based and targeted sequencing, we identified multiple rare TNFRSF1A variants, including a de novo truncating variant in a patient with monophasic sJIA. Integrating single cell RNA-seq with in vitro and ex vivo functional assays, we uncovered a patient-specific, unique monocyte population marked by high inflammatory cytokine production. These cells display impaired endosomal and Golgi trafficking, dysregulated autophagy, and increased markers of cellular stress and immune activation. Confocal microscopy revealed aberrant TNFR1 retention within the Golgi apparatus. These monocytes were refractory to LPS-induced cell death, maintained a M1-like inflammatory phenotype and produced proinflammatory cytokines even at steady state. Despite conferring a loss of function in TNFR1 signaling, these variants paradoxically drive a hyperinflammatory phenotype. We propose that this results from combined effects of reduced TNFR1 signaling and cellular stress induced by retention of the mutant receptor in the Golgi.

title: Addendum: A meta-analysis of GFR slope as a surrogate endpoint for kidney failure.
authorString: Inker LA, Collier W, Greene T, Miao S, Chaudhari J, Appel GB, Badve SV, Caravaca-Fontán F, Del Vecchio L, Floege J, Goicoechea M, Haaland B, Herrington WG, Imai E, Jafar TH, Lewis JB, Li PKT, Maes BD, Neuen BL, Perrone RD, Remuzzi G, Schena FP, Wanner C, Wetzels JFM, Woodward M, Heerspink HJL, CKD-EPI Clinical Trials Consortium.

title: Silent brain infarction and clinical outcomes in rheumatic mitral stenosis: A prospective cohort study.
authorString: Naik N, Mantoo MR, Roy A, Rai N, Kumar K, Sharma M, Kumar S, Jagia P, Ramakrishnan L, Yadav R, Sharma G, Singh S.
abstractText:
Background

Rheumatic mitral stenosis (MS) affects a relatively young population. Thromboembolic risk in MS is traditionally attributed to atrial fibrillation (AF), although silent brain infarction (SBI) may occur in sinus rhythm. Further, the contribution of underlying atrial disease independent of rhythm remains uncertain.

Objectives

To determine the prevalence and correlates of SBI and evaluate associations with subsequent cerebrovascular and clinical outcomes.

Methods

In this prospective cohort, 211 adults with moderate-to-severe rheumatic MS underwent baseline brain MRI, echocardiography, biomarker assessment, and rhythm evaluation. Firth penalized logistic regression was used for SBI and longitudinal outcomes. Clinical follow-up was available in 194 patients.

Results

SBI was present in 44 patients (20.9%). SBI occurred in 25.4% with AF and 18.6% in sinus rhythm (unadjusted OR 1.49, 95% CI 0.70-3.10; p = 0.284); adjusted AF was not significantly associated with SBI (OR 0.82, 95% CI 0.37-1.76; p = 0.605). Each doubling of BNP was associated with SBI overall (OR 1.34, 95% CI 1.01-1.82; p = 0.040) and in sinus rhythm (OR 1.56, 95% CI 1.12-2.27; p = 0.007). During follow-up, 15 patients developed stroke/TIA; baseline SBI was associated with subsequent stroke/TIA (17.1% vs 5.2%; adjusted OR 3.40, 95% CI 1.14-9.96; p = 0.029). BNP was associated with stroke/death (49 events; OR per doubling 1.45, 95% CI 1.09-2.00; p = 0.010) and death (40 events; OR 1.57, 95% CI 1.14-2.25; p = 0.005), but not stroke/TIA.

Conclusions

SBI is common in rheumatic MS and identifies patients at higher subsequent cerebrovascular risk. BNP is associated with SBI and broader adverse prognosis, particularly mortality. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require further validation.

title: Technological advances in the molecular diagnosis of Chagas disease from the perspective of the Fio-Chagas Translational ProgrammeFIRST REVIEW ROUND - REVIEWERS' COMMENTSREVIEWERS' COMMENTS.
authorString: Britto C, Moreira ODC.
abstractText: An estimated 6 to 8 million people worldwide are infected with Trypanosoma cruzi, the parasite that causes Chagas disease (CD). Of those infected, an alarming 70% to 90% remain undiagnosed, making it one of the most under-recognised global health burdens. To celebrate the 25th anniversary of the Fiocruz Translational Programme in Chagas Disease (Fio-Chagas), this narrative review presents a chronological account of the development of polymerase chain reaction (PCR)-based assays for the molecular detection of T. cruzi. It highlights the significant contributions made by the Fio-Chagas Programme to the development and availability of a diagnostic product for the molecular diagnosis of CD. Following the proof of concept, the qPCR-based Biomol Chagas kit was manufactured using reagents produced by the Institute of Molecular Biology of Paraná (IBMP). After analytical and clinical validation, the kit was registered in 2022 by the Brazilian Health Regulatory Agency (ANVISA). Additional studies under field conditions were required for a cost-effectiveness analysis by the National Commission for the Incorporation of Technologies into the Brazilian Unified Health System (CONITEC). Currently, the kit has been incorporated into clinical studies across Latin America to diagnose congenital transmission, monitor the impact of antiparasitic treatment in chronic CD (CCD), and evaluate oral transmission in the Northern region of Brazil.

title: Association of Germanic Cultural Preservation with Cardiovascular Risk and Subclinical Atherosclerosis in Adults from Southern Brazil.
authorString: Braga RAM, Markus MRP, Dörr M, Völzke H, Bahls M, Starke S, Zimmermann SL, Helena ETS, Santos RD, Bortolotto LA, Coronado J, Damasceno NRT.
abstractText:
Background

Migration involves cultural and lifestyle transitions that may influence cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk. Cultural preservation and adaptation may affect cardiovascular health through behavioral and social mechanisms.

Objective

To assess the association of Germanic cultural preservation with CVD risk and subclinical atherosclerosis among residents of Pomerode, southern Brazil, stratified by age group and sex.

Methods

This cross-sectional study used baseline data collected from 2014 to 2018 from the Study of Health in Pomerode cohort and included 727 individuals aged 20-79 years with complete data. Germanic cultural preservation was defined as regularly speaking German at home and participating in German cultural associations. Subclinical atherosclerosis was defined as the presence of three or more carotid plaques. 10-year atherosclerotic CVD risk was estimated using the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Pooled Cohort Equations. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05.

Results

Mean age was 43.7 years, and 51.9% of participants were women. Germanic cultural preservation was reported by 65.61% of participants and was more common among older adults, White individuals, Protestants, and individuals of middle socioeconomic status (p < 0.05). Participants reporting Germanic cultural preservation also had less sedentary behavior, greater use of antihypertensive medications, and a less favorable cardiometabolic profile. In adjusted age-stratified models, Germanic cultural preservation was associated with hypertension (odds ratio [OR]: 2.79; 95% CI: 1.49-5.22) and subclinical atherosclerosis (OR: 3.01; 95% CI: 1.07-8.40) among individuals aged 50 years or older. After adjustment for hypertension, the association with subclinical atherosclerosis was attenuated and was no longer statistically significant.

Conclusions

Germanic cultural preservation was associated with hypertension and subclinical atherosclerosis among adults aged 50 years or older, highlighting the importance of considering cultural context when characterizing cardiovascular risk in aging populations.

title: Association between keratoconus and arterial stiffness: a cross-sectional study.
authorString: Demirci M, Ozben B, Ersoy EE, Karaca S, Sayar N, Mustafayev U, Esen F, Sunbul M.
abstractText:
Objective

Keratoconus is a progressive corneal ectasia characterized by stromal thinning and collagen disruption. Despite being primarily considered an ocular disease, recent evidence suggests the possibility of systemic connective tissue involvement. The aim of this study was to evaluate arterial stiffness parameters in patients with keratoconus to explore potential systemic vascular alterations.

Methods

The study included 43 consecutive patients with keratoconus (mean age: 38.4±12.5 years, 21 male) and 50 healthy controls (mean age: 39.8±7.9 years, 29 male). Arterial stiffness was assessed in all participants using the Mobil-O-Graph system.

Results

The patients with keratoconus had significantly higher pulse wave velocity (6.1±1.1 m/s vs. 5.6±0.5 m/s, p=0.014), augmentation index (21 vs. 12%, p=0.005), peripheral systolic blood pressure (123±12 mmHg vs. 115±8 mmHg, p<0.001), peripheral pulse pressure (46±11 mmHg vs. 39±9, p=0.001), central systolic blood pressure (112±12 mmHg vs. 107±8 mmHg, p=0.016), and central pulse pressure (34±9 mmHg vs. 30±8 mmHg, p=0.037) compared to controls. Pulse wave velocity was significantly correlated with age, systolic blood pressure, body mass index, Kmax, thinnest corneal thickness, and posterior corneal elevation. Keratoconus remained independently associated with pulse wave velocity after adjustment for age, sex, systolic blood pressure, and body mass index (B=0.289, 95%CI 0.083-0.494, p=0.006).

Conclusion

Patients with keratoconus had higher pulse wave velocity and augmentation index values than controls, suggesting an association between keratoconus and increased arterial stiffness. These findings highlight the need to consider cardiovascular risk assessment in individuals with keratoconus.

title: Splenic Artery Aneurysm Rupture Masquerading as a Metabolic Emergency: A Case Report.
authorString: Sylqa A, Elshani A, Leci-Tahiri L.
abstractText: Rupture of a splenic artery aneurysm (SAA) is a rare but life-threatening vascular emergency that may mimic other acute abdominal conditions and delay diagnosis. We report the case of a 59-year-old woman who presented with nonspecific abdominal symptoms and marked hyperglycemia (19.5 mmol/L) and was initially admitted with suspected new-onset type 2 diabetes mellitus and abdominal pain. Progressive hemodynamic deterioration and a rapid decline in hemoglobin (from 9.9 to 5.5 g/dL) prompted CT angiography, which demonstrated a ruptured splenic artery aneurysm (23 × 22 mm), hemoperitoneum, and an adjacent pancreatic pseudocyst. Emergency laparotomy, splenectomy, and ligation of the splenic artery were performed, followed by a complicated but ultimately successful recovery. This case highlights the risk of diagnostic anchoring on prominent laboratory abnormalities when occult hemorrhage is present. In a patient with abdominal symptoms and hemodynamic instability, a falling hemoglobin concentration should prompt urgent evaluation for intra-abdominal bleeding, even when a concurrent metabolic abnormality appears to offer an explanation.

title: Werner Syndrome With Multisystem Manifestations in a 35-Year-Old Bangladeshi Man: A Case Report.
authorString: Nargis H, Saifuddin M, Hossain F, Basu KC, Prasad I.
abstractText: Werner syndrome, also known as adult progeria, is a rare autosomal recessive disorder characterized by premature aging and multisystem involvement. We report the case of a 35-year-old Bangladeshi man who presented with growth arrest during adolescence resulting in short stature, bilateral posterior subcapsular cataracts, diabetes mellitus, hypothyroidism, chronic non-healing ulcers, scleroderma-like skin changes, muscle wasting, and ankle ankylosis. Molecular genetic analysis identified a pathogenic WRN gene variant (c.3233 + 2 T >C in intron 26), confirming the diagnosis of Werner syndrome. A younger sister exhibited similar phenotypic features, suggesting possible familial occurrence; however, she was not genetically tested. Laboratory investigations revealed normocytic normochromic anemia, hypertriglyceridemia, elevated gonadotropin levels, markedly reduced serum testosterone, and marked hyperferritinemia. In addition, radiological evaluation demonstrated generalized osteopenia with talocalcaneal and ankle joint ankylosis, while electrocardiography revealed left ventricular hypertrophy. Management focused on long-term control of metabolic and endocrine comorbidities together with comprehensive wound care for chronic ulcers. This case highlights the importance of early recognition, molecular confirmation, multidisciplinary management, and regular surveillance for cardiovascular complications and malignancies in patients with Werner syndrome.

title: Chronic Organizing Mediastinal Hematoma Causing Mechanical Prosthetic Tricuspid Valve Dysfunction.
authorString: Binder MS, Dearani J, Marcotte F, Francois C, Ammash N.
abstractText:
Background

Mechanical prosthetic valvular dysfunction is typically thought to be secondary to thrombosis or pannus formation on the valve. Cross-sectional imaging can help with identification of the etiology of prosthetic valvular dysfunction.

Case summary

A 39-year-old man with tricuspid atresia and prior biventricular repair with a right atrial to right ventricular conduit presented for an increasing mechanical tricuspid valve gradient and change in his valve clicking sound. Fluoroscopy revealed reduced disc excursion. Three doses of low-dose thrombolytics were trialed without improvement. Computed tomography imaging suggested an intermediate-density mass compressing the conduit and causing extrinsic dysfunction of the tricuspid prosthesis. Surgical examination revealed a chronic mediastinal hematoma causing conduit compression in addition to pannus formation.

Discussion

Mediastinal hematomas are rare and typically provoked by trauma but can be spontaneous particularly with warfarin anticoagulation.

Take-home message

Mechanical tricuspid prosthesis dysfunction is often from thrombosis or pannus formation, but extrinsic compression should additionally be considered.

title: Aurones in medicinal chemistry: synthetic strategies, biological activities, structure-activity relationships and challenges.
authorString: John D, Radhakrishnan EK.
abstractText: Aurones are 2-benzylidenebenzofuran-3(2H)-ones whose compact conjugated framework supports broad substitution, semisynthesis and pharmacophore hybridization. This review adds a chemistry-to-evidence framework that was not provided by earlier activity-centred surveys: it defines the boundary between aurones and related scaffolds, links each synthetic diversification strategy to matched-series SAR, separates experimental target evidence from computational hypotheses, and compares translational maturity across therapeutic areas. A reproducible literature audit through July 2026 integrates classical chalcone cyclization, benzofuranone-aldehyde condensation, late-stage O-functionalization, CuAAC, glycosylation, aminoalkylation, and natural-product derivatization. Anticancer studies dominate, with the strongest progression observed for tubulin-directed semisynthetic aurones supported by cellular, mechanistic and organism-level experiments. Neurochemical, metabolic, cardiovascular, anti-inflammatory, musculoskeletal and anti-infective studies identify additional leads, but their SAR remains series- and assay-specific. The principal barriers are inconsistent structural and geometrical assignment, limited selectivity controls, sparse quantitative physicochemical and pharmacokinetic data, uncertain target engagement, incomplete tissue-exposure measurements, and little chronic safety evidence. No aurone-based approved medicine or interventional clinical study was identified. Progress therefore depends on chemically verified structures, matched-series SAR, orthogonal target validation and exposure-guided lead selection rather than further unprioritized analogue expansion.

title: Current Status of Pain-Related Patient-Reported Outcomes and Perioperative Pain Management among 40,785 Patients: A Prospective Multicenter Study.
authorString: Liu Y, Lv X, Li H, Yang H, Hou A, Han S, Wang J, Li L, Wu J, Hou D, Li F, Zhang Z, Diao Y, Han Y, Yang JJ, Zhang J, Mi W.
abstractText: This study analyzed self-reported pain-related outcomes of 40,785 surgical patients from 125 centers collected by CAPOPS (China Acute Postoperative Pain Study) between September 2019 and August 2023, to characterize the current status of acute postoperative pain management protocols and pain prognoses in Chinese medical institutions. Every participant completed the International Pain Outcome Questionnaire on the first postoperative day. Patient self-reported pain outcomes were assessed across the domains of pain severity, interference with activities and emotional well-being, adverse events, and perception of care. Outcome differences across geographic regions, time periods, and surgical types were analyzed. Risk factors associated with severe pain (score ≥ 7 on a 0-10 scale) were also evaluated with logistic regression. Overall, 12.6% of patients reported severe pain. Compared with earlier CAPOPS datasets, the prevalence of severe pain decreased consistently across surgical specialties, procedure categories, and geographic regions. Although such improvements were observed, perioperative pain management remained suboptimal in certain subgroups, particularly obstetric patients. We noted growing adoption of intraoperative non-opioid analgesics, combined regional anesthesia techniques, postoperative patient-controlled analgesia, and greater patient participation in pain management decision-making. Multivariable regression analysis demonstrated that these practices were significantly associated with a reduced risk of severe postoperative pain.

title: Deciphering the Mechanisms Underlying Therapeutic Resistance in Cancer through Single-Cell and Spatial Transcriptomics Technologies: Current Approaches and Future Perspectives.
authorString: Li Z, Chen Q, Xiang M, Li Z, He X, He Y, Ou C.
abstractText: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics (ST) technologies are recent high-throughput sequencing advancements that enable transcriptome-wide profiling and characterization of cellular populations at single-cell resolution while preserving tissue spatial context. Their integration has been increasingly applied to cancer research, facilitating a deeper understanding of tumor biology and improving diagnostic and therapeutic strategies. Growing evidence suggests that combining single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) with ST offers a robust approach for exploring mechanisms underlying therapeutic resistance. Together, these technologies support the prediction and monitoring of treatment responses and help identify novel therapeutic targets by revealing critical signaling pathways and immune cell populations associated with resistance. Artificial intelligence, including deep learning, computer vision, and generative models, further enhances the integration and analysis of data generated by scRNA-seq and ST, contributing to tumor resistance research. This review summarizes recent advances in the integrated application of scRNA-seq and ST to study tumor resistance and discusses the opportunities, challenges, and future directions of these technologies as a theoretical foundation for identifying therapeutic targets and developing treatment strategies.

title: Multi-omics models for hypertension prediction using blood pressure PRS and omics scores
authorString: Wang Z, Hrytsenko Y, Almogy S, Spitzer BW, Purushotham Y, Taylor K, Lin HJ, Tahir U, Raffield LM, Rich SS, Rotter JI, Chen ZZ, Sofer T.
abstractText:
Background

Hypertension is a major modifiable risk factor for cardiovascular disease, yet the relative contributions of proteomic (ProtS), metabolomic (MetS), and polygenic risk scores (PRS) to incident hypertension risk remain incompletely characterized.

Methods

We developed ProtS and MetS for systolic (SBP) and diastolic blood pressure (DBP), and hypertension using Elastic Net regression in the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA). We incorporated these scores with previously developed BP PRSs into 5 incremental XGBoost models, with external validation in the Jackson Heart Study (JHS). We further applied transfer learning to adapt the MESA-derived models to JHS. Elastic Net selected proteins were prioritized using Mendelian randomization, colocalization, and functional analyses.

Results

In MESA, model discrimination improved with the addition of omics scores, with the combined model achieving an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.72 compared with 0.63 for the clinical baseline model. In JHS, ProtS showed the highest AUC of 0.68 and the smallest cross-cohort performance decline, compared to MetS and PRS. Incorporating measured SBP and DBP substantially improved discrimination, with the PRS+BP model achieving an AUC of 0.80 in MESA and the baseline+BP model achieving an AUC of 0.74 in JHS. Among JHS participants with normal baseline BP, ProtS provided the strongest discrimination among models without measured BP (AUC = 0.62), while PRS+BP model achieved an AUC of 0.69. Leaf-weight refreshing consistently improved calibration in JHS while preserving discrimination. Mendelian randomization identified 77 proteins associated with BP traits or hypertension, involved in vascular, inflammatory, renal, and natriuretic pathways.

Conclusions

ProtS demonstrated superior predictive performance and cross-cohort transferability among the omics modalities evaluated, while measured BP remained the strongest predictors of incident hypertension. Proteomic and genetic information may provide complementary biological signals for identifying individuals at elevated hypertension risk, particularly before clinically elevated BP is detectable.

title: Experimental Evidence for Effects of Chronic Infra-Sound Exposure on the Heart – A Narrative Review
authorString: Bellut-Staeck U, Dastan M, Zhou J, Pirapaharan A, Lehmann C.
abstractText: This narrative review outlines potential pathophysiological mechanisms in the mammalian heart in response to chronic infrasound exposure from technical installations. Recent research findings suggest that repeated exposure to infrasound can activate the heart's mechanosensitive PIEZO-1 channels. PIEZO-1 plays an important role in cardiac contractility via modulation of Ca²⁺ release and is involved in ROS homeostasis. The increasingly widespread sources of technical infrasound - which often exhibit high sound pressure intensities at infrasonic frequencies - should be reevaluated with regard to their impact on living organisms. Experimental overexpression of cardiac PIEZO-1 in mice serves as an example of potential effects of chronic infrasound exposure on the heart. Associated reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation reveals links to inflammatory pathways. Continued PIEZO-1 (over)stimulation appears to disrupt Ca²⁺ and ROS homeostasis in the long term, ultimately resulting in cardiomyopathy and arrhythmogenicity.

title: Application of appropriate use criteria, triage, and diagnostic yield of overnight transthoracic echocardiograms.
authorString: Meno MK, Sandhu NS, Ruiz R, Chow C, Tran T, Kirkpatrick JN, Huang GS.
abstractText:
Background

There are limited data to guide the appropriate use and triage of transthoracic echocardiograms (TTE) overnight when resources may be limited. The appropriate use criteria (AUC) assess whether a TTE is reasonable to perform, but do not address urgency or which overnight studies may be deferred until business hours. The purpose of this study was to describe the appropriateness, institutional triage classification, and diagnostic yield of overnight TTE studies completed during the study period.

Methods

This was a retrospective review of inpatient TTEs completed between the hours of 17:30 to 07:00 from June 2021 to May 2022 at two academic centers. All studies were performed by sonographers on adult patients. Electronic medical records were reviewed to determine the context in which TTEs were performed. The indications were then rated using the 2011 AUC and the authors' institutional criteria for triaging overnight TTEs. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with new and clinically important TTE findings.

Results

Of 251 studies completed overnight, 97.6% of indications were "always" appropriate according to the 2011 AUC and 91.6% met institutional "emergency/STAT" criteria. These two classifications reflect separate dimensions, appropriateness of performing the study versus urgency of timing, and are reported independently. New and clinically important findings were noted in 49% of the studies.
