Echocardiography and histopathology were used to evaluate how HFD affected myocardial remodeling at the overall, ultramicroscopic, and microscopic levels. Using proteomics, the STRING database, molecular biology analysis, and reverse validation via an in vitro model, we further gathered mechanistic insights.

Results

HFD caused severe lipid metabolism disorders in the STZ/HFD group. HFD induced more severe inhomogeneous hypertrophy, cardiac diastolic dysfunction, interstitial collagen deposition, and lipid droplet accumulation in the myocardium of T1DM hamsters. Mechanistically, HFD influenced the protein composition profile, mainly in lipid metabolism as well as mitochondrial metabolism. Furthermore, HFD caused more severe damage to mitochondrial morphology. Moreover, metabolic disorder of branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs) was mediated by PPM1K, which finally aggravated surplus oxidative stress accumulation and damage in the myocardium of T1DM hamsters.

Conclusions

Mitochondrial repair, especially the metabolic replenishment of BCAAs, holds potential as a treatment in situations with excessive fat intake in T1DM and should be investigated in vivo and in clinical validation studies in the future.

title: Endothelial SULF1 in cardiovascular disease: Structural basis of heparan sulfate editing and context-dependent pharmacology.
authorString: Wu J, Yi X, Guo Y, Yue Z, Song J.
abstractText: Heparan sulfate 6-O-endosulfatase 1 (SULF1) is an extracellular enzyme that edits mature heparan sulfate and thereby influences the binding and availability of extracellular signaling molecules. We focus on the role of endothelial SULF1 in cardiovascular disease. We also summarize its main structural domains, extracellular processing, catalytic features, and substrate recognition. Then we discuss how SULF1 affects heparan sulfate-dependent signaling, with particular attention to fibroblast growth factor (FGF), vascular endothelial growth factor A (VEGF-A), and Wnt pathways. Available evidence suggests that the effects of SULF1 vary across disease settings. After myocardial infarction, SULF1 may promote vascular repair by increasing the availability of matrix-bound VEGF-A. In atherosclerosis, increased SULF1 expression has been linked to endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition, cellular senescence, and plaque instability. Its role in pulmonary vascular remodeling remains less certain. The review also considers current inhibitors and other possible approaches to SULF1 modulation. Although SULF1 is accessible in the extracellular space, its therapeutic value is limited by incomplete structural information, weak isoform selectivity, and possible effects on normal vascular repair. Further studies are needed before SULF1 can be regarded as a practical cardiovascular drug target.

title: Inflammation and the Association of Early-stage Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome with Incident Cardiovascular Disease and All-cause Mortality: Findings from the CARDIA and MESA Cohorts.
authorString: Tian L, Vu THT, Jacobs DR, Schreiner PJ, Shah NS, Lewis CE, Khan SS, Bhatt A, Wilkins JT, Allen NB, Lloyd-Jones DM, Greenland P, Rasmussen-Torvik LJ, Carnethon MR, Feinstein MJ.
abstractText:
Background

Limited data exist on whether inflammation modifies the association between early-stage cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome and clinical events.

Methods

We included 9,894 participants free of cardiovascular disease (CVD) from the Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults study (CARDIA, Year 20, 2005-2006) and the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA, Exam 1, 2000-2002). We examined whether interleukin-6 (IL-6; primary) and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP; ≥2 mg/L; secondary) modified associations of early-stage CKM syndrome (stages 2-3 vs 0-1) with incident CVD and all-cause mortality. IL-6 was dichotomized at cohort- and sex-specific medians. Cohort-stratified Cox models were adjusted for age, sex, race/ethnicity, education, smoking, and physical activity; multiplicative and additive effect modification were assessed.

Results

During follow-up, 1,635 atherosclerotic CVD events, 567 heart failure events, and 2,593 deaths occurred. After adjustment for CKM stage, IL-6 at or above the median was associated with higher risks of atherosclerotic CVD (hazard ratio, 1.48; 95% CI, 1.33-1.64), heart failure (1.69; 1.41-2.03), and mortality (1.48; 1.36-1.61); hsCRP associations were smaller. IL-6 showed additive effect modification with CKM stage for atherosclerotic CVD (relative excess risk due to interaction, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.17-1.46) but no multiplicative effect modification (P = 0.59), and no effect modification for heart failure or mortality. hsCRP showed no consistent effect modification.

Conclusions

Higher IL-6 and hsCRP were each associated with higher cardiovascular and mortality risks independent of early-stage CKM syndrome. IL-6 showed additive effect modification with CKM stage for atherosclerotic CVD, indicating a positive relative excess risk due to interaction among adults with CKM stages 2-3.

title: Real-World Performance of a Novel Wearable Cardioverter-Defibrillator System: Primary Results From a National Prospective Post-Approval Registry Study (ACE-PAS).
authorString: Poole JE, Gleva MJ, Branch KRH, Birgersdotter-Green U, Doshi RN, Sridhar AR, Gustavson LM, Zulueta SA, Levy WC.
abstractText:
Introduction

Wearable cardioverter defibrillators (WCDs) protect patients at elevated risk of sudden cardiac death (SCD) but are effective only when worn. The ASSURE WCD was designed to address historical limitations related to false alarms and patient adherence. The objective of this post-approval study was to assess safety and effectiveness in a large, real-world cohort.

Methods

The study population was comprised of patients meeting WCD indications who were fitted with the ASSURE WCD. The primary effectiveness endpoint was overall shock conversion success for ventricular tachycardia (VT) or ventricular fibrillation (VF) (performance goal ≥ 89%), and the primary safety endpoint was the incidence of inappropriate shocks (performance goal ≤ 0.0075 per patient-month).

Results

Among 21 612 patients (mean age 64.0 years, 33.9% female), median daily use was 23.1 h/day (IQR 16.1-23.9) over 54 days (IQR 20-97). WCD indications included cardiomyopathy (63.8%), post-myocardial infarction (19.3%), sustained VT/VF (11.9%) and ICD explant/other (5.0%). Both primary effectiveness and safety endpoints were met. All 303 VT/VF shock events in 261 patients (1.2%) were successfully converted, yielding an overall shock conversion success of 100% (95% CI: 98.8%-100%), with first-shock success of 97.0% (95% CI: 94.4%-98.5%). The incidence rate of inappropriate shocks was 0.0065 per patient-month (95% CI: 0.0057-0.0073). False-positive alarms occurred in 6.0% of patients. The 90-day Kaplan-Meier estimated risk of VT/VF was 3.4%, varying by WCD indication (p < 0.001) but not by left ventricular ejection fraction (p = 0.16).

Conclusion

In routine practice, the ASSURE WCD effectively terminated VT/VF with low false alarm and inappropriate shock rates and high patient adherence. Most VT/VF events occurred early during WCD wear. Collectively, these findings provide important contemporary evidence to inform the selection of patients who may benefit from WCD therapy during periods of elevated arrhythmic risk.

Trial registration

NCT05135403.

title: Association Between Pulmonary Artery Diameter on CT and Clinical Outcomes in COVID-19: A 1000-Patient Retrospective Analysis.
authorString: Yarmahmoodi F, Elahi M, Saeedi-Moghadam M, Razavinejad SM, Zeinali-Rafsanjani B.
abstractText:
Background

We evaluated the association between main pulmonary artery (PA) diameter on chest CT and CT-defined lung involvement, intensive care unit (ICU) hospitalization, and in-hospital mortality in patients hospitalized with COVID-19.

Methods

This retrospective cohort included 1000 adults with PCR-confirmed COVID-19 treated at Namazi and Shahid Faghihi Hospitals in 2020. For each patient, the first routine noncontrast chest CT obtained after admission was analyzed, provided it had been performed within the first 72 h. Main PA diameter was measured manually on axial images proximal to the PA bifurcation. Associations with age, sex, CT severity, ICU hospitalization, and in-hospital outcome were evaluated.

Results

The mean age was 56 ± 17.7 years; 525 patients (52.5%) were men and 475 (47.5%) were women. Mean PA diameter was 27.07 ± 3.84 mm. Men had a larger mean PA diameter than women (27.40 ± 3.77 vs. 26.69 ± 3.88 mm; p = 0.004), and age showed a weak positive correlation with PA diameter (r = 0.282, p < 0.001). PA diameter increased across CT severity categories and was greater among patients who died and among those hospitalized in the ICU (all p < 0.001).

Conclusions

Larger PA diameter was associated with greater CT-defined lung involvement, ICU hospitalization, and in-hospital mortality. Because the analyses were unadjusted and observational, these findings do not establish independent or incremental prognostic value.

title: Surgical Management of Thoracic Aortic Mural Thrombus: Operative Strategy and Early Outcomes in a Two-Decade Retrospective Single-Center Experience.
authorString: Burgard C, Romano G, Jahn J, Lange A, Arif R, Karck M, Dib B.
abstractText:
Objective

Thoracic aortic mural thrombus (TAMT) is a rare but life-threatening condition due to the risk of systemic embolization. In this single-center retrospective surgical case series, we evaluated perioperative management, operative strategy and outcomes after surgical thrombectomy for TAMT, a condition with limited evidence and no established treatment standard.

Methods

Between 2004 and 2025, 14 patients (median age 57.5 years; 9 male) underwent open thrombectomy for TAMT at our institution. TAMT was defined as an intraluminal, imaging-confirmed thrombus attached to a non-aneurysmal and non-dissected aortic wall without identifiable cardiac or proximal embolic source.

Results

Acute systemic embolization represented the first clinical manifestation in the majority of patients, including stroke (n = 6), limb ischemia (n = 6) and visceral ischemia (n = 2). Thrombus localization included the ascending aorta (n=1), aortic arch (n=6), combined ascending aorta and arch (n=5), arch and descending thoracic aorta (n=1), and multiple thoracic aortic levels (n=1). All procedures were performed under cardiopulmonary bypass and hypothermic circulatory arrest allowing complete thrombus removal in all patients. One patient died within 30 days in hospital due to sepsis. Two disabling postoperative strokes and one new postoperative peripheral embolic event occurred. Median follow-up time was 3.5 months (IQR 0.4-60.7). No persistent or recurrent TAMT was observed during imaging follow-up (median imaging follow up 0.6 months).

Conclusion

Open surgical thrombectomy with hypothermic circulatory arrest permitted complete macroscopic thrombus removal in this selected surgical cohort and was technically feasible.

title: Endoscopic Resection of Plantar Ganglion of the Great Toe via the Midline Plantar Portals.
authorString: Pan X, Lui TH, Pan Y, Li CCH, Slocum AMY, Su W, Sun Y.
abstractText: Toe ganglion cysts can be painful because of shoe compression or pressure during walking. Moreover, they can present as repeated rupture, infection, and continuous discharge. Surgery is recommended for symptomatic ganglion recalcitrant to conservative treatment. Open ganglionectomy has potential risk of wound complications, formation of painful scar, and high recurrence rate. The purpose of this technical note is to describe the details of endoscopic resection of plantar ganglion of the great toe via the midline plantar portals. This is a combination of both resection and internal drainage of the ganglion. This minimal invasive approach may help to reduce the risk of recurrence and the risk of injury to the digital neurovascular bundle.

title: Retroperitoneal Robot-Assisted Radical Nephroureterectomy Using the Hugo RAS System in a 135-cm-Tall Adult: Technical Strategies for Minimizing External Arm Interference.
authorString: Morizane S, Hasegawa A, Tamura J, Yamane H, Shimizu R, Teraoka S, Nishikawa R, Kimura Y, Hikita K, Takenaka A.
abstractText:
Introduction

The Hugo RAS system uses four independent arm carts, making external arm interference a potential challenge in adults with very short stature. We report retroperitoneal robot-assisted radical nephroureterectomy in a 135-cm-tall adult.

Case presentation

A woman in her 80s with a bladder tumor and cT1N0M0 left renal pelvic cancer underwent transurethral resection of the bladder tumor and retroperitoneal Hugo RAS robot-assisted radical nephroureterectomy during a single anesthetic session using a previously reported four-robot-port free-access configuration. After renal mobilization, the ports were reassigned and all four carts repositioned caudally for distal ureteral dissection and bladder cuff excision. Total elapsed time was 338 min (287 min for nephroureterectomy); estimated blood loss was 50 mL, with no perioperative complications. The system log recorded one arm-interference error without procedural interruption or clinical impact.

Conclusion

This configuration was feasible in this patient. Further experience is needed to define patient selection and broader applicability.

title: Buffalo Hump in an HIV-Negative Patient: A Case Report of Preoperative Imaging Limitations and Cardiometabolic Considerations.
authorString: Zhou Y.
abstractText: An HIV-negative man with cardiometabolic comorbidities presented with a dorsocervical fat pad. Histopathology confirmed substantial fibrosis; however, 11-month postoperative MRI alone could not establish that non-contrast CT underestimated the original fibrotic burden, given possible postsurgical confounders and the absence of same-timepoint imaging.

title: Surgical Decision-Making in <i>Staphylococcus aureus</i> Infective Endocarditis With Structural Valve Destruction Despite the Absence of Overt Heart Failure: The Role of the Endocarditis Team.
authorString: Adnan M, Taher T, Ashraf H, Grogono J, Tobin E.
abstractText: In young patients with Staphylococcus aureus bacteraemia, early transoesophageal echocardiography plays a pivotal role in the detection of destructive infective endocarditis and promotes timely surgical management.

title: Primary Pericardial Synovial Sarcoma Presenting as a Giant Intrapericardial Mass: A Case Report.
authorString: Zhou X, Liu H, Sun W, Hua Z.
abstractText: Primary pericardial synovial sarcoma is an extremely rare malignant tumor with nonspecific presentation and poor prognosis. We report the case of a 29-year-old woman whose pericardial mass was detected during a workplace health examination. Transthoracic echocardiography revealed a giant intrapericardial mass predominantly compressing the left atrium. Computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a heterogeneous intrapericardial mass extending from the left margin of the main pulmonary artery to the left atrioventricular groove, with partial invasion of the left atrial cavity. Ultrasound-guided biopsy showed a monophasic spindle-cell neoplasm. Immunohistochemistry showed focal weak positivity for pancytokeratin and epithelial membrane antigen, positivity for vimentin and D2-40, weak positivity for CD99, and a Ki-67 labeling index of approximately 15%. Fluorescence in situ hybridization using an SS18 break-apart probe demonstrated split red and green signals in tumor-cell nuclei, consistent with SS18 rearrangement. The patient declined surgical resection and adjuvant therapy and died 22 months after diagnosis. This case emphasizes that multimodality imaging is essential for defining tumor extent but cannot establish histological subtype. Integrated histology, immunohistochemistry, and SS18 fluorescence in situ hybridization are required for diagnostic confirmation.

title: Sesamin Ameliorates Insulin Resistance in Association With Gut Microbiota Remodeling and ICA-AhR-GLP-1 Signaling in Diabetic Mice.
authorString: Li Z, Chen M, Zhang Y, Ling K, Wang Q, Wu F, Qiu Z, Ding D, Zhang Y, Wang D, Lv K, Zha L, Hou X, Kong X.
abstractText: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is closely associated with insulin resistance and gut microbiota dysbiosis. Here, we identified a microbiota-associated indole-3-carboxaldehyde (ICA)-AhR-GLP-1 pathway that contributes to the glucose-lowering effect of sesamin (Ses), a major sesame lignan. In db/db mice, Ses improved hyperglycemia and insulin resistance, while remodeling the gut microbiota and enriching Ligilactobacillus. Fecal microbiota transplantation from Ses-treated donors partially transferred these metabolic benefits. Integrated bacterial isolation, Ses-based fermentation, fecal metabolomics, and clinical LC-MS/MS analysis identified ICA as a Ses-responsive microbiota-associated metabolite. Serum ICA levels were reduced in newly diagnosed patients with T2DM and negatively correlated with FBG, HbA1c, and HOMA-IR. Oral ICA reproduced key metabolic effects of Ses and enhanced intestinal Gcg expression and GLP-1 production. Mechanistically, ICA bound to AhR, promoted AhR nuclear translocation, increased AhR occupancy at the XRE-containing region of the Gcg promoter, and stimulated GLP-1 secretion in STC-1 cells and intestinal organoids. AhR inhibition reduced Ses-induced GLP-1 production and partially attenuated its metabolic effects, whereas acute GLP-1R blockade blunted Ses- and ICA-induced improvements in glucose tolerance and early insulin secretion. Together, these findings support a model in which Ses improves glucose homeostasis in association with gut microbiota remodeling and engagement of an ICA-AhR-GLP-1 pathway.

title: KRT16 From Diverse Tumors Induces Atrial Remodeling and Fibrillation via Endothelial-to-Mesenchymal Transition.
authorString: Zhan G, Yang X, Xue G, Li J, Wang X, Dong H, Yang X, Meng X, Dong Y, Zhang Y, Pan Z, Xia Y.
abstractText: Anticancer therapy increases the incidence of atrial fibrillation (AF), the most common sustained cardiac arrhythmia worldwide. However, whether multiple cancers directly promote AF independently of anticancer therapy through shared mechanisms remains unclear. Here, retrospective clinical analyses revealed significantly increased AF prevalence in pre-treatment female patients with breast cancer (BC), lung cancer (LC), and colorectal cancer (CRC), independent of anticancer therapy. Consistently, orthotopic tumor-bearing mouse models exhibited enhanced AF inducibility accompanied by atrial enlargement, fibrosis, and electrical remodeling. Integrated transcriptomic analyses, combined with the TCGA datasets, identified endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EndMT) as a shared atrial remodeling pathway underlying tumor-associated AF across multiple cancers. Mechanistically, keratin 16 (KRT16) acted as a shared circulating factor across multiple malignancies. KRT16 accumulated in atrial endothelial cells and promoted EndMT through annexin A2 (AnxA2)-dependent activation of TGF-β1/Smad signaling. KRT16 promoted abnormal membrane retention of AnxA2 by suppressing Tyr23 phosphorylation, thereby sustaining profibrotic signaling and atrial remodeling. Genetic silencing of KRT16 in cancer cells or endothelial knockdown of AnxA2 markedly attenuated EndMT, atrial fibrosis, and AF susceptibility in tumor-bearing mice. Our findings demonstrate that multiple cancers directly induce atrial remodeling and AF through a shared mechanism centered on KRT16-driven EndMT, identifying this pathway as a potential therapeutic target.

title: Periodontitis Exacerbates Bone Destruction in Rheumatoid Arthritis Through Porphyromonas gingivalis-Induced Carbamylated Neutrophil Extracellular Traps.
authorString: Yu M, Zhou Y, Dong S, Lian S, Wang W, Chen X, Chen Y, Liu L, Sun Y.
abstractText: Positive correlations between periodontitis and rheumatoid arthritis (RA) are well-documented, yet the underlying causality and mechanisms remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to elucidate the causal role of periodontitis in RA progression and to investigate the mechanisms. Here, we identified carbamylated neutrophil extracellular traps (cNETs), a structure closely associated with bone destruction in RA, as a key mediator. Clinically, synovial samples from RA patients with periodontitis exhibited significantly elevated cNET levels compared to those from periodontally healthy RA patients, and cNET abundance positively correlated with higher rheumatoid factor levels, deeper probing depth and greater clinical attachment loss. In a murine model combining periodontitis and RA, periodontitis exacerbated RA severity, accompanied by increased cNETs formation, particularly upon exposure to Porphyromonas gingivalis. Mechanistically, transcriptomic sequencing and functional assays revealed that cNETs promote osteoclastogenesis and aggravate bone erosion in RA by enhancing RANKL secretion via the MAPK pathway. Therapeutically, chemical inhibition of carbamylation markedly reduced ankle joint inflammation and bone destruction, concomitant with decreased cNET levels and MAPK phosphorylation. Together, our findings establish a causal link between periodontitis and RA aggravation, mediated by P. gingivalis-triggered cNETs that fuel osteoclast formation. Targeting cNETs may thus represent a promising therapeutic strategy for RA.

title: The impact of CYP3A5 genotype on tacrolimus pharmacokinetics in children following heart transplant.
authorString: Rower JE, Freeman TS, Deering-Rice CE, Molina KM.
abstractText: Tacrolimus is a first-line immunosuppressant used after solid organ transplantation that suffers from extensive intra- and inter-patient variability and a narrow therapeutic window. Tacrolimus clearance is predominantly mediated by CYP3A4 and CYP3A5, with evidence indicating that pharmacogenetic (PG) differences in these enzymes drive significant changes in tacrolimus pharmacokinetics (PK) and therapeutic tacrolimus dosing. The current study investigates the hypothesis that CYP3A4/5 genetic variation alters tacrolimus dose requirement and metabolite concentration in children following pediatric heart transplant. Saliva and whole blood samples were collected from children who previously received a heart transplant as part of a tacrolimus PG/PK study. A total of 64 children were included in the analysis, which found that children carrying a CYP3A5*1 allele required a 2.7-fold higher tacrolimus dose (p < 0.0001) than individuals with the CYP3A5*3/*3 genotype. Weight-adjusted dose-normalized concentrations of tacrolimus (p < 0.0001) and its M-I (p = 0.0049) and M-II (p = 0.0043) metabolites were significantly lower in children with the CYP3A5*1 allele. Combined, these data support the impact of CYP3A5 genotype on tacrolimus PK and demonstrate the need for larger studies to confirm the clinical importance of this genotype for appropriate tacrolimus dosing in pediatric heart transplant recipients.

title: PFI-3 attenuates atherosclerotic plaque vulnerability and modulates a BRG1-SLUG-miR-193b-3p-CD47 axis in cultured vascular smooth muscle cells.
authorString: Liu B, Zhang M, Li Y, Li H, Sun Z, Liu Q, Hou J.
abstractText:
Aims

CD47, a "don't-eat-me" signal overexpressed in atherosclerotic lesions, impairs efferocytosis and promotes plaque instability. BRG1 (SMARCA4), the catalytic ATPase of the SWI/SNF chromatin-remodeling complex, drives vascular inflammation, yet its role in CD47 regulation remains unknown. We investigated whether PFI-3, an inhibitor of the BRG1/SMARCA4, BRM/SMARCA2, and PBRM1 bromodomains, attenuates plaque vulnerability and delineated the BRG1-dependent cascade regulating CD47 in vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs).

Materials and methods

High-fat-diet-fed ApoE-/- mice received oral PFI-3 or vehicle; plaque burden, composition, and efferocytosis were assessed histologically. LPS-stimulated mouse VSMCs (mVSMCs) underwent BRG1 knockdown or PFI-3 treatment followed by macrophage engulfment assays. ChIP-qPCR, dual-luciferase, and epistatic rescue experiments defined the regulatory cascade.

Key findings

PFI-3 reduced plaque area, necrotic core size, and macrophage infiltration while increasing collagen and α-SMA content, without altering circulating lipids. Free apoptotic cells decreased and macrophage-associated clearance increased. In vitro, LPS co-upregulated BRG1, SLUG, and CD47 in mVSMCs. BRG1 silencing suppressed SLUG and CD47 and enhanced phagocytosis. ChIP confirmed BRG1 occupancy at the SLUG promoter; SLUG repressed miR-193b-3p, which targeted the CD47 3'-UTR. PFI-3 phenocopied BRG1 knockdown by restoring miR-193b-3p and suppressing CD47.

Significance

This study identifies a BRG1 → SLUG→miR-193b-3p → CD47 cascade in mVSMCs whereby BRG1 elevates CD47 under inflammation to impair efferocytosis. PFI-3 suppresses this axis in vitro and attenuates plaque vulnerability in vivo - although contributions from BRM/SMARCA2 and PBRM1 inhibition cannot be excluded. These findings support further investigation of PFI-3 and this regulatory axis in atherosclerosis.

title: Centrality of the periphery: Small muscle mass to bypass O<sub>2</sub> transport limitations and maximize the benefits of exercise training in heart failure.
authorString: Iannetta D, Laginestra FG, Broxterman RM, Simonelli C, Amann M, Paneroni M.
abstractText: Heart failure (HF) is a complex, systemic cardiovascular condition characterized by a severe impairment in O<sub>2</sub> transport to skeletal muscle that drives exercise intolerance and reduces quality of life. Although exercise training (ET) is a cornerstone of HF clinical management, patients often exhibit limited improvements in peak oxygen uptake ( V̇O2peak ) following traditional whole-body, aerobic exercise recruiting a large muscle mass (e.g., cycling). In patients with HF, adaptations within skeletal muscle (e.g., capillarization) exert a proportionally greater influence on changes in V̇O2peak than adaptations in cardiac performance. In this review, we discuss the mechanisms by which traditional ET prescription may be suboptimal to elicit peripheral adaptations and argue that dynamic exercise recruiting only a small muscle mass (e.g., quadriceps) may be more effective in achieving this goal. Indeed, small muscle mass exercise reduces the cardiovascular restraints imposed by the failing heart, allowing the muscle to reach much greater metabolic rates and to be exposed to much larger degrees of homeostatic perturbations, a key factor triggering adaptations in O<sub>2</sub> transport and utilization at the peripheral level. The intent of this review is to discuss the influence of muscle mass on exercise tolerance and adaptations to ET in HF, with the ultimate goal of promoting the integration of small muscle mass exercise into contemporary cardiac rehabilitation programmes.

title: Hiding in Plain Sight: An Inferior Sinus Venosus Defect With Anomalous Right Middle and Lower Pulmonary Veins.
authorString: Siddiqui Z, Shing H, Rigby M.
abstractText: Sinus venosus defects are uncommon interatrial communications located outside the oval fossa. We describe a case of a seven-year-old girl with a history of fainting episodes, brought to the emergency department after several witnessed vacant episodes at school. Neurological examination was normal, but cardiovascular examination detected an ejection systolic murmur at the upper left sternal edge (pulmonary area). She was observed for 48 hours in hospital with ambulatory electrocardiographic monitoring, which showed sinus rhythm with no arrhythmia. She was seen in the cardiology clinic six months later, where she reported to be well and asymptomatic. Initial transthoracic echocardiography showed right atrial and ventricular dilatation with a left-to-right shunt, which initially looked suspicious to be at or near atrial level, later confirmed on further transthoracic echocardiography and cardiac computed tomography to be a large inferior sinus venosus defect (approximately 11 mm in diameter on echocardiography and 16 x 8 mm on computed tomography), with anomalous connection of the right lower and right middle pulmonary veins to the right atrium through a common channel overriding the atrial septum, with associated marked right heart volume loading with preserved biventricular function. She is planned for surgical repair. This case shows how an unrelated presentation led to the diagnosis of a rare congenital anomaly and highlights the difficulty of identifying inferior sinus venosus defects on transthoracic echocardiography, and the less commonly described involvement of the right middle pulmonary vein, with an isolated anomalous connection of the right lower pulmonary vein being the usual finding.

title: The Surgical Removal of A Giant Intracardiac Thrombus and Pulmonary Embolectomy.
authorString: McCarthy TJ, Cagney PS, Kirby F, McCarthy JF.
abstractText: A mobile thrombus traversing a patent foramen ovale in the setting of high-risk acute pulmonary embolism carries an immediate risk of both pulmonary and systemic embolization. Early multidisciplinary recognition and prompt surgical thrombectomy with PFO closure can provide definitive treatment in selected hemodynamically unstable patients.

title: Serous Ovarian Carcinoma Presenting With Synchronous Breast Metastasis: A Case Report and Literature Review.
authorString: Omranipour R, Nozheh A, Esmaeilian S, Karkeabadi N, Zand S, Tavasooliniyasari N.
abstractText: Synchronous breast metastasis from ovarian cancer is exceptionally rare. A 53-year-old woman with FIGO IIIC high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma underwent cytoreductive surgery, chemotherapy, and breast radiotherapy. Immunohistochemistry confirmed metastatic disease. Complete response persisted for over 7 years before platinum-resistant recurrence, emphasizing accurate diagnosis and multimodal treatment in selected patients.

title: A Focal "Inferno Sign" With an Aberrant Innominate Artery Feeder: A Thyroid Arteriovenous Malformation Mimicking Malignancy in a Young Woman.
authorString: Nyakubaho A, Ayikoru B, Okwir MA, Nyakake J, Ochom J, Babirye D.
abstractText: Arteriovenous malformations (AVMs) of the thyroid gland are exceptionally rare, with only 11 cases identified in our review of the literature. They are clinically important because their hypervascularity on imaging can raise suspicion of malignancy, and biopsy or surgery may provoke life-threatening hemorrhage. We present a case of a 30-year-old female with a decade-long history of anterior neck swelling that recently became painful and enlarged. Ultrasound demonstrated a well-defined hypoechoic right-lobe nodule with marked color Doppler hypervascularity (described here as a focal "inferno sign"), a tangled vascular nidus, low-resistance arterial flow in the dominant feeding vessel, and early arterialization of the draining vein; together, these findings suggested arteriovenous shunting. Computed tomography angiography (CTA) characterized the lesion as a 1.0 cm × 0.9 cm intensely enhancing nodule supplied by an aberrant artery arising directly from the innominate artery, immediately medial to the origin of the right common carotid artery, with drainage into the right internal jugular vein. A radiological diagnosis of thyroid AVM was made without histopathological or angiographic confirmation, and fine-needle aspiration (FNA) was avoided because of the bleeding risk. The patient was referred for multidisciplinary management but was lost to follow-up. To our knowledge, this is the first reported thyroid AVM supplied by an innominate artery branch, a variant relevant to surgical and endovascular planning. Thyroid AVM should be considered in the differential diagnosis of hypervascular thyroid nodules, and CTA is valuable for mapping its vascular anatomy noninvasively.

title: Cardiac Tamponade Masquerading as Lactic Acidosis.
authorString: Firoz A, Tran A, Mahmood T, Bhat A, Schivo M.
abstractText: An 85-year-old male presented with acute dyspnea and syncope, with pertinent initial vital signs including hypertension, normal heart rate, tachypnea, and hypoxemia requiring oxygen supplementation. The Medical Intensive Care Unit (MICU) team was consulted for treatment of acute hypoxic respiratory failure, severe hyperglycemia, and lactic acidosis; on MICU evaluation, bedside point of care ultrasonography (POCUS) revealed a large, circumferential pericardial effusion. Despite ongoing intravenous fluid resuscitation, the patient rapidly developed cardiac tamponade with pulsus paradoxus and hypotension. Given the severe hyperglycemia and likely resultant osmotic diuresis, his atypical presentation may have represented low-pressure cardiac tamponade phenotype. He was emergently taken for pericardiocentesis and drain placement with immediate resolution of clinical tamponade; the etiology of his pericardial effusion was deemed idiopathic, although a hemorrhagic effusion from anticoagulation use cannot be ruled out. Ultimately, this case highlights POCUS as an essential clinical tool that should be utilized upon initial assessment of ICU level of care patients to avoid missing indolent but fatal conditions, such as developing or manifest cardiac tamponade. Once cardiac tamponade is identified, careful intravenous fluid resuscitation may be appropriate under the correct circumstances, although definitive treatment involves emergent pericardiocentesis.

title: tsRNA-076 Promotes VSMC Autophagy and Vascular Remodeling by Activating IGF2BP2 Transcription.
authorString: Cao S, Zhang Q, Wang S, Wang S, Tang Q, Wang Z, Cao Y, Dong Z, Luo W, Yang L, Chen L, You D, Zhao Y, Zheng M, Sun S.
abstractText: tRNA-derived small RNAs (tsRNAs) are an emerging class of regulatory non-coding RNAs involved in diverse biological processes, yet their functions in the nucleus remain poorly understood. Here, we identify a nuclear-enriched tsRNA, tsRNA-076, that is markedly upregulated in synthetic vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) and plays an important role in vascular remodeling. Mechanistically, tsRNA-076 functions as an endogenous small activating RNA (saRNA) by directly associating with the IGF2BP2 (insulin-like growth factor 2 mRNA binding protein 2) promoter and facilitating recruitment of the transcription factor ETV2 (ETS variant transcription factor 2), thereby driving transcriptional activation of IGF2BP2. Elevated IGF2BP2 enhances ATG5 expression by stabilizing its mRNA in an m<sup>6</sup>A-dependent manner, thereby promoting VSMC autophagy. Inhibition of tsRNA-076 attenuates VSMC autophagy and alleviates vascular remodeling in vitro and in vivo. Together, these findings uncover a previously unrecognized RNA activation mechanism mediated by tsRNA-076 and provide new insights into vascular remodeling.

title: Artificial Intelligence as a Catalyst for Value-Based Care in Vascular Disease.
authorString: Raskin D, Ahmed M, Barash Y, Partovi S, Katzen BT, Piazza G, Kirksey L.
abstractText: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in vascular imaging, risk prediction, clinical text analysis, workflow coordination, and procedural planning, but its value depends on whether it turns available data into appropriate action and better outcomes at acceptable cost. In this structured narrative review of literature and regulatory sources through September 2026, we summarize a practical AI toolkit for vascular care in 5 categories: imaging, surveillance, procedural planning, workflow management, and decision support. Several tools are cleared by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, mostly for aortic measurement, triage, and procedural guidance, but evidence remains largely retrospective and technical, with few studies of clinical action, outcomes, cost, or equity. We propose a value-based framework that evaluates AI across 5 steps (data, detection, context, action, and outcome) and offer practical questions to guide adoption. In conclusion, the value of vascular AI depends on whether it improves care and patient outcomes across complete clinical pathways, with attention to resource use, safety, and equity.

title: When Less Is More: Conservative Dietary Management of Congenital Chylous Ascites in an Infant: A Case Report From Tanzania.
authorString: Ntinika S, Ngowi E, Thomas J, Omary S, Thaver S, Gabone J, Abdallah Y, Mwamanenge N, Noorani M, Salum HM.
abstractText: Chylous ascites is a rare condition resulting from lymphatic system dysfunction; most often due to congenital malformations. It carries significant morbidity related to nutritional, immunologic, and electrolyte losses. Management is primarily conservative, focusing on dietary modification with additional interventions including therapeutic drainage and pharmacological therapy, whereas surgical approaches are generally reserved for refractory cases. A 5-week-old girl with antenatally detected ascites presented with progressive abdominal distension and post-feed vomiting. Examination and ultrasonography confirmed isolated severe ascites, and diagnostic paracentesis yielded milky fluid with a markedly elevated triglyceride concentration (6870 mg/dL), supporting the diagnosis of chylous ascites. Because the infant remained clinically stable and commercial MCT formula was unavailable, she was managed with skimmed expressed breast milk supplemented with multivitamins and coconut oil as a locally available medium-chain triglyceride-containing source. Feeding tolerance improved, abdominal girth progressively decreased, and follow-up ultrasonography demonstrated substantial resolution of the ascites. This case suggests that carefully monitored skimmed breast milk supplemented with coconut oil, a readily available fat source containing a substantial proportion of medium-chain triglyceride source may represent a feasible conservative option in resource-limited settings.

title: PREGNANCY OUTCOMES IN A CONTEMPORARY COHORT OF WOMEN WITH REPAIRED TETRALOGY OF FALLOT.
authorString: Franch MJA, Pijuan-Domenech A, Ródenas-Alesina E, Aviles ACS, Barrio BM, Gordon B, González-Fernández V, Cubiles IAL, Goya M, Martínez EDB, Lerma MLP, Edo ES, Mendoza VA, Subirà LD.
abstractText: Most women with repaired Tetralogy of Fallot (rTOF) now reach reproductive age, but pregnancy outcomes in contemporary cohorts, particularly after pulmonary valve replacement (PVR), remain uncertain. The aim of this study as to assess maternal cardiac, obstetric and neonatal outcomes in a contemporary cohort of women with rTOF. We retrospectively included all pregnancies in women with rTOF followed at a tertiary referral center for complex congenital heart disease (CHD) and high-risk pregnancy between 2013 and 2024. A total of 44 pregnancies in 32 women with rTOF were included, resulting in 45 live births. Severe PR was present in 43% of pregnancies, and 40% had undergone prior PVR. Maternal cardiac events occurred in 6.8%: 2 cases of supraventricular arrhythmias and 1 case of thrombosis on an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) lead. Among women with prior PVR, transvalvular gradients increased transiently during pregnancy and returned to baseline postpartum. Mean gestational age was 38 weeks, vaginal birth was preferred and cesarean section was performed in 18% of pregnancies. The most frequent adverse obstetric and neonatal outcomes were low birth weight (22%) and preterm birth (11%), both associated with lower pre-pregnancy right ventricular ejection fraction (RVEF) possibly reflecting impaired uteroplacental perfusion related to right ventricular dysfunction. In conclusion, in this contemporary cohort, pregnancy in women with rTOF was associated with low risk of maternal cardiac events, mainly supraventricular arrhythmias. However, low birth weight and preterm birth remained frequent and were associated with lower pre-pregnancy RVEF, underscoring the importance of specialized cardio-obstetric follow-up.

title: From Bernoulli to Bedside: Fifty Years of Doppler Echocardiography for Valvular Pressure Gradients: Lessons in Translating Ideas into Clinical Practice.
authorString: Thomas JD, Smiseth OA.

journal.title: Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography : official publication of the American Society of Echocardiography

title: Risk factors of in-hospital mortality in adult emergency department patients with atraumatic acute abdominal pain: a retrospective cohort study.
authorString: Breßer M, Röttgen J, Dohmen J, Kalff JC, Matthaei H, Gräff I, Henn J.
abstractText:
Background

Acute abdominal pain (AAP) accounts for 7-10% of adult emergency department (ED) visits and represents a heterogeneous presentation. While diagnostic pathways have improved, early prognostic assessment remains limited. Identifying routinely available parameters associated with in-hospital mortality may provide prognostic information at initial triage. Therefore, we aimed to identify such parameters in adult AAP patients.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adult patients assigned to the "abdominal pain in adults" Manchester Triage System flowchart at the University Hospital Bonn ED (2023-2025). Candidate predictors comprised all structured parameters available at initial triage. Missing data were handled using multiple imputation. Group differences were assessed using Fisher's exact and Mann-Whitney U tests. We fitted a multivariable logistic regression model to assess associations between candidate predictors and in-hospital mortality. P-values were Bonferroni-adjusted. A focused literature search contextualized mortality.

Results

Among 6,370 encounters, 94 (1.5%) ended in death during the ED encounter or subsequent hospitalization. In-hospital mortality (1.5%) was within previously published ranges (0.4-8.0%). Patients who died were older and had lower systolic and diastolic blood pressure and SpO₂, higher pain NRS scores, and a different distribution of GCS scores at initial triage after adjustment for multiple testing. In multivariable analysis, age (OR 1.067 per year; 95% CI 1.052-1.082), lower diastolic blood pressure (OR 0.953 per mmHg; 95% CI 0.932-0.976), higher heart rate (OR 1.022 per beat/min; 95% CI 1.009-1.036), lower SpO₂ (OR 0.885 per percentage point; 95% CI 0.833-0.940), and higher pain NRS scores (OR 1.283 per point; 95% CI 1.126-1.462) were associated with mortality after adjustment for multiple testing. Among patients who died, vascular or bleeding disorders, bowel ischemia, and malignancy were the leading diagnostic categories.

Conclusions

In adult ED patients presenting with atraumatic AAP, in-hospital mortality was 1.5%, within the previously reported range. Age, lower diastolic blood pressure, higher heart rate, lower SpO₂, and higher pain intensity were independently associated with mortality after adjustment for multiple testing. These routinely available parameters may provide prognostic information at initial triage, but their value for improving risk prediction or clinical decision-making requires further investigation.

title: High levels of large HDL particles in long-term survivors of type 1 diabetes or familial hypercholesterolemia free from coronary heart disease events.
authorString: Narum M, Christensen JJ, Melnes T, Holven KB, Berg TJ, Sveen KA.
abstractText: Both individuals with type 1 diabetes and individuals with familial hypercholesterolemia (FH) are at increased risk of developing coronary heart disease (CHD). Nevertheless, some of these individuals appear to be free of CHD. We aimed to study similarities in lipoproteins and other metabolites in long-term survivors of type 1 diabetes or FH free from CHD events, to identify potential common cardioprotective biomarkers. In 102 subjects with type 1 diabetes, 83 subjects with FH and 61 control subjects, we used a nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy platform to quantify a set of circulating metabolites. For FH subjects, previous history of CHD events was identified in patient charts. Subjects with type 1 diabetes and controls without information about previously established CHD performed a computed tomography coronary angiography (CTCA). Multivariate analyses showed that both the CHD event-free subgroup of type 1 diabetes and the CHD event-free subgroup of FH had significantly higher particle concentration of extra-large (XL) high-density lipoprotein (XL-HDL), large-HDL (L-HDL) and medium-HDL (M-HDL) compared to the CHD event-free controls. XL-HDL and L-HDL also correlated inversely with the inflammatory marker GlycA for all study groups. CHD event-free individuals with either long-term type 1 diabetes or FH were characterized by higher levels of larger HDL particles compared to CHD event-free controls, which also associated inversely with GlycA. These results suggest a protective linkage between larger HDL particles and less inflammation, thereby potentially contributing to an attenuation of the development of CHD in these very high-risk populations.

title: FUNDC1-Mediated Mitophagy in Cardiovascular Disease: Context-Dependent Regulation of Mitochondrial Quality Control and Dysfunction.
authorString: Niu Z, Li J, Fan G, Zhou R, Cui Z, Shi S, Wang P.
abstractText: Mitochondrial quality-control failure contributes to cardiovascular injury, but the consequences of mitophagy depend on the nature and timing of stress. FUN14 domain-containing protein 1 (FUNDC1) is an outer mitochondrial membrane mitophagy receptor that also regulates mitochondrial dynamics, mitochondria-endoplasmic reticulum contacts, and Ca2⁺ homeostasis. This review synthesizes the regulation of FUNDC1 and critically examines its context-dependent effects in myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury (MIRI), heart failure and myocardial remodeling, and metabolic cardiomyopathy. In several MIRI and heart-failure models, impaired FUNDC1-associated mitochondrial quality control is linked to injury, whereas excessive or mistimed FUNDC1-associated mitophagy may be detrimental in selected reperfusion and pulmonary vascular settings. In metabolic cardiomyopathy, hyperglycemia-associated FUNDC1-IP3R2 signaling promotes abnormal organelle contacts and mitochondrial Ca2⁺ overload, whereas FUNDC1 deficiency during lipid overload is linked to mitochondrial damage and heightened lipotoxic susceptibility. These apparently divergent effects may reflect differences in cellular context, stress exposure, disease stage, and mitophagy-independent FUNDC1 functions; however, the underlying causal mechanisms remain incompletely defined. We highlight inconsistencies among experimental models and distinguish evidence from direct mitophagy-flux measurements from conclusions based on indirect markers. Given the predominance of preclinical evidence, further mechanistic and translational studies are needed before FUNDC1-directed therapies can be considered for clinical use.

title: Progressive morphological changes of a bioprosthetic mitral valve on serial chest CT preceding severe haemodynamic deterioration in systemic sclerosis: a case report.
authorString: Nguyen HQ, Bui PD, Alvarez Plascencia RM, Duong AT, Dang HQ.
abstractText:
Background

Structural valve deterioration is an important cause of bioprosthetic valve dysfunction. Morphological abnormalities may precede clinically significant haemodynamic deterioration, but recognition of this progression may depend on longitudinal comparison of imaging studies.

Case summary

A 76-year-old man with a surgical bioprosthetic mitral valve implanted in 2014 was diagnosed with systemic sclerosis-associated interstitial lung disease in 2022 and subsequently underwent serial chest computed tomography (CT). Echocardiography in 2022 and March 2023 demonstrated preserved prosthetic valve haemodynamics. In August 2024, he was admitted with progressive heart failure and severe bioprosthetic mitral stenosis. Retrospective review of serial CT demonstrated progressive leaflet changes, from a relatively thin appearance in 2022 to mild thickening in 2023 and marked diffuse thickening with an apparent fusion-like configuration in May 2024. Transoesophageal echocardiography demonstrated severe leaflet thickening and restriction with a suspected superimposed thrombotic component. Despite therapeutic enoxaparin, recurrent pulmonary oedema prompted redo mitral valve replacement. Operative examination demonstrated diffuse leaflet thickening, rigidity, and commissural fusion, with non-dominant pannus and thin thrombotic material.

Discussion

This case illustrates the value of longitudinal comparison of existing imaging studies. Progressive morphological changes of a bioprosthetic valve were retrospectively identified on chest CT performed for a non-cardiac indication before severe haemodynamic deterioration was recognized by echocardiography. This does not support routine CT surveillance; rather, abnormalities encountered on existing extracardiac imaging may provide an additional signal to consider earlier cardiac reassessment.

title: Phenotypic Characterization and Spatial Distribution of Eruptive versus Non-Eruptive Calcified Nodules: A Comparative Multimodality Imaging Analysis.
authorString: Watanabe T, Usui E, Kanaji Y, Ueno H, Sayama K, Watanabe T, Murakami R, Hiroi S, Hosokawa K, Yonetsu T, Kakuta T.
abstractText:
Aim

Calcified nodules (CNs) represent a high-risk morphological subset of coronary atherosclerosis, categorized into eruptive and non-eruptive subtypes. Although previous studies have noted morphological differences, the interplay between plaque composition, spatial distribution, and eruption biomechanics across clinical presentations remains incompletely understood.

Methods

We performed a multimodality intravascular imaging study using optical coherence tomography (OCT) and near-infrared spectroscopy-intravascular ultrasound (NIRS-IVUS) in patients with coronary CNs across chronic and acute coronary syndromes. We assessed calcium architecture, lipid content (maximum lipid core burden index within 4-mm, maxLCBI4mm), and anatomical distribution to evaluate factors associated with the eruptive phenotype.

Results

We identified 70 CNs (31 eruptive, 39 non-eruptive) in 64 patients. Eruptive CNs exhibited greater calcium angles, increased thickness, longer longitudinal extent, and significantly higher maxLCBI4mm compared to non-eruptive CNs. Topographically, eruptive CNs preferentially clustered within high-biomechanical-stress regions (mid-right coronary artery and proximal left anterior descending artery), whereas non-eruptive CNs were homogeneously distributed. A multivariable analysis confirmed hemodialysis, mid-RCA location, and elevated maxLCBI4mm as independent factors associated with the eruptive phenotype.

Conclusion

Eruptive CNs reflect a potential "two-hit" mechanism, wherein a vulnerable substrate (heavily calcified, lipid-rich plaque) interacts with a permissive mechanical environment (vascular flexion/hinge points) to promote eruption. Integrating plaque composition with anatomical location enhances the phenotypic characterization of calcified coronary disease.

title: Plasma Pyrophosphate Levels in Calcification of Joints and Arteries Compared with Generalized Arterial Calcification of Infancy.
authorString: Hidaka N, Takamura T, Sakai N, Niida Y, Ura H, Tanaka M, Nakazato H, Kimura S, Kato H, Adachi N, Furukawa K, Irie K, Hoshino Y, Hasegawa Y, Makita N, Nangaku M, Saito T, Tanaka S, Ito N.
abstractText:
Aim

Calcification of joints and arteries (CALJA) is a rare disorder caused by loss-of-function variants in NT5E, characterized by adult-onset ectopic calcification in lower-extremity arteries and periarticular tissues. Although ectopic calcification has been linked to an inorganic pyrophosphate (PPi) deficiency, as observed in generalized arterial calcification of infancy (GACI), the plasma PPi levels in CALJA have not been reported. We provide the first measurement of the plasma PPi levels in CALJA and compare them with GACI.

Methods

The plasma PPi levels were measured in a 44-year-old woman with CALJA and three patients with GACI. Two adult patients with GACI had a regression of arterial calcification, while serial samples were analyzed in a 4-year-old girl with GACI1 during a partial regression of calcification.

Results

The plasma PPi concentration in the patient with CALJA was 0.63 µM (mean of two measurements at a four-month interval), approximately 50% of the lower end of the range reported in healthy adults. However, this level was approximately 30-fold higher than that observed in patients with GACI during the active disease phase and it was also higher than that in those after a resolution of arterial calcification. The serum inorganic phosphate-to-PPi ratio was lower in the CALJA patient than in those with GACI.

Conclusion

Although the PPi levels were reduced in CALJA, they remained substantially higher than those observed in active GACI, indicating that calcification in CALJA cannot be explained by a systemic PPi deficiency alone. These findings suggest a role for adenosine deficiency and local PPi dysregulation in the pathogenesis of CALJA.

title: Identification of Prognostic Lactylation-Related lncRNA Signatures and Immune Infiltration Characteristics in Gastric Cancer.
authorString: Ge J, Xuan J, Hu G, Li M, Zhang M, Li Y, Su J, Zheng Y, Hu J, Yu X, Zhang H.
abstractText:
Background

Lactylation, a novel epigenetic modification, plays a pivotal role in tumor metabolic reprogramming and regulation of the immune microenvironment. Long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) may be associated with gastric cancer (GC) progression and immune modulation through lactylation-related processes.

Methods

GC transcriptomic and clinical data were obtained from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA). Lactylation-related genes were retrieved from GeneCards. Lactylation-related long noncoding RNAs (LLRs) were identified using Pearson correlation analysis. Prognosis-related differentially expressed LLRs were screened using univariate Cox regression and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression analyses. Multivariable Cox regression analysis was performed to identify independent prognostic LLRs and construct a GC risk model. Patients were stratified into high- and low-risk groups, followed by comparative analyses of Kaplan-Meier (K-M) survival, the tumor microenvironment (TME), immune cell infiltration, tumor mutational burden (TMB), and immune evasion.

Results

An 8-LLR-based prognostic model was established to stratify patients with GC, and patients in the high-risk group exhibited poorer overall survival. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis demonstrated moderate predictive performance, with a 5-year area under the curve (AUC) of 0.727. Multivariable Cox regression analysis confirmed that the risk score was an independent prognostic factor. Significant differences in the TME, immune cell infiltration, TMB, and immune evasion were observed between the high- and low-risk groups. Quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) confirmed differences in LLR expression between normal gastric epithelial cells and GC cell lines.

Conclusion

This bioinformatic study explores the potential associations between LLRs, GC prognosis, and the tumor immune microenvironment. The 8-LLR risk model demonstrated moderate predictive performance and provides an exploratory framework for GC risk stratification and the identification of candidate lncRNAs for further investigation.

title: Recent advances in fluorescent probes for diagnostics and targeted therapeutics at the biomedical frontier.
authorString: Bhattacharjee P, Iyer MR.
abstractText: Fluorescence probes have contributed immensely to the understanding of cellular dynamics, pathology, and complex molecular interactions of biomolecules in living systems. There has been a resurgence in fluorescence imaging field mainly due to breakthroughs in advanced high-resolution techniques, thus propelling the development of innovative probes with superior therapeutic potential. This review emphasizes the design of fluorescent probes and the significant advancements in diagnostic modalities over the last five years.

title: Mycotic extrarenal pseudoaneurysm with iliac artery disruption following renal transplantation: a rare case.
authorString: Ramu L, Paul S, Kumar V.
abstractText: Transplant renal artery pseudoaneurysm is a rare but dangerous vascular complication following renal transplantation. We report a case of a 30 year-old male recipient presenting after 2 months with complains of limb swelling and graft dysfunction. On imaging, a pseudoaneurysm at the external iliac anastomosis along with venous compression was noted. Surgical exploration showed complete anastomotic disruption of the transplant renal artery requiring graft nephrectomy and iliac artery reconstruction with an interposition graft that restored the lower limb viability. This case highlights the importance of early recognition and timely surgical intervention in such life-threatening scenarios.

title: Young-Onset Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma Developing after Allogeneic Bone Marrow Transplantation for Fanconi Anemia: A Case Report.
authorString: Furuhara Y, Okumura T, Araki T, Miwa T, Numata Y, Nagamori M, Sakurai T, Fukasawa M, Kimura N, Takeda N, Mori K, Sukegawa K, Watanabe T, Sekine S, Hashimoto I, Shibuya K, Yoshioka I, Fujii T.
abstractText:
Introduction

Fanconi anemia (FA), a rare genetic disorder, is characterized by defective DNA repair and an increased risk of early-onset squamous cell carcinoma. Although hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) improves survival, long-term survivors experience a high risk of secondary malignancies, including esophageal cancer. Owing to extreme sensitivity to chemotherapy and radiotherapy, treatment of FA-associated esophageal cancer is particularly challenging.

Case presentation

A 22-year-old woman with FA who had undergone unrelated allogeneic bone marrow transplantation in childhood developed esophageal squamous cell carcinoma. Preoperative endoscopy, CT, and PET showed no lymph node or distant metastases, and the tumor was staged as cT2N0M0, cStage II. Because of the anticipated severe toxicity of DNA-damaging chemotherapy and radiotherapy in FA, an upfront surgery strategy was selected. Thoracoscopic subtotal esophagectomy with 2-field lymph-node dissection achieved R0 resection. Despite the absence of radiologically or macroscopically suspicious lymph nodes, histopathological examination revealed adventitial invasion, marked lymphovascular invasion, and metastases in 3 of 25 lymph nodes (pT3N2M0, pStage IIIB). Postoperative systemic therapy was considered, but its initiation was deferred because of incomplete postoperative recovery and concern regarding treatment toxicity. Multiple recurrences became evident 4 months after surgery, before systemic therapy could be reconsidered, and the patient died 10 months postoperatively.

Conclusions

This case highlights the therapeutic dilemma in FA-associated esophageal cancer between substantial toxicity from standard cytotoxic therapy and the risk of undertreatment with upfront surgery. The marked discrepancy between clinical and pathological staging illustrates the difficulty of excluding occult nodal or systemic disease when neoadjuvant therapy cannot readily be administered. Previous reports suggest that reduced-dose chemotherapy or chemoradiotherapy may retain antitumor activity but can still cause substantial toxicity, indicating an extremely narrow therapeutic window. Treatment therefore requires individualized multidisciplinary decision-making, while further accumulation of detailed data on treatment intensity, toxicity, response, and outcomes is needed.

title: Pressure-enabled thyroid artery embolization: minimizing the risk of non-target embolization.
authorString: Khoury JK, Camacho JC.
abstractText: Thyroid artery embolization (TAE) conventionally involves embolization of both superior thyroid arteries (STAs) and one inferior thyroid artery (ITA), preserving the contralateral ITA to maintain parathyroid perfusion. Selective STA catheterization carries risks of reflux-related non-target embolization and cerebral thromboembolism due to its origin from the carotid arterial system. Pressure-enabled TAE (PED-TAE) is an ITA-first technique that exploits intrathyroidal anastomoses between the STA and ITA to achieve ipsilateral lobar embolization without direct STA catheterization. The technique uses a valved microcatheter with a self-expanding braided nitinol mesh to reduce reflux and facilitate distal embolic delivery through pressure modulation. This technical letter provides a comprehensive, step-by-step guide to PED-TAE, covering preprocedural vascular assessment, arterial access and device selection, optimal microcatheter positioning, cone-beam CT evaluation, embolization technique, procedural endpoints, and peri- and postprocedural medication management. A practical workflow for patient selection and a procedural decision-making algorithm are presented to guide clinical decision-making, address anatomical and technical challenges, and facilitate reproducible application of the technique. Further prospective multicenter studies are warranted to establish the safety, efficacy, and long-term durability of PED-TAE relative to conventional TAE and surgical management.

title: Targeted Modulation of Matrix-Remodeling: Enzymes, Adhesion Receptors, and Signaling Hubs as Precision Strategies for Antifibrotic Therapy.
authorString: Roeb E, Weiskirchen R.

journal.title: Journal of cell communication and signaling

abstractText: Liver fibrosis is increasingly recognized as a dynamic, spatially organized, and potentially reversible process of maladaptive wound healing rather than a passive consequence of collagen accumulation. Persistent liver injury activates multicellular fibrotic niches composed of hepatic stellate cells, macrophages, endothelial cells, fibrocytes, circulating myeloid populations, and extracellular matrix components that interact through reciprocal signaling networks. This review outlines a precision-oriented antifibrotic framework centered on three interconnected target classes: matrix-remodeling enzymes, adhesion receptors, and intracellular signaling hubs. Matrix metalloproteinases and tissue inhibitors of metalloproteinases regulate extracellular matrix turnover and determine whether fibrotic scars persist, remodel, or regress, indicating that productive fibrolysis should be restored rather than globally enhanced or suppressed. Adhesion receptors, particularly integrins, connect extracellular matrix composition and stiffness to intracellular mechanotransduction, latent TGF-β activation, hepatic stellate cell activation, and fibro-inflammatory cell recruitment. Signaling hubs such as TGF-β\SMAD, GARP-TGF-β, FAK-RhoA/ROCK, PAK, NF-κB, and YAP/TAZ integrate mechanical, inflammatory, and stromal cues into persistent profibrotic cellular states. Recent single-cell, spatial transcriptomic, and spatial multi-omics studies indicate that fibrosis is driven by disease-specific cellular neighborhoods rather than uniform activation of single pathways or cell types. These findings support mechanism-guided strategies that combine molecular target selection with spatial and temporal restriction to preserve physiological repair, immunity, regeneration, and tissue homeostasis. Future antifibrotic therapy will likely depend on identifying the dominant fibrotic niche in individual patients and selectively reprogramming the matrix, cell-matrix interface, and signaling networks that prevent fibrosis resolution.

title: Early versus delayed impella unloading during venoarterial ECMO for cardiogenic shock: a propensity-matched analysis.
authorString: Divya A, Dalal N.

journal.title: Journal of artificial organs : the official journal of the Japanese Society for Artificial Organs

abstractText: Venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) restores perfusion in cardiogenic shock but increases left-ventricular afterload. Impella unloading (ECPELLA) is increasingly used, but optimal timing remains uncertain. We retrospectively analyzed adults with cardiogenic shock treated with VA-ECMO and Impella from 2016 to 2025. Early ECPELLA was Impella placement from the calendar day before through the day after VA-ECMO initiation; delayed ECPELLA was placement 2-7 days after VA-ECMO initiation. One-to-one propensity-score matching balanced 35 covariates. The primary outcome was 30-day all-cause mortality. Sensitivity analyses included acute kidney injury (AKI) restriction, VA-ECMO-indexed follow-up, and a 7-day landmark analysis. Matching yielded 282 per group. Mortality was similar at 30 days (48.9% vs. 49.6%; risk ratio [RR] 0.99, 95% CI 0.83-1.17), 90 days (RR 1.01, 95% CI 0.87-1.17), and 1 year (RR 1.03, 95% CI 0.89-1.18). Early ECPELLA was associated with more renal-replacement therapy (RRT) at 30 days (37.4% vs. 21.7%; RR 1.73, 95% CI 1.29-2.31), but not when follow-up began at VA-ECMO initiation in AKI-restricted cohorts (RR 1.00, 95% CI 0.81-1.22; adjusted hazard ratio 1.02, 95% CI 0.82-1.26). Major bleeding, sepsis, and limb ischemia were similar. Durable LVAD implantation was less frequent with early ECPELLA at 1 year (RR 0.57, 95% CI 0.34-0.95), but not in sensitivity analyses. Early ECPELLA was not associated with improved survival compared with delayed ECPELLA. The RRT association was not reproduced with aligned follow-up. Residual confounding and immortal-time bias limit causal inference and warrant randomized trials.

title: Knowledge Mapping and Research Hotspots of Comorbidities in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: A Bibliometric Analysis of the Past 20 Years.
authorString: Liu W, Zhong J, Liu L, Lin C.
abstractText: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a complex autoimmune disease, whose health impact extends beyond itself and its treatment, and is also associated with various comorbidities. Early identification of comorbidities and development of personalized treatment plans are associated with improved clinical outcomes. This study aims to summarize the knowledge structure in the field of SLE comorbidities and further explore its research hotspots and trends through bibliometrics. A search was conducted in the Web of Science Core Collection and PubMed for literature on comorbidities of SLE from 2005 to 2025. VOSviewer and CiteSpace were used for collaborative network analysis, co-citation analysis of references, and keyword co-occurrence analysis on these publications. The analysis included 2140 records, with the United States leading in publication volume. Major contributing institutions included Harvard University, Harvard University Medical Affiliates, and the University of London, and the most productive authors were Chiara Tani and Eloisa Bonfa. The most cited reference was Anders HJ (2020) with 724 citations. Key themes identified by keyword co-occurrence analysis included autoimmune comorbidities, cardiovascular risk, clinical management, patient-reported outcomes, and methodological innovations. Co-citation analysis suggested a shift from an earlier focus on classical comorbidities to reproductive health and COVID-19, and a more recent shift to global epidemiology, updated treatment guidelines, and cardiovascular risk management. This bibliometric analysis provides a comprehensive overview of research on SLE comorbidities over the past 20 years, highlighting the growth trend, collaborative mechanisms, research priorities, and progress in clinical trials in this field, while emphasizing emerging hot topics such as autoimmune diseases and atherosclerosis. These findings reflect patterns and thematic concerns of research activity rather than direct measures of research quality or clinical importance. Future research may benefit from increased international collaboration and further exploration of emerging comorbidities.

title: Identifying Pediatric and Developmental Screening Targets With Biologically Informed Molecular Representations.
authorString: Acitores Cortina JM, Schut MC, Tatonetti NP.
abstractText: More than 75% of Food and Drug Administration approved drugs lack pediatric dosing, efficacy, or safety data, and roughly 40% of medications prescribed to children are used off-label. For most therapies children receive, dose, formulation, or indication has never been formally evaluated in anyone under 18. In this work, we build on our previous model, BioMADE, to identify toxicity screening targets whose relevance is specific to defined developmental stages. We analyzed 3.8 million drug-condition records from KidSIDES across 7 developmental stages and 6 system organ classes. Univariate analysis identified biologically coherent genes associated with pediatric conditions, including known genes like GABRB1 (pathogenic variants cause developmental and epileptic encephalopathy), SLC6A1 (associated with developmental encephalopathies), and GRIN2A (defining gene of epilepsy-aphasia spectrum). Signals were the strongest in early life, spanning multiple organ systems. The highest univariate model was gene CTSS, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.776; 95% confidence interval 0.62-0.90. Multivariate models surpassed 0.8 area under receiving operator curve in 13 datasets (0.81-0.91), indicating that multi-gene drug interaction profiles carry predictive signal beyond single-target associations. We further identify secondary targets that may influence pediatric development and contribute to pediatric-specific adverse drug events, many of which are not included in current safety screening panels. Our findings support the development of novel pediatric-specific safety screening panels, with a particular emphasis on respiratory and congenital disorders in early life. Prioritizing relevant drug targets for pediatric screening can potentially reduce the challenges of pediatric clinical trials and advance safer, more precise pediatric drug therapies.

title: MicroRNAs in Intracranial Aneurysm: From Vascular Cell Dysfunction to Candidate Non-Invasive Biomarkers of Formation and Rupture.
authorString: Czech A, Samsel K, Koper-Lenkiewicz OM, Lenda B, Balcerczak E, Matowicka-Karna J, Kamińska J.
abstractText: Intracranial aneurysms (IAs) are pathological dilatations of the cerebral arterial wall that affect 2-5% of the population and may rupture, causing subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) with a mortality rate approaching 40%. Despite advances in neuroimaging, a reliable circulating biomarker capable of detecting IAs or accurately predicting rupture risk remains lacking. MicroRNAs (miRNAs), small non-coding RNAs regulating gene expression at the post-transcriptional level, have emerged as promising, minimally invasive biomarkers due to their stability in body fluids, and involvement in pathways fundamental to vascular homeostasis. This review evaluates current evidence on circulating and tissue-derived miRNAs implicated in IA formation and rupture. Numerous studies demonstrate differential expression of specific miRNAs in patients with unruptured (UIA) and ruptured aneurysms (RIA), as well as in relation to aneurysm morphology, multiplicity, and individual vascular risk factors. Low miR-21 expression appears to promote vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) apoptosis and weaken arterial wall integrity, suggesting a potential role in rupture susceptibility, although the reported direction of change is not consistent across studies. Conversely, miR-29a contributes to extracellular matrix remodeling and VSMC apoptosis, with elevated circulating levels correlating with IA presence and, in some studies, rupture. Several miRNAs, including miR-143, miR-200a-3p, miR-16, miR-26a, miR-448-3p, and miR-1246, exhibit expression patterns associated with aneurysm progression, inflammation, and vascular remodeling. Exosomal miR-152-3p and circulating miR-126 demonstrate particularly strong diagnostic potential, independently predicting rupture risk or postoperative complications. Collectively, the available evidence supports the biological plausibility of miRNAs as candidate biomarkers of IA detection and rupture risk. Their translation is, however, constrained by pronounced inter-study heterogeneity in biological compartment, normalization strategy and preanalytical handling, by the scarcity of independent replication, and by the fact that none of these molecules is specific to intracranial aneurysm, being equally dysregulated in aortic aneurysm or atherosclerosis. On present evidence, miRNAs in IA are best regarded as etiopathogenetically informative rather than as validated diagnostic tests, and large-scale, multi-centre studies with standardized methodology and prospective validation remain necessary.

title: Physician-Pharmacist PBPM for Intensive Lipid Management After Acute Myocardial Infarction.
authorString: Aso H, Arai R, Iwabuchi S, Imai T, Hotsubo Y, Nagao T, Sumida R, Tanaka Y, Hori K, Fukumoto K, Ebuchi Y, Migita S, Kojima K, Sudo M, Okumura Y.
abstractText:
Aim

A physician-led lipid-lowering protocol increased early proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 inhibitor use after acute myocardial infarction (AMI), but workflow barriers remained. We evaluated a physician-pharmacist protocol-based pharmacotherapy management (PBPM) program designed to address these limitations.

Methods

This single-center observational study included 438 patients with AMI who underwent percutaneous coronary intervention and survived to discharge across PBPM (n = 162), physician-led (n = 160), and pre-protocol (n = 116) eras. The prespecified primary comparison was PBPM versus physician-led care. The primary and key secondary outcomes were evolocumab initiation and chronic-phase low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), respectively. Exploratory analyses examined outcomes across day-2 LDL-C treatment flows. Protocol adherence and reasons for non-initiation were also assessed.

Results

Evolocumab initiation increased across the pre-protocol, physician-led, and PBPM eras (2.6%, 13.1%, and 24.7%; overall P＜0.001) and was more frequent with PBPM than physician-led care (24.7% vs. 13.1%, P = 0.008), although the adjusted association was nonsignificant (odds ratio 2.01, 95% confidence interval 0.94-4.29; P = 0.071). Chronic-phase LDL-C was 49.0 versus 51.5 mg/dL (P = 0.074), whereas exploratory achievement of the contemporary LDL-C ＜55 mg/dL target was more frequent with PBPM (67.6% vs. 54.0%, P = 0.034). Among eligible patients, evolocumab initiation increased from 40.0% to 61.0% (P = 0.047), while system-related non-initiation decreased from 44.4% to 4.3%. Exploratorily, chronic-phase LDL-C was lower with PBPM among patients with day-2 LDL-C ≥ 90 mg/dL (24 vs. 47 mg/dL; P = 0.011; interaction P = 0.010).

Conclusions

PBPM was associated with greater adherence to the existing lipid-lowering protocol, more frequent evolocumab initiation at discharge, and fewer system-related reasons for non-initiation compared with physician-led care after AMI.

title: White Matter Hyperintensities Modify CYP2C19 Effect on Stroke Progression in Small Vessel Occlusion.
authorString: Sun X, Liu X, Wang L, Zhu R, Wang M, Zhang Z.

journal.title: Annals of clinical and translational neurology

abstractText:
Background

The association between CYP2C19 loss-of-function (LOF) alleles and early neurological deterioration (END) in acute small vessel occlusion (SVO) patients receiving dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) remains inconsistent. We hypothesized that white matter hyperintensities (WMH) burden act as a key moderator and investigated whether this modulates the association between CYP2C19 LOF and END.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective study of SVO patients receiving DAPT. CYP2C19 genotypes were classified as LOF carriers or non-carriers. The primary endpoint was END; secondary and safety endpoints included severe END, 90-day mRS 0-2, symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH), bleeding, and mortality. Multivariable regression and interaction analyzes assessed associations between CYP2C19, WMH, and clinical outcomes.

Results

A total of 247 patients (median age 67.0 years; 28.7% female; 60.7% CYP2C19 LOF carriers), 54 (21.9%) experienced END. Multivariable analysis identified infarct diameter (aOR 1.26, 95% CI 1.13-1.39, p < 0.001) and total cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) burden (aOR 2.02, 95% CI 1.37-2.98, p < 0.001) as independent predictors. A significant multiplicative interaction was observed between CYP2C19 LOF and severe WMH on END risk (aOR 9.34, 95% CI 2.06-48.10, p = 0.005). Stratified analysis showed CYP2C19 LOF significantly increased END risk specifically in patients with severe WMH (aOR 3.44, 95% CI 1.12-10.55, p = 0.030), but not mild WMH. Predicted probability curves suggested a Fazekas score threshold of approximately 2.70. Secondary and safety outcomes were infrequent.

Conclusions

CYP2C19 LOF alleles increase END risk in SVO patients specifically with severe WMH. These findings highlight the value of integrating genetic and neuroimaging markers for risk stratification and personalized antiplatelet therapy.

title: Successful percutaneous intervention for post-operative coronary artery stenosis in a child: a case report.
authorString: Gilchrist J, Morgan C, Salam A, Dedieu N, Smith EJ.
abstractText:
Background

Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for coronary artery stenosis in young children is rare, and evidence guiding management remains limited. Established indications for PCI in children include reversing or preventing ischaemia, as well as preventing sudden cardiac death. Guidance on optimal revascularization approaches and long-term outcomes remains underreported. We report successful PCI for significant post-operative right coronary artery (RCA) stenosis in a 7-year-old.

Case summary

The patient presented with acute onset cardiac failure aged 5 years. Echocardiography demonstrated aneurysmal aortic root dilatation with severe aortic regurgitation and left ventricular dysfunction. The aetiology was found to be infectious, and the patient underwent aortic root replacement. The postoperative course was complicated by myocardial ischaemia and right ventricular dysfunction, necessitating RCA re-implantation before discharge. At age 7, although asymptomatic, follow-up imaging demonstrated progressive proximal RCA stenosis. Stress cardiac magnetic resonance imaging revealed inducible perfusion defects, and exercise testing confirmed dynamic ECG changes consistent with ischaemia. Selective coronary angiography demonstrated critical proximal RCA stenosis. In collaboration with adult interventional cardiologists, PCI with coronary stent implantation was performed successfully, restoring coronary perfusion and improving functional capacity.

Discussion

This case highlights the feasibility of PCI with coronary stenting for complex post-operative coronary stenosis in paediatric patients. Input from adult interventional cardiologists allowed for technical challenges to be navigated and resulted in restoration of coronary perfusion with substantial improvements to patient quality of life.

title: Operating room extubation: experience from a public Brazilian pediatric cardiovascular center.
authorString: Vieira TC, Tinoco BC, Souza GEL, Vieira LC, Oliveira FX, Silva FAMD, Teixeira RDS.

journal.title: Revista paulista de pediatria : orgao oficial da Sociedade de Pediatria de Sao Paulo

abstractText:
Objective
