To investigate the incidence and success of intentional postoperative operating room extubation after elective congenital cardiac surgery at a Brazilian federal referral center and identify factors associated with non-extubation and extubation failure.

Methods

This historical cohort study was conducted in a pediatric and neonatal cardiac intensive care unit over five years. Patients aged 0-18 years with congenital heart disease who underwent elective corrective or palliative cardiac surgery without preoperative mechanical ventilation were included. The primary outcome was operating room extubation, and the secondary outcome was extubation success, defined as no reintubation within 48 postoperative hours. Multivariable Poisson regression with robust variance identified factors independently associated with nonextubation and extubation failure (p<0.05).

Results

Among 637 patients, 37% were extubated in the operating room, with a 98% success rate. They were older, had higher body weight, shorter noninvasive ventilation duration, shorter intensive care unit stays, and lower mortality. Increasing age reduced the risk of non-extubation. The need for noninvasive ventilation and longer intensive care unit stay were independently associated with non-extubation and extubation failure, although only four failures occurred.

Conclusions

Operating room extubation was feasible in a substantial proportion of pediatric patients and achieved a high success rate, supporting its safety in selected cases. Greater surgical complexity, need for noninvasive ventilation, and longer intensive care unit stay increased the risk of non-extubation, whereas increasing age reduced this risk.

title: Trends and causes of maternal mortality in Taiyuan, China, 2016-2024: A population-based observational study.
authorString: Wang F, Yang H.
abstractText:
Background

Although China has made major advances in maternal health, city-level epidemiological evidence on maternal mortality remains scarce. Using maternal surveillance data from Taiyuan (2016-2024), we assessed trends in the maternal mortality ratio (MMR), examined causes of death, and identified associated factors to inform region-specific strategies for reducing MMR.

Methods

We extracted and validated data on maternal deaths and live births from the Taiyuan Municipal Maternal and Child Health Annual Reports. MMR was calculated per 100,000 live births. Poisson regression was used to examine temporal trends, and chi-square or Fisher's exact tests were used for between-group comparisons. Analyses were stratified by geographic region, cause of death, and place of death; the study period was divided into three phases (2016-2018, 2019-2021, 2022-2024) for subgroup analysis.

Results

Between 2016 and 2024, Taiyuan recorded 424,392 live births and 33 maternal deaths, yielding an overall MMR of 7.76 per 100,000 live births (95% CI 5.35 to 10.92). Urban MMR declined significantly (P < 0.0001), whereas rural MMR showed no significant temporal change (P = 0.313) and remained higher than urban levels (9.57 vs 7.58 per 100,000). Indirect obstetric causes accounted for 66.7% of maternal deaths, compared with 33.3% for direct causes, with no significant temporal trends in either category. Women aged 30-39 years accounted for 63.6% of maternal deaths, and 83.9% of deaths occurred in tertiary hospitals.

Conclusion

Taiyuan has maintained a low MMR through sustained investment in maternal healthcare; however, substantial urban-rural disparities remain. Indirect obstetric causes predominated among maternal deaths, suggesting a transition in the spectrum of maternal causes of death. Continued efforts to strengthen rural maternal health services and promote equitable, life-course-oriented maternal care are essential to further reduce preventable maternal deaths.

title: Factors Associated with Unplanned 28-Day Index-Hospital Readmission After Open Heart Valve Surgery: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
authorString: Sittiwong G, Anpanya O, Silarat S, Banharak S.
abstractText:
Background

Unplanned readmission after cardiac surgery indicates the quality of discharge preparation and transitional care. Evidence after open heart valve surgery in Thailand is limited.

Objective

To determine the rate of, and factors associated with, unplanned index-hospital readmission within 28 days of discharge after open heart valve surgery.

Methods

This retrospective cohort study included adults who underwent open heart valve surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass at a tertiary cardiac referral center in northeastern Thailand from 2021 to 2025, with one operation per patient. Patients who died before discharge, were discharged against medical advice, or were transferred elsewhere were excluded. Readmissions were identified in the hospital information system of the study center; readmissions to other hospitals were not captured. Covariates were selected on clinical grounds, without reference to bivariable significance, and Firth penalized logistic regression was used.

Results

Of 1,543 operation records, 1,336 patients were analyzed. Unplanned readmission within 28 days occurred in 97 patients (7.26%; 95% confidence interval [CI], 5.93-8.79). Anticoagulation-related problems were the most frequent documented reason (24.7%), followed by heart failure (18.6%) and arrhythmia (13.4%). After adjustment, readmission was associated with a mechanical prosthesis compared with repair without a replacement prosthesis (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 3.98; 95% CI, 1.97-8.25), acute kidney injury defined by creatinine criteria (aOR, 2.00; 95% CI, 1.10-3.53), and longer cardiopulmonary bypass time (aOR per 30 minutes, 1.16; 95% CI, 1.03-1.29). Odds were also higher with a mechanical than with a bioprosthetic valve (aOR, 2.95; 95% CI, 1.65-5.32). Results were consistent in six sensitivity analyses.

Conclusion

About 1 in 14 patients had an unplanned index-hospital readmission within 28 days, a figure that may underestimate overall readmission. A mechanical prosthesis, acute kidney injury, and longer bypass time were associated with readmission. Targeted discharge preparation and anticoagulation follow-up for these patients are candidates for evaluation.

title: Positive Vitreous Pressure in Phacoemulsification Cataract Surgery: A Narrative Review of Pathophysiology, Risk Factors, Prevention, and Intraoperative Management.
authorString: Gong W, Krews JP, Bahr C, Peterson H, Dolinsky G, Mano F, Shelby CL, Coleman Iii W, LoBue SA.
abstractText:
Purpose

To review the pathophysiology, risk factors, prevention strategies, and intraoperative management of positive vitreous pressure (PVP) during modern phacoemulsification cataract surgery.

Methods

English-language literature up to July 2026 was identified through PubMed and Google Scholar searches using the terms "positive vitreous pressure", "positive posterior pressure", "fluid misdirection syndrome", "suprachoroidal hemorrhage", "phacoemulsification", "cataract surgery", "cataract extraction", and related terms. Additional relevant studies were identified through screening of reference lists.

Results

PVP is a clinical intraoperative phenomenon that may arise from three principal mechanisms: external compression on the globe, acute choroidal expansion (eg, choroidal congestion, effusion and hemorrhage), and acute increases in vitreous volume. Risk factors include obesity, short axial length, shallow anterior chamber, primary angle-closure disease, brunescent cataract, and pseudoexfoliative syndrome. Prevention strategies include risk identification and modification, preventing intraoperative hypotony and direct external scleral compression, optimization of conditions that impair venous return to the heart, appropriate ophthalmic viscoelastic device use and controlled fluidics, avoidance of large-incision surgery when possible, and prophylactic pars plana vitreous decompression in selected cases. When PVP is encountered intraoperatively, early recognition, wound closure and cause-specific management are essential, and surgical deferral may be necessary in some cases.

Conclusion

PVP remains a clinically significant challenge in modern cataract surgery. Systematic preoperative risk identification and prevention strategies may reduce the likelihood or severity of PVP-related complications, while timely recognition and appropriate management are essential when PVP occurs.

title: Salvage Heart Transplantation for Severe Biventricular Failure Associated with Systemic Sclerosis-Rheumatoid Arthritis Overlap Syndrome.
authorString: Hara A, Hashimoto T, Kodono Y, Mizokami K, Sakamoto T, Yoshida K, Matsushima S, Misumi K, Fujino T, Katsuki S, Matsuura H, Nishimura N, Iwasaki T, Ushijima T, Sonoda H, Shiose A, Abe K.
abstractText: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a multisystem autoimmune disease characterized by vasculopathy and fibrosis, and it often affects the heart, leading to ventricular dysfunction, conduction abnormalities, and arrhythmias. Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is also complicated by pericarditis, valvular heart diseases, and diastolic dysfunction. SSc-associated right ventricular (RV) dysfunction is a rare but life-threatening condition. Herein, we present a case of SSc/RA overlap syndrome associated with catastrophic biventricular failure mimicking arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy/arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (ACM/ARVC), requiring central extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO). Urgent heart transplantation (HTx) successfully saved the patient's life, and he experienced no rejection, allograft dysfunction, or relapse of SSc/RA post-transplant.

title: Let-7b-5p Attenuates Ox-LDL-Induced Endothelial Pyroptosis by Targeting HMGB1.
authorString: Zhong B, Zhang M, Wu Q, Wang X.
abstractText: Endothelial pyroptosis contributes to vascular inflammation during atherosclerotic progression. Oxidized low-density lipoprotein (ox-LDL) induces endothelial injury and inflammatory responses; however, the molecular mechanisms involved have not been fully characterized. This study examined the role of let-7b-5p and its target gene, high-mobility group box 1 (HMGB1), in ox-LDL-induced endothelial pyroptosis.Human aortic endothelial cells (HAECs) were exposed to ox-LDL to establish an in vitro model of endothelial pyroptosis. Let-7b-5p and HMGB1 expression were determined by quantitative real-time PCR and Western blotting. Lactate dehydrogenase release, interleukin-1β secretion, transmission electron microscopy, and pyroptosis-related protein expression were used to evaluate cellular injury and pyroptotic responses. The interaction between let-7b-5p and HMGB1 was verified using a dual-luciferase reporter assay. In addition, paired aortic intima and internal mammary artery intima specimens from 41 patients undergoing coronary artery bypass graft surgery were analyzed.Ox-LDL treatment reduced let-7b-5p expression and increased HMGB1 expression in HAECs. Let-7b-5p overexpression attenuated ox-LDL-induced LDH release, interleukin-1β secretion, and pyroptosis-associated protein expression. Luciferase assays confirmed HMGB1 as a direct target of let-7b-5p. Furthermore, HMGB1 overexpression partially abolished the protective effects of let-7b-5p. Consistent with the cellular findings, aortic intima specimens exhibited lower let-7b-5p expression and higher HMGB1 expression than paired internal mammary artery specimens.Let-7b-5p attenuates ox-LDL-induced endothelial pyroptosis through regulation of HMGB1. These findings support the involvement of the let-7b-5p/HMGB1 axis in endothelial inflammatory injury associated with atherosclerotic disease.

title: Describing the pre-moyamoya stage: Lesion distribution, disease progression, and the impact of RNF213.
authorString: Sasagasako T, Mineharu Y, Funaki T, Chihara H, Ganesh A, Okuchi S, Park S, Nakajima K, Okawa M, Kikuchi T, Fushimi Y, Arakawa Y.
abstractText:
Objective

Stenosis at the terminal portion of the internal carotid artery (ICA) is a characteristic feature of moyamoya disease (MMD). However, MMD may develop in patients with initially preserved terminal ICAs, and the lesion distribution and predictors of progression during the pre-moyamoya stage remain poorly defined.

Methods

We conducted a single-center retrospective longitudinal cohort study of consecutive patients with intracranial arterial stenosis (ICAS) in the anterior circulation to characterize the pre-moyamoya stage of MMD, including the distribution of initial lesions and predictors of progression. Clinical, angiographic, and genetic data were analyzed.

Results

Among 624 patients with ICAS, 458 were diagnosed with MMD at the last follow-up. Of these, 33 patients with bilaterally preserved terminal ICAs subsequently progressed to MMD over a median interval of 55.3 months (IQR, 12.5-97.3), representing 7.2% of all MMD cases. Among the 66 hemispheres in patients with MMD progression, M1 stenosis was the most common initial lesion (54.5%), followed by A1 (12.1%) and C2 stenosis (7.6%). RNF213 p.R4810K genotyping was performed in 304 patients, of whom 74.0% harbored the mutation. Multivariable Cox regression analysis showed that the RNF213 p.R4810K mutation (HR, 20.2; 95% CI, 2.63-155; P = 0.004) and younger age (HR per 1-year increase, 0.953; 95% CI, 0.931-0.975; P < 0.001) were independently associated with progression to MMD.

Conclusion

The pre-moyamoya stage is characterized by heterogeneous stenotic patterns, with M1 steno-occlusive lesions representing the most common initial manifestation. RNF213 p.R4810K genotyping may help identify patients at increased risk of progression to MMD.

title: Haemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis Presenting With a Renal Infarct of Unclear Aetiology and Persistent Fever: A Diagnostic Dilemma.
authorString: Barud Y.
abstractText: Haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) is a rare and potentially fatal hyperinflammatory syndrome characterised by excessive immune activation and progressive multisystem dysfunction. Diagnosis in adults can be challenging due to overlap with infection and malignancy. This case is based on a gentleman in his mid-30s who presented with acute right-sided flank pain and a right renal infarction. From the second day of admission, he developed persistent pyrexia despite antipyretic therapy and broad-spectrum antibiotics. Over the following two weeks, he developed anaemia, thrombocytopenia, marked hyperferritinaemia, and hypertriglyceridaemia. An H-score of 220 supported the diagnosis of HLH, and his case met 5/8 of the HLH-2004 criteria. Thrombophilia, antiphospholipid, and vasculitis testing were negative; haematology considered the infarct likely arterial, although no cause was identified. A blood culture grew gram-positive cocci in clusters; repeat cultures following readmission were negative after treatment was commenced. Bone marrow examination showed no malignancy or convincing haemophagocytosis. Following multidisciplinary review, treatment with intravenous methylprednisolone and anakinra was associated with clinical and biochemical improvement. This case highlights the need to consider HLH in patients with persistent fever, falling blood counts, and markedly elevated ferritin despite treatment for an alternative acute diagnosis.

title: Transcatheter edge-to-edge repair for dynamic severe atrial functional mitral regurgitation identified during handgrip exercise echocardiography: a case report.
authorString: Zhang W, Xie P, Cai X, Liao X, Zhuang X.
abstractText:
Background

Atrial functional mitral regurgitation (AFMR) is a dynamic disease, and dynamic severe AFMR is associated with poor prognosis.

Case summary

We present a 77-year-old man with recurrent chest tightness and palpitations over the past 9 years. Handgrip exercise echocardiography demonstrated dynamic severe AFMR, with features of atriogenic leaflet tethering and an eccentric regurgitant jet. Then the patient underwent transcatheter edge-to-edge mitral valve repair (TEER). Post-procedure, the patient's symptoms improved, and a reduction in left atrial size was observed.

Discussion

This case provides preliminary evidence supporting the potential application of TEER in the treatment of dynamic severe AFMR and offers a possible direction for AFMR management.

title: Health behaviors as a pathway between early life adversity and cardiometabolic risk for previously institutionalized youth.
authorString: Donzella B, Aran Ö, Tsakonas NC, Knutson A, Evanoff NG, Linden MA, Kelly AS, Dengel DR, Gunnar MR, Reid BM.
abstractText: Early life adversity including caregiving stress and neglect has been linked to elevated cardiometabolic risk. Children adopted from institutional care represent a well-characterized model of this exposure limited to the first few years of life, with elevated cardiometabolic risk documented as early as adolescence, even in the absence of overweight or obesity. The present study examines whether health behaviors such as diet, sleep quality measured as daytime drowsiness, and physical activity serve as pathways through which early life adversity shapes cardiometabolic risk during adolescence. Ninety-five previously institutionalized youth (MeanAdoptionAge = 16.2, SD = 12 months, 63% female) and 95 birth-reared youth (MeanAge = 15.8, SD = 2.4 years, 52% female) reported on diet, daytime drowsiness, and physical activity. Two years later, they visited the lab for cardiometabolic health assessment via SphygmoCor, Dual X-ray absorptiometry scan, and blood draws. Cardiometabolic risk was indexed by insulin resistance, cholesterol, arterial stiffness (aortic augmentation index and pulse wave velocity), and android fat percentage. Eating an inflammatory diet and greater drowsiness, but not physical activity, emerged as significant indirect pathways linking early adversity and cardiometabolic risk. Specifically, previously institutionalized youth ate more inflammatory diets and were drowsier during the day than birth-reared youth, which in turn, was associated with higher cardiometabolic risk. These findings raise questions about the mechanisms linking early life adversity to later eating and sleep behaviors and suggest that these behaviors may be modifiable targets for reducing cardiometabolic risk in adolescents with histories of early adversity.

title: Positive fluid balance and the incidence of acute kidney injury in the postoperative period of cardiac surgery.
authorString: Prado BS, Moitinho MS, Santos ES, Pinto TDS, Santos ML, Fonseca CDD.
abstractText:
Objective

To elucidate the relationship between postoperative fluid balance and acute kidney injury in patients who had undergone cardiac surgery.

Methods

This integrative review followed the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. The searches were conducted in the PubMed, Scopus, Cochrane Library, SciELO, MEDLINE, and LILACS databases. The research question was defined using Population, Exposure, Comparison, Outcome framework. The inclusion criteria were adult patients undergoing cardiac surgery between 2015 and 2024.

Results

Of the 226 articles identified, eight studies met the inclusion criteria, and all of the studies had an observational design. Seven studies reported that a positive postoperative fluid balance was associated with a higher risk of acute kidney injury. A fluid balance of >30 mL/kg within 48 h or ≥5% within 24 h was associated with an increased incidence of acute kidney injury.

Conclusion

Postoperative positive fluid balance is an important contributor to development of acute kidney injury following cardiac surgery.

title: Primary Angiosarcoma of the Urinary Bladder Without Prior Radiation Exposure: A Case Report.
authorString: Nonoyama S, Koike K, Sekine K, Katsuoka Y, Hashimoto R, Kobayashi H, Hattori T.
abstractText:
Introduction

Primary angiosarcoma of the urinary bladder is an exceptionally rare and aggressive endothelial malignancy, with fewer than 40 cases reported in the English-language literature, making diagnosis challenging.

Case presentation

A 76-year-old woman presented with a 1-week history of gross hematuria and severe anemia. Computed tomography demonstrated intravesical lesions without another bleeding source. Transurethral electrocoagulation and resection were performed despite poor visualization due to hematuria and blood clots. Histopathological examination showed a highly cellular neoplasm with predominantly epithelioid morphology, arranged in sheets and irregular vascular channel-like structures. Immunohistochemistry revealed CD31 positivity and negativity for D2-40, CD34, AE1/AE3, p63, and GATA3, supporting a diagnosis of angiosarcoma. Hematuria recurred postoperatively, and the patient declined further treatment because of her religious beliefs.

Conclusion

Primary bladder angiosarcoma should be considered as a rare differential diagnosis in patients presenting with severe hematuria, particularly when hemostasis is difficult to achieve because of the tumor's highly vascular nature.

title: Common meat inspection findings in sheep in Finland.
authorString: Stenius J, Keski-Saari R, Nihtilä N, Nordgren H, Mustonen E, Lindeberg H, Rautiainen J, Fredriksson-Ahomaa M, Laukkanen-Ninios R.
abstractText:
Background

Sheep meat is produced on a small scale in Finland, with ca. 50,000 animals slaughtered annually. In 2024, over 20% of sheep meat produced in Finland was organic. Legislative requirements differ between organic and conventional production, which may be reflected in differences in animal health and welfare between the two production systems. Meat inspection data can be used to assess the health and welfare of production animals. However, studies on meat inspection findings in sheep and comparative research on lesion and condemnation prevalences between the two production systems are scarce. In this study, data were collected from a slaughterhouse that received over 20% (n = 11,355) of all sheep slaughtered in Finland in the year 2024. Lambs (sheep under one year of age) constituted 79% of the slaughtered animals, with 37% of all animals being organically reared.

Results

No lesions or condemnations were recorded in 96% of all carcasses originating from 132/228 (58%) farms. Whole- and partial-carcass condemnations were more frequent in adult sheep than in lambs in both organic and conventional production, but no significant difference was observed between the production systems. The lesions with the highest animal and farm prevalences, respectively, were dicrocoeliasis caused by the lancet liver fluke Dicrocoelium dendriticum (2.5% and 3.5%), pleuritis (0.8% and 22.4%), bone fracture (0.4% and 9.7%), acute bruise (0.3% and 6.6%), pneumonia (0.2% and 7.0%), and liver abscesses (0.1% and 3.9%). The prevalence of D. dendriticum was significantly higher in organic production (p < 0.001) and in adults (p < 0.001) than lambs. Additionally, dicrocoeliasis was a farm-specific problem, with only eight positive farms (3.5%). In addition to dicrocoeliasis, pleuritis was also age-related, with a significantly higher prevalence in adults than in lambs in both production systems.

Conclusions

The results indicate a good health status of sheep in Finland. Differences between animal age groups seem to be greater than those between production systems. Meat inspection results can help identify underlying health and welfare issues on the farm. However, since the results may be affected by such factors as animal nutrition, more research on lesion etiology in Finland is required.

title: Piezo1 in acute and critical illnesses: From mechanosensing to organ dysfunction (Review).
authorString: Zhang L, Gu H, Zhu Y, Tang L, An J, Zhu J, Jin H, Tuo B.
abstractText: Acute and critical illnesses are typically accompanied by hemodynamic instability, tissue edema, mechanical ventilation and extracellular matrix remodeling. Abnormal shear stress, mechanical stretch, pressure loading and tissue deformation continuously reshape the local mechanical microenvironment. Piezo1 is a mechanosensitive cation channel that converts mechanical stimuli into intracellular signals dominated by Ca²<sup>+</sup> influx and contributes to vascular homeostasis, immune regulation and tissue repair. In sepsis‑associated intestinal epithelial injury, pulmonary endothelial mechanical loading and infection‑related immune responses, Piezo1‑associated Ca²<sup>+</sup> signaling has been implicated in intestinal barrier injury, mitochondrial stress and apoptosis, endothelial barrier disruption or protection, and enhanced host defense. The direction of its effects depends on the cell and experimental context and cannot be determined solely by the intensity or duration of activation. The present review summarizes the fundamental mechanisms of Piezo1‑mediated mechanosensing and mechanotransduction in sepsis, acute respiratory distress syndrome, acute kidney injury and trauma/hemorrhagic shock. It also discusses the therapeutic potential and translational challenges of targeting Piezo1. Mechanical alterations in acute and critical illnesses may influence cellular processes, including inflammatory regulation, endothelial barrier function, mitochondrial stress and cell injury, through Piezo1‑associated signaling. However, direct evidence and the direction of effects vary between diseases, and shared mechanisms across organs remain to be validated. Defining the cell‑specific and stimulus‑ and disease stage‑dependent effects of Piezo1 may deepen understanding of organ dysfunction in acute and critical illness and provide a basis for research into interventions targeting mechanical signaling.

title: Gross motor development of infants with Down syndrome in the first year: Longitudinal comparison with reference curves.
authorString: Soares GCC, Camargos MJ, de Souza J, Castro ALO, Gonçalves RV.
abstractText:
Objective

To describe gross motor development during the first year of life in infants with Down syndrome (DS), compare it with published reference data, and examine its associations with maternal age, congenital heart disease, and home affordances.

Methods

In this longitudinal observational study, 25 infants with DS, all receiving weekly physical therapy at an early intervention center since early infancy, were assessed at 6, 9, and 12 months (corrected age) with the Gross Motor Function Measure (GMFM-88). The age of attainment of six World Health Organization motor milestones was recorded prospectively. Home affordances were assessed with the Affordances in the Home Environment for Motor Development-Infant Scale. A pre-specified linear mixed model examined associated factors.

Results

By 12 months, 92% of infants sat without support, 52% stood with assistance, and 36% crawled; none stood or walked independently. Crawling was more frequent and standing alone less frequent than reference probabilities. Mean GMFM-88 scores rose from 17.3% to 48.5%, exceeding reference curves at 12 months. Older maternal age was associated with lower scores across assessments (β = -0.75 per year, p = 0.028), but not with the rate of gain. Infants with congenital heart disease (32%) scored lower at 12 months, although not significantly (adjusted difference - 6.7 points, p = 0.116). Home affordances were not associated with motor trajectories.

Conclusions

Early horizontal milestones were within or above reference expectations, whereas upright skills lagged behind. These longitudinal first-year data support monitoring against DS-specific references to identify infants at risk of delayed upright skills.

title: Post remote ischaemic conditioning and early pre remote ischaemic conditioning reduces the extent and severity of bowel injury in an animal model of necrotising enterocolitis.
authorString: Jones IH, Tao D, Vagdama B, Lau L, Collins J, Hall NJ.
abstractText:
Purpose

Remote ischaemic conditioning (RIC) has a protective effect in an experimental model of severe necrotising enterocolitis. We investigated the impact of delivering RIC at different time-points.

Methods

We used an established intestinal ischaemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) model in rat pups. RIC was delivered by means of a lower limb ligature. Animals were randomly allocated to intestinal IRI only, RIC before IRI (preRIC), RIC after IRI (postRIC), RIC 48 h before IRI (earlyRIC), RIC 48 h and immediately before IRI (early + preRIC), or control. Macroscopic and microscopic intestinal injury are reported. Serum cytokine levels were assayed. Data are median (inter-quartile range).

Results

Animals receiving RIC had reduced severe macroscopic intestinal injury: pre-RIC 4% (0-21%, p = 0.0019), postRIC 4% (0-44%, p = 0.0021), earlyRIC 3% (0-42%, p = 0.0054) and early+preRIC 0% (0-39%, p = 0.0018) vs. IRI 78% (30-90). The preRIC and postRIC groups compared had reduced injury scores compared to IRI alone: 3.5 (1.25-5, p = 0.002) and 4.25 (4-5, p = 0.031) vs. 5.5 (4-6). RIC 48 h prior to IRI did not reduce injury but injury was lowest in early+preRIC group [2.375 (1.625-3) 0.4375, p = 0.0001]. IFN-γ, IL-4 and IL-5 were increased following RIC.

Conclusion

RIC reduces the extent and severity of intestinal injury. Two doses of RIC delivered 48 h apart has the greatest effect. Cytokines IFN-γ, IL-4 and IL-5 may be important in the transmission of RIC.

title: Beyond Seizure Control: Building the Infrastructure for Disease-Modifying Therapies in Epilepsy.
authorString: Ziobro JM, Axeen E, Demarest S, Gupta K, Hixson J, Joshi S, Patel AD, Robbins-Hood V, Smith L, Sullivan J, Parent J.
abstractText: Rapid advances in disease-modifying therapies (DMTs) for epilepsy, including gene-based therapies, antisense oligonucleotides, and stem cell-derived approaches, are reshaping the treatment landscape. As these therapies move through clinical trials and toward regulatory review, they introduce complex clinical, operational, ethical, and equity considerations that extend well beyond traditional antiseizure medication management. Successful integration will require careful attention to patient selection, genetic and biomarker testing, multidisciplinary care models, infrastructure readiness, referral pathways, long-term safety monitoring, informed consent for novel and potentially irreversible interventions, access to clinical trials, and cost and reimbursement challenges. Significant investments in personnel, systems, and facilities may be necessary, raising important questions about implementation across diverse practice settings and the risk of widening disparities in care. Here, we review the evolving therapeutic pipeline and outline key considerations for safe, ethical, and equitable implementation.

title: Best Evidence Summary of Phase II Exercise-Based Cardiac Rehabilitation for Patients with Dilated Cardiomyopathy After Cardiac Resynchronization Therapy.
authorString: Wang X, Liu Y, Han L, Wang H, Zhang M, Xi Y, Xiong J, Dou X.
abstractText:
Background

This study aimed to systematically summarize the available evidence on Phase II exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation (CR) for patients with dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) after cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT), so as to provide an evidence-based framework for clinical nursing practice.

Methods

A comprehensive computerized search was conducted in PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, CINAHL, Web of Science, CNKI, WanFang, VIP, and SinoMed, as well as guideline repositories, evidence-based databases, and professional association websites. The included document types were clinical decisions, guidelines, expert consensus or consensus documents, evidence summaries and systematic reviews.

Results

Twenty-eight publications were included: 2 clinical decisions, 10 guidelines, 1 systematic review, 11 expert consensus or consensus documents and 4 evidence summaries. A total of 42 pieces of evidence items were summarized across 12 themes: multidisciplinary collaboration, indications and contraindications for exercise rehabilitation, pre-exercise assessment, pre-exercise preparation, exercise prescription, aerobic exercise, resistance training; pulmonary rehabilitation training, flexibility training, personalized adjustment, remote supervision and support, and emergency management.

Conclusion

This study synthesized available evidence on Phase II exercise-based CR for patients with DCM after CRT. Most included evidence was derived from broader heart failure or cardiac rehabilitation populations; direct evidence specific to DCM after CRT remains limited. These findings may inform the development of individualized rehabilitation protocols, but recommendations should be applied with caution.

Registration

This evidence summary was registered with the Fudan University Center for Evidence-Based Nursing (Registration No. ES202610091).

title: Unlocking the Ability of Generative Artificial Intelligence to Improve Health Communication and Health Education.
authorString: Amin KS, Skaggs DL, Doshi RH, Khosla P, Amin S, Mayes L.
abstractText:
Introduction

While large language models (LLMs) can simplify information for patients, they are often ineffective at reaching specific reading levels. Here, we demonstrate a novel approach that may help improve readability and aid in the dissemination of health information to children and adolescents.

Methods

We selected for analysis 200 common and diverse pediatric conditions and symptoms. We used ChatGPT to generate 36 explanations for each condition and symptom. For each explanation, we calculated reading grade levels (RGLs) and word counts. From the 36 outputs, we then selected single outputs for 5th-6th grade (level 1), 7th-8th grade (level 2), 9th-10th grade (level 3), and 11th-12th grade (level 4) by selecting outputs within 0.25 RGLs of the median of the grade range (ie, 5.25-5.75 for level 1). Three full professors then reviewed outputs related to their pediatric specialties for accuracy and completeness; they modified all incorrect information and added relevant missing information. We then tabulated RGLs, word counts, and the number of modifications for the edited outputs.

Results

Prompt architectures varied in how well they initially resulted in a desired RGL, and few prompts resulted in requested RGLs at baseline. After output selection and accuracy edits, median RGLs were 5.8 (5.4-6.4) for level 1, 7.5 (7.4-7.7) for level 2, 9.5 (9.4-9.7) for level 3, and 11.5 (11.3-11.7) for level 4. Accuracy edits were minimal, with 93.5%, 95.5%, 95.5%, and 95.0% of outputs requiring no word additions or deletions for levels 1 through 4, respectively.

Conclusion

Our approach offers health care providers a way to generate health information at a chosen reading grade level throughout the care continuum.

title: Placental transcriptomes differ in human pregnancies complicated by severe fetal left heart obstruction.
authorString: Leon RL, Lu H, Ossa Galvis MM, Mir IN, Xiong B, Wang T, Udayakumar D.
abstractText: The etiology of severe left-sided obstructive lesions (LSOL) of the heart, a common form of congenital heart disease (CHD), often remains unknown even after comprehensive genetic testing. Preclinical models implicate placental perturbations in abnormal cardiogenesis; however, little is known about connections between human placenta and fetal cardiac diseases. We profiled term placentas from severe LSOL pregnancies (n = 20) with and without placental pathologies and healthy controls (n = 10) to test whether severe fetal LSOL is associated with distinct transcriptomic and cellular states. Bulk RNA-sequencing of archival formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissues identified 1,030 differentially expressed protein-coding genes (580 [up], 450 [down]). Upregulated programs involved heart-valve development, endothelial signaling, and extracellular-matrix processes; while endocrine, trophoblast and gamma-aminobutyric acid signaling processes were downregulated. Severe LSOL pregnancies with histologically normal placentas showed enrichment of lymphatic-vascular development and cyclic-nucleotide signaling. Digital deconvolution analysis inferred reduced trophoblast fractions with reciprocal increase in endothelial and immune cell types. These findings support a unique placental gene expression in abnormal cardiac development, even in the absence of overt placental histopathology. These RNA expression signatures may serve as candidate biomarkers and lay the groundwork for mechanistic studies of the heart-placenta axis and future risk stratification in pregnancies with fetuses diagnosed with severe LSOL.

title: Respiratory viral detection and severity risk factors in hospitalized children with community-acquired pneumonia following relaxation of COVID-19 non-pharmaceutical interventions: a 20-month retrospective cohort in Guilin, China.
authorString: Wang X, Bu J, Wan Q, Yin Z, Zhang X, Gu Y.
abstractText:
Background

After the withdrawal of COVID-19 non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs) in China, we characterized the demographic, clinical and virological features of virus-positive community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) in children younger than 5 years during the post-NPI period.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective study using electronic medical records from a tertiary hospital in Guilin, China. We enrolled 1,255 children hospitalized with CAP between December 2022 and July 2024. All participants were tested for five respiratory viruses: respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), parainfluenza virus (PIV), adenovirus (ADV), influenza-A (Flu-A) and influenza-B (Flu-B).

Results

Of 1,255 hospitalized CAP cases, 681 (54%) were virus-positive, including 112 (16% of virus-positive cases) who met severe CAP (SCAP) criteria. RSV showed the highest detection rate (23%, 292/1,255), followed by PIV, ADV, Flu-A and Flu-B; detection patterns differed significantly across age groups. Bacterial co-detection was common among virus-positive cases. Multivariable analysis identified bacterial co-detection (OR 1.90, 95% CI [1.12-3.23]), wheeze (OR 1.59, 95% CI [1.02-2.49]), and chronic comorbidities (OR 2.44, 95% CI [1.5 7-3.78]) as independent risk factors for severe disease, whereas rhinorrhoea was associated with reduced severity (OR 0.43, 95% CI [0.27-0.66]).

Conclusion

Among virus-positive cases, RSV was the most frequently detected virus in children younger than 5 years hospitalized with CAP during the post-NPI period in Guilin, China. Early identification of independent risk factors for SCAP may help clinicians's recognition high-risk children promptly.

title: First-Attempt Video Laryngoscopic Intubation in an Adult With Down Syndrome and Severe Tracheal Compression From a Giant Retrosternal Goiter.
authorString: Naco M, Bulku E, Domi R, Llukacaj A, Kurushi E, Mana F, Memelli M, Dhima A, Lilaj K, Naco E, Cani A, Eljezi V.
abstractText: Giant retrosternal goiters can cause severe tracheal compression and pose substantial challenges for airway management and surgical resection. These challenges may be further increased in adults with Down syndrome (DS), in whom craniofacial abnormalities, macroglossia, obesity, limited neck mobility, and potential cervical spine abnormalities may contribute to difficult airway management. We report the perioperative management of a 29-year-old woman with DS and a giant multinodular retrosternal goiter causing marked rightward tracheal deviation and critical tracheal narrowing to approximately 7 mm, requiring combined cervical resection and median sternotomy. Preoperative assessment identified multiple predictors of difficult mask ventilation and tracheal intubation, while severe intellectual disability made awake airway management impractical. A multidisciplinary airway and surgical strategy were therefore developed, incorporating optimized positioning and preoxygenation, video laryngoscopy as the planned primary intubation technique, flexible bronchoscopy for confirmation and rescue, and predefined escalation to surgical airway and extracorporeal support if conventional airway management failed. Following controlled intravenous induction, tracheal intubation was achieved on the first attempt with a 6.0-mm endotracheal tube without hypoxemia or hemodynamic instability. Total thyroidectomy and median sternotomy were completed uneventfully. After an adequate cuff-leak test and confirmation of full neuromuscular recovery, the patient was extubated in the operating room and received postoperative bilevel positive airway pressure and overnight intensive care monitoring. No respiratory or other major postoperative complications occurred, and she was discharged home on postoperative day 5. This case illustrates the individualized integration of established difficult-airway principles when DS coexists with severe mechanical tracheal compression from a giant retrosternal goiter. Successful management depended not on a single airway technique, but on careful preoperative anatomical and functional assessment, selection of a feasible primary approach, optimized oxygenation, and an immediately executable multidisciplinary rescue pathway.

title: Compromised Endothelial Regeneration as a Potential Contributor to Long-Term Cardiovascular Complications in Childhood Cancer Survivors.
authorString: Markandran K, Ng TJ, Tan E, Clemente CKM, Wang RMQ, Lim YP, Attal K, Clemente KNM, S H, Foo SYR, Chen CK.
abstractText: Anthracyclines are central to childhood cancer therapy but predispose patients to cardiovascular toxicity and long-term cardiovascular risk. Endothelial injury and impaired repair contribute to this, yet paediatric data remain limited. This study longitudinally assessed endothelial injury and repair by quantifying circulating endothelial cells (CECs) and endothelial progenitor cells (EPCs). In a single-centre prospective cohort, children (<18 years) with leukaemia (n = 35) or lymphoma (n = 13) were studied at four timepoints: pre-treatment (Pre), ~1 month post-treatment (End), 3 months (3M), and 1 year (1Y). Blood mononuclear cells were analysed by flow cytometry to quantify CECs and EPCs, and EPC fate by p16 (senescence) and Annexin V (apoptosis). Cardiac biomarkers and left ventricular function were assessed. Longitudinal trends of CEC and EPC counts were similar between leukaemia and lymphoma participants. CECs were highest at pre-treatment and declined significantly thereafter, though they remained marginally elevated during remission compared with healthy controls, indicating endothelial damage had largely subsided following treatment. EPCs were highest at pre-treatment and decreased below healthy controls during remission, suggesting impaired baseline endothelial maintenance and repair. While EPC fate did not alter significantly from healthy controls before and after treatment in leukaemia patients, in lymphoma patients the EPCs were pre-dominantly senescent right after treatment completion and apoptotic activity gradually returned to healthy control levels, suggesting reduced EPC involvement in tumour-associated angiogenesis following treatment and persistent impairment of endothelial regenerative capacity, although their relative contributions cannot be determined from the present study. In summary, this study demonstrates that endothelial injury largely subsides following treatment, but regeneration, and hence repair, remains impaired during remission.

title: Ciprofol-Based Total Intravenous Anesthesia During Pediatric Laparoscopic Surgery: A Double-Blind, Randomized Controlled, Non-Inferiority Clinical Trial.
authorString: Xu L, Pan R, Dai X, Xu A.
abstractText:
Background

This double-blind, randomized controlled trial evaluated whether ciprofol is non-inferior to propofol as the primary agent for total intravenous anesthesia (TIVA) in pediatric laparoscopic surgery, with respect to extubation time and safety profile.

Methods

Children aged 2-12 years (ASA I-II) undergoing laparoscopic surgery were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive either ciprofol or propofol for TIVA. The primary outcome was time to extubation, with a predefined non-inferiority margin (Δ) of 4.8 minutes. Secondary outcomes included recovery metrics, emergence delirium, pain scores, hemodynamic profiles, and safety indicators.

Results

A total of 86 children (43 per group) were enrolled. Extubation time was 17.3±4.9 min in the ciprofol group and 20.1±4.9 min in the propofol group (mean difference, -2.79 min; 95% CI, -4.9 to -0.7). The upper bound of the 95% CI (-0.73 min) was well below the non-inferiority margin of 4.8 min, confirming non-inferiority (one-sided P < 0.0001). Anesthesia and surgery times, recovery metrics, and pain scores did not differ significantly between groups. The incidence of emergence delirium was similar (7.0% vs 2.3%, P=0.616). In exploratory analyses, individuals in the ciprofol group seemed to have overall higher systolic, diastolic, and mean blood pressure than those in the propofol group, while heart rate did not differ between the two groups.

Conclusion

Ciprofol was non-inferior to propofol for extubation time in pediatric TIVA for laparoscopic surgery. Although exploratory analyses suggested potential favorable hemodynamic trends, larger multicenter studies are needed to evaluate comparative safety and clinical relevance.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Pulmonary Hypertension: Advancements, Opportunities, and Challenges.
authorString: Li X, Zhang L, Zhang L, Xie Y, Xie M, Ji M, He Q, Wu Z, Qin S, Li Y.
abstractText: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is a progressive cardiopulmonary disorder associated with high morbidity and mortality. Delayed diagnosis, heterogeneous disease phenotypes, and variable treatment responses remain major clinical challenges. Artificial intelligence (AI), including machine learning and deep learning, has emerged as a promising tool for improving PH management. AI-based models have demonstrated promising performance in screening, diagnosis, classification, risk stratification, and prognosis prediction using multimodal data such as electrocardiography, chest radiography, computed tomography, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, echocardiography, and electronic health records. Furthermore, AI may support individualized risk assessment, treatment-response prediction, early identification of right ventricular deterioration, and longitudinal remote monitoring. Emerging technologies, including explainable AI, federated learning, large language models, and digital twins, may further advance precision medicine in PH. Despite these advances, data quality, interpretability, privacy, and clinical implementation of AI remain challenges. This review summarizes current applications, opportunities, and challenges of AI in PH and discusses future directions for AI-assisted precision healthcare.

title: Changes in antibiotic prophylaxis prescribing and infective endocarditis admissions in England and Scotland following changes in national guidance: a quasi-experimental longitudinal study.
authorString: Thornhill MH, Prendergast B, Dayer M, Lockhart P, Baddour LM.
abstractText:
Background

Use of antibiotic prophylaxis (AP) prior to invasive dental procedures (IDPs) to prevent infective endocarditis (IE) fell dramatically in the UK when the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) recommended its cessation in 2008. However, guidance implementation by dentists, general medical practitioners (GPs) and others differed in England and Scotland, particularly after 2018 when the Scottish Dental Clinical Effectiveness Programme advised Scottish dentists to consider AP for high-risk individuals. We compared the effects of this differing guidance on AP prescribing and IE-admissions.

Methods

A quasi-experimental (natural) longitudinal-study design was used to compare aggregated national AP prescribing (2002-2025) and IE-admissions data (1998-2025) for England and Scotland. Interrupted time series and difference-in-differences analyses were used to evaluate changes.

Findings

AP prescribing fell 93% in England after the 2008 NICE guidelines and remained low (2567 [95% CI 2433-2701] prescriptions/million/annum before 2008 vs 185 [95% CI 165-204] prescriptions/million/annum after 2021/2, p < 0.0001), while IE-admissions increased by 112% (26 [95% CI 25-27] admissions/million/annum before 2008 vs 55 [95% CI 54-56]/million/annum after 2021/2, p < 0.0001). In Scotland, AP prescribing fell less, because GP prescribing replaced some dental prescribing, then rose again after 2018 and finished 2.86 times higher than in England (1884 [95% CI 1816-1952] prescriptions/million before 2008 vs 528 [95% CI 350-705] prescriptions/million after 2021/2). Correspondingly, Scottish IE-admissions rose less (24 [95% CI 23-25] admissions/million before 2008 vs 34 [95% CI 32-37] admissions/million after 2021/2, p < 0.0001) than in England, and English IE-admissions/million ended 61% higher than in Scotland (p < 0.0001).

Interpretation

Although our data do not establish causality, they suggest that cessation of AP may be followed by a significant increase in IE-admissions compared with policies recommending AP for high-risk individuals.

Funding

None.

title: Exertional syncope caused by acquired obstruction of the pulmonary artery due to an organized thrombus in a dog.
authorString: Szatmári V, Bergmann W, Grinwis GCM.
abstractText: An 8.5-year-old Boxer was referred for evaluation of frequently occurring exercise-induced seizure-like episodes for 2.5 months. Cardiac auscultation revealed a left basilar systolic murmur with an intensity of IV/VI. Echocardiography showed severe pulmonary arterial obstruction with a pressure gradient of 90 mmHg due to a suspected intraluminal mass. Cardiac catheterization was performed, where a right ventriculogram revealed a large rounded filling defect in the pulmonary artery trunk. No balloon angioplasty, biopsy or stenting were attempted. After euthanasia, post-mortem examination revealed an organized thrombus of unknown etiology attached to the wall of the pulmonary artery trunk. The adjacent arterial wall showed a markedly thickened intimal layer. The etiology remains unclear, primarily due to the chronic nature of the condition. Antemortem blood tests and postmortem examination failed to reveal any prothrombotic conditions. Acquired causes of pulmonary arterial obstruction are extremely rare in dogs, and an organized thrombus has not been reported yet.

title: Segmental jejunal necrotizing enterocolitis mimicking malrotation with midgut volvulus in a term newborn with abnormal prenatal bowel sonography: A case report.
authorString: Sidikov O, Mirzakarimov B, Toshmatov K, Kholmatov D, Quziyev D, Mamajonov U.
abstractText: Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is uncommon in term infants and rarely presents within hours of birth, when bilious vomiting more often reflects malrotation with midgut volvulus or intestinal atresia. A male infant was born by cesarean section at 38 weeks of gestation (3230 g). Prenatal ultrasound at approximately 34 weeks had shown a dilated, aperistaltic bowel segment with a whirlpool-like configuration and polyhydramnios. Bilious vomiting began 2 hours after birth, followed by upper abdominal distension, rectal bleeding, and failure to pass meconium. On day 3, an upper gastrointestinal contrast study showed a tapered obstruction just beyond the duodenum with an indeterminate duodenojejunal junction; radiography and ultrasound showed pneumatosis intestinalis without portal venous gas, and color Doppler ultrasound showed the superior mesenteric vein wrapping around the superior mesenteric artery. Malrotation with midgut volvulus was diagnosed. At laparotomy, rotation was normal and there was no volvulus; a 4-cm necrotic jejunal segment enveloped by fibrinous and fibrous adhesions was resected, and a Bishop-Koop enterostomy was created. Histopathology showed hemorrhagic mucosal necrosis, subserosal pneumatosis, inflammation, bacterial colonies, vascular thrombi, and granulation tissue, consistent with NEC. At 5 months, the infant was thriving. A whirlpool sign, even with the superior mesenteric vein wrapping around the artery, may occur without malrotation when a necrotic jejunal segment tethers adjacent loops. Segmental NEC can present within hours of birth in a term newborn, and the prenatal and subacute histopathological findings suggest that the intestinal injury may begin before birth.

title: Astrocytic mitochondria restore neuronal bioenergetics and function in Parkinson disease models.
authorString: Singh J, Tiwari V, Sharma A, Shukla S.
abstractText: Mitochondrial dysfunction contributes to neuronal injury in Parkinson's disease, and astrocyte-derived mitochondria may offer neuroprotection by restoring neuronal bioenergetics. Here, we investigated the therapeutic potential of astrocyte-derived mitochondria in 6-OHDA models of Parkinson's disease. Using mitochondrial labeling and co-culture assays, we obtained evidence consistent with the release of astrocytic mitochondria, their uptake by injured neurons, and their association with the neuronal mitochondrial network. Building on this observation, we investigated whether direct delivery of functional astrocytic mitochondria could augment endogenous support during neuronal injury. Infused astrocytic mitochondria reduced oxidative stress, restored mitochondrial membrane potential, improved mitochondrial respiration, normalized calcium homeostasis, reduced early neuronal apoptosis, and restored mitochondrial mass. Astrocytic mitochondrial delivery enhanced dendritic arborization in primary neurons. In vivo, stereotactic infusion restored TH immunoreactivity in the SNpc and improved motor and non-motor behavioral deficits. These findings support the potential of astrocyte-derived mitochondria as a promising cell-free therapeutic approach for Parkinson's disease.

title: Maternal exposure to nitrate in drinking water and risk of cyanotic congenital heart defects.
authorString: Wu F.
abstractText:
Background

The rate of cyanotic congenital heart defects (CCHD), a group of major birth defects, has increased 88% from 2016 to 2023 in Utah. However, few studies have identified risk factors for this increasing trend. Therefore, this study assessed the association of drinking water contaminants with CCHD in Utah.

Methods

This study uses an ecological design to analyze the association between CCHD and drinking water contaminants in Utah. Birth data were collected from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention National Center for Health Statistics birth database, and drinking water contaminant data were collected from the Environmental Protection Agency and United States Geological Survey Water Quality database. Multivariable logistic regression analyses were used to identify associations between drinking water contaminants and CCHD.

Results

Nitrate concentration in drinking water was positively and significantly associated with CCHD in Utah (OR: 3.41, 95% CI: 2.22-5.24, p-value <0.001). Furthermore, fertilizer expenditure and nitrate concentration showed similar increasing trends, suggesting fertilizers may be correlated with nitrate contamination in drinking water.

Conclusion

These findings suggest the CCHD increasing trend in Utah may be correlated with nitrate concentration in drinking water, and nitrate in drinking water may be correlated with fertilizers. Thus, decreasing the use of nitrate fertilizers may decrease the nitrate concentration in drinking water and the risk of CCHD in Utah.

title: Multimodality imaging of advanced right ventricular remodelling in late-presenting isolated pulmonary valve stenosis.
authorString: Noparatkailas N, Kanjanavanit R, Thonghong T.

title: Renal Involvement in Down Syndrome: Developmental and Clinical Perspectives.
authorString: Andrejić Višnjić B, Samardžić Lukić M, Stojanović V, Trivunić Dajko S, Šunjević M, Kovač N, Bosanac M.
abstractText: With the increasing life expectancy of individuals with Down syndrome (DS), kidney disease has emerged as an important yet under-recognized contributor to long-term morbidity and mortality in this population. This narrative review summarizes current knowledge regarding the developmental, structural, histopathological, and clinical aspects of renal involvement in DS. A literature search was conducted, and studies addressing renal structure, function, development, or pathology in individuals with DS (clinical studies, autopsy studies, case reports, and experimental studies) were included. Available evidence indicates that renal involvement in DS extends beyond congenital anomalies to include altered nephrogenesis, acquired glomerulopathies, and progressive functional impairment. Histopathological studies of fetal kidneys suggest altered nephrogenesis and delayed renal maturation in DS, potentially resulting in reduced nephron endowment. However, the long-term functional consequences of these developmental findings remain uncertain. Reported acquired glomerular diseases are heterogeneous and include IgA nephropathy, focal segmental glomerulosclerosis, membranous nephropathy, ANCA-associated glomerulonephritis, and several rarer entities. Conventional renal biomarkers may underestimate kidney dysfunction in DS because of altered body composition and reduced muscle mass, while evidence regarding novel biomarkers such as NGAL and KIM-1 remains limited. Renal involvement in DS is multifactorial and likely reflects the interplay between disturbed nephrogenesis, developmental renal abnormalities, and acquired renal disease, resulting in increased renal vulnerability throughout life. Improved awareness, earlier nephrological surveillance, and validation of sensitive renal biomarkers may facilitate earlier detection of kidney injuries and improve long-term renal outcomes in individuals with DS.

title: Research progress of artificial intelligence applications in obstetrics.
authorString: Zhang L, Liu Y, Zhao Y, Ma J, Pan L, Wang L.
abstractText: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being applied across obstetrics, with applications spanning electronic medical record analysis, prenatal ultrasound, fetal monitoring, prediction of pregnancy complications, labor management, postpartum care, and telemedicine. The evidence reviewed in this article indicates that AI can improve automated information extraction, image and signal interpretation, and risk discrimination across multiple obstetric tasks, with particularly consistent advances in fetal ultrasound analysis, cardiotocography (CTG) interpretation, and early prediction of gestational diabetes, preeclampsia, and preterm birth. However, model performance is heterogeneous and is often reported using discrimination or classification metrics rather than patient-centered clinical outcomes. In CTG research, models differ substantially in whether they classify interpretation categories, detect fetal hypoxia or acidemia, or predict neonatal outcomes, making direct comparison difficult. Similarly, high predictive accuracy for pregnancy complications does not establish that AI implementation itself improves maternal or neonatal outcomes, and the clinical benefit of treatment should not be attributed to the predictive model without intervention studies. Across obstetric applications, limited external validation, dataset shift, class imbalance, calibration, interpretability, workflow integration, and data governance remain major barriers to clinical translation. This review therefore emphasizes the distinction between technical model performance and demonstrated clinical utility, and highlights the evidence required to move AI applications from retrospective development toward prospective, clinically integrated obstetric care.

title: Endpoint design in pulmonary arterial hypertension therapeutic trials permitting pediatric enrollment: a ClinicalTrials.gov registry analysis.
authorString: Zheng X, Hua Y.
abstractText:
Background

Pediatric therapeutic development depends not only on age-appropriate dosing but also on endpoints whose administration and interpretation remain coherent across developmental stages.

Methods

An expanded ClinicalTrials.gov search was performed on 2 October 2026 using pulmonary hypertension terms plus the structured Child age filter (birth-17 years), while restricting eligibility to records first posted on or before 8 August 2026. The combined inventory contained 394 unique records. Seventy-two records formed the main analysis set; 69 were assigned to 57 traceable trial families and three continuation records remained unassigned at family level. Endpoint domains were counted once per family.

Results

Fifty-two families had registered outcomes available for domain analysis (42 first posted before 2017 and 10 in 2017-2026). Biomarker/laboratory measures occurred in 12/42 versus 9/10 families and functional capacity/activity in 38/42 versus 6/10. The study-level registered maximum permitted age was 18 years or younger in 14/42 earlier and 9/10 later families; this was used only for an age-scope sensitivity stratum and was not an eligibility criterion. In this age-scope stratum, several era contrasts attenuated, including PK/PD/dosing (9/14 vs. 7/9; difference +13.5 percentage points, 95% CI -24.4 to +43.6). A core-primary sensitivity analysis excluding four families whose registry records were updated after the eligibility cutoff produced the same qualitative pattern of no recent functional primary entries and wider uncertainty in the smaller later-era group. Five families with completely missing outcome modules were all in the earlier era; extreme-case analyses are reported in the supplement.

Conclusion

Endpoint portfolios differed across registration eras, but age-scope composition, differential missingness, and incomplete historical registry reconstruction limit a temporal interpretation. Public endpoint descriptions should specify the clinical construct, measurement method, reporter or data source, capability rule, and handling of children unable to complete an assessment.

title: Restrictive lung function defined by body plethysmography is common in children with Fontan palliation and functionally relevant.
authorString: Ofenheimer A, Usemann J, Moeller A, Vogt A, Vogt S, Kellenberger C, Burkhardt BEU, Valsangiacomo Buechel ER, Callegari A.
abstractText:
Background

Pulmonary dysfunction is common in single ventricle (SV) patients with Fontan circulation, yet the prevalence and clinical relevance of true restrictive lung disease remain poorly characterized as most studies relied on spirometry alone. This study comprehensively assessed lung function using spirometry and body plethysmography, examined its relationship with cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR)-derived lung volumes, evaluated its impact on exercise capacity, and identified clinical correlates of restrictive physiology.

Methods

In this prospective, single-centre study, 31 children and adolescents with Fontan circulation underwent spirometry, body plethysmography, cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET), and CMR. Restrictive lung function was defined by reduced (ResultsRestrictive lung function was identified in n = 8 (26%) participants. TLC correlated strongly with CMR-derived total lung volume (r = 0.889, p < 0.001). Patients with restrictive physiology demonstrated significantly reduced exercise capacity, including lower peak oxygen uptake, tidal volume, and minute ventilation, with reduced breathing reserve and higher peak respiratory rate, indicating clinically relevant ventilatory limitation. Restrictive physiology was associated with lower ventricular ejection fraction and impaired global circumferential strain. In multivariable analysis, TLC was the strongest predictor of peak oxygen uptake.

Conclusions

Restrictive lung physiology confirmed by body plethysmography is common in children and adolescents with Fontan circulation and associates with impaired exercise performance and reduced ventricular function. Comprehensive pulmonary function testing including body plethysmography may be considered in routine follow-up to identify patients at increased risk of adverse outcomes.

title: Recognizing pediatric post-intubation tracheal stenosis: lessons from delayed diagnosis and tissue-preserving endoscopic management.
authorString: Schnee SV, Gunst L, Matheisl D, Fuchs H, Schneider H.
abstractText:
Background

Post-intubation tracheal stenosis (PITS) is a rare but potentially life-threatening complication of endotracheal intubation in children. Because early symptoms often mimic common pediatric respiratory disorders, diagnosis may be delayed until critical airway obstruction develops. We aimed to characterize the diagnostic course, clinical presentation, and outcomes of pediatric PITS treated using a minimally invasive, tissue-preserving endoscopic strategy.

Methods

We retrospectively reviewed all children with endoscopically confirmed PITS treated at a tertiary pediatric airway center between 2019 and 2026. Clinical presentation, timing of diagnosis, treatment, and outcomes were analyzed descriptively.

Results

Eight infants were included in this cohort, all of whom had subglottic PITS. Median age at intubation was 4.5 months and median duration of initial mechanical ventilation was 3.5 days. Respiratory symptoms developed after a median of 4.5 days following extubation, whereas PITS was diagnosed only after a median of 65 days, indicating substantial diagnostic delay. Six patients presented with stridor and dyspnea, while two developed severe respiratory failure requiring emergency intubation without preceding stridor. Six patients had Myer-Cotton grade III and two grade II stenosis. Morphology-guided endoscopic treatment included balloon dilation (n = 4), mechanical dilation (n = 3), or membrane resection (n = 1), combined with temporary postoperative airway stabilization through invasive ventilation as well as local and systemic anti-inflammatory therapy. No patient developed restenosis or required tracheostomy or open airway reconstruction during long-term follow-up.

Conclusions

Delayed recognition appears to be a major challenge in pediatric PITS. Early endoscopic airway evaluation should be considered in children with persistent respiratory symptoms after intubation, even after short-term ventilation or in the absence of stridor. Selected patients may be successfully managed using a minimally invasive, tissue-preserving endoscopic approach.

title: Quantitative 3-Dimensional Characterization of Aortic and Carotid Artery Tortuosity in Mucopolysaccharidosis Type IVa: An Exploratory Comparative Imaging Study.
authorString: Lollert A, Gökce S, Hoffmann C, Souschek F, Rossmann H, Häuser F, Maiurano L, Staatz G, Hennermann JB.
abstractText: Background/Objectives: Vascular involvement has been described in mucopolysaccharidosis type IVa (MPS IVa), but the morphology of the aorta and carotid arteries has not been comprehensively characterized. This study aimed to quantitatively assess aortic and carotid artery tortuosity and kinking using contrast-enhanced three-dimensional (3D) magnetic resonance (MR) angiography. Methods: In this retrospective exploratory comparative imaging study, six patients with confirmed MPS IVa underwent clinically indicated 3D MR angiography of the aorta and supraaortic vessels; two were excluded due to motion artifacts, leaving four patients for analysis. Two radiologists independently assessed vascular kinking and tortuosity. For comparison, 12 age- and sex-matched polytrauma patients without documented vascular abnormalities were retrospectively evaluated using computed tomography angiography. Results: All four patients with MPS IVa showed multiple kinking sites of the descending aorta and increased tortuosity of the common and internal carotid arteries. Aortic tortuosity indices ranged from 2.01 to 2.68. Carotid tortuosity indices were also increased, particularly in the internal carotid arteries. Compared with controls, all assessed tortuosity indices were consistently higher in patients with MPS IVa (exploratory p = 0.001). Despite multiple aortic kinking sites, no marked anatomical luminal narrowing was observed. Conclusions: This exploratory study provides quantitative evidence of differences in aortic and carotid geometry between a small, highly selected MPS IVa cohort and external imaging controls. Larger studies using harmonized imaging protocols and longitudinal follow-up are needed to assess prevalence, disease-specific causation and clinical significance of these findings.

title: Ulnar Polydactyly: Family History, Phenotypes, Associated Anomalies, and Surgical Treatment in a Prospective 7-Year Registry Study.
authorString: Tallay E, Nirmalanathan I, Winge MI, Jokihaara J, Sletten IN.

journal.title: Journal of hand surgery global online

abstractText:
Purpose

Ulnar polydactyly (UP) is a common congenital upper limb anomaly, yet prospective data on inheritance patterns, phenotypic distribution, associated anomalies, and treatment outcomes remain limited.

Methods

We conducted a registry-based observational study of consecutive children with UP enrolled in a prospectively maintained congenital upper limb anomaly registry at a tertiary referral center between 2018 and 2025. Data included family history, pregnancy characteristics, Congenital Upper Limb Differences database classification of phenotypes (A1-A6 and B), laterality, associated anomalies and genetically verified syndromes, and interventions. We analyzed the strength of associations between hand presentation and associated anomalies using multivariable logistic regression.

Results

We included 98 patients with 160 affected hands. Fifty-four percent had a non-Nordic family background, substantially exceeding the proportion of individuals with a non-Nordic background in the general population. Forty-two percent reported a positive family history of UP. Type B UP predominated (85%). Associated lower limb anomalies occurred in 24% of patients. Phenotypes A and bilateral affection showed strong associations with lower limb anomalies and genetic syndromes and/or anomalies besides the limbs. Our unit performed all surgeries without any complications, yet we reoperated many patients after inadequate ligation of type B UP in the maternity wards.

Conclusions

Ulnar polydactyly comprises phenotypic subgroups with differing risks of associated anomalies, supporting a phenotype-based approach to clinical assessment. We recommend genetic evaluation for all patients with phenotype A and for those with bilateral type B with associated lower limb anomalies. In contrast, unilateral and bilateral type B without lower limb involvement or associated anomalies on routine clinical examination do not require further evaluation.

Type of study/level of evidence

Clinical II.

title: Association of Left Ventricular Epicardial Adipose Tissue and Lipomatous Metaplasia With Ventricular Tachycardia Circuitry and Recurrence Following Ablation in Patients With Non-Ischemic Cardiomyopathy.
authorString: Xu L, Galal B, Liao TE, Sohail Z, Callans DJ, Marchlinski FE, Witschey WR, Desjardins B, Nazarian S.
abstractText:
Background

Patients with nonischemic cardiomyopathy (NICM) have complex intramural ventricular tachycardia (VT) circuitry and relatively high postablation recurrences.

Objectives

This study evaluated the association of left ventricular epicardial adipose tissue (LV EAT) and lipomatous metaplasia (LM) with critical VT circuitry and postablation VT recurrence in patients with NICM.

Methods

In this retrospective study, we quantified LV EAT and LM via cardiac contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CECT) in a cohort of consecutive patients with NICM before VT ablation. CECT image registration with VT critical sites in electroanatomic mapping was performed in a subset. Mixed-effects and subdistribution proportional hazard models were used to examine the association of image features with VT circuitry elements and outcomes, respectively.

Results

In 48 patients with coregistered CECT-electroanatomic mapping, segmental maximal EAT thickness was associated with critical VT sites (OR: 1.36 per mm increase; P < 0.001), and a threshold of >4.7 mm EAT achieved 72% sensitivity and 71% specificity (OR: 2.15; P = 0.006) for VT site identification. This association remained significant after adjusting for LM, with a significant EAT-LM interaction (P = 0.027). Among all 119 patients, 52 experienced VT recurrence during a median follow-up of 1.7 years (Q1-Q3: 0.7-4.0). Lower LV EAT attenuation was independently associated with time to VT recurrence (subdistribution HR: 1.04 per 1 HU decrease; P = 0.012) after multivariable adjustment including LM and a significant LM interaction (P = 0.020).

Conclusions

LV EAT density and thickness are associated with VT circuitry and postablation recurrence in patients with NICM, and demonstrate a significant statistical interaction with LM.

title: Prognostic value of native T1 mapping and extracellular volume fraction in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
authorString: Wang Q, Liu W, Shi J, Li W, Lin J, Wang Z, Gao Y.
abstractText:
Background

Accurate risk stratification in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) remains challenging, and the prognostic significance of cardiovascular magnetic resonance-derived native T1 mapping and extracellular volume fraction (ECV) remains uncertain.

Aims

To systematically evaluate the prognostic value of native T1 mapping and ECV in HCM patients.

Methods

PubMed, Embase, MEDLINE, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to February 6, 2026. Eligible studies assessed native T1 and/or ECV for prognosis in HCM. Baseline values, mean differences, and hazard ratios (HRs) were synthesized using random-effects models. Effect estimates were standardized as HRs per 30-ms increase in native T1 and per 1% increase in ECV.

Results

Eight longitudinal cohort studies involving 2539 HCM patients were included. Elevated native T1 was significantly associated with an increased risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) (HR=1.27, 95% CI: 1.12-1.44, P < 0.001), as was higher ECV (HR=1.10, 95% CI: 1.07-1.14, P < 0.001). For sudden cardiac death-related outcomes, the association with native T1 was not significant, whereas elevated ECV was associated with an increased risk (HR=1.14, 95% CI: 1.01-1.28, P = 0.04), although substantial heterogeneity was observed and sensitivity analysis indicated limited robustness (HR=1.05, 95% CI: 0.97-1.14, P = 0.21). For heart failure-related outcomes, only ECV was associated with risk (HR=1.10, 95% CI: 1.05-1.15; P < 0.001).

Conclusions

Native T1 and ECV were associated with MACE risk in HCM, and ECV was additionally associated with heart failure-related outcomes. Their value for sudden cardiac death-related risk prediction requires further validation.

Prospero registration number

CRD420261406609.

title: Necrotizing enterocolitis as a disorder of neonatal mucosal immune ecology: from dysbiosis and barrier failure to regulated cell death and precision prevention.
authorString: Sun S, Yu Z, Zhou M, Li M, Wang S, Cheng Y, Qu Y, Yan C, Tian J.
abstractText: Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) remains one of the most severe gastrointestinal emergencies of prematurity. Although survival of extremely preterm infants has improved, NEC continues to cause substantial mortality, intestinal failure, neurodevelopmental impairment, and prolonged neonatal intensive care. Its pathogenesis has traditionally been described as a convergence of prematurity, enteral feeding, intestinal ischemia, and abnormal bacterial colonization. This model remains useful, but it does not fully explain why only a subset of high-risk infants develop NEC or why single interventions show inconsistent benefit. This narrative review examines classic preterm NEC as a disorder of neonatal mucosal immune ecology, while distinguishing it from spontaneous intestinal perforation and predominantly hemodynamic injury in congenital heart disease. Epithelial immaturity, dysbiosis, altered microbial metabolism, exaggerated pattern-recognition signaling, immune-cell activation, endothelial dysfunction, thromboinflammation, and regulated cell death amplify one another. Particular attention is given to cell-specific signaling, the interaction of vascular and epithelial injury, and the distinction between protective autophagy and destructive stress responses. These mechanisms inform translational opportunities involving mother's own milk, donor human milk, strain-specific probiotics, postbiotics, defined microbial metabolites, extracellular vesicles, organoids, and multi-omics biomarkers. A mucosal immune-ecology model supports precision prevention based on developmental timing, microbial function, immune state, and injury mechanism.

title: First-trimester maternal exposures and offspring congenital heart defects: a Hungarian population-based case-control study, 1980-2009.
authorString: Suo Z, Váradi A, Hegyi P, Rancz A, Ács N.
abstractText:
Background

Congenital heart defects (CHDs) are a major cause of infant morbidity and mortality. Identifying modifiable maternal exposures during early pregnancy is important for CHD prevention and maternal and child health.

Objectives

To examine associations between first-trimester maternal active smoking and alcohol consumption and offspring CHDs, and to explore associations of selected maternal diseases and related treatments with CHD outcomes.

Methods

This population-based case-control study used data from the Hungarian Case-Control Surveillance of Congenital Abnormalities (1980-2009), including 7,362 CHD cases and 56,894 controls. Overall CHDs were the primary outcome, with ventricular septal defect (VSD) and atrial septal defect (ASD) examined as secondary outcomes. Complete-case multivariable logistic regression estimated odds ratios (ORs) for smoking and alcohol consumption, with mutual adjustment and additional adjustment for maternal age, socioeconomic status, and offspring sex. Multiple imputation was performed as a sensitivity analysis. Maternal disease and treatment analyses were crude and exploratory.

Results

First-trimester maternal smoking was associated with higher odds of overall CHDs (adjusted OR 1.50, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.30-1.71), VSD (1.36, 1.11-1.66) and ASD (1.62, 1.35-1.93). Multiple-imputation estimates were similar to the complete-case estimates. No statistically significant associations were observed between maternal alcohol consumption and CHD outcomes in either the adjusted complete-case analysis or the multiple-imputation analysis. Maternal epilepsy, migraine, anxiety disorder and anemia showed positive crude associations with one or more CHD outcomes.

Conclusion

Maternal smoking reported during the first trimester was associated with higher odds of overall CHDs, VSD, and ASD, supporting smoking cessation before conception and during pregnancy as a prevention priority. Exploratory associations involving maternal diseases and treatments require further investigation and should not be used to infer treatment effects or guide treatment decisions.

title: Patient-specific heart rate modulates developmental electrophysiology in transcriptomic-guided in silico models of pediatric human atrial cardiomyocytes.
authorString: Ellks GM, Mendez MJ, Guerrelli D, Miller JA, Desai M, d'Udekem Y, Posnack NG, Weinberg SH.
abstractText: Cardiac electrophysiology adapts throughout pediatric development, driven by factors including age-associated ion channel expression changes and decreasing heart rate.
