Our prior transcriptomic-guided simulations of human atrial cardiomyocytes predicted developmental-associated changes in electrophysiology biomarkers at a fixed pacing rate, leaving the contribution of age- and patient-specific heart rate unresolved. In this study, we incorporated intrinsic heart rate into gene expression-guided computational models to predict the interaction between developmental maturation and pacing rate to shape atrial electrophysiology. Virtual patient-specific populations of atrial cardiomyocytes were generated from the right atrial cardiomyocyte gene expression data from 117 patients, spanning neonates to young adults. We simulated each population at pacing rates corresponding to each patient's intrinsic ECG-based heart rate and at fixed rates corresponding to the patient cohort minimum, median, and maximum. We also simulated each population at the patient's intrinsic heart rate in the presence of isoproterenol. Action potential and calcium transient biomarkers were quantified, and partial least squares regression assessed key biomarker dependencies. For intrinsic-rate pacing conditions, action potential duration at 50% and 90% repolarization increased with age, whereas early repolarization shortened; maximum upstroke velocity increased, resting membrane potential became more negative, and alternans prevalence decreased. Developmental differences persisted during fixed-rate pacing conditions, indicating that differences were not explained solely by the faster heart rates of younger patients. Notably, intrinsic-rate simulations exhibited stronger age associations for upstroke velocity and alternans than fixed-rate simulations. Further, isoproterenol induced age-dependent responses, with most notably opposite directional changes in action potential duration. Sensitivity analyses indicated that electrophysiological phenotypes arose from interactions among ionic conductances, calcium handling, age, and heart rate. Collectively, we find that pediatric atrial electrophysiology reflects both intrinsic developmental remodeling and rate-dependent modulation.

title: Reference values for cord blood N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide in preterm neonates.
authorString: Tong C, Cai C, Zhao Y, Jiang S, Peng H, Liu Y, Liu J, Zhao C, Wang L, Chen Y.
abstractText:
Purpose

The aim of this work is to establish reference values for cord blood N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) in preterm neonates and to examine the associations between NT-proBNP concentrations and perinatal factors.

Methods

Cord blood NT-proBNP levels were measured in 174 preterm infants born at 26-36 weeks of gestation. Infants were stratified by gestational age (GA), and reference intervals for cord blood NT-proBNP were calculated as the 5th-95th percentiles for each GA subgroup. Correlations between NT-proBNP concentrations and selected perinatal variables were also assessed.

Results

The study revealed that NT-proBNP levels showed negative correlations with GA, birth weight (BW), and Apgar scores at 1 and 5 min, with correlation coefficients of -0.229, -0.278, -0.264, and -0.290, respectively, all statistically significant at P < 0.01. However, no significant associations were observed between NT-proBNP concentrations and infant gender, cord blood pH, premature rupture of membranes (PROM), mode of delivery, or early ejection fraction (EF).

Conclusion

Reference intervals for cord blood NT-proBNP in preterm infants should be stratified by GA, with levels decreasing as GA and BW increase. Neither vaginal delivery nor PROM was associated with elevated NT-proBNP levels, suggesting that these perinatal factors do not independently induce significant cardiovascular stress in the fetus.

title: Invasive <i>Candida viswanathii</i> infections in critically ill neonates: clinical challenges and management insights from a case series.
authorString: De Rose DU, Maddaloni C, Martini L, Santisi A, Cortazzo V, Raimondi S, Vrenna G, Calò Carducci F, Lancella L, Capolupo I, Bernaschi P, Ciofi Degli Atti ML, Perno CF, Dotta A, Ronchetti MP, Raponi M.
abstractText:
Background

Candida species continue to be a major cause of invasive fungal infections in neonatal intensive care units, with a growing awareness of new non-Albicans Candida species that pose diagnostic and therapeutic problems in critically ill neonates. Candida viswanathii is an uncommon pathogen with poor clinical evidence, particularly in neonatal critical care units.

Methods

From April to August 2025, we conducted a case series of five newborns admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) of Bambino Gesù Children's Hospital in Rome, Italy, who had bloodstream infections caused by C. viswanathii. Whole-genome sequencing (WGS), chromogenic agar evaluation, MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry, and traditional culture were all used in microbiological identification. Broth microdilution was used to test for antifungal susceptibility. Retrospective clinical data on risk factors, treatment, and results were collected.

Results

Six cases of candidemia were reported in five critically unwell newborns, the majority of whom were premature or had severe congenital comorbidities. All of the patients had central venous catheters and had been in intensive care for an extended period of time. Initial identification methods misidentified isolates as Candida tropicalis, however molecular research revealed a clonal cluster of C. viswanathii. The BCID2 panel failed to detect the organism. All isolates had higher fluconazole minimum inhibitory concentrations, but echinocandins and amphotericin B had lower MIC values. Systemic echinocandin therapy was the primary treatment, with liposomal amphotericin B added in severe instances, as well as rigorous source control measures such as catheter removal and antifungal lock therapy. Microbiological clearance was documented in all six candidemia episodes. Three patients were discharged, whereas two died because of their underlying cardiopulmonary disease.

Conclusions

Invasive C. viswanathii infection represents a diagnostic and therapeutic challenge in the NICU. Advanced microbiological techniques, prompt source control, and targeted antifungal therapy are essential for effective management of this emerging pathogen.

title: Clinical characteristics of brain abscesses secondary to <i>Streptococcus intermedius</i> in children: a case report and systematic literature review.
authorString: Zhang F, Liao Q, Zhu Y, Zou T.
abstractText:
Background

Brain abscess is a relatively rare and potentially life-threatening infection in children. Streptococcus intermedius (S. intermedius) is one of the primary causes of brain abscess in children. Multiple brain abscesses due to S. intermedius are rare in immunocompetent children without underlying diseases.

Case presentation

We report a single case of a 7-year-old Chinese immunocompetent boy without underlying disease who was diagnosed with multiple brain abscesses caused by S. intermedius. The PubMed database was screened for English- and French-language articles concerning brain abscess due to S. intermedius in children. Forty-two patients with individual information were identified. All included reports were analyzed in terms of baseline characteristics, clinical presentation, diagnosis, management, and outcomes of described patients.

Conclusion

Male predominance was observed in children with S. intermedius brain abscess. Most cases occur from the ages of 6-18 years. Not all children with brain abscesses due to S. intermedius have chronic underlying diseases or acute predisposing factors. Healthcare professionals should remain alert to indicative clinical symptoms, ensuring timely diagnosis and comprehensive treatment for a favorable prognosis.

title: The impact of nesting care on the growth and neurological development of premature infants in neonatal intensive care units.
authorString: Chen L, Wang H.
abstractText:
Objective

To examine the associations of nesting care with growth, nighttime sleep-wake measures, and early neurodevelopmental outcomes in preterm infants admitted to a neonatal intensive care unit (NICU).

Methods

This single-center retrospective observational study compared two noncontemporaneous cohorts at the Maternal and Child Health Hospital of Linping District, Hangzhou. Fifty preterm infants receiving nesting care from March 2024 to March 2025 and 50 receiving traditional care from February 2023 to February 2024 were manually selected from the eligible population to achieve approximate baseline comparability. Growth was assessed at birth and 3 months corrected age, sleep-wake activity by actigraphy at baseline and day 7, and neurodevelopment using the Gesell Developmental Schedules at 40 weeks postmenstrual age (PMA) and 3 months corrected age. Longitudinal sleep and Gesell outcomes were analyzed using adjusted change-score regression models with HC3 robust standard errors and Holm correction.

Results

At 3 months corrected age, the nesting-care group had higher body weight (difference, 195.12 g; 95% CI, 26.00-364.24), greater body length (2.04 cm; 95% CI, 0.68-3.40), and greater head circumference (median difference, 1.00 cm). From baseline to day 7, improvement in total sleep duration was greater in the nesting-care group (adjusted difference in change, 1.09 h; 95% CI, 0.36-1.81; Holm-adjusted P = 0.010), while mean awakening duration decreased more (-0.57 h; 95% CI, -0.70 to -0.45; P < 0.001). For neurodevelopment, adjusted improvements from 40 weeks PMA to 3 months corrected age were greater for fine motor (4.40 points), adaptive (3.95), language (2.18), and personal-social domains (1.60), whereas gross motor change was not statistically significant after adjustment (P = 0.054).

Conclusions

In this retrospective comparison of noncontemporaneous cohorts, nesting care was associated with more favorable growth, nighttime actigraphy-derived sleep-wake measures, and several early neurodevelopmental outcomes. These findings should be interpreted cautiously because residual confounding and calendar-period effects cannot be excluded.

title: Clinical phenotype and diagnostic pathways of 22q11.2 deletion syndrome in a Ukrainian cohort.
authorString: Boyarchuk O, Bondarenko A, Hilfanova A, Romanyshyn Y, Nazarenko L, Tykholaz O, Lazaruk M, Yarema N, Volianska L, Hariyan T, Kinash M, Kovalchuk T, Savchak I, Malko O, Tsanko T, Urbas O, Hrabovska I, Kalyuzhko S, Polishchuk I, Makukh H, Olkhovych N.
abstractText:
Introduction

Chromosome 22q11.2 deletion syndrome (22q11.2DS) is a common multisystem genomic disorder with marked phenotypic variability and diagnostic delay. Data on diagnostic pathways and specialist involvement in Eastern Europe remain limited. We aimed to characterize diagnostic pathways and clinical triggers, assess specialist involvement and follow-up, and identify factors associated with diagnosis before or after 1 year of age in a Ukrainian cohort.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective multicenter observational study of patients with 22q11.2DS registered in the Ukrainian National Registry of Primary Immunodeficiencies. Clinical manifestations, diagnostic triggers, specialists involved in diagnosis and follow-up, immunological findings, and age at diagnosis were analyzed.

Results

The cohort included 126 patients, with a median age of 12 years (range, 0.1-39 years) and median age at diagnosis of 1.0 year (range, 0.1-18 years). Among 120 patients with available diagnostic timing, 63 (52.5%) were diagnosed within the first year, including the two antenatal cases. Congenital heart disease (CHD) was the most frequent major manifestation (74/89, 83.1%), followed by craniofacial dysmorphism (62/74, 83.8%), thymic hypoplasia (54/65, 83.1%), developmental delay (46/62, 74.2%), and recurrent infections (44/65, 67.7%). Among 83 patients with documented diagnostic triggers, CHD was the most frequent (61/83, 73.5%). Developmental delay was more frequent among patients diagnosed after 1 year than within the first year (22.9% vs. 4.4%, p = 0.0135). Immunodeficiency was a diagnostic trigger in 10/83 patients (12.0%), despite T-cell lymphopenia in 31/59 (52.5%). Immunologists and geneticists were most frequently involved in diagnosis. Cardiothoracic surgeons and cardiologists were more frequently involved among patients diagnosed within the first year than after 1 year (27.9% vs. 9.1%, p = 0.0411). Among 13 patients diagnosed after implementation of TREC/KREC newborn screening, two were identified following an abnormal screening result.

Conclusions

In this Ukrainian cohort, 22q11.2DS diagnosis was predominantly phenotype-driven, with CHD representing the principal diagnostic trigger. Developmental delay was associated with diagnosis after 1 year, whereas immunological abnormalities relatively infrequently initiated diagnostic evaluation. Broader recognition of non-cardiac presentations, standardized referral criteria, coordinated multidisciplinary care, and continued development of newborn and prenatal screening may improve timely diagnosis of 22q11.2DS in Ukraine.

title: Mid-term outcomes of right atrial appendage-derived pulmonary valve reconstruction during transannular repair of tetralogy of Fallot.
authorString: İrdem AK, Doyurgan O.
abstractText:
Objectives

Transannular patch (TAP) repair remains necessary when pulmonary annular preservation is not feasible during tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) repair, but the resulting pulmonary regurgitation (PR) may contribute to progressive right ventricular volume loading and late reintervention. We evaluated early and mid-term outcomes of right atrial appendage (RAA)-derived bicuspid pulmonary valve reconstruction compared with monocusp and valve-free TAP reconstruction.

Methods

We conducted a two-center retrospective comparative cohort study of 49 patients undergoing TOF repair requiring transannular RVOT reconstruction by a single surgeon. Twenty-two patients underwent RAA-derived bicuspid pulmonary valve reconstruction, 14 underwent monocusp TAP reconstruction, and 13 underwent valve-free TAP reconstruction. The three reconstruction strategies were analyzed separately, with an additional RAA-versus-monocusp sensitivity comparison. Because age at repair differed among groups, an additional sensitivity analysis for the principal echocardiographic outcome was restricted to the overlapping age range of the RAA and monocusp groups.

Results

Median follow-up was 31.5 months (IQR, 28.0-36.0) after RAA reconstruction, 25.5 months (23.0-34.5) after monocusp TAP, and 30.0 months (26.0-36.0) after valve-free TAP (p = 0.224). At the last available follow-up echocardiographic examination, moderate/severe PR was present in 1 of 22 patients (4.5%) after RAA reconstruction, 13 of 14 (92.9%) after monocusp TAP, and 13 of 13 (100%) after valve-free TAP (p < 0.001). The association persisted in the direct RAA-versus-monocusp comparison (4.5% vs. 92.9%; risk ratio, 0.05; 95% CI, 0.01-0.33; Fisher's exact p < 0.001) and in the age-restricted sensitivity analysis [1/16 [6.3%] vs. 9/10 [90.0%]; Fisher's exact p < 0.001]. No patient in the RAA or monocusp group underwent pulmonary valve replacement (PVR), whereas three patients in the valve-free TAP group underwent PVR during subsequent clinical follow-up.

Conclusions

RAA-derived bicuspid pulmonary valve reconstruction was feasible and was associated with a lower prevalence of moderate/severe PR during mid-term follow-up compared with both monocusp and valve-free TAP reconstruction in this retrospective cohort. The association persisted after exclusion of the valve-free TAP group and in an age-restricted sensitivity analysis. These findings warrant confirmation in larger prospective studies with standardized longitudinal imaging and longer follow-up before conclusions regarding long-term durability, right ventricular remodeling, or PVR risk can be established.

title: Natural History, Complications and Long-Term Prognosis of Patients with Cardiac Ascites.
authorString: Ben Yosef Lavi M, Yaari S, Ackerman Z.
abstractText: Introduction and Objectives: The natural history of patients with cardiac ascites (CA) due to congestive heart failure (CHF) remains poorly documented. This study aims were to characterize the natural history of patients with CA including its complications and long-term prognosis, in comparison to patients with ascites secondary to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). Patients and Methods: We conducted a retrospective evaluation of 98 patients presenting with ascites due to either CHF (N = 51) or MASLD (N = 47). Results: Patients with CHF exhibited a higher prevalence of cardiac-specific pathology compared to patients with MASLD. Throughout the study period, both groups presented a decline in serum and ascitic total protein and albumin levels. In patients with CHF, the decline in ascitic total protein was so substantial that levels dropped below 25 g/L in 16 patients. Furthermore, Fibrosis-4 Index (FIB-4) values increased during the study, with a more significant rise observed in the patients with MASLD. Patients with CHF had a significantly longer mean survival time compared to those with MASLD (25.0 ± 3.5 vs. 17.0 ± 2.1 months, p = 0.041). Independent predictors of shorter survival included a higher monthly frequency of paracentesis and rising FIB-4 scores during the study period. Conversely, higher admission levels of ascitic fluid albumin were associated with improved survival. Conclusions: Patients with CA demonstrate better survival outcomes than those with ascites secondary to MASLD. As cardiac disease progresses, serum and ascitic albumin and total protein levels typically decline. These findings suggest that the utility of ascitic fluid analysis in the differential diagnosis of ascites may be limited in cases of advanced CHF.

title: Altered Hepatic Hydrogen Sulfide-Related Homeostasis in Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease and Its Changes Following Sleeve Gastrectomy.
authorString: Han Y, Chen J, Xu Y, Sun L, Dai X.
abstractText: Background: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is closely associated with obesity and metabolic dysfunction. Hydrogen sulfide (H2S) is involved in hepatic glucose and lipid metabolism and redox homeostasis, but alterations in hepatic H2S-related homeostasis in MASLD and their changes following sleeve gastrectomy (SG) remain incompletely understood. This study investigated hepatic H2S metabolism in MASLD and its changes following SG. Methods: Liver tissues from five patients with MASLD and five non-MASLD controls were analyzed for histology, H2S levels, and expression of cystathionine β-synthase (CBS), cystathionine γ-lyase (CSE), and 3-mercaptopyruvate sulfurtransferase (MPST) by qPCR, Western blotting, and immunohistochemistry. A high-fat diet-induced obese rat model was used to evaluate the metabolic, biochemical, histological, and hepatic H2S-related effects of SG. Results: Patients with MASLD showed marked hepatic steatosis, a reduced hepatic H2S-related sulfide pool and CSE expression, increased MPST expression, and unchanged CBS expression. Similar alterations were observed in obese rats. Compared with Sham rats, SG reduced body weight and food intake, improved glucose and lipid metabolism and liver function, and attenuated hepatic steatosis. These improvements were accompanied by an increased hepatic H2S-related sulfide pool and CSE expression and decreased MPST expression, whereas CBS remained stable. Conclusions: MASLD was associated with altered hepatic H2S-related homeostasis characterized by a reduced H2S-related sulfide pool, decreased CSE expression, increased MPST expression, and relatively stable CBS expression. In obese rats, metabolic improvement following SG was accompanied by corresponding changes in hepatic H2S-related homeostasis toward the pattern observed in controls. Whether these H2S-related changes contribute functionally to the metabolic benefits of SG remains to be determined.

title: Incremental Diagnostic Yield of Fetal MRI After Targeted Neurosonography in Fetuses with Agenesis of the Corpus Callosum: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
authorString: Aykut S, Evrüke İC, Demir SC, Kurt A, Nessar AZ, Önder AB.
abstractText: Background/Objectives: This study aimed to assess additional findings reported on fetal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) after targeted neurosonography in fetuses with agenesis of the corpus callosum (ACC). Methods: This retrospective cohort included 129 singleton pregnancies with complete or partial ACC evaluated at a tertiary referral center between January 2020 and January 2023. All underwent fetal MRI within 7 days of neurosonography. Incremental findings were abnormalities not identified on the preceding examination. Final isolated or non-isolated classification incorporated both modalities. Results: MRI reported at least one incremental intracranial or craniofacial finding in 42/129 fetuses (32.6%). The most frequent findings were cerebellar hypoplasia (15/129, 11.6%), vermian agenesis (11/129, 8.5%), and arachnoid cysts (9/129, 7.0%). Final classification identified 71 isolated and 58 non-isolated cases. Among 77 tested fetuses, 15 had aneuploidy; the frequency was higher in non-isolated cases (14/37 versus 1/40; p < 0.001). Conclusions: MRI provided additional anatomical information after neurosonography in approximately one-third of this referral cohort. These findings support assessment beyond confirmation of ACC, but do not establish diagnostic accuracy, improved parental decisions, or long-term prognostic benefit.

title: Patterns of Combined Prenatal Supplement Use and Associations with Birth Outcomes and Early Infant Growth: A Multicenter Prospective Mother-Infant Cohort Study in China.
authorString: Zhang H, Bian Z, Zhang Y, Wu Y, Xiong Z, Teliewubieerde A, Cai W, Duan S, Yan Y, Wang H.
abstractText:
Background

Women often use several prenatal supplements together, yet most studies evaluate products one at a time.

Objective

To identify longitudinal patterns of combined prenatal supplement use and assess their associations with cesarean delivery, birth size, jaundice, and early infant growth.

Methods

This multicenter cohort included 1758 mother-infant pairs from 16 provinces in China. Supplement use was reported once in the baseline questionnaire: on or before delivery for 876 women (median gestational age 38.57 weeks) and after delivery for 809. For each of seven supplements, use frequency was reported once, and participants indicated the pregnancy periods during which the supplement was used. One frequency was assigned to every period endorsed from preconception through the third trimester, giving 28 indicators for latent class analysis. Associations were estimated in exploratory multivariable models, with Benjamini-Hochberg correction within outcome families.

Results

Six patterns were identified. They differ in product combination, endorsed periods, and one recorded frequency per product, and are not ordered by dose (C6 (low use), 25.7%; C4 (all-supplement high-frequency), 7.0%). Membership differed by region, parity, and pregnancy complications. Compared with C6, mid-late high-frequency core use (C5) was nominally associated with lower odds of cesarean delivery (adjusted OR 0.72, 95% CI 0.53-0.99). Persistent multi-supplement high-frequency use (C3) and all-supplement high-frequency use (C4) were nominally associated with higher odds of physiological jaundice recorded at the 40-60-day follow-up (1.65, 1.00-2.70 and 1.86, 1.04-3.27), and C4 with shorter birth length (adjusted β -0.46 cm, 95% CI -0.81 to -0.10). These associations did not remain significant after within-family correction. Macrosomia, infant eczema, and gains in length and weight showed no association. Greater head-circumference gain in mid-late moderate core use (C1) remained significant after correction (adjusted β 0.87 cm, 95% CI 0.34-1.40; q = 0.019) among 513 infants in the adjusted analysis.

Conclusions

Supplement use clustered into six patterns of timing and reported frequency. The associations are observational and do not show that changing a supplement regimen would change these endpoints.

title: Identification of multi-omics molecular programs from the peripheral circulation of patients with PAH.
authorString: Kheyfets VO, Sweatt AJ, Zhang H, Li M, Hu CJ, Nemkov T, Aizin MA, Heerdt P, Dzieciatkowska M, Stephenson D, LaCroix IS, D'Alessandro A, Cendali FI, Oldham WM, Hansen KC, Zamanian RT, Stenmark KR.
abstractText: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) involves progressive remodeling of the pulmonary vasculature and right ventricle, yet much of our understanding of disease progression relies on rodent studies because opportunities for investigation in humans are limited. We integrated plasma proteomic, metabolomic, and lipidomic profiles from 402 patients with PAH and 76 healthy controls using latent-network discovery and graphical modeling, with validation in an external cohort and comparison with human and bovine tissue. PAH was associated with broad molecular remodeling across peptides, metabolites, and lipids, with multiple multi-Omic programs converging on disruptions in the TCA cycle. Of note, elevated 2-hydroxyglutarate distinguished PAH across etiologies and comorbidity profiles, was associated with survival and treatment intensity, and was replicated externally. Related TCA-cycle changes were also observed in pulmonary vascular stromal and immune cells. These findings reveal coordinated remodeling across multiple molecular axes and highlight plasma multi-omics as a bridge between clinical phenotypes and tissue-level metabolic reprogramming.

title: Bioprosthetic valve performance of transcatheter aortic valves.
authorString: Windecker S, De Backer O, Pibarot P, Delgado V, Tomii D.

journal.title: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology

abstractText: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation is used increasingly in younger patients with longer life expectancy, necessitating long-term effectiveness. Randomised clinical trials have demonstrated comparable or superior haemodynamic performance of transcatheter heart valves (THVs) to surgical aortic valve replacement over midterm follow-up. Within a lifetime management framework, haemodynamic performance and durability of THVs are central considerations in patients undergoing aortic valve replacement for severe aortic stenosis. This review provides an overview of THV design and function along with contemporary clinical evidence, with a focus on current haemodynamic assessment considerations, challenges in cross-platform interpretation of valve performance, and limitations of randomised comparative evidence, as well as future directions in the evaluation of THV performance.

title: A 10-Year Single-Center Experience in Pediatric Thromboembolism: Management Strategies and Clinical Outcomes.
authorString: Özay M, Aras T, Bicakci Z, Keskin Z.

journal.title: Mediterranean journal of hematology and infectious diseases

abstractText:
Background

Pediatric thromboembolism is uncommon but clinically important, and its epidemiology varies according to age, underlying disease, catheter exposure, and referral patterns. This study evaluated the epidemiology, risk factors, management, and outcomes of pediatric thromboembolism over a 10-year period in a tertiary care center.

Methods

We retrospectively reviewed children aged 0-18 years with symptomatic, radiologically confirmed thromboembolism between January 2010 and January 2020. Incidentally detected asymptomatic thromboses and cases without imaging confirmation were excluded. Venous and arterial events were analyzed separately.

Results

Among 51,025 pediatric admissions, 70 patients had thromboembolism, corresponding to an admission-based rate of 13.7 per 10,000 admissions. Venous thromboembolism accounted for 51 cases (72.9%) and arterial thromboembolism for 19 cases (27.1%). Median age at diagnosis was 6 years (range, 1 day-18 years), and 49 patients (70.0%) were male. The central nervous system was the most frequent anatomical region involved. Central venous catheterization was the leading modifiable acquired risk factor. Active antithrombotic or interventional treatment was used in 68 patients (97.1%); low molecular weight heparin containing regimens were used in 46 patients (65.7%). Complete recovery was documented in 55 patients (78.6%), recurrence in 12 (17.1%), and mortality in 3 (4.3%). Recurrence was more frequent after venous than arterial events (23.5% vs 0%; p = .028).

Conclusion

In this 10-year cohort, venous events predominated and catheter related thrombosis remained a major preventable contributor. Recurrence was confined to venous events, supporting careful long term follow up and individualized secondary prevention for high risk children. Standardized catheter care practices and selective, appropriately timed thrombophilia testing are practical priorities.

title: Stress Hyperglycemia Ratio and Triglyceride-Glucose Index for Predicting In-Hospital Mortality and Heart Failure in Acute Myocardial Infarction.
authorString: Varim P, Çakmak BS, Çakmak AC, Eynel E, Demirci T, Tatli E.
abstractText:
Background

Metabolic dysregulation substantially contributes to adverse outcomes in acute myocardial infarction (AMI). While the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index reflects chronic insulin resistance, the stress hyperglycemia ratio (SHR) represents acute stress-related glycemic perturbation.

Methods

In this retrospective cohort study, 494 patients with STEMI who underwent primary PCI were included. SHR was calculated using admission blood glucose, whereas the TyG index was calculated using glucose and triglyceride levels obtained from routine morning blood samples, generally collected between 04:00 and 06:00 a.m. The primary outcomes were in-hospital mortality and congestive heart failure (CHF). Multivariable logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses were performed to evaluate independent associations and discriminative performance.

Results

Patients who developed CHF or in-hospital mortality exhibited significantly higher SHR and TyG index levels compared with those without adverse outcomes (all p < 0.05). SHR demonstrated a moderate positive correlation with TyG index (r = 0.441, p < 0.001), supporting the interplay between chronic insulin resistance and acute metabolic stress during AMI. For in-hospital mortality, SHR had a numerically higher area under the ROC curve [AUC: 0.823 (95% CI: 0.727-0.920)] than TyG [AUC: 0.714 (95% CI: 0.605-0.824)]; a formal comparison of the AUCs was not performed. At a cut-off value of 1.45, SHR demonstrated 76.5% sensitivity and 80.0% specificity for in-hospital mortality. In the original multivariable model, the SHR group was associated with in-hospital mortality (OR: 9.61, 95% CI: 2.599-35.578; p = 0.001), although the small number of deaths and incomplete adjustment for established clinical prognostic factors limit interpretation.

Conclusions

Among patients with STEMI, both chronic insulin resistance and acute stress-related hyperglycemia were associated with adverse in-hospital outcomes. However, SHR demonstrated superior discriminative capacity and independently predicted mortality, highlighting the dominant prognostic impact of acute metabolic stress during AMI. Integrated assessment of chronic and acute metabolic dysfunction may improve early risk stratification in high-risk myocardial infarction patients.

title: Clinical Outcomes of Invasive Home Mechanical Ventilation in Children With Trisomy 13 and Trisomy 18.
authorString: Kumar E, Green GE, Hassan F, Ramsey AM, Hershenson MB, Saba TG.
abstractText:
Introduction

Trisomy 13 and 18 (T13/18) are rare aneuploidies traditionally associated with severe congenital cardiac, pulmonary, neurologic and other anomalies and high 1-year mortality. Mortality has been improving with greater adoption of life-sustaining interventions including cardiac surgery, tracheostomy and home mechanical ventilation (HMV) but long-term outcomes of invasive HMV in this population is not known. The objective of this study was to evaluate outcomes of invasive HMV in T13/18. We hypothesized longer times to HMV liberation among children with T13/18 (Group 1) compared to other children on invasive HMV (Group 2, trisomy 21; Group 3, tracheo-bronchomalacia without aneuploidy; Group 4, all other causes of respiratory failure without aneuploidy).

Methods

This was a retrospective, descriptive, observational study of electronic medical records. Median duration of mechanical ventilation was compared using non parametric tests.

Results

Among 20 patients with T13/18 initiated on invasive HMV, 5 were liberated (25%). All patients liberated also underwent cardiac surgery and gastrostomy tube placement. A greater proportion of patients in Group 2 (68%), Group 3 (66%) and Group 4 (41%) were liberated from HMV. Among patients liberated from invasive HMV in all 4 groups, there was no significant difference in the median duration, in months (IQR), of invasive HMV: Group 1, 25 (15.5-41.5); Group 2, 23 (14-31); Group 3, 21 (16.25-27.75); Group 4, 19 (13-37.5); p = 0.928. Failed liberation from HMV in patients with T13/18 was attributed to additional comorbidities including seizures and gastrointestinal disease.

Conclusion

Although the proportion of children with T13/18 liberated from HMV was lower than other groups, the duration of HMV among those who were liberated was comparable to that of children without T13/18, when accompanied by other life-sustaining interventions.

title: Anterior mitral leaflet modification to prevent left ventricular outflow tract obstruction during transcatheter mitral valve replacement: the PROTECT-LVOT registry.
authorString: Ruberti A, Praz F, Martí G, De Backer O, Amat-Santos I, Estevez-Loureiro R, Garot P, Rudolph V, Sabaté M, Echarte-Morales J, Roura G, Comin J, Gercek M, Muntané-Carol G, Gómez-Lara J, Occhipinti G, Basile M, Gomez-Hospital JA, Angellotti D, Akodad M, Regazzoli D, Martin P, Moreno R, Regueiro A, Romaguera R.

journal.title: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology

abstractText:
Background

Left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction remains the major limitation of transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR). Anterior mitral leaflet (AML) modification has emerged as a key preventive strategy, yet real-world data remain limited and residual risk is still unknown.

Aims

We sought to evaluate the outcomes of TMVR with concomitant AML modification across valve-in-mitral annular calcification (ViMAC), valve-in-ring (ViR), and valve-in-valve (ViV) substrates.

Methods

We established a multicentre retrospective registry of consecutive patients undergoing TMVR with AML modification between 2017 and 2025. The co-primary in-hospital safety endpoint was a composite of cardiovascular death, stroke/transient ischaemic attack, and major bleeding.

Results

A total of 55 patients were included (67% females). The median age was 78 years (interquartile range [IQR] 73-81); the median Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality was 6.7% (IQR 4.8-9.5). AML modification was performed in 65.5% of cases with the Laceration of the Anterior Mitral leaflet to Prevent Outflow ObstructioN technique and in 34.5% with the Balloon-Assisted Translocation of the Mitral Anterior Leaflet technique. AML modification was successful in 96.4% of cases. Despite successful AML modification, haemodynamically significant LVOT obstruction occurred in 12.7% of cases. The co-primary in-hospital safety endpoint occurred in 20.0% of patients, driven by cardiovascular death in 14.5% of patients. Overall in-hospital mortality was 16.4%. The ViMAC substrate was associated with the numerically highest LVOT obstruction rate (ViMAC 20.7%, ViR 0.0%, ViV 8.3%, odds ratio [OR] 4.72, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.89-47.86; p=0.070). The aortomitral angle showed a borderline association with LVOT obstruction (OR 1.22 per degree, 95% CI: 0.99-1.48; p=0.059).

Conclusions

AML modification enables TMVR in high-risk anatomies with high feasibility but does not eliminate LVOT obstruction. ViMAC represents the most challenging substrate.

title: Three-year outcomes of balloon-expandable valve-in-valve aortic valve implantation for failed transcatheter versus surgical valves.
authorString: Shitan H, Patel V, Suruga K, Guo Y, Nagasaka T, Ng M, Buss E, Gandhi N, Ng D, Patel D, Menda J, Gupta A, Chakravarty T, Cheng W, Okada Y, Jilaihawi H, Nakamura M, Makkar RR.

journal.title: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology

abstractText:
Background

Clinical outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve (TAV)-in-TAV compared with TAV-in-surgical aortic valve (SAV) implantation for failed bioprosthetic valves have been limited to short-term outcomes.

Aims

This study compared midterm outcomes between patients undergoing TAV-in-TAV and those undergoing TAV-in-SAV.

Methods

From June 2015 to June 2024, 543 consecutive patients undergoing valve-in-valve (ViV) transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) were identified at our centre. After exclusion of ineligible patients, 109 patients undergoing TAV-in-TAV and 349 undergoing TAV-in-SAV were included. Following propensity score matching, 214 patients (107 per group) were analysed.

Results

Three-year all-cause mortality did not differ between the TAV-in-TAV and TAV-in-SAV groups (hazard ratio 1.06, 95% confidence interval: 0.56-1.98; p=0.867). Similarly, no significant differences were detected in secondary outcomes. Over 3 years, the aortic valve mean pressure gradient was consistently lower and the aortic valve area was consistently larger in the TAV-in-TAV group compared with the TAV-in-SAV group. Concomitant percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) and coronary obstruction were more frequent in the TAV-in-SAV group than in the TAV-in-TAV group (22.4% vs 8.4%; p=0.006; 10.3% vs 0.9%; p=0.018, respectively). Post-ViV-TAVI computed tomography analysis showed that the waist level was the least expanded segment in both groups. However, expansion at this level was significantly greater in the TAV-in-TAV group than in the TAV-in-SAV group.

Conclusions

There was no significant difference in 3-year mortality between the TAV-in-TAV and TAV-in-SAV groups. However, TAV-in-SAV was associated with higher rates of concomitant PCI and coronary obstruction, as well as lower valve expansion.

title: Early outcomes of tricuspid valve replacement in patients with tricuspid regurgitation: the Trisol Early Feasibility Study.
authorString:
Yadav P, Goel K, Thourani V, Lim DS, Makkar R, Ascione G, Kodali S, Saxon J, Barker C, Stewart J, Rajagopal V, Sayegh H, Pretorius M, Vaturi M, Leon MB, George I, 
                    on behalf of the Trisol investigators
                .

journal.title: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology

abstractText:
Background

Transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR) could lead to a paradigm shift in treating tricuspid regurgitation (TR) and improving patient quality of life.

Aims

We aimed to report the 30-day outcomes of the Trisol Early Feasibility Study (EFS).

Methods

The Trisol EFS was a single-arm, multicentre study that enrolled patients with symptomatic ≥severe TR despite optimal medical therapy to undergo TTVR with the Trisol system via transjugular access. The primary safety endpoint was the rate of device-related serious adverse events, including death, myocardial infarction, disabling stroke, life-threatening bleeding, renal failure requiring dialysis, and the need for surgery. The primary performance endpoints included technical and procedural success, while secondary endpoints included echocardiographic as well as functional and quality-of-life measures.

Results

A total of 19 patients, who were treated with a latest-generation Trisol 12-anchor valve, were included from August 2023 to September 2025. The mean age was 75.8 years (range 62 to 91), 78.9% were female, and 78.9% were in New York Heart Association (NYHA) Class III or IV. TR was reduced to mild or less in 87.5% of the subjects and moderate or less in 100% of the subjects. The 30-day composite major adverse event rate was 10.5% (2/19) due to one cardiovascular death and one pacemaker implantation. No other complications were observed. NYHA Class significantly improved to Class I/II (87.5%), and the Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire score improved by a mean of 13.6±34.6 points.

Conclusions

In this early clinical experience, the Trisol TTVR system demonstrated technical feasibility, overall safety, significant TR reduction, and the ability to improve quality of life and functional status in TR patients.

title: Transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement after failed edge-to-edge repair.
authorString: Besler C, Bartko PE, De Marco F, Costa M, Geisler T, Frerker C, Adam M, Ruf T, Kister T, Toggweiler S, Mehrkens D, Paiva L, Jantsch C, Seidler T, Deharo P, Campante Teles R, Rebeiras R, Voss F, Wild MG, Tarkhnishvili A, Le Ruz R, Lurz P, Westermann D, Polzin A.

journal.title: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology

abstractText:
Background

Residual or recurrent tricuspid regurgitation (TR) after transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) is a growing concern in clinical practice and is associated with inferior outcomes.

Aims

We sought to evaluate the early experience of transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR) in patients with failed TEER.

Methods

This multicentre, retrospective cohort study included patients undergoing TTVR for recurrent or residual severe TR after TEER. Clinical, echocardiographic, and computed tomography findings were evaluated. The primary outcome was clinical success at 30 days after TTVR.

Results

Of the 28 patients included (age 78.5±6.3 years, 61% female), 20 (72%) had residual TR and 8 (28%) had recurrent TR diagnosed within a median of 182 days after TEER. Patients were severely symptomatic (New York Heart Association [NYHA] III/IV in 97%), and 64% had massive/torrential TR. In 6 patients (21%), a commissural TEER device was evident, enabling direct TTVR (neocommissure strategy). Engagement of TEER devices with single leaflet device attachment during TTVR was carried out in 12 patients (43%), and electrosurgical laceration and stabilisation to facilitate TTVR in 10 patients (36%). Clinical success at 30 days was 93%. NYHA Functional Class improved in 93% of patients, with 85% being in NYHA I/II at 1 month after TTVR. Two patients died from non-cardiac reasons, and during a median follow-up of 69 days, 4 patients suffered a heart failure hospitalisation despite procedural success.

Conclusions

In this small patient cohort, three different TTVR strategies after failed TEER resulted in significant clinical success at 30 days and led to substantial symptom relief during short-term follow-up.

title: Acute right ventricular response to transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement.
authorString: Herrera-Flores C, Rosch S, Wolff C, Passoke F, Schöber A, Bombace S, Herrera-Flores J, Schlotter F, Ruf T, von Bardeleben RS, Rommel KP, Thiele H, Kister T, Emrich T, Lurz P, Cruz-Gonzalez I, Kresoja KP.

journal.title: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology

abstractText:
Background

Changes in right ventricular (RV) function are frequent after transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR), yet their mechanisms and prognostic implications remain incompletely defined.

Aims

We sought to characterise acute RV functional changes following TTVR and evaluate their prognostic impact.

Methods

This multicentre study included consecutive patients treated with TTVR between 2019 and 2025 with complete imaging data. RV function was assessed by echocardiography at baseline, intraprocedurally, and before discharge. RV end-systolic elastance (Ees), effective arterial elastance (Ea), and RV-pulmonary artery coupling (Ees/Ea) were derived from non-invasive single-beat pressure-volume loop analysis. Changes over time were assessed using paired tests, and associations with mortality were investigated using Cox regression analysis with Firth's penalised likelihood.

Results

Sixty-seven patients (median age 78 years; 72% female; EVOQUE n=49; LuX-Valve Plus n=18) were included. At discharge, both cohorts showed declines in absolute RV free-wall longitudinal strain (aRV-FWLS; -10.4%; p<0.001 for EVOQUE; -10.4%; p=0.001 for LuX-Valve Plus) and fractional area change (FAC; -18.0%; p<0.001 for EVOQUE; -13.5%; p=0.005 for LuX-Valve Plus). Overall, 58% of patients met the criteria for severe RV dysfunction after TTVR. Over a median follow-up of 19 months, 15 patients died. Device type, acute RV functional changes, Ees, and Ees/Ea were not associated with mortality (allp>0.05). In contrast, computed tomography-derived RV coupling (hazard ratio [HR] 0.02, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.01-0.89) and the coexistence of baseline longitudinal (tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion <17 mm and/or aRV-FWLS <23%) and circumferential (RV-FAC ≤35%) RV dysfunction (HR 3.93, 95% CI: 1.10-14.47) were associated with mortality.

Conclusions

TTVR is associated with an acute decline in RV systolic function. Although common, early postprocedural RV dysfunction was not associated with midterm mortality.

title: Percutaneous Closure of Unroofed Coronary Sinus: A Novel Approach.
authorString: Giannico MB, Giugno L, Pagliaroli E, Vaccarella M, Gasparotti E, Capellini K, Celi S, Carotti A, Gaspardone A, Santoro G.
abstractText:
Background

Unroofed coronary sinus (CS) is a rare cause of left-to-right shunting and right-sided volume overload. Transcatheter treatment is feasible only in selected anatomies.

Case summary

A 48-year-old woman with prior congenital heart surgery presented with acute heart failure and massive pleural effusion. Multimodality evaluation, including cardiac magnetic resonance and cardiac catheterization, diagnosed an unroofed CS with a significant left-to-right shunt. At the heart team evaluation, a percutaneous approach was planned because the patient refused surgery. However, because of the large size and unfavorable morphology of the defect, direct closure was deemed unfeasible. Thus, after confirmation of the tolerability of the procedure by a temporary balloon occlusion test, closure of the CS ostium into the right atrium was performed. At 5-month follow-up, no residual shunt was detected, pulmonary pressure improved, and functional capacity was preserved without exercise-induced desaturation.

Discussion

This case highlights the importance of individualized, anatomy-driven percutaneous strategies in complex congenital heart disease.

Take-home messages

CS ostial occlusion may provide a feasible percutaneous option when conventional closure is anatomically unsuitable. Three-dimensional preprocedural simulation, multimodality imaging, and temporary balloon occlusion are key to procedural planning and safety assessment.

title: Childhood Immunization Schedule for National Immunization Program Vaccines, China (Version 2026).
authorString: Administration NDCAP, China NHCOTPRO.
abstractText: In June 2026, the National Disease Control and Prevention Administration and the National Health Commission issued the Childhood Immunization Schedule for National Immunization Program Vaccines (Version 2026). Compared with the 2021 version, the key updates include optimization of the five-dose Diphtheria-Tetanus-acellular Pertussis vaccine schedule (with the first dose advanced to 2 months of age and the fifth dose administered at 6 years of age); inclusion of the bivalent human papillomavirus vaccine in the National Immunization Program as a two-dose series for girls aged 13 years (Table 1); and expanded and refined vaccination guidance for children with medical conditions, including preterm and low-birthweight infants, children with allergies, children born to mothers living with human immunodeficiency virus, children with immune function abnormalities, jaundice, common congenital diseases, or common neurological diseases, and children receiving blood products. This English translation provides a reference for public health professionals.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Echocardiographic Platform for Automated Measurements in Children.
authorString: Chan KL, Ho SC, Ho JP, Chan YY, Wong WH, Cheung YF.
abstractText:
Purpose

This study assessed the accuracy of a novel artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted echocardiographic platform for automated measurements in children.

Methods

In this prospective, blinded, comparative, single-center pilot study, transthoracic echocardiography was performed in pediatric subjects aged 5 to 18 years using the Siemens Acuson Origin cardiovascular ultrasound system. For spectral Doppler assessments, two echocardiographic acquisitions were required: one using the AI-assisted protocol with automatic spectral Doppler marker placement, and one with manual marker placement. For all other analyses, a single manual acquisition was required for subsequent AI and manual assessments. Images were initially analyzed with the AI-assisted protocol, followed immediately by manual evaluation by a pediatric cardiologist blinded to the AI-derived results. Indices included B-mode, M-mode, Doppler, speckle tracking, and four-dimensional (4D) parameters. Agreement between AI-assisted and manual measurements was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) and Bland-Altman analysis.

Results

Thirty subjects (23 males; age 12.2±3.8 years) were studied, including 23 with structurally normal heart, six with congenital heart diseases, and one with dilated cardiomyopathy. Feasibility exceeded 90% for 2D AI-assisted assessment and 80% for 4D ventricular volumetry, but was below 35% for 4D atrial volumetry. Agreement between AI-assisted and manual measurements was strong for all parameters except septal (ICC 0.2) and left ventricular posterior wall thickness (ICC 0.5). Bland-Altman analysis showed no significant systematic differences.

Conclusion

Our pilot findings suggest that a commercially available AI-assisted echocardiographic system may be feasible and reasonably accurate for conventional and advanced quantitative echocardiographic assessment for children in a real-world setting.

title: A Dual Molecular Diagnosis of Sotos Syndrome and KBG Syndrome in a Six-Year-Old Girl With a Blended Phenotype.
authorString: Nishi E, Yanagi K, Matsuda K, Kaname T, Okamoto N.
abstractText:
Background

Dual molecular diagnoses involving pathogenic variants in multiple disease-associated genes are increasingly recognized with the widespread use of genome-wide sequencing; however, their clinical presentation and diagnostic challenges remain incompletely understood. We report a patient with a dual molecular diagnosis of Sotos syndrome and KBG syndrome.

Methods

Trio-based genome sequencing was performed in a six-year-old girl with global developmental delay and nonspecific clinical features. Variants were interpreted according to ACMG/AMP guidelines.

Results

The patient showed global developmental delay, intellectual disability (developmental quotient 53 at 5 years 10 months), hyperactivity, impulsivity, and sensory hypersensitivity. Growth was near average with delayed bone age. Hallmark features of both syndromes were attenuated or absent, and neither syndrome was clinically suspected. Genome sequencing identified de novo heterozygous pathogenic variants in NSD1 and ANKRD11. Intellectual disability severity was within the reported range for each syndrome.

Conclusion

This co-occurrence demonstrates that blended phenotypes may obscure diagnostic features, emphasizing the importance of comprehensive genomic testing and integrated clinical management, including genetic counseling, in atypical presentations.

title: CN-RNN: a deep learning framework for copy number variants detection with exome sequencing data.
authorString: Wang D, Qin F, Bao W, Bacher R, Chung D, Lu Q, Efron PA, Cai G, Xiao F.
abstractText: Copy number variations (CNVs) are major structural genomic variants that contribute to a wide range of human diseases. Accurate CNV detection from whole-exome sequencing (WES) data remains challenging because existing callers often exhibit high false-positive rates and limited sensitivity for short CNVs. Moreover, current deep learning approaches do not fully integrate the complementary information provided by local read-depth patterns and region-level genomic features. Here we present CN-RNN, a two-stage framework that combines high-sensitivity candidate generation with deep learning-based candidate classification. The framework integrates a bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) branch, which captures local depth changes and contextual dependencies across neighboring exons, with a parallel multi-layer perceptron (MLP) branch that incorporates region-level features including GC content, mappability, and exon length. The model was trained using parent-offspring trios from the Autism Sequencing Consortium (ASC), with training labels constructed through Mendelian inheritance filtering. In internal validation and evaluation with two independent external datasets constructed using distinct reference sets, CN-RNN consistently outperformed existing WES-based CNV callers and deep learning methods. These results demonstrate that integrating sequential read-depth patterns with region-level genomic features improves the accuracy and generalizability of CNV detection from WES data. CN-RNN provides a scalable tool for CNV profiling in population and clinical sequencing studies and is available at https://github.com/FeifeiXiao-lab/CN-RNN.

title: From Autoantigens to GlycoRNAs: The Prehistory of RNA at the Cell Surface.
authorString: Wittmann J.

journal.title: BioEssays : news and reviews in molecular, cellular and developmental biology

abstractText: The discovery of glycoRNAs in 2021 transformed the study of cell-surface biology, but it did not emerge from a vacuum. A substantial, though heterogeneous, body of evidence accumulated over four decades, suggesting that several nuclear and cytoplasmic RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) can access the outer plasma membrane under defined biological conditions. This historical perspective traces that development from the earliest hints in 1981, through the founding observations of 1989-1990 when La/SSB, nucleolin, and Ku70 were independently detected at the cell surface, to the consolidation period of 1990-1995 that connected surface-expressed RNP autoantigens to neonatal lupus and photosensitive cutaneous lupus, and finally to the glycoRNA era beginning in 2021. Throughout, early researchers working with limited tools identified the key phenomenon: surface-expressed nuclear RBPs as potential autoimmune triggers. They articulated the core hypothesis that modern glycoRNA biology is now positioned to test.

title: Situs Inversus Totalis with Mirror-Image Dextrocardia and Acute Type A Aortic Dissection Treated by Ascending Aorta Replacement Plus Total Arch Replacement and Frozen Elephant Trunk Using an Inverted Four-Branched Graft: A Case Report.
authorString: He L, Zhang Z, Tang T.
abstractText: Situs inversus totalis (SIT) is a rare congenital condition characterized by a complete mirror-image reversal of the thoracic and abdominal viscera, usually accompanied by dextrocardia. Acute type A aortic dissection (AAD) is a highly lethal cardiovascular emergency, and its coexistence with SIT is exceedingly rare. To the best of our knowledge, apart from a recently reported pregnant patient, no case of AAD in a non-pregnant adult with SIT has been treated with ascending aorta replacement combined with total arch replacement (TAR) and frozen elephant trunk (FET) implantation. In this report, we present such a case and share our surgical experience, particularly the inverted four-branched graft technique used to resolve the mismatch between the commercially available graft and the mirrored anatomy. The postoperative course was complicated by right renal malperfusion and stage 2 acute kidney injury. Overall renal function recovered with conservative management, although the right kidney subsequently became atrophic; otherwise, recovery was satisfactory. Computed tomographic angiography (CTA) at 10 months showed the graft and all reconstructed branches patent and the FET in position without endoleak, and the patient remained in good condition at the telephone follow-up approximately 3 years after surgery.

title: PCSK6 in Pathophysiology and Its Potential Involvement in Pulmonary Fibrosis.
authorString: Tian Q, Spek CA, Duitman JW.
abstractText: Proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 6 (PCSK6) is a proteolytic enzyme that may act on a broad spectrum of substrates, including growth factors, extracellular proteases, adhesion molecules, protease activated receptor 1, the prorenin receptor, and Corin. As a consequence of its broad-spectrum substrate activity, PCSK6 is implicated in a wide range of pathophysiological processes such as cardiovascular disease, neurological disorders, arthritis and cancer. Of special interest, PCSK6 has recently been shown to be highly expressed in patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) and PCSK6 has been associated with reduced survival of IPF patients, linking PCSK6 to pulmonary fibrosis for the first time. Of note however, PCSK6 levels in plasma were not associated with respiratory outcomes in IPF patients and higher PCSK6 levels were even associated with a lower hazard of 10% FVC decline in non-IPF ILD patients. In this review, we summarize the molecular biology of PCSK6, including its structural features and its major (potential) substrates, and outline its pathophysiological roles across various diseases. Furthermore, we propose and discuss the potential involvement of PCSK6 in pulmonary fibrosis to guide future research.

title: FetalSegNet: Automatic Segmentation of the Fetus and Sub-Anatomical Structures in Prenatal Ultrasound Images Using Hybrid Deep Learning Models.
authorString: Özsoy HGT, Urtekin EN, Urfalı FE, Aydın GA, Bekirçavuşoğlu AF, Dandıl E.
abstractText: Background/Objectives: Automatic segmentation of fetal anatomical structures in prenatal ultrasound images is challenging because of low tissue contrast, noise caused by speckles, anatomical variability and the fact that structures are only partially visible within individual image frames. This study has developed and evaluated FetalSegNet, a multi-label deep learning framework that can simultaneously perform segmentation of the fetus and selected sub-anatomical structures, including the head, arms, legs and heart. Methods: A dataset comprising 3321 prenatal ultrasound images obtained from 217 patients was created, with pixel-level annotations generated under expert supervision. FetalSegNet was implemented using four hybrid encoder-decoder configurations that combine EfficientNetV2-M and MaxViT-S encoders with UNet++ and Feature Pyramid Network (FPN) decoders. Performance was evaluated on an unseen test set using Dice score, intersection over union (IoU), precision, recall, 95th percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95) and average symmetric surface distance (ASSD). The presence of anatomical structures was also assessed using classification metrics, while HiResCAM was used to examine the spatial relevance of model activations. Results: Among the FetalSegNet configurations, the EfficientNetV2-M-UNet++ model achieved the highest overall segmentation performance, with a Dice (DSC) score of 0.9232, IoU of 0.8746, HD95 of 4.23 mm, and ASSD of 1.02 mm. Class-specific results indicated better performance in segmentation for the head and fetus, whereas the leg and heart classes showed comparatively poorer and more inconsistent results. The models also achieved high F1-scores and a high level of accuracy in assessing the presence of anatomical structures. HiResCAM analyses showed that model activations were predominantly concentrated within the corresponding anatomical regions. Conclusions: FetalSegNet provides a unified, multi-label framework for simultaneously segmenting the fetus and multiple sub-anatomical structures in prenatal ultrasound images. By combining a hybrid deep-learning architecture with independent output-mask channels, comprehensive boundary-based evaluation, and activation-based interpretability analysis, the framework offers an integrated strategy for fetal anatomical segmentation. These findings support further investigation of FetalSegNet for automated and interpretable analysis of prenatal ultrasound images.

title: Potential Role of a Rare HCCS Variant Associated With Microphthalmia With Linear Skin Defects and Phenotypic Heterogeneity.
authorString: Zhang L, Zhuang J, Chen Y, Chen W, Huang N.
abstractText:
Background

Pathogenic variants in the HCCS gene have been reported to cause microphthalmia with linear skin defects (MLS). This study reports a rare HCCS variant that co-occurs with a recurrent 2q13 microdeletion in a fetus with multiple congenital malformations, to deepen our understanding of unexplained copy number variants (CNVs).

Methods

A fetus with multiple prenatal ultrasound anomalies, including flat facial profile, anophthalmia, cleft lip and palate, and widened cerebral fissures, was recruited from the Quanzhou region of China. Chromosomal microarray analysis (CMA) was performed to detect chromosomal abnormalities. Trio whole exome sequencing (trio WES) was further conducted to identify additional genetic variants within the family, and candidate variants were validated by Sanger sequencing and/or quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR).

Results

CMA revealed a 482.1 kb microdeletion at 2q13 (arr [GRCh37] 2q13 (110498142_110980295) × 1) encompassing the NPHP1 gene, which was inherited from the clinically unaffected father. Additionally, trio WES identified a heterozygous missense variant NM_005333.5:c.572A>T p.(Glu191Val) in the HCCS gene of the fetus, inherited from the clinically asymptomatic mother. Notably, a 1.56 Mb microdeletion spanning 16p13.11p13.12 was detected in the mother. This deletion covers the recurrent 16p13.11 BP2 to BP3 region, which includes the MYH11 gene, and is classified as a pathogenic CNV.

Conclusion

To our knowledge, this is the first report of the rare HCCS variant NM_005333.5:c.572A>T p.(Glu191Val) combined with a 2q13 microdeletion in a fetus with multiple malformations. Our findings further enhance the diagnostic utility of WES in the etiological investigation of cases with unexplained CNVs.

title: Ageing begins early: developmental origins of ageing trajectories.
authorString: Moldakozhayev A, Eames AW, Mitchell W, Tskhay A, de Magalhães CG, Alba-Linares JJ, Ying K, Zhang B, Zhang S, Iqbal S, Yucel AD, Tyshkovskiy A, Van Raamsdonk JM, Gladyshev VN.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Philos Trans R Soc Lond B Biol Sci
journal.title: Philosophical transactions of the Royal Society of London. Series B, Biological sciences
journal.isoabbreviation: Philos Trans R Soc Lond B Biol Sci

abstractText: Ageing has traditionally been viewed as a process of late-life organismal deterioration, with interventions aimed at slowing ageing being administered after the ageing process has already begun. However, recent advances in quantifying ageing indicate that the process of molecular ageing starts as early as the end of gastrulation. Further, growing evidence suggests that the foundations of how different systems of an organism age are established during prenatal and postnatal development. Herein, we review the impact of early-life environmental conditions on disease susceptibility, adaptation, energy metabolism, microbiome and neurodevelopmental processes to ascertain how changes early in life can affect ageing-related features late in life. We also link growth, reproductive capacity and ageing by providing examples when the balance between longevity and reproduction is shifted towards a longer life through the growth axis at a cost of fecundity across species. We encourage researchers to investigate interventions aimed at mitigating ageing during the developmental period of life, with the important note that such interventions must be assessed with extra caution, given that many life-extending strategies may attenuate growth and reproduction, which may be detrimental for the organism during development. This article is part of the theme issue 'Developmental circuits in ageing'.

title: Right ventricular failure across load and myocardial phenotypes: anatomy, plasticity and therapeutic implications.
authorString: Scelsi L, Greco A, Acquaro M.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Eur Heart J Imaging Methods Pract
journal.title: European heart journal. Imaging methods and practice
journal.isoabbreviation: Eur Heart J Imaging Methods Pract

abstractText: The right ventricle (RV) is a load-dependent chamber whose performance reflects myocardial reserve, loading conditions, and ventricular interdependence. Volume overload, pressure overload, and intrinsic myocardial dysfunction produce distinct, often overlapping remodelling trajectories and therapeutic targets. This review integrated contemporary imaging and prognostic evidence into a mechanism-to-decision framework. Its clinical contribution is to explain how deformation and chamber geometry should be interpreted with regurgitant burden and forward flow in volume overload, vascular load and coupling in pressure overload, and regional motion and tissue injury in intrinsic disease. Echocardiography combines these measurements with valve assessment, pulmonary outflow Doppler, left-heart filling phenotype and systemic venous congestion. Cardiovascular magnetic resonance, computed tomography, right heart catheterization and stress testing resolve selected anatomical or physiological uncertainty. Automated measurements can support serial phenotyping but require image and contour review. Reverse remodelling describes favourable structural change; meaningful recovery additionally requires preserved or restored effective forward performance and improvement in clinical or venous consequences after treatment of the causal load, lesion or myocardial substrate. This framework helps recognize discordant findings, select further assessment and judge treatment response without equating a single load-dependent index with myocardial recovery.

title: Machine learning models for predicting plastic bronchitis in hospitalized children with <i>Mycoplasma pneumoniae</i> pneumonia undergoing clinically indicated bronchoscopy: a single-center retrospective study.
authorString: Yu S, Li Y, Liu Q, Xue Z, Gao Y, Yang Y, Li Y.
abstractText:
Objective

To develop and compare multiple machine learning models for predicting the risk of plastic bronchitis (PB) in children with Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia (MPP) and to establish an interpretable early risk identification tool.

Methods

A retrospective study was conducted involving 702 hospitalized children with MPP (477 non-PB and 225 PB) admitted to the Affiliated Hospital of Yan'an University from January 2023 to January 2026. Clinical characteristics, laboratory findings, and imaging data were collected. Key predictors were identified using a two-stage Lasso-Boruta approach. The dataset was randomly divided into training and test sets at a ratio of 7:3. Eight machine learning models, including CatBoost, XGBoost, LightGBM, Random Forest, Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine, Gaussian Naive Bayes, and K-Nearest Neighbors, were developed. Hyperparameters were optimized using five-fold stratified cross-validation with grid search or random search based on the F1 score. Model performance was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, calibration, and decision curve analysis. SHAP analysis was applied for model interpretation. Temporal validation and bootstrap optimism correction were further performed to assess temporal generalizability and optimism in model performance.

Results

The Lasso-Boruta approach identified nine PB-related predictors, including fever duration, peak temperature, WBC, CRP, ALB, LDH, FDP, D-dimer, and pulmonary consolidation. All eight models demonstrated predictive capability in the test set, with ROC-AUC values ranging from 0.854 to 0.881. RF achieved an accuracy of 0.853, precision of 0.804, recall of 0.721, F1 score of 0.759, and ROC-AUC of 0.881, whereas CatBoost achieved an accuracy of 0.853, precision of 0.793, recall of 0.736, F1 score of 0.762, and ROC-AUC of 0.871. In temporal validation, RF achieved the highest accuracy (0.925) and F1 score (0.900), whereas CatBoost achieved the highest ROC-AUC (0.970) and PR-AUC (0.956). Considering the complementary performance profiles across different evaluation dimensions and the results of bootstrap optimism correction, RF and CatBoost were retained as candidate models for further interpretation and risk prediction tool development. SHAP analysis provided individual-level explanations of the contributions of the selected predictors to PB risk.

Conclusions

Machine learning models based on clinical manifestations, laboratory indicators, and imaging features showed potential for PB risk identification in children with MPP. RF and CatBoost exhibited complementary predictive strengths across different evaluation dimensions, while SHAP analysis facilitated individual-level interpretation. Further multicenter external validation is required.

title: Nonischemic and normothermic beating cardiac xenotransplantation.
authorString: Wolbrom DH, Matsumura N, Moroi MK, Chauhan I, Fujiwara S, Qudus S, Brewer M, Ekanayake-Alper D, Hajosi D, Schweitzer L, Takeda K, Levy RJ, Juergensen SM, Barry O, Sekulic M, Sachs DH, Sykes M, Nowak G, Goldstone AB.
abstractText: Cardiac xenotransplantation-the transplantation of a heart from one species to another- offers a clinically viable solution to the organ shortage problem. Despite significant advances in genetic engineering technologies and new immunosuppressive medications such as co-stimulatory blockade, bringing cardiac xenotransplantation to the clinic still has several challenges. Perioperative cardiac xenograft dysfunction is a major limitation to long-term xenograft survival and is attributed to the ischemia-reperfusion damage associated with the procurement and transplant of the porcine heart. This dysfunction can be reduced by utilizing commercial ex vivo perfusion devices which limit the cold ischemia time. Unfortunately, these devices still require an obligatory ischemic period during the initial arrest with cardioplegia and subsequent explanting of the organ, and then again during the implantation of the heart. These commercial devices also do not support smaller pediatric sized hearts, reducing the pool of recipients eligible for xenografts. We sought to establish a novel method of explanting and orthotopically implanting beating donor hearts from genetically modified pigs without any ischemia, while maintaining normothermic perfusion in a pig-to-nonhuman primate model. Eliminating cold and warm ischemia has never previously been achieved in cardiac xenotransplantation and has important implications for bringing it to the clinic, as well as broader translatability in allotransplantation. We performed a proof-of-concept experiment utilizing our novel technique in a non-survival model and then performed a successful experiment with nearly 8 weeks of survival of a single GGTA1 knockout pig heart. Our initial data suggest that utilization of a normothermic coronary perfusion circuit in cardiac xenotransplantation is feasible and safe and may be a plausible method towards achieving survival.

title: Four-dimensional left atrial quantification for predicting major adverse cardiovascular events in patients with uremia: an interpretable LASSO-logistic model.
authorString: Ma L, Jin M, Lin Z, Cui R, Huang X, Chen M.
abstractText:
Background

This study aimed to develop a machine learning model using four-dimensional left atrial quantification (4D-LAQ) parameters to the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in patients with uremia.

Methods

A total of 223 patients with uremia treated at the Second Affiliated Hospital of Hainan Medical University between January 2021 and January 2026 were retrospectively enrolled and followed up for the occurrence of MACE. LASSO regression was utilized for feature selection, followed by the development of eight prediction models. Logistic regression (LR) was identified as the final algorithm based on DeLong's test. A nomogram was constructed, and Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) analysis was performed to enhance model interpretability. Model performance was comprehensively evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration plots, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Intra- and inter-observer reproducibility were assessed using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC).

Results

During the follow-up period, 94 patients (42.1%) developed MACE. The MACE group exhibited left ventricular remodeling, mainly characterized by left atrial volume enlargement and a decrease in strain. The LR model achieved an AUC of 0.840 (95% CI: 0.749-0.931) in the validation set. Multiple validation approaches, including five-fold cross-validation, nested 5×5 cross-validation, and bootstrap internal validation, yielded AUCs of 0.873, 0.856, and 0.869, respectively. The calibration analysis showed good consistency (Hosmer-Lemeshow test, P > 0.05). The AUC of DCA (AUDC) was 0.208 (0.206 - 0.208), and the maximum net benefit was 0.43. The optimal risk stratification threshold, determined by the maximum Youden index in the training set, was 0.41. SHAP analysis identified left atrial reservoir strain (LASr) as the most influential predictive feature in this cohort.

Conclusion

The LASSO-LR model integrating 4D-LAQ parameters may help MACE risk in patients with uremia, with LASr emerging as an important predictor.

title: Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest as the First Manifestation of ALCAPA in a 9-Week-Old Infant: Survival to Discharge After Emergency Repair and VA-ECMO.
authorString: Wróbel G, Gruszka J, Lewitowicz P, Adamczyk-Gruszka O.
abstractText: Background and Clinical Significance: Anomalous origin of the left coronary artery from the pulmonary artery (ALCAPA) usually presents with heart failure at 2-3 months of age; cardiac arrest as the first manifestation is rare and often recognized only at autopsy. Case Presentation: A previously healthy girl collapsed at home at 65 days of age. After dispatcher-assisted parental resuscitation, the emergency team found asystole and achieved return of spontaneous circulation after approximately 4 min of professional resuscitation; the total low-flow time was not recorded. She was in cardiogenic shock (left ventricular ejection fraction 19.8%, high-sensitivity troponin T 2620 ng/L) with acute kidney injury and coagulopathy consistent with disseminated intravascular coagulation. Echocardiography showed a dilated right coronary artery and no flow from the aorta into the left coronary artery. Emergency repair on day 1 was followed by venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) for 4 days and continuous renal replacement therapy. The Simpson ejection fraction reached about 50% by day 9, fell to 37-40% during respiratory deterioration and was 45-50% on day 27; mitral regurgitation, graded as massive during VA-ECMO, regressed to trace without valve surgery. She was discharged on day 42 with impaired diastolic indices; no formal neurological assessment was documented. Conclusions: ALCAPA should be considered in every infant with unexplained cardiac arrest, and post-resuscitation echocardiography should assess the coronary origins. Emergency repair with VA-ECMO can achieve survival to discharge despite multiorgan failure, but long-term cardiac and neurodevelopmental follow-up is required.

title: Proteomic profiling of non-ischemic myocardium following acute mechanical cardiac unloading in ischemic heart failure.
authorString: Mavropoulos SA, Kho C, Fava M, Lee A, Leonard K, Veera S, Sakata T, Mazurek R, Ravichandran AJ, Marx JM, Yin X, Mayr M, Ishikawa K.

journal.title: Journal of molecular and cellular cardiology plus

abstractText:
Background

The cardiac proteome responds to various physiological and pathological stimuli. While acute left ventricle (LV) unloading by catheter-based LV assist device is now a therapeutic option for heart failure, its impact on cardiac proteins is unknown. We sought to characterize proteomic remodeling associated with altered LV load in ischemic heart failure.

Methods

Sixteen Yorkshire pigs underwent myocardial infarction (MI) and were subjected one week later to either 2-hour acute mechanical LV unloading (n = 6), 2-hour LV overloading with mechanically-induced acute aortic regurgitation (n = 4), or no load interventions (n = 6). Non-ischemic remote myocardium was processed for proteomics. Age-matched naïve pigs (n = 6) served as reference. Protein abundance was analyzed using four-group LIMMA moderated ANOVA and pairwise LIMMA moderated t-tests. These were followed by functional enrichment and STRING functional association network analysis of ANOVA-significant proteins together with exploratory screening for load-associated candidates.

Results

A total of 1713 proteins were identified, of which 1552 were included in the statistical analysis, and 7 remained significant after multiple-testing correction. Pairwise analyses revealed that significant protein-level differences were predominantly observed between the MI and Sham groups, whereas protein changes in response to 2-h of acutely altered LV load were limited. An exploratory screening identified six load-associated candidate proteins, with ITIH1 and MYOZ2 selected as representative candidates. Independent human transcriptomic analysis suggested disease-related context of these candidates.

Conclusions

Proteomic remodeling of the non-ischemic remote myocardium in response to acutely altered LV load was less prominent compared to the impact of MI. Exploratory analysis identified LV load-associated candidate proteins.

title: Recurrent pulmonary infection, a vicious cycle of multifactorial interactions, and prevention/treatment strategies.
authorString: Shen C, Li Y, Xiang Z, Zhao M, Wang J, Wang X.
abstractText: Recurrent pulmonary infection (RPI) refers to the frequent and repeated episodes of lower respiratory tract infections. At its core, it represents a vicious cycle arising from the disruption of the homeostatic balance among pathogens, host immunity, and pulmonary architecture. RPI accounts for a considerable proportion of pediatric pneumonia cases, and the cumulative incidence among elderly patients hospitalized for pneumonia is also markedly elevated, imposing a substantial disease burden.
