The etiologies are notably diverse, beyond common pathogens such as bacteria and viruses, the ubiquity of asymptomatic colonization, underlying comorbidities, immune deficiencies, medication-related factors, and aspiration all constitute critical predisposing factors. This review summarizes the pathogenic characteristics of RPI, host-related factors, and the mechanistic roles of structural lung damage in infection recurrence. It further focuses on the current advances and limitations of precision diagnostic approaches (metagenomic sequencing), immunomodulatory and microbiome-targeted interventions, and vaccination strategies. Existing evidence suggests that the clinical benefits of these interventions in RPI remain to be validated by more high-quality studies. The aim of this article is to provide a reference for the clinical management of RPI and to inform future research directions.

title: The developing fetal immune landscape and congenital viral infection.
authorString: Chima SC, Sun SJ, Duell T, Friese S, Sindhu V, Adams Waldorf K.
abstractText: Fetal development is a complex process that can lead to adverse health consequences when impaired, such as congenital anomalies, fetal growth restriction, preterm birth, and stillbirth. Although there is a well-developed literature on the timing of adaptive immune cell appearance in the fetus, comparatively little is known about the ontogeny and functional maturation of the innate immune system over gestation. This knowledge gap limits our understanding of how intrauterine infections influence fetal development and contribute to adverse obstetric and neonatal outcomes. Thus, the goal of this review is to summarize existing knowledge of the ontogeny of the fetal adaptive and innate immune systems throughout gestation, and how they are impacted by infection. We examine the emergence of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells, while highlighting changes in immune lineages across the fetal brain, liver, thymus, bone marrow, spleen, and placenta, which play critical roles in immune competency and tolerance. The role of innate immunity in immunocompetence and pathogen responses is highlighted when known. Finally, we address how vertically transmitted and teratogenic viral infections disrupt normal immune and tissue development. Collectively, these studies demonstrate the dynamic, tissue-specific immune landscape that evolves throughout gestation.

title: Tongue image analysis for early warning of neonatal necrotizing enterocolitis: a translational perspective integrating tongue phenotyping and microbiome dynamics.
authorString: Yang J, Li J, Lv Y, Cai L, Gao W.
abstractText: Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) remains a life-threatening challenge in neonatology, primarily due to the lack of sensitive early biomarkers that precede overt clinical and radiological signs. This Perspective proposes a hypothesis-generating, non-invasive early-warning framework by integrating quantitative tongue image analysis with modern pathophysiological insights. We hypothesize a dynamic association between tongue phenotypic changes (e.g., a transition from pale to purplish color) and the progression of dysbiosis and intestinal microcirculatory disturbance, which correspond to two distinct but potentially complementary pathways. The proposed biological link rests on evidence for the candidate oral-gut microbial relationship, with such evidence derived primarily from adult and non-neonatal studies; gut dysbiosis-known to precede NEC-may be associated with changes in the tongue-coating microbiome, offering a potential remote yet accessible window into intestinal health. We outline a three-phase translational research roadmap: (I) prospective discovery of tongue-image biomarkers and establishment of dynamic baselines for each infant, (II) development of an exploratory machine-learning-based risk prediction model, and (III) mechanistic exploration using multi-omics approaches and animal models. Critically, we propose three testable hypotheses regarding temporal changes in tongue colorimetric and microbial parameters before NEC onset. If prospectively validated, this approach may eventually contribute to a dynamic bedside monitoring tool for NEC risk stratification.

title: Novel cholesterol-high-density lipoprotein-glucose index is associated with 1-year recurrence of atrial fibrillation after catheter ablation.
authorString: Kamili K, Xu S, Li X, Wang D, Gao P, Tian G, Xing H.
abstractText:
Objective

Insulin resistance (IR) plays a pivotal role in the pathogenesis of atrial fibrillation (AF). The novel cholesterol-high-density lipoprotein-glucose (CHG) index, which integrates total cholesterol (TC), high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C), and fasting blood glucose (FBG), has not been validated for predicting AF recurrence following radiofrequency catheter ablation (RFCA). This study aimed to evaluate the association between the CHG index and 1-year AF recurrence after RFCA, and to compare its performance with the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index.

Methods

A retrospective cohort of 813 AF patients who underwent first-time RFCA was enrolled. The primary outcome was any atrial tachyarrhythmia lasting ≥ 30 s after a 3-month blanking period. Cox regression, ROC curve, net reclassification improvement (NRI), and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI) were used to assess predictive performance.

Results

During 1-year follow-up, 142 patients (17.5%) had recurrent atrial tachyarrhythmia, with significantly higher CHG levels in the recurrence group (P < 0.001). Each unit increase in the CHG index was associated with a 4.23-fold higher risk of recurrence (HR = 4.231, 95% CI: 3.406-5.257, P < 0.001). The restricted cubic spline curve shows a dose-response relationship between CHG and AF recurrence. The CHG index yielded an AUC of 0.765, superior to TyG (AUC = 0.673). Adding the CHG index to the traditional risk model significantly improved NRI (0.434, P < 0.001) and IDI (0.200, P < 0.001), with greater improvement than adding the TyG index. Subgroup analyses demonstrated consistent predictive effects across different populations.

Conclusions

The CHG index is an independent risk marker for 1-year recurrence after AF ablation and demonstrates superior discriminative ability compared to the TyG index.

title: Outcomes of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation in critically ill patients with sickle cell disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authorString: Flurin L, Vidal E, Parent T, Rollé A.
abstractText:
Purpose

Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) may be considered as rescue therapy in patients with sickle cell disease (SCD) presenting with life-threatening cardiorespiratory failure, particularly acute chest syndrome (ACS). However, outcomes of ECMO in this population remain poorly defined, especially in adult populations. We aimed to synthesize available evidence on mortality and complications associated with ECMO use in adult and pediatric populations with SCD.

Methods

We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies reporting ECMO use in patients with confirmed SCD. MEDLINE, EMBASE, PubMed, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from January 2000 to January 2025. Risk of bias for included studies was assessed using the ROBINS-I tool. Random-effects meta-analysis of proportions was performed to estimate pooled mortality. Exploratory study-level meta-regression was used to examine associations between mortality and prespecified moderators, including age group, ECMO modality, and ACS as the indication for ECMO.

Results

Seven retrospective studies including 252 patients were included in the meta-analysis. The pooled mortality estimate was 64.5% (95% CI, 39.3-86.0%), with heterogeneity across studies (I² = 80%). Mortality estimates appeared numerically higher in studies including predominantly adult populations, greater use of veno-arterial ECMO, and a higher proportion of patients with ACS at cannulation. Exploratory meta-regression suggested trends toward higher predicted mortality with increasing proportions of adult patients and ACS, and lower mortality with higher proportions of veno-venous ECMO. Reporting of ECMO-related complications was inconsistent, and hemolysis was systematically assessed in only one study.

Discussion

ECMO use in patients with SCD is associated with high mortality, particularly in severe clinical contexts such as ACS. Substantial heterogeneity and methodological limitations preclude firm conclusions. These findings underscore the need for prospective, disease-specific registries to better define patient selection and management strategies.'

title: Beyond Automation: A Conceptual Framework for Medical Responsibility and Human Competencies in AI-Driven Healthcare.
authorString: Tambone V, Campanozzi LL, Di Palma G, Giacomobono F, Refolo P, Oliva A, De Micco F.
abstractText: Background/Objectives: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in clinical reasoning, documentation, prediction, communication, and delegated digital and physical action via agentic and embodied systems. The central ethical challenge is no longer limited to identifying which tasks AI can automate, but determining which human competencies become essential as technological capabilities expand. Methods: This concept paper employs a five-step analysis: technological horizon mapping, selective synthesis of work-transformation evidence, conceptual analysis of medical action, normative synthesis, and medico-legal interpretation. Results: We propose a four-domain framework addressing four core questions of responsible medical action: epistemic (What is true?), normative (What ought to be done?), anthropological-relational (Who is the subject of care?), and systemic-hermeneutic (What does this mean here and now?). Grounded in a conception of technology as augmentative alteration, the framework recognises that technological capabilities can enhance beneficial action but also amplify harm; technological capability alone therefore cannot determine its appropriate use. We also distinguish interpersonal relationships from clinical human-machine interaction, propose professional exigibility as an analytical medico-legal category, and argue that meaningful human oversight requires more than mere human presence. Conclusions: The findings outline key implications for clinical practice, medical education, healthcare organizations, regulation, and a future empirical research agenda focused on human-AI error convergence.

title: An <i>LRRC37A2</i> single nucleotide variant is associated with emphysema in Japanese patients with rheumatoid arthritis.
authorString: Higuchi T, Oka S, Shimada K, Tsunoda S, Ito S, Fujimori M, Nakamura T, Suzuki M, Saisho K, Shinohara S, Matsui T, Migita K, Nagaoka S, Tohma S, Itoh K, Furukawa H.
abstractText:
Objective

Extra-articular manifestations commonly complicate RA and include chronic lung diseases (CLDs), e.g. interstitial lung disease or emphysema (EMP). These confer a poor prognosis. Genetic studies of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) or EMP were conducted. However, there are limited genetic studies on EMP in RA. We examined whether a single nucleotide variant associated with susceptibility to IPF was associated with EMP in Japanese RA patients.

Methods

rs199526 [C/G] genotyping of LRRC37A2 in samples from 88 RA patients with EMP and 425 RA lacking CLD was conducted.

Results

LRRC37A2 rs199526C was significantly associated to EMP in RA according to an allele model [P = 0.0083, odds ratio (OR) 1.72 (95% CI 1.14, 2.59)] or a recessive model for major alleles [P = 0.0139, OR 1.82 (95% CI 1.13, 2.94)], although it was protectively associated against IPF in European populations. Multiple logistic regression analyses revealed an independent association with age, Steinbrocker stage and Steinbrocker class. An association between LRRC37A2 rs199526 and RA per se was detected.

Conclusion

An association between rs199526 and EMP was noted in Japanese RA patients. Differential roles of the single nucleotide variant between EMP in RA and IPF were suggested.

title: Intra-arrest blood pressure monitoring during paediatric in-hospital cardiac arrest: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authorString: Gray J, Christoff A, Nuthall G, Frazier M, Sahai A, Loeb D, Carlisle MA, Acworth J, Rossano J, Topjian A, Cunningham J, Morrison LJ, Scholefield BR.
abstractText:
Aim

To evaluate the use of intra-arrest blood pressure monitoring and association between blood pressure thresholds and outcomes in infants and children.

Methods

A systematic review was performed, registered with PROSPERO (CRD42024590080). We executed the search strategy on MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials all years until April 1, 2026. We used GRADE and the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale to assess the evidence found. Critically important outcomes included return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC), survival to hospital discharge, and survival with favourable neurological outcome, as defined in the Paediatric Core Outcome Set for Cardiac Arrest.

Results

Six studies were included in the final analysis. Two studies (577 events) were pooled. A diastolic blood pressure (DBP) of ≥25 mmHg for infants <1 year and ≥30 mmHg for children 1-≤18 years, averaged over the first ten minutes of CPR, was associated with improved rates of ROSC, survival to hospital discharge, and survival with favourable neurological outcome, with very low certainty of evidence. The analysis did not find a statistically significant association for intra-arrest systolic blood pressure (SBP) thresholds and the described outcomes.

Conclusion

In infants and children with invasive arterial monitoring in place during IHCA, a DBP of ≥25 mmHg (infants) or ≥30 mmHg (children) during the first 10 min of CPR was associated with improved survival and neurological outcome. The evidence is observational and of very low certainty, and does not establish that titrating resuscitation to these thresholds improves outcomes.The protocol for this systematic review was registered as PROSPERO ID CRD42024590080.

title: Duration of Induced Hypothermia After Pediatric Cardiac Arrest: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Kim J, Chung TN.
abstractText: Background/Objectives: Pediatric guidelines retain induced hypothermia as an option, but its optimal duration is uncertain. We compared survival and favorable neurologic outcomes across duration-specific strategies. Methods: Five databases and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched through 20 August 2026. A random-effects network meta-analysis compared 24, 48, and 72 h hypothermia (HT) with heterogeneous Control strategies. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool and the Risk Of Bias In Non-randomized Studies of Interventions tool; certainty was assessed using Confidence in Network Meta-Analysis (CINeMA). Results: Survival included five studies (three randomized, two observational; 785 participants), and neurologic outcomes included four (three randomized, one observational; 615 participants). HT-72 h was associated with higher survival than Control (risk ratio [RR], 2.01; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.24-3.25); 72% of this estimate derived from one observational study measuring 1-month survival, versus 12 months in the randomized 48 h trials. The estimate versus HT-48 h (RR, 1.77; 95% CI, 1.05-2.97) was entirely indirect and depended on merging different Control strategies. The neurologic estimate versus Control (RR, 10.92; 95% CI, 1.32-90.40) depended on a single observational study at serious risk of bias and was extremely imprecise. Superiority over shorter durations was not robust. Certainty for HT-72 h versus Control was very low for both outcomes. Conclusions: Evidence remains compatible with equipoise and does not establish an optimal duration. Funding: No external funding. Registration: Open Science Framework, 10.17605/OSF.IO/9MNDB (retrospective).

title: Effect of lung transplantation on biventricular function in pulmonary arterial hypertension: A systematic review.
authorString: Mohammed AS, Gurram P, Mellacheruvu SP, Lekkala SP, Takagi MA, Kanagala SG, Yasmeen U, Lababidi H, Gandhi ZJ, Mohammed BK, Kambali S, Desai R, Kambali S.
abstractText: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) leads to progressive right ventricular (RV) failure and secondary left ventricular (LV) dysfunction due to chronic pressure overload and ventricular interdependence. Lung transplantation (LTx) is an established treatment for end-stage PAH, yet patterns of biventricular recovery and the role of veno-arterial perioperative extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) remain incompletely defined. A PubMed search identified studies published from 1990 to 2025 using MeSH terms related to lung transplantation, ventricular function, echocardiography, cardiac MRI, and ECMO. Prospective studies, retrospective analyses, and case series evaluating post-transplant cardiac function in PAH were included. A total of 13 studies were included. Across studies, LTx resulted in rapid and substantial RV reverse remodeling, with improvements in RV size, mass, systolic function, tricuspid regurgitation, and pulmonary pressures. This reduction in RV afterload was accompanied by progressive improvement of RV output. In contrast, LV recovery was more variable, possibly due to chronic underfilling and LV remodeling. Cardiac MRI and echocardiography demonstrated progressive biventricular structural and functional adaptation over time. Perioperative VA-ECMO may provide hemodynamic support during this transition by unloading the RV and maintaining perfusion while ventricular loading conditions rapidly change. Lung transplantation for PAH initiates transition from chronic RV pressure overload and LV underfilling to improved pulmonary vascular conditions and subsequent biventricular recovery. Further longitudinal studies are needed to identify predictors of maladaptive LV responses and determine which patients may benefit from prolonged perioperative VA-ECMO support.

title: TFAM Expression, rs1937 Variant, and Mitochondrial DNA Copy Number in Egyptian Myocardial Infarction Patients.
authorString: El Naidany SS, Khader HF, Kenawy AA, Elhelbawy MG, Abouelatta ZAM, Abdelmoneim HA, Aboukhalil RA, Tawfik W, Abouelenin MAH.
abstractText: Myocardial infarction (MI) is a fatal condition that causes damage to the heart muscle by abruptly stopping blood flow and oxygenation. Mitochondrial transcription factor A (TFAM) and mitochondrial DNA copy number (mtDNA CN) show an increased rate of association with development of several human diseases and malignancies. This paper, therefore, aims to identify the possible relation among mtDNA CN and its regulating gene TFAM (expression of the gene and rs1937 polymorphism) as markers in myocardial infarction among Egyptians. A total of 200 participants were enrolled and divided into two groups. Group 1 included 100 myocardial infarction patients with ST-segment elevation (STEMI) recruited from from the Coronary Care Unit (CCU) of Menoufia University Hospitals, while group 2 included 100 Controls. Blood samples were collected from all participants immediately after diagnosis of MI and before beginning therapy. TFAM SNP (rs1937) was determined by the allelic discrimination TaqMan technique, and mtDNA CN and TFAM gene expression were detected using real-time quantitative PCR in 100 MI patients and 100 controls. TFAM mRNA expression and mtDNA copy number were profoundly reduced in MI patients than controls. Analysis of genotype showed that the TFAM rs1937 variant distribution was in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium. The C allele and the GC genotype were substantially more frequent in the patients' cohort (p = 0.006 and 0.005, respectively). The GC genotype of the TFAM polymorphism (rs1937) showed a preliminary association with MI in STEMI patients. Limitations of this study are the absence of longitudinal pre-MI or post-recovery data. TFAM mRNA expression and mtDNA copy number were measured in whole blood without adjustment for leukocyte subpopulations or platelet counts. Small number of C carriers of TFAM rs1937 variant and absence of CC genotype limited statistical power and requires replication in larger Egyptian cohort. These findings suggest that decreased TFAM gene expression and mtDNA CN were significant biomarkers associated with acute myocardial infarction in STEMI patients.

title: Ceramides as Biomarkers of Risk Prediction and Prognosis in Cardiovascular and Other Diseases: Are We There Yet?
authorString: Garikipati T, Dubey P, Work D, Oli S, Sharma DA, Chatterjee S.
abstractText: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death worldwide, yet roughly 70% of major adverse cardiovascular events occur in statin-treated patients with optimized Low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), a gap that cholesterol-based risk panels do not close. Ceramides are bioactive sphingolipids whose plasma species and ratios carry risk information absent from standard lipid panels, and ceramide-based scores (CERT and CERT2) are already in clinical use. Whether this value extends beyond CVD is unclear. We reviewed ceramide species and ratios as biomarkers for disease prediction, prognosis, and disease activity across cardiovascular, metabolic, autoimmune rheumatic, inflammatory bowel, pulmonary, kidney, and oncologic contexts, searching PubMed and Scopus from January 1990 to June 2026 and extending the search for the historical literature. In CVD, CERT and CERT2 predicted cardiovascular events and mortality independently of LDL cholesterol, including in statin-treated and kidney disease populations. In metabolic and autoimmune rheumatic disease, ceramide profiles tracked cardiovascular risk and disease activity. In inflammatory bowel disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and most cancers, the evidence is mechanistically strong but limited to single-cohort or observational studies. Ceramides are emerging biomarkers that complement, not replace, established risk tools. Broader clinical use requires prospective validation, diverse cohorts, standardized assays, and demonstrated cost-effectiveness.

title: Coexistence of a Retroesophageal Aberrant Right Subclavian Artery and a Bicarotid Trunk: A Cadaveric Case Report.
authorString: Tinker B, Thompson K, Gorrell C, Cooper A, Funk S.
abstractText:
Introduction

The major arterial branches of the aortic arch supply blood to the head, neck, and upper extremities. Typically, the brachiocephalic trunk is the first branch, followed by the left common carotid artery and then the left subclavian artery. The current cadaveric case report describes a variation with an aberrant right subclavian artery (ARSA) and a bicarotid trunk (BCT) with a nonrecurrent right inferior laryngeal nerve.

Case presentation

The anterior chest wall of the donor body of a 78-year-old woman was dissected to evaluate the branches of the aortic arch. An ARSA branched from the posterior surface of the aortic arch and coursed to the right, posterior to the trachea and esophagus. A BCT arose from the superior surface and bifurcated into right and left common carotid arteries. A nonrecurrent right inferior laryngeal nerve coursed directly to the larynx from the cervical portion of the right vagus nerve. Structures of interest were measured using a vernier dial caliper.

Conclusion

The presence of an ARSA with a BCT is clinically important because it increases risk for dysphagia and thoracic aortic disease. Better understanding of the characteristics and prevalence of aortic arch branching variations is important for surgeons and radiologists who may encounter an ARSA or BCT in practice. Similarly, a nonrecurrent right inferior laryngeal nerve may be injured during neck procedures. Given these anatomic variants are rare, more studies are necessary to characterize the course and anatomic relationships of these structures.

title: Heart Rate Recovery Index and Pulse Wave Velocity in HFpEF: Exploratory Cutoff Values from a Cross-Sectional Study.
authorString: Suciu BS, Pătru O, Luca S, Faur-Grigori AA, Enache B, Cozma D.
abstractText: Background/Objectives: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) remains challenging to diagnose, and established algorithms such as HFA-PEFF and H2FPEF frequently classify patients within intermediate probability categories requiring additional testing. Arterial stiffness and cardiac autonomic dysfunction are increasingly recognized as relevant components of HFpEF pathophysiology, yet the combined discriminatory value of pulse wave velocity (PWV) and heart rate recovery index (HRRI) has not been well established. This study aimed to evaluate the individual and combined discriminatory performance of PWV and HRRI for HFpEF and to assess their incremental contribution beyond established clinical risk factors. Methods: In this prospective, single-center, cross-sectional study, 180 participants were included, comprising 86 patients with HFpEF and 94 participants without heart failure. Group allocation was clinically assigned by the treating cardiologist with access to PWV and HRRI results. PWV was assessed non-invasively using an oscillometric device, and HRRI was derived from standardized cycle ergometer exercise testing. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, and likelihood-ratio testing were performed to assess independent associations and incremental model contribution. Sensitivity analyses evaluated the influence of age modelling and beta-blocker use. Results: Both PWV and HRRI were independently associated with clinically assigned HFpEF status after adjustment for age, sex, body mass index, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, dyslipidemia, and atrial fibrillation (adjusted OR 1.330 per 1 m/s increase in PWV and 0.857 per 0.1-unit increase in HRRI; both p ≤ 0.023). PWV and HRRI demonstrated AUCs of 0.770 and 0.792, respectively, with Youden index-derived cutoff values of ≥9.60 m/s and ≤1.97. Their combination significantly improved discrimination compared with either marker alone (AUC 0.833). Adding both markers to the clinical model improved model fit, but the AUC increase from 0.865 to 0.896 was not statistically significant after Holm adjustment (adjusted p = 0.132). The associations of both markers with HFpEF remained essentially unchanged after adjustment for beta-blocker therapy. Conclusions: PWV and HRRI were associated with clinically assigned HFpEF status; the observed discrimination does not establish independently validated diagnostic accuracy. Incremental discrimination beyond clinical characteristics and clinical usefulness remain to be established. The cutoff values are exploratory and should not be used as clinical decision thresholds without formal measurement reliability assessment and independent prospective validation.

title: Evaluation of Functional Activity of Ciliated Epithelium in Patients with Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia.
authorString: Kyian T, Demchenko A, Solovova O, Tarasov M, Smirnikhina S, Nazarova A, Bragina E, Ryzhkova O, Kondratyeva E, Kutsev S.
abstractText: Primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) is a heterogeneous recessive disorder of cilia that leads to respiratory tract disorders and organ laterality defects. Objectives: This study was designed to diagnose PCD in patients using various methods: genetic, immunofluorescence, transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and assessment of ciliary beat frequency (CBF) in ALI cultures. Methods: The study included (n = 35) patients with primary ciliary dyskinesia and (n = 10) healthy controls (HC). The diagnosis of PCD was established using molecular genetic analysis: WES, TEM, immunofluorescence staining of ALI-culture, and high-speed videomicroscopy. Ciliogenesis of ciliated epithelial cells was performed in patients with PCD and HC to improve the diagnosis of PCD. Results: Genetic sequencing was conducted for all patients and variants in 17 genes were found. All variants were known. A comparison of CBF assessment in PCD patients and HC using high-speed videomicroscopy showed that the CBF in PCD patient nasal cells was significantly reduced (p < 0.0001), with sensitivity of 91% and specificity of 89.2%. CBF was independent of age and showed no statistical difference between adults and children. Conclusions: The diagnosis of PCD was confirmed in all patients using various diagnostic methods, including the assessment of CBF of ALI culture. The creation of databases of ALI cultures, combined with genotypic and structural abnormalities, is necessary both for diagnosis and, in the future, for use as models in the development of targeted therapies and for assessing their effectiveness.

title: Exercise Reprograms the Epigenetic-Mitochondrial Axis: Mechanisms of Healthy Aging across Muscle, Brain, and Heart.
authorString: Wan Y, He B.
abstractText: Aging manifests as a progressive, multi-hallmark deterioration involving epigenetic dysregulation, mitochondrial impairment, proteostatic collapse, and persistent inflammaging. Accumulating evidence positions habitual physical exercise as one of the most effective non-pharmacological geroprotectors, capable of inducing beneficial, partially reversible epigenetic reprogramming across multiple tissues. This comprehensive review synthesizes current understanding of how different exercise modalitiesendurance, resistance, and high-intensity interval trainingelicit targeted changes in DNA methylation, histone posttranslational modifications, and microRNA (miRNA) networks, collectively restoring mitochondrial biogenesis, dynamics, mitophagy, and redox homeostasis in aging skeletal muscle, brain, and heart. Special emphasis is placed on the dual role of reactive oxygen species (ROS): physiological, exercise-induced ROS pulses function as pivotal redox signals that interface with AMPK-SIRT1-PGC-1α signaling, TET-mediated demethylation, Class IIa HDAC nuclear export, and miRNA maturation, thereby driving adaptive mitochondrial and proteostatic responses rather than oxidative damage. Circulating exerkines and myokines (irisin, IL-6, BDNF, apelin) further orchestrate interorgan communication, linking muscle-derived signals to hippocampal neuroplasticity and cardiac metabolic resilience. Sex-specific epigenetic patterns and differential responsiveness to exercise intensity are highlighted, revealing important sources of individual variability in geroprotective outcomes. By integrating acute versus chronic adaptive signatures and tissue-specific mechanisms, this synthesis underscores exercise as a powerful, systems-level modulator of the epigenetic-mitochondrial axis. These insights pave the way for precision exercise prescriptions and mechanistically informed mimetic strategies aimed at extending healthspan, compressing morbidity, and attenuating major age-related pathologies in heterogeneous aging populations.

title: Psychometric Evaluation of a Cardiac Genetic Knowledge Scale Across Pretest Education Models.
authorString: Christian S, Hover J, Gierl MJ, Kiamanesh O.
abstractText: Accurate assessment of patient knowledge is an essential component of informed decision-making in cardiac genetic testing. An eight-item cardiac genetic knowledge scale was previously developed to support evaluation of informed choice within the Multidimensional Model of Informed Choice, but its psychometric properties have not been formally assessed. Data were pooled from 318 adults with hypertrophic or dilated cardiomyopathy who received pretest education through a genetics webinar (n = 121), cardiologist-led counseling (n = 61), or a prerecorded educational video (n = 136). Exploratory factor analysis (EFA), confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), and two-parameter logistic item response theory (IRT) modeling were used to evaluate factor structure, item performance, and measurement precision. Mean knowledge scores ranged from 6.2 to 7.1 out of 8, with 62%-91% of participants classified as having adequate knowledge (≥ 75%). EFA supported a two-factor solution reflecting disease-related and testing-related knowledge; however, CFA demonstrated substantial overlap between these domains (r = 0.81), with one- and two-factor models showing comparable fit. Overall, findings supported a dominant general knowledge construct. IRT analyses demonstrated acceptable model fit (M2 = 39.35, df = 20, p = 0.006) and meaningful variability in item performance. Two items showed strong discrimination across the knowledge continuum, while several items contributed less information. All items had negative difficulty parameters, indicating that the scale was primarily targeted toward individuals with below-average knowledge. Test information curves showed greatest measurement precision at low-to-moderate knowledge levels. Raw scores were highly correlated with latent trait estimates (r = 0.97, p < 0.001), supporting the practicality of simple sum-score interpretation. This study provides preliminary evidence supporting the internal structural validity of the eight-item cardiac genetic knowledge scale. The scale demonstrated acceptable item performance in this sample and effectively identified individuals with lower levels of knowledge and specific educational gaps across care models, supporting its potential use as the knowledge component of informed decision-making measures in cardiac genetic testing.

title: Difficult Extubation After Thoracoscopic Surgery in a Patient With Hypothyroidism: A Case Report.
authorString: Li Y, Cui Y, Guan Y.

journal.title: The American journal of case reports

abstractText: BACKGROUND Hypothyroidism is a common endocrine disorder with a prevalence of 0.4% to 1.7%, affecting predominantly women and older adults. Common anesthetic and surgical complications in patients with hypothyroidism include delayed emergence, myocardial and pulmonary infarction, respiratory arrest, hemorrhage, and fluid or electrolyte imbalance. Severe hypothyroidism can rarely trigger myxedema. This case report describes the case of a patient with hypothyroidism who underwent difficult extubation after thoracoscopic lung surgery. CASE REPORT A 62-year-old woman with hypothyroidism developed shortness of breath, stridor, hypoxemia, and decreased muscle strength in the extremities following the removal of a double-lumen endotracheal tube after thoracoscopic resection of the right lung S6 segment. Reintubation revealed marked periglottic edema. Upon admission to the intensive care unit, she presented with lethargy, cold extremities, and edema of the eyelids and dorsum of the feet. A detailed medical history revealed irregular use of levothyroxine sodium and self-discontinuation of the medication for 3 days prior to surgery. Postoperative laryngeal edema was considered the direct cause of extubation difficulty, while inadequately controlled hypothyroidism was identified as a major contributing factor to tissue edema, impaired respiratory muscle function, and delayed postoperative recovery. Following respiratory support and supplementation with levothyroxine sodium, respiratory function and muscle strength gradually improved, and the patient was discharged on the sixth postoperative day. CONCLUSIONS This case suggests that in patients with hypothyroidism experiencing difficulty with extubation during the perioperative period, a comprehensive assessment of common causes, such as airway edema and residual neuromuscular blockade, is necessary, and the adverse effects of hypothyroidism on airway edema and recovery from anesthesia should be given due attention.

title: Carotid CTA with automated plaque quantification for risk stratification of coexisting obstructive coronary artery disease.
authorString: Xu L, Zhao M, Zhou C, Li J, Zhao S, Li J, Tang H, Chen S, Liu R, Zhu W, Liu Y, Zhang Y, Jin Q, Cui W, Jiang P, Wu D, Cheng X, Zhang L.
abstractText:
Objectives

To evaluate whether automated carotid plaque quantification on carotid computed tomography angiography (CTA) can serve as an adjunctive risk stratification tool for identifying patients with coexisting obstructive coronary artery disease (OCAD).

Materials and methods

This dual-center retrospective study included 2533 adults undergoing paired carotid and coronary CTA within 3 months. Carotid plaque components (calcified, fibrotic, and lipid) were quantified automatically. In the modeling cohort, three diagnostic models for OCAD (stenosis ≥ 50%) were developed using LASSO regression: clinical, plaque, and integrated models. Performance was assessed by AUC (with DeLong's test), decision curve analysis, and calibration curves, with validation in an internal validation set and a temporally independent validation cohort. Sensitivity analysis was performed using severe stenosis (≥ 70%) as the outcome.

Results

All carotid plaque volumes were significantly associated with OCAD (p < 0.001). Calcified plaque volume (OR, 2.43; 95% CI: 1.95-3.04) and fibrotic plaque volume (OR, 1.37; 95% CI: 1.01-1.85) were independent predictors. The plaque model achieved an AUC of 0.785 (95% CI: 0.761-0.810) in the training set, comparable to the integrated model (AUC, 0.800) and superior to the clinical model (AUC, 0.723; p < 0.001). Performance remained robust in the internal (AUC, 0.824) and external validation set (AUC, 0.813). The integrated model demonstrated good calibration. Sensitivity analysis yielded consistent results.

Conclusion

In this retrospective study, automated carotid plaque quantification on CTA provides an adjunctive risk stratification tool to identify patients at high risk for coexisting OCAD, potentially guiding decisions regarding downstream coronary examinations.

Key points

Question Quantitative analysis of carotid plaque components on CTA may help identify patients with OCAD. Findings A model integrating automated carotid plaque volumes and clinical factors effectively identified OCAD. Clinical Relevance This study demonstrates that automated carotid plaque quantification on CTA may serve as an adjunctive risk stratification tool to guide downstream coronary testing in patients with cerebrovascular disease.

title: Acute postoperative pain in surgical patients with cognitive impairment: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
authorString: Andrusiak J, Tanabe J, Wong AK, Cui A, Sanjebad MN, Saripella A, Englesakis M, Yan E, Chung F.
abstractText: Acute pain in the postoperative period and pre-existing cognitive impairment (CI) are both independently associated with increased postoperative adverse outcomes. Pre-existing cognitive impairment may interfere with the reporting, recognition, and treatment of pain in this population. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the impact of pre-existing cognitive impairment on pain and analgesic consumption after surgery in adults. MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane Central, and Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews were searched for randomized controlled trials and cohort studies for adults undergoing non-cardiac, emergency, or elective surgery until April 9, 2026. Surgical patients with pre-existing cognitive impairment were compared to cognitively intact peers. The primary outcomes assessed were subjective ratings of pain and analgesic consumption postoperatively. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I and certainty of evidence was rated by GRADE. Meta-analysis used standard mean differences (SMDs) with 95% confidence intervals. Thirteen studies (37,918 patients) were included. Approximately one third (33%; 95% CI 0.25-0.41) of adult surgical patients screened positive for preoperative cognitive impairment. Subjective pain scores did not differ significantly between patients with and without cognitive impairment (Hedge's g: 0.11 (SD -0.15-0.36, I2 85.3%, T2 0.073). Patients with cognitive impairment had significantly less analgesic consumption than their cognitively intact counterparts (Cohen's d: 0.53 (0.29-0.76, I2 67.4%, T2 0.028). Despite comparable pain scores, those with cognitive impairment received significantly less postoperative analgesia, raising concern for systematic under-recognition and undertreatment of pain. Increased awareness of this discrepancy and the use of standardized analgesia protocols may improve postoperative outcomes. International Registry of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO:1117357).

title: Omega-3 Fatty Acid Supplementation Has Coronary and Other Selective Health Benefits: Comprehensive Results from the VITamin D and OmegA-3 TriaL (VITAL).
authorString: Manson JE, Bassuk SS, Cook NR, Lee IM, Mora S, Luttmann-Gibson H, Albert CM, Mehrtash F, D'Agostino D, Ridge C, Bubes V, Walter JA, Danik JS, Buring JE, VITAL Research Group.
abstractText: The VITamin D and OmegA-3 TriaL (VITAL) is the only large-scale randomized trial of marine omega-3 fatty acid (n-3 FA) supplementation for the primary prevention of cardiovascular disease (CVD) and cancer in a general population unselected for elevated risk. This article provides an integrated overview of the results of the n-3 FA component and its ancillary studies. VITAL is a completed nationwide, randomized, placebo-controlled, 2x2 factorial trial of n-3 FAs (1 g/day) and vitamin D3 (2000 IU/day) for a median of 5.3 years for primary prevention of CVD and cancer among 25,871 U.S. men aged ≥50 and women aged ≥55 years. Ancillary studies investigated effects on heart failure, atrial fibrillation (AF), autoimmune disease, and other endpoints. Compared with placebo, the n-3 FA supplement did not significantly reduce the primary endpoint of major CVD events (hazard ratio [HR]=0.92 [95% confidence interval 0.80-1.06]) but did significantly reduce total myocardial infarction (MI; HR=0.72 [0.59-0.90]), fatal MI (HR=0.50 [0.26-0.97]), percutaneous coronary intervention (HR=0.78 [0.63-0.95]), and recurrent hospitalization for heart failure (HR=0.86 [0.74-0.998]). The intervention was not associated with AF risk. Supplemental n-3 FAs did not reduce total cancer incidence, other cancer endpoints, or all-cause mortality but was associated with significantly decreased risk of autoimmune disease (confirmed plus probable cases; HR=0.82 [0.68-0.99]). Effect modification by demographic, dietary, and clinical factors was observed for several endpoints, with greater benefits in Black participants and those with lower fish intake or cardiovascular risk factors, but with variable effects in women vs. men. Supplemental n-3 FAs did not significantly reduce major CVD events or cancer but decreased multiple cardiac endpoints and autoimmune disease. Several factors modified treatment effects. Although the findings do not support routine n-3 FA supplementation among healthy adults for prevention of chronic disease, targeted supplementation of those with low fish intake and other select groups warrants consideration.

title: Invasive pulmonary artery pressure monitoring in heart failure: evidence, clinical application, and future directions.
authorString: Aimo A, Tomasoni D, Martone P, Giannoni A, Codina P, Coceani M, Bayes-Genis A.
abstractText: Hemodynamic congestion frequently precedes overt deterioration in heart failure (HF), offering an opportunity for earlier intervention through remote invasive monitoring. Among available systems, pulmonary artery pressure (PAP)-guided management with CardioMEMS has the most mature randomized evidence for reducing recurrent HF hospitalizations and improving health status, although a consistent survival benefit across the HF spectrum has not been established. Clinical implementation requires individualized pressure targets, sustained trend interpretation, regular patient transmissions, and prompt therapeutic responses. The most directly actionable interventions are adjustments to decongestive treatment; prognostic HF therapies should be prescribed and maintained according to guideline indications rather than PAP readings alone. Persistent worsening-HF events warrant reassessment of signal quality, therapeutic response, and alternative mechanisms of deterioration. Device longevity must be distinguished from long-term calibration accuracy, while post-marketing safety data require cautious interpretation. The incremental benefit of pressure monitoring in patients receiving fully contemporary pharmacological treatment remains uncertain. Emerging pulmonary artery, left atrial, and inferior vena cava platforms have different physiological targets, monitoring workflows, and levels of clinical evidence. This narrative review critically appraises the physiological rationale, randomized and real-world evidence, clinical management, device performance, safety, and future development of implantable hemodynamic monitoring in HF.

title: Translating Perivascular Inflammation Imaging into Precision Coronary Care: An Ex plainable Nomogram Integrating Pericoronary Adipose Tissue Attenuation Index with Anatomical and Functional CT Biomarkers for Acute Coronary Syndrome Discrimination
authorString: qi y, Zhang H, Li Y, Ni T, Zhou S, Dong J, Yu M, Liu X.
abstractText:
Background: Acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and stable coronary artery disease (SCAD) present overlapping clinical phenotypes, yet mandate divergent therapeutic strategies—urgent revascularization versus pharmacological optimization. Current diagnostic reliance on high-sensitivity cardiac troponin dynamic monitoring introduces hazardous delays (4–6 hours detection window) and yields false negatives in 20% of non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction. Pericoronary adipose tissue attenuation index (FAI), quantifying vascular inflammation through computed tomography (CT) attenuation changes in pericoronary fat, offers mechanistic insight into coronary plaque destabilization. However, the translational pathway from this biomarker to clinically actionable decision support remains incompletely realized, particularly regarding integration with established anatomical and functional parameters and explicit clinical interpretability. Hypothesis: A mechanistically grounded, multi-dimensional nomogram combining FAI with coronary CT angiography (CCTA)-derived anatomical stenosis (%DS), left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), and smoking status—rendered interpretable through SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)—would achieve robust ACS-SCAD discrimination while providing transparent, auditable decision logic suitable for clinical implementation.

Methods:

In this prospective diagnostic accuracy study adhering to TRIPOD 2019 guidelines, 388 patients (ACS 117 [30.2%], SCAD 271 [69.8%]) underwent CCTA with standardized FAI, %DS, and LVEF acquisition. Stratified randomization (7:3) produced training (n=271) and validation (n=117) sets with preserved outcome distribution. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression with 10-fold stratified cross-validation compared lambda.min versus lambda.1se selection criteria, followed by multivariable logistic regression. Performance was assessed by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration, Brier score, and decision curve analysis. KernelSHAP parsed individualized decision contributions. Regulatory-readiness was evaluated through predetermined change control documentation and explanation stability assessment.

Results:

LASSO lambda.min retained %DS, FAI, LVEF, RVEF, and smoking; lambda.1se selected only %DS and FAI. Final model incorporated %DS, FAI, LVEF, and smoking based on mechanistic non-overlap (RVEF-LVEF functional redundancy) and epidemiological importance. Multivariable analysis demonstrated %DS (OR 1.03, 95% CI: 1.01–1.04, P < 0.001) and FAI (OR 1.04, 95% CI: 1.02–1.06, P < 0.001) as positive ACS predictors; LVEF as protective (OR 0.96, 95% CI: 0.92–0.99, P = 0.032); smoking as marginally non-significant (OR 1.83, 95% CI: 0.87–3.86, P = 0.110) but incrementally contributory. Nomogram achieved AUC 0.86 (95% CI: 0.82–0.91) in training and 0.82 (95% CI: 0.75–0.90) in validation. Optimal cutoff 0.291 (Youden index) yielded training sensitivity 0.80, specificity 0.82, negative predictive value 0.91; validation sensitivity 0.73, specificity 0.72, negative predictive value 0.83. Calibration was satisfactory (Hosmer-Lemeshow P = 0.347 and P = 0.405). Decision curve analysis demonstrated net benefit across threshold probability 0.10–0.55. SHAP analysis established a mechanistic hierarchy: %DS and FAI as dominant drivers (mean |SHAP| 0.75 and 0.70), LVEF as a functional protective modifier (0.35), and smoking as a behavioral risk stratifier (0.20). Individual force plots enabled case-level explanation with documented contribution stability.

Conclusions:

The %DS-FAI-LVEF-smoking nomogram achieves favorable ACS discriminatory accuracy with acceptable generalization. SHAP-enhanced interpretability satisfies emerging transparency requirements for artificial intelligence-enabled medical devices, supporting regulatory-ready clinical translation. Translational Significance: This study bridges the critical T1–T2 translational gap by converting perivascular inflammation biology (FAI) into an evidence-based diagnostic tool validated for a specific clinical decision context. The "one-stop" CCTA acquisition strategy—yielding anatomical, inflammatory, and functional data from a single examination—addresses implementation barriers in time-critical emergency settings. Explicit SHAP-based explainability exceeds current "black box" machine learning limitations, aligning with FDA and EMA guidance on predetermined change control and transparency documentation for clinical artificial intelligence. These design elements collectively reduce translational friction from research prototype to prospective clinical trials and eventual regulatory approval, advancing precision coronary care through mechanism-informed, transparently interpretable decision support.

title: Trimethylamine N-Oxide (TMAO), Inflammation, and Cardiovascular Risk Factors in Adults With Overweight and Obesity: Impact of Fresh Watermelon Consumption in a Randomized Controlled Crossover Trial.
authorString: Bollish EM, Ager E, Santos AL, Sydykova B, Nguyen B, Renfro M, Tanahara J, Pascua J, Hong MY.
abstractText: Elevated trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO) levels are associated with increased cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk. Watermelon consumption has been shown to improve cardiovascular function by favorably modulating lipid profiles and endothelial function. However, its impact on circulating TMAO levels remains unknown. This study examined the effects of daily watermelon consumption on TMAO and other cardiovascular risk markers in adults with overweight and obesity. In this randomized crossover clinical trial, 32 participants (16 men, 16 women; mean age 25.6 ± 6.0 years; mean BMI 29.0 ± 3.7 kg/m2) consumed 330 g/day of fresh watermelon (100 kcal) or an isocaloric control (low-fat cookies, LFC) for 4 weeks, separated by a 4-week washout period. Body weight and BMI changed numerically during the watermelon intervention, but these changes were not statistically significant (p = 0.056 and p = 0.070, respectively). TMAO concentrations decreased significantly from baseline following watermelon consumption (p = 0.005); however, the difference between the watermelon and LFC interventions at week 4 was not statistically significant (p = 0.091). Triglycerides and LDL cholesterol were significantly reduced following the watermelon intervention (p < 0.05). ICAM-1 levels were numerically, but not statistically significantly, lower after watermelon consumption (p = 0.083). Inflammatory markers TNF-α and IL-1β decreased significantly following the watermelon intervention (p < 0.05). Total antioxidant capacity (TAC) increased compared to LFC (p = 0.022). In conclusion, TMAO and selected cardiometabolic risk markers showed favorable within-intervention changes during the watermelon period; however, the between-intervention difference in TMAO was not statistically significant, although a numerical difference was observed. These exploratory findings require confirmation in larger, adequately powered studies. Trial Registration: The study was registered at clinicaltrials.gov (NCT06323070).

title: Transverse versus longitudinal mucosotomy during peroral endoscopic myotomy: results of a multicenter randomized controlled trial.
authorString: Rodríguez-Fajardo JA, Frías-Ordoñez JS, Marulanda-Fernandez H, Otero-Regino W, Jaramillo-Trujillo G.
abstractText: Peroral endoscopic myotomy (POEM) is an established first-line therapy for achalasia; however, technical variability persists in key procedural steps. The optimal orientation of mucosal entry remains uncertain. We evaluated whether transverse mucosotomy improves procedural efficiency and reduces gas-related events compared with the conventional longitudinal approach. In this multicenter, parallel-group randomized clinical trial conducted at three tertiary centers, 140 adults undergoing POEM were assigned (1:1) to a standardized 15-mm transverse or longitudinal mucosotomy. The primary outcome was time from initial mucosal incision to effective entry into the submucosal tunnel, assessed by independent anonymized video review using predefined objective timestamp criteria. Secondary outcomes included need for hemostasis, mucosotomy closure time, number of clips used, gas-related events, and 30-day complications. Analyses followed the intention-to-treat principle. All randomized patients were included in the primary analysis. Transverse mucosotomy significantly reduced time to submucosal entry (median 228 vs. 269 s; adjusted mean difference - 44 s; 95% CI - 78 to - 10), need for hemostasis (38.6% vs. 57.1%; relative risk 0.68; 95% CI 0.49-0.95), closure time (662 vs. 1020 s; p < 0.001), and number of clips used (median 3 vs. 7; rate ratio 0.44; 95% CI 0.36-0.54). Pneumoperitoneum occurred less frequently with the transverse approach (34.3% vs. 51.4%; relative risk 0.67; 95% CI 0.46-0.97). Rates of serious adverse events and 30-day readmission were low and comparable between groups. In a multicenter randomized trial, transverse mucosotomy during POEM improved intraoperative efficiency and reduced gas-related events without compromising short-term safety. These findings support mucosal entry orientation as a modifiable technical factor that may optimize procedural workflow and resource utilization in submucosal endoscopic surgery. NCT07425977.

title: Hemodynamic and respiratory effects of non-invasive ventilation modalities in very preterm infants: a randomized crossover trial.
authorString: Naknin N, Yangthara B, Kitsommart R, Altit G, Wutthigate P.
abstractText: Non-invasive ventilation (NIV) minimizes lung injury in preterm infants. We compared the short-term hemodynamic and respiratory effects of different NIV modalities. Infants <32 weeks' gestation or birthweight <1500 g on nasal continuous positive airway pressure (NCPAP) were randomized, in a two-sequence crossover design to 2 h each of non-synchronized NIPPV (NS-NIPPV) and neurally synchronized NIPPV (S-NIPPV). Ventricular output and function were assessed by echocardiography, with diaphragm activity and lung aeration evaluated. Linear mixed-effects models were used for analysis. No significant differences were observed in right (RV) or left ventricular (LV) output across modes. RV output tended to be higher during S-NIPPV than NS-NIPPV (mean difference 24 mL/kg/min [95% CI; -3 to 51]; p = 0.08). NS-NIPPV was associated with a greater magnitude of LV peak global longitudinal strain (-2.54 [95% CI; -4.61 to -0.48]; p = 0.02) and strain rate (-0.45 [95% CI; -0.78 to -0.11]; p = 0.008) compared to NCPAP. S-NIPPV reduced peak Edi (7.2 ± 5.1 µV vs NCPAP 10.0 ± 6.8 µV; p < 0.01). Both NIPPV modes improved lung ultrasound score (p < 0.001). S-NIPPV showed a non-significant trend toward higher RV output and significantly reduced diaphragm activity compared with NS-NIPPV; both NIPPV modes improved lung aeration relative to NCPAP. Thai Clinical Trials Registry. Registration number TCTR20240804002. Web link: https://www.thaiclinicaltrials.org/show/TCTR20240804002 . In clinically stable very preterm infants, short-term exposure to NCPAP, NS-NIPPV, and S-NIPPV preserved biventricular output and myocardial performance, addressing concerns regarding hemodynamic compromise with higher airway pressures. S-NIPPV was associated with a significant reduction in diaphragmatic workload (peak Edi) and a non-significant trend toward higher RVO, without evidence of adverse cardiac effects; lung aeration improved with both NIPPV modes relative to NCPAP. These exploratory findings generate the hypothesis that the observed benefits are driven by effective pressure delivery rather than synchronization alone, offering mechanistic insight to refine NIV optimization in contemporary neonatal care.

title: Giant Coronary Artery Aneurysm at the Left Main Bifurcation Managed With Stent-Assisted Endovascular Coil Embolization.
authorString: Hoque A, Barforoshi S, Megowan N.
abstractText: Giant coronary artery aneurysms (CAAs), defined as exceeding 4 times the reference vessel diameter or 20 mm, are rare, with no randomized trials or guidelines directing treatment. A 78-year-old woman with exertional angina was found to have a 30 mm giant CAA at the left main (LM) bifurcation with 70% mid-LM and ostial left anterior descending stenosis. Given poor surgical candidacy, a fully percutaneous approach was used: a drug-eluting stent was placed from the distal LM into the proximal left anterior descending, followed by stent-assisted coil embolization with 13 detachable coils. Final angiography showed no residual stenosis, near-complete aneurysm exclusion, and restoration of TIMI flow grade 3 in the left circumflex artery, suggesting the aneurysm had been causing coronary steal. The patient was discharged chest pain-free on dual antiplatelet therapy. This case demonstrates stent-assisted coil embolization as a viable percutaneous option for giant LM bifurcation CAAs and highlights coronary steal as a potential consequence.

title: Evaluation of a novel transseptal puncture device for use in cardiac procedures requiring left atrial access.
authorString: Quinn RW, Singh GD, Ebner A, Pasrija C, Bradshaw A, Rumer C, Mester D, Purcell C, Gammie JS.
abstractText: Transseptal puncture (TSP) is the first step in percutaneous left-heart interventions including atrial fibrillation ablation, left atrial appendage occlusion, and percutaneous mitral valve repair/replacement. Current TSP techniques remain limited by suboptimal imaging visualization, lack of precise control over puncture sites, and a steep learning curve. The Protaryx transseptal puncture device was designed to address these limitations by incorporating a novel atraumatic highly echogenic deployable and retractable nitinol mesh end effector mounted on an extendable catheter. The key advantages of the Protaryx TSP device are the maneuverability of the extendable catheter and the visibility of the end effector that combine to enable precise targeting of the fossa ovalis during TSP. Here, we provide an overview of challenges with transseptal puncture, an overview of the Protaryx device, and early clinical evidence. This includes results of the 5-patient prospective non-randomized observational first-in-human experience with the Protaryx TSP catheter. This study demonstrated early feasibility and safety, with rapid on-target puncture of the fossa ovalis, zero adverse events, and 100% success of structural heart interventions following TSP. The United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approval of the Protaryx device has increased options for interventional cardiologists and electrophysiologists seeking to streamline left-sided structural heart intervention.

title: Atrial Fibrillation During Zanubrutinib Treatment in Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia With a Historical Ibrutinib Control.
authorString: Visentin A, Martino EA, Cellini A, Angotzi F, Pitino A, Duminuco A, Vigna E, Pasquale R, Ferrarini I, Moia R, Sanna A, Motta M, Moratti M, Sportoletti P, Chiarenza A, Maggi A, Zammit V, Merli M, Innocenti I, Giordano C, Nocilli L, Postorino M, Stelitano C, Ferrario A, Frustaci AM, Riva M, Pepe S, Ibatici A, Scardino S, Borza PA, Ballotta L, Mancuso S, Malaspina F, Mele A, Galimberti S, Catania G, Giordano A, Angeletti I, Schiattone L, Pennese E, Miccolis R, Fama A, Giordano G, Califano C, Bruzzese A, Farina G, Bulian P, Loseto G, Pocali B, Innao V, Galieni P, Fraticelli V, Vitale C, Romeo A, Rossi M, Scortechini I, Vozella F, Malandruccolo L, Varettoni M, Morello L, Pietrantuono G, Conte E, Cantelli M, Murru R, Caracciolo D, Derenzini E, Martina VD, Marasca R, Principe MID, Figuera A, Coscia M, Renzo ND, Laurenti L, Amodio N, Allegra A, Fabro VD, Fiumara P, Scalise L, Stagno F, Tona G, Musto P, Caruso L, Liso A, Tedeschi A, Gaidano G, Mauro FR, Tripepi G, Morabito F, Palumbo GA, Raimondo FD, Gattei V, Trentin L, Gentile M.
abstractText:
Introduction

Atrial fibrillation (AF) complicates Bruton tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy in chronic lymphocytic leukemia.

Methods

We retrospectively evaluated 679 zanubrutinib-treated patients across 52 Italian centers, with 354 historical ibrutinib-treated controls. Shanafelt AF scores were assessed.

Results

Nine zanubrutinib-treated patients developed AF (1.33%) during median treatment of 15.5 months, versus 42 historical controls (11.9%) over median observation of 25 months. Five zanubrutinib events occurred among patients scoring ≥ 5. No affected patients experienced embolic or bleeding complications.

Conclusion

AF was uncommon during zanubrutinib treatment, even in the higher-risk subgroup. Historical comparisons remain limited, and exploratory score findings require confirmation with longer follow-up.

Trial registration

The authors have confirmed clinical trial registration is not needed for this submission.

title: Tirzepatide and inflammation: a critical reappraisal of the immunometabolic case for incretin-based therapy.
authorString: Jabbar AD.
abstractText: Tirzepatide, a dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist, lowers high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP) by 29-55% across randomised trials in obesity, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and obstructive sleep apnoea, and interleukin-6 by 25-30% at 72 weeks. Much of this is not weight-mediated: in SURPASS-4 the fall in hsCRP correlated with that in body mass index at r = 0.07, and mediation analysis of trials of semaglutide, a selective GLP-1 receptor agonist, attributes only 21-62% of its hsCRP effect to change in glycated haemoglobin and/or weight. The mechanism, however, is not the one usually given: the account reproduced in most reviews, that incretin receptors on macrophages and T lymphocytes signal through cyclic AMP to restrain nuclear factor-κB, is not supported by the best-controlled data. The principal antibody used to detect the T-cell GLP-1 receptor gives signal in receptor-null cells; Glp1r is undetectable by quantitative PCR in peritoneal and adipose macrophages; and haematopoietic receptor deletion does not abolish semaglutide's anti-atherosclerotic effect. I therefore propose a three-route model, graded by evidence: limited direct signalling in a few validated lymphocyte populations, a central neuro-immune relay, and a large indirect metabolic contribution. That adipose macrophages are refractory to tirzepatide while Kupffer cells respond, and that C-reactive protein is hepatocyte-derived, suggest a substantially hepatic rather than adipose effect. Because the mechanistic evidence concerns GLP-1 receptor agonism almost entirely, the appraisal applies to incretin-based therapy as a class, tirzepatide being the worked example. Five falsifiable propositions are advanced with the experiments that would refute them.

title: Silent cerebral ischemia after anticoagulation- or TEE-guided cardioversion: The randomized AFTER-CV trial.
authorString: Ozaydin M, Ersoy I, Isik IB, Aksoy F, Degirmenci B, Degirmenci H, Bas HA, Karabacak M, Adali K, Arslan A.
abstractText:
Background

Silent cerebral ischemia after elective cardioversion is incompletely characterized, and randomized MRI-based evidence comparing anticoagulation-guided and transesophageal echocardiography (TEE)-guided pathways is limited.

Methods

AFTER-CV was a prospective, randomized, open-label, parallel-group trial of 112 patients undergoing elective cardioversion, assigned 1:1 by sealed-envelope randomization to at least 3 weeks of therapeutic oral anticoagulation or a TEE-guided strategy. Brain diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (DWI-MRI) was performed before and 1 week after cardioversion and was interpreted by an experienced radiologist blinded to treatment allocation. Clinical thromboembolic and bleeding outcomes were assessed during 2 years of follow-up.

Results

New silent cerebral ischemic lesions were detected in 2 of 56 patients (3.6%) in the anticoagulation-guided group and 4 of 56 (7.1%) in the TEE-guided group (absolute risk difference, -3.6 percentage points; 95% CI, -13.7 to 6.0; Fisher exact p = 0.68). No statistically significant between-group differences were detected for the reported long-term clinical efficacy, bleeding, or composite outcomes.

Conclusions

New MRI-detected cerebral ischemic lesions were uncommon in both randomized groups. The small sample, few imaging events, single-center design, and predominantly warfarin-treated cohort preclude conclusions of equivalence or non-inferiority.

title: Clinical outcomes of GLP-1 receptor agonists VS placebo among patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authorString: Davis E, Alexander L, Tobian N, Theja FA, Kristianto A, Hananta L.

journal.title: The Egyptian heart journal : (EHJ) : official bulletin of the Egyptian Society of Cardiology

abstractText:
Background

Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is a complex form of heart failure which is marked by impaired diastolic function. It has complex pathophysiology involving systemic inflammation, myocardial fibrosis and arterial stiffness. The existence of other comorbidities namely obesity and diabetes further worsens these processes. Currently there is limited treatment option for HFpEF.

Methods

Systematic search from 5 databases was conducted to identify studies that evaluated the impacts of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 RA) on the clinical outcomes of HFpEF. Quantitative analysis was performed using random effect model were performed on clinical outcomes. Results are presented as odds ratio (OR) along with its 95% confidence interval.

Results

3 Studies involving 1463 patients were included. GLP-1 RA reduced NT-pro Brain Natriuretic Peptide (NT-pro BNP) levels and enhanced 6-minute walking test, Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire clinical summary score. Significant reduction in adjudicated heart failure event was observed (OR 0.32, 95% CI: 0.15-0.67, p < 0.05, I2 = 5%). No significant difference in all-cause mortality (OR 0.63, 95% CI: 0.27-1.48, p = 0.29, I2 = 0%) and cardiovascular mortality (OR 0.27, 95% CI: 0.04-1.66, p = 0.16, I2 = 0%) were observed.

Conclusion

GLP-1 RA was effective in improving quality of life parameters and lowered the risk of cardiovascular events of HFpEF patients; however it did not significantly reduce mortality in those who suffered from HFpEF.

title: Post-mortem CT angiography for fatal vascular lesions in forensic death investigation: a systematic review of diagnostic performance, added value, and pitfalls.
authorString: Marinelli L, Cappabianca F, Cappabianca S.
abstractText:
Purpose

Post-mortem CT angiography (PMCTA) is increasingly used in forensic death investigation to assess vascular disease, haemorrhage, and traumatic or natural vascular causes of death. However, its practical value depends on the lesion being investigated, the angiographic protocol, and the way imaging findings are integrated with autopsy and pathology. This systematic review evaluated the diagnostic performance, added value, and main pitfalls of PMCTA for fatal vascular lesions.

Methods

PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Cochrane/CENTRAL were searched for human post-mortem studies evaluating PMCTA in forensic, medico-legal, coronial, or post-mortem settings. Eligible studies compared PMCTA with autopsy, histopathology, targeted vascular dissection, or autopsy-based consensus. Evidence was grouped according to practical forensic use, including coronary stenosis assessment, autopsy triage, global vascular lesion detection, haemorrhage-source localization, aortic or traumatic vascular injury assessment, coronary plaque characterization, and artifact-related pitfalls. Risk of bias was assessed using a QUADAS-2-based approach adapted to forensic PMCTA studies.

Results

The available evidence did not support unrestricted pooling of all fatal vascular lesions. PMCTA was used for different forensic questions, and only coronary stenosis provided data close to conventional diagnostic accuracy assessment. In this domain, available studies showed high specificity but only moderate sensitivity for critical stenosis. Autopsy-triage studies suggested that PMCTA may reduce or guide invasive autopsy in selected adult coronial workflows. Global comparison studies showed added value for vascular lesion detection, and haemorrhage-source studies suggested that PMCTA may help localize bleeding vessels. Evidence on fatal coronary plaque characterization is emerging. Pitfall studies showed that post-mortem clots, incomplete vascular filling, contrast leakage, and extravasation artifacts may mimic or obscure vascular pathology.

Conclusion

PMCTA is best interpreted as a complementary tool in forensic vascular death investigation rather than as a general substitute for autopsy. Its contribution is strongest when it answers a specific vascular question, such as documenting coronary stenosis, guiding autopsy, mapping vascular lesions, localizing haemorrhage, or supporting targeted histopathology. Careful correlation with autopsy, pathology, case circumstances, and protocol-related artifacts remains essential.

title: MicroRNA as Biomarker For Neuroprognostication following Cardiac Arrest: A Systematic Review.
authorString: Maisenbacher M, Vu SP, Sadikot RT, Gress D, Mathew S.
abstractText: Accurate prognostication of neurologic outcomes after cardiac arrest (CA) remains challenging due to a shortage of robust predictors. An ideal biomarker should directly reflect the prognosis-defining injury and allow for objective, reproducible measurement through standardized assays. MicroRNAs (miRs) are promising candidates because of their close relationship to cellular metabolism, high stability, and detectability across multiple body fluids. To evaluate the current evidence for potential clinical utility of miRs in neuroprognostication after CA, we conducted a systematic literature search across MEDLINE, EMBASE, SCOPUS, and The Cochrane Library through July 2025 using predefined keywords related to microRNA, cardiac arrest, and prognostication. Two independent reviewers screened and selected studies according to predefined inclusion criteria, and relevant data were compiled into a structured dataset. Twelve studies met the inclusion criteria, reporting on 28 distinct miRs across 3021 samples. Among these, miR-124 was the most frequently studied, while miR-122, miR-9, miR-21, miR-574, and miR-483 were each investigated in more than one study. Methodological approaches varied, and reporting was not uniform across studies. Prognostic performance was expressed using different metrics, including odds ratios, area under the curve (AUC), and mean group differences. MiR-124 was the most extensively evaluated candidate, with the highest reported AUC of 0.89 (95% CI 0.80-0.97) at 48 hours post-ROSC for poor prognosis. However, this was not uniformly reproduced across studies and will require external validation. Evidence supporting specific miRs as prognostic biomarkers after cardiac arrest is thus growing but remains limited in scope and weakened by heterogeneity in study design and reporting. Within these limitations, current evidence weakly supports including nine miR candidates, namely miR-124, miR-9, miR-483, miR-191, miR-125b-1, miR-129, miR- 6511b, let-7a, and let-7c in descending order of strength of evidence, in standardized and large-scale studies to further clarify the clinical utility of miR-based prognostication.

title: Association between dietary inflammatory index and high blood pressure in children: a meta-analysis.
authorString: Liu Y, Deng J.
abstractText:
Background

Emerging evidence suggests an association between the dietary inflammatory index (DII) and cardiovascular health in children, but its relationship with high blood pressure (BP) remains inconsistent. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate this association.

Methods

PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Wanfang, and China National Knowledge Infrastructure were searched from inception to June 12, 2026. Observational studies involving individuals <18 years were included. Odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using random-effects models.

Results

Six cross-sectional studies involving 56,741 participants (nine independent datasets) were included. Higher DII was associated with increased odds of high BP (OR: 1.33, 95% CI: 1.04-1.70; p = 0.02), with moderate heterogeneity (I² = 65%). Leave-one-study-out analyses yielded ORs ranging from 1.23 to 1.46, although statistical significance was lost after excluding certain studies. Subgroup analyses revealed no significant differences by geographic region, age, sex, DII cutoff, BMI adjustment, or study quality (all p > 0.05). Univariate meta-regression identified study quality as a significant moderator, with weaker associations in higher-quality studies (coefficient = -0.12, 95% CI: -0.23 to -0.01; p = 0.04).

Conclusions

Higher DII may be associated with increased odds of high BP in children and adolescents. However, the cross-sectional designs, heterogeneous outcome definitions, and sensitivity of pooled estimates to individual studies limit the certainty of this association.

title: Maternal cardiovascular and pregnancy outcomes among pregnant patients with mechanical and bioprosthetic valves.
authorString: Essa A, Kovell LC, Wilkie GL.
abstractText:
Introduction

Patients with mechanical heart valves in pregnancy are at a substantially higher risk of adverse maternal and fetal outcomes. Management of patients with mechanical heart valves poses a unique challenge, and strategies for anticoagulation in these patients remain controversial. The goal of this project was to determine rates of adverse maternal and perinatal outcomes in patients with mechanical valves compared to those with bioprosthetic valves, and assess outcomes in patients with mechanical valves using low molecular weight heparin and warfarin.

Methods

A retrospective query was performed using Epic Cosmos to evaluate pregnancies affected by mechanical and bioprosthetic heart valves between January 1, 2023 and January 1, 2026. Patient demographics and rates of adverse cardiac outcomes in the perinatal period, including heart failure, arrhythmia, and stroke, were assessed. The rate of anticoagulation with low molecular weight heparin and warfarin in patients with mechanical heart valves was evaluated, and cardiac and perinatal outcomes were determined and compared between groups. Rare outcomes were reported as <10 to protect patient privacy.

Results

Baseline demographics between patients with mechanical and bioprosthetic heart valves were similar. Rates of heart failure (22.9%) and stroke (11.7%) were significantly higher in patients with mechanical compared to bioprosthetic heart valves, though the rates of maternal arrhythmia were similar between groups. Valve thrombosis was a rare outcome for patients with mechanical valves, with fewer than 10 events in the study sample. Perinatal outcomes including preterm and cesarean delivery were similar between groups.

Conclusion

In conclusion, mechanical heart valves are associated with high rates of heart failure and stroke in pregnancy. Rates of adverse events may be similar for patients using low molecular weight heparin compared to warfarin for anticoagulation in pregnancy.

title: Computed Tomography Coronary Angiography for Patients with Chest Pain: Ethnic Variation in Use, Coronary Atherosclerotic Burden, and Effect on Statin Treatment (ANZACS-QI 90).
authorString: Lee S, Lee M, Kerr AJ, Turaga M, Lamacie M, Tang SY, Wu F, Harrison W, Gabriel RS, Looi JL.
abstractText:
Background

We assessed ethnic differences in computed tomography coronary angiography (CTCA) utilisation, extent of coronary artery disease (CAD), and statin use among patients with chest pain at Middlemore Hospital, New Zealand.

Method

Patients without prior revascularisation (n=4,519) who underwent CTCA (2020-2024) were identified from the Aotearoa New Zealand Acute Coronary Syndrome Quality Improvement (ANZACS-QI) cardiac computed tomography registry. CTCA utilisation was assessed relative to incident acute coronary syndrome (ACS) hospitalisations in each age and ethnic group, which served as a surrogate for population CAD burden. CAD extent was assessed using the segment involvement score. Statin dispensing data were obtained from the national pharmaceutical data set.

Results

The cohort comprised 37.8% European/Other, 13.4% Māori, 19.8% Pacific, 15.5% Indian, and 13.5% other Asian patients. Māori, Pacific, and Indian patients (mean age, 55.7, 54.8, and 54.0 years, respectively) were younger than other Asian and European/Other patients (59.2 and 60.4 years, respectively; p<0.001). CTCA utilisation among those aged <55 years was lowest among Māori and Pacific patients, intermediate among European/Other and Indian patients, and highest among other Asian patients (CTCA-to-incident-ACS ratios, 2.5, 2.2, 3.0, 3.8, and 8.0, respectively). Indian and other Asian patients were most likely to have normal coronary arteries (p<0.001), while Māori and Pacific patients had the most extensive atherosclerosis (p<0.001). Post-CTCA statin use, for equivalent disease severity, was similar across ethnicities.

Conclusions

Young Māori and Pacific patients with chest pain are underinvestigated and undertreated relative to their population CAD burden. However, when CAD is identified, statin treatment is equal across ethnic groups. Therefore, CTCA facilitates equitable treatment for Māori and Pacific patients presenting with chest pain.

title: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists in adults with overweight/obesity and alcohol use disorder: A retrospective cohort study.
authorString: Maurer GE, Tuan WJ, Evans A, Chu KS, Devaraj T, Zhang A, Leggio L, Parthasarathy S, Zgierska AE.
abstractText: Emerging evidence suggests glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) may improve outcomes in alcohol use disorder (AUD), which is associated with cardiovascular risk and mortality. Evaluate the association between initiation of GLP-1RAs and clinical outcomes among adults with AUD and overweight or obesity. A retrospective cohort study using electronic health records from TriNetX research network, with participants enrolled between January 1, 2015 and December 31, 2024 and followed through December 31, 2025. Inverse probability of treatment weighting, based on propensity scores, balanced baseline characteristics.
