Weighted logistic regression models estimated the adjusted odds ratios (aORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) at 1-year follow-up. Adults ≥18 years old with overweight or obesity and AUD, without prior GLP-1RAs, or cancer or non-nicotine substance use disorder diagnoses. At least one GLP-1RA prescription issued after enrollment (Treatment cohort); none for Controls. Presence (Yes/No) of all-cause and alcohol-related hospitalizations, mortality, and major cardiovascular events (MCVE) since the GLP-1RA initiation (Treatment cohort) or post-enrollment (Control cohort). Among 163,681 participants (mean age 53.7 ± 14.4 years; 35.6% female), 10,445 (6.4%) initiated GLP-1RAs. At 1-year follow-up, Treatment cohort had lower likelihood of all-cause (aOR=0.28, 95%CI: 0.28,0.29) and alcohol-related (aOR=0.20; 95%CI: 0.20,0.21) hospitalizations, death (aOR=0.20, 95%CI: 0.19,0.21), and MCVE (aOR=0.72, 95%CI: 0.71,0.74). Exploratory analyses showed that these associations remained consistent at 3 and 5 years. GLP-1RA initiation was associated with reduced risk of MCVE, hospitalization, and mortality among adults with AUD and overweight/obesity, supporting potential role of GLP-RAs in AUD. Prospective studies are warranted.

title: Blockage of Pcsk6-mediated autophagy is involved in the protection of Znf667 against myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury.
authorString: Li H, Wang K, Wei L, Tian W, Lao M, Zhang H, Zhang M, Liu Y.
abstractText: The objective of this study is to elucidate the function and mechanism of Pcsk6 in myocardial ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury. Serum PCSK6 levels were increased in ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction patients following primary percutaneous coronary intervention (p < 0.0001) and positively correlated with cTnI (r = 0.511) and NT-proBNP levels (r = 0.464). Pcsk6 levels were elevated in myocardial tissues 6 h after I/R (p = 0.0001) and cardiomyocytes 12 h after hypoxia-reperfusion (H/R) (p < 0.0001). Pcsk6 knockdown reduced the LC3B-II/I ratio in myocardial tissues and H/R-treated cardiomyocytes (p < 0.0001 and p = 0.0020, respectively) and decreased INF/AAR in mice (p = 0.0303). Conversely, Pcsk6 overexpression increased the LC3B-II/I ratio (p = 0.0338) and reduced cell viability (p = 0.0293) under H/R. Znf667 was downregulated in H/R cardiomyocytes (p = 0.0096). Znf667 overexpression reduced wild-type Pcsk6 promoter activity (p = 0.0004) and Pcsk6 mRNA expression (p = 0.0011). Moreover, Znf667 overexpression reduced INF/AAR in mice (p = 0.0216) and the Nf-κB p-p65/total p65 ratio in H/R cardiomyocytes (p = 0.0164), which were restored by combined overexpression of Pcsk6 (p = 0.0005 and p = 0.0297). In H/R cardiomyocytes overexpressing both Znf667 and Pcsk6, BAY11-7082 increased cell viability (p = 0.0203) and reduced the LC3B-II/I ratio (p = 0.0146). In conclusion, Znf667 alleviates enhanced autophagy and myocardial I/R injury by transcriptionally suppressing Pcsk6. The current findings suggest that Nf-κB may be involved in this process and that PCSK6 may be a biomarker for assessing reperfusion injury.

title: Endogenous hypercortisolism and cardio-liver-metabolic dysfunctions: from pathogenesis to the effects of therapeutic strategies targeting hypercortisolism.
authorString: Pivonello R, Di Paola N, Crescenzo EM, Menafra D, Negri M, Pivonello C, Simeoli C, Colao A.
abstractText: Endogenous hypercortisolism, namely Cushing's syndrome (CS) is a rare but severe endocrine disorder caused by chronic exposure to excess glucocorticoids and characterized by substantial morbidity and increased mortality. Persistent hypercortisolism profoundly affects multiple cardiovascular and metabolic pathways, leading to a broad spectrum of cardio-liver-metabolic complications including arterial hypertension, cardiac and vascular remodelling, thrombotic diathesis, hepatic steatosis, visceral obesity, impaired glucose metabolism, and dyslipidemia. These alterations arise from complex interactions between direct glucocorticoid effects on target tissues and indirect mechanisms, mainly involving insulin resistance, endothelial dysfunction, chronic inflammation, and altered lipid metabolism. The primary therapeutic objective in CS is the normalization of cortisol excess through surgery, radiotherapy, or medical therapy, namely pharmacological treatment. In recent years, the availability of medical drugs targeting pituitary ACTH secretion, adrenal steroidogenesis, or glucocorticoid receptor signalling has expanded therapeutic options for patients with CS, especially with persistent or recurrent disease. Beyond biochemical control of hypercortisolism, namely normalization of urinary free cortisol (UFC) (UFC ≤ upper limit of normal), accumulating evidence suggests that these treatments may improve several cardiometabolic manifestations associated with cortisol excess. However, although remission of hypercortisolism leads to significant clinical improvement, complete normalization of cardio-liver-metabolic alterations is not consistently achieved. Many patients continue to exhibit persistent cardiovascular and metabolic abnormalities even after long-term biochemical remission, highlighting the need for active long-term monitoring and multidisciplinary management to prevent disease progression and optimize long-term outcomes. This mini-review briefly outlines the pathogenesis of cardio-liver-metabolic dysfunctions and discusses the potential effects of currently available therapeutic strategies targeting hypercortisolism on these comorbidities.

title: Emergencies at Sea: Sudden Death on Cruise Ships For the BELTRAN Study (BaskEtbaLl and soccer sTadiums: Registry on Automatic exterNal defibrillators).
authorString: Sheth S, Gupta S, Patel D, Gupta S, Bassi MD, Garagiola LM, Bornancini N, Fitz-Maurice M, Chango DX, Del Sueldo M, Baranchuk A.
abstractText: Sudden death on cruise ships represents a rare but critical public health and medical concern, occurring in a uniquely resource-limited, geographically isolated environment, with delayed access to definitive hospital care. This narrative review aimed to synthesize current evidence on the incidence, causes, circumstances, and response systems related to sudden death on cruise ships, and to examine the medical, logistical, legal, and public health frameworks relevant to these events. A literature search of PubMed, MEDLINE, and EMBASE was conducted using terms related to sudden death and cruise ships, with inclusion of English-language studies from 2010 to 2025. Results suggest that sudden death on cruise ships is rare, with reported mortality estimates of approximately 1.8 deaths per 100,000 cruise passengers. Research highlights that deaths occurring among passengers are predominantly due to natural causes, especially cardiovascular disease, including myocardial infarction and cardiac arrest. Factors such as delayed diagnosis, limited onboard diagnostic capacity, and barriers to timely evacuation have been noted to contribute to preventable mortality. However, deaths occurring among crew are predominantly due to traumatic deaths, particularly falls overboard, and suicide, which calls for increased safety measures and better mental health support for crew. Substantial variability remains in standards for onboard medical response, including accessibility of automated external defibrillator (AED) availability, cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) training, and emergency preparedness. Overall, the findings highlight the need for stronger cardiac emergency protocols, broader AED deployment, enhanced crew training, improved telemedicine and medevac coordination, and regulatory frameworks to reduce preventable deaths at sea.

title: Cardiac biomarkers for risk stratification based on clinical outcomes after ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack.
authorString: Gloystein TS, Jensen M, Lezius S, Cheng B, Schulz R, Oetjen E, Magnus T, Thomalla G, Schwedhelm E, Zeller T, Choe CU.

journal.title: Journal of stroke and cerebrovascular diseases : the official journal of National Stroke Association

abstractText: Following ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack, patients remain at increased risk of adverse neurological and cardiovascular events. Cardiac biomarkers reflecting distinct pathomechanisms may improve risk stratification. We evaluated associations of N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), midregional pro-atrial natriuretic peptide (MR-proANP), and high-sensitivity troponin I (hsTnI) with stroke severity and adverse events and explored a two-step biomarker approach to identify high-risk patients. In the prospective, single-center bioMARKers in STROKE (MARK-STROKE) cohort (University Medical Center Hamburg Eppendorf, Germany), MR-proANP, NT-proBNP, and hsTnI were measured in 374 patients with ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack. Biomarker concentrations were log2-transformed, with effect estimates expressed per doubling. Follow-up was available for 273 patients. Stroke severity was assessed by the National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS). Adverse events (death, myocardial infarction, recurrent stroke, rehospitalization) were recorded during a median of 278 days (interquartile range 184-367). Associations were investigated using age- and sex-adjusted linear, logistic, and Cox regression models. To explore whether combining biomarkers provides additional prognostic information, patients were stratified by the MR-proANP median, with those above the median further stratified by the subgroup-specific hsTnI median. Higher MR-proANP concentrations were associated with higher NIHSS scores on admission (adjusted β 0.64; 95% CI 0.25-1.02; p=0.001) and an increased risk of adverse events (adjusted HR 1.50; 95% CI 1.21-1.87; p<0.001). NT-proBNP showed similar but weaker associations, whereas hsTnI was not significantly associated with adverse events. Among patients with MR-proANP concentrations above the median, those with hsTnI concentrations above the subgroup-specific hsTnI median had the lowest event-free survival in Kaplan-Meier analysis (log-rank p=0.008). Cardiac biomarkers, particularly MR-proANP, provide prognostic information after ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack. A two-step algorithm using MR-proANP for initial classification and hsTnI for refinement may identify patients at increased risk and requires prospective validation.

title: GDF-15 and sST2 as independent predictors of long-term mortality in hospitalized older adults: a prospective cohort study.
authorString: Giordani C, Di Rosa M, Matacchione G, Sbriscia M, Fantone S, Marchegiani F, Recchioni R, Caccese S, Francini E, Piacenza F, Cardelli M, Giacconi R, Bevilacqua R, Giuliani ME, Bigossi G, Moretti M, Longhi E, Cherubini A, Spannella F, Bonfigli AR, Lattanzio F, Giuliani A, Olivieri F, Sabbatinelli J.
abstractText: Growth differentiation factor-15 (GDF-15) and soluble ST2 (sST2) reflect systemic biological stress, inflammation, and aging-related processes, but their prognostic relevance in hospitalized older adults remains unclear. We prospectively studied 966 patients aged ≥65 years from the Report-AGE cohort. Circulating GDF-15 and sST2 were measured at hospital admission, and all-cause mortality was evaluated using Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for demographic characteristics, frailty, comorbidity burden, and routine laboratory parameters. Incremental prognostic value was assessed using likelihood ratio tests, Harrell's C-index, and time-dependent ROC analyses. Over a median follow-up of 4.2 years, 805 deaths occurred. Higher GDF-15 and sST2 levels independently predicted mortality after multivariable adjustment (GDF-15: HR 1.32, 95% CI 1.17-1.49; sST2: HR 1.24, 95% CI 1.12-1.36; both p<0.001). Each biomarker significantly improved model fit, with additional gains when both were jointly included. Model discrimination improved modestly but consistently over time. In patients with cardiovascular disease, GDF-15 retained incremental prognostic value, whereas that of sST2 was attenuated. Their complementary prognostic information may capture distinct, partially overlapping pathways of biological vulnerability not fully reflected by conventional measures. Overall, combined assessment of GDF-15 and sST2 may improve long-term risk stratification beyond conventional clinical and laboratory markers in hospitalized older adults.

title: QRICH1 promotes PDK4-dependent mitochondrial dysfunction and pyroptosis in diabetic cardiomyopathy.
authorString: Sun M, Huang Z, Dong H, Lu X, Liu S, Zhang Y, Gong L, Zhong L.
abstractText:
Background

Diabetic cardiomyopathy (DCM) is characterized by myocardial metabolic remodeling and inflammatory cell death, yet the transcriptional regulators linking metabolic stress to cardiomyocyte injury remain poorly defined.

Methods

Glutamine-rich protein 1 (QRICH1) expression was examined in hearts of mice with high-fat diet and streptozotocin-induced type 2 diabetes and in cardiomyocytes exposed to high glucose plus palmitic acid. QRICH1 transcriptional regulation of pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase 4 (PDK4) was verified by chromatin immunoprecipitation and dual-luciferase assays, and the effects of QRICH1 overexpression and PDK4 knockdown were assessed in vitro. Drug repurposing was performed by molecular docking and a drug affinity responsive target stability assay.

Results

QRICH1 was markedly upregulated in diabetic myocardium and under glucolipotoxic conditions. QRICH1 directly bound the PDK4 promoter and transactivated its expression. QRICH1 overexpression induced caspase-1-dependent pyroptosis, impaired mitochondrial respiration, and promoted cytosolic mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) leakage with inflammatory signaling activation, and these changes were partially reversed by PDK4 knockdown. Vericiguat showed the strongest binding affinity for QRICH1 among screened cardiovascular drugs. In DCM mice, vericiguat significantly improved cardiac function, downregulated PDK4, and restored myocardial AKT phosphorylation.

Conclusions

QRICH1 sustains PDK4 expression under glucolipotoxic stress, driving mitochondrial dysfunction, mtDNA release, and pyroptosis, and vericiguat represents a repurposing candidate for myocardial protection in DCM.

title: Renal Replacement Therapy in Cardiogenic Shock supported by microAxial Flow Pumps: A European multicentre study.
authorString: Ughetto A, Beurton A, Fürholz M, Schrage B, Kuliczkowski W, Bonello L, Leurent G, Hurtado A, Gaudard P, Bouisset F, Sundermeyer J, De Cuniac M, Tycinska A, Kociecka MZ, Pichené H, Lemarchand L, Jacomet M, Blaziak M, Klotzka A, Cherbi M, Delmas C.
abstractText: Microaxial flow pumps (mAFP) improve hemodynamics and outcomes in myocardial infarction-related cardiogenic shock (CS) but are associated with an increased risk of acute kidney injury (AKI) requiring renal replacement therapy (RRT). We aimed to determine the incidence and factors associated with RRT and evaluate its association with mortality in a real-world cohort of miscellaneous CS patients supported with mAFP. We conducted a retrospective multicentre registry including CS patients supported with mAFP across 11 European centres. The association between RRT and the primary outcome of 180-day all-cause mortality (with survival censored at heart transplantation or durable left ventricular assist device implantation) was assessed using a 1:1 propensity score-matched cohort. Factors associated with RRT were identified using multivariable logistic regression. Among 1043 patients, 972 were included, of whom 340 (35.0%) required RRT. RRT was associated with higher 180-day all-cause mortality both before (Kaplan-Meier estimates, 59.7% vs. 35.2%; HR 2.04, 95% CI 1.67-2.49; p < 0.01) and after propensity score matching (59.0% vs. 41.4%; HR 1.48, 95% CI 1.14-1.92; p < 0.01); restricted mean survival difference -25.5 days, 95% CI - 39.9 to -10.2. Factors associated with RRT included BMI ≥ 30 kg/m² (adjusted OR [aOR] 1.69; 95% CI 1.15-2.46), baseline serum creatinine (per 20 µmol/L increase: aOR 1.18; 95% CI 1.12-1.24), norepinephrine use (aOR 1.72; 95% CI 1.19-2.49), and lactate ≥4 mmol/L at implantation (aOR 1.56; 95% CI 1.11-2.20). In this large European registry of mAFP-supported CS, RRT was frequent and associated with increased 180-day mortality and greater shock severity.

title: Rationale and Design of The Congenital Cardiac Research Collaborative Pulmonary Vein Stenosis Registry.
authorString: O'Byrne ML, Nicholson G, Whiteside WM, Qureshi AM, Krishnan U, Glatz AC, Goldstein B, McCracken CE, Pinto N, Zhang Y, Zampi JD, Petit CJ, Callahan R.
abstractText:
Rationale

Historically, congenital/childhood-onset pulmonary vein stenosis (PVS) was associated with progressive anatomic narrowing, right ventricular failure, and mortality. Comprehensive care of PVS with intensive surveillance, serial reintervention, and medical therapy have shown potential to improve outcomes. Important knowledge gaps persist in measuring severity of PVS, optimal patient- and vein-level outcomes, and which treatment(s) and comorbid conditions influence outcomes.

Design

The Congenital Cardiac Research Collaborative Pulmonary Vein Stenosis Registry will provide a longitudinal dataset of pediatric patients with multi-vessel pulmonary vein stenosis treated at 19 US centers with ambispective data collection creating a cohort of patients beginning on 1/1/2022 with ongoing longitudinal follow-up. Data beginning at their initial evaluation and intervention (including clinical and demographic factors) and continued with longitudinal follow-up, resource utilization, reintervention(s), medical therapy, and (patient- and vein-level) outcomes will be collected.

Conclusion

The registry will provide an efficient means of improving outcomes in this vulnerable patient population. Evaluating current outcomes, resource utilization, and practice variation in this population will guide quality improvement efforts, and the registry may serve as a structure for future research and quality improvement efforts.

title: Machine-Learning Derived Individual Risk Prediction in Congenital Heart Surgery: Development and internal validation of risk prediction models for in-hospital mortality after congenital heart surgery using data from the Pediatric Cardiac Critical Care Consortium (PC4) registry.
authorString: O'Byrne ML, Huang J, Faerber JA, Huang YV, Allen KY, Banerjee M, Graham EM, Griffis HM, Lasa JJ, Newburger JW, O'Connor MJ, Schumacher KR, Glatz AC, Pasquali SK, Gaynor JW.
abstractText:
Background

Machine learning (ML) methods may improve prediction of individual risk of mortality risk after congenital heart surgery (CHD) by identifying nonlinear relationships/novel combinations of variables. Improved risk discrimination may improve outcomes by optimizing resource allocation and patient surveillance.

Methods

Children and adolescents (age≤18 years) undergoing CHD surgery at Pediatric Cardiac Critical Care Consortium hospitals 9/1/2014-12/30/2019 were studied. Non-collinear potential predictors were identified empirically and used to create a logistic regression risk (LR) model (mimicking traditional risk-adjustment models) and ML (random forest and gradient boosting model) models. Model performance was evaluated using net reclassification index (NRI), the proportion of subjects in which either the absolute risk category or estimated risk relative to other subjects changed between each model and one composed only of STAT category as the primary outcome. This metric reflects how often a model changes how a clinician views the risk of a patient relative to a parsimonious model and provides some measure of the utility of these models. Secondary analyses compared overall model fit.

Results

In total 51,475 operative encounters from 52 hospitals were studied. Subjects were 45% female, 20% neonates, and 5% underwent STAT 5 operations. C-statistics and Brier scores did not differ significantly between ML and LR models. For absolute risk categorires, point estimates for NRI between ML-models and STAT category (0.76 95%CI: 0.68-0.83) suggested at best modest improvements compared to logistic regression model (0.75 95%CI 0.67-0.83), but the difference was not significant. Similarly, for rankings of risk within the cohort, NRI for ML models (0.26 95%CI: 0.19-0.32) was not significantly different to that for the LR model (0.24 95%CI: 0.17-0.33).

Conclusion

ML derived models did not improve overall model fit. Magnitude of improvement in reclassification was at best modest and not statistically significant. Future research is necessary to evaluate the added values of incorporating more comprehensive data and/or advanced computational techniques and use of reclassification in risk prediction.

title: Socioeconomic inequalities in NSTEMI outcomes persist despite universal healthcare: A nationwide Belgian study.
authorString: Giangiacomi F, De Potter T, Popelier B, Testerini F, Lochy S, von Kemp M, Benvenuto CP, Zivelonghi C, Vermeersch P, Biondi-Zoccai G, Cosyns B, Argacha JF.
abstractText:
Aims

To comprehensively evaluate the impact of socioeconomic status on in-hospital mortality and access to PCI in patients with NSTEMI.

Methods

This study included all patients hospitalized in Belgium between 2012 and 2021 with NSTEMI. In-hospital mortality, procedures, and relevant clinical variables were recorded. Socioeconomic factors included neighborhood-level income and education, residential population density and residential greenness, sex, marital status, occupational category, and personal income.

Results

The study population consisted of 64,890 subjects, 33,3% females, median age 73 years. 50,4% of patients underwent PCI, while 8,8% underwent CABG. In-hospital mortality was 5,0%. Neighborhood-level income was significantly associated with in-hospital mortality (OR 0,83, p 〈0,01). When stratified by neighborhood income quartiles, patients in the lowest quartile had a higher risk compared to those in the highest quartile (OR 1,48, p < 0,01). Residential population density slightly increased NSTEMI mortality (OR 1,01, p < 0,01), whereas greenness decreased NSTEMI mortality (OR 0,94, p = 0,02). At the individual level, marital status was significantly associated with the outcome, with single status showing the strongest association (OR 1,42, p < 0,01). Female sex and unemployment were not significantly associated with the outcome, whereas personal income decreased in-hospital mortality (OR 0.67, p < 0,01). Female sex was independently associated with a lower likelihood of undergoing PCI (OR 0,74, p < 0,01). Both neighborhood-level income and educational attainment were also associated with the likelihood of undergoing PCI (OR 1,02, p = 0,02 and OR 0.84, p < 0,01 respectively).

Conclusion

In this large nationwide study, both neighborhood and individual incomes were associated with NSTEMI in-hospital mortality and access to PCI. These findings highlight the importance of integrating social determinants of health, as financial precarity, into cardiovascular risk assessment to reduce disparities in care and outcomes.

title: Ferroptosis meets immunity: Bidirectional crosstalk and therapeutic potential.
authorString: Qiu B, Li S, Yi X, Jiang DS.
abstractText: Ferroptosis is an iron-dependent, lipid peroxidation-driven form of regulated cell death that is increasingly recognized as both a target and a regulator of immune responses. Emerging evidence reveals extensive bidirectional communication between ferroptotic cells and the immune system. Ferroptotic cells release damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) and iron-related signals that shape innate and adaptive immunity, whereas immune cells and cytokines actively govern ferroptotic susceptibility by remodeling iron metabolism, antioxidant defenses, and lipid peroxidation pathways. These reciprocal interactions establish a dynamic ferroptosis-immune circuit (FIC) that integrates metabolic stress, cell death signaling, and immune regulation. Here, we review the molecular architecture of this circuit and examine its context-dependent functions in human disease. We discuss how ferroptosis interfaces with antitumor immunity and immunotherapy in cancer, drives inflammatory injury and remodeling in cardiovascular and neurological diseases, modulates immune dysregulation in autoimmune and inflammatory disorders, and influences host-pathogen interactions during infection. We further evaluate emerging therapeutic approaches targeting ferroptosis-immune circuit and propose future directions for translating mechanistic insights into disease-specific therapeutic strategies.

title: Contactless Oxygen Desaturation Prediction and Oxygen Desaturation Index (ODI) Estimation from Nocturnal Breathing Sounds via Deep Learning.
authorString: Choi H, Cho E, Kim S, Heo S, Moon S, Hong J, Lee D, Lee S, Kim JW, Yoon IY.
abstractText: Intermittent hypoxemia is increasingly recognized as a stronger predictor of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality in obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) than the apnea-hypopnea index (AHI). We developed a sound-based AI model to detect oxygen desaturation events and estimate the oxygen desaturation index (ODI) from nocturnal breathing sounds in a fully contactless manner. The model was trained using 2,973 nights of synchronized polysomnography (PSG) and audio recordings obtained from hospital- and home-based settings. Validation and independent testing were performed on 664 and 802 nights, respectively. Audio signals were converted into Mel spectrograms and processed using a Vision Transformer-based architecture. Performance was evaluated at the 30-second epoch level using sensitivity, specificity, precision, F1 score, accuracy, and Cohen's κ. ODI estimation was assessed using Pearson correlation, Bland-Altman analysis, mean absolute error (MAE), and root mean square error (RMSE). For epoch-by-epoch desaturation detection, the model achieved a sensitivity of 0.79, specificity of 0.95, precision of 0.78, F1 score of 0.79, overall accuracy of 0.92, and κ of 0.74. Estimated ODI showed agreement with PSG-derived ODI (r = 0.93, R² = 0.87, p < 0.001). Bland-Altman analysis demonstrated a mean bias of -0.29 events/h with 95% limits of agreement from -14.73 to 14.14 events/h. Breathing sound-based deep learning enables contactless detection of oxygen desaturation events and reliable ODI estimation. This approach may provide a scalable, non-contact method for sleep-disordered breathing assessment in real-world settings.

title: Modulation of the gut microbiota-arginine axis restrains inflammation and reduces post-infarction fibrosis.
authorString: Liu X, Wang C, Ma X, Shu X, Wu Y, Dong Z, Liu F.
abstractText: Myocardial infarction (MI) triggers a robust inflammatory response that critically dictates the trajectory of cardiac repair, making the modulation of immune cells a vital therapeutic target. While the gut-heart axis is increasingly recognized in cardiovascular diseases, the upstream gut-derived signals regulating post-infarction immunity remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to characterize the dynamic changes in gut microbiota and metabolite profiles post-MI and investigate their role in cardiac inflammation and fibrosis. Using a murine model of MI, the study integrated 16 S rRNA sequencing, untargeted metabolomics, flow cytometry, and histological analyses. MI induced severe intestinal barrier dysfunction and progressive gut dysbiosis, significantly depleting Desulfovibrionaceae and Helicobacteraceae. This microbial remodeling converged on a profound reduction in both intestinal and circulating arginine levels. Consequently, this metabolic deficit was associated with an exacerbated accumulation of pro-inflammatory Ly6Chigh monocytes and CD80+ M1-like macrophages in the ischemic myocardium at day 3, driving extensive fibrotic remodeling by day 14. To validate this functional axis, targeted interventions were employed. Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) promoted partial microbial reconstitution and attenuated myocardial fibrosis in antibiotic-pretreated MI mice. Similarly, systemic L-arginine supplementation reduced the early accumulation of inflammatory myeloid populations and reduced myocardial fibrosis at day 14. Overall, the identified gut microbiota-arginine-immune axis acts as a critical determinant of infarct healing. These findings demonstrate that targeting upstream intestinal metabolic perturbations, through microbiota-directed therapies or metabolic recalibration, represents a biologically plausible strategy to mitigate adverse ventricular remodeling and heart failure after MI.

title: Preventive dental scaling and cardiovascular disease according to periodontal disease status: a nationwide cohort study.
authorString: Lee KH, Choi YY.
abstractText: This study aimed to evaluate the association between the frequency of preventive dental scaling and the incidence of cardiovascular disease (CVD) in a nationwide population-based cohort. Data from the Korean National Health Insurance Service-Health Screening Cohort were used in this study. A total of 381,530 participants were included, of whom 10,889 experienced new CVD events during the follow-up period. Preventive dental scaling was assessed using insurance claim codes over two years from 2013 to 2015, and categorized into three groups: no scaling, one session, and two or more sessions. The primary outcome was incident CVD, defined as hospitalization owing to stroke, myocardial infarction, or heart failure. Hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated using Cox proportional hazard regression models. Compared with the no-scaling group, the fully adjusted HRs for incident CVD were 0.85 (95% CI, 0.81-0.90) in the one-session group and 0.68 (95% CI, 0.61-0.76) in the two-or-more-sessions group (P for trend < 0.001). Subgroup analyses revealed a significant inverse association among participants without claims-defined periodontal disease, whereas no significant association was observed among those with periodontal disease (P for interaction = 0.019). Preventive dental scaling was associated with a lower hazard of incident CVD, with a more pronounced association among participants without claims-defined periodontal disease. A causal protective effect cannot be established from these observational findings. The observed association between dental scaling and cardiovascular outcomes warrants further investigation but does not establish scaling as a measure for CVD prevention.

title: The prognostic value of the triglyceride-glucose index in individuals with hypertension.
authorString: D'Elia L, Galletti F, La Fata E, Ciampa C, Salvatore V, Stranges S.
abstractText: Hypertension frequently coexists with metabolic abnormalities that contribute to cardiovascular risk. The triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index is a simple surrogate marker of insulin resistance that may also reflect early cardiometabolic and cardiovascular vulnerability. This narrative review examines the prognostic relevance of TyG for all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, and fatal or non-fatal cardiovascular events in hypertension. PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched through 5 October 2026, without date or language restrictions. Evidence from primary hypertensive cohorts generally supports associations between higher TyG and adverse outcomes, although their magnitude and shape vary, with both linear and nonlinear patterns reported. Findings are most consistent among hypertensive patients with diabetes, whereas results from other high-risk settings and hypertension-specific subgroup analyses are more heterogeneous. Differences in TyG calculation, modeling, glycemic status, clinical settings, and overlapping cohorts complicate comparisons across studies. Overall, TyG may represent a readily available, low-cost marker of early cardiometabolic and cardiovascular vulnerability, beyond its role as a surrogate of insulin resistance, with potential to refine cardiovascular risk stratification in hypertension. Further prospective validation should establish its incremental predictive value beyond conventional cardiovascular risk factors and established risk scores.

title: Nursing Care for Managing Excess Fluid Volume (00026) in Chronic Kidney Disease Hemodialysis Patients: An Integrative Review.
authorString: Sapula CDCN, Ferreira RC, Zuchatti BV, de Lima JF, Quirino LP, Duran ECM.
abstractText: IntroChronic kidney disease affects 8-16% of the global population and is the seventh leading risk factor for mortality worldwide. An estimated 850 million people live with kidney disease, primarily in low- and middle-income countries. The rising prevalence of this disease is driven by rapid population growth, aging, and the dual burden of infectious and noncommunicable diseases such as diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and hypertension. In advanced stages, hemodialysis remains the most common renal replacement therapy, accounting for approximately 88% of treatments worldwide. Thus, this study aims to present the main nursing interventions, activities, and outcomes related to the nursing diagnosis Excess Fluid Volume, identified through an integrative literature review.MethodsIntegrative literature review was conducted using a systematic and rigorous methodological approach. Searches were performed in the following databases: Virtual Health Library (VHL), Cochrane Library, Excerpta Medica Database (Embase), Medical Literature Analysis and Retrieval System Online (MEDLINE), PubMed, SciVerse Scopus, Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature (CINAHL), Web of Science, Nursing Database (BDENF), Latin American and Caribbean Health Sciences Literature (LILACS), Spanish Bibliographic Index in Health Sciences (IBECS), and ProQuest LLC.ResultsThe review included 13 studies that identified key nursing care related to the diagnosis Excess Fluid Volume. Main interventions involved nursing consultation, clinical follow-up, fluid management, and health education focused on self-care and treatment adherence. Activities emphasize monitoring vital signs, weight, edema, and fluid balance, as well as medication and diet guidance. Reported outcomes included improved fluid and blood pressure control, reduced hypervolemia and symptoms, greater adherence to therapeutic regimens, prevention of cardiovascular complications, and decreased morbidity and mortality.ConclusionThe care for this population extends beyond clinical assessment, encompassing health education, self-care promotion, and complication prevention. Such nursing interventions strengthen treatment adherence, maintain hemodynamic stability, and minimize adverse events.

title: Alcohol and cardiovascular disease: inter-organ crosstalk, microvascular dysfunction, and cardiovascular ageing.
authorString: Yokus B, Ungvari Z, Haskó G, Lohoff FW, Thum T, Pacher P.
abstractText: Alcohol-related cardiovascular risk is being fundamentally reappraised. Observational associations suggesting cardioprotection with light-to-moderate drinking have been challenged by contemporary cohort analyses, Mendelian-randomization studies, biomarker-informed investigations, and updated public-health guidance. Uncertainty nevertheless persists at very low exposure levels and for selected coronary or all-cause outcomes. Alcohol is therefore best viewed as a dose-, pattern-, and host-dependent cardiovascular stressor. Acute or binge drinking, sustained heavy intake, chronic intake with episodic binges, and withdrawal produce overlapping but distinct phenotypes, including hypertension, atrial fibrillation, ventricular arrhythmias, sudden death, alcohol-associated cardiomyopathy, heart failure, stroke, and vascular disease. A systems-cardiology framework is presented in which direct myocardial injury, electrical instability, haemodynamic and autonomic stress, vascular and microvascular dysfunction, and disrupted inter-organ signalling interact. Ethanol and acetaldehyde toxicity, redox imbalance, microbial and inflammatory mediators, neurohumoral activation, and metabolic or electrolyte disturbances can impair endothelial signalling, mitochondrial energetics, excitation-contraction coupling, electrical stability, and repair. Pathway dominance varies across exposure patterns and susceptible hosts; coronary microvascular dysfunction may represent a convergence pathway rather than an obligatory mediator. Cumulative injury can diminish perfusion, contractile, electrical, autonomic, and exercise reserve. Alcohol-related cardiovascular ageing is proposed as a unifying cumulative phenotype encompassing mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative and nitrative stress, inflammageing, senescence, impaired repair, circadian and epigenetic dysregulation, fibrosis, and ventriculo-arterial uncoupling, although direct human evidence remains incomplete. Age, biological sex, genetics, comorbidities, sleep-circadian disruption, nutrition, medications, and polysubstance misuse may modify pathway dominance and reversibility. Structured exposure assessment and alcohol reduction or abstinence, when indicated, are actionable components of cardiovascular prevention and care.

title: Potential Brain Predictors of Stroke Risk: A Structural, Functional, and Central Autonomic Network Framework
authorString: Chen J, Wilke M, Bähr M.
abstractText: Stroke risk is assessed using factors such as hypertension, diabetes, smoking and atrial fibrillation. However, these factors describe sources of risk but do not reveal how long-term vascular, metabolic and cardiac stress has affected the brain. Structural MRI can show accumulated brain injury, whereas functional MRI reflects dynamic brain states and may provide complementary information about vulnerability. Their temporal sequence and predictive value require longitudinal validation. This Review evaluates brain imaging features as candidate stroke-risk markers and proposes the central autonomic network as a mechanistic framework linking brain function with cardiac rhythm, blood pressure, inflammation and metabolism.

title: Potential Brain Predictors of Stroke Risk: A Structural, Functional, and Central Autonomic Network Framework
authorString: Chen J, Wilke M, Bähr M.
abstractText: Stroke risk is assessed using factors such as hypertension, diabetes, smoking and atrial fibrillation. However, these factors describe sources of risk but do not reveal how long-term vascular, metabolic and cardiac stress has affected the brain. Their temporal sequence and predictive value require longitudinal validation. title: Multimorbidity Extent and Contributing Factors Among Hospitalized Chronic Kidney Disease Patients in Resource-Limited Settings.
authorString: Zeleke TK, Ferede AA, Tamene FB, Limenh LW, Wondm SA, Abebe RB, Abdela OA.
abstractText: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is frequently accompanied by multimorbidity, resulting in increased hospitalization, healthcare expenditure, and medication burden. Despite this, evidence on the extent and contributing factors of multimorbidity among CKD patients in Ethiopia is scarce. This study assessed the prevalence of multimorbidity and its associated factors among hospitalized CKD patients. A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted among hospitalized CKD patients in three comprehensive specialized hospitals. Participants were selected using simple random sampling. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize the data, and comparisons were made using the chi-square test and the t-test. Factors associated with multimorbidity were identified using binary logistic regression. Statistical significance was defined as a p value of less than 0.05 with a 95% confidence interval. The prevalence of multimorbidity was 85.7%, with participants having an average of two comorbid conditions. Hypertension was the most common comorbid condition. Multimorbidity was significantly associated with aging (AOR = 1.67 (95% CI 1.21-2.31), higher body mass index (AOR = 1.70 (95% CI 1.23-2.35), and lower creatinine clearance (AOR = 0.95 (95% CI 0.92-0.99)). Multimorbidity is highly prevalent among hospitalized CKD patients in Ethiopia. Aging, increased body mass index, and reduced renal function were significant contributing factors. Clinical management strategies should prioritize early detection and tailored care for elderly and overweight patients and those with impaired kidney function.

title: Dynamic blood glucose trajectory is 28-day all-cause mortality in critically ill patients with heart failure: A survival prediction analysis.
authorString: Cun SH, Meng R, Jiang MH, Pan JM, Zou WH, Wang P, Yang HY, Yu F, Li DM, Weng ZY, He GH.

journal.title: Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine

abstractText: BackgroundHeart failure (HF) is a global public health issue. Blood glucose influences HF progression, but research on its dynamic changes and mortglity remains limited.ObjectiveThis study aimed to investigate the association of baseline admission blood glucose and its dynamic changes with all-cause mortality in patients with HF.MethodsThis retrospective cohort study used data from MIMIC-IV and a tertiary hospital. We identified distinct glycemic trajectories using group-based trajectory modeling (GBTM) and assessed their association with 28-day all-cause mortality via Cox proportional hazards models and restricted cubic spline analysis (RCS). Machine learning models were applied to evaluate the predictive value of glycemia.ResultsA total of 6142 patients from the MIMIC-IV database and 391 local patients were included. Results showed that five dynamic blood glucose trajectory groups were identified. Among them, the moderate-to-high and high-level groups exhibited elevated mortality risk [HR (95% CI): 1.546 (1.231-1.942); 1.572 (1.140-2.168)]. Incorporating blood glucose trajectories into predictive models moderately improved the predictive performance for outcomes, and the Deepsurv model demonstrated better predictive accuracy and stability.ConclusionAlthough current retrospective design limits causal inference and warrants prospective validation, the present study provides evidence that dynamic blood glucose fluctuations demonstrate superior prognostic value compared to baseline measurements for predicting mortality in severe HF patients. Furthermore, machine learning based on glucose trajectory modeling enables early identification of high-risk individuals.

title: Massive subchorionic thrombohematoma (Breus' mole): A nationwide retrospective study in Japan.
authorString: Nagao T, Ito Y, Suemitsu T, Hasegawa A, Goto M, Hino Y, Honda I, Ishibashi H, Kinjo T, Nagasaki S, Oyama R, Takahashi N, Tamaki R, Tsumura K, Waratani M, Yamamoto H, Yamamoto M, Yanaihara N, Samura O.

journal.title: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics

abstractText: To estimate the incidence, diagnostic features, and perinatal outcomes of massive subchorionic thrombohematoma (MST) in Japan. This nationwide multicenter retrospective study (2018-2023) analyzed confirmed cases of MST, defined as a laminated hematoma with a maximum thickness ≥1 cm. Maternal characteristics, sonographic patterns, and perinatal complications were evaluated. Of 346 741 deliveries across 87 tertiary perinatal centers, 69 pathologically confirmed MST cases were identified at 27 centers, yielding an incidence of 0.019% (69/346 741). Median maternal age was 33 years and body mass index (BMI) was 21.1. Chronic hypertension was present in 8.7% (6/69). Diagnoses occurred antenatally in 81.2% (56/69) and postpartum in 18.8% (13/69). Ultrasound findings included placentomegaly or a placental mass with variable echogenicity. During follow-up, echogenicity changed in 28% of cases and lesion size in 57%. Perinatal outcomes included induced abortion in 13.0% (9/69), miscarriage before 22 weeks in 5.8% (4/69), stillbirth in 7.2% (5/69), preterm birth in 52.2% (36/69), and term delivery in 21.7% (15/69). Among preterm births, one neonatal death and two infant deaths occurred. After excluding induced abortion and miscarriage before 22 weeks, small-for-gestational-age status was present in 53.6% (30/56) of infants, pre-eclampsia occurred in 16.1% (9/56), and preterm premature rupture of membranes occurred in 23.2% (13/56). Neonatal intensive care unit admission was required for 82.4% (42/51) of live births. MST is a rare but high-risk placental disorder associated with miscarriage, stillbirth, preterm birth, impaired fetal growth, and pre-eclampsia. When MST is suspected antenatally, close maternal and fetal surveillance is warranted.

title: Comprehensive reporting of acute aortic syndromes: a practical approach for radiologists.
authorString: Dessouky R, Shabaan RRA, Abdul Rahman AAE, Khalil MF, Frere RAF.
abstractText: Acute aortic syndromes (AAS) are a group of aortic pathologies with high morbidity and mortality. In the emergency setting, an accurate diagnosis is usually achieved by aortic computed tomography angiography (CTA). Recently, reporting and management guidelines have evolved due to modifications in surgical techniques and the expansion in utilization of endovascular techniques. This being said, radiologists require a more in-depth knowledge of key points to report to surgeons, their clinical implications, and some insights into available imaging-guided treatment options. Given the urgent nature of AAS, the need for rapid, detailed, and standardized reporting is crucial. In this review, we aim to introduce a step-by-step approach to accurate reporting of AAS, discussing recent guidelines and the role of imaging in the preprocedural evaluation of each disease entity (namely, intramural hematoma, penetrating aortic ulcer, and aortic dissection). Additionally, we will highlight the role of key imaging findings in the management of each disease entity. KEY POINTS: Question Acute aortic syndromes require rapid, sufficiently detailed, and accurate diagnosis to allow for timely patient management. Findings In this article, we propose a step-by-step approach using a structured reporting checklist. Clinical relevance Using a stepwise approach will allow timely reporting, give important details, and help guide further patient care.

title: Fenestrated Endografts Provide Superior Outcomes Compared to Branched Devices in Juxtarenal Aortic Repair.
authorString: Torrealba JI, Berndt R, Nana P, Apostolidis G, Panuccio G, Kölbel T.
abstractText:
Introduction

Urgent endovascular juxtarenal aortic repair with custom-made fenestrated devices is not feasible due to its long elaboration time. Off-the-shelf branched devices can be used, however, durability of the target vessels, especially renal artery branches, is of concern. Our objective is to compare mid and long-term patency of target vessels (TV), especially renal arteries (RA) in juxtarenal fenestrated or branched aortic endovascular repair.

Methods

Single-center retrospective study identifying all patients undergoing fenestrated or branched endovascular repair (f/bEVAR) for juxtarenal aortic aneurysms (JAA) between 2011-2022. A FEVAR group with use of fenestrations to incorporate target vessels (TV) and a BEVAR group, with use of branches were created. Clinical and anatomical characteristics as well as perioperative technical success and complications were compared. The primary endpoint was the assessment of RA primary patency, freedom from endoleaks and instability (endpoint including occlusion, endoleak or need for reintervention) at follow-up. Secondary endpoints were the assessment of CT-SMA patency rates, freedom from endoleak and instability at follow-up and the evaluation of the anatomical and clinical factors associated with renal artery bridging covered stent (BCS) occlusion.

Results

From 2011-2022, FEVAR was performed in 212 patients and BEVAR in 57. There were no statistical differences in demographics. The BEVAR group presented more frequently as urgencies (61% vs 11% for FEVAR p <,001). 955 TV were incorporated, including 536 RA. Technical success was 99%. BEVAR patients experienced higher perioperative death rates (14% vs 3% in FEVAR; p 0,005) and major complications (53% vs 17% in FEVAR; p <,001). Primary patency of RA in FEVAR was 99% at 3 years vs 74% for BEVAR (p < ,001). Freedom from RA BCS endoleaks were 97% at 3 years for the FEVAR group vs 87% in the BEVAR group (p <,001). Freedom from RA instability at 3 years was 95% in the FEVAR group vs 63% for the BEVAR group (p <,001). For CT-SMA only freedom from instability showed significant better outcomes at 3 years in the FEVAR group (96% vs 88% for BEVAR ; p ,006). In the multivariate analysis, the use of branches was the only factor associated with loss of patency in the RA.

Conclusions

In complex aortic repair for JAA, fenestrated devices achieved high patency rates while branched devices, mostly done for urgencies, are associated with significantly worse RA outcomes.

title: Successful Non-Coronary Cusp Ablation in Type B Wolff-Parkinson-White Syndrome With an rS Pattern in Lead V1.
authorString: Yamauchi Y, Sagawa Y, Murata K, Oda A, Aonuma K.
abstractText: A Type B Wolff-Parkinson-White pattern with an rS morphology in Lead V1 suggested a right anterior or anterolateral accessory pathway, whereas detailed activation mapping identified a para-Hisian accessory pathway. Despite atypical ECG features, including relatively large initial r-wave amplitudes in Leads V1 and V2, radiofrequency ablation from the noncoronary cusp successfully eliminated the pathway. This case highlights the limitations of ECG-based localization and supports consideration of the noncoronary cusp when ablation from the right para-Hisian region is unsuccessful.

title: Central Obesity and Estimated Coronary Heart Disease Risk Among Jordanian Women Aged 30-50 Years: A Framingham Risk Score Analysis.
authorString: Alboqai OK, Obeidat B, Ebqa'ai MA, O Ibrahim M, Bleedy N, Al-Sa'adi TIS, Salma BMA, Alkadri D, Alrabadi N, Gamal M.
abstractText:
Background

Obesity is a well-established modifiable risk factor for cardiovascular disease (CVD), particularly coronary heart disease (CHD). Its high prevalence among Jordanian women aged 30-50 years highlights the need for early cardiovascular risk assessment to support targeted preventive strategies.

Objective

To estimate the 10-year risk of CHD among Jordanian women aged 30-50 years using the Framingham risk score (FRS) and to examine the associations between general obesity, central obesity, cardiometabolic risk factors, and estimated CHD risk.

Methods

A cross-sectional study was conducted among 230 Jordanian women aged 30-50 years who were recruited using a multistage cluster sampling technique. Standardized anthropometric measurements, including body weight, height, and waist circumference (WC), were obtained to calculate body mass index (BMI) and waist-to-height ratio (WHtR). Blood pressure was measured according to standardized procedures, and fasting blood samples were analyzed to determine fasting blood glucose and lipid profile parameters. Smoking status and physical activity were assessed using structured questionnaires. The 10-year risk of CHD was estimated using the FRS. Descriptive and inferential statistical analyses were performed to evaluate the associations between obesity indices and estimated CHD risk.

Results

General obesity was identified in 39.1% of participants, while 40.9% had central obesity based on WC (≥ 88 cm). Nearly half of the participants (47.0%) were current smokers, and 21.3% reported low levels of physical activity. According to the FRS, 66.1% of participants were classified as having low CHD risk, 16.5% as moderate risk, and 17.4% as high risk. Higher BMI and central obesity were significantly associated with elevated blood pressure, fasting blood glucose, triglyceride levels, and LDL cholesterol, as well as lower HDL cholesterol (all p < 0.001). Smoking, physical inactivity, and both general and central obesity were significantly associated with an increased estimated risk of CHD.

Conclusion

Jordanian women aged 30-50 years exhibited a substantial burden of both general and central obesity, accompanied by an increased estimated risk of CHD. These findings underscore the importance of routine cardiovascular risk assessment and comprehensive lifestyle interventions focusing on weight management, smoking cessation, and regular physical activity. Because the FRS has not been specifically validated in Jordanian women, the estimated absolute cardiovascular risk should be interpreted with caution.

title: Incidental Detection of a Pulmonary Valve Thrombus in a 60-Year-Old Woman: A Case Report.
authorString: Singh A, Sharma N, Bhatia V.
abstractText: Pulmonary valve thrombus is a rare cardiac finding, particularly when identified incidentally in a patient without established venous thromboembolism or infective endocarditis. We report the case of a 60-year-old woman who presented with atypical chest discomfort and exertional dyspnoea. She described a sensation of being unable to take an adequate breath, while her husband had noticed increased breathing effort during routine walking. She had no previous history of ischemic heart disease or cerebrovascular disease and was a lifelong non-smoker. Cardiovascular examination was unremarkable, with normal blood pressure and oxygen saturation. Transthoracic echocardiography initially demonstrated no significant structural cardiac abnormalities or valvular pathology. CT coronary angiography, performed to investigate her symptoms, demonstrated no flow-limiting coronary artery disease but incidentally identified a filling defect associated with the pulmonary valve. Dedicated CT pulmonary angiography excluded pulmonary embolism but confirmed the pulmonary valve lesion. Cardiac MRI demonstrated a mass associated with the pulmonary valve, with appearances most consistent with thrombus. There was no clinical, laboratory, or imaging evidence of infective endocarditis. The patient was treated with warfarin anticoagulation. Follow-up CT pulmonary angiography after three months demonstrated complete resolution of the pulmonary valve lesion, supporting the diagnosis of thrombus. This case highlights the importance of considering pulmonary valve thrombus in the differential diagnosis of an incidentally detected valvular mass and demonstrates the value of multimodality cardiac imaging in differentiating thrombus from infective vegetation and benign valvular tumours.

title: Phenotypic Presentation of Atypical Familial Partial Lipodystrophy in a Patient With a Rare Mutation in the <i>LMNA</i> Gene: A Case Report and Literature Review.
authorString: Pereira RZ, Santana YWS, Monti G, Fernandes VO, Montenegro RM, Zajdenverg L, Negrato CA.
abstractText:
Background

Variants in the LMNA gene are classically associated with familial partial lipodystrophy type 2 (FPLD2/Dunnigan syndrome). However, certain mutations produce severe multisystemic phenotypes that may mimic congenital generalized lipodystrophy (CGL). This case adds to the literature by delineating the distinct syndromic expression of the LMNA p.Arg349Trp variant and underscoring the need for early recognition to guide cardiovascular and renal surveillance.

Clinical findings

A 41-year-old woman presented to a specialized diabetes clinic serving low-income populations with severe lipoatrophy of the face and limbs, relative preservation of truncal adiposity, refractory diabetes, severe hypertriglyceridemia, arterial hypertension, and heart failure. Due to the pattern of lipodystrophy, severe systemic involvement, and absence of compensatory cervicofacial fat accumulation, CGL (Berardinelli-Seip syndrome) was initially suspected.

Diagnoses interventions and outcomes

Next-generation sequencing identified a heterozygous pathogenic LMNA variant, c.1045C>T (p.Arg349Trp). At baseline, the patient presented with established proteinuric nephropathy, severe hypertriglyceridemia, and cardiovascular disease. Following multidisciplinary care and an optimized pharmacological protocol, transient improvement in metabolic and glycemic profiles was achieved. However, despite good therapeutic response, socioeconomic barriers disrupted access to high-cost medications, and she deteriorated to cardiovascular and hepatic failure, dying from cardiogenic shock and sepsis of abdominal origin in less than 2 years of follow-up.

Conclusion

This case highlights the high clinical severity of the LMNA p.Arg349Trp variant. Recognizing it as a distinct syndromic entity is crucial to prevent diagnostic delays, enabling timely cardiovascular and renal surveillance, particularly in resource-limited settings where treatment interruptions can have fatal consequences.

title: Left Atrial Appendage Aneurysm Presenting With Atrial Fibrillation in a Young Woman: A Case Report.
authorString: Parvizi R, Meshgi S, Rostamzadeh M, Negargar S, Bilehjani E, Fakhari S, Faravan A.
abstractText: Left atrial appendage aneurysm (LAAA) is a rare cardiac anomaly. We report a 25-year-old woman with LAAA presenting with atrial fibrillation and dyspnea. Multimodality imaging enabled diagnosis, and successful surgical resection was performed. Histopathology confirmed a benign aneurysm. At 6-month follow-up, no recurrence or thromboembolic events were observed.

title: Dapagliflozin transfer in breast milk may be clinically insignificant-An opportunity for optimization of evidence-based management of heart failure in postpartum patients.
authorString: Bartell A, Erickson J, Anderson LJ, Boitos L, Katzman HR, Mohamed M, Dwyer S, Tumbarello J, Kirschen GW, Langen E, Grabowski A, Gregg B.
abstractText:
Background

Dapagliflozin (DAPA), a sodium-glucose co-transporter inhibitor (SGLT2i), has been shown to prevent the development of heart failure and slow the progression of pre-existing heart failure; however, there are limited data published to demonstrate the safety of postpartum lactating individuals taking SGLT2is.

Methods

Lactating patients received two oral doses of 10 mg DAPA over a 48-h period. Breast milk and plasma were collected 2 h after the second dose. Samples were processed via liquid chromatography mass spectrometry (LCMS) analysis. Breast milk concentrations of DAPA were divided by plasma concentrations of DAPA (in ng/mL). The absolute (AID; i.e., daily infant dose) and relative infant doses (RID) were performed. An RID of 10% was considered the limit of acceptable exposure.

Results

Three of four participants were able to produce enough sample for assessment. Across three samples, the mean DAPA concentrations in plasma and breast milk were 77.6 ± 10.2 and 16.8 ± 3.1 ng/mL, respectively. Mean AID was 8.04 × 10-3 ± 2.50 × 10-3 mg/day and the mean RID was 7.73 ± 3.9%.

Conclusions

This study demonstrates that human breast milk collected at peak anticipated maternal concentrations of DAPA has a mean RID below 10%. This is the first report of human transfer levels for DAPA, generating preliminary lactation-specific pharmacokinetic data that are essential to support evidence-based treatment of breastfeeding individuals and reduce disparities in their representation within cardiovascular therapeutic research.

title: Perioperative management of aortic root thrombus following HeartMate 3 implantation: review of the literature.
authorString: Izumida T, Imamura T, Nakamura M, Nakagaito M, Yokoyama S, Nagura S, Doi T, Kinugawa K.

journal.title: Journal of artificial organs : the official journal of the Japanese Society for Artificial Organs

abstractText: Aortic root thrombosis (ART) is an increasingly recognized complication in patients supported with continuous-flow left ventricular assist devices (LVADs), although its incidence, prognosis, and optimal management remain poorly defined. We report 2 cases of early, asymptomatic ART detected on postoperative day 2 by routine transthoracic echocardiography after HeartMate 3 implantation. In both cases, ART developed in the setting of a persistently closed aortic valve and was identified before embolic complications occurred. Both patients were successfully managed with intensified anticoagulation, temporary pump speed escalation to maintain valve closure, and temporary restriction of physical activity. ART resolved completely without symptomatic embolic events, invasive intervention, or antiplatelet therapy, and no recurrence was observed during follow-up. These cases and the available literature suggest that early ART may be clinically silent and underrecognized even in the contemporary HeartMate 3 era. Routine early echocardiographic surveillance may facilitate timely detection, and a conservative, physiology-guided strategy focused on anticoagulation and flow adjustment appears effective in carefully selected patients under close monitoring.

title: The Impact of Prolonged Pre-Heart Transplantation Left Ventricular Assist Device on Post-Transplantation Outcomes.
authorString: Puspitarani RADA, Legtenberg S, Erasmus ME, Ter Maaten JM, Krikken JA, van den Broek SAJ, Droogh JM, Verhaegh AJFP, Kuijpers M, Douglas YL, Westenbrink BD, Damman K.
abstractText: Durable mechanical circulatory support with a left ventricular assist device (LVAD) serves as bridge to heart transplantation (HTx) in patients with advanced heart failure. LVAD therapy is associated with improved outcomes, but has inherent limitations, including device-related complications. In this study, we aimed to evaluate the impact of prolonged LVAD support in patients who underwent HTx as compared to those without LVAD support. We retrospectively analysed 148 HTx recipients at University Medical Center Groningen, the Netherlands (2007-2023): 52 with prior LVAD support and 96 direct HTx patients. Outcomes included post-HTx survival, rejection requiring treatment, 1-year cardiac haemodynamics, and need for kidney replacement therapy. Median LVAD duration was 757 days (range 16-2,113). The LVAD group had fewer females (21% vs 54%; p<0.001). After a median 3.5-year follow-up, post-HTx survival was similar between groups (hazard ratio 0.83; 95% confidence interval 0.40-1.6; p=0.52). No significant differences were observed in the incidence of rejection requiring therapy (p=0.91) nor need for kidney replacement therapy (p=0.05-0.42). At 1-year post-HTx, the LVAD group showed modestly elevated pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (12.7 vs 10.6 mmHg; p=0.03) and reduced cardiac index (3.0 vs 3.3 L/min/m2; p=0.03) compared to direct HTx recipients. Prolonged LVAD support as bridge-to-transplantation showed no statistically significant differences with direct HTx in terms of post-HTx survival, rejection rates, and renal function despite minor differences in 1-year haemodynamic parameters.

title: Sensor-Based Force-Frequency Relation Assessment in Personalised Cardiovascular Care: An Overview.
authorString: Bombardini T, Bianchini E.
abstractText: Contractility is the intrinsic ability of the heart muscle to generate force and shorten. The force-frequency relation can reveal initial alterations between normal and abnormal contractility, making it a practical index for clinical evaluation. This narrative review provides a picture of force-frequency relationship assessment, including stress echocardiography laboratories (echo labs), nuclear laboratories (nuclear labs), implantable systems, ambulatory sensors, and wearable sensors. Different approaches have been investigated in the literature, and their translation into practice could be valuable, even if challenging. With a vision for the future, real-time monitoring systems based on wearable or implantable devices, able to continuously track force-frequency changes during daily activities, could constitute a concrete opportunity for improved management of conditions such as chronic heart failure and coronary artery disease.

title: Danggui-Shaoyao-San Alleviates Hyperlipidemia-Induced Vascular Endothelial Barrier Dysfunction and Modulates the Rap1/PI3K/AKT Pathway in ApoE<sup>-/-</sup> Mice.
authorString: Zhao Y, Shi H, Zhang W, Li K, Lin G, Chen Y, Lin X, Zhao X, Fan H.
abstractText:
Ethnopharmacological relevance

Hyperlipidemia (HL) is a major cardiovascular risk factor that can induce early endothelial dysfunction and compromise vascular endothelial barrier integrity. Danggui-Shaoyao-San (DSS), a traditional Chinese herbal formula, has shown potential vascular protective effects. However, the circulating DSS-associated constituents and molecular pathways potentially involved in its protective effects against HL-induced endothelial barrier dysfunction remain incompletely understood.

Materials and methods

ApoE-/- mice fed a high-fat diet (HFD) were used to establish a model of HL-associated vascular endothelial barrier injury and to evaluate the effects of different doses of DSS. UPLC-Q-TOF-MS was used to characterize DSS-associated constituents detected in serum. Metabolic parameters, inflammatory markers, vascular permeability, aortic histopathology, endothelial ultrastructure, and junctional protein expression were evaluated. Transcriptomic analysis and molecular docking were integrated to explore potential targets and signaling pathways. Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) was subsequently performed to evaluate the direct binding of representative serum constituents to RAP1B. Rap1-GTP pull-down, Western blotting, and immunofluorescence analyses were further used to assess Rap1 activation, PI3K/AKT phosphorylation, and endothelial junctional proteins.

Results

Mass spectrometry enabled the putative annotation of 19 DSS-associated serum constituents. DSS treatment alleviated HFD-induced metabolic derangements and systemic inflammation, reduced aortic permeability, and preserved endothelial morphology and junctional integrity. Transcriptomic analysis and molecular docking analyses highlighted Ras-related protein 1 (Rap1) and PI3K/AKT-related signaling for subsequent experimental investigation. SPR analysis revealed concentration-dependent binding of paeoniflorin, albiflorin, and ligustilide to RAP1B, with apparent dissociation constants (K_D) of 4.158, 4.240, and 28.71 μM, respectively. Rap1 activation, quantified as the GTP-Rap1/total Rap1A/1B ratio, was reduced in the HFD model group and increased following DSS treatment. The DSS-associated increase in Rap1 activation were accompanied by increased PI3K and AKT phosphorylation and expression of endothelial junctional proteins, including ZO-1, occludin, claudin-1, and VE-cadherin.

Conclusion

DSS alleviated HL-associated vascular endothelial barrier dysfunction in HFD-fed ApoE-/- mice, accompanied by improvements in metabolic homeostasis and preservation of endothelial junctional integrity. The in vitro binding of selected serum constituents to recombinant RAP1B, together with restored Rap1 activation and increased PI3K/AKT phosphorylation, is consistent with the potential involvement of Rap1-associated signaling in the vascular protective effects of DSS. These findings provide preclinical evidence supporting further investigation of DSS for hyperlipidemia-associated vascular injury.

title: Cumulative exposure and longitudinal changes in KDM age Acceleration-Integrated insulin resistance indices in relation to incident cardiometabolic multimorbidity among individuals with Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic syndrome stages 0-3: A prospective cohort study.
authorString: Tan MY, Jiang ZN, Huang SJ.
abstractText: Insulin resistance (IR) and biological aging may jointly contribute to cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome progression, but longitudinal evidence for cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) is limited. Using the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study, we included participants with CKM stages 0-3 who were free of CMM. KDM age acceleration was integrated with TyG and related IR indices. Cox models assessed baseline and Wave 3 levels, cumulative exposure, annualized change, and longitudinal exposure profiles in relation to incident CMM. Predictive performance was evaluated using the C-index, time-dependent AUC, Brier score, and reclassification metrics. Higher baseline and Wave 3 levels of all KDM age acceleration-integrated IR indices were associated with higher CMM risk when modeled continuously, whereas associations with cumulative exposure were less consistent. Per 1-SD increase, the adjusted HRs were 1.28, 1.24, and 1.21 for baseline, Wave 3, and cumulative KDM age acceleration × TyG, respectively. In exploratory longitudinal exposure-profile analyses, higher-level profiles were associated with increased CMM risk for several indices, although these profiles mainly reflected relative exposure levels across the two assessments rather than distinct temporal trajectories. The cumulative KDM age acceleration × TyG model achieved an optimism-corrected C-index of 0.762 and a 5-year AUC of 0.770. Higher single-time-point levels of KDM age acceleration-integrated IR indices were associated with incident CMM, whereas associations with cumulative exposure were less consistent and annualized changes were not significantly associated with risk. Incremental predictive performance was modest.

title: Rab32 exacerbates myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury via PKA/P300/H3K18la-dependent glucose metabolic reprogramming.
authorString: Yao BF, Xing HN, Tan JM, Lu LQ, Luo XJ, Peng J.
abstractText: Glucose metabolic reprogramming, defined by uncoupling between glycolysis and glucose oxidation, is a critical determinant of cardiac dysfunction after ischemia/reperfusion (I/R), yet its upstream drivers remain elusive. RAB32, a mitochondrial Rab GTPase with A-kinase anchoring protein (AKAP) activity, participates in mitochondrial homeostasis, but its role in myocardial I/R injury and glucose metabolic reprogramming is unknown. We used cardiomyocyte-specific RAB32 knockout mice subjected to left anterior descending coronary artery ligation and H9c2 cells exposed to hypoxia/reoxygenation (H/R), combined with integrated transcriptomic profiling of I/R myocardium and metabolomic profiling of RAB32-knockdown cardiomyocytes. Using these complementary approaches, we identify RAB32 as a key driver of glucose metabolic reprogramming after I/R. RAB32 was upregulated in I/R myocardium and H/R cardiomyocytes. Cardiomyocyte-specific RAB32 deletion reduced infarct size, decreased CK, cTnI, and LDH levels, preserved cardiac function, and maintained mitochondrial homeostasis. Conversely, RAB32 knockdown attenuated, whereas RAB32 overexpression aggravated, H/R-induced cardiomyocyte injury and mitochondrial dysfunction. Mechanistically, RAB32 bound protein kinase A (PKA) through its AKAP domain, promoting PKA-dependent P300 phosphorylation and H3K18la elevation. H3K18la was enriched at promoter regions of HK2 and PDK4 and drove their transcription; HK2 enhanced glycolysis, whereas PDK4 phosphorylated and inhibited PDHA1, blocking pyruvate oxidation and uncoupling glycolysis from glucose oxidation. RAB32 ablation reversed these metabolic alterations, restoring ATP levels and coupling between glycolysis and glucose oxidation. These findings identify the RAB32/PKA/P300/H3K18la axis as a previously unappreciated epigenetic checkpoint governing glucose metabolic reprogramming in mouse hearts following I/R, nominating RAB32 and its downstream pathway as potential therapeutic targets for myocardial I/R injury.

title: <sup>1</sup>H MRS reveals impact of early adversity and age on neurometabolic profiles in women.
authorString: Mekle R, Fleck L, Bauer M, Deelchand DK, Buss C, Entringer S, Stein M, Fiebach JB, Endres M, Heim C.
abstractText: Exposure to early-life stress (ELS), including neglect or abuse, is known for its detrimental effects on brain health. This study investigated how ELS interacts with chronological age to impact on brain metabolism in middle-aged women using proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy (1H MRS) at 3 T. High-quality spectra from the hippocampus (HC) and posterior cingulate cortex (PCC) from 75 women, including 53% with ELS exposure before puberty, were analyzed. Generalized additive models assessed non-linear effects of ELS severity and chronological age on neurometabolites related to neuroinflammation and neurotransmitter cycling. Significant interactions emerged for myo-inositol (Ins) in both regions and glutamine (Gln) in the PCC, where greater ELS severity was linked to age-related increases in Ins and Gln concentrations. These results were robust when additionally controlling for symptoms of depression, anxiety, and PTSD, as well as SES, education, menopause status, and smoking. The observed patterns suggest that ELS exposure before puberty, at the older age range, is associated with glial and glutamatergic alterations that are indicative of neuroinflammation, potentially reflecting vulnerability to adverse brain health outcomes.

title: The conversion of pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells to eosinophil-like cells exacerbates the progression of pulmonary arterial hypertension with increased secretion of 12-HETE.
authorString: Jiao Z, Xu G, Zhu F, Zhang Y, Xu J, Chen Z, Yan A, Piao M, Dong Z, Chen L, Jia T, Zhang Y, Wang C, Chen Y, Xu J, He Q, Zhang J.
abstractText: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is characterised by progressive pulmonary arterial (PA) vascular remodeling, with abnormal phenotypic transformation of pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells (PASMCs) playing a central role. Arachidonic acid (AA) metabolites have been implicated in this process, yet the underlying cellular and molecular mechanisms by which its metabolite 12-hydroxyeicosatetraenoic acid (12-HETE) contributes to PAH remain incompletely understood. Plasma concentrations of 12-HETE were significantly elevated in PAH patients. In SU5416/hypoxia (SuHx)-induced PAH mouse model, the 12/15-lipoxygenase (12/15-LOX) inhibitor ML-351 markedly attenuated disease progression. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) analysis revealed a unrecognized phenotypic transdifferentiation of a subset of PASMCs into eosinophil-like (Eos-like) cells. Mechanistically, studies utilizing EOS-deficient (ΔdblGATA) mice demonstrated that these newly Eos-like cells, along with native eosinophils (EOS), secrete 12-HETE. In vitro CCK-8 assays confirmed that hypoxia-induced PASMC proliferation was attenuated by the leukotriene B4 receptor 2 (BLT2) antagonist LY255283, confirming that the 12-HETE/BLT2 axis drives PASMC proliferation, thereby creating a positive feedback loop that amplifies vascular remodeling. These findings establish the 12-HETE as a critical mediator of a novel EOS-PASMC signaling axis that drives PA vascular remodeling in PAH. This study highlights a promising new therapeutic strategy for PAH.

title: Altered directional brain-heart interactions across resting states and frequency bands in schizophrenia.
authorString: Peng X, Zhao L, Cheng Y, Zhang Y, Shen B, Huaihong A, Wang Y.
abstractText: Schizophrenia is associated with abnormalities in cortical activity and autonomic regulation, but directional brain-heart interaction (BHI) across resting states and frequency bands remains unclear. Resting-state electroencephalography (EEG) and electrocardiography (ECG) were recorded simultaneously in 33 medicated men with schizophrenia and 29 healthy men during eyes-open and eyes-closed conditions. Directional BHI was assessed across two coupling directions, two cardiac frequency components, and five EEG frequency bands. Global-average and spatial cluster-based permutation analyses were performed, with family-wise error rate correction across all 40 predefined BHI features. Compared with healthy controls, patients with schizophrenia showed higher theta, alpha, and beta EEG power during eyes-open rest and higher theta and alpha EEG power during eyes-closed rest after false discovery rate correction. Cardiac low-frequency (LF) and high-frequency (HF) spectral power did not differ significantly between groups. During eyes-open rest, patients showed lower global-average brain-to-heart high-frequency (BtH-HF) coupling across all five EEG bands (global family-wise error rate-corrected p = 0.0151-0.0349; Hedges' g = -0.911 to -0.841). This finding was supported by spatial cluster analysis and multitaper sensitivity analysis. No eyes-closed BtH-HF effects survived global correction. Although four eyes-open heart-to-brain (HtB) clusters were initially significant under the fixed-order model, none survived the Bayesian information criterion-based order sensitivity analysis. No significant Condition × Group interaction was detected across the five BtH-HF features. Schizophrenia was associated with reduced eyes-open BtH-HF coupling across EEG bands, indicating altered statistical brain-heart coupling.

title: Safely Navigating the MR-Linac: A New Risk Framework for Prostate SBRT Patients with Cardiac Devices.
authorString: Cooney JD, Gambino H, Lee D, Amodio N, Stojanovska J, Chen T, Wang H, Lee S, Lu S, Galavis P, Colangelo N, McCarthy A, Barbee D, Vargas HA, Chinitz LA, Zelefsky MJ.
abstractText: Prostate stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT) on a 1.5-T magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) linear accelerator (MR-linac) combines high-contrast intrafraction imaging with online adaptive replanning and enables focal dose intensification. Patients with cardiac implantable electronic devices (CIEDs) nonetheless face barriers to MR-guided radiotherapy (MRgRT), because existing guidance addresses diagnostic MRI and radiotherapy exposures separately and does not specify fraction-level requirements for their combination. We developed and implemented a framework integrating both domains in one operational pathway. A multidisciplinary group synthesized diagnostic MRI, radiotherapy, and MR-linac safety evidence into a dual-axis risk model. The MRI/CIED axis is keyed to device exposure (generator-lead configuration, manufacturer conditions, and sequence-level radiofrequency and gradient compliance) rather than anatomic field of view. The radiotherapy (RT)/CIED axis stratifies neutron production, cumulative generator dose, generator-to-field geometry, and pacing dependence. A failure mode and effects analysis translated high-priority scenarios into hold points and role assignments; the pathway is implemented prospectively for CIED patients on a 1.5-T MR-linac. The two axes intersect in a matrix assigning every patient to one of six classes: LOW, LOW/INTERMEDIATE, INTERMEDIATE, INTERMEDIATE/HIGH, HIGH, or HOLD. Each class specifies monitoring, consent, interrogation, programming, personnel, and platform requirements. These are implemented through a day-of-treatment workflow with named role ownership and sequential hold points aligned with the 2026 American College of Radiology Manual on MR Safety. Two determinations override the matrix: MR-hold defers MRgRT irrespective of radiotherapy category, and RT-high defaults to computed tomography-guided radiotherapy. By unifying MRI- and radiotherapy-specific device risks, the dual-axis framework converts categorical CIED exclusion into a graded, prospectively assigned disposition and makes every decision auditable. It is in prospective clinical use and offers appropriately selected patients a conservative route to MRgRT and the documentation from which multi-institutional validation can be built.

title: PIAS1 mitigates vascular calcification through regulating mitochondrial DNA leakage mediated by VDAC1-NLRX1 axis in diabetic models.
authorString: Wang L, Huang Q, Liu W, Xie B, Zhao A, Liu J, Wang Q, Meng L, Zhang M, Luo Y, Lai S, Wang W, Wan L, Huang Q.
