abstractText: Vascular calcification, an important pathological process of cardiovascular remodeling, is primarily driven by the transition of vascular smooth muscle cells from contractile to osteogenic phenotype. Protein inhibitor of activated STAT1 (PIAS1) is closely associated with diabetes and vascular diseases, but its role and underlying mechanisms in the progression of diabetic vascular calcification (DVC) remain unclear. Herein, we investigated the role of PIAS1 in DVC by genetic modulation and explored its molecular mechanisms by transcriptomics and co-immunoprecipitation with mass spectrometry (Co-IP-MS). We demonstrate that PIAS1 expression is downregulated in both in vitro and in vivo DVC models; furthermore, PIAS1 overexpression alleviates DVC, whereas PIAS1 knockout exacerbates it. Mechanistically, Co-IP-MS analysis reveals an interaction between PIAS1 and voltage-dependent anion channel 1 (VDAC1), which enhances the SUMOylation of VDAC1 while inhibiting its oligomerization. PIAS1 also reduces the binding between NLR family member X1 (NLRX1) and VDAC1, ultimately attenuating mitochondrial DNA leakage into the cytoplasm. More importantly, we find that Ginsenoside Ro is a PIAS1-targeting natural product which alleviates DVC. These findings identify PIAS1 as a novel therapeutic target for DVC and provide a new candidate for DVC prevention and treatment.

title: Impact of preoperative cardiology consultations on perioperative management in patients undergoing non-cardiac surgery: a prospective cohort study.
authorString: Tarot A, Rineau E, Bière L, Trouillard M.
abstractText: Cardiology consultations may be requested during preoperative anesthetic assessment before non-cardiac surgery. However, data regarding their impact on perioperative management are limited. This study aimed to evaluate the effect of preoperative cardiology consultations on perioperative patient management. We conducted a prospective, observational, single-center study in the Department of Anesthesiology and Critical Care at Angers University Hospital from September 1st, 2024, to August 31st, 2025. All patients referred for cardiology assessment after the anesthetic consultation were included. The primary endpoint was any change in perioperative management, including specific preoperative cardiac treatment, postponement or cancellation of surgery, and modification of anesthetic or surgical protocols. The secondary endpoint was to assess adherence of preoperative cardiac evaluation to current guideline recommendations. Among 9,621 preoperative anesthetic consultations, 138 (1%) patients were referred for cardiology assessment by the anesthesiologist and included in the study. 59 (43%) patients experienced a change in perioperative management. Of them, surgery was postponed in 52 (38%) patients, with a median delay of 81 [47-145] days, whereas only 6 patients underwent an invasive cardiac intervention (angioplasty, valvuloplasty, or electrical cardioversion). A previously unknown cardiac condition was identified in 19 (15%) patients. 111 (80%) cardiology referrals were consistent with current recommendations. In our study, preoperative cardiology consultations requested by an anesthesiologist were rare but frequently responsible for modification of perioperative management. These consultations often resulted in postponement of surgery, while only a small proportion of patients underwent an invasive cardiac intervention.

title: Electrocardiographic markers of ventricular repolarization in early and late-onset preeclampsia: implications for maternal cardiovascular involvement.
authorString: Işık E, Özgü Erdinç AS, Gürbüz HS, Çıtırke A, Altınsoy H, Sezgin A, Kara Ö, Şahin D.
abstractText: This study aimed to evaluate electrocardiographic (ECG) parameters in pregnant women with early-onset and late-onset preeclampsia (PE) compared with healthy controls, and to explore their association with maternal cardiovascular involvement. This prospective case-control study included 91 pregnant women with PE and 130 healthy controls. ECG parameters, including PR interval, QRS duration, QT and corrected QT (QTc), were measured between 28 and 37 weeks of gestation. Subgroup analyses were performed to compare early- and late-onset PE. ROC curve analysis was used to evaluate the discriminative performance of ECG parameters. PR interval, QRS duration, QT and QTc were significantly prolonged in the PE group compared with controls (p < 0.001). These alterations were more pronounced in early onset PE. In ROC analysis, QTc demonstrated the highest discriminatory performance for identifying early-onset PE (AUC = 0.78), followed by PR interval and QRS duration. PE particularly early-onset PE, was associated with significant alterations in electrocardiographic parameters, including QTc interval prolongation. These findings suggest that preeclampsia may be accompanied by changes in maternal cardiac electrical activity. Further prospective studies are needed to clarify the underlying mechanisms and determine the potential clinical relevance of these electrocardiographic alterations.

title: Extracellular vesicles in viral myocarditis: Mechanisms, biomarkers and emerging therapeutic strategies.
authorString: Bahreyni A, Luo H.
abstractText: Viral myocarditis (VM) is an inflammatory heart disease most commonly triggered by viral infection and represents a major cause of acute cardiac dysfunction and chronic inflammatory cardiomyopathy. Although cardiomyocyte injury and immune activation are central to VM pathogenesis, the mechanisms by which viral infection coordinates intercellular communication to drive disease progression remain incompletely understood. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) have emerged as key mediators of cell-to-cell signaling, capable of transporting viral components and host-derived factors that modulate immune responses and cardiac function. In this review, we integrate preclinical and clinical evidence to define the mechanistic roles of EVs in VM and evaluate their translational potential. We highlight circulating EVs as minimally invasive biomarkers for early diagnosis and disease monitoring. We further discuss emerging strategies to therapeutically target or engineer EVs to modulate both viral replication and maladaptive host responses.

title: The impact of temperature variation on the incidence of cardiovascular diseases in hypertensive populations: Evidence from CHARLS and the UK biobank.
authorString: Wang XY, Wang XY, Xu YM, Yu GB, Hao XX, Wang XL, Li ZM, Yao HW, Sun HR, Wang SY.
abstractText: Hypertension is the most prevalent chronic disease. The link between temperature changes and cardiovascular disease incidence in hypertensive populations is not well understood. To explore how temperature fluctuations affect cardiovascular disease incidence in hypertensive populations and identify the most impacted cardiovascular diseases. Using data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) and the UK Biobank, which provide long-term follow-up information on hypertensive patients, we applied logistic regression and Cox proportional hazards regression models to analyze the relationship between temperature and cardiovascular disease occurrence. In CHARLS (2011-2020), 4321 hypertensive individuals were studied, with 1079 developing cardiovascular diseases. A significant positive correlation was found between annual average daily temperature difference and cardiovascular disease incidence (OR: 1.01, 95% CI: 1.01-1.02, P < 0.001). In the UK Biobank, 30,551 participants were followed for an average of 12.4 years, with 3611 diagnosed with cardiovascular diseases. Those exposed to alternating cold and hot temperatures had a higher risk of cardiovascular events (HR: 1.19, 95% CI: 1.09-1.29, P < 0.001). Specifically, heart failure (HR: 1.45, 95% CI: 1.21-1.73, P < 0.001), multivalvular disease (HR: 1.32, 95% CI: 1.04-1.68, P < 0.05), and chronic ischemic heart disease (HR: 1.15, 95% CI: 1.03-1.28, P < 0.05) were associated with such temperature exposure. Our study highlights the need to enhance cardiovascular disease monitoring and management in hypertensive populations under varying temperatures, which is crucial for disease prevention and control.

title: Prevalence, underdiagnosis, and its impact on exercise capacity and physical activity of lower extremity artery disease in Japanese patients with stable chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: A cross-sectional study.
authorString: Kobayashi T, Murakami T, Ono H, Takahashi T.

journal.title: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care

abstractText: Although lower extremity artery disease (LEAD) is a common cardiovascular comorbidity in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), its prevalence and clinical impact in Japanese patients remain unclear. To determine the prevalence of LEAD, including the proportion of previously undiagnosed cases, in Japanese patients with stable COPD, and to compare exercise capacity and physical activity between patients with and without LEAD. LEAD was defined as an ankle-brachial index (ABI) ≤ 0.90 in either leg. Six-minute walk distance (6MWD) and physical activity assessed using a triaxial accelerometer were compared between patients with and without LEAD, with adjustment for potential confounders using analysis of covariance. The associations of ABI as a continuous variable with exercise capacity and physical activity were examined using restricted cubic spline analysis. Among 101 patients with COPD (median age, 75.0 years; 88 % male), 18 (18 %) had coexisting LEAD; 78 % were previously undiagnosed and 72 % were asymptomatic. In crude analyses, patients with LEAD had significantly shorter 6MWD (p = 0.007), lower daily step count (p = 0.011), and more comorbidities. After adjustment, differences in 6MWD (-47.9 m; 95 % CI, -124.0 to 28.5) and step count (-1,035 steps/day; 95 % CI, -2,645 to 575) were not statistically significant, whereas ABI was significantly associated with 6MWD (p = 0.009). A substantial proportion of patients with COPD and coexisting LEAD were previously undiagnosed. Lower exercise capacity and step counts in unadjusted comparisons were not significant after adjustment, suggesting that these differences may reflect multiple contributing factors.

title: Subclinical cardiac autonomic and pulmonary dysfunction in ambulatory patients with cervicothoracic intradural spinal tumours: A prospective cross-sectional study.
authorString: Parani L, Gopalakrishna KN, Prabhuraj AR, Pruthi N, Sathyaprabha TN, Udupa K.

journal.title: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia

abstractText: Cervicothoracic intradural spinal tumours (C1-T12) may compromise autonomic and respiratory function due to proximity to sympathetic and cardiopulmonary regulatory centres. This study aimed to evaluate autonomic and pulmonary dysfunction in these patients using heart rate variability (HRV), autonomic function tests (AFTs), pulmonary function tests (PFTs), and echocardiography, with a subgroup analysis comparing intramedullary (IDIM) vs extramedullary (IDEM) conditions. In this prospective cross-sectional study, 68 ambulatory patients (mean age 36.9 ± 12.5 years; 30 male, 38 female) with radiologically confirmed cervicothoracic intradural tumours (Modified McCormick functional grades I-III) and 68 age- and gender-matched healthy, non-smoking controls, free of cardiopulmonary, neurological and endocrine disease and not taking medication, underwent preoperative heart rate variability (HRV) analysis, conventional autonomic function tests (AFT), pulmonary function tests (PFT) and echocardiography. Group comparisons used Student's t or Mann-Whitney U tests. Associations with functional grade were examined using Spearman correlation and chi-square tests. IDIM-IDEM comparisons were unadjusted and exploratory. Compared with controls, patients had lower SDNN (median 26.43 vs 40.01 ms; p = 0.0017), RMSSD (15.13 vs 31.96 ms; p < 0.0001), total power (695.7 vs 1335 ms2), low-frequency (LF) power (178.1 vs 369.1 ms2) and high-frequency (HF) power (106.4 vs 400.5 ms2), higher normalised LF with lower normalised HF, and a higher resting heart rate (84.93 vs 75.19 beats/min; p < 0.0001). Deep-breathing difference, Valsalva ratio, orthostatic heart-rate ratio and handgrip diastolic-pressure response were lower in patients (all p < 0.0001). Forced vital capacity and FEV1 (% predicted), inspiratory capacity, vital capacity, expiratory reserve volume and maximal voluntary ventilation were also lower. None of the HRV, AFT or PFT measures was significantly associated with Modified McCormick functional grade (all p ≥ 0.054). IDIM tumours spanned more vertebral segments than IDEM tumours (more than 3 segments in 56.4 % vs 24.1 %) and the groups differed in age. In unadjusted comparisons, resting heart rate was higher in IDIM tumours, whereas deep-breathing difference, handgrip response, FVC and ERV were lower in IDEM tumours. Ambulatory patients with cervicothoracic intradural spinal tumours demonstrated alterations in cardiac autonomic modulation and pulmonary function despite preserved ambulatory status and the absence of overt cardiopulmonary disease. The cross-sectional design shows associations, not causation. Differences between intramedullary and extramedullary tumours may reflect tumour compartment; they could also reflect differences in tumour level, extent and patient characteristics, and require confirmation in larger studies with adjusted analyses and longitudinal postoperative assessment.

title: Mechanical Ventilation Strategies and Monitoring in Patients with Right Ventricular Failure.
authorString: Miller PE, Mantini D, Grubb CS, Hardin EA, Thibodeau JT, Hall EJ.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Eur Heart J Acute Cardiovasc Care
journal.title: European heart journal. Acute cardiovascular care
journal.isoabbreviation: Eur Heart J Acute Cardiovasc Care

abstractText: Respiratory failure is the predominant etiology for admission to the contemporary cardiac intensive care unit (CICU) and frequently requires invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV). Positive pressure ventilation (PPV) delivered by IMV reverses the normal physiology of spontaneous breathing and uniquely impacts the right ventricle (RV). By increasing intrathoracic pressure, PPV reduces preload and can increase RV afterload. Given these potentially detrimental effects on the RV, patients with RV dysfunction can decompensate with instituting PPV. The peri-intubation period is particularly high-risk for these patients and requires careful planning and monitoring, which includes both non-invasive and invasive modalities. During IMV, it is necessary to optimize oxygenation, acid-base status, and reduce atelectasis while limiting airway pressures to avoid potentially worsening RV function. In this review, we discuss the epidemiology of RV and respiratory failure in the CICU, pathophysiology of PPV as it relates to the RV, and management immediately before, during, and liberation from IMV.

title: RNA-binding protein Rbfox2 establishes lipid gene programs through hierarchical control of transcription factors in the embryonic heart.
authorString: Verma SK, Hasan Chowdhury MI, Raghav Y, Bluemn T, Harris BN, Mueller C, DeLancey RL, Zadrozny K, Bushra S, Hendrix EE, Viet A, Sheynkman G, Saucerman JJ, Lincoln J, Levental KR, Levental I, Platig J, Kuyumcu-Martinez MN.
abstractText: The role of RNA-binding proteins in metabolic gene regulation is unclear. Here, we uncover a hierarchical circuit where RNA-binding protein RBFOX2 establishes lipid gene programs and lipidome in embryonic hearts by governing transcription factors (TFs) using multi-transcriptomic and lipidomics approaches. We identified TF and lipid genes as RBFOX2 targets in the embryonic heart. TF SOX4 is a key target of RBFOX2 that drives lipid gene programs. RBFOX2 binds human SOX4 3' UTR and regulates its mRNA stability. SOX4 in turn initiates a lipid gene program by binding promoters of lipid enzymes/regulators. Restoration of SOX4 level, rescues lipid gene expression defects upon RBFOX2 loss. Strikingly, Rbfox2 loss in embryonic hearts modulates cardiac lipidome and leads to accumulation of lipid droplets. We reveal an RNA-mediated mechanism that establishes lipidome identity in the developing heart and may provide unique metabolic nodes vulnerable for pharmaceutic intervention of congenital heart disease in the future.

title: Evaluation of the Parasympathetic Tone Activity monitor in horses anesthetized with different isoflurane concentrations.
authorString: Medina-Bautista F, Ruíz-López P, Navarrete-Calvo R, Morgaz J, Domínguez JM, Quirós-Carmona S, Granados MDM.
abstractText: Parasympathetic Tone Activity (PTA) monitoring has been proposed as an indicator of nociception during general anesthesia in veterinary medicine. However, the influence of anesthetic depth on PTA responses remains poorly characterized in horses. Ten healthy horses were anesthetized at three end-tidal isoflurane concentrations (FE'ISO; 0.9%, 1.2%, and 1.5%). After stabilization, standardized electrical nociceptive stimulation (SENS) was applied. Immediate (PTAi) and mean (PTAm) PTA indices, heart rate, and arterial blood pressures were recorded before, during, and after stimulation. Data were analyzed using generalized linear mixed models, cross-correlation, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses. SENS significantly decreased PTAi and PTAm (p = 0.001), whereas FE'ISO had no significant effect (p = 0.818 and p = 0.915, respectively). PTAi decreased from 75 (95% CI: 73-77) to 48 (95% CI: 43-52), representing a 36% reduction. PTAi and PTAm reached their nadirs 1.2 and 2.2-2.7 min after stimulation, respectively. A significant FE'ISO × timepoint interaction was identified for PTAi (p = 0.001). MAP increased immediately after SENS and preceded PTAi decreases by 1.1 min. PTAi moderately identified cardiovascular responses to SENS (ROC AUC 0.707; 95% CI: 0.650-0.765). Overall, PTAi and PTAm responded to SENS across the FE'ISO concentrations evaluated; however, the moderate discriminative ability of PTAi indicated a limited relationship between PTA and mean arterial pressure.

title: Wearable-Derived Physical Activity Patterns in Preclinical and Clinical Obesity.
authorString: Zahid S, Yao Z, Grimes SN, Peng AW, Awol K, Blumenthal RS, Battle A, Martin SS, Blaha MJ.
abstractText: The Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology Commission issued a new obesity definition to move beyond BMI and prioritize excess body fat and dysfunctional adiposity, stratified by preclinical and clinical groups. We evaluated the physical activity patterns across obesity groups with wearable-derived accelerometry and risk for cardiovascular disease. We performed a retrospective cohort analysis of step count, moderate-to-vigorous exercise, and sedentary time in 24,679 adults with Fitbit and electronic health records from the All of Us Research Program, stratified by no, preclinical, and clinical obesity groups. There was a decline in physical activity across obesity groups: median daily steps were 7846, 6702, and 5128, weekly moderate-to-vigorous physical activity exercise 140, 91, and 35 min; and daily sedentary time 12.2, 12.8, and 13.4 h for no, preclinical, and clinical obesity, respectively. Physical activity decreased with BMI and obesity-related multimorbidity. Wearable-derived physical activity patterns show distinct patterns for preclinical and clinical obesity.

title: Machine Learning-Driven ZnO NRs@Ag SERS Platform for Rheumatoid Arthritis Liquid Biopsy in a Multicenter-Recruited Cohort.
authorString: Han S, Chen C, Zhou X, Wu L, Lv X, Jia Z, Zhao X, Wu X, Li M, Chen C.
abstractText: The analytical chemistry diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis (RA) faces challenges such as the time lag of conventional serological assays and matrix masking in complex biofluid analysis. This study proposes a label-free liquid biopsy framework integrating band-regulated surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) sensing with machine learning algorithms. Experimental characterizations (XPS and TRPL) and density functional theory (DFT) calculations confirm that the ZnO NRs@Ag heterojunction drives efficient spatial separation of charge carriers via stepped band alignment. This achieves a deep synergy between electromagnetic (EM) and chemical enhancements (CM), significantly improving the signal selectivity of metabolites against high-abundance backgrounds. Meanwhile, the substrate exhibits good batch-to-batch structural reproducibility and environmental storage stability. Based on this sensing platform, a patient-level internal validation was conducted on a multicenter-recruited serum cohort. By averaging replicate spectra to prevent data leakage, the model classification was strictly performed on 74 independent patient-level input features (comprising 66 RA cases and 8 healthy controls). Under a leave-one-patient-out cross-validation architecture coupled with dynamic in-fold oversampling, the linear classification model (PLS-DA) achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.9337. Furthermore, utilizing the SHAP method, the model identified putative spectral features that influenced the classification decision, providing a reference for exploring related pathological metabolic changes. This study elucidates the synergistic enhancement mechanism of the heterojunction at the electronic state level and verifies the preliminary diagnostic potential of the platform in decoding high-dimensional metabolic profiles, offering a methodological foundation for applying SERS technology to autoimmune disease screening.

title: Cardiac transcriptomics identifies S100A8/A9 as novel dual biomarkers and therapeutic targets for acute myocardial ischemia.
authorString: Chen L, Lin J, Shen Y, Ye X.
abstractText: Postmortem diagnosis of acute myocardial ischemia (AMI) within the first 6 h remains difficult in both clinical and forensic practice because early myocardial histological changes are often nonspecific. This study aimed to identify biomarkers for AMI in autopsy tissues and to preliminarily explore their roles in ischemic injury. Herein, we reanalyzed a previously generated RNA-seq dataset from a mouse model of AMI and sham controls to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs). Candidate molecules were validated using RT-qPCR, Western blot, immunohistochemistry, and immunofluorescence in both in vivo and in vitro AMI models. Additionally, their diagnostic value was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis in human cardiac tissue samples. Reanalyzed identified 593 differentially expressed genes (501 upregulated, 92 downregulated) between AMI and sham mice. RT-qPCR confirmed significant upregulation of S100A8 and S100A9, which increased progressively with early ischemia in mouse myocardium and under hypoxia in AC16 cells. In human samples, immunohistochemistry showed markedly higher S100A8/A9 expression in AMI compared with controls, independent of age and postmortem interval. ROC analysis highlighted the diagnostic potential of S100A8/A9 for AMI, with combined detection achieving optimal sensitivity (91.3%) and an AUC of 0.8092 in differentiating AMI from controls. Notably, treatment with the S100A8/A9-specific inhibitor Paquinimod effectively alleviated hypoxia-induced cardiomyocyte apoptosis, mitochondrial dysfunction, and inflammatory responses, indicating a pivotal role of S100A8/9 in myocardial ischemic injury. Overall, our findings indicate that S100A8/A9 may serve as valuable postmortem diagnostic markers for AMI and represent promising therapeutic targets for mitigating AMI-induced myocardial damage.

title: Balanced Block of hERG/K<sub>v</sub>11.1, Ca<sub>V</sub>1.2, and Na<sub>V</sub>1.5 in Proarrhythmic Risk Assessment: An Integrated Review of In Vitro Electrophysiology, In Silico Modeling, and hiPSC-CM Evidence.
authorString: Ma Y, Yang J, Zheng X, Chen H, Liu J, Liu H.
abstractText: Drug-induced torsade de pointes (TdP) risk is commonly assessed by measuring inhibition of the rapid delayed rectifier potassium current (IKr), mediated by Kv11.1/hERG, together with QT-interval prolongation. These endpoints are sensitive but incompletely specific because concomitant inhibition of the L-type calcium current (ICaL) or late sodium current (INaL) can attenuate IKr-block-mediated repolarization delay. This narrative review evaluates balanced ion-channel block using recombinant-cell electrophysiology, in silico models, and human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (hiPSC-CMs). Potency ratios can describe relative channel inhibition but cannot alone establish a validated risk threshold or low clinical TdP liability. Concentration-response slopes, binding kinetics, unbound exposure, active metabolites, trafficking effects, and patient susceptibility also influence outcome. The CiPA-modified O'Hara-Rudy ventricular model and qNet-derived Torsade Metric Score are model-specific integrators rather than direct measurements of clinical repolarization reserve. The fixed-block simulations presented here illustrate interactions between inward and outward currents. hiPSC-CMs provide complementary functional evidence but remain limited by cellular immaturity and assay variability. The ICH E14/S7B Q&As (R1), adopted in August 2026, support integrated assessment and permit qualified alternative assays in defined contexts of use.

title: Association between embolic protection strategy and distal embolization during Jetstream atherectomy for calcified femoropopliteal lesions.
authorString: Tsujimura T, Yoshii D, Hata Y, Fujihara M, Okina Y, Toyoshima T, Minamiguchi H, Ichibori Y, Nakamoto K, Mori N, Kanda T, Tsutsui H, Matsumura M, Nakawatase S, Shibuya Y, Minami S, Koda K, Abe N, Ikeuchi Y, Hyogo T, Okamoto S, Iida O.
abstractText:
Background

Distal embolization remains a significant complication during endovascular therapy (EVT) with atherectomy for femoropopliteal lesions. We evaluated the association between embolic protection strategies, including a novel flow-controlled anti-embolic technique (FCAT), and distal embolization.

Methods

This multicenter retrospective study included 147 limbs in 126 patients with peripheral artery disease who underwent EVT using the Jetstream™ atherectomy system and drug-coated balloon treatment for calcified femoropopliteal lesions. Treated limbs were categorized by embolic protection strategy: no protection (n = 25), embolic protection device (EPD) alone (n = 63), EPD with proximal protection (n = 37), and FCAT (n = 22). The primary outcome was distal embolization incidence. Secondary outcomes included 6-month primary patency, target lesion revascularization (TLR), and major amputation.

Results

Distal embolization occurred in 21.1% of lesions, with significant differences among groups (28.0%, 30.2%, 13.5%, and 0% for no protection, EPD alone, EPD with proximal protection, and FCAT, respectively; p = 0.012). Increasing protection intensity showed a stepwise reduction in distal embolization (p for trend = 0.008). In multivariable analysis, chronic limb-threatening ischemia was associated with increased distal embolization risk (adjusted odds ratio 2.68, 95% CI 1.10-6.54, p = 0.031), whereas embolic protection device with proximal protection including FCAT were associated with lower risk (adjusted odds ratio 0.26, 95% CI 0.07-0.96, p = 0.043). Six-month outcomes were comparable among groups, with no major amputations.

Conclusion

Embolic protection strategies incorporating proximal protection, including FCAT, were associated with a lower incidence of distal embolization during EVT using the Jetstream atherectomy system. Although no distal embolization was observed in the FCAT group, this FCAT-specific finding should be considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating.

title: Lifestyle Changes for the Treatment of Hypertension.
authorString: Stein J, Thompson A, Thomas A, Janakiraman A, Cohen JB.
abstractText: Lifestyle interventions are foundational to hypertension prevention and treatment. We review recent evidence for weight management, dietary patterns, sodium and potassium intake, physical activity, stress reduction, alcohol reduction, and avoidance of blood pressure-raising substances, with emphasis on implementation and contemporary guidelines. Recent trials extend Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) benefits to grocery delivery in populations facing barriers to food access, while potassium-enriched salt-substitution studies support cardiovascular benefit but require attention to hyperkalemia risk. Alcohol reduction lowers blood pressure most among individuals with higher baseline intake or blood pressure, and avoidance of other pressor substances remains important. Evidence for time-restricted eating and stress-reduction strategies is uncertain. Lifestyle modification is recommended for all adults with elevated blood pressure or hypertension, but sustained adherence and equitable access are major barriers. Future research should prioritize scalable, durable, culturally responsive strategies and outcomes beyond short-term blood pressure change.

title: Associations of dietary magnesium intake with glomerular and tubular injury markers in type 2 diabetes: The Fukuoka Diabetes Registry.
authorString: Ohmura I, Ohkuma T, Iwase M, Fujihira M, Sakamoto W, Higashi T, Ago T.
abstractText: Higher dietary magnesium intake has been associated with reduced risk of cardiovascular disease and its risk factors. However, its association with CKD remains unclear. This study examined this association using glomerular and tubular injury markers. A total of 4,923 participants with type 2 diabetes were classified into quintiles of dietary magnesium intake. CKD was defined as decreased estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFRcr <60 mL/min/1.73 m2) and/or albuminuria (urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio [UACR] ≥ 30 mg/g). Odds ratios (ORs) for CKD were calculated using logistic regression. Associations of dietary magnesium intake with eGFRcr, UACR, neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin (NGAL), liver-type fatty acid-binding protein (L-FABP), and kidney injury molecule-1 (KIM-1) were evaluated using linear regression. Higher dietary magnesium intake was associated with lower prevalence of CKD. Compared with the lowest quintile, the multivariable-adjusted ORs (95% confidence intervals) for CKD across increasing quintiles were 0.84 (0.68-1.04), 0.73 (0.57-0.93), 0.58 (0.44-0.76), and 0.50 (0.35-0.71) (P for trend < 0.001). Similar inverse associations were observed for decreased eGFRcr and albuminuria analyzed separately. Higher magnesium intake was also associated with lower urinary NGAL and L-FABP. These findings suggest a potential role of dietary magnesium intake in preserving glomerular and tubular kidney health.

title: Circulating miR-125b-5p and miR-210-3p are reduced in long-term breast cancer survivors with cardiovascular disease.
authorString: Sicurella M, Sanz JM, Raparelli V, Sergi D, Greatti A, Ghirardini C, Dipinto A, Mindicini N, Spaggiari R, Calabrò L, Neri LM, Passaro A.
abstractText: Long-term female breast cancer survivors are at increased risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD), yet the biological mechanisms underlying this vulnerability remain poorly defined. Identifying non-invasive biomarkers capable of capturing early cardiovascular alterations in this population represents a relevant unmet clinical need. Twenty-four long-term female breast cancer survivors were enrolled and stratified according to cardiovascular disease history (CVD+, n = 12; CVD-, n = 12) and matched by age. A selected panel of 13 circulating microRNAs (miRNAs), together with adipokines and inflammatory cytokines, was analyzed in plasma samples. No significant differences were observed between groups in circulating adipokines or inflammatory markers. In contrast, miR-125b-5p and miR-210-3p were significantly downregulated in survivors with CVD compared with matched CVD- subjects. Correlation analyses revealed distinct, condition-specific association patterns between miRNA expression and cardiometabolic parameters. The reduced circulating expression of miR-125b-5p and miR-210-3p in long-term breast cancer survivors with cardiovascular disease suggests a potential involvement of these miRNAs in vascular homeostasis and hypoxia-related pathways. These findings support circulating miRNAs as promising exploratory biomarkers for cardiovascular risk stratification in cancer survivorship, warranting validation in larger prospective studies.

title: Endovascular aortic repair for abdominal aortic aneurysm with horseshoe kidney using a physician-modified endograft to preserve an accessory renal artery.
authorString: Nakashima T, Kawajiri H, Yaku Y, Okamoto U, Gondai T, Manabe K, Kobayashi T, Kanda K, Oda S.

journal.title: Journal of artificial organs : the official journal of the Japanese Society for Artificial Organs

abstractText: Horseshoe kidney (HSK) associated with abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is rare, and surgical repair is technically demanding because of complex anatomical variations, particularly accessory renal arteries (ARAs). The indication for ARA reconstruction remains a critical operative consideration. We report a 72-year-old man with a 43-mm AAA, a 40-mm left common iliac artery aneurysm (CIAA) and HSK. Preoperative contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) demonstrated two ARAs (5 mm and 1.8 mm) supplying the renal isthmus. Endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) was performed with a physician-modified fenestrated endograft (PMEG); the dominant 5-mm ARA was reconstructed with a bridging stent. The postoperative course was uneventful and renal function was preserved (serum creatinine 0.82 → 0.76 mg/dL; eGFR 70.6 → 76.8 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>); renal parenchymal volume was 87% of baseline. At 6-month CT, the aneurysm was stable, and at 2-year CT, both the AAA and the left CIAA had decreased by approximately 2 mm in diameter, with renal function unchanged. PMEG-based EVAR with dominant ARA reconstruction may therefore be a feasible option for AAA with HSK.

title: Correlation between systemic inflammatory indicators and coagulation-fibrinolysis markers in patients with periodontitis at different stages: A cross-sectional study.
authorString: Liu Y, Li C, Zhao Y, Zhong LQ, Li Y, Xiao Z, Chen X.
abstractText: This study aims to investigate the correlation between systemic inflammatory indicators and coagulation-fibrinolysis markers in patients with periodontitis at different stages. The participants were classified according to diagnostic criteria into Stage I (n = 25), Stage II (n = 30), Stage III (n = 31), Stage IV (n = 30), and a healthy control group (n = 32). Systematic inflammatory indicators and coagulation-fibrinolysis biomarkers were compared across groups. Spearman correlation analysis was employed to investigate the relationship between periodontal inflammation severity and systemic inflammatory markers, as well as between systemic inflammatory markers and coagulation-fibrinolysis markers. Additionally, discriminatory potential of the systemic inflammatory markers for periodontitis was assessed using receiver operating characteristic curves. Compared with the stage I periodontitis group, the stage IV periodontitis group showed significantly elevated levels of white blood cell count (WBC), neutrophil count (NEUT), fibrinogen (FIB) (P < 0.05), SII (P < 0.01), and tissue plasminogen activator-inhibitor complex (t-PAIC) (P < 0.001). Correlation analysis revealed that the severity of periodontal inflammation was positively correlated with systemic inflammatory indicators; moreover, these systemic inflammatory markers were also positively correlated with coagulation-fibrinolysis markers (P < 0.05). Area under curve (AUC) of the WBC, NEUT, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), lymphocyte-to-monocyte ratio (LMR), and systemic immune-inflammatory (SII) for the distinction of Stage IV periodontitis were 0.730, 0.787, 0.797,0.699 ,0.676, and 0.793, respectively. Patients with periodontitis exhibit significantly elevated levels of systemic inflammatory indicators, which are positively correlated with coagulation and fibrinolysis markers. The study shows that certain inflammatory and coagulation/fibrinolysis-related biomarkers associated with cardiovascular conditions are also altered in patients with periodontitis. These findings suggest that there may be common inflammatory pathways linking periodontitis with cardiovascular-related systemic diseases, which calls for further longitudinal and mechanistic investigations.

title: SGLT2 Inhibitors in Fontan Circulation: Bridging the Evidence Gap Between Adult Heart Failure Data and Single-Ventricle Physiology.
authorString: Predeus IR, de Moraes GC, Cunha ABN, Levin GCA, de Sant'Anna Melo E.
abstractText: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors have transformed the management of heart failure in adults and are now used empirically in children with Fontan-palliated single-ventricle circulation, despite an absence of trials in this population. Early observational data suggest that SGLT2 inhibitors are well tolerated in Fontan circulatory failure, with signals of reduced natriuretic peptide levels and modest improvement in ventricular function, but no study has been designed or powered to establish efficacy. This gap is compounded by a physiological mismatch: the Fontan circulation is characterized by the absence of a subpulmonary pumping chamber, resulting in passive pulmonary blood flow. Under these unique hemodynamic conditions, systemic ventricular preload is primarily determined by pulmonary vascular resistance, ventricular diastolic properties, and atrial filling pressures. These distinctive physiological characteristics may have important implications for the mechanisms underlying the effects of sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors. Notably, diastolic dysfunction is increasingly recognized as a prevalent feature of Fontan circulatory failure. Given the established clinical benefits of SGLT2 inhibitors in adults with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, their potential therapeutic effects in the Fontan population may extend beyond conventional preload modulation to include improvements in diastolic function and ventricular filling dynamics. In this Perspective, we examine whether the principal mechanisms of SGLT2 inhibitor benefit described in adults-osmotic diuresis and preload reduction, a myocardial substrate shift toward ketone metabolism, and blockade of the cardiac sodium-hydrogen exchanger-plausibly translate to Fontan physiology, review the available pediatric evidence and its limitations, and outline a framework for a prospective, phenotype-stratified multicenter trial. We argue that current practice has outpaced the evidence specific to this population, and that closing this gap requires a Fontan-specific research agenda rather than continued extrapolation from adult heart failure trials.

title: Primary Cardiac Lymphoma Presenting as Recurrent Pericardial Effusion and Tamponade: Diagnostic and Palliative Management Considerations.
authorString: Hong JM, Rogers N, McGillivray E, Wong-Sefidan I, Ho G.
abstractText:
Background

Primary cardiac lymphoma is a rare cause of pericardial effusion and tamponade that can present without a solid mass.

Case summary

An 85-year-old frail man with ischemic cardiomyopathy presented with tamponade from an isolated, rapidly enlarging hemorrhagic pericardial effusion. Fluid cytology and positron emission tomography-computed tomography confirmed human herpesvirus 8-negative, effusion-based large B-cell lymphoma. Given his high surgical risk and comorbidities, a tissue biopsy was avoided. He was managed with low-dose palliative chemotherapy and adjunctive intrapericardial triamcinolone, which successfully halted persistent high-output drain output, allowing safe pericardial drain removal and pericardial effusion control without invasive surgery.

Discussion

This case demonstrates that effusion-based lymphomas can occur without mass lesions or overt immunosuppression. It highlights the utility of fluid cytology over invasive biopsy in frail patients, and showcases intrapericardial steroids as a conservative tool to control refractory malignant drain output.

Take-home message

Conservative management of primary cardiac lymphoma combining systemic chemotherapy with intrapericardial steroids may help delay or avoid high-risk surgical procedures in frail patients.

title: Exploiting New Opportunities to Deliver High Fibre in White Bread and Other Bakery Products.
authorString: Shewry PR, Griffiths S, Berwick R, Brennan J, Edwards C, Frost G, Gillett N, Joy EJM, Lignou S, Lovegrove JA, Mathers J, Millar S, Poole M, Tudor E, Warren F, Lovegrove A, Stanner S.
abstractText: Dietary fibre (DF) is essential for health, with higher levels of DF consumption being associated with reduced risk of cardiovascular diseases, type 2 diabetes and colorectal cancer. However, most UK consumers fall far below the recommended dietary intake of 30 g of DF a day for adults. Wheat is an important source of DF, with white bread and other products made from white flour being most widely consumed. White bread is an excellent vehicle to deliver increased intake of DF, being widely available and consumed and affordable to all socio-economic groups. Modern elite bread wheat genotypes differ in their content of DF, particularly soluble DF, in white flour and wheat breeders are now able to select for higher DF in their breeding programmes. This paper is the outcome of a 1-day discussion meeting, which focused on identifying and removing barriers to the development and cultivation of wheat types with high fibre in white flour and the delivery of high fibre products to consumers and makes recommendations for future research.

title: Heart rate variability associated with cardiometabolic risk factors in Ghanaian adults with hypertension: A quantile regression analysis.
authorString: Owusu BO, Kontor EK, Jain N, Ussher FA, Assan C, Baffour HK, Nyarko SA, Adjei DA, Asare BT, Boateng D.

journal.title: Clinical and experimental hypertension (New York, N.Y. : 1993)

abstractText: Obesity modifies cardiovascular risk in hypertension, but associations with cardiac autonomic regulation may be heterogeneous and missed by mean-based analyzes. We assessed whether obesity relates to short-term heart rate variability (HRV) among hypertensive adults in Ghana using quantile regression, a distribution-aware approach. In a cross-sectional study at Ejisu Government Hospital, Ghana, adults (≥18 years) with hypertension were classified as obese (body mass index; BMI ≥ 30 kg/m2) or non-obese. Five-minute resting ECG recordings were used to derive relevant HRV parameters. We compared groups using ordinary least-squares, rank-based regression, and quantile regression. Among 223 participants, 79 (35.4%) were obese and 144 (64.6%) were non-obese. Dimensionality-reduction showed substantial overlap between obesity groups without distinct HRV clustering. Mean-based models were largely null, whereas quantile regression revealed marked distributional heterogeneity. Diabetes was consistently associated with lower HRV across multiple indices, with the strongest effects in lower quantiles of SDNN, rMSSD, and HF power distributions. BMI-defined obesity showed minimal association with HRV across quantiles, while high-risk waist circumference showed selective quantile-specific associations including lower rMSSD and HF power and higher LF/HF ratio, particularly in upper-middle portions of the LF/HF distribution. MAP showed little evidence of association with HRV across quantiles. In hypertensive adults in Ghana, HRV profiles were heterogeneous and not clearly partitioned by BMI-defined obesity. Diabetes and central adiposity showed distribution-specific associations with HRV that were partly missed by mean-based analyzes, although several adiposity-related findings remained sensitive to alternative adjustments.

title: The p.Ser143Pro lamin A/C mutation leads to dilated cardiomyopathy and activates the unfolded protein response pathway in a knock-in mouse model.
authorString: Lindholm F, West G, Virtanen L, Kähäri L, Ståhle M, Nammas W, Stenvall CA, Bouvy-Liivrand M, Zhang FP, Sipilä P, Gardberg M, Toivola DM, Salmi M, Saraste A, Rinne P, Taimen P.
abstractText: Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) is characterized by progressive ventricular dilation, systolic dysfunction, and an increased risk of arrythmias and sudden cardiac arrest. Variants in the LMNA gene, which encodes the nuclear lamins A and C, have been linked to the familial form of the disease and the founder variant p.Ser143Pro is particularly common among Finnish patients with DCM. To elucidate the complex and poorly understood pathogenic mechanisms behind LMNA-related DCM, we generated a mouse model carrying the p.Ser143Pro mutation in the Lmna gene. All genetically modified mice appeared normal at birth. However, based on echocardiography, necropsy, natriuretic peptide B (Nppb) expression levels, and histopathological data, homozygous males developed progressive left ventricular dilatation, myocardial fibrosis, and cardiac failure after 6 months of age, with all succumbing before 10 months. A reduced disease penetrance was observed in heterozygous male and homozygous female mice, with one-year survival rates of 40% and 60%, respectively. No signs of skeletal myopathy were observed in mice carrying the mutation. Whole-transcriptome RNA sequencing analysis of left ventricular cardiac tissue from asymptomatic two-month-old homozygous male mice revealed an upregulation of classical heart failure markers, such as natriuretic peptide A (Nppa) and myosin heavy chain 7 (Myh7), and an elevated unfolded protein response signaling, as shown by elevated DNA damage inducible transcript 3 (Ddit3), BAG cochaperone 3 (Bag3) and CCAAT enhancer binding protein beta (Cebpb) levels. In conclusion, p.Ser143Pro-Lmna mice closely mimic the clinical phenotype observed in patients with the p.Ser143Pro LMNA variant and offer a valuable in vivo model for investigating the underlying pathogenic mechanisms of LMNA-related DCM. © 2026 The Author(s).
