title: Urinary peptidomic classifier for the non-invasive diagnosis of Alport syndrome.
authorString: Byrska J, Goma Garces E, Siwy J, Mischak H, Kondyli M, Catanese L, Furlano M, Pilco-Teran M, Fernandez-Fernandez B, Belen Sanz A, Torra R, Sanchez-Niño MD, Ortiz A, Perez Gomez MV, Alport Marató TV3 working group.

journal.title: Nephrology, dialysis, transplantation : official publication of the European Dialysis and Transplant Association - European Renal Association

abstractText: Alport syndrome (AS) is an inherited glomerular disease that often presents with non-specific clinical and histological features overlapping with other forms of chronic kidney disease (CKD). Consequently, AS may remain unrecognised or misclassified, particularly where genetic testing is unavailable and biopsy is delayed or infeasible. We hypothesised that a non-invasive urinary peptide signature can distinguish AS from other CKD aetiologies, patients with diabetes and healthy individuals. In this multicentre study, we included 165 adults with genetically confirmed AS. Comparator groups comprised patients with non-Alport CKD, diabetes and healthy individuals, matched to the AS cohort by age, sex and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR). Urinary peptide profiles were generated by capillary electrophoresis-mass spectrometry. Group differences in peptide abundance were analysed, and a supervised multipeptide classifier specific for AS was constructed and evaluated in matched test cohorts and in two external validation cohorts: 145 patients with IgA nephropathy (IgAN) and 15 further patients with AS. We identified 419 urinary peptides that differed between AS and comparator groups, of which 178 were incorporated into the AS-specific classifier Alport178. In matched test cohorts, Alport178 achieved an AUC of 0.999 (95% CI 0.997-1.00), with 100% sensitivity for AS and high specificity in CKD, diabetic and healthy control groups. In external validation cohorts, the classifier identified most AS cases and classified the majority of IgAN patients as non-Alport. The most informative peptides were predominantly collagen alpha chain fragments. A urinary peptidomic classifier specific for AS enables differentiation of AS from other CKD entities, patients with diabetes, healthy individuals and IgAN. This non-invasive approach may facilitate earlier recognition of AS, reduce the need for invasive diagnostic procedures and prioritise patients for confirmatory genetic testing and targeted management.

title: Joint association of the triglyceride-glucose index and central obesity with clinically significant coronary artery calcification in asymptomatic adults.
authorString: Wang CL, Hsu CY, Lin CY.
abstractText:
Introduction

Clinically significant coronary artery calcium (CAC ≥100) is associated with increased cardiovascular risk. The triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index and central obesity are established markers of metabolic dysfunction and visceral adiposity, respectively. However, whether their combined assessment identifies asymptomatic individuals with clinically significant CAC remains unclear. We investigated the independent and joint associations of the TyG and central obesity with CAC ≥100 in asymptomatic adults.

Materials and methods

This cross-sectional study included 2,729 asymptomatic adults who underwent comprehensive health examinations, including computed tomography for CAC assessment, at Taichung Veterans General Hospital between January 2015 and August 2025. Participants were categorized by TyG quartiles and four phenotypes defined by elevated TyG and central obesity. Multivariable logistic regression evaluated associations with CAC ≥100 after adjustment for cardiovascular risk factors.

Results

Compared with the lowest TyG quartile, the highest quartile had a significantly higher likelihood of clinically significant CAC (adjusted OR 1.54, 95% CI 1.11-2.13; p = 0.009). Compared with the low-TyG with normal-waist group, participants with isolated central obesity and those with isolated high TyG had higher adjusted odds of CAC ≥100. Participants with both elevated TyG and central obesity had the highest likelihood of CAC ≥100 (adjusted OR 1.79, 95% CI 1.30-2.46; p < 0.001).

Conclusions

A higher TyG index was associated with clinically significant coronary artery calcification. The coexistence of metabolic dysfunction and central obesity identified asymptomatic adults with the highest likelihood of clinically significant CAC, suggesting that joint assessment of the TyG index and central obesity may provide additional information regarding subclinical coronary atherosclerosis.Individuals with both an elevated triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index and central obesity had the highest likelihood of clinically significant coronary artery calcification (CAC ≥100).The combined high-TyG with central-obesity phenotype was associated with CAC ≥100 in both men and women and with higher odds across CAC severity categories.Joint assessment of the TyG index and central obesity may provide complementary information on subclinical coronary atherosclerosis in asymptomatic adults.

title: Sociodemographic and Clinical Determinants of Treatment Adherence and Illness Acceptance in Patients With Hypertension.
authorString: Uchmanowicz I, Pustelak K, Kwaśny A, Janiszewska J, Woźniak A, Kędra K, Kalecińska P, Czapla M.
abstractText: To identify the sociodemographic and clinical factors associated with adherence to blood pressure-lowering treatment and with illness acceptance in adults with hypertension attending specialist outpatient care. Single-centre cross-sectional study. We studied 229 adults with physician-diagnosed hypertension attending routine follow-up visits at a specialist hypertension clinic. Adherence was measured with the Hill-Bone Compliance to High Blood Pressure Therapy Scale and illness acceptance with the Acceptance of Illness Scale (AIS). Two multivariable linear regression models with the same 11 sociodemographic and clinical predictors were fitted. STROBE. Treatment adherence and illness acceptance were moderately correlated. Medication burden was the only factor independently associated with both poorer treatment adherence and lower illness acceptance. Better adherence was also associated with a higher number of comorbidities, rural residence, and a family history of hypertension, although the latter two associations were less robust after adjustment for multiple testing. Patients with the highest medication burden had the poorest adherence and the lowest illness acceptance. Adherence and illness acceptance are related but distinct aspects of living with hypertension. The number of medications was the only factor independently associated with both outcomes, suggesting that medication burden should be considered in individualised care. Assessing adherence and illness acceptance together may help nurses to separate patients who need education about their treatment from those who need psychological support or a simpler regimen. Adherence and illness acceptance had different determinant profiles in patients with hypertension, with medication burden as the only factor common to both. The findings support individualised nursing assessment and multidisciplinary management of hypertension. Patients completed validated questionnaires and provided clinical information during routine outpatient visits. They were not involved in the study design, data analysis, interpretation or manuscript preparation.

title: Longitudinal Progression of 6-Minute Walk Test-Derived Fatigability in Spinal and Bulbar Muscular Atrophy: A Retrospective Study.
authorString: Zanovello M, Sabbatini D, Paredi F, Romito A, Blasi L, Musso G, Pennuto M, Minicuci GM, Pegoraro E, Bello L, Sorarù G.
abstractText: Fatigue is a major disabling symptom in Spinal and Bulbar Muscular Atrophy (SBMA), yet objective fatigability, the decline in physical performance during sustained activity, has not been characterized longitudinally. We aimed to characterize the progression of 6-min walk test (6MWT)-derived fatigability and its associations with disease severity. In this retrospective longitudinal study of genetically confirmed SBMA patients able to walk, disease severity was assessed with 6MWT distance, the SBMA Functional Rating Scale (SBMA-FRS), its modified version (m-SBMA-FRS, the sum of trunk and lower-limb subscores), the Adult Myopathy Assessment Tool, and forced vital capacity. Fatigability was the percentage decline in distance walked between the first and sixth 6MWT minutes; values ≥ 10% indicated fatigability. Cross-sectional associations were assessed using logistic regression and Spearman correlations. Longitudinal trajectories were analyzed with generalized estimating equations. A total of 168 patients contributed 703 visits. Among 141 patients with baseline 6MWT total distance and distance per minute data, 65 (46.1%) were fatigable (median fatigability index 8.5%, IQR 16.8%). Fatigability was associated with the m-SBMA-FRS (OR 0.619, 95% CI 0.523-0.717) and 6MWT distance (OR 0.988, 95% CI 0.983-0.991; 0.53 per 50 m). Fatigability index correlated negatively with m-SBMA-FRS (ρ = -0.596) and 6MWT distance (ρ = -0.617). Fatigability increased over time (+1.61%/year, 95% CI +0.71 to +2.51), in parallel with 6MWT decline (-16.84 m/year, 95% CI -20.20 to -13.48). Fatigability is common in ambulant SBMA patients, worsens progressively over time, and is associated with lower-limb and trunk impairment, supporting its use in clinical assessment and natural history studies.

title: Spatially Patterned Heteromultivalency Enhances Nucleic Acid Recognition at Nanochannel Outer Surface.
authorString: Zhao J, Xiao Y, Wang L, Liu X, Shao W, Zou J, Xu Z, Yi X, Lin M, Xia F.
abstractText: Solid-state nanochannels offer a versatile platform for label-free biosensing by transducing interfacial target recognition into ionic current signals. However, the sensing performance of such systems has mainly relied on regulating probe grafting density, while the impact of probe architecture and nanoscale spatial organization remains insufficiently explored. Here, we report a nanochannel biosensor constructed by immobilizing spatially patterned heteromultivalent probes at the outer surface of gold-coated polyethylene terephthalate nanochannels (PHP@OS) to enhance nucleic acid capture. We show that target binding at nanochannel outer surface induces changes in surface charge that enhance ionic current. Compared with homomultivalent and randomly arranged heteromultivalent designs, the spatially patterned interface exhibits up to approximately 6.6-fold higher hybridization efficiency and 7-fold faster binding kinetics, together with an approximately 3-10-fold improvement in apparent binding affinity. Moreover, the PHP@OS enables sensitive and selective detection of bacterial 16S ribosomal RNA in cell lysate samples, highlighting the robustness of this design under biologically relevant conditions. This work demonstrates that spatially organized heteromultivalent probe architectures provide an effective route to engineer the outer surface for high-performance nanochannel biosensing and may be extended to other biomolecular sensing systems by tailoring probe architecture and spatial organization.

title: An Intelligent Deep Learning Framework for Cardiac Arrhythmia Detection and Risk Prediction
authorString: S N, A.M G, G M, P P, A V.
abstractText: Cardiac Arrhythmia detection using continuous ECG monitoring is challenging because abnormal heartbeats occur irregularly, and their patterns may vary from one person to another. ECG signals can also contain noise caused by body movements, muscle activity, and baseline variations, which can affect the accuracy of detection. To address these challenges, this project proposes an intelligent deep learning framework that combines a 1D Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) network, and an Attention Mechanism to detect and classify heartbeats into five AAMI classes. The CNN extracts important features from ECG signals, while the BiLSTM learns the sequential patterns of heartbeats. The CNN extracts important features from ECG signals, particularly the QRS complex, while reducing the influence of less relevant information and noise. To improve the interpretability of the results, a gradient-based Explainable AI (XAI) method is used to generate saliency heatmaps that highlight important regions of the ECG signals. The framework also includes a risk stratification module that categorizes detected cases into low, medium, and high-risk levels based on predefined criteria. The proposed model is evaluated using the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database, with ECG signals segmented into 0.6 second windows around the R-peaks. The target is to achieve high classification accuracy while providing understandable results and useful risk information. This framework aims to support continuous ECG monitoring and assist healthcare professionals in identifying abnormal heartbeat more efficiently.

title: Trajectory of physiologic indices in the cardiac intensive care unit after flow restrictor placement in functionally univentricular multidistributive circulation: hypothesis generation using high-fidelity data
authorString: Fox J, Nugent A, O’Halloran CP, Patel ND, Sourour W, Rao A, Shah A, Critchfield D, Griffiths J, Loomba RS.
abstractText: Background Transcatheter pulmonary flow restrictors are increasingly used to limit pulmonary overcirculation in infants with functionally univentricular multidistributive circulation, but post-procedural physiology remains poorly characterized. This study evaluated cardiovascular and oximetric trajectories during the first 48 hours after cardiac intensive care unit admission following flow restrictor placement. Methods Eight patients were retrospectively studied using high-fidelity physiologic data. Fifteen measured and derived indices were evaluated, including heart rate, arterial pressures, central venous pressure, pulse oximetry saturation, cerebral and renal oxygen extraction, indexed systemic and pulmonary blood flow, pulmonary-to-systemic blood flow ratio, indexed systemic vascular resistance, mean circulatory filling pressure, and venous resistance. Mixed-effects models incorporated time as a natural cubic spline with 4 degrees of freedom, vasoactive-inotrope score, patient-level random intercepts, and autoregressive residual correlation. Sensitivity analyses separately adjusted for hemoglobin and body surface area. Results Heart rate increased significantly over 48 hours, from a modeled 132.6 to 155.5 beats/min (p < 0.01). Central venous pressure increased from 8.74 to 11.39 mmHg (p < 0.01), while indexed systemic vascular resistance decreased from 19.43 to 15.16 Wood units·m² (p < 0.01). Cerebral oxygen extraction demonstrated a significant nonlinear trajectory in both sensitivity analyses, while mean circulatory filling pressure became significant after body surface area adjustment. Indexed systemic flow, indexed pulmonary flow, and pulmonary-to-systemic flow ratio did not significantly change. Conclusion Post-flow-restrictor physiology remained dynamic over 48 hours despite relative stability in pulmonary-systemic flow balance. Changes were most apparent in systemic vascular resistance, venous pressures, heart rate, and regional oxygen extraction, identifying candidate physiologic targets for future multicenter validation.

title: Structural and mechanistic insights for calpain drug development.
authorString: Shapovalov I, Bell MA, Harper DT, Lewtas V, Dykstra-MacPherson T, Varty-Higgs A, Simonetti J, Davies PL, Greer PA.
abstractText:
Introduction

Calpains are Ca2+-activated cysteine proteases with broad roles in cell signaling, cytoskeletal remodeling, cell survival, differentiation, and tissue homeostasis. Calpain activity is implicated in multiple facets of human physiology, and its dysregulation has been reported in numerous pathologies. Yet, therapeutic targeting of calpains has been limited by challenges in achieving calpain-specific inhibition, owing to their complex biology and substrate diversity.

Areas covered

This review covers structural-, molecular- and cell-biology, disease associations, and recent intellectual property activity relevant to calpain drug development. Structural aspects include the domain architecture of classical and non-classical calpains, ancillary domains, calpastatin-mediated inhibition, homo- and heterodimerization, and emerging structural models. Calpains are considered in the broader landscape of cysteine proteases to highlight likely off-target liabilities. Disease- and pathology-focused sections discuss calpain-mediated signaling in neurodegeneration, muscular dystrophy, ocular disease, diabetes, endometriosis, cardiovascular pathology, fibrosis, and cancer. Strategies for calpain modulation are overviewed, including active-site, calpastatin-mimetic, and allosteric inhibitors, gene therapy, and RNA-based approaches.

Expert opinion

A shift beyond pan-calpain inhibition toward isoform-selective drug discovery, improved biomarkers, and accumulating structural insights offers new opportunities. Developing calpain-specific and isoform-selective therapeutics remains an exciting unmet opportunity in cancer, neurodegeneration, retinopathy, muscular dystrophy, and other diseases.

title: Impact of a multi-site, multidisciplinary self-measured blood pressure monitoring program.
authorString: Oprinovich S, Galdo JA, Guthrie KD.

journal.title: Journal of the American Pharmacists Association : JAPhA

abstractText: Improving hypertension control is designated as a Healthy People 2030 Leading Health Indicator. Self-measured blood pressure (SMBP) monitoring programs can help fill care gaps for underserved patients, including patients in rural locations. Local community healthcare institutions can expand SMBP program access to people with transportation and telemedicine barriers. To quantify the effects of a multi-site, multidisciplinary SMBP monitoring program on participant blood pressure measurements in 11 rural, underserved counties. The MPower Consortium, a regional health improvement network, serves 11 Southeast Missouri counties through collaborations among community pharmacies, public health departments, non-profit organizations, Federally Qualified Health Centers, and behavioral health organizations. Following a successful pilot, a SMBP monitoring program was expanded across the consortium. This study evaluated the first year of the MPower Consortium SMBP monitoring program. The program included initial patient education and three follow-up visits conducted by Community Health Workers, pharmacists, and nursing professionals in 11 counties. Outcomes included change in blood pressure and percent of participants meeting hypertension treatment goals. There were 302 patients included in the intent-to-treat analysis. Mean systolic blood pressure decreased from 144.3±21.9 mmHg to 134.2±14.8 mmHg (p<0.001) and mean diastolic blood pressure decreased from 83.1±13.3 mmHg to 77.5±9.0 mmHg (p<0.001). There was a statistically significant increase in percent of participants meeting goal blood pressure (p=0.008). The ANOVA analysis was significant for decrease in systolic blood pressure at each visit (p<0.001). There was no significant difference in the average systolic blood pressure decrease between the intent-to-treat and per-protocol groups (p=0.85). This multisite, multidisciplinary SMBP monitoring program lowered blood pressures in patients in rural, underserved areas. This study demonstrates benefit of a collaborative SMBP monitoring program performed by a multidisciplinary group of local healthcare organizations in reaching a vulnerable population.

title: Risk factors associated with ocular hypertension after steroid use in children.
authorString: Huang A, He J, Ying GS, Binenbaum G, Abbasian J, Oatts JT.
abstractText: To identify patient characteristics associated with ocular hypertension after steroid use in children. Retrospective cohort study. Children ≤18 years of age seen at a tertiary care children's hospital between 2009 and 2025 who were prescribed any type of steroid and had a documented intraocular pressure (IOP) measurement within 1 to 60 days of steroid initiation. Children with any IOP measurement >21 mmHg recorded prior to or on the day of steroid initiation were excluded. Steroid type, route of administration, and patient characteristics, including comorbidities, were extracted from the electronic medical record. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression models were used to identify factors independently associated with ocular hypertension after steroid use. Ocular hypertension among children who underwent IOP measurement after steroid initiation, defined as IOP >21 mmHg measured within 1 to 60 days of steroid initiation. Of 5,687 children included (mean age at steroid initiation 8.8 years; 54.4% male), 1,034 (18.2%) developed ocular hypertension. The most frequently prescribed steroid was fluticasone (20.0%), and the most common route of administration was inhaled/intranasal (24.8%). In multivariable analysis, glaucoma conferred the highest odds of ocular hypertension after steroid use (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 6.77; 95% CI, 5.21-8.79), followed by prednisone relative to dexamethasone (aOR, 3.37; 95% CI, 2.30-4.93), juvenile arthritis (aOR, 1.56; 95% CI, 1.09-2.24), and uveitis (aOR, 1.52; 95% CI, 1.16-1.99). Compared with topical administration, ocular (aOR, 3.57; 95% CI, 2.39-5.33) and intravenous (aOR, 2.63; 95% CI, 1.78-3.89) routes each independently conferred higher odds of ocular hypertension. Age, sex, race, ethnicity, diabetes, and asthma were not independently associated with ocular hypertension. Nearly 1 in 5 children with an IOP measurement within 1 to 60 days of steroid initiation developed ocular hypertension. Glaucoma, uveitis, juvenile arthritis, and non-topical routes of administration-particularly ocular and intravenous-were the strongest risk factors, highlighting the importance of ophthalmic monitoring in children receiving glucocorticoid therapy.

title: Comparison of pegfilgrastim and daily G-CSF for CD34<sup>+</sup> cell mobilization in healthy donors and post-transplant engraftment: The Pegfilgrastim-23 Study.
authorString: Hatase M, Goto H, Shimizu H, Toya T, Sugita J, Nishida T, Okada K, Yamauchi T, Umemoto Y, Takahashi S, Fujii N, Onozawa M, Shiratori S, Kamisawa M, Horita I, Inomata M, Oikawa T, Kobayashi M, Yamashita A, Doki N, Hino M, Teshima T.
abstractText: Pegfilgrastim (Peg-G), a long-acting formulation of granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (G-CSF), enables single-dose administration and effectively mobilizes CD34+ cells into the peripheral blood of healthy donors undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. However, prospective comparisons with conventional daily G-CSF (Daily-G) regarding mobilization efficacy and safety remain limited. Moreover, no previous studies have compared the differentiation profiles of CD34+ cells mobilized by these two agents. In this multicenter, prospective observational study, we assessed the efficacy, kinetics, safety and differentiation profiles of mobilized CD34+ cells induced by either 7.2 mg dose of Peg-G on day 1 (n = 29) or Daily-G at 400 μg/m2/day from day 1 (n = 31) in 60 healthy related donors scheduled to undergo CD34+ cell collection. Hematopoietic engraftment was also evaluated in 60 recipients following infusion of the collected peripheral blood stem cells. Of the 60 enrolled donors, 50 were evaluable for peripheral blood CD34+ cell counts. The mean CD34+ cell counts were 85.6 ± 48.0 × 10⁶/L in the Peg-G group and 84.6 ± 42.4 × 10⁶/L in the Daily-G group, with no significant difference between the groups (P = .992). Similar findings were observed in the analyses stratified by collection on days 4 and day 5. No significant differences were observed in the differentiation profiles of mobilized CD34⁺ cells. The kinetics of peripheral blood cell counts were generally comparable between the groups in both the day 4 and day 5 collection cohorts, except for a higher white blood cell count on day 4 in the Peg-G group among donors collected on day 5. In exploratory analyses, CD34⁺ cell mobilization efficacy was not correlated with day 4 serum G-CSF concentrations, donor age, body weight, body mass index, or body surface area in either of the treatment groups. Adverse events were common but predominantly consisted of pain-related symptoms that were manageable with supportive care. Grade 3 adverse events included liver dysfunction in three donors and hypertension in one. All laboratory abnormalities and clinical symptoms resolved by the follow-up assessment, and no grade ≥4 adverse events were observed in any donor. Median times to neutrophil engraftment were 16 and 15 days in the Peg-G and Daily-G groups, respectively (P = .73), and those to platelet engraftment were 30 and 27 days, respectively (P = .68). Single-dose 7.2-mg Peg-G and conventional Daily-G resulted in comparable peripheral blood CD34⁺ cell mobilization and differentiation profiles of mobilized CD34⁺ cells in healthy related donors, with generally manageable safety profiles. No significant differences in the time to neutrophil or platelet engraftment were observed between recipients in the two groups. These findings suggest that both mobilization strategies are clinically applicable and that regimen selection may be tailored according to drug-specific characteristics and donor convenience.

title: Mu (μ) opioid receptors (MOP) in food addiction.
authorString: Meir K, Era IH, Tolentino L, Muhammad AB, Lutfy K.
abstractText: The 21st century has been plagued with obesity worldwide, mostly in developed countries where access to food is plentiful. Obesity can be a precursor for many other diseases, such as hypertension, hyperlipidemia, type 2 diabetes mellitus, etc. Therefore, the underlying mechanism of obesity must be understood to cease its progression to other morbidities. There are two aspects of food intake: homeostatic feeding, which regulates energy intake so that the organism has a balanced energy level, and the hedonic feeding, which often causes the organism to consume food greater than its metabolic needs due to the food palatability and motivational alterations. The opioid system, specifically the mu (μ) opioid receptor (MOP), has been heavily implicated in playing an important role in both of these feeding processes. This article aims to review the literature regarding the role of the MOP on different aspects of food intake, including homeostatic and hedonic feeding, binge eating, as well as the existence of sexual dimorphism in food intake regulation via MOP.

title: Measurement error and repeatability of weighing scales: implications for heart failure care.
authorString: Merrild E, Poulsen CB, Lauridsen KG, Birn H, Løfgren B.

journal.title: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care

abstractText: Body weight guides decongestion in acute decompensated heart failure and is frequently used as a trial outcome, but scale performance in routine care is insufficiently characterized. To assess how closely household and medical scales measured known reference loads, how much measurements varied between scales, and how consistently scales performed during repeated measurements and across measurement days. We tested 37 digital scales (29 household and 8 medical) at two Danish hospitals using reference loads from 25 to 125 kg. Each scale underwent three measurements per load on two days. Household scales showed modest mean measurement error at most reference loads, but variability between devices increased and repeated and day-to-day measurements became less consistent as load increased. At 125 kg, median absolute measurement error was 1.13 kg on Day 1 and 1.43 kg on Day 2, while between-scale standard deviations (SDs) were 2.30 kg and 6.27 kg, respectively. Medical scales showed mean errors of 0.00-0.25 kg, between-scale SDs of 0.00-0.12 kg, consistently high repeatability, and small day-to-day differences. Among the scales tested, household scales showed modest mean measurement error but substantial between-scale variability and poorer repeatability at higher loads, whereas medical scales performed consistently. These findings support preferential use of medical scales in hospitals and use of the same device for serial measurements when household scales are used.

title: Perioperative management of patients with recent concussion undergoing noncardiac extracranial surgery: A modified Delphi consensus study.
authorString: Elganga M, Ma K, Zeiler FA, Sharma D, Rahim IA, Thakur J, Bryant A, Graves S, Benz D, Englesakis MF, Chowdhury T, Concussion Delphi Collaborators.
abstractText: Many patients present for surgery soon after concussion, when cerebral physiologic regulation may remain disturbed, and no evidence-based guideline or standardized consensus recommendations exist. We sought expert consensus for adults with recent concussion undergoing noncardiac extracranial surgery. We conducted a two-round modified Delphi study (November 2025-March 2026). Round 1 items, drafted from a systematic literature search, included case vignettes. Experts identified by bibliographic screening, directories, and nomination rated items on a five-point Likert scale; "do not know" responses were excluded from the denominator. Consensus was defined a priori as 75% agreement or greater, and strong consensus as 85% or greater. Thirty-five experts (33 anesthesiologists) from 17 countries completed both rounds; 13 of 16 Round 2 statements reached consensus. Agreement was unanimous for preoperative screening for concussion symptoms and neurologic red flags, and for avoidance of hypoxemia, abnormal carbon dioxide tension, sustained hypotension, and marked hypertension. Strong consensus supported generally deferring elective surgery until concussion symptoms resolve (97%), preoperative counseling (97%), structured follow-up (94%), and extended postoperative monitoring in higher-risk patients (91%). Consensus was not reached for regional anesthesia or monitored anesthesia care over general anesthesia (74%), electroencephalography-based depth of anesthesia monitoring (73%), or cautious long-acting neuraxial opioid use (69%). The panel did not define symptom resolution and established no symptom-independent waiting interval or concussion-specific numeric physiologic threshold. This anesthesiology-led consensus supports symptom-guided timing, physiologic stability, counseling, and structured follow-up; anesthetic technique, electroencephalographic monitoring, and neuraxial opioid use remain unresolved. The statements form an expert-informed framework, not an evidence-based practice guideline.

title: Global Burden of Heart Failure Attributable to Chronic Kidney Disease from 1990 to 2021 and Future Projections to 2050: A GBD 2021 Study.
authorString: Li MJ, Liu HY, Zhang YQ, Zhang JH, Li SR, Yang XL, Zeng Y.
abstractText: Heart failure attributable to chronic kidney disease (CKD) represents an important manifestation of the cardiorenal syndrome. However, its global burden, long-term trends, and relative contribution to the overall heart failure burden remain insufficiently characterized. In this observational, GBD-based analysis, data were obtained from the Global Burden of Disease 2021 study. We analyzed prevalence and years lived with disability (YLDs) of heart failure attributable to CKD from 1990 to 2021 at global, socio-demographic index (SDI) quintile, and national levels. Temporal trends were assessed using age-standardized rates, joinpoint regression, and age-period-cohort analysis. The relative contribution of CKD was calculated as CKD-attributable all-age numbers divided by total heart failure numbers. Future YLD rates were projected to 2050 using a Bayesian age-period-cohort model. Globally, prevalent cases increased from 506,142 in 1990 to 1,543,034 in 2021. The age-standardized prevalence rate rose from 10.44 to 19.14 per 100,000 population, and the age-standardized YLD rate increased from 1.33 to 2.42 per 100,000. The CKD-attributable share of total heart failure prevalence increased from 2.03% to 2.90%, and the corresponding YLD share increased from 2.74% to 3.86%. The projected global YLD rate reached 4.67 per 100,000 by 2050. CKD-attributable heart failure increased substantially from 1990 to 2021 and is projected to continue rising. CKD accounted for a small but increasing share of the global heart failure burden, supporting integration of kidney disease detection and management into heart failure prevention strategies.

title: Pre-capillary pulmonary hypertension associated with HHV-8-negative multicentric Castleman disease.
authorString: Li JY, Dang Y, Guo F, Zhang TY, Tian Z, Zhang L.
abstractText: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) has been reported in HHV-8-positive multicentric Castleman disease (MCD); however, its association with HHV-8-negative idiopathic MCD (iMCD) remains undocumented. We report a 29-year-old woman with iMCD who presented with exertional dyspnea and systemic inflammation and had pre-capillary PH confirmed by right heart catheterization. Siltuximab plus corticosteroids improved symptoms and hemodynamics; after relapse on sirolimus, tocilizumab induced complete clinical remission with biomarker normalization. This first report of iMCD-associated PH underscores the need to evaluate cardiopulmonary involvement in iMCD and highlights interleukin-6-driven immune dysregulation as a potential therapeutic target in this PH subgroup.

title: Complete remission achieved by multidisciplinary immunosuppressive therapy including plasma exchange in Kimura disease-associated membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis pattern of injury: a case report.
authorString: Kinguchi S, Oizumi T, Kumagai E, Koike J, Eto H, Komiya S, Urate S, Shinozaki S, Hirawa N, Tamura K.
abstractText: Kimura disease (KD) is a rare chronic inflammatory disorder characterized by cervical lymphadenopathy or subcutaneous masses in the head and neck region, accompanied by peripheral eosinophilia and elevated serum immunoglobulin E (IgE) levels. Nephrotic syndrome is a well-recognized complication of KD. Herein, we report a case of refractory nephrotic syndrome due to KD-associated membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis (MPGN) pattern of injury, in whom complete remission was achieved following multidisciplinary immunosuppressive therapy including plasma exchange (PE). A 33-year-old man with a history of KD presented to our hospital with nephrotic syndrome accompanied by a painless left cervical mass and elevated serum IgE levels. Kidney biopsy revealed MPGN pattern of injury. Nephrotic-range proteinuria and elevated serum IgE levels persisted, despite initiation of prednisolone (60 mg/day) and cyclosporine (150 mg/day) therapy. Six sessions of PE were subsequently administered, during which both proteinuria and serum IgE levels decreased. Because proteinuria tended to increase again after completion of PE, mycophenolate mofetil (1000 mg/day) was added. Prednisolone was successfully tapered to a maintenance dose of 7.5 mg/day, and complete remission has been maintained for 6 months. Th2-predominant immune responses and increased cytokine production have been implicated in the pathogenesis of KD, and elevated serum IgE levels have been associated with an elevated risk of disease recurrence. PE was used to rapidly remove circulating immune mediators potentially involved in KD. Our case suggests that PE may serve as a bridging intervention within multidisciplinary immunosuppressive therapy for refractory nephrotic syndrome due to KD-associated MPGN pattern of injury, although its independent therapeutic contribution remains uncertain.

title: Epiberberine attenuates diabetic atherosclerosis by inhibiting the Raf/MEK1/2/ERK1/2 pathway.
authorString: Wang G, Zhao Y, Zhang X, Zhang Y, Zhang X.
abstractText:
Background

Diabetic atherosclerosis (DA) is a major macrovascular complication of diabetes with limited therapeutic options. Epiberberine (EPI), an isoquinoline alkaloid, has shown anti-inflammatory and cardioprotective effects, but its role in DA remains unknown. This study investigated whether EPI ameliorates DA and explored the mechanisms involving endothelial pyroptosis and the Raf/MEK1/2/ERK1/2 signaling pathway.

Methods

Diabetic apolipoprotein E-deficient mice were induced by streptozotocin (55 mg/kg daily for 5 days). Mice with fasting blood glucose >15 mM were randomly assigned to control, low-dose EPI (50 mg/kg/day), or high-dose EPI (100 mg/kg/day) groups. A non-diabetic control group received citrate buffer. All treatments were administered orally for 10 weeks. Human umbilical vein endothelial cells were treated with high glucose plus oxidized low-density lipoprotein, with or without EPI (20 or 40 μM). Aortic plaque area, serum lipids, pyroptosis markers (cleaved-caspase 1 and gasdermin D N-terminal domain), inflammatory cytokines, and Raf/MEK1/2/ERK1/2 pathway activation were assessed.

Results

EPI reduced aortic plaque area by 31.4% (low dose) and 57.9% (high dose). Serum low-density lipoprotein cholesterol decreased from 2.5 mmol/L (diabetic controls) to 1.9 mmol/L (low-dose EPI) and 1.2 mmol/L (high-dose EPI). EPI also reduced cleaved-caspase 1 and gasdermin D N-terminal domain expression, indicating suppressed endothelial pyroptosis, and inhibited Raf/MEK1/2/ERK1/2 pathway activation in both endothelial cells and aortic tissues.

Conclusions

EPI alleviates vascular inflammation and atherosclerotic progression in diabetic mice, likely by suppressing endothelial pyroptosis through inhibition of the Raf/MEK1/2/ERK1/2 pathway. EPI represents a promising therapeutic strategy for diabetic macrovascular complications.

title: Impact of True and False Lumen Origins on Target Vessel Instability in Post-Dissection F/BEVAR.
authorString: Gomes VC, Farber MA, Beck AW, Eagleton MJ, Oderich GS, Kanamori LR, Schmid B, Schanzer A, Sweet MP, Zettervall SL, Timaran CH, Li X, Cantor RS, Parodi FE, U.S. Aortic Research Consortium.
abstractText:
Objective

To evaluate the occurrence of target artery-related adverse events in post-dissection F/BEVAR patients, based upon artery origin from the true or false lumen.

Methods

This is a multicenter, prospective, cohort study evaluating post-dissection patients treated with F/BEVAR, in the US Aortic Research Consortium. The primary endpoint was 5-year target vessel instability (TVI). Secondary endpoints included 5-year primary patency, freedom from secondary interventions (SIs), and type Ic and IIIc endoleaks. The analysis was performed on a per-vessel basis.

Results

A total of 1052 target arteries were analyzed, primarily including the celiac, superior mesenteric, and renal arteries, with individual hepatic and splenic arteries occasionally incorporated in the repair. Of the 277 patients included, 75% were men, and 19% were black, with a mean age of 66.8 ± 10.3 years. The mean aneurysm sac diameter was 66.0 ± 11.4 mm, with extent II thoracoabdominal aneurysms being the most prevalent (72.6%) among this cohort. Technical success was obtained in 96% of the cases. As primary outcome, the incidence of target vessel instability (TVI) was significantly lower (P<0.001) among the true-lumen vessels (16.4%) compared to false-lumen (29.9%) and dual-lumen arteries (43.8%). As for the secondary outcomes, the incidence of type Ic endoleak was significantly higher (P=0.001) in false-lumen vessels (9.6%) and dual-lumen vessels (8.6%) compared to true-lumen vessels (3.3%). There was no significant difference in the incidence of type IIIc endoleak (p=0.241) or target vessel occlusion (P=0.458). Target artery stenosis was significantly more common among arteries originating from the false lumen compared to true lumen (2.6% vs 0.4%, P=0.009). Fenestrations were associated with a higher incidence (30.5%) of TVI when compared to branches (5.9% P=0.005), however, this was observed only among dual-lumen vessels. Arteries incorporated by a fenestration and that had a dual-lumen origin, were associated with a higher occurrence of secondary interventions (23.7%) compared to true-lumen vessels (8.6%, P=0.010). The same was not observed among the arteries incorporated by a branch configuration. The time-to-event analysis demonstrated a significantly higher 5-year freedom from TVI in true-lumen vessels compared to false and dual-lumen ones (True lumen: 83.6%; False=70.1 %; Dual=56.2 %; Log-rank P=0.0002). Freedom from secondary interventions at 5 years was significantly higher in true-lumen vessels compared to dual-lumen ones (Log-rank P=0.0104), but not to false-lumen arteries (Log-rank P=0.0847). The 5-year primary patency did not differ significantly among groups (True lumen: 98.3%; False = 92.6%; Dual=93.9%; Log-rank P=0.1368). On Cox proportional hazards analysis, dual-lumen (95% CI 1.24-3.28, p=0.005) and false-lumen (95% CI 1.04 - 2.60, p=0.0325) target arteries were associated with an increased hazard of TVI, when compared to true lumen arteries, having 2.02 (P=0.005) and 1.65 (P=0.0325) times more risk of presenting TVI than a true-lumen vessel CONCLUSIONS: In F/BEVAR for post-dissection aneurysms, target vessel instability and secondary intervention are significantly lower in target arteries originating from the true lumen, when compared to false-lumen or dual-lumen vessels. Device design, with use of fenestrations or branches may also play a role, with a significant difference only observed in dual-lumen target arteries.

title: Lesion-targeting and vascular matrix-penetrating siRNA nanotherapeutics for the treatment of abdominal aortic aneurysm.
authorString: Wang S, Zhu R, Lei Y, Ren M, Zhou R, Zhou Y, Wei Y, Chen Y, Yin L.

journal.title: Journal of controlled release : official journal of the Controlled Release Society

abstractText: Inefficient aneurysmal aorta enrichment and vascular matrix penetration represent major challenges against siRNA delivery for the management of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA). Herein, platelet membrane (PM)-reversibly camouflaged nanocomplexes (NCs) are developed to deliver Poldip2 siRNA (siPoldip2) into vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs), which then restore vascular homeostasis by promoting phenotypic switching and mitigating oxidative stress. The NCs comprise a cationic nanocore assembled from siPoldip2 and a guanidinated and fluorinated bifunctional helical polypeptide (8FP), a charge-reversal intermediate layer of poly(<sub>l</sub>-lysine)-cis-aconitic acid (PC), and an outer shell of PM. After systemic administration in CaCl<sub>2</sub>-induced AAA rats, the NCs could preferentially accumulate at the aneurysmal site due to PM-mediated recognition of RGD-containing extracellular matrix proteins. The slightly acidic aneurysmal microenvironment subsequently triggers charge reversal of PC from negative to positive, which promotes the detachment of both PM and PC layers. The exposed 8FP/siPoldip2 nanocore penetrates the vascular matrix due to fluorocarbon-assisted repulsion of collagen mesh adsorption, followed by effective internalization by VSMCs. Consequently, Poldip2 expression in VSMCs is downregulated, which restores the contractile phenotype, and improves the aortic elasticity as well as structural integrity. This study provides a promising strategy for overcoming vascular delivery barriers and highlights the therapeutic promise of siRNA-based medical intervention for AAA.

title: Computed tomography derived cardiometabolic biomarkers in high-risk breast cancer using fully automated deep learning algorithms.
authorString: Tsou TC, Yang Z, Wang T, Qi H, Blackford A, Visvanathan K, Summers RM, Sheng JY.
abstractText:
Purpose

Cardiometabolic disease and obesity are important factors when considering breast cancer risk and survivorship. We aimed to utilize a fully automated deep learning algorithm to evaluate CT-derived cardiometabolic biomarkers in patients with breast cancer.

Methods

We applied fully automated deep learning algorithms to derive cardiometabolic markers from baseline computed tomography (CT) abdomen scans of females with breast cancer diagnosed between 2016 - 2018 at Johns Hopkins.

Results

Among 127 females (64.6% postmenopausal; 57.5% White and 26.8% Black race), BMI (body mass index) was positively correlated with CT-derived adipose tissue area and​ muscle area, and negatively correlated with liver intensity, but not associated with presence of aortic calcification. However, myosteatosis and menopausal status outperformed BMI as clinical markers of cardiometabolic health​ in breast cancer, as they were associated with both adiposity (especially visceral adiposity) and the presence of aortic calcification, with myosteatosis also being associated with liver steatosis.

Conclusion

Artificial intelligence algorithms can feasibly and directly quantify body composition, liver fat, and abdominal aortic plaque, and be a tool in evaluating metabolic disease risk in patients with breast cancer.
