title: Risk Factors for Diabetic Foot-Related Lower Extremity Amputation in Low- and Middle-Income Countries: A Systematic Review.
authorString: Eteuati J, Ntiamoah ME, Pitesa R, Mahadevan G, Hill AG.
abstractText:
Background

Diabetic foot disease is a major cause of lower limb amputation (LLA) in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where evidence on adjusted risk factors remains limited. This systematic review evaluates the risk factors for LLA and amputation-related mortality in diabetic foot disease across LMICs.

Methods

Embase, MEDLINE, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (via Ovid), PubMed, and Scopus were searched from inception to March 2026. Studies of adults with diabetes in LMICs reporting LLA with adjusted effect estimates were included. Pooling of effect estimates was prespecified to require at least three comparable studies per domain. Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale or AXIS.

Results

Sixteen studies (19,529 participants; 1604 amputation events) provided usable effect estimates; 12 reported adjusted estimates from multivariable models. No domain contained three or more comparable estimates, so quantitative synthesis was not undertaken. Osteomyelitis was independently associated with amputation in both studies assessing it (aOR 5.60, 95% CI 2.93-10.78; aOR 11.8, 95% CI 5.1-27.5). Peripheral arterial disease was associated with LLA in two of three studies using objective vascular assessment (aOR 2.80, 95% CI 1.52-5.11; aOR 3.23 per grade, 95% CI 2.68-3.89). Prior amputation was associated with LLA in two DFU cohorts reporting concordant estimates (aOR 2.86 and 3.08). Ulcer severity was associated with amputation in every study assessing it, using five different classification systems. Prolonged ulcer duration carried an adjusted odds ratio of 10.3 (95% CI 4.06-26.13), and each additional preoperative day was associated with a 9.3% increase in the odds of major amputation. Neuropathy showed no independent association of meaningful size in any adjusted analysis, and HbA1c was not associated in the largest adjusted DFU cohort analysis, although a smaller study with 10 outcome events reported a positive association.

Conclusion

Peripheral arterial disease, ulcer severity, osteomyelitis, prior amputation, and delayed access to care were associated with LLA in LMIC settings. Neither neuropathy nor HbA1c showed an independent association of meaningful size in adjusted analyses of established DFU cohorts. Prospective LMIC cohorts using standardized definitions are needed.

title: A detailed analysis of First pass Reperfusion and Number of Passes in MeVO Stroke Thrombectomy.
authorString: Stebner A, Bosshart SL, Diprose W, Uchida K, Dowlatshahi D, Volders D, Jumaa MA, Möhlenbruch M, Nimjee S, Booth T, Buck B, Kennedy J, Hill MD, Goyal M, Ospel J, ESCAPE-MeVO investigators.
abstractText:
Background and purpose

Reperfusion success after EVT and the number of EVT passes may be associated with clinical and imaging outcomes in patients with acute stroke due to Medium Vessel Occlusion (MeVO).

Material and methods

Secondary analysis of patients randomized to EVT in the ESCAPE-MeVO trial. Final reperfusion was assessed with the MeVO-expanded Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction (MeVO-eTICI) Score. First pass near-complete reperfusion was defined as MeVO-eTICI 2c-3 after 1 pass and multi-pass near-complete reperfusion as MeVO-eTICI 2c-3 after >1 pass. The primary outcome was the modified Rankin Score (mRS) at 90 days. Secondary outcomes included 24-hour NIHSS and 24-hour infarct volume, among others. Associations were assessed using regression models.

Results

Of 255 patients randomized to EVT (48.3%), 206 remained for the final analysis. First pass near-complete reperfusion was associated with decreased infarct volume (median 12.8ml [IQR 0.15-25.3] versus: 22.4ml [6.71-56.38ml], adjusted beta-coefficient -1.68 [95%CI::-2.54-(-0.81)]) and improved 24-hour NIHSS (median 7 [2-13.5] versus: 2.5 [1-6.5], adjusted beta-coefficient -0.56 [95%CI:-0.74-(-0.38)]), but not with clinical outcomes. Similarly, improved reperfusion status was associated with lower infarct volumes and improved 24-hour NIHSS but not with clinical outcomes. Number of EVT passes was associated with higher 90-day mRS (acOR 1.41 [95%CI: 1.04-1.91] per 1-additional pass), higher 24-hour NIHSS and larger infarct volume.

Conclusions

Improved first-pass reperfusion with EVT in MeVO stroke patients was associated with reduced infarct volumes and improved 24-hour NIHSS. Performing more EVT passes was associated with increased infarct volume and poorer 24-hour and 90-day outcomes.

title: Distinct Plasma and Fecal Lipidomic Responses to Stearic, Palmitic and Oleic Acids-Enriched Diets in Postmenopausal Women.
authorString: Zhang W, Matuszek G, Dolnikowski GG, Ausman LM, Lamon-Fava S, Lichtenstein AH, Matthan NR.
abstractText: Dietary saturated fat intake is associated with an unfavorable plasma lipidomic profile and increased CVD risk. Stearic acid (18:0), a saturated fatty acid (SFA) has been shown to lower plasma LDL-cholesterol concentrations compared to other shorter-chain SFAs, but its broader lipidomic effects remain unclear. We aimed to address this by analyzing fasting and non-fasting plasma and fecal lipidomes using samples from a randomized crossover study in postmenopausal women (N=20, 64±7 years, BMI 26.4±3.4kg/m<sup>2</sup>) who consumed isocaloric diets enriched in 16:0, 18:0, and 18:1 for 5 weeks each, with 2-week washouts. Lipidomic profiles (cholesteryl esters [CE], diglycerides and triglycerides [DG, TG], phosphatidylcholines [PC], ceramides (Cer), sphingomyelins [SM], and free fatty acids [FFA]) were measured by QTOF mass spectrometry. Partial least squares-discriminant analysis, and spearman correlation analyses assessed diet separation (Variable Importance of Projection score >1.0) and associations between lipidomic and circulating lipid profiles, respectively. The 16:0 diet resulted in higher fasting plasma concentrations of lipid species across multiple classes relative to the 18:0 and 18:1 diet. The nonfasting lipidome showed higher long-chain glycerolipids, PC species, and CE 16:1 concentrations after the 18:0 compared to the 16:0 diet, and higher FFAs and several sphingolipid species in the fecal lipidome relative to the 18:1 diet. Several SM, DG, TG, and PC species were positively associated with LDL cholesterol and TG concentrations (r= 0.68 to 0.75, FDR<0.1) in fasting plasma following the 18:0 diet. These findings demonstrate that individual SFAs exert differential effects across metabolic compartments, influencing circulating lipid concentrations.

title: Drug Repurposing in Pre-Eclampsia: Maternal Pharmacokinetic and Pharmacodynamic Considerations for Clinical Trial Design.
authorString: Phogole CM, Algharably EA, Decloedt EH, Cluver CA, Lorente VP.
abstractText: Pre-eclampsia is a hypertensive disorder of pregnancy affecting 3-8% of pregnancies worldwide, with no disease-modifying therapy currently available. Drug repurposing offers a promising strategy, yet no candidate has been validated to date. Pregnancy-associated physiological changes alter drug pharmacokinetics (PK), and pre-eclampsia itself may further modify drug disposition, complicating dose selection and contributing to inconclusive clinical trial outcomes. A structured literature search identified six prospective or randomized controlled trials of repurposed drugs for established pre-eclampsia: esomeprazole, omeprazole, sulfasalazine, pravastatin, recombinant antithrombin, and metformin. All drugs were well tolerated, with metformin the one to show promising clinical benefit by prolonging gestation; the remaining five drugs yielded inconclusive or null efficacy outcomes. Critically, PK sampling was conducted in only three trials, and none systematically characterized exposure-response relationships using key pre-eclampsia biomarkers, including soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase-1, soluble endoglin, and placental growth factor. Further common methodological limitations included small sample sizes (12-120 participants), heterogeneous gestational age eligibility criteria, and dosing regimens extrapolated from non-pregnant populations without pregnancy-specific optimization. These shortcomings likely contributed to the translational gap between promising preclinical findings and positive clinical trial outcomes. Model-informed drug development (MIDD) approaches, including physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) and population pharmacokinetic (popPK) modeling, optimal sampling strategies, and simulation-based dose selection, offer a framework to improve pre-eclampsia trial design. Future studies should integrate these approaches with biomarker-guided exposure-response analyses and prediction of fetal exposure throughout pregnancy to enhance therapeutic development, optimize maternal-fetal safety, and accelerate the identification of effective disease-modifying therapies for pre-eclampsia.

title: Health Seeking Behaviour Related to Hypertension Among Adults in Africa: A Scoping Review.
authorString: Sanyang M, Khan HTA, Vohra S.
abstractText: Hypertension is a major public health challenge in Africa, yet evidence on health-seeking behaviour and its determinants remains fragmented. This scoping review aimed to map the available evidence on health-seeking behaviour and its determinants related to hypertension among adults in Africa. The scoping review was conducted in accordance with the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodological guidance for scoping reviews and reported in line with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). Seven electronic databases were searched for peer-reviewed studies published between January 2010 and January 2025. Studies involving adults aged 18 years and older in African countries and addressing health-seeking behaviour or its determinants in relation to hypertension were eligible for inclusion. Sixteen studies from nine African countries were included. Healthcare-seeking behaviours were influenced by socio-economic status, cultural beliefs, social support, health system factors and knowledge of hypertension. Medical pluralism and delayed healthcare utilization were commonly reported. Hypertension-related health-seeking behaviour in Africa is shaped by individual, social, cultural and health-system factors. Interventions that address these factors are needed to improve hypertension prevention, early detection, treatment uptake and control.

title: Associations of short and long sleep duration with multiple adverse health outcomes among ageing adults in South Africa.
authorString: Pengpid S, Peltzer K, Hajek A.
abstractText: The aim of this study was to assess the longitudinal associations between short and long sleep duration with multiple adverse health outcomes (mortality, hypertension, cardiovascular disease, diabetes mellitus, functional limitations, depressive symptoms, loneliness, posttraumatic stress (PTSD) symptoms, impaired cognition, dynapenia, addominal obesity, dynapenic abdominal obesity, and general obesity) among community-residents 40 years and older, also broken down by sex. Data from three waves of the "Health and Ageing in Africa: A Longitudinal Study of an INDEPTH Community in South Africa (HAALSI)" (2015-2022) were utilized. There were 10483 observations of people who were 40 years of age or older. The American National Sleep Foundation was used to measure self-reported sleep duration. The association between sleep duration and 7-year mortality was assessed using hazard ratios. The longitudinal relationships between short and long sleep duration (using normal or recommended sleep length as a reference) and unfavorable health outcomes were estimated using linear, conditional, and multinomial logistic fixed effects (FE) regressions. This study showed an association between short sleep duration and mortality, hypertension, depressive symptoms, and cardiovascular disease, while there were no significant associations between short sleep duration and diabetes, functional limitations, loneliness, PTSD symptoms, impaired cognition, dynapenia, abdominal obesity, dynapenic abdominal obesity and general obesity. Furthermore, this study found an association between long sleep duration and functional limitations, depressive symptoms, loneliness, PTSD symptoms, impaired or lower cognition, dynapenia, abdominal obesity, dynapenic abdominal obesity and general obesity, while there were no significant associations between long sleep duration and mortality, cardiovascular disease, hypertension, and diabetes. Short sleep duration was associated with four and long sleep duration with nine adverse health outcomes. The results can be applied to health literacy and education initiatives to promote getting adequate sleep, which is a crucial aspect of total sleep health. Future studies from other countries are recommended.

title: Single-Access Retrieval of an Entrapped Rotational Atherectomy Burr Using Parallel-Wire STAR Technique.
authorString: Hussain A, Elsherif A, Khattak S, Shahid F, Khan SQ.
abstractText: Rotational atherectomy facilitates percutaneous coronary intervention in heavily calcified coronary lesions. Burr entrapment occurs in <1% of procedures, but it may cause vessel occlusion and myocardial ischemia. An 81-year-old woman with recurrent angina underwent rotational atherectomy-assisted percutaneous coronary intervention to a heavily calcified right coronary artery. The 1.5-mm burr became entrapped, resulting in inferior ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction. Successful retrieval of the burr was achieved via a single 7-F access by cutting the burr and extracting the drive shaft sheath, followed by subintimal tracking and re-entry (STAR) with a parallel wire, then external crushing to modify the calcified plaque. This case demonstrates parallel-wire balloon-assisted plaque modification as an effective percutaneous bailout strategy for an entrapped rotablation burr. Subintimal tracking and re-entry (STAR) with a parallel wire and external plaque crushing by a balloon is feasible from a single 7-F sheath by cutting the burr and extracting the drive-shaft sheath.

title: Prognostication of end-stage heart failure using a machine learning model based on haemodynamics and cardiac energetics data.
authorString: Blanco PJ, Bulant CA, Goswami R, Torii R, Brittain EL, Annis JS, Belkin MN, García-García HM, Bourantas C, Grinstein J.
abstractText:
Aims

In the evolving landscape of heart failure treatment, clinicians face challenges in predicting which end-stage heart failure patients will require heart replacement therapies, such as left ventricular assist devices or transplantation, or are at risk of death. Traditional risk models often fail to accurately stratify patients due to complex interactions of guideline-directed medical therapy, individual responses, and haemodynamic or shock phenotypes.

Methods and results

This study introduces a novel approach using machine learning to predict patient outcomes by analysing a comprehensive set of haemodynamic variables, including metrics tied to cardiac energetics-an emerging field focused on heart energy dynamics during failure. A dataset of 2904 patients across the spectrum of heart failure was used to train and test the models, which underwent rigorous model selection, cross-validation, and hyperparameter tuning on 70% of the data, using forward feature selection. Metrics for the remaining 30% used for testing resulted in an area under the curve of 0.81, a Matthews correlation coefficient of 0.35, and an accuracy of 0.74 to predict the composite endpoint of survival free from death, left ventricular assist devices, or transplant at 1 year. We also demonstrate consistency across the different patient databases used for training, validation, and testing, supported by an F1 score of 0.65 overall and 0.82 for patients who received medical management. The model shows a promising negative predictive value of 0.92, but external validation with a prospective database is needed before clinical application.

Conclusion

This approach is novel in integrating haemodynamics and cardiac energetics with machine learning towards more individualized and effective treatment for heart failure patients.

title: Single-AAV-mediated cardiomyocyte-specific adenine base editing ameliorates cardiac hypertrophy in vivo
authorString: Monnikhof T, Han SJ, Stumpo L, Koshian S, Agirman C, de Ruiter H, Luppino A, Wigman T, Chevalier M, Perini I, Versteeg D, Wehrens M, de Leeuw AE, Wright-Clark M, van Kampen SJ, Zentilin L, Sahtoe DD, Konkalmatt PR, Mandegar MA, Reid CA, Ivey KN, Giacca M, Boogerd CJ, van Rooij E.
abstractText: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is the most common inherited cardiac disorder, frequently accompanied by cardiac hypercontractility, diastolic dysfunction, heart failure and sudden cardiac death. The disease is predominantly caused by pathogenic variants in genes encoding sarcomeric proteins and current therapeutic strategies largely focus on symptom management. Adeno-associated virus-based (AAV) delivery of base editing tools has emerged as an alternative strategy that acts directly on the genetic cause of disease. However, canonical SpCas9-based editors are too large to package into a single-AAV vector which mandates dual-AAV approaches that require higher overall vector doses with elevated toxicity risk and increased manufacturing costs. Here, we report the development and application of a single vector approach for cardiomyocyte-specific adenine base editing to correct a Dutch founder mutation in  MYBPC3 (c.2827C>T, p.Arg943Ter) that causes HCM. We systematically compared compact base editors in human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (hiPSC-CMs) and selected the most efficient configuration, which reversed disease-associated hypercontractility in engineered human myocardium (EHM). To fit the editor/guide construct in a single-AAV vector, we screened a library of rationally designed small chimeric promoters and identified 6C2 to effectively drive expression in hiPSC-CMs and cardiac tissue of both mice and non-human primates (NHP) with exceptional specificity. Delivered in a single next-generation cardiotropic AAV capsid, we achieved therapeutic correction in an HCM mouse model at doses 20-fold below published dual-AAV cardiomyopathy base editing approaches. These results establish cardiomyocyte-specific, single vector-mediated base editing as a viable therapeutic strategy for inherited cardiomyopathies.

title: Oxygen Uptake Efficiency Slope (OUES) and Mortality in Chronic Heart Failure: Comparisons of Absolute and Percent-predicted Values across Different Equations
authorString: Leopoldino Costa G, Donelli Costa G, Colares Barros F, Menegazzo WR, Saadi MP, Goulart Prata Oliveira Milani J, Milani M, Van Der Sand L, da Silveira AD.
abstractText:
Aim:

The oxygen uptake efficiency slope (OUES) is a prognostic indicator obtained from cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPX) in chronic heart failure (CHF) patients. Although various equations exist for calculating predicted OUES, it remains unclear whether absolute or percent-predicted values offer a more accurate prognostic assessment. To investigate and compare mortality prediction in CHF patients using the OUES absolute values or the percent-predicted approach, incorporating the equations of Hollenberg, Buys, and Milani.

Methods:

Retrospective cohort study involving CHF patients evaluated at a tertiary university hospital between July 2013 and July 2023. All patients underwent maximal CPX and were followed in a specialized outpatient clinic. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality. To compare the prognostic accuracy between different approaches, we performed receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis and Cox proportional hazards regression.

Results:

A total of 1.180 patients were included, 57% male, with a mean age of 55 ± 12 years. The median follow-up was 5.0 years (IQR 3.0 to 7.2 years), resulting in 147 deaths (12.5%). The area under de curve (AUC) was 0.71 to 0.72 for males, and 0.60 to 0.63 for females, without statistical difference in the AUC between absolute and percent-predicted OUES. Different cut-offs were identified for each sex for predicting mortality and all OUES metrics remained independent predictors in multivariate models using sex and age.

Conclusions:

OUES, in both absolute and percent-predicted forms, demonstrated similar accuracy in predicting mortality in CHF, with sex-specific cut-offs influencing clinical assessment.

title: How I Do It: An Intensivist's guide to RV Failure and Right Ventricular Assist Devices.
authorString: Sridhar M, Patel M, Manek G, Chowdhury J, Villalobos N, Soto F, Jose A, Sood N, Shlobin OA, Rali P, Akkanti B, Cardiology/CV Surgery Section, Pulmonary Vascular Disease and Cardiovascular Network..
abstractText: Right ventricular failure (RVF) is a high-mortality form of cardiogenic shock frequently encountered in critical illness and is often underrecognized due to its heterogeneous presentation. This article presents a physiology-driven, stepwise approach to the diagnosis and management of acute RVF using a longitudinal case in the intensive care unit. We highlight practical bedside tools for recognition, including point-of-care ultrasound and invasive hemodynamics, and review targeted strategies for preload optimization, afterload reduction, and contractility support. Special emphasis is placed on airway management, vasoactive medications, and timely escalation to mechanical circulatory support (MCS) in appropriately selected patients. This bedside "How I Do It" guide is written for intensivists and pulmonary/critical care clinicians and translates advanced hemodynamic and device concepts into practical decision points for acute care management.

title: Targeted Methotrexate Treatment in Cesarean Scar Pregnancy: A Case Report and Literature Review.
authorString: Adamczyk M, Limowska H, Zwierzchowska A, Merks P, Barcz E.

journal.title: Case reports in obstetrics and gynecology

abstractText: Cesarean scar pregnancy (CSP) represents a rare form of ectopic pregnancy, though its incidence is expected to rise in countries with rising rates of deliveries by cesarean section (CS). Delayed diagnosis and treatment can result in uterine rupture and hemorrhage. Diagnosis is based on transvaginal ultrasonography (TVUS). No standardized treatment protocol for CSP has been established; however, local ultrasound-guided methotrexate (MTX) injection into the gestational sac (GS) is widely recognized as a highly effective therapy. A 38-year-old woman with a history of CS 2 years prior was admitted to the hospital due to moderately heavy vaginal bleeding that had started 4 days before. Her general condition was assessed as stable. The last menstrual period occurred 6 weeks and 2 days earlier. A β-hCG test performed on presentation showed a level of 10,775 mIU/mL. TVUS revealed a GS measuring 8.6 mm located within the CS scar, containing a yolk sac and an embryo with a CRL of 2.8 mm. Cardiac activity had not been detected. A diagnosis of CSP was made. Other laboratory tests showed no abnormalities. On the following day, the β-hCG level had increased to 13,001 mIU/mL. Under TVUS guidance, 80 mg of MTX was injected into the GS. Following days showed a gradual decline in β-hCG levels, reaching 927.77 mIU/mL on the third day postprocedure. A follow-up TVUS revealed no visible GS. The patient remained in stable condition and was discharged from the hospital. On Day 10 postprocedure, the β-hCG level had decreased to 62.04 mIU/mL. Aside from mild uterine bleeding, the patient reported no other complaints. In the presented case, early detection followed by timely ultrasound-guided MTX injection into the GS achieved complete resolution without requiring additional interventions, highlighting its potential as a safe and effective conservative approach when CSP is diagnosed early.

title: Longitudinal Cardiac Remodeling in High-Output Heart Failure From Intravascular Leiomyomatosis.
authorString: Cooke B, Ong KL, Mace H, Carlyle J, Morgan W.
abstractText: Intravascular leiomyomatosis can extend into nearby pelvic vasculature and to sites as distant as the heart and form arteriovenous malformations, leading to shunting and eventual high-output heart failure. A 45-year-old woman with biopsy-proven intravascular leiomyomatosis presented with biventricular dysfunction. Right heart catheterization demonstrated significant left-to-right shunting with high cardiac output. Serial echocardiography over 12 years showed the development of both left- and right-sided cardiac dysfunction. With treatment, left ventricular function recovered; however, right ventricular dilation and functional tricuspid regurgitation from annular dilation established a self-sustaining cycle of right-sided failure. Prior reports capture a single point in time; this 12-year echocardiographic course documents how shunt-mediated volume overload can progress to structural, self-perpetuating right heart failure independent of the original precipitant. Shunt-mediated high-output heart failure can produce progressive cardiovascular deterioration. Early recognition and multidisciplinary care are essential to prevent irreversible structural remodeling.

title: An Infiltrative Left Atrial Mass With Valvular Involvement: Rare Case of Primary Cardiac Intimal Sarcoma.
authorString: Pateqi N, Brar A, Ghannam H, Paruchuri N, Aziz KA, Leddon J, Wang J, Laipply K, Louis L, Harris D.
abstractText:
Background

Primary cardiac intimal sarcoma is an exceedingly rare and aggressive malignant cardiac tumor, often associated with poor prognosis.

Case summary

We report a case of a 38-year-old woman with progressive dyspnea who was found to have a large left atrial mass involving the mitral valve apparatus, resulting in severe mitral regurgitation and stenosis. Multimodality imaging demonstrated several features concerning for malignancy, including local infiltration, heterogeneous tissue characteristics, and central necrosis. The patient underwent surgical resection with initial pathology suggesting leiomyosarcoma, though next-generation sequencing ultimately established the diagnosis of cardiac intimal sarcoma.

Discussion

This case emphasizes the role of multimodality imaging in the evaluation of intracardiac masses. Although there are no established guidelines for the treatment of cardiac intimal sarcoma, the mainstay of treatment is surgical resection, with adjuvant chemotherapy considered on an individualized basis.

Take-home messages

Primary cardiac intimal sarcoma is an exceptionally rare but aggressive cause of an intracardiac mass. Multimodality imaging can help distinguish malignant from benign cardiac masses and guide operative planning. Accurate diagnosis of cardiac intimal sarcoma remains challenging because histopathologic features can overlap with other subtypes of sarcomas.

title: Late Percutaneous Retrieval of a Septal Occluder to Facilitate Left Atrial Access.
authorString: Dowaikh AM, Al Sahari AH, Alhebaishi YS, Momenah T.
abstractText:
Background

We describe intentional retrieval of a well-seated septal occluder device for left atrial access.

Case summary

A 28-year-old woman with platypnea-orthodeoxia and exertional desaturation down to 50% underwent patent foramen ovale closure. She developed refractory atrial tachycardia requiring left atrial mapping. Twenty days later, the device was retrieved percutaneously. Partial endothelization prevented resheathing, so the device and sheath were withdrawn together. The snare slipped in the inferior vena cava, and the device migrated into the main pulmonary artery before recapture and extraction. After multiple electrophysiology procedures, a Gore Cardioform occluder was implanted to preserve future transseptal access.

Discussion

This case demonstrates the technical challenges of retrieving a partially endothelialized occluder and the value of proactive device-control strategies.

Take-home messages

Device retrieval during early endothelialization can carry migration risk due to device stiffness; balloon stabilization may prevent it. Anticipating future transseptal needs should guide device choice at reclosure.

title: Mapping the Literature on Preoperative Oral Carbohydrate Loading: A Bibliometric Analysis.
authorString: Çetinkaya MM, Taylan S, Eti Aslan F.

journal.title: Journal of perianesthesia nursing : official journal of the American Society of PeriAnesthesia Nurses

abstractText: This study aims to provide a structured, macroscopic overview of nursing research on preoperative oral carbohydrate loading through bibliometric analysis. It also examines the characteristics and development of this research field. Bibliometric analysis study. The Web of Science database was selected for the bibliometric analysis, and the data analyzed included publications up to December 1, 2024. The analysis was performed using the "Biblioshiny" application in the Bibliometrix R package. Between 1977 and 2024, 292 nursing articles related to preoperative oral carbohydrate loading were published in 167 sources. When examining the annual scientific output of nursing studies related to preoperative oral carbohydrate loading, the most productive journals were found to be Clinical Nutrition (n = 15), Journal of Perianesthesia Nursing (n = 11), and British Journal of Surgery (n = 10). According to analyses based on Bradford's Law of Scattering, there are 167 productive journals in the nursing literature related to preoperative oral carbohydrate loading. These journals are distributed as follows: 16 journals in the first region, 55 journals in the second region, and 96 journals in the third region. Authors and articles were organized according to Lotka's Law. Of the authors (n = 2145), 92.1% had one article, 6.2% had two articles, 1.0% had three articles, and 0.1% (n = 6) had more than five articles. Gaps in the literature were identified in the following areas: cardiac surgery, gastric fluid volume, hyperglycemia, length of stay, major abdominal surgery, and protocols. The countries with the highest number of publications were China, the United States, and the United Kingdom. Global collaborations related to this topic included: Sweden-United Kingdom (n = 9), United States-United Kingdom (n = 6), and United States-Canada (n = 5). This bibliometric study provides a comprehensive and integrative review of the global literature on preoperative oral carbohydrate loading in nursing.

title: Advances in HFpEF Research Based on Characteristics of Older Adults.
authorString: Li R, Hashim R.
abstractText: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is the most common heart failure phenotype in older adults, associated with significant functional impairment and poor prognosis. Increasing evidence suggests that HFpEF should be considered a systemic, age-related syndrome, rather than an isolated cardiac disease. This review summarizes recent advances in the epidemiology, pathophysiology, and cellular mechanisms of HFpEF, with a particular focus on the frailty-sarcopenia-malnutrition triad. Age-related inflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and anabolism resistance interact with the hemodynamic abnormalities specific to HFpEF, leading to decreased exercise tolerance and functional decline. Frailty, muscle loss, and malnutrition often coexist in elderly patients with HFpEF and synergistically exacerbate clinical outcomes. Exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation and narrative lifestyle interventions are effective strategies for addressing these geriatric syndromes, and this review will address these issues. This article is a narrative review synthesizing current evidence on geriatric vulnerability phenotypes and rehabilitation-based interventions in older adults with HFpEF.

title: Acute Pulmonary Oedema and Hypercapnic Respiratory Failure During a Probable Autonomic Dysreflexic Episode in Chronic Cervical Spinal Cord Injury: A Case Report.
authorString: Ghannoum A, Young AC, Rao R.
abstractText: Autonomic dysreflexia is a life-threatening complication affecting individuals with spinal cord injuries at or above the sixth thoracic level. While episodic hypertension is its clinical hallmark, serious cardiovascular and respiratory complications may occur. We report the case of a 67-year-old male with long-standing C5-C6 tetraplegia and established autonomic dysreflexia who was admitted with community-acquired pneumonia (CAP). At approximately 01:00 on hospital day 4, after receiving approximately 3 L of maintenance intravenous fluid for poor oral intake over the preceding 72 hours, he developed sudden severe breathlessness and loss of consciousness despite a previously improving oxygen requirement. Oxygen saturation fell to 77% despite oxygen therapy, while systolic blood pressure rose from a baseline of approximately 125-130 mmHg to 167 mmHg. Physical examination revealed bilateral crackles and reduced air entry. Arterial blood gas analysis showed profound hypercapnic acidaemia (pH 7.009; partial pressure of carbon dioxide 18.5 kPa). A chest radiograph showed rapidly progressive bilateral airspace opacities consistent with pulmonary oedema. His blood pressure returned towards baseline, and following high-concentration oxygen and intravenous furosemide, his oxygen requirement subsequently decreased. Computed tomography pulmonary angiography excluded pulmonary embolism, and echocardiography showed low-normal left ventricular systolic function without a major structural or valvular abnormality. The sudden respiratory deterioration, clinically significant rise in blood pressure from baseline, rapid radiographic evolution, and subsequent improvement supported acute pulmonary oedema occurring during a probable autonomic dysreflexic episode. No discrete precipitating stimulus was confirmed, although concurrent pneumonia was considered the most likely trigger for autonomic dysreflexia. Recent intravenous fluid administration and underlying cardiac vulnerability may have lowered the threshold for pulmonary oedema. This case highlights the importance of recognising a clinically meaningful rise from baseline blood pressure when a patient with high spinal cord injury develops sudden respiratory deterioration.

title: Fabrication of Pt-decorated MXene-chitosan nanocomposite electrodes for non-enzymatic electrochemical detection of biomolecules.
authorString: N S, Sasikumar S, Mohapatra A, Bhole KB, Arya SB, Murugesan S.
abstractText: Cholesterol and hydrogen peroxide (H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub>) are essential biomolecules for maintaining the physical equilibrium, and their abnormal levels cause cancer and several cardiovascular diseases. To address the drawbacks of enzymatic techniques, including poor stability, high fabrication cost, and sensitivity to environmental conditions, a platinum nanoparticle (Pt) anchored MXene-chitosan composite (Pt/MX-Chit) was coated on an ITO substrate to develop a robust non-enzymatic platform. The integration of highly conductive MXene, electrocatalytically active Pt nanoparticles, and a biocompatible, film-forming chitosan matrix enables efficient electron transfer, improves the structural stability, and increases the number of surface-active sites compared to the existing non-enzymatic platforms. The fabricated electrode provides enzyme-free cholesterol detection by the catalytic oxidation of cholesterol and H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub> by catalytic reduction. The structural characteristics and surface morphology of the synthesized materials were examined by SEM, XRD, TEM, AFM, and FTIR. The developed sensor exhibited a linear response to H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub> concentration (0-160 µM) with a sensitivity of 1.29 µA µM<sup>-1</sup>, and an estimated LOD value of 4.57 µM and LOQ of 15.25 µM, which shows the strong catalytic reduction capability of the Pt/MX-Chit composite electrode interface. Non-enzymatic cholesterol detection was also performed with a positive response within the range of 0-20 µM through the oxidation of cholesterol in the anodic oxidation region. The sensor achieved a sensitivity of 14.6 µA µM<sup>-1</sup>. The estimated LOD and LOQ are 0.30 µM and 1.01 µM, respectively. The fabricated Pt/MX-Chit-ITO electrode offers a cost-effective and fast detection platform for biosensing applications.

title: Epidemiology of TB in the hot zone of Sudan's armed conflict following 3 years of catastrophic war.
authorString: Mohammed AKY, Humida EHM, Hamid NA, Ahmed HG.
abstractText: TB is a major global health problem, particularly in low-resource, armed conflict areas. This study aimed to assess the epidemiology of TB in a hot conflict zone after 3 years of continuing armed conflict in western Sudan. This is a retrospective descriptive study conducted at El-Obeid Teaching Hospital in North Kordofan State, Sudan, from April 2023 to April 2026. We obtained all data on patients diagnosed with TB from the hospital. The sample size includes all TB patients throughout the designated period. About 3,498 people displayed signs of TB, of whom 2,193 got a confirmed diagnosis. The overall prevalence of TB was 85 cases per 100,000 people. The prevalence of pulmonary TB was 57 per 100,000, and extra-pulmonary TB was 28 per 100,000 individuals. Men represented 70.2%, and women were 29.8%. The 21-29 age group had the highest prevalence, followed by 30-39, 40-54, 55+, and ≤20 years, with rates of 22.5%, 20.8%, 20.7%, 19.2%, and 16.6%. There is an increase in the prevalence of TB in Western Sudan, particularly among younger adult men and gold mining workers. This data indicates that TB is a major public health issue in the region, particularly among at-risk populations.

title: Rare Differentiation in Genes XIRP1 and XIRP2 Associated With Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.
authorString: Wang F, Yuan T, Zhao W, Shao G, Li S, Lv L, Li R, Liu J, Li X, Wang W, Liu F, Shang X, Hu S.
abstractText:
Objective

The molecular mechanisms underlying hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) phenotypes remain incompletely understood. Xin actin-binding repeat containing 1 and 2 (XIRP1 and XIRP2) are adhesion proteins localized to the adherens junctions of intercalated discs (ICDs). While mutations in these genes are known to cause cardiomyopathy, their specific contribution to HCM phenotypes is unclear.

Methods

The study was conducted on heart tissue samples from 36 patients diagnosed with HCM and 8 healthy donors. The upregulation of XIRP2 has been observed, which was confirmed by Quantitative RT-PCR analysis. We further evaluated the association between genetic variants of XIRP1 and XIRP2 genes and HCM phenotype by targeted resequencing in 619 unrelated HCM patients and 307 healthy controls who did not carry any mutation in eight genes commonly mutated in myofilament disease. Using capillary Sanger sequencing, which excludes polymorphisms and probably neutral variants, the number of rare variants was verified in HCM patients.

Results

mRNAs demonstrating a statistically significant difference in expression levels of at least twofold (p < 0.01) between experimental groups were chosen for subsequent analysis. The prevalence of rare variants in XIRP1 and XIRP2 genes was higher in HCM patients compared to controls [9.0% (56/619) vs. 3.9% (12/307), χ 2 = 7.96, p = 0.005], particularly XIRP2 (6.0% vs. 2.0%, p = 0.006). In HCM tissues, the expression of XIRP2 had increased dramatically by more than nine times (p < 0.001). The rates of inexplicable syncope (p = 0.036) and LV outflow obstruction (p = 0.012) and myocardial fibrosis (p = 0.010) were higher in the carriers.

Conclusions

Rare variants in XIRP1 and XIRP2 correlate with adverse HCM phenotypes, implicating ICD dysfunction in disease progression. Thereby giving more in-depth information about the relationship between the prognosis of HCM and XIRP1 and that of XIRP2.

title: Giant cell myocarditis mimicking cardiac amyloidosis with apical sparing pattern in echocardiography: a case report.
authorString: Sawada S, Miura M, Endo H, Ono S, Nakamura A.
abstractText:
Background

Giant cell myocarditis typically has a poor prognosis among the various types of myocarditis. Early diagnosis and treatment are essential to save lives. Immunosuppressive therapy is used for giant cell myocarditis; however, evidence in patients on mechanical circulatory support is insufficient.

Case summary

A woman in her 60 s with no history of heart disease or medication was admitted to our hospital because of congestive heart failure. Echocardiography revealed an apical sparing pattern suggestive of cardiac amyloidosis. However, owing to the rapid deterioration of symptoms, an urgent right heart catheterization and myocardial biopsy were performed. Right heart catheterization revealed a cardiac index of 1.20 L/min/m2, and rapid myocardial histology indicated inflammatory cell infiltration. She was later diagnosed with giant cell myocarditis with cellular infiltration of irregular multinucleated giant cells in the myocardium. Her condition improved after starting mechanical circulatory support and sequential immunosuppressive therapy, and after successful rehabilitation, she was discharged as an outpatient on Day 183.

Discussion

Early diagnosis and prompt initiation of immunosuppressive therapy are essential in giant cell myocarditis; however, specific findings are lacking. Early myocardial biopsy and prompt mechanical circulatory support initiation should be performed in patients with rapidly deteriorating heart failure presenting with amyloidosis-like echocardiographic findings and in cases where only troponin is elevated and creatine phosphokinase MB is not, considering the possibility of severe oedema. Combination immunosuppressive therapy under mechanical circulatory support is associated with a high infection risk, and starting with single-drug immunosuppressive therapy with careful haemodynamic monitoring is acceptable.

title: Comparative Prognostic Value of the Triglyceride-Glucose Index, hs-CRP, and the Derived C-Reactive Protein-Triglyceride-Glucose Index for Major Adverse Cardiovascular and Cerebrovascular Events in Acute Coronary Syndrome: Insights From a Prospective Cohort.
authorString: Wang W, Meng X, Zhang Y, Lin L, Zhao Z, Han J, Feng R, Bai Y, Guo L, Ding Y, Zeng Y.
abstractText: The C-reactive protein-triglyceride-glucose index (CTI) combines inflammation with metabolic status, but its prognostic value in patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) remains unclear. We studied 9131 patients with ACS admitted between 2021 and 2024 to examine the associations of CTI, the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) with long-term major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE). Cox regression models, restricted cubic spline analyses, and predictive performance analyses were performed. After a median follow-up of 707 days, 801 patients developed MACCE. In fully adjusted models, CTI (hazard ratio [HR] = 1.248, 95% CI: 1.150-1.355), the TyG index (HR = 1.235, 95% CI: 1.115-1.367), and hs-CRP (HR = 1.031, 95% CI: 1.018-1.047) were all significantly associated with MACCE risk. Patients in the highest CTI quartile had a greater risk of MACCE than those in the lowest quartile (HR = 1.651, 95% CI: 1.333-2.045). Restricted cubic spline analyses showed positive associations without significant nonlinearity. CTI yielded a numerically higher area under the curve (AUC) than the TyG index and hs-CRP, although the improvement was modest. These findings suggest that CTI may provide supplementary metabolic-inflammatory information for MACCE risk assessment in ACS, but external validation is needed.

title: Artificial intelligence-enhanced electrocardiography for detection and prediction of dilated cardiomyopathy.
authorString: Sieliwonczyk E, Sau A, Liang Y, Patlatzoglou K, McGurk KA, Pastika L, Theotokis P, Barker J, Zeidaabadi B, Tayal U, Halliday BP, Prasad S, O'Regan DP, Peters NS, Beelen NJ, Verdonschot JAJ, Saenen J, Van Leuven O, Gorissen P, Loeys B, Ge J, Kramer DB, Waks JW, Ware JS, Ng FS.
abstractText:
Background and aims

A major challenge in dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) care is the identification and management of individuals at risk before disease manifestation. An artificial intelligence (AI) model applied to electrocardiography (ECG) was developed to detect and predict the echocardiographic DCM phenotype (left ventricular dilatation with systolic dysfunction) and was evaluated for its ability to stratify the risk of incident DCM in familial cohorts.

Methods

A deep learning model was trained to detect the echocardiographic DCM phenotype and to predict its future onset, using more than 330 000 ECG-echocardiogram pairs from the Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, Boston. Model performance was validated in cohorts from the UK Biobank, Zhongshan Hospital, and Antwerp University Hospital, and compared with models based on traditional ECG features and echocardiographic traits. To assess performance in familial DCM, genetically predisposed individuals identified through cascade screening at the cardiogenetics clinics of Antwerp University Hospital (n = 166, 18% DCM positive) and Maastricht University Medical Center (n = 177, 18% DCM positive) were evaluated.

Results

The AI-ECG model achieved areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of .87-.97 for diagnosing the prevalent DCM phenotype, outperforming traditional ECG parameters. AI-ECG was comparable to echocardiography for predicting future DCM (C-index .80-.87 and .80-.90, respectively). In familial cohorts, 5-year negative predictive values were 95.5% (Antwerp) and 91.5% (Maastricht), with corresponding positive predictive values of 42.4% and 39.4%, while high-risk scores were associated with a 5.1-6.4-fold increased risk of incident DCM.

Conclusions

The explainable AI-ECG model detects the echocardiographic DCM phenotype and predicts future disease, and supports the exclusion of short- to mid-term disease in genetically at-risk individuals. This low-cost tool could help reduce surveillance burden and facilitate earlier intervention.

title: A 3D Print-Based Experimental Framework for the Assessment of Haemocompatibility in Rotodynamic Blood Pumps.
authorString: Suria AJ, Crescenti N, Torner B, Zimpfer D, Granegger M.
abstractText:
Objective

Variability of 3D-printed rotodynamic blood pumps (RBP) indicators is a crucial factor in haemocompatibility evaluation. Thus, the aim is to investigate the reproducibility of a 3D printed-based framework for further use on systematic haemocompatible studies when changing key impeller parameters in RBPs.

Methods

Reproducibility was assessed in terms of standard deviation (SD), of the normalized index of haemolysis (NIH) and generated pressure head between 3 RBPs. A conventionally manufactured benchmark RBP, one 3D printed (3DP) exact replica, ( β2=79° ), and one 3DP with a modification ( β2=155° ) (n = 7). In vitro haemolysis experiments were carried out. Newly 3DP impellers were used for each experiment to study the manufacturing reproducibility. Moreover, pressure head-flow rate curve analysis and computational fluid dynamic (CFD) simulations were performed to support the findings.

Results

The mean NIH ± SD in mg/100 L for the 3 RBPs was 4.25 ± 1.95 for the benchmark, 6.40 ± 2.68 for the exact replica, and 7.75 ± 1.87 for the modified version. Only a significant difference (p < 0.05) between the benchmark and modified version was found. Conversely, no strong statistical differences were found between the 3DP RBPs. Furthermore, SD values of pressure heads were similar between all the groups. The resulting damage index for the 3DP geometries was 2.37 (·10-4) and 2.32 (·10-4) for the replica and modified version respectively. Suggesting a probable small effect when variating β2 in free stream pumps.

Conclusions

Same NIH and pressure head SD range has shown the viability of the 3DP experimental framework, proposing an economic and rapid path for systematic haemocompatibility studies of parameters in RBPs.

title: Airway collapse in small breed dogs and its association with clinical and anatomic variables.
authorString: Kelly D, Labrador J, Peak K, Doyle E, Calleja S, Vecin M, Lomp T, Smith A, Rasmussen-Clark B, Pollard D.

journal.title: The Journal of small animal practice

abstractText:
Objectives

The objective of the study was to evaluate associations between clinical and anatomic variables in small breed dogs with lower airway collapse.

Materials and methods

One hundred and fifty dogs with chronic cough presenting between July 2017 and July 2023 were retrospectively included. Bronchoscopy recordings were reviewed to identify presence, location and severity of airway collapse. Anatomic variables were measured on computed tomography images. Cardiac variables were assessed with echocardiography or thoracic radiographs.

Results

Decreasing thoracic height:width ratio (Estimate: -51.75; 95% CI: -82.54 to -20.96), increasing body condition score (BCS) (Estimate: 6.45; 95% CI: 3.35 to 9.55) and presence of left atrial enlargement (Estimate: 21.97; 95% CI: 7.02 to 36.92) were associated with increasing cumulative bronchial collapse scores. Decreasing thoracic height:width ratio (OR: 0.02; 95% CI: 0.0004 to 0.63), increasing age (OR: 1.02; 95% CI: 1.01 to 1.03) and increasing body condition score (OR: 1.41; 95% CI: 1.04 to 1.92) were associated with increasing bronchomalacia scores. Decreasing thoracic height:width ratio (OR: 0.001; 95% CI: 0.00000758 to 0.08), increasing body condition score (OR: 1.63; 95% CI: 1.18 to 2.29), presence of left atrial enlargement (OR: 4.89; 95% CI: 1.19 to 21.65) and presence of airway neutrophilic inflammation (OR: 3.98; 95% CI: 1.10 to 17.39) were associated with increasing left principal bronchus collapse scores. Decreasing thoracic height:width ratio (OR: 0.003; 95% CI: 0.0001 to 0.07), increasing body condition score (OR: 1.54; 95% CI: 1.20 to 1.99) and presence of left atrial enlargement (OR: 4.85; 95% CI: 1.38 to 18.99) were associated with increasing left caudal lobar bronchus collapse scores.

Clinical significance

Variations in thoracic conformation might be involved in the aetiopathogenesis of airway collapse and reduced thoracic height:width ratio is associated with increasing airway collapse scores. Increasing body condition score is a modifiable variable associated with increasing airway collapse scores. Left atrial enlargement is associated with increased bronchial collapse scores but might directly contribute only to pre-existing collapse of the left caudal lobar bronchus.

title: Persistent Hyperphosphataemia as a Surrogate Marker of Permanent Hypoparathyroidism After Total Thyroidectomy in a Resource-Limited Setting.
authorString: Karunakaran P, Rajamanickam R, Parameswaran R.
abstractText:
Background

Permanent hypoparathyroidism remains a significant complication after total thyroidectomy (TT), particularly with rising thyroid cancer incidence and increasing surgical extent. Long-term consequences include hypocalcaemic symptoms, renal impairment, cardiovascular morbidity, neurocognitive dysfunction, reduced quality of life, and increased healthcare utilization. Although intact parathyroid hormone (iPTH) is the standard biomarker for diagnosis and surveillance, its availability and affordability remain limited in many low-resource settings. This prospective study evaluated the utility of serum phosphate as a surrogate marker for permanent hypoparathyroidism after TT.

Methods

This cohort study compared patients with and without permanent hypoparathyroidism, defined as iPTH < 10 pg/mL persisting beyond 6 months post-TT. Demographic, clinico-pathological, and biochemical variables, including serum calcium, phosphate, iPTH, and 25-hydroxyvitamin D (25OHD), were analyzed at baseline, postoperative day 2 (POD2), and 6 months.

Results

Among 328 patients (mean age 38.7 years; 77.1% women), transient postoperative hypoparathyroidism occurred in 195 (59.5%) and permanent hypoparathyroidism in 18 (5.5%). Multivariable analysis identified POD2 iPTH (odds ratio 10.7, 95% confidence intervals 1.3-88.1); parathyroid autotransplantation (OR 8.4[1.6-43.5]); six-month phosphate (OR 3.9[1.2-13.5]); six-month 25OHD level (OR 3.2[1.03-10.1]) and POD2 calcium (OR 1.7[1.0-3.0]) as independent predictors, each p < 0.05. In receiver operating characteristic analysis, both POD2 iPTH < 6 pg/mL (AUC = 0.781) and 6-month phosphate > 4.9 mg/dL (AUC = 0.743) demonstrated good discriminatory performance (p < 0.001) and were comparable by DeLong's test (p = 0.671).

Conclusion

Postoperative iPTH below 6 pg/mL is the principal marker for early risk stratification of permanent hypoparathyroidism following TT, whereas persistent hyperphosphataemia may serve as a surrogate biochemical marker during long-term surveillance.

title: VectBox Sync: a web application for vectorcardiographic analysis of ventricular synchrony from 12-lead electrocardiograms
authorString: Goldman R, Spagnuolo DN, Chara O, Fernandez JM.
abstractText: We introduce VectBox Sync, a browser-based application that implements a published vectorcardiographic (VCG) dyssynchrony index for exploratory assessment of ventricular electrical synchrony from the 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG). Despite guideline-directed patient selection, a substantial fraction of patients who receive cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) do not obtain the expected benefit. QRS duration and morphology remain the principal electrical criteria, yet they do not capture the three-dimensional trajectory of ventricular activation. VectBox Sync prioritizes native digital ECG recordings, including matrices and common clinical and research waveform formats; optional manufacturer-PDF import and externally digitized numerical files extend access when paper-like archives are the only available source. After optional preprocessing, the user selects a QRS interval, and the application calculates the dyssynchrony index relative to a calibrated control cutoff. It also provides companion VCG descriptors (voltage and speed integrals, loop angles, and planarity), together with VCG trajectories, synchrony-field maps, and a multilingual PDF report. Labeled conditions from the same session can be overlaid for comparison, for example across successive pacing settings. VectBox Sync makes this VCG-based assessment accessible through an integrated web application, providing quantitative descriptors that complement conventional ECG criteria. The application is available at https://vectbox.com/sync for research and educational use.

title: One-Pot CVD Growth of WS<sub>2</sub>/MoS<sub>2</sub> Vertical Heterobilayers With Twist-Angle-Dependent Optoelectronic Characteristics.
authorString: Fei S, Chen F, Chen X, Feng Q, Shu H, Lu H, Su W.
abstractText: Transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) heterobilayers (HBLs) with twist-angle (θ<sub>t</sub>) near 0° or 60° exhibit great promise for the rational design of novel valleytronic devices. However, the scalable growth of high-quality TMD vertically stacked HBLs (vHBLs) with controllable θ<sub>t</sub> near 0° or 60° remains a significant challenge for conventional chemical vapor deposition (CVD) techniques. Herein, we report a one-pot atmospheric-pressure CVD (APCVD) strategy that enables the controlled growth of high-quality vHBLs of WS<sub>2</sub>/MoS<sub>2</sub>. In contrast to the conventional CVD-grown MoS<sub>2</sub> homobilayers flakes typically exhibiting large θ<sub>t</sub>, the vHBL flakes synthesized in this work display predominantly θ<sub>t</sub> distribution statistically near 0° or 60° and can be tuned by varying the growth temperature. Furthermore, we observe pronounced θ<sub>t</sub>-dependent modulations in optoelectronic properties including contact potential difference (CPD), interlayer coupling strength, photoluminescence (PL) energies, and degree of valley polarization (DVP). This work introduces a significantly simplified one-step synthetic approach and paves the way toward scalable production of twist-engineered heterostructures, which thereby benefits the rational design of large-area valleytronic devices and deepens the fundamental understanding of their structure-property relationships.

title: Choroid plexus remodeling in aging and cerebrovascular disease revealed by contrast-enhanced 7T MRI.
authorString: Huang P, Zhen Z, Lin M, Zhou S, Chen K, Hsu Y, Sun Z, Liu C, Chen W, Zhang R.
abstractText:
Background

The choroid plexus is essential for brain homeostasis, yet its in vivo morphology remains incompletely characterized. Conventional MRI visualizes only part of the choroid plexus and may therefore misrepresent age- and disease-related structural changes. We aim to develop a 7T contrast-enhanced black-blood imaging (CeBBI) framework for whole-brain visualization and quantitative morphologic characterization of the choroid plexus, and to examine its associations with aging and cerebrovascular disease.

Methods

We retrospectively included 234 participants referred for evaluation of intracranial atherosclerotic disease who underwent CeBBI. A deep learning model was trained to segment the whole choroid plexus. Choroid plexus volume, centerline-based shape features and cystic components were quantified. Segmentations derived from CeBBI were compared with those obtained using a validated T1-weighted MRI-based method. Associations with age, ventricular size and vascular imaging markers were assessed.

Results

7T CeBBI enabled visualization of the choroid plexus across all ventricular compartments. The segmentation model achieved high accuracy (Dice score=0.901±0.013), and recovered more than twice the choroid plexus volume detected by the T1-weighted method. Total choroid plexus volume was not associated with age. However, with advancing age, the lateral ventricular choroid plexus became shorter (left r=-0.250, right r=-0.303, both P<0.001) and showed greater cross-sectional area (left r=0.174, right r=0.176, both P=0.007). Choroid plexus cyst number (r=0.187, P=0.004) and cyst volume (r=0.159, P=0.015) also increased with age. Cerebral microbleeds were independently associated with greater lateral ventricular choroid plexus volume (standardized β=0.178, P=0.012).

Conclusions

Our method enables robust whole-brain visualization and quantitative morphologic assessment of the choroid plexus. Rather than undergoing simple age-related hypertrophy, the choroid plexus showed complex remodeling characterized by shortening, cross-sectional expansion and cystic change. The association between cerebral microbleeds and larger choroid plexus volume further supports a potential role of vascular dysfunction in choroid plexus remodeling.

title: Identifying Exploratory Physical Activity Thresholds Associated With Symptom Severity in Older Adults With Parkinson's Disease.
authorString: Kim Y, Ridgel A, Kim JH.
abstractText: This research identified exploratory physical activity (PA) thresholds associated with symptom severity in older adults with Parkinson's disease and assessed their association with cardiometabolic and cognitive health. Data were collected from 3,259 participants (age: 65.64 ± 10.37) in the Fox Insight database. PA was measured using Physical Activity Scale for the Elderly. Quadratic regression identified exploratory PA thresholds for managing motor, nonmotor, and depressive symptoms, with minimum thresholds based on literature-defined cut points and optimal thresholds based on symptom plateaus. Logistic regression assessed relationship between these thresholds and prevalence of hypertension, diabetes, and mild cognitive impairment. Analyses identified exploratory minimum and optimal Physical Activity Scale for the Elderly threshold of 150 and 245. Meeting minimum PA threshold was associated with lower odds of hypertension (21.1%), diabetes (40.6%), and mild cognitive impairment (57.9%; p < .01). These findings provide evidence-based exploratory PA thresholds to guide future research on PA patterns in older adults with Parkinson's disease.

title: Protocol for generating parasympathetic neurons from hiPSCs and their coculture with hiPSC-atrial cardiomyocytes.
authorString: Thomas AM, Chiong IN, Neves JF, Tinker A, Denk F, Fedele L.
abstractText: Peripheral parasympathetic ganglia lie adjacent to their target organs and are difficult to access for primary culture; their dysfunction contributes to diseases like atrial fibrillation. Here, we present a protocol to differentiate human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) into parasympathetic neurons and assess their function by electrophysiological recordings, nicotinic receptor activity, and expression of cholinergic and autonomic markers. We also describe how to establish a coculture system with hiPSC-atrial cardiomyocytes that allows neuromodulation of cardiomyocyte activity.

title: Sex-Specific Determinants of Noncommunicable Diseases Among Respondents From Wealthier Households in Bangladesh.
authorString: Roy S, Islam RB, Noor STA, Sarkar S, Hossain MI.
abstractText: Noncommunicable diseases (NCDs), including hypertension and diabetes, have emerged as a major global public health concern in low- and middle-income countries like Bangladesh. In light of this, the current study aims to identify the sociodemographic factors associated with NCDs among Bangladeshi men and women, with a particular focus on those from wealthier households, to gain a deeper understanding of NCD risk in a rapidly evolving health landscape. Data were used from the nationally representative Bangladesh Demographic and Health Survey (BDHS) 2022. A total of 2729 men and 3441 women from wealthier households were included in the analysis. NCD status was defined as the presence of hypertension, diabetes, or both, and the χ2 test of independence was used to assess associations between NCDs and background characteristics. Separate binary logistic regression models for both men and women were employed to estimate the effects of sociodemographic factors on NCDs. This study estimated a higher prevalence rate of NCDs among women (41.3%) compared to men (37.4%). Both adult men and women had a higher association with NCDs, with the effect more noticeable among the age groups 30-44, 45-59, and 60+ years. Secondary and higher levels of education were less likely associated with NCDs among women, whereas men with higher levels of education had an increased association with NCDs. Overweight (aOR = 1.80) and obese (aOR = 4.08) men had a higher likelihood of association with NCDs with respect to normal body mass index (BMI), and a similar trend was found among overweight (aOR = 1.73) and obese (aOR = 3.00) women. This study shed light on the sex-specific higher association with NCDs among rich Bangladeshi people. Increased age and higher BMI are associated with the development of NCDs among both men and women.

title: Smoking Status Modifies the Association Between Ultra-Processed Food Consumption and Serum Uric Acid Levels: Findings From the Tehran Lipid and Glucose Study.
authorString: Golmohammadi M, Hosseinpour-Niazi S, Tohidi M, Mirmiran P, Hadaegh F, Azizi F.
abstractText: Ultra-processed food consumption (UPF) has been linked to various chronic health issues; however, its effect on serum uric acid (SUA) levels is not well understood. This study aims to investigate the association between UPF consumption and SUA levels among the adult population and to assess whether this association is modified by demographic and lifestyle factors. The study involved 5643 participants from the Tehran Lipid and Glucose Study. The consumption of UPF was evaluated using the NOVA classification system through a validated semi-quantitative food frequency questionnaire. To analyze the relationship between UPF intake and SUA levels, linear regression analysis was conducted, adjusting for demographic and lifestyle variables, including age, sex, physical activity levels, education levels, occupation status, smoking status, marital status, estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), body mass index (BMI), hypertension (HTN), Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), total energy intake, dietary fiber, vegetables, fruit, dairy products, and red meat. The mean (SE) SUA level was 4.8 (0.02) mg/dL. The median (interquartile range) intake of UPF was 14.5% (9.1-20.4) of total energy intake. Total UPF consumption was not associated with SUA levels in either crude or adjusted models. When examining components of UPF, soft drinks (β = 0.20, p trend < 0.001) and pizza (β = 0.11, p for trend = 0.033) were positively associated with SUA levels, after adjustment for confounders. When stratified by smoking status, there was a positive association between UPF intake and SUA levels among current smokers (β = 0.41, p trend = 0.015). UPF was not significantly associated with SUA levels across strata of age, sex, BMI status, physical activity levels, T2DM, HTN, chronic kidney disease, and insulin resistance status. High intake of UPF, when accompanied by smoking, may be associated with high SUA levels. Prospective cohort studies are needed to further investigate these associations and their potential mechanisms.

title: Changing tonometers, changing intraocular pressure? Rethinking intraocular pressure interpretation in dogs.
authorString: Yogo T.

journal.title: The Journal of small animal practice

abstractText: Intraocular pressure measurement is fundamental to the diagnosis and management of canine glaucoma, yet the value reported by a tonometer is inherently dependent on the instrument used. Successive generations of veterinary tonometers have improved portability, usability, standardisation and agreement with manometric pressure; however, measurements obtained with different devices are not necessarily interchangeable. Recorded intraocular pressure is also influenced by corneal properties, measurement technique, patient state and the clinical environment. These sources of variability are particularly important during longitudinal monitoring, because replacement or recalibration of a tonometer may produce an apparent change in intraocular pressure that does not reflect biological change within the eye. For practitioners, a change in tonometer should therefore be regarded as a change in the measurement system rather than simply replacement of equipment. The tonometer model and generation should be documented, and when instruments are changed, paired measurements with the old and new devices should be obtained when feasible to help establish a new clinical baseline. Population-level inter-device differences should not be applied as simple correction factors to individual patients, and numerical thresholds for ocular hypertension or suspicion of glaucoma should not be assumed to have equivalent clinical meaning across tonometers. When an unexpected change in intraocular pressure is detected, clinicians should consider both biological change and changes in the measurement context. Glaucoma diagnosis and longitudinal monitoring should therefore integrate intraocular pressure with visual function and structural assessment of the retina and optic nerve. Preserving the clinical meaning of intraocular pressure, rather than numerical continuity alone, should guide the interpretation of serial measurements as tonometric technology evolves.

title: Pathology-targeted PET/CT imaging of early lupus nephritis via a <sup>68</sup>Ga-labeled single-stranded DNA probe.
authorString: Huang Z, Li W, Zhou M, Huang Z, Wei Y, Yin Z, Yang C, Ma Z, Shen M, Gong Q, Braunstein Z, Rao X, Jiang D, Zhong J.
abstractText: As a major cause of morbidity in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), the prognosis of lupus nephritis (LN) critically depends on early detection and timely intervention. However, current diagnostic approaches remain suboptimal: renal biopsy is invasive and unsuitable for longitudinal monitoring, while conventional urine tests lack sensitivity for early-stage disease. Here, we report a molecular imaging strategy designed to target the pathogenic DNA-anti-dsDNA antibody axis for non-invasive detection of LN. We engineered a gallium-68-labeled single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) probe ([<sup>68</sup>Ga]Ga-NOTA-ssDNA) and evaluated its diagnostic performance and biosafety in the spontaneous MRL/lpr lupus mouse model. The probe showed disease-associated and sustained renal accumulation in 16-week-old diseased MRL/lpr mice, with progressively increasing kidney-to-background contrast. More importantly, [<sup>68</sup>Ga]Ga-NOTA-ssDNA enabled detection of renal immune complex deposition as early as 10 weeks of age, preceding abnormalities in conventional renal function markers and positive findings in renal histology by approximately two weeks. Mechanistically, the ssDNA backbone demonstrated favorable biocompatibility, without exacerbating autoimmune phenotypes or inducing Toll-like receptor-mediated signaling pathways. In conclusion, this study establishes a robust proof-of-concept for pathology-targeted PET/CT imaging of immune complex deposition. By directly visualizing the disease-driving renal autoantibody deposition at the preclinical stage, prior to overt organ damage, this strategy shifts LN diagnosis to non-invasive, mechanism-based molecular visualization.

title: Optimizing recurrent pericarditis management through IL-1 inhibition and the evolving multidisciplinary pharmacist-led care to comprehensive patient management.
authorString: Al-Taie A, Atal D.
abstractText: Recurrent pericarditis is a relapsing inflammatory disorder driven by overlapping autoimmune and autoinflammatory mechanisms, with interleukin-1 (IL-1) playing a central role in disease pathogenesis. Although first-line treatment with nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and colchicine, with the use of corticosteroids when necessary, effectively controls disease in most patients, a subset remains refractory or corticosteroid-dependent, experiencing frequent relapses despite optimal conventional therapy. Biologic agents targeting IL-1 in clinical applications, including anakinra and rilonacept, have demonstrated rapid symptom relief, reduced recurrence rates, decreased corticosteroid exposure, and favorable safety profiles, particularly in patients with elevated inflammatory markers and clinical features consistent with an autoinflammatory phenotype. Pharmacists are well positioned to address these gaps through medication review, patient education, interaction screening for biologics, vaccination counseling, and reinforcement of exercise restriction. Therefore, integrating pharmacists into multidisciplinary pericarditis care pathways can improve clinical outcomes, reduce recurrence rates, and enhance overall quality of life. This review provides an extensive overview of the current evidence supporting the use of IL-1 inhibitors in the treatment of recurrent pericarditis and explores the expanding role of pharmacists within multidisciplinary care teams. It also emphasizes strategies to optimize pharmacotherapy, reduce reliance on corticosteroids, enhance medication adherence and safety, and ultimately decrease the risk of disease recurrence.

authorString: Maes L, Peluso JP, Demeestere J, Wouters A, Nerney D, Desfontaines P, De Pauw A, Collins R, McCabe DJH, Cronin S, Williams DJ, De Raedt S, Purroy F, Vanhooren G, Pope G, Vanacker P, Cassidy T, Walsh C, Bos D, Kelly P, Lemmens R.

title: Immunization and Cardiovascular Disease in Latin America. The CorVacc Study: Sub Analysis by Regions.
authorString: Wyss F, Piskorz D, Lopez-Santi R, Gutiérrez LY, Márquez-Gonzales H, Parada FE, Ullauri V, Echeverri AM, Gómez JE, Valdez O, Méndez M, Almonte C, Ponte-Negretti C, Rivera MAM, Rivera IR, Villar R, Rivera JA, de Paz DP, Barrientos AI, Jordan E, Piskorz G, Lopez-Santi P, CorVacc study investigators. Cardiovascular Prevention Council (SIAC-PREVENT) of the Inter-American Society of Cardiology (SIAC).
abstractText:
Introduction

In Latin America, the mortality rate from influenza and pneumococcal disease has increased in recent years. Several challenges limit the implementation of vaccination strategies. These factors contribute to lower-than-expected immunization rates in Latin America.

Objective

The objective of this sub-analysis of the Inter-American Registry of Influenza and Pneumococcal Vaccination (CorVacc) is to determine vaccination rates and analyze the factors that influence the North - Central America and Carribean Spanish Speaking (NCC); Andean region (AR) and South Cone (SCR).

Methods

A cross-sectional survey of the general population was conducted in 19 Latin American countries. Adults aged 18 and older completed a 34-question online survey. Data were grouped into seven categories: demographic, socioeconomic, and non-demographic. Multivariate logistic regression comparisons were performed between regions to assess the association between vaccination rates and their explanatory variables.

Results

Influenza, Pneumococcus and ≥3 doses of COVID-19 vaccination was received by 4,126 (45.18%) CAC, 3,576 (50, 13%) AR and 3,024 (62, 99%) SC; 5,904 (65, 09%) CAC, 5,162 (68, 9%) AR and 3,486 (72, 61%) SC; and 6,266 (68, 61%) CAC, 6,001 (80, 09%) AR and 2,892 (79, 99%), respectively. No association was detected between the regions and the likelihood of receiving the influenza vaccine: AR OR 0.94 (95% CI 0.84-1, 06; p = 0.33), CAC OR 0.81 (CI 0.80-1, 00; p = 0.053). On the contrary, a positive association was detected with Streptococcus pneumoniae vaccination: AR OR 1.12 (CI 1, 01-1, 24; p = 0.032), CAC OR 1.33 (CI 1, 20-1, 47; p < 0.001). A negative association was observed in CAC with COVID-19 ≥ 3 doses vaccination: OR 0.56 (CI 0, 65; p = 0.032; p < 0.001). Social, economic and confidence barriers were identified, but cardiovascular risk factors and comorbidities were not significantly associated with lower vaccination rates.

Conclusions

Social, economic, and cultural, but not cardiovascular risk factor or disease variables in Latin American region could explain the lower-than-expected rates of vaccination and the differences observed between regions in vaccination frequencies.

title: Hyperhomocysteinemia: A Rare Cause of Isolated Ischemic Abducens Nerve Palsy in Young Adults.
authorString: Kashyap DS, Pandey PK, Singh A, Kumar B.

journal.title: The British and Irish orthoptic journal

abstractText: Ischemic ocular motor nerve palsies typically manifest as an isolated unilateral event in patients over the age of 45 years who have known risk factors, such as hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and dyslipidemia. Blood dyscrasias, hypercoagulable states, sickle cell disease, and congenital cardiac disease are likely culprits in younger age groups. Hyperhomocysteinemia is an unusual presentation of ischemic cranial nerve palsy, but it has been linked to thromboembolic states due to its propensity to damage the vascular endothelium lining. We report six young patients (age 18-45 years) with isolated unilateral abducens nerve palsy, who presented with an acute onset of painless uncrossed diplopia. Elevated homocysteine level of >40 μmol/L (mean value of 51.78 µmol/L) was the only biochemical abnormality detected. There was an uneventful and almost complete recovery in all six cases, over a period of three months after supplementation with vitamins B6, B12, and folic acid. Therefore, serum homocysteine should be investigated in every young patient presenting with an isolated ischemic cranial nerve palsy.

title: Implementing Pulse Oximetry Screening for Critical Congenital Heart Disease in São Tomé and Príncipe: Lessons from a Pilot Programme.
authorString: Pereira SC, Cassandra M, Bandeira S, Carvalho D, Pires A, Mertens TE, Abecasis A.
abstractText: Pulse oximetry (POX) screening improves early detection of critical congenital heart disease (CCHD) but has rarely been implemented in newborn care in sub-Saharan Africa. We introduced POX screening at São Tomé and Príncipe's main maternity unit, integrating staff training and a simplified screening algorithm. Six CCHD diagnoses were documented at the maternity unit after positive screens, two in already symptomatic infants. Screening coverage is unknown and screen-negative infants were not systematically followed up, so sensitivity cannot be determined and missed cases cannot be excluded. Staff interviews identified workforce shortages, equipment limitations, difficulties interpreting the algorithm, caregiver reluctance to delay discharge, and inconsistent documentation. Training was reinforced, caregiver materials and wrap-type neonatal probes were introduced, and the maternity informatic system was adapted. POX screening was delivered within routine care, but reliable documentation and post-discharge follow-up are needed before coverage or accuracy can be assessed.

title: Piloting cannabis for sleep disturbance in palliative care over 5 weeks: The pillow study protocol.
authorString: Newton AM, Krok-Schoen JL, Stevens EE, Babalonis SL, Wagener TL, Hinton A, Benzo R, Brasky TM.
abstractText:
Background

Sleep disturbance affects 60% of cancer patients, 3-fold that of the general population, and is frequently driven by clinical characteristics, physical symptoms, and psychological distress. Sleep disturbance and other symptoms often exacerbate one another, leading to reduced health-related quality of life (HRQOL). Sleep is the most commonly reported reason for cannabis use among adults with cancer, yet clinical evidence supporting its use for symptom management remains limited.

Objectives

This report describes a protocol for a pilot randomized trial designed to evaluate the safety and feasibility of a cannabis-based intervention and to explore its preliminary efficacy for sleep disturbance and HRQOL.

Methods

This pilot parallel-arm randomized clinical trial will enroll 50 patients from the Ohio State University Comprehensive Cancer Center (OSUCCC; anticipated Fall 2026). Eligible participants will be new to the OSUCCC's Palliative Care clinic and report at least moderate sleep disturbance. Participants will be randomized by sex and race strata to receive either usual care or a nightly oral cannabis gummy containing 5 mg Δ-9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) and 5 mg cannabidiol (CBD), taken 1 hour before bedtime for 30 days. Adverse events will be monitored throughout the study. Sleep, HRQOL, and related symptoms will be assessed using self-reported questionnaires, ecological momentary assessments, and actigraphy.

Conclusions

Findings will provide critical safety, feasibility, and preliminary efficacy data to support a future large-scale, multisite trial targeting sleep disturbance and symptom palliation in cancer care.

title: Healthy Lifestyle Score and the Risk of Cardiovascular Disease, Cancer, and Mortality in an Asian Population: Prospective Cohort Study.
authorString: Park SH, Ho PJ, Liang X, van Dam R, Chong MF, Lim CGY, Sim X, Chia A.
abstractText:
Background

Healthy lifestyle behaviors are key modifiable factors for the prevention of chronic diseases and premature mortality. Composite lifestyle scores provide a practical framework for capturing the combined impact of multiple health behaviors, but prospective evidence from multiethnic Asian populations remains limited.

Objective
