This study examined the associations between a composite healthy lifestyle score and the risk of cardiovascular diseases, cancer, and all-cause mortality in a multiethnic Asian population.

Methods

We analyzed prospective data from 9920 participants of the Singapore Multi-Ethnic Cohort who were free of major chronic diseases at baseline. A healthy lifestyle score was constructed from 5 components: BMI, smoking, physical activity, diet quality, and screen time. Scores ranged from 0 to 10, with higher scores reflecting healthier lifestyles. An expanded score, including mental well-being, was examined in a subset. Hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% CIs were estimated using the Cox proportional hazards model for acute myocardial infarction (AMI), stroke, cancer, and all-cause mortality, adjusting for sociodemographic factors, energy intake, family history of cancer or heart disease, and menopause status.

Results

During a median follow-up of 14 years, 457 AMI cases, 322 stroke cases, 707 cancer incident cases, and 631 deaths were identified. More favorable lifestyle scores were associated with lower risk of cardiovascular outcomes and mortality, consistent with a dose-response relationship. Compared to participants scoring 8 to 10, those with the lowest score (0-3) had more than 2 times the risk of AMI (HR 2.13, 95% CI 1.47-3.07), stroke (HR 3.21, 95% CI 2.12-4.85), and all-cause mortality (HR 2.01, 95% CI 1.46-2.78). In contrast, no significant associations were observed for cancer incidence. Incorporating mental well-being into the lifestyle score yielded similar results.

Conclusions

Adherence to a healthy lifestyle was associated with a lower risk of AMI, stroke, and mortality in a multiethnic Asian cohort, highlighting the importance of integrated lifestyle approaches for chronic disease prevention.

title: AI Applications in Aortic and Peripheral Artery Disease: Risk Prediction, Imaging, Procedural Support, and Longitudinal Surveillance.
authorString: Robert JD, Bannikov S, Atkins AD, Rahimi M.
abstractText: Aortic disease and lower-extremity peripheral artery disease (PAD) generate substantial morbidity, mortality, and longitudinal imaging burden. Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly studied for vascular risk prediction, image analysis, procedural support, and surveillance, but the maturity of these applications is heterogeneous. This review evaluates recent AI applications in aortic disease and PAD, emphasizing the distinction between algorithmic performance, external validation, demonstrated workflow impact, and proven patient benefit. Automated image segmentation and opportunistic abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) detection have the most mature evidence base, including retrospective external validation and, for AI-assisted AAA case finding, nonrandomized evidence of improved downstream evaluation and follow-up. Conversely, while machine-learning models for vascular risk prediction and disease progression often report high retrospective accuracy, their clinical readiness remains strictly investigational. Across most aortic and PAD applications, there is a persistent lack of independent external validation, decision-curve analysis, and prospective testing against standard care. Image-fusion guidance has clinical evidence for reducing procedural resource use, but this evidence should not be conflated with autonomous AI or robotic navigation. Cardiovascular digital twins remain largely mechanistic, computational, or early-development frameworks. AI can augment vascular imaging and risk assessment, but high retrospective accuracy is not equivalent to clinical utility. Current guideline thresholds for repair, revascularization, and surveillance should not be altered on the basis of investigational radiomics or prediction models. Translation requires multicenter external validation, prospective workflow evaluation, calibration and net-benefit assessment, transparent reporting, and trials demonstrating improved patient outcomes.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Valvular Heart Disease: Imaging, Quantification, Risk Prediction, and Potential Clinical Decision Support.
authorString: Fakikh Y, Malahfji M.
abstractText: Valvular heart disease (VHD) affects a substantial proportion of the population and remains a major cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality worldwide. Despite advances in surgical and transcatheter therapies, important challenges persist. VHD remains underdiagnosed, assessment of disease severity is often variable, and the optimal timing of intervention continues to evolve. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising tool across the spectrum of VHD care. AI-based electrocardiogram analysis can identify both existing and future VHD, while AI-guided point-of-care ultrasound extends screening to nonspecialist settings. Across multimodality imaging, machine learning (ML) and deep learning algorithms enable automated, reproducible assessment of VHD. In echocardiography, AI supports grading of disease severity across the main valvular lesions, including Doppler interpretation and automated report generation. AI-enhanced cardiac magnetic resonance facilitates automated assessment of ventricular remodeling and myocardial fibrosis, while AI-assisted cardiac computed tomography improves procedural planning for transcatheter interventions. In parallel, ML has identified distinct patient phenotypes in multiple valvular lesions with differing clinical trajectories and responses to intervention. This review summarizes current applications of AI in detection, multimodality imaging, and potential clinical decision support for VHD and discusses opportunities and challenges for integration into routine practice.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Preventive Cardiology: Risk Prediction, Exposomics, and Personalized Interventions.
authorString: Magnino C, Coker M, Avenatti E.
abstractText: Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Prevention has shifted from a narrow focus on atherosclerosis to the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) framework, which requires integrating data across organ systems, specialties, and care settings. Artificial intelligence (AI) can work with the high-dimensional, weakly structured data this integration produces, and its use in prevention is now endorsed by major cardiovascular societies. This review covers two applications. The first encompasses risk prediction, spanning electrocardiogram-based models that reframe routine tracings as general biomarkers of cardiovascular health, AI-enhanced cardiac imaging that extracts biological signals invisible to standard reads, opportunistic analysis of scans acquired for unrelated indications, and emerging efforts to quantify environmental and neighborhood-level exposomic risk. The second is the management of modifiable risk factors across early CKM stages: lifestyle behavior, obesity phenotyping, hypertension monitoring, dyslipidemia detection, glycemic management, and chronic kidney disease risk stratification. In both domains, retrospective discriminative performance is frequently excellent, while prospective evidence that AI-guided intervention improves patient-relevant outcomes remains limited.

title: Association of GH and IGF-1 Levels with Increased Carotid Intima-Media Thickness and Cardiovascular Risk Scores in Acromegaly: A Cross-Sectional Study.
authorString: Kartal Baykan E, Akhanlı P, Usta Çiftel S, Pir A, Tulun ÖF, Yavuz İ, Akyüz Kotan E, Çalgın MZ, Baykan AR.
abstractText: This study aimed to evaluate carotid intima-media thickness (CIMT), lipid abnormalities, and cardiovascular risk scores in acromegaly patients and assess their association with disease activity and growth hormone (GH)/insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) levels. A retrospective cross-sectional study included 104 acromegaly patients (54 female, 50 male; mean age 47.1 ± 11.0 years) and 50 age-/sex-matched healthy controls. CIMT, fasting glucose, HbA1c, lipid profile, GH, and IGF-1 were measured. Ten-year cardiovascular risk was calculated using the Systematic Coronary Risk Evaluation (SCORE) algorithm. Multiple linear regression analysis was performed to identify independent correlates of CIMT; SCORE was used only for between-group comparisons and correlation analyses, not as a dependent variable in any regression model. Acromegaly patients had significantly higher glucose, HbA1c, total cholesterol, LDL, and triglycerides (p < 0.001), and lower HDL (43.2 vs 48.6 mg/dL, p < 0.001). CIMT and SCORE were significantly elevated (0.79 vs 0.57 mm, p < 0.001; 6.50 vs 1.80, p < 0.001). CIMT correlated with GH (R = 0.798) and IGF-1 (R = 0.618, both p < 0.001). Active disease (GH ≥ 1 ng/mL, n = 82) showed higher CIMT (0.83 vs 0.60 mm, p < 0.01) and SCORE (7.02 vs 2.62, p < 0.01) than remission (n = 22). Multiple regression identified GH (β = 0.402), IGF-1 (β = 0.323), and age (β = 0.293) as independent correlates of CIMT; the final model explained 68.4% of the variance in CIMT (R2 = 0.684, p < 0.001), although this value reflects the entire multivariable model rather than GH and IGF-1 alone. Traditional risk factors (BMI, glucose, lipids) showed no significant independent association (p > 0.05). Acromegaly, especially active disease, is associated with increased CIMT and cardiovascular risk. GH and IGF-1 independently correlate with subclinical atherosclerosis beyond traditional risk factors. Further longitudinal studies are needed to determine whether achieving biochemical remission translates into reduced cardiovascular risk.

title: Nanotherapeutic Strategies Targeting Senescent Microenvironment for Aging-Related Chronic Diseases.
authorString: Ma J, Li X, He Z, Sun X, Lv G.
abstractText: DCellular senescence is a central driver of age-related chronic diseases, including neurodegeneration, atherosclerosis, metabolic disorders, and fibrosis. The persistent accumulation of senescent cells and their associated secretory phenotype (SASP) creates a shared microenvironmental basis for disease progression across multiple organ systems. Senolytic and senomorphic strategies targeting senescent cells have shown therapeutic promise, yet their clinical translation remains constrained by insufficient targeting specificity, off-target toxicity, and poor tissue penetration. Nanotechnology-enabled delivery systems offer a programmable approach to overcome these barriers through rationally designed carriers that enable selective recognition of senescent cells, microenvironment-responsive drug release, and enhanced tissue accessibility. This review develops an integrated framework that links nanoplatform design principles to mechanistic intervention categories and disease-specific evidence. We first outline the molecular basis of cellular senescence and its pathological roles in age-related diseases. We then systematically examine four mechanistic dimensions of nanotherapeutic intervention in the senescent microenvironment: redox homeostasis modulation, inflammatory reprogramming, senescent cell clearance, and immune surveillance reactivation. These dimensions target reactive oxygen species, pro-inflammatory cytokines, senescent cells, and immune effector cells, respectively. Representative nanoplatforms applied to neurodegenerative, cardiovascular, metabolic, musculoskeletal, and fibrotic diseases are discussed. We further analyze key translational challenges, including senescent cell heterogeneity, impaired drug delivery in aged tissues, and regulatory uncertainty. Finally, we discuss emerging directions in precision rejuvenation, offering a conceptual framework for the next generation of senescence-targeted nanotherapies.

title: Paradoxical Pleuroperitoneal Reaction Following Corticosteroid Withdrawal During Treatment of Tuberculous Meningitis: A Case Report.
authorString: Rasikh AS, Yousufzai MS.
abstractText: Paradoxical reactions during tuberculosis treatment may manifest as new lesions or worsening of pre-existing disease despite an otherwise favorable response to therapy. Pleuroperitoneal manifestations during treatment of tuberculous meningitis (TBM) are unusual and may mimic treatment failure or malignancy. An 18-year-old woman presented with fever, progressive headache, nausea, vomiting, and altered consciousness and was diagnosed with TBM based on cerebrospinal fluid findings and positive Xpert MTB/RIF. An initial abdominal CT performed before anti-tuberculosis treatment revealed mesenteric and retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy, suggesting possible pre-existing abdominal tuberculosis. She received first-line anti-tuberculosis therapy and adjunctive dexamethasone for TBM, resulting in marked neurological recovery. Approximately two weeks after completing an 8-week dexamethasone taper, she presented with fever, dyspnea, dry cough, and abdominal distension. Imaging demonstrated bilateral pleural effusions, ascites, peritoneal thickening, omental nodularity, and necrotic mesenteric and para-aortic lymphadenopathy, with findings favoring tuberculous pleuroperitoneal involvement. Pleural fluid was lymphocyte-predominant, with an adenosine deaminase level of 38.5 U/L. Given her marked neurological recovery, the temporal relationship with dexamethasone withdrawal, and findings favoring tuberculosis, a paradoxical pleuroperitoneal reaction was considered. Anti-tuberculosis therapy was continued, and prednisolone 30 mg/day was initiated. Her symptoms improved markedly, with complete resolution of the pleural effusions and substantial reduction of ascites. This case highlights the importance of recognizing extra-neurological paradoxical reactions when pleuroperitoneal manifestations develop during otherwise successful treatment of TBM, particularly following corticosteroid withdrawal.

title: Multifocal Gastrointestinal Melanoma Metastases More Than Two Decades After Primary Diagnosis: Complete Resection and Long-Term Follow-Up.
authorString: Nyman P, Gustavsson M, Söderman O, Bagge RO, Nyqvist-Streng J.
abstractText: Melanoma may present with gastrointestinal metastases decades after primary diagnosis. A man treated for cutaneous melanoma in 1992 had local recurrence in 1993 and an in-transit metastasis in 2013. Intestinal metastases were resected in 2017. No further recurrence was documented through June 2026. Gastrointestinal symptoms or unexplained anemia warrant investigation.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Congenital Heart Disease: A Roadmap.
authorString: Dhar R, Dave D, Heiss J, Kormos K, Tandon A.
abstractText: Congenital heart disease (CHD) is a lifelong condition that requires ongoing monitoring due to its heterogeneous anatomy, physiology, and clinical course. Despite major advances in diagnosis and treatment, challenges remain in early detection, risk stratification, and long-term management. Artificial intelligence (AI) has the potential to enhance CHD care by extracting actionable insights from complex clinical data. This review examines current and emerging applications of AI in three key domains: cardiovascular imaging, wearable technologies, and clinical registries. We highlight opportunities to improve diagnosis, monitoring, and outcome prediction, while discussing important challenges related to data quality, validation, interpretability, and clinical implementation. Together, these areas illustrate both the promise and the barriers to integrating AI into CHD care.

title: Ropivacaine in oblique subcostal transversus abdominis plane block for laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy: a randomized, double-blind clinical trial.
authorString: Pinto LEV, Lima RC, Nogueira Neto J, Dibai Filho AV, Oliveira CMB, Moura ECR, Scheibe CL, Valadão JA, Sakata RK, Leal PDC.
abstractText:
Purpose

To evaluate the analgesic efficacy, opioid consumption, and inflammatory response of oblique subcostal transversus abdominis plane (OSTAP) block with 0.2% ropivacaine versus control in patients undergoing laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy (LSG).

Methods

This is a prospective, randomized, double-blind, clinical trial. After standardized anesthetic induction, patients received a bilateral OSTAP block with 0.2% ropivacaine or 0.9% saline. Pain, rescue morphine, postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV), Quality of Recovery-15 (QoR-15), enhanced recovery after bariatric surgery (ERABS) discharge criteria, and inflammatory markers were assessed.

Results

Rest pain was similar between groups at all time points. During movement, a lower score was observed at 24 h in the ropivacaine group (RG), median 1 (0-6) versus 2 (0-6), but the difference was not statistically significant after adjustment (p = 0.024; Benjamini-Hochberg [BH] adjusted p = 0.096). Total morphine consumption was similar, 10 (2-50) versus 11 mg (1-30), p = 0.926, as were PONV, QoR-15 118 points, p = 0.717, diet resumption 98, ambulation 76, and ERABS discharge criteria. Interleukin-8 at T3 was numerically lower in the RG, 7.2 (0.6-27.1) versus 9.8 (1.3-18.6) pg/mL, without statistical significance after adjustment (p = 0.073; BH adjusted p = 0.142).

Conclusion

OSTAP block with 0.2% ropivacaine was not associated with consistent differences in analgesic, recovery, or inflammatory outcomes.

title: Predicting Persistent Left Ventricular Dysfunction After Cardiac Resynchronization Therapy Upgrade in Pacing-Induced Cardiomyopathy.
authorString: Simka J, Praus R, Jager J, Matatko M, Fialova M, Cermakova E, Stritecky J, Haman L, Parizek P.
abstractText: Background/Objectives: Pacing-induced cardiomyopathy (PICM) is potentially reversible after cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) upgrade, but severe left ventricular dysfunction persists in some patients. We evaluated predictors of persistent left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) ≤ 35% after CRT upgrade and long-term outcomes. Methods: We analysed 60 patients undergoing CRT upgrade for PICM. The primary outcome was persistent LVEF ≤ 35% at 12 months. Clinical, electrocardiographic, echocardiographic, and long-term outcomes were assessed. Results: At 12 months, median LVEF increased from 30% to 45% (p < 0.01), and 82% of patients recovered to an LVEF > 35%. Persistent severe left ventricular dysfunction was associated with lower baseline LVEF (22% vs. 30%; p < 0.01), greater left ventricular end-diastolic diameter (LVEDD) (65 mm vs. 58 mm; p = 0.03), and longer post-CRT QRS duration (154 ms vs. 140 ms; p = 0.02); none remained independently significant after multivariable adjustment. No patient with baseline LVEF > 25% and LVEDD < 65 mm had persistent severe LV dysfunction, compared with 46% of those with LVEF ≤ 25% and LVEDD ≥ 65 mm. In the 12-month landmark analysis, mortality through 60 months after CRT upgrade was 55% in patients with persistent severe LV dysfunction and 31% in those with LVEF recovery. Conclusions: CRT upgrade was associated with substantial recovery of LV systolic function in patients with PICM. Severe baseline LV dysfunction and LV dilatation were associated with a lower likelihood of recovery to an LVEF > 35%. These exploratory findings may aid risk stratification but require prospective validation.

title: Macrophage lipid metabolism: a hidden driver of aging and chronic diseases.
authorString: Li R, Tang X, Li Y, He W, Zhu Y, Li M, Liu B, Zou Z, Zhang Y, Luo J, Cao M, Wang J, Huang Y, Fu Y, He M.
abstractText: Chronic metabolic diseases, such as type 2 diabetes, non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) and atherosclerosis, constitute a major burden on global health. The pathogenesis of these diseases is closely related to immune-metabolic disorders. Immunometabolism refers to the changes in intracellular metabolic pathways within immune cells that alter their functions. The lipid metabolism of macrophages is an important aspect of immunometabolism. Macrophages play a crucial role in tissue homeostasis and inflammatory responses through their plasticity. Aging macrophages show distinct lipid metabolic characteristics in comparison with young cells, which may be associated with the progression of chronic metabolic diseases. This article aims to explore how normal and aging macrophages affect the occurrence and development of chronic metabolic diseases.

title: Ultraprocessed Food Consumption and Incident Heart Failure: The Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis.
authorString: Haidar A, Marupudi A, Rikhi R, Watson KE, Wood AC, Shapiro MD.
abstractText: Ultraprocessed foods (UPFs) are associated with adverse cardiometabolic outcomes and increased atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk. However, the relationship between UPF intake and incident heart failure (HF) remains incompletely understood. The aims of this study were to examine the relationship between UPF consumption and incident HF and to evaluate potential biological mediators. A sample of 6,531 U.S. adults 45-84 years of age without cardiovascular disease at baseline from MESA (Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis) was analyzed. UPF intake was classified according to the Nova system. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models evaluated associations between UPF intake and incident HF. Phenotypes were classified as heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) (ejection fraction <50%) and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) (ejection fraction ≥50%). Mediation analyses were conducted to evaluate the potential mediating role of waist-to-height ratio as a surrogate measure for central adiposity. Higher UPF intake was significantly associated with increased risk of incident HF across sequentially adjusted models. In the primary model (model 2), each additional daily serving of UPF was associated with a 5% higher risk of incident HF (HR: 1.052; 95% CI: 1.002-1.103). When stratified by phenotype, UPF intake remained significantly associated with HFpEF (HR: 1.096; 95% CI: 1.016-1.183) but not HFrEF. Participants in the upper 80% of UPF intake had a >2-fold higher risk for HFpEF than those in the lowest 20% (HR: 2.234; 95% CI: 1.289-3.874). In mediation analyses, waist-to-height ratio statistically accounted for ∼51% of the association between UPF intake and total HF and 49% of the association between UPF intake and HFpEF. Higher UPF consumption was significantly associated with an increased risk for incident HF, with associations driven primarily by the HFpEF phenotype. Central adiposity, measured by waist-to-height ratio, demonstrated a potential mediating role, suggesting that obesity-related cardiometabolic pathways may represent an important pathway linking UPF consumption to HF risk.

title: The Effect of S616L, a CPVT1-Associated Mutation, on the Stability and Structure of Human Cardiac RyR2.
authorString: Bauer JA, Benko M, Šutová Ľ, Beck K, Nowak J, Bellová J, Baráth P, Bauerová-Hlinková V.
abstractText: Catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia type 1 (CPVT1) is a heritable genetic disease caused by mutations to hRyR2, the cardiac isoform of the human ryanodine receptor. One such mutation, S616L, is found in the α-helical part (NSol) of the hRyR2 N-terminal domain (NTD) close to a three-way junction between the NTD, junctional solenoid (JSol), and bridging solenoid (BSol) domains. In this study, we use molecular dynamics simulation to study the effect of S616L on the residues of this junction. We find that the mutation slightly weakens the interface between the N-terminal domain and the bridging solenoid by changing the preferred conformation of the residues at the interface, thereby promoting a slight opening between these domains. In addition, we determined the impact of this mutation on the biophysical and biochemical properties of a 655-residue fragment containing the entire hRyR2 N-terminal domain, finding that it slightly increases the thermal stability of the fragment.

title: Carotid Plaque, Aortic Stiffness, and Left Ventricular Longitudinal Function in Adults with Preserved Ejection Fraction.
authorString: Stoichescu-Hogea G, Pah AM, Movila D, Savencu C, Ples C, Duda D, Dragan SR.
abstractText: Background/Objectives: Carotid plaque and aortic pulse wave velocity (PWV) capture distinct aspects of vascular disease. We examined their associations with left ventricular global longitudinal strain (GLS) in adults with ejection fraction ≥50%. Methods: This single-center retrospective cross-sectional secondary analysis used the 2018-2019 institutional cohort, comprising preserved-EF ischemic heart disease, hypertension, and reference control groups. The primary outcome was signed GLS, for which a higher (less negative) value indicates worse shortening. Multivariable linear regression simultaneously included plaque and PWV, adjusting for age, sex, systolic blood pressure, diabetes, and source group; HC3 robust confidence intervals were used. Results: Of 128 records, 127 had evaluable PWV and GLS. Mean age was 60.8 years; 51/127 (40.2%) were women, and 37/127 (29.1%) had recorded plaque. PWV correlated with GLS (Pearson r = 0.426; p < 0.001). Adjusted GLS was 0.618 percentage points less negative per 1 m/s higher PWV (95% CI 0.280-0.956; p < 0.001). Plaque presence had no clearly detectable independent association (β = -0.348, 95% CI -1.358 to 0.661; p = 0.499). Conclusions: Higher aortic PWV was associated with less favorable longitudinal function despite preserved ejection fraction. The plaque estimate was imprecise. Cross-sectional data cannot establish temporal order or causality, and the historical ICpFE label does not independently validate an HFpEF diagnosis.

title: Accurate Differentiation of Acute Aortic Syndrome from Acute Coronary Syndrome: A Machine Learning Diagnostic Model Based on Routine Admission Variables.
authorString: Peng X, Wang B, Tang T, Wang S, Ma X, Nienaber CA.
abstractText: Background/Objectives: Acute aortic syndrome (AAS) is an underdiagnosed, time-critical medical emergency. Initial misdiagnosis as acute coronary syndrome (ACS) is common, delaying definitive treatment and exposing patients to inappropriate antithrombotic therapy. We aimed to develop and temporally test a machine learning (ML) model using routine admission variables to distinguish AAS from ACS. Methods: In this single-center retrospective study, we included 2828 consecutive adults with confirmed AAS or ACS (September 2018-April 2025); the initial 1979 patients formed the development cohort and the subsequent 849, a temporally separated test cohort. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression selected predictors from nine prespecified candidates. Seven algorithms were fitted and assigned fixed Youden-derived cutoffs in the development cohort, then applied to the test cohort. Results: Six predictors were selected: D-dimer, leukocyte count, troponin I, C-reactive protein, oxygen saturation, and ST-segment changes. In the test cohort (112 AAS [13.2%]; 737 ACS), area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) ranged from 0.925 to 0.956 across the seven models. Extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) showed the highest observed AUC (0.956; 95% confidence interval (CI), 0.935-0.976) and the lowest Brier score (0.047; 95% CI, 0.037-0.057), with sensitivity 0.884, specificity 0.931, and negative predictive value 0.981 at the development-cohort-derived cutoff (0.199); decision curve analysis indicated net benefit within the AAS/ACS test cohort. Shapley additive explanations ranked D-dimer as the dominant contributor. Conclusions: Six routine admission variables discriminated AAS from ACS across all seven ML algorithms in this single-center cohort. These findings support further prospective evaluation in a broader diagnostic population.

title: Bleeding Following Frozen Elephant Trunk Surgery: A Proposed Reporting Dataset and Research Agenda.
authorString: Staicu RE, Manzur AR, Boca MI, Cozlac AR, Pop-Crisan A, Deutsch P, Lascu A.
abstractText: Perioperative bleeding after frozen elephant trunk (FET) surgery is reported using heterogeneous endpoints. This structured narrative review examines bleeding sources, measurement and haemostatic management, prioritising recent literature while retaining established landmark definitions. Twelve primary FET clinical publications are tabulated, with technical reports and wider cardiac-surgery evidence providing context. Re-exploration, postoperative drainage, estimated blood loss, transfusion and fabric oozing describe related but distinct phenomena. Established classifications, particularly the Universal Definition of Perioperative Bleeding (UDPB), provide a severity-reporting reference and should not be displaced by a new FET scale. We propose six parallel reporting domains: procedural context; bleeding measurement; haemostatic status; verified source; treatment exposure; and outcomes.. The study-level mapping shows that published FET reports often permit extraction of drainage, re-exploration or treatment exposure, whereas haemostatic status and a directly verified bleeding source are rarely recoverable from published reports. The dataset therefore makes these information gaps explicit and supports prospective evaluation; it does not infer an anatomical source from laboratory findings, drainage or treatment. The proposed reporting dataset is not a validated severity scale or treatment algorithm.

title: Sentinel Lymph Node Mapping in Endometrial Cancer in the Molecular Era: Current Evidence, Clinical Controversies, and Unresolved Questions.
authorString: Tinelli R, Sorrentino F, Surico D, Messina A, Angioni S, Bogani G, Aquino CI, Peiretti M, Libretti A.
abstractText: Sentinel lymph node (SLN) mapping is an established approach to nodal staging in presumed uterine-confined endometrial cancer, but its integration with molecular risk assessment raises unresolved clinical questions. This narrative review examines tracer and injection-site selection, persistent mapping failure, high-risk histologies, para-aortic assessment, low-volume nodal disease, and interpretation across POLEmut, MMRd, NSMP and p53abn tumors. A focused literature update and bibliographic verification were performed in October 2026. Cervical indocyanine green injection with near-infrared imaging supports reproducible pelvic mapping; comparative tracer studies favor it over blue dye. Prospective high-risk cohorts demonstrate high diagnostic accuracy when a complete algorithm is applied, but do not establish survival non-inferiority within every histologic or molecular subgroup. An unmapped hemipelvis requires technical reassessment and management according to baseline staging indication and operative feasibility. Negative pelvic SLNs do not exclude all para-aortic disease; additional assessment should address a defined treatment-planning question. Micrometastases constitute nodal metastasis, whereas isolated tumor cells are reported as pN0(i+). Molecularly annotated cohorts refine prognostic interpretation, but do not validate subgroup-specific treatment rules for low-volume disease. Future trials should evaluate treatment changes, morbidity and oncologic outcomes, rather than detection alone. The review distinguishes current staging practice from prognostic observations and hypotheses requiring prospective validation.

title: Serial Red Cell Distribution Width and Mortality After TAVR: An Observational Cohort Study.
authorString: Zhu Z, Feng T, Zhao Z, Wei J, Peng Y, Chen Y, Feng Y, Chen M.
abstractText: Background/Objectives: Preprocedural red cell distribution width (RDW) is associated with mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), but the prognostic relevance of serial measurements and native leaflet morphology remains uncertain. Methods: This single-center retrospective cohort included 1369 patients who underwent native-valve TAVR from January 2019 to October 2023. The primary analysis evaluated baseline RDW-coefficient of variation (RDW-CV) and mortality in the overall cohort. Exploratory landmark analyses examined postprocedural RDW-CV changes among survivors with repeat measurements. Valve-disease phenotype and leaflet morphology were evaluated as potential effect modifiers. Results: During a median reverse Kaplan-Meier follow-up of 58.7 months, 196 patients died. Higher baseline RDW-CV was associated with mortality over all follow-up (adjusted HR per 1-SD increase, 1.17; 95% CI, 1.02-1.34; p = 0.022). After adjustment for baseline RDW-CV and clinical covariates, greater increases at 3 months (HR per window-specific 1-SD increase, 1.53; 95% CI, 1.20-1.94; p < 0.001) and 6 months (HR, 1.37; 95% CI, 1.08-1.73; p = 0.009) were associated with subsequent mortality. Exploratory analysis suggested a stronger 6-month association in bicuspid than tricuspid valves (HR, 2.47 [95% CI, 1.65-3.69] vs. 1.02 [0.75-1.40]; interaction p = 0.002). Adding 6-month RDW-CV change increased the cross-validated 2-year AUC from 0.628 to 0.651. Conclusions: Baseline RDW-CV was associated with mortality after TAVR. Among patients with repeat testing, increases at 3 and 6 months were associated with subsequent mortality, with an exploratory stronger association in bicuspid aortic valve. Standardized prospective sampling is required to confirm these longitudinal findings.

title: Rapid Infrarenal Aortic Rupture During Persistent Methicillin-Susceptible <i>Staphylococcus aureus</i> Bacteraemia: Serial CT Evolution and Staged Endovascular Treatment-A Case Report.
authorString: Kukliński F, Chlabicz M, Woźniak A, Rydzewski Ł, Fernandez Moreno T, Tycińska A, Głowiński J.
abstractText: Background and Clinical Significance: Persistent Staphylococcus aureus bacteraemia can seed an atherosclerotic aorta. Early CT may show only wall thickening and periaortic inflammation, mimicking a degenerative penetrating aortic ulcer (PAU) when no ulcer crater is visible. Case Presentation: An 80-year-old woman (BMI 19.5 kg/m2) presented with hypogastric and lumbar pain. Multiphasic CT showed a calcified infrarenal aorta with periaortic inflammation but no haemorrhage. Blood cultures obtained on two occasions confirmed persistent methicillin-susceptible S. aureus bacteraemia. Interval CT angiography showed an enhancing circumferential cuff and a small anterior contrast focus without a definite ulcer crater. Eight days after the initial CT, hypotension developed; CT angiography showed focal aortic wall disruption, active extravasation, and a large retroperitoneal haematoma. Emergency aorto-bi-iliac EVAR controlled the bleeding. An inferior mesenteric artery-fed type II endoleak filled the fresh rupture cavity and was treated by coil embolisation via mesenteric collaterals. One-month CTA showed a patent graft without endoleak. At six weeks, the patient remained clinically well with healed wounds and no need for further vascular intervention. CRP fell from 148.1 mg/L on postoperative day 5 to 49.4 mg/L at six weeks and 24.2 mg/L at approximately 12 weeks; the next outpatient review was scheduled in three months, although microbiological clearance remained undocumented. Conclusions: Serial imaging and persistent MSSA bacteraemia support probable infective aortitis with focal wall disruption; an infected degenerative PAU remains possible. Persistent bacteraemia, focal pain, and a progressive periaortic cuff should prompt early vascular review and short-interval imaging.

title: Curious Case of <i>Curvularia</i>: Aortic Graft Infection Caused by <i>Curvularia</i> Species.
authorString: Batch ST, Johnson NA, Brigmon MM.
abstractText: We present a unique case of a patient with an aortic graft infected by Curvularia species that presented with bilateral vision loss. He was found to have a mass along a previously placed aortic graft, which was revealed to be Curvularia spp. by Karius testing.

title: Combined antegrade-retrograde technique in urgent carotid stenting for true lumen compression after total arch replacement.
authorString: Ng YY, Zhuang TFJ, Ling TH, Chu YLE.
abstractText: Type A aortic dissection extending into the carotid arteries with true lumen compression poses a significant risk of cerebral hypoperfusion and neurological sequelae. This case report describes an elderly patient who developed an extension of the right common carotid artery dissection with associated true lumen compression immediately following total arch replacement for acute Type A aortic dissection. Urgent carotid stenting was performed using a combined antegrade-retrograde approach (trans carotid and trans radial approach) to restore blood flow. Postprocedural imaging confirmed patency without major complications. This technique highlights a viable salvage strategy for managing complex aortic dissections when traditional methods fail. A literature review discusses the combined antegrade-retrograde approach used in urgent carotid stenting, as well as the advantages of ultrasound in selecting the true lumen and its minimally invasive nature.

title: Dual Targeting of Alcohol Use Disorder and Alcohol-Associated Liver Disease: Emerging Molecular Targets Along the Gut-Liver-Brain Axis.
authorString: Ryu T, Chung BS, Yang K.
abstractText: Alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) is the hepatic end of alcohol use disorder (AUD), yet only abstinence and transplantation modify it, and recent liver-only programmes in alcohol-associated hepatitis have not delivered. This review asks whether the receptors, ligands and transporters setting drinking behaviour and alcohol-related liver injury are largely one set along the gut-liver-brain axis, so one molecule could lower both. Where resolved, it is cell-specific: hepatic glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor sits, in non-alcohol models, on sinusoidal endothelial and CD8<sup>+</sup> T cells, not hepatocytes, and ethanol induces hepatocyte fibroblast growth factor 21, whose analogue acts on β-Klotho<sup>+</sup> amygdala neurons. Organised by target, not organ, each candidate is appraised separately on both sides, negatives, terminations and non-replications counting alike. Of sixteen targets spanning incretin, hepatokine, glutamatergic and microbial or neuroimmune families, three are supported on both sides in the desired direction but only in separate experiments, three point in opposite directions, and ten have had no manipulation read out on both; for none were both organs read out in one experiment. Dual targeting changes what trials must measure: only one of 64 registered trials makes both endpoints primary, so objectively measured intake and a liver endpoint must be co-primary.

title: Right Ventricular Remodeling Using Three-Dimensional Echocardiography in Pediatric Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension Associated with Congenital Heart Disease: A Case-Control Study.
authorString: Șuteu CC, Făgărăşan A, Gozar L, Muntean I, Şuteu N, Toma D, Paşc AS, Blesneac C, Beligan L, Cerghit-Paler A, Iurian DR, Iancu M.
abstractText: Background: Three-dimensional echocardiography (3DE) enables comprehensive assessment of right ventricular (RV) remodeling, but its role in children with pulmonary arterial hypertension associated with congenital heart disease (PAH-CHD) remains incompletely characterized. Methods: In the current case-control study, eleven children with catheterization-confirmed PAH-CHD and 50 healthy controls underwent conventional, three-dimensional, and speckle-tracking echocardiography. Three-dimensional RV geometry and function were compared between groups, and their discriminative performance and relationships with conventional and deformation indices were evaluated. Results: Children with PAH-CHD showed increased RV volumes and transverse dimensions, reduced longitudinal dimension, and impaired systolic function compared with controls (all adjusted p < 0.05). RV fractional area change (RV_FAC_3D) and RV ejection fraction (RV_EF_3D) measured by 3DE demonstrated acceptable-to-good discriminative performance (AUC = 0.88, 95% CI: [0.73,1] and AUC = 0.85, 95% CI: [0.70,1], respectively), whereas 3D tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (RV_TAPSE_3D) and RV_SV_3D did not achieve significant discrimination after correction for multiple comparisons. After controlling for PAH-CHD duration, significant partial Pearson correlations were observed between RV end-systolic volume (RV_ESV_3D) and left ventricular end-diastolic mass (LV_ED_mass_3D): partial r = 0.85, p = 0.0017, p-corrected = 0.012, LV_ED_mass_3D: RV_SV_3D and RV_Ld_3D were both negatively correlated with LV_AIS (partial r = -0.81, p = 0.0042 and partial r = -0.85, p = 0.0016, respectively p-corrected = 0.0352). Conclusions: Most 3D indices discriminated PAH-CHD from controls with acceptable-to-good accuracy. RV volumetric and functional indices correlated broadly with conventional 2D and diastolic Doppler parameters, with LV geometry and segmental mechanics, and, more selectively, with right atrial contractile strain although not all correlations remained significant after correction for multiple comparison. These exploratory findings suggest that 3DE may complement conventional echocardiography in the multiparametric assessment of pediatric PAH-CHD.

title: Clinical and Genetic Landscape of Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia in Turkey: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study on Genotype-Phenotype Correlations.
authorString: Kuzu Kuşaklı A, Emiralioğlu N, Sunman B, Akgül Erdal M, Alboğa D, Çapraz Yavuz B, Karahan S, Karakoç E, Yalçın EE, Doğru Ersöz D, Kiper N, Özçelik U.
abstractText:
Background

Primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) is a genetic disorder impairing mucociliary clearance. This study provides a comprehensive analysis of clinical and genetic characteristics in a large Turkish cohort with frequent parental consanguinity.

Methods

A retrospective cohort study was performed on 145 patients (selected from 361) with regular follow-up since 2017 to ensure longitudinal data consistency. The diagnostic work-up included nasal nitric oxide measurement and high-speed videomicroscopy, while confirmation was established through genetic testing and/or transmission electron microscopy. Patients were classified according to the 2025 ATS/ERS diagnostic framework. Patients were evaluated for clinical predictors, longitudinal pulmonary function, and genotype-phenotype correlations based on structural protein localization.

Results

Among 145 patients (mean age 15.91 ± 6.26 years), early diagnosis was significantly associated with neonatal respiratory distress syndrome (p = 0.014), NICU admission (p < 0.001), situs inversus totalis (p < 0.001), and congenital heart disease (p < 0.001). The mean PICADAR score was 7.8 ± 3.4, showing a moderate negative correlation with age at diagnosis (r = -0.50, p < 0.001). According to the 2025 ATS/ERS diagnostic framework, 63 patients (43.4%) were classified as confirmed PCD, 13 (9.0%) as PCD highly likely, and 69 (47.6%) as suspected PCD. Among confirmed PCD patients, the most frequent genetic findings were DNAH5, CCDC40, and DNAAF1. Lower final FEV1 values were observed in selected rare genotype subgroups, particularly CCNO, although variant-specific comparisons were limited by small subgroup sizes.

Conclusion

Early recognition of neonatal respiratory distress requiring NICU admission and laterality defects, particularly situs inversus totalis, remains critical for reducing diagnostic delay. In populations with high consanguinity, genetic testing is particularly important for confirming diagnosis and identifying potentially high-risk genotypes. Multidisciplinary follow-up focusing on nutrition, infection control, and preservation of lung function is essential for long-term care in PCD.

title: Obesity in Repaired Tetralogy of Fallot: Implications for Symptoms, Right Ventricular Assessment, and Pulmonary Valve Replacement.
authorString: Di Salvo G, Pomiato E, Marino F, Alras Y, Shoaib Shah A, Prati F, Galzerano D, Pergola V.
abstractText: Obesity complicates assessment after repair of tetralogy of Fallot (rTOF) because it can influence symptoms, exercise performance, ventricular remodeling, and the normalization of ventricular measurements. This narrative review examines the direct rTOF evidence, almost all observational, and its implications for pulmonary valve replacement (PVR) decision-making. Obesity is present in approximately 15-20% of patients (12-26% across the cohorts reviewed). In studies using absolute, height-indexed, or ideal-BSA-indexed volumes, obesity was associated with larger biventricular volumes and lower ventricular ejection fractions, and the RV volume association persisted after adjustment for PR in one study. These findings have implications for the interpretation of cardiac findings in patients with moderate-to-severe PR after rTOF. Decisions are best made by integrating all findings, with extra attention to patients with obesity. We propose an integrated assessment of symptoms, rhythms, exercise findings, and ventricular measurements.

title: Ambulatory Blood Pressure Monitoring in Adults with Congenital Heart Disease.
authorString: Kiel AJ, Gupta PR, Matloff R, Fairchild W, Han F, Upadhyay S, Dodeja AK.
abstractText: Background/Objectives: Adults with congenital heart disease (ACHD) are at high risk for late cardiac sequelae and hypertension (HTN). Ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) is superior to office measurements in reproducibility, association with cardiovascular outcomes, and detection of masked and white coat HTN (WCH). The utility of ABPM in the ACHD population is not well studied. This study aims to determine the prevalence of hypertension in the ACHD population and evaluate the utility of ABPM in diagnosing hypertension in the ACHD population. Methods: This is a single-center retrospective analysis of ACHD patients who completed ABPM from 2021 to 2024. Results: Forty ACHD patients underwent ABPM during the study period. Twenty-nine (73%) had hypertension (HTN) in clinic. On ABPM, nine (23%) were confirmed normotensive, 15 (38%) had white coat hypertension (WCH), 14 (35%) were confirmed hypertensive, and two (5%) had masked HTN. There was a 33% decrease in patients meeting criteria for HTN on ABPM compared to in clinic (p = 0.002). Ten patients with HTN on ABPM had follow-up, during which seven (70%) had improved clinic blood pressure. One patient (2.5%) had an antihypertensive removed following WCH diagnosis on ABPM. Conclusions: ABPM is a useful way to diagnose and monitor hypertension in the ACHD population. Based on ABPM, many patients (43%) were found to have either WCH or masked HTN, and 15% had their HTN stage reclassified. ABPM results led to 33% of patients having subsequent medication adjustment. Data from ABPM can help optimize medical management, in turn reducing cardiac strain and acquired heart disease risk in ACHD patients.

title: Inferior Vena Cava-left Atrial Connection Hidden Beneath Large Secundum Defect. A Case Report.
authorString: Putri AY, Tiyantara MS.

journal.title: Journal of the Saudi Heart Association

abstractText: Inferior vena cava (IVC) drainage into left atrium is an exceptionally rare congenital anomaly and may remain unrecognized when associated with a large atrial septal defect (ASD). A 35-year-old-man presented with progressive exertional dyspnea and fatigue. Transthoracic echocardiography, transesophageal echocardiography, and cardiac catheterization demonstrated a large secundum ASD with severe septal malalignment, while systemic venous drainage was interpreted as normal. During surgical ASD repair, an unexpected IVC-to-left atrium connection was identified and redirected to right atrium. Careful assessment of IVC inflow is essential in patients with large malaligned ASD despite normal oxygen saturation.

title: Beyond the Segmental Code: Anatomic Diversity and Surgical Pathways in Left Atrial Appendage Isomerism with the {A,L,I} Combination.
authorString: Şerifoğlu Ş, Şengül FS, Nalbant M, Günyel B, Ayyıldız P, Yıldız O, Gökalp S, Cansever AT, Haydin S, Güzeltaş A.
abstractText: Background/Objectives: Left atrial appendage isomerism (LAAI) is associated with substantial variation in venous connections and intracardiac anatomy. A subgroup of LAAI patients has L-loop ventricular topology together with a particular great artery relationship-a combination that corresponds historically to Van Praagh's {A,L,I} segmental notation-but this subgroup has not been separately characterized. We aimed to describe the anatomical spectrum, rhythm and conduction abnormalities, biventricular repair eligibility, and surgical pathways in this subgroup. Methods: This single-center retrospective study included 15 patients with LAAI, L-loop ventricular topology, and a specific great artery relationship (aorta left-sided, pulmonary artery right-sided)-a combination corresponding historically to Van Praagh's {A,L,I} notation-evaluated between January 2010 and December 2025. Diagnosis was confirmed independently by echocardiography and cardiac computed tomography in all patients. Anatomical suitability for biventricular repair was determined by multidisciplinary consensus. Results: Median age at presentation was 3.0 months, and median follow-up was 31.0 months. An interrupted inferior vena cava was present in all patients. The great artery relationship was aorta left-posterior/pulmonary artery right-anterior in 12 patients, aorta left-anterior/pulmonary artery right-posterior in 2, and side-by-side in 1. Ventriculoarterial connection was concordant in 8 patients, double-outlet right ventricle in 6, and double-outlet left ventricle in 1. A common atrioventricular valve was present in 7 patients. Right ventricular outflow tract obstruction was present in 7 patients. Arrhythmia was documented in 6 patients, and 2 required permanent pacemaker implantation. Ten patients (66.7%) were considered anatomically eligible for biventricular repair; repair had been completed in 4, 2 had received interim palliation, and 4 remained awaiting surgery. The remaining 4 patients followed a single-ventricle pathway. One death was confirmed, and 2 patients were lost to follow-up. Conclusions: Within LAAI, the coexistence of L-loop ventricular topology and a specific great artery relationship was associated with ventriculoarterial concordance in most patients, which may support biventricular repair. Anatomical eligibility for repair, however, did not always translate into completed repair. Larger, multicenter studies are needed to confirm these findings.

title: Giving voice to the next generation in paediatric cardiology and congenital heart diseases.
authorString: Moscatelli S, Heying R, Michel-Behnke I, McMahon CJ, Krupickova S, Duncker D, Sommer P.

title: Lymphopenia in thymectomized infants following congenital heart disease repair: implications for protective measures.
authorString: Abulhamail A, O Alsulami A, Samargandy S, Ekpal Mahboob H, Alahmadi BA, Ywsef KA, B Habiballah S, Jobah MB.
abstractText:
Background

Congenital heart disease (CHD) is a common birth defect frequently requiring surgical repair with thymectomy. While transient neonatal lymphopenia is usually benign, persistent lymphopenia may increase susceptibility to infections and immune dysregulation. This study examines the prevalence and longitudinal course of lymphopenia after thymectomy in infants with CHD, contributory factors, and infection risk.

Method

This is a retrospective cohort study in which all children <2 years who underwent first congenital heart surgery with thymectomy between 2017-2022 for conotruncal defects were recruited. Baseline, post-operative, long-term lymphocyte counts, and episodes of infections for 3 years following the surgery were collected.

Results

The data were collected from 95 patients with median age at the time of surgery 9.0 (IQR 5.0, 12.0) months and median weight 5.0 (1.0, 25.0) Kg. Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) represented 53.68% of the sample. Prevalence of baseline lymphopenia was 11.6%, and within 1 week following the surgery increased to 54.7%. Being lymphopenic at baseline was associated with a decrement in lymphocyte count postoperatively by 1.2 × 10^9/L (P = 0.02) even after adjustment for failure to thrive.

Conclusion

Immediate and long-term lymphopenia is highly prevalent post CHD surgical repair. Earlier age at the time of surgery, baseline lymphopenia, and being failure to thrive were significant predictors for lymphopenia post CHD surgical repair with total thymectomy. Subsequent lymphopenia not necessarily correlates with increase rate or severity of the infections. Pre-, post-operative and long-term lymphocyte count screening and clinical monitoring are warranted.

title: Clinical characterization and genotype-phenotype correlations in Chilton-Okur-Chung syndrome.
authorString: Duz MB, Lasa-Aranzasti A, Cazurro-Gutiérrez A, Hackett A, Cueto-González AM, Périco AA, Ruivenkamp CAL, Gómez-Andrés D, Curic E, Palmer EE, Jones EA, Aliu E, Veenstra-Knol HE, Goel H, Marti IC, Legebeke J, Klein Wassink-Ruiter JS, Ewans L, Thomas MA, Codina-Solà M, den Hollander NS, Martínez-Gil N, Gates R, Kana SL, McKee S, Banka S, Sell S, Chung WK.
abstractText:
Background

Chilton-Okur-Chung neurodevelopmental syndrome is a rare disorder characterized by global developmental delay, variable intellectual disability, behavioral challenges, and structural brain anomalies caused by variants in CDC42BPB. CDC42BPB encodes MRCKβ, a ubiquitously expressed serine/threonine kinase involved in cytoskeletal regulation. The phenotypic spectrum and genotype-phenotype relationships remain incompletely characterized.

Methods

We aggregated data from 20 newly identified individuals and 17 previously reported individuals. We analyzed the data for genotype-phenotype correlations according to variant type.

Results

Developmental delay was the most common phenotype, affecting 85% of individuals, with early delays notable in walking and speech. Intellectual disability was observed in 62%. Behavioral diagnoses included autism spectrum disorder (68%) and ADHD (60%). Structural brain abnormalities were present in 48% of cases, predominantly affecting the cerebellum and ventricles. Dysmorphic features were present in 83% of cases. Hypotonia was present in 68%, seizures in 41%, and macrocephaly in 38%. Genotype-phenotype analysis indicated that predicted loss-of-function (LoF) variants were generally associated with milder neurodevelopmental features than missense variants. A male predominance was observed despite this being an autosomal dominant condition, suggesting a possible protective effect in females. Some heterozygous predicted LoF variants were inherited from self-reported unaffected parents or with subtle neurodevelopmental or cardiac features, supporting incomplete penetrance and variable expressivity.

Conclusions

Our findings highlight the differences between predicted loss-of-function and missense variants. Future studies assessing biochemical differences in kinase activity and substrate specificity may explain these clinical differences.

title: Applications of organoid technology in basic and translational research on liver diseases.
authorString: Zhang W, Song L, Zhang H, Li W, Sun P.
abstractText: Liver organoids (LOs) are derived from pluripotent stem cells, adult stem cells (ASCs), or primary hepatic tissues using three-dimensional (3D) culture systems. These models self-assemble in vitro and recapitulate key hepatic structures and functions, thereby creating complementary platforms for liver development studies, as well as research on disease pathogenesis, drug metabolism/toxicity, and translational applications. The continuous improvement in engineering technologies has permitted LOs and liver-on-a-chip platforms to be applied to a variety of liver diseases such as fatty liver disease, inherited liver disorders, drug-induced liver injury (DILI), fibrotic liver disease, and hepatocellular carcinoma. Nevertheless, the widening deployment of LOs is impeded by numerous source-specific limitations. Although pluripotent stem cell-derived LOs are often immature, fetal-like, and lineage-biased, tissue-derived LOs continue to be hampered by limited sample availability, donor-to-donor variability, expansion-related phenotypic drift, and challenges in their standardization. Incomplete recapitulation of the native microenvironment, as well as high cross-batch variability, continues to hinder clinical translation in both systems.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Obstetrics and Prenatal Medicine: Current Evidence, Clinical Validation and Implementation.
authorString: Recker F.
abstractText:
Introduction

Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly entering obstetrics and prenatal medicine, particularly in prenatal ultrasound, fetal echocardiography, fetal magnetic resonance imaging, genomic screening, risk prediction and clinical decision support. The aim of this review was to summarize current evidence, recent developments and implementation requirements for AI-based applications in prenatal care.

Materials and methods

A structured narrative review was performed with emphasis on peer-reviewed and clinically relevant literature published from 2021 to 2026, supplemented by landmark methodological, regulatory and reporting guidance. Priority was given to systematic reviews, diagnostic accuracy studies, external validation studies, prospective evaluations, randomized educational or clinical studies, regulatory documents and reporting standards relevant to AI in medicine.

Results

The strongest current evidence supports AI-assisted standard-plane recognition, image-quality assessment and fetal biometry, followed by emerging applications in fetal cardiac screening, blind-sweep ultrasound, fetal MRI segmentation, placental phenotyping, prediction of fetal growth restriction, preterm birth and preeclampsia, and machine learning-enhanced cfDNA analysis. Generative and multimodal AI systems may support report drafting, guideline retrieval and education, but remain insufficiently validated for autonomous clinical decision-making.

Discussion

AI has the potential to improve access, standardization, efficiency and quality assurance in prenatal medicine. However, most applications remain limited by retrospective design, enriched datasets, insufficient external validation, unclear calibration, limited fairness analyses and incomplete workflow evaluation. Clinical adoption should therefore follow a human-in-the-loop model with prospective validation, transparent reporting, regulatory oversight, bias monitoring and post-market surveillance. AI should augment rather than replace specialist expertise in obstetrics and fetal medicine.

title: Association of Accelerated Biological Age in Midlife with Cardiovascular Events, Dementia, and All-Cause Mortality in the Framingham Offspring Study.
authorString: Pan S, Beiser AS, Mitchell GF, Seshadri S, Xanthakis V, Vasan RS.
abstractText:
Accelerated biological age (ABA) better capture the aging process than chronological age (CA) and has been linked to adverse health outcomes, but long-term associations remain unclear. We modeled ABA using anthropometric and biochemical biomarkers across three examination cycles (1991-2001) in 3046 Framingham Offspring Study participants. Stratified by sex, BA was estimated using the Klemera and Doubal method with principal components and categorized as accelerated (> 1SD), concordant (± 1SD), or decelerated (DBA; < -1SD) based on standardized residuals from CA. Multivariable-adjusted time-dependent Cox and competing risk models were used to relate ABA with cardiovascular disease (CVD), dementia, and mortality. Over a median follow-up of 26 years (maximum 31), participants (mean age 55 years, 55% women) experienced 713 CVD events, 265 dementia cases, and 1105 deaths. Compared with DBA, men with ABA had higher risks of CVD (HR 1.6; 95% CI 1.07-2.28; p = 0.02) and death (HR 2.3; 95% CI 1.73-3.18; p < 0.0001). Women with ABA had higher risks of CVD (HR 1.8; 95% CI 1.24-2.64; p = 0.002), dementia (HR 2.1; 95% CI 1.03-4.32; p = 0.04), and death (HR 1.8; 95% CI 1.27-2.54; p = 0.0009). Accelerated midlife BA was associated with increased risk of adverse outcomes, particularly dementia in women, supporting the importance of healthy multisystem aging over the life course.

Supplementary information

The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-64591-9.

title: Dysbiosis of gut fungi and bacteria in patients with HBV with low-level viremia compared with sustained virologic responders and healthy controls.
authorString: Wang Q, An J, Chen Y, Zheng X, Wu K, Yuan H, Tong G, Du Y, Zhang L.
abstractText:
Background

Although bacterial dysbiosis in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) is well established, the role of the gut mycobiome-particularly its functional interplay with bacteria during virological remission versus treatment failure remains unexplored. In this study, the gut bacteriome and mycobiome were characterized in hepatitis B virus (HBV) patients with low-level viremia (LLV) or sustained virological response (SVR) and healthy controls (HCs).

Methods

This study enrolled a cohort comprising 28 healthy controls (HCs) and 43 patients with CHB from the Second Affiliated Hospital of Hainan Medical University. The patients with CHB were further stratified into LLV (n = 22) and SVR (n = 21) groups. The bacterial and fungal compositions of the collected fecal samples were characterized by 16 S rRNA gene sequencing and internal transcribed spacer (ITS) sequencing, respectively.

Results

Compared with HCs, patients with CHB presented increased bacterial richness but decreased fungal richness. Beta diversity analysis revealed distinct microbial clustering between the HC and CHB groups (LLV and SVR). Patients with LLV showed enrichment of Bacteroides/Faecalibacterium and depletion of Blautia (vs. HCs) as well as lower levels of Lactobacillus and higher levels of Faecalibacterium (vs. patients with SVR). Fungal taxa such as Kazachstania were reduced in the LLV group compared with the HC group, and Candida was less abundant in the LLV group than in the SVR group. A diagnostic model based on the Eubacterium coprostanoligenes grouping variable, Actinomyces, Bacteroides, Lachnoclostridium, and Phascolarctobacterium achieved high accuracy (AUC = 0.804) in distinguishing patients with LLV from HCs.

Conclusion

Compared with patients with SVR and HCs, patients with HBV with LLV exhibit distinct gut bacterial and fungal dysbiosis.

title: Impact of alcohol use discontinuation on adipose tissue insulin resistance among Latino patients with and without underlying chronic liver disease.
authorString: Patel S, Do A, Shui A, Khalili M.
abstractText: We evaluated the effect of short-term moderate alcohol discontinuation on adipose tissue insulin resistance (adipo-IR) and factors associated with its change in Latinos with and without hepatitis C virus (HCV). Nondiabetic Latino adults without (N = 17) or with (N = 7) HCV underwent clinical, laboratory, genetic, and metabolic testing. Metabolic testing was repeated after 6.5 weeks of moderate alcohol discontinuation. Adipo-IR was measured using a 2-step insulin suppression test. Multivariable linear regression, including HCV status, identified factors associated with change in adipo-IR. Median age was 50 years, 58% female, median BMI 26.3 kg/m². Genetic ancestry was 57% European, 36% Native American, and 3.5% African. CYP2E1 genotyping showed 14% were homozygous for [c2/c2] risk-allele. No significant changes in adipo-IR occurred after alcohol discontinuation. On multivariable regression, CYP2E1 homozygous risk-allele (vs. none, estimate 0.25 mmol/L, p < 0.001) and overweight/obesity (vs. normal weight, estimate 0.13 mmol/L, p = 0.02), but not HCV, were associated with change in adipo-IR following alcohol discontinuation. Although there was no significant overall change in adipo-IR following short-term moderate alcohol discontinuation, CYP2E1 homozygous risk-allele and overweight/obesity were associated with changes in adipo-IR. These exploratory findings suggest that host genetic and metabolic characteristics may influence metabolic responses to alcohol discontinuation and warrant validation in larger prospective studies.

title: Acute Myeloid Leukemia in a Patient with Fontan Circulation - Case Report.
authorString: Strah D, Joshirao M, Narayan HK, Ganesan AP, Carter C, Silva-Sepulveda J.
abstractText: Patients with single ventricle heart disease require a series of palliative surgeries, culminating in the Fontan, which results in passive pulmonary arterial blood flow after direct connection of the venae cavae to the pulmonary arteries.<sup>1</sup> Fontan circulation leads to complications impacting multiple organ systems, however cancers outside of hepatocellular carcinoma are not reported frequently.<sup>1</sup> Anthracycline-based chemotherapeutic regimens, frequently used to treat pediatric cancers, carry a significant dose-dependent risk of cardiotoxicity. Protocols require monitoring of left ventricular ejection fraction to detect declines in cardiac function and guide treatment. Monitoring cardiac function in Fontan patients with systemic right ventricle presents unique challenges due to limitations of echocardiography to assess right ventricular systolic function, lack of established values for quantitative measures of systemic right ventricular function, and limited applicability of heart failure regimens for systemic right ventricles.<sup>1</sup> Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging and computed tomography can better quantitate right ventricular systolic function, however these modalities are limited by ferromagnetic artifacts from prior interventions and contraindicated with renal dysfunction, respectively.<sup>2</sup> We present a patient with Fontan physiology and systemic right ventricle, diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) requiring multi-disciplinary management with a goal of curative treatment of AML while minimizing cardiac and nephrotoxicity.

title: Building CRESCENDO - a global registry of glomerulonephritis with crescents.
authorString: Ivković V, Kronbichler A, Bruchfeld A, CRESCENDO Investigators .
abstractText: Crescents represent a non-specific mechanism in response to severe glomerular injury and show a temporal pattern evolving from cellular and fibrocellular to fibrous. Crescentic glomerulonephritis (GN) is defined as ≥50% cellular crescentic glomeruli on kidney histology and is frequently characterized by rapid deterioration of kidney function and features of nephritis. However, little is known about how different types and proportions of crescents affect prognosis and this may differ across diseases forming the spectrum of crescentic GN. To explore this, we devised CRESCENDO, a multinational, longitudinal, observational registry collecting clinical, laboratory and histopathology data from patients with GN and crescents. The registry aims to enrol patients from all continents to explore the prognostic value of crescents on a continuum, ranging from one crescentic glomerulus to 100% crescents on biopsy. We also aim to explore other potential prognostic and diagnostic predictors of a wide range of outcomes (not limited to mortality and kidney survival, but also infections, malignancy and kidney function recovery), leverage exploratory machine learning approaches of scanned kidney biopsies and test the efficacy and safety of different therapies across the crescentic GN spectrum. The findings of CRESCENDO will hopefully help close gaps in the understanding of crescentic GN and will generate further hypotheses providing the basis for subsequent research.

title: Predicting Gastrointestinal Complications After Cardiac Surgery From Mean Arterial Blood Pressure Under a Data-Driven Threshold for Hypotension: Protocol for an Advanced Database Study.
authorString: Rømer V, Wiberg S, Itenov TS, Linde JJ, Corbascio M, Holbek BL.
abstractText:
Background

Hypotension during cardiopulmonary bypass may increase the risk of gastrointestinal complications due to insufficient splanchnic autoregulatory capacity. We hypothesize that both duration and level of blood pressure below a data-driven threshold during cardiopulmonary bypass are associated with the risk of gastrointestinal complications.

Methods

Patients who underwent cardiac surgery at Copenhagen University Hospital, Rigshospitalet, during 2018-2022 will be included if they underwent on-pump valve surgery, coronary artery bypass grafting, and/or surgery on the ascending aorta. The primary outcome is major gastrointestinal complications within 30 days, defined as acute intestinal ischemia, abdominal surgery, bowel perforation, or gastrointestinal hemorrhage. Secondary endpoints are serious gastrointestinal complications, delayed recovery of bowel function, cholinesterase inhibitor administration, and 30-day mortality. The exposure is the exposure to lower blood pressure, calculated as the product of the duration and level of blood pressure below a data-driven threshold. To identify the optimal threshold, we split the population in a training (75%) and validation cohort (25%). In the training cohort we will identify the threshold with the highest area under the receiver operating curve for the primary outcome. The selected threshold will then be applied to quantify the exposure to lower blood pressure for each patient. Patients will be grouped using a modified Youden's index (weighing sensitivity 80%) as a cutoff for high versus low exposure to lower blood pressure, and association with the study endpoints will be determined in the validation cohort.

Conclusion

Under the assumption of pressure-dependent perfusion outside of an autoregulatory plateau, the exposure to blood pressure below a threshold might reflect the risk of gastrointestinal complications more accurately than point measures or averages. The results from this study may lead to relevant hypotheses for prospective testing.

title: Physical Activity Among Bangladeshi Immigrant Families Living in the United States: A Qualitative Study of Multi-Family Member Interviews.
authorString: Gupta-Louis SK, Roychowdhury L, Roychowdhury L, Mercedes J, Bhinder SK, Islam NS, Revenson TA.
abstractText:
Background

South Asian immigrants (SAIs) are at an elevated risk for cardiovascular disease (CVD). One way to decrease CVD risk is by increasing physical activity (PA). Research on increasing PA among SAIs has identified the family as having an important influence, yet little research has incorporated a family perspective.

Objective

This study aimed to describe PA at the family-level, drawing on qualitative interviews from families who immigrated from Bangladesh to the United States (US).

Methods

Multi-family member interviews, conducted in English or Bengali, were coded using a thematic analysis, with the family as the unit of analysis.

Results

Ten families were interviewed (80% in Bengali, 20% in English). The 10 families included 25 individuals ( M age = 48.7 years; 68% female). Most family members (79.2%) reported they had engaged in PA in the week before the interview. Examples of PA included structured exercise, culturally-specific practices (eg, Muslim prayer), and activities of daily living. PA was described as a shared health behavior that aligns with a collective value of health consciousness.

Conclusions

Findings suggest a family-level approach to research and intervention design may be beneficial to increase PA among SAIs living in the US at risk of CVD.

title: Sunbathing in Primates: Experimental Evidence Discounting Vitamin D<sub>3</sub> Synthesis as a Primary Function in Ring-Tailed Lemurs (Lemur catta).
authorString: Chhoker A, Patacsil-Tesoy N, Gourlie S, Bridgett GR, Ricci M, Steffens TS, Teichroeb JA.
abstractText:
Background

The function of sunbathing is often assumed to be thermoregulation, but UV-B wavelength light also allows subcutaneous synthesis of vitamin D3. We sought to determine the primary function of sunbathing in ring-tailed lemurs.

Methods

We gave five lemurs at the Toronto Zoo choice of two sunbathing spots (one UV-B and one UV-A lamp, counter-balanced for site preference) as their diet was increased in vitamin D3. We measured sunbathing bouts at each lamp using a video camera trap.

Results

Positional sunning behavior was more frequent in the darkest months, when it was colder, and during sunnier conditions. The lemurs had a strong site preference and basked more at the UV-A lamp. Increasing dietary vitamin D3 did not change their lamp and site preferences.

Conclusion

We found no supporting evidence that sunbathing in ring-tailed lemurs primarily functions for vitamin D3 synthesis, but we include methodological suggestions for others to revisit this hypothesis.

title: Hemodynamic effects of cycle ergometry versus dynamic unilateral arm exercise during right heart catheterization: a prospective observational study.
authorString: Berezucki E, Heinrich M, Rueß A, Lange TJ, Perl M, Stadler S.
abstractText:
Background

The reintroduction of exercise pulmonary hypertension (EPH) to the pulmonary hypertension (PH) definition by the European guidelines underlines the importance of examining the hemodynamic response to exercise during right heart catheterization. Because the standard exercise modality of cycle ergometry (CE) is not universally accessible, we compared its hemodynamic effects with those of dynamic single-arm exercise (AE) in patients undergoing right heart catheterization (RHC).

Methods

50 consecutive patients with indication for RHC were enrolled. Hemodynamic parameters were assessed at rest, followed by randomized exercise periods with an intervening rest phase. Thermodilution was used to determine cardiac output. The intensity of the AE was patient-determined, whereas CE was conducted at a fixed work rate ranging from 10 to 50 watts, based on the patient's physical status. Oxygen uptake (VO₂) was estimated using the reverse Fick principle to compare relative exercise intensity between modalities. EPH was defined by an mPAP/cardiac output slope > 3 mmHg·L⁻¹·min⁻¹, and exercise-induced left heart disease by a rise in PAWP from ≤ 15 mmHg at rest to > 25 mmHg during exercise.

Results

Mean pulmonary arterial pressure increased by 12 mmHg with CE compared to 3 mmHg with AE (p<0.001), pulmonary artery wedge pressure increased by 5 mmHg versus 2 mmHg (p<0.001), cardiac output increased by 2.2 L/min versus 0.6 L/min (p<0.001) and mean pulmonary vascular resistance decreased by 0.05 WU with CE (p=0.761) and by 0.32 with AE (p=0.03). Estimated VO₂ during AE reached only 24% of the increase observed during CE, corresponding to an external workload equivalent of approximately 6 W. No patient showed an increase in pulmonary artery wedge pressure during exercise above 25mmHg to unmask left heart disease. In patients without PH at rest, CE led to the diagnosis of EPH in 5 patients while the used AE protocol was not suitable to detect EPH.

Conclusion

AE proved to be a safe exercise modality in our study but, with the protocol applied here, produced significantly smaller hemodynamic changes during RHC than CE and is thus not an adequate substitute in this form, leaving open whether an intensity-matched protocol could achieve comparable hemodynamic effects.

title: Xiao Chai Hu Decoction ameliorates doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity through an Akkermansia muciniphila-associated gut-heart mechanism.
authorString: Zhai F, Tao L, Xia Y, He Q, Lin H, Liu D.
abstractText:
Background

Doxorubicin (DOX) induces cardiotoxicity partly through ferroptosis. Xiao Chai Hu Decoction (XCHD) has anti-inflammatory and organ-protective activities, but its effects on DOX-induced cardiac injury and the gut-heart axis remain unclear.

Purpose

This study investigated whether XCHD attenuates DOX-induced cardiotoxicity through gut microbiota remodeling, with particular emphasis on the contribution of Akkermansia muciniphila and the downstream involvement of BMP10-associated ferroptosis.

Methods

Male C57BL/6 mice received DOX (5 mg/kg/week for 4 weeks; cumulative dose, 20 mg/kg) and XCHD (5-20 g/kg/day). Cardiac function, myocardial injury, histopathology, iron accumulation, and ferroptosis-related indices were evaluated. Cardiac transcriptomics and fecal 16S rRNA sequencing were combined with antibiotic-mediated microbiota depletion, fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT), and A. muciniphila supplementation to assess microbiota involvement. H9c2 cells treated with XCHD-containing serum and subjected to BMP10 knockdown were used to examine the downstream role of BMP10.

Results

XCHD improved cardiac function and reduced myocardial injury, fibrosis, iron accumulation, and ferroptosis-associated alterations. Transcriptomic analysis identified BMP10 as a candidate downstream factor suppressed by DOX and restored by XCHD. In H9c2 cells, XCHD-containing serum attenuated ferroptosis-associated changes, whereas BMP10 knockdown weakened these effects, supporting a functional contribution of BMP10 in vitro. XCHD also preserved intestinal barrier integrity, reshaped the gut microbiota, and enriched A. muciniphila. Microbiota depletion abolished the protective effects of XCHD, whereas FMT transferred the protective phenotype. A. muciniphila supplementation reproduced key cardiac and anti-ferroptotic effects, with live bacteria producing greater benefits than heat-inactivated bacteria; these changes were accompanied by restoration of myocardial BMP10 expression.

Conclusion

XCHD alleviates DOX-induced cardiotoxicity through an A. muciniphila-associated, microbiota-dependent gut-heart mechanism involving intestinal barrier preservation and attenuation of ferroptosis-associated injury. These findings support a "TCM formula-gut microbiota-host response-regulated cell death" framework for XCHD-mediated cardioprotection.

title: Predictors of mortality in patients treated with ECMELLA after cardiac surgery – a single- center experience
authorString: Salah N, Bechtel M, Strauch JT, Moustafine V, Haldenwang PL, Buchwald D, Loesaus S, Becker S, Zahn PK, Berres DM.
abstractText: Background Postcardiotomy cardiogenic shock (PCS) remains a serious complication after cardiac surgery associated with high perioperative mortality. Over the last years, the use of veno-arterial extracorporeal life support (VA-ECLS) combined with left ventricular unloading by a microaxial flow pump (ECMELLA) has increased. Data on mortality predictors in patients treated with ECMELLA for PCS remain limited. We aimed to identify factors associated with 30-day all-cause mortality after ECMELLA implantation. Methods We retrospectively analyzed consecutive patients who received concomitant VA-ECLS and a microaxial pump after cardiac surgery at our university center between 2019 and 2024. Clinically relevant surrogate parameters were assessed along with 30-day mortality. Discriminative ability was assessed by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. Survival was analyzed using Kaplan–Meier estimates with log-rank testing, and predictors of 30-day mortality were identified using univariable and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression. Results Of the 34 patients, 26 (76.5%) died within 30 days. The Model for End-stage Liver Disease (MELD) score was significantly higher in non-survivors than in survivors (18.5 [IQR 10.7] vs. 14.9 [IQR 2.8], p = 0.010). The MELD excluding INR (MELD-XI) score was likewise higher in non-survivors (17.6 [IQR 9.7] vs. 10.2 [IQR 2.6], p = 0.001). Lactate levels were significantly lower in survivors at 12 hours (p = 0.03), 18 hours (p = 0.004) and 24 hours (p = 0.02) after ECMELLA initiation. Discrimination was best at 18 hours (AUC 0.824, p < 0.001).
