Prompt diagnosis, aggressive surgical debridement, and rigorous management of complications are essential. In cases of aortic valve regurgitation causing heart failure, TAVI implantation might serve as a temporary bridge until definitive open valve replacement becomes feasible.

title: The global research landscape of emergency medical services in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest.
authorString: Krishnan R, Gadikota P, Ganti L, Banerjee P.
abstractText:
Background

Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) remains a major cause of death, and emergency medical services (EMS) are central to recognition, resuscitation, transport, and linkage to post-arrest care. Although previous bibliometric studies have mapped the broader cardiac arrest and cardiopulmonary resuscitation literature, the intersection of EMS and OHCA warrants focused characterization.

Methods

We performed a retrospective bibliometric analysis of records indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection from 1972 through June 2026. The search combined OHCA terms with terms for EMS, paramedics, and emergency medical technicians. Annual output, research categories, journals, authors, and countries were described. VOSviewer version 1.6.20 was used for author co-authorship, keyword co-occurrence, and cited-reference co-citation analyses.

Results

The search identified 3,005 records. Annual output increased markedly after 2010, peaked at 244 publications in 2021, and remained above 200 publications per year from 2022 to 2025; 130 records were indexed for the partial 2026 year. Emergency Medicine (1,745; 58.1%) and Critical Care Medicine (1,014; 33.7%) were the most frequently assigned Web of Science categories. Resuscitation published 694 records (23.1%). The United States had the greatest country-level output (1,022; 34.0%), followed by Japan (375; 12.5%) and Canada (281; 9.4%). The most prolific author was Shin SD (98 publications). Co-authorship mapping showed registry-centered regional communities, while keyword analysis yielded ten interpreted domains spanning epidemiology, resuscitation interventions, dispatch, registries, extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation, equity, and technology-related topics. Co-citation analysis identified four major intellectual communities.

Conclusion

EMS-focused OHCA publications indexed in Web of Science show sustained output and international collaboration associated with established registries. Limited visibility of low- and middle-income settings within this database warrants further investigation. Equity, implementation, and digital and resuscitative technologies are potential areas for further research; the pooled network analysis does not establish their temporal growth.

title: Mechanism and clinical Fdiagnostic performance of miR-10b-3p as a novel biomarker for coronary artery disease.
authorString: Li Y, Xu K, Qiu H, Cao L, Li B.
abstractText: Coronary artery disease (CAD) continues to demonstrate escalating global incidence and mortality rates, imposing substantial burdens on both healthcare systems and socioeconomic development. This study aimed to analyze the predictive value and potential molecular mechanism of miR-10b-3p in patients with CAD. miR-10b-3p and DERL3 levels were determined by RT-qPCR. ROC curve analysis was performed to evaluate the diagnostic performance. Correlations were tested by Pearson's correlation test. The viability of the cells was assessed by CCK-8 and flow cytometry. Compared with the control group, miR-10b-3p was down​regulated in CAD patients, and the expression in ischemic group was lower than that in non-ischemic group. miR-10b-3p serves as an effective biomarker for distinguishing healthy individuals from CAD patients, as well as differentiating ischemic from non-ischemic patients. Additionally, miR-10b-3p combined with CT-FFR parameters has a high diagnostic efficacy for ischemic stenosis in CAD patients. Mechanistically, miR-10b-3p mimic inhibited the proliferation and MDA levels of HASMCs after ox-LDL exposure, while promoting​ apoptosis and SOD activity. Upregulation of DERL3 partially reversed the regulation of miR-10b-3p mimic on HASMCs biological function. miR-10b-3p has a predictive effect on ischemic stenosis of CAD, and mechanistic studies indicate upregulated miR-10b-3p's protective effects via DERL3 inhibition.

title: The Right-to-Try Does Not Apply to Brain Death.
authorString: Lewis A.
abstractText: The 2018 federal Right-to-Try Act allows patients in the United States with life-threatening conditions to access experimental interventions outside the context of research. This viewpoint addresses concerns about the highly publicized suggestion that the Right-to-Try Act applied to a 2026 case in Texas in which the family of an infant with suspected brain death/death by neurologic criteria (BD/DNC) objected to formal evaluation and requested treatment with hyperbaric oxygen or stem cells. There are varying religious, cultural and philosophical perspectives about defining the end-of-life, but BD/DNC is the legal equivalent of cardiac death/death by circulatory-respiratory criteria in the United States and across much of the world. While the Right-to-Try is applicable to patients with life-threatening neurologic conditions, it is not relevant once catastrophic brain injury is so severe that there is suspicion for BD/DNC, or after BD/DNC declaration. Media stories about cases like this are unfortunately often inaccurate, misleading and/or sensationalized. Because public trust is integral to the practice of medicine, when a case related to BD/DNC is in the news, stakeholder organizations (e.g., the hospital and relevant state and national medical societies) should distribute educational materials to media outlets and/or direct media to curated content. Additionally, organizations that represent clinicians should promote deference to expertise and call out misinformation or obfuscation of scientific data, such as the suggestion that the Right-to-Try Act is relevant to BD/DNC.

title: The 6-Min Walk Test-Based STEP Index for Prognosis in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease.
authorString: Choi JY, Kim SH, Lee J, Jung JY, Kim H, Koo HK, Hwang KE, Moon JY, Yoo KH, An TJ.
abstractText:
Objectives

The 6-minute walk test (6MWT) is widely used to assess functional capacity in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD); however, individual test components remain underutilized despite their independent prognostic value. We aimed to evaluate a 6MWT-derived index for predicting long-term mortality and exacerbation risk in COPD.

Methods

We analyzed 2063 COPD patients from the prospective Korean COPD Subgroup Study. The STEP (Speed Terminate Early Performance) index combined gait speed (<1.0m/s), early test termination, and the distance-saturation product (<290m%). The primary outcome was 10-year all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included respiratory and cardiovascular mortality, exacerbations, and symptom trajectories. Discrimination was compared with the BODE and BODEx indices using Harrell C-index and time-dependent AUCs.

Results

Higher STEP scores were associated with older age, lower body mass index, more severe airflow limitation, and a greater history of exacerbations, along with higher baseline symptom burden. Higher STEP scores were associated with increased rates of moderate-to-severe and severe exacerbations. Ten-year mortality increased from 9.4% in STEP 0 to 37.5% in STEP 3 (P<0.001). The STEP, BODE, and BODEx indices showed similar discrimination for all-cause mortality (C-index 0.750, 0.739, and 0.742, respectively). Adjusted hazard ratios for all-cause mortality were 1.61, 2.61, and 4.78 for STEP 1, 2, and 3, respectively, compared with STEP 0. Respiratory mortality increased significantly with higher STEP categories, whereas cardiovascular mortality showed no gradient.

Conclusion

The STEP index provides robust prognostic stratification using only 6MWT parameters, with performance similar to the BODE and BODEx indices.

title: Comparing surgical shunting with transcatheter stenting for initial palliation of cyanotic tetralogy of fallot: An inverse probability treatment weighting study.
authorString: Lîm HK, Wu MH, Wang JK, Chiu SN, Lu CW, Tseng WC, Chen YS, Huang SC, Chou HW, Chen CA, Lin MT.

journal.title: Journal of the Formosan Medical Association = Taiwan yi zhi

abstractText:
Background/purpose

To compare surgical shunting with transcatheter stenting for initial palliation of cyanotic tetralogy of Fallot, including high-risk infants.

Methods

This retrospective two-center study included 101 infants who underwent palliation before 1 year of age, including 76 who underwent surgical shunting and 25 who underwent transcatheter stenting. Outcomes were evaluated using stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting with doubly robust adjustment. The primary composite outcome was death, cardiopulmonary resuscitation, or extracorporeal membrane oxygenation. Secondary outcomes included recovery, reintervention, medical expenses, and pulmonary artery (PA) development.

Results

After adjustment, the primary composite outcome and overall perioperative complication rate did not differ significantly between groups. Surgical shunting was associated with longer log-transformed intubation duration (β = 0.948, 95% CI 0.203-1.693; P = 0.013), intensive care unit stay (β = 0.584, 95% CI 0.050-1.118; P = 0.032), and hospital stay (β = 0.558, 95% CI 0.071-1.046; P = 0.025), but lower odds of reintervention (OR = 0.112, 95% CI 0.033-0.379; P < 0.001). In high-risk patients, surgical shunting was associated with more perioperative complications (OR = 7.712, 95% CI 1.569-37.913; P = 0.013), higher medical expenses, and lower McGoon and PA symmetry indices at total correction.

Conclusion

No significant between-group differences were observed in the primary composite outcome or overall perioperative complication rate. Transcatheter stenting was associated with faster recovery but more frequent reintervention. Among high-risk infants, it was associated with fewer perioperative complications, lower index hospitalization expenses, and more favorable PA development.

Clinical registration number

The Research Ethics Committee of National Taiwan University Hospital (No. 202602073RIND), waived informed consent.

title: Short- and Mid-Term Effects of Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement on Heart Rate Variability in Patients With Aortic Valve Stenosis.
authorString: Pacaci E, Yildirim A, Evlice M, Tras G, Suleymanoglu C, Ates MS, Coskun M, Sezici E, Gursoy MO, Sen O, Genc O, Kurt IH.
abstractText:
Background

Heart rate variability (HRV) reflects autonomic nervous system balance and has emerged as a potential prognostic marker in cardiovascular diseases. However, the relationship between HRV and mortality following transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) remains unclear.

Method

This prospective cohort study included 230 patients with symptomatic severe aortic stenosis who underwent TAVR between June 2022 and June 2024. Twenty-four-hour Holter electrocardiography recordings were obtained one day before and at 3 months after the procedure to assess HRV using both time- and frequency-domain parameters.

Results

Among the 230 patients enrolled, the 12-month all-cause mortality rate was 14.3%. Among frequency-domain parameters, the pre-TAVR low frequency/high frequency (LF/HF) ratio improved markedly from 2.20±1.45 to 1.54±0.85 (p<0.001). In the time domain, standard deviation of NN intervals (89-103 ms, p=0.027), standard deviation of the averages of NN intervals (68-83 ms, p=0.003), and percentage of successive RR intervals (10.0%-12.0%, p=0.036) all showed significant improvements, while root mean square of successive RR interval differences remained unchanged. The pre-TAVR LF/HF ratio was significantly lower in survivors and provided the best discrimination for 1-year mortality prediction (area under the curve 0.815; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.750-0.881). Calibration analysis confirmed excellent predictive accuracy (C-index, 0.81; Brier score, 0.104; pseudo-R2, 0.285). Patients with a pre-TAVR LF/HF ratio>1.34 had significantly lower mortality at follow-up (hazard ratio [HR] 0.103; 95% CI 0.042-0.250; log-rank p<0.001), and this association remained significant in landmark analysis beyond 3 months (HR 0.163; log-rank p<0.001).

Conclusions

HRV parameters provide meaningful prognostic information in patients undergoing TAVR. Among them, a reduced pre-TAVR LF/HF ratio is independently associated with increased 1-year mortality and may serve as a practical, non-invasive marker for risk stratification.

title: Elevated malonic acid and 15d-PGJ2 in MASLD rats with diabetes triggered pathological cardiac remodeling through impairment of mitochondrial health and cellular metabolism.
authorString: Malladi N, Jorvekar SB, Shukla I, Kumar Y, Yadav R, Arava SK, Priya MRK, Tandon R, Borkar RM, Banerjee SK.

journal.title: Journal of molecular and cellular cardiology

abstractText: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) significantly raises the risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD) and makes it the leading cause of death in affected individuals. Despite growing evidence, the liver-heart connection remains poorly understood. MASLD was induced in male SD rats using an 8-week high-fat diet along with a single streptozotocin dose at week 6. Cardiac changes were assessed by echocardiography, electrocardiography, and histopathology. Two altered metabolites identified by LC-MS/MS were evaluated in cardiomyoblasts (MTT, JC-1, MitoSOX, & Seahorse) and in rats to assess cardiac structure and function. MASLD rats with diabetes exhibited increased LV mass, wall thickness, diastolic diameter, and volume, with reduced ejection fraction, fractional shortening, cardiac output, and stroke volume. Histology confirmed cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, fibrosis, and hepatic lipid accumulation. LC-MS/MS identified elevated malonic acid and 15-deoxy-12,14-prostaglandin J2 (15d-PGJ2) in serum. In cardiomyoblasts, these metabolites increased mitochondrial ROS, reduced membrane potential, and decreased metabolites such as taurine, arginine, succinate, and l-glutamine. Eight weeks of in vivo treatment with malonic acid and 15d-PGJ2 induced pathological cardiac remodeling, fibrosis, and subendocardial ischemia. Metabolite-treated hearts also showed an increase in inosine and 12R-HETE, with reduced isovaleric acid, creatine, proline, and N-acetyl-L-histidine. Altered cardiac structure and function in MASLD rats were associated with elevated serum malonic acid and 15d-PGJ2, which impair mitochondrial homeostasis and cellular metabolism. These findings support a liver-heart axis and highlight potential therapeutic targets for MASLD-related CVD.

title: Changes in Ventilation Associated with Worsening Heart Failure in Ambulatory Patients.
authorString: Gardner RS, Rials SJ, Aktas MK, Capucci A, Gold MR, Molon G, Thakur PH, Averina V, Kwan B, Okeson B, Kupfer M, Clark AL, Boehmer JP.
abstractText:
Background

Breathlessness is a cardinal symptom of heart failure (HF) and reflects abnormal ventilation, particularly during exercise. Cardiopulmonary exercise testing provides only a snapshot of ventilatory physiology and cannot capture longitudinal changes associated with deterioration. Continuous physiologic monitoring from implantable devices offers an opportunity to characterize ventilatory trends preceding HF events in ambulatory patients.

Methods

The MultiSENSE study followed 900 patients with a cardiac resynchronization therapy defibrillator (CRT-D) modified to record high fidelity physiologic data. Ventilatory variables derived from thoracic impedance were examined before adjudicated HF events (hospitalization for HF or outpatient visit requiring IV diuretics) and between clinic visits associated with worsening dyspnea. Variables included respiratory rate (RR), tidal volume (TV), minute ventilation (MV) and Rapid Shallow Breathing Index (RSBI; RR/TV). Patient activity was assessed using a device-embedded accelerometer.

Results

A total of 130 HF events from 92 patients were analyzed. In the 3 days preceding HF events, mean daily RR increased (adjusted mean change: 0.59 [95% CI: 0.31, 0.86], relative change: 3.56%, p<0.0001) and mean daily TV decreased (-0.07 [-0.10, -0.04], -7.4%, p<0.0001), resulting in a significant increase in RSBI (2.34 [1.56, 3.12], 10.5%, p<0.0001). Daily MV decreased (-0.72 [-1.2, -.23], -4.4%, p=0.0042), largely reflecting reduced activity. When accounting only for resting periods, a similar increase in RSBI was observed in the 3 days preceding HF events (1.98 [1.10, 2.86], 7.32%, p<0.0001) relative to baseline, whereas MV showed no significant change. In patients with worsening dyspnea between clinic visits, mean daily RR and RSBI increased significantly without a significant change in TV or MV.

Conclusions

Worsening HF in ambulatory patients is characterized by a shift toward rapid shallow breathing. RSBI significantly increased prior to HF events and with worsening dyspnea.. These findings suggest that RSBI may be a sensitive marker for worsening HF and may provide clinically relevant insight for monitoring ambulatory patients.

title: Two-Year Clinical and Hemodynamic Outcomes After Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement in Severe Mitral Annular Calcification.
authorString: Thourani VH, Ailawadi G, Rogers JH, Bethea B, Guerrero ME, Lim DS, Hebeler R, Cowger J, Allen KB, Sun B, Badhwar V, Stoler R, Ahmed M, Yadav P, Wang J, Asch FM, Blanke P, Sorajja P.
abstractText:
Background

The SUMMIT-MAC trial is evaluating the safety and effectiveness of the Tendyne Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement (TMVR) system in patients with severe mitral annular calcification (MAC). Primary outcomes demonstrated significant improvements in mitral regurgitation severity, heart failure symptoms, and quality-of-life; leading to FDA approval of Tendyne. Intermediate term TMVR outcomes have not been reported.

Methods

The SUMMIT-MAC cohort (NCT03433274) enrolled high surgical-risk patients with severe MAC (average volume 5,679 ± 5,670; range 741 to 37,437 mm3) and significant mitral valve dysfunction. Independent assessments of mitral disease were performed at an echocardiography core laboratory and adverse events were adjudicated by a clinical events committee. Two-year follow-up visits were achieved in 95% of available patients, with an average follow-up of 18.7 months.

Results

The cohort included 103 patients from 37 sites. Mean age was 78.0±6.5 years, 55% were women, 74% were in NYHA functional class III/IV, and mitral regurgitation was present in nearly all patients at baseline (97% grade >2+). At 2 years all-cause mortality was 32.3% (32 patients) and cardiovascular mortality was 23.6% (23 patients). 97% (56/58) of patients with available echocardiograms at 2 years had ≤1+ mitral regurgitation. Additionally, at 2 years, 84% of patients were in NYHA functional class I/II and quality-of-life improved significantly (KCCQ-OS, Δ24.2±19.6 points; p<0.0001).

Conclusions

In a high-risk cohort of patients with mitral valve disease and severe MAC, Tendyne TMVR had acceptable sustained clinical outcomes and quality-of-life over 2 years. The reduction of mitral regurgitation severity was sustained through 2-years post TMVR.

title: Multi-arterial Grafting: From Highly Selective to Routine Use in Females and the Elderly - A Statewide Quality Improvement Analysis.
authorString: Caruso V, Topcu AC, Modukuri S, He C, Clark MJ, Nemeh HW, Schwartz CF, Sell TL, Pruitt AL, Schwann TA.
abstractText:
Background

This study evaluated the impact of the Michigan Society of Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgeons Quality Collaborative initiative to increase multiarterial bypass grafting, focusing on elderly and female patients.

Methods

Adults undergoing isolated, coronary artery bypass grafting with a left internal thoracic artery and >1 additional graft were included in the analysis (2014-2025). Patients were classified as single-arterial or multiarterial grafting (>2 arterial coronary anastomoses) including bilateral internal thoracic artery or internal thoracic artery with radial artery. Primary outcomes included multiarterial grafting utilization overall and within elderly (≥70 years) and female patients. Secondary outcomes included STS risk-adjusted, recalibrated observed-to-expected ratios for 30-day or operative mortality and major morbidity/mortality.

Results

Of 51,739 patients, 11,705 (22.6%) underwent multi-arterial grafting of whom 2836 (24.2%) were elderly and 1896 (16.2%) were female. Multiarterial grafting increased over-time (2014:7.5%; 2024: 42.8%, p < .001), driven largely by the use of radial artery (2014: 5.7% vs 2024: 33.7%, p value < .001]. Utilization remained lower among female and the elderly, reaching only 32% (n = 302) and 26.8% (n = 482) in 2024, respectively. Recalibrated observed-to-expected ratios for mortality and major morbidity/mortality were similar between single arterial and any multiarterial grafting, while they were lower than expected for the radial artery group.

Conclusions

This statewide quality improvement initiative was associated with a safe increase in multiarterial grafting overall, and among the elderly and women; however, disparities persisted in these groups. These findings highlight the need for targeted initiatives to further expand the adoption of multiarterial grafting.

title: Two Decades of Single Ventricle Palliation: Survival Improvement and the Persistent Burden of Fontan Morbidity.
authorString: Lim JH, Kim MJ, You J.
abstractText:
Background

Population-level data on long-term outcomes after single ventricle staged palliation in East Asian cohorts are lacking. We examined era-specific trends in survival, Fontan completion, and morbidity in a Korean nationwide cohort.

Methods

This retrospective cohort study used Korean National Health Insurance Service claims data (2002-2023). Patients undergoing Stage I palliation were stratified into four calendar-period eras and followed through December 2023. Survival and morbidity were assessed by Cox regression; Fontan completion was analyzed by Fine-Gray competing risk methods and at fixed post-palliation horizons.

Results

Among 1,732 patients (median follow-up 20.0-199.9 months), adjusted mortality hazard ratios (HRs) were 0.54 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.43-0.69) and 0.35 (95% CI, 0.26-0.48) in eras 3 and 4 versus era 1 (both P<.001), with the largest gains in hypoplastic left heart syndrome. Fontan completion did not differ across eras; at 36 months, cumulative incidence was 17.3%-19.4% (P=.80). Heart failure (HR, 2.12), thromboembolism (HR, 2.37), and reintervention hazards rose in era 4, whereas arrhythmia declined (HR, 0.26). Female sex, preterm birth, and hypoplastic left heart syndrome independently predicted mortality, as did socioeconomic position below the highest stratum in a categorical specification.

Conclusions

Over two decades, survival after single ventricle palliation improved substantially in Korea, most strikingly in hypoplastic left heart syndrome, whereas Fontan attainment did not improve at a common horizon. The rise in heart failure and thromboembolism, together with higher mortality below the highest socioeconomic stratum, identifies a growing population requiring lifelong surveillance and targeted support.

title: Using an Artificial Intelligence ECG-Derived Biological Age for Risk Stratification of Patients Undergoing Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement.
authorString: Sawma T, Schaff HV, Arghami A, Danesh S, Rowse PG, Dearani JA, Aslahishahri M, Friedman P, Attia ZI, Greason KL, Crestanello JA.
abstractText:
Background

Artificial intelligence using a convolutional neural network can estimate patients' age from ECG data. We aimed to assess the prognostic value of AI ECG-derived age in predicting outcomes following surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR).

Methods

Preoperative ECGs obtained within 30 days before surgery were used to calculate AI ECG-derived age in 5,503 patients undergoing SAVR. Age gap was defined as AI ECG-derived age minus chronological age. Associations between age gap and postoperative outcomes were evaluated. A threshold of age gap >5 years was used to define advanced ECG age.

Results

Median chronological age was 73.2(65.3-79.5) years, and AI ECG-derived age was 70.4(64.6-74.8) years. Median age gap was -3.0(-8.4 to 2.5) years. In 35.7% of patients, AI ECG-derived age exceeded chronological age, and in 16.7% it was >5 years. Patients with advanced ECG age were younger but had higher rates of diabetes, renal failure, and current smoking and had higher BMI. Postoperatively, advanced ECG age was associated with increased risk of 30-day mortality (OR 1.69, p=0.043), blood transfusion (OR 1.44, p<0.001), gastrointestinal complications (OR 1.83, p=0.022), prolonged ventilation (OR 1.41, p=0.047), higher postoperative creatinine levels (B +0.09 mg/dL, p=0.014), longer ICU stay (B +13.3 hours, p=0.001), and longer hospital stay (B +0.7 days, p=0.007). Advanced ECG age was also independently associated with increased long-term mortality (HR 1.25, p=0.003).

Conclusions

AI ECG-derived age identifies a subgroup of SAVR patients with advanced physiological aging. An elevated age gap is independently associated with worse early postoperative outcomes and reduced long-term survival following SAVR.

title: Higher HDL-C is associated with less acute kidney injury-associated delirium after CABG surgery.
authorString: Patzwall A, Smith DK, Smith LE.
abstractText: Delirium occurs after 15-52% of cardiac surgeries and is associated with an increased risk of long-term cognitive impairment and death. HDL-C is associated with less delirium after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) surgery in patients ≥65 years old. Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a risk factor for delirium after cardiac surgery. We hypothesized that higher preoperative HDL-C is associated with less AKI-associated delirium after CABG, particularly in patients ≥65 years old. We analyzed 13,027 medical records from CABG patients. To address potential selection bias arising from substantial missingness in HDL-C measurements, we calculated a propensity score representing the probability of HDL-C availability based on age, date of surgery, and preoperative comorbidities including hypertension, type 1 (T1D) and 2 diabetes mellitus (T2D) and chronic kidney disease (CKD). Propensity score adjusted multivariable logistic regression models were used to estimate associations between HDL-C and AKI, delirium, and AKI-associated delirium. Higher HDL-C was associated with less AKI after CABG among all patients with an available HDL-C measurement (OR 0.92, p=0.04, n=3716) and in patients ≥65 years old (OR 0.86, p=0.004, n=2120). Higher HDL-C was not associated with less delirium (p=0.17) after CABG in the entire cohort but in patients ≥65 years old it was associated with less delirium (OR 0.80, p=0.046, n=2120) and with less AKI-associated delirium (OR 0.58, p=0.007, n=2120). These hypothesis-generating associations suggest that HDL-C warrants further study as a risk factor for AKI and delirium after CABG, particularly in elderly patients at high risk for both AKI and delirium.

title: Effect of natural variants causing primary carnitine deficiency on the OCTN2 carnitine transporter.
authorString: Frigeni M, Ingoglia F, Balakrishnan B, Corona RI, Longo N.
abstractText: Primary carnitine deficiency results from defective OCTN2 carnitine transporters encoded by the SLC22A5 gene. Patients can present early in life with acute metabolic decompensation or later with skeletal and cardiac myopathy or sudden death from arrhythmia. Most identified pathogenic variants in the SLC22A5 gene are missense, but the mechanisms by which they impair OCTN2 activity remain unclear. Pathogenic variants (n=65) identified in affected patients were stably expressed in Chinese Hamster Ovary cells and assessed for their effect on carnitine transport, OCTN2 protein abundance, and subcellular localization. Functional analysis revealed two distinct mechanisms: pathogenic variants affecting hydrophilic domains were more likely to result in reduced OCTN2 protein abundance and retention of OCTN2 transporters in the cytoplasm, thus disrupting plasma membrane trafficking. By contrast, variants in transmembrane domains were more likely to retain normal OCTN2 protein abundance and membrane localization, but impaired carnitine transport activity. Incubation of selected variants with the molecular chaperone 4-phenylbutyric acid resulted in increased protein abundance for the mutants as well as the wild-type OCTN2 transporters. Carnitine transport activity improved in most variants affecting hydrophilic domains, possibly reflecting improved plasma membrane trafficking. By contrast, most of the variants localized in transmembrane domains showed little to no functional improvement despite enhanced plasma membrane localization, indicating irreversible structural or catalytic defects. This study underscores the necessity of precision medicine approaches to address both trafficking and functional deficiencies in disorders of membrane transport and provides a framework for developing targeted therapies tailored to patients' genetic profiles.

title: Anemia and Iron Deficiency Across Renal Function in Hospitalized Heart Failure: Insights From OPPORTUNITIES Registry.
authorString: Fazzini L, Giaccherini C, Spagnolin M, D'Elia E, Chiesa E, Zucchi A, Gavazzi A, Gori M, Senni M.
abstractText:
Background

Anemia and iron deficiency (ID) are highly prevalent among patients hospitalized for heart failure (HHF). Their prognostic contributions in the acute setting, particularly across kidney function, remain incompletely understood.

Objectives

We investigated the association of anemia, transferrin saturation (TSAT), and ID according to kidney function, with postdischarge outcomes in HHF patients.

Methods

Consecutive HHF patients enrolled in the OPPORTUNITIES registry with available hemoglobin and TSAT at discharge. The primary endpoint was HF-free survival, a composite of all-cause death, urgent heart transplantation, heart failure (HF) hospitalization, and urgent emergency department referral for HF worsening at 12 months. Adjusted Cox regression models were applied.

Results

A total of 454 HHF patients were included. The median age was 77 (69-83); 37.9% were women, and 55% of patients were anemic. Anemic patients were older and exhibited a greater burden of comorbidities. Hemoglobin and TSAT showed a modest positive correlation overall (rho = 0.276, P < 0.001), which disappeared in patients with estimated glomerular filtration rate <30 mL/min/1.73 m2. Lower hemoglobin was independently associated with a higher risk (adjusted HR: 0.82; 95% CI: 0.75-0.91; P < 0.001), whereas TSAT was not independently predictive. A significant interaction between hemoglobin and renal function was observed (P = 0.025), indicating that the hemoglobin effect varied according to kidney function. Among ID definitions, only TSAT <20% independently identified patients at an increased risk (HR: 1.44; 95% CI: 1.03-2.03; P = 0.035).

Conclusions

In HHF patients, the prognostic relevance of anemia varies according to renal function. TSAT <20% was the only ID definition independently associated with adverse outcomes.

title: Left Ventricular Unloading With Self-Expanding Pump During Venoarterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation in Acute Myocardial Infarction.
authorString: Cai W, Ma J, Bai N, Xi Q, Wang IW, Bai M, Lu A.

journal.title: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)

abstractText: Increased left ventricular (LV) afterload and distension during venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) support may impede myocardial perfusion in acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Active LV unloading has been associated with improved outcomes. We report the first clinical use of a self-expanding percutaneous ventricular assist device (NyokAssist; magAssist, Suzhou, China) for LV unloading during VA-ECMO in a 56 year old man with AMI-related cardiogenic shock (CS). Successful coronary angiography and percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) of the culprit left circumflex (LCx) lesion were performed with NyokAssist + VA-ECMO support. The patient was successfully weaned from VA-ECMO on post-procedure day 5 and remained on NyokAssist support alone for an additional 7 days before being transferred on VA-ECMO to a heart transplant center for consideration of advanced heart failure therapies due to limited myocardial recovery. No device-related complications were observed. This case demonstrates the technical feasibility of early implementation of a combined VA-ECMO and NyokAssist support strategy, enabling LV unloading, temporary hemodynamic stabilization, end-organ improvement, and VA-ECMO decannulation in a patient with AMI-related CS. As this report describes a single-patient experience, further clinical studies are warranted to define the safety, efficacy, and potential role of the use of NyokAssist in combination with VA-ECMO in the management of AMI-related CS.

title: Task Force 7: Clinical Considerations for the Care of Competitive Athletes with Aortopathy or Spontaneous Coronary Artery Dissection.
authorString: Churchill TW, Braverman AC, D'Ascenzi F, Kim JH, Baggish AL, Levine BD, Phelan D.

journal.title: Medicine and science in sports and exercise

abstractText: Aortic disease represents an uncommon but important cause of sudden death among young competitive athletes. Important etiologies of aortic dilation in this population include bicuspid aortic valve, heritable thoracic aortic disease, and tricuspid aortic valve with unexplained aortic dilation. This document outlines a structured approach to the evaluation of young athletes with aortic disease with an emphasis on precise measurement of aortic dimensions with regular surveillance, careful evaluation for underlying etiologies, and shared decision-making. For each condition, we delineate low, moderate, and high-risk phenotypes and provide tailored guidance regarding sport participation. Additionally, guidance for athletes with spontaneous coronary artery dissection is also reviewed.

title: Task Force 6: Clinical Considerations for the Care of Competitive Athletes with Congenital Heart Disease.
authorString: Brothers JA, Dean PN, Molossi S, Kim JH, Baggish AL, Levine BD, Shafer KM.

journal.title: Medicine and science in sports and exercise

abstractText: Athletes with congenital heart disease are commonly restricted from competitive sports participation based on limited data regarding exercise-induced sudden cardiac death risk. For most athletes, the myriad of benefits derived from participating in competitive sports outweighs the risk. This document reviews the cardiac assessment that may be considered for children, adolescents, and young adults with congenital heart disease. By utilizing anatomy, physiology, symptoms, and cardiac testing, together with shared decision-making, the authors propose a strategy to help guide medical providers advising their patients on sports participation.

title: Task Force 2: Clinical Considerations for the Pre-Participation Cardiac Evaluation of Competitive Athletes.
authorString: Krishnan S, Drezner JA, Sharma S, Claessen G, Phelan DM, Pelliccia A, Kim JH, Baggish AL, Levine BD, Papadakis M.

journal.title: Medicine and science in sports and exercise

abstractText: Sudden cardiac arrest (SCA) is the leading cause of sudden death during sports and exercise. Pre-participation cardiac screening is one component of the comprehensive pre-participation evaluation (PPE), aiming to identify previously unrecognized cardiovascular conditions that may increase the risk of SCA/D during sports participation. It warrants careful planning to maximize efficacy and minimize potential harms, including exacerbating health disparities. Core elements of the PPE include a focused history & physical (H&P) and the 12-lead electrocardiogram conducted by well-trained clinicians, with readily accessible expert consultation for secondary evaluation when necessary. As no primary prevention screening approach provides absolute protection against SCA, a well-developed emergency action plan is an essential part of comprehensive cardiovascular care for athletes of all levels.

title: Association Between Invasive Coronary Investigation Before Permanent Pacemaker Implantation and Mortality in a Historical Cohort with a One-Year Follow-Up: CorInPace Study.
authorString: Silvestrini TL, Ronsoni RM, Lima HDN, Passuello GG, Fontoura SDCP, Leiria TLL.
abstractText:
Introduction

Permanent pacemaker (PPM) implantation is standard therapy for symptomatic bradyarrhythmias. In emergencies, limited assessment may lead to underdiagnosis of concomitant coronary artery disease (CAD).

Objective

To evaluate the impact of coronary cineangiography (CAG) before urgent PPM implantation on mortality.

Methods

This cohort included patients undergoing urgent PPM implantation between July 2016 and June 2021, divided into those undergoing CAG (Group A) and those not undergoing CAG (Group B). The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality; secondary endpoints included mortality/readmission, acute coronary syndrome (ACS), and hospital stay.

Results

Of 895 patients, 841 were included (Group A: 160; Group B: 681). Group A patients were younger (70.2 vs. 75.2 years; P < 0.001), more frequently male (63.1% vs. 51.8%; P = 0.010), had more CAD (36.2% vs. 19%; P < 0.001), and less frequently had estimated glomerular filtration rate < 45 ml/min/1.73 m2 (10.2% vs. 22.9%; P < 0.001). Mortality (hazard ratio [HR] 0.96, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.56 - 1.66; P = 0.898) and mortality/readmission (HR 1.05, 95% CI 0.74 - 1.50; P = 0.776) did not differ between groups. Multivariate analysis showed no significant impact of CAG on either outcome. ACS was more frequent in Group A (7.5% vs. 2.7%; P = 0.005), and hospital stay was shorter in Group B (6 vs. 9 days; P < 0.001).

Conclusion

In our study, CAG before PPM implantation was not associated with mortality or mortality/readmission but was associated with longer hospitalization and a higher incidence of ACS.

title: Impact of Surgical Timing on Mortality in Infective Endocarditis Patients with Neurological Complications.
authorString: Kızılay M, Yıldız Z.
abstractText:
Introduction

The optimal timing of cardiac surgery in infective endocarditis (IE) patients with neurological complications remains controversial.

Objective

To evaluate the effects of early surgical intervention compared with medical therapy on in-hospital and one-year mortality, highlighting the prognostic value of neurological severity and clinical variables.

Methods

This retrospective study included 109 patients with neurological complications out of a total of 452 patients diagnosed with infective endocarditis at our hospital between January 2013 and December 2023. The patients were divided into a surgical group (n = 48) and a medical therapy group (n = 61). Surgical cases were further classified as early (≤ 7 days) and late (> 7 days). Demographic data, echocardiographic findings, vegetation size (≥ 1 cm), mobility, causative microorganisms, and stroke severity were assessed using the National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) method (mild-moderate-severe). Mortality predictors over a one-year period were evaluated using multivariate logistic regression.Result: When comparing one-year in-hospital and post-discharge mortality between the medical and surgical patient groups, mortality was significantly higher in the medically treated group (54.1% and 46.4%, respectively) compared to the surgical group (16.7% and 0%, respectively, P < 0.001). No significant difference was observed between the early and late surgical subgroups. Age and NIHSS were independent predictors of in-hospital mortality, while age, treatment type, NIHSS, white blood cells, and hemoglobin were associated with one-year mortality.

Conclusion

In IE patients with neurological complications, early cardiac surgery, when carefully selected and managed using a multidisciplinary approach, does not increase mortality compared to late surgery and may improve long-term survival.

title: Preoperative Dependent Functional Status Is Associated with Worse 30-Day Pulmonary Complications in Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement: An Insight from the American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program Database From 2005-2021.
authorString: Li R, Prastein DJ.
abstractText:
Introduction

While current cardiac surgery risk scores do not account for preoperative functional status, it has been linked to adverse outcomes in transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). However, in surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR), preoperative functional status remains underexplored.

Objective

To examine the impact of preoperative functional status on 30-day SAVR outcomes to provide insights into clinical decision-making and postoperative care. Methods: Patients undergoing SAVR were identified from the American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program database from 2005 to 2021. A 1:3 propensity-score matching was applied to patients with dependent (DFS) and independent (IFS) functional status. Thirty-day outcomes were assessed.

Results

After propensity-score matching, DFS and IFS patients showed similar mortality (11.11% vs. 9.42%, P = 0.39) and major adverse cardiovascular events (9.91% vs. 9.11%, P = 0.66). Patients with DFS had higher risks of pulmonary complications (29.43% vs. 21.64%, P < 0.01) including pneumonia (13.21% vs. 9.21%, P = 0.04) and prolonged mechanical ventilation over 48 hours (25.83% vs. 15.42%, P < 0.01) but lower bleeding requiring transfusion (51.65% vs. 67.49%, P < 0.01). DFS patients were more likely to be discharged not to home (71.52% vs. 47.75%, P < 0.01) and had longer operation time (315.2 ± 130.5 vs. 293.5 ± 119.8 min, P < 0.01) and LOS (18.47 ± 14.30 vs. 15.07 ± 12.83 days, P < 0.01).

Conclusion

While SAVR is relatively safe in eligible DFS patients considering its mortality and cardiac outcomes, it is imperative to emphasize preoperative functional status assessments and closely monitor postoperative pulmonary complications.

title: The Relationship Between Preoperative Hemoglobin, Albumin, Lymphocyte, and Platelet Score and Postoperative Outcomes in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Undergoing Coronary Artery Bypass Surgery.
authorString: Yucel C, Ketenciler S, Gokkurt Y, Ozgol İ, Yildiz S, Koyuncu AO, Oksen D, Yesiltas MA.
abstractText: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) significantly increases the risk of morbidity and mortality following coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). Identifying preoperative prognostic indicators is critical for improving postoperative outcomes in this patient population. This study aimed to investigate the relationship between the preoperative Hemoglobin, Albumin, Lymphocyte, and Platelet (HALP) score and postoperative complications and mortality in T2DM patients undergoing isolated CABG surgery. A total of 675 T2DM patients who underwent isolated CABG surgery between 2018 and 2024 were retrospectively analyzed. Patients were grouped according to their preoperative HALP scores. Demographic characteristics, postoperative complications, intensive care and hospital stay durations, revascularization needs, and one-year mortality rates were compared between groups. Patients with lower HALP scores experienced significantly higher rates of postoperative infections, pneumonia, renal dysfunction, longer intensive care unit/hospital stays, and increased one-year mortality (P < 0.001). These findings indicate a strong correlation between nutritional/immune status and surgical outcomes in diabetic patients. Preoperative HALP score may serve as a reliable, cost-effective associated factor of postoperative complications and mortality in T2DM patients undergoing CABG. Incorporating HALP scoring into routine preoperative assessment could enhance risk stratification and perioperative management strategies.

title: Risk Factors of Clinically Relevant Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding in Cardiovascular Intensive Care Unit.
authorString: Polat A, Gulmez S.
abstractText:
Introduction

Upper gastrointestinal bleeding (UGIB) is a serious but underexplored complication in cardiovascular intensive care unit (CV-ICU) patients, with often self-limiting, yet clinically relevant, worsening outcomes.

Objective

This study aimed to identify independent predictors of new-onset UGIB in CV-ICU patients.

Methods

In this retrospective cohort study, 50 patients who underwent bedside upper gastrointestinal endoscopy in the CV-ICU due to overt UGIB were analyzed. Clinical data, laboratory parameters, and intensive care unit (ICU)-related variables were compared between patients with clinically relevant and non-relevant UGIB. Logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent risk factors.

Results

Clinically significant UGIB occurred in nine patients (18%), with a mortality rate of 77.8% (7/9). Multivariate analysis revealed that Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation (APACHE) II score (odds ratio [OR] 1.47, P = 0.018), Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score (OR 1.08, P = 0.045), and ICU stay before bleeding (OR 1.49, P = 0.049) were independent risk factors. Receiver operating characteristic analysis showed strong discriminative ability of APACHE II (area under the curve [AUC] 0.927, sensitivity 100%, specificity 85.4%), whereas SOFA demonstrated moderate performance (AUC 0.772, sensitivity 77.8%, specificity 78.0%). The use of anticoagulants, antiplatelets, or dual therapy was not significantly associated with clinically relevant bleeding (P > 0.05).

Conclusion

Higher SOFA and APACHE II scores, as well as prolonged ICU stay, were independent risk factors for clinically significant new-onset UGIB in CV-ICU patients. APACHE II provided superior predictive accuracy compared with SOFA. Clinically relevant UGIB was strongly linked to mortality, while antithrombotic therapy type showed no significant effect.

title: Sleep duration and cause-specific mortality among US adults with heart disease: A NHIS-NDI linkage cohort study.
authorString: Adebile TV, Oloyede T, Azu E, Olagunju M, Asifat O, Paul TM, Ipede O, Abwa W, Biswas P, Yu L.
abstractText: Sleep duration is increasingly recognized as a component of cardiovascular health, yet its prognostic significance among adults with established heart disease remains unclear. We examined associations between sleep duration and mortality among US adults with heart disease. We analyzed data from 3,287 adults with heart disease participating in the 2004 National Health Interview Survey linked to the National Death Index through December 31, 2019. Sleep duration was categorized as ≤6 hours, 7-8 hours, and ≥9 hours. Cox proportional hazards models stratified by variables violating the proportional hazards assumption estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for all-cause, heart-related, and non-heart-related mortality. Restricted cubic splines evaluated nonlinear dose-response relationships. During 15 years of follow-up, 49.4% of participants died, including 16.7% from heart-related causes and 32.6% from non-heart-related causes. Compared with 7-8 hours of sleep, long sleep duration (≥9 hours) was associated with higher risks of all-cause mortality (HR:1.51 [95% CI:1.32-1.73]), heart-related mortality (HR:1.53 [95% CI:1.22-1.92]), and non-heart-related mortality (HR:1.50 [95% CI:1.27-1.77]). Restricted cubic spline analyses demonstrated nonlinear associations, with the lowest predicted mortality risk occurring at 6-7 hours. Findings remained robust across multiple sensitivity analyses and age and sex subgroups. Among US adults with heart disease, long sleep duration was consistently associated with higher risks of all-cause, heart-related, and non-heart-related mortality. Sleep duration may represent a simple marker of residual risk that could enhance risk stratification among adults living with heart disease.

title: Clinical effectiveness of outpatient cardiac rehabilitation according to myocardial injury after acute myocardial infarction.
authorString: Kataoka T, Kawabata R, Watarai K, Terashima S, Takeda S, Matsunaga S, Takahara K, Mamiya K, Harada K, Nagao T, Shinoda N, Harada K, Murohara T.
abstractText:
Background

Cardiac rehabilitation (CR) is recommended after acute myocardial infarction (AMI), but whether its benefit differs by infarct size remains uncertain. We examined whether the effectiveness of CR varies according to peak creatine phosphokinase (CPK), a surrogate marker of myocardial injury.

Methods

We retrospectively analyzed 535 AMI survivors who underwent emergency percutaneous coronary intervention between January 2015 and November 2025. Patients were divided into CR and non‑CR groups. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as all‑cause death, recurrent myocardial infarction, or heart failure hospitalization. Patients were stratified by peak CPK (<2000 vs. ≥2000 U/L), and Kaplan-Meier and Cox analyses were performed.

Results

Among 535 patients, 165 (31%) participated in CR. CR was associated with lower MACE incidence in the overall cohort (hazard ratio [HR] 0.23, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.14-0.81, p = 0.01). In the high‑CPK subgroup, CR significantly reduced MACE (HR 0.21, 95% CI 0.04-0.96, p = 0.04), whereas the low‑CPK subgroup showed only nonsignificant trend. Similar findings were observed in patients who underwent cardiopulmonary exercise testing.

Conclusions

Outpatient CR was associated with improved outcomes after AMI, with greater benefit in patients with higher peak CPK. Myocardial injury severity may help identify patients most likely to benefit from CR.

title: Association of Second Anti-hypertensive Agent with Outcomes in People with CKD on ACEi/ARB Therapy.
authorString: Gregg LP, Perkins A, Yang H, Vu C, Nambi V, Winkelmayer WC, Hedayati SS, Navaneethan SD, Alvarez CA.

journal.title: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology : JASN

abstractText:
Background

Angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors (ACEi) and angiotensin receptor blockers (ARB) are first-line treatment for hypertension in chronic kidney disease (CKD). However, guidelines do not recommend subsequent medication classes if additional blood pressure-lowering effect is desired.

Methods

This target trial emulation using national outpatient data from the Veterans Health Administration from January 1, 2010, to December 31, 2016, included adults with non-dialysis CKD stages G1-G5 on an ACEi/ARB who initiated treatment with a second antihypertensive medication, classified as a thiazide diuretic, loop diuretic, calcium channel blocker, or β-blocker. Outcomes included composite cardiovascular events (fatal or nonfatal myocardial infarction or stroke, hospitalization for heart failure, coronary revascularization), all-cause death, and composite kidney outcomes (dialysis initiation, kidney transplantation, sustained creatinine doubling). Clinically important characteristics were included as covariates in the analysis.

Results

Of 150,369 individuals already on ACEi/ARB treatment, 45,836 (30%) were prescribed a thiazide diuretic, 17,589 (12%) a loop diuretic, 33,172 (22%) a calcium channel blocker, and 53,772 (36%) a β-blocker. Those receiving thiazide diuretics and calcium channel blockers had the highest baseline blood pressure. Those receiving loop diuretics were more likely to have more advanced CKD or heart failure. Over a median (IQR) follow-up of 1282 (621, 1979) days, compared to thiazide diuretics, cardiovascular event risk was higher for calcium channel blockers, aHR 1.18 (95% CI 1.15-1.22), β-blockers, aHR 1.63 (95% CI 1.58-1.67), and loop diuretics, aHR 1.97 (95% CI 1.90-2.04). Composite kidney outcomes were also higher with calcium channel blockers, aHR 1.42 (95% CI 1.33-1.52), β-blockers, aHR 1.13 (95% CI 1.06-1.21), and loop diuretics, aHR 1.98 (95% CI 1.83-2.15).

Conclusions

Adding a thiazide diuretic rather than a calcium channel blocker, β-blocker, or loop diuretic on top of ACEi/ARB treatment was associated with favorable clinical outcomes among people with CKD.

title: Clinician-Initiated Palliative Care Referral Versus Advanced Heart Failure Referral Criteria in Hospitalized Patients With Heart Failure: A Retrospective Study.
authorString: Chen YW, Huang HL, Juang JM, Cheng SY, Chen YH, Chen JY, Wang PY, Chen ST, Lee CY, Tang CC.
abstractText:
Aim

The overall aim was to examine clinician-initiated palliative care referral practices in relation to referrals indicated by the advanced heart failure (AHF) referral criteria among hospitalized patients with heart failure.

Design

A retrospective observational study.

Methods

Medical records of 450 adults hospitalized with heart failure during 2023-2024 were reviewed. Clinician-initiated palliative care referral was compared with AHF referral criteria. Firth logistic regression examined referral-associated factors. Six-month mortality from the index admission was a pragmatic prognostic endpoint, not a measure of palliative care needs.

Results

Among 450 patients, clinician-initiated palliative care referral was uncommon, and most patients meeting the advanced heart failure referral criteria were not referred. Agreement between the two approaches was low. Metastatic cancer and New York Heart Association functional class were associated with referral in the adjusted model. The referral criteria showed greater sensitivity for six-month mortality, whereas clinician-initiated referral showed greater specificity.

Conclusion

Clinician-initiated referral and the AHF referral criteria identified different proportions of hospitalized patients with heart failure. Their differing performance for six-month mortality supports further prospective evaluation; clinical utility for identifying palliative care needs remains unestablished.

Implications for the profession and/or patient care

The findings identify an opportunity for nurses and multidisciplinary teams to assess needs among criteria-positive patients without specialist referral. Whether screening improves care requires prospective evaluation.

Impact

The study documents differences between clinician-initiated referral and AHF referral criteria in a broader hospitalized heart failure population. It provides a basis for evaluating systematic needs assessment alongside existing referral practices.

Reporting method

Reporting followed the RECORD extension of the STROBE statement.

Patient or public contribution

This study did not include patient or public involvement in its design, conduct, or reporting.

title: Painless Stanford type A aortic dissection presenting with isolated bilateral lower-limb neurological deficits: a case report.
authorString: Fang D, Zhao B, Li J, Wu B.

journal.title: The Egyptian heart journal : (EHJ) : official bulletin of the Egyptian Society of Cardiology

abstractText:
Introduction

Stanford type A aortic dissection (AAD) constitutes a life-threatening cardiovascular emergency. Painless AAD manifesting exclusively as isolated bilateral lower-limb neurological deficits represents an uncommon but recognised presentation of aortic dissection that is prone to misdiagnosis. This case report adds real-world clinical data regarding atypical AAD and delivers practical diagnostic and surgical insights for front-line clinicians.

Main symptoms and important clinical findings

A 58-year-old Han Chinese female presented with acute-onset bilateral lower-limb numbness and weakness lasting one hour, in the absence of chest, back or abdominal pain. Physical examination uncovered an inter-arm systolic blood-pressure discrepancy together with bilateral lower-limb motor weakness (3/5). Emergency non-contrast chest-abdominal CT identified the aortic double-lumen sign and inward-displaced aortic wall calcified plaques, whereas bilateral distal peripheral pulses remained preserved.

Main diagnoses, therapeutic interventions, and outcomes

Painless Stanford type A aortic dissection complicated by suspected transient spinal cord malperfusion was diagnosed. Following urgent inter-hospital transfer, the patient underwent emergency Bentall procedure combined with aortic arch reconstruction and frozen elephant-trunk graft implantation, with a distal landing zone in the proximal descending thoracic aorta. Her bilateral lower-limb neurological deficits had fully resolved by postoperative day 2. A residual chronic dissection with a thrombosed false lumen persisted distally below the stent-graft and remained stable without interval enlargement. Six-month follow-up confirmed complete functional recovery without residual neurological sequelae or proximal dissection recurrence.

Conclusion

Undiagnosed painless Stanford type A aortic dissection presenting with isolated bilateral lower-limb neurological deficits is associated with substantial mortality. Routine bilateral upper-arm blood-pressure measurement and recognition of calcification displacement signs on non-contrast CT facilitate early clinical suspicion. Timely confirmation by CTA and urgent comprehensive surgical reconstruction are essential to reverse end-organ malperfusion and optimize neurological as well as survival outcomes.

title: Non-cardiac comorbidities and functional impairment in acute heart failure: a hospital-wide real-world cohort study (COMPACT-HF).
authorString: Melchio R, Galliano R, Marro S, Dupuis A, Ruocco I, Posillico F, Ferrua A, Mao F, Dogliani B, Candela C, Dutto N, Giamello JD, Abbona A, Benso P, Pontremoli R, Bracco C, Fenoglio LM.
abstractText: Acute heart failure (AHF) is a leading cause of hospitalization among older adults and is associated with non-cardiac comorbidities (NCCs) and functional impairment. Their prognostic and therapeutic implications remain incompletely characterized. COMPACT-HF was a retrospective cohort study of adults discharged after hospitalization for AHF at a tertiary teaching hospital in 2023. Comorbidity burden was assessed using the age-adjusted Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI) and predefined NCCs. Functional impairment was defined as loss of ≥ 1 basic activity of daily living (ADL). Primary outcome was 12-month all-cause mortality. We included 456 patients (mean age 82.6 ± 8.6 years; 50% male); 96% had ≥ 1 NCC and 48% had functional impairment. Twelve-month mortality was 31%. CCI was independently associated with mortality (HR 1.17 per point; 95% CI 1.07-1.27, p < 0.001), while functional impairment provided additional prognostic information beyond comorbidity burden. Advanced chronic kidney disease, dementia, and active malignancy were among the NCCs most strongly associated with mortality. Among patients with reduced or mildly reduced ejection fraction, dementia, advanced chronic kidney disease, chronic lung disease, and functional impairment were associated with lower prescription of ≥ 3 of 4 guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) classes, whereas CCI was not; GDMT prescription also varied substantially according to discharge ward. In this hospital-wide real-world cohort of patients discharged alive after AHF hospitalization, NCCs and functional impairment were highly prevalent and associated with mortality, while specific clinical conditions and discharge ward were associated with GDMT implementation. Integrating comorbidity and functional assessment may improve risk stratification and support a holistic approach to AHF management.

title: GSTM1 Deficiency Exacerbates Cisplatin-Induced Kidney Injury via Increased Oxidative Stress.
authorString: Chen L, Ayon RJ, Mekhaiel KE, Beane T, Zhao Y, Mone Y, Wang YT, Alnuaimi A, Ruiz P, Le TH.
abstractText: Cisplatin, a potent chemotherapeutic agent, is highly effective in various cancers but its use is significantly limited by kidney injury, occurring in approximately 30% of patients. Cisplatin-induced kidney injury compromises optimal dosing, reducing cancer survival, and leads to permanent eGFR decline, increasing chronic kidney disease (CKD) risk and cardiovascular mortality. Increased reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation is central to cisplatin nephrotoxicity. Glutathione-S-transferase Mu-1 (GSTM1), a phase II detoxification enzyme, protects against oxidative stress. A common GSTM1 null deletion variant is highly prevalent in human populations. We hypothesized that GSTM1 deficiency increases susceptibility to cisplatin nephrotoxicity. Using a clinically relevant low-dose, repeat-cycle cisplatin mouse model, we found that cisplatin treatment significantly induces renal Gstm1 expression in wild-type mice, suggesting a protective role. Gstm1 knockout mice exhibited more severe kidney injury, evidenced by elevated creatinine, BUN, KIM-1, 4-HNE adducts, and histological damage. This exacerbated injury was associated with significantly higher renal ROS and NOX2 expression and mitochondrial ROS. In vitro studies using primary mouse proximal tubular cells deficient in Gstm1 and human HK-2 cells endogenously lacking GSTM1 demonstrated that GSTM1 deficiency leads to increased mitochondrial ROS and NOX2 expression following cisplatin treatment; conversely, overexpression of GSTM1 in HK-2 cells significantly attenuated cisplatin-induced mitochondrial ROS and NOX2 expression. Furthermore, GSTM1 protected against NF-κB activation and cell death. Our findings establish GSTM1 as a critical cytoprotective factor against cisplatin nephrotoxicity, mitigating oxidative stress, inflammation, and apoptosis, and identify the highly prevalent GSTM1 null variant as a potential genetic risk factor for cisplatin-induced kidney injury.

title: Sex differences in myocardial ketone oxidation capacity in cardiometabolic disease with coincident ischemic heart disease
authorString: Bugga P, Stoner M, Manning J, Mushala B, Sharifi-Sanjani M, Bhattarai N, Scott I.
abstractText:
Background:

Myocardial infarction (MI) in patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is associated with worse outcomes than MI in individuals without HFpEF. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying this increased vulnerability remain poorly understood. We investigated sex differences in cardiac ketone body (KB) metabolism in patients with diabetes-associated ischemic heart disease, and in a mouse model of HFpEF complicated by MI (HFpEF-MI).

Methods:

Cardiac BDH1 and OXCT1 expression was assessed in male and female patients with diabetes, with or without ischemic heart disease. Male and female mice received a high-fat diet and L-NAME for 10 weeks to induce HFpEF, followed by coronary artery ligation to induce MI. Glucose tolerance, cardiac function, survival, cardiac KB oxidative capacity, and circulating KB levels were evaluated.

Results:

Cardiac BDH1 and OXCT1 abundance was significantly reduced in male patients with diabetes-associated ischemic heart disease but preserved in female patients. In mice, 10 weeks of high-fat diet and L-NAME administration increased fasting blood glucose and impaired glucose tolerance. MI reduced systolic function in control and HFpEF mice of both sexes. Male HFpEF-MI mice exhibited higher mortality than female HFpEF-MI mice. Consistent with our human results, male HFpEF-MI mice showed reduced cardiac ketolytic enzyme expression alongside elevated circulating KB levels, whereas female mice maintained cardiac KB oxidative capacity.

Conclusion:

Reduced cardiac ketolytic enzyme expression and impaired KB oxidative capacity are associated with greater mortality in male HFpEF-MI mice, whereas female mice exhibit preserved KB oxidative capacity and improved survival. Similar sex differences in ketolytic enzyme expression were observed in patients with diabetes-associated ischemic heart disease. These findings identify cardiac ketone metabolism as a potential therapeutic target warranting further investigation in HFpEF complicated by MI.

title: LRPPRC gene replacement therapy preserves cardiac function and prevents premature death in a mouse model of mitochondrial disease
authorString: Zanin S, Lager F, Simon-Sola M, Gaborit C, Renault G, Mingozzi F, Rotig A, Cavazzana M, Metodiev M, Ruzzenente B.
abstractText: Pathogenic variants in LRPPRC disrupt mitochondrial gene expression, causing severe and incurable mitochondrial disease with neurological involvement accompanied by hepatopathy or cardiomyopathy. The development for gene therapy for LRPPRC-linked disease is hindered by the large LRPPRC coding sequence exceeding AAV cargo capacity when combined with classical regulatory elements. Here, we engineered compact single rAAV9 vectors expressing human or mouse LRPPRC and administered them intravenously to heart and skeletal muscle-specific Lrpprc knockout mice. This approach restored cardiac LRPPRC expression, preserved oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) function, prevented cardiomyopathy and markedly extended survival. While skeletal muscle rescue was partial, the therapy effectively prevented fatal cardiac dysfunction. These findings provide the first in vivo proof-of-concept that AAV-mediated LRPPRC gene replacement can preserve OXPHOS function and prevent lethal cardiomyopathy, supporting its potential as a therapeutic strategy for mitochondrial disease linked to LRPPRC deficiency.

title: Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices of Advance Care Planning in Patients with Neurosurgical Conditions and Their Caregivers
authorString: Huynh VA, Lim MJR, Ong SE, Lim A, Koh GCH, Foong PS.
abstractText:
Introduction:

Advance care planning (ACP) enables quality end-of-life (EOL) care that reflects patients' values and preferences. However, ACP remains limited among individuals with neurosurgical conditions — such as stroke, glioma, or metastatic brain tumours — who often experience rapid decline and short prognoses. When ACP discussions occur only after cognitive deterioration or acute events, opportunities for meaningful conversations are lost. This study aims to assess the baseline knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) of ACP among neurosurgical patients and their caregivers in Singapore.

Methods:

We conducted a cross-sectional survey of 30 patients with symptomatic intracerebral haemorrhage (SICH) or brain tumours at the National University Hospital and their caregivers. Using validated ACP engagement questionnaires, we assessed participants' KAP, and readiness on 5-point Likert scales (1 lowest - 5 best), alongside nine ACP knowledge statements.

Results:

Patients demonstrated below-average ACP knowledge (mean = 4.1 / 9) and largely neutral attitudes (3.2 / 5) and perceptions (3.1 / 5). Misconceptions were common, including beliefs that ACP documents are legally binding, that preferred care cannot be delivered without ACP, and that ACP is solely a doctor's responsibility. Consequently, both patients and caregivers showed low levels of ACP engagement.

Conclusion:

The findings highlight the need to introduce ACP education and conversations earlier in the care journey, especially for individuals at risk of cerebrovascular or cardiovascular events. Early engagement, particularly among those with hypertension or other risk factors, presents a crucial window for preparing patients and families for future care decisions.

title: L-selectin shedding regulates post-infarction neutrophilia without altering myocardial injury or ventricular remodelling.
authorString: Maselli D, Hart S, Yang Y, Tomczyk M, Trevelin S, Cash D, Simmons C, Sawyer G, Zhang X, Giacca M, Shah A, Ivetic A.
abstractText: Myocardial infarction (MI) triggers rapid neutrophil mobilisation from the bone marrow (BM), resulting in systemic neutrophilia that is widely associated with myocardial injury. However, whether the magnitude of this response directly influences cardiac injury and subsequent ventricular remodelling remains unclear. Ectodomain shedding of L-selectin is a hallmark of neutrophil activation, although its contribution to neutrophil mobilisation following MI has not been established. Using mice expressing a non-cleavable L-selectin mutant (L(E)), we investigated the role of L-selectin shedding in post-MI neutrophilia. Under homeostatic conditions, WT and L(E) mice exhibited comparable BM neutrophil maturation and circulating neutrophil representation. Following permanent coronary ligation, however, L(E) mice exhibited markedly attenuated neutrophilia, associated with reduced circulating CXCL2 and decreased surface CXCR2 expression on BM neutrophils. Intravenous recombinant CXCL2 increased circulating neutrophil representation in WT but not L(E) mice, suggesting that impaired mobilisation cannot be explained solely by reduced ligand availability. Despite attenuated neutrophilia, myocardial neutrophil representation was comparable between genotypes at 24 hours post-MI. Circulating cardiac troponin I concentrations and MRI-quantified infarct size also showed no detectable differences. Longitudinal cardiac MRI at days 1, 14 and 28 revealed comparable ventricular structure and function, while histological scar size was similar at day 28. These findings identify L-selectin shedding as a regulator of post-MI neutrophilia and suggest that the magnitude of this systemic response can be dissociated from acute myocardial injury and subsequent ventricular remodelling.

title: Time to Blood Pressure Control and Its Determinant Factors among Hypertensive Patients at a Tertiary Teaching Hospital in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia: A Retrospective cohort study
authorString: Sitotaw A, Mulugeta S, Mersha A, Getachew Y, Endazena G, Zeleke A, Abebe Y, Dagne K, Solela G, Wereka A, Masresha G, Tesfaye B, Teferi L, Wondafrash G, Mengistu M, Tibebu T, Abiyu M, Arega B.
abstractText: Background Hypertension, affecting over 1.28 billion adults globally, and being a major public health challenge in Ethiopia, with an adult prevalence of approximately 20%, is a major contributor to cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. Achieving timely blood pressure (BP) control is critical for reducing complications; however, evidence on the time to control and its determinants within Ethiopian hospital settings remain limited. Objective To assess the time required to achieve BP control and to identify factors associated with delayed control among hypertensive patients attending the medical outpatient department at Yekatit 12 Hospital Medical College in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, from May 09, 2024 to December 09, 2025 Methods A retrospective cohort study was conducted using 12 months of patient records. Adult hypertensive patients (≥ 18 years) with at least three follow-up visits were included. Time to BP control (< 140/90 mmHg) for all hypertensive patients and (< 130/80) for hypertensive patients with diabetes and/or CKD was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier estimation and Cox proportional hazards regression. For clinical interpretability, results are presented as Time Ratios (TR), where TR > 1 indicates a longer time to control. Adjusted TRs with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) are reported. Results A total of 502 participants were included in the cohort (response rate: 96.2%). By 12 months of follow-up, the cumulative incidence of blood pressure (BP) control was 72.3% (95% CI: 68.2–76.2%), with a median time to BP control of 5.3 months. In the final adjusted model, older age (aTR = 1.06 per year, 95% CI: 1.00–1.08, p = 0.006), higher baseline systolic BP (aTR = 1.10 per mmHg, 95% CI: 1.01–1.11, p < 0.001), and the presence of diabetes (aTR = 1.39, 95% CI: 1.10–1.72, p = 0.005) were independently associated with longer time to achieve BP control. Conclusion Although most patients achieved BP control within one year, the duration was significantly prolonged for older patients, those with higher initial systolic BP, and those with diabetes. These findings support the need for risk-stratified management, including earlier treatment intensification and closer monitoring for high-risk groups to shorten the time to BP control.

title: Safety and ragional differences of Isatuximab- pomalidomide-dexamethasone combination in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma: an external validation using FAERS and Lecheng real-world database
authorString: Chen Q, You J, Huang Z, Chen X, Zhang L.
abstractText: Isatuximab approved by FDA in 2020 for the treatment of relapsed and refractory multiple myeloma (RRMM), although ICARIA-MM trial established its efficacy, leaving gap in different regional healthcare systems and reporting methodologies. This study investigated the AE profile of Isatuximab combined with pomalidomide-dexamethasone (Isa-Pd), focusing on safety of Isa-Pd, and regional differences between Lecheng and French in FAERS (FR). Lecheng data (2022Q3–2024Q2) were extracted from a prospective observational real-world study in China (IsaFiRsT), while FAERS reports (2020Q1–2025Q4) were obtained from the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System database. AE terms were standardized using MedDRA, and data mining used ROR, PRR, BCPNN, and MGPS algorithms. Our study divided into 2 parts: 1. Analysis all Isa-Pd-related data in FAERS and Lecheng. 2. Comparing the database of French in FAERS with Lecheng to get regional differences. A total of 507 AE reports were analyzed, with 200 reports from Lecheng and FR used for regional comparison. Strong overall signals included infections and infestations, blood/lymphatic system disorders, investigations, and cardiac disorders. Beyond known hematological toxicities, this study identified unexpected risk signals, including cardiac failure, hypertension, hypokalemia, and Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia, which are not fully characterized in current prescribing information. No specific fatal risk was attributed to Isa-Pd. Regional differences were observed between Lecheng and FR: Lecheng group had more males (Lecheng 62.5% vs FR 48.21%), and lderly patients(≥65 years: Lecheng 70.45% vs FR 58.93%). AEs reported group show difference, all data in Lecheng by physicians, and FR data reported almost equally by pharmacist (56.25%) and physician (42.86%). Lecheng shows frequent hospitalization (100%) in outcome, while FR showed a broader outcome spectrum (hospitalization 53.57%, Life-Threatening 12.50%, death 4.5%). Onset was shorter in Lecheng (Median Lecheng 9.50 vs FR 13.50), Lecheng AE signals concentrated in Investigations (Neutrophil count decreased, ROR=172.21; Platelet count decreased, ROR=22.75). FR group AE signals distributed across Blood and lymphatic system disorders (Lymphopenia, ROR=58.15; Neutropenia, ROR=31.76), Infections and infestations (COVID-19, ROR=12.11), and Vascular disorders (Hypertension, ROR=18.28). These regional differences may be related to population variations, regional management, and distinct post-AE medication regimens. Crucially, by introducing a prospective local real-world cohort (Lecheng) as an external validation for FAERS, this study overcomes the inherent under-reporting biases of spontaneous systems. It comprehensively characterizes the Isa-Pd safety profile, uncovers unexpected risks, and provides robust pharmacological evidence for individualized safety monitoring and risk mitigation.

title: Impact of Proton Pump Inhibitor Use on 90-Day and 2-Year Postoperative Complications Following Intermedullary Nailing for Intertrochanteric Femur Fractures and ORIF for Proximal Humerus Fractures: A Retrospective Cohort Study
authorString: Wang J, Ibrahim K, Zaman R, Nguyen P, Tanas Y, Cho D, Patel K, Horani K, Weiss W.
abstractText:
Purpose: To evaluate the association between proton pump inhibitor (PPI) and postoperative outcomes following intermedullary nailing (IMN) of intertrochanteric femur fractures and open reduction internal fixation (ORIF) of proximal humerus fractures.

Methods:

Two parallel retrospective cohort analyses were performed using the TriNetX Research Network. Adults (>18 y/o) undergoing IMN for intertrochanteric fractures (n=10,605 per cohort) or ORIF for proximal humerus fractures (n=3,114 per cohort) were grouped by PPI use within 90 days preoperatively. Propensity score matching balanced demographic and clinical characteristics. Outcomes were assessed within 90 days and 2 years postoperatively, reported as risk ratios (RR) with significance as p<0.05.

Results:

After IMN, PPI use was associated with an increased risk of pulmonary embolism (RR:1.4, p=0.014), acute kidney injury (RR:1.3, p=0.001), and myocardial infarction (RR:1.3, p=0.033 at 90-days follow-up. At 2-years, PPI use was linked to higher rates of deep vein thrombosis (RR:1.1, p=0.031), acute kidney injury (RR:1.2, p=0.006), and pneumonia (RR:1.1, p=0.010). After ORIF, PPI use within 90 days postoperatively was associated with wound disruption (RR:1.7, p=0.05), infection (RR:1.8, p=0.002), deep vein thrombosis (RR:1.8, p=0.026), and pulmonary embolism (RR:2.8, p=0.003). At the 2-years, PPI users experienced increased risks of infection (RR:1.5, p=0.003), DVT (RR:1.8, p=0.002), PE (RR:1.8, p=0.019), UTI (RR:1.3, p=0.022), nonunion (RR:1.7, p=0.004), and malunion (RR:2.1, p=0.025).

Conclusion:

PPI use is associated with adverse postoperative outcomes following IMN of intertrochanteric fractures and ORIF for proximal humerus fractures. Prospective studies are needed to clarify the causal relationships and isolate the effect of PPI use on postoperative outcomes.

title: Pharmacological and Transcriptomic Exploration of β2-Adrenergic Receptor-Gα15 Signaling in THP-1-Derived Macrophages
authorString: Sun Y, Li Q, English JG.
abstractText: Myocardial infarction and heart failure are leading global causes of mortality. Chronic β-adrenergic receptor (βAR) activation in cardiomyocytes promotes heart failure via Gαs signaling after myocardial infarction, whereas β2AR activation may also provide cardiac protection and repair through alternative pathways. Macrophages play a pivotal role in cardiac repair, and β2AR has been reported to signal via the hematopoietic-specific Gα15 in these cells. We aimed to characterize signaling bias between Gαs and Gα15 downstream of β2AR and to elucidate their roles in macrophage polarization. Using TRUPATH triple assays, we observed that several β2AR agonists activate Gα15 with at least an order of magnitude greater potency than Gαs in this system. In addition, clinically used β-blockers may exhibit differential inhibition on these two pathways. Macrophages are briefly classified into M1 and M2 polarization according to their activating stimuli and functional properties. Transcriptomic profiling of THP-1-derived macrophage-like cells treated with the β2AR agonist clenbuterol revealed enrichment of M1 transcriptional profile and repair-related hallmarks. Knockdown of Gαs showed M1 enrichment, whereas Gα15 knockdown was associated with negative M2 enrichment as well as M1 enrichment. Loss of either Gαs or Gα15 negatively affected repair-associated hallmarks. In contrast, pharmacological intervention of the Gαs-cAMP signaling produced opposing M1/M2 transcriptional responses, while suppressing repair-associated hallmarks. These in vitro findings explore the distinct pharmacological profiles of β2AR ligands toward Gαs and Gα15 and reveal how β2AR agonism may modulate macrophage function through dual-transducer signaling.
