title: Multi-Scale Modeling of the Effects of Optimizing Speed Bumps and Speed Humps on Patients, Occupants, and Drivers: A Convolutional Neural Network and Biomechanical Modeling Approach
authorString: Hosseinikhah S, Mirzahossein H, Asadi MA, Naderan A.
abstractText: Traffic calming is recognized as a set of physical interventions aimed at reducing vehicle speeds and enhancing the safety of vulnerable road users. However, speed bumps and speed humps can exert considerable adverse effects on patients, occupants, and drivers. This study aimed to conduct multi-scale modeling of the effects of optimizing the number and location of speed bumps and speed humps on these three groups. To this end, a convolutional neural network was employed to determine the optimal number of obstacles across 48 urban roadways. Subsequently, the effects of reducing obstacles on eight patient groups (cardiovascular, spinal, intubated, CPR, post-surgical, pregnant women, osteoporosis, and stroke) and on occupant and driver groups were quantified using biomechanical and clinical models. The results indicated that scenario S5, with 39 speed bumps and 45 speed humps, exhibits the best performance, achieving a 51.3% reduction in the number of speed bumps and a 55.9% reduction in the number of speed humps compared with the existing condition. This reduction led to a 51.7% decrease in the cumulative driver anger index, a 51.3% reduction in zero occupant comfort, a 42.6% reduction in cardiovascular risk, a 66.7% reduction in endotracheal tube displacement, and a 45.5% improvement in CPR quality. Dynamic analysis using the reference vehicle demonstrated that although the road acceleration at speed bumps is 16.8 times that at speed humps, due to suspension damping, the actual acceleration on the vehicle seat is only 22.8 times greater, and the actual VDV is approximately 3.3 times greater. The findings indicate that reducing the number of speed bumps takes higher priority than reducing speed humps.

title: Extensive Bilateral Internal Thoracic Artery Grafting in a Population with a High Burden of Diabetes: Sternal Safety, Survival and Stroke in a Weighted Retrospective Cohort Study
authorString: Juárez Del Río JI, Urso S, Recio Cruz CP, González Martín JM, Doñate Bertolín L, Estigarribia Bernal AJ, Muinelo Paul A, Torres Clarés A, Soriano Hernández M, Portela Torrón F.
abstractText:
Background:

/Objectives: Concern about sternal wound complications limits bilateral internal thoracic artery (BITA) grafting, particularly in patients with diabetes and obesity. We evaluated the mid-term results of a program of extensive BITA grafting in the Canary Islands, the Spanish region with the highest diabetes-related mortality.

Methods:

We retrospectively analyzed 667 consecutive patients undergoing non-emergent, first-time, isolated multivessel coronary artery bypass grafting between 2017 and 2025; 472 (70.8%) received BITA and 195 (29.2%) single internal thoracic artery (SITA) grafting. Outcomes were compared using inverse probability of treatment weighting.

Results:

Half of the patients (49.8%) had diabetes. Median follow-up was 46.2 months. After weighting, BITA and SITA grafting did not differ in all-cause mortality (hazard ratio [HR] 0.90; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.55–1.47; p = 0.68), myocardial infarction (HR 0.65; 95% CI 0.28–1.51), repeat revascularization (HR 0.76; 95% CI 0.32–1.83) or major adverse cardiovascular events (HR 0.81; 95% CI 0.52–1.25). Stroke was less frequent after BITA grafting (HR 0.24; 95% CI 0.07–0.77; p = 0.016). Sternal wound complications occurred in 8.7% vs. 6.2% of patients (odds ratio 1.45; 95% CI 0.75–2.82; p = 0.35), with no excess among patients with diabetes (8.8% vs. 8.7%).

Conclusions:

In a population with a high burden of diabetes, BITA grafting was delivered to 70.8% of unselected patients without a significant excess of sternal wound complications. It did not improve mid-term survival, but stroke was less frequent after BITA grafting, a hypothesis-generating finding that requires confirmation.

title: Safety and Efficacy of Transvenous Lead Extraction Using a Right-Sided Approach.
authorString: Demian J, Callahan T, Martin DO, Kochar A, Santangeli P, Taigen T, Farwati M, Tabaja C, Kanj M, Baranowski B, Hussein AA, Chung M, Saliba W, Wazni OM, Younis A.
abstractText:
Background

Despite extensive experience with transvenous lead extraction (TLE) overall, outcomes for systems implanted on the right chest remain underexplored, largely because of their low incidence.

Objectives

The objective was to evaluate whether system laterality influences TLE outcomes.

Methods

Using our institutional, prospectively maintained ExTRACT registry, we analyzed all consecutive patients undergoing TLE procedures at the Cleveland Clinic between 1996 and 2022. Patients were categorized by system laterality. Baseline characteristics, procedural characteristics, and complications were assessed. Multivariable logistic regression models evaluated the association between right-sided TLE and adverse events.

Results

Among 4,989 patients, 494 (9.9%) had right-sided and 4,495 (90.1%) had left-sided TLE. Compared with left-sided cases, right-sided cases had longer total lead dwell times (13.83 vs 9.26 years, P < 0.001) and were more likely to be extracted because of infection (47.57% vs 39.71%, P = 0.001). Fluoroscopy time was longer (15.95 vs 12.1 minutes; P < 0.001), and femoral workstation use more frequent (7.89% vs 4.05%, P < 0.001), yet complete extraction was lower (94.53% vs 96.44%, P = 0.034). Right-sided TLE had higher rates of sternotomy (2.83% vs 1.25%, P = 0.004) and superior vena cava or right atrial tear/perforation (2.49% vs 1.10%, P = 0.009). Thirty-day mortality was low and comparable (0.61% vs 0.47%, P = 0.727). Multivariable regression showed that right-sided TLE was associated with higher odds of sternotomy (OR = 1.92, 95% CI: 1.01-3.46, P = 0.037) and superior vena cava or right atrial tear/perforation (OR = 2.02, 95% CI: 1.01-3.78, P = 0.037).

Conclusions

Right-sided TLE is associated with a lower rate of complete extraction and increased procedural risk, particularly sternotomy and major vascular injury, compared with left-sided TLE. These findings should be carefully weighed when implanting or extracting right-sided systems.

title: Electronic Children's Hospital Early Warning Score: Development and Validation of a Novel Machine Learning Algorithm Predicting Critical Deterioration Events in a Retrospective, Single-Center Cohort.
authorString: Saleh L, Akhondi-Asl A, Kleinman ME, Geva A.

journal.title: Pediatric critical care medicine : a journal of the Society of Critical Care Medicine and the World Federation of Pediatric Intensive and Critical Care Societies

abstractText:
Objective

To develop and validate a novel, machine learning prediction model for critical deterioration events.

Design

Retrospective cohort study.

Setting

Single quaternary care freestanding pediatric hospital.

Patients

All patients up to 21 years old admitted to acute care wards (excluding cardiac and psychiatry units) between January 2012 and June 2023.

Interventions

None.

Measurements and main results

The primary outcome was a critical deterioration, defined as utilization of advanced respiratory support or continuous IV medication infusions not administered on acute care units. Secondary outcome was ICU transfer. Each outcome was evaluated between 6 and 30 hours after each prediction score. Among 179,074 unique hospitalizations with 2,803,017 windows of scoring data, 10,656 (0.4%) had a subsequent critical deterioration event. Compared with the legacy Children's Hospital Early Warning Score (CHEWS), the model, which we call electronic CHEWS (eCHEWS), had a higher area under the precision-recall curve (0.157; 95% CI [0.150-0.164]) vs. 0.017; 95% CI [0.013-0.027]). At sensitivity approximately 44%, CHEWS had positive predictive value (PPV) 1.8% (number needed to alert [NNA] 55), whereas eCHEWS had PPV 11.4% (NNA 9).

Conclusions

eCHEWS outperforms traditional early warning scores for predicting critical deterioration among acute care inpatients and can detect critical deterioration at least 6 hours before occurrence. If prospectively validated, eCHEWS could serve as an early warning trigger integrated into the electronic health record to support proactive rounding, escalation decisions, and timely transfer to ICUs.

title: Sepsis Point Prevalence Across Ibero-Latin America PICUs: The 2024 Sepsis Prevalence Assessment Database in Pediatrics (SPREAD PED IBERO-LATAM).
authorString: de Souza DC, Fernández-Sarmiento J, Sanchez-Pinto LN, de Oliveira CF, Jaramillo-Bustamante JC, Soares Lanziotti V, Almonte E, Fuenmayor Arocha A, Bandeira-Paiva P, Barberena J, Bustos JD, Bustos B R, Campos-Miño S, Cantillano Quintero EM, Casson N, Delgadillo L, Dominguez J, Marques Duarte C, González G, Guzmán LJ, Mack R, Márquez MP, Monteverde N, Pilar-Orive J, Ríos B, Morales Torres G, Machado FR, Jabornisky R, and the SPREAD PED IBERO-LATAM Investigators.

journal.title: Pediatric critical care medicine : a journal of the Society of Critical Care Medicine and the World Federation of Pediatric Intensive and Critical Care Societies

abstractText:
Objectives

To determine the prevalence and outcome of sepsis in PICUs across Ibero-Latin America; to identify patient- and institution-level factors associated with mortality; and to explore the prognostic performance of pediatric sepsis definitions.

Design

Multinational, multicenter, prospective point prevalence study with follow-up to hospital discharge.

Setting

One hundred sixty-eight PICUs in 21 countries across Latin America, Spain, and Portugal.

Patients

Children of 28 days to 18 years with a clinical diagnosis of sepsis or septic shock admitted to participating PICUs between September 9 and September 13, 2024.

Interventions

None.

Measurements and main results

Among 1318 screened PICU patients, 340 met criteria for clinical sepsis, yielding a point prevalence of 25.8% (95% CI, 23.5-28.2%). Complete outcome data were available for 324 patients. PICU mortality was 42 of 324 (13.0% [95% CI, 9.5-17.1%), and total in-hospital mortality was 49 of 324 (15.1% [95% CI, 11.4-19.4%]). Cardiovascular and respiratory dysfunction were most frequent, whereas multivariable logistic regression identified greater odds of PICU mortality associated with renal dysfunction (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 3.2 [95% CI, 1.5-7.5]) and immunologic dysfunction (aOR, 12.7 [95% CI, 4.6-37.5]).In multivariable analysis, abnormal nutritional status, lack of vaccination, renal dysfunction, and admission to PICUs with intermediate or low resource availability were associated with greater odds of PICU mortality. In exploratory analyses, the Phoenix sepsis criteria identified 95.2% of PICU deaths, but the positive predictive value of the score for mortality was no different from the 2005 International Pediatric Sepsis Consensus Conference criteria.

Conclusions

In 2024, in Ibero-Latin American PICUs, sepsis affected approximately one in four admissions, and the diagnosis was associated with mortality. Both patient vulnerability and institutional resource availability were associated with greater odds of mortality, underscoring the potential influence of health system capacity on pediatric sepsis outcomes in the region.

title: Venous thromboembolism and transfusion outcomes following intravenous tranexamic acid in primary total hip arthroplasty: A prospective two-center cohort study.
authorString: Rincon-Hoyos JA, Rincon D, Manrique J, Restrepo A, Casas J, Munoz-Medina S, Torres-Mayorga A.
abstractText:
Introduction

Tranexamic acid (TXA) is widely used during total hip arthroplasty (THA) to reduce perioperative blood loss and transfusion requirements. Although extensive evidence supports its use, prospective real-world data from Latin America are limited. This study aimed to describe the incidence of symptomatic venous thromboembolism (VTE) and blood transfusion among patients receiving intravenous TXA during primary total hip arthroplasty (THA) at two institutions in Bogotá, Colombia.

Methods

This prospective, observational, descriptive, two-center cohort study included consecutive adults who underwent elective primary THA. Patients received intravenous TXA according to institutional protocols. The primary outcome was the occurrence of symptomatic VTE, including deep vein thrombosis (DVT), pulmonary embolism, ischemic stroke, and myocardial infarction during a 10-week follow-up period. The secondary outcomes included blood transfusion requirements, postoperative hemoglobin levels, and emergency department visits.

Results

A total of 151 primary THAs were performed in 133 patients. One case of symptomatic DVT was diagnosed, corresponding to a VTE incidence of 0.75%. Five patients (3.8%) required postoperative blood transfusions, including two complex reconstructive procedures. The mean postoperative hemoglobin level was 11.8 ± 1.9 g/dL. No pulmonary embolism, ischemic stroke, or myocardial infarction was observed during the follow-up period.

Conclusions

In this prospective two-center cohort of patients receiving intravenous TXA during primary THA, including both conventional and complex cases, a low incidence of symptomatic VTE and transfusion was observed. These results provide prospective real-world evidence from a Latin American population and contribute to the regional literature on perioperative blood conservation strategies for primary THA.

title: Predictors of Thrombotic Events and Mortality in Patients Treated With Andexanet: A Pooled Analysis.
authorString: Sharma M, Xu L, Eikelboom JW, Cohen AT, Demchuk AM, Członkowska A, Lindgren AG, Molina CA, Bereczki D, Toni D, Seiffge DJ, Tanne D, Sandset EC, Tsivgoulis G, Christensen H, Beyer-Westendorf J, Coutinho JM, Crowther M, Verhamme P, Amarenco P, Roine RO, Mikulik R, Lemmens R, Veltkamp R, Middeldorp S, Milling TJ, Poli S, Gibson CM, Siegal DM, Knutsson M, Falkenberg C, Narayan R, Kurlyandskaya R, Ladenvall P, Shoamanesh A, ANNEXa-4 and ANNEXa-I Investigators.
abstractText:
Background

Andexanet reduces hematoma expansion compared with usual care for acute FXa (factor Xa) inhibitor-associated intracerebral hemorrhage but is associated with a risk of thrombotic events (TE). We pooled data from andexanet-treated trial participants to determine baseline predictors of TE.

Methods

Secondary analyses of andexanet-treated participants in ANNEXA-I (Andexanet Alfa, a Novel Antidote to the Anticoagulant Effects of Factor Xa Inhibitors in ICH) and ANNEXA-4 (Andexanet Alfa, a Novel Antidote to the Anticoagulation Effects of Factor Xa Inhibitors), which included adults with acute life-threatening hemorrhage on FXa inhibitors. Stratified Cox proportional hazards models were used to examine associations between baseline variables and arterial or all TE and mortality. A stratified Cox regression model with arterial events as time-dependent covariates was used to examine associations of arterial events with mortality, adjusted for clinical covariates.

Results

Of 741 participants (mean age, 78.5 years; 54.5% male), 593 (80.0%) had intracranial hemorrhage and 109 (14.7%) had gastrointestinal hemorrhage. Seventy-seven (10.4%) participants had ≥1 TE, and 147 (19.8%) died. Arterial and venous thromboembolism events occurred a median of 3.5 days (interquartile range, 2.0-12.0) and 14.0 days (interquartile range, 10.0-20.0), respectively, after randomization. No baseline factors were associated with all TE. Arterial TE were associated with prior myocardial infarction (hazard ratio [HR], 2.64 [95% CI, 1.33-5.26]), high-dose eligibility (HR, 2.44 [95% CI, 1.33-4.48]), female sex (HR, 1.78 [95% CI, 1.00-3.16]), and age (HR per year, 1.04 [95% CI, 1.00-1.08]). Mortality was associated with arterial TE (HR, 2.68 [95% CI, 1.64-4.36]), prior congestive heart failure (HR, 2.53 [95% CI, 1.76-3.63]), intracerebral hemorrhage or intraventricular hemorrhage (HR, 1.90 [95% CI, 1.20-3.01]), and age (HR per year, 1.06 [95% CI, 1.03-1.08]). The initiation of anticoagulation after randomization was associated with a reduction in TE.

Conclusions

In FXa inhibitor-associated hemorrhage treated with andexanet, baseline factors are associated with arterial TE and can be used to inform treatment decisions. Initiation of anticoagulation reduces the occurrence of TE.

title: Mild aortic regurgitation as an independent predictor of major adverse cardiovascular events in non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndrome: insights from a multicentre propensity score-matched cohort study.
authorString: Zhao P, Fang W, Li H, Zhou B, Zhu T, Zhu J, Tang L, Wu S, Wu B, Wang J, Liu J.
abstractText:
Background

Non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndrome (NSTE-ACS) remains a leading cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality worldwide, making accurate risk stratification beyond conventional clinical parameters a critical need. Mild aortic regurgitation (AR) is frequently detected on routine echocardiography in patients with coronary artery disease, yet its prognostic significance in the high-risk context of NSTE-ACS remains poorly defined.

Methods

This multicentre retrospective cohort study included 1,290 patients with NSTE-ACS and mild AR from six tertiary cardiovascular centres in China. Propensity score matching targeting an approximately 1:3 ratio identified 3,872 matched controls without AR or other valvular heart disease. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs), comprising cardiac death, heart failure rehospitalisation, and unplanned coronary revascularisation, over a median follow-up of 50 months.

Results

Covariates included in the propensity-score model were adequately balanced after propensity score matching (absolute standardised mean difference <0.10). Mild AR was associated with higher risks of MACEs (HR = 1.47; 95% CI = 1.26-1.72, P < 0.001), cardiac death (HR = 1.51; 95% CI = 1.13-2.02, P = 0.002), heart failure rehospitalisation (HR = 1.57; 95% CI = 1.12-2.20, P = 0.004), and unplanned coronary revascularisation (HR = 1.34; 95% CI = 1.08-1.67, P = 0.004). After multivariable adjustment, mild AR remained independently associated with MACEs (HR = 1.329; 95% CI = 1.144-1.545, P < 0.001). Mild AR was also associated with higher neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (β = 0.56; 95% CI = 0.37-0.74, P < 0.001), systemic immune-inflammation index (β = 161.73; 95% CI = 119.36-204.10, P < 0.001), and remnant cholesterol (β = 0.21; 95% CI = 0.16-0.26, P < 0.001). Exploratory mediation analyses showed modest statistical indirect associations between mild AR and MACEs (~6.8%) and between mild AR and cardiac death (~10.0%), operating through left atrial diameter.

Conclusions

In patients with NSTE-ACS, mild AR was independently associated with MACEs and modest differences in inflammatory indices and remnant cholesterol. Mild AR may, therefore, be a readily available marker for risk stratification in this high-risk population.

title: Early clinical experience with vericiguat after acute decompensated heart failure in elderly patients with HFrEF: a prospective observational study.
authorString: Acanfora D, Rengo G, Acanfora C, Calabrò P, Galasso G, Incalzi RA, Komici K, Provitera V, Caporaso G, Casucci G.
abstractText: Vericiguat has demonstrated clinical benefit in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), particularly in those at high risk of recurrent heart failure events. However, evidence regarding its early use in elderly patients following hospitalization for acute decompensated HF (ADHF) remains limited. In this prospective single-center case series, 143 consecutive patients aged > 70 years hospitalized for ADHF with HFrEF were enrolled and vericiguat was administrated. Clinical evaluations, left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), six-minute walk test (6MWT), Minnesota Living with Heart Failure Questionnaire (MLHFQ), and laboratory parameters were assessed at baseline and after 4 weeks. After 4 weeks of treatment with vericiguat, 44.8% of patients were in NYHA class II and 55.2% in NYHA class III, no patients were in NYHA class IV (p < 0.001); LVEF improved from 34 ± 4.7% to 46.8 ± 7.5% (p < 0.0001); exercise capacity increased significantly (p < 0.001), while a significant decrease in MLHF-Q, NT-proBNP levels and hsCRP was observed (p < 0.001). No symptomatic hypotension, syncope or relevant deterioration in renal function or electrolytes occurred during the observation period. In this single-arm cohort of older patients with HFrEF recently stabilized after ADHF, initiation of vericiguat was feasible and coincided with substantial short-term changes in functional status, LVEF, and circulating biomarkers, without major safety signals during 4 weeks of observation. Given the absence of a control group, these changes cannot be attributed to vericiguat and may reflect, at least in part, recovery from the acute event, decongestion, optimization of background therapy, learning effects, and regression to the mean. These findings should therefore be considered descriptive and hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in controlled studies.

title: Apixaban Benefit in Subclinical Atrial Fibrillation Accounting for Competing Risks: A Reanalysis of the ARTESIA Trial.
authorString: Lo SW, Ko D, Kim DH, Ngo LH, Singer DE, Shah SJ.
abstractText: In the ARTESIA trial, apixaban reduced stroke and systemic embolism compared with aspirin in patients with subclinical atrial fibrillation (AF), but the primary analysis treated death and AF progression as censoring rather than competing events. We estimated the absolute risk reduction (ARR) at 3.5 years treating death and AF progression as competing events. We used event-level data reconstructed from published Kaplan-Meier curves to probabilistically impute status and timing of competing events. The ARR was 1.94% when treating death and AF progression as censoring events vs. 1.62% treating them as competing events (difference 0.33 percentage points; 95% CI 0.04 to 0.62). Absolute benefit estimates depend on how competing events are handled. Competing risk analyses can provide more realistic estimates of expected therapeutic benefit at the point of treatment decisions when competing events are common.

title: Global Burden of Stroke-related Heart Failure in GBD 2021 from 1990 to 2021.
authorString: Song Q, Li S, Yang J, Li R, Wang Z, Shao G.

journal.title: Journal of stroke and cerebrovascular diseases : the official journal of National Stroke Association

abstractText:
Background

Stroke-related Heart Failure (HF) is a modeled cause-impairment outcome in the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) study. Its population distribution should be distinguished from all HF occurring among people with a history of stroke. We examined temporal patterns, demographic contributions, and socioeconomic disparities in this GBD-defined outcome.

Methods

We analyzed GBD 2021 prevalence and years lived with disability (YLDs) estimates for 1990-2021 across global, regional, and national settings. Full-period estimated annual percentage change (EAPC) and segmented regression described trends. Age- and sex-specific rates supplemented absolute counts. Spearman correlations, explicitly defined inequality indices, and demographic decomposition characterized differences in burden. Bayesian age-period-cohort projections were evaluated using two held-out time windows and a last-observed-rate benchmark.

Results

Global prevalent cases increased from 900,446 in 1990 to 1,983,544 in 2021, while age-standardized prevalence and YLD rates declined modestly over the full period. The middle-SDI group had high aggregate burden, but this does not imply uniform country-level patterns. Male age-specific rates remained higher at ages 80-89 despite a crossover in absolute counts at age 80. Ischemic stroke and intracerebral hemorrhage accounted for 47.46% and 46.64% of prevalent cases in the subtype estimates. Population aging and growth contributed 55.95% and 49.81% of the net increase in cases. Inequality estimates depended on weighting and the selected estimator; a robust widening was not established. Forecasts performed worse than the simple benchmark in both validation windows.

Conclusion

Increasing absolute burden despite modest declines in standardized rates supports planning for the needs of ageing populations. Country-specific estimates and local assessments of access to care should guide priorities. Count-based sex differences, ecological associations, inequality trends, and exploratory forecasts require cautious interpretation.

title: Incidence and predictors of de novo atrial fibrillation in patients with heart failure undergoing continuous rhythm monitoring.
authorString: Rodríguez-Mañero M, García-Rodeja F, Tilves C, Cardeso B, Cordero A, Ramón Núñez-Caamaño J, Rodríguez-Iglesias AI, Rincón-Díaz LM, Muñoz-Esparza C, Moreno Arribas J, Quintanilla-Tello M, Gómez-Otero I, Pascual-Figal D, Jiménez-Candil J, Sánchez PL, Martínez-Monzonis MA, Eiras S, Ramón González-Juanatey J.
abstractText:
Introduction and objectives

Atrial fibrillation (AF) is associated with adverse clinical outcomes in patients with heart failure (HF). The true incidence of de novo AF in HF, however, remains uncertain. Moreover, the role of clinical variables and circulating biomarkers in AF risk stratification in this population is not well established. This study aimed to determine the incidence of AF in patients with HF using long-term continuous rhythm monitoring and to identify clinical, structural, and biomarker-based predictors.

Methods

This multicenter, prospective study included patients with HF and reduced or preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF). Long-term rhythm monitoring was performed using implantable loop recorders or single-chamber defibrillators without atrial leads and with ventricular pacing < 20%. Serial blood samples were obtained at baseline, during follow-up, and during HF decompensation, and analyzed using a multiplex panel of selected biomarkers. Multivariable analyses were performed using both baseline biomarker levels and laboratory values closest to AF onset or HF decompensation.

Results

A total of 345 patients were enrolled (79% male; median age 68 years; 53% with LVEF< 40%. During a median follow-up of 756 days, 86 patients (24.9%) developed AF episodes lasting > 6 minutes, and 64 patients (18.5%) died. Hypertension, left atrial volume, beta-blocker use, CA-125, NT-proBNP, COL4A1, and AT1-AA were independently associated with AF, whereas aldosterone receptor antagonist therapy was associated with a lower risk of HF (C-index, 0.74). Patients with persistent AF as the initial manifestation had significantly higher mortality than those with paroxysmal AF or no AF. NT-proBNP and COL4A1 were associated with mortality. Clinically relevant bradyarrhythmias and ventricular tachyarrhythmias were also detected.

Conclusion

De novo AF is a common complication in patients with HF. Integrating clinical variables, structural parameters, and biomarkers improves the identification of patients at increased risk of developing AF. Continuous monitoring enables early detection of rhythm abnormalities that may influence therapeutic management.

title: Bridging Evidence and Practice: Recent Advances in Hypothyroidism Management during Pregnancy.
authorString: Osman M, Sheikh Z, Ripa FA, Khair NZ, Khair IZ.

journal.title: Hormone and metabolic research = Hormon- und Stoffwechselforschung = Hormones et metabolisme

abstractText:
Abstract

Deficiency of thyroid hormones, primarily thyroxine and triiodothyronine, results in the clinical condition known as hypothyroidism, a prevalent endocrine disorder globally, particularly in women of childbearing age. Dynamic changes occur in thyroid function during pregnancy to provide adequate levels of thyroid hormones to the mother and the fetus. Hashimoto thyroiditis remains the most widespread reason for gestational hypothyroidism in iodine-sufficient regions and in mildly iodine deficient populations. Iodine plays a vital role in the synthesis and regulation of thyroid hormones; therefore, during pregnancy, iodine consumption must be increased by 50% to produce the required amount of maternal thyroid hormones and meet the increased demand of the developing fetus. Evidence-based studies have shown that even minor alteration in maternal thyroid function can cause pregnancy-related complications and adverse pregnancy outcomes (e.g. miscarriage, perinatal death, pre-eclampsia, pregnancy-induced hypertension, low birth weight and postpartum hemorrhage). Therefore, the timely assessment and appropriate management of gestational hypothyroidism is crucial to ensure optimal maternal and fetal outcomes. Levothyroxine remains the standard treatment for hypothyroidism, significantly reducing the risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes in women with hypothyroidism. The present review provides an update on the diagnosis and management of hypothyroidism in pregnant women, highlighting the different types, causes, signs and symptoms of hypothyroidism, and the obstetric outcomes of each type of hypothyroidism along with the treatment strategy. Current key recommendations based on clinical evidence by health practitioners are also provided to assist in planning and choosing the individualized treatment regimen for patients with hypothyroidism before and during pregnancy.

title: Association of Site Volume and MitraClip Outcomes in Secondary Mitral Regurgitation: The COAPT PAS Registry.
authorString: Goel K, Makkar R, Naik H, Atmakuri S, Mahoney P, Morse MA, Aiyer J, Huang R, Thourani V, Lindenfeld J, Lindman BR, Barker C.
abstractText:
Background

The number of sites performing transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) for secondary mitral regurgitation (SMR) has increased. Despite concerns that low-volume sites may have worse outcomes, data are limited on the association between site volume and TEER outcomes.

Objectives

This study aimed to assess the association between site volume and mitral TEER outcomes in SMR.

Methods

The COAPT PAS (COAPT Post-Approval Study) included patients with SMR who underwent TEER with the MitraClip device from March 2019 to September 2020 following Food and Drug Administration approval. Sites were categorized by number of patients treated: low (≤25), medium (25-50), and high (>50).

Results

Of 5,000 patients, 2,632 were from low-, 1,527 from medium-, and 841 from high-volume sites. High-volume sites treated sicker patients with higher Society of Thoracic Surgeons scores and prior heart failure hospitalization rates. Procedures at low-volume sites had similar device implant rates (low: 97%, medium: 99%, high: 98%), used fewer number of clips (low: 1.4 ± 0.6, medium: 1.5 ± 0.6, high: 1.6 ± 0.7 clips, P < 0.001), and had longer device (low: 68 ± 55, medium: 56 ± 53, high: 57 ± 42 min, P < 0.001) and procedure times (low: 153 ± 67, medium: 131 ± 59, high: 128 ± 56 min, P < 0.001). Technical success was comparable (low: 93%, medium: 94%, high: 95%, P = 0.92). MR reduction to ≤2+ and ≤1+ was also similar. There was no difference in heart failure hospitalization (low: 19%, medium: 18%, high: 20%, P = 0.50) or all-cause mortality (low: 23%, medium: 21%, high: 20%, P = 0.27).

Conclusions

Technical success, MR reduction, and 1-year clinical outcomes were comparable across volume strata during the early adoption phase, without significant differences between low- and high-volume centers.

title: Antimicrobial stewardship in critical care: Applying PK/PD and optimised antimicrobial dosing to improve care.
authorString: Mehta R, Barreto EF, Conway Morris A, Koulenti D, Maves RC, Pertzborn M, Roger C, Smeets TJL, Roberts JA.
abstractText: Life-threatening infections are common in critically ill patients and remain a major cause of morbidity and mortality in the intensive care unit (ICU). Antimicrobial stewardship (AMS) aims to optimise antimicrobial use by balancing effective treatment with minimising toxicity, resistance and unnecessary exposure. This review examines AMS in critical care with a focus on antimicrobial dose optimisation. Core AMS principles in the ICU include diagnostic stewardship, appropriate antimicrobial initiation, de-escalation and treatment duration. Dose optimisation is fundamental but challenging because critical illness causes profound and dynamic changes in pharmacokinetics (PK) and pharmacodynamics (PD). These alterations result in marked interpatient variability and increase the risk of subtherapeutic or toxic drug exposure. Understanding key PK parameters, including volume of distribution, clearance and half-life, together with PD targets such as Cmax/MIC, fT > MIC and AUC0-24/MIC is essential for individualising therapy. Factors including sepsis, organ dysfunction, augmented renal clearance and extracorporeal support can substantially alter antimicrobial exposure and dosing requirements. Strategies to improve target attainment include loading doses, prolonged infusions, therapeutic drug monitoring and model-informed precision dosing, although implementation may be limited by local resources. Integrating PK/PD-informed dosing into routine ICU practice can improve clinical outcomes, reduce toxicity and strengthen AMS in critically ill populations.

title: Verifiable summarization of electronic health records using large language models to support chart review.
authorString: Verma R, Alsentzer E, Strasser Z, Chang L, Roman K, Gershanik E, Hernandez C, Linares M, Rodriguez J, Thakral D, Unlu O, You J, Zhou L, Bates D.

journal.title: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA

abstractText:
Objectives

Information overload in electronic health records hampers clinicians' ability to efficiently extract and synthesize critical information from a patient's longitudinal health record, leading to increased cognitive burden and delays in care. This study explores the potential of large language models (LLMs) to address this challenge by generating problem-based admission summaries for patients admitted with heart failure, a leading cause of hospitalization worldwide.

Materials and methods

We developed an extract-then-abstract approach guided by disease-specific "summary bundles" to generate summaries of longitudinal clinical notes that prioritize clinically relevant information. Through a mixed-methods evaluation using real-world clinical notes, we compared physicians' ability to answer patient-specific clinical questions with the LLM-generated summaries vs standard chart review.

Results

While summary access did not significantly reduce overall questionnaire completion time, frequent summary use significantly contributed to faster questionnaire completion (P = .002). Individual physicians varied in how effectively they leveraged the summaries. Importantly, summary use maintained accuracy in answering clinical questions (88.0% with summaries vs 86.4% without). All physicians indicated they were "likely" or "very likely" to use the summaries in clinical practice, and 87.5% reported that the summaries would save them time. Preferences for summary format varied, highlighting the need for customizable summaries aligned with individual clinician workflows.

Discussion

This exploratory, mixed-methods pilot study provides one of the first extrinsic evaluations of LLMs for longitudinal summarization, demonstrating their potential to enhance clinician efficiency, alleviate workload, and support informed decision-making in time-sensitive care environments.

Conclusion

Our findings suggest that problem-based longitudinal summarization could improve chart review efficiency and standardize the presentation of clinical information, Variability in summary preferences and use underscores the need for user-centered evaluations to guide the development of LLM-generated summaries that align with clinician workflows.

title: Atrial fibrillation in chronic kidney disease - treatment standard.
authorString: Schneppe C, Heine GH, Eitel I, Evans M, Urbanek L, Winkelmayer W, De Vriese AS.

journal.title: Nephrology, dialysis, transplantation : official publication of the European Dialysis and Transplant Association - European Renal Association

abstractText: The prevalence of atrial fibrillation (AF) is high among patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD). While patients with CKD Stages G1 - G3b may be treated similarly to patients without CKD, little evidence guides therapeutic strategies for CKD G4 - G5 patients. Dosing of most drugs used for rate and rhythm control requires adjustment to kidney function. Recurrence rates after cardioversion and ablation for rhythm control are higher in patients with advanced CKD than those without it. Regarding the prevention of stroke and systemic embolism, the benefit-to-risk ratio of oral anticoagulation (OAC) is disputed among patients with CKD stages G4 - G5 with AF, in particular among those receiving hemodialysis given their high risk for severe bleeding events. Novel strategies for stroke and systemic embolism prevention, particularly factor XI inhibitors and left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO), have not yet fulfilled their initial promise as safe and effective alternatives.

title: Association between admission D-dimer level and post-stroke epilepsy in patients with acute ischemic stroke: a retrospective cohort study
authorString: Li Z, Liang D, Wang Y.
abstractText: Background: D-dimer reflects thrombus formation and fibrinolysis and is associated with stroke severity and outcome, but whether it predicts post-stroke epilepsy (PSE) is unclear. We examined whether admission D-dimer predicts PSE and assessed its diagnostic and incremental predictive value in acute ischemic stroke (AIS). Methods: A total of 21,459 patients with AIS were analyzed. Admission D-dimer was divided into quartiles; the two lowest were merged as the reference. Multivariable logistic regression with three adjustment models, restricted cubic spline and subgroup analyses were performed. Discrimination (ROC/AUC), decision curve analysis, and the net reclassification index (NRI) and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI) assessed predictive value. Results: Within one year, 936 (4.4%) patients developed PSE. Each 1 mg/L increase in D-dimer was associated with higher PSE risk (fully adjusted OR 1.46, 95% CI 1.37-1.57); compared with the merged Q1+Q2 reference, fully adjusted ORs were 9.13 (Q3) and 15.23 (Q4) (P for trend < 0.001). The association was non-linear (P < 0.001), with a threshold at 0.867 mg/L, and was stronger in men, younger patients, and those without hypertension (P for interaction < 0.001). D-dimer discriminated PSE with an AUC of 0.822 (95% CI 0.810-0.835), higher than ALT, uric acid, creatinine and urea; adding it to a baseline model (age, gender, NIHSS, hypertension) raised the AUC from 0.866 to 0.920 (P < 0.001; NRI 0.8438, IDI 0.2031). Conclusions: Admission D-dimer was independently and non-linearly associated with PSE and improved discrimination and reclassification beyond conventional factors. It may aid early identification of AIS patients at high PSE risk.

title: Recorded non-cancer comorbidity burden and inpatient service use among cancer-related admissions at a secondary hospital in China, 2014–2025
authorString: Li Y, Xu H, Chen C, Wu Y.
abstractText: Background Evidence on non-cancer chronic comorbidity and inpatient service use among cancer-related admissions to secondary hospitals in China remains limited. This study examined recorded comorbidity patterns and their associations with length of stay (LOS) and hospitalization expenditure at a Chinese secondary hospital. Methods This retrospective observational study included 26,562 adult admissions with an ICD-10 C00–C97 code in any diagnosis field during 2014–2025. Comorbidity burden was measured using 17 selected non-cancer chronic condition categories and grouped as 0, 1, 2, 3, or ≥ 4 conditions. Outcomes included LOS, cumulative inpatient days, and hospitalization expenditure expressed in US dollars at 2025 prices. Negative binomial and gamma-log generalized linear models estimated adjusted mean ratios for LOS and expenditure, respectively, controlling for age, sex, discharge year, cancer diagnosis position, and recorded cancer site group. Sensitivity analyses examined alternative specifications, recent periods, and patient-level clustering. Results Cancer appeared only in secondary diagnosis fields in 85.3% of admissions. Overall, 55.1% had ≥ 1 selected condition and 22.7% had ≥ 2. These proportions increased from 47.6% and 17.5% in 2014 to 62.2% and 29.1% in 2025, respectively, and were higher among older admissions. Hypertension, diabetes, and chronic liver disease were the most commonly recorded conditions. Admissions accounted for 229,888 inpatient days; median LOS was 6 days (IQR, 4–10), and median expenditure was US$810.44 (IQR, 435.76–1,484.68). Admissions with ≥ 2 conditions contributed 25.9% of inpatient days. Higher burden corresponded to longer LOS and higher expenditure in unadjusted comparisons. After adjustment, mean LOS ratios were 1.07 (95% CI, 1.02–1.12) for three conditions and 1.13 (95% CI, 1.02–1.25) for ≥ 4 conditions versus none. Neither comparison met the significance threshold after multiple-testing correction. Adjusted expenditure ratios remained close to 1. In patient-clustered analyses for 2020–2025, all burden-category confidence intervals included 1 for both outcomes. Conclusions Recorded non-cancer chronic conditions were common, and admissions with multiple conditions contributed a greater share of inpatient days than of admissions. Evidence for adjusted LOS differences was limited, and expenditure showed no consistent gradient. These findings provide a local basis for planning integrated cancer and chronic disease care.

title: Racial cuts: Explanations of race inequities in cesarean births in U.S. government and medical discourse.
authorString: Carter SK, Bell JM, Tehrani S.
abstractText: Cesarean births are increasingly common worldwide, constituting what some experts call a cesarean epidemic and attracting public health initiatives to reduce cesarean rates. The U.S. cesarean epidemic is racialized, consisting of cesarean overuse in low-risk contexts and underuse in high-risk contexts for Black birthing people. Research shows health initiatives portray Black women as non-compliant with health directives, justifying inequitable outcomes in reproductive contexts, including birth, breastfeeding, and pre-pregnancy health. However, research has not examined initiatives to reduce cesareans, which are distinct because they occur within hospitals and are authorized by medical professionals. This study used critical discourse analysis to investigate constructions of race inequities in cesareans across 59 documents published between 2010 and 2025 by U.S. government agencies and medical organizations. Findings revealed cesareans are constructed as lifesaving procedures that carry inherent risks of detrimental outcomes, including death. Documents acknowledged race inequities in cesareans, but associated them with comorbidities (e.g. hypertension) rather than structural or obstetric racism; explaining and eradicating race inequities was rarely addressed. By centering behavioral and biomedical risk factors, discourses reproduce Black birthing people as inherently "high-risk," thereby legitimizing cesarean overuse. Centering cesareans as a discursive site of racialization, this study shows how surgical intervention is justified through language that marks Black bodies as pathologically susceptible to "risk." These findings illustrate that cesarean birth functions not only as a medical intervention but also as a site of racialized reproductive governance.

title: Two Decades of Cardiovascular Prevention Science at CDC: A Bibliometric Analysis, 2006-2025.
authorString: Coronado F, Vaughan AS, Carlson SA, Joshi N, Schooley M, Presley-Cantrell L.
abstractText:
Background

The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's Division for Heart Disease and Stroke Prevention (DHDSP) provides national leadership for cardiovascular disease (CVD) prevention, including efforts to improve hypertension control. Scientific publications document surveillance, program implementation, evaluation, and dissemination of evidence-based strategies. This study describes DHDSP's scientific productivity, focus, and reach across two decades of CVD prevention work.

Methods

We conducted a bibliometric analysis of publications authored or coauthored by DHDSP staff during 2006-2025. Publications were identified from internal records and PubMed searches, verified for eligibility, and categorized by condition and topic area. Citation metrics, Relative Citation Ratio (RCR), Altmetric Attention Scores, policy and guideline mentions, authorship role, and collaboration indicators were summarized descriptively.

Results

DHDSP contributed to 841 publications ranging annually from 12 in 2006 to 67 in 2017. Publications accrued 88,636 citations (median: 19; 25-75 percentiles: 7;48). Median RCR was 1.15 (25-75 percentiles: 0.50-2.53), and median Altmetric Attention Score was 6.0 (25-75 percentiles: 0.5-23.5). DHDSP publications were cited or mentioned in 637 policy documents and 410 guidelines indexed by Altmetric. Most focused on core DHDSP conditions, including hypertension, with surveillance and epidemiology the most common topic. Overall, 240 publications (28.5%) included a focus on hypertension.

Conclusions

DHDSP's publication portfolio demonstrates sustained scientific productivity and broad dissemination across two decades of CVD prevention. Hypertension was an important component, alongside research addressing heart disease, stroke, and other cardiovascular risk factors and outcomes. The portfolio documents the evolution of public health science and contributes to the evidence base for cardiovascular disease prevention and control.

title: Clinical Outcomes of Patients With Atrial Septal Defect and Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.
authorString: Baek D, Kim DH, Lee PH, Sun BJ, Lee S, Kang DH, Song JK, Song JM.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: World J Pediatr Congenit Heart Surg
journal.title: World journal for pediatric & congenital heart surgery
journal.isoabbreviation: World J Pediatr Congenit Heart Surg

abstractText: BackgroundIndications for atrial septal defect (ASD) closure in patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) have not been established. We evaluated medium-term outcomes in such patients with regard to the effect of ASD closure and prognostic predictors.MethodsThis single-center retrospective study included 39 patients with pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) ≥ 2 Wood units (WU). The primary adverse outcome was defined as a composite of major cardiovascular events, including cardiac death or hospitalization for heart failure.ResultsOf the 39 patients, 32 underwent shunt closure, whereas 7 did not. Among patients with PVR ≥ 5 WU, over a median follow-up of 3.8 years, 3-year clinical event rates were 27.3% (3/11) in the closure group (n = 11) and 14.3% (1/7) in the no-closure group (n = 7); the difference was not statistically significant. The maximal velocity of tricuspid regurgitation significantly decreased during follow-up in the closure group; no significant change was observed in the no-closure group. In patients with PVR ≥ 5 WU, systemic arterial oxygen saturation (SaO2) showed a significant association with the primary composite outcome; ASD closure and PVR were not. Among patients with PVR ≥ 5 WU who underwent ASD closure, those with SaO2 < 93% (n = 4) had a significantly higher rate of adverse outcomes than those with SaO2 ≥ 93% (n = 7) (hazard ratio, 17.8; P = .014), whereas no composite adverse events occurred in patients with SaO2 ≥ 93%.ConclusionsIn patients with ASD and severe PAH, SaO2 < 93% showed a significant association with adverse outcomes and may complement PVR in risk stratification. These exploratory findings require prospective validation.

title: Beyond Surgical Palliation Success: Uncovering the Profound Mental Health Burden Among Children With Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome in the United States.
authorString: Mehdizadeh-Shrifi A, Menninger T, Faateh M, Turner D, Chappell G, Hogue S, Kasparian N, Ricci M, Ashfaq A, Morales DLS.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: World J Pediatr Congenit Heart Surg
journal.title: World journal for pediatric & congenital heart surgery
journal.isoabbreviation: World J Pediatr Congenit Heart Surg

abstractText: ObjectiveMajor initiatives have assessed the burden of mental health in children, but longitudinal analysis of incidences in hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HLHS) is limited. We performed an analysis of neurodevelopmental and mental health conditions (NDMHC) on the single-ventricle journey.MethodsThe Pediatric Health Information System (PHIS) registry was queried for pediatric patients (<18 years of age) with International Classification of Diseases codes for HLHS from 2004 to 2024. Patients without birth admission and no Stage-I-palliation were excluded.ResultsThe study included 9348 children and 2617 were diagnosed with an NDMHC. A 1-year-old child had an NDMHC incidence of 2% [1%-2%], a 5-year-old of 12% [11%-13%], a 10-year-old of 27% [25%-20%], and an 18-year-old of 55% [48%-62%]. If overall in-hospital days increase above the 75th percentile, the incidence increases to over 65%. Children with NDMHC were more likely treated at low-volume centers (NDMHC: 34% vs No NDMHC: 23%, P < .001) and came from low household income environments (NDMHC Low Income: 27% vs No NDMC Low Income: 24%, P < .001). Cox regression for the development NDMHC revealed prolonged hospitalization (75th total hospitalization length of stay) (2.26 [2.01-3.53], P < .001), treatment at low-volume centers (4.30 [2.72-6.81], P < .001) and low-income household (3.84 [3.10-5.71], P < .001) were predictors for NDMHC development.ConclusionAs a successfully palliated child enters adulthood, over half will have a neurodevelopmental and mental health condition. This percentage increase significantly as the overall days spent in-hospital increases. This report urges congenital cardiac providers to explore strategies to mitigate the mental health burden.

title: Sex differences in fibrillar collagen composition are linked to subcutaneous adipose tissue expandability and adipocyte precursor proliferation.
authorString: Vujičić M, Broderick I, Bauzá-Thorbrügge M, Perian C, Campanher Pereira G, Jansson PA, Blüher M, Benrick A, Wernstedt Asterholm I.
abstractText:
Background

Physiological expansion of subcutaneous adipose tissue (SAT) protects against harmful lipid deposition and metabolic disease and is generally greater in women than men. We hypothesised that sex differences in fibrillar collagen composition and remodelling contribute to differences in SAT expansion and function.

Methods

SAT from age- and BMI-matched men and women, SAT from male and female mice exposed to a high-fat diet to induce adipose tissue expansion and obesity, and publicly available human SAT and VAT RNA sequencing data sets were analysed. SAT was assessed by proteomics, histology, Western blot, qRT-PCR and flow cytometry. The 3T3-L1 preadipocyte cell line was used to test the effect of altered collagen type 1-to-3 ratio.

Results

Men showed greater SAT fibrosis than women. Fibrillar collagen levels correlated negatively with BMI in women but positively with cholesterol and liver enzyme levels in men. Despite similar adiposity, HFD-induced obese female mice had healthier metabolic profiles and fewer fibroinflammatory SAT changes than males. HFD preferentially induced Col1a1 in males and Col3a1 in females. Unchallenged male mice had a higher collagen type 1-to-3 ratio than females, and a similar sex difference was observed in humans. A lower, female-like collagen type 1-to-3 ratio increased preadipocyte proliferation. Consistently, acute HFD increased proliferation of SAT PDGFRβ+ adipogenic stem cells in females only.

Conclusions

Sex differences in fibrillar collagen composition and remodelling may promote greater SAT expansion in females by facilitating adipogenic precursor proliferation and limiting fibroinflammatory changes during obesity.

title: Etoposide-induced angina in a patient with small cell lung carcinoma: a case report.
authorString: Otsuka S, Chiba Y, Otsuka K, Shimazu K, Imagawa S, Hiraoka K, Yonezawa K, Anzai T, Iwashiro N.
abstractText:
Background

The combination of cisplatin and etoposide is a standard therapy for small cell lung cancer; however, ischemic heart disease is a known complication. We report a rare case of effort angina pectoris that worsened during initial treatment of small cell lung cancer with etoposide.

Case presentation

A 73-year-old Asian male was admitted to our hospital with effort angina. Coronary angiography revealed severe stenosis with significant calcification of the proximal right coronary artery. Computed tomography revealed a 21-mm-sized nodule in the right upper lobe and hilar lymphadenopathy suggestive of lung cancer. The patient underwent thoracoscopic wedge resection before coronary revascularization, and intraoperative findings indicated a small cell carcinoma with hilar lymph node metastases. Early postoperative definitive treatment consisting of chemotherapy with cisplatin plus etoposide and accelerated hyperfractionated radiation was planned. During the first chemotherapy session, on postoperative day 7, the patient complained of chest pain, and an electrocardiogram showed slight ST depression in leads V5 and V6 while receiving etoposide; nitroglycerin improved his symptoms. Although treatment was resumed with the administration of nicorandil the next day, the same symptoms were observed during the infusion of etoposide. Accordingly, chemoradiation therapy was suspended and revascularization of the right coronary artery was performed. Etoposide and cisplatin were readministered 3 days after revascularization, without any chest symptoms.

Conclusion

Chemotherapy for malignant tumors carries the risk of progression to coronary artery disease. To prevent serious ischemic events, sufficient discussions between oncologists and cardiologists and careful observation of chest symptoms are needed.

title: Deep learning denoising and deep learning-augmented contrast enhancement improve ultra-high-resolution photon-counting-detector CCTA image quality.
authorString: Steinmetz S, Kilburg A, Sanner AP, Kronfeld A, Grebe AW, Hell M, Varga-Szemes A, Emrich T, Bäuerle T, Brockmann MA, Othman AE, Halfmann MC.
abstractText:
Objective

Ultrahigh-resolution (UHR) coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) using a photon-counting detector (PCD) provides excellent spatial resolution but is limited by increased image noise. We evaluated whether deep learning (DL)-based denoising and contrast enhancement can further improve UHR-CCTA image quality.

Materials and methods

UHR-CCTA scans from 25 patients with coronary artery disease were retrospectively analyzed. Images were reconstructed at 0.2-mm slice thickness without and with quantum iterative reconstruction (QIR, Qoff-Q4), and subsequently processed using a DL tool for denoising and increasing iodine contrast enhancement. Subjective image quality (sharpness, noise, vessel wall delineation, and overall quality) was assessed by three radiologists using a 5-point Likert scale. Objective analysis included signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR), and coronary wall sharpness. Differences between image sets were analyzed using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests.

Results

DL-based CCTA demonstrated significantly superior subjective image quality across all parameters compared to standard reconstructions, with an overall median image quality ([interquartile interval, IQR]: 4 [3-5] versus 2 [2-3], p < 0.001). SNR and CNR were significantly higher for DL-based CCTA across all QIR levels (all p < 0.001). The highest values were observed for DL-based CCTAQ4 versus UHR-CCTAQ4 (SNR: 258.0 ± 147.5 versus 145.2 ± 50.1; CNR: 25.8 ± 17.1 versus 11.1 ± 4.5; both p < 0.001). Coronary wall sharpness was improved for DL-based CCTA for Q1-4 (all p < 0.027).

Conclusion

DL-based denoising and iodine contrast enhancement effectively reduce noise and improve anatomic detail in UHR-CCTA, providing incremental value beyond vendor-specific reconstruction, particularly at high QIR strength levels.

Key points

Question Deep learning reduces noise and enhances contrast in ultrahigh-resolution coronary CT angiography. Findings Image quality improves beyond standard iterative reconstruction methods, and vessel wall sharpness and diagnostic clarity significantly increase. Relevance statement This study aimed to determine at which levels of vendor-specific iterative reconstruction, DL-based denoising and contrast enhancement perform best in UHR CCTA, providing a foundation for future investigations on how these technical improvements may translate into diagnostic benefits.

title: Antenatal inflammation drives postpartum cardiac dysfunction in hypertensive disorders of pregnancy.
authorString: Bert S, Christensen AP, Bulletti M, Ward EJ, Wilcox UR, Dignam JP, Haider T, Yap EP, Malone KM, Maughan RT, Greco E, Dufton NP, Fanti S, Herrey A, Thronton S, Marelli-Berg FM, Perretti M, Nadkarni S.
abstractText: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDPs), including preeclampsia and gestational hypertension, are strongly associated with maternal cardiac dysfunction during and after pregnancy. We hypothesized that maternal inflammation drives persistent postpartum cardiac maladaptation after HDPs. We conducted a prospective longitudinal study assessing cardiac function and circulating inflammatory profiles during pregnancy and 3-6 months postpartum, complemented by a preclinical mechanistic mouse model recapitulating key antenatal and postpartum immune and cardiac features of HDPs. Here we show that distinct antenatal inflammatory signatures, including elevated chemokines, correlated with adverse left ventricular structure and function 3-6 months postpartum, despite resolution of systemic inflammation. Mechanistically, our preclinical HDP mouse model demonstrates that reduced antenatal progesterone, also observed in patients with HDPs, drives inflammation and postpartum cardiac dysfunction. Antenatal (embryonic day 14.5), but not postpartum (postpartum day 28), progesterone treatment prevented postpartum cardiac dysfunction, identifying both a potential mechanistic and therapeutic strategy to reduce long-term maternal cardiovascular morbidity.

title: Multiparametric assessment of TNNI3 variant phenotypes in human iPSC-cardiomyocytes correlates with disease severity in patients.
authorString: Staudt DW, Tran PP, Floyd BJ, Dunn K, Han D, Carhuamaca X, Serrano R, Hnatiuk AP, Bang S, Parikh VN, Ashley EA, Mercola M.
abstractText: Routine genetic testing of patients with cardiomyopathy has identified many causative genetic variants. However, in most instances, the impact of these variants on physiological function and clinical outcomes remains unclear. Here we develop a high-throughput human induced pluripotent stem-cell-based platform to measure the effects of variants in cardiac troponin I (encoded by TNNI3) on systolic and diastolic force generation and calcium handling. By integrating contractility and calcium signaling, we accurately distinguish pathogenic from nonpathogenic TNNI3 variants and characterize the pathogenic effects of variants of uncertain significance. Further, by evaluating the clinical presentations of patients with TNNI3 cardiomyopathy from a single site, we demonstrate that diastolic function in vitro correlates with age at onset (R<sup>2</sup> = 0.6), a measure of disease severity. The ability to comprehensively characterize in vitro variant effects that correlate with clinical outcomes should help identify mechanisms underlying variable disease severity and enhance the discovery of class-targeted treatments.

title: Contextualizing biological heterogeneity in brain structural normativity assessments across the aging continuum with the nearest neighbor normativity framework.
authorString: Leenings R, Winter NR, Ernsting J, Konowski M, Holstein V, Meinert S, Spanagel J, Barkhau C, Fisch L, Goltermann J, Gerdes MF, Grotegerd D, Leehr EJ, Peters A, Krist L, Willich SN, Pischon T, Völzke H, Haubold J, Kauczor HU, Niendorf T, Richter M, Dannlowski U, Berger K, Jiang X, Cole J, Opel N, Hahn T, ADNI consortium.
abstractText:
Background

Despite established consensus about the individuality of brain physiology and structural changes, current neuroimaging biomarker paradigms heavily rely on population averages. Here, we define normativity not as a single reference point but as a landscape of permissible configurations arising from diverse physiological manifestations.

Methods

We introduce the Nearest Neighbor Normativity (N3) framework, designed to parse the natural heterogeneity in brain structural measurements into a diversity-aware biomarker of brain structural decline. Through repeated comparisons within different demographic subgroups, N3 contextualizes an individual's measurements from several viewpoints along the aging continuum. Relying on local density estimation, it accommodates multiple, shared normative configurations within and across age groups. We use T1-weighted MRI data from 29,883 individuals for training and 7,013 individuals for validation, and benchmark our framework against Brain Age models and Normative Modeling. We evaluate each biomarker's ability to detect neurodegenerative diseases, using them as representative models of atypical brain structural decline.

Results

In group-level analyses, the N3 biomarker shows the largest effect sizes in the detection of Mild Cognitive Impairment, Alzheimer's Disease, and Frontotemporal Dementia. Similarly, the N3 biomarker achieves the highest predictive performance in the classification of neurodegenerative diseases on a single subject level. Notably, the N3 estimates remain stable across age and robust to compositional changes in the reference sample. Finally, correlation analyses indicate that it captures distinct and complementary aspects of brain structural variation compared to existing approaches.

Conclusions

Our findings underscore that rethinking normativity assessments to explicitly accommodate natural inter-individual variability can advance our collective efforts toward truly personalized patient care.

title: Relationship between the MTHFR C677T polymorphism and essential hypertension: A clinical correlation study.
authorString: Meng Y, Li F, Cheng W, Zhang L, Lu M, Li C.
abstractText:
Background

The methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR) C677T polymorphism affects homocysteine metabolism and may influence essential hypertension (EH), but the associated clinical phenotype in hyperhomocysteinemic patients remains unclear. We focused on differences between patients with the homozygous mutation (TT) genotype and those with non-TT genotypes.

Methods

A total of 30 patients with EH and hyperhomocysteinemia (Hcy≥15μmol/L) admitted to Jincheng General Hospital from March 1, 2025, to July 31, 2025, were enrolled. MTHFR gene polymorphisms were determined. According to the MTHFR C677T genotype, patients were assigned to the TT group and the non-TT group (CT and CC genotypes). Demographic characteristics, blood pressure measurements, and duration of hypertension of the two groups were recorded and compared. Biochemical measures including homocysteine (Hcy), folic acid, vitamin B12, blood lipids, and fasting blood glucose were measured. Pulse pressure, mean arterial pressure (MAP), pulse pressure index (PPI), and hypertension cumulative risk index were calculated. Spearman correlation analysis was used to examine associations between folic acid levels and Hcy, pulse pressure, and PPI.

Results

Compared with the non-TT group, the TT group had significantly higher concentrations of Hcy and vitamin B12, a significantly shorter hypertension duration, and significantly lower systolic blood pressure (SBP), pulse pressure, PPI, and hypertension cumulative load index. Spearman rank correlation analysis showed that folic acid levels correlated inversely with Hcy, pulse pressure, and PPI.

Conclusions

The association between the MTHFR C677T TT genotype and cardiovascular risk may be confounded by vitamin B12 nutritional status and disease duration, complicating interpretation of the genotype as a simple risk factor.

title: Liver transplant team involvement in level III and IV renal tumor thrombectomy: Perioperative and oncologic outcomes.
authorString: Zahalka AH, Brooks B, Bingham N, Gereta S, Woldu SL, Gaston K, Vagefi PA, Margulis V.
abstractText:
Purpose

Resection of renal cell carcinoma with inferior vena cava (IVC) tumor thrombus above the hepatic veins requires extensive liver mobilization using techniques derived from liver transplantation. We assessed whether dedicated liver transplant team involvement in radical nephrectomy with IVC thrombectomy for thrombi above the hepatic veins (level III and IV) was associated with perioperative and oncologic outcomes.

Materials and methods

In this unplanned, hypothesis-generating analysis of a single-center retrospective cohort (2018-2024), cases were classified by liver transplant team involvement, and intraoperative factors, 90-day outcomes, and survival were compared. Because liver transplant team involvement was adopted progressively, sensitivity analyses adjusting for year of surgery and restricted to the adoption period were performed.

Results

Of 36 cases, 18 (50%) involved the liver transplant team. Intraoperative factors were similar. Liver transplant team involvement was associated with fewer major complications (Clavien grade ≥3: 11% vs. 50%, P = 0.03) and less hepatic dysfunction (0% vs. 39%, P = 0.01) within 90 days, with similar recurrence-free and overall survival. Adjusting for cardiac bypass, liver transplant team involvement was associated with lower odds of major complications (odds ratio [OR] 0.05, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.005-0.57) and hepatic dysfunction (OR 0.04, 95% CI 0.002-0.83). After adjustment for year of surgery, point estimates were similar but neither association remained statistically significant (OR 0.13, 95% CI 0.01-1.24; OR 0.04, 95% CI 0.001-1.22).

Conclusions

Liver transplant team involvement was associated with fewer major complications and less hepatic dysfunction. Although this association could not be reliably separated from calendar time, these findings warrant prospective, multi-institutional evaluation of liver transplant team involvement in high-level renal tumor thrombectomy.

title: Feasibility Assessment of Smartphone Camera-Based Atrial Fibrillation Detection Compared With Portable Electrocardiogram: Single-Patient Case Study.
authorString: Patel B, Buckley D, Cruickshank G, Ginn C, Mogg L.
abstractText:
Background

Atrial fibrillation (AF) affects more than 33 million people globally, with many cases remaining undiagnosed due to the paroxysmal nature of the condition. Current portable AF detection devices require additional hardware, and their cost may limit their accessibility in community screening programs. Facial camera-based remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) is a novel alternative to conventional fingertip-based photoplethysmography (PPG) that enables contact-free cardiac rhythm assessment.

Objective

This study aimed to assess the technical feasibility of a novel smartphone camera-based facial rPPG AF detection system by comparing its performance with that of a portable electrocardiogram (ECG) device under real-world home monitoring conditions.

Methods

We conducted a prospective, single-patient volunteer case study involving a patient with diagnosed paroxysmal AF and atrial flutter with variable block over 12 consecutive days. Simultaneous 60-second recordings were scheduled 3 times daily using the electronRx smartphone app and a Kardia portable ECG device to obtain a total of 36 paired recordings. The primary outcome was device agreement in rhythm classification between the 2 systems. Secondary outcomes included assessment of the effect of signal quality on device agreement and analysis of discordant recordings to identify technical limitations.

Results

Of the 36 scheduled recording sessions, 35 were attempted, yielding 24 successful simultaneous recordings. Of these, 23 paired recordings met the quality criteria, and device agreement was achieved in 21 (91.3%) recordings. The smartphone system detected 4 of the 5 episodes classified as AF by the Kardia device and agreed with 17 of the 18 recordings classified as normal sinus rhythm. A total of 2 discordant cases were identified: 1 false negative associated with atrial flutter presenting as a fixed 3:1 atrioventricular block and 1 false positive related to poor signal quality due to suboptimal lighting conditions. Signal quality significantly affected performance, with 94.7% agreement in recordings of good quality compared with 75% in recordings of poor quality.

Conclusions

This case study demonstrates the technical feasibility of using a smartphone facial camera-based rPPG rhythm analysis for AF detection. The approach shows promise as an accessible screening tool. However, the single-patient design, data attrition resulting from synchronization and signal quality issues, and the identified technical limitations highlight the need for larger validation studies before clinical application can be considered.

title: Single-nucleus transcriptomics reveals cardiomyocyte injury and fibro-inflammatory remodeling in early PKP2-deficient ARVC.
authorString: Liu T, Wang Y, Zhang S, Liu X, Lin J, Wang J, Wu X, Zhang X, Guo X, Wu L, Zhang B.

journal.title: Journal of molecular and cellular cardiology

abstractText:
Background

Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (ARVC) is an inherited cardiomyopathy caused primarily by mutations in desmosomal genes, among which pathogenic PKP2 variants being the most common genetic cause. Previous studies on ARVC have mainly focus on its middle and late pathological stages, whereas the early cellular and molecular events triggered by PKP2 loss remain poorly defined.

Methods and results

We generated a cardiomyocyte-specific Pkp2 knockout mouse line and performed single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) to delineate the early cellular landscape of ARVC. PKP2 loss triggered pathological remodeling of cardiomyocytes and induced a large-scale phenotypic shift in cardiac fibroblasts from a homeostatic state to an activated, matrix-producing population. Concomitantly, proangiogenic endothelial subsets expanded and Ccr2+/Spp1+ proinflammatory macrophages accumulated, reshaping the cardiac microenvironment. Cell-cell communication network analysis demonstrated enhanced intercellular crosstalk at the early stage of ARVC, with aberrant activation of profibrotic and inflammatory signaling pathways. By integrating transcriptomic analysis, immunofluorescence staining and ligand-receptor interaction analysis, we identified CCN2 may serve as a potential mediator in early-stage PKP2-related ARVC.

Conclusion

Our study proposes a multicellular relay model of early ARVC pathogenesis and identifies CCN2 as a putative intercellular communication factor in PKP2-deficient hearts. These findings highlight intercellular communication networks as critical mediators of disease progression and potential therapeutic targets.

title: Heat shock proteins in DNA damage response and repair: A graphical review.
authorString: Zhao Y, Sin YY.
abstractText: Heat shock proteins (HSPs) are molecular chaperones primarily recognised for maintaining proteostasis, but increasing evidence indicates that they also regulate cellular responses to DNA damage. HSPs influence DNA damage sensing, checkpoint signalling, repair complex assembly, DNA repair, and damage tolerance through mechanisms that largely reflect chaperone-dependent regulation of client stability, assembly and localisation. This graphical review summarises experimental evidence linking HSP27, HSP40, HSP60, HSP70, HSP90, and HSP110 to major genome maintenance pathways, including homologous recombination, non-homologous end joining, mismatch repair, base excision repair, nucleotide excision repair, and translesion DNA synthesis. We examine how individual HSPs affect the stability, subcellular localisation, assembly, and activity of DNA repair and checkpoint proteins, while highlighting differences in the strength and type of supporting evidence. We also propose a conceptual "chaperone-to-repair shift", in which genotoxic stress may alter the relative engagement of HSP networks with DNA damage response (DDR) proteins. This proposed framework provides a testable perspective on the relationship between proteostasis and genome maintenance, without implying a universal switch from one function to the other.

title: The mitophagy-ferroptosis nexus in cardiac aging: a proposed exercise-responsive framework.
authorString: Rahmani BB, Saeidi A, Razi O, Hejazi K, Supriya R, Laher I, Zouhal H.
abstractText: Cardiac aging is traditionally framed as a progressive loss of energetic capacity, yet accumulating evidence indicates that iron-dependent lipid peroxidation and ferroptotic susceptibility may contribute to age-related myocardial vulnerability. Here, we integrate evidence linking mitochondrial quality control, membrane lipid remodeling, antioxidant capacity, and iron handling to the emergence of a ferroptosis-permissive state in aging cardiomyocytes. We further propose that aerobic exercise may shift this state toward greater resilience by coordinating mitochondrial turnover, redox adaptation, metabolic remodeling, and systemic physiological regulation. Evidence is strongest for exercise-responsive mitochondrial quality control, AMPK-SIRT1-PGC-1α signaling, and glutathione-dependent antioxidant defenses, whereas proposed links involving p53 compartmentalization, TIGAR/NADPH/FSP1 signaling, the Parkin-ACSL4 interface, and chronic hepcidin-ferroportin regulation in aged cardiomyocytes remain incompletely resolved. We therefore conceptualize ferroptotic susceptibility as a tunable, trajectory-dependent phenotype rather than an inevitable consequence of cardiac aging. Importantly, this framework distinguishes organelle-level mitochondrial stress and selective quality-control responses from whole-cell ferroptotic commitment. By separating established cardiac biology from cross-tissue inference and hypothesis-generating mechanisms, our model identifies experimentally testable interfaces through which exercise may preserve myocardial resilience and functional reserve during aging.

title: Risk-Oriented Assessment of Transfusion Medicine Knowledge Among Residents at the Lebanese University: A Cross-Sectional Survey.
authorString: Haddad A, Hamadeh W, Hamdan A, Abdayem C, Azzi G, Assi TB.

journal.title: Transfusion clinique et biologique : journal de la Societe francaise de transfusion sanguine

abstractText:
Background

Overall knowledge scores may obscure clinically important deficiencies in transfusion medicine. The objective is to assess the transfusion medicine knowledge among medical and surgical residents at the Lebanese University and identify knowledge gaps with potential implications for patient safety using a weighted score and a secondary risk-oriented item-level analysis.

Materials and methods

A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 216 clinical residents who completed a 40-item electronic questionnaire between January and March 2024. Knowledge scores ranged from 0 to 60, with a score of ≥40 defined as the passing threshold based on expert consensus. Low-performing safety-related items were also identified, and factors associated with passing were analyzed using multivariable logistic regression.

Results

The mean knowledge score was 39.3 ± 7.4/60, with 54.2% of residents achieving the predefined passing threshold. Surgical residents had higher adjusted odds of passing than medical residents (aOR 2.36, 95% CI 1.15-4.86; p = 0.01). Postgraduate year was also significantly associated with passing overall (p = 0.008), with PGY III residents showing higher adjusted odds than PGY I residents (aOR 4.11, 95% CI 1.77-9.55; p = 0.001). Low performance levels were identified in post-transfusion monitoring (22.2%), transfusion thresholds for severe cardiac disease (22.7%), infectious screening requirements (25.5%), indications for irradiated components (44.4%), and haemovigilance reporting responsibilities (50.5%).

Conclusion

Moderate overall transfusion medicine knowledge coexisted with important deficiencies across different dimensions of transfusion safety, including bedside decision-making, blood safety and haemovigilance. These findings identify priorities for targeted, competency-based education but should be interpreted in light of the single-institution design and the non-validated, expert-derived scoring and secondary risk-oriented framework.

title: Establishing a passive registry of patients with heart failure enabled by natural language processing and language models.
authorString: Portela GT, Krüger N, Schneeweiss S, Ngan K, Gu B, Lii J, Yang J, Vaduganathan M, Desai RJ.
abstractText:
Background

Significant budgetary and resource requirements for data collection remain a barrier to launch and maintain disease registries. Automated data collection from electronic health records (EHRs) is a possible solution, but certain data elements critical for research endeavors in heart failure (HF) are not routinely available as structured data fields.

Methods

Using EHRs from a large tertiary care system in Boston, we address this challenge by using natural language processing (NLP) and language models. First, patients with HF were identified using diagnosis codes and NLP of physician notes. Among the patients included, ejection fraction (EF) and New York Heart Association (NYHA) class were extracted using rule-based NLP. Large language models were used to extract social determinants of health (SDoH). EHRs were deterministically linked to insurance claims data from Medicare and Medicaid and state vital statistics files for a comprehensive view of healthcare receipt and outcomes.

Results

A total of 69,007 patients with HF were included, among whom mean age was 75.8 years (SD, 12.8) and 51.5% were female. 38,620 patients (56.0%) were classified into HF with reduced, mildly reduced, or preserved EF with average EF of 30.8% (SD, 7.0), 45.0% (SD, 1.7), and 61.9% (SD, 7.3), respectively. 215,627 valid NYHA class mentions were extracted for 16,147 patients (23.4%) and 67,432 patients (97.7%) had some element of social history recorded.

Conclusions

The infrastructure and processes we developed can facilitate a diverse portfolio of future research activities aimed at characterizing and improving outcomes of patients with HF.

title: Successful Implementation of Standardized Longitudinal Follow-up after Surgery for Congenital Heart Disease.
authorString: Devlin PJ, Gaynor JW, Viers S, Kennedy A, Lowery R, Booth E, Arbit M, Olsen R, Les A, Tomlinson AZ, Gonzalez K, Sanderlin R, O'Byrne M, Chen JM, Romano JC, Pasquali SK.
abstractText:
Background
