To understand and improve long-term congenital heart surgery outcomes, longitudinal data are essential but challenging to capture. We evaluated a novel program to facilitate routine longitudinal data collection.

Methods

Patients undergoing Society of Thoracic Surgeons Benchmark Operations at two centers (2007-2019) were included. Annual follow-up data (vital status and age-specific burden of disease questionnaires) were collected using an automated email system along with medical record and local registry data queries, with coordinator follow-up if needed. Completeness of follow-up and associated factors were analyzed in multivariable logistic regression.

Results

Of 4,075 subjects, vital status was captured for 98% (median follow-up 6.0 years; IQR 3.1-9.2). Vital status at one year was known for 95%; overall follow-up completeness (observed-to-potential follow-up time) was 81%. At least one follow-up questionnaire was completed by 85%, with 58% utilizing the automated email system. Those with genetic/non-cardiac abnormalities (OR 2.28, 95%CI 1.28-4.28), single ventricle palliation (Norwood OR 11.2, 95%CI 3.01-72.7; Glenn/hemi-Fontan OR 7.79, 95%CI 2.21-49.5), and tetralogy of Fallot repair (OR 2.43, 95%CI 1.11-5.59) had higher odds of known vital status. Follow-up questionnaire completion had higher odds for non-Hispanic white patients (OR 1.54, 95%CI: 1.27-1.86) and higher median income households (OR 1.05/$10,000, 95%CI: 1.01-1.09).

Conclusions

This program captured vital status and burden of disease, with one-year survival determined for nearly all patients. Automation reduced human resource needs by more than half. Future efforts will focus on expanding to other centers and improving follow-up for disadvantaged groups.

title: Impaired Left Atrial Contractile Strain and Late Pacemaker Implantation After the Cox-Maze Procedure Despite Maintained Sinus Rhythm.
authorString: Woo JU, Bae Y, Lee HJ, Jang WS, Yoon S, Kim YS, Song K.
abstractText:
Background

Late bradyarrhythmia requiring permanent pacemaker implantation remains a challenge after the Cox-Maze procedure. We evaluated whether left atrial contractile strain at 1 year predicts late pacemaker implantation in patients with normal sinus rhythm.

Methods

We retrospectively analyzed 259 patients who underwent the Maze procedure between 2012 and 2024 and maintained normal sinus rhythm at 1 year. Left atrial contractile strain was assessed using two-dimensional speckle-tracking echocardiography.

Results

Of 329 patients screened, 50 were excluded for atrial fibrillation recurrence at 1 year (1-year freedom from atrial fibrillation, 83.8%). During follow-up (median 58 months), 22 patients required pacemaker implantation. The optimal strain cutoff was -1.8% (area under the curve 0.658), and patients with impaired left atrial function (strain ≥ -1.8%) had a higher incidence of pacemaker implantation (log-rank P < 0.001). Impaired left atrial contractile strain (hazard ratio 3.99; 95% confidence interval, 1.41-11.35), fine fibrillatory waves (3.64; 1.32-10.01), and increased preoperative left atrial volume (1.004 per mL; 1.001-1.008) were independent predictors, and a combined model improved predictive accuracy (area under the curve 0.782). The excess risk was concentrated within the first 5 years after surgery (hazard ratio 8.47 versus 2.22 thereafter).

Conclusions

Impaired left atrial contractile strain 1 year after the Cox-Maze procedure independently predicts late pacemaker implantation despite stable normal sinus rhythm, particularly within the first 5 years, highlighting a dissociation between electrical and functional recovery. It may serve as a surrogate for atrial fibrosis and latent conduction disturbance, warranting intensified surveillance in high-risk patients during this period.

title: Changes in neurovascular coupling among older adults with poor level of cardiovascular health and its association with cognitive function.
authorString: Huang S, Zhao Z, Liu M, Wang J, Zeng X, Liu Y, Wang H, Yu X, Wang Z, Lv X.
abstractText:
Background

Cardiovascular health (CVH) affects cognitive function among older adults, yet its neuropathological mechanism remains unclear. Neurovascular coupling (NVC), the process by which the brain regulates cerebral blood flow to support neural activity, provides a promising perspective for exploring the association between CVH and cognitive function.

Methods

Our study included 64 community-dwelling older adults without dementia. According to their CVH scores, participants were stratified into ideal (score ≥ 9) or poor (score < 9) CVH groups. A series of cognitive assessments was used to evaluate global cognition and six cognition domains. Multimodal magnetic resonance imaging was also conducted to acquire perfusion and functional data, followed by the derivation of cerebral blood flow (CBF) and fractional amplitude of low-frequency fluctuation (fALFF) images. NVC was assessed using two spatially derived proxies, namely, the CBF-fALFF correlation coefficient and CBF/fALFF ratio. Multiple linear regression was used to examine whether the altered NVC was associated with the relationship between CVH and cognitive function in older adults, adjusting for sex, age, years of education, and marital status.

Results

Older adults with poor CVH (n=27) performed significantly worse in global cognition, memory, and visuospatial function. The poor CVH group exhibited a lower CBF/fALFF ratio in the cerebellar vermis and a higher ratio in the right inferior temporal gyrus. Moreover, the CBF/fALFF ratio in cerebellar vermis was significantly associated with visuospatial function (β=9.98, P=0.049).

Conclusions

These findings offer insights into changes in NVC associated with visuospatial function and provide empirical support for investigating the neuroimaging correlates of the relationship between CVH and cognitive function among older adults.

title: Behavioral and electrocardiographic evaluation of juvenile Rhinoclemmys punctularia (Daudin, 1801) (Aperema) submitted to isoflurane anesthesia.
authorString: Lins A, Cardoso DL, Quirino LE, Braga BSDS, Hartcopff PFP, Hamoy MKO, Hayasaki NDC, da Silva LAW, Guimarães DAA, Nascimento AJS, Nascimento ABV, Guimarães LPC, Hamoy M.
abstractText: Inhalational anesthesia is widely used in experimental studies; however, its cardiovascular effects remain poorly characterized in ectothermic vertebrates, particularly in juvenile chelonians. This study evaluated behavioral and electrocardiographic responses of juvenile Rhinoclemmys punctularia exposed to isoflurane, aiming to characterize anesthetic induction, maintenance, and recovery, and to assess its effects on cardiac electrical activity. Juveniles (48 h post-hatching) were exposed to isoflurane under controlled temperature conditions. Electrocardiographic recordings were obtained before anesthesia (control), during maintenance (5 and 10 min), and during recovery. Isoflurane induced rapid anesthetic induction followed by gradual recovery. During maintenance, significant bradycardia, reduction in ECG spectral power, decreased QRS amplitude, and prolongation of RR, PQ, and QRS intervals were observed, while sinus rhythm was preserved. These findings indicate a reversible depression of cardiac electrical conduction during anesthetic exposure. During recovery, parameters progressively returned toward baseline values. Juvenile R. punctularia exhibit marked cardiovascular sensitivity to isoflurane, reinforcing the importance of continuous cardiac monitoring in chelonians and contributing to comparative cardiovascular physiology.

title: PPARγ activation attenuates mechanical ventilation-induced diaphragmatic dysfunction.
authorString: Lu Q, Yu J, Yang L, Zhang Z, Xiao JJ, Wu X, Li G, Ma H.
abstractText: Mechanical ventilation is an indispensable life-support strategy, but prolonged use can induce ventilator-induced diaphragmatic dysfunction (VIDD), a major contributor to difficult weaning. The mechanisms underlying VIDD remain incompletely defined, particularly the role of epitranscriptomic regulation. In this study, we established a 24-hour mechanically ventilated rat model and performed integrated RNA sequencing and methylated RNA immunoprecipitation sequencing analyses. Mechanical ventilation induced marked transcriptomic remodeling and altered N6-methyladenosine (m6A) modification profiles in the diaphragm, accompanied by suppression of the peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor (PPAR) signaling pathway and downstream lipid metabolic networks. Integrated multi-omics analysis identified Pparg as a key candidate with reduced m6A modification and decreased expression. In dexamethasone-induced myotube atrophy, PPARγ expression was similarly reduced, whereas PPARγ activation attenuated atrophy-related molecular changes. IGF2BP3 was associated with Pparg mRNA and supported PPARγ expression. IGF2BP3 knockdown counteracted rosiglitazone-associated suppression of Atrogin-1 and MuRF1 in DEX-treated myotubes. In vivo, rosiglitazone-mediated PPARγ activation ameliorated mechanical ventilation-induced diaphragmatic contractile dysfunction, muscle fiber atrophy, and sarcomeric ultrastructural disruption. These findings suggest a possible m6A-associated IGF2BP3-PPARγ relationship in VIDD and support PPARγ signaling as a potential therapeutic target for ventilator-associated diaphragmatic atrophy.

title: Relationship between integrated myocardial flow reserve and obstructive coronary artery disease and major adverse cardiac events: Findings from the multicenter REFINE PET Registry.
authorString: Hijazi W, Mostafavi S, Shanbhag A, Ramirez G, Lemley M, Miller RJH, Kavanagh PB, Liang JX, Kamagate A, Alexanderson E, Carvajal-Juarez I, Slipczuk L, Travin M, Knight S, Le VT, Mason S, Packard RRS, Al-Mallah M, Acampa W, deKemp RA, Feher A, Rosamond T, Chareonthaitawee P, Buechel RR, Einstein AJ, Berman D, Dey D, Di Carli M, Slomka P.

journal.title: Journal of nuclear cardiology : official publication of the American Society of Nuclear Cardiology

abstractText:
Introduction

Although myocardial flow reserve (MFR) is a powerful marker of prognosis in patients undergoing positron emission tomography myocardial perfusion imaging (PET MPI), MFR cannot distinguish between epicardial and microvascular disease. Integrated MFR (iMFR) has been proposed to better detect epicardial coronary artery disease (CAD) by combining MFR with focal perfusion abnormalities.

Methods

We studied 34,761 patients as part of the REFINE PET registry of patients undergoing 82Rb or 13N-ammonia PET MPI. A subset of the above population without prior CAD (N=2,869) had a diagnostic angiogram within 180 days of PET MPI. Regions with an MFR <2 and a regional perfusion defect by total perfusion deficit (TPD) were defined as 'focally impaired' on a pixel by pixel basis. Regions with an MFR <2 without a regional perfusion defect were defined as 'diffusely impaired'. We also evaluated a separate angiographic cohort imaged with a third tracer, 18F-flurpiridaz, in the Flurpiridaz-301 trial (N=231). iMFR metrics were evaluated for the prediction of obstructive CAD and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE).

Results

Of the 34,761 registry patients, 9,782 (28%) experienced MACE over a median follow-up of 3.8 years. In the angiographic cohort, 1,597 of 2,869 patients (56%) had obstructive CAD. For the diagnosis of obstructive CAD, the extent of focally impaired myocardium had an AUC of 0.77 (95% CI 0.75-0.79), outperforming conventional minimal-segment MFR (AUC 0.73, 95% CI 0.71-0.74, P<0.001), but did not differ significantly from ischemic TPD or physician visual scoring. For the prediction of MACE, the extent of diffusely impaired myocardium provided the most prognostic information in multivariable Cox models (adjusted HR per SD 1.35, 95% CI 1.32-1.38; C-statistic 0.723), compared with global MFR (C-statistic 0.722) and focally impaired myocardium (C-statistic 0.711).

Conclusion

The extent of focally impaired myocardium by iMFR outperformed conventional MFR for the diagnosis of obstructive CAD but performed similarly to ischemic TPD and physician visual scoring. For the prediction of MACE, the extent of diffusely impaired myocardium provided more prognostic information than focally impaired myocardium or global MFR.

title: When CTPA is not Cardiac CT: An Acquisition-Aware Approach to Cardiovascular Findings Beyond Pulmonary Embolism.
authorString: Dutta N, Mekala B, Gupta D.
abstractText: CT pulmonary angiography (CTPA) answers a pulmonary vascular question, but the scan also covers the heart, pericardium and thoracic aorta. Cardiovascular findings in a CTPA report can be relevant, yet their interpretation is constrained by non-ECG-gated acquisition and pulmonary arterial phase contrast timing. This focused narrative review covers cardiovascular abnormalities including coronary artery and cardiac valve calcifications, pericardial effusion, pulmonary artery dilatation or right-heart enlargement, and thoracic aortic abnormalities. It explores the diagnostic value and limitations of these findings in clinical practice and offers a pragmatic framework for the acute medical take, to help clinicians decide which findings require urgent assessment, inpatient work-up, planned outpatient follow-up, or no further action.

title: Delayed Candida glabrata-associated infected thoracic aortic aneurysm after candidemia supported by identical serial MLVA profiles: a case report.
authorString: Takao R, Iwanaga N, Nakaji S, Hirayama T, Koga S, Ito Y, Ashizawa N, Takeda K, Ide S, Hosogaya N, Takazono T, Tanaka T, Miura T, Izumikawa K, Yanagihara K, Mukae H.

journal.title: Journal of infection and chemotherapy : official journal of the Japan Society of Chemotherapy

abstractText: Candida-associated infected aortic aneurysms (AAs) are exceptionally rare and frequently fatal. A 76-year-old man developed Candida glabrata candidemia after surgery for ascending colon cancer; the postoperative course was complicated by an anastomotic leak and intra-abdominal infection. Echinocandin therapy was discontinued because of profound neutropenia after 12 days of treatment, following negative blood cultures. Approximately 1 year later, an enlarging descending thoracic AA was detected and treated with thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR). Despite initially negative blood cultures, a normal or only minimally elevated serum β-D-glucan concentration, and negative Candida antigen testing, the aneurysm subsequently enlarged and required repeat TEVAR. Periaortic soft-tissue changes transiently regressed, further obscuring the diagnosis. Three months after the second TEVAR, computed tomography revealed renewed aneurysm enlargement and perigraft gas. C. glabrata was recovered from one of five blood culture sets. On the fifth day of admission, the patient experienced abrupt circulatory collapse with hemoptysis and died, likely due to aneurysm rupture through an aortobronchial fistula. All available intra-abdominal and bloodstream isolates of C. glabrata obtained throughout the clinical course had identical six-locus multiple-locus variable-number tandem-repeat analysis (MLVA) profiles. A prior episode of candidemia remains clinically relevant when a new or progressive aortic lesion develops, even after prolonged culture negativity. Serial aneurysm enlargement, periaortic inflammation, and delayed perigraft gas should outweigh apparently reassuring blood cultures or fungal biomarkers and should prompt early multidisciplinary reassessment, pursuit of tissue diagnosis when feasible, source control, and prolonged antifungal therapy.

title: Extent of myocardial deposition and its association with heart failure in ATTR amyloidosis: tomographic patterns of [99mTc]Tc-DPD uptake.
authorString: Sebastián Palacid F, Álvarez Mena N, Jaramillo López BM, Suazo Montero ÁR, Negrete Montiel PA, Redondo Del Río MP, Ruano Pérez R.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Rev Esp Med Nucl Imagen Mol (Engl Ed)
journal.title: Revista espanola de medicina nuclear e imagen molecular
journal.isoabbreviation: Rev Esp Med Nucl Imagen Mol (Engl Ed)

abstractText:
Objective

To assess the association between the percentage of myocardium affected as determined by SPECT/CT and heart failure in patients with ATTR cardiac amyloidosis, and to characterize the associated tomographic uptake patterns.

Materials and methods

ECG-gated SPECT/CT was performed in 147 patients with ATTR confirmed by [99mTc]Tc-DPD scintigraphy, a Perugini score of ≥ 2, and exclusion of AL amyloidosis. The polar maps, obtained from the summed images, were classified into six predefined tomographic patterns. The percentage of affected myocardium was derived from the calculation of myocardial extent provided by QPS/QGS, expressed inversely to the usual percentage of extent. LVEF was derived from the gated acquisition.

Results

Statistically significant differences were observed in the percentage of affected myocardium between the different tomographic patterns (p < 0.001), with the lowest values in the septal pattern (47.7 ± 8.0%) and the highest in the diffuse pattern (84.8 ± 12.9%). The presence of heart failure was associated with a higher percentage of affected myocardium both in the overall cohort (74% vs. 68%; p = 0.042) and in the subgroup of patients with Perugini grade 3 (75% vs. 68.5%; p = 0.026). There was no significant association between tomographic patterns and LVEF.

Conclusion

The percentage of affected myocardium calculated by SPECT/CT was associated with the presence of heart failure in patients with ATTR amyloidosis. The identification of tomographic patterns enabled this extent of myocardial involvement to be characterized, providing information that complements the Perugini scale. Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) derived from ECG gating was not associated with the uptake patterns. These results suggest that quantifying the extent of myocardial deposition by SPECT/CT may be of clinical interest in ATTR.

title: Machine learning-enhanced analysis of vascular regression in diabetic retinopathy.
authorString: Ma E, Dawkins BA, Hsu N, Rudenko Y, Xie J, Cai J, Griffin CT.
abstractText: Diabetic retinopathy is an ischemic retinal disease characterized by early capillary regression (i.e., vascular rarefaction) followed by pathological angiogenesis. Accurate quantification of vascular regression is essential for understanding disease mechanisms and evaluating therapeutic strategies, yet current methods often rely on manual counting of regression markers and remain limited in throughput and reproducibility. In this study, we identified regressed capillaries by constricted basement membrane sleeves that persist after endothelial cell loss. These sleeves immunostain positively for Collagen IV but are negative for the endothelial marker CD31. Using a streptozotocin-induced diabetic mouse model, we observed capillary regression across all three layers of the retinal vasculature, with more regression sleeves in the deep vascular plexus compared to the superficial and intermediate layers. To quantify capillary regression, we developed complementary workflows for detecting regression sleeves, including manual annotation in Adobe Photoshop, two semi-automated approaches using ImageJ and Python, and a fully automated deep-learning approach based on a UNet convolutional neural network. The deep learning model was trained using manually annotated images and generated prediction masks that closely matched manual annotations in independent test images. Across diabetic retinas, the UNet-based approach produced sleeve counts comparable to manual quantification. In addition to sleeve count, the UNet approach enabled quantitative assessment of sleeve length, revealing a trend toward increased average sleeve length in diabetic retinas compared with non-diabetic controls. Together, these findings establish a flexible, scalable, and reproducible toolkit for quantifying retinal vascular regression. This work may facilitate mechanistic studies of vascular remodeling and improve quantitative assessment of pathological vascular regression in early stages of diabetic retinopathy.

title: Tailored therapy for bradyarrhythmias: integrating leadless pacing, conduction system pacing, and cardioneuroablation.
authorString: Mazzotta R, Cosco L, Bernardini A, Paoletti-Perini A, Padeletti M, Milli M, Ricciardi G, Bambagioni G, Perrotta L, Pieroni M, Checchi L, Pieragnoli P, Giomi A.
abstractText: Bradyarrhythmias represent a heterogeneous group of disorders ranging from intrinsic cardiac disease to functional autonomic disturbances. Although conventional transvenous pacing remains the cornerstone of treatment, a uniform device-based approach may not adequately address the diverse pathophysiological substrates underlying bradyarrhythmias. Device-related complications, pacing-induced ventricular dysfunction, and the growing recognition of vagally mediated bradyarrhythmias have highlighted the need for a more individualized therapeutic strategy. Recent advances have expanded the available treatment options through the development of leadless pacing, conduction system pacing (CSP), and cardioneuroablation (CNA). Importantly, these therapies should not be viewed as interchangeable alternatives, but rather as complementary approaches targeting distinct clinical scenarios. Leadless pacing minimizes transvenous hardware and may be particularly advantageous in patients at increased risk of device-related complications, limited venous access, or low anticipated pacing requirements. CSP preserves physiological ventricular activation and may reduce the risk of pacing-induced cardiomyopathy in patients with a high expected ventricular pacing burden or a vulnerable ventricular substrate. Conversely, CNA provides a mechanism-based, device-free therapeutic option for carefully selected patients with functional, vagally mediated bradyarrhythmias. In this review, we propose a practical framework for patient selection based on three complementary phenotypes: the high-risk and low-pacing-burden patient, the high-pacing-burden and vulnerable ventricle, and the vagal phenotype (see Central Illustration). By integrating pathophysiology, anticipated pacing burden, ventricular susceptibility, and autonomic substrate, contemporary management can move beyond the traditional device-centered paradigm toward a tailored approach aimed at delivering the right therapy to the right patient.

title: Long-term cumulative exposure and longitudinal profiles of the cholesterol, high density lipoprotein, and glucose (CHG) index, versus the metabolic score for insulin resistance (METS-IR) for incident heart failure risk: A prospective cohort study.
authorString: Xu W, Li X, Yang J, Chen C, Wu S, Xia Y, Guo Y.
abstractText:
Background

The cholesterol, high-density lipoprotein, and glucose (CHG) index and the metabolic score for insulin resistance (METS-IR) are considered surrogate indexes of insulin resistance (IR). However, the associations of their cumulative exposure patterns and longitudinal profiles with incident heart failure (HF) have not been comprehensively investigated.

Methods

We included 71,078 participants aged 20-98 years from the Kailuan Study who completed three consecutive health examinations between 2006 and 2015. Time-weighted cumulative measures and longitudinal profiles of CHG and METS-IR were calculated to characterize long-term metabolic exposure. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate their associations with incident HF.

Results

During a median follow-up of 12.78 years, 1,803 incident HF events were documented. In the multivariable-adjusted model, each 1-SD increment in TW-cumCHG and TW-cumMETS-IR was associated with a higher risk of incident HF, with corresponding HRs of 1.27 (95 % CI, 1.21-1.33) and 1.37 (95 % CI, 1.28-1.48), respectively. Participants with jointly elevated TW-cumCHG and TW-cumMETS-IR had the highest risk of incident HF (HR, 1.71; 95 % CI, 1.51-1.94). K-means clustering identified three distinct longitudinal profiles for both CHG and METS-IR, with the persistently high groups exhibiting the greatest HF risk.

Conclusions

Higher cumulative exposure and persistently unfavorable profiles of CHG and METS-IR were independently associated with increased incident HF. Individuals with elevated levels of both indices had the highest risk of HF, suggesting that their concomitant elevation may reflect a greater cardiometabolic burden and highlighting the importance of comprehensive cardiometabolic risk management in HF prevention.

title: Integrative analysis of genome-wide DNA methylation and gene expression profiles associated with incident chronic kidney disease: the longitudinal Pros-RODAM cohort study.
authorString: Mungamba MM, Venema A, Purushothama MK, Meeks KAC, Chilunga FP, van der Linden EL, Hayfron-Benjamin CF, Sewani-Rusike CR, Vogt L, Born BVD, Darko SN, Owusu-Dabo E, Nkeh-Chungag BN, Agyemang C, Henneman P.
abstractText: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is increasing rapidly in African populations, yet its molecular determinants remain poorly characterised. While epigenome-wide studies have been largely confined to high-income settings, comparable longitudinal epigenetic data from African populations are scarce, despite distinct genetic and environmental contexts. We conducted a longitudinal epigenome-wide study of CKD in an African population, integrating DNA methylation and gene expression to identify epigenetic changes associated with CKD and related kidney function decline. DNA methylation was profiled using the Illumina EPIC (850K) array in 274 Ghanaian participants from the RODAM-Prospective cohort (92 incident CKD cases and 182 matched controls), providing 548 DNA methylation observations across baseline and ∼6-year follow-up, with high-quality DNA methylation data available at both timepoints. Epigenome-wide association studies (EWAS) were performed for incident CKD, change in estimated glomerular filtration rate (ΔeGFR), and change in urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (ΔACR), adjusting for demographic, clinical, and technical covariates. Differentially methylated regions (DMRs) were identified using bumphunter with family-wise error rate control. Differential gene expression (RNA-seq) analyses were conducted, followed by covariate-adjusted expression quantitative trait methylation (eQTM) analyses to link methylation with gene expression. At baseline, significant differentially methylated positions (DMPs) were detected at INF2 (incident CKD), CLIP4 (ΔeGFR), and TMEM109 (ΔACR), alongside DMRs at HLA-DPB1 and SH2D1B (incident CKD) and ZFP57 and OR2T11 (ΔACR). At follow-up, a progression-related DMR in C4orf39/TRIM61 (ΔACR) was identified, with recurrent signals at hypermethylated HLA-DPB1 and hypomethylated ZFP57 and OR2T11 across timepoints. Integrative eQTM analysis revealed methylation-expression associations at recurrent loci including ZFP57, HLA-DRB5, SLC39A4, and SPATC1L, with predominantly inverse associations at ZFP57, HLA-DRB5, and SLC39A4, highlighting associations with metabolic and immune regulatory pathways. We identified epigenetic changes associated with incident CKD and kidney function decline in an African population. These methylation signals, supported by gene expression patterns, highlight immune and kidney-related pathways associated with CKD risk and progression. Our findings provide a foundation for future studies investigating the potential of epigenetic markers in CKD risk stratification and prevention in African populations. European Commission; European Research Council.

title: A simple algorithm allows triaging of dogs with mitral valve disease into cardiac or noncardiac causes of dyspnea.
authorString: Rishniw M, Dickson D, Caivano D, Vatne L, Harris J, Pavelkova E, Hung YW.

journal.title: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association

abstractText:
Objective

To create a simple algorithm for diagnosis of congestive heart failure (CHF) in dogs with myxomatous mitral valve disease (MMVD).

Methods

Data were collected between November 2, 2015, and December 7, 2017, from dogs presented to investigators after a tentative diagnosis of CHF by first-opinion clinicians. Investigators completed a data-submission form and provided a final diagnosis of CHF or subclinical MMVD. Data included each of the 8 variables of the original algorithm. Variables that did not change diagnostic accuracy were removed from the model.

Results

120 dogs were included: 46 with CHF and 74 with subclinical cardiac disease and an alternate diagnosis for clinical signs; 82 dogs (36 with CHF) were referred for coughing. All dogs with CHF had loud or palpable murmurs, as did 59 without CHF. Forty-five dogs with CHF and 26 without CHF lacked sinus arrhythmia. All nonpanting dogs with CHF and 7 of 56 without CHF had tachypnea or dyspnea. All dogs with CHF had moderate-to-severe left atrial enlargement versus 25 of 35 dogs without CHF. Examined in series, these 4 variables yielded an algorithm sensitivity of 98% and specificity of 95% for diagnosing CHF.

Conclusions

Clinicians who are presented with a dog suspected of having CHF secondary to MMVD should be able to determine whether CHF is likely using 3 to 4 simple variables: a loud or palpable murmur, lack of sinus arrhythmia, tachypnea or dyspnea, and at least moderate left atrial enlargement.

Clinical relevance

This algorithm might improve first-opinion practitioners' diagnosis of CHF in dogs with MMVD.

title: Emergency Action Plans in Aquatic Sports: A Call to Action and Guide for Aquatic Leadership.
authorString: McClintick DJ, Casper M, Shah A, Denq W, Friedman EM.
abstractText: With increasing participation in aquatics athletics at the youth, amateur, and professional levels, it is critical to provide sport and venue-specific emergency action plans (EAP) to ensure safe participation for athletes with and without cardiovascular disease. Current EAPs are typically geared toward land-based sports and do not address major aquatic-specific obstacles including identification of emergency, extraction, automated external defibrillator availability, emergency medical services access, and transport to hospital. This document provides guidance on creating EAP for aquatic athletes based on sport type and venue (pool-based, open-water immersion, and open-water adjacent) with guidance and proposed solutions for each. It also highlights the growing need for detailed aquatic EAPs to ensure safe athlete participation for water-based athletes. Finally, we call upon leaders in aquatic sports to involve all stakeholders and consider implementing more structured training in addition to basic life support, cardiopulmonary resuscitation, and first-aid to maximize aquatic athlete safety.

title: Impact of the 2026 Dyslipidemia Guideline on ASCVD Reclassification and Statin Recommendations in MESA.
authorString: Murphy BS, Hershey MS, Huang S, Nam Y, Post WS, Bertoni AG, Blumenthal RS, McClelland RL, DeFilippis AP.
abstractText:
Background

The 2026 American College of Cardiology (ACC)/American Heart Association (AHA)/Multisociety Guideline on the Management of Dyslipidemia recommends the use of the PREVENT (Predicting Risk of cardiovascular disease EVENTs) equations to predict atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk while concurrently revising previous risk-category thresholds. The impact of these reclassifications is yet to be described.

Objectives

The authors characterized ASCVD reclassification and statin recommendations under the 2026 guideline, evaluated clinical events under this reclassification, and examined risk enhancement with risk enhancers and coronary artery calcium (CAC) burden.

Methods

Adults (N = 6,098) from the MESA (Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis) were assessed, comparing the Pooled Cohort Equations (PCE) and 2013 thresholds to PREVENT with 2026 thresholds. We evaluated the degree of directional reclassification, impact on statin recommendations, and risk enhancement with biomarkers and CAC burden.

Results

Over a median follow-up of 10 years, 6.0% of participants had an ASCVD event. PREVENT reclassified 16.4% to a lower and 13.1% to a higher risk category as compared to the PCE. The statin recommendation under PREVENT was 50.4% compared to 55.2% under PCE. Of those who were no longer recommended for statin use, 4.9% went on to have an event. Individuals who were reclassified downward but had elevated CAC or any risk-enhancing factors had a higher event rate.

Conclusions

Adherence to the 2026 guideline may lead to a small net downward reclassification of predicted ASCVD risk. Statin recommendations will fall modestly, however, not accompanied by a substantial number of subsequent events. Risk enhancers and elevated CAC identify higher risk subgroups than their PREVENT risk would suggest, emphasizing their supporting role in risk prediction.

title: Noninvasive pulse wave velocity measurement: technological progress, clinical validation, and translation challenges.
authorString: Zhang M, Zheng M, Han L, Wu Z, Sun J.
abstractText: Pulse wave velocity (PWV) is increasingly recognized as a vital noninvasive metric for assessing arterial stiffness and an established independent predictor of cardiovascular risk. Despite its well-recognized clinical value, the accurate and reliable measurement of PWV remains methodologically challenging due to inherent physical ambiguities, technological heterogeneity across devices, and a lack of comparability between measurements obtained by different systems. This review provides a comprehensive synthesis of the physical foundations, mainstream detection technologies, signal-processing pipelines, and current clinical standardization status for PWV assessment. Although classical frameworks such as the Moens-Korteweg and Bramwell-Hill equations theoretically link PWV to the mechanical properties of the arterial wall, the intrinsic dependence of PWV on instantaneous blood pressure complicates the precise evaluation of structural arterial stiffness in clinical settings. We categorize existing measurement modalities into four principal types: mechanical-pressure sensing, optical techniques, advanced medical imaging, and emerging contactless approaches, each demonstrating unique trade-offs among measurement fidelity, clinical applicability, and operational convenience. Presently, three major barriers hinder the clinical translation of novel technologies: insufficient operational automation, inadequate cross-population validation, and a scarcity of longitudinal prognostic evidence. Future transformative advancements will likely rely on AI-driven, fully automated continuous monitoring systems optimized for real-world daily settings, large-scale multicenter trials across diverse demographics, and extensive long-term cohort studies utilizing wearable devices. These developments will collectively extend PWV assessment from intermittent clinical evaluation toward decentralized, personalized cardiovascular risk management.

title: A Guytonian Atlas of Venous Return in Septic Shock: Reconstruction of Hemodynamic States.
authorString: Chalkias A, Mavridis T, Papagiannakis N, Katsifa K, Nikolaidis I, Laou E, Prekates A, Tselioti P.
abstractText: To reconstruct venous return physiology across published studies of septic shock and characterize the distribution of circulatory states represented in the literature. Exploratory physiologic reconstruction study. Secondary analysis of published hemodynamic observations. Adult patients with septic shock reported in studies containing sufficient information for reconstruction of mean circulatory filling pressure analogue (Pmca) and related parameters including venous return driving pressure (VRdP) and resistance to venous return (RVR). None. A total of 150 observations were available. Median Pmca, central venous pressure (CVP), VRdP, and RVR were 17.3 mm Hg, 9.0 mm Hg, 7.9 mm Hg, and 1.04 mm Hg/min/L, respectively. Empirical quartiles identified four recurrent circulatory phenotypes: reduced filling pressure/gradient, preserved venous return, elevated venous pressure, and high-resistance venous return. The preserved venous return pattern demonstrated the highest median cardiac output (CO), whereas the high-resistance pattern exhibited the lowest flow despite comparable filling pressures. In exploratory adjusted analyses incorporating available vasopressor exposure and fluid-therapy context, VRdP remained strongly associated with CO (β, 1.03 L/min/mm Hg; 95% CI, 0.80-1.25; p < 0.001). When Pmca and CVP were entered separately, Pmca was positively associated with CO (β, 1.02; 95% CI, 0.79-1.25; p < 0.001), whereas CVP was inversely associated with CO (β, -1.03; 95% CI, -1.26 to -0.80; p < 0.001). Published hemodynamic observations in septic shock occupy distinct Guytonian phenotypes characterized by different combinations of circulatory filling pressure, venous pressure, and RVR. Reconstruction of venous return geometry may provide a physiologic framework for interpreting circulatory heterogeneity in septic shock.

title: Self-Reported Clinician Confidence in and Familiarity With Long COVID Care Following Continuing Medical Education Webinars: Unmatched Pre-Post Study.
authorString: Xin VZ, Kling SMR, Hosakote S, Adewuya R, Bragdon C, Brown-Johnson C, Lazarow S, Levy V, Miglis MG, Moskatel LS, Paleru A, Patel ZM, Quach TC, Simpson N, Stranberg S, Sum-Ping OR, Yang PC, Shaw JG, Bonilla H, Geng LN, Grossman L.
abstractText: An estimated 18-23 million Americans have had long COVID (LC), yet 54% and 72% of US physicians reported not being confident in diagnosing and treating LC, respectively. Continuing medical education (CME) is crucial to maintaining and improving clinical skills, and CME that incorporates need-based educational methods is associated with improved patient outcomes. Given limited clinician familiarity with LC, there is a need for an effective, widely accessible LC CME program. This study assessed the effectiveness of 2 Stanford University-organized LC CME webinars, which aimed to provide comprehensive, up-to-date evaluation and management strategies through multidisciplinary didactic presentations and question-and-answer sessions. Data from webinar attendees were collected through CME registration and prewebinar/postwebinar surveys. Registration surveys consisted of multiple-choice questions on profession, practice setting, experience treating vulnerable populations, and perception of LC. Prewebinar/postwebinar surveys consisted of multiple-choice questions on perception of LC, confidence in diagnosing LC, and familiarity with LC care. Prewebinar/postwebinar responses were compared using logistic regression, with Bonferroni adjustment to account for multiple testing. Statistical significance was defined as P<.05. The August 2024 webinar had 449 registrants: 48.6% (n=218) were physicians, and 29.0% (n=130) reported an affiliation with an academic medical center. The attendee count was 248, with 116 and 90 attendees completing the prewebinar and postwebinar surveys, respectively. The proportion of respondents indicating that LC is a very or somewhat serious problem did not significantly differ between the pre-CME (93/115, 80.9%) and post-CME (75/88, 85.2%) surveys (adjusted P>.99). There were significant pre-to-post increases in the proportion of respondents indicating they were very confident in their LC diagnosis ability (11/102, 10.8% to 25/79, 31.6%; adjusted P=.004) and very familiar with LC care (10/91, 11.0% to 22/75, 29.3%; adjusted P=.02). The May 2025 webinar had 468 registrants: 52.6% (n=246) were physicians, and 24.8% (n=116) identified an academic medical center affiliation. The attendee count was 264, with 135 and 119 attendees completing the prewebinar and postwebinar surveys, respectively. The proportion of respondents indicating that LC is a very or somewhat serious problem did not significantly differ between the pre-CME (105/134, 78.4%) and post-CME (102/118, 86.4%) surveys (adjusted P=.49). There was a significant pre-to-post increase in the proportion of respondents indicating they were very familiar with LC care (12/116, 10.3% to 60/111, 54.1%; adjusted P<.001). CME participation was associated with significant increases in the proportions of respondents reporting confidence in diagnosing LC and familiarity with LC care, highlighting the potential of virtual CME programs to support clinician education.

title: Assessing outcomes and recovery following anterior cervical discectomy and fusion in patients aged 75 years and older: a propensity score-matched review with 2-year follow-up.
authorString: Rezner AC, Hannon KM, Tippins NP, Alentado VJ, Mobasser JP, DePowell JJ, Potts EA, Anokwute MC.
abstractText: The longitudinal efficacy of anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (ACDF) in the population of older individuals is debated. The authors aimed to determine the long-term outcomes of patients aged ≥ 75 years compared to those of their younger peers. A prospectively collected quality registry of patients undergoing elective ACDF was retrospectively reviewed. Cohorts included patients who were ≥ 75 years compared to < 75 years of age. Patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) were collected at baseline and 3, 12, and 24 months postoperatively. Demographics, surgical characteristics, complications, Eating Assessment Tool-10 (EAT-10) dysphagia rates, North American Spine Society satisfaction, and PROMs were compared between groups. All analyses were repeated following 1:1 propensity score matching by demographics, baseline PROMs, comorbidities, symptoms, and surgical factors. A total of 1155 patients met inclusion criteria with 1082 (94%) aged < 75 years and 73 (6%) ≥ 75 years. Prior to propensity score matching, the ≥ 75-year cohort had a lower mean BMI (29.0 ± 4.3 vs 30.9 ± 6.6 kg/m2, p = 0.028), fewer daily smokers (4.1% vs 16%, p = 0.005), fewer currently employed workers (5.5% vs 52%, p < 0.001), and lower rates of anxiety (15% vs 28%, p = 0.017) and depression (12% vs 23%, p = 0.041). The ≥ 75-year cohort had more osteoarthritis (47% vs 24%, p < 0.001) and coronary artery disease (23% vs 6.5%, p < 0.001). The ≥ 75-year cohort had significantly better neck pain visual analog scale, arm pain visual analog scale (AP-VAS), Neck Disability Index, EuroQol 5-Dimension, and EuroQol visual analog scale baseline scores (all p < 0.05), but similar modified Japanese Orthopaedic Association scores (p = 0.2). By the 2-year follow-up, all PROM scores were similar except for the AP-VAS score, for which the ≥ 75-year cohort reported less arm pain (1.2 ± 2.5 vs 1.7 ± 2.7, p = 0.044). Propensity score matching yielded 138 patients, with 69 in each cohort. Residual demographic differences included the ≥ 75-year cohort having fewer employed workers (5.8% vs 42%, p < 0.001) and more individuals with a professional degree (25% vs 8.7%, p = 0.012). The propensity score-matched cohorts achieved parity in all baseline, postoperative, and change-from-baseline PROM scores through the 2-year follow-up. Patients aged ≥ 75 years experience benefit comparable to that of younger patients across outcome measures following propensity score matching. Age alone does not predict worsened outcomes in carefully selected older patients undergoing elective ACDF, and older patients may benefit from knowledge of comparable favorable outcomes.

title: Task Force 11: Additional Cardiac Conditions and Considerations in Competitive Athletes.
authorString: Hsu JJ, Baggish AL, Economy KE, Emery MS, Link MS, Singh T, Stewart KM, Levine BD, Kim JH, Lagerche A.

journal.title: Medicine and science in sports and exercise

abstractText: The recently updated AHA/ACC Scientific Statement: Clinical Considerations for Competitive Sports Participation for Athletes with Cardiovascular Abnormalities provides a comprehensive framework for guiding clinicians in the evaluation and management of competitive athletes. Divided into 11 Task Forces, it covers a broad range of cardiovascular diseases and clinical scenarios. Task Force 11 was devoted to cardiac conditions and considerations in athletes not included in the other Task Forces. Here, we present the detailed rationale for the clinical considerations covered in this section of the Scientific Statement. These topics include hypertension, commotio cordis, pulmonary embolism, performance-enhancing drugs and supplements, exercise in extreme environments (specifically altitude and scuba diving), and pregnancy.

title: Task Force 10: Clinical Considerations for the Care of Masters Athletes with Underlying Cardiovascular Disease.
authorString: Dineen EH, Bӧrjesson M, Chung EH, Eijsvogels TMH, Baggish AL, Levine BD, Thompson PD, Kim JH.

journal.title: Medicine and science in sports and exercise

abstractText: Masters athletes are individuals ≥35 yr of age who place a high premium on exercise training and competition. This document details important cardiovascular conditions, risk factors, and data-driven discussion, which serve as the rationale for Section X from the 2025 AHA/ACC Scientific Statement: Clinical Considerations for Competitive Sports Participation for Athletes Cardiovascular Abnormalities. Disease-specific risk stratification and shared decision-making are the cornerstones for Masters athletes when considering competitive sports participation. Coronary artery disease, atrial fibrillation, incidental myocardial fibrosis, aortic enlargement and aneurysms, and valvular heart disease are included in this Task Force document.

title: Task Force 9: Clinical Considerations for the Care of Athletes with Cardiac Channelopathies.
authorString: Gray B, Chung EH, Etheridge S, Link MS, Kim JH, Baggish AL, Levine BD, Ackerman MJ.

journal.title: Medicine and science in sports and exercise

abstractText: Cardiac channelopathies, including long QT syndrome, catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, Brugada syndrome, and short QT syndrome, are heterogeneous conditions, which can lead to varying risks in athletes depending on their symptoms, disease severity, genotype, and therapies initiated. Historically, athletes with these conditions were excluded from participation with blanket restrictions, despite an absence of data. More recently, a number of studies have provided more scientific evidence to guide decision making and have been incorporated into these guidelines for athletes with cardiac channelopathies. Many athletes with these conditions may be supported in their decision to return to play as part of a shared decision-making model when they have been assessed, risk stratified, and appropriately treated by a specialist with expertise in these conditions.

title: Task Force 8: Care of Competitive Athletes with Arrhythmias and Sudden Cardiac Arrest: Clinical Considerations and Electrocardiogram Interpretations.
authorString: Darden D, Chung EH, Harmon KG, Kim JH, Link M, Salerno J, Baggish AL, Levine BD, Lampert R.

journal.title: Medicine and science in sports and exercise

abstractText: This document outlines recommendations for managing competitive athletes with arrhythmias and risks of sudden cardiac arrest, emphasizing individualized risk assessment, shared decision-making, and return-to-play protocols tailored to each athlete's cardiac profile and sport demands. It provides evaluation strategies for ventricular arrhythmias, implantable cardiac defibrillators, atrial fibrillation, supraventricular tachycardia, Wolff-Parkinson-White pattern/syndrome, and syncope, alongside guidance for electrocardiogram interpretation in athletes. A key focus is placed on differentiating between low-risk and high-risk conditions, with recommendations for treatment strategies and ongoing monitoring to ensure athletes' safety.

title: Task Force 5: Clinical Considerations for Myocarditis and Selected Cardiovascular Conditions, Including Valvular Heart Disease.
authorString: Guseh JS, Allen LA, Castelletti S, Baggish AL, Levine BD, Kim JH, Wilhelm M, Martinez MW.

journal.title: Medicine and science in sports and exercise

abstractText: Athletes with myocarditis, pericarditis, valvular heart disease, and other acquired cardiovascular conditions require careful evaluation when considering competitive sports participation. This document outlines key clinical considerations, risk factors, and expert consensus, serving as the rationale for Section V of the recent AHA/ACC Scientific Statement: Clinical Considerations for Competitive Sports Participation for Athletes with Cardiovascular Abnormalities. Disease-specific risk stratification and shared decision-making are essential in determining return-to-play eligibility. This Task Force document addresses myocarditis, pericarditis, the cardiovascular impact of respiratory viral infections, incidental myocardial fibrosis, Kawasaki disease, infiltrative cardiomyopathies, and valvular heart disease.

title: Task Force 4: Clinical Considerations for the Care of Athletes with Genetic Cardiomyopathies.
authorString: Gati S, Ackerman MJ, Baggish AL, Kim JH, Levine BD, Maron M, Martinez M, Day SM.

journal.title: Medicine and science in sports and exercise

abstractText: The updated AHA/ACC Scientific Statement on Clinical Considerations for Competitive Sports Participation for Athletes with Cardiovascular Conditions presents the clinical considerations for athletes with genetic cardiomyopathies, including hypertrophic, dilated, arrhythmogenic, and left ventricular hypertrabeculation. This ACSM Official Pronouncement complements the 2020 ACC/AHA Scientific Statement by providing athlete-specific context, practical guidance for shared decision-making, and genotype-informed risk assessment for competitive sports participation, moving away from blanket sports disqualifications. Sports participation recommendations for each condition are tailored to risk levels, symptomatology, and genotype. Regular follow-ups and close surveillance are advised. This evolving approach underscores the importance of individualized care, ongoing research, and the integration of new data to better inform shared decision-making on the risks and benefits of competitive sports in athletes with cardiomyopathies.

title: Task Force 3: Ethical and Legal Aspects of Sports Participation.
authorString: Shah AB, Allen LA, Dickert NW, Kim JH, Levine BD, Lampert R, Halle M, Baggish AL.

journal.title: Medicine and science in sports and exercise

abstractText: Competitive sports eligibility recommendations historically have endorsed a paternalistic care model in which physicians unilaterally determined eligibility for competitive athletes with cardiovascular disease. However, competitive sport participation may have implications for athletes that are not obvious to clinicians in the absence of effective engagement. Shared decision making is supported by fundamental ethical principles, has been endorsed in other realms of cardiology, and now represents the preferred approach to determine future sports participation among competitive athletes diagnosed with cardiovascular disease. The primary emphasis of this task force is to discuss the rationale for and clinical implementation of shared decision making during consideration of competitive sports participation among athletes with cardiovascular disease, and to highlight potential legal implications.

title: Task Force 1: Sports Classifications.
authorString: Wasfy MM, Emery MS, Kim JH, Baggish AL, Kovacs RJ, Levine BD.

journal.title: Medicine and science in sports and exercise

abstractText: Competitive sports differ with regards to their physiological demands and risk of collision/impact. With the goal of informing disease-specific recommendations for athletes with cardiovascular disease, we present the sport-specific physiology inherent to the typical practice of common competitive sports. We also classify sports by collision/impact risk, which is particularly relevant to athlete antiplatelet and anticoagulant use. Finally, we discuss how sport-specific cardiovascular adaptations to exercise training manifest on athletes' cardiovascular testing.

title: Compendium of Task Forces for Clinical Considerations for Competitive Sports Participation for Competitive Athletes with Cardiovascular Abnormalities.
authorString: Kim JH, Levine BD, Baggish AL.

journal.title: Medicine and science in sports and exercise

abstractText: The scientific statement on competitive sports participation for competitive athletes with cardiovascular abnormalities, sponsored by the American Heart Association and American College of Cardiology, was recently published. The following is a compendium of Task Forces, composed of international experts in sports cardiology, sports medicine, sports science, and the respective clinical topics, that forms the basis and rationale for the clinical considerations presented in the scientific statement. This compendium of Task Forces represents an official statement by the American College of Sports Medicine.

title: A Comparison of Different Models to Compute Cardiac Output by Open-Circuit Inert Gas Wash-In.
authorString: Faricier R, Gregory DW, Keir DA.

journal.title: Medicine and science in sports and exercise

abstractText: Cardiac output (Q̇) can be measured non-invasively during exercise using the open-circuit acetylene (C2H2) uptake method. However, it is unclear whether different calculation techniques for these breathing-based Q̇ measurements yield consistent values and how variations in breathing patterns affect them. This study compared breathing-derived Q̇ estimates from three validated models (Wagner et al.: WAG, Gan et al.: GAN, and Iterative: ITER) and examined the effect of doubling breathing frequency on these estimates during continuous cycling exercise. Fourteen healthy adults completed two 28-min constant-work-rate cycling stages at moderate (MOD) and heavy (HVY) intensities. At each stage, Q̇ was measured under normal, self-selected breathing (NF) and under controlled high-frequency breathing (HF) at 200% of NF. For every C2H2 uptake trial, Q̇ was calculated using WAG, GAN, and ITER models. Doubling breathing frequency had model-specific effects on Q̇ estimates. WAG produced significantly lower Q̇ during HF breathing compared with NF at both MOD (3.3±1.1 L·min -1; p<0.001) and HVY (2.8±1.8 L·min -1; p<0.001) intensities. In contrast, ITER yielded significantly higher Q̇ under high-frequency breathing (MOD: -1.7±1.0 L·min -1 and HVY: -3.0±1.6 L·min -1; p<0.001 for both). GAN showed only a small significant difference between breathing conditions at MOD (-0.4±0.7 L·min -1; p=0.039), but not at HVY (p=0.845). These findings demonstrate that breathing frequency can meaningfully influence C2H2-derived Q̇ estimates and that computational models differ markedly in their sensitivity to ventilatory pattern. GAN appears to be the most robust to altered breathing frequency compared to WAG and ITER. Consistency in model selection is essential when using inert-gas uptake techniques to assess Q̇ during exercise.

title: Cardiorespiratory Fitness as Mediator in the Association Between Physical Activity and Health-Related Quality of Life in Patients with CMD or OA.
authorString: Schumacher CCA, Wildekamp M, Jelsma JGM, van den Akker-Scheek I, Bouma AJ, Dekker R, van Dijk ML, van Hooff M, Te Loo LM, van Mechelen W, Portegijs E, Zwerver J, Vrijsen J, LOFIT-consortium.

journal.title: Medicine and science in sports and exercise

abstractText: Diseases like cardiovascular metabolic disease (CMD) and osteoarthritis (OA) impact health-related quality of life (hr-QoL). In the general population, hr-QoL is associated with physical activity (PA), sedentary time (ST) and cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF). This study aims to examine 1) associations between device-based and self-reported PA and ST, and hr-QoL, and 2) the influence of self-reported CRF in these associations in people with (or at risk for) CMD and/or OA. Data from the Lifestyle front Office For Integrating lifestyle medicine in the Treatment of patients (LOFIT) study was used. Participants included patients with (or at risk for) CMD and/or OA (n=273) within the Netherlands. PA and ST were measured using device-based (activPAL™) and self-reported methods (International Physical Activity Questionnaire - Short Form and Marshall Sitting Questionnaire). CRF was assessed by estimating peak oxygen uptake per kilogram bodyweight (VO2peak mL·kg -1·min -1) using the FitMáx questionnaire. Hr-QoL was assessed using EQ-5D-5L. The associations were examined using linear regression and cross-sectional mediation models. Higher levels of device-based, and self-reported PA were associated with higher hr-QoL (b=0.007, 95% CI=0.000, 0.013 per 1000 steps, b=0.001 95% CI= 0.000, 0.002 per 30 minutes). Higher levels of device-based and self-reported ST were associated with lower hr-QoL (b=-0.006, 95% CI=-0.012, -0.000 per 30 minutes, b=-0.004, 95% CI=-0.007, -0.001 per 30 minutes). A cross-sectional indirect association via CRF was observed in the association between PA and hr-QoL. Higher PA and lower ST are associated with enhanced hr-QoL, where CRF influences the relationship between PA and hr-QoL in this patient population. Reducing ST could be a more feasible first step, if increasing PA is challenging. Moreover, the influence of CRF emphasizes the need for interventions focusing on improving fitness levels.

title: State of the Art of Aortic Valve Reimplantation for Aortic Root Aneurysms.
authorString: David TE.
abstractText: This article describes the development of aortic valve-sparing operations and their current status in surgical practice. They are classified into two general types of operations: aortic root remodeling and aortic valve reimplantation. Both techniques have been modified over the years from their original descriptions, but both remain useful in appropriately selected patients with aortic root and proximal aortic aneurysms, provided the aortic valve cusps are reasonable. Aortic valve reimplantation has proven more durable in young patients with aortic root aneurysms associated with genetic syndromes, whereas remodeling of the aortic root may be appropriate for older patients with ascending aortic aneurysms, dilated sinotubular junction, and secondarily dilated aortic sinuses. These operations were developed to preserve the native aortic valve and have expanded the armamentarium to treat patients with aortic root aneurysms and reasonably normal aortic cusps. In addition to a description of their development, a summary of current results of aortic valve reimplantation worldwide is presented, along with the author's personal perspective on its reproducibility.

title: Impact of Right Ventricular Dysfunction on Acute Kidney Injury and Major Adverse Cardiac and Cerebrovascular Events in Isolated Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting.
authorString: Aksoy R, Yiğit F, Timur B, Baş K, Aydogdu NC, Karpuzoğlu OE, Kocogullari CU.
abstractText:
Introduction

Right ventricular dysfunction (RVD) may influence perioperative hemodynamics after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). This study evaluated the association between preoperative RVD, defined by tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE), and postoperative acute kidney injury (AKI) and major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) after isolated CABG.

Methods

This retrospective single-center cohort included 392 adults undergoing isolated CABG between 2020 and 2023. RVD was defined as TAPSE < 17 mm. AKI was assessed at 24 and 48 hours according to Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) criteria. MACCE was evaluated as a predefined composite outcome. Logistic regression was used to explore factors associated with AKI and MACCE.

Results

Preoperative RVD was present in 2.3% of patients and was associated with a higher rate of KDIGO stage 1 AKI at 24 hours (P < 0.001). RVD was not independently associated with MACCE. Higher preoperative white blood cell count (odds ratio [OR] 1.13, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.03 - 1.24; P = 0.013) and KDIGO stage at 48 hours (OR 7.44, 95% CI 3.32 - 18.77; P < 0.001) were associated with MACCE.

Conclusion

Preoperative RVD was associated with early renal vulnerability after CABG but not with MACCE. Postoperative AKI severity and preoperative inflammatory status were independently associated with MACCE. These exploratory findings require validation in larger cohorts and suggest that right ventricular assessment may improve perioperative risk stratification.

title: Establishment and Assessment of a Predictive Model for Atrial Fibrillation Complications Following Off-Pump Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting - A Retrospective Case-Control Study.
authorString: Sun J, Wang H, Zhang Z, Song D, Wang X, Wei X, Liu C, Zhao W, Tian Y.
abstractText:
Introduction

Postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF), the most common arrhythmia after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), occurs in 15 - 50% of cases.

Objectives

To investigate the incidence and risk factors of POAF after off-pump CABG (OPCABG) and to establish a nomogram prediction model.

Methods

This retrospective study enrolled 179 patients who underwent OPCABG between October 2018 and October 2022. Patients were divided into POAF (n = 43) and non-POAF (n = 136) groups. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent risk factors. A nomogram was developed and evaluated for discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility.

Results

POAF incidence after OPCABG was 24.04%, peaking on postoperative day two. Independent predictors identified were age, hypertension, left atrium anteroposterior dimension > 40 mm, New York Heart Association (NYHA) class ≥ III, and intraoperative potassium < 4.5 mmol/L. A nomogram incorporating these factors was developed. Validation showed excellent discriminative power (area under the curve = 0.919, 95% confidence interval: 0.8747 - 0.9637), good calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow P = 0.80), and significant clinical utility via decision curve analysis across a wide probability range (0.2% - 98%).

Conclusion

Age, hypertension, left atrium anteroposterior dimension > 40 mm, NYHA class ≥ III, and intraoperative potassium < 4.5 mmol/L were identified as independent risk factors for POAF after OPCABG, and these factors can serve as predictors for POAF. By implementing appropriate health management strategies, the POAF complications following OPCABG may be reduced.

title: H3K9 demethylase KDM3A potentiates interferon signaling and macrophage-driven inflammation in atherosclerosis.
authorString: Siebeler R, Chen HJ, Kuznetsova T, Neele AE, van der Velden S, Gijbels MJJ, Griffith GR, van Roomen CPAA, Prange KHM, Boshuizen MCS, Seijkens TTP, Palm KCA, Mokry M, Lutgens E, Hoeksema MA, de Winther MPJ.
abstractText: Macrophages drive atherosclerosis through inflammatory activation programs shaped by metabolic and epigenetic reprogramming. H3K9 methylation enforces heterochromatin states and represses transcription, whereas removal of this histone modification creates transcriptionally permissive chromatin. Here, we identified KDM3A-mediated H3K9 demethylation to enhance chromatin accessibility at interferon (IFN) signaling loci, thereby promoting IFN production and downstream IFN-dependent transcriptional and chemokine responses. In a mouse model of atherosclerosis, hematopoietic Kdm3a deficiency reduces lesion size, necrotic core formation, and neutrophil recruitment. Mechanistically, Kdm3a-deficient macrophages show impaired chemokine secretion and reduced neutrophil recruitment both in vitro and in vivo. In primary human macrophages, KDM3A knockdown suppressed IFN responses; consistently KDM3A-dependent gene signatures were enriched in IFN-inducible macrophages within human atherosclerotic plaques, and computational modeling predicted a shift toward more stable plaque phenotypes upon KDM3A inhibition. Together, these findings establish KDM3A as an epigenetic regulator that sustains IFN-driven macrophage activation and promotes progression of atherosclerosis, nominating KDM3A as a potential target for selectively modulating IFN-dependent inflammation.

title: Agreement of an invasive angiography-derived computational model of coronary microvascular physiology against continuous thermodilution.
authorString: Taylor DJ, Newman T, Tlałka K, Yones E, Anigboro K, Saxton H, Xu X, Biancardi AM, Gosling R, Czechowicz K, Narracott A, Hose DR, Ciupek D, Maino A, Marin F, Fawaz S, Halliday I, OxAMI Investigators, Gunn JP, De Maria GL, Keeble TR, Morris PD.
abstractText: Coronary microvascular dysfunction is associated with myocardial ischaemia and an adverse prognosis, but accurate invasive assessment is technically challenging, requires dedicated hardware and increases procedure time and cost. Assessment can be performed with three-dimensional (3D) computational fluid dynamics (CFD) modelling, but this technique lacks robust in vivo validation. In this study, we compared the accuracy of a 3D CFD method against continuous thermodilution (CIT). Patients with acute and chronic coronary syndromes, undergoing CIT and angiography-derived assessment, were prospectively recruited from two tertiary cardiac centres. Invasive coronary angiographic images were used to reconstruct 3D anatomy in silico. Microvascular resistance reserve (MRR) and absolute flow were computed using 3D CFD in reconstructed coronary arteries. Invasive pressure measurements, recorded during fractional flow reserve assessment, informed the CFD boundary conditions. Paired flow results were available for 131 arteries from 89 patients. Median FFR was 0.81 [0.70 - 0.89] and 108 (81%) vessels contained an epicardial stenosis. Median computed MRR was 2.31 [1.83 - 3.00], which was significantly lower than CIT assessed MRR (2.79 [2.21 - 3.52], z = 3.57, p = 0.0004). There was evidence of a moderate relationship between computed and measured MRR (ρ = 0.58, p < 0.0001) and area under the receiver operator characteristic curve was 0.77 (95% CI 0.68-0.86), indicating fair classification. There was a moderate relationship between computed and measured hyperaemic vessel inlet flow (ρ = 0.44, p < 0.0001). For both MRR and flow, agreement improved at lower, more clinically relevant, values. In this clinical validation study, when compared with CIT, the novel CFD method demonstrated a moderate correlation, and fair diagnostic accuracy. This CFD method may be a useful, low-cost and less-invasive tool in the assessment of microvascular physiology that could complement current invasive techniques.

title: Loneliness and barriers to medication adherence in older adults: A multicenter cross-sectional study.
authorString: Brazzolotto BF, Bertoldi K, Bernardelli RS, Monti ACB, Tonet C, Furlan LS, Faria GN, Nogueira GB, Hornung FL, Fernandes KBP, Baena CP.
abstractText: Population aging is linked to the increase of chronic diseases and use of multiple medications. Consequently, medication non-adherence constitutes a global challenge. Therefore, we aimed to analyze the factors associated with the implementation phase of non-adherence. A multicenter cross-sectional study was conducted with older adults (age ≥ 60) in outpatient clinics of the public health system in Brazil. Medication adherence was assessed by the Measure of Adherence to Treatment (MAT), with non-adherence defined by a score below 5 points. Data were obtained through structured interviews, including the evaluation of loneliness (UCLA-BR scale) and barriers (adapted BMQ), and analyzed using multivariable logistic regression (Wald, p < 0.05). The study included 597 patients (M age = 71.3, SD = 7.2, 56.3% female) with comorbidities (cardiovascular 84.4%, endocrinological 82.4%). Non-adherence was present in 22.4% (n = 134) and was independently associated with recruitment site (Curitiba vs. Londrina: OR = 1.878, 95% CI [1.119, 3.153], p = 0.017), belief-related barriers (OR = 2.259, 95% CI [1.434, 3.557], p < 0.001), and practical barriers (OR = 2.662, 95% CI [1.361, 5.207], p = 0.004). A graded association emerged between loneliness and non-adherence: each additional point in the UCLA-BR score increased the odds of non-adherence by 3.0% (OR = 1.030, 95% CI [1.013, 1.047], p < 0.001). The findings reveal implementation non-adherence as a sociobehavioral phenomenon. Loneliness, practical and belief barriers, and recruitment site were independently associated with higher odds of non-adherence and could be potential targets for adherence interventions in an older population.

title: Health Care Utilization Among Patients With Coronary Artery Disease Using mHealth Wearable Devices: Feasibility Observational Study.
authorString: Bardhan I, Clifford G, Basit M, Willett D, Guo T, Taylor H.
abstractText:
Background

Although prior research has explored patient engagement with health care providers through software applications such as patient portals, the impact of patient engagement with mobile health (mHealth) technologies on subsequent utilization of health care resources remains poorly understood. Specifically, it remains unclear whether physiological data collected from wearable devices can be linked to future health care encounters across different modes of care utilization.

Objective

This pilot study was aimed at evaluating the feasibility of an mHealth prototype for analyzing cardiovascular disease outcomes and health care utilization among patients using digital health interventions. Specifically, we examined the feasibility of integrating physiological data from wearable devices to examine associations with future care utilization, offering early evidence for the effectiveness of patient engagement with mHealth platforms.

Methods

Patients with a history of coronary artery disease were recruited from the cardiology clinic of a large academic medical center. Before data collection, the study coordinator trained 20 patients on the use of Garmin devices, of whom 19 were included in the analyses. Data collected from the use of wearable devices were analyzed together with electronic health record data. Patient health outcomes were tracked from June 2019 to May 2021, including approximately 1500 health care encounters that encompassed hospital and outpatient visits, telehealth visits, and other encounters. Beyond establishing the feasibility of the mHealth platform, this work provided preliminary evidence of associations between (1) mHealth device use and future health care utilization and (2) physiological data and the frequency of future health care encounters.

Results

This study demonstrated the feasibility of an mHealth prototype for collecting and analyzing data to measure care utilization among patients with cardiovascular disease. Participants' use of the wearable mHealth device was associated with a statistically significant lower frequency of subsequent hospital and outpatient visits but greater utilization of other health care services, such as procedures, infusions, and medication refills, during the study period. However, none of these associations were statistically significant when the pretreatment period was restricted to the COVID-19 era. Minimum heart rate was associated with a higher frequency of future hospital and outpatient utilization, whereas activity time was associated with a higher frequency of procedural and refill visits.

Conclusions

This pilot study provides preliminary evidence that mHealth device use is associated with a reduction in future inpatient and outpatient visits and an increase in the number of visits for other health care services. It also indicates that patients' physiological data, such as minimum heart rate and activity time, are associated with the frequency of future health care encounters. These findings should be interpreted as exploratory signals rather than statistically definitive conclusions. This study provides proof of concept that an integrated mHealth platform can generate physiologically meaningful measures associated with subsequent care utilization, supporting its potential as a scalable tool for patient engagement and care coordination.

title: Deep-Learning Analysis of Peripheral Blood Smear for Prediction of Acute Inflammatory States and Chronic Comorbidities: Development and Internal Validation Study.
authorString: Jang J, Lee M, Park YR, Song J.
abstractText: Peripheral blood smear (PBS) examination provides morphological information on immune cells that reflects systemic pathophysiology, yet whether it can be used to predict systemic states has not been systematically established. This study aimed to develop and evaluate an integrated deep learning framework that leverages cell-level morphology from routine PBS examinations to discriminate acute inflammatory states and chronic comorbidities. An integrated deep learning framework was developed for PBS analysis, in which cell-level morphological features were extracted and aggregated into slide-level representations to predict systemic states. A total of 51,369 PBS examinations were used for self-supervised cell-level pretraining and 9211 for slide-level downstream tasks. Outcomes comprised acute inflammatory states and chronic comorbidities. Acute inflammatory states included white blood cell (WBC) count (categorized as low, normal, or high), elevated C-reactive protein (CRP), elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), and septic shock. Chronic comorbidities included the Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI), cardiovascular disease (CVD), chronic kidney disease (CKD), and diabetes mellitus (DM). Discriminative performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) with 95% CIs, computed on the test set of the development dataset and on the holdout dataset. The framework was compared with a demographic model based on age and sex and with a cell-type-only model without morphological features. As a secondary analysis, temporal validation was performed using a chronological split. The framework discriminated acute inflammatory states, achieving development and holdout AUROCs of 0.852 (95% CI 0.836-0.867) and 0.849 (0.833-0.864) for WBC count, 0.891 (0.870-0.913) and 0.896 (0.876-0.915) for CRP, 0.838 (0.794-0.878) and 0.844 (0.799-0.882) for ESR, and 0.849 (0.807-0.886) and 0.822 (0.783-0.853) for septic shock. Discrimination of chronic comorbidities was more modest but consistent across the 2 datasets, with AUROCs of 0.792 (0.762-0.818) and 0.781 (0.751-0.808) for CCI, 0.696 (0.665-0.727) and 0.680 (0.654-0.708) for CVD, 0.724 (0.690-0.755) and 0.728 (0.696-0.756) for CKD, and 0.645 (0.610-0.680) and 0.638 (0.603-0.674) for DM. The framework significantly outperformed the cell-type-only model for all outcomes in both datasets but did not significantly outperform the demographic model for CVD in the holdout dataset or for DM in either dataset. AUROCs in the temporal holdout dataset ranged from 0.621 for DM to 0.883 for CRP, consistent with those in the temporal development test set (0.666 to 0.889). An integrated deep learning framework for automated PBS analysis can provide information associated with inflammation-related laboratory results and clinical outcomes, with stronger discrimination for acute inflammatory states than for chronic comorbidities. These exploratory findings suggest the potential of deep learning-based PBS analysis as a novel approach to assessing systemic states in clinical practice.

title: Brassica rapa L. leaf hydroalcoholic extract attenuates L-NAME-induced hypertension in rats: associations with the Ang II-NO axis, oxidative stress, and inflammatory markers.
authorString: Dhondsekar D, Mandlik D.
abstractText: Brassica rapa L. leaves are a potential source of phenolic and flavonoid compounds associated with antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities. This study evaluated the effects of Brassica rapa L. leaf hydroalcoholic extract (BRLHE) in L-NAME-induced hypertension in rats. 48 rats were allocated to six groups (n = 8/group). L-NAME (40 mg/kg/day) was administered orally for 28 days, with concurrent BRLHE administration (100, 200, or 400 mg/kg/day) and captopril (25 mg/kg/day). Endpoint analyses included six animals per group. BRLHE exhibited total phenolic content of 34.50 ± 0.70 mg GAE/g extract, total flavonoid content of 11.86 ± 0.43 mg QE/g extract, and a 2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl IC₅₀ of 33.70 µg/mL. LC-MS/MS tentatively identified 11 phytoconstituents, including Apigenin, Berberine, Luteolin, Kaempferol, Curcumin, β-sitosterol, Caffeic acid, Rutin, p-coumaric acid, Quercetin, and Naringenin. BRLHE (400 mg/kg) reduced systolic blood pressure (120.8 ± 9.86 vs. 186.0 ± 20.52 mmHg), diastolic blood pressure (81.43 ± 10.33 vs. 145.9 ± 19.21 mmHg), and mean arterial pressure (94.49 ± 9.38 vs. 159.3 ± 19.50 mmHg) compared with L-NAME alone (P < 0.001 for all). BRLHE also improved electrocardiographic parameters, increased tissue SOD, GSH, CAT, and NOx, and reduced MDA, angiotensin II, NF-κB, TNF-α, and IL-6. Quantitative RT-PCR demonstrated increased AKT1 and NOS3/eNOS mRNA expression. Histopathological evaluation revealed attenuation of L-NAME-induced structural alterations in the cardiac, aortic, and renal tissues following BRLHE treatment. Overall, BRLHE attenuated L-NAME-induced hypertensive and associated biochemical alterations, supporting further preclinical investigation.

title: Implication of Perivascular Adipose Tissue as a Potential Therapeutic Target for the Vascular Defensive Actions of Incretin-Based Therapies and SGLT2 Inhibitors.
authorString: Balakumar P, Khan NA, Easwaran V, Orayj KM.
abstractText: Cardiovascular disease is a predominant cause of illness in individuals with type 2 diabetes mellitus and obesity. Although glucose reduction has traditionally been the principal therapeutic target for treating hyperglycemia, recent cardiovascular outcome trials have revealed that incretin-based therapies and sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors provide significant cardiovascular benefits beyond merely lowering blood glucose levels. The precise mechanisms underlying the multifaceted vascular effects of these therapies are not fully understood. Perivascular adipose tissue (PVAT) has been identified as an active player in regulating vascular tone and inflammation. Under physiological conditions, PVAT exhibits anticontractile and vasoprotective effects; however, under metabolic and cardiovascular pathological conditions, PVAT undergoes inflammatory and oxidative remodeling, which can lead to endothelial dysfunction, increased arterial stiffness, and hypertension. Recent experimental and translational studies suggest that incretin-based therapies and SGLT2 inhibitors may help improve the homeostasis of PVAT, consequently enhancing vascular function and regulating blood pressure. Despite these developments, the potential role of PVAT as a target for metabolic therapies has not been thoroughly reviewed. This review aims to address this critical knowledge gap and proposes PVAT and its signaling as novel therapeutic targets through which incretin-based treatments and SGLT2 inhibitors could provide vascular protection, thereby redefining cardiometabolic pharmacotherapy.

title: Microplastic Detection in the Ascending Aorta: An Exploratory Study Using Pyrolysis-Gas Chromatography/Mass Spectrometry (Py-GC/MS).
authorString: Shen H, Hou Y, Tang Y, Liu T, Zhang Z, Huang H, Chen Y, Shen Z.
abstractText: Microplastics (MPs) have emerged as significant environmental pollutants that have been detected in various human tissues.
