We applied 9.4 T magnetic resonance imaging to evaluate atherosclerotic lesions. Single-cell RNA sequencing was performed on carotid arteries. Apolipoprotein E (ApoE) knockout mice with caspase-1 deletion and macrophage-specific cGAS knockdown were used for in vivo validation. JASPAR prediction and dual-luciferase reporter assays were implemented to verify transcriptional regulation of NLRP3.

Key results

IR substantially aggravated atherosclerotic progression, accompanied by elevated pyroptosis-related gene expression in macrophages within atherosclerotic plaques. Mechanistically, IR promoted cytoplasmic mtDNA release to activate the cGAS/STING/TBK1 axis and cause p-IRF3 nuclear translocation. Phosphorylated IRF3 bound to the NLRP3 promoter and enhanced its transcription. Genetic ablation of caspase-1 or macrophage-specific cGAS knockdown alleviated IR-driven AS progression.

Conclusions and implications

Macrophage pyroptosis drives IR-accelerated AS progression through the mtDNA/cGAS/STING/p-IRF3 axis-dependent transcriptional up-regulation of NLRP3. Targeting the cGAS-STING pathway may provide a therapeutic strategy for IR-associated atherosclerotic plaque progression.

title: Dynamics of Mitochondrial Structure, Biogenesis and Function in Skeletal Muscle of Critically Ill Patients.
authorString: Wickert A, Grunow JJ, Wollersheim T, Engelhardt LJ, Groß S, Timm S, Ochs M, Meinhardt J, Stenzel W, Boschmann M, Weber-Carstens S, Fielitz J.
abstractText:
Objectives

To define the timing and phenotype of mitochondrial ultrastructural remodeling and electron transport chain (ETC) function in skeletal muscle during early critical illness.

Design

Secondary analysis of a prospective observational study with serial muscle biopsies.

Setting

Adult ICU.

Patients

Thirty-three mechanically ventilated ICU patients (median age, 49 yr; 27% women) with Sequential Organ Failure Assessment greater than or equal to 9 on three consecutive days; skeletal muscle biopsies of the vastus lateralis muscle at ICU day 5 (n = 29) and day 15 (n = 22). Healthy subjects served as controls.

Interventions

None.

Measurements and main results

Vastus lateralis biopsies were analyzed by electron microscopy with stereology, quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR), Western blotting, and spectrophotometric ETC enzyme assays (reported per tissue weight and normalized to citrate synthase [CS]). Intact mitochondrial profiles were reduced vs. controls (fold change vs. controls: day 5, 0.24 [0.18-0.34]; p = 0.039 and day 15, 0.20 [0.16-0.33]; p = 0.011) and disturbed profiles increased (day 5, 5.62 [3.20-7.17]; p < 0.001 and day 15, 5.20 [3.67-6.36]; p = 0.001), with reduced volume density of intact mitochondria (day 5, 0.33 [0.20-0.49]; p = 0.009 and day 15, 0.32 [0.21-0.50]; p = 0.005). Inner mitochondrial membrane surface-to-volume ratio was reduced at day 5 (0.69 [0.49-0.89]; p = 0.022) and remained unchanged at day 15. Complex III tissue activity was reduced at day 5 (85.6 [22.1-133.3] vs. 151.4 [100.5-205.0]; p = 0.015) and day 15 (50.5 [36.0-69.8]; p = 0.001), remaining reduced after CS normalization (day 5, 0.83 [0.34-1.49]; p = 0.040 and day 15, 0.87 [0.65-0.93]; p = 0.007). Complex IV activity remained reduced before and after CS normalization at both time points (all p < 0.001). CS activity declined by day 15 (56.3 [52.7-65.1] vs. 95.6 [80.1-133.0]; p = 0.001 and day 15 vs. day 5; p = 0.041). qRT-PCR and Western blot supported reduced ETC components and altered biogenesis signaling.

Conclusions

Skeletal muscle mitochondrial ultrastructure is altered by ICU day 5 and remains abnormal at day 15, with persistent complex III/IV dysfunction after CS normalization. These findings define an early sustained mitochondrial remodeling phenotype in skeletal muscle during critical illness.

title: Fatal Congenital Pulmonary Lymphangiectasis and Beckwith-Wiedemann Syndrome in a Newborn: A Case Report.
authorString: Kivikallio A, Kero A, Laurikainen T, Mattila JM, Arola A, Lehtonen L, Laine J.

journal.title: Pediatric and developmental pathology : the official journal of the Society for Pediatric Pathology and the Paediatric Pathology Society

abstractText: Congenital pulmonary lymphangiectasis (CPL) is a rare developmental disorder characterized by the dilatation of the lymphatics of the lung. CPL can occur in a primary or secondary setting and has been reported in various genetic syndromes. Here, we describe a newborn with fatal CLP together with Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome (BWS). The newborn presented with cyanosis soon after birth and died at the age of 3.5 hours due to severe hypoxemia leading to acidosis and cardiac dysfunction. Pathological examination revealed severe CLP as well as adrenal and pancreatic findings suggestive of BWS. The latter diagnosis was confirmed via methylation analysis, as the infant showed a sporadic maternal loss of methylation of IC2. To our knowledge, CPL has previously not been reported with BWS.

title: Hyperuricemia, disease activity, and 10-year cardiovascular risk in chronic inflammatory arthritis: a post-hoc analysis of the CARMA project.
authorString:
Avilés-Hernández A, Lamuedra A, Sánchez-Alonso F, Castañeda S, López R, Sánchez CO, Rey JS, Moreno Gil MP, Belmonte MA, Bachiller J, Pinto-Tasende JA, Juan A, Rueda A, Barbadillo C, Nolla JM, Lasanta ML, Babío Herraiz J, Chamizo Carmona E, Expósito SR, Manero FJ, Pardo SM, Tornero J, González-Gay MÁ, Andrés M, CARMA Project Collaborative Group
.
abstractText:
Objectives

To determine the prognostic impact of hyperuricemia on cardiovascular events and its association with inflammatory markers and disease activity in patients with chronic inflammatory arthritis (CIA).

Methods

Post-hoc analysis of a 10-year prospective cohort (2010-2022) including 1,552 patients with CIA and 349 controls from 67 Spanish hospitals. Hyperuricemia was defined as serum urate (SU) >6.8 mg/dL at baseline, and its impact on major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) during follow-up was assessed using multivariable logistic regression. Associations of hyperuricemia and SU levels with inflammatory markers and individual (swollen joint count, tender joint count, global VAS) and composite disease activity indices (DAS28, BASDAI) were analyzed using Pearson correlation and Mann-Whitney U test.

Results

Hyperuricemia prevalence was 11.2% in both CIA and controls, with a mean serum urate level of 5.0 ± 2.3 in the CIA group and 5.0 ± 1.4 in controls. Hyperuricemia independently increased the risk of MACE in CIA (adjusted OR 1.87, 95% CI 1.23-2.86), particularly in axial spondyloarthritis (adjusted OR 4.02, 95% CI 1.96-8.24), but not in rheumatoid arthritis or psoriatic arthritis; SU levels were not predictive. Hyperuricemia correlated with higher hsCRP levels in axial spondyloarthritis, psoriatic arthritis, and controls, but not in rheumatoid arthritis. No associations were found with ESR or disease activity indices.

Conclusion

Baseline hyperuricemia is an independent prognostic factor for cardiovascular events in CIA, particularly in axial spondyloarthritis, but not in non-inflammatory controls. It was also associated with higher hsCRP levels, without any effect on disease activity indices. Individualized management strategies are needed in CIA.

title: Risk Factor Profiles May Differ Between Younger-Onset and Late-Onset Colorectal Cancer: An Exploratory Analysis of Individual and Cumulative Risk Factors Among the Prostate, Lung, Colorectal and Ovarian Cohort.
authorString: Wigston L, Ahmed M, Abebe Z, Pandol SJ, Melaku YA, Barreto SG.
abstractText:
Background

Rates of young-onset colorectal cancer (CRC) are on the rise globally. Despite this growing burden, the drivers of young-onset adult CRC remain largely unknown.

Aims

This study aimed to compare risk factor profiles between younger-onset and late-onset CRC to evaluate differences in their risk factor profiles.

Methods

The Prostate, Lung, Colorectal and Ovarian Cancer Screening Trial dataset, comprising ∼155,000 US participants including 1219 CRC cases, was analysed. Participants were stratified by age (≤59 vs. ≥60 years). Associations of demographic, clinical and behavioural risk factors with CRC were computed using multivariable Cox regression with the multiplicative interaction of exposures. Reduced rank regression was used to derive dietary patterns (DPs).

Results

Among the ≤59-year cohort, no individual risk factor (excluding age) was independently associated with the risk of CRC. However, the multiplicative effect of hypertension and smoking had a nominal association with younger-onset CRC (p = 0.047). In contrast, in the ≥60-year cohort, individual (sex, body mass index, diabetes and alcohol) as well as combinations of risk factors were associated with CRC. Significant DPs appeared exclusively to impact the risk of CRC in the ≥60-year cohort. However, no interactions remained significant following correction for multiple testing; findings should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating.

Conclusions

These findings suggest that the drivers of CRC in younger individuals may be different from their older counterparts. These exploratory findings offer novel insight into CRC risk in the young and highlight the need to reconsider interactions between CRC risk factors.

title: High Per-capita Area of Accessible Urban Green Space and Lower Self-reported Anxiety/Depression Problems among Older Adults in Korea: A Nationwide Multilevel Study   ​.
authorString: Ju YJ, Kim W, Lim H, Lee SY.

journal.title: Journal of urban health : bulletin of the New York Academy of Medicine

abstractText: Although a growing body of literature has linked urban green space to better mental health, less is known about population-normalized area-level green-space provision intended for everyday use, particularly among older adults. This study examined the association between district-level per-capita living-area urban forest area and self-reported anxiety/depression problems among older adults in South Korea. We analyzed data from 79,931 participants aged 65 years or older in the 2024 Korea Community Health Survey. Anxiety/depression problems were assessed using the anxiety/depression dimension of the EQ-5D-3L. Exposure was measured using the 2023 Korea Forest Service per-capita living-area urban forest indicator, assigned to each participant's district of residence, and categorized into quartiles. Associations were examined using two-level random-intercept logistic regression models accounting for clustering within public health center areas and adjusting for individual-level covariates, including the urban-rural residential classification. Overall, 17.5% of participants reported anxiety/depression problems. Compared with the lowest exposure quartile (< 9.7 m<sup>2</sup>/person), the highest quartile (≥ 31.8 m<sup>2</sup>/person) was associated with lower odds of anxiety/depression problems (adjusted odds ratio, 0.74; 95% confidence interval, 0.63-0.87), whereas no statistically significant associations were observed for the intermediate quartiles. These findings suggest that a high level of district-level living-area urban forest provision may be associated with lower odds of anxiety/depression problems among older adults, with potential implications for age-friendly urban planning.

title: Early Postoperative Complications After Decompressive Craniectomy for Pediatric Severe Traumatic Brain Injury.
authorString: Semenova ZB, Bragin DE, Rogozhin EA, Lukyanov VI, Meshcheryakov SV.
abstractText:
Background

Decompressive craniectomy (DC) is used to treat refractory intracranial hypertension after pediatric severe traumatic brain injury (sTBI), but early postoperative neurosurgical complications and their predictors-particularly intracranial pressure (ICP) burden-remain inconsistently characterized.

Methods

We performed a retrospective cohort study of consecutive pediatric patients (< 18 years) with sTBI [Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) 3-8] who underwent DC at a single high-volume trauma center. Early postoperative neurosurgical complications were defined a priori as events occurring within 7 days after DC or before hospital discharge: secondary intracranial hemorrhage, central nervous system (CNS) infection, wound dehiscence, and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) leak. Associations with injury severity, imaging, and ICP variables (mean intraoperative ICP; cumulative duration of ICP > 20 mm Hg before DC) were evaluated.

Results

Of 104 screened records, 83 children were included. At least one early neurosurgical complication occurred in 33/83 patients (39.8%). Secondary intracranial hemorrhage occurred in 29/83 (34.9%), CNS infection in 7/83 (8.4%), wound dehiscence in 6/83 (7.2%), and CSF leak in 4/83 (4.8%). Among the 69 children with ICP monitoring, patients with complications had significantly higher intraoperative ICP (40.5 ± 13.5 vs. 28.6 ± 4.3 mm Hg; p = 0.0058) and longer pre-DC duration of ICP > 20 mm Hg (4.1 ± 5.9 vs. 1.6 ± 2.5 h; p = 0.0296). At 6 months, 25/83 (30.1%) had died; among survivors, 28/58 (48.3%) achieved a favorable outcome [Glasgow Outcome Scale (GOS) 4-5].

Conclusions

Early postoperative complications after pediatric DC were common and predominantly hemorrhagic. Greater ICP burden before and during DC was associated with these events. The co-occurrence of CSF leak and CNS infection highlights the importance of dural closure strategies that minimize CSF egress and the need for vigilant postoperative surveillance.

title: Nitric oxide, prone positioning, and sedation and analgesia in mechanical ventilation.
authorString: Estepa Pedregosa L, González Gómez JM, Vivanco Allende A, Ortiz Pérez M, Inguanzo Ortiz M, Nieto Faza M, Parrilla Parrilla J.
abstractText: There are complementary treatments to mechanical ventilation in critically ill pediatric patients that are essential for optimizing oxygenation, gas exchange, and adaptation to respiratory support. Inhaled nitric oxide is a selective pulmonary vasodilator useful in specific situations such as pulmonary hypertension, right ventricular failure, and refractory hypoxemia, especially as rescue therapy, although its routine use in pediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) has not been found to improve survival. The prone position improves ventilation/perfusion distribution, promotes alveolar recruitment, and reduces ventilator-associated lung injury, making it a valuable adjunctive strategy in patients with severe ARDS and persistent hypoxemia. Although its impact on pediatric survival is still being evaluated, it represents a physiologically sound tool for protective ventilation. Protocolized sedation and analgesia are essential to ensure comfort, synchrony with the ventilator, and prevention of complications such as delirium, withdrawal syndrome, or oversedation. The rational use of opioids, alpha-2 agonist sedatives, and neuromuscular blocking agents, along with monitoring using validated scales, allows for optimized clinical outcomes and reduced adverse effects. The individualized combination of these strategies is currently a cornerstone of advanced respiratory support for critically ill pediatric patients.

title: From Diagnosis to Adaptation: Meaning-Making Throughout the Illness Experience of Patients With Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension-A Hermeneutic Phenomenological Study.
authorString: Miao YT, Tsai HC, Chen MY, Wei CW.
abstractText:
Aim

To explore the illness experience and meaning-making of patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension from diagnosis to adaptation.

Design

A qualitative study using a Heideggerian hermeneutic phenomenological design.

Methods

From July to December 2025, purposive sampling recruited 12 adults with PAH from a teaching hospital in northern Taiwan. Semi-structured interviews were conducted, with data collection and analysis occurring concurrently. Transcripts were read, compared, and interpreted through the hermeneutic circle, supported by field notes and reflexive notes.

Results

Six interrelated themes and 15 categories were identified: (1) Cycles of hope and disappointment; (2) Physical decline and disruption to daily life after disease onset; (3) Waiting on the edge of collapse; (4) Information gaps and unmet information needs; (5) Rediscovering possibilities for living; and (6) Finding a place in life within the limits of the disease. Patients experienced diagnostic delays, physical decline, treatment waiting, and information gaps. As treatment stabilised, they shifted from hoping to return to pre-illness lives to adjusting expectations, roles, and attitudes and engaging in disease management. Adaptation was an ongoing process.

Conclusion

Participants' retrospective accounts suggest that adaptation to PAH involves more than accepting the illness. Patients continuously reinterpret the illness, themselves, and their future amid physical and daily-life changes. Family, peers, and healthcare professionals support hope and adaptation.

Implications for the profession and/or patient care

Care for pulmonary arterial hypertension should extend beyond disease control and symptom management. Nurses can support patients through case management, information, and family and peer support across illness stages.

Impact

This study highlights illness adaptation as a continuous process of adjusting perspectives on illness, self, and future, suggesting that care for PHA should address patients' long-term lives alongside disease management.

Reporting method

This study was reported in accordance with the COREQ guidelines.

Patient or public contribution

No patient or public contribution.

title: Mechanistic and Clinical Implications of Apolipoprotein Abnormalities in Preeclampsia.
authorString: Wang H, Liu W, Wan S, Peng J, Zhou T, Luo W, Ai Z, Hua X.
abstractText: Preeclampsia (PE) is a pregnancy-specific disorder characterized by hypertension and organ dysfunction. Lipid disturbances are associated with PE, but conventional lipid concentrations do not fully describe the accompanying changes in lipoprotein function. This narrative review examines apolipoprotein physiology during pregnancy, reported abnormalities in PE, and their possible mechanistic and clinical implications. Human observational and proteomic studies report changes in apolipoprotein A-I (ApoA-I), apolipoprotein B (ApoB), apolipoprotein C-III (ApoC-III), and apolipoprotein E (ApoE), although their direction and magnitude vary with gestational timing, population, and disease phenotype. Experimental studies support selected pathways involving cholesterol handling and vascular protection; emerging research on apolipoprotein D (ApoD) also implicates placental ferroptosis in model systems. Direct causal evidence for an apolipoprotein M (ApoM)-sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P) pathway in PE remains limited, although gestation-dependent alterations in ApoM and S1P have been reported in late-onset preeclampsia (LOPE). The available evidence supports a bidirectional conceptual framework in which placental hypoxia may influence maternal lipid and vascular dysfunction, while maternal metabolic disturbances may also aggravate placental injury. Apolipoprotein alterations could therefore be contributors, consequences, or both. Their potential use as complementary biomarkers requires prospective validation and demonstration of added value beyond established clinical and angiogenic assessment. Pregnancy-specific efficacy and safety data are also needed before apolipoprotein-directed therapies can be considered for PE.

title: Hypertension Dissociates Radiographic and Symptomatic Progression in a Male Rat Model of Post-Traumatic Osteoarthritis.
authorString: Yip SL, Zhang Y, Zhang L, Lu X, Yau SY, Dong C, Au MT, Wen C.
abstractText:
Objective

This study investigated the impact of hypertension on the relationship between structural damage and pain sensitivity in a post-traumatic osteoarthritis (OA) rat model, and explored possible neurovascular factor underlying radiographic-symptomatic dissociation in OA.

Method

The 6-month-old male rats underwent anterior cruciate ligament transection (ACLT) to induce post-traumatic OA in spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHR) and normotensive Wistar Kyoto (WKY) inbred strains. Joint structural changes were assessed via micro-CT and histology at 8 weeks post-surgery. Mechanical sensitivity and motor function were longitudinally monitored at baseline, 4-week and 8-week post-surgery. Based on lumbar dorsal root ganglia (DRG) RNA sequencing results, in vivo calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) replenishment experiment was performed for proof-of-concept.

Results

SHR exhibited comparable articular cartilage degradation and subchondral bone loss to WKY following ACLT surgery. Strain-specific differences in surgical responses were confined specifically to mechanical pain processing, where WKY developed marked post-traumatic mechanical hypersensitivity (ACLT week 0 vs 8: 41.48 ± 15.76 gf vs 26.14 ± 9.404 gf; 95% CI: 0.3918 to 30.27, p = 0.0436), whereas SHR maintained hypoalgesia (ACLT week 0 vs 8: 31.88 ± 6.482 gf vs 42.73 ± 7.056 gf; 95% CI: -18.94 to -2.766, p = 0.0092), indicating a dissociation between the severity of joint damage and pain sensitivity. DRG transcriptomic analysis revealed the downregulation of CGRP-mediated nociceptive signalling in hypertensive rats. Exogenous CGRP replenishment partially restored mechanical sensitivity in SHR without affecting joint structural integrity or affective and cognitive behaviour.

Conclusion

Hypertension decouples structural damage from mechanical sensitivity in male rats with post-traumatic OA. While joint degradation progresses to a comparable extent in both strains, hypertensive rats maintain higher pain thresholds despite severe structural breakdown, with CGRP as a plausible neurovascular factor underlying this phenomenon.

title: Hypertension was common and associated with serum cholesterol concentrations in dogs with Cushing syndrome.
authorString: McKinley G, McAtee R, Lashnits E.

journal.title: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association

abstractText:
Objective

To estimate the prevalence of systemic hypertension in dogs with newly diagnosed Cushing syndrome (CS) and evaluate associations with hypothesized hypertension-associated variables.

Methods

A retrospective observational study was performed with dogs diagnosed with CS by ACTH stimulation or low-dose dexamethasone suppression testing at University of Wisconsin Veterinary Care from 2005 to 2025. Dogs with systolic blood pressure (SBP) measured within 8 weeks of diagnosis and before CS or antihypertensive treatment were included. Data included signalment, body condition score, platelet count, select serum biochemistry variables, and urine protein-to-creatinine ratio. Hypertension prevalence and associations between SBP and variables were assessed.

Results

Among 117 dogs with CS, 57 dogs (49%) had SBP measured and met inclusion criteria. With an SBP cutoff ≥ 160 mm Hg, 61.4% of dogs (95% CI, 48.4% to 73.0%) were hypertensive and 26.3% were prehypertensive (SBP of 140 to 159 mm Hg). Median serum cholesterol was higher in hypertensive than nonhypertensive dogs (378.5 vs 287 mg/dL) and positively associated with SBP (OR, 1.10/10 mg/dL; 95% CI, 1.03 to 1.21). Serum potassium was lower in hypertensive dogs than nonhypertensive dogs (4.4 vs 4.85 mmol/L). No significant associations were identified for urine protein-to-creatinine ratio, platelet count, age, or body condition score.

Conclusions

Hypertension was common in dogs with CS, yet SBP was not consistently measured at diagnosis. Serum cholesterol was associated with hypertension, and lower serum potassium concentrations were observed in hypertensive dogs.

Clinical relevance

Routine SBP assessment is warranted in dogs with CS. Cholesterol and potassium regulation may be affected in dogs with CS.

title: Habitual Golden Milk Consumption Is Associated with a Favorable Redox and Cardiometabolic Biomarker Profile in Older Men: A Cross-Sectional Study.
authorString: Merzouk AZ, Bendimerad S, Mokhtari MR, Benyelles M, Mokeddem M, Benmansour M, Merzouk H.

journal.title: Journal of the American Nutrition Association

abstractText:
Objective

Aging is characterized by increased oxidative stress, chronic low-grade inflammation, and metabolic alterations. Golden Milk is a milk-based beverage containing turmeric, ginger, cinnamon, and black pepper, with potential antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. This study examined the association between habitual Golden Milk consumption and redox, inflammatory, and lipid biomarkers in older men.

Methods

This cross-sectional study included 124 men aged ≥70 years, comprising 64 regular Golden Milk consumers and 60 non-consumers. Oxidative stress and antioxidant defense were assessed using malondialdehyde (MDA), peroxynitrite, glutathione (GSH), catalase, and superoxide dismutase (SOD). Inflammatory and lipid biomarkers were also measured. Between-group comparisons, effect sizes, false discovery rate correction, and multivariable linear regression adjusted for age, BMI, diabetes and hypertension status were performed.

Results

Compared with non-consumers, Golden Milk consumers had significantly lower MDA, peroxynitrite, CRP, total cholesterol, and triglycerides, and significantly higher GSH, catalase, SOD, and HDL-C (all FDR-adjusted p < 0.001). After adjustment for age, BMI, diabetes and hypertension status, Golden Milk consumption remained associated with lower MDA (-1.61 µmol/L), peroxynitrite (-3.45 µmol/L), CRP (-1.03 mg/L), total cholesterol (-35.05 mg/dL), and triglycerides (-29.56 mg/dL), and with higher GSH (+1.34 µmol/L), catalase (+25.72 U/mL), SOD (+43.41 U/mL), and HDL-C (+13.84 mg/dL). CRP and the granulocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio were also significantly correlated with redox biomarkers.

Conclusion

Habitual Golden Milk consumption was associated with a more favorable redox, inflammatory, and lipid profile in older men. Prospective studies are required to confirm these associations and establish causality.

title: Sociodemographic and clinical characteristics of adolescent pregnancies at an IMSS hospital in Cuernavaca Mexico from 2020 to 2024
authorString: Melendez Loredo AV, Salgado RC, Calva LLR.
abstractText:
Background:

Local descriptions of adolescent pregnancy can identify priorities for prenatal care and postpartum follow up. This study characterized adolescents with pregnancy records at an IMSS hospital in Cuernavaca, Morelos, Mexico.

Methods:

We conducted a retrospective, descriptive, observational cross-sectional review of records covering 2020 to 2024 at Hospital General Regional con Medicina Familiar No. 1. All eligible records were included. Sociodemographic, reproductive and clinical characteristics were summarized using frequencies, percentages, and the median and interquartile range for age.

Results:

Thirty-nine records were analyzed. Median age was 15 years (interquartile range 15 to 6; range 12 to 17). Secondary education was recorded in 61.54%, and 46.15% were students. Most adolescents were primigravidas (97.44%). The first prenatal visit occurred in the second trimester in 53.85%. Overweight or obesity was recorded in 71.8%. Urinary tract infection occurred in 66.67%, gestational hypertension in 28.21%, and preeclampsia in 7.69%. No preterm births or obstetric hemorrhages were recorded. Vaginal delivery accounted for 51.28% and cesarean delivery for 48.72%. Postpartum contraceptive method was unspecified in 64.10% of records.

Conclusions:

This small, single-center study identified frequent urinary tract infections, a high recorded proportion of overweight or obesity, prenatal entry commonly after the first trimester, and incomplete postpartum contraceptive documentation. These findings identify local priorities for care and record quality; they do not establish causal relationships or population prevalence.

Keywords:

adolescent pregnancy; prenatal care; reproductive health; medical records; family medicine; Mexico.

title: Comorbidity and Spousal Concordance of Hypertension and Diabetes Among Couples in Nigeria: Findings From the 2023 – 2024 Nigeria Demographic and Health Survey
authorString: Owolabi RO, Umar Y, Ogunniran IA, Ajibade OA, Garba B.
abstractText: Background The rise in the prevalence of hypertension and diabetes in Nigeria, coupled with the risk of the two conditions coexisting in an individual, poses major challenges to achieving Sustainable Development Goal 3. This requires re-strategising prevention and care through more integrated, equitable, and targeted approaches. Objectives This study aimed to evaluate gaps in the prevention and care of hypertension and diabetes among couples, and to assess comorbidity, spousal concordance, and factors associated with these conditions. Methods A secondary analysis of 6,828 couples from the 2024 Nigeria Demographic and Health Survey was conducted using survey-weighted proportions and multivariable logistic regression. Survey-weighted means and adjusted Wald tests were used to assess within-couple differences, and a design-based Pearson chi-square test was used to assess spousal association in disease status. Results Blood pressure screening is higher among wives than husbands (62.8% vs 41.3%). Husbands (17.0%; 95% CI: 15.3, 18.9) reported a hypertension diagnosis more than wives (13.1%; 95% CI: 11.8, 14.5), despite wives having higher screening coverage, while reporting diabetes diagnosis differs within couples by 5.3% points (95% CI: -7.7, -2.1; p-value < 0.001). There are noteworthy differences in the care cascade of diabetes and hypertension, and the prevalence of comorbidity is more than two times higher among husbands than wives (3.4% vs 1.3%). Spousal concordance is 3.8% (95% CI: 2.9, 4.9) for reported hypertension diagnosis; husbands whose wives reported a hypertension diagnosis have 83% higher odds of reporting a diagnosis (OR: 1.83; 1.32, 2.55). The odds of hypertension and diabetes increase with age among wives and husbands. Conclusion There is a notable difference in the hypertension and diabetes care cascade and comorbidity among couples, emphasising the necessity for an integrated, couple-focused approach to the prevention and care in Nigeria.

title: Functional Independence, Widowhood, and Cardio-metabolic Health: Evidence from India's Longitudinal Ageing Study
authorString: Arora A.
abstractText: India's population of female older women is growing rapidly and out of this number, more than 50 per cent are likely to spend the final years of their life as widows. This study explores whether the ability to perform basic daily activities without assistance, known as functional status, protects widowed women from hypertension and sleep problems in the same way as it protects their married peers. Using nationally representative data on 16,512 women aged 60 and above from Wave 1 (2017-18) of the Longitudinal Ageing Study of India (LASI), I estimate logistic regression models of hypertension and regular trouble sleeping as functions of functional status, marital status, and their interaction. Results show that better functional status is associated with remarkably lower odds of both hypertension (adjusted OR = 0.88, 95% CI 0.79–0.98) and sleep trouble (OR = 0.73, 95% CI 0.66–0.81). Widowed and separated women have 16% higher chances of having hypertension than married women (OR = 1.16, 95% CI 0.99–1.35, significant only at the 10% level) and the protective association between functional status and hypertension is significantly weaker among widows (interaction OR = 1.15, 95% CI 1.02–1.31, p = .026). Inverse-probability-weighted estimates suggest that widowhood is associated with roughly two percentage points higher probabilities of hypertension and of sleep trouble. An instrumental-variables check, using regional variation in widowhood prevalence, corroborates the sleep-trouble estimates but not the hypertension estimates. Together, the results suggest that physical independence is a less reliable health buffer once the spousal relationship is gone, that widowhood’s harm operates mostly through channels other than functional decline, and that health policy for older adults should treat widowhood itself, not just functional status, as a target for intervention.

title: Serologic Discrimination of Histologic Classes in Lupus Nephritis: A Cross-Sectional Analysis with Exploratory 12-Month Outcomes.
authorString: Fatfat A, Batish I, Sharma A, Arevalo Salazar D, Albadri ST, Majithia V, Aslam N, Bobart SA.
abstractText:
Background

Anti-dsDNA positivity and hypocomplementemia are markers of active lupus nephritis (LN), but their ability to discriminate between histologic phenotypes remains underexplored, particularly for mixed proliferative/membranous LN (mixed LN). We compared baseline serologic markers across proliferative LN, membranous LN, and mixed LN, and evaluated their discriminative performance for histologic class.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional study of 132 patients with biopsy-proven LN, categorized according to the International Society of Nephrology/Renal Pathology Society (ISN/RPS) classification into proliferative LN (class III/IV), membranous LN (class V), and mixed LN (class III/IV+V). Baseline anti-dsDNA and complements C3 and C4 were compared across groups. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis assessed the ability of individual and combined markers to discriminate between histologic classes. Kidney outcomes at 12 months were explored in a secondary cohort (n=88).

Results

Of 132 patients, 57 had proliferative LN, 32 had membranous LN, and 43 had mixed LN. Anti-dsDNA was significantly higher, and C3 and C4 significantly lower, in proliferative and mixed LN compared to membranous LN (P<0.05 for all), while proliferative and mixed LN did not differ significantly. On ROC analysis, individual markers achieved AUCs of 0.68-0.71 for distinguishing proliferative or mixed LN from membranous LN, with combined models yielding AUCs of 0.73. However, discrimination between proliferative and mixed LN was poor (combined AUC 0.62). At 12 months, kidney outcomes were comparable across groups.

Conclusions

Mixed LN exhibits a serologic profile resembling proliferative LN, both sharing elevated anti-dsDNA and low complement levels, but distinct from membranous LN. Serology could inform suspicion for LN class but cannot replace kidney biopsy.

title: Sphingolipids as Mediators of the Markers of Kidney Function/Heart Failure Association: The Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis.
authorString: Lidgard B, Hoofnagle AN, Zelnick LR, de Boer IH, Fretts AM, Siscovick DS, Sotoodehnia N, Umans JG, Jensen P, Lemaitre RN.
abstractText:
Background

Heart failure is a common complication of CKD. Sphingolipids, including ceramides and sphingomyelins, are lipid molecules with regulatory and signaling properties. Sphingolipids associated with kidney function and incident heart failure. We previously demonstrated that sphingolipids partially mediate the association between kidney function and incident heart failure. We sought to confirm this finding in the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis.

Methods

All sphingolipids were measured at baseline using tandem-mass spectrometry. Baseline kidney function was assessed using albuminuria and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR). Associations of albuminuria and eGFR with heart failure were tested by Cox and Weibull regressions. We tested the mediation effect of sphingolipids on the associations of eGFR and albuminuria with heart failure via quasi-Bayesian Monte Carlo method based on normal approximation with 2,000 simulations. Analyses tested Bonferroni-corrected p-values 0.00625 (0.05/8 sphingolipids).

Results

Among 3,959 participants, the mean (SD) eGFR was 95 (17) mL/min/1.73 m2, and median (Q1, Q3) albuminuria was 5.10 (3.20, 10.2) mg/g creatinine. We observed 438 incident heart failure events over a median (Q1, Q3) follow-up of 18.9 (15.0, 19.6) years. Greater ceramide and sphingomyelin 16:0 and lesser sphingomyelin 20:0 were associated with higher heart failure risk. Sphingomyelin 16:0 was associated with partial 9%, 95% CI 3%, 30%) mediation of the association between eGFR and heart failure, and 4% (1%, 9%) mediation of the association between albuminuria and heart failure. Sphingomyelin 20:0 partially mediated the eGFR/heart failure association (6%, 95% CI 1%, 21% of association mediated).

Conclusions

Plasma sphingomyelins were associated with partial mediation of the associations of eGFR and albuminuria with incident heart failure.

title: Renal Outcomes and Variant Effects in Monoallelic COL4A3/COL4A4-Related Alport Syndrome: A Single-Center Cohort Study.
authorString: Fernandes da Rocha D, Reis Almeida J, Pestana Silva R, Louro P, Neto AP, Pinto Moura C, Moreira Ferreira S, Paulo Oliveira J.
abstractText:
Background

Autosomal dominant Alport syndrome (AD-AS) is caused by pathogenic/likely pathogenic (P/LP) variants in COL4A3 and COL4A4. Its clinical spectrum ranges from isolated hematuria to proteinuric chronic kidney disease (CKD) eventually progressing to kidney failure (KF). We aimed to characterize the clinical and genetic profile of AD-AS in northwest Portugal, with particular focus on the recurrent COL4A3 c.1219G>C p.(Gly407Arg) variant.

Methods

We conducted an observational cohort study at a major university hospital. Eligible participants were heterozygous for COL4A3 or COL4A4 variants. Demographic, clinical, and genetic data were collected. Time to CKD≥3 and CKD5/KF was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method. Subcohorts were defined by gene, variant type, and variant of interest.

Results

A total of 218 individuals (16 children) from 123 families were included. Definitive molecular diagnosis was obtained in 75%. Among COL4A3 carriers, 117 had P/LP variants, predominantly missense; among COL4A4 carriers, 47 had P/LP variants, predominantly truncating. COL4A3 p.(Gly407Arg) represented 62% of COL4A3 P/LP variants and 44% of the patient cohort. History of microscopic hematuria was present in 93% of patients, whereas history of significant proteinuria was documented in 68% and hypertension in 48%. CKD≥3 developed in 33%, and 21% progressed to CKD5/KF. Proteinuria independently predicted CKD progression (p=0.001). Carriers of COL4A3 p.(Gly407Arg) had earlier onset of hypertension and higher prevalence of proteinuria than carriers of other COL4A3 P/LP variants. Glomerular basement membrane thinning was noted on electron microscopy in all biopsy specimens. Extrarenal manifestations were uncommon.

Conclusions

Heterozygous COL4A3/4 P/LP variants are frequently associated with progressive CKD. COL4A3 p.(Gly407Arg) apparently confers a more penetrant renal phenotype. AD-AS demonstrates a continuum of phenotypes even among relatives, underscoring the importance of early identification, longitudinal monitoring, and renoprotective therapy.

title: Dysregulated apoptosis in the spleen from patients with splenomegaly due to cirrhosis.
authorString: Zhao B, Liu L, Lu J, Li J, Zhang H, Zhong Y, Chu H, Xu Y, Liu T.
abstractText:
Introduction

Splenomegaly (SM) secondary to portal hypertension is characterized by the pathological enlargement of the spleen due to chronically elevated portal venous pressure. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying its pathogenesis remain largely unclear.

Material

AND M: ETHODS: Sixteen patients with hepatitis B-related liver cirrhosis and SM who underwent subtotal splenectomy with omental plasty and retroperitoneal fixation were enrolled in the SM group, whereas 15 patients who underwent splenectomy for traumatic splenic rupture (without SM) served as the traumatic splenic rupture control (TSRC) group. Splenic tissue samples were collected for hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining, terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase dUTP nick-end labeling (TUNEL) assay, immunohistochemistry (IHC), quantitative reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction, and Western blotting (WB).

Results

H&E staining revealed dilated red pulp, fibrotic splenic cords, atrophic white pulp, and a thickened splenic capsule in the SM group. A significant increase in the proportion of apoptotic cells was noted in the spleens of patients with SM. Moreover, differences were observed in apoptotic protein expression assessed by IHC between the two groups. The expression of apoptosis-related genes, including BAX, CASP3, and CASP9, was significantly upregulated, whereas BCL2 expression was significantly reduced in the SM group. WB confirmed that the levels of BAX, cleaved CASP3, and cleaved CASP9 were elevated in the SM group, whereas splenic BCL2 expression was below the detection limit in both groups.

Conclusions

Apoptosis was dysregulated in the spleen of patients with portal hypertension-associated SM secondary to liver cirrhosis. Our findings suggest that SM contributes to a pro-apoptotic environment in the spleen of patients with liver cirrhosis.

title: Multimodal Validation and Disease Stage Dependency of ATTR Cardiomyopathy Red Flags in Patients With LV Thickening.
authorString: Piwowarski J, Gröschel J, Romero Dorta E, Schulz-Menger J, Mattig I, Zernikow J, Wetz C, von Landenberg-Roberg V, Heidecker B, Werhahn SM, Wetzel PJ, Wieder NW, Pernice H, Koehler F, Hindricks G, Hahn K, Barzen G, Spethmann S.
abstractText:
Introduction

Timely diagnosis of transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) is critical to improving outcomes and remains challenging. Guidelines recommend assessing for red flags (RFs) to facilitate ATTR-CM detection, but their diagnostic validation remains incomplete. This study aimed to multidimensionally validate these RFs in patients with left ventricular thickening (LVT).

Methods

Prospective registry study including all patients with LVT and standardized workup at tertiary amyloidosis center. For validated RFs, "high-risk" (specificity for ATTR-CM>90%) and "low-risk" (false-negative rate<5%) findings were predefined.

Results

425 patients (321 ATTR-CM,104 control group) were included. Heart failure (97%) and polyneuropathies (78%) were among most sensitive clinical findings, while bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome (bCTS) was more specific (80%) but less sensitive (45%). Diverse ECG changes were common, yet mostly unspecific. Marked elevations of NT-proBNP and troponin were most discriminative among non-imaging RFs (Youden's index[YI]:59%). Apical sparing (Apical-to-Basal-strain-ratio≥2.0) was the most effective, stage-independent echocardiographic parameter (YI62%), followed by biatrial enlargement, advanced diastolic dysfunction, and LVGLS impairment (YI48-55%). Normal ECG without conduction disorders history and normal levels of both NT-proBNP and hs-troponin-T constituted "low-risk" findings. Heart failure with concomitant bCTS, peripheral low voltage, right ventricular dysfunction, 5-5-5 sign, restrictive filling pattern and apical sparing with LVGLS impairment represented "high-risk" RFs. Contrary to most non-imaging RFs, most echocardiographic RFs showed association with advancing disease stage (p<0.05). All aforementioned RFs were associated with ATTR-CM independently of age, sex, and LVT-severity (p<0.05).

Conclusions

ATTR-CM is frequently associated with validated RFs that differ in their diagnostic characteristics, which should be considered when evaluating for ATTR-CM.

title: Heart Failure in Anthracycline Cardiotoxicity: From Mechanisms to Clinical Management.
authorString: Polovina MM, Viduljević M, Tomić M, Stanković S, Krljanac G, Geavlete O, Zdravković M, Abdelhamid M, Adamo M, Chioncel O, Savarese G, Seferović PM.
abstractText: Anthracyclines remain a cornerstone therapy for haematological malignancies and solid tumours, but their use is limited by cardiotoxicity, ranging from asymptomatic left ventricular dysfunction to overt heart failure (HF). The risk increases with cumulative doxorubicin-equivalent exposure exceeding 250-300 mg/m2, although susceptibility varies substantially according to patient characteristics, pre-existing cardiovascular disease, genetic predisposition, and modifiable risk factors. Clinically overt HF occurs in ∼6-9% of patients, while subclinical cardiac dysfunction develops in up to 18%. The pathophysiology is multifactorial, involving interconnected mechanisms that disrupt cardiomyocyte homeostasis and promote endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, fibrosis, and adverse remodelling. Yet evidence connecting molecular mechanisms with long-term HF outcomes in humans remains incomplete. Risk stratification, incorporating clinical variables, cardiac biomarkers, echocardiography and, when appropriate, cardiac magnetic resonance enables earlier recognition of cardiac dysfunction. Trials of preventive neurohormonal treatment and statins have produced heterogeneous results, often relying on imaging rather than clinical HF endpoints. Once cardiac dysfunction develops, prompt initiation of foundational HF treatment and multidisciplinary decisions on cancer therapy are essential. Early detection and prompt initiation of HF therapies may reverse myocardial dysfunction, whereas delayed recognition is associated with a poorer treatment response and prognosis. This narrative review integrates current evidence on the mechanisms, risk stratification, surveillance, prevention, and management of anthracycline cardiotoxicity and HF, while highlighting gaps in knowledge, emerging therapeutic strategies, and future directions for clinically meaningful, risk-guided research.

title: Cellular and molecular mechanisms of arrhythmogenesis in Takotsubo syndrome (Review).
authorString: Xu D, Chen X, Hao M, Xu Q, Zhao B, Huang W, Zhou X, Xu Q, Lan H.
abstractText: Takotsubo syndrome (TTS), an acute stress‑induced heart failure, is frequently complicated by arrhythmias that significantly worsen prognosis. Despite advances in understanding its pathology, the electrophysiological basis of these arrhythmias remains incompletely elucidated. The present review synthesizes current evidence to explore the core electrophysiological mechanisms underlying arrhythmogenesis in TTS, including abnormal calcium handling, repolarization abnormalities, altered conduction and refractoriness due to structural remodelling, and autonomic nervous system imbalance. The corresponding clinical manifestations of ventricular arrhythmias, atrial arrhythmias and bradyarrhythmias were further delineated, and contemporary diagnostic and therapeutic strategies were discussed. By integrating clinical observations with experimental findings, the present review aims to bridge the knowledge gap between mechanistic insights and clinical practice. Finally, critical research gaps were highlighted and future directions were proposed, emphasizing the need for personalized medicine and novel therapeutic targets to improve arrhythmia management and patient outcomes in TTS.

title: Predictive Value of PET-Derived Myocardial Flow Reserve for New-Onset Atrial Fibrillation.
authorString: Alwan M, El Ghazawi A, Sayed A, Ahmed AI, El Yaman A, Aljizeeri A, Al Rifai M, Al-Mallah MH.
abstractText:
Background

Atrial fibrillation (AF) commonly coexists with coronary artery disease, heart failure, and coronary microvascular dysfunction, sharing common risk factors and pathophysiologic mechanisms. Whether myocardial flow reserve (MFR), a positron emission tomography-derived measure of epicardial and microvascular function, predicts incident AF remains uncertain.

Methods

We included 10 500 patients without prior AF who underwent positron emission tomography MPI at 2 centers. The primary outcome was new-onset AF during follow-up. Multivariable Cox models adjusted for demographics, comorbidities, resting left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), and LVEF reserve were used to evaluate the association between MFR and incident AF. Incremental predictive value was assessed using χ2, Akaike's information criterion, Bayesian information criterion, C-index, and a likelihood ratio test comparing models with and without MFR.

Results

Over a median follow-up of 640 days, 288 patients (2.74%) developed AF. Impaired MFR (<2) was associated with a higher incidence of AF (20.5 versus 8.3 per 1000 person years). In multivariable analysis, MFR was a significant predictor of AF (hazard ratio per 1 interquartile range increase, 0.58 [95% CI, 0.47-0.72]; P<0.0001), whereas stress and rest myocardial blood flow were not. MFR improved risk prediction beyond clinical variables and LVEF (C-index increased from 0.675-0.726 when added to clinical variables and from 0.758-0.770 when added to clinical variables, LVEF, and summed stress score; P<0.001). Similar incremental improvement was observed when MFR was added to the Cohorts for Heart and Aging Research in Genomic Epidemiology-Atrial Fibrillation risk score (C-index increased from 0.638 to 0.711). The association between MFR and incident AF was numerically greater in patients with preserved EF, although the interaction term was not statistically significant.

Conclusions

Impaired positron emission tomography-derived MFR is independently associated with increased risk of new-onset AF and enhances risk prediction beyond clinical factors and LVEF, suggesting a role for coronary microvascular dysfunction in early AF pathogenesis.

title: Pentadecanoic acid as an emerging microbial-metabolic node for cardiometabolic health.
authorString: Yang R, Deng C, Tang X.

journal.title: Trends in endocrinology and metabolism: TEM

abstractText: The mechanisms underlying the gut microbiota's role in cardiometabolic health remain largely unknown. In a recent article in Nature, Yin et al. identify pentadecanoic acid from Bacteroides uniformis as an HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor that regulates cholesterol metabolism and atherosclerosis. This work reveals an unrecognized microbial-metabolic axis for cardiometabolic health.

title: Arsenic metabolism is associated with muscle area and adiposity: The Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA).
authorString: Clemens Z, Bai H, Glabonjat RA, Schilling K, Allison M, Anderson WA, Sanchez TR, Wu HC, Sahu A, Cvejkus RK, Navas-Acien A, Barchowsky A, Miljkovic I.
abstractText: Environmental arsenic (As) exposure is a known contributor to cardiometabolic disease. Yet while animal models suggest As impairs skeletal muscle quality, this is largely unexplored in humans. We hypothesized that inorganic As (iAs) and its metabolites monomethylarsonate (MMA) and dimethylarsinate (DMA) are associated with lower muscle quality, characterized by lower muscle area and higher muscle adiposity (myosteatosis). We examined urinary As species data and abdominal computed tomography (CT) data in 1597 U.S. adults (ages 44-84 years, 49% female, 60% non-white) participating in the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis. We constructed linear regression models of associations between CT-derived muscle area or myosteatosis (measured by muscle density, which inversely associates with adiposity) and total urinary inorganic arsenic (ΣAs), the relative percentage of As metabolites (iAs%, MMA%, and DMA%), or primary and secondary methylation indexes (PMI, SMI) which indicate As metabolic efficiency. In fully-adjusted models, MMA% was associated with lower abdominal muscle area (β per 5% increase = -1.62 cm<sup>2</sup>). Furthermore, a doubling of PMI, indicating incomplete As metabolism, was associated with lower muscle area (β = -1.95 cm<sup>2</sup>) and density (β = -1.20 Hounsfield Units). Leave-one-out models provided further evidence. Regardless of which other metabolite was included in the model, MMA% was associated with lower muscle area and density. These results indicate previously unreported associations between As metabolism and abdominal muscle adiposity in middle-aged and older adults with low-moderate As exposure. MMA and PMI consistently showed adverse associations with abdominal muscle quality, indicating the importance of considering As metabolism in studies of its toxicology in human populations.

title: Extracellular vesicles from Lactobacillus plantarum improve aging-related endothelial dysfunction via VDR/SIRT1/SOD2 signaling axis.
authorString: Li X, Guo H, Guo X, Liu Y, Cui Z, Zhang Z, Tang J, Zhang H.
abstractText:
Background

Lactobacillus plantarum exhibits antioxidant properties and has been shown to improve vascular injury. However, its effects and underlying mechanisms on aging-associated endothelial dysfunction remain unclear. Bacterial extracellular vesicles are mediators of host-microbial communication. This study aimed to investigate the effects of Lactobacillus plantarum-derived extracellular vesicles (L.p EVs) on aging-associated endothelial dysfunction and elucidate the underlying mechanisms.

Methods

L.p EVs were isolated through ultracentrifugation plus filtration. Aortic rings from aged or H₂O₂-treated C57BL/6 mouse aortas were used for wire myography to assess endothelial function after EV treatment. Comparative transcriptomics identified the target molecules, and immunoblotting with gene silencing verified the essential role of VDR, SIRT1, and SOD2 in the beneficial effect of L.p EVs in aging-associated endothelial dysfunction.

Results

Both in vivo and ex vivo experiments demonstrated L.p EVs reversed H₂O₂-induced endothelial senescence, restored impaired endothelium-dependent relaxation (EDR), and attenuated oxidative stress in aged mice's aortas. Transcriptomic analysis identified VDR and SOD2 as key molecular targets of L.p EVs, and immunoblotting confirmed L.p EVs upregulated VDR, SIRT1, and SOD2 expression. Gene silencing confirmed that these molecules mediated the antioxidant and endoprotective effects of L.p EVs. Specifically, VDR regulated the SIRT1/SOD2 axis, while SIRT1 and SOD2 engaged in a mutual positive regulatory feedback loop. Together, they suppressed COX-2, NOX2, and ET-1 expression induced by H₂O₂ in endothelial cells.

Conclusion

This study demonstrates that L.p EVs ameliorate aging-associated endothelial dysfunction by activating the VDR/SIRT1/SOD2 signaling axis, highlighting their potential as a novel nanobiological strategy to improve aging‑ associated vascular endothelial dysfunction.

title: The phenomic landscape of rare gain- and loss-of-function variation
authorString: Kars ME, Stein D, Wu Y, Chen Z, Deng S, Abe H, Stenson PD, Cooper DN, Raffield LM, Lange LA, Tsai M, Goodarzi MO, Rich SS, Rotter JI, Cohen P, Gerszten RE, Itan Y.
abstractText: Current large-scale phenome-wide association studies do not distinguish between genetic variants with distinct functional consequences, despite evidence that gain-of-function (GoF) and loss-of-function (LoF) variants can produce different phenotypes. Consequently, the phenotypic consequences of variants stratified by predicted GoF and LoF effects have not been systematically characterized at scale. Here, we systematically analyzed rare predicted GoF and LoF variants in 18,214 genes across 1,244 binary and 202 quantitative traits using whole-exome sequencing and electronic health records from the Mount Sinai Million Health Discoveries Program, a phenotypically rich hospital-based biobank comprised of 50,067 participants, primarily representing African, Admixed American and European ancestries. We identified numerous established and previously unreported ancestry-specific and shared gene- and variant-level associations, many of which were supported by complementary evidence from both diagnostic phenotypes and clinical measurements. Proteomic evaluation of the previously unreported association between VNN1 LoF variants and body mass index in the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis revealed reduced circulating vanin-1 levels with LoF variants, which in turn were associated with body composition and additional cardiometabolic phenotypes. Functional stratification of predicted GoF and LoF variants revealed gene-trait associations that were attenuated when these variants were combined, demonstrating that traditional aggregation of variants with different functional effects can obscure association signals. These findings underscore the importance of incorporating predicted functional consequences into association analyses and establish a comprehensive resource linking exome-wide predicted GoF and LoF variants to the human phenome across ancestry-specific and multi-ancestry analyses.

title: Predicting Blood Flow in Reconstructed Intestines Based on Abdominal Aortic Calcification and Clinical Effects of Left Colic Artery Preservation in Colorectal Cancer Surgery: A Subanalysis of the HiSCO-09 Study.
authorString: Ishikawa S, Shimomura M, Shimizu W, Miguchi M, Ikeda S, Nakahara M, Mukai S, Yoshimitsu M, Kochi M, Ohdan H.
abstractText:
Aim

To clarify the relationship between the abdominal aortic calcification score on preoperative computed tomography and intraoperative regional tissue oxygen saturation (rSO2), assess the feasibility of predicting perfusion impairment through imaging, and evaluate whether left colic artery preservation improves blood flow and reduces the risk of anastomotic leakage in patients with impaired perfusion.

Methods

In this subanalysis of the HiSCO-09 trial, rSO2 was measured using INVOS in the intestinal segment at the intended intestinal anastomosis site following mesenteric preparation as a blood flow indicator. Patients were categorized according to the abdominal aortic calcification score based on preoperative computed tomography findings into low (≤ 2.13 mL) and high (> 2.13 mL) groups.

Results

Of the 282 patients, the high abdominal aortic calcification group included 135 patients. Compared with the low group, the high group showed significantly higher incidence of anastomotic leakage (4.8% vs. 12.6%, p = 0.019) and consistently lower rSO2 values. Abdominal aortic calcification score correlated negatively with rSO2 at the anastomosis site (p = 0.011). Within the high group, left colic artery preservation was associated with higher rSO2 and a lower incidence of anastomotic leakage (p = 0.032).

Conclusions

Preoperative abdominal aortic calcification assessment was weakly associated with reduced intraoperative rSO2. Exploratory subgroup analysis indicated that left colic artery preservation was associated with better perfusion and fewer anastomotic leakages in patients with high calcification. Although insufficient as a stand-alone predictor, abdominal aortic calcification may serve as a complementary factor in multifactorial preoperative risk assessments for future prospective evaluation.

title: Feasibility of omitting the unenhanced phase in CT angiography for acute aortic pathologies.
authorString: Cho SB, Byun J.
abstractText:
Objectives

To evaluate the feasibility of a contrast-only computed tomography angiography (CTA) protocol versus a conventional multiphase protocol for detecting and characterizing acute aortic pathologies, and reducing radiation dose.

Materials & methods

This retrospective study included 160 patients who underwent multiphase CTA for evaluating acute aortic syndrome. Two readers independently evaluated 640 predefined aortic segments for the presence of aneurysms, dissections, intramural hematomas (IMH), and penetrating atherosclerotic ulcers (PAU). Non-inferiority was assessed using generalized estimating equations with a prespecified 5% margin. Inter-protocol and inter-reader agreements were calculated using Cohen's kappa. Radiation dose also was compared.

Results

The contrast-only protocol demonstrated non-inferiority to the full protocol for detecting all major aortic pathologies, with all confidence intervals falling within the 5% margin. Detection rates were identical for aneurysms (33.6% vs. 33.6%; p = 1.000) and similar for dissections (15.6% vs. 15.9%; p = 0.500). Detection rates were slightly higher with the contrast-only protocol for IMH (5.8% vs. 5.0%) and PAU (5.8% vs. 4.7%), primarily reflecting false-positive interpretation. Interprotocol agreement was perfect for aneurysm shape and rupture status (kappa = 1.000) but lower for mural thrombus characterization (kappa = 0.703). The contrast-only protocol achieved a 32.1 ± 5.7% reduction in mean DLP and 32.4 ± 4.5% for CTDI vol (both, p < 0.001).

Conclusion

In patients with acute aortic pathology, a contrast-only protocol demonstrated non-inferior diagnostic performance to the full multiphase protocol, with comparable reader agreement and a 32% reduction in radiation dose. These findings suggest that omitting the unenhanced phase may be feasible in selected clinical scenarios, particularly in patients undergoing serial surveillance imaging, where cumulative dose reduction is a priority.

title: Zero-Contrast Transcatheter Aortic Valve-in-Valve Replacement Guided by Continuous Hemodynamic Monitoring.
authorString: Miura M, Watanabe Y, Omiya J, Kozuma K.

journal.title: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions

abstractText: An 89-year-old man with structural deterioration of a surgical aortic bioprosthesis and renal dysfunction underwent zero-contrast transcatheter aortic valve-in-surgical valve (TAV-in-SAV) implantation. A SavvyWire provided continuous left ventricular pressure monitoring and rapid pacing during the procedure. After implantation of a 23-mm self-expanding valve, a residual transvalvular gradient was detected, prompting balloon postdilatation under rapid pacing. Repeat invasive hemodynamic assessment showed improvement, and echocardiography demonstrated a mean gradient of 12 mmHg. At 12 months, the patient was in New York Heart Association class I, with preserved renal function and a mean gradient of 8 mmHg. Continuous pressure monitoring may support intraprocedural assessment and guide valve optimization when contrast exposure is being avoided in patients with renal dysfunction.

title: Impact of Coronary Sinus Reducer on the Extent of Ischemia in Functional Stress Tests.
authorString: Gefen S, Mashiah G, Perez Y, Stsiapanava E, Revivo M, Shmilovich H, Banai S, Ben-Shoshan J, Konigstein M.
abstractText:
Background

The coronary sinus reducer is an established therapy for patients with refractory angina due to obstructive coronary artery disease who are not candidates for further revascularization. Although symptomatic benefits are well documented, its effect on objective measures of ischemia remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the association between coronary sinus reducer implantation and inducible myocardial ischemia assessed by functional stress testing.

Methods

We retrospectively analyzed a prospectively maintained registry of consecutive patients undergoing coronary sinus reducer implantation between 2011 and 2024. Baseline assessment included Canadian Cardiovascular Society angina class, 6-minute walk test, stress echocardiography, and dipyridamole single-photon emission computed tomography imaging, repeated at 6 months. Coprimary outcomes were changes in stress wall motion score index and in the proportion of patients with moderate or severe ischemia on single-photon emission computed tomography. Clinical nonresponders were defined as no improvement in Canadian Cardiovascular Society class at 12 months.

Results

Among 153 treated patients, 118 had complete imaging data. Median stress wall motion score index improved from 1.38 to 1.23 (P<0.001), and stress left ventricular ejection fraction increased from 55% to 60% (P=0.019). The proportion of patients with moderate or severe ischemia on single-photon emission computed tomography decreased from 52% to 24% (P<0.001). The summed difference score, available in 45 patients, did not change significantly. Clinically, 86% improved by ≥1 Canadian Cardiovascular Society class at 6 months.

Conclusions

Coronary sinus reducer implantation was associated with reduced inducible ischemia on stress echocardiography and with clinical improvement. The proportion of patients with moderate or severe ischemia on single-photon emission computed tomography decreased following Reducer implantation.

title: Portal Vein Recanalization in Children with Extrahepatic Portal Vein Obstruction: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
authorString: Miotto DADSM, Riaño AS, Grunewald STF, Renoste SR, Lopes LHC, de Carvalho LHPM, Shehan TSM.
abstractText:
Purpose

To synthesize the technical success, safety, durability, and clinical efficacy of percutaneous portal vein recanalization in children with non-cirrhotic extrahepatic portal vein obstruction without underlying liver disease.

Materials and methods

PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched from inception to May 2026 for pediatric patients with non-cirrhotic extrahepatic portal vein obstruction who underwent percutaneous portal vein recanalization. Random-effects meta-analyses estimated pooled proportions with 95% confidence intervals and prediction intervals.

Results

Five retrospective single-center cohorts (73 children; variceal bleeding, hypersplenism, or both) were included. Pooled denominators were 67 for technical success, 54 for safety and mortality (Pimpalwar contributed to technical success only), and 16 for post-recanalization durability. Technical success was 55.0% (95% confidence interval 41.0-68.0; prediction interval 28.6-79.4). Procedure-related and all-cause mortality were both 0% (0/54); procedure-related hemorrhage 7% (95% confidence interval 2-23); and portal-biliary fistula 3% (95% confidence interval 0-27). Among the 16 children with successful recanalization and imaging follow-up, assisted portal vein patency was 87% (95% confidence interval 61-97); 50.8% required at least one endovascular re-intervention during surveillance, without surgical conversion; freedom from recurrent variceal or gastrointestinal bleeding among those with variceal bleeding as indication was 100% (prediction interval 73.8-100).

Conclusion

In children with chronic native-vessel extrahepatic portal vein obstruction, percutaneous portal vein recanalization may be feasible. No procedure-related mortality was observed, bleeding events were infrequent, and no recurrent variceal bleeding occurred after successful recanalization in patients for whom this outcome was reported.

Level of evidence

Level 4, meta-analysis of case series and retrospective cohort studies.

Trial / protocol registration

Prospectively registered with the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO): CRD420261395918.
