title: Severe gastric distension in a teenage boy.
authorString: Chang E, Wolfson S, Heuckeroth RO, Medne L, Nomakuchi TT, Murrell J, Reichert SL, Weckselblatt B, Webster J.
abstractText: A 16-year-old male presented with acute abdominal pain, nausea, and distension and was found to have severe gastric dilation on imaging. Antroduodenal manometry showed erythromycin-induced phase 3 migrating motor complex beginning in the antrum but post-prandial antral hypoactivity. Mitochondrial DNA sequencing was normal. Exome analysis revealed a rare variant of uncertain significance in the smooth muscle myosin heavy chain 11 (MYH11) gene (NM_002474.3: c.4123G>A, p.Asp1375Asn), which is necessary for smooth muscle contraction. Pathogenic MYH11 alterations cause multiple disorders, including autosomal dominant (AD) familial thoracic aortic aneurysm, AD visceral myopathy, and autosomal recessive megacystis-microcolon-intestinal-hypoperistalsis syndrome. Amino acid p.Asp1375 is within the rod region of the MYH11 protein that self-assembles to form thick filaments; thus, pathogenic variants in this region may affect filament formation and impair interactions with thin filaments. While the phenotype overlap is compelling, further research is needed to determine the clinical significance of this alteration.

title: Associations of Physical Activity With Mortality and Cardiovascular Diseases in Adults With Chronic Kidney Disease: A Community-Based Cohort Study.
authorString: Xu C, Yu C, Zhang S, Xu S, Xiao Y, Zeng X, Zhang Q, Abduldayeva AA, Doszhanova GN, Iskakova SA, Zhao L, Li T, Chen J, Chen H, Yan X.
abstractText:
Background

Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is linked to elevated risks of mortality and cardiovascular diseases (CVDs). This study aimed to investigate the dose-response associations of moderate-to-vigorous-intensity physical activity (MVPA) with all-cause mortality and CVD risk in adults with CKD.

Methods

We included 3927 UK Biobank participants with CKD. Weekly MVPA duration was evaluated by wrist-worn accelerometers and a machine learning model. The primary outcomes were all-cause mortality and CVDs (heart failure, myocardial infarction, and stroke). Cox proportional hazards models and restricted cubic splines were used to assess the dose-response associations.

Results

CKD participants engaged in less MVPA than healthy controls. During a median follow-up of 7.92 years, 393 deaths and 445 CVDs occurred. Moderate-to-vigorous-intensity physical activity showed nonlinear associations with mortality and CVD risk. Mortality risk declined sharply up to 150 minutes per week MVPA and plateaued thereafter. Cardiovascular disease risk reached its lowest at approximately 300 minutes per week. Compared with <150 minutes per week, ≥150 minutes per week MVPA was associated with lower risks of mortality (hazard ratio = 0.64; 95% CI, 0.51-0.80) and CVDs (hazard ratio = 0.68; 95% CI, 0.55-0.83). Replacing sedentary behavior with MVPA for 10 min/d was associated with a significantly reduced mortality rate among less active CKD participants (hazard ratio = 0.70; 95% CI, 0.56-0.86).

Conclusions

In adults with CKD, engaging in MVPA of ≥150 minutes per week was associated with significantly lower risks of mortality and CVDs. These findings underscore the value of physical activity promotion in CKD management.

title: Painless Takotsubo Syndrome Triggered by Acute Exacerbation of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD): A Retrospective Observational Study of Seven Cases.
authorString: Kirchenchtejn C, Besborodco A, Wolff Fridman M, Millner LH.
abstractText: Takotsubo syndrome (TS) as a manifestation of acute chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) exacerbation is uncommonly reported. Emotional and adrenergic stress, hypoxemia, negative intrathoracic pressure, and the use of beta-agonists are frequently implicated in triggering myocardial dysfunction in this setting. We present a retrospective study of seven cases of TS in patients with COPD exacerbation in which none reported typical chest pain, representing a diagnostic challenge in patients with an apparent clinical justification for their dyspnea. All patients had electrocardiographic changes and elevated cardiac biomarkers, underwent echocardiography and coronary angiography or coronary computed tomography angiography, and received a confirmed diagnosis of TS. Five patients achieved complete recovery of ventricular function, one had partial recovery, and one died during hospitalization due to refractory ventricular arrhythmia. Systematic use of electrocardiography and cardiac biomarkers in COPD exacerbation enabled early diagnosis and appropriate management in the absence of typical angina.

title: Serglycin regulates macrophage differentiation and is associated with human atherosclerotic plaque stability.
authorString: Gialeli C, Fountas P, Bocci M, Sun J, Shami A, Nitulescu M, Persson A, Bengtsson E, Knutsen E, Pietras K, Kolset SO, Theocharis AD, Edsfeldt A, Gonçalves I.

journal.title: American journal of physiology. Cell physiology

abstractText: Inflammation contributes to the destabilization of atherosclerotic plaques and increases the risk of cardiovascular events such as myocardial infarction and stroke. Extracellular matrix components modulate inflammation and immune responses within the plaque microenvironment. Serglycin (SRGN), is a proteoglycan primarily expressed by immune cells that regulates inflammation, but its role in human atherosclerotic plaques remains unclear. SRGN protein levels were quantified by ELISA in carotid endarterectomy samples from patients in the Atherosclerotic Plaque Imaging Project and compared between symptomatic and asymptomatic plaques. SRGN spatial localization was evaluated by multispectral imaging and histology. Glycosylation patterns were examined by immunoprecipitation and immunoblotting. Functional effects were investigated using CRISPR-mediated SRGN knockout in THP-1 monocytes differentiated into macrophages and exposed to oxidized low-density lipoprotein (oxLDL). SRGN levels were higher in plaques from asymptomatic patients compared with plaques from symptomatic patients and localized primarily to macrophage- and lipid-rich regions. Plaque SRGN was positively associated with histological markers of plaque stability, displayed heterogeneous molecular forms and showed an inverse association with the plaque vulnerability index. In vitro, SRGN deficiency was associated with a more pro-inflammatory macrophage profile, impaired M2-like polarization, and increased lipid retention following oxLDL exposure. These findings indicate that SRGN is associated with inflammatory cell presence, lipid accumulation, and features of plaque stability in human plaques, and suggest a role for SRGN in macrophage differentiation and lipid handling in atherosclerotic lesions.

title: Early versus delayed surgery to prevent hemorrhagic transformation in patients with septic cerebral emboli from infective endocarditis.
authorString: Lao JY, Lutfi W, Sperry AE, Guo J, Kurzan P, Taveras C, Catalano MA, Holmes JH, Lawrence K, Desai ND, Srinivasan VM, Brown C.

journal.title: The Journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery

abstractText:
Objective

The optimal timing of cardiac surgery in patients with infective endocarditis and ischemic septic cerebral embolism remains uncertain, largely because of concern for perioperative hemorrhagic transformation. This study evaluates the association between surgical timing and outcomes in this population.

Methods

Patients with infective endocarditis and preoperative septic cerebral emboli who underwent cardiac surgery were identified from an institutional database (1999-2025). After excluding those with preoperative cerebral hemorrhage, 240 patients with ischemic stroke were stratified by interval from stroke to surgery: early (≤7 days, n=109) versus delayed (8-30 days, n=131). Propensity score matching was used to balance baseline confounders. The primary outcome was postoperative hemorrhagic transformation; secondary outcomes included new postoperative stroke, intensive care unit and hospital length of stay, four-year survival assessed by Kaplan-Meier analysis, and mortality assessed by Cox proportional hazards modeling.

Results

Matching yielded 194 patients. Postoperative hemorrhagic transformation occurred in 10 of 194 (5.2%) patients and did not differ by timing (6.2% early vs. 4.1% delayed, p=0.73). New postoperative stroke occurred in 19 of 194 patients (9.8%) and was similar (10.3% early vs. 9.3% delayed, p>0.99), as was 30-day mortality (6.2% early vs. 10.3% delayed, p=0.42). Four-year survival did not differ by timing (68.0% early vs. 57.4% delayed, p=0.07), and there was no significant association between surgical timing and mortality (HR 0.67 [0.44-1.03]; p=0.07).

Conclusions

In patients with infective endocarditis and ischemic stroke, early surgery (≤7 days) was not associated with increased rates of postoperative hemorrhagic transformation, new stroke, or 30-day or long-term mortality compared with delayed surgery.

title: CCL17-CCR4 Signalling Attenuates Pressure Overload-Induced Cardiac Remodelling Through IGFBP6 Suppression in Cardiac Fibroblasts
authorString: Dai Y, Guo W, Zhang Y, Yan W, Zheng P, Lian Z, Gu G, Wang X, Chen X, Wong C.
abstractText:
Background and Aims:

Chemokines regulate immune-cell trafficking, inflammation, and tissue repair in cardiovascular disease. C-C motif chemokine ligand 17 (CCL17) has been linked to adverse remodelling after myocardial infarction and neurohumoral stress, but its role during sustained mechanical pressure overload remains unclear. We investigated whether CCL17 regulates ventricular remodelling through signalling in cardiac fibroblasts. Methods We performed serum proteomic screening and assessed CCL17 in human serum and myocardial samples. We evaluated CCL17 function in mice subjected to transverse aortic constriction using global Ccl17 deletion and adeno-associated virus-mediated CCL17 augmentation. We used cardiac transcriptomics and pharmacological, small interfering RNA, and promoter-reporter experiments in cardiac fibroblasts to investigate downstream signalling. We tested the functional contribution of Igfbp6 in vivo using fibroblast-directed silencing. Results Serum CCL17 concentrations and myocardial CCL17 abundance were higher in patients with aortic stenosis than in controls. Cardiac and circulating CCL17 increased rapidly after transverse aortic constriction. Ccl17 deletion aggravated systolic dysfunction, hypertrophy, and fibrosis after pressure overload, whereas CCL17 augmentation attenuated these changes. Cardiac transcriptomics identified insulin-like growth factor-binding protein 6 (IGFBP6) as a candidate downstream mediator. In cardiac fibroblasts, CCL17 reduced cellular and secreted IGFBP6 levels and alpha-smooth muscle actin expression through C-C chemokine receptor 4 (CCR4)-dependent signalling, accompanied by suppression of early growth response 1 (EGR1). Genetic perturbation and promoter-reporter experiments supported a role for EGR1 in the regulation of Igfbp6 downstream of CCR4. Fibroblast-directed Igfbp6 silencing improved systolic function and reduced hypertrophy and fibrosis in Ccl17-deficient mice after transverse aortic constriction. Conclusions CCL17 attenuates maladaptive cardiac remodelling in mice subjected to pressure overload. The findings support a mechanism in which CCL17 acts through CCR4 and EGR1 to suppress IGFBP6 in cardiac fibroblasts.

Keywords:

Aortic stenosis, CCL17, cardiac fibrosis, fibroblasts, IGFBP6, pressure overload

title: Rezafungin for sternal wound infection caused by multidrug-resistant Candidozyma auris: a case report.
authorString: Luthra S, David A, Thirukumaran D, Yam TS.
abstractText: Introduction. Candidozyma auris is an emerging multidrug-resistant fungal pathogen associated with healthcare outbreaks and significant mortality. Management can be challenging due to antifungal resistance and the need for prolonged intravenous therapy. Case Presentation. A 58-year-old man developed a postoperative sternal wound infection caused by multidrug-resistant C. auris following aortic valve replacement, coronary artery bypass grafting and ascending aortic interposition graft surgery. His postoperative course was complicated by Staphylococcus epidermidis prosthetic graft infection requiring redo valve replacement and graft repair and placement of vacuum-assisted closure. Two weeks after discharge home, persistent wound discharge yielded C. auris. Following surgical debridement and initiation of intravenous caspofungin with oral itraconazole, once-daily intravenous antifungal therapy was transitioned to once-weekly intravenous rezafungin to facilitate outpatient treatment coordinated with vacuum-assisted wound therapy. Conclusion. After 12 weeks of dual antifungal therapy, complete clinical and microbiological resolution was achieved without adverse events. This case highlights the feasibility of rezafungin as an outpatient treatment strategy for complex multidrug-resistant C. auris infections.

title: Persistent metabolic remodeling after dietary salt reduction reveals sex differences in the adaptation to chronic high-salt intake.
authorString: Göktaş SŞ, Spégel P, Magnusson M, Meissner A, Duarte JMN.
abstractText:
Background

Excessive salt intake is a risk factor for cardiovascular disease, yet its systemic metabolic consequences and its relationship to differential cardiovascular adaptations in males and females remain poorly understood. Here, we performed plasma metabolite profiling in male and female mice subjected to long-term high-salt diet (HSD) exposure during aging.

Methods

Mice were fed HSD (8.6% NaCl) or low-salt normal diet (ND; 0.6% NaCl) from 9 to 23 months of age, with a subset of mice undergoing diet reversal to ND after 7 months of HSD. Plasma metabolites were analyzed using gas chromatography/mass spectrometry and related to previously reported measurements of arterial blood pressure and cardiac function.

Results

Female mice developed salt-sensitive hypertension driven by vascular dysfunction, whereas male mice exhibited cardiac and vascular remodeling independent of blood pressure. Among 48 measured metabolites, HSD induced substantial alterations in levels of glucose, glycerol, glycerol phosphates, and fatty acids. Males showed a near-complete normalization of metabolite profiles following 7 months of salt reduction, whereas females retained a metabolomic signature different from ND despite normalization of blood pressure. In particular, metabolites related to energy metabolism, lipid handling, and osmotic balance were influenced by both diet and sex, with linoleate showing a significant sex-diet interaction. Correlation analyses demonstrated associations between metabolite profiles and cardiovascular parameters with different patterns in males and females.

Conclusion

Our findings demonstrate that chronic high-salt consumption induces persistent plasma metabolite alterations displaying different patterns in male and female mice that are not fully reversed by a salt-lowering dietary intervention. The dissociation between physiological recovery and metabolic normalization, particularly in females, suggests that metabolic alterations may represent an additional layer of cardiovascular risk beyond blood pressure control in mice.

title: Alpinia zerumbet leaf extract attenuates cardiovascular remodeling in 2K1C renovascular hypertension: Association with AT1 receptor and redox-inflammatory responses.
authorString: Beserra-Silva DL, de Menezes MP, Dos Santos GP, da Silva AM, Cavalheira MA, de Oliveira BC, de Bem GF, da Costa CA, Resende AC, Ognibene DT.
abstractText: Renovascular hypertension involves persistent activation of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system, oxidative stress, inflammation, and cardiovascular remodeling. Alpinia zerumbet leaf extract (ALE) is a polyphenol-rich preparation with known antihypertensive properties. This study investigated the effects of chronic ALE treatment on cardiovascular remodeling in the two-kidney, one-clip (2K1C) model of renovascular hypertension. Male Wistar rats (45 days old; n = 11 per group) were allocated into four groups: Sham, Sham + ALE, 2K1C, and 2K1C + ALE. Animals were subjected to 2K1C surgery or laparotomy (Sham) and received ALE (50 mg/kg/day in drinking water) or vehicle for seven weeks. Blood pressure was monitored throughout the protocol, and vascular reactivity was evaluated in the mesenteric arterial bed. Histological and immunohistochemical analyses assessed structural remodeling, cardiomyocyte cross-sectional area (CSA), fibrosis, and AT1 receptor, TGF-β, and MMP-2 immunostaining in the aorta and heart. Cardiovascular oxidative damage, antioxidant defenses, inflammatory cytokines, nitrite levels, and plasma angiotensin II concentrations were also evaluated. ALE significantly attenuated the rise in systolic, diastolic, and mean blood pressure in 2K1C rats, despite not improving endothelial dysfunction in the mesenteric arterial bed. Treatment prevented increased AT1 receptor immunostaining in the aorta and heart without altering plasma angiotensin II levels. Furthermore, ALE partially reduced aortic hypertrophy, prevented cardiac concentric remodeling, fibrosis, and cardiomyocyte CSA, and reduced TGF-β and MMP-2 immunostaining in both tissues. In addition, ALE reduced lipid peroxidation and inflammatory cytokine levels while restoring antioxidant defenses in the plasma and cardiovascular tissues. ALE attenuates cardiovascular remodeling in renovascular hypertension, associated with reduced AT1 receptor expression and redox-inflammatory responses.

title: Left Bundle Branch Optimized Resynchronization Therapy for Persistent Ventricular Dysfunction After Complex PCI and TAVR.
authorString: Chin EYH, Koh KT, Said AB, Pang IX, Khor HK, Fong AYY, Ong TK, Oon YY.
abstractText:
Background

Severe aortic stenosis with complex coronary artery disease presents challenges in patients unsuitable for surgery. Persistent left bundle branch block (LBBB) after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) may impair ventricular recovery.

Case summary

A 67-year-old man underwent high-risk left main-left anterior descending percutaneous coronary intervention, complicated by cardiogenic shock and severe left ventricular (LV) dysfunction. Subsequent TAVR achieved favorable valve hemodynamics but was followed by new-onset left bundle branch block and persistent LV dysfunction. Left bundle branch pacing achieved complete correction only at high output. A coronary sinus lead was added for left bundle branch-optimized cardiac resynchronization therapy with a defibrillator (LOT-CRTD). At 3 months, LV function fully recovered with reverse remodeling and marked symptom improvement. Why Beyond the Guideline: Optimal percutaneous coronary intervention-TAVR timing and device strategies for post-TAVR LBBB with LV dysfunction remain poorly defined in current guidelines.

Discussion

LOT-CRTD may provide effective cardiac resynchronization when isolated left bundle branch pacing cannot achieve optimal correction.

Take-home message

Sequence of PCI-TAVR remained individualized. LOT-CRT is a viable strategy to facilitate ventricular recovery for post-TAVR LBBB.

title: "Whiplash Motion" in Cardiac Intimal Sarcoma With Functional Mitral Stenosis and Dynamic LVOT Obstruction.
authorString: Oshiro N, Yoshida T, Kakii B, Higuchi T, Mitsuyama S, Furui M, Suzuki H, Kawashima T, Nakatsuka SI, Kubo Y.
abstractText:
Background

Cardiac intimal sarcoma (CIS) usually presents as an isolated left atrial mass; pan-left-heart involvement producing simultaneous inflow and outflow obstruction is rare.

Case summary

A 43-year-old man presented in acute heart failure (B-type natriuretic peptide 948.8 pg/mL; right ventricular systolic pressure 59 mm Hg). Imaging showed a tumor in the left atrium and ventricle: an atrial mass infiltrated the mitral leaflet, causing functional mitral stenosis, whereas a mobile papillary-muscle component showed a "whiplash motion," prolapsing into the left ventricular outflow tract and protruding through the aortic valve in systole. Emergency debulking and mechanical mitral valve replacement followed; histopathology confirmed CIS (mouse double minute 2 homolog/cyclin-dependent kinase 4 positive, mouse double minute 2 homolog-amplified). Although adjuvant carbon-ion radiotherapy provided temporary control, the patient died 20 months later.

Discussion

We propose the "whiplash motion" sign and highlight the trade-off between mechanical-valve durability and bleeding risk during thoracic radiotherapy.

Take-home message

CIS can cause dual left-heart obstruction through multicomponent tumor dynamics; prosthetic valve choice should anticipate multimodality oncologic management.

title: Age-Stratified Disproportionality Analysis of Bruton's tyrosine kinase inhibitors in FAERS and VigiBase.
authorString: Qu H, Jia Y, Liu Z, Li Z, Zhao X, Wu Z, Fan G, Lou Y.
abstractText:
Introduction

Bruton's Tyrosine Kinase inhibitors (BTKis) are increasingly used because of their efficacy; however, safety concerns are emerging.

Methods

This study extracted data from FAERS and VigiBase and divided patients into four age groups. The Reporting Odds Ratio (ROR) was used to identify safety signals.

Results

Regarding cardiac disorders, zanubrutinib showed a specific cardiac arrest signal in the 0-60-year age group in FAERS, and the Atrial Fibrillation (AF) signal intensity increased with age in VigiBase. Conversely, the AF signals decreased across successive age groups for acalabrutinib in VigiBase and for ibrutinib in both databases. Several cardiac PTs for acalabrutinib met the signal criteria in the 61-70-year group. For skin and subcutaneous tissue disorders, multiple nail-related Adverse Drug Events (ADEs) were observed in all age groups for ibrutinib; acalabrutinib and zanubrutinib exhibited no nail-related signals, whereas other skin-related signals were primarily detected in patients aged >60 years. Regarding bleeding ADEs, thirty types were detected for ibrutinib and four for acalabrutinib; zanubrutinib showed no age-specific bleeding signals. For infections and infestations, among the PTs detected in three or more age groups, aspergillus infection, bronchopulmonary aspergillosis, and onychomycosis were consistently ranked among the top ten signals for ibrutinib based on VigiBase ROR025 across all four age groups, with ROR025 values decreasing with increasing age. Signals for different types of pneumonia were detected in all age groups for the BTKis, except in the 0-60- year age group of zanubrutinib. Moreover, the specific signals warrant further attention.

Discussion

This comprehensive analysis of FAERS and VigiBase data highlights age-related differences in ADE reporting across BTKi therapies. These findings identify age-stratified reporting patterns that may help prioritize further safety investigations. A limitation of this study is the lack of integration of potential biological mechanisms underlying BTKi-related ADEs.

Conclusion

This study identified age-stratified reporting patterns for three BTKis in two spontaneous reporting systems. These findings are hypothesis-generating and do not establish differences in clinical risk across age groups or causal relationships.

title: Recurrent Hypertensive Carcinoid Crisis Despite Somatostatin Analog Therapy.
authorString: Ghannoum A, Young AC, Rao R.
abstractText: Carcinoid crisis is a rare, life-threatening complication of neuroendocrine tumors characterized by hemodynamic instability. Although hypotension is more commonly described, severe hypertension can also occur. An 84-year-old woman who had undergone resection of a grade 1 terminal ileal neuroendocrine tumor and two hepatic metastases presented with worsening flushing, severe headaches, mild wheeze, palpitations, and chest tightness. She was receiving maintenance long-acting lanreotide and had used the maximum prescribed dose of rescue subcutaneous octreotide for two weeks without sustained benefit. Her blood pressure was highly labile, with a peak systolic reading of 198 mmHg, and her heart rate reached 110 beats/min. The endocrinology team diagnosed a hypertensive carcinoid crisis. Her symptoms and hypertension resolved within 24 h of commencing a continuous intravenous octreotide infusion, and a plan was made to shorten the lanreotide dosing interval from three weeks to two weeks. Eleven days after discharge, she was readmitted with recurrent flushing, palpitations, tachycardia, and hypertension after the dose due under the revised lanreotide schedule was delayed. Subcutaneous octreotide improved the flushing and hypertension, while bisoprolol was introduced for persistent symptomatic tachycardia. Cardiac investigations showed no sustained arrhythmia or major structural abnormality. Biochemical markers measured after treatment were within their reference ranges. Subsequent somatostatin receptor positron emission tomography/computed tomography demonstrated new receptor-avid disease in the liver and left pelvis that had not been identified on preceding conventional imaging. This case demonstrates that hypertension can be the predominant hemodynamic manifestation of carcinoid crisis and highlights the limited value of normal biomarkers obtained after somatostatin analog treatment, which should not be used in isolation to exclude an acute crisis.

title: Chronic polystyrene nanoplastics exposure reprograms gene expression, alternative splicing, and disrupts host-microbiome-metabolic networks to promote atherosclerosis in LDLr⁻/⁻ mice.
authorString: Khan A, Vasquez DEC, Si Y, Vidar WS, Wu K, Chiu N, Jia Z.
abstractText: Micro- and nanoplastics have been detected in human blood and carotid atheromas, yet their mechanistic contribution to atherogenesis is poorly defined, and chronic exposure studies of nanoplastics are limited. This multi-omics study investigates chronic (12-week) oral exposure to 80 nm polystyrene nanoplastics in LDLr⁻/⁻ mice, integrating aortic plaque quantification, hepatic transcriptomics with alternative splicing profiling, gut microbiome 16S sequencing, and liver untargeted metabolomics into a unified host-microbiome-metabolite network. Nanoplastics increased aortic lipid deposition, suppressed hepatic detoxification and anti-atherogenic lipid pathways at the transcriptional and post-transcriptional levels including alternative splicing events. Exposure induced gut dysbiosis, reduced SCFA-producing commensals and enriched pro-atherogenic pathobionts, shifts co-occurring directionally with hepatic transcriptional modules. Hepatic genes (down-regulated Fbp1, Ccn1 and Cyp2c29; upregulated Chka) and gut genera (depleted Bacteroides; enriched Faecalibaculum and Streptococcus) were confirmed by RT-qPCR and genus-specific qPCR. Untargeted metabolomics showed elevated aromatic and branched-chain amino acids such as tryptophan and methionine, and depletion of glutathione precursor γ-glutamylcysteine and the antioxidant taurine, implicating oxidative stress and amino-acid dysregulation. Concordance with human MASLD (GSE135251) and atherosclerotic plaque (GSE100927) transcriptomes and gut signatures matching human atherosclerotic microbiome profiles suggest plausibility for human relevance. This research implicates nanoplastics as a cardiovascular risk factor involving splicing reprogramming and gut-liver crosstalk.

title: Environmental Chemical Exposures and Accelerated Epigenetic Aging: Links to Metabolic and Age-Related Health Outcomes
authorString: Shin H, Kim J, Song E, Kim N, Heo M, Kim Y, Oh J, Cho YM, Hong Y, Kim WJ, Won S.
abstractText: Environmental chemical exposures may influence biological aging, but their relationships with epigenetic aging and related health outcomes remain incompletely understood. In this study, we evaluated the associations of 13 environmental exposures, including heavy metals, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), and volatile organic compounds (VOCs), with epigenetic aging in 666 older adults from the Forensic Research via Omics Markers in Environmental Health Vulnerable Areas (FROM) cohort. Among the evaluated epigenetic aging biomarkers, GrimAge acceleration showed the most prominent associations, with 2-hydroxyfluorene (2-HF), 2-naphthol (2-NAP), blood cadmium (bCd), and methylhippuric acid (MHA) exhibiting significant positive associations (strongest for 2-HF: beta = 0.491 years per doubling of exposure, P = 1.22 x 10-14). Quantile g-computation showed that combined environmental exposures were significantly associated with increased GrimAge acceleration (psi = 0.497, 95% CI: 0.013-0.981, P = 0.044), and Bayesian kernel machine regression identified 2-HF and 2-NAP as major contributors. Among clinical traits, white blood cell count (WBC) and gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT) were significantly and positively associated with GrimAge acceleration, and two-sample Mendelian randomization provided nominal support for a positive effect of GrimAge acceleration on GGT. Mediation analyses identified significant indirect effects through GrimAge acceleration for the associations of 2-HF, 2-NAP, bCd, and MHA with GGT. Exploratory disease analyses further suggested potential associations with diabetic nephropathy and osteoporosis, together with an inverse association with cardiac valvular disease. These findings suggest that environmental chemical exposures are associated with accelerated epigenetic aging, which may represent a biological pathway linking environmental exposures to metabolic and age-related health outcomes.

title: Recurrent Multi-territory Thromboembolism As the Initial Presentation of Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma and Suspected Nonbacterial Thrombotic Endocarditis.
authorString: Alsammak R, Ferry P.
abstractText: Nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis (NBTE), also known as Marantic endocarditis, is an uncommon complication of malignancy that may cause systemic embolization. We report a 74-year-old woman who developed a right gastrocnemius deep vein thrombosis followed by recurrent right middle cerebral artery occlusions requiring two mechanical thrombectomies. Her subsequent course was complicated by further deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, and acute limb ischemia. Repeat echocardiography demonstrated mitral valve vegetations, initially raising concern for infective endocarditis. However, repeated blood cultures and cultures of retrieved thrombotic material were negative. Imaging revealed widespread metastatic disease, and biopsy of a left supraclavicular lymph node confirmed metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma. The combination of recurrent arterial and venous thrombosis, advanced malignancy, and negative microbiological investigations favored a clinical diagnosis of NBTE. This case illustrates how extensive thromboembolic disease may precede the diagnosis of pancreatic cancer and highlights the diagnostic challenge posed by valvular vegetations in this setting.

title: Viral Gene Therapy for Danon Disease: From LAMP2 Biology to Clinical Translation.
authorString: Gunes EA, Patel U, Iyer S, Taub A, Lee-Guest E, Cline S, Arakelyan T, Tiwari K, Tran L, Hong K, Adler E.
abstractText:
Purpose of review

Danon disease is a rare, highly penetrant and morbid X-linked cardioskeletal myopathy caused by loss-of-function variants in the lysosome-associated membrane protein 2 (LAMP2) gene. We review the rationale for LAMP2B gene replacement, the basis for adeno-associated virus serotype 9 (AAV9) vector selection, the first-in-human clinical evidence, and immunological barriers that define its therapeutic window.

Recent findings

Preclinical models demonstrating restoration of autophagic flux via human LAMP2B gene delivery have provided the basis for clinical translation. The first-in-human phase 1 clinical data highlights the progress of recombinant adeno-associated virus serotype 9 carrying human LAMP2B (AAV9.LAMP2B) gene therapy (RP-A501). Seven male patients received a single intravenous infusion of AAV9.LAMP2B with transient immunomodulation. Myocardial transduction was achieved; LAMP2B protein was detectable by immunohistochemistry, autophagic vacuoles were reduced, left ventricular mass index fell by a median of 23%, cardiac troponin I and natriuretic peptides declined, and functional class improved in all evaluable patients. Toxicity was dose-limiting. Emerging clinical data supports that viral LAMP2B gene therapy is a viable disease-modifying strategy, although from a small cohort, for Danon disease. The long-term durability of transgene expression, patient safety and toxicity profiles with exclusion of affected females remain unresolved. The pivotal single-arm phase 2 study (NCT06092034) is ongoing.

title: Novel Transcatheter Device Use in Patent Ductus Arteriosus Closure in an 800-g Infant.
authorString: Gritti MN, Fitzgerald N.
abstractText:
Background

Outcomes of transcatheter patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) occlusion in premature infants have improved with low-profile devices. The Azur Vascular Plug is a soft, uncovered, microcatheter-deliverable device described as a novel option for PDA closure in premature infants.

First-in-human/early reports

We report a successful Azur implantation in a 21-day-old infant weighing 830 g at the time of the procedure, representing the lowest procedural weight reported for this device.

Discussion

The ductal anatomy was unsuitable for a 3-2 mm Piccolo device because of aortic obstruction from extrinsic compression. After Azur deployment, there was no residual shunt or obstruction to adjacent vessels.

Novelty

This is the smallest patient reported to undergo Azur device closure of a premature PDA, extending its application for this off-label indication.

Take-home message

The Azur device may provide an effective, low-profile option for PDA closure in extremely premature infants with challenging ductal anatomy.

title: Extensive Native Aortic Valve Infiltration and Early Bioprosthetic Valve Degeneration in Low-Grade Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia.
authorString: Wu KY, Chaudhry I, Sterrett RW, Gyenes GT, Church MF, Paterson DI, Sonnenberg BH.
abstractText:
Background

Cardiac manifestations of chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) are extremely rare, particularly involving valves.

Case summary

A patient with low-grade CLL presented with symptomatic severe aortic stenosis. Following surgical aortic valve replacement, the patient experienced rapid degeneration of her surgical bioprosthetic aortic valve, necessitating valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve replacement. Re-evaluation of her excised native aortic valve tissue on histology with immunohistochemical confirmation revealed extensive CLL infiltration.

Discussion

Extensive CLL infiltration of the aortic valve is an extremely rare phenomenon. This case raises the hypothesis that a clonal lymphoproliferative process may contribute to calcific aortic stenosis and possibly early bioprosthetic structural valve deterioration. Additional studies are needed to further evaluate this association.

Take-home messages

CLL can rarely affect cardiac valves and may contribute to the development of native valve stenosis. Additional studies are required to determine whether CLL is a risk factor for early prosthetic structural valve deterioration.

title: Agreement of noninvasive multimodality imaging measurements with balloon sizing in the cardiac catheterization laboratory prior to percutaneous pulmonary valve implantation.
authorString: Rao S, Suntharos P, Liu W, Prieto L, Worley S, Schoenhagen P, Komarlu R.
abstractText:
Objectives

Right ventricular outflow tract (RVOT) dysfunction is common in repaired congenital heart defects resulting in right ventricular (RV) dilation and dysfunction. Emerging transcatheter options enable placement of a competent pulmonary valve, obviating the need for surgery. Multimodality imaging plays a key role in determining the type and timing of intervention prior to percutaneous pulmonary valve implantation (PPVI). The authors sought to assess correlation of noninvasive RVOT measurements with cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) and cardiac computed tomography (CT) with balloon sizing in the catheterization laboratory prior to PPVI.

Methods

A retrospective review was performed on patients who had undergone PPVI with preprocedural CMR and cardiac CT scan. Three-dimensional multiplanar reconstruction (MPR) of the narrowest RVOT diameter on magnetic resonance angiography (MRA), whole heart sequence (WHS) images, and CT scan images were performed using commercially available software; balloon sizing prior to PPVI was recorded. Concordance correlation coefficients were used to assess agreement with the clinically acceptable limit between the modalities set at +/- 2 mm. Additionally, mean difference was used to quantify the difference in measurements among the 2 modalities.

Results

For maximal waist dimensions, correlation between MRA and WHS images with balloon sizing was 0.70 to 0.79, while correlation between CT scan and balloon sizing was 0.65 to 0.75. For minimal waist dimensions, correlation between MRA and WHS images was 0.72 to 0.82; correlation between CT scan and balloon sizing was 0.64 to 0.73.

Conclusions

Cardiac CT and CMR are complementary modalities that provide essential information for preprocedural planning for PPVI.

title: Perioperative neurocognitive outcomes after robot-assisted pelvic surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis of reported proportions, comparative risk and prognostic factors.
authorString: Drobot RB, Skorupka JJ, Lipa M.
abstractText: Delirium and cognitive decline may complicate recovery after robot-assisted pelvic surgery, but their frequency and relationship to positioning remain uncertain. We assessed reported proportions, comparative surgical risk and prognostic factors. PubMed, CENTRAL, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, ClinicalTrials.gov and WHO ICTRP were searched through 4 August 2026. Eligible adult robotic pelvic studies reported objective cognitive testing or delirium. Two reviewers performed original screening, extraction and question-specific bias appraisal. Post hoc logit random-effects meta-analyses summarized prospective cohorts using restricted maximum likelihood and modified Hartung-Knapp intervals in R. Twenty-six reports represented 25 studies. Five cognitive cohorts (356 participants) yielded 29.0% (95% confidence interval [CI] 20.2-39.8%); excluding Beck yielded 31.8% (20.7-45.4%). Three delirium cohorts (245 participants) yielded a descriptive model summary of 10.3% (2.2-37.0%). Individual delirium proportions were 8/82 (9.8%; exact 95% CI 4.3-18.3%), 4/80 (5.0%; 1.4-12.3%) and 14/83 (16.9%; 9.5-26.7%). The approximate 95% prediction interval from the delirium meta-analysis was very wide (<0.1-99.8%). The same-procedure prostatectomy comparison yielded an unadjusted risk ratio of 1.06 (0.73-1.55) for early cognitive decline. Comparative evidence was of low or very low certainty. Definitions, surveillance and selection limited interpretation; Trendelenburg-duration findings were inconsistent. These proportions describe selected study-defined outcomes. They do not establish attributable robotic or positioning risk, a safe exposure threshold, or benefit from horizontal breaks. Standardized prospective measurement is needed.

title: Associations of metabolic score for insulin resistance (METS-IR) with cardiovascular mortality risk in peritoneal dialysis patients.
authorString: Tsai CC, Hsieh YP, Chang YJ, Tsai SM, Chiu PF.
abstractText:
Background

Metabolic score for insulin resistance (METS-IR) is considered a simple, reliable, and cost-effective alternative indicator of insulin resistance (IR). Our study aimed to assess whether the METS-IR index was associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular (CV) death in our peritoneal dialysis (PD) cohort.

Methods

This observational study included 553 patients commencing PD for end-stage renal disease between 2003 and 2017, and they were divided into three groups according to the tertiles of METS-IR. The assessed predictor was the METS-IR index at enrollment. Cox proportional hazards models and competing risk analysis using the Fine-Gray models were used to analyze the association between the METS-IR index and CV mortality, with adjustments of potential confounding factors including medication use, demographic characteristics, comorbidities, PD-related data, and laboratory data. Furthermore, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was used to determine the exploratory cutoff value of the METS-IR index for predicting CV mortality, and the area under the ROC curve (AUC) was calculated.

Results

During follow-up, the crude CV mortality rate increased significantly, with 16 CV deaths (8.6%) in the first tertile of the METS-IR index, 32 CV deaths (17.4%) in the second tertile, and 41 CV deaths (22.3%) in the third tertile (p < 0.001). In the full adjusted model, patients in tertile 2 were associated with an HR of 1.90 (95% CI, 1.01-3.61) and those in tertile 3 was associated with an HR of 1.91 (95% CI, 1.03-3.55) compared with tertile 1. The exploratory cut-off point of METS-IR index was 33.3 (75.3% sensitivity and 48.3% specificity) with an AUC (95% CI) of 0.617 (0.557-0.677; p < 0.001), indicating modest discrimination. The results from the Fine-Gray model are consistent with those from the Cox model.

Conclusions

METS-IR can identify PD patients at high risk of CV death. However, METS-IR has limited discriminative ability in predicting CV mortality and further research is needed to validate its potential role in risk stratification.

title: Micro- and nanoplastics at the vascular interface: experimental insights into endothelial pathways and clinical evidence.
authorString: Trippel N, Schiebisch H, Brüstle F, Schieffer B, Grote K.
abstractText: Micro- and nanoplastics (MNPs) are increasingly recognized as environmental contaminants with potential implications for cardiovascular health. Their detection in the human circulation and vascular tissues raises the question of how circulating plastic particles interact with the vessel wall. As the primary cellular interface between the circulation and surrounding tissues, the vascular endothelium is uniquely positioned to encounter circulating MNPs. In this Review, we integrate experimental and human evidence on MNP-endothelium interactions and critically examine whether endothelial injury may provide a mechanistic link between circulating MNPs and cardiovascular disease. Experimental studies increasingly support direct effects of MNPs on endothelial homeostasis, including inflammatory and oxidative stress responses, impaired barrier integrity, and alterations in endothelial phenotype and function. Human studies, in contrast, primarily demonstrate circulating and vascular MNP burden and associations with atherosclerotic disease and cardiovascular outcomes, without yet establishing direct endothelial dysfunction or causality. Major differences between experimental exposure conditions and human internal exposure, together with analytical uncertainties in MNP detection, further complicate translation of these findings. Understanding how the endothelium functions as an interface for circulating MNPs, and to what extent it mediates their vascular effects, will be essential for defining the cardiovascular relevance of human MNP exposure.

title: Current Approaches to the Treatment of Hepatorenal Syndrome.
authorString: Rosales CA.
abstractText: Hepatorenal syndrome (HRS) is a life-threatening complication of advanced cirrhosis that requires early recognition, treatment of precipitating factors, and coordinated transplant assessment. This narrative review examines pharmacological treatment, fluid management, kidney replacement therapy (KRT), transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS), and liver transplantation in adults, with emphasis on HRS with acute kidney injury (AKI). Contemporary diagnostic criteria recognize that hepatorenal physiology can coexist with tubular injury or chronic kidney disease (CKD) and discourage a routine 48-hour albumin challenge. Clinical assessment should integrate perfusion, oxygenation, and congestion, with ultrasound used as an adjunct when available. Terlipressin with individualized albumin improves renal reversal in suitable patients, but a consistent overall survival benefit has not been established, and respiratory failure remains a major safety concern. Norepinephrine is an important alternative where appropriate monitoring is available; midodrine with octreotide has a limited fallback role. Albumin dosing should reflect serial volume assessment rather than a serum albumin target. Kidney replacement therapy supports patients with metabolic or volume complications, while evidence for routine shunt placement in acute HRS remains insufficient. Liver transplantation addresses the underlying disease, although kidney recovery is variable. Biomarkers may assist clinical phenotyping, but their use to guide treatment requires prospective validation. The review emphasizes timely diagnosis, individualized treatment, and distinguishing renal recovery from survival.

title: Scleredema Diabeticorum Mimicking Systemic Sclerosis in a 75-Year-Old Female: A Case Report.
authorString: Imran MW, Nawaz SS, Abbasi H, Khurshid F, Khattak W, Iqbal T.
abstractText: Scleredema diabeticorum is a rare sclerosing cutaneous disorder characterized by diffuse, nonpitting, woody skin induration, most commonly occurring in patients with long-standing diabetes mellitus. Its clinical resemblance to systemic sclerosis (SSc) may result in diagnostic confusion, particularly in atypical presentations. We report a 75-year-old woman with a 20-year history of insulin-dependent Type 2 diabetes mellitus who developed progressive, generalized skin thickening. The disease initially involved the lower extremities and subsequently progressed proximally to the trunk, upper limbs, and face, with prominent facial and periorbital involvement and sparing of the hands and feet. She was initially suspected to have SSc because of diffuse skin induration and positive antinuclear antibodies and was treated with corticosteroids. However, the absence of characteristic distal scleroderma features, negative SSc-specific antibody testing, and histopathological findings of marked dermal thickening with broad collagen bundles and mucin deposition supported a diagnosis of scleredema diabeticorum. Management was complicated by diabetic nephropathy and concurrent cardiac disease, requiring individualized immunomodulatory therapy, close monitoring, and optimization of glycemic control. UVA1 phototherapy was attempted but discontinued because of immediate clinical intolerance. The patient subsequently received systemic immunomodulatory treatment with clinical improvement during follow-up. This case highlights the importance of distinguishing scleredema diabeticorum from SSc, particularly when atypical clinical features and positive nonspecific autoantibodies may lead to diagnostic uncertainty. Careful clinical assessment, appropriate serological evaluation, and histopathology are essential for accurate diagnosis and management.

title: Association between TyG‑BMI and repeat percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) risk: exploratory stratification by glucose metabolism status.
authorString: Fei W, Yang F, Zhu Y, Le Y, Wang S, Sun D, Zhang X.
abstractText: Most patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) are diagnosed with coronary heart disease (CHD). The triglyceride glucose‑body mass index (TyG‑BMI) has been reported to be associated with CHD. This study aimed to investigate the association between TyG‑BMI and the risk of repeat PCI among post‑PCI patients, with additional exploratory stratification analyses according to glucose‑metabolism status. Data for this study were derived from resident health‑record follow‑up records of Yipeng Community Health Service Center, covering January 2015 to January 2025. Logistic regression models and restricted cubic spline (RCS) were used to evaluate the association between TyG‑BMI and the risk of repeat PCI among post‑PCI patients, with exploratory stratification by glucose‑metabolism status. Logistic regression and restricted cubic spline analyses showed no significant linear or nonlinear association between TyG‑BMI and repeat PCI (OR=0.999,95%CI:0.994 ~ 1.003, P = 0.534; nonlinear χ2 = 0.91, df = 3, P = 0.8223). Stratified analyses by glucose metabolism status also revealed no significant correlation in any stratum(P > 0.05). No independent association between TyG‑BMI and repeat PCI was identified in post‑PCI patients, even within different glucose‑metabolism strata. Relevant findings require further verification in larger prospective cohorts.

title: Fabrication of guggulsterone-E-integrated chitosan-zinc nanohybrids: surface chemical insights, biointerface interactions and multi-target antidiabetic mechanisms.
authorString: Boomija RV, Kamaraj C, Karthick Rajan D, Thirunavukkarasu S, Al-Ghanim KA.
abstractText: The research focuses on evaluating the potential anti-diabetic efficacy of encapsulating guggulsterone-E extract within chitosan-ZnO NPs (Gu@ChZn NPs) through a sustainable production method. UV-vis, FT-IR, FE-SEM, HR-TEM, EDX, XPS, and XRD characterizations were used to identify the physicochemical properties of the Gu@ChZn NPs. The UV-visible absorption peak was noted at 320 nm, and morphological analysis revealed that the particles were mainly spherical with uneven surface characteristics and sizes of 5-45 nm. Based on the biological evaluation, it was found that compared with guggulsterone-E alone, Gu@ChZn NPs had a greater inhibitory effect on selected enzymes such as lipase, α-glucosidase, and α-amylase. Critical genes related to diabetes, including KCNJ11, TCF7L2, IRS-1, HNF1A, HXK4, and ABCC8, were predicted to interact with guggulsterone-E via network pharmacology. Molecular docking analysis revealed substantial binding affinities, with ABCC8 exhibiting the most significant interaction at -9.07 kcal mol-1. The Gu@ChZn NPs exhibit potential as a promising bio-functional nanocomposite with enhanced enzyme inhibitory properties relevant to diabetes-associated metabolic regulation.

title: Spectrum of <i>FGFR2</i> Mutations and Plausible Phenotypic Modifiers Contributing to the Etiology of Syndromic Craniosynostosis in Sub-Saharan Africans.
authorString: Gowans LJJ, Asante MD, Sabbah DK, Mensah GO, Tsri B, Asamoah CO, Dordor JB, Obiri-Yeboah S, Busch T, Butali A, Donkor P, Cunningham ML.
abstractText: Craniosynostosis, the premature fusion of cranial sutures resulting from disrupted molecular and cellular mechanisms of suture patency, ranks as the second most common craniofacial birth defect. It manifests as syndromic (15%-30%) or nonsyndromic (70%-85%) forms and has multifactorial etiology. This cross-sectional, observational, family-based study is aimed at elucidating the genetic basis of syndromic craniosynostosis in a Ghanaian cohort presenting with characteristic phenotypes of FGFR2-related syndromes. Eight case-parent trios with syndromic craniosynostosis were recruited, and saliva/buccal swab samples were collected for DNA extraction. Whole exome sequencing (WES) of DNA samples was performed on the Illumina HiSeq platform at 100x read depth in a paired-end configuration. Quality control, read alignment, and variant calling followed the Sentieon V202112.01 workflow, with variant annotation utilizing Ensembl VEP V104. Variants were filtered for minor allele frequency < 0.01 across databases, and pathogenicity was evaluated using 11 dbNSFP-embedded tools and SpliceAI. ClinVar and LOVD were used to verify the pathogenicity of variants. Gene expression, enrichment and interaction analyses, and associated phenotype ascertainment utilized various databases such as DECIPHER and OMIM. Five probands harbored de novo pathogenic variants in FGFR2 (p.Asp336Gly, p.Cys342Ser, p.Pro253Arg, p.Gly272del, and p.Ser252Trp). However, lack of paternal samples limited the determination of the de novo status of two variants (p.Ser252Trp and p.Cys342Gly) in three probands. These variants affected multiple cranial suture types, including coronal, sagittal, metopic, and lambdoid, and were associated with the clinical diagnoses of Apert and Crouzon syndromes. Additional likely pathogenic variants in other genes that may plausibly contribute to phenotypic variability were also observed. In silico functional analysis buttressed the role of FGFR2 and plausible variants contributing to phenotypic variability. Thus, FGFR2 variants contribute to syndromic craniosynostosis among Ghanaians, with additional genetic variants plausibly influencing phenotypic variability among probands. This study may impact genetic counseling (prenatal testing and recurrence risk) and other clinical management of craniosynostosis.

title: Serum FT3/FT4 ratio may indicate the degree of T3 compensation in congenital hypothyroidism.
authorString: Yamauchi T, Keidai A, Tomobe Y, Tomotaki S, Iwanaga K, Takita J, Kawai M.
abstractText:
Background

Clinical guidelines for hypothyroidism recommend measuring serum thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) and free thyroxine (FT4) levels as diagnostic and treatment efficacy indicators. However, they do not recommend measuring serum free triiodothyronine (FT3) levels because serum FT3 levels often remain within the normal range. However, serum TSH and FT4 levels alone make diagnosis and treatment decision-making difficult in conditions such as central hypothyroidism, suggesting the need for an additional indicator distinct from serum TSH levels. We investigated whether the serum FT3/FT4 ratio could be an indicator of congenital hypothyroidism (CH) severity, instead of serum TSH level.

Methods

Thirty-seven newborns were diagnosed with CH (severe group (n = 13): serum TSH ≥ 30 mIU/L; moderate group (n = 24): serum TSH ≥ 5 to < 30 mIU/L). All infants in the severe group received thyroid hormone (TH) replacement therapy vs 13 infants in the moderate group (moderate group with CH). Serum TSH, FT4, FT3, and FT3/FT4 ratios were compared between each group and the two control groups of different ages at diagnosis and 2 months after treatment.

Results

The serum FT3/FT4 ratio was elevated before treatment compared with the control group, reflecting CH severity. Two months after TH replacement, the serum FT3/FT4 ratio decreased significantly: severe group: at diagnosis, 0.48 vs 2 months, 0.27, p =<0.0001; moderate group with TH: 0.38 vs 2 months, 0.26, p < 0.0001. No change was observed in infants without TH replacement.

Discussion

A high serum FT3/FT4 ratio in CH could reflect the degree of systemic T3 compensation and is an indicator of CH severity. This ratio may also be applicable in conditions in which serum TSH levels are not useful for diagnosis or when assessing treatment outcomes.

Conclusion

A high serum FT3/FT4 ratio may be an indicator of hypothyroidism severity.

title: sST2 for Predicting Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events in STEMI Patients: A Prospective Cohort Study.
authorString: Wang J, Du W, He X, Cheng J, Liu Z.
abstractText:
Background

Soluble suppression of tumorigenicity 2 (sST2) has emerged as a promising prognostic biomarker for cardiovascular conditions. Nevertheless, the prognostic value of sST2 following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) has been insufficiently studied. This study aimed to explore the association between sST2 levels and the incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in STEMI patients post-PCI.

Methods

This prospective, single-center study enrolled 289 STEMI patients, who were randomly divided into training (n = 202) and validation (n = 87) cohorts at a 7:3 ratio. The primary endpoint was the occurrence of MACE within 6 months post-STEMI. The relationships between sST2 concentrations and MACE were analyzed using Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, Cox proportional hazards regression models, and restricted cubic spline (RCS) plots. The predictive accuracy of sST2, NT-proBNP, and their combined model was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, concordance indices (C-index), calibration plots, decision curve analysis (DCA), and net reclassification improvement (NRI). Subgroup analyses were conducted by stratifying patients based on age, gender, body mass index (BMI), and culprit vessel characteristics.

Results

A total of 289 patients were included in the analysis. Kaplan-Meier survival curves in the training cohort demonstrated a higher cumulative incidence of MACE among patients with elevated sST2 levels. Multivariate Cox regression analysis confirmed sST2 as an independent predictor of MACE (HR = 1.012, 95% CI 1.006-1.018, p < 0.001). When compared to the traditional biomarker NT-proBNP, sST2 displayed a comparable discriminative capability, with each biomarker offering unique strengths regarding accuracy and clinical usefulness. In the validation cohort, sST2 similarly exhibited acceptable predictive performance for MACE. Adding sST2 to the NT-proBNP baseline model did not significantly improve the predictive performance for MACE in STEMI patients. Subgroup analyses did not reveal any significant interactions with sST2.

Conclusion

In this study, sST2 was independently associated with MACE within 6 months post-PCI in patients with STEMI and showed some discriminative ability when used alone. However, adding it to NT-proBNP did not significantly improve risk prediction, and its incremental prognostic value and clinical utility remain limited and uncertain.

title: Invisible exposure, visible harm: air pollution and the global burden of cardiovascular disease.
authorString: Thakur N, Biswas H, Das A, Thakur S, Ghosh R.

journal.title: Genes and environment : the official journal of the Japanese Environmental Mutagen Society

abstractText:
Background

Air pollution is a major modifiable environmental risk factor for cardiovascular disease (CVD). In the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2021 study, air pollution was the second-leading risk factor for death worldwide, accounting for an estimated 8.1 million deaths from all causes in 2021, and particulate matter (PM) pollution (ambient plus household) was associated with approximately 4.5 million cardiovascular deaths.

Main body

This narrative review, based on a structured search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus and Web of Science, summarizes evidence on the sources of the main pollutants (fine particulate matter [PM₂.₅], coarse particulate matter [PM₁₀], ultrafine particles [PM₀.₁/UFP], nitrogen dioxide [NO₂], sulfur dioxide [SO₂], ozone [O₃] and carbon monoxide [CO]); the global burden of pollution-attributable CVD; epidemiological evidence from major cohort and multi-city studies; biological mechanisms, distinguishing those supported by human data from those derived mainly from cell and animal models; the associations with specific cardiovascular phenotypes (ischemic heart disease, stroke, hypertension, heart failure, arrhythmia and vascular disease); susceptible populations; transcriptomic, proteomic, lipidomic, epigenetic and microRNA findings; and preventive strategies graded by strength of evidence. Observational studies consistently associate short- and long-term exposure to PM₂.₅ with cardiovascular events and mortality, and controlled-exposure, quasi-experimental and mechanistic studies support a causal interpretation for PM₂.₅. Evidence for individual gaseous pollutants is less consistent, and most multi-omics findings remain exploratory.

Conclusion

PM₂.₅ should be regarded as a cardiovascular risk factor in clinical and public-health practice. Key uncertainties include the shape of the exposure-response relationship at very low concentrations, the relative toxicity of particle components, and whether reducing individual exposure lowers hard cardiovascular outcomes. Priorities include prospective multi-omics studies with clinical endpoints in low- and middle-income countries, causal-inference designs, and trials testing exposure-reduction and targeted therapeutic strategies in highly exposed populations.

title: En Bloc Sutureless Patch Repair of the Inferior Vena Cava and Right Hepatic Vein in a Patient with Invasive Renal Cell Carcinoma: A Case Report.
authorString: Amakura K, Yajima S, Yoshioka D, Kawashima A, Hasegawa S, Kawamura T, Kawamura A, Misumi Y, Miyagawa S.
abstractText:
Introduction

In patients with invasive renal cell carcinoma, extensive involvement of the inferior vena cava (IVC) and right hepatic vein presents a unique surgical challenge. We report a case of a man with invasive renal cell carcinoma of the left kidney who developed massive hemorrhage and hypovolemic shock due to right hepatic vein laceration during surgery, which necessitated an emergency repair procedure. This procedure was effective and might be useful in other patients with invasive renal cell carcinoma with IVC and hepatic vein involvement.

Case presentation

A 72-year-old man presented with severe acute left-sided epigastric pain. Plain abdominal CT and MRI revealed an enlarged left kidney with a low-density mass extending from the left renal vein to the IVC. Renal biopsy revealed renal cell carcinoma of the left kidney. The patient was treated with neoadjuvant therapy and underwent surgery. A median laparotomy was performed to expose and dissect the IVC. During the Kocher maneuver to mobilize the liver, the right hepatic vein was lacerated because the venous wall had been weakened by tumor thrombus. This led to massive hemorrhage and hypovolemic shock, necessitating an emergency repair procedure. The IVC defect and transected right hepatic vein were reconstructed en bloc using an autologous pericardial patch. The upper half of the patch was sutured directly to the liver parenchyma (not to the right hepatic vein), whereas the lower half was attached to the residual IVC wall. After vascular reconstruction, the left kidney and associated renal veins were excised. Postoperative contrast-enhanced abdominal CT revealed patent blood flow from the right hepatic vein through the patch to the IVC. Pre-existing small pulmonary nodules subsequently increased in size and were considered likely metastatic lesions. The patient died of respiratory failure on POD 120.

Conclusions

Sutureless patch repair offers an alternative to conventional grafting methods and may be useful in cases of invasive carcinoma that require combined reconstruction of the hepatic veins and IVC.

title: Assessment of Lipoprotein(a) in Patients with Cancer: Relevance for Cardio-Oncology Practice.
authorString: Wójtowicz M, Bortnowski W, Grzenkowicz A, Lewicka-Potocka Z, Smolarek D, Sławiński G, Daniłowicz-Szymanowicz L, Lewicka E.
abstractText: Cardiovascular disease is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in patients with cancer and in cancer survivors. Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is a largely genetically determined causal risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and calcific aortic valve disease, acting through proatherogenic, proinflammatory, and potentially prothrombotic pathways. These mechanisms may be relevant in cancer, where inflammation, hypercoagulability, metabolic disturbances, and treatment-related cardiovascular toxicity increase cardiovascular risk. Observational studies have also linked circulating Lp(a) to tumor characteristics, disease stage, or prognosis in several malignancies. However, these findings are heterogeneous, often derived from small, retrospective, or single-center cohorts, and do not establish a causal role for Lp(a) in cancer development or progression. Evidence relating Lp(a) specifically to cancer therapy-related cardiovascular toxicity remains limited, and a prospective biomarker cohort found no association between baseline Lp(a) and major adverse cardiovascular events. This review summarizes the biology and measurement of Lp(a), critically evaluates its reported oncological associations, and examines its relevance in cardio-oncology. Currently, Lp(a) should be interpreted primarily as part of comprehensive cardiovascular risk assessment rather than as a cancer-specific or cardiotoxicity biomarker. Prospective, treatment-specific studies are needed to determine whether Lp(a) improves risk prediction or represents an actionable therapeutic target in this population.

title: AI-driven opportunistic screening for carotid atheroma calcification on dental radiographs.
authorString: Chini CF, Correia IBMC, Ferreira MVDS, Dias BSS, Melo NS, Leite AF, Farias MCQ.
abstractText: To develop a labeled image dataset of suspected carotid artery calcifications (CACs) on dental panoramic radiographs (PRs) and to propose a deep learning-based framework for their automated detection and segmentation. A retrospective dataset comprising 19,205 PRs obtained from our institution (between 2015 and 2023) was analyzed. After manual labeling, 372 images showing CACs and 322 controls were included. A hybrid architecture combining FasTVit, AttentionNet, and DC-UNet was implemented for classification, detection, and segmentation. Model performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, the Dice coefficient, intersection over union (IoU), and area under the curve (AUC). The study evaluated two scenarios: one in which detection and segmentation were performed after classification, and another in which the classification was omitted. The classification model achieved an accuracy of 0.8780, a precision of 0.8779, a recall of 0.8795, and a specificity of, 0.8795. Incorporating the classification step improved precision from 0.48 to 0.93, accuracy from 0.79 to 0.97, and specificity from 0.75 to 0.98. The final framework achieved an area under the ROC curve of 0.96. The proposed hybrid artificial intelligence (AI) framework showed promising internal performance for the opportunistic detection and localization of radiographic findings suggestive of CACs on PRs. Within the limitations of this study, the proposed framework may serve as a complementary aid to dentists by flagging suspected CACs during routine interpretation of PRs and facilitating timely referral for confirmatory cardiovascular assessment.

title: Aortic valve calcification and one-year paravalvular leak after transcatheter aortic valve replacement: limited role of asymmetry.
authorString: Basera P, Mousavi RA, Enwere C, Soroa M, Argulian E, Alizadeh L, Ferrandez-Escarabajal M, Mannina C, Chopra L, Sharma SK, Kini AS, Lerakis S.
abstractText:
Objectives

Paravalvular leak (PVL) is a significant complication after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). Although total aortic valve calcification (AVC) burden and self-expandable valves are predictors of PVL, the impact of leaflet-specific AVC asymmetry remains uncertain. The authors evaluated the association between AVC asymmetry and mild or greater PVL at 1 year after TAVR and its interaction with valve type.

Methods

Patients undergoing TAVR between January 2022 and May 2025 with preprocedural noncontrast cardiac computed tomography and 1-year transthoracic echocardiography were included. Asymmetric AVC was defined as greater than 50% of total AVC on a single cusp.

Results

Among 530 patients (mean age, 79 ± 8 years; 45.5% female), 130 (24.5%) had mild or greater PVL at 1 year. Total AVC was higher in women (1747 vs 1125 AU; P less than .001) and men (2612 vs 2063 AU; P less than .001) with mild or greater PVL, with greater calcification across all cusps. AVC asymmetry was comparable between PVL and non-PVL groups (33.1% vs 41.4%; P = .093). Total AVC independently predicted PVL (adjusted odds ratio [OR], 1.036 per 100 AU; P < .001), whereas asymmetry did not (adjusted OR, 0.912; P = .681). No significant interaction occurred between valve type, AVC asymmetry, and PVL (P = .224).

Conclusions

Total AVC independently predicts mild or greater PVL at 1 year after TAVR, whereas leaflet-specific asymmetry and valve type provide no additional predictive value.

title: Pectoralis muscle features assessed by chest CT and their associations with clinical and functional outcomes in children and adolescents with cystic fibrosis: a cross-sectional study.
authorString: da Costa MS, Amor-Barbosa M, Sbruzzi M, Vendrusculo FM, Fischer DL, Carvalho FM, Andrade RGF, Pinto LA, Donadio MVF.
abstractText:
Objective

To evaluate the cross-sectional area and thickness of the pectoralis major muscle using chest CT and to investigate their associations with nutritional, respiratory, and functional parameters in children and adolescents with cystic fibrosis (CF).

Methods

This was a cross-sectional study including patients 6-18 years of age with a confirmed diagnosis of CF. Anthropometric data were collected, as were data related to lung function and muscle strength assessed by dynamometry, as well as pectoralis muscle area and thickness measured by chest CT. Aerobic fitness was assessed with cardiopulmonary exercise testing.

Results

The mean age of the participants was 11.2 ± 3.3 years, and the mean BMI was 17.1 ± 2.8 kg/m2. Oxygen pulse was found to correlate significantly with pectoralis muscle area (r = 0.51; p = 0.02), FEV1 (r = -0.58; p = 0.01), and BMI z-score (r = 0.60; p < 0.01). Pectoralis muscle area showed a moderate correlation with muscle strength (r = 0.42; p = 0.03), whereas muscle thickness showed only a weak association with FEV1.

Conclusions

Our findings suggest that the cross-sectional area of the pectoralis muscle is a more relevant indicator of muscle function than is thickness. Integrating muscle morphology, strength, and aerobic fitness may contribute to a more comprehensive clinical assessment in patients with cystic fibrosis.

title: Premature Senescence and Cardiovascular Disease Following Cancer Treatments: Mitochondria-Mediated Mechanistic Insights.
authorString: Pandey S.
abstractText: The remarkable enhancement in cancer survival attained over recent decades has shifted attention toward the long-term cardiovascular effects of anticancer therapies. Beyond overt cardiotoxicity, accumulating evidence indicates that many conventional chemotherapeutics, including radiotherapy, targeted agents, and emerging immunotherapies, accelerate biological aging of the cardiovascular system through the induction of premature cellular senescence. Senescent endothelial cells, cardiomyocytes, vascular smooth muscle cells, cardiac fibroblasts, and resident immune cells exhibit persistent growth arrest accompanied by metabolic reprogramming, chronic inflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and acquisition of a senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP), collectively contributing to adverse cardiac remodeling, vascular dysfunction, myocardial fibrosis, and accelerated atherosclerosis. Among the interconnected mechanisms driving therapy-induced senescence, mitochondria have emerged as central regulators integrating oxidative stress, DNA damage responses, bioenergetic alterations, impaired mitophagy, mitochondrial dynamics, calcium dysregulation, and innate immune activation. Through the production of reactive oxygen species (ROS), chronic inflammatory signaling, the release of mitochondrial DNA, and the activation of inflammasomes, dysfunctional mitochondria actively amplify senescence rather than acting only as organelles that produce energy. This creates self-sustaining feed-forward loops that promote cardiovascular aging long after cancer treatment is completed. This review critically examines the molecular mechanisms linking anticancer therapies to premature cardiovascular senescence with particular emphasis on mitochondria-centered signaling networks. I address therapy-specific mitochondrial alterations induced by HER2-targeted treatments, immune checkpoint inhibitors, ionizing radiation, platinum-based drugs, anthracyclines, and more recent anticancer modalities, emphasizing interconnected pathways despite disparate fundamental mechanisms of action. Emerging biomarkers of mitochondrial dysfunction and senescence, together with therapeutic prospects involving senolytics, senomorphics, mitochondria-targeted antioxidants, metabolic modulators, and interventions reestablishing mitochondrial quality control, are also evaluated. Finally, I identify unresolved questions limiting clinical translation and propose future research directions aimed at preserving cardiovascular health in the rapidly expanding population of cancer survivors.

title: Excess Cardiovascular Burden Among Young Patients with Cancer: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Kiyani M, Heins RJ, Yazji JH, Almimar H, Lopes GL.
abstractText: Background: Young patients with cancer may develop cardiovascular complications decades earlier than the general population, yet their long-term cardiovascular risk remains incompletely defined. Most prior evidence derives from older adults or therapy-specific analyses, leaving adolescents and young adults understudied as a distinct population. Methods: We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of observational cohort, registry-based, and population-based studies evaluating cardiovascular outcomes or mortality among young patients with cancer (adolescents and young adults [15-39 years], <45 years, <50 years, or clearly defined young age subgroups) compared with age-matched comparators. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception through 26 February 2026. Two reviewers independently screened studies and assessed risk of bias using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Evidence certainty was evaluated with GRADE. Random-effects models were used for pooled analyses. Results: Fifty-eight studies were included. Young patients with cancer had significantly increased risks of heart failure (HR, 4.08; 95% CI, 2.20-7.57), pulmonary embolism (HR, 4.63; 95% CI, 3.03-7.06), venous thrombosis (HR, 4.06; 95% CI, 2.51-6.58), and cardiomyopathy (HR, 3.52; 95% CI, 2.21-5.63). Cardiovascular mortality was also elevated (SMR, 4.30; 95% CI, 3.06-6.05), although a trim-and-fill analysis resulted in an adjusted pooled SMR of 1.79 (95% CI, 1.05-3.05, p = 0.0313). Overall cardiovascular disease risk was approximately 2-fold higher, with additional increases in stroke, arrhythmia, and hypertension. Heterogeneity was high for several key outcomes (I2, overall cardiovascular disease HR 96.0%; cardiovascular mortality SMR 99.1%; heart failure HR 92.5%; venous thrombosis HR 94.1%), and evidence certainty was low for most. Conclusions: Young patients with cancer face substantially increased risks of cardiovascular disease, particularly heart failure, cardiomyopathy, and thrombotic complications. Prospective studies are needed to determine whether earlier cardiovascular surveillance improves outcomes.

title: Analysis of the Use of shRNA in Atherosclerosis Therapy: Current Status.
authorString: Blagov AV, Maksaeva AO, Kovyanova TI.
abstractText: Atherosclerosis remains the principal pathological substrate of myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke and peripheral artery disease, and its progression is driven by an interlocking set of processes, including hepatic and vascular lipid metabolism, chronic vascular inflammation, macrophage foam cell formation and vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) proliferation, none of which is fully controlled by currently approved pharmacotherapy. Short hairpin RNA (shRNA) technology, in which a DNA template encoding a stem-loop transcript is delivered to a cell and processed intracellularly into small interfering RNAs (siRNAs) that trigger sequence-specific mRNA degradation, offers a route to durable, vector-encoded gene silencing that is mechanistically distinct from transiently acting synthetic siRNA or antisense oligonucleotides and that, although non-permanent at the level of the target gene, is not readily reversible at the level of the vector, which cannot easily be withdrawn once administered. This review analyzes the current status of shRNA-based strategies for atherosclerosis therapy. We summarize the molecular mechanism and vector design principles of shRNA-mediated RNA interference (RNAi); critically examine preclinical studies in which shRNA delivered by lentiviral or adeno-associated viral (AAV) vectors has been used to silence hepatic lipid-metabolism genes (PCSK9, ApoB,), the endothelial gene ANGPTL2, inflammasome and inflammatory mediators (NLRP3, TACE/ADAM17), and genes driving VSMC proliferation in restenosis models (connexin 43); we explicitly distinguish this direct shRNA evidence from complementary target-validation studies that use antisense oligonucleotides (e.g., ANGPTL4), synthetic siRNA, genetic knockout, or antimiR approaches (e.g., lncRNA AK136714, CD36, miR-33, P2X7R); and discuss the principal delivery vectors, their tissue tropism, and the toxicity arising from saturation of the endogenous microRNA-processing machinery. We further place shRNA in the context of competing and complementary RNA-based and gene-editing modalities, including clinically approved synthetic siRNA drugs (inclisiran, patisiran) and CRISPR-based gene editing of PCSK9 and ANGPTL3, both of which have now yielded human phase 1 data, to clarify why, despite two decades of robust preclinical proof-of-concept, no shRNA construct has yet reached clinical use in atherosclerosis; we further compare this with the clinical trajectory of vector-encoded shRNA in other indications, in which anti-CCR5 and anti-HCV constructs have already been administered to patients in phase 1/2 trials, in order to establish that the limiting factor is not the hairpin itself but the risk-benefit case obtainable in a chronic, largely asymptomatic disease for which withdrawable and outcome-validated therapies already exist. We conclude that shRNA remains a mechanistically attractive but clinically immature modality whose translation will depend on vector engineering that limits off-target saturation of the RNAi pathway and achieves durable, cell type-restricted expression in the liver, endothelium, macrophages or vascular wall, and, equally, on the identification of an atherosclerosis indication-most plausibly a small, high-residual-risk or locally treatable population-in which durability outweighs the vector-level irreversibility, immunogenicity and manufacturing burden of a viral vector.

title: Nanotechnology in Cardiovascular Medicine: Advances in Diagnostics, Targeted Therapy, and Translational Challenges.
authorString: Li S, Li Q, Liu X.
abstractText: Despite significant progress in prevention, imaging, drugs, and interventions, cardiovascular diseases continue to be one of the most frequent causes of death and disability in the world. This narrative review highlights recent developments in the field of cardiovascular diagnostics and therapy through the use of nanotechnology, covering topics such as nano-based biosensors, molecular imaging probes, targeted drug/nucleic acid delivery, and nanoengineering in cardiovascular device interfaces. For this review, literature was chosen from databases PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar, and special attention was paid to peer-reviewed sources. The review considers the current state of in vitro, animal, human-tested, and clinically applied technologies, analyzing their quantitative performance, safety, targeting efficiency, and translatability.
