Special attention is given to specific problems of nanomedicine in cardiovascular diseases, including blood contact, shear stress, thrombogenesis, protein corona formation, biodistribution, large-scale manufacturing, and regulation. Despite the existence of multiple nanotechnology-based platforms that show good performance both in diagnostics and therapy in pre-clinical models, clinical verification remains rare. The key translational challenge consists in proving reproducibility of performance, safety, and scalable manufacturing.

title: Multi-Omics Mendelian Randomization Identifies DDX17 as a Potential Mediator Linking Gut Microbiota-Immune-Metabolism Axis to Alzheimer's Disease.
authorString: Xiao Z, Qin Y, Dong M, Wei S, Ma Q, Luo C, Li Y, Chen F, Wu G, Wei P, Hu R, Huang Z, Liu C.
abstractText:
Introduction

The gut microbiota-immune-metabolism axis has been implicated in Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathogenesis; however, the key host molecular targets linking peripheral dysregulation to central neurodegeneration remain elusive.

Methods

In this study, we systematically integrated large-scale GWAS data covering 1,903 gut microbiota taxa, 14,696 immune cell features, and 34,843 metabolite features with AD GWAS summary statistics, using two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) to identify causal genes. These genes were intersected with differentially expressed genes from three GEO datasets, followed by protein-protein interaction network construction using four Cytoscape algorithms (MCC, EPC, DMNC, Degree) and feature selection via three machine learning methods (Support Vector Machine, Random Forest, LASSO). Single-cell transcriptomics (GSE188545) localized key gene expression, Support Vector Machine virtual knockout (scTenifoldKnk) analyzed downstream regulatory networks, with in vitro validation performed in okadaic acid-treated SH-SY5Y cells using RT-qPCR and Western blotting.

Results

MR analysis revealed multiple causal associations among microbial taxa, immune phenotypes, metabolites, and AD. Integration of MR causal genes with DEGs, PPI network analysis, and machine learning refinement prioritized six key genes: BYSL, DDX17, HSPA6, RRN3, C4B, and NCKAP1L. Among them, only DDX17 showed robust expression in AD-associated neuronal populations in single-cell transcriptomics, whereas the other five genes showed low expression and may act through non-cell-autonomous mechanisms. Virtual knockout predicted that the PI3K/AKT pathway was the most significantly enriched downstream of DDX17 perturbation. In vitro, DDX17 was significantly upregulated in an OA-induced AD cell model, and siRNA-mediated knockdown partially reversed tau hyperphosphorylation (total P-tau and P-tau Thr217), while restoring AKT phosphorylation at Thr308 and Ser473.

Conclusion

These findings suggest that DDX17 is a potential downstream host candidate linking peripheral dysregulation to tau pathology in AD, partially through PI3K/AKT pathway modulation. However, these results are primarily hypothesis-generating, and direct mechanistic and in vivo validation remain essential.

title: Identification of m6A-Associated mRNAs, lncRNAs, and m6A Regulators in Endometriosis.
authorString: Ren C, He Y, Qu Y, Zhao Y, Zhang G.
abstractText:
Background

Endometriosis (EMs), which causes significant pain and infertility, continues to affect women of reproductive age, yet its molecular mechanisms remain inadequately defined. N6-methyladenosine (m6A) modification is the most prevalent post-transcriptional modification in mammalian mRNA, and recent studies have increasingly focused on elucidating the relationship between m6A and EMs, to provide theoretical insights for clinical prevention and treatment.

Methods

Using human m6A-mRNA and lncRNA epigenomic microarray techniques, functional and pathway enrichment analysis, protein-protein interaction network (PPI), and R packages, we conducted exploratory analyses to identify mRNAs and lncRNAs with differential methylation, as well as important m6A regulators associated with EMs. These findings were verified using external databases, along with RNA extraction and quantitative real-time PCR (qPCR), immunohistochemistry, and immunofluorescence techniques.

Results

Specifically, our analysis revealed 1631 hyper-upregulated, 219 hypo-upregulated, and 6483 hypo-downregulated differentially methylated and expressed genes (DMEGs). Additionally, we identified 8 candidate hub genes-RHOA, KCNA2, BDNF, CACNA1C, FGFR1, IL18, KCNIP2, and RPL17-and characterized their enriched pathways. Furthermore, we observed 6 significantly hypermethylated and 14 significantly hypomethylated lncRNAs in EMs. Our screening identified two key m6A regulators, WTAP and RBM15, which may represent candidate molecules worthy of further investigation in the context of EMs.

Conclusion

This exploratory screening analysis delineates aberrant expression signatures of m6A regulators and their associated mRNAs and lncRNAs in endometriosis tissues, yielding preliminary molecular profiles that merely reflect correlations rather than causal or definite functional relationships.

title: Chrysin Alleviates Diabetic Angiopathies via Targeting KDR and Downregulating the KANK4/Talin-1/PI3K/AKT Pathway.
authorString: Xu P, Zheng L, Wei X, Li X, Xi D, Guo Y, Wang Y, Ma K.
abstractText:
Objective

Diabetic vasculopathy is important for the development of cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events. Chrysin is a bioactive flavonoid monomer derived from Ziziphora bungeana Juz. Nevertheless, the impact of chrysin on diabetic angiopathies and its potential mechanisms remain to be elucidated.

Methods

Bioinformatics analysis, Western blot, qRT-PCR, EdU, molecular docking, Transwell, wound scratch assay, confocal laser scanning, Cellular Thermal Shift Assay (CETSA), Co-Immunoprecipitation (Co-IP), Lentiviral shRNA knockdown, Immunohistochemistry, Masson's trichrome staining, and type 1 diabetes model in C57BL/6 mice were used in this study.

Results

Chrysin reduced blood glucose levels, improved aortic media thickness and vascular fibrosis in DM mice, significantly inhibited the proliferation and migration of VSMCs, and promoted the transition of VSMCs from a synthetic phenotype to a contractile phenotype. In addition, chrysin improved HG-induced gap junction communication dysfunction in VSMCs by increasing the expression of Cx43, Occludin and ZO-1. Transcriptome sequencing combined with GEO database analysis identified KANK4 as a key regulatory gene in diabetic vasculopathy. Network pharmacology, molecular docking, and CETSA revealed that chrysin can target KDR. Co-immunoprecipitation assays suggested a potential interaction between KDR and KANK4, and confocal laser scanning microscopy revealed that KANK4 and Talin-1 were colocalized. Mechanistically, chrysin targets KDR to inhibit the KANK4-mediated activity of the Talin-1/PI3K/AKT pathway to improve diabetic vasculopathy.

Conclusion

Chrysin targets KDR, inhibits KANK4 expression, downregulates the Talin-1/PI3K/AKT pathway, improves gap junction communication impairment, switches the phenotype from synthetic to contractile, and inhibits proliferation and migration, thereby ameliorating high glucose-induced vascular lesions in diabetic mice.

title: Effect of furosemide deresuscitation on fluid distribution and bioelectrical impedance analysis parameters in septic patients: a secondary analysis of a double-blind, randomized controlled trial.
authorString: Aditianingsih D, Hidayat J, Djaja AS, Rahardja TS.

journal.title: Journal of critical care medicine (Universitatea de Medicina si Farmacie din Targu-Mures)

abstractText:
Introduction

Sepsis is a leading cause of mortality globally, accounting for 11 million deaths annually, particularly in ICU patients. Fluid therapy is critical in sepsis management, yet aggressive resuscitation often leads to fluid overload, worsening outcomes. Bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA) is a noninvasive method for monitoring body fluid distribution, providing insights into fluid imbalances associated with sepsis mortality.

Aim

This study evaluates the impact of furosemide-induced fluid deresuscitation on fluid distribution and clinical outcomes in patients with sepsis.

Methods

A secondary analysis of a double-blind, randomized controlled trial was conducted in forty sepsis patients with cumulative fluid balance >1,500 mL and urine output <0.8 mL/kg/hour. Patients were randomised to the intervention (furosemide infusion) and control (placebo) groups. BIA was used to assess total body water (TBW), extra-cellular water (ECW), intracellular water (ICW), and related parameters at baseline and after 48 hours. Outcomes included changes in fluid distribution, ICU length of stay, RRT use, and 28-day mortality.

Results

At baseline, no significant differences were observed in demographic or clinical characteristics between the groups. All BIA parameters showed no significant differences, except for the ECW/ICW ratio and ICW levels. After 48 hours, the intervention group exhibited a significant reduction in ECW/ICW ratio (P = 0.005) and ICW levels (P = 0.004), while the control group showed increases in ICW and TBW. Mortality rates were higher in the control group (36.8% vs 25.0%), though not statistically significant (P = 0.423). Severe hypoalbuminemia was more frequent in the control group, potentially contributing to fluid imbalance.

Conclusions

While furosemide-induced deresuscitation may influence fluid redistribution, its effect on clinical outcomes remains inconclusive.

title: Mixed venous oxygen saturation identifies high-risk physiology in advanced cardiogenic shock.
authorString: Pham TX, Nguyen MD, Van Dang H, Nguyen DT, Nguyen T, Ha HT, Van Nguyen C, Nguyen QH, Nguyen TA.

journal.title: Journal of critical care medicine (Universitatea de Medicina si Farmacie din Targu-Mures)

abstractText:
Background

Early identification and risk stratification in cardiogenic shock remain clinically important. Mixed venous oxygen saturation (SvO2) may provide additional information for identifying patients at higher risk within a given SCAI stage.

Objectives

To evaluate the role of mixed venous oxygen saturation (SvO2) and hemodynamic parameters in combination with Society for Cardiovascular Angiography and Interventions (SCAI) staging, stratifying 30-day mortality risk in patients with cardiogenic shock due to acute myocardial infarction.

Methods

A retrospective analysis of baseline data was conducted in 84 patients with cardiogenic shock due to acute myocardial infarction, selected from a larger study registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT07062744). Hemodynamic parameters and indices of oxygen delivery-consumption were collected immediately after insertion of the pulmonary artery catheter (T0). The Society for Cardiovascular Angiography and Interventions (SCAI) stage was determined at the same time point. Associations between baseline hemodynamic variables and 30-day mortality were evaluated using group comparison tests, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, Kaplan-Meier survival analysis with log-rank testing, and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression. The proportional hazards assumption was assessed by including time-dependent interaction terms between each covariate and follow-up time. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality within 30 days, prespecified in the registered protocol.

Results

Thirty-day mortality in the overall study population was 32.1% (27/84). Within the same SCAI stage, SvO2 further stratified patients into groups with different observed mortality risks. Mortality risk classification using a threshold of 53% of SvO2. Lower SvO2 was associated with reduced 30-day survival and remained associated with mortality risk after adjustment in Cox regression analysis.

Conclusions

Mixed venous oxygen saturation (SvO2) with a threshold of 53% was associated with differences in 30-day mortality risk among patients with cardiogenic shock within the same SCAI stage. It may provide additional risk stratification during early invasive hemodynamic assessment.

title: Neonatal outcome of dicephalus parapagus twins with a shared heart: A case report and review of prognostic factors.
authorString: Alsehli H, Alsaif S.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Int J Cardiol Congenit Heart Dis
journal.title: International journal of cardiology. Congenital heart disease
journal.isoabbreviation: Int J Cardiol Congenit Heart Dis

abstractText: Conjoined twins are a rare type of monoamniotic twins, occurring in 1.47 per 100,000 births worldwide. Prognosis depends on the extent of organ sharing, particularly the heart. We report a case of parapagus dicephalus tribrachius dipus conjoined twins diagnosed at 19 weeks in a 24-year-old Saudi woman. Ultrasound showed twins with two heads, four upper limbs, two lower limbs, and sharing major organs. Fetal echocardiography showed one structurally normal heart and another small heart with a single outflow tract. A cesarean section was performed at 33 weeks of gestation, delivering cyanosed twins who died 53 minutes after birth. Parapagus dicephalus twins are among the most common forms of conjoined twins and carry a high risk of perinatal mortality, especially when a single functional heart is shared. Early prenatal diagnosis, multidisciplinary counseling, and discussion of management options, including termination when appropriate, are crucial for guiding parental decisions and optimizing care.

title: Hypoplastic left heart syndrome: anatomical spectrum, clinical management, and brain defects.
authorString: Bell-Cheddar Y, Devine W, Diaz-Castrillon CE, Tang R, Castro-Medina M, Solt SA, Christopher A, Morales R, Xu X, Lo CW, Lin JI.
abstractText: Hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HLHS) is a complex congenital heart disease (CHD) involving hypoplasia of the left ventricle (LV) and the aorta (Ao), along with aortic and mitral valve stenosis/atresia with or without coarctation. It is a physiologically single-ventricle lesion, previously uniformly fatal, but now survivable with a 3-stage surgical palliation ending with the Fontan circulation, a circulation for only one working ventricle. In the classical definition of HLHS, the ventricular septum is intact; however, HLHS variants have been described with similar single-ventricle pathophysiology in which the hypoplastic LV is not hemodynamically coupled to the aortic outflow. Evidence for a genetic etiology for HLHS is indicated by its high recurrence risk, the association with various chromosomal abnormalities, and the demonstration of mutations in mice causing HLHS. Despite surgical advances allowing survival of patients with HLHS, there is still high morbidity and mortality after their first-stage palliation. The causes of such high morbidity and mortality are not well understood, but most deaths are likely related to cardiovascular/hemodynamic causes. Studies in the animal models of HLHS show that this cardiac lesion arises early in embryogenesis, decreases left-sided inflow, and is associated with metabolic dysfunction, cell proliferation, and differentiation defects. Findings indicate HLHS is also associated with intrinsic cell deficits, deficits that may also contribute to the high risk of heart failure and adverse neurodevelopment. In this article, we update a previous review by describing the basic pathophysiology; pertinent pre- and postoperative management of HLHS and its anatomical variants; and novel insights from the HLHS mouse model on the causes of HLHS-associated heart failure and poor neurodevelopment, as well as potential therapeutic strategies.

title: Imaging findings and clinical outcomes in neonates with isolated subependymal echogenicity on cranial ultrasound: a retrospective cohort study.
authorString: Xiang Y, Chen J, Huang S, Shi H, Li X, Jiang J, Zhang X.
abstractText:
Objective

To describe clinical and imaging findings in neonates with isolated subependymal echogenicity on cranial ultrasound and examine associations with recorded mortality and cerebral palsy.

Methods

This retrospective single-center cohort included 317 neonates admitted between January 2015 and December 2018 with an initial ultrasound finding suspicious for isolated subependymal hemorrhage. Clinical records, available MRI findings, and follow-up information were reviewed. Cerebral palsy was ascertained from rehabilitation or neurology diagnostic records, supplemented by telephone follow-up in January 2026, independently of developmental test scores. The primary adjusted analysis compared death with all survivors using an exploratory six-item comorbidity count and clinical covariates; hospitalization duration was excluded, and laterality was coded as unilateral or bilateral.

Results

There were 52 deaths (16.4%), 9 survivors with recorded cerebral palsy (2.8%), and 256 survivors without recorded cerebral palsy (80.8%). MRI findings were compatible with hemorrhage in 61 of 90 examined infants (67.8%). In the complete-case mortality model (n = 316), each additional comorbidity was associated with greater odds of death (adjusted OR, 2.462; 95% CI, 1.787-3.391; p < 0.001). The other included covariates were not statistically significant. White matter abnormalities were recorded in nine infants, including eight of the nine infants with cerebral palsy and one without recorded cerebral palsy.

Conclusion

Systemic comorbidity burden was associated with mortality within this ultrasound-defined cohort. White matter abnormalities accompanied most recorded cerebral palsy cases, but this observation remains descriptive. Specialist diagnostic records and later telephone follow-up characterize persistent clinical diagnoses; they do not establish the independent effect of subependymal echogenicity or normal development across all domains in survivors without cerebral palsy.

title: The emerging discipline has emerged: cardio-oncology as a medical specialty.
authorString: Ghebre YT, Shyr DR, Fasinu PS.
abstractText: Remarkable advances in cancer therapeutics have transformed many malignancies into chronic, manageable diseases, creating an unprecedented population of long-term cancer survivors. However, these gains have been accompanied by a growing burden of cardiovascular disease resulting from both cancer therapies and shared biological mechanisms between cancer and cardiovascular disease. Cardio-oncology has emerged to address this challenge by integrating cardiovascular prevention, surveillance, diagnosis, and treatment throughout the range of cancer care. What began as a consultative niche focused largely on anthracycline-induced cardiomyopathy has rapidly evolved into a multidisciplinary specialty supported by international guidelines, dedicated clinical programs, structured surveillance strategies, specialized training initiatives, and expanding research networks. This perspective argues that cardio-oncology has crossed the threshold from an emerging field to an established medical discipline. We discuss the milestones that define its maturation, the challenges that remain, and the priorities required to ensure equitable implementation worldwide.

title: Development and evaluation of a transesophageal echocardiography-derived left atrial appendage structure-function coupling index across the atrial fibrillation disease continuum.
authorString: Zhu J, Ni C, Ruan Y, Jiang Y, Zhu L, Huang Y, Jiang Z, Liu X.
abstractText:
Background

Atrial fibrillation (AF) is a progressive disorder associated with atrial remodeling and thromboembolic risk. We developed a transesophageal echocardiography (TEE)-derived left atrial appendage (LAA) structure-function coupling index (LAA-SFCI), defined as LAA volumetric load relative to longitudinal deformation, and assessed its distribution along the AF disease continuum and its potential for risk re-stratification of patients without documented AF.

Methods

This single-center, prospective, cross-sectional study included 267 patients undergoing clinically indicated TEE, classified by the 2023 American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association/American College of Clinical Pharmacy/Heart Rhythm Society (ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS) framework as Stage 1 (n = 68), Stage 2 (n = 65), Stage 3a (n = 66), or Stage 3b (n = 68). Seven candidate LAA-SFCIs were calculated as the LAA volume index (LAA-VI) divided by a functional measure, and the principal index was selected by ordinal logistic regression using the Akaike information criterion. Discrimination was compared using the DeLong test and internally validated by bootstrapping, and patients without documented AF (Stages 1-2) were stratified by the exploratory cutoff.

Results

LAA-VI/LAA-GLS (LAA global longitudinal strain) provided the best model fit and rose across AF stages from 0.33 ± 0.11 to 0.86 ± 0.36 (mL/m2)/% (P < 0.001). In ordinal regression with the log-transformed index, each 1-SD increase remained associated with higher AF stage after adjustment for age, sex, body mass index, left ventricular ejection fraction, and left atrial volume index (odds ratio 11.04, 95% confidence interval 7.17-16.98). For Stage 1-2 versus Stage 3a-3b, its area under the curve (0.904; optimism-corrected 0.900) was significantly higher than those of LAA-VI (0.661) and LAA-GLS (0.824) (both DeLong P < 0.001). Among 133 patients without documented AF, 18 (13.5%) exceeded the cutoff of 0.460 (mL/m2)/%; these patients did not differ from the others in left atrial volume index or age.

Conclusion

In this cross-sectional study, LAA-VI/LAA-GLS characterized LAA structure-function uncoupling along the AF disease continuum. In patients without documented AF undergoing clinically indicated TEE, it identified a subgroup with an AF-like LAA phenotype not captured by conventional atrial size measures. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require external validation and longitudinal follow-up to determine their prognostic value.

title: Comprehensive Evaluation of Fontan-Associated Liver Disease: The Role of Magnetic Resonance Imaging.
authorString: Ortega-Zhindón DB, Nuñez-Bupunari RV, Calderón-Colmenero J, de la Mora-Cervantes R, Campuzano-González D, Pérez-Hernández N, Rodríguez-Pérez JM, Meléndez-Ramirez G, García-Montes JA, Cervantes-Salazar JL.
abstractText: Background: Fontan-associated liver disease (FALD) develops as a consequence of chronic systemic venous congestion, which alters hepatic hemodynamics and promotes sinusoidal congestion, inflammation, and fibrosis. Our objective was to evaluate liver changes using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) in patients with a Fontan circuit. Methods: We conducted a retrospective study including patients who underwent the Fontan procedure between January 2005 and December 2019 and were evaluated using T1, T2 and apparent diffusion coefficient mapping. Patients were classified into two groups: none-to-mild FALD (≤5 points) and moderate-to-severe FALD (≥6 points). FALD severity was characterized, and logistic regression analysis was performed to evaluate the association between the variables of interest and the outcome. The discriminative performance of quantitative MRI parameters was also assessed using ROC curves. Results: Thirty-nine patients were included, with a median age at surgery of 9.3 years (IQR 5.9-10.8); 61.5% (n = 24) were female. The most frequent diagnosis was tricuspid atresia (51.3%, n = 20), and the Fontan procedures were mainly performed using an extracardiac conduit (97.4%, n = 38). No factors were significantly associated with moderate-to-severe FALD. T1 mapping of segment I demonstrated the highest discriminative performance (AUC = 0.771; 95% CI: 0.500-1.000), with a cutoff value of >734 ms, yielding a sensitivity of 83.3% (95% CI: 43.65-99.15) and a specificity of 75% (95% CI: 57.89-86.75). Conclusions: After 10 years of follow-up, 15% had moderate-to-severe FALD. T1 mapping of segment I demonstrated the highest discriminative performance, with a sensitivity greater than 80% for identifying moderate-to-severe FALD.

title: p22phox-dependent redox pathways contribute to placental oxidative injury and adverse embryonic outcomes following transient gestational hypoxia-reoxygenation.
authorString: Hierdeis K, Bajuk-Bogdanović D, Mechakra A, Nakarada Đ, Ružičić A, Chalupský K, Papanakli L, Kerth S, Zhang Z, Steiger K, Petry A, Djordjević J, Mojović M, Görlach A, Kračun D.
abstractText: Placental development occurs in a physiologically low-oxygen environment, but disturbances in oxygen availability may disrupt placental function. Hypoxia followed by restoration of oxygen availability can promote oxidative injury and cellular stress responses; however, the contribution of p22phox-dependent NADPH oxidases to these processes during early placentation remains unclear. We thus investigated placental and embryonic responses to transient gestational hypoxia followed by return to normoxia (TGH) using wild-type mice and mice with global deletion of Cyba, encoding the NADPH oxidase subunit p22phox. In wild-type placentae, TGH increased oxidative DNA damage and lipid peroxidation and was associated with inflammatory signaling, DNA damage response (DDR), unfolded protein response/integrated stress response (UPR/ISR), and apoptosis-associated changes. TGH also altered trophoblast-associated phenotypes and was accompanied by increased embryonic lethality and impaired growth. These stress-associated placental responses were broadly attenuated in p22phox-deficient placentae, alongside improved embryonic outcomes. Furthermore, TGH increased HIF1α and HIF2α protein abundance and Vegf mRNA expression in wild-type placentae, whereas these responses were attenuated in p22phox-deficient placentae. Human preeclamptic placentae exhibited partially overlapping molecular signatures, including altered redox status, increases in NADPH oxidase component abundance, oxidative damage, and DDR-, UPR/ISR-, and apoptosis-associated markers. Raman spectroscopy revealed protein- and lipid-associated biochemical differences. Exploratory single-cell transcriptomic reanalysis identified cell type-specific expression of redox- and stress-associated genes and transcriptional differences involving DNA repair, metabolism, and cell-cycle pathways in extravillous trophoblasts. Together, these findings implicate p22phox-dependent redox pathways in placental oxidative injury and cellular stress responses following TGH and identify overlapping redox- and stress-associated signatures in human preeclamptic placentae.

title: Serial Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio and Mortality in Culture-Positive Pediatric Postoperative Sepsis Following Congenital Heart Surgery.
authorString: Basaran R, Yurtseven N.

journal.title: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia

abstractText:
Objectives

To evaluate the association between serial neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) measurements and in-hospital mortality in children with culture-positive postoperative sepsis following congenital heart surgery.

Design

Retrospective observational cohort study.

Setting

Tertiary pediatric cardiac surgical center.

Participants

Microbiologically confirmed postoperative sepsis developed in 237 of 2,458 children who underwent congenital heart surgery between 2018 and 2022. At the time of sepsis evaluation (T2), patients with infection-associated organ dysfunction and a Phoenix Sepsis Score ≥ 2 were classified as having postoperative sepsis and were eligible for inclusion. Eight patients with unavailable follow-up NLR data through day 14 were excluded, leaving 229 patients for analysis.

Interventions

None.

Measurements and main results

NLR was measured preoperatively (T1), at sepsis diagnosis (T2), and on days 7 (T3) and 14 (T4). Among 229 patients, 66 (28.8%) died during hospitalization. NLR was significantly higher in nonsurvivors at T2, T3, and T4, with day 7 NLR showing the highest discriminatory performance for mortality (area under the curve, 0.74; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.67-0.81). The Phoenix Sepsis Score showed a weak positive correlation with concurrent NLR at sepsis diagnosis (ρ = 0.252, p < 0.001). After multivariable adjustment, each unit increase in NLR at T2 (odds ratio [OR], 1.06; 95% CI, 1.01-1.12; p = 0.018) and T3 (OR, 1.04; 95% CI, 1.01-1.08; p = 0.012) was independently associated with higher odds of in-hospital mortality.

Conclusions

Serial NLR measurements, particularly during the first week after sepsis diagnosis, were independently associated with in-hospital mortality and may provide complementary prognostic information in pediatric patients with postoperative sepsis after congenital heart surgery.

title: Long-term trajectories of invasive hemodynamic parameters and clinical outcomes after durable left ventricular assist device implantation.
authorString: Legtenberg S, Ter Maaten JM, Erasmus ME, Kuijpers M, Douglas YL, Droogh JM, de Felice E, van den Broek SAJ, Krikken JA, Voors AA, Damman K.
abstractText:
Background

Long-term hemodynamic changes after durable left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation are not well characterized. Characterizing these trajectories is clinically relevant, as persistent or evolving abnormalities in filling pressures and pulmonary circulation may identify patients at risk for adverse outcomes.

Method

We conducted a retrospective single-center study including all patients who underwent durable LVAD implantation at the University Medical Center Groningen (2012 to 2025). We evaluated serial right heart catheterization (RHC) measurements to describe hemodynamic trajectories. Repeated measures, mixed-effect models were used to analyze hemodynamic trajectories up to 60 months of follow-up, including mean pulmonary artery pressure (mPAP), pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (PCWP), right atrial pressure (RAP), and pulmonary artery pulsatility index (PAPi). Trajectories were compared according to survivor status, baseline LVAD strategy, development of late right ventricular failure (RVF), presence of aortic regurgitation (AR), and worsening renal function (WRF).

Results

Among 199 patients (176 HeartMate 3; 23 HeartMate II), mean PAP (-10.1 mmHg, 95% CI -13.1 to -7.1) and PCWP (-9.9 mmHg, 95% CI -12.5 to -7.2) decreased significantly within the first 6 months after LVAD implantation, while RAP (0.0 mmHg, 95% CI -0.8 to 0.8) remained unchanged. Cardiac index (+0.6 L/min/m², 95% CI 0.4-0.8) and cardiac output (+1.3 L/min, 95% CI 0.9-1.7) increased significantly over the same interval. Beyond 6 months, trajectories for most hemodynamic parameters remained generally stable. Non-survivors and patients developing late RVF showed consistently higher filling pressures with trajectories largely parallel to those of survivors or those without RVF. Hemodynamic trajectories did not differ by initial LVAD strategy. In contrast, clinically significant aortic regurgitation and WRF were associated with distinct hemodynamic trajectories.

Conclusion

Hemodynamic parameters after durable LVAD implantation improved early and remained largely stable thereafter. Patients with adverse clinical outcomes showed persistently higher and/or altered hemodynamic profiles. These findings suggest that longitudinal hemodynamic assessment may enable early identification of patients at risk for adverse outcomes.

title: Early experience with sotatercept in adult patients with repaired and unrepaired congenital heart disease and pulmonary hypertension.
authorString: Gao H, Channick R, Saggar R, Troy M, Lin J, Lluri G, Reardon L, Aboulhosn J.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Int J Cardiol Congenit Heart Dis
journal.title: International journal of cardiology. Congenital heart disease
journal.isoabbreviation: Int J Cardiol Congenit Heart Dis

abstractText:
Background

Pulmonary arterial hypertension associated with congenital heart disease (ACHD-PAH) is a condition underrepresented in initial clinical trials investigating sotatercept, a first-in-class activin signaling inhibitor. Patients with unrepaired defects or complex congenital heart disease were excluded from these trials. Here, we describe real-world outcomes in a cohort of ACHD-PAH patients treated with sotatercept.

Methods

A single-center retrospective review was performed of 14 adults with ACHD-PAH initiated on sotatercept between May 2024 and January 2026. Patients had heterogeneous congenital anatomy; with half having unrepaired defects. Paired pre- and post-treatment measures were compared, and each patient served as their own control, over a median follow-up of 542 days.

Results

Eleven of 14 patients (79%) continued therapy. Three patients discontinued: one for epistaxis and two for clinical deterioration leading to heart-lung transplant listing. Adverse effects occurred in 50% of patients, most commonly epistaxis (43%). Hemoglobin increased by a median of 1.5 g/dL (p = 0.002). Symptomatic improvement was reported by 79%, and 29% improved by at least one WHO functional class. Exertional oxygen-saturation nadir improved in 71%. Echocardiography showed favorable subpulmonary ventricular remodeling, with increased fractional area change (+5.0%, p = 0.020) and reductions in right ventricular basal, mid-chamber, and longitudinal dimensions (all p ≤ 0.03). Lack of response was associated with advanced disease, pulmonary veno-occlusive physiology, and systemic ventricular dysfunction.

Conclusions

In this cohort of ACHD-PAH patients, sotatercept was generally well-tolerated and was associated with symptomatic improvement and echocardiographic signs of favorable ventricular remodeling.

title: One-year follow-up of pediatric LVAD implantation vs heart transplantation: a pilot observational study.
authorString: Hong X, Lin R, Zhu Y, Mo Y, Wang H, Liu Y, Wang G, Chen Y, Chen C, Zhou G, Li J, Zhao Z, Shu Q.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Int J Cardiol Congenit Heart Dis
journal.title: International journal of cardiology. Congenital heart disease
journal.isoabbreviation: Int J Cardiol Congenit Heart Dis

abstractText:
Background

Heart transplantation (HTx) is regarded as the definitive therapy for advanced heart failure. Scarcity of donor organs has necessitated the use of mechanical circulatory support. Data exploring mid-term clinical outcomes between pediatric patients undergoing HTx and left ventricular assist devices (LVADs) remain limited.

Methods

This two-center retrospective pilot study included pediatric patients between June 2023 and November 2025. Patients were divided into two groups: the LVAD group and the pediatric HTx (PHT) group. Pre-procedural data were collected. At the one-year follow-up, clinical outcomes, functional status, and laboratory parameters were reassessed. Continuous variables were compared using the Mann-Whitney U test, and categorical variables were analyzed using Fisher's exact test. Between-group differences were estimated using the Hodges-Lehmann median difference with corresponding 95% confidence intervals.

Results

During the study period, 22 patients were included, with 11 in the LVAD group and 11 in the PHT group. At one-year follow-up, mortality was similar, with one death occurring in each group. Among the surviving patients, two patients got respiratory infection in LVAD group and one in PHT group had an acute rejection during the follow-up period. The three patients got unplanned readmission. No other adverse events were observed during the whole follow-up.

Conclusion

In this small retrospective two-center pilot cohort, one-year mortality was numerically similar between children treated with LVAD implantation and heart transplantation. These exploratory findings support the feasibility of further comparative studies but should not be interpreted as evidence of equivalent outcomes between LVAD and transplantation.

title: Cardiovascular Changes in Pregnant Women After Mild COVID-19 Infection: An Examination of Endothelial and Autonomic Functions.
authorString: Seymen H, Safak I, Gülesir ME, Kurtar Mansiroglu A.
abstractText:
Introduction

 Pregnant women constitute a special group regarding the cardiovascular effects of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19). We employed transthoracic echocardiography, 24-hour rhythm Holter monitoring, and flow-mediated dilation (FMD) to evaluate the cardiac implications of COVID-19 in pregnant women diagnosed within the past six months.

Methods

 This study involved 80 pregnant women, 36 of whom were diagnosed with COVID-19 in the last six months of their pregnancy, while 44 served as healthy control subjects. The findings of transthoracic echocardiography, FMD, and 24-hour rhythm Holter monitoring were analyzed in all participants. All results were deemed statistically significant at a p-value threshold of less than 0.05.

Results

Echocardiography, FMD, and Holter monitoring of the COVID-19 group were performed 43 days (range: 32-174) after diagnosis. FMD values were lower in the COVID-19 group (7.90 (3.45-14.09)% vs. 14.30 (10.32-22.56)%, p=0.005). Epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) was thicker in the COVID-19 group (p=0.021). Systolic pulmonary artery pressure (sPAP) was lower in the COVID-19 group (p=0.013). The platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR) was higher in patients with a history of COVID-19 (157.36 (129.10-195.39) vs. 118.90 (101.10-152.29), p<0.001). Other echocardiographic and Holter parameters showed no differences. Adjusting for pregnancy week in a multivariable model attenuated the association between COVID-19 history and FMD (p=0.122). Gestational age acts as a confounder.

Conclusions

Mild COVID-19 during pregnancy is associated with lower unadjusted FMD and higher PLR in the recovery phase. Gestational age is a major confounder. Future studies require strict age matching.

title: Repurposing incretin-based therapies for alcohol use disorder: a systematic review of efficacy and safety relative to standard pharmacotherapies in a recent comparative context.
authorString: Alevizopoulos AG, Vasilakos V, Kritikos I, Alevizopoulou M, Korompoki E, Psaltopoulou T, Paschou SA.
abstractText:
Background

Alcohol use disorder (AUD) affects millions worldwide, but current treatments, such as disulfiram, naltrexone, acamprosate, and topiramate, have limitations in efficacy and tolerability. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs), commonly used for diabetes and obesity, may offer a new approach by targeting brain pathways involved in alcohol cravings.

Objectives

This review aims to systematically evaluate the preliminary efficacy and safety of GLP-1 RAs and other incretin-based therapies in treating AUD within a recent comparative context, alongside standard pharmacotherapies.

Design

Systematic review.

Data sources and methods

A comprehensive literature review was conducted by searching the PubMed/Medline, Web of Science, and Scopus databases from February through June 2025. The studies included were either randomized controlled trials (RCTs) or observational studies, written in English. Studies were selected based on their evaluation of GLP-1 RAs or comparator drugs in reducing alcohol consumption or related outcomes in patients with AUD.

Results

The selected 12 studies correspond to a population of 95,004 participants, but only 663 were from RCTs, while the majority were from a single registry cohort. Emerging data suggest GLP-1 RAs may reduce heavy drinking days, particularly in individuals with a higher BMI. Furthermore, observational analyses indicate a potential association between GLP-1 RA use and reduced alcohol-related hospitalizations, while metabolic data suggest biologically plausible, albeit unconfirmed, hepatoprotective effects.

Conclusion

While the large, aggregated sample size highlights the therapeutic promise of GLP-1 RAs for AUD, particularly for patients with metabolic comorbidities, the heavy reliance on observational data precludes claims of clinical equivalence with established pharmacotherapies. Appropriately powered, dedicated RCTs are required to confirm direct efficacy and long-term safety.

Trial registration

Not registered.

title: ClinicalAge, a framework for modelling ageing trajectories from longitudinal electronic health records in the UK: a model development and validation study.
authorString: Lian J, Fan Z, Fan W, Rao S, Yang Q, Zeng G, Petrazzini BO, Ahmed N, Bidel Z, Nazarzadeh M, Do R, Clegg A, Wamil M, Rahimi K.
abstractText:
Background

Ageing is a key determinant of morbidity and mortality. In this study, we aimed to develop and assess a new ageing biomarker, ClinicalAge, derived from routinely collected longitudinal electronic health record (EHR) data.

Methods

In this model development and validation study, we used UK Biobank data for model development and UK Clinical Practice Research Datalink (CPRD) Aurum data for model validation. The UK Biobank is a longitudinal population-based cohort of approximately 500 000 individuals aged 40-69 years at recruitment (March 16, 2006, to Oct 1, 2010), with linked EHR from the November 2022 UK Biobank data release. CPRD Aurum is a primary care EHR database containing anonymised longitudinal data from over 30 million patients across the UK, including diagnoses, medication, procedures, and laboratory results. A transformer-based deep learning model was trained from longitudinal EHR data to generate ClinicalAge using the validated biomarker PhenoAge as reference. We used a UK Biobank cohort for model development and internal validation, and three CPRD Aurum cohorts for external validation, longitudinal trajectory analysis, and comparison with the electronic frailty index. ClinicalAge was evaluated for associations with 17 functional measures, ten biological ageing biomarkers, 31 ageing-related diseases (11 cancer diagnoses and 20 non-cancer diseases), and all-cause, cancer, and cardiovascular mortality. We further examined longitudinal ClinicalAge trajectories and investigated clinical and disease-specific factors associated with accelerated ageing.

Findings

The UK Biobank cohort included 320 891 participants (median chronological age 58·0 years [IQR 51·0-63·0]; median PhenoAge 56·0 years [48·6-62·0]; 173 067 [53·9%] were female; and 147 824 [46·1%] were male) and the CPRD cohort included 4 728 376 individuals (51·0 years [44·0-60·0]; 2 293 243 [48·5%] were female and 2 435 133 [51·5%] were male). ClinicalAge had an R2 score of 0·819 with PhenoAge and showed a significant association with the 17 functional measures and ten biological ageing biomarkers. It was also significantly associated with the incidence of all 20 non-cancer diseases in both datasets, as well as nine (82%) of 11 cancers in UK Biobank (seven positive associations and two negative) and ten (91%) of 11 cancers (eight positive associations and two negative) in CPRD. Moreover, ClinicalAge was significantly associated with all-cause mortality (UK Biobank adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 1·23 [95% CI 1·21-1·24]; CPRD adjusted HR 1·36 [1·36-1·36]), cancer mortality (UK Biobank adjusted HR 1·12 [1·10-1·14]; CPRD adjusted HR 1·17 [1·16-1·17]), and cardiovascular mortality (UK Biobank adjusted HR 1·33 [1·29-1·36]; CPRD adjusted HR 1·36 [1·35-1·36]), after adjustment for clinical covariates and lifestyle factors. Midlife was identified as a key window for divergence, with early acceleration in individuals developing diabetes, hypertension, depression, or lifestyle disorders.

Interpretation

ClinicalAge is a non-invasive biomarker that leverages routinely collected EHR data to quantify ageing across the life course. It shows strong associations with ageing-related biomarkers, functional decline, disease risk, and mortality. Its interpretability and anticipatory signal offer a practical tool for the early identification of individuals at risk of accelerated ageing, enabling targeted preventive strategies such as lifestyle modification, cardiometabolic control, and mental health support.

Funding

None.

title: Imaging in Systemic Sclerosis (Scleroderma).
authorString: Aswani Y, Nasirul Islam GM, Scholz FJ, Zattar LC, Bello RM, Barloon T, Ansari MS, Polamraju P, Khatri G, DiSantis DJ, Revzin MV.

journal.title: Radiographics : a review publication of the Radiological Society of North America, Inc

abstractText: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) or scleroderma is a multisystem autoimmune disorder characterized by a variable pattern of skin thickening and involvement of visceral organs. The pathophysiology is similar across all organs, which is chronic low-grade inflammation, with vasculopathy and eventual fibrosis. Diagnosis is primarily clinical, particularly in patients with established disease comprising characteristic skin and visceral manifestations, with a supportive role of laboratory and imaging findings. The presence of radiologic signs such as hidebound bowel or a combination of patulous lower esophageal sphincter, pulmonary fibrosis, skin thickening, and Raynaud phenomenon is relatively specific for SSc. Nevertheless, imaging in SSc is primarily used to determine the pattern, severity, and complications of visceral organ involvement, rather than for diagnosis of SSc. Radiologic evaluation in SSc employs a wide gamut of investigations, depending on the organ of interest. For example, US is used for the skin and superficial tissues; fluoroscopy, CT, or MR enterography for the gastrointestinal tract; endoanal US or MRI for the internal anal sphincter; high-resolution CT for the lungs; echocardiography and cardiac MRI for SSc-related pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) and cardiac disease; and radiography, CT, or MRI for musculoskeletal involvement. Early diagnosis of treatable features, such as PAH and gastroesophageal reflux, can help reduce the morbidity and mortality associated with SSc. Imaging is additionally useful to prognosticate and monitor the disease. The authors focus on the multisystem, multimodality imaging manifestations of SSc with relevant differential diagnoses to bridge the gaps in knowledge about SSc. <sup>©</sup>RSNA, 2026.

title: Handling Consults with Poise: A Practical Guide to Phone and In-Person Consults for Radiology Trainees.
authorString: Ramasamy SK, Lam PL, Mittal A, Yuan J, Cao Y.

journal.title: Radiographics : a review publication of the Radiological Society of North America, Inc

title: Medication Safety Risks Associated With Inappropriate Use of Non-Crushable Tablets in Enterally Fed Patients: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
authorString: Wang FL, Shih RL, Wang KH, Wang SR, Yang CC, Peng SM, Zhang QY, Shia BC, Chen M, Wang WM.
abstractText:
Background and objectives

Hospitalized patients receiving enteral feeding are at high risk of medication administration errors. In clinical practice, non-crushable oral tablets may be inappropriately prescribed, potentially resulting in adverse outcomes. This study examined the association between inappropriate use of non-crushable oral tablets during hospitalization and early post-discharge emergency department (ED) visits among patients receiving enteral feeding.

Methods

We conducted a nationwide population-based cohort study using a national health insurance claims database in 2020, including 173,476 hospitalized patients receiving enteral feeding. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate the association between inappropriate use of non-crushable tablets and the hazard of the first ED visit during the 3-day post-discharge follow-up period.

Results

Among 173,476 patients, 40.2% were exposed to inappropriate medication use. Exposure was associated with a significantly higher hazard of a first ED visit during the 3-day post-discharge follow-up period (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.954; 95% confidence interval, 1.721-2.217). The association varied significantly across age groups and inpatient departments, with the largest adjusted hazard ratios observed among patients aged <65 years and those treated in hematology and oncology, infectious diseases, and neurosurgery. Selected comorbidities, including hypertension, cerebrovascular accident, and dementia, were also associated with a higher hazard of an early ED visit.

Conclusion

Orders for non-crushable tablets among hospitalized patients receiving enteral feeding were common and were associated with a substantially higher hazard of an early post-discharge ED visit. The association varied across age groups and inpatient departments, although these subgroup findings should be interpreted cautiously. These findings highlight an important medication safety concern during transitions of care and support further evaluation of system-level strategies, including prescribing safeguards, clinical decision support, and multidisciplinary medication review, to improve the quality and safety of medication management.

title: Antihypertensive treatment - achievements and perspectives in Europe by 2026 Italian, Swiss and Norwegian patient care.
authorString: Kjeldsen SE, Gravning J, Stokke MK, Burnier M, Grassi G, Mancia G.
abstractText:
Purpose

The aim of this perspective review paper is to provide a concise overview of selected aspects of contemporary hypertension care in Norway, Switzerland, and Italy; European countries with populations of approximately 5.5, 9, and 61 million inhabitants, respectively. These countries show remarkably similar prevalences of hypertension, as well as comparable proportions of hypertensive patients who are diagnosed, treated, and controlled.

Methods

Each country has contributed to the development of hypertension management in distinctive ways. This is illustrated by the evolution of hypertension care in the three countries-which advanced hypertension management through different but complementary contributions.

Results

Italy has provided extensive clinical and research expertise, together with sustained engagement in the European Society of Hypertension and in the development of European guidelines. Norway has been strongly involved in the design and conduct of many large clinical trials that helped define the clinical evidence base in the field, and with general practitioners as investigators. Also, the government financed major surveys and epidemiological studies with blood pressure (BP) as a key variable including collecting data for modern risk assessment in old people (SCORE2-Old People). Switzerland, for its part, made important contributions to the development of new antihypertensive drugs, particularly blockers of the renin-angiotensin system and calcium antagonists. Switzerland was also among the first European countries to accept, promote, and reimburse ambulatory blood pressure monitoring performed by general practitioners, already by the late 1980s.

Conclusion

We summarise novelties in text boxes besides basic principles, recent clarifications, and important unresolved issues, supported by selected key references.

title: Contemporary pharmacotherapy for familial hypercholesterolemia in children and adolescents.
authorString: Juliani FC, Borges KM, Henares BB, Alvo CS, Santos RD, Rocha VZ.
abstractText:
Introduction

Familial hypercholesterolemia (FH) elevates low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) from birth, accelerating early atherosclerosis and offering an opportunity for prevention in childhood.

Areas covered

This review addresses diagnosis and treatment of heterozygous and homozygous FH in children and adolescents, covering statins, ezetimibe, PCSK9 monoclonal antibodies, inclisiran, bile acid sequestrants, bempedoic acid, evinacumab, lomitapide, and lipoprotein apheresis. Pediatric dosing, efficacy, safety, vascular effects, follow-up, and recommendations are evaluated. Sources include PubMed/MEDLINE publications through September 2026, guidelines, consensus statements, and FDA/EMA information.

Expert opinion

Statins remain first-line therapy, but LDL-C targets often require early combination treatment to minimize lifelong exposure. Evidence is strongest for short-term lipid lowering and statin safety; outcome trials are impractical, and long-term data for newer drugs remain limited. Registries should assess sustained safety, adherence, development, imaging, and cardiovascular outcomes. Underdiagnosis and unequal access remain major barriers. Screening with cascade testing, genotype-informed treatment, long-acting PCSK9-directed therapies, and LDL receptor-independent approaches for homozygous FH will likely shape care. Earlier diagnosis and prompt treatment intensification should prioritize preventing atherosclerosis onset.

title: Indications for Dose Adjustment of Thyroid Hormones in Older Patients.
authorString: Bojunga J, Koehler VF, Drey M, Jaursch-Hancke C, Denkinger M.
abstractText:
Background

Thyroid dysfunction is common in older people (persons aged 65 and above). A meta-analysis of data from European countries revealed a 4.1% prevalence of undiagnosed subclinical hypothyroidism. It was found in a primary care study from the United Kingdom that approximately 10 percent of people over age 70 were under treatment for hypothyroidism.

Methods

This narrative review is based on findings in relevant publications retrieved by a PubMed search and on the guidelines of the European Thyroid Association and the American Thyroid Association.

Results

Overtreatment with levothyroxine increases the risk of cardiovascular, cognitive, and skeletal complications (hazard ratio 1.37-2.02). Randomized controlled trials have not shown that treatment with levothyroxine (T4) improves presumed symptoms of hypothyroidism, body weight, or fatigue. In patients who are now taking levothyroxine, lowering the dose or stopping the drug should be considered; in older patients, the target range for thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) should be 4-10 mU/L. After levothyroxine is stopped, some patients remain euthyroid; in the absence of an indication, gradual tapering may be considered. Levothyroxine should not be given over the long term to patients with thyroid nodules. Subclinical hyperthyroidism in older people is associated with clinically relevant risks, particularly atrial fibrillation and bone fractures, and should therefore be treated. Its most common cause, however, is levothyroxine treatment that is either not indicated or improperly dosed.

Conclusion

While overt hypothyroidism and hyperthyroidism must be treated at any age, the need to treat subclinical hypothyroidism should be individually assessed; subclinical hyperthyroidism, by contrast, generally warrants treatment given its associated risks. In view of the risks of inadequately treated hyperthyroidism and excessively dosed levothyroxine, physicians should regularly review the indication for treatment, the dosage, and the possibility of lowering the dose or discontinuing the drug.

title: Beyond Complete Revascularization in STEMI: Revisiting the Vulnerable Plaque Hypothesis and the Emerging Role of Preventive PCI in Non-Culprit Coronary Arteries.
authorString: Madanat L, Prasad A, Gulati R, Madder R, Jabri A, Patel P, Singh M, Lee JK, Wei A, Bell M, Simard T, Hibbert B, Santo PD.

journal.title: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions

abstractText: Complete revascularization is the preferred treatment strategy for hemodynamically stable patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and multivessel coronary artery disease. However, substantial residual cardiovascular risk persists despite successful treatment of angiographically or physiologically significant lesions, highlighting the limitations of revascularization strategies based solely on stenosis severity or ischemia. Increasing evidence demonstrates that many subsequent acute coronary syndromes originate from biologically high-risk, non-flow-limiting non-culprit plaques rather than flow-limiting lesions. In this review, we discuss the evolution of STEMI management from the recent focus on complete revascularization toward plaque-guided strategies, including the role of invasive and non-invasive imaging for vulnerable plaque assessment, the emerging evidence supporting preventive PCI of high-risk non-culprit lesions, and ongoing clinical trials shaping this field. Collectively, these advances provide a framework for investigating precision revascularization strategies that integrate plaque morphology, coronary physiology, multimodality imaging, and patient-level cardiovascular risk. Ongoing randomized trials are essential to determine whether plaque-guided preventive intervention improves clinically meaningful outcomes beyond contemporary approaches to revascularization and optimal medical therapy.

title: Beta-blocker therapy and angina burden after myocardial infarction: A prespecified substudy of the BETAMI-DANBLOCK trial.
authorString: Kristensen AMD, Holmager TLF, Rykind-Eriksen F, Fagerland MW, Halvorsen S, Olsen MH, Bakken A, Atar D, Munkhaugen J, Prescott E.
abstractText: The effect of beta-blockers initiated after myocardial infarction (MI) on subsequent angina burden remains uncertain. This pre-specified BETAMI-DANBLOCK substudy included patients with MI and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF)≥40% randomized to beta-blockers or no beta-blockers. Endpoints comprised angina-related hospital contacts/diagnostic ischemia tests, coronary revascularization, anti-anginal medications (≥2 prescriptions for calcium-channel blockers/nitrates), and patient-reported angina symptoms [Canadian Cardiovascular Society (CCS) class 0-4]. Subdistribution hazard ratios (SHR) were estimated by Fine-Gray models. Anti-anginal prescriptions were compared using 95% confidence intervals (CI) for differences in proportions.A total of 5574 patients were randomized to beta-blockers (n=2783, median dose 50 mg metoprolol) or no beta-blockers (n=2791). During median 3.5 years follow-up, an angina-related hospital contact/diagnostic ischemia test occurred in 724 patients (26.0%) in the beta-blocker group vs. 834 (29.9%) in the no beta-blocker group (SHR 0.85; 95% CI, 0.77-0.94). Coronary revascularization occurred in 108 (3.9%) vs. 110 patients (3.9%)(SHR 0.99; 95% CI 0.76-1.29). Fewer patients in the beta-blocker group were treated with calcium-channel blockers [630(22.7%) vs. 738(26.6%); -3.9 percentage points (95% CI, -6.2 to -1.6)], whereas nitrate use [342(12.3%) vs. 356(12.8%); -0.5 (95% CI, -2.2 to 1.2)] and CCS-scores were similar between groups (difference in change at 12-months, -0.04; 95% CI, -0.14-0.05). In patients with MI and LVEF≥40%, a moderate dose of beta-blockers was associated with a lower incidence of first angina-related hospital contact/diagnostic ischemia testing, and lower use of calcium-channel blockers. The absence of differences in coronary revascularization, nitrate use and patient-reported angina symptoms suggests that the overall benefit on angina is limited.

title: SGLT2 Inhibitors in Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus: The Kidney and Heart Perspective.
authorString: Pongrac Barlovic D, Groop PH.
abstractText: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) have become a cornerstone of cardio-kidney protection in type 2 diabetes, yet their role in type 1 diabetes remains incompletely defined. While randomized controlled trials in type 1 diabetes have consistently demonstrated improvements in glycemic control, body weight, and insulin requirements, they were not designed to assess cardiovascular or kidney outcomes. Consequently, current evidence for cardio-kidney protection in type 1 diabetes is derived largely from physiological studies, surrogate biomarkers, and observational data.Accumulating evidence however suggests potential kidney benefits in type 1 diabetes. Across clinical and real-world studies, SGLT2i has been associated with up to 40% reduction in albuminuria and attenuation of the estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) decline. These observations are consistent with mechanistic studies demonstrating restoration of the tubuloglomerular feedback and reduction of the intraglomerular pressure as the principal kidney-protective mechanisms of SGLT2i. However, evidence for cardiovascular protection remains substantially more limited. Studies demonstrate improvements in several established cardiovascular risk factors, including reductions in body weight (up to 3.4 kg), systolic blood pressure (approximately 2-4 mmHg), and fasting glucose. Yet direct evidence for reductions of cardiovascular events, kidney failure, or mortality is currently unavailable.Despite these limitations, the potential for early kidney protection in type 1 diabetes is particularly attractive, given the long natural history of diabetic kidney disease and the opportunity for intervention before irreversible kidney damage occurs. However, the increased risk of diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) remains the major obstacle to widespread use and regulatory approval of SGLT2i in this population. Careful patient selection, structured education, ketone body monitoring, and implementation of DKA risk-mitigation strategies are therefore essential when considering this therapy. Future studies incorporating dedicated cardio-kidney endpoints and advances such as continuous ketone body monitoring may help clarify the benefit-risk balance and determine whether SGLT2i can ultimately assume a broader role as adjunctive cardio-kidney protective therapy in type 1 diabetes.

title: Should romosozumab be used in patients with a history or risk of CVD?
authorString: Liu H, Liu L, Rosen CJ.
abstractText: Romosozumab offers substantial fracture protection, but its use in patients with cardiovascular disease or risk factors for cardiovascular disease remains uncertain. Randomized trials have yielded conflicting cardiovascular findings, and meta-analyses have not definitively excluded clinically relevant harm. Observational studies generally report no increased risk compared with other osteoporosis treatments, including in some patients with previous cardiovascular events. However, these findings are limited by treatment-selection bias, heterogeneous outcome definitions, and relatively short follow-up. Thus, in patients with established cardiovascular disease, a potential risk remains biologically plausible but unproven. Careful patient selection is still required, and individuals with established cardiovascular disease should be excluded based on US and European labeling advice. More studies are still needed to understand the basic biology of sclerostin relative to atherosclerosis and vessel calcification.

title: Fixed-Dose Combination Versus Add-On Therapy: Clarifying the Role of Cilostazol-Rosuvastatin in Peripheral Artery Disease.
authorString: Lu D, Kuang C.
abstractText: The randomized trial by Kemalasari et al. provides evidence supporting the addition of cilostazol to rosuvastatin in patients with symptomatic peripheral artery disease. However, because the study compared the fixed-dose combination (FDC) with rosuvastatin plus placebo, it does not establish whether the FDC formulation offers advantages over an equivalent free-combination regimen. Evidence from other cardiovascular settings suggests that FDC formulations may improve medication adherence and treatment persistence, although their effects on long-term clinical outcomes remain uncertain. Future randomized studies directly comparing fixed-dose and free-combination regimens, with adherence assessed over 12 months and longer-term cardiovascular and limb outcomes evaluated, are needed to clarify the clinical value of the formulation itself.

title: Lipoprotein(a) in Cardiovascular Disease: Integrating Epidemiology, Clinical Guidelines, Molar Measurement, and Emerging Therapies.
authorString: Thomas PE, Vedel-Krogh S, Kronenberg F, Nordestgaard BG.
abstractText:
Background

Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is a causal risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD = myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke, peripheral artery disease) and aortic valve stenosis. Plasma concentrations of Lp(a) are >90% genetically determined. Multiple drugs in development reduce lipoprotein(a) by 80% to 98%. While the recently announced topline results, the phase 3 Lp(a)HORIZON trial of pelacarsen did not meet its primary cardiovascular endpoint despite lowering Lp(a), and 3 other cardiovascular outcomes trials remain ongoing. Lipoprotein(a) testing is currently increasing rapidly in many countries.

Content

Most guidelines on dyslipidemia and prevention of cardiovascular disease worldwide now advise that Lp(a) should be measured once in all adults, ideally jointly with the first lipid profile ordered. If previous lipid profiles were taken, then Lp(a) should be included in the next lipid profile. Lipoprotein(a) should ideally be measured in nmol/L, and repeat measurements are relevant if drugs are given to lower Lp(a) concentrations, initially at suspected acute coronary syndrome or stroke and again after 1 month, and sometimes in women after menopause. Measuring Lp(a) levels alongside a standard lipid profile provides a more comprehensive initial assessment of a patient's overall cardiovascular risk. Clinical chemistry laboratories that measure lipid profiles should therefore also offer Lp(a) testing. This is easily done as Lp(a) assays can be run on most major clinical chemistry platforms. High Lp(a) is >105 nmol/L (>50 mg/dL).

Summary

As use of Lp(a) testing is increasing rapidly worldwide, more clinical chemistry laboratories will likely offer this test locally. Measuring Lp(a) levels alongside a standard lipid profile provides a more comprehensive initial lipid assessment of a patient's cardiovascular risk.

title: Long-term outcomes of biodegradable- versus durable-polymer drug-eluting stents in patients with advanced chronic kidney disease undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention: a 7-year retrospective cohort study.
authorString: Yeh JK, Huang MS, Chang HY, Lee WH, Liu PY, Liu YW.
abstractText:
Objectives

Patients with advanced chronic kidney disease (CKD) or end-stage renal disease (ESRD) undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) have high event rates, but long-term outcomes after contemporary drug-eluting stent (DES) implantation remain insufficiently defined. This study compared 7-year outcomes between biodegradable polymer DES (BP-DES) and durable polymer DES (DP-DES) in patients with stage 5 CKD or ESRD undergoing PCI.

Methods

We retrospectively analyzed patients with stage 5 CKD or ESRD who underwent PCI with DES implantation between 2010 and 2019. The primary outcome was target lesion failure (TLF), defined as cardiac death, target-vessel myocardial infarction, or clinically driven target lesion revascularization. The secondary outcome was all-cause mortality. Outcomes were compared using Cox regression, competing-risk analysis, and overlap-weighted propensity score analysis.

Results

Among 417 patients, the mean age was 66.8 ± 10.4 years, 60.4% were male, and the median follow-up was 80 months. The 84-month cumulative incidence of TLF was 49% with BP-DES and 39% with DP-DES (Gray's test, P = 0.235). The observed 7-year mortality was 37.5 and 32.6%, respectively. DP-DES was not significantly associated with TLF [adjusted hazard ratio vs. BP-DES: 0.79, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.54-1.14; P = 0.207] or mortality (adjusted hazard ratio: 0.91, 95% CI: 0.63-1.33; P = 0.634). Older age and diabetes mellitus independently predicted mortality.

Conclusion

In patients with stage 5 CKD or ESRD undergoing PCI, 7-year TLF and mortality were frequent and did not differ significantly by DES polymer type.

title: Age-adjusted baseline D-dimer predicts thrombotic events during readmission in anticoagulated patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation
authorString: Wang X, Zhang L, Zhang D, Yu J, Dai Z, Li Q, Yan X.
abstractText: Background Patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF) remain at substantial risk of thrombotic and bleeding events despite oral anticoagulation, and readmission is a common and costly consequence. D-dimer reflects persistent coagulation and fibrinolysis activation and has been associated with adverse outcomes in atrial fibrillation, but whether a single baseline measurement can predict events during readmission remains unclear. Methods We retrospectively studied 1,108 anticoagulated patients with NVAF who had multiple hospitalisations at our institution between 2018 and 2022. Patients were stratified by baseline D-dimer according to an age-adjusted cut-off. The primary endpoint was a composite of thrombotic events, major bleeding and death during readmission, adjudicated by a hierarchical first-event rule. Multivariable Cox regression was performed in the 899 patients with complete CHA₂DS₂-VASc and HAS-BLED scores. Sensitivity analyses included propensity score matching (230 pairs) and a competing-risk model and a 30-day landmark analysis. The incremental value of the age-adjusted D-dimer cut-off beyond CHA₂DS₂-VASc was assessed by the C-statistic. Results The abnormal-D-dimer group had a higher incidence of the composite endpoint (24.0% vs 9.6%, P < 0.001) and of thrombotic events (19.7% vs 8.2%, P < 0.001). Abnormal D-dimer independently predicted the composite endpoint (adjusted HR 1.64, 95% CI 1.09–2.47) and thrombotic events (adjusted HR 2.02, 95% CI 1.30–3.15), but not major bleeding (HR 1.46, 95% CI 0.44–4.90) or death during readmission (HR 1.73, 95% CI 0.54–5.52). Sensitivity analyses were consistent for the composite and thrombotic endpoints, whereas bleeding and death events were too few for reliable estimates. Adding D-dimer to CHA₂DS₂-VASc improved discrimination (ΔC = 0.034, 95% CI 0.006–0.076) and reclassification (24-month NRI = 43.8%; IDI = 0.025). Conclusions In anticoagulated patients with NVAF, a baseline D-dimer above the age-adjusted cut-off independently predicts thrombotic events during subsequent readmission and provides incremental predictive information beyond CHA₂DS₂-VASc.

title: The Detection of Atrial Fibrillation by Implantable Event Recorders: A Study of Patients Who Have Had a Cryptogenic Stroke.
authorString: Wagner F, Günther A, Kirsch K, Schulze CP, Klingner C, Geis C, Brodoehl S, Weigel K, Klinner C.
abstractText:
Background

Arial fibrillation (AF) plays a role in approximately one-third of ischemic strokes. In embolic strokes of undetermined source (ESUS), paroxysmal atrial fibrillation often escapes detection; if detected, it could be an indication for oral anticoagulation. In the ARTESiA trial, the absolute benefit of anticoagulation was higher in patients who had already had a stroke or transient ischemic attack (TIA) than in those who had not.

Methods

We retrospectively analyzed data from 233 consecutive ESUS patients at the Jena University Hospital who had received an implanted loop recorder (ILR) over the period 2021-2025. We additionally provide a narrative review on the detection rates associated with various monitoring strategies based on pertinent publications that were retrieved by a literature search.

Results

The 12-month detection rate of paroxysmal AF was 24.0% (56/233, 95% confidence interval [19.0; 29.9]). 73.2% of the initial detections were within the first 90 days. All patients in whom AF was detected were orally anticoagulated. The 12-month detection rate was higher than in the CRYSTAL-AF trial (12.4%) and the PER-DIEM trial (15.3%), but lower than was reported by Pikija et al. (31.3%). The cutoff values with the highest positive predictive value were a stroke risk analysis (SRA) index of 2 or above (38.4%) and age 75 or above (37.9%).

Conclusion

Early, risk-adapted diagnostic testing with ILR in selected ESUS patients can detect clinically relevant AF. Advanced age and an elevated SRA index may be useful patient selection criteria. A robust number needed to treat (NNT) for the ILR strategy cannot be derived from the available one-armed registry data. The indication for ILR should be linked to its therapeutic relevance, the probability of detecting AF, and the individual hemorrhagic risk.

title: Hemodynamic effects of a novel counter-pulsatile system for extracorporeal membrane oxygenation.
authorString: Bastos MB, Knigge S, Schmack B, Schana L, Malchin O, Schumacher F, Merzah AS, Popov AF, Weymann A, Ruhparwar A, Dogan G, Schmitto JD.
abstractText: Background and aimsMortality from heart failure is still high despite all the recent advances. Continuous-flow (CF) Veno-arterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation (VA-ECMO) can temporarily maintain systemic and pulmonary hemodynamics, at the cost of overloading the left ventricle (LV). A new Pulsatile Ventricular Assist Platform (pVAP) could offer a more physiological hemodynamic support.Methods6 large porcine models of acute ischemic left ventricular (LV) failure received the pVAP in a VA-ECMO configuration. Invasive systemic and intraventricular hemodynamic measurements were taken with synchronized counter-pulsatile flow (SCPF) and CF support at the same flow rate. The measurements were compared with no support (ON vs OFF) in both modalities.ResultsThe pVAP successfully delivered VA-ECMO in acute ischemic heart failure. The device maintained stable hemodynamics and increased the forward cardiac output (CO<sub>F</sub>) without overloading the LV and with no change in the LV pressure-volume area (PVA). SCPF, but not CF, was associated with improved LV afterload and ventricular-arterial coupling compared to no support.ConclusionThe findings suggest that the pVAP is feasible also in a VA-ECMO configuration, supporting hemodynamics with more physiological effect on effect on the LV dynamics.

title: Differential characteristics of takotsubo cardiomyopathy according to clinical context.
authorString: Kim BG, Jeong WJ, Jeong H, Kim SE, Oh HJ, Hwang JW, Kwon SU, Doh JH, Namgung J, Kim DG, Kim MS, Cho SW.

journal.title: The Korean journal of internal medicine

abstractText:
Background/aims

Takotsubo cardiomyopathy (TC) occurs in diverse clinical settings and generally has a favorable prognosis; however, little is known about its characteristics and outcomes across different contexts. We evaluated the clinical features and in-hospital mortality of TC according to clinical setting.

Methods

A total of 153 patients diagnosed with TC from 2008 to 2020 were included. Patients were classified as having primary TC (presenting as the primary reason for care, n = 31) or secondary TC (n = 122), which was further subdivided into infection (n = 58), medical/surgical illness (n = 38), and stroke (n = 26).

Results

Prior cerebrovascular accident was more frequent in the infection and stroke groups. Length of hospital stay, intenincludsive care unit stay, and ventilator use were greatest in the stroke group, whereas inotropic agent use was most frequent in the infection group. N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide levels differed across groups, with the highest levels observed in the primary form (p = 0.025). Echocardiographic parameters were generally comparable, although left atrial diameter was larger in the primary form and smaller in the stroke group. Overall in-hospital mortality was 13.1% and occurred exclusively in secondary TC. Mortality was highest in the infection group, but the difference was not statistically significant (p = 0.053). In multivariate regression analysis, age, bacteremia, and follow-up right ventricular systolic pressure (RVSP) were independently associated with in-hospital mortality.

Conclusions

The prognosis of primary form of TC was excellent, while the patients with infection had higher tendency of in-hospital death. Age, bacteremia, and follow-up RVSP were independent predictors of in-hospital death in TC patients.

title: Statin-Ezetimibe Therapy and Incident Myocardial Infarction Across Modified Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Risk Groups: A Nationwide Target Trial Emulation.
authorString: Kwon RJ, Lim Y.
abstractText: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome integrates metabolic risk, kidney dysfunction, and cardiovascular disease. Whether statin-ezetimibe combination therapy is associated with lower subsequent myocardial infarction risk than statin monotherapy among patients across modified cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic risk groups remains uncertain. Using the Korean National Health Insurance Service database, we emulated separate two-arm landmark target trials within modified early and late cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic risk groups. Adults aged 30-74 years with dyslipidemia who received prescriptions covering a total of 180 days with statin monotherapy or a fixed-dose statin-ezetimibe combination were eligible. Treatment was assigned at the 180-day landmark. Stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting and cause-specific Cox regression were used to calculate hazard ratio (HR) and 95% confidence interval (CI), with death treated as a competing event for cumulative incidence estimation. Among 309,371 treated participants, 239,954 had modified early risk and 69,417 had modified late risk. Compared with statin monotherapy, statin-ezetimibe therapy was associated with lower myocardial infarction risk after weighting in both early-risk participants (HR 0.87, 95% CI 0.81-0.95) and late-risk participants (HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.79-0.98). 10-year weighted cumulative incidence was 1.97% versus 2.23% in the early-risk group and 3.52% versus 3.94% in the late-risk group. In same-intensity comparisons, the association was most evident with moderate-intensity therapy, particularly in the early CKM group (HR, 0.87; 95% CI, 0.79-0.95). Among adults with dyslipidemia who received prescriptions covering a total of 180 days, statin-ezetimibe combination therapy was associated with a lower subsequent risk of myocardial infarction than statin monotherapy across modified CKM risk groups. The association was most evident in moderate-intensity comparisons.

title: Creatinine-Cystatin C eGFR Discordance Identifies Long-Term Cardiorenal Risk in Acute Coronary Syndrome: A Cohort Study.
authorString: García Majado C, Baldeón Conde C, Rodrigo Calabia E, Pasache Chong JE, Fernández Fresnedo G, Ruiz JC, Hernández JL.
abstractText: Discordance between creatinine- and cystatin C-based estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) is common and has been associated with adverse outcomes in population-based cohorts. However, its relevance in patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) remains uncertain. We conducted a retrospective cohort study including 808 patients with ACS admitted to the Cardiac Intensive Care Unit of Marqués de Valdecilla University Hospital (Santander, Spain) between 1 January, 2012 and 31 December, 2015, for whom measurements of creatinine and cystatin C at admission were available. Discordance between creatinine- and cystatin C-based eGFR was assessed using continuous indices (eGFR difference and ratio) and categorical definitions based on a threshold of 15 mL/min/1.73m². Associations with all-cause mortality, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), and kidney function decline were evaluated using Cox regression models adjusted for cardiovascular risk factors and creatinine-cystatin C eGFR. Creatinine-cystatin C eGFR discordance was present in 44.2% of patients. Over a median follow-up of 8.4 years, lower cystatin C-based relative to creatinine-based eGFR was associated with higher risks of all-cause mortality, MACE, and kidney function decline. These associations persisted among patients with preserved creatinine-based kidney function.
