If future studies confirm our findings, these results may have implications for the development of new preventive therapies.

title: Prevalence of type 2 diabetes mellitus, risk factors, and complications in Middle East and North African region: A systematic review.
authorString: Lovelin Auguskani JP, Gurusamy V, Muttipoll Dharmarajlu S, Chellathurai A, Arulappan J.
abstractText: BackgroundType 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM) is a rapidly growing health challenge in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region, contributing to increasing morbidity and mortality.ObjectivesThis review synthesizes evidence on the prevalence of T2DM, risk factors, and complications in the MENA region.MethodsFollowing PRISMA reporting guidelines and PROSPERO registration (CRD420251111168), systematic searches were conducted for studies published between 2015 and 2025.ResultsAcross the 19 included studies, the prevalence and burden of T2DM varied considerably across the MENA region. Regional data indicated an 85.5% increase in diabetes prevalence between 1990 and 2019, while individual population-based studies reported T2DM prevalence of 32.0% in north-eastern Tunisia and 15.3% in southwestern Iran. In Jordan, age-standardized diabetes prevalence increased from 13.0% in 1994 to 23.7% in 2017. Older age, obesity, physical inactivity, hypertension, central adiposity, family history of diabetes, and socioeconomic factors were commonly associated with T2DM. Among individuals with established T2DM, microvascular and macrovascular complications were reported in 17.7% and 10.7%, respectively, while diabetic neuropathy affected 15.3%-23.0% in selected studies. Suboptimal glycaemic and cardiovascular risk-factor control was also frequently reported.ConclusionT2DM constitutes a substantial and heterogeneous public health challenge across the MENA region. The findings indicate a need for context-specific strategies that integrate prevention, early detection, culturally appropriate lifestyle interventions, and comprehensive long-term disease management. Strengthening multidisciplinary approaches and addressing modifiable risk factors may help reduce the future health burden associated with T2DM across the region.

title: Risk factors associated with in-hospital mortality and a composite of major complications following paediatric congenital cardiac surgery: A systematic review protocol.
authorString: Mogane P, Kebalepile M, Motshabi Chakane P.
abstractText:
Background

Approximately 70% of patients born with congenital heart disease (CHD) require medical or surgical treatment in their first year of life. A reported 90-95% will survive to adulthood due to advances in paediatric cardiology, cardiac surgery and anaesthesia. These reported advances are still not available for over 90% of the children born with CHD in low-and middle-income countries (LMIC). The objectives of this study are to determine the pooled incidence of in-hospital all-cause mortality; identify risk factors associated with in-hospital all-cause mortality and a composite of major complications in paediatric patients undergoing congenital cardiac surgery; and to compare these risk factors between LMICs and high-income countries (HICs).

Methods

A systematic review will be conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines; this has been registered with PROSPERO 2024 (CRD42024618297). The Population, Exposure and Outcome (PEO) framework will guide the search strategy. Eligible studies will include prospective and retrospective cohort studies, case-control studies, interventional studies and registry/database studies reporting risk factors for in-hospital all-cause mortality and/or major postoperative complications in paediatric patients (≤18 years) undergoing cardiac surgery for CHD. A comprehensive electronic search of PubMed, Scopus, CINAHL, Cochrane Library and Web of Science will identify peer-reviewed English-language studies published from January 2000-2026. Two reviewers will independently screen studies, extract data using a standardised data extraction form, and assess risk of bias using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale or ROBINS-I, as appropriate to study design. Where appropriate, we will perform random-effects meta-analysis to estimate pooled effect measures and 95% confidence intervals. Statistical heterogeneity will be assessed using the I² statistic, and results will otherwise be synthesised narratively. Where sufficient data are available, risk factors will be compared between LMICs and HICs.

Discussion

In-hospital mortality and major complications following paediatric congenital cardiac surgery are associated with a combination of patient-, surgical- and perioperative risk factors. Identifying these facilitates early risk stratification and optimisation of modifiable risk factors to support targeted perioperative interventions and resource allocation, particularly in LMICs where evidence remains limited. A meta-analysis is not anticipated because of substantial heterogeneity in the study population.

title: New-Onset Atrial Fibrillation in Critically Ill Patients: A Systematic Review of In-Hospital and Post-Discharge Outcomes.
authorString: Tan SWZ, Lee QH, Ding W, Song Z, Koh JCK, Das Gupta K, Samuel M, Vu HL, Soong JTY, Cove ME.
abstractText:
Objectives

This systematic review and meta-analysis determines the incidence of new-onset atrial fibrillation (NOAF) in critically ill patients, risks of post-discharge systemic thromboembolism, anticoagulation therapy, and the proportion diagnosed with AF post-discharge.

Data sources

A search of registered databases (PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and CINAHL) was performed from inception to April 20, 2026.

Study selection

Eligible studies included critically ill patients (≥ 18 yr old) who developed NOAF during admission to general ICUs or high-dependency units. NOAF was defined as AF in patients without prior history of AF.

Data extraction

Data were independently extracted from full-text versions of included studies by nonblinded reviewers.

Data synthesis

A Bayesian meta-analysis was conducted on 54 studies (367,896 patients) with a random-effects model using R (Version 4.3.3). Pooled incidence of NOAF in critically ill patients was 10.6% (95% credible interval [CrI], 8.6-12.9%). Absolute risk of post-discharge systemic thromboembolism was 7.1% (95% CrI, 4.5-11.0%), changing to 6.9% (95% CrI, 4.2-11.6%) after age and sex adjustment. Evidence from six studies reports that critically ill patients with NOAF had 1.94 times (95% CrI, 1.23-3.29) higher relative risk of systemic thromboembolism post-discharge than patients without NOAF, rising to 2.01 (95% CrI, 1.54-2.80) with adjustment. Absolute and relative risk are evaluated with follow-up durations ranging from 1.5 months to 5 years, with variable anticoagulation exposure. Anticoagulation rates were low: 32.9% in-hospital (95% CrI, 14.6-57.9%) and 35.9% post-discharge (95% CrI, 19.7-55.9%). On follow-up, 23.9% (95% CrI, 13.9-38.5%) of critically ill patients with NOAF were subsequently diagnosed with AF.

Conclusions

Our review suggests that NOAF during critical illness is associated with significantly increased risk of post-discharge systemic thromboembolism and subsequent AF diagnosis. However, rates of anticoagulation initiation remain low, highlighting the need for improved risk stratification and targeted strategies post-discharge.

title: Subclinical atherosclerosis in immune-mediated inflammatory rheumatic diseases: a meta-analysis.
authorString: Wang L, Du J, Lu Y, Wang Y, Jiang S, Pan H, Li X, Luo L.
abstractText:
Objective

This meta-analysis aims to investigate the association between immune-mediated inflammatory rheumatic diseases (IMIRDs) and subclinical atherosclerosis.

Methods

A comprehensive search was conducted in PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library. Data were pooled using a random-effects model and presented as odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI). Heterogeneity was evaluated using the I2 statistic. Publication bias was assessed by funnel plots, Begg's test, and Egger's test.

Results

Fifteen studies were included. The main analysis showed that IMIRDs were associated with subclinical atherosclerosis, with a pooled OR of 2.76 (95% CI 2.22-3.43). Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of this finding: exclusion of the RR-based estimate yielded a pooled OR of 2.90 (95% CI 2.33-3.61), and the leave-one-out analysis showed no substantial change in the overall estimate. In subgroup analyses, the pooled ORs were 3.04 for SLE, 2.56 for SS, 2.02 for RA, and 4.98 for SSc, while the single PsA study reported an OR of 3.87. By outcome, the pooled ORs were 2.77 for prevalent plaque, 6.45 for dichotomized IMT, and 3.80 for composite subclinical atherosclerosis; one study assessing prospective progression reported an OR of 2.64. Overall heterogeneity was low (I2 = 17.4%).

Conclusions

IMIRDs were associated with subclinical atherosclerosis-related imaging abnormalities. Given differences in outcome definitions and effect measures, pooled estimates reflect an overall association rather than a precise increase in clinical risk. Causality cannot be inferred.

title: Nurse-coordinated multidisciplinary prehabilitation for older adults with frailty undergoing elective transcatheter aortic valve replacement: protocol for a randomised controlled trial.
authorString: Luo Z, Li Y, Zhang X, Wang Y, Liu X, Yu P, Miao C.

title: Clonal Hematopoiesis and Cardiovascular and Microvascular Outcomes in Type 2 Diabetes: A Retrospective Analysis of the UK Biobank.
authorString: Gao Y, Zhang C, Chen D, Shi Z, Shi Q, Gu Y, Shi B, Ma C, Guo Q, Wang Y, Zhang Z, Geng B, Li M.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

Clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) has been associated with cardiovascular disease, but its associations across cardiovascular and microvascular complications in type 2 diabetes remain incompletely characterized.

Methods

We retrospectively analyzed 17 893 UK Biobank participants with type 2 diabetes, whole-exome sequencing, and no prevalent cardiovascular or microvascular complications. CHIP was defined from the curated UK Biobank call set by ≥1 driver variant with a variant allele fraction ≥2%. Associations with incident outcomes were evaluated using Fine-Gray models with multiple imputation for missing covariates. Driver-gene, clone-size, proteomic, and metabolomic analyses were exploratory.

Results

CHIP was present in 670 participants (3.7%) over a median follow-up of 14.6 years. CHIP was associated with the composite cardiovascular outcome (subdistribution hazard ratio [SHR], 1.19 [95% CI, 1.00-1.42]), with heart failure showing the clearest component association (SHR, 1.43 [95% CI, 1.13-1.81]); acute coronary syndrome and stroke were not significantly associated. CHIP was also associated with the composite microvascular outcome (SHR, 1.34 [95% CI, 1.15-1.56]), broad chronic kidney disease (SHR, 1.28 [95% CI, 1.05-1.57]), and retinopathy (SHR, 1.43 [95% CI, 1.15-1.77]) but not neuropathy or strict diabetes-specific nephropathy. Ten-year adjusted risk differences were 1.94% and 3.46% for the cardiovascular and microvascular composites, respectively. Among 2919 proteins, ZBP1 (Z-DNA-binding protein 1) was the only protein retained after false-discovery-rate correction; no metabolite module was associated with CHIP after correction, whereas selected lipoprotein and amino acid/lactate modules were associated with cardiovascular outcomes, particularly heart failure.

Conclusions

In adults with type 2 diabetes, CHIP was associated with a higher risk of incident microvascular complications and, among cardiovascular outcomes, most consistently with heart failure. Exploratory multiomic findings, including a protein-wide ZBP1 signal and selected metabolic associations with cardiovascular outcomes, provided additional biological context but require independent validation.

title: Evaluating the Low-Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol Paradox in Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction.
authorString: Xue R, Lee A, Jiang Y, Lau YH, Teo LLY, Wong RCC, Soon DKN, Shum KL, Huang W, Loh SY, Lin W, Chiang BSQ, Chow W, Hausenloy DJ, Yeo KK, Yap J.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

Hypercholesterolemia is an established cardiovascular risk factor. However, studies in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) showed an association between low low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) and increased mortality, termed the "LDL-C paradox." This study examined the impact of LDL-C on clinical outcomes in patients with HFrEF and identify distinct hypocholesterolemia subgroups using latent class analysis.

Methods

Consecutive patients with HFrEF (left ventricular EF <40%) from national registries (2016-2022) were stratified by LDL-C quartiles, with the lowest quartile ≤1.73 mmol/L. Latent class analysis was performed to identify subsets of patients in the lowest quartile. Outcomes included 1-year all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, readmission, and composite end points.

Results

Among 2188 patients, the lowest LDL-C quartile had higher 1-year all-cause mortality than Quartile 2 and 3 (P<0.05) but not Quartile 4, with no intergroup differences in cardiovascular mortality, readmissions, or composite outcomes between groups. Latent class analysis identified 2 hypocholesterolemia subgroups: pathological and nonpathological hypocholesterolemia. The pathological subgroup was older, lower weight, with higher comorbidity burden. Compared with patients with hypercholesterolemia, the pathological hypocholesterolemia subgroup had higher 1-year all-cause mortality (adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 2.14 [95% CI, 1.17-2.69], P<0.001), cardiovascular mortality (adjusted HR, 1.93 [95% CI, 1.46-2.54], P<0.001), and composite end points (adjusted HR, 1.15 [95% CI, 1.01-1.30], P=0.037), and the subgroup with nonpathological hypocholesterolemia showed comparable outcomes.

Conclusions

A distinct subset of patients with HFrEF with low LDL-C demonstrates different clinical characteristics (older and higher comorbidity burden) and poorer outcomes, potentially elucidating the "LDL-C paradox" cause in patients with HFrEF.

title: Thirty-Day All-Cause Readmissions After Pregnancy-Associated Hospitalizations With Heart Failure in the United States: Analysis of the Nationwide Readmissions Database.
authorString: Barry E, Kim MJ, Goldstein S, Denoble A, Hsueh C, Chavez P, Tabtabai S.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of pregnancy-related morbidity and mortality in the United States. There is a paucity of data regarding pregnancy-associated heart failure readmissions. This study aims to characterize the 30-day heart failure readmission patterns in pregnancy-associated admissions.

Methods

The National Readmission Database from 2016 to 2021 was used to identify women aged 13 to 49 with an index hospitalization with heart failure as the primary or secondary diagnosis during a pregnancy-related admission, identified by diagnosis-related group codes and International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision (ICD-10) codes. The primary outcome was 30-day all-cause readmission. Survey-weighted descriptive analyses and hierarchical multivariable logistic regression were used to characterize readmission patterns and identify independently associated factors.

Results

Among 19 452 eligible index hospitalizations, 2659 were followed by a 30-day readmission; the survey-weighted readmission rate was 13.5%. In the fully adjusted model, Medicare and Medicaid coverage, residence in a small metropolitan area, greater All Patient Refined Diagnosis-Related Group severity, discharge with home health care, and discharge against medical advice were associated with higher odds of readmission. Deficiency anemia, chronic pulmonary disease, diabetes without chronic complications, renal failure, solid tumor without metastasis, and cardiovascular or respiratory disorders complicating pregnancy were also independently associated with increased readmission.

Conclusions

Approximately 1 in 7 pregnancy-associated hospitalizations complicated by heart failure was followed by a 30-day all-cause readmission. Readmission risk reflected a combination of illness severity, discharge disposition, payer status, geographic location, and selected medical and pregnancy-related comorbidities. These findings support the development and evaluation of individualized, multidisciplinary transitional-care strategies for patients at highest risk.

title: Incidence of Cardiovascular Disease in a Primary Care Population of Young Adults by Disaggregated Race and Ethnicity.
authorString: Chapman R, King S, Jose PO, Avery B, Narayan GA, Rodriguez F, Yan X.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death in the United States, with well-documented racial and ethnic disparities. Data are limited on incidence among patients aged <50 years, particularly within disaggregated Asian and Hispanic subgroups and individuals identifying with multiple racial or ethnic groups. We estimated CVD incidence rates for these groups and assessed whether disparities are explained by other clinical and demographic risk factors.

Methods

This retrospective cohort study used Sutter Health Electronic Health Record data (2010-2024) for adults aged 18 to 49 years with at least 2 primary care visits and a 2-year observed baseline period free of CVD. Incident CVD was defined as myocardial infarction, stroke, or heart failure. We estimated incidence rates, applied age and sex standardization, and fit Cox proportional hazards models adjusting for additional risk factors.

Results

In a cohort of 1 178 551 patients, incidence was 1.14 cases per 1000 person-years (95% CI, 1.12-1.17). After standardization, Pacific Islander individuals (hazard ratio [HR], 2.90 [95% CI, 2.29-3.52]) and non-Hispanic Black individuals (HR, 2.82 [95% CI, 2.58-3.06]) had the highest incidence. Within the Asian group, Filipino individuals had the highest incidence (HR, 1.60 [95% CI, 1.42-1.79]). Hispanic subgroups showed less heterogeneity. Elevated HRs persisted among some groups after adjustment with Cox models.

Conclusions

Young adult CVD incidence varied across racial and ethnic subgroups. Elevated risk persisted in several groups after adjustment, consistent with the influence of unmeasured social drivers. These findings support collection of granular racial and ethnic data and validation of existing risk prediction tools in young adult subgroups.

title: Prognostic Value of Right Ventricular-Pulmonary Artery Coupling in Mitral Valve Surgery and Impact of Concomitant Tricuspid Valve Repair.
authorString: Kahrovic A, Herkner H, Gangl C, Zilberszac R, Coti I, Kocher A, Andreas M, Zimpfer D, Werner P.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

The prognostic impact of baseline right ventricular-pulmonary artery coupling on clinical outcomes following mitral valve surgery with specific consideration of concomitant tricuspid valve repair remains uncertain.

Methods

A total of 214 patients who underwent mitral valve surgery and presented with moderate tricuspid regurgitation at the index procedure were included. Patients were classified after baseline right ventricular-pulmonary artery coupling (impaired versus normal). The primary study end point was a composite outcome of all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization. Secondary study end points included all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization.

Results

Impaired right ventricular-pulmonary artery coupling was observed in 112 patients (52%), while 102 patients (48%) had normal right ventricular-pulmonary artery coupling. The rate of concomitant tricuspid valve repair was similar between study groups (50.0% versus 49.0%, P=0.886). Impaired right ventricular-pulmonary artery coupling was associated with a higher hazard of the composite outcome (adjusted hazard ratio 2.60, 95% CI 1.32-5.14, P=0.006), heart failure hospitalization (adjusted hazard ratio 3.29, 95% CI 1.27-8.54, P=0.014), and all-cause mortality (adjusted hazard ratio 2.25, 95% CI 1.11-4.59, P=0.025) during follow-up. Additionally, concomitant tricuspid valve repair in patients with moderate tricuspid regurgitation was associated with a lower hazard of the composite outcome (adjusted hazard ratio 0.45, 95% CI 0.26-0.80, P=0.007).

Conclusions

Impaired right ventricular-pulmonary artery coupling is a predictor of adverse outcomes after mitral valve surgery. Concomitant tricuspid valve repair for moderate tricuspid regurgitation seems to be associated with improved outcomes.

title: Adeno-Associated Virus-Induced Humanized Hypertensive Mouse Model Validates N-Acetylgalactosamine-Conjugated Small Interfering RNA Targeting Angiotensinogen as a Long-Acting Antihypertensive Therapy.
authorString: Xiong J, Zhang S, Cheng K, Sheng Y, Lin J, Liu X, Liu T, Guo X, Zhu D, Wu L, Li R, Zhang B.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

Hypertension remains a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality, yet current therapeutic strategies lack sustained efficacy and long-term stability. Our study aimed to construct a humanized rodent model for drugs development especially currently prevalent small interfering RNA medication.

Methods

A humanized hypertensive mouse model was generated by subcutaneous injection of neonatal mice with adeno-associated viruses encoding hAGT (human angiotensinogen) and hRENIN (human renin). Blood pressure was monitored weekly via tail-cuff plethysmography. Expression of hAGT and hRENIN was assessed by ELISA, Western blot, and reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction. Cardiac function was evaluated by echocardiography at 4 and 6 months postinjection. Hypertension-associated comorbidities were examined through histological analysis and ELISA. A modified N-acetylgalactosamine-conjugated small interfering RNA targeting human hepatic AGT (GalNAc-siAGT) was screened and subcutaneously administered to humanized hypertensive mice, either alone or in combination with valsartan, to evaluate therapeutic efficacy.

Results

The dual adeno-associated virus-induced humanized hypertensive model exhibited a sustained hypertension for 6 months and manifested prevalent comorbidities, including heart failure and kidney disease. This modified GalNAc-siAGT demonstrated significant activity in knocking down hAGT both in vitro and in vivo. Only a single subcutaneous injection of GalNAc-siAGT in humanized hypertensive mice led to a sustained reduction in blood pressure lasting for 2 months, accompanied by cardio- and renoprotective effects. Moreover, combining GalNAc-siAGT with the renin-angiotensin system blocker, valsartan, significantly enhanced therapeutic efficacy.

Conclusions

Our study validated the antihypertensive therapeutic effect of GalNAc-siAGT in a humanized hypertensive murine model while highlighting the translational potential of this model for clinical drug development.

title: Prevalence of hypertension and associated factors among users of the Centre Hospitalier Médico-Diététique Père Morand Kleiber in Butembo, DRC: A quantitative cross-sectional study
authorString: Mundeke B, Musavuli G, Munyambethe J, Lukulirwa L, Mwenge G, Musimbulwa R, Vutseme N, Muyisa RM, Sabuni L.
abstractText: Background Hypertension is a major public health concern, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. However, local evidence on its burden and associated factors in Eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) remains limited. This study aimed to determine the proportion of hypertension and identify its associated factors among users of the Centre Hospitalier Médico-Diététique Père Morand Kleiber in Butembo. Methods A quantitative cross-sectional study was conducted from June 2025 to May 2026 among 145 adults aged 25 years and older. Participants were selected using non-probability convenience sampling. Data on sociodemographic characteristics, behavioral factors, anthropometric measurements, blood pressure, and biochemical parameters were collected. Binary logistic regression was performed to identify factors independently associated with hypertension. Results Among the 145 participants, 65 (44.8%) were hypertensive. The proportion of hypertension increased with age, from 13.6% among participants aged 25–34 years to 80.0% among those aged 65 years and older. In multivariable analysis, abdominal obesity (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 3.1; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.7–5.8; p < 0.001), male sex (aOR = 2.1; 95% CI: 1.2–3.9; p = 0.009), current smoking (aOR = 2.1; 95% CI: 1.0–4.5; p = 0.049), sedentary lifestyle (aOR = 1.9; 95% CI: 1.1–3.5; p = 0.03), and increasing age (aOR = 1.04 per year; 95% CI: 1.01–1.07; p = 0.01) were independently associated with hypertension. Unhealthy diet and alcohol consumption were not significantly associated with hypertension after adjustment. Conclusion A high proportion of participants had hypertension, with age, male sex, abdominal obesity, smoking, and sedentary lifestyle identified as independently associated factors. Strengthening routine blood pressure screening, waist circumference assessment, and lifestyle interventions may improve hypertension prevention and management in Butembo. Larger population-based studies are needed to confirm these findings.

title: Clinical characteristics, management, and short-term outcomes of acute superior mesenteric artery embolism in a cohort with a high prevalence of cardiogenic risk factors: a single-center retrospective cohort study
authorString: Yang J, Zhao J, Li G.
abstractText: Background Acute superior mesenteric artery embolism (ASMAE) is a rare, life-threatening systemic embolism associated with cardiogenic risk factors. We described its clinical features, management, and outcomes in a single-center cohort. Methods This retrospective cohort study included 28 patients with ASMAE treated between March 2023 and March 2026. Isolated mesenteric venous thrombosis, non-occlusive mesenteric ischemia, and superior mesenteric artery dissection were excluded. All patients underwent computed tomography angiography (CTA), and operative patients had surgical or pathological confirmation. Clinical, treatment, complication, discharge, and available post-discharge follow-up data were collected. Continuous variables are reported as mean ± standard deviation and categorical variables as counts and percentages. Results We included 17 men and 11 women (mean age, 71.04 ± 9.06 years). Atrial fibrillation was present in 22 patients and valvular heart disease in 12. The proximal, middle, and distal superior mesenteric artery was involved in 7, 12, and 9 patients, respectively; 9 had concurrent infarction and 11 had peritonitis. Four patients received conservative treatment and 24 entered an operative pathway. The mean operative duration was 172.04 ± 63.02 minutes. Operations included Fogarty embolectomy alone (12), embolectomy plus bowel resection (9), bowel resection alone (1), laparotomy alone (1), and AcoStream aspiration followed by open surgery (1). Intestinal ischemia occurred in 21 patients, transmural necrosis in 14, and bowel resection with anastomosis in 10. Eleven patients were discharged against medical advice; 1 survived and 10 died after discharge (post-discharge mortality, 35.7%). Seventeen patients improved before discharge, and 1 later recovered, yielding 18 patients with a favorable short-term outcome. Five of 14 operative patients with a favorable outcome were lost to follow-up; one had residual distal embolism at 1 month. Conclusions ASMAE in patients with cardiogenic risk factors was associated with a high burden of intestinal ischemia, bowel necrosis, and post-discharge death. An open revascularization-dominant strategy enabled assessment of bowel viability and resection of nonviable intestine. These findings are descriptive, not comparative; prospective studies with standardized criteria and complete follow-up are needed.

title: Beyond Cure: Post-Treatment Survival and Health Outcomes Among Pulmonary Tuberculosis Survivors in Rural India
authorString: Rai J, Rawther SCH, Kulal R.
abstractText: Background: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a major public health challenge in India, particularly in rural areas. While successful treatment is marked by microbiological cure, many individuals continue to face long-term physical and emotional health complications. Globally and nationally, post-treatment outcomes are gaining attention due to their impact on quality of life, relapse risk, and mortality. Recognizing factors associated with survival and post-treatment health is essential for targeted follow-up and support. This study aimed to assess the post-treatment survival and health status of pulmonary tuberculosis (TB) patients and to identify factors influencing these outcomes. Methods: A retrospective descriptive design was used. The study was conducted among 200 pulmonary TB patients who had completed treatment at selected villages in Ramanagara district, Bangalore. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire covering socio-demographic details, treatment adherence, clinical variables, post-treatment survival, and health status including clinical, functional, and emotional domains. Descriptive and inferential statistics were used for analysis, including chi-square tests for associations. Results: Among the 200 patients, 96.5% were alive and 3.5% had died post-treatment. Most patients (90.7%) had optimum clinical health, 58% showed high functional ability, and 93.8% reported only mild emotional symptoms. Statistically significant associations were found between post-treatment survival and age, occupation, and income. Post-treatment health status was significantly influenced by ventilation, hypertension, smoking, and tobacco chewing. Clinical variables such as BMI and type of medication were not significantly associated with health outcomes. Conclusions : Post-treatment survival was high among pulmonary TB patients, but several continued to experience health limitations. Socio-demographic factors, comorbidities, and personal habits played a crucial role in determining long-term health outcomes. Emphasis on follow-up care, lifestyle modification, and supportive interventions is essential for improving the quality of life of TB survivors.

title: Predictors of In-Hospital Mortality among Hospitalized Adults with Diabetes Mellitus in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia: A Multicenter Prospective Cohort Study
authorString: Bahru YD, Berha AB, Ahmed A, Chelkeba L.
abstractText: Background Diabetes mellitus (DM) significantly increases the risk of adverse hospital outcomes; however, data on mortality predictors in sub-Saharan African hospital settings remain scarce. This study aimed to identify independent predictors of in-hospital mortality among DM patients admitted to three Ethiopian tertiary hospitals. Methods A multicenter prospective cohort study was conducted from July 2023 to February 2024, enrolling 398 DM adult patients. Baseline demographic, clinical and laboratory data were collected. Patients were followed from admission until discharge or death. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis with the log-rank test estimated median survival times (MST). Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression was used to identify independent predictors of mortality, with statistical significance set at p < 0.05. Results Among 398 patients (55% male, median age 60 years [IQR: 50–70]), 82.9% had Type 2 DM and 93.7% had a known history of diabetes. Hypertension (61.3%) and heart failure (37.7%) were the most prevalent comorbidities. The overall in-hospital mortality rate was 7.5% (n = 30). Kaplan-Meier analysis revealed significantly shorter MST for patients with > 3 comorbidities (p = 0.002), acute hemorrhagic stroke (MST: 23 vs. 55 days, p = 0.002), sepsis (MST: 35 vs. 90 days, p = 0.001), and hospital-acquired urinary tract infection (UTI) (MST: 25 vs. 55 days, p = 0.015). After adjustment in the multivariable Cox model, five factors remained independently associated with increased mortality: >3 comorbidities (AHR = 5.50; 95% CI: 1.96–15.40; p = 0.001), community-acquired sepsis (AHR = 7.98; 95% CI: 2.44–26.14; p = 0.001), acute hemorrhagic stroke (AHR = 4.54; 95% CI: 1.07–19.24; p = 0.040), hospital-acquired UTI (AHR = 6.87; 95% CI: 1.63–29.02; p = 0.009), and failure to achieve target blood glucose levels (AHR = 3.63; 95% CI: 1.12–11.76; p = 0.032). Conclusion In-hospital mortality in Ethiopian diabetic patients is profoundly driven by acute severe infections, cerebrovascular events, high comorbidity burden, and poor glycemic control. Early risk stratification, aggressive infection management, and strict glycemic monitoring are essential to reduce the high mortality rate in this vulnerable population.

title: The role of comorbidities in the incidence and mortality of lung cancer: a large, nationwide retrospective study based on Hungarian datasets
authorString: Farkas A, Andrási K, Takács E, Temesi G, Belicza É.
abstractText: Introduction: The mortality and overall survival of lung cancer depend on various factors. In our study, we examined the prevalence and effect on mortality of comorbidities. Method Data records from Hungarian patients diagnosed with lung cancer between 2012 and 2020 were enrolled. We examined the occurrence of comorbidities and the Charlson comorbidity index prior to lung cancer diagnosis with a matched-pairs methodology. Multivariate logistic regression assessed short- and long-term mortality, while Kaplan-Meier curves and Cox regression analyzed survival probabilities. Results 42,207 patients were enrolled. The differences in the occurrences of diabetes, arrhythmia, and renal failure were not significant between case and control groups. Anemia was moderate, cardiological conditions were significantly more frequent in the case group. Charlson index showed a less favorable risk profile in the case group. Surgical patients had significantly lower crude mortality rate. The odds of mortality are significantly increased at the 0.1% level with another primary tumor appearance, anemia, cerebrovascular disease, heart failure, arrhythmia, COPD, or pneumonia. The odds of mortality are significantly lower for patients diagnosed with hypertension or asthma (p < 0.001). Operated patients have a lower Charlson comorbidity index and better hazard ratios. Higher Charlson comorbidity category is associated with higher hazard ratio for survival. Conclusion Our study demonstrates that while high Charlson Comorbidity Index scores, COPD, heart failure, cerebrovascular disease, arrhythmia, pneumonia, and anemia increase lung cancer mortality, surgery – and surprisingly, hypertension and asthma – are linked to significantly better survival. This phenomenon should be noted for screening, diagnostic methods, and treatment choice.

title: Blood Pressure Control and Variability Reduction with Clevidipine in Hypertensive Intracerebral Hemorrhage (CLEVER-ICH): A Prospective Observational Study
authorString: Hassett C, Ahrens C, Conroy G, Li Y, Lapin B, Moseley S, Lindsay J, Nagesh AB, Gomes J.
abstractText: Background Acute systolic hypertension after spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) is associated with hematoma expansion and worse outcomes. Although rapid blood pressure lowering is recommended, the physiologic effects of clevidipine on high-frequency systolic blood pressure variability (BPV) in acute ICH remain incompletely characterized. Methods We conducted a single-center, prospective, open-label observational study of adults with spontaneous supratentorial ICH presenting within 12 hours of last known well who required continuous intravenous antihypertensive therapy. Clevidipine was initiated at 1 mg/hour and titrated to a target systolic blood pressure (SBP) of 130–160 mmHg. Beat-to-beat arterial SBP was recorded at 300 Hz after neurointensive care unit admission. Primary outcomes were descriptive measures of BPV before and after clevidipine initiation, including standard deviation, average real variability (ARV), and coefficient of variation (CV). Secondary outcomes included time to target SBP, time to control with stability, hematoma expansion, neurologic deterioration, hypotension exposure, and in-hospital mortality. Results Twenty patients were enrolled between March 2022 and February 2025. Mean age was 57.8 ± 15.4 years, 60% were female, and 70% were Black/African American. Median peak pre-enrollment SBP was 193.5 mmHg. Median time to achieve SBP 130–160 mmHg was 5.9 minutes (IQR 0.6–10.2), and median time to control with stability was 6.3 minutes (IQR 1.7–14.2). Patients remained within target SBP for a median 73.7% of infusion time. Relative hypotension (SBP < 130 mmHg) occurred during 9.6% of infusion time, whereas absolute hypotension (SBP < 90 mmHg) was rare (0.05%). Mean SBP decreased from 169.5 mmHg before infusion to 151.9 mmHg in the first hour and remained controlled through 12 hours. Standard deviation and ARV did not significantly change after clevidipine initiation, while CV increased modestly (7.1% vs 9.9%, p = 0.037). Hematoma expansion occurred in 30% and in-hospital mortality was 20%. Conclusions In acute spontaneous ICH, clevidipine provided rapid, sustained SBP control with minimal clinically significant hypotension and no clear increase in absolute short-term BPV. These findings support its feasibility and safety for intensive hyperacute blood pressure management.

title: Association Between Stroke Subtype and Outcomes of Edaravone Dexborneol: A Subgroup Analysis of the EXPAND (Effectiveness and Safety of Edaravone Dexborneol in Acute Ischemic Stroke) Study.
authorString: Ma G, Song Z, Hu J, Raynald, Firdaus M, Wang J, Qiu J, Shao Y, Xu J, Pan J, Zuo Y, Nguyen TN, Zhang Q, EXPAND investigators.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

The effectiveness of edaravone dexborneol among acute ischemic stroke subtypes remains unclear. We evaluated its association with clinical outcomes by stroke subtype.

Methods

This secondary analysis of the prospective EXPAND (Effectiveness and Safety of Edaravone Dexborneol in Acute Ischemic Stroke) study included patients with acute ischemic stroke treated at 72 Chinese stroke centers from December 2022 to October 2023. Patients were classified as having large artery atherosclerosis (LAA) or non-LAA stroke and grouped by edaravone dexborneol use. Primary outcomes were 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) scores of 0 or 1 and 0 to 2 and ordinal mRS shift. Safety outcomes were 90-day mortality, intracranial hemorrhage, and in-hospital adverse events.

Results

Among 4401 patients, 1061 (24.1%) had LAA and 3340 (75.9%) had non-LAA stroke; the median age was 65 years, and 66.8% were men. Edaravone dexborneol was associated with improved 90-day functional outcomes in the non-LAA group, including higher odds of achieving mRS 0 or 1 (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.25 [95% CI, 1.06-1.47]), mRS 0 to 2 (aOR, 1.40 [95% CI, 1.15-1.71]), and a favorable mRS shift (aOR, 1.28 [95% CI, 1.12-1.46]; all P<0.05). No significant functional benefit was observed in the LAA group of mRS 0 or 1 (aOR, 0.91; P=0.50), mRS 0 to 2 (aOR, 0.88; P=0.43), or mRS shift (aOR, 0.92; P=0.50). Significant interactions were observed between edaravone dexborneol and stroke subtype (P for interaction=0.03 for mRS 0 or 1, P=0.005 for mRS 0 to 2, and P=0.009 for favorable mRS shift). Safety outcomes were comparable between treatment groups.

Conclusions

Edaravone dexborneol was associated with improved 90-day functional outcomes in non-LAA but not LAA stroke.

title: Clinical Observation of Precision Haemodynamic Management Guided by Pulse Index Continuous Cardiac Output in Patients with Septic Cardiomyopathy.
authorString: Yuan B, Cao Y, Cao Y, Chang X, La H, Shao J, Ma X, Liu P.
abstractText: ObjectiveThis study aimed to investigate the value of pulse index continuous cardiac output (PICCO) monitoring in assessing the relationship between cardiac function, haemodynamic evolution and prognosis in patients with septic cardiomyopathy (SCM).MethodsSixty patients with SCM were categorised into normal (left ventricular ejection fraction [LVEF] ≥ 50%, n = 21) and reduced (LVEF < 50%, n = 39) cardiac function groups. Haemodynamic parameters (cardiac index [CI], global end-diastolic volume index [GEDVI], systemic vascular resistance index [SVRI], extravascular lung water index and pulmonary vascular permeability index) were dynamically monitored via PICCO at 0, 6, 12, 24, 48 and 72 h. The 21-day mortality was recorded.ResultsThe reduced group was significantly older (62.4 ± 11.9 vs 36.4 ± 8.7 years, P < .001) with higher Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II scores (P = .028) than the normal group. Their CI remained significantly lower than that of the normal group at all time points, reaching a nadir at 24 h (2.46 ± 0.62 vs 3.65 ± 1.03 L/min·m2, P < .001). Unlike the normal group, the reduced group showed a significant GEDVI rebound at 24 h (P ≤ .05). No significant difference in SVRI was found between groups (P > .05). The 28-day cumulative mortality was 38.5% in the reduced group versus 19.0% in the normal group (P = .211).ConclusionPulse index continuous cardiac output monitoring effectively identifies haemodynamic differences across SCM cardiac functions. Patients with reduced LVEF exhibit severe cardiac depression and a 24-h decompensation window. Although mortality differences were not statistically significant in this cohort, PICCO provides vital quantifiable targets for individualised management.

title: Cytokine Signatures of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Myocarditis and the Modifying Role of Clonal Hematopoiesis: A Machine-Learning and Multi-Omics Study
authorString: Manchanda N, Chehayeb RJ, Hong D, Jeyashanmugaraja A, Singh J, Cross JL, Vijayram A, Martinez CM, Jayakrishnan R, Christofides A, Lin D, Im Y, VanOudenhove J, Biancon G, Ibrahim E, Ardasheva A, Lin EYS, Levine R, Cheng E, Halene S, Hwa J, Smith N, Villani C, Zhu H, Jha A, Kwan JM.
abstractText:
Background:

Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) myocarditis affects up to 2% of patients on ICI and has up to a 50% mortality. Clonal Hematopoiesis of Indeterminate Potential (CHIP) is a risk factor for ICI myocarditis. Objectives To leverage a multi-omics approach to evaluate cytokines associated with ICI myocarditis, immunosuppression resistance, CHIP in ICI myocarditis and implicated pathways and cell type contributions. Methods 236 cardio-oncology patients were enrolled, including 88 who were on ICI. Cytokine profiling from patients on ICI were sampled and analyzed using machine learning and explainable artificial intelligence. Single-cell multi-omics of peripheral blood from Yale (n=19), Stanford (n=25), and MGH (n=63) evaluated cell-type contributions of cytokines and implicated pathways. Validation of Yale proteomic analyses was done using the Stanford CYTOF dataset. Results Top features associated with ICI myocarditis included IL13, CXCL10, PDGFA, CCL13, CCL17 and KITlg. Top KEGG pathways associated with ICI myocarditis and immunosuppression resistant ICI myocarditis included JAK STAT signaling, IL17 signaling and lipid/atherosclerosis pathways. At the single-cell level, the consensus signals distinguishing myocarditis from non-myocarditis across cohorts was predominantly driven by module-level JAK STAT, T cell, and Toll like receptor activation. Similar transcription gene programs were activated in CHIP carriers including modules implicated in the pro-inflammatory immune response, such as NF kappa B, IL17, MAPK, and TNF pathways within CHIP cells spanning lymphoid (cytotoxic CD8+ NKT, and natural killer cells) and myeloid lineages. Conclusions Across cohorts, JAK STAT signaling emerges as a convergent and potentially actionable axis in ICI myocarditis that is further amplified in CHIP carriers, supporting cytokine-guided risk stratification and JAK STAT directed immunosuppression as testable strategies.

title: Hybrid and endovascular repair of aberrant subclavian artery aneurysms and Kommerell diverticulum: single-center experience and long-term outcomes.
authorString: Bozzani A, Visciglia E, Destefanis Gallo E, Quaretti P, Cionfoli N, Arbustini E, Rossini R, Salzillo I, Arici V.
abstractText:
Background

Aberrant subclavian artery (ASA) represents the most frequent congenital anomaly of the aortic arch and may occasionally develop aneurysmal dilation (aASA) at risk of dissection or rupture. Early diagnosis and tailored management are therefore crucial. We report our long-term single-center experience with endovascular and hybrid repair of aASA and Kommerell's diverticulum (KD).

Methods

We retrospectively analyzed all consecutive patients treated for aASA between January 2010 and June 2024 at our tertiary referral center. Primary endpoints were primary technical success, perioperative and late mortality, and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Secondary endpoints included symptom evolution, reinterventions, and complications.

Results

Ten patients (5 females, 50%; mean age 62±19 years, range 16-80) were included. Seven (70%) presented with right ASA, and two (20%) with right aortic arch and left ASA. Seven patients (70%) were symptomatic; 43% had acute type B aortic dissection, 14% type A, and 28% descending thoracic aortic aneurysm. Four patients (40%) underwent total endovascular repair, and four (40%) hybrid procedures. Primary technical success was achieved in all cases, with no intraoperative deaths. Perioperative mortality was 10% and late mortality 30%. Complications included type II endoleak, access-site hematoma or infection, and transient upper-limb ischemia. No MACE occurred during the study period.

Conclusions

Hybrid and endovascular approaches appear to represent safe and effective alternatives to open repair for complex aASA anatomy when performed in experienced referral centers. Given the limited cohort size, these findings should be interpreted as descriptive and hypothesis-generating.

title: Prognostic Impact of Post-Contrast Acute Kidney Injury in Patients With Chronic Kidney Disease Undergoing Endovascular Aortic Repair.
authorString: Akabane K, Nakamura K, Kuroda Y, Mizumoto M, Hirooka S, Ochiai T, Arai S, Uchida T.

journal.title: Journal of endovascular therapy : an official journal of the International Society of Endovascular Specialists

abstractText:
Background

Post-contrast acute kidney injury (PC-AKI) has been regarded as a serious complication after contrast administration, particularly in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD). However, the prognostic significance of PC-AKI following endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) remains controversial due to heterogeneity in previous study populations. This study evaluated the association between PC-AKI and longitudinal changes in postoperative renal function and mortality in a well-defined CKD cohort undergoing EVAR.

Methods

We conducted a single-center retrospective study of patients with CKD undergoing elective, primary, and non-complex infrarenal EVAR. Patients were classified according to the presence or absence of PC-AKI. Longitudinal changes in serum creatinine after EVAR, dialysis initiation, all-cause mortality, and the association between contrast volume and PC-AKI were evaluated.

Results

Among 479 EVAR procedures, 164 patients with CKD were included, of whom 17 (10.4%) developed PC-AKI. The linear mixed-effects model showed a significant group-by-time interaction (P < .001). Serum creatinine remained significantly higher in the PC-AKI group than in the non-PC-AKI group at all postoperative time points. However, in the PC-AKI group, model-adjusted mean serum creatinine decreased significantly from 1.75 mg/dL in the postoperative period to 1.46 mg/dL at 12 months with an estimated change of -0.29 mg/dL (95% CI, -0.50 to -0.09; P = .003). No significant differences were observed in dialysis initiation (5.9% vs 0.7%; P = .197) or all-cause mortality (29.4% vs 23.8%; P = .565). Kaplan-Meier analysis showed no significant difference in overall survival between the groups (log-rank P = .246). In the multivariable analysis, contrast volume was not independently associated with PC-AKI (odds ratio [OR], 1.00; 95% CI, 0.98-1.01; P = .845), whereas lower preoperative estimated glomerular filtration rate remained significantly associated with PC-AKI (OR, 1.06 per 1 mL/min/1.73 m2 decrease; 95% CI, 1.01-1.12; P = .018).

Conclusion

In this study, PC-AKI may not necessarily be associated with adverse subsequent renal or survival outcomes. In addition, underlying renal vulnerability may be more closely associated with the development of PC-AKI than contrast volume alone. While PC-AKI should not be disregarded, judicious contrast use to ensure appropriate assessment may be reasonable even in patients with CKD.Clinical ImpactPost-contrast acute kidney injury (PC-AKI) occurred in approximately 10% of patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) undergoing elective, primary, non-complex infrarenal endovascular aortic repair (EVAR). Although serum creatinine remained higher in patients with PC-AKI at all postoperative time points, it decreased significantly from the postoperative period to 12 months. No significant differences were observed in dialysis initiation or overall survival between the groups. In addition, contrast volume was not independently associated with PC-AKI, whereas lower preoperative estimated glomerular filtration rate was. These findings suggest that contrast use should not be excessively restricted solely because of concerns regarding PC-AKI, and that judicious contrast use to ensure appropriate assessment may be reasonable even in patients with CKD.

title: Routine adjunctive porcine fibrin sealant sac embolization during emergency endovascular repair for ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm: a before-and-after cohort study
authorString: Zheng L, Lu Z, Li P, Li X, Zhao Y, Zhang L.
abstractText: Background Routine adjunctive sac embolization extends aneurysm sac management beyond endograft exclusion during emergency endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) for ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm (rAAA). We evaluated implementation of this strategy and 30-day outcomes. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 31 consecutive patients with rAAA who commenced an emergency EVAR strategy. The historical control group included 14 patients treated between 2019 and 2022; between January 2023 and June 2026, 17 patients underwent routine adjunctive porcine fibrin sealant (PFS) sac embolization. The primary outcome was 30-day postoperative all-cause mortality. We calculated the unadjusted risk difference and its 95% confidence interval. Results All 17 patients treated with PFS completed the planned embolization. Several baseline features were less favorable in the PFS era, although Edinburgh score distributions were similar between eras. Thirty-day mortality was 3/17 (17.6%) in the PFS era and 3/14 (21.4%) in the historical era. The unadjusted risk difference was − 3.8 percentage points (95% confidence interval: -32.3 to 23.4). No nontarget embolization was recorded. Two additional rupture-related deaths occurred in the PFS era beyond 30 days. Conclusions Routine adjunctive PFS sac embolization was feasible within this center's emergency EVAR workflow. This consecutive rAAA cohort provides a clinical basis for prospective controlled evaluation of the strategy and its perioperative outcomes.

title: Institutional Variation in Electroencephalography Utilization in Neonates With Complex Congenital Heart Disease Across the United States and Its Association With Outcomes.
authorString: Aly S, Elsisy MF, Qattea I, Newburger JW, Aly HZ.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

Neonates with complex congenital heart disease are at increased risk for perioperative brain injury and seizures. Electroencephalography (EEG) detects clinical and subclinical seizures, but national utilization patterns remain poorly characterized.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the Pediatric Health Information System (2016-2025) of neonates ≤28 days with dextro-transposition of the great arteries or single-ventricle physiology undergoing surgical repair or palliation. Mixed-effects logistic regression with hospital as a random effect identified predictors of EEG utilization.

Results

Among 13 202 neonates, 1654 (12.5%) underwent EEG monitoring. EEG monitoring was performed in only 10.8% of neonates with dextro-transposition of the great arteries, 16% of those with hypoplastic left heart syndrome, and 13% of those with non- hypoplastic left heart syndrome single-ventricle lesions. EEG utilization increased from ~6% in 2016 to >14% in 2025, while seizure detection among EEG-monitored patients increased from 13% to ~26% (both P-trend<0.01). Utilization varied substantially across hospitals (0% to >40%), persisting after adjustment for surgical volume. EEG-monitored neonates had higher seizure detection (21.8% versus 5.2%), longer length of stay (33 versus 24 days), and higher hospitalization costs ($344 719 versus $174 865; all P<0.01). In multivariable analysis, EEG utilization was independently associated with seizures (OR ~4), dextro-transposition of the great arteries, and hypoplastic left heart syndrome, but not with cardiac arrest, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, or hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy.

Conclusions

EEG utilization in neonates with complex congenital heart disease is increasing but remains low and highly variable across US centers. The association of EEG use with higher mortality and costs may reflect confounding by indication or illness severity. Standardized protocols are needed to optimize neurologic monitoring and improve long-term outcomes.

title: Association of maternal gestational exposures and child/family characteristics with non-PFO congenital heart disease in children: a multicenter retrospective case-control study
authorString: Wang H, Li W, Alifu A, Wu S, Lin S, He J, Lin S, Chen R.
abstractText: Background Congenital heart disease (CHD) is a major cause of infant morbidity and mortality. Previous studies often combined patent foramen ovale (PFO) with structural cardiac malformations, potentially increasing phenotypic heterogeneity. Objectives To identify maternal gestational exposures and child/family characteristics associated with non-PFO CHD and develop a preliminary prediction model. Methods This multicenter retrospective case-control study included 208 children from Hainan Province: 130 with non-PFO CHD and 78 with PFO. Fifty-five candidate variables were assessed. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression was used for feature selection, followed by five machine learning models. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis was used to interpret feature importance, and a nomogram was constructed. Results LASSO selected eight features, of which seven had nonzero global SHAP importance: child age in months, maternal protein intake frequency during pregnancy, history of CHD in other offspring, folic acid supplementation, frequency of family conflicts during pregnancy, maternal preconception smoking, and first-trimester hazardous substance exposure. Linear discriminant analysis (LDA) showed the best test-set performance, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.702 and a Brier score of 0.232. The nomogram achieved an AUC of 0.732, and decision curve analysis indicated potential net benefit across the evaluated threshold range. Conclusions Candidate predictors associated with non-PFO CHD were identified, and an internally evaluated nomogram was developed for preliminary risk stratification. External validation is required before clinical use.

title: Advancing Health Equity Through Community Ownership, Small-Scale Built Modification, and Meaningful Engagement: the JUMP Initiative.
authorString: Wu H, Ruaño G, Ajibola TF, Slivinsky M, Rohithkumar K, Cagganello M, Grady JJ, Laurencin CT.

journal.title: Journal of racial and ethnic health disparities

abstractText:
Issue

Chronic diseases like diabetes, hypertension, and cardiovascular disease are among the main causes of illness and death in the United States, and they hit Black and Hispanic communities especially hard. Food insecurity and limited access to nutritious foods play a major role in these disparities by making healthy eating and exercise harder and reducing the effectiveness of disease prevention efforts. Although lifestyle interventions are often used to address chronic disease, they usually depend on education or individual counseling and often do not address the bigger social and structural factors that shape people's choices.

Description

The Just Us Moving Program (JUMP) was designed to fill these gaps through a connected, community-engaged approach to sustainable health promotion in food-insecure communities. JUMP incorporates small-scale, community-driven change within trusted community settings, culturally responsive lifestyle education, immersive educational experiences, train-the-trainer capacity-building, and ongoing community work. The approach to JUMP is based on an integrated conceptual framework that includes community-based participatory research (CBPR), the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR), and the Assessing Community Engagement (ACE) framework. Core program components include community aeroponic gardens, experiential and community-based learning activities, SMART goal-setting, motivational interviewing, and iterative community feedback processes.

Lessons learned

Current evidence applicable to JUMP is formative and derived from early research, community engagement, and pilot studies rather than a formal effectiveness trial. Formative evidence from pilot activities and community outreach suggested interest in lifestyle change, relevance of structural food access supports, and the importance of trust-building, long-term partnership, cultural responsiveness, shared stewardship, and ongoing community involvement. Current findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and encouraging for next-phase implementation and assessment rather than conclusive proof of impact.

Conclusion

JUMP represents a theory-informed, community-engaged model for sustainable health promotion in food-insecure communities. The initiative integrates structural supports, culturally responsive education, implementation science, and meaningful community engagement within a community-rooted framework intended to support future evaluation of sustainability, community ownership, implementation outcomes, and health-related impacts over time.

title: Covert brain infarction in the emergency department: incidence and outcomes.
authorString: Ferguson E, Leafloor C, Hodgins C, Maher J, Perry JJ.
abstractText:
Objectives

Covert brain infarction (CBI) is defined by neuroimaging evidence of cerebral infarction without history of stroke or transient ischemic attack (TIA). The prevalence and management of covert brain infarction in the emergency department (ED) is not well understood. This study aimed to examine the prevalence, management, and one-year outcomes of patients with covert brain infarction detected during ED neuroimaging for non-stroke or TIA reasons.

Methods

This retrospective observational cohort study included ED patients from two academic hospitals with 24/7 access to computed tomography (CT). The primary outcome was detection of covert brain infarction on CT; secondary outcomes included stroke prevention therapy initiation or modification, specialist referral, and one-year adverse outcomes. Eligible patients were 50 years or older without history of stroke, TIA, or intracranial hemorrhage, who underwent CT in the ED for reasons unrelated to stroke or TIA from January 1 to December 31, 2022. Exclusion criteria included evidence of intracranial hemorrhage or final ED diagnosis of stroke/TIA.

Results

Of 6,535 eligible individuals, a total of 102 patients (1.6%) had covert brain infarction detected on neuroimaging. These patients (age: 78.5 ±10.7 years; 61% male) had substantial vascular risk factors, including hypertension (62.7%), dyslipidemia (45.1%), atrial fibrillation (26.5%), diabetes (20.6%), and smoking (41.2%). Prior to ED visit, 18.6% of patients were on antiplatelets and 23.5% were on anticoagulation. Among those with covert brain infarction discharged from the ED, 91.7% received no change in therapy. In one year after the index visit, 1 patient had a stroke/TIA (1.0%), 4 had a myocardial infarction (3.9%), 2 were diagnosed with new atrial fibrillation (2.0%), and 14 died (13.7%).

Conclusion

Patients with covert brain infarction detected in the ED had multiple vascular risk factors, and ED physician initiation or modification of new stroke therapy was uncommon, underscoring the need for further characterization and ED-specific pathways for management of this population.

title: PARP1 deficiency induces aging-associated cardiac failure via activation of Akt signalling.
authorString: Sumi TS, Mishra S, Shrama A, Chowdhury A, Shivanaiah B, Davis D, Nagesh D, Francis F, Roy S, Munjal A, Bhelave AY, Somasundaram K, Nair D, Sundaresan NR.
abstractText: PARP1, a major poly-ADP-ribose transferase, plays a critical role in maintaining genomic stability, transcription, cellular energy metabolism, and cell death. In the heart, PARP1 inhibition protects cardiomyocytes against oxidative and genotoxic stress and attenuates ischemia-reperfusion injury caused by myocardial infarction. However, the role of PARP1 in aging-associated heart failure remains unexplored. In this study, we demonstrate the crucial role of PARP1 in regulating aging-associated cardiac remodelling and failure. The levels of PARP1 are down-regulated in aging mouse hearts, and PARP1 deficiency induces aging-related cardiac remodelling and contractile dysfunction in mice. The RNA-seq analysis revealed hyperactivation of Akt signalling, a major signalling pathway involved in aging, in PARP1-deficient hearts. In the heart, PARP1 deficiency spontaneously activates the Akt signalling pathway, leading to the development of aging-related cardiac hypertrophy and failure. Our findings reveal two distinct mechanisms by which PARP1 regulates Akt signalling, involving the direct interaction of PARP1 with Akt and the transcriptional regulation of phosphatases, including the expression of PTEN by PARP1. Mechanistically, PARP1 binds to the PTEN promoter and might transcriptionally promote its expression. In addition, PARP1 binds and inhibits Akt by poly-ADP-ribosylating Akt at the PH domain, which impairs Akt plasma membrane recruitment and subsequent activation. Inhibition of Akt reversed hypertrophy in PARP1-depleted cardiomyocytes and improved the contractile dysfunction in PARP1-deficient hearts. These findings reveal a previously unrecognized regulatory role for PARP1 in aging-associated cardiac failure.

title: Efficacy of SGLT2 inhibitors in pulmonary arterial hypertension: a systematic review and meta-analysis of preclinical studies.
authorString: Qubbaj FB, Saeed AE, Younis OM, Al-Awamleh N, Al-Sharif Z, Shaban Q, Sulaiman S, Turk AZ.

title: Effects of shared decision-making aids for anticoagulation in atrial fibrillation: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authorString: Zhang W, Shen Y, Tao ZH, Guo YQ.

title: Trends in Outcomes and Regional Rates of Pulmonary Thromboendarterectomy: A National Analysis.
authorString: Chiu SF, Romary DJ, Logan CD, Baldridge AS, Chowdhury R, An S, Kruse J, Schimmel DR, Freed BH, Raza Y, Samant M, Mylvaganam R, Cuttica MJ, Malaisrie SC.
abstractText:
Background

Pulmonary thromboendarterectomy (PTE) is the guideline-recommended treatment for chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH). Here, we report modern-era national-level outcomes and identify regions that lack access to PTE.

Methods

The STS Adult Cardiac Surgery Database was queried from 2012 to 2024 for patients in the USA who underwent PTE with circulatory arrest for chronic disease. Patient characteristics, region, travel distance, area deprivation index (ADI), temporal trends (2012-2018 vs 2019-2024), and center volume (≤15/year vs >15/year) were described and evaluated for association with 30-day mortality. Multivariable logistic regression was conducted, reported as adjusted odds ratios (aORs).

Results

Over the study period, 4,101 PTEs were performed; 1,238 in 2012-2018 and 2,863 in 2019-2024. Between the two periods, 25 centers closed and 35 centers opened. Higher volume centers (>15 PTE/ year) had significantly lower 30-day post-operative mortality rates compared to lower-volume centers (2.6% vs. 5.5%, p<0.001) including after adjustment for preoperative characteristics, ADI, and patient travel distance, low center volume (aOR=1.81, p<0.001). Patients from the Mountain and Great Lakes regions had the highest rate of PTE, while patients from the East South Central region appeared to have disparately low access to PTE.

Conclusions

The volume-outcome relationship for 30-day mortality after PTE persists over time and there is regional variation in rates of PTE. Development of regional centers of excellence is imperative to ensure access to high-quality CTEPH treatment.

title: Disruptions in U.S. Heart Transplantation: When Innovation Outpaces Evidence.
authorString: Goldstein DJ, Kanwar MK.

journal.title: The Journal of heart and lung transplantation : the official publication of the International Society for Heart Transplantation

abstractText: For nearly four decades, heart transplantation was defined by a stable, predictable paradigm: brain-dead donors, ice-cooler transport, uniform three-drug immunosuppression, and biopsy-based surveillance. Within a few years, that paradigm has been upended. In this perspective, we examine the disruptions now reshaping heart transplantation in the United States. Some are desirable: new preservation platforms and the rapid growth of donation after circulatory death, which now accounts for nearly a quarter of U.S. heart transplants, have expanded the donor pool, and cardiac xenotransplantation has reached clinical testing. Others remain controversial: the 2018 allocation policy has altered listing and support practices, normothermic regional perfusion raises unresolved questions about the determination of death, and inconsistent definitions of ischemic intervals undermine comparisons across DCD studies. Still others are troubling: OPTN restructuring, uneven OPO performance, outsourced procurement, rising costs, and press reports of donors showing signs of life have strained public trust. Underlying all of these is a data gap: national registries capture few DCD procurement and preservation variables, and little about recipients' long-term health beyond survival. Innovation has outpaced our ability to evaluate its consequences. We propose a shared DCD clock built on fixed timestamps, national ethical standards for normothermic regional perfusion, transparency in procurement and its costs, longitudinal outcome reporting, and accountability shared by OPOs and transplant centers. The challenge facing the field is no longer simply how to transplant more hearts, but how to ensure that more transplantation becomes better transplantation.

title: Management of Orthostatic Hypotension in Hospitalised Patients: Empirical Evidence, Expert Opinion, and Open Questions.
authorString: Polmann M, Berlot AA, Lipsitz LA, Freeman RL, Juraschek SP, Wagner BA.
abstractText: Orthostatic hypotension (OH) is prevalent yet underappreciated among hospitalised adults, affecting more than two-thirds of older inpatients and carrying a considerable burden of falls, cardiovascular events, mortality, prolonged hospitalisations, and readmissions. This article presents practical frameworks for inpatient OH evaluation and management. Standardised measurement protocols and a systematic diagnostic approach aid in identifying neurogenic and non-neurogenic causes. Medication review and nonpharmacological interventions-including fluid administration, behavioural modifications, compression garments, and graduated mobilisation-form the cornerstones of management. Pharmacotherapy should be reserved for refractory cases, guided by autonomic phenotype and side-effect profiles. Coexistent supine hypertension warrants careful consideration. Disposition planning, patient education, and structured follow-up are essential components of care. Important knowledge gaps persist: inpatient OH phenotypes are incompletely characterised, evidence for inpatient interventions is sparse, and validated discharge frameworks are lacking. Greater clinical awareness and translational research are needed to improve outcomes for this vulnerable population.

title: Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation in Infants With Omphalocele: A Contemporary ELSO Registry Analysis.
authorString: Giron A, Joachim A, Wilhelm S, Fan W, Jiang L, Odegaard A, Guner YS, Yu PT.
abstractText:
Background

Omphalocele is a rare congenital abdominal wall defect frequently associated with pulmonary hypoplasia, pulmonary hypertension, congenital heart disease, and severe respiratory failure. Infants with omphalocele requiring extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) represent a high-risk population; however, contemporary multicenter data evaluating survival and predictors of mortality remain limited. We aimed to characterize outcomes and identify factors associated with mortality among infants with omphalocele requiring ECMO.

Methods

We performed a retrospective cohort study using the Extracorporeal Life Support Organization Registry from 2000-2025. Demographic, clinical, ECMO-related, and complication variables were compared between survivors and non-survivors, and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression was performed to identify independent predictors of mortality.

Results

88 infants with omphalocele requiring ECMO were identified, with 41% overall survival to hospital discharge. On bivariate analysis, cannulation at <28 days of age (p=0.048) and female sex (p=0.047) were associated with mortality. ECMO-related complications occurred in 70% of patients and were associated with decreased survival probability. On multivariable analysis, the presence of any ECMO-related complication remained independently associated with mortality (HR 2.33, 95% CI 1.23-4.34, p=0.009). When compared to congenital lung malformations and congenital diaphragmatic hernia, omphalocele ECMO cases demonstrated a more pronounced increase in frequency over time.

Conclusion

Infants with omphalocele requiring ECMO experience substantial mortality despite advances in neonatal and ECMO care. ECMO-related complications were independently associated with mortality. These findings add to risk stratification and multidisciplinary perinatal planning for this population. Further studies evaluating long-term outcomes and optimal patient selection are needed.

Level of evidence

Level III (Retrospective Cohort Study.

title: Gender and Racial Disparities in Patients with Portopulmonary Hypertension: A Three-Year National Inpatient Sample Analysis.
authorString: Abdullah KM, Feghali EJ, Sanchez-Ato L, Jain A, Iqbal H, Roytman M, Sahay S.
abstractText:
Background

Portopulmonary hypertension (POPH) carries a poor prognosis, yet the influence of gender and race on inpatient outcomes is not well defined. Prior registry data suggested that POPH occurred more frequently in Hispanic patients and was associated with higher all-cause mortality. We examined whether gender and race were associated with inpatient outcomes in POPH hospitalizations.

Methods

We analyzed the 2017-2019 National Inpatient Sample. Adult hospitalizations carrying concurrent Group 1 pulmonary arterial hypertension and portal hypertension codes were identified using the International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision. Multivariable logistic and linear regression models estimated the independent association of gender and race with in-hospital mortality, length of stay, total hospital charges, shock, and sepsis.

Results

We identified a weighted total of 36,090 POPH hospitalizations. After multivariable adjustment, neither gender nor race was independently associated with in-hospital mortality, length of stay, shock, or sepsis. The only significant disparity was in total hospital charges, which were higher among Hispanic than White patients (adjusted difference $17,585; 95% CI $2015-$33,155; p = 0.027).

Conclusions

In this contemporary national cohort, gender and race were not independently associated with in-hospital mortality or major complications in POPH, in contrast to prior reports. The higher hospital charges observed for Hispanic patients, in the absence of differences in clinical outcomes, warrant further study of resource utilization and access to care.

title: Addressing health-related social needs and providing care coordination for patients with cardiovascular disease.
authorString: Rayborn LM, Fish H, Estes J, Nazar C, Galdo JA, Brown M.

journal.title: Journal of the American Pharmacists Association : JAPhA

abstractText:
Background

Rural communities in the U.S. Stroke Belt experience disproportionately high rates of cardiovascular disease and stroke, compounded by limited access to preventive care and unmet health-related social needs (HRSNs). Community pharmacies, supported by pharmacy-based community health workers (PCHWs), offer an accessible, team-based model for cardiovascular risk screening, transitions-of-care support, and longitudinal care coordination to improve population health in underserved communities.

Objective

The primary objective of this study was to evaluate the implementation of a pharmacy-based cardiovascular disease screening and care coordination program across rural community pharmacies participating in CPESN Community Health. Secondary objectives were to describe patient characteristics, screening activities, identified HRSNs, and care coordination services provided by rural pharmacies supported by pharmacy-based community health workers.

Methods

This retrospective program evaluation included data from 25 rural community pharmacies participating in a multi-state cardiovascular disease screening initiative. Pharmacy teams, consisting of pharmacists and PCHWs, documented patient encounters using the Pharmacist eCare Plan data standard. Program data were analyzed descriptively to characterize implementation, patient reach, cardiovascular screening activities, transitions-of-care interventions, HRSN screening, and referrals generated during routine care.

Results

The 25 pharmacies included in the program were from six states and employed 111 PCHWs. 11,188 encounters were logged for 9820 patients in 694 different zip codes, documenting 9,845 American Heart Association (AHA) stroke screenings, 2,434 atrial fibrillation screenings, 8,207 HRSN screenings, and 195 TOC screenings.

Conclusion

Community pharmacies have a critical role in access to screenings that are needed, especially for those who are in rural, socially vulnerable communities. CHWs on the pharmacy team can increase the opportunity to identify and assist with the execution and operation of these services.

title: The PELICANS Registry: Peripartum Cardiomyopathy Extended Longitudinal Investigation of Clinical Outcomes-Adverse Events, Nonrecovery, and Survival.
authorString: Santana AUL, Singh M, Pachariyanon P, Bogabathina H, Jaisingh K, Vyas R, Speakes N, Voshburg J, Modi M, Vutukuri NM, Bhoite GR, Modi K.
abstractText:
Background

Peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM) disproportionately affects Black women, yet long-term outcome data in socially vulnerable, predominantly Black cohorts remain limited.

Objectives

The purpose of this study was to characterize long-term outcomes and baseline predictors of survival, major adverse events (MAEs), and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) recovery in a U.S. PPCM cohort.

Methods

This retrospective-prospective registry included 159 women with PPCM (1982-2024). Primary outcomes were all-cause mortality, MAEs, and LVEF recovery (≥50%). Multivariable and extended Cox models evaluated predictors, adjusting for LVEF recovery and subsequent pregnancy.

Results

The cohort was 80.5% Black. Over a median 9.0-year follow-up (IQR: 3.4-15.5), 41 patients (25.8%) died and 64 (40.3%) had MAEs. Among 148 patients with echocardiographic follow-up, 69 (46.6%) had sustained LVEF recovery, though 23 (25.0% of initially recovered) declined to LVEF <50%. Independent mortality predictors included elevated creatinine (adjusted HR [aHR]: 2.86; 95% CI: 1.37-5.97), lower index LVEF (aHR: 0.94; 95% CI: 0.90-0.98), family history of cardiomyopathy or heart failure (aHR: 3.27; 95% CI: 1.41-7.56), and non-O blood type (aHR: 2.36; 95% CI: 1.04-5.33), retaining significance after adjusting for LVEF recovery and subsequent pregnancy (n = 62). Elevated creatinine increased MAE odds (adjusted OR: 7.09; 95% CI: 1.98-32.9), while higher LVEF, parity, and obesity reduced them. Baseline LV dilation (≥60 mm), Black race, older age, and family history of cardiomyopathy or heart failure predicted lower LVEF recovery odds.

Conclusions

This long-term predominantly Black PPCM cohort had high mortality, low LVEF recovery, and frequent late relapse. These findings highlight the importance of baseline risk stratification and sustained echocardiographic surveillance to guide clinical decision-making.

title: Outcomes of elderly hospitalized patients with influenza after the COVID-19 pandemic: decline of functional independence and frailty.
authorString: Ishida T, Ito A, Nakanishi Y, Tateda K, Fujita J, Izumikawa K, Nagai H, Seki M.
abstractText:
Background

Influenza remains a heavy burden to the elderly and the situation has been affected by the COVID-19 pandemic. The objective of this study was to clarify outcomes of elderly hospitalized patients with influenza after the COVID-19 pandemic.

Methods

The clinical data of patients 65 years of age or older who were severely ill with influenza and required hospitalization in one center were gathered between September 2023 and March 2026 (3 influenza seasons after the COVID-19 pandemic). The outcomes, functional independence, and frailty of them were analyzed.

Results

A total of 210 elderly patients were enrolled. The median age was 79 and 32 cases were judged as having mild or more frailty by the clinical frailty scale (CFS) before admission. Pneumonia was the most common disease indicated as cause for hospitalization, followed by a poor general condition and heart failure. The median duration of hospitalization was 13 days and in-hospital deaths were recorded for 17 patients (8.1%). Sixty cases changed hospital due to further treatment or deterioration of activity of daily living, and the functional independence measure (FIM) of 37 cases (17.6%) remained under a score of 70 even after rehabilitation. The CFSs worsened in 19 cases (9.0%) at the time of discharge.

Conclusions
