title: Genetic primary adrenal insufficiency in children: a narrative review.
authorString: Dai L, Bao Y, Hu L.
abstractText:
Background and objective

Pediatric primary adrenal insufficiency (PAI) beyond common 21-hydroxylase deficiency comprises rare monogenic disorders affecting adrenal development, steroidogenesis, adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) signaling, or cellular stress responses. Clinical overlap is substantial, but associated features such as disorders of sex development, hypogonadism, alacrima and achalasia, neurologic disease, growth restriction, or immunodeficiency can guide etiologic testing. This review summarizes the molecular basis, genotype-phenotype relationships, diagnostic approach, and emerging therapies for these disorders.

Methods

Literature from 2015 to 2025 was retrieved from PubMed using keywords: pediatric adrenal insufficiency; non-congenital adrenal hyperplasia; monogenic endocrine disorders; steroidogenesis; next-generation sequencing. Papers were filtered by pre-set inclusion and exclusion criteria. This review synthesizes current diagnostic algorithms, highlighting the critical integration of baseline biochemical profiling with high-throughput next-generation sequencing (NGS) and whole-exome sequencing (WES) to achieve precise molecular characterization and mitigate missed diagnoses.

Key content and findings

Severe loss-of-function variants in genes required for adrenal development or steroidogenesis generally present early with combined glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid deficiency, whereas hypomorphic variants may cause later-onset or isolated glucocorticoid deficiency. Extra-adrenal findings narrow the differential diagnosis and should determine the first genes analyzed. Biochemical phenotyping remains essential, but targeted panels or WES improve diagnostic yield when presentations overlap. Hormone replacement prevents mortality but does not reproduce physiologic cortisol exposure or treat the neurologic, reproductive, or immune components of syndromic disease.

Conclusions

Diagnosis should integrate the age at onset, pattern of steroid deficiency, associated phenotype, and molecular testing rather than rely on a single clinical feature. Current limitations include incomplete genotype-phenotype prediction, variants of uncertain significance, uneven access to functional testing, and limited pediatric outcome data for modified-release or infusion-based hydrocortisone. Near-term priorities are prospective registries, standardized variant interpretation, and genotype-stratified studies. Gene editing, gene replacement, and cell-based adrenal restoration remain experimental and should be matched to the affected tissue and mutation mechanism; hematopoietic transplantation can treat selected immune or neurologic complications but does not restore adrenal steroidogenesis.

title: Risk factors and day-14 prediction models for bronchopulmonary dysplasia and coexisting retinopathy of prematurity in very-low-birth-weight or very preterm infants.
authorString: Fan Y, Ge H, Li S, Han X, Huang X, Wu W, Wang Y, Zhang Y, Liu J, Zou L, Ren C, Li H.
abstractText:
Background

Bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) and retinopathy of prematurity (ROP) share developmental, oxygen-related, and inflammatory susceptibility. We examined factors associated with BPD and with ROP among infants with BPD and developed prediction models restricted to information available by postnatal day 14.

Methods

This retrospective two-center study included 437 infants born before 32 weeks of gestation or weighing less than 1,500 g at birth. Conventional logistic regression evaluated mutually adjusted associations. For prediction, 15 prespecified variables available by day 14 were entered into elastic-net logistic regression. Preprocessing and hyperparameter selection were confined to the training data after an outcome-stratified 8:2 split. The classification threshold was selected from training-set out-of-fold predictions; the held-out test set was used once. Discrimination, calibration, Brier score, and repeated nested cross-validation were assessed.

Results

Among 437 infants, 172 (39.4%) had BPD; among those with BPD, 89 of 172 (51.7%) had ROP. In the association analysis, lower gestational age, longer invasive ventilation and oxygen therapy, and later first feeding were associated with BPD. Among infants with BPD, longer cumulative respiratory support, lower platelet distribution width (PDW) at 24 hours and day 14, male sex, and shorter birth length were associated with ROP. The day-14 BPD model yielded a held-out area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.789 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.688-0.880], a Brier score of 0.199, and an accuracy of 0.739. The ROP model yielded an AUC of 0.690 (95% CI: 0.500-0.859), a Brier score of 0.235, and an accuracy of 0.629. Mean AUCs across repeated nested cross-validation were 0.846 and 0.752, respectively.

Conclusions

Routinely available information through day 14 provided moderate internal discrimination for BPD and for ROP among infants with BPD. The models define a transparent prediction landmark and avoid use of later cumulative treatment variables, but require external and prospective validation before clinical use.

title: Mitral annular disjunction associated with myxomatous mitral valve disease, infundibular pulmonic stenosis and ventricular septal defect in a dog: a case report.
authorString: Tavares LCJ, Santos BA, Goldfeder GT.

journal.title: Journal of veterinary cardiology : the official journal of the European Society of Veterinary Cardiology

abstractText: Mitral annular disjunction is an abnormality of the mitral valve characterized by a displacement of the mitral annulus in which the annulus is functionally decoupled from the left ventricle and moves toward the atrium during systole. In human medicine, it is commonly associated with an increased risk of mitral valve prolapse, cardiac arrhythmias, and sudden cardiac death but rarely described in veterinary medicine. This article describes a case report of a six-year-old male Shih tzu dog with signs of frequent syncope episodes diagnosed by echocardiography with mitral annular disjunction associated with myxomatous mitral valve disease, infundibular pulmonic stenosis, and perimembranous ventricular septal defect with bidirectional shunting. Due to the patient's congenital heart defects, clinical signs, and laboratory results, the hemodynamic profile was determined to be functionally analogous to the Tetralogy of Fallot. Conservative drug therapy with β-blocker propranolol was chosen rather than a surgical approach. Short-term follow-up showed initial improvement of clinical signs, followed by progressive worsening. The total survival time was 19 months from the initial diagnosis and the conservative palliative therapy. To the authors' knowledge, this is the first report of mitral annular disjunction associated with congenital abnormalities in dogs.

title: [Long-term Outcomes and Treatment Strategies for Minimally Invasive Mitral Valve Repair].
authorString: Yamamoto M, Hiraoka A, Totsugawa T, Sakaguchi T.

journal.title: Kyobu geka. The Japanese journal of thoracic surgery

abstractText: We have actively adopted minimally invasive mitral valve plasty (MICS-MVP) since the early phase of its introduction. Between October 2012 and March 2021, we performed MICS-MVP in 264 patients with degenerative mitral regurgitation. The mean age was 58.5 (range, 18~82) years;104 patients (39 %) were female, and 60 patients had concomitant atrial fibrillation. Concomitant procedures were performed in 150 patients, including tricuspid valve surgery in 56 patients, arrhythmia surgery in 59, left atrial appendage procedures in 58, and congenital heart disease surgery in 39. The mean operative time was 254 minutes. Regarding repair techniques, artificial chordae were used in 139 cases;annuloplasty was performed using a full ring in 101 cases and a partial band in 162 cases. The 5-year survival rate was 98.1%, and the 5-year freedom from major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) was 92.8%. There were no cardiac deaths, and 7 readmissions for heart failure. Compared with the fullring group, the partial-band group showed a significantly lower mean mitral valve pressure gradient (p<0.001). By multivariable analysis for MACCE incidence and readmission for heart failure, none of the factors-including surgical technique and choice of annuloplasty device-were detected as significant predictors. In recent years, annuloplasty with partial band and artificial chordae has become our standard procedure to prevent functional mitral stenosis. Further standardization of surgical techniques may contribute to improve long-term outcomes.

title: Harmony™ Valve Implantation in the Right Pulmonary Artery in a Patient with Repaired Tetralogy of Fallot and Left Pulmonary Artery Occlusion: A Case Report.
authorString: Yabusaki M, Hasegawa S, Nakano S, Kojima T.
abstractText:
Transcatheter pulmonary valve implantation using the Harmony™ valve (Medtronic, Minneapolis, MN, USA) has expanded treatment options for pulmonary regurgitation in patients with enlarged right ventricular outflow tracts. However, complex pulmonary artery anatomy may preclude standard implantation in the main pulmonary artery. We report a 41-year-old woman with repaired tetralogy of Fallot and complete left pulmonary artery occlusion who developed severe pulmonary regurgitation and advanced biventricular dysfunction. Implantation in the main pulmonary artery was not feasible because of unfavorable anatomy and a significant pressure gradient. A 25-mm Harmony™ valve was therefore successfully implanted in the proximal right pulmonary artery, preserving branch perfusion and without creating additional pressure gradients. The patient's clinical condition stabilized without procedural complications. This case suggests that right pulmonary artery implantation of the Harmony™ valve may be a viable alternative in carefully selected patients with unilateral pulmonary artery occlusion when standard implantation is not feasible.

Learning objectives

This case highlights that the Harmony™ valve can be implanted in the proximal right pulmonary artery when standard main pulmonary artery implantation is not feasible. In patients with complex pulmonary artery anatomy, careful anatomical and hemodynamic assessment may enable alternative implantation strategies that preserve branch perfusion without creating additional pressure gradients.

title: Feasibility and acceptability of prenatal parental palliative care in congenital heart disease: a pilot study.
authorString: Hock KM, Dodenhoff E, Clark MG, Patrician PA, Landier W, Rice M, Shan L.
abstractText:
Background

Ductal dependent congenital heart disease (ddCHD) is associated with significant parental anxiety, yet palliative care (PC) support is rarely offered in the prenatal period. While prior studies have evaluated PC postnatally, little is known about feasibility and acceptability of prenatal PC interventions for this population. The purpose of this study is to assess feasibility and acceptability of prenatal PC support sessions (PCSS) for parents whose fetus has been diagnosed with ddCHD requiring neonatal cardiac intervention.

Methods

This prospective single-center feasibility study enrolled English-speaking parents referred to a pediatric cardiology clinic after fetal echocardiographic diagnosis of ddCHD. Eligible participants were offered monthly prenatal PCSS, in person or via videoconference, led by a dual-certified pediatric critical care and hospice/palliative medicine physician. Feasibility was defined as ≥75% session attendance and very/extremely easy scheduling and attendance ratings; acceptability was defined as ≥75% satisfied/very satisfied ratings.

Results

Of 26 eligible parents, 15 (58%) (10 mothers, 5 fathers) consented to participate. Sixteen sessions were scheduled; 14 (87.5%) were attended, with median duration of 42 min. Most sessions (75%) occurred via videoconference. Thirteen participants (86.7%) rated scheduling and attendance as "very easy" or "extremely easy." All attendees rated the sessions as "satisfied" or "very satisfied."

Conclusion

Prenatal PC support for families facing a ddCHD diagnosis may be feasible and acceptable, with high rates of participation and satisfaction at a single tertiary care hospital. Larger, multi-center studies are warranted to assess outcomes and develop sustainable models for integrating prenatal PC into congenital heart disease care pathways.

title: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation in pediatric cardiac surgery: retrospective survival analysis.
authorString: Abdelrehim AR, Elhady M, Alnajjar AA, Allugmani M, Benouadah D, Sabtirul M, Wally A, Alothmali A, Qawalh A, Elsayed MS, Alabsi FA, Elderie A, Alashwal M, Al-Muhaya MA, Salem SS.
abstractText:
Background

Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is a life-saving therapeutic modality in children. Outcome is multifactorial with debates regarding predictors of weaning success and mortality.

Objective

To explore predictors of ECMO outcome in children with surgically corrected congenital heart disease (CHD).

Method

This single-center retrospective cohort study included children with operated CHD who were admitted to a tertiary-care cardiac center in Saudi Arabia during 2022-2025. Demographic data, clinical characteristics, as well as operative and ECMO details were recorded. Predictors of weaning failure and overall mortality during follow-up were analyzed.

Results

Thirty children aged 15 days to 12.8 years were included. ECMO connection was applied in day zero in 23 patients (76.6%). ECMO duration ranged between 1 and 15 days. Successful ECMO weaning was achieved in 56.7%. ECMO complication included renal injury in 36.7%, neurological complications in 16.7% and wound infection in 10%. The overall mortality rate was 46.7%. Residual cardiac lesions (OR 20; 95%CI:2.037-196.37 and OR 25.6; 95%CI:2.544-257.566) and ECMO complication (OR 5.4; 95%CI:1.12-26.044 and OR 7.5.6; 95%CI:1.484-37.905) were associated with ECMO failure and mortality during follow-up.

Conclusion

Residual cardiac lesions and ECMO-related complications were associated with poor outcome in children with surgically corrected CHD who require ECMO. The complexity of cardiac surgery and delayed initiation of ECMO are associated with prolonged ECMO stay duration. Proper timing of ECMO Initiation may reduce complications and improve survival.

title: Impact of timing on outcomes following redo-sternotomy after initial CABG or valvular surgery.
authorString: Yan J, McKinnerney J, Al Janabi T, Vranian MN, Kashyap R.
abstractText:
Objective

The optimal timing of reoperation for those who need repeat coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) and valve surgery is not well established. Early re-entries may be technically challenging due to adhesions and incomplete healing, while delayed interventions may expose patients to progressive cardiac disease.

Methods

Patients undergoing redo-sternotomy for CABG and valve surgery were identified from the TriNetX database and categorized into three cohorts based on the interval from their initial sternotomy: <1 year, 1-5 years, and > 5 years. Redo-sternotomies performed < 30 days after the initial procedure were excluded, as these typically represent early interventions for acute complications rather than planned reoperations. Two independent propensity score-matched analyses compared < 1 year vs. 1-5 years and 1-5 years vs. > 5 years, with separately matched 1-5 years cohorts for each comparison. Propensity score matching (PSM) was performed based on demographics, comorbidities, prior cardiac procedures, medications, and laboratory parameters including BMI. Primary outcomes included all-cause mortality, major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE), and emergency department or hospital readmissions. Secondary outcomes included postoperative infection, atrial fibrillation, acute kidney injury, dialysis, cardiogenic shock, respiratory failure, and cerebrovascular events.

Results

After PSM in the < 1 year vs. 1-5 years analysis (N = 305 in each group), redo-sternotomy within 1 year showed no significant differences in mortality, MACCE or readmissions. Combined cerebrovascular events were significantly reduced in the < 1 year group. In the 1-5 years vs. > 5 years analysis (N = 439 in each group), outcomes were similar between groups, with no significant differences in mortality, MACCE, or readmissions. Atrial fibrillation was significantly higher in the 1-5 years group. All other secondary outcomes, including combined cerebrovascular events, were comparable.

Conclusion

Redo-sternotomy within 1 year appears to be equally safe compared to later intervals, with comparable rates of adverse events, including mortality, MACCE, readmissions, postoperative infection, or AKI.

title: Preliminary experience of mechanical thrombectomy treatment in pediatric arterial ischemic stroke: a retrospective case series.
authorString: Zhou Y, Li S, Zhuang Y, Li Z, Yang K.
abstractText:
Objective

To evaluate the feasibility and efficacy of mechanical thrombectomy in the treatment of pediatric acute ischemic stroke (AIS).

Methods

The clinical data, radiographic results and management outcomes of children diagnosed with AIS and treated at our hospital between 2016 and 2021 were retrospectively analyzed.

Results

A total of 8 patients (4 male and 4 female) were included, with a mean age of 7.8 ± 2.8 years. All patients presented with focal neurological deficits at onset, including hemiplegia, facial deviation, mild limb weakness, dizziness, and headache, with Pediatric National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (PedNIHSS) scores ranging from 4 to 12 on presentation. Six patients had isolated middle cerebral artery occlusion, one bilateral posterior cerebral artery occlusion, and one had combined middle cerebral and anterior cerebral artery occlusion. Half of the patients underwent two mechanical thrombectomy procedures. After treatment, all patients achieved a modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction (mTICI) score of ≥2b. The median follow up duration was 20.13 months (range, 6-32 months). At the 6-month follow-up, all patients had the pediatric modified Rankin Scale (mRS) scores of 0 to 1.

Conclusion

Our preliminary experience suggests that mechanical thrombectomy is technically feasible and may be associated with favorable short- to medium-term functional outcomes in carefully selected pediatric patients with large vessel AIS. However, due to the retrospective design, small sample size, and lack of a control group, further multicenter prospective studies are warranted to better evaluate the safety and clinical outcomes of this procedure in pediatric patients.

title: Comparison of lung ultrasonography and chest radiography in detecting neonatal respiratory distress as a composite clinical condition: a prospective cross-sectional diagnostic accuracy study at Muhimbili National Hospital.
authorString: Dadi HK, Baraka BM, Mhalu IH, Mkony MF.
abstractText:
Background

Neonatal respiratory distress (RD) is a leading cause of neonatal morbidity and mortality. While chest radiography (CXR) is the traditional modality of diagnosis, lung ultrasound (LUS) has emerged as a bedside, radiation-free alternative for evaluating neonatal respiratory conditions.

Aim

To determine the diagnostic performance of lung ultrasonography (LUS) compared to chest radiography (CXR) in detecting neonatal respiratory distress (RD) as a composite clinical condition at Muhimbili National Hospital (MNH).

Methods

A prospective cross-sectional diagnostic accuracy study was conducted at Muhimbili National Hospital (MNH) between June and December 2022. A total of 179 neonates with clinical signs of respiratory distress were consecutively enrolled. All neonates underwent both LUS and CXR within 6 h. Demographic and clinical data were collected using a structured tool. Diagnostic performance was assessed for overall respiratory distress rather than individual disease etiologies. Sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV), and diagnostic accuracy (DA) were calculated using a composite clinico-radiological reference standard. Agreement was assessed using Cohen's kappa with 95% confidence intervals and significance set at p < 0.05.

Results

Among 179 neonates (mean gestational age: 32 ± 4 weeks; mean birth weight: 1,769 ± 856 g), LUS demonstrated high diagnostic performance in this setting, with higher sensitivity (95.1% vs. 90.3%), specificity (94.7% vs. 89.5%), positive predictive value (PPV) (96.1% vs. 92.1%), negative predictive value (NPV) (93.5% vs. 87.2%), and diagnostic accuracy (95% vs. 90%) compared to chest radiography (CXR). We observed almost perfect agreement between lung ultrasonography and the reference standard (κ = 0.898) and substantial agreement between lung ultrasonography and chest radiography (κ = 0.806).

Conclusion

Lung ultrasonography demonstrated high diagnostic performance in this setting for detecting neonatal respiratory distress as a composite clinical condition. However, interpretation should consider the use of a composite reference standard that included chest radiography, which may have introduced incorporation bias. Additionally, the composite outcome limits interpretation for individual respiratory conditions. Despite these limitations, LUS appears to be a useful adjunct imaging modality in resource-limited settings, where access to radiography may be constrained.

title: Risk factors for pulmonary consolidation in 316 pediatric cases of chlamydia pneumoniae pneumonia: a single-center retrospective study.
authorString: Wang P, Ma R, Ba C, Zhang F, Hu D, Zhang Y.
abstractText:
Background

Chlamydia pneumoniae (CP) infection in children is increasingly recognized, with a growing proportion developing pulmonary consolidation. Early identification of risk factors is critical for timely intervention, yet systematic pediatric studies remain limited. We aimed to identify independent predictors of pulmonary consolidation and develop a nomogram for individualized risk assessment.

Methods

This retrospective study enrolled 316 children with Chlamydia pneumoniae pneumonia (CPP) at Hebei Children's Hospital (Jan-Dec 2025), divided into consolidation (n = 79) and non-consolidation (n = 237) groups. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, and imaging data were compared between the two groups. Multivariable logistic regression was used to screen for independent predictors, which were then incorporated into a nomogram. Model discrimination was assessed by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), and calibration was evaluated using the Hosmer-Lemeshow test and a calibration curve with 1000 bootstrap resamples.

Results

Multivariable analysis identified age, pre-admission illness duration, peak temperature, platelet count (PLT), C-reactive protein (CRP), and D-dimer as independent predictors (all P < 0.05). A nomogram was constructed based on peak temperature, PLT, CRP, and D-dimer. The nomogram showed good discriminative ability, with an AUC of 0.868 (95% CI: 0.823-0.912). Calibration was satisfactory: the bias-corrected curve closely followed the 45-degree ideal reference line, with a mean absolute error of 0.022, indicating excellent model calibration, and the Hosmer-Lemeshow test confirmed good fit (χ² = 9.736, df = 8, P = 0.284). At the optimal cutoff, the model yielded a sensitivity of 79.7% and a specificity of 79.7%.

Conclusions

The combined model (peak temperature, PLT, CRP, and D-dimer) demonstrated promising discrimination for identifying pulmonary consolidation in children with Chlamydia pneumoniae pneumonia. The identified cutoffs may indicate increased risk of existing consolidation and could support early risk stratification. However, given the retrospective cross-sectional design, these findings should be interpreted as associations rather than prospective predictions; external validation in prospective studies is required before clinical application.

title: Quality assessment of primary health care for infants and young children in Hunan Province of China.
authorString: Li T, Zhang S, Jia N, Dai Y.
abstractText:
Objective

To comprehensively evaluate the service quality of primary health care (PHC) for children aged 0-3 years in healthcare facilities of China, and to identify strengths and existing gaps to provide evidence for optimizing regional child health service policies.

Methods

A multi-stage stratified random sampling method was used to select 35 healthcare facilities from 4 geographical regions in Hunan province of China. Data were collected using the WHO Western Pacific Regional Office Primary Health Care Quality Improvement Guide, which included facility assessments, medical record reviews, and caregiver interviews. All indicators were assessed against China national basic public health service standards and WHO PHC quality benchmarks. Chi-square test was used for comparative analysis between sick and healthy children.

Results

The overall PHC foundation was sound: 85.0% of service rooms had qualified handwashing facilities, 92.0% were equipped with alcohol rub, and over 97% of facilities had standardized protocols for breastfeeding screening and infection control. The key basic medicines and routine growth monitoring supplies achieved an availability rate above 91.4%. The under-6-month exclusive breastfeeding rate was 38.9%, and National Immunization Programme (NIP) vaccine coverage remained over 90% for most routine vaccines. However, significant gaps existed. Well children showed far higher health screening rates than sick children, with growth measurement completion rates of 93.9% vs. 72.2% for weight and 92.1% vs. 9.0% for height; respiratory rate screening remained extremely low at around 17% in both groups. Non-NIP vaccine coverage was only 28.5%-47.1%. The availability of therapeutic food, special vaccines and essential emergency medicines was below 30%, and only 45.8% of rooms were equipped with sharps containers and merely 28.6% of facilities had child abuse and neglect management protocols. Additionally, the staff IMCI training rate was only 54.2%, and patient-staff ratios ranged from 48.6% to 65.9% across clinics.

Conclusion

Child PHC services in Hunan Province perform well in basic infrastructure, routine health management and national immunization, but have prominent deficiencies in standardized clinical assessment for sick children, breastfeeding promotion, non-NIP vaccine accessibility, child protection system construction, essential drug supply, and human resource allocation. Targeted interventions on clinical standardization, material guarantee, professional training and child protection mechanism improvement are needed to further elevate the overall quality and equity of early childhood PHC services.

title: Infective endocarditis due to a novel <i>Gemella</i> species revealed by metagenomic sequencing.
authorString: Sekikawa Y, Horiba K, Hashino M, Soneda K, Kato T.
abstractText:
Background

Gemella species are rare causes of infective endocarditis, and accurate species identification can be challenging with routine diagnostic methods. We report infective endocarditis caused by a novel Gemella species, highlighting the diagnostic value of sequencing-based approaches for bacteria not registered in public databases and the risk of misclassification when novel species are not represented in reference databases.

Case summary

A 55-year-old Japanese man presented with fatigue, anorexia, and altered mental status. Echocardiography revealed vegetations on the mitral and tricuspid valves with severe mitral regurgitation, and imaging demonstrated multiple systemic embolic events. Blood cultures grew gram-positive cocci that were initially identified as Gemella bergeri by matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry. The patient received antimicrobial therapy and underwent mitral valve replacement and tricuspid valve repair. Culture of the excised valve tissue was negative. Metagenomic sequencing of the valve vegetation detected a Gemella species distinct from G. bergeri. Genome assembly from sequencing data showed 94.5% average nucleotide identity with a reference G. bergeri genome, supporting classification as a novel species. Whole-genome sequencing of the blood culture isolate demonstrated near-complete concordance with the organism detected in the valve tissue. The patient recovered with a 6-week course of intravenous penicillin G after blood cultures became sterile.

Conclusion

This case demonstrates that rare Gemella infections may be misidentified by routine mass spectrometry. It underscores the importance of sequencing-based methods for accurate pathogen identification and highlights a diagnostic pitfall associated with database-dependent identification in infective endocarditis.

title: Isolated systemic arterial supply to the normal lung presenting with massive hemoptysis in a child: CT angiographic diagnosis and endovascular management.
authorString: Singh R, Gupta V, Yadav R, Ghasi RG.
abstractText: Isolated systemic supply to normal lung (ISSNL) is an uncommon bronchopulmonary vascular abnormality in which a section of normally ventilated lung gets arterial blood from the systemic circulation, without accompanying bronchial or pulmonary abnormalities. We discuss a case of a 12-year-old boy who had a single episode of significant hemoptysis. Computed tomographic angiography (CTA) identified a significant convoluted anomalous artery originating from the mid-descending thoracic aorta, supplying the left lower lobe, with no evidence of fistulous connection to pulmonary arteries. The diagnosis of ISSNL was confirmed, and the patient was effectively treated with endovascular embolization with a vascular plug. At the 3-month follow-up, no recurrence of hemoptysis was seen. While often asymptomatic, ISSNL may manifest as hemoptysis or signs of volume overload. CTA is essential for diagnosis, anatomical characterization, and treatment strategy formulation. Timely identification of this condition is crucial, since endovascular embolization provides a safe and effective alternative to surgical intervention with less morbidity.

title: Risk factors for post-extubation stridor in pediatric cardiac intensive care unit: a single-center retrospective study.
authorString: Saengsin K, Wongyikul P, Phinyo P, Borisuthipandit T, Sittiwangkul R, Silvilairat S, Makonkawkeyoon K, Sethasathien S, Ayurag T, Wiwatkamonchai N, Sunkonkit K.
abstractText:
Background

Post-extubation stridor (PES) is a frequent and clinically significant complication among pediatric cardiac intensive care unit (PCICU) patients, particularly those with congenital heart disease (CHD). This study aimed to determine the incidence, associated risk factors, and outcomes of PES in this population.

Methods

This retrospective cohort study included children aged 1 month to 18 years who underwent planned extubation after more than 24 h of mechanical ventilation in the PCICU at Chiang Mai University Hospital between July 2016 and June 2024. Demographic, clinical, and ventilatory variables were retrieved from electronic medical records. Univariable and multivariable mixed-effects logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent predictors of PES.

Results

Among 494 extubation episodes from 380 children, PES occurred in 25.5% of attempts. Patients who developed PES were younger, low body weight, and had longer ventilation duration compared with those without PES. In multivariable analysis, lower body weight (OR 0.84; 95% CI, 0.73-0.97) and mechanical ventilation exceeding 7 days (OR 1.83; 95% CI, 1.04-3.23) remained significant independent predictors.

Conclusions

PES was common among pediatric cardiac patients and was independently associated with lower body weight at extubation and prolonged mechanical ventilation. Recognition of children at higher risk may support targeted preventive strategies and improve post-extubation outcomes.

title: A case of mucopolysaccharidosis I with severely increased albuminuria and Graves' disease, and functional analysis of previously uncharacterized variant.
authorString: Dong K, Peng JJ, Zhou X, Zhu Q, Li C, Yang Y.
abstractText:
Background

Mucopolysaccharidoses (MPS) are a group of inherited lysosomal storage disorders which results in accumulation of glycosaminoglycans throughout the body. MPS I is a subtype characterized by mutations in the α-L-iduronidase (IDUA) gene with subsequent multiorgan dysfunction.

Case description

Here, we describe an adult patient with MPS I who presented with anasarca, as well as severely increased albuminuria, and was initially diagnosed with hyperthyroidism. Subsequent testing revealed clinical characteristics and deficient IDUA enzyme activity consistent with MPS I. Genetic testing identified two variants of interest in the IDUA gene: IDUA c·265C > T (p.R89W) and IDUA c.1403-2A > G.

Methods

IDUA enzymatic activity was measured in HEK293T cells transfected with wildtype or p. R89W mutant IDUA expression constructs using the fluorogenic substrate 4-methylumbelliferyl-α-L-iduronide (4MU-iduronide). A minigene splicing assay was performed using IDUA exon 9-11 (including intron 9 and 10) DNA fragments cloned into the pMini-CopGFP vector, with the mutant plasmid containing the IDUA c.1403-2A > G variant generated using site-directed mutagenesis. HEK293T cells were transfected with either the wildtype or mutant plasmids, and splice products were separated by gel electrophoresis with distinct bands excised for Sanger sequencing.

Results

The IDUA c·265C > T (p.R89W) mutant construct was cloned into HEK293T cells and showed significantly decreased intracellular (10.86 ± 0.36%, p < 0.01) and extracellular (1.18 ± 0.09%, p < 0.01) enzymatic activity compared to wild type. A minigene splicing assay of the previously uncharacterized IDUA c.1403-2A > G splice site variant found retention of intron 9 between exon 9 and 10 leading to a premature termination codon.

Conclusion

This manuscript describes a unique clinical presentation of MPS I with simultaneous Graves' disease and severely increased albuminuria. Functional analysis of the IDUA variants identified in our patient adds to the current understanding of genetic variants implicated in the disease.

title: Integrated bioinformatics analysis and mouse validation identify C7 and MFAP4 as candidate genes associated with type 2 diabetes and atherosclerosis.
authorString: Wang L, Chen Y, Ding P, Wang H, Wu C, Li P, Ou C, Xie Z, Jin J, Hu J, Yu J, Wang Y.
abstractText:
Background

Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is closely associated with accelerated atherosclerosis (AS), but the molecular features linking these two conditions remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify candidate genes associated with T2DM and AS and to explore their potential biological relevance.

Methods

Public GEO transcriptomic datasets were analysed. GSE38642 and GSE100927 were used as T2DM and AS training datasets, while GSE41762 and GSE57691 were used for validation. Differentially expressed genes were identified using limma, and disease-associated modules were screened by weighted gene co-expression network analysis. Candidate genes were obtained by intersecting differentially expressed genes with module genes, followed by protein-protein interaction analysis, cytoHubba-MCC, and MCODE screening. Expression validation, receiver operating characteristic analysis, cross-validation, permutation testing, GeneMANIA, GSEA, ssGSEA-based immune infiltration analysis, regulatory network construction, and exploratory drug-gene enrichment analysis were performed. Selected genes were further examined in mouse models.

Results

21 overlapping genes were identified, and six candidate hub genes were further screened. Among them, C7 and MFAP4 showed reproducible but disease-context-dependent expression patterns and exploratory discriminatory performance across the training and validation datasets. Functional analyses suggested that C7 and MFAP4 were associated with inflammatory response, complement activation, TNF-α/NF-κB signaling, oxidative phosphorylation, extracellular matrix remodeling, and immune-related alterations. Additional robustness analyses supported the exploratory relevance of these two genes, particularly MFAP4, while also indicating that the findings should be interpreted cautiously. In mouse models, C7 and MFAP4 showed disease-associated expression changes, supporting their potential relevance to metabolic stress and vascular remodeling.

Conclusion

This integrated bioinformatics and experimental validation study identified C7 and MFAP4 as exploratory candidate genes associated with T2DM and AS.

title: Cardiovascular effects of methylphenidate, risperidone, and their combination in children and adolescents with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder: a prospective 3-month observational study.
authorString: Oveisi S, Jafari E, Bahari MM, Farshidgohar M.
abstractText:
Background

We aimed to evaluate changes in hemodynamic parameters and electrocardiographic (ECG) indices related to ventricular arrhythmia risk after three months of treatment with methylphenidate (MPH), risperidone (RIS), or their combination in children and adolescents with ADHD.

Methods

A total of 150 children and adolescents with DSM-5-diagnosed ADHD were prospectively enrolled at Qods Hospital. Participants received methylphenidate (n = 50), risperidone (n = 50), or combination therapy (n = 50). Cardiovascular outcomes were assessed using age- and weight-adjusted two-way repeated-measures ANCOVA to evaluate changes over time and differences among treatment groups.

Results

Significant group × time interactions were observed for systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, heart rate, and QTc interval after adjustment for baseline age and weight. After three months, systolic and diastolic blood pressure increased in the methylphenidate and combination therapy groups, while heart rate showed an overall increase, with the greatest rise observed in the methylphenidate group. QTc interval increased over time across all treatment groups, with the largest prolongation observed in the combination therapy group (377.9 ± 25.4 to 424.5 ± 24.9 ms). However, mean QTc values remained below commonly accepted thresholds for clinically significant QT prolongation, and no significant longitudinal changes were observed in QRS duration or PR intervals.

Conclusion

Treatment with methylphenidate, risperidone, and combination therapy was associated with modest changes in heart rate, blood pressure, and QTc interval over three months. These findings highlight the importance of baseline and follow-up cardiovascular monitoring in children and adolescents receiving ADHD medications.

title: The Italian Spina Bifida registry: insights from the first 1,000 patient data.
authorString: Salvatore M, Rocchetti A, Buoncuore G, Rendeli C, Capriati M, Taverna M, Redaelli T, Leo A, Bruno R, Dieci MC, Torreri P, Spina Bifida registry group.
abstractText:
Background

Spina bifida (SB) results from failure of fusion of the caudal neural tube leading to complications in several organ systems and considerable disability. The causes of this disorder are heterogeneous and multifactorial. Medical and surgical management is a lifelong necessity for people with SB (pwSB) and should be provided by a multidisciplinary team. Standardized collection of data in ad hoc registries represents an important tool to (i) collect clinical and epidemiologic data, (ii) assess the clinical management including the diagnostic delay, (iii) improve patients' care and (iv) foster research to identify new therapeutic solutions. The present study aimed to shed light on the analyses from the first 1.000 patients included in the Italian SB registry (period 2020-23) thus boosting the contribution of registries of pathology in the improvement of knowledge and research.

Methods

The Italian SB registry was established in 2020 to (i) describe the natural history of the disease, (ii) determine the clinical effectiveness of health care services, (iii) measure and monitor the quality of care of patients. It is based on a web-customizable-based system for the collection of demographics, diagnosis and genetics, patient status, therapy, quality of life and mortality data. Clinical data are updated annually during follow-up visits. Data quality is ensured by an automatic check performed by the system enabling a constant longitudinal and vertical control of data included in the registry. Descriptive statistics, including absolute and relative frequencies, mean, standard deviation, median, and percentiles, were used to summarize the quantitative variables of interest. the Pearson's Chi-Square Test was conducted to study the association between the qualitative variables under study.

Results

A total of 1.000 pwSB were enrolled in the first 36 months after registry establishment (period: October 2020 to October 2023) from 15 Referral paediatric and adult Italian Centres; 66,8% and 33,2% of patients were enrolled in a paediatric and an adult Centre respectively (53% female versus 47% males). Forty-point-4% (40,4%) of patients was characterized by open spina bifida (OSB) while 59,6% by a closed spina bifida (CSB). Diagnoses were performed during the prenatal period (26,6%), at birth (41,7%) and within the first year of life (15%), most of these latter cases being characterized by a CSB. Associated primary malformations were reported in 57.4% of patients; among these, Arnold-Chiari II malformation was significantly associated with OSB (p < 0.001). Lesions were mainly localized in the lumbosacral region (82.3%). Plastic surgery was performed in 549 patients, predominantly among OSB cases (73.5%).

Conclusions

The analyses of our data form, allowed to highlight important demographic and clinical aspects of SB useful to inform future actions to be taken by national health care services and health professionals. The present study represents the first report describing the Italian Spina Bifida Registry, aiming at demonstrating the feasibility and successful implementation of a national registry, which may serve as a foundation for future studies with direct implications for patient care.

title: Microbiota in liver carcinogenesis: Illuminating the complex relationship.
authorString: Chuaypen N, Dissayabutra T, Bajaj JS.
abstractText: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) develops predominantly in patients with cirrhosis, yet the biological mechanisms underlying the transition from cirrhosis to malignancy remain incompletely understood. Increasing evidence suggests that the oral-gut-liver axis contributes to this process through coordinated interactions among oral and intestinal microbiota, the epithelial barrier, the immune system, and the liver. While previous reviews have primarily focused on gut dysbiosis in cirrhosis and its complications, emerging evidence indicates that microbiome-associated alterations actively contribute to hepatocarcinogenesis. In this review, we propose a transition-state model in which disruption of the oral-gut-liver axis promotes progression from cirrhosis to HCC through functional microbiome insufficiency, epithelial barrier dysfunction, microbial translocation, inflammatory remodeling, and immune dysregulation. We emphasize that disruption of microbial metabolic functions, including reduced butyrate biosynthesis, bile acid remodeling, altered tryptophan metabolism, and enrichment of virulence-associated pathways may be more biologically relevant than taxonomic changes alone. We further discuss emerging biomarkers representing distinct domains of the gut-liver axis, including butyryl-CoA:acetate CoA-transferase (BCoAT) as a marker of microbial function, intestinal fatty acid-binding protein (I-FABP) as a marker of epithelial injury, and lipopolysaccharide-binding protein (LBP) as a marker of microbial translocation and endotoxemia. Finally, we discuss the translational implications of integrating microbiome-derived functional biomarkers with immune and clinical profiling for biological risk stratification, early detection, and precision hepatology as well as therapeutic strategies based on microbiome modulation. This framework shifts the focus from descriptive dysbiosis toward mechanistic host-microbiome interactions, highlights the oral-gut-liver axis as an active contributor to hepatocarcinogenesis, and provides a conceptual foundation for future microbiome-informed surveillance, risk stratification, and therapeutic strategies.

title: Cardiac Organoids Uncover an Association of CHD7 Deficiency with Congenital Heart Disease.
authorString: Sun S, Feng Z, Na W, Gao Y, Min S, Zhuang Q, Lin S, Zhao Q, Huang X, Song H, Sheng W, Huang G.
abstractText:
CHD7 (Chromodomain helicase DNA-binding protein 7) encodes an ATP-dependent chromatin remodeler, and pathogenic disruption of CHD7 underlies CHARGE syndrome(Coloboma, Heart defects, Atresia choanae, Retarded growth and development, Genital abnormalities, Ear abnormalities syndrome), a congenital disorder frequently accompanied by complex cardiac malformations. However, how CHD7 contributes to human cardiogenesis remains poorly defined. Here, we use multi-chamber cardiac organoids derived from human embryonic stem cells, which capture key features of early cardiac morphogenesis and regional lineage patterning, to interrogate CHD7 function. CHD7 loss leads to attenuation of cardiac progenitor gene programs, disrupted chamber organization, reduced efficiency of cardiomyocyte differentiation, and markedly impaired contractile function. Bulk RNA sequencing further reveals broad misregulation of transcriptional modules involved in cardiogenic signaling, regional progenitor patterning, and myocardial maturation. Together, these data establish a human organoid framework for modelling CHD7-associated congenital heart disease and identify CHD7 as a key regulator of cardiac morphogenesis and the acquisition of functional cardiomyocyte properties.

title: The Effect of Adding Dexmedetomidine to Modified Del Nido Cardioplegia Solution on Myocardial Protection in Children Undergoing Congenital Heart Defect Surgery - A Prospective, Randomized, Triple-Blind, Controlled Trial.
authorString: Samadieh F, Maleki MH, Razeghian M, Izanlou T, Sistani MN, Fazli B, Yaghubi M.
abstractText:
Introduction

The myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) is an indispensable factor in pediatric congenital heart defect (CHD) surgery. Although effective myocardial protection strategies are crucial, the issue remains a dilemma. This study aimed to evaluate the effect of adding dexmedetomidine to modified Del Nido cardioplegia on myocardial protection in children undergoing CHD surgery.

Methods

This was a prospective, randomized, triple-blind, controlled clinical trial. A total of 60 pediatric patients were enrolled and randomized 1:1 into two groups - an intervention group that received dexmedetomidine-enriched modified Del Nido cardioplegia and a control group that received standard modified Del Nido cardioplegia with normal saline. Primary outcomes included serum troponin I and creatine kinase-MB levels, as well as coronary sinus lactate levels. Secondary outcomes were the vasoactive-inotropic score, weaning time from mechanical ventilation, and intensive care unit length of stay.

Results

Adding dexmedetomidine to modified Del Nido cardioplegia significantly improved myocardial protection in children undergoing CHD surgery. The intervention group showed significantly lower troponin I levels at all postoperative time points compared to the control group (P < 0.001). Similarly, the dexmedetomidine group had significantly lower vasoactive-inotropic score at all time points (P < 0.001). Patients in the intervention group also experienced a significantly shorter mean ventilator weaning time (P < 0.001) and intensive care unit stay duration (P < 0.001). The overall distribution of postoperative morbidities did not differ significantly between the groups (P = 0.059).

Conclusion

Adding dexmedetomidine to modified Del Nido cardioplegia significantly improved myocardial protection in children undergoing corrective CHD surgery.

title: Double-Inlet single ventricle associated with transposition of the great arteries, <i>situs inversus</i>, and criss-cross heart in an unrepaired adult: A case report.
authorString: Vargas-Lucio B, Bravo-Alvarado J, Gaibor-Gaibor S, Vargas-Lucio E, Almache-Palacios A.

journal.title: Archivos peruanos de cardiologia y cirugia cardiovascular

abstractText: The single ventricle represents a group of complex congenital heart diseases characterized by the mixing of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood, chronic cyanosis, and ventricular volume overload. The combination of a double-inlet single ventricle with transposition of the great arteries, situs inversus, and a criss-cross heart is extremely rare, reported only in isolated cases in the literature. Most of these patients require early palliative interventions, such as the bidirectional Glenn procedure and eventual Fontan circulation, to optimize oxygenation and reduce ventricular overload. We present the case of a 26-year-old man with a history of cyanotic congenital heart disease, scheduled for surgery at age 12 but managed conservatively due to high surgical risk. Survival into adulthood without definitive surgical correction is likely due to a favorable hemodynamic balance conferred by pulmonary stenosis, which limits pulmonary overcirculation and protects the dominant ventricle. Currently, the patient remains clinically stable, classified as New York Heart Association functional class II, with no recent episodes of cardiovascular decompensation, hospitalizations, or documented thromboembolic events. This case highlights the anatomical rarity and underscores the importance of specialized follow-up in adults with complex univentricular congenital heart disease who have not undergone corrective surgery.

title: Heart transplant in an adult patient with dysfunctional Fontan circulation at a high-complexity cardiovascular center in Peru: A case report.
authorString: Conde Moncada RY, Robles Velarde V, Zamudio Silva R, Masabel Chicoma EA, Zavala Castillo SM, Soplopuco Palacios FR.

journal.title: Archivos peruanos de cardiologia y cirugia cardiovascular

abstractText: Fontan circulation failure represents a progressive condition associated with multiorgan dysfunction and increased morbidity and mortality. In this context, heart transplantation has become the definitive treatment for this subgroup of patients. Reported survival rates after heart transplantation in patients with Fontan circulation are approximately 80% at 1 year, 74% at 5 years, and 59% at 10 years. We present the case of a 46-year-old patient with a history of Ebstein anomaly who underwent intracardiac Fontan surgery, which progressed to progressive Fontan circulation failure, and who underwent orthotopic heart transplantation with reconstruction of the pulmonary branches.

title: Acute cardiac failure in pregnancy: diagnosis and treatment.
authorString: Muñoz-Ortiz E, Gándara-Ricardo JA, Holguín-González É, Velázquez-Penagos JA, Flórez-Muñoz JP, Giraldo-Serna MB, Arana-Escandón YI.

journal.title: Archivos peruanos de cardiologia y cirugia cardiovascular

abstractText: Heart disease affects approximately 4% of pregnancies and is the leading non-obstetric cause of maternal death during pregnancy in many countries. The physiological hormonal and haemodynamic changes that occur during this period can unmask previously undiagnosed cardiac disease and destabilise pre-existing cardiovascular conditions. Acute heart failure during pregnancy is uncommon; however, it can lead to severe maternal and fetal complications. Although the diagnostic criteria are the same as those used in the general population, diagnosis can be challenging because the cardinal signs and symptoms of heart failure overlap with several symptoms and clinical findings that commonly occur during pregnancy. A comprehensive clinical history therefore remains fundamental to the diagnostic approach, enabling the rational use of complementary investigations and, in many cases, guiding treatment. Management of acute heart failure during pregnancy must be highly individualised and may involve decisions regarding continuation of the pregnancy and the optimal mode of delivery. Care should therefore be led by an experienced multidisciplinary team with expertise in the diagnosis and management of cardiovascular disease during pregnancy, with the aim of achieving the best possible outcomes for both the mother and the fetus.

title: Neurologic presentation unmasks arrhythmogenic channelopathy: KCNH2 variant Long-QT syndrome managed with subcutaneous implantable cardioverter-defibrillator. A case report.
authorString: Vallejos-Barrientos A, Centeno-Araujo A, Soto-Becerra R, Cabrera-Saldaña M, Guevara-Caicedo C, Gonzales-Luna AC, Payano-Rojas M, Cueva-Parra Á, Calle-García R, Ramos-Godoy C, Zelaya-Castro P.

journal.title: Archivos peruanos de cardiologia y cirugia cardiovascular

abstractText: A previously healthy 10-year-old boy developed febrile seizure-like episodes after an appendectomy, which were diagnosed as epilepsy despite a normal electroencephalogram. He later presented with dyspnea and palpitations and was prescribed propafenone for frequent premature ventricular complexes. The electrocardiogram showed a markedly prolonged QTc interval of 550 ms with a notched T wave in lead V2. Phenytoin and propafenone were discontinued, and propranolol was initiated, but QTc prolongation persisted. The combination of severely prolonged QTc, characteristic T-wave morphology, and absence of structural heart disease redirected the diagnosis toward a repolarization channelopathy; genetic testing confirmed long-QT syndrome type 2 due to a pathogenic KCNH2 c.1814C>T variant. β-blocker therapy was optimized, QT-prolonging triggers were avoided, and a subcutaneous implantable cardioverter-defibrillator was implanted. Cascade genetic screening identified no additional KCNH2 carriers. One variant-negative sister had frequent idiopathic right ventricular outflow tract premature ventricular complexes and was referred for catheter ablation.

title: Feasibility and Early Outcomes of Intraoperative Extubation in Pediatric Atrial and Ventricular Septal Defect Repair via Axillary Thoracotomy.
authorString: Seçici S, Terkanlıoglu S.
abstractText:
Introduction

This retrospective study evaluated the feasibility, safety, and early recovery outcomes of intraoperative extubation combined with minimally invasive axillary thoracotomy for atrial septal defect (ASD) and ventricular septal defect (VSD) repair in pediatric patients.

Methods

Sixty-one consecutive pediatric patients who underwent ASD (n = 43) or VSD (n = 18) repair via axillary thoracotomy between March 2017 and December 2023 were included. Patients were categorized by extubation timing into intraoperative (operating room [OR] group) and postoperative (intensive care unit [ICU] group). Baseline characteristics, operative variables, and postoperative outcomes were compared.

Results

In the ASD cohort, patients extubated intraoperatively had a shorter hospital stay compared with those extubated in the ICU (2.78 ± 1.24 vs. 3.60 ± 0.99 days, P < 0.001). In the VSD cohort, the OR group included younger and lower-weight patients yet demonstrated a significantly shorter hospital stay (3.56 ± 0.73 vs. 5.78 ± 3.35 days, P = 0.013). Across the entire cohort, on-table extubation was associated with reduced hospital stay (P < 0.001), with no increase in reintubation or major complications.

Conclusions

Intraoperative extubation following axillary thoracotomy for ASD and VSD repair in pediatric patients appears safe and feasible and was associated with a significantly shorter hospital stay, even in lower-weight patients. These findings suggest that intraoperative extubation may be considered as part of enhanced recovery strategies in pediatric congenital heart surgery.

title: Camptodactyly and Early-Onset Scoliosis in Snijders Blok-Campeau Syndrome.
authorString: Miura M, Kobayashi Y, Hojo M, Yamada K, Fujii H, Eimori K, Yanagi K, Kaname T, Nagasaki K, Nyuzuki H, Ikeuchi T, Tohyama J.
abstractText: Snijders Blok-Campeau syndrome is caused by a heterozygous CHD3 pathogenic variant, and characterized by features including macrocephaly, speech delay, hypotonia, and joint laxity. In the hereby-presented case, a Japanese girl with Snijders Blok-Campeau syndrome displayed bilateral middle finger camptodactyly and early-onset scoliosis, beyond the characteristic symptoms such as intellectual disability, facial abnormalities, macrocephaly, and hypotonia due to a recurrent CHD3 pathogenic variant. This case expands our knowledge of the phenotypic spectrum of Snijders Blok-Campeau syndrome.

title: Clinical study on feasibility and repeatability of left ventricular systolic function assessment in patients with chronic kidney disease using artificial intelligence-based automatic strain technique.
authorString: Tian F, Wu Z, Zhong L, Qiu J, Tang H.

journal.title: Malawi medical journal : the journal of Medical Association of Malawi

abstractText:
Background

Cardiovascular damage is a common complication in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD), and left ventricular longitudinal strain (GLS) is superior to LVEF in evaluating systolic function. However, it has not been widely adopted clinically because it requires proficiency and is time-consuming. This study aimed to investigate the feasibility, reproducibility, and predictive value of automated GLS compared with manual GLS, providing a reference for clinical evaluation and reduction of cardiovascular events in CKD patients.

Methods

A total of 285 CKD patients (aged 52 ± 12.85) without dialysis were enrolled from Hainan Provincial People's Hospital. GLS was measured using three methods on identical apical three-, two-, and four-chamber views: (1) fully automatic GLS analyzed by machine functions, (2) semi-automatic GLS corrected by researchers, and (3) manual GLS measured by experts. Five cases were excluded due to poor image quality. Clinical outcomes were followed up by telephone and outpatient visits.

Results

About 35% of automatic GLS results required manual correction, with significant differences among the three methods (P < 0.01). The correlation and consistency between semi-automatic and manual GLS were higher than those of automatic GLS (P < 0.01). During 2-year follow-up, 55 patients (19.6%) experienced cardiovascular events. Automated GLS predicted events but with lower accuracy than semi-automatic GLS. The analysis time for automatic (15.23 ± 0.75 s) and semi-automatic GLS (75.06 ± 19.01 s) was markedly shorter than manual analysis (236.81 ± 45.41 s, P < 0.01).

Conclusions

Automated GLS assessment in CKD patients is feasible and reproducible. As some images still require manual correction, the semi-automated approach currently offers the optimal balance between efficiency and predictive value.

title: Prenatal diagnosis of agenesis of the portal system type II Abernethy malformation associated with trisomy 21.
authorString: Mendes Ribeiro AC, Araújo M, de Nazaré Miziara A, de Figueiredo LRAS, de Abreu YR, Araujo Júnior E, Peixoto AB.
abstractText: Congenital agenesis of the portal vein (CAPV) is a rare vascular anomaly characterized by absence of the portal vein, resulting in abnormal shunting of splenic and mesenteric blood directly into the systemic circulation without adequate hepatic perfusion. This case report describes a fetus diagnosed prenatally with CAPV associated with trisomy 21 (Down syndrome), confirmed postnatally. Detailed ultrasonographic and Doppler findings revealed a porto-caval shunt and vascular abnormalities, while genetic analysis confirmed the chromosomal anomaly. The newborn presented with moderate pulmonary hypertension and mild congenital heart defects, requiring multidisciplinary management. This report highlights the importance of early prenatal diagnosis through imaging, enabling appropriate obstetric planning and postnatal care. The association between CAPV and trisomy 21, although rare, underscores the need for genetic investigation in fetuses with vascular malformations. Follow-up demonstrated persistence of the porto-caval shunt - type II Abernethy malformation, reinforcing the pathological nature of the condition and necessity for specialized monitoring. This case contributes to the understanding of the clinical spectrum and embryological origins of CAPV and its syndromic associations.

Preoperative Lower Respiratory Tract Infection and Postoperative Mortality in Elderly Hip Fracture Patients: A Retrospective Cohort Study
authorString: Chu L, Chen X, Liu W, Zhang S, Wang X, Liu Z, Xi C.
abstractText: Background Preoperative lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI) is common in elderly hip fracture patients, but its prognostic significance remains understudied. We aimed to investigate whether preoperative LRTI is independently associated with postoperative mortality in this population. Methods This retrospective cohort study included 1,922 elderly patients (≥ 60 years) who underwent hip fracture surgery at a single Level I trauma center between 2015 and 2021. Preoperative LRTI was identified from medical records according to European guidelines. The primary outcomes were 30-day and 1-year all-cause mortality. Hierarchical Cox regression models (Models 1–5) were used to sequentially adjust for demographics, nutritional and inflammatory status, comorbidities, surgical factors, and postoperative complications. Subgroup analyses were performed. Results Preoperative LRTI was present in 319 patients (16.6%). In fully adjusted models, preoperative LRTI was independently associated with increased 30-day mortality (HR 2.68, 95% CI 1.67–4.33) and 1-year mortality (HR 1.71, 95% CI 1.30–2.26). Patients with preoperative LRTI also had significantly higher rates of postoperative cardiac events (8.8% vs. 2.9%) and new-onset pneumonia (21.6% vs. 6.8%). In exploratory subgroup analyses the association appeared stronger in patients with low neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), although this finding requires validation in future studies. Conclusions Preoperative LRTI is an independent risk factor for both short- and medium-term mortality in elderly hip fracture patients. Preoperative LRTI should be actively screened for and incorporated into preoperative risk stratification. Future multicenter prospective studies are needed to validate these findings and determine whether preoperative optimization can improve outcomes.

title: Association of the admission albumin–bilirubin score with long-term major adverse cardiovascular events among patients who survived to discharge after percutaneous coronary intervention for non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction: a single-center cohort study
authorString: Lin Y, Yao J, Lin C, Wu J, Li S.
abstractText: Objective To investigate the association of admission albumin–bilirubin (ALBI) score with long-term major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs) among patients who survived to discharge after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI), and to assess whether ALBI provides prognostic information beyond the admission GRACE score. Methods We retrospectively included 681 patients hospitalized between January 1, 2023, and September 1, 2025, who survived to discharge after PCI for NSTEMI. Patients were categorized into ALBI tertiles (T1, T2 and T3). Kaplan–Meier analysis, multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression and restricted cubic spline analysis were used to evaluate the association between ALBI and long-term MACEs. Missing data were handled using predictive mean matching, generating 50 imputed datasets. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses were performed. The discriminatory performance of the admission GRACE-based model was compared before and after ALBI was added. Follow-up continued through September 6, 2026. Results Among 681 patients, the median follow-up duration was 585 days, during which 186 MACEs occurred, representing 27.3% of the cohort. The cumulative proportions of MACEs in T1, T2 and T3 were 18.1%, 29.1% and 34.8%, respectively, differing significantly among groups (all P < 0.001). After adjustment, each 1-standard-deviation (1-SD) increase in ALBI was associated with a 25% higher risk of long-term MACEs (HR = 1.25, 95% CI: 1.06–1.46, P = 0.007). Compared with T1, the corresponding HRs were 1.59 for T2 and 1.60 for T3. Restricted cubic spline analysis showed no evidence of a significant nonlinear association. The results were therefore compatible with an approximately linear association within the observed ALBI range. The direction of association remained positive in sensitivity analyses, although the complete-case estimate was less precise and was not statistically significant. Adding ALBI produced small, statistically nonsignificant increases in the GRACE model’s C-index and 365-day time-dependent AUC. Conclusion Among patients who survived to discharge after PCI for NSTEMI, a higher admission ALBI score was independently associated with increased risk of long-term MACEs, with an approximately linear pattern across the observed range. ALBI may serve as a simple marker of long-term risk. Its incremental predictive value beyond the GRACE score requires validation in multicenter prospective studies.

title: An Efficient Microfluidic Platform for Organ-Specific Cyclic Multiaxial Loading and Differentiation of Progenitor Cells
authorString: Murugesan N, Arkat S, Aristotle D, Saha S, Paul A, Guhathakurta S, Mullasari A, Shah P, Kamath SR, Mahapatra NR, Das SK.
abstractText: Mechanical loading is a fundamental regulator of tissue development, maturation, and function, yet existing  in vitro systems predominantly apply uniaxial load/strain to cell-laden hydrogels, limiting their ability to reproduce physiologically relevant multiaxial on-chip tissue mechanics. Here, we present an engineered system to apply controlled multiaxial mechanical loading to real scaffolds with undifferentiated cells. The system enables programmable cyclic stretching and relaxation at the cell scaffold level and is compatible with both cell-laden native scaffold and engineered soft tissues. We have quantified the strain field experienced by the tissue with distinct mechanical loading periods using computation simulations and validated these with systematic experiments, demonstrating reproducible and various organ-relevant multiaxial strain profiles. As proof of concept, we applied the approach to human cardiac tissues, where cyclic multiaxial mechanical loading of mononuclear cells laden native tissue scaffold promoted cardiac structural organization and supports the emergence of spontaneous contractile activity. This approach provides a generalizable method for reproducing physiologically relevant tissue mechanics  in vitro and enables systematic investigation of mechano-regulation across a plethora of human tissues.

title: Submembrane geography dictates GPCR signalling compartmentation and physiological function
authorString: Froese A, Qi B, Feng M, Böer G, Morhenn K, Kupsch S, Sun X, Subramanian H, Sanchez-Alonso JL, Medvedev R, Wright PT, Gallego M, Revuelta D, Beck NI, Molina CE, Miragoli M, Rossi S, Ehmke H, Gorelik J, Parak WJ, Feliu N, Nikolaev VO.
abstractText: G-protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) are key mediators of intercellular signalling and targets for the vast majority of current therapeutics. Numerous biochemical and biophysical studies have uncovered that individual GPCRs activated at different subcellular locations can mediate distinct functional effects due to compartmentalization of the downstream second messengers in subcellular nanodomains. However, the reasons why a single receptor subtype activated at the same subcellular compartment such as plasma membrane leads to various functional responses have remained poorly understood. Here, we used β  1 -adrenergic receptor and cardiomyocytes as classical examples of a therapeutically relevant GPCR and highly compartmentalized cell, to study communication between membrane receptors and subcellular cAMP nanodomains based on a combination of nanoscale scanning ion conductance microscopy assisted local receptor activation with Förster resonance energy transfer based live cell imaging of the cAMP pathway. Unexpectedly, this approach revealed that β  1 -adrenoceptors located in cardiomyocyte T-tubular membrane are strongly coupled to the regulation of cardiac contractility, whereas receptors residing in the outer non-tubular membrane preferentially engage nuclear nanodomains linked to hypertrophy. This unique mechanism of spatially segregated signalling was maintained in failing rodent and human hearts, indicating that it is conserved across species and preserved in disease. Finally, we explored potential therapeutic targeting of this mechanism by generating submembrane-specific beta-blockers acting exclusively at the outer non-tubular membrane. These improved compounds could ameliorate hypertrophy and cardiac remodeling without reducing contractility  in vitro and  in vivo . Together, these findings uncover an unexpected level of spatial organization of GPCR signaling within the same subcellular compartment and show that not only its identity but also its submembrane location determines cellular signaling and functional response engaged by the same GPCR.

title: Symptom-Demand journey map for patients with cardiometabolic multimorbidity undergoing the periprocedural pathway of percutaneous coronary intervention: A qualitative study
authorString: Shi Y, Li T, Li Y, Wang Z, Cai Z, Zhou J, Tao J.
abstractText: Background Patients with cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) face complex physical, psychosocial, and self-management demands, yet their stage-specific symptoms and care needs across the PCI pathway remain insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to map these stage-specific experiences and construct a patient journey map to inform tailored nursing care. Methods Guided by the Timing It Right (TIR) framework, we conducted a qualitative descriptive study using maximum-variation purposive sampling. Sixteen patients with CMM undergoing PCI were recruited from the Department of Cardiology at a tertiary hospital in Wuhan, China, from June to July 2026 and participated in 20 semi-structured interviews. Qualitative content analysis used four prespecified journey-map domains with inductive development of subthemes, which were synthesized into a patient journey map. Results The PCI pathway was represented by three phases: preprocedural preparation, postprocedural recovery, and transition. Forty-eight subthemes were identified across four domains: symptoms, care needs, emotions, and pain points. Preprocedural accounts emphasized symptom recognition, gaps in chronic disease self-management, and needs for procedural information and reassurance; postprocedural accounts centered on symptom burden, prognostic uncertainty, and rehabilitation support; before discharge, patients anticipated difficulties coordinating multimorbidity self-management and expressed needs for structured, multidisciplinary continuity of care. Conclusions The journey map identified distinct stage-specific patterns in symptoms, emotions, care needs, and pain points among patients with CMM undergoing PCI. These findings may help align nursing support with preprocedural information and reassurance needs, postprocedural symptom and rehabilitation needs, and pre-discharge preparation for coordinated multimorbidity self-management.

title: Native-to-fibril structural remodelling reveals an amyloid-selective transthyretin epitope for AI-guided binder design
authorString: Lomoio U, Carbonari V, Roncada P, Urbani A, Lio' P, Veltri P, Guzzi PH.
abstractText: Transthyretin (TTR) amyloidosis involves conversion of the native tetramer into cross-$\beta$ fibrils, creating potential targets for conformation-selective binders. Full-assembly solvent-accessibility analysis of 30 patient-derived fibril structures, spanning wild-type TTR and ten hereditary variants, identifies increased exposure of an N-terminal region adjacent to Cys10. Using a common normalisation reference, mean relative solvent accessibility for residues 11--15 is 0.089 in native TTR and at least 0.168 in fibrils. Modification mapping, saturation-mutagenesis stability predictions and steric PTM models provide molecular context. BoltzGen and RFAntibody generate candidate binders, and sequence-only Boltz-2 counter-predictions place selected nanobodies at the Pro11/Met13/Lys15 region in fibril-derived constructs but at distal surfaces in native-state constructs. Vitreous-fibril designs also engage cardiac-fibril constructs, suggesting cross-tissue epitope recognition. These results support structure-guided candidate prioritisation, while fibril geometry, binding affinity and disease-state selectivity require experimental validation.

title: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome and reproductive factors in postmenopausal Chinese and United States women: a cross-sectional analysis of two national survey cohorts
authorString: Chen C, Wen Y, Huang W, Yang L, Huang X, Zhang Z, Lin X.
abstractText: Background Whether female reproductive history is associated with cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome staging and cardiometabolic multimorbidity, and whether such associations differ between populations, is unclear. We examined age at menarche, parity, and age at first birth in relation to these outcomes in two national cohorts of postmenopausal women in China and the United States. Methods We analyzed 3,876 women in China postmenopausal at the 2011 examination and 4,357 naturally postmenopausal United States women. Using harmonized definitions, including a modified CKM staging based on the American Heart Association framework, we estimated prevalence ratios (PRs) by modified Poisson regression for CKM stage ≥ 2 (primary), CKM stage ≥ 3, and cardiometabolic multimorbidity, and tested whether PRs differed between cohorts. Results Later menarche was associated with lower CKM stage ≥ 2 prevalence in both cohorts (China PR 0.985/year [95% CI 0.974–0.996]; United States 0.982 [0.969–0.995]), but survived correction in the United States only. Later age at first birth was associated with lower CKM stage ≥ 2 prevalence in the United States (0.991 [0.985–0.996]) but not in China (0.997 [0.992–1.003]). For multimorbidity, later menarche was associated with lower prevalence in the United States (0.919 [0.873–0.967], survived correction), whereas age at first birth showed only a nominal association in China (0.967 [0.940–0.994], not surviving correction). Parity was not associated with any outcome. Conclusions Later menarche was associated with lower CKM stage ≥ 2 prevalence in both cohorts, with similar magnitude, although this survived correction in the United States only; later age at first birth was associated with lower prevalence in the United States only. For multimorbidity, only later menarche in the United States survived correction. Parity was not associated with any outcome, and no cross-cohort difference survived correction. In these cross-sectional analyses, reproductive history appears to be a life-course marker of modest effect size, warranting prospective evaluation rather than causal or clinical use.

title: Targeting Ferroptosis-Inflammation Crosstalk: A Novel Strategy for the Prevention and Treatment of Myocardial Ischaemia Reperfusion Injury
authorString: Zhang¹ M, Ji¹ X, Wan¹ L, Wang¹ B, Deng¹ L, Xing¹ Z, Fan¹ G, Wang¹˒² Y.
abstractText: Myocardial ischaemia-reperfusion injury (MIRI) is a major cause of residual myocardial damage following coronary revascularisation. Unfortunately, effective mechanism-based pharmacological interventions that can be translated into clinical practice remain limited. Emerging evidence indicates that ferroptosis and inflammation mutually reinforce each other and constitute a critical pathological process responsible for the amplification of myocardial injury during the early phase of reperfusion. Upon myocardial reperfusion, ferroptotic cardiomyocytes release damage-associated molecular patterns and disrupt tissue barriers, thereby activating the innate immune system and initiating inflammatory responses. In turn, inflammation promotes oxidative stress, dysregulation of iron metabolism and lipid peroxidation through the activation of inflammatory signaling pathways and the release of pro-inflammatory mediators, ultimately exacerbating ferroptosis. This reciprocal interaction establishes a self-perpetuating vicious cycle that contributes to the progression of MIRI. Encouragingly, several Western medicines and bioactive compounds derived from traditional Chinese medicine have shown therapeutic potential in modulating MIRI. This review systematically summarizes the molecular mechanisms underlying the bidirectional interaction between ferroptosis and inflammation in MIRI and discusses emerging pharmacological strategies targeting this pathological network. Collectively, the available evidence suggests that future therapeutic approaches to MIRI should extend beyond reperfusion therapy, antioxidant treatment, or anti-inflammatory intervention alone and instead consider combined strategies that simultaneously suppress inflammation and ferroptosis. Such an integrated approach may provide a novel translational framework for early risk assessment, therapeutic response prediction and targeted intervention in patients with MIRI.

title: Deceleration Capacity of the Heart Rate: Measurement Characteristics and Biological Determinants
authorString: de Ven Sv, Gevonden MJ, Noordzij ML, de Geus EJ.
abstractText: Purpose Deceleration capacity is becoming a more widely used predictor for health outcomes and cardiac autonomic dysfunction, but its measurement characteristics and biological determinants remain insufficiently understood. This study examined these factors in a large population-based sample (n = 1291) from the Netherlands Twin Register. Methods Participants wore an physiological monitoring device for 24 hours, and deceleration capacity was computed through phase-rectified signal averaging. To test whether short recordings might suffice, deceleration capacity estimates derived from 5-minute segments were compared with estimates obtained from full 24-hour ambulatory recordings. Temporal stability was examined in a subsample of participants measured again roughly three years later, and twin modeling was used to determine how much of the individual variance was explained by environmental and genetic factors. Results The results indicated that short-term deceleration capacity derived from 5-minute segments can deviate substantially from those derived from the full 24-hour recording, and that these deviations vary systematically across the day. It showed moderate to strong temporal stability across two measurement occasions roughly three years apart (r = .74, ICC(A,1) = .74).
