Overall, 102 cases were included, comprising 71 RSV (69.6%) and 31 hMPV (30.4%). hMPV cases were significantly older than RSV cases (41.5 years, interquartile range 3.5-63.0 vs. 1.5 years, interquartile range 0.2-31.0; p < 0.001) and had a higher burden of comorbidities. Myocarditis was the most frequently reported cardiac complication in both groups (87.1% hMPV vs. 74.6% RSV), followed by heart failure and pericarditis. ICU admission was more frequent among hMPV cases (96.8% vs. 77.5%; p = 0.034), whereas overall clinical outcomes did not significantly differ between groups. In exploratory multivariable analyses, dyspnea (aOR 16.280, 95% CI 1.370-193.475) and cough (aOR 6.059, 95% CI 1.062-34.552) were associated with hMPV diagnosis, whereas rhinorrhea (aOR 0.031, 95% CI 0.003-0.286) and lethargy/altered mental status (aOR 0.103, 95% CI 0.015-0.712) were associated with RSV diagnosis. ICU admission was also associated with hMPV diagnosis (aOR 11.033, 95% CI 1.125-108.173). These estimates were characterized by wide confidence intervals and should be interpreted cautiously. MCA showed substantial overlap between RSV and hMPV cases, without clear separation of their overall clinical presentation, while most between-group differences were attenuated in age-stratified analyses. In conclusion, both RSV and hMPV can be associated with a broad spectrum of potentially severe cardiac complications, with myocarditis representing the predominant reported manifestation. Despite some differences in demographic and clinical characteristics, their overall cardiac and clinical phenotypes substantially overlap. These findings support greater awareness of potential cardiac involvement during severe RSV and hMPV infections, while highlighting the need for prospective, systematically investigated cohorts to establish the incidence, mechanisms, and long-term outcomes of these complications.

title: Clinical Profile of RSV Breakthrough Infections After Nirsevimab Introduction.
authorString: Vittucci AC, Antilici L, Salvatori A, De Rose DU, Scutari R, Di Maio VC, Rotondi Aufiero L, Pisani M, Musolino AM, Dotta A, Perno CF, Villani A.
abstractText: The introduction of universal prophylaxis with nirsevimab for all children in their first epidemic season has substantially reduced the burden of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). However, a small number of breakthrough infections continue to occur despite immunization, mostly in previously healthy infants, and these cases remain incompletely characterized. We conducted a retrospective study across three epidemic seasons at a third-level hospital, including 536 RSV-positive children under 12 months of age hospitalised for bronchiolitis. Immunised infants with breakthrough infection showed a higher prevalence of prematurity and comorbidities than unimmunised infants, and were more frequently represented in the 9-12-month age group, with a median of 291 days since nirsevimab administration. Immunised infants had significantly lower odds of requiring supplemental oxygen (aOR 0.33, 95% CI 0.19-0.57, p < 0.001). However, once oxygen therapy was required, immunisation status did not independently predict the need for advanced ventilatory support. Severe breakthrough cases requiring invasive mechanical ventilation occurred even among infants without traditional risk factors. These findings confirm the substantial real-world impact of universal nirsevimab prophylaxis while underscoring the need for continued clinical vigilance and further research into the mechanisms underlying breakthrough disease.

title: Dual Role of <i>CACNA1C</i>/Ca<sub>V</sub>1.2 in Cardiac and Neuropsychiatric Disease.
authorString: Königstein D, Kisko TM, Michels S, Alferink J, Wöhr M, Culmsee C, Kockskämper J.
abstractText: The CACNA1C gene encodes the α1C subunit of voltage-gated CaV1.2 calcium channels, serving many pivotal functions throughout the body, including in the heart and brain. Clinical and genetic evidence implicates altered expression and/or function of CACNA1C/CaV1.2 in both cardiac and neuropsychiatric disease, including hypertension, cardiac arrhythmias, coronary artery disease, schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, depression, and autism. Gain-of-function mutations in CACNA1C cause Timothy syndrome, a potentially lethal multi-organ disorder with severe cardiac and neuropsychiatric defects. Conversely, the complete loss of Cacna1c is lethal in mice. The development of viable mouse and rat models with Cacna1c haploinsufficiency has allowed us to study the consequences of reduced expression and function of Cacna1c/CaV1.2 for heart and brain function from the molecular and cellular to the behavioral level. We review recent findings from these rodent models, revealing (i) alterations in behavior and (ii) in neuronal and non-neuronal function, as well as (iii) an impaired ability of the heart and its cardiomyocytes to adapt to (sympathetic) stress. Results lend further support to the notion that CACNA1C/CaV1.2 dysfunction represents a common link between cardiac and neuropsychiatric disorders and that appropriately targeting CACNA1C/CaV1.2 in selected patients may hold the promise of treating both conditions effectively with a single drug.

title: Beyond the Image: Pitfalls, Cognitive Biases, and Safety Gaps in Non-Cardiac Neonatal Point-of-Care Ultrasound.
authorString: Costache A, Vasilescu DI, Vasilescu SL, Gogoncea AR, Dan AM.
abstractText: Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) is now part of everyday work in neonatal intensive care, supporting diagnosis, procedures, and decisions in acutely unwell infants. Its spread has outpaced the development of training, credentialing, and quality assurance structures, and the neonatal literature rarely describes how and why the technique fails. In this perspective, we focus on non-cardiac neonatal POCUS (lung, cranial, and abdominal). We adapt existing frameworks into four error domains: indication, image acquisition, image interpretation, and clinical integration. We also separate errors that can occur in any ultrasound examination from those tied to the point-of-care setting, including confirmation, anchoring, and availability bias, time pressure, and fatigue. Using illustrative cases and comparative tables, we describe common look-alike findings, summarize thermal and mechanical bioeffects by organ, and discuss probe and gel hygiene in the neonatal unit. We then outline a stepwise pathway for training, supervision, credentialing, and quality assurance, and suggest practical safeguards: structured protocols and reports, simple debiasing habits, image archiving with periodic expert review, and close collaboration with radiology and cardiology. Seen in this way, investment in safety is part of the value of neonatal POCUS rather than an added cost.

title: PAI-1, <i>MTHFR</i>, and FVL Thrombophilic Polymorphisms as Risk Factors for Fetal Growth Restriction: A Case-Control Study from a Tertiary Care Center.
authorString: Pană RC, Anghel-Savciu NL, Dinu M, Ruican D, Petrescu AM, Dan AO, Târtea EA, Greșiță A, Hădăreanu DR, Tudorașcu DR, Târtea G.
abstractText: Background/Objectives: Fetal growth restriction (FGR) is one of the main causes of perinatal morbidity and mortality, and in most cases the mechanism is placental dysfunction of vascular origin. Hereditary thrombophilias have been evaluated as factors that favor maternal vascular malperfusion, but the data in the literature remain contradictory. The objective of the study was to evaluate the association between the PAI-1 4G/5G, MTHFR C677T and factor V Leiden G1691A polymorphisms and fetal growth restriction, as well as to analyze the dose-effect relationship between the number of thrombophilic variants and the severity of restriction. Methods: This was a retrospective case-control study including 480 singleton pregnancies: 240 cases with fetal growth restriction and 240 pregnant women with eutrophic fetuses, followed up for a period of five years. Cases were defined biometrically as an estimated fetal weight below the 10th centile, without Doppler confirmation, and the phenotype therefore corresponds to small-for-gestational-age rather than to the full consensus definition of fetal growth restriction; a secondary analysis restricted to cases below the 5th centile, performed in response to review, is reported. Maternal characteristics, genotypes, perinatal outcomes, and cumulative pattern of thrombophilic variants were analyzed. Results: PAI-1 4G allele carriers were significantly more frequent in the growth restriction group compared to the control group (70.8% vs. 44.6%; OR 3.02; 95% CI 2.07-4.40; p < 0.001), as were MTHFR C677T allele carriers (57.1% vs. 39.2%; OR 2.07; 95% CI 1.44-2.97; p < 0.001) and factor V Leiden carriers (33.3% vs. 12.1%; OR 3.64; 95% CI 2.27-5.83; p < 0.001). Carrier prevalence increased progressively with severity of restriction for the PAI-1 4G allele and, most steeply, for factor V Leiden (from 12.1% in controls to 75.0% below the 3rd centile; trend test p < 0.001); for the MTHFR 677T allele the increase was confined in the two case strata above the 3rd centile, and the estimate in the smallest subgroup was uninformative. The risk of growth restriction increased with the number of coexisting thrombophilic variants: OR 2.12 (95% CI 1.24-3.64) for one variant, OR 5.60 (95% CI 3.21-9.78) for two, and OR 24.42 (95% CI 7.87-75.78) for all three, compared with the absence of any variant. In multivariable analysis, the three polymorphisms remained independent predictors, with the strongest adjusted association being that of factor V Leiden (adjusted OR 3.33; 95% CI 2.03-5.47). Carriage of each variant was associated with a lower birth-weight centile: -12.3 points for PAI-1 4G, -10.2 for factor V Leiden and -8.0 for MTHFR C677T (all p < 0.001). Conclusions: In this study, PAI-1 4G/5G, MTHFR C677T, and factor V Leiden polymorphisms were independently associated with fetal growth restriction. The results are compatible with a contribution of hypofibrinolysis and inherited thrombophilia to the placental insufficiency phenotype, most clearly in the more severe strata, but they are associative and require confirmation in prospective cohorts incorporating Doppler assessment and placental histopathology.

title: Risk Stratification, Exercise Prescription, and Sport Participation in Individuals with Aortic Valve Disease.
authorString: Perone F, Conte E, Palermi S, Halasz G, Ambrosetti M, Sciarra L, Frati G, Peruzzi M, Cavarretta E, Pingitore A.

journal.title: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease

abstractText: Aortic valve disease (AVD), including bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) and aortic regurgitation (AR), presents a complex challenge in sports cardiology. Balancing the cardiovascular benefits of physical activity with the hemodynamic risks associated with valvular dysfunction and aortopathy requires precise risk stratification. The present review comprehensively analyses the contemporary criteria for exercise prescription and competitive sports participation in individuals with AVD, highlighting also the distinctions between the European guidelines (European Society of Cardiology-ESC), the Italian Sports Cardiology Guidelines for competitive sport practice (COCIS 2023) and the recommendations for exercise prescription in cardiovascular diseases promoted by the Italian Sports Cardiology Society (SIC Sport) and the Italian Federation for Sports Medicine (FMSI). Relevant differences with the 2025 AHA/ACC recommendations are also highlighted where they may influence sports eligibility. Eligibility hinges primarily on the degree of valvular defect, left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), and aortic dimensions. Furthermore, post-operative sports participation is highly contingent on the intervention type, post-operative results and follow-up. Ultimately, safe exercise prescription relies on meticulous clinical surveillance, advanced imaging, maximal stress testing, and a shared decision-making process to maximize cardiovascular health while mitigating the risk of acute adverse events.

title: Histomorphometry and Immunohistochemistry of Xenogeneic Collagen Matrix: A Randomized Split-Mouth Clinical Study.
authorString: Barros MSV, Nunes MP, Clark ATR, Pinho RCM, Godoy GP, Fontan C, Vajgel BCF, Cimões R.
abstractText:
Objectives

To histomorphometrically evaluate collagen formation and immunohistochemically assess soft tissue vascularization around implants after treatment with xenogeneic acellular collagen matrix versus connective tissue graft in a randomized split-mouth clinical study.

Materials and methods

Nine patients underwent implant rehabilitation with connective tissue graft and xenogeneic acellular collagen matrix in contralateral edentulous areas. A total of 24 grafts were performed (12 each). Grafts were assigned to healing times of 30 (n = 4), 90 (n = 4), or 180 days (n = 4), at which time samples were collected for histological and immunohistochemical analysis. Collagen quality and density were assessed histologically. Vascularization, vessel density, and diameter were evaluated immunohistochemically. Samples were stained with Masson's trichrome for collagen and immunostained with CD34 for vascular endothelium; the grafted site was the unit of analysis.

Results

The percentage of collagen was higher in sites biopsied at 180 days for both grafts and was similar between groups at all healing periods. Xenogeneic acellular collagen matrix showed vascularization patterns similar to autogenous connective tissue graft, with higher vessel density and vascular percentage at 90 days, while differences between groups were observed only at 30 days.

Conclusions

Within the limitations of this study, xenogeneic acellular collagen matrix demonstrated collagen maturation at the later healing periods and vascularization patterns with histological characteristics similar to those of the connective tissue graft during the evaluated healing periods.

Trial registration

Brazilian Registry of Clinical Trials (ReBEC), RBR-4vgzyt.

title: Cardiac Computed Tomography in Infective Endocarditis: A Radiological Perspective on Structural Complications and Emerging Diagnostic Technologies.
authorString: Popa LE, Boca B, Jula DT, Tomoaia R, Schiau C, Ștefan PA, Rancea R, Beyer RȘ, Molnar A, Lupșor-Platon M.
abstractText: Background: Infective endocarditis (IE) remains a life-threatening disease associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. Transthoracic and transesophageal echocardiography are the first-line imaging modalities, but their diagnostic performance may be reduced in patients with prosthetic valves, intracardiac devices, previous cardiac surgery, extensive calcification, or suspected periannular extension. Cardiac computed tomography (CT) provides complementary high-resolution anatomical information and has gained increasing importance within contemporary multimodality diagnostic pathways. Scope: This Review critically examines the current role of cardiac CT in IE, including acquisition and reconstruction strategies, lesion-specific imaging findings, applications in native, prosthetic, transcatheter, and device-related infection, extracardiac assessment, and preoperative planning. Comparative observations regarding echocardiography and selected multimodality techniques are integrated where directly relevant. Emerging applications of spectral CT, photon-counting detector CT, deep learning reconstruction, radiomics, and artificial intelligence are appraised according to four levels of evidence: clinically validated IE applications, preliminary IE-specific evidence, indirect cardiovascular evidence, and conceptual applications. Main Findings: Cardiac CT is particularly valuable for detecting and anatomically characterizing periannular complications, including abscesses, pseudoaneurysms, fistulous tracts, inflammatory extension, and prosthetic dehiscence. Multiphase electrocardiography (ECG)-gated acquisition improves the assessment of dynamic valvular and prosthetic abnormalities. Transesophageal echocardiography remains more sensitive for small or highly mobile vegetations, leaflet perforation, regurgitant jets, and intracardiac flow abnormalities, demonstrating that the two techniques are complementary rather than interchangeable. Cardiac CT also contributes to coronary assessment, surgical planning, evaluation of previous grafts and reconstructive material, and selected extracardiac complications. Conclusions: Cardiac CT is an important component of contemporary multimodality IE assessment, but it should not be regarded as a replacement for echocardiography. Its clinical value depends on the infected substrate, suspected complication, acquisition protocol, and integration with echocardiographic, microbiological, surgical, and clinical findings. Emerging technologies may improve image quality and quantitative characterization, but most remain supported by preliminary IE-specific, indirect cardiovascular, or conceptual evidence and should not yet be considered established IE-specific diagnostic tools.

title: Incidence, Mortality, and Survival Trends of Liver Cancer in the Canton of Zurich, Switzerland, Between 1980 and 2022.
authorString: Zuber N, Suter F, Wanner M, Korol D, Rohrmann S.
abstractText:
Background

The global burden of liver cancer has been increasing over recent decades, whereas the incidence in Switzerland has remained relatively stable. This study assessed long-term trends in incidence, mortality, and 1- and 5-year relative survival of primary liver cancer in the Swiss canton of Zurich from 1980 to 2022, stratified by sex and age.

Methods

This population-based retrospective analysis included all primary liver cancer cases diagnosed in the canton of Zurich and registered in the Cancer Registry of the cantons of Zurich, Zug, Schaffhausen and Schwyz between 1980 and 2022. Mortality data were obtained from the Federal Statistical Office. Cases were classified according to ICD-O-3 topography and morphology and, from 2003 onward, TNM stage. Age-standardised incidence and mortality rates were calculated using the 1976 European standard population. Temporal trends were analysed using Joinpoint regression and reported as Average Annual Percentage Changes (AAPCs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Relative survival was estimated using the Ederer II method and standardised according to international standards.

Results

Among 3866 incident cases, 71.3% were hepatocellular carcinomas and 70.7% occurred in men. Overall age-standardised incidence remained stable in both men (AAPC -0.1%, 95% CI -0.6 to 0.3%) and women (-0.2%, -0.9% to 0.4%). However, incidence increased significantly among individuals younger than 65 years, particularly in women (AAPC 2.3%, 1.3%-3.3%) and men (1.2%, 0.6%-1.9%). Mortality remained broadly stable in men and increased modestly in women. One- and five-year relative survival improved substantially, from 13.8% and 3.5% in 1980-1999 to 53.9% and 25.8% in 2016-2022, respectively. Improvements were greater in men than women.

Conclusion

These findings reflect major advances in liver cancer diagnosis and treatment over the past four decades. Continued prevention, targeted screening of high-risk groups, and epidemiological monitoring remain important.

title: NSG Mice Lacking Apoe: An Immunodeficient Mouse Model of Atherosclerosis.
authorString: Megathlin HR, Burzenski L, Coleman DA, Albert B, Farley ML, Brehm MA, Greiner DL, Shultz LD.

journal.title: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology

abstractText: Murine research on atherosclerosis has been conducted largely on the C57BL/6 (B6) strain background, and most commonly, the B6.129P2-Apoe<sup>tm1Unc</sup>/J (B6-ApoE<sup>KO</sup>) strain. The use of the B6 background strain limits translatability for immunotherapy development due to inherent species differences between human and mouse immune systems. A proposed solution to this limitation is a humanized mouse model of atherosclerosis that would support the engraftment of human lymphoid and myeloid cell populations. The development of such a model has been hindered by the lack of a mouse strain that both develops atherosclerosis and supports human immune cell engraftment. In this paper, we report on a NOD.Cg-Prkdc<sup>scid</sup>Il2rg<sup>tm1Wjl</sup>/Sz (NSG) immunodeficient mouse strain that has a 383 bp deletion in the Apoe gene which prevents ApoE protein expression. When maintained on a high fat diet, NSG-ApoE<sup>KO</sup> mice develop hypercholesteremia and atherosclerosis at levels similar to B6-ApoE<sup>KO</sup> mice. While atherosclerosis in B6-ApoE<sup>KO</sup> mice has been widely studied in many laboratories under multiple conditions, our initial study of disease development in NSG-ApoE<sup>KO</sup> mice was limited and future comparative studies with B6-ApoE<sup>KO</sup> mice are necessary. NSG-ApoE<sup>KO</sup> mice concomitantly support human cell engraftment while developing atherosclerosis, thereby making them useful to study human-specific immune aspects.

title: When the Conversation Is the Intervention: Serious Illness Communication Skills in Adult Congenital Heart Disease.
authorString: Serfas JD, Jersak TH.

title: Incident Atrial Fibrillation Following Anthracycline-Based Adjuvant Chemotherapy in Women with Breast Cancer: A Single-Centre Retrospective Cohort Study.
authorString: Arslan A, Çağaç Ö, Beşiroğlu F, Hünük B.
abstractText: Background/Objectives: Anthracyclines carry considerable cardiotoxicity risk, and atrial fibrillation (AF) during cancer treatment adversely affects morbidity and mortality. We compared the incidence of clinically documented AF and explored its early clinical correlates between anthracycline-containing and non-anthracycline adjuvant regimens in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). Methods: This single-centre retrospective cohort included consecutive women with stage II TNBC treated with breast-conserving surgery and adjuvant doxorubicin-cyclophosphamide followed by docetaxel (AC-T) or docetaxel-cyclophosphamide (TC) between 2018 and 2023. ECG and echocardiography were performed at baseline, month one, and month six. Clinically documented AF was defined as AF documented on a scheduled or symptom-triggered 12-lead ECG or as AF lasting ≥30 s on symptom-triggered 72 h Holter monitoring. Patients with structural or coronary heart disease, complete bundle branch block, or non-sinus rhythm were excluded. Results: Among 140 women (mean age, 64 ± 12 years; 64 AC-T), 17 (12.1%) developed clinically documented AF within six months. AF was more frequent with AC-T (18.8% vs. 6.6%; absolute risk difference, 12.2% [95% CI, 1.1-23.3%]; risk ratio, 2.85 [1.07-7.58]; log-rank p = 0.030), and the association persisted after inverse probability of treatment weighting (OR, 3.28 [1.05-10.24]). At one month, PR prolongation > 20 ms was associated with incident AF (OR, 5.16 [1.79-14.89]), whereas conventional echocardiographic changes did not differ between regimens. Conclusions: The AC-T regimen was associated with more clinically documented incident AF than TC. Early PR prolongation, occurring without detectable changes in conventional echocardiographic parameters, may be an informative early electrical signal of AF risk, although prospective validation is required.

title: Monthly variations in admissions of pediatric asthma versus respiratory infections during spring: A multicenter study.
authorString: Alharbi NS, Alhassan I, Alenizi AS, Alanazi A, Alharbi AH, Alqurashi FO, Yousef AA, Alsohime F.
abstractText:
Background

Asthma and acute lower respiratory tract infections (LRTI), including pneumonia and bronchiolitis, are leading causes of pediatric hospitalizations. In arid regions, environmental factors such as desert dust storms vary across spring months and may differentially influence asthma compared with infectious respiratory illnesses. Whether asthma hospitalizations demonstrate month-specific variation during spring remains unclear.

Methods

We conducted a multicenter retrospective study at four tertiary centers in Saudi Arabia. Pediatric patients aged ≤14 years admitted with asthma, pneumonia, or bronchiolitis during the spring months (March-May) of 2018 and 2019 were included. Admissions were categorized as asthma or LRTI. Demographic characteristics, clinical outcomes, respiratory viral detection, and monthly distribution were compared using nonparametric and Chi-square tests.

Results

Among 729 admissions, 153 (21.0%) were for asthma and 576 (79.0%) for LRTI. Children with asthma were older (median: 48 [interquartile ranges 24-96] vs. 16 [6-34] months; P < 0.001) and had shorter hospital stays (3 [2-4] vs. 4 [3-7] days; P < 0.001). No significant differences were observed in sex distribution, intensive care unit admission, or ventilatory support. Respiratory viral detection was lower in asthma than LRTI (3.2% vs. 24.7%; P = 0.003). The monthly distribution of asthma relative to LRTI did not differ across March, April, and May.

Conclusion

Pediatric asthma hospitalizations during spring were characterized by older age, shorter stays, and lower viral detection compared with LRTI. Asthma did not demonstrate month-specific variation, suggesting that fluctuating environmental exposures did not generate population-level surges. These findings support diagnosis-specific interpretation of seasonal pediatric respiratory admissions and warrant investigation into nonviral asthma triggers.

title: Association of the Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index with Ascending Aortic Diameter and Dilatation: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study.
authorString: Yılmaz S, Nahir M, Çelik A.
abstractText: Background and Objectives: Complete blood count-derived inflammatory indices are inexpensive and widely available, but data on their relationship with ascending aortic size are limited. This study examined the association between the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) and ascending aortic diameter, and compared these indices according to the presence of ascending aortic dilatation (AAD) defined by a 40 mm threshold. Materials and Methods: In this single-centre retrospective cross-sectional study, 251 patients aged 18 years or older (mean age, 53.1 ± 16.7 years; range, 18-95 years; 160 men) who underwent thoracic computed tomography angiography were grouped by maximum tubular ascending aortic diameter (<40 mm, n = 158; ≥40 mm, n = 93). Inference for the primary linear model was based on heteroscedasticity-consistent (HC3) standard errors. Height and weight were not recorded, so the models could not be adjusted for body size. Results: In unadjusted comparisons, platelet and neutrophil counts, creatinine and all five inflammatory indices were nominally higher in the dilated group (all p < 0.05), whereas C-reactive protein did not differ. In the primary adjusted model, each 100-unit increase in SII was associated with a 0.59 mm greater ascending aortic diameter (HC3 95% CI 0.28 to 0.90; β = 0.197; p < 0.001), approximately 1.6 mm across the interquartile range of SII; the model explained 26.9% of the variance. Higher SII was also associated with AAD in the secondary logistic model (odds ratio per 100 units, 1.34; 95% CI 1.17 to 1.53; p < 0.001). Discrimination was weak (area under the curve for SII, 0.658; 95% CI 0.590 to 0.726); the sample-derived cut-off gave a positive likelihood ratio of 1.38, and its 2.5-97.5th percentile interval on bootstrap internal validation was 305 to 579. None of the 75 correlations survived false discovery rate adjustment, and the SII-by-sex interaction was not significant (p = 0.621). Conclusions: Higher SII was associated with a greater ascending aortic diameter and with the presence of AAD after adjustment for the measured covariates; because body size could not be accounted for, residual confounding cannot be excluded. The adjusted difference was modest and discrimination was weak. These findings do not support the use of SII as a standalone diagnostic marker for ascending aortic dilatation.

title: Preoperative Advanced Lung Cancer Inflammation Index and Acute Kidney Injury After Adult Cardiac Surgery: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
authorString: Gan H, Zhang R, Fan R, Yin L, Ning S, Wang J, Liu D, Chen W, Chen X, Qiu Z.

journal.title: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease

abstractText: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is common after cardiac surgery. We assessed the association between the preoperative advanced lung cancer inflammation index (ALI) and postoperative AKI. This retrospective cohort included adults undergoing cardiac surgery from 2 January 2019 to 16 March 2026. The primary outcome was the first in-hospital AKI recorded within 168 h using stored Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes creatinine and kidney-replacement-therapy classifications. Among 11,890 adults, AKI was recorded in 3380 (28.4%). Each ALI doubling was associated with a lower adjusted AKI rate (hazard ratio, 0.83; 95% confidence interval, 0.80-0.86; p < 0.001); the fixed-horizon risk ratio was 0.86 (95% confidence interval, 0.83-0.88; p < 0.001). Adjustment for available preoperative shock, resuscitation, intubation, infective endocarditis, acute aortic disease, and catecholamine indicators attenuated the hazard ratio to 0.90 (95% confidence interval, 0.87-0.94). Association magnitude differed across mutually exclusive procedure categories (interaction p < 0.001). The coefficient constraints imposed by ALI were rejected, and the positive BMI association persisted with flexible modeling. Lower ALI was associated with more recorded AKI, but differential monitoring, residual confounding, and unsupported component constraints limit interpretation of the composite.

title: Efficacy of Ultrasound-Guided Pectointercostal Fascial Block Versus Control and Alternative Regional Techniques in Cardiac Surgery: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis with Dose-Response Analysis.
authorString: Elnahas M, Zidan M, Abusamra Y, Hassan M, Saravi B, Hochrein S, Lang P.
abstractText: Background and Objectives: Ultrasound-guided pectointercostal fascial block (USG-PIFB) is increasingly used for post-sternotomy analgesia, but its efficacy remains uncertain. Prior meta-analyses pooled ultrasound-guided blocks with surgeon-performed infiltration, introducing heterogeneity. We aimed to determine the analgesic efficacy of USG-PIFB in adult cardiac surgery by restricting inclusion to ultrasound-guided techniques. Materials and Methods: Six databases were searched through December 2025, with an update search of open sources and trial registries in September 2026, for randomized controlled trials comparing USG-PIFB with control (Comparison 1) or with an alternative regional technique (Comparison 2) in adults undergoing sternotomy. The primary outcome was 24-h opioid consumption in intravenous morphine milligram equivalents. Random-effects meta-analysis (REML, Knapp-Hartung), subgroup, sensitivity and meta-regression analyses, an exploratory trial sequential analysis and GRADE assessment were performed. Results: Twenty-nine trials (2664 participants) were included: 24 in Comparison 1 and eight in Comparison 2. In 13 trials (902 participants), USG-PIFB reduced 24-h opioid consumption (mean difference -6.60 mg; 95% CI, -10.92 to -2.27; I2 = 97.7%), but the 95% prediction interval (-22.24 to 9.04 mg) included no effect and small-study effects could not be excluded. Pain scores were lower by 0.8 to 1.4 points at rest (extubation, 12 and 24 h) and during movement (12 h). Extubation was earlier and intensive care stay shorter, with extreme heterogeneity. No dose-response relationship was detected, and the difference from deep parasternal techniques was near zero. No local anesthetic systemic toxicity or block-attributable pneumothorax was reported; one block-site hematoma occurred in a USG-PIFB recipient. Certainty of evidence was low for rescue analgesic use and block-related complications and very low for all other outcomes. Conclusions: USG-PIFB may modestly reduce 24-h opioid consumption, but the magnitude and reproducibility of this effect across clinical settings remain uncertain. It is best regarded as one component of multimodal analgesia, and adequately powered multicentre trials are needed.

title: Genetic Patterns in Familial Thoracic Aortic Aneurysm Disease.
authorString: Harling LC, Zafar MA, Changez MIK, Papanikolaou D, Celik NB, Grewal N, Elefteriades JA.
abstractText:
Background and aims

We examined familial patterns and phenotypes of thoracic aortic aneurysms and dissections (TAAD) in the 3746 patients currently populating our Yale Aortic Institute Database.

Methods

Patient charts and electronic medical records were retrospectively reviewed for the entire cohort. TAAD disease was categorized as syndromic (with extra-aortic manifestations) or non-syndromic (without) for each patient. Family patterns and whole exome sequencing results were assessed. Family history was considered 'proven' when a patient's relative(s) had an arterial aneurysm or dissection confirmed by an imaging study, surgical treatment, or postmortem examination. Family history was termed 'likely' when at least one relative suffered sudden death at ages ≤50 for males and ≤60 for females, and 'possible' with a history of sudden death at any age.

Results

Of the 3746 patients in the database, family history of aneurysm or dissection and connective tissue status was able to be determined for 3113 patients, divided into 109 (3.5%) syndromic and 3004 (96.5%) non-syndromic TAAD patients. Findings were as follows: (1) In the syndromic group, 46 (42.2%) patients had a 'proven' family history, 6 (5.5%) had a 'likely' family history, 4 (3.7%) had a 'possible' family history, and 18 (16.5%) had 'none'. For 35 patients (32.1%) their family history was unknown. (2) In the non-syndromic group, 587 (19.5%) patients had 'proven' family history, 147 (4.9%) had 'likely' family history, 210 (7.0%) had 'possible' family history and 1444 (48.1%) had no family history, thus representing sporadic TAAD. A total of 616 (20.5%) had an unknown family history. (3) There was a significant difference between the rate for 'proven' and 'none' family history between the syndromic and non-syndromic groups (42.2% vs. 19.5% and 16.5% vs. 48.1%, respectively; p < 0.001). (4) Syndromic patients presented at a significantly younger age than non-syndromic or sporadic patients (41.2 vs. 63.3 or 63.6; p < 0.001). (5) There was no significant difference in age of presentation between familial non-syndromic (patients with 'proven', 'likely', and 'possible' family history) and sporadic patients (63.3 vs. 63.6; p = 0.64). (6) Overall, of the 3746 patients in the database, 631 patients (25 syndromic, 552 non-syndromic, and 54 with unknown status) underwent Whole Exome Sequencing (WES). Sequencing revealed 170 disease-causing or suspicious variants [13 pathogenic, 16 likely pathogenic, 7 not classified, and 134 Variants of Uncertain Significance (VUS)] found in the exomes of 141 (22.3%) patients (12 syndromic, 103 non-syndromic TAAD patients plus a remaining 26 of unknown connective tissue status). Seventy (49.6%) of these patients had a 'proven' family history. (7) Familial TAAD patients were more likely to find a variant in their WES result than patients without a family history (70 vs. 26; p < 0.001). Recognition of these strong familial patterns, even in non-syndromic cases, encourages intensive investigation of family in order to save lives by detecting silent TAA disease.

Conclusions

Our large-scale, clinical and sequencing-based study clearly demonstrates the strongly familial and genetically mediated nature of thoracic aortic disease. We vividly demonstrate and characterize this familial nature of TAAD, both clinically and by genetic sequencing. Our findings strongly support vigorous family investigation when a new patient is diagnosed with thoracic aortic aneurysm, as well as vigorous application of whole exome sequencing for these families.

title: Beyond Remodeling: Four Structural-Functional Recovery Patterns as a Framework for Interpreting Ventricular Recovery After Reperfused STEMI.
authorString: Crăciun-Mirescu A, Mirea O, Toader DE, Berceanu MC, Rădulescu VM, Moise CG, Delcea RD, Militaru C, Militaru C.
abstractText: Background/Objectives: Ventricular recovery after ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) is commonly assessed using either structural (volumetric) or functional (ejection-fraction) criteria, although these may capture different aspects of recovery. We examined whether their cross-classification identifies distinct recovery patterns and whether myocardial mechanics and left atrial function provide additional information. Methods: We prospectively followed 101 patients with first STEMI and single-vessel coronary artery disease treated with PCI. Echocardiography was performed 12-24 h after reperfusion and at 12 ± 2 months. Structural recovery (≥15% reduction in 3D LV end-systolic volume) and functional recovery (≥5-point absolute LVEF increase) were cross-classified into four recovery patterns. Results: Among 53 patients with complete paired measurements, 10 (18.9%) showed concordant recovery, 7 (13.2%) isolated structural recovery, 9 (17.0%) isolated functional recovery, and 27 (50.9%) no recovery; 30.2% therefore showed discordant recovery. The no-recovery group was heterogeneous, including both volumetric deterioration and stable or improving volumes below the recovery threshold. Continuous changes in 3D-ESV and LVEF were only moderately correlated (ρ = 0.353, p = 0.0095), and discordance persisted in sensitivity analyses. Myocardial mechanics and LASR did not differentiate recovery patterns, but several of these baseline markers showed exploratory associations with clinical outcomes after false-discovery-rate correction. Conclusions: Structural and functional recovery after STEMI are complementary rather than interchangeable, and this discordance persisted across extensive sensitivity analyses; however, assignment of individual patients to specific recovery categories remained sensitive to the chosen thresholds and LVEF measurement method. Myocardial mechanics and LASR may provide additional information about clinical expression.

title: Evidence of Selective Response in the Free-Breeding Dog Population in Chornobyl.
authorString: Dillon MN, Roberts RB, Betz JA, Mousseau TA, Kleiman NJ, Breen M.
abstractText: Background/Objectives: Understanding genomic responses to environmental contamination is essential for assessing long-term ecological and genetic risk. The free-breeding dogs inhabiting the Chornobyl Exclusion Zone (CEZ) offer a unique, multigenerational model for investigating these responses within a chronically contaminated landscape. Following the 1986 radioecological disaster at the Chornobyl Nuclear Power Plant, and subsequent remediation activities, the surrounding environment was contaminated by ionizing radiation, heavy metals, organic compounds, and other environmental toxicants. Our previous work identified significant genetic differentiation between two distinct but geographically proximate dog populations within the CEZ, a pattern not explained by breed composition, spatial isolation, or increased mutation rates. Methods: In this study, we tested the hypothesis that the dogs residing at the nuclear power plant show genomic signatures consistent with adaptive evolution in response to chronic environmental stressors. This work extends prior population-genetic analyses by integrating whole-genome selection scans with estimates of effective population size and comparative measures of population divergence, providing a framework to evaluate whether the observed genomic differentiation is more consistent with selection than demography. Using these whole genomic data, we evaluated chromosome-level FST metrics, estimated effective population size (Ne), and analyzed a geographically isolated island dog population as a comparative reference for genetic divergence. Results: We continued to find that the levels of genetic differentiation are not comparable to other free-breeding dog populations. Genome-wide outlier analyses identified candidate loci showing evidence of positive selection across multiple metrics. Conclusions: Genes associated with these loci were enriched for biological functions related to DNA replication and repair, cell death and survival, cellular compromise, immune response, and cancer-associated pathways, suggesting biologically plausible mechanisms through which chronic environmental stress could influence fitness. These findings are consistent with directional selection in the nuclear power plant population, which could potentially be associated with the environmental variables present, and advance our understanding of local adaptation and genomic resilience under chronic environmental contamination.

title: Efficiency of Blood Utilization in Elective Neurosurgery Patients and Development of a Maximum Surgical Blood Order Schedule.
authorString: Javed Z, Siddiqui M, Bari F, Laghari AA, Hussain N, Bari ME.
abstractText: Objectives Primary Objective  To evaluate the efficiency of perioperative blood utilization in elective neurosurgical procedures using the crossmatch-to-transfusion (C/T) ratio, transfusion probability (TP), and transfusion index (TI). Secondary Objective  To develop procedure-specific maximum surgical blood ordering schedules (MSBOS) using Mead's criteria, categorizing procedures according to the need for no routine preoperative blood preparation, type-and-screen (T&S) only, or preoperative crossmatching, and to determine the recommended number of packed cell volume (PCV) units for procedures requiring crossmatching. Materials and methods A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted over six months at a tertiary care hospital. A total of 142 patients (100%) undergoing elective neurosurgical procedures were included. Details of blood grouping, cross-matching, and blood transfusion were recorded for each patient. Blood utilization was assessed using the C/T ratio, TP, and TI, and the MSBOS was formulated according to Mead's criteria. Statistical analysis The C/T ratio, TP, and TI were calculated using standard formulae. The MSBOS was derived using the formula MSBOS = 1.5 × TI to recommend the appropriate number of preoperative blood units for elective neurosurgical procedures. Results Blood grouping and cross-matching were performed in 136 (95.7%) and 135 (95.4%) patients, respectively. Blood transfusion was required in 29 patients (20.4%), with 44 units transfused. The overall C/T ratio was 9.1, while the TP and TI were 22.3% and 0.33, respectively, indicating inefficient blood utilization. Relatively efficient blood utilization was observed in spinal tumour surgery, aneurysm clipping, and meningioma resection. Based on the calculated MSBOS, one unit of packed red blood cells (PRBCs) was recommended for laminectomy, spine fixation, spinal tumour surgery, aneurysm clipping, and posterior fossa surgery, whereas two units were recommended for meningioma resection. Conclusions Blood utilization in elective neurosurgical procedures was inefficient. Implementation of a procedure-specific MSBOS may reduce unnecessary cross-matching, optimize blood resource utilization, and improve transfusion practices in neurosurgical patients.

title: Human Milk, Protein Adequacy, and Neurodevelopment in Preterm Infants: A Narrative Review.
authorString: Mizuno K.
abstractText: Human milk is increasingly recognized not only as a source of nutrition but also as a biological regulator of organ development in preterm infants. Beyond supporting growth, human milk contains a complex array of bioactive components that influence intestinal maturation, immune function, vascular development, and brain development during a critical period of extrauterine adaptation. This narrative review summarizes current evidence regarding the role of human milk in multi-organ development in preterm infants. We review clinical and mechanistic studies demonstrating associations between human milk exposure and reduced risks of necrotizing enterocolitis, late-onset sepsis, bronchopulmonary dysplasia, and retinopathy of prematurity. Particular attention is given to the interconnected gut-immune-lung-retina-brain axis and the biological pathways through which human milk may influence developmental outcomes. We further discuss the importance of early enteral feeding, adequate protein delivery, and human milk-derived fortification in supporting growth quality, lean mass accretion, head growth, and structural brain development. Emerging evidence suggests that nutritional strategies promoting early and sustained human milk exposure may contribute not only to protection from major prematurity-related morbidities but also to improved neurodevelopmental trajectories. By integrating current biological and clinical evidence, this review highlights the role of human milk as a foundation for developmental nutrition in preterm infants and provides a practical perspective for optimizing nutritional care in the neonatal intensive care unit.

title: Learning Curve and Early Outcomes of Thoracoscopic Esophageal Atresia Repair in an Emerging Pediatric Minimally Invasive Surgery (MIS) Program: A Cumulative Sum Analysis.
authorString: Moga A, Cîmpeanu P, Bălănescu L, Bălănescu R.
abstractText:
Background

Thoracoscopic repair of esophageal atresia with tracheoesophageal fistula (EA/TEF) remains technically challenging due to the rarity of these procedures and the demanding intracorporeal suturing within the confined neonatal thorax. The aim of this study is to report the learning curve and early outcomes during the transition from open to thoracoscopic EA/TEF repair at a single center, evaluated using the cumulative sum (CUSUM) method.

Methods

We retrospectively reviewed data of 79 consecutive EA/TEF patients operated on between January 2015 and June 2026. Twenty-eight underwent thoracoscopic repair and 51 open repairs. The open cohort served as a historical institutional comparator, reflecting the standard of care prior to the adoption of thoracoscopic technique. The thoracoscopic group was stratified into three learning curve phases: Early (n = 9), Intermediate (n = 9), and Proficient (n = 10). Anastomotic leak was defined by contrast extravasation on postoperative esophagogram. Complications were graded using the Clavien-Dindo classification.

Results

The mean operative time was 2.9 ± 1.2 h (thoracoscopic) vs. 2.3 ± 1.2 h (open; p = 0.036). CUSUM analysis demonstrated a learning curve of approximately 15 cases, with operative time decreasing from 3.4 h (Phase 1) to 2.5 h (Phase 3; p = 0.034). Anastomotic leak occurred in 9/28 (32.1%) vs. 7/51 (13.7%; p = 0.137; underpowered comparison). Within the thoracoscopic group, long-gap patients (n = 8) had significantly higher stricture rates (37.5% vs. 0%; p = 0.017) and longer hospital stays (66 vs. 30 days; p = 0.005). The three long-gap patients with stricture required 11 total endoscopic dilation sessions. No statistically significant difference in mortality was observed (7.1% vs. 5.9%; p = 1.000).

Conclusions

Thoracoscopic EA/TEF repair is feasible in an emerging MIS program with acceptable complication rates. The CUSUM-based learning curve was 15 cases. Long-gap thoracoscopic repair carries significantly higher stricture risk.

title: Specific Factors Associated with Iatrogenic Withdrawal Syndrome in Children After Cardiac Surgery.
authorString: Hüners I, Schumann S, Schön G, Biermann D, Denecke J, Gottschalk U, Jürgensen PP, Siebel LC, Jess F, Simons SHP, Gleitze-Nolting C, Carstens H, Hübler M, Kozlik-Feldmann RG, Reiss IKM, Harms SH.
abstractText: Background/Objectives: Iatrogenic withdrawal syndrome (IWS) is common but underrecognized in critically ill children, and data from pediatric cardiac intensive care units (pCICUs) remain limited. This study determined the frequency of IWS after cardiac surgery and the factors associated with it. Methods: Retrospective, single-center cohort study of all pediatric patients admitted to a pCICU after cardiac surgery over 15 months. IWS screening was performed using the Withdrawal Assessment Tool-1 (WAT-1) at least three times daily post-extubation. IWS was defined as at least one WAT-1 score of 3 or higher. A prespecified multivariable logistic regression model with ten perioperative variables was fitted in the complete-case population. A subgroup analysis in ventilated children examined sedative and analgesic exposure, including the grouped duration of remifentanil infusion, in an adjusted model. Results: Of 311 patients, 294 (94.5%) were screened, and IWS occurred in 136 patients (46.3%, 95% CI 40.6-52.0). In the complete-case population (n = 286), univentricular physiology (OR 2.51, p = 0.044), suspected postoperative infection (OR 5.28, p = 0.023), and invasive ventilation for 10-100 h (OR 2.75, p = 0.021) or beyond 100 h (OR 5.29, p = 0.003) were independently associated with IWS, whereas postoperative lactatemia (>2 mmol/L for >6 h) was associated with lower odds (OR 0.39, p = 0.039). In mechanically ventilated children (n = 162), after adjustment, no sedative or analgesic exposure was significantly associated with IWS, while odds were substantially higher in patients receiving remifentanil beyond 48 h (OR 2.64, p = 0.114) and midazolam (OR 3.95, p = 0.057). Conclusions: In our institution, IWS was highly frequent after pediatric cardiac surgery, in particular in patients with univentricular physiology. In sedated patients, midazolam and prolonged remifentanil showed substantially higher, though not statistically significant, odds of developing IWS. These hypothesis-generating associations require prospective confirmation.

title: Novel Homozygous Consensus Splice Site Variant in the BORCS8 Gene Associated With Fetal Semi-lobar Holoprosencephaly.
authorString: Tamhankar PM, Tamhankar V, Shah D, Kachhadiya T, Mithbawkar S, Vaniawala S, Suvarna JC, Vaniawala S, Menon P, Mane S, Kumar D.
abstractText: Holoprosencephaly (HPE) is a structural malformation of the brain resulting from incomplete cleavage of the forebrain (prosencephalon) into right and left hemispheres, deep brain structures, olfactory bulbs, optic bulbs, and tracts. Mutations in any of the following genes, C2CD3, CDON, CNOT1, CENPF, DHCR7, DISP1, DLL1, EMX2, FGF8, FGFR1, GLI2, GLI3, ICK, IFT80, KMT2D, PPP1R12A, PRRX1, PTCH1, RAD21, SHH, SIX3, SMC1A, STAG2, STIL, TGIF1, WDR81, and ZIC2, can lead to HPE. Herein, we report for the first time, to the best of our knowledge, recurrent fetal semi-lobar HPE in association with a homozygous pathogenic consensus splice site variant in the BLOC-1-related complex subunit 8 (BORCS8) gene (c.150+1G>T, NM_001145784.2) or (chr19-19186892 C>A, GRCh38 format), identified on exome sequencing. Chromosomal microarray results were normal. However, the gene BORCS8 (MEF2B) was found in a region of loss of heterozygosity arr[hg19] 19p13.2p12(13,017,875-20,684,670) hmz (around 7667 kilobases), which suggested identity of this region by descent (result of consanguinity). Parental Sanger sequencing confirmed them as asymptomatic carriers (heterozygous) for the same variant (autosomal recessive inheritance). The BORCS8 gene encodes a protein subunit of the BLOC-one-related complex (BORC) in lysosomes that helps them to be transported to the peripheral cytoplasm in non-neuronal cells and the distal axon in neurons. Homozygous loss-of-function variants in the BORCS8 gene have been recently shown to lead to severe early childhood-onset neurodegenerative disorder. Clinical features described in these cases were cerebral and cerebellar atrophy, hypomyelination, and a thin corpus callosum. However, fetal presentation of HPE has not been described in the literature to date. We postulate that this could be due to a homozygous amorphic (complete loss-of-function) variant in our case, compared to the homozygous hypomorphs (partial loss-of-function) or compound heterozygous amorphic-hypomorphic variants described in the previously published childhood-onset cases. This case report expands the phenotypic spectrum of the BORCS8 gene-related disease. The BORCS8 gene may thus represent a candidate gene for HPE and further studies or reports of similar cases are needed to confirm or refute a causative association. This is the third published paper related to the BORCS8 gene-related disease as per the PubMed database (MEDLINE).

title: Nirsevimab in the New Era of RSV Prevention: Current Evidence, Emerging Challenges, and Future Perspectives.
authorString: Vasou M, Sokou R, Kafalidis G, Tsantes AG, Moutsopoulou RA, Grigoropoulos F, Katsianou E, Xixi NA, Magklara EP, Leontari K, Iliodromiti Z, Boutsikou T, Iacovidou N.
abstractText: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is the leading cause of lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI) and hospitalization in infants and young children worldwide, with the highest disease burden occurring in otherwise healthy term infants during the first 6 months of life. The recent introduction of long-acting monoclonal antibodies and maternal RSV vaccination has fundamentally changed preventive strategies against severe RSV disease. Evidence from randomized clinical trials and large real-world studies consistently demonstrates that a single dose of Nirsevimab provides season-long protection against RSV-associated LRTI and reduces hospitalization rate across diverse infant populations, while maintaining an excellent safety profile. Emerging data also support its effectiveness in routine clinical practice, although important uncertainties remain regarding long-term epidemiological effects, viral evolution, resistance, comparative effectiveness with maternal immunization, and optimal implementation across different healthcare settings. Current evidence supports Nirsevimab as a major advance in infant RSV prevention. However, continued surveillance, comparative effectiveness studies, and equitable global implementation will be essential to maximize its long-term public health impact. This narrative review summarizes current evidence on Nirsevimab, with emphasis on its clinical efficacy, safety, real-world effectiveness, resistance, implementation challenges, cost-effectiveness, and its role alongside maternal RSV vaccination.

title: Evaluation of Diastolic Dysfunction in Pituitary Adenomas: A Comparative Single-Center Study Among Acromegaly, Prolactinoma, and Nonfunctioning Pituitary Adenomas.
authorString: Eker Akıllı R, Altuntaş SÇ, Tepe O, Akray A, Zubaroglu ÜPA, İltaş A, Erdem T, Akbal E, Çağlayan EÇ.
abstractText: Background and Objectives: Pituitary adenomas may be associated with metabolic and cardiovascular abnormalities, but comparative evidence across subtypes is limited. We compared cardiometabolic and echocardiographic profiles, left ventricular diastolic dysfunction (LVDD), and carotid intima-media thickness (CIMT) among patients with prolactinoma, acromegaly, or nonfunctioning pituitary adenoma (NFPA) and healthy controls and investigated factors associated with LVDD. Materials and Methods: This cross-sectional comparative study included 214 participants evaluated between 2016 and 2018: 91 with prolactinoma, 26 with acromegaly, 45 with NFPA, and 52 healthy controls. Participants underwent clinical, biochemical, echocardiographic, and CIMT assessment. LVDD was diagnosed and graded according to the 2016 American Society of Echocardiography (ASE) and European Association of Cardiovascular Imaging (EACVI) recommendations. Factors associated with LVDD were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression. Results: The mean age was 41.3 ± 12.4 years, and 64.5% of participants were women. Acromegaly was associated with the highest fasting glucose, HbA1c, insulin, and homeostasis model assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR) values (all p < 0.001) and, compared with controls, a higher left atrial volume index (LAVI) and average E/e' ratio and lower left ventricular ejection fraction (despite preserved ejection fraction), E/A ratio, and lateral e' velocity. CIMT was higher in NFPA than in prolactinoma. LVDD was present in 21.5% of the cohort and in 5.8%, 19.8%, 46.2%, and 28.9% of the control, prolactinoma, acromegaly, and NFPA groups, respectively (p < 0.001); 84.8% of cases were grade I. Increasing age was independently associated with LVDD (OR 1.265 per year, 95% CI 1.155-1.385; p < 0.001), and diagnostic group was independently associated with LVDD overall (p = 0.004). Compared with controls, adjusted LVDD odds were higher in prolactinoma (OR 10.9, 95% CI 1.34-89.68), acromegaly (OR 167.5, 95% CI 10.3-2721.4), and NFPA (OR 12.0, 95% CI 1.4-104.8). Conclusions: Pituitary adenoma subtypes were associated with distinct cardiometabolic and echocardiographic profiles and a higher prevalence of LVDD than in healthy controls, particularly in acromegaly. Most LVDD cases were grade I, indicating predominantly impaired relaxation. Although age and diagnostic group were associated with LVDD in the adjusted analysis, the wide confidence intervals warrant cautious interpretation and validation in larger cohorts.

title: Molecular Signaling in Pulmonary Vein Stenosis: Toward Lesion-Specific Phenotyping and Individualized Therapy.
authorString: Moss ME, Klouda T.
abstractText: Pulmonary vein stenosis (PVS) is a rare but life-threatening disease affecting young children, characterized by progressive narrowing of the pulmonary veins. Multimodal treatment, including surgical and catheter-based interventions combined with medical therapy, can improve survival; however, disease recurrence and progression are common. Currently, there is no therapy able to reverse existing disease, leaving lung transplantation the only option for patients with advanced, treatment-resistant disease. Studies using animal models and human tissue have identified several mechanisms that contribute to PVS, including mechanosensitive signaling and endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition. In parallel, advances in cardiac imaging and hemodynamic profiling of individual pulmonary veins have improved risk stratification and provided opportunities to modify treatment strategies. Despite these advances, the development of disease-modifying therapies able to improve patient outcomes will require a more thorough understanding of the underlying pathophysiology. In this review, we examine the histological features of PVS and summarize the cellular contributions and signaling pathways implicated in disease development. We will also explore the potential of integrating patient- and lesion-specific phenotypes and molecular signatures to guide individual treatment strategies, as well as the current limitations and future directions of PVS research.

title: In Memoriam: David S. Cannom, MD, FHRS, 1940-2026.
authorString: Singh JP, Prystowsky EN, Youngblood JH, Lampert R, Ruskin JN.

title: Prospective Associations of Diet Quality During Pregnancy With Cardiovascular Health (Life's Essential 8) Among Women in Midlife.
authorString: Rifas-Shiman SL, Aris IM, Hivert MF, Zhang M, Chavarro JE, Oken E.

journal.title: Journal of human nutrition and dietetics : the official journal of the British Dietetic Association

abstractText:
Introduction

Cardiovascular health (CVH) often declines in midlife. Diet during pregnancy, a similarly sensitive period involving physiological changes, may influence long-term CVH, but few studies have examined this relationship. We examined the associations between diet during pregnancy and CVH in midlife.

Methods

Participants are 776 women enroled in Project Viva during early pregnancy (1999-2002, mean 32.7 years). Participants completed food frequency questionnaires during the first and second trimesters, from which we calculated three diet scores (higher scores = better diet): Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH), Mediterranean Diet (MD) and Dietary Inflammatory Index (DII × -1). We averaged scores across trimesters and generated internal z-scores. At the midlife visit (2017-2021, mean 51.1 y), we assessed CVH using the American Heart Association's Life's Essential 8 (range 0-100; higher scores = better CVH), including behavioural (diet, physical activity, sleep, smoking) and biomedical (BMI, blood pressure, lipids, glucose) subscores. We assessed associations using linear regression adjusted for age, race and ethnicity, nativity, education, parity, marital status and income at enrolment.

Results

Most participants were non-Hispanic White (70%) and college graduates (76%). Mean midlife CVH score was 76.3 points. Higher (per 1-SD) DASH z-scores were associated with better overall (β 3.3; 95% CI 2.2-4.3), behavioural (3.5; 2.5-4.4) and biomedical (3.1; 1.5-4.7) CVH scores. Higher MD z-scores were associated with better overall CVH (2.4; 1.4-3.4), behavioural (2.6; 1.6-3.5) and biomedical (2.6; 1.0-4.2) scores. Higher DII (× -1) z-scores were associated with better overall CVH (2.6; 1.6-3.7), behavioural (2.7; 1.7-3.7) and biomedical (2.5; 0.9-4.1) scores. A better pregnancy diet was associated with higher CVH scores for diet, physical activity and BMI, and both DASH and DII with blood pressure.

Conclusions

Women who consumed healthier diets during pregnancy had better CVH two decades later. Dietary assessment in pregnancy may identify women at risk for both short-term and long-term health problems.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Electrocardiogram Screening for Detection of Low Ejection Fraction in Routine Care: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
authorString: Ahmed AAO, Ahmed OAO, Ahmed RAO, Dishean AS, Gilbert C, Mohamed MMA, Ahmed Y, Abdelmageed MH, Eissa AA.

journal.title: Annals of noninvasive electrocardiology : the official journal of the International Society for Holter and Noninvasive Electrocardiology, Inc

abstractText:
Background

Left ventricular systolic dysfunction (LVSD) is common and treatable but often undiagnosed, especially in early stages with non-specific symptoms. AI applied to standard ECGs offers low-cost screening for low ejection fraction (EF), yet its real-world impact on diagnosis remains unclear.

Methods

A systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs assessed AI-ECG screening for low EF in clinical practice. The protocol was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261287652). Databases (PubMed, Scopus, Cochrane Central, Google Scholar) were searched from inception to January 18, 2026, for RCTs comparing AI-ECG screening to usual care in adults without known heart failure undergoing routine ECGs. The primary outcome was new low EF (≤ 50%) confirmed by echocardiography. Secondary outcomes included echocardiography referral rates, positive predictive value, and cardiology referral rates. Pooled risk ratios (RR) with 95% CIs were calculated using a random-effects model.

Results

Three RCTs were included (two individual and one cluster) with 37,467 participants. After adjusting for clustering, AI-ECG screening significantly improved detection of new low EF diagnoses compared to usual care (RR 1.36, 95% CI 1.12 to 1.64; p = 0.002; I2 = 0%), with a number needed to screen of 204. No significant difference was found in echocardiography referral rates (RR 1.02, 95% CI 0.96 to 1.09; p = 0.55; I2 = 36%). The PPV of the AI tool ranged from approximately 20% to 34% across studies.

Conclusion

AI-ECG screening added to routine care improves low EF detection without substantially increasing echocardiography referrals. These findings support AI-ECG for earlier LVSD detection in at-risk populations, though further validation across diverse AI platforms is warranted.

title: Incidence of Intensive Care Unit Delirium After Heart Surgery: A Feasibility Study of a Forest Environment Intervention.
authorString: Wagner-Skacel J, Schörghuber M, Kumpitsch C, Skacel P, Stross T, Miksch E, Pilz R, D'Avia C, Wilding M, Jauk E, Lamprecht D, Brandstätter A, Stanschus L, Reininghaus K, Dalkner N, Mörkl S, Reininghaus EZ, Horvath A, Bengesser S.
abstractText:
Background

Postoperative delirium is a serious complication in intensive care units (ICUs), particularly following cardiac surgery. It is associated with circadian rhythm disruption, sleep disturbances and adverse outcomes. ICU environments often lack natural time cues, which may exacerbate circadian misalignment and increase delirium risk.

Aim

The primary aim of the study was the evaluation of the implementation of two chronotherapeutic ICU interventions regarding recruitment, implementability and safety. Its secondary aim was to descriptively assess postoperative delirium across intervention groups.

Study design

This randomized feasibility study was conducted in a tertiary cardiac surgery ICU in Austria. Adult patients undergoing elective cardiac surgery were allocated to one of three groups: (1) forest environment, (2) light exposure or (3) standard ICU care. Interventions were applied for 12 h daily. Delirium was assessed at three postoperative time points using the confusion assessment method for the ICU (CAM-ICU) and intensive care delirium screening checklist (ICDSC).

Results

This study was conducted between March 2020 and 2025. Seventy-seven patients were enrolled, and 64 remained in the final analytical cohort. Interventions were delivered within routine care. Patients and ICU staff did not report intervention-related concerns. Implementation challenges included ICU restructuring, patient transfers due to COVID-19 and deviations from randomized allocation because of operational constraints. No intervention-related adverse events occurred. Delirium assessments were limited at several time points because of sedation, early ICU discharge or transfer. Across all groups, postoperative delirium was detected in 5 of 130 CAM-ICU completed assessments (3.8%) and 8 of 115 ICDSC completed assessments (6.9%), precluding inferential group comparisons.

Conclusions

Chronotherapeutic environmental interventions were feasible and safe in ICU care. Feasibility results highlighted challenges related to ICU logistics, sedation-related assessment limitations and pandemic-related disruptions. The unexpectedly low delirium incidence limited conclusions regarding intervention efficacy. Future trials should include larger high-risk populations and prospectively defined feasibility outcomes.

Relevance to clinical practice

Optimized ICU environments, including noise reduction and light management, may support delirium prevention. Chronotherapeutic environmental interventions are feasible additions to routine ICU care.

title: Synergistic Promotion of Ferroptosis in Cardiomyocytes by Tumor Cell Secretory Factors and PD-1 Blockade.
authorString: Ma X, Li X, Qu F, Cheng H, Liu Y, Liu C.

journal.title: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology

abstractText: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) targeting PD-1 frequently cause severe cardiotoxicity, yet the mechanisms involving tumor-host crosstalk remain poorly defined. Emerging evidence implicates ferroptosis, an iron-dependent regulated cell death, in cardiac injury during cancer immunotherapy. Primary neonatal murine ventricular cardiomyocytes (NMVCs) were exposed to lung cancer-derived tumor-conditioned media (TCM; tumor-conditioned media) enriched with exosomes, anti-PD-1 antibody, or both. Ferroptotic markers, mitochondrial bioenergetics, inflammatory signaling, and exosomal microRNA cargo were systematically evaluated using standardized biochemical assays, quantitative PCR, and targeted pharmacological rescue experiments. TCM primed cardiomyocytes for ferroptosis by downregulating the GPX4/SLC7A11/Nrf2 antioxidant axis, depleting glutathione, and elevating labile iron and lipid peroxidation. Anti-PD-1 treatment alone induced minimal oxidative stress but synergized with TCM to amplify ferroptosis > 4.7-fold, triggering profound mitochondrial depolarization and upregulating pro-ferroptotic enzymes ACSL4/LPCAT3. Tumor-derived exosomal miR-214-3p and miR-23a-3p directly suppressed GPX4 and Nrf2, mediating cellular vulnerability. The combined insult hyperactivated NF-κB and STING pathways in a mitochondria-dependent manner, markedly increasing pro-inflammatory cytokine secretion. Co-treatment with ferrostatin-1, deferoxamine, or Nrf2 activators effectively reversed ferroptotic markers and restored mitochondrial function. Tumor-derived exosomal factors and PD-1 blockade synergistically drive ferroptotic cardiomyocyte death by crippling antioxidant defenses and amplifying inflammatory signaling. Targeting ferroptosis or its upstream regulators presents a promising cardioprotective strategy for patients receiving cancer immunotherapy.

title: Renal Function and 4-Year Outcomes in Edoxaban-Treated Patients: A Sub-Analysis From the ETNA-AF Europe Study.
authorString: De Caterina R, Fronk EM, Nunes J, Lamparter M, Kirchhof P, Zoccali C, ETNA‐AF Europe Investigators.
abstractText:
Background

Non-vitamin K oral anticoagulants, like edoxaban, are essential in managing atrial fibrillation (AF). The impact of renal function on edoxaban dosages in real-world settings remains unclear. This 4-year ETNA-AF-Europe study follow-up analysis investigated how chronic kidney disease (CKD) stages affect the safety and effectiveness of usual edoxaban doses.

Methods

ETNA-AF-Europe (NCT02944019) was an observational study conducted from 2016 to 2022 across 776 centres in 10 European countries. Hazard ratios (HR) and annualized event rates were calculated for all-cause death, cardiovascular (CV) death, stroke and bleeding events for the overall population and participants stratified by dose (30/60 mg) and CKD stages at baseline.

Results

Of the 13,164 participants in the full analysis set, 9114 participants with CKD (Stage 1, n = 2064; Stage 2, n = 4855; Stage 3, n = 1985; Stage 4, n = 135; missing, n = 75) received label-recommended edoxaban doses. Compared with CKD Stage 1, higher CKD stages were associated with increased risks for stroke (Stage 3: HR [95% CI]: 1.889 [1.240-2.878], p = 0.003) and CV death (HR [95% CI]; Stage 4: 14.450 [8.270-25.247], Stage 3: 4.672 [3.312-6.969], Stage 2: 2.066 [1.394-3.062], all p < 0.001). All-cause death followed a similar trend. After adjusting for age, sex, body weight, CHA2DS2-VASc and modified HAS-BLED scores, most bleeding and effectiveness outcomes showed no nominally significant differences across CKD stages.

Conclusions

Edoxaban in patients with AF is effective and well tolerated across CKD stages and appropriate label dosing can offset the risk from renal impairment.

title: Evidence for the Existence of Neural Stem-Like Cells in Adult Rodent Intrinsic Cardiac Nervous Ganglia.
authorString: Jean A, Lizot G, Gourmelon M, Antigny F, Cousin L, Crotti M, Arnault P, Bescond J, Bois P, Constantin B, Coronas V, Chatelier A.

journal.title: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology

abstractText: Cardiac function is modulated by the intrinsic cardiac nervous system (ICNS), which integrates autonomic signals and undergoes remodeling in pathological conditions. Here, we demonstrate that adult rodent ICNS ganglia harbor neural stem-like cells that proliferate in vitro, form neurospheres, self-renew, and generate neurons expressing βIII-tubulin and PGP 9.5. In vivo, cells expressing the stem cell marker SOX2 are detected within ICNS ganglia. Moreover, cardiac injury induced by monocrotaline increases the number of SOX2-positive cells expressing the cell cycle marker Ki67 and the number of EdU-incorporating, nestin-expressing cells within the ICNS. Together, our data provide the first evidence of neural stem-like cells in adult ICNS ganglia and suggest their potential role in cardiac neuroplasticity.

title: Rapid Response System Escalation During Recovery of Hospital Bed Occupancy: An Observational Longitudinal Study.
authorString: Noguchi A, Yamada T, Anzai T, Oka K, Ai M, Uchimura Y, Toba M, Takahashi K, Moriwaki M, Wakabayashi K.
abstractText:
Background

Early warning scores (EWS) identify patient deterioration, but their impact depends on how they are integrated into workflows and escalation culture, particularly as hospitals recover from pandemic-related bed pressures.

Aims

To evaluate changes in rapid response system (RRS) escalation processes and rare safety outcomes after embedding an EWS within proactive Critical Care Outreach Team (CCOT) rounds as hospital bed occupancy recovered.

Study design

Observational longitudinal study at a single tertiary hospital in Japan comparing one pre-intervention year (2021) with three post-intervention years (2022-2024). In January 2022, a standardised EWS was embedded into proactive CCOT rounds and used as a prompt for shared clinical reasoning rather than a strict numeric trigger. Monthly aggregated ward-level data were analysed using Poisson regression, adjusting for seasonality, patient characteristics and bed occupancy.

Results

Across 71 985 admissions and 692 942 general-ward patient-days, rates of nurse-initiated escalations, RRS activations and resuscitation-status updates per 1000 patient-days increased in post-intervention analyses, but these differences were attenuated after full adjustment. In fully adjusted models, post-intervention incidence rate ratios (IRRs) were close to 1.0 for all process outcomes. For nurse-initiated escalations, IRRs ranged from 0.94 to 1.14, and all 95% confidence intervals included 1.0. Rates of unexpected in-hospital cardiac arrest and unplanned ICU admission remained low and stable. Bed occupancy increased over the study period, but within-year associations with outcomes were weak.

Conclusions

After adjustment for patient characteristics and hospital bed occupancy, embedding an EWS within proactive CCOT rounds was associated with broadly stable escalation process indicators and no clear evidence of deterioration in rare safety outcomes.

Relevance to clinical practice

These findings suggest that approaches to the RRS afferent limb that embed EWS use within structured dialogue between ward nurses and outreach teams may provide one plausible mechanism for sustaining escalation behaviours under operational pressure.

title: Sequential Associations of Sleep Architecture, Nocturnal Oxygenation, and Respiratory Disturbance With a Composite PSG-Derived Rhythm-Event Index.
authorString: Nikoubakht N, Kashaninasab F, Ghalehbandi MF, Khoozan M, Nazari MA.
abstractText:
Background

Sleep-disordered breathing (SDB), particularly obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), has been associated with cardiovascular complications including cardiac arrhythmias. However, the relative contributions of respiratory, oxygenation, and sleep architecture indices to composite PSG-derived rhythm-event index remain incompletely understood.

Objective

To investigate the sequential associations of sleep architecture, nocturnal oxygenation, and respiratory disturbance indices with the composite PSG-derived rhythm-event index in patients undergoing polysomnography (PSG).

Methods

Demographic, respiratory, oxygenation and sleep-architecture variables were extracted from PSG records. The primary outcome was a composite PSG-derived rhythm-event count, estimated as round(arrhythmia index × TST_hours) from the PSG-exported arrhythmia index, which was calculated during total sleep time only. Negative binomial regression used an offset of log(TST_hours). Because the outcome demonstrated overdispersion, negative binomial regression with an offset of log(TST hours) was used. Because the original 14-predictor model was over-parameterized for the sample size, a six-predictor model (age, sex, BMI, AHI, T90, and sleep efficiency) was chosen post hoc. This reduced model was not prespecified before the original analysis. Sleep efficiency was retained because it showed a strong signal in the exploratory 14-predictor model. The resulting p-values should therefore be interpreted as optimistic and exploratory. A sequential model-building approach (Model 1: age, sex, BMI, AHI; Model 2: plus T90; Model 3: plus sleep efficiency) was used to document the incremental contribution of each domain. A fully adjusted 14-predictor model was fitted only as a supplementary analysis. Wald 95% CIs and bootstrap percentile 95% CIs (2000 resamples) are reported.

Results

Forty-one participants were included (mean age 47.8 ± 13.5 years; median BMI 29.4 kg/m2). Severe OSA (AHI ≥ 30 events/hour) was present in 56.1%. Median arrhythmia index was 3.2 events/hour, with marked overdispersion. In the six-predictor model, only higher sleep efficiency was associated with lower arrhythmia rate (IRR = 0.946 per 1 percentage-point increase, 95% CI 0.921-0.972, p < 0.001; bootstrap 95% CI 0.888-0.984). T90 was associated in the Wald inference (IRR = 1.034, 95% CI 1.006-1.063, p = 0.016) but this association was not robust under bootstrap resampling (95% CI 0.979-1.067). AHI was not associated with arrhythmia rate (IRR = 1.000, 95% CI 0.987-1.014, p = 0.954). Age, sex and BMI were also not significant. A 14-predictor exploratory model had a marginally lower AIC (411.4) but a substantially higher BIC (438.8), consistent with overfitting.

Conclusion

In this exploratory selected sleep-center cohort, AHI and other respiratory-event indices were not independently associated with the composite PSG-derived rhythm-event index. Only higher sleep efficiency showed a robust association with lower arrhythmia rate, but this finding is hypothesis-generating and may reflect unmeasured confounding. These results require confirmation in larger prospective studies and should not guide clinical risk stratification.

title: Immediate drug hypersensitivity severity is associated with cardiovascular risk.
authorString: Okumus Guclu A, Seren OT, Ozaydin Unal SE, Kocabas ME, Aksu B, Ozmen U, Hafizoglu M, Bayrak Degirmenci P.
abstractText: Background: Drug hypersensitivity reactions (DHR) exhibit substantial clinical heterogeneity. Although established cardiovascular disease is a known risk factor for severe anaphylaxis, the impact of subclinical cardiovascular risk on DHR severity remains poorly understood. Objective: This study investigated the association between Systematic Coronary Risk Evaluation 2 (SCORE2) estimated cardiovascular risk and the severity of immediate-type DHRs. Methods: This retrospective study included 161 patients ages 40-69 years (median age, 49 years; 79.5% women) with immediate-type DHRs. To assess the subclinical risk, those with known cardiovascular disease, diabetes, or chronic kidney disease were excluded. Reaction severity was graded by using the Brown system, and SCORE2 was calculated by using clinical data from the 12 months preceding the reaction. Results: Reaction severity was graded as mild (35.4%), moderate (34.8%), or severe (29.8%). The median SCORE2 values were significantly higher in the severe group versus the mild group (4.10% versus 2.50%; p = 0.022). The proportion of patients in high or very high SCORE2 risk categories increased stepwise with reaction severity (35.1% in the mild group versus 64.6% in the severe group; p = 0.011). In an univariable ordinal logistic regression, each 1-point increase in SCORE2 percentage was associated with higher odds of greater reaction severity (odds ratio 1.144 [95% confidence interval, 1.041-1.257]; p = 0.005). This association remained significant after adjusting for the culprit drug class (p = 0.008).
