title: Fetal arrhythmia and heart disease during COVID-19 pandemic in patients who underwent echocardiography.
authorString: Mattos FA, Tavares GMP, Callado GY, Marra AR, Simioni C, Castello RG, Sanchez RC, Santana EFM.

journal.title: Revista brasileira de ginecologia e obstetricia : revista da Federacao Brasileira das Sociedades de Ginecologia e Obstetricia

abstractText:
Objective

To evaluate the characteristics and the occurrence of fetal heart diseases and arrhythmias in pregnancies that underwent fetal echocardiography examination during COVID-19 pandemic.

Methods

A retrospective cohort study was conducted using data extracted from the Fetal Ultrasound and Fetal Medicine Departments of Hospital Israelita Albert Einstein, a tertiary hospital in São Paulo, Brazil, from January to December 2021. The sample was analyzed using chi-square or Fisher's exact tests, and Student's t-test or the Mann-Whitney test. Logistic regression was performed to assess the risk of fetal arrhythmia and/or heart disease.

Results

A total of 148 fetuses were included in the analysis. The prevalence of fetal heart disease/arrhythmia was higher among patients with maternal comorbidities (73.3% vs. 39.1%), fetal defects (14.3% vs. 0.8%), and functional abnormalities (26.7% vs. 4.5%). Maternal COVID-19 showed no significant association with fetal cardiac outcomes. Maternal comorbidity, fetal malformation, and the presence of functional abnormalities were identified as independent risk factors.

Conclusion

Maternal comorbidities were associated with fetal arrhythmia and/or heart disease, but no causal relationship was found between COVID-19 and adverse fetal cardiac outcome.

title: Clinical and Echocardiographic Characterization of Stage B Heart Failure in Asymptomatic Adults With Cardiovascular Risk Factors.
authorString: Amir MA, Hannan A, Shabbir MF, Nathaniel E, Ilgizovich AI, Haleem F, Saeed S, Arshad MU, Idris Abubakr IM, BaniKhalaf S.
abstractText:
Background

Stage B heart failure (pre-HF) is characterized by objective cardiac abnormalities without HF symptoms. This study assessed the prevalence and clinical and echocardiographic characteristics of those who were asymptomatic yet had cardiovascular risk factors and Stage B HF.

Methods

This cross-sectional study included 900 asymptomatic adults with cardiovascular risk factors, consecutively recruited from participating hospitals from October 2025 to July 2026. We performed clinical evaluation and a standardized transthoracic echocardiogram. Stage B/pre-HF was defined as the presence of objective cardiac structural or functional abnormalities in the absence of heart failure symptoms or signs. We evaluated independent factors associated with Stage B/pre-HF using multivariable logistic regression.

Results

In this hospital-based cohort, Stage B/pre-HF was determined in 261 (29.0%) participants. Hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and obesity were more prevalent in the Stage B group, occurring in 154 (59.0%), 118 (45.2%), and 109 (41.8%), respectively. Stage B/pre-HF was characterized descriptively by lower left ventricular ejection fraction and higher left ventricular mass index, left atrial volume index, E/e' ratio, and tricuspid regurgitation velocity, along with impaired diastolic function. Hypertension was the strongest independent association (OR = 5.930, 95% CI: 3.815-9.217), followed by diabetes (OR = 2.945, 95% CI: 1.913-4.532), age, sex, and BMI. The model showed good fit (Nagelkerke R² = 0.565; Hosmer-Lemeshow p = 0.449).

Conclusion

Stage B/pre-HF was common among asymptomatic adults with cardiovascular risk factors and was characterized by structural and functional cardiac abnormalities. These findings support the potential value of early identification and management of modifiable cardiovascular risk factors in asymptomatic adults at risk for HF.

title: Anomalous Left Brachiocephalic Vein Draining into the Right Internal Thoracic Vein: A Case Report.
authorString: Kang DW, Seo JW, Lee BY.

journal.title: Journal of the Korean Society of Radiology

abstractText: The left brachiocephalic vein (LBCV) rarely exhibits an anomalous course and its major patterns have been described in several studies. Although LBCV anomalies are mostly asymptomatic, their identification and recognition are important in clinical settings such as cardiovascular intervention or surgery. Herein, we report a rare anomalous LBCV that was incidentally detected on chest computed tomography in a 59-year-old female. Instead of directly draining into the superior vena cava (SVC), this anomalous LBCV travelled an extraordinarily long, downward trajectory to drain into the right internal thoracic vein and consequently into the SVC.

title: Severe Pulmonary Hypertension in Critically Ill Children: A 10-Year Single-Center Case Series and Practical Management Considerations.
authorString: Straka K, Polymerou I, Christakou E.
abstractText: Severe pulmonary hypertension (PH) in children may decompensate rapidly during intercurrent illness and is associated with substantial morbidity and mortality in the pediatric intensive care unit (PICU). We describe the clinical presentation, intensive care management, and outcomes of four children with severe PH admitted to a tertiary PICU between January 2014 and December 2024. Three patients were infants, and one was an 11-year-old girl with a history of extreme prematurity and bronchopulmonary dysplasia. All four presented with acute respiratory distress, hypoxemia, and cardiovascular compromise following a recent respiratory tract infection. PH was documented predominantly by echocardiography, with findings including elevated estimated pulmonary pressures, right ventricular (RV) pressure overload, interventricular septal flattening, and/or RV dysfunction. Right heart catheterization was performed in one patient. All patients received supplemental oxygen, diuretics, and sildenafil. Two required invasive mechanical ventilation and vasoactive support, while one patient received additional prostanoid and endothelin receptor antagonist therapy. The median PICU length of stay was 15 days (range: 10-24 days). Two patients survived to hospital discharge, whereas two died following refractory pulmonary hypertensive crises. These cases highlight respiratory infection as an important potential precipitant of acute decompensation in children with severe PH and illustrate the challenges of supporting the failing RV in the PICU. Although the small sample size and retrospective design preclude conclusions regarding treatment efficacy or prognostic factors, the cases emphasize several practical management priorities: early recognition of deterioration, prompt correction of factors that increase pulmonary vascular resistance, preservation of RV function and systemic perfusion, cautious escalation of respiratory support, and early multidisciplinary involvement. Based on these principles and the published pediatric PH literature, we propose a practical, physiology-based management algorithm for severe PH and pulmonary hypertensive crisis in the PICU.

title: <i>TRPM4</i>-related left bundle branch block-induced cardiomyopathy reversed by left bundle branch area pacing-based cardiac resynchronization therapy: a case report.
authorString: Wu S, Wang X, Zhou B, Zou T, Yu X.
abstractText:
Background

Progressive cardiac conduction disease (PCCD) is a rare inherited disorder characterized by degeneration of the His-Purkinje system. Although primarily considered an electrical disease, chronic left bundle branch block (LBBB) may result in mechanical dyssynchrony and reversible cardiomyopathy.

Case summary

A 59-year-old man presented with progressive left ventricular (LV) dilation and systolic dysfunction. Electrocardiography showed complete LBBB with a QRS duration of 165 ms. Ischaemic and infiltrative cardiomyopathies were ruled out. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging revealed LV enlargement without late gadolinium enhancement but with marked mechanical dyssynchrony. Genetic testing identified a likely pathogenic TRPM4 c.393G>C variant, considered contributory to the conduction phenotype. LBBB-induced cardiomyopathy and heart failure with reduced ejection fraction were diagnosed. The patient underwent left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP)-based cardiac resynchronization therapy. The QRS duration narrowed to 115 ms, and follow-up echocardiography demonstrated marked reverse remodelling with LV ejection fraction improving from 26% to 48%.

Discussion

This case suggests that TRPM4-related PCCD may present with isolated LBBB leading to dyssynchrony-mediated cardiomyopathy. LBBAP can effectively restore electrical synchrony and promote reverse LV remodelling. This favourable response highlights the importance of timely physiological resynchronization in potentially reversible LBBB-related cardiomyopathy.

title: Histopathology Versus Imaging: A Comparative Study of Liver Biopsy, Ultrasonography, and Triphasic Computed Tomography in Paediatric Patients With Chronic Liver Disease.
authorString: Karim F, Hussain F, Shabbir H, Naureen S, Seerat I.
abstractText:
Background

Assessment of liver fibrosis and cirrhotic changes in children with chronic liver disease (CLD) can be challenging, particularly when invasive assessment is limited by clinical factors. This study compared ultrasonography and triphasic computed tomography (CT) findings with histopathology in paediatric patients with CLD.

Aim

The aim of the study is to compare ultrasonography and triphasic CT findings with liver biopsy findings in paediatric patients with CLD and to assess their concordance with histopathology using predefined study-specific categories of good, partial, and poor agreement.

Materials and methods

A prospective analytical observational study was conducted at the Department of Paediatrics and Paediatric Gastroenterology, Pakistan Kidney and Liver Institute and Research Center, Lahore, from April 10, 2026 to July 10, 2026. A total of 100 children aged 0-15 years with CLD or decompensated CLD were included. Clinical, biochemical, ultrasonographic, triphasic CT, and liver biopsy findings were recorded. Histopathology was used as the reference standard. Agreement analysis was performed in patients with adequate biopsy samples using predefined study-specific criteria. Paired binary comparisons were assessed using the McNemar test, while the Bowker test was used for comparison across the three agreement categories. A p-value of less than 0.05 was considered statistically significant.

Results

Liver biopsy was performed in 93 patients, with adequate biopsy samples obtained in 90 patients. Among patients with adequate biopsy samples, 81/90 (90%) had F3 or F4 fibrosis. Good agreement with histopathology was observed more frequently with triphasic CT than with ultrasonography (59/90 versus 17/90, p < 0.001). Good or partial agreement was also higher with triphasic CT than with ultrasonography (83/90 versus 61/90, p < 0.001).

Conclusion

Triphasic CT demonstrated greater concordance with histopathology than ultrasonography in this predominantly advanced CLD cohort. These findings mainly reflect the assessment of advanced fibrosis and cirrhotic changes and should not be extrapolated to early-stage disease. Triphasic CT may provide complementary structural information, while liver biopsy remains necessary when definitive histological diagnosis or fibrosis staging is required.

title: She Never Had a Period: A Case of Mayer-Rokitansky-Küster-Hauser Syndrome.
authorString: Saber A, Rammah T.
abstractText: Primary amenorrhea is a common concern in adolescent females and can place significant emotional pressure on both the patient and her parents. Although often attributed to benign causes, it may reflect underlying congenital anomalies even in the presence of normal pubertal development. We report the case of a 15-year-old girl of Middle Eastern descent who presented with absence of menarche. She reported normal pubertal development and denied disordered eating or excessive exercise. Hormonal evaluation demonstrated follicle-stimulating hormone and estrogen levels within normal limits. Pelvic magnetic resonance imaging revealed non-visualization of the uterus with normal-appearing ovaries, findings later confirmed by pelvic ultrasonography. Brain magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated an unremarkable pituitary gland. These findings led to the diagnosis of Mayer-Rokitansky-Küster-Hauser syndrome. This case underscores the importance of structural imaging in the evaluation of primary amenorrhea, even when hormonal studies and pubertal development are normal.

title: Correlation Between Serum Ferritin and Electrocardiographic and Echocardiographic Markers of Cardiac Dysfunction in Children With Transfusion-Dependent β-Thalassemia Major.
authorString: Kasaudhan V, Singh VK, Sharma B, Singh P, Singh KK, Bhatnagar R.
abstractText:
Background

Cardiac complications resulting from iron overload remain the leading cause of morbidity and mortality in children with transfusion-dependent β-thalassemia major. Early identification of myocardial dysfunction using non-invasive markers is essential, particularly in resource-limited settings where cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) T2* is not readily available.

Objectives

To evaluate the correlation between serum ferritin levels and electrocardiographic and echocardiographic markers of cardiac dysfunction in children with β-thalassemia major.

Methods

This analytical cross-sectional study was conducted in the Department of Pediatrics, Baba Raghav Das Medical College, Gorakhpur, India, from January 2025 to December 2025. Eighty children aged two to 16 years with transfusion-dependent β-thalassemia major were enrolled and stratified into three groups according to serum ferritin levels: <2500 ng/mL, 2500-5000 ng/mL, and >5000 ng/mL. All participants underwent clinical evaluation, electrocardiography (ECG), conventional echocardiography, and tissue Doppler imaging. Pearson correlation and multivariate linear regression analyses were performed.

Results

Higher serum ferritin levels were associated with significant prolongation of the corrected QT (QTc) interval and QT dispersion and associated with impairment of left ventricular systolic and diastolic function. Serum ferritin showed significant negative correlations with left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) (r = -0.684), E/A ratio (r = -0.582), lateral early diastolic mitral annular velocity (r = -0.658), and tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (r = -0.512), and positive correlations with the ratio of early transmitral flow velocity to early diastolic mitral annular velocity (E/Ea ratio) (r = 0.726), QTc interval (r = 0.648), and myocardial performance index (r = 0.672) (all p < 0.001). Multivariate analysis identified serum ferritin as the strongest independent predictor of reduced LVEF (β = -0.562, p < 0.001).

Conclusions

Elevated serum ferritin levels are significantly associated with subclinical and overt cardiac dysfunction in children with β-thalassemia major. Combined assessment using serum ferritin, ECG, and echocardiography may facilitate early detection of iron overload cardiomyopathy and help optimize chelation therapy, particularly in settings where advanced cardiac imaging is unavailable.

title: Risk factor for impaired lung function in asthmatic children: predictive value of 25-OH-D, BMI and inflammatory markers.
authorString: Zhang Y, Liu X, Zhang W, Wang Y, Qi C, Zhang M, Lv M.
abstractText:
Objective

This cross-sectional study investigated the associations between modifiable metabolic risk factors (vitamin D status and obesity) and pulmonary function decline in children with asthma, independent of disease duration and airway inflammation.

Methods

Medical records of 430 asthmatic children (aged ≤14 years) were retrospectively analyzed. Using FEV1%pred <80% as the cutoff, 171 children with pulmonary function impairment were compared with 259 children with normal pulmonary function. Clinical characteristics, pulmonary function parameters, and laboratory indices (25-(OH)-D, BMI, CRP, IL-6, TNF-α) were collected. Multivariate logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses were performed.

Results

Among the 430 enrolled children, 171 (39.75%) presented with pulmonary function impairment, predominantly of mild-to-moderate severity. Compared with children with normal pulmonary function, those with impaired pulmonary function had longer disease duration, lower ACT scores, decreased 25-(OH)-D levels, and elevated BMI, CRP, IL-6, and TNF-α levels (all P<0.05). 25-(OH)-D levels were positively correlated with FEV1%pred and FEV1/FVC, and negatively correlated with BMI, CRP, IL-6, and TNF-α (all P<0.001). Multivariate logistic regression analysis identified prolonged disease duration (OR=1.789, 95% CI: 1.333-2.401), elevated BMI (OR=1.205, 95% CI: 1.035-1.403), increased IL-6 (OR=1.193, 95% CI: 1.086-1.312), elevated CRP (OR=1.362, 95% CI: 1.118-1.658), and secondhand smoke exposure (OR=3.336, 95% CI: 1.567-7.102) as independent risk factors for pulmonary function impairment (all P<0.05). Conversely, higher ACT scores (OR=0.763, 95% CI: 0.675-0.861) and 25-(OH)-D levels (OR=0.818, 95% CI: 0.730-0.916) were associated with a lower likelihood of pulmonary function impairment (all P<0.01). Ten-fold cross-validated ROC analysis demonstrated that the mean AUC values of 25-(OH)-D, BMI, IL-6, CRP, and TNF-α were 0.883, 0.806, 0.862, 0.845, and 0.827, respectively.

Conclusion

Vitamin D status and secondhand smoke exposure were significantly associated with pulmonary function impairment in children with asthma. Our findings suggest a metabolic component in childhood asthma, although causal inference is limited by the cross-sectional design. Prospective studies are warranted to validate these associations and further clarify underlying mechanisms.

title: Predictive value of soluble growth stimulated expression gene 2 (sST2) for recurrence after radiofrequency ablation in patients with atrial fibrillation.
authorString: Chen J, Liang L, Shen B, Qin X, Deng F, Tu C.
abstractText:
Objectives

To assess the prognostic utility of preoperative soluble growth stimulated expression gene 2 (sST2) for post-ablation Atrial fibrillation (AF) recurrence and develop a multi-marker nomogram to optimize preprocedural risk assessment.

Methods

This monocentric retrospective study enrolled 517 AF patients undergoing radiofrequency ablation (RFA) between January 2020 and December 2024, with a 12-month postprocedural follow-up. We collected baseline clinical characteristics, left atrial diameter (LAD), and serum biomarkers including high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP), N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), interleukin-6 (IL-6), and sST2. Multivariable logistic regression revealed the independent risk factors for recurrence after ablation; we then constructed a nomogram and performed internal validation.

Results

AF recurrence occurred in 172 patients (33.27%). LAD, hs-CRP, NT-proBNP, IL-6, and sST2 were confirmed as independent predictors of recurrence. sST2 demonstrated the strongest individual predictive performance, with an optimal cutoff value of 32.69 ng/mL and an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.825. The combined nomogram achieved AUCs of 0.950 in the training set and 0.935 in the validation set, which was significantly better than the traditional CHA2DS2-VASc and HATCH scores. Calibration curves and decision curve analysis confirmed excellent model fit and substantial clinical net benefit.

Conclusions

Preoperative sST2 is a robust independent predictor of AF recurrence after RFA. The novel nomogram integrating sST2 with LAD and inflammatory/neurohormonal biomarkers enables more accurate risk stratification and supports personalized perioperative management.

title: Uptake of Respiratory Syncytial Virus Prefusion F Protein Vaccination during Pregnancy and nirsevimab among Infants over Two Seasons in a Single Health System.
authorString: Kerr JE, Calzadilla AJ, Liu H, Rick AM.
abstractText:
Objective

To describe the uptake of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) prevention products during the first 2 seasons after availability in the US in a large health system.

Study design

Using multisource immunization data from a single health system, we identified a retrospective cohort of infants born from October 2023 to April 2024 (season 1) and from September 2024 to April 2025 (season 2) and their birth parents. We described the uptake of RSV prefusion F protein (RSVpreF) vaccination and nirsevimab and evaluated factors associated with receipt using multivariable logistic regression.

Results

Among 10 196 infants, 5868/10 196 (57.6%) were exposed to an RSV-preventive product. Overall, in our maternal-infant dyads, 3850/10 196 (37.8% of total) received RSVpreF, 1837/10 196 infants (18.0% of total) received nirsevimab, and in 181/10 196 (1.8%), both were received. Uptake increased from 2100/4555 (46.1%) in season 1 to 3768/5641 (66.8%) in season 2 (P < .001). Maternal RSVpreF vaccination increased from 1280/4555 (28.1%) to 2570/5641 (45.6%), and nirsevimab uptake increased from 749/4555 (16.4%) to 1088/5641 (19.3% both P < .001). Nirsevimab receipt at <6 days of life increased from 242/749 (32.2%) to 502/1088 (46.1%, P < .001). RSVpreF uptake was higher among older, privately insured pregnant individuals and those engaged in other preventative care and lower among those with higher area deprivation, more complex obstetric histories, or other children. Nirsevimab uptake was higher among infants with prematurity or from multifetal births and lower among those with siblings, later-season birth, or no early outpatient care. Social and structural disparities in nirsevimab uptake improved in the second season, whereas disparities in RSVpreF uptake persisted.

Conclusions

The uptake of RSV preventive strategies increased across 2 seasons, with a higher uptake of maternal RSVpreF vaccination than nirsevimab.

title: Nasal and Nasopharyngeal Airway Obstruction in Neonates: A Pictorial Essay.
authorString: Gala F, Jain N, Mahapatra S.

journal.title: Journal of the Korean Society of Radiology

abstractText: Neonates are obligate nasal breathers. Therefore, any obstruction of the nasal cavity or nasopharynx can result in severe respiratory distress, cyanosis, feeding difficulties, and failure to thrive. This condition can be life-threatening. Bilateral obstruction typically presents with severe symptoms that present in the neonatal period, whereas unilateral nasal obstruction presents later in life. In this pictorial essay, we illustrate the imaging features of various causes of neonatal nasal and nasopharyngeal airway obstruction and emphasize the role of cross-sectional imaging in prompt diagnosis.

title: Angiotensin receptor neprilysin inhibitor (ARNI) in right ventricular failure and preserved LV ejection fraction: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
authorString: Safari M, Safari Z.
abstractText:
Background

Right ventricular (RV) failure with preserved left ventricular (LV) ejection fraction (LVEF ≥50%) is a distinct clinical entity often associated with pulmonary hypertension (PH), chronic lung diseases, or congenital heart defects, leading to significant morbidity and mortality. Angiotensin receptor neprilysin inhibitors (ARNI), such as sacubitril/valsartan, have demonstrated efficacy in left-sided heart failure, but their role in isolated RV failure remains understudied.

Methods

A PRISMA-compliant search of PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and Google Scholar was conducted from 2010 to 2025 for RCTs and prospective cohorts assessing ARNI in patients with RV failure and preserved LVEF. Inclusion: Adults with RV dysfunction (e.g., TAPSE <17 mm or RV S' <9.5 cm/s) and LVEF ≥50%; ARNI vs. standard care or pre-treatment; reporting RV parameters, sPAP, NT-proBNP, 6MWD, or NYHA class.

Results

Three studies (1 RCT, 2 prospective cohorts; n=120 patients) were included. ARNI improved TAPSE (WMD 1.2 mm, 95% CI 0.7-1.7; p<0.001; I²=0%), RV S' (WMD 0.5 cm/s, 95% CI 0.2-0.8; P=0.002; I²=0%), and reduced sPAP (WMD -7.5 mmHg, 95% CI -10.2 to -4.8; p<0.001; I²=15%). NT-proBNP decreased (WMD -1200 pg/mL, 95% CI -1700 to -700; p<0.001; I²=0%). 6MWD increased (WMD 30 m, 95% CI 10-50; P=0.003; I²=0%). NYHA class improved (RR 1.65 for ≥1 class improvement, 95% CI 1.15-2.37; P=0.007; I²=0%).

Conclusion

ARNI enhances RV function, reduces pulmonary pressures, and improves functional status in RV failure with preserved LVEF.

title: Prevalence, risk factors, and outcomes of infective endocarditis in people living with HIV: A systematic review and meta-analysis of intravenous drug use and microbiological profiles.
authorString: Eini P, Eini P, Doosti-Irani A.
abstractText:
Background

Infective endocarditis (IE) poses a significant challenge in people living with human immunodeficiency virus (PLWH), with risk factors and outcomes potentially differing from HIV-negative counterparts. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to explore the prevalence, risk factors, mortality, and clinical characteristics of IE in PLWH versus HIV-negative patients.

Methods

Methods : Six databases (PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, ScienceDirect, Embase, and ProQuest) were searched up to January 2025 using terms including "Infective Endocarditis" and "Human Immunodeficiency Virus." Random-effects meta-analyses with Freeman-Tukey transformation were used to estimate pooled prevalence, mortality, and odds ratios (ORs) for IE by HIV status. Between-study heterogeneity (I²) and meta-regression were assessed to explore sources of variation.

Results

Results : Seventeen independent studies collectively reported 3,082 IE cases (2,095 among PLWH and 987 among HIV-negative individuals), analyzed as separate study-level data rather than a single combined cohort. The pooled prevalence of IE among PLWH was 33.2% (95% CI: 14.97-54.45%), with substantial heterogeneity (I² > 90%), highlighting the exploratory nature of these estimates. Among PLWH with IE, 85.5% (95% CI: 65.8-98.1%) reported intravenous drug use (IVDU), and 60-80% had right-sided IE (predominantly tricuspid valve), contrasting with left-sided predominance in HIV-negative patients. Mortality among PLWH with IE was 14.7%, compared with 22.3% in HIV-negative individuals. Staphylococcus aureus was the leading pathogen (24-73%).

Conclusions

Given the high and persistent heterogeneity, findings should be interpreted as exploratory. PLWH with IE frequently exhibit IVDU and right-sided involvement, while mortality appears comparable to HIV-negative patients after accounting for IVDU, emphasizing behavioral rather than virologic determinants of risk.

title: AHA/ACC/ESC/WHF Expert Consensus Document: Second Universal Definition of Heart Failure (2026) : AHA/ACC/ESC/WHF CONSENSUS DOCUMENT
authorString: Walsh M, Kober L, Sliwa K, Adamo M, Agarwal A, Banerjee A, Bozkurt B, Cikes M, Damasceno A, Desai A, Felker G, Hogan G, Kinugawa K, Kittleson M, Lam C, McDonagh T, Metra M, Mullens W, Ribeiro A, Vaughn Y, Vest A.

title: Assessment of Pulmonary Thromboembolism on Chest Radiographs Using Quantitative AI-Based Cardiovascular-Border Analysis.
authorString: Ok JY, Lee JE, Choo KS, Yang DH.

journal.title: Journal of the Korean Society of Radiology

abstractText:
Purpose

To address the utility of an AI-based cardiovascular border analysis of chest radiographs (CXRs) in patients with pulmonary thromboembolism (PTE).

Materials and methods

This retrospective single-center study included patients with PTE diagnosed using cardiothoracic ratio (CTR) pulmonary angiography between January 2023 and June 2024, along with age-matched and sex-matched controls. The AI model quantified distances from the midline to the cardiovascular borders, including the superior vena cava/ascending aorta (SVC/AO), right atrium (RA), aortic arch, pulmonary trunk (PT), left atrial appendage (LAA), and left ventricle (LV), as well as the CTR. Measurements were standardized as age-adjusted and sex-adjusted Z-scores. Diagnostic performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis.

Results

In total, 390 participants (195 with PTE and 195 controls; median age, 68 years) were included in the study. Patients with PTE showed greater values for the PT, SVC/AO, LAA, LV, and CTRs than the controls (p < 0.05). Among 165 patients with follow-up CXRs, post-treatment reductions in values for the PT, SVC/AO, RA, LAA, LV, and CTRs were observed (p < 0.05). ROC analysis showed modest discriminative performance, with the PT Z-score demonstrating the highest area under the curve (AUC, 0.658), improving further in the central PTE subgroup (AUC, 0.700).

Conclusion

AI-based cardiovascular-border analysis of CXRs demonstrated modest diagnostic performance but may support treatment monitoring in patient with PTE.

title: Deep Versus Moderate Hypothermia in Pediatric Cardiac Surgery: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Early Postoperative Outcomes
authorString: Zoupas I, Covell J, Naranjo J, Podgorsek B, Chen P, LaPar D, Greenleaf C.

title: Unique Opportunities and Challenges of Artificial Intelligence in Pediatric Imaging.
authorString: Gupta A, Agrawal A, Jana M.

journal.title: The Indian journal of radiology & imaging

abstractText: Artificial intelligence (AI) in pediatric imaging is evolving rapidly but lags behind and remains fundamentally distinct from adult radiology AI, due to various factors, such as developmental variability, differing disease epidemiology, unique imaging constraints, and limited data ecosystems. This narrative review examines the biological, technical, and structural factors that shape pediatric imaging AI, summarizes current and emerging applications, and highlights key barriers to safe clinical translation. Evidence indicates that the most immediate and impactful applications of pediatric AI lie in image acquisition, dose reduction, and workflow optimization, while interpretive and prognostic tools remain variably mature, with bone age assessment and chest radiograph interpretation representing the most established use cases. However, broader deployment is constrained by small, fragmented datasets, lack of standardized reference labels, limited generalizability, insufficient prospective validation, and gaps in regulatory and clinical integration frameworks. Furthermore, adult-trained models frequently underperform in children, reinforcing the need for pediatric-specific design and evaluation. The review emphasizes the importance of ethical governance, stakeholder trust, and multidisciplinary collaboration in guiding implementation. Future progress will depend on shared data infrastructures, federated learning approaches, rigorous age-stratified validation, and outcome-focused evaluation aligned with pediatric care priorities. Overall, pediatric imaging AI should be regarded as a distinct clinical, technical, and ethical domain requiring evidence-driven, child-centered development to ensure safe, effective, and equitable adoption in practice.

title: Prognostic value of Fibrosis-4 Index and preoperative dynamic changes in heart transplantation.
authorString: Lai J, Shan Y, Yim WY, Chen K, Li C, Hou J, Peng Y, Chen Y, Xia T, Zheng Y, Xiong T, Luo Y, Zhang J, Wang Y, Wang Y, Wang G.
abstractText:
Introduction

The Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) Index has shown prognostic value in cardiovascular diseases, but its role in heart transplantation (HTx) and the impact of dynamic preoperative changes remain unclear. This study evaluated the prognostic value of preoperative FIB-4 for mortality after HTx and investigated whether dynamic changes in FIB-4 before transplantation are associated with post-transplant survival.

Methods

This single-centre retrospective cohort study included 791 adult patients who underwent orthotopic HTx between January 2015 and December 2024, with follow-up through June 2025. Patients were stratified by preoperative FIB-4 into low (<1.30), intermediate (1.30-2.67), and high (>2.67) risk groups. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality. Analyses employed Cox models, restricted cubic splines, and five machine learning survival models, including Random Survival Forest (RSF).

Results

During a median follow-up of 28.8 months, 218 patients (27.6%) died. Preoperative FIB-4 showed a non-linear association with mortality (inflection point: 2.03) and was an independent predictor of death [hazard ratio (HR) per unit increase, 1.04; 95% CI, 1.02-1.07; P < .001]. In the RSF model, FIB-4 was the most important prognostic variable (Variable Importance = 0.068), outperforming traditional donor and surgical factors. Sensitivity analyses confirmed that FIB-4's prognostic value was independent of age (interaction P = .745) and superior to its individual components (aspartate aminotransferase, alanine aminotransferase, and platelet count). Correlation analyses showed no significant association between FIB-4 and invasive haemodynamic parameters, tricuspid regurgitation severity, or MELD/MELD-XI scores, supporting its distinction from haemodynamic congestion. Among high-risk patients (n = 153), preoperative improvement in FIB-4 category was associated with significantly lower mortality (adjusted HR, 0.49; 95% CI, 0.29-0.82; P = .007). Preoperative use of glutathione was independently associated with FIB-4 improvement [odds ratios (OR), 1.50; 95% CI, 1.01-2.22; P = .04].

Conclusion

Preoperative FIB-4 is a robust and independent predictor of post-transplant mortality, with greater predictive importance than traditional surgical risk factors. Dynamic improvement in FIB-4 before transplantation is associated with better survival. Integrating FIB-4 into routine preoperative assessment may refine risk stratification and guide pre-transplant management.

title: The association of anxiety, depression, developmental disabilities, and congenital heart disease in US children and adolescents.
authorString: Yu B, Li B, Deng X, Tang J, Chen R, Guo T.
abstractText:
Background

Congenital heart disease (CHD) has been linked to the risk of mental health or some developmental disabilities, but there is limited research on the effect of CHD on children and adolescents' mental health and developmental disabilities (varying severity) in the general children and adolescents' population.

Methods

This nationally representative study included 52,846 children and adolescents aged 6-17 years who participated in the 2022-2023 National Survey of Children's Health (NSCH) in the US from July 2022 to January 2024. Weighted adjusted odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated by multivariable logistic regression models to investigate the association of CHD with anxiety, depression, and multiple developmental disabilities.

Results

Finally, 52,846 children and adolescents representing 38 million US youth aged 6-17 years (mean age 11.47 years, 95% CI: 11.41-11.52) were included. Children and adolescents with CHD was associated with a higher presence of of anxiety (OR, 1.80 [95% CI, 1.37-2.37]), depression (OR, 1.52 [95% CI, 1.02-2.27]), Down syndrome (OR, 25.59 [95% CI, 14.27-61.36]), behavior problems (OR, 2.39 [95% CI, 1.77-3.24]), developmental delay (OR, 3.16 [95% CI, 2.39-4.18]), intellectual disability (OR, 3.81 [95% CI, 2.29-6.33]), speech disorder (OR, 2.61 [95% CI, 1.99-3.43]), learning disability (OR, 2.39 [95% CI, 1.80-3.17]), autism spectrum disorder (ASD) (OR, 2.11 [95% CI, 1.35-3.28]) and attention deficit disorder/attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADD/ADHD) (OR, 2.04 [95% CI, 1.52-2.72]), respectively. In stratified analyses, the ORs for depression, Tourette syndrome, behavior problems, developmental delay, speech disorder, learning disability, ASD, and ADD/ADHD were higher in moderate or severe status than in mild status. The results were similar in the sensitivity analyses.

Conclusion

In conclusion, this is the first nationally representative, population-based study to demonstrate that children and adolescents with CHD are associated with increased presence of anxiety, depression, and developmental disabilities in US children and adolescents. The presence of depression and developmental disabilities was higher in moderate or severe status than in mild status. Our findings suggested that early prevention, risk assessment, and support of mental health conditions and developmental disorders in high-risk children and adolescents, such as those with CHD.

Clinical trial number

Not applicable.

title: Maternal risk factors associated with neonatal necrotizing enterocolitis: a meta-analysis and systematic review.
authorString: Burnham L, Lichstein W, Lyford A.
abstractText:
Background

Neonatal Necrotizing Enterocolitis (NEC) is a multifactorial intestinal disorder that affects 2-5% of premature infants and has a mortality rate of 20-30%. Maternal factors such as breastmilk feeding and antenatal corticosteroid therapy have been found to influence NEC development in infants, yet other maternal and perinatal contributors have not been analyzed in detail. A better understanding of the role of specific maternal factors in NEC development can help identify infants at risk. This meta-analysis aims to investigate the pooled association between Cesarean section delivery, smoking, preeclampsia, chorioamnionitis, diabetes mellitus, and maternal education on the development of NEC.

Methods

We systematically searched for journal articles published before April 2025 in Springer Nature Link, Scopus, PubMed, and Google Scholar. Results were narrowed down using the Boolean search string ("necrotizing enterocolitis" OR "neonatal necrotizing enterocolitis") AND (("maternal risk" OR "maternal factors") OR ("smoking" OR "preeclampsia" OR "chorioamnionitis" OR "diabetes")). Studies were included if they reported NEC incidence rates for any of the examined factors. Two evaluators independently screened and extracted literature, and disagreements were resolved through discussion. Interrater reliability was assessed using Cohen's Kappa.

Results

We identified 74 manuscripts that met the inclusion criteria, of which 26 were suitable for our meta-analysis. We calculated unadjusted ORs from extracted 2 × 2 data, as adjusted estimates were infrequently reported and were not pooled. The unadjusted pooled risk calculation showed a higher odds of NEC for both preeclampsia (OR: 2.11, 95% CI: 1.15-3.06, n = 4) and smoking during pregnancy (OR: 1.97, 95% CI: 1.66-2.28, n = 6). Funnel plots and Egger's regression tests indicated no evidence of publication bias for maternal factors with more than 10 studies.

Conclusions

This study highlights a significant pooled unadjusted association between maternal smoking and preeclampsia during pregnancy and the development of NEC. Chorioamnionitis and Cesarean sections alone were not significantly associated with NEC in this pooled unadjusted analysis, despite conflicting claims from other studies. This meta-analysis underscores the need for more research to be conducted to analyze the association between maternal smoking, preeclampsia, Cesarean sections, chorioamnionitis, and maternal education on the development of NEC.

title: Association between coronary angiography-derived index of microcirculatory resistance and ischemic stroke in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction.
authorString: Cui C, Sun Z, Du M, Lu P, Lu Y, Zhang H, Xiao Q, Yang F.
abstractText:
Background

Stroke is a devastating complication following ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). Coronary microcirculatory dysfunction (CMD) is implicated in adverse post-STEMI outcomes, but its relationship with subsequent stroke is unknown. We aimed to investigate the association of the coronary angiography-derived index of microcirculatory resistance (caIMR), a novel non-invasive tool for assessing CMD, for new-onset ischemic stroke in STEMI patients undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (pPCI).

Methods

This single-center, retrospective cohort study enrolled 602 consecutive STEMI patients who underwent successful pPCI between July 2020 and February 2025. The caIMR was calculated post-procedure using specialized software. The primary endpoint was new-onset ischemic stroke. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression and restricted cubic spline analyses were used to assess the association between caIMR and stroke risk.

Results

Over a median follow-up of 29.3 months, 38 patients (6.3%) developed a new-onset ischemic stroke. In the multivariable Cox model, caIMR was independently associated with the risk of ischemic stroke (HR: 1.044, 95% CI: 1.022-1.065, P < 0.001), along with new-onset atrial fibrillation (HR: 9.113, 95% CI: 4.587-18.107, P < 0.001). A linear dose-response relationship was observed between caIMR levels and the risk of stroke (P for non-linearity = 0.975). Reclassification analysis showed that adding caIMR improved risk classification, with an IDI of 0.0307 (95% CI: 0.0031-0.0636; P = 0.030) and an NRI of 0.3887 (95% CI: 0.3156-0.4618; P < 0.001).

Conclusion

Elevated caIMR is independently associated with an increased risk of long-term ischemic stroke in STEMI patients after pPCI. This easily accessible metric may serve as a valuable tool for future risk stratification in this patient population.

title: The CML/esRAGE ratio as a potential biomarker of early diastolic impairment in asymptomatic type 1 diabetic patients without overt heart disease.
authorString: Wang D, Lin J, Chen S.
abstractText:
Background

Heart failure is a prevalent complication of diabetic microangiopathy, and early identification of myocardial dysfuntion is crucial. Advanced glycation end products (AGEs) bind to their receptor RAGE and further promote diabetic late complications as well as heart failure. Two soluble RAGE isoforms, endogenous secretory RAGE (esRAGE) and the cleaved extracellular fragment of membrane RAGE (collectively termed sRAGE), are believed to exert cardioprotective effects by acting as RAGE decoy receptors. This pilot study aimed to investigate the associations of AGEs, sRAGE and esRAGE with early cardiac dysfunction identified via advanced echocardiography.

Methods

We enrolled 29 type 1 diabetic patients without known heart disease(EF ≥ 50%) and 31 healthy controls. Plasma levels of two major AGEs, carboxymethyllysine(CML) and methylglyoxal-derived hydroimidazolone 1(MG-H1), as well as sRAGE and esRAGE were measured using immunoassay. Conventional, tissue Doppler, and speckle-tracking echocardiography were performed.

Results

In the diabetic group, global longitudinal strain (GLS) and peak early diastolic velocity at the lateral mitral annulus [e(lat)] were significantly lower, while E/e(lat) was higher. CML levels and CML/esRAGE ratio were increased, and esRAGE was decreased in the diabetic group. Pearson correlation analysis showed GLS was significantly associated with disease duration, total cholesterol (TC), HbA1c, esRAGE, and CML/esRAGE ratio; Univariate linear regression confirmed that higher CML/esRAGE ratio was associated with lower e(lat) (β = -0.006, P = 0.047).Variables with P < 0.1 in univariate regression together with pre-specified clinical covariates including age, gender, HbA1c, disease duration, and heart rate were incorporated into stepwise multiple regression; the model demonstrated that CML/esRAGE was independently associated with e(lat) (β = -0.006, 95%CI: [-0.012, -0.001], P = 0.049).

Conclusion

Elevated CML/esRAGE ratio is associated with impaired left ventricular diastolic function, and may represent a candidate biomarker for early diastolic dysfunction. Our study also suggest that CML/esRAGE ratio may not associated with GLS abnormalities reflecting subclinical systolic dysfunction. All observations from this pilot study require further validation in large independent prospective cohorts.

title: Prenatal ultrasound diagnosis and follow-up tracking of a case of congenital coronary artery fistula.
authorString: Huang H, Liang Y, Yu Y, Zhao X, Sun L.
abstractText:
Background

Congenital coronary artery fistula (CAF) is a rare congenital cardiovascular malformation characterized by an anomalous connection between a coronary artery and a cardiac chamber or great vessel. Prenatal diagnosis remains challenging. A 29-year-old G2P1 pregnant woman was diagnosed with fetal left coronary artery-to-right ventricle fistula via prenatal ultrasound at 21 weeks. Postpartum follow-up showed progressive coronary dilation, leading to surgical repair. A cardiac enhanced CT scan also confirmed the diagnosis of CAF. One-year postoperative ultrasound revealed improved cardiac structure with residual mild complications.

Conclusion

Prenatal ultrasound is pivotal for early CAF diagnosis, guiding postnatal intervention and improving prognosis.

title: Anticoagulation therapy in children with SARS-CoV-2 pneumonia: a retrospective observational study on dosage, efficacy, and safety.
authorString: Phung NTN, Tran TT, Van Nguyen N, Nguyen DH, Nguyen MAT.
abstractText:
Background

Coagulopathy is a significant complication in pediatric COVID-19, yet optimal anticoagulation dosing in children remains uncertain due to the lack of randomized controlled trials. This study aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of prophylactic versus therapeutic anticoagulation dosing in children hospitalized with SARS-CoV-2 pneumonia.

Methods

A retrospective observational study was conducted at Children's Hospital 1 in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, from July 2021 to May 2022. Pediatric patients with confirmed COVID-19 who received enoxaparin were included. Following the national paediatric protocol, patients were stratified by enoxaparin dose into a prophylactic-dose group (0.5 mg/kg every 12 h; total ≤ 1 mg/kg/day) and a therapeutic-dose group (1 mg/kg every 12 h; total > 1 mg/kg/day). Because thrombotic events and deaths were rare, length of hospital stay and changes in inflammatory and coagulation biomarkers were examined as exploratory surrogate outcomes, while in-hospital mortality and bleeding events were reported descriptively. Multivariable regression and inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) were used to reduce, but not eliminate, confounding by indication.

Results

Of 181 eligible patients, 140 were included (99 prophylactic-dose, 41 therapeutic-dose). The therapeutic-dose group had a higher proportion of severe/critical disease (82.9% vs. 55.6%, p = 0.003). After multivariable adjustment, therapeutic dosing was not associated with a significant difference in length of hospital stay (β = 0.041, 95% CI: -0.165 to 0.246, p = 0.698), changes in D-dimer (β = 0.195, p = 0.797), C-reactive protein (β = 0.122, p = 0.985), or ferritin levels (β = 191.6, p = 0.509). No thrombotic events occurred in either group. In-hospital mortality was low (5/140, 3.6%) and did not differ between the prophylactic- and therapeutic-dose groups (4.0% vs. 2.4%, p = 1.000). Major bleeding was confined to two patients (4.9%) in the therapeutic-dose group; with only two events, no reliable safety comparison between dosing strategies was possible. IPTW sensitivity analysis was consistent with these results.

Conclusions

After adjusting for disease severity and other confounders, we did not detect a statistically significant difference in efficacy outcomes between prophylactic- and therapeutic-dose anticoagulation. Because of the retrospective design, small sample, strong confounding by indication, and the absence of thrombotic events, these findings are exploratory and hypothesis-generating; the lack of a statistically significant difference should not be interpreted as evidence of equivalence between the two strategies. Prospective, adequately powered studies are needed before any dosing strategy can be recommended for children with SARS-CoV-2 pneumonia, particularly in resource-limited settings where anti-Xa monitoring is unavailable.

title: Incidence and predictors of early neonatal mortality among neonates admitted to neonatal intensive care units in public general hospitals in Northwest Ethiopia: a multicenter prospective cohort study.
authorString: Melese YA, Kassie DG, Agumas SH, Mekonnen HS.
abstractText:
Background

Early neonatal mortality remains a major public health concern in Ethiopia, particularly among high-risk neonates requiring intensive care. However, prospective evidence from general hospital settings is limited. This study aimed to determine the incidence and predictors of early neonatal mortality among neonates admitted to neonatal intensive care units in Northwest Ethiopia.

Methods

A multicenter prospective cohort study was conducted in seven public general hospitals from April 11 to July 14, 2025. Neonates aged < 7 days were followed from NICU admission until death, discharge, or completion of seven days of life. Data were collected using structured interviews and chart reviews. Modified Poisson regression with robust variance was used to identify predictors of early neonatal mortality. Variables with a p-value < 0.2 in bivariable analysis were included in the multivariable analysis. Multicollinearity was assessed using the Variance Inflation Factor (VIF). Adjusted risk ratios (ARR) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were reported. Statistical significance was set at a p-value < 0.05.

Result

Of the 380 enrolled neonates, 369 (97.1%) were included in the final analysis. Most neonates (86%) were admitted within the first 24 h of life, and 55.6% were male. A total of 63 deaths occurred during follow-up, yielding a cumulative incidence proportion of 17.1% (95% CI: 13.2-20.9). Independent predictors of early neonatal mortality included prolonged rupture of membranes ≥ 12 h (ARR: 2.48; 95% CI: 1.58-3.88), perinatal asphyxia (ARR: 2.31; 95% CI: 1.42-3.75), prematurity (ARR: 2.11; 95% CI: 1.15-3.88), and early-onset neonatal sepsis (ARR: 1.92; 95% CI: 1.16-3.16).

Conclusion

Early neonatal mortality remains high among general hospital-admitted neonates in Northwest Ethiopia and is strongly associated with preventable maternal and neonatal predictors. Strengthening obstetric care, neonatal resuscitation, and infection prevention strategies is essential to reduce mortality. However, these findings are specific to NICU-admitted populations and should not be interpreted as population-level estimates.

title: Development of a nomogram for risk factors of wheezing in infants with Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia.
authorString: Jianlong C, Yingying Y, Zhiling Z, Weifang Z, Wei J, Chu C.
abstractText:
Objective

To construct a nomogram model for analyzing risk factors of wheezing in infants with Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia (MPP), so as to provide evidence for clinical intervention.

Methods

A retrospective analysis was performed on clinical data of 569 infants with MPP hospitalized in the Department of Respiratory Medicine and Department of Infectious Diseases, Children's Hospital of Soochow University. They were divided into a wheezing group (204 cases) and a non-wheezing group (365 cases) according to symptoms. Demographic characteristics, clinical manifestations, laboratory examinations, bronchoscopy frequency and chest imaging findings were collected. Differences in clinical and laboratory indicators between the two groups were compared. Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) regression was used for preliminary screening, followed by Logistic regression to identify independent risk factors for wheezing in infants with MPP. Finally, a nomogram prediction model was established, and its performance was evaluated by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve and decision curve analysis (DCA).

Results

1. Univariate and multivariate analysis of predictors for wheezing in MPP: Univariate Logistic regression screening revealed 16 potential risk factors: fever, cough, history of wheezing, history of eczema, WBC, N#, L#, PLT, CRP, IgG, IgM, CKMB, D-D (ug/L), HRV, HRSV, HMPV (P < 0.05). Multivariate Logistic regression showed that history of wheezing (OR = 5.894, 95%CI: 3.541-9.812), history of eczema (OR = 1.951, 95%CI: 1.295-2.939), elevated IgG (OR = 1.166, 95%CI: 1.074-1.266), elevated CKMB (OR = 1.083, 95%CI: 1.007-1.164), and combined HRSV infection (OR = 3.430, 95%CI: 1.819-6.468) were risk factors, while fever (OR = 0.389, 95%CI: 0.252-0.599) was a protective factor against wheezing in infants with MPP. 2. Establishment and validation of the nomogram model: Based on multivariate Logistic regression, six indicators were included to construct the nomogram for predicting wheezing in MPP: history of wheezing, history of eczema, elevated IgG, elevated CKMB, combined HRSV infection, and fever. Each predictor was scored independently, and the total score corresponded to the predicted probability of wheezing caused by MPP. Model evaluation: Training set: AUC = 0.7862, sensitivity = 72.4%, specificity = 78.1%; Internal validation set: AUC = 0.6863, sensitivity = 53.7%, specificity = 79.5%, indicating favorable discrimination. DCA suggested potential clinical applicability.To further evaluate the robustness of the nomogram and to correct for potential optimism, we performed 200 bootstrap resampling iterations within the development cohort. The optimism-corrected area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was calculated by subtracting the average optimism (estimated from the difference between apparent performance in each bootstrap sample and the performance applied to the original dataset) from the training-set AUC. The corrected AUC was 0.705 (95% CI: 0.662-0.748), which is consistent with the internal validation result (AUC = 0.686) and indicates moderate discriminative ability. Although the corrected AUC remained above 0.70, the decline from the training-set AUC (0.786) suggests some degree of overfitting, likely attributable to the single-center retrospective design and limited sample size. These bootstrap-corrected estimates support the potential clinical utility of the nomogram.

Conclusion

Atopic constitution and mixed viral infection are risk factors for wheezing in infants with MPP. The nomogram model is clinically valuable for predicting wheezing in infants with MPP.

title: COL10A1<sup>+</sup> fibroblasts define rupture-prone abdominal aortic aneurysms and enable molecular risk stratification.
authorString: Zhuo H, Ou C, Duan M, Yang J, Liu D.
abstractText:
Background

Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) rupture remains the leading cause of AAA-related mortality, while current clinical management relies primarily on aneurysm diameter, which inadequately predicts rupture risk. Increasing evidence suggests that stromal cell heterogeneity critically shapes vascular remodeling; however, the specific fibroblast states associated with AAA rupture predisposition remain poorly defined.

Methods

We integrated cross-species single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets spanning the full spectrum of AAA progression to systematically characterize fibroblast heterogeneity and state transitions. Pseudotime trajectory analysis, transcriptional regulatory network inference, and ligand-receptor interaction modeling were applied to delineate fibroblast-associated microenvironmental programs. Based on these findings, a fibroblast-derived molecular signature was constructed and validated in an independent human AAA cohort.

Results

Single-cell analysis revealed a progressive transition from homeostatic IGFBP6+ fibroblasts to a disease-associated COL10A1+ fibroblast state during AAA progression. COL10A1+ fibroblasts were selectively enriched in rupture-prone lesions and exhibited transcriptional programs linked to extracellular matrix remodeling and osteogenic-like activation. Intercellular communication analysis indicated that COL10A1+ fibroblasts were predicted to engage macrophage populations through coordinated ligand-receptor signaling pathways, including MDK, CSF1, and CXCL12, collectively delineating a rupture-associated vascular microenvironment. Translationally, leveraging this fibroblast state enabled the development of a minimal two-gene risk score (COL10A1-IGFBP6), which stratified AAA patients by molecular rupture risk independently of aneurysm diameter in the validation cohort.

Conclusions

This study identifies a COL10A1+ fibroblast-associated transcriptional state that defines a rupture-prone vascular microenvironment in abdominal aortic aneurysm. The derived COL10A1-IGFBP6 signature establishes a biologically informed framework for molecular risk stratification, complementing anatomical size-based assessment and providing a foundation for future development of mechanism-guided strategies to refine AAA risk evaluation.

title: Clinical spectrum and risk factors for severe arrhythmias in non-surgical pediatric patients: a single-center retrospective study.
authorString: Yang L, Deng C, Zhang B.
abstractText:
Objective

To analyze the clinical spectrum and identify risk factors for severe arrhythmias in children.

Methods

A single-center retrospective study was conducted on 428 consecutive children (0-18 years) diagnosed with arrhythmia between January 2021 and October 2025. Patients were classified as having severe arrhythmia-related clinical presentation (severe group, n = 107) or non-severe presentation (non-severe group, n = 321) according to the presence of hemodynamic instability, syncope, heart failure, or malignant arrhythmia features. Clinical spectrum characteristics were collected. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent risk factors for severe arrhythmias. Electrocardiographic (ECG), echocardiographic, and serological parameters were compared.

Results

The severe group had higher proportions of infants/toddlers (0-3 years), underlying cardiac disease, syncope history, and class III-IV heart function (P < 0.05). Multivariate analysis identified these as independent risk factors (P < 0.05): infant/toddler age [2.30 (1.08-4.89)], underlying cardiac disease [12.66 (6.01-26.68)], syncope history [45.84 (12.74-164.91)], and class III-IV heart function [32.97 (13.39-81.17)]. The prediction model showed good fit (Hosmer-Lemeshow P = 0.171) and discrimination (AUC = 0.925, 95% CI: 0.893-0.958). The severe group also exhibited longer QTc, wider QRS, more third-degree atrioventricular block, higher ventricular premature burden, larger cardiac dimensions (LVEDD/LAD Z-score), higher pulmonary artery systolic pressure and myocardial injury/heart failure markers (CK-MB, cTnI, BNP, NT-proBNP), but lower heart rate variability (SDNN), left ventricular ejection fraction, and serum potassium (P < 0.05).

Conclusion

Infant/toddler age, underlying cardiac disease, syncope history, and advanced heart failure are independent clinical risk factors for severe pediatric arrhythmias. A model incorporating these factors demonstrates strong predictive ability for early high-risk identification.

title: Effects of bracing on pulmonary function in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis: a systematic review.
authorString: Law YT, Hon LS, Lam KH, Lam OK, Yeung KC, Tsang SMH, Lau AYC.
abstractText:
BACKGROUND CONTENT: Adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) is the most common form of 3-dimensional pediatric spinal deformity, characterized by abnormal lateral displacement and rotation. Full-time rigid bracing is often prescribed to prevent curve progression during skeletal growth. Directed force is applied to the apex via the rib cage to achieve satisfactory in-brace correction. The short- and long-term effects of bracing on the pulmonary function remain unclear.

Purpose

To study the effects of bracing on the pulmonary function of AIS patients.

Study design

Systematic review.

Outcome measures

FEV1, FVC, VC and FEV1/FVC ratio.

Methods

Following the PRISMA guidelines, PubMed, Cochrane Library, Scopus, EBSCOhost and PEDro were analyzed from inception to 15 October 2025, searching keywords of "AIS", "bracing" and "Pulmonary function". Original English research reporting outcomes on AIS patients with bracing as a core intervention and measurements of pulmonary function parameters are included, while research including other interventions are excluded. 15 studies were selected, totaling 578 patients and 731 controls. ROBINS-I (Risk Of Bias In Non-randomized Studies -of Interventions) was used to assess risk of bias. Data extraction is performed on the papers, while the quality appraisal was done using the MINORS methodology score. Due to the heterogeneity of bracing regimen and pulmonary function outcomes adopted across included studies, a structured narrative synthesis approach instead of the meta-analysis was taken to summarize the findings.

Results

Short-term: Bracing is associated with a reduction in pulmonary function; however, there is no change in FEV1/FVC ratio. Long-term effects: AIS patients show a decrease in pulmonary function when the brace on in both the first and eighth month of bracing compared to brace off. Adolescents who received bracing treatment showed an improvement in pulmonary function 25 years after treatment compared to those untreated; however, their respiratory function remains worse than that of those without scoliosis.

Conclusions

The principle and mechanism of bracing pose a restrictive pattern on patients with AIS. There is an immediate decrease in the pulmonary function when the patients are braced. The decline in pulmonary function both in and out-brace increases when the patient is braced over a prolonged period of time (1 month vs 8 months). However, in longitudinal follow-up of up to 25 years post-treatment revealed that the pulmonary functions (both FEV1 and VC) improved significantly compared to pre-bracing (p < 0.001, with medium standard mean difference of 0.4 and 0.614 respectively), suggesting possible long-term benefits of bracing.

title: Sudden cardiac arrest during diagnostic workup: a rare case of high-risk interarterial left anterior descending artery anomaly.
authorString: Buzzelle Smith YG, Pérez Barrows BE, Rujano Mendieta PE, Guerra Núñez MA.
abstractText:
Background

Coronary artery anomalies are anatomical abnormalities involving abnormal origin, course, or termination of any of the three main epicardial arteries. These abnormalities may go unnoticed during a person's lifetime; however, they can occasionally present acutely or chronically as angina, myocardial infarction, cardiac arrhythmias, or even sudden cardiac death.

Case presentation

A 65-year-old woman with angina and stress-induced ST-segment depression in a treadmill test. Coronary angiography showed the absence of the left main coronary artery with separate origins of the left anterior descending artery and circumflex artery. During a planned cardiac computed tomography angiography scan, the patient presented with cardiac arrest secondary to ventricular fibrillation and was hospitalized. A high-risk interarterial course of the left anterior descending artery was identified, and coronary artery bypass grafting with surgical mobilization of the left anterior descending artery along its interarterial course, where it was ligated with a hemoclip prior to the first septal branch to prevent competitive flow. The postoperative course was uneventful.

Conclusions

When this rare anomaly is detected in the population, clinicians must identify the risk of fatal events and determine appropriate management based on age, symptoms, vascular anatomy, and the presence of arrhythmia.

title: Intubation videoendoscopy in a preterm infant with congenital tracheal stenosis and laryngotracheoesophageal cleft: a case report.
authorString: Namikata Y, Motokura K, Tenma Y, Eriguchi K, Watanabe K, Inaguma K, Okamoto S, Nishida Y.
abstractText:
Background

The co-occurrence of congenital laryngotracheoesophageal cleft and tracheal stenosis is extremely rare. Diagnosis is difficult and many affected neonates die within hours to days.

Case presentation

A male neonate was delivered at 32 weeks and 5 days of gestation. Birth weight was 1364 g. Severe asphyxia and respiratory failure were apparent soon after birth. Endotracheal intubation was not successful and esophageal intubation did not provide effective ventilation. Flexible intubation videoendoscopy was performed immediately while continuing mask bagging, which identified congenital laryngotracheoesophageal cleft and tracheal stenosis. Considering the diagnosis, our inability to intubate, and the patient's other anomalies including left diaphragmatic hernia and congenital heart disease, palliative care was proposed and the family agreed. He died 4 h after birth.

Conclusions

Congenital laryngotracheoesophageal cleft and tracheal stenosis, a rare and mostly fatal anomaly, can be diagnosed in neonates using intubation videoendoscopy. Rapid diagnosis allows for the early introduction of palliative care.

title: Left-sided surgical approach for tricuspid valve replacement in congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries with dextrocardia and situs inversus totalis: A case report.
authorString: Yue C, Tan T, Sun P, Li J, Ren C, Lai Y, Cui H.
abstractText:
Background

Congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries (ccTGA) is a rare congenital cardiac anomaly characterized by atrioventricular and ventriculoarterial discordance, resulting in a physiologically corrected circulation. When ccTGA is combined with dextrocardia and situs inversus totalis, surgical management becomes particularly challenging because of the mirror-image anatomy and altered spatial orientation.

Case presentation

A 61-year-old man presented with progressive dyspnea and was diagnosed with ccTGA accompanied by dextrocardia and situs inversus totalis. Transthoracic echocardiography revealed severe regurgitation of the systemic atrioventricular valve (morphological tricuspid valve) with dilation and systolic dysfunction of the systemic right ventricle. Comprehensive preoperative imaging confirmed atrioventricular and ventriculoarterial discordance, right-sided cardiac apex, and complete visceral inversion. Tricuspid valve replacement was performed via a median sternotomy with the surgeon standing on the patient's left side to accommodate the mirror-image anatomy. Cardiopulmonary bypass was established safely after meticulous identification of the great vessels. A mechanical prosthetic valve was successfully implanted. The postoperative course was uneventful, and follow-up echocardiography at six months confirmed satisfactory prosthetic valve function without complications.

Conclusions

This case illustrates that tricuspid valve replacement can be safely and effectively performed in patients with ccTGA complicated by dextrocardia and situs inversus totalis. A left-sided surgical approach, combined with thorough preoperative imaging and careful intraoperative anatomical verification, may help restore operative orientation and reduce technical complexity in patients with mirror-image cardiac anatomy.

title: Isolated Left Innominate Artery with a Right Arch and Bilateral Patent Arterial Ducts in a Patient with 22q11 Microdeletion: Report of a Rare Case.
authorString: Bou Hussein H, Salameh R, Zareef R, El Rassi I, Bitar F, Bulbul Z.

journal.title: Journal of cardiovascular and thoracic research

abstractText: Isolated left innominate artery with right-sided aortic arch and bilateral patent ducts is a rare congenital abnormality. It has been described in association with various intracardiac lesions. In this report we describe the clinical presentation, investigations, and surgical management of a very peculiar case of a 4-year-old female with isolated left brachiocephalic trunk and bilateral patent arterial ducts without associated congenital heart defect, in the setting of 22q11 microdeletion.
