title: Comparative Outcomes of Left Anterior Thoracotomy Versus Resternotomy for Pulmonic Valve Replacement After Tetralogy of Fallot Repair.
authorString: Taksaudom N, Phothikun A, Horsatidkul J, Thepsuwan T, Woragidpoonpol S.
abstractText:
Objective

Redo pulmonary valve replacement (PVR) in patients with prior tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) repair is surgically challenging. This study aimed to compare the clinical outcomes of the left anterior minithoracotomy (LAT) approach with the traditional resternotomy approach for PVR.

Methods

A retrospective analysis was conducted on 38 TOF patients who underwent redo PVR, categorized into LAT (n = 20) and resternotomy (n = 18) groups. Patients requiring concomitant valvular surgeries or repair of residual intracardiac shunts were excluded. We compared demographics, operative details, and postoperative outcomes.

Results

Baseline demographics were comparable between groups, except for a higher proportion of males in the LAT group (75% vs 38.9%, P = 0.047). The LAT approach demonstrated nonsignificant favorable trends, including shorter operative times (157.05 ± 49.42 vs 178.06 ± 58.69 min, P = 0.239) and shorter postoperative hospital stays (4.75 ± 1.21 vs 6.17 ± 4.38 days, P = 0.173). Vasoactive-inotropic scores were significantly lower in the LAT group both immediately postoperatively (0.05 ± 0.22 vs 4.36 ± 6.95, P = 0.009) and on postoperative day 1 (0 vs 2.17 ± 4.52, P = 0.039). Postoperative complications, such as atrial fibrillation and pleural effusion, were similar between groups. There was no mortality in either group.

Conclusions

The LAT approach for PVR after TOF repair is a safe alternative to resternotomy. Comprehensive preoperative imaging evaluation is crucial for determining the optimal incision site. Further studies with larger cohorts are needed to confirm the potential benefits of this approach.

title: Neurodevelopmental risk in a referred sample of hospitalized children with congenital heart disease: interrelation between communication and feeding vulnerabilities.
authorString: Pimentel-Piemonte C, Sassi FC, Ritto AP, Medeiros GC, Andrade CRF.
abstractText:
Objective

To determine the prevalence of communication developmental risk in hospitalized children with Congenital Heart Disease (CHD) and to identify clinical, surgical, and hospitalization-related factors independently associated with increased risk.

Methods

This cross-sectional observational study was conducted at a tertiary pediatric cardiac center between September 2024 and April 2025. Sixty-five children referred for speech-language pathology assessment underwent communication development screening using a structured developmental observation protocol. Functional feeding status was assessed using the Pediatric Functional Oral Intake Scale. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors independently associated with communication developmental risk, with Firth's penalized logistic regression performed as a sensitivity analysis given the low events-per-variable ratio.

Results

Twenty-five children (38%) were classified as being at risk for delayed communication development. Hospitalization in a ward setting, compared with intensive care, was independently associated with lower odds of risk classification (adjusted OR = 0.13, 95% CI 0.02‒0.77, p = 0.025), an association confirmed by the Firth sensitivity analysis (adjusted OR = 0.18, 95% CI 0.03‒0.80, p = 0.024). Length of hospital stay, cyanotic physiology, cardiopulmonary bypass duration, and aortic cross-clamp time were not independently associated with risk. Children classified as at risk also showed significantly greater feeding restrictions.

Conclusion

Communication developmental risk was common among hospitalized children with CHD. Hospitalization setting and feeding performance, rather than traditional markers of clinical severity, were associated with communication risk, suggesting a multifactorial model that integrates biological, functional, and environmental factors. These findings suggest that feeding function, alongside hospitalization setting, may help flag children at higher developmental risk before formal communication assessment is available. These exploratory findings support incorporating structured developmental surveillance into routine pediatric cardiac care.

title: Impact of the Extent, Pattern, and Location of Replacement Myocardial Fibrosis on Clinical Outcomes in Aortic Regurgitation.
authorString: Li B, Dai L, Liu Y, Han Z, Tang Y, Chen X, Zhang A, Ma X, Zhou P, Jia X, Xu W, Aisikaier K, Han S, Sa F, Yang K, Zhao K, Yan C, Zhao S, Chen X.
abstractText:
Aims

The prognostic significance of late gadolinium enhancement (LGE)-detected replacement myocardial fibrosis in aortic regurgitation (AR) remains incompletely understood. This study aims to explore the association between the extent, pattern, and location of LGE and clinical outcomes in patients with chronic AR.

Methods and results

Between 2010 and 2024, consecutive patients with moderate-to-severe AR and no significant coronary artery stenosis who underwent contrast-enhanced cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) were included. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as cardiovascular mortality, heart transplantation, or rehospitalization for heart failure. The association between LGE characteristics and MACE was evaluated. Overall, 363 patients (mean age 52.6 ± 14.2 years; 54 female) were included. Over a median follow-up of 56.6 months, 73 patients experienced MACE. LGE was present in 200 patients (55.1%). An LGE extent threshold of 2.6% provided robust risk stratification, yielding the highest C-index of 0.797, a likelihood ratio chi-square of 97.30, and the lowest Akaike information criterion of 681.06. Furthermore, predominant subendocardial-involved LGE was present in 13.5% of LGE-positive patients and was independently associated with MACE after adjusting for LGE extent (HR 3.028; 95% CI 1.216-7.539; P = 0.017). Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated that patients with both LGE extent >2.6% and predominant subendocardial-involved LGE pattern were at the highest risk of MACE.

Conclusions

In AR, an LGE extent > 2.6% predicts MACE better than LGE presence alone. Furthermore, non-ischemic predominant subendocardial-involved LGE is independently associated with MACE. The coexistence of both features further amplifies the risk of MACE.

title: Single-Ventricle Physiology as a Dominant Determinant of Mortality, Resource Utilization, and Pulmonary Vein Reintervention in Total Anomalous Pulmonary Venous Connection: A Large Multicenter Study.
authorString: Turner D, Mehdizadeh-Shrifi A, Lee B, Ahmed HF, Chappell G, Batlivala S, Lehenbauer D, Ashfaq A, Morales DLS, Ricci M.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: World J Pediatr Congenit Heart Surg
journal.title: World journal for pediatric & congenital heart surgery
journal.isoabbreviation: World J Pediatr Congenit Heart Surg

abstractText: BackgroundChildren with single ventricle (SV) physiology and total anomalous pulmonary venous connection (TAPVC) face high surgical risk. Despite advances in single ventricle care, survival in SV/TAPVC patients has plateaued. We investigated multicenter outcomes, reintervention rates, and healthcare burden in this complex population.MethodsThe Pediatric Health Information System was queried for TAPVC repairs (2015-2024). Infants were stratified by single-ventricle versus biventricular (BiV) anatomy.ResultsAmong 1258 infants undergoing TAPVC repair, 10% (N = 120) had SV and 90% (N = 1138) had BiV anatomy. SV/TAPVC patients showed higher prematurity (11% [13/120] vs 8% [91/1138], P < .001), low birthweight (14% [17/120] vs 9% [102/1138], P < .001), and neurologic abnormalities (13% [16/120] vs 5% [60/1138], P < .001). Postoperatively, SV/TAPVC had increased delayed sternal closure (11% [13/120] vs 4% [45/1138], P < .001) and ECMO use (7% [8/120] vs 3% [34/1138], P < .001). Healthcare burden was substantially higher in SV/TAPVC children: 5-fold longer hospitalizations (102 vs 29 days, P < .001), 6-fold more hospital visits (6 vs 1, P < .001), and 5-fold higher costs ($1,019,390 vs $259,303, P < .001). Survival at 1 year after repair was severely reduced (SV: 52% vs BiV: 88%, P < .001). Pulmonary vein reinterventions were substantially higher (12-month cumulative incidence: 32% vs 5%, P < .001). Single ventricle physiology was a strong mortality predictor (HR: 3.69, P < .001), particularly pulmonary atresia with intact septum (HR: 6.62, P < .001) and hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HR: 4.42, P < .001).ConclusionsSingle ventricle physiology remains a powerful predictor of adverse outcome in children with TAPVC, with 1-year survival rates approaching 50%. Children with SV/TAPVC face substantially longer hospitalizations, higher reintervention rates, higher hospital visits, and overall 5-fold greater healthcare costs.

title: Infracardiac and mixed total anomalous pulmonary venous connection: Surgical challenges and practical solutions.
authorString: Alsoufi B, Alsoufi M.
abstractText: BackgroundTotal anomalous pulmonary venous connection (TAPVC) remains a complex congenital cardiac malformation. Despite improved survival, infracardiac and mixed variants continue to carry disproportionate risks of early mortality, postoperative pulmonary venous obstruction (PVO), and reintervention.MethodsThis narrative review examines the anatomic and technical challenges of infracardiac and mixed TAPVC, mechanisms and consequences of postoperative PVO, and contemporary strategies to reduce residual or recurrent obstruction, with particular emphasis on primary sutureless repair and anatomy-specific surgical approaches.ResultsContemporary operative mortality for TAPVC is approximately 3-10% but remains higher in patients with preoperative obstruction. Postoperative PVO occurs in approximately 5-15% and is an important determinant of reintervention and late mortality. In infracardiac TAPVC, obstruction may occur along with the descending vertical vein, producing severe pulmonary venous hypertension and physiologic instability. Mixed TAPVC presents additional challenges from heterogeneous drainage, multiple or small confluences, isolated veins, and complex geometry. Primary sutureless repair has evolved from treatment of recurrent PVO to a preventive strategy in high-risk primary TAPVC by avoiding pulmonary venous suture lines and facilitating wide, unobstructed drainage.ConclusionsManagement of infracardiac and mixed TAPVC requires an anatomy-specific approach focused on preventing postoperative PVO. Important strategies include selective preoperative stabilization, primary sutureless reconstruction in high-risk anatomy, a no-touch approach to selected isolated veins in 3 + 1 mixed TAPVC, and complete reconstruction of the cardiac component when appropriate.

title: Beyond conventional anthropometry: Muscle-related indicators and muscle strength in adults with congenital heart disease: A retrospective study with a comparison group.
authorString: de Sousa HRP, Pinho CPS.

journal.title: Nutrition in clinical practice : official publication of the American Society for Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition

abstractText: Anthropometric characteristics and muscle strength remain insufficiently characterized in adults with congenital heart disease (CHD). The aim of the study was to characterize anthropometric indicators and muscle strength in hospitalized adults with CHD and examine differences according to cardiac lesion complexity. Exploratory comparisons with adults without CHD were performed as secondary analyses. This cross-sectional study included 109 hospitalized adults with CHD and an external convenience group of 115 adults without CHD. Body mass index (BMI), mid-upper arm circumference (MUAC), triceps skinfold thickness (TSF), mid-arm muscle circumference (MAMC), arm muscle area (AMA), corrected arm muscle area (cAMA), and handgrip strength (HGS) were assessed. Cardiac defects were classified as mild, moderate, or complex. Associations of lesion complexity and previous cardiac surgery with anthropometric indicators and HGS were examined using multivariable linear regression. Comparisons with adults without CHD were conducted as exploratory analyses using the same approach. Among adults with CHD, 57.8% had mild, 24.8% moderate, and 17.4% complex defects. Lesion complexity was associated with MAMC (P = 0.032); participants with complex defects had lower MAMC than those with mild defects (B = -2.44 cm; 95% CI: -4.26 to -0.63). Previous cardiac surgery was associated with higher BMI, MUAC, MAMC, and AMA. In adjusted exploratory comparisons, adults with CHD had lower weight, height, BMI, MUAC, MAMC, AMA, and HGS than adults without CHD, whereas TSF was similar. Values below reference ranges for BMI, MUAC, MAMC, cAMA, and HGS were more frequent in CHD. Greater lesion complexity was associated with lower MAMC, whereas previous cardiac surgery was associated with higher BMI, MUAC, MAMC, and AMA. Muscle-related anthropometric measures and HGS may provide complementary information beyond body size and adiposity in adults with CHD.

title: Impact of Socioeconomic Status and Rurality on the Rate of Prenatal Detection of Major and Critical Congenital Heart Disease in Western Australia.
authorString: Hurwitz SB, O'Connell E, MacDonald B, Kothari D, Dickinson JE, Yim D.

journal.title: Journal of paediatrics and child health

abstractText:
Aim

Prenatal diagnosis of congenital heart disease (CHD) is associated with reduced infant morbidity and mortality. Location and subsequent socioeconomic status influence rates and timing of prenatal diagnoses of CHD. We investigated the impact of socioeconomic status and rurality on the rate of prenatal diagnosis of critical and major CHD in Western Australia (WA).

Methods

This retrospective cross-sectional study reviewed all critical (surgical intervention ≤ 30 days of life) and major (surgical intervention ≤ 1 year of life) CHD in WA between 2017 and 2021. Patients were identified from the WA Fetal Cardiology and Perth Children's Hospital Cardiology Databases. Clinical records were used to identify diagnoses, outcomes, postcode, rurality (via the Modified Monash Model [MMM]) and socioeconomic status (Socio-Economic Indexes for Areas [SEIFA] Index of Relative Socio-economic Disadvantage). Postcode was used to estimate SEIFA index and MMM rurality.

Results

There were 478 cases with major CHD; 282 (59%) were prenatally diagnosed, of which 268 cases were critical CHD, with a 77% detection rate. Seventy-four percent of patients were from metropolitan areas. The distribution of SEIFA decile (p = 0.15) and MMM (p = 0.09) were not significantly different between pre- and postnatal groups. The diagnosis rate of univentricular CHD was 94% (n = 102) and 49% (n = 180) for CHD undergoing biventricular repair.

Conclusion

Critical CHD increases the likelihood of prenatal diagnosis in WA; however, rurality and socioeconomic status were not found to influence diagnosis rates. Further studies are needed to review the availability of obstetric services in rural communities to ensure equitable healthcare.

title: 4D Flow Acquisition Parameters as Technical Correlates of Hemodynamic Measurements: An Analysis of the multicenter Tetralogy of Fallot Registry of 4D flow Energetics and Kinetics (TREK).
authorString: Loke YH, Lee M, O'Hara R, Muegge W, Drews K, Gonzalez B, Axt-Fliedner R, Klein J, Friesen R, Dove M, Ta H, Kochav J, Goyal A, Schoeneberg L, Christopher A, Olivieri L, Krishnamurthy R, Balaras E, d'Udekem Y, Sotelo J, Taylor M, Fricke S, Bilionis I, Meyers BA, Capuano F.

journal.title: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance

abstractText:
Background

Advanced 4D flow cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) biomarkers such as kinetic energy (KE), vorticity (ω), and viscous energy loss (VEL) are increasingly used to characterize abnormal flow in repaired tetralogy of Fallot (rTOF), but their sensitivity to acquisition parameters including magnet vendor, sequence and signal quality has not been defined. We sought to evaluate the real-world variability in 4D flow sequences and technical correlates to 4D flow measurements of the aorta (Ao) and right ventricle, leveraging the multicenter Tetralogy of Fallot 4D flow Registry of Energetics and Kinetics (TREK).

Methods

This was a multicenter observational analysis of clinically acquired 4D flow CMR processed at a core laboratory. The technical analysis focused on systolic Ao and diastolic RV hemodynamic measurements of KE, ω and VEL. Time-resolved hemodynamic curves were summarized and compared across sequence/reconstruction type, contrast agents and sequence parameters. Interobserver variability was assessed with Bland-Altman analysis and intraclass correlation coefficients. Apparent signal-to-noise ratio (aSNR), apparent velocity-to-noise ratio (aVNR) and presence of velocity aliasing were also measured. Multivariable linear/logistic regression was used to identify acquisition parameters associated with aSNR, aVNR and aliasing. Multivariable linear regression models were constructed to evaluate associations of aSNR, aVNR, and aliasing with KE, ω, and VEL after adjustment for clinical covariates.

Results

The cohort included 345 datasets (295 rTOF studies and 50 controls). Sequence/reconstruction type, field strength, voxel volume, temporal resolution, and VENC were associated with aSNR and aVNR in multivariable models. Aliasing was associated with lower VENC. ω and VEL varied substantially across sequence/reconstruction type and contrast groups, whereas KE was comparatively more stable. In multivariable models, lower aSNR was associated with higher measured hemodynamic values after adjustment for clinical covariates, with stronger associations for ω and VEL rather than KE.

Conclusions

In a real-world multicenter 4D flow CMR registry, measured advanced hemodynamic biomarkers were associated with acquisition/reconstruction characteristics, apparent image quality, and residual aliasing. 4D Flow harmonization efforts should therefore extend beyond vendor types alone and explicitly account for aSNR, aVNR, and aliasing when interpreting derivative-based 4D flow measurements.

title: Weight-stratified analysis of the heterogeneous effects of miniaturized cardiopulmonary bypass on perioperative outcomes in children with congenital heart disease: A retrospective cohort study.
authorString: Ti Y, Wang Y, Zhang S, Zhou X, Liu H, Wang P, Yang H, Wu W, Zheng F, Zhang R, Du J, Chen B, Meng B, Hua Z.
abstractText: IntroductionMiniaturized cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) circuits may reduce intraoperative transfusion in pediatric cardiac surgery, but their effects across body weight categories remain unclear. This study compared transfusion and outcomes between conventional and miniaturized CPB circuits, emphasizing weight-stratified analyses.MethodsThis retrospective study included 3,196 pediatric cardiac surgery patients (2015-2024) receiving conventional (n = 548) or miniaturized (n = 2,648) circuits. Primary outcomes were transfusion avoidance during CPB, in the ICU, and combined. Secondary outcomes included ICU length of stay, mechanical ventilation, ultrafast-track extubation, 24-h chest tube drainage (normalized to mL/kg), and hematocrit dynamics. Multivariable logistic regression and subgroup analyses were performed.ResultsMiniaturized circuits improved CPB transfusion avoidance overall (47.9% vs. 29.0%; P < 0.001), especially in children weighing 3-9 kg (all P < 0.01). ICU transfusion avoidance was lower with miniaturized circuits overall (82.1% vs. 94.5%; P < 0.001), except in the 1-2 kg subgroup. Combined avoidance was higher with miniaturized circuits across 3-9 and 12-13 kg (all P < 0.05). ICU length of stay was shorter with miniaturized circuits in most weight subgroups, whereas it was prolonged in the 2-3 kg subgroup (150 vs. 75 h; P < 0.001). Overall mean 24-h chest tube drainage was significantly lower in the miniaturized group (9.05 ± 9.10 vs. 10.82 ± 7.76 mL/kg; P < 0.001); however, stratified analysis showed a significant increase only in the 4-5 kg subgroup (14.52 ± 7.88 vs. 11.96 ± 6.69 mL/kg; P = 0.046), with no differences in other weight strata. Multivariable analysis indicated that miniaturized circuits were an independent predictor of increased ICU transfusion risk (OR 2.59; P < 0.001), whereas higher body weight was associated with reduced risk (OR 0.76 per kg; P < 0.001).ConclusionsMiniaturized CPB circuits reduce intraoperative transfusion, particularly in children weighing 3-9 kg, but are associated with higher postoperative ICU transfusion and variable effects on chest tube drainage that are weight-dependent. The net benefit appears weight-dependent. These findings underscore the need for weight-stratified circuit selection, although further prospective studies are warranted.

title: The Fontan Procedure in Patients with Single-Lung Physiology: Insights from a Case Report and Scoping Review.
authorString: Guerrero-Becerra AF, Rubio-Duarte AF, Fontecha-Vargas EA, Márquez-Bohorquez D.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: World J Pediatr Congenit Heart Surg
journal.title: World journal for pediatric & congenital heart surgery
journal.isoabbreviation: World J Pediatr Congenit Heart Surg

abstractText: The Fontan operation represents the third stage of single-ventricle palliation and requires optimal cardiovascular and pulmonary conditions to achieve success. We report a 6-year-old boy with tricuspid atresia, pulmonary atresia, and functional single-lung circulation secondary to severe left pulmonary artery (LPA) hypoplasia and disconnection after previous palliation. Following comprehensive clinical, hemodynamic, and anatomic evaluation, including unsuccessful attempts at LPA recruitment, the patient underwent an extracardiac fenestrated single-lung Fontan procedure. At 2 years of follow-up, he remained in good functional status without Fontan-related complications or the need for reintervention. Additionally, we present a scoping review of published case reports and case series of children with single-lung physiology undergoing the Fontan procedure, focusing on early and follow-up survival. This case, together with the available literature, suggests that single-lung Fontan completion may be feasible in carefully selected patients following meticulous multidisciplinary evaluation, although long-term outcomes remain uncertain.

title: Postnatal evolution of electrocardiographic parameters in preterm infants: a prospective longitudinal cohort study.
authorString: Satpathy SK, Choudhary S, Paswal CM, Singh AK, Gupta N, Soni JP, Kumar RK, Choudhary R.
abstractText:
Electrocardiography (ECG), an indispensable bedside tool in neonatal intensive care, complements echocardiography by providing assessment of cardiac rhythm and conduction, and when advanced imaging is unavailable, serves as a screening tool. Preterm birth alters cardiac and autonomic maturation. Applying term-based ECG norms may misclassify physiological findings in preterm. We aimed to characterise serial ECG maturation in preterms from birth to term-equivalent age and define gestational- and postnatal-age-specific patterns relevant to clinical interpretation. In this prospective cohort, infants between 28⁰/₇ and 36⁶/₇ weeks' gestation without congenital heart disease underwent serial 11-lead ECG recording within 24 h of birth, on day 7, day 28 and at term-equivalent age. Postnatal and gestation-based differences in ECG parameters were analysed and centile charts were generated. Among 249 infants (mean gestation-334/₇ weeks), 213 completed follow-up until term-equivalent age. ECG parameters demonstrated consistent maturation across time points. The mean QRS axis shifted leftward from 117° at birth to 82° at term-equivalent age (p < 0.001). PR-interval, QRS and P-wave duration remained stable across all time points. Mean QTc showed minimal overall change. Transient QTc prolongation occurred in 8.1% of infants and resolved by term-equivalent age. Right precordial R-wave amplitudes declined over time, whereas left precordial amplitudes increased. At term-equivalent age, very preterm infants exhibited a more leftward QRS axis compared with late preterm infants. Infants with bronchopulmonary dysplasia showed trends toward right ventricular dominance.

Conclusion

Preterm ECG findings are dynamic, gestation-dependent markers of cardiovascular transition. This study characterises longitudinal ECG maturation in preterms and provides reference values, supporting improved decision-making in preterm care.

What is known

• Electrocardiographic reference nomograms used in neonatal practice are primarily based on paediatric cohorts or cross-sectional studies of term infants. These references provide limited information on longitudinal electrophysiologic maturation in preterm neonates.

What is new

• In a cohort of 249 preterm infants, serial ECG measurements demonstrated changes in axes, QTc, and precordial voltages from birth to term-equivalent age. • These gestation and age-specific trajectories support cautious interpretation of preterm ECGs using term-derived standards.

title: 2026 update on the COVADIS diagnostic criteria of international standardization for microvascular angina.
authorString: Ong P, Camici PG, Beltrame J, Berry C, Crea F, Escaned J, van de Hoef T, Kaski JC, Pepine C, Sechtem U, Shimokawa H, Zeitz C, Merz NB.
abstractText: Microvascular angina, in the context of ischemia with non-obstructed coronary arteries (INOCA), is a highly prevalent clinical condition in cardiovascular medicine. Although it remains frequently underdiagnosed, clinical research and practice have made substantial progress in the last 10 years. This includes better characterisation of affected patient cohorts, new data on the prevalence of coronary vasomotor disorders and improved diagnostic assessments (non-invasive and invasive). The aim of this paper is to update our previous 2018 recommendations for the standardization of diagnostic criteria for microvascular angina. The updated COVADIS (Coronary Vasomotor Disorders Study Group) criteria focus on the following 4 criteria: (1) symptoms of myocardial ischemia; (2) non-obstructive coronary disease (stenosis <50%); (3) objective evidence of myocardial ischemia and (4) evidence of impaired coronary microvascular function. The updated criteria incorporate new suggestions for endotype definitions based on the invasive assessment of coronary physiology including coronary flow reserve and the index of microvascular resistance during pharmacological stress as well as acetylcholine testing for epicardial and/or microvascular spasm. The updated criteria should contribute to improved recognition and better management of this condition.

title: Prognostic associations of left atrial strain with major adverse cardiovascular events and atrial fibrillation: Data from the Akershus Cardiac Examination (ACE) 1950 Study.
authorString: Solberg MG, Rønningen PS, Berge T, Enger S, Pervez MO, Orstad EB, Kvisvik B, Aagaard EN, Lyngbakken MN, Omland T, Røsjø H, Steine K, Tveit A.
abstractText:
Background

Left atrial (LA) reservoir (LASr), conduit (LAScd) and contractile (LASct) strain are known to reflect atrial remodeling and is prognostic in atrial fibrillation (AF) and heart failure. Evidence is scarce on prediction of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in general populations. LA mechanical dispersion (LA MD) and stiffness index (LASI) are less studied strain-derived indices of AF and cardiovascular risk.

Methods

The Akershus Cardiac Examination 1950 Study included 3706 participants from the general population who underwent baseline echocardiography in 2012-2015. MACE (cardiovascular death, non-fatal stroke, non-fatal myocardial infarction or coronary intervention) and incident AF were recorded through 2022. Prognostic value of LA strain was assessed by Cox regression.

Results

In 3229 participants with baseline LA strain analysis, MACE was recorded in 242 (7.5%) and incident AF in 157 (5.0%) over a median 8.3 years (IQR 7.9-8.9) of follow-up. LASr, LAScd and LASI were associated with MACE in univariable analyses, and LASI remained independently associated with MACE after multivariable adjustment (HR per 1SD increment 1.12, 95% CI 1.04-1.21). LASr (HR per 1SD decrement 1.21, 95% CI 1.01-1.45), LASct (HR per 1SD decrement 1.26, 95% CI 1.04-1.52) and LA MD (HR per 1SD increment 1.23, 95% CI 1.03-1.48) were independently associated with incident AF after multivariable adjustment. Accounting for competing risk of all-cause death, LA MD remained independently associated with incident AF, whereas LASr and LASct did not.

Conclusion

In a general population, LASI was independently associated with MACE, whereas LASr, LASct and LA MD were associated with incident AF.

title: Long-Term Outcomes After Heart-Lung Transplantation: A Contemporary 20-Year Single-Center Experience.
authorString: Székely M, Yousefzai R, Lopez-Trevino M, Chihara R, Del Val FR, Gecse II, Ghobrial RM, Duarte V, Martin C, Huang HJ, Guha A, Akay MH, Bhimaraj A, Reardon MJ, Quarti AG.

journal.title: The Journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery

abstractText:
Objective

(s): We aimed to evaluate long-term outcomes after heart-lung transplantation (HLTx) including comparisons between adult congenital (CHD) and non-congenital (non-CHD) recipients and outcomes before and after implementation of the 2018 United Network for Organ Sharing heart allocation system change.

Methods

Consecutive patients undergoing HLTx between February 2006 and February 2026 were retrospectively reviewed. The primary endpoint was overall survival. Secondary endpoints included chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD)-free survival and perioperative outcomes. Kaplan-Meier analysis was used for time-to-event outcomes.

Results

Sixty-two patients underwent HLTx, including 20 (32.3%) with CHD and 42 (67.7%) with non-CHD etiologies. Despite greater operative complexity, perioperative outcomes were comparable between groups, with an overall 30-day mortality of 11.3%. Median overall survival was 7.8 years with estimated 1-, 5-, and 10-year survival of 80.1%, 58.8%, and 37.9%, respectively. Median CLAD-free survival was 5.9 years with estimated 1-, 5-, and 10-year rates of 76.6%, 53.5%, and 24.0%, respectively. Overall and CLAD-free survival were similar between CHD and non-CHD recipients (p=0.151 and p=0.354, respectively). Most late deaths were lung-related (20/27, 74%), whereas cardiac causes were uncommon (1/27, 3.7%), and CAV developed in two patients (3.2%). Recipients transplanted after the allocation change demonstrated improved survival (p=0.022), mainly due to a decline in perioperative mortality from 17.5% to 0% (p=0.044).

Conclusions

Long-term outcomes after HLTx remain primarily limited by CLAD and lung-related complications. Adults with CHD achieved survival comparable to non-CHD recipients. Improved contemporary outcomes appear to be driven predominantly by reduced perioperative mortality.

title: Establishing the reliability of non-contrast 4D flow in congenital heart disease at 1.5T.
authorString: Brown NK, Romberg EK, Schmitt C, Pinto NM, Howard W, Robinson JD, Soriano B, Buddhe S.
abstractText:
Background

4D flow has been shown to correlate well with 2D phase-contrast (2D PC) flow measurements, although most of the current literature is based on post-contrast imaging.

Objective

Given recent interest in non-contrast techniques, we hypothesized that non-contrast 4D flow (NC 4D Flow) would correlate well with 2D PC and ventricular stroke volumes.

Methods and materials

A prospective cohort of pediatric and young adult patients with suspected/confirmed congenital heart disease (CHD) underwent cardiac MRI at 1.5T with acquisition of NC 4D Flow and 2D PC. Pearson correlation, linear mixed-effect correlations, and Bland-Altman comparisons were performed to compare these methods with secondary analyses of internal consistency and image quality/noise.

Results

In our cohort of 30 patients (age, 8-20 years), NC 4D Flow correlated strongly with 2D PC for net flow (r=0.76), peak velocity (r=0.9, P<0.001), and regurgitant fraction (r=0.75, P<0.001). By Bland-Altman comparison, NC 4D Flow was 10.1% lower for net flows and 18.9% higher for peak velocity compared to 2D PC. NC 4D Flow also slightly underestimated ventricular stroke volumes (18.1% lower for ascending aorta vs. left ventricular stroke volume and 13.9% lower for main pulmonary artery vs. right ventricular stroke volume). Both datasets were internally consistent; 2D PC had a higher relative signal intensity, but no difference in signal-to-noise or contrast-to-noise ratios (SNR/CNR).

Conclusion

Non-contrast 4D flow correlates well with 2D PC in CHD with a slight underestimation in flows and overestimation in peak velocities, but good internal consistency and comparable SNR/CNR.

title: Association between the inferior vena cava collapsibility index and Fontan pressure in patients with Fontan physiology: a two-centre prospective pilot study.
authorString: Campbell MD, Mir A, Behere S, Huang JH, Burch G, Alnoor M, Madriago E.
abstractText:
Introduction

Patients with functional single ventricle anatomy undergo staged surgical palliation in early childhood culminating in the Fontan procedure whereby the inferior vena cava is connected to the pulmonary artery. Fontan circulation inherently requires elevated central venous pressure to maintain adequate pulmonary blood flow; however, excessive elevation is associated with morbidity and mortality. In adults, a key component of echocardiographic evaluation is the use of a "sniff test" as a surrogate of downstream right atrial pressure. This technique has not yet been validated as a measure of pressure assessment in patients with Fontan circulation.

Methods

This was a two-center prospective study of patients with functional single ventricle physiology who had undergone the Fontan procedure and were undergoing previously scheduled transthoracic echocardiogram and cardiac catheterization as part of their standard clinical care. We correlated collapsibility index on echocardiogram with directly obtained Fontan pressure measurements from cardiac catheterization performed the same day.

Results

15 patients were enrolled and analyzed for the study. Collapsibility index demonstrated an inverse correlation with Fontan pressure, (Pearson r = -0.72, R2 = 0.51, p = 0.003). Collapsibility index was significantly higher for patients with non-elevated Fontan pressure (45% vs 30%, p = 0.0005). Using a collapsibility index threshold of 35.0% demonstrated a 100% positive predictive value for detecting elevated Fontan pressure (greater than 14 mmHg).

Conclusions

There was a significant inverse relationship between the collapsibility index and Fontan pressure. These findings may suggest a possible association between collapsibility index and Fontan pressure, warranting further investigation in larger studies.

title: National Survival Estimates After Surgical Repair of Congenital Heart Disease.
authorString: Fundora MP, Gauvreau K, Yang Y, Jacobs JP, Oster ME, Jenkins KJ, Kochilas L.
abstractText:
Background

Survival estimates after congenital heart surgery (CHS) in the United States are essential for planning healthcare services for this growing, resource-intensive patient population. However, the absolute number of individuals living after interventions for congenital heart disease is unknown because nationally representative survival estimates are unavailable. Understanding postoperative survival from a representative national sample is a critical first step toward estimating the size and future healthcare needs of this population. This study aimed to develop nationally representative long-term survival estimates after CHS in the United States, focusing on benchmark procedures defined by the Society of Thoracic Surgeons.

Methods

We used 3 US data sets of children aged 0 to 20 years at the time of their benchmark CHS from 1998 to 2002 and surviving to hospital discharge. The Pediatric Cardiac Care Consortium (PCCC), a multi-institutional clinical registry, was matched to the National Death Index to determine mortality through December 2019. The Kids' Inpatient Database 2000, a nationally representative administrative claims data set, was used to derive age- and sex-specific weights. Kaplan-Meier curves were estimated from the PCCC-National Death Index cohort for benchmark operations, and Kids' Inpatient Database 2000 weights were applied. Unweighted PCCC survival estimates were also compared with those of Boston Children's Hospital, a large tertiary care center.

Results

Nationally representative survival curves were generated for 7 benchmark CHS from 7973 cases; 3802 (48%) were female, and 4505 (57%) were infants at the time of CHS. These weighted national survival curves closely mirrored the unweighted curves derived from PCCC-National Death Index. Unweighted survival estimates from PCCC also closely approximated those from BCH, with only modest differences observed for selected lesions.

Conclusions

The weighted PCCC-National Death Index methodology provides the first nationally representative estimates of long-term survival after benchmark congenital heart disease in the United States. These estimates provide an important resource for healthcare planning and research for the growing population of individuals with congenital heart disease.

title: Mechanism of Mortality in Individuals with Elevated Risk Pulmonary Emboli: A Multicenter Analysis of a Contemporary Cohort.
authorString: Rozenbaum Z, Gnall E, Gholam A, Chang MF, Divya A, Sanina C, Wiley J.
abstractText: The underlying causes of mortality in patients with pulmonary embolism have been investigated in the past, yet management of pulmonary emboli has evolved and newer therapeutic options are available. Data from four hospitals during 2022-2025 were analyzed and all patients with intermediate-high risk and high risk pulmonary emboli who died during follow up were included. The results depicted in the research letter provide insight into the mechanism of morality in patients with pulmonary emboli by risk category and thereby help improve care and patient selection for interventions.

title: A 0/2-Hour Algorithm Using a Novel Point-of-Care High-Sensitivity Cardiac Troponin I Assay for Suspected Myocardial Infarction.
authorString: Koechlin L, Lopez-Ayala P, Boeddinghaus J, Sigg N, Durak K, Nestelberger T, Wildi K, Strebel I, Bima P, Crisanti L, Recuenco LH, Yueksel A, Miró Ò, Martin-Sanchez FJ, Kawecki D, Keller DI, Christ M, Buser A, Biefer HRC, Dzemali O, Broughton MN, Mahfoud F, Mueller C, APACE investigators.
abstractText: This letter describes the derivation and internal validation of an assay-specific hs-cTnI-SPINCHIP 0/2h-algorithm for rapid triage of patients with suspected myocardial infarction (MI) in the emergency department (ED). The algorithm provided very high safety for rule-out, high accuracy for rule-in, and enabled definitive triage within 2 hours in approximately 80% of patients. These findings support the clinical potential of the novel point-of-care hs-cTnI-SPINCHIP assay for accelerated ED decision-making.

title: Aortic coarctation and McArdle disease in histiocytosis-lymphadenopathy plus syndrome: expanding the <i>SLC29A3</i> spectrum.
authorString: Rehman B, Hassan SMD, Sagri MN, Kirmani S, Arif M.
abstractText: Histiocytosis-lymphadenopathy plus syndrome (HLPS) is a rare inherited disorder caused by SLC29A3 variants. We report 2 Pakistani brothers with HLPS and markedly different clinical features despite identical genotypes. The 15-year-old had severe growth failure, facial dysmorphism, insulin-dependent diabetes, hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, and coarctation of the aorta (CoA) requiring balloon dilatation. Genetic testing identified SLC29A3 and PYGM variants, indicating concurrent HLPS and McArdle disease. His 20-year-old brother had insulin-dependent diabetes and celiac disease from age 3, later developing hypertension, proteinuria, and characteristic skin changes. This case highlights marked intrafamilial variability in HLPS and identifies CoA as a rare cardiovascular feature. It also supports comprehensive genetic testing in patients with early-onset diabetes and multisystem disease.

title: Elevated lithium levels in drinking water are associated with higher prevalence of Wolff-Parkinson-White diagnoses.
authorString: Teraoka JT, Agarwal A, Tang JJ, Dewland TA, Marcus GM.
abstractText:
Background

Supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) and Wolff-Parkinson-White (WPW) are potentially highly symptomatic and, rarely, lethal arrhythmias associated with atrioventricular accessory pathways. While the etiology of accessory pathways remains largely unknown, they are frequently observed with Ebstein's Anomaly, a congenital heart disease associated with maternal medicinal lithium use. Therefore, we evaluated whether in utero exposure to lithium from environmental sources is associated with the prevalence of accessory pathways.

Methods

We conducted a county-level ecological comparison of lithium levels in drinking water versus prevalence of WPW diagnoses among patients < 18-years-old in California using multivariable logistic regression. Children were analyzed given their high likelihood to reside in the same county during fetal development. WPW cases were identified using diagnostic codes. Positive and negative controls, including falsification endpoints, were analyzed.

Results

Among 2,329,090 patients (mean age 8.2 ± 5.9 years, 47.8% female), 686 (0.03%) were diagnosed with WPW. Areas where lithium levels ≥ 75th percentile were associated with 71% greater odds of WPW (OR 1.71, 95% CI 1.44 to 2.03). Areas above the lithium health-based screening limit had 29% greater odds of WPW (OR 1.29, 95% CI 1.05 to 1.58). Similar results existed in a New York statewide cohort. In validation analyses, areas where lithium levels ≥ 75th percentile were associated with a higher prevalence of SVT, syncope, palpitations, and catheter ablation procedures.

Conclusions

Higher lithium levels in drinking water were associated with a greater prevalence of childhood-diagnosed WPW, implicating a potentially modifiable risk factor for the development of accessory pathways.

title: Right Ventricular Function Assessed by Speckle Tracking Echocardiography in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Pulmonary Valve Replacement.
authorString: Kucuk M, de Alba CG, Zablah J, Leahy R, Taylor A, Iskander C, Rajic B, Morgan GJ.
abstractText: The effect of pulmonary valve replacement (PVR) on right ventricular (RV) function remains unclear. Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) is the gold standard for RV assessment but has practical limitations. Speckle tracking echocardiography (STE) may offer an alternative for evaluating RV systolic function. This study used STE to assess changes in RV systolic strain and right atrial (RA) strain following PVR. STE parameters including RV free-wall longitudinal strain (RVFWSL), RV four-chamber strain (RV4CSL), regional basal, mid-ventricular, apical RV strain, RA reservoir and contraction strain were assessed in 50 patients who underwent TPVR at pre-, post-operative day 1 and at six-month follow-up. RV systolic strain significantly improved after TPVR. RVFWSL increased from - 20.3 ± 5.1% at baseline to - 23.3 ± 5.2% (P < 0.001), and RV4CSL improved from - 18.5 ± 4.1% to - 21.3 ± 4.1% (P < 0.001). Regional RV strain also significantly improved at the basal, mid-cavity and apical levels (- 18.1 ± 4.3% to - 21.4 ± 5.5%, P < 0.001). RA reservoir and contraction strain, did not change significantly. Patients with RV end-systolic volume index < 80 mL/m<sup>2</sup> demonstrated greater improvement in RV4CSL than those with larger RV systolic volumes. Transcatheter PVR is associated with significant improvement in RV systolic strain at six months, with no significant change observed on postoperative day 1. This delayed recovery highlights the importance of longitudinal assessment, for which STE may serve as a feasible complementary tool to CMR in guiding follow-up imaging.

title: VSD Device Removal Due to Intermittent Complete Heart Block.
authorString: Farhati A, Ben Othman R, Msaad H, Hakim K, Arab R, Lehmayer E, Ouarda F.
abstractText:
Background

Percutaneous closure of perimembranous ventricular septal defects (pmVSDs) has markedly increased with the development of newer, softer occlusion devices.

Case summary

We report a 12-year-old girl who underwent percutaneous pmVSD closure. One week later, she was admitted for paroxysmal complete heart block (CHB). She was started on intravenous corticosteroids. A percutaneous retrieval of the device was performed successfully. Sinus rhythm was maintained throughout the 8-month follow-up period.

Discussion

Paroxysmal CHB is a rare but serious complication following percutaneous pmVSD closure. Its management remains challenging because of the potential for recurrence despite medical therapy. To our knowledge, percutaneous retrieval of a well-positioned ventricular septal defect occluder in this context represents the first case reported in the literature.

Take-home messages

Selecting the optimal device for pmVSD closure is crucial to ensure procedural success and reduce the risk of complications. CHB may occur immediately, early, or late after defect closure.

title: Comparison of Effectiveness of Caudal Dexmedetomidine vs. Caudal Fentanyl with Bupivacaine during Pediatric Cardiac Surgery with regards to Hemodynamic Fluctuations and Postoperative Pain.
authorString: Manwani RN, Wadaskar D, Panbude P, Mankhair S, Kanakam S.
abstractText:
Background

Optimum analgesia, reflecting into attenuation of stress response, is pertinent in pediatric cardiac surgery. Narcotics are still the mainstay in providing analgesia, and they are a common adjunct in caudal epidural analgesia. Unwanted effects of narcotics warrant a constant search for nonopioid analgesics.

Objective

To compare dexmedetomidine vs. fentanyl as an adjuvant in caudal anesthesia in pediatric cardiac surgery.

Materials and methods

Sixty patients, 1 to 8 years of age, with acyanotic congenital heart disease were divided into two groups randomly: group A received caudal dexmedetomidine 0.5 µg/kg with 2 mg/kg bupivacaine diluted to 1.6 ml/kg with normal saline. Group B received caudal fentanyl 1 µg/kg with 2 mg/kg bupivacaine diluted to 1.6 ml/kg with normal saline.

Results

Stress response assessed by surge in heart rate and blood pressure after induction was significantly lower in group A (Dexmedetomidine group). The mean time to successful discontinuation of mechanical ventilation was significantly lower in the dexmedetomidine group (1.2 ± 0.4 vs. 1.73 ± 0.58 h). Children in the dexmedetomidine group had lower FLACC pain scores at 4 hours postextubation (2.93 ± 1.04 vs. 3.83 ± 0.83), implying better pain control. The time to need for rescue analgesia was longer in the dexmedetomidine group (6.1 ± 1.21 vs. 3.96 ± 0.96 h).

Conclusion

Caudal dexmedetomidine gave better control of hemodynamic parameters when compared with fentanyl and was associated with earlier extubation postoperatively. It also has superior and prolonged analgesia compared to caudal fentanyl as an adjunct.

title: The Importance of Family Centered Care and Cascade Screening in Patients with Heritable Thoracic Aortic Aneurysm Disease.
authorString: Schwartz BJ, Starr LJ, Cratsenberg D, Gonzalez V, Yetman AT.
abstractText: Heritable thoracic aortic aneurysm diseases (HTAAD) may be either syndromic or non-syndromic. While family screening for all forms of HTAAD has been recommended, providing care to an entire family is often fragmented in our siloed healthcare delivery model. We sought to determine the frequency of cascade family screening in the current era with either cardiovascular imaging (cascade cardiac screening) and/or genetic testing (cascade genetic screening), and to assess the impact of such testing on adverse outcomes in first degree family members. Of the 184 HTAAD patients who presented to our academic center without a known family history of aneurysmal disease, 84 were followed in a cardiology clinic, 40 in a genetics clinic and 60 in a combined cardiovascular genetics clinic for both children and adults. Cascade cardiac or genetic screening of ≥ 1 family member occurred during the course of care in 138 of 184 (75%) families. Complete cascade screening (genetic and/or cardiac) of all at-risk first-degree family members occurred in only 61 (33%) families and varied by clinic type (12%, 10% and 78%, p = 0.001) for those initially evaluated in a cardiology, genetics, or combined cardiovascular genetics clinic. As a result of cascade screening or an aortic event, 461 additional family members were identified as at risk for an aortic event. Of these, 53 family members from 42 families experienced an unexpected HTAAD-related event. Cascade screening was associated with a lower incidence of an event (1/53 vs. 52/53, p < 0.0001) during follow-up. Clinics that offer family-based care and on-site cascade screening facilitate timely diagnosis and intervention thereby reducing mortality from aortic disease.

title: The Prognostic Value of Entropy from T1 Mapping in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.
authorString: Zhao J, Guo J, He J, Chen C, Liu X, Yin L, Pu S, Li Y, Xu Y, Wang J, Wan K, Han Y, Chen Y.

journal.title: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance

abstractText:
Background

The prognostic value of left ventricular (LV) entropy from T1 mapping in pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) remains unexplored.

Study design and methods

This prospective study enrolled patients with PAH who underwent cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) within 72h of right heart catheterization (RHC). Myocardial native T1, extracellular volume fraction (ECV) and entropy were calculated in mid-ventricular short-axis slice. The primary endpoint was defined as all-cause mortality or lung transplantation. Outcomes were further analyzed across groups stratified by survival status using Cox proportional hazards regression and Kaplan-Meier survival analysis.

Results

A total of 312 patients were analyzed over a median follow-up of 36.10 months, with 59 deaths. Elevated LV entropy was positively correlated with log-transformed NT-proBNP, right ventricular (RV) end-systolic, end-diastolic volume indices, LV native T1 and ECV, and inversely correlated with RV ejection fraction (all P < 0.01). LV entropy did not differ significantly across etiological subgroups, whereas LV entropy without IPs was higher in congenital heart disease-associated PAH. Both LV entropy ≥8.60 and LV entropy without IPs ≥8.30 independently predicted all-cause mortality (HR, 2.207; 95% CI, 1.324-3.678; P = 0.002; and HR, 2.357; 95% CI, 1.405-3.955; P = 0.001, respectively) and were associated with reduced survival (both log-rank P < 0.005). Adding LV entropy improved ESC models (χ²: 55.79 to 60.61, C-statistic: 0.782 to 0.801) and ESC-CMR models (χ²: 35.31 to 41.77, C-statistic: 0.805 to 0.813).

Conclusions

Elevated LV entropy was related to disease severity, RV dysfunction, and adverse clinical outcomes, and served as an independent predictor of all-cause mortality in patients with PAH.

title: High-Potency P2Y12 Inhibitors Among Patients With Chronic Coronary Syndrome Undergoing PCI: An Analysis From the NCDR CathPCI Registry.
authorString: Fath AR, Rymer J, Marks A, Wojdyla D, Gilchrist IC, Sandoval Y, Shah B, Brilakis E, Rao SV, Elgendy IY.
abstractText:
Background

Clinical practice guidelines recommend the use of clopidogrel among patients with chronic coronary syndrome undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention. The frequency of high-potency P2Y12 inhibitors, such as ticagrelor or prasugrel, in this setting is not well known.

Methods

Using the National Cardiovascular Data Registry CathPCI registry, we analyzed patients with chronic coronary syndrome undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention from April 2018 to June 2024, excluding those discharged on oral anticoagulants. Temporal trends in high-potency P2Y12 inhibitor prescription were examined. A mixed-effects multivariable logistic regression model with a random intercept for hospital was used to identify patient-, procedural-, and institutional-level factors associated with high-potency P2Y12 inhibitor prescription while accounting for within-hospital clustering. Between-hospital variation was quantified using the median odds ratio.

Results

Among 783 977 patients across 1815 hospitals, 35% were prescribed a high-potency P2Y12 inhibitor at discharge. The use of high-potency P2Y12 inhibitors declined from 35% in 2018 to 31% in 2024 (P-trend=0.019), driven by a reduction in ticagrelor (from 29% to 23%, P-trend <0.001) despite a modest increase in prasugrel use (from 6.2% to 8%, P-trend=0.10). Male sex, prior myocardial infarction, and markers of procedural complexity (high-complexity/type C lesions, left main coronary artery, proximal left anterior descending artery, or use of mechanical circulatory support) were associated with higher odds of high-potency P2Y12 inhibitor prescription. In contrast, older age (≥75 years), prior stroke/transient ischemic attack, prior coronary artery bypass graft, severe renal dysfunction, and chronic total occlusion were associated with lower odds. University hospitals had lower odds of prescribing high-potency P2Y12 inhibitors, with considerable variability in prescription patterns among institutions (median odds ratio, 2.59).

Conclusions

Nearly one-third of chronic coronary syndrome patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention were discharged on high-potency P2Y12 inhibitors, with decreasing trends over time. Practice patterns reflected perceived ischemic versus bleeding risk and significant institutional variation, underscoring opportunities for quality improvement and guideline alignment.

title: Prospective assessment of myocardial deformation in fetuses with suspected aortic coarctation.
authorString: Zwanenburg F, Trigler-Rinner J, Smit RM, Oberhoffer R, Wacker-Gussmann A, Ten Harkel ADJ, Haak MC.
abstractText:
Introduction

Prenatal identification of true aortic coarctation (CoA) remains challenging as evidenced by high false-positive rates. Myocardial deformation has been proposed to improve prediction of postnatal outcome. This prospective study aimed to determine whether fetal myocardial deformation analysis can differentiate true CoA from false-positive cases throughout gestation.

Methods

All fetuses with a prenatal suspicion of isolated CoA were prospectively recruited at our fetal cardiology services. Cases were classified as true CoA or false-positives based on their postnatal diagnosis. Speckle-tracking echocardiography was performed longitudinally to assess left and right ventricular global longitudinal strain (GLS), strain rate, and segmental strain throughout gestation. Measurements were compared between true CoA and false-positive cases.

Results

Thirty-eight fetuses were included (19 true CoA, 19 false-positives). True CoA cases exhibited smaller left-sided cardiac dimensions, including the aortic valve (mean Z-score -3.2 vs. -1.6, p<0.001), aortic isthmus (-3.5 vs. -1.7, p=0.001), and mitral valve (-4.9 vs. -3.1, p<0.001), whereas right-sided cardiac dimensions were comparable (pulmonary valve Z-score 3.0 vs. 2.6, p=0.64; arterial duct Z-score 1.9 vs. 3.2, p=0.61). No clinically relevant differences in myocardial deformation parameters were observed between groups, with similar left ventricular GLS (-20.1% vs. -20.5%, p=0.57), right ventricular GLS (-20.0% vs. -19.1%, p=0.13), strain rates and segmental strain.

Conclusion

Fetal myocardial deformation analysis does not provide additional predictive value for postnatal outcome in prenatally suspected isolated CoA. Conventional assessment of cardiac dimensions and flow patterns remains the cornerstone of prenatal CoA diagnosis, yet current imaging modalities cannot provide sufficient diagnostic certainty to safely triage perinatal management.

title: An Extremely Rare Association of the Giant Right Atrium with Uncorrected Tetralogy of Fallot in an Adolescent Male Patient.
authorString: Maiti A, Guha A.
abstractText:
Abstract

Uncorrected tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) can be associated with widespread abnormalities, but the giant right atrium (RA) is an extremely rare one. The giant RA can cause additional problems causing atrial arrythmias, thromboembolism, and compression of adjacent structures. Tricuspid regurgitation is common with annular dilatation. In symptomatic cases, reduction atrioplasty is recommended. Sternotomy should be careful to avoid damage to the giant RA. In asymptomatic cases, anticoagulation should be carried out. We report a rare case of uncorrected TOF associated with the giant RA and got successfully treated with surgery.

title: Management of Non-cardiac Surgery in an Elderly Patient with Uncorrected Double Inlet Left Ventricle: Utility of the Pulse Contour Analysis-Based Cardiac Output Monitor.
authorString: Honda J, Yamazaki Y, Hasegawa T, Noji Y, Inoue S.
abstractText:
Abstract

Double inlet left ventricle (DILV) is a rare congenital heart disease that usually requires surgical treatment in childhood but can survive to old age untreated under certain conditions. In such patients, general anesthesia management requires an understanding of their unique hemodynamics and pathophysiology, along with the ability to maintain these conditions. In this case, long-term survival was possible due to the maintenance of an appropriate pulmonary-systemic blood flow balance achieved by pulmonary artery stenosis (PS), necessitating anesthesia management that preserved this balance. We report a case of non-cardiac anesthesia in an untreated adult patient with DILV, where systemic vascular resistance (SVR) monitoring and anesthesia management using remimazolam were employed to maintain stable circulatory control.

title: Early-Onset Gastric Varices After Fontan Completion Associated with a Pre-Existing Gastro-Renal Shunt.
authorString: Takenaka S, Shinohara T, Yasuda M, Kimura H, Koyama S, Saitoh S.
abstractText: Gastroesophageal varices are recognized complications of Fontan-associated liver disease, but clinically significant varices have generally been reported more than 10 years after Fontan completion. The mechanisms of early variceal formation remain unclear. We report a child with tricuspid atresia who developed isolated gastric varices approximately 7 years after extracardiac Fontan completion in the presence of a pre-existing gastro-renal shunt (GRS). The patient underwent bidirectional Glenn palliation at 9 months of age. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) performed before Fontan completion incidentally demonstrated a GRS, which progressively dilated after Fontan completion. At 8 years of age, contrast-enhanced CT obtained during evaluation for hypoxemia incidentally revealed isolated gastric varices. The patient had no ascites, marked splenomegaly, thrombocytopenia, or evidence of advanced hepatic dysfunction. Cardiac catheterization showed an inferior vena cava (IVC) pressure of 14 mmHg. Given the potential risk of massive hemorrhage, the gastric varices were successfully treated with transvenous coil embolization and balloon-occluded retrograde transvenous obliteration through the GRS. No recurrence was observed during follow-up. This case suggests that a pre-existing GRS may contribute to the relatively early development of gastric varices after Fontan completion, even in the absence of markedly elevated systemic venous pressure or other clinical features of advanced portal hypertension. Because a pre-existing GRS could predispose patients to gastric variceal formation after Fontan completion, preoperative assessment of the abdominal venous anatomy using contrast-enhanced CT could be important.

title: Effect of Postoperative Arrhythmia in Children Less Than 18 Years of Age Following Congenital Cardiac Surgery: A Prospective Study.
authorString: D R, Mk S, Ms K, Sp S, S T, V D.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: World J Pediatr Congenit Heart Surg
journal.title: World journal for pediatric & congenital heart surgery
journal.isoabbreviation: World J Pediatr Congenit Heart Surg

abstractText: BackgroundPostoperative arrhythmias are common among children after congenital cardiac surgery, potentially compromising hemodynamic stability and postoperative recovery. This study aimed to assess the impact of arrhythmias on hemodynamics and clinical outcomes.Material and MethodsThree hundred and twenty-nine children under 18 years of age undergoing congenital cardiac surgery were studied prospectively. In addition to standard postoperative hemodynamic monitoring, electrical cardiometry (ICON®) was used to assess hemodynamic parameters across time points (prearrhythmia, during arrhythmia, and postarrhythmia). Repeated measures were analyzed using Friedman test followed by Wilcoxon signed-rank test with Bonferroni correction for pairwise comparisons. Poisson regression with robust variance estimation was used to identify independent predictors and calculate incidence rate ratios (IRR).ResultsPostoperative arrhythmias occurred in 53/329 patients (16.1%). Junctional ectopic tachycardia (34%, [18/53]) and supraventricular tachycardia (30.2%, [16/53]) were the most common. Arrhythmias were associated with low cardiac output (IRR 3.43; 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.27-5.17; P < .001), ventricular dysfunction (IRR 2.55; P < .001), acute kidney injury (IRR 2.01; P = .006), and liver dysfunction (IRR 4.56; P = .002) on unadjusted analysis. However, these associations were attenuated after adjustment for prearrhythmia hemodynamic variables like central venous pressure (CVP) and vasoactive-inotropic score (VIS) on multivariable analysis. Elevated CVP, VIS, and hypokalemia were predictors of arrhythmia.ConclusionsArrhythmias occurred in approximately one-sixth of children following congenital cardiac surgery and were associated with adverse hemodynamic changes, organ function, and recovery. However, these associations were attenuated after adjustment for prearrhythmia hemodynamic variables (CVP and VIS), suggesting that arrhythmia may reflect underlying instability rather than a primary causal factor.

title: Coronary artery imaging in Kawasaki disease: recent updates in imaging techniques and clinical indications.
authorString: Patharateeranart K, Goo HW, Kotoku A, Haifa AL, Wen L.

journal.title: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging

abstractText: Coronary artery involvement in Kawasaki disease should be evaluated throughout all disease stages. Generally, multimodality imaging is necessary for both the acute and chronic phases of coronary artery abnormalities. This review summarizes current clinical indications and recent technical advances in coronary artery imaging in Kawasaki disease with an emphasis on the roles of computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging. Echocardiography remains the first-line modality in all disease stages for evaluating coronary artery lesions and ventricular function. Recent technical developments in coronary computed tomography angiography can provide the accurate diagnosis of coronary artery lesions including stenosis and thrombus at substantially reduced radiation dose, supporting its selective use in serial follow-up. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging offers the comprehensive evaluation of inducible myocardial ischemia, ventricular function, inflammation, and fibrosis. Invasive catheter angiography is reserved for complex or interventional cases. This review also addresses technical considerations and potential pitfalls for each imaging modality. Continued technical developments and their optimization with standardized imaging protocols and reports are expected to enhance diagnostic precision and eventually improve clinical outcomes in children with Kawasaki disease.

title: Cardiovascular effects of continued vs. discontinued anabolic-androgenic steroid use: a longitudinal follow-up study.
authorString: Abdullah R, Bjørnebekk A, Hullstein IR, Thorsby PM, Helle-Valle T, Edvardsen T, Haugaa KH, Almaas VM.
abstractText:
Aims

Anabolic-androgenic steroid (AAS) use is prevalent among men engaged in strength training and is associated with adverse structural and functional cardiac changes, but longitudinal data are lacking. This follow-up study examined myocardial effects of AAS with continued use and reversibility following discontinuation.

Methods and results

Participants of a previously published cohort (2017-19) of 101 AAS users and 71 non-using weightlifting controls (WLCs) were invited for a follow-up study and underwent interviews, hormonal profiling, and transthoracic echocardiography. Current AAS users at baseline were continued or discontinued users at follow-up, while former users at baseline were those with continued abstinence and those who relapsed.Among those re-enrolled, 70 were AAS users, of whom 35 continued, 15 discontinued, 14 maintained abstinence, and 6 relapsed, and 35 were WLCs. Continued AAS users had persistent indexed left ventricular mass (LVMI 119 ± 30 g/m2), reduced LV ejection fraction (LVEF 48 ± 10%), and worsened diastolic function. Continued AAS users receiving antihypertensive therapy showed improved LVEF compared with untreated users (Δ = 5 ± 8 vs. -4 ± 8%, P = 0.005). Discontinued AAS users showed reduction in LVMI (Δ = -21 g/m2, P = 0.01) and improved LVEF (Δ = 6%, P < 0.001). At follow-up, these changes were comparable with WLCs, which showed statistically but clinically insignificant differences.

Conclusion

Continued AAS use was associated with sustained LV hypertrophy, LV systolic dysfunction, and worsening diastolic function. Antihypertensive therapy among ongoing AAS users was associated with improved LV systolic function. Discontinuation of AAS use was associated with improvement in cardiac structure and function towards values observed in WLCs.

title: Multichannel Dysfunction Associated With a Dominant-Negative <i>KCNH2</i> Missense Variant, p.G604S, Results in Action Potential Duration Prolongation and Early Afterdepolarizations in a Patient-Specific, Reengineered Cardiomyocyte Model of Type 2 Long-QT Syndrome.
authorString: Huynh T, Ye D, Zhou W, Tester DJ, Garmany R, Giudicessi JR, Ackerman MJ.
abstractText:
Background

Type 2 long-QT syndrome results from KCNH2-encoded Kv11.1 loss-of-function, but whether secondary inward-current dysfunction amplifies dysfunction remains unclear.

Methods

We characterized sodium (SCN5A, INa) and L-type calcium channel (CACNA1C, ICa) function in KCNH2-G604S and variant-corrected isogenic control induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (iPSC-CMs). Whole-cell patch-clamp measured action potential duration at 90% repolarization (APD90), and potassium (IKr), sodium (INa), and calcium (ICa, L) currents. Fluo-4 imaging quantified calcium transients. A modified Kernik-Clancy iPSC-CM model incorporated experimentally measured persistent INa,L and ICa,L fractions and simulated isolated and combined current defects.

Results

KCNH2-G604S caused severe IKr loss-of-function (72.5% reduction). APD90 was prolonged in G604S-iPSC-CMs (765±58 ms) compared with isogenic controls (368±37 ms; P<0.005), with early afterdepolarizations in 50% of G604S cells. Nifedipine, verapamil, and mexiletine successfully shortened APD90 and abolished early afterdepolarizations. Compared with isogenic control, INa,L (0.60±0.1% versus 0.26±0.06%; P<0.01), persistent ICa,L (2.88±0.55% versus 1.26±0.35%; P<0.05), and calcium transient decay times (P<0.0001) were greater in G604S iPSC-CMs. Increased persistent ICa,L was phenocopied by E-4031 in isogenic controls and reduced by nifedipine in G604S iPSC-CMs. In silico modeling revealed that the IKr defect alone prolonged APD90 to only 620 ms. The addition of the observed INa,L defect had a small additive effect (+20 ms); however, incorporating persistent ICa,L synergistically extended APD90 to 758 ms, replicating the experimental phenotype. Flux dynamics analysis indicated that this persistent Ca2+ entry suppresses the forward-mode sodium-calcium exchanger, forcing a compensatory reliance on sarcoplasmic-endoplasmic reticulum Ca-ATPase that primes for calcium instability.

Conclusions

The KCNH2-G604S variant drives a severe multihit phenotype via primary IKr loss-of-function and secondary state-dependent gain-of-function in persistent ICa,L. These comprehensive validations demonstrate that the remodeled persistent ICa,L acts as the essential amplifier driving extreme action potential duration prolongation and Ca2+ mishandling.

title: Pulsed field ablation with Renal denervation for persistent Atrial fibrIllation: Rationale and design of the PRAISE-AF randomized trial.
authorString: Guo J, Qin M, Jiang W, Ji Q, Miao Y, Sang Z, Li R, Hou X, Han W.
abstractText:
Background

Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common sustained cardiac arrhythmia worldwide and is associated with increased risks of stroke, heart failure, hospitalization, disability, and mortality. Catheter ablation has become an established rhythm-control strategy for symptomatic AF; however, the recurrence rate after ablation remains substantial, especially in patients with persistent AF. Pulsed field ablation (PFA) is an emerging nonthermal ablation technology with myocardial tissue selectivity and a potentially improved safety profile compared with conventional thermal ablation. Renal denervation (RDN) reduces sympathetic nervous system activity and has shown promising effects in reducing AF recurrence when combined with catheter ablation, mainly in patients with paroxysmal AF and hypertension. Whether RDN combined with PFA improves rhythm outcomes in patients with persistent AF remains unknown.

Trial design

This is a single center, prospective, randomized, patient-blinded, sham-controlled pilot exploratory trial. A total of 86 patients with symptomatic persistent AF undergoing first-time catheter ablation will be enrolled and randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive either PFA combined with RDN or PFA combined with a sham RDN procedure. Antiarrhythmic drugs (AADs) will be discontinued after the index procedure in both groups. The primary endpoint is freedom from documented atrial tachyarrhythmia recurrence, including AF, atrial flutter, or atrial tachycardia lasting more than 30 seconds, within 12 months after a single ablation procedure without AADs. Secondary endpoints include freedom from atrial tachycardia recurrence within 3 months, AF burden, blood pressure changes, and major adverse cardiovascular events. Safety endpoints include cardiac, vascular, renal, and other procedure-related adverse events.

Conclusions

This trial will assess the safety and efficacy of PFA with RDN in a postablation contemporary persistent AF patient population.

Trial registration

ClinicalTrials.gov:NCT07320768.

title: Long-term outcomes following modified Blalock-Taussig-Thomas shunt placement in 13 dogs with cyanotic congenital heart disease.
authorString: Rossanese M, Hannabuss J, Brockman D.

journal.title: The Journal of small animal practice

abstractText:
Objectives

To describe long-term outcome and owner-perceived quality of life in dogs with cyanotic congenital cardiac disease undergoing modified Blalock-Taussig-Thomas shunt procedure.

Materials and methods

Medical records of dogs that underwent Blalock-Taussig-Thomas shunt between 2009 and 2025 at a small animal referral hospital were retrospectively reviewed. Complications, long-term outcomes and quality of life were assessed via clinical examination and/or contact with owners or referring veterinarians.

Results

Thirteen dogs were included. The predominant clinical signs were exercise intolerance, cyanosis and a heart murmur. Diagnosis included tetralogy of Fallot (n = 8), double outlet right ventricle (n = 3); tetralogy of Fallot-double outlet right ventricle spectrum (n = 1) and tetralogy of Fallot with pulmonary atresia spectrum (n = 1). All dogs survived surgery. Follow-up was available for 12 dogs, ranging from 58 to 2094 days. Eight dogs died or were euthanased for cardiac-related reasons, three were alive at follow-up and one dog was alive 278 days after surgery at last point of contact. All dogs showed a marked postoperative clinical improvement. Shunt obstruction or partial obstruction was documented in three of 12 dogs at 265, 587 and 693 days. Postoperative balloon valvuloplasty was performed in three of the 12 dogs, one died during the procedure and two dogs showed clinical improvement and extended good quality survival. Owners' perception of the procedure outcome and quality of life was described as good, with only mild adjustments needed for exercise.

Clinical significance

Blalock-Taussig-Thomas shunt is an effective palliative option for dogs with cyanotic congenital cardiac diseases associated with reduced pulmonary blood flow, providing sustained clinical improvement and quality of life. Recurrence of clinical signs could indicate shunt obstruction and warrants prompt assessment.

title: Assisted Reproductive Technology and Risk of Congenital Heart Defects in the Offspring: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Rinaldi R, Bujak K, Laudani C, Occhipinti G, Caffè A, Animati FM, Scarica V, Łajczak P, Flores-Umanzor E, Luna-Lopez R, Nicolini E, Piva T, Pawlas N, Regueiro A, Freixa X, Gąsior M, Ottani F, Crea F, Montone RA.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

To date, >10 million children have been conceived via assisted reproductive technology (ART) globally. However, there are some concerns about potential adverse outcomes associated with ART-conceived pregnancies, including the risk of congenital heart defects (CHDs). This meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the association between ART and the risk of major CHDs as well as their specific subtypes.

Methods

Major electronic databases were screened for studies comparing the incidence of CHD following ART-conceived pregnancies versus spontaneous conception. The primary end point was study-defined incidence of CHDs. Secondary end points included incidence of tetralogy of Fallot, transposition of the great arteries, aortic coarctation, ventricular septal defect, atrial septal defect, pulmonary valve atresia, tricuspid valve atresia, and hypoplastic left heart. Pairwise meta-analyses were performed using frequentist random-effect models to calculate risk ratios and 95% CIs.

Results

Thirteen studies, encompassing a total of 45 916 925 subjects (4986 conceived via ART), were included in the quantitative synthesis. ART was significantly associated with a higher risk of major CHD compared with natural pregnancy (risk ratio, 2.35 [95% CI, 1.68-3.28]), with significant heterogeneity across the studies. An increased risk of tetralogy of Fallot, ventricular septal defect, and atrial septal defect following ART-conceived pregnancies was found, while no difference was found on other CHDs. Prespecified sensitivity analyses were in line with the primary findings of the meta-analysis.

Conclusions

Our meta-analysis shows a potential link between ART and increased risk of major CHDs, particularly on tetralogy of Fallot, ventricular septal defect, and atrial septal defect.
